title: Wyden, Merkley Press Officials for Answers on UAS Testing Pauses in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook
text:
Oregon senators: “Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today asked the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and its designated administrator of unmanned aircraft system (UAS) test sites in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook for an update about the recent suspension of all flight operations at those three Oregon locales.

The Oregon senators said their letter comes after operations at those three UAS test sites were paused on Sept. 11 due to concerns at the University of Alaska Fairbanks UAS test site, which serves as the FAA’s designated administrator to test and develop UAS technology, and to oversee operations for test sites across the West.

“While we understand that the pause was necessary due to the FAA’s concerns regarding safety practices, oversight, and documentation, the situation has disrupted flight activity at all other test sites that operate under the University of Alaska Fairbanks,” Wyden and Merkley wrote FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and Dr. Catherine F. Cahill, Director of the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft System Integration. “In Oregon, this pause delays testing and development for aerospace and defense contractors, federal customers, and commercial UAS companies who operate at the Pendleton UAS Range, Northwest UAV in McMinnville, and Tillamook UAS Test Range.”

Wyden and Merkley wrote that the testing pause has created significant uncertainty for Oregon communities, noting for example that the Pendleton UAS range generates roughly $2.4 million annually for the Eastern Oregon Regional Airport -- roughly 82 percent of the airport’s total revenue at the airport.

“Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution,” the senators wrote. “We appreciate the FAA’s efforts to review safety practices and conduct oversight. We also recognize the timeliness and importance of resuming operations at all test sites that have been impacted by the pause.”

The senators asked for responses to their letter by Oct. 7, given the significant economic uncertainty facing the test sites.

The entire letter is here.

title: Rep. Smith and Rep. Krishnamoothi Introduce Legislation to Help Immigrants Enter the Health Care Workforce
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (October 1, 2026) – Today, Congressman Adam Smith (WA-09) and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) introduced the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act and the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act, two bills to help immigrants enter the U.S. health care workforce and address the nation's growing shortage of health care providers. A 2022 study by the Migration Policy Institute found that 2.1 million college-educated immigrants are unemployed or underemployed, even as sectors like health care face mounting workforce shortages — including a projected shortfall of up to 48,000 primary care physicians by 2034, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges.

“We have thousands of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals in this country whose training and expertise are going to waste because their professional expertise is not recognized and they face numerous barriers to achieve the needed licensure. At the same time, our health care system is stretched thin and patients are waiting longer for care,” said Congressman Adam Smith. “This bill package helps immigrants put their skills to work and serve their communities and will rebuild the health care system.”

“Skilled doctors, nurses, and other health professionals should have the opportunity to put their training and expertise to work caring for patients,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our legislation would help qualified immigrants overcome unnecessary barriers to entering the health care workforce while helping communities address critical provider shortages. When we make better use of the talent already in our communities, we strengthen our health care system and expand access to care.”

Statements of Support

“Across the U.S., communities face critical health workforce shortages, yet immigrant and refugee health professionals—who possess in-demand skills—remain underemployed. Communities need this talent, and recognizing it is an essential step. By streamlining licensure and addressing unnecessary barriers, we can meet urgent labor needs and improve access to quality care. We support efforts, including at the state and federal levels, to advance policies that promote community prosperity by ensuring that immigrants can fully contribute their training and skills to their local economy.” - Kit Taintor, Head of US Policy and Practice, World Education Services (WES)

“We are proud to support these bills, which will expand opportunities for immigrant professionals while helping address critical workforce shortages in the healthcare sector," said Alice Kang, President of Upwardly Global. "With demand for healthcare workers rising nationwide, we should be creating pathways that allow qualified immigrants and refugees to contribute their expertise. This legislation will strengthen our healthcare system, bolster the economy and support safer, more resilient communities. Upwardly Global will continue to stand with Rep. Smith in moving this work forward.”

"Many members of our team hold advanced education and expertise in medicine, nursing, and behavioral health. Yet they are unable to practice here due to costly additional education requirements and complex licensing procedures. At a time when we are confronted with a significant healthcare provider shortage—and as we work to diversify the healthcare workforce—it is critical to consider policies that create pathways for these highly skilled professionals to contribute to patient care,” said Tamara Cyhan Cunitz, MN, RN, Executive Director, Nashi Immigrants Health Board. “These bills introduced by Rep. Smith would expand opportunities for immigrant healthcare professionals to serve patients in our community and region. These measures would not only strengthen our workforce with qualified providers but also enable community members to receive care from clinicians who understand their language and cultural background.”

Background

The Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act would help immigrants, regardless of previous health care experience, enter the nursing and allied health workforce by:

Creating grants for programs that provide training, licensing, certification, and case management for immigrants interested in entering the health care field; and

Opening eligibility for the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to non-U.S.-citizen immigrants.

An estimated 200,000 nurses per year will need to be hired to meet increased demand and replace retiring nurses. This bill supports immigrants entering nursing or an allied health profession, including dental hygienists, dietitians, medical technologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech language pathologists.

A fact sheet about the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

The Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act would help internationally trained physicians (ITPs) obtain a U.S. medical license by:

Incentivizing states to create temporary licensing programs allowing internationally educated immigrants with medical degrees to practice under supervision while completing the training and certification needed for a U.S. medical license;

Establishing guaranteed medical residency slots for ITPs to practice in predominantly medically underserved communities; and

Providing grants to help cover the cost of exam preparation, testing, certification, ESL classes, and case management for ITPs in need of financial assistance.

Apart from Canada, internationally trained physicians cannot immediately apply to sit for the U.S. Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE), and the cost of licensing, test preparation, and certification often puts a U.S. medical license out of reach, even for highly trained professionals. Many states have created alternative licensure pathways, but more must be done at the federal level to support these reforms nationwide to expand high-quality health care access.

A fact sheet about the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

Endorsements: International Medical Graduates Academy (TIMGA), Nashi Immigrants Health Board, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Sea Mar Community Health Center, Seattle Indian Health Board, Spring Institute for Intercultural Learning, Talent Beyond Boundaries, Upwardly Global, World Education Services (WES)

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces Nearly $5 Million in Grants for Childcare and Career Programs at Cal State San Bernardino
text:
The funding will help with childcare for student parents and support learning and job preparation in STEM and healthcare industries for working-class students at CSUSB

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced a total of $4,871,289 in grants for California State University, San Bernardino (CSUSB) to support student parents by providing childcare services as well as strengthening STEM and healthcare educational opportunities for low-income students to prepare them for good-paying careers.

The funding includes a $3,541,904 grant for CSUSB to provide affordable childcare services to Pell Grant-eligible undergraduate students with children between the ages of 6 months and 12 years old. This will allow student parents to pursue their degrees while their children receive quality care.

Also included in the funding is $1,329,385 that will allow CSUSB to develop new academic programs and career pathways in STEM and healthcare for low-income and rural students. The university will invest in educational outreach programs, create undergraduate research opportunities and help connect students with internships and apprenticeships related to careers in these industries. Rep. Aguilar wrote a letter to the Department of Education in support of CSUSB’s application for this important grant.

“Whether you’re a new parent in school or come from a working-class community, where you start out shouldn’t decide whether you finish a degree and land a good-paying job,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “I am proud to announce this funding for CSUSB, which will provide childcare support for student parents so they can stay in school and expand academic opportunities in STEM and healthcare for low-income students. I’m excited to see how these grants help Inland Empire residents of all backgrounds be successful.”

“Cal State San Bernardino is grateful to the U.S. Department of Education for awarding the university nearly $4.9 million through two grants: the Strengthening Institutions and Child Care Access Means Parents in School programs,” said Terri Gómez, President, California State University, San Bernardino. “The $1.3 million Strengthening Institutions grant will expand educational and career pathways in STEM and health care and strengthen support for low-income and rural students. The $3.5 million Child Care Access Means Parents in School (CCAMPIS) grant will help student parents continue their education by providing access to essential childcare services. We sincerely thank Congressman Pete Aguilar for his continued advocacy on behalf of CSUSB and the Inland Empire, including his letter supporting our Strengthening Institutions Program application. His partnership helps the university expand opportunity, improve student success, and prepare graduates to meet the workforce needs of our region.”

The $3.5 million grant comes from the U.S. Department of Education’s Child Care Access Means Parents in School (CCAMPIS) Program (84.335A). The $1.3 million grant comes from the U.S. Department of Education’s Strengthening Institutions Program (84.031A).

title: Alford Introduces Legislation to Strengthen SBA’s Rural and Faith-Based Outreach
text:
Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04), Chairman of the House Small Business Committee’s Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations, introduced the Faith and Rural Small Business Act to strengthen the Small Business Administration’s (SBA) ability to serve rural and faith-based communities.

The legislation would codify the SBA’s Office of Rural Affairs and elevate its leadership to an Assistant Administrator. It would also establish a Center for Faith within the SBA’s Office of Entrepreneurial Development, led by a Director appointed by the SBA Administrator.

“The SBA should meet entrepreneurs where they are, whether that’s on Main Street in rural Missouri or in a faith community serving its neighbors. This legislation supports the SBA’s reorganization by strengthening its focus on rural America and faith-based entrepreneurship and ensuring more entrepreneurs can access the resources they need to succeed,” said Congressman Alford.

Read the full text of the legislation here.

Background:

The legislation builds on Alford’s efforts to make the SBA more responsive to communities outside Washington, D.C. In 2025, Alford introduced the Rural Innovation and Small Business Support Act to expand SBA outreach in rural communities and the Returning SBA to Main Street Act, which passed the House Small Business Committee and would decentralize SBA personnel across the country.

This legislation continues those efforts by strengthening the SBA’s Office of Rural Affairs and codifying a Center for Faith within the agency’s Office of Entrepreneurial Development.

The bill would amend the Small Business Act to formally establish both offices within the SBA’s organizational structure.

title: RI Delegation Announces $9.1 Million to Boost Public Safety & Support Local Law Enforcement
text:
Washington, DC – In an effort to improve public safety, U.S. Senators Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse and U.S. Representatives Seth Magaziner and Gabe Amo today announced $9,101,109 in federal funding to support police officers, law enforcement agencies, crime victims, and nonprofit organizations.

This federal funding will be used to implement a range of crime reduction strategies, criminal justice initiatives, and assistance for crime victims, and to help keep people and communities safe, including:

• Combating violence and various forms of crime with evidence-based, collaborative strategies and programs;

• Preventing domestic violence and sexual assault and assisting survivors and victims of crime through court and hospital visits;

• Upgrading critical technological infrastructure and acquisition of public safety vehicles and protective gear.

“This federal funding will improve public safety, prevent crimes, and serve justice. I am committed to ensuring our law enforcement officers are well-equipped and well-trained. This federal funding will help them take a comprehensive approach to reducing crime, supporting victims, and strengthening relationships between law enforcement and the communities they serve,” said Senator Reed.

“As a former U.S. Attorney and attorney general, I’ve seen firsthand how increasing resources for local law enforcement and community organizations can make a difference in people’s lives,” said Senator Whitehouse, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee. “Our delegation has helped deliver federal funding to modernize our criminal justice system, expand behavioral and mental health services, and protect public safety.”

“Every Rhode Islander deserves to feel safe and supported in their community. This federal funding will equip our police officers with resources to protect the public, while making sure survivors of violence and abuse get the support they need,” said Magaziner. “I am proud to join my colleagues to bring home more federal funding for law enforcement officers across our state and will continue to stand up for first responders.”

“Rhode Islanders deserve to feel safe in their communities,” said Congressman Gabe Amo. “This federal funding will help support survivors, strengthen local law enforcement, and give communities the resources they need to prevent and respond to crime. I will continue to work alongside our delegation in Congress to provide the resources our communities need to remain safe and secure.”

Background

This round of federal funding, which was secured in recent appropriations laws, will be distributed to the state, as well as to local police departments, state agencies, support organizations, and nonprofits, including:

$4,583,223 for Rhode Island’s Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) funds to provide direct services like counseling, personal advocacy, court advocacy, client transportation, and support services to victims of crimes including domestic violence, sexual violence, child abuse, and elder abuse as they move through the criminal justice system.

$2,657,307 for the Rhode Island Department of Public Safety to provide supplemental crisis response services for victims.

$791,279 to the Rhode Island Department of Public Safety for the Sexual Assault Services Formula Program.

$343,065 for the Office of Violence Against Women (OVW) State and Territory Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Coalitions Program to coordinate victim services activities.

$265,000 from the Crime Victims Fund to enhance State Victim Compensation payments to eligible crime victims.

$197,757 for the Providence Police Marine Unit to purchase a marine enforcement operation vessel for use in and around the waterways of the Providence and Seekonk Rivers, enabling effective rapid response and public safety enforcement within these complex urban estuarine environments.

$76,359 for the Pawtucket Police Department to support the Pawtucket Police JAG Overtime Initiative.

$60,948 for the Woonsocket Police Department to sustain community policing programs (bicycle patrols and the Police Explorers Post) and purchase a thermal drone.

$31,021 for the Cranston Police Department to implement a specialized Drone as First Responder initiative.

$25,254 for the Central Falls Police Department to purchase information technology equipment and supplies.

$19,090 for the Warwick Police Department to support the acquisition of critical underwater communication equipment for its Underwater Search & Recovery Team.

$16,107 for Newport Police to integrate technology to increase the probability of peaceful resolutions when communicating with suspects or individuals in crisis.

$14,118 for the City of East Providence to purchase equipment in relation to speed enforcement.

$10,539 for the North Providence Police Department to purchase body armor gear.

$10,042 for the Coventry Police Department to purchase Honor Guard uniforms.

title: Ansari, Bennet, Padilla, Hickenlooper, Schiff, Luján Introduce Legislation to Protect Public Lands and Taxpayers from Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) and Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet led U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) to introduce the Stop Orphaned Wells Act, legislation that would prevent oil and gas companies from abandoning oil wells on public lands, a practice that shifts well cleanup costs from oil and gas companies to the American taxpayer.

“Trump asked oil and gas executives to bankroll his campaign with a $1 billion contribution in exchange for a big payback. Meanwhile, Americans are left footing the bill for the damage they leave behind,” said Ansari. “Orphaned wells threaten our water, wildlife, and air. I’m proud to lead the effort alongside Senator Bennet to make the oil and gas industry clean up its own mess. Our bill would ensure oil and gas companies pay to clean up the wells they abandon.”

“For too long, taxpayers have footed the bill to clean up abandoned wells after companies walk away from their responsibilities,” said Bennet. “As the Trump administration moves to weaken the safeguards that hold companies accountable, Congress must protect taxpayers and the public lands that power Colorado’s outdoor economy, while making sure oil and gas companies pay the cost of cleanup, rather than Colorado's future generations.”

“Across California, there are over 5,000 orphaned oil wells that pose a threat to the health and safety of our communities and the environment,” said Padilla. “When wells are left abandoned, drinking water is polluted, greenhouse gases are emitted, and the climate crisis is accelerated. This bill will help ensure orphaned oil and gas wells are plugged so Californians and communities across the country are protected from toxic emissions and contaminated air and water.”

“Abandoned wells put Colorado communities in danger,” said Hickenlooper. “As Governor, we capped as many of these wells as we could, and that work continues here in the Senate, where we’re protecting taxpayers from getting stuck with the bill. Capping wells creates jobs and lowers pollution. It’s a win-win.”

“Oil companies can’t just walk away from abandoned oil and gas wells and leave taxpayers to bear the cleanup costs,” said Schiff. “I’m joining Senator Bennet and other colleagues to make sure that Big Oil is responsible for cleaning up their messes. Americans should not have to deal with the consequences of an oil company’s negligence.”

“In New Mexico and across the country, abandoned wells pose serious environmental harm and threaten the health of our communities,” said Luján. “We must ensure that oil and gas companies are held accountable and that taxpayers are not on the hook for the cost of cleanup. I've long fought to address abandoned wells, including championing the REGROW Act that was passed into law, and continue to work to ensure we identify and plug the thousands of abandoned wells nationwide. That’s why I’m cosponsoring this legislation to prevent companies from abandoning their wells and help reduce the number of abandoned wells in New Mexico and across the country.”

“When an oil and gas company goes bankrupt, New Mexicans shouldn’t be the ones left to pick up the tab for cleanup costs,” said Heinrich. “Right now, the Trump administration is making it easier for these companies to walk away without enough money set aside to clean up their wells. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act ensures that companies set aside money to meet their cleanup responsibilities, so taxpayers aren’t left paying the bill.”

Until 2024 when the Biden administration added agency rules, oil and gas fiscal assurance requirements were minimal, leading companies to abandon wells instead of remediating the land after drilling. The Trump administration is now rolling back these essential protections for public lands and American taxpayers. Nationwide, there are currently over 140,000 documented orphaned wells, including more than 15,000 on federal lands, and hundreds of thousands more that may be orphaned. Additionally, the number of documented orphaned wells in the United States has more than doubled since 2020. These sites are not only a significant liability for taxpayers and a growing threat to water resources, air quality, wildlife habitat, and private lands, but also jeopardize public health, ecosystems, grazing lands, outdoor recreation sites, and cultural resources that are at high risk from contamination.

This legislation is supported by 20 organizations, including Earthjustice Action, Colorado Fiscal Institute, Conservatives for Responsible Stewardship, Conservation Colorado, Montana Wildlife Federation, National Parks Conservation Association, Natural Resources Defense Council, Nevada Wildlife Federation, New Mexico Wildlife Federation, Public Land Solutions, Rocky Mountain Wild, San Juan Citizen’s Alliance, Sierra Club, Taxpayers for Common Sense, Trout Unlimited, Western Colorado Alliance, Western Organization of Resource Councils, Western Resilience Center, Wild Montana, Wilderness Workshop, and The Wilderness Society. In addition, this legislation was endorsed by U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

title: As Grocery Prices Skyrocket, Congresswoman Barragán Sounds the Alarm on New Trump SNAP Cut Taking Effect Today
text:
As new cuts kick in, 5 million have already lost SNAP after initial Trump cuts

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

October 2, 2026

Contact: Jin.Choi@mail.house.gov

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Barragán (CA-44) warned that another SNAP cut from H.R. 1, the Republican Reconciliation Law, has gone into effect.

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is federally funded and administered by states. H.R. 1 cut the federal share of funding for SNAP administrative costs in half, meaning that states are now required to cover 75% of SNAP administrative costs. Those cuts became effective on October 1, 2026. Nationwide, this represents over $16 billion in reduced funding for SNAP.

In California, this means the state will have to pay at least $670 million more to keep the program operating. For state-by-state estimates of SNAP funding cuts effective today, click here.

The reduction of administrative funding leaves states with fewer resources to process applications, determine eligibility, and ensure families receive the benefits they are eligible for. This massive funding cut also jeopardizes other state and local services as states struggle to replace this lost funding. A similar cost shift, cutting federal payments to states for SNAP benefits, will go into effect October 1, 2027.

“Donald Trump and Republicans chose to give tax breaks to billionaires while making it harder for working families to put food on the table,” said Congresswoman Barragán. “Now, they are forcing states to pick up the tab for SNAP as they pile on new requirements and red tape onto a program that millions of Americans rely on to feed their families. That is the wrong choice, and families in California are paying the price. No parent should have to worry about whether they can afford their next meal because Republicans decided billionaires needed another tax break. I will continue fighting to reverse these cruel cuts, protect SNAP, and make sure families—not billionaires—are our priority.”

“Trump and Republicans in Congress passed tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires on the backs of families who are already struggling to afford sky-high grocery costs. Over 5 million Americans have already lost SNAP food assistance because of Trump’s cuts, and today, another SNAP cut from the Big Ugly Law kicks in. Trump and Republicans have handed states huge SNAP funding cuts, with more cuts coming next year. Worse still, these administrative cuts are coming as Republicans have also made SNAP more difficult to access. They’ve created new paperwork and new requirements, then cut the funding used to enroll people. Congress must fix these cuts through the Farm Bill and protect families who rely on SNAP to keep food on the table,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown, Vice Ranking Member on the House Agriculture Committee.

According to USDA data, more than 5 million Americans, including about 2 million children, have already lost SNAP since H.R. 1 was enacted in July 2025. In California, over 330,000 have lost SNAP coverage in the last year.

H.R.1’s SNAP cuts were enacted alongside cuts to Medicaid and other programs to pay for tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefited large corporations and the wealthiest Americans. The Republican Farm Bill which passed the House and is currently under consideration in the Senate, locks in $187 billion in SNAP cuts. Republicans rejected all Democratic attempts to roll back SNAP cuts in the House Farm Bill.

title: Egypt Human Rights Caucus Co-Chairs Urge Immediate Release of Detained Egyptian Journalists
text:
U.S. Representatives Don Beyer (D-VA) and Suzan DelBene (D-WA), Co-Chairs of the Egypt Human Rights Caucus, today urged the Egyptian government to immediately and unconditionally release the six journalists affiliated with independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash and end its escalating crackdown on independent media:

“As co-chairs of the Egypt Human Rights Caucus, we call on Egyptian authorities to immediately and unconditionally release the six journalists affiliated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash. The arrest of the outlet’s entire newsroom is a clear escalation in the government’s campaign to stifle press freedom in the country.

“Even prior to these arrests, Egypt has consistently ranked as one of the world’s most repressive regimes and has a long history of unfairly targeting independent media outlets and drastically limiting freedom of expression. Egyptian authorities regularly claim, without sufficient evidence or due process, that critics of the government are members of the Muslim Brotherhood. The recent arrests are the latest and most alarming case of this tactic on display.

“We have tried to engage constructively with the Egyptian government on our concerns about the country’s human rights situation, including its arbitrary detention of journalists and targeting of media outlets. These arrests demonstrate why Congress must strengthen its resolve, demand better from its partner, and continue to condition U.S. military aid to Egypt on demonstrable rights reforms.”

title: Scott Statement on September Jobs Report
text:
As originally released by the Committee on Education and Workforce, Democrats

WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the Bureau of Labor Statistics announced that the economy gained 29,000 jobs in September, and the unemployment rate increased from 4.1 percent to 4.2 percent.

“This Trump economy might be working for the wealthy and the well connected, but it clearly is leaving workers behind. CEO pay is skyrocketing, while for working people, it's a daily struggle just to cover groceries and rent. Workers’ wages are failing tokeep up with inflation, and the increasing cost of daily expenses are eating into workers’ paychecks. According to the Century Foundation, inflation-adjusted debt payments grew faster than income in recent years as working families have struggled to make ends meet.

“The jobs numbers show the same strain: Trump has added only 776,000 jobs between January 2025 and September 2026, while the Biden administration added 10.7 million within its first 20 months. Since President Trump returned to office, not one month has reached the average monthly job creation under the Biden administration. In fact, he has not even achieved 70 percent of Biden’s monthly average.

“And now, as a result of the ‘Big Ugly Bill’s’ cuts to the SNAP program, families are losing their food assistance. An estimated 4.5 million people have lost their SNAP benefits, including more than 1.5 million children. Across the country, people are feeling the impact. In North Carolina, demand at food pantries and food banks is up 20 percent this year, as SNAP enrollment has plummeted by more than 110,000 people since September 2025. In Kansas, one pantry reports distributing 50 percent more food than a year ago. In Oregon, pantry directors say they have gone from being a supplemental resource to the primary source of food, and many incoming families have never had to ask for help before. This is what happens when tax breaks for the wealthy are paid for by taking food off the tables of working families.

“That's why I, alongside my Democratic colleagues, am fighting to put working families first. Children cannot learn on an empty stomach, and parents cannot build a better life when they cannot afford groceries. We will keep pushing to protect school meals, strengthen job training, lower the cost of college, and make sure every worker can earn a living wage and retire with dignity.”

title: REP. BOEBERT: COLORADO’S FOURTH DISTRICT 2026 CONGRESSIONAL APP CHALLENGE DEADLINE LESS THAN ONE MONTH AWAY
text:
EATON, CO Rep. Lauren Boebert (CO-04) announced today that less than one month remains before the deadline for the 2026 Congressional App Challenge.

Since 2015, the Congressional App Challenge has encouraged middle and high school students to explore careers in STEM and software development. Rep. Boebert’s office participates in the challenge and selects district winners based on the quality of each entry. The competition is nonpartisan and is an official duty of congressional offices that choose to take part.

“I’m looking forward to seeing what students in the Fourth District can develop this year,” said Rep. Boebert. “This challenge is a great way for young people to build real skills in technology and show what they can create.”

Teachers can incorporate the challenge into lesson plans, and students may also complete entries outside the classroom. The submission deadline for the Congressional App Challenge is October 26, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. EST. Winners will be announced in early December.

Students can register and learn more at: https://www.congressionalappchallenge.us/students/student-registration/

For more information on the 2026 challenge and how to submit entries for Rep. Lauren Boebert’s Fourth Congressional District, contact the Eaton Office at 970-702-2136.

title: REP. BOEBERT WELCOMES NEARLY $2.4 MILLION IN VETERANS SUICIDE PREVENTION GRANTS BENEFITTING COLORADO’S 4TH DISTRICT
text:
Lone Tree, CO — Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04) today welcomed nearly $2.4 million in grants from the Department of Veterans Affairs for four organizations benefitting veterans in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District through the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program.

The awards are part of $112 million the VA is distributing nationwide for community suicide prevention. The four organizations are:

Rocky Mountain Veterans Advocacy Project — $750,000

Veterans Community Project — $748,663

Healing Warriors Program — $477,458

Eastern Plains Healthcare Consortium — $400,000

“Too many veterans are still lost to suicide, and rural Colorado cannot be an afterthought,” said Rep. Boebert. “These grants put prevention resources where veterans live across the 4th District so the VA meets the men and women who already served this country.”

The Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program funds community groups that reach veterans who may not be enrolled in VA care, including help with mental health, social connection, financial stability, and access to services. Congress authorized the program to expand suicide prevention beyond VA clinics.

Veterans in crisis, and their families, can call 988 and press 1, text 838255, or chat at VeteransCrisisLine.net.VA

title: Casar, Brown Demand Answers on FBI’s Plan to Buy Flock Cameras and Other Mass Surveillance Systems
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX), Ranking Member of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) sent a letter demanding answers and transparency from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel on the FBI’s planned increase of mass surveillance systems, such as Flock.

In May 2026, the FBI issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to acquire automatic license plate readers (ALPR) systems, including Flock and Motorola Solutions, that offer the ability to search for license plate information “and other descriptive data such as vehicle description information, time/date criteria, and geo-location criteria.” Flock and Motorola Solutions, whose ALPR systems are used by local police departments, likely possess the capabilities to satisfy this RFP. While the FBI already runs a License Plate Reader (LPR) program through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to facilitate LPR information sharing with and between its law enforcement partners, the FBI’s plan to obtain direct access to an extensive network of cameras—such as those operated by Flock and Motorola—would dramatically expand the license plate data currently held by the FBI and institute “near real time” surveillance of civilians.

The Members of Congress write: “The American people are clearly concerned about law enforcement having access to Flock data and about government surveillance more broadly. Entering into a contract that would give the nation’s largest law enforcement agency access to Flock data across the country would subvert the clear preference of the American people.”

The Oversight and Government Reform Committee Democrats are requesting information by October 16, 2026.

Read the full letter here.

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.

title: Castro, Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats Issue Statement on State Department’s Partial Production of Venezuela Oil Deal Documents
text:
Reps. Joaquin Castro, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Democratic Members of the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, issued the following statement after the State Department provided the Committee with one document related to the Trump Administration’s deal signed with Alejandro Betancourt to acquire a stake in North American Blue Energy Partners:

“We appreciate that State has provided this document, but a single document falls far short of the records Democrats have requested as we conduct oversight over the Trump administration’s Venezuela policy. When Democrats sought to subpoena the documents on September 15, Republicans, led by Chairwoman Maria Elvira Salazar, voted to shield the administration from accountability and protect Alejandro Betancourt and Delcy Rodriguez from scrutiny.

“Democrats will continue to examine the Trump administration’s actions with respect to Venezuela, and we call on Secretary Rubio to produce to the Committee all remaining requested documents, including the agreement between Delcy Rodriguez and Betancourt, as well as KPMG’s independent audits of the Foreign Government Deposit Funds, the account Trump established after his administration began seizing Venezuelan oil revenues.

“Congress cannot conduct meaningful oversight based on selective disclosures. Providing one document while withholding other central records raises further questions about what the administration is trying to conceal.”

Congressman Castro added, “Last month, I motioned to subpoena the Trump Administration for records regarding its deal with Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt for Venezuelan oil. This week, we were able to secure a limited set of documents from the administration regarding this shady deal. It's a start but no where near what the Administration must provide Congress. There's billions of dollars moving hands and next to zero accountability. Americans are sick of corruption, and Venezuelans are too. We will continue these investigations until we have accountability.”

Additional background:

On February 13, 2026, HFAC Democrats requested information regarding the Trump administration’s decision to route Venezuela oil revenues into an offshore account in Qatar.

On April 17, 2026, Congressional Democrats requested the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a full audit of this deal. The GAO accepted the request and the audit remains ongoing. Read the full details of the audit and the full letter here.

On September 10, 2026, HFAC Democrats requested KPMG audits of the deal to be transmitted to Congress within 30 days of completion. The members also requested a complete accounting of all disbursements made from the fund since its establishment. The Members request a response by October 8, 2026. Read the full letter here.

title: During San Antonio Field Hearing, Castro, Local Leaders Demand Accountability For ICE Operations And Proposed Warehouse
text:
SAN ANTONIO, TX — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) hosted a field hearing in San Antonio, entitled, “Examining the Community Impacts of Mass Deportation and Proposed ICE Warehouse.” He was joined by elected officials at the dais including Texas State Senator Roland Gutierrez (TX-19), Texas State Senator José Menéndez (TX-26), Texas State Representative Barbara Gervin-Hawkins (HD-120), Councilwoman Phyllis Viagran, City Council District 3. Hearing witnesses included Kristin Etter, Director of Policy and Legal Services, Texas Immigration Law Council, Priscilla Olivarez, Managing Policy Attorney with the Immigrant Legal Resource Center, and the Reverend Father Jimmy Drennan, St. Margaret Mary Catholic Church, COPS/Metro Alliance. Additional San Antonio leaders expressed their support for the hearing, including Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones and Councilman Ric Galvan, City Council District 6.

“San Antonio is one of the epicenters for ICE activity and ranks fourth in the nation for arrests,” said Congressman Castro. “The first American citizen shot by ICE, Ruben Ray Martinez, was a son of San Antonio. South of the city, the Dilley Trailer Prison has locked away thousands of children without proper food, medical care, and schooling. Texas National Guardsmen and local police in Texas have been deputized by ICE, supercharging arrests and detentions. Our community has become collateral damage in Trump’s mass deportation machine. Now this proposed warehouse on the East Side would extend these abuses deeper into our community and our lives. None of this is making life easier or more affordable for San Antonio families—it is tearing families apart, targeting our communities, and leaving a dark stain on our nation.”

“ICE is a rogue agency that shoots first and asks questions later. They are terrorizing our communities and torturing people with impunity,” said Senator Gutierrez. “The cruelty must end now”.

“The Trump Administration and Governor Abbott have colluded to stoke fear in our communities and incite human rights violations across our country. We must hold them accountable to protect people and restore basic human rights. Thank you, Congressman Castro and his team, for organizing a safe space for experts in the field and community members to discuss the threats to us all,” said Senator Menéndez.

“Today, I join U.S. Representative Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and other community leaders for a San Antonio field hearing to examine community impacts of mass deportation and the proposed ICE warehouse in San Antonio's East side in House District 120 that I represent. Like many faith leaders and others, I view the care and support of migrants not as a political issue, but as a fundamental obligation of human morality, compassion, and dignity. I will continue to fight for those that are being harmed and oppressed by this unjust system. I simply ask you to join us in this fight for human decency,” said Texas State Representative Barbara Gervin-Hawkins (HD-120).

“This was an excellent opportunity to work alongside my state and federal colleagues to identify a real path forward to prevent ICE facilities from entering the City of San Antonio. I am committed to working with my Council colleagues on a solid plan to address the inequities and impacts an ICE facility would have on our city, particularly on the East Side. I want to thank all of the community members who came out to listen, participate, and support their elected officials in this effort. Our panelists did an excellent job providing critical information and perspectives that will help inform our work as we move forward,” said Councilwoman Phyllis Viagran.

“A new detention center in Texas only works to expand the capacity to detain more of our community members and separate more families. The harm reaches beyond the household; we have seen that when parents and workers are detained, families lose income, businesses lose employees, and local economies lose the spending that helps them thrive. Our communities need investments that help families put down roots and thrive. We urge leaders to reject this expansion and focus on keeping Texas families, communities, and local economies together,” said Kristin Etter, Director of Policy and Legal Services, Texas Immigration Law Council.

“If the ICE warehouse is allowed to open, vital city resources will be misused to support the unlawful detention of our loved ones,” said Priscilla Olivarez, Managing Policy Attorney with the Immigrant Legal Resource Center. “I stand alongside the San Antonio community who are rightfully demanding DHS complete all federally mandated impact assessments before further steps are taken to open the ICE warehouse. San Antonio residents deserve to know the full adverse impact the ICE facility will have on those detained within its walls and the critical resources the facility will divert from our city.”

“What we are witnessing now is the re-institutionalization of discrimination in our law enforcement community, specifically ICE, against American citizens and our immigrant neighbors alike. People who are not properly vetted and not properly trained are coming into our institutions, and it is going to rip the fabric of our community apart unless it is brought to an end," said the Reverend Father Jimmy Drennan. “These are real people. I've looked into their eyes, and I've heard their stories. Their fear is real, and their fear is justified. In San Antonio, our community will keep pushing back.”

“I reiterate my opposition to the proposed ICE processing facility on San Antonio’s East Side. San Antonians deserve to feel safe taking their children to school, going to work, and calling police when they need help. Immigration enforcement must respect due process and basic human dignity,” said Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones. “We have pressed the federal government for transparency about this proposal, including its plans for the facility and the potential demands on our water, infrastructure, and emergency services. Our residents deserve answers, and our city deserves a meaningful voice in decisions that affect our neighborhoods. I thank Congressman Castro for convening this hearing and will continue demanding accountability on behalf of San Antonio,” said Mayor Ortiz Jones.

“We must continue to challenge every level of government to take action upon the acts of terror that ICE has committed upon our neighbors—noncitizen and citizen alike. We must demand the accountability of a rogue federal agency that continues to violate constitutional rights here in San Antonio and across our country. We must not back down from the fight. ICE has no home in San Antonio, and it must answer for its crimes against our community,” said Councilmember Ric Galvan.

"The first thing that Congress needs to do is pass a bill to shut down all of the infrastructure for these additional ICE buildings for the detention of human beings," said Bexar County Commissioner Tommy Calvert. "Congress should require the federal government to comply with local zoning regulations and health and safety measures as a check on unbridled tyrants."

“COPS/Metro represents 32 institutions across our city, and we have seen firsthand the impacts of detention and deportation. We are deeply concerned about the human toll of recent ICE arrests in our community and oppose the proposal for an East Side detention center. When parents are detained at workplaces, courthouses, or outside their homes, the harm reaches far beyond the individual. Children are left without caregivers, families lose their income, and entire neighborhoods live in fear. That fear has real consequences. Families are separated, children are kept home from school, and they hesitate to report crimes or cooperate with police. When people are afraid to take part in ordinary civic life, public safety and community trust suffer for everyone. We believe immigration enforcement must respect due process, family unity, and basic human dignity. We call on officials to: Limit enforcement actions at schools, hospitals, houses of worship, and courthouses; Ensure access to legal counsel for people in detention; Provide transparency about who is being detained and why; and pursue lasting, humane reforms to the immigration system. We stand with our immigrant neighbors and will continue to support families affected by these actions,” said Arturo Rodriguez, Leader, COPS/Metro Alliance.

Background:

San Antonio has become one of the cities hit hardest by Trump’s mass deportation campaign, ranking fourth in the nation in ICE arrests. Across Texas, the toll is reaching classrooms, with public schools losing more than 14,000 immigrant students last year. State leaders are continuing to deepen Texas’s role in ICE enforcement, requiring county sheriffs to enter 287(g) agreements with ICE. These agreements deputize local police officers as ICE agents, acting as a force multiplier for ICE arrests, detentions, and deportations. In August, Congressman Castro led a delegation of elected officials representing Bexar County urging cities to withdraw from their 287(g) agreements with ICE.

On March 25, 2025, San Antonio resident Ruben Ray Martinez was shot and killed by an ICE agent. Congressman Castro pushed for accountability when the news became public after the agency didn’t acknowledge its role in his death for nearly a year. ICE has also targeted children, detaining elementary students at their bus stops in San Antonio, including the Uzategui-Labrador family. These children and many others have been detained at the Dilley Trailer Prison, where children, some only a few months old, are held in inhumane conditions.

In January, ICE bought a nearly 640,000-square-foot warehouse on San Antonio’s East Side for $66.1 million. In August, it awarded a $17.3 million contract to GardaWorld Federal Services, the company behind “Alligator Alcatraz,” to retrofit the proposed detention facility and provide wrap-around services. The proposed site would hold 1,000 to 1,500 people daily.

title: Rep. Smith, Sen. Lankford lead over 125 lawmakers in letter urging HHS Inspector General to investigate Planned Parenthood
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ) and Sen. James Lankford (R-OK) today led 126 Members of Congress in sending a letter to T. March Bell, the Inspector General (IG) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), urging his Office to review and investigate the activities and federal funding streams of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and its affiliates.

“Serious concerns have long been raised regarding the organization’s compliance with applicable federal laws, regulations, and program requirements governing the receipt and use of federal funds,” the Republican lawmakers write.

“In particular, these concerns relate to whether Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and the organization’s affiliates have adhered to applicable requirements governing program integrity, financial accountability, and the proper use of funds provided through HHS-administered programs,” they continue.

Rep. Smith, Co-Chairman of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, said: “Planned Parenthood should not receive taxpayer dollars. Since 1970, it has killed over ten million unborn babies in its clinics—and today exterminates over 1,000 unborn babies every single day. Moreover, as the author of our Nation’s first anti-human trafficking law, the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 (TVPA) (PL 106-386), I remain deeply concerned by Live Action’s credible accusations against Planned Parenthood involving its affiliates’ enabling of human sex trafficking. In addition to reports of covering up and perpetuating sexual exploitation and abuse, Planned Parenthood has been haunted by allegations of trafficking fetal tissue, fraudulently using federal funds, and violating health codes. Aided by allies in Congress, the media, and academia, Planned Parenthood has largely escaped scrutiny and accountability, all while fostering a culture of death, denial, disrespect and discrimination against babies. It is long overdue for a comprehensive investigation and review, and I urge the HHS OIG to look closely to determine whether it has violated federal standards for federal funding recipients.”

Sen. Lankford, Chairman of the Senate Values Action Team (VAT), said: “Congress has taken action to ensure taxpayer dollars are not funding organizations that perform abortions, but our work to protect taxpayers and ensure federal law is followed does not stop there. Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have faced serious allegations involving the use of federal funds and compliance with federal law. Those allegations deserve a thorough review. The HHS Inspector General should follow the facts, determine whether federal laws and funding requirements have been violated, and hold accountable anyone who has misused taxpayer dollars.”

In the bicameral letter—first reported by Fox News Digital—the 128 lawmakers cite the Small Business Administration’s (SBA) recent investigation into “whether Planned Parenthood affiliates illegally received $88 million in loans during the COVID-19 pandemic,” and they raise concerns about “other reports of fraud, making false statements, violating federal criminal laws, and knowingly failing to disclose violations of criminal law.”

The Members of Congress further note that “given the significant taxpayer resources that flow through federal health and human services programs, it is critical that recipient organizations operate with transparency, integrity, and full compliance with federal standards.”

The lawmakers go on to urge IG Bell to review the funding streams for Planned Parenthood and its affiliates, including HHS programs, grants, contracts, or subawards; assess whether the organization and its affiliates have complied with applicable statutory, regulatory, and grant conditions associated with those funds; and determine what enforcement actions may be warranted if misconduct—such as waste, fraud, abuse, misrepresentation, or other violations affecting federal health programs—is identified.

“We also ask that the OIG coordinate with relevant oversight bodies within the Department, including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and the Office of Management and Budget, to ensure a comprehensive review of the organization’s activities. Thank you for your continued commitment to protecting the integrity of federal health programs and safeguarding taxpayer dollars,” the co-signatories conclude.

title: Fox News Digital exclusive article on Smith-led letter'EXCLUSIVE: 128 GOP lawmakers call for federal probe into Planned Parenthood's taxpayer funding'
text:
By Jasmine Baehr

Published October 2, 2026 at 5:30am EDT

FIRST ON FOX: A coalition of 128 Republican lawmakers is pressing the federal government to scrutinize Planned Parenthood's taxpayer funding and potentially launch an investigation into the organization and its affiliates.

Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., and Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., led the bicameral effort, asking Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General T. March Bell to review Planned Parenthood's federal funding and determine whether the organization and its affiliates have complied with federal laws and funding requirements.

"We write to request that the Office of Inspector General (OIG) review and, if appropriate, initiate an investigation into the activities of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and the organization's affiliates," the lawmakers wrote.

Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., speaks during an event on Capitol Hill. Smith and Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., led 128 Republican lawmakers in asking the HHS inspector general to review Planned Parenthood’s federal funding and activities.(Getty Images)

Their request casts a rather wide net.

The lawmakers want the OIG to scrutinize funding flowing through HHS programs, grants, contracts and sub-awards and determine whether evidence exists of fraud, waste, abuse, misrepresentation or other violations affecting federal health programs.

If misconduct is uncovered, they want the watchdog to consider consequences ranging from administrative remedies and suspension to exclusion from federal healthcare programs or referrals to other authorities.

"Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have faced serious allegations involving the use of federal funds and compliance with federal law. Those allegations deserve a thorough review," Lankford said.

Republican lawmakers are asking the HHS inspector general to review Planned Parenthood’s federal funding and compliance with federal requirements.(Boston Globe via Getty Images, File)

"The HHS Inspector General should follow the facts, determine whether federal laws and funding requirements have been violated, and hold accountable anyone who has misused taxpayer dollars," he added.

The push comes as the Small Business Administration (SBA) separately reviews more than $88 million in COVID-era Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans received by 38 Planned Parenthood affiliates.

The lawmakers cited the SBA action in their letter, characterizing it as an investigation into whether Planned Parenthood affiliates "illegally received $88 million" in pandemic loans. SBA has described its action as a review of whether the affiliates were eligible for the loans. The review itself is not a finding that the affiliates violated the law.

But the lawmakers want federal scrutiny to go well beyond the pandemic loans.

Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., co-led a bicameral letter asking the HHS inspector general to review Planned Parenthood’s federal funding and, if appropriate, launch an investigation into the organization and its affiliates.(Getty Images)

They are asking the OIG to examine Planned Parenthood's broader HHS funding and coordinate with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on what they described as a "comprehensive review" of the organization's activities.

HHS-OIG told Fox News Digital Wednesday evening that it had not yet received the letter.

"We have not received the letter and will review it for appropriate action once received," HHS-OIG said.

Smith, co-chairman of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, said the scrutiny was "long overdue," citing allegations involving federal funding, reporting requirements, sexual exploitation and fetal tissue.

Activists opposing funding for Planned Parenthood demonstrate in front of the U.S. Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.(Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, via Getty Images, File)

"It is long overdue for a comprehensive investigation and review, and I urge the HHS OIG to look closely to determine whether it has violated federal standards for federal funding recipients," Smith said.

The congressional letter also points to reports alleging failures to comply with mandatory reporting requirements involving suspected child abuse or neglect. The lawmakers are asking federal officials to examine those allegations. They have not been established as findings by HHS-OIG.

"Given the significant taxpayer resources that flow through federal health and human services programs, it is critical that recipient organizations operate with transparency, integrity, and full compliance with federal standards," the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers closed by asking OIG to coordinate across the federal government to conduct a "comprehensive review" of Planned Parenthood's activities.

"Thank you for your continued commitment to protecting the integrity of federal health programs and safeguarding taxpayer dollars," they wrote.

Planned Parenthood did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: 39 Members of Congress send letterSmith leads letter strongly supporting implementation of Pres. Trump’s EO on Protecting Vulnerable Newborn and Infant Children
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), Co-Chair of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, led 38 Members of Congress in sending a letter to U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr., fully supporting and urging the implementation of President Trump’s Executive Order (EO) on Protecting Vulnerable Newborn and Infant Children—issued during his first term—to protect premature infants from discrimination.

“All infants—especially those with disabilities or conditions requiring life-sustaining care after birth—deserve love, compassion, and equal protection under the law,” said Smith. “I am grateful for Sec. Kennedy and President Trump’s ongoing work to help those in need—and through the full implementation of the Protecting Vulnerable Newborn and Infant Children EO, we can continue to protect and defend the most vulnerable among us.”

In the bicameral letter, first reported by the Washington Examiner, the Republican lawmakers cite the heartbreaking case of McKenna West—a surrogate pressured to abort the baby she was carrying after a 20-week ultrasound diagnosed a serious, but treatable, heart condition—as evidence of “the need for quick federal action on this matter.”

Although Ms. West says that she faced pressure to abort from the baby’s biological parents, she refused and offered to raise the baby herself or find him a loving home. She relocated to Texas to be near a hospital equipped to provide the baby with lifesaving care after he was born. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton intervened in McKenna’s case, and a Texas judge issued an order directing that the baby receive life-sustaining care after birth and preventing his removal from the state of Texas.

“We are grateful that Texas law recognized and protected the rights and personhood of Ms. West’s surrogate baby and acted to save his life. Sadly, this protection is not uniform in all the states across our nation,” the Members of Congress write.

“Leadership from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is needed to ensure that all vulnerable infants receive equal protection under the law, instead of being at the mercy of health care systems that may unjustly declare them unworthy of life.”

The lawmakers then urge Secretary Kennedy to elevate the directives embedded within President Trump’s EO on Protecting Vulnerable Newborn and Infant Children—issued on September 25, 2020, and never formally rescinded by the Biden Administration—which clarifies that all individuals, including vulnerable infants, are protected under federal law, such as the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) (42 U.S.C. 1395dd), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 794), and The Born-Alive Infants Protection Act (1 U.S.C. 8).

The co-signatories note that the directives for the HHS Secretary in the EO “offer important opportunities to ensure vulnerable newborns, including newborns with diagnosed disabilities, are receiving the care they deserve, no matter where in the United States they are born.”

They also urge Secretary Kennedy to consider reissuing a rule highlighting federal law protecting premature infants and adults with disabilities from discrimination. In January 2021, during President Trump’s first Administration, the HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) had issued a proposed rule, entitled “Special Responsibilities of Medicare Hospitals in Emergency Cases and Discrimination on the Basis of Disability in Critical Health and Human Service Programs or Activities.”

title: Smith leads intergovernmental survey of Nor’easter damage across NJ-04 shore towns
text:
Today, Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ) led a group of federal, state, and local officials and experts in surveying the extensive damage to Manasquan, Point Pleasant Beach, Bay Head, and Ocean Gate beaches following last week’s severe Nor’easter, which caused significant flooding and beach erosion.

During the tour, which spanned both Monmouth and Ocean counties, Smith was joined by Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Region 2 Administrator Chris Hartnett; New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) Deputy Commissioner Joe Seebode; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Philadelphia District Commander Lt. Baum; USACE NY District Project Manager Jason Shea; New Jersey State Police Operations Officer Major James Boland; Monmouth County Sherriff Shaun Golden; Ocean County Sherriff Mike Mastronardy; NJ LD-10 Assemblyman Paul Kanitra; Ocean County Commissioner Jennifer Bacchione; Manasquan Mayor Mike Mangan; Bay Head Mayor Bill Curtis; Ocean Gate Mayor Robert Curtin; and numerous elected and municipal officials representing Manasquan, Point Pleasant Beach, Bay Head, and Ocean Gate.

title: The Washington Examiner exclusive article on Smith-led letter'Republicans ask RFK Jr. to protect disabled infants after McKenna West surrogacy battle'
text:
By Gabrielle Etzel

Published October 2, 2026 5:00am ET

EXCLUSIVE — Congressional Republicans are ramping up pressure on the Trump administration to strengthen protections for infants born with disabilities following the heated custody battle between a California couple and their surrogate over a child born with a heart defect.

A total of 30 House members and nine senators from the anti-abortion wing of the GOP sent a letter, obtained by the Washington Examiner, to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on Thursday, requesting that the Trump administration create a federal standard for healthcare professionals to provide lifesaving care to infants born extremely premature or with life-limiting disabilities.

The letter, principally authored by Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ) and leadership in the House Pro-Life Caucus, highlights the case of Alaska resident McKenna West, who contracted to be a surrogate for Omar Ahmed and Nausheen Gilkar.

At her 20-week ultrasound, West was informed that the fetus had hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a congenital defect in which the left side of the heart is underdeveloped. After the diagnosis, West traveled to Texas to secure life-saving care for the child upon birth, despite a directive from the biological parents to abort.

West delivered the child in Texas on Aug. 12, but the courts eventually ruled in favor of Ahmed and Gilkar taking full custody of the child to continue his care in California.

The congressional delegation highlighted the difference in Texas law, which encouraged life-saving interventions, and California law, which would only encourage palliative care, as indicative of the need for a federal standard.

“Leadership from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is needed to ensure that all vulnerable infants receive equal protection under the law instead of being at the mercy of a health care system that may unjustly declare them unworthy of life,” the delegation wrote.

In addition to the 30 Republican House members who signed onto the letter, four senators are seeking re-election in November: Sens. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), Darline Graham Nordone (R-SC), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), and Pete Ricketts (R-NE).

Smith and his colleagues point to an executive order from President Donald Trump’s first term, in September 2020, as giving Kennedy the authority to “strengthen the protection available for vulnerable newborns and their parents.”

The Trump 1.0 executive order, which clarified that infants born with disabilities or in medical distress must be given stabilizing medical treatment under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act, or EMTALA, was not rescinded by former President Joe Biden.

The executive order, and corresponding HHS guidance drafted a few months later, came after HHS had investigated several cases in which hospital staff did not provide potentially life-saving care to severely premature infants despite the parents’ request for intervention.

Although modern medical interventions have allowed extremely premature infants to be born alive as young as 21 weeks of pregnancy, these exceedingly rare cases often result in the child requiring long-term neonatal intensive care. Severe premature birth increases the child’s risk of developing chronic conditions like lung disease, cognitive impairment, and vision or hearing loss.

The executive order’s corresponding proposed rule from the HHS Office of Civil Rights in January 2021, which was abandoned by the Biden administration, would have protected infants born premature or with significant disabilities and their parents from unlawful denials of emergency screening or stabilizing treatment.

The proposed rule would have also prohibited healthcare providers from making life and death medical decisions based on the perceived value or worth of the patient’s life with a disability and prohibited providers from steering patients towards end-of-life care on the basis of disability.

Revisiting the Trump 1.0 rule would not be the first time Kennedy and his team enforced an anti-abortion interpretation of EMTALA under the current administration.

EMTALA was at the heart of the Biden administration’s lawsuit against Idaho over the state’s strict prohibition on abortion, in which the Justice Department argued that terminating a pregnancy can constitute stabilizing care for the mother under the law. The Supreme Court ruled in 2024 to allow emergency physicians to carry out abortion procedures in Idaho despite the state’s ban.

In early 2025, Trump’s HHS Office of Civil Rights swiftly replaced Biden’s guidance on abortion protocols under EMTALA with a more anti-abortion interpretation of the statute.

Smith and his colleagues urged Kennedy to “evaluate and consider reissuing a rule” to standardize care for newborns with life-limiting conditions.

“We are eager to work with you to ensure our nation values human life, provides equal justice under the law, and respects the rights of individuals with disabilities,” the delegation wrote.

title: ICYMI: Ciscomani’s Chiricahua National Park Act One Signature Away From Law
text:
Tucson, AZ - Following the U.S. Senate’s unanimous passage of the bipartisan H.R. 6380Chiricahua National Park Act, local and statewide media highlighted Representative Juan Ciscomani’s years-long effort to designate Chiricahua National Monument as Arizona’s fourth national park.

The legislation, which Ciscomani first introduced as the second bill of his congressional career within his first 100 days in office, passed the House in March and cleared the Senate on September 30. The bill now heads to the President’s desk for signature.

"It’s been a long hike, but we’re at the summit. After years of work and persistence, Arizona is one signature away from having its fourth national park," said Representative Ciscomani. "Chiricahua has long deserved this designation. As the second bill I ever introduced and in my first 100 days in Congress, I am proud to have worked across the aisle and across both chambers to deliver this victory for our district. This is an Arizona priority and a true team effort. I’m grateful to our local partners, including the City of Willcox, public lands advocates, and everyone who has worked alongside us to make this happen. I’m incredibly proud that we are now one signature away from making Chiricahua Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District’s second national park during our nation’s 250th birthday.”

Local media across Arizona is applauding Ciscomani’s instrumental leadership in getting this bill across the finish line after a decades long fight.

AZPM highlighted Ciscomani’s continued work to advance the designation, noting that he introduced the legislation twice since taking office and emphasizing the bipartisan effort behind the bill. Ciscomani told AZPM that he expects the bill to be signed into law within the coming days and emphasized the economic opportunities the designation could bring to southeastern Arizona.

AZ Family reported that Chiricahua could soon become America’s 64th national park and highlighted Ciscomani’s role in advancing the legislation through Congress. The outlet also noted the potential for increased tourism, regional economic development, and greater visibility for rural communities in Cochise County.

Gila Valley Central highlighted the legislation’s passage through both chambers and its potential to attract additional visitors to northern Cochise County. The outlet reported Ciscomani’s efforts to work with local leaders, including Willcox Mayor Greg Hancock, on plans to capitalize on increased tourism once Chiricahua receives its national park designation.

The Gila Herald also highlighted Ciscomani’s legislation reaching its final legislative hurdle, noting that the bill would elevate the profile of the 12,000-acre Chiricahua landscape and support tourism and economic opportunities throughout southeastern Arizona. The coverage comes as Chiricahua stands just one presidential signature away from becoming Arizona’s fourth national park, joining the Grand Canyon, Petrified Forest, and Saguaro National Parks. If signed into law, Chiricahua would become the nation’s 64th national park and the second national park located in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

After more than a decade of advocacy and years of congressional work, the Chiricahua National Park Act is now one step away from becoming law and bringing a new national designation to southeastern Arizona.

title: Courtney Statement on New Contract Awards for TTM Technologies & Electric Boat
text:
NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee and a senior Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, highlighted recent contract awards for two defense manufacturers in Connecticut’s Second District.

This week, TTM Technologies in Stafford Springs was awarded 6% of a $511 million contract for their work on the Navy’s SPY-6 radar systems. In July, TTM Technologies also received 6% of a $1.809 billion contract for their work on SPY-6 radar systems. TTM Technologies employs roughly 1,000 people between its Stafford and Stafford Springs facilities, which produce electronic systems for the aerospace, space, and maritime defense industries.

Last month, Electric Boat was awarded three contracts totaling $239 million for continued work for the Virginia-class submarine program. Following July’s $76.6 billion contract awards to Electric Boat for construction of nine Block VI Virginia-class submarine and five Build II Columbia-class submarines, September’s contracts are smaller, incremental awards to support the entire Virginia-class submarine program.

Virginia-class submarines, Columbia-class submarines, and all U.S. Navy ships that the SPY-6 radar system operates on are authorized by the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee.

“These new contract awards are further proof that the growth of Connecticut’s defense manufacturing industry is not just a blip on the shoreline; it’s a wide-reaching enterprise driving our region’s long-term economic growth,” Courtney said. “On the heels of this summer’s record-breaking submarine contracts for Electric Boat, the work to support our region’s defense manufacturers isn’t finished. In particular, the Seapower Subcommittee and the Education and Workforce Committee must expand investments in the successful skills training pipelines that have grown Connecticut’s next-generation manufacturing workforce."

title: Rep. Craig Secures Nearly $2.3 Million in Federal Funding for Rosemount Fire Department to Hire Additional Firefighters

The Shakopee Fire Department will receive $81,818 and the Woodbury Fire Department will receive $55,680 through the Assistance to Firefighters (AFG) grant program.
