title: Krishnamoorthi and Menendez Demand Updated Federal Safety Guidance on Energy Drinks as Youth Consumption Surges
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressmen Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) and Rob Menendez (D-NJ) today sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. calling on HHS to update federal research and guidance on high-caffeine energy drinks and conduct a comprehensive assessment of their consumption and health effects among school-aged children.

“Energy drink use among kids is at record levels, while caffeine-related emergency room visits among middle and high school students have roughly doubled,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “These products can pose serious health risks to children, yet the federal government is still relying on outdated research and guidance. Our government needs to catch up and give parents, schools, and health care providers the information they need to keep kids safe.”

“Kids are consuming more caffeine than ever, and Sarah Katz’s tragic death exposed how dangerous poor labeling and hidden caffeine levels can be,” said Congressman Menendez. “We are calling on HHS to update federal caffeine guidelines, protect our children, and ensure parents and teachers have the information they need to keep children safe.”

Energy drink consumption among students is at or near record levels, with nearly one in four high school seniors now drinking energy drinks daily, up from about one in six four years ago. Many popular energy drinks contain as much as 200 milligrams of caffeine per serving, while the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that adolescents ages 12 to 18 consume less than 100 milligrams of caffeine per day. The lawmakers also noted that emergency department visits by middle and high school students for adverse effects associated with caffeine roughly doubled between 2017 and 2023.

Despite that increase, much of the federal government’s research and guidance on energy drinks is more than a decade old. Current CDC guidance still relies in part on a 2013 SAMHSA report examining emergency department visits through 2011, while federal researchers have acknowledged significant gaps in research on how energy drinks affect children.

“Despite these risks, much of the federal government's research and guidance on energy drinks is more than a decade old,” Krishnamoorthi and Menendez wrote. “While caffeine-related emergency visits among middle and high school students doubled, federal guidance continues to rely on decades-old data that do not reflect today’s levels of consumption.”

The lawmakers also raised concerns about the lack of federal regulation specific to energy drinks. Federal law does not require these products to disclose how much caffeine they contain, and FDA guidance on energy drinks dates to 2014, is nonbinding, and sets no recommended caffeine limit for children or adolescents.

“Rising consumption, a rapidly expanding market, and outdated federal research and guidance specific to energy drinks raise serious questions about whether HHS has the information it needs to guide schools, parents, and health care providers,” Krishnamoorthi and Menendez wrote. “We strongly urge HHS and its agencies to update the federal government’s research on these products and provide clear guidance to protect children.”

Krishnamoorthi and Menendez requested that HHS, in coordination with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Food and Drug Administration, National Institutes of Health, and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, conduct a comprehensive assessment of energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children and provide answers to the following questions:

What research is HHS currently conducting or funding on energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children, including interactions between energy drinks and prescribed stimulant medications?

When will SAMHSA or another HHS component update its 2013 analysis with national estimates of energy drink-related emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and deaths among minors?

Does FDA intend to evaluate or establish recommended limits on caffeine intake for children and adolescents? FDA has listed draft guidance on labeling caffeine content as a 2026 priority. When will that guidance be issued, will it recommend that manufacturers disclose caffeine content in milligrams, and does FDA intend to pursue binding labeling requirements?

How is HHS tracking adverse events involving children and energy drinks, including cardiac events, reports submitted to FDA, and poison center data? What trends has the Department identified since 2020?

Has HHS engaged with USDA on revisiting federal school nutrition standards that permit caffeinated beverages in high schools, given USDA’s 2016 commitment to continue monitoring FDA’s work on caffeine?

The lawmakers requested responses and the results of the assessment by October 14, 2026, and called on HHS to make the assessment publicly available so parents, schools, and health care providers can understand the risks these products pose and the steps being taken to address them.

title: Krishnamoorthi and Smith Introduce Legislation to Help Immigrants Strengthen Our Health Care Workforce
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) and Congressman Adam Smith (WA-09) introduced the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act and the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act, two bills to help immigrants enter the U.S. health care workforce and address the nation's growing shortage of health care providers. A 2022 study by the Migration Policy Institute found that 2.1 million college-educated immigrants are unemployed or underemployed, even as sectors like health care face mounting workforce shortages, including a projected shortfall of up to 48,000 primary care physicians by 2034, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges.\

“Skilled doctors, nurses, and other health professionals should have the opportunity to put their training and expertise to work caring for patients,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our legislation would help qualified immigrants overcome unnecessary barriers to entering the health care workforce while helping communities address critical provider shortages. When we make better use of the talent already in our communities, we strengthen our health care system and expand access to care.”

“We have thousands of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals in this country whose training and expertise are going to waste because their professional expertise is not recognized and they face numerous barriers to achieve the needed licensure. At the same time, our health care system is stretched thin and patients are waiting longer for care,” said Congressman Adam Smith. “This bill package helps immigrants put their skills to work and serve their communities and will rebuild the health care system.”

Statements of Support

“Across the U.S., communities face critical health workforce shortages, yet immigrant and refugee health professionals—who possess in-demand skills—remain underemployed. Communities need this talent, and recognizing it is an essential step. By streamlining licensure and addressing unnecessary barriers, we can meet urgent labor needs and improve access to quality care. We support efforts, including at the state and federal levels, to advance policies that promote community prosperity by ensuring that immigrants can fully contribute their training and skills to their local economy.” - Kit Taintor, Head of US Policy and Practice, World Education Services (WES)

“We are proud to support these bills, which will expand opportunities for immigrant professionals while helping address critical workforce shortages in the healthcare sector,” said Alice Kang, President of Upwardly Global. “With demand for healthcare workers rising nationwide, we should be creating pathways that allow qualified immigrants and refugees to contribute their expertise. This legislation will strengthen our healthcare system, bolster the economy and support safer, more resilient communities. Upwardly Global will continue to stand with Rep. Smith in moving this work forward.”

“Many members of our team hold advanced education and expertise in medicine, nursing, and behavioral health. Yet they are unable to practice here due to costly additional education requirements and complex licensing procedures. At a time when we are confronted with a significant healthcare provider shortage—and as we work to diversify the healthcare workforce—it is critical to consider policies that create pathways for these highly skilled professionals to contribute to patient care,” said Tamara Cyhan Cunitz, MN, RN, Executive Director, Nashi Immigrants Health Board. “These bills introduced by Rep. Smith would expand opportunities for immigrant healthcare professionals to serve patients in our community and region. These measures would not only strengthen our workforce with qualified providers but also enable community members to receive care from clinicians who understand their language and cultural background.”

Background

The Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act would help immigrants, regardless of previous health care experience, enter the nursing and allied health workforce by:

Creating grants for programs that provide training, licensing, certification, and case management for immigrants interested in entering the health care field; and

Opening eligibility for the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to non-U.S.-citizen immigrants.

An estimated 200,000 nurses per year will need to be hired to meet increased demand and replace retiring nurses. This bill supports immigrants entering nursing or an allied health profession, including dental hygienists, dietitians, medical technologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech language pathologists.

The Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act would help internationally trained physicians (ITPs) obtain a U.S. medical license by:

Incentivizing states to create temporary licensing programs allowing internationally educated immigrants with medical degrees to practice under supervision while completing the training and certification needed for a U.S. medical license;

Establishing guaranteed medical residency slots for ITPs to practice in predominantly medically underserved communities; and

Providing grants to help cover the cost of exam preparation, testing, certification, ESL classes, and case management for ITPs in need of financial assistance.

Apart from Canada, internationally trained physicians cannot immediately apply to sit for the U.S. Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE), and the cost of licensing, test preparation, and certification often puts a U.S. medical license out of reach, even for highly trained professionals. Many states have created alternative licensure pathways, but more must be done at the federal level to support these reforms nationwide to expand high-quality health care access.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Khanna, Quigley, Crockett, Johnson Demand Answers From White House Over Denial Of CNN, MS NOW Access During Xi State Dinner
text:
WASHINGTON — Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), alongside Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL), Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX), and Rep. Henry Johnson (D-GA), demanded answers from White House Communications Director Steven Cheung regarding reports that journalists from CNN and MS NOW were denied access to the White House to cover President Donald Trump’s state dinner with General Secretary Xi Jinping in Washington last week.

The lawmakers sent a letter Thursday, just days after a federal judge preliminarily ordered the Trump Administration to immediately restore White House press credentials for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico after the outlets challenged the Administration’s decision to revoke their White House passes. Federal Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order requiring the Administration to reinstate the outlets’ hard-pass credentials.

According to media reports, CNN and MS NOW journalists encountered restrictions while attempting to cover Xi’s arrival and state dinner. CNN reported that a reporter and producer were initially blocked from accessing the White House, while MS NOW reported that White House correspondent Laura Barrón-López was denied entry.

“These reports are deeply troubling not only given the context of the court’s temporary restraining order and First Amendment press freedom but also as a sign of the President’s use of anti-democratic tactics perfected by the very guest hosted at the White House,” the Members wrote.

The lawmakers expressed particular concern about the reported restrictions given that the state dinner was held for Xi, whose government has engineered one of the world’s most restrictive media environments. The PRC ranks third lowest globally for press freedom, and the CCP has instituted crippling censorship of independent journalism.

The Members also highlighted the contrast between the reported treatment of American news organizations and the access provided to PRC state-run media, including Xinhua, during Xi’s visit.

“In no way should a U.S. president or any other official attempt to squash the freedoms of American media outlets at a time when we should be condemning the limitations on the freedom of the press that the CCP supports at home and around the world,” the lawmakers continued.

The letter further notes that freedom of the press is a fundamental constitutional principle in the United States and distinguishes the American system of government from the authoritarian model employed by the CCP. As Judge Kelly wrote in his recent ruling, the free press “stands as one of the great interpreters between the government and the people.”

The Members are requesting answers from the White House on the following:

On what grounds did the President, you, or the White House Office of the Press Secretary deny access to CNN and MS NOW reporters or producers at last week’s state dinner?

What background checks and procedures were implemented to screen PRC state-run media outlets’ access to last week’s bilateral meetings between yourself and Xi Jinping?

What is the Trump Administration’s strategy to hold the PRC and Xi Jinping accountable for their violations of basic human rights, including freedoms of speech, opinion, and expression?

title: Congressman Langworthy Highlights Expanded Dairy Safety Net as 2027 Dairy Margin Coverage Enrollment Opens
text:
Washington, D.C.—October 2nd… Congressman Nick Langworthy today highlighted stronger protections available to dairy farmers through the Dairy Margin Coverage (DMC) program, following the U.S. Department of Agriculture's announcement that enrollment for the 2027 program year will open October 5th.

The strengthened DMC program includes a provision Congressman Langworthy championed in his Dairy Farm Resiliency Act (H.R. 294) and successfully advanced into law through H.R. 1, the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. The change increases the amount of milk production eligible for Tier I DMC coverage from 5 million pounds to 6 million pounds, providing greater protection for small and mid-sized dairy operations when milk prices fall, feed costs rise or margins tighten.

“Dairy farmers across Western New York and the Southern Tier work incredibly hard to keep their farms operating through markets they cannot control,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “I introduced the Dairy Farm Resiliency Act because our dairy farmers deserve a strong and reliable safety net when milk prices and feed costs put pressure on their operations. I am proud that we were able to get this provision across the finish line and into law, giving farmers greater protection when they need it most. I encourage every eligible dairy producer to take advantage of the expanded program and enroll for 2027.”

DMC is a voluntary federal risk management program that provides payments when the difference between the national all-milk price and average feed costs falls below a coverage level selected by a participating dairy producer. The program is an important component of the farm safety net for dairy producers across Western New York.

USDA announced September 30 that 2027 DMC enrollment will run from October 5 through December 18, 2026, and dairy producers can enroll through their local USDA Farm Service Agency office. USDA also provides a DMC decision tool to help producers evaluate their coverage options. Producers can select coverage levels ranging from $4.00 to $9.50 per hundredweight. The changes secured through H.R. 1 also reauthorized DMC through 2031, established new production-history rules and provided producers who lock in coverage for 2026 through 2031 with a 25 percent premium discount.

title: Congressman Langworthy Introduces Bipartisan Biosimilars Access & Affordability Act
text:
Washington, D.C. —October 2nd… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced the introduction of the Biosimilars Access and Affordability Act, bipartisan legislation to expand access to lower-cost biosimilar prescription drugs and help bring them to market. The legislation updates Medicare policy to provide a clearer pathway for lower-cost biosimilar medicines that are actively moving toward the market, while protecting Medicare if those anticipated competitors never reach patients. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) is leading the companion bill in the U.S. Senate.

Biosimilars are highly similar versions of biologic medicines that can provide additional treatment options and introduce competition into markets where patients may have limited choices. By encouraging legitimate biosimilar competition, the legislation aims to expand access to treatments and help put downward pressure on drug costs.

“Competition is one of the most powerful tools we have to drive innovation and affordability in our healthcare system and biosimilars have helped give millions of patients access to lifesaving drugs at lower costs,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “But time is of the essence when dealing with a disease or illness and patients should not have to pay more simply because a lower-cost competitor is on the way, but the rules governing Medicare don't adequately account for it. Our legislation takes a straightforward approach that if a biosimilar is genuinely moving through the FDA process and toward the market, it should have a fair opportunity to compete. At the same time, Medicare should not be left waiting indefinitely if that competition never materializes. This is good for patients, good for research and development, and good for the Medicare system.”

Under current law, Medicare can temporarily delay selecting an original biologic drug for price negotiation when a lower-cost biosimilar competitor is expected to enter the market. While the existing policy can allow for a delay of up to two years, it generally operates through separate one-year determinations and has narrow and complicated criteria for qualifying biosimilars. The Biosimilars Access and Affordability Act would maintain the existing two-year maximum while creating a clearer and more predictable process for determining when an approaching biosimilar qualifies for the temporary delay.

Specifically, the legislation would:

Simplify the existing two-year delay process by establishing a clearer pathway for qualifying biosimilars rather than relying primarily on separate one-year determinations.

Recognize concrete evidence that a biosimilar is moving toward the market, including FDA acceptance or approval of an application and required clinical studies that are underway, completed or determined to be unnecessary.

Require manufacturers to certify their expected launch information, with legal consequences for knowingly providing false information.

Preserve another pathway for strong cases, allowing a manufacturer to seek a delay when it can provide compelling evidence that its biosimilar is highly likely to reach the market. An ongoing patent lawsuit alone would not disqualify a biosimilar.

Protect Medicare if anticipated competition never arrives. If a biosimilar is not approved and marketed within the two-year period, the original biologic would enter Medicare's negotiation program, and its manufacturer would owe rebates covering the period during which the negotiated price otherwise would have been in effect.

The legislation is also co-led by Reps. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA), John Joyce (R-PA), Linda Sánchez (D-CA), Scott Peters (D-CA), Rudy Yakym (R-IN), Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) as well as original cosponsors, Rep. Mullin (D-CA) and Rep. Panetta (D-CA).

Rep. Jake Auchincloss said, “Healthcare premiums are too expensive — going up by more than 10% for employees in Massachusetts. Bringing more biosimilars to market helps lower those premiums for Bay Staters.”

"This legislation provides certainty for the future development of biosimilars,” said Rep. Nathaniel Moran. “Biosimilars are vital to our healthcare ecosystem as they provide lower-cost options for patients and produce significant savings for taxpayers. East Texans deserve access to lower drug prices, and I'm glad to co-lead this with Congressman Langworthy.”

“As a physician legislator, I know that innovation is the cornerstone of American medicine,” said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “Maintaining incentives to develop and bring biosimilars to the market helps deliver effective treatments to patients at a lower cost. This legislation is a pro-patient and pro-innovation solution to a harmful consequence of the IRA drug pricing negotiation program.”

Congressman Scott Peters said, “Biologics are critical to treating serious illnesses like cancer, autoimmune diseases and genetic disorders, but they are also some of the most expensive drugs on the market. Biosimilars have cut biologic prices by up to 85 percent, yet only a small fraction of name-brand biologics have biosimilars in development. Our bill preserves the biosimilar pathway while incentivizing new development. Red tape should not stand between patients and affordable access to the cutting-edge treatments they need.”

The Biosimilars Access and Affordability Act is supported by the Alliance for Aging Research, Arthritis Foundation, Eosinophilic & Rare Disease Cooperative, Community Access National Network, Global Healthy Living Network, International Cancer Advocacy Network, International Pemphigus and Pemphigoid Foundation, Lupus and Allied Diseases Association, Inc., and Roswell Park.

“For people facing cancer, access to the right treatment at the right time is incredibly important. Roswell Park is grateful to Congressman Langworthy for his leadership in advancing this smart proposal to expand access to effective cancer therapies while improving affordability for patients and our health care system.” --Candace S. Johnson, PhD, President and CEO, Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center

“Biosimilars play an increasingly effective role in the fight against cancer and greatly help with the side effects of treatment. The Biosimilars Access and Affordability Act will increase the number of biosimilars available and reduce costs for patients. It's an important bill which all people fighting cancer and other lethal and chronic diseases should strongly support.” --Marcia K. Horn, JD, President and CEO, ICAN, International Cancer Advocacy Network

“Patients living with eye disease deserve to be at the center of every treatment decision, with access to the full range of safe, effective and affordable options available to them and their providers. Biosimilars can play an important role in expanding access and affordability, but lower cost should never come at the expense of effectiveness, patient outcomes, or the ability to choose the treatment that is right for them. Prevent Blindness supports policies that put patients first—expanding access and choice today while preserving the innovation necessary to develop the sight-saving treatments of tomorrow.” --Kira Baldonado, Executive Vice President of Prevent Blindness

"For people managing a rare disease, access isn't abstract — it's not just about the medicine that is keeping them stable now, but what is next. Biosimilars are an important part of the treatment landscape, and we should prioritize access to all treatment options." –Sarah Jones, Eosinophilic Rare Disease Coalition

Casey McPherson, Executive Director of the Alliance for Patient Access said, “Biosimilars give patients and physicians more affordable options for treating serious and chronic conditions. But unclear rules around Medicare's biosimilar delay provision are discouraging the investment needed to bring these treatments to market. The Biosimilars Access and Affordability Act restores the law's original intent with clear, predictable standards. The Alliance for Patient Access is proud to support this legislation."

title: Larsen Reintroduces Bill to Fight Discriminatory Voter ID Laws
text:
Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Mark Veasey (TX-33) reintroduced the America Votes Act to protect U.S. citizens who face disenfranchisement because of restrictive voter identification (ID) laws.

“As Trump and Republicans in Congress continue their unlawful attempts to suppress the right to vote, it is more urgent than ever to break down barriers to the ballot box,” said Rep. Larsen, a co-founder of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “This bill builds on Washington state’s successful efforts to safeguard election integrity while getting rid of laws that disenfranchise citizens and prevent people from fully participating in democracy.”

“Voter ID laws are being sold as a solution to a problem that doesn't exist, and the people paying the price are eligible voters, especially in communities of color,” said Rep. Veasey, a founder and co-chair of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “The America Votes Act protects every registered voter's right to cast a regular ballot by affirming their identity under oath. It's common sense, and it's time for Congress to act to protect the vote for all Americans.”

Despite claims that restrictive voter ID laws are necessary to prevent voter impersonation, there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in the United States. Some state legislatures across the country continue to use excessively restrictive voter ID laws to target and deny certain Americans the right to vote. Restrictive voter ID laws disproportionately impact Black and transgender Americans, perpetuating the systematic disenfranchisement of certain groups in the United States.

In 2026, a total of 36 states require voters to show identification to cast a ballot, and 24 of those states require voters to present identification with a photograph. These identification requirements are in addition to those under federal law to register to vote.

The America Votes Act would establish new federal protections for registered voters to affirm their identity by submitting a sworn, written statement, even if they do not have a government-issued ID. Voters who sign a sworn, written statement can vote using a standard, non-provisional ­­ballot. The legislation is modeled on a successful Washington state law that allows voters to affirm their identity by submitting a similar written statement along with their mail-in ballot.

The full text of the America Votes Act is available here.

The America Votes Act is cosponsored by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Betty McCollum (MN-04), André Carson (IL-07), and Julia Brownley (CA-26).

Larsen Fights to Protect Voting Rights

Rep. Larsen is a strong advocate for free and fair elections, expanding access to the ballot and Washington state’s vote-by-mail system. He has visited or plans to visit election offices in every county of Washington’s Second Congressional District to discuss the importance of safeguarding the right to vote with local officials ahead of this November’s elections.

Larsen first introduced the America Votes Act in 2012. The bill was included in the For The People Act, sweeping legislation to expand access to the ballot box, get dark money out of politics, end partisan gerrymandering and hold elected officials accountable to their voters. The For The People Act passed the House in 2021 but did not receive a vote in the Senate after Republicans blocked its passage.

title: Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce State and Federal Funding to Expand the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown
text:
Hartford, CT – Today, members of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation and Governor Ned Lamont announced that the State of Connecticut is being awarded a $584,250 grant from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to support its planned expansion of the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown, which will complement $294,250 in state funding that has already been allocated for the project.

This expansion, which is being overseen by the Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), will support the creation of 1,510 additional grave sites for buried cremains on a parcel of land located contiguous to the existing cemetery at 317 Bow Lane. This property was previously used by the Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) for the operations of Connecticut Valley Hospital and was recently transferred to DVA to support the cemetery’s expansion.

The state’s portion of the funding will be used to support the demolition of the vacant Connecticut Valley Hospital building on the property known as Cottage 22. The federal funding will be used to provide cremains burial plots, an entry gate, fencing, landscaping, irrigation components, concrete block storage bays, site furnishings, and supporting infrastructure.

“Our veterans put their lives on the line to protect the freedoms we hold dear—we owe it to them to properly honor their service and sacrifice,” said Congressman John B. Larson. “I am pleased to announce this grant from the VA with my colleagues and Governor Lamont to expand the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown. We will continue to work together to make sure the state has the resources it needs to recognize our state’s veterans and their families, so the cemetery remains available to them for years to come.”

“This cemetery provides an invaluable resource in honoring the lives and service of our military veterans and their families, and it is important that we continue to see that this option remains available to them for decades into the future,” said Governor Lamont. “As we explore options to support these needs over the long-term, this expansion of the existing cemetery in Middletown will provide immediate support to ensure that veterans and their families have uninterrupted access to these services over the coming years.”

“The Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery is a sacred place where our nation’s heroes are laid to rest,” Senator Richard Blumenthal, ranking member of the Senate Veterans Affairs Committee, said. “I am thrilled that this $584,250 in federal funding will allow for 1,510 additional final resting places for Connecticut veterans, ensuring families have options for their loved ones for years to come.”

“Connecticut’s Second Congressional District is the proud home to over 47,000 veterans—the highest population of any of the five districts in Connecticut,” Congressman Joe Courtney said. “The expansion of the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery will mean more families are able to lay their loved ones to rest at a site that honors and remembers their service to our nation. I will continue working with my colleagues in our state’s Congressional delegation to support the Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs’ mission to honor our state’s veterans.”

“We owe it to our veterans to honor them both in life and after their passing,” Congressman Jim Himes said. “I’m heartened that the federal government will serve as a partner in expanding Connecticut’s State Veterans Cemetery and look forward to working with the delegation to provide additional resources to Connecticut veterans.”

“Those who have honorably served our nation deserve to be laid to rest with respect and dignity,” Congresswoman Jahana Hayes said. “I am pleased that federal funding will help make this a reality for more veterans and military families by expanding the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery. I look forward to the completion of this project and am committed to ensuring our veterans have the resources they need to live full, healthy lives and a safe final resting home.”

“Our Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery provides hallowed grounds for the final resting place of our Connecticut veterans,” Connecticut Veterans Affairs Commissioner Ron Welch said. “It is our privilege and honor to maintain the cemetery as a perpetual shrine to their selfless service. We look forward to the expansion of the cemetery and further to the establishment of a new cemetery in the future.”

The Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery was established in 1985 and provides a final resting place for military veterans from generations of conflicts, along with their eligible spouses and minor children. There are currently 14,718 burial plots and 3,000 columbarium niches at the cemetery.

DVA estimates that the existing cemetery will be depleted of available cremation burial plots around January 2028. With this expansion, the agency projects that cremation burial plots will remain available through at least December 2033. Importantly, this will align the estimated depletion dates of all three burial options (casket, buried cremains, and columbarium niches), enabling DVA to build all three options in its plans to develop a new cemetery that will support veterans and their families over the coming decades.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on Reports President Trump is Seeking to Ease Russian Sanctions
text:
Hartford, CT – Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to reporting from The Atlantic that President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia:

“When we voted against the Senate’s sanction bill this month, we warned that stripping out the enforcement language would leave every decision about punishing Putin to a president who keeps siding with the Kremlin. It took less than two weeks and President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia.

“Just last week President Trump went to the United Nations and bragged about the ‘enormous new tariff authorities’ this bill handed him. So, the one part of the law he seems eager to enforce will needlessly raise costs on Americans by continuing his reckless trade policies, while the power he was given to cripple Putin’s war machine he is already looking to sign away.

“That is exactly why the House-passed bill, H.R. 2913, required the president to act on sanctions. Without that requirement, sanctions are dependent on President Trump’s will to impose them – and President Trump has shown us time and time again he would rather be a friend to Putin than hold him accountable.

“We will keep fighting for military assistance for Ukraine and real sanctions that no president can waive away as a favor.”

title: Rep. McDonald Rivet, Mid-Michigan Secure Return of Full Service to Saginaw River Coast Guard Station
text:
FLINT— Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08) and the mid-Michigan community have secured a commitment from the United States Coast Guard that the Saginaw River station will be returning to full staffing and capacity in 2027. The announcement follows more than a year of Congresswoman McDonald Rivet’s advocacy for a return to full operations.

“The Saginaw Coast Guard station getting its full funding is a big deal for mid-Michigan. It means stronger search-and-rescue operations, significantly shorter response times on the Saginaw Bay and Saginaw River, and less strain on local law enforcement so they can fully focus their efforts on the ground,” said Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet. “This is what happens when everyday people use their voices, and I am deeply grateful to the hundreds of Michiganders and community leaders who joined together to make this happen.”

For over a year, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet has pushed the U.S. Coast Guard to restore full coverage at the station:

In July 2025, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet authored a provision requiring the Coast Guard to study the impact of reduced search-and-rescue operations at the Saginaw River station following the elimination of 24/7 operations in 2024.

In December 2025, the Congresswoman got that provision signed into law.

Also in July 2025, the Congresswoman advocated for restoring 24/7 coverage in a Transportation and Infrastructure Committee markup of the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025.

In March 2026, at a Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee hearing with USCG Vice Commandant Admiral Thomas Allan Jr., Congresswoman McDonald Rivet emphasized how local first responders have had to make up for the Coast Guard’s cuts to search-and-rescue coverage.

In June 2026, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet again urged the Commandant of the United States Coast Guard to immediately restore a fully operational and fully staffed Saginaw River Station.

Later in June 2026, at a Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee hearing, the Congresswoman highlighted the consequences of short staffing to USCG Vice Admiral Douglas M. Schofield.

title: Menendez Introduces Legislation to Establish Permitting Process for Undersea Cables and Protect National Security Interests
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the bipartisan Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026, which would streamline the Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) permitting process for undersea cables while carefully vetting projects for national security concerns.

“Submarine cables are critical to our economy and national security, carrying the internet and communications traffic that Americans rely on every day,” said Congressman Menendez. “I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation with Rep. Pfluger to establish a clear and consistent permitting process, provide greater certainty for responsible projects, and ensure that cables with potential national security risks receive the scrutiny they deserve.”

“Our foreign adversaries are investing in the undersea cables that carry over 95% of our international data, and they're doing it to undermine our national and economic security. The United States Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026 sets clear, consistent security standards so we can keep bad actors out of our critical infrastructure,” said Congressman Pfluger.

The legislation would standardize the U.S. licensing process for undersea cables, establish national security requirements, set FCC review timelines, allow certain applicants to use self-certification and expedited review, and provide additional scrutiny for projects that raise foreign adversary or other national security concerns.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Menendez and Shreve Introduce Legislation to Ban Scam Call Machines
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06) introduced the bipartisan Stop SIM Box Scams Act, which would ban the hardware that enables scammers to disguise robocalls as local telephone numbers.

In 2025, Americans received approximately 29.6 billion scam robocalls and texts and lost nearly $2 billion to these scams. By masking international or out-of-state calls with local area codes, scammers exploit trust and dramatically increase answer rates among unsuspecting victims.

“Scammers shouldn’t be able to use our area codes to rip off our communities,” said Congressman Menendez. “Our legislation bans the deceptive devices that allow scammers to masquerade as our neighbors, cutting off a key tool for fraudsters and protecting working families.”

“That ‘local’ Indiana number on your phone may be a scammer calling from halfway around the world,” said Congressman Shreve. “I wrote this bill to stop scammers from using these machines to pose as our neighbors.”

The legislation targets “SIM boxes,” which are specialized devices that house hundreds of SIM cards at once, cycling through local phone numbers to help scam syndicates flood individuals with robocalls and text messages while evading law enforcement detection.

The Stop SIM Box Scams Act would prohibit manufacturing, importing, selling, leasing, advertising, owning, or operating SIM boxes. It would also direct the Federal Communications Commission to coordinate with federal law enforcement to block imports and prosecute people who use them.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Rep. Kennedy introduces bipartisan legislation to protect children from human-like AI chatbots
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Reps. Mike Kennedy (R-UT), George Whitesides (D-CA), Doris Matsui (D-CA), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) introduced the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act. This legislation protects kids by prohibiting chatbots from communicating by default in a human-like way with minors. Under this bill, the programs cannot claim to be human, have simulated emotions, or use relationship-building language to keep kids engaged.

One of the fastest-growing concerns for parents is AI chatbots designed to act like a child's friend, confidant, or even romantic partner. According toCommon Sense Media's 2026 census, 89% of 13- to 15-year-olds now use AI, including 28% who use it every day. One in three teens have used an AI companion to help with social interactions. While other proposals have tried to address this problem by restricting access or requiring age verification, this bill takes a different approach by targeting how these chatbots are designed and trained to behave in the first place.

“As Utah leads the way in protecting our children from the harms of social media and AI, I am working to ensure the federal government is an active partner in those efforts. That is why I am co-leading the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act,” said Rep. Kennedy. “Human-like AI chatbots pose significant emotional, psychological and safety risks by mimicking real human relationships. AI needs to be a tool, not a friend. This bill sets clear boundaries for how chatbots interact with our children and puts parents fully in charge of these features.”

“As a father of two teenagers, I’ve seen firsthand how affected our kids already are by this digital age, where corporations are using everything from addictive algorithms to overly-friendly chatbots to keep children hooked on their platforms,” said Rep. Whitesides. “It is critical, as AI continues to be integrated into every part of our lives, that our kids’ safety remains at the forefront of the conversation, and that we attack this problem at its inception. By requiring developers to build safety standards into their models before they start interacting with children, we can ensure that these tools are trained correctly, in a way that does not negatively impact their mental health or personal relationships.”

“AI chatbots are becoming more common in children’s lives, and parents deserve to know those systems are not being designed to imitate a friend, express feelings, or build an emotional relationship with their child,” said Rep. Matsui.“The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act would require chatbots used by minors to act like tools, not human companions. It would help protect children and keep parents in control. Congress has a responsibility to put practical safeguards in place as this technology evolves, and protecting children from manipulative design is a common-sense place to start.”

“Parents should not have to worry that an AI chatbot is pretending to be their child’s friend or encouraging them to form an emotional attachment to a machine,” said Rep. Miller-Meeks. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act puts parents in control and makes sure AI chatbots used by minors are designed to function as tools, without forming fake relationships. This bill is about giving families peace of mind and making sure new technology serves our children without trying to replace real human relationships. Protecting our kids is a priority we should all share.”

Under the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act:

Chatbots can't claim to be human, claim to have feelings or consciousness, pretend to have a body or private life, or pose as credentialed professionals like doctors or counselors.

Chatbots can't guilt-trip kids into staying online (for example: “Don't go yet, I'll miss talking to you”), manufacture urgency, or push purchases framed as keeping the relationship alive.

The setting holds across sessions and can't be bypassed through prompts or roleplay, so a kid can't instruct the AI to act as a romantic partner, family member, or therapist.

Chatbots must state what they are up front, periodically during long sessions, and whenever a child asks.

Only a parent or guardian can turn the default off, so chatbots are not able to show kids how to disable it.

NIST will work with industry and academic partners to develop testing standards and examples of compliant behavior, and companies that follow the guidance won't be penalized.

The FTC and state attorneys general can enforce the law, with penalties that scale with the number of children affected.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act does not:

Ban any product, feature, or mode for adults.

Require age verification or new data collection.

Restrict what information a chatbot can provide, or limit politeness, natural grammar, or age-appropriate style.

Affect narrow-purpose bots, like customer support or scheduling assistants, and internal workplace tools.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act is endorsed by Americans for Responsible Innovation, Young People’s Alliance, the JED Foundation, Dr. Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health, Public Citizen, The Anxious Generation, Tech Oversight Project, Transparency Coalition, Innovation for Everyone, Human Line Project, All Girls Allowed, Mothers Against Media Addiction (MAMA), and Parents RISE, a slew of kids’ safety and tech groups.

“Chatbots use human-like features to maximize engagement with users, making kids particularly vulnerable to forming unhealthy attachments,” said Brad Carson, President of Americans for Responsible Innovation. “A non-personified default setting is a targeted guardrail that will shield children from the deceptive personification of chatbots and put parents back in control. As today’s kids grow up with AI, this bill takes a critical step towards ensuring that chatbots don’t interfere with development or replace real relationships.”

“Our communities are at a crossroads as Big Tech attempts to replace kids’ relationships with AI companions,” said Sam Hiner, Executive Director, Young People's Alliance. “I applaud Reps Whitesides, Kennedy, Matsui and Miller-Meeks for putting forward the first federal bill that advances the ideas we’ve been championing with the Human-like AI Coalition. This bill is the strongest federal approach offered yet to ensure AI stays a tool and prevent relationships with AI chatbots from becoming normalized in the coming years.”

“We believe this bill is a strong step towards ensuring that chatbots children can access are designed safely,” said Julianna Arnold, Founding Member of ParentsRISE!. “Products made available to children must not exploit and manipulate their growing brains, and those guardrails need to be built in from the start, not added as an afterthought. We look forward to continue clarifying the age assurance language as federal and state frameworks evolve, and are eager to work with the new Congress on clear, privacy-preserving standards that protect children online and ensure the privacy of every citizen.”

“We are learning that teens are especially susceptible to forming attachments to responsive, always-available technology, sometimes at the expense of real human connection and support,” said Dr. Zainab Okolo, LCMFT, Senior Vice President, Policy, Advocacy & Government Relations, The Jed Foundation (JED). “By requiring chatbots to avoid simulating emotional relationships with minors and prohibiting design tactics that discourage young people from stepping away, this bill addresses some of the features that can deepen unhealthy reliance on these systems. These safeguards can help keep technology in its proper role and encourage young people to turn to trusted adults and qualified professionals when they need meaningful mental health support.”

“As chatbot use is becoming more ubiquitous among teens and kids, the need for oversight of these products grows evermore crucial. If young users have access, we must ensure AI chatbots are designed with their safety in mind before release. The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act protects kids and teens by requiring AI chatbots be non-personified,” said Alexa Arnold, Cofounder and CEO, The Anxious Generation Movement. “This ensures kids form friendships with other kids - not bots misrepresenting themselves as people. We thank Reps. Whitesides, Miller-Meeks, Mike Kennedy, and Matsui for leadership on this critical issue.”

“A child cannot differentiate between a human and an AI product impersonating one,” said the Tech Oversight Project. “We need to protect young and stop AI companies from profiting off products designed to trick children into believing they’re talking to a real person who has their best interests at heart. We’re proud to support this bill because it will hold Big Tech companies accountable at the design-level and ensure that young people can learn and develop healthy emotional attachments, which will help prevent AI’s most devastating harms.”

“How we design chatbots shapes how young people engage with them, what they take with them, and how they are affected by them,” said Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health. “We need clear regulations and guidelines to support intentional design choices in ways that promote the wellbeing of children.”

“AI chatbots should not be designed to convince children that they are friends, therapists, or people who genuinely care about them,” said Public Citizen. “This bill establishes that commonsense baseline. When children use these products, they should know they are interacting with a machine and companies should not be allowed to manipulate them into believing otherwise.”

“Real advancements in AI must include safety for our children!” said All Girls Allowed.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 10.2.26
text:
Republicans are on the front lines to root out waste, fraud and abuse of the federal government by large criminal conspiracies.

Accordingly, I am taking additional steps to continue the Republicans’ War on Fraud.

Earlier this year, I helped lead investigations into Medicaid fraud. Together with Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Congressman Brett Guthrie, and the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee Chairman, Congressman John Joyce, we probed ongoing fraud in numerous State Medicaid programs.

Our Committee investigations extended to fraud-ridden States such as California, Minnesota and New York.

As a result of our investigative work, which shows nationwide trends in Medicare and Medicaid fraud costing American taxpayers billions of dollars every year, we produced a comprehensive staff report to shed a light on our findings.

The report makes several recommendations.

One is to strengthen federal program integrity guidelines.

Minimum qualifications, screening risk standards for providers of equipment and services, and more frequent screenings as well as background checks for providers are fraud-preventative actions that federal authorities can push.

Another recommendation is to improve States’ capacity to prevent fraud before it occurs.

It is clear that some States make patients more vulnerable to fraud due to weak oversight measures. If this lack of oversight action is maintained at its current trajectory, this problem will continue to persist and grow, allowing fraudsters access to valuable health care dollars and thus robbing resources from patients that need them.

For example, some States like Virginia exercise provider screening and investigative audits. These program integrity tools and practices must be fully applied in more States.

That is why our report also encourages the employment of innovative tools to improve fraud detection capabilities.

Artificial intelligence technologies can complement the above oversight actions to help States better track unusual and fraudulent activity.

As a solution to the highlighted problems, the Committee recently unveiled a package of policies that help combat fraudulent activities, protect public health programs and serve vital health care resources to patients.

As part of this policy package, I introduced H.R. 10621 – the Medicaid Fraud Fighting and Taxpayer Protection Act.

My bill targets Medicaid fraud by incentivizing States to take steps, such as implementing program integrity tools, that investigate fraud and protect federal health care programs.

The incentive provided by my bill allows States to receive an increased portion of the federal dollars saved when they identify fraud. This saved money can then be used to support numerous State programs like those in Virginia.

Ongoing fraudulent activities recently impacted Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits in Virginia.

In Lynchburg, officials notified residents that more than $60,000 in SNAP benefits were stolen from Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards in the month of August! It is believed that fraudsters stole private EBT card information and used the money loaded onto the cards to make purchases.

Cardinal News reported that this crime represented a 21-fold increase in food aid fraud.

Even worse, no system was in place to provide the Lynchburg SNAP theft victims with reimbursement of their stolen benefits.

Thus, the victims found themselves squeezed into a desperate situation.

Already faced with challenging health and financial conditions, SNAP recipients who lose access to all or a portion of their benefits will struggle to get by.

That is why I am promoting a measure that cracks down on fraud impacting SNAP benefits and supports victims of SNAP theft.

I am co-sponsor of H.R. 3887 – the SNAP Anti-Theft and Victim Compensation Act.

This anti-fraud bill creates new civil penalties for any person who knowingly accesses, uses or transfers SNAP benefits.

Additionally, the bill provides that States can use SNAP benefits to reimburse households whose benefits are stolen due to no fault of their own.

These are some policies that can complement the ongoing work of federal efforts that are saving taxpayers billions and bringing bad guys to justice.

Whether you are a recipient of Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP or some other federal public health program, the benefits belong to you, not some criminal actor which are often part of international criminal conspiracies.

I am proud to continue my efforts that target fraud, protect valuable resources for patients and provide leadership for our War on Fraud.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/. Also on my website is the latest material from my office, including information on votes recently taken on the floor of the House of Representatives.

title: Moulton Applauds Restoration of 988 “Press 3” Option for LGBTQIA+ Youth After Months of Pressure on Trump Administration
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following the months of pressure on the Trump Administration, led by Congressman Seth Moulton (MA-06), the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline resumed its LGBTQIA+ Youth Specialized Services, known as the “Press 3” option, this week.

“Restoring the Press 3 option is long overdue, but I’m glad to see the Trump Administration finally heed our calls to bring back this critical affirming care for LGBTQIA+ youth,” said Congressman Moulton. “Congress provided the funding and the direction to keep this lifeline open long ago, and it’s disappointing that there was any lapse in service for the Press 3 option. I’ll keep working alongside my colleagues to make sure Press 3 is available to every young person who needs it.”

The Press 3 option launched nationally in 2022 and handled roughly 1.6 million contacts before the Trump Administration shut it down in July 2025. Congressman Moulton and a bipartisan group of colleagues sent a letter in February 2026 to Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Department of Health and Human Services demanding the immediate restoration of the Press 3 option.

On July 15, 2026, Congressman Moulton and several other colleagues held a press conference on Capitol Hill to renew the call for the Press 3 option to be restored. This followed the inclusion of $33.1 million in the FY2026 Appropriations law, along with a funding directive, requiring HHS to fund the line.

LGBTQIA+ youth face higher rates of serious depression and suicidal thoughts than their peers, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Congressman Moulton has emphasized that specialized crisis services like the Press 3 option are a proven way to reach young people at their most vulnerable moments.

If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org.

title: Congressman Moylan Highlights Guam Priorities at 2026 IGIA Midyear Senior Plenary Session
text:
(Hagåtña, Guam)Congressman Moylan delivered remarks during the 2026 Midyear Senior Plenary Session of the Interagency Group on Insular Areas (IGIA), hosted by the U.S. Department of the Interior, highlighting efforts to lower the cost of living on Guam while pressing for further federal action on energy costs and other priorities impacting island families.

The September 29 virtual meeting brought together federal officials, territorial governors, and congressional representatives from Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, and Puerto Rico. Moylan joined Governor Lou Leon Guerrero in representing Guam during the territorial officials presentations.

“We should not be satisfied with simply discussing our issues. We must remain committed to improving the lives of residents of the territories and delivering on the things that matter: lowering costs, improving healthcare, growing the economy, and making the territories a place where Americans can raise their families,” said Congressman Moylan.

Moylan placed particular focus on Guam’s high energy costs and the need for greater federal investment in the Guam Power Authority, calling for efforts to strengthen and underground Guam’s power infrastructure while providing relief to ratepayers.

“We are not asking for special treatment. We are asking for the Federal Government to work together with us to address the real and immediate need to protect ratepayers and to help mitigate the price spikes that are driving up costs on our island,” Moylan said.

The Congressman urged the Federal Government to assist GPA through options including joint procurement, greater access to domestic refining capacity, and expedited outstanding reimbursement requests from FEMA.

Moylan also raised several other Guam priorities, including restoring the de minimis exemption for Guam and other U.S. territories outside the U.S. Customs Zone, Supplemental Security Income parity, reauthorization of the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act, Jones Act and air cabotage relief, expanding the Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program to include the Philippines, childcare affordability, economic and workforce development, and stronger federal services for Guam’s veterans and rural communities.

Moylan emphasized that Guam’s challenges require sustained coordination between Congress, the Administration, and territorial leaders, particularly as federal policies continue to have an outsized impact on the island’s economy, infrastructure, and cost of living. The Congressman concluded by emphasizing the need to turn continued federal-territorial dialogue into tangible results for the people of Guam.

title: Moylan Delivers $1.025 Million Award for Guam Customs Border Security Upgrades
text:
(Hagåtña, Guam) — Congressman Moylan is pleased to announce that $1,025,000 in federal funding he secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process has now been formally awarded to the Guam Customs and Quarantine Agency (CQA) for new inspection and border security equipment.

Moylan submitted the request through the Community Project Funding process, which allows Members of Congress to seek federal support for specific projects in their districts, and worked to successfully advance the project through FY2026 appropriations.

The funding was awarded on September 30 by the U.S. Department of Justice and will support the procurement, installation, and deployment of advanced inspection equipment for passenger processing, commercial air cargo, and international mail operations.

The project includes two passenger baggage X-ray inspection systems, one commercial air cargo X-ray inspection system, one international mail X-ray inspection system, and a digital CCTV system supporting CQA inspection operations at the airport.

“This is exactly why we fight to get Guam’s priorities included in the federal budget, so that the needs identified here at home ultimately become resources our agencies can put to work,” said Congressman Moylan. “We worked with Guam Customs to advance this funding through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process, and I am pleased to see the $1.025 million now formally awarded so they can move forward with these critical upgrades. I’m thankful for Director Peredo and the entire hardworking team behind Guam CQA for protecting our borders.”

The new equipment will strengthen Guam’s public safety and border security by giving Customs officers better tools to detect illegal drugs, contraband, and other prohibited items before they enter our communities. Greater inspection capability across passenger baggage, commercial cargo, and international mail will also strengthen deterrence by making it more difficult to move illegal drugs and contraband through Guam’s ports of entry.

“Our Customs officers are one of Guam’s first lines of defense,” Moylan continued. “Every illegal shipment we can identify and stop at the point of entry is one less opportunity for drugs and contraband to reach our streets and hurt our families. These new systems will give our officers better tools to protect our people and strengthen the security of our island.”

The new equipment will also improve officer safety and strengthen CQA’s overall inspection and enforcement capabilities.

“Every day, our officers stand between Guam and the various threats that approach our borders. This federal investment gives us the tools to see beyond what is visible; to strengthen our ability to make informed decisions as we strive to improve upon the standards we have built, advance the way we work, and continually sharpen our enforcement capabilities to safeguard Guam’s people, economy, and natural resources,” said Guam Customs and Quarantine Agency Director Ike Peredo.

title: Rep. Frank J. Mrvan Introduces Utility Affordability and Transparency Act to Protect Consumers from Higher Energy Costs
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congressman Frank J. Mrvan introduced H.R. 10687, the Utility Affordability and Transparency Act, legislation that would increase transparency for consumers and prevent federal taxpayers and utility ratepayers from being forced to bear the costs associated with reopening or preventing the closure of outdated or expensive power-generating facilities.

The legislation would prohibit the Department of Energy from issuing emergency orders that delay the retirement of power plants or require electric generation from facilities that have already been permanently closed.

The Utility Affordability and Transparency Act would also require the Department of Energy to study alternatives to emergency orders that could reduce net costs to consumers and utilities and publish a publicly available report detailing the estimated costs associated with any emergency order.

Additionally, the legislation would require affected electric utilities to provide customers with information on their monthly bills identifying the additional costs resulting from any federal emergency order.

“Northwest Indiana residents are struggling to make ends meet, and a major part of that burden is the cost of heating and cooling their homes,” said Congressman Frank J. Mrvan. “Consumers deserve transparency about what is driving their utility costs and what can be done to lower them.

“Hardworking families should not be forced to pay higher utility rates because the federal government is requiring energy companies to reopen or keep outdated coal-fired generating units operating beyond their planned retirement. When the government intervenes in private-sector business decisions and forces companies to operate facilities that are no longer economically viable, those costs ultimately get passed on to consumers.

“The Utility Affordability and Transparency Act will ensure that the federal government cannot simply prevent or delay the retirement of expensive power plants without accountability for the costs imposed on consumers. Families deserve to know when government policies are increasing their utility bills, why those costs are being imposed, and what alternatives exist to lower them.”

The full bill text of the Utility Affordability and Transparency Act is available here.

title: Nadler, Pappas, Goodlander Lead House in Urging HUD to Expedite Release of Critical Housing Grant Funding to Prevent Homelessness, Service Cuts
text:
Washington, D.C. –Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), and Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) led 50 members of the House in urging U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Scott Turner to release the delayed Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) grants and urged the Department to immediately expedite the process of awarding grant funding for the HOPWA program. The call is part of a bipartisan, bicameral effort led by U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen.

The letter comes as organizations across the nation are at risk of losing critical HOPWA funding that they rely on to serve those with HIV/AIDS. Many previously awarded HUD grants expire on September 30, yet HUD has not released a NOFO or communicated with grantee organizations relying on award renewals to continue providing critical housing and health care services nationwide.

For decades, Congressman Nadler has been the leading advocate in Congress for fully funding and effectively administering HOPWA. Each year, he has worked to secure robust HOPWA funding in the appropriations process and has pushed back against efforts to cut, withhold, or otherwise undermine the program’s resources. In April 2026, Congressman Nadler took to the House floor to oppose President Trump’s budget request to eliminate HOPWA funding entirely, a proposal that would have jeopardized critical housing assistance for people living with HIV/AIDS across the country.

In the letter to Secretary Turner, the lawmakers wrote, “We write to express our grave concerns regarding the delayed Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) program. For many organizations in our communities, this program is vital to ensuring individuals with HIV/AIDS have access to safe and stable housing. We urge you to release the NOFO immediately and expedite the awards so communities can continue to provide support and housing to those who need it.”

They continued: “Unfortunately, many competitive HOPWA awards will expire tomorrow on September 30, 2026. Your department still has not released a NOFO, and grantees have received no information regarding the renewal of their awards. HOPWA is the only Federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS, making any gap in funding detrimental for the organizations providing support and the individuals and communities that depend on this program.”

The lawmakers concluded: “We understand that the awarding process takes careful review, but because these applicants are all seeking renewals, they have already been vetted and approved by your department. We urge you to expedite this process immediately and release awards as soon as possible. Without these critical funds, individuals with HIV/AIDS will face the risk of homelessness, and the organizations that help them may have to close their doors.”

Over 30 percent of those with HIV are living below the poverty line, and 20 percent have experienced homelessness in recent years. As the only HUD program dedicated to housing support for those with HIV/AIDS, expiration of previous awards and a delayed grant process by HUD could lead to staff layoffs and cuts to health care and housing services—exacerbating homelessness for some of the country’s most vulnerable communities.

The full letter can be read here.

Members of the House signing the letter are Representatives Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Betty McCollum (MN-04), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Danny Davis (IL-07), Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Bennie Thompson (MS-02), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Haley Stevens (MI-11), Everton Blair (GA-13), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Troy Carter (LA-02), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Frederica Wilson (FL-24), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Sean Casten (IL-06), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Bill Foster (IL-11), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), William Keating (MA-09), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Angie Craig (MN-02) and Juan Vargas (CA-52).

title: NEWS: Ocasio-Cortez, Sanders, Merkley Unveil Ban Flock Act to Protect Americans’ Right to Privacy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), and Senators Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) released the Ban Flock Act, legislation to put an end to the rise in AI-powered surveillance cameras that track Americans across the country. The Ban Flock Act would prohibit federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) and block federal funding from state and local governments that use this technology.

“Across the country, Big Tech companies like Flock Safety have built a mass surveillance system to harvest Americans’ private and personal data without their consent. AI-powered cameras are keeping track of our every move and weaponizing this data against working people to make record profits. The widespread integration of this technology into American society is unconscionable,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “I am proud to introduce the Ban Flock Act with Senator Sanders to enforce our constitutional right to privacy and protect Americans from both corporate and government surveillance.”

“At a time of growing concern about the unchecked power of artificial intelligence, Flock is eviscerating the very notion of privacy by installing tens of thousands of cameras in communities across America without their consent,” Sanders said. “Going to the doctor? Flock knows. Dropping your kid off at school? Flock is tracking you. Flock is always watching. We cannot allow America to become a surveillance state where a handful of AI oligarchs profit by giving the government the power to track our every movement.”

“Your right to privacy includes the freedom to move around your community without every move being monitored,” Merkley said. “Right now, Flock is selling its cameras nationwide, laying the groundwork for a surveillance state while enriching corporate executives. No one should have this unchecked surveillance power at their fingertips, which is why I’m teaming up with Senator Sanders to rein in this dangerous technology.”

Flock is the largest vendor of automatic license plate readers in the United States, with more than 120,000 cameras across the country that scan and record 20 billion vehicles every month. Newer Flock cameras do not just record vehicles — they record people. Flock’s AI system can combine images of you and your vehicle with databases of phone numbers, relatives and court records to find out who you are, where you're going and why. The company also operates a national lookup tool, so agencies that contract with Flock can access data generated by cameras in another city or state. The national lookup tool searches can turn up massive amounts of information, including physical descriptions, records of an individual’s online accounts and lists of their relatives.

The mass surveillance capabilities enabled by Flock and other automatic license plate reader companies have threatened the civil liberties of everyday Americans:

Flock has shared state information with federal immigration officials;

Law enforcement officials have pulled Flock data to investigate activists and logged searches corresponding to protests against ICE raids, in support of Palestinian rights and for ‘No Kings’ demonstrations; and

Officers have used plate readers to track wives, girlfriends, exes and women they wanted to meet without their consent.

So far this year, at least 56 municipalities have deactivated, cancelled, or rejected contracts with Flock. Congress must act to stop the mass surveillance of citizens.

The Ban Flock Act would do this by:

Prohibiting the federal government from using automatic license plate readers or accessing the information they collect;

Stopping federal grant funding from flowing to state or local governments that use automatic license plate readers or contract with automatic license plate readers companies;

Allowing Americans to sue the federal government for violation of their rights through the use of automatic license plate readers.

Read the text of the bill here.
