title: Booker, Crapo Recognize September as National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – To commemorate the end of Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Mike Crapo (R-ID) and led the introduction of a bipartisan Senate Resolution to recognize September as National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month. The resolution also encourages all Americans to take part in efforts to increase early detection, improve treatment and discover more breakthroughs for the disease, which has a 99 percent survival rate if caught in the earliest stage.

"Prostate cancer is one of the most treatable cancers when it's caught early, yet too many men aren't getting screened in time, and the toll falls especially hard on Black men, who are more likely to be diagnosed with and die from the disease," said Senator Booker. "Early detection saves lives. I urge every man to talk with his doctor about screening, and I'm grateful to Senator Crapo for partnering with me on this resolution to raise awareness and advance the research that will lead to better outcomes."

“Routine health screenings contribute to early prostate cancer detection,” said Senator Crapo. “Treatment is most effective when caught early. I encourage all men to discuss screening options with their health care provider and educate themselves further about early detection.”

"Prostate Cancer Awareness Month serves as a vital call to action, urging men to know their risk, seek early detection, and explore the treatment options that can save their lives," said Courtney Bugler, President and CEO of ZERO ProstateCancer. "We are incredibly grateful to Senator Crapo and Senator Booker for their unwavering dedication to this cause. Their leadership continues to drive meaningful progress in awareness, research, and support for the men and families navigating this disease. As we mark another Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, we are proud to stand with them and our champions in Congress, not just this month, but every day, as we press forward in our mission to ensure no man faces prostate cancer alone."

Additional co-sponsors of the resolution include U.S. Senators Jim Risch (R-ID) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD).

Prostate cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer-related deaths among men in the United States. One in eight men in the United States will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetimes, and one in 44 men in the United States will die from the disease.

title: Booker, Salinas Lead Eight Lawmakers Urging RV Industry to Eliminate Deforestation-Linked Timber from Supply Chains
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-6) are calling on the nation’s leading recreational vehicle manufacturers to adopt more sustainable sourcing practices and remove hardwood linked to global deforestation from their supply chains. In a new letter, the lawmakers urge companies to transition toward responsibly sourced domestic hardwoods or composite alternatives.

“Families buy RV’s to get closer to nature, and they should never have to wonder whether their vehicle was built with wood from a destroyed rainforest,” wrote the lawmakers. “The RV industry has the influence and the practical alternatives to clean up its supply chain, and we are calling on these companies to do it.”

The letter follows a recent New York Times investigation that revealed Indonesian rainforest timber harvested from environmentally sensitive areas has been used in American RVs. According to the report, this logging has accelerated the destruction of rainforests and peatlands, displaced Indigenous communities, fueled labor abuses, and threatened endangered species such as orangutans.

The lawmakers emphasized that the RV industry — a major player in outdoor recreation — has both the responsibility and the capacity to lead on sustainable sourcing.

In addition to Senator Booker and Congresswoman Salinas, the letter was signed by U.S Representatives Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), and Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), as well as Sens. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI)

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt joins Transportation Secretary Duffy, Governor Kay Ivey, Senator Tommy Tuberville at Mobile Bridge and Bayway Groundbreaking
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) today joined Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Governor Kay Ivey, Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.), members of the Alabama House delegation, and other state leaders in celebrating the groundbreaking of the Mobile River Bridge and Bayway Project. Totaling $3.2 billion in construction costs, the project is one of the largest investments in Alabama’s history and will transform travel along the Gulf Coast.

Senator Britt delivered the following remarks:

“Good morning, everyone. It is wonderful to be gathered here with everyone today. You have seen who all is here. There are so many people who have helped make this happen. This event is a testament to what can happen when local, state and federal leaders work together as a team. But this journey was not easy. As you’ve heard, it started quite some time ago. Back even before 1997, when people knew there was a need for this, tirelessly, people in this community have worked to elevate this to the highest level. Every person played an important role in this, but I will say this would not have happened without President Trump. If you look at where we are today, and that conversation that Coach Tuberville did such a great job of remembering, Coach, I that’s how I heard it go down too. You and I sitting there saying, we need it, this one right here … [President Trump] knew our tactics, too. He called us out. He said, Katie, you’re going to call him, and then he’s going to call me and Coach, you’re going to play golf with him, and then he’s going to call me.

“Secretary Duffy, without your willingness to listen and try to figure out what is a pathway forward—that’s what a servant leader is, is not someone who just immediately says no, but says, ‘let me hear what you need and let me see, is there a pathway forward?’. Without you, without Susie Wiles, and without President Trump, we wouldn’t be standing here today. So, thank you so much, Secretary Duffy. You not only recognize the importance of the project, but you help us cut through the red tape. That’s what we have to do more and more.

“And today’s groundbreaking is yet another opportunity for us to remember the critical work of Governor Ivey. Governor Ivey, throughout your tenure, you have secured record-breaking investments in Alabama. This is a game changer. You laid the foundation at the very beginning of your term as governor, and today we are seeing the fruits of that labor. Generations of Alabamians are going to have different things possible as a result of your service. And we all stand here today to say thank you for helping make this happen. Your decades of leadership have no doubt propelled Alabama into the future. And obviously, we have to thank all of the local leaders here, from the NPOs to the mayors. But chief among them is Mayor Stimpson. Let me tell you something. I remember sitting there with him when I wanted to talk about a ton of different things, and he just wanted to talk about this. He was laser-focused because he knew that this would be a game changer, not just for Alabama and Mobile and Baldwin County, but for the region and for the nation. His tenacity has helped lead us here today. So, to everyone who’s played a role, our congressional delegation, our state elected officials, local elected officials, we say thank you. It’s truly a full-circle moment and decades (of) families, and commuters, and local businesses, and visitors are going to benefit from this long-awaited bridge that today we make a reality.

“This corridor is going to be a lifeline for Alabama, for the region and for the nation. It’s going to connect the Port of Mobile. It’s going to connect our shipbuilders, our military assets, our hard-working Alabamians and wonderful Americans who travel to visit our great state. This investment will mitigate ongoing safety concerns and also strengthen our hurricane evacuation routes.

“So today, I am thrilled to say we are finally here and thank everybody who played a role in making this happen. What an incredible day and a milestone for our state. There is a lot more to come. God Bless.”

You can watch the Senator’s full remarks here.

Senator Britt’s advocacy and efforts for the construction of the Mobile Bridge and Bayway have been extensive. She urged Secretary Duffy to commit to seeing the project through and twice led the entire Alabama delegation in advocating for investing federal funds towards the project. Last year, the Senator applauded Secretary Duffy’s announcement finalizing $550 million in federal funding for the project.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named to TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars List
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) this week was named to the TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars list. Senator Britt is the only Republican lawmaker and the only Alabamian named to this year’s list. She is just the second Alabamian ever to receive the honor.

The announcement from TIME can be read below:

“Senator Katie Britt has quickly learned how to wield influence in Donald Trump’s Republican Party while avoiding its hardest edges.

“Not long after she became in 2022 the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, Mitch McConnell invited her to join his weekly leadership meetings as an adviser, giving her access to the GOP’s longtime power center.

Her ability to bridge divides within the GOP while cultivating bipartisan relationships has made Britt an increasingly consequential player in the Senate.”

“I’m deeply humbled by this recognition, but it truly belongs to the people of Alabama. Every single day, I’m focused on making sure the hardworking families in our state and across our nation have the opportunity to thrive — whether that’s making childcare more affordable and accessible, ensuring continued nationwide access to IVF, keeping our nation safe and secure, or protecting our kids online. Serving Alabama is the honor of a lifetime, and I’ll keep fighting day in and day out to put the people I represent in a stronger place as a result of my service.”

title: Budd, Rosen Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Cybersecurity Readiness by Driving a Partnership Between the DoD & Universities
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Ted Budd (R-N.C.) and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), members of the Senate Armed Services Committee, introduced the bipartisan Cyber Centers of Excellence Partnership Act to strengthen America’s cybersecurity readiness and workforce development nationwide. The bill would establish a partnership between the Department of Defense (DoD) and universities designated by the National Security Agency as National Centers of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity, creating opportunities to share research, best practices, and emerging approaches between the public and private sectors. This program would not only increase collaboration between top research institutions and our specialized military cyber units but also create direct pathways for qualified students into federal cybersecurity careers.

“American military dominance depends on our nation’s ability to operate in cyberspace, making it essential to maintain a robust cybersecurity workforce. I’m proud to work across the aisle with Senator Rosen to strengthen the pipeline of cyber talent by establishing programs where students in our nation’s NSA-designated Centers of Academic Excellence can get real-world experience conducting critical cyber operations in defense of our homeland,” said Senator Budd.

“As technological advancements become more heavily integrated into modern warfare, it is more important than ever that our nation has the talent and personnel needed to handle looming threats,” said Senator Rosen. “This bipartisan bill would ensure that our military and top universities can keep up with every wave of ever-changing cyber threats, while also attracting the country’s most talented young minds and bolstering our cyber-ready workforce.”

Read the full bill text HERE.

BACKGROUND

DoD faces a growing demand for skilled cyber professionals to support offensive and defensive operations. NSA-designated Centers of Academic Excellence programs can help meet that demand by equipping students with the cyber skills needed to enter government service and strengthen our national security workforce.

The Cyber Centers of Excellence Partnership Act would:

• Expand the cyber talent pipeline available to the DoD.

• Increase collaboration between operational cyber units and leading cybersecurity research institutions.

• Provide students with practical experience supporting military cyber missions.

• Identify barriers to onboarding cyber talent, including clearance processing and network access requirements.

• Improve recruitment and retention of highly skilled cyber professionals for national security missions.

title: PHOTOS: Capito Makes Stops in Huntington

Jezierski, as well as the team, have been responsive to the needs of the food bank but more importantly, the voices of the West Virginians we serve. title: ICYMI: Cassidy Applauds Trump Administration’s Steps to Implement his School Choice Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) today released a statement celebrating the Trump administration’s plan to advance his Educational Choice for Children Act (ECCA) that he championed and secured as part of last year’s Working Families Tax Cuts. On October 1, the U.S. Department of Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service unveiled plans to implement the Education Freedom Tax Credit ahead of its January 2027 launch.

“Parents want to make decisions that allow their child to succeed. This law helps them do that,” said Dr. Cassidy. “I’m proud to have led efforts on this historic expansion of educational freedom.”

Background

As Chairman of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, Cassidy is a longtime advocate for school choice. ECCA provides scholarships for an estimated two million students in elementary and secondary education settings for tuition, fees, supplies, and equipment for the enrollment or attendance at an elementary or secondary school. Cassidy also led efforts to encourage U.S. Governors to opt-in to the federal school choice scholarship tax credit.

Cassidy worked with U.S. Representative Adrian Smith (R-NE) on legislation to ensure scholarship donors’ tax benefits are not reduced based on their marital status. Treasury’s newly announced proposal reflects that approach: married couples filing jointly could claim up to $3,400 annually for scholarship donations.

Additionally, Cassidy led a HELP Committee hearing on increasing education options for families at the beginning of the year.

title: Senator Collins Applauds G7 Release of Diesel and Crude Oil
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins issued the following statement after Secretary of Energy Chris Wright called to inform her that the Group of Seven (G7) European nations—France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom—have agreed to collectively release 50 million barrels of diesel and 50 million barrels of crude oil over the next four months:

“Secretary Wright called me today to share this welcome news following our frequent conversations about the harmful effects that escalating home heating oil prices are having on Maine families. I applaud this announcement, which will increase the supply of diesel, which can also be used to heat homes this winter, and crude oil, putting immediate downward pressure on gasoline and diesel prices. This will help to lower costs for Americans heating their homes and fueling up cars and trucks, farmers and other businesses producing and transporting goods, and households purchasing the everyday products they depend on.

“Approximately half of Maine households rely on fuel oil to heat their homes. That is why I have repeatedly urged the Administration to use every tool available to increase supply and bring down energy costs. Today’s agreement from the G7 European nations will help provide much-needed relief to Maine families this winter.”

+++

Last month, Senator Collins and Senator Angus King urged President Trump to release home heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve to help protect Mainers from rising costs. In their letter to the President, the Senators noted that heating oil prices in Maine had increased by 74 percent compared to the previous year, adding approximately $675 to the cost of filling a standard heating oil tank. Senator Collins has also raised the issue of escalating home heating oil prices directly with Secretary Wright in multiple conversations.

title: Senator Collins, Colleagues Urge DOJ to Further Investigate Illegal Chinese Marijuana Operations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Susan Collins, Tom Cotton (R-AR), Pete Ricketts (R-NE), and Ted Budd (R-NC) wrote to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche urging the Department of Justice (DOJ) to investigate the increasing number of illicit drug enterprises operated by Chinese criminal organizations on American soil.

Their letter cites a Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) report that described the wide-ranging network of illegal Chinese marijuana grow operations that have expanded across the United States.

Earlier this year, Senator Collins helped secure provisions to address Chinese-linked illicit drug operations in the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, which was signed into law in February. The law directed the Secretary of State to submit a report on Chinese-linked illegal drug operations in the United States. The bill also included $150 million to counter the flow into the United States of fentanyl and synthetic drugs, which are often produced using precursor chemicals originating in China.

“We write requesting that the Department of Justice (DOJ) investigate the growing role of Chinese transnational criminal organizations in America’s cannabis and intoxicating-hemp markets,” the Senators wrote. “Recent reporting and investigations suggest Chinese criminal networks are exploiting vulnerabilities in federal law to operate expansive illicit drug enterprises that threaten our communities and national security.”

“The Drug Enforcement Administration's 2025 National Drug Threat Assessment found that Chinese transnational criminal organizations dominate marijuana cultivation and distribution in the United States, especially in states with legal cannabis markets,” they continued. “These organizations purchase and lease American land for illegal grow operations, traffic foreign workers, and use toxic pesticides and fertilizers shipped from China, including chemicals banned in the United States. The scale and complexity of these networks make them difficult to track and raise concerns about what other illicit or synthetic products they may be introducing into the U.S. market.”

“Congress has recognized the need to address vulnerabilities in this market, including closing gaps in the 2018 Farm Bill that allowed unregulated intoxicating hemp and THC products to proliferate. These reforms are set to take effect on December 11, 2026.” […] “While this will address harmful products currently in the market, questions remain about who is financing and supporting these organizations operating within the industry. We therefore request that the DOJ fully investigate these criminal networks, including their financing, land usage, chemical imports, and any connections to the Chinese Communist Party,” the Senators concluded.

The complete text of the letter can be read here.

+++

Senator Collins’ work on this issue began in 2022, when she wrote to Maine’s DEA Director Roy McKinney regarding a constituent’s report that a neighboring house caught fire, apparently due to an illicit drug operation.

Since then, Senator Collins has repeatedly pressed senior federal officials in letters, meetings, and oversight hearings to address these illegal operations. This includes the Attorney General, DEA Administrator, FBI Director, and Secretary of State during the Biden Administration, and the DEA Administrator, FBI Director, former Secretary of Homeland Security, former Attorney General, and Secretary of the Treasury during the Trump Administration.

title: Cornyn, Colleagues’ Mystic Alerts Act Heads to President’s Desk
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators John Cornyn (R-TX) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) and Representative August Pfluger (TX-11) released the following statements after their Mystic Alerts Act, which will allow wireless emergency alerts (WEAs) to be delivered via satellite communications technologies when other pathways fail during emergencies, including disasters like the Fourth of July floods in Central Texas last year, passed the Senate unanimously and now heads to the President’s desk:

“More than 130 people were tragically killed in the July 4th floods that ravaged Central Texas last year, many of whom did not receive emergency alerts due to compromised cellular networks that were knocked out by the storm,” said Sen. Cornyn. “This bill will address this technology shortfall and honor the memory of those lost by ensuring Texans and all Americans can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite even when disaster strikes, and I look forward to President Trump signing it into law soon.”

“When storms, disasters, or threats to public safety threaten our state, crisis management is key,” said Sen. Ossoff. “This bipartisan bill with Senator Cornyn will help upgrade America’s emergency alert systems to keep Georgia families safe and informed.”

“I am grateful that the Mystic Alerts Act is now heading to President Trump’s desk to be signed into law. The July 4th floods of 2025 were a heartbreaking tragedy that claimed lives across our state. My legislation will ensure that Americans in rural areas receive life-saving alerts when disaster strikes and traditional networks fail. I thank Senator Cornyn for his partnership in leading the Mystic Alerts Act in the Senate, and Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz for advancing it through his committee. This marks a crucial step in updating emergency preparedness nationwide,” said Rep. Pfluger.

Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) led this legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives, which passed it unanimously on April 20, 2026.

title: PASSED: Cortez Masto Legislation to Support Traumatic Brain Injury Patients
text:
Washington, D.C. – The Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto’s (D-Nev.) Dennis John Benigno Traumatic Brain Injury Program Reauthorization Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation to support traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients. Alongside Senator Cortez Masto, the legislation was led by Senators Alan Armstrong (R-Okla.) and Andy Kim (D-N.J.).

The legislative package, which now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration, contained two key provisions authored by Senator Cortez Masto: the Public Safety Officer Concussion and Traumatic Brain Injury Act and the Protecting Survivors from Traumatic Brain Injury Act.

The Public Safety Officer Concussion and Traumatic Brain Injury Act would require the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to collect and make publicly available information on TBIs specifically for public safety officers and provide recommendations and protocols for identifying, diagnosing, and treating concussions.

The Protecting Survivors from Traumatic Brain Injury Act would require the Department of Health and Human Services to report information to Congress about individuals who may be at higher risk for TBIs, such as domestic violence or sexual assault survivors. The legislation would help assess how prevalent these injuries are and inform service providers about the resources and support survivors need.

“Every year, more than 2.5 million Americans get a traumatic brain injury,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “We have a responsibility to do everything we can to both prevent these injuries from happening and support patients through the recovery process. I am glad the Senate unanimously passed my legislative package, and I urge my House colleagues to immediately do the same.”

Senator Cortez Masto has consistently fought to ensure all Nevadans can access high-quality, affordable health care. She has led other legislative efforts to study TBI prevalence among victims of domestic violence and required the Government Accountability Office to report on federal efforts to study TBIs. She has also championed efforts to lower drug costs for seniors, hold Big Pharma accountable, and expand Medicare drug price negotiation. She has championed legislation to strengthen Medicare-funded behavioral health services and telehealth services, as well as protect access to ambulance services in rural and underserved areas.

title: Cotton, Senators to Hegseth, Lutnick: Preserve Domestic Critical Mineral Supply Chain to Beat Communist China
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Tatum Wallace or Hannah McCarthy

October 2, 2026

Cotton, Senators to Hegseth, Lutnick: Preserve Domestic Critical Mineral Supply Chain to Beat Communist China

WASHINGTON—Senator Tom Cotton (R-Arkansas), along with Senators John Boozman (R-Arkansas), Chuck Schumer (D-New York), Thom Tillis (R-North Carolina), Ted Budd (R-North Carolina), and Mark Kelly (D-Arizona), sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick encouraging action to preserve domestic manufacturing of silicon carbide to respond to Communist China’s increased production. Silicon carbide is a key component of the semiconductors that are used in advanced defense systems, AI data centers, electric grid infrastructure, 5G telecommunications, and the auto industry.

In part, the Senators wrote:

“We write to draw your attention to a critical matter at the intersection of national security, economic competitiveness and trade policy: the accelerating Chinese government effort to dominate the global silicon carbide semiconductor industry and supply chain, and the urgent need for a whole-of-government response to preserve and strengthen trusted domestic and allied manufacturing of silicon carbide.”

Full text of the letter may be found here and below.

October 1, 2026

The Honorable Pete Hegseth

Secretary of Defense

1000 Defense Pentagon

Washington, D.C. 20301-1000

The Honorable Howard Lutnick

Secretary of Commerce

1401 Constitution Avenue, N.W.

Washington, D.C. 20230

Dear Secretaries Hegseth and Lutnick:

We write to draw your attention to a critical matter at the intersection of national security, economic competitiveness and trade policy: the accelerating Chinese government effort to dominate the global silicon carbide semiconductor industry and supply chain, and the urgent need for a whole-of-government response to preserve and strengthen trusted domestic and allied manufacturing of silicon carbide.

Silicon carbide is the foundational substrate for a critical class of next-generation semiconductors that are indispensable across advanced defense systems, AI data centers, electric grid infrastructure, 5G telecommunications, and the modern automotive sector. Silicon carbide’s unique combination of high-voltage tolerance, thermal conductivity, and switching speed makes it irreplaceable in high-performance air, land and sea propulsion systems, directed energy weapons, and air and missile defense systems.

Since launching its Made in China 2025 initiative, Beijing has recognized the military and economic importance of silicon carbide and made global domination in the sector a national industrial priority. In the last five years, Chinese producers have increased their share of the global silicon carbide wafer market from less than 5 percent to nearly 50 percent today.

Clearly, China intends to undermine another strategically important industry built on American technology and ingenuity. If this campaign succeeds, the United States will find itself dependent on adversary supply chains for materials essential to our most advanced defense systems and critical technological infrastructure. The domestic supply chain is already under significant pressure and we are at risk of losing industry leaders and globally competitive manufacturers to this coordinated campaign. The time to act is now, before we reach the crisis stage where remedies are impossible or far more expensive and time-consuming.

We encourage you to leverage Defense Production Act authorities, critical minerals designations, Buy America requirements, and any other authorities at your disposal to ensure the U.S. can protect its silicon carbide supply chain.

Sincerely,

Tom Cotton

United States Senator

title: Crapo, Booker Commemorate End of National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month
text:
Washington, D.C.--To commemorate the end of Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, U.S. Senators Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) and Cory Booker (D-New Jersey) led introduction of a Senate Resolution to recognize September as National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month. The resolution also encourages all Americans to take part in efforts to increase early detection, improve treatment and discover more breakthroughs for the disease, which has a 99 percent survival rate if caught in the earliest stage.

“Routine health screenings contribute to early prostate cancer detection,” said Senator Crapo. “Treatment is most effective when caught early. I encourage all men to discuss screening options with their health care provider and educate themselves further about early detection.”

"Prostate cancer is one of the most treatable cancers when it's caught early, yet too many men aren't getting screened in time, and the toll falls especially hard on Black men, who are more likely to be diagnosed with and die from the disease," said Senator Booker. "Early detection saves lives. I urge every man to talk with his doctor about screening, and I'm grateful to Senator Crapo for partnering with me on this resolution to raise awareness and advance the research that will lead to better outcomes."

"Prostate Cancer Awareness Month serves as a vital call to action, urging men to know their risk, seek early detection, and explore the treatment options that can save their lives," said Courtney Bugler, President and CEO of ZERO Prostate Cancer. "We are incredibly grateful to Senator Crapo and Senator Booker for their unwavering dedication to this cause. Their leadership continues to drive meaningful progress in awareness, research, and support for the men and families navigating this disease. As we mark another Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, we are proud to stand with them and our champions in Congress, not just this month, but every day, as we press forward in our mission to ensure no man faces prostate cancer alone."

Additional co-sponsors of the resolution include Senators Jim Risch (R-Idaho) and Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland).

Prostate cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer-related deaths among men in the United States. One in eight men in the United States will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetimes, and one in 44 men in the United States will die from the disease.

Read the full Resolution HERE.

title: Sen. Cruz Applauds Senate Passage of Resolution Honoring Texas A&M’s 150th Anniversary
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) applauded Senate passage of the joint resolution he introduced with U.S. Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) commemorating the 150th anniversary of Texas A&M University. Texas A&M formally opened its doors on October 4, 1876, as the state’s first public institution of higher education and now enrolls more than 81,000 students across its campuses.

Sen. Cruz said, “Texas A&M has produced generations of Texan, American, and global leaders committed to the values of excellence, integrity, leadership, loyalty, respect, and selfless service. These young men and women received a life-changing education in Aggieland and went on to address significant challenges around the world. I am proud to celebrate this remarkable milestone with fighting Aggies everywhere and look forward to the university’s continued success. Gig ‘em!”

The Texas Legislature established the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas in 1871, with formal opening ceremonies and the first day of classes on October 4, 1876.

Texas A&M’s core values include excellence, integrity, leadership, loyalty, respect, and selfless service. Texas A&M has played a pivotal role in the American Dream by providing generations of students with access to a quality, life-changing education.

title: Duckworth, Durbin Announce $300,000 in Funding for Jersey Community Hospital District
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today announced $300,000 in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) for Jersey Community Hospital District, specifically for rural emergency medical service training. The funding, which was created through Durbin’s Supporting and Improving Rural EMS Needs (SIREN) Act, will go toward supporting EMS agencies in training and recruiting staff, conducting certification courses, purchasing equipment, and supporting community efforts to address substance use across rural America.

“Rural EMS providers are often the first to answer the call when a neighbor is in crisis, and they need the training, equipment and resources to be ready,” Duckworth said. “This $300,000 federal investment will help Jerseyville strengthen its EMS workforce and better serve families across the region.”

“Across Illinois, rural EMS agencies are the first on the scene to respond to community emergencies, the opioid crisis, or natural disasters. But EMTs must have the proper training, equipment, and steady funding to support their efforts to care for their community,” Durbin said. “I worked hard to pass the SIREN Act to meet the needs of our rural EMS agencies, and I’m encouraged to see this funding make its way to Jerseyville to address the region’s health needs.”

Durbin’s bipartisan SIREN Act was signed into law in 2018 as part of the Farm Bill. Since then, Durbin and U.S. Senator Susan Collins (R-ME) have led the appropriations effort to grow the program from $5 million annually to $13.5 million this year—resulting in a total of $40 million in grants nationwide across 42 states. The SIREN Act has resulted in new funds to rural EMS and fire agencies in Carbondale, Nauvoo, Amboy, Jerseyville, Mt. Carmel, Paris, and Gibson City, Illinois.

In September 2024, then-President Biden signed Durbin’s bipartisan SIREN Reauthorization Act into law, extending funding for an additional five years for SIREN Act grants to rural fire and EMS agencies nationwide.

A decline in primary care and hospital service availability, health care workforce shortages, great distances between health care facilities, and low insurance reimbursement for transport and emergency treatment have all strained rural EMS agencies. At the same time, first responders are often the only health care providers in their area and face difficulties in both securing expensive equipment and with recruitment and retention of personnel. As a result, EMS agencies today are tasked with ever-greater responsibilities—preparing for natural and manmade disasters and bioterror threats, supporting the chronic and emergency care needs of an aging population, and responding on the front lines of the opioid epidemic.

title: Durbin, Duckworth Join Cortez Masto, Wyden To Demand Trump Administration Abandon Plan To Strip Tax Credits From 700,000 American Taxpayers
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) and U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) joined Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Ron Wyden (D-OR), and five of their Senate colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration abandon a plan that would prevent up to 700,000 Deferred Action on Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and Temporary Protected Status (TPS) recipients and other tax-paying immigrants from claiming tax credits they are eligible for.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of Treasury are proposing a rule change that would prevent hundreds of thousands of taxpayers from claiming the Adoption Tax Credit, the American Opportunity Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit, and the Earned Income Tax Credit. DACA and TPS recipients have been lawfully claiming these taxes for decades.

“According to your own estimates, the proposed rule change could affect up to 700,000 taxpayers,” the Senators wrote in a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS CEO Frank Bisignano. “This would include more than 300,000 individuals living in households with a DACA recipient, two-thirds of whom are U.S. citizens and who have, on average, lived in the United States for over 28 years. The practical effect of these new regulations would be to deny tax credits to immigrants who are legally eligible for them and lawfully present in our country, and to create a byzantine and unworkable system for both tax preparers and taxpayers.”

“The Administration has no legal authority to change congressionally enacted tax law via regulation,” they continued. “Since the passage of PRWORA in 1996, no federal agency has interpreted refundable tax credits as federal public benefits restricted to qualified immigrants. If Congress intended for refundable tax credits to be treated as federal public benefits, it has had over 30 years to clarify the statute.”

“The proposed rule is clear regulatory overreach that would have disastrous impacts for lawfully present immigrants and their families who are legally eligible for refundable tax credits,” they concluded.

In addition to Senators Durbin, Duckworth, Cortez Masto, and Wyden, the letter was signed by Senators Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Michael Bennet (D-CO), and Patty Murray (D-WA).

The full text of the letter is available here.

title: Durbin Receives Distinguished Service Award From Illinois Health And Hospital Association
text:
Durbin receives award in honor of his decades of supporting Illinois hospitals and working to expand Americans’ access to health care

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today was presented with the Distinguished Service Award by the Illinois Health and Hospital Association (IHA) for his longstanding efforts to support hospitals and expand access to health care. Durbin spoke before receiving the award, highlighting his efforts to protect rural hospitals, bolster the health care workforce, and reinstate Medicaid funding after congressional Republicans slashed $1 trillion from the program. Durbin also offered his gratitude to the IHA and hospital leaders who worked with him to launch the Chicago HEAL Initiative, a collaboration between hospitals and community partners to address the root causes of gun violence through economic, health, and community projects in Chicago neighborhoods with the highest rates of violence, poverty, and health disparities.

“Instead of building on the success of the Chicago HEAL Initiative and improving our nation’s health care system, Republicans in Washington have enacted some of the most drastic cuts to Americans’ health coverage by slashing funding for the ACA and Medicaid. Not only are Illinoisans losing their coverage, but hospitals are being forced to navigate mountains of new administrative red tape created by this Administration just to provide care for their patients,” Durbin said. “But IHA and our hospital leaders are doing all they can to continue to provide quality service to Illinoisans. And it’s been an honor to be their partner in that effort.”

Photos of Durbin receiving the award can be found here.

Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), which passed last year, cut $1 trillion from Medicaid and $300 billion from Affordable Care Act coverage over the next decade in order to fund tax cuts for billionaires. Following passage of OBBBA, Durbin sent a letter to every hospital in Illinois to survey the projected impact on hospitals. Across the 129 responses Durbin received, hospitals across Illinois, especially those in rural areas, detailed fears about pending cuts to services and staff while emergency room wait times increase.

In response to rural hospitals’ concerns about potential cuts or forced closures, Durbin has advanced his bipartisan Rural Hospital Closure Relief Act. The legislation would update Medicare’s “Critical Access Hospital” (CAH) designation so more rural hospitals can qualify for this financial lifeline and continue to serve their communities with quality, affordable health care services.

To address the health care workforce shortage, Durbin has worked across the aisle to introduce legislation that would bring more health care professionals to rural areas, support health care educators, and build up the health care workforce. In March, Durbin reintroduced the bipartisan Rural America Health Corps Act, legislation that would incentivize more health professionals to serve and plant roots in rural communities by creating a new program under the Health Resources and Services Administration’s (HRSA) National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to test whether an increased loan repayment amount would improve the retention of health providers in rural areas.

In January, Durbin reintroduced the bipartisan Nurse Faculty Shortage Reduction Act to address the critical nursing faculty shortage by creating a pilot grant program to help nursing schools increase wages for nurse educators. In 2025, Durbin introduced the bipartisan Healthcare Workforce Resilience Act, which would allow for the recapture of 25,000 unused immigrant visas for nurses and 15,000 unused immigrant visas for physicians that Congress has previously authorized—providing a desperately needed boost to our health care system in rural and urban areas.

title: ICYMI: Who Are the Millionaires Collecting Unemployment? IRS Letter to Ernst Reveals the Answer
text:
WASHINGTON – In a May letter to U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), the IRS revealed that 10,100 million-dollar earners collected nearly $97.4 million in unemployment benefits in 2024 alone. The top occupations among the jobless millionaires included engineers, software engineers, financial professionals, lawyers, executive managers, doctors, and consultants, concentrated in California, New York, Massachusetts, New Jersey, and Washington.

On Monday, The Washington Times reported the IRS’s data, released in response to an Ernst inquiry. Read the story here.

In a companion op-ed, Ernst called out the "freebies for freeloading fat cats":

"In 2024 alone, 10,100 million-dollar earners received nearly $97.4 million in unemployment compensation. That amounts to each being paid $9,650, roughly the cost of a new Rolex watch. Coincidentally, it is also the amount spent on healthcare by a typical Iowan over the course of a year."

"From the fields in Iowa to the battlefields in Iraq, I have worked my entire life. Unlike most of my colleagues in the Senate, I am not a millionaire. I know what it is like to live paycheck to paycheck."

"Because unemployment programs are funded primarily by taxing employers, this federal mandate is effectively a reverse Robin Hood tax that takes from struggling small businesses to give to the idle rich and self-sufficient."

"My message to the affluent finance bros being cut off from Uncle Sam's unemployment trust fund is simple: If you are fortunate enough to make $1 million or more per year without having to work, then you should be counting your blessings — not collecting jobless benefits."

Read the full op-ed here.

Background:

Ernst has led the fight to end jobless payments to millionaires since 2020. Last year, the Senate unanimously passed her Ending Unemployment Payments to Jobless Millionaires Act as an amendment to the One Big Beautiful Bill, which President Trump signed into law. The law is now in effect, barring anyone earning $1 million or more from collecting unemployment benefits. The Congressional Budget Office estimates it could save as much as $100 million over the next decade.

title: Gallego Celebrate Passage of Bill to Protect American’s Access to ATMs
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) celebrated the Senate unanimously passing his bipartisan legislation to crack down on ATM crime. The Safe Access to Cash Act will make sure that federal penalties that are in place for bank robberies apply to off-site ATM robberies.

“As bank branches reduce their physical footprint, ATMs remain key for allowing families and business to access their accounts. But criminals have figured out that standalone ATMs are easier targets than banks and, under the current law, these robberies aren’t treated the same as bank robberies.” said Senator Gallego. “We’re now one step closer to safeguarding Americans’ financial security from these threats, and I urge the House to immediately pass this bill and send it to the president’s desk.”

Robbers and thieves are increasingly targeting ATMs, with theft rates rising dramatically each year since 2019. ATMs can be robbed in as little as three minutes and may hold as much as $250,000. However, the Federal Bank Robbery Act of 1934currently only protects banks and financial institutions, not standalone ATMs in malls, convenience stores, and public locations. The Safe Access to Cash Act ensures that robberies involving off-site ATMs receive federal penalties equal to those imposed for on-site robberies of financial institutions.

Read the full legislation HERE.

title: Gallego, Colleagues Reintroduce Legislation to Expand Access to Women’s Preventative Health Services
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) and 14 Senate Democrats in reintroducing the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act, legislation that would increase the availability of preventive, life-saving cancer screenings at safety-net health care providers like Planned Parenthood.

The bill would create new grant and pilot programs to expand access to preventive services and screenings for breast and gynecological cancers — especially for low-income women and women of color — and train health care providers in providing high-quality cancer screening, early detection, and follow-up care.

“The reintroduction of this bill is an important step toward ensuring women everywhere have access to the preventive health care that can mean the difference between life and death,” said Senator Gallego. “I’m proud to stand with my colleagues to expand access to lifesaving cancer screenings and break down the barriers too many women continue to face, regardless of their income or background. In doing so, we honor Jeannette Acosta’s legacy and stand with every woman and family whose lives have been impacted by cancer.”

“I’m proud to reintroduce the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act in honor of Jeanette Acosta, a fierce advocate who fought to make sure every woman could get the health care she needs,” said Senator Murray. “Too many women suffer preventable deaths because they didn’t have access to the cancer screenings that would have detected their condition early on. That is an unacceptable tragedy. We know that early detection saves lives — not to mention health care costs — and investing in preventive services to help more women get treatment before it’s too late is just common sense. I’m not going to stop fighting to pass this crucial piece of legislation in Jeanette’s memory.”

In addition to Gallego and Murray, the bill was sponsored by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

The bill is endorsed by: American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Black Women’s Health Imperative, Human Rights Watch, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Council of Jewish Women, National Family Planning & Reproductive Health Association, National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

title: Gallego, Kelly Celebrate Chiricahua Officially Becoming Arizona’s Fourth National Park
text:
Bipartisan legislation to make this happen passed the Senate this week, now heads to the president’s desk to be signed into law

WASHINGTON — This week, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) celebrated the final passage of the Chiricahua National Park Act, bipartisan legislation to designate Chiricahua National Monument in Cochise County as Chiricahua National Park. Representatives Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-06) and Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04) introduced the legislation in the House, which passed in March.

The designation will make Chiricahua Arizona’s fourth national park, alongside Grand Canyon, Petrified Forest, and Saguaro National Parks. It will protect Chiricahua’s unique landscape while bringing more visitors and economic opportunities to rural southeastern Arizona.

“The unique landscape of Chiricahua National Park will unite people from around the world while opening economic and tourism opportunities for Arizona. The passage of this bill is a win for huge win for Arizona and honors the culture and preservation of the land,” said Senator Gallego. “Thank you to the Senate and the House for passing this bill, and I look forward to the president signing this into law.”

“Chiricahua is one of Arizona’s most extraordinary places. Designating it as our state’s fourth national park will protect this remarkable landscape for generations and bring new visitors and economic opportunities to southeastern Arizona,” said Senator Kelly. “I’m grateful to everyone involved for working together to get this across the finish line.”

title: Gallego, Kelly Celebrate Senate Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Help Prevent Catastrophic Wildfires
text:
Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act makes it easier for states and communities to use prescribed fires to reduce wildfire risk

WASHINGTON — This week, the Senate unanimously passed Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly’s (D-AZ) Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation to make it easier for states and communities to use prescribed fires to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives.

Prescribed fires are one of the most effective tools available to reduce hazardous fuels before they contribute to larger and more destructive wildfires. However, current federal air quality rules can make it harder for states to use prescribed fires proactively. The Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act would give states greater certainty that they will not be penalized under the Clean Air Act for responsibly using prescribed burns to reduce wildfire risk.

“Prescribed burns are essential to protecting millions of Americans who are threatened by wildfires each year, including in many communities across Arizona,” said Senator Gallego. “I urge the House to take up this common-sense bill and send it to the President’s desk.”

“Arizona communities know how much damage catastrophic wildfires can do, and we need to do everything we can to reduce that risk before a fire starts,” said Senator Kelly. “Prescribed burns are a proven way to clear out dangerous fuels and keep our forests and communities safer. I look forward to getting it across the finish line.”

Gallego and Kelly introduced the bill alongside Senators John Curtis (R-UT), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), John Boozman (R-AR), and Alex Padilla (D-CA). The legislation advanced unanimously out of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee earlier this month.

title: Grassley, Blumenthal Work to Strengthen Democracy and Stability in Serbia
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) introduced bipartisan legislation to address democratic backsliding in Serbia, improve treatment of student-led and civic protests, and combat the authoritarian influence of Russia, China and Iran. The Supporting the Rule of Law, Building Institutional Justice, and Accountability Act (SRBIJA) would help strengthen Serbia’s democratic institutions, advance the rule of law and promote accountability in the U.S.-Serbia relationship. The legislation would sunset five years after enactment.

“Serbia plays a critical role in preserving peace and security in the Western Balkans. It’s critical to prevent Russia, China or Iran from influencing Serbia and destabilizing the region. Our bipartisan legislation would help strengthen Serbia’s democratic institutions, and it contains key accountability measures like sanctions to promote the country’s return to a strong democracy,” Grassley said.

“This bipartisan measure recognizes that the U.S.-Serbian relationship must embody shared democratic values and commitment to combating autocracy. Since taking power, the current government in Serbia has deepened its ties to Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. This legislation will give the administration new tools to sanction individuals who enable democratic backsliding and show that the United States remains a defender of democracy. I am proud to help lead this effort in the Senate,” Blumenthal said.

The SRBIJA Act expresses Congress’s concern about Serbia’s serious democratic backsliding, including in the rule of law, judicial independence, media freedom and corruption. The measure specifically cites the government’s response to sustained student-led and civic protests, as well as the November 2024 collapse of the Novi Sad railway station canopy. The concerns are especially timely given the upcoming snap parliamentary elections in Serbia on October 25, 2026. Last Sunday, Aleksandar Vucic resigned as Serbia’s president, laying the groundwork to keep his grip on power by taking over as prime minister if his governing party wins the election.

The legislation supports Serbia’s democratic institutions by conditioning additional U.S. assistance on a presidential certification that Serbia has made significant and sustained progress toward judicial accountability, media freedom and alignment with the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).

Additionally, the SRBIJA Act would:

Combat bad actors by supporting the use of existing sanctions authorities against individuals engaged in corruption, serious human rights abuses or who are undermining democratic institutions or threatening peace and stability in the Western Balkans.

In July 2026, the Serbian government sent a cabinet minister to Tehran to attend the funeral of former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, joining delegations from Russia and China at a time when most European governments were not represented.

Evaluate the impact of Russian and Chinese influence by requiring a report to Congress about Russia and China’s political, economic, energy and security ties with Serbia and its implications on American interests. The measure also includes clear, verifiable requirements for the State Department to continue its participation in the U.S.-Serbia Strategic Dialogue.

Require a detailed strategy for U.S. engagement with Serbia that addresses these concerns.

Click HERE for text of the legislation.

In the U.S. House of Representatives, the legislation was introduced by Helsinki Commission co-chairman U.S. Rep. Joe Wilson (R-S.C.) and by U.S. Rep. William Keating (D-Mass.).

Background:

Grassley has consistently worked to advance peace and stability in the Western Balkans, including efforts to address Bosnia and Herzegovina’s constitutional and political crisis.

Serbia’s political, economic and historical ties to Republika Srpska in Bosnia make the country an important factor in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s ongoing constitutional and political crisis. Serbia’s growing ties with Russia and China also impact the broader strategic and security environment in the Western Balkans.

title: Grassley, Klobuchar Lead Effort to Extend Key Tax Credit for Small Agri-Biodiesel Producers
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) introduced the bipartisan Small Agri-Biodiesel Producer Credit Extension Act to extend a key tax credit that supports small biodiesel producers, family farmers and the rural communities they sustain across America.

The legislation would extend the Small Agri-Biodiesel Producer Credit, which is currently scheduled to expire at the end of 2026, through the end of 2029.

“Biofuels support over 31,000 jobs across Iowa. They’re good for the rural economy, good for national security and good for the environment. This credit gives small biodiesel producers the certainty they need to plan investments in rural communities and to create or maintain good paying jobs while doing their part to lower prices at the pump through increased fuel production,” Grassley said.

“With the war in Iran impacting fuel prices across the country, we must continue to invest in homegrown biofuels that strengthen our energy independence, support our farmers, bolster rural economies, and lower fuel prices,” Klobuchar said. “By extending this tax credit, farmers and small biodiesel producers will have the certainty they need to continue manufacturing biofuels and strengthening commodity markets.”

The legislation is endorsed by Clean Fuels Alliance America, the Iowa Renewable Fuels Association, and Western Iowa Energy in Wall Lake.

“Small biodiesel producers are making an outsized contribution to America’s energy security right now, providing lower-cost drop-in distillate fuel that’s needed to move consumer goods across the country. They are investing in rural communities, creating and preserving jobs, and running full out to provide cleaner, better, more affordable fuel. We thank Senators Grassley and Klobuchar for proposing to extend the Small Agri-Biodiesel Producer Credit and providing policy certainty for small producers across the country,” said Kurt Kovarik, Vice President of Federal Affairs at Clean Fuels Alliance America.

“Small biodiesel producers are an important part of Iowa’s rural economy, and they need certainty to keep investing and producing,” said Monte Shaw, executive director of the Iowa Renewable Fuels Association. “This extension gives Iowa producers the runway they need to keep turning Iowa-grown feedstocks into homegrown fuel, supporting farmers and strengthening rural communities.”

“The Small Agri-Biodiesel Producer Credit has been a crucial lifeline for biodiesel producers as they respond to the nation’s demand for affordable, cleaner diesel fuels. Western Iowa Energy is running at full capacity to meet the Trump administration’s goal of massively increasing domestic production of renewable fuel to improve America’s energy security. Extension of the small producer credit will help us maintain production and local jobs in our community,” said Brad Wilson, President and General Manager of Western Iowa Energy.

Click HERE for text of the legislation.

Background:

The Working Families Tax Cuts Act temporarily extended the Small Agri-Biodiesel Producer Credit to 2026. Under the credit, eligible small producers can receive a 20-cent-per-gallon tax credit on the first 15 million gallons of qualifying agri-biodiesel. To qualify, a producer must have a productive capacity of no more than 60 million gallons.

title: Heinrich Unveils Landmark Bipartisan Legislation to Lower Costs, Create Jobs, and Force Data Centers to Fully Pay for Costs They Incur
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, hosted a virtual press conference to unveil the landmark Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, major legislation that will reform and speed up the federal process for reviewing and approving energy projects to lower utility bills and create more jobs — while codifying Tribal consultation in statute, maintaining key environmental protections, and forcing AI data centers to fully pay for their grid upgrades, as well as their share of the existing grid, resulting in savings for families.

VIDEO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich, Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, hosts a virtual press conference to unveil his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, September 30, 2026.

“For New Mexico, this deal could be transformational. New Mexico has proven itself to be a state full of opportunities to expand energy production and build big projects. SunZia is just one example – but it is not the only one. Other projects like Western Spirit, the Crossroads-Hobbs-Roadrunner Transmission Line, and the Atrisco Solar and Storage Project all show the opportunity New Mexico offers to support and expand our energy grid. New Mexico can export clean electrons and import greenbacks,” said Heinrich. “Beyond any one project, New Mexico has the skilled talent, the geography, and the resources to be a key part of our clean energy future. This deal means that we can do that, while protecting safeguards that are important to our Tribes, our public lands, our wildlife. And that includes funding a first-of-its-kind Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund, which will help New Mexico clean up the tens of thousands of abandoned hardrock mines across our state.”

“Negotiating this bill has not been easy. But after months of back-and-forth with my colleagues, I am proud to share this bipartisan permitting reform with the public and bring it to the Senate floor later in November for honest, good faith debates. America is defined by our resourcefulness, our skill, our determination – from the Hoover Dam to the Brooklyn Bridge to the SunZia transmission line. And my dad was just one part of that American story. I'm honored to be part of it today, as well. America needs to build big things again, and I'm confident that our Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act can help us do just that,” Heinrich concluded.

The full video of Heinrich’s press conference is here.

The full text of Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is here.

Heinrich’s press release announcing the bill is here.

A fact sheet on the bill is here and below:

Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will deliver cheaper energy, good-paying jobs, and responsible growth in New Mexico and nationwide, while protecting important environmental review and historic preservation processes.

Cheaper Energy

As demand increases, America needs more electricity, and we need it cheaper and faster. This deal will increase energy supply, expand the grid, and drive costs down for families and businesses.

Builds more transmission, faster by strengthening the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (FERC) “backstop” siting authority — giving the federal government more authority to approve major interstate power lines – and allowing transmission applications to be processed simultaneously with state reviews, helping needed projects move through permitting faster.

Gets more energy onto the grid by:

Requiring regional and interregional transmission planning that accounts for where new transmission is needed and plans ahead for future electricity demand, helping to get more electricity to the places that need it and putting downward pressure on electricity costs.

Requiring grid-enhancing technologies and automated systems to speed up the process of connecting new energy projects to the grid and making better use of the grid we already have, increasing the supply available to consumers.

Requiring wholesale electricity markets to allow distributed generation sources and virtual power plants to participate, helping meet growing demand with more available supply.

Forces data centers pay their fair share by requiring data centers to pay for all of their associated transmission costs, rather than relying on a voluntary structure, preventing costs from being passed on to American families or small businesses.

Good-Paying Jobs

America has enormous energy and infrastructure needs, but we cannot create the jobs that come with building those projects if projects spend decades stuck in the permitting process.

Creates jobs across the energy supply chain by boosting the build out of more transmission, clean energy, supply manufacturing, and other grid infrastructure.

Creates greater certainty for projects permitted and financed across presidential administrations by prohibiting any administration from delaying or blocking permitting of a class of energy projects – meaning no administration can block all solar, wind, or other class of energy project permits without facing legal action and fines.

Responsible Growth

Getting to a “yes” or “no” on permitting faster does not mean eliminating environmental protections, Tribal consultation, or the ability to challenge projects in court. This deal keeps important safeguards in place, while creating clear timelines and rules for permitting projects.

Sets clear deadlines for environmental reviews — including a two-year deadline for Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) reviews and a one-year deadline for Environmental Assessment reviews, with consequences for agencies that miss those deadlines. That means environmental reviews still happen, but not indefinitely.

Establishes a new National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) consultation process that runs alongside National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) reviews with a defined time limit, securing a statutory role for Tribes in determining how projects affect historic and cultural resources and protecting Tribes’ rights to formally consult during the processes — two things the Section 106 reforms attempted to eliminate.

Limits the types of impacts that projects are required to mitigate, creating clearer boundaries around which effects a project must mitigate or minimize.

Sets clear limitations on when and how a project may be legally challenged.

Sets a 150-day deadline for legal challenges under the Clean Water Act (CWA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), NEPA, and NHPA.

Generally limits who can bring a legal challenge to people or groups that participated in the relevant comment period or Tribal consultation process.

Limits when a court can temporarily stop a project from moving forward, while preserving the existing ability to seek that relief under the Administrative Procedures Act.

Allows states to handle endangered species consultations if they have demonstrated staffing, expertise, and resource capacity to do so.

Clarifies the limits on state water-quality reviews (under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act) by limiting state certifications to water pollution directly caused by a specific source for gas pipelines and transmission lines and prohibiting use of the process to address unrelated issues.

Prevents the federal government from changing the rules after the fact for certain wetlands and waterways by stopping the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) from preemptively or retroactively removing areas of land from the federal water-quality certification process.

title: Hickenlooper, Curtis Celebrate Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Improve Snowpack Monitoring, Manage Drought
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper and John Curtis celebrated the Senate passage of their bipartisan bill, the Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program Reauthorization Act, to help better predict and measure water supply to manage drought in the West. Passage comes as Colorado, Utah, and the entire West are experiencing a historic 1,200-year climate-driven drought, causing Colorado’s snowpack to reach record lows this past year.

“We can’t make informed decisions about our water supply without the right measurement and monitoring tools,” said Hickenlooper. “We’re in dire straits with this drought in the West, but this bill will help us better manage our precious water resources and give us more accurate water predictions.”

“Water is one of the defining challenges facing Utah and the West, and we need good information to make good decisions,” said Senator Curtis. “In a state where so much of our water supply depends on mountain snowpack, better forecasting helps farmers, communities, and water managers plan ahead and make the most of every drop. I’m pleased the Senate passed our bipartisan bill to strengthen these tools and give Western states better information to manage their water resources.”

Companion legislation introduced by Colorado Representatives Joe Neguse and Jeff Hurd passed the House.

As much as 80% of Colorado’s annual surface water supply comes from snowmelt runoff. Accurate measurements of snowpack are necessary to have a clear picture of the snowmelt that feeds rivers and streams across the West.

The bipartisan legislation would reauthorize the Bureau of Reclamation’s (BOR) Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program which provides grants to advance emerging snow monitoring technology that improve water supply predictions.

Specifically, the bill would:

Reauthorize BOR’s Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program through 2031:

Continue authorized funding of $15 million over five years; and

Update language in existing authorization to emphasize water supply forecasting activities that inform interstate water management decisions.

As governor, Hickenlooper helped negotiate the 2019 Colorado River Basin Drought Contingency Plan, which helped protect critical levels at Lake Powell and Lake Mead and ensured continued compliance with the 1922 Colorado River Compact.

In the Senate, Hickenlooper convened the bipartisan Colorado River Caucus to help address the Colorado River crisis and accompanying drought. Hickenlooper also helped secure millions in funding for water conservation projects in the West from both the Inflation Reduction Act and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

The bipartisan Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program Reauthorization Act is supported by American Rivers, the Southwestern Water Conservation District, Colorado River District, Upper Colorado River Commission, Denver Water, Colorado Department of Natural Resources, Colorado Water Congress, Colorado Municipal League, Associated Governments of Northwest Colorado, the Environmental Defense Fund, The Nature Conservancy, the National Ski Areas Association, the Family Farm Alliance, the National Audubon Society, and the Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership.
