title: Hickenlooper, Kelly, Gallego, Peters Call for Investigation Into Policies Preceding Knowles Firefighter Deaths
text:
Senators seek answers following June deaths of four Rifle Helitack Crew firefighters

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), and Gary Peters (D-Mich.) called on the Department of the Interior to investigate the policies that preceded the deaths of four Rifle Interagency Helitack Crew members responding to the Gore and Knowles Fires on June 27th.

The fallen firefighters, Nick Hutcherson, 27, Emily Barker, 38, Sydney Watson, 27, and Nathan Matthews, 43, grew up in communities across the country before finding their way to federal wildland firefighting in Western Colorado. The senators represent states with connections to the four firefighters.

“The tragedy of the loss of these four lives necessitates a thorough examination of departmental policies that guide fire suppression,” the senators wrote. “This year has seen the highest number of entrapments in two decades, as well as the deaths of 13 federal wildland firefighters, pilots, and contractors in incidents across the West. Now is the time to examine the policies that can help us avoid any additional devastating losses.”

In a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, the senators called for the investigation to examine:

Interior’s “full suppression” strategy: Whether the department’s presumption of full suppression for every wildfire adequately weighs risks to life, property, and natural resources.

Direct attack by default: Whether the approach used on the Knowles Fire was influenced by broader agency policy rather than an assessment of the specific fire behavior and conditions crews faced.

Firefighter safety and weather conditions: Federal forecasts warned of wind gusts up to 60 mph, low humidity, and potentially severe impacts the morning the Rifle Helitack Crew deployed. The crew was inserted two hours later and remained on the ground amid new ignitions, strong winds, and near-zero visibility, according to preliminary investigation reports.

Staffing and organizational changes: Whether Interior’s reorganization of wildfire operations and recent staffing losses affected operations or firefighter safety.

The letter comes as the senators continue seeking answers about the tragedy. Interagency procedures call for serious accident investigations to be completed within 45 days, meaning the internal review should have been completed by August 11. Requests for a briefing on the investigation’s status have not been fulfilled, and no new information has been released since a July 30 update.

“Wildland firefighter safety is a non-negotiable imperative,” the senators wrote. “We call on you to ensure the Department takes a thorough, clear-eyed assessment of the multiple factors that led to four deaths and one serious injury in response to the Knowles Fire.”

Read the full letter HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Burgum:

We write to call for an investigation into the agency-level policy decisions that preceded the deaths of four wildland firefighters while responding to the Gore and Knowles Fires on June 27, 2026.

The four Rifle Interagency Helitack Crew members who lost their lives—Nick Hutcherson, Emily Barker, Sydney Watson, and Nathan Matthews—as well as the fifth firefighter who was severely injured, all acted bravely in their response to the Knowles fire that day. These firefighters grew up in communities in our states across the nation, but all found their way to federal wildland firefighting in Western Colorado, acting as heroes in one of the most severe fire years on record.

The tragedy of the loss of these four lives necessitates a thorough examination of departmental policies that guide fire suppression. This year has seen the highest number of entrapments in two decades, as well as the deaths of 13 federal wildland firefighters, pilots, and contractors in incidents across the West. Now is the time to examine the policies that can help us avoid any additional devastating losses.

The investigation should examine:

Interior’s “Full Suppression Strategy”: Specifically, we ask for a thorough examination of the Department of the Interior’s policy which presumes a “full suppression strategy applied to every wildfire.” Fire scientists recognize that full suppression has made our megafire crisis worse by allowing fuels to accumulate. While it is critical to protect communities at risk of wildfire, it is notable that the Knowles Fire was several miles away from the nearest town when the Rifle Helitack Crew was deployed. We call on Interior to closely examine whether value is added by presuming full suppression at all times, rather than assessing the risks to life, property, and resource values before determining the approach to any given fire.

Direct Attack by Default: An Interior memo additionally indicates that direct attack—meaning measures closer to the fire perimeter—should be the default in this full suppression approach, rather than emphasizing key factors like fire intensity, flame length, and spread rates that may favor indirect attack of a fire. The Department’s investigation should detail whether a direct attack approach was used for the Knowles Fire, and whether that decision was influenced by the larger agency policy rather than an assessment of fire behavior, if so.

Prioritizing Firefighter Safety in Decision-making: Furthermore, we call on Interior to investigate how decision-making structures are prioritizing the safety of our firefighters. In the instance of the Knowles Fire, we believe the Department should examine whether information-sharing—specifically in regard to fire-weather and conditions—led to adequately informed decisions, and whether improvements can or should be made going forward. Notably, the National Incident Management Situation Report issued the morning of the Rifle Helitack Crew’s deployment, predicted wind gusts of up to 60 miles per hour, low humidity, and a likelihood of severe impacts. Still, the Rifle Helitack Crew was inserted into the fire two hours later. And the crew remained on the ground, despite new ignitions, strong winds, and near-zero visibility, according to the preliminary reports from the ongoing investigation of this incident.

Shifts to Agency Structure and Staffing: Additionally, this investigation should examine whether high-level changes to the agency’s structure and staffing contributed to the events of June 27th. The Department’s reorganization of fire activities into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service, which has not been authorized by Congress, merits review in the context of this tragedy and the high number of other incidents this fire season. Additionally, the Department should assess the impact of major staffing cuts and shortages on its fire suppression operations—a pressing question given that the agency has lost 17% of its employees, and the federal wildland firefighters still on staff are covering the gaps with as much as 1,000 hours of overtime. With major organizational changes and staffing losses, we are deeply troubled by reports of low morale and firefighter crews spread thin.

We appreciate that a Serious Accident Investigation Team is conducting a review of the Knowles Fire incident, and we call on Interior to brief our offices on the status of that investigation. Interagency procedures require internal investigation to be completed within 45 days10—which means that the internal review should have been completed by August 11th. As of the writing of this letter, requests for a briefing on the status of this investigation have not been filled, and no new information has been provided since the issuance of a July 30th update on the investigation. The prompt release of this investigation’s findings is crucial to public safety and to that of our wildland firefighters, particularly in this remarkably tragic year.

Wildland firefighter safety is a non-negotiable imperative. It is with this in mind that we call on you to ensure the Department takes a thorough, clear-eyed assessment of the multiple factors that led to four deaths and one serious injury in response to the Knowles Fire. We ask for you to ensure that this information is shared with our offices, and with the families of the Rifle Helitack Crew, in a prompt manner. This information is crucial to the healing of the families and to ensuring that we can learn how to avoid future tragedies.

Sincerely,

###

title: Hoeven to Hold Fireside Chat With NASA Administrator, Golden Dome Director at UAS Summit
text:
GRAND FORKS, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today announced his guests for the 2026 Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) Summit in Grand Forks, including:

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

General Michael Guetlein, Director of Golden Dome for America.

Hoeven invited Isaacman and Guetlein to the state as part of his efforts to advance North Dakota’s role as a leader in drone and counter-drone technology and space operations. The senator will hold a fireside chat at the summit with his two guests on the morning of Tuesday, October 13. Hoeven, Isaacman and Guetlein will then tour the University of North Dakota’s (UND) space facilities, including its simulated space habitat and space suit lab. That afternoon, they will meet with UND researchers and leaders and hold a Q&A session with university students.

“North Dakota is a global leader in unmanned technology, and we are leveraging our unique UAS ecosystem to grow our state’s role in the development of counter-drone technology and the next generation of space operations. I appreciate Administrator Isaacman and General Guetlein for accepting my invitation to this year’s UAS Summit, where we will discuss these efforts and outline how our state will help ensure the U.S. is prepared to meet the defense challenges of tomorrow,” said Hoeven.

title: Husted, Boozman in Oakwood with Ohio farmers
text:
“It was great to host Chairman Boozman in Ohio and spend time listening to hardworking Ohio farmers who are keeping our state fed and fueled.”

OAKWOOD, Ohio – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition and Forestry Chairman John Boozman (R-Ark.) today visited Cooper Farms Hatchery in Oakwood to spend time with Ohio farmers and hear directly about the issues facing the agricultural industry.

“It was great to host Chairman Boozman in Ohio and spend time listening to hardworking Ohio farmers who are keeping our state fed and fueled. The Working Families Tax Cuts Act modernized the farm safety net, helping producers have more certainty when planning for their business and farm operations. The Farm Bill includes five bills that I am championing to support Ohio farmers through agricultural loans, community college agriculture programs, fertilizer research and assistance for rural seniors,” said Husted.

“Senator Husted has been a strong champion for Ohio agriculture, delivering historic investments for farmers through the Working Families Tax Cuts. Farm families will start to see those benefits this month, with Buckeye State producers expected to receive $544 million in ARC and PLC payments––76% more than they would have received without the Republican-supported bill. He listens directly to producers about what they need, and that input helped shape Farm Bill 2.0. I look forward to working together to strengthen the future of agriculture and get a new farm bill signed into law this year that reflects the priorities of Ohio producers,” said Boozman.

Cooper Farms is a family-owned and operated company in Northwest Ohio known for its egg, chicken, turkey and pork operations.

Husted and Boozman held a roundtable with Ohio farmers to hear their concerns and discuss their work in the Senate to support Ohio’s agricultural industry.

Husted highlighted several key provisions in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act that strengthen Ohio’s agricultural industry, including eliminating the death tax for family-run farms, making permanent the 20% Qualified Business Income deduction for farmers and increasing Section 179 expensing limits to help farmers invest in new machinery, equipment and expanded operations.

Ohio is set to receive $544 million in ARC/PLC payments beginning this month. This is nearly double the amount farmers would have received without the improvements made by the Working Families Tax Cuts Act.

Ohio also received 885,000 new base acres that will be available for 2026 payments next fall.

title: President grants disaster declaration for state of Ohio after Husted, Ohio delegation request
text:
“Ohioans have been hit hard by these storms, and I’m grateful to President Trump and the administration for acting quickly to provide Ohio with federal assistance.”

COLUMBUS – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today praised President Donald Trump’s announcement that he will grant the state of Ohio a major disaster declaration following devastating damage caused by severe storms that moved through Ohio from Aug. 10 to 23, 2026.

The announcement comes after Husted helped lead the effort requesting an expedited disaster declaration from Trump and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

“Ohioans have been hit hard by these storms, and I’m grateful to President Trump and the administration for acting quickly to provide Ohio with federal assistance. I’ll continue pushing to make sure Ohioans have the support to recover and rebuild,” said Husted.

Federal assistance is necessary to supplement the efforts and resources available to the state, local governments and disaster relief organizations as Ohio communities recover from the storm damage.

title: Kelly, Gallego Celebrate Senate Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Help Prevent Catastrophic Wildfires
text:
Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act makes it easier for states and communities to use prescribed fires to reduce wildfire risk

This week, the Senate unanimously passed Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego’s Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act (WEPA) of 2026, bipartisan legislation to make it easier for states and communities to use prescribed fires to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives.

Prescribed fires are one of the most effective tools available to reduce hazardous fuels before they contribute to larger and more destructive wildfires. However, current federal air quality rules can make it harder for states to use prescribed fires proactively. The Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act would give states greater certainty that they will not be penalized under the Clean Air Act for responsibly using prescribed burns to reduce wildfire risk.

“Arizona communities know how much damage catastrophic wildfires can do, and we need to do everything we can to reduce that risk before a fire starts,” said Kelly. “Prescribed burns are a proven way to clear out dangerous fuels and keep our forests and communities safer. I look forward to getting it across the finish line.”

“Prescribed burns are essential to protecting millions of Americans who are threatened by wildfires each year, including in many communities across Arizona,” said Gallego. “I urge the House to take up this common-sense bill and send it to the President’s desk.”

Kelly and Gallego introduced WEPA with Senators John Curtis (R-UT), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), John Boozman (R-AR), and Alex Padilla (D-CA). The legislation advanced unanimously out of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee earlier this month.

Background:

This builds on Kelly’s efforts to keeping Americans safe by reducing wildfire risk. This month, Kelly joined Senate colleagues in demanding the Federal Emergency Management Agency to ensure that all communities receive the federal resources they need to respond to and prevent wildfires. Additionally, Kelly’s Wildfire Prevention and Recovery Act, which directs the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to conduct periodic wildfire risk assessments and study the impacts of wildfires on Corps-managed lands through a pilot program beginning in Arizona, passed the EPW committee as part of the 2026 Water Resources Development Act (WRDA).

title: Kelly, Hickenlooper, Gallego, Peters Call for Investigation into Policies Preceding Knowles Firefighter Deaths
text:
Senators seek answers following June deaths of four Rifle Helitack Crew firefighters

Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), and Gary Peters (D-MI) called on the Department of Interior (DOI) to investigate the policies that preceded the deaths of four Rifle Interagency Helitack Crew members responding to the Gore and Knowles Fires on June 27, 2026.

The fallen firefighters—Nick Hutcherson, 27; Emily Barker, 38; Sydney Watson, 27; and Nathan Matthews, 43—grew up in communities across the country before finding their way to federal wildland firefighting in Western Colorado. The senators represent states with connections to the four firefighters.

“The tragedy of the loss of these four lives necessitates a thorough examination of departmental policies that guide fire suppression,” the senators wrote. “This year has seen the highest number of entrapments in two decades, as well as the deaths of 13 federal wildland firefighters, pilots, and contractors in incidents across the West. Now is the time to examine the policies that can help us avoid any additional devastating losses.”

In their letter, the senators called for the investigation to examine:

DOI’s “full suppression” strategy: Whether the department’s presumption of full suppression for every wildfire adequately weighs risks to life, property, and natural resources.

Direct attack by default: Whether the approach used on the Knowles Fire was influenced by broader agency policy rather than an assessment of the specific fire behavior and conditions crews faced.

Firefighter safety and weather conditions: Forecasts warned of wind gusts up to 60 mph, low humidity, and potentially severe impacts the morning the Rifle Helitack Crew deployed. The crew was inserted two hours later and remained on the ground amid new ignitions, strong winds, and near-zero visibility, according to preliminary investigation reports.

Staffing and organizational changes: Whether DOI’s reorganization of wildfire operations and recent staffing losses affected operations or firefighter safety.

The letter comes as the senators continue seeking answers about the tragedy. Interagency procedures call for serious accident investigations to be completed within 45 days, meaning the internal review should have been completed by August 11, 2026. Requests for a briefing on the investigation’s status have not been fulfilled, and no new information has been released since a July 30 update.

“Wildland firefighter safety is a non-negotiable imperative,” the senators wrote. “We call on you to ensure the Department takes a thorough, clear-eyed assessment of the multiple factors that led to four deaths and one serious injury in response to the Knowles Fire.”

title: King Resolution Designating September 30th as National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day Passes Senate Unanimously
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Angus King (I-ME) and Thom Tillis (R-NC) today welcomed news that their bipartisan resolution designating September 30th as “National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day” passed the U.S. Senate unanimously. The resolution recognizes the lasting physical injuries and emotional trauma that can result from military service. The resolution also supports the families and loved ones who bear the loss when a veteran dies by suicide, learning from their experiences, and strengthening early intervention efforts to help with future prevention.

“National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day is a solemn reminder of our responsibility to the veterans we have lost, and to the families who carry their memory forward,” said Senator King. “Their experiences demonstrate the critical importance of early support and reliable access to care. We remain committed to strengthening the systems that provide veterans and their loved ones with effective and compassionate services.”

Senator King had previously led bipartisan legislation to reduce the risk of veteran suicide. The Saving Our Veterans’ Lives Act would authorize a program through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide free firearm lockboxes to veterans to put time and space between at-risk individuals and lethal means, such as firearms.

In 2025, the Department of Veterans Affairs reported that each day, there was an average of 17.5 veteran suicides, making it the 12th leading cause of death among veterans, and the 2nd leading cause among veterans under the age of 45. This accounts for a disproportionate percentage of adult suicides in the United States. Additionally, 75% of veteran suicide deaths involve a firearm, which reaffirms safe firearm storage as an essential part of suicide prevention measures.

The National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day resolution is endorsed by Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW), The American Legion, National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), Disabled American Veterans (DAV), and the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS).

Representing one of the states with the highest rates of military families and veterans per capita, Senator King is a staunch advocate for America’s servicemembers and veterans. In March, Senator King was honored by The American Legion with its 2026 Distinguished Public Service Award. Last year, Senator King was honored by the Disabled American Veterans as its 2025 Legislator of the Year. He was also recognized by the Wounded Warrior Project as the 2024 Legislator of the Year for his “outstanding legislative effort and achievement to improve the lives of the wounded, ill, and injured veterans.”

title: Luján, Wyden Lead Colleagues in Calling on IRS to Drop Unnecessary and Harmful Immigration Status Question on Tax Form
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), a member of the Senate Finance Committee, and U.S. Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member, led nine colleagues in calling on Frank Bisignano, Chief Executive Officer of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), to drop the newly proposed citizenship and work authorization checkbox from the final version of the 2026 Form 1040. In the letter, the senators outlined that adding an immigration question for the first time serves no clear tax purpose and could result in hundreds of billions of dollars in unpaid taxes. The letter also pushes for the release of the updated tax gap estimate, which has been delayed almost a year.

“We write to urge you to drop the newly proposed citizenship and work authorization checkbox from the final version of the 2026 Form 1040. Adding this question for the first time in history appears to serve no legitimate tax administration purpose and risks increasing the tax gap by hundreds of billions of dollars,” wrote the senators.

“Turning the 1040 into an immigration tracker actively sabotages voluntary tax compliance and undermines the IRS’s core tax collection responsibilities. Public trust is already at a low point after the IRS illegally handed over the private data of more than 42,000 taxpayers to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Putting this question on the front page of the Form 1040 will only discourage people from filing altogether,” continued the senators.

In addition to Senators Luján and Wyden, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.).

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Mr. Bisignano:

We write to urge you to drop the newly proposed citizenship and work authorization checkbox from the final version of the 2026 Form 1040. Adding this question for the first time in history appears to serve no legitimate tax administration purpose and risks increasing the tax gap by hundreds of billions of dollars.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) does not need this checkbox to collect taxes. Nonresidents already file Form 1040-NR, and the agency checks work authorization against Social Security Administration data.

Turning the 1040 into an immigration tracker actively sabotages voluntary tax compliance and undermines the IRS’s core tax collection responsibilities. Public trust is already at a low point after the IRS illegally handed over the private data of more than 42,000 taxpayers to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Putting this question on the front page of the Form 1040 will only discourage people from filing altogether.

This is a multi-billion-dollar mistake at a time when our national debt is pushing $40 trillion. The Yale Budget Lab estimates that weaponizing tax filing could cost the federal government $313 billion over the next decade and endanger the $66 billion that unauthorized workers currently pay in taxes each year.

Additionally, we want to know when the Treasury Department will publish the IRS’s updated tax gap estimates or projections, which should be a key focus of any IRS leader. Former Commissioner Werfel committed to releasing these annually, yet recent reporting indicates that the IRS is deliberately sitting on the data. The IRS released its last tax gap report in October 2024, which projected the tax gap for tax year 2022 was nearly $700 billion per year, even though it omitted perhaps the largest parts of the tax gap attributable to corporate income tax, income from flowthrough entities, foreign activities, and digital assets.

An updated report covering the 2023 tax year was scheduled to be released in the fall of 2025. The report is now almost a year late.

Please answer the following questions by October 22, 2026:

Whether the IRS will remove the costly new checkbox, and if not:

Whether this change was directly or indirectly directed by the White House, and if so, provide a copy of any such communications?

Whether any change in tax law requires the IRS to add this checkbox?

Whether the IRS considered the negative impact on voluntary tax compliance and the tax gap before proposing to add this checkbox?

What is the IRS’s estimate of the effect of this change on voluntary tax compliance and the tax gap?

When will the IRS publish an updated estimate or projection of the tax gap?

Will the next tax gap report cover tax year 2024, as the IRS promised, or will it focus on 2023?

Will the next tax gap report cover the tax gap attributable to pass-throughs, corporations, offshore avoidance, and digital assets?

We expect your timely response.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senator Markey, Reps. Tlaib, Pressley Announce Legislation to Stop Big Banks from Bankrolling the Climate Crisis
text:
Legislation requires large bank holding companies to adopt emission transition plans to reduce financial sector emissions

Bill Text (PDF)

Washington (October 2, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, today announced the reintroduction of the Fossil Free Finance Act. The legislation would require banks to adopt emission transition plans to reduce financial sector emissions and deforestation risks. The legislation is led in the House by Representatives Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Ayanna Pressley (MA-07).

Under this legislation, large bank holding companies would be required to implement plans to reduce financial sector emissions 50 percent by 2035 and reach zero financial sector emissions by 2050. Additionally, it would require banks to discontinue financing for new or expanded fossil fuel projects within 60 days of enactment, immediately discontinue thermal coal financing and facilitation, and eliminate facilitation of deforestation risk commodities. Despite climate-driven wildfires, floods, and other disasters continuing to devastate regions across the country, banks continue to invest in contributing fossil fuel projects. Plans created from this legislation will help the financial sector align with science-based projections for emissions.

“Our economy and global financial systems have a codependent relationship with the fossil fuel industry. We cannot wait for big banks to address the very climate crisis they are financing if we are serious about reducing greenhouse gas emissions and deforestation. It’s like giving an arsonist a hose for one hand while they hold a gas can in the other,” said Senator Markey. “The Fossil Free Finance Act would require our financial institutions, including banks, to protect Americans’ savings, investments, and our economy by addressing the threats posed by climate change. We need to put the planet over profit and get fossil fuels out of our finances.”

“Our financial institutions and banks are funding the pollution of our air and water that make us sicker. They choose to invest billions of dollars in dirty fossil fuel projects,” said Rep. Tlaib. “Instead of acting to protect us, the Federal Reserve allowed these banks to finance the destruction of our planet and our health. I’m taking action with Senator Markey and Congresswoman Pressley to require the Federal Reserve to finally do something and address the dangers of our climate crisis.”

“We should be using every tool available to protect our planet, our people, and our economy, and one way we can do that is by stopping giant banks from financing fossil fuel projects,” said Rep. Pressley. “Our Fossil Free Finance Act would help confront the climate crisis by stopping financial institutions, including our nation’s largest banks, from providing trillions in fossil fuel financing and deepening the health inequities and harms that already plague our communities. I’m grateful to Senator Markey and Congresswoman Tlaib for their ongoing partnership on this bill to take urgent action to help prevent a massive, climate-induced economic collapse.”

“Major US banks’ ongoing finance for fossil fuel expansion is driving worsening climate change and putting the entire financial system and public at risk,” said Alex Martin, Climate Finance Policy Director at Americans for Financial Reform. “The Fossil Free Finance Act would recognize the role that fossil fuel finance plays in driving climate-related financial risk, and require banks to develop climate action plans that address those risks, creating a critical safeguard for the public and the financial system.”

“While financial policymakers around the world actively work to decarbonize their economies, U.S. policymakers have fallen behind, leaving our financial system exposed to the impacts of climate change,” said David Arkush, Director of Public Citizen’s Climate Program. “Financial institutions continue to finance, invest, and underwrite unnecessary projects—creating systemic risks that can reverberate across the economy. Rather than continuing to create risks for the financial system, large and systemically important financial institutions should be required to reduce their financed and facilitated emissions in line with science-driven targets. Neither Congress nor the Federal Reserve should wait for a financial crisis to address climate-related financial risk.”

The Fossil Free Finance Act of 2026 would address climate-related threats to financial stability and help align the financial sector with science-based emissions targets by redefining financial sector emissions, mandating bank holding companies with at least $50 billion in assets to align with science-based emissions targets, and requiring the Federal Reserve to report to Congress on financial sector emissions, commitments by covered institutions, progress toward emissions targets, regulatory gaps, data challenges, and equitable transition needs.

The Fossil Free Finance Act of 2026 is cosponsored by Senators Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.).

The legislation is endorsed by Public Citizen and Americans for Financial Reform.

Senator Markey has consistently worked to hold powerful international institutions accountable for their complicity in the climate crisis.

In April, Senator Markey led his colleagues in requesting that the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations legislation include language that would prohibit the use of taxpayer funds to stop the construction of offshore wind energy facilities.

In November 2024, Senator Markey partnered with Representative Lisa Badum of Germany and Senator Rosa Galvez of Canada to lead over 130 leaders from around the world in sending an open letter during the United Nations global climate conference, COP29, urging world leaders and UN-level negotiators to support an immediate moratorium on the expansion of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) infrastructure worldwide.

In May 2023, Senator Markey and Representative Yvette Clarke (NY-09) announced the reintroduction of the Block All New (BAN) Fossil Fuel Exports Act, legislation that would amend the Energy Policy and Conservation Act and ban the export of American crude oil and natural gas abroad to protect frontline communities from dangerous export infrastructure, prioritize U.S. consumers against fossil fuel profiteering, and help ensure the United States meets its climate and clean energy commitments on the world stage.

Senator Markey, and Representatives Tlaib, Pressley, and former Rep. Mondaire Jones (NY-17) first introduced the Fossil Free Finance Act during the 117th Congress in September 2021. Senator Markey first reintroduced the legislation with Senator Merkley in March 2023.

In October 2022, Senator Markey reintroduced the OPEC Accountability Act, legislation to require the U.S. President to initiate consultations with the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and some non-OPEC countries to reduce crude oil production.

title: Merkley Relaunches Effort to Protect Driver’s Privacy
Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez, Merkley Unveil Ban Flock Act to Protect Americans’ Right to Privacy
text:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 2 — Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) today released the Ban Flock Act, legislation to put an end to the rise in AI-powered surveillance cameras that track Americans across the country. The Ban Flock Act would prohibit federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) and block federal funding from state and local governments that use this technology.

“At a time of growing concern about the unchecked power of artificial intelligence, Flock is eviscerating the very notion of privacy by installing tens of thousands of cameras in communities across America without their consent,” Sanders said. “Going to the doctor? Flock knows. Dropping your kid off at school? Flock is tracking you. Flock is always watching. We cannot allow America to become a surveillance state where a handful of AI oligarchs profit by giving the government the power to track our every movement.”

“Across the country, Big Tech companies like Flock Safety have built a mass surveillance system to harvest Americans’ private and personal data without their consent. AI-powered cameras are keeping track of our every move and weaponizing this data against working people to make record profits. The widespread integration of this technology into American society is unconscionable,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “I am proud to introduce the Ban Flock Act with Senator Sanders to enforce our constitutional right to privacy and protect Americans from both corporate and government surveillance.”

“Your right to privacy includes the freedom to move around your community without every move being monitored,” Merkley said. “Right now, Flock is selling its cameras nationwide, laying the groundwork for a surveillance state while enriching corporate executives. No one should have this unchecked surveillance power at their fingertips, which is why I’m teaming up with Senator Sanders to rein in this dangerous technology.”

Flock is the largest vendor of automatic license plate readers in the United States, with more than 120,000 cameras across the country that scan and record 20 billion vehicles every month. Newer Flock cameras do not just record vehicles — they record people. Flock’s AI system can combine images of you and your vehicle with databases of phone numbers, relatives and court records to find out who you are, where you’re going and why. The company also operates a national lookup tool, so agencies that contract with Flock can access data generated by cameras in another city or state. The national lookup tool searches can turn up massive amounts of information, including physical descriptions, records of an individual’s online accounts and lists of their relatives.

The mass surveillance capabilities enabled by Flock and other automatic license plate reader companies have threatened the civil liberties of everyday Americans:

Flock has shared state information with federal immigration officials;

Law enforcement officials have pulled Flock data to investigate activists and logged searches corresponding to protests against ICE raids, in support of Palestinian rights and for ‘No Kings’ demonstrations; and

Officers have used plate readers to track wives, girlfriends, exes and women they wanted to meet without their consent.

So far this year, at least 56 municipalities have deactivated, cancelled, or rejected contracts with Flock. Congress must act to stop the mass surveillance of citizens.

The Ban Flock Act would do this by:

Prohibiting the federal government from using automatic license plate readers or accessing the information they collect;

Stopping federal grant funding from flowing to state or local governments that use automatic license plate readers or contract with automatic license plate readers companies;

Allowing Americans to sue the federal government for violation of their rights through the use of automatic license plate readers.

title: VIDEO: Senate Democrats Block Senator Moody’s National Fraud Enforcement Division Act
Padilla Conducts Unannounced Oversight Visit of SFO De Facto Immigration Detention Facility
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, conducted an unannounced oversight visit to San Francisco International Airport’s (SFO) de facto Customs and Border Protection (CBP) immigration detention facility.

Following direct inquiries to his office and recent reporting about conditions at the facility, Padilla conducted the unannounced visit to see conditions firsthand and ensure the federal government is meeting its legal and humanitarian obligations to people in its custody.

“No one in our state or country should have to live in fear of this Administration’s cruelty and attacks on immigrants. And yet, there are extremely concerning reports that valid green card holders and other immigrants are being detained at SFO for days on end without access to adequate medical care or legal representation,” said Senator Padilla. “Constituents have reached out to my office with serious concerns about what is happening inside immigration detention facilities, including spaces like the one at SFO, and those concerns demand answers. As a United States Senator, I have a constitutional responsibility to conduct oversight, see these facilities firsthand, and hold the federal government accountable for how it treats people in its custody. Today’s visit was an important step in continuing to shine a light on a cruel and inhumane system enabled by the Trump Administration that operates without transparency or accountability.”

This year, Padilla has made multiple visits to immigration detention facilities across California, including the California City and Otay Mesa detention centers, where he heard directly from people being detained and witnessed abhorrent conditions firsthand. His visits have underscored the importance of congressional oversight at a time when the Trump Administration is rapidly expanding immigration detention with limited transparency and accountability.

Last month, Padilla called out the Trump Administration’s continued abuses of power and inhumane treatment of detained immigrants. He also demanded DHS immediately halt its reckless plan to equip Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers with electric shock gloves.

In June, Padilla and Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) sounded the alarm over the significant increase in deaths among detainees in ICE custody since January 2025, expressing concern over the announcement of the 50th reported death in ICE custody under the Trump Administration. Padilla also condemned Republicans’ partisan bill to provide ICE and CBP with an extra $70 billion without necessary reforms and forced a vote on his amendment that would require ICE officers to wear body cameras while on-duty.

title: Padilla, Kim, Schatz, Schiff Introduce Legislation to Increase Loan Forgiveness for Teachers of English Learners
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced the Supporting Providers of English Language Learning (SPELL) Act to address the national multilingual teacher shortage by increasing loan forgiveness for teachers of English learners (ELs). Representatives Adriano Espaillat (D-N.Y.-13) and Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.-07) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

Currently, if a highly-qualified teacher has been employed for five consecutive years in a low-income school, they are eligible for up to $5,000 of student loan forgiveness. Historically, math, science, and special education teachers have been in high demand, so, to achieve higher recruitment and retention rates, certain teachers who go into these subjects are eligible for an increased benefit of $17,500 of student loan forgiveness. To help address the growing EL teacher shortage, the SPELL Act adds EL teachers to this high demand category, making them eligible for additional debt relief.

“Educating students learning English requires specialized instruction and unique teacher strategies,” said Senator Padilla. “Yet, we are facing a devastating shortage of teachers with the skills needed to support these students. By lessening the financial burden, we can help incentivize a greater number of passionate, and highly qualified teachers to enter and stay in the classroom.”

“Every student deserves a fair chance to succeed and thrive at school; teachers of English Learners are essential to making that possible,” said Senator Kim. “In the face of nationwide teacher shortages and attacks on critical education programs, this legislation would make it possible for more to answer the call to serve in our schools and to help generations of students along the way.”

“A shortage of multilingual teachers means students learning English often don’t have the support they need. By increasing loan forgiveness for these teachers, our bill will help English learners get the high-quality education they deserve,” said Senator Schatz.

“English Learners are among the fastest-growing groups of students in the country, especially in California, and it is crucial that they have qualified, passionate teachers in their classrooms,” said Senator Schiff. “The SPELL Act will encourage more prospective English teachers to pursue that path by ensuring the same loan forgiveness standards as math, science, and special education teachers. I am proud to join Senator Padilla in this effort, and I will continue to work with him to ensure that California’s students and teachers are in a position to succeed.”

ELs are one of the fastest-growing populations in the country and now represent nearly 10 percent of all students enrolled in U.S. public elementary and secondary schools. California has the most ELs in the country, with nearly six million students that identify as ELs. However, the Department of Education has reported that 32 states have a shortage of teachers for EL students, making them unable to meet students’ needs and resulting in a discouraging academic achievement gap for this growing population. The cost of teacher preparation programs can be an obstacle for many to enter the profession, but data shows an association between teachers’ preparation level and their teaching effectiveness and retention. Research demonstrates that loan forgiveness programs are successful at encouraging teachers to take positions in fields and at locations where they are most needed, and forgiveness programs also help to support retention.

Specifically, the bill would provide up to $17,500 in loan forgiveness for teachers of ELs, bilingual students, and/or dual language immersion students. This matches the same level of enhanced forgiveness available to math, science, and special education teachers.

The SPELL Act is endorsed by organizations including TESOL, AFT, UnidosUS, and the California Community Colleges.

“The SPELL Act recognizes the specialized preparation and expertise required to teach English learners, bilingual students, and students in dual language programs,” said TESOL International Association. “More than five million English learners attend our public schools, yet many states face shortages of the teachers prepared to serve them. By expanding student loan forgiveness and cancellation for these professionals, the SPELL act will help make this vital career more attainable and support schools and states in recruiting and retaining qualified educators. TESOL International Association is proud to support Senator Padilla’s introduction of the SPELL Act.”

“At a time when the Trump administration seems intent on attacking English language learners, public school educators continue to fulfill their mission to serve each and every child who comes through their classroom door,” said AFT President Randi Weingarten. “ELL teachers have dedicated their lives to helping kids, but student debt and the cost of living are dragging them down. The Supporting Providers of English Language Learning Act would allow ELL teachers to qualify for the highest level of Teacher Loan Forgiveness so they can pursue their careers free from the specter of permanent student debt.”

“To prepare students to succeed in school and beyond, they should have access early on to bilingual educators who understand their language, culture, and learning needs. Yet schools across the country continue to face shortages of bilingual and English learner teachers,” said Carmen M. Feliciano, Vice President of Policy and Advocacy, UnidosUS. “The SPELL Act is a commonsense investment in strengthening that workforce by expanding student loan relief for educators who dedicate their careers to serving English learners and students in bilingual and dual-language programs. UnidosUS applauds Senator Padilla for championing this legislation and helping remove financial barriers to entering and remaining in the teaching profession. By investing in these educators, we are investing in the success of millions of English learners and in a stronger, more representative teacher workforce.”

Padilla has been a leading advocate for increasing access to education, fighting back against the Trump Administration’s continued assault on the Education Department. Last month, Padilla reintroduced the Basic Assistance for Students In College (BASIC) Act to help higher education institutions address unmet basic needs of their students. Padilla also joined Senator Ben Ray Lujan (D-N.M) in reintroducing the Loan Forgiveness for Educators Act, legislation that would expand and modernize the federal loan forgiveness program for educators. This legislation would help address educator shortages and increase children’s access to a diverse and well-prepared educator workforce by strengthening the federal Teacher Loan Forgiveness (TLF) Program. In June, Padilla led Senate colleagues in condemning the Trump Administration’s attacks on English learners and the dissolution of the Department of Education’s Office of English Language Acquisition (OELA).

title: After Delivering $3.25M Federal Investment, Reed & Town Leaders Celebrate Critical Coventry Sewer Upgrade
text:
COVENTRY, RI – Not a lot of people talk about their sewage or septic system…until it stops working. Making investments in modern wastewater systems is critical to protecting the environment, public health, and clean water.

In an effort to expand the reach of Coventry’s sewer system and replace the high school’s obsolete wastewater system to better serve local students and residents, U.S. Senator Jack Reed delivered a $3.25 million federal earmark for Coventry to extend its sewer line and connect it to Coventry High School to protect local water quality and help save town resources.

Senator Reed joined Coventry Town Manager Daniel Parrillo, Jr., Council Vice President Frank Brown, School Superintendent Don Cowart, and other local leaders to celebrate the upgrades and discuss the importance of modern water systems to safeguarding the environment and enhancing local water quality.

“Today, we celebrate the sweet smell of success. Or more accurately, the smell that no longer lingers! The High School’s outdated wastewater system clearly needed to be replaced, and I was proud to deliver a $3.25 million federal earmark to get the job done for students, teachers, and local residents,” said Senator Reed, a leading member of the Appropriations Committee. “This critical sewer extension not only better serves the High School, helps keep the groundwater clean, and saves critical Town tax dollars. It will also allow for residents along Reservoir Avenue to connect with the sewer system down the line to increase the environmental benefits from this project by replacing other outdated septic systems in the neighborhood.”

“The Town of Coventry thanks Senator Reed for his leadership and commitment to our residents and students in securing this $3.25 million grant to replace the Coventry High School sewer line. This critical upgrade to our infrastructure will not only benefit the high school, but the residents and businesses in the surrounding area who will now have the opportunity to tie in to the line and make their property more valuable,” said Coventry Town Manager Daniel Parrillo, Jr. “This project would not have happened without Senator Reed’s investment in Coventry and we look forward to working with him on more projects in the future.”

Coventry High School currently enrolls approximately 1,200 students and includes the CHS Regional Career Center which welcomes students from nearby communities for vocational education opportunities.

Now complete, the new sewer line extension on Reservoir Road replaces the school’s failing wastewater treatment system that was built in 1973, eliminating a potentially serious source of environmental pollution, safeguarding local water quality, and reducing pollution risks within the Narragansett Bay watershed.

Before this upgrade, the school’s outdated wastewater system had become inoperable. Serving as a sewage holding tank, the outdated system required daily transfers to the Cranston Wastewater Treatment Facility and resulted in significant costs for the Town.

The new 3,400-foot extension will also allow for new connections for homes along Reservoir Road in the future, eliminating septic systems which can also be a source of groundwater pollution. Approximately 35 properties will have connection access to the new sewer extension funded by Reed’s earmark.

title: RI Delegation Announces $9.1 Million to Boost Public Safety & Support Local Law Enforcement
text:

title: Senator Ricketts Applauds Implementation of His Streamlining Rural Housing Act

title: Sens. Rick Scott, Ashley Moody Introduce Bill to Maintain Military Readiness in the Gulf of America
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ashley Moody introduced the Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act to protect the critical Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range (EGTTR) from interference that could otherwise hamper the U.S. Department of War’s (DOW) ability to maintain military readiness in the Gulf of America.

Senator Rick Scott said, “The federal government’s first priority is to keep the American people safe. That means our military needs the irreplaceable value that the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range provides to our warfighters. Protecting the range means protecting America’s military readiness. I am glad to have Sen. Moody’s support on this bill, and I look forward to working with President Trump and his administration to use every tool we have to deliver more abundant, cheap energy while ensuring our military remains the most lethal fighting force on earth.”

Senator Ashley Moody said, “The Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range is a national military asset that can't be replicated anywhere else in the country, and the work done there directly shapes the lethality of our future military. I'm proud to join Senator Scott on the Protecting Florida's Offshore Military Readiness Act to keep the range as exactly what it was intended to be – a testing ground. Protecting Eglin is about our national security, and it's about preserving the Gulf Coast Floridians love.”

BACKGROUND:

In an effort to expand American energy dominance and lower the cost of living, the U.S. Department of the Interior has recently been identifying potential lease sales for drilling in areas of the Gulf of America that are currently held in a moratorium from the first Trump administration to keep the EGTTR active.

The EGTTR is a key national security asset that provides the U.S. military with vital air, sea, and joint testing and training capabilities. Unleashing American energy production can be done without compromising this unique military resource. Codifying President Trump’s previous protections for the range allows for uninterrupted access for critical operations and ensures America’s armed forces remain prepared to respond to emerging threats.

title: Rosen, Budd Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Cybersecurity Readiness and Workforce Development
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV), ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, and Ted Budd (R-NC) introduced a bill to strengthen the United States’ cybersecurity readiness and workforce development nationwide. The Cyber Centers of Excellence Partnership Act would establish a partnership between the Department of Defense and universities designated by the National Security Agency as National Centers of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity, creating opportunities to share research, best practices, and emerging approaches between the public and private sectors. This program would not only increase collaboration between top research institutions and our specialized military cyber units, but also create direct pathways for qualified students into federal cybersecurity careers.

“As technological advancements become more heavily integrated into modern warfare, it is more important than ever that our nation has the talent and personnel needed to handle looming threats,” said Senator Rosen. “This bipartisan bill would ensure that our military and top universities can keep up with every wave of ever-changing cyber threats, while also attracting the country’s most talented young minds and bolstering our cyber-ready workforce.”

“American military dominance depends on our nation’s ability to operate in cyberspace, making it essential to maintain a robust cybersecurity workforce. I’m proud to work across the aisle with Senator Rosen to strengthen the pipeline of cyber talent by establishing programs where students in our nation’s NSA-designated Centers of Academic Excellence can get real-world experience conducting critical cyber operations in defense of our homeland,” said Senator Budd.

“UNLV’s sustained recognition as a National Center of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity (NCAE-C) underscores our dedication to cutting-edge research, hands-on training, and real-world defense. The Cyber Center of Excellence Partnership Act introduced by Senator Jacky Rosen and Senator Ted Budd creates a vital bridge between our academic rigor and the Department of Defense’s operational missions,” said Rama Venkat, Dean of the University of Nevada, Las Vegas College of Engineering. By leveraging existing programs such as our CyberCorps Scholarship for Service (SFS) initiative, this legislation will accelerate recruitment, eliminate onboarding barriers for federal service, and empower UNLV students to defend the nation’s digital ecosystem.”

As the first and only computer programmer to serve in the U.S. Senate, Senator Rosen understands how important cybersecurity is for our national security. In March, she introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation to support and expand apprenticeship programs in cybersecurity. Last year, she introduced bipartisan legislation to strengthen the cybersecurity of the U.S.’s health care system. She also helped introduce bipartisan legislation to protect sensitive federal data from adversarial nations like the People’s Republic of China.

title: Rounds Calls for Federal Gas and Diesel Tax Suspension to Lower Prices at Pump, President Trump to Invoke Defense Production Act
text:
PIERRE – Senator Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) called for a suspension of the federal gas and diesel tax for 90 days in a letter today to President Donald Trump. Additionally, Rounds asked states to consider suspending their own gas and diesel taxes. This would temporarily save consumers on average 60 cents per gallon on diesel fuel and 52 cents per gallon on gasoline. To offset the loss of revenue to the Highway Trust Fund, Congress can consider authorizing a one-time transfer from the General Fund. Rounds also urged President Trump to consider using his authority under the Defense Production Act to help domestic refineries expand their capacity, including refining capacity that is already online.

“The prices at the pump are being driven by a global shortage of refining capacity,” wrote Rounds. “Americans feel the impact of this refining bottleneck every time they fill up at the pump, but farmers can’t stop their tractors and combines in the middle of harvest, and truckers can’t quit running their routes. We need to act now to bring down the price of diesel. The solution is one that you have promoted since your first Administration: unleash American energy dominance.”

“Broader regulatory changes will of course take time. What we can and should do right now is explore suspending the federal gas tax through the end of the year to give Americans immediate relief,” continued Rounds. “The federal gas tax is 24.4 cents per gallon on diesel fuel and 18.4 cents per gallon on gasoline…Those savings would make a huge difference for the American people.”

Read the full text of the letter HERE or below.

+++

Dear President Trump:

I write to urge you to use your authority under the Defense Production Act to help domestic refineries expand their capacity. Democrats are telling the American people that the conflict with Iran is the sole cause of high fuel costs and that, if the conflict ended today, fuel prices would magically plummet tomorrow. As you know, that is false. Oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. The prices at the pump are being driven by a global shortage of refining capacity—a weakness in the global fuel supply chain that we should start addressing here at home.

Severe refining deficits across Russia and the Middle East have left the United States and China as the last major refining powers standing. Americans feel the impact of this refining bottleneck every time they fill up at the pump, but farmers can’t stop their tractors and combines in the middle of harvest, and truckers can’t quit running their routes. We need to act now to bring down the price of diesel. The solution is one that you have promoted since your first Administration: unleash American energy dominance. In this case, that means invoking the Defense Production Act to expand domestic refining capacity.

Your authority under the Defense Production Act is tied to national defense, which Congress defined to include “programs” for “energy production or construction.” The Act authorizes you to prioritize contracts relating to “materials, equipment, and services” in order to “expand . . . refining” and to “provide for the modification or expansion of privately owned facilities.” You also have the authority to incentivize domestic refinery expansion through loans and loan guarantees, subsidy payments, and purchase commitments. Together, these authorities can be wielded as powerful tools to expand refining capacity, including refining capacity that is already online. We won’t see the results overnight, but the sooner we start, the better.

More broadly, we need to ease permitting requirements and cut through the other bureaucratic red tape obstructing American fuel production. As we clear these regulatory logjams, we also need to confront the bigger question of why no new major refinery has opened in the United States since the 1970s. Oil and gas companies are understandably hesitant to invest billions in new refineries when a change in the political winds could spell disaster. After all, onerous regulations and high compliance costs in California, a notoriously oil-and-gas-unfriendly state, recently forced two refineries to close. We need laws and policies that give oil and gas companies confidence to invest in large-scale refineries here at home, not regulations that stifle the industry.

These broader regulatory changes will of course take time. What we can and should do right now is explore suspending the federal gas tax through the end of the year to give Americans immediate relief. The federal gas tax is 24.4 cents per gallon on diesel fuel and 18.4 cents per gallon on gasoline. To offset the loss of revenue to the Highway Trust Fund, Congress can consider authorizing a one-time transfer from the General Fund. I also strongly encourage States to consider suspending, or at the very least reducing, their own gas taxes. The average State gas tax is 35.5 cents per gallon on diesel fuel and 33.3 cents per gallon on gasoline. Suspending both federal and State gas taxes would amount to an average savings of 60 cents per gallon on diesel fuel and 52 cents per gallon on gasoline. Those savings would make a huge difference for the American people.

Please let me know how I can be of assistance. I greatly appreciate your consideration.

###

title: NEWS: Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez, Merkley Unveil Ban Flock Act to Protect Americans’ Right to Privacy
text:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 2 — Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) today released the Ban Flock Act, legislation to put an end to the rise in AI-powered surveillance cameras that track Americans across the country. The Ban Flock Act would prohibit federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) and block federal funding from state and local governments that use this technology.

“At a time of growing concern about the unchecked power of artificial intelligence, Flock is eviscerating the very notion of privacy by installing tens of thousands of cameras in communities across America without their consent,” Sanders said. “Going to the doctor? Flock knows. Dropping your kid off at school? Flock is tracking you. Flock is always watching. We cannot allow America to become a surveillance state where a handful of AI oligarchs profit by giving the government the power to track our every movement.”

“Across the country, Big Tech companies like Flock Safety have built a mass surveillance system to harvest Americans’ private and personal data without their consent. AI-powered cameras are keeping track of our every move and weaponizing this data against working people to make record profits. The widespread integration of this technology into American society is unconscionable,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “I am proud to introduce the Ban Flock Act with Senator Sanders to enforce our constitutional right to privacy and protect Americans from both corporate and government surveillance.”

“Your right to privacy includes the freedom to move around your community without every move being monitored,” Merkley said. “Right now, Flock is selling its cameras nationwide, laying the groundwork for a surveillance state while enriching corporate executives. No one should have this unchecked surveillance power at their fingertips, which is why I’m teaming up with Senator Sanders to rein in this dangerous technology.”

Flock is the largest vendor of automatic license plate readers in the United States, with more than 120,000 cameras across the country that scan and record 20 billion vehicles every month. Newer Flock cameras do not just record vehicles — they record people. Flock’s AI system can combine images of you and your vehicle with databases of phone numbers, relatives and court records to find out who you are, where you’re going and why. The company also operates a national lookup tool, so agencies that contract with Flock can access data generated by cameras in another city or state. The national lookup tool searches can turn up massive amounts of information, including physical descriptions, records of an individual’s online accounts and lists of their relatives.

The mass surveillance capabilities enabled by Flock and other automatic license plate reader companies have threatened the civil liberties of everyday Americans:

Flock has shared state information with federal immigration officials;

Law enforcement officials have pulled Flock data to investigate activists and logged searches corresponding to protests against ICE raids, in support of Palestinian rights and for ‘No Kings’ demonstrations; and

Officers have used plate readers to track wives, girlfriends, exes and women they wanted to meet without their consent.

So far this year, at least 56 municipalities have deactivated, cancelled, or rejected contracts with Flock. Congress must act to stop the mass surveillance of citizens.

The Ban Flock Act would do this by:

Prohibiting the federal government from using automatic license plate readers or accessing the information they collect;

Stopping federal grant funding from flowing to state or local governments that use automatic license plate readers or contract with automatic license plate readers companies;

Allowing Americans to sue the federal government for violation of their rights through the use of automatic license plate readers.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla, Bennet, Ansari, Hickenlooper, Luján Introduce Legislation to Protect Public Lands and Taxpayers from Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.), joined U.S. Senators Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) and U.S. Representative Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) to introduce the Stop Orphaned Wells Act, legislation that would prevent oil and gas companies from abandoning oil wells on public lands, a practice that shifts well cleanup costs from oil and gas companies to the American taxpayer.

“Oil companies can’t just walk away from abandoned oil and gas wells and leave taxpayers to bear the cleanup costs,” said Schiff. “I’m joining Senator Bennet and other colleagues to make sure that Big Oil is responsible for cleaning up their messes. Americans should not have to deal with the consequences of an oil company’s negligence.”

“Across California, there are over 5,000 orphaned oil wells that pose a threat to the health and safety of our communities and the environment,” said Padilla. “When wells are left abandoned, drinking water is polluted, greenhouse gases are emitted, and the climate crisis is accelerated. This bill will help ensure orphaned oil and gas wells are plugged so Californians and communities across the country are protected from toxic emissions and contaminated air and water.”

“For too long, taxpayers have footed the bill to clean up abandoned wells after companies walk away from their responsibilities,” said Bennet. “As the Trump administration moves to weaken the safeguards that hold companies accountable, Congress must protect taxpayers and the public lands that power Colorado’s outdoor economy, while making sure oil and gas companies pay the cost of cleanup, rather than Colorado’s future generations.”

“Trump asked oil and gas executives to bankroll his campaign with a $1 billion contribution in exchange for a big payback. Meanwhile, Americans are left footing the bill for the damage they leave behind,” said Ansari. “Orphaned wells threaten our water, wildlife, and air. I’m proud to lead the effort alongside Senator Bennet to make the oil and gas industry clean up its own mess. Our bill would ensure oil and gas companies pay to clean up the wells they abandon.”

“Abandoned wells put Colorado communities in danger,” said Hickenlooper. “As Governor, we capped as many of these wells as we could, and that work continues here in the Senate, where we’re protecting taxpayers from getting stuck with the bill. Capping wells creates jobs and lowers pollution. It’s a win-win.”

“In New Mexico and across the country, abandoned wells pose serious environmental harm and threaten the health of our communities,” said Luján. “We must ensure that oil and gas companies are held accountable and that taxpayers are not on the hook for the cost of cleanup. I’ve long fought to address abandoned wells, including championing the REGROW Act that was passed into law, and continue to work to ensure we identify and plug the thousands of abandoned wells nationwide. That’s why I’m cosponsoring this legislation to prevent companies from abandoning their wells and help reduce the number of abandoned wells in New Mexico and across the country.”

“When an oil and gas company goes bankrupt, New Mexicans shouldn’t be the ones left to pick up the tab for cleanup costs,” said Heinrich. “Right now, the Trump administration is making it easier for these companies to walk away without enough money set aside to clean up their wells. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act ensures that companies set aside money to meet their cleanup responsibilities, so taxpayers aren’t left paying the bill.”

Until 2024 when the Biden administration added agency rules, oil and gas fiscal assurance requirements were minimal, leading companies to abandon wells instead of remediating the land after drilling. The Trump administration is now rolling back these essential protections for public lands and American taxpayers. Nationwide, there are currently over 140,000 documented orphaned wells, including more than 15,000 on federal lands, and hundreds of thousands more that may be orphaned. Additionally, the number of documented orphaned wells in the United States has more than doubled since 2020. These sites are not only a significant liability for taxpayers and a growing threat to water resources, air quality,wildlife habitat, and private lands, but also jeopardize public health, ecosystems, grazing lands, outdoor recreation sites, and cultural resources that are at high risk from contamination.

In Colorado alone, there are nearly 1,400 orphaned wells, with almost a third of these wells on federal or Tribal lands. Estimates from Colorado’s Energy & Carbon Management Commission predict that it could cost over $36 million to clean up all of the existing orphaned wells on federal and Tribal lands in Colorado. Moreover, there are currently 245 idled federal wells in Colorado that have the potential to eventually become orphaned, which could cost taxpayers approximately $23 million to remediate. Due to new leasing policies enacted by Congress in 2025, executive orders to increase federal oil and gas drilling, and the financial assurance rollback, industry is likely to drill as many as 3.8 million wells on national public lands in the coming years, and to then pass as much as $753 billion in potential financial liabilities back onto local communities and taxpayers.

The Stop Orphaned Wells Act builds on Bennet’s Oil and Gas Bonding Reform and Orphaned Well Remediation Act and recent state-level reforms in Colorado, New Mexico, Texas, and Utah to fix this broken system and close long-standing industry loopholes around orphaned wells. This legislation would ensure operators, not taxpayers, pay for cleanups and aligns directly with the interests of Western voters, nearly 9 in 10 of whom believe oil and gas companies should cover reclamation costs once drilling ends.

“In La Plata County, orphaned wells are a nuisance for property owners and a danger for people and animals alike. This bill builds on Colorado’s innovative work to ensure that federal regulation protects our communities, livestock, and wildlife – and prevents this public health issue from happening in the first place,” said Marsha Porter-Norton, La Plata County Commissioner.

“The Board of County Commissioners strongly supports Senator Bennet’s Stop Orphaned Wells Act. When a well is abandoned, local communities must shoulder the risks to their health, environment, and taxpayer dollars. This legislation provides the accountability needed to ensure oil and gas companies, not our community, pay to restore the lands they use,” said Jody Shadduck-McNally, Larimer County Commissioner and Chair of the Board of County Commissioners.

“Adams County is glad to see Senator Bennet leading the charge on this significant bipartisan issue, as it is of critical importance to our communities. Our county has the second highest number of orphaned wells in the state; taking action to preserve the health and safety of both our residents and our environment is a top priority for our Board. We look forward to working with the Senator in honing this legislation to be as helpful and effective as possible,” said Commissioner Julie Duran Mullica, Chair of the Adams County Board of Commissioners.

“Like countless places across the country, San Miguel County has been forced to clean up after reckless operators. Orphaned wells are not only an unfair burden on our taxpayers but also a dangerous polluter of our beloved natural resources and public lands. Senator Bennet’s bill takes long-overdue actions to strengthen regulations and hold irresponsible companies accountable,” said Galena Gleason, San Miguel County Commissioner.

“The Stop Orphaned Wells Act is urgently needed in Western Colorado, where orphaned, non-producing wells irresponsibly emit harmful methane gas and harm our health, air and water quality, and critical wildlife habitat. This Act will finally make producers responsible for properly closing, remediating, and reclaiming lands after they stop producing oil and gas,” said Lynn Padgett, Ouray County Commissioner.

Bennet has consistently worked to deliver funding to clean up abandoned orphaned wells to keep communities safe and to strengthen bonding requirements to hold companies accountable for future cleanup. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act builds on Bennet’s previous legislation introduced in July, 2021, the Oil and Gas Bonding Reform and Orphaned Well Remediation Act, which would restore the public’s vital role in shaping oil and gas leasing decisions on public lands. In August 2026, Bennet and U.S. Representative Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) led their Democratic colleagues to oppose the recent rescission of two key Bureau of Land Management oil and gas rules on leasing and waste prevention. In November 2025, Bennet joinedSenators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Hickenlooper, and Luján to urge U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum and Bureau of Land Management Acting Director Bill Groffy to maintain the federal oil and gas bonding requirements in the 2024 Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing Rule to hold developers accountable for the costs of site cleanup on federal lands. In July 2023, Bennet issued a statement after the U.S. Department of Interior released a proposed rule that includes oil and gas bonding reform for wells drilled on public lands. In July 2023 and December 2022, Bennet sent letters to the Biden administration urging them to finish the work envisioned in his bill by reforming our antiquated oil and gas bonding system. In August 2022, Bennet and Hickenlooper welcomed $25 million in grant funds from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to create jobs cleaning up orphaned oil and gas wells across Colorado.

This legislation is supported by 20 organizations, including Earthjustice Action, Colorado Fiscal Institute, Conservatives for Responsible Stewardship, Conservation Colorado, Montana Wildlife Federation, National Parks Conservation Association, Natural Resources Defense Council, Nevada Wildlife Federation, New Mexico Wildlife Federation, Public Land Solutions, Rocky Mountain Wild, San Juan Citizen’s Alliance, Sierra Club, Taxpayers for Common Sense, Trout Unlimited, Western Colorado Alliance, Western Organization of Resource Councils, Western Resilience Center, Wild Montana, Wilderness Workshop, and The Wilderness Society. In addition, this legislation was endorsed by U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.
