title: READ: In The Bakersfield Californian, Sen. Schiff Condemns Trump Administration’s Targeting of the Sikh Community
text:
Schiff: “We must stand up for our neighbors — the Sikh workers, students and families who are at risk from this rhetoric and these harmful policies.”

Read the fullop-edhere.

Bakersfield, CA — U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), published an op-ed in The Bakersfield Californian condemning the Trump administration’s policies and rhetoric that have fueled the uptick in targeted hate and violence against Sikh Americans.

In his op-ed, Schiff points to the recent escalating and alarming actions across the nation, including the recent stabbing of a Sikh truck driver from Sacramento at a Wyoming rest area, the recent openly discriminatory social media posts by the Department of Homeland Security, and the tightening of requirements for non-domiciled Commercial Driver’s Licenses — a targeted attempt to deprive members of the Sikh community of their livelihoods.

“The most powerful tool in our arsenal to combat this hatred is one we can all use — our voices. Speaking up forced the administration to remove some of the racist posts that fuel the kind of violence we witnessed in Wyoming. Let’s keep speaking out. On behalf of the Sikh community, the Latino community, the Haitian community, and every other community in America that has become the target of choice for dehumanization by this administration. I stand with the Sikh community. And I ask you to join me,” Senator Schiff wrote.

Background: Earlier this year, Schiff traveled to Bakersfield specifically to meet with Sikh truck drivers, businesses, and community members to talk about the ongoing threat of losing their commercial driver’s license (CDLs) and the impact this has on their livelihoods, community, and local economies. Schiff expands more on this in his op-ed.

Schiff also led 21 colleagues in urging the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) to restore $160 million in FY2027 National Highway Performance Program funds to California – critical transportation funding that was withheld following the state delaying the cancellation of 17,000 commercial driver’s licenses.

Read the full op-ed here and below:

The Bakersfield Californian: SEN. ADAM SCHIFF: The Sikh community and the tragic consequences of a policy born of bigotry

By U.S. Senator Adam Schiff

California is fortunate to have a thriving community of Sikh Americans who have helped our state flourish: building businesses, shaping California’s booming agriculture industry, holding leadership positions in civil service, and so much more. But while their contributions are woven into the fabric of America, this community has also confronted dangerous hate in the place they call home. One terrible tragedy, driven by such hate, just took place.

Just days ago, a Sikh truck driver from Sacramento was stabbed repeatedly in the bathroom of a Wyoming rest area. This violence came just four days after President Trump’s Department of Homeland Security shared a now-deleted social media post that painted the entire Sikh community as a threat — telling them to “self-deport or find out.” The post was abhorrent, and the link to real violence against the Sikh community is hard to dispute.

In a country founded on the ideal that “all men are created equal,” the Trump White House and DHS have turned starkly away from our Founders’ vision. They have implemented policies that deny Sikh Americans opportunities to earn an honest living and applied pressure and provocative rhetoric to deliberately target and hurt this community.

And now, more than half a million Sikh Americans are scared — looking over their shoulders on the street or afraid to show up for work because of the dangerous environment that these policies and practices have created.

The Trump administration has pushed an agenda that is openly xenophobic. The DHS website urged citizens to report undocumented drivers, while displaying an image of a Sikh man, as if people could look into the cab of a truck and identify whether someone was a citizen or not. The plain implication was that if someone was Sikh, they should be presumed to be violating the law and be reported.

In addition to these hateful practices, the administration has used other punitive measures to discriminate against the Sikh community. In January 2025, DHS rescinded restrictions limiting immigration enforcement at “protected areas.” This change exposed Sikh gurdwaras, and other houses of worship, to Immigration and Customs Enforcement surveillance and arrests — potentially chilling religious expression and practice.

The administration then decided to tighten requirements for non-domiciled Commercial Driver’s Licenses — a targeted attempt to deprive members of the Sikh community of their livelihoods. And when California did not capitulate to the federal government’s unreasonable demand to cancel thousands of CDLs — many of which impact Sikh drivers — the administration threatened to withhold $160 million in federal funds. Yet, the U.S. Department of Transportation’s own data shows that these drivers have a better safety record than most other drivers. None of this is about safety.

In a meeting with Sikh truck drivers in Bakersfield, Sikh leaders told me that community members have been hit hard by the administration’s policy and political attacks on their community.

“We’re actually more afraid now and subject to more abuse now than we were after 9/11,” a community member confided in me. In the aftermath of that deadly attack on America, the Sikh community — which played no role in the attacks — experienced terrible hatred and discrimination. Twenty-five years later, the community feels even more under siege as a result of the rhetoric directed against it by leaders in the highest positions of our government. This is un-American and unacceptable.

In our nation’s 250 years, we have battled this kind of hostility and prejudice before. We have taken on institutional policies that reinforced it. And in this moment, we must look to that history as we confront a new variation on an old hatred. We must stand up for our neighbors — the Sikh workers, students and families who are at risk from this rhetoric and these harmful policies.

The most powerful tool in our arsenal to combat this hatred is one we can all use — our voices. Speaking up forced the administration to remove some of the racist posts that fuel the kind of violence we witnessed in Wyoming. Let’s keep speaking out. On behalf of the Sikh community, the Latino community, the Haitian community, and every other community in America that has become the target of choice for dehumanization by this administration.

I stand with the Sikh community. And I ask you to join me.

title: Senate passes Sen. Scott’s resolution designating September 2026 as Childhood Cancer Awareness Month
text:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Senate unanimously passed Senator Tim Scott’s (R-S.C.) resolution designating September 2026 as National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month. The resolution recognizes the human toll of childhood cancer and pledges to make its prevention and cure a public health priority.

“No child or their family should face the fight against cancer alone,” said Sen Scott. “Children should be focused on learning, growing, and following their dreams, yet these patients face their diagnosis every day with incredible strength and courage. title: ICYMI: In New Editorial, The Eagle-Tribune Calls for Passage of Shaheen’s INSULIN Act, Underscoring Legislation’s Broad Bipartisan Support
text:
(Washington, DC) – In a new editorial titled, “Our View: Politicians can at least agree on insulin price caps,” New Hampshire’s The Eagle-Tribune editorial board expressed its strong support for the INSULIN Act, legislation championed by U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Co-Chair of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus, to cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35. The editorial argues that Shaheen’s legislation is a commonsense step Congress can take to protect Americans from being forced to shell out thousands of dollars a year for insulin, and that passage of the bill would be a chance for lawmakers to prove that Congress is still able to deliver bipartisan solutions for the American people.

Shaheen’s bipartisan INSULIN Act would cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 a month for all Americans with insurance, expanding the effective price cap for Americans on Medicare. Currently, a majority of states do not have a $35 a month cap on insulin costs. Shaheen’s INSULIN Act would immediately change that, lowering prices for millions and ensuring that the state one lives in doesn’t determine whether they can afford their life-saving insulin. The Eagle-Tribune’s editorial comes as momentum continues to build for the INSULIN Act, with both Senate Democrats and Republicans expressing their support for the legislation in Washington last week.

Click HERE to read the editorial in The Eagle-Tribune. The text of the piece has been provided below.

Our View: Politicians can at least agree on insulin price caps

Congress has a chance to show at least a small bit of bipartisanship by supporting New Hampshire Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s proposal to make insulin affordable for all Americans.

The so-called INSULIN Act, of which Shaheen is the lead sponsor, would cap insulin costs at $35 for a month’s supply.

Insulin is already $35 a month for those on Medicare, thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022.

Shaheen’s bill would extend that cap to those who carry private insurance. It would also launch a pilot program in 10 states that would cap insulin costs for uninsured patients.

The measure would bring some clarity and fairness to the millions of Americans who use the drug to treat their diabetes. Currently, how much you pay depends on how good your insurance is. If you are on Medicare, or you have decent insurance, the cost tops out at $35. If you don’t, you’re often left guessing. It shouldn’t be a crapshoot.

To its credit, New Hampshire is one of 29 states that has price caps on insulin for those with commercial insurance. A 30-day supply of insulin in the Granite State costs $30. In Massachusetts, the cap is set at $25.

It makes sense: There is no reason for the cost of insulin to be so high, other than profiteering. Those who need the drug to treat their diabetes have no other option than to use insulin. That allows all manner of jockeying among pharmaceutical companies to squeeze all the profit they can out of the drug, which was first developed a century ago.

Without the cap, and without decent insurance, the cost of insulin can run into thousands of dollars a year.

“This is just really overwhelming to have to think about living with this disease for the rest of my life,” Auburn, New Hampshire, 17-year-old Portia Joy said at a Nashua forum organized by Shaheen last month. “And I’m contemplating if I’m going to be able to afford the medicine that I need to live.”

It’s a dilemma faced by many Americans.

“This is not only the right thing to do,” Shaheen said of her bill, “but it’s an opportunity for us to provide some relief for so many families who are really struggling with high costs.”

The bill has a better chance than most of passing in an increasingly divided Congress. Fourteen Republican senators, including Susan Collins of Maine, have signed on in support of the proposal.

“I don’t know why it should divide Republicans,” Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Missouri, told Politico. “Who is in favor of allowing these pharma companies to rip off people with high insulin prices when there is no supply issue or production issue?”

Still, the bill remains a long shot as the November midterm elections approach. The measure has yet to make it to the floor, and there is no House version in the works.

And this wouldn’t bankrupt pharmaceutical companies. Eli Lilly, for example, agreed last year to cap what it charges for insulin.

“Lilly was the first company to cap what patients pay at $35 per month for all of our insulins, and has been working for years to reduce insulin out-of-pocket costs for people with diabetes, against the headwind of those that benefit from rebates and choose higher list-price medicines over lower-priced options,” company spokesperson Jared Shapiro told Politico.

If a drug company can cap the price of insulin, why can’t the federal government?

###

title: Ranking Member Shaheen and Senate Democratic Members Publish New Report on U.S. Commitment to Afghan Allies, Call for Immediate Resumption of Afghan SIV Program
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, along with U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-DE), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and Jacky Rosen (D-NV), published a comprehensive new report this week detailing the history and importance of the Afghan Special Immigrant Visa (SIV) program, the sacrifices made by Afghans who served alongside U.S. troops and diplomats and the consequences of the Trump Administration’s actions to dismantle protections for our allies.

Commissioned by U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, the report underscores America’s longstanding commitment to the Afghans who risked their lives and the lives of their families in service to the U.S. mission in Afghanistan. Since 2014, more than 160,000 Afghan SIV recipients and their family members have safely resettled in the United States. The report finds that the SIV program has not only provided a lifeline to Afghans targeted by the Taliban for their service to the United States but has also supported U.S. national security by demonstrating to current and future partners that America keeps its promises.

The 69-page report, titled “Standing Strong with Our Afghan Allies: The Imperative of Continuing the Afghan Special Immigrant Visa Program to Uphold Our Commitment to Afghan Allies,” traces the bipartisan history of the Afghan SIV program, highlights the stories of Afghan allies and the American service members who depended on them and details the extensive security screening and vetting that applicants undergo. It also documents the systematic effort by the second Trump Administration to dismantle the SIV program and other protections for Afghans, including suspending refugee admissions, ending relocation assistance, dismantling the State Department office responsible for coordinating Afghan relocation efforts and terminating Temporary Protected Status for Afghans.

“For nearly two decades, the Afghan Special Immigrant Visa program has reflected a bipartisan commitment to stand by the Afghans who stood with us in our hour of need,” said Ranking Member Shaheen. “These allies were essential to our mission in Afghanistan, and the Taliban targeted them precisely because of their service to the United States. For years, Republicans and Democrats understood that keeping our word to these allies was a bipartisan matter of American credibility and national security. But the Trump Administration has chosen to politicize a program that has enjoyed strong bipartisan support since its inception. Turning our backs on people who risked their lives alongside American service members does not make America safer, stronger or more prosperous. In fact, it sends exactly the wrong message to anyone we may ask to stand with us in the future. This report provides an objective accounting of the Afghan SIV program—its successes, its shortcomings and the lessons we must carry forward. From Vietnam to Iraq to Afghanistan, the United States has relied on local partners to advance our national security, and we will undoubtedly need to do so again. Our allies and adversaries alike are watching to see whether America keeps its word.”

The report details the bipartisan origins of the Afghan SIV program, including the passage of the Afghan Allies Protection Act in 2009, led by Senators Shaheen and John McCain, which established a pathway to permanent resident status for qualifying Afghans who served the United States and faced serious threats because of that service. Since 2014, Congress has repeatedly authorized additional visas to continue the program but failed to do so in 2025.

Key findings and takeaways from the report include:

Afghan allies were essential to the U.S. mission and put themselves and their families at extraordinary risk. Afghan interpreters, translators, engineers, security contractors, intelligence partners, administrative staff and drivers worked alongside U.S. troops and diplomats throughout two decades of war. Many joined American troops in combat, provided intelligence and helped U.S. personnel navigate local communities. Their work made them targets for Taliban threats, kidnappings and killings.

The Afghan SIV program has successfully brought more than 160,000 Afghan allies and their families to safety. Since 2014, more than 160,000 Afghan SIV holders and their eligible family members have resettled in the United States, where many have built businesses, served in the U.S. military and become integral members of their communities.

Afghan SIV applicants undergo extensive, multilayered security vetting. Applicants are screened throughout the visa process, including identity verification, employment verification, security checks and Intelligence Community vetting. Many were also vetted before they ever began working alongside the U.S. government. In a review of sampled applications from 2021, the State Department Inspector General found that the SIV application review process was functioning as designed.

The Trump Administration has suspended Afghan SIV issuance while more than 155,000 applicants remain in the pipeline. The report finds that although some administrative processing continues, the State Department has suspended immigrant visa issuance to Afghan nationals, including Afghan SIVs. As of the Department’s May 2026 report to Congress, no Afghan SIVs had been issued in 2026.

The Administration dismantled infrastructure built to relocate and resettle Afghan allies. The Administration eliminated the State Department’s Coordinator for Afghan Relocation Efforts (CARE) office, which had served as the central coordinating body for third-country processing, flight coordination, family reunification and case escalation. Congressional briefings from CARE also stopped after the Administration took office.

Afghan allies remain stranded in dangerous and uncertain conditions abroad. The report details the circumstances facing Afghans in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iran and at Camp As-Sayliyah in Qatar. Today, there are approximately 1,100 Afghans remaining at Camp As-Sayliyah. The vast majority have legal pathways to the United States, but the Administration is trying to relocate them to third countries instead.

Abandoning Afghan allies risks long-term consequences for U.S. national security. The report warns that future partners will judge the credibility of U.S. commitments by how the United States treats Afghans who risked their lives in support of the American mission. Failure to keep those commitments could make future local partners less willing to support U.S. diplomatic, military and intelligence operations.

The report concludes with key recommendations:

Immediately Resume Afghan SIV Issuance and Fully Resource Processing: The Administration should immediately resume issuing Afghan SIVs and provide the National Visa Center and Afghan SIV Unit with sufficient staffing and resources to address the backlog.

Authorize Additional Visas and Extend the Application Deadline: Congress should authorize 100,000 additional visas to ensure that remaining eligible applicants can receive an SIV and allow for the responsible wind-down of the existing Afghan program once the current pipeline has been processed.

Establish a Permanent Wartime Allies Program: Congress and the Administration should apply lessons learned from the Afghan SIV program to create a permanent mechanism to protect local partners who put themselves at risk supporting future U.S. missions. The program should provide flexibility to account for different conflicts and partner forces, streamline processing, clearly delineate responsibilities across federal agencies, strengthen record retention and provide sufficient resources for long-term administration.

Increase Transparency and Congressional Oversight: A permanent wartime allies program should include recurring reports to Congress, public reporting on applicant numbers and processing trends and regular Inspector General review to ensure the program is meeting congressional requirements and functioning effectively.

The full report is available HERE.

title: U.S. Senator Tina Smith Requests Cost Estimate of Big Beautiful Bill’s Data Center Tax Incentives
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tina Smith (D-MN), in her capacity as the top Democrat on the Senate Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Growth Subcommittee, is requesting an analysis to shed light on the extent to which OBBBA tax breaks went to data center development. Smith sent the request to the Joint Committee on Taxation after reports that some of the country’s largest corporations taking advantage of the generous corporate tax breaks in Republicans’ signature legislation to subsidize the development of data centers.

“We’ve seen reports that tax breaks from the Big Beautiful Bill are being used by some of the biggest tech companies in the world to pad their pockets and boost the buildout of data centers. These companies have billions of dollars of revenues, and I question the fiscal rationale behind rewarding them for investments they would have made regardless of the tax benefits,” says Senator Smith. “How is it that Republicans could find the money for these massive companies to build deeply unpopular data centers, but not the money for health care and nutrition assistance? It’s complete hypocrisy and reeks of corruption, considering these same companies routinely donate millions of dollars to the President’s campaign.”

Data centers and the trillion-dollar tech companies building them have reported record profits, which likely were boosted thanks to the OBBBA. OBBBA provisions most commonly utilized include expanded breaks for research and development programs, immediate deductions for the cost of investments, and a new subsidy for manufacturing structures. Senator Smith questions the fiscal rationale of the federal government subsidizing projects that are widely opposed by local communities and driving up electricity and water bills across the country, particularly at a time where the federal deficit and national debt have each reached record levels.

You can find full text of the request here or below.

Thomas A. Barthold, Chief of Staff

Joint Committee on Taxation

502 Ford House Office Building

Washington, DC 20515

Dear Mr. Barthold:

Thank you for your ongoing work to provide Congress with information related to P.L. 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

As you know, this legislation included several tax provisions designed to spur business investment. But by the time it was enacted in July 2025, domestic investment was already growing, fueled in large part by record spending on artificial intelligence data centers and related infrastructure. Recent reports suggest the tax incentives enacted by OBBBA have resulted in a windfall for companies spending heavily on the AI data center buildout, rewarding them for investments they would have made regardless of the tax benefits.

Last month, the Congressional Budget Office found that corporate income receipts decreased by 25 percent over the first 11 months of FY 2026, even as corporate profits surged to historic levels. This cost is ultimately borne by taxpayers. As corporations pad their profits, the United States’ fiscal outlook is worsening, resulting in higher prices and borrowing costs for Americans.

To help Congress better understand the deficit impact of OBBBA, I request that the Joint Committee on Taxation analyze the extent to which the bill’s tax provisions have subsidized the AI data center buildout thus far, including the revenue effects of these benefits.

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Sincerely,

Tina Smith

Ranking Member

Subcommittee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Growth

title: Senate Passes Warner Legislation to Strengthen Cybersecurity in Health Care
text:
WASHINGTON –U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and John Cornyn (R-TX) celebrated the U.S. Senate’s passage by unanimous consent of their Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act, legislation to protect Americans’ health data by strengthening cybersecurity.

“Cyberattacks on our health care systems can have life-or-death consequences for patients and put the sensitive information of millions of Americans at risk,” said Sen. Warner. “I’m proud to have helped pass this critical legislation through the Senate, and I urge the House to act quickly. This bill will strengthen our cybersecurity, better protect patients and their information, and give rural health care providers in Virginia and across the country additional tools to defend against cyber threats.”

“Cyberattacks can shut down hospitals and expose patients’ private medical records,” said Dr. Cassidy. “At a time when hostile actors are increasingly using sophisticated tactics to breach health care systems, the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resilience Act will help health care providers strengthen their defenses against cyber threats and protect patients’ health data.”

“Cyberattacks have exposed patients’ private medical information and disrupted critical patient care in New Hampshire and across the country,” said Sen. Hassan. “This bipartisan legislation will help hospitals and health care providers, particularly those in rural communities with fewer resources, strengthen their cybersecurity and respond faster to attacks. I’m pleased to see that the Senate came together to pass this bill, and I’ll keep working across the aisle to protect patients and strengthen our health care system.”

“Patients deserve absolute confidence that their sensitive medical data stored online is protected and shielded from cybersecurity breaches or ransomware attacks,” said Sen. Cornyn. “This legislation would strengthen interagency coordination and improve security practices for rural providers, ensuring Texans’ health care is not delayed or compromised by cyberattacks.”

The Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act:

Strengthens cybersecurity in the health care sector by authorizing grants to health entities to improve cyberattack prevention and response.

Provides training to health entities on cybersecurity best practices.

Supports rural communities by providing best practices to rural health clinics and other providers on cybersecurity breach prevention, resilience, and coordination with federal agencies.

Improves coordination between the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to better respond to cyberattacks in the health care sector.

Modernizes current regulations so entities covered under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) use the best cybersecurity practices.

Requires the HHS Secretary to develop and implement a cybersecurity incident response plan.

title: Warner, Himes Push for Transparency on Election Security
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and U.S. Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton regarding the upcoming midterm election, urging transparency to Congress and the public around possible foreign threats to the midterms.

“Career intelligence community (IC) analysts recently briefed the House Committee about the latest assessments regarding foreign threats to the upcoming midterms,” the lawmakers wrote. “These briefings, as well as additional briefings given to staff of both committees, provided valuable insight into how our intelligence professionals are monitoring potential attempts by our adversaries to influence or interfere in U.S. elections, and how such foreign malign activity compares to prior cycles. Between now and Election Day, it is critical the IC continue to inform policymakers, state and local election administrators, and the American people about threats to our elections.”

They continued, “While we have received the first in a series of statutorily required reports about foreign adversaries targeting this election, there are still several outstanding statutorily required products owed to the Committees. It is essential that the IC complete production of its remaining assessments in a timely manner, so that policymakers remain up-to-date regarding any emerging intelligence or shifts in the analytic line before the midterm elections. This process should include the declassification and public issuance of the Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA) about foreign threats to the 2024 presidential election. The lack of a public ICA contravenes the law and undercuts needed transparency about IC efforts to keep our elections secure from outside interference.”

In addition to these statutory requirements, the lawmakers requested a full interagency classified update for members before the election, a commitment to provide real-time notification about emerging threats to elections, and the responsible release of unclassified election assessments to keep the public informed about possible threats and other relevant context.

“A statement noting the absence of indications of significant foreign interference efforts is just as important as a statement exposing any such activities. Regardless, the American people should receive as much information as we can responsibly provide prior to the election,” they concluded.

title: Warnock, Ossoff Secure More Than $11 Million in Federal Funding for Roadway Improvements in Savannah
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff secured more than $11.3 million in federal funding to improve Savannah’s roadways and reduce traffic congestion

The funding will improve DeRenne Avenue, the primary corridor for Hunter Army Airfield, Memorial Health University Medical Center, Candler Hospital, and freight moving to and from the Port of Savannah

In June, Senator Warnock urged Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to award the City of Savannah funding through the Department of Transportation’s Infrastructure for Rebuilding America grant program

Senator Reverend Warnock: “Upgrades to this central corridor will promote economic opportunity, improve safety, and reduce traffic for Georgians across Savannah”

Savannah, GA – Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) successfully secured more than $11.3 million in federal funding for the Freight Mobility, Military and Workforce Readiness Corridor Project on DeRenne Avenue. The funding will support right-of-way acquisition for the project, which will improve a key transportation corridor serving Hunter Army Airfield, Memorial Health University Medical Center, Candler Hospital, and freight moving to and from the Port of Savannah. The funding was provided by the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Infrastructure for Rebuilding America grant program and will help relieve chronic congestion, improve military operational readiness, support economic growth, and boost public health and safety. This grant is funded by the bipartisan infrastructure law, which Senators Warnock and Ossoff championed.

“To ensure that Memorial Health University Medical Center and Candler Hospital are accessible during emergencies and Hunter Army Airfield can stay connected to strategic partners across the country, we need strong investments to modernize Savannah’s vital roadway infrastructure,” said Senator Warnock. “Upgrades to this central corridor will promote economic opportunity, improve safety, and reduce traffic for Georgians across Savannah.”

“The City of Savannah remains committed to improving DeRenne Avenue, and we’re excited about the continued momentum with the support of United States Department of Transportation (USDOT), Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT), Hunter Army Airfield, Savannah Technical College, Memorial Health University Medical Center (MHUMC), the Georgia Motor Trucking Association, Senator Warnock, and Senator Ossoff,” said Mayor Van R. Johnson, II. “DeRenne Avenue carries regional significance, but it’s also the way that our residents rely on every day to get to work, school, and home. This project continues to be an incredible example of partnership, and we’re proud to keep it moving forward.”

This funding will help the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) and the City of Savannah complete a key component of Project DeRenne, a major four-part infrastructure initiative aimed at reducing traffic congestion and improving transportation and neighborhood connectivity along the DeRenne Avenue corridor. Specifically, the funding will support a new connection between I-516 and White Bluff Road and widen Hampstead Avenue to improve pedestrian and bicycle access.

Senator Warnock has long championed infrastructure projects across Georgia. Earlier this year, he pressedU.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to approve the City of Savannah’s request for federal funding to support Project DeRenne. Senator Ossoff also urged Secretary Duffy to provide funding for the project in July. In a similar effort, Senators Warnock and Ossoff successfully secured over $54 million in federal DOT funding to improve Georgia’s roadway infrastructure and help strengthen road safety for bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers. From this effort, the City of Savannah received $2 million to develop a digital emergency services platform.

title: Welch Joins Bipartisan, Bicameral Legislation to Address Vermont’s Housing Shortage, Speed Construction of Affordable Homes
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit, joined U.S. Senators Angus King (I-Maine), John Curtis (R-Utah), and Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) in introducing the Build American Efficiency Act, bipartisan, bicameral legislation that would streamline the process for home builders to determine and locate domestically sourced materials that comply with the Build America, Buy American Act (BABA). This small legislative step would help homebuilders cut costs and red tape as they work to address the national housing shortage.

“Our nation’s housing crisis is an urgent problem, and Congress needs to take action. In Vermont, we’re going to need 36,000 new housing units by 2030 to address our shortage—cutting through red tape that makes it harder to build a home is a major part of helping us close that gap,” said Senator Welch. “The Build American Efficiency Act is a commonsense, bipartisan solution that will help builders construct high-quality homes at a price that families can afford.”

“Despite our country’s desperate need for additional affordable housing options, American homebuilders face steep costs and bureaucratic red tape,” said Senator King. “The Build American Efficiency Act would empower the Department of Housing and Urban Development to share information to help builders, manufacturers, and housing providers navigate complicated compliance requirements and identify verified American-made products. Eliminating this time-consuming and costly additional step for homebuilders will allow them to build more homes faster. It’s a three-page bill that amounts to a common-sense helping hand.”

“Utah’s impressive growth has unfortunately brought with it the strain of rising housing costs—which has already been made worse by unnecessary federal red tape,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill is a commonsense fix that makes it easier for builders to identify American-made materials, cut through bureaucracy, and get more affordable homes built faster.”

“I’m committed to using every federal resource available to make building homes in Alaska more streamlined and affordable across the board,” said Senator Murkowski. “This legislation will help identify products that are made in America more easily, cutting through red tape to get more homes built with American-made materials around the country.”

America’s nationwide housing crisis has hit the state of Vermont especially hard, with median home sale prices surging 40% since 2019. In addition to skyrocketing housing costs, dwindling market supply has made it even tougher for lower-income families—including the nearly 4,000 Vermonters facing homelessness—to purchase a home. Vermont is projected to need an additional 24,000–36,000 housing units by 2030 to replace outdated housing stock and meet demand.

To accomplish its goals, the Build American Efficiency Act would encourage the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to share industry-led initiatives to certify products and facilities that comply with BABA requirements. The BABA standards were passed in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. More specifically, the Build American Efficiency Act would:

Clarify that the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development has the authority to recognize auditable and verifiable systems that document products that comply with Build America, Buy America domestic content requirements;

Allow HUD to treat documentation generated under the Make It American Process Standard, or similar standards that provide an auditable and verifiable certification process, as sufficient evidence for domestic content certification;

Help manufacturers, builders, and funding recipients more easily determine which products comply with BABA requirements;

Reduce time spent navigating waiver requests, duplicative paperwork, and uncertainty over which products have or have not been approved; and

Preserve flexibility by ensuring the bill does not mandate the use of any one database or prohibit recipients from using other lawful methods to certify compliance.

Companion legislation was introduced in the House by Reps. Mark Alford (R-MO-04), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Tracey Mann (R-KS-01), Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02), and Brad Finstad (R-MN-01).

The Build American Efficiency Act is supported by ABB, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Associated General Contractors, Eaton, National Association of Electrical Distributors, National Association of Realtors, National Association of State Housing Agencies, National Electrical Contractors Association, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Prysmian, Schneider, Siemens, and Southwire.

Senator Welch has led bipartisan efforts to address Vermont’s affordable housing crisis. Last month, the Senator introduced the Supporting Small Affordable Housing Developers Act, new legislation that would exempt grants supporting affordable housing development from taxation to empower small, rural housing developers to build more affordable housing.

In March, Senator Welch introduced the bipartisan FARM Home Loans Act to spur rural economic growth by helping more homebuyers qualify for rural housing assistance. The Senator is also a cosponsor of the First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act, legislation that aims to support middle-class Americans purchasing their first home, and the End Rent Fixing Act, which would crack down on companies that help landlords increase rents in already high-priced markets. The Senator is also a cosponsor of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which was signed into law earlier this year.

The Senator’s bipartisan, bicameral HOPE for HOMES Act, which helps lower energy costs for homeowners and reduce greenhouse gas emissions while also investing in the workforce, was included as part of the Biden-Harris Administration’s historic Inflation Reduction Act.

title: Whitehouse and Dingell Introduce New Bill Creating Alert System to Notify Survivors of Illegal Gun Purchase Attempts by Domestic Abusers
text:
Bicameral Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure domestic violence survivors are notified when an abusive partner is trying to obtain a firearm illegally

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI) have introduced the Domestic Violence Survivors Alerted for Emergency (SAFE) Notice Act, new legislation to establish notification systems that would alert survivors of domestic violence offenses when their domestic abuser attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Loopholes in federal and state law can allow domestic violence offenders to purchase guns notwithstanding their criminal history – situations that can be life threatening for survivors. Even when offenders are unsuccessful, the fact they are trying to purchase a firearm illegally can be a warning sign for survivors. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help keep survivors safe by setting up systems to notify domestic violence survivors when an abusive partner has obtained or is trying to obtain a firearm illegally.

“I spent years prosecuting domestic violence cases in Rhode Island, and I know the toll it can take on survivors as they rebuild their lives. Our legislation will help ensure survivors are made aware when the government has information about an abuser’s attempt to buy a firearm, so survivors and their loved ones can make decisions in the interest of their own safety and wellbeing,” said Senator Whitehouse, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee and former Rhode Island Attorney General and U.S. Attorney.

“When a domestic violence survivor is rebuilding their life, safety and peace of mind are everything. We know that an abusive partner’s access to a firearm dramatically increases the risk of fatal violence. By ensuring survivors receive immediate alerts if an offender attempts to purchase a gun illegally, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act empowers victims with time-sensitive information that can save lives,” said Congresswoman Dingell.

The legislation is cosponsored by Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

“As a former prosecutor, I have seen firsthand the serious emotional and physical toll domestic violence can take on victims, especially when guns are involved. The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, now law, included provisions from my bill that closed the dangerous boyfriend loophole to keep firearms out of the hands of dating partners convicted of domestic violence,” said Senator Klobuchar. “This new legislation builds on that progress by creating a notification system for survivors of domestic violence, alerting them when their abuser attempts to purchase a firearm illegally. This common-sense legislation will protect victims and help save lives.”

“Current loopholes in federal and state law can allow domestic violence offenders to purchase guns despite their criminal history, which seriously compromises survivor safety,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “This Domestic Violence Awareness Month, I am proud to partner with my colleagues to create this essential alert system that will ensure no victim is unprepared if their abuser breaks the law to obtain a dangerous firearm.”

Domestic violence offenders and protective order respondents are generally prohibited under federal and many state laws from purchasing firearms. However, that prohibition does not always stop offenders from trying to purchase firearms anyway. FBI data shows that almost 160,000 gun purchases were denied from 2018 to 2023 because of the purchaser’s domestic violence background. These situations can be life threatening for domestic violence survivors. A male abusive partner’s access to a gun significantly increases the risk of an intimate partner homicide.

Specifically, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would:

Direct the FBI to establish a notification system to alert survivors of federal domestic violence offenses when the offender attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Permit survivors to register or de-register at will.

Provide key alerts about an offender’s attempted illegal firearm purchase, including if the sale went through or law enforcement has recovered the firearm.

Provide additional alerts about related events, such as a pardon that restores an offender’s ability to purchase firearms legally.

Authorize grants for states to pilot state-run alert systems, so survivors can receive alerts related to protective orders and non-federal domestic violence offenses.

Enable states to use funds to expand existing systems or set up new ones.

Require reports on the success of and challenges related to these pilot projects, including recommendations for expanding the projects to other states.

The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act has been endorsed by the National Domestic Violence Hotline, National District Attorneys Association, Association of Prosecuting Attorneys, Survivor Justice Center, Jewish Women International, National Alliance of Trauma Recovery Centers, National Advocacy Center of the Sisters of the Good Shepherd, Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd (U.S. Region), the Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence, National Council of Jewish Women, Just Solutions, Futures Without Violence, Union for Reform Judaism, Ujima, National Network to End Domestic Violence, Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault, Sakhi for South Asian Survivors, National Organization for Victim Advocacy, Asian Pacific Institute on Gender-Based Violence, Lovelace Consulting Services, Inc., National Indigenous Women’s Resource Center, Colorado Organization for Victim Assistance, National Crime Victim Law Institute, Yup’ik Women’s Coalition, Life Span, Women of Reform Judaism, and Alliance of Tribal Coalitions to End Violence.

“Survivors often must make complex safety decisions in real time, and having timely information about an abusive partner’s attempt to obtain a firearm can be critical to that decision-making. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure survivors have access to information that could allow them to take additional safety precautions, seek support, and make informed decisions for themselves and their families. The Hotline is grateful to Rep. Debbie Dingell and Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse for introducing this legislation and for their continued commitment to the safety and well-being of survivors of domestic violence,” said Katie Ray-Jones, Chief Executive Officer of the National Domestic Violence Hotline.

“The National District Attorneys Association is proud to support the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act, which establishes a common-sense notification system to alert victims when offenders unlawfully attempt to acquire a firearm as well as other firearm-related updates. NDAA commends this victim-centered approach that promotes public safety,” said Nelson Bunn, Executive Director of the National District Attorneys Association.

title: Senator Wicker Honors Mississippi “Angels in Adoption” Honorees
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss., this week honored Sara and Nic Pendleton and Thomas Dent as honorees for the 2026 “Angels in Adoption” award. Senator Wicker nominated the Pendletons while Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., nominated Mr. Dent. This recognition honors years of foster parent service and dedicated advocacy for underprivileged children.

“Sara, Nic, and Thomas represent the best of Mississippi. They have selflessly devoted their lives to providing loving and nurturing environments for children in need of a home. These honorees have unquestionably changed many lives for the better. It is the least we can do to recognize them for this outstanding work,” said Senator Wicker.

Sara and Nic Pendleton, of Biloxi, Mississippi, have opened their homes to more than 25 Mississippi children in foster care. The Pendletons have oriented their home to children with health challenges, providing these children with outstanding medical care and emotional stability. The couple has raised one biological child and adopted five more. Outside of their parental work, the Pendletons are also fierce advocates for the needs of fellow caregivers and of children in vulnerable situations, particularly those with special needs.

Thomas Dent, of Ridgeland, Mississippi, has spent years supporting Mississippi children who need care in both professional and personal settings. For over five years, Mr. Dent worked in the Mississippi Department of Child Protection Services as the Director of Faith-Based and Volunteer Services and as Foster Parent Liaison. He is also an adoptive father and a former foster parent. For Mr. Dent, his commitment to supporting others is driven by his deeply rooted Christian faith.

The Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute, which sponsors the “Angels in Adoption” program, is a nonprofit organization that works to raise awareness about the needs of children without families and to remove policy barriers that hinder children from knowing the love and support a family provides.

title: Amo Honors Rhode Island Veterans at Third Annual Resource Fair and BBQ
text:
Warren, RI – Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) hosted his third annual Veterans Resource Fair and Barbecue at Pete Sepe Pavilion in Warren, bringing together Rhode Island Veterans, military families, and organizations that serve the Veteran community.

A day of food and fun, the event brought together the military community with Veterans advocacy organizations, health care providers, and education and support groups from across Rhode Island. Veterans and their families enjoyed a barbecue lunch and had the opportunity to connect directly with Veterans service organizations (VSOs).

“We owe Rhode Islanders who have served our nation in uniform and their families a lifetime of gratitude for their sacrifices in defense of our values and democracy,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “It was an honor to spend time with Veterans and their families at today’s barbecue to thank them for their service and help connect them with the resources they’ve earned. If you or a Veteran you know is having trouble getting help from a federal agency, my office is here to help.”

Background

Congressman Amo is committed to supporting Rhode Island’s Veterans. If constituents of Rhode Island’s First Congressional District need help with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or another federal agency, they can reach out to Congressman Amo’s office for help by calling (401) 729-5600 or submitting a request here.

Amo hosts a District Veterans Advisory Committee made up of a broad and diverse group of key Veterans and military stakeholders, to ensure he remains focused on achieving results and serving those who have served our country.

On May 21st, 2026, Amo signed onto Discharge Petition No. 22 to force a vote on H.R. 2102, the Major Richard Star Act, which would ensure that combat-disabled veterans receive the full benefits they deserve.

On September 16, 2025, Amo led the Rhode Island Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to Secretary of Veterans Affairs, Douglas Collins, demanding that he explain the loss of Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) employees across the United States and provide an update on the status of Rhode Island’s federal VA workforce.

On September 14, 2025, Amo hosted his second annual Veterans Barbecue and Resource Fair.

On July 3, 2025, Amo voted no on Trump’s Big, Ugly Law, which gutted SNAP, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act. An estimated 3,000 Rhode Island Veterans received SNAP between 2021 and 2023. As of 2023, 4,200 Rhode Island Veterans were enrolled in Medicaid.

On May 15, 2025, Amo introduced a bicameral, bipartisan resolution to support Veteran mental health by establishing “Vets Get Outside Day.”

On February 13, 2025, Amo introduced a bipartisan bill with Senator Sheldon Whitehouse to recognize America’s first integrated military unit — the First Rhode Island Regiment — by posthumously awarding its members with the Congressional Gold Medal.

On August 28, 2024, Amo hosted his first Barbecue to honor the Veterans of Rhode Island’s First Congressional District.

title: TAPInto Middletown article on Smith-led survey of Nor'easter damage'Rep. Smith Leads Survey of Nor’easter Damage Along Monmouth and Ocean County Shore'
text:
By Jeanne Wall

Published October 3, 2026 at 1:46 AM

MONMOUTH AND OCEAN COUNTIES, NJ — In the aftermath of last week’s powerful Nor’easter, U.S. Rep. Chris Smith led a group of federal, state and local officials on a tour of several shore communities to assess damage caused by flooding, erosion and severe weather.

The tour included stops in Manasquan, Point Pleasant Beach, Bay Head and Ocean Gate, where officials examined the condition of beaches and coastal infrastructure and discussed both immediate needs and longer-term strategies to better protect the communities from future storms.

Smith was joined by Federal Emergency Management Agency Region 2 Administrator Chris Hartnett; New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Deputy Commissioner Joe Seebode; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Philadelphia District Commander Lt. Col. Ryan A. Baum; USACE New York District Project Manager Jason Shea; New Jersey State Police Operations Officer Major James Boland; Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden; Ocean County Sheriff Mike Mastronardy; NJ Legislative District 10 Assemblyman Paul Kanitra; Ocean County Commissioner Jennifer Bacchione; Manasquan Mayor Mike Mangan; Bay Head Mayor Bill Curtis; Ocean Gate Mayor Robert Curtin; and other elected and municipal officials.

Rep. Smith Leads Survey of Nor'easter Damage Along Monmouth and Ocean County Shore. Photo Credit: File Photo

The group surveyed areas affected by the storm while discussing the challenges facing the individual communities and the steps that could be taken to strengthen coastal protection.

“Today, an impressive, comprehensive group of experts—with extensive backgrounds in environmental, structural engineering, and beach replenishment initiatives—came together to not only survey the severe damage wrought by last week’s Nor’easter, but also to collaborate on creative solutions for immediate needs and future resilience efforts,” Smith said.

Local officials came prepared to show the federal and state representatives the specific impacts their communities experienced and to discuss potential improvements.

“Municipal officials and local leaders came fully prepared, offering tangible examples of the damages they sustained and providing ideas for new initiatives that could bolster their towns’ resilience against future storms,” Smith said.

The tour also provided an opportunity to look at how investments and protective measures implemented following previous storms have affected the latest storm's impact.

Officials noted that although the Nor’easter caused damage in the communities visited, existing protections helped mitigate some of the effects in certain areas.

That experience is providing another opportunity for officials to evaluate what has worked, where additional improvements may be needed and how communities can prepare for increasingly severe coastal weather.

Smith said the participation of federal, state and local representatives demonstrated the importance of cooperation when addressing storm damage and coastal resilience.

“I am truly encouraged by the intergovernmental partnership and determination demonstrated today,” Smith said. “Building upon what we’ve learned from previous storms and tapping into the continued knowledge and expertise shared today, I look forward to working alongside our great state and local officials to strengthen our shore communities’ resilience and preparation for future severe weather events.”

title: Senator Collins Honors Fallen Firefighters at Annual Memorial Service in Augusta
text:
Click HERE, HERE, and HERE for individual photos.

AUGUSTA, ME – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins delivered remarks at the annual Firefighter Memorial Service at the Maine Fallen Firefighters Memorial in Augusta. During the service, a roll call of Maine firefighters who passed away over the previous year was read, with a bell rung once in honor of each fallen firefighter. The event was attended by more than 100 firefighters and their families, other first responders, community residents, and local and state leaders.

Two Maine firefighters were lost in the line of duty this past year and were given unique honors during the ceremony: Morrill Volunteer Firefighter Andrew Cross and Searsmont Assistant Fire Chief Wayne Woodbury, who both lost their lives due to injuries sustained responding to the tragic explosion and fire at Robbins Lumber in Searsmont this May.

“Whether they were on duty or retired, every name read today belongs to a hero. Every ring of the bell is an echo, not just of who they were, but of the dedication that all firefighters share and of the gratitude that unites all whom they serve,” said Senator Collins during her remarks. “Those qualities of character and commitment are found throughout Maine. Whether you are a full-time firefighter or an on-call volunteer, you are a critical first line of defense. Whether you serve in a large city or a small town, whether you are called to a major catastrophe or a local emergency, you respond when the alarm sounds, whenever that may be.”

“This annual memorial service is always powerful and inspiring. It has a special significance this year as we honor two firefighters who made the ultimate sacrifice battling the horrific explosion at Robbins Lumber in Searsmont last May,” she continued. “Andrew Cross, a young man of extraordinary accomplishments, served with the Morrill Volunteer Fire Department. Wayne Woodbury dedicated more than 60 years as a volunteer firefighter in both Belmont and Searsmont, where he was assistant chief. We extend our deepest condolences to the families of these heroes, both their families at home and their brothers and sisters at the firehouse.”

“Most of us will never know where the bravery to rush toward danger comes from. We can’t begin to imagine the courage and dedication it takes to enter a burning building or approach a blazing truck that may be about to explode, especially when others are running in the opposite direction. But we are deeply grateful to you who take this courage and dedication, this skill and discipline, with you every day. Thank you, and may God bless you all,” Senator Collins concluded.

+++

As a co-chair of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus, Senator Collins has been an advocate for Maine's firefighters, helping to better ensure they have additional resources and support as they protect our communities.

Through her role as Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, she has secured nearly $87 million over the past five years to rehabilitate, expand, or replace 45 fire stations across Maine.

In 2024, Senator Collins' bipartisan Fire Grants and Safety Act was signed into law, reauthorizing through 2028 the Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) and Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant programs, as well as the U.S. Fire Administration. These programs help local fire departments address staffing needs, purchase equipment, develop training and education programs, and improve emergency medical services.

Senator Collins also championed the Firefighter Cancer Registry Act, enacted in 2018, which established the National Firefighter Registry for Cancer to improve understanding of the connection between firefighting and cancer and help reduce occupational cancer risks for firefighters. More than 50,000 firefighters nationwide have since enrolled in the registry.

title: Heinrich Statement on Major League Baseball Reversing Course on Plan to Host Baseball Game in Grand Teton National Park
text:
MLB withdraws proposal after Heinrich sent a letter urging MLB to back down from their plan to host a baseball game in the treasured national park

WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, released the following statement in response to Major League Baseball (MLB) Commissioner Robert Manfred withdrawing the league's interest in hosting a baseball game in Grand Teton National Park after Heinrich pressed Manfred to withdraw his proposal.

“This week, I sent a letter to MLB Commissioner Manfred urging him to stand down on pursuing a baseball stadium in Grand Teton National Park. While I’m glad that he has listened and agreed not to pursue this Grand Teton National Park plan, I am concerned that MLB may still be considering other National Park locations,” said Heinrich. “Let’s be clear: our national parks are no place for hosting professional sports games. Building stadiums in our national parks defies logic and is just plain wrong. I’ll continue to demand answers on whether other national park sites are being considered for any MLB games.”

In his letter to MLB Commissioner Manfred, sent Tuesday, September 29, Heinrich urged MLB to withdraw its proposal to build a baseball stadium in Grand Teton National Park, citing concerns over national park preservation and the precedent hosting a baseball game would set for future national park land use.

“Since 1916, the mission of the National Park Service has been to conserve the scenery, natural and historic objects, and wildlife in the parks, and to provide for their enjoyment in a way that leaves them unimpaired for future generations of Americans. This all makes national parks sacred ground and not a proper venue for a stadium built for a single commercial event. As Americans, we have an obligation to protect and preserve our national parks at every turn,” Heinrich wrote.

Heinrich also expressed concern over the lack of public input from MLB or the Trump administration in making this decision. Recent reporting from The Washington Post found that National Park Service (NPS) Deputy Director for Operations Frank Lands recently visited Teton County, but made no mention of hosting an MLB game in Grand Teton National Park.

“The public and local communities deserve an opportunity to voice their concerns about visitor safety and the protection of federal lands and ecosystems. Neither MLB nor the Trump administration has sought public input,” Heinrich continued.

“MLB has its choice of at least 30 different stadiums all over the country to host a baseball game. Hosting a baseball game at a national park, however, should not be one of those venues given the heightened threat to local ecosystems and wildlife habitats. I therefore request that you withdraw your proposal to host a baseball game at a national park and instead pursue a more viable alternative venue,” Heinrich concluded.

Yesterday, MLB Commissioner Manfred responded to Heinrich’s letter, sharing that MLB will no longer be considering Grand Teton National Park as a potential site for a baseball game, but making no commitments regarding other National Park sites.

Read the full text of Heinrich’s letter here and below.

Dear Commissioner Manfred:

I write to express strong opposition to Major League Baseball (MLB) hosting a baseball game at a national park. I strongly urge you to withdraw your proposal.

According to recent reports, MLB has approached the Trump administration about hosting a major league baseball game in Grand Teton National Park. This news is highly concerning. Grand Teton National Park holds a singular place in our nation’s conservation history. First protected by Congress in 1929, the park preserves the Teton Range, the valley of Jackson Hole, and one of the most intact ecosystems in the lower 48 states. It is home to grizzly bears, moose, bison, and it sustains the pronghorn’s ancient migration route, one of the longest land migrations in North America. The same land that makes the area attractive to construction is the same habitat these animals depend on for grazing, calving, and passage.

Since 1916, the mission of the National Park Service has been to conserve the scenery, natural and historic objects, and wildlife in the parks, and to provide for their enjoyment in a way that leaves them unimpaired for future generations of Americans. This all makes national parks sacred ground and not a proper venue for a stadium built for a single commercial event. As Americans, we have an obligation to protect and preserve our national parks at every turn. The public and local communities deserve an opportunity to voice their concerns about visitor safety and the protection of federal lands and ecosystems. Neither MLB nor the Trump administration has sought public input. According to The Washington Post, Deputy Director Frank Lands recently visited Teton County, but made no mention of hosting an MLB game in Grand Teton National Park.

Baseball is a treasured American pastime – drawing millions of fans to ballparks every year. MLB has its choice of at least 30 different stadiums all over the country to host a baseball game. Hosting a baseball game at a national park, however, should not be one of those venues given the heightened threat to local ecosystems and wildlife habitats. I therefore request that you withdraw your proposal to host a baseball game at a national park and instead pursue a more viable alternative venue.

Sincerely,

title: Congressman Bishop Statement on the Mass Shooting in Vienna, Georgia
text:
COLUMBUS, Ga. – Congressman Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02) issued the following statement in the aftermath of the mass shooting in the early morning hours of Sunday, October 4, 2026, in Vienna, Georgia:

“Homecoming is supposed to be about coming home — to family, to old friends, to the neighborhoods that raised us. Early this morning in Vienna, a celebration of home became a scene of unspeakable grief.

“Two young men, just 20 and 23 years old, will not come home again. Dozens more are lying in hospital beds, and their families are keeping watch, praying for every breath.

“Vivian and I join the people of Vienna and Dooly County in mourning. We lift up the families who lost sons, the wounded and those who love them, and every person who ran toward danger to help a neighbor. I am grateful to the Dooly County Sheriff’s Office, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, first responders, and the doctors and nurses working through the night.

“Scripture tells us that the Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart. Vienna’s heart is broken today. But this community is strong, and it is not alone. My office stands ready to help in every way we can, and we will continue to pray for healing, for justice, and for peace.”

title: Latta Visits Savannah River Site, Nuclear Facility
text:
Congressman Bob Latta, Chairman of the Energy Subcommittee on Energy and Commerce, visited the Department of Energy's Savannah River Site (SRS) to receive an in-depth tour of the facilities and receive updates on the process for the disposal of nuclear waste. Congressman Latta released the following statement after his visit:

"It was great to see the Savannah River Site (SRS) in South Carolina, where the Department of Energy is taking on the federal government's statutory responsibility to clean up nuclear waste.

"The site plays a vital role in advancing our nation's nuclear interests, both domestically and internationally, and SRS's focus on cleaning up nuclear components is critical for protecting the health and well-being of every American.

"As a member of the Environment Subcommittee on the Energy and Commerce Committee, I understand how important it is for our country to safely dispose of nuclear waste so that surrounding communities are protected from environmental hazards.

"Seeing the site's comprehensive process for safe disposal, and watching the expert professionals who operate this facility has given me even further confidence in our ability as a nation to handle complex energy waste issues.

"Last month, the Energy Subcommittee held a hearing with the Department of Energy and industry professionals to discuss the future of spent nuclear fuel storage and how we can support every stage of our nuclear fuel cycle moving into the future.

"With tremendous support for nuclear power, it's critical that we continue to focus on generating more affordable, and reliable power in efficient and safe ways. Advancing safe nuclear power for America is paramount to our national security and environmental safety."

Details of the visit:

During his time at the facility, Congressman Latta focused on SRS's integrated radioactive liquid waste treatment facility that handles by-products from the processing of nuclear materials.

Congressman Latta first visited the H tank farm, one of two tank farms, where SRS stores about 32 million gallons of radioactive waste in 43 underground carbon-steel waste tanks.

The Congressman also visited the Salt Waste Processing Facility (SWPF), where SRS treats the radioactive salt components that make up more than 90% of the contents of the tanks. Congressman Latta also participated in a sampling discussion at the SWPF.

At the Defense Waste Processing Facility (DWPF), Congressman Latta viewed where SRS takes radioactive sludge from the tanks, and combines it with higher activity salt waste components to be turned into glass for storage and disposal.

The Congressman's final facility viewing was a drive through the Saltstone Disposal Units (SDUs) where lower level salt solutions from the nuclear waste are permanently stored.

Once a tank from the farm is emptied and the contents are treated and safely disposed of or stored, the tank is cleaned and operationally closed.

title: Reps. Houlahan, Smith Lead Members of Congress Demanding Answers on End to Tenured Appointments at Military Service Academies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) and Adam Smith (WA-09) demanded answers on the Department of Defense’s decision to end appointments to tenured positions at military service academies. Specifically, the lawmakers questioned Secretary Pete Hegseth about the Department’s legal authority for this action, its intended application, and effects on existing faculty.

“Congress has long recognized that the service academies have a dual mission: preparing cadets and midshipmen for military service while providing a rigorous academic education,” wrote the lawmakers. “Civilian faculty play an important role in making that possible.”

The lawmakers continued, “Given this statutory and institutional history, we are concerned about the legal basis for the Department’s new policy and whether the directive is intended to prohibit future grants of tenure or to alter the status and employment protections of faculty who are currently tenured.”

Rep. Houlahan is Ranking Member of the House Military Personnel Subcommittee and Rep. Smith is Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee. The Members were joined by Representatives Bobby Scott (VA-03), Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, Pat Ryan (NY-18), representing the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), representing the U.S. Naval Academy, Joe Courtney (CT-02), representing the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, and Chris Deluzio (PA-17).

Secretary Hegseth is asked to provide a response by October 16, 2026. The full letter can be found here.

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces Nearly $730,000 for El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center to Improve the Health and Well-Being of Inland Empire Residents
text:
El Sol will use the grant to teach and connect people to healthcare

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced a $728,610 federal grant for El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center to hire more Community Health Workers and reach more people in the Inland Empire who need help finding healthcare and social resources.

El Sol’s health workers build trust with residents, teach them about their health in ways that match their culture and language, figure out their health needs and find the right doctors and care. Additionally, health workers connect people to basic needs support like housing, food assistance, domestic violence shelters, transportation, Medicare, Medi-Cal and more.

“Everyone deserves to find a doctor that’s right for them or get help with food, housing and other needs,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “El Sol’s Community Health Workers help build a bridge between our neighbors and the healthcare and support they need. This grant will bring more of these workers to our communities so that people in the Inland Empire can be healthy, happy and successful.”

“This federal investment recognizes the vital role that community-based organizations play in reaching people where they are and building trust where it matters most,” said Alexander Fajardo, Executive Director, El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center. “At El Sol, we will use these resources to strengthen our community health worker workforce and expand our ability to connect individuals and families with health education, resources, and support. When we invest in trusted community organizations, we invest directly in the health and well-being of our communities.”

This funding comes from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ Mental Health & Substance Abuse Service Grants.

title: Ansari Secures Long-Delayed Combat-Related Compensation for Wounded Marine Veteran
text:
PHOENIX – Last week, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) met with Marine Corps combat veteran Sergeant Alecsaiah Tree, whose combat-related compensation claim was delayed five months past the processing times after nearly two years without an update. Following concerted efforts by Ansari’s office, Sergeant Tree secured approval for Combat-Related Special Compensation with a 100 percent combat-related disability rating, retroactive to April 1, 2024.

“Sergeant Tree served our country for more than 11 years and was wounded while helping evacuate people from Afghanistan. He should not have had to wait this long for the compensation he earned,” said Rep. Ansari. “I’m glad my office was able to help him secure approval. Our responsibility to service members continues long after they leave the military, and I remain committed to helping Arizona veterans access the benefits and support they deserve.”

“After waiting nearly two years for an update, I’m grateful that Congresswoman Ansari’s office helped move my case forward,” said Sergeant Tree. “Having someone follow up and help me navigate the process made a real difference. Veterans should be able to get the benefits they earned without having to fight for them.”

Sergeant Tree was wounded in the August 26, 2021, attack at Abbey Gate during the military evacuation from Afghanistan. He contacted Rep. Ansari’s office after waiting 23 months for an update on his compensation request—five months beyond the agency’s stated processing timeframe. Ansari’s office contacted the Department of the Navy and worked to get Sergeant Tree’s claim processed.

Ansari with Sergeant Tree and his service dog, Zeus

AZ-03 residents in need of assistance with federal agencies are encouraged to reach out to Rep. Ansari’s office. Visit ansari.house.gov or contact her Phoenix office by phone at (602) 956-2285.

title: Riley Gaines Endorses Arrington Bill to Protect Women’s Sports
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, House Budget Chairman Jodey Arrington (TX-19) announced that he is teaming up with 12-time NCAA All-American and women’s sports advocate Riley Gaines to pass his Title IX Clarification Act, legislation to codify that Title IX nondiscrimination requirements tied to federal education funding are based on the biological reality of sex.

“Riley Gaines is one of the most impactful voices in the fight to protect women’s sports, which is why I’m thrilled to have her as a champion for my Title IX Clarification Act,” said Chairman Arrington. “Title IX was created to provide equal opportunity for our daughters, not to push a radical gender ideology that jeopardizes their safety, and taxpayer dollars should not be used to advance extreme social policies. My legislation stops the abuse of Title IX by affirming a simple truth: there are only two sexes — male and female — and we cannot allow protections for our daughters to be erased the next time a Democrat administration takes control of the White House. I’m proud to stand with Riley in this fight and grateful to have her support as we work together to get this bill across the finish line.”

“Title IX was created to ensure that women and girls have equal opportunities in education and athletics,” said Riley Gaines. “That promise only means something if the word ‘sex’ actually means sex. I support Congressman Jodey Arrington’s Title IX Clarification Act because Americans should not have to wonder what protections under Title IX mean from one administration to the next. The law should be clear, consistent, and grounded in biological reality as it was intended in 1972. The American people have had enough of the attacks on women and the truth. We are desperate for clarity, honesty, and accountability. Thanks to Congressman Arrington for leading the charge.”

Background:

Chairman Arrington introduced the Title IX Clarification Act (H.R. 8781) on May 13, 2026. The legislation defines “sex” under Title IX as an individual’s biologically determined sex, either male or female, for education programs and activities receiving federal financial assistance.

The bill advanced out of the House Committee on Education and Workforce on July 21, 2026.

The bill establishes statutory definitions for “male” and “female” under Title IX and would apply those definitions to education programs and activities receiving federal financial assistance after enactment.

On October 1, 2026, Chairman Arrington published an opinion in the Daily Caller calling on Congress to define biological sex in Title IX and establish a statutory standard that does not depend on changing administrative interpretations.
