title: Kingsley Field Authorized to Receive F-35s!
text:
Klamath Falls — Congressman Cliff Bentz (R-OR) is delighted to announce today that the Secretary of the Air Force, Dr. Troy Meink, signed the Record of Decision, giving Kingsley Field Oregon Air National Guard Base, home of the 173rd Fighter Wing, formal authorization to begin preparations for a squadron of F-35A Lightning II jets.

The Record of Decision allows Kingsley Field to begin facility construction for F-35A Lighting II jets set to arrive in Summer 2027.

The Congressman and his staff have worked closely with Department of the Air Force, the Trump Administration, and Kingsley Field to identify and qualify the Kingsley Field airbase as the premier location for the jet.

The Congressman would like to thank the National Guard Bureau, Secretary Troy Meink, the Oregon National Guard, Colonel Adam Gaudinski (Commander of the 173rd Fighter Wing), and Micah Lambert (Deputy Commander of the 173rd Fighter Wing) for their hard work and dedication in the transition of Kingsley Field from the F-15C Eagle to the F-35A Lightning II.

Said Congressman Bentz: “The decision by Airforce Secretary Meink is extraordinarily good news for Kingsley Field, Klamath Falls, the State of Oregon, and our nation. The airspace in Southern and Eastern Oregon provides an immensely large and mostly empty airspace for absolutely essential training of the men and women who will fly one of the most amazing aircraft in the world, the F-35A Lightning II. This decision is also of significant importance to the economic future of the Klamath Basin and the people who live there. A huge thank you is due to the leadership at Kingsley Field, the Oregon National Guard, and the National Guard Bureau in Washington, D.C.”

Said Colonel Gaudinski: “Kingsley Field is officially an F-35 base, securing its place at the forefront of American airpower for generations to come. From here, we will forge the fighter pilots who will deter our adversaries, defend our nation, and ensure America maintains air supremacy anywhere in the world. America’s Air Supremacy starts here.

“Representative Cliff Bentz has been an incredible champion for Kingsley Field and the men and women of the 173d Fighter Wing. His leadership, advocacy, and unwavering support helped make today possible, ensuring Kingsley will train America’s F-35 pilots and strengthen our nation’s airpower for generations to come. We are incredibly grateful for his commitment to Kingsley, Southern Oregon, and our national defense.”

title: Congressional 4-H Caucus Leaders Introduce National 4-H Week Resolution
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15), Angie Craig (MN-02), and Andy Harris (MD-01), co-chairs of the bipartisan 4-H Caucus, introduced a resolution today to designate the week of October 4 through October 10 as "National 4-H Week.”

As the youth development program of the Cooperative Extension System of Land-Grant Universities, 4-H engages young people in hands-on projects in the critical areas of agriculture, health, science, and civic leadership. 4-H is the largest youth development organization in the country, with six million current members and 35 million alumni.

“Georgia is proud to be an early home for 4 H, starting in 1904, with programs reaching every county in our state and preparing young people to lead in agriculture, science, and civic life. I’ve had the pleasure to meet with National 4 H Council President & CEO Jill Bramble to discuss how 4 H continues to strengthen youth leadership nationwide. As an Eagle Scout, I know how essential positive role models and supportive environments are for young people, and 4 H delivers that every day. As Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Appropriations Subcommittee, I remain committed to investing in programs that uplift rural communities and build a stronger future for Georgia and our nation,” Rep. Bishop said.

“The work ethic and curiosity of each 4-H member I’ve met over the years is one of the reasons I feel so confident in the future of our country's agriculture industry. I am proud to introduce this bipartisan resolution to recognize the important work of 4-H members across the country, and encourage others to get involved as well,” Rep. Thompson said.

“The work that 4-H does to develop our youth into the next generation of leaders in agriculture and beyond is more important than ever. American agriculture has come under great pressure, and fostering a love of agriculture in young people is crucial for America’s future. I am proud to celebrate 4-H today and stand with them as they work to empower America’s youth,” Rep. Craig said.

“4-H gives young people in Maryland and across our nation the chance to experience agriculture firsthand. Representing farming communities across Maryland’s First District, I understand the hard work that farming requires and why it matters for young people to learn about agriculture and the work behind it. I’m proud to recognize National 4-H Week and the millions of young Americans who participate in 4-H,” Rep. Harris said.

“We are grateful for the bipartisan support of the Congressional 4-H Caucus and its recognition of the millions of young people who are building the skills and confidence to be ready for work and life. For nearly 125 years, 4-H and Cooperative Extension have helped young people discover what they’re capable of, explore career skills and opportunities, and become Beyond Ready for what comes next,” National 4-H Council President and CEO Jill Bramble said.

Read the full resolution here.

title: NEW DOE AWARD TO IMPROVE GRID AND POSITIVELY IMPACT FAMILIES IN THE 4TH DISTRICT
text:
Lone Tree, CO — Rep. Lauren Boebert (CO-04) continues to work with the U.S. Department of Energy to improve the grid in Colorado, including a new $250 million award from the Department’s Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades (SPARK) program.

"This Department of Energy announcement is about keeping the lights on and the bill down for families in the 4th District,” Rep. Boebert said. “The line starts in Lamar. That is our district. Families in Prowers, Kiowa, Cheyenne, Lincoln, and the rest of the Eastern Plains need power they can count on.”

“These selected SPARK projects put advanced transmission technologies to work, modernizing critical infrastructure, maximizing the capacity of existing lines, and unlocking more than 20 gigawatts of additional grid capacity,” said Office of Electricity Assistant Secretary Catherine Jereza.

"We need to do everything we can to improve reliability, affordability, and cost for households, farms, and small towns,” Rep. Boebert said. “We need to do as much as possible to improve energy in Colorado and reduce costs for families. More transfer capacity can help families avoid outages and bring in power when we need it. The 4th District will take transmission that serves agriculture, oil and gas, and rural families.”

The award will upgrade the Lamar Tie. The project moves the Colorado end of the connection from Lamar to the May Valley substation and ties it into the Power Pathway network on the Eastern Plains. It raises transfer capacity from 210 megawatts to 700 megawatts, with room to reach 2,000 megawatts.

title: Washington Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Emily Randall (D, WA-06), and Representatives Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

title: Rep. Chu Introduces Resolution to Designate October 5th as National Beyond the Milky Way Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced a resolution to designate October 5, 2026, as “National Beyond the Milky Way Day,” commemorating the groundbreaking discovery that the Milky Way is just one of countless galaxies and celebrating the scientific research that fundamentally transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe.

The resolution recognizes a transformative breakthrough in astronomy made possible by American scientific leadership, the pioneering work of astronomers at Carnegie Science, and the world-class facilities at Mount Wilson Observatory in the San Gabriel Mountains.

On October 5, 1923, Carnegie Science astronomer Edwin Powell Hubble, working overnight at Mount Wilson Observatory, identified a Cepheid variable star in what was then thought to be the Andromeda Nebula. Using the period-luminosity relationship discovered by Harvard astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt, now known as Leavitt’s Law, Hubble was able to determine the star’s distance from Earth. His observations provided decisive evidence that Andromeda was not a nebula within the Milky Way, but an entirely separate galaxy far beyond its boundaries.

This discovery fundamentally transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe, establishing that the Milky Way was not the entirety of the universe, but just one galaxy among countless others in an unimaginably vast universe. It remains one of the most consequential discoveries in the history of astronomy.

“More than a century ago, right here in the San Gabriel Mountains, a groundbreaking discovery forever changed humanity’s understanding of our place in the universe,” said Rep. Chu. “I’m proud to honor the scientists and institutions whose pioneering work made that discovery possible. Their achievement is a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish when we invest in scientific research, discovery, and collaboration, and I will always fight to ensure America continues making those investments for generations to come.”

"Our founder, Andrew Carnegie, foresaw that investing in scientific research would pay dividends for all of humankind. Discovery science, like the astronomical breakthroughs pioneered by Edwin Hubble, have fed our collective hunger to understand our place in the universe and we continue to push the boundaries of discovery today," said Carnegie Science President John Mulchaey. "We are so grateful to Rep. Judy Chu for her tireless advocacy for science both here in Pasadena and nationwide. Her work enables the next generation of Hubbles and Leavitts to advance our knowledge of the natural world."

The resolution is co-sponsored by Reps. Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), and Ted Lieu (CA-36).

It is endorsed by Carnegie Science.

title: Ciscomani Leads Bipartisan, Bicameral Effort to Honor Arizona Marine Nicholas Quets
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani today introduced a bipartisan, bicameral legislative package to honor the life and legacy of Arizona Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets and strengthen protections for Americans traveling in Mexico. After Nicholas was tragically killed while traveling in Mexico, Ciscomani has worked to ensure his life is honored and turn this tragedy into meaningful action to better protect American families traveling abroad.

The package would honor Nicholas’s service, strengthen coordination between the United States and Mexico in responding to crimes against Americans, and advance protections for Americans traveling in Mexico.

The package, led by Representative Ciscomani, includes:

A resolution honoring Nicholas’s life and service, recognizing his sacrifice and dedication to our country.

The Nicholas Douglas Quets U.S.-Mexico Rapid Response for Victims of Crime Act, which would strengthen coordination between the United States and Mexico to ensure American victims of crime receive timely support and assistance.

Representative Ciscomani is also proud to have recently joined Representative Eli Crane in introducing the Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Safety Travel Act.

"Nicholas was a true American hero," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "His tragic passing demands action and lasting change. It is an honor to work closely with Nicholas’s family, Senator Kelly, and Rep. Crane on this much-needed package to honor Nicholas’ life and legacy. These legislative measures represent a long-overdue response, and I will fight relentlessly to ensure this bipartisan package receives the national attention and momentum required to protect Americans and deliver justice in Nicholas’ name."

"We thank Juan Ciscomani for his bipartisan leadership in working with Senator Kelly and Representative Crane to introduce a comprehensive legislative package, including a resolution honoring my son’s legacy and service, the Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Travel Safety Act, and the Nicholas Douglas Quets U.S.-Mexico Rapid Response for Victims of Crime Act. Representative Ciscomani reached out to our family within days of the targeted attack against Nicholas by the Sinaloa cartel on October 18, 2024. Nicholas was an innocent U.S. Marine Corps veteran and Pima County employee, and Representative Ciscomani has stood by our family ever since. Preventing tragedies like Nick’s is best achieved when governments and agencies work together to confront and neutralize the transnational threats that plague us all. This legislative package, which many would call common sense, strengthens cooperation and helps ensure that victims of violent crime and their families receive the justice envisioned as a foundation of the U.S. Constitution. We are honored by Representative Ciscomani’s sponsorship of this legislation, and we believe his commitment to Nick’s case is emblematic of his commitment to all of his constituents," said Warren D. (Doug) Quets, Jr. Lieutenant Colonel (Retired), U.S. Army, Nicholas Quets’ father.

"Nicholas Quets, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and hardworking member of his community, represented the very best of America. While driving to Puerto Peñasco, Nicholas was chased down and murdered by Sinaloa Cartel gunmen after fleeing an illegal checkpoint. The cowardly killing of this tremendous young man is yet another tragic instance of Americans being targeted by sinister cartels that operate with near-total impunity across Mexico. After listening to his father, retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel Doug Quets, I was honored to work with him and Representative Juan Ciscomani on two bills and a resolution in Nicholas’ name. Our measures will warn travelers of dangerous areas before they cross the border, push for faster coordination with Mexican authorities when U.S. citizens are victims of serious crimes, formally honor his service, and condemn the criminals responsible for his death. No family should ever endure what the Quets family has, and I’m hopeful this approach will save innocent lives, hold these murderous organizations accountable, and ensure this fallen patriot is never forgotten," said Rep. Eli Crane.

Nicholas Quets, a Tucson native and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, was murdered on October 18, 2024, in Mexico during a vicious attack perpetrated by Sinaloa Cartel-affiliated narcoterrorists. In the wake of this act of violence, Nicholas’s family has led the charge to transform their grief into real action, fortifying national security and demanding robust safeguards for Americans who fall victim to violent crime abroad.

The resolution honoring Nicholas Douglas Quets recognizes his life and service, pays tribute to his family and unequivocally condemns cartel violence. The Nicholas Douglas Quets U.S.-Mexico Rapid Response for Victims of Crime Act would establish a robust, binational rapid response protocol for serious crimes against U.S. citizens in Mexico therefore fortifying communication and coordination between U.S. and Mexican authorities, leading to mandating improved evidence sharing and joint investigative and extradition efforts to guarantee transparent communication with victims’ families.​ The Nicholas Douglas Quets Border Travel Safety Act would mandate warning signage at land ports of entry and along routes near high-risk areas identified in Department of State travel advisories. It would equip travelers with up-to-the-minute safety information and digital resources, while requiring forcing heightened coordination with state and local transportation and public safety agencies.

​This legislative package builds upon Rep. Ciscomani’s determined efforts to defend Americans and law enforcement along the southern border. As the representative of a border district, Ciscomani has led the fight for increased accountability for those who threaten law enforcement, including spearheading the Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act, which passed the House to enact tough federal penalties for individuals who fail to yield during high-speed pursuits involving federal, state, or local law enforcement supporting the federal government.

​Building on their shared commitment to protect Arizonans, Reps. Ciscomani and Crane are working to turn Nicholas’ tragic death into meaningful action. Their efforts will strengthen protections for Americans, improve U.S.-Mexico coordination, and hold those responsible for violence against Americans fully accountable for their actions.

Rep. Ciscomani serves as lead sponsor of the Quets resolution and Rapid Response Act, with Rep. Crane as co-lead. Rep. Crane leads the Border Travel Safety Act, with Rep. Ciscomani as co-lead. Each bill has a Senate companion introduced by Senator Kelly earlier this year.

title: ICYMI: Ciscomani Celebrates Grand Opening of the Albers Aerospace Location in Tucson
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani joined the Tucson community for the ribbon-cutting ceremony of Albers Aerospace Profile, a veteran-owned company specializing in defense and aerospace container solutions. The company’s expansion strengthens Southern Arizona’s growing defense and aerospace manufacturing sector, bringing new jobs and investment to the region.

"Time after time, this community continues to demonstrate that it’s the right place to invest, and the people here are the right people to help that growth and investment. This is the right place for you all to be, and we welcome you with arms wide open," said Representative Ciscomani. "I am proud to support this team of warfighters who make a difference in our communities by strengthening our local economy, creating more jobs in our district, and helping lay the foundation for stronger national security."

Ciscomani was joined at the grand opening by Marine Corps Colonel John Albers, founder and CEO of Albers Aerospace, to celebrate the company’s new investment in Southern Arizona.

"We are honored to have the Congressman attend today. The values he represents in serving his district mirror Albers Aerospace’s values," said Albers. "We chose to expand in Tucson because of the tremendous defense ecosystem. We look forward to making an impact here together with our teammates, customers, and community."

The expansion builds on Albers Aerospace’s acquisition of local precision manufacturer Parallel Ventures in early 2025. The new Tucson location is expected to double the company’s local workforce, creating opportunities for manufacturing engineers, CNC programmers and machine operators, assembly technicians, and inspectors.

Local leaders, business organizations, and community stakeholders joined the September grand opening to celebrate the investment and its potential to support continued regional economic growth.

"Albers Aerospace represents exactly the type of advanced manufacturing aerospace and defense company we want to see grow and succeed," said Pima County District 1 Supervisor Rex Scott. "With over 70,000 Pima County residents employed in aerospace and defense, its major role in our regional and statewide economy is undeniable. We will see continued growth and prosperity as more companies like Albers Aerospace choose to invest here. That is why today’s milestone is so significant."

"We want to thank you for your investment, and we welcome you," said Joe Sell, president and CEO of The Chamber of Southern Arizona, extending congratulations on behalf of the organization’s board of directors and 1,500 investors. "This kind of investment is what pays the bills. This is how you get roads built, how you get parks built. It takes a tax base. So we thank you."

Ciscomani’s support for Arizona’s workforce extends beyond economic development to ensuring veterans have the tools and opportunities to succeed in civilian careers. As a member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, he has championed legislation to expand career and educational opportunities for nearly 80,000 veterans in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District and veterans nationwide.

Additionally, Ciscomani has led efforts to strengthen the Veterans Readiness and Employment Program through the Veterans Readiness and Employment Program Integrity Act (H.R. 3579), which focuses on evaluating program effectiveness, collecting data on veteran employment outcomes, and identifying opportunities for improvement. Building upon these efforts for local veterans, the House passed Ciscomani’s VETS Opportunity Act of 2025 (H.R. 1458) earlier this year which aims to modernize GI Bill benefits by expanding educational opportunities and allowing veterans to use their earned benefits for nontraditional education pathways.

title: Davids Celebrates Opening of KCKCC Downtown Center, Highlighting Her Secured Investment for Workforce Training
text:
KANSAS CITY, KS — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined Kansas City Kansas Community College (KCKCC) leadership, local officials, and community partners for the official dedication of the new downtown Community Education, Health and Wellness Center. During the ceremony, Davids highlighted nearly $2 million in federal funding she secured to outfit KCKCC’s Automated Engineering Technology Program with state-of-the-art training equipment.

"If we want a future that is 'Made in Kansas,' we have to give our students the tools to actually build it right here at home," said Davids. "This new Downtown Center is a direct pipeline to good-paying jobs. I was proud to work across the aisle to deliver federal investments so KCKCC students can train on the exact, state-of-the-art automation systems used in high-tech manufacturing and defense today. This is about bypassing D.C. politics, setting our workers up to succeed, and keeping our local economy moving forward."

The $1.9 million secured by Davids equips KCKCC’s Automation Engineering Technology program with real-world machinery, preparing students directly for high-demand, high-wage roles in advanced manufacturing and logistics. By training on the exact, state-of-the-art automation systems used across modern industrial and defense sectors, students will gain the hands-on experience needed to transition seamlessly from the classroom straight into high-paying local careers.

The new facility, a public-private partnership between KCKCC, Swope Health, and Community America Credit Union, offers holistic education, healthcare, and career training services.

title: Davids Fights Washington Healthcare Cuts with Plan to Lower Costs, Protect Kansas Hospitals
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Sharice Davids (KS-03) introduced a comprehensive package of healthcare legislation that directly counters Washington’s recent healthcare rollbacks, which are increasing monthly costs and closing rural hospitals. Davids’ efforts would protect Kansas families from rising medical costs, block new federal red tape, and keep local hospitals and health clinics open.

“At a time when families are stretching every dollar to cover groceries, energy, and housing, Washington shouldn't be making healthcare more expensive just to give billionaires a tax break,” said Davids. “I’m fighting back because hard-working Kansans deserve practical solutions, not higher medical bills and shuttered clinic doors. My healthcare package focuses on what actually matters to our neighbors: bringing down out-of-pocket costs, cutting through bureaucratic red tape, and making sure our local hospitals and birthing centers stay open.”

Last year, Davids voted against the extreme, partisan budget law, which included the largest cuts to Medicaid in American history. The law strips health coverage from 92,937 Kansans, puts six rural hospitals at risk of closure, restricts reproductive healthcare, and increases ACA premiums by an average of $708 per year for families in Kansas’ Third District.

Medicaid is a lifeline for Kansas hospitals, especially in rural communities, and the cuts could take more than $78 million a year from hospitals, increasing uncompensated care costs and potentially forcing Kansans to travel farther for emergency or specialized care. Higher ACA premiums could also push healthier people out of the insurance market, driving costs even higher for those who remain.

While party leaders in D.C. continue pushing partisan legislation that raises costs on working families, Davids’ package is focused on common-sense, bipartisan solutions that deliver tangible savings and protect access to care across Kansas.

Restoring eliminated tax credits: The Healthy Communities Act would permanently restore enhanced ACA tax credits, saving Kansas families an average of $700 a year on premiums. It would also eliminate new Medicaid paperwork requirements, increase incentives for states like Kansas to expand coverage to working adults, and close Kansas’ Medicaid coverage gap, giving thousands of low-income Kansans access to ACA tax credits.

Keeping rural operating rooms open: The Rural Surgery Sustainability Act would raise the federal reimbursement cap for surgical procedures at critical access hospitals, helping hospitals afford the nurse anesthetists needed to keep surgical services running.

“Access to local surgical procedures and maternity care is essential for rural Kansas communities, and maintaining a reliable anesthesia care team is critical to providing those services. However, the current Medicare reimbursement threshold has not been updated in more than two decades despite significant increases in the cost of recruiting and retaining these professionals. Updating this outdated policy would give rural hospitals greater flexibility to sustain these essential services and better meet the needs of their communities,” said Chad Austin, President and CEO, Kansas Hospital Association.

Protecting seniors from insurance discrimination: The Guaranteeing Access to Supplemental Plans Act would give seniors an annual opportunity to switch Medicare Supplement plans without being denied coverage or charged more because of a pre-existing condition.

“My husband and I have been experiencing Medigap premium increases that are quite high considering how frequent they are. We are penalized for having a couple of minor “pre-existing” conditions, one of which requires no treatment. We are held hostage by our insurance providers because we cannot change companies without underwriting, resulting in even higher rates or refusal of coverage. Who at 65 or older does not have some form of a pre-existing condition? I appreciate Rep. Davids’ efforts to address this problem and work toward a solution that gives seniors more options and protects us from being trapped by our insurance providers,” said Shelly Toft, Lenexa resident.

Protecting rural hospitals from sudden funding cuts: The Long-Term Rural Health Investment Act would phase in reimbursement changes and prevent abrupt federal payment limits from putting rural emergency care at risk.

Keeping local clinics open when hospitals close: The Access to Community Care Act would prioritize federal grants for safety-net clinics that take on patients displaced by nearby healthcare facility closures, helping families maintain access to local primary care.

Keeping maternity care close to home: The Maternity Care for Rural Communities Act would protect labor and delivery services at rural and Tribal hospitals from federal funding cuts, helping prevent new maternity care deserts.

Making healthcare available to people with early-onset Alzheimer’s: The Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Coverage Act would allow adults diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s who do not qualify for Social Security Disability to buy into Medicare and access treatment, prescriptions, and specialized care.

“When my husband was diagnosed with younger-onset Alzheimer’s, our world turned upside down — and finding out he didn't qualify for Medicare because they spent years raising our children at home felt like a punch in the gut. Stay-at-home parents sacrifice so much for their families, and they shouldn't be cut off from life-saving healthcare when tragedy strikes. This bill is a true lifeline. I am so grateful to Representative Davids for standing up for families like mine, listening to our pain, and taking real action to fix this broken system,” said Nina Westvold, Overland Park resident.

"Healthcare costs are putting an enormous strain on Kansas families,” said April Holman, Executive Director, Alliance for a Healthy Kansas. “We hear from Kansans who are putting off needed care, rationing medication, or going without necessities to afford basic medical care. As premiums and deductibles continue to rise, so do medical debt. We need comprehensive solutions to lower costs, protect access to care in rural communities, and ensure every Kansan has access to affordable, quality healthcare in every stage of life."

“The high cost of living is crippling Kansas families, and the soaring costs of health care are a top concern," said David Jordan, President and CEO of the United Methodist Health Ministry Fund. "Unfortunately, health care costs will only go up for Kansans due to HR 1 and the failure of Congress to extend enhanced premium tax credits. Representative Sharice Davids’ (KS-03) comprehensive health care package will help reverse harmful cuts and help make care more affordable. The package will also help protect vulnerable rural Kansas hospitals and help keep maternity care close to home. This package is win for Kansas families, Kansas hospitals and providers, and Kansas communities.”

title: Congresswoman Dean Reintroduces the Improving Justice Programs through Science Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) reintroduced legislation to create a Science Advisory Board at the Office of Justice Programs (OJP) within the Department of Justice (DOJ). The Board will be responsible for integrating scientific knowledge into crime-reduction efforts, as well as for using research, data, and evidence to guide the OJP’s grants, programs, and activities. The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act is cosponsored by Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05).

The Science Advisory Board was originally chartered by the Obama Administration in 2010 and provided OJP with guidance in proactive criminal justice reform efforts, including developing trauma-informed care, building trust between police and communities, and understating youth brain development and its implications for juvenile justice programs. The Board also made numerous contributions to the public safety investments of OJP, including guidelines for implementing and evaluating place-based crime reduction interventions and a tool for police departments to enhance communications with communities about their operations and successes.

“Americans want our criminal justice system to do its job — make all of us safer not just by punishing criminals today, but also by preventing crime in the future,” Rep. Dean said. Reducing recidivism and protecting our communities requires a deliberate strategy built on the best available data and science. The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act would create a Science Advisory Board to advise on evidence-based criminal justice policies and ensure that we are getting the highest quality data to inform future decisions. This is about getting the most out of our tax dollars, and making our streets safer today, tomorrow, and years from now.”

“In order to do justice, particularly with respect to juveniles, it is important that we have access to the best current research and information,” Rep. Scanlon said. “Advances in science which can promote both public safety and rehabilitation, and reduce recidivism, must be incorporated in our criminal justice system. I’m proud to join Rep. Dean in introducing this bill to make our justice system more effective and fair.”

This bill will establish a Science Advisory Board comprised of 26 criminologists and criminal justice researchers appointed by the Attorney General for terms of four years. The Board will:

Meet on a regular basis to discuss the relationship between science, research, and ongoing criminal and juvenile justice departmental activities;

Coordinate with other Federal, State, local, tribal, territorial, and private sector partners; and

Advise the Assistant Attorney General on policy development, program implementation, and evaluation; identify research needs and opportunities and make policy recommendations.

The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act is endorsed by American Psychological Association, American Political Science Association, American Sociological Association, Consortium of Social Science Associations, Council of Professional Associations on Federal Statistics, and Union of Concerned Scientists. Congresswoman Dean previously introduced the Improving Justice Programs through Science Act during her first term, in the 116th Congress, as well as the 117th Congress.

Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

title: Dingell, Whitehouse Introduce Bill to Create Alert System to Notify Survivors of Illegal Gun Purchase Attempts by Domestic Abusers
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) introduced the Domestic Violence Survivors Alerted for Emergency (SAFE) Notice Act, new legislation to establish notification systems that would alert survivors of domestic violence offenses when their abuser attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Loopholes in federal and state law can allow domestic violence offenders to purchase guns notwithstanding their criminal history – situations that can be life threatening for survivors. Even when offenders are unsuccessful, the fact they are trying to purchase a firearm illegally can be a warning sign for survivors. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help keep survivors safe by setting up systems to notify domestic violence survivors when an abusive partner has obtained or is trying to obtain a firearm illegally.

“When a domestic violence survivor is rebuilding their life, safety and peace of mind are everything. We know that an abusive partner’s access to a firearm dramatically increases the risk of fatal violence. By ensuring survivors receive immediate alerts if an offender attempts to purchase a gun illegally, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act empowers victims with time-sensitive information that can save lives,” said Congresswoman Dingell.

“I spent years prosecuting domestic violence cases in Rhode Island, and I know the toll it can take on survivors as they rebuild their lives. Our legislation will help ensure survivors are made aware when the government has information about an abuser’s attempt to buy a firearm, so survivors and their loved ones can make decisions in the interest of their own safety and wellbeing,” said Senator Whitehouse.

Domestic violence offenders and protective order respondents are generally prohibited under federal and many state laws from purchasing firearms. However, that prohibition does not always stop offenders from trying to purchase firearms anyway. FBI data shows that almost 160,000 gun purchases were denied from 2018 to 2023 because of the purchaser’s domestic violence background. These situations can be life threatening for people in abusive situations, especially women. An abusive partner’s access to a gun significantly increases the risk of an intimate partner homicide.

The bicameral Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure domestic violence survivors are notified when an abusive partner is trying to obtain a firearm illegally.

Specifically, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would:

Direct the FBI to establish a notification system to alert survivors of federal domestic violence offenses when the offender attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Permit survivors to register or de-register at will.

Provide key alerts about an offender’s attempted illegal firearm purchase, including if the sale went through or law enforcement has recovered the firearm.

Provide additional alerts about related events, such as a pardon that restores an offender’s ability to purchase firearms legally.

Authorize grants for states to pilot state-run alert systems, so survivors can receive alerts related to protective orders and non-federal domestic violence offenses.

Enable states to use funds to expand existing systems or set up new ones.

Require reports on the success of and challenges related to these pilot projects, including recommendations for expanding the projects to other states.

“Survivors often must make complex safety decisions in real time, and having timely information about an abusive partner’s attempt to obtain a firearm can be critical to that decision-making. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure survivors have access to information that could allow them to take additional safety precautions, seek support, and make informed decisions for themselves and their families. The Hotline is grateful to Rep. Debbie Dingell and Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse for introducing this legislation and for their continued commitment to the safety and well-being of survivors of domestic violence,” said Katie Ray-Jones, Chief Executive Officer of the National Domestic Violence Hotline.

“The National District Attorneys Association is proud to support the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act, which establishes a common-sense notification system to alert victims when offenders unlawfully attempt to acquire a firearm as well as other firearm-related updates. NDAA commends this victim-centered approach that promotes public safety,” said Nelson Bunn, Executive Director of the National District Attorneys Association.

title: DelBene Moves to Force Trump Administration to Release Files on AI Medicare Experiment
text:
Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) announced that she is filing a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to force the Trump administration to release unseen information on the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) program, which pays private companies to use AI to review Medicare claims.

Since the program began in January in Washington and five other states, patients have been left in severe pain and unable to access care prescribed by their doctors. In June, DelBene announced that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) ordered the company administering WISeR in Washington to submit a corrective action plan for delays in reviewing claims following an audit. Neither the audit nor the corrective action plan has been released to Congress or the public. DelBene previously requested information on the model's performance from the administration and then moved to require CMS to release these documents through an amendment during a House Ways & Means Committee markup. The majority of Ways & Means Republicans rejected the amendment by an 18-19 vote.

DelBene announced her latest move to force the release of these documents and hold the administration accountable in an op-ed in the Everett Herald.

“Washington seniors have borne the brunt of this experimental program’s malfunctions,” DelBene wrote. “From January to March, over half of the claims submitted in Washington were denied and far exceeded the 72-hour decision deadline. This triggered an internal CMS audit and corrective action plan. This shouldn’t come as a surprise because the program pays these private companies for every claim they deny, which incentivizes them to reject more care.”

“The audit and corrective action plan have never been released, which would further help inform lawmakers, health care providers, and patients about how WISeR is failing to function,” DelBene continued. “This stonewalling must end. That’s why I am filing a new FOIA request for these specific documents in addition to the audits and corrective action plans of any other private company participating in WISeR.”

This effort follows a bombshell report from the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EEF) on the failures of WISeR that detailed widespread delays and denials, rushed implementation, and incentives for private companies reviewing claims to deny care. EFF obtained access to the documents uncovered in the report through a FOIA request and lawsuit. The report also revealed that the administration plans to expand WISeR to cancer treatments and other types of care despite clear, documented evidence of the program’s flaws.

DelBene introduced legislation last November to repeal WISeR and has led multiple other legislative efforts to stop the program.

title: WA Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Answers About Forest Service Coordination with ICE on Public Lands
text:
Today, Representatives Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Emily Randall (WA-06), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), and Andrea Salinas (OR-06) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz demanding answers and transparency regarding recent immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) may have coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.

As of October 1, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” the lawmakers wrote.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganization efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on its original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced it would still close 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of its worst wildfire seasons to date, with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The lawmakers concluded the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

The full letter can be found here.

title: Doggett Statement on New GAO Report on Insurer-Owned Pharmacies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Ranking Member of the House Ways & Means Health Subcommittee, released the following statement after a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report he requested found that large health insurers often give their own pharmacies better terms on lower-cost generic drugs:

“There is a real danger that consumers and taxpayers are being ripped off by giant health conglomerates. Three insurer-pharmacy benefit managers control 80% of prescription drug claims. This report is the first detailed study of these insurer-pharmacy contracts and exposes frequent preferential treatment for insurer-owned pharmacies. Americans are struggling with higher and higher costs for medications and other care. Congress must act to restrain health care monopolies and oligopolies.”

title: Congressman Don Davis Introduces Bill to Ban Federal Candidates from Betting on Their Own Elections
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) introduced the No Betting on Your Own Race Act, which would ban federal candidates seeking elected office from trades tied to their own races.

The No Betting on Your Own Race Act would prohibit federal candidates, their spouses or dependent children, and authorized campaign committees from buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, or holding contracts tied to the candidate’s election.

"We don't want our athletes to bet on their games. A candidate running for federal elected office should be treated exactly the same and should not be allowed to trade on their own election," said Congressman Don Davis. "The No Betting on Your Own Race Act aims to prevent market interference, insider trading, as well as candidates and their family members from cashing in. To establish consistency and ensure all federal candidate campaign committees understand this, Congress must pass this common-sense legislation."

Violators will incur a $10,000 civil penalty for each violation. If there is a net financial gain, the penalty will be three times the gain, or $10,000, whichever is greater. The new law also provides that a candidate who is running for office at the federal level must be notified during the filing period.

title: Congresswoman Escobar Statement on Fort Bliss Data Center Project Update
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) released the following statement after attending a community stakeholder meeting on the Fort Bliss data center project:

“Today, the Army and Carlyle Group held a meeting of El Paso community stakeholders to discuss the latest updates on the Fort Bliss data center.

"Since March, when my team and I first learned of this project, we have asked that the public and local representatives be kept in the loop and be allowed to voice their concerns and ask questions. I’m grateful to the Army and Carlyle for their continued engagement.

"I’ve consistently had a number of requests, including that they:

Move the data center far away from any neighborhood;

Preserve our water;

Use renewable energy for the electrical generation;

Be transparent and accountable.

"Today we learned that the location of the data center has indeed been moved, but it is still too close to residential areas. Close proximity to homes is not acceptable, and I will continue to advocate for a different location.

"We also learned that their water use will likely be of brackish water that will be sent to the Kay Bailey Hutchison Plant for desalination, which I see as a positive development. And while the scale of the data center has also been reduced, they are still on track to utilize gas generation for their power needs. The gas generation for power remains an additional serious concern. We must protect our community’s air quality, and I will continue to push for the use of renewable energy.

"As more information becomes available, my team and I will continue to keep the community updated."

title: Nation’s Largest Law Enforcement Organization Endorses Figures’ Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for the Children of Police Officers
text:
MONTGOMERY – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures announced that the National Fraternal Order of Police – the nation’s largest organization of sworn law enforcement officers – has endorsed his bipartisan bill, the Public Service Educational Assistance Act, to cover the cost of college and job training for the children of law enforcement officers, other first responders, educators, and social workers.

“Every day, our police officers put their lives on the line to keep our streets and communities safe,” said Figures. “They and their families make tremendous sacrifices for us, and we should be there to give back to them in any way that we can. That’s why I introduced this bipartisan bill to recognize the vital work of our law enforcement officers by investing in their families' future.”

“Public servants are the backbone of America, serving in vital roles that ensure the safety and well-being of their communities every day. As law enforcement in America faces a critical recruitment and retention crisis, and as postsecondary education becomes more expensive and crucial in our modern world, it is vital that the Federal government ensures that our public servants have the necessary funding and opportunities to receive postsecondary education,” said Patrick Yoes, National President of the National Fraternal Order of Police. “On behalf of the more than 382,000 members of the Fraternal Order of Police, thank you both for your leadership on this important issue.”

Figures’ bill establishes a federal education assistance program covering the full cost of postsecondary education and training opportunities – including those enrolled in trade schools and vocational programs – for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers who have completed at least 20 years of qualifying service.

Congressman Figures is joined in introducing this legislation by Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Representatives Jahana Hayes (CT-05) and Mike Ezell (MS-04).

In addition to the National Fraternal Order of Police, this bill is also endorsed by the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Association of Social Workers, the International Association of Fire Fighters, the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians, and the Major Cities Chiefs Association.

title: Finstad Leads Minnesota Congressional Delegation in Letter Urging USDA Action on Virus-Related Turkey Losses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01), member of the House Committee on Agriculture, led members of Minnesota’s Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins regarding the significant loss Minnesota turkey growers have experienced from avian metapneumovirus (aMPV). Specifically, the letter urges USDA to recognize qualifying aMPV-related turkey mortality as eligible for assistance through the Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP), USDA’s program that pays farmers and ranchers for animal deaths or injuries above normal levels.

Avian metapneumovirus resulted in the loss of over 2.2 million birds in 2024 alone and has continued to severely impact Minnesota flocks. As the leading turkey-producing state, the spread of aMPV raises serious concerns about the impact on the poultry sector.

The letter reads:

Dear Secretary Rollins:

We write to renew and emphasize our request that the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) allow turkey growers to utilize the Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP) to recover a portion of the devastating losses caused by avian metapneumovirus (aMPV). We further ask USDA to provide a process for growers to submit applications retroactively for eligible losses incurred in 2024 and 2025.

Based on the merits of turkey grower claims, veterinary expert opinions, and the program’s eligibility standards, it is unclear why the USDA has deemed aMPV as ineligible under LIP. Avian metapneumovirus is transmitted via vectors, and growers had no commercially available vaccine to protect their flocks during the years in question. Due to this, producers could not reasonably prevent these losses despite following recommended biosecurity practices and working closely with their veterinarians.

The rapid spread of aMPV hit small and independent growers especially hard, with some sustaining repeated losses before an effective vaccine became commercially available. These losses were beyond normal mortality and were caused by circumstances outside the growers’ control.

USDA’s National Appeals Division has issued decisions establishing significant administrative precedent regarding the eligibility of aMPV-related losses under LIP. These decisions recognize that aMPV can and should qualify as an eligible disease when producers provide sufficient evidence demonstrating that the disease directly caused mortality beyond normal levels. USDA should apply that reasoning consistently and fairly to similarly situated growers rather than requiring each producer to pursue a lengthy and costly individual appeal.

Accordingly, we respectfully request that USDA:

Formally recognize qualifying aMPV-related turkey mortality as eligible for assistance through LIP;

Direct the Farm Service Agency to apply the precedent established through the National Appeals Division consistently across aMPV claims;

Establish a retroactive application or reconsideration process for qualifying losses sustained in 2024 and 2025; and

Provide clear guidance to county FSA offices and turkey growers regarding the documentation needed to support these applications.

This relief would not make producers whole, but it could provide a critical lifeline to Minnesota farm families who have endured losses beyond normal mortality through no fault of their own. For some small and independent growers, this assistance may determine whether their operations, and the opportunity for the next generation to continue farming, survive.

Providing this assistance also aligns with the administration’s priority of reducing food costs for American families. Disease-related losses reduce domestic production, increase costs throughout the supply chain, and threaten the long-term availability of an affordable source of protein. Helping growers remain in business through programs designed to provide this type of assistance strengthens our domestic food supply and protects consumers from further price pressures.

Minnesota is the nation’s leading turkey-producing state, and its family farms are an important part of our rural communities and agricultural economy. We urge USDA to act quickly and use every available administrative authority to ensure these growers are treated fairly and have meaningful access to the assistance Congress intended LIP to provide.

Thank you for your consideration. We stand ready to work with you, the Farm Service Agency and Minnesota’s turkey industry to develop a fair and workable process.

Sincerely,

Brad Finstad, Member of Congress

Amy Klobuchar, United States Senator

Angie Craig, Member of Congress, Ranking Member, Committee on Agriculture

Michelle Fischbach, Member of Congress

Tina Smith, United States Senator

Pete Stauber, Member of Congress

Betty McCollum, Member of Congress

Kelly Morrison, Member of Congress

CC: Kurt Blomgren, Minnesota FSA Executive Director

title: Franklin Introduces Establishing Gold Standard Science Act To Restore Transparency and Accountability To EPA's Scientific Advisory Process
text:
Rep. Scott Franklin (FL-18), Chairman of the House Science Committee’s Environment Subcommittee, today introduced the Establishing Gold Standard Science Act, legislation to strengthen transparency, accountability and scientific integrity in the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) scientific advisory process.

“Americans should be able to trust that science informing federal policy is based on sound research, not politics or predetermined outcomes,” said Congressman Scott Franklin. “That means research should be transparent, independently verifiable and repeatable, with conflicts of interest disclosed and the full weight of the available evidence considered. This bill puts safeguards in place at EPA to help restore public confidence that decisions affecting our economy, communities and families are grounded in a scientific process the American people can trust.”

At the center of the legislation are new standards for EPA’s Science Advisory Board, which provides independent scientific advice to the agency. The bill would strengthen conflict-of-interest and disclosure requirements, require the Board to consider the full weight of scientific evidence and ensure different and dissenting scientific viewpoints are considered as part of the advisory process. Those provisions track the substantive safeguards described in the original release.

The legislation also codifies key provisions of President Trump’s May 2025 Restoring Gold Standard Science executive order at EPA, including greater transparency, consideration of the weight of scientific evidence, open scientific debate and safeguards against conflicts of interest. The executive order established government-wide standards intended to improve the transparency, rigor and reliability of federally conducted and funded science.

The bill builds on Franklin’s work as Chairman of the Environment Subcommittee overseeing federal science policy. During a July House Science Committee hearing with White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, Franklin discussed strengthening public confidence in federal scientific advisory processes and ensuring policymakers have reliable evidence to inform their decisions.

“Federal decisions should be informed by credible, reliable, and impartial scientific evidence,” said Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23). “The Establishing Gold Standard Science Act will help ensure the EPA follows rigorous, transparent scientific practices, acknowledges uncertainty, and considers the full weight of the available evidence.”

“Americans deserve to know that decisions made by their government are based on science, not politics,” said Congressman Mike Haridopolos (FL-08). “The Establishing Gold Standard Science Act will strengthen transparency and accountability at the EPA by ensuring its scientific advice is based on reliable evidence, free from conflicts of interest, and open to rigorous debate. I’m proud to support this legislation and help restore trust in the scientific process.”

“Washington has gotten far too comfortable telling Americans to ‘trust the science’ while asking them not to look too closely at who funded it, who influenced it, or what evidence was left out,” said Congressman Harrigan (NC-10). “I’m cosponsoring the Establishing Gold Standard Science Act because trust is earned through transparency. Put the financial interests on the table, keep paid lobbyists out of decisions they stand to benefit from, make room for dissenting evidence, and let the strongest science win. When federal decisions can reshape entire industries and hit families directly, ‘trust us’ isn’t good enough.”

“Americans deserve to know that when decisions are made, they're based on sound science,” said Rep. Weber (TX-14). “The Establishing Gold Standard Science Act brings much-needed transparency and accountability to the science behind EPA's decisions by shining a light on conflicts of interest. Good science starts with honest discussion and rigorous scrutiny. I'm proud to join Rep. Franklin in setting the gold standard and making informed decisions that help American families thrive.”

“I am proud to cosponsor Rep. Scott Franklin’s Establishing Gold Standard Science Act, which will hold those conducting scientific reviews within the federal government to a higher standard of accountability,” said Rep. Van Epps (TN-07). “In the past, we’ve seen the federal government weaponize so-called scientific findings against Americans and stifle American innovation. This legislation will help ensure government policy is grounded in rigorous, credible science—not unproven theories or political agendas.”

“As Chairman of the Environment Subcommittee, Congressman Franklin has been a consistent advocate for using Gold Standard Science to develop regulations,” said Chris Jahn, President and CEO of the American Chemistry Council. “We appreciate his leadership and work on legislation that will promote scientific transparency and accountability at the EPA. The end result will be better policy that helps protect the environment and public health while ensuring the competitiveness of American manufacturers.”

“There have long been significant problems with the use and dissemination of science at the EPA,” said Daren Bakst, Director of the Center for Energy and Environment and Senior Fellow at the Competitive Enterprise Institute. “Too often, there is little transparency and sound science is rejected in favor of achieving desired policy outcomes. Rep. Franklin should be commended for introducing important legislation that will help address and shed light on science integrity problems at the agency and will lay the foundation for even more reforms in the future.”

Specifically, the Establishing Gold Standard Science Act would:

Require EPA’s Science Advisory Board to consider the full weight of scientific evidence in its advice and recommendations.

Promote the open exchange of ideas and consideration of different and dissenting scientific viewpoints.

Prohibit federally registered lobbyists from serving on the Science Advisory Board.

Strengthen conflict-of-interest and recusal requirements for members whose work, financial interests or affiliations are directly involved in matters before the Board.

Require members to disclose relevant financial relationships, government grants, professional activities and other potential conflicts and keep those disclosures updated.

Require EPA to report relevant Science Advisory Board membership and disclosure information to Congress.

Establish a process for investigating scientific misconduct and removing members found responsible.

Require EPA to establish a scientific-integrity training program for agency employees.

Franklin serves as Chairman of the House Science, Space and Technology Committee’s Environment Subcommittee, which has jurisdiction over environmental research and development.

Original cosponsors include: Reps. Jay Obernolte (CA-23), Darrell Issa (CA-48), Mike Haridopolos (FL-08), Keith Self (TX-03), Randy Weber (TX-14), Daniel Webster (FL-11), Rich McCormick (GA-07), Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03), Jake Ellzey (TX-06), Matt Van Epps (TN-07), Pat Harrigan (NC-10) and Jim Baird (IN-04).

Supporting organizations include: Competitive Enterprise Institute and American Chemistry Council
