title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Calls on the NJDEP to Rescind Eviction Notices for Andover-Aeroflex Airport
text:
Above: Gottheimer visits Andover-Aeroflex Airport with Woman-Owned Small Business Owner, Damian DelGaizo, and Andover Mayor Thomas Walsh Jr.

ANDOVER, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) toured and then spoke at Andover-Aeroflex Airport after the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) moved to evict the woman-owned Andover Flight Academy, the airport’s aircraft maintenance shop, and several other aircraft owners from their hangars. The flight school teaches military pilots how to land on short runways and in open fields. Gottheimer announced he is sending a letter to Governor Mikie Sherrill and NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak urging them to rescind the eviction notices, which were mailed last week by the NJDEP Commissioner to the small business owners. Gottheimer is asking the NJDEP to work with the Governor’s office, tenants, local leaders, and his office on a plan that will keep these small businesses at Aeroflex. Gottheimer is also calling on the NJDEP Commissioner to come and tour the facility with him and provide further explanation for the closure.

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

Gottheimer sent this letter to the Governor and NJDEP Commissioner, Ed Potosnak.

“I’m frustrated, and so are the people standing next to me,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I’m not going to let you guys get thrown out. It’s not happening. We’re going to fight this thing.”

New Jersey’s own site claims that it would cost $4.7 million to make repairs the state wants to the hangars and $8 million to demolish them. The state is planning to demolish the location — costing taxpayers double.

Multiple discrepancies were identified in the NJDEP’s reasons for issuing evictions. The agency falsely reported that the building lacked running water — a claim that would also make the location unsuitable for the NJ Forest Fire Service — but Gottheimer found the water was working just fine (VIDEO).

NJDEP also claims that the evictions will create necessary additional space for the NJ Forest Fire Service, which was “sharing space and had their items placed in a corner of the hangar.” But, upon touring the facility, there appeared to be ample available space within the Forest Fire Service’s designated individual hangar area (VIDEO).

The NJDEP claimed that the flight school office was in disrepair, but that could not have been further from the truth (VIDEO).

New Jersey is short on hangar space, and pilots wait years on lists for a spot. The Andover Aeroflex is one of only two remaining airports in Sussex County, New Jersey, and the only site within 100 miles that trains pilots on how to land on shorter runways and in open spaces. The school also draws in many pilots from around the country to learn, like actor Harrison Ford (VIDEO), which also greatly helps the local economy.

Many of the planes at Aeroflex are antiques with fabric skins that the sun and rain would wreck if left outside. If the flight school and the shop are lost, the airport loses the small businesses that bring in pilots and revenue, and the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) has warned this puts the whole airport at risk of becoming a glorified parking lot.

Gottheimer criticized the NJDEP’s lack of transparency through this entire process. His office has repeatedly requested information and a timeline from the department and has received almost nothing in return. In his letter, Gottheimer asks Governor Sherrill, a former Navy helicopter pilot, to rescind the eviction notices and direct the NJDEP to work with her office, the tenants, local leaders, and his office on a plan that keeps these businesses at Aeroflex.

Additionally, the NJDEP says the hangar is unsafe, yet still allows the New Jersey Forest Fire Service to use it, a double standard that makes no sense. And the numbers don’t add up. The state’s own engineering assessment calls for roughly $4.7 million in renovations. Their assessment claims the demolition would cost $8 million — nearly twice the price. Construction of a replacement building for the Fire Service would be more than $11 million. A licensed engineer who walked the property found the buildings in fair condition with no outstanding code violations, and said targeted repairs would cost only about $267,000.

Gottheimer is calling for no evictions until a clear timeline is set with a solution that does not hurt small businesses and families, and for the NJDEP Commissioner to tour the facility and see firsthand the status of the airport.

Gottheimer was joined by Andover Mayor Thomas D. Walsh Jr., Andover Flight Academy Founder Damien DelGaizo, and Andover Flight Academy Owner Justine Pasniewski.

Below: Gottheimer visits Andover-Aeroflex Airport.

title: Rep. Grijalva Statement on Border Patrol Raid Near Lochiel, Arizona
text:
Nogales, Arizona – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the below statement following reports of a U.S. Border Patrol raid and the toppling of a centuries-old cottonwood tree along the U.S.-Mexico border near Lochiel, Arizona. This comes after a U.S. Forest Service announcement posted on its website – without any prior public input or notification – last week closing roads and restricting public access to miles of lands along the U.S.-Mexico border as they proceed with wall construction.

“Just days after the U.S. Forest Service closed miles of public lands along the border, armed Border Patrol agents conducted a raid that injured protesters and uprooted the last of four century-old cottonwood trees. This is what the militarization of our borderlands looks like – and it’s all because DHS has more taxpayer dollars than it knows what to do with, and is wasting them on a reckless and useless second border wall. Our borderlands are home to unique ecosystems and world-class biodiversity, including some of the last remaining habitat for the Sonoran jaguar in the United States.

DHS and its private contractors have repeatedly shown they cannot be trusted to protect sensitive cultural and environmental sites. That is why public access and oversight are so critical. Instead, DHS is following the same playbook: shut out the public, evade scrutiny, and recklessly bulldoze our lands. Administrations come and go, but unfortunately the damage the Trump administration is inflicting on our irreplaceable borderlands cannot simply be undone.”

title: Guthrie Leads Members of Congress in Submitting Amicus Brief in Support of Kentucky Lawsuit Against the EPA
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On Friday, Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, led in filing an amicus brief on behalf of 12 Members of Congress in support of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and other states’ request that the Supreme Court of the United States hear an appeal in a significant Clean Air Act case, Commonwealth of Kentucky, et al. v. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, et al.

Petitioning states argue that the Biden-Harris Administration’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) revised the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in 2024 without conducting the “thorough review” required by the Clean Air Act. These revised standards, imposed by the Biden-Harris EPA, will restrict the construction of new American manufacturing plants and energy projects, as well as improvements at existing sites, in many parts of the country.

“For four years, the Biden-Harris Administration imposed countless burdensome environmental regulations that handcuffed American industries and made everyday life more expensive,” said Congressman Guthrie. “I am proud to lead my colleagues in filing this amicus brief in support of the Commonwealth of Kentucky’s lawsuit to vacate the Biden-Harris Administration’s PM2.5 NAAQS finalized rule, arguing that the revised NAAQS was adopted on an incomplete scientific record and without the required thorough review. If implemented, this rule would devastate American manufacturing and energy and stifle American innovation. I am hopeful the Supreme Court will grant the petitioning states a Writ of Certiorari and that the petitioning states will ultimately prevail in court.”

The full text of the amicus brief can be viewed HERE.

The amicus brief is supported by Reps. Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Rick Allen (GA-12), Troy Balderson (OH-12), Andy Barr (KY-06), Julie Fedorchak (ND-AL), Craig Goldman (TX-12), Morgan Griffith (VA-09), Diana Harshbarger (TN-01), Erin Houchin (IN-09), Nick Langworthy (NY-22), August Pfluger (TX-11), Hal Rogers (KY-05), and Randy Weber (TX-14).

Background:

In 2020, the Trump Administration EPA finalized a rule for the PM2.5 NAAQS under the Clean Air Act, which was conducted as part of the standard 5-year review required under the Act and kept the standard at 12 micrograms/cubic meter.

In 2024, the Biden-Harris EPA revised the Trump Administration’s EPA ruling, lowering the PM2.5 standard to 9 micrograms/cubic meter.

Throughout the 119th Congress, the House Committee on Energy and Commerce has held multiple hearings and taken action on legislation to ensure the Clean Air Act continues protecting human health and the environment and without stopping economic development and growth. During this work, the Committee has found that the Biden Administration’s new NAAQS standards are very close to background levels and will make it very difficult to build and permit new facilities.

While the Clean Air Act allows the EPA to reconsider a NAAQS outside of the normal 5-year review cycle, the Biden-Harris Administration EPA did not follow the required process of conducting a “thorough review” of the science before establishing a new NAAQS under the Clean Air Act.

Kentucky, and other petitioning states, sued the EPA, along with several industry groups, in 2024. The Trump Administration EPA tried to have the Biden-Harris NAAQS vacated, but in a June 2026 decision, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals denied EPA’s motion to vacate the 2024 NAAQS and upheld the Biden-Harris Administration’s burdensome mandates.

Petitioning states are requesting that the Supreme Court rule on the following questions:

Whether the Clean Air Act gives EPA the authority to revise NAAQS without conducting a thorough review merely because the revision occurs before the normal, five-year review.

Whether the Clean Air Act bars EPA from considering the costs and feasibility of revising NAAQS when deciding whether to exercise its discretion to undertake a revision before the normal, five-year review.

title: Congressman Andy Harris Urges Senate to Fund the Fight Against Illicit Chinese Vapes
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Andy Harris, M.D. (MD-01), Chairman of the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Subcommittee on Appropriations, called on the Senate to support the House-passed initiatives in its Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bills to give the federal agencies the resources they need to shut down the illicit nicotine marketplace, including vapes and e-cigarette products designed to appeal to children, and protect Americans from these dangerous products.

“Illegal vapes from China continue to make their way onto shelves and into the hands of unsuspecting Americans,” said Rep. Harris. “The House passed the Fiscal Year 2027 Agriculture Appropriations Act this summer, and I urge the Senate to move forward with its appropriations bills so we can strengthen enforcement against these illegal products.”

The House-passed Agriculture-FDA bill directs FDA to dedicate at least $200 million in tobacco user fees to enforcement against illegal e-cigarettes and vapes. That includes $20 million for the ENDS Enforcement Task Force, a joint effort of the Department of Justice, the Department of Homeland Security, and FDA to target the illegal manufacture, importation, distribution, and sale of these products, a majority of which are produced in China. The bill also directs FDA to expand its enforcement priorities to flavored disposable vapes and to report regularly to Congress on seizures of illicit products, support for state enforcement, and efforts to educate retailers about which products are legal to sell.

The Agriculture-FDA bill is one part of a whole-of-government strategy House appropriators have advanced this year. Across five other FY2027 bills, the Appropriations Committee has directed the Department of Justice to lead the ENDS Enforcement Task Force and pursue trade fraud, smuggling, and money laundering cases against illicit importers. It has provided $5 million each to Customs and Border Protection for the task force and to Homeland Security Investigations for criminal investigations into illegal imports. It has also directed Treasury and the State Department to disrupt the financial networks behind the trade, directed the U.S. Trade Representative to seek an enforceable agreement with China to stop illicit exports at the source, and directed the Department of Transportation to crack down on mislabeled lithium-battery vapes shipped on passenger and cargo aircraft.

“This has become a national security problem,” said Rep. Harris. “Illegal vapes put money in the pockets of the Chinese Communist Party and the criminal cartels operating inside our borders. House appropriators have given every agency with a role in stopping this trade clear direction and the resources to act, and now those resources need to be put to work.”

“Responsible retailers are at a competitive disadvantage as long as bad actors continue to sell illicit products,” said Margaret Mannion, director of government relations at the National Association of Convenience Stores. “The convenience industry supports every effort to stop the flood of illegal vapes onto our market, and we applaud Chairman Harris’s support for enhanced federal enforcement against illicit tobacco products. American consumers deserve access to authorized, legal products, and it will take coordinated action across government, like the work of the ENDS Enforcement Task Force, to make that happen. There’s no time to waste.”

“I will continue fighting to stop the flow of illegal vapes into our country and give FDA and federal law enforcement the resources they need to crack down on this illicit trade,” said Rep. Harris. “Foreign bad actors, especially China, should not be able to profit from flooding the American market with illegal flavored disposable vapes that are designed to appeal to children.”

title: ICYMI: Hinson Highlights Legislation to Help Women Access Long-Lasting Birth Control
text:
Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

The Telegraph Herald

Adult women should be able to access safe birth control methods that work best for them, regardless of their ZIP code.

For some women, the best option is oral contraceptives they can pick up at their local pharmacy. For others, it may be a long-lasting option like an IUD or arm implant. Women should be able to talk with their healthcare provider, decide what works best for them, and access that care as close to home as possible. That’s just common sense.

That’s why I introduced new legislation to help women access long-lasting birth control options at their local community health centers.

Right now, a woman may talk through her options with her local provider and decide an IUD or arm implant is right for her, only to learn the health center doesn’t have a trained provider or the option isn’t available onsite. That can mean scheduling additional appointments, another long drive, or taking more time off work. It shouldn’t be that complicated.

My bill would help community health centers in underserved areas train providers and keep long-lasting birth control options on hand so women can safely access contraception without unnecessary barriers. It also improves telehealth options to help women who live far from a provider can discuss their options and connect with a physician who can provide the care that works best for them.

Community health centers are often the front door to healthcare in rural Iowa. We should give trusted local providers the tools they need to meet women where they are, not force women to navigate around gaps in the healthcare system.

This new bill builds on work I’ve been doing since my time in the Iowa Legislature. I’ve long believed adult women should be able to access safe, FDA-approved contraception over the counter, and I’ve led that effort in Congress.

As a mom raising two teenage boys, I’m on the other side of those early years of starting a family. But I continue to hear from Iowa women about the barriers they face accessing the care that works for them. I’ll keep working with anyone who is willing to break down those barriers and support Iowa women.

This piece was originally published in The Telegraph Herald on October 5, 2026.

title: John James introduces Skilled JOBS Act to expand apprenticeship opportunities
text:
Ford’s CEO warned at the end of September that America needs to fill 1.7 million skilled trade openings every year through 2035, but that the country is only producing 55 workers for every 100 needed.

Part of the problem is that current rules result in a strict one-to-one ratio of journeymen (experienced workers) to apprentices, which limits how many people can train for these roles. Rep. John James recently introduced legislation to solve this problem by expanding apprenticeship opportunities.

“Current regulations create an artificial bottleneck that is contributing to our labor shortage and driving up costs,” said James, R-Shelby Township. “Solving this problem will make it easier for companies to grow and expand here in Michigan, and it will result in more people working in high paid jobs.”

H.R.10560, also known as the Skilled JOBS Act, formalizes Industry Recognized Apprenticeship Programs. This sets a clear process for private industry groups to create and oversee their own apprenticeship programs instead of relying on traditional government or union programs. The bill sets a minimum ratio of one journeyman to three apprentices, which will let more people train under the guidance of a more experienced worker. The bill allows further adjustments to that ratio after a required study.

Keith Ledbetter, President & CEO of Associated Builders and Contractors of Southeast Michigan, spoke in support of the bill:

“Michigan’s construction industry needs more skilled professionals, and employers need the flexibility to train them. ABC of Southeastern Michigan appreciates Congressman John James’ leadership on the Skilled JOBS Act and his efforts to address restrictive apprentice ratios. This legislation would give contractors greater flexibility to grow their workforce, expand apprenticeship opportunities, and invest in the next generation of skilled professionals,” Ledbetter said.

Tim Golding, State Director of Americans for Prosperity-Michigan, also spoke in support:

"Michigan has always been a state that builds – but our shops and job sites can't find enough electricians, welders, plumbers, and machinists, and the people who want those careers are getting turned away at the door. That's not a shortage of talent. It's a shortage of training slots, created by federal rules that let just one apprentice train under each Journeyman worker. The Skilled JOBS Act fixes it by recognizing the high-quality apprenticeship programs industry already runs and setting up a sensible floor of three apprentices for every Journeyman worker. Americans for Prosperity is proud to support Rep. John James' bill, and we urge Congress to move it."

The bill was referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

James represents Michigan’s 10th Congressional District, which includes portions of Oakland and Macomb counties.

title: Brownley, Raskin, Schatz Fight Back Against MAGA Book Bans and Attacks on First Amendment Rights of the Free Press and of Citizens in Schools, Libraries and Museums
text:
Washington, DC – Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) joined Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and Senator Brian Schatz (D-HI) in introducing a resolution standing strong for the American freedom to read, write and learn. The lawmakers’ resolution condemns MAGA’s escalating campaign of book bans in school libraries and censorship targeting the Smithsonian Institution and other public museums, parks and facilities.

The lawmakers’ resolution specifically cites book bans issued by the Trump Administration, MAGA state legislatures, local libraries and schools across America. This year, federal officials, at the direction of President Trump, censored books and educational materials at the Smithsonian Institution and Department of Defense Education Activity schools.

More than 12,000 individual books were banned in America between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report by PEN America. This includes books like “The Bluest Eye” by Toni Morrison and “MARCH” by former Congressman and Civil Rights Movement hero John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell.

PEN America’s report captures the proliferation of MAGA book bans that specifically target books written by and about outsiders and individuals from marginalized backgrounds. Books with LGBTQ+ characters or themes face a disproportionate risk of being banned.

According to PEN America, from July 2025 to June 2026, 24 States across the country limited access to certain books, including:

Texas, where at least 8,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 45 school districts;

Florida, where at least 3,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 35 school districts;

Ohio, where at least 115 books in total have been banned or restricted in one school district;

Utah, where at least 100 books in total have been banned or restricted in five school districts; and

Michigan, where at least 65 books in total have been banned or restricted in two school districts.

The resolution is endorsed by PEN America and the American Library Association (ALA); Authors Against Banned Books; Banned Books Week Coalition; Center for American Progress; EdTrust; EveryLibrary; Freedom to Learn Foundation; Florida Freedom to Read Project; Freedom to Read Project; Hatchette Book Group; Interfaith Alliance; JCRC of Greater Washington; Jewish Community Relations Council of Portland; Jewish Council for Public Affairs; Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester; Lee & Low Books ; Let Utah Read; Macmillan Publishing; National Coalition Against Censorship; National Council for Jewish Women; National Council of Teachers of English; National Education Association; Penguin Random House; PFLAG National; Red Wine and Blue Education Fund; Simon & Schuster; Texas Freedom to Read Project; and the Tucson Jewish Museum & Holocaust Center.

title: Kaptur Announces Additional Federal Funds for Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Plant in Oak Harbor
text:
Oak Harbor, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, welcomed the Department of Energy’s announcement of a Federal loan of up to $4.2 Billion to Vistra Corp. to modernize three nuclear power plants, including the Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Plant in Oak Harbor, Ohio. The investment will increase reliable power generation and grid capacity across Northern Ohio. At Davis-Besse, the project is expected to add 80 Megawatts of generating capacity and extend the reactor’s operating life by 25 years.

“This Federal support is timely given rising demands on our electrical grid and the need for additional power to protect jobs and attract new and expanded manufacturing facilities, while also helping avoid further rate increases on residential ratepayers,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09).

Kaptur emphasized the need for continued accountability and ratepayer protection following the plant’s history under its former owner, FirstEnergy, and the corruption associated with Ohio House Bill 6. She continues to advocate for her Ratepayer Justice and Commercial Power Accountability Act, which would seek to return funds improperly taken from ratepayers and prioritize future Federal investment in communities harmed by utility misconduct.

Kaptur also highlighted Federal investments in the region’s nuclear workforce. In April, the US Department of Energy awarded $19.2 Million to the University of Toledo for the Great Lakes Partnership to Enhance the Nuclear Workforce, under a new national nuclear workforce training program Congresswoman Kaptur created. The initiative, in partnership with Vistra, UToledo, the University of Michigan, Owens Community College, IBEW, and others, is a first of its kind industry commitment to develop workforce training and nuclear reactor safety credentials for current and future workers.

“These efforts are interconnected: delivering ratepayer justice, moving toward a new energy future, training a workforce focused on safety, and upgrading Davis-Besse to meet growing electricity demand,” Congresswoman Kaptur concluded.

The Vistra projects at Davis-Besse, the Perry nuclear facility in Ohio, and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania are expected to preserve nearly 4 Gigawatts of reliable baseload power, add 433 Megawatts of new nuclear capacity, support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs, and preserve thousands of permanent jobs across the region. Davis-Besse, which began operating in 1977, was acquired by Vistra from FirstEnergy in 2024 and currently employs approximately 530 workers.

As Ranking Member of the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee, Congresswoman Kaptur continues to oversee DOE programs supporting power generation, grid modernization, nuclear safety, and ratepayer protection in Northern Ohio.

title: Reconnecting with SHRM on Building a More Stable Workforce for the CNMI
text: A stable workforce is essential to rebuilding our economy. Our businesses need the ability to plan beyond the next few years, our workers need greater certainty about their futures, and the Commonwealth needs a workforce system that reflects the realities of our islands. That was at the center of my conversation with the SHRM general membership last week. SHRM was the first organization I spoke to when I started my term as Delegate, so it was good to return and report on the progress we have made since then. We talked about our legislation to bring Wagner-Peyser employment services to the CNMI, our work to eliminate the CW-1 touchback requirement, and the broader Northern Mariana Islands Labor Stabilization Act to provide greater workforce stability beyond 2029. We also talked about where workforce fits into the larger work of rebuilding our economy. Tourism, power costs, access to capital, transportation, and workforce all affect whether businesses can grow, whether people can find opportunity here, and ultimately whether our economy can move forward. Thank you to SHRM for the opportunity to return, share where this work stands, and hear directly from the people who deal with these challenges every day.

title: Rota’s Thomas Manglona Named Marianas Science Fellow
text:
It's always fun to see a journalist making the news. Congratulations to Rota native Thomas Manglona II on being named the inaugural Marianas Science Communications Fellow by the University of Guam Center for Island Sustainability and Sea Grant. Thomas’ passion for journalism began in Rota, and he has since built an impressive career telling stories across the Marianas and the Pacific. A graduate of UC Berkeley and Stanford University, Thomas is a Gates Millennium Scholar, Obama Asia-Pacific Leader, Rosalynn Carter Journalism Fellow, and Nia Tero Storytelling Fellow, with his work appearing in outlets including ABC News, CNN and Al Jazeera. We are proud to see a son of Luta using his talents to highlight our islands, our environment, and the science that will help shape our future. Way to go, Thomas!

title: Talking Saipan’s Priorities with Mayor RB
text: A lot of the work we do in Washington begins with understanding what our communities are dealing with here at home. The people working on the front lines of public safety, disaster recovery, village needs, and everyday community services see those challenges up close, and that perspective should help shape the federal work we pursue. Saipan Mayor Ramon “RB” Camacho stopped by the District Office last week to talk about his advocacy for federal support for CNMI needs and to strategize how his work serving the Saipan community and our work in Washington can be leveraged to produce tangible progress for our people. Anyone who knows Mayor RB knows he does not mince words. I appreciated the opportunity to sit down with a fellow straight talker, get down to business, and talk frankly about where we are, where we need to go, and how we can work together to get to a better place.

title: Turning Territorial Priorities Into Federal Action
text: On Wednesday, the Department of the Interior held the 2026 Interagency Group on Insular Affairs (IGIA) Midyear Senior Plenary Meeting virtually, bringing together Governors and Members of Congress from across the U.S. territories to discuss issues affecting our islands and ongoing federal initiatives. During my remarks, I called for IGIA to become more project- and action-oriented. Rather than focusing primarily on broad policy discussions, IGIA can serve as a forum for territorial leaders and senior federal officials to work together on specific priorities identified by the territories and develop concrete steps to move them forward. The proposal received support from participants and the Office of Insular Affairs, which committed to following up on ways IGIA can evolve. I will continue working to ensure federal programs and policies translate into tangible, effective results for the people of the Northern Mariana Islands and other U.S. territories.

title: Washington Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

The full text of the letter is available here.

title: Rep. Mary Miller Takes Action to Protect Families from Radical Gender Policies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Mary Miller (IL-15) introduced theYaeli Martinez Child Protection Act to protect parents from being punished by state child-welfare systems for affirming their child’s biological sex or shielding them from irreversible medical procedures.

“Raising your son as a boy or your daughter as a girl is fundamental to parenthood, not child abuse,” said Congresswoman Mary Miller. “The Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act defends the constitutional rights of mothers and fathers and stops bureaucrats from using taxpayer-funded child-welfare systems to tear children away from loving families.”

The legislation is named in honor of Yaeli Martinez, a California teenager who was separated from her mother amid a dispute over her gender identity and spent years in the state’s child-welfare system before dying by suicide at age 19 in 2019.

The Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act would:

Protect parents from wrongful abuse allegations by clarifying that affirming a child’s biological sex does not constitute child abuse.

Safeguard parental custody by barring federally funded state child-welfare systems from removing children from fit parents simply because those parents affirm their child’s biological sex.

Ensure foster and adoptive families cannot be denied placement solely because they affirm a child’s biological sex.

Amend the Parental Kidnapping Prevention Act to prevent states from wrongfully asserting custody over a child.

Hold states accountable through federal funding consequences and a private right of action for violations of the Act.

Original Cosponsors: Reps. Josh Brecheen (OK-02), Sheri Biggs (SC-03), Barry Moore (AL-01), Randy Fine (FL-06), John Rose (TN-06), Mark Alford (MO-04), Rich McCormick (GA-07), Robert Aderholt (AL-04), Marlin Stutzman (IN-03), Mark Harris (NC-08), Diana Harshbarger (TN-01), and Erin Houchin (IN-09).

title: Reps. Massie, Pingree Introduce the Red Meat Inspection Exemption Act
text:
For Immediate Release

Contact: massie.press@mail.house.gov

Contact #: 202-225-3465

Washington, D.C.- Today, Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) and Rep. Chellie Pingree (D-ME) introduced the Red Meat Inspection Exemption Act (RMIEA). The bill allows qualifying small farmers to slaughter and process their own livestock for direct-to-consumer sale without federal interference. Similar inspection exemptions already exist for poultry producers. Rep. Massie's legislation fulfills a promise that President Trump made in August "to allow Farmers and Ranchers to be given the right to PROCESS THEIR OWN FOOD."

"Americans are concerned about the rising cost of red meat and are looking for solutions that will lower prices," said Rep. Thomas Massie. "The Red Meat Inspection Exemption Act will reduce the regulatory burden placed on small meat producers and enhance their ability to sell directly to local consumers. President Trump announced this great idea, but pressure from the international meat packing lobby and limits on executive power prevent him from making good on his promise. It’s up to Congress to change the law and deliver relief to American farmers and ranchers. Under U.S. law, poultry farmers are already allowed to process their own birds, so why not let small-scale livestock farmers do the same?"

"Americans increasingly want to know where their food comes from. Maine has established a constitutional right to food, with rural communities across the state adopting direct farm-to-consumer sales. Our bipartisan bill would build on that work," said Congresswoman Pingree. "By allowing producers to process a limited number of animals on their farms and sell meat directly to consumers, this bill will strengthen access to locally-raised meat and provide another avenue for farmers to sell their products. Farmers and consumers have waited long enough for relief, and this bill will deliver."

"The biggest obstacle to a prosperous local food system in this country is the lack of slaughterhouse infrastructure," said Pete Kennedy, consultant for the Weston A. Price Foundation (WAPF). Kennedy continued, "This situation has primarily been brought on by the 1967 Wholesome Meat Act which preempted state laws on meat regulation and generally prohibited the sale of on-farm slaughtered meat. This bill restores a deeply rooted historical tradition, the sale of meat from livestock slaughtered on a farm direct from the farmer to the consumer, which can help strengthen food security and the rural economy. Many thanks to Representatives Massie and Pingree for taking a significant step towards food emancipation and improving the quality of the American food supply."

"Why is beef so expensive? Because beef processors act as a cartel, paying farmers too little for their herds and charging customers too much," said Dr. Meryl Nass, M.D., President, Save Our Food and Farms, a project of Door to Freedom. "All three of the largest beef processors in the US (JBS, Tyson, and Cargill) were forced to settle with the DOJ for price-fixing in 2025 and 2026. Isn't it time our local farmers and ranchers were allowed to compete with them? This bill throws a life raft to America's small farmers. Between 2017 and 2022 the US lost 142,000 farms. Providing farmers a chance to avoid being squeezed by the Big 4 meat processors will give them another chance at prosperity."

The Red Meat Inspection Exemption Act creates a federal meat-inspection exemption for small livestock producers who slaughter and process animals raised on their own farms for direct distribution to consumers. Producers seeking an inspection exemption may slaughter no more than 25 cattle, 60 swine, 250 sheep, or 250 goats annually.

The legislation requires that meat exempted from inspection requirements must be labeled “Exempt—21 U.S.C. 623,” must include the name and address of the producer, must remain subject to federal adulteration and misbranding standards, and must comply with any food-safety or special-handling requirements established by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). The bill also expressly preserves state laws that provide broader exemptions for on-farm slaughter, processing, or sale of meat.

The text of the Red Meat Inspection Exemption Act is available at this link.

title: MATSUI, DUCKWORTH, SCHUMER LEAD BIPARTISAN CALL REQUIRING FAA TO GUARANTEE EVERY EMERGENCY MEDICAL KIT ABOARD FLIGHTS INCLUDE LIFE-SAVING EPINEPHRINE
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Co-Chair of the Congressional Food Allergy Research Caucus, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL),Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation, and U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) led a group of 20 bipartisan, bicameral lawmakers in calling on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to guarantee that emergency medical kits (EMK) on every commercial aircraft include epinephrine, a life-saving medication to treat passengers who go into anaphylactic shock. Today is the final day for the American people to submit public comments on the FAA’s dangerous new proposed rule that would result in medications being less consistent and dependable for passengers experiencing health emergencies on commercial flights—a severely misguided proposal that prioritizes flexibility for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.

“Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly,” wrote the lawmakers in their official public comment to the FAA’s proposed rule. “The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.”

In the landmark 2024 FAA Reauthorization Law that Congresswoman Matsui supported, the FAA requires commercial airlines to have adequate emergency medical kits on board to treat conditions like anaphylaxis. And yet, the FAA’s proposed rule would not require them to carry epinephrine—the only medication that reliably treats this medical emergency—in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training.

The lawmakers continued, “If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended ‘pre-measured auto-delivery device’ be on the EMK contents list.”

In their letter, the lawmakers hammered the FAA’s proposed rule for ignoring expert recommendations, creating an even greater lack of transparency and consistency in EMKs for the flying public—who rely on EMKs during a medical emergency—and for needlessly putting the lives of commercial airline passengers at greater risk.

“To ensure the safety of all airline passengers, we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight,” the lawmakers concluded.

In light of the FAA’s misguided and dangerous proposed rule change, Matsui, Duckworth, and Schumer are calling on the FAA to heed their concerns—as well as the more than 1,500 public comments that have been submitted to express deep concern over this would-be policy failure that would place cost cutting and convenience for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.

In addition to Matsui, the letter is co-signed in the House by U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08), LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), Kelly Morrison (D-MN-03) and Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). In addition to Duckworth and Schumer, the letter is co-signed in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

Full text of the letter can be found below and HERE.

Dear Administrator Bedford:

We write to provide our comments on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) published on August 5, 2026, which would make drastic changes to how the FAA determines the composition of the emergency medical kit (EMK) carried aboard aircraft. The proposed rule is opaque and dangerous, and it threatens to undermine previous work the FAA has done to ensure the safety of the traveling public.

EMKs are supposed to enable initial treatment of a passenger experiencing moderate to severe injuries or illnesses until the aircraft can land and the passenger can be transferred to emergency medical personnel. Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly.

The proposed rule would make harmful steps to reverse work done at the agency to direct operators to include epinephrine in aircraft EMKs. Having multiple doses of epinephrine on every aircraft, in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training, is more urgent than ever. This is due to the on-flight presence of food items containing unlabeled allergens, a steady increase in the number of children with food allergies, the increased prevalence of a tick-borne illness that could create life-threatening allergies and the very real possibility that more than one passenger may require epinephrine during a single flight.

The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.

Our concerns about the proposed rule are outlined below:

Lack of Alignment with Previous Recommendations

The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 directed the FAA to assemble a panel of experts to make recommendations on EMKs and issue a proposed rule. The FAA Onboard Medical Kits Working Group included aerospace medicine experts and physicians, physiologists, psychologists, human factors specialists, cabin safety professionals and researchers. This working group submitted its report, dated May 1, 2025, to the FAA. The report stated:

“The items proposed … are intended to provide initial stabilizing Basic Life Support (BLS) care for immediately life-threatening conditions such as cardiac arrest, airway emergencies, major hemorrhage, andanaphylaxis (emphasis added), as well as to facilitate provision of limited basic first-aid interventions for minor injuries and illnesses that are known to occur in-flight.”

Importantly, the proposed EMK content list in the report includes both “pre-measured auto-delivery device” or “vial-drawn kit.” Yet, just one year later, the FAA publicly defied the recommendations in this report developed by the expert working group the FAA itself commissioned.

No Clear Requirement for Epinephrine

Through rulemaking, the Trump administration is seeking to downgrade the EMK content list, from a binding requirement to mere optional guidance. The proposed rule would allow operators to determine what components should be included in EMKs, so long as the EMK is “practical and sufficient” to address nine conditions, including anaphylaxis:

“…FAA recommends sufficient resources for anaphylaxis (sudden/acute severe allergic reaction), which may include the following signs and symptoms: hives; swelling of the mouth, throat, or tongue; difficulty breathing, rapid or weak pulse, dizziness; stomach pain; nausea or vomiting; or loss of consciousness. Treatment options could (emphasis added) include medication such as epinephrine.”

Epinephrine is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The final rule must contain a clear directive that EMKs shall include epinephrine.

No Requirement for Epinephrine in Easily Self-Administered Forms

If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended “pre-measured auto-delivery device” be on the EMK contents list.

Currently, JetBlue, Southwest, Breeze and Frontier stock their EMKs with epinephrine auto-injectors, and American Airlines’ EMKs include both adult- and pediatric-dose epinephrine auto-injectors. Delta is in the process of transitioning its fleet to include auto-injectors in their EMKs by September 2027, and, this year, United Airlines and Allegiant Airlines will begin the work to include auto-injectors in EMKs. Even with tight profit margins, including epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered, is possible. Through the rulemaking process, the FAA must direct airlines to include epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily administered and not reverse course from its previous recommendations by abandoning the requirement to include epinephrine in EMKs in entirety.

Lack of Transparency on Compliance

The proposed rule would eliminate the exemption process, which was created to account for challenges in stocking EMKs due to drug shortages and allow airlines to substitute drugs, “without requesting an FAA exemption.” Airlines are not required to publicly or centrally report the real-time inventory and exact contents of their EMKs and have continued to operate under exemptions granted by the FAA for years. EMK suppliers and airlines can track when an EMK is opened and needs restocking, but only in instances where the kit was used. There is no means of systematically tracking incidents of allergic reactions or anaphylaxis, especially when passengers use their own epinephrine. For medical conditions that can be treated by multiple, accessible options, eliminating the need for the exemption process may make sense. However, epinephrine is the only first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The public also deserves to know when certain items are not included in a flight’s EMK, and a rationale for the exclusion.

Conclusion

The proposed rule will reduce public safety and trust when flying by increasing ambiguity, subjectivity and opacity of EMK components. The proposed rule argues that increased flexibility is needed to keep up with advances in medicine but, without appropriate reporting and tracking, the Trump administration is significantly increasing the risk of major inconsistencies in EMKs from flight to flight. Predictability, consistency and transparency are all necessary to ensure passengers’ safety, particularly in cases of anaphylaxis, when minutes, or even seconds, matter.

To ensure the safety of all airline passengers,we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight.

We call on the FAA to address the concerns outlined in this letter.

title: McBath Bill to Stop Human Trafficking Passes Senate, Heads to President’s Desk
text:
Washington, DC – Legislation led Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.) and Chairman of the U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) has passed the Senate unanimously and is headed to the President’s desk to be signed into law. The bipartisan, bicameral Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act is led by Senators Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).

This bill directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to train its employees to identify human trafficking and refer suspected trafficking crimes to law enforcement. While DOL employees are on the ground conducting workplace inspections, they will be able to spot human trafficking behavior in real time.

“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that preys on the most vulnerable and robs victims of their freedom and dignity. We have a responsibility to ensure that those on the front lines in our communities and across the federal government have the tools necessary to help combat this crime and provide survivors with a path to safety. Strengthening training for Department of Labor employees is an important step toward recognizing the signs of human trafficking, protecting victims, and connecting them with the resources they need. I thank my colleagues for their support,” said McBath.

“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it. This law will help ensure federal workers are equipped to spot the signs of human trafficking and refer suspected crimes to law enforcement. I’m proud this bill will be my fourth bill signed into law since I took office. This is a great example of the bipartisan work we can accomplish for the American people, and I look forward to the lives this law will help save,” said Husted.

“The fight against human trafficking should never be a partisan issue. Survivors and victims in Michigan and across the country are owed justice, accountability, and meaningful action to prevent these crimes from happening in the first place. Our bipartisan bill, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, provides the Department of Labor with the necessary framework to address these unthinkable crimes head-on. I am proud to have worked alongside my colleagues to get this important legislation passed and look forward to seeing it signed into law,” said Slotkin.

“Human trafficking can hide in plain sight, and this bill will help more people recognize the warning signs. I’m glad the Senate unanimously passed my bill and sent it to President Trump’s desk. By giving Department of Labor employees the right training, we can help identify victims sooner and get potential cases to law enforcement,” said Walberg.

McBath and Walberg introduced the companion bill to the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking in the House of Representatives, where it passed on March 3, 2026.

title: Rep. McBride, Senator Coons, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm
text:
DEWEY BEACH, Del. – U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senator Chris Coons (both D-Del.), joined by the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, local elected officials, and community leaders surveyed damage on Friday morning from last week’s nor’easter that battered Delaware’s coast for four days and caused severe beach erosion, dune damage and flooding in communities all along the coast. The storm damaged homes and businesses, caused road closures, and shut down beaches. Following their assessment of the damage, Senator Coons and Representative McBride called for additional federal support to help Delaware’s coastal communities recover and replenish their beaches.

Rep. McBride and Senator Coons were joined on Friday by officials from the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, Dewey Beach Town Manager Bill Zolper, Dewey Beach Mayor Bill Stevens, South Bethany Mayor Edie Dondero, Bethany Beach Mayor Ron Calef, State Sen. Russ Huxtable and State Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall.

“Delaware’s beaches are critical to our communities, our economy, and our way of life, and we need to make sure they have the resources they need to recover from this storm and prepare for the next one,” said Senator Coons. “I’m going to keep fighting for the funding Delaware needs to rebuild and recover. That means working with our local leaders, DNREC, the Army Corps and our entire congressional delegation to make sure we’re doing everything we can to protect our coast.”

“The damage Senator Coons and I saw is a stark reminder that investing in the resilience of our coastal communities is not optional,” said Rep. McBride. “We cannot prevent these storms from happening, but we can take action to keep people safe and help our communities withstand their impacts. That’s why I’ve been working with partners at every level of government to strengthen our coastline, combat coastal erosion, and ensure Delaware is prepared when severe weather strikes. I’m grateful to Mayor Stevens, our first responders, local leaders, and everyone who stepped up to keep our neighbors safe during the nor’easter. I’ll keep working to make sure Delaware has what it needs to recover from this storm, prepare for the next one, and protect our beaches for generations to come.”

Earlier this year, Senators Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester and Representative McBride helped secure $10 million for beach replenishment along the Delaware coast from Cape Henlopen to Fenwick Island and are working with the Army Corps of Engineers to make that funding available as quickly as possible. Senator Coons is also working with the federal delegation and DNREC to secure an additional $30 million in federal beach replenishment funding this year to help address the state’s ongoing coastal needs.

title: McClellan, Morelle and Virginia Democrats Fight Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting, Pledge to Protect Every Vote
text:
Fairfax, VA – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25) and members of Virginia’s Democratic Congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing on Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation.

The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.

In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.

“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”

“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”

“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”

“Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote,” said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. “Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone’s right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight.”

“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”

“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.

The experts urged voters to check their registration, make a plan to vote and consult trusted election officials.

title: Congressman Menefee Announces Major Constituent Casework Milestone
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) announced that his casework team has closed more than 500 constituent cases since he took office. This milestone reflects eight months of delivering results for the people of Texas’s 18th Congressional District. After TX-18 went more than 330 days without representation in Congress, this accomplishment is a clear sign that our district is back to having a strong, responsive office working for the people.

“Helping constituents navigate the bureaucracy of the federal government and alleviating their hardships is my top priority,” said Rep. Menefee. “We built this office from the ground up. Every call answered and every case closed is a step closer to delivering on the promise I made to the people of the 18th. From Veterans’ benefits to visa assistance, we’re going to keep showing up and helping folks get the help they need.”

Since taking office, Congressman Menefee's team has:

Closed more than 500 constituent cases out of the nearly 1,000 opened.

Recovered more than $1 million in eligible and/or delayed funds for constituents.

Successfully closed cases involving immigration, expedited passports, Veterans’ benefits, Social Security, Medicare, the Department of Education, the IRS, OPM, and the U.S. Postal Service.

Delivered more than 7,000 congressional recognitions throughout the District, celebrating the people and businesses that shape TX-18.

Constituents who need assistance with a federal agency can call 713-655-0050 or visit our website at Menefee.House.Gov.

title: Menendez Leads Push to Expand and Modernize the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail
text:
JERSEY CITY, NJ – Congressman Rob Menendez partnered with Hudson County Complete Streets and local transit advocates to elevate key community priorities for the continued expansion and modernization of the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail (“HBLR”). In a letter to New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, NJ TRANSIT President and CEO Kris Kolluri, and New Jersey Department of Transportation Commissioner Priya Jain, Menendez urged state leadership to prioritize critical infrastructure upgrades and advance service expansions.

The HBLR serves more than 55,000 people daily commuters across New Jersey’s most densely populated region, where roughly one in three Hudson County households rely on public transportation.

“Investing in public transit directly improves daily quality of life for New Jersey families,” said Congressman Menendez. “Partnering with Hudson County Complete Streets and state leadership to modernize the HBLR means faster, more reliable commutes and better access to jobs and economic opportunity across our region. I am grateful to our transit advocates for their continued commitment to strengthening our transit network and look forward to continuing our work together.”

“The Hudson-Bergen Light Rail does more than simply move 55 thousand daily riders to their destinations, it supports economic growth, connects communities, and creates opportunity for both individuals and businesses,” said Jack McKee, Campaigns Manager, Hudson County Complete Streets. “It’s for these reasons that Hudson County Complete Streets is committed to realizing the asks laid out by our campaign.”

“Approximately 1 in 3 households in Hudson County do not have access to a vehicle at home. The Hudson Bergen Light Rail (HBLR) is a vital connector for communities across Hudson County,” said Dana Haymon, Campaign Lead, Better Light Rail. “Expanding this essential service to Bergen County and deeper into Jersey City is absolutely necessary to connect us with jobs, reduce our environmental impact, and just make getting around safer and easier for the thousands of folks that want to ride the HBLR. This is why we are asking for service expansion and investment at all levels to make our campaign goals happen.”

To accelerate ongoing planning and build on the state’s existing efforts, Congressman Menendez urged state leaders to prioritize the following key actions:

Frequency and Reliability: 10-minute off-peak service intervals and state-of-good-repair infrastructure investments to minimize travel disruptions.

Service Expansion: Collaborative planning timelines to extend service across Route 440 in Jersey City, into Bergen County, and toward Newark.

Rider Experience: Upgraded real-time train tracking systems and potential new local stops in Jersey City and Hoboken.
