title: Meuser Thanks Treasury Secretary Bessent for Touting Benefits of Auto-Enrollment for Trump Accounts
text:
HARRISBURG, PA — Today, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09) issued the following statement after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s press conference in Harrisburg, PA, where he discussed what automatic enrollment for Trump Accounts means for Pennsylvania families.

“I’d like to thank Secretary Bessent for being in Harrisburg today highlighting the opportunities that Trump Accounts are creating for Pennsylvania families,” said Congressman Meuser. “Through participatory capitalism, we are creating the opportunity for families to set their children up for financial success and empowering parents to teach their children the benefits of responsible financial management and participation in our markets. Thanks to auto-enrollment, over 60 million children now have an account that can easily be claimed by their parents. Created by the Republican’s Working Families Tax Cuts Act, Trump Accounts are giving millions of young Pennsylvanians a financial head start. I’m grateful to Secretary Bessent and President Trump for their hard work in ensuring every American child has access to the wealth-building opportunities Trump Accounts provide.”

Background on Trump Accounts:

Created by the GOP’s Working Families Tax Cuts Act, these tax-free investment accounts will harness the strength of financial markets to reignite the American Dream of a comfortable retirement for America’s youth. Supercharged by a one-time contribution of $1,000 from Treasury, Trump Accounts allow families to contribute up to $5,000 per year to boost their child’s long-term savings. Additionally, employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year to Trump Accounts for their employees’ children, expanding the pool of potential investments. Republicans in Congress were careful in crafting the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to ensure the healthy growth of Trump Accounts. When families invest in their child’s Trump Account, the funds are allocated to a diversified portfolio of low-cost index funds, mutual funds, or exchange-traded funds designed to maximize long-term growth while minimizing risk.

With automatic enrollment complete, every eligible child under the age of eighteen with a valid Social Security number now has a Trump Account. A parent or guardian must claim the child’s automatically enrolled Trump Account to manage it and allow for family members, friends, and employers to contribute. Automatic enrollment also allows businesses, financial institutions, and philanthropists to contribute individual stocks into the accounts of thousands or even millions of children. To claim your child’s Trump Account, download the official Trump Accounts app, available for iOS and Android. During the claiming process, a parent or guardian will verify their identity and relationship to their child, review the child’s information, and accept the account terms. Eligible children born between January 21, 2025, and December 31, 2028, are eligible to receive the one-time $1,000 seed contribution. For more information, visit TrumpAccounts.gov.

Since Trump Accounts went live on July 4, 2026, 7 million children have already had a Trump Account created for them by their families. With Automatic Enrollment now in effect, over 60 million additional children now have an account created in their name. According to the White House Council of Economic Advisors, Trump accounts are projected to grow anywhere from roughly $6,000 (with only the initial $1,000 federal seed and no extra contributions) to over $300,000 by age 18 if maximum annual contributions of $5,000 are made. This is money that young Americans can use for their college education, to buy a home, or other important life expenses.

title: ICYMI: Miller-Meeks, Trump Announce Largest-Ever Steel Plant Coming to Lee County
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) and President Donald Trump announced the largest steel plant ever built in the United States is coming to Lee County, Iowa. This $15 billion steel plant will create 1,750 new, permanent jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and generate an estimated $95 billion in U.S. economic output over construction and the first decade of operations.

“For too long, Iowa families have watched their jobs shipped overseas and their communities hollowed out. Not anymore", said Rep. Miller-Meeks. "The largest steel plant in America is coming to Lee County with more than 1,700 permanent, good-paying jobs. I’m proud to have helped make this historic investment a reality. There’s no better place than Iowa to make things IN America, BY Americans.”

“I want to thank President Trump for his commitment to bringing steel manufacturing back to America, and Mesabi Metallics for choosing Iowa as its partner and future home. This is a transformational opportunity for our country, our state, and American families—one that strengthens national security, creates thousands of high-paying jobs, and provides a reliable supply of high-quality, American-made steel for strategic goods and everyday products", said Gov. Reynolds. "Our commitment in Iowa to fiscal responsibility, tax competitiveness, and long-term economic stability has created one of the nation’s strongest environments for business investment. Now, this opportunity will fundamentally change the economic trajectory of our state and the entire region for decades to come.”

“This massive investment is the largest steel plant project in U.S. History. It means over 1,750 good-paying, family-supporting, steel working jobs for Southeast Iowa", said Iowa Attorney General Bird. "This announcement is not just good news for Iowa, it’s good for the entire country. Thanks to President Trump for his leadership and continued commitment to American jobs for American citizens and to Governor Reynolds for her hard work bringing this great opportunity to Iowa.”

“GR8 NEWS Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 BILLION steel mill in IA Remember GOP is working 2 bring down costs 4 families + create jobs This historic investment is AMERICA FIRST+builds on success of our Working Families Tax Cuts law which also prevented largest tax increase ever", said Sen. Grassley.

“Proud to join @POTUS today announcing a historic $15 BILLION investment in eastern Iowa, the largest steel plant in American history, and over 1700 permanent jobs in Iowa! Thank you, President Trump, for bringing jobs, investment, and American manufacturing back home", said Sen. Ernst.

“This will be a game-changing investment for our state — creating 1,700 jobs & incredible opportunities for growth. There is no better place to invest and build than in Iowa because we have the best people", said Rep. Hinson.

“This is a major opportunity for Southeast Iowa: Mesabi Metallics’ proposed $15 billion investment in Lee County could support 1,700 good-paying jobs and produce American steel right here in Iowa", said Rep. Nunn. "We’ve worked to bring manufacturing home and secured nearly $5 million to strengthen skilled trades training at DMACC, Iowa Western, and Indian Hills. Now, we need to make sure Iowa workers have the skills to be first in line for these jobs and ready to build the next generation of American steel.”

“This historic investment is a major win for Iowa workers and further cements Iowa’s role in the future of American manufacturing. As the largest steel plant investment in U.S. history, this project will generate over 1,700 good-paying Iowa jobs, create new opportunities for Iowa families, and drive economic growth. Iowa has the workforce, work ethic, resources, and business climate to compete with anyone, and we are proud to welcome this project to our state. The administration’s pro-American manufacturing policies are incentivizing companies to invest, build, and create jobs in the U.S. We thank Governor Reynolds for her leadership in making Iowa a great place to do business and ensuring our state benefits from these policies by attracting transformational investments like this one", said the Iowa Congressional Delegation.

“This project would be a gamechanger for southeast Iowa and leave a lasting impact on our state’s manufacturing footprint. This will bring real jobs that mean stable careers for working families, giving more young people a chance to proudly call Iowa home", said Iowa Speaker of the House Pat Grassley. I’ve made it my mission in the Iowa House to make sure we bring opportunities for growth to all parts of the state and delivering this plant follows through on that promise.”

“For years, we have been passing legislation to help Iowa grow, draw people to our rural communities, and strengthen our state’s economy. Iowa has an opportunity to bring billions of dollars of investment into our state, good quality jobs, and bring people to a part of Iowa looking for growth", said Iowa Senate Majority Leader Mike Kilmesh. "These are the kinds of opportunities we have been looking for and that Iowa needs. As we look to remain competitive on the national level, the largest private investment in Iowa history makes it clear our state is open for business.”

“$15 BILLION dollar investment in Iowa (largest ever, by far)! Thank you President Donald J. Trump & Governor Kim Reynolds for your leadership on this historic project", said Iowa State Rep. Norman.

“HUGE day for Iowa! The President is announcing a $15 billion investment to build America’s largest steel mill right here in our state — more than 1,750 good-paying jobs for Iowa families. This didn’t happen by accident. For years, Iowa has done the hard work of cutting taxes, slashing red tape, and making it cheaper and faster to build here than almost anywhere else in the country", said Iowa State Rep. Harris. "Companies don’t drop $15 billion on a handshake. They go where the rules are clear, the tax climate is competitive, and the workforce can get the job done. That’s Iowa. We made ourselves the place they wanted to be. Now it will pay off in paychecks, apprenticeships, suppliers, and communities that will feel this for a generation. I am proud of this state and proud of the workers who are about to make history. Iowa is open for business! Let’s get to work!”

“To have one of the largest steel plants in American history built right here in Lee County would be a huge win for our area", said Iowa State Rep. Watkins. "It would mean thousands of high-paying, dependable jobs that would give young Iowans a reason to stay, grow their families, and thrive right here in Southeast Iowa. I’ve been fighting for this kind of opportunity in the Iowa House, and I will fight to get this project over the finish line in the Iowa House.”

“As a Burlington native, I recognize this announcement for what it is: a once-in-a-generation economic development victory for Iowa. Since being elected to the Iowa House, my priorities have included securing high-paying careers to ensure more people can call Iowa home, and keeping our state competitive in manufacturing apprenticeships and training", said Iowa State Rep. Rinker. "The announcement of one of the largest steel plants in American history built right here in Iowa shows that the work we’ve done at the Statehouse, including reducing the tax burden and keeping government spending fiscally responsible is working. In the House, I will fight to deliver this opportunity for my district.”

“Today is a great day for eastern Iowa. A $15 billion investment with more than 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs would be transformational for our region, and we congratulate Mesabi Metallics on today’s announcement", said Emily Benjamin, CEO of Lee County Economic Development Group President.

“What’s great for the southeast Iowa region is great for Burlington and what’s great for Burlington is great for southeast Iowa", said Burlington Mayor Jon Billups.

"Steel mill will deliver overwhelming benefits to Iowa", said former Iowa Gov. Branstad.

“Thank you, Mr. President, for bringing back the importance of building things in America", said Rewant Ruia, Mesabi Metallics Chairman. "With the new steel complex in Iowa, we will complete the fully integrated American supply chain from mine to mill. American ore carried on American railroads to an American steel plant powered by American energy, built and operated by an incredibly hardworking and talented American workforce.”

“This is a major moment for U.S. made steel, combining the highest quality direct-reduction grade iron ore pellet from Minnesota’s Iron Range with the most advanced DRI to EAF steelmaking technology in Iowa to supply the high-quality, all-American steel that our national defense, cars and trucks, shipbuilding, household appliances, energy, and infrastructure depend on", said Mesabi Mettalics CEO Joe Broking.

“What we’re really talking about today is America’s economic security… What you see here today is private capital flowing in to rebuild America and to build America’s future", said Export-Import Bank of the United States Chairman John Jovanovic.

“President Trump’s Section 232 steel tariffs continue to energize the American iron and steel industry. AISI welcomes today’s announcement of another significant new investment in steelmaking in the United States. The sizeable investment by Mesabi Metallics in the new Iowa plant and also its Nashwauk, Minnesota, iron ore mine will further boost U.S. ironmaking and steelmaking capacity, create jobs and strengthen the U.S. economy", said American Iron and Steel Institute President and CEO Kevin Dempsey.

“This is coming to Lee County, an area in Iowa really in dire need of revitalization", said John Boyd, The Boyd Company Principal. "This is the right project at the right time."

“President Trump announces a historic $15 BILLION steel plant coming to Iowa — the largest in American history. 6,000 construction jobs. Nearly 2,000 permanent jobs. 10 MILLION tons of American steel produced every year. American steel is BACK", said America First Policy Institute.

title: Miller-Meeks Introduces Bill to Protect Medicaid Whistleblowers from Retaliation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, M.D. (IA-01) has introduced the Medicaid Whistleblower Protection Act, legislation to establish clear federal protections for state and local employees who report fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid programs. The bill comes after widespread reports of retaliation against whistleblowers in states like Minnesota, where public servants say they were punished for raising early warnings about fraud that later cost taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars.

The bill amends Title XIX of the Social Security Act to prohibit adverse employment actions against Medicaid workers who make protected disclosures, and it establishes a clear administrative and judicial process for whistleblowers to seek relief, including reinstatement, back pay, and damages.

"No public servant should have to choose between their conscience and their livelihood. Whistleblowers who report fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid are protecting taxpayer dollars and the vulnerable people this program is meant to serve, and they deserve real protection, not retaliation," said Dr. Miller-Meeks. "The Medicaid Whistleblower Protection Act gives whistleblowers a clear legal process to report wrongdoing and seek relief if they're punished for speaking up. I will fight to make sure the people willing to tell the truth are protected, not silenced."

The Medicaid Whistleblower Protection Act is one of 14 bills in House Energy and Commerce Republicans' "Continuing the Fight Against Fraud" package, a sweeping program-integrity agenda introduced under Chairman Brett Guthrie (KY-02) to give states better data and technology, stronger enforcement incentives, and clearer accountability to detect and recover improper Medicaid payments.

“The amount of fraud that the Biden-Harris Administration allowed to go unchecked in government health programs is unacceptable. Every dollar stolen by fraudsters or wasted on improper payments is a dollar taken away from supporting families in need who rely on these programs,” said Chairman Guthrie. “While states are on the front lines of confronting this fraud, we must take commonsense steps to ensure that they are able to recoup their costs, providing incentives to do the vital work that is needed, including needed data sharing and new technologies that support enforcement, to ensure the program can continue to work for the Americans it was designed to serve. By using enhanced data analytics to find and eliminate fraud, incentivizing states to crack down on fraud more diligently, and fortifying the integrity of critical health programs, Republicans are leading the charge to restore the long-term vitality of federally funded health systems. Our multi-faceted program integrity package will help to combat the fraud that has plagued our system for far too long, I’m grateful for the consistent focus of our bill sponsors and their tireless effort to protect these programs, and we look forward to continuing the fight ensure Americans have access to the care they need.”

"I am so grateful for the leadership of Congresswoman Miller-Meeks and the House Energy & Commerce Committee for introducing this whistleblower protection bill. Too often, as we have seen in Minnesota, brave whistleblowers are retaliated against by politicians and agency leaders who are more interested in protecting their political base than taxpayers and vulnerable citizens. The federal, state and county workers who run these programs are often the first to see red flags, but, as we have seen time and again in Minnesota, if they dare to point it out, they are called racist, accused of creating a hostile work environment, demoted, reassigned or otherwise harmed personally and professionally," said Kristin Robbins, Minnesota State Representative, House District 37A. "The Whistleblower Protection bill will expand protections for federal, state and county employees so they can do what they do best: serve the public, help vulnerable citizens and protect taxpayers' hard-earned money."

Miller-Meeks is also leading a second bill in the package, the WALZ Act, which requires the HHS Office of Inspector General to review whether a 10 percent increase in a state's Medicaid spending may be attributable to fraud, waste, or abuse, giving Congress and states a data-driven early warning system for the kind of unchecked spending growth whistleblowers say went ignored in Minnesota for years.

Background

The Medicaid Whistleblower Protection Act would:

Prohibit adverse employment actions, including discharge, demotion, suspension, threats, harassment, or other discrimination, against covered individuals who make a protected disclosure related to a State Medicaid program.

Establish an administrative process for whistleblowers to seek relief, with the right to judicial review if they disagree with the outcome.

Provide remedies including reinstatement, two times back pay with interest, compensation for litigation costs and attorneys' fees, and punitive damages in cases of malice or reckless indifference.

Define protected disclosures broadly to include violations of law, fraud, waste, or abuse involving federal or state funds, gross mismanagement, abuse of authority, or a substantial danger to public health or safety.

The legislation follows a letter submitted to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform on January 7, 2026, by current and former Minnesota Department of Human Services employees, describing a pattern of retaliation against workers who raised early concerns about fraud in DHS programs. The letter states that employees flagged contracting irregularities, unusual financial transactions, and signs of fraud as far back as 2019, and that those who spoke up faced surveillance, repeated investigations, reassignment, and termination. It was entered into the congressional record and referenced in subsequent testimony before the Oversight Committee.

The bill also follows a Majority Staff Report released by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, through the work of the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations chaired by Congressman John Joyce, M.D. (PA-13), detailing how fraud has continued to undermine the integrity of critical taxpayer-funded health care programs and the disparities in oversight and enforcement across state Medicaid programs. The report outlines 13 investigative findings and 37 recommendations to strengthen program integrity and keep fraudsters out of Medicare and Medicaid. During the investigation, the Committee sent 12 letters, held three Oversight and Investigations hearings, and reviewed more than 100,000 pages of documents. Read the full report here.

"The Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee is focused on rooting out fraud that threatens the future of Medicare and Medicaid. These crimes hurt patients and steal from the American taxpayer," said Chairman Joyce. "We will continue to expose those who exploit the system, hold fraudsters accountable, and advance commonsense recommendations that states can implement. This cannot be solved alone. Protecting the integrity of these programs must be a shared goal, because millions of Americans are counting on us to get it right."

About the "Continuing the Fight Against Fraud" package: Medicaid remains vulnerable to waste, fraud, abuse, and improper payments going undetected. The 14-bill package strengthens program integrity in three ways: better data and technology for states to detect fraud, stronger enforcement tools and incentives to recover improper spending, and clearer accountability requiring states to identify vulnerabilities and take corrective action. In addition to the Medicaid Whistleblower Protection Act and the WALZ Act, the package includes bills from Chairman Guthrie and Committee Republicans, such as Griffith's Medicaid Fraud Fighting and Taxpayer Protection Act, Balderson's SMART Act, Joyce's Medicaid Integrity Improvement Act, and Pfluger's Medicaid Integrity and Fiscal Accountability Act, among others.

title: Rep. Neguse Leads Colleagues in Letter to State Department Urging Additional Support for Nepal Floods Response
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Nepal Caucus, led a dozen colleagues in a letter to the United States Department of State, urging they provide additional aid to Nepal as the country recovers from devastating floods in the Trishuli River region.

In late August, a glacier collapse on the Nepal-China border, caused catastrophic flooding, destroying homes, workplaces, roads, bridges, and energy infrastructure. The floods killed 1,450 people and nearly 6,000 people are still missing, including 90 Americans.

In their letter, Neguse and his colleagues noted that the United States has been a longstanding partner in Nepal’s development and called on the State Department to provide much needed support and stability to the country as it recovers and eventually rebuilds.

Full text of the letter is available HERE and below.

It was signed by André Carson (IN-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), James McGovern (MA-02), Janice Schakowsky (IL-09), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Emilia Sykes (OH-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Nydia Velázquez (NY-07).

October 1, 2026

The Honorable Marco Rubio

Secretary of State

U.S. Department of State

2201 C Street NW

Washington, DC 20520

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to respectfully request your administration provide further assistance to aid Nepal in its recovery efforts following the devastating floods in the Trishuli River region. Given the scale of this tragedy, we implore your department to act swiftly.

As you know, this unprecedented disaster has claimed at least 1,300 lives, with an estimated 5,000 people still missing—including 90 American citizens. Further, the destruction has left many in the region without access to clean drinking water, food, shelter, and other basic services, including thousands of children. As Nepal continues to recover, the U.S. is uniquely positioned to provide critical infrastructure support and essential supplies to aid these efforts.

The U.S. has been a longstanding partner in Nepal's development, supporting improvements in public health, education, infrastructure, and industry. Continued U.S. assistance would provide much needed stability to the country and help it to rebuild at this critical time.

As such, we urge the Department of State to work to assist search and rescue efforts across Nepal and to provide additional assistance to the country to ensure a speedy recovery.

Sincerely,

title: Nunn Hosts Air Force Secretary Meink, Makes Case for New 132d Wing Air Mission
text:
“Iowa’s Airmen have answered every mission our country has asked of them, and on Friday Secretary Meink saw that commitment firsthand at the 132d Wing,” said Rep. Nunn. “Having served in the Air Force for more than 20 years, I know how much it means to these Airmen and their families to have the Secretary here to see their work up close. I’m grateful to Secretary Meink for making the trip to Des Moines, and I look forward to working with him as the Air Force plans for the next generation of American air dominance.”

“Last week’s visit to the 132nd ANG was an awesome opportunity to see the professionalism, dedication, and capabilities of Iowa’s Airmen,” said Secretary Meink. “They are critical to keeping our nation secure, and I appreciate the opportunity to further assess how the Department can best leverage the capabilities, infrastructure, and talent already in place here in Des Moines.”

Rep. Nunn and Secretary Meink met with 132d Wing leadership, toured the Wing’s remotely piloted aircraft, cyber, and intelligence operations, and recognized the Airmen who carry out those missions. Mrs. Nunn and Mrs. Meink also visited the Wing’s Airman & Family Readiness Center, which supports the families of Iowa Airmen while their loved ones are deployed or on duty.

Following the tour, Rep. Nunn held a press conference outside the Wing, where he highlighted his work in Congress to deliver federal dollars to the airport and bring a permanent flying mission back to the 132d. Rep. Nunn helped deliver $26 million to modernize the airport’s air traffic control system through the Working Families Tax Cut and secured $4 million for its deicing apron expansion.

Rep. Nunn led an amendment included in the House-passed FY27 National Defense Authorization Act directing the Air Force to identify Air National Guard installations that have active runways but no manned aircraft that are well-positioned to host next-generation flying missions. The amendment was supported by the entire Iowa delegation in the House and is being led by Senator Joni Ernst and supported by Senator Chuck Grassley in the Senate.

Last month, Rep. Nunn wrote to Secretary Meink requesting a comprehensive feasibility study of the 132d Wing and invited the Secretary to Des Moines to see its capabilities firsthand. The proposed study would evaluate the 132d’s existing facilities, workforce and recruiting capacity, airfield access, and potential mission sets.

“We don’t need to pour billions into new concrete when the runway that can support next-generation aircraft is already here,” continued Rep. Nunn. “The House passed our amendment unanimously, and with Senator Ernst and Senator Grassley leading in the Senate, I’m confident we’ll get it signed into law and put the 132d Wing in a strong position to compete for a permanent flying mission.”

title: Pou Demands Answers After 5,500-Gallon Data Center Diesel Spill
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) is seeking answers from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) following a massive diesel fuel spill at an Equinix data center in Secaucus that contaminated local waterways in her district.

Pou called for a full accounting of the roughly 5,500-gallon spill, its environmental impact, and the safeguards being put in place to prevent another data center disaster.

“This spill in the Ninth District was the largest data center fuel spill on record in our state. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. We need to understand how it happened, ensure the cleanup is complete, and put protections in place to prevent another one happening again. Our residents deserve clear answers now,” Congresswoman Pou writes to New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Commissioner Ed Potosnak.

Secaucus and surrounding communities have lived with pollution for decades. Contamination from industrial sites and landfill runoff led the Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River a Superfund site in 2022. Now as a major cleanup is underway, the September 11 Equinix spill has dumped another 5,500 gallons of diesel into the local environment.

The Secaucus spill comes amid growing national concern over the environmental impact and public costs of rapidly expanding data centers. These facilities consume large amounts of electricity and can require significant water for cooling. Also, as seen in Secaucus, they can often store large quantities of diesel to power backup generators.

Data center electricity demand is rising rapidly, raising questions about energy costs and who should pay for the infrastructure needed to serve these facilities. The Secaucus spill highlights what can happen when the systems designed to keep these massive facilities running fail.

Pou concludes, “NJDEP has a vital role in protecting New Jersey’s environment and holding data centers and their owners accountable when safeguards fail. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. . . . Thank you for your attention to this matter.”

A copy of Congresswoman Pou’s letter is below.

Dear Commissioner Potosnak:

I write to express my concern about the recent fuel spill at the Equinix data center in Secaucus that contaminated nearby waterways. Over the last decade, several data centers have experienced large-scale fuel spills, including several in New Jersey. In 2017, roughly 600 gallons of fuel spilled into Clifton’s storm drains from the Digital Realty EWR21 Data Center. Then, in 2022, more than 1800 gallons leaked from an Equinix-owned data center in North Bergen. Now, just weeks ago, Secaucus has experienced the largest data center diesel spill on record in our state. Residents and local officials deserve to know how this happened, what damage it caused, and what safeguards will keep this from happening again.

Secaucus and the surrounding communities have a long history of dealing with pollution. Decades of contamination from manufacturing plants and landfill runoff into the Hackensack River prompted the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River as a Superfund site in 2022. The river is already undergoing a major cleanup after those years of contamination.

Against that backdrop, the September 11 spill is especially alarming. According to public reports, roughly 5,500 gallons of diesel fuel escaped the Equinix data center into a creek and tributary connected to the Hackensack River.5 The spill reportedly occurred during an automated fuel-recycling process and has been attributed to a “computer glitch.”

Three weeks later, the public still lacks a full accounting of the spill’s impact on local waterways and wildlife. The incident also raises broader questions about the environmental risks posed by data centers, including the storage and handling of large quantities of backup fuel. Those questions are particularly urgent here given the major federal cleanup underway on the Hackensack River.

I appreciate that NJDEP is working to investigate and address the spill. But NJDEP must provide a clear account of exactly what happened and what is being done to prevent another spill to ensure transparency and accountability. To that end, please provide answers to the following questions no later than October 9, 2026.

1) Please identify the best available timeline for when each of the following events occurred on September 11, 2026 and any days thereafter:

a) Equinix began its fuel recycling process.

b) The system failed, and fuel began spilling.

c) Equinix first identified the spill.

d) The flow of fuel was stopped.

e) Equinix first contacted emergency responders.

f) Equinix first notified NJDEP.

g) The emergency response team arrived on site.

h) Crews began containment efforts to prevent the diesel from spreading.

i) NJDEP first notified Secaucus officials about the spill and the response.

j) Any barges or other cleanup equipment that were removed from the site, and the basis for determining they were no longer needed.

2) Has NJDEP continued to brief Secaucus on the containment and cleanup? If so, please provide the dates of those communications. If not, please explain why.

3) Following the spill, has NJDEP required Equinix or other data centers to adopt human, on-site monitoring and other safeguards for automated fuel systems or other risks to the community? If so, please describe those requirements. If not, please explain why.

4) Has NJDEP determined whether diesel from the spill reached the Hackensack River? If so, please provide its findings and any information on remediation and cleanup.

5) When does NJDEP expect to complete its investigation and issue a final public report on the spill?

NJDEP has a vital role in protecting New Jersey’s environment and holding data centers and their owners accountable when safeguards fail. This spill in the Ninth District was the largest data center fuel spill on record in our state. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. We need to understand how it happened, ensure the cleanup is complete, and put protections in place to prevent another one happening again. Our residents deserve clear answers now.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response.

Sincerely,

Nellie Pou

Member of Congress

title: Reps. Ramirez, Salinas Introduce Legislation to Require the Federal Government to Share Evidence with Local Law Enforcement in DHS Use-of-Force Incidents
text:
Washington, DC – Recently, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, and Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) introducedH.R.10698, the ICE Shootings Transparency Act, to provide local and state law enforcement agencies unfettered access to evidence in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer-involved shootings and other use of force incidents.

“DHS lies to avoid accountability. DHS agents use reckless and unlawful force, and then DHS issues public statements justifying the use of force that are repeatedly proven false or highly misleading,” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “That’s why I’m joining Rep. Salinas to require DHS and the Attorney General to share evidence related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers with local law enforcement agencies to carry out investigations. We will not stop until we have justice for every person who was killed or harmed at the hands of DHS agents. We will reimagine true safety, abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, and hold all perpetrators accountable.”

“When an ICE or CBP agent kills or injures someone in our community, transparency needs to be the bare minimum,” said Rep. Salinas. “Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the federal government has often refused to provide local law enforcement with critical evidence in shootings and other use-of-force incidents involving ICE and CBP officers. My bill would ensure that when these incidents occur, state and local law enforcement agencies would have unrestricted access to this evidence to deliver full justice to victims and their families.”

In January 2026, when ICE killed Renee Good, Minnesota’s Bureau of Criminal Apprehension was tapped to conduct a joint investigation with the FBI. However, shortly after the announcement, the state agency said that they had been kicked out of the investigation, leaving the investigation in the hands of the Trump Administration. Several months later, ICE agents killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and have also refused to work with state and local law enforcement. The administration’s actions have included blocking local and state law enforcement officials from accessing investigatory materials, such as Salgado Araujo’s work van and the scene of the incident.

The members introduced the ICE Shootings Transparency Act to address issues that some local agencies and prosecutors have encountered with ICE and CBP officers-involved shootings that result in the injury or death of a civilian. Their bill would require the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Attorney General to share evidence on an ongoing basis with appropriate local law enforcement agencies related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers that injure or kill someone.

Additionally, this bill would require DHS and the Attorney General to provide access to the location of the incident to state and local law enforcement agencies with jurisdiction over the area to carry out regular investigative functions.

The ICE Shootings Transparency Act is cosponsored by Reps. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-At Large), Jim Costa (CA-21), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29).

The legislation is endorsed by the National Immigration Law Center (NILC).

BACKGROUND:

Congresswoman Ramirez has led the calls for accountability of DHS and its leadership. In September 2026, Ramirez stood with Illinois public officials, civil society, and community members to announce the Reimagining Safety Act.The landmark community-led legislation would create a new human- and community-centered federal department that promotes collective safety, repeal the authorities that give the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) its power, and redirect DHS funds to programs that working families rely on. title: WA Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Emily Randall (D, WA-06), and Representatives Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

title: Raskin and Schatz Fight Back Against MAGA Book Bans and Attacks on First Amendment Rights of the Free Press and of Citizens in Schools, Libraries and Museums
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.— Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and Senator Brian Schatz (D-HI) introduced a resolution standing strong for the American freedom to read, write and learn. The lawmakers’ resolution condemns MAGA’s escalating campaign of book bans in school libraries and censorship targeting the Smithsonian Institution and other public museums, parks and facilities.

The lawmakers’ resolution specifically cites book bans issued by the Trump Administration, MAGA state legislatures, local libraries and schools across America. This year, federal officials, at the direction of President Trump, censoredbooks andeducational materials at the Smithsonian Institution and Department of Defense Education Activity schools.

“The freedom to read, write and think independently are all rights enshrined in the First Amendment to our Constitution,”said Rep. Raskin."MAGA’s book bans and censorship campaigns seek to control the freedom of thought in schools, libraries and government, but we are fighting back against this authoritarian assault on free expression and American democracy.”

“Any attempt to ban books because someone has an ideological disagreement or doesn’t believe in capturing the full scope of history is un-American,”said Senator Schatz. “Freedom of expression is a founding principle of our country, and it's up to all of us to stand up against these attacks on this fundamental right.”

More than 12,000 individual books were banned in America between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report by PEN America. This includes books like “The Bluest Eye” by Toni Morrison and “MARCH” by former Congressman and Civil Rights Movement hero John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell.

PEN America’s report captures the proliferation of MAGA book bans that specifically target books written by and about outsiders and individuals from marginalized backgrounds. Books with LGBTQ+ characters or themes face a disproportionate risk of being banned.

According to PEN America, from July 2025 to June 2026, 24 States across the country limited access to certain books, including—

Texas, where at least 8,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 45 school districts;

Florida, where at least 3,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 35 school districts;

Ohio, where at least 115 books in total have been banned or restricted in one school district;

Utah, where at least 100 books in total have been banned or restricted in five school districts; and

Michigan, where at least 65 books in total have been banned or restricted in two school districts.

The resolution is endorsed by PEN America and the American Library Association (ALA); Authors Against Banned Books; Banned Books Week Coalition; Center for American Progress; EdTrust; EveryLibrary; Freedom to Learn Foundation; Florida Freedom to Read Project; Freedom to Read Project; Hatchette Book Group; Interfaith Alliance; JCRC of Greater Washington; Jewish Community Relations Council of Portland; Jewish Council for Public Affairs; Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester; Lee & Low Books ; Let Utah Read; Macmillan Publishing; National Coalition Against Censorship; National Council for Jewish Women; National Council of Teachers of English; National Education Association; Penguin Random House; PFLAG National; Red Wine and Blue Education Fund; Simon & Schuster; Texas Freedom to Read Project; and the Tucson Jewish Museum & Holocaust Center.

The resolution is cosponsored in the House by Representatives Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Shontel Brown (OH-11), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Andre Carson (IN-07), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Emmanuel Cleaver (MO-5), Jim Costa (CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Betty McCollum (MN-04), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Grace Meng (NY-06), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Scott Peters (CA-50), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).

title: RILEY DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM VERIZON OVER RURAL LANDLINE SHUTOFFS
text:
BINGHAMTON, NY – Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) is demanding answers from Verizon about notices the company has sent to residents across Upstate New York warning that their copper landline telephone service may soon be shut off. These notices followed Verizon’s September 9, 2026 application to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) seeking approval to discontinue this service as soon as November 30, 2026.

In a letter to Verizon CEO Dan Schulman, Riley expressed concern that alternatives to copper landline service, such as fiber and wireless networks, are not a reliable solution for Upstate New York communities. In many rural areas, the landline is how people call 911, how medical alert and monitoring devices work, and how families stay connected. Unlike the alternatives, traditional landlines keep working during a blackout, and in rural New York, blackouts are frequent and can last for days.

“For many Upstate New Yorkers, discontinuing copper landline service would mean losing the only phone service they can count on,” Riley said. “Rural communities present real challenges, but rather than rising to meet them, Verizon appears to be walking away from us. Upstate New Yorkers should not be forced to pay the price in new equipment, higher monthly bills, or fears about whether their phone will work in an emergency.”

In the letter, Riley demanded Verizon provide the following information to his office:

The number of residential and business customers in New York’s 19th Congressional District whose copper landline service could be discontinued under Verizon’s application, broken down by county.

A full list, by county, town, and ZIP code, of every area in New York’s 19th Congressional District where Verizon is seeking to discontinue copper landline service. For each area, indicate whether affected customers currently have access to an alternative voice service, such as fiber or wireless, or whether they will have no alternative option available.

For each affected customer, the specific alternative service that will be available, and how Verizon has confirmed that it is fully operational at that customer’s location.

Whether Verizon will commit not to discontinue service to any customer until a working alternative has been confirmed at that customer’s location, and what will happen to customers for whom no reliable alternative exists.

The financial impact on affected customers, including whether they will be protected against rate increases after switching to a new service, and whether Verizon will cover all necessary equipment, installation and setup costs.

How replacement services will function during power outages, and how Verizon will ensure uninterrupted access to 911 and other emergency services.

The steps Verizon will take to engage affected customers, county emergency management offices, and local governments before any service is discontinued, including whether Verizon will commit to holding public meetings in affected communities.

Why Verizon believes a November 30, 2026 timeline gives customers sufficient time to transition, and whether it will agree to extend that timeline.

title: Rep. Kelly and Rep. Latimer Introduce Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Congresswoman Robin Kelly (D-IL) and U.S. Congressman George Latimer (D-NY) introduced the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026, a bill to create and expand partnerships between community health centers and emergency feeding operations to provide access to food at these centers.

In the face of unprecedented cuts to SNAP and Medicaid, emergency feeding operations and community health centers have provided critical support to countless Americans. Partnerships between community health centers and emergency feeding operations have enabled underserved populations to reduce food insecurity. It is well established that access to food is critical to primary health. As Americans continue to struggle with access to food and healthcare, partnerships between organizations like these are vital tools to alleviate these crises. This bill would enable these existing partnerships to be expanded and for new ones to be created.

Congresswoman Kelly and Congressman Latimer previously championed this cause by sending a letter to the leadership of the Labor-HHS-Education Appropriations subcommittee urging them to include report language in the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bill encouraging the expansion of partnerships between emergency feeding operations and community health centers.

Congresswoman Kelly stated, “What makes us sick, or keeps us well, starts long before we ever walk into a doctor's office. Over 40 million Americans have limited access to affordable groceries, and the Big, Ugly Law has now gutted SNAP and Medicaid on top of that. Community health centers and emergency feeding operations are already stepping up. This bill helps them do it together, through on-site food pantries and mobile distribution, so patients can get both the care and the healthy food they need. I'm proud to partner with Congressman Latimer to ensure that everyone has access to nutritious food, no matter their zip code.”

Congressman Latimer stated, “I am proud to introduce this critical legislation alongside Congresswoman Robin Kelly at a time when far too many across our country are facing food insecurity and the rising cost of living. Food access is directly linked to health outcomes, and this bill aims to address the food insecurity that patients experience when seeking essential care. I am grateful to the national, statewide, and local partners who stand alongside us to ensure patients receive the comprehensive care. I look forward to working alongside our stakeholders as we work towards passing this necessary legislation.”

Judith Watson, RN BSN MPH, HD, CEO of Westchester Community Health Center, stated, “Congressman Latimer came to our health centers, met our staff and patients, and saw firsthand how food insecurity affects our community. Then he did something about it. That is what leadership looks like, and it is truly inspiring. Hunger is a pressing issue that impacts the health of our community, including our patients and many neighbors who are not our patients. You cannot manage diabetes or high blood pressure without access to healthy food. Our partnership with Feeding Westchester has shown what a health center and a food bank can do together. We are grateful to Congressman Latimer and Congresswoman Kelly for introducing the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act, which would help health centers across the country bring nutritious food to their communities.”

Kristine Borok, President and CEO of Feeding Westchester, stated, “At Feeding Westchester, we believe food is a fundamental right, and access to nutritious food is fundamental to our health. When people lack reliable access to nutritious food, chronic conditions become harder to manage, preventable health problems escalate, and too often the result is a medical crisis. Food as Medicine addresses this by recognizing that our food and healthcare system cannot operate in isolation. We are grateful to Congressman Latimer, who saw this work firsthand at our Food as Medicine partner sites and responded with the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act. This bill would create a grant program to help community health centers provide food pantry access to their patients, bringing nutritious food to the very places people go for care.”

Rose Duhan, President and CEO of the Community Health Care Association of New York State, stated, “Community health centers see every day how food insecurity can affect a patient’s health and make chronic conditions harder to manage. By bringing health centers and local food providers together, the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would make it easier for patients to access both the care and the resources they need in their communities. Good health starts with having access to the basics, and CHCANYS appreciates Representatives Latimer and Kelly for recognizing the important connection between food access and health.”

Jerome Nathaniel, Director of Policy and Government Relations at City Harvest, stated, “Food security and health are directly connected, which is why community health centers and food access organizations should be collaborating more deeply, especially at a moment when rates of food insecurity are staggeringly high. The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would help bring those systems together, making it easier for organizations like City Harvest to make nutritious food more accessible where people already receive trusted health care and helping address food insecurity as part of supporting healthier communities.”

Anne Kauffman Nolon, MPH, CEO of Sun River Health, stated, “As New York's largest community health center network, we know firsthand that no prescription can make up for an empty refrigerator. The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would help health centers and food banks provide food right where patients receive care. With federal SNAP cuts taking hold, this model has never mattered more. We are proud to support it and grateful to Congressman Latimer for recognizing that food access is health care.”

Leslie Gordon, President and CEO of Food Bank For NYC, stated, “We applaud Representatives Latimer and Kelly for introducing the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act and are proud to join the bill’s coalition of supporters. By investing in partnerships between community health centers and food banks, this legislation recognizes a simple truth: access to nutritious food is essential to good health. This grant program would help deliver meaningful support to families while strengthening the community infrastructure they already trust and rely on.”

The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026:

● Directs the HHS Secretary to establish a grant program to facilitate food access in CHCs.

● Enables emergency feeding operations and CHCs to apply jointly for these grants.

● Eligibility for these grants includes projects that involve creating or expanding a physical space in or adjacent to a CHC (e.g., an on-site food pantry or a mobile distribution vehicle) that assists with providing access to food.

● Specifies the maximum award per partnership as $500,000.

● Requires the HHS Secretary to report on 1) the effectiveness of the program, 2) the impact of the program on the food insecurity of patients of community health centers, and 3) recommendations to improve the program.

The bill has been endorsed by City Harvest, Community Health Care Association of New York State (CHCANYS), Feeding America, Feeding Westchester, Food Bank for NYC, Food Bank of the Southern Tier, Greater Chicago Food Depository, Sun River Health, and Westchester Community Health Center.

title: Ruiz Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Fix Medicare Advantage Payments in Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. Today, Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25), joined by Congressman Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), Congressman Darren Soto (D-FL), and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act. This bipartisan bill would correct a long-standing formula gap that underpays Medicare Advantage in Puerto Rico.

How it works

Medicare Advantage plans receive a fixed monthly payment from the federal government for each senior they enroll. Part of that payment is based on the local cost of care, which is measured by the average geographic adjustment (AGA). Puerto Rico's AGA is much lower than it should be. The formula relies on spending in traditional Medicare (fee-for-service), but very few beneficiaries in Puerto Rico use fee-for-service, since most are enrolled in MA. Basing the AGA on such a small population understates what care actually costs on the island, and MA plans receive a lower benchmark payment for each senior as a result.

This bill would set Puerto Rico's AGA equal to that of the U.S. Virgin Islands, a territory with similar socioeconomic circumstances, so that payments reflect the true cost of delivering care.

The problem

Over 650,000 Puerto Rico beneficiaries rely on Medicare Advantage, over 90 percent of all Medicare beneficiaries on the island.

Puerto Rico receives about 40 percent less per beneficiary than the U.S. average.

Benchmark rates run roughly 20 percent below those in the U.S. Virgin Islands.

The payment gap has led to smaller provider networks and reduced benefits, and doctors and hospitals absorb lower reimbursements. This threatens the quality and availability of healthcare services in Puerto Rico.

"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned."

"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz and Soto in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers."

“I am proud to join Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans." said Congressman Darren Soto.

“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández.

“This legislation represents an important step toward addressing a longstanding structural challenge in Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico. With approximately 96% of Medicare beneficiaries on the Island choosing Medicare Advantage, the methodology used to establish Puerto Rico’s benchmarks must reflect the reality of the market it serves. We thank Congressman Ruiz, Representatives Bilirakis and Soto, and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández Rivera for coming together on a bipartisan solution that would use the U.S. Virgin Islands as a comparable geographic reference and help strengthen access to care for hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. MMAPA strongly supports this effort and looks forward to continuing to work with Congress and CMS to advance a more stable and sustainable Medicare Advantage program for Puerto Rico”, said Solage De Lahongrais, President of the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA)

The legislation would create a self-adjusting link: if the U.S. Virgin Islands' adjustment changes, Puerto Rico's would move with it. It is a targeted fix for a formula that has never reflected the true cost of care on the island.

title: Congresswoman Scholten Announces Her Inaugural Congressional Youth Advisory Council
text:
GRAND RAPIDS, MI – Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) announced her inaugural Congressional Youth Advisory Council (CYAC) for the 2026-2027 school year. 18 students were chosen from a competitive pool of applicants across West Michigan. The students will serve a one-year term, meeting five times over the course of the school year and advising the office on key issues facing their generation.

“Young people bring an energy and thoughtfulness that shapes our political discourse in ways that can invigorate unique ideas. The policy we create in Washington impact not only their day-to-day lives right now, but also, critically, their future. These young people deserve a say in their representation as well, said Congresswoman Scholten. “This class of students embodies West Michigan through their work ethic, care for community, and commitment to public service.”

Throughout the academic year, members of the Congressional Youth Advisory Council participate in policy-focused sessions where student-led committees work together to identify and examine key issues facing their communities. They will work directly with Congresswoman Scholten and her team to turn their ideas into real, workable recommendations for her to consider. While each meeting focuses heavily on one main committee topic, the group also sets aside time to review other upcoming bills. This setup gives students a genuine chance to weigh in on federal legislation, share their perspectives, and make sure young voices have a direct line to Congress.

Meeting one will be an introductory overview to cover the foundations of the program, set expectations, and get everyone ready for the year ahead.

Meeting two will focus on economic policy, where the economy committee will take the lead, guiding a deep dive into the specific financial and economic issues the students want to focus on.

Meeting three will focus on education policy and the education committee will take the floor to explore different facets of the education system and brainstorm potential solutions.

Meeting four will focus on environmental policy. The environment committee will lead discussions on ecological issues and how federal policy can address them.

Meeting five will be an opportunity for the various committees to present their research and policy proposals. Congresswoman Scholten will take the proposals into consideration and the students will be able to answer questions based on their research.

“I’m honored to be part of Congresswoman Scholten’s inaugural Youth Advisory Council. This opportunity allows students like me to share their perspectives, learn more about public service, and contribute to conversations that affect our schools, communities, and future. I look forward to working with Congresswoman Scholten and other student leaders from across West Michigan to make a positive impact,” said Youth Council Member Patrick Latchana.

“I am deeply excited for this opportunity! It is extremely important to hear the voices of the youth, as they will be the next generation in government. Hillary Scholten’s Youth Advisory Council is a step towards making youth’s voices heard state and nationwide,” said Youth Council Member Emma Palmer.

This program reflects Congresswoman Scholten’s ongoing commitment to lifting up the next generation of West Michigan leaders and giving young people a seat at the table in the decisions that shape their future. Read more here.

title: Congresswoman Schrier, WA Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
text:
Letter follows Labor Day incident where individuals were arrested in the middle of the night while camping at Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, 4 of 5 are still being held at Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center

PNW records devastating 2026 wildfire season – Members voice concern USFS is misusing taxpayer funds by directing resources outside of USFS scope and mission

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Representatives Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.

As of October 1, 2026, four of the five men arrested still remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

The full text of the letter is available HERE.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Steube’s Op-Ed Highlights President Trump’s Historic Greenland Security Deal
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) penned an opinion piece in the Washington Times highlighting President Trump’s historic security agreement on Greenland and the importance of strengthening America’s position in the Arctic as Russia and China seek to expand their influence in the region. Read the opinion piece below and in the Washington Times.

Trump’s Arctic Plan Pays Off: A Security Win in Greenland

By Rep. Greg Steube

This past week, President Trump again proved that he is the dealmaker-in-chief by securing a new security deal for Greenland. When the President first raised his desire to renegotiate U.S. access to basing, overflight, and other security parameters for the world’s largest island, those who disagreed accused him of wanting to invade NATO territory. Once again, the President’s style of negotiating has proven the critics wrong and has advanced American security interests.

The Arctic region is strategically critical to U.S. national security. It is no secret that our adversaries are expanding their missions in the great north while the U.S. has focused attention on other areas of the world. The Arctic is the last truly unconquered frontier, one that has been in a state of geopolitical stalemate for centuries. In recent years, however, Russia has begun a significant build-up in the region, with reports estimating that the Federation operates several times the number of permanent bases the U.S. maintains there. China has also sought to establish a robust foothold in the Arctic. In 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping stated his intention to make China a “polar great power.”

Greenland is an epicenter of great power competition for several key reasons, including potential new shipping lanes around the island and space domain awareness afforded by both the latitude and lack of light pollution. The U.S. already has a presence on Greenland with Pituffik Space Base, which maintains critical capabilities such as early-warning systems for ICBMs and plays a large role in transatlantic air traffic, hosting thousands of flights each year. Beyond its

location, the island also holds vast supplies of the critical minerals needed for the economy of today and tomorrow. According to some reports, Greenland holds over thirty-five of the fifty minerals our government deems critical.

The final agreement signed on Tuesday, September 22, will establish new architecture that will allow for greater U.S. basing access and will bar non-NATO nations from establishing their own bases or making investments on the island that threaten our security. The agreement is also being hailed by all the leaders involved, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling it a “historic agreement [that] permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer,” and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen saying the deal “strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area.”

Against the odds and over the loud objections of the Beltway class, President Trump has proven once again that America can secure deals that put Americans first and provide for global security. As he has long said and proven, the two are not separate and should not be treated as such. This agreement is a testament to the strength of our alliances and partnerships, and it will provide for the common defense for decades to come.
