title: Subramanyam, Walkinshaw, Morelle and Virginia Democrats Fight Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting, Pledge to Protect Every Vote
text:
FAIRFAX, VA — Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), and members of Virginia’s Democratic congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation, and misinformation.

The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.

In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.

“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”

"In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”

"Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote," said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. "Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone's right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight."

“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”

“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”

The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.

The experts urged voters to check their registration, make a plan to vote and consult trusted election officials.

View photo gallery here.

title: “Hometown Heroes!” Suozzi Honors Local Police Officers at 7th Hometown Heroes Ceremony
text:
Glen Cove, NY – Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today hosted his seventh “Hometown Heroes” ceremony, continuing a tradition he began to recognize, honor, and thank local law enforcement officers who have demonstrated extraordinary courage and heroism in the line of duty. At this year’s ceremony, held outside the Glen Cove Police Department, Suozzi honored nine officers across five police departments. He recognized five of the officers for protecting victims and apprehending their violent offenders, one for saving a life by de-escalating a mental health crisis, one for saving a child’s life, one for his vigilance and professionalism in removing an illegal firearm, and one for dedicating 20 years to the force, including 15 years handling domestic violence cases.

The nine recognized officers were from the Nassau County Police Department, Glen Cove Police Department, Brookville Police Department, and three precincts of the New York City Police Department: the 105th, 109th, 111th. Suozzi shared the stories of the officers’ heroic actions and the lives they helped save while serving their communities.

“I have made it a tradition to hold these Hometown Heroes ceremonies because the men and women who protect our communities every day deserve our support and our thanks,” said Suozzi. “Police officers have one of the toughest jobs there is. They run toward danger when the rest of us are running away, and too often the extraordinary things they do every day go unnoticed.”

“These Hometown Heroes represent the very best of law enforcement. Their courage, quick thinking, and willingness to put themselves at risk to help others saved lives. I am proud that this is now the seventh time we have come together to recognize these remarkable officers and, most importantly, to say: thank you for keeping us safe.”

Suozzi began his Hometown Heroes tradition to shine a spotlight on the often-unheralded acts of courage performed by local law enforcement officers and to underscore his longstanding support for the men and women who serve in local police departments. This year’s event marks the seventh Hometown Heroes ceremony Suozzi has hosted.

This year’s honorees include officers from the Nassau County Police Department 6th Precinct, Glen Cove Police Department, Brookville Police Department, and three precincts of the New York City Police Department: the 105th, 109th, 111th.

Suozzi presented each officer with an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol and a Congressional citation recognizing their service and heroism.

The following officers were honored by Suozzi at this year’s ceremony:

Police Officers Terrell Carter-Ballier and Matthew Russo

Sixth Precinct

Nassau County

On April 25, 2026, the Sixth Precinct received a call from a woman screaming for help on an open line and a man yelling, “Shut up or I will keep choking you” and “I will kill both of us.” Upon arriving on the scene, Officer Russo heard screams coming from inside the locked house and kicked open the front door. He and Officer Carter-Ballier rescued the victim as she ran up the stairs away from the subject, her estranged husband. She told the officers that he was carrying a rope and a metal baton. The officers found him in the basement holding a lawn stake with 6-inch-long prongs to his chest, which he refused to drop. Both officers initially drew their firearms due to the confined space and the unstable subject who could have charged them with the stake, and tried for several minutes to deescalate the situation by working to get him to drop the stake. Both officers then put away their weapons, despite the precarious situation, in an attempt to gain compliance with the subject.

Officer Russo continued speaking to the subject while Officer Carter-Ballier drew his taser. The subject threatened to take his life and tried to hide in a closet that was partially open. He continued to disobey commands and began stabbing himself in the stomach. At the appropriate time, Officer Carter-Ballier deployed his taser, causing the subject to fall backwards away from the object.

Officers Russo and Carter-Ballier were able to make entry into the room, secure the lawn stake, and take the subject into custody after a struggle. Their apprehended the subject without major injury and potentially saved the victim’s life.

Police Officers Sara Palagonia, Nicholas Zanfardino, and Jonathan Pesce

105th Precinct

New York Police Department

On Wednesday, March 25, 2026, Officers Palagonia, Zanfardino and Pesce were conducting daily patrols in the 105th. They responded to a 9-1-1 call of an assault with a knife. Upon arrival, the officers discovered the victim inside, bleeding heavily from multiple stab wounds all over his body. Officer Pesce immediately assessed the victim’s condition and rendered first aid by applying direct pressure to the wounds and applying a chest seal. He monitored the victim’s responsiveness until EMS arrived. Due to the officer’s quick actions and effective control of the bleeding, the victim was stabilized enough for transport, which was instrumental in saving his life.

Officers Palagonia and Zanfardino did a thorough canvas and were able to successfully apprehend a male suspect at the corner of 115th Road and 229th Street. The suspect was in possession of a large kitchen knife with blood on the blade. The perpetrator was identified and arrested.

Officers Palagonia, Zanfardino and Pesce are being recognized for their quick response, teamwork, and actions that contributed both to saving the victim’s life and apprehending the individual responsible.

Police Officer Liang Lin

109th Precinct

New York Police Department

On April 11, 2026 at approximately 5:30 pm, NYPD responded to a report of a woman threatening to jump off of a building. Upon arrival, Officer Lin went up to the roof of the building. The woman was on the ledge. Without hesitation, Officer Lin took swift and decisive action, safely pulling her off the ledge. He then secured the woman and made sure she was placed in custody so she could get the care she needed.

Officer Lin is being recognized for his decisive action, saving a life and preventing a potential tragedy.

Detective Stephanie Tringali

111th Precinct

New York Police Department

Detective Stephanie Tringali is being honored today for 20 years of dedicated service in the New York Police Department. Being in law enforcement is no ordinary career: it requires thousands of shifts, countless sacrifices, missed birthdays, birthdays, endless paperwork, and an unwavering commitment to keeping the peace.

Detective Tringali started her career in the 115th Precinct. After about a year, she was assigned to the 111th Precinct, and for the past 15 years, has proudly worked in the Domestic Violence Unit, a position that not many could handle.

Domestic violence investigations are some of the most complex, emotionally exhausting, and critical calls handled by a police department. It takes a unique kind of person to step into the center of someone else's darkest moments day after day. Officers in the Domestic Violence Unit don't just see the aftermath of a crime; they see people at the absolute lowest, most vulnerable moments of their lives. It takes a heavy toll for everyone involved. It requires a rare combination of an iron stomach and a massive heart.

For the last decade and a half, Detective Tringali has been the voice for those who felt silenced. She has developed strong cases, brought offenders to justice and literally saved lives. Detective Tringali has been the shield for people who didn't think anyone was left to fight for them. She has guided survivors from fear to a place of safety, dignity, and hope. She is an irreplaceable asset to the 111th Precinct.

Detective Vasilios “Billy” Rabie

Brookville Police Department

On March 14, while on routine patrol, Detective Vasilios Rabie observed a white 2023 Dodge Charger traveling northbound on Route 107 at a speed well above the posted limit and operating in an unsafe manner. After initiating a traffic stop, Detective Rabie encountered the driver, who was unable to produce a valid driver’s license.

During the course of the investigation, the officer observed what appeared to be a black Glock-style handgun inside the vehicle’s glove compartment. The car’s operator was immiediately directed away from the weapon and safely detained. The firearm was later determined to be an imitation BB pistol designed to closesly resemble a real handgun.

Continuing the investigation and subsequent inventory search of the vehicle, the officer recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .38 Special revolver along with additional ammunition concealed inside.

Through careful observation, sound judgement and adherence to officer safety tactics, this incident was resolved without injury and resulted in the recovery of an illegally possessed loaded firearm. Detective Rabie and the Brookville Police Department are being recognized for the detective’s professionalism, vigilance and commitment to public safety.

Sergeant Peter Michaleas

Glen Cove Police Department

On June 24, 2026, police responded to a 9-1-1 call from two 12-year-old boys reporting that their friend had severely cut his arm on a glass door. Sergeant Peter Michaleas was the first officer to arrive and immediately took command of a tense scene.

While playing, the child had accidently thrust his arm through a glass windowpane, severing a major artery. Recognizing the severe blood loss and impending shock, Sgt. Michaeleas maintained complete composure, reassuring the terrified youth that help was here and their friend would be okay. Taking decisive, life-saving actions, Stg. Michaleas applied a tourniquet to halt the arterial bleeding and stabilized the child. He then coordinated aviation support to medevac the boy to the nearest trauma center for emergency treatment.

Sgt. Michaleas’ leadership, calm demeanor under pressure, and immediate medical intervention directly saved the life of a child.

title: Congressional 4-H Caucus Leaders Introduce National 4-H Week Resolution
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.), Angie Craig (D-Minn.), Andy Harris (R-Md.), and Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (D-Ga.), co-chairs of the bipartisan 4-H Caucus, introduced a resolution today to designate the week of October 4 through October 10 as "National 4-H Week.”

As the youth development program of the Cooperative Extension System of Land-Grant Universities, 4-H engages young people in hands-on projects in the critical areas of agriculture, health, science, and civic leadership. 4-H is the largest youth development organization in the country, with six million current members and 35 million alumni.

“The work ethic and curiosity of each 4-H member I’ve met over the years is one of the reasons I feel so confident in the future of our country's agriculture industry. I am proud to introduce this bipartisan resolution to recognize the important work of 4-H members across the country, and encourage others to get involved as well,” Rep. Thompson said.

“The work that 4-H does to develop our youth into the next generation of leaders in agriculture and beyond is more important than ever. American agriculture has come under great pressure, and fostering a love of agriculture in young people is crucial for America’s future. I am proud to celebrate 4-H today and stand with them as they work to empower America’s youth,” Rep. Craig said.

“4-H gives young people in Maryland and across our nation the chance to experience agriculture firsthand. Representing farming communities across Maryland’s First District, I understand the hard work that farming requires and why it matters for young people to learn about agriculture and the work behind it. I’m proud to recognize National 4-H Week and the millions of young Americans who participate in 4-H,” Rep. Harris said.

“Georgia is proud to be an early home for 4‑H, starting in 1904, with programs reaching every county in our state and preparing young people to lead in agriculture, science, and civic life. I’ve had the pleasure to meet with National 4‑H Council President & CEO Jill Bramble to discuss how 4‑H continues to strengthen youth leadership nationwide. As an Eagle Scout, I know how essential positive role models and supportive environments are for young people, and 4‑H delivers that every day. As Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Appropriations Subcommittee, I remain committed to investing in programs that uplift rural communities and build a stronger future for Georgia and our nation,” Rep. Bishop said.

“We are grateful for the bipartisan support of the Congressional 4-H Caucus and its recognition of the millions of young people who are building the skills and confidence to be ready for work and life. For nearly 125 years, 4-H and Cooperative Extension have helped young people discover what they’re capable of, explore career skills and opportunities, and become Beyond Ready for what comes next,” National 4-H Council President and CEO Jill Bramble said.

Read the full resolution here.

title: Rep. Norma Torres Secures $25 Million For State Route -71 Gap Closure Project in Pomona
text:
Torres previously urged the Department of Transportation to support the project, which will reduce congestion, improve safety, and strengthen a critical freight corridor

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35), a member of the Appropriations Subcommittee that oversees all federal transportation funding, announced that the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro) will receive $25 million in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for Phase 2 of the State Route 71 (SR-71) Gap Closure Project in Pomona.

The funding, awarded through the DOT’s Fiscal Year 2026 Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highway Projects (INFRA) Grant Program, will help upgrade the existing four-lane expressway between Interstate 10 (I-10) and Mission Boulevard into an eight-lane freeway. The project will add one high-occupancy vehicle lane and one mixed-flow lane in each direction, construct auxiliary lanes, replace aging railroad bridges, install soundwalls, and construct an ADA-compliant pedestrian overcrossing at 9th Street.

Congresswoman Torres previously wrote to U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in support of LA Metro’s application, emphasizing the project’s importance to commuters, public safety, the regional economy, and the movement of goods throughout Southern California.

“Anyone who drives the 71 knows how badly these improvements are needed,” said Congresswoman Torres. “I urged the Department of Transportation to support this project because families in Pomona and across the Inland Empire deserve safer roads, shorter commutes, and infrastructure that can keep up with our growing region. This $25 million investment will help eliminate a major bottleneck, improve the movement of goods, and strengthen a corridor that our communities and economy depend on every day. I am thrilled to see federal dollars coming home to move this critical project forward.”

“Metro is pleased to be receiving a $25 million INFRA grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the State Route 71 Gap Closure Project,” said Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins. “We are grateful for the remarkably strong support for this project from Congresswoman Norma Torres, a senior member of the House Committee on Appropriations, Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development. This Measure M voter-approved project will significantly reduce congestion and travel times, improve safety and connectivity – all while enhancing the movements of goods and people across our region. I welcome this infusion of federal funding that will help complete this project and express my appreciation to the local, state, and federal stakeholders whose collaboration are making this project a reality.”

The SR-71 corridor connects communities across Los Angeles, San Bernardino, and Riverside counties and serves as an important route for commuters and freight movement. Phase 2 will address approximately two miles between I-10 and Mission Boulevard and help create consistent improvements along SR-71 from SR-91 to I-10.

The INFRA program provides competitive federal funding for highway and freight projects of national and regional significance that improve the safety, efficiency, and reliability of moving people and goods.

title: Reps. Carter, Matsui Introduce the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act for Suicide Prevention Month
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In honor of Suicide Prevention Month, Congressman Troy A. Carter Sr. (D-LA) and Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA) introduced the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act. This legislation builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.

“America is not only experiencing a mental health crisis – but a severe mental health workforce shortage,” said Congressman Carter. “Every year, millions of Americans rely on the 988 Crisis Line to connect them to care, to specialists, and to hope. But without a properly trained and substantial workforce, individuals with mental health needs aren’t getting the care they deserve. This commonsense legislation will ensure that our behavioral health professionals have the support and resources necessary to continue providing care to those who need it.”

“When someone calls 988, they are often reaching out on one of the hardest days of their life. We need to make sure there is a trained professional ready to answer that call and help them through what comes next,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “I’m proud to partner with Congressman Carter on this impactful legislative effort to build the behavioral health workforce communities need and turn 988 from a number people can call into a system that can truly respond when someone is in crisis.”

Background

Nationwide, 137 million Americans live in a Mental Health Professional Service Area, and many states specifically report they have a shortage of crisis care providers. Without dedicated recruitment and retention programs, we will continue to fall short of the workforce needs for a robust crisis care continuum.

The 988 Crisis Response Workforce Act builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA) and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.

Specifically, this bill:

Directs the Secretary to collect data on the availability and shortage of crisis response professionals and facilities.

Creates a $10 million pilot program to train professionals who provide crisis management services, including those delivered at crisis call centers, as part of a mobile crisis response team, or through a crisis receiving and stabilization program, as part of the Minority Fellowship Program,

Authorizes $10 million to add crisis workforce training programs as part of the Behavioral Health Workforce Education and Training program.

The 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act was included in a larger 988 package – the 988 Implementation Act, which was introduced earlier this month. The 988 Implementation Act is cosponsored by Congressmembers Doris Matsui (CA-07), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Troy Carter (LA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Don Beyer (VA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Becca Balint (VT-AL), and Kim Schrier (WA-08). The comprehensive legislative package will provide states with federal resources to build the crisis response infrastructure behind the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

title: Congressman Van Drew Secures $500,000 for HERO Campaign Expansion
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Van Drew announced that he secured $500,000 in federal funding for the John R. Elliott HERO Campaign to expand its Police Patrol Car program beyond New Jersey. The funding, provided through the U.S. Department of Justice, will help the HERO Campaign wrap police vehicles across the country with its signature designated driver message: Be a HERO. Be a Designated Driver.® The grant is expected to support approximately 125 additional police cruisers.

The HERO Campaign was founded in memory of Navy Ensign John Elliott of Egg Harbor Township, who was killed by a drunk driver in 2000 shortly after graduating from the U.S. Naval Academy. Since then, the campaign has worked with law enforcement, schools, colleges, businesses, and highway safety agencies to promote the use of safe and sober designated drivers.

"The Elliott family has done incredible work for a very long time, and this funding will help them take that work even further," said Congressman Van Drew. "Every one of these police cars is another reminder to people not get behind the wheel after drinking. If that reminder stops even one person from making that decision, that is a life potentially saved. I am very proud we were able to secure this funding for them."

title: Van Duyne Introduces H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act Raising Penalties for Abuse in the H-1B Visa Program
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Beth Van Duyne (R-TX-24) introduced H.R. 10643, the H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act, to increase penalties for willful H-1B violations, extend minimum sponsorship bans, and strengthen fines for immigration document fraud.

“When a business can lie to the government and push American workers aside for cheaper labor, and the worst it faces is a $5,000 fine, many view that as the cost of doing business,” said Rep. Van Duyne. “The H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act changes the penalties. American jobs should go to American workers, and fraudsters should face real accountability for their actions.”

Earlier this year, Rep. Van Duyne led a request with fellow North Texas Members of Congress, Reps. Pat Fallon (R-TX-04), Ronny Jackson (R-TX-13), and Brandon Gill (R-TX-26) to Vice President Vance, Secretary Rubio, then Acting-Secretary Sonderling, and Secretary Mullin urging the Trump Administration to investigate H-1B fraud in North Texas.

As Vice President Vance recently said, Congress needs to act to fix the H-1B visa program. The H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act does that by raising penalties so violators face real consequences.

Since the request, Rep. Van Duyne has met with administration officials on what can be done:

Received confirmation from Secretary Mullin that as of June 2026 nearly 60% of H-1B fraud investigations of employers nationwide are concentrated in the North Texas region.

In August, Labor Department Inspector General D’Esposito visited North Texas and found nearly 500 instances of likely H-1B visa fraud in one building alone. At the addresses he visited where an H-1B application had been approved, no one answered the door.

“I’m thankful for the Administration’s quick response,” said Rep. Van Duyne. “American workers should not lose opportunities because an employer is willing to break the law to get cheaper labor. If a business decides it makes more economic sense to break the law and kick American workers to the curb, they should feel major pain for undercutting our economy and our hardworking employees.”

Summary and Key Provisions:

The H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act increases civil penalties for willful, serious H-1B violations, extends minimum sponsorship bans, and strengthens monetary fines for immigration document fraud. The bill gives federal enforcement agencies stronger tools to hold violators accountable, with the highest H-1B penalties reserved for violations involving displacement of U.S. workers.

Higher penalties for “willful violations”

Raises the maximum civil penalty from $5,000 to $100,000 for covered willful H-1B violations, such as lying about the job being performed or underpaying a worker.

Stronger consequences for worker displacement

Raises the maximum civil penalty from $35,000 to $250,000 for violations involving the willful displacement of U.S. workers.

Longer sponsorship bans

Increases the minimum ban of H-1B sponsorship from two to five years for a serious, willful violation, and from three to ten years for violations additionally involving worker displacement.

Tougher immigration document fraud provisions

Raises civil penalties to a minimum of $1000 and a maximum of $10,000 per document, and from a minimum of $20,000 to a maximum of $50,000 per document for violations after a prior order. These penalties apply to covered immigration document fraud, including H-1B cases.

The H-1B Visa Fraud Crackdown Act is co-sponsored by: U.S. Representatives Brian Babin (R-TX-36), Pat Fallon (R-TX-04), Brandon Gill (R-TX-26), Keith Self (R-TX-03), and Pete Sessions (R-TX-17).

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Sends Letter to FAA Demanding Reversal of Decommissioning of Critical Air Safety Technology
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) partnered with Rep. Stansbury and Rep. Leger Fernández to urge the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to not decommission critical air safety technology used by the Double Eagle Airport II (DEII) in Albuquerque. The FAA recently initiated a study to decommission the Instrument Landing System (ILS) at the Double Eagle Airport without providing answers regarding the recent airspace closure and plane crash incidents in and around New Mexico airspace. Pilots in New Mexico use both ILS and GPS to land due to the unique challenges posed by flying commercial aircraft near military bases.

“We respectfully urge the FAA to maintain use of this critical technology given the unique demands of New Mexico that require aviation redundancy to maintain public safety and to provide our office with a briefing on airspace safety,” wrote the members. “In light of this change, the recent crash outside Ruidoso and other recent aviation incidents involving navigation technology issues, more information is needed before moving forward.”

The FAA recently began a study to determine whether ILS technology should be decommissioned at the DEII, which conducts tens of thousands of flights annually. ILS is a ground based guidance system for aircrafts typically used when pilots are unable to find the runway. It complements modern GPS-enabled navigation that only provides lateral guidance to the runway. While GPS-enabled navigation works in most conditions, New Mexico has its own set of unique airspace challenges due to nearby military bases that force a need for both ILS and GPS.

“The FAA has still not provided sufficient answers regarding the recent airspace closure in El Paso and plane crash in Ruidoso – and has still not shown that it is improving coordination with other agencies or ensuring that my constituents’ are safe,” said Vasquez. “In light of their recent failures, the public must have a lot more information before the FAA orders decommissioning any navigation safety tools or resources for our pilots.”

“DEII plays a critical role in our region’s aviation system as a reliever airport for the Sunport and an important facility for flight training and public safety operations. Maintaining ILS capability is essential to ensuring the airport can continue to serve these functions safely and effectively, particularly when reliable navigation is needed most,” said Manny Manriquez, Director of Aviation, City of Albuquerque.

Read the full letter HERE.

Rep. Vasquez continues to lead Congressional oversight efforts following multiple aviation incidents affecting southern New Mexico, including:

Demanding answers from the Department of Defense and Department of Transportation on their coordination with each other to keep our skies safe.

Securing an NTSB briefing on July 14 after demanding greater transparency and answers about the deadly Ruidoso plane crash.

Pressing the FAA and Department of Defense for accountability following the February closure of El Paso airspace.

Successfully secured passage of an amendment to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act requiring the Department of Defense to improve coordination with the FAA before testing military technologies that could impact civilian aviation.

title: Vindman, Subramanyam, Warren Warn Utility Merger May Increase Prices, Urge Federal Regulator to Scrutinize Deal
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (D-Va.-07) joined Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.-10) and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) in a letter warning the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) about the potential consequences of the proposed merger between NextEra Energy, Inc. (“NextEra”) and Dominion Energy (“Dominion”), and urged the regulator to closely examine the deal and block it if it would increase consumers’ energy costs or otherwise fail to meet public interest requirements.

On May 18, 2026, NextEra announced a $66.8 billion deal to merge with Dominion. The proposed deal would eliminate a competitor in the energy generation market and create the largest regulated electric utility in the world. It would be the fourth largest merger of all time and would create a company worth $420 billion.

A NextEra-Dominion entity would serve about 10 million homes and businesses across Virginia, Florida, North Carolina, and South Carolina, but the effects of the merger — including higher electricity rates — could extend even further. Residential electricity prices have risen 15 percent since January 2025, and families are projected to spend an average of $110 more on electricity bills in 2026 than they did last year.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

“The merger would give the combined company control over approximately a quarter of the electricity in the New England region, leading to considerable negotiating leverage over states and the ability to demand abusive terms at the expense of households,” wrote the lawmakers. “This megamerger may consolidate competitive power markets and raise electricity rates even more for American families.”

Under the Federal Power Act, FERC shall approve a merger of public utilities only if the applicants demonstrate that the merger is in the public interest and does not pose a risk of harmful cross-subsidization, and may block a merger that is not “consistent with the public interest.”

“Our fundamental concern is that this new entity will be both a gigantic power generator and a gigantic power-providing utility,” wrote the lawmakers. “We urge you to closely scrutinize this merger and block it if the Commission determines it would increase market concentration or have an adverse effect on costs for consumers—or if the acquisition is otherwise not in the public interest.”

The lawmakers are concerned that a NextEra-Dominion merger would create an even larger vertically integrated electricity utility and electricity generator that will squash competition and raise prices. Previous utility mergers have coincided with increases in household electricity costs. Additionally, a merger increasing the market share of already vertically integrated utility companies could make it even easier for the combined entity to engage in improper “cross-subsidization,” a practice by which corporations unfairly shift onto consumers the cost of transactions between utility companies and affiliate companies, which researchers say forces households to pay higher electricity rates.

“The consequences of failing to address utility merger harms, including by imposing insufficient mitigation measures, are not theoretical: when FERC allows utility companies to gain enough power to stamp out competition in an entire region, higher prices have followed,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers also warned that large utility companies that are intertwined with generating entities have strong incentives to oppose building transmission connections to bring in cheaper power from other regions, a problem that could get worse with the creation of a giant like NextEra-Dominion. New England states have accused NextEra of using its existing power to obstruct new transmission infrastructure projects.

“We therefore urge FERC to closely examine whether this deal may decrease competition or cause electricity rates for households to climb even higher; to remain skeptical of mitigation conditions that have historically failed to blunt the negative impacts of large utility merges; and to deny the application unless the applicants demonstrate that the transaction will have no adverse effect, now or in the future, on competition, rates, or regulation and will not result in impermissible cross-subsidization or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets,” concluded the lawmakers. “If the present record is insufficient to make those findings, the Commission should deny the application.”

Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Representatives Chris Deluzio (Pa.-17), Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-2), Raja Krishnamoorthi (Ill.-08), and Seth Magaziner (R.I.-02) also signed the letter.

BACKGROUND

In August, Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) was the first member of the Virginia delegation to speak out against the proposed merger. He sent a letter to members of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) urging them to reject the proposed merger between Dominion Energy and NextEra energy. In the letter, Vindman warned that the deal would put Wall Street profits ahead of Virginia families, weaken local accountability, and increase costs for consumers. You can read his letter here.

Later that month, Vindman launched a district-wide survey asking for constituents’ thoughts on the proposed merger. The results were clear: of 950 respondents, the overwhelmingly majority opposed the merger between Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy, underscoring widespread concerns about the deal’s potential impact on Virginia ratepayers.

title: Walkinshaw, Morelle and Virginia Democrats Fight Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting, Pledge to Protect Every Vote
text:
FAIRFAX, VA — Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25) and members of Virginia’s Democratic congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation, and misinformation.

The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.

In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.

“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”

"In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”

"Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote," said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. "Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone's right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight."

“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”

“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”

“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.

The experts urged voters to check their registration, make a plan to vote and consult trusted election officials.

title: Wasserman Schultz Introduces Bipartisan Agriculture Relief Bill to Provide Florida Farm, Citrus Support
text:
Washington, D.C.— Today, U.S. Reps. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Scott Franklin (FL-18), Darren Soto (FL-09) and Kat Cammack (FL-03) introduced the Restore Agricultural Investment, Stability and Expansion (RAISE) Act of 2026, to provide the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) with the standing authority to help American farmers and growers recover after natural disasters by issuing block grants.

“Congress needs to have the back of America’s farmers, and I’m proud to work across the aisle to make sure the crops and agricultural resources that fuel American families are protected from increasingly extreme weather threats, something our own citrus industry faces in Florida,” said Wasserman Schultz. “From timber to food on our tabletops, we need every tool at hand to help farmers recover from natural disasters.”

“The devastating freeze Florida farmers faced this past February was another reminder of how quickly a natural disaster can threaten years of hard work,” said Franklin. “Our growers face hurricanes, freezes, droughts, floods and other disasters, and they need a reliable way to recover when disaster strikes. This bill gives USDA permanent authority to provide flexible block grants for high-value and specialty crop losses so assistance can reach producers faster. I’m pleased we secured this provision in the House-passed Farm Bill and will continue working with Congresswoman Wasserman Schultz to get it across the finish line.”

“Glad to join Reps. Franklin, Wasserman Schultz, and Soto on this effort to support our Florida producers,” said Cammack. “When extreme weather threatens our crops, as is often the case in the Sunshine State, we must be prepared to help our farmers recover and continue the important work of feeding our nation.”

“In Central Florida, our farmers, ranchers, and growers have struggled after devastating hurricanes,” said Soto. “As these natural disasters get stronger, we must work to ensure that they have the resources to recover, maintain their livelihoods, and keep feeding America.”

“Florida's citrus industry knows firsthand the devastating impacts of freezes, hurricanes and other disasters on crops. In times of disaster, America's growers and farmers need timely support to recover and replant,” said Matt Joyner, EVP and CEO of Florida Citrus Mutual. “Florida's citrus growers are grateful to our state’s Congressional members, including Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Kat Cammack, Darren Soto and Scott Franklin, for their leadership and commitment to advancing the RAISE Act. The legislation seeks to give the United States Department of Agriculture tools to quickly deliver block grant assistance in the wake of disasters, helping Florida citrus and the greater agriculture industry recover and continue producing for America's families.”

More than 90 percent of all Florida citrus production was impacted by hurricanes in 2022, totaling 375,302 acres. The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services expects these devastating losses to cost the industry as much as $675 million. Florida citrus generates $6.8 billion in annual revenue and supports 33,000 jobs.

title: Rep. Whitesides Pushes for a National Film Tax Credit to Bring Production Jobs Back to Santa Clarita and the Antelope Valley
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Rep. George Whitesides (CA-27) announced his cosponsorship of the bipartisan, bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. The bill would create a national film tax credit to bring film and television production, and the crew, trades and small-business jobs that come with it, back to the United States.

“Our region is at the heart of film and television production, and we owe it to the hardworking crews who live in our area to bring American production home,” said Rep. Whitesides. “This bipartisan bill invests in the people, sound stages, movie sets, and scenery we have right here in our backyard, and gives productions an incentive to keep good-paying jobs in Southern California. I’ll keep fighting alongside this bipartisan coalition to make sure our local film economy is able to thrive.”

In 2019, Santa Clarita issued a record 576 film permits for 1,490 days of location filming, generating an estimated $35.9 million for the local economy. In 2025, the city issued 338 permits, generating an estimated $14.6 million, a drop of nearly 60%. Across the region permitted by FilmLA, which includes Palmdale and the unincorporated communities of north Los Angeles County, on-location shoot days fell 16% from 2024 to 2025, and television shooting ran 50% below its five-year average. Nationwide, more than 100,000 production jobs have disappeared since October 2022 as 65 countries now offer incentives to lure American productions overseas.

Under the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act:

Feature films, TV pilots, and TV seasons costing more than $1 million earn a 20% credit on American labor costs if at least 75% of filming takes place in the U.S.

Productions earn bonus credits of 5% each, up to 30% total, for filming in rural opportunity zones or disaster areas, for independent productions, for hiring across 10 or more states, and for bringing work home from overseas.

Post-production and visual effects work done in the U.S. qualifies.

The credit is transferable, so independent producers who don’t owe enough in taxes can sell it for cash up front.

The credit applies to productions beginning in taxable years after December 31, 2026.

The legislation is led in the House by Representatives Laura Friedman (CA-30), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Brian Jack (GA-03), David Kustoff (TN-08), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mike Carey (OH-15) and Tom Suozzi (NY-03), and in the Senate by Senators Tim Scott (SC) and Adam Schiff (CA). It is endorsed by the American Federation of Musicians, ASCAP, Coalition for American Production, CreativeFuture, Directors Guild of America, FilmUSA, Independent Film and Television Alliance, IATSE, Motion Picture Association, Paramount, Producers Guild of America, SAG-AFTRA, Teamsters, Television Academy, Writers Guild of America East, and Writers Guild of America West.

title: Womack Hosts Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in Arkansas’s Third District
text:
ARKANSAS—October 5, 2026…Today, House Appropriations Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (THUD), and Related Agencies Subcommittee Chairman Steve Womack (AR-3) welcomed U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy to Arkansas’s Third Congressional District. During the visit, Chairman Womack highlighted to Secretary Duffy how federal investments are helping the region respond to rapid growth by supporting the construction of critical transportation infrastructure.

Chairman Womack said, “Strong transportation infrastructure keeps our communities moving and our economy growing. From getting people to work and school, to connecting or communities by air, to moving freight and goods, we need infrastructure that can keep pace with our current and future demand—both regionally and nationally. The federal government is an important partner in making that happen. I’m glad Secretary Duffy is here in Arkansas’s Third District to see firsthand how federal investment is helping to move forward critical infrastructure projects that will not only contribute to our region’s continued prosperity but to that of the nation.”

Secretary Duffy said, “Arkansas is fortunate to have a Representative like Steve Womack in Washington advocating on their behalf to get big, beautiful infrastructure projects like I-49 and the XNA expansion done. His role as Chairman of the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Subcommittee has helped secure crucial dollars for AR-3. During the President’s second term, USDOT has awarded over $71 million to Arkansas’s Third District. Representative Womack played a crucial role in delivering those dollars to the Natural State.”

Chairman Womack’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 THUD appropriations bill provides a total discretionary allocation of $28.29 billion to the Department of Transportation (USDOT), which is $1.177 billion above the FY 2026 enacted level. The bill invests in modernizing our national airspace system and strengthening infrastructure, including roads, bridges, railways, and maritime facilities across the country.

Read more bill highlights HERE.

Visit Highlights

Chairman Womack and Secretary Duffy started the day by viewing the ongoing construction of Phase 1 of the 14‑mile Alma‑to‑Barling segment of I‑49. This phase includes the Arkansas River Bridge Crossing—the project’s most critical component. Once completed, this section of I-49 will deliver much‑needed congestion relief for Fort Smith and Van Buren and will spur economic development along the connector, attracting businesses, creating jobs, and strengthening regional commerce.

On a national level, the completed project will also mark significant progress toward closing the 155‑mile I‑49 gap between Alma and Texarkana. Closing this gap will create a continuous north–south interstate connection from Canada to Louisiana, supporting supply‑chain efficiency and reliability.

Chairman Womack has secured $21 million for the project’s construction through the appropriations process, including $18 million in FY 2022 and $3 million in FY 2026. With Chairman Womack’s support, the Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT) received a $25 million USDOT RAISE grant in 2024 for the project.

title: NEWS: Baldwin Blasts Trump Admin for Slashing $11 Million in Rural Housing Funding for Wisconsin
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) is calling out the Trump Administration for slashing $11 million in federal funding that helps low-income families in rural Wisconsin afford to buy a home. This year, despite the Trump Administration having the resources to fully fund the program across the country, Wisconsin received roughly $2 million through the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans program, compared to an average of $13.1 million in previous years – a decrease of more than $11 million. Democrats and Republicans in Congress passed a law to provide $1 billion for the program, but President Trump’s USDA refused to allocate nearly half of it.

“Wisconsin families are working harder than ever, but too many folks feel stuck or are falling behind with the rising costs of just about everything. The price of housing is crushing families and is putting the dream of homeownership further and further out of reach,” said Senator Baldwin. “And for folks in our rural areas – which is about 1 in 4 Wisconsinites – this pinch can drive them out of the places they love and out of Wisconsin’s iconic agriculture economy. Instead of helping these folks afford the roof over their heads, the Trump Administration is making matters worse by slashing resources that help working families in our rural communities afford a home. The Trump administration has the money, but they are making an active choice not to use it and not to invest in rural America. I’m fighting to bring housing costs down and make sure every Wisconsinite, no matter where they live, has every opportunity to live a good life and own a home.”

The USDA’s Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans program helps low-income families in rural communities get the financing they need to afford a home. The drastic drop in funding for Wisconsin comes as the Trump Administration failed to spend nearly half of the $1 billion Congress provided for the program nationwide. While $250 million of the nearly half billion in unspent funds can be used in the next fiscal year, the Administration allowed more than $230 million in funding to expire, resources that could have helped approximately 850 more rural families across the country afford to buy a home.

Senator Baldwin has long worked to lower housing costs and expand access to affordable homeownership for Wisconsin families. Earlier this year, the Baldwin-backed 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a bipartisan bill to build more affordable housing and bring down housing costs, became the law of the land.

title: Blumenthal Statement on Release of Annual Veteran Suicide Report
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) today issued a statement following the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) release of its National Veterans Suicide Prevention annual report, revealing a slight decrease in the rate of veteran suicide from 2023 to 2024.

“The high rate of veteran suicide remains distressing. We need to allocate every resource we can to reduce this grim number. That starts with safeguarding resources for the Veterans Crisis Line, hiring more mental health professionals at VA, and ensuring every single veteran seeking mental health care gets that care in a timely manner. I’ll continue working to bolster the suicide prevention and mental health care programs veterans need and fight the Trump Administration’s efforts to cut mental health care positions amid the hemorrhaging of providers at the Department.”

VA’s report shows 6,488 veterans died by suicide in 2024. Additionally, 62% of veterans who died by suicide in 2024 had no contact with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) and were not receiving VA benefits. This data highlights the importance of both strengthening VA’s direct care system and expanding outreach and suicide prevention efforts for veterans who are not engaged in VHA health care. The report also details that firearms were involved in approximately 74% of veterans suicides, up 68% since 2001. This is the area with the least progress after 20 years.

Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, VA Secretary Collins has eliminated thousands of mental health care clinical positions instead of bolstering them. From January 2025 to June 2026, VA cut 600 psychologist and 1,600 social worker positions, barring medical centers from being able to recruit for those roles. In January, Blumenthal’s released a comprehensive report, Breaking the Pact: Impacts of Trump, DOGE, and Doug Collins’ Ongoing Assault on Veterans, detailing the harm and impacts of the Trump Administration’s draconian directives and cuts on veterans. Among its many findings, the report revealed a historic loss of staff, dire health care staffing shortages, and spiking VA mental health care wait times.

Blumenthal has been a stanch fighter to improve and expand veterans’ mental health care. In 2025, he introduced the BRAVE Act—comprehensive legislation to strengthen VA’s mental health workforce, infrastructure, and services, including renewing the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program. This first-of-its-kind grant provides funding for local organizations combatting veteran suicide. Blumenthal also successfully attached an amendment to protect the life-saving Veterans Crisis Line from future cuts by the Trump Administration in the Fiscal Year 2026 federal funding bill.

title: Blumenthal & Fischer Bipartisan Resolution to Promote Road Safety & Reduce Roadside Deaths Passes Senate
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – The bipartisan National Move Over Law Day Resolution led by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Deb Fischer (R-NE) passed the U.S. Senate last week.

The resolution highlights Slow Down, Move Over laws across the country in an effort to reduce struck-by-vehicle injuries and fatalities. The resolution also recognizes and honors the important role fire and rescue personnel, emergency medical services personnel, law enforcement officers, tow truck operators, and transportation workers play in road safety.

“Slow Down, Move Over saves lives. It’s the law in every state, but it needs to be amplified and elevated. Every year, failures to Slow Down and Move Over cause needless, senseless injuries and deaths to roadside workers like police, firefighters, emergency responders, tow truck operators, construction workers, and more. This resolution aims to make them safer by reminding drivers to slow down and move over,” said Blumenthal.

“From emergency personnel to roadside crews, countless individuals work every day to keep our roads safe. Slowing down and moving over a lane is a simple way we can help protect them. I’m proud to support this resolution and grateful for all who keep us safe,” said Fischer.

Blumenthal honored Elvin Hernandez, a Connecticut Department of Transportation worker struck and killed while working in Fairfield in September, and Alexander John Ramos, a tow truck driver who was struck and killed responding to a disabled vehicle in Bloomfield in September.

Today, all 50 states have Slow Down, Move Over laws that direct motorists to reduce speed or change lanes for stopped emergency and maintenance vehicles. Still, many drivers are unaware of these laws, and they vary state-by-state, leading to continued roadside fatalities and injuries across the country.

The resolution was endorsed by Flagman, National Safety Council, AAA National, American Driver and Traffic Safety Education Association, National District Attorneys Association, CTDOT, National Association of State EMS Officials, Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance, Governors Highway Safety Association, the International Association of Fire Chiefs, AFSCME, American Association of State Troopers, and the National Association of Police Organizations.

The text of the resolution is available here.

title: Blumenthal, Boozman Introduce Bill to Improve Support for Veterans Crisis Line Employees
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee, and U.S. Senator John Boozman (R-AR) recently introduced the Veterans Crisis Line Support and Safety Act—bipartisan legislation that would improve mental health support and workplace conditions for Veterans Crisis Line (VCL) employees, many of whom are veterans themselves.

“Veterans Crisis Line employees do lifesaving work every day in the most difficult circumstances. Unfortunately, these workers often face emotionally challenging situations. Our bipartisan bill will provide these employees much-needed mental health services and increased workplace protections to ensure they are given the support and space they need to serve veterans,” said Blumenthal.

“The men and women providing instant and critical mental health support to veterans during some of their most difficult moments are an invaluable, life-saving resource. Many VCL employees are veterans themselves and understand the challenges those they serve are facing. I am proud this bipartisan legislation would ensure they have access to key tools and protections for their wellbeing ensuring assistance for veterans in crisis is not delayed or denied,” said Boozman.

The VCL provides a life-saving service for responding to veterans in crisis and is an important tool for preventing veteran suicide—offering 24/7 confidential assistance through call, text, or chat support. The Senators’ legislation was drafted with input from VCL employees who provided testimony about being harassed in their jobs and needing additional workplace protections given the sensitive and emotional hardships of their work. Full impact statements from VCL responders can be found HERE, HERE, and HERE.

“…[T]his work comes with a serious emotional and mental cost. In addition to supporting people experiencing suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, and other crises, I have endured racist comments, sexual harassment, hateful language, and threats from both civilian and Veteran callers…Being on the receiving end of this abuse is disturbing, degrading, and emotionally exhausting,” said Shonta Thomas, Vice President for AFGE Local 518, who is 10-year U.S. Navy veteran and VCL responder. “The cumulative impact of these interactions has contributed to mental burnout. It is difficult to absorb racist abuse, sexual harassment, or threats and then move into another crisis conversation that requires patience, compassion, and focused attention. The previous interaction does not simply disappear when the call ends. There is an emotional weight that comes with repeatedly being targeted while also carrying the responsibility of helping someone through a crisis.”

“I have dedicated years of service to the Veterans and Military Crisis Line and remain committed to supporting Veterans who reach out during moments of crisis. At the same time, supporting Veterans should not require frontline responders to absorb repeated abusive behavior without adequate protection, communication, training, or organizational support,” said a service-connected veteran who works as Veterans and Military Crisis Line responder. “Clear communication, appropriate training, consistent procedures, and meaningful protections for responders are essential to maintaining a safe and effective Crisis Line for both Veterans and the employees who serve them.”

“Responders are often expected to provide callers with the very things they may desperately need in their most vulnerable moments—respect, safety, emotional support, compassion, care, and reassurance. I believe responders deserve those same things in the workplace,” said another VCL responder. “I remain committed to the VCL mission and to serving Veterans. That commitment is precisely why I believe this conversation is necessary. Protecting responders is not a departure from the mission—it is an investment in the people who carry it out every day. If we want responders to continue providing compassionate, effective, and consistent care, we must create an environment in which they are also afforded compassion, protection, support, and care.”

Among its many provisions, the Veterans Crisis Line Support and Safety Act would:

Offer VCL employees free, confidential counseling and mental health care from licensed providers experienced in PTSD, trauma, and compassion fatigue;

Establish peer support programs, critical incident stress debriefing, and annual resiliency/burnout-prevention training;

Provide critical mental health services during and outside of scheduled work hours through VA and outside providers;

Implement reasonable limits on VCL employees’ workload and shift duration;

Require mandatory rest and recovery periods after high-risk or traumatic interactions;

Designate dedicated staff for complex or disruptive cases; and

Ensure staffing levels at the VCL are informed by data on the volume of calls and workforce assessments.

The Veterans Crisis Line Support and Safety Act is endorsed by the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE) National Veterans Affairs Council.
