title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Cortez Masto, Reed, Banking Democrats Request Full Banking Hearing with FHFA Director Bill Pulte
text:
Banking Democrats call for public forum to question Pulte on documented abuses of power

U.S. SenatorsLisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.),Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), andJack Reed (D-R.I.) joined their Democratic colleagues on the Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee in a letter to Chair Tim Scott (R-S.C.) requesting a hearing with Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) Director Bill Pulte. The Senators’ request follows various reported abuses of power by Pulte, including last week’s unprecedented move to cut the funding to the agency’s Office of the Inspector General (FHFA-OIG) by 60 percent and risk future operations.

“We request you invite Director Pulte to testify before the Senate Banking Committee so our committee can fulfill its oversight functions and explore how his decisions are affecting FHFA’s ability to ensure Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the FHLBanks (collectively, “the government-sponsored enterprises,” or GSEs) operate in a safe and sound manner and provide a reliable source of liquidity and funding for housing finance and community investment. The hearing would provide Director Pulte the opportunity to explain his record,” wrote the Senators.

Bill Pulte’s proposed cuts to FHFA-OIG – which is tasked with investigating waste, fraud, and abuse at FHFA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Federal Home Loan Banks – come while he remains under increased scrutiny for his abuses of power. Pulte is under investigation by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) for potentially misusing his federal authority and resources to publicly accuse prominent Democrats and President Donald Trump’s perceived political enemies of mortgage fraud. Pulte also faces questions for his apparent involvement in the President’s scheme to demolish the Kennedy Center and his brief tenure as Acting Director of National Intelligence.

The Senators also call into question his mismanagement of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which back 70 percent of mortgages in the United States: “Since failing to respond to congressional inquiries on his activities, Director Pulte has fired more staff at Fannie Mae, including about a dozen high-ranking executives. These now-fired executives were responsible for multifamily loans, low-income housing tax credit investments, and finance, and also included regulatory and communications officials. Director Pulte has not publicly explained the reasoning behind these most recent terminations and how these firings will impact Fannie Mae’s ability to provide price stability across the mortgage market.”

Pulte’s cuts to the FHFA-OIG would result in a layoff of 70-80% of staff, including experienced law enforcement officers who serve as the primary watchdogs for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and keep the mortgage market stable. These staff are tasked with investigating title and mortgage fraud, protecting mortgage lenders and home buyers from predatory practices, and ensuring a sound and secure mortgage and banking system.

“We must fulfill our oversight responsibilities related to potential harm being done by Director Pulte to our nation’s housing finance market and in turn, to the supply and cost of housing,” conclude the Senators.

title: Booker, Blumenthal, Padilla Urge Secretary Mullin to Immediately Remove ICE Officers Hired Without Background Checks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), and Alex Padilla (D-CA), members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, call on Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin to immediately remove all U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers hired during the Department’s 2025 hiring surge. In a new oversight letter that comes days after new reports of the agency's plans to hire 5,000 new officers before year’s end, the senators demand that DHS complete comprehensive retraining and re-vetting for all current officers.

“Over the past year, ICE and other DHS personnel have fatally shot and killed multiple people during vehicle stops and enforcement operations, including several instances in which agents opened fire on people inside their own cars,” wrote the senators. “These killings, combined with the whistleblower’s account of corners cut on both vetting and training, make clear that officers hired during the surge did not receive adequate instruction in de-escalation, use-of-force standards, and vehicle-stop protocols before being sent into communities with the authority to use deadly force.”

Republicans poured $75 billion into ICE through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and then added $38.5 billion more this summer, allowing ICE to hire thousands of new officers with incentives including a signing bonus of up to $50,000 and up to $60,000 in student-loan repayment. The agencies dropped hiring standards and cut corners on background checks to meet the hiring demand, leading to heightened concerns of unqualified and poorly trained officers conducting immigration arrests. Several incidents of death and violence led to increased congressional oversight. ICE is preparing a second hiring surge of 5,000 employees before year’s end–roughly 17 percent in three months–without having completed background investigations for thousands of hires from the first.

The letter follows reporting from the New York Times detailing a formal whistleblower complaint from 17-year ICE veteran overseeing background investigations. The complaint revealed job offers were extended to candidates without completion of basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks and evaded by political appointees. A former ICE Academy instructor and agency attorney also disclosed that ICE cut training hours on use of force, firearms safety, and the constitutional rights of the public during this same period. According to another New York Times report, 7,500 active officers with arrest authority hired during last year’s surge are still awaiting the full background investigations required for their positions.

On January 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Minneapolis, Minnesota, fatally shot Renée Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, as she attempted to drive away from agents during an enforcement operation.

Less than two weeks later, Border Patrol agents fatally shot Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, during the same wave of Minneapolis enforcement operations.

On July 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Houston, Texas fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old construction worker and father of three, while he was driving a work crew to a job site.

Six days later, on July 13, 2026, an ICE officer in Biddeford, Maine, fatally shot Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old father, in his car after agents rammed his vehicle and fired multiple rounds through it while executing a warrant for someone else. Mr. Durán Guerrero was not the target of the operation and was authorized to work in the United States.

“DHS cannot allow officers whose backgrounds were never properly vetted, and who may never have received adequate use-of-force training, to remain on the streets with arrest authority and firearms,” concluded the senators.

In the letter, the lawmakers urge DHS to:

Immediately suspend field enforcement duties for all ICE officers hired during the 2025 hiring surge, pending completion of full background checks and training.

Provide a full accounting of how many current ICE officers received job offers or field assignments before completing fingerprint, identity, and credit checks, and how many of those officers have discharged a firearm in the course of duty.

Provide ICE’s 2026 hiring plan, including

All documents, memoranda, internal communications, staffing assessments, and analyses of staffing needs.

The vetting and training protocols.

The name and title of each official who approved the plan.

Provide a copy of the whistleblower’s complaint and any Office of Inspector General findings or corrective action plan arising from it.

Provide a detailed accounting of the use-of-force policy and vehicle-stop protocol changes DHS has made since January 2026.

Including how those changes have been implemented and audited across ICE field offices.

title: Boozman, Klobuchar Lead Senate Recognition of National 4-H Week
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry Chairman John Boozman (R-AR) and Ranking Member Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), co-chairs of the Senate 4-H Caucus, applauded Senate passage of a resolution designating October 4-10, 2026 as National 4-H Week.

“4-H has made a lasting impact on countless Arkansans, including my three daughters, who benefited from their participation in this program. I’m proud to support 4-H as it continues developing future generations of leaders and equips young people with the skills and values they need to succeed,” Boozman said.

“Minnesota 4-H is preparing over 50,000 young Minnesotans to lead in their communities,” said Klobuchar. “I’m glad to partner with Senator Boozman to recognize the work of 4-H by celebrating this week as National 4-H Week. As co-chair of the 4-H Caucus, I’ll continue working with my colleagues to support exciting opportunities for youth engaged in agriculture.”

As the country’s largest youth development organization, 4-H operates as part of the Cooperative Extension System across land-grant universities. It reaches nearly six million young individuals through hands-on experiences in agriculture, science, health and civic engagement annually including 130,000 in Arkansas and 50,000 in Minnesota.

title: U.S. Senators Katie Britt, James Lankford, Colleagues Celebrate 50th Anniversary of the Hyde Amendment, Protecting American Taxpayers from Funding Abortions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Katie Britt (R-Ala.), James Lankford (R-Okla.), and several of their Republican colleagues recently introduced a resolution recognizing the Hyde Amendment’s 50th anniversary and its enduring legacy of protecting unborn children and upholding the conscience rights of American taxpayers.

“Fifty years ago, the bipartisan Hyde Amendment affirmed a simple principle: no American should be forced to fund a procedure that takes an innocent life,” said Senator Britt. “Today, when many demand that abortion be paid for by taxpayers, Hyde remains a critical protection for religious freedom and for Americans who do not want their hard-earned dollars subsidizing elective abortions. Proud to join my colleagues in recognizing this anniversary and reaffirming our strong, continued support for Hyde.”

The resolution commemorates 50 years of the Hyde Amendment by recognizing its legacy of saving more than 2.6 million lives while affirming that federal taxpayers should not be compelled to fund abortions in violation of their deeply held religious and moral beliefs.

“For 50 years, the Hyde Amendment has been an important protection for American taxpayers,” said Senator Lankford. “Every child is valuable. No American should ever wonder if the check they’re sending to the IRS on April 15 will be used to pay for someone’s elective abortion. Hyde was a bipartisan agreement five decades ago, and it has been included in appropriations bills every year since. We should keep that commitment in place.”

Joining Senators Britt and Lankford in introducing the resolution are Senators Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), Jim Justice (R-W.V.), Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.), Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Jim Risch (R-Idaho), Josh Hawley (R-Mo.), Rick Scott (R-Fla.), Ted Budd (R-N.C.), Mike Rounds (R-S.D.), Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.), Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.V.), Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Jim Banks (R-Ind.), Deb Fischer (R-Neb.), Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), Mike Lee (R-Utah), John Hoeven (R-N.D.), Darline Graham (R-S.C.), Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), and Dave McCormick (R-Pa.).

The resolution is also supported by CatholicVote, Americans United for Life, National Right to Life Committee, Live Action, March for Life Action, Concerned Women for America, Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America, Students for Life Action, Heritage Action, Alliance Defending Freedom, Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission, Heartbeat International, United States Council of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), and Family Research Council. You can read the full text of the resolution here.

Senator Britt is a proud supporter of the Hyde Amendment. She is a cosponsor of the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act and has worked tirelessly to ensure it remains included in annual appropriations bills. She is also a cosponsor of the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act to ban federal Title X family-planning grants from going to any entity that performs or funds abortions.

title: PHOTOS: Capito Attends Events in Support of First Responders, Veterans, and Youth Fellowship
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – This weekend, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), made stops in Bridgeport and Morgantown to celebrate first responders and veterans in West Virginia. She also made a visit to Summersville for a building dedication.

To begin the day, Senator Capito delivered remarks at the WV Chiefs of Police Association Annual Conference in Bridgeport, W.Va. to celebrate the successes of West Virginia’s police force, which she continuously supports through the Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) process. Additionally, Senator Capito received updates on the association’s recent collaborative efforts and priorities.

“I was excited to join our law enforcement officers and celebrate them for their outstanding service to West Virginia—which I have been proud to support through my work in the U.S. Senate,” Senator Capito said. “I appreciated the opportunity to hear firsthand how the association is promoting communication and professional development across the state through our police departments. Through the CDS process, I’ve worked to strengthen our local police departments, expand our police force, and provide them with the proper resources to keep West Virginian’s safe. I am impressed by association’s efforts to connect West Virginia’s police force, and I’m proud to partner with them to keep that collaboration moving forward.”

“The West Virginia Chiefs of Police Association Fall Conference provides an important opportunity for law enforcement leaders from across our state to come together, strengthen partnerships, and discuss the issues facing our profession and the communities we serve,” Chief Mark Rogers, Bridgeport Police Department, WV COPA Board Member said. We are honored to welcome United States Senator Shelley Moore Capito to this year’s conference. We recognize the tremendous demands on her schedule, and her willingness to spend time with West Virginia’s law enforcement leaders is sincerely appreciated and makes her attendance especially meaningful to our association.”

Next, Senator Capito traveled to Morgantown, W.Va. to attend Operation Activet’s Annual Veterans Bash. While there, she delivered remarks celebrating Operation Activet’s success and met with veterans. Operation Activet plays a vital role in West Virginia, connecting veterans and first responders through community events across the state.

“It was an honor to celebrate our men and women in uniform. Connecting our veterans and first responders through meaningful opportunities is so important. I am proud of the work being done here and deeply appreciative of Operation Activet’s efforts in creating a community for those who have sacrificed so much for our country,” Senator Capito said.

“Operation Activet was founded by my son, C.J., an Army veteran who served in Afghanistan, because he wanted to give back and help his fellow veterans,” Chuck Ghuste, President of Operation Activet, said. “After we lost C.J. in 2019, our family and so many dedicated volunteers committed ourselves to keeping his dream alive. Today, we’re proud to bring veterans and first responders together through activities, camaraderie, and a strong community of support. We’re grateful to Senator Capito for taking the time to visit with us, learn more about our mission and show her support for the veterans and first responders we serve.”

To end the day, Senator Capito traveled to Summersville, W.Va. where she delivered remarks at WV Young Life’s dedication of three new buildings: the Dining Hall, Club Room, and dorms. During the visit, she also toured the facility to view progress.

“WV Young Life’s campus is a remarkable place that reflects the faith, vision, and persistence of so many people who believed in what this property could become,” Senator Capito said. “I’m proud to have played a role in supporting the infrastructure needed to bring this vision to life, and I’m grateful that generations of young West Virginians will now have a place of their own to grow, build relationships, and share God’s love.”

title: Cassidy Discusses Social Security Win with Passage of Claiming Age Clarity Act on Mornings with Fox Business
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) applauded the U.S. Senate’s passage of the bipartisan Claiming Age Clarity Act, legislation he led in the Senate to make Social Security terminology clearer and help Americans make more informed decisions about when to claim benefits. Cassidy also discussed the need to address Social Security’s looming insolvency in six years and outlined his plan to establish a separate investment fund that could cover 60 to 70 percent of the projected shortfall.

“We’ve got to fix Social Security both for the individual receiving it and for the taxpayer who funds it. And one way is to not mislead people,” said Dr. Cassidy.

“The trust fund goes insolvent in six years. When it goes insolvent, by law, the amount going out has to match the amount coming in. When the trust fund goes empty, then the amount going out will fall up to 28.5 percent,” continued Dr. Cassidy.

Background

Cassidy has been outspoken in the media on the need to rescue Social Security from insolvency. He has outlined his plan to create a sovereign wealth fund independent of the Social Security Trust Fund. He has written extensively on his proposal in the Washington Post, the Wall Street Journal, State Affairs, and the Washington Examiner. On the U.S. Senate floor, Cassidy has repeatedly called on Congress to act to save the program, and challenged the U.S. Senate to stop being good politicians and start being good senators.

title: Senators Coons, Representative McBride, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm
text:
DEWEY BEACH, Del. – U.S. Senator Chris Coons and U.S. Representative Sarah McBride (both D-Del.), joined by the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, local elected officials, and community leaders surveyed damage on Friday morning from last week’s nor’easter that battered Delaware’s coast for four days and caused severe beach erosion, dune damage and flooding in communities all along the coast. The storm damaged homes and businesses, caused road closures, and shut down beaches. Following their assessment of the damage, Senator Coons and Representative McBride called for additional federal support to help Delaware’s coastal communities recover and replenish their beaches.

Senator Coons and Representative McBride were joined on Friday by officials from the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, Dewey Beach Town Manager Bill Zolper, Dewey Beach Mayor Bill Stevens, South Bethany Mayor Edie Dondero, Bethany Beach Mayor Ron Calef, State Sen. Russ Huxtable and State Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall.

“Delaware’s beaches are critical to our communities, our economy, and our way of life, and we need to make sure they have the resources they need to recover from this storm and prepare for the next one,” said Senator Coons. “I’m going to keep fighting for the funding Delaware needs to rebuild and recover. That means working with our local leaders, DNREC, the Army Corps and our entire congressional delegation to make sure we’re doing everything we can to protect our coast.”

“The damage Senator Coons and I saw is a stark reminder that investing in the resilience of our coastal communities is not optional,” said Rep. McBride. “We cannot prevent these storms from happening, but we can take action to keep people safe and help our communities withstand their impacts. That’s why I’ve been working with partners at every level of government to strengthen our coastline, combat coastal erosion, and ensure Delaware is prepared when severe weather strikes. I’m grateful to Mayor Stevens, our first responders, local leaders, and everyone who stepped up to keep our neighbors safe during the nor’easter. I’ll keep working to make sure Delaware has what it needs to recover from this storm, prepare for the next one, and protect our beaches for generations to come.”

Earlier this year, Senators Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester and Representative McBride helped secure $10 million for beach replenishment along the Delaware coast from Cape Henlopen to Fenwick Island and are working with the Army Corps of Engineers to make that funding available as quickly as possible. Senator Coons is also working with the federal delegation and DNREC to secure an additional $30 million in federal beach replenishment funding this year to help address the state’s ongoing coastal needs.

title: Cornyn Praises Delivery of $7.5 Billion in Border Security Reimbursement Funds He Secured for Texas
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) released the following statement praising the delivery of $7.5 billion in border reimbursement funds that he, Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11), and Texas’ congressional delegation secured from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, also known as the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, to the State of Texas:

“Texas taxpayers shouldn’t have had to cover the costs of the Biden administration’s border crisis, and I am proud to have worked alongside Congressman Pfluger and my colleagues in the Texas delegation to ensure that the State would rightfully be repaid,” said Sen. Cornyn. “I am glad to see these dollars finally make their way to the Lone Star State, and I urge the Department of Justice to continue its disbursements of the remaining funds to Texas communities, which must be made whole for their role in trying to secure the border.”

Background:

The Working Families Tax Cuts Act included a total of $13.5 billion in funding secured by Sen. Cornyn, Rep. Pfluger, and the Texas congressional delegation to reimburse states like Texas for stepping up during the Biden administration to try and secure the border. The law created two funds, one administered by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the other by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ).

DHS officially opened the Cornyn-created State Border Security Reinforcement Fund for applications from eligible states in June. In addition to this nearly $10 billion fund, the DOJ opened the Bridging Immigration-related Deficits Experienced Nationwide (BIDEN) Program for applications the same month.

title: PASSED: Cortez Masto Bill to Extend Reporting Deadline for Emergency Tribal Health Care
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – The Senate unanimously passed bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) to extend the reporting deadline for Indian Health Service (IHS) patients who seek emergency care outside of IHS facilities. The IHS Emergency Claims Parity Act now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

“During a medical emergency, the last thing a patient should have to worry about is submitting burdensome paperwork to the government,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “Our bill gives patients the time to focus on rest and recovery while still getting they health care coverage they are eligible for. I thank my Senate colleagues for passing this measure and will continue working to get this bill passed into law.”

Currently, in emergency cases, IHS beneficiaries must notify IHS’ Purchased and Referred Care office within 72 hours of receiving care from a non-IHS facility. Tribal patients determined to be elderly or disabled are given 30 days to notify the IHS of emergency medical care received from non-IHS medical providers or at non-IHS medical facilities.

The IHS Emergency Claims Parity Act would increase the window for timely consideration of emergency care payments to 15 days for all IHS beneficiaries. This extension excludes reporting requirements for patients considered to be elderly or disabled, which would remain at 30 days.

Senator Cortez Masto is a fierce advocate for Nevada’s Tribal communities. She is leading three bipartisan bills to address the crisis of Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women (MMIW). In addition to fighting to improve public safety in Indian Country, Cortez Masto has pushed to better health care, maintain voting rights, and deliver tax parity for Tribes.

title: Duckworth Announces Illinois Native and Longtime Advisor Kelsey Becker as Chief of Staff
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) announced that her Deputy Chief of Staff Kelsey Becker has been promoted to Chief of Staff following Kalina Thompson’s departure from the role. Becker, a Schaumburg native, has served Duckworth’s team since 2012 in a range of leadership roles in both the Senator’s House and Senate offices as well as her campaigns.

“For over a decade, Kalina Thompson has been a kindred public servant, a true force for good, and beyond it all, a fiercely loyal friend,” said Duckworth. “While Kalina will be deeply missed, I’m excited to see all the good she’ll do in her next chapter and have the utmost confidence handing the reins over to Kelsey Becker.”

“As Deputy Chief of Staff and after years of service to my team, Kelsey has proven herself to be more than ready for this new role and keep up our work for the people of Illinois,” continued Duckworth. “She has been a trusted advisor and an astute political strategist—helping deliver key wins to the benefit of her fellow Illinoisans. Through her tireless efforts, Kelsey has helped institute policies and pass legislation that has made being a working parent easier for so many folks in our office, in our state and throughout the nation. Having been a valued part of our office for so many years, Kelsey brings deep institutional knowledge and a consistent record of dedication that will continue to serve our team and the people of Illinois well.”

Becker holds a Master of Arts in International Development, with a focus on Gender and Democracy, from George Washington University, and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Political Science from Butler University. She also served as a Peace Corps Volunteer in Mali, where she partnered with a local women’s association to strengthen business practices and support economic development.

For the past three years, Becker has served as Co-Lead of the Senate Moms Group, a bipartisan organization comprised of over 200 moms who work in the Senate and help drive policies that empower parents and families in Congress. Becker lives in the DC area with her husband and their three children.

title: Duckworth Join Colleagues in Pressing EPA, AI Companies on Rollback of Public Input Rules for Data Center Air Permits
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), co-chair of the Senate Environmental Justice Caucus, joined U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and other members of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, in sending two letters opposing the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) proposal to eliminate the 30-day mandatory public notice period that allows communities to provide input on proposed facilities, like data centers, that may affect the air they breathe. One letter is addressed to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin urging him to withdraw the proposed rule. The other letter is addressed to nine major data center companies—Anthropic, AWS, Fermi, Google, Joule, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and xAI—calling on them to maintain current public participation standards regardless of the rule's outcome.

“We agree that permitting should be efficient, predictable, and capable of supporting the infrastructure our country needs. But faster permitting should not come at the expense of transparency or communities’ ability to shape the decisions that affect them,” the Senators wrote.

“Data center companies like yours also have a responsibility not to use weaker requirements to limit public participation or communities’ ability to meaningfully shape decisions that affect them,” wrote the Senators to the data center companies. “America can build the infrastructure needed to compete and innovate while keeping communities informed and involved in the decisions that affect them.”

In addition to Duckworth, Kelly and Whitehouse, the letter to the EPA was co-signed by U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Edward Markey (D-MA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

In addition to Duckworth, Kelly and Whitehouse, the letter to the data companies was co-signed by Ron Wyden (D-OR), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

The full letter to the EPA is available on Senator Duckworth’s website.

The full letter to the data companies is also available on Senator Duckworth’s website.

title: Duckworth, Schumer, Matsui Lead Bipartisan Call Requiring FAA to Guarantee Every Emergency Medical Kit Aboard Flights Include Life-Saving Epinephrin
text:
The lawmakers’ call comes as the public comment period closes on the FAA’s dangerous proposed rule that would make epinephrine optional on flights

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL)—Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation—U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) and U.S. Representative Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Co-Chair of the Congressional Food Allergy Research Caucus, led a group of 20 bipartisan, bicameral lawmakers in calling on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to guarantee that emergency medical kits (EMK) on every commercial aircraft include epinephrine, a life-saving medication to treat passengers who go into anaphylactic shock. Today is the final day for the American people to submit public comments on the FAA’s dangerous new proposed rule that would result in medications being less consistent and dependable for passengers experiencing health emergencies on commercial flights—a severely misguided proposal that prioritizes flexibility for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.

“Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly,” wrote the lawmakers in their official public comment to the FAA’s proposed rule. “The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.”

In the landmark 2024 FAA Reauthorization Law that she co-authored, Duckworth successfully secured a provision which required the FAA to ensure commercial airlines have adequate emergency medical kits on board to treat conditions like anaphylaxis. And yet, the FAA’s proposed rule would not require them to carry epinephrine—the only medication that reliably treats this medical emergency—in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training.

Duckworth and Schumer have been pushing for years to require epinephrine designed for self-administration aboard all commercial aircraft, ever since they heard from their own constituents in 2019 who shared the life-threatening scares they experienced aboard flights that lacked this key medication and delivery method. The Senators detailed these harrowing stories in a letter to airline CEOs last month, in which they called on air carriers to ensure this life-saving medication is included in all their EMKs.

The lawmakers continued, “If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended ‘pre-measured auto-delivery device’ be on the EMK contents list.”

In their letter, the lawmakers hammered the FAA’s proposed rule for ignoring expert recommendations, creating an even greater lack of transparency and consistency in EMKs for the flying public—who rely on EMKs during a medical emergency—and for needlessly putting the lives of commercial airline passengers at greater risk.

“To ensure the safety of all airline passengers, we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight,” the lawmakers concluded.

In light of the FAA’s misguided and dangerous proposed rule change, Duckworth, Schumer and Matsui are calling on the FAA to heed their concerns—as well as the more than 1,500 public comments that have been submitted to express deep concern over this would-be policy failure that would place cost cutting and convenience for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.

In addition to Duckworth and Schumer, the letter is co-signed in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

In addition to Matsui, the letter is co-signed in the House by U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08), LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), Kelly Morrison (D-MN-03) and Mike Quigley (D-IL-05).

Full text of the letter can be found below and on Senator Duckworth’s website:

Dear Administrator Bedford:

We write to provide our comments on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) published on August 5, 2026, which would make drastic changes to how the FAA determines the composition of the emergency medical kit (EMK) carried aboard aircraft. The proposed rule is opaque and dangerous, and it threatens to undermine previous work the FAA has done to ensure the safety of the traveling public.

EMKs are supposed to enable initial treatment of a passenger experiencing moderate to severe injuries or illnesses until the aircraft can land and the passenger can be transferred to emergency medical personnel. Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly.

The proposed rule would make harmful steps to reverse work done at the agency to direct operators to include epinephrine in aircraft EMKs. Having multiple doses of epinephrine on every aircraft, in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training, is more urgent than ever. This is due to the on-flight presence of food items containing unlabeled allergens, a steady increase in the number of children with food allergies, the increased prevalence of a tick-borne illness that could create life-threatening allergies and the very real possibility that more than one passenger may require epinephrine during a single flight.

The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.

Our concerns about the proposed rule are outlined below:

Lack of Alignment with Previous Recommendations

The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 directed the FAA to assemble a panel of experts to make recommendations on EMKs and issue a proposed rule. The FAA Onboard Medical Kits Working Group included aerospace medicine experts and physicians, physiologists, psychologists, human factors specialists, cabin safety professionals and researchers. This working group submitted its report, dated May 1, 2025, to the FAA. The report stated:

“The items proposed … are intended to provide initial stabilizing Basic Life Support (BLS) care for immediately life-threatening conditions such as cardiac arrest, airway emergencies, major hemorrhage, and anaphylaxis (emphasis added), as well as to facilitate provision of limited basic first-aid interventions for minor injuries and illnesses that are known to occur in-flight.”

Importantly, the proposed EMK content list in the report includes both “pre-measured auto-delivery device” or “vial-drawn kit.” Yet, just one year later, the FAA publicly defied the recommendations in this report developed by the expert working group the FAA itself commissioned.

No Clear Requirement for Epinephrine

Through rulemaking, the Trump administration is seeking to downgrade the EMK content list, from a binding requirement to mere optional guidance. The proposed rule would allow operators to determine what components should be included in EMKs, so long as the EMK is “practical and sufficient” to address nine conditions, including anaphylaxis:

“…FAA recommends sufficient resources for anaphylaxis (sudden/acute severe allergic reaction), which may include the following signs and symptoms: hives; swelling of the mouth, throat, or tongue; difficulty breathing, rapid or weak pulse, dizziness; stomach pain; nausea or vomiting; or loss of consciousness. Treatment options could (emphasis added) include medication such as epinephrine.”

Epinephrine is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The final rule must contain a clear directive that EMKs shall include epinephrine.

No Requirement for Epinephrine in Easily Self-Administered Forms

If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended “pre-measured auto-delivery device” be on the EMK contents list.

Currently, JetBlue, Southwest, Breeze and Frontier stock their EMKs with epinephrine auto-injectors, and American Airlines’ EMKs include both adult- and pediatric-dose epinephrine auto-injectors. Delta is in the process of transitioning its fleet to include auto-injectors in their EMKs by September 2027, and, this year, United Airlines and Allegiant Airlines will begin the work to include auto-injectors in EMKs. Even with tight profit margins, including epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered, is possible. Through the rulemaking process, the FAA must direct airlines to include epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily administered and not reverse course from its previous recommendations by abandoning the requirement to include epinephrine in EMKs in entirety.

Lack of Transparency on Compliance

The proposed rule would eliminate the exemption process, which was created to account for challenges in stocking EMKs due to drug shortages and allow airlines to substitute drugs, “without requesting an FAA exemption.” Airlines are not required to publicly or centrally report the real-time inventory and exact contents of their EMKs and have continued to operate under exemptions granted by the FAA for years. EMK suppliers and airlines can track when an EMK is opened and needs restocking, but only in instances where the kit was used. There is no means of systematically tracking incidents of allergic reactions or anaphylaxis, especially when passengers use their own epinephrine. For medical conditions that can be treated by multiple, accessible options, eliminating the need for the exemption process may make sense. However, epinephrine is the only first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The public also deserves to know when certain items are not included in a flight’s EMK, and a rationale for the exclusion.

Conclusion

The proposed rule will reduce public safety and trust when flying by increasing ambiguity, subjectivity and opacity of EMK components. The proposed rule argues that increased flexibility is needed to keep up with advances in medicine but, without appropriate reporting and tracking, the Trump administration is significantly increasing the risk of major inconsistencies in EMKs from flight to flight. Predictability, consistency and transparency are all necessary to ensure passengers’ safety, particularly in cases of anaphylaxis, when minutes, or even seconds, matter.

To ensure the safety of all airline passengers, we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight.

We call on the FAA to address the concerns outlined in this letter.

-30-

title: Gallego, Colleagues Demand Hearing with Bill Putle Following Announced Cuts to Crucial FHFA Office of Inspector General
text:
Banking Democrats call for public forum to demand answers from Pulte on documented abuses of power

WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Jack Reed (D-RI), and their Democratic colleagues on the Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, in sending a letter to Chair Tim Scott (R-SC) requesting a hearing with Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) Director Bill Pulte.

The Senators’ request follows various reported abuses of power by Pulte, including last week’s unprecedented move to cut the funding to the agency’s Office of the Inspector General (FHFA-OIG) by 60 percent and risk future operations.

“We request you invite Director Pulte to testify before the Senate Banking Committee so our committee can fulfill its oversight functions and explore how his decisions are affecting FHFA’s ability to ensure Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the FHLBanks (collectively, “the government-sponsored enterprises,” or GSEs) operate in a safe and sound manner and provide a reliable source of liquidity and funding for housing finance and community investment. The hearing would provide Director Pulte the opportunity to explain his record,” the senators wrote.

Bill Pulte’s proposed cuts to FHFA-OIG — which is tasked with investigating waste, fraud, and abuse at FHFA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Federal Home Loan Banks — come while he remains under scrutiny for his abuses of power. Pulte is under investigation by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) for potentially misusing his federal authority and resources to publicly accuse prominent Democrats and President Donald Trump’s perceived political enemies of mortgage fraud. Pulte also faces questions for his apparent involvement in the President’s scheme to demolish the Kennedy Center and his brief tenure as Acting Director of National Intelligence.

The senators also addressed his mismanagement of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which back 70 percent of mortgages in the United States: “Since failing to respond to congressional inquiries on his activities, Director Pulte has fired more staff at Fannie Mae, including about a dozen high-ranking executives. These now-fired executives were responsible for multifamily loans, low-income housing tax credit investments, and finance, and also included regulatory and communications officials. Director Pulte has not publicly explained the reasoning behind these most recent terminations and how these firings will impact Fannie Mae’s ability to provide price stability across the mortgage market.”

70-80 percent of staff, including experienced law enforcement officers who serve as the primary watchdogs for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and keep the mortgage market stable, would be impacted by a layoff with Pulte’s cuts to the FHFA-OIG. These staff are tasked with investigating title and mortgage fraud, protecting mortgage lenders and home buyers from predatory practices, and ensuring a sound and secure mortgage and banking system.

“We must fulfill our oversight responsibilities related to potential harm being done by Director Pulte to our nation’s housing finance market and in turn, to the supply and cost of housing,” the senators concluded.

title: Gallego, Colleagues Demand Investigation into Recent Knowles Firefighter Tragedy
text:
Senators call to examine policies following June deaths of four Rifle Helitack Crew firefighters

WASHINGTON – Last week, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), and Gary Peters (D-MI) sent a letter to the Department of the Interior (DOI) demanding an investigation into the policies that preceded the deaths of four Rifle Interagency Helitack Crew members responding to the Gore and Knowles Fires on June 27.

The fallen firefighters, Nick Hutcherson, 27, Emily Barker, 38, Sydney Watson, 27, and Nathan Matthews, 43, grew up in communities across the country before finding their way to federal wildland firefighting in Western Colorado. The senators represent states with connections to the four firefighters.

“The tragedy of the loss of these four lives necessitates a thorough examination of departmental policies that guide fire suppression,” wrote the senators. “This year has seen the highest number of entrapments in two decades, as well as the deaths of 13 federal wildland firefighters, pilots, and contractors in incidents across the West. Now is the time to examine the policies that can help us avoid any additional devastating losses.”

In a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, the senators called for the investigation to examine:

Interior’s “full suppression” strategy: Whether the department’s presumption of full suppression for every wildfire properly weighs risks to life, property, and natural resources.

Direct attack by default: Whether the approach used on the Knowles Fire was influenced by broader agency policy rather than an assessment of the specific fire behavior and conditions crews faced.

Firefighter safety and weather conditions: Whether information-sharing—specifically in regard to fire-weather and conditions — led to adequately informed decisions, and whether improvements can or should be made going forward. Federal forecasts warned potentially severe impacts the morning the Rifle Helitack Crew deployed. The crew was inserted two hours later and remained on the ground amid new ignitions, strong winds, and near-zero visibility, according to preliminary investigation reports.

Staffing and organizational changes: Assess the impact of whether major staffing cuts and shortages on its fire suppression operations in relation to the Knowles Fire tragedy.

The letter comes as the senators continue seeking answers about the recent deaths. Interagency procedures call for serious accident investigations to be completed within 45 days, meaning the internal review should have been completed by August 11. Requests for a briefing on the investigation’s status have not been fulfilled, and no new information has been released since a July 30 update.

“Wildland firefighter safety is a non-negotiable imperative,” continued the senators. “We call on you to ensure the Department takes a thorough, clear-eyed assessment of the multiple factors that led to four deaths and one serious injury in response to the Knowles Fire.”

title: Gallego Introduces Bill to Reduce Student Cell Phone Use in School
text:
WASHINGTON — Last week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) introduced the Supporting Focus in Schools Act, legislation that would help public schools limit classroom cell phone use by creating a grant program to cover the costs of phone storage and teacher training.

“Kids are getting phones younger and younger, and we’re seeing the consequences in the classroom: more distractions, less learning. As a dad of three young kids, I worry about the repercussions this has for their future,” said Senator Gallego. “It’s time to get cell phones out of the classroom. Kids should engage with what they’re learning — without a phone constantly pulling their attention away.”

The Supporting Focus in Schools Act would create a grant program under the Department of Education to support restricting the use of cellular phones and other personal electronic devices at Title I schools during instructional time. Funding may be used to purchase equipment for the program, such as lockers and phone pouches, and to provide training for teachers and administrators.

Exceptions can be made at the discretion of the school administrator regarding:

Cell phone usage by students for medical purposes or emergencies.

School laptops and other electronic devices used for instruction and provided by the school.

Last month, Senator Gallego announced his education titled “Class in Session: A Plan to Fix America’s Public Education System,” aimed at focusing on strengthening our public school system to ensure the success of our students as they move into the workforce.

title: Gallego, Kelly Celebrate Passage of Bill to Restore the Grand Canyon’s North Rim Out of Committee
text:
WASHINGTON – Last week, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) celebrated the unanimous passage of the North Rim Restoration Act out of the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (ENR). The legislation addresses recovery efforts of the North Rim at the Grand Canyon after the devastating Dragon Bravo Fire.

If enacted, the legislation would streamline the restoration process by granting National Park Service (NPS) emergency contracting authority to bypass standard delays and accelerate renewals. The legislation covers fire-related recovery efforts, including forest management, maintenance, rebuilding, and infrastructure improvements. This would allow the NPS to quickly hire, approve, and oversee contractors for cleanup and reconstruction efforts.

“The Grand Canyon is not only a marvel to look at — the tourists it attracts act as the economic engine for rural communities in Northern Arizona. These communities have been devastated by the Dragon Bravo fire and need help now,” said Senator Gallego. “I urge the full Senate to take up this bill and provide the resources needed to get these communities back on their feet.”

“Rebuilding the North Rim of the Grand Canyon is critical for the communities and small businesses that depend on it,” said Senator Kelly. “We’re one step closer to cutting red tape, restoring the park, and bringing visitors back to the area.”

“We applaud Senator Gallego and Senator Kelly’s leadership and support of the North Rim Restoration Act introduced by Representative Crane and its passage through committee. The bill’s passage by unanimous consent represents a critical bipartisan step by Congress to ensure we move as quickly and thoughtfully as possible to rebuild the Grand Canyon’s North Rim. We look forward to working with Senator Gallego, Senator Kelly, Representative Crane, and the full Arizona delegation to ensure the North Rim Restoration Act becomes law, and the funding for the rebuild is duly and expeditiously allocated. This will allow federal agencies to quickly begin work supporting communities hit hardest by last summer’s wildfires,” said Ethan Aumack, Executive Director Grand Canyon Trust.

In July of 2025, the Dragon Bravo fire initiated following lightning strikes on the North Rim in Grand Canyon National Park, burning thousands of acres of National Park Service land. Over 100 structures were destroyed, including the historic Grand Canyon Lodge, several historic cabins and the North Rim Visitor Center in the Grand Canyon National Park, and a wastewater treatment plant, resulting in a chlorine gas leak.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Introduce Bicameral Legislation To Depoliticize Military Promotions
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, joined a bicameral group of colleagues to introduce the Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act. This bill would protect qualified military officers from being arbitrarily removed from promotion consideration for ideological or political reasons by establishing clear standards, basic due process, and meaningful independent review.

“Officers who have earned a promotion deserve to be judged on their qualifications and nothing else,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Secretary Hegseth has pushed out our best and brightest, cutting some of the most highly trained, most qualified people in our armed services and leaving our military rudderless. I will keep fighting to curb Secretary Hegseth’s ability to jeopardize our national security and military preparedness and ensure our military is led by qualified officers capable of keeping Americans safe.”

Defense Secretary Hegseth has repeatedly blocked women and minority officers from promotions and criticized diversity initiatives in the military. The new legislation reins in Secretary Hegseth’s inconsistent and politicized leadership and mandates that an officer can only be removed from promotion recommendations based on the following criteria:

The officer engaged in misconduct;

Newly discovered, material adverse information unavailable to the promotion selection board materially affects the qualifications of the officer for promotion;

The officer no longer satisfies statutory qualifications for promotion; or

Removal is required for reasons of national security or military necessity

Senator Gillibrand has been a leading voice in holding Secretary Hegseth accountable for his reckless leadership of the Department of Defense. During his confirmation hearing, she challenged his previous denigration of women in the military and has repeatedly called for his resignation, most recently after eight sailors in the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide. In April, after reports that Hegseth blocked or delayed promotions for more than a dozen Black and female senior officers, she called for a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on the matter.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the legislation is cosponsored in the Senate by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), and Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI). It is cosponsored in the House by U.S. Representatives Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06) and Marilyn Strickland (D-WA-10).

The bill is endorsed by VoteVets, Protect Democracy, the National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), and Retired Major General Steve Lepper, co-founder of the Former JAG Working Group.

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Following Senator Hassan’s Push, President Trump Backs Down From Taxpayer-Funded Political Ads
text:
WASHINGTON – Following U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan’s recent push for immediate answers and transparency around President Donald Trump’s plainly-illegal taxpayer-funded political advertisements, President Trump this evening announced that he would back down from the effort and direct his campaign and his super PAC to pay for the ads instead. The ads, one of which included footage that was directly from a 2024 Trump campaign video, have reportedly already cost taxpayers more than $10 million as part of a reported $20 million contract.

“These campaign ads never should have run on the taxpayer’s dime to begin with. They were clearly wrong and clearly illegal, which is why the President should also immediately repay the taxpayers for the amount already spent on these ads,” said Senator Hassan, Ranking Member of the Joint Economic Committee and senior member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee in response to the news. “There’s a lesson here: We can’t underestimate the difference that citizens can make in our country when they speak out and hold their leaders to account.”

Reports of President Trump’s taxpayer-funded political ad push first became public on September 24, and Senator Hassan immediately launched an effort to get answers for people and force the President to reverse course. Senator Hassan began by calling for White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles to immediately tell the American people how these political advertisements, which clearly violated federal law, were developed, who authorized them, and where the funds were coming from. Senator Hassan also took to the Senate Floor for answers, introducing and moving to pass a Senate resolution condemning the ads and saying they should not be paid for by taxpayer dollars. Senate Republicans blocked consideration of the effort. Finally, Senator Hassan kept up the pressure on the Administration, pushing President Trump on multiple televisionnetworks about the unprecedented and unacceptable nature of these ads.

Finally, this evening, President Trump relented, announcing that he would pay for the television ads himself, as well as through funds he has raised for his super PAC. It is not immediately clear how the President, who is legally barred from coordinating with his Super PAC, could direct them to do anything while remaining in compliance with federal law.

title: Senator Hassan Highlights the Cost of Trump’s Vanity Projects During Speech on Senate Floor
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan recently delivered remarks on the floor of the U.S. Senate highlighting President Trump’s failure to fulfill his promise to lower costs for American families, while spending taxpayer dollars on projects that honor himself.

Since President Trump took office, the average American household has had to spend more than $4,200 extra on goods and services because of rising costs, according to a recent Joint Economic Committee – Minority report. Meanwhile, a separate Committee report found that President Trump’s vanity projects – including construction of the new White House ballroom and the no-bid contract to paint the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, among others – are expected to cost more than $1.8 billion. Using this total, the Committee created an Interactive Cost Calculator where users can explore how this $1.8 billion could instead be spent to lower costs and help the American people.

Click hereto watch Senator Hassan’s full remarks, and see key quotes and a full transcript below:

“Not only has the President failed to make good on his pledge to bring down costs, not only is it evident that he never even bothered to try, but it’s clear that on virtually every metric, it costs more to be an American than it did two years ago when this President was sworn in and the 119th Congress began.”

“The President had nearly two years to try to lower costs, and instead families had $4200 more dollars taken out of their pockets.”

“The President has been clear about his priorities: He is not interested in lowering costs for families. He would rather raise monuments to honor himself.”

“The American people don’t want the President to build a golden ballroom; they want him to build homes that they can afford.”

“In short, it tells us that the President seeks to rule; but he is unable to lead. He seeks to honor himself; but he is unable to honor his word.”

Two years ago, the American people elected a new Congress and a new President. The American people did so based on a promise that the President and his allies in Congress would work to bring down high costs.

So now, it’s worth asking a simple question, one that the American people will ask their elected representatives when they return home in a few days:

Did the President and his allies in Congress make good on their pledge to bring down costs for American families?

The answer is clear: No. Not only has the President failed to make good on his pledge to bring down costs, not only is it evident that he never even bothered to try, but it’s clear that on virtually every metric, it costs more to be an American than it did two years ago when this President was sworn in and the 119th Congress began.

It’s worth taking a moment to go line by line, cost by cost, broken promise by broken promise, to examine the ways in which the President’s policies – including his tariffs and his war – have driven costs higher and higher.

Before the President took office, he promised that he would bring gas prices down from $3 a gallon to less than $2. But under this President and his majorities in Congress, gas prices haven’t just failed to go down, they’ve instead shot up to around $4.50 a gallon, meaning gas costs 50% more now than when Donald Trump entered office.

Since the President began his reckless war with Iran without a plan to win, the American people have paid an additional $93 billion on gas in less than a year. And on average, each American family has had to spend $790 more on gas since this war began.

And the President failed even more catastrophically to bring down diesel prices. Diesel now costs around $3 more a gallon than it did when the President took office. Farmers and truckers are weathering the highest prices for diesel in American history, with costs at the pump exceeding $6.50 a gallon last week.

Now, it’s one thing to fail on a promise to lower the price of something, it’s quite another to be responsible for the highest price of that good ever recorded in our country’s history.

The President also promised to make health care “affordable again.” Of course, that is not at all what happened. Instead, the President gutted Medicaid to take away health care from millions of Americans in order to pay for tax giveaways to billionaires like himself.

He also allowed health insurance premiums to surge, meaning more families now pay more for insurance every single month, even if they don’t get sick.

Just before the President took office, the average monthly cost for health insurance was $468 a month. The President did not reduce those premiums by a dime.

Instead, families now pay $611 a month, that is almost $150 more monthly, almost $2000 more per year. $2000 dollars…dollars that could otherwise be spent on the mortgage, the rent, repairs for the car, let alone parents just using it to do something nice for their kids.

And what about the cost of groceries? The President promised repeatedly that he would bring grocery costs down. Well, let’s look at the numbers. Since the President took office, ground beef has risen to $7 a pound. And coffee has risen from about $7 a pound to more than $9.

Now I don’t know if the President is right when he says that groceries are an “old fashioned word” as he often claims, but I do know that old-fashioned math tells us that $9 is more expensive than $7.

And let’s say we take everything all together…all the goods and services that we pay for every day and add it all up. How much, if at all, did the President and his allies in Congress, reduce costs?

They failed to reduce costs at all. The American people have had to pay an additional $4,200 on goods and services since the President took office. The President had nearly two years to try to lower costs, and instead families had $4,200 more dollars taken out of their pockets.

This isn’t a partisan point, this isn’t spin, this is just basic, mathematical facts — facts that make evident that the President both completely failed to lower costs and honestly didn’t even try.

So, if the President failed to bring down costs, what has he been working on these last two years?

Well, the President has been clear about his priorities: He is not interested in lowering costs for families. He is interested in raising monuments to honor himself.

He hosted military parades in his honor. He destroyed the East Wing to build himself a golden ballroom. He’s been trying to put his name on other monuments. He is running taxpayer-funded ad campaigns praising himself.

And, according to a new report from the Joint Economic Committee Minority, while the American people are paying more to keep up with high costs, the President wants to spend $1.8 billion on projects to flatter his own vanity.

Now, we throw lots of numbers around in Washington, but it’s worth remembering what the American people know full well: This is real money we’re talking about. It’s the American people’s money. We owe it to them to ask: How could that same 1.8 billion dollars help them?

What can $1.8 billion buy when it’s not being diverted by an apprentice dictator who, rightly fearing that no one will ever honor his presidency after he is gone, rushes to build gilded tributes to himself?

$1.8 billion, it can buy a lot of things.

It can pay for the electric bills for 12 million families for a month.

It can fill up more than 35 million tanks of gas, even at the President’s new high prices.

It can buy 600 million school lunches, fully paid for, so our children can have a good, healthy meal at school.

$1.8 billion could hire around 30,000 new fire fighters to keep our communities safe.

And it can pay all the medical expenses, every medical bill for more than 88,000 American veterans for an entire year.

If the President insists on spending the people’s money on himself, he owes them an explanation. So, if I have one request today, it’s this: I want the President to explain why a monument to honor himself is a better use of taxpayer dollars than paying for health care for veterans?

Is a ballroom to make one man feel like a King, more important than health care for a year for the heroes who fought to keep our country free?

What more did America’s heroes, people who have given everything to this country, what more need to do, to deserve the $1.8 billion the President would rather spend to honor himself?

And when in America did honoring service become less important than honoring one man’s ego?

I know that a majority of Americans, including many of my Republican colleagues, also find the President’s vanity projects distasteful. But I think we all are doing a bit of play-acting if we forget that the President’s determination to shower himself in honors is not simply excessive, or a distraction, but is wrong, and is distinctly un-American.

Consider our other Presidents. George Washington didn’t order the construction of the Washington Monument; Abraham Lincoln and Thomas Jefferson didn’t pick out sculptors to build their memorials; John F. Kennedy didn’t name the Kennedy Center; and none of them tried to put themselves on our currency.

They received these honors from grateful citizens after their time in office.

The current President is the only exception to this rule. George Washington was a rich man as well, but he used his wealth to support the Continental Army, he didn’t use his office to enrich himself. Nor did he have any interest in being a King.

The reason why this matters is because the President’s desire to appease his own vanity and his failure to bring down costs are linked. Because it’s deeply telling that the President will go to such extravagant lengths to honor himself…he will break with American values and precedent when they stand in the way of his whims, he will use a wrecking ball to tear down buildings.

He will spend great time and effort planning every detail, he will file court appeals while defying court orders, he will pilfer taxpayer funds, and even ignore the law and the Constitution…all just in his mission to leave a gilded tribute to himself…but he can’t be bothered to lift a finger to bring down costs…despite his promise to do so.

What does this all reveal? It reveals that the President is uninterested in listening to what the American people want:

The American people don’t want the President to build a golden ballroom; they want him to build homes that they can afford.

They’re not asking for parades and car races on the National Mall; they want to pay less at the pump on their way to work.

They don’t want his face on our currency; they want to keep more money in their pockets.

So, in closing, what does the final accounting of the President’s broken promise tell us? Since the President took office, Americans have had to pay $4,200 more to keep up with rising costs…while the President spends $1.8 billion to keep up with his own ego.

In short, it tells us that the President seeks to rule; but he is unable to lead.

He seeks to honor himself; but he is unable to honor his word.

title: Senator Hassan Speaks at Youth Addiction Prevention Summit in Plymouth
text:
PLYMOUTH – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan spoke at the Communities for Alcohol- and Drug-Free Youth (CADY) 24th Annual Prevention Summit in Plymouth. During her speech, Senator Hassan highlighted efforts to combat addiction and support people working on the front lines of prevention, treatment, and recovery.

The CADY Summit brought together prevention and recovery professionals, health care providers, law enforcement, students, and community members to discuss strategies to prevent substance misuse and strengthen prevention efforts across New Hampshire.

Senator Hassan continues to work to combat addiction and expand access to evidence-based addiction treatment. At the end of last year, Senator Hassan played a key role in spearheading the passage of the bipartisan SUPPORT Act, which included important support for federal funding for fentanyl test strips. Additionally, Senator Hassan helped introduce the Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act, bipartisan legislation to improve access to medication-assisted treatment by allowing more addiction specialists to prescribe methadone. In 2022, Senator Hassan successfully passed into law her bipartisanMainstreaming Addiction Treatment (MAT) Act to increase the number of medical professionals authorized to prescribe medication-assisted treatment.

Read highlights from Senator Hassan’s remarks as prepared below:

“Thanks in part to the work of many of the people in this room, New Hampshire has made real, steady progress combatting fentanyl. Overdose deaths are down. Medication-assisted-treatment, the gold standard for treatment, is now much more readily available. And law enforcement officers continue to find new ways to stop the spread of illicit fentanyl on our streets.”

“It’s important for us to note that none of this progress happened by accident. We made this progress because people like all of you in this room worked to make it happen.”

“While we’ve made important progress, we also know that there is much more work to do. One of the challenges of the fentanyl and synthetic drug crisis, as everyone here understands full well, is that it’s a constantly changing threat. Every time we seem to get a handle on it, we encounter a new illicit drug showing up on our streets, or some other new challenge. That’s why it’s vital that we don’t let up. We need to continue building on the progress that we’ve made.”

“It’s also critical that we continue to ramp up efforts to promote prevention, including in schools. We need to understand which educational programs and strategies work and which don’t.”

"Students often tell us that dealing with addiction on their own, without the support system that they need, cases them to retreat into themselves; they feel all alone... Any successful anti-addiction strategy is going to need students and young leaders having a key role.”
