title: Padilla, Booker, Blumenthal Urge Mullin to Immediately Recall ICE Officers Hired During Hiring Surge
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) called on Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin to immediately remove from field duty all U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers hired during the Department’s 2025 hiring surge. In an oversight letter that comes days after new reports of the agency’s plans to hire 5,000 new officers before year’s end, the Senators demanded DHS complete comprehensive retraining and re-vetting for all officers hired during the 2025 surge period.

“Over the past year, ICE and other DHS personnel have fatally shot and killed multiple people during vehicle stops and enforcement operations, including several instances in which agents opened fire on people inside their own cars,” wrote the Senators. “These killings, combined with the whistleblower’s account of corners cut on both vetting and training, make clear that officers hired during the surge did not receive adequate instruction in de-escalation, use-of-force standards, and vehicle-stop protocols before being sent into communities with the authority to use deadly force.”

Republicans poured $75 billion into ICE through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and then added another $38.5 billion more this summer, allowing ICE to hire thousands of new officers with incentives including a signing bonus of up to $50,000 and up to $60,000 in student-loan repayment. To meet the hiring demand, the agency lowered hiring standards and cut corners on background checks, raising concerns about unqualified and poorly trained armed officers conducting immigration arrests. Several incidents involving death and violence led to increased calls for oversight by Senate Democrats. ICE is now reportedly preparing for a second hiring surge of 5,000 employees, including deportation officers, before the end of the year – roughly a 17% increase in three months – without having completed background investigations for thousands of hires from the first surge.

The letter follows recent New York Times reporting detailing a formal whistleblower complaint to the DHS Office of Inspector General from a 17-year ICE veteran overseeing background investigations. The complaint alleged that job offers were extended to candidates without completion of basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks and were evaded by political appointees. In another whistleblower disclosure to the Senate, a former ICE Academy instructor and agency attorney disclosed that ICE cut training hours on use of force, firearms safety, and the constitutional rights of the public during this same period. According to another New York Times report, 7,500 active officers with arrest authority hired during last year’s surge are still awaiting the full background investigations required for their positions.

“DHS cannot allow officers whose backgrounds were never properly vetted, and who may never have received adequate use-of-force training, to remain on the streets with arrest authority and firearms,” concluded the Senators.

In the letter, the Senators also urged DHS to:

Immediately suspend field enforcement duties for all ICE officers hired during the 2025 hiring surge, pending completion of full background checks and training.

Provide a full accounting of how many current ICE officers received job offers or field assignments before completing fingerprint, identity, and credit checks, and how many of those officers have discharged a firearm in the course of duty.

Provide ICE’s 2026 hiring plan, including

All documents, memoranda, internal communications, staffing assessments, and analyses of staffing needs;

The vetting and training protocols; and

The name and title of each official who approved the plan.

Provide a copy of the whistleblower’s complaint and any Office of Inspector General findings or corrective action plan arising from it.

Provide a detailed accounting of the use-of-force policy and vehicle-stop protocol changes DHS has made since January 2026.

Including how those changes have been implemented and audited across ICE field offices.

Padilla has been a leader in holding the Trump Administration accountable for its cruel and reckless mass deportation agenda. Last week, Padilla conducted an unannounced oversight visit to the de facto ICE detention facility at the San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Last month, Padilla called out the Trump Administration’s continued abuses of power and inhumane treatment of detained immigrants, after sounding the alarm on the significant increase in deaths among detainees in ICE custody since January 2025. He also demanded DHS immediately halt its reckless plan to equip ICE officers with electric shock gloves. Padilla also condemned Republicans’ partisan bill to provide ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) with an extra $70 billion without necessary reforms and forced a vote on his amendment that would require ICE officers to wear body cameras while on-duty.

Full letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Mullin:

We write to demand that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) immediately remove from field duty all U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers hired and trained during the 2025 hiring surge, and that those officers be required to complete comprehensive retraining and re-vetting before being permitted to return to enforcement operations. Over the past year, public reporting on DHS’s hiring and training requirements, and the conduct of its officers in the field, demonstrates that ICE officers hired during this surge cannot be trusted with a badge and the authority to make arrests. These concerns are heightened now that ICE is preparing a second hiring surge of 5,000 employees before year’s end without having completed background investigations for thousands of hires from the first.

On September 3, 2026, The New York Times reported that a 17-year ICE veteran who oversaw background investigations made a formal whistleblower complaint last year, expressing concern about a systemic breakdown in the vetting of thousands of ICE recruits brought on during the agency’s rapid expansion. According to the complaint, ICE’s human resources division routinely extended final job offers before candidates had completed basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks, and political appointees were permitted to bypass standard background investigations to obtain national security eligibility. The complaint, filed with the DHS Office of Inspector General, warned that this unprecedented lowering of hiring standards left the agency vulnerable to insider threats, infiltration, and foreign influence, and it called on DHS to immediately suspend the improper practices, hold accountable those responsible, and review recent hires for potential insider threats. A separate whistleblower, a former ICE Academy instructor and agency attorney, separately disclosed that ICE cut training hours on use of force, firearms safety, and the constitutional rights of the public during this same period.

New reporting confirms that the vetting failures the whistleblower described persist today. On September 29, 2026, The New York Times reported that nearly 7,500 individuals hired during last year’s surge are still awaiting the full background investigations required for their positions, and that they may work on a limited basis in the meantime. ICE had already removed hundreds of surge hires by this spring. Before even addressing this problem, ICE now intends to hire 5,000 more employees by year’s end—a workforce expansion of roughly 17 percent in three months—and most will serve as deportation officers with arrest authority. DHS’s assurances that it will apply rigorous standards to this new cohort cannot be taken at face value when it has not yet cleared the officers it already hired.

These vetting and training failures preceded a series of violent and deadly incidents involving ICE officials. Over the past year, ICE and other DHS personnel have fatally shot and killed multiple people during vehicle stops and enforcement operations, including several instances in which agents opened fire on people inside their own cars:

On January 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Minneapolis, Minnesota fatally shot Renée Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, as she attempted to drive away from agents during an enforcement operation. Witnesses reported that federal officers blocked bystanders and medics from rendering aid.

Less than two weeks later, Border Patrol agents fatally shot Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, during the same wave of Minneapolis enforcement operations.

On July 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Houston, Texas fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old construction worker and father of three, while he was driving a work crew to a job site. Witnesses have disputed DHS’s account that Mr. Salgado Araujo used his vehicle as a weapon.

Six days later, on July 13, 2026, an ICE officer in Biddeford, Maine fatally shot Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old father, in his car after agents rammed his vehicle and fired multiple rounds through it while executing a warrant for someone else. Mr. Durán Guerrero was not the target of the operation and was authorized to work in the United States.

A review of shootings by federal immigration officers during this Administration found that the overwhelming majority—19 of 22 incidents identified as of July 2026—began with a vehicle stop, underscoring that ICE’s current tactics for approaching and stopping vehicles are placing officers and the public in unnecessary danger. These killings, combined with the whistleblower’s account of corners cut on both vetting and training, make clear that officers hired during the surge did not receive adequate instruction in deescalation, use-of-force standards, and vehicle-stop protocols before being sent into communities with the authority to use deadly force.

DHS cannot allow officers whose backgrounds were never properly vetted, and who may never have received adequate use-of-force training, to remain on the streets with arrest authority and firearms. We therefore request that DHS:

Immediately suspend field enforcement duties for all ICE officers hired and deployed during the 2025 hiring surge, pending completion of full background revetting and use of-force retraining.

Provide a full accounting of how many current ICE officers received job offers or field assignments before completing fingerprint, identity, and credit checks, and how many of those officers have discharged a firearm in the course of duty.

Provide ICE’s plan to hire 5,000 employees by the end of 2026, including all documents, memoranda, internal communications, staffing assessments, and analyses of staffing needs related to the plan; the vetting and training protocols that will apply to the new hires; and the name and title of each official who approved the plan.

Provide a copy of the whistleblower’s complaint and any Office of Inspector General findings or corrective action plan arising from it.

Provide a detailed accounting of the use-of-force policy and vehicle-stop protocol changes DHS has made since January 2026, including how those changes have been implemented and audited across ICE field offices.

Finally, we are deeply concerned by indications that DHS and ICE leadership may not be taking whistleblower complaints seriously. ICE’s public response to this most recent whistleblower complaint focused on defending its vetting practices rather than addressing the substance of the allegations. Whistleblowers who come forward in good faith to report waste, fraud, abuse, or threats to public and national security are protected by federal law, and DHS has an obligation to ensure that employees who raise these concerns through proper channels are not retaliated against, sidelined, or pushed out of the agency. We therefore ask that DHS confirm, in writing, the specific steps it is taking to ensure that whistleblower complaints related to ICE hiring, vetting, and training are investigated promptly, that whistleblowers are protected from retaliation consistent with the Whistleblower Protection Act and related authorities, and that findings are shared with the appropriate oversight bodies, including Congress.

We request a written response to this letter, including responses to the items above, no later than October 13, 2026. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.

Sincerely,

title: Senate Passes Peters and Slotkin Legislation to Extend Federal Funding and Protections for the Great Lakes
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – The Senate unanimously passed legislation championed by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (MI) and Elissa Slotkin (MI) to protect the Great Lakes and vital waterways across Michigan. The legislation would extend the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI), authorizing $475 million in annual funding for the program through 2030. The GLRI combines federal and nonfederal efforts to stop the spread of invasive species, restore coastline and habitats connecting our streams and rivers, clean up environmentally damaged Areas of Concern, and prevent future contamination.

“The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative is the most significant investment ever made to restore and protect our Great Lakes from things like invasive species, pollution, and shoreline erosion,” said Senator Peters. “Now more than ever, we need to ensure this vital program has the funding it needs to continue supporting projects that will keep these treasured bodies of water healthy and vibrant for years to come. I’ll keep working in a bipartisan way to get this commonsense bill signed into law.”

“Millions of Michiganders rely on the Great Lakes for their livelihood and protecting it is existential for Michigan,” said Senator Slotkin. “The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative will help protect the lakes, our economy and our way of life – from vital programs that work to mitigate coastal erosion to protecting against harmful invasive species like Asian Carp. I will always fight for our Great Lakes and will continue to work with people in both parties to do just that.”

“The Great Lakes Commission applauds the Senate for advancing bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, a proven program that is delivering environmental and economic results for communities across the Great Lakes basin,” said Erika Jensen, Executive Director of the Great Lakes Commission. “Continued federal investment in the GLRI is essential to restoring degraded areas, protecting water quality, combating invasive species, and strengthening communities across the basin. We thank Senators Peters and Slotkin and their colleagues for their leadership and urge the House to move quickly to pass this critically important legislation."

“The GLRI is integral to the health of the Great Lakes and the 30 million people who depend on them for drinking water,” said Laura Rubin, Director of Healing Our Waters-Great Lakes Coalition. “Reauthorizing the GLRI is essential to maintaining the momentum we have built in restoring one of the nation’s most treasured natural resources, and we are grateful for the leadership of the Great Lakes delegation for advancing this legislation, preventing interruption to the GLRI’s vital work.”

Since its inception, the GLRI has spurred tremendous progress in Michigan and throughout the Great Lakes region, including nearly half of a million acres of habitat protected, restored, or enhanced, a five-fold increase in the successful cleanup and delisting of Areas of Concern, a ten-fold increase in the remediation of environmental and public health impairments, and reducing the threat of harmful algal blooms. The GLRI’s efforts have also resulted in economic returns of more than 3 to 1 across the region.

The senators’ legislation is supported by the League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, Sierra Club, National Parks Conservation Association, Council of Great Lakes Governors, Great Lakes Fishery Commission, American Great Lakes Ports Association, Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative, American Rivers, American Sportfishing Association, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership, Ducks Unlimited, Trout Unlimited, Congressional Sportsmen's Foundation, National Audubon Society - Great Lakes, Environmental Law & Policy Center, and other key stakeholders in Great Lakes protection.

Peters and Slotkin have been steadfast supporters of the Great Lakes, including by enacting the single-largest-ever investment in the GLRI through the bipartisan infrastructure law to accelerate the restoration of nine high-priority areas in Michigan whose lakes, rivers and watersheds flow into the Great Lakes.

title: Senator Peters Applauds United States Coast Guard Decision to Restore Full Operations & Staffing at USCG Station Saginaw River
text:
ESSEXVILLE, MI – U.S. Senator Gary Peters (MI) applauded the United States Coast Guard’s (USGC) decision to fully restore staffing and operations at USCG Station Saginaw River in Essexville:

“United States Coast Guard search and rescue units play a vital role in ensuring the safety of Michigan’s Great Lakes communities, and I’m thrilled that full operations are returning to Station Saginaw River in Essexville,” said Senator Peters. “Since operational changes were announced at Coast Guard stations across Michigan, I’ve raised the importance of these resources to communities and called on the Department of Homeland Security to address staffing shortages and restore operations. Thanks in part to this advocacy, Coast Guard recruitment is at record levels, leading to the return of full operations in Saginaw Bay. This announcement will improve the Coast Guard’s ability to respond to crises on the water, keeping Michiganders safe and secure. While this is a positive step forward, the job is not finished until full operations are restored at every impacted Coast Guard station in Michigan, and I’ll keep pushing until that happens.”

“We are very thankful that Senator Peters pushed for the return of staffing at the Saginaw River Station,” said Bay City Fire Chief Kurt Corradi. “The Coast Guard’s operational changes have put a strain on local emergency response teams, so the return to full staffing is welcome news for our partners across the Bay Region.”

Peters led the effort to reverse the previously announced staffing changes at USCG Stations throughout Michigan. In November 2025, he raised these concerns with Admiral Kevin E. Lunday, then-nominee to be Commandant of the USCG. In May of 2025, he called on the Trump Administration to prioritize funding for U.S. Coast Guard recruitment and retention. In a letter to Admiral Lunday, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought, and U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, Peters also outlined how critical Coast Guard operations have been disrupted as a result of personnel shortages and underscored that further investment is needed to support ongoing recruitment and retention efforts for the Great Lakes region to address these shortages.

title: In Case You Missed It… Sen. Rick Scott, Dr. Rebeccah Heinrichs in The Hill: “If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead.”
text:
NAPLES, Fla. – Last week, U.S. Senator Rick Scott and Dr. Rebeccah Heinrichs of the Hudson Institute published a joint op-ed in The Hill that discusses the numerous threats to America’s prosperity — and how to confront them.

In the op-ed, Senator Scott and Dr. Heinrichs argue that America is facing a growing list of threats from an “authoritarian alliance,” as China, Russia, North Korea, Iran and its proxies, and others consolidate power to steer the world away from the U.S.-led global order. The solution, they argue, is to recommit to American strength and leadership on the world stage.

Senator Scott and Dr. Heinrichs wrote, “Lately, a foolish worldview is growing in popularity among elected leaders in Washington. You hear it from voices ranging from Tucker Carlson to Hasan Piker. Some on the left and right have become convinced that solving America’s domestic issues requires our retreat from leadership on the world stage.”

…

“What the Tucker-Piker camp fails to understand is that America still has enemies. Communist China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba have created an anti-American coalition — an authoritarian alliance — to undercut us as the global superpower and sever the ties between the U.S. and the Western coalition.”

…

“If we retreat and allow this authoritarian alliance to take hold, America will suffer. Communist China and its accomplices will starve us, isolate us, and deprive us of every resource possible until America is weak and dependent. We will have no autonomy, no opportunity, and no freedom. Our financial markets will be powerless to fuel innovation, our business will shutter, and the American Dream will die.”

…

“We cannot sacrifice national and global security to a false dilemma of domestic versus overseas issues. It is not a zero-sum equation. To believe it would destroy a century of American greatness and the American Dream itself. Americans deserve a future that is safe, prosperous and free. For that to happen, America must lead.”

title: Rosen Calls Out Trump Admin for Shortchanging Rural Nevada Families on Home Loans

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff Highlights New Report Detailing Increased Offshoring of U.S. Film and TV Production, Need for Federal Film Tax Incentive
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) is highlighting a new study documenting increased offshoring of U.S. film and TV production over the past 25 years. The report highlights the need for Congress to pass Senator Tim Scott’s (R-S.C.) and Schiff’s Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act to create a federal film tax incentive to keep film and television production in the United States.

“The jobs in the film and TV industry are enormously important to our country and must stay here in the United States. This report demonstrates the urgent need to act and pass a federal film tax proposal to stop the exodus of production to other countries offering more competitive incentives. With the support of the President, and our strong bipartisan and bicameral coalition, our bill will help create hundreds of thousands of jobs across the nation and bring the movie magic back to America. Now is the time to get this done,” said Senator Schiff.

According to the report:

“The share of production spending by major U.S. studios on movies filmed partially or primarily in the U.S. declined from 74% to 42%.

The share of films by major U.S. studios on movies filmed partially or primarily in the U.S. declined from 66% to 54%.

For total cast and crew working on major studio films, the share of cast and crew working on movies filmed partially or primarily in the U.S. declined from 72% to 43%.

From 1999 to 2024, the share of production spending in the U.S. among the 25 highest-budget films by major U.S. studios declined by 40%.

The share of television production spending by major U.S. studios on television episodes filmed partially or primarily in the U.S. declined from 94% to 64%.”

Background: For years, Schiff has highlighted the need to increase film production in America and has continued to build bipartisan support in Congress for his federal film incentive proposal. During his time in the California State Senate, Schiff helped lead efforts to increase film production in California and protect local jobs.

As a member of the U.S. House of Representatives, Schiff spearheaded efforts in Congress to extend California’s film tax credit, including in 2014 when he led 28 members of the California Democratic delegation in urging the leaders of the California State Senate and Assembly to reauthorize and enhance the tax credit. In 2024, Schiff sent a letter to the Bureau of Economic Analysis and the Bureau of Labor Statistics requesting detailed data on the impact of foreign production incentives on the domestic industry.

In March 2026, Senator Adam Schiff hosted a spotlight hearing in Burbank, California to highlight the importance of bolstering American film production and tackling the challenges including generous tax incentives provided by other countries.

title: Shaheen Joins Effort to Expand Coverage of Birth Control as Trump Administration Continues Attacks on Contraception and Family Planning
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) helped introduce the bicameral Affordability is Access Act, which would require insurers to fully cover over-the-counter birth control without any fees or out-of-pocket costs, once it is Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved. The introduction comes as the Trump Administration continues its senseless attacks on reproductive care, family planning and contraception, including moves to cancel teen pregnancy prevention grants, attempts to decimate Title X and the U.S. State Department’s extremist decision to falsely label birth control products as abortifacients.

“As the Trump Administration continues its relentless efforts to strip women of our bodily autonomy and limit access to basic reproductive health care, we must do all we can to increase access to contraception and family planning methods,” said Senator Shaheen. “Our legislation would build on successful provisions in the Affordable Care Act that have made birth control more readily available by ensuring over-the-counter options are also available at no cost.”

Under the Affordable Care Act, all private health insurance plans are required to fully cover – without copays or out-of-pocket costs – prescribed FDA-approved, granted or cleared methods of contraception. The Affordability is Access Act would also maintain the FDA’s sole authority to determine the safety and efficacy of drugs and make them available over the counter without a prescription and ensure retailers provide contraception without a prescription. The legislation states that any retailer that stocks contraception that the FDA has approved, granted or cleared without a prescription may not interfere with a consumer’s access to or purchase of such contraception.

title: Warner Statement on the Appointment of Jay Clayton to Coordinate Federal AI Policy
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after President Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to serve in an additional role overseeing the administration’s artificial intelligence policy:

“Artificial intelligence is one of the defining national security challenges of our time, and I welcome the administration recognizing that this technology requires serious, sustained attention at the highest levels of government. But creating a new title is not a substitute for having a coherent strategy. So far, the administration has resisted meaningful safeguards without offering a serious alternative for addressing the national security risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems. We still do not know what authority this new role will have, whether it will include developing safety standards or reviewing the most advanced models, or how it fits into the administration’s broader approach to AI. That lack of clarity is especially concerning as leading AI companies themselves are confronting increasingly capable systems that can evade safeguards and exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

“There is real bipartisan interest in Congress in getting this right. I hope this appointment is an opportunity for the administration to move beyond slogans and toward a serious, coordinated national strategy for AI. As I have said repeatedly, that coordination must include the Intelligence Community, where some of our nation’s foremost technical experts on cyber reside. And as Vice Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, I look forward to working with Director Clayton on ensuring the United States stays ahead of China and other adversaries, strengthening the security and resilience of our most advanced AI systems, and establishing rigorous testing and safeguards so that increasingly powerful systems remain secure, reliable, and under human control. ”

Sen. Warner has been a leading voice in Congress on the national security, economic, and societal implications of artificial intelligence. Earlier this year, he unveiled A Framework for America’s AI Future, a comprehensive legislative agenda focused on AI safety and competition, national security, workforce disruption, and the infrastructure needed to power the technology. Most recently, Warner introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 with Sens. Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Andy Kim (D-NJ), legislation that would establish enforceable safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems, including pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity requirements, and mandatory reporting of serious AI safety and security incidents. Warner and his colleagues took to the Senate floor this week to seek unanimous consent to pass the legislation.

title: Warnock Statement on Reporting that Trump Admin Let Millions in Rural Housing Development Dollars Expire
text:
According to reporting by POLITICO, the Trump Administration refused to spend around $232 million in federal funding meant to help low-income families in rural communities

The funding officially expired last week

The funding was allocated by Congress to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans Program

In Georgia, rural communities received over $14 million less in mortgage assistance compared to the prior years’ average, a 68% decrease

Senator Reverend Warnock: “Time and time again the Trump administration shows its true colors. By denying money to Georgians who need it, the President demonstrates that he doesn’t care about rural and low-income families.”

Washington, D.C. – Today, Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) released the following statement after new reporting by POLITICO found that the Trump administration threw away more than $230 million in federal funding Congress already allocated to help low-income families in rural communities.

“Time and time again, the Trump administration shows its true colors. By denying money to Georgians who need it, the President demonstrates that he doesn’t care about rural and low-income families, rising housing costs, and the affordability crisis plaguing this country,” Senator Reverend Warnock said. “Housing provides dignity and security, particularly in rural communities. When this administration fails to do its job, it is hardworking Georgians in rural communities across our state who pay the price.”

Congress allocated the funding to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans Program. As of today, USDA has only used $518 million of the $1 billion in available funding for the program.

About $250 million of the unspent money will carry over to the next fiscal year, but roughly $232 million expired last week with the end of the fiscal year, preventing hundreds of families across Georgia and the country from getting the assistance they need. Each year, the program finances roughly 5,500 mortgages. The $230 million in funding could have helped approximately 850 rural households achieve homeownership across the country.

title: Rep. Young Kim Introduces Resolution Recognizing National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) introduced a resolution recognizing October 5th as National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day to raise awareness of these rare genetic disorders and recognize the patients and families impacted by them.

Peroxisomal disorders are estimated to affect roughly 1 in 50,000 births. These rare genetic conditions can affect nearly every system in the body, and severe forms are often terminal in childhood. Patients may experience hearing and vision loss, developmental delays, adrenal insufficiency, neurological complications, and feeding difficulties. There is currently no cure for peroxisomal disorders, and treatment options remain extremely limited.

For families, a diagnosis brings years of specialist visits, complex daily care, and financial and emotional strain, often with few answers along the way. For the Overly family of Lake Forest, this struggle is all too real. Brooke Overly’s daughter Melody was diagnosed with a Peroxisomal Disorder. Melody’s grandfather, Michael Curry, helped spearhead the effort to establish National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day.

“After meeting Melody and her mother Brooke, I saw firsthand the strength it takes for a family to face a rare diagnosis with so few answers,” said Rep. Young Kim. “No parent should have to navigate a devastating diagnosis with so little information available about specialists, treatments, or what comes next. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to raise awareness of peroxisomal disorders, recognize families like the Overlys, and bring greater attention to the need for better understanding, treatments, and ultimately a cure.”

title: Smith, Boyle Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect the Integrity of College Athletics
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE-03) and Brendan F. Boyle (D-PA-02), members of House Ways and Means Committee, introduced the Fair Play Enforcement Act, to protect the integrity of college athletics by holding colleges and universities accountable for fielding athletes who violate established standards of fair competition.

“College athletics have a long history of bringing people together, fostering competition, and teaching us what it means to represent something bigger than ourselves. Unfortunately, recent developments continue to put the values and traditions that make college sports unique at risk. I introduced my Fair Play Enforcement Act to ensure that colleges and universities uphold fair competition and preserve the values that have long defined college athletics for generations to come,” said Smith.

“College sports depend on honesty and fair play. Schools should not be fielding players who have bet on games or who have been on professional sports teams. Our commonsense legislation creates a financial consequence for schools that cross that line and helps protect the integrity of college athletics,” said Boyle.

BACKGROUND:

The Fair Play Enforcement Act holds colleges and universities accountable for fielding athletes who violate the standards of collegiate competition. The legislation would impose an excise tax penalty on a school that knowingly or reasonably should have known it was fielding a player in a sanctioned competition who:

Gambled on collegiate sports; or

Signed a contract with and was rostered by a professional sports team in the same sport in which the player subsequently competed at the collegiate level.

Excise Tax Penalty:

If a school is found in violation, the legislation would impose an excise tax based on a percentage of the institution’s total gross athletic revenue, including but not limited to ticket sales, media rights, conference and postseason distributions, sponsorships, licensing and merchandising, athletic donations, concessions, and other revenue attributable to the athletic program.

Safeguards:

Documented determination: Requires a final, documented determination from the appropriate governing body, such as the NCAA, that the player violated the applicable prohibition before a penalty may be imposed.

School knowledge: Applies only when a college or university knew or reasonably should have known that it was fielding a player who violated the applicable standard.

Judicial safe harbor: Provides a safe harbor when a court orders a school to roster or field a player who would otherwise be subject to the prohibition.

title: Barrett Continues Support for Workers, Small Businesses in Mid-Michigan
text:
Howell, Mich. — Today, Congressman Tom Barrett welcomed Administrator of the U.S. Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler and Administrator of the U.S. General Services Administration Ed Forst to Howell to highlight their efforts to support small businesses and workers.

Barrett, Loeffler, and Forst met with leadership and staff at Highland Engineering, a family-owned business that designs and builds critical equipment for the U.S. military. The visit showcased the important partnership between small businesses and the federal government, and the officials also discussed their work to lower taxes and foster an economy where workers and small businesses can succeed.

“At Highland Engineering and small businesses across mid-Michigan, people work hard to do their jobs and provide for their families,” said Barrett. “I’ve been leading the charge to build an economy where everyone can succeed, and that starts with lowering costs for families. We delivered no tax on overtime, no tax on tips, and other tax relief that has put more money back in people’s pockets — and there is a lot more to be done. Thank you to Administrator Loeffler and Administrator Forst for coming to Howell to see the good work happening here in our communities.”

“Michigan has long been at the heart of America’s industrial strength, and in visiting Highland Engineering today we saw that legacy in action,” said Loeffler. “New orders are fueling growth and more opportunities for its employees — a powerful example of what the America First economic agenda means for Michigan’s 7th Congressional District. Thanks to President Trump’s commitment to American industry and its workers, and with leadership from congressional leaders like Congressman Barrett, we are bringing vital industries home and restoring the jobs that sustain families and communities across the state.”

“Small businesses like Highland Engineering are the backbone of our economy and critical partners in strengthening our nation's industrial and defense capabilities,” said Forst. “In line with President Trump’s commitment to American manufacturing, GSA is opening doors for domestic innovators like Highland to win the federal contracts and secure opportunities necessary to put the American people and products first.”

Highland Engineering began in 1986 as a fixture and automation design firm serving the automotive industry and now is a leading defense contractor, providing the military with equipment for classified information facilities, water purification, electricity, medical care, cargo transportation, and more.

title: REP. BOEBERT: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY ORDER KEEPS CRAIG COAL UNIT OPEN
text:
LONE TREE — Rep. Lauren Boebert announced the Department of Energy order keeps Craig Station Unit 1 available and the jobs tied to that unit continue.

"Colorado families and businesses cannot afford to lose baseload power while demand keeps climbing,” Rep. Boebert said. “This order keeps Craig Unit 1 online through the end of the year so the grid has the coal generation it needs, and the jobs tied to the unit that remains open continue.”

Craig Station is a coal-fired power plant in Craig, Colorado, the county seat of Moffat County in the northwest corner of the state. It sits just outside town along the Yampa River. Several hundred jobs are connected to the plant and the mines that supply it.

Secretary Chris Wright issued the order under section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act, finding an emergency in the WECC–Rocky Mountain region from rising demand and a shortage of generation. The order directs Tri-State, the co-owners, and Southwest Power Pool to keep the 446-megawatt coal unit available through December 25, 2026, and to dispatch it only when needed to meet the emergency and limit costs to ratepayers.

Rep. Boebert will continue to work with Secretary Wright on what is best for the 4th District.

title: Buchanan Backs Bipartisan Bills to Help Kids Eat Better and Lead Healthier Lives
text:
Legislation Would Support Florida’s Specialty Crop Growers, Improve Student Nutrition and Tell Families Exactly What Their Children Are Eating

WASHINGTON— Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, announced he is cosponsoring two bills to improve the health of students across Florida: the Local Foods for Healthy Schools Act (H.R. 9474), bipartisan legislation introduced by Congressman Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (D-Mich.), as well as the Know What’s on the Tray Act (H.R. 9951), introduced by Congressman Tom Barrett (R-Mich.).

“A child who isn’t eating well can’t learn well,” said Congressman Buchanan. “Healthy kids become strong students, and strong students grow into the leaders our country will depend on. Children are 25% of our population, but 100% of our future, and these bills put fresh, local food in our schools and clear information in the hands of parents. That is an investment in the health of our children and grandchildren.”

The Local Foods for Healthy Schools Act would permanently reinstate and modernize USDA’s Local Food for Schools program, which USDA ended in 2025. This program would once again connect local producers and school districts, opening new opportunities for farmers while providing healthy, nutrient-rich meals to students.

The Know What’s on the Tray Act would require schools in the National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program to post information about every menu item on their school or district website at least seven days before the meal is served. The information would include its ingredients, the manufacturer or producer, where it was made and whether it was locally sourced or produced on a family farm. The bill would give families more insight into what their children eat and encourage healthier school meals.

Diet-related disease is one of the largest drivers of health care costs in America, and habits formed in childhood often last a lifetime. By connecting schools with nearby farms and giving families clear information about school meals, these bills invest in students’ health and classroom success while supporting local farmers. As Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, Buchanan has made prevention a priority, including bipartisan legislation he introduced to help veterans manage chronic disease through nutrition.

title: Bynum Secures Over One Million for Scio Rural Fire
text:
Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) announced that the Scio Rural Fire Protection District has received a $1.19 million federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to support firefighter safety and fire prevention. Congresswoman Bynum advocated for the funding by writing a letter to FEMA in support of Scio Rural Fire’s grant application.

“When you call 911, you shouldn’t have to wonder if there are enough firefighters to answer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This $1.19 million is a big deal for Scio, Jefferson, and the communities they serve. It means more support for the people running toward emergencies and a stronger response when our neighbors need help most. This is exactly what bringing federal dollars home should look like.”

"These grants are a significant opportunity and an important first step in building the capacity our Fire & Life Safety Division needs," said Albany Fire Chief Chris LaBelle. "A community our size, with the growth and unique industries we have, requires a more proactive approach to risk reduction. This position moves us in that direction and supports our mission to Prevent and Protect from Harm."

"Redmond Fire & Rescue would like to thank Senators Merkley and Wyden and Congresswoman Bynum for their support,” said Redmond Fire Chief Ryan Herrera. "With members of our organization having navigated a past cancer diagnosis, and with the recent passing of Firefighter/Paramedic Michael Kienzle from a Line-of-Duty cancer, this funding marks another meaningful step forward in our commitment to carcinogen reduction and improving the long-term health and safety of our firefighters."

"As costs continue to rise faster than available revenue, small fire districts like ours face difficult choices about how to best use limited resources. Recruiting, training, and retaining volunteer firefighters can too often be delayed as we focus on meeting the immediate costs of providing emergency services,” said Scio Fire Chief Kevin White. "This grant is an important investment in the future of our department and our community. It will strengthen our efforts to recruit and retain volunteers, grow our membership, and ensure we have the people and resources needed to provide the high-quality emergency services our community depends on. We are grateful for this support and the opportunity to build a stronger, more sustainable fire department."

FEMA awarded the funding through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant Program, which helps fire departments hire additional firefighters and strengthen recruitment and retention efforts.

FEMA also issued funding under the SAFER Grant Program to the following areas:

More than $2.3 million to Boise Fire Department in Boise, Idaho

More than $1.7 million to South Kitsap Fire and Rescue in Port Orchard, Washington.

More than $1.7 million to Spokane County Fire District 9 in Mead, Washington.

More than $1.1 million to Umatilla Rural Fire Protection District in Umatilla, Oregon.

$1 million to North Whidbey Fire and Rescue in Oak Harbor, Washington.

title: Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, Huffman Lead Colleagues in Urging Removal of Hunt Amendment from Annual Defense Bill
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and House Natural Resources Committee top Democrat Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), led 30 of their colleagues in calling on House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to reject the Hunt Amendment’s provision (Section 2835) in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which would grant unprecedented eminent domain authority to the federal government to benefit Sable Offshore Corporation.

“The NDAA has long served as a bipartisan vehicle to strengthen our national security and support our servicemembers. However, we are deeply concerned by the inclusion of Section 2835, which would grant extraordinary eminent domain authority to the federal government to circumvent established environmental protections for the benefit of a single private company. Given the sweeping implications of this provision, we believe this policy rider does not belong in the NDAA and, therefore, should be removed from the final conference agreement,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers explain how this provision would jeopardize the California coastal economy and do little to strengthen our nation’s energy security.

“California’s coastal economy supports roughly 511,000 jobs and generates over $51.3 billion in GDP from marine-economy activities — largely in tourism and recreation. Another oil spill from a corrosion-prone pipeline that has spilled before would jeopardize the economic security of everyday Americans that rely on our coastal economy for their livelihoods,” the lawmakers continued. “In addition, there is no evidence that this provision would meaningfully advance our nation's energy security. Recent spikes in gasoline prices driven by market uncertainty surrounding the war in Iran underscore that global oil markets—not a single offshore project—continue to dictate prices at the pump.”

The letter goes on to highlight the unprecedented nature of Section 2835, which would grant the federal government extraordinary powers to seize property for the sole benefit of a single private organization.

“The NDAA should not be used to circumvent established permitting processes or create special authorities for individual projects that have failed to secure the approvals required under existing law. The federal government's power of eminent domain is among its most significant authorities and should be exercised only when there is a clear and compelling public purpose—not to resolve private infrastructure disputes or increase the profitability of a single company—at the expense of communities who have to live with the consequences of an oil spill,” said the lawmakers.

The full letter is available HERE.

Joining Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, and Huffman the letter is co-signed by U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Mike Thompson (D-CA-04), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA-11), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Derek Tran (D-CA-45), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Juan Vargas (D-CA-52), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15), Mark Takano (D-CA-39), Ami Bera, M.D. (D-CA-06), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Pete Aguilar (D-CA-33), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), George Whitesides (D-CA-27), Luz Rivas (D-CA-29), and Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51).

Background

Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations.

Carbajal has been a leader in opposing the Sable pipeline’s forced restart.

In September 2026, Carbajal led a bicameral group of colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast. The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority.

In July 2026, Carbajal spoke on the House floor against the NDAA’s Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.

title: Rep. Carson Seeks Answers on Canceled Naturalization Ceremonies
text:
WASHINGTON, DC—This week, Congressman André Carson (IN-07) led 26 Members of Congress in seeking answers from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) about repeated cancelations of naturalization ceremonies.

In Indianapolis, USCIS canceled at least three naturalization ceremonies since July, citing a “lack of candidates.” But field offices report they have pending naturalization applications that are awaiting action from USCIS.

“Citizenship is a life-changing milestone, and people who have spent years following the law deserve a government that honors its commitments,” said Rep. Carson. “Canceling naturalization ceremonies without a clear explanation leaves families in Indianapolis in limbo and undermines trust in the process. These families deserve more than canceled ceremonies and unanswered questions. USCIS must explain these cancellations and ensure eligible applicants can take their oath without unreasonable delay. I will keep pressing this administration for answers and accountability.”

“We are concerned that lawful permanent residents are experiencing delays in the final stages of their naturalization across the country,” the lawmakers state in the letter. “Applicants who have spent years complying with immigration requirements should not face unexplained or unreasonable delays after becoming eligible for citizenship because of the political or ideological whims of a particular administration. These delays prevent lawful permanent residents from fully exercising the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, including voting, obtaining a U.S. passport, pursuing certain employment opportunities, and petitioning for family members. Congress has made it clear that the fair and timely processing of eligible citizenship applicants is a priority.”

Rep. Carson and his colleagues requested a response from USCIS by October 7, 2026, including the number of pending naturalization applications, how long those applications have been pending, and how many applicants have completed naturalization interviews but are still awaiting final decisions.

The full letter is HERE.

title: Castro Challenges Trump To Visit Dilley Trailer Prison During San Antonio Visit
text:
SAN ANTONIO, TX —Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) renewed his invitation to President Donald Trump to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison during his visit tomorrow in San Antonio, Texas.

“Donald Trump will be in San Antonio tomorrow. I invite him to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison and see for himself the trauma he is inflicting on children and babies, some as young as two months old.”

Castro first challenged the President to see firsthand the conditions facing children at the only family detention center in the country at a march protesting ICE’s proposed detention center in San Antonio. Transcript below:

“President Trump, you're coming to San Antonio. I would invite you to go to Dilley to see what Stephen Miller, who sits with you at the White House, has done to these children. To see the lifelong lasting trauma he's caused to these kids, to see what he's doing in the name of Americans. And I would say, because I would bet that the President has never been into a detention center, that he's certainly not been into a detention center, this trailer prison, where kids are held. Let me say this: the President of the United States is the leader of the country, the leader of the free world. If you can't stand there and go inside and look into the eyes of these kids and tell them that despite the fact they've done nothing wrong, that they belong there just because of where they were born, just because of the color of their skin, just because of the language that they speak, then you don't deserve to be President of the United States.”

“Presidente Trump, vas a venir a San Antonio. Yo te invito a ir a Dilley para ver lo que Stephen Miller, que se sienta contigo en la Casa Blanca, les ha hecho a estos niños. Para ver el trauma duradero que les ha causado a estosniños, para ver lo que está haciendo en nombre de Estados Unidos. Y yo diría esto, porque apostaría a que el presidente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención. Que ciertamente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención, esta prisión de tráileres, donde tienen detenidos a niños. Déjenme decir esto: el Presidente de los Estados Unidos es el líder del país, el líder del mundo libre. Si no puedes estar ahí, entrar y mirar a estos niños a losojos y decirles que, a pesar de que no han hecho nada malo, pertenecen allí simplemente por el lugar donde nacieron, simplemente por el color de su piel, simplemente por el idioma que hablan, entonces no mereces ser Presidente de los Estados Unidos.”

title: Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.

Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most watched and financially successful productions.

El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.

“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country," said Congressman Castro. "Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”

“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”

“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”

“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”

“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen," said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. "Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”

“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”

“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”

Read the full text of the resolution here.

title: Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Chair Emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), CAPAC Chair Grace Meng (NY-06), Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) Chair Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) Chair Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), and Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. opposing HHS’s proposed Head Start rule which would mandate English-only instruction and eliminate longstanding language-access protections for children and families.

Head Start is a critical program that provides high-quality early childhood education and comprehensive support services for low-income children and their families. While the Members urge HHS to withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety, their letter focuses specifically on its harmful changes to language-access protections. Nearly 40 percent of children enrolled in Head Start are dual-language learners, representing almost 290,000 children nationwide, and 30 percent of enrollees come from families whose primary home language is not English.

In the letter, the Members explain that dual-language instruction helps children learn English and prepare for school:

“We share the goal of ensuring that every Head Start child develops strong English-language skills. But requiring English-only instruction is not supported by the evidence and risks undermining that very goal. For many children, Head Start is their first experience in a classroom. Providing an environment in which young children can understand, communicate, and participate supports their ability to learn and successfully transition into school.

The Members also warn that the proposed rule conflicts with Congress’s explicit directives in the Head Start Act:

“Congress directed the Secretary to establish standards ensuring that children with limited English proficiency make progress toward acquiring English while simultaneously making meaningful progress in other developmental domains, including through “culturally and linguistically appropriate instructional services” (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(a)(1)(B)(x)). Congress further directed the Secretary, when revising Head Start standards, to ensure that revisions do not eliminate or reduce the quality, scope, or types of educational, parental-involvement, health, or other services required under longstanding Head Start standards (42 U.S.C. § 9836a(a)(2)(C)). And the Head Start Act explicitly requires agencies to ensure teachers receive literacy training “in methods to promote vocabulary development and phonological awareness (including phonemic awareness) in a developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate manner and support children’s development in their native language” (42 U.S. Code § 9843(d)(2)(B)). Eliminating longstanding language-access protections appears directly at odds with these congressional directives, and the Department has not adequately explained how its proposal can be reconciled with them.”

The Members detail how eliminating bilingual staffing requirements could undermine parents’ ability to participate in their children’s education and jeopardize accurate developmental screenings and assessments:

“Congress recognized that informed and engaged parents are essential to children’s success and required Head Start programs to conduct family needs assessments and communicate with parents, to the extent practicable, in a language they understand (42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(J)(vii); 42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(K); 42 U.S. Code § 9836a(f)(2)). Eliminating language-access staffing requirements without providing an adequate alternative could make it more difficult for parents to understand their children’s progress, participate in their education, communicate with teachers and staff, and access the comprehensive services Head Start provides.

We are particularly concerned about the consequences for developmental screenings and assessments. The Head Start Act requires measures used by Head Start programs to be developmentally, linguistically, and culturally appropriate; valid and reliable in the language in which they are administered; administered by appropriately trained staff; and accompanied by appropriate accommodations for children with limited English proficiency (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(b)(2)). These protections are critical. A screening or assessment administered in a language a young child does not sufficiently understand risks mistaking normal second-language development for a developmental delay or, conversely, failing to identify a genuine disability or developmental concern. Either outcome could delay appropriate early intervention at precisely the age when it can make the greatest difference.”

Finally, the Members warn that the proposal would impose significant disruption and costs on Head Start providers while weakening services for hundreds of thousands of children:

“The scale of the disruption caused by the proposed rule’s language-access changes would be substantial. Almost 290,000 dual-language learners nationwide could be affected […] Although the proposal is titled Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs, affected programs could be forced to change curricula, replace classroom materials, and retrain or replace teachers, resulting in an estimated $99 million in costs.”

“HHS should not reverse decades of evidence-based practice, impose new costs on providers, and weaken language-access protections for hundreds of thousands of children without a compelling evidentiary or legal basis for doing so. Accordingly, we strongly urge HHS to withdraw the proposed English-only instruction requirement and retain the longstanding language-access protections that allow Head Start programs to effectively serve dual-language learners and their families. Congress expressly directed Head Start to support English-language acquisition through culturally and linguistically appropriate services, and HHS should uphold, not undermine, that mandate.”

title: García, Colleagues Issue Joint Statement Condemning Israel’s Persecution of Palestinian Healthcare Workers
text:
CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), along with Congressmembers Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), and Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) released a joint statement condemning the Israeli government’s systematic persecution of Palestinian healthcare workers, and called for their immediate release from arbitrary detention.

“Over the last three years, the Israeli government has systematically destroyed the health system in Palestine, murdering at least 1,700 Palestinian doctors, nurses, paramedics, and other healthcare workers and destroying dozens of hospitals. It has arrested and arbitrarily detained hundreds of Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 16 physicians who continue to be held in inhumane conditions. Among them is Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, whom the Israeli government has arbitrarily detained since 2024 and tortured to the point of near-death after previously murdering his son and brutally attacking his hospital,” said the Members.

“Israel’s systematic annihilation of medical facilities and healthcare workers is not an accident or unfortunate consequence of war; it is an intentional policy designed to further occupation, apartheid, and genocide against the Palestinian people. We demand the immediate release of Dr. Abu Safiya and all other arbitrarily detained healthcare workers and Palestinian prisoners. And we demand an end to U.S. arms transfers to Israel, including the Trump Administration’s latest $2.8 billion sale of bombs. Congress must block this sale and pass the Block the Bombs Act to finally end our government’s shameful complicity in Israel’s mass atrocities.”

Congressman García also recently led a letter condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank, and called for the release of Marwan Barghouti who has been detained and tortured in Israeli prison for over 20 years.

title: Ciscomani Highlights $6.3 Million in Federal Investments for Graham County
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani toured four Community Project Funding sites in Graham County, highlighting the $6.3 million in preliminary federal funding he has secured to support infrastructure, healthcare, roads, and teacher housing across Thatcher, Safford, and the greater Graham County area.

"These $6.3 million in preliminary investments across four projects will deliver lasting improvements for communities across Graham County," said Representative Ciscomani. "From improving essential roads and modernizing the courthouse to expanding access to healthcare and supporting teacher housing, these projects address real needs identified by local leaders. As Arizona’s sole appropriator, I am committed to bringing federal resources home, moving these projects forward, and delivering results that matter for Graham County families."

The funding was awarded through the highly competitive Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations process. Graham County’s four projects stood out among more than 70 applications submitted to Ciscomani’s office and will support key priorities across the community:

$3 million will support the reconstruction and widening of 1st Avenue Road in Thatcher, improving a critical local roadway and making travel safer and more efficient for residents, businesses, and the surrounding community.

$2 million will support modernization and improvements to the Graham County Courthouse in Safford, helping upgrade a critical public facility and ensure it can continue meeting the needs of Graham County residents.

$650,000 will help Mt. Graham Regional Medical Center purchase a new mammography unit, bringing advanced breast cancer screening and diagnostic services closer to home and reducing the need for local patients to travel outside the community for care.

$650,000 will support teacher housing at Fort Thomas Unified School District, helping provide more affordable housing options for educators and strengthening the district’s ability to recruit and retain teachers in the community.

Thatcher Mayor Jenny Howard praised Ciscomani’s advocacy and commitment to the community.

"He gets rural," said Thatcher Mayor Jenny Howard. "He gets the state, he gets this district, but he gets rural; he knows we struggle."

​Howard continued:

"The Town of Thatcher is incredibly grateful for Representative Ciscomani’s leadership and advocacy as he works to secure this $3 million investment for our community. We were proud to host him yesterday and show him firsthand why this project is so important to Thatcher and the surrounding region. This investment would be a game changer for our community and will truly have a lasting impact. We appreciate Representative Ciscomani’s commitment to seeing this project through and bringing this critical investment home to Southern Arizona. This is the kind of investment that will make a real difference for our community for years to come."

These investments build on more than $60 million in Community Project Funding Ciscomani has delivered for Arizona in Fiscal Years 2024 and 2026, including $5.5 million for Graham County.

Previous Graham County projects include:

$2 million for a new Pima Fire Station

$1.3 million for the Graham County Gila River Linear Park

$1.2 million for new waterlines at the Graham County Fairgrounds

$1 million for a new road to Pima High School

This $6.3 million investment for Graham County is a testament to Representative Ciscomani’s commitment to delivering for rural Arizona. This year, he has preliminarily secured funding for 20 projects totaling $42.7 million, bringing critical resources back home to Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District. As Arizona’s sole member of the House Appropriations Committee, Ciscomani’s efforts ensure stronger communities, better infrastructure, and a brighter future for families across the region.

For coverage on Ciscomani’s visits, HERE and HERE.

“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”

Read the full text of the resolution here

Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.
