title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna Re-Presents Legion of Merit to Captain Stanley Beach
text:
Washington, D.C. — On Monday, Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) formally re-presented the Legion of Merit to retired U.S. Navy Captain Stanley Beach after helping correct his military record to officially reflect the award he received upon his retirement from the Navy in 1987.

Captain Beach served 30 years in the Navy, including 27 years in the Chaplain Corps and service alongside Marines in Vietnam. His distinguished career earned him recognition as a “living legend” within the Chaplain Corps. Decades after his retirement, he discovered that the Legion of Merit had never been recorded on his DD-214. Rep. Luna worked with the Department of the Navy to correct his record and secure a DD-215 formally adding the award.

“Captain Beach spent nearly three decades serving our country, and his military record should reflect every honor he earned,” said Rep. Luna. “Correcting this decades-old omission is the least our nation owes him for his service and sacrifice, and I am grateful my office could help make it happen.”

Captain Beach’s son, Police Chief Randall Beach, hosted the ceremony and credited Rep. Luna and her office with helping resolve the issue on his father’s behalf. “What really made this happen was the leadership of Representative Anna Paulina Luna and her staff,” said Beach. “You cannot do this without Congress. It matters!”

A DD-214 is the primary separation document issued to service members and records key details of their military service, including decorations and awards. A DD-215, formally known as a Correction to DD Form 214, is issued when information on that original separation record must later be corrected or added. Unlike the DD-214, it is not routinely issued to veterans, making it a comparatively uncommon document that reflects a formal amendment to an existing military record.

Captain Beach enlisted as a Sailor in 1953 and entered the Chaplain Corps in 1960. After volunteering to serve with Marines in Vietnam, he joined the 3rd Marine Division and later served with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines at Phu Bai and during intense fighting at Mutter’s Ridge. While under enemy fire, Beach ministered to wounded Marines and carried them to aid stations before sustaining severe injuries to his leg and stomach that required his own evacuation.

For his actions in Vietnam, Beach received the Bronze Star with Valor, the Purple Heart, and the Navy Commendation Medal with Combat “V.” He later served as Director of the Navy Chaplains School and received the David E. White Leadership Award in 2007. In 2012, and the Naval Chaplaincy School and Center named its building Stanley J. Beach Hall in recognition of his heroic service with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines during the Vietnam War.

Rep. Luna re-presented the Legion of Merit to Captain Beach at Freedom Square in Seminole alongside local officials and members of the community.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Celebrates Groundbreaking For New Beaufort County VA Clinic
text:
PORT ROYAL, S.C. (Oct. 6, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace marked an important milestone for Lowcountry veterans with the groundbreaking of the new Department of Veterans Affairs Community-Based Outpatient Clinic in Beaufort County. As a member of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, Rep. Mace supported a $30.4 million authorization for the facility to deliver Lowcountry veterans timely, high-quality care close to home.

"This groundbreaking is more than the start of a construction project. It is a promise to our veterans," said Congresswoman Mace. "For years, veterans across the Lowcountry have waited for better access to care. Now, a facility built just for them is finally on the way. Nearly 17,000 veterans call Beaufort County home, and they deserve first-class healthcare close to home. Not long drives. Not red tape. Not bureaucratic delays."

The clinic, located at 1844 Ribaut Road in Port Royal near Parris Island and MCAS Beaufort, will expand access to primary care, mental health services, specialty care, and other critical VA programs. The project will also create construction and healthcare jobs across the Lowcountry.

"Our obligation to support our servicemembers does not end once their military service does," Mace added. "Our responsibility continues long after every uniform comes off. We will keep working until every veteran receives the care they earned. Washington should deliver results, not excuses."

The clinic is expected to open in 2028 and represents a major investment in improving healthcare access for veterans across South Carolina's First Congressional District.

title: Congressman McCormick Calls on Trump Administration to Investigate Suspected H-1B Visa Fraud in North Metro Atlanta
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) sent a letter to Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling, and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin calling on the Trump Administration to investigate suspected H-1B visa fraud and abuse in and around Georgia’s 7th Congressional District.

Fox News Digital first reported on McCormick’s letter and concerns surrounding suspected H-1B fraud in North Metro Atlanta. Read the story HERE.

Following reports from constituents, stakeholder engagement, and recent federal investigation and enforcement activity targeting entities in and around GA-07, McCormick is urging the Administration to focus federal resources on allegations of fraud and abuse in North Metro Atlanta.

“In America, we don’t tolerate illegal immigrants unlawfully crossing our border, and we shouldn’t tolerate bad actors who profit from manipulating and abusing our legal immigration system, particularly through programs like the H-1B visa,” said Congressman McCormick. “This fraud hurts American workers and American wages, erodes the public’s trust in our immigration laws, and insults legal immigrants who come to our country the right way. I am asking the Trump Administration to take a hard look at what is happening in and around my congressional district and hold accountable anyone found to be gaming the system.”

In the letter, McCormick highlights concerns that bad actors are using fraudulent or abusive practices to obtain below-market labor, increase competition for American jobseekers, and subject H-1B holder employees to exploitation and abusive working conditions.

McCormick specifically requested that the Departments of Homeland Security, Labor, State, and other relevant federal agencies focus investigative and enforcement resources on allegations of H-1B fraud and abuse in and around GA-07. The Congressman also offered to work with the Administration on any legislation necessary to strengthen federal enforcement efforts and to help facilitate cooperation with Georgia agencies and law enforcement.

title: Chairman Meuser Releases Staff Report on Public Housing Agency Failures
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09), Chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and Congressman French Hill (AR-02), Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, released a staff report examining Public Housing Agencies (PHAs) nationwide.

This report is the culmination of a year-long Subcommittee-led investigation into serious mismanagement of PHAs across the country. On February 9, 2026, Chairman Meuser, Chairman Hill, and Congressman Mike Flood (NE-01), Chairman of the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance, sent letters to 32 PHAs designated by HUD as “troubled,” seeking information on living conditions, management, and financial oversight. This was followed by an Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing examining management failures at PHAs and ways to improve conditions for residents. During the hearing, witnesses outlined severe shortcomings at PHAs due to mismanagement from previous administrations and discussed best practices for reversing the trend.

On March 13, 2026, Chairman Meuser held a Subcommittee field hearing in Little Rock, Arkansas, focused on failures at the city’s PHA—the Metropolitan Housing Alliance (MHA)—and its impact on residents. Committee leadership also sent a letter to the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas urging an investigation into MHA.

Federal law requires PHAs to provide housing that is decent, safe, and sanitary. However, the Subcommittee’s investigation found that many troubled PHAs failed to meet these requirements due to management issues and oversight problems, resulting in significant waste of taxpayer resources and poor living conditions.

The Housing Authority of Champaign County is a good example of a PHA that has implemented commonsense Trump Administration policies, such as Moving to Work (MTW) requirements and voluntary time limits, that strengthen public housing standards and promote solutions that improve financial management.

“For years, the Biden Administration allowed PHAs to fail without proper support or oversight. Mismanagement and a lack of accountability in PHAs have wasted taxpayer dollars meant to support our most vulnerable citizens and led to unacceptable living conditions,” said Subcommittee Chairman Meuser. “This report shows that taxpayers and residents pay the price when leadership at PHAs falls short. Democrat administrations allowed this problem to fester for far too long. I appreciate Chairman Hill’s leadership, as well as President Trump and HUD Secretary Turner for their efforts to enhance federal support for public housing and demand greater accountability. This report supports and builds on that work to ensure that taxpayer-funded resources are well managed, and that Americans in need can benefit from decent, safe, and sanitary housing. I look forward to implementing our report’s recommendations and providing these crucial reforms to America’s most vulnerable citizens.”

“Americans living in federally supported housing deserve access to housing that is safe, clean, and livable,” said Chairman Hill. “PHAs exist to deliver on that promise. Unfortunately, as we've seen firsthand in my hometown of Little Rock, too many PHAs are failing the tenants who rely on them and the taxpayers who are footing the bill. I thank Subcommittee Chairman Meuser for his work holding PHAs accountable, protecting tenants, and for advocating for responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars.”

“PHA accountability and addressing waste, fraud, and abuse are key priorities for President Trump, Secretary Turner, and myself. At HUD, we are committed to restoring compliance and operational integrity. Our residents need it, and taxpayers expect it. HUD will continue working with Chairman Hill and Congress to ensure America’s public housing authorities are providing quality housing to America’s most vulnerable,” said HUD Assistant Secretary for Public and Indian Housing Ben Hobbs.

Key Findings:

PHA Leadership: Frequently, PHA Boards lack sufficient understanding of housing programs to effectively manage the PHA.

HUD’s Assessment Systems Disincentivize Rent Collection: HUD’s assessment system awards up to 16 points for occupancy but only 6 for rent collection, so a PHA that collects no rent can still pass HUD’s operations assessment.

Between 15 and 30 percent of residents at struggling PHAs pay only the minimum rent. The COVID-era eviction moratoriums caused unpaid rent to rise sharply.

Data and Due Diligence Issues: Troubled PHAs have insufficient data retention and due diligence standards across their operations, but particularly as it relates to their contracting and procurement standards.

PHAs struggle to find staff: PHAs struggle to find staff with sufficient experience and understanding of their roles and responsibilities. PHAs have particularly struggled to hire and retain maintenance staff, who can often find higher pay and more flexibility as independent contractors.

What HUD is Doing:

Proposed rule allowing work requirements and time limits: PHAs could opt in to work requirements of up to 40 hours a week and time limits of two years or more for work-capable adults. The comment period has closed, but the rule isn't final yet.

Reformed NSPIRE Inspections: HUD retrained inspectors, issued more guidance, improved its online inspection systems, and reorganized how inspectors are assigned to cut costs. It set February 1, 2027, for full implementation of these new standards.

More Inspections: HUD did 25 percent more inspections in 2025 than in 2024, and PHAs say inspections have become more consistent.

Took steps on safety: HUD launched a national public housing crime hotline, required stricter background checks for applicants, and rescinded guidance that had allowed people with criminal records to live in Section 9 housing.

Key Report Recommendations:

PHAs should develop systems and policies to enhance oversight of employees and contractors.

PHAs should conduct self-inspections at least quarterly and require before-and-after photos of maintenance work. They should also digitize their records, strengthen oversight of staff and contractors, and better enforce rent collection.

HUD and Congress should set baseline qualifications for PHA board members and executives and give HUD the authority to remove poor leaders.

Congress should consider legislation that permanently allows for and encourages PHAs to implement time limits and work requirements on public housing assistance for able-bodied adult residents.

title: Dr. Miller-Meeks Joins Iowa Delegation in Push for More Rural Health Care Funding
text:
IOWA – Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, M.D. (IA-01) joined the Iowa congressional delegation in urging Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz to support Iowa’s latest funding request through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), known as Healthy Hometowns. The program, created through the Working Families Tax Cuts law, has already delivered $209 million to strengthen rural health care across Iowa in its first year.

“Iowa’s rural communities deserve access to high-quality health care close to home, and we are already seeing these investments make a difference,” said Dr. Miller-Meeks. “As a doctor and a representative of rural Iowa, I will continue fighting to bring more resources home, strengthen our rural health care workforce, and make sure Iowans can get the care they need without having to travel hours from home.”

In addition to Miller-Meeks, the letter was signed by U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA), U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst (R-IA) and U.S. Reps. Ashley Hinson (IA-02), Zach Nunn (IA-03) and Randy Feenstra (IA-04).

“In January, Iowa became the first state in the nation to award Rural Health Transformation Program funding as part of its Healthy Hometowns initiative, and it has ensured resources are going directly to rural communities, not bureaucrats. In year one of the program, Iowa’s $209 million federal investment is improving cancer prevention and treatment, workforce recruitment and retention, chronic disease care, and maternal and child health,” the members wrote.

“As we each travel throughout Iowa, visiting hospitals, health centers, clinics, and more, we witness firsthand how these investments are making a difference toward the health, well-being, and quality of life in rural communities. During your visit to the University of Iowa in May, you learned how our state is using telehealth and a hub-and-spoke model to increase access to care and improve health outcomes in our rural communities,” the members continued.

The members noted how communities across Iowa are already benefiting from these federal investments, including through the following six projects:

Mahaska Health in Oskaloosa is purchasing a new PET/CT system with cardiac imaging capability and recruiting an OB/GYN and a general surgeon physician assistant.

Washington County Hospital in Washington is purchasing a new CT scanner that is improving diagnostic capabilities and patient outcomes.

Lucas County HealthCenter in Chariton is purchasing its first-ever MRI machine to bring early detection cancer screenings to residents.

North Iowa Medical Center in Mason City is purchasing a new robotic bronchoscopy system that detects lung cancer earlier than previously possible.

Sioux Center Health in Sioux Center is expanding prenatal care through a new regional maternal health coordinator.

Wayne County Hospital in Corydon is standing up a radiation oncology center and will be serving as a combat cancer health hub.

Background

Dr. Miller-Meeks has been a strong advocate for expanding access to health care in rural Iowa. She has held three roundtables focused on the Rural Health Transformation Program, bringing together Iowa health care providers and stakeholders to discuss how the program can strengthen rural health care and expand access.

Miller-Meeks also raised the need for additional rural health resources directly with CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz during his visit to Iowa. Iowa’s timely and proactive implementation of its Rural Health Transformation Program could position the state to receive additional funding if other states do not utilize their available resources.

title: Neal, Wyden Object to Treasury’s Proposed Boost for Private School Tax Credits
text:
WASHINGTON, DC— House Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) today objected to the Treasury Department’s recently issued proposed regulations on new Internal Revenue Code section 25F that further Republican attempts to undermine public school systems by directing taxpayer money toward private and religious schools.

In a letter to Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, Ranking Members Neal and Wyden called out the Administration’s actions as a blatant attempt to circumvent the clear rules established by Congress to funnel even more taxpayer funds away from public education and use it to subsidize the private school education of children from wealthy families. Treasury’s baseless interpretation of federal statute would allow married couples filing jointly to potentially claim double the credit that is authorized under the law.

“This interpretation is wildly inconsistent with the longstanding treatment of other provisions that use identical or near-identical language,” Neal and Wyden wrote. “This throws doubt upon Treasury’s interpretation of many provisions of the Code, creates a great deal of uncertainty in the administration of our tax laws, and could balloon the deficit,” Neal and Wyden noted, adding that it could increase the cost of the credit by an additional $150 billion over the next decade.

The Democratic Committee leaders closed by demanding the Administration provide written answers and explanations to how the new interpretation of the law will impact taxpayers, how it came to be and was coordinated internally, which other tax provisions taxpayers might take a return position that is different from previously listed guidance based on new interpretations, and other pressing matters.

Read the full letter to Secretary Bessent HERE.

title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Urges HUD to Implement Whole Home Repairs Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) joined U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) and U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) in a letter to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner urging an establishment of a Whole Home Repairs program through the Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.

The Members wrote:

“Almost 7 million Americans live in homes that are in need of significant repair, with deficiencies including leaky roofs, faulty wiring, and mold. This is an issue that disproportionately affects America’s seniors, many of whom would like to downsize but do not want to sell the home at a steep discount due to the updates required. As we saw in Commonwealth of Pennsylvania’s successful Whole Home Repairs program, providing grants for repairs allowed seniors to sell larger homes to growing families.”

The Whole-Home Repairs Act was signed into law with the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The Whole Home Repairs pilot program will provide renovation and repair grants to homeowners and small landlords. This will help ensure America’s aging homes do not fall out of the housing supply.

The Members continued:

“The language in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act authorizes you to operate a Whole Home Repairs program through 2031. We want to show the nation that repairing America’s crumbling homes is not a red or blue issue. Creating greater access to housing is an American issue. Any delays will mean millions of American families may never realize the benefit of this program. We were proud to help the Whole Home Repairs bill become law, and we stand ready to support you in making it a reality for Americans.”

title: Nunn, Iowa Delegation Push for Continued Rural Health Care Investment
text:
DES MOINES, IA — Representative Zach Nunn (IA-03) joined Iowa’s congressional delegation in urging the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to fully consider Iowa’s request for a second year of Rural Health Transformation Funding. This new phase of funding would build on the initial $209 million awarded in 2026 to strengthen rural healthcare statewide.

“Where you live shouldn’t determine whether you can get the health care you need,” said Rep. Nunn. “That’s why we fought to bring $209 million back to Iowa to strengthen rural health care. In Wayne County, that means a patient fighting cancer can get treatment close to home instead of spending hours on the road — near the family and neighbors helping them through it. That’s the difference these investments can make. Rural hospitals have been asking for this support for years, and now they’re putting it to work for their patients. I’m urging CMS to keep that progress going for Iowa’s rural communities next year.”

The Rural Health Transformation Program was established through the Working Families Tax Cuts, which invested a historic $50 billion over five years to strengthen rural health care nationwide. This year, Iowa led the nation as the first state to roll out these funds, delivering grants to 58 awardees for rural healthcare worker recruitment, 42 awardees for new medical equipment, and five for new Combat Cancer Health Hubs, along with investments in chronic disease prevention and maternal and child health.

Four of Iowa’s five Combat Cancer Health Hubs are located in the Third District: Wayne County Hospital in Corydon, Ottumwa Regional Health Center, Greater Regional Medical Center, and Shenandoah Medical Center. These hubs will build regional cancer care networks to expand treatment access in rural communities. Together with other investments through the Rural Health Transformation Program, these funds will help rural health care providers expand services through new medical equipment, workforce recruitment, telehealth, and partnerships with other providers.

The delegation’s letter highlights the immense progress already underway across Iowa’s healthcare system and urges CMS to give the state’s fiscal year 2027 Rural Health Transformation Program funding request full and fair consideration to continue this historic investment.

A copy of the letter can be found here.

title: Nunn, Secretary Rollins Tour Animal Rescue League, Highlight Puppy Mills CrackDown
text:
“Man’s best friend deserves better than a lifetime of cruelty at the hands of puppy mill operators chasing a profit,” said Rep. Nunn. “I secured a bipartisan crackdown on puppy mills in the House-passed Farm Bill, and I’m grateful to work alongside Secretary Rollins to turn that authority into action: enforce the law, stop the abuse, and protect dogs before shelters have to rescue them.”

“Animal cruelty has no place in this country, and breeders who break the law must be held accountable,” said Secretary Rollins. “USDA is strengthening inspections and enforcement to protect dogs from abuse before rescue becomes their only hope. I’m grateful to Congressman Nunn for his leadership and to the Animal Rescue League of Iowa for its tireless work giving these animals the care and the second chance they deserve.”

Iowa remains one of the largest puppy mill states in the nation. In 2024 alone, the Animal Rescue League of Iowa and partner organizations rescued more than 400 animals from puppy mills, hoarding, and other inhumane conditions across the state. Rep. Nunn secured a bipartisan amendment in the House-passed Farm Bill reinforcing USDA’s authority to crack down on abusive breeders.

In September, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) deployed a new Animal Protection Bureau to identify unlicensed breeders, strengthen inspections, and coordinate enforcement against illegal operations. So far in 2026, USDA has conducted more than 2,000 inspections of dog breeder and broker facilities, suspended six licenses, and revoked five more from chronic violators.

title: Olszewski Applauds $3.7 Billion Investment in Tradepoint Atlantic at Sparrows Point
text:
(Baltimore, MD) — Maryland Congressman Johnny Olszewski today applauded Anduril Industries’ plans to build a new advanced manufacturing facility at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point, a $3.7 billion investment expected to create 3,100 direct jobs and more than 10,000 indirect jobs building Virginia-class submarines for the U.S. Navy.

“Every family deserves the dignity that comes with a good paycheck, and this project will help deliver that promise to thousands of Marylanders,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “As someone whose roots run deep in Sparrows Point, I know what this historic site has meant to generations of Marylanders. I’ve had the privilege of fighting for its future as a state delegate, Baltimore County Executive, U.S. Congressman — and, most importantly, as someone who has always called this community home.

“For years, we’ve worked to transform Sparrows Point from a symbol of industrial decline into a center of opportunity, and today’s announcement is a powerful sign of how far we’ve come. This investment – with the help of commitments by the State of Maryland and Baltimore County – brings good-paying jobs, advanced manufacturing and new capabilities that will strengthen our national security back to a site with a proud history of building for America.

“I’m proud of the role I’ve played in helping lay the groundwork for Sparrows Point’s next chapter, and I’m even prouder to see that work creating new opportunities for working families. This is an investment in Baltimore County, in Maryland’s manufacturing future and in the workers who will build it.”

title: Pappas Meets with NH CAP Leaders on Rising Energy Costs and LIHEAP
text:
Yesterday Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) hosted a roundtable with leaders of New Hampshire Community Action Partnership agencies for a discussion on the impact of rising energy costs on Granite Staters and the importance of the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).

New Hampshire households could pay $2,300 for home heating oil this winter because of President Trump’s war with Iran, a 31% increase. The cost of groceries rose 2.9 percent overall this year, and families paid $310 more for food during President Trump's first year in office compared to 2024. In total, American families have spent over $3,800 more on goods and services since President Trump took office.

“Electricity prices are up, natural gas and home heating oil prices are up, and diesel fuel is hitting record highs. Granite Staters don’t need federal data to tell them this: they are feeling it with every electric and gas bill. As we enter the colder months, tackling the rising cost of energy could not be more urgent,” said Congressman Pappas. “My new legislation would lower energy costs by increasing federal support for heating assistance, expanding eligibility to more families, and lowering gas and diesel costs. I will continue fighting to lower costs for families and put more money back in their pockets.”

Pappas recently introduced three new bills to lower energy costs.

The LIHEAP Act would expand the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), one of the most successful programs aimed at reducing energy costs for working families.

The American Homes First Act would increase funding for LIHEAP by redirecting $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush fund.

The Consumer Fuel Prices Relief Act would provide federal fuel tax relief until the end of September 2027 by pausing the gas tax, the diesel tax, and the aviation fuel tax, while ensuring the benefit is immediately passed on to consumers in full. The legislation builds on his bicameral Gas Prices Relief Act of 2026, introduced in March, which would have suspended the federal gas tax through October 1, 2026. The legislation safeguards and maintains funding for roads, bridges, and gas spill remediation, and holds corporations accountable if they fail to pass along savings to individual consumers.

Background:

LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff and President Trump’s repeated efforts to fully defund the program have put this assistance at risk.

In September 2026, Pappas led 116 of his Congressional colleagues across the aisle in urging for LIHEAP funds to be delivered to states as soon as possible, and no later than November 1st. He previously led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025, and has repeatedly led bipartisan calls for the Trump administration to distribute LIHEAP funds in a timely manner.

title: Pou Statement On Release of Martin Soto from ICE Detention
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Tonight, U.S. Representative Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) celebrated the release of Martin Soto, a resident of the Ninth Congressional District who was held in ICE custody for several months.

“I am so overjoyed that Martin Soto is finally freed from ICE custody,” stated Rep. Nellie Pou, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security. “Martin was undeniably targeted and mistreated, being moved from Delaney Hall to the Elizabeth Detention Center and held in solitary confinement. For months my office has been pushing ICE to release Martin and tonight justice is finally being done. It should have happened months ago. ICE remains out of control in our state and we must continue to oppose its rampant abuses. But tonight we can be grateful the hard work from so many paid off and Martin is being reunited with his family.”

Initially detained in Newark, Martin Soto was moved to the Elizabeth Detention Center in retaliation for his role in the hunger and labor strike to highlight the deplorable conditions at Delaney Hall. There, Martin experienced harsh retribution including isolation.

Rep. Pou and her staff have been working with the Soto family, advocates, and other elected officials to obtain his release for months.

“I am so happy Martin is finally being released from ICE custody,” said Gabby Soto, wife of Martin Soto. “I want to thank Congresswoman Nellie Pou for all of her work on his case. Her efforts were critical to us finally reaching this moment.”

title: WATCH: Pressley, Wu, Breadon Condemn USPS Service Cuts and Proposed Closure of Allston Post Office
text:
Transcript: Rep. Pressley Condemns USPS Plan to Close Allston Branch

October 5, 2026

Allston, MA

In serving on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, I was conducting a lot of oversight in the fight to send Postmaster DeJoy on his way. And I thought when we did that that we might be getting on a path to what the people deserve, and certainly the dedicated postal workers deserve. Instead, we find ourselves here.

But the reason why, in the midst of this, I still have hope, is because I believe in the power of pressure.

I believe in the power of organizing. I believe in the power of solidarity.

I was looking at Representative Honan and remembering the fight to save our branch libraries when we all came together and understood that they are a public good, a lifeline to and for the community, and so this is that same kind of fight. This is about livelihoods. This is about lives. This is about commerce. This is about connectivity. So that’s what brings us all here today.

I’m so grateful for the leadership of everyone who has been named and who has not been named, I’m so grateful to our mayor for convening us, and certainly grateful to our Council President, President Breadon, who has been indefatigable, and that is what we need to be in this fight.

Folks were shuddering a little bit. Maybe it’s a little chilly. It’s hot one second, cold the next. Yeah, welcome to perimenopause.

But the point is, the point is, you might be a little uncomfortable, but deal with it, so that we are never complacent in our advocacy.

I grew up in a family of proud letter carriers, postal workers, nurses, first responders. That was how we built the middle class. These good union jobs. They take pride in that work, no matter the weather, no matter the season, no matter the ingratitude, so that’s what brings us here today.

So I thank you all for showing up, for giving a damn, to show your support for reopening your neighborhood’s post office, which has been closed since 2019.

It is a shame, and the reason why we have to agitate, resist, and give our feedback, we see this is a very slippery slope because they’re trying to bring the same pain to Dorchester, which is why solidarity is so essential in this moment.

But everyone here, your advocacy, your love of community is inspiring. Now, while this injustice has gone on for too long, you refuse, you accept it as an inevitability, and let it be quietly swept under the rug.

So again, I say thank you to everyone, and especially to Scott Hoffman and all of our brothers and sisters at the American Postal Workers Union, who stand up every day for their members, as well as service and reliability for our neighbors.

For the past seven years, Allston residents have gone without retail post office services and had to travel to Brighton, to Brookline, or Cambridge to do their daily business. In that time, USPS has made commitments to my office, my colleagues’ offices, and the folks living in this community that they were searching for a new location and would indeed reopen.

There have been ups and downs, but finally, finally, it appeared we were close to having the branch reopen. A lease had been agreed to, construction plans were in place with the developer. Now we are told that this plan is to keep this branch permanently closed.

This is unconscionable. This is unacceptable.

With last week’s announcement of the quote-unquote “temporary” closure of the Fields Corner Post Office, I find it hard to believe that this is just a coincidence. And to be clear, these efforts to close our local branches are all part of a coordinated campaign.

Y’all are tired of me saying it as the co-founder of the Stop Project 2025 Task Force, but it was all laid out. It was not a blueprint. It was a playbook. They want to privatize the USPS. They want to privatize these essential services that our constituents need every single day.

The USPS has been serving our communities for 250 years, delivering our mail, our checks, our prescriptions, and our ballots.

The dedicated carriers who are out on our sidewalks six days per week are members of our community. They know our neighbors, and they are the way folks most often interact with the federal government.

These services are not nice to haves—they are must haves. And you, along with every other community, has come to depend upon them and rightly deserve them.

These efforts to degrade and undermine the postal service are intended to exhaust you and your neighbors, so that you’ll give up and do your business somewhere else. Hell no, we won’t go. But the services provided by USPS are a public good and should not be left to billionaires and for-profit private corporations to play games with.

Today, I’m proud to stand with Allston and everyone here, calling for the Postal Service to keep their word to this community.

They must reverse the decision, work to reopen the Austin branch, and restore daily service.

If they intend to follow through with this closure plan, they must give the community a way to have their voice heard, not simply hold a midday Zoom meeting when folks are at work or at school.

The 87,000 Allston-Brighton residents, our neighbors in Fields Corner, folks in Somerville, Grove Hall, and Mission Hill all need and should have an accessible and conveniently located post office to do their business.

So we will not stop advocating for what you deserve.

Again, I believe in the power of pressure, of organizing, and of solidarity.

We will not stop fighting the Republican campaign, because they are the architects of this, to privatize the postal service, and we will not stop fighting until Allston has a post office again.

And now, as someone who comes from a long line of letter carriers, it is my privilege to introduce a man who fights for better service for our friends and neighbors every single day, national business agent for the American Postal Workers Union, Scott Hoffman.

—

title: Rep. Sara Jacobs Responds to Trump’s Dangerous Comments on San Diego
text:
Following President Trump’s comments suggesting that hypothetical Iranian attacks on San Diego or Los Angeles would be a “small price to pay,” Rep. Sara Jacobs released the following statement:

“The President sent San Diegans into a panic with his dangerous comments last night. I’ve received a flood of texts, calls, and emails from my constituents wondering if we’re safe, if there’ve been credible threats, and if we’re under attack. I’ve personally spoken with the local FBI field office and military leaders today, and they relayed to me that there are currently no increased threats to San Diego.

“It’s unbelievably distressing that President Trump is the cause of this stress when he’s supposed to protect and reassure our country. His comments are inexcusable. They don’t need more context, and we don’t need a thicker skin to understand them. San Diego and Los Angeles aren’t expendable, and neither are the service members who’ve already been killed in President Trump’s war with Iran. We need to end this war now before President Trump decides that all Americans can be collateral damage.”

title: Congresswoman Scholten Introduces COIN Act to Help Small Businesses Evaluate Uses of Digital Assets
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), member of the House Small Business Committee, introduced the Currency Options, Information, and Navigation (COIN) Act. This legislation would direct the Small Business Administration (SBA) to create learning modules to help small businesses learn how to evaluate the use of digital assets, such as cryptocurrency, for their operations. According to PayPal, 39 percent of American merchants currently accept cryptocurrency at checkout, and 84 percent believe payments using cryptocurrency will become common within the next five years.

“Small businesses keep our state and country running, but too many owners are being asked to navigate rapidly changing technology without clear, reliable guidance or learning opportunities,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “Digital assets like cryptocurrency are becoming more and more common at checkout counters, which is why I’m proud to introduce the COIN Act to make sure Main Street businesses have what they need to adapt and succeed.”

The bill requires these learning modules to be made with detailed information on the benefits and drawbacks of digital assets, and would provide entrepreneurs information on the logistics involving this technology, including tax implications and security risks if they choose to adopt any kind of digital asset. Additionally, this bill directs the SBA Administrator to work with relevant agencies to achieve accuracy in the information provided, with the goal of creating a comprehensive resource for small businesses. Finally, the bill establishes an Advisory Working Group made up of members from academia, industry, and financial consumer advocates to inform the creation of these learning modules.

This bill reflects the Congresswoman’s ongoing efforts to support small business owners in Michigan and across the country. Earlier this year, Congresswoman Scholten’s bipartisan Investing in All of America Act was signed into law, and her Main Street Competes Act, AI WISE Act, and AI for Main Street Actall passed the House.

title: Smucker Makes Case for Bipartisan Fiscal Commission on 584 Vetoes Podcast
text:
WASHINGTON — Rep. Lloyd Smucker (PA-11), Vice Chairman of the House Budget Committee and a senior member of the House Ways and Means Committee, joined the 584 Vetoes podcast to discuss the nation’s $40 trillion national debt and the need for bipartisan action to put the country on a more sustainable fiscal path. The podcast was hosted by Brian Miller, MD, MBA, MPH, FACPM, a practicing hospitalist, Associate Professor of Medicine at the Johns Hopkins University, and a Visiting Fellow at the Hoover Institution.

Listen here on Spotify | Listen here on YouTube | Listen Here on Apple Podcasts |

Read more and listen here on Substack

During the conversation with host Brian Miller, Smucker made the case for establishing a bipartisan fiscal commission that would bring lawmakers, experts, and the American people into a national conversation about the country’s fiscal future.

“The commission would be a vehicle to discuss the options that we have available, and perhaps even more important, it would be a discussion with the American public,” Smucker said. “That, I think, is the value of a commission.”

Smucker said he envisions a commission holding hearings across the country to engage Americans directly in understanding the nation’s fiscal challenges and the consequences of failing to address them.

“People get that and people want to see us solve this,” Smucker said. “The commission would engage the public and then bring the experts in and provide the recommendations that would lead to that legislation.”

Smucker also discussed the impact of the federal government spending more than $1 trillion annually on interest on the debt, the need to strengthen Social Security and Medicare for future generations, and the combination of stronger economic growth and responsible spending reforms necessary to improve the nation’s fiscal outlook.

Smucker said the House Budget Committee has an important role to play in driving that conversation, describing the committee as the “conscience of the conference and of Congress” and saying it should hold Congress accountable while providing “the road map and the path to better fiscal policy.”

The full episode of 584 Vetoes, “It’s Time for a Fiscal Commission to Fix the Debt with Congressman Lloyd Smucker,” is available here.

title: Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) announced an award of $1.5 million in federal grants for the mansion and outbuildings of the fifth President of the United States, James Monroe. Oak Hill, located in Loudoun County, has been preserved for hundreds of years and provides the local community and visitors access to American history and educational programming. Earlier this year, the Virginia General Assembly approved Governor Spanberger’s budget amendment to designated Oak Hill as a State Park. That amendment was championed by Senator Russet Perry and Delegate John McAuliff.

“Oak Hill is an important part of our history and has survived hundreds of years. This funding will ensure it can continue to live on for generations. I am proud that federal funding will help maintain and preserve this historical landmark. I look forward to seeing people of all ages in our community and across the world visit Oak Hill for many years to come,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanayam.

“For more than two years, we fought in Richmond to make Oak Hill a state park and protect more than 1,200 acres of Loudoun County and President Monroe’s historic home. We got it done, and now the work is making sure Oak Hill has what it needs to thrive for the long term. This $1.5 million in federal funding will help us do that, and I’m grateful to Congressman Subramanyam for securing these resources and being a partner in Oak Hill’s future. I’m looking forward to continuing this work and getting Oak Hill State Park open to the public,” said Senator Russet Perry.

"Oak Hill will be an enormous investment in the quality of life and conservation of Western Loudoun by opening up over 1,200 acres of farm and forestland for recreational use. The new funding secured by Congressman Subramanyam and State budget language provided by Gov. Spanberger ensures this land and history will be treasured by generations to come," said Delegate John McAuliff.

“Oak Hill stands as a powerful reminder of our nation’s founding story, and these grants ensure that story will be preserved for generations to come. We’re grateful to Rep. Subramanyam and our federal partners at the National Park Service for recognizing what this site means – not just to Loudoun County, but to the story of our nation as we mark 250 years of independence,” said Heather Richards, Mid-Atlantic Vice President, The Conservation Fund.

Of the $1.5 million in grants for preservation and restoration, $750k from Save America’s Treasures and $750k from Semiquincentennial grants. View the NPS announcements of funding here and here.

title: Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and María Elvira Salazar (R-FL) introduced the bipartisan Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act, which would make it easier for nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attack to access federal grant funding for target hardening and physical security enhancements.

“We can all agree that our children should be able to go to school and that families should be able to worship without fear. As hate crimes rise throughout the country, nonprofit organizations, churches, synagogues, mosques, and religious schools are diverting their scarce resources away from serving their communities to pay for security cameras, guards, and emergency trainings,” said Congresswoman Lee. “No organization should be forced to choose between keeping their members safe or their financial stability. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will help nonprofit organizations fund security improvements and overall preparedness, so they can keep those they serve safe amid increased violence and harassment.”

“Every American should be able to worship without fear. When a church, synagogue, or other place of worship is approved for a federal security grant, it should be able to spend the money to improve security immediately. The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act gets security dollars out the door faster and helps protect our communities,” said Congresswoman Salazar.

Congress created the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) in 2004 to help nonprofit organizations prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from terrorist or extremist attacks. The program funds target hardening, physical security improvements, and related preparedness activities for nonprofits at high risk of terrorism or hate-motivated violence.

Under current law, nonprofit organizations selected to receive an NSGP grant through a competitive application process must pay out of pocket for approved critical security upgrades and then wait months—or even years—to be reimbursed. This places these organizations in an impossible situation: cut into their limited budgets to ensure the safety of those they serve without any idea of when they might see that money or forgo critical security upgrades to ensure they can continue their work unabated.

The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would amend the current law to require that NSGP awards be issued to approved nonprofits in advance, rather than as a reimbursement for costs already incurred. By allowing advance payments, FEMA could better support approved nonprofits that lack upfront capital, speed implementation of needed security measures, and strengthen protection for vulnerable communities.

“Synagogues and nonprofit are paying out of pocket for essential security, then waiting months or years to get their money back,” said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO and National Director. “Providing funding upfront to institutions already approved for security grants would help ease that financial burden and allow them to make critical security improvements sooner. We thank Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for advancing this commonsense solution to get security dollars where they’re needed, when they’re needed.”

“According to American Jewish Committee’s (AJC) State of Antisemitism in America 2025 Report, 28% of American Jews say that at least one Jewish institution they are affiliated with has been a target of antisemitic incidents in the last five years. As threats against Jewish institutions continue to rise, we applaud Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for introducing the Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act,” said Julie Rayman, AJC’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Political Affairs. “By removing a financial barrier that can delay or prevent needed security upgrades, this legislation will help at-risk institutions better protect the communities they serve.”

“Counties are on the front lines of keeping communities safe, but too often they are left filling the gap when nonprofits can’t afford to pay upfront for critical security upgrades,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would allow approved nonprofits to receive funding upfront, helping them strengthen security sooner rather than delaying upgrades due to lack of capital. That means safer facilities, stronger coordination with local law enforcement and more resilient communities. Counties urge Congress to advance this bipartisan legislation quickly.”

“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) is an important resource for houses of worship to better secure themselves against acts of hate and prepare for all kinds of emergencies, but the logistical burdens of the process can pose barriers to applicants. This important proposal to disburse funds up front rather than requiring a reimbursement-based model removes one such major hurdle. With these kinds of improvements, as well as timely and apolitical execution by the Department of Homeland Security, NSGP can continue to serve more of our nation's most vulnerable communities in a time of increased threats.” – Mannirmal Kaur, Senior Federal Policy Manager, The Sikh Coalition.

The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act is endorsed by Jewish Nevada, American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), National Association of Counties (NACO), Secure Community Network, and The Sikh Coalition.

title: Representatives Lee, Fulcher Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Establish National Critical Minerals Council, Federal Strategy on Critical Minerals
text:
Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and Congressman Russ Fulcher (ID-01) introduced the bipartisan National Critical Minerals Council Act, which would establish a National Critical Minerals Council to develop and implement a national strategy on critical minerals and build reliable supply chains at home and abroad. U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Tim Sheehy (R-MT), and Kevin Cramer (R-ND) introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

“Critical minerals are used in everything from our phones to solar panels and aircraft used by the Department of Defense. It’s essential we develop our domestic critical mineral supply chains and reduce our dependence on foreign countries for rare earths,” said Congresswoman Lee. “That’s why I’m proud to join my colleagues in introducing the bipartisan, bicameral National Critical Minerals Council Act. This commonsense legislation will ensure the United States continues to grow our domestic supply of critical minerals, strengthening our national security and energy grid.”

Critical minerals power our modern way of life, including vehicles, smartphones, defense systems, medical equipment, AI and clean energy. Yet, China dominates the market, processing or refining about 70% of the world’s critical minerals. The U.S. is fully reliant on imports for 16 critical minerals. Given the scale of the challenge, our federal response remains fragmented, with more than 15 federal agencies and departments working on critical minerals issues. Absent a unified effort, the U.S. risks falling behind in securing the minerals essential to our competitiveness and leadership in energy security and national defense.

“For far too long, our country has depended on foreign adversaries for vital minerals that support many of our defense capabilities and energy systems. This legislation will establish important structures for mineral development and help build critical partnerships,” said Congressman Russ Fulcher. “I am proud to co-lead the National Critical Minerals Council Act with my colleague, Congresswoman Lee. By securing the critical minerals we have here at home today, we can build stronger energy security for tomorrow.”

“China doesn’t need to fire a shot. It just needs to stop a shipment,” said Senator John Hickenlooper. “We need a national strategy on critical minerals now. Otherwise, Beijing decides who gets the supply — and who doesn't.”

“As the world races to acquire and leverage the critical minerals that power the modern economy, the United States needs an efficient and effective plan to secure these important resources,” said Senator Jacky Rosen. “I am proud to help introduce this bipartisan bill to ensure the United States has the infrastructure it needs to secure critical minerals and remain at the forefront of modern development.”

“The United States can no longer afford to take a piecemeal approach to address our critical minerals needs,” said Senator Thom Tillis. “I am proud to reintroduce this bipartisan legislation to establish a comprehensive and unified strategy to secure the minerals that are essential to our national security and economic stability.”

“It’s common sense: we cannot continue to rely on adversaries like China, which dominates the world’s critical minerals processing, for our critical mineral needs because it puts America's national security at risk and threatens our competitive edge,” said Senator Tim Sheehy. “This crucial legislation reduces our dependence on others and bolsters America’s critical mineral supply chains by centralizing federal coordination, strategy, and research, making our nation more secure and self-reliant. I’m proud to cosponsor this legislation as we work to ensure America’s needs can be securely met.”

“We cannot afford to become more dependent on other countries for the critical minerals needed to power our economy and strengthen our national security,” said Senator Kevin Cramer. “Our bill establishes a National Critical Minerals Council to unite all federal investment, research, and development on critical minerals under a single national strategy. The demand for critical minerals is growing every single day, and we need to seize every opportunity to jumpstart domestic production.”

The Secretary of the Interior, the National Security Adviser, and the Director of the National Economic Council would co-chair the council. They would appoint a Chief Minerals Adviser to oversee the Council’s operations and collaborate with experts from universities, industry, national labs, governments, Tribes, non-profits, and civil society.

Specifically, the council would:

Develop a national critical minerals strategy to reduce our reliance on foreign adversaries.

Work with allied nations and private entities to make the U.S. the partner of choice on critical minerals projects.

Track foreign investments in global critical mineral projects.

Coordinate education and workforce development.

Oversee the responsible development of domestic resources.

Congresswoman Lee has worked consistently to strengthen America's domestic critical mineral supply chain and reduce our reliance on foreign sources of key minerals and materials. Her bipartisan Critical Mineral Consistency Act (H.R. 755) recently passed the U.S. House of Representatives unanimously. This legislation will provide much-needed clarity to industry and federal agencies by conferring the same benefits — including federal tax credit and financing opportunities — to both “critical materials,” as identified by the Department of Energy, and “critical minerals,” as identified by the U.S. Geological Survey within the Department of the Interior.

title: Congressman Taylor Joins Ohio Trucking Leaders in Roundtable Discussion
text:

title: Thompson, Keating Highlight German-American Partnership
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Bill Keating (D-Mass.), co-chairs of the bipartisan German-American Caucus, introduced a resolution reaffirming German-American Friendship and supporting continued cooperation between the United States and Germany.

More than 36 years after the fall of the Berlin Wall, this resolution reaffirms the importance of the alliance between the United States and Germany and underscores our shared commitment to democracy. It also supports the “Wunderbar Together” initiative, which aims to celebrate German-American art, culture, science, friendship, and more.

“Pennsylvania has one of the largest populations of Americans with German heritage, and this resolution is an opportunity to acknowledge the strong alliance between the United States and Germany. I look forward to continuing to foster this partnership for years to come, and celebrating our two countries shared interests,” Rep. Thompson said.

“Germany and the United States share a relationship based on values, traditions, and friendship between peoples. This resolution recognizes the profound contributions of Germans to the United States and Congress’ unwavering support for the US-German relationship. As Co-Chair of the Congressional German-American Caucus, I look forward to strengthening our relationship in the years to come," Rep. Keating said.

“The transatlantic partnership between Germany and the United States remains a cornerstone of our economic ties and is grounded in shared values and interests. At a time of significant global economic and geopolitical challenges, strong transatlantic cooperation is more important than ever. The Representative of German Industry and Trade (RGIT) is pleased to reaffirm its support for Representative Thompson’s and Representative Keating's resolution and for continued cooperation between Germany and the United States.”– Representative of German Industry and Trade

Representative of German Industry and Trade (RGIT) is the liaison office of the Federation of German Industries (BDI) and the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DIHK) in Washington, D.C.

title: Trahan, Warren, Lynch, Lead Demands to Trump Administration to Provide Relief for Skyrocketing Winter Heating Bills Amid Iran War
text:
LOWELL, MA – Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Congressman Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08) led 24 of their colleagues from Northeastern states in pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter, the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities.

“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.

The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year.

In addition to increasing the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by:

Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.

Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.

Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families.

“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued.

“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded.

The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).

title: Dân Biểu Derek Trần giới thiệu dự luật giảm chi phí nhà ở cho các gia đình Nam California
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) giới thiệu Dự Luật Hỗ Trợ Chi Phí Sinh Hoạt Nhà Ở cho Người Thuê Nhà (COST) Act, để hỗ trợ cư dân tại Nam California đang phải đối mặt với chi phí nhà ở ngày càng tăng. Dự luật thiết lập các khoản tín dụng thuế dành cho người thuê nhà, tiếp nối nỗ lực của Dân Biểu Derek nhằm giúp người dân có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận nhà ở với chi phí hợp lý.

“Chi phí nhà ở trên cả nước, đặc biệt tại Nam California, đã tăng đến mức báo động. Nhiều gia đình phải chật vật mới đủ tiền trả tiền thuê nhà, chưa nói đến việc tiết kiệm cho tương lai,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Dự luật này sẽ mang lại sự hỗ trợ thiết thực và kịp thời cho những người thuê nhà đang gặp khó khăn, giúp họ trang trải tiền thuê nhà, có thêm ngân sách cho các chi phí sinh hoạt hằng ngày, hoặc thậm chí dành dụm để mua nhà. Tôi tự hào dẫn đầu nỗ lực này vì các gia đình khắp nước Mỹ.”

Các gia đình tại Nam California phải đối mặt với mức chi phí nhà ở thuộc hàng cao nhất cả nước. Tại Orange County, tiền thuê nhà trung bình hiện vượt $3,200 mỗi tháng, tăng gần 40% kể từ năm 2017.

Dự luật đề nghị một khoản tín dụng thuế hoàn lại ở mức căn bản 8% dành cho các gia đình có tổng thu nhập từ $150,000 trở xuống, với mức hỗ trợ tối đa $333 mỗi tháng cho mỗi gia đình, tương đương $4,000 mỗi năm. Riêng tại Địa Hạt 45 của California, hơn 75,000 gia đình có thể được hưởng lợi từ chính sách này.

Trong khi những giải pháp khác nhằm giảm chi phí nhà ở có thể cần nhiều thời gian để thực hiện, dự luật này sẽ trực tiếp giúp người thuê nhà có thêm tiền để trang trải thực phẩm, thuốc men, chi phí chăm sóc trẻ em, và các nhu cầu thiết yếu khác.

Nỗ lực lập pháp này tiếp nối những hoạt động của Dân Biểu Derek Trần nhằm giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở trong khu vực:

Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã vận động thành công $250,000 ngân sách liên bang để hỗ trợ xây dựng 2,700 căn nhà ở giá phải chăng lâu dài khắp Orange County.

Dân Biểu Derek đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Saving the American Dream Act, nhằm thành lập một lực lượng đặc nhiệm liên cơ quan để giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng nhà ở, và Dự Luật Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act, hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm các khu nhà ở nhiều căn.

Ngoài ra, Dân Biểu Derek đã bỏ phiếu ủng hộ Dự Luật 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, được ký thành luật vào Tháng Bảy, 2026, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng nhà ở và giảm bớt các thủ tục hành chính không cần thiết.

Toàn văn dự luật có thể được xem TẠI ĐÂY.

title: Congressman Van Drew Calls on FERC to Determine Refunds and Rate Relief for South Jersey
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Van Drew sent a letter to Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Chairman Laura Swett calling on the Commission to independently review how much Atlantic City Electric (ACE) customers were overcharged after a federal audit found the company overbilled transmission customers from 2021 to 2025.

"Atlantic City Electric cannot be allowed to decide for itself how much it overcharged people and then tell everyone the answer is less than two cents a month," said Congressman Van Drew. "First, we were told there was nothing wrong. Then we were told that residential customers were not impacted. Once the federal audit proved there was overbilling, suddenly the answer became that people were owed almost nothing. Meanwhile, they have continued asking for rate increases while bringing in record profits. Anyone opening an electric bill in South Jersey knows why people are not buying that.

"The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities should have gotten to the bottom of this, but they have not. With the state refusing to act, I am asking FERC to use the authority available to it to independently determine what customers are owed from these transmission overcharges and what relief should follow. We need independent numbers and full refunds with interest to bring relief for South Jersey families."

title: Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 6, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service (USFS) Chief Tom Schultz strongly opposing the Administration’s proposed rule expanding vehicle access to public lands and trails that are already facing maintenance backlogs. Vasquez was joined by 28 of his House and Senate colleagues in his call to keep the 2005 Travel Management Rule in place.

“New Mexicans deserve public lands that are safe and well-managed. Ending the long-established Travel Management Rule would put public safety at risk and open the door to damage that will take generations to undo,” said Vasquez. “Hikers, hunters, and ranchers alike shouldn’t have to worry about more folks driving through the spaces they use for recreation and grazing. Instead of opening more of our public lands to vehicle access in places where access already exists, the Forest Service should focus on maintaining existing trails and roads. This broad reversal is unnecessary."

The USFS and the Bureau of Land Management have separate but similar rules requiring our public land agencies to provide clear, consistent guidance for how public lands are used, including where motorized vehicles, including cars and ATVs, can travel. For those who enjoy our public lands, whether on foot or on wheels, these rules help keep trails open, accessible, and responsibly managed. They also require public input before designating routes, produce Motor Vehicle Use Maps that show visitors where they can go, give rangers clear standards to enforce, and allow exceptions for emergency, military, and law enforcement vehicles.

Changing the 2005 rule, as proposed by USDA, could endanger public safety, reduce quality access to our public lands, and degrade the quality of trails, lands and waters that support our nation’s wildlife and outdoor recreation economy.

The letter demands that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule preserve the following core principles:

Maintain the current default of keeping routes and areas closed to motorized use unless expressly designated as open.

Carry forward criteria that guide local land management decisions and protect critical public land values, including soil, watersheds, vegetation, and wildlife habitat, as well as reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing.

Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input.

The agencies must retain the ability to protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources.

The agencies should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted.

The agencies should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering their transportation system before adding new routes or expanding access.

“This is yet another egregious attack in the systematic dismantling of public lands management of our national forests,” said Paul Sanford, director for equitable access policy advocacy at The Wilderness Society. “Travel management provides the basic guardrails that let hikers, hunters, anglers, and riders share the same forest without chaos; removing those guardrails threatens the freedom of all public lands users to safely enjoy our national forests the way they choose. Paired with the proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule, this destructive agenda sells out future generations’ enjoyment of our forests in order to hand them over for corporate profits.”

“We’re grateful to see Congressional Leaders pushing back on federal agency proposals to gut travel management regulations and prioritize off-road vehicles at the expense of wildlife, cultural sites, desert waterways and other recreationists, proposals that will make visiting Utah’s canyon country worse for everyone,” said Laura Peterson, Senior Attorney at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance (SUWA). “The Trump Administration’s vision for public lands is not about balance or reasonable access, it is about blanketing landscapes with off-road vehicle routes, transforming quiet, wild places into motorized playgrounds.”

"We stand with Rep. Vasquez and his urgent request to keep the Travel Management Rule intact,” said Taylor Rush, government relations representative at Defenders of Wildlife. "For more than two decades, this rule has protected our cherished wildlife, outdoor recreationists, clean water supply and local communities from the harmful impacts of unmanaged motorized vehicle use. Weakening the framework used to reduce habitat damage and social conflict would result in dangerous degradation of our wild places and wildlife."

title: Vindman Stands Up for Roadless Rule to Protect Virginia’s Natural Resources, Local Economies
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — the only Virginian on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee — joined Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04) in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins opposing the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, commonly referred to as the “Roadless Rule.”

Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.

The letter was also signed by U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and U.S. Representatives Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) and James Walkinshaw (Va.-11).

“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”

The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.

“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”

text:
Today, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) welcomed Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 5 Administrator Anne Vogel to southwestern Michigan for a visit to a local brownfield site and a stakeholder roundtable focused on Great Lakes priorities.

Walberg. "Strong partnership with the EPA is essential to meeting the challenges facing the Great Lakes basin, accelerating cleanup efforts, and ensuring Michigan communities remain resilient and thriving for generations to come.”
