title: Congressman Gabe Evans Introduces More Beef, Lower Prices Act to Rebuild America’s Cattle Herd
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Gabe Evans introduced the More Beef, Lower Prices Act to give American cattle producers additional tools to rebuild the domestic herd, strengthen the U.S. beef supply, and address high beef prices for families across Colorado and the nation.

America’s cattle herd sits at a historical low. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the United States had 86.2 million cattle and calves as of January 1, 2026 - the lowest supply in 75 years. This decline does not just endanger our nation’s food security, but a low cattle supply makes American producers vulnerable to volatile markets. Our beef producers need more options, not constraint.

The More Beef, Lower Prices Act will amend the Federal Crop Insurance Act to expressly include bred cattle, replacement heifers, and cull cattle in the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Livestock Risk Protection (LRP) programs beginning in crop year 2027. Expanding these widely-utilized risk-management tools will deliver certainty to producers as they plan the long-term investments necessary to maintain and rebuild America’s domestic cattle herd.

“Colorado ranchers raise the highest-quality beef in the world, but rebuilding a cattle herd takes years, significant investment, and a willingness to take on tremendous risk. I’ve heard directly from producers across Colorado’s Eighth District that they need better tools to lower risks on those important investments. That’s exactly why I introduced the More Beef, Lower Prices Act. Instead of becoming dependent on foreign beef, we should be giving American ranchers better tools to raise more cattle right here at home. This bill grows the domestic supply of high-quality American beef, strengthening America’s food security, stabilizing food costs, and supporting our rural communities.”–– Congressman Gabe Evans

The legislation is supported by the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association.

BACKGROUND:

Livestock producers operate in a market where rebuilding a herd requires significant upfront investment and years of planning. Replacement heifers and other breeding cattle are particularly important to expanding future cattle supplies because producers must retain and invest in animals today before additional calves can reach the market.

Federal livestock insurance programs provide producers with tools to protect against unexpected declines in market prices. USDA’s LRP program is one such tool, widely utilized by livestock producers to protect against risks.

The Trump Administration has also recognized the importance of expanding risk-management tools to help rebuild America’s cattle herd. In August, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins announced USDA’s Ranchers First Initiative, which includes a new Beef Retention and National Development (BRAND) endorsement for LRP. The new tool is designed to help producers manage the financial risk of retaining heifers for breeding rather than sending them to market, supporting efforts to rebuild the domestic herd.

The More Beef, Lower Prices Act builds on this same principle by strengthening federal livestock risk-management policy and requiring bred cattle, replacement heifers, and cull cattle to be included under the Federal Crop Insurance Act’s livestock pilot program beginning with crop year 2027.

By expanding access to risk-management protections, the legislation is designed to give cattle producers greater confidence to invest in their operations and support rebuilding the domestic herd.

title: Gallagher Helps Return Nearly $6 Million to North State Taxpayers
text:
PARADISE, CA — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) announced Wednesday that his office helped return nearly $6 million to North State taxpayers through constituent casework during Fiscal Year 2026.

Gallagher’s office resolved 195 cases totaling more than $5.88 million for constituents across California’s First Congressional District. The money included funds taxpayers were already owed but had struggled to recover through the normal federal process.

“Behind that $5.88 million number are real people. These are families and small business owners who were waiting on money that belonged to them,” said Congressman Gallagher. “Sometimes our most important work has nothing to do with passing a bill in Washington. It’s helping somebody back home cut through the bureaucracy and get a problem solved. If someone in the North State is stuck dealing with the IRS or another federal agency, my office is here to help. title: Gallagher Introduces Bill to Lower Electricity Costs and Make Energy More Affordable for Communities That Power California
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) introduced the Affordable Power for Host Communities Act, legislation aimed at lowering electricity bills for families living in the rural communities that help power California.

Rural Northern California is a renewable energy powerhouse. From hydroelectric and geothermal power to biomass and solar, the North State produces a tremendous amount of the clean, renewable electricity used across California. Yet many of the families living in these communities face significantly higher electricity bills than customers of municipal utilities that rely on this power. Gallagher’s bill would require states and nonregulated utilities to consider providing customers in qualifying host counties with a 20 percent discount on their electricity rates.

“Rural Northern California is a renewable energy powerhouse. We produce a tremendous amount of the clean power that keeps the lights on across this state, but the families who live here are still paying significantly higher electricity bills,” said Congressman Gallagher. “If our communities are helping power California, we deserve some recognition for that when we open our own power bills. This bill is about fairness and affordability.”

The Affordable Power for Host Communities Act amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (PURPA) to establish a new federal standard for states and nonregulated utilities to consider. Under the standard, electricity rates for customers in qualifying host counties would be discounted by 20 percent compared with rates charged to customers in the same class outside those counties.

The legislation recognizes communities that are home to major power generation facilities, including hydroelectric and geothermal facilities as well as biomass, solar and wind generation. To qualify under the bill, a facility must have a capacity of at least five megawatts, supply electricity for sale and meet other requirements established in the legislation.

“There’s something backwards about rural communities producing renewable power for the rest of California while the people who live here pay significantly higher electricity bills,” Gallagher continued. “The North State helps keep California running. We produce the power, and our families deserve more affordable electricity in return.”

Under the legislation, state regulatory authorities and nonregulated utilities would have one year after enactment to begin considering the discounted-rate standard and two years to complete that process. The bill also recognizes prior state action to avoid duplicating proceedings where a comparable policy has already been implemented or recently considered.

The legislation is designed to recognize the role rural communities play in producing the power used across California while providing a path toward meaningful utility-bill relief for the people who call those communities home.

title: RELEASE: On Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly, Gottheimer Marks Third Anniversary of October 7th
text:
Above: Gottheimer announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly alongside Alexander Family.

TENAFLY, NJ — Today, Wednesday, October 7, 2026, on the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined local leaders, community members, and the family of former hostage Edan Alexander on Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly to remember the victims, honor the hostages and their families, and announce new efforts to combat terror. Gottheimer, along with U.S. Representatives Lois Frankel (FL-22), Joe Wilson (SC-2), and Young Kim (CA-40), and dozens of their colleagues, introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th.

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here and here.

“We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head. And we will never stop fighting for the day when Hamas lays down its arms for good, and communities can live in peace free from terror,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.”

Gottheimer also announced new and continuing efforts to combat terror and antisemitism:

October 7th Remembrance Resolution: The bipartisan resolution honors every person murdered on October 7th, condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust, and honors the hostages and their families. It also supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. The resolution also condemns the rise in antisemitism at home, including in schools and on college campuses. The House resolution is endorsed by the American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), Hadassah, Jewish Women International, and the Israel Allies Foundation.

Holding the United Nations accountable: New legislation with Congressman Lawler (NY) that would bar U.S. funds from going toward U.S. contributions to the United Nations until the U.N. has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. This is critical as UNRWA currently does not screen for Hamas ties in its hiring of teachers and other employees, leading to Hamas terrorists infiltrating its ranks. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

October 7th Gold Medal Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Lawler (NY) to award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Hostages and Missing Families Forum, American Jewish Committee (AJC), the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, the Weitzman National Museum of Jewish American History, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

October 7th Remembrance Education Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA) to direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the attacks committed on October 7 and the antisemitism that followed. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

The announcement builds on Gottheimer’s work since the attacks, including securing $100 million in the defense bill for his U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border; House passage last month of his bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses; and legislation with Congressman Lawler to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance out of the hands of Hamas terrorists. At home, Gottheimer continues to work across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program so that every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.

Gottheimer noted the sharp rise in antisemitism since October 7th: the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States last year, a 68 percent increase since 2022, with New Jersey ranking third highest in the country and Bergen County recording 139 incidents, the most in the state.

“Three years later, the horror of October 7th remains seared into our hearts,” said Congresswoman Lois Frankel. “We remember those who were murdered, honor the survivors and hostages and their families, and stand firmly against antisemitism and terrorism. Now we must build a future where Hamas is disarmed, Israel is safe and secure, and Palestinians and Israelis can live in peace and dignity.”

“Today marks the third anniversary of the massacre of 1,200 and kidnapping of 251 innocent men, women, and children in Israel by the Iranian terrorist puppet, Hamas. This cowardly act will forever be remembered around the world, but no more meaningful than to the families and friends who lost loved ones. I am grateful for the leadership of President Donald Trump, with the support of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and our allies, for ensuring that all hostages, living and deceased, were brought home,” said Congressman Joe Wilson.

“Three years ago, the world witnessed unspeakable evil as Hamas carried out the deadliest massacre of the Jewish people since the Holocaust. We remember the 1,200 innocent lives lost, the hostages who faced unimaginable suffering in Hamas captivity, families whose lives were irrevocably changed, and the extraordinary courage and selflessness shown by ordinary Israelis on that day,” said Congresswoman Young Kim. “We will never forget the darkness of October 7th or allow the world to forget what happened. As antisemitism continues to rear its ugly head around the world, the United States must stand firmly with the Jewish people and confront this hatred in all its forms.”

“Three years after Hamas’s October 7th attack on Israel, we remember and mourn the more than 1,200 innocent people brutally murdered, honor the hostages who have finally returned home and the families who endured unimaginable pain, and stand with all those whose lives were forever changed. American Jewish Committee proudly supports this bipartisan resolution introduced by Representatives Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Young Kim (R-CA), Lois Frankel (D-FL), and Joe Wilson (R-SC), which ensures the atrocities of October 7 are never forgotten and reaffirms America’s commitment to Israel’s security and the fight against antisemitism,” said Ted Deutch, CEO of American Jewish Committee.

“The tragedy of October 7 and the surge in antisemitism that followed that day will forever be etched in the memory of the Jewish people,” said ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt. “On this solemn third anniversary of the attack, we remember the innocent lives lost, the hostages who were taken, and the survivors whose lives were changed forever. We thank Reps. Gottheimer, Wilson, Frankel, and Kim for introducing this bipartisan resolution and for honoring the victims and survivors of October 7, and reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that ‘Never Again’ truly means never again.”

“Three years after October 7, we honor the memory of every person murdered by Hamas and its terrorist allies, and we honor the hostages and their families who endured unimaginable suffering. This resolution is an important affirmation that complete disarmament of Hamas and dismantling of its terrorist infrastructure are essential to ensuring that October 7 can never happen again and to building a future of security, peace, and dignity for Israelis and their neighbors. It also reinforces that we must confront the dangerous rise of antisemitism that has followed October 7 and continue to work hand-in-hand with government to ensure that our communities are secure in the face of this violent threat,” said Eric D. Fingerhut, President & CEO of Jewish Federations of North America.

“On the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, we pray for the innocent lives lost and renew our resolve to thwart future threats to peace. Hamas has yet to capitulate and disarm in Gaza, and terror groups continue to operate alongside Israel’s borders, sustained by state sponsors of terrorism. On this solemn day, we recognize that peace has not yet been achieved, and that further efforts are needed to safeguard civilians and demilitarize those bent on perpetuating violence,” said Tyler Stapleton, Senior Director of Government Relations, FDD Action.

“As we mark three years since Hamas terrorists carried out the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust, we remember and honor all those who were murdered, injured, tortured, raped or held captive by Hamas. We thank Representatives Lois Frankel, Josh Gottheimer, and Joe Wilson for introducing this resolution, which condemns the atrocities of October 7, 2023, affirms Israel’s right to self-defense and supports the critical conditions of the ceasefire, including the disarmament of Hamas. We urge members of Congress to support this bipartisan resolution and to continue to confront the rise in violent antisemitism across the country and around the world,” said Carol Ann Schwartz, National President, Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America.

“I listened with horror to whispers of the sexual atrocities committed by Hamas. I watched with horror the video of young women, pulled from their beds and pushed bloodied into trucks to be taken into Gaza. I saw with horror the photo of a naked, bound woman surrounded by terrorists raising guns in victory. I sat with horror in the silence of the world, in the silence of the feminist organizations. In the three years since, the silence, the denial, the distortion, and the hate not only continue; they grow. It is virulent and dangerous. Resolutions like this are critical in the fight against hate and disinformation. We are grateful to Representatives Gottheimer, Frankel, and Joe Wilson for standing up to hate and amplifying the truth. For those who died, and those who survived, we owe them as much,” said Meredith Jacobs, CEO of Jewish Women International (JWI).

Gottheimer was joined by Tenafly Mayor Mark Zinna, Tenafly Councilwoman Lauren Dayton, Tenafly Councilwoman, Jenny Jackson, Adi and Yael Alexander, and Rabbi Kirshner of Temple Emanu-El, Debra Mazon and her colleagues from Hadassah, Rabbi Levy from AJC, Brandi Katz Rubin from the ADL, and Shlomo Schorr from Agudath Israel, Rabbi Shmuel Bergman from Young Israel of Fort Lee, Rabbi Genack and his wife Sarah from Englewood, Tenafly Police Chief Michael Greenly, Rabbi Krishner with Temple Emanu-El, Rabbi Zev Reichman from East Hill Synagogue, and the Alexander family.

Below: Gottheimer Announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Good morning. Thank you all for joining us on this solemn day as we mark three years since October 7th, the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust. As many of you know, for 842 days the posters of every single hostage held in Gaza hung on the wall outside my office in Washington – right next to the Israeli flag.

It was a reminder to everyone who visited the United States Capitol of the responsibility we held here in the United States to do our part, not only for our key ally, but for what is right, until every hostage was returned to their families. The hostage photos were not just Israelis. They were of Americans. Of Thais. French. British. Filipinos. They were young and old. L’dor vador, from generation to generation. We all had a responsibility to do everything in our power, in every corner of the globe, to bring them home. It is a relief that this anniversary is the first without the need to wear yellow ribbons calling for the return of those being held.

Yet, as I walk past the empty wall into my office every day, I can still see those images, staring at me. It’s almost a reminder to me that we must never forget what happened – and of the work that lies ahead to heal and bring us back together. As it’s said in Isaiah, “Your ancient ruins shall be rebuilt; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; you shall be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of streets to live in.”

Let’s be honest. We have a great deal of repairing and restoration ahead of us.

But, on this third anniversary of October 7th, while we mourn those we lost, we also have much to be grateful for – for all the hostages who were reunited with their loved ones, who are rebuilding their lives. Among those taken that day, and who came home, was our very own Edan Alexander, a young man from right here in Tenafly. A graduate of Tenafly High School, who swam on the swim team and biked on these streets, a Jersey boy through and through. Today, we are standing here on Edan Alexander Way, a street we named last year in honor of his unshakable strength and courage.

To Adi and Yael Alexander: thank you for being with us today. I know Edan can’t be here, but I know he is living his life to the fullest today in Israel. I met your family on October 23rd, 2023, just over two weeks after the attack, and you have been like family to me and Marla ever since. For nearly two years, while Edan endured the unimaginable, you never — not for a single moment — surrendered hope. You called for action, and you would not be quieted until your son came home.

You pressed me, as you pressed so many others in our community, for action and for answers. And, I was proud to carry the courage and conviction you gave me, both on my trips to the Middle East and in the halls of Congress every single day.

I especially want to thank the people of Tenafly. Three years ago today, the world changed, and this community was asked to carry something unimaginable. But, you never recoiled – you never looked away. You stood here with the Alexander family while Hamas terrorists held their son for 584 days.

You stood in Huyler Park at five o’clock in the morning to watch him be released – I was there – and you filled these streets by the thousands to welcome Edan home in May of last year. You showed what a town can do when it stands together.

You’ve also shown us the importance of never forgetting.

That’s especially important today when some are actually glorifying Hamas terrorists as martyrs – or trying to justify the actions that day, when Hamas terrorists brutally murdered, raped, burned alive, decapitated, and kidnapped more than twelve hundred people – including innocent babies, children, women, men, and elderly people, and dozens of Americans, while taking 251 hostages into tunnels in Gaza. It’s unfathomable.

Some may try to bury their head in the sand or rewrite history. But, anybody who has seen the videos and images of those heinous and unthinkable acts knows what Hamas and its accomplices are capable of. They sowed terror at the Nova music festival, in the kibbutzim, in cities across Southern Israel. Like many of you, I traveled to Israel afterward to see their path of destruction with my own eyes – to give me the first-hand knowledge to confront the haters.

But, despite the truth, since Hamas’s devastating attack, we have unfortunately witnessed a tidal wave of antisemitism that has only grown more persistent, starting just hours after the terrorists attacked Israel. Instead of empathy from people and organizations around the globe, there was a flood of criticism and blame, and it hasn’t stopped.

Just days after the October 7 attack, during the “Day of Rage” in New York City, someone shouted at a group of Jewish people: “I wish Hitler was still here; he would’ve wiped all of you out.” Other protestors said: “Say it loud, say it clear, we don’t want Zionists here!”

At Columbia University, Jewish students were chased out of their dorms, received death threats, were spat upon, stalked, and pinned against walls. People in masks screamed, “Go back to Poland!” and “Globalize the Intifada.” On October 8th, the day after the largest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust, a faculty member at Rutgers declared October 7th “awesome.”

Three years later, the protests continue – including today – against Jews simply practicing their religion in America.

Recently, at one just outside a synagogue chanting hateful slogans like “We are all Hamas,” “Death to Zionists,” and “Long live October 7th” at worshippers. Businesses have even boycotted my Jewish colleagues – refusing to serve them.

Last year, the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States. That’s a 68 percent increase since 2022, before October 7th. And here in New Jersey, we ranked third highest in the entire country. Right here in Bergen County, we had 139 incidents, the most in New Jersey.

No other county in our state had more than 80. That’s our backyard. And, now you have internet personalities like Hasan Piker and Candace Owens spreading misinformation and hate to millions of followers online, with comments like calling a Jewish reporter a “Pig Dog,” justifying the violence on October 7th as “resistance”, blood libel, and conspiracy theories about Jewish control.

I say this not only as your Congressman, but also as a member of the Jewish community. This is deeply personal for me.

But, even in those moments of despair, we have also seen moments that give us hope. Light through the darkness.

Just a month ago, I joined the Chancellor of Vanderbilt, along with leaders from colleges ranging from the University of Alabama to Washington University to the University of Texas, in saying that hatred and religious discrimination against anyone isn’t welcome on their campus. We’ve had leaders in business, nonprofits, in the arts, in Hollywood, and in government stand strong against antisemitism, even though it has cost them personally.

Nations like the UAE and Argentina have bucked their own history and doubled down to protect the Jewish people.

And, of course, the greatest light. On May 12th of 2025, Edan came home. I will never forget the moment I first met him after his release. His humility, poise, and self-assurance stopped me in my tracks. He told me he was not a hero, that the real heroes were the ones still there … those who gave their lives. And, then he said something that will echo in my heart forever: “My story doesn’t end with survival. It continues with service.”

He meant it. Edan returned to the Israel Defense Forces and has since been promoted to Sergeant First Class. Just this summer, he stood before the world at the opening ceremony of the Maccabiah Games to explain why he went back into uniform. He has refused to let evil triumph. So neither can we.

A year ago this month, the remaining twenty living hostages came home. And in the months since, the remains of the fallen were returned, including Americans Omer Neutra and Itay Chen, whose families waited and waited until the last were finally brought home in January. Today, we remember every one of them.

We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in parts of Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.

That is why today, three years later, I am proud to announce new efforts to combat terror.

First, I’ve introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th. It honors every person murdered by Hamas. It condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.

It honors the hostages and their families. It supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. And, it condemns the rise in antisemitism here at home, including in our schools and on our college campuses. I’m proud to be joined by Representatives Lois Frankel, Joe Wilson, and Young Kim, as well as fifty of my colleagues in introducing this resolution.

Second, I’m introducing legislation to hold the United Nations accountable.

Here’s the simple, shocking truth: the UN has never designated Hamas or Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. Not before October 7th. Not after. The Security Council maintains sanctions lists for ISIS and al-Qaeda, but not for Iran’s proxies. And, because Hamas isn’t on the list, UN agencies, including UNRWA, don’t even screen for Hamas membership when they hire. The USAID Inspector General has found more than 100 UNRWA staff with Hamas affiliations, even though we believe there are far more, and only nine have been fired for direct involvement in the October 7 attacks. That is unacceptable.

So, my bill is straightforward. No U.S. funds can go toward our contributions to the United Nations until the Security Council has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as the terrorist organizations that they are.

Today, we are also recommitting to two bipartisan bills I introduced last year, and that I am continuing the fight to pass them.

The October 7th Gold Medal Act, with Congressman Lawler from New York, will award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza.

And, the October 7th Remembrance Education Act, with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick from Pennsylvania, will direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the heinous and brutal attacks committed on October 7th, and the antisemitism that followed.

We can’t afford for our children to learn history – and be filled with anti-American, antisemitism-filled disinformation — from TikTok. From Hasan Piker. The truth and the facts – history – should be taught in every classroom across America.

This builds on the work we’ve been doing since that terrible day. This summer, I secured $100 million in the defense bill for my U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border.

Just last month, the House passed my bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses. With Congressman Lawler, I also introduced legislation to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance we can trust, out of the hands of Hamas terrorists.

Here at home, we’re going to keep working across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program, so every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.

This is not a red or blue issue. It’s about the safety of our families. Our Jersey Values mean that we don’t allow our communities to be torn apart. We stand together and protect one another. That’s exactly what we’re doing here today in Tenafly, just feet from Edan Alexander.

So today, we remember. We honor those we lost. We thank the heroes. And we recommit ourselves to the work ahead.

We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head.

And we will never stop fighting for a day when Hamas has laid down its arms for good, and Israelis and Palestinians alike can live in peace.

If we keep doing that, I know that here, in the greatest country in the world, antisemitism and hate will lose, and our best days will be ahead of us.

Thank you. God bless. And may God continue to bless and watch over the United States of America.

###

title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility
text:
Marana, Arizona — Yesterday, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined local community members in Marana for a press conference addressing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s new contract with Management and Training Corporation (MTC) to open an immigration detention facility in Marana within the next 60 days.

The press conference brought together community members and local voices to raise concerns about the proposed facility and the record of MTC, the company contracted to operate it. MTC has previously operated correctional facilities in Arizona that faced allegations and documented concerns involving conditions including sexual abuse, inadequate food, extreme heat, and prison riots. The State of Arizona has terminated previous contracts with MTC under both Democratic and Republican governors.

Earlier this year, Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem. This comes after Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem and joined community members earlier in the year at a press conference alongside Reps. Stanton and Ansari.

A copy of her remarks are below:

“Buenas tardes. Thank you to PRICE for organizing this press conference.

We’re here today because DHS is once again rushing to open another private detention facility in Arizona.

Eso no está bien. Nuestra comunidad merece respuestas.

This is happening as deaths in ICE custody reach record levels – and as the agency fails to provide even the most basic care for the people already in its custody.

Just today, I learned about another disease outbreak - this time at a facility in Eloy.

Yet instead of addressing these conditions, this Administration is marching full steam ahead to fuel its cruel mass-deportation agenda.

And there is another reason we should be deeply concerned about this particular facility: Management & Training Corporation, or MTC, has a long and documented history of serious problems at facilities it has operated.

Here in Arizona, that history includes allegations of sexual abuse that were not properly reported, chronic understaffing and inadequate training, major security failures, and destructive prison riots.

In 2010, three inmates escaped from an MTC-operated prison in Kingman due to serious security failures.

While on the run, two of the escapees brutally murdered an elderly couple in New Mexico, leading to a large wrongful death settlement between the state of Arizona and the victims’ family.

Five years later, after riots at the same prison, an investigation found a “culture of disorganization, disengagement, and disregard.”

Those aren’t my words. Those are the findings that led Republican Governor Doug Ducey to terminate the state’s contract with MTC.

In 2017, at an MTC-operated ICE Processing Center in New Mexico, the DHS Office of the Inspector General raised concerns about the treatment and care of detainees.

Two people detained there died after pleading for medical help from facility staff.

This is the company the federal government is entrusting with the lives of hundreds of people here in Marana.

And they are moving fast. MTC says it plans to have this facility up and running within 60 days of signing its contract with ICE.

Sixty days.

That should alarm every person in this community, especially when there are still so many unanswered questions.

First and foremost: How many people are actually going to be held here?

A document earlier this year suggested more than 1,300, but the contract MTC signed says up to 775. Both of these numbers are significantly above the 513-bed capacity the state prison previously operated under.

Regardless of what the final number is, one thing is abundantly clear: local residents do not want this facility.

La gente de Marana merece tener voz.

Since President Trump returned to office, at least 56 people have died in ICE custody, including four in Arizona.

And now the federal government has awarded MTC a contract with a potential value of more than $355 million to operate this facility.

That is a drop in the bucket of the nearly $261 BILLION Congress has approved for immigration enforcement under Trump.

Our communities are tired of our taxpayer dollars being wasted on these private detention centers to meet arbitrary deportation quotas.

We are tired of seeing private companies profit off Trump’s cruel and inhumane immigration agenda.

No queremos más dinero para compañías privadas

While the federal government operates in secrecy, local residents and their elected officials across the country are pushing back against these facilities, using zoning, public nuisance laws, and other means.

MTC’s history of poorly-run facilities, combined with the track-record of abuses at DHS, underscore the concerns of Marana residents.

Unfortunately, the responsibility of oversight has fallen on local governments because the federal government is willfully asleep at the wheel.

We will continue asking questions.

We will continue demanding accountability.

And we will continue fighting to ensure that the people of Marana have a voice in what happens in their own community.

Vamos a seguir luchando por nuestra comunidad.

Thank you. Muchas gracias.”

###

title: Grothman Announces $17.9 Million in FEMA Aid for Storm and Tornado Recovery
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) welcomed President Donald Trump’s announcement of $17.9 million in federal disaster relief for Wisconsin communities affected by the July 27, 2026, storms in Forest, Outagamie, Vilas, and Winnebago counties.

“Thank you to President Trump for supporting Wisconsin’s recovery,” said Grothman. “I was proud to lead our bipartisan congressional delegation in urging federal support following the devastating July storms and tornado. Local officials, first responders, and community members have worked hard to help their communities recover, and federal assistance can help build on those efforts. I especially want to thank the volunteers who have given their time to help neighbors clean up and begin rebuilding. Their generosity reflects the best of Wisconsin.”

Residents with questions about federal disaster assistance or who need help working with FEMA or another federal agency are encouraged to contact Congressman Grothman’s Fond du Lac office at (920) 907-0624.

Background Information

The July 27, 2026, storms caused extensive damage across Forest, Outagamie, Vilas, and Winnebago counties. An EF3 tornado tore through the Fox Valley, causing widespread destruction in communities including Appleton and Menasha. It remained on the ground for more than 20 minutes, traveled approximately 12 miles, reached nearly one mile in width, and produced estimated winds of 136 to 165 miles per hour. More than 30,000 homes and businesses lost power.

Damage assessments conducted by FEMA and Wisconsin Emergency Management identified 2,346 residential structures affected, including 84 destroyed and 412 with major damage, with estimated losses exceeding $8.2 million. Public-sector damage exceeded $13.8 million, surpassing Wisconsin’s per-capita threshold by more than $2.4 million.

Congressman Grothman led two letters signed by every member of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation seeking federal support:

August 12: The delegation urged FEMA to work with Wisconsin Emergency Management on a Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment, an essential step toward determining eligibility for federal disaster assistance.

August 27: Following completion of those assessments, the delegation urged President Trump to approve a Major Disaster Declaration and make Individual Assistance, Public Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation assistance available.

title: Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter
text:
ATLANTA, GA — Today, four of the five members of the Georgia U.S. House of Representatives Democrat delegation and Rep. Joe Morelle of New York, the Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration that oversees federal elections, sent a letter to the Georgia State Election Board pushing back on its Sept. 30 letter to the Department of Justice seeking their intervention in the state’s voting machines ahead of the November midterms elections, which are now in just 27 days.

“We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law — and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice — is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.”

Read the full letter HERE and below.

Georgia State Election Board

2 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive SE

Floyd West Tower

Suite 324

Atlanta, Georgia 30334

Dear Mr. Mills:

We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law—and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice—is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.

There is absolutely no ambiguity on this point: The voting system used by Georgia voters complies with state and federal law. Your unsubstantiated claim that Georgia’s voting system is “inconsistent” with the requirements of the Help America Vote Act (“HAVA”) is deeply troubling; one would expect that someone in your position would have some basic understanding of applicable federal election law. HAVA mandates that the United States Election Assistance Commission (“EAC”) “provide certification, decertification, and recertification of voting systems, as well as the accreditation of voting system testing laboratories.” The EAC also issues Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (“VVSG”), which cover “pre-voting, voting, and post-voting operations consistent with the definition of a voting system in HAVA Section 301(a).” And, as you should know, a state’s voting devices and software “must meet [VVSG specifications] in order to receive certification from the EAC.” Of course, Georgia’s voting system has undergone the EAC’s thorough testing process, as evidenced by the fact that the EAC has certified Georgia’s voting system, as required by Georgia’s statutory and regulatory regime.

The intent of your letter is clear—to serve as a pretext for undermining public confidence in Georgia’s election results this November. Americans should know that the State Election Board does not administer Georgia’s elections. That responsibility rests with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of State’s Elections Division. The SEB has important statutory oversight and rulemaking responsibilities, but those responsibilities should not be conflated with the actual administration and certification of Georgia elections. Nor should any erroneous SEB communication to the Department of Justice concerning Georgia’s elections be understood as anything more than partisan political actors’ attempt to justify future attempts to overturn a free and fair American election—an extraordinarily serious, and cynical, misuse of official communication.

Public confidence in elections depends in substantial part upon public officials communicating accurately, responsibly, and within the scope of their statutory authority—and without incompetently, or intentionally, mischaracterizing the law. Georgians have used the state’s voting system for three straight federal elections—elections won by both Republicans and Democrats. And Georgia has one of the most rigorous, robust post-election audit regimes in the country—this is how we know that Georgia’s elections are free, fair, and secure. You should therefore promptly clarify the record, correct any inaccurate characterization of HAVA or Georgia’s voting-system requirements, and make clear that Georgia’s elections are administered by the Secretary of State and conducted using voting systems that have satisfied the certification requirements established by state and federal law.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Reps. Joe Morelle (NY-25), Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Everton Blair (GA-13).

###

title: Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó nueva información y documentación sobre el proceso de adquisición y contratación de generación temporera adjudicado al consorcio encabezado por Power Expectations, LLC, tras identificar interrogantes en los documentos producidos al Congreso sobre la investigación y el manejo de alegaciones surgidas durante el proceso competitivo.

En una carta dirigida al Zar de Energía, Josué Colón Ortiz, y al presidente del Third Party Procurement Office (3PPO), Osvaldo Carlo Linares, el Comisionado Residente solicita información para esclarecer qué se investigó sobre la alegada firma no autorizada de Enchanted Rock, quién realizó esa revisión, con qué autoridad, y por qué transcurrieron casi más de siete semanas antes de referir el asunto a las autoridades competentes.

La gestión da seguimiento a una carta enviada por el Comisionado Residente el 3 de septiembre. Tras examinar los informes, referidos y comunicaciones producidos al Congreso, su oficina identificó que un informe de 3PPO del 8 de agosto describió una “revisión exhaustiva” de las alegaciones, mientras que una comunicación enviada al día siguiente indicó que la revisión se había limitado a evaluar la suficiencia de la documentación sometida durante el proceso competitivo.

“Desde nuestra primera solicitud hemos estado revisando cuidadosamente los documentos y siguiendo los hechos. La información que recibimos nos permitió avanzar, pero también levantó preguntas adicionales que ahora corresponde aclarar”, expresó el Comisionado Residente. “Queremos entender con precisión qué se revisó, qué se determinó y cómo se tomaron las decisiones durante este proceso.”

A partir de esa revisión, el Comisionado Residente identificó varias áreas que aún requieren aclaración y, en esta carta, busca precisar:

El propósito y alcance de la revisión realizada por 3PPO y qué asuntos permanecían sin resolver.

La cronología de las gestiones realizadas entre el 17 de junio y el 10 de agosto.

Qué información y hallazgos existían cuando el asunto fue referido al Departamento de Justicia de Puerto Rico y a las autoridades federales.

Cuándo fueron informadas la AEE y la Junta de Supervisión Fiscal, y cómo se tomaron las decisiones de informarles.

Las comunicaciones y documentos internos relacionados con la revisión y el manejo de las alegaciones.

La información deberá ser entregada no más tarde del 15 de octubre de 2026.

“Estamos dando seguimiento a lo que surge de los propios documentos y vamos a continuar procurando las respuestas que aún están pendientes”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

###

title: Hoyer Statement Marking Three Years Since the October 7th Attack on Israel
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement marking three years since Hamas' attack on Israel on October 7, 2023:

“As Israel and Jewish communities around the world mark the somber anniversary of the 10/7 attacks, I join in mourning those lost, grieving with families whose pain remains fresh, and extending my prayers to those trying to rebuild their lives in freedom after being rescued from captivity. Spending time with hostages’ families while they were still held in Gaza, I saw firsthand the pain they suffered. No family should ever have to experience what they went through. I remain awed by the resolve I witnessed in them as we worked to secure their loved-ones’ release.

“Three years ago, the world witnessed the brutality and inhumanity of Hamas terror in disturbing detail. The 10/7 attacks were not only the worst massacre committed against the Jewish people since the Holocaust. They were also a reminder of what can happen when vile hatreds are allowed to fester unchecked, taught to schoolchildren and celebrated instead of expunged from society. The events of that day made it clear that the likes of Hamas can never again be allowed to rule over a population. The innocent people of Gaza must be freed from Hamas terror, just as Israelis must be able to live without the constant threat of another 10/7.

“Make no mistake: 10/7/23 was a day of murder, of sexual violence, of destruction, and of the kidnapping of innocents of all ages. It was a day when attempted genocide met heroic resistance, as Israelis fought bravely to protect their homes and their children against a vicious attempt to erase the Jewish people from their ancestral homeland through violence. Anyone who questions or denies the truth of that day must reckon with the overwhelming evidence of Hamas’s brutality against civilians, which can never be justified.

“I will continue to stand with the people of Israel against hatred and terror, against isolation and disinformation. I will continue to stand up for the Zionist ideal of a safe and secure Israel living at peace with its neighbors and safeguarding the equal rights of all its citizens through a flourishing democracy. That is what Israelis have strived for over decades, what Jews worldwide have prayed for over centuries, and what all who cherish freedom and justice ought to defend now.

“May the memory of all who were lost on 10/7 and in the three years since be a comfort and a blessing to Israel and to us all as we work for the better future we know is still possible.

title: Maryland Delegation Members Push for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), and Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) were joined by Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and U.S. Representatives Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) in requesting $11 million for U.S. Cyber Command as Congress works to complete the Fiscal Year 2027 defense appropriations. In the letter to Appropriations Committee leadership, the lawmakers stressed the importance of the health and wellbeing of the service members and civilian employees of U.S. Cyber Command, as well as the importance of their work to our national security. The $11 million program increase would fund U.S. Cyber Command’s high-performance team training, an operation aimed at improving care for service members, including helping commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, care, and resilience practices.

The lawmakers begin, “We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent military operations missions.”

“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” they continue.

On the need for funding for High Performance Team Training at Cyber Command, the lawmakers note, “The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Dear Chairman Cole, Ranking Member DeLauro, Chair Collins, and Vice Chair Murray:

We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions.

As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear.

Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively “deployed in place” for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.

These challenges are particularly relevant at Fort Meade, where U.S. Cyber Command, the National Security Agency, military cyber components, and other national security organizations operate within a highly secure and interconnected environment. Although Maryland has a significant network of military, federal, and civilian health resources, traditional centralized-care models do not always give cyber personnel timely access to appropriately cleared professionals in the facilities where they work.

Congress and the Department have already recognized this gap. Congress previously directed a review of the psychological and occupational demands placed on cyber operators, and the Department subsequently acknowledged that existing resources did not fully meet the needs of the U.S. Cyber Command. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) also expanded mental health services intended to address the U.S. Cyber Command’s unique requirements by integrating behavioral health professionals with security clearances within cyber units. Nevertheless, dedicated support teams and embedded care have not been implemented consistently across the force.

The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.

This represents a modest investment compared with U.S. Cyber Command’s broader annual budget and the strategic value of its highly trained workforce. Recruiting, clearing, and developing cyber operators takes years. Losing experienced personnel harms Maryland families, disrupts operational teams, increases replacement and training costs, and reduces the Nation’s ability to defend critical systems and conduct cyber missions.

Accordingly, we respectfully request that the final Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act retain the following program increase:

12D CYBERSPACE OPERATIONS

High Performance Team Training ........................................ $11,000,000

Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again.

We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families.

title: Reps. Jackson and Mfume Introduce Bill Requiring the U.S. to Rejoin the WHO and Help Contain the Fastest-Growing Ebola Outbreak on Record
text:
Image

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

October 7, 2026

Reps. Jackson and Mfume Introduce Bill Requiring the U.S. to Rejoin the WHO and Help Contain the Fastest-Growing Ebola Outbreak on Record

WASHINGTON, DC – In September, Congressman Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01) and Congressman Kweisi Mfume (MD-07) introduced the Epidemic Barrier and Outbreak Leadership Act, or the EBOLA Act (H.R.10345), which would require the President to rejoin the World Health Organization within 30 days of enactment and direct the United States to begin working with the WHO immediately on the Ebola outbreak in Central and Eastern Africa. The bill is the House companion to legislation introduced by Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

Per the World Health Organization's September 20 Situation Report, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has passed 7,700 confirmed cases and 3,732 confirmed deaths in a little over two months, a faster rate of spread than any previous Ebola outbreak. By comparison, the 2014 West Africa outbreak had roughly 40 suspected cases when the international response began. Fighting between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Rwanda-backed M23 has cut off humanitarian access to some of the areas where the virus is spreading fastest, and the WHO and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention are running the global response without American participation.

"Every American family should be concerned that when this dangerous outbreak began, our own government did not hear about it for nine days because we are no longer in the room," said Congressman Jackson. "While Ebola continues to spread and communities are living in fear and desperate for support, the United States is on the sidelines, cruelly abandoning the humanitarian mission that our nation guided for decades. In June, I co-led a letter with 74 of my colleagues warning that America's retreat from the global health system would leave us exposed and vulnerable. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CDC Acting Director Jay Bhattacharya did not heed our warnings, and that's exactly what has happened. The answer is straightforward: America is safer when we invest in partnerships that have long advanced both our moral responsibilities and American interests. I am proud to co-lead this legislation with Congressman Mfume to require the U.S. to rejoin the WHO and stop treating the health of families in Central and Eastern Africa as separate from the health of families on the South Side of Chicago."

"President Trump pulled the United States out of the World Health Organization and told Americans we would be safer for it. It was a foolish decision the day he made it, and sadly, with Ebola now spreading faster than any outbreak of it we have seen, it did not take long to become a dangerous one," said Congressman Mfume. "This Administration also cut foreign assistance and stalled funding for the vaccine organizations that stop outbreaks abroad before they reach us, including Gavi. Every one of those choices made this crisis worse and left Americans more vulnerable. Protecting American families means working alongside the health experts tracking this virus, not turning our backs on them. The House should take this bill up without delay."

President Trump signed Executive Order 14155 in January 2025, beginning the withdrawal of the United States from the WHO, and the withdrawal was completed in January 2026. It ended nearly all American support for the organization and pulled back U.S. personnel and contracts. One consequence is that the State Department and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention cannot retrieve personal protective equipment that American taxpayers paid for and that is being held in WHO facilities near the affected region. Another is timing: the United States did not learn of this outbreak until nine days after the WHO did.

Additional House Cosponsors include: Yvette Clarke, Jasmine Crockett, Danny Davis, Madeleine Dean, Pramila Jayapal, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Stephen Lynch, Sarah McBride, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Johnny Olszewski, Ilhan Omar, Deborah Ross, Rashida Tlaib, Nydia Velázquez.

title: Brownley and Houchin Introduce National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month Resolution
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN) announced the introduction of a resolution recognizing October 2026 as National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month. Observed annually in October, National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month raises public awareness of learning disabilities, promotes early and accurate diagnoses, and highlights the importance of ensuring individuals have access to the resources, tools, and support they need to succeed in school, the workplace, and their communities.

“Having a learning disability should never stand in the way of a person’s ability to pursue their goals and achieve success,” said Congresswoman Brownley. “I began my career in public service to ensure that individuals like my daughter, who has dyslexia, have access to the resources and tools that empower them to learn and grow with confidence. I am grateful for Congresswoman Houchin’s partnership in recognizing National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month as we work to foster positive and supportive learning environments and improve learning outcomes and lived experiences for people with learning disabilities.”

“Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, and that starts with the early identification of learning disabilities,” said Congresswoman Houchin. “Students who struggle quickly fall through the cracks of our education system. That’s why I am proud to recognize National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month alongside Congresswoman Brownley. We can, and should, do more to screen children as early as possible for learning challenges, like dyslexia, and this resolution brings awareness to the issue.”

This resolution is endorsed by the National Center for Learning Disabilities, a leading non-profit organization focused on building community, sharing resources, and shaping policy to help individuals with learning and attention issues.

The full text of the resolution can be found here.

title: Brownley, Congressional Colleagues Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) joined 189 Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.

In the House, the letter is led by Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13). In the Senate, the letter is led by Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Senator Ben RayLuján (D-NM).

The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.

“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”

Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page482 of Project 2025.

title: Kamlager-Dove, Meeks Push State Department for Answers on Brazil
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Co-Chair of the Congressional Brazil Caucus, and Gregory W. Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, led 10 Members of Congress in demanding answers from the State Department about its decision to revoke Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s diplomatic visa.

In their letter, the lawmakers condemned the decision as an unnecessary escalation that threatens U.S.-Brazil relations and undermines American interests in the Western Hemisphere. They emphasized Brazil’s importance as a major democracy and regional security and trading partner.

“This unnecessary escalation is the latest of a series of actions that has driven a rupture in our relationship with the largest democracy and economy in South America. At a time when the Trump Administration claims to be prioritizing the Western Hemisphere, this misguided decision further damages America’s reputation in the region and pushes Brazil closer to the hands of our adversaries,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers also criticized what they described as the Trump Administration’s sustained effort to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections. They cited State Department officials’ meetings with former President Bolsonaro, sanctions against Supreme Court Justice de Moraes, and statements questioning the integrity of Brazil’s elections as actions threatening the country’s democratic institutions and electoral processes.

“Congress therefore has an obligation to understand why the Department of State departed from established practices and took the extraordinary step to revoke the Brazilian Ambassador’s visa,” concluded the lawmakers.

The letter can be viewed in full here.

In addition to Reps. Kamlager-Dove and Ranking Member Meeks, the letter was signed by James P. McGovern, Pramila Jayapal, Nydia M. Velázquez, Jonathan L. Jackson, Sylvia R. Garcia, Dina Titus, Yvette D. Clarke, Mike Quigley, Jasmine Crockett, and Madeleine Dean.

title: Kamlager-Dove Statement on Three Years Since October 7th
text:
"October 7th is a deeply painful day for so many here in Los Angeles and around the world. Today, we remember the nearly 1,200 innocent lives murdered on the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, as well as the dozens of hostages who died in Hamas captivity. We also remember the immense pain, suffering, and loss experienced by both Israelis and Palestinians in the war that followed, including the tragic deaths of 60,000 civilians in Gaza.

There can never be another October 7th, nor a repetition of the brutality and suffering that followed. title: Whip Clark, Markey, Warren, Massachusetts Delegation Members Statement on Massachusetts Nurses Negotiations
text:
BOSTON, MA — Today, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA-05), Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Representatives Richard Neal (MA-01), Jim McGovern (MA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), and Bill Keating (MA-09) released the following statement urging Mass General Brigham (MGB) and the Massachusetts Nurses Association (MNA) to continue their negotiations to avert a strike at Brigham and Women’s Hospital.

“Nurses are the backbone of our healthcare system—our loved ones and communities rely on them each and every day. Our nurses deserve fair contracts that reflect that standard of care. Their voices must be heard.

“The nurses at Brigham and Women’s Hospital have demonstrated their willingness to continue negotiating with Mass General Brigham leadership to arrive at an agreement that works for nurses, patients, and our hospitals. A strike has the potential for serious impacts on our communities, patients, and healthcare workers, which we know no nurse or patient wishes to experience.

“We call on Mass General Brigham to remain at the bargaining table with the Massachusetts Nurses Association and work to reach a good faith agreement that addresses the needs of nurses, patients, and our constituents. Massachusetts is renowned for its healthcare system, in which Mass General Brigham and its nurses are crucial partners, and we hope the parties can reach an agreement.”

title: Kean Delivers $1 Million in Federal Funds to Hopatcong for Lead Service Line Replacements
text:
(October 7, 2026) HOPATCONG, NJ – On Monday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) presented $1 million to Hopatcong Borough for the initial phase of lead service line replacements along various roadways in Hopatcong.

Through the replacement of these lead service lines, Hopatcong will improve the quality of drinking water and reduce the risk of lead contamination in water, which poses negative health risks and negative consequences to those who ingest it.

“Families in our communities deserve safe and clean water and to know that their health, and the health of their children, is not at risk,” said Congressman Kean. “I was pleased to secure this federal funding to ensure that the water that members of the Hopatcong community use to wash their hands, to clean their dishes, and to drink is lead-free.”

“This $1 million investment in Hopatcong will make a tremendous difference as we continue the important work of replacing lead service lines and strengthening our water infrastructure,” said Hopatcong Mayor Marie Galate. “These improvements are about more than pipes—they are about protecting our residents, safeguarding our drinking water, and investing in the future of our community. I am extremely grateful to Congressman Tom Kean Jr. for advocating for Hopatcong and helping bring these critical federal dollars directly back to our residents.”

“As a member of the assembly environment committee, I think a lot about the quality of drinking water in Northwest New Jersey,” said Assemblyman Mike Inganamort. “The Hopatcong area is providing millions of gallons of drinking water to millions of New Jerseyans, and lead service line replacement is critically important for our natural environment and human health. Hopatcong, as a result of Congressman Kean’s leadership, is going to continue to be a better, stronger, healthier, more resilient community. I want to emphasize the incredible privilege it is for all of us to have someone as passionate and dedicated to New Jersey as Congressman Tom Kean, Jr., a tremendous advocate for our community.”

“This vital investment will not only modernize Hopatcong’s infrastructure but also protect public health,” said Sussex County Commissioner David Silverthorne. “These funds will help complete the initial phase of lead service line replacements, securing clean, safe drinking water for every resident. I want to sincerely thank Congressman Kean for his leadership in securing this funding, as well as Mayor Galate, the Borough Council, and the dedicated Borough employees for their untiring work to uphold and improve Hopatcong’s quality of life for its residents.”

“Being the municipal engineer for 20 years and knowing a lot of the residents, this project really hits home for Hopatcong families,” said Hopatcong Municipal Engineer John Ruschke. “Hopatcong has been struggling for years and years to keep up with water infrastructure, and it is critical that we change the dilapidated systems currently in place and keep our residents safe and healthy. It’s great to see families benefitting directly from this federal funding, because alongside improving the infrastructure, we’re improving quality of life for Hopatcong residents.”

Since taking office, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. has secured more than $14.5 million for water infrastructure in New Jersey’s Seventh Congressional District through the Community Project Funding process.

title: Kean Delivers $560,000 in Federal Funds to Mount Arlington for Memorial Pond Stormwater Dredging
text:
(October 7, 2026) MOUNT ARLINGTON, NJ – On Monday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) presented $560,000 to Mount Arlington Borough to address stormwater drainage in the local community.

Mount Arlington’s Memorial Pond manages stormwater and acts as a basin before it enters Lake Hopatcong. Over time, the pond has filled up with sediment, and this federal funding will support a necessary dredging project.

“I am pleased to deliver this federal funding in order to protect the health and water quality of both Memorial Pond and Lake Hopatcong,” said Congressman Kean. “This $560,000 will fund a dredging project in Memorial Pond that will help ensure that Lake Hopatcong can continue being used by New Jerseyans for recreational activities.”

“Thanks to a $560,000 federal investment secured by Congressman Tom Kean, Jr., Mount Arlington can move forward with the engineering, environmental analysis and dredging needed to restore Memorial Pond, improve stormwater management and help protect the water quality of Lake Hopatcong,” said Mount Arlington Mayor Michael Stanzilis. “This funding will support the work necessary to restore the pond’s beauty and environmental health while strengthening the protection of this important regional natural resource.”

Mayor Stanzilis continued, “As Mayor, protecting our environment, and particularly Lake Hopatcong, has always been a priority. Memorial Pond is a beautiful and special part of our community, and I look forward to seeing it restored for future generations. I thank Congressman Kean for recognizing the importance of this project and for his continued partnership with Mount Arlington.”

“With this money, Memorial Pond can be cleaned for the use and benefit of all residents,” said State Senator Anthony Bucco. “When this pond is cleaned and dredged, it will have a direct impact on making sure that Lake Hopatcong continues to have the quality of water that this area needs for recreation and the economy. The residents of Mount Arlington are winners today as a result of the work of Congressman Kean.”

“Congressman Kean reminds us that no project or town is too small,” said Assemblywoman Aura Dunn. “This was needed funding for a project that could not have otherwise happened. We thank Congressman Kean for his leadership down in Washington and for making sure they all remember how important Mount Arlington is.”

“Congressman Kean’s work to secure this grant for a small town like Mount Arlington will not only impact this park, but also everything downstream,” said Morris County Commissioner Tayfun Selen. “Morris County and Sussex County share Lake Hopatcong, and what is being done to improve a tiny pond and the environment of this small community, will flow downstream to improve the quality of life for an entire region.”

“What enters Memorial Pond doesn't stay in Memorial Pond, eventually it all flows straight into Lake Hopatcong,” said Kyle Richter, Executive Director of the Lake Hopatcong Foundation. “Removing years of built-up sediment means fewer nutrients feeding harmful algal blooms, cleaner water at our beaches, and a healthier future for New Jersey's largest lake. We're grateful to Congressman Kean Jr. for securing the funding for this critical project and helping to protect and improve Lake Hopatcong.”
