title: Raskin Introduces Legislation to Preserve and Document Trump Propaganda and Educate Future Generations on Resistance to Corruption and Authoritarianism
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.— As the Trump Administration prepares propaganda signage to adorn the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced legislation to ensure future generations learn about President Donald Trump’s commitment to censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history. The Preserving and Remembering the History of Trump and other Tyrants Act directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to collect and preserve artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism during the Trump presidencies as the basis for a permanent exhibition in the National Museum of American History.

Last month, the Department of the Interior—under orders from President Trump—created propaganda signage to place outside of the National Museum of American History, warning visitors of curators’ “personal, radical ideologies.” Preserving these signs will educate Americans on how authoritarians attempt to control media, government and culture.

“Unlike President Trump’s project of censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history, my legislation will forever preserve his manifestations of authoritarian narcissism and his propagandistic assault on American history and American democracy,” said Rep. Raskin. “To avoid repeating this descent into authoritarianism, we must study this corrupt President’s actions and allow the public to learn about the numerous tools he deployed while attempting to remake American history in his own image and according to his own autocratic and white nationalist beliefs.”

The legislation directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to preserve the banners bearing President Trump’s face that are currently displayed outside of certain federal agencies; still images and videos from the media; personal narratives of American citizens who resisted and opposed the rise in authoritarianism in the United States; and other artifacts that the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution determines to have historical significance. The legislation also directs officials from the National Park Service to remove any signage that was erected near the National Museum of American History without the consent of Congress.

Rep. Raskin has drawn on his expertise as an American constitutional scholar as he speaks out against the Trump Administration’s authoritarian tactics. This month, he introduced a Resolution condemning President Trump and MAGA’s campaign of book bans and censorship and advocating for the American freedom to read and think freely.

title: Congresswoman Scholten Statement on New Proposal to Narrow the Scope of the Clean Water Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), Vice Ranking Member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment, released the following statement on the new proposal from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers that would narrow the scope of the Clean Water Act by redefining what qualifies as “Waters of the United States,” stripping protections from freshwater wetlands across Michigan and the country.

“Clean water should never be a partisan issue. Every family, every child, every individual deserves access to clean water – for drinking, for recreation, and for business. This unilateral move by the Trump Administration threatens to reverse decades of work and progress cleaning up our lakes, rivers, and wetlands. As Vice Ranking Member of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee, I’ve seen firsthand how the protections from the Clean Water Act keep our communities safe and have cleaned our waterways. Our children and our children’s children could be doomed to inherit polluted waterways–a problem we’ve already addressed and nearly solved. We cannot afford to go back.”

Earlier this year, Congresswoman Scholten published an article in the Harvard Law School Journal of Legislation titled “The Retreat of Cooperative Federalism: Water Rights in a Fragmented Regulatory Era.” The article argues that Congress must work with states to maintain baseline environmental protections, following decades of Supreme Court decisions — including Sackett v. EPA — that have weakened the Clean Water Act of 1972.

title: Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Bennet Demand Answers on Childhood Vaccines EO, Measles Deaths, & Delayed Vaccine Access
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Senator Michael Bennet (D-CO) led 25 colleagues in a letter to Dr. Erica Schwartz, the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to call out efforts to reject settled vaccine science and demand answers about the CDC’s efforts to implement President Trump’s childhood vaccine Executive Order (EO), underreport measles-associated deaths, and delay access to childhood immunizations.

“[...] As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health,” began the lawmakers.

The United States is facing a decline in childhood immunization rates. Recently, the CDC reported that 280,000 kindergartners did not complete their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine series. This comes as the Trump Administration has actively worked to lower the number of recommended immunizations, break up safe and effective combination shots, and promote legal action against states unaligned with such efforts.

Additionally, the CDC has a long-standing agency precedent and prides itself on “objective data collection and reporting.” At the beginning of September, numerous reports exposed that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public outbreak tracker for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continued to track these fatalities. This omission breaks with agency standards, and raises serious questions about the CDC’s willingness to resist political pressure over settled science.

“The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing,” concluded the lawmakers.

title: Congressman Brad Sherman Marks Three Years Since October 7th Attack on Israel
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), Co-Chair of the House Israel Allies Caucus, Ranking Member Emeritus of the Middle East Subcommittee, and senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement marking three years since Hamas’s October 7th, 2023 terrorist attack on Israel:

“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a barbaric and unprovoked attack against Israel, murdering more than 1,200 innocent men, women and children, including Americans, and taking some 250 people hostage in the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.

Today, we must continue to remember those who were murdered, honor their memories, stand with the survivors and families whose lives were forever changed, and recommit to ensuring that Hamas and any like-minded terrorist entity can never be allowed to govern again.

Last October, after more than two agonizing years of captivity, the remaining twenty living hostages held in Gaza finally returned home. Their release brought enormous relief, but it did not erase the suffering inflicted upon the hostages and their families, nor diminish our obligation to ensure that every terrorist organization that participated in the October 7th attack is held accountable.

The acts of brutality committed on that day – including rape and torture – should have inspired global solidarity. Instead, 3 years later, we are witnessing the return of extreme vilification of the Jewish people and the Jewish state, including through the manufactured and libelous accusation of genocide.

The United States must reject this disinformation campaign and remain steadfast in supporting Israel’s security. Hamas can never again carry out such an attack and Gaza must be governed not by terrorists, but by legitimate leadership committed to peace. This is critical to ending the tragic cycle of violence and finally allowing innocent Israelis and Palestinians to live in security.

The U.S.–Israel partnership has endured because of our shared democratic values and common determination to confront terrorism and pursue lasting security and peace. We must stand up to the antisemitism and coordinated disinformation that threatens this alliance. On this solemn anniversary, we remember the victims of October 7th and reaffirm our commitment to building a future of greater peace and security for Israelis, Palestinians, and the region.”

Since the October 7th attack, Congressman Sherman has led and co-sponsored numerous measures to support Israel’s security and hold Hamas and other terrorist organizations accountable, including legislation to sanction the Popular Resistance Committees for their participation in the October 7th massacre, strengthen Israel’s missile-defense capabilities, and counter the flow of Iranian funds to terrorist proxies.

title: Congresswoman Simon, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Landmark Olmstead Court Decision Supporting Americans with Disabilities on 27th Anniversary
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Simon (CA-12) alongside Reps. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-05), Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), and Tom Kean (R-NJ-07) introduced a bipartisan resolution commemorating the 27th anniversary of the landmark Supreme Court decision, Olmstead v. L.C.. The Olmstead decision prohibits the unnecessary institutionalization of people with disabilities and ensures Americans with disabilities can live full, independent lives and categorized the unjustified institutionalization of people with disabilities as discrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). As the Olmstead decision comes under attack from the Trump Administration, this bipartisan resolution reaffirms the right that people with disabilities have to live, work, and participate in their own homes and communities with independence and dignity.

As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, Congresswoman Simon is committed to defending the disability community from attacks by the Trump Administration and advancing policies that expand accessibility. Congresswoman Simon recently condemned the Trump Administration’s Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services’ move to dispute the Olmstead integration mandate and undermine the key protections outlined by the Olmstead decision.

"Community-based services and supports work. They are more cost-effective, produce better health and quality-of-life outcomes, and honor people with disabilities’ autonomy and self-determination. The consequences of weakening the integration mandate would be profound and impact millions of Americans’ ability to access home and community-based services that allow them to remain among their families, maintain employment, pursue education, and participate in civic life," said Congresswoman Simon. "That's why as the first congenitally blind Member to serve in Congress, I am proud to join my colleagues to reaffirm our bipartisan commitment to the Olmstead decision and fight any attempts to diminish the civil rights of the disability community."

"It is essential that people with disabilities continue to have the right to live, work, and thrive in their own communities with dignity," said Congresswoman Dingell. "This bipartisan resolution reaffirms that we will not allow hard won progress to be rolled back, and that we will continue to protect and support the rights enshrined by the Olmstead decision for every person whose lives it has changed for the better."

"Although the Olmstead decision was issued more than twenty‑five years ago, its significance remains just as strong today. I am pleased to join my colleagues in introducing this resolution, reaffirming our commitment to ending discrimination based on disability," said Congressman Kean.

"For 27 years, the Supreme Court’s decision in Olmstead v. L.C. has informed the advancement of policies to empower individuals with disabilities to live and work independently in our communities," said Congresswoman Scanlon. "Recent attempts to undermine the Olmstead integration mandate and roll back those policies raises new opportunities for discrimination against our friends and neighbors with disabilities, and harms the larger community. I’m proud to join my House colleagues in recognizing Olmstead’s anniversary and recommitting ourselves to protecting community integration for the good of all."

"Olmstead affirmed a fundamental principle: every American deserves the freedom and opportunity to build a full life in the community they call home. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Disabilities Caucus, that principle has always been at the heart of my work to break down barriers, strengthen independence, and ensure all Americans with disabilities have the resources, support, and opportunities they need to thrive. Twenty-seven years later, our responsibility is not simply to recognize the progress Olmstead made possible, but to protect it, build upon it, and ensure that progress is never reversed," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.

The resolution is endorsed by the Caring Across Generations, United Spinal, ANCOR, Autism Self Advocacy Network, National Council on Independent Living, American Association of People with Disabilities, and the National Disability Rights Network.

A copy of the resolution can be found HERE.

title: Rep. Sykes Announces $33,000 for Canal Fulton-Lawrence Township Fire Department
text:
CANAL FULTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department is receiving two Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) grant awards that will fund new firefighting equipment and a community fire safety training tool. Congresswoman Sykes supported both grant applications with letters of support.

The City of Canal Fulton received the following awards:

$17,055.55 in federal funding for a regional fire hose replacement, with a local share of $852.78, for a total project investment of $17,908.33. The project will replace attack and supply hose within the departments' shared response system.

$16,737.14 in federal funding for a fire extinguisher training system, with a local share of $836.86, for a total project investment of $17,574.00. The project will provide an augmented-reality training system that allows hands-on public education without live fire, smoke, chemical discharge, or cleanup.

Together, the awards provide $33,792.69 in federal funding toward a total investment of $35,482.33 in public safety projects.

“Our firefighters and EMS crews show up to keep our neighbors safe every day, and they must have the tools to do their jobs safely. I am proud to have supported Canal Fulton's grant applications, and I congratulate Chief Yerian and the entire department on these well-earned awards,”said Congresswoman Sykes.

“Receiving these FEMA awards is tremendous news for the Canal Fulton community and our regional fire service,” said Shawn Yerian, Fire Chief of the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department. “The funding will allow us to replace outdated fire hose that our firefighters rely on every day, while also providing a new fire extinguisher training system that addresses one of the most frequent safety-training requests we receive from local businesses.

“These are important investments in both firefighter safety and community education, and they are projects we would not have been able to move forward with at this time without federal assistance. We are extremely grateful for Congresswoman Sykes' support of our applications and her continued support of local fire and EMS services. Her assistance helped make it possible for us to bring these resources back to the community we serve.”

Congresswoman Sykes congratulates Chief Yerian and the entire Canal Fulton - Lawrence Township Fire Department on these awards and thanks them for their service to the community.

title: Rep. Sykes Announces $493,000 for TRIO Programs at the University of Akron
text:
AKRON, OHIO — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced the Department of Education has awarded the University of Akron $493,314 as part of the TRIO talent search program. This grant will be awarded annually for five years, beginning in 2026, and is expected to serve nearly 900 students each year.

“Programs like TRIO provide deserving students with the opportunity to pursue higher education,” said Rep. Sykes. “I congratulate the University of Akron for supporting first generation college students participating in the TRIO program who will go on to make a meaningful impact in our community. I am a proud supporter of TRIO and other programs that help our families in Ohio’s 13th Congressional District reach higher heights.”

“The University of Akron Educational Talent Search Program is honored to continue this important work for another five years.” said Dr. Fedearia Nicholson, Vice Provost for Student Pathways and Dean of the Williams Honors College. “This investment from the U.S. Department of Education will create meaningful opportunities for Akron and Summit County students to prepare for college, careers, and the workforce. title: Trahan Unveils CLAIM Act Discussion Draft to Hold AI Developers Accountable for Harms Caused by Their Agents
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released a discussion draft of the Clear Liability for Artificial Intelligence Misconduct (CLAIM) Act. The legislation would give those harmed by AI agents a clear path to recovery by holding developers responsible when their systems engage in conduct that would be unlawful if committed by a person.

“When someone breaks the law and hurts you, you can take them to court. That shouldn't change just because the wrongdoer is an AI agent,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Developers have already built systems capable of acting on their own and causing real damage. The CLAIM Act makes sure they answer for what their systems do.”

Specifically, the CLAIM Act:

Holds developers liable for AI misconduct. If an AI system injures a third party through conduct that would constitute negligence, an intentional tort, or a crime if committed by a person, the developer is liable. Liability does not apply where the user or a company that modified the system intended the conduct or was negligent.

Resolves uncertainty around AI and intent. Courts would presume an AI system acted with the state of mind a person taking the same actions would have had. Developers could not argue that AI is incapable of intent.

Establishes a federal cause of action. Injured parties may bring claims in federal or state court.

Preserves state law. The bill sets a federal floor and does not preempt any state law. Existing state claims and state AI laws remain fully available.

The risks the CLAIM Act addresses already exist. In July, AI agents undergoing an evaluation by OpenAI escaped their test environment and hacked into Hugging Face, another AI company. No one instructed them to do so. Leading experts have called the incident a warning shot for a future of increasingly capable AI agents acting outside their users’ control.

Under current law, third parties harmed by a misaligned AI agent face significant hurdles. Many serious harms, including hacking and fraud, require proof of intent, and courts have not settled whether an AI system’s conduct can meet that standard. Negligence and product liability claims typically require showing that a company failed to take a specific precaution or ignored a safer design. Because AI alignment remains an unsolved technical problem, developers can argue the harm occurred despite their best efforts, leaving injured parties without a remedy.

The CLAIM Act complements the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which Trahan introduced with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) to address catastrophic risks from the most advanced AI models. FRONTIER establishes transparency, independent verification, and incident reporting requirements. The CLAIM Act adds a robust liability regime that rewards developers who invest in making their systems safer.

Trahan is releasing the CLAIM Act as a discussion draft and welcomes feedback from experts, industry, advocates, and the public. In addition to comments on the draft legislation, the office welcomes answers to important questions related to the CLAIM Act and AI liability located HERE.

Comments can be submitted to MA03Leg@mail.house.gov.

A copy of the bill text can be accessed HERE.

title: Congressman Van Drew Announces Townsends Inlet Dredging
text:
Washington, DC -Today, Congressman Van Drew announced a dredging project for the Townsends Inlet Bridge in Cape May County. The navigation route under the bridge has become increasingly dangerous, with shifting sand narrowing the channel.

"Over the years, the route through Townsends Inlet has gotten smaller and more dangerous," said Congressman Van Drew. "As of today, we have an agreement in place to dredge at the bridge and make the inlet safer for recreational and commercial boats. My office is working with local, state, and federal governments to fund, permit, and execute this project. We are using dredging equipment already in the area for the Avalon beach replenishment project to get this done quickly while saving millions of dollars for taxpayers. Looking ahead, I am working to have Townsends Inlet studied as a federal navigation channel so we can establish a permanent plan for maintaining this waterway."

"Avalon deeply appreciates the direction and guidance provided by Congressman Van Drew to achieve our mutual stakeholder objective of providing safe navigation through Townsend's Inlet," said Avalon Mayor John McCorristin. "Courtesy of an emergency beach fill acquired by the Congressman for the Borough, we are now able to partner with our neighbors in Sea Isle and the dredging company already in the Inlet to improve navigational safety and preserve the commercial and recreational boating opportunities that have a long lineage in Avalon and in Cape May County."

"This project shows what effective government looks like when we work together with a shared commitment to getting things done," said Sea Isle Mayor Len Desiderio. "Thanks to Congressman Van Drew's leadership and our strong partnership with Avalon, we are moving forward with a plan that will ensure a safe and reliable navigational route through this vital waterway."

"Cape May County is putting $250,000 toward this emergency dredge because Townsends Inlet bridge is at risk of becoming an unsafe maritime passage," said Cape May County Commissioner Patrick Rosenello. "With the dredge company already mobilized for the Avalon beach fill, the $1.5 million estimated construction costs are significantly less. Thanks to Congressman Van Drew for bringing Avalon, Sea Isle City, the Army Corps, the Bridge Commission, and NJDEP together quickly to address a project that simply could not wait."

"The Bridge Commission is contributing $50,000 towards the project, which will help protect the Townsends Inlet bridge," said Cape May County Bridge Commission Chair Carol Brand. "The Bridge Commission is happy to support this much needed project, and we applaud Congressman Van Drew's efforts in facilitating the necessary emergency permits."

title: Vindman, Krishnamoorthi Introduce Legislation to Strengthen U.S. Military Readiness Through Lessons from Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), a 25-year Army veteran, and Raja Krishnamoorthi (Ill.-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, introduced legislation that would require the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.

The Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training.

“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. “As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”

“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” said Krishnamoorthi. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”

BACKGROUND

Vindman first announced the legislation following a bipartisan congressional delegation visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials to discuss the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.

In September 2026, Vindman voted to pass legislation that would impose sanctions on Russia.

Following his retirement from the U.S. Army, Vindman spent 18 months investigating war crimes in Ukraine, completing 14 trips as a senior consultant for a Department of State-funded program. Since coming to Congress, he has returned to Ukraine twice on bipartisan congressional delegation trips. Vindman is a recognized expert in international criminal law and has published extensively on national security and international relations.

title: Sen. Banks Calls for Stronger Protections Against Insider Threats at Frontier SI Companies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought supporting the Trump administration’s work to deploy advanced super intelligence (SI) across the Department of War and calling for continued action to protect the military SI systems from insider threats.

The Department has established partnerships to deliver American capabilities to U.S. warfighters and preserve America’s advantage over communist China. As these partnerships grow, a compromised or malicious insider at SI company could expose sensitive information about military SI applications, steal model weights, sabotage systems, or insert backdoors that threaten department missions.

Read the full letter here or below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth and Director Vought,

I commend the Department of War (DOW) for moving quickly to put advanced super intelligence (SI) in the hands of our warfighters. The agreements the Department announced in May with companies like OpenAI and Google will help America keep its lead over the People’s Republic of China (PRC).[1] At the same time, as the Department relies more on these companies, insider threats in the frontier SI industry are becoming a direct risk to military operations. I am writing to encourage and support your essential work to assess and reduce these insider threats.

The Department has correctly recognized that the race to develop and deploy advanced SI will be a defining national security issue of our time. Secretary Hegseth has seen the need to deploy SI rapidly throughout DOW, highlighting that America must maintain an advantage in the SI race and emphasizing that DOW is “trying to do everything we can to maintain that advantage.[2]”

To maintain the SI advantage, the Department has entered into strong partnerships with leading frontier SI developers in private industry. As frontier models develop stronger capabilities in areas like cyber-offense and military planning, these agreements with frontier SI companies will become increasingly important for U.S. national security.

Meanwhile, the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) also recognizes the strategic importance of frontier SI, and the CCP is taking strong steps to target America’s SI industry. One particularly concerning threat comes from insiders at American SI companies. In January, a federal jury convicted a former Google engineer of economic espionage. He stole over 2,000 pages of confidential information about Google’s SI technology to benefit PRC-based companies.[3] This is not surprising: the CCP has a long history of conducting economic espionage against U.S. industries, especially those that are critical for national security.

As the Department continues to expand its partnerships with the frontier SI industry, mitigating insider threats will become increasingly important. Frontier SI companies employ researchers from around the world, including many from the PRC. Unfortunately, a single compromised or malicious insider with sufficient access could reveal secret information about military uses of SI, expose model weights, or attempt to sabotage SI systems via backdoors. This is especially significant in the context of partnerships between DOW and the frontier SI industry, as insider threats at companies can threaten the effectiveness of Department warfighting activities.

The frontier SI companies already have some sort of security programs to manage insider threats. However, the scale of the threat from the CCP is enormous, and private industry will not be able to sufficiently handle this threat on its own. An ongoing conversation between the Department and private industry will be needed to ensure that insider threats are adequately assessed and mitigated. These efforts will also require sufficient resources. DOW, the Office of Management and Budget, and Congress will need to work together to provide sufficient funding and personnel for counterintelligence programs and insider threat reduction efforts.

As a first step, I believe Congress must ensure that the Department has the information and resources it needs to assess these threats. The Department should be empowered to obtain relevant information from the frontier SI companies about how they currently assess insider threats, the counterintelligence measures they have in place, which assets they consider most sensitive, the access controls protecting the most sensitive assets, and gaps in current programs.

This approach does not fully solve the problem, but it is a critical first step. It would provide the Department with greater visibility into the threat environment, ensure it has access to information to better assess the current state of security efforts, and help identify areas in which government and industry can work together to strengthen protections against insider threats.

As you strengthen partnerships with frontier SI companies and work to protect SI systems from insider threats, I request a staff-level briefing to discuss the following topics:

Risks from insider threats.What are the most significant national security risks from CCP-linked insiders at frontier SI companies, including espionage on DOW SI use, model theft, or the insertion of backdoors?

Current work on insider threat reduction. Which offices within the Department lead efforts to assess insider threats at frontier SI companies? How does the Department currently work with private industry to assess and mitigate insider threats? What are the most significant gaps relating to assessing existing practices or developing mitigation strategies?

Resources and budget. What additional funding, personnel, or other resources would help DOW work with frontier SI companies to assess and mitigate insider threats?

Partnerships between the Department and frontier SI companies are essential for ensuring American SI dominance. These partnerships must be secure against PRC insider threats, and I look forward to supporting your work on this critical topic.

title: Bennet, Schrier Lead Colleagues to Demand Answers on Childhood Vaccines EO, Measles Deaths, & Delayed Vaccine Access
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet and U.S. Representative Kim Schrier, M.D. (D-Wash.) led 29 colleagues in a letter to Dr. Erica Schwartz, the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to call out efforts to reject settled vaccine science and demand answers about the CDC’s efforts to implement President Trump’s childhood vaccine Executive Order (EO), underreport measles-associated deaths, and delay access to childhood immunizations.

“[…] As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health,” began the lawmakers.

The United States is facing a decline in childhood immunization rates. Recently, the CDC reported that 280,000 kindergartners did not complete their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine series. This comes as the Trump administration has actively worked to lower the number of recommended immunizations, break up safe and effective combination shots, and promote legal action against states unaligned with such efforts.

Additionally, the CDC has a long-standing agency precedent and prides itself on “objective data collection and reporting.” At the beginning of September, numerous reports exposed that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public outbreak tracker for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continued to track these fatalities. This omission breaks with agency standards, and raises serious questions about the CDC’s willingness to resist political pressure over settled science.

“The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing,” concluded the lawmakers.

Bennet has consistently fought against the Trump administration’s anti-science agenda. In September 2026, Bennet reiterated his call on the Senate floor for Trump to rescind the unscientific childhood vaccine executive order and fire the HHS Secretary, Robert Kennedy Jr. Bennet also questioned HHS Deputy Secretary Nominee Chris Klomp during his confirmation hearing before the Senate Finance Committee about Trump and Kennedy’s reckless anti-vaccine efforts resulting in chaos and confusion for children and families. In August 2026, Bennet led 90 of his Congressional colleagues to demand Trump rescind his executive order that directs federal health agencies to overhaul longstanding childhood vaccine recommendations and encourages states to reconsider school immunization requirements. Bennet also issued a statement immediately following the announcement of that executive order.

In April 2026, Bennet questioned Kennedy during a Senate Finance Committee hearing on his skepticism of childhood vaccines amidst the largest measles outbreak in the U.S. in over thirty years. Additionally, in March2025 and 2026, Bennet joined his colleagues in sending a letter to Kennedy to demand the department reverse changes to the CDC and the Food and Drug Administration websites that promote false and dangerous information about autism. In September 2025, he questioned Kennedy during a Senate Finance Committee hearing on his actions undermining vaccine safety and access for American families. Bennet also joined members of the Senate Finance Committee in issuing a statement calling on Kennedy to resign due to the danger he poses to America’s health, his lies to Congress, and his spread of disinformation.

In addition to Bennet and Schrier, U.S. Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) as well as U.S. Representatives Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.), Troy Carter (D-La.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.), Chris Deluzio (D-Pa.), Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.), Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), Jonathan Jackson (D-IlI.), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IlI.), Mike Levin (D-Calif.), Doris Matsui (D-Calif), Betty McCollum (D-Minn.), Joseph Morelle (D-N.Y.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Brittany Pettersen (D-Colo.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Mark Takano (D-Calif.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) signed the letter.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dr. Schwartz:

At your confirmation hearing, you said that your “sacred responsibility” as Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) would be to provide “clear, honest, and evidence-based” public health guidance and to “never betray the science.” In the short time since your confirmation as CDC Director, the health and safety of our children have been subjected to further chaos and confusion. As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health.

The CDC recently reported that the number of children up-to-date on their immunizations has continued to decline, including 280,000 kindergartners who did not complete the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) series. Instead of spending time and dedicating resources to promote the need for childhood immunizations, President Trump called for breaking up combination shots like the MMR vaccine into single-disease shots that are not available in the United States, cutting the number of diseases every child is recommended to be protected against from 18 to 11, and directing the Attorney General to advance legal challenges to state laws. Following this EO, HHS issued an RFI on the childhood immunization schedule, aimed at bypassing the CDC and the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, which have developed recommendations for over 60 years. These efforts are only a part of the systematic attacks spearheaded by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. CDC’s scientists, not political appointees, should be at the center of any decision about the childhood immunization schedule.

During this same timeframe, CDC’s public actions under your leadership raise serious concerns regarding your willingness to counter these unscientific measures – including reports that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public national mortality count for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continue to track these fatalities. This is a clear break from long-standing agency precedent, including last year’s standard reporting of measles deaths in Texas and directly contradicts the commitment to “objective data collection and reporting” that has been CDC’s foundation. If the agency under your leadership is altering verified state data to fit political preferences, the pledge you made at your confirmation hearing has already been broken.

We request responses to the following questions in writing by October 16, 2026.

CDC Role on the Executive Order on Childhood Vaccines

Did anyone from the White House or HHS consult you about the Executive Order either before or after it was issued?

a. If so, who reached out, what was discussed, and when did these communication(s) occur?

b. If not, have you raised, or do you plan to raise, any concerns with President Trump, Secretary Kennedy, or any other administration official(s)?

How is the CDC planning to implement the provisions outlined in the EO? What steps have been taken already and what are planned? Please provide a detailed summary of these plans.

What role, if any, did CDC career scientists have in developing the EO’s recommendations?

The EO directs the Secretary, acting through the HHS Task Force on Safer Childhood Vaccines, to present plans to the President within 90 days on single-disease vaccine options, the timing and sequencing of childhood vaccines, and safety monitoring. What role does the CDC have in developing those plans, and which CDC officials are participating?

The EO recommends reducing the number of routine immunizations from 18 to 11. Do you support that specific recommendation? What scientific evidence supports removing the other diseases from the immunizations recommended for all children, and has the CDC estimated the additional illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths that could result?

Do you agree that spacing out immunizations across additional visits lengthens the window of vulnerability for infants and young children? If not, please provide the evidence on which CDC relies.

The EO recommends separating combination shots like MMR into single-disease shots. No single-disease MMR vaccine is currently available in the United States. Other countries that have tried this – like Japan in the 1990s – saw increased outbreaks, ultimately resulting in them reverting to a combination shot. Do you support this specific provision even though it is not currently available in the U.S., would require more shots and doctor visits, and lacks scientific backing? Why is the federal government recommending an option to families that does not exist, causing additional confusion?

What scientific evidence supports separating combination vaccines like MMR into single-disease doses? Please provide CDC analyses of peer-reviewed studies, epidemiological analyses, or international precedent that demonstrates this change would actually improve health outcomes. If no such evidence exists, will you decline to implement this provision?

The public comment period for the HHS RFI closed on September 20, 2026. Did CDC scientists review or contribute to the RFI before it was published? What role will CDC scientists have in reviewing the comments and in any resulting changes to the categories of federal vaccine recommendations?

Data Collection and Reporting

Has the CDC instituted a new policy for reviewing, altering, or withholding state-reported health data before public posting?

a. If so, what scientific evidence supports this change and what deliberations occurred?

b. If there is no such policy, on what basis were Pennsylvania’s measles deaths excluded from the public tracker, and who at CDC authorized that exclusion?

As of today, the CDC has only included two of the measles-associated deaths reported by the State of Pennsylvania. What specific technical, scientific, or epidemiological basis justified excluding Pennsylvania’s state-reported measles deaths from the CDC’s public tracker while still including them on internal trackers?

Did any White House or HHS officials contact you or your staff regarding the public reporting of Pennsylvania’s measles deaths? Please provide all communication between CDC leadership and any White House or HHS official regarding the reporting of state-verified measles deaths since your confirmation.

Vaccines for Children Program

Why did the CDC delay opening orders for COVID vaccines through the Vaccines for Children Program (VFC)? Please provide the timeline of when decisions were made concerning the VFC program.

What made the CDC decide to open ordering for COVID vaccines through the VFC program on September 24, 2026 and not earlier?

Have you personally been asked by Secretary Kennedy, the White House, or any other HHS or Trump administration official to delay or condition VFC activation for the COVID vaccine? If so, please describe the request and identify who made it. If such a request was made in writing, please provide it.

Who at CDC, HHS, or the White House made the decision to delay VFC activation for the COVID vaccine, and on what basis? Please produce all internal communications, memoranda, and legal or scientific analyses supporting that decision.

What guidance has CDC provided to state health departments, pediatricians, and VFC providers about the status of COVID vaccines under VFC? How soon can VFC vaccines be expected to be in the possession of clinicians and accessible for children?

The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing.

title: Booker, Blunt Rochester Recognize October as World Menopause Awareness Month
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.–U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) introduced a resolution recognizing October 2026 as World Menopause Awareness Month. The resolution recognizes the widespread impact of menopause. It also raises awareness of the need for more reliable resources for women facing menopause symptoms and additional training for health care workers on menopause.

“Our health care system has failed women struggling with menopausal symptoms that disrupt their livelihoods, and this unfortunate reality disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic women,” said Senator Booker. “This resolution is a reminder that we must do more to support women navigating menopause and provide them with the resources they need. Menopause should not be a barrier to the quality of life every woman deserves.”

"Generations of women have faced the transition to menopause, yet for too long this experience has been overlooked, under-researched, and treated as taboo,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “It’s far past time we ensure women have the care and support they need to feel their best in all phases of life. I’m proud to introduce the World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution to elevate the challenges of menopause and encourage further investments into research that will help women meet this transition with confidence."

Women in the workforce are burdened by severe menopausal symptoms that can last an average of 7 to 9 years or longer. As many as 40 percent of menopausal women say their symptoms interfered with their work performance or productivity weekly, and nearly 1 in 5 have left or considered leaving their jobs because of menopause. Menopause may also increase the risk of osteoporosis, heart disease, and stroke, making informed health decisions crucial during this period. Black and Hispanic women are more likely to experience menopause earlier and more intense symptoms, including memory loss, urinary problems, depression, and anxiety.

title: Arkansas Delegation: Working Families Tax Cuts Delivering $1 Billion to State’s Farm Families
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman John Boozman (R-AR), Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR), and Congressmen Rick Crawford (AR-01), French Hill (AR-02), Steve Womack (AR-03) and Bruce Westerman (AR-04) announced Arkansas farmers will begin receiving an estimated $1 billion in enhanced farm safety net benefits this month, thanks to improvements secured through the Working Families Tax Cuts.

“Agriculture is a cornerstone of Arkansas’s economy, supporting families, communities and business across our state. Farmers need the tools to manage risk as well as the certainty and predictability to plan ahead. The improvements to the farm safety net delivered through the Working Families Tax Cuts are an important step in providing Natural State producers the support they need to continue producing our nation’s food and fiber. Our delegation is pleased that these benefits are now getting in the hands of our farmers, and we’re building on that momentum to deliver a comprehensive five-year farm bill to be signed into law this year,” Boozman said.

“Last year’s Republican-led tax cuts included vital lifelines for Arkansas farmers after years of neglect under Joe Biden, including an estimated $1 billion in enhanced farm safety net benefits spearheaded by Senator Boozman. I’m pleased our farmers will receive these benefits this month to help them continue to grow, harvest, and operate,” Cotton said.

“Farmers have faced rising input costs and volatile markets for multiple years, and the existing safety net programs have not kept pace. Enhanced ARC and PLC payments, including updated statutory reference prices and modernized payment limits, will give farmers and producers the economic certainty they need to stay viable. I thank Sen. Boozman for his leadership in securing these investments for our ag economy. When our family farms are secure, our nation has a safe and dependable food supply,” Crawford said.

“Our farmers and ranchers need the tools and resources to grow, compete, and plan for the future. I am proud that Arkansas’s entire congressional delegation voted for the Working Families Tax Cuts, which supports our rural communities and strengthens the farm safety net, including with more than $1 billion now headed to producers across our state. We still have more work to do, including getting a strong Farm Bill across the finish line, but this is another example of how the Working Families Tax Cuts continues delivering for Arkansas,” Hill said.

“Our delegation delivered for all Arkansans by modernizing our nation’s most crucial farm safety net programs in the Working Families Tax Cuts law. Updated reference prices were long overdue, and this month, farmers will see the benefits of our work through increased support. I am proud to have worked with my colleagues to pass this landmark legislation and deliver much-needed support to the men and women who work tirelessly to provide our nation’s food, fiber, and fuel,” Womack said.

“For generations, agriculture has defined Arkansas’ proud legacy. To maintain this heritage and support this multi-billion-dollar industry that drives our economy, our farmers need greater certainty. The Republican-backed improvements to the farm safety net payments provided under the reconciliation package are an excellent step toward that goal. Farming families from every corner of Arkansas are the backbone of our economy – feeding, clothing, and fueling millions. I want them to know their concerns are being heard in Congress. While I join my colleagues in celebrating this win for Arkansas agriculture, the fight to secure more long-lasting financial security for its future is far from over,” Westerman said.

The increased Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) and Price Loss Coverage (PLC) payments are part of the $13.8 billion approved by Congress to modernize the farm safety net and strengthen risk management tools for agricultural producers, more than doubling the support farmers were expected to receive before these changes.

Implementation for improvements to ARC and PLC follows the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s rollout of other Working Families Tax Cuts provisions, including expanded access to and eligibility for standing disaster programs such as the Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees, and Farm-Raised Fish Program (ELAP) and Livestock Forage Program (LFP), in addition to measures making crop insurance more affordable.

title: Cantwell Outlines Comprehensive Governance Framework for Safe and Secure Frontier AI
text:
Cantwell Outlines Comprehensive Governance Framework for Safe and Secure Frontier AI

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, outlined a comprehensive AI governance framework built upon six principles that must drive the legislative and executive actions needed to address catastrophic risks and other AI harms.

“To manage risks from advanced AI systems we need clear safety standards, continuous testing, and reporting of serious failures,” Sen. Cantwell said. “America can lead the world in AI by building systems that are not only more capable, but safer and more secure.”

Frontier AI systems require constant oversight and vigilance at home and abroad. The United States should establish clear, transparent, enforceable safety standards, developed by federal experts at NIST in coordination with other relevant federal agencies. Covered models should not be released until they have undergone an independent audit confirming that they meet these safeguards and standards.

Sen. Cantwell’s framework is built around six principles, many of which she has promoted for years as Ranking Member and former Chair of the Commerce Committee:

Clear, Enforceable Federal Safety Standards for Frontier AI Development and Deployment

Continuous Testing, Reviewing and Auditing to Verify Standards are Met

Transparency and Accountability Through Disclosure, Oversight and Consequences

Public Private Partnerships to Benefit the Public Good

Protections for Children, Support for Workers and Human Oversight of Consequential AI

U.S. Led Global Cooperation in Adopting and Upholding Common AI Safety and Security Standards

ENFORCED STANDARDS

Set standards for safe AI development and deployment

Federal Standards: NIST should develop clear, transparent, measurable, risk-based standards for AI systems that could cause catastrophic harm

Catastrophic Risks: Standards must address catastrophic risks, including AI-enabled cyberattacks; chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear threats; potential for loss of human control; and automated improvement and autonomous agents escaping secure testing environments

Risk Management and Controls: Standards should establish proportionate safeguards and risk-management requirements, with heightened review and oversight for systems that exhibit dangerous capabilities or are capable of self-improvement that may bypass safety controls

Open-Source Protections: Specialized standards should be developed for open-source AI models to reduce the risks of catastrophic misuse while providing developers with the clear guidance necessary to accelerate U.S. leadership of the open-source ecosystem

Keeping Pace: Federal standards should be regularly updated as AI evolves

INDEPENDENT TESTING

Verify AI safety through continual review, constant oversight

Continuous Testing: Government and independent experts should provide constant oversight and continually scrutinize and stress test covered AI models against catastrophic risk standards, particularly where testing requires specialized expertise, sensitive information or secure facilities

Built-In Safeguards: AI systems must be stress-tested to ensure they halt self-modification that bypasses safety controls, monitoring or human oversight

Independent Audits: Audit firms should conduct comprehensive audits of AI developers, akin to outside auditors examining a company’s financial statements, to ensure AI products are meeting applicable federal standards and safeguards

TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Safety requires disclosure, oversight, and consequences

Independent Access: Developers should provide qualified independent testers and auditors with access and information necessary to assess catastrophic risks, investigate serious incidents and verify that safety and security safeguards are functioning as intended

Public Disclosure: Developers should provide clear, plain-language disclosures of material safety and security risks, and mitigation modeled on the risk disclosures public companies provide to investors

Incident Reporting: Developers must promptly report material AI safety and security incidents, including loss of control over autonomous agents, dangerous cyber capabilities, failures of critical safeguards and unsafe recursive self-improvement

Accountability: Developers must remain liable under applicable civil and criminal law for foreseeable harms and unlawful conduct arising from their AI systems, including when their design, deployment, modification or failure to implement reasonable safeguards materially contributes to that harm

Whistleblower Protection: Employees and contractors who report safety, security or compliance concerns should be protected from retaliation

PUBLIC PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS

Get the best experts working for the public good

Defensive AI: Government should work with industry to develop and deploy defensive AI that detects and contains malicious activity, identifies and patches cyber vulnerabilities and protects critical infrastructure from increasingly automated attacks

Shared Capabilities: Leading AI companies should contribute compute, technical expertise and advanced defensive tools, so small and medium sized businesses, critical infrastructure operators and public institutions can benefit from capabilities they may not be able to build on their own

Public-Interest Compute: Government and industry should expand access to advanced computing and AI tools for universities, researchers and public-interest projects working on national security, scientific discovery, health, energy and other national priorities

Local Resilience: Federal agencies should equip state and local governments and private-sector operators with technical assistance, training and resources needed to protect critical infrastructure and essential services

DEFEND AGAINST SOCIAL HARM

Make AI work for people, not against them

Online Child Safety: AI products used by children should protect their safety and healthy development, rather than exacerbate social media harms such as addictive design, harmful content or data exploitation

Worker Opportunity and Protections: AI companies should help fund apprenticeships, education and other worker training so that AI expands workers’ skills, productivity and earning power rather than displacing them, while guardrails protect the products of human creativity and incentivize employers to use AI to improve jobs rather than eliminate them

Human Judgment: When AI informs consequential decisions about employment, health care, credit or other essential services, it must be transparent and fair and be subject to meaningful human oversight—particularly where AI-assisted prior authorization, such as CMS’s WISeR model, could delay or deny needed care

Recourse: People should be able to understand when and how an AI system materially affected a consequential decision, challenge the outcome and receive timely review by a qualified human decision-maker

ADVANCE GLOBAL COOPERATION

Lead global adoption of trusted American AI

Align Standards: The United States should work with allies and partners to adopt common, rigorous AI safety and security standards that reduce conflicting requirements and expand global markets for trusted American AI

Standards Leadership: The United States should lead in international standards-setting bodies, including ISO/IEC, to translate U.S. technical leadership in AI testing, risk measurement and safeguards into widely adopted global standards

Shared Risk Information: Allies should establish secure mechanisms to share information on serious AI incidents, emerging catastrophic capabilities, evaluation methods and effective safeguards

U.S.–China Crisis Channel: The U.S. should establish a secure channel with China like the Soviet era red phone for rapid communication when a significant AI incident or system-control failure could threaten either country or international security

Secure Access: Export controls should ensure that America’s most advanced AI technologies are not made accessible to our adversaries and available only to countries that protect them from diversion and misuse and uphold U.S.-led safety and security standards

Additional information about Sen. Cantwell’s leadership on AI policy and legislation can be found HERE.

title:
Capito Announces CDS Awards for 
Economic Development Projects
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), a leader on the Senate Appropriations Committee, announced Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) awards from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to support economic development projects across West Virginia.

These awards, which were secured through Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) requests made by Senator Capito in Fiscal Year (FY) 2026, will help support business incubation, economic revitalization efforts, and education programs.

“These awards are a significant investment in the economic development of West Virginia,” Senator Capito said. “I am proud to have helped secure funding for these projects, which will support the growth of our small businesses and improve the quality of life for West Virginians. I will continue to work to deliver results that benefit our communities and strengthen our state’s future.”

Individual award details listed below:

$2,502,000 CDS award to Marshall University Aviation Program (Charleston, W.Va.) to increase capacity at Marshall University Aviation with additional training tools and equipment.

$800,000 CDS award to the Capital Area Development Corporation of West Virginia and Charleston Area Alliance (Charleston, W.Va.) for renovations to the historic Small Business Incubator and Business Hub, which supports small business development, entrepreneur training, and economic growth in Kanawha County and serves as a catalyst for development in downtown Charleston.

$750,000 CDS award to the New River Gorge Regional Development Authority (Beckley, W.Va.) to implement a public-private cohort model that expands access to affordable childcare by engaging local employers in a shared subsidy structure, stabilizing an existing childcare facility, and piloting a sustainable framework for rural communities.

$750,000 CDS award to the WV Hive Network, Inc. (Beckley, W.Va.) to provide direct technical assistance to entrepreneurs, helping eliminate early-stage barriers through expert support in legal structure, marketing, accounting, website development, and business planning.

$748,000 CDS award to West Virginia Food and Farm Coalition, Inc. (Charleston, W.Va.) to strengthen West Virginia’s agricultural economy by supporting small businesses and local producers in bringing value-added products to market.

$500,000 CDS award to the Putnam County Development Authority (Hurricane, W.Va.) to provide ready-to-use industrial space in the Putman County, West Virginia area.

$500,000 CDS award to the Hatfield McCoy Convention and Visitors Bureau (Logan, W.Va.) to promote small business formation and growth in the City of Logan and the Town of Man in cooperation with the Hatfield McCoy Convention & Visitors Bureau.

$500,000 CDS award to West Virginia Women Work, Inc. (Morgantown, W.Va.) to help small businesses in West Virginia recruit and train skilled employees to bolster capacity and long-term economic growth.

$371,000 CDS award to the West Virginia Department of Agriculture (Charleston, W.Va.) to foster economic growth by promoting West Virginia’s agribusinesses through marketing support, resources, workshops, and events to prepare producers for domestic and international markets.
