title: ICYMI: Buchanan, Tonko Make Bipartisan Case for Early Alzheimer’s Detection in The Hill Op-Ed
text:
“The time for waiting is over. We must act ASAP.”

WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the Ways & Means Committee and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, penned an op-ed in The Hill with Congressman Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), highlighting the momentum behind their Alzheimer’s Screening and Prevention (ASAP) Act and the bipartisan need for broader access to Alzheimer’s screening tools.

“Broadening access to Alzheimer’s screening tools can help people understand their risk for the disease long before symptoms appear,” wrote Buchanan and Tonko in the op-ed. “This is especially key for patients in rural and underserved communities, where access to specialists and advanced diagnostic facilities can be limited and where a simple blood test could reduce the burden of traveling long distances for care.”

Read the full op-ed HERE or below:

A rare healthcare issue that both parties agree on: A solution to Alzheimer’s that can’t wait

Reps. Vern Buchanan (R-Fla.) and Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.)

As members of Congress on opposite sides of the aisle, we don’t see eye-to-eye on everything. But Alzheimer’s disease doesn’t care about politics. It affects families in every state, congressional district and neighborhood across America. Over 7 million of us currently live with Alzheimer’s — more than 1 million in our two states alone — a number that is expected to nearly double in the decades ahead. Changing the trajectory of Alzheimer’s in America isn’t a luxury — it’s a necessity.

Alzheimer’s can start more than a decade before memory loss and other signs become evident. Early detection is critical to helping patients start Alzheimer’s treatment sooner, when it’s most effective. Sadly, many patients are diagnosed too late for treatment or other health interventions to help.

Thankfully, decades of investment in research and development have led to scientific breakthroughs that are revolutionizing Alzheimer’s care. For too long, diagnosing Alzheimer’s required lengthy referrals and invasive, expensive procedures. Today, simple blood-based biomarker tests can help identify the disease earlier and more conveniently than ever. These developments have the potential to transform patient care, particularly with more treatments now approved.

Yet despite these advances, coverage policies have not kept pace. Medicare can only cover preventive services that Congress has specifically authorized or that are recommended by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force. This process can delay coverage for years after screening tests receive FDA clearance.

That’s why we came together to introduce the ASAP Act. Our bipartisan, bicameral legislation authorizes the secretary of Health and Human Services to provide a pathway for Medicare coverage for FDA-approved or cleared blood-based biomarker tests for the early detection of Alzheimer’s and other dementias.

Broadening access to Alzheimer’s screening tools can help people understand their risk for the disease long before symptoms appear. This is especially key for patients in rural and underserved communities, where access to specialists and advanced diagnostic facilities can be limited and where a simple blood test could reduce the burden of traveling long distances for care.

Catching Alzheimer’s early is critical because it is among the most expensive diseases to manage. Late-stage care often requires extensive medical services and long-term support, imposing significant costs to families and taxpayers alike. It can also place an enormous burden on caregivers, who often shoulder years of financial, emotional and logistical responsibilities as a loved one’s condition progresses. Earlier detection can give families more time to plan, pursue treatment and prepare for the challenges ahead.

As our country’s population ages, rates of Alzheimer’s will rise. In fact, the U.S. is on pace to spend more than $1 trillion treating Alzheimer’s and other dementias by 2050. The cost of inaction is exorbitant.

It’s fair to debate whether Medicare should cover new services, but modern blood tests are much softer on taxpayers than a typical PET scan. Yet despite their cost-effectiveness, blood tests can still be financially challenging for the average patient to obtain. By significantly easing out-of-pocket costs, the ASAP Act helps fix this problem.

The legislation reflects principles that both parties can get behind. It encourages prevention, innovation, patient choice and fiscal responsibility — values Republicans have long championed. By increasing access to quality medical care, the ASAP Act advances a more equitable healthcare system where a person’s ability to benefit from the latest innovation isn’t determined by their income status or where they live — a key priority for Democrats.

Ultimately, scientific advancements achieve their full potential only when people can access them. In 1990, Congress voted to ensure Medicare coverage of mammograms, saving the lives of millions of women through early detection and treatment of breast cancer. Today, we have the chance to change Alzheimer’s trajectory and write a new story.

Families deserve access to earlier diagnosis and treatment without being forced to pay out of pocket just to get care. FDA-cleared Alzheimer’s tests are now available; coverage rules need to keep up. Every month we delay costs Americans opportunities to benefit from advances that could make a meaningful difference in their lives.

Two hundred twenty-four of our House colleagues have co-sponsored our bill, a sign of momentum we should not squander. The time for waiting is over. We must act ASAP.

Vern Buchanan serves Florida’s 16th District. He is vice chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, chairman of its Health Subcommittee, and the longest-serving Republican to represent Southwest Florida in the U.S. House of Representatives. Paul Tonko serves New York’s 20th District. He is a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee and serves as ranking member of its Environment Subcommittee.

title: “The cruel injustice of abortion need not be forever”: Rep. Smith addresses crowds at 2026 New Jersey March for Life
text:
The following are excerpts of remarks delivered by Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), Co-Chair of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, at the 2026 New Jersey March for Life in Trenton, NJ:

I met my dear wife, Marie, more than fifty years ago in the pro-life movement. We spent many days lobbying here at our state capital. Today, like you, we remain hope-filled.

Special thanks to Marie Tasy for her extraordinary leadership, courage, wisdom and tenacity in the defense of the weakest and most vulnerable. Thank you to each and every one of you for being here.

Today’s March for Life is an engraved invitation to all of us to seriously recommit and rededicate ourselves, with love and compassion, to tangibly assist women—especially through the extraordinary work of pregnancy care centers—in order to protect their precious babies and their own lives from the violence and cruelty of abortion.

We stand in absolute solidarity with First Choice Women’s Resource Center and remain encouraged by the U.S. Supreme Court’s unanimous 9-0 decision last April.

As you know, pregnancy care centers are on the front lines of providing compassionate care to mothers and their precious children—offering free support and resources, which can range from pregnancy tests and ultrasounds to parental education programs and lactation consultations, and much more.

30 Members of the House and Senate and I had asked the Supreme Court to send a clear message to New Jersey and other states that this kind of bullying and infringement of constitutionally protected freedoms be given no sanction.

Regrettably, New Jersey has not respected the Supreme Court decision. Tragically, pregnancy care centers are under siege, especially here in NJ, while abortion clinics flourish—since 1970, Planned Parenthood has killed more than 10.6 million babies by abortion nationwide—almost 1,200 every single day. That’s more than the entire population of New Jersey, exterminated by just one organization.

NJ’s discrimination against pregnancy centers because they refrain from promoting or participating in the killing of unborn children by abortion is an unconscionable abuse of power. It is utterly shameful that New Jersey would go to these lengths to strip women of life-affirming options and support.

It motivated the Let Pregnancy Centers Serve Act of 2025 (HR 2226), federal legislation I introduced to prohibit federal, state and local governments from discriminating against the nearly 2,700 pregnancy care centers across the United States.

Each and every one of these centers is an oasis of love, compassion, empathy, and respect, offering quality care for both mothers and their precious children. Yet state governments, like New Jersey, and some lawmakers seek to discriminate against pregnancy care centers by violating fundamental conscience rights to compel complicity in abortion.

Fifty years ago, last week—on September 30th, 1976—Congress first enacted an amendment offered by the late, great Congressman Henry Hyde of Illinois to prohibit federal Medicaid funds from being used to subsidize the killing of unborn children by abortion.

During debate in the House, Henry said: “An innocent, defenseless human life, in a caring and humane society, deserves better than to be flushed down a toilet or burned in an incinerator. The promise of America is that life is not just for the privileged, the planned, or the perfect.”

The Hyde amendment continues to ensure that this promise is still true today.

According to Dr. Michael J. New of the Charlotte Lozier Institute, approximately 2.7 million people are alive today—and each year, another 60,000 evade abortion and survive—because of Henry Hyde’s amendment.

That’s 2.7 million people—who would have otherwise been aborted if taxpayers paid for their demise—who have experienced the joys and challenges and given the opportunities to thrive.

It’s truly sad that far too many politicians—who know or should know better—have abandoned unborn children and their mothers to the violence of abortion. With respect and a deep sense of urgency, I—we—ask them, including Governor Sherrill, to rethink and reconsider.

Listen to others who once shared your view, but upon seeing the humanity of the child in the womb, changed. Listen to NARAL founder and abortionist turned pro-lifer Dr. Bernard Nathanson, who wrote in the New England Journal of Medicine: “I am deeply troubled by my own increasing certainty that I had in fact presided over 60,000 deaths.”

Listen to former Planned Parenthood abortion clinic director Abby Johnson, who wrote: “I was asked to participate in an ultrasound-guided abortion procedure… And I watched in horror as a 13-week-old baby fought and struggled for his life against the abortion instrument. I knew that there was humanity in the womb, and that what I had seen was the taking of an innocent human life. I realized I was on the wrong side of this debate, and so I ended up leaving.”

Listen to Dr. Anthony Levatino: “I don’t remember exactly how long it was after Heather’s death [his 6-year-old daughter died in a car accident], but I started to perform a second-trimester abortion… and I got sick. For the first time, I didn’t see a right to choose, and I didn’t see what a wonderful doctor I was helping the patient with her problem. I didn’t even see the $800 I had made in just 15 minutes. All I could see was somebody’s son or daughter.”

Listen to former abortionist Dr. Kathi Aultman: “I recognized that the innocent victim in all of this was the baby. Being unwanted was no longer enough justification for me to take the child’s life. And that was the end of my abortion career.”

Listen to Dr. Alveda King, niece of the late Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., who, after having two abortions, became a powerful right to life leader and wrote a book entitled: How Can the Dream Survive If We Murder the Children? ABORTION IS NOT A CIVIL RIGHT!

And listen to Elizabeth Gillette, who, after being pressured by Planned Parenthood to take the abortion pill, wrote: “I found myself on the bathroom floor in a pool of blood until I ended up expelling the entire amniotic sac with my baby — a recognizable baby inside. The trauma from this horrific experience still follows me today in the form of post-traumatic stress disorder. This is nothing like what they told me would happen.”

That abortion pill—mifepristone—kills the baby by starving the child to death, while other methods of abortion dismember and decapitate the baby.

We now know that mifepristone is extremely dangerous to women. The Ethics and Public Policy Center conducted the largest-known study of the abortion pill ever and is based on analysis of data from an all-payer insurance claims database that includes 865,727 prescribed mifepristone abortions from 2017 to 2023 and found that 10.93 percent of women experience sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days following a mifepristone abortion.

The real-world rate of serious adverse events following mifepristone abortions is at least 22 times as high as the summary figure of “less than 0.5 percent” in clinical trials reported on the drug label.

Bottom line: we are a people of persevering faith in God, willing to bear any burden and endure any attack. We know that the cruel injustice of abortion need not be forever and that each day, despite setbacks, many unborn children and their mothers have, are, and will be protected. We have hope. We have much work to do.

title: TIP Report exposes China’s continued failure, Hong Kong’s backslidingSmith welcomes release of the State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report
text:
Congressman Chris Smith (R-NJ), author of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 (TVPA) (PL 106-386), issued the following statement upon the release of the State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report:

“The 2026 TIP Report is a stark reminder that modern-day slavery remains a global scourge—and that governments must be held accountable when they fail to protect vulnerable people.

“China remains on Tier 3—the lowest ranking—reflecting its continued failure to meet the minimum standards for eliminating trafficking. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) use and enabling of forced labor—including the systematic exploitation of Uyghurs and other persecuted minorities—is deeply troubling and deserves the greatest level of scrutiny.

“Moreover, the horrific, ongoing consequences of China’s one-child per couple policy can still be seen and felt today, as the Report notes that a gross disparity—tens of millions more boys than girls—has driven the demand for commercial sex trafficking and coercive marriages in the country.

“Additionally, Hong Kong’s drop to Tier 3 is yet another serious warning sign about the erosion of protections against trafficking under Beijing’s increasingly authoritarian rule.

“Other governments also moved in the wrong direction. The Republic of the Congo fell to Tier 3, while Seychelles dropped from Tier 1 to Tier 2. These downgrades should be a wake-up call to their governments that failing to protect victims and hold traffickers accountable has severe consequences.

“Thankfully, the report recognizes meaningful progress as well. Israel and Ghana moved up to Tier 1, and Papua New Guinea improved from Tier 3 to the Tier 2 Watch List. These changes show that governments can make real progress when they strengthen enforcement, protect victims, and take anti-trafficking initiatives seriously.

“Governments on Tier 3—including China, North Korea, Iran, Russia, Burma, Belarus, Cambodia, Cuba, Laos, Nicaragua, Sudan, South Sudan, and Venezuela—can and must do more. Tier 3 must never become a permanent designation; it should serve as a dire warning and a call to action.

“Human trafficking is an assault on human dignity and freedom, and the United States must continue to use every tool at its disposal—including the TIP Report—to expose human trafficking whenever it rears its ugly head, protect survivors, and press foreign governments to end this blight upon humanity.”

title: ICYMI: Ciscomani Celebrates 100 Years of Service from Casa Grande Rotary Club
text:
Casa Grande, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani joined the Casa Grande community for the 5th Annual Casa Grande Oktoberfest to celebrate a century of service from the Casa Grande Rotary Club and recognize the organization’s lasting impact on the community.

"One hundred years of service is an incredible milestone, and it is a testament to the people who have dedicated their time and energy to making Casa Grande stronger through the Rotary Club," said Representative Ciscomani. "The Casa Grande Rotary Club has spent a century bringing people together, serving local families, and investing in the future of our local community. I’m proud to have celebrated this milestone alongside leaders of the Rotary Club and the Casa Grande community, presenting them with a congressional certificate, and I look forward to seeing the impact of their service continue for generations to come."

Community leaders joined Ciscomani for the celebration, bringing together families and residents for an evening that showcased Casa Grande’s vibrant community, rich culture, and German heritage.

"The Casa Grande Rotary Club has been an incredible part of our community for 100 years, and this milestone is a testament to the countless volunteers and leaders who have given their time to make Casa Grande a better place," said Casa Grande City Council Member Matt Herman. "It was an honor to celebrate this incredible milestone alongside Congressman Ciscomani and our community at Oktoberfest, and to recognize the lasting impact the Rotary Club continues to make across Casa Grande."

"I was thrilled to honor the Casa Grande Rotary and be part of their 100th anniversary celebration with Congressman Ciscomani," said Pinal County Supervisor Stephen Q. Miller. "Organizations like the Rotary are vital to communities across the state and the Congressman's support helps this organization continue its important work."

This year’s celebration also marked a special milestone for the Casa Grande Rotary Club, which has supported local families for the past 100 years and fostered growth and meaningful improvements through education, healthcare, youth programs, and volunteerism in the local community.

Casa Grande Rotary Club President Zoe Cooper also highlighted the event.

"Celebrating 100 years of the Rotary Club of Casa Grande was a significant milestone for our organization, and we were grateful to have Rep. Ciscomani with us at Casa Grande Oktoberfest to help celebrate. He has consistently supported Rotary, making time to attend our meetings and community events whenever he can. His willingness to engage with our members and support the causes we care about is greatly appreciated. We are grateful for his continued partnership and commitment to service, youth and volunteerism," said President Zoe Cooper.

As Arizona’s sole member of the House Appropriations Committee, Ciscomani has worked to deliver federal investments that support Casa Grande’s continued growth and strengthen the community. In previous years, he helped secure:

$1 million for the Casa Grande Elementary School District Community Center Revitalization Project, which will repurpose an existing school building into a community center providing critical support and services to students and families.

$1.8 million for affordable workforce housing through the Casa Grande Union High School District, supporting the construction of affordable teacher housing to help attract and support new educators.

$3.79 million for the City of Casa Grande’s Thornton Road Widening Project to widen Thornton Road and improve traffic flow.

This year, Ciscomani also worked to secure $2.73 million in federal funding for the Burris Road–Peters Road to Highway 84 project, which will provide an essential north-south connection and enhance transportation infrastructure in Casa Grande. title: CLARKE, COLLEAGUES INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN, BICAMERAL RESOLUTION TO ESTABLISH WORLD MENOPAUSE AWARENESS MONTH AND WORLD MENOPAUSE DAY
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

October 8, 2026

MEDIA CONTACT:

e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov

c: 202.913.0126

WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-09) and Julia Letlow (R-LA-05) introduced a bipartisan, bicameral resolution to establish October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18th as World Menopause Day. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced the resolution’s companion in the Senate.

These observances will contribute to the spread of global awareness and access to care during menopausal transition and post-menopause, as well as provide organizations and individuals around the world with an opportunity to advocate for resources and support for the 75 million American women in perimenopause, menopause, and post-menopause.

“Throughout our lives, women deserve the support we need to confront every trial and embrace every triumph each of our chapters has in store for us. Menopause is a natural experience that we all must face, yet the stigma that follows it continues to inflict needless ridicule and shame on women at a time when all we ask for is acceptance and understanding,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “World Menopause Awareness Month and World Menopause Day will be the bridges to normalizing menopause and ensuring the women confronting it have the resources, care, and confidence they need to tackle their new horizons head on, and I am proud to lead this bipartisan legislation to see both codified as national observances.”

“Through any stage of life, women need access to reliable information to make educated decisions about their health. World Menopause Awareness Month shines a light on the millions of women undergoing menopause every year, highlighting the need for women to have a better understanding of the treatments and options available to them,” said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.

“Generations of women have faced the transition to menopause, yet for too long this experience has been overlooked, under-researched, and treated as taboo,” said Lisa Senator Blunt Rochester. “It’s far past time we ensure women have the care and support they need to feel their best in all phases of life. I’m proud to introduce the World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution to elevate the challenges of menopause and encourage further investments into research that will help women meet this transition with confidence.”

“Our health care system has failed women struggling with menopausal symptoms that disrupt their livelihoods, and this unfortunate reality disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic women,” said Senator Cory Booker. “This resolution is a reminder that we must do more to support women navigating menopause and provide them with the resources they need. Menopause should not be a barrier to the quality of life every woman deserves.”

“The resolution introduced by Congresswoman Yvette Clarke represents another important step toward breaking down the barriers that have too often left women without the information, care, and relief they need throughout the menopause transition,” said Donna Klassen of Let’s Talk Menopause. “We proudly support this resolution and applaud Congresswoman Clarke’s leadership in bringing greater attention to menopause, expanding access to trusted health information and care, and ensuring women have the resources they need to navigate this stage of life with confidence and support.”

“Menopause is a universal experience for women, and yet, for too long menopause has been understudied. This has left us with significant knowledge gaps about menopause itself, including its symptoms and treatments, but also about the effects of menopause on overall health and healthy aging. Fortunately, we now have momentum to course correct. The Society for Women’s Health Research thanks Representative Clarke for her leadership on the resolution designating October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18 as World Menopause Day. We must collectively continue raising awareness about menopause, which can help shape research priorities and ensure women and health care providers have the evidence and information needed to make informed decisions about menopause care,” said Lindsey Miltenberger of the Society for Women’s Health Research.

Menopause is more than a personal, biological transition—it has lasting implications for women’s health and well-being, and for families, workplaces, and society. The Black Women’s Health Imperative endorses this resolution to recognize October as World Menopause Awareness Month and expand awareness, provider education, and access to the resources and care that women, particularly Black women, need for a healthy, dignified menopause, ” said Ifeoma Udoh, Ph.D. of the Black Women’s Health Imperative.

The resolution is endorsed by the American Medical Association, Astellas, Greater New York Hospital Association, Healthcare Association of New York State, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Mount Sinai Health System, National Medical Association, National Minority Quality Forum, Novo Nordisk, Inc., NYU Langone Health, One Brooklyn Health System, Reproductive Health Access Project, Ritual, The Fibroid Foundation, and The White Dress Project.

title: Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H.Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day."

"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."

"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."

"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," Congressman Tonko said. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."

"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Congressman Valadao.

"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.

"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."

BACKGROUND

National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.

The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power.

U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Representatives Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors.

title: Arizonans Invited to Help Shape the Future of the Grand Canyon’s North Rim
text:
On July 4, 2025, a lightning strike sparked the Dragon Bravo Fire, which scorched nearly 150,000 acres across Northern Arizona. The blaze damaged or destroyed more than 100 structures at the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park, including the historic Grand Canyon Lodge. As a result, park staff, concessioners, small businesses, and gateway communities have endured great uncertainty and financial loss.

In the aftermath, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) visited the region and met with impacted stakeholders to craft a federal response. Building on those conversations, he introduced the North Rim Restoration Act of 2025 to grant the National Park Service (NPS) emergency contracting authority. The legislation would cut through red tape and accelerate all fire-related work, such as forest management, reconstruction, and infrastructure upgrades.

The Coconino County Board of Supervisors quickly endorsed the bill, signaling bipartisan buy-in for the approach. In March, the House of Representatives passed it unanimously, and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources advanced it by unanimous consent on September 30. Rep. Crane is urging the Senate to finish the job and send the measure to the President’s desk before the 119th Congress concludes.

Meanwhile, the NPS is drafting a long-term blueprint for managing and redeveloping the North Rim. Although the fire took a heavy toll, the agency reports that the landscape is already showing signs of natural regrowth. Officials seek to preserve the area’s history while modernizing facilities to better serve visitors, employees, and park operations.

On Tuesday, the Park Service began accepting public feedback and released its planning materials for review. These documents outline the plan’s purpose and goals, recovery progress to date, a draft vision for what comes next, and three preliminary redevelopment concepts. The comment window closes November 6, 2026, and all submissions must go through the project website.

Throughout October, the agency will host virtual and in-person meetings where attendees can learn more about the effort and provide input. Dates and details for each session are available online.

title: Dingell, Colleagues Express Concern Over Workplace Safety at Pontiac USPS Facility
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), and Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) are expressing concerns about workplace safety at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan and across other Southeast Michigan USPS Facilities. Since May 2026, employees have raised safety concerns and offered solutions to management, but to date employees report that nothing has been done to rectify the situation.

“On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers continued: “According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan. This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.”

In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, the lawmakers noted that the USPS has a responsibility to ensure that employees are safe and protected on the job.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

This letter is regarding workplace safety concerns at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan. We are concerned by the reports of unsafe practices at this facility and across Southeast Michigan.

On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate.

According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan. This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.

Given the USPS’s role in ensuring worker safety, we request clarification on this matter and written responses to the following questions:

1. Was USPS aware that a non-maintenance supervisor had knowledge of and used a maintenance bypass code on multiple occasions, which could have led to serious, life-threatening consequences?

2. What steps will USPS take to ensure that only qualified employees have access to the maintenance code?

3. Have any disciplinary actions been taken, and if not, what correctional actions will USPS pursue?

4. How often are program evaluations, service talks, safety observations, and inspections conducted at this facility, as described in the Employee and Labor Relations Manual, and how will USPS adapt the safety training and protocols to address this problem at the facility?

5. What are the appropriate procedures for employees to communicate complaints or concerns with the appropriate staff when a supervisor is involved in an unsafe practice?

6. What future actions will USPS put in place to ensure a similar situation does not recur?

Ensuring worker safety remains our top priority. Thank you, and we look forward to your full and prompt response.

title: DelBene, Dexter Introduce Legislation to Stop Future Capture, Breeding of Whales for Public Display
text:
Today, Congresswomen Suzan DelBene (WA-01) and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) reintroduced the Strengthening Welfare in Marine Settings (SWIMS) Act, legislation that would end the future capture and breeding of whales for public display.

Certain cetaceans, such as orcas, beluga whales, pilot whales, and false killer whales, are cognitively, emotionally, and socially complex animals who cannot thrive in captivity, according to multiple studies. Whales held for display often exhibit signs of suffering and distress and have significantly shorter lifespans than whales in the wild. Currently, there are approximately 70 whales held in captivity in the United States.

The SWIMS Act would:

Prohibit the taking, importation, or exportation of these whales for public display.

Prohibit any breeding of these whales for future public display.

Allow exemptions for animals being transported to a sanctuary setting or released to the wild.

“Whales and dolphins are treasures to the Pacific Northwest, and they belong in the wild,” said DelBene. “Scientific evidence shows that when these majestic animals are kept in captivity, they suffer significant distress and shorter life spans. This legislation would prevent the capture and breeding of whales for public display to ensure they remain in their natural habitats and free from abuse and exploitation.”

“Whales belong in the open ocean, not behind glass,” said Dexter. “These extraordinary animals are icons of the Pacific Northwest, forming deep family bonds and playing a vital role in healthy oceans. Captivity robs them of the space, freedom, and connection they need to thrive. Their lives should be defined by the ocean’s possibilities, not the walls of a tank.”

“Science increasingly supports the conclusion that we cannot provide conditions in a concrete enclosure that accommodate the size, wide-ranging nature, and physiological, behavioral, and social needs of these species,” said Dr. Naomi Rose, senior scientist for marine mammal biology at the Animal Welfare Institute. “The SWIMS Act recognizes that reality and offers a path forward by prohibiting breeding, trade, and capture for public display. Let this be the last generation in captivity of these ocean predators.”

The SWIMS Act is supported by the Animal Legal Defense Fund, Animal Welfare Institute, Born Free USA, Cetacean Society International, CompassionWorks International, Humane World Action Fund, Humane World for Animals, International Marine Mammal Project of Earth Island Institute, Last Chance for Animals, Oceanic Preservation Society, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, Whale and Dolphin Conservation, Whale Sanctuary Project, and World Animal Protection.

title: WA Delegation Supports Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington
text:
Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.

For the first time, on August 1, the National Weather Service upgraded a Red Flag Warning for fire weather conditions to a Particularly Dangerous Situation, which is very rare and typically reserved for extreme fire weather conditions. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane: the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead. The Spokane Complex Fires forced 67,000 people to evacuate, burned nearly 10,000 acres, with damages predicted to exceed $1 billion.

This was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and threatening lives, property, businesses, and livestock. In Okanogan County, the Kaiser Canyon, Modrite, and Sinlahekin fires burned over 350,000 acres total.

“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” the lawmakers wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”

The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”

“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.

Joining DelBene in the letter to President Trump were Washington Senators Patty Murray and Maria Cantwell, and Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Dan Newhouse (WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (WA-05), Emily Randall (WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Kim Schrier M.D. (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).

The full letter can be found here.

title: Congressman Deluzio Announces $200,000 for Mental Health Services in Beaver County
text:

title: Congressman Gabe Evans Introduces Resolution Standing Up for American Farmers and Ranchers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Gabe Evans introduced a pro-animal agriculture resolution to stand united with America’s livestock producers and recognize the critical role animal agriculture plays in feeding Coloradan families, supporting rural communities and local economies.

The resolution comes as farmers and ranchers across the country face rising input costs, prolonged drought periods, extreme weather conditions, workforce shortages, livestock disease outbreaks, and growing regulatory pressure. It pushes back against government mandates that limit consumer choice, increase food costs, and threaten the livelihoods of those who make American animal agriculture possible.

“In Colorado, agriculture isn’t just an industry—it’s a way of life. Unfortunately, radical activists and politicians have spent years attacking animal agriculture with burdensome regulations and proposals that threaten small family farms, kill jobs, and drive up food costs at the grocery store. We saw it firsthand in Colorado when activists tried to shut down Superior Farms—Denver’s only livestock processing industry at the time—but was overwhelmingly rejected by Coloradans. My resolution sends a simple message: Cut red tape to support domestic livestock agriculture and protect consumer choice. I am proud to represent Colorado’s farmers and ranchers who work tirelessly every day to raise livestock, and I’m grateful for the essential products they provide to families across the state and nation. ” –– Congressman Gabe Evans

The resolution specifically highlights the importance of a strong domestic livestock industry in reducing U.S. reliance on foreign food production and strengthening our food security. It also recognizes that approximately 97% of U.S. farms are operated by families and that they collectively account for 85% of the total agricultural production value.

This resolution is endorsed by the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association, National Pork Producers Council, Colorado Farm Bureau, Colorado Livestock Association, Colorado Cattlemen’s Association, Colorado Pork Producers Council, Colorado Wool Growers Association, Weld County Farm Bureau, Colorado Livestock Marketing Association, Colorado Egg Producers, National Chicken Council, American Sheep Industry Association, and Meat Institute.

BACKGROUND:

Animal agriculture is a critical part of America’s food supply, rural economy, and agricultural heritage. In 2024, radical activists created a ballot measure to permanently shut down livestock processing facilities in the city boundaries.While Denver voters rejected the measure by a wide margin, proposals such as Denver Initiated Ordinance 309 unfairly targets farmers and ranchers by imposing costly mandates, closing off markets, or confiscating agriculture operations.

Permanent closures of small to mid-sized farms would devastate our local and national economies, which is why this resolution:

Recognizes and thanks American agriculture workers involved in raising, processing, packaging, distributing, selling, and transporting animal agriculture products.

Supports greater access to nutrient-dense animal products, particularly for vulnerable populations including mothers, infants, and seniors.

Denounces government mandates that restrict consumer choice and increase food costs in pursuit of ideological policies.

Calls on federal, state, and local governments to suspend unreasonable regulatory mandates on livestock production that harm American agriculture workers.

Commits to advancing policies that prioritize the economic welfare and well-being of American farmers and ranchers.

H.Res. 1598 was introduced with Representatives Jeff Crank (CO-05), Jeff Hurd (CO-03), Dan Newhouse (WA-04), Tracey Mann (KS-01), Claudia Tenney (NY-24), Adrian Smith (NE-03), Kat Cammack (FL-03), Daniel Webster (FL-11), and Randy Fine (FL-06) as original cosponsors.

title: Gallagher Presses USTR to Protect California Winegrape Growers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) is calling on U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to address trade and regulatory policies putting California winegrape growers at a disadvantage as the industry faces declining domestic consumption and continued uncertainty in international markets.

In a letter to Ambassador Greer, Gallagher raised concerns from California growers about federal rules that allow wine labeled “United States” or “American” to contain up to 25 percent imported wine without disclosing that foreign origin on the label.

Gallagher also called for a review of federal duty drawback treatment for imported bulk wine and urged USTR to help expand international market access for American wine.

“North State growers produce some of the best winegrapes in the world, but right now they are competing in a market where federal policy can actually make it easier to use foreign products than grapes grown here at home,” said Congressman Gallagher. “We need to make sure our trade policies are working for American growers while opening new markets where California wine can compete and win.”

“California winegrape growers are facing an incredibly difficult market, and federal policies should not make it harder for American-grown grapes to compete,” said Natalie Collins, President of the California Association of Winegrape Growers. “We appreciate Congressman Gallagher raising these concerns with USTR and pushing for policies that better support domestic growers while expanding opportunities for American wine in international markets.”

Under current Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) appellation rules, wine may carry a “United States” or “American” appellation when at least 75 percent of the wine comes from U.S.-grown agricultural products and the wine is fully finished in the United States. That allows up to 25 percent to come from foreign-grown products without disclosure of that foreign origin on the label. Growers have warned that the policy can put downward pressure on California grape prices and blur the distinction between wine made entirely from American agricultural products and wine containing foreign components. Gallagher asked USTR to coordinate with the Department of the Treasury and TTB to examine the rule and its impact on domestic growers.

Gallagher also raised concerns about the duty drawback treatment available for imported bulk wine. Under the current structure, federal excise taxes paid on imported wine may be refunded based on the export of substituted wine, including in certain circumstances where the exported wine did not bear an equivalent federal excise-tax burden. Gallagher urged USTR to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in reviewing the practice and its effect on domestic growers.

The letter also asks federal agencies to examine bulk products imported from Canada that do not meet the U.S. definition of wine but nevertheless receive customs and tax treatment applicable to wine.

At the same time, Gallagher is pushing to give California producers more opportunities to sell their products overseas. With access to the Canadian market severely reduced, California growers and wineries are increasingly dependent on new international markets. Gallagher urged USTR to prioritize opening promising markets such as India and Vietnam while working to restore access to Canada.

“California growers don’t need Washington making a tough market even tougher,” Gallagher said. “We should be looking for ways to give them a fair shot here at home and more opportunities to sell American wine around the world.”

As the 2026 harvest draws to a close, Gallagher called on USTR to work with industry stakeholders to address these issues and provide meaningful relief for growers that remain an important part of California’s rural economy.

title: Goodlander Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Expand Outdoor Recreation for Veterans
text:
Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country connect with community and strengthen their well-being

Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and Congressman Jeff Hurd (CO-03) introduced the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act, legislation to help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country access outdoor recreation programs that support their mental and physical well-being.

The Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would establish a grant program through the Department of Veterans Affairs for state veterans’ agencies to develop, administer, and expand outdoor recreation programs for veterans. States could operate programs directly or partner with local outfitters, guides, nonprofit organizations, and community-based outdoor recreation providers.

“Our obligation to those who served doesn’t end when the uniform comes off. In New Hampshire, our mountains, lakes, and trails offer veterans opportunities to build community and strengthen their physical and mental well-being,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “I’m proud to help introduce the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act with Congressman Hurd to make those opportunities available to more veterans. By helping cover equipment, transportation, and program costs, our bill would help more veterans get outdoors, connect with one another, and find the support they’ve earned.”

“For many veterans, the transition from military service can mean losing the sense of purpose, community, and connection that came with serving alongside others,” said Congressman Hurd. “Colorado’s public lands and outdoor spaces offer opportunities to rebuild those connections while supporting veterans’ physical and mental well-being. This bipartisan legislation gives states more tools to work with local organizations and expand outdoor recreation opportunities so that more veterans can benefit from time outdoors and with one another.”

Under the legislation, grant funding could be used to reduce financial barriers that may prevent veterans from participating in outdoor recreation programs, including the costs of equipment, program fees, and reasonable transportation expenses. Funding could also support outreach to veterans and the expansion of existing programs.

The bill would also encourage state veterans’ agencies to work with federal land management agencies, including the National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Forest Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, to expand veterans’ access to outdoor spaces, reduce administrative barriers, and identify appropriate locations for organized activities.

The legislation defines eligible outdoor recreation programs broadly as nature-based activities designed to improve veterans’ mental and physical well-being through physical engagement, peer connection, skill-building, or therapeutic benefit. Programs may also include adaptive or accessible activities for veterans with disabilities.

Each eligible state entity whose application meets the bill’s requirements would receive at least $200,000 per fiscal year, subject to available appropriations. The legislation authorizes $10 million annually for the grant program. Participating states would also report information including the number of veterans served, types of activities offered, participation frequency, and observations related to veterans’ well-being, social connectedness, and physical activity.

title: RELEASE: Squeezed by High Costs, Gottheimer Hosts Agriculture Roundtable with Sussex County Farmers
text:
Above: Gottheimer hosts agriculture roundtable.

AUGUSTA, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted an agriculture roundtable with farmers from across New Jersey’s Fifth District to hear how rising diesel, fertilizer, and equipment costs, low dairy prices, and a shrinking number of farms in the Garden State are putting family farms under pressure, along with concerns about fewer cooperative plants and fewer meat processing facilities, and concerns about shrinking access to milk haulers. Gottheimer also laid out his priorities for the final Farm Bill, focusing on specialty crops, dairy, and agritourism, and asked farmers what they need to see in the final bill.

“It’s because of all of you, and the more than 1,000 farms in New Jersey’s Fifth District, that families across our state and nation have fresh, high-quality, nutritious meals on the table,” said Gottheimer (NJ-5). “You do your part, every single day, rain or shine. The question for Washington is whether they’re doing everything they can for you. And right now, the clearest test of that is the Farm Bill.”

Farmers are getting squeezed from every direction. For a family farm already running on razor-thin margins, those costs add up fast. When it costs more to fuel the tractor, buy supplies, and get the crop to market, even a good harvest may not be enough.

Then came the freeze. Last April, a hard freeze hit right as crops were budding and blooming. Many growers lost a huge share of their harvest, including peaches, cherries, apples, strawberries, blueberries, and more, adding up to estimated losses of $300 million. For too many farmers, the help has not been there. New Jersey’s Fifth District is home to more than 1,000 farms, and New Jersey is a top-ten specialty crop state. Right now, a specialty crop grower can lose a season to a freeze and find that crop insurance does not fit the risk.

Meanwhile, the Farm Bill, which last became law in 2018, has been kicked down the road with one extension after another, leaving farmers unable to plan their planting season, equipment purchases, or hiring.

At the roundtable, he announced the Farmer Recovery Opportunity and Support for Temperatures (FROST) Relief Act, new federal legislation to help growers recover from the April freeze that caused an estimated $300 million in losses.

The FROST Relief Act and the TEMP Act will:

Create a Block Grant Program for Freeze Losses: The FROST Relief Act would create a block grant program for farmers in the 13 states hit by the April freeze: Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia.

Get Resources to Farmers Without Red Tape: The money goes to the states that were hit, so it can reach the farmers who lost their crops without months of red tape.

Develop Temperature-Based Crop Insurance: The TEMP Act directs federal crop insurance to develop an affordable, temperature-based policy that covers freeze and cold-weather losses for specialty crop growers.

Gottheimer’s additional actions:

Fight to Expand Rural Eligibility: In April, Gottheimer offered an amendment to the Farm Bill to raise the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) population cap for “rural” eligibility from 20,000 to 50,000, so more North Jersey communities can qualify for broadband and infrastructure support. It did not make it into the House bill, and it remains a top priority for the final bill.

End the Hiring Freeze at the Farm Service Agency: Gottheimer offered amendments to end the hiring freeze at the Farm Service Agency (FSA), so loans and assistance get processed faster, especially for new and beginning farmers.

Restore Local Food Resources: The Administration cut more than $1 billion from the Local Food for Schools and Local Food Purchase Assistance programs. Because of those cuts, New Jersey lost $26 million in commitments that would have supported 46 local farms and food producers, including 11 in the Fifth District. Gottheimer has demanded the resources be restored and offered a Farm Bill amendment to do it.

Fix the SNAP Provisions in the House Bill: As written, the House bill would force New Jersey to cover 5 percent of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and raise the state’s share of administrative costs, adding up to $200 million a year in new costs for Jersey taxpayers. It would also push families off SNAP, stripping their children of automatic eligibility for free school meals. Gottheimer is urging the Senate to fix it, and he introduced the Feed Our Kids Act, which would provide free school meals to every student and push schools to buy nutritious food locally when they can.

Back Specialty Crops and Rural Communities: Gottheimer is backing more resources for the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program, more help fighting invasive species including the spotted lanternfly, more investment for meat and poultry processors, and reliable, affordable broadband for rural communities.

Stand Up for Jersey Dairy Farmers: After farmers raised the issue at a previous roundtable, Gottheimer backed whole milk in schools, and the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act was signed into law in January. He is also a member of the Dairy Caucus, so he can continue working across the aisle on commonsense solutions for dairy producers and sellers.

Support the Next Generation of Jersey Agriculture: Ahead of National 4-H Week, celebrated annually during the first full week of October, Gottheimer reaffirmed his support for 4-H and USDA’s Positive Youth Development programs.

Lower Costs and Go After Price Collusion: Gottheimer is pushing an All-of-the-Above Energy Plan to boost domestic capacity and bring down diesel and fertilizer costs, and he helped pass legislation to go after meat and poultry companies that collude to rig prices on the backs of hard-working families.

Gottheimer was joined by Ed Wengryn, New Jersey Secretary of Agriculture; Senator Parker Space, LD24 Senator; Louis Crescitelli, Chief of Staff to Senator Space; Commissioner Alan Henderson, Sussex County Commissioner; Commissioner Jill Space, Sussex Director Board of County Commissioners; Ken Schwemmer, Confidential Assistant to Commissioners; Liz Thompson, NJ Farm Bureau Executive Director; Paul Hlubik, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency State Committee Chair and NJ Agricultural Society President; Dave Foord, 4-H Senior Program Coordinator, RCE Sussex County, State 4-H Enrollment Coordinator; Holly Systema, Member of New Jersey State Board of Agriculture and the owner of The Farm at Windy Flats; Rocky Hazelman, President of the Passaic County Board of Agriculture and the Chairman of the Passaic County Agriculture Development Board; Stacey Kennedy, NJ Agricultural Society Director; Joe Atchison III, NJ Department of Agriculture Assistant Secretary and NJ Department of Agriculture Marketing and Development Director; Mike Burger, Sussex County Board of Agriculture President; Lindsay Caragher, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency Deputy State Executive Director; Rich Byma, Dairy Farmer at By-Acre Holsteins; Phil and Keri Brodhecker, Beef and Grain Farmers at Brodhecker Farms; Jason Swarts, Dairy Farmer for Deckertown Holsteins; Pete Southway, Springhouse Creamery; Mitchell Jones, Mountain Top Farm in Warren County.

title: Spirit Airlines to Sell Employee Data to Train Google AI, Horsford and Warren Lead Call for Worker Privacy Protections
text:
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Elizabeth Warren led 119 Members of Congress in a letter to Spirit Airlines CEO, Dave Davis, and Google CEO, Sundar Piachi, urging the companies to protect the privacy of thousands of former Spirit employees. The letter responds to the proposed $10 million sale of Spirit’s internal data to Google for the purpose of training artificial intelligence systems.

Court findings revealed that the proposed sale would include approximately 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages, employee records, timecards records, payroll and tax information, and employment contracts. Workers created and provided this information as a condition of their employment, and it may contain highly sensitive details, including medical information and accommodation requests.

“Spirit’s workers handed over this information because their jobs required it, not so it could be sold to train a different company’s AI,” said Rep. Horsford. “In Las Vegas alone, nearly 1,000 people were laid off from Spirit. They should not have to worry about their payroll records, disciplinary files, and private messages being used by a company they never worked for. Innovation cannot come at the expense of workers’ privacy, and no employee data should move until real, enforceable safeguards are in place.”

"Spirit Flight Attendants and other former employees are on the tip of the spear of this new threat to workers' rights," said Sara Nelson, president of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, representing 55,000 Flight Attendants at 20 airlines including Spirit." Senator Warren, Representative Horsford and 119 of their colleagues, with very little time and without either chamber in session, acted quickly to urge protections for workers as they face immediate risk in the bankruptcy court. But the outcome of conditions on this proposed sale to Google carries tremendous implications for workers across the economy. We thank the lawmakers for their swift action in their oversight role, as they recognize the immediate concern for our Spirit members. Flight Attendants across the industry and workers across the economy also thank them for recognizing the dangerous precedent it could set in this new frontier of unregulated AI and the intrusion of privacy for all Americans."

“Spirit Airlines workers deserve better than having their private information become a bargaining chip in a $10 million AI data deal. We are demanding that Spirit and Google exclude employee information wherever possible and keep confidential safety reporting out of this transaction. Removing names is not enough—workers deserve a voice in the safeguards and enforceable protection against profiling or misuse of their information. The IAM Union is at the forefront of protecting workers in the age of AI and big data, and we will keep fighting to ensure new technology respects our members’ rights, privacy and dignity,” said IAM Union Air Transport Territory General Vice President Richie Johnsen.

Google has stated it will not receive personally identifiable information and that the data will undergo third-party scrubbing before transfer. The Members warn that removing names, email addresses, and other direct identifiers does not necessarily make a dataset anonymous, particularly when modern AI systems can identify patterns across large datasets and connect seemingly unrelated pieces of information. The National Institute of Standards and Technology has recognized that de-identified data can be re-identified in certain circumstances.

“Spirit Airlines caused economic damage to workers, and now they are trying to hurt them even more by sharing sensitive data without proper safeguards," Transport Workers Union of America International President John Samuelsen said. "The least Spirit can do as it settles debts and gives Big Tech more data to train their AI models is to fully protect workers who gave years of hard work to the airline.”

This letter urges Google and Spirit to take specific actions before employee-related information is approved for transfer: exclude employee information from the transaction to the greatest extent possible, including records, timecards, payroll information, and Microsoft 365 content containing flight attendant information; establish a meaningful de-identification protocol developed with input from affected workers; maintain heightened protections for sensitive records such as disciplinary files, medical or accommodation requests, and compensation information, even after de-identification; conduct an independent employee confidentiality review and set enforceable limits on downstream use, disclosure, retention, and transfer; and establish a former review protocol that expressly prohibits using the data to identify, profile, evaluate, or draw inferences about identifiable groups of workers.

"As the nation’s largest transportation labor federation, we represent hundreds of thousands of workers who build, operate, and maintain transportation network across the United States," said Greg Regan, President of the Transportation Trades Department, AFL-CIO (TTD). "As our society confronts a new technology era, regulators, legislators, and organizations have a responsibility to set guardrails around its use. That includes privacy guardrails for employee data that is collected by employers and whether this sensitive information can be transferred or sold to another party. Employers are entrusted with highly sensitive employee records and communications, and workers deserve to have their data protected instead of being exposed to privacy risks. We commend Congressman Horsford and Senator Warren for leading this letter urging Spirit and Google to commit to guidelines for handling sensitive employee information if a data transfer occurs."

"Spirit's workers shared personal information because their jobs required it, not so it could be sold to train AI," said Capt. Jason Ambrosi, President of ALPA. "Our safety system works because pilots and other airline workers trust that when they speak up, it stays confidential. Break that trust and people stop reporting. We thank Senator Warren and Representative Horsford and dozens of Members of Congress for acting quickly to seek answers before this sale is final. Google and Spirit must put real, enforceable protections in place before a single employee record changes hands."

The Members are calling for no employee-related information to be transferred until protections are in place to ensure that workers’ sensitive information cannot be identified, profiled, or misused.

title: Gov Watchdog Finds Geothermal Developers Lack Permitting Tools Oil and Gas Companies Already Have
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a new report showing that companies trying to build geothermal power on public lands lack basic permitting tools that oil and gas companies already have and face confusing rules with no way to see where their permits stand, even as demand for geothermal development has grown more than fortyfold since 2020.

The watchdog report, requested by U.S. House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) found that the permitting process can be inconsistent and lacks transparency, creating uncertainty for geothermal developers and federal land managers. Oil and gas companies file permits online, track them through a dedicated system, and work from public handbooks, while geothermal developers submit permit applications in writing, wait on unpublished handbooks, and have no system tracking their permits.

The report comes as Congress has shown bipartisan interest in expanding geothermal energy development and private-sector interest in federal lands has grown significantly. According to GAO, nominations of federal lands for geothermal development increased from approximately 25,000 acres in 2020 to more than one million acres in 2025.

Despite this growing interest, geothermal developers reported to GAO inconsistent permitting decisions for exploration activities. BLM has developed handbooks intended to clarify terminology and provide consistent guidance, but those documents have remained in draft form since at least 2022.

GAO also found that BLM lacks a comprehensive mechanism for tracking geothermal permitting activity. BLM shut down its geothermal tracking system in 2021, and the system that took its place has no way to track geothermal permits. Oil and gas wells, however, are tracked in a dedicated system from initial permitting through final closure. As a result, BLM has limited visibility into permitting timelines and workloads, making planning more difficult for both developers and federal officials to anticipate project timelines and resource needs.

The House has already voted to address these problems. The bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act (H.R. 5631), which passed the House in June, includes legislation sponsored by Rep. Lee, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.). Rep. Ansari’s Geothermal Gold Book Development Act would require the Bureau to publish standard permitting procedures, in line with GAO’s recommendation.

title: Rep. Ronny Jackson Announces $9.75 Million Federal Investment in West Texas A&M Beef Cattle Research
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) announced that West Texas A&M University (WTAMU) has been awarded $9.75 million in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) to support construction of a center for beef cattle research and innovation.

NIFA awarded the grant through its Research Facilities Act Program. The federal award requires a dollar-for-dollar match, with $4.875 million from The Texas A&M University System and another $4.875 million from Texas Cattle Feeders Association, its members, West Texas A&M University (WTAMU) donors and other sources. Together, the federal grant and matching funds bring the total investment for the project to $19.5 million.

The Paul Engler College of Agriculture and Natural Sciences at WTAMU has established itself as a nationally recognized leader in beef cattle research. Approximately 25 percent of the nation’s fed cattle are produced within 150 miles of the university’s campus, placing WTAMU at the center of one of the nation’s most significant cattle-producing regions. The Texas Panhandle is also the third-largest milk-producing region in the United States, making the area a critical hub for both beef and dairy production.

The new center will strengthen applied research, workforce development, and collaboration with the beef and dairy industries across the High Plains region. The investment will help WTAMU expand its ability to conduct research under conditions that more closely reflect the realities of commercial cattle operations.

In Congress, Rep. Jackson has been a strong advocate for this project, supporting this foundational investment in August 2026. Additionally, the research feedlot will be located next to the Paul F. and Virginia J. Engler Foundation Feedlot Education Facility, which is currently under construction at WTAMU following federal community project funding secured by Rep. Jackson, which included $2.1 million in fiscal year 2024 and $1 million in fiscal year 2026.

“This funding is an investment in the future of the Texas Panhandle and in the people who keep our agricultural economy strong,” said Rep. Jackson. “WT has the expertise, the location, and the industry partnerships needed to put this investment to work. I look forward to seeing the research and opportunities this center will create for generations of producers and agricultural professionals.”

“We are grateful to USDA for recognizing the value of this work and to the partners helping WT bring it forward,” said Robert Albritton, chairman of the Board of Regents of The Texas A&M University System. “The A&M System is investing $4.875 million because research that strengthens Texas agriculture also serves the state and the nation.”

“Beef production is vital to the Panhandle, to Texas and to the country. This facility will help WT address practical questions facing cattle producers while expanding the research and training the industry needs,” said Glenn Hegar, chancellor of The Texas A&M University System. “I appreciate Congressman Jackson’s work to support WT and the region through the separate funding for the education facility.”

“The magnitude of the USDA grant, funding from the A&M System, and significant donor support underscore the critical role the Texas Panhandle plays in the beef cattle industry,” said Dr. Neil Terry, interim president. “As the university serving the Texas Panhandle, WT takes great pride in its ability to support the industry’s future through an educational center and a research feedlot that will be the best in the world.”

“The facility’s design was developed over the past three years with multiple virtual and in-person planning sessions with industry leaders,” said Dr. Kevin Pond, dean of the Paul Engler College of Agriculture and Natural Sciences. “I am grateful that our community partners have worked so hard to make this vision a reality. WT is now positioned to become a world leader in beef cattle feeding research and education, and that would not be possible without support from Congressman Jackson, the USDA, the A&M System, TCFA and many others.”

“Cattle feeding plays a significant role in the economy and communities across Texas, Oklahoma and New Mexico. Training the next generation of feedyard employees and conducting research to advance the industry is critically important for enhancing cattle feeding production practices and increasing beef production in our region,” said Ben Weinheimer, TCFA president and CEO. “The funding provided by USDA helps us continue the mission of expanding training and research initiatives at the WT research feedlot."
