title: John James introduces plan to shield Michigan from tariffs
text:
Rep. John James on Tuesday introduced legislation to shield Michigan from the effect of tariffs in the ongoing trade war with Canada, while still preserving them as a tool to protect American jobs.

Under his plan, the Tariff Relief for American Development and Employment Act (also called the TRADE Act for short), the U.S. would set aside a portion of tariff revenue into funds meant to help reshore jobs and provide temporary relief to businesses that can show they have suffered real economic harm.

“Michigan is disproportionally affected by the trade war, so it’s reasonable to use tariff revenue to reduce the effect on Michigan businesses and workers,” said James, R-Shelby Township. “Our country needs to push back on unfair trade practices, but states like Michigan should not have to shoulder that burden alone.”

Michigan has lost around 300,000 manufacturing jobs since the year 2000, and many of those jobs went to Canada. The current situation with Canada is not reciprocal, James said. Adding to the problem is that Canada is allowing China to dump auto parts into the Canadian market, which then find their way into U.S. supply chains, as a way of avoiding tariffs on Chinese products.

James has talked with the U.S. trade representative about resolving the trade dispute, and he has publicly called for Canada and the United States to return to the negotiating table.

“I fought with Canadians in Iraq. We have a deep and abiding bond that will not extinguish. I’m committed to making sure we continue to improve and deepen our relationships, and making sure our differences are resolved in a civil manner, quickly,” James said. “Our countries need to work out a reciprocal, fair, and mutually beneficial arrangement so we can bring back jobs and protect our industry.”

Before serving in Congress, James served as CEO of his family’s shipping and logistics firm, so he deeply understands cross-border trade and the auto parts industry.

The TRADE Act will help prevent U.S. companies from being forced to cut production, delay investment, or eliminate jobs solely because of extra tariff-related costs, James said. It will also reward businesses that keep jobs here, expand domestic production, and reshore supply chains.

There are two main parts to the plan. The bill establishes a Tariff Impact Relief Program, which dedicates a portion of the tariff revenue to strengthening United States domestic productive capacity.

It also establishes a Tariff Relief for American Development and Employment Fund (TRADE Fund) to help offset economic harm due to tariffs (and retaliatory tariffs) by providing targeted, temporary assistance to U.S. businesses that demonstrate actual tariff-related economic injury.

To qualify for assistance, recipients would have to agree to several “Keep It in America” conditions: keep production in the United States, maintain domestic employment numbers (aside from ordinary business fluctuations), and spend funds on things like working capital, payroll, domestic investment, domestic sourcing, training, or productivity.

The legislation includes guardrails to prevent abuse and ensure funds are being used to protect American jobs. For example, assistance may not be used for stock buybacks, to pay dividends, or to increase executive compensation. The funds likewise cannot be used to relocate production to a foreign country or to acquire a competitor, unless the Secretary of Commerce determines that the acquisition meaningfully expands domestic production capacity.

The legislation also requires the Secretary of Commerce to establish clawback provisions to recover money from fraud and violations of the domestic production requirements. Recipients will have to repay the assistance, in whole or in part, if they materially violate any of the requirements.

H.R. 10759 was referred to the Committee on Financial Services and to the Committee on Ways and Means.

James represents Michigan’s 10th Congressional District, which includes portions of Oakland and Macomb counties.

title: Jayapal Statement on Trump Suspending Microsoft from the PERM Program
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, released the following statement regarding the Trump administration’s actions to suspend Microsoft’s ability to sponsor workers through the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.

“This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.

“The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.

“You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN BROOKLYN: “WE’RE FIGHTING FOR AN AFFORDABLE AMERICA”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries held a press conference in Brooklyn, where he emphasized that House Democrats are committed to lowering the high cost of living, making healthcare affordable and holding the crooks who are ripping off the American people accountable.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Welcome to the Shirley Chisholm State Office Building here in Brooklyn. It’s an honor and a privilege to represent this area and to represent a district that Shirley Chisholm once represented here in Brooklyn in large measure. And the late, great Shirley Chisholm was a champion for making life more affordable for the people of Brooklyn, New York City and all across the country. Unfortunately, I think Shirley Chisholm would be horrified by what she’d see and what has unfolded here in the United States of America under Donald Trump and Republican control of Congress.

Donald Trump promised that costs here in the United States of America would go down on day one. But costs haven’t gone down. Costs have gone up. Life has become way too expensive as a direct result of policy decisions made by Donald Trump and the Republican-controlled Congress. The Trump Tariffs have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. House Democrats will continue to strongly oppose those tariffs and to fight to roll them back.

Donald Trump promised to love and cherish Medicaid. He then signed the Republican One Big Ugly Bill that enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, ripping healthcare away from people here in New York City, across New York State and throughout America. Donald Trump and Republicans refused to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And as a result, tens of millions of people are experiencing—including right here in New York City—dramatically increased premiums, copays and deductibles, in some cases increasing by more than $1,000 a month. These are everyday New Yorkers and everyday Americans who are no longer able to afford to go see a doctor when they need one because of decisions made by Donald Trump and the Republican-controlled Congress.

Donald Trump promised not to start endless wars in the Middle East but to stop them and then turned around and did the exact opposite by getting the country involved in a reckless and costly war of choice in Iran that hasn’t made our country any safer but has certainly made the American people economically weaker, particularly as it relates to gas prices. House Democrats are uniformly and strongly opposed to Donald Trump’s reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, and we will fight it every day until it comes to an end.

We’re fighting for an affordable America, and we’re committed, as House Democrats, for the people here in New York City, across New York State and throughout the country, to lower the high cost of groceries, lower the high cost of gas and lower the high cost of housing, which is way too expensive all across this country. We’re committed, as House Democrats, to fighting to make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American because in this great country of ours, access to high-quality and affordable healthcare shouldn’t simply be a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. It should be a right available to every single New Yorker and every single American.

And as House Democrats, finally, we are certainly committed to combating the unprecedented corruption that the Trump cartel continues to unleash on the American people. Every day brings a new revelation, including the most recent one related to the U.S. Ambassador to Greece. What we’ve seen from the Trump cartel is that they’re more focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors than they are with making life more affordable for the American people. And our promise to the country in the new Congress is that, beginning on day one, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable.

Full press conference can be watched here.

title: Rep. Mike Kelly, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright highlight federal support for steel production in Butler
text:
BUTLER, PA -- On Tuesday, October 6, U.S. Representative Mike Kelly (R-PA) joined U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves, and other local officials at Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works plant to highlight recent investments into the plant's production of Grain Oriented Electrical Steel (GOES).

Officials shared the progress of the Cleveland-Cliffs' $200 million investment in Butler Works, supported by a $75 million award from the U.S. Department of Energy, which will strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity for a critical material used in electrical transformers that support the nation's power grid.

"Thanks to the support of Secretary Wright and the Trump administration, we are strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity for a critical material used in electrical transformers that support the nation's power grid. This steel powering the world is made right here in Butler," said Rep. Kelly.

BACKGROUND

Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works is the only steel manufacturer in the United States that produces GOES, a critical component for electrical distribution transformers. Securing this supply chain is not only important for local jobs, but also for our national security.

In 2024, Kelly led opposition to a Biden-era Department of Energy rule that would have required transformers to use amorphous metal instead of grain oriented electrical steel under strict energy efficiency standards. Pressure from Kelly and members of UAW Local 3303 ultimately forced the Biden administration to revise its rule, protecting the more than 1,300 jobs at the Butler Works plant.

title: Congressman Krishnamoorthi to Honor Captain Smit Machchhar in Congressional Record for His Heroism During Flydubai Hijacking Attempt
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) announced today that he will enter a statement into the Congressional Record on Friday honoring Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery aboard Flydubai Flight 1073 on September 30, 2026. After being attacked by the flight’s first officer, who attempted to seize control of the aircraft, Captain Machchhar’s actions helped save the lives of 172 passengers and his fellow crew members.

Congressman Krishnamoorthi’s full statement follows:

“Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize Captain Smit Machchhar of India, a husband, father, and pilot with 17 years of flying experience, including 11 as a captain, whose extraordinary bravery on September 30, 2026, helped save the lives of 172 passengers and his fellow crew members aboard Flydubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, including 4 United States citizens and 27 children.

Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked Captain Machchhar with the aircraft's emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls. The aircraft plunged approximately 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar fought his way to the cockpit door and opened it, allowing passengers and crew members to enter and overpower his attacker. Two reserve Flydubai pilots traveling aboard the aircraft then took control and landed it safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Even as Captain Machchhar fought for his own life, he understood that the lives of everyone aboard depended on what he did next. Despite his injuries, his years of experience told him that the aircraft was going down, and he found the strength to reach that door. His presence of mind, determination, and courage gave the passengers and crew the chance they needed to stop the attack and avert a catastrophe.

Behind every person aboard Flight 1073 is a family that was spared an unimaginable loss. Because Captain Machchhar refused to give up, the passengers and crew aboard that aircraft had the chance to return to the people who love them.

Mr. Speaker, I ask my colleagues to join me in honoring Captain Smit Machchhar, whose extraordinary courage helped save hundreds of lives aboard Flight 1073. We extend our warmest wishes to him, his wife Sonal, their two children, and their entire family, and we hope for the captain’s full-speed recovery from his injuries at the earliest.”

title: President Donald Trump Signs Congressman David Kustoff’s Identity Theft Bill into Law
text:
WASHINGTON – Congressman David Kustoff (R-TN-08) announced that President Donald Trump signed H.R. 5345, the Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act, into law on October 7, 2026. The bipartisan legislation will provide Social Security identity theft victims with a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration (SSA) until their case is resolved.

“Americans recovering from identity theft should not have to fight through layers of red tape to receive help,” said Congressman David Kustoff. “With President Trump’s signature, victims will have a trained Social Security Administration employee responsible for coordinating their case and seeing it through to resolution. I appreciate President Trump and my colleagues in both chambers for working with me to deliver this commonsense reform and create a more reliable recovery process.”

"The theft of someone's Social Security number can do real damage to that person's life. Cleaning up that mess should not require a call center scavenger hunt or being bounced from one Social Security official to the next. This law fixes that. It puts a dedicated team in charge of a victim's case from the first call to the last, so that families can now spend their energy getting their life back instead of repeating their story to a new stranger every time they call. I want to commend Representative Kustoff for identifying a simple, commonsense solution, and I thank President Trump for signing this into law and his continued leadership in cutting government red tape for the American people." -- Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith (MO-08)

Under the new law, trained SSA employees serving as points of contact will coordinate with other offices, maintain continuity of case records, and remain accountable until each case is resolved. The law will also apply when a Social Security card is lost in the mail.

Congressman Kustoff introduced H.R. 5345 on September 15, 2025. The House Committee on Ways and Means advanced the bill by a vote of 39–1, and the House passed it by unanimous consent on December 1, 2025. The Senate unanimously passed the legislation on September 17, 2026. Click here to read the bill text.

title: Larson Joins Bipartisan Colleagues to Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
text:
Washington, D.C. - Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Jim Costa (CA-21), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H. Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day." National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.

As Co-Chair of the bipartisan Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Caucus, Rep. Larson has long championed fuel cell technology and has been a forceful advocate for extending the Investment Tax Credit for fuel cells and linear generators, securing its extension in both 2018 and 2022 as part of the Inflation Reduction Act. He co-led introduction of the bipartisan Technology for Energy Security Act to extend the tax credit for another eight years and the American Affordability Act, to bring down costs for households, including a plan to spur the development of American-made clean energy by providing a tax credit to companies that reduce carbon emissions by producing "green" and "blue" hydrogen and fuel cells.

"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."

The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power. Larson, Costa, Tonko, Valadao, Fitzpatrick, and Bilirakis are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Reps.Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) led the introduction of the Senate Resolution, with Senators Bill Cassidy (R-LA), Chris Coons (D-DE), and Chris Murphy (D-CT) joining as original cosponsors.

"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."

"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," said Tonko. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."

"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Valadao.

"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Fitzpatrick.

"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of the Fuel Cell and Hydrogen Energy Association (FCHEA). "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large.”

title: Sánchez, House Democratic colleagues oppose rule denying legal immigrants tax credits
text:
WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.) led her House Democratic colleagues today in calling on the Trump administration to withdraw a proposed IRS rule that would strip certain legal immigrants of refundable tax credits.

The rule would reclassify these credits as “Federal public benefits” under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA), imposing strict citizenship requirements on recipients. It is similar to a failed attempt by the Department of Health and Human Services last year to block certain legal immigrants from health services, an effort the courts struck down.

“The rules regarding the eligibility criteria for refundable tax credits are clearly defined by Congress in the Internal Revenue Code, and PRWORA was clearly never intended to separately address them,” the members wrote. “Yet, this proposed regulation would strip hundreds of thousands of people of their deserved tax refunds by redefining refundable tax credits as ‘Federal public benefits’ under PRWORA, harming our constituents, their families, and our communities.”

The members continued, “The administration’s apparent desire to change the law to attack immigrant communities does not change Congress’s intent when it passed PRWORA, nor does it change the law.”

In addition to Sánchez, the letter was signed by Representatives Mike Thompson (D-Calif.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Gwen Moore (D-Wis.), Sylvia Garcia (D-Texas), Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Danny Davis (D-Ill.), Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Jesús “Chuy” García (D-Ill.), Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.), Steven Horsford (D-Nev.), Dan Goldman (D-N.Y.), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.)

The full text of the letter is available HERE and follows:

October 7, 2026

Honorable Frank Bisignano

Chief Executive Officer

U.S. Internal Revenue Service

1111 Constitution Avenue NW

Washington, DC 20224

Honorable Scott Bessent

Secretary

U.S. Department of the Treasury

1500 Pennsylvania Ave, NW

Washington, DC 20220

Dear Secretary Bessent and CEO Bisignano,

We write to express our strong opposition to the proposed rule on the Application of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (PRWORA) to the Refunded Portion of Certain Federal Refundable Tax Credits. The rules regarding the eligibility criteria for refundable tax credits are clearly defined by Congress in the Internal Revenue Code, and PRWORA was clearly never intended to separately address them. Yet, this proposed regulation would strip hundreds of thousands of people of their deserved tax refunds by redefining refundable tax credits as “Federal public benefits” under PRWORA, harming our constituents, their families, and our communities.

Congress has modified these credits since PRWORA was enacted (most recently in Public Law 119-21 (2025)) but never made the changes Treasury proposes in this rule. Therefore, Congress clearly did not intend to import PRWORA’s limits on eligibility for federal public benefits into these refundable tax credits. In fact, Congress’s decision in P.L. 119-21 to limit the American Opportunity Tax Credit to people with a valid Social Security number would be nonsensical under Treasury’s reading of the statute, because those without one would have already been excluded. The Congressional Budget Office would not have estimated this provision to reduce the deficit by $247 million had the assertions in this proposed rule been accurate. Similarly, Congress’s decision in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2018) to limit Child Tax Credit eligibility to people with a valid Social Security number would not have made sense if PRWORA already imposed a much stricter interpretation.

The administration’s apparent desire to change the law to attack immigrant communities does not change Congress’s intent when it passed PRWORA, nor does it change the law. As the notice of rulemaking states, “Section 401(c)(1)(B) of PRWORA (8 U.S.C. 1611(c)(1)(B)) defines the term “Federal public benefit,” in relevant part, as “any retirement, welfare, health, disability, public or assisted housing, postsecondary education, food assistance, unemployment benefit, or any other similar benefit for which payments or assistance are provided to an individual, household, or family eligibility unit by an agency of the United States or by appropriated funds of the United States. ” Tax credits are absent from that list, which clearly consists of direct assistance programs delivered through federally funded programs. Congress would have explicitly specified tax credits if it had intended their inclusion. Wholly adopting a novel and unsupported interpretation of PRWORA to fit President Trump’s anti-immigrant agenda goes directly against the law as written and congressional intent.

In fact, PRWORA separately addressed the issue of immigrants qualifying for refundable credits when it originally passed in 1996. Section 451 of PRWORA restricted the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) by barring those without a Social Security Number from the tax credit. The remaining eligible population is a much broader group than those deemed “qualified” immigrants under that law. If Congress intended to restrict refundable tax credits to only “qualified” immigrants, it would have not included this separate section in a distinct section of that law.

The proposed regulation relies on the 2020 Department of Justice Office of Legal Counsel opinion stating that any payment to a taxpayer may be classified as a benefit under PRWORA regardless of congressional intent and history. The proposal fails to justify why this new interpretation, upending 30 years of precedent, is valid given Congress’s past decisions to make very clear which immigrants were or were not eligible for refundable tax credits. Had Congress intended to bar immigrants from taking advantage of refundable tax credits, it would have clarified the statute in any of the numerous changes made to PRWORA or refundable tax credits in the years since 1996.

We urge you to withdraw this proposed regulation, which has no basis in the law, upends decades of precedent and runs counter to congressional intent.

Sincerely,

###

title: Malliotakis Highlights Breast Cancer Awareness, Prevention & Treatment at Staten Island University Hospital
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — In recognition of October being Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) visited Staten Island University Hospital’s Florina Rusi Marke Comprehensive Breast Center to highlight the importance of early detection and lifesaving screenings, as well as initiatives in Congress to support cancer research and expand access to quality care.

Malliotakis joined physicians and medical professionals from Staten Island University Hospital to discuss breast cancer prevention and treatment, advances in patient care and the resources available to women in the community. The Congresswoman also highlighted several efforts she is supporting in Congress to improve access to breast cancer screenings, treatment and care.

Congresswoman Malliotakis' Legislative Efforts to Expand Breast Cancer Screening & Care:

EARLY Act Reauthorization (H.R. 4541): In July, the Congresswoman voted for House passage of legislation that supports breast-health education and awareness for younger and higher-risk women and includes provisions of the SCREENS for Cancer Act to strengthen the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program, which provides screening and diagnostic services for underserved women. Staten Island University Hospital, Richmond University Medical Center and NYU Langone Health’s Perlmutter Cancer Center— all benefit from this program.

Women's Health Initiative: Additionally, the Congresswoman has supported and protected federal funding for one of the nation's largest and longest-running studies of women's health, whose research includes breast cancer and other major conditions affecting women.

Find It Early Act (H.R. 6182): Congresswoman Malliotakis cosponsored bipartisan legislation that would expand insurance coverage for breast cancer screening and diagnostic imaging without patient cost-sharing, including mammograms, ultrasounds and MRIs for women with dense breasts or an increased risk of breast cancer.

Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act (H.R. 2048): The Congresswoman cosponsored legislation to eliminate the waiting periods for Social Security Disability Insurance and Medicare coverage for individuals diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer.

The Congresswoman is also advocating that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz review Medicare coverage for supplemental breast ultrasounds for women with dense breast tissue after the Biden Administration issued a 2024 rule that stopped Medicare coverage of ultrasounds for breast cancer prevention.

“Early detection and access to quality care can save lives, which is why it’s so important that women have access to the screenings, treatment and resources they need,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “During Breast Cancer Awareness Month, we’re highlighting the tremendous work being done right here on Staten Island to prevent, detect and treat breast cancer, while continuing our efforts in Congress to expand access to screenings, support critical research and ensure patients can get the care they need.”

“Congressmember Malliotakis’ support of the Find It Early Act brings important attention to an issue that directly affects women and families across Staten Island and beyond,” said Meagan Sills, Senior Vice President and Hospital President of Staten Island University Hospital. “Nearly 18,000 women in New York are diagnosed with breast cancer each year, and for many women, a routine mammogram may only be the first step. Breast density, family history, and other individual risk factors can require additional imaging such as an ultrasound or MRI. When that testing is medically appropriate, cost should not stand between a patient and the care her physician recommends. We appreciate Congressmember Malliotakis’ advocacy to help reduce those barriers and support greater access to early detection.”

title: McGovern calls for the release of detained Egyptian journalists
text:
WASHINGTON—Today, Congressman James P. McGovern (D-MA) released the following statement calling for the release of detained Egyptian journalists:

“As the Democratic Co-Chair of the bipartisan Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, I condemn the arrest of six journalists affiliated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash and call on the government of Egypt to release them immediately.

"On September 28, Egyptian security forces raided the homes of and arrested Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira and Abdullah Qadri, both of whom are editors at Matsadaash. Later that day, Egyptian state security arrested four additional journalists, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud, and Mohamed Adel, constituting the entirety of the newsroom. Authorities have not publicly issued charges against the journalists or justification for their arrest.

"This comes after the Trump Administration shamefully released $320 million in military aid to Egypt which had been withheld due to human rights concerns.

"Matsadaash has repeatedly been targeted by Egyptian authorities for its open-source investigative reporting. The recent arrest of its newsroom represents an alarming escalation of repression against independent media and freedom of expression in Egypt, particularly as some of the detainees report having been tortured. Pursuant to its obligations as a state party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the Convention Against Torture, Egypt must respect the rights of its citizens to freedom of expression and freedom from arbitrary detention and torture.

"As a partner in the Defending Freedoms Project, which campaigns to free prisoners of conscience around the world, I demand that the Egyptian government release the six detained journalists immediately. I also call on authorities to refrain from further targeting of members of the Matsadaash platform and other press workers.”

title: GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION TASK FORCE CHAIR THOMPSON, JUDICIARY COMMITTEE RANKING MEMBER RASKIN AND REP. MCBATH LEAD 174 MEMBERS CALLING ON DOJ TO ENFORCE YOUTH HANDGUN LAW
text:
Washington – Gun Violence Prevention Task Force Chair Mike Thompson, Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin, and Rep. Lucy McBath lead a bipartisan letter with 174 members calling on the Department of Justice (DOJ) to enforce the 1968 law which prohibits licensed gun dealers from selling handguns to 18-20-year-olds.

“DOJ’s decision to block the enforcement of the 1968 law which prohibits 18-20-year-olds from buying handguns is unconstitutional, and will make our communities, and especially our schools less safe,” said Mike Thompson. “It is outrageous that DOJ would unilaterally overturn the law and allow an 18-year-old high school student to buy a handgun, buy a silencer, and have them shipped to their house without ever leaving their basement. That is just wrong.”

“For generations, the landmark provision prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds has saved countless lives. Yet, now, the Trump Department of Justice has released a baseless opinion that this provision is unconstitutional and cannot be enforced. This reckless decision will allow young adults to obtain the firearms most often used in crime, jeopardizing public safety and putting those most at risk for gun violence in greater danger. Brady thanks Chair Thompson and Ranking Members Raskin and McBath for leading the effort to oppose this senseless decision and for their dedication to protecting America’s youth from gun violence,” said Mark Collins, Director of Federal Policy, Brady.

“The math here is simple: 18- to 20-year-olds commit gun homicides at triple the rate of people 21 and older, which is why more than 80% of Americans want 21 to be the minimum age to buy a gun,” said John Feinblatt, president of Everytown for Gun Safety. “Trump’s MAGA DOJ is handing the gun industry something it could never win in Congress or at the ballot box, and America will pay for it in lives lost and communities shattered.”

"The Office of Legal Counsel has no authority to erase a federal gun law and put more handguns in the hands of teenagers. This decision disregards clear evidence that minimum-age laws save lives,” said GIFFORDS Executive Director EmmaBrown. “The Trump administration must immediately reverse this dangerous action. I thank Representatives Jamie Raskin, Lucy McBath, and Mike Thompson, as well as the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, for their leadership in defending this lifesaving law.”

The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others. Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns.

The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.

Dear Attorney General Blanche,

We urge the Department of Justice to immediately rescind its opinion illegally declaring that a 1968 law prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds by federally licensed firearms dealers “may not be enforced.”

Since the passage of the Gun Control Act of 1968 some 58 years ago, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has faithfully enforced it according to clear congressional intent and defended its constitutionality. The Supreme Court has never questioned, much less invalidated, this statute. Its policy rationale—that 18-to-20-year-olds lack the cognitive judgment required to safely own and handle handguns has only grown more compelling with advancements in our understanding of brain development over the last six decades and the record of gun violence already associated with that age group.

The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support, and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others.

DOJ’s sudden epiphany that this essential law, which has been enforced by Democratic and Republican Attorneys General continuously for more than a half-century, is unconstitutional would override the judgment of the last 29 Congresses, which have staunchly stood by the law. Your personal reinterpretation would now allow 18-to-20-year-olds to purchase easily concealable handguns, a kind disproportionately used in violent crimes.

We already have a problem with young men in the 18-20 year range obtaining a firearm from family, friends or the criminal underground and using it to conduct a mass shooting. Millions of Americans remember when a 20-year-old gunman in Newtown, Connecticut killed 27 people, overwhelmingly children, in the deadliest elementary school massacre in American history. According to a study published in the American Journal of Public Health, one in eight mass shooters was between 18 and 20 years old.[1] Indeed, 18-to-20-year-olds have already been shown to be responsible for a disproportionate share of school shootings. [2] In fact, they comprise just 4 percent of the US population, but account for 17 percent of known gun homicide offenders generally. [3]

Teens and young adults are also already at higher risk for firearm suicide. Limiting access to firearms has been a proven and effective way of lowering rates of firearm suicide. One study demonstrated that when states restricted handgun sales to individuals under the age of 21, the firearm suicide rate declined 12 percent among 18-to-20-year-olds. [4]

Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns. FBI crime statistics from 2020 to 2024 show that 92 percent of firearms identified in murders were handguns, 6 percent were rifles, and 2 percent were shotguns. The lack of legal access to handguns by people under the age of 21 explains why crime guns traced to 18-, 19-, and 20-year-olds remain relatively low compared to the next age cohort of 21-, 22-, and 23-year-olds. The rate at which firearms recovered in crimes are traced back to young purchasers jumps 10-fold at age 21 before peaking at age 22.[5] This sharp increase tracks with the legal minimum age to purchase handguns and would therefore begin rising earlier after DOJ’s baffling new refusal to enforce the 1968 law.

Young adults engage in crime at a higher rate than the rest of the adult population and lowering the age to purchase a handgun would make an even larger percentage of youths vulnerable to coercion or cooption by traffickers. According to the ATF, “The most frequent age of a purchaser of a crime gun was 22 years old, with purchasers between 21 and 25 years old accounting for almost as many traced crime guns as all purchasers ages 45 and older.” One reason most crime guns are purchased by people in this age group is because traffickers frequently use, and often force younger individuals who don't have criminal backgrounds to straw-purchase their weapons for them.

DOJ’s reckless U-turn interpretation of the 1968 law is made exceptionally more dangerous when combined with ATF’s proposed rule that would allow Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) to engage in more “non-over-the-counter” gun sales than ever before. In other words, with this new opinion and if ATF’s rule is finalized as proposed, FFLs will be able to sell handguns to purchasers between the ages of 18 and 20 without them ever setting foot in a gun store and then deliver those guns directly to their door. This would eliminate critical opportunities for responsible FFLs to observe suspicious behavior that may indicate criminal intent and to exercise their discretion to decline such sales. This would be inconsistent with congressional intent and unnecessarily endanger public safety.

The sensible restriction on FFLs from selling handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds is constitutional and is helping save lives every day. Your duty is to enforce the law as Congress writes it, not to make up new laws you prefer and substitute them for the public will as expressed through Congress. We urge you to immediately rescind your unlawful and dangerous opinion.

Sincerely,

[1] Joshua D. Brown and Amie J. Goodin, “Mass Casualty Shooting Venues, Types of Firearms, and Age of Perpetrators in the United States, 1982–2018,” American Journal of Public Health 108, no. 10 (2018): 1385–138.7

[2] Paul M. Reeping et al., “State Firearm Laws, Gun Ownership, and K-12 School Shootings: Implications for School Safety,” Journal of School Violence 21, no. 2 (2022): 132–146.

[3] Eighteen to 20 year olds commit 18% of gun homicides, despite comprising just four percent of the US population. Giffords Law Center analysis of FBI Supplementary Homicide Report (SHR) data, 2016–2020.

[4] Emma E. Fridel et al., “Examining the Impact of Minimum Handgun Purchase Age and Background Check Legislation on Young Adult Suicide in the United States, 1991–2020.” American Journal of Public Health 0 (2024).

[5] https://www.atf.gov/media/15426/download

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

title: Rep. Panetta Stands with Local Community Leaders  to Call on the United States Postal Service  to Restore Mail Service to Brookdale
text:
To watch his remarks, click HERE.

For additional photos and b-roll, click HERE.

Brookdale, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together local elected leaders and community members at the Brookdale Lodge to voice their unified opposition to the U.S. Postal Service’s (USPS) proposed permanent closure of the Brookdale Post Office. Rep. Panetta was joined at the press conference by Santa Cruz County Supervisor Monica Martinez, Jason Patel of the Brookdale Lodge, and other concerned Brookdale residents. With more than 30 community members present, the group called on USPS to restore mail service as soon as they can to Brookdale.

After nearly two years of delays, missed deadlines, and inconsistent statements, USPS recently launched a discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office without proposing an alternative location in the community or expanded local service. The proposed closure would leave the people of Brookdale without local postal services in a community that already lacks USPS home delivery.

“For nearly two years, the people of Brookdale have waited in good faith while USPS sat on its hands, missed deadlines, and failed to provide a reliable timeline for restoring service,” said Rep. Panetta. “Now, instead of finding a new location or restoring local service, USPS is studying whether to permanently close the Brookdale Post Office. We are standing shoulder to shoulder to call for USPS to halt the study and restore postal services for the Brookdale community.”

“It is unfair for USPS to further burden Brookdale residents, who have already had to assume additional costs in the aftermath of the CZU Lightning Fire Complex, by asking them to travel out of town to access their mail during work hours. If they won’t reestablish a post office, USPS should offer home delivery in Brookdale, like it does in neighboring towns,” said Santa Cruz County Supervisor Monica Martinez.

“After nearly two years without local postal service, Brookdale residents deserve a solution, not a permanent closure. Brookdale residents don’t get home mail delivery, making the post office their only way to receive their prescriptions, ballots, and bills. Since the fire, they have had to drive to Boulder Creek or Ben Lomond to pick up their mail. I stand with Congressman Panetta and Brookdale residents in calling on USPS to restore postal service in Brookdale,” said Assemblymember Gail Pellerin.

“We, the residents of Brookdale, respectfully request the restoration of a permanent U.S. Post Office in the community of Brookdale, Zip Code 95007,” said Brookdale Resident Sally Lussier.

USPS plays a fundamental role in making sure Americans stay informed and participate in our democracy, receive essential government services, pay their bills, and maintain access to lifesaving medication. However, postal services in Brookdale have been suspended since a fire damaged the community’s post office in December 2024. Since then, Brookdale residents have had to travel to Boulder Creek to receive essential mail and conduct the everyday business of their lives. That burden falls especially hard on seniors, people with disabilities, working families, and residents without reliable transportation.

With USPS closing the study’s comment period on October 11, Rep. Panetta and local leaders urged residents to submit their questionnaires and feedback before the deadline. Rep. Panetta also collected comment cards from Brookdale residents expressing their opposition to the proposed permanent closure, which he will submit directly to USPS this week. Those who could not attend the event in person can complete the form linked here by October 9 to have their concerns submitted by Rep. Panetta’s office.

USPS was invited to attend the event but declined to participate, citing its September 11 virtual meeting on the discontinuance feasibility study.

Rep. Panetta has repeatedly pressed USPS leadership to restore postal services in Brookdale. Last week, Rep. Panetta wrote to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding that USPS immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, identify a new location in Brookdale, and expand appropriate postal services to serve the community. In a February 2026 letter to the Postmaster General, he called on USPS to repair and reopen the facility with a clear project timeline and provide temporary postal service within the community in the interim. After USPS missed its promised May 1 reopening date, Rep. Panetta sent a May 2026 letter requesting that the USPS Inspector General review the agency’s management, communication, and decision-making, the adequacy of interim services, and the feasibility of restoring service through a temporary or alternative facility.

Rep. Panetta will continue to oppose the USPS proposal to permanently close the Brookdale Post Office and demand a permanent postal facility that serves the Brookdale community.

title: ICYMI: Pappas-Backed AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act Passed House
text:
The House passed the bipartisan AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, legislation cosponsored by Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01). This legislation would ensure Americans continue to have access to AM radio in all new vehicles.

“In addition to being a source of news, music, and community connection, AM radio is a lifeline in emergencies for Americans to get important information and stay safe. This bipartisan legislation will help make sure people do not lose access to this free service in their cars,” said Congressman Pappas.

More than 50 million Americans listen to AM broadcast radio every month, and it remains one of the most reliable ways to reach the public during emergencies because it can travel long distances and reach broad geographic areas. AM radio is the backbone behind America’s National Public Warning System, which provides emergency-alert and warning information to the public during major natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, chemical incidents, health emergencies, and other domestic threats, often when cellular and Internet networks fail.

Despite the clear public safety uses of AM broadcast radio, many manufacturers stopped including it in their vehicles because they did not want to spend the minimal funds to ensure public safety during emergencies.

The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act will require the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all automakers include AM radio as standard equipment in their vehicles, at no additional cost to consumers.

title: Congressman Patronis Joins Senator Scott and Local Officials in Pensacola Ahead of Hurricane Isaias
text:
PENSACOLA, FL –Today, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (R-FL) joined Senator Rick Scott (R-FL), Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves, Representative Michelle Salzman, Representative Alex Andrade, Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons, and other state and local officials in Pensacola to discuss hurricane preparedness ahead of Hurricane Isaias.

To view the full clip click here or above.

Congressman Patronis: . Thank you, Senator Scott. You can always count on Senator Scott showing up. There is nobody who I think has taken a better interest in making sure that our citizens, our elected officials, our law enforcement, and our first responders have what they need to do their job. And so you being here the day before the storm, that’s just true to form.

I told the senator, you know, for about the past nine years, I’ve dealt with nine storms. We learn something from every storm. So I’m gonna try to leave you with about three good hits to walk away from. As you’re trying to focus, you think about what you’re doing, maybe four hits.

When you think about your insurance and your insurance recovery, today’s really the last day that you can do your insurance and your fiscal health preparation. And what I mean by that is I want you to take, we’re a smartphone society, I want you to take your smartphone, I want you to walk around the outside of your house and shoot a video of that house. Show that there’s no damage done to the outside of the house. Inside, you’re gonna do a little bit of a different video. You’re gonna do an inventory. You’re gonna take a picture of your wardrobe, video of your floor covering, your TV, what’s in your garage.

Here’s why you’re gonna do that, and you’re gonna email it to yourself. You’re gonna put it in a virtual place, okay? And if you got a copy of your insurance policy, take a picture of it. Email those to yourself. Now, fast forward where the storm is hitting, and God forbid you get hit by a tornado or some storm-force winds or a tree falls on your house. Now you’ve got photographic evidence of what your place looked like before the storm, okay? What’s gonna happen, the insurance company’s gonna send an adjuster out. That’s just a different way of saying an investigator. They’re coming out to investigate what damage they are liable for. So now you’ve got photographic evidence before and after where it makes it a lot easier to show your insurance company, this is what you owe me because this is all new damage.

Second, I want you to understand, the predators are going to be pre-staged outside of your neighborhoods better than the power company is, okay? These guys will canvas your neighborhoods. They hate it when I say this, but they are what they are. They’re locusts. They canvas your neighborhoods. They are there because you are vulnerable. You are not prepared to deal with the destruction that a hurricane can bestow on you, your family, your neighborhood, your community, and they know that. So what do they do? They try to get in between you and your insurance claim by getting you to sign something.

So here’s the easy part. Just don’t sign anything. As long as you don’t sign any documents, you have no way to get hurt financially by the storm. If your first phone call is to your insurance agent, your insurance carrier, the Department of Financial Services, heck, call my office. We will help put you in touch with the proper insurance authority in getting the claim process started. I want you to also be on the lookout in your inbox, because most insurance companies, they’re not living under a rock. They see this storm approaching the coast also. You’ve probably already got an email from your insurance company saying, hey, it’s coming your way. Why don’t you go ahead and pre-start the claim filing process? Because there is a probability you’re going to have damage, and they want to get you in the pipeline. This is great that they’re doing this, because they’re leaning forward to try to get ahead of the curve of potentially hundreds or maybe even thousands of claims. So please look up that email, fill it out, pay attention. Do it now while you’re not under stress.

Now, the last thing I kinda wanna leave with ya is we have seen a growth, a huge spike in EVs, but more so e-bikes. A lot of people, a lot of our friends, they’re great, they get you around fast, not a lot of exercise to ’em. The problem is, is you’re—if you’re in a two-story home, you’re not gonna take that thing upstairs. Those are operated by lithium-ion batteries. When those things interact with salt water, it becomes a thermal runaway. They do not distinguish with water. You can literally throw ’em in the bay, and they’re still gonna burn. The problem you’re gonna run into, as soon as you have any flood in a low-lying area, and it engages that salt water, now you’ve got a fire that can’t be put out, and if it’s at the bottom of your house or in your garage, you know what’s gonna happen? It’s gonna burn down your house, ’cause maybe it survived the storm, but it’s not gonna survive the EV.

So, if you’ve got an EV, I want you to take it to higher ground. If you’ve got a golf cart, I want you to get it away from that low-lying area. If you’ve got an e-bike, I want you to get it upstairs. And lastly, look, your first responders, these guys are superheroes. They may not wear capes, but they’re superheroes. They are going to be putting themselves in harm’s way, and just like the senator said, don’t be a knucklehead. Don’t think you can handle this storm. We’ve got 1.8 million new Floridians in the state of Florida since 2018. A lot of those folks have no idea what they’re in for. I’m glad they’re in our state, and I’m glad they’ve decided to retire here and bring their businesses, but they don’t know what a hurricane can do to them, and this is no different. Err on the side of caution. If you’re told to evacuate, please leave. Now here’s another superhero. You got your cape on? We’ve got Sheriff Chip Simmons, our sheriff here in Escambia County. Sheriff.”

title: Congressman Patronis Warns Floridians About EV, Scooter Fire Risks Ahead of Hurricane Isaias
text:
NAVARRE BEACH, FL – Today, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (R-FL) is urging Floridians to take precautions with electric vehicles, scooters and other battery powered devices ahead of Hurricane Isais.

“Many Floridians don’t realize that electric vehicles and scooters exposed to saltwater storm surge can pose a serious fire risk if their batteries are damaged,” said Congressman Patronis. “If your electric scooter or vehicle is in an area vulnerable to flooding or storm surge, move it to higher ground before the storm arrives. There are a lot of lithium-ion batteries around our tourist destinations, and they can pose a huge fire risk if exposed to saltwater. Get them out of harm’s way before the storm hits.”

Saltwater flooding and storm surge can damage lithium-ion batteries, creating a potential fire hazard even after floodwaters recede. Congressman Patronis is urging residents in flood-prone areas to move electric vehicles and scooters to higher ground before the storm arrives. These fires can be harder to put out and can reignite even after they appear to be extinguished.

Residents should:

Move EVs and scooters to higher ground before flooding begins.

Avoid putting vehicles or battery-powered devices in standing or moving water.

Keep damaged batteries away from structures. If a battery-powered vehicle has been exposed to flooding or appears damaged, keep it away from homes, garages and other buildings.

Pay attention to push notifications from your electric vehicle’s apps for important safety updates and instructions.

Follow guidance from local emergency officials and fire departments.

title: Amata Highlights Facts About ‘Trump Accounts’ for American Samoa’s Children
text:
Pago Pago – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is highlighting the upcoming possibility for American Samoa’s children to begin a new investment growth account, known as Trump accounts, funded by the child’s guardian.

“The federal law creating Trump account investments does not prevent U.S. nationals from participating, so I want our people to be informed to make their own decisions,” said Congresswoman Aumua Amata. “The children of our islands who are U.S. nationals can be included, and must have their U.S. Social Security number to participate along with U.S. citizens.”

“I know that every hard-earned dollar is precious to our families, and needed in your current household budget, but starting an early investment even with a small amount has potential to build up in the future for a child with a full lifetime of growth earnings ahead of them, so this is information for your consideration, prayer, and counsel,” continued Aumua Amata.

What to know:

These accounts do not apply to residents of American Samoa who are not U.S. nationals or citizens.

Trump Accounts are traditional Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs) for minors under age 18, managed by an adult guardian to build growth for them through U.S. stock market investments. While owned by the child, they are administered by a parent or legal guardian as custodian until the owner turns 18. Only the adult can start the account, using the official app from Trump Accounts (Trumpaccounts.gov) or via the IRS using Form 4547.

An account holder may contribute up to $5,000 per year in regular individual contributions per child. At their choice, employers may contribute up to $2,500 tax-free annually.

Note that your individual contributions are made with after-tax dollars (non-deductible), but the earnings then grow tax-deferred. The investments are placed in low-cost mutual funds or ETFs tracking major U.S. equity indexes like the S&P 500.

In general, no withdrawals are permitted while the beneficiary is a minor. Full control transfers to the individual at age 18. The account converts fully to a standard traditional IRA, with standard retirement or qualified penalty-free distribution rules.

Congress and President Trump created these accounts through Public Law 119-21, signed into law in 2025, which was designated the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, also called the Working Families Tax Cuts.

title: Amata Highlights NOAA Ocean Observation Funds, and Her Record of Legislative Support
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is welcoming the announcement of NOAA funding for regional and national ocean observing. The 11 new five-year cooperative agreements announced Thursday will enable U.S. IOOS regional associations to operate regional coastal observing systems (RCOSs) throughout U.S. waters, with $45.7 million in overall funding for the first year, supporting operation and modernization of observing capabilities for coasts, ocean, and the Great Lakes. The Pacific Islands region, including American Samoa, is supported at over $4 million ($4,033,322) for fiscal year 2027.

Wave buoys like these are essential instruments in ocean observing and there are over 600 assets, including buoys, reporting wave data throughout IOOS. Wave information is important for weather forecasting, safe navigation, port operations, coastal planning, coastal hazard prediction and mitigation, and many more applications. Photo credit: PacIOOS

Congresswoman Amata has supported and cosponsored bipartisan legislation to authorize, boost funding, and enhance these capabilities for Pacific waters, as well as volcano warning systems. In this Congress, as an original cosponsor, Amata co-led the House-passed bill, H.R 2294, to reauthorize this program. She also supported the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law in 2021 that has funded these same 11 NOAA project areas, including the buoys. Also this Congress, she supported in committee the bipartisan bill, H.R. 3176, which has passed the House, to reauthorize national volcano early warning systems for five years. She has supported Pacific volcano study legislation, and numerous related bills for tsunami response, since her first year in Congress.

“In American Samoa, just days ago, we observed our anniversary of the dreadful 2009 tsunami that cost many lives and caused much devastation. Our Manu’a Islands have experienced rumblings and scientists keep watch on the Vailulu’u Seamount, and in 2022, Tongo experienced a massive, deadly volcanic blast and tsunami,” said Aumua Amata. “We depend on the important science of ocean observations for quality data, like wave measurements, for services, decision-making and storm readiness. We have a buoy named in memory of longtime Port Director Chris King for his years of service to American Samoa.”

Under the agreements, announced Thursday by NOAA, the Pacific Islands Ocean Observing System (PacIOOS) will operate and maintain the regional coastal observing system (RCOS) for Pacific Islands, including the State of Hawai‘i; the territories of Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands; the Freely Associated States the Republic of Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Republic of the Marshall Islands; and the U.S. Minor Outlying Islands (Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston, Kingman, Midway, Palmyra, and Wake).

The data collected from ocean observations:

Supports fishermen, aquaculturists, shipping and logistics managers, and coastal communities in making sound economic and safety decisions;

Supports management and mitigation of coastal hazards, such as flooding and harmful algal blooms; and

Provides essential information for weather forecasting and national defense.

The regional associations are a fundamental part of the national observing system, and help ensure that the system is both effective and efficient. They are federally certified to collect and manage high-quality observing data, forming robust partnerships with local stakeholders and coastal communities. As the regional component of the nationwide U.S. IOOS network, regional associations meet local needs by using stakeholder feedback to guide the development of RCOSs while also integrating national priorities and requirements.

These cooperative agreements are awarded every five years through a competitive process and support the continued operation and modernization of our nation’s coastal, ocean and Great Lakes observing capabilities. Total awards include additional funding from other NOAA offices in the National Ocean Service, National Weather Service, NOAA Fisheries, NOAA Satellites and NOAA Research.

title: Scalise: House Republicans are Lowering Costs and Bringing Back American Manufacturing
text:
NEW ORLEANS, La. — Today, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) joined Fox Business Network’s Mornings with Fox Business to discuss House Republicans’ efforts to lower costs, Senate Democrats' obstruction, and America's manufacturing boom thanks to President Trump's leadership.

title: Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.

2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.

In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.

“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”

Joining Congresswoman Schrier in the letter to President Trump were Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), and U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).

The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”

“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Visit Oakland Head Start Facility and Community Health Center, Condemn Republican Cuts to Childcare, Healthcare, and Education Programs
text:
OAKLAND, CA – This week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) hosted, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA-05), the highest-ranking woman in the House of Representatives, in Oakland’s Fruitvale neighborhood. They visited the Unity Council’s Head Start and Early Head Start Preschool facilities and La Clínica de La Raza, a federally qualified health center, to meet with families, frontline health care staff, and care workers who have been impacted by Republicans’ devastating federal aid cuts.

President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ “One Big, Cruel, Ugly Bill” has made deep cuts to federal funding for healthcare, childcare, education, and food assistance programs. In California’s 12th Congressional District, it is estimated that 31,000 people are experiencing rising healthcare costs and 35, 595 people will lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medi-Cal and decision to end enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits. In Congress, Congresswoman Simon has consistently fought against cuts to Medicaid/Medi-CAL and SNAP and attempts to gut Head Start.

“My daughter was a Head Start child, and I know intimately that federally supported childcare and healthcare is a lifeline for many families. It allows children to learn safely and be healthy while their parents attend school or work in our local businesses,” said Congresswoman Simon. “Whip Clark and I are taking everything we heard from our visit back to D.C., where we are hell bent on fighting this Administration and reversing their harmful policies so our Head Starts, our community health centers, our care workers, our families have everything they need to continue growing and being brilliant.”

"Congresswoman Lateefah Simon is an unrivaled champion for working families," said Democratic Whip Katherine Clark. "It was a privilege to join her in Oakland to see firsthand what communities need from the federal government: investments in healthcare, childcare, and the wellbeing of regular people, not giveaways to the ultra-rich. While the Republican Party continues to bend its knee to the billionaire class, Democrats are ready to take back the People's House and get to work for the working class.”

“We are honored to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark to Fruitvale and share firsthand the impact of The Unity Council’s work,” said CEO of The Unity Council, Chris Iglesias. “From giving our youngest learners, a strong foundation at our De Colores Head Start, to bringing La Catrina de Oakland to Fruitvale as a powerful celebration of culture and community, our work is rooted in creating opportunities and strengthening families. Their visit underscores the importance of continued investment in the people, programs, and places that allow communities like Fruitvale to thrive."

“At our De Colores Head Start Center, we see every day how a strong start can shape not only a child’s future, but an entire families’,” said Chief Early Learning Officer of The Unity Council, Luis Arenas. “Head Start creates opportunities for children to learn and grow while giving parents the support and resources they need to move their families forward. We were proud to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark into our classrooms and share the real, lasting impact this work has on families throughout our community.”

“We are deeply grateful to Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for visiting La Clínica and for their tireless advocacy on behalf of the communities we serve. Their visit shows what federal investment looks like on the ground, and highlights what is at risk when coverage and resources for community health centers are reduced,” said La Clínica CEO, Jane García. “What’s at stake is whether parents can get their children to the doctor, whether patients can access dental and behavioral health care along with primary care, whether families can afford their medications, and whether community health centers have the resources to keep the staff who provide this care. La Clínica thanks Whip Clark and Congresswoman Simon for listening to our patients and staff and for bringing their voices back to Washington. The decisions made there have very real impacts here in the Bay Area.”

title: Rep. Steube Backs Punta Gorda’s Trabue Park Redevelopment Grant Application
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) sent a letter to the National Park Service supporting the City of Punta Gorda’s Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership Program application to redevelop Trabue Park.

“Punta Gorda has worked hard to rebuild and strengthen its community following Hurricane Milton, and this project would give residents more opportunities to enjoy one of the city’s greatest assets: its waterfront,” said Rep.
