title: Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on USS Lincoln’s Return
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Ranking Member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Oversight Subcommittee, issued the following statement on USS Abraham Lincoln’s return home after the end of a record long deployment.

“I am thankful for the return of the servicemembers aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. They and their families have paid an unnecessary cost for Trump’s endless war of choice with Iran. They deserve all of our respect and support. During the USS Lincoln’s deployment, servicemembers endured a record number of days without a port call. They faced insufficient amounts of food, unfit living conditions, and inadequate mental health support. I will continue to advocate for the respect and safety of our troops. We have a duty to make sure this never happens again by holding the Pentagon accountable, ” said Ranking Member Subramanyam.

In August of this year, Oversight Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Congressman Suhas Subramanyam demanded answers from the Department of Defense (DOD) about conditions on the USS Lincoln. In the letter to DOD Secretary Hegseth, the Ranking Members asked for information on the inventory of food, medical supplies, and other critical resources for the sailors and Marines. They also asked for clarification on the timeline of when the USS Lincoln would be relieved by another aircraft carrier.

The letter can be found HERE and below.

###

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write regarding the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, specifically, the living conditions and access to mental health resources for the sailors. Recent reports have revealed disturbing sanitation conditions, food shortages, and deteriorating mental health among those deployed on the aircraft carrier, including multiple suicide attempts, with one sailor jumping overboard. Our sailors deserve better while they serve our country, and these deplorable conditions negatively impact morale and readiness. As Members of Congress, we have a duty to support our troops, and it is clear that additional oversight is needed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

The USS Abraham Lincoln holds more than 5,000 sailors and Marines and departed San Diego last November. Now redirected to the Middle East to support the Iran War in Operation Epic Fury, the carrier has been deployed for over 250 days and has spent a record-setting 200 consecutive days at sea. At a town hall with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, families of those aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln voiced their concerns directly. Among them were food shortages, water contamination, and disruptions in mail.

As the Ranking Members of the Oversight Committee and the Oversight Committee’s Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, we request a classified briefing on the USS Abraham Lincoln’s conditions and answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:

What is the current inventory of food aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln?

Please detail the food supply and delivery schedule over the course of the carrier’s deployment.

What sanitation issues have been identified aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, including broken bathroom facilities?

What health care, including mental health care, are available to the sailors aboard?

What behavioral health care professionals are on board and accessible to those seeking help?

How quickly can someone on board the ship meet with a behavioral health care professional after seeking help?

What steps can be taken to mitigate the disruptions to the mail system that sailors have experienced?

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao reportedly told family members that the USS Theodore Roosevelt is preparing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Without jeopardizing national security, what details can be shared about the timeline for the ship’s relief?

The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X. If you have any questions about this request, please contact Committee Democratic staff at (202) 225-5051. Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.

title: Rep. Summer Lee Receives Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services
text:
Photos/Video (Dropbox)

PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 8, 2026 — Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) received the Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services (RHLS), joining housing advocates, nonprofit developers, legal aid leaders, and community partners from across Pennsylvania at the organization’s annual awards reception in Downtown Pittsburgh.

Rep. Lee was recognized for her work advancing affordable housing and tenant protections in Congress and delivering federal investments for housing across Western Pennsylvania.

“I am proud to receive this award, but this one belongs to the tenants fighting to stay in their homes, the families trying to keep a roof over their heads, the organizers, lawyers, advocates, and nonprofit developers doing the hard work to keep our communities whole,” said Rep. Lee. “In Congress, I have been focused on putting federal dollars and federal protections behind that work, from bringing millions home for affordable housing to fighting for legal representation for tenants facing eviction and taking on Wall Street investors buying up our homes for profit. Nobody should have to watch their neighborhood finally get investment just in time to be priced out of it. We are going to keep fighting until staying in the community you helped build is something every single family can count on.”

Rep. Lee has brought millions of federal dollars home for affordable housing and community development, including $3 million for affordable housing projects across Allegheny County and $1 million to help convert underused office buildings in Downtown Pittsburgh into housing through her Community Project Funding initiatives.

Rep. Lee also helped advance the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a sweeping housing package that passed Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support and included provisions to limit additional single-family home purchases by large institutional investors, support home repairs and housing preservation, improve small-dollar mortgage access, and strengthen protections for homeowners challenging inaccurate appraisals. When President Trump initially withheld his signature from the bill, Rep. Lee publicly pushed for the housing relief to move forward without delay.

Her work in Congress has also focused on keeping families in their homes and preventing displacement. Rep. Lee introduced the Eviction Right to Counsel Act, which would help guarantee legal representation for low-income tenants facing eviction, and has fought to preserve affordable housing in historically underserved communities.

Rep. Lee also helped reintroduce the Stop Wall Street Landlords Act, legislation aimed at ending federal tax advantages that help large institutional investors buy up single-family homes and compete with working families.

During the event, Rep. Lee was honored alongside Pennsylvania Senate Minority Leader Jay Costa, Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato, State Rep. Lindsay Powell, and State Rep. Brandon Markosek.

title: Suozzi Convenes Long Island Robotics Roundtable
text:
Glen Cove, NY—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today convened business, technology, and workforce development leaders for a roundtable discussion on how to position Long Island to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing. The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in conjunction with CEO Evan Beard, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in the United States.

“Standard Bots is a great example of why Long Island has the talent, the universities, the skilled workforce, and the entrepreneurial spirit to be the nation’s leader in robotics and advanced manufacturing. We need to bring all those pieces together and make sure we are competing for the businesses and jobs of the future,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Robotics and advanced manufacturing are going to play an increasingly important role in our economy, not only because of their effectiveness but because the industry creates high-skilled, high-tech jobs that have good wages for the people of Long Island.”

The roundtable brought together leaders from the robotics, manufacturing, financial, and economic development sectors to discuss the rapid growth of the domestic and international robotics industry, the role of robotics in strengthening American manufacturing, the future of robotics and physical AI on Long Island, and the opportunities for Long Island to attract robotics companies, develop a skilled local workforce, and improve its existing strengths in technology, manufacturing, engineering, and research. Participants also explored federal initiatives that could promote robotics, including tariffs, grant opportunities, research and development supports, expansion of workforce development initiatives, tax credits, safety standards for newer AI-powered robots, and more.

The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in Glen Cove, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in America. Suozzi opened the event and moderated a discussion featuring Evan Beard, Co-Founder, CEO and Chief Engineer of Standard Bots; Robert Kufner, President and CEO of Designatronics; Tommy McNulty, Head of Platform Sales at Erebor Bank; Cara Longworth, VP, Long Island Regional Director of Empire State Development; and Amy Erickson, Executive Director of Long Island Manufacturing Extension Partnership.

Beard delivered the keynote address on the state of the domestic and international robotics industry and the opportunities ahead for Long Island and the United States.

“The next era of manufacturing will be won by the countries that build their own robots, and we believe America should lead it. That's why we design and build our robots right here in Glen Cove, with some of the most talented engineers, machinists, and builders anywhere in the world. Long Island has a proud manufacturing legacy, and we're grateful to Congressman Suozzi for bringing industry, government, and investors together to make this region a home for American robotics,” said Evan Beard, CEO & Co-founder, Standard Bots.

“Robotics is the fastest growing market in the world. It will fundamentally change how work gets done in your home and in nearly all business segments. Unfortunately, much of the global supply of robots has come from outside the U.S., but the through the good work of Rep. Suozzi and leaders across industries on Long Island that have the capability to build robots, it has been recognized that future supply can and must be made domestically with American made products. Long Island’s proximity to New York City where hundreds of robotics startups are being nurtured gives it a distinct advantage to support their growth as well as the thousands of other robotics companies across the country that are getting ready to scale. Long Island has a long history in advanced manufacturing and already has all the components to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing with the right amount of coordination,” said Robert Kufner, President and CEO, Designatronics.

title: Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09), joined by 21 Members of Congress, demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.

Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.

“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”

The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.

“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”

The letter, led by Reps. Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

The letter was also endorsed by 38 organizations: American Friends Service Committee, Americans for Justice in Palestine Action, Arab American Caucus of the California Democratic Party, Arlington for Palestine, Asian Americans Advancing Justice – Atlanta, CAIR Action, Center for Constitutional Rights, Codepink, Community Alliance for Peace and Justice, Demand Progress, Havertown-Community Action Network, IMEU Policy Project, Indiana Center for Middle East Peace, Institute for Policy Studies New Internationalism Project, Maine Coalition for Palestine, Majdal: Arab Community Center of San Diego, MARUF CT, Massachusetts Peace Action, Methodist Federation for Social Action, Muslim Advocates, National Political Prisoner Coalition, NE Oakland Indivisible, NH Peace Action, Palestine Legal, Peace Action Montgomery, Peace Justice Sustainability NOW!, Philly Neighborhood Networks, Pittsburgh Palestine Solidarity Committee, Project TAHA, Restore The Fourth – Action, ReThinking Foreign Policy, River Valley for Palestine, The Justice Coalition, United Methodists for Kairos Response, US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Virginia for Palestine, Whistleblower & Source Protection Program at ExposeFacts, Worcester Multifaith for Palestine.

title: Rep. Torres Introduces the Improving Access to WIC Act to Ease Access to Nutrition Support for Moms and Children
text:
With More Than 4 in 10 WIC-eligible families Not Enrolled, Legislation Closes Gap by Helping States Strengthen Partnerships with Healthcare Providers, Lower Barriers to Participation, and Boost Outreach Efforts

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) introduced the Improving Access to WIC Act, legislation to make it easier to enroll in and stay connected to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). As families struggle with the ongoing affordability crisis, WIC helps feed mothers from the moment they find out they are pregnant to when their children are five years old. WIC not only helps moms access free, healthy foods, but also helps with breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health resources.

Nearly 25,000 mothers, infants, and children benefit from WIC in California’s 35th Congressional District. Nationwide, in fiscal year 2025, WIC served 6.9 million participants every month. The program is proven to save lives and improve lifetime health outcomes. Despite this, the most recent data show that more than 4 in 10 eligible individuals do not participate in WIC, and WIC utilization is lower for pregnant mothers and 1- to 4-year-olds. This legislation will tackle this participation gap.

The Improving Access to WIC Act would establish a federal grant program for states, tribes, and territories to improve access to, participation in, and retention in WIC. States that opt into the program would receive flexible funding to help strengthen partnerships between WIC agencies and healthcare providers, modernize the enrollment experience, improve community outreach, and help enroll mothers and children on SNAP and Medicaid who already qualify for WIC but do not yet participate.

“WIC provides critical nutrition assistance to moms, babies, and young children, and getting enrolled should not mean jumping through unnecessary hoops,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Moms are already juggling doctor’s appointments, work, child care, and countless responsibilities. We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible families to access the support they need. My Improving Access to WIC Act will help states integrate WIC enrollment with healthcare providers, reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork, and make it easier for families to enroll and stay on WIC.”

“Despite the incredible public health benefits of WIC, we are still reaching only a little more than half of eligible families. Investing in targeted outreach, data sharing, and healthcare linkages will make it easier for families who qualify to connect with WIC. We thank Rep. Torres for her leadership and support for WIC.” Georgia Machell, President & CEO, National WIC Association

“WIC is an evidence-based, time-limited program with proven positive outcomes for families and communities, yet there is a significant portion of eligible families not connected to services. Supporting innovative outreach methods and healthcare linkages to improve access to the program is an important investment. We appreciate Rep. Torres’s support for WIC and young families.” Megan Esparza, Executive Director, California WIC Association

“The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) is one of the most critical tools pediatricians have to ensure infants and young children can receive proper nutrition support in their earliest years. The Improving Access to WIC Act would provide states with resources to make enrolling eligible families in WIC easier, more efficient, and more effective. The American Academy of Pediatrics thanks Representative Torres for introducing this important legislation and calls on Congress to advance it,” said Andrew D. Racine, MD, PhD, FAAP, President of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

“The American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists has a long history of supporting the WIC program and is proud to endorse the Improving Access to WIC Act,” said ACOG President Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE. “Families are facing growing financial pressure, and putting healthy food on the table can be especially difficult during pregnancy and after a baby is born. With significant changes to SNAP under H.R. 1, making WIC easier to access is more important than ever. This bill would help eligible families get the nutrition support they need instead of getting stuck in red tape. ACOG thanks Rep. Norma Torres for her leadership and commitment to strengthening the WIC program.”

"WIC is a proven intervention that supports the health of women, babies, and young children. Yet far too many eligible families are missing out on the many benefits of the program. We applaud Rep. Torres for introducing the Improving Access to WIC Act. Establishing a federal grant program to help states improve access to and participation in WIC would make it easier for eligible families to connect with this critical support. We urge Members of Congress to co-sponsor this legislation, so more families are connected to the nutrition they need to thrive." - Crystal FitzSimons, President of the Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).

The bill is supported by: National WIC Association (NWA), California WIC Association (CWA), American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), Food Research and Action Center (FRAC), Alliance to End Hunger, Coalition on Human Needs.

Bill Summary:

The Improving Access to WIC Act authorizes $50 million for Fiscal Years 2027 through 2031 for the grant program. States, tribes, and territories that choose to opt in would receive, to the maximum extent practicable, $200,000 and an additional amount based on each participating state’s national share of WIC participants.

The bill also requires the U.S. Department of Agriculture to publicly report on the program’s outcomes, including its impact on WIC participation and retention, and share best practices that states can use to improve enrollment and access.

Under the legislation, participating states could use grant funding to:

Connect more eligible families with WIC by:

Improving outreach in clinical settings and building up systems to make it easier for doctors and health care providers to directly refer patients to WIC, including through statewide referral systems, and

Expanding outreach in trusted community settings, including at Head Start and Early Head Start programs, preschools, schools, and other places to meet WIC-eligible families where they are.

Improve secure data sharing between health care providers and WIC agencies to streamline WIC referrals and certification, while protecting privacy, requiring individual consent, and maintaining federal confidentiality protections.

Reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork by making it easier for health care providers, consistent with applicable laws and with individuals’ consent, to securely provide WIC agencies with information such as height, weight, hemoglobin measurements (blood tests), and other documentation needed for WIC certification.

Modernize the enrollment process, including by establishing or expanding online WIC applications.

Help reach and enroll moms and children on Medicaid (Medi-Cal) or SNAP (CalFresh) who already qualify for WIC, but are not participating.

title: Reps. Carter, Thompson Reintroduce the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act to Address the Evolving Challenges Posed by AI
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA), Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, and Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee, re-introduced the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Task Force Act.

This legislation will establish a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) dedicated to addressing safety and national security challenges posed by AI. The task force and reporting requirements will ensure effective DHS coordination as AI threats and challenges evolve. Recently, Rep. Carter appeared on CNBC to discuss how to regulate AI while preserving innovation.

“As technology advances in sophistication and use, our commitment to safeguarding against emerging threats and ensuring the responsible advancement of AI technologies must grow stronger too,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m introducing the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing AI Task Force Act to take an essential step towards managing the impact of AI on our cybersecurity landscape.”

“Advancements in AI technology are expanding by the day and we need to make sure our cybersecurity defenses are moving with it,” said Ranking Member Thompson. “This bill creates a dedicated CISA task force so the agency can better understand the risks that come with AI and make sure we are prepared to protect the systems and infrastructure Americans rely on every day. I am proud to work alongside Representative Carter to reintroduce this critical legislation and help ensure our defenses are ready for what comes next.”

Background

The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act would:

Establish a Task Force - Within one year of enactment, the Director of CISA will establish a Task Force comprised of personnel from various offices and divisions to coordinate AI-related directives and activities.

Address AI Challenges - The Task Force will ensure coordination of efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI. It will assess relevant safety and security initiatives, advise stakeholders on potential cyber risks associated with AI deployment, and identify workforce gaps.

Increase Accountability - The Task Force will provide biannual briefings to the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate on its activities.

title: Valadao, Bipartisan Colleagues Reintroduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
text:
WASHINGTON – This week, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) joined Reps. Jim Costa (CA-21), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), John Larson (CT-01), Gus Bilirakis (FL-12), and Paul Tonko (NY-20) to reintroduce a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. Today highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth right here in the Central Valley and across the nation.

"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day,” said Congressman Valadao. “Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive.”

"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."

"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.

"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."

"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," said Congressman Tonko. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."

"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."

Read the resolution here.

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Statement on EPA Promoting Methane Emissions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 8, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) issued the following statement after the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced the rollback of key regulations restricting harmful methane gas emissions:

"Energy production drives our state's economy and provides good-paying jobs, and we can continue to do it while strengthening, not weakening, protections for clean air for the workers and families who work in and near the industry,” said Vasquez. “Excess methane emissions are known to cause respiratory disease and other ailments, and many producers in the Permian Basin have implemented new technology to prevent leaks and capture more methane, and that work must continue. This harmful rollback is the wrong choice for the health of our workers, communities, and companies that have responsibly worked toward reducing excess emissions."

The 2023 methane rule established stronger nationwide standards to reduce methane pollution from oil and gas operations, including requirements for companies to regularly monitor equipment for leaks, quickly repair breaks, limit routine flaring, and reduce emissions from wells, storage tanks, compressors, and other equipment. The rule also required states to develop plans to reduce methane emissions from existing oil and gas facilities. The Administration’s rollback would weaken these protections, reducing requirements on oil and gas producers to detect and address methane pollution and potentially allowing more wasted natural gas and harmful emissions into New Mexico communities.

title: Rep. Vasquez Leads Effort with State and Local Officials to Push for Federal Coordination in Response to Recent Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 8, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) led a delegation of federal, state, and local leaders in a letter to federal agencies urging them to tour the damage and provide all available resources to those affected by the recent flooding across southern New Mexico.

The letter asks the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC) to visit affected communities, work with local leaders, and provide assistance to homes, communities, farms and businesses impacted by the flooding.

“It is imperative that your agencies act now to cut red tape, reduce bureaucratic barriers, increase communication and responsiveness, and act as a partner in this recovery,” wrote Vasquez. “Due to the nature of this area, the complex patchwork of federal land, critical agricultural areas, and proximity to the border, this response will require your agencies to work hand-in-hand with state, county, and local leaders on both short-term recovery and long-term mitigation efforts.”

The letter is joined by State Senator Jeff Steinborn, State Representative Nathan P. Small, Hatch Mayor Dennis Torres, and Caballo Soil and Water Conservation District Chairman Harvey Morrow.

On October 4th, Rep. Vasquez hosted a meeting in Doña Ana County with local elected officials and visited families and farms impacted by the recent flooding. He visited Hatch, the McLeod/Garfield Dam, and surrounding areas to assess the impact of the flooding and what the community needed for recovery firsthand. During this visit, Rep. Vasquez also discussed Hatch’s immediate recovery needs, available state and federal resources, and opportunities for continued coordination to support the community’s recovery and infrastructure needs.

title: Blackburn Leads Tennessee Delegation in Urging Army to Make Tennessee National Guard First in Nation to Field MV-75 Aircraft
text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.), U.S. Senator Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), and the entire Tennessee delegation sent a letter to Acting United States Secretary of the Army Adam Telle urging him to make the Tennessee Army National Guard the first in the nation to field the MV-75 Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft. The MV-75 Cheyenne II represents the next generation of Army assault aviation, providing increased speed, range, operational reach, and flexibility for distributed operations and large-scale, long-range air assault.

Proximity to 101st Airborne Division Would Help Power MV-75 Dominance

Tennessee is uniquely positioned to partner with the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) at Fort Campbell, the Army’s first operational formation designated to field the MV-75. Tennessee’s 1-230th Assault Helicopter Battalion is a proven assault aviation unit supported by experienced aviators, crew members, maintainers, and flight operations personnel. 1-230th regularly integrates with the 101st providing a tested foundation for accelerated MV-75 integration. With the geographic proximity of these two formations, recurring cross-training and shared access to the Army’s emerging MV-75 instructors, simulation capabilities, training areas, maintenance expertise, tactics development, and operational lessons learned would be maximized. The proximity would also reduce travel and temporary-duty expenses, minimize lost training time, and allow limited National Guard training resources to be applied directly to readiness.

Tennessee Is Investing in Aviation Infrastructure Designed to Support MV-75

Further, Tennessee is currently investing in aviation infrastructure designed and capable of supporting MV-75 requirements and has a newly opened National Guard Readiness Center located on Fort Campbell. Synchronizing these National Guard investments with the Active Component would support shared training, sustainment, maintenance, and simulation while avoiding unnecessary infrastructure and resource duplication. We believe that selecting Tennessee would establish an integrated COMPO 1 - COMPO 2 MV-75 ecosystem, with the partnership reducing transition risk and reducing transition cost, while accelerating operational cross talk and program feedback. We respectfully request that the Department of the Army and National Guard Bureau give Tennessee full consideration as the first Army National Guard organization to field the MV-75. Should you have any questions or require additional information, please do not hesitate to contact our staff.

CO-SIGNERS

U.S. Senator Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), and U.S. Representatives Chuck Fleischmann (R-Tenn.), Matt Van Epps (R-Tenn.), Diana Harshbarger (R-Tenn.), Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.), John Rose (R-Tenn.), Scott DesJarlais (R-Tenn.), Andy Ogles (R-Tenn.), David Kustoff (R-Tenn.), and Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.) joined Senator Blackburn in sending this letter.

title: Blumenthal & Warren Call on FTC to Crack Down on Deceptive Security Deposit Schemes Hurting Tenants
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) wrote to Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chair Andrew Ferguson calling on the FTC to investigate the emerging consumer protection issues posed by security deposit alternatives.

According to recent reporting by the New York Times, landlords and management companies are increasingly offering tenants security deposit alternatives, in which tenants are allowed to pay smaller monthly or annual fees that replace the traditional lump sum of a security deposit before moving in. While these alternatives seem helpful to consumers, they expose tenants to significant financial risks—tenants are still financially responsible for any damages that occur, and unlike a typical security deposit, the alternative payments are generally non-refundable. In their letter, Blumenthal and Warren call on the FTC to investigate and take action against these deceptive fee practices.

“The misleading marketing and lack of transparency surrounding these products can lead tenants to believe they function like traditional security deposits, but at a lower cost… However, in a report analyzing security deposit alternatives, the National Consumer Law Center (NCLC) found that these products typically cost more than traditional security deposits over the course of a lease, may lack the protections afforded by state security deposit laws, and often fail to clearly disclose the fees tenants will be required to pay,” wrote the Senators.

“From non-refundable fees and misleading marketing to inadequate disclosures, these products can take advantage of vulnerable tenants who are already struggling to afford the high cost of rental housing,” continued the Senators.

Blumenthal and Warren are calling on the FTC to take action to protect tenants from these deceptive and misleading security deposit alternatives, writing, “As security deposit alternatives are becoming increasingly common, the FTC should take action to investigate, provide consumer notice, and combat misleading tactics with respect to security deposit alternatives. In particular, the Commission should issue rules requiring disclosures regarding the full costs and fees, reimbursement obligations, and non-refundable nature of these products, while also prohibiting misleading marketing practices that misrepresent how these products compare to traditional security deposits. These measures would help protect consumers, improve transparency, and ensure tenants understand the true costs and obligations associated with security deposit alternatives.”

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Chair Ferguson,

As housing costs continue to rise and millions of Americans struggle to pay rent each month, we call on the Federal Trade Commission (the Commission) to investigate and take action to address the emerging issue of security deposit alternatives.1 These products often expose consumers to significant financial risks through misleading marketing, inadequate disclosures, and non-refundable fee structures.2 Given the Commission's ongoing Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on unfair and deceptive fee practices in connection with rental housing, we urge the Commission to ensure that its rulemaking also addresses the consumer protection issues posed by security deposit alternatives.3

While Americans renting houses or apartments have grown accustomed to traditional security deposits to cover damage or other costs, landlords are increasingly offering these security deposit alternatives.4 These alternatives are often provided by third parties and allow a tenant to pay monthly or recurring fees, instead of paying a traditional deposit before moving in. Although these products may seem enticing to tenants at first, they differ significantly from traditional security deposits: they are typically not subject to state laws governing security deposits, the fees are generally nonrefundable, and tenants remain responsible for reimbursing the provider or landlord for covered damages.5 As a result, tenants may pay recurring fees throughout their lease, receive no refund at move-out, and still be liable for damages.6

The misleading marketing and lack of transparency surrounding these products can lead tenants to believe they function like traditional security deposits, but at a lower cost. For example, Rhino, the largest provider in this sector, claims its product “covers your rental just like a cash deposit would” on its website, while Homebody, another major provider, asserts that renters can “save hundreds” and that its product “is an alternative to a security deposit that still provides similar protection” in its advertising materials.7 However, in a report analyzing security deposit alternatives, the National Consumer Law Center (NCLC) found that these products typically cost more than traditional security deposits over the course of a lease, may lack the protections afforded by state security deposit laws, and often fail to clearly disclose the fees tenants will be required to pay.8

Recent reporting by The New York Times and the NCLC highlights the real-world impacts of the misleading marketing and inadequate disclosures for tenants who use security deposit alternatives. As reported in the NCLC report, a tenant explained “I paid 4 years of premiums totaling $600 . . . I was scammed out of $600 over 4 years only to still have to pay everything a deposit would have covered.”9 Another renter cited in the NCLC report described being required to pay a monthly fee to a security deposit alternative provider, only to learn that after two years and over $400 in payments, none of the money would be returned at move-out or applied toward the landlord's full charge for damages.10 From non-refundable fees and misleading marketing to inadequate disclosures, these products can take advantage of vulnerable tenants who are already struggling to afford the high cost of rental housing.

As security deposit alternatives are becoming increasingly common, the FTC should take action to investigate, provide consumer notice, and combat misleading tactics with respect to security deposit alternatives. We support the Commission's ongoing ANPRM on junk fee practices in connection with rental housing, and urge the Commission to extend its rulemaking scope to cover the consumer protection concerns associated with security deposit alternatives.11 In particular, the Commission should issue rules requiring disclosures regarding the full costs and fees, reimbursement obligations, and non-refundable nature of these products, while also prohibiting misleading marketing practices that misrepresent how these products compare to traditional security deposits. These measures would help protect consumers, improve transparency, and ensure tenants understand the true costs and obligations associated with security deposit alternatives.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: Blumenthal Demands Answers from Cantor Fitzgerald About Relationship with Tether After PSI Report Finds Cryptocurrency Firm Props Up Iran’s Shadow Banking System
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), today demanded answers from Cantor Fitzgerald Chairman Brandon Lutnick about the firm’s lucrative relationship with the cryptocurrency issuer Tether.

As PSI Ranking Member, Blumenthal is leading an inquiry into the illicit use of cryptocurrencies and the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms. As part of this investigation, Blumenthal recently released a report detailing how Tether and its dollar-pegged stablecoin have become a significant financial lifeline within Iran’s shadow banking network. In a letter sent today to Brandon Lutnick, Blumenthal sought information about Cantor Fitzgerald’s practices for detecting violations of banking and sanctions laws in light of PSI’s findings. Brandon Lutnick is the son of Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, who was Chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald until his confirmation as Commerce Secretary in February 2025, at which time he handed control of the company to his adult children.

“President Trump has made over $2 billion since his return to office, with most of this sum coming from his family’s crypto ventures. Similarly, Cantor Fitzgerald’s former Chairman and current Secretary of the Department of Commerce, Howard Lutnick, has made over $250 million in that same time period, including a $192 million distribution from Cantor Fitzgerald,” Blumenthal wrote.

Blumenthal continued, “Cantor Fitzgerald has benefited alongside Lutnick in the last two years, in large part due to its partnership with Tether. Since the President’s return to office, Cantor Fitzgerald’s five percent stake in Tether has increased in value from $600 million to an estimated $10 billion, in addition to the tens of millions of dollars the company collects every year from the assets it holds for Tether.”

Blumenthal continued, “Just as Tether has made untold millions in interest and investments from the stablecoins used in these illicit activities, so has Cantor Fitzgerald profited from its relationship with Tether. Given the longstanding and deeply intertwined relationship between Tether and Cantor Fitzgerald, and its substantial relationships within the Trump Administration, I am writing to request information about your business partnership with Tether and to learn about your practices for detecting violations of American banking and sanctions laws.”

“While Tether claims to operate out of El Salvador, the vast majority of its assets reside in the United States under your custodianship. As Congress considers how to best regulate digital assets, your partnership with Tether will provide important insights into the inner workings of this industry,” Blumenthal concluded.

The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Lutnick is available here and below. PSI’s report, “Tethered to Terrorism: Crypto & Iran’s Shadow Banking Network,” is available here.

Brandon Lutnick

Chairman

Cantor Fitzgerald LP

110 East 59th St

New York, NY 10022

Dear Mr. Lutnick:

The Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (“PSI” or the “Subcommittee”) Minority is investigating the illicit use of cryptocurrencies and the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms. President Trump has made over $2 billion since his return to office, with most of this sum coming from his family’s crypto ventures.[1] Similarly, Cantor Fitzgerald’s former Chairman and current Secretary of the Department of Commerce, Howard Lutnick, has made over $250 million in that same time period, including a $192 million distribution from Cantor Fitzgerald.[2] Cantor Fitzgerald has benefited alongside Lutnick in the last two years, in large part due to its partnership with Tether. Since the President’s return to office, Cantor Fitzgerald’s five percent stake in Tether has increased in value from $600 million to an estimated $10 billion, in addition to the tens of millions of dollars the company collects every year from the assets it holds for Tether.[3]

Disturbingly, Cantor Fitzgerald’s lucrative business arrangements with Tether come at the expense of America’s national security. On September 28, the Subcommittee released a new report, “Tethered to Terrorism: Crypto & Iran’s Shadow Banking Network,” which demonstrated that Tether and its dollar-pegged stablecoin USDT have become a crucial tool for Iranian shadow banking.[4] The Subcommittee analyzed a comprehensive set of cryptocurrency wallets that have been targeted for their association with Iran and its terrorist proxies. This analysis shows how these actors have transitioned to predominantly relying on Tether. Furthermore, the Subcommittee found that Tether had failed to freeze or destroy funds in wallets that were clearly providing or receiving millions of dollars—even tens or hundreds of millions—from terrorist financiers and other illicit actors. The Subcommittee’s report reinforces longstanding research and media investigations regarding Tether’s broader role in illicit finance, human trafficking, scams, cartel violence, terrorism, and more.[5]

Just as Tether has made untold millions in interest and investments from the stablecoins used in these illicit activities, so has Cantor Fitzgerald profited from its relationship with Tether.[6] Given the longstanding and deeply intertwined relationship between Tether and Cantor Fitzgerald, and its substantial relationships within the Trump Administration, I am writing to request information about your business partnership with Tether and to learn about your practices for detecting violations of American banking and sanctions laws.[7] As the largest issuer of stablecoins in the world, Tether is a key player in the cryptocurrency industry.[8] While Tether claims to operate out of El Salvador, the vast majority of its assets reside in the United States under your custodianship. As Congress considers how to best regulate digital assets, your partnership with Tether will provide important insights into the inner workings of this industry.

To assist the Subcommittee in its inquiry, please preserve all documents, records,[9] and communications[10] related to Cantor Fitzgerald’s relationship with Tether, and please provide responses to the following document and information requests by October 23, 2026:[11]

When did Cantor Fitzgerald first enter into a business partnership with Tether, and what were the circumstances under which the firm began to do business with the stablecoin issuer?

Please provide the annual revenue Cantor Fitzgerald has received from its partnership with Tether since it began.

Please provide the annual amount the Lutnick Family has made from Cantor Fitzgerald’s partnership with Tether since it began.

Do you require regular audits of Tether and its operations from a credible independent auditor to verify the value of its assets?

What measures are in place to regularly monitor and assess Tether’s compliance with OFAC and other anti-money laundering regulations?

Please describe the circumstances under which Cantor Fitzgerald would terminate a business relationship and whether such a review has taken place for Tether.

Please describe services provided to Tether, investment positions held in Tether or on Tether’s behalf, decision-making or oversight roles relevant to the partnership, or any other pertinent details regarding the relationship between Cantor Fitzgerald and Tether.

Please describe Cantor Fitzgerald’s custodial relationship with Tether and provide any related records, including financial audits or other documentation related to your holdings on behalf of Tether.

Please provide all records relating to:

Cantor Fitzgerald’s ownership stake in Tether;

The terms under which Howard Lutnick relinquished his ownership stake in Cantor Fitzgerald; and

The terms of any loan or other provision extended to Howard Lutnick or the Lutnick Family by Tether that enabled him to transfer his ownership stake to his children.

Please describe all steps Cantor Fitzgerald has taken to investigate allegations that Tether’s stablecoin has been used in illicit finance and money laundering, including within Iran’s shadow banking network and for purposes of Russia sanctions evasion.

Please provide all policies and procedures relating to:

Know-Your-Customer (“KYC”) and other Anti-Money-Laundering (“AML) practices as they relate to business partners;

Ongoing due diligence of Cantor Fitzgerald’s business relationship with Tether; and

Cantor Fitzgerald’s procedures for de-risking business partners in foreign jurisdictions.

Please provide all records and communications sent by Howard Lutnick as an employee of Cantor Fitzgerald regarding Tether. This includes, but is not limited to, Tether’s compliance with AML regulations, any discussion of Tether with the White House or state and federal regulators, lobbying on Tether’s behalf, custodial activities on behalf of Tether, or compliance with any laws and regulations applicable to Tether.

Please provide all records and communications with or regarding Secretary Lutnick and his involvement with Tether since he relinquished his role as Chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald, including any communications involving fundraising for Tether or regulatory matters involving the firm.

Please provide all communications between Cantor Fitzgerald and Tether regarding Tether’s compliance with banking and sanctions laws, Tether’s financial backing for its tokens, any potential fundraising, or the Lutnick Family’s ownership interests in Tether.

Please provide all communications between Cantor Fitzgerald and any member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Digital Assets.

Please contact the Subcommittee if you have any questions about responding to these requests.

Sincerely,

title: Blumenthal, Welch, & Schiff Continue to Probe into DHS Misuse of Taxpayer Dollars, Demand Answers from Mullin over Luxury Jet Purchases
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), Peter Welch (D-VT), and Adam Schiff (D-CA) today sought records and information from Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin about the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) squandering of taxpayer funds and repeated steering of no-bid contracts to political allies. In a letter sent today to Mullin, the Senators urged the Department to ensure accountability for corrupt contracting decisions and ensure open competition among future prospective contractors.

The Senators pointed to allegations recently reported in The New York Times that in the final hours of former Secretary Kristi Noem’s tenure, DHS “delivered a windfall to one of her political donors by buying five airplanes from the man’s firm at a substantial markup.”

The Senators wrote, “On the last day of Secretary Noem’s tenure, DHS purchased one Boeing 737 jet from Daedalus for $108 million, despite that aircraft previously appearing on the market with an asking price below $90 million. The interior of that aircraft included ‘a stand-up bar, two bedrooms, marble showers and a table covered in manta ray skin.’ Another two 737 aircraft were purchased by DHS from Daedalus for $45 million each, prices that experts estimated ‘were millions of dollars higher than the typical market value for jets of that age.’”

The Senators continued, “The staggering sums expended on these aircraft and the eleventh-hour approval of the no-bid contract used to purchase them from a company led by a political donor to Secretary Noem appears to illustrate a brazen giveaway by Secretary Noem to her political ally, William Walters. The fact that a separate company led by Mr. Walters, Salus Worldwide Solutions, has received separate no-bid contracts under Secretary Noem’s leadership only amplifies the appearance of impropriety and potential violations of federal law.”

“Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential corruption involved in the Department’s aircraft purchases and widespread no-bid contracting,” the Senators concluded.

Blumenthal, Welch, and Schiff previously wrote to Mullin seeking information about DHS’s wasteful purchase of 10 airplanes for $464 million via a no-bid contract and raising concerns that the owner of the company that received the award is connected to allegations of kickback payment schemes involving former DHS official Corey Lewandowski.

The full text of today’s letter to Mullin is available here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin:

We write for the fourth time since you took office as Secretary to demand prompt answers and full transparency into the most recent allegations that senior Department of Homeland Security (“DHS” or “the Department”) personnel steered lucrative no-bid aircraft purchase contracts that enriched a political ally. The mounting evidence of alleged contracting improprieties within the highest ranks of the Department constitutes an urgent crisis that risks squandering taxpayer funds and entrenching the wasteful and secretive process of awarding DHS contracts without the full and open competition required by federal procurement laws and regulations. We urge you to take decisive action to ensure accountability for any uncovered misconduct and ensure open competition among future DHS contractors. This includes promptly providing answers and producing records responsive to the following requests.

On October 4, 2026, public reporting revealed that in the final hours of former Secretary Kristi Noem’s tenure, DHS “delivered a windfall to one of her political donors by buying five airplanes from the man’s firm at a substantial markup.”[1] Previous reporting uncovered that the Department under Secretary Noem purchased 10 aircraft for $464 million via a no-bid contract in the fall of 2025 and that many of these planes sat idle despite claims by the Department that they were purchased to remove non-citizens from the United States.[2] The October 4 reporting alleges that DHS significantly overpaid for five of these aircraft in a contract modification made in the closing hours of Secretary Noem’s tenure, securing a potential profit of tens of millions of dollars for the seller, Daedalus Aviation Corporation (“Daedalus”).[3] The Chairman of Daedalus is Mr. William Walters; in 2024, he contributed $10,000 to Ms. Noem’s American Resolve political action committee.[4]

On the last day of Secretary Noem’s tenure, DHS purchased one Boeing 737 jet from Daedalus for $108 million, despite that aircraft previously appearing on the market with an asking price below $90 million.[5] The interior of that aircraft included “a stand-up bar, two bedrooms, marble showers and a table covered in manta ray skin.”[6] Another two 737 aircraft were purchased by DHS from Daedalus for $45 million each, prices that experts estimated “were millions of dollars higher than the typical market value for jets of that age.”[7] Similarly, on the same day, DHS purchased two 10-year-old Gulfstream jets from Daedalus for $53 million each, a markup of more than $11 million each.[8] The unusually high prices paid by DHS for aircraft purchased from Daedalus prompted one analyst to conclude that “[t]his does not resemble any aspect of an airline marketplace.”[9]

The staggering sums expended on these aircraft and the eleventh-hour approval of the no-bid contract used to purchase them from a company led by a political donor to Secretary Noem appears to illustrate a brazen giveaway by Secretary Noem to her political ally, William Walters. The fact that a separate company led by Mr. Walters, Salus Worldwide Solutions, received separate no-bid contracts under Secretary Noem’s leadership only amplifies the appearance of impropriety and potential violations of federal law.[10] Possibly recognizing the potential for misconduct and waste generated by these contracts, you reportedly “explored backing out of the deal” but “feared a significant financial penalty.”[11] After sharing that concern with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, she reportedly “told [you] that [you] should not seek to block the purchase.”[12] DHS went on to pay Daedalus “more than $2 million in both May and June” 2026 to store the purchased aircraft, and the Department now claims that “four of the 737 airliners will not be used for deportation flights, but rather will be used to fly government leaders and members of Congress on overseas trips.”[13] To date, DHS has not confirmed when, if ever, any of the aircraft will be used for the purpose for which they were purchased, to operate deportation flights.

Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential violations of federal law involved in the Department’s aircraft purchases and widespread no-bid contracting. Although DHS reportedly declined to disclose “documents laying out the agency’s rationale for awarding Daedalus its no-bid contract” because they would allegedly “compromise national security or create other security risks,” such a rationale is not a legitimate basis on which to withhold information and records from Congress.[14] Moreover, any ongoing audit or investigation by the DHS Inspector General into related matters is not a legitimate basis for withholding information and records from Congress.

Our offices are reviewing allegations of misconduct arising from federal contract awards to assess whether and the extent to which laws and regulations governing honest services and federal procurement may require legislative reform. In order for us to better understand the award of this contract, plans for these airplanes moving forward, and remedial measures for the American taxpayer, please provide the following information and records[15] by October 22, 2026:

Provide the contract(s) or any other operative agreement(s) governing each purchase of any aircraft by DHS from Daedalus.

Provide any addendum, appendix, schedule, or other modification or supplement to the records described in request 1.

Describe in detail the purchase price, maintenance costs, operation costs, storage costs, and current disposition of each aircraft purchased by DHS from Daedalus.

Provide all communications[16] among or between William Walters or any agent of Daedalus and former Secretary Noem, former Senior Advisor Corey Lewandowski, or any other current or former DHS personnel or agent responsible for the awarding or administration of Department contracts.

Please contact our offices if you have questions about responding to this request. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

U.S. Senators Katie Britt, James Lankford, Colleagues Urge Inspector General to Investigate Planned Parenthood
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) recently joined James Lankford (R-Okla.) and 128 members of Congress in sending a letter to the Inspector General (IG) of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) urging the IG to review and investigate the activities and federal funding streams of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc., and its affiliates.

“Serious concerns have long been raised regarding the organization’s compliance with applicable federal laws, regulations, and program requirements governing the receipt and use of federal funds,” the Republican lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers argue these concerns warrant a comprehensive review of Planned Parenthood’s use of federal funds and compliance with federal law.

“In particular, these concerns relate to whether Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and the organization’s affiliates have adhered to applicable requirements governing program integrity, financial accountability, and the proper use of funds provided through HHS-administered programs,” they continued.

The letter follows a recent Small Business Administration (SBA) investigation into whether Planned Parenthood affiliates improperly received approximately $88 million in loans through the Paycheck Protection Program during the COVID-19 pandemic. The lawmakers are also raising concerns about additional allegations involving fraud, false statements, potential violations of federal criminal law, and failures to disclose potential violations to the federal government.

The lawmakers are asking the HHS IG to review the federal funds Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have received and determine whether they were used in accordance with federal law. They also urged the IG to coordinate with other federal oversight agencies, including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), as needed.

You can read the full text of the letter here.

Senator Britt is a proud champion for protecting the unborn and supporting mothers and families. She recently celebrated the 50thanniversary of the Hyde Amendment, which prevents taxpayer funded abortion. She is a cosponsor of the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act and the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act. In 2024, Senator Britt joined her colleagues in a bicameral letter to the Government Accountability Office to investigate the federal funding awarded to abortion providers.

title: Cantwell Calls for Federal Assistance in Aftermath of Devastating Wildfires
text:
Cantwell Calls for Federal Assistance in Aftermath of Devastating Wildfires

ICYMI: Cantwell Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor Ferguson’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State

EDMONDS, WA – Today, U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and senior member of the Finance Committee, joined Washington state’s entire congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance.

The declaration would unlock federal dollars to help state, local, and tribal governments recover and repair damage from the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.

“We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” Sen. Cantwell and other members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”

“Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets,” the lawmakers continued. “Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”

“We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.

This was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and threatening lives, property, businesses, and livestock. Statewide, more than 900,000 acres burned, well above historical averages.

For the first time, on August 1, the National Weather Service upgraded a Red Flag Warning for fire weather conditions to a Particularly Dangerous Situation, which is very rare and typically reserved for extreme fire weather conditions. The Spokane Complex Fires – consisting of three major fires – forced 67,000 people to evacuate, destroyed or damaged more than 900 structures, and burned nearly 10,000 acres, with damages predicted to exceed $1 billion. In Okanogan County, the Kaiser Canyon, Modrite, and Sinlahekin fires burned over 350,000 acres total.

Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA) led the letter. Joining Sen. Cantwell as cosigners were U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Kim Schrier (D, WA-08), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).

A background document detailing Sen. Cantwell’s work to bolster wildfire preparedness is available HERE.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Mr. President:

As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible.

Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.

Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.

An initial damage assessment revealed that the state sustained an estimated $133.7 million in damages across eleven counties and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. In Spokane County, the Spokane Complex Fires, which burned nearly 10,000 acres, severely damaged electrical distribution systems, public water systems, transportation infrastructure, municipal equipment, public lands, and solid-waste infrastructure, resulting in over $70 million in damages.

These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe.

We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter.

title: Cantwell Celebrates Grand Opening of Vancouver’s Main Street Revitalization Project
text:
Cantwell Celebrates Grand Opening of Vancouver’s Main Street Revitalization Project

City of Vancouver used $12 million in American Rescue Plan Act funds to cover all project design costs and 41% of construction costs

VANCOUVER, WA – Yesterday, U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), senior member of the Senate Finance Committee and ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, joined Vancouver Mayor Anne McEnerny-Ogle, Vancouver Downtown Association Executive Director Michael Walker, and local business owners and community members to celebrate the grand opening of the Main Street Promise project.

“Every time ... I'm visiting this area, we are celebrating something, but that's okay with me,” said Sen. Cantwell. “It could be the STEM workforce, more affordable housing, the I-5 bridge. Each time, this community just grows stronger and stronger. So for more than 30 years ... Vancouver had a vision for Main Street, and what that vision today has become, is a reality -- a $26 million investment by both federal and local officials to improve Main Street and create a revitalization of this neighborhood for more celebration, more economic development, and most importantly, more community.”

The celebration marks the completion and grand finish of the multi-year Main Street Promise revitalization project, which broke ground in December 2024. The project upgraded traffic signals and ADA accessibility, widened sidewalks, added e-bike charging stations, expanded outdoor seating, added community gathering places, upgraded lighting, planted more than a hundred trees, and ultimately transformed the historic downtown corridor along Main Street from 5th Street to 15th Street.

The City of Vancouver secured $12 million in federal funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), which Sen. Cantwell supported, to help finance the $26.5 million infrastructure project. The ARPA funding went toward design and construction of street improvements and wastewater infrastructure that replaced 100-year-old utilities.

title: PHOTOS: Capito Makes Stops in Mineral and Hampshire Counties
text:
ROMNEY, W.Va. – Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) traveled to Mineral and Hampshire counties to make stops focused on recent Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) allocations she helped secure.

First, Senator Capito traveled to Ridgeley, W.Va. to visit the Ridgeley Volunteer Fire Department and receive an update on their recent CDS allocation. In March, she helped secure a $2,841,000 CDS allocation to construct a new fire station to replace their current 54-year-old facility. Through this allocation, the fire department will help ensure the protection of life and property in Ridgeley, Carpendale, and the surrounding communities. Senator Capito previously secured a $1.2M FY24 CDS allocation for Ridgeley’s town hall and police department.

“It was great to be in Ridgeley to receive updates from the Ridgeley Volunteer Fire Department,” Senator Capito said. “I was proud to help secure their CDS allocation that will help enhance public safety in the surrounding area. This investment reflects my continued commitment to equipping our community partners in the state with the resources they need to serve.”

“We sincerely thank Senator Shelley Moore Capito for securing the congressionally directed funding to help construct the new Ridgeley fire station. Her support represents a lasting investment in our volunteers and the safety of Ridgeley, Carpendale, and the surrounding communities. This funding brings us closer to a modern facility that will protect our equipment, support our operations, and allow us to serve our community for generations to come. We are grateful to Senator Capito for recognizing the importance of this project and helping us build a facility that would not have been possible without her support,” Steve Shipley, Assistant Fire Chief of the Ridgeley Volunteer Fire Department, said.

title: Senator Collins Helps Cut the Ribbon at North Windham Wastewater Treatment Facility
text:
Click HERE, HERE, HERE, HERE, and HERE for individual photos.

WINDHAM, ME – U.S. Senator Susan Collins delivered remarks and took part in a ribbon cutting ceremony today for the North Windham Wastewater Treatment Facility. The new facility will help improve water quality and support economic development and residential growth in the North Windham area.

“This great achievement is the result of the Town of Windham, the Portland Water District, and Windham Raymond Schools working with state and federal partners to address two issues that are crucial to this community and to our state – protecting the environment and providing opportunity. Maintaining and upgrading drinking water and wastewater infrastructure is vital to strengthening the economic and environmental health of communities throughout Maine. I am so impressed by the care and vision that Windham’s community leaders and involved citizens have put into this important project, and I am delighted to have been able to contribute to its success,” said Senator Collins.

In 2022, Senator Collins secured $2 million through her role on the Senate Appropriations Committee to support the installation of a new sewer and wastewater treatment system utilizing a Membrane Bio-Reactor. This state-of-the-art system will clean the water to a much higher standard than existing subsurface waste disposal systems. In the past five years, Senator Collins has secured more than $164 million for 83 water and wastewater projects.

Prior to this project, North Windham did not have public wastewater infrastructure, relying instead on individual septic systems. The new facility will provide the infrastructure needed to support future housing, businesses, and community growth in the area. The new system is also expected to replace more than 100 septic systems in North Windham and prevent approximately 22,000 pounds of nitrogen and 3,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the North Windham aquifer each year, helping to protect groundwater and surrounding waterways.
