title: Cortez Masto, Rosen Secure Over $2.4 Million for Nevada Law Enforcement Projects
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) secured $2,422,000 in grants for law enforcement projects. The funding comes from the Department of Justice’s Byrne Jag Grant Program and will be distributed to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the City of Henderson, and the Nevada Department of Public Safety.

“Local law enforcement is the backbone of public safety in Nevada, but too often our officers are being asked to do more with less,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “From improving training to modernizing equipment, this critical funding will support police officers from Reno to Henderson. I’ll never stop working to deliver for local law enforcement and ensure all Nevadans feel safe in their communities.”

“Our law enforcement officers work around the clock to keep Nevadans safe, and I’m committed to supporting them in any way I can,” said Senator Jacky Rosen. “I am proud to have helped secure this funding for law enforcement agencies across our state to ensure that they have the equipment and training they need to keep us safe.”

Three grants constitute the $2,422,000 in funding:

$1,031,000 for the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department’s (LVMPD) Air Support Equipment Enhancement Protect. This funding will be used to modernize essential air support equipment to improve the Department’s airborne law enforcement, search and rescue, and emergency response operations. This grant is on top of $1 million in federal funding the Senators secured for LVMPD’s Air Support Unit earlier this year.

$1,031,000 for the City of Henderson to support law enforcement responses to and prosecutions of nonfatal strangulation cases, increase the local forensic examination capacity, and improve protective and medical services to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault.

$360,000 for the Nevada Department of Public Safety for new law enforcement training technology for departments throughout the state.

Senators Cortez Masto and Rosen have consistently stood behind Nevada’s law enforcement. They have fought for funding for the Byrne JAG grant program, the source of these grants and the leading source of criminal justice funding in the country. Cortez Masto and Rosen introduced legislation to redirect excessive funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to local law enforcement. Last year, Cortez Masto’s bill to ensure the families of retired law enforcement officers killed as a result of their service have access to benefits was signed into law and her legislation to strengthen public safety in Indian Country passed the Senate. She is leading bipartisan legislation to combat human trafficking along America’s interstates, airways, railroads, and waterways.

title: Sen. Cruz Joins President Trump at White House to Announce Automatic Enrollment for Trump Accounts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) joined President Donald Trump at the White House yesterday to discuss the automatic enrollment of millions of American children in Trump Accounts. Sen. Cruz authored and passed into law the legislation establishing Trump Accounts last year.

On October 1, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the completion ofautomatic enrollment for Trump Accounts. The Treasury established accounts for more than 60 million additional eligible children.

Click here or on the image above to watch the full announcement.

Please see below for Sen. Cruz's remarks as prepared for delivery:

“Thank you, Mr. President, for bringing us together today to celebrate this incredible milestone for Trump Accounts. And thank you to Brad and Michael for everything you’ve done to turn this idea into reality.

“Mr. President – between school choice and Trump Accounts, there has never been a president who has done more for children than you.

“Today is an important day for Trump Accounts.

“When I wrote this legislation, we had a simple goal: every child in America should have the opportunity to begin life with an investment account and a stake in the extraordinary economic engine that is the United States of America.

“That is why I deliberately drafted the legislation to provide for auto-enrollment—so Treasury could open accounts for all 70 million American children under the age of 18. And I’m proud to stand here today seeing that become reality.

“For children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, the federal government will make a one-time $1,000 contribution to get them started.

“But the bigger idea here goes far beyond that first $1,000.

“For decades, we’ve talked about how to teach young Americans the value of saving, investing, and building wealth. Trump Accounts actually gives them the tools to do it.

“When a young person turns 18 and looks at an account that has been growing alongside them their entire life, capitalism is no longer an abstract concept.

“They’re an investor. They’re an owner. They have skin in the game.

“And my hope is that, decades from now, we look back at Trump Accounts as the beginning of an entire generation of Americans who became investors and owners from childhood.

“There is incredible momentum behind these accounts, and we are seeing more and more companies pledging to contribute to their employees’ accounts, which will only continue to help the next generation of Americans.

“Secretary Bessent – thank you for your leadership in making automatic enrollment a reality.

“Mr. President, you understood the potential of this idea from the beginning, and your leadership was critical to getting it across the finish line.

“And to those listening – these accounts have been created for you, but please take the time to claim your child’s account so that their investments can start today.

“I’m proud of what we accomplished together—and even more excited about what it will mean for millions of American kids in the years ahead.”

BACKGROUND

Trump Accounts, legislation authored by Sen. Cruz and established by law as part of theWorking Families Tax Cuts Act, are private, tax-advantaged accounts for every American child, seeded with a $1,000 investment from the federal government for children born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028. Trump Accounts, available now for all children 18 and under, allow for contributions from individuals, family members, and friends up to $5,000 annually. Employers may contribute $2,500 per year.

title: As USS Lincoln Returns Home, Duckworth Renews Her Call for Public Hearings to Investigate Toll of Trump’s Illegal War on Servicemembers
text:

“Pete Hegseth likes to say ‘war is hell,’ but what happened aboard the USS Lincoln was a level of pain that could’ve been avoided. The Trump Administration just chose not to.

title: Duckworth Reacts to Army Report on DCA Crash, Reiterates Calls for FAA and DoD to Implement Urgently Needed Safety Recommendations to Prevent Next Tragedy
text:
Trump’s FAA and DoD have yet to fully implement all recommendations made by the NTSB to fix the problems that led to America’s first deadly commercial aircraft collision since 2009

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL)—Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation—today released the following statement after the U.S. Army released its report that detailed numerous systemic failures leading up to the deadly DCA mid-air collision between a commercial aircraft and a Blackhawk helicopter that claimed the lives of 67 people:

“Ever since the tragic DCA midair collision stole 67 lives, the families of Flight 5342, the National Transportation Safety Board, aviation experts and I have sounded the alarm and called for action to prevent the next tragedy. This long-awaited Army investigation reaffirms what we’ve been calling for all along.

“Without delay, every aircraft must be equipped with and consistently use collision avoidance technology that is needed to see other aircraft in the sky and react in real time to keep the flying public safe. The FAA and Department of Defense must also improve coordination at all levels. And we urgently need to modernize our air traffic control system. In our modernization efforts, we need to focus on not just replacing outdated equipment but rebuilding a depleted controller workforce that has been chronically understaffed and overworked, including on that tragic night of the DCA crash when a single controller was forced to handle helicopter control and local control duties.

“As much as ever, the DCA midair collision reminds us how catastrophic the toll can be if we don’t take action. With this report out, there are simply no more excuses keeping the DoD and FAA from immediately implementing and exceeding the urgent safety recommendations handed down by both the Army and NTSB. The families who lost their loved ones that tragic day deserve action and the flying public’s safety depends on it.”

Duckworth has long been a leading voice in the push to make our skies safer. For years, she has been sounding the alarm that we must make critical aviation safety investments immediately to prevent all-too-often near-misses from becoming catastrophic tragedies. Last month, two bipartisan bills led by Duckworth and U.S. Senator John Hoeven (R-ND) to support the health of our aviation workforce and strengthen aviation safety passed the Senate with unanimous consent.

Last Congress, Duckworth chaired two CST Aviation Subcommittee hearings—one last December and the other a year prior—to address our aviation industry’s chilling surge in near-deadly close calls and underscore the urgent need to improve air traffic control systems to protect the flying public.

Duckworth helped author the landmark bipartisan FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 that was signed into law to extend the FAA’s funding and authorities through Fiscal Year 2028. The reauthorization included several of her provisions to safeguard the 1,500-hour rule, improve consumer safety, expand the aviation workforce and enhance protections for travelers with disabilities.

title: Durbin, Judiciary Committee Democrats Demand Full Production Of Committee Records Following Jack Smith Hearing
text:
Documents used by Schmitt and Hawley have yet to be shared with Democratic Committee Members or their staff, violating the standing rules of the Senate

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, led the Senate Judiciary Committee Democrats in a letter to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA) demanding a full production of all Committee records following last week’s oversight hearing with former Special Counsel Jack Smith. During the hearing, Senators Eric Schmitt (R-MO) and Josh Hawley (R-MO) questioned Mr. Smith about documents that had not been shared with Democratic Members or their staff prior to the hearing. It violates Senate Rules XXVI and XXVII to withhold committee records from Members or their staff. Republican Members asking a witness about documents that had not been shared with Democratic Members or their staff is a particularly egregious breach of these rules, a breach that has not yet been rectified as these records still have not been produced to Committee Democrats.

The letter also requests an apology to Mr. Smith and emphasizes that Republicans’ attempt to withhold these documents to manufacture a viral moment against Mr. Smith instead created an embarrassing stain on the Committee’s reputation.

“We write to object to the Committee violating Senate rules by failing to provide committee records to the minority in advance of the hearing… As of the date of this letter, we still have not received these records,” the Senators wrote. “We request that you immediately provide these and all other documents that you have withheld, commit to fully complying with Senate rules in the future, and apologize to Mr. Smith on behalf of the Committee for the unacceptable personal attacks and false accusations of perjury he faced during this hearing.”

The Senators’ letter continues, “Committee Republicans have now wasted months in their attempt to undermine Mr. Smith’s investigations into President Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election and illegally retain highly classified government documents. Rather than unveiling any credible new insights, the majority has merely cast petty, personal, and partisan aspersions on Mr. Smith and his nonpartisan career staff while ignoring President Trump’s crimes. This farce culminated in a national embarrassment for the Committee, when, in their eagerness to ambush a witness and manufacture a viral moment, Republican Members violated Senate rules by not sharing committee records with the minority and falsely accused a witness of perjury based on their own misunderstanding of these records.”

The letter concludes, “We ask that you immediately provide all committee records that you have withheld, commit to fully complying with Senate Rules XXVI and XXVII going forward, and apologize to Mr. Smith on behalf of the Committee.”

During the Biden Administration when Democrats were in the majority, then-Chair Durbin shared all committee records with the minority in a timely manner because it is required by Senate Rules, is a longstanding bipartisan Senate Judiciary Committee practice, and is necessary for the Committee to conduct meaningful oversight and carry out its constitutional duties. Additionally, unlike the Trump Administration, the Biden Administration had a practice of producing documents requested by the majority or minority to both the Chair and Ranking Member simultaneously.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

October 7, 2026

Dear Chairman Grassley:

We write to object to the Committee violating Senate rules by failing to provide committee records to the minority in advance of the hearing titled, “Oversight of Jack Smith’s Abuse of Authority and the Targeting of Republicans and Related Matters” on September 29, 2026. As of the date of this letter, we still have not received these records. We request that you immediately provide these and all other documents that you have withheld, commit to fully complying with Senate rules in the future, and apologize to Mr. Smith on behalf of the Committee for the unacceptable personal attacks and false accusations of perjury he faced during this hearing.

During the hearing, Senator Schmitt questioned Mr. Smith about committee records that you have not shared with Democratic Members or staff: texts between a counsel in the Special Counsel’s office and a U.S. Marshal regarding Mr. Smith’s attendance at a basketball game, and a readout of an August 17, 2024 phone call between Mr. Smith and the Department of Justice (DOJ) Public Integrity Section (PIN). Senator Hawley also displayed a chart of the same notes from the August 17, 2024 call with PIN during his questioning.

Withholding committee records from Members and their staff violates Rules XXVI and XXVII of the Standing Rules of the Senate, which require that all committee records be shared with the minority. When Democrats were in the majority on this Committee, Chair Durbin shared all committee records with the minority in a timely manner because it is required by Senate Rules, is a longstanding bipartisan Senate Judiciary Committee practice, and is necessary for this Committee to conduct meaningful oversight and carry out its constitutional duties. Additionally, unlike the Trump Administration, the Biden Administration had a practice of producing documents requested by the majority or minority to both the Chair and Ranking Member simultaneously.

The folly of withholding information was made clear when Republican Senators’ claims based on these documents were quickly revealed to be incorrect. The Special Counsel’s call notes, which purportedly stated that Mr. Smith filed a superseding indictment against President Trump against the advice of PIN, were actually Mr. Smith’s notes from a call prior to receiving PIN’s approval for an amended superseding indictment. And the texts concerning the basketball game—which Senator Schmitt claimed proved that Mr. Smith attended a game in Atlanta between the Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks on February 3, 2024—were an effort to manufacture a connection between Mr. Smith and the Fulton County Georgia District Attorney. The texts established only that Senator Schmitt had not done the basic due diligence of verifying a document before relying on it. Nonetheless, Senator Schmitt incorrectly asserted to Mr. Smith, “I think you’ve already perjured yourself,” and inexcusably branded him “a dirtbag,” language which is beneath the dignity of this Committee and the Senate.

Because these records had not been shared in advance, Democratic Members were forced to synthesize these baseless accusations and respond in real time. This caused needless confusion, slowed down the business of the Committee, introduced the possibility that false information would be entered uncontested into the record, and created an embarrassing stain on one of the most important committees in Congress.

While Senator Klobuchar successfully clarified that Mr. Smith had attended a basketball game in a different state on the date in question, and subsequent reporting confirmed the same, Senator Schmitt has since doubled down on his false assertions. He has continued to publicly call Mr. Smith a liar and “dirtbag.”

Committee Republicans have now wasted months in their attempt to undermine Mr. Smith’s investigations into President Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election and illegally retain highly classified government documents. Rather than unveiling any credible new insights, the majority has merely cast petty, personal, and partisan aspersions on Mr. Smith and his nonpartisan career staff while ignoring President Trump’s crimes. This farce culminated in a national embarrassment for the Committee, when, in their eagerness to ambush a witness and manufacture a viral moment, Republican Members violated Senate rules by not sharing committee records with the minority and falsely accused a witness of perjury based on their own misunderstanding of these records.

We ask that you immediately provide all committee records that you have withheld, commit to fully complying with Senate Rules XXVI and XXVII going forward, and apologize to Mr. Smith on behalf of the Committee.

Sincerely,

title: Busted: Ernst Law Forces Washington to Come Clean on Billion-Dollar Boondoggles
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Joni Ernst's (R-Iowa) Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act is now law, signed today by President Trump. It requires the federal government to publicly report every project that is $1 billion or more over budget or five or more years behind schedule.

The law arrives as Ernst exposes five new boondoggles that together total nearly $100 billion over budget. These boondoggles are in addition to those she exposed in her 2025 Off the Rails report, which found $162.9 billion in cost overruns on federally funded projects.

"Washington math doesn't add up, but my Billion Dollar Boondoggle law will restore accountability to its shady accounting. Taxpayers deserve this transparency, and it will protect them from being put on the hook for hundreds of billions of dollars sunk into failed and mismanaged projects plagued by massive cost overruns and never-ending delays," said Sen. Ernst.

"While government boondoggles abound, the term is now officially in the law books for the first time. No politician wants their prized pet project to carry that label, but now there's no escaping it," Sen. Ernst added.

The five additional boondoggles:

F-35 Modernization (Department of War): $89.5 billion over budget since being rebased in 2012, increasing from $395.7 billion to $485.2 billion, and five years behind schedule, now expected in 2031.

Hudson River Tunnel (Department of Transportation): $3 billion over budget, increasing from $12.7 billion to $15.7 billion, and three years behind schedule, now expected in 2038.

Rebuilding Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge (Department of Transportation): Up to $3.5 billion over budget, increasing from as low as $1.7 billion to as high as $5.2 billion, and two years behind schedule, now expected in 2030.

Saturn Dragonfly Spacecraft (NASA): $2.5 billion over budget, nearly quadrupling from $850 million to $3.35 billion, and more than two years behind schedule, now expected in July 2028.

Palo Alto VA Medical Center (Department of Veterans Affairs): $1.2 billion over budget, increasing from $450.3 million to $1.6 billion, and 21 years behind schedule, now expected in 2036 instead of 2015.

The law builds on the Trump administration's efforts to rein in runaway project costs. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has been leading the way, providing Ernst with the Department's data on over-budget and delayed projects, and pulling $4 billion in unspent federal funding from California's high-speed rail project.

Ernst led the bill in the Senate with Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), and Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa) championed it in the House. The bill passed both chambers of Congress before heading to the President's desk. Hassan and Miller-Meeks joined Ernst in celebrating the new law.

“Granite Staters deserve to know that their hard-earned tax-dollars are being spent responsibly,” said Sen. Hassan. “This commonsense, bipartisan bill will give the public greater visibility into how their tax dollars are being used and it will help Congress identify wasteful spending. I am pleased to see this bill signed into law and I will continue working with my colleagues of both parties to protect taxpayer dollars and increase government transparency.”

“Washington has gotten far too comfortable wasting the taxpayers’ money, and that ends with transparency and accountability,” said Rep. Miller-Meeks. “Senator Ernst and I worked together to give Congress and the American people greater visibility into federal projects that go over budget and fall behind schedule. I’m proud to see our bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act signed into law, and I thank Senator Ernst for her partnership in getting this across the finish line. Taxpayers work too hard for their money to see it wasted in Washington, and they deserve to know that every dollar is being spent responsibly.”

title: Senator Hassan Presses RFK Jr to Reinstate Critical Program for the Research of Maternal and Infant Health
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on Health Care, is pressing Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to reinstate the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS), which is the only nationwide system that tracks the experiences of women and their infants before, during, and after birth. As the United States faces a maternal health crisis, the Department of Health and Human Services chose to shut down PRAMS at the start of the Trump Administration in January 2025. PRAMS helped lawmakers and public health officials across the country develop and strengthen programs to protect maternal and infant health by providing a nationwide snapshot of the challenges that women face during prenatal and postpartum care, their mental and physical health, and the health of their babies.

“Before January 2025, the federal Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System, or ‘PRAMS,’ was the only nationwide system that helped us understand whether the programs that are intended to reduce maternal and infant deaths are working. Each month, states asked women who have recently given birth about their health and experiences before, during, and after pregnancy,” Senator Hassan wrote in a request to Secretary Kennedy to restore the program. “For decades, this information had been collected, anonymized, and posted in the PRAMS system by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, providing a nationwide snapshot of the challenges that women face during prenatal and postpartum care, their mental and physical health, and the health of their babies.”

The Senator continued, “Researchers and policymakers have used information from PRAMS to design programs that stop preventable maternal and infant deaths. For example, the system helped health workers in New Hampshire more effectively screen for and treat substance use in pregnant women... I am deeply concerned that disruptions to PRAMS have left permanent gaps in our understanding of maternal and infant health.”

Hassan is pressing Secretary Kennedy and his department to restore the PRAMS program, reinstate the staff working on it, and make all data on material and infant health that has been collected in the last year and half publicly available. Hassan’s push to restore PRAMS is supported by several organizations including the March of Dimes and the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists.

“It cannot be overstated how important PRAMS is to the collective effort to improve U.S. maternal and infant health outcomes,”said Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE, FACOG, President of the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. “For nearly 40 years, PRAMS has been the only tool we have that captures detailed, self-reported, state-specific information on topics such as prenatal and postpartum care, mental health, breastfeeding, housing, and income. This information gives ob-gyns important insights into maternal behaviors and experiences that help improve care delivery. Yet, for more than a year, PRAMS has been unable to function optimally without the necessary staff to provide states with analysis and technical assistance. It is imperative that PRAMS staff be reinstated so that we can stay abreast of emerging issues and continue monitoring changes in maternal and infant health that will ultimately help save lives.”

Senator Hassan has led a number of efforts to ensure that new and expecting mothers have access to high-quality health care. Last year, Hassan led her colleagues in introducing the bipartisan Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act to support rural health care facilities in providing urgent obstetric care. The bill advanced from committee in July. Senator Hassan and the New Hampshire Congressional delegation also had previously fought to secure nearly $1 million in federal funding for Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center to strengthen maternal health care in the North Country. She introduced the Keep Obstetrics Local Act (KOLA), to help keep labor and delivery units in rural and underserved communities stay open, and the bipartisan Healthy Moms and Babies Act to strengthen health care for women before, after, and during childbirth. In 2023, thanks to Senator Hassan’sbipartisan legislation to improve mental health for new mothers, the Department of Health and Human Services launched theTask Force on Maternal Mental Health.

Read the full text of Senator Hassan’s request to Secretary Kennedy here or below.

Dear Secretary Kennedy:

The United States faces a maternal health crisis. A larger share of American women and infants die from preventable causes than women and infants in peer nations. Despite this crisis, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services chose in January 2025 to shut down the only nationwide system that helps the public track the performance of federal programs that are intended to keep mothers and babies from dying preventable deaths. We urge you to immediately reinstate access to this centralized system and publicly release unpublished data from the past year and a half.

Before January 2025, the federal Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System, or “PRAMS,” was the only nationwide system that helped us understand whether the programs that are intended to reduce maternal and infant deaths are working. Each month, states asked women who have recently given birth about their health and experiences before, during, and after pregnancy. For decades, this information had been collected, anonymized, and posted in the PRAMS system by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), providing a nationwide snapshot of the challenges that women face during prenatal and postpartum care, their mental and physical health, and the health of their babies.

Researchers and policymakers have used information from PRAMS to design programs that stop preventable maternal and infant deaths. For example, the system helped health workers in New Hampshire more effectively screen for and treat substance use in pregnant women. In West Virginia, the state used PRAMS to identify high rates of unintended pregnancies among women battling addiction and used that information to target resources and reduce the number of babies born with opioid withdrawal syndrome. Through PRAMS, the State of Maine found that pregnant women in that state used tobacco at a high rate, and in response, Maine created a new program to support smoking cessation among pregnant and postpartum women.

In January 2025, the administration shut down the PRAMS software that states use to collect maternal health data and the portal that the public used to access it. This forced many states to stop collecting responses for an average of three months, and in some cases for as long as eight months. You fired the CDC staff responsible for managing the program and have yet to restore the system that researchers used to study national PRAMS data.

I am deeply concerned that disruptions to PRAMS have left permanent gaps in our understanding of maternal and infant health. I urge you to reinstate the CDC staff working on PRAMS, restore public access to the portal for studying national PRAMS data, and release PRAMS data that has not been made publicly available for the past year and a half.

title: SIGNED INTO LAW: Hassan-Grassley Legislation to Support Victims of Identity Theft
text:
WASHINGTON – The Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act authored by Senators Maggie Hassan and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) was signed into law yesterday. The bipartisan legislation makes it easier for identity theft victims to get help from the Social Security Administration.

“Too often, victims of identity theft are forced to navigate a long, confusing process to get support from the Social Security Administration. This process is frustrating to victims and unnecessarily drains the agency’s resources,” said Senator Hassan. “My bipartisan bill will help streamline support from SSA for so that victims of identity theft can get the help that they need more quickly. I worked with colleagues across the aisle to pass this commonsense legislation, and I am glad to see it signed into law. I will continue pushing to make the government work more efficiently for victims of theft, fraud, and scams.”

“Millions of Americans suffer from identity theft each year, and Social Security numbers are a top target. Unfortunately, when an identity theft victim calls up the Social Security Administration, they can be jerked around from one contact to another, having to reexplain the situation each time. By providing victims a single point of contact at the agency, our bill will help ease this frustrating and stressful process and make life easier for Iowans who may find themselves in this unfortunate situation. I want to thank my colleagues for their overwhelming support to get this legislation over the finish line,” said Senator Grassley.

The Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act provides a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration to more efficiently and quickly resolve and identity-theft victim’s issues.

The legislation was endorsed by numerous groups, including AARP, Social Security Works, the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSSM), Justice in Aging, and the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives (NOSSCR).

Read the full text of the bill here.

This bill builds on Senator Hassan’s longstanding efforts to protect taxpayers, prevent waste and fraud, and help government work more effectively for the American people. Earlier this year, she introduced the bipartisan ReportScams.gov Act to establish a centralized portal where Americans can report scams and get help. She also introduced the bipartisan No Aid for Ghost Students Act to prevent fraudsters from using stolen identities to steal federal student aid. As Ranking Member of the Joint Economic Committee, Senator Hassan is leading a comprehensive investigation into combating scams, and as part of that, she led a Committee hearing earlier this year during which she secured commitments from the FBI and Department of Justice to improve coordination and strengthen the federal response to scams.

title: King, Colleagues Demand Answers on Trump Administration Directive to Reject Established Vaccine Science
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME) is joining his colleagues in questioning the Trump Administration’s directives to reject established vaccine science, as the United States faces the largest measles outbreak in 35 years. In a letter to Dr. Erica Schwartz, the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the lawmakers confront her on dangerous efforts to reject established vaccine science, and demand answers about the CDC’s attempts to implement President Trump’s childhood vaccine Executive Order (EO), underreport measles-associated deaths, and stall access to childhood immunizations.

The United States is facing a decline in childhood immunization rates. Recently, the CDC reported that 280,000 kindergartners did not complete their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine series. This comes as the Trump administration has actively worked to lower the number of recommended immunizations, break up safe and effective combination shots, and promote legal action against states unaligned with such efforts.

The lawmakers began, “[...] As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule.”

“At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health,” they continued.

“The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient,” concluded the lawmakers.

In addition to King, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Michael Bennet (D-CO), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD.), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Ed Markey (D-MA), and Jeff Merkley (D-OR).

Last year, Senator King spoke on the Senate floor to discuss the removal of Congressionally-approved funding from critical public services including, but not limited to, the World Health Organization (WHO), which leads global efforts to expand universal health coverage and directs and coordinates the world’s response to health emergencies before they can pose a threat to American lives. Calling it an “abdication of Congressional-authority,” he shared how some of the Trump Administration’s decisions have gone from bad policy to downright dangerous. Since then, he has called out multiple Trump Administration officials for their willingness – or lack thereof—to speak the truth, even when it is politically inconvenient.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

+++

Dr. Schwartz:

At your confirmation hearing, you said that your “sacred responsibility” as Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) would be to provide “clear, honest, and evidence-based” public health guidance and to “never betray the science.” In the short time since your confirmation as CDC Director, the health and safety of our children have been subjected to further chaos and confusion. As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health.

The CDC recently reported that the number of children up-to-date on their immunizations has continued to decline, including 280,000 kindergartners who did not complete the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) series. Instead of spending time and dedicating resources to promote the need for childhood immunizations, President Trump called for breaking up combination shots like the MMR vaccine into single-disease shots that are not available in the United States, cutting the number of diseases every child is recommended to be protected against from 18 to 11, and directing the Attorney General to advance legal challenges to state laws. Following this EO, HHS issued an RFI on the childhood immunization schedule, aimed at bypassing the CDC and the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, which have developed recommendations for over 60 years. These efforts are only a part of the systematic attacks spearheaded by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. CDC’s scientists, not political appointees, should be at the center of any decision about the childhood immunization schedule.

During this same timeframe, CDC’s public actions under your leadership raise serious concerns regarding your willingness to counter these unscientific measures – including reports that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public national mortality count for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continue to track these fatalities. This is a clear break from long-standing agency precedent, including last year’s standard reporting of measles deaths in Texas and directly contradicts the commitment to “objective data collection and reporting” that has been CDC’s foundation. If the agency under your leadership is altering verified state data to fit political preferences, the pledge you made at your confirmation hearing has already been broken.

We request responses to the following questions in writing by October 16, 2026.

CDC Role on the Executive Order on Childhood Vaccines

Did anyone from the White House or HHS consult you about the Executive Order either before or after it was issued?

a. If so, who reached out, what was discussed, and when did these communication(s) occur?

b. If not, have you raised, or do you plan to raise, any concerns with President Trump, Secretary Kennedy, or any other administration official(s)?

How is the CDC planning to implement the provisions outlined in the EO? What steps have been taken already and what are planned? Please provide a detailed summary of these plans.

What role, if any, did CDC career scientists have in developing the EO’s recommendations?

The EO directs the Secretary, acting through the HHS Task Force on Safer Childhood Vaccines, to present plans to the President within 90 days on single-disease vaccine options, the timing and sequencing of childhood vaccines, and safety monitoring. What role does the CDC have in developing those plans, and which CDC officials are participating?

The EO recommends reducing the number of routine immunizations from 18 to 11. Do you support that specific recommendation? What scientific evidence supports removing the other diseases from the immunizations recommended for all children, and has the CDC estimated the additional illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths that could result?

Do you agree that spacing out immunizations across additional visits lengthens the window of vulnerability for infants and young children? If not, please provide the evidence on which CDC relies.

The EO recommends separating combination shots like MMR into single-disease shots. No single-disease MMR vaccine is currently available in the United States. Other countries that have tried this – like Japan in the 1990s – saw increased outbreaks, ultimately resulting in them reverting to a combination shot. Do you support this specific provision even though it is not currently available in the U.S., would require more shots and doctor visits, and lacks scientific backing? Why is the federal government recommending an option to families that does not exist, causing additional confusion?

What scientific evidence supports separating combination vaccines like MMR into single-disease doses? Please provide CDC analyses of peer-reviewed studies, epidemiological analyses, or international precedent that demonstrates this change would actually improve health outcomes. If no such evidence exists, will you decline to implement this provision?

The public comment period for the HHS RFI closed on September 20, 2026. Did CDC scientists review or contribute to the RFI before it was published? What role will CDC scientists have in reviewing the comments and in any resulting changes to the categories of federal vaccine recommendations?

Data Collection and Reporting

Has the CDC instituted a new policy for reviewing, altering, or withholding state-reported health data before public posting?

If so, what scientific evidence supports this change and what deliberations occurred?

If there is no such policy, on what basis were Pennsylvania’s measles deaths excluded from the public tracker, and who at CDC authorized that exclusion?

As of today, the CDC has only included two of the measles-associated deaths reported by the State of Pennsylvania. What specific technical, scientific, or epidemiological basis justified excluding Pennsylvania’s state-reported measles deaths from the CDC's public tracker while still including them on internal trackers?

Did any White House or HHS officials contact you or your staff regarding the public reporting of Pennsylvania’s measles deaths? Please provide all communication between CDC leadership and any White House or HHS official regarding the reporting of state-verified measles deaths since your confirmation.

Vaccines for Children Program

Why did the CDC delay opening orders for COVID vaccines through the Vaccines for Children Program (VFC)? Please provide the timeline of when decisions were made concerning the VFC program.

What made the CDC decide to open ordering for COVID vaccines through the VFC program on September 24, 2026 and not earlier?

Have you personally been asked by Secretary Kennedy, the White House, or any other HHS or Trump administration official to delay or condition VFC activation for the COVID vaccine? If so, please describe the request and identify who made it. If such a request was made in writing, please provide it.

Who at CDC, HHS, or the White House made the decision to delay VFC activation for the COVID vaccine, and on what basis? Please produce all internal communications, memoranda, and legal or scientific analyses supporting that decision.

What guidance has CDC provided to state health departments, pediatricians, and VFC providers about the status of COVID vaccines under VFC? How soon can VFC vaccines be expected to be in the possession of clinicians and accessible for children?

The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing.

###

title: Luján, Colleagues Lead Nearly 190 Members of Congress in Slamming HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
text:
Luján, Leaders Schumer & Jeffries, Senators Sanders and Warnock, Representatives Scott, Bonamici and Budzinski Lead Bicameral Group of Lawmakers in Demanding Trump Administration Halt Planned Gutting of Head Start

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), one of two Head Start graduates to serve in the U.S. Senate, joined colleagues in leading nearly one hundred ninety Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.

In the Senate, the letter is led by Senator Luján, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), and Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA). In the House, the letter is led by House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13).

The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.

“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”

Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page 482 of Project 2025.

title: Senator Marshall, Drug Czar Carter Host Kansas Roundtables on Drug Prevention & Combating Drug Crisis
text:
Wichita – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas) and Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, or “Drug Czar,” Sara Carter hosted two roundtables in Kansas focused on preventing drug use, strengthening community partnerships and combating the drug crisis. The discussions brought together education, prevention, community and law enforcement leaders to address the drug threats facing Kansas and identify ways to better protect communities.

Click here for more photos.

The first roundtable, held at Wichita Northwest High School, focused on youth drug prevention and the role schools, families, community organizations and law enforcement can play in keeping young people away from drugs. During the discussion, Carter and Marshall announced a new partnership between the Drug Free Communities Support (DFC) program and Wichita Northwest High School to develop the nation’s first youth-to-youth primary prevention toolkit.

The toolkit will be led by students and guided by adults, giving young people a direct role in developing prevention strategies for their peers. The initiative will bring together Wichita Northwest High School, the DFC program and High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) partners, with a goal of launching the toolkit at the start of the 2027-28 school year.

“We don’t want the next generation to inherit the drug crisis we are fighting today. We need to empower young people to take this crisis on head-on because they know what their friends and classmates are facing,” said Senator Marshall. “I appreciate Director Carter and ONDCP for putting young people at the center of this effort and giving them the tools to lead. It’s great to see a Kansas school setting an example and empowering students to take ownership in this fight.”

“The DFC program has been successful because it empowers local leaders- those who know their communities best- with federal resources to make a difference in the lives of countless young Americans. Among those leaders, and some of our most powerful advocates, are youth themselves,”said Drug Czar Sara Carter. “The students developing this toolkit know better than anyone the pressures their peers face, and how to best overcome them. I look forward to the release of their work.”

“We are excited that students of our district were selected to help create this national toolkit, giving young people a voice in shaping youth engagement efforts nationwide,” said Superintendent Kelly Bielefeld.

The second roundtable, held at the Kansas City, Kansas Police Department, focused on the law enforcement response to the drug crisis and brought together federal, state and local law enforcement leaders to discuss drug trafficking, strengthen coordination between agencies and address the threats facing Kansas communities.

Senator Marshall has made combating the drug crisis and protecting Kansas communities a priority. He has advocated for full funding of the Midwest HIDTA program, which supports law enforcement agencies across the region in disrupting drug trafficking. He also championed the Cooper Davis Act to address the online trafficking of counterfeit drugs and has pressed federal officials to take action against dangerous substances, including concentrated 7-OH.

title: Daines, Merkley Announce Sweeping Bipartisan Proposal to “Save the Senate”
text:
End the Senate’s Dysfunction and Deliver Results for the American People

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.) and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) today announced the rollout of a sweeping bipartisan proposal that would enact major changes to the Senate’s governing rules. These changes would help restore the Senate’s purpose of robust debate and bipartisan policymaking so that the Senate can legislate effectively and tackle pressing challenges facing the country.

These major reforms will “Save the Senate.”

“For much of our history the American people could rely on the Senate to tackle our hardest challenges. But over the past 50 years, deliberation in the U.S. Senate has all but ground to a halt due to toxic, partisan political culture. As a result, the Senate has become unnecessarily—and unacceptably—diminished as the world’s greatest deliberative body.

“Both parties had a role in creating the Senate’s dysfunction, and both parties have a responsibility to fix it. That’s why we’re working together—a Democrat and a Republican—to put forward this proposal to Save the Senate.

“Our proposal will incentivize bipartisan cooperation, strengthen committees, empower members of both parties to bring and amend bills on the Senate floor, help prevent government shutdowns, and reduce needless procedural delays. These reforms will help the Senate solve our nation’s problems and deliver results for the American people,” said Daines and Merkley.

Specifically, the proposal would:

Increase time for debate on more legislation by eliminating cloture votes on nominations, motions to proceed, and amendments. Retains cloture vote prior to final passage under regular order.

Create a Senate version of the House “suspension” calendar. Bipartisan bills that have cleared committee would be eligible for swift Senate passage at a two-thirds threshold.

Create a fast-track tool that would allow bipartisan bills that have cleared committee to be processed, amended, and passed at a simple majority threshold.

Create another fast-track tool that would allow bipartisan spending bills to be brought to the Senate floor, amended, and passed in two days.

Read the full details of Daines’ and Merkley’s proposals HERE.

title: Wyden, Merkley Announce More Than $1 Million to Support Addiction and Recovery Services in Eastern Oregon
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today announced more than $1 million in federal awards to help combat the opioid epidemic and to support addiction and recovery services in Eastern Oregon.

“The opioid epidemic continues to harm communities across the state, especially in rural areas that often have limited addiction treatment resources,” Wyden said. “I applaud this federal award to the Oregon Washington Health Network that will strengthen addiction and recovery services for Eastern Oregonians, and I will continue to fight for every possible resource to support mental health services and combat the opioid epidemic across Oregon.”

“I have heard heart-wrenching stories from Oregonians who have lost loved ones after a prescription for an injury or treatment turned into an addiction,” said Merkley. “Communities need access to addiction and treatment services, and this critical support will help Pendleton improve access to critical services for opioid use disorder.”

The $1.05 million in federal awards from Health Resources and Services Administration’s Rural Communities Opioid Response Program will be distributed to The Oregon Washington Health Network, a non-profit based in Pendleton dedicated to health equity in Umatilla, Union, and Morrow counties in Oregon, and Walla Walla County in Washington. The award will be used to improve access to treatment and recovery services for substance use disorder and opioid use disorder.

“In rural communities, access isn’t just about whether a service exists, but whether it’s available when and where people actually need it. These awards give us the opportunity to strengthen the services already working in our communities, expand peer and recovery supports, and create new pathways for people to stay connected to recovery close to home,” said Jenna Stenrud, Executive Director of Oregon Washington Health Network.

Fresh Off CODEL to the Gulf, Murphy Accuses Trump, Hegseth of 'Active Cover Up' of Iran War, Addresses Future of U.S.-Saudi Relations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) offered his first takeaway on his Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to the Middle East, which included stops in Doha, Qatar and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to members of the press to share reflections and answer questions. Murphy was the first Democratic Senator to visit the Gulf since the start of Trump’s war with Iran.

Murphy spoke on the growing chaos he witnessed on the ground in the Middle East, as Trump's Iran War continues to spiral: “I saw firsthand how this war is spiraling downward very quickly. The Riyadh airport is functionally closed, with hundreds of flights being delayed or canceled. The day that I left there were Iranian attacks on the airport. You can sense that Saudi Arabia is a country at war right now. They are starting a major ground campaign with their Yemeni government partners, and you feel in Saudi Arabia how this war has become a regional war. This was, of course, completely foreseeable and predictable.”

Murphy chronicled how Pete Hegseth is orchestrating a cover-up of the Iran war, blocking members of Congress from conducting standard oversight of military bases, or even speaking to military leadership in the Gulf: “There is an active cover-up going on right now… I spoke personally to Admiral Cooper and asked him to give us access. I told him during a briefing that we had with him right before I left that not only had I been denied access to the bases, but that military leadership wasn't even going to speak with me while I was in Qatar. I will tell you he was surprised to learn that the policy also prevented him and his leadership from speaking to me at that meeting. At that briefing we had with him early last week, he promised that it would be possible to at least provide a briefing. My impression was certainly—I do not want to speak for him—but my impression was that he didn't support either policy: neither the policy to deny access to bases nor the policy to refuse briefings. But apparently he couldn't change Secretary Hegseth's mind because when I arrived in Qatar, I was told that not only would I not be able to see Al Udeid, but I would not have any access to military leadership while I was there. But this cover-up is real. Hegseth is determined to hide the cost and the consequences of this war from the American public. It is absolutely outrageous that I and Republican senators are being denied the ability to see the damage for ourselves.”

Murphy laid out the long, bipartisan history of Members of Congress conducting oversight in active war zones, and how Hegseth’s Department of Defense blocked Murphy’s efforts to visit Al Udeid Air Base: “It is absolutely ordinary for members of Congress to travel to areas of conflict and get to talk directly to the military leaders and the soldiers that are involved in the conflict, and see for ourselves the damage that has been done to our bases and equipment. I traveled to both Iraq and Afghanistan at the height of those wars. I was in Baghdad during one of the most dangerous offensives there. I was flown by the military to a forward operating base in Afghanistan at the very moment that base was under attack by the Taliban. Why? Because it's Congress that decides whether to fund a war or whether to defund a war, whether to authorize a war, and we can't do our job without seeing in-person the consequences of the war. I made every effort I could to be able to carry out my responsibility as a member of the Senate. We reached out to the Department of Defense to tell them we were coming weeks in advance and asked them for access to bases there, in particular Al Udeid, which is our biggest military installation in the region in Qatar. We followed that up with a formal request in writing, and then I spoke personally to Admiral Cooper and asked him to give us access.”

Describing the extensive, long-term damage to the American Embassy in Saudi Arabia, Murphy emphasized that Trump's recklessness put dozens of American lives at risk: “I was able to view the damage at our embassy in Saudi Arabia. It was extraordinary. Had that attack happened during the daytime, there's no doubt that there would have been many, many Americans killed. I saw the damage at Raslif, the big Qatari gas plant. 17% of their exports have been eliminated, probably at least for the next three years as they repair that damage. I saw only one LNG tanker in port, whereas they normally have six tankers in that port. One is leaving per day on average compared to ten before the war.”

Murphy described his candid conversations with leadership in the region funneling money to the Trump family, pressing them to end the corruption: “I told the Qataris that no matter how much pressure they got from Donald Trump to gift that plane, they should have said no, because it is obvious what's happening here. The plane is going to be in U.S. hands for a matter of years, and then Trump is going to take it knowing that this was a corrupt deal. The Qataris should have said no. I also spoke very candidly to Mohammed bin Salman and told him that his investments in Jared Kushner's private equity funds and his invitation to Trump and his business entities to partner on projects in Saudi Arabia was an enormous problem for the U.S.-Saudi relationship in the long run. Both leaders told me that they believe this to be good business, and they claimed, of course, that they were doing nothing illegal on their end of the deal. Even if that's true, the problem is that Trump is shaping our foreign policy in order to try to get deals in the region.”

As one of the Senate’s loudest critics of the Saudi regime, Murphy explained his decision to meet with Mohammed Bin Salman and stressed the need for multiple American perspectives in the region: “I definitely thought long and hard about whether I should meet with Mohammed bin Salman, given my criticism and given the legitimacy that sometimes comes with meetings with leaders in the United States. But I worry that the Saudis, in particular, are hearing only one view from the United States, and I think it was important for them to hear from my side of the aisle that cares about the corruption and wants there to be more political space for dissidents to operate in Saudi Arabia and throughout the region.”

Murphy recognized how far Saudi Arabia has come over the last decade, but maintained that more must be done for political dissidents: “One of the reasons I wanted to go to Saudi Arabia is because I do know that there is a social transformation happening in that country, and I wanted to see it for myself. It is real. Just a decade ago, there were no movie theaters or concert halls open. Men and women weren't sitting with each other in cafes. Certainly, women were not allowed to walk around in public uncovered. All of those things are happening. There is a legitimate social and cultural transformation happening in Saudi Arabia and it was I think important for me to see it for myself. That being said, there's no defense for what has also happened in Saudi Arabia in the last 10 years—a massive contraction of political space. There is no room to dissent from the kingdom's policies, and that's unacceptable.”

In an unprecedented move, the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) under Secretary Pete Hegseth’s leadership denied Murphy access to the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, despite decades of precedent for DOD supporting CODELs to American military bases under active threat to uphold Congress’s oversight duties. Prior to his CODEL, Murphy requested access to the base via a letter and direct appeal to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) leadership to no avail. While DOD denied him access to U.S. military facilities, the U.S. Department of State supported Murphy’s trip to the region.

In Saudi Arabia, Murphy sat down with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; met with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud; toured the damage done to the U.S. embassy in Riyadh; engaged with economic and cultural leaders; and talked with University of New Haven students at the first American university campus in Saudi Arabia, among other things.

In Qatar, Murphy met with His Highness the Emir of the State of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Additionally, Murphy met with Ali Al Thawadi, Qatari Minister for Strategic Affairs and a key diplomat who coordinates U.S.-Iran shuttle diplomacy; Qatari royal and Qatar Foundation Vice Chair Sheikha Hind Al Thani in Education City to discuss the presence of American universities in Qatar; and Qatar Energy CEO Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, among others.

title: In Olympia, Murray Hears from State Leaders on WA Efforts to Regulate AI; Murray Emphasizes Need for Federal Action Without Preemption
text:
Senator Murray: “We can’t afford to regulate AI with nothing but a pinky promise. We cannot just wait for the worst risks of this technology to become reality before we take action.”

Murray has opposed the Trump administration’s efforts to stamp out state-level regulations of AI

ICYMI: In Seattle, Murray Highlights Urgent Need to Deploy AI Safely, Transparently, and to Benefit Working People; Murray Says Pro-Worker, Pro-Family Policies Don’t Have to Wait

***VIDEO HERE***

Olympia, WA — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, held a roundtable discussion with state leaders on Washington state’s latest efforts to regulate AI and underscored the need for a strong federal floor to ensure AI is deployed safely, transparently, and benefits working people.

Joining Senator Murray for the discussion today were: Beau Perschbacher, Senior Policy Advisor to Governor Bob Ferguson; Yuki Ishizuka, Senior Policy Analyst and Technology Policy Manager at the Washington State Office of the Attorney General; Gretchen Peri, Chief Technology Officer at Washington Technology Solutions (WaTech); and Rob Eleveld, Chief Executive Officer at the Transparency Coalition.

“I’m not an expert in AI, I’m a former preschool teacher. But I’ll tell you what: I ran for office exactly because I believe regular people deserve a say in how their government is run—the exact same is true for the development of this technology. There are real opportunities with AI—in medicine, in discovery. But this technology will also likely mean disruption and it poses real challenges and threats. And right now regulation of AI is virtually nonexistent at the federal level. I want America to develop and deploy this technology in a way that is transparent and safe—and we have got to make sure the benefits of AI are for everyone, not just billionaires and giant corporations. And we have to stay ahead of the risks too,” said Senator Murray. “I recently spoke with the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, he made it absolutely clear that there are real safety risks that require urgent action. When the stakes are this high, we cannot take safety for granted. That’s just common sense. No one would say nuclear plants can regulate themselves—or drug companies. Why would we ignore something as powerful and potentially dangerous as AI?”

“At minimum, over in Congress, we need to think about a floor of basic, bipartisan guardrails the entire country can get behind: for that to happen, we need hearings, briefings, testimony from industry leaders, markups, debate, and more. So far the Republican majority has done nothing. Trump wants to call AI risks a ‘hoax’ and call it a day. His most significant AI policies to date? He tried to rename it, and threatened states’ funding if they dare to regulate it. Trump shaking hands with billionaires and saying they can regulate themselves is not going to cut it,” continued Senator Murray. “We can’t afford to regulate AI with nothing but a pinky promise. We cannot just wait for the worst risks of this technology to become reality before we take action.”

“In Congress, we need to think about a floor of basic, bipartisan guardrails the entire country can get behind. There’s no time to delay AI safety. When it comes to the economy, I absolutely want to explore big ideas. But we already know what working families need: paid leave, universal health care and child care, and stronger unions. If we’re expecting major economic disruption, we should write that safety net into law now, not after workers have already been left behind,” said Senator Murray in closing. “Washington state has been leading on these questions, and I came to Olympia to hear directly from state leaders about what they’ve done and what they’re considering next. I’m taking what I heard back to the other Washington, because the people of this state, and this country, deserve a government that is ready for what’s coming.”

Senator Murray made clear that while policymakers can’t yet predict exactly how AI will change our economy and how we work, there is no reason for Congress to delay in passing so many of Murray’s longstanding legislative priorities that would benefit working people like stronger labor laws and enforcement, national paid leave, universal health care, the Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act, affordable child care for every working family, and much more.

“We need guardrails to ensure that AI development does not infringe on our rights, harm our families, or pose an existential risk to our country,” said Attorney General Nick Brown. “Congress should act swiftly to put these protections in place, and I appreciate Senator Murray’s leadership on this issue.”

“Artificial intelligence is reshaping how we work and serve the public, so Washington is approaching this moment with intention,” said WaTech’s Gretchen Peri, the State Chief Technology Officer for Washington. “The statewide AI strategy we’ve developed is committed to human‑focused, trustworthy innovation, and gives state agencies the tools, guardrails, and shared platforms they need to deploy AI safely and transparently. Backed by new state laws that reinforce accountability and public trust, we’re proving that government can lead AI adoption with responsibility, foresight, humanity, and dignity.”

“We at Transparency Coalition want to thank Senator Murray for pulling together the AI Safety and Transparency roundtable today. We have been honored to work closely with Attorney General Nick Brown’s office, Governor Ferguson’s office and a number of legislators starting with Representative Callan on some key AI laws passed in 2026 including protecting minors from addictive and manipulative AI chatbots,” said Rob Eleveld, CEO and Co-founder, Transparency Coalition. “Looking forward, our position across many states is the best way to hold AI companies accountable is to use existing product liability laws, the reason we all trust the brakes in our cars, to require a duty of care to not harm customers with AI products.”

Earlier this year, Senator Murray met with leading AI experts in Seattle about the challenges and opportunities associated with AI to discuss how leaders can work to deploy AI safely, transparently, and in a way that benefits working people—not just giant corporations and billionaires.

As vice chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Senator Murray negotiated the Commerce‑Justice‑Science (CJS) Appropriations Bill for Fiscal Year 2026, which is currently the largest federal investment in AI standards and testing ever passed through a CJS bill. The CJS bill includes $1.8 billion for the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) overall, an increase of $690 million over last year’s funding level. This includes no less than $55 million for AI research, an increase of $20 million, and up to $10 million for NIST’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation to advance AI research, standards, and testing. Senator Murray fiercely defended science agencies from President Trump’s proposed reductions, which threatened to cut NIST by more than 28 percent.

Senator Murray also played a key role in helping to pass the bipartisan Chips and Science Act which makes historic investments in American manufacturing, and research and development. The bill included AI scholarships through NSF, funding for the Department of Energy’s research and development on AI and machine learning, support for NIST’s work on AI and quantum information science, and resources for the creation of a NSF Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships which will focus on domestic development of AI and other quantum computing.

Senator Murray has called for Congress to regulate AI and been outspoken against President Trump’s efforts to ban states from regulating AI. As President Trump called AI safety concerns a “hoax” and rolled out the red carpet for Xi Jinping, Senator Murray sent a letter urging him to take the threat seriously and work out real AI safeguards with China. She recently introduced legislation to halt the A.I.-Driven Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) model which is overruling doctors and delaying care for Medicare beneficiaries.

title: Murray Leads WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
text:
ICYMI: Murray Leads WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee led Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.

For the first time, on August 1, the National Weather Service upgraded a Red Flag Warning for fire weather conditions to a Particularly Dangerous Situation, which is very rare and typically reserved for extreme fire weather conditions. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead. The Spokane Complex Fires forced 67,000 people to evacuate, burned nearly 10,000 acres, with damages predicted to exceed $1 billion.

This was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and threatening lives, property, businesses, and livestock. In Okanogan County, the Kaiser Canyon, Modrite, and Sinlahekin fires burned over 350,000 acres total.

“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” Senator Murray and other members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”

Joining Senator Murray in the letter to President Trump were Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), and U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Kim Schrier (D, WA-08), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).

The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”

“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Mr. President:

As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible.

Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.

Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.

An initial damage assessment revealed that the state sustained an estimated $133.7 million in damages across eleven counties and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. In Spokane County, the Spokane Complex Fires, which burned nearly 10,000 acres, severely damaged electrical distribution systems, public water systems, transportation infrastructure, municipal equipment, public lands, and solid-waste infrastructure, resulting in over $70 million in damages.

These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe.

We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter.
