title: Sen. Rick Scott Urges Floridians to Make a Plan, Prepare for Life-Threatening Storm Surge Following Hurricane Isaias Briefing
text:
PENSACOLA, Fla. – Today, U.S. Senator Rick Scott received a briefing at the Port of Pensacola from local and state leaders, law enforcement, and emergency management officials in Pensacola ahead of Hurricane Isaias’s expected landfall along the northern Gulf Coast tomorrow evening. Following the briefing, Senator Scott urged Floridians in the Panhandle to take immediate action to prepare for Hurricane Isaias, heed evacuation orders and instructions from local officials, make a disaster plan and gather necessary supplies.

Senator Scott was joined by Congressman Jimmy Patronis, Florida State Representative Alex Andrade, Florida State Representative Michelle Salzman, Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons, Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves, Escambia County Public Safety Director Eric Gilmore, Pensacola Police Chief Eric Winstrom, and other local officials.

Senator Rick Scott said, “Hurricane Isaias will be a big and serious storm. Do not underestimate it or ignore it. I talked with President Trump yesterday and we’ll be making sure the federal government shows up so Florida can fully recover from this storm – but first we need every person to do their part to stay alive. We’re expecting landfall late Friday night or very early on Saturday morning. We could see up to 10 inches of rain, there’s a big risk of tornados, and we’re expecting 5-7 feet of storm surge across the Emerald Coast and Big Bend. You cannot survive 5 to 7 feet of storm surge – IT WILL KILL YOU.

“Nobody in our state needs to die during a storm or after a storm. So, the biggest thing is you’ve got to take charge of your life. That means you have to decide to evacuate TODAY. We’ve got great first responders: the Sheriff’s office, the police, fire and rescue – they all want to take care of you. But they can’t come out in the middle of a storm. If you’re in an evacuation zone get out and get to a shelter. It’s not worth risking your life. I always say you can rebuild that house, but you can’t rebuild your life. Be safe, make a plan at ready.gov, and listen to local officials. We will get through this together.”

title: Rosen, Cortez Masto Secure Over $2.4 Million for Nevada Law Enforcement Projects
text:
LAS VEGAS, NV – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) secured $2,422,000 in grants for law enforcement projects. The funding comes from the Department of Justice’s Byrne JAG Grant Program and will be distributed to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the City of Henderson, and the Nevada Department of Public Safety.

“Our law enforcement officers work around the clock to keep Nevadans safe, and I’m committed to supporting them in any way I can,” said Senator Jacky Rosen. “I am proud to have helped secure this funding for law enforcement agencies across our state to ensure that they have the equipment and training they need to keep us safe.”

“Local law enforcement is the backbone of public safety in Nevada, but too often our officers are being asked to do more with less,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “From improving training to modernizing equipment, this critical funding will support police officers from Reno to Henderson. I’ll never stop working to deliver for local law enforcement and ensure all Nevadans feel safe in their communities.”

Three grants constitute the $2,422,000 in funding:

$1,031,000 for the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department’s (LVMPD) Air Support Equipment Enhancement Project. This funding will be used to modernize essential air support equipment to improve the Department’s airborne law enforcement, search and rescue, and emergency response operations. This grant is on top of $1 million in federal funding the Senators secured for LVMPD’s Air Support Unit earlier this year.

$1,031,000 for the City of Henderson to support law enforcement responses to and prosecutions of nonfatal strangulation cases, increase the local forensic examination capacity, and improve protective and medical services to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault.

$360,000 for the Nevada Department of Public Safety for new law enforcement training technology for departments throughout the state.

Senator Rosen has been a champion for Nevada’s law enforcement. She has secured millions of federal dollars for Nevada law enforcement, including $1 million earlier this year for the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department to acquire equipment to support their flight operations. Senator Rosen also joined Senator Cortez Masto in introducing legislation to redirect excessive ICE funding toward local law enforcement. At the beginning of this year, a Rosen-backed bipartisan bill to ensure access to federal benefits for the families of first responders who pass away or become permanently disabled from service-related cancers was signed into law.

title: Senators Rosen & Lankford, Representative Bell Call for Defense Bill to Keep Provision Requiring Consistent Hate Symbol Policy Across Military Branches
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and James Lankford (R-OK), co-founders and co-chairs of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, and Representative Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) called on the Senate and House Armed Services Committees to retain a provision in the final 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) requiring the Department of Defense to establish a single, department-wide policy on hate symbols. Existing hate symbol policies vary across branches of military service, creating inconsistent standards and potential enforcement gaps when it comes to addressing the display of hateful imagery, including swastikas and nooses. As a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Rosen secured the provision in the Senate version of the annual defense bill.

“This lack of uniformity makes it harder to prevent, identify, and address symbols that promote hate, and can even allow displays to go unaddressed depending on branch-specific rules,” wrote the lawmakers. “These symbols include swastikas and nooses, potent symbols of hate that have long been used to intimidate, harass, and discriminate against Jewish and Black communities.”

“When symbols associated with violent extremism, racial supremacy, or targeted intimidation appear in military workplaces, they undermine unit cohesion, erode morale, and threaten the good order and discipline upon which military readiness depends,” they continued. “Our bipartisan provision, incorporated in both the Senate and House FY27 NDAAs, provides a practical path forward. By requiring the DoD to establish clear, context-based standards, update guidance for commanders and investigators, and provide training to the force, the provision will ensure that there are consistent definitions, enforcement, and accountability across components.”

Read the full letter HERE.

As the third Jewish woman to ever serve in the U.S. Senate, Senator Rosen has been a leader in fighting antisemitism and hate. Last year, she, along with Senator Lankford, successfully pushed the U.S. Coast Guard to reverse its decision to no longer prohibit or classify swastikas and nooses as symbols whose display constituted “potential hate incidents.” The bipartisan pair also demanded additional answers from the Coast Guard about changes regarding the investigative process for the display of such symbols.

title: STATEMENT: Sen. Schiff on the Return of the USS Abraham Lincoln to San Diego after 321 Days of Deployment
text:
Schiff: “This war must end. Not just for the sake of the higher costs this war has imposed on the American people, but for the sake of those servicemembers who have paid an even higher price. Those who have been asked to miss holidays, birthdays, births and weddings for nearly a year in order to sustain this war of choice.”

San Diego, CA — Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) issued the following statement on the return to port of the USS Abraham Lincoln, which was deployed to the Middle East for more than 300 days during the ongoing Iran War:

“321 days. That’s how long the USS Abraham Lincoln and its thousands of servicemembers have been away from their families and their home port of San Diego. And today, for the first time in 10 months, they return home. They hug loved ones. They sleep out of harm’s way.

“In the time these men and women were deployed as the tip of the spear in the Iran War, they worked tirelessly. And that service took a heavy toll – a price we have come to know through harrowing stories shared by family members and even the military’s own leadership. The crew of the Abraham Lincoln has faced long and grueling shifts, diminished supplies and even mental health crises. Those burdens of such a long deployment have been shouldered by the crew and their families back in San Diego.

“As we welcome them home today, and we hear more of those stories of hardship and sacrifice, I hope these heavy burdens resonate through the halls of the White House and the Pentagon. With no clear objective and no measurable progress, this war must end. Not just for the sake of the higher costs this war has imposed on the American people, but for the sake of those servicemembers who have paid an even higher price. Those who have been asked to miss holidays, birthdays, births and weddings for nearly a year in order to sustain this war of choice.

“Only last week, the USS Theodore Roosevelt and its carrier strike group left San Diego. All signs point to its crew being relief for a beleaguered force still deployed in the Middle East. I hope for the sake of our sailors, Marines, soldiers and airmen that this new deployment of Californians does not repeat the hardships of the Abraham Lincoln.”

Background: Senator Adam Schiff has pushed the Department of Defense on the Abraham Lincoln’s prolonged time away from its home port of San Diego. In August, he joined Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representatives Scott Peters (D-Calif.-50), Juan Vargas (D-Calif.-52), Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49), and Sara Jacobs (D-Calif.-51) in a letter to the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General seeking more information regarding Carrier Strike Group 3’s deployment.

Schiff also recently highlighted constituent stories from servicemembers’ families on the Senate Floor, emphasizing how the prolonged deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln has sent shockwaves throughout the San Diego community as he continued his call for an end to the Iran War.

title: In New Video, Shaheen Underscores Nationwide Impact of INSULIN Act, Highlights That Most States Do Not Cap Monthly Insulin Costs at $35
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Co-Chair of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus, today released a new video highlighting the importance of passing her INSULIN Act and revealing that 27 states currently do not have a $35 cap on monthly insulin costs. Shaheen then underscores that passage of her bill is a step Congress could take to immediately lower health care costs and protect Americans, regardless of the state they live in, from being forced to pay thousands of dollars a year for their life-saving insulin.

Click HERE to watch the full video.

Key Quotes from Senator Shaheen:

“In the richest nation on Earth, no American should have to choose between affording groceries for their families or the insulin they need to survive. Unfortunately, as I’ve heard from too many students, families and health care providers […] this is happening every day.”

“While some states have already taken steps to cap insulin costs at $35 or less, most haven’t. That means Americans in states such as South Dakota, Wyoming and Pennsylvania could be forced to pay thousands of dollars a year for the insulin they need to stay alive.”

“Diabetes is a condition that touches the lives of so many Americans across the country, and the state you live in shouldn’t determine whether you can afford your life-saving insulin.”

Shaheen’s bipartisan Improving Needed Safeguards for Users of Lifesaving Insulin Now (INSULIN) Act would cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 a month for Americans with insurance, expanding the effective price cap for Americans on Medicare. Shaheen has championed efforts to lower insulin costs throughout her time in office, and the bill is closer than ever before to passing out of the U.S. Senate. In July, the INSULIN Act advanced out of the U.S. Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and in September companion legislation was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives. Shaheen’s newest video comes as lawmakers on both sides of the aisle continue to point to the INSULIN Act as an immediate step Congress can take to lower costs for millions.

Senator Shaheen has worked tirelessly to lower health care costs for Granite Staters and Americans. As co-chair of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus, Senator Shaheen has consistently pressed to hold insulin manufacturers, insurers and pharmacy benefit managers accountable for the skyrocketing cost of life-saving insulin and otherwise support patients and families facing diabetes. Polling released from the American Diabetes Association this summer found that 40% of respondents who rely on insulin report paying more than $150 per month for insulin, and 76% of respondents across political parties support a $35 limit on cost sharing for insulin.

title: Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Highlight $300,000 in Federal Funding to Support Opportunities for Baltimore’s Refugee, Immigrant Communities
text:

title: Welch Urges IRS to Prevent Big Tech from Abusing Tax Credits to Construct AI Data Centers, Protect Americans from Higher Energy Costs
text:
Welch: “The IRS has a responsibility to ensure tax credits are being claimed as intended by Congress.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Member of the Senate Finance Committee and the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, this week urged the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to ensure that Big Tech companies are not using the research and experimentation (R&E) tax credit to subsidize the construction of Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers. In his letter to IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, Senator Welch raised concerns that Big Tech companies are abusing the R&E tax credit at the expense of the American people.

“Congress’ intent in establishing the R&E credit was to support private investment in nascent

technologies that have uncertain commercial viability in the future. Congress structured the R&E credit to be incremental, designed to reward new research spending and to limit the cost to taxpayers. Instead, its reported use by major technology companies raises concerns that the credit is being used not to support new research, but to subsidize the physical infrastructure needed to build AI data centers,” wrote Senator Welch.

According to recent public reports, Meta used the R&E credit to cut its federal tax bill by nearly $4 billion in 2025 alone. Meta reportedly claimed this credit on thousands of acres of data center development to train and further develop its network of computer chips—a process that is now widespread across the technology industry and tied to some of the most profitable businesses in the world. Meta itself acknowledged the potential for IRS to deny the R&E credit, disclosing in last year’s annual report billions in “unrecognized tax benefits” that could become additional tax liability if challenged by the IRS. Meta is not alone in this practice, as other major technology companies have similarly used the R&E credit in connection with the development of AI infrastructure and data centers.

“In 2025, Meta paid an effective federal income tax rate of just 3.5%—roughly one-sixth of the 21% statutory corporate rate. That same year, the company earned a record $79 billion in U.S. income,” the Senator continued. “Meanwhile, Americans are bearing the direct costs of rapid data center expansion, including rising electricity bills and added strain on local infrastructure. This summer, our national debt surpassed $40 trillion. The most recent IRS tax gap estimate puts the gross shortfall at $700 billion for tax year 2022, while the next update has yet to be released,” the Senator continued.

Senator Welch concluded: “The IRS has a responsibility to ensure tax credits are being claimed as intended by Congress. Holding large technology companies accountable to their tax obligations is a straightforward step toward ensuring that every company pays its fair share.”

Senator Welch requested answers to the following questions by October 26, 2026:

Please provide a list of companies that claimed the R&E tax credit for expenses related to AI data centers in filing years 2020 to 2025.

What was the value of each tax credit issued in filing years 2020 to 2025 broken down by the company that claimed each?

On average, how many full-time equivalent (FTE) IRS employees are dedicated to reviewing and examining R&E tax credit claims annually?

How many enforcement actions did the IRS initiate related to the R&E tax credit for filing years 2020 to 2025?

Will the IRS pursue updated guidance or rulemaking to ensure that the R&E credit is used only for its intended purpose?

Read and download Senator Welch’s full letter to IRS CEO Bisignano.

title: Whitehouse Introduces Bicameral Bill Creating Alert System to Notify Survivors of Illegal Gun Purchase Attempts by Domestic Abusers
text:
Bicameral Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure domestic violence survivors are notified when an abusive partner is trying to obtain a firearm illegally

Providence, RI – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) has introduced the Domestic Violence Survivors Alerted for Emergency (SAFE) Notice Act, new legislation to establish notification systems that would alert survivors of domestic violence offenses when their domestic abuser attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Loopholes in federal and state law can allow domestic violence offenders to purchase guns notwithstanding their criminal history – situations that can be life threatening for survivors. Even when offenders are unsuccessful, the fact they are trying to purchase a firearm illegally can be a warning sign for survivors. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help keep survivors safe by setting up systems to notify domestic violence survivors when an abusive partner has obtained or is trying to obtain a firearm illegally.

“I spent years prosecuting domestic violence cases in Rhode Island, and I know the toll it can take on survivors as they rebuild their lives. This legislation will help ensure survivors are made aware when the government has information about an abuser’s attempt to buy a firearm, so survivors and their loved ones can make decisions in the interest of their own safety and wellbeing,” said Senator Whitehouse, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee and former Rhode Island Attorney General and U.S. Attorney.

Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI) led the introduction of legislation in the House of Representatives. The legislation is also cosponsored by Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act has been endorsed by the Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence, Sojourner House, Family Service of Rhode Island, Women’s Resource Center RI, Day One, and the Rhode Island Office of the Attorney General.

“Keeping victims safe at every stage of the justice process is a top priority for my Office,” said Rhode Island Attorney General Peter F. Neronha. “With the support of our federal partners, we are continuing to expand the resources available to victims to ensure they remained informed of updates to case information in real time. When convicted perpetrators of domestic violence try to get their hands on a firearm, they demonstrate a consistent willingness to break the law, which poses a real risk to survivors. This legislation is an investment in the safety of survivors, and we would happily welcome this vital resource.”

“When a person who uses violence to gain power and control over their family has access to a gun, the results are too often tragic. Women in abusive relationships are five times more likely to be murdered by their partners when that partner can access a firearm. Even the threat of using a gun is a terrifying coercive control tactic often used by abusers. We are thankful that Rhode Island’s Senator Whitehouse, along with Representative Dingell in the U.S. House, have sponsored this legislation to close lethal loopholes faced by survivors of intimate partner abuse who are threatened with gun violence,” said Lucy Rios, Executive Director of the Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence.

“Leaving an abusive relationship doesn’t always end a dangerous situation. At Sojourner House, we help survivors rebuild their lives while navigating ongoing threats to their safety. Knowing that an abuser has attempted to purchase a firearm illegally could give a survivor critical time to update a safety plan, connect with an advocate, and protect themselves and their children. We thank Senator Whitehouse and Congresswoman Dingell for advancing legislation that recognizes survivors’ right to information that could help them save their lives,” said Vanessa Volz, President and CEO of Sojourner House in Rhode Island.

“Every survivor deserves to feel safe, be heard, and have the support to rebuild their life with dignity. When an offender tries to obtain a firearm illegally, timely information can give survivors a critical opportunity to seek support and safety while making informed decisions for themselves and their children. The responsibility for stopping violence must never rest on survivors alone. We thank Senator Whitehouse and Congresswoman Dingell for advancing legislation that puts survivors’ safety and choices at the center,” said Margaret Holland McDuff, Chief Executive Officer of Family Service of Rhode Island.

“We are incredibly grateful to Senator Whitehouse and Congresswoman Dingell for introducing this important piece of legislation that will provide a peace of mind for survivors of domestic violence all across the country. We know that the presence of a firearm during a domestic violence assault significantly increases the chance of lethality. Of the 26 domestic violence homicides that occurred in RI between 2016 and 2020, 42% involved a firearm. This legislation will prevent future tragedies and save countless lives,” said Jessica Walsh, Executive Director of Women’s Resource Center RI.

“The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act is an important step in promoting increased safety for survivors of interpersonal violence. This legislation offering notification and information will assist survivors in their own personal safety planning. Senator Whitehouse continues to be at the forefront promoting protections and legislation for survivors. Day One is grateful for the Senator’s leadership on this matter and looks forward to continued partnership on these critical services and protections for survivors,” said Michelle Loranger, Executive Director of Day One.

Domestic violence offenders and protective order respondents are generally prohibited under federal and many state laws from purchasing firearms. However, that prohibition does not always stop offenders from trying to purchase firearms anyway. FBI data shows that almost 160,000 gun purchases were denied from 2018 to 2023 because of the purchaser’s domestic violence background. These situations can be life threatening for domestic violence survivors. A male abusive partner’s access to a gun significantly increases the risk of an intimate partner homicide.

Specifically, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would:

Direct the FBI to establish a notification system to alert survivors of federal domestic violence offenses when the offender attempts to purchase a firearm illegally.

Permit survivors to register or de-register at will.

Provide key alerts about an offender’s attempted illegal firearm purchase, including if the sale went through or law enforcement has recovered the firearm.

Provide additional alerts about related events, such as a pardon that restores an offender’s ability to purchase firearms legally.

Authorize grants for states to pilot state-run alert systems, so survivors can receive alerts related to protective orders and non-federal domestic violence offenses.

Enable states to use funds to expand existing systems or set up new ones.

Require reports on the success of and challenges related to these pilot projects, including recommendations for expanding the projects to other states.

title: Wyden, Merkley Announce More Than $1 Million to Support Addiction and Recovery Services in Eastern Oregon
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today announced more than $1 million in federal awards to help combat the opioid epidemic and to support addiction and recovery services in Eastern Oregon.

“The opioid epidemic continues to harm communities across the state, especially in rural areas that often have limited addiction treatment resources,” Wyden said. “I applaud this federal award to the Oregon Washington Health Network that will strengthen addiction and recovery services for Eastern Oregonians, and I will continue to fight for every possible resource to support mental health services and combat the opioid epidemic across Oregon.”

“I have heard heart-wrenching stories from Oregonians who have lost loved ones after a prescription for an injury or treatment turned into an addiction,” said Merkley. “Communities need access to addiction and treatment services, and this critical support will help Pendleton improve access to critical services for opioid use disorder.”

The $1.05 million in federal awards from Health Resources and Services Administration’s Rural Communities Opioid Response Program will be distributed to The Oregon Washington Health Network, a non-profit based in Pendleton dedicated to health equity in Umatilla, Union, and Morrow counties in Oregon, and Walla Walla County in Washington. The award will be used to improve access to treatment and recovery services for substance use disorder and opioid use disorder.

title: Rep. Houlahan Statement on Sec. Hegseth Announcing Execution of Fort Hood Shooter Will Be Livestreamed
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representative Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), shared the following statement on Secretary Hegseth's announcement that the execution of the Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed:

"Nidal Hasan is a murderer and terrorist who will face justice as determined by the unanimous verdict of a jury, in accordance with the principles of due process that our democracy is built on.

What did the jury not have a say in? Livestreaming the execution for the public to see. The U.S. hasn’t held a public execution in over a century, and with good reason. I urge Secretary Hegseth to reconsider this decision and to treat justice for this heinous act with the seriousness it requires."

title: Houlahan, Smith Respond to Inaccurate Casualty Reporting, Lack of Transparency on Human Cost of Trump's War
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – House Military Personnel Subcommittee Ranking Member Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) and Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Adam Smith (WA-09) released the following statement responding to the Department of Defense announcing publicly that it had miscounted the number of U.S. service members who have died in the Central Command Area of Responsibility as part of Operation Epic Fury and other Overseas Operations.

“Today’s public correction in the number of U.S. service members who have died in the Middle East since President Trump launched his disastrous war of choice against Iran was the direct result of congressional oversight. Specifically, this committee discovered a discrepancy in the Pentagon’s reporting of casualty numbers, brought it to the Trump Administration’s attention, and worked to ensure they publicly corrected this incredibly important record.

“There is no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude. While we take seriously our duty to serve as the voice of the American people and hold the executive branch accountable as a co-equal branch of government, requiring Congress to step in to rectify such an egregious error is an embarrassment for the Department. The failure of Secretary Hegseth to immediately take ownership of the problem also does a grave disservice to the men and women putting their lives on the line in service to our country.

“We are glad to see the error has been corrected, and we will continue to fight for transparency and accountability. While this public correction is an important first step, we expect the Department to make the necessary changes to policies and procedures to ensure this mistake is not repeated and that they are more transparent with the public going forward.”

--end--

title: Smith, Budzinski Lead Letter Urging the Admin to Support America’s Biofuel Industry
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE) and Nikki Budzinski (D-IL), led a bipartisan letter with 37 of their colleagues to U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin and U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright urging the administration to maintain its commitments to America’s biofuel industry.

In the letter, the lawmakers ask the administration to uphold its commitment to American grown energy by proposing a supplemental rule that preserves the integrity of the Renewable Fuel Standard’s (RFS) biofuel volume requirements for 2026 and 2027 by October 16, 2026. They warn that delays would undermine much-needed market certainty for American farmers and biofuel producers while putting savings at the pump for American families at risk.

The lawmakers write: "The stakes for our constituents could not be higher. Biofuel demand keeps commodity prices competitive for farmers, sustains tens of thousands of rural manufacturing jobs, and delivers measurable savings at the pump for working families. E15 saves drivers an average of 30 cents per gallon compared to E10. B20 biodiesel runs approximately 11 cents cheaper than regular diesel. The 2026 and 2027 volumes in Set 2 were built to capture these cost-savings at scale, but SREs alongside a flawed reallocation approach would erase them."

In addition to Smith and Budzinski, the letter was signed by U.S. Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS), Ashley Hinson (R-IA), Emmanuel Cleaver (D-MO), Angie Craig (D-MN), Ann Wagner (R-MO), Eric Sorensen (D-IL), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA), Randy Feenstra (R-IA), Zach Nunn (R-IA), Brad Finstad (R-MN), Darin LaHood (R-IL), Jim Baird (R-IN), Michelle Fischbach (R-MN), Mike Bost (R-IL), Robin Kelly (D-IL), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Kristen McDonald Rivert (D-MI), Mary Miller (R-IL), Wesley Bell (D-MO), Derrick Van Orden (R-WI), Mark Alford (R-MO), James Comer (R-KY), Jonathan Jackson (D-IL), John Rose (R-TN), Derek Schmidt (R-KS), Don Bacon (R-NE), Lauren Underwood (D-IL), Dusty Johnson (R-S.D.), Mark Messmer (R-IN), Rudy Yakym (R-IN), Shontel Brown (D-OH), Mark Pocan (D-WI), Mike Flood (R-NE), Haley Stevens (D-MI), Max Miller (R-OH), Julie Fedorchak (R-N.D.), and Donald Davis (D-N.C.).

Read the full letter here or below:

Administrator Zeldin and Secretary Wright:

The Set 2 Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs) are the strongest in the history of the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS), supporting a much-needed market for American farmers, feedstock processors, biofuel producers, and rural economies. Our constituents responded to that call to action with investment, expansion, and hiring across the biofuels value chain. Further, the administration’s commitment to reallocate the waived Small Refinery Exemption (SRE) volumes announced on August 31, 2026, reinforced this market signal.

We write today to urge swift action to propose a supplemental rule by October 16th which ensures obligated volumes are in line with those announced under Set 2 for compliance years 2026 and 2027. Until the supplemental rule process is complete, the market will not be able to fully respond, putting the momentum of the Set 2 RVO, and the lower fuel prices that homegrown biofuels provide for American families, at risk.

The stakes for our constituents could not be higher. Biofuel demand keeps commodity prices competitive for farmers, sustains tens of thousands of rural manufacturing jobs, and delivers measurable savings at the pump for working families. E15 saves drivers an average of 30 cents per gallon compared to E10. B20 biodiesel runs approximately 11 cents cheaper than regular diesel. The 2026 and 2027 volumes in Set 2 were built to capture these cost-savings at scale, but SREs alongside a flawed reallocation approach would erase them.

Now more than ever, our biofuels policy must deliver certainty for American farmers, feedstock processors, biofuels producers, and consumers. We stand ready to work with you in implementing a supplemental rule which is consistent with Set 2 projections, and encourage you to ensure that DOE conducts meaningful, transparent engagement with biofuel stakeholders on any methodology change for adjudicating future SREs.

title: Ansari Celebrates Los Abogados’ 50th Anniversary with Congressional Record Recognition
text:
PHOENIX – In honor of Hispanic Heritage Month, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) celebrated the 50th anniversary of Los Abogados, Arizona’s Hispanic Bar Association, with a Congressional Record recognition honoring the organization’s five decades of service, advocacy, leadership, and commitment to expanding opportunity within Arizona’s legal community.

“It is an honor to recognize Los Abogados and the incredible work they have done to build community, create opportunities, and advance the interests of Arizona’s Latino communities,” said Rep. Ansari. “At a time when we are seeing fundamental rights come under attack this work is more important than ever. I will continue fighting in Congress to protect Arizonans’ rights and conducting oversight to ensure accountability and equal justice.”

The celebration hosted at Univision Studios in Phoenix featured the unveiling of a commemorative 50th Anniversary artwork by Los Abogados’ Artist of the Year, Michael Padilla, and a panel moderated by Congresswoman Ansari with Danny Ortega, Marian Zapata-Rossa, and Salvador Macias on the organization’s history, impact, and future.

READ TEXT OF ANSARI’S CONGRESSIONAL RECORD

Mister Speaker, I rise today to honor the 50th anniversary of Los Abogados, Arizona’s Hispanic Bar Association.

Founded in 1976 by Latino lawyers and law students, Los Abogados has spent five decades building community, creating opportunities, and advancing the interests of Arizona’s Latino communities within the legal profession and beyond.

Today, Latinos comprise only approximately roughly 5% to 6% of all licensed lawyers in the United States. Through programming, mentorship, leadership development, and community engagement, Los Abogados works to address the systemic and cultural barriers that Latinos continue to encounter throughout their legal careers.

For 50 years, Los Abogados has remained steadfast in its commitment to diversity and inclusion, advocacy, and education. The Hispanic Bar Association actively promotes diversity within Arizona’s legal and judicial professions. Supporting Latino lawyers and expanding their representation is essential to narrowing the significant representation gap and ensuring that our legal system better reflects the communities it serves.

Los Abogados’ Civil Rights Committee supports the equitable and just application of civil rights, advocating for Arizona’s Latino communities. The committee organizes “Continuing Legal Education” seminars to update legal professionals about current voting rights, civic engagement, and racial profiling positions. Additionally, Los Abogados hosts citizenship fairs, providing essential immigration resources and assistance to Arizonans.

As we commemorate this important milestone, we recognize Los Abogados for 50 years of service, advocacy, and leadership. I congratulate its members, past and present, and commend their enduring commitment to strengthening Arizona’s legal community and ensuring greater access, representation, and opportunity for all.

On behalf of the United States Congress, I extend my deepest gratitude and congratulations to Los Abogados on their 50th Anniversary.

###

title: Barrett Introduces Legislation to Address Growing Threats from Artificial Intelligence, Other Emerging Technology
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) formally introduced the Artificial Intelligence Governance and Emerging Threats Act to address AI threats and increase accountability in light of warnings from AI researchers about the risks associated with this rapidly developing technology that companies are further advancing by the day.

Specifically, the legislation would create the U.S. Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats, which would be led by a representative presidentially appointed and Senate-confirmed to serve in the president’s Cabinet. The mission of the office would be to spearhead development and implementation of federal policy on AI and other technological risks.

“The United States government has a fundamental responsibility to protect its citizens from all threats, including those we might not see coming. The rapid development of AI technology, which has potential to improve our society, has exposed the serious dangers that can come with it,” said Barrett. “We are already seeing it replace American jobs, threaten our national security, and degrade human dignity. These risks cannot be ignored, so it’s time to create a seat at the table for someone to monitor AI technology, ensure strong guardrails are in place, and prepare us for this new era of technological innovation and beyond.”

The representative in charge of the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats would serve as the principal adviser to the president on AI and emerging technological threats; coordinate among federal departments to ensure a cohesive federal approach to AI; and monitor risks and opportunities related to AI and other technologies. The representative would also be required to testify regularly before Congress on AI developments and threats.

The Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats would be housed within the Executive Office of the President. In addition to the representative, the office would have five Senate-confirmed deputy representatives to spearhead specific responsibilities:

Deputy representative for intergovernmental coordination;

Deputy representative for international engagement;

Deputy representative for private sector engagement;

Deputy representative for national security and emerging technology threats; and

Deputy representative for economic and workforce impacts.

The Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats is patterned after the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which coordinates among federal intelligence agencies and also traditionally has a seat in the president’s Cabinet.

Background

Barrett has been a leader on increasing accountability and transparency for artificial intelligence and data centers. Last week, he wrote a letter calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio and U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz to work with other nations to negotiate a treaty setting international guardrails on AI. In addition to his call for international collaboration, Barrett has introduced or co-sponsored the following bills in Congress:

The Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act (H.R. 9729) to ensure that no autonomous or artificial intelligence-enabled weapon system used by the United States military can carry out an intentionally lethal strike without meaningful human oversight or a human decision-maker in the loop.

The Children Harmed by AI Technology (CHAT) Act (H.R. 7218) to require AI chatbots to implement age verification measures to protect minors. The bill requires parental consent for minors using chatbots, bans chatbots from engaging in sexually explicit communications with minors, and requires chatbots to notify a minor’s parent if the minor’s chat shows signs of suicidal ideation.

The AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (H.R. 9965) to test advanced AI systems to prevent risks to nuclear safety.

The Doctors Not AI Act (H.R. 10210), introduced by Barrett and Landsman, to ensure that artificial intelligence cannot make or dictate health insurance coverage decisions involving medical judgment.

The VA Claims AI Accountability Act (H.R. 10418) to require VA employees — not AI — to make the final decisions for approval of disability claims or benefits. The bill also strengthens oversight and accountability for the VA’s digital benefits system.

The VA AI Transparency Act (H.R. 10417) to require the VA to disclose to every veteran any use of AI by the VA, including in claims processing and customer service chats.

The Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (H.R. 10119) to prohibit federal agencies from overriding local land-use, zoning, siting, or permitting authority related to data centers.

The No Data Center NDAs Act (H.R. 10118) to prohibit members of Congress from signing non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) about data centers, including any information about possible locations or how much water or energy a facility is expected to consume.

The No Secrets for Data Centers Act (H.R. 10570) to prohibit and invalidate NDAs signed by federal, state, and local government officials to conceal details of data center projects. The bill would also prohibit data center operators from receiving government incentives if the conditions include entering an agreement to keep information about the project confidential.

title: Congressman Bell Calls for Greater Accountability in Local ICE Enforcement Practices
text:
St. Louis, Missouri – Today, Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) issued the following statement on the need for greater accountability and humane treatment in the practices of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"Consistent with opposing any expansion of ICE’s involvement in local policing, I support local law-enforcement agencies reviewing their 287(g) agreements and considering whether continued participation aligns with community safety, public trust, and the appropriate use of local resources. I also recognize that decisions regarding these agreements must be addressed by the appropriate governing authorities.

I support accountability regarding ICE’s involvement in local policing and encourage the appropriate authorities to review the 287(g) agreements. Any request to rescind these agreements should be directed to the officials or governing bodies with the legal authority to make that decision.”

title: Congressman Bell, Senators Rosen & Lankford Call for Defense Bill to Keep Provision Requiring Consistent Hate Symbol Policy Across Military Branches
text:
The bipartisan provision, already in both the House and Senate bills, would require one department-wide standard for swastikas, nooses, and other symbols of hate

Congressman Bell, a member of the House Armed Services Committee, worked to secure the provision in the House version of the defense bill

Bell also serves on the Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism

ICYMI from Jewish Insider: Lawmakers call for Congress to mandate creation of Pentagon hate symbols policy

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, and Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and James Lankford (R-OK) called for the Senate and House Armed Services Committees to retain a provision in the final 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) requiring the Department of Defense to establish a single, department-wide policy on hate symbols.

Existing hate symbol policies vary across branches of military service, creating inconsistent standards and potential enforcement gaps when it comes to addressing the display of hateful imagery, including swastikas and nooses.

As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, Bell worked to secure the provision in the House version of the annual defense bill.

“This lack of uniformity makes it harder to prevent, identify, and address symbols that promote hate, and can even allow displays to go unaddressed depending on branch-specific rules,” wrote the lawmakers. “These symbols include swastikas and nooses, potent symbols of hate that have long been used to intimidate, harass, and discriminate against Jewish and Black communities.”

“When symbols associated with violent extremism, racial supremacy, or targeted intimidation appear in military workplaces, they undermine unit cohesion, erode morale, and threaten the good order and discipline upon which military readiness depends,” they continued. “Our bipartisan provision, incorporated in both the Senate and House FY27 NDAAs, provides a practical path forward. By requiring the DoD to establish clear, context-based standards, update guidance for commanders and investigators, and provide training to the force, the provision will ensure that there are consistent definitions, enforcement, and accountability across components.”

Bell has a record of bipartisan work against hate and extremism. In June 2025, he and Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE-02) led a letter urging social media companies to act against hate speech. Rep. Bell serves on the Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism and is a member of the House Armed Services Committee.

The full letter text can be found HERE and below:

“Dear Chairmen Wicker and Rogers, and Ranking Members Reed and Smith:

We write in support of a critical, bipartisan provision adopted in both the House and Senate Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to require the Department of Defense (DoD) to establish a single, department-wide hate symbol policy applicable to all servicemembers and DoD civilian employees. As you continue negotiations for the FY 2027 NDAA, we strongly urge you to retain this important bipartisan provision in the final bill.

Existing DoD hate symbol policies vary across our military service branches, creating inconsistent standards and potential enforcement gaps when it comes to addressing their display. This lack of uniformity makes it harder to prevent, identify, and address symbols that promote hate, and can even allow displays to go unaddressed depending on branch-specific rules. These symbols include swastikas and nooses, potent symbols of hate that have long been used to intimidate, harass, and discriminate against Jewish and Black communities. Just last year, the US Coast Guard (USCG) was planning on implementing a policy to reclassify symbols such as the swastika and noose as “potentially divisive” symbols rather than as hate symbols. Such a change would have allowed these horrific symbols of hate to potentially be displayed in official Coast Guard workplaces and during the performance of official Coast Guard duties. It was only after repeated bipartisan pushback from Members of Congress on USCG and Department of Homeland Security leadership that this change in policy was ultimately reversed.

The swastika is not potentially divisive. It is one of the most universally recognized symbols of hatred in human history. It represents antisemitism, racial supremacy, violent extremism, and the systematic persecution and murder of millions. The noose is not potentially divisive. It is a symbol of racial terror. It carries the legacy of lynching, intimidation, and violence used for generations to threaten Black Americans and deny them their fundamental rights and humanity. The USCG incident underscores why a consistent, uniform hate symbol policy is needed across DoD and across all the U.S. Armed Forces.

When symbols associated with violent extremism, racial supremacy, or targeted intimidation appear in military workplaces, they undermine unit cohesion, erode morale, and threaten the good order and discipline upon which military readiness depends. Our bipartisan provision, incorporated in both the Senate and House FY27 NDAAs, provides a practical path forward. By requiring the DoD to establish clear, context-based standards, update guidance for commanders and investigators, and provide training to the force, the provision will ensure that there are consistent definitions, enforcement, and accountability across components.

We ask our servicemembers to defend the Constitution and represent the very best of our country. They deserve a workplace free from symbols of intimidation, extremist affiliation, and racial or ethnic hostility. This provision helps ensure that context-based, uniform standards are clear and consistently enforced across the DoD.

We therefore strongly urge you to keep this provision in the final text of the FY27 NDAA.

Sincerely,”

###

title: Beyer Joins Call with McClain Delaney, Ocasio-Cortez, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
text:
Congressman Don Beyer (VA-08) is leading a congressional letter with co-leads Representatives April McClain Delaney, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Kweisi Mfume, Suhas Subramanyam, and Sarah Elfreth urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.

The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.

The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” said Congressman Don Beyer.

“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”

“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume.

“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”

At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.

The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.

The lawmakers request answers in three areas:

Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.

Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.

Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.

title: Congressman Biggs Applauds EPA Action to Protect Maricopa County
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA –This week, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin convened a roundtable to announce a major development regarding air quality regulations in Maricopa County.

Under a soon-to-be-finalized emissions rule, Air Quality Rule 204 (“Emissions Offsets Generated by Voluntary Nonroad Engine Emission Reductions”), industries across Maricopa County would be permitted to use emission reduction credits generated through voluntary reductions in nonroad engine emissions. The rule would provide businesses with greater flexibility to build and expand production while ensuring that overall emissions do not increase.

Congressman Andy Biggs (AZ-05) attended the roundtable and issued the following statement:

“I applaud the Trump Administration and Administrator Zeldin for continuing to reverse destructive environmental policies that threaten economic growth and opportunity in Maricopa County. Arizona—and Maricopa County specifically—is home to extraordinary economic and technological development that is improving the lives of Arizonans and Americans across the country. For years, Washington bureaucrats have ignored the fact that much of the air pollution affecting Arizona originates outside our state and beyond our control, while imposing increasingly burdensome local regulations that do little to meaningfully improve air quality. That approach threatens jobs, investment, housing, and economic opportunity without addressing the underlying problem.

“This announcement is welcome news for those of us who understand that protecting our environment and promoting economic growth are not mutually exclusive. We can pursue responsible environmental stewardship without crushing businesses and families in one of the fastest-growing regions in the nation.”

Congressman Biggs has been a leading advocate for rolling back burdensome federal regulations that threaten economic growth in Maricopa County. In February 2025, Congressman Biggs led a letter to the White House urging the Administration and EPA to prevent Maricopa County’s Clean Air Act ozone nonattainment designation from being reclassified from “moderate” to “serious.”

Approximately 80 percent of the emissions attributed to Arizona originate from natural or international sources beyond the state’s control. Congressman Biggs warned that imposing even stricter federal requirements on Arizona businesses and families would do little to address the underlying causes of the region’s air quality challenges while inflicting significant economic costs on the Valley.

In March, the EPA announced that it would not escalate Maricopa County’s ozone designation from “moderate” to “serious,” sparing Arizona families and businesses from another wave of costly and ineffective federal regulations.

This week’s announcement represents another significant step toward a more practical approach—one that allows Maricopa County to continue growing and creating jobs while pursuing meaningful emissions reductions.

title: Scott Calls on Watchdog to Investigate Whether or Not HHS Lied in Litigation
text:
As originally released by the Committee on Education and Workforce, Democrats

WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03) urged the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General to investigate HHS’s potential submission of inconsistent or fraudulent information in active litigation.

On February 6, 2025, Ranking Member Scott called on the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) to assess the security of HHS's information technology (IT) systems after reports that Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) accessed data from various government agencies. However, HHS has refused to comply with GAO’s requests, citing potential discrepancies between what was produced in litigation and would be provided to GAO.

Furthermore, during the Committee’s oversight hearing on April 17, 2026, Secretary Kennedy could not provide a clarification when questioned by Ranking Member Scott whether the Department is providing false or inaccurate information in litigation and failed to follow up with information on the matter.

“On May 17, 2026, I wrote to Secretary Kennedy to follow-up and request a detailed explanation about what the Department meant when it informed GAO that it could not cooperate or accommodate an observational walkthrough, artifacts, screenshots, and other documentation out of concern for discrepancies with what HHS produced in litigation and what it would provide to GAO, and whether HHS did provide false, incomplete, or inaccurate information in litigation.6 I have given the Department ample opportunity to respond to my requests and refute the assertion that it has provided misinformation to one or more courts and yet have received no response to date,” wrote Ranking Member Scott.

“Accordingly, given the serious nature of the allegation, I request the Office of Inspector General to initiate an investigation immediately of whether HHS has provided false, incomplete, or inaccurate information, materials, items, or other documentation in litigation since January 20, 2025.”

title: Scott, DeSaulnier Demand Answers from Trump Administration on Ability to Protect 155 Million Workers’ Benefits
text:
As originally released by the Committee on Education and Workforce, Democrats

WASHINGTON – House Committee on Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) and Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Subcommittee Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) demanded the Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA) Assistant Secretary Daniel Aronowitz share a detailed accounting of the agency’s staffing, the damage done by the Trump-Musk federal workforce cuts, and its actions to effectively enforce the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA).

ERISA governs 2.8 million health plans, 837,000 retirement plans, and 521,000 other employee benefit plans that cumulatively cover 155 million Americans. However, under the Trump Administration, EBSA has experienced chronic underfunding, reduced staff, and weakened enforcement capacity, allowing bad actors to evade accountability for harming workers’ hard-earned benefits.

“The chaotic nature of the Trump Administration’s campaign to slash the federal workforce has also obscured the exact scope and severity of the damage imposed on the Agency’s workforce. Over the last 20 months, we have had to rely on media reports and top-line figures in annual budget requests to ascertain EBSA’s capacity, which are often vague or outdated. Moreover, your responses to the Committee’s questions for the record after your appearance failed to provide any substantive information on staffing. In order for the Committee to evaluate EBSA’s ability to effectively carry out its mission, as well as to advocate for more resources, it is imperative we have a robust and up-to-date picture of the Agency’s workforce changes and composition,”wrote Ranking Members Scott and DeSaulnier.

The Ranking Members requested the agency turn over documents and information related to this request no later than October 22, 2026.

Background:

On November 18, 2025, the Ranking Members urged the Trump Administration to adequately staff EBSA to ensure it can fulfill its enormous mission and called on Secretary Aronowitz to tackle wrongful claim denials by group health plans and insurance companies and secure coverage for working people under ERISA.

title: REP. BOEBERT IN THE DENVER GAZETTE ON FIGHTING FOR WATER PROJECTS AND COLORADO’S FUTURE
text:
Lone Tree, CO — Rep. Lauren Boebert (CO-04) published a guest opinion in the Denver Gazette on the fight for drinking water, storage, and treatment in Colorado’s 4th District, and on stopping efforts that would divert South Platte water out of the state.

"Water decides whether a farm stays in the family, whether a small town can fight a fire, and whether our kids have a reason to stay. I will always fight for it,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

“Families in the southeast still drink groundwater that can carry radium and uranium. Towns on the Eastern Plains are one well failure away from a boil order. Cities along the Front Range are trying to get off nonrenewable groundwater before the wells run down,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “It gets fixed with storage, pipes, treatment plants and a spine in Washington.”

Rep. Boebert’s legislative work for Colorado water includes:

Thirteen community project requests signed into law, including $11.75 million for water projects: a Plum Creek-to-Rueter-Hess pipeline for Castle Rock; a Cobb Lake treatment plant for Severance, Windsor, Eaton, and Weld County neighbors; consolidation of the Prairie View Ranch system near Wiggins; a wastewater plant in Lamar; well redundancy in Kiowa; reverse-osmosis treatment in Brush; and upgrades in Ovid, Louviers, and Walsh

Finish the Arkansas Valley Conduit language that has passed the House twice in the last three months, aimed at 39 communities and roughly 50,000 people in Bent, Crowley, Kiowa, Otero, Prowers, and Pueblo counties who were promised clean water from Pueblo Reservoir

Opposition to the Perkins County Canal and Senate Water Resources Development Act language that would force the Army Corps of Engineers to approve a permit so Nebraska can cut through Sedgwick County and take South Platte water

“If that Senate language moves forward and the Corps is pushed to sign off, the Supreme Court won’t matter,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “The permit becomes the project. I will not trade away Sedgwick County in a permitting deadline written for another state.”

“These are not headlines. They are pipes in the ground,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “Colorado water should stay under Colorado control. Water is how Colorado works. I am never giving it up.”

title: 99 Democratic Lawmakers Slam Department of Education for Failure to Enforce Title IX and Protect Student Survivors
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) member Maxine Dexter (OR-03), DWC member Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), DWC Chair Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) and Rep. Mark Takano (CA-41) led a letter to the Office of the Inspector General at the Department of Education. The letter urges the Acting Inspector General to open an investigation into the Department’s gutting of the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) and Title IX rollbacks and its impact on the Department’s ability to enforce Title IX protections for student survivors of sexual assault and harassment. 99 House Democrats joined the effort.

The call for the investigation comes after Jane Doe’s story from Cornell University and Kendall Francis’ story from Louisiana State University (LSU) sparked a national outcry about the high rate of sexual violence on college campuses. Additionally the survivors’ stories have renewed scrutiny of how colleges and universities respond, and how the Department of Education enforces Title IX protections for survivors.

One in four undergraduate women experience sexual assault or rape while in college. Sexual violence against women on college campuses is a public health crisis, yet significant barriers remain that block accountability and protections for students. Changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities under the Trump administration have only made that worse and have undermined the Department’s ability to properly investigate complaints and enforce Title IX protections.

As of January 2025, OCR reportedly faced a backlog of nearly 12,000 civil rights cases, while the administration reduced OCR’s workforce by nearly half. The Department has closed zero college sexual harassment or sexual violence cases. The Department also formalized weaker protections and processes for student survivors: narrowing the definition of sexual harassment, reducing school liability, and implementing intimidating investigative and hearing procedures that are retraumatizing to survivors.

Without proper federal enforcement and institutional accountability, Title IX protections become just words on a page. The Department of Education is failing student survivors. Protections for survivors are not partisan and should always be a priority, however the Department’s rollback of vital protections creates additional barriers for survivors and is leaving them to fend for themselves in their most vulnerable moments.

In their letter, the members explained how the Department’s changes will leave student survivors vulnerable and why an investigation is necessary:

“We urge the Office of Inspector General to immediately open an investigation into the Department’s failure to adequately enforce Title IX protections for survivors of sexual harassment and assault, including whether changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities have undermined the Department’s ability to protect students, investigate complaints in a timely manner, and hold institutions accountable.”

The members outlined the Department’s policies that have weakened protections for student survivors:

“At the same time that OCR’s staff and regional capacity were substantially reduced, the Department announced and pursued Title IX enforcement priorities concerning transgender students’ participation in athletics and access to sex-separated facilities, and also dismantling Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) programs. These reprioritizations do nothing to address the backlog of sexual violence cases.”

The letter also explains how reprioritizations and restructuring by the Department have decreased OCR’s capacity to investigate cases of sexual violence on campus:

“This restructuring threatens to further delay investigations, erode OCR’s institutional expertise, and create additional barriers for survivors seeking accountability. These reprioritizations, staff reductions, and the interagency agreement raise significant questions about whether OCR has sufficient capacity to investigate Title IX complaints, communicate with complainants, and fulfill its civil rights enforcement responsibilities in a timely and effective manner.”

The members also outlined what they are urging the Inspector General to investigate:

Examining whether the Department has fulfilled its legal and administrative responsibilities to investigate and resolve Title IX complaints in a timely and effective manner.

The causes and consequences of the absence of resolution agreements involving college sexual harassment and assault complaints since January 2025.

Whether reductions in OCR staffing, the closure of regional offices, or changes in enforcement priorities have contributed to delays, backlogs, or failures to resolve these complaints.

Examining whether OCR has sufficient staffing, resources, policies, and procedures to effectively enforce Title IX and protect students from sex discrimination, including sexual harassment and violence.

Identifying how survivors have been harmed by these changes.

Lastly, the members asked the Inspector General to answer the following questions:

How many Title IX sexual harassment and sexual violence complaints are currently pending before OCR, and how long have they been pending?

How have processing times, case closures, investigations, and resolution agreements changed since January 2025?

Have staffing reductions or office closures affected OCR’s ability to investigate complaints or communicate with survivors?

Have Department officials directed, formally or informally, OCR personnel to deprioritize certain categories of Title IX complaints?

What safeguards are currently in place to ensure Title IX complaints involving sexual violence receive timely and appropriate review?

What corrective actions are necessary to ensure the Department is meeting its obligations to protect students under Title IX?

Read the full letter here.

title: Bresnahan, Dingell, Mann, and Frankel Introduce Legislation to Delay 340B Rebate Model, Protect Access to Affordable Medicine
text:
WASHINGTON, DC: Today, U.S. Representatives Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (PA-08), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Tracey Mann (KS-01), and Lois Frankel (FL-22) introduced the 340B Rebate Model Delay Act, bipartisan legislation to delay implementation of the federal government’s 340B rebate model, citing concerns that the new system could create significant financial and administrative risks for healthcare providers and patients.

“Patients and providers should not have to bear the risks of an untested change to a program that helps deliver affordable medicines to communities across the country,” said Rep. Bresnahan. “Congress needs more time to evaluate the potential financial and administrative consequences of the rebate model and ensure that any changes to 340B protect patients and the providers who serve them.

Under the rebate model, participating providers would pay the full price of certain prescription drugs upfront and receive the 340B discount later through rebates. This could create cash-flow pressures, increase administrative burdens, and make it more difficult for community health centers, hospitals, and other safety-net providers to maintain access to affordable medications.

“Families in Michigan are already struggling to pay for healthcare,” said Rep. Dingell. “Safety-net providers are not in the financial position to front this money, especially in light of Medicaid cuts, and will either have to hike up prices for patients or stop offering lifesaving drugs. This bill would delay the implementation of this rebate model so we can ensure people’s lives are not put at risk.”

“Rural hospitals and health care providers across the Big First District rely on the 340B program to stretch limited resources and continue providing quality care close to home,” said Rep. Mann. “The new rebate model would force these providers to pay higher upfront costs and wait to be reimbursed, putting unnecessary financial strain on facilities that already operate on tight margins. This legislation provides certainty for our rural health care providers by stopping the rebate model through 2028 and protecting their ability to serve patients in rural communities.”

“Safety-net hospitals and community health centers are lifelines for low-income families, seniors, and people without health insurance,” said Rep. Frankel. “Our bipartisan bill stops a new requirement forcing these providers to pay full price for prescription drugs and then wait for rebates. Their limited resources should go toward caring for patients, not waiting for drug companies to pay them back. We should be making it easier for people to get the medicine they need, not putting more financial strain on the hospitals and clinics they depend on.”

The 340B Drug Pricing Program allows eligible healthcare providers serving underserved communities to purchase covered outpatient drugs at discounted prices and stretch limited resources to provide care.

The 340B Rebate Model Delay Act is endorsed by Advocates for Community Health, America’s Essential Hospitals, Children’s Hospital Association, National Association of Community Health Centers, Catholic Health Association, Alliance of Safety-Net Hospitals (ASH), Health West, Hospital Association of Pennsylvania (HAP), 340B Health, American Society of Health-System Pharmacists, Ryan White Clinics for 340B Access, American Association of Medical Colleges, National Rural Health Association, Michigan Primary Care Association, Florida Association of Community Health Centers, Community Health Center Association of Mississippi, Idaho Community Health Center Association, Community Health Center Association of Connecticut, Georgia Primary Care Association, Oregon Primary Care Association, Washington Association for Community Health, and American Hospital Association.
