title: Trenton Monitor article on New Jersey March for Life'Thousands gather in Trenton for annual New Jersey March for Life'
text:
By Mary Stadnyk, Associate Editor

Published October 9, 2026

Thousands of pro-life advocates gathered at the New Jersey Statehouse Annex in Trenton Oct. 8 for the annual Rally and March for Life, calling on lawmakers to protect women and unborn children.

PHOTO GALLERY: NJ March for Life

The event brought together people of all ages, including pro-life organizations from every diocese in the state, as well as Catholic school and parish delegations. Speakers included state legislators, representatives of the National and New Jersey March for Life organizations and faith leaders, including Bishop Kevin J. Sweeney from the Paterson Diocese. The day included the added focus of supporting mothers facing difficult pregnancies.

Pro-life advocates carry signs proclaiming “Life Is a Gift” as they participate in the New Jersey March for Life in Trenton Oct. 8. The march followed the third annual Mass for Life, bringing together Catholics and other supporters from across the state to witness publicly to the dignity and value of human life.

Rep. Christopher Smith (R-NJ, 4th District), a parishioner of St. Elizabeth Ann Seton Parish, Whiting, described the March for Life as “an engraved invitation to all of us to seriously recommit and rededicate ourselves, with love and compassion, to tangibly assist women – especially through the extraordinary work of pregnancy care centers – in order to protect their precious babies and their own lives from the violence and cruelty of abortion.”

“We are a people of persevering faith in God, willing to bear any burden and endure any attack,” the congressman said. “We know that the cruel injustice of abortion need not be forever and that each day, despite setbacks, many unborn children and their mothers have, are and will be protected. We have hope. We have much work to do.”

Marie Tasy, executive director of New Jersey Right to Life, highlighted the historic significance of gathering in Trenton during the nation’s 250th anniversary year. She recalled George Washington’s victory in December 1776, which helped turn the tide of the American Revolution and renewed hope for the young nation.

“Just months earlier, our founders had proclaimed that our unalienable rights come not from government, but from our Creator, beginning with the right to life,” Tasy said.

“Today, 250 years later, we gather in that same historic city, at the doorstep of our state house, to defend that founding principle,” she said, urging participants to continue speaking out, standing firm and working to protect every human life.

Reiterating that New Jersey continues to pursue policies that expand abortion and deny meaningful protection for unborn children, Tasy emphasized the importance of elected officials hearing from the people they represent.

“The New Jersey March for Life is a powerful reminder that there is a strong and compassionate pro-life movement throughout our state who remains steadfast in our commitment to protecting mothers and their unborn,” she said.

Father James O’Neill, pastor of St. John Parish in Lakehurst and Ocean County’s Respect Life chaplain, said the annual gathering demonstrates the solidarity of New Jersey’s pro-life community.

“Even though New Jersey has several million residents, I marvel at how (it) feels like a close-knit community at the Mass for Life and Rally for Life,” he said.

Father O’Neill referred to the Rally for Life as an event that extends beyond “us Catholics to include our non-Catholic neighbors.”

title: EWTN News article featuring Smith's commentary'Transnational online scam operations on the rise, U.S. State Department says'
text:
By Amira Abuzeid

Published October 9, 2026 at 5:18 PM ET

The State Department released its 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report on Oct. 8, showing criminal organizations and repressive governments are using trafficking for profit in new ways.

The report, released more than three months after the June 30 deadline, said the spread of industrial-scale online scam operations “pose a direct threat to US national security.”

Transnational crime organizations, mostly run by Chinese nationals and long based in Southeast Asia, have moved into Africa, the Middle East, Europe, and Latin America, destabilizing local communities and cheating people out of billions of dollars each year, according to the report.

Fraudulent online romance, gambling, and cryptocurrency schemes have defrauded people in more than 125 countries, with Americans, the primary targets, losing at least $18.2 billion in 2025 to compounds operating out of Southeast Asia, according to the report.

Credit: Pungux/Shutterstock

The organizations recruited people from at least 80 countries over the past few years through fraudulent schemes, often pushing them into forced labor and holding them in guarded compounds and manipulating them through violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation, and other acts. They are often coerced into committing crimes, the report found.

The report, an annual assessment required by the Trafficking Victims Protection Act (TVPA) of 2000, covers April 1, 2025, through March 31.

The State Department said it relied on information from embassy reporting, government officials, nongovernmental and international organizations, published reports, news articles, and other sources.

The State Department said that governments that fail to punish traffickers and protect victims should be held accountable.

12 governments cited

Twelve governments are cited in the report for a “policy or pattern” of state-sponsored human trafficking: Afghanistan, Belarus, Burma, Cambodia, China, Cuba, Eritrea, Iran, North Korea, Russia, South Sudan, and Sudan. This designation covers “trafficking in government-funded programs, forced labor in government-affiliated medical services or other sectors, sexual slavery in government camps, or the employment or recruitment of child soldiers.”

Under the Child Soldiers Prevention Act, the department listed 14 countries whose forces or state-backed militias recruited or used children in any capacity during hostilities, including as sex slaves: Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Nigeria, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela, and Yemen.

Among country rankings reported so far, Israel returned to Tier 1, the highest category, for the first time since 2021, after five years on Tier 2. The Republic of Congo was downgraded to Tier 3, the lowest, for failing to meet minimum standards and not making significant efforts. A Tier 3 listing can restrict certain U.S. assistance, including security assistance, the report said.

A Tier 1 ranking does not mean that a country has no human trafficking. Instead, according to the report, “a Tier 1 ranking indicates that a government has made efforts to address the problem … and met the TVPA’s minimum standards.”

Rep. Chris Smith, R-New Jersey, author of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act, said in a statement on Oct. 8 that the report’s findings are “a stark reminder that modern-day slavery remains a global scourge — and that governments must be held accountable when they fail to protect vulnerable people.”

“Human trafficking is an assault on human dignity and freedom,” the congressman wrote. “The United States must continue to use every tool at its disposal — including the TIP Report — to expose human trafficking whenever it rears its ugly head, protect survivors, and press foreign governments to end this blight upon humanity.”

“China remains on Tier 3 — the lowest ranking,” Smith continued, “reflecting its continued failure to meet the minimum standards for eliminating trafficking. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) use and enabling of forced labor — including the systematic exploitation of Uyghurs and other persecuted minorities — is deeply troubling and deserves the greatest level of scrutiny.”

“Moreover, the horrific, ongoing consequences of China’s one-child per couple policy can still be seen and felt today, as the Report notes that a gross disparity — tens of millions more boys than girls — has driven the demand for commercial sex trafficking and coercive marriages in the country,” Smith wrote.

“Governments on Tier 3 — including China, North Korea, Iran, Russia, Burma, Belarus, Cambodia, Cuba, Laos, Nicaragua, Sudan, South Sudan, and Venezuela — can and must do more. Tier 3 must never become a permanent designation; it should serve as a dire warning and a call to action,” Smith wrote.

title: Rep. Chu Leads 29 Members of Congress Demanding Answers on Barriers to Release from ICE Detention
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) led 29 Members of Congress in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Mullin, Attorney General Blanche, and Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) Acting Director Owen demanding answers about rising immigration bond denials, increasingly unaffordable bond amounts, and concerns about the independence of immigration judges under the Trump administration.

Immigration bond allows eligible individuals to be released from immigration detention while their cases proceed, subject to certain conditions, including appearing for future court proceedings. But since President Trump took office, bond denials have increased substantially, while individuals granted bond are increasingly being required to pay amounts that many families cannot afford.

According to data cited in the letter, immigration bond requests more than doubled from 34,845 in 2024 to 80,130 in 2025, an increase of approximately 130 percent. Meanwhile, the percentage of bond requests denied by immigration judges rose from approximately 36 percent in 2024 to 43 percent in 2025, reaching 55 percent in the first three months of 2026. The national median bond amount, which stood at $6,000 between January 2024 and November 2025, rose to $7,500 after November 10, 2025, with the average reaching $9,211.

These trends are particularly alarming at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, which Rep. Chu has fought to close for more than a decade. Since November 2025, immigration judges have denied 57 percent of bond requests from individuals detained at Adelanto, compared to 39 percent during the preceding period. The median bond amount at Adelanto has also climbed to $10,000, well above the national median. In one particularly troubling case, a man who had lived in the United States for 25 years, maintained steady employment, supported a family, and had no criminal record was assigned a $50,000 bond, an amount an amount immigration practitioners say has traditionally been reserved for exceptional cases.

The Members also raised serious concerns about potential interference with immigration judges' ability to make independent bond determinations. Following reports that judges were being required to provide written justifications to supervisors when granting bond, EOIR released heavily redacted records in response to a Freedom of Information Act request, leaving critical questions unanswered about what instructions or guidance immigration judges may have received.

In their letter, the Members wrote:

"Taken together, these developments paint a disturbing picture. The sharp increase in bond denials and bond amounts, coupled with unresolved questions regarding potential directives and supervisory practices governing immigration judges, raises serious concerns about whether immigration judges retain sufficient independence to make individualized bond determinations based on the facts and applicable law."

“Everyone deserves a fair shot at freedom while they fight their case,” said Rep. Chu. “But under this administration, more people are being denied bond, and those who are granted it are facing amounts their families simply cannot afford. Immigration judges must be free to make decisions based on the facts and the law, not political pressure. The Trump administration owes the American people answers about whether immigration judges are being pressured to deny bond rather than make independent decisions based on the facts and the law.

“This sharp increase in bond denials shows yet again how the Trump administration is manipulating the court system to advance its anti-immigration agenda while jeopardizing the independence of judges and due process for families caught in the system,” said Kel White, Associate Director, Public Education & Training at Acacia Center for Justice. “The few people who do receive bonds are told to pay an exorbitant amount and in cash. Not only is this unheard of, especially for people with no criminal record, it is nearly impossible for a parent to do. Courts must rely on facts and the law, not an out of control anti-immigrant agenda, otherwise this is a slap in the face of meaningful due process.”

"The widespread use of bond denials and excessive bonds, regardless of the individual facts of a case, underscores why our immigration courts must be truly independent. Immigration judges should be empowered to independently interpret the law and weigh the facts of each individual case, not be reduced to rubber stamps for the administration’s detention policies. The growing practice of denying bond or imposing exorbitant bonds on people with no criminal history comes at a significant cost to not only the individuals caught in the web of injustice, but there is a cost to American taxpayers. At a time when families are struggling with affordability and rising healthcare costs, taxpayers are being asked to foot the bill for the unnecessary detention of people who have lived in our communities for decades and have no criminal record," said Benjamin Johnson, Executive Director of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA).

title: Ciscomani Wraps Up District Work Week Focused on CPF Visits and Celebrating Local Organizations
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani wrapped up a successful district work week focused on visiting several Community Project Funding (CPF) locations and celebrating the accomplishments of organizations throughout Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

"District work weeks provide me with the ability to connect with constituents, hear their needs and priorities, and discuss how I am fighting for them in Washington. From joining leadership at Mt. Graham Regional Medical Center to discuss funding for a new mammography unit, to meeting with Mayor Lisa Fitzgibbons about funding for improvements at Burris Road-Peters Road, this week included several great opportunities to share how I am fighting to deliver results for Southern Arizona," said Rep. Ciscomani. "I also had the privilege of joining Albers Aerospace, Florence Copper, the Casa Grande Rotary Club, and Pima JTED to celebrate each of their achievements and the ways they help move Southern Arizona forward. I am proud to partner with organizations like these to advocate for and advance Arizona’s unique priorities."

As the only appropriator from Arizona in both the House and Senate, Representative Ciscomani is working to secure over $42 million across 20 projects across AZ-06 through the 2027 Appropriations process. As part of this district work week, the congressman visited five of these projects to discuss with local leadership the critical impacts these federal investments will have on their communities.

Ciscomani visited four projects in Graham County, which will support key needs for local communities:

$3 million for the reconstruction and widening of 1st Avenue Road in Thatcher, improving a critical local roadway and improving travel safety and efficiency.

$2 million for modernization and improvements to the Graham County Courthouse in Safford, to ensure it can continue meeting the needs of the county’s residents.

$650,000 for Mt. Graham Regional Medical Center to purchase a new mammography unit, bringing advanced breast cancer screening and diagnostic services closer to home for rural patients.

$650,000 for teacher housing at Fort Thomas Unified School District, helping provide more affordable housing options for educators while strengthening the district’s ability to recruit and retain teachers in the local community.

Read more about the Graham County CPF sites HERE, HERE, and HERE.

Ciscomani also visited a project in Pinal County, which will support infrastructure needs throughout Casa Grande:

$2.7 million for improvements at the intersections of Burris Road & Highway 84 and Burris Road & Peters Road, improving safety and ease of travel at critical transportation points.

While in Casa Grande, Ciscomani attended the 5th Annual Casa Grande Oktoberfest to celebrate the Casa Grande Rotary Club’s 100th anniversary and recognize the organization’s lasting impact on the community. In its century of service, the Casa Grande Rotary Club has accomplished.

To conclude this week's CPF visits, Rep. Ciscomani visited the Sahuarita Police Department joined by Rep. Nathaniel Moran of Texas, to discuss a project that will deliver vital support for the department's needs:

$2 million for the Sahuarita Police Department's purchase of a critical solar battery backup system to strengthen the facility's operations.

"At the local level you can make such a huge difference, but you've got to have a partner in Washington, D.C. that's willing to work with you, listen to good ideas, and then actually fight to make it happen," said Rep. Moran. "Nobody outworks Juan Ciscomani in Washington, D.C. I guarantee it."

Rep. Ciscomani also joined with leadership at two critical organizations which represent the best of Arizona. Albers Aerospace marked the opening of their Tucson location with a ribbon cutting, which Rep. Ciscomani was proud to take part in. The company’s expansion to Tucson strengthens and advances Southern Arizona’s defense and aerospace manufacturing sector, bringing in new jobs while aiding national security.

Read more about the event HERE.

Rep. Ciscomani also joined Florence Copper leadership and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin to commemorate the operation’s success in domestic copper production. Florence Copper is the first new source of copper in the United States in nearly two decades and represents Arizona’s commitment to domestic copper production and critical mineral supply.

To round out the week, Ciscomani joined the Pima JTED community for a beam signing ceremony at the new Pima JTED Innovation Learning Center. I am proud to have championed $2.7 million in federal funding for the construction of this center and look forward to how it will impact students for decades to come.

As Ciscomani continues the October district work period, he remains committed to partnering with local leaders and organizations across Southern Arizona to deliver real results for Arizona’s Sixth District.

title: CORREA, TLAIB REINTRODUCE RESOLUTION HONORING ALEX ODEH
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Lou Correa (CA-46) and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) today reintroduced a resolution remembering and honoring the life and legacy of Alex Odeh. The resolution acknowledges Alex's impact on his community and the country, and reaffirms the importance of pursuing justice against those responsible for his death.

“Alex Odeh was a teacher, a poet, and a man of peace, and he was murdered in our community simply for speaking up for civil and human rights,” said Correa. “He was a voice for peace and dignity in Orange County. Remembering him is the least we can do, and pursuing justice for his family is our obligation.”

Rep. Correa represents the district where Alex and his family lived and where the attack took place.

“Alex Odeh dedicated his life to achieving true equality and equity for all. For daring to push for a better tomorrow, Alex was assassinated by members of the Jewish Defense League, and his killers have yet to be brought to justice,” said Tlaib. "This horrific act of anti-Arab and anti-Palestinian violence was, and is not, new. But this violence will never silence us. Those who continue to fear-monger and incite hate against us will not win. Arab and Palestinian Americans are still here, loud and proud, carrying on Alex’s legacy.”

Read the bill text here.

About Alex Odeh

Alex was born in Jifna, Palestine, and lived in Orange County, California, for most of his adult life, including Santa Ana. He was a peace activist who worked to promote civil liberties for Arab-Americans in the United States. Alex Odeh was the Southern California Regional Director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC).

On October 11, 1985, Alex was killed when a pipe bomb exploded as he entered the ADC regional office in Santa Ana, California. Although the primary suspects have long been known, no one has been brought to justice. The investigation remains open.

title: Op-Ed: Health care premiums continue to rise. Congress can lower them
text:
By Rep. Joe Courtney (Published in the Day, October 9th, 2026)

Last month, Connecticut’s state insurance department officially approved an 11.3% average rate increase in 2027 for state-regulated, individual and small business health care coverage plans.

This double-digit increase, far above an already high general inflation rate, has justifiably been met with deep frustration from both individual patients and health care plan administrators, with small businesses in particular feeling the squeeze.

It is clear from the persistent high trajectory of the state insurance department rate increases that the mounting cost of health care is creating a burden that will not be sustainable over the long term. It is time for policy makers to stop this trend by digging deeper into these decisions to identify which health services are spiking in cost.

The 2026 rate decision could not be clearer. A leading driver of this year’s health care premium increase is prescription drug cost increases. According to the Connecticut Department of Insurance, 30% of a Connecticut health care premium dollar is consumed by prescription drug costs. This amount has doubled since 2010.

That trend screams out for action, not just in Hartford, but also in Washington, where over the last four years, real reductions in drug costs have been achieved because of Medicare price negotiations.

Along those lines, I am a co-sponsor of the Lowering Drug Costs for American Families Act (H.R. 6166), which would empower the Medicare program to negotiate with pharmaceutical companies for lower prescription drug costs, not just for Americans 65 and older, but for all Americans on employer-based plans and individual ACA marketplace plans (Access Health CT here in Connecticut).

This bill builds on the price negotiation success of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, which by law has saved both patients and Medicare billions. As a result of price negotiations, the diabetes drug Januvia saw its price lowered from $527 to $113, blood thinners Eliquis and Xarelto went from $521 to $231 and $517 to $197, respectively, and the Asthma and COPD drug Trelegy went from $654 to $175, to name just a few.

Expanding drug price regulation has strong public support. At least two-thirds of U.S. adults across all parties, including 68% of Republicans, say that there is not enough government regulation when it comes to the price of prescription drugs, according to 2026 polling by KFF.

Even President Trump and Congressional Republicans clearly recognize the success and popularity of drug price negotiation.

In 2025, when they cut nearly $1 trillion from the Medicaid program in their so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” (H.R. 1) and allowed Affordable Care Act marketplace (Access Health CT) premiums to skyrocket for middle-class Americans, Trump and the GOP very carefully left the Biden-era Medicare drug price negotiation in intact.

What about Trump Rx, the three-year deal with big pharma, you might ask? A close look at the Trump Rx portal that claims to provide lower drug prices in most cases recycles drug coupons for discounted prices that already exist.

In addition, Americans are only able to use Trump Rx to purchase drugs outside of their commercial health plans, meaning it does nothing to lower Connecticut premium rates. After three years, the Trump Rx deal expires, unlike the statutory permanence of the 2022 law that will expand the list of drugs subject to price reduction.

It is very clear, to lower Connecticut health care premiums, Congress should pass the Lowering Drug Costs for American Families Act into law and create cost-saving parity for working age Americans on par with Medicare. It’s simple and it will work.

title: Rep. Crank Introduces Bill to Expand Educational Freedom
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) introduced the Religious Education Liberty Assurance (RELA) Act, to ensure that Education Freedom Tax Credit (EFTC) dollars go to all students, including those who attend a private or religious school.

Created as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, the EFTC allows taxpayers to donate annually up to $1,700 per person to Scholarship Granting Organizations (SGOs) and receive a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit. SGOs use this money to provide tuition assistance, free or reduced-cost tutoring, educational supplies, and many other tools and resources for families and students who need them. States must opt-in to the tax credit for SGOs and families to be eligible, and so far, 30 states have done so, including Colorado.

The RELA Act would prevent states that opt-in from discriminating against religious or private schools, allowing the funds raised through the EFTC program to be available for use at all schools, in any education context, and for all children, regardless of whether the education provided is faith-based or not.

“Our nation’s families deserve the right to decide where their children receive education,” said Rep. Crank.“The RELA Act expands educational freedom by making sure private and religious schools are not shut out, so every family can use these resources to find the right path for their child.”

Quotes of support for the RELA Act:

“Parents should be able to choose the education that is right for their children without government interference, and the Education Freedom Tax Credit (EFTC) should be able to serve families without unnecessary government control,” said P. George Tryfiates, VP for Public Policy and Legal Affairs, Association of Christian Schools International. “The Religious Education Liberty Assurance Act makes clear that states may not exclude or discriminate against private and religious schools participating in the tax credit. After all, there is no meaningful school choice without religious schools. The Association of Christian Schools International, which represents millions of students, parents, and faculty worldwide is grateful for Rep. Crank’s leadership in recognizing the important role that educational freedom, parental choice, and religious liberty play in ensuring families have meaningful options for their children’s education.”

“Families should never face religious discrimination when choosing the education that is right for their children," said the Family Policy Alliance. "As a national organization headquartered in Colorado Springs, Family Policy Alliance is especially grateful to Congressman Jeff Crank for leading the Religious Education Liberty Assurance Act. We know how important strong religious liberty protections are in Colorado, and families and faith-based schools across the country deserve those same protections. The RELA Act will help ensure that no state can exclude or discriminate against families and schools simply because of their faith. We’re proud to support Congressman Crank’s leadership in defending religious freedom and educational opportunity for families nationwide.”

“Parents Defending Education Action is pleased to support Rep. Jeff Crank’s Religious Education Liberty Assurance (RELA) Act of 2026," said Terry Stoops, Director of Government Affairs at Parents Defending Education Action. "The RELA Act of 2026 will prevent attempts to both undermine the exercise of citizens’ First Amendment rights and to disadvantage faith-based elementary and secondary schools that will benefit greatly from the Education Freedom Scholarship Tax Credit. Rep. Crank's timely legislation insulates communities of faith from hostile government actors and ensures they will be able to freely participate in the Education Freedom Scholarship Tax Credit.”

title: Crow Hosts Election Security Roundtable with Colorado Leaders
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, hosted an election security roundtable alongside local officials from Denver County and Arapahoe County. Crow’s roundtable was an opportunity for elections officials, law enforcement, and other leaders to coordinate and discuss efforts to keep Colorado’s election system strong.

Joining Crow’s roundtable were Denver District Attorney John Walsh, Arapahoe County District Attorney Amy Padden; Arapahoe County Clerk and Recorder Joan Lopez; Arapahoe County Sheriff Tyler Brown; and Ben Hess from the Committee for Safe and Secure Election.

At the roundtable, Colorado leaders discussed ensuring Coloradans have the right information to help them vote early; security protocols that keep ballot drop-off boxes secure; and exercises used by law enforcement officers and local officials to help them prepare for any potential incidents before, during, and after Election Day.

“Colorado’s elections are the gold standard. Our same-day registration, open primaries, and mail-in-ballot program not only encourage one of the highest voter turnout rates in the nation but are also extremely safe and secure,” said Congressman Crow. “I assembled this roundtable to ensure that our leaders are working together to protect our elections at every turn. Every qualified Coloradan must have the chance to make their voice heard without fear or intimidation.”

Congressman Crow has long fought to ensure that all Coloradans are able to make their voices heard at the ballot box. He voted against Congressional Republicans’ voter suppression bills, while working to ensure our elections are secure from bad actors through his leadership on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. Crow is also leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act and SHINE Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections.

title: Dingell Releases Latest Response from U-M Regarding Los Alamos
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) is continuing to demand greater transparency on behalf of her constituents in Ypsilanti Township as it relates to the proposed University of Michigan (U-M) Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) research computing center at the Textile Road site.

title: De La Cruz Announces $31M for Jim Wells County Wastewater System
text:
WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (TX-15) joined officials from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to announce more than $31 million in available funding for Jim Wells County Fresh Water Supply District #1. Secured through the FY26 government funding legislation, the grant will fund critical infrastructure improvements in Ben Bolt. Specifically, the project will construct a new wastewater collection system connected to the City of Alice wastewater treatment plant and deliver sewer service to Ben Bolt for the first time. "This $31 million investment will be truly transformational for the community of Ben Bolt. I am thrilled to help secure funding that delivers first-time sewer service to enhance sanitation, water quality, and public health standards. This is not just an infrastructure upgrade, it is a long-term investment for Texas families and the community for decades to come." - Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz

Background:

Alongside USDA, Congresswoman De La Cruz announced a grant of $29.3 million and a loan of $2.5 million for the Jim Wells County Fresh Water Supply District #1. The funding will create a new wastewater collection system, including new sewer lines, manholes, force mains, and three lift stations, to ensure safe collection and treatment of wastewater. The system will be the first sewer service in Ben Bolt.

Earlier this year, Congresswoman De La Cruz supported $445.9 million in funding for the USDA Rural Water and Waste Disposal Program in the FY26 Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act.

title: Dexter, Bonamici, Merkley Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Portland ICE Facility After Reports of Denied Access to Legal Counsel
text:
PORTLAND, OR – Today, Congresswomen Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) processing facility on Macadam Avenue in Portland following troubling reports that attorneys were repeatedly denied access to detained clients.

“No one should be denied access to legal counsel, regardless of their immigration status,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “It is a major concern when attorneys are repeatedly prevented from meeting with their clients. ICE is not above the law, and the Trump administration must be held accountable for how people are treated in federal custody. We are demanding answers, transparency and accountability.”

Rep. Dexter’s office received information from the Portland Immigrant Rights Coalition that attorneys were denied access to four clients on 12 separate occasions Tuesday. These reports, coupled with an uptick in ICE enforcement activity in the Portland area, prompted the lawmakers to conduct an oversight visit to demand answers and examine conditions at the facility.

“I just conducted a Congressional oversight visit at the ICE processing facility in Portland with Rep. Dexter and Senator Merkley,” Congresswoman Bonamici said. “ICE is not making us safer and this surge is increasing fear in the community. I encourage everyone to make a safety plan and take care of each other. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”

“ICE and Border Patrol agents are terrorizing our friends and neighbors,” Senator Merkley said. “Time after time, they are trampling civil rights, denying due process, and utilizing secret police tactics, totally wrong in our democratic republic. I'll keep doing all I can to stop them.”

During the visit, the lawmakers asked about access to lawyers, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law. The visit builds on Rep. Dexter’s ongoing work to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable and protect the dignity and legal rights of people in ICE custody.

title: Ezell, Bonamici Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Reauthorize Regional Ocean Partnerships
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congressman Mike Ezell (MS-04) and Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) introduced the bipartisan Regional Ocean Partnerships Reauthorization Act, legislation to strengthen cooperation among coastal states, federal agencies, and local stakeholders to address shared ocean and coastal challenges.

Regional Ocean Partnerships bring together states and stakeholders to coordinate efforts involving coastal resilience, marine resources, ocean research, and maritime economic development. These partnerships allow regions to identify shared priorities and develop solutions tailored to their unique coastal environments and economies.

“Along the Mississippi Gulf Coast, our economy and way of life depend on healthy coastal waters, strong fisheries, and a thriving maritime industry,” Ezell said. “Regional Ocean Partnerships give states and local stakeholders a seat at the table when it comes to protecting these resources and addressing the challenges facing our coastal communities. I'm proud to work with Congresswoman Bonamici to reauthorize this program, strengthen regional cooperation, and ensure these partnerships remain focused on delivering results without adding unnecessary federal regulations.”

"The ocean, coasts, and Great Lakes face complex challenges, and the people who depend on them need tools to respond,” Bonamici said. “Regional Ocean Partnerships – like the West Coast Ocean Alliance – are proven solutions that convene state, tribal, local, and federal leaders to tackle shared problems with the science and resources they need. A healthy ocean and thriving coastal economies rely on collaboration. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan House Oceans Caucus, I'm pleased to work with Congressman Ezell to strengthen these partnerships and equip the people who live and work along our coasts with what they need to plan for a more resilient future."

The Regional Ocean Partnerships Reauthorization Act would extend federal support for these collaborative efforts through fiscal year 2031, helping participating states continue working together on shared coastal and marine priorities.

Specifically, the legislation would:

Reauthorize Regional Ocean Partnerships through FY2031, providing continued federal support for regional coordination and collaboration.

Authorize approximately $10.6 million in FY2028, with incremental increases through FY2031 to support partnership activities.

Strengthen accountability by requiring an additional report to Congress five years after enactment.

Protect against regulatory overreach by prohibiting partnership funding from being used to develop regulatory proposals, model regulations, or compliance programs.

For Mississippi, regional collaboration plays an important role in addressing issues affecting the Gulf of America, including coastal resilience, marine habitats, fisheries, and the maritime economy.

title: Congressman Flood Celebrates 100 Days of Successful Trade Deal with European Union
text:
LINCOLN, NEBRASKA – Today, Congressman Mike Flood (NE-01) released a statement celebrating the first 100 days since the European Union eliminated its tariffs on American industrial goods and opened new market access for American agricultural products as part of the broader U.S.-EU trade agreement. The agreement took effect July 1, 2026.

U.S. agricultural exports to the EU are up 17% this year, according to USDA Foreign Agricultural Service data, led by Nebraska’s top exports:

Ethanol exports to the EU have already surpassed all of 2025, with four months still to go.

Corn exports are up 82% on the year.

Beef exports are up 42% on the year.

“For too long, American farmers and ranchers have played by one set of rules while our trading partners played by another,” said Congressman Flood. “Over the last two years, we’ve renegotiated our trade deals to level the playing field, and our agreement with the European Union shows that it’s working. Europe is buying more American corn, ethanol, and beef than it has in years. When Nebraska producers can compete on fair terms, they win, and this deal gives them that opportunity for years to come.”

Earlier this year, Congressman Flood met with U.S. Ambassador to the European Union Andrew Puzder about the opportunities the deal creates for Nebraska producers.

Nebraska is the nation’s largest beef exporter and is a top exporter of corn, soybeans, and ethanol. The European Union is one of Nebraska’s top five agricultural export markets.

title: Fong, Valadao Welcome VA Secretary Collins to Bakersfield for New Clinic Announcement
text:
BAKERSFIELD, CA – Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) and Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) hosted Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Secretary Doug Collins in Bakersfield to announce the new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic. This new clinic will replace the existing inadequate, decades-old clinic in Bakersfield which is unable to meet increased patient demand and support existing services.

“Today is a significant step forward for the veterans of Kern County and it has been a long time coming,” said Congressman Fong. “After years of frivolous legal delays, the VA has accepted this new modernized clinic, with a target to welcome its first patients this December. Our veterans will finally be receiving care in a modern space worthy of their service, but we are not done. Today allows us to build and construct the permanent facility our veterans were promised, and I will not stop until that job is finished. Thank you to Secretary Doug Collins and the entire Trump Administration for making this a priority and delivering for the veterans of the Central Valley.”

“For too long, Bakersfield Veterans had to make do with a clinic that suffered from HVAC and plumbing problems, and didn’t have enough space to meet Veterans’ growing needs,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “Under President Trump’s leadership, and thanks to the advocacy of Reps. Valadao and Fong, Veterans will get the modern facility they deserve. The new clinic also enables VA to exit a horrible lease agreement that was costing us millions of additional dollars per year for a sub-standard facility – that means we can direct more resources to Veteran care.” ​​

“Our veterans have sacrificed so much to protect our nation and preserve our freedoms, and when they come home, they deserve access to high-quality VA healthcare in their communities,” said Congressman Valadao. “For over thirty years, the existing Bakersfield clinic has served thousands of veterans across our region, but that facility is aging, patient demand has only grown, and it doesn’t have the space or resources needed to meet our veterans’ needs. The new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic will better meet demand and expand access to essential services, including primary care, mental health, dental, rehabilitation, and other specialty services. This is an important investment in the health and well-being of our Central Valley veterans, and I want to thank Secretary Collins, the administration, and Congressman Fong for their continued partnership in making this project a reality. I look forward to seeing our Valley veterans benefit from this new facility soon!”

Background:

The new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic will replace the existing decades-old facility, which has struggled to keep pace with growing patient demand and provide the space needed to expand services.

In 2009, 17 years ago, Congress authorized this project to provide much-needed improved healthcare services to local veterans. However, repeated legal challenges stalled construction, leaving veterans without access to modernized care for over a decade. Thanks to the advocacy and leadership of Congressman Fong, Congressman Valadao, Secretary Collins and President Trump, the project is moving forward following a July 2025 court ruling in favor of the City of Bakersfield.

The approximately 30,000-square-foot facility will offer a full slate of expanded care options, including primary care, audiology and speech pathology, mental health, homeless services, dental, eye care, enrollment and eligibility, laboratory services, nutrition and food services, physical medicine and rehabilitation, telehealth, and women’s health. Veterans will continue receiving care from their existing providers, with the new facility providing additional space to meet their needs. The new clinic will also allow the VA to redirect funding previously spent on the outdated facility’s rent toward serving veterans.

title: Rep. Foushee Introduces Legislation to Promote Use of Low-Emission Anesthetic Gases
text:
DURHAM, NC (October 9, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Low Emission Anesthetics Act to incentive the use of certain low-emission anesthetic gases by health care facilities.

Certain traditional anesthetic gases including desflurane or nitrous oxide used by healthcare providers have been found to have an outsized impact on greenhouse gas emissions, despite the existence of proven low-emission anesthetic gases like isoflurane or sevoflurane.

“While it is clear that the climate crisis is being driven by large corporations and fossil fuels, Congress has a duty to explore all routes to make meaningful reductions to greenhouse gas emissions—and anesthetic gasses are one way we can make a difference. Moving away from anesthetic gases that have an outsized impact on greenhouse gas emission while viable alternatives already exist in the market is one small step we can take to be better environmental stewards,” said Congresswoman Valerie Fosuhee (NC-04). “I am proud to introduce the Low Emission Anesthetics Act to encourage the use of anesthetic gases that are less harmful to the environment, and I will continue to fight to keep the environment safe for generations to come.”

Specifically, the Low Emission Anesthetics Act would establish a low-emission anesthetic gas credit for any health care facility making strides to phase out high-emissions anesthetic gases, with escalating tax credits for facilities making significant strides in this area.

title: Franklin Demands Immediate Action As Sulfur Crisis Threatens Florida Fertilizer Production
text:
Congressman Scott Franklin (FL-18) today sent a letter to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick demanding immediate, coordinated federal action to address the sulfur supply and cost crisis already threatening domestic fertilizer production. With phosphate producers already cutting operations and idling facilities, Franklin warned continued delays threaten American jobs, Central Florida businesses, farm profitability and put the nation's food security at risk.

“American fertilizer producers are cutting production now due to the high cost of sulfur needed to convert phosphate rock into fertilizer. Farmers and workers cannot afford more delays,” said Congressman Scott Franklin. “This crisis reaches beyond the plant gates to the machine shops, contractors, truckers and small businesses that support Florida’s phosphate industry. Reviewing the problem is not enough. The Administration must secure additional sulfur suplies, remove federal barriers driving up costs and protect the domestic production we already have. Food security is national security.”

In the letter, Franklin called on USDA and Commerce to:

Designate a senior official to coordinate the federal response and provide an action plan with specific steps and implementation timelines.

Work with domestic suppliers, Canada and other reliable trading partners to increase sulfur supplies available to U.S. producers.

Resolve transportation, storage and handling constraints and remove unnecessary federal barriers increasing costs or limiting availability.

Accelerate eligible projects that expand sulfur recovery and logistics capacity or restore curtailed fertilizer production.

Evaluate existing emergency authorities, including the Defense Production Act, and identify any additional authorities or appropriations needed from Congress.

Sulfur is used to produce sulfuric acid, an essential input in phosphate fertilizer manufacturing with no readily available substitute in the production process. According to the Florida Phosphate Council, the industry generates an estimated $5 billion in economic impact in the Tampa region. In Polk County and across Central Florida, phosphate operations support equipment suppliers, machine shops, maintenance contractors, transportation providers and other local businesses. Prolonged production cuts threaten supplier orders, contract work and workers’ paychecks, with ripple effects throughout the local economy.

The crisis also threatens to deepen financial pressure on American farmers. According to an American Farm Bureau Federation survey, 70 percent of respondents could not afford the fertilizer they needed. Further production cuts risk tightening supplies, increasing costs and making the United States more dependent on foreign fertilizer producers.

Last month, Franklin led members of Florida's congressional delegation in urging President Trump and Secretary Lutnick to address rising sulfur costs and supply disruptions. He also joined the bipartisan effort that helped secure phosphate's inclusion on the U.S. critical minerals list in 2025.

Read the full letter here.

title: Gallagher Pushes Back on Proposed Federal Changes to Head Start Programs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) joined Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-04) in calling on the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to reconsider proposed changes to Head Start programs that local providers warn could reduce access to critical early childhood services for families across Northern California.

In a bipartisan letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the California lawmakers raised concerns about the proposed Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs rule, which would eliminate or reduce several federal standards governing classroom staffing and services for children with disabilities.

“Head Start is a lifeline for a lot of working families in rural Northern California,” said Congressman Gallagher. “When I hear from local providers that these changes could mean fewer teachers in classrooms or children missing out on early developmental support, I take that seriously. We should absolutely be looking for ways to cut unnecessary bureaucracy, but that shouldn't come at the expense of the kids and families these programs are meant to serve.”

Gallagher and Thompson pointed to concerns raised by E Center, which serves families across eight Northern California counties, and North Coast Opportunities, which provides Head Start services in Lake and Mendocino Counties and surrounding communities.

Both organizations warned that eliminating federal standards for staff-to-child ratios and classroom sizes could result in larger classrooms with fewer teachers. The lawmakers also raised concerns that reducing health and developmental screening requirements could delay identifying children who need additional support.

These concerns are especially significant in communities recovering from devastating wildfires. Families in Butte and Lake Counties continue to face housing instability and displacement, making reliable access to Head Start services particularly important.

“We are deeply grateful for the strong bipartisan leadership of Representatives Thompson and Gallagher,” said Melanee Cottrell, Executive Director of Head Start California. “Their advocacy is critical to protect comprehensive, high-quality Head Start programs – one of America's most successful investments in young children and families.”

The letter also raises concerns about reducing the administrative spending cap from 15 percent to 5 percent, which local providers warn could force reductions in services across rural communities.

Gallagher and Thompson urged HHS to withdraw or modify the proposed rule and work directly with Head Start providers to identify improvements that preserve the services children and families depend on.

title: Rep. Garbarino Celebrates Columbus Day, Recognizes Contributions of Italian Americans to Long Island
text:

Garbarino (NY-02), Vice Chair of the Italian American Congressional Delegation, is recognizing the generations of Italian Americans who have helped shape Long Island and communities across the country. Garbarino. “Italian Americans have played an enormous role in shaping Long Island into the place we are proud to call home, which can be seen in our small businesses, neighborhoods, and communities across the Island. title: Golden, Blue Dog leaders introduce comprehensive reform package to fix broken budget process
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Reps. Jared Golden (ME-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) and Adam Gray (CA-13) — leaders in the House Blue Dog Coalition — today introduced the Congressional Budget Reform Act of 2026.

The legislation would fix Congress’s broken budgeting process, strengthen fiscal guardrails and checks and balances, and provide greater transparency about the fiscal health of the United States.

“Washington has spent years cutting taxes while increasing spending, and the bill is catching up with us,” Golden said. “Debt payments have grown so large that they eclipse nearly every other line item in the budget. They are crowding out investments in education, national security and other priorities and threatening Social Security and Medicare. Now, our record-breaking $40 trillion debt is driving up interest rates, making it more expensive for Americans to own a home, buy a car or start a small business. Congress needs to get serious about the debt and start making responsible choices again.”

“Working people know what debt actually means — it’s the difference between whether you can afford your kid’s next season of sports or winter coat. Meanwhile, Congress has spent years treating hard-earned income like it’s monopoly money to throw around without a second thought,” said Gluesenkamp Perez, a member of the Appropriations Committee. “We’re introducing these reforms because we recognize that we have a job to do here, and the cost of not doing it is too high. Congress needs to show that there is a respect for the work it takes to earn money and for what it means to be a good steward of the economy. We want our kids to inherit an economy of stability, not one of flippant waste.”

“Passing a responsible budget is one of the most basic responsibilities Congress has, and the current system clearly isn’t working,” Gray said. “We shouldn’t accept shutdowns, trillion-dollar deficits and last-minute spending bills as business as usual. These reforms put some common sense back into the process, strengthen guardrails against runaway debt and make it easier for Congress to do what people expect us to do: pass a budget and make government work.”

The bill contains nine reforms to Congressional budgetmaking. These include:

Fixing a Broken Process:

Bundle the 12 Appropriations bills into four “minibus” bills: This will reduce procedural bottlenecks and encourage on-time enactment of appropriations.

Implement the Prevent Government Shutdowns Act: This would enact automatic 14-day Continuing Resolutions in the event of a lapse in government funding and require Congress to stay in session until Appropriations bills are completed.

End the fast-track for impoundment in the Senate: This would strengthen checks and balances by instituting the same 60-vote threshold on executive rescissions that is required to pass appropriations in the first place.

Clarify that so-called “pocket rescissions” are illegal: Close the door on presidents seeking to bypass congressional authority and unilaterally cancel funding by submitting a rescission request and withholding funding at the end of a budget cycle, when Congress does not have enough time to take up the request.

Strengthening Fiscal Guardrails:

Enforceable debt-to-GDP targets: Require Congress to set either debt-to-GDP or deficit-to-GDP targets in the annual budget resolution and create a special reconciliation process to enforce the target if it is exceeded.

Strengthen PAYGO: Require the House to take a recorded vote before exempting legislation from the PAYGO Scorecard or other actions that cook the books rather than meet statutory fiscal responsibility rules.

Deficit Reduction Accounts: Create new accounts in Appropriations bills to allow savings to go directly toward reducing the deficit.

Improving Information and Data Available to Congress:

Fiscal State of the Nation: Require an annual, nonpartisan briefing in a joint hearing of the House and Senate Budget committees from the Comptroller General.

Report on Fiscal Contingency Preparedness: Require the Treasury Department and OMB to conduct and publish an annual assessment of the government’s fiscal resilience to major emergencies, subject to independent Government Accountability Office review.

(For more information, click here to see full text of the bill and here to read a more detailed summary.)

The Budget Reform Act of 2026 is endorsed by the Blue Dog Coalition and supported by several independent, nonpartisan organizations dedicated to fiscal responsibility:

Maya MacGuineas, President, Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget: “We appreciate the Blue Dog Coalition putting forward the Congressional Budget Reform Act. The legislation includes multiple reforms to strengthen transparency and accountability in the federal budget process. Exploding deficits are an affordability issue, and reducing them can help temper inflation, lower everyday costs and boost incomes over time. Process reforms cannot substitute for the hard policy choices lawmakers will ultimately have to make. Still, this bill would be a step in the right direction by helping reduce the crisis-driven nature of the current budget process and enhancing the tools available to hold lawmakers accountable. We look forward to continuing to work with the Blue Dog Coalition to improve the nation’s fiscal outlook.”

Ben Ritz, VP of Policy Development, Progressive Policy Institute: “The Blue Dogs’ Congressional Budget Reform Act is a good first step to modernize the budget process and push Congress to manage federal finances more responsibly.”

Carolyn Bourdeax, Executive Director, Concord Action: “We appreciate the Blue Dog Coalition's leadership in proposing the Congressional Budget Reform Act of 2026. Restoring regular order, strengthening fiscal guardrails and improving transparency are good ways to begin righting the ship after being off course far too long. At the same time, Concord Action will continue to emphasize the urgent need for a concrete, enforceable plan to cut the deficit in half to ensure long-term fiscal sustainability and economic stability.”

Brett Loper, Executive Director, Peterson Solutions Fund: “Budgeting from one crisis to the next not only threatens our economy, but it contributes to our $40 trillion and rising national debt. We commend members of the Blue Dog Coalition for putting forward the Congressional Budget Reform Act of 2026, which includes commonsense proposals to strengthen fiscal guardrails, provide meaningful information to Congress and the public and better align budgeting with the goals of fiscal responsibility. In particular, setting a debt-to-GDP target is a commendable step to highlight our runaway long-term debt outlook and what is required to put our nation on a more sustainable path.”

title: Gooden Seeks Clayton’s Assessment of U.S. AI/SI Defenses, Offers Congressional Support
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-05) asked DNI Jay Clayton for an assessment of whether current measures are sufficient to counter emerging AI/SI threats and where congressional support could strengthen those defenses. Clayton was recently chosen by President Trump to lead the White House’s Super Intelligence Force.

Gooden’s letter cites recent reports from leading American AI developers detailing instances in which agentic systems exceeded the intended boundaries of testing environments and accessed external systems. The letter also highlights reports of foreign actors using agentic AI to target Americans.

“As agentic AI becomes more powerful, China and other adversaries will look for every weakness they can exploit,” said Rep. Gooden. “Congress needs to know whether our current defenses are able to keep pace and where we need to act before the next threat becomes a crisis.”

An excerpt from the letter:

“Accordingly, we wish to inquire about the efficacy of existing measures in adequately preventing potential threats and misuse of AI by foreign adversaries like China and request you to identify and share with us any areas that could benefit from legislative action. We request your analysis of any possible shortcomings under current laws that must be addressed, especially any gaps or ambiguities that could impede your ability to effectively counter foreign adversaries using AI to target key U.S. assets and infrastructure.”

Gooden has been a leading voice in Congress in addressing foreign threats to American innovation and policymaking. He introduced theThink Tank and Nonprofit Foreign Influence Disclosure Act, which requires think tanks and nonprofits to publicly disclose significant contributions from foreign governments and political parties. Gooden has alsoworked alongside Attorney General Todd Blanche to address concerns surrounding foreign influence in our AI policy.

The letter was featured in anexclusive article byPunchbowl and is co-signed by Reps. Randy Weber (TX-14), Erin Houchin (IN-09), and Don Bacon (NE-02).

Read the full letterhere.

title: Goodlander Pushes Back Against Trump Administration Plan to Dismantle Head Start, Protects New Hampshire Children and Working Families
text:
Goodlander joins 190 colleagues urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw proposed rule that would dismantle safeguards for early education, child safety, and health services.

Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) joined House and Senate colleagues this week in urging U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to withdraw a proposed rule that would weaken Head Start standards protecting children and supporting working families across New Hampshire.

The letter opposes the Administration’s proposed “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs” rule, warning that it would remove more than 90 percent of existing program standards and undermine the high-quality early education, health services, and family support that make Head Start a lifeline for families.

“Every child in New Hampshire deserves a safe place to learn, grow, and get a fair shot at success. Head Start helps deliver on that promise while helping hardworking parents stay in the workforce and provide for their families,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “At a time when Granite Staters are struggling to find and afford childcare, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy is brazenly trying to dismantle Head Start, and make it harder for kids and families to get the care they need. That is unacceptable. I’m fighting to protect Head Start and make quality childcare more affordable and accessible for New Hampshire families.”

The lawmakers warn that the proposal would eliminate federal requirements governing staff-to-child ratios and class sizes, weaken staff qualifications and safety training, and roll back standards for developmental screenings, dental care, and mental health services. They also raise concerns that shorter program hours would leave working parents scrambling to find additional childcare, while new documentation requirements would create barriers for families with the greatest needs.

The letter further objects to removing detailed protections for children with disabilities and children experiencing homelessness, and to changes that would undermine instruction for dual-language learners.

Read the full letter HERE.

BACKGROUND ON GOODLANDER’S ADVOCACY FOR CHILDREN AND WORKING FAMILIES

Congresswoman Goodlander is working to lower childcare costs, expand access to early education, and support the educators and programs New Hampshire families rely on.

Defending Head Start: Goodlander previously joined the Democratic Women’s Caucus in urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw the same proposed rule, opposing efforts to weaken standards for child safety, early learning, health services, and support for children with disabilities.

Making quality childcare more affordable: Goodlander helped introduce the Child Care for Working Families Act, which would cap working families’ childcare expenses at seven percent of income, expand the supply of quality care, and increase wages for early childhood educators. The legislation would also support full-day, full-year Head Start programs and higher wages for Head Start workers.

Helping children and families get to school: Goodlander introduced the bipartisan PATH to Education Act to improve affordable, reliable transportation to Head Start centers and educational institutions. The bill would help connect transit routes to schools and better align transportation schedules with program hours.

Investing in New Hampshire’s childcare workforce: Goodlander helped secure nearly $1 million for Nashua Community College’s Early Childhood Education Center. The center will help prepare future early childhood educators and expand access to quality childcare, with opportunities for students to observe, collaborate, and teach alongside Head Start teachers.

Expanding childcare in New Hampshire communities: Goodlander helped secure federal Community Project Funding, including $1 million for Bristol’s Tapply-Thompson Community Center, $688,000 for the Gorham Community Learning Center, and $1.6 million for Sullivan County’s Regional Childcare Enhancement Project. These investments will support a new community center in Bristol, conversion of a vacant bank into a childcare facility in Gorham, and a new childcare center on Sullivan County’s Unity Campus.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Urges FDA to Establish Clear Standards for Rare Disease Status
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Sarcoidosis Caucus, and thirty-eight of his colleagues sent a bipartisan letter to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and U.S. Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Marty Makary urging the agencies to establish clear, consistent standards for defining rare disease patient populations.

“When 95 percent of rare diseases do not have cures, we cannot risk discouraging innovation in areas where scientific progress is rapidly outpacing regulatory adaptation,” the letter reads. “These challenges are not merely technical — they have real implications for patients… This means if the FDA considers prevalence rate with the higher estimate as the prevailing rate, diseases like Sarcoidosis are no longer capable of receiving crucial rare disease funding to find cures even though the patient population that needs treatment is well below the current FDA standard for rare.”

The letter raises concerns about the lack of clear, consistent FDA standards on how patient populations should be defined, how prevalence should be measured, and what evidentiary standards sponsors must meet. Advances in genomics and precision medicine are enabling researchers to identify increasingly specific disease subtypes, but the FDA has no clear roadmap for how to characterize those populations in regulatory submissions. The letter warns that this uncertainty can lead to unpredictable regulatory outcomes and discourage investment in therapies for small or complex patient populations.

This lack of clarity is already causing harm. Diseases like sarcoidosis, multiple myeloma, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, and pulmonary hypertension — serious, often life-altering conditions — risk losing rare disease status depending on how patient populations are counted. For example, while some estimates place sarcoidosis prevalence just above 200,000, only about 60,000 patients actually require treatment. If the FDA relies on the higher estimate, diseases like sarcoidosis could lose access to rare disease-specific research funding and incentives, even though the population that needs treatments is well below the 200,000-person threshold.

The lawmakers urge HHS and the FDA to:

Establish standardized definitions for how patient populations are delineated, including the role of genetic, biomarker, and clinical criteria.

Issue clear guidance on acceptable methodologies for calculating and submitting prevalence data, including preferred data sources, timeframes, and analytic approaches.

Outline how real-world data and registry-based studies should be incorporated into regulatory submissions.

Provide greater transparency into how population definitions and prevalence estimates are evaluated during review.

Clarify the role of treatment-eligible patient populations in determining rare disease status.

Engage patient groups, researchers, and industry to develop consensus-driven best practices for population identification and data submission.

The letter is co-signed by Reps. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA), Don Bacon (R-NE), Nanette Díaz Barragán (D-CA), Wesley Bell (D-MO), André Carson (D-IN), Yvette Clarke (D-NY), Steve Cohen (D-TN), Jim Costa (D-CA), Danny Davis (D-IL), Don Davis (D-NC), Madeleine Dean (D-PA), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), Lois Frankel (D-FL), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH), Adam Gray (D-CA), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ), French Hill (R-AR), Jim Himes (D-CT), Jonathan Jackson (D-IL), Hank Johnson (D-GA), Ro Khanna (D-CA), Darin LaHood (R-IL), Mike Lawler (R-NY), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Sarah McBride (D-DE), Max Miller (R-OH), Kelly Morrison (D-MN), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Mark Pocan (D-WI), Linda Sánchez (D-CA), Eric Sorensen (D-IL), Darren Soto (D-FL), Tom Suozzi (D-NY), Shri Thanedar (D-MI), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL).

“The letter builds on Gottheimer’s longstanding work on sarcoidosis and rare diseases. He has led an annual bipartisan appropriations letter urging research funding for sarcoidosis through the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), founded the Bipartisan Congressional Sarcoidosis Caucus, and has met with patients, advocates, and leading medical professionals from across New Jersey to discuss the disease. Importantly, Gottheimer secured language in the Fiscal Year 2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations bill that passed out of committee this year. The language encourages the NHLBI to advance research into sarcoidosis — the first-ever mention of the disease in this appropriations bill. For the sarcoidosis community, this is not just an abstract regulatory debate. It is about whether patients will have access to the treatments and research they desperately need in the future. Estimates put sarcoidosis prevalence at just over 200,000, but only about 60,000 patients are currently estimated to require treatment. At the same time, we know sarcoidosis is frequently misdiagnosed or goes undiagnosed, particularly for patients who lack access to specialists either geographically or financially, who recognize the disease. If FDA and HHS rely on inconsistent methodologies or incomplete data to define these populations, they risk overlooking the very patients who need greater investment in research and treatment. The treatment eligible population, and the patients who have yet to be diagnosed, must be part of this conversation. We sincerely thank Representative Gottheimer for leading this effort and for recognizing the need for clear, consistent, science based standards that accurately reflect the realities facing patients with rare diseases like sarcoidosis,” said Saul Kuciauskas, Vice President and Board Chair, Life & Breath Foundation.

“Foundation for Sarcoidosis Research (FSR) is grateful to Representative Josh Gottheimer and the Sarcoidosis Congressional Caucus for your extraordinary leadership. Sarcoidosis has been a largely neglected and underfunded disease. Complicated rare diseases, like sarcoidosis, require thoughtful engagement with the FDA and the NIH to ensure that drug development and research advance in a way that meets the real-world needs of the community. In short order, the Sarcoidosis Caucus has taken bold steps to clear the path to a brighter future for all impacted by sarcoidosis,” said Mary McGowan, President and CEO of FSR.

Gottheimer, a Rare Disease Caucus member, is also leading Gwenn’s Law, which would increase the number of women in NIH clinical research trials to help drive treatments and cures for rare diseases, and Cameron’s Law, which would restore the Orphan Drug Tax Credit to support rare disease drug development.
