title: Gov. Beshear, Congressman Rogers Announce More Than $22 Million for Economic Revitalization in Eastern Kentucky
text:
CORBIN, Ky. (Oct. 9, 2026) – Today, at the Shaping Our Appalachian Region (SOAR) Summit, Gov. Andy Beshear and U.S. Congressman Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) announced more than $22 million to help support healthcare, emergency services, infrastructure, energy, education, tourism and economic development in Eastern Kentucky.

“The people of Eastern Kentucky have supported this country through two world wars, our Industrial Revolution and by building the greatest middle class in the history of the world. These hardworking families deserve to know there is a bright future ahead of them and the investments we announced today will help make that possible,” said Gov. Beshear. “By focusing these dollars on healthcare, infrastructure and ongoing economic growth, we are making sure everyone across this important region has a chance to live out the American Dream.”

The funding announced today comes through the Abandoned Mine Lands Economic Revitalization (AMLER) program, established by Congressman Rogers in 2016. More than $1.3 billion in federal funding has gone toward AMLER since the program’s founding, of which more than $280 million has been awarded for 120 projects in Kentucky.

“Over the past decade, the bipartisan AMLER grant program has helped our coal-producing counties pursue new opportunities to revitalize our region through stronger infrastructure, workforce development, adventure tourism, advancing access to healthcare and education, expanding broadband and much more,” said Congressman Rogers. “These new grants continue our work to create new jobs and opportunities where we need them most.”

Today, the Governor and Congressman awarded:

More than $4 million to the Leslie County Fiscal Court to install over 35,000 linear feet of gas line to support existing and future businesses. The project will serve 12 businesses, over 100 households and six schools and churches once complete.

$3.5 million to the City of London Convention and Tourism Commission in Laurel County to improve and complete infrastructure for the Wilderness Road Event Center. The project anticipates up to 65,000 visitors within the first two years and will create five full-time jobs at opening date.

$2.9 million for Johnson County Schools to support the growth of the nursing and agriculture programs at the Johnson Central Career and Technical Center. The nursing program will create a healthcare learning environment that stimulates real life situations through the purchase of simulation equipment and supplies. The school will also expand its agriculture program by creating a hands-on learning environment with the purchase of high tunnels and farming equipment. The agriculture program anticipates training 246 students within the first year and the nursing program expects to train 75 students within the first year and lead to the creation of 50 jobs within the first five years.

$2.76 million to AdventHealth Manchester in Clay County to allow the hospital to purchase a DaVinci 5 Robotic Surgical System. The system will provide five new surgical services with a less invasive approach and is expected to serve 360 patients within the first year.

$2.5 million to the Elliott County Fiscal Court to replace the current emergency medical services (EMS) facility in Sandy Hook with a larger, modernized structure that will better support EMS operations and services. The county anticipates a 3% increase in patients treated within the first year of operation.

More than $2.2 million to the City of Cumberland in Harlan County to replace its aging water distribution infrastructure and provide dependable access to safe water by adding new water lines. The project is anticipated to serve 194 households and 50 businesses within the first year after completion.

$2.15 million to Letcher County Water and Sewer District (LCWSD) to install new waterline and provide water services for the Mountain Comprehensive Health Corp. (MCHC) Children’s Autism Center, as well as 200 households.

$1.64 million to the City of Booneville in Owsley County for the Sag Hollow Business Development Phase II, which will expand overnight lodging at the Sag Hollow area through the construction of three executive cabins. The project anticipates 2,800 visitors and the creation of two new jobs within the first year, with an expected revenue increase of over $150,000 by the second year of operation.

$600,000 to the Pike County Fiscal Court to construct a build-ready pad at the Wolfpit Industrial Park. This project is expected to generate create $125,000 in occupational tax revenue within the first year and will help attract even more economic investment.

The Governor and Congressman also presented $25.7 million to the Center for Rural Development for six BEAD award projects to expand high speed internet to over 3,000 homes across 12 counties. Gov. Beshear first announced this project on Wednesday, as part of a record $78.8 million awarded to Kentucky from the Appalachian Regional Commission in fiscal year 2026. Congressman Rogers continues to protect federal funding for the ARC each year.

In 2026, the AMLER program awarded 14 grants in Kentucky, totaling more than $35 million. Those include two awards totaling $6.6 million for Eastern Kentucky coal communities announced in June, three awards totaling $6.6 million for Western Kentucky coal communities announced in September and nine awards announced today totaling more than $22.2 million for Kentucky’s Appalachian region. When completed, the 14 projects are expected to retain or create 257 jobs and train up to 500 Kentuckians annually. Infrastructure projects and workforce training will serve 165 businesses and 3,369 households; the community wellness projects will serve over 160,000 people annually; and the tourism projects will help bring in nearly 67,800 visitors annually.

Energy and Environment Cabinet Secretary John Lyons selected the projects for initial vetting by the Kentucky Division of Abandoned Mine Lands. Sec. Lyons said 112 applications (requesting over $268 million) were received for consideration.

“The AMLER program is one of the most fulfilling programs we’re involved in,” said Secretary of the Energy and Environment Cabinet John Lyons. “These projects bring new life to our coal communities and create innovative solutions for tourism and business. They also bring much-needed services to our coal regions.”

Information about the AMLER program can be found on the Energy and Environment Cabinet website or by contacting Samantha Johnson, director of the Kentucky Division of Abandoned Mine Lands, at 300 Sower Boulevard, Frankfort, KY 40601. Office: 502-782-9913, e-mail: SamanthaM.Johnson@ky.gov.

Award Recipient Quotes

“We are deeply grateful to Congressman Hal Rogers for his support in securing this AMLAR grant and to our AdventHealth Manchester team whose dedication helped make this possible,” said Nick Bejarano, president and CEO of AdventHealth Manchester. “This investment will help bring advanced surgical care closer to home for people across southeastern Kentucky, giving more patients access to the care they need without having to travel far from their families and support systems. It is an important step forward in our vision to make high-quality, whole-person care more accessible and to help build a healthier future alongside the communities we call home.”

“On the behalf of MCHC and the children and families affected by autism, I would like to humbly thank Gov. Beshear and Congressman Rogers for this water and sewer extension grant,” said Mike Caudill, CEO of MCHC. “The grant provides the final link needed for MCHC to construct a 15,000+ square foot state-of-the-art clinic dedicated solely for the diagnosis and treatment of autistic children. Without this grant, this much-needed project may never have come to fruition. Thank you.”

“On behalf of the Johnson County School system, I want to express my sincere gratitude to the AMLER program for awarding us this grant,” said Thom Cochran, superintendent of Johnson County Schools. “This funding is a critical piece for our district as we construct our new Career and Technical Center. Specifically, these resources will allow us to continue construction of our health science classrooms and labs, as well as build new high tunnel greenhouses for our agriculture pathways. Investments like this directly support our mission to provide students with hands-on learning environments that truly prepare them for life beyond high school, and we are deeply appreciative of the continued support for our schools and community.”

“The Leslie County Fiscal Court is extremely grateful to receive $4,030,000 in AMLER funding for Phase III of the Gas Line Project,” said Judge Executive William Lewis. “This award represents a significant investment in the future of Leslie County and will allow us to continue expanding critical infrastructure that can improve the quality of life for our citizens and create opportunities for future growth. We appreciate the continued support of our state and federal partners and everyone who has worked to make this project possible. We are proud to continue moving this important project forward and investing in the future of Leslie County.”

“Pike County is very thankful for the AMLER program,” said Judge Executive Ray S. Jones II. “This award is the final phase of the Wolfpit Industrial & Technology Park. The funding will be used to construct a building pad and enable this site to be ‘Build Ready.’ The Wolfpit Industrial & Technology site is an 88-acre industrial park with the potential to create 250 much-needed manufacturing or technology jobs.”

Zeke Little, Owsley County Judge Executive, said: “This is an absolute win for Booneville and Owsley County!”

His support for this investment recognizes the importance of facilities like the Wilderness Road Event Center to our region’s economy, tourism industry and quality of life.”

For more information about Congressman Rogers' work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: Congressman Hamadeh Encourages Students to Submit Applications for Service Academy Nominations Before Deadline
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) is encouraging graduating high school students in Arizona’s 8th Congressional District who are interested in attending one of the nation’s prestigious U.S. service academies to submit their applications for a congressional nomination before the October 30, 2026, deadline.

Completed application packages for the Class of 2031 must be submitted to Congressman Hamadeh’s office no later than 3:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026.

Congressman Hamadeh looks forward to nominating exceptional student leaders, scholars, and athletes from Arizona’s 8th Congressional District to four of the nation’s five U.S. service academies: U.S. Military Academy (West Point) — West Point, New York; U.S. Naval Academy — Annapolis, Maryland; U.S. Air Force Academy — Colorado Springs, Colorado; and U.S. Merchant Marine Academy — Kings Point, New York.

The fifth institution, the U.S. Coast Guard Academy in New London, Connecticut, does not require a congressional nomination for admission.

“As a former U.S. Army officer, I understand firsthand the tremendous honor and responsibility that come with serving in our nation's Armed Forces,” stated Congressman Hamadeh. “Our service academies represent the very best of American military tradition, providing an exceptional education while developing the leadership, character, and discipline necessary to serve our great nation. It is a distinct privilege to help outstanding young men and women from Arizona’s 8th Congressional District pursue their dreams of attending one of these prestigious institutions.”

Admission to a U.S. service academy is among the most competitive and prestigious educational opportunities available to graduating high school students. In addition to receiving a world-class education and extensive leadership training, graduates accept a commitment to serve their country following graduation. Most graduates are required to serve a minimum of five years on active duty, although service obligations vary by academy and program.

While a congressional nomination is an essential step in the admissions process for four of the five academies, it does not guarantee an appointment. Each academy makes its own final admissions decisions based on academic achievement, leadership potential, physical fitness, character, and other qualifications.

Students seeking a congressional nomination for the Class of 2031 must submit their completed application packages to Congressman Hamadeh’s district office by 3:00 p.m. on October 30, 2026.

title: Hayes, Landsman, Carter Introduce Bipartisan Clean School Bus Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05), was joined by Congressman Greg Landsman (OH-01) and Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01) to introduce the Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act, bipartisan legislation to reauthorize $1 billion in funding to help school districts across the country replace traditional school buses with electric bus alternatives. Specifically, the legislation would provide $1 billion for the Clean School Bus program at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

Every day, 20 million children and thousands of bus drivers breathe polluted air during their commute to school, which negatively impacts student health and attendance, particularly for students with asthma and other respiratory conditions. The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act addresses this challenge by providing school districts with grants to invest in bus replacement, charging infrastructure, and workforce development.

“Since I came to Congress in 2019, I have advocated for clean school bus funding. As an educator with over a decade of classroom experience, I know how damaging diesel exhaust can be for student well-being and learning. The consequences of diesel emissions extend to our environment, exacerbating the effects of greenhouse gas emissions. The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Actwill help to provide cleaner and healthier air for school children in Connecticut and across the country, support clean energy jobs, and protect our environment for decades to come,” said Congresswoman Hayes.

“School buses that run on clean energy have a major impact on the environment, and they save money for our school districts. The Clean School Bus Act is an important investment in our education system that will keep our kids and our communities safe for years to come”, said Congressman Landsman.

“Getting students to and from school safely and reliably is a priority for families and school districts across Georgia. By extending the Clean School Bus Program, this legislation will give schools greater certainty as they plan for the future, replace aging buses, and make transportation decisions that best meet the needs of their communities. I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan effort to help ensure our schools have the tools they need to keep students moving safely and reliably,’ said Congressman Carter.

The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act builds on efforts led by Congresswoman Hayes since her first time in Congress.

In 2019, Congresswoman Hayes introduced the Clean School Bus Act to establish a grant program authorized for up to $1 billion over five years for school districts, particularly those with lower-income students, to replace diesel school buses with electric school buses.

In 2021, Congresswoman Hayes introduced the Clean Commute for Kids Act to invest $25 billion to replace existing diesel buses with electric buses.

Congresswoman Hayes fought for clean school bus funding in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, signed into law in 2021. This led to the inclusion of over $5 billion for the EPA to administer rebates, grants, and contracts to replace a portion of the nearly 500,000 school buses with more environmentally safe models.

In 2023, Congresswoman Hayes joined her colleagues to urge President Biden to include at least $300 million in additional funding for clean school buses in his FY24 budget request.

In June of 2023, The Congresswoman joined Brenda Mallory, Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and other officials to announce the award of 25 zero-emission school buses to DATTCO Inc. to provide school transportation services for the Connecticut Technical Education and Career System (CTECS).

In 2024, the EPA announced 67 recipients for the first Clean School Bus Program Grants Competition. The grants help awardees purchase over 2,700 clean school buses in 281 school districts across 36 states including Connecticut. The Congresswoman released the following statement.

During Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations, Congresswoman Hayes led over 120 of her colleagues to request $300 million for the Clean School Bus program.

The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act is endorsed by the American School Bus Industry Coalition which includes Blue Bird, First Student, Beacon Mobility, National Express, Highland, Greenpower Motor Company, National School Transportation, Student Transportation of America, and IC Bus. Additional endorsers include the American Bus Association, American Asthma and Allergy Foundation (AAFA), League of Conservation Voters, Moms Clean Air Force, Sierra Club, Union of Concerned Scientists, and World Resources Institute’s (WRI) Electric School Bus Initiative.

“Reauthorizing the Clean School Bus Program is important to American manufacturing, American workers, our nation’s school children and local communities throughout the country. As Americans, we can take pride in the fact that almost all school buses sold in the United States, including electric school buses, are also manufactured in the United States by American workers. The school bus industry has seen great enthusiasm and increased demand for alternative fuel and zero-emissions school buses from parents and school districts, and the Clean School Bus Program has significantly expanded access to these vehicles. On behalf of U.S. school bus manufacturers, and private school bus operators, the American School Bus Industry Coalition commends Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Greg Landsman and Rep. Buddy Carter for the bipartisan introduction of a five-year reauthorization bill that will positively benefit our nation’s kids.” – American School Bus Industry Coalition

title: Hoyer Statement on Trump Administration Decision to Lift Sanctions on Russian Diesel
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after President Donald Trump announced a 180-day suspension of sanctions on Russian diesel and indicated that the U.S. may purchase large quantities of the fuel:

"It is outrageous for the President of the United States to purchase tons of diesel from Russia in direct contravention of legislation he signed three weeks ago imposing the toughest sanctions on Russia’s oil and gas. Doing so would fuel the very war of aggression in Ukraine that our sanctions are meant to stop. It is a sudden and mendacious shift in policy from the pressure of our sanctions to actively aiding and abetting the war effort of Russia against Ukraine - and an infusion of economic assistance to Russia. Both of these are the exact opposite of Congress’s intent and the President’s statement in enacting and signing the Lindsay O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act three weeks ago. This action bails out both Putin and Trump - for Putin, his faltering war effort and economy; for Trump, the consequences of a war of choice in Iran: exorbitant fuel costs for Americans.

"President Trump’s action of helping Russia while at the same time asking our allies to shoulder more of the burden of support for Ukraine is clearly duplicitous.

“Congress must take action, drawing on the strong bipartisan support behind the sanctions law, to prevent a penny of American funds from being used to purchase Russian petroleum products, on which Putin relies to fund his war.”

title: Congressman Glenn Ivey (D-MD), Impacted Families, Legal Experts, and Advocates Sound the Alarm on TPS Legal Limbo Hitting Salvadoran Families
text:
For Immediate Release: October 9, 2026

Contact: Ramon.Korionoff@mail.house.gov

WATCH: Congressman Glenn Ivey (D-MD), Impacted Families, Legal Experts, and Advocates Sound the Alarm on TPS Legal Limbo Hitting Salvadoran Families

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Glenn Ivey (D-MD) joined Alianza Americas, the Catholic Legal Immigration Network (CLINIC), CARECEN DC, and America’s Voice for a virtual press event marking one month since DHS failed to make a decision on the future of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for El Salvador. Speakers, including the son of a Salvadoran TPS holder, detailed the human and legal toll of that inaction: lost jobs, blocked driver’s license renewals, and the threat of family separation for mixed-status households.

This legal limbo follows the Supreme Court’s June 25 ruling in Mullin v. Doe, which held that federal courts are largely barred from reviewing the Secretary of Homeland Security’s TPS decisions and cleared the way for terminations previously slowed by litigation. More than 170,000 Salvadorans who have lived and worked legally in the U.S., some for more than 25 years, now face the loss of their jobs and driver’s licenses, putting them at risk of immigration detention and deportation. Speakers called on the administration to follow the law and extend TPS for El Salvador, and on Congress to pass a permanent solution.

“Many Salvadorans have been here in Prince George’s County for 20, 30 years or more. They work hard. Their kids go to school with our kids, and they go to church with us,” said Rep. Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), whose district is home to approximately 90,000 Salvadorans. “The administration said it was going to focus on the worst of the worst. But this is disrupting families of people who’ve committed no crimes and have been making a difference here.”

“My mother has lived and worked in the United States for over 20 years under TPS. Now she faces the threat of being detained out of nowhere,” said Ronnie, a 24-year-old U.S. citizen and son of a Salvadoran TPS holder. “If she were detained, I would become my younger sister’s guardian, and realistically, I don’t think I could support her by myself. I want Americans to understand what thousands of children of immigrants are feeling right now. I just want a sense of normalcy for our family.”

“Government inaction is not a victory, and uncertainty is not protection. For more than two decades, Salvadoran TPS holders have built their lives in the United States, raising families, contributing to our economy, and strengthening our communities. Yet today, they face the consequences of the government's failure to provide clear legal guidance, putting their jobs, livelihoods, and futures at risk,” said Dulce Guzmán, Executive Director of Alianza Americas. “DHS must follow the law and provide clarity, but another temporary extension cannot be the ultimate solution. Salvadoran TPS holders deserve a pathway to permanent residency. Congress must act.”

“As an architect of the TPS law passed in 1990, we find it devastating to see these protections fall. TPS holders undergo background checks every time they reapply and have complied with every request this government has made of them,” said Abel Núñez, Executive Director of CARECEN of Washington, D.C. “This announcement has created chaos. Employers have terminated workers, and because driver’s licenses are tied to work permits, protections now depend on which state you live in. Salvadorans have earned a pathway to legal status and citizenship.”

“This uncertainty is not of their own making. It stems from this administration’s failure to make a decision as required by law, and no formal determination has been published in the Federal Register,” said Elnora Bassey, Policy Attorney at CLINIC. “That silence leaves mixed-status families fearing separation, workers unsure of the validity of their employment authorization, and legal practitioners unable to confidently advise their clients. We call on the administration to issue a formal determination, explain its legal basis, and provide clear guidance on TPS protections and work authorization.”

“Hundreds of thousands of people remain in the TPS program, but their lives are in limbo because this administration has refused to extend TPS for El Salvador,” said Mario Carrillo, Campaigns Director at America’s Voice, who facilitated the call. “And TPS for other countries is also ending, putting even more lives at great risk.”

title: Larsen Continues to Hold ICE Accountable at Ferndale HSI Facility
text:

“I am committed to getting answers for the people I represent about immigration operations in Northwest Washington. Today, I went to ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) facility in Ferndale. This visit is a follow-up from my visit to ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) facility in July.

“I will continue to conduct robust, close oversight of Trump’s immigration enforcement in Northwest Washington. On questions that I was not able to get complete answers to from ERO and HSI, I will keep fighting for more information for the people I represent.

“1. HSI was created to investigate human trafficking, financial crimes, narcotics and cross-border smuggling – not civil immigration violations. Agents told me that HSI staff were assigned to do ERO’s civil immigration enforcement in 2025 because ERO was not yet staffed up to fulfill Trump’s aggressive deportation agenda. I will be following up to get more information about HSI’s operations in 2025. I support HSI’s mission to stop child and drug trafficking, and HSI agents should do HSI work.

“2. HSI agents said that while they were supporting ERO operations in 2025, they stopped at the start of this year.

“3. HSI’s facility does have holding space for detaining people, and they told me they haven’t held anyone longer than four hours this year. They cannot hold an individual for more than 12 hours, and detained people have access to food, a phone room and medical treatment if needed.

“This is not case-closed on oversight of ICE activity in our region. I will be following up with more questions for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and ICE, and I will keep pushing for answers. “My office stands ready to help family members locate their loved ones in ICE custody and access legal services – call 425-252-3188 or go to larsen.house.gov/helping-you/visas-and-immigration.htm.”

title: Latta Delivers Keynote Address on Autonomous Vehicles, SELF DRIVE Act
text:
Congressman Bob Latta (OH-5) was the keynote speaker at the Ohio Chamber of Commerce's Future Forum at the Transportation Research Center in East Liberty, Ohio where he spoke on the importance of autonomous vehicles, the need for federal standards on AVs, and Ohio's leadership in the future of transportation. Congressman Latta released the following statement after the event:

"I was honored to deliver the keynote address in East Liberty at the Ohio Chamber’s Future Forum event focused on autonomous vehicles. From the traffic light to the self starter, Ohio has led the world in transportation and historically has played a major role in the evolution of this industry. This work is being done right here at the Transportation Research Center, the largest multi-user automotive testing facility in North America. Autonomous vehicles are the next chapter of this transformation, and it must be written here in Ohio.

"With autonomous vehicles becoming increasingly prevalent on streets across America, it's paramount that Congress acts to ensure the safety of these vehicles and all who encounter them. As co-chair of the Autonomous Vehicle Caucus in the House of Representatives and as a legislator who has been working on this issue for nearly a decade, safety is at the heart of all I do.

"Thousands of Americans die each year in traffic crashes. We lose family members, friends, and loved ones every day to these horrible incidents, but tragedies like these are not inevitable, and autonomous vehicles can help. It's critical that we write the law correctly to ensure safe and positive deployments for the ushering in of this new technology that will help us lower crash fatalities.

"That's why, since 2017, I have worked tirelessly on the SELF DRIVE Act, holding hundreds of meetings with stakeholder groups, co-founding the AV caucus alongside my friend, Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan, and working on numerous discussion drafts. While the legislation has evolved, my priorities have not. Safety first, a single federal framework, and American leadership are at the forefront of this work.

"This legislation would require companies to prove that their self-driving vehicles are safe before they deploy onto our roads. The bill would also establish a national crash reporting repository so the public knows how these vehicles perform. While setting a federal standard, the bill would also preserve the role of the states, allowing their longstanding authorities on traffic laws, vehicle registration, and insurance to continue.

"In addition to saving lives by lowering crashes, this new technology can enable mobility for millions of Americans including seniors and those with disabilities. This industry will offer many new jobs, especially in manufacturing, which flourishes in Ohio's Fifth Congressional District. Additionally, we cannot cede the future of auto manufacturing to Communist China who is working to out-compete us in AV production.

"Until a federal AV framework becomes law, I will not stop working on this issue, and I am confident that we will eventually be able to find a bipartisan path forward."

title: Liccardo Leads Bipartisan Push to Bring Whale Alerts to West Coast Mariners
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Bay Area Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) led a bipartisan effort to leverage technology to protect whales on the West Coast. His recent letter to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Federal Communications Commission, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration requests an expansion of Automatic Identification System (AIS) messaging technology to send whale-safety information directly to mariners along the West Coast.

“With at least 145 gray whale collisions already reported along the West Coast in 2026, we must do more to keep both whales and mariners safe,” said Liccardo. “By implementing AIS whale-safety messages, we can give real-time warnings to mariners and help them avoid deadly collisions, without disrupting maritime activities."

Liccardo and his cosigners request the agencies identify areas where AIS messaging could support voluntary speed reductions messages, determine whether existing whale detection programs can transmit information directly to mariners through AIS, and identify ways to streamline approval timelines while maintaining navigation and spectrum safeguards.

On the East Coast, federal agencies and regional partners already use AIS messaging to send vessel location-specific alerts in whale speed reduction zones. Expanding AIS whale-safety messaging to the West Coast would use technology already familiar to mariners to provide additional information about whale activity.

“Expanding this capability is particularly relevant along the West Coast, where vessel traffic and whale activity increasingly overlap,” the lawmakers wrote.

The effort builds on Liccardo’s Save Willy Act, which would establish a “Whale Desk” at the Coast Guard’s San Francisco station to centralize whale sightings and alert vessel operators when whales enter the Bay.

“Using AIS technology to identify high-risk areas and alert mariners in real time can help prevent deadly vessel collisions with whales off California while keeping vital maritime traffic moving safely,” said Geoff Shester, Director of Fishery Innovation and Senior Scientist at Oceana. “This proven technology would give agencies and ship operators a practical, science-based tool to protect whales and improve safety in our busy coastal waters for all who use them.”

“Vessel strikes are a leading cause of death and serious injury for large whales and can result in substantial property damage for mariners as well as pose a significant safety risk to those onboard. IFAW has worked tirelessly in the pursuit of reducing the threat of vessel strikes and strongly supports the use of AIS as a warming system for mariners. We're grateful to Representatives Liccardo, Case, Krishnamoorthi, Min, Moylan, and Pallone for championing the use of AIS to improve mariner safety and help reduce the risk of vessel strikes on whales along the West Coast," said Kathleen Collins, International Fund for Animal Welfare Senior Marine Campaign Manager.

Congressmembers Ed Case (HI-01), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Dave Min (CA-47), Frank Pallone (NJ-06), and James Moylan (Guam) signed the letter.

title: USPS responds to Delaware delegation on future of Ocean View Post Office
text:
OCEAN VIEW, Del. — U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester (all D-Del.) today announced that they have received a formal response from the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) regarding the continued closure and future of the Ocean View Post Office.

The response follows a letter from the delegation to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding greater transparency, a clear timeline, improved interim services, and a permanent solution for Ocean View residents who have been without a fully functioning local Post Office for more than a year.

The Ocean View Post Office closed for emergency repairs in October 2025 after problems with the facility were identified. USPS initially announced plans to repair the building, then announced in June that further evaluations had determined a full rebuild was necessary, with construction expected to begin in spring 2027 and conclude that fall.

In its latest response to the delegation, however, USPS said additional engineering concerns prompted officials to further evaluate their plans. USPS is now conducting a search for existing properties in the Ocean View community to determine whether leasing a new location would be preferable to constructing a new facility on the existing property.

“For more than a year, the people of Ocean View have dealt with changing plans and far too much uncertainty about the future of their Post Office,” said Congresswoman McBride and Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester. “We appreciate that USPS is seriously analyzing every option to restore full postal service to Ocean View, however that looks. But residents still deserve what we asked for in our letter: a permanent solution, a clear timeline, and regular, transparent communication about how USPS intends to get there. We will continue pressing USPS until Ocean View has the reliable, fully functioning Post Office this community deserves.”

USPS also addressed concerns raised by the delegation regarding interim postal services. The agency said it is preparing to replace the existing collection box at 220 Atlantic Avenue with a larger collection box, though the 11 a.m. pickup time will remain unchanged. USPS had previously announced in April that the larger box would be installed by May 30. The agency acknowledged the delay and said it expects the new box to be installed soon.

While the Ocean View facility remains closed, retail and Post Office Box services continue to operate through the Bethany Beach Post Office, just over two-and-a-half miles away, while carrier delivery continues through the Sussex County Carrier Annex in Frankford.

The delegation had also requested an in-person meeting with Postmaster General Steiner. USPS indicated that it is willing to meet with the delegation and committed to contacting congressional staff when it has a substantive update regarding the facility search. The delegation will continue working with USPS, state and local officials, and Ocean View residents to press for a timely permanent solution and ensure the community is kept informed as the process moves forward.

title: McClain Delaney Leads Call with Ocasio-Cortez, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (MD-06) is leading a congressional letter with co-leads Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Don Beyer, Kweisi Mfume, Suhas Subramanyam, and Sarah Elfreth urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.

The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.

“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”

“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” Congressman Don Beyer.

"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume.

“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”

At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.

The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.

The lawmakers request answers in three areas:

Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.

Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.

Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.

title: McIver Moves For Appeal To Be Heard En Banc By Third Circuit, Refuses to Back Down
text:
NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) and her legal counsel filed a brief requesting that the full U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit hear her case en banc.

The appeal highlights major constitutional problems with the charges the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) brought against McIver arising out of her May 2025 oversight inspection of Delaney Hall, ICE detention facility in her district. This move for hearing en banc comes after a divided panel of three Third Circuit judges refused to dismiss the case against McIver in August.

By appealing, McIver continues her fight to protect her constitutional and statutory authority to oversee ICE, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and the rest of the executive branch. The full text of the brief can be found here.

“As I have said since last May, oversight is my job. I am pursuing this step in no small part because every single day since last May, we have seen only more terror surrounding Delaney Hall—from brutality outside of its gates to retribution behind its walls and horror stories from the detainees I’ve spoken with on my many visits. What’s happening here and in ICE facilities nationwide only further proves why members of Congress need to be able to do this critical oversight work to protect people—work that Trump’s administration wants to stop by locking me in prison for 17 years,” said McIver. “Members of Congress have a right to do oversight even, and especially, when the administration does not like what they find. I will fight like hell to protect that right. I will continue to oppose these baseless charges and this intimidation, and I will keep doing my job, not without fear, but in spite of it.”

Paul J. Fishman, counsel to McIver, added context about the stakes of the case and the court’s August ruling on the same issues.

“This case is about whether the Executive Branch can interfere with and try to intimidate members of Congress who are doing the oversight the Constitution requires of them. Congresswoman McIver has been incredibly brave in taking on a fight against an administration that targeted lawmakers and others for speaking out when they see abuses,” said Fishman. “The executive branch should not and cannot be allowed to use its power over criminal prosecutions to retaliate against those it would like to silence.”

The charges against McIver stem from an oversight visit she conducted at Delaney Hall, a controversial ICE detention center in her district, in May, 2025. She is the only member of Congress under indictment by the Trump DOJ for performing constitutionally protected oversight of ICE and, if convicted, faces up to 17 years in federal prison.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 10.9.26
text:
American leadership in space represents a new frontier for technological progress.

Elon Musk’s company, SpaceX, recently undertook an orbital mission with the launch of its Starship rocket. Not to be confused with the Enterprise of Star Trek fame, the Starship launch is a steppingstone for something greater. SpaceX and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) are working together to lead manned flights to the moon.

The first step in reaching this goal will rely on low-Earth orbit (LEO). LEO refers to the lowest reach of space closest to Earth and the same altitude where the International Space Station operates. The Starship launch successfully reached LEO for the first time, setting in motion the next phase for Americans to return to the moon.

SpaceX’s LEO satellite technologies are not just seen as critical to our prospects in space.

At the federal level, I continue to advocate for LEO technologies with helping rural communities access satellite internet.

Most recently, I delivered opening remarks at an online event hosted by the Connect Everyone Coalition. The webinar focused on the two-year anniversary of Hurricane Helene and connectivity lessons from the natural disaster.

During my remarks, I highlighted the connectivity issues that impacted Ninth District communities.

Helene devastated our public communications networks. The disaster disabled services provided by our cell phone carriers. Further, the floods that swamped our region also washed away fiber optic infrastructure.

Because of the loss of communications, family members struggled to confirm the safety of their loved ones and first responder crews faced challenges with emergency operations.

These issues went on for days.

It was unclear when internet and cell phone coverage would be restored, so one group relied on SpaceX for help.

Wise County’s Health Wagon, which traveled to Damascus to help serve and treat those affected by Helene, turned to SpaceX’s Starlink.

Starlink consists of a network of LEO satellites which serves high-speed, reliable broadband internet to communities on Earth. This network reduces connectivity dead zones and provides more coverage in regions like Southwest Virginia.

Thus, Starlink is particularly helpful for mountainous and rural regions where fiber installation is extremely difficult and cost prohibitive. Amazon is launching a similar LEO program which should be available in Virginia in late 2027.

Thanks to a portable Starlink unit, a rarity in our area at the time, the Health Wagon could access internet service.

This episode showed that even in times of emergency, cell phone users can take advantage of LEO technologies.

As the recovery from Helene continues, I remain committed to expanding our broadband capabilities through LEO technologies to prepare our region for the next Helene.

Federal initiatives to support broadband innovations like LEO technologies include the Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment (BEAD) program.

In 2024, I advocated for Governor Youngkin’s BEAD Final Proposal. This set in motion various opportunities to expand broadband in Virginia.

The federal entity that runs BEAD is the National Telecommunications Information Administration (NTIA).

This summer, NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth testified before the House Committee on Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, on which I serve.

During the hearing, she discussed BEAD as well as signaled support for LEO technologies.

Later in the summer, Administrator Roth visited Bedford County to tour local broadband projects.

There are approximately 1,600 Bedford County addresses that will gain new access to broadband through BEAD funding, according to the NTIA. While new fiber installation will serve a majority of these Bedford County locations, SpaceX and Amazon will make LEO broadband available to eligible hard-to-reach locations.

Aside from BEAD, LEO broadband will get an additional boost from a bipartisan Congressional bill.

In the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, I supported the SAT Streamlining Act. Following Subcommittee approval, I voted for the bill again in the full Energy and Commerce Committee.

This bill would modernize a federal agency’s satellite licensing process by setting more precise timelines and a more predictable list of requirements for satellite applications.

In effect, we make it easier for groups to bring LEO technologies to the market to better provide reliable and secure internet access.

I am proud to have taken these actions to bridge the digital divide in Virginia and the United States.

Broadband in rural America can help our hospitals, schools, businesses and more.

As your federal representative, I will keep fighting for our rural communities to get a fair shot at broadband access.

With the same technologies, we can succeed with broadband while keeping our feet on the ground and reaching for the moon.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Rep. Panetta Convenes Local Healthcare Leaders to Address Challenges Ahead of Medicare Open Enrollment
text:
Rep. Panetta convened a roundtable to discuss provider shortages

and service challenges ahead of October 15 Medicare open enrollment.

To watch his remarks, click HERE or on the above photo.

For additional photos, click HERE.

Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together local physicians, hospital leaders, and community health providers at Santa Cruz Community Health to address seniors’ challenges accessing care ahead of Medicare open enrollment and discuss his bipartisan efforts to ensure they have coverage they can afford and rely on. With Medicare open enrollment set to start October 15, the roundtable and subsequent press availability focused on local provider shortages, rising prescription drug plan premiums, and the need for Medicare payments to keep pace with the cost of providing care.

For many seniors in California’s 19th Congressional District, choosing Medicare coverage does not guarantee they can find a local doctor accepting new patients. Medicare physician reimbursements have failed to keep pace with inflation, making it harder for practices to recruit and retain physicians and continue serving seniors in a region with a high cost of living. These pressures leave beneficiaries facing fewer options and longer waits for the benefits they earned through a lifetime of work.

“As Medicare open enrollment begins October 15, seniors deserve coverage that they paid into and can rely on. Too often in our community, however, having coverage does not mean having access to care,” said Rep. Panetta. “That’s why I helped author, introduce, and am working to pass the bipartisan Strengthening Medicare for Patients and Providers Act and the Patients First Act that would strengthen physician payments and reduce administrative burdens, helping keep local doctors in practice so seniors can access the care they earned.”

“I appreciate the opportunity to share ideas with Congressman Panetta for strengthening Medicare to better support patients and providers. The Medicare Hospice Benefit has not been updated since its introduction in 1982, despite significant changes in disease trajectories and treatments. Safety-net providers like Hospice of Santa Cruz County increasingly care for patients with complex needs and short stays, yet the current Medicare reimbursement does not adequately reflect the intensity or cost of providing this care. Without meaningful updates to the benefit, high-quality hospices like ours face growing challenges in sustaining the level of care our patients need and deserve,” said Cathy Conway, CEO, Hospice of Santa Cruz County.

A 2022 California Medical Association survey found that 76% of responding physicians reported that traditional Medicare payments do not cover their costs of providing care, and 87% reported difficulty recruiting and retaining physicians because of low Medicare payment rates and the high costs of operating a practice in California. Additionally, 41% said they planned to close their practices to new Medicare patients.

Rep. Panetta co-leads the bipartisan Strengthening Medicare for Patients and Providers Act to index physician payments to inflation and better reflect the cost of delivering care. He also helped introduce the bipartisan Patients First Act to strengthen physician payments, support primary care, and reduce administrative burdens. Together, these proposals would help sustain practices and improve seniors’ access to care.

Rep. Panetta’s bipartisan REAL Health Providers Act, signed into law this year, will require annual updates to Medicare Advantage provider directories beginning in 2028 so seniors have more accurate information when choosing coverage. He previously voted for the Inflation Reduction Act’s cap on annual out-of-pocket Medicare Part D prescription drug costs and its option to spread those expenses across the year.

title: Pappas, 189 Members of Congress Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
text:
Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) joined 189 Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.

The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.

“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”

Since the beginning of the second Trump administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely.

title: Congressman Patronis Files House Companion Bill Curtailing Drilling in the Gulf of America
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Patronis (R-FL) filed in the House of Representatives a companion bill introduced by Senators Scott and Moody, which would curtail oil drilling in the Gulf of America on the basis of protecting the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range (EGTTR).

Congressman Patronis said, “This bill is intended to protect the military test range for our military readiness. It should go without saying that while the Panhandle is facing a major hurricane, Hurricane Isaias, and the economy is tethered to tourism, this region needs to be protected from future oil and gas explorations.”

The EGTTR is a critical national security asset that supports vital military testing and training. This legislation strengthens protections for the range, ensuring uninterrupted access for military operations and helping keep our armed forces prepared for emerging threats.

The Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act would:

Stop new oil and gas activity in the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range.

Protect Eglin’s military testing and training from outside interference.

Leave existing leases in place.

Allow the moratorium to end if the Secretary of War determines the range is no longer critical.

title: ICYMI: Pelosi Joins Congressional Efforts to Protect Federal Services and Uphold Americans’ Rights
text:
Washington, D.C. — Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi joined Congressional Democratic colleagues in a series of recent letters, legislative proposals and court briefs addressing federal policies affecting San Franciscans. The efforts include calls to release housing and energy assistance funding, maintain Medicare and Head Start protections, preserve public lands and access to historical records, and protect voting rights and student survivors of sexual assault.

Protecting health care and essential services for children and families:

Pelosi joined colleagues in urging the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to reverse its decision to end the Medicare Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration, which has helped lower prescription drug coverage premiums for nearly 25 million seniors and people with disabilities. Ending the program without a plan to maintain lower costs would increase out of pocket costs for the most vulnerable San Franciscans.

Read the full letter here.

To defend early childhood education, Pelosi joined 190 of her colleagues in a bicameral letter demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s federal performance standards. Members warned that the proposal would weaken classroom safety protections, diminish the already struggling child care workforce and reduce critical health screenings and essential services. Members warned the Administration that these changes would undermine critical childhood development and leave working families without reliable child care.

Read the full letter here.

Keeping San Franciscans housed and helping them afford their energy bills:

Pelosi joined colleagues in urging the Department of Housing and Urban Development to release overdue guidance on preventing Emergency Housing Voucher funding shortfalls, warning that delays put families at risk of losing their critical rental assistance and becoming unhoused. With more than 44,000 vouchers still in use, including 920 in San Francisco, Members demanded answers from HUD to prevent interruptions in housing assistance.

Read the full letter here.

Pelosi also joined colleagues in urging the Department of Housing and Urban Development to immediately release the delayed funding notice for Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS grants and expedite renewal awards. As a proud author of HOPWA, the only federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS, this initiative supports housing development and provides critical rental assistance and resources for individuals and their families. Any disruptions to HOPWA, including expiring grants and uncertainty over renewals, threatens to interrupt these critical services and put people at risk of homelessness.

Read the full letter here.

Pelosi joined 116 of her colleagues in a bipartisan letter urging the Department of Health and Human Services to distribute Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program funding as soon as possible, which impacts 3,052 households in San Francisco. Members warned the Administration that repeated funding delays and high energy costs could leave families without heat or force them to choose between heating their homes and paying for food, medication or rent.

Read the full letter here.

Defending California’s public lands:

Pelosi joined 156 of her colleagues in a bipartisan, bicameral letter urging Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to abandon a proposed transfer of land within Yosemite National Park to provide access to a privately owned ranch. Members argued that the unprecedented transaction would brazenly benefit a private landowner and diminish public access to the historic, world-renowned park, and vigorously opposed the misuse use of the Land and Water Conservation Fund.

Read the full letter here.

Pelosi joined colleagues in overwhelmingly opposing the Administration’s shameless actions with the Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monuments, which removed nearly three million acres from protection. Members warned that opening these lands to mining and drilling threatens sacred Tribal sites, wildlife habitats, scientific resources and local recreation economies. The letter also condemns the dissolution of the Bears Ears Commission and the lack of meaningful Tribal consultation.

Read the full letter here.

Preserving San Francisco’s history:

Pelosi joined a bipartisan, bicameral letter led by Representatives Kevin Mullin and Judy Chu urging the National Archives and Records Administration to oppose closure of its San Bruno facility. Members warned the Archives that dispersing its records to six facilities across the country would make it harder for families and researchers to access California’s history, including records related to the Chinese Exclusion Act and the incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II.

Read the full letter here.

Pelosi also cosponsored the National Archives Protection Act, which would require congressional approval before the National Archives and Records Administration could close or significantly restrict access to existing regional facilities. The legislation would protect access to historical and personal records, many of which have not been digitized and can only be viewed in person, helping families and ensure researchers easily explore our history.

Read the full bill here.

Safeguarding voting rights and Americans’ personal information:

Pelosi joined a bipartisan group of current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to sustain an injunction blocking the Administration’s new Postal Service restrictions on mail-in voting in place. The brief argues that the Administration cannot unilaterally impose mail-ballot requirements on states or bar election officials from using the Postal Service to send ballots. Members emphasized that the Constitution assigns authority over federal election rules to states and Congress, and that Congress has not authorized the Postal Service to exercise the powers claimed by the Administration.

Read the full brief here.

Pelosi joined a bipartisan group of current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to reject the Administration’s emergency request to implement a federal citizenship verification database that risks disenfranchising voters. The brief argues that linking Social Security records to a government-wide system for bulk searches of sensitive personal information is illegal This action is another overt effort by this Administration to undermine the Congress and violate the separation of powers as envisioned by our Founders.

Read the full brief here.

Protecting students from sexual harassment and assault:

Pelosi joined colleagues in calling for an immediate investigation by the Department of Education’s Office of Inspector General into the Department’s failure to adequately enforce Title IX protections for student survivors. The letter urges investigators to examine whether staffing cuts, regional office closures and changes in enforcement priorities have delayed investigations and undermined accountability for campus sexual harassment and assault.

title: Pocan, Bacon Introduce Resolution Recognizing National PrEP Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -

U.S. Representatives Mark Pocan (WI-02) and Don Bacon (NE-02) today introduced a resolution recognizing October 10, 2026, as National PrEP Day and highlighting the importance of access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a critical tool for preventing HIV.

“PrEP is one of the most effective tools we have to prevent HIV, yet too many people who could benefit from it continue to face barriers to access,” said Rep. Pocan, Chair of the Congressional HIV/AIDS Caucus. “National PrEP Day is an opportunity to raise awareness, reduce stigma and ensure people across the country know about this proven HIV prevention tool.”

“PrEP is a proven tool that can prevent HIV, and we should make sure people who can benefit from it know it is available and can access it,” said Rep. Bacon. “National PrEP Day is an opportunity to raise awareness, improve access and give people the information they need to protect their health. I'm joining Rep. Pocan on this bipartisan resolution supporting evidence-based efforts to prevent HIV and help more Americans access the care they need.”

When taken as prescribed, PrEP reduces the risk of acquiring HIV through sex by about 99 percent. Despite the effectiveness of PrEP, disparities in access and uptake persist due to factors including cost, stigma and barriers to health care.

Cosponsors include Representatives Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Mark Takano (CA-39) and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

title: Scanlon, Welch, Blumenthal, Min Initiate Probe into Improper Influence of Cabinet Members in Trump Pardons
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Constitution and Limited Government, today joined Senator Peter Welch (D-VT), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on The Constitution, Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Anti-Corruption Task Force, in raising questions about the role of cabinet members in securing presidential pardons, as part of their ongoing investigation into executive clemency actions since January 20, 2025.

The bicameral group of lawmakers are looking into whether U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin used their access to inappropriately influence President Trump’s decision to grant full presidential pardons to convicted felons Trevor Milton and Troy Lake.

“Public reports of high-profile individuals—including yourself—appealing directly to the President on behalf of pardon recipients risk subversion of the established pardon review processes by financial influence and political access,” write the lawmakers. “Article II, Section 2, Clause 1 of the U.S. Constitution authorizes the President to ‘grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offenses against the United States, except in Cases of Impeachment.’ The U.S. Supreme Court has characterized executive clemency as ‘an act of grace’ exercised for the ‘public welfare.’ President Trump’s use of this authority appears to deviate from this traditional purpose.”

The lawmakers conclude: “Congress has a compelling interest in ensuring that the constitutional pardon power is exercised with fairness and transparency. Given these circumstances, we are seeking additional information to better understand the extent to which influence and access have overridden the standard pardon review process.”

In their letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the lawmakers request answers about Secretary Kennedy’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to pardon convicted fraudster Trevor Milton, who defrauded and misled investors regarding technology and products related to his company, Nikola Corporation. The victims of Mr. Milton’s fraud include individuals who lost their retirement savings and others who had never invested in the stock market before. President Trump’s pardon eliminated Milton’s obligation to potentially pay $660 million in court-ordered restitution to his victims. Milton did not serve any of his four-year prison sentence.

“According to public reporting, you personally appealed to the President to grant Mr. Milton a pardon, arguing that he had been unfairly prosecuted by the previous administration’s Justice Department. Days before granting Mr. Milton’s pardon request, President Trump reportedly told him to call you and thank you for convincing the President to grant him a pardon,” write the lawmakers. “Your reported involvement in this matter is particularly troubling, given that Mr. Milton reportedly donated $750,000 to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) Political Action Committee (PAC), which was launched in late 2024 by senior members of your presidential campaign to unite your supporters behind President Trump. Public reporting also indicates that Mr. Milton and his wife donated approximately $1,800,000 to President Trump’s 2024 reelection campaign a month before the election.”

In their letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin, the lawmakers demand answers about the administrator’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to grant a full presidential pardon to Troy Lake, and a subsequent corporate pardon to Lake’s company, Elite Diesel Service Inc. Lake’s conviction arose from allegations that he and his company disabled the monitoring components of emissions control systems on hundreds of heavy-duty commercial trucks.

The lawmakers write: “According to public reporting, two friends of Mr. Lake petitioned you in an August 2025 email, urging you to reach out to the President to request a pardon. Mr. Lake’s wife publicly attributed progress on her husband’s pardon efforts to your subsequent intervention. Such progress included a phone call with Sean Hayes, a White House attorney who works closely on pardons.”

The lawmakers’ letters seek information from HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin regarding:

The nature of their relationships with the pardoned felons;

The process by which clemency requests were initiated and considered;

Whether intermediaries, lobbyists, or advocates were involved;

Any contacts with Trump Administration officials or associates;

Their role in any other clemency decisions made by the Trump Administration;

Whether financial contributions or payments were made in connection with clemency efforts; and

The extent of third-party advocacy supporting the requests.

Read the lawmakers’ full letters to HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin.

title: Schakowsky, Trahan, Kean Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect FTC Whistleblowers as The Social Reckoning Hits Theaters
text:
Full Text of Bill (PDF)

WASHINGTON– As The Social Reckoning, a new film about Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen, hits theaters nationwide, Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) today introduced bipartisan legislation to protect whistleblowers who disclose wrongdoing at their current or former workplaces that fall under the jurisdiction of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).

The FTC Whistleblower Act of 2026 would protect current and former employees from retaliation when they disclose violations of consumer protection and antitrust laws to the FTC. The legislation would also establish incentives for whistleblowers to come forward with information about unlawful conduct.

“Frances Haugen took an enormous risk when she came forward with information about what was happening inside Facebook,” said Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky. “Her courage helped expose serious concerns about the impact of social media on our children and families. But no worker should have to choose between doing the right thing and losing their livelihood. Our bipartisan bill makes sure whistleblowers who expose wrongdoing to the FTC have the protections they deserve.”

“When something goes wrong inside a company, the workers there are often the first to know. Today, if they bring that information to the FTC, they take the risk alone,” said Congresswoman Lori Trahan. “The FTC Whistleblower Act gives them real protections and a real reason to come forward. That’s good for workers, good for families, and good for the companies doing things the right way. Frances Haugen showed what one person can do. Nobody should have to be that brave just to tell the truth.”

“The FTC Whistleblower Act would empower workers to safely report corporate misconduct without fear of retaliation. By protecting whistleblowers who report misconduct, the bill will allow the FTC to uncover violations and build strong enforcement cases,” said Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. “With increased transparency into harmful practices, the bill ensures companies can’t operate in the shadows and protects workers from retaliation.”

The FTC is the federal agency responsible for enforcing a broad range of consumer protection and antitrust laws. Unlike some other federal agencies, the FTC does not have a comprehensive whistleblower protection and award program for employees who report violations within its jurisdiction.

“This legislation is an excellent opportunity for Congress to apply cohesive rights across federal agencies, including the FTC, in accordance with their sustained leadership on whistleblower protections. The FTC’s ability to protect consumers and keep big businesses in check goes hand in hand with whistleblowers keeping Americans safe. Providing protections and best practice incentives for whistleblowers coming forward with original information to the Commission is a nonpartisan issue and essential to good governance,” said Maya Efrati, Director of Legislation & Congressional Affairs at Government Accountability Project.

“Whistleblowers are our most effective safeguard against corporate fraud and corruption. This bill strengthens essential protections and incentives so that insiders can more safely expose wrongdoing that harms American families and consumers. POGO appreciates Congresswoman Schakowsky’s leadership on this crucial bill that will enhance regulatory oversight, hold powerful corporations more accountable, and protect the public’s trust," said Joe Spielberger, Senior Policy Counsel, Project On Government Oversight.

The need for stronger protections was highlighted by Haugen’s 2021 disclosures of internal Facebook documents, which became known as the “Facebook Files.” Haugen later testified before Congress about the company’s practices and their potential impact on young people.
