title: Congresswoman Simon Introduces Legislation to Reduce Voting Barriers, Expand Voting Poll Access, and Protect Voters with Disabilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12) introduced two bills to reduce voting barriers by improving accessibility for voters, especially older Americans and people with disabilities, and bolster election security. She joined Reps. Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), and Jamie Raskin (MD-08) in introducing The Accessible Voting Act; and she joined Reps. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) and Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) in introducing The Dropbox Access Act.

The Accessible Voting Act would establish the Office of Accessibility within the Election Assistance Commission (EAC) to oversee state and local elections to ensure that voter accessibility needs are adequately met, by expanding the number of options to fairly cast ballots. The bill would also establish a website for National Voter Accessibility and fund a National Resource Center to further train election officials and poll workers on accessibility.

The Dropbox Access Act, would require states to provide in-person, secure, and clearly labeled ballot drop boxes in every county for federal elections. The bill would require counties to provide a minimum of one drop box per 20,000 voting-age residents and require that drop boxes are accessible 24 hours a day starting from 45 days before the election until polls close.

As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, Congresswoman Simon is committed to defending the civil rights of Americans with disabilities and has continuously opposed rollbacks of disability protections. She has introduced numerous pieces of legislation aimed at expanding accessibility in small businesses and public transportation, and she has pressed the Trump Administration on their failure to protect workers with disabilities.

“Our elders fought for our voting rights with blood, sweat, and tears – and yet too many people, particularly older Americans and Americans with disabilities, still face barriers to voting such as inaccessible polling locations or access to voter information. Both the Accessible Voting Act and Dropbox Access Act will improve voter accessibility for requesting mail-in ballots, accessing voter registration info, and when showing up to the ballot box,” said Rep. Simon. “As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, improving accessibility to ensure that all Americans can equally access resources and participate in society is a top priority of mine. I am proud to lead on these bills with Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon to ensure ALL individuals can equally participate in local and federal elections to make their rightful voices heard.”

“Our democracy thrives when every eligible voter is able to participate, and these bills will remove barriers that all too often make it more difficult for Americans to cast their ballots. I’ve seen how expanding accessibility and access to ballot boxes has improved voter turnout and engagement in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,” said Rep. Scanlon. “I’m proud to introduce these bills to advance more equitable and just voting policies for all Americans.”

“American democracy works best when all citizens can participate and vote, no matter where they’re from, what language they speak or whether they live with a disability,” said Rep. Raskin. “Our Accessible Voting Act strengthens access to the ballot box and addresses a wide range of systemic deficiencies, so no eligible voter is left alone to overcome barriers to casting a ballot.”

“The ability for everyone to have their voice heard is central to our American ideals—yet too often people with disabilities face unnecessary barriers in both registering to vote and casting their ballots, preventing them from fully participating in our democracy,” said Rep. Dean. “This legislation will help improve registration processes and eliminate barriers to voting, including by reauthorizing grants to improve voting accessibility for older Americans and those with disabilities. By breaking down these barriers, our communities can be better represented by every voice. I'm thankful to partner with Congresswoman Scanlon and Congressman Raskin to pass these essential bills.”

“We should be making it more accessible for Americans to vote, not harder,” said Rep. Garcia. “But the Trump administration and its Republican allies continue to attack voting rights and put up new barriers to the ballot box. That is why I am proud to once again co-lead the Dropbox Access Act, a practical bill to make sure voters have fair, accessible options to return their ballots. We should be protecting the right to vote, not suppressing it.”

title: Congresswoman Lee, Senator Cortez Masto Highlight Legislation to Help Human Trafficking Survivors
text:
Watch and download video here

LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, at the Harry Reid International Airport, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) announced the reintroduction of their bipartisan, bicameral Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act. They were joined by Clark County Commission Chairman Michael N. Naft, and Lauren Boitel, Co-Founder of the Nevada Policy Council on Human Trafficking. This legislation will help survivors of human trafficking access air travel to escape their abusers and get the care they need.

“When fleeing violence and abuse, many human trafficking survivors do not have access to the identification documents they need to travel by plane, like drivers’ licenses or passports. Human traffickers often control access of victims’ identification documents, and when trafficking victims flee, many must leave their documents behind,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “Our legislation will facilitate air travel for these survivors so that they may return to their families and communities and begin to heal.”

“Jimmy Deal was an American hero – a man who made it easier for survivors of human trafficking to get approved for air travel without their IDs,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “Our legislation, introduced in his honor, will make it easier for human trafficking survivors to escape their captors and get the help they need. We will keep pushing to make sure it becomes law.”

The legislation recognizes the late TSA officer James “Jimmy” Deal, who took the role of Assistant Federal Security Director in the Reno-Tahoe International Airport and led the effort to raise awareness of human trafficking at the airport, while also working with agencies in Nevada to assist victims of human trafficking to escape.

“As one of the nation’s busiest airports, Harry Reid International Airport has both an opportunity and a responsibility to help raise awareness of human trafficking and connect people with resources. Supporting survivors means recognizing the challenges they may face beyond escaping a trafficking situation, including something as fundamental as having the identification needed to travel. This legislation helps address that barrier and reinforces the important role airports can play in helping survivors reach safety,” said Chairman Naft.

“No survivor should have to navigate the journey to safety alone. When someone finds the courage to leave exploitation, they deserve compassion, dignity, and support—not additional barriers because they lack identification or are navigating an unfamiliar and overwhelming system. The Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act helps ensure survivors can access trauma-informed assistance and trusted support to reach safety and begin rebuilding their lives, and we are grateful to Congresswoman Lee and Senator Cortez Masto for advancing a more compassionate, survivor-centered response to human trafficking,” said Lauren Boitel, Co-Founder of the Nevada Policy Council on Human Trafficking.

The Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act will:

Encourage collaboration between Transportation Security Administration (TSA) agents and non-profits that provide services to trafficking survivors.

Create a process to assist trafficking survivors with air travel by:

Establishing a “Trafficking Survivor Point of Contact” (TSPoC) position by the TSA at each airport where it conducts screenings of passengers and property.

Calling for the establishment of contact, communication, and relationships between service-providing organizations and the TSPoCs to pre-emptively create avenues for identity verification of escaping survivors.

Include requirements of adequate training for each TSPoC to create a more seamless process with specialized focus.

Required trainings and responsibilities incorporate trauma-informed services and ensure that survivors and escapees are supported throughout the process of reunification with their families and communities.

title: Rep. Sykes Hosts 2026 Women in Leadership Conference
text:
Pictured: Congresswoman Sykes with Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, Rep. Shontel Brown (OH-11), and Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51) at the Women in Leadership Conference.

AKRON, OH — U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted the 2026 Women in Leadership Conference at the Akron Art Museum, bringing together more than 200 women entrepreneurs, elected officials, labor leaders, and community members from across Ohio's 13th Congressional District. The conference connected local entrepreneurs, innovators, and community members in a collaborative environment to share knowledge, build relationships, and help one another grow.

“Today was a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish when women lift each other up,” said Rep. Sykes. “I'm grateful to every speaker and guest who joined us for honest conversations about leadership, economic empowerment, and public service. I look forward to continuing to build a pipeline of women leaders across our community, and to keep fighting for policies that give every woman the opportunity to thrive.”

Rep. Sykes was joined by U.S. House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, Rep. Shontel Brown (OH-11), and Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51) for a panel on women in Congress, where they discussed the barriers women face in seeking elected office and the unique perspective women legislators bring to policymaking.

Local female business leaders, including Elizabeth Bartz, Misty Beasley, and Mary Fantozzi, shared what it takes to build and sustain a business in a moderated conversation facilitated by Rep. Jasmine Crockett (TX-30).

The day closed with a fireside chat between Rep. Sykes and United Steelworkers International President Roxanne D. Brown, inspired by the 1912 "Bread & Roses" labor movement and the idea that working people deserve both security and dignity. The conversation focused on inspiring the next generation of women leaders and the importance of representation in decision-making roles.

Attendees also had the opportunity to connect with Rep. Sykes' constituent services team, who were on hand to help residents with issues involving federal agencies. This was the second Women in Leadership Conference hosted by Rep. Sykes. Those interested in learning more about her work for Ohio's 13th Congressional District can visit sykes.house.gov.

title: Reps. Tlaib, Correa reintroduce resolution honoring Alex Odeh
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Lou Correa (CA-46) today reintroduced a resolution remembering and honoring the life and legacy of Alex Odeh. The resolution acknowledges Alex’s impact on his community and the country, and reaffirms the importance of pursuing justice against those responsible for his death.

“Alex Odeh was a teacher, a poet, and a man of peace, and he was murdered in our community simply for speaking up for civil and human rights,” said Correa. “He was a voice for peace and dignity in Orange County. Remembering him is the least we can do, and pursuing justice for his family is our obligation.”

Rep. Correa represents the district where Alex and his family lived and where the attack took place.

“Alex Odeh dedicated his life to achieving true equality and equity for all. For daring to push for a better tomorrow, Alex was assassinated by members of the Jewish Defense League, and his killers have yet to be brought to justice,” said Tlaib. “This horrific act of anti-Arab and anti-Palestinian violence was, and is not, new. But this violence will never silence us. Those who continue to fear-monger and incite hate against us will not win. Arab and Palestinian Americans are still here, loud and proud, carrying on Alex’s legacy.”

Read the bill text here.

About Alex Odeh

Alex was born in Jifna, Palestine, and lived in Orange County, California, for most of his adult life, including Santa Ana. He was a peace activist who worked to promote civil liberties for Arab-Americans in the United States. Alex Odeh was the Southern California Regional Director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC).

On October 11, 1985, Alex was killed when a pipe bomb exploded as he entered the ADC regional office in Santa Ana, California. Although the primary suspects have long been known, no one has been brought to justice. The investigation remains open.

title: Congressman Valadao Introduces Legislation to Recognize Armenia for Hosting the Convention on Biological Diversity
text:
WASHINGTON – This week, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) and Rep. Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) introduced a bipartisan resolution commending Armenia for hosting the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations (U.N.) Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17). This gathering in Yerevan, Armenia provides an important opportunity for nations around the world to come together and discuss the environmental challenges facing our planet.

The resolution also recognizes the United States’ leadership in advancing agroforestry and conservation research around the globe through our universities, nonprofit organizations, agricultural producers, and scientists. Additionally, it highlights Armenia’s efforts to plant nearly 10 million trees and celebrates the strong cooperation between the United States and Armenia on conservation and environmental stewardship.

“As co-chair of the Congressional Caucus on Armenian Issues, I’m proud to introduce this bipartisan resolution recognizing Armenia’s strong commitment to conservation and environmental stewardship,” said Congressman Valadao. “COP17 provides an important opportunity for leaders around the world to come together to address critical environmental challenges, and I commend Armenia for taking a leading role in this important conversation while strengthening the enduring partnership between our two nations.”

“Armenia holds a special place in my heart, and I have been proud to stand with the Armenian people throughout my time in Congress,” said Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. “Hosting COP17 gives Armenia a great opportunity to show the world the beauty of the country they have fought so hard to preserve. As nations come together in Yerevan to confront the loss of biodiversity and find better ways to protect our natural resources, Armenia will be at the center of that important work. I’m proud to help lead this bipartisan resolution celebrating this moment and ensuring Armenia can protect its natural heritage for generations to come.”

"Conservation is not independent of security or sovereignty," said Armenia Tree Project Founder Carolyn Mugar. "By welcoming Armenia as host of COP17 and affirming U.S.-Armenia cooperation on forestry, water management, and wildfire prevention, this resolution treats Armenia's forests as the strategic national asset that they are. We thank the leadership of the Congressional Armenian Caucus for this important legislative initiative."

title: Valadao, Fong Welcome VA Secretary Collins to Bakersfield for New Clinic Announcement
text:
BAKERSFIELD – Today, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) and Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) hosted Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Secretary Doug Collins in Bakersfield to announce the new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic. This new clinic will replace the existing decades-old clinic in Bakersfield which is unable to meet increased patient demand and support existing services.

As a member of the House Committee on Appropriations, Congressman Valadao has secured language in the Fiscal Year 2022, 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027 Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Acts encouraging VA to move forward with construction.

“Our veterans have sacrificed so much to protect our nation and preserve our freedoms, and when they come home, they deserve access to high-quality VA healthcare in their communities,” said Congressman Valadao. “For over thirty years, the existing Bakersfield clinic has served thousands of veterans across our region, but that facility is aging, patient demand has only grown, and it doesn’t have the space or resources needed to meet our veterans’ needs. The new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic will better meet demand and expand access to essential services, including primary care, mental health, dental, rehabilitation, and other specialty services. This is an important investment in the health and well-being of our Central Valley veterans, and I want to thank Secretary Collins, the administration, and Congressman Fong for their continued partnership in making this project a reality. I look forward to seeing our Valley veterans benefit from this new facility soon!”

“Today is a significant step forward for the veterans of Kern County and it has been a long time coming,” said Congressman Fong. “After years of frivolous legal delays, the VA has accepted this new modernized clinic, with a target to welcome its first patients this December. Our veterans will finally be receiving care in a modern space worthy of their service, but we are not done. Today allows us to build and construct the permanent facility our veterans were promised, and I will not stop until that job is finished. Thank you to Secretary Doug Collins and the entire Trump Administration for making this a priority and delivering for the veterans of the Central Valley.”

“For too long, Bakersfield Veterans had to make do with a clinic that suffered from HVAC and plumbing problems, and didn’t have enough space to meet Veterans’ growing needs,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “Under President Trump’s leadership, and thanks to the advocacy of Reps. Valadao and Fong, Veterans will get the modern facility they deserve. The new clinic also enables VA to exit a horrible lease agreement that was costing us millions of additional dollars per year for a sub-standard facility – that means we can direct more resources to Veteran care.”

Background:

The new, modernized Bakersfield VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic will replace the existing decades-old facility, which has struggled to keep pace with growing patient demand and provide the space needed to expand services. After years of delays related to site availability and legal challenges, the project is moving forward following a July 2025 court ruling in favor of the City of Bakersfield.

The approximately 30,000-square-foot facility will offer a full slate of expanded care options, including primary care, audiology and speech pathology, mental health, homeless services, dental, eye care, enrollment and eligibility, laboratory services, nutrition and food services, physical medicine and rehabilitation, telehealth, and women’s health. Veterans will continue receiving care from their existing providers, with the new facility providing additional space to meet their needs. The new clinic will also allow the VA to redirect funding previously spent on the outdated facility’s rent toward serving veterans.

title: Rep. Van Epps’ STORK Act Reduces the Financial Burden of Welcoming a Child
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Rep. Matt Van Epps (TN-07) introduced the Savings for Tomorrow’s Opportunities, Raising Kids (STORK) Act. This legislation raises the Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution limit by $2,000 per child in the year a family welcomes a child through birth or adoption. This will give parents the tax-advantaged savings they need to help cover maternity care, delivery, and newborn medical expenses.

Rep. Van Epps said, “Making families stronger and setting them up for success will strengthen our nation as a whole. The United States is one of the most expensive countries to give birth in, costing the average family $25,000, with only a portion of that covered by insurance. It's time to help parents fill in the gap.”

He continued, “My wife and I know how hard and how expensive it is to care for a newborn. Getting an unexpectedly expensive hospital bill just as you're figuring out your infant’s sleeping and feeding schedule can be overwhelming. That’s why I want to give new families more choice and more power over their finances. My STORK Act empowers parents to increase their HSA contributions to help meet the costs of maternity care, delivery, and newborn healthcare. Having a baby is expensive; we should empower parents to plan ahead, and Health Savings Accounts are a great way to do that.”

title: Velázquez, Grijalva Lead Resolution Recognizing World Contraception Day
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Reps. Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ) introduced a House resolution recognizing World Contraception Day and calling for expanded access to contraception and reproductive health care in the United States and around the world.

“Access to contraception is fundamental to giving people the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies, families, and futures,” said Rep. Velázquez. “Yet millions of people still face barriers to getting the care and information they need. On World Contraception Day, we are reaffirming that contraception is essential health care and that everyone deserves affordable, reliable access to it. I am proud to join Congresswoman Grijalva in continuing this fight for reproductive freedom at home and around the world.”

“Everyone deserves access to contraception and the freedom to make decisions about their own health and future,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Too many people still face barriers to the care they need, especially in communities that have been underserved for far too long. On World Contraception Day, we’re standing up for affordable, accessible reproductive health care for everyone.”

The resolution highlights persistent barriers to contraceptive access in the United States and globally. An estimated 218 million women in economically developing countries have an unmet need for modern contraception. In the United States, one-third of adult women who have attempted to obtain prescription contraception have reported barriers to access, while more than 19 million women of reproductive age who need publicly funded contraception live in areas without reasonable access to a health center offering the full range of contraceptive methods.

The resolution also recognizes longstanding racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic disparities in reproductive health care and the barriers faced by communities of color, Native people, immigrants, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people living in areas with limited access to reproductive health providers.

Among other provisions, the resolution calls on Congress and the administration to expand access to free or affordable contraception, ensure access to medically accurate information and comprehensive insurance coverage, address contraceptive deserts and reproductive health disparities, and expand access and coverage for over-the-counter birth control and other forms of contraception.

The resolution further recognizes the broader benefits of contraceptive access, including allowing people to plan and space pregnancies and pursue their educational, career, and life goals.

title: Vindman Supports Legislation to Prevent Illegal Domestic Troop Deployments and Voter Intimidation Ahead of Midterm Election
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) joined Congressman Pat Ryan (N.Y.-18) and four of their Democratic Veteran colleagues in the U.S. House in introducing legislation to prevent the president from weaponizing the military to interfere with elections. Specifically, the bill would empower Congress to stop or reverse any domestic troop deployment ordered by the president.

The introduction follows months of threats and actions by the Trump Administration to interfere with the November midterm elections and amid new reports from the Atlantic that advisors close to the President are encouraging him to declare martial law. Trump has repeatedly refused to rule out declaring a national emergency on elections, has already deployed thousands of U.S. troops against U.S. citizens in American cities, and suggested that Republicans should “nationalize” the midterm elections and “take over” the voting process. When asked directly in a House Armed Services Committee (HASC) hearing, a senior Trump military official refused to rule out troop deployments to polling sites.

“As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our troops should never be asked to carry out the political will of a president at the expense of our democracy. Our military swears an oath to the U.S. Constitution and the American people, not any one president or political party,” said Vindman. “The prospect of using our armed forces to influence or interfere with our elections is dangerous and fundamentally at odds with the oath every service member takes. Congress must make clear that our military cannot be weaponized to interfere with Americans’ right to vote, and that our elections must remain free from intimidation, and military interference.”

“Patriots in uniform sign up to fight for fundamental American freedoms – not against them. Trump using U.S. servicemembers as political pawns is straight-up un-American, and we’re not going to let him get away with it,” said Ryan. “Trump and those around him are scared – they know the American people are fed up with the war in Iran and skyrocketing prices. Instead of working to lower costs, Trump and his team are cooking up ways to intimidate voters, refusing to rule out domestic troop deployments. This bill provides a necessary check on the President. If he deploys troops, Congress can and will stop him. We won’t let this chickenhawk president exploit our servicemembers just because he can’t face the fact that the American people are fed up with his failed agenda of higher costs and unprecedented corruption.”

Joining Vindman and Ryan are fellow Democratic veterans and U.S. Representatives Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-02), Chris Deluzio (Pa.-17), Chrissy Houlahan (Pa.-06), and Jimmy Panetta (Calif.-19).

Senator Elissa Slotkin (Mich.) introduced companion legislation in the Senate. The bicameral legislation also includes $1 billion in new resources for state and local law enforcement on the ground.

BACKGROUND

Vindman is a 25-year Army veteran and member of the Democratic Veterans Caucus; Vindman also sits on the House Armed Services Committee, where he has become the leading voice of opposition to Trump’s war in Iran.

title: Baldwin Demands Answers from Verizon on Plans to End Landline Service
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) demanded answers from Verizon CEO Dan Schulman regarding the company’s plan to transition away from copper-based voice service, raising concerns that some Wisconsinites could be left without reliable phone service if an adequate alternative is not in place, particularly in rural areas where wireless or other replacement services may be limited. Baldwin’s call comes as Verizon plans to retire copper facilities at 136 Wisconsin wire centers and discontinue traditional landline service.

"While I recognize the need to modernize aging telecommunications infrastructure, I am concerned that some affected Wisconsinites, particularly those in rural areas, may not have access to an immediate, adequate and reliable replacement service,” wrote Senator Baldwin in the letter to Verizon CEO Dan Schulman. “These concerns are especially important where customers rely on landline service for emergency communications."

"I request that Verizon commit to ensuring that no Wisconsin customer loses copper-based voice service until an adequate replacement has been successfully installed and activated,” Baldwin concluded.

Despite Verizon’s assurances, Wisconsin communities remain concerned that available alternatives may be inadequate because of geographic limitations, high costs associated with certain replacement options, and existing gaps in reliable cellular coverage.

In her letter, Senator Baldwin pressed Verizon to answer several questions about its plans to retire copper-based telephone service across Wisconsin, including:

How many Wisconsin customers currently receive voice service over copper facilities Verizon intends to retire? Please provide the number of residential and business customers, broken down by county and wire center.

What replacement voice services has Verizon identified for affected Wisconsin customers, including fiber, fixed wireless, mobile wireless, cable/VoIP, or service provided by another carrier? How many customers are expected to rely on each type of replacement?

How many affected Wisconsin customers, if any, do not currently have a verified replacement voice service available?

How will Verizon verify that replacement service is available at a customer’s location? Does verification mean map coverage, an address-level serviceability check, confirmation that service can actually be ordered and installed, on-site testing, or some other standard?

What process is available when a customer disputes Verizon’s determination that an adequate replacement exists? Will Verizon maintain existing copper service while such a dispute is resolved?

What protections will replacement services provide for reliable 911 access during power outages and other emergencies? What battery-backup capabilities will Verizon provide, and for how long are those systems expected to operate during an outage?

How will the cost of replacement services, including installation, equipment, and recurring charges, compare with the cost of customers’ existing copper-based voice service?

Are any affected customers located in areas where Verizon or Frontier plans to deploy fiber or other upgraded infrastructure? If so, will Verizon maintain existing copper voice service until that planned network is operational and available to the customer?

Full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. Schulman,

I am reaching out regarding Verizon’s planned discontinuance of legacy telecommunications services, including Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM) and Plain Old Telephone Service (POTS), and the related retirement of copper facilities across Wisconsin. As part of Verizon and Frontier Communications’ Section 214 discontinuance application (WC Docket No. 26-170), Verizon may begin discontinuing covered TDM/POTS voice services on or after November 16, 2026. Separately, Verizon has announced plans to retire remaining copper facilities at 136 wire centers across Wisconsin. While I recognize the need to modernize aging telecommunications infrastructure, I am concerned that some affected Wisconsinites, particularly those in rural areas, may not have access to an immediate, adequate and reliable replacement service. These concerns are especially important where customers rely on landline service for emergency communications.

To better understand how Verizon intends to protect affected customers during this transition, I request that you provide answers to the following questions:

How many Wisconsin customers currently receive voice service over copper facilities Verizon intends to retire? Please provide the number of residential and business customers, broken down by county and wire center.

What replacement voice services has Verizon identified for affected Wisconsin customers, including fiber, fixed wireless, mobile wireless, cable/VoIP, or service provided by another carrier? How many customers are expected to rely on each type of replacement?

How many affected Wisconsin customers, if any, do not currently have a verified replacement voice service available?

How will Verizon verify that replacement service is available at a customer’s location? Does verification mean map coverage, an address-level serviceability check, confirmation that service can actually be ordered and installed, on-site testing, or some other standard?

What process is available when a customer disputes Verizon’s determination that an adequate replacement exists? Will Verizon maintain existing copper service while such a dispute is resolved?

What protections will replacement services provide for reliable 911 access during power outages and other emergencies? What battery-backup capabilities will Verizon provide, and for how long are those systems expected to operate during an outage?

How will the cost of replacement services, including installation, equipment, and recurring charges, compare with the cost of customers’ existing copper-based voice service?

Are any affected customers located in areas where Verizon or Frontier plans to deploy fiber or other upgraded infrastructure? If so, will Verizon maintain existing copper voice service until that planned network is operational and available to the customer?

I request that Verizon commit to ensuring that no Wisconsin customer loses copper-based voice

service until an adequate replacement has been successfully installed and activated.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter, and I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

###

title: NEWS: Baldwin Calls Out Trump Admin for Canceling $1.5 Million in Funding for Appleton Airport
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) is calling out the Trump Administration for canceling $1.5 million in federal funding for the Appleton International Airport that would have helped the airport cut energy costs and improve resiliency.

“The Appleton International Airport plays a critical role for the Fox Valley economy – bringing visitors and tourism dollars into our communities, connecting local businesses to customers and markets, and supporting good-paying jobs,” said Senator Baldwin. “Now, President Trump is playing politics and shutting down a commonsense project that would modernize the airport and lower energy costs for years to come. This is flat out wrong, and the administration should reverse this decision immediately. Wisconsin families deserve to have their hard-earned dollars invested back in their communities, and I’m going to keep fighting to do just that.”

The $1.5 million was awarded through the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Airport Improvement Program (AIP) and would have been used to install a solar array and microgrid system with battery storage. The project would enhance sustainability and ensure that the Airport remains operational during grid outages and adverse weather conditions. The Trump Administration’s Department of Transportation (DOT) discontinued the grant, claiming that the project did not meet agency priorities.

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper Introduce Legislation to Protect Nonprofit And Religious Community Spaces at Heightened Risk of Attack
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper introduced the Safer Spaces for All Act, legislation to better equip at-risk nonprofit institutions to protect their visitors and help ensure that all Americans can visit their places of worship, schools, and community centers freely and without fear. Congressmen Joe Neguse (D-Colo.) and Don Bacon (R-Neb.) led companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“In light of the recent surge in anti-Semitic, Islamophobic, and other violent hate-based incidents in the United States, the importance of programs that provide religious communities with increased security cannot be overstated,” said Bennet. “We have a responsibility to confront prejudice everywhere, and the Safer Spaces for All Act is an essential step forward for Colorado.”

“Antisemitism, Islamaphobia, and other forms of hate have no place in our country,” said Hickenlooper. “Unfortunately, we see hate rear its ugly head all too often. This bill will ensure that Americans feel secure when they enter their places of worship.”

The Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) provides at-risk nonprofit organizations – like synagogues, mosques, schools, community centers and other places of gathering – with critical resources to bolster their security amid heightened risk of attack. The program is particularly important to faith-based organizations that are encountering a troubling rise in prejudice and animosity.

The NSGP Improvement Act of 2022 expanded the eligible uses of NSGP funds to include payments to contracted security personnel and administrative expenses. However, grantees currently cannot use NSGP funds to pay permanent salaried security employees, or hire personnel to apply for NSGP funds. For organizations in remote areas particularly, it can be logistically difficult to reliably find private security vendors or off-duty law enforcement to hire for their level of security needed. This bill would help the NSGP accomplish its intended goal to keep at-risk organizations safe by further expanding eligible uses of NSGP funds.

Specifically, the Safer Spaces for All Act would allow NSGP funds to be used to:

Hire permanent onsite security personnel;

Hire off-duty police officers; and

Hire personnel to apply for NSGP funding (capped at 5% of total grant) so that applying organizations do not have to rely solely on volunteers.

“Security is not one-size-fits-all. For many houses of worship, community centers, and other nonprofits – trained personnel and the capacity to manage security funding are just as critical as the cameras, barriers, and other physical improvements. The Safe Space for All Act would provide institutions the flexibility to use NSGP funding where it can have the greatest impact – making the program more accessible, responsive, and effective. JEWISHcolorado and the Jewish Community Relations Council thank Senator Bennet for his continued leadership in strengthening this vital program and helping communities gather, worship, learn, and serve safely,” said the Jewish Community Relations Council.

“Having an off-duty Denver Police Officer present during our daily and Friday prayers transformed our security landscape. While physical fortifications are essential, they cannot replace the immediate deterrence and peace of mind that a trained officer provides. For our community to truly feel secure while fulfilling our daily worship, grant programs like the NSGP must allow funding for active security personnel,” said Rafaat Ludin, Executive Director of the Downtown Denver Islamic Center.

Bennet has a strong record of working to protect religious communities from targeted violence. In December 2025, Bennet led his Colorado Democratic colleagues – U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper and U.S. Representatives Joe Neguse, Diana DeGette, Brittany Pettersen, and Jason Crow – on a letter to former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem urging the DHS to protect religious communities in Colorado and across the country by implementing the Nonprofit Security Grant Program Improvement Act, legislation passed through the Fiscal Year 2023 National Defense Authorization Act. In June 2025, Bennet and Hickenlooper wrote to Senate leadership advocating for $500 million for the NGSP program in Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations bills. In April 2024, Bennet led the effort to pass the April 2024 national security supplemental, which included $400 million for the NGSP.

The text of the bill is available HERE. A summary of the bill is available HERE.

title: Senator Blumenthal: Week in Review 10/2/2026-10/9/2026
text:
Urging Roadside Safety Measures

[Hartford, CT] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) joined law enforcement, tow truck operators, and road safety advocates to remind motorists to slow down and move over for emergency vehicles, first responders and others on Connecticut roads. Over the last month, a Connecticut Department of Transportation worker and a tow truck driver were killed while on the job. Elvin Hernandez was performing regular maintenance on I-95 when he was struck and killed by a driver in broad daylight. Alexander John Ramos was responding to a disabled vehicle in Bloomfield when he was struck and killed by a driver.

“As sad and angry as we may be, action is what’s needed, and we should honor them with action—to raise awareness, to toughen penalties, and to provide more rules for enforcement,” said Blumenthal at the press conference.

The press conference comes after Blumenthal’s bipartisan Slow Down Move Over Resolution with U.S. Senator Deb Fischer (R-NE) passed the U.S. Senate last week. Blumenthal introduced this year’s Slow Down Move Over Resolution to honor Elvin and Alexander and urge awareness while driving on Connecticut roads.

“Slow Down, Move Over saves lives. It’s the law in every state, but it needs to be amplified and elevated. Every year, failures to Slow Down and Move Over cause needless, senseless injuries and deaths to roadside workers like police, firefighters, emergency responders, tow truck operators, construction workers, and more. This resolution aims to make them safer by reminding drivers to slow down and move over,” said Blumenthal.

The resolution highlights Slow Down, Move Over laws across the country in an effort to reduce struck-by-vehicle injuries and fatalities. The resolution also recognizes and honors the important role fire and rescue personnel, emergency medical services personnel, law enforcement officers, tow truck operators, and transportation workers play in road safety.

Blumenthal further highlighted the need for Slow Down, Move Over laws and for increased roadside safety measures on Twitter/X.

“Tragically, two workers were killed on CT highways just last month. My bipartisan legislation supporting Slow Down, Move Over education & enforcement can help save lives,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Demanding Home Heating Help

Blumenthal joined advocates to call on the Senate to pass at least $7 billion for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) this winter. LIHEAP is a vital federal program that helps residents of low-income households afford to heat their homes. As fall and winter begin, demand is expected to increase, in part because of skyrocketing home heating oil prices. The cost of home heating oil in Connecticut is currently $5.91 per gallon, up 50% from June and 86% from last September.

Blumenthal is demanding the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee commit $7 billion for home heating assistance this year, and urges swift release of all LIHEAP funding ahead of the coldest winter months.

“The cost of home heating oil is going to be crushing—a severe and painful hardship for many families in Connecticut that simply cannot afford it, the absolutely crushing effects, emotionally as well as physically, of a winter that requires this kind of financial commitment to keep homes livable,” said Blumenthal at the press conference. “We’re facing a perfect storm in home heating oil—soaring prices, a harsh winter, and stable, flat amounts of LIHEAP. 86 percent higher costs for home heating oil and the harshness of this winter means LIHEAP must be increased—it’s a matter of simple humanity.”

Calling for Immigration Warrant Reform Amid Unlawful ICE Arrests & Detentions

Blumenthal held a press conference in Hartford discussing the Immigration Warrant Reform Act, legislation he is co-sponsoring to clarify existing requirements for immigration arrests and codify statutory procedures to prevent unlawful arrests and detentions. The legislation, introduced by U.S. Senators Dick Durbin (D-IL) and Alex Padilla (D-CA) would bring immigration enforcement procedures in line with standards that all state and local law enforcement already follow.

“ICE’s violent, warrantless dragnet must be stopped. And that’s why I’m introducing a measure that will require standards—send a warrant, and then a public hearing where bail can be granted in public, within 24 hours. This basic standard in my view is a matter of constitutional law, but ICE has failed to follow it, and so we need to put it into our statutory law,” said Blumenthal.

Blumenthal further highlighted the need for immigration warrant reform on Twitter/X.

“ICE should be held to the same standards as our state & local police. That’s why I’m introducing a measure that will require a warrant for most immigration detentions,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Blumenthal has led an investigation into DHS’s abuses. Over the last year, Blumenthal and U.S. Representative Robert Garcia (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, have hosted five public forums on Capitol Hill as part of their ongoing inquiry into the lawless and abusive tactics used by federal immigration agents.

Blumenthal also hosted a public forum to receive testimony from the Danbury community about ICE’s destructive and indiscriminate detentions. Blumenthal was joined by Mayor Roberto Alves; attorney Glenn Formica with the American Legal Immigrant Clinic; and members of Danbury United for Immigrants.

More information and videos from these forums can be found here, here, here, here, here, and here.

Sounding the Alarm on Deceptive Housing Deposit Schemes

Blumenthal and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) wrote to Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chair Andrew Ferguson calling on the FTC to investigate the emerging consumer protection issues posed by security deposit alternatives.

According to recent reporting by the New York Times, landlords and management companies are increasingly offering tenants security deposit alternatives, in which tenants are allowed to pay smaller monthly or annual fees that replace the traditional lump sum of a security deposit before moving in. While these alternatives seem helpful to consumers, they expose tenants to significant financial risks—tenants are still financially responsible for any damages that occur, and unlike a typical security deposit, the alternative payments are generally non-refundable. In their letter, Blumenthal and Warren call on the FTC to investigate and take action against these deceptive fee practices.

“The misleading marketing and lack of transparency surrounding these products can lead tenants to believe they function like traditional security deposits, but at a lower cost… However, in a report analyzing security deposit alternatives, the National Consumer Law Center (NCLC) found that these products typically cost more than traditional security deposits over the course of a lease, may lack the protections afforded by state security deposit laws, and often fail to clearly disclose the fees tenants will be required to pay,” wrote the Senators.

“From non-refundable fees and misleading marketing to inadequate disclosures, these products can take advantage of vulnerable tenants who are already struggling to afford the high cost of rental housing,” continued the Senators.

Blumenthal and Warren are calling on the FTC to take action to protect tenants from these deceptive and misleading security deposit alternatives, writing, “As security deposit alternatives are becoming increasingly common, the FTC should take action to investigate, provide consumer notice, and combat misleading tactics with respect to security deposit alternatives. In particular, the Commission should issue rules requiring disclosures regarding the full costs and fees, reimbursement obligations, and non-refundable nature of these products, while also prohibiting misleading marketing practices that misrepresent how these products compare to traditional security deposits. These measures would help protect consumers, improve transparency, and ensure tenants understand the true costs and obligations associated with security deposit alternatives.”

The full text of the letter can be found here.

Blumenthal held a press conference in Hartford highlighting his letter calling on the FTC to investigate and take action to address the emerging issue of security deposit alternatives.

“I am demanding that the Federal Trade Commission begin an investigation of these security deposit schemes, because they can be devastatingly costly to renters—especially at a time when the price of everything else, gas to groceries, is rising as well. Tenants need more protection,” said Blumenthal at the press conference.

Blumenthal Bulletin

Blumenthal slammed President Trump for lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, fueling Putin’s war machine.

Blumenthal demanded answers from Cantor Fitzgerald about its relationship with Tether after his PSI report finds the cryptocurrency firm props up Iran’s shadow banking system.

Blumenthal demanded FanDuel fess up about celebrity promotional videos after VIP message was used to target a gambling addict.

Blumenthal continued to probe into the Department of Homeland Security’s misuse of taxpayer dollars, demanding answers from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin over luxury jet purchases.

Blumenthal released a statement on the release of the annual veteran suicide report.

Blumenthal introduced legislation to improve support for Veterans Crisis Line employees.

Blumenthal attended the Wallingford Town Fair.

Blumenthal attended the opening of Elena’s Light new community center.

Blumenthal attended the CT Hospice annual gala.

-30-

title: Booker Demands Answers Regarding Unjustified Prison Transfer of Convicted Child Sexual Predator Ghislaine Maxwell
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee (SJC) is pressing Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) Director William Marshall III for answers about Ghislaine Maxwell’s transfer from FCI Tallahassee, a maximum security penitentiary to Federal Prison Camp (FPC) Bryan, a minimum security facility in August 2025.

Maxwell, a convicted child sexual predator, is currently serving a 20 year federal prison sentence for sex trafficking minors and conspiring with Jeffrey Epstein to sexually abuse underage girls.

“Threats to anyone in federal custody must be taken seriously, but the American people deserve to know who requested this transfer, on what basis, and under what legal authority it was approved,” wrote Senator Booker. “A sex offender with a Public Safety Factor should not be placed in a minimum security camp without a clear, documented, and consistent justification.”

On September 14, 2026, BOP’s press office confirmed to the Marshall Project that Rick Stover, special assistant to the director, was the “approving official” in the transfer. Senator Booker’s letter asks about the role of Stover, then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, and Shannon Robbins, Chief of the Designation and Sentence Computation Center (DSCC) in the transfer decision. The letter also requests the unredacted Form 409 request for a waiver of Maxwell’s Public Safety Factor.

Under BOP policy, Maxwell has been assigned a sex offender Public Safety Factor, which prohibits housing sex offenders in minimum security facilities. She was nonetheless transferred to FPC Bryan on August 1, 2025, one week after meeting with then-Deputy Attorney General Blanche. BOP retroactively changed its policy on designation and redesignation on May 5, 2026—nine months after Maxwell was transferred.

The Department has not explained the transfer to Congress or the public, aside from Mr. Blanche’s statement at his July 15, 2026 confirmation hearing that Maxwell was not safe in the higher security facility. Senator Booker’s letter notes that his testimony offered no facts about the alleged threats, their timing, his knowledge of them, or how they relate to his meeting with Maxwell and her transfer.

Senator Booker has asked BOP to respond by Monday, October 19, 2026.

title: Booker Statement Regarding ICE Incident on Harrison Avenue
text:
NEWARK, NJ—U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) issued the following statement after a video posted online appears to show ICE agents violently dragging a man away from two small children on Wednesday in Harrison, New Jersey:

"Last week, I demanded that Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin immediately remove all ICE agents brought on during the Department's 2025 hiring surge.

“We must have stronger oversight and accountability across the immigration detention system. That’s why earlier this year, I introduced comprehensive legislation that would ban private detention centers, end family detention, strengthen detention standards, improve oversight, and better protect the health, safety, and civil rights of people in ICE’s custody.
