title: Grassley to Senate Judiciary Democrats: Join My Efforts to Hold Jack Smith Accountable
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) sent a letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee Minority debunking Democrats’ complaints regarding access to Arctic Frost records and pointing to numerous examples in which Democrats have broken Committee and Senate rules by withholding records from Republicans.

Since January 2025, Grassley has made public nearly 2,200 pages of records related to Arctic Frost and Jack Smith’s Special Counsel team. As Grassley points out to Democrats, “If you want to use those records, you’ve been given access to do so. But the important question is, where is the outrage from your side about [Smith’s] clearly abnormal investigative tactics?”

Last week, Grassley exposed Smith for secretly subpoenaing bank records from nearly 5,000 Americans across the county. Zero Judiciary Committee Democrats have condemned Smith’s actions, despite a collective 914 constituents in their states being impacted. Grassley is calling on Democrats to demand an apology from Smith for his abuse of authority and invasion of Americans’ privacy, and encouraging Democrats to join his efforts to hold Smith accountable, instead of undermining them.

“By now it should go without saying that my Democratic colleagues had every chance to assist in my constitutional duty to conduct oversight of these matters. They all failed to lend a hand or request to join my oversight,” Grassley wrote.?“For instance, during an Executive Business Meeting of this Committee nearly a year ago to the date, I asked my Democratic colleagues for their assistance in investigating Arctic Frost, stating, ‘I urge my Democratic colleagues to join us in further uncovering this unconstitutional breach by the Biden Administration.’ Nobody from your side took me up on the offer.”?

“I received the same cold shoulder when I worked without bipartisan help to release records related to the Durham Annex, Clinton Annex, Crossfire Hurricane, the decision by Smith and his Special Counsel staff to secretly obtain phone data on members of this Committee, and their actions to proceed with a fishing expedition in seeking records and communications from more than 430 Republican individuals, donors, and organizations,” Grassley continued. “My door has been open, and not one person on your side has walked through, other than to complain and try to undermine my long-standing work.”?

“I also note that Smith has withheld more than 800 pages of emails at the center mass of this Committee’s investigation, which I requested again this week without a response yet. I requested that information in October last year via a public letter and, should we have received it, would’ve gladly shared it with you, just like I have shared records with you in advance of every oversight hearing I’ve held this Congress. I’m committed more than ever to ensuring that any improper conduct by Smith or his Special Counsel staff is brought to the attention of the American people. For these reasons and more, my oversight will continue and I encourage you – yet again – to join my efforts instead of undermining them,” Grassley concluded.

The full text of Grassley’s letter is available HERE and below.

October 8, 2026

VIA ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION

The Honorable Richard J. Durbin

Ranking Member

Committee on the Judiciary

United States Senate

Dear Ranking Member Durbin and Members of the Senate Judiciary Committee:

I received your letter dated October 7, 2026. As I’ve written before, my Democratic colleagues can’t have it both ways. In the past, some of the Democratic members of this Committee have run roughshod over Committee rules for unjustifiable reasons and have claimed violations by Republicans when the facts don’t fit simply to drum up headlines in the partisan national press. I need not remind you that my oversight of this matter is years in the making, has been supported by courageous whistleblowers who came to my office concerned about the rotten political bias at the heart of Jack Smith’s investigation, and has been transparent with the American people and my Democratic colleagues from the get-go.

Since January 2025, I’ve released nearly 2,200 pages of records related to Arctic Frost and Jack Smith’s Special Counsel team, and I’ve continued to release records since the hearing nearly a week ago, which have been available to you. Indeed, just this week I’ve shared additional records with Ranking Member Durbin’s office. And as another example, I made public records last month that showed a core member of Jack Smith’s Special Counsel staff thought of themselves as an “advocate for repealing the” Speech or Debate clause enshrined in the U.S. Constitution, that the Special Counsel staff issued far-reaching preservation requests to Apple for Member of Congress accounts, including for the accounts of at least one member of this Committee, and that Smith’s Special Counsel staff collected donor data, including checks from nearly 5,000 Americans in all 50 states. If you want to use those records, you’ve been given access to do so. But, the important question is, where is the outrage from your side about these clearly abnormal investigative tactics?

Contrary to your misguided statement, the major embarrassment of the hearing was Democrats falling over themselves defending unlawful and unconstitutional actions by Jack Smith. By now it should go without saying that my Democratic colleagues had every chance to assist in my constitutional duty to conduct oversight of these matters. They all failed to lend a hand or request to join my oversight. For instance, during an Executive Business Meeting of this Committee nearly a year ago to the date, I asked my Democratic colleagues for their assistance in investigating Arctic Frost, stating, “I urge my Democratic colleagues to join us in further uncovering this unconstitutional breach by the Biden Administration.” Nobody from your side took me up on the offer.

I received the same cold shoulder when I worked without bipartisan help to release records related to the Durham Annex, Clinton Annex, Crossfire Hurricane,1 the decision by Smith and his Special Counsel staff to secretly obtain phone data on members of this Committee, and their actions to proceed with a fishing expedition in seeking records and communications from more than 430 Republican individuals, donors, and organizations. My door has been open, and not one person on your side has walked through other than to complain and try to undermine my long-standing work. Which reminds me of Democratic colleagues who actively worked to undermine my and Senator Johnson’s Biden family investigation by falsely accusing us of advancing Russian disinformation. You see, those types of ad hominem attacks on my and Senator Johnson’s character, oversight work and staff serve no other purpose than to obstruct and frustrate our good government oversight. So, call me skeptical when I receive a letter like the one you just sent me complaining about my office’s conduct when I and others have been subject to inappropriate conduct for years, such as when Minority Leader Schumer and Ranking Member Wyden publicly tried to offer a resolution on the Senate floor attacking me and Senator Johnson and were shut down by the parliamentarian.

And when we included Ranking Member Wyden and Ranking Member Peters in our Biden investigation, our work product began to leak. In one example, Senator Johnson and I sent a letter to the Treasury. Then a Yahoo News article published stating, “[t]he senators’ requests to the Treasury have borne fruit, according to the ranking Democratic senator on the Finance Committee, Ron Wyden of Oregon[.]” Senator Wyden’s spokesperson was also quoted as saying, “the Treasury Department [is] rapidly complying with Senate Republican requests—no subpoenas necessary—and producing ‘evidence’ of questionable origin.” The Yahoo News article stated that the Department of Treasury had “complied with Republican senators’ requests for highly sensitive and closely held financial records about Hunter Biden and his associates[.]” Further, on the same day the Yahoo News article published, Buzzfeed News reported that the Committees had begun coordinating interviews with potential witnesses. Indeed, during that inquiry, the Democratic side also made public previously undisclosed and non-public information pertaining to our investigation. In the end, we made public authentic bank records proving the legitimacy of our work. To date, not one of our Democratic colleagues has apologized to us even though they violated Senate Rules.

My inclusion of my Democratic colleagues undercut the inquiry, and my act of inclusion wasn’t reciprocated. For example, on July 1, 2020, Ranking Member Wyden and Ranking Member Peters released a COVID-19 report that included non-public government information that was not shared with Senator Johnson or me, we were excluded from document production requests and were provided a fake draft report that was represented as the final but had little connection to what was actually finally released. I can go on with other examples, but the point is made.

You see, your side can’t argue about Rules when your side doesn’t play by them.

In short, my oversight has been made possible in large part by whistleblowers and their legally protected disclosures—not my Democratic colleagues—who have urged me to bring transparency and a public accounting to the sordid history of Arctic Frost, Jack Smith’s partisan prosecution, and, ultimately, the years-long weaponization of the Justice Department against members of the Republican party—from Members of Congress down to individual American citizens exercising their constitutionally given rights to support candidates and causes with their hard-earned dollars. These investigative efforts should’ve been bipartisan, but your side failed to engage.

Turning to the claims you raise, I first want to note that my office complied with the Senate Rules when, before the hearing on September 29, 2026, my staff provided Democratic staff with hundreds of pages of records. But, other records have been transmitted to your staff this Congress in advance of oversight hearings, and even more records have been made available to you on the Committee’s website. As you are aware, since your side has done the same, as Chairman, I can decide the manner, mode, and timing of when access to records will be afforded, and additional considerations are always at play when whistleblower equities are involved. Unlike Jack Smith, who has no regard for the evils of whistleblower retaliation, I presume that you understand the risks at issue when whistleblowers disclose information confidentially.

I don’t remember any of my colleagues raising similar concerns when Democratic members of this Committee publicly admitted that they “broke committee rules” or that they believed they knowingly violated Senate Rules in releasing records to the press during this Committee’s consideration of then-Supreme Court Justice nominee Brett Kavanaugh. One Democratic member on this Committee publicly hailed their breaking of Senate Rules as an act of civil disobedience. So, please spare me the outrage regarding your misapplied standards. And given that history, whistleblowers are much more hesitant to allow my staff to share records with you.

Further, I’ve served with my Judiciary colleagues on other committees, including on the Budget Committee, in which a report and records were not provided to me or my staff in a timely manner. In one instance, my staff waited for nearly eight months to obtain records in preparation for a hearing chaired by Senator Whitehouse on climate change all while his staff was, unbeknownst to us, working with House Democrats on the matter. The Washington Post published a story on the committee report before my staff had a chance to review it. My Democratic colleagues gave the report to outside interests before giving it to committee members in advance of a hearing. Moreover, then-Chairman Leahy unilaterally released 8,500 pages of investigative records before my staff had a chance to review. So, again, spare me the complaints about your misapplied standards.

This pattern of conduct also held true when this Committee considered the nomination of Emil Bove to the federal bench. My Democratic colleagues failed to timely share information regarding unsubstantiated allegations involving Judge Bove. Your side received records from the whistleblower, whom I defended as a whistleblower, on July 1 and July 7 last year–a fact which has not been disputed. But your side hid those records from Republicans because we didn’t receive them until July 10, the day Judge Bove’s nomination was originally scheduled for markup. It should be noted, of course, that Judge Bove addressed these allegations in a public letter–in stark contrast from Jack Smith’s refusal to answer the questions in my October 23, 2025, letter.

Further, I publicly stated that Mr. Reuveni, who made the unsubstantiated allegations against Judge Bove, was a whistleblower even though this administration didn’t. That’s in stark contrast to Special Counsel Smith’s partisan prosecutors J.P. Cooney and Molly Gaston who asked that the Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General target whistleblowers with a retaliatory investigation for making legally protected disclosures to my office about their–and Smith’s–abuse of authority. During his hearing, Mr. Smith failed to answer my question whether whistleblowers who make lawful disclosures about his taxpayer-funded work should be investigated or if he stood by his former staff targeting whistleblowers who made legally protected disclosures to Congress. Will my Democratic colleagues stand with me to support my whistleblowers and disavow former Special Counsel Smith’s staff in targeting them? If not, why not?

It’s worth noting that many of the records I’ve obtained throughout my Arctic Frost investigation were provided by patriotic whistleblowers, and I’ve made many of them public. Whistleblower disclosures require caution before sharing because they often provide information in confidence and face severe backlash for their disclosures. As I said on the Senate floor, “I’ve made a career out of protecting and defending whistleblowers, and never in my time have I, my staff and my whistleblowers received more attacks for doing that job than this Congress.”

The attacks made by some of those on the Democratic side of the aisle and the partisan media create a chilling effect on whistleblowers. That chilling effect causes whistleblowers to withhold permission sharing certain records or, in some cases, making them public out of fear they will be targeted with retaliation, like Cooney and Gaston called for with my whistleblowers and of which Smith didn’t disagree. Accordingly, there are some records that I am unable to provide you access to currently. However, my staff are working to obtain an agreement to provide you access to those types of records and spending considerable time in doing so. In fact, my staff have already reached out to yours to schedule a meeting next week to review records as well as the ones you’ve recently written me about. On that point, will you commit to providing my staff access to the records that you’ve obtained? We have not received any from you on this matter, and, if there are other matters for which you have received records, we ought to discuss.

Ultimately, the public still awaits a full accounting of Jack Smith and his Special Counsel staff’s conduct. The investigation is active, the hearing is not the end of my work, and therefore some records will not be shared with you until a later date. But, rest assured, as I have in the past, you will be given access to those records, including next week when our respective staff meet.

I also note that Smith has withheld more than 800 pages of emails at the center mass of this Committee’s investigation which I requested again this week without a response yet. I requested that information in October last year via a public letter and should we have received it, would’ve gladly shared it with you just like I have shared records with you in advance of every oversight hearing I’ve held this Congress. I’m committed more than ever to ensuring that any improper conduct by Smith or his Special Counsel staff is brought to the attention of the American people. For these reasons and more, my oversight will continue, and I encourage you–yet again–to join my efforts instead of undermining them.

Sincerely,

Charles E. Grassley

Chairman

Committee on the Judiciary

On Grassley’s Arctic Frost oversight:

“[It’s a] pretty darn big [deal] because it shows the power of government, when you weaponize the FBI and the Justice Department to put an ex-president...in jail, so he couldn't ever run for president again.

“... [Jack Smith] went about not only going after [President] Trump, but he went after 50 journalists with subpoenas. So, you can see how sweeping his fishing expedition was, and you could easily conclude that it wasn't only to hurt Trump. It was to hurt all of the Republican machinery.

...

And so, 4,700 Americans had their bank records subpoenaed. And of those 4,700, there were 42 Iowans that had their bank records checked. And why would Smith need bank records of 42 Iowans? When you get something in the government files, [then] the FBI is going to have the names and the signatures and the addresses and the routing numbers and where the bank accounts are of 42 Iowans and 4,700 Americans. Because if you use diesel in the field, you shouldn't pay road use [for] that. They're going to be able to use dyed diesel in their trucks, and that will save them $0.24/gallon at the federal level, and I think something like $0.20[/gallon] at the state level. Governor Reynolds followed on by taking [the state tax] off. So, that's going to be some help for...diesel.”

On next week’s Federal Judiciary Youth Summit:

“Everybody knows what the president does. Most everybody knows what the Congress does, but hardly anybody has an appreciation for the judicial branch of government. And it's a very important branch of government because it serves as a referee between government and the people. It serves as a referee between powers of the president versus powers of the Congress, and so many other ways.

“And [the judicial branch has] the job of looking at the facts and the laws that apply to the facts. And I don't think people understand it. So, [this will be the seventh] time we've had such a thing for high school students to bring them greater acquaintance with the judicial branch of government, so they have an appreciation for the importance of the judiciary.”

title: Q&A: Cancer Screening Saves Lives
Hawley Seeks Answers About Data Used in FDA Abortion Drug Study
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) sent a letter to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas raising concerns that the FDA’s long-promised safety study of the abortion drug mifepristone may be using incomplete data. The letter raises questions about whether the study can adequately assess the effect of the Biden Administration’s 2023 Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy(REMS)—which removed important safeguards—and whether the FDA is reviewing all relevant data in its effort to complete the study.

“I write with concern that FDA’s long-promised safety study of the abortion drug mifepristone may be using incomplete data. On October 7, the Department of Justice filed a status report on FDA’s behalf in Louisiana v. FDA, the litigation challenging FDA’s 2023 removal of the in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone during the Biden Administration. According to the filing, FDA’s safety study of the drug relies in part on ‘a variety of data sources contained within Sentinel,’ the agency’s distributed database of insurance claims and health records. Yet the filing does not provide the time horizon for its source data. To ensure credibility, FDA must confirm its review includes data from the period after the Biden Administration gutted safety regulations in 2023,” wrote Senator Hawley.

He continued, “As you know, in April 2021, FDA announced that it would not enforce its in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone during the COVID-19 public health emergency. And on January 3, 2023, it formally modified the mifepristone REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy) to eliminate in-person dispensing and to allow certified retail pharmacies to dispense the drug. Louisiana and other states have challenged that 2023 decision in court.”

“FDA’s confirmed reliance on Sentinel data, along with ambiguity as to whether FDA acquired other commercially available data, raises questions about whether FDA’s study can adequately assess the impact of the Biden Administration’s 2023 REMS. According to the Sentinel Initiative, the date range of available data varies by source. For example, the end date of Sentinel’s Medicaid data appears to be 2021—leading to a nearly 50 percent drop in database enrollment after that year—while data from 2024 ‘and possibly 2023’ appear incomplete from publicly available sources.” Senator Hawley asserted.

Read the full letter here or below.

The Honorable Kyle Diamantas

Acting Commissioner of Food and Drugs

U.S. Food and Drug Administration

10903 New Hampshire Avenue

Silver Spring, MD 20993

Dear Acting Commissioner Diamantas:

I write with concern that FDA’s long-promised safety study of the abortion drug mifepristone may be using incomplete data. On October 7, the Department of Justice filed a status report on FDA’s behalf in Louisiana v. FDA, the litigation challenging FDA’s 2023 removal of the in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone during the Biden Administration. According to the filing, FDA’s safety study of the drug relies in part on “a variety of data sources contained within Sentinel,” the agency’s distributed database of insurance claims and health records.[1] Yet the filing does not provide the time horizon for its source data. To ensure credibility, FDA must confirm its review includes data from the period after the Biden Administration gutted safety regulations in 2023.

As you know, in April 2021, FDA announced that it would not enforce its in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone during the COVID-19 public health emergency. And on January 3, 2023, it formally modified the mifepristone REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy) to eliminate in-person dispensing and to allow certified retail pharmacies to dispense the drug. Louisiana and other states have challenged that 2023 decision in court. A recent independent study has shown that nearly 11% of women have suffered a serious adverse health event within 45 days of using mifepristone.[2]

FDA’s confirmed reliance on Sentinel data, along with ambiguity as to whether FDA acquired other commercially available data, raises questions about whether FDA’s study can adequately assess the impact of the Biden Administration’s 2023 REMS. According to the Sentinel Initiative, the date range of available data varies by source. For example, the end date of Sentinel’s Medicaid data appears to be 2021—leading to a nearly 50 percent drop in database enrollment after that year—while data from 2024 “and possibly 2023” appear incomplete from publicly available sources.[3]

Compounding the uncertainty, FDA’s filing states that its study confirmed adequate exposures and outcomes “across relevant time periods,” but it never identifies those periods.[4] This suggests that if the agency primarily relies on data from Sentinel, its analysis may rest largely on procedures that occurred before the 2023 REMS took effect and possibly exclude analysis of a large Medicaid population after that date. If the FDA’s review does not capture this population, the study may not properly inform the agency’s analysis about whether to modify the REMS by excluding women who have received the drug by mail. Other commercially available data from all-payer claims could help fill the gap left by Sentinel’s time-limited Medicaid data. Yet according to the DOJ status report, while the FDA “continues to gather and analyze additional data” outside Sentinel, it does not say what those datasets are or even what years they cover.[5]

To resolve these issues and provide assurance to patients that FDA is reviewing all relevant data, please answer the following questions in writing by October 22, 2026:

Does the FDA’s Sentinel database include all data after 2021 or 2023, such as that of the Medicaid population?

Has the FDA sought to acquire this data? If not, why not?

Identify the “additional data” outside Sentinel that FDA is gathering and analyzing, and the precise period each source covers.

Did the FDA originally plan to acquire a broader set of insurance data? If so, when and why did the agency change to reviewing primarily Sentinel data?

Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.

Sincerely,

title: What They’re Saying: Heinrich’s Bipartisan Permitting Reform Deal Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
text:
Labor, energy producers, and nonprofits voice strong support for Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

WASHINGTON – Since four Senators from across the political spectrum introduced their Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act last week, a broad coalition of labor leaders, energy producers, and nonprofits has voiced support for the permitting reform plan, noting that it will deliver cheaper energy, more jobs, and responsible growth. The legislation was drafted by U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, and Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairwoman of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards. The legislation provides greater certainty for projects that have already been permitted and financed, including by preventing future administrations from arbitrarily blocking entire classes of energy projects, while establishing clear timelines for environmental reviews and legal challenges. It also includes targeted reforms to expand and modernize the electric grid, speed the development of geothermal and other energy projects, and ensure that rapidly growing data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs rather than passing those costs on to families and small businesses. The legislation reflects input from members of Congress on both sides of the aisle and a diverse group of stakeholders.

The bill text is available here.

Labor

“For LIUNA, the key consideration is whether a permitting package will translate to good union jobs, with prevailing wages and robust apprenticeship opportunities. S.5653 exceeds those standards while maintaining proper regulations and safeguards that protect both our members on the job as well as the local communities in which projects take place. Moreover, it will lower energy costs for all Americans at a time when prices of everyday living expenses are at an all-time high,” said Brent Booker, LIUNA General President. “For more than a decade LIUNA has testified before Congress, submitted comments, participated in roundtables, and endorsed numerous iterations of permitting bills only to see every effort and attempt fail in final hours of the congressional calendar. Congress has another opportunity to get this done. We urge lawmakers in both parties to seize this moment, pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, and finally deliver meaningful permitting reform. It is time to stop making permitting reform the Groundhog Day of Congress.”

“In our industry, uncertainty means one thing: unemployment. It is long past time that Congress enacts meaningful permitting reform to put UA members to work faster delivering reliable and affordable energy to American communities. Today’s announcement is the culmination of a long process to reach a bipartisan deal and take a critical step towards a long-overdue modernization of our country’s permitting process. This bipartisan legislation, led by Chairs Lee and Capito and Ranking Members Heinrich and Whitehouse, will increase project certainty, streamline federal review timelines, and create thousands of good-paying jobs – all while maintaining reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input. The UA looks forward to continuing our work with members of both parties in the Senate to advance this critical legislation and with all members in the House to ultimately pass it into law,” said Mark McManus, United Association of Union Plumbers and Pipefitters (UA) General President.

“We have seen too many projects unnecessarily delayed for years through litigation, and other projects abandoned by contractors or terminated by the federal government because of our nation’s antiquated permitting process. As a result, thousands of good-paying union jobs have been lost, and taxpayers have been deprived of safer infrastructure and more affordable energy,” said John L. Downey, General President of the International Union of Operating Engineers. “Passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will result in building energy transmission capacity faster, delivering more energy to the grid, creating greater certainty for projects permitted and financed across administrations, and setting clear deadlines for environmental reviews. These reforms will put thousands of Operating Engineers to work, along with other highly skilled crafts people, while making energy more affordable and reliable for American families.”

Nonprofits

“If America is going to meaningfully reduce our emissions and truly address climate change, we need to connect much more clean energy to the grid,” said Rick Bradley, Citizens Climate Lobby’s Executive Director. “This bill will make remarkable, rapid progress toward that goal. We’re proud to endorse it, and we’re excited to mobilize our grassroots volunteers in full support.”

“For decades, the Club for Growth has championed deregulation and permitting reform. We commend President Trump and Senate leaders for moving this agreement forward with legislative text. These reforms are critical to expanding American energy production and lowering energy costs for families and businesses. Excessive regulation has constrained production and contributed to higher costs for American consumers. We urge the Senate and House to act swiftly and pass these important permitting reforms,” said David McIntosh, President for Club for Growth.

“The Climate Leadership Council is encouraged by progress on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. Council analysis projects U.S. electricity demand to grow nearly 60% by 2050, and meeting that demand will require building energy infrastructure faster than our current system allows. Permitting reform is essential to keep pace with the demands of a modern economy, and the energy infrastructure it unlocks is what drives clean energy deployment and innovation. CLC looks forward to continued engagement with stakeholders and policymakers as the bill moves forward,” said Erin Alejandre, Director of Policy at the Climate Leadership Council.

“On behalf of grassroots activists across the country, we strongly applaud the introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). Your work over much of this Congress to negotiate the details and make a bipartisan package a reality is a major step forward for the American people and for our energy, technological, and national future,” said Brent Gardner, Chief Government Affairs Officer at Americans for Prosperity.

“After years of working toward this goal, lawmakers from both parties have reached a deal to fix the broken system that keeps America from building the power plants and power lines that would bring costs down. This is a huge bipartisan win at a moment when our politics has made wins like this rare,” said Derek Kaufman, President of Inclusive Abundance Action. “Families are paying too much for electricity because new energy projects wait years on government reviews, then years more in court, and even once they clear, partisan politics can still take them out. That scarcity is a choice. Today, Congress is choosing differently.”

“The need for reform is one of the few things Republicans and Democrats agree on, and these Senate leaders have translated that consensus into a comprehensive, bipartisan bill. Permitting reform cannot wait, and the time to act is now,” said Michele Stockwell, President of Bipartisan Policy Center Action. “BPC Action has long argued that durable permitting reform must be bipartisan, technology-neutral, and maintain strong environmental standards. We urge swift action and look forward to working with members of both parties to get this bill to the president’s desk this Congress.”

“Pacific Legal Foundation strongly supports the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026,” said John Nagle, Federal Policy Manager at Pacific Legal Foundation. “Americans should not have to navigate years of costly and unpredictable government processes simply to build a home, develop new energy resources, or create the infrastructure our communities need. Reforming our permitting system is essential to removing unnecessary government barriers that delay projects, drive up costs, and discourage investment. We encourage Congress to move quickly to pass this bill to lower costs for Americans, protect property rights, and restore America’s ability to build.”

“Today, one of America’s most important supply lines is its electric grid, and we are not building it fast enough to meet the moment. Our military installations depend on the same civilian grid as every American household. When a transmission line takes a decade or more to approve, that is not just an economic problem. It is a strategic vulnerability, and our adversaries are not waiting years to build. This bill addresses that vulnerability. It sets firm deadlines on environmental reviews, speeds approvals for the transmission lines and power projects the country needs, and gives the federal government tools to move interstate power lines forward when they stall. Just as important, it ensures that once a project is permitted, no administration can revoke it for political reasons. At the same time, it preserves the government's ability to act in the face of a genuine safety or national security threat, and it keeps reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input in place. That kind of certainty matters for every form of American energy, including the clean energy that will power our future. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is pro-union and pro-veteran,” said Major General Paul D. Eaton, U.S. Army (Ret.), Senior Advisor at VoteVets.

“[The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act] is better than I could have expected. Sens. Capito (R-W.Va.), Heinrich (D-N.M.), Lee (R-Utah), and Whitehouse (D-R.I.) negotiated a compromise bill where each side got real, meaningful wins. This bill would fix our permitting processes so that we can review and build efficiently, reducing costs, improving quality of life, growing our economy, and improving economic outcomes. It’s truly a win-win. I’m optimistic that this incredible bill can be signed into law this year,” said Xan Fishman, Vice President, Energy, Bipartisan Policy Center.

“Permitting reform has stalled for years because Democrats feared losing environmental protections and Republicans feared a deal that would only help renewables. Sens. Heinrich, Lee, Capito and Whitehouse have shown there is a bargain that works for both sides,” said Colin Mortimer, Senior Director of Partnerships at the Progressive Policy Institute. “This bill would get power lines, clean energy and critical infrastructure built faster and lower costs for families while keeping strong safeguards in place.”

“If you care about decarbonizing the economy or reshoring American manufacturing, or cutting bills for ratepayers, then you should support this bill. No agreement is perfect, but there’s something in this permitting reform agreement that will, on net, benefit everybody. And there isn’t a better deal out there,” said Jane Flegal and Pavan Venkatakrishnan of the Searchlight Institute.

“NAHB applauds Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich and Whitehouse and for their leadership and bipartisan approach to crafting the most meaningful reforms in decades to several key federal environmental permitting programs. The housing sector stands to benefit from many of these federal permitting reforms, including an increase in acreage thresholds under the Clean Water Act’s (CWA) Nationwide Permit program along with extending the statutory timeframe from five to 10 years for the CWA permit programs. These provisions provide the industry with needed clarity and consistency during the federal permitting process,” said Bill Owens, Chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB).

Energy Companies and Associations

“The American Clean Power Association greatly appreciates the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich in developing strong, technology neutral permitting reform legislation that includes an Administration commitment to approve wind projects. All energy industries must be able to confidently rely on the durability of federal permitting decisions. The transmission provisions will also enhance grid reliability and enable economic growth. If adopted, the legislation will substantially increase the deployment of clean resources. Passage before the end of the year is essential to enable the construction of critical energy infrastructure and lower consumer prices,” said Jason Grumet, CEO of American Clean Power Association.

“Washington has a generational opportunity to fundamentally transform a broken permitting system and help address the affordability challenges facing American consumers,” said Mike Sommers, President and CEO of American Petroleum Institute. “President Trump and Senators Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich deserve credit for working across party lines to bring durable reform within reach. The bipartisan package would modernize NEPA, reduce duplicative reviews and unnecessary litigation, and provide greater certainty for critical projects. Congress should seize this moment and finish the job—making it easier to build the infrastructure America needs and helping keep costs down for consumers.”

“We support this bipartisan effort and applaud Senators Capito, Heinrich, Lee, and Whitehouse for advancing meaningful reforms to help meet America’s growing energy needs. As one of the nation’s largest electric utilities and the operator of the country’s largest transmission network, AEP understands firsthand the critical need for diverse generation and transmission infrastructure to serve our customers and help meet the unprecedented demand for electricity. The process to permit, site and construct energy infrastructure can take years due to unnecessary hurdles that delay projects needed to support reliability, affordability and economic growth. This legislation will help accelerate the process to bring critical infrastructure projects online, supporting the investments required to enhance reliability for our customers, reduce costs, and create new economic opportunities in the states we serve. Congress should pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 now,” said Bill Fehrman, Chairman, President and CEO of American Electric Power (AEP).

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 represents an historic opportunity to modernize the grid and meet customers’ electricity demand with reliable, affordable power. If enacted into law, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 would safeguard critical environmental standards while providing greater process certainty for environmental reviews and ensure that the customers we serve benefit from our nation’s diverse energy resources. It will also unlock trillions of dollars in private sector investment and job creation to expedite the construction of critically needed energy infrastructure,” said Mark Hewett, President and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Energy.

“Independent oil and natural gas producers are ready to build, produce, and create jobs, and permitting delays and uncertainty can turn attractive projects into missed opportunities—especially for small producers. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 gives Congress an opportunity to deliver bipartisan permitting reform with clear and enforceable timelines, greater levels of certainty, and fewer unnecessary delays—without compromising the environmental and safety standards that protect our communities and natural resources. Republicans and Democrats should seize that opportunity and move swiftly. American energy shouldn’t have to wait in line for Washington’s bureaucracy. American energy shouldn’t be held back by a permitting system that doesn’t keep pace with energy demand. This is an opportunity to celebrate what bipartisan cooperation can accomplish, providing real solutions to the complex problems that surround America’s broken permitting system,” said Edith Naegele, President and CEO of the Independent Petroleum Association of America (IPAA).

“This is the kind of bipartisan action America needs to meet growing energy demand, put downward pressure on energy prices, and deploy more affordable, exactly reliable solar and storage for American families and businesses,” said Tim Pawlenty, CEO of the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA).

“Affordable advanced energy resources, including solar, wind, storage, and transmission are delivering for America, but opaque, politicized, and endless red tape is getting in our industry’s way of building as much as is needed. That’s why we welcome technology-neutral permitting reform from Congress. This bill text demonstrates bipartisan support for building more advanced energy, faster. With fair competition, better planning, and less red tape, we can move more electrons and tamp down energy costs. Thank you to Sen. Capito, Sen. Mike Lee, Sen. Whitehouse, and Sen. Heinrich on their leadership. We encourage Congress to build on this progress and to prioritize these critical reforms,” said Heather O’Neill, President and CEO of Advanced Energy United.

“Constraining abundant, domestic clean energy could cost the U.S. at least $121 billion in additional energy expenses in the coming years,” said Rich Powell, Clean Energy Buyers Association (CEBA) CEO. “This bipartisan package is a generational opportunity to unleash American energy through faster infrastructure permitting and improved transmission planning. Thank you to Chairs Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee, Ranking Members Sheldon Whitehouse and Martin Heinrich, and President Donald Trump for your leadership on this critical issue. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act presents an incredible opportunity for clean energy, and we look forward to seeing it cross the finish line.”

“This bipartisan breakthrough goes big to durably reform a broken permitting system that needlessly drives up energy costs and puts America’s energy security at risk. These comprehensive reforms would unlock generational investments to make energy more affordable and position America to win the global energy race that will define our future. We urge the Senate to act with the urgency this moment in history demands by passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act,” said Anne Bradbury, the American Exploration & Production Council (AXPC) CEO.

“American economic growth requires an energy permitting system built on predictable, durable, bipartisan principles that will outlast two- and four-year election cycles,” said Ray Long, (American Council on Renewable Energy) ACORE President and CEO. “Clean energy builders and financers have made it clear they intend to keep investing in clean energy. The bipartisan legislation released today represents momentum toward providing the policy certainty the market needs to unleash capital and build the energy infrastructure we need.”

“Pass the frickin’ bill so we can start building things again,” said the U.S. Oil & Gas Association.

“Failing to pass permitting reforms would have real consequences for all of us,” said Zach Zimmerman, Director of Research and Policy for Grid Strategies. “Every year that major transmission projects are delayed means higher system costs and less ability to move power where it is needed during extreme weather. Without reform, we will continue to pay more for the grid.”

Business and Manufacturing Groups

“Manufacturers are all in on this game-changing agreement and getting it across the finish line. Our nation’s permitting system is outdated and burdensome, delaying projects across industries and contributing to rising costs across the economy. Costly, duplicative permitting delays are costing manufacturers $8 billion annually, limiting manufacturers’ ability to hire new workers, build and expand their operations. Removing these barriers would unlock greater investment and growth. Manufacturers are ready to build, and modernized permitting will help us race to the future,” said Jay Timmons, President and CEO of National Association of Manufacturers.

“BCSE commends the continued bipartisan work in Congress to modernize the nation’s permitting system and the further development of a comprehensive legislative permitting reform package. Building on the important progress made by the House of Representatives, Congress now has an opportunity to advance comprehensive, durable permitting reform that can provide greater certainty for investment and accelerate the deployment of critical energy infrastructure,” said Lisa Jacobson, President of the Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE).

“We appreciate all the work that made this strong package possible. Any bipartisan compromise will have trade-offs, but the permit certainty, transmission, and grid modernization components of this deal are strong, and now is the time to deliver reforms that allow us to build the clean energy infrastructure we need to reduce costs for American businesses and consumers,” said Zach Friedman, Senior Director of Federal Policy at Ceres. “We look forward to continuing to work with companies, partners, and key lawmakers to meet the moment and advance this package to drive down costs by accelerating deployment of affordable, homegrown clean energy infrastructure.”

“Business Roundtable strongly supports the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. This vital legislation would create a faster, more durable permitting process that gives businesses the certainty they need to invest, build and grow,” said Joshua Bolten, CEO of Business Roundtable. “Advancing wide-ranging permitting reform is one of the most consequential steps Congress can take to unlock America’s economic potential. By accelerating approvals for critical infrastructure projects, this bill would help lower costs, create good-paying jobs and strengthen America’s long-term competitiveness.”

“For too long, America’s broken permitting system has turned the ability to receive a permit into a barrier to job creation and economic growth. This bipartisan agreement represents a major step toward changing that. By establishing more reliable timelines, creating greater certainty and breaking down longstanding barriers to building, Congress can help ensure that projects across the economy move from the drawing board to the job site,” said Brandon Farris, Executive Vice President of Steel Manufacturers Association.

“The legislation would modernize federal environmental review and permitting processes for infrastructure projects, provide greater certainty for federal permits and authorizations, and help enable the all-of-the-above energy resources needed to meet America's growing energy and manufacturing demands,” said the American Chemistry Council. “America cannot build, power, and compete without modern infrastructure. Whether it’s expanding energy production, strengthening manufacturing, building next-generation infrastructure, projects cannot move forward if permitting delays and regulatory uncertainty stand in the way. This bipartisan legislation is an important step toward creating a permitting system that is more predictable, transparent, and effective.”

“We are undeniably in the age of demand – from energy to semiconductors, drones to transmission lines – and securing robust supplies of the mined materials that allow us to build, manufacture and power almost everything is key to meeting this moment. Standing in our way is a permitting process mired in duplication, endless litigation and uncertainty that has hobbled U.S. competitiveness with the second longest timeline in the world to bring a mine online. Our elected officials on both sides of the aisle have long acknowledged that the status quo cannot continue. We applaud the work that has been done to date and urge Congress to pass commonsense, much-needed reforms that will benefit all Americans,” said Rich Nolan, President and CEO of the National Mining Association.

“The Senate's progress toward a comprehensive, bipartisan permitting reform deal brings us one step closer to streamlining the outdated process that is holding up critical projects of all kinds, from energy and water infrastructure to roads, broadband, and manufacturing,” said Rodney Davis, Senior Vice President and Head of Government Affairs at the U.S. Chamber. “We appreciate the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee, and Heinrich to bring us to this point, and now we urge swift action in Congress to get this bill to the President’s desk as soon as possible.”

State and Local Government

“The National Governors Association and its partners are encouraged by the introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and look forward to working with Congress to further develop this legislation. Working with governors, NGA has long championed commonsense permitting reform to build the infrastructure our country needs. With priorities centered on federal partnership, interstate cooperation, and sound energy and environmental policy, NGA worked across the aisle and across sectors to deliver federal reform recommendations to Congress, using states as proving ground. Reform will help grow our economy, reduce costs, and improve quality of life for all Americans,” said Brian Tatum, CEO of the National Governors Association.

“Counties are on the front lines of delivering the energy, water and transportation infrastructure projects that residents depend on,” said Matthew Chase, Executive Director of National Association of Counties. “The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act recognizes counties as cooperating agencies in federal environmental protection statutes. This legislation would modernize the federal permitting process, reduce unnecessary delays, accelerate project delivery and ensure local expertise is incorporated into federal decision-making. Counties applaud Senators Lee, Heinrich, Capito and Whitehouse for their leadership and urge Congress to advance this bipartisan permitting reform package.”

“Unfortunately, outdated federal bureaucracy continues to delay critical energy and infrastructure projects and drive up costs for hardworking families at a time when speed and efficiency matter most. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an opportunity to change that. By bringing greater certainty and accountability to the permitting process, we can unleash American energy dominance, strengthen our grid, bring manufacturing and investment back home, and ensure the United States leads the next generation of economic growth,” said 21 Governors in a Statement.

title: Zuni Tribe’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration Approved for July Storms and Flash Flooding Following Letter from N.M. Congressional Delegation
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, the Zuni Tribe’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration was approved to support recovery efforts following severe storms and flash flooding that occurred between July 16 and 28, 2026. The Major Disaster Declaration was granted on October 7 by President Donald Trump, immediately following a letter sent October 6 from U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) and U.S. Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), and Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) calling on the President to approve the Major Disaster Declaration request.

The Zuni Tribe is one of the oldest continuously inhabited communities in North America, serving as a steward of a nationally significant historic, cultural, and religious landscape. The storms and flash flooding caused extensive damage to seven ceremonial trails and multiple culturally significant locations, affecting the ancestral, ceremonial, and historic resources central to the Tribe’s cultural heritage, along with damage to public infrastructure and private property. This declaration designated the Pueblo of Zuni for both Individual Assistance and all categories of Public Assistance. Federal funding will help ensure that those historic sites and public infrastructure can be repaired and that impacted families can recover from these devastating floods.

In a letter sent to President Trump on October 6, 2026, New Mexico’s Congressional Delegation wrote, “We respectfully request that you take immediate action on the Zuni Tribe’s recent request for a major disaster declaration in response to severe storms that triggered significant flash flooding and caused extensive damage in the Pueblo of Zuni between July 16, 2026, to July 28, 2026. The severity and magnitude of the storms and subsequent flash flooding overwhelmed Zuni Tribal resources, and they require supplemental, Federal assistance to ensure the Tribal Nation can recover.”

The lawmakers continued, “Three thunderstorm events on July 16, 21, and 28, 2026, in the Zuni Pueblo area produced heavy rainfall, with National Weather Service (NWS) radar and local rain gauge data indicating it was a 100-year flood event. This rainfall overtopped levees, riverbanks, and earthen dams, flooding paved roads and Zuni Village itself, and caused significant damage to private property, community infrastructure, ceremonial trails, and culturally significant sites. Sixty-one families were displaced, twelve families required sheltering, and four individuals required swift water rescue; six families are still in shelters.”

“In totality, the impacts from these floods will require federal assistance, as they have exceeded the capabilities of the Zuni Tribe,” the lawmakers concluded. “We fully support the Zuni Tribe’s request, and we urge you to act without delay. It is imperative that the federal government provides full support to the Zuni Tribe to recover from the devastation caused by this flooding.”

Read the full text of the lawmaker’s letter here and below:

Dear President Trump,

We respectfully request that you take immediate action on the Zuni Tribe’s recent request for a major disaster declaration in response to severe storms that triggered significant flash flooding and caused extensive damage in the Pueblo of Zuni between July 16, 2026, to July 28, 2026. The severity and magnitude of the storms and subsequent flash flooding overwhelmed Zuni Tribal resources, and they require supplemental, Federal assistance to ensure the Tribal Nation can recover.

The Zuni Tribe is requesting Public Assistance (PA), Categories A through G, as well as Individual Assistance (IA), including Disaster Unemployment Assistance, Small Business Administration (SBA) Disaster Assistance, Disaster Case Management, and Individuals and Households Program Assistance, and statewide assistance from the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program. We ask that you expeditiously grant the declaration and make this federal assistance available as soon as possible.

Three thunderstorm events on July 16, 21, and 28, 2026, in the Zuni Pueblo area produced heavy rainfall, with National Weather Service (NWS) radar and local rain gauge data indicating it was a 100-year flood event. This rainfall overtopped levees, riverbanks, and earthen dams, flooding paved roads and Zuni Village itself, and caused significant damage to private property, community infrastructure, ceremonial trails, and culturally significant sites. Sixty-one families were displaced, twelve families required sheltering, and four individuals required swift water rescue; six families are still in shelters.

The Zuni Tribe is a federally recognized sovereign Tribal Nation and one of the oldest continuously inhabited communities in North America. The Zuni Tribe serves as a steward of a nationally significant historic, cultural, and religious landscape. And in addition to extensive damage to public infrastructure and private property, the flash floods described above also severely impacted seven ceremonial trails and multiple culturally significant locations. Washouts, erosion, and material loss to those paths and sacred ruins – some dating back to the early 1500s – have affected the ancestral, ceremonial, and historic resources central to the Tribe’s cultural heritage. Restoration work will need to be performed using culturally appropriate methods, require specialized preservation oversight, and preserve the confidentiality of these sites.

In the wake of the flash flooding, the Zuni Tribe requested federal assistance with a Preliminary Damage Assessment, and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) staff and Zuni staff conducted site visits throughout the entire reservation. As of September 25, 2026, FEMA’s estimate for the assessed damage was $1,222,135. The severity and extent of the flooding required tribal resources to be diverted to emergency protective measures and hazardous debris removal. Recovery will require repairs to roadways and drainage systems, utility restoration, support for displaced families, and culturally appropriate preservation work. In totality, the impacts from these floods will require federal assistance, as they have exceeded the capabilities of the Zuni Tribe.

We fully support the Zuni Tribe’s request, and we urge you to act without delay. It is imperative that the federal government provides full support to the Zuni Tribe to recover from the devastation caused by this flooding.

Thank you for your consideration of this important request.

Sincerely,

title: Hickenlooper Rebukes EPA’s Methane Rules Rollback
text:
Hickenlooper: “The Trump administration is pushing policies that will allow more pollutants into our air. That’s not leadership. It’s shortsighted.”

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper released the following statement following reports that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) will propose changes that weaken federal methane rules for oil and gas operations.

“The Trump administration is pushing policies that will allow more pollutants into our air. That’s not leadership. It’s shortsighted,” said Hickenlooper. “As governor, we brought the energy industry and environmentalists together to monitor methane leaks, cut pollution, and protect our clean air. This administration is hell-bent on doing the opposite. We’ll keep standing up for our environment and the air we all breathe.”

The EPA will reportedly announce plans to overhaul Biden-era standards requiring oil and gas facilities to monitor for and repair methane leaks. The proposed changes are expected to weaken pollution safeguards, including monitoring requirements for smaller, older wells that produce relatively little oil and gas but account for a disproportionate share of methane emissions.

As governor, Hickenlooper brought environmentalists and the energy industry together to create the world’s first methane regulations in 2014. Between 2010 and 2017, those rules reduced methane emissions from Colorado’s oil and gas sector by 70%.

As senator, Hickenlooper has championed stronger federal methane rules modeled on Colorado’s. In 2021, he led members of the Colorado congressional delegation in urging the EPA to strengthen methane regulations for the oil and gas sector. He helped negotiate and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which created a $4.7 billion federal program to plug orphaned wells on Federal, State, and Tribal lands. President Trump froze these funds in March 2025, though some of the funds have been subsequently released.

Hickenlooper has repeatedly pressed the EPA to improve methane emissions tracking and celebrated $162.3 million in loan guarantees from the Inflation Reduction Act to support the installation of a real time methane emissions monitoring network across Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, Colorado, North Dakota, and New Mexico.

title: Hickenlooper, State Leaders Seek SBA Recovery Funding for Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires, Appeals Hazard Mitigation Grant Denial
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper joined Governor Jared Polis in announcing that Colorado has requested U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) disaster assistance to help individuals, families, homeowners, renters, and businesses recover from the Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires and burn scar flooding. Colorado has also appealed the federal denial of Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) funding to help affected communities reduce the risk of future disaster damage. In September, the Trump Administration approved the Public Assistance (PA) portion of Colorado’s Major Disaster Declaration (MDD) request and denied the Individual Assistance and HMGP funding portions.

“Losing a home to wildfire doesn’t end when the fire does,” said Hickenlooper. “Colorado families are still sorting through insurance claims, unsure how they’ll pay for basic repairs. Every week they wait is another week they can’t start rebuilding. Federal disaster loans are the fastest way to help families and local businesses move forward.”

“Today, I have submitted Colorado’s request for SBA assistance and have appealed the denial of hazard mitigation funding. Doing so will allow Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain communities to access more federal resources as quickly as possible. This SBA assistance will allow homeowners, families, and businesses an opportunity to start work on home repairs and replacements, personal property damaged by the disasters, and help small businesses,” said Polis.

To expedite SBA assistance, Colorado will not appeal the President’s denial of FEMA Individual Assistance (IA). Federal procedures prevent the SBA from declaring an independent physical disaster while a FEMA IA appeal is active or pending, requiring Colorado to resolve the appeal before SBA assistance can proceed. An IA appeal could take months, with no federal deadline for the President to decide on a state’s MDD appeal request. Given that uncertainty and recent delays in disaster assistance nationwide, Colorado is pursuing SBA assistance as the most reliable and immediate path to additional recovery resources for affected families and businesses.

“The families and communities devastated by the Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires have already endured tremendous loss. They should not have to navigate unnecessary delays and bureaucratic hurdles to get the help they need to rebuild. This recovery will take years, and we need to make sure our communities have the resources to rebuild safely and protect against future disasters. I will continue working with state and local leaders, regardless of party, to make sure Western and Southern Colorado are not left behind,” said U.S. Representative Jeff Hurd.

“Some of our communities in Colorado lost everything and are still trying to rebuild after the devastating wildfires this summer. These fires were just the final straw for so many business owners, and it’s essential they get the support they need to move forward and rebuild,” said U.S. Representative Brittney Pettersen.

“The Small Business Administration provides a wide variety of tools for homeowners, non-profits, and businesses impacted by this disaster. This decision will allow them to get on the ground quickly to start meeting with community members in order to provide financial assistance for the rebuilding and recovery process,” said Trevor Denney, Director of the Colorado Office of Emergency Management.

“Since the Aspen Acres Fire began on June 29, our residents have been waiting for a clear path to rebuild, and SBA assistance gives them one they can act on now. These are loans that must be repaid, so Pueblo County will keep pushing for every dollar of hazard mitigation funding and will stand with families as they decide what’s right for them,” said Pueblo County Commissioner Miles Lucero.

SBA disaster assistance provides low-interest loans that must be repaid. Subject to SBA approval and individual eligibility, available assistance can include:

Home repairs and replacement: Up to $500,000 for homeowners to repair or replace a damaged primary residence.

Personal property: Up to $100,000 for homeowners and renters to repair or replace disaster-damaged belongings, including furniture, appliances, and vehicles.

Business and nonprofit recovery: Up to $2 million for eligible businesses and private nonprofits to repair or replace damaged property, equipment, and inventory. Qualified rental properties may also be eligible.

Small business operating expenses: Economic Injury Disaster Loans can provide working capital to help eligible small businesses meet expenses during recovery, even without physical property damage.

Colorado’s separate HMGP appeal seeks funding for long-term disaster prevention, including flood prevention, stormwater upgrades, and wildfire risk reduction. FEMA research shows that disaster risk reduction grants save an average of $6 for every $1 spent.

Colorado received federal approval for PA for the Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires on September 4th, supporting eligible recovery work by affected communities. On September 18th, Colorado learned that IA and HMGP funding had been denied. On October 2, Governor Polis announced that the State would cover 75% of Ouray, Pueblo, and Custer County’s cost-share for Emergency Watershed Protection efforts through the USDA’s Natural Resources Conservation Service. The HMGP appeal and pursuit of SBA assistance builds on the PA already approved.

title: Support Rolls in from Policymakers and National Organizations for Kelly’s Make AI Work for Americans Act
text:
Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) introduced the Make AI Work for Americans Act, landmark legislation designed to make sure companies benefiting the most from AI pay their fair share and invest in American workers. The bill establishes a dedicated federal trust fund to support American workers, job seekers, and communities as the economy changes. Since its introduction, the bill has received broad support from national leaders.

See what supporters of the Make AI Work for Americans Act are saying here:

“It’s critical that legislators in Washington and in state capitols around the country begin to act now to help Americans make a successful transition to an AI economy. We can’t leave workers behind — as we have in the past — if we want to win the global AI competition. I applaud Senator Kelly for his leadership on this issue in Congress and for his legislation to make sure that AI works for working people,” said Gina Raimondo, CEO, RAISE US, former U.S. Secretary of Commerce.

“Senator Mark Kelly has introduced legislation that says the companies profiting from artificial intelligence have an obligation to the workers that technology displaces. His bill puts real money behind job training, behind paid work that carries a credential, and behind a stronger safety net for people who lose employment through no fault of their own,” said Reverend Al Sharpton, President, National Action Network.

Click here to read NAN’s full letter of support.

“At a time when many are urging our policymakers to take AI’s potential disruption seriously, it is good to see in this legislation a set of policies aimed at mitigating AI’s negative impacts on workers—from those just starting out to those displaced mid-career,” said Erika McEntarfer, former Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

“The early part of my career was building Internet platforms and I watched policy arrive years after the consequences did. We cannot repeat that same mistake in the AI era. Senator Kelly’s bill strengthens protections for workers before the disruption hits. And it is paid for by the industry, so the cost doesn’t fall on workers alone,” said Jason Goldman, technologist and former White House Chief Digital Officer.

“The public is looking for Congress to step up quickly to make sure AI development and deployment benefits workers, not just wealthy investors and executives. Senator Kelly’s bill offers many good ideas to push AI adoption in a pro-worker direction,” said Bharat Ramamurti, former Deputy Director of the White House National Economic Council.

“Senator Kelly’s Make AI Work for Americans Act represents a major step forward in rejecting an AI future that concentrates gains for the few while leaving millions of hard-working Americans behind. The Act provides admirably detailed revenue proposals to ensure that those profiting from AI-induced displacement of workers, help fund a major increase in opportunities for workers to transition to new careers, start new businesses, attain National Service jobs while also ensuring that unemployment benefits are substantial enough to support a worker’s family while they strive to attain these new jobs. Importantly, Senator Kelly’s call for a major expansion of National Service jobs could provide entry level workers being squeezed out by AI the chance to both serve their country and gain valuable work experience, judgment and managerial skills,” said Gene Sperling, Director of the National Economic Council for Presidents Clinton and Obama, Senior Advisor to President Biden, Director of the Economic Dignity Lab at McCourt School at Georgetown.

Gene Sperling on X: Kudos to @SenMarkKelly for not waiting for major AI job dislocation to start laying the foundation for putting jobs & workers first. His bill admirably lays out specific AI revenue sources to fund not only needed training, but also National Service jobs & entrepreneurship.

“Senator Kelly has been thoughtfully wrestling with the concerns that real Americans are facing with the adoption of AI — job displacement, costs, and ensuring that the benefits of this technology don’t just accrue to the few. This keeps the focus on ensuring Americans win,” said Mieke Eoyang, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy.

“The companies that are ushering in AI should pay to fix the societal harms it will cause. Senator Kelly’s legislation is built on that idea. This bill puts industry dollars into supporting workers whose jobs are changing and gives everyone the resources to adapt. It will take effort from private companies and government leadership to make sure this technology develops responsibly, and I believe this bill is the right way to start,” said Jon A. Shirley, former President, Chief Operating Officer, and Director of Microsoft.

“A safe AI future and a fair AI economy are two sides of the same promise. With one in five American workers expected to be Latino by 2030, our community has an enormous stake in seeing that promise kept. Senator Kelly’s Make AI Work for Americans Act ensures that as the AI industry grows, so do our investments in the workers who power the American economy. This legislation invests in paid service-to-career pathways, community college and apprenticeship programs, and capital for new small businesses. It gives workers who lose their jobs real stability as they retrain and find their next opportunity; and it helps close the digital divide by supporting digital access for participants, building AI literacy into our workforce system, and making resources available to people with limited English proficiency. It also gives workers and civil rights organizations a seat at the table as AI enters the workplace. This legislation lays the foundation for modernizing how we support workers and workplaces in the age of AI. UnidosUS is proud to endorse it and urges Congress to pass it,” said Eric Rodriguez, Senior Vice President of Policy & Advocacy, UnidosUS.

“Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the nature of work, and our workforce development systems must evolve alongside it. JFF is proud to support the Make AI Work for Americans Act, which invests in the systems already serving workers while expanding access to education and training, strengthening service-to-career pathways, supporting entrepreneurship, and helping workers navigate technological change. We applaud Senator Kelly’s leadership in advancing a vision for AI that puts workers at the center and helps ensure technological progress creates greater economic opportunity for people and communities across the country,” said Maria Flynn, President and CEO, Jobs for the Future (JFF).

“The greatest barrier to older Americans participating in the AI economy is not their willingness to learn, but access to opportunities. Older Americans are ready to embrace AI and develop the skills needed to succeed in a changing workplace. What they need is access to training and investments in their potential. Our economy cannot afford to overlook this extraordinary source of talent,” said Gary. A. Officer, Founder & CEO, CWI Labs.

“Senator Kelly’s Make AI Work for Americans Act is a series of policy proposals focused on what Americans will need most in the AI age. If AI has the transformative impact on our society that those who are building it say it will, we will need new ideas and a safety net for our workforce, small businesses, and more. This bill focuses on how to deliver real benefits to Americans impacted by AI and makes sure companies pay their fair share to ensure that AI works for all of us. It’s refreshing to see real leaders rising to the challenge of the AI age and we applaud the Senator for his efforts,” said Neera Tanden, President and CEO of the Center for American Progress.

“As artificial intelligence transforms our classrooms and communities, we have a generational responsibility to ensure that every student and worker is equipped to navigate this new landscape. The Make AI Work for Americans Act takes a vital, inclusive approach, anchored by robust investments in education, AI literacy, and workforce alignment, so that all Americans can share in the remarkable opportunities of artificial intelligence while safeguarding against its risks,” said Erin Mote, CEO, InnovateEDU.

“It is important that Congress recognizes that we need a greater investment in worker transitions, particularly given the possibility for a dramatic reshaping of our economy due to rapid advancement in technology. Senator Kelly and his staff have done a great job thinking about the most pressing issues with unemployment insurance, especially right now. I hope this legislation gets the serious consideration that it deserves,” said Michele Evermore, Senior Fellow for Worker Transitions, National Employment Law Project.

“This act would empower underserved communities with the necessary tools to help shape their lives and our collective future via system innovation, especially for small businesses. At the same time, it addresses the existing digital divide by opening new pathways to unexplored economic opportunity, competition, and equity. It turns AI into a participatory device accessible to all, rather than a passive application intended for and controlled by a few,” said Robert Alvarado, Senior Vice President, Chicanos Por La Causa.

“AmeriCorps and the nation’s state service commissions connect service to careers, provide hands-on experience, skill development, and pathways to meaningful work. We applaud Senator Kelly’s leadership in introducing the Make AI Work for Americans Act and his recognition of the National Service for America’s Future program to expand paid service opportunities that lead to credentials, careers, and durable skills. As technology reshapes the workplace, national service can play an important role in preparing workers and strengthening communities. State service commissions stand ready to help turn this vision into opportunities that meet local workforce needs across the country,” said John Kelly, CEO, America’s Service Commissions.

“Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the labor market, including many of the entry-level jobs that have traditionally helped young people get a foothold in the workforce. The Make AI Work for Americans Act recognizes that national service should be part of the solution. By building on AmeriCorps as a backbone for new service-to-career opportunities and exploring ways to strengthen AmeriCorps, this legislation would help more Americans build durable skills, gain meaningful work experience, and pursue credentials and careers while meeting critical needs in their communities. We thank Senator Kelly for recognizing national service as an important part of the workforce infrastructure our country will need as AI transforms the economy,” said AnnMaura Connolly, President, Voices for National Service.

“As Congress writes the rules for what comes next, young people must be at the center of it. They’re entering a job market where the entry-level roles that used to launch careers are changing fast. Americans across the ideological spectrum support national service, and states are equipped to scale it. Every time this country has faced a shift this large, it has answered with service, from the Civilian Conservation Corps in the Depression to the GI Bill after World War II. Today’s challenge deserves an answer of the same ambition. Senator Kelly is putting one on the table, and we are grateful for his leadership,” said Vicky Hausman, Founder & CEO, American Service Project.
