title: At New Mexico Piñon Coffee, Luján Hears Directly About Impact of Tariffs on New Mexico Small Businesses and Consumers
text:
Albuquerque, N.M. – This week, U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) visited New Mexico Piñon Coffee in Albuquerque to tour the company’s roastery and hear directly from staff about how tariffs are impacting the local business, increasing operating costs, and raising prices for consumers.

During the visit, Senator Luján toured the facility and met with staff to discuss the impact of tariffs on coffee imports and the challenges that increased costs create for New Mexico businesses. Senator Luján also heard concerns about the uncertainty that future tariffs create for businesses trying to plan, invest, and keep costs down for their customers.

“New Mexico small businesses, like New Mexico Piñon Coffee, are the backbone of our communities and help drive our local economies,” said Senator Luján. “This week, I had the honor of visiting and hearing directly from the folks at New Mexico Piñon Coffee about how these increased costs are impacting their operations and customers. New Mexico businesses and families should not have to bear the cost of Trump’s policies that make it more expensive to keep the doors open and buy everyday goods. I’ll continue working to lower costs and support small businesses across New Mexico.”

“We were honored to welcome Senator Luján and his team to New Mexico Piñon Coffee and share firsthand what it takes to grow a business right here in New Mexico. Since 1994, we’ve grown from a small local coffee company into a regional brand, and we’re incredibly proud of the jobs we’ve created and the opportunities ahead. Like many manufacturers and small businesses, we continue to navigate rising costs, tariffs, and the challenges that come with growth. We appreciate the opportunity to have an open conversation about these realities and the importance of supporting businesses that are investing in New Mexico’s future,” said Matthew Bregar, President of New Mexico Piñon Coffee.

In March, Senator Luján called on the Trump administration to put in place an automatic tariff refund process. In February, Senator Luján introduced the Tariff Refund Act of 2026, legislation to require full refunds of President Trump’s illegal tariffs. In June of 2025, Senator Luján hosted a forum that examined how President Trump’s tariff policies fuel economic instability, raise costs on working families, harm the travel and tourism sector, and benefit special interests.

title: Zuni Tribe’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration Approved for July Storms and Flash Flooding Following Letter from N.M. Congressional Delegation
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, the Zuni Tribe’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration was approved to support recovery efforts following severe storms and flash flooding that occurred between July 16 and 28, 2026. The Major Disaster Declaration was granted on October 7 by President Donald Trump, immediately following a letter sent October 6 from U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) and U.S. Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), and Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) calling on the President to approve the Major Disaster Declaration request.

The Zuni Tribe is one of the oldest continuously inhabited communities in North America, serving as a steward of a nationally significant historic, cultural, and religious landscape. The storms and flash flooding caused extensive damage to seven ceremonial trails and multiple culturally significant locations, affecting the ancestral, ceremonial, and historic resources central to the Tribe’s cultural heritage, along with damage to public infrastructure and private property. This declaration designated the Pueblo of Zuni for both Individual Assistance and all categories of Public Assistance. Federal funding will help ensure that those historic sites and public infrastructure can be repaired and that impacted families can recover from these devastating floods.

In a letter sent to President Trump on October 6, 2026, New Mexico’s Congressional Delegation wrote, “We respectfully request that you take immediate action on the Zuni Tribe’s recent request for a major disaster declaration in response to severe storms that triggered significant flash flooding and caused extensive damage in the Pueblo of Zuni between July 16, 2026, to July 28, 2026. The severity and magnitude of the storms and subsequent flash flooding overwhelmed Zuni Tribal resources, and they require supplemental, Federal assistance to ensure the Tribal Nation can recover.”

The lawmakers continued, “Three thunderstorm events on July 16, 21, and 28, 2026, in the Zuni Pueblo area produced heavy rainfall, with National Weather Service (NWS) radar and local rain gauge data indicating it was a 100-year flood event. This rainfall overtopped levees, riverbanks, and earthen dams, flooding paved roads and Zuni Village itself, and caused significant damage to private property, community infrastructure, ceremonial trails, and culturally significant sites. Sixty-one families were displaced, twelve families required sheltering, and four individuals required swift water rescue; six families are still in shelters.”

“In totality, the impacts from these floods will require federal assistance, as they have exceeded the capabilities of the Zuni Tribe,” the lawmakers concluded. “We fully support the Zuni Tribe’s request, and we urge you to act without delay. It is imperative that the federal government provides full support to the Zuni Tribe to recover from the devastation caused by this flooding.”

Read the full text of the lawmaker’s letter here and below:

Dear President Trump,

We respectfully request that you take immediate action on the Zuni Tribe’s recent request for a major disaster declaration in response to severe storms that triggered significant flash flooding and caused extensive damage in the Pueblo of Zuni between July 16, 2026, to July 28, 2026. The severity and magnitude of the storms and subsequent flash flooding overwhelmed Zuni Tribal resources, and they require supplemental, Federal assistance to ensure the Tribal Nation can recover.

The Zuni Tribe is requesting Public Assistance (PA), Categories A through G, as well as Individual Assistance (IA), including Disaster Unemployment Assistance, Small Business Administration (SBA) Disaster Assistance, Disaster Case Management, and Individuals and Households Program Assistance, and statewide assistance from the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program. We ask that you expeditiously grant the declaration and make this federal assistance available as soon as possible.

Three thunderstorm events on July 16, 21, and 28, 2026, in the Zuni Pueblo area produced heavy rainfall, with National Weather Service (NWS) radar and local rain gauge data indicating it was a 100-year flood event. This rainfall overtopped levees, riverbanks, and earthen dams, flooding paved roads and Zuni Village itself, and caused significant damage to private property, community infrastructure, ceremonial trails, and culturally significant sites. Sixty-one families were displaced, twelve families required sheltering, and four individuals required swift water rescue; six families are still in shelters.

The Zuni Tribe is a federally recognized sovereign Tribal Nation and one of the oldest continuously inhabited communities in North America. The Zuni Tribe serves as a steward of a nationally significant historic, cultural, and religious landscape. And in addition to extensive damage to public infrastructure and private property, the flash floods described above also severely impacted seven ceremonial trails and multiple culturally significant locations. Washouts, erosion, and material loss to those paths and sacred ruins – some dating back to the early 1500s – have affected the ancestral, ceremonial, and historic resources central to the Tribe’s cultural heritage. Restoration work will need to be performed using culturally appropriate methods, require specialized preservation oversight, and preserve the confidentiality of these sites.

In the wake of the flash flooding, the Zuni Tribe requested federal assistance with a Preliminary Damage Assessment, and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) staff and Zuni staff conducted site visits throughout the entire reservation. As of September 25, 2026, FEMA’s estimate for the assessed damage was $1,222,135. The severity and extent of the flooding required tribal resources to be diverted to emergency protective measures and hazardous debris removal. Recovery will require repairs to roadways and drainage systems, utility restoration, support for displaced families, and culturally appropriate preservation work. In totality, the impacts from these floods will require federal assistance, as they have exceeded the capabilities of the Zuni Tribe.

We fully support the Zuni Tribe’s request, and we urge you to act without delay. It is imperative that the federal government provides full support to the Zuni Tribe to recover from the devastation caused by this flooding.

Thank you for your consideration of this important request.

Sincerely,

title: Senator Marshall, Secretary Duffy Highlight Aviation Infrastructure & Modernization in Kansas
text:
Olathe – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), today joined U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Congressman Tracey Mann (KS-01) for visits to Kansas City Downtown Airport (MKC) and Indra Group’s radar manufacturing facility in Olathe, Kansas, to highlight aviation safety, air traffic control modernization, and critical transportation infrastructure investments across Kansas and the region.

“Kansas has a proud aviation history, and we need to make sure our infrastructure is keeping up. From modernizing our air traffic control systems to investing in our airports, these improvements are critical to keeping travelers safe, supporting good-paying jobs, and keeping America the gold standard in aviation,” said Senator Marshall. “I appreciate Secretary Duffy being here today to discuss how we can strengthen our aviation infrastructure and make sure Kansas remains a key part of America’s transportation future.”

“Thanks to President Trump, Senator Marshall, and Congressman Mann, the Working Families Tax Cut Act is fueling an $11 million modernization investment right here at MKC and boosting American jobs in the region,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “We’ve made historic progress, but the job’s not finished. To finally fix air travel for the American people, we need to pass the Modern Skies Act and I’m relying on our partners in Congress, including Reps. Marshall and Mann to get that done.”

At MKC, the group toured the airport’s air traffic control tower, originally built in 1942, where $11 million from the Republican passed Working Families Tax Cut Act is funding upgrades to modernize equipment and improve the technology air traffic controllers rely on to safely manage air traffic. The upgrades, scheduled over the next 18 months, include new voice communication systems, high-speed fiber connections to replace outdated copper wiring, a new Surface Awareness Initiative system, and updated controller displays. The new IP voice switches have already been installed.

Click here for more photos.

The group then visited Indra Group’s new radar manufacturing facility in Olathe, where the company manufactures next-generation air traffic control technology, including communications and radar systems for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The facility is on track to produce 40% of the radars being installed nationwide, underscoring Kansas’ role in strengthening America’s aviation infrastructure and supporting domestic manufacturing.

Click here for more photos.

The visits come as Kansas continues to benefit from federal transportation investments in highway improvements, airport infrastructure, freight movement, and other projects that support the state’s economy and connect communities across the region.

title: Dexter, Bonamici, Merkley Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Portland ICE Facility After Reports of Denied Access to Legal Counsel
text:
PORTLAND, OR – Today, Congresswomen Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) processing facility on Macadam Avenue in Portland following troubling reports that attorneys were repeatedly denied access to detained clients.

“No one should be denied access to legal counsel, regardless of their immigration status,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “It is a major concern when attorneys are repeatedly prevented from meeting with their clients. ICE is not above the law, and the Trump administration must be held accountable for how people are treated in federal custody. We are demanding answers, transparency and accountability.”

Rep. Dexter’s office received information from the Portland Immigrant Rights Coalition that attorneys were denied access to four clients on 12 separate occasions Tuesday. These reports, coupled with an uptick in ICE enforcement activity in the Portland area, prompted the lawmakers to conduct an oversight visit to demand answers and examine conditions at the facility.

“I just conducted a Congressional oversight visit at the ICE processing facility in Portland with Rep. Dexter and Senator Merkley,” Congresswoman Bonamici said. “ICE is not making us safer and this surge is increasing fear in the community. I encourage everyone to make a safety plan and take care of each other. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”

“ICE and Border Patrol agents are terrorizing our friends and neighbors,” Senator Merkley said. “Time after time, they are trampling civil rights, denying due process, and utilizing secret police tactics, totally wrong in our democratic republic. I’ll keep doing all I can to stop them.”

During the visit, the lawmakers asked about access to lawyers, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law. The visit builds on Rep. Dexter’s ongoing work to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable and protect the dignity and legal rights of people in ICE custody.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody and Governor DeSantis Warn Floridians in Pensacola Ahead of Isaias Landfall
Murphy, Lujan, Democratic Senators Say Broadcasters Owe Americans On Trump's Taxpayer-funded Campaign Ads
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) and Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) led Senate Democrats in a letter to American broadcasters demanding the release of all documentation on the decision to air Donald Trump’s self-promoting, federally-funded campaign ads.

The letter asserts, by allowing Trump’s publicly funded campaign ads to air, broadcasters failed to follow the law and have an obligation to reimburse taxpayers. Despite committing to pay for future campaign ads through his super PAC, Trump this week refused to reimburse the Treasury for the more than 10 million in taxpayer dollars already spent.

The Senators wrote: “Under the law, President Trump’s ads might plausibly fall into two categories: the ads are either produced by a ‘legally qualified candidate’ and therefore broadcasters are limited in their ability to censor the ads’ content, or President Trump’s ads are ‘public service announcements’ (PSAs) which would require broadcasters generally to follow all associated rules around the publication of PSAs. In either scenario, broadcasters appear to have failed in their duty to adhere to the spirit and letter of the law.”

In the letter, the Senators made the political nature of Trump’s ads clear, while pointing out the criminal consequences of using federal funds to air them: “These ads are instead a campaign ad designed to bolster the image of an unpopular president and to boost the electoral chances of the slate of Republican congressional candidates. But liability protection for broadcasters does not extend to non-candidates. Furthermore, broadcasters can still refuse to air campaign ads if they violate federal laws. In this case, there are several federal criminal provisions implicated by these ads. They include, but are not limited to, the Anti-Deficiency Act (ADA), the Hatch Act,2 and several appropriations provisions involving the use of taxpayer funds for propaganda and notably the purpose statute.4 Lastly, if they were campaign ads, the ads certainly could not be paid for with taxpayer funds, which should have been obvious to any first-year law student.”

Dismissing Trump’s ludicrous claim that these ads were ‘public service announcements,’ the Senators continued: “To most reasonable people, an ad that solely features the President covering the President’s alleged successes, choreographed to a musical performance and aired immediately before an election is undoubtedly a campaign ad. It’s ridiculous to assert otherwise. Furthermore, if these ads are considered PSAs, as the President asserts, they raise several legal and liability questions for broadcasters.

The Senators concluded: “We ask that you voluntarily release all communications with the President, any federal agency, or White House official about the ads to ensure transparency for the American public and clarify which funds you received, from which federal agency, and release the terms of the contract as soon as possible. Additionally, you should recognize these ads are not PSAs, and reimburse the Treasury.”

In addition to Murphy and Lujan, Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), and Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) also joined the letter.

The full letter is available here and below:

Broadcasters based in the United States:

We write today about the unprecedented self-promoting, taxpayer-funded ads starring President Donald Trump that ran across broadcast networks and online earlier this month. These bizarre ads prominently featured President Trump in a cinematic style with a soundtrack that begged Americans to love him. On October 5, 2026, after facing intense public backlash, the President announced that going forward he would pay for the ad using his super PAC.1 Given the unusual nature of these ads, we write to ask that you ensure the Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC) rules are followed. Specifically, we request that you voluntarily make any records related to these ads publicly available for inspection and reimburse the Treasury for the ads funded with taxpayer dollars.

Under the law, President Trump’s ads might plausibly fall into two categories: the ads are either produced by a ‘legally qualified candidate’ and therefore broadcasters are limited in their ability to censor the ads’ content, or President Trump’s ads are “public service announcements” (PSAs) which would require broadcasters generally to follow all associated rules around the publication of PSAs. In either scenario, broadcasters appear to have failed in their duty to adhere to the spirit and letter of the law.

Regarding the first category, Trump is not a candidate. These ads are instead a campaign ad designed to bolster the image of an unpopular president and to boost the electoral chances of the slate of Republican congressional candidates. But liability protection for broadcasters does not extend to non-candidates. Furthermore, broadcasters can still refuse to air campaign ads if they violate federal laws. In this case, there are several federal criminal provisions implicated by these ads. They include, but are not limited to, the Anti-Deficiency Act (ADA), the Hatch Act, and several appropriations provisions involving the use of taxpayer funds for propaganda and notably the purpose statute. Lastly, if they were campaign ads, the ads certainly could not be paid for with taxpayer funds, which should have been obvious to any first-year law student.

Regarding the second category, to most reasonable people, an ad that solely features the President covering the President’s alleged successes, choreographed to a musical performance and aired immediately before an election is undoubtedly a campaign ad. It’s ridiculous to assert otherwise. Furthermore, if these ads are considered PSAs, as the President asserts, they raise several legal and liability questions for broadcasters. A Public Service Announcement (PSA) has been defined by the FCC as “one for which no charge is made and which promotes programs, activities, or services of Federal, State or local governments (e.g., recruiting, sales of U.S. Savings Bonds, etc.) or the programs, activities or services of nonprofit organizations (e.g., UGF, Red Cross Blood Donations, etc.) or any other announcements regarded as serving community interests. PSAs are by definition, “announcements that are made for the good of the people.”

In other words, PSAs are generally required to be ads that inform the public. The ‘love me’ ad does not promote a program or a service of the federal government; it promotes alleged successes of the President and public reporting suggests broadcasters might already have taken millions in federal funds. As such, broadcasters have a duty to ensure that PSAs comply with applicable rules and could have easily refused to air the ads as PSAs.

In sum, we ask that you voluntarily release all communications with the President, any federal agency, or White House official about the ads to ensure transparency for the American public and clarify which funds you received, from which federal agency, and release the terms of the contract as soon as possible. Additionally, you should recognize these ads are not PSAs, and reimburse the Treasury.

title: In Vancouver, Senators Murray & Wyden Affirm Commitment to Protecting Medicare from AI Prior Authorization
text:
ICYMI: At HELP Hearing, Murray Grills Trump Nominees on AI Denying Seniors’ Health Care

ICYMI: On Senate Floor, Murray Urges Colleagues to End Trump Administration’s AI Program that is Delaying and Denying Seniors’ Health Care

***VIDEO OF FULL ROUNDTABLE DISCUSSION HERE***

***PHOTOS HERE***

Vancouver, WA — Today, U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and former chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and Ron Wyden (D-OR), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Finance, held a roundtable discussion with providers to discuss how the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) model, a new pilot program implemented by the Trump administration that’s using artificial intelligence (AI) to conduct prior authorization in Traditional Medicare, has been overruling doctors and denying or delaying critical health care for seniors. The WISeR pilot model began on January 1, 2026, and is set to last for six years in six selected states, including Washington state.

Joining Senators Murray and Wyden for the discussion at the Area Agency on Aging & Disabilities of Southwest Washington today were: Dr. Keren Rosenblum, MD, MBA, President, The Vancouver Clinic; Dr. Leon McCook, family medicine physician, PeaceHealth; and Dr. Ettore Palazzo, MD, FACP, CEO, EvergreenHealth.

“Despite a lot of empty promises from Republicans to not cut Medicare—Trump’s new WISeR model is essentially a cut to Medicare. What else do you call it when seniors are getting cut off from the health care they need, for no good reason? Under this dystopian system—Washington state seniors are seeking doctor-recommended care to treat debilitating pain, only to be told by Trump’s AI system that Medicare won’t pay for it, or that they must wait weeks on end to get their treatment,” said Senator Murray. “The truth is—the WISeR model has been a complete mess. This cannot continue—and it absolutely cannot expand. That’s why I’m here to continue talking with folks on the ground—patients, doctors and more—and gathering evidence and stories we can use to make the case back in Congress. We are going to keep pushing hard to stop private companies from raiding Medicare, and cheating seniors with AI. Republicans may be sitting on their hands but a Democratic majority will be aggressive in pushing back and working to end this experiment, and save Medicare.”

“Dr. Frankenstein isn’t the only one conducting dangerous experiments this Halloween season. The mad scientists given free rein in the Trump administration are quite willing to risk seniors’ access to lifesaving health care with their latest scheme grafting AI on to authorization decisions for traditional Medicare,” said Senator Wyden. “As the ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee overseeing Medicare, I’m proud to stand with Senator Murray in the battle against Trump empowering unaccountable AI companies to delay and deny certain types of care in traditional Medicare.”

“Physicians support innovation and efforts to reduce waste and improve value in health care. But those goals should not come at the expense of timely access to medically necessary care,” said Dr. Keren Rosenblum, MD, MBA, President, The Vancouver Clinic. “WISeR moves Traditional Medicare toward the same prior authorization system physicians already know creates administrative burdens, delays appropriate care, and creates uncertainty for patients. At a time when physicians are already facing significant administrative burdens and workforce challenges, we should be looking for ways to make health care simpler—not adding new layers of complexity. Innovation should strengthen the patient-physician relationship, not create new obstacles between patients and the care their physicians believe they need.”

“After almost a full year of WISeR, it is clear how its implementation has negatively impacted our patients and staff, but we are still unsure if the program is achieving its intended purpose. As a community-owned public hospital district, EvergreenHealth supports efforts to reduce fraud, waste and the inappropriate utilization of Medicare benefits. However, we must pursue those goals in a way that does not delay care nor create unnecessary hardship for the patients we serve,” saidDr. Ettore Palazzo, MD, FACP, CEO, EvergreenHealth. “In the months following WISeR’s January implementation, we saw patients live with prolonged pain due to delayed authorizations for their treatment. Confusion and inconsistent processes have created additional workloads for our providers, making it difficult for them to support their patients effectively. Let’s continue to improve quality, value and program integrity in Medicare, but let’s focus on patient-centered implementation, timely decision-making and reducing unnecessary burdens on our care teams.”

Under the WISeR model, patients on Traditional Medicare across six states—Arizona, New Jersey, Oklahoma, Ohio, Texas, and Washington—are subject to prior authorization requirements for several types of procedures or treatments, meaning that a claim needs to run through an opaque A.I.-driven system that may deny it with limited explanation. This forces starting the whole approval process over again and setting the patient back weeks in the process. Several of the procedures subject to prior authorization under the WISeR model are treatments for patients experiencing debilitating pain, who are now having to wait to receive necessary care. Before this model, patients would have been able to receive care within the same week, or even day, in most cases. Prior authorization requirements are used routinely by Medicare Advantage plans and private insurers, but rarely in Traditional Medicare—which is often one of the reasons seniors choose it for their coverage. While the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has described the model as voluntary, it is effectively mandatory for providers and their patients with Traditional Medicare in the selected states.

Each participating state is operating the pilot through a different for-profit company that contracts with CMS to use AI technology to process prior authorizations and conduct reviews for the specific services subject to WISeR. These participants are compensated based on a share of “averted expenditures.” In other words, they are financially incentivized to deny prior authorization requests, as they profit from denied services.

Senators Murray and Wyden have been pushing back on this harmful pilot program from the start, and for the past year and a half, Murray has been meeting with providers and patients across the state to hear about the implementation and harms of this program. In September of last year, Senators Murray, Wyden and other Senate Democrats sent a letter to CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz and Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) Director Abe Sutton, urging CMS to halt implementation of the model until a full analysis is conducted of the program’s impact on patient access—which, they argued, should include input from beneficiaries and their families, consumer and patient advocates, health care providers and suppliers. In December last year, Senators Murray and Wyden introduced the Seniors Deserve SMARTER (Streamlined Medical Approvals for Timely, Efficient Recovery) Care Act, legislation that would prohibit CMS from implementing the WISeR model that began on January 1, 2026.

This July, Murray and Wyden forced a vote on a Congressional Review Act (CRA) resolution to overturn the WISeR program—Republicans chose to side with the Trump administration and blocked the CRA. In September, Senator Murray grilled Chris Klomp, the nominee to be Deputy Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), on the WISeR model and how the private companies conducting the prior authorization assessments are profiting from the denials.

Senator Murray is also an original cosponsor of the bipartisan Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 to streamline and crack down on prior authorization practices in Medicare Advantage plans.

title: Padilla, Schmitt Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Critical Infrastructure from Theft and Vandalism
text:
Legislation would strengthen federal protections for copper, fiber, and coaxial cables

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.) introduced the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act, bipartisan legislation to combat the growing problem of theft and vandalism targeting critical infrastructure used to provide telecommunications and information services. The bill would strengthen federal protections for critical communications networks by making the willful or malicious theft, destruction, or damage of copper, fiber, and coaxial cables used to provide telecommunications and information services a federal criminal offense.

“Californians and consumers across the country deserve protection from the critical infrastructure attacks that have driven up service costs and disrupted internet service,” said Senator Padilla. “When critical infrastructure is vandalized, communities immediately feel the impacts — emergency phone calls are disrupted, communications networks experience widespread outages, and public safety is put at risk. Our bill would ensure protections for critical infrastructure across the state and country, strengthen connections across communities, and hold those who steal or vandalize such infrastructure responsible.”

“Missouri families and businesses rely on broadband every day, and when critical infrastructure is vandalized or stolen, they are the ones who ultimately pay the price through service disruptions and higher costs. My bill gives law enforcement another tool to protect the infrastructure that keeps communities connected and holds those who deliberately damage these networks accountable,” said Senator Schmitt.

California has experienced numerous incidents of theft and vandalism at critical communications sites. Such incidents can disrupt essential internet service and result in costly repairs that are often ultimately borne by consumers through higher service costs.

Last year, California had the most attacks on communications networks in the country, with more than 6,000 incidents reported and an estimated $252.6 million in losses. Los Angeles alone experienced a reported 1,131 attacks, the most of any city in the country.

The Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act would amend Section 1362 of Title 18 of the United States Code, which imposes penalties for vandalizing certain federal communications facilities. The legislation would expand the law to cover privately-operated facilities used to provide telecommunications and information services.

Specifically, the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act would:

Protect critical infrastructure: Explicitly includes copper, fiber, and coaxial cables used to provide telecommunications and information services within Section 1362’s purview;

Cover privately owned networks: Extends federal protections to facilities operated by private entities, including privately-owned broadband networks;

Penalize theft and vandalism: Imposes criminal penalties for the willful or malicious injury, destruction, or theft of covered copper, fiber, and coaxial cables, as well as attempts or conspiracies to commit those offenses; and

Protect lawful activities: Maintains protections for certain lawful concerted activities and excludes customer premises equipment from the new provisions.

“We applaud Sens. Schmitt and Padilla for introducing the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act, building important bipartisan, bicameral momentum to address the growing threat of vandalism to our nation’s critical communications infrastructure,” said NCTA, The Internet & Television Association. “These networks are essential to public safety, national security, and daily life, yet increasing copper theft and intentional damage are disrupting emergency services, harming communities, and leaving consumers without vital connectivity. Strengthening federal law with tougher deterrents and penalties will help protect these critical networks and the millions of Americans who rely on them every day.”

“America’s wireless networks must not only be built and operated effectively, but also protected,” said Kelly Cole, Senior VP of Government Affairs of CTIA. “Vandalism and theft are a growing reality impacting our critical infrastructure, and this legislation is a meaningful step toward deterring these crimes and holding bad actors accountable. We thank Senators Schmitt and Padilla for their leadership on this important issue and look forward to working with Congress to keep our networks safe and secure.”

“We’re grateful to Senators Schmitt and Padilla for stepping up to protect the critical communications networks Americans rely on every day,” said Spectrum. “The Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act takes meaningful action to update federal law to ensure all networks are protected.”

“We appreciate the leadership of Senators Schmitt and Padilla in introducing the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act,” said Elad Nafshi, Chief Network Officer of Comcast. “America’s broadband networks are the backbone of our small businesses, hospitals, schools, and homes, and this legislation is an important step to securing them.”

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: WATCH: Padilla Confirms Immigration Proceedings Taking Place in Basement of Downtown L.A. Federal Building During Unannounced ICE Oversight Visit
text:
LOS ANGELES, CA — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, conducted an unannounced oversight visit yesterday to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) holding facility at the federal Edward R. Roybal Building in downtown Los Angeles, where he learned that immigration proceedings are being conducted hidden away from public view in the building’s B-18 basement area. These hearings are taking place in the basement despite the existence of an immigration court in the same building on the fourth floor. Proceedings in immigration court are generally open to the public, with limited exceptions. The building’s B-18 area is not accessible to the public, raising serious concerns about transparency and accountability as this Administration continues to carry out its mass deportation agenda.

The visit comes as the Trump Administration reportedly launched a 45-day immigration enforcement surge in California, raising urgent questions about yet another expansion of federal immigration enforcement and the transparency and due process afforded to people in government custody. This marks Padilla’s second unannounced visit to an immigration detention facility in as many weeks as he continues to conduct oversight of the Trump Administration’s immigration enforcement operations across California.

“The Trump Administration is ramping up its indiscriminate immigration enforcement across California, and we know what that means: arrest first, questions later — even for people with legal status and, in some cases, U.S. citizens,” said Senator Padilla. “That’s why these oversight visits are so important. We need to know what’s happening behind closed doors inside these detention facilities. The fact that immigration proceedings are taking place in the basement of a federal building that is not easily accessible by the public raises serious questions about transparency, access to legal representation, and due process for people in government custody. As a United States Senator, I have a constitutional responsibility to conduct oversight and hold this Administration accountable. I will continue showing up, asking questions, and demanding answers about how ICE and this Administration are treating people and whether their rights are being respected.”

The Trump Administration’s expanding immigration crackdown has raised growing concerns about the treatment of people detained by federal immigration authorities, the conditions in which they are held, and the lack of transparency surrounding enforcement operations.

Padilla has repeatedly conducted oversight visits to immigration detention facilities across California to examine conditions firsthand and demand accountability from federal officials. His visits have included facilities in California City, Otay Mesa, San Francisco International Airport, and now downtown Los Angeles. These efforts come as the Trump Administration expands its immigration crackdown while providing limited transparency into its enforcement and detention operations.

title: Peters, Schiff, Bilirakis, Pallone Lead Colleagues in Urging State Department to Help End Azerbaijan’s Military Presence in Armenia and Secure the Release of Armenian Prisoners Illegally Held by Azerbaijan
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), along with U.S. Representatives Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12) and Frank Pallone (D-NJ-06), led more than 100 of their colleagues in sending a bipartisan, bicameral letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the State Department to prioritize the release of Armenian detainees being unlawfully held in Azerbaijan. Those being detained include political and military leaders of Nagorno-Karabakh who have been illegally imprisoned since Azerbaijan’s attack on the region in 2023. Additionally, the letter calls on Secretary Rubio to advocate for the removal of Azerbaijani military forces from within Armenia. Currently, Azerbaijan maintains a military presence in over 200 square kilometers of land within Armenia. Furthermore, the letter instructs the State Department to withhold military assistance from Azerbaijan if the government remains uncooperative on addressing these issues.

“June 23rd, 2026, marked the 1000th day of unlawful detention for the Armenian prisoners in Azerbaijan’s custody,” the lawmakers wrote. “It is imperative that the United States applies meaningful pressure on Azerbaijan to ensure their release, as required under international law.”

The lawmakers continued, “We call on the administration to engage with Azerbaijan to secure the release of the detainees and encourage the removal of Azerbaijani military forces from sovereign Armenian land. If meaningful steps are not taken, we urge your administration to withhold U.S. military assistance in order to demonstrate the United States’ commitment to ensuring all parties take the peace process seriously.”

“As Azerbaijan continues to unlawfully detain Armenian hostages, destroy Artsakh’s ancient Christian heritage, and occupy Armenia’s sovereign territory, the U.S. should not be subsidizing the very regime responsible for these abuses. Instead, Washington should use its leverage to hold Baku accountable for its aggression and advance a truly just, durable, and dignified peace in the South Caucasus,” said Armenian National Committee of America Executive Director Aram Hamparian. “The ANCA thanks Senator Peters, Senator Schiff, and Representatives Bilirakis and Pallone for leading this bipartisan, bicameral call to withhold U.S. military assistance to Azerbaijan. The support of 101 Members of Congress on this letter sends a clear message: Azerbaijan’s destabilizing conduct and repeated violations of international law must not be rewarded with U.S. taxpayer dollars.”

“The extent of bipartisan and bicameral support reflects a clear recognition in Congress that U.S. policy toward Azerbaijan must be grounded in accountability and measurable outcomes. The unlawful detention of Armenian hostages remains a serious humanitarian and rule-of-law concern that has direct bearing on U.S. policy. Section 907 equips the government with leverage that should ensure U.S. military assistance to Azerbaijan is aligned with concrete progress toward accountability, regional stability, and a durable peace. Congress has sent a clear signal that these concerns warrant sustained attention by the Administration’s engagement in the region. U.S. policy should guarantee a lasting peace,” said Mariam Khaloyan, Director of Congressional Relations at the Armenian Assembly of America.

Peters visited the Armenia-Azerbaijan border in September 2023 and viewed firsthand the Azerbaijani blockade of the Lachin corridor. In response to his visit, he introduced the Armenian Protection Act, which unanimously passed in the Senate in November 2023. The Armenian Protection Act would end U.S. assistance to the Azerbaijani government that is currently allowed under a waiver to Section 907 of the Freedom Support Act. Although the Freedom Support Act generally prohibits most bilateral assistance to Azerbaijan, following the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, waiver authority was added to Section 907 granting additional discretion to the President to provide aid to Azerbaijan. The waiver authority has been invoked annually by Presidents of both parties until 2023 when the Biden Administration withheld the renewal of the waiver following Azerbaijan’s attack on Nagorno-Karabakh. The Trump Administration has since reauthorized the waiver in August 2025 and August of 2026.

title: Reed Blasts Hegseth for Planning to Live-Stream the Execution of Fort Hood Shooter
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In response to U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announcing plans to live-stream the military execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, a former U.S. Army psychiatrist who opened fire on dozens of people at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center in Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, Senate Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Jack Reed (D-RI) issued the following statement:

“Live-streaming an execution is a barbaric spectacle. This is yet another stunt by Secretary Hegseth to distract from his tenure’s repeated failings which have only weakened our national security and standing in the world.

“The Trump Administration should reconsider this abhorrent move, which only gives the shooter what he wants: more attention and more control. Instead of forcing the shooter to face justice, the Trump Administration is literally handing him more power and offering him a global platform to amplify his hateful, anti-American message. This is a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters. It is absolutely shameful and damaging to America’s interests and core values.”

Army Regulation 190-55 governs who may witness military executions and does not provide for unrestricted public attendance, but it may be waived by the Commander-in-Chief.

title: Reed Seeks to Ban Exploitative AI-Enabled Price Discrimination
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI -- As major retailers begin using artificial intelligence (AI) to make so-called ‘surveillance pricing’ or ‘personal pricing’ more intrusive, unfair, and opaque, U.S. Senator Jack Reed is seeking to prevent companies from unfairly charging consumers more based on personal data algorithms.

Personalized or individualized price discrimination broadly refers to the practice of retailers “using troves of personal data to set individualized prices. As a result, people are paying different amounts for the same exact product, just because businesses are better equipped to infer who will pay more.”

During a visit to the Bom Café in Providence today, Senator Reed joined café owner Rosie Santana and Nina Harrison, Policy Director of the Economic Progress Institute (EPI), for a conversation about the importance of marketplace fairness and preventing unfair AI-enabled cost manipulation.

“Consumers deserve transparent pricing and equal treatment, not hidden technology that misuses their personal data to set different prices for the same item and charge some shoppers more than others. AI is a powerful tool, but it presents real and pressing challenges. This is one of them and Congress needs to take thoughtful, concrete steps to ban exploitative AI-enabled price discrimination and ensure fairness in the marketplace. Whether it’s food, coffee, or basic staples, no family should pay hidden premiums and higher prices for the same product based on their personal online data that has been collected without their knowledge or consent,” said Senator Reed.

The Economic Progress Institute recently released its biennial Rhode Island Standard of Need report offering a snapshot of what it costs for individuals and families to afford a no-frills life in Rhode Island. The 2026 report calculates monthly and annual budgets for housing, food, transportation, health care, child care, and other essentials—and shows that nearly 40 percent of Rhode Island households may not have enough income to meet their basic needs.

“Rhode Islanders literally cannot afford to have surveillance pricing in this state. They cannot afford for companies to take their personal information and use that personal information against them to raise prices and make things even less affordable. Working families can’t afford it. We can't allow it. And that’s why I’m so grateful to Senator Reed for doing this work and raising this issue to try to get ahead of it and prevent surveillance pricing before it harms Rhode Islanders,” said EPI’s Policy Director Nina Harrison.

An investigation by Consumer Reports and Groundwork Collaborative found that popular grocery apps like Instacart used AI-enabled pricing experiments to inflate the grocery bills of some users. AI-powered algorithms led to some shoppers getting charged $3.99 for a box of Wheat Thins, while another shopper from the same store at the same time was charged $4.89. Based on how much Instacart estimates a typical household of four spends on groceries, the average price variations observed could translate into a cost swing of $1,200 per year on food alone.

Senator Reed says there should be federal guardrails and clear, durable consumer protection laws in place that keep pace with the needs of Americans and rapidly-evolving technology.

Businesses have long used algorithmic pricing to determine how much consumers are willing to pay for products and services. But those systems set general prices for the masses based on supply, demand, competitor prices, and other broad data points. These new exploitative AI-enabled algorithms use personal data as a tool for price discrimination to try to ensure every consumer pays the maximum.

As AI becomes more common-place, more companies are starting to experiment with ‘personalized’ or ‘surveillance’ pricing, including the use of personal information such as browsing history, demographics, or behavioral patterns, and companies typically collect and analyze the data using AI and algorithms to charge different prices for different customers, based on a range of factors, such as their income, zip code/geolocation, mouse movements, or other personal data.

Reed is urging Congress to take bipartisan action to crack down on algorithmic price discrimination and prevent companies from using non-public data and artificial intelligence to unfairly squeeze every last penny out of consumers.

“If federal lawmakers fail to act, online shoppers will be at increased risk of price gouging, cost manipulation, and data privacy threats as more businesses use AI to target the finances, privacy, and equality of consumers,” said Senator Reed. “To ensure a healthy and prosperous Rhode Island, we must ensure working families can afford basic necessities. I will work across the aisle to ban AI-enabled price discrimination while ensuring companies can continue offering targeted discounts, promotions, rewards, loyalty and membership benefits, or contextual pricing.”

Many consumers are already being charged more money through ‘dynamic pricing’ for things like rideshares, airline tickets, and hotels whose prices can go up when demand is high and change based on timing and location. But even dynamic pricing is a concept that raises prices for all consumers, not just certain individuals.

title: Sens. Rick Scott, Ashley Moody Support Florida’s Request for Pre-Landfall Emergency Declaration for Hurricane Isaias
text:
NAPLES, Fla. – Today, U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ashley Moody sent a letter to President Donald Trump requesting his immediate approval of the State of Florida’s request for a pre-landfall emergency declaration for 27 Florida counties ahead of Hurricane Isaias’s expected landfall along the Gulf Coast tonight. Hurricane Isaias is now a major category 3 hurricane, bringing severe weather and life-threatening storm surges to communities throughout the Florida Panhandle.

Senator Scott received a briefing yesterday at the Port of Pensacola from local and state leaders, law enforcement, and emergency management officials in Pensacola ahead of Hurricane Isaias’s anticipated landfall. He continues to receive daily briefings from the National Hurricane Center on Hurricane Isaias, and spoke to President Trump on Wednesday, October 7, about the federal response to this storm.

Read the full letter HERE or below:

Dear Mr. President:

We write in support of Florida Governor Ron DeSantis’s request for a pre-landfall emergency declaration covering 27 Florida counties in preparation for Hurricane Isaias, which has strengthened into a major hurricane and is expected to make landfall along Florida’s western Panhandle this evening.

Hurricane Isaias poses a serious threat to Florida communities, with life-threatening storm surge, destructive winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding expected across the affected region. With landfall imminent, timely federal assistance is critical to supporting state and local emergency response efforts and protecting Floridians, their property, and their communities.

We urge you to promptly approve Governor DeSantis’s request for a pre-landfall emergency declaration to ensure Florida has access to the federal resources necessary to prepare for and respond to this dangerous storm.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent matter and for your continued support of Florida.

Sincerely,

Senator Scott encourages all Floridians to visit his website at www.rickscott.senate.gov/hurricane-preparedness to get prepared today. See the latest on Hurricane Isaias from the National Hurricane Center at nhc.noaa.gov or @NHC_Atlantic on X, formerly known as Twitter, and from the Florida Division of Emergency Management at floridadisaster.org or @FLSERT.

Additionally, Senator Scott encourages those recovering from previous hurricanes who need assistance with a federal agency, including FEMA and the SBA, or any other federal issue to contact his office at www.rickscott.senate.gov/contact/casework.

title: Rosen Helps Introduce Bill to Strengthen Critical Minerals Supply Chain
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) helped introduce legislation to strengthen the United States’ supply chain for critical minerals. The Critical Mineral Executive Coordination Act would improve diplomatic training and executive branch coordination, creating a more comprehensive strategy for the acquisition of these important minerals and addressing vulnerabilities in global critical mineral supply chains. Critical minerals and rare earth metals play a key role in most modern technology.

“With the People’s Republic of China controlling global critical minerals supply chains, the United States needs a durable strategy to secure reliable access to the resources that power our modern economy,” said Senator Rosen. “I am proud to help introduce this bipartisan bill to make sure our government has the training, skill, and supply chains necessary to maintain and grow the United States’ critical mineral leadership and ensure we’re not just playing catch-up to China.”

Senator Rosen has worked to solidify U.S. global leadership in critical minerals and rare earth elements. Earlier this year, she introduced bipartisan legislation to strengthen American STEM education and build a workforce pipeline to support the growing domestic critical mineral mining industry through the creation of a mining Fulbright exchange program. Senator Rosen has also worked to promote responsible hardrock mining practices in Nevada and around the world. In February, Senator Rosen’s bill to combat illicit gold mining in the Western Hemisphere passed out of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. Last Congress, Senator Rosen helped secure a provision in the bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act to grow the next generation of mining engineers, promote the use of critical minerals, and develop a secure and reliable supply chain.

title: NEWS: Sanders, 189 Colleagues Demand RFK Withdraw Latest Attempt to Illegally Dismantle Head Start
text:
WASHINGTON, October 7 — After the Trump administration proposed removing over 90% of Head Start’s standards and leaving children nationwide to face the possibility of becoming ineligible overnight, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, Rep. Bobby Scott (D-Va.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Education and Workforce, and 188 members of Congress called on Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to withdraw this latest attempt to illegally dismantle the federal Head Start program.

“Let us be very clear: what you are proposing seriously weakens the high-quality, comprehensive research-backed services required by law, undermines access to critical services, restricts access for children and families, and creates uncertainty for Head Start programs across the nation,” Sanders and the lawmakers wrote. “This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year.”

Since taking office, the Trump administration has undertaken unprecedented efforts to gut Head Start — the program that has provided high-quality early education and comprehensive services for more than 40 million children and working-class families for over 60 years. President Trump has fired federal staff, threatened to eliminate the program entirely, illegally withheld funds from Head Start and slashed critical programs for children and families to pay for $1 trillion in tax breaks for the top 1% and over $900 billion in tax breaks for large corporations. Today, nearly 800,000 children receive early education, health and dental care, and healthy meals through Head Start, while their families access referrals for job training, adult education, nutrition services and housing support.

“Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” the lawmakers wrote. “Under your proposal, 80% of children in Head Start will face worse staff-to-child ratios. Nearly 1 in 10 children currently served in Head Start could become ineligible for services overnight. Key Head Start health, dental, mental health, and developmental services will be reduced nationwide. And the duration of the Head Start school day could be cut in half in many communities, leaving working families stranded and without child care. That is unacceptable.”

The Trump administration’s proposed rule would illegally weaken the protections and services required under the Head Start Act. Specifically, it would:

Eliminate critical quality and safety standards for Head Start classrooms, including requirements for safe learning environments, appropriate staff-to-child ratios, qualified teachers and staff, and high-quality instruction.

Cut critical health services that children and families depend on, including preventive, oral health, and mental health services.

Shorten Head Start operating hours, reducing the amount of time children can access early education and comprehensive services.

Eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, putting vulnerable children at greater risk of losing access to Head Start.

Undermine services for dual language learners, making it harder for children to receive the support they need to succeed in the classroom.

“You made a commitment to Congress to ‘preserve’ Head Start, yet this proposed rule is the latest attempt by the Administration to deteriorate and ultimately eliminate the program by gutting the core standards and services that have long-defined and ensured its success.” The senators concluded: “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”

Joining Sanders as cosigners on the letter are Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Christopher Coons (D-Del.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Timothy Kaine (D-Va.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

title: ICYMI: Sen. Schiff Talks AI Guardrails, Competition with China, and Outlook for Tech Regulation in New Congress at Punchbowl News Tech Summit
text:
San Francisco, CA — This week, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) discussed his view on rapidly developing AI capabilities and the role of Congress in regulating the technology during an interview with Punchbowl News co-founders Jake Sherman and Anna Palmer at the publication’s first-ever Tech Summit in San Francisco.

In the wide-ranging discussion, Schiffhighlighted his legislation to ensure private industry pays for the energy they use amid the buildout of data centers – so that Americans are not forced to pay higher energy costs as a result of the AI boom – and discussed Democrats’ approach to AI oversight next year, noting that Americans should “expect constructive oversight, not destructive oversight.”

Schiff also discussedthe risks he sees in rapidly advancing AI models and argued that concerns about competition with China should include prioritization of safety, developing a skilled workforce, and improving education.

View the full interview here.

Key Excerpts:

On Democrats’ AI priorities should control of Congress flip:

[…] I think the industry should expect constructive oversight, not destructive oversight. I think it should expect a Democratic majority that wants technology to succeed, wants these jobs to stay in America, wants their contribution to the economy and medicine and science but believes in regulation. Does not believe that any group of people be by dint of their wealth are empowered to make decisions affecting all of society for themselves. I think that’s what they should expect.

[…] What I do want to see is oversight that leads to sensible regulation of an industry that can do a lot of good and can do a lot of harm. To minimize the harms, to protect against the harms, do what government is supposed to do. I want to see a Congress that does what we have done in the past when we also had massive powerful corporations but we’re not afraid to regulate them. That is a basic function of government.

On why Congress must move quickly to put guardrails on advanced AI:

[…] I do think we need to put in place protocols and monitors, a system to make sure that as these frontier models are developing, they’re developing safely. That there are processes in place where we don’t have to simply take the word of the companies that ‘don’t worry we’re doing it safely.’ I certainly don’t believe the self-policing; the moral authority argument is sufficient. There’s just too much profit motive, too much of a collective action problem that confronts the whole industry globally.

[…] You train the power of AI to find out everything it can about a single individual. Do we really think that their health records or their purchases or their subscriptions or any of their data is beyond the reach of an AI agent, sophisticated model, trying to find out the personal information? And with all the Flock cameras and with all the other CCTV cameras and the vulnerability of those systems, are we going to have any privacy left? And I think unless Congress acts, there won’t be any privacy left.

On ensuring AI development is safe as we compete with China to establish AI dominance:

[…] I get that we should be very concerned about China’s advances in this area. I don’t want to dismiss that argument. That’s an argument that says that we need to reach some kind of an accord with China, which won’t be easy to do, but we need to do our best. It is not an argument though that, because China is making advances and we want to stay ahead of China, that we should rush headlong with the development of these models and regenerative AI in such a way that well, ‘let’s be sure that if we kill ourselves we do it first rather than letting China do it.’ We still want to make sure what we’re doing is safe for our people and safe for others.

[…] Why don’t we focus on improving our education system? Improving STEM education, making sure that everyone who graduates from high school has a good solid education, that the doors of higher education are open. Let’s compete with China on a skilled workforce. Let’s compete with China in how we think about the integration and the manufacturing of products that will incorporate AI. That’s where a lot of the economic benefits are going to come.

On passing legislation to protect Americans from absorbing higher costs from data center buildouts:

[…] I introduced an early bill on this that would insist essentially that these data centers pay their own way. That they not only develop their own energy, but also that they have additional capacity to put energy into the grid during peak times. That they are responsible for the upgrades to the regional system that those costs are not socialized to others. It’s not hard to require that. It’s certainly not going to be done just by some kind of, ‘well, we give you our word.’

[…] There should be complete transparency. I don’t think people should be misled about a project and then suddenly learn it’s going to be a data center in their backyard. But I don’t think everywhere is the same and I think communities should make the decision. Do they want it? Do they not want it? And some communities may want it, and many will not want it and that ought to be a decision that is made locally and I think not nationally. But we should be insistent nationally that those costs and burdens not be socialized onto others.

On the Senate’s latest proposal for permitting reform:

[…] We absolutely need permitting reform, and it looks like we may be close. What I’m going to be particularly looking at, and the text was just released, so we’re all kind of digging through it, is this going to be just regulatory reform for the oil and gas industry? Is this really just going to be used to advance those two sources of energy or, is this going to be advantageous to renewables? And what about in an administration in which there is almost a theocratic objection to anything but oil and gas? We’ve seen our state punished repeatedly by this president who only represents those states that he won. Is that going to continue? Are there any meaningful limits on that in this permitting reform? That’s what I’m going to be looking at.

###

title: NEWS: Schiff, Peters, Bilirakis, and Pallone Lead 100+ Colleagues in Urging State Department to Help End Azerbaijan’s Military Presence in Armenia and Secure the Release of Armenian Prisoners Illegally Held by Azerbaijan
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Gary Peters (D-Mich.), along with U.S. Representatives Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.-12) and Frank Pallone (D-N.J.-06), led over 100 lawmakers in sending a bipartisan, bicameral letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the State Department to prioritize the release of Armenian detainees being unlawfully held in Azerbaijan.

“We are concerned that amid these positive steps Azerbaijan continues to undermine the peace process. Azerbaijan’s decision to sentence the unlawfully detained Armenian prisoners of war demonstrates a willingness to upend stability. Additionally, the presence of Azerbaijani military forces in more than 200 square kilometers of Armenian territory creates asymmetry in ongoing talks,” the lawmakers wrote.

Those being detained include political and military leaders of Nagorno-Karabakh who have been illegally imprisoned since Azerbaijan’s attack on the region in 2023. Additionally, the letter calls on Secretary Rubio to advocate for the removal of Azerbaijani military forces from within Armenia. Currently, Azerbaijan maintains a military presence in over 200 square kilometers of land within Armenia. Furthermore, the letter instructs the State Department to withhold military assistance from Azerbaijan if the government remains uncooperative on addressing these issues.

“The United States has a critical role in ensuring that ongoing talks yield results that advance peace and security in the region,” the lawmakers continued.

“As Azerbaijan continues to unlawfully detain Armenian hostages, destroy Artsakh’s ancient Christian heritage, and occupy Armenia’s sovereign territory, the U.S. should not be subsidizing the very regime responsible for these abuses. Instead, Washington should use its leverage to hold Baku accountable for its aggression and advance a truly just, durable, and dignified peace in the South Caucasus,” said Aram Hamparian, Executive Director of Armenian National Committee of America. “The ANCA thanks Senator Peters, Senator Schiff, and Representatives Bilirakis and Pallone for leading this bipartisan, bicameral call to withhold U.S. military assistance to Azerbaijan. The support of 101 Members of Congress on this letter sends a clear message: Azerbaijan’s destabilizing conduct and repeated violations of international law must not be rewarded with U.S. taxpayer dollars.”

“The extent of bipartisan and bicameral support reflects a clear recognition in Congress that U.S. policy toward Azerbaijan must be grounded in accountability and measurable outcomes. The unlawful detention of Armenian hostages remains a serious humanitarian and rule-of-law concern that has direct bearing on U.S. policy. Section 907 equips the government with leverage that should ensure U.S. military assistance to Azerbaijan is aligned with concrete progress toward accountability, regional stability, and a durable peace. Congress has sent a clear signal that these concerns warrant sustained attention by the Administration’s engagement in the region. U.S. policy should guarantee a lasting peace,” said Mariam Khaloyan, Director of Congressional Relations at the Armenian Assembly of America.

Background: Tuesday, June 23, 2026 marked 1,000 days since Armenian prisoners of war and civilian hostages were unlawfully detained by Azerbaijan following the ethnic cleansing of Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh) in 2023. At least 19 Armenians are still held as POWs and 120,000 civilians were forcefully displaced.

California is home to nearly 250,000 Armenians – more than half of the Armenian diaspora in the United States – and Senator Schiff has been a strong champion for the Armenian community, leading Congress to formally recognize the Armenian Genocide in 2019.

Schiff has consistently submitted provisions to be included in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to bring home Armenian POWs following Azerbaijan’s ethnic cleansing of Artsakh in 2023. He will continue pushing for the release of POWs.

Most recently, Schiff urged the Department of State to highlight Azerbaijan’s human rights abuses in its Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for 2025 and push for an end to Azerbaijan’s continued human rights violations.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We recognize the work this administration has done to mediate peace negotiations between Armenia and Azerbaijan. Furthermore, we note efforts by Armenia and Azerbaijan to resolve longstanding border disputes through consistent talks. However, we are concerned that amid these positive steps Azerbaijan continues to undermine the peace process. Azerbaijan’s decision to sentence unlawfully detained Armenian prisoners of war demonstrates a willingness to upend stability. Additionally, the presence of Azerbaijani military forces in more than 200 square kilometers of Armenian territory creates asymmetry in ongoing talks. This context illustrates Azerbaijan’s fragile commitment to the process and emphasizes the importance of the United States remaining engaged on this issue. As Azerbaijan’s conduct threatens to compromise the integrity of the peace process, we note with concern the recent decision to reauthorize the waiver of Section 907 of the FREEDOM Support Act [U.S. Public Law No: 102-511]. Despite the issuance of the waiver, we urge your administration to withhold U.S. military assistance to Azerbaijan if they continue to jeopardize the success of negotiations. The United States has a critical role in ensuring that ongoing talks yield results that advance peace and security in the region.

In February 2026, Azerbaijan sentenced 16 Armenian detainees to extended terms ranging from 15 years to life in prison. These sentences followed a series of trials that were widely rebuked by international human rights organizations, legal experts, and the European Parliament as a miscarriage of justice. Azerbaijan continues to imprison scores of domestic journalists, opposition leaders, and activists on politically motivated and unfounded charges. The decision to proceed with the trials and sentencing of Armenian detainees is consistent with Azerbaijan’s practice of denying fundamental due process and rule of law. The detainees included political and military leaders of Nagorno-Karabakh who have been held illegally since Azerbaijan’s military assault on the region in 2023. Almost three years have passed since Azerbaijan’s attack on Nagorno-Karabakh forcibly displaced over 100,000 Armenian inhabitants in what has been widely characterized as an act of ethnic cleansing. In addition to forced displacement there continue to be reports of the destruction of Armenian Churches in Nagorno-Karabakh. The pattern of cultural erasure in the region and the decision to move forward with sentencing these individuals calls into question Azerbaijan’s genuine commitment to long term peace and stability.

On April 29, 2026, Armenia and Azerbaijan held the thirteenth meeting to discuss border delimitation. Addressing longstanding border disputes remains a critical task to ensure the stability of any future peace agreement. So far, the only practical outcome from these talks has come from Armenia’s efforts to address Soviet-era territorial disputes. In May of 2024 Armenia returned four Azerbaijani enclave villages that had been under Armenian control since the first Karabakh war. However, these efforts have been complicated by Azerbaijan’s ongoing occupation of an estimated 241.4 sq kilometers of Armenian territory, following military encroachments into Armenia in 2021 and 2022. Azerbaijan’s recent encroachments and entrenched military presence within Armenia’s internationally recognized borders presents a security challenge and sets the stage for asymmetric negotiations. A just outcome to these talks is imperative to maintaining the integrity of Armenian sovereignty and ensuring long-term stability in the region. We encourage the administration to use existing leverage, such as withholding military assistance, to ensure positive outcomes.

Following a White House summit with the leaders of Armenia and Azerbaijan last year, the waiver of Section 907 of the FREEDOM Support Act was extended. Although the summit was an important step in the right direction there is still significant work to be done to address unresolved humanitarian and security issues. It is clear, that the decision to waive Section 907 has not induced Azerbaijan’s engagement on ensuring the release of detainees. As a result, we are concerned that Azerbaijan’s inconsistent behavior jeopardizes the prospect of a just and long-lasting peace in the region – and that the continued waiver of Section 907 without a commitment to addressing these concerns will only further encourage destabilizing actions.

June 23rd, 2026, marked the 1000th day of unlawful detention for the Armenian prisoners in Azerbaijan’s custody. It is imperative that the United States applies meaningful pressure on Azerbaijan to ensure their release, as required under international law. We call on the administration to engage with Azerbaijan to secure the release of detainees and encourage the removal of Azerbaijani military forces from sovereign Armenian land. If meaningful steps are not taken, we urge your administration to withhold U.S. military assistance in order to demonstrate the United States’ commitment to ensuring all parties take the peace process seriously.

We thank you for your consideration and look forward to the opportunity to work with you on efforts to ensure peace and stability in the region.
