title: WATCH: Sen. Schiff Calls for Stronger Guardrails on AI, Promises Vigorous Oversight of Rogue Agent Episodes on The Verge’s Decoder Podcast
text:
Schiff on the need for bipartisan action on AI regulation: “Increasingly, as people hear from their constituents, there’ll be bipartisan interest in legislating this area.”

Washington, D.C. – This week, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) detailed his AI priorities during an appearance on The Verge’s Decoder Podcast with Nilay Patel. During the interview, Schiff highlighted the need for enforceable industry-wide guardrails that protect against the potential harms of frontier AI development and underscored that voluntary commitments like the framework put forward by Donald Trump would not be enough.

Schiff also noted that if control of Congress changes, Democrats will pursue oversight of harmful AI incidents, noting: “You’re going to see vigorous oversight in this area… We’re going to want the leaders of this industry to come in and talk about all of the times that their own agents have gotten away from them, how it happened, what’s been done about it, and what they’re doing about it. We’re going to want these companies to be transparent with Congress about it.”

The Senator also voiced support for the establishment of a regulatory body designed with the high expertise and discretion necessary to keep up with advanced model development.

View the full interview here.

Key Excerpts:

On how Congress’s failure to regulate social media should inform its approach to putting guardrails on AI:

I’ll be honest, very circumspect about Congress and legislating the tech sector because we did such a — I don’t know what language I’m allowed to use here — but such a shitty job when it comes to any kind of regulation of the harms, the societal harms coming out of social media. We’re going to have to do a much better job and much more quickly when it comes to AI, because the threats are even more significant and we’re already at the point of strong potential harms. It can’t wait. We certainly can’t take the kind of years we’ve taken to try to even wrap ourselves around social media.

On how Democrats would conduct tech industry oversight if control of Congress flips:

You’re going to see vigorous oversight in this area to begin with. We’re going to want the leaders of this industry to come in and talk about all of the times that their own agents have gotten away from them, how it happened, what’s been done about it, and what they’re doing about it. We’re going to want these companies to be transparent with Congress about it. We’re going to want to legislate in this area, and that may come into conflict with the president, but there’s a lot of bipartisan work product here. And I think that given where the country is and where it’s moving, it becomes increasingly difficult for this president to veto bipartisan work product coming out of the Congress. So that is my hope. It’s certainly a far better prospect than we have today. This is going to be a very central priority for the American people. We want to harness AI for the good it can do. We want to use it to bring down the cost of things. That’s our central priority. And there are ways that AI might be useful in bringing down certain costs. We want to protect the dignity of work also, but we want to make sure that this doesn’t pose a threat to the American people.

On Trump’s voluntary AI regulatory framework not being enough to match the threat of frontier advancements:

It was interesting to see all those tech leaders there signing onto this voluntary pledge on the one hand and on the other hand, away from the White House grounds, away from the president, being very public and saying, “We need regulation. We don’t want this to be just ‘Trust us, we’ll do the right thing.’” So yeah, it was very distant, very jarring. None of these companies want to incur the wrath of this very vengeful president. Apparently, they will say what he wants them to say in his presence. But the reality is, there is a real national security threat here. As these models become more and more advanced, as they advance themselves through this recursive AI, we have less and less of a sense of what they’re doing, how they’re deciding what they’re deciding, and what they’re trying to access lawfully or unlawfully. That is a national security concern of the highest order. There are other security concerns too.

On the need for a regulatory body to keep up with advanced model development:

This debate is going to keep evolving as AI evolves and at a speed that is really much faster than Congress has proven capable of legislating. I like to say that in the technology world, Moore’s law is increasing productivity, doubling it every 18 months, and with AI, maybe that’s quadrupling it every five months. The legislative calendar works more on a Murphy’s law timetable. And I think that disparity is even more pronounced in the area of AI. What I think that translates into is that we’re going to need a regulatory body that has real discretion and real expertise that can move a lot quicker than Congress can. Whether that looks like an FDA for artificial intelligence or some other agency, I think that’s ultimately going to be necessary. That agency’s going to have to have real power and teeth and real expertise. It’s going to be a challenge, as with these independent monitors: if there’s a government component there, how do we afford that? Because there’s so much talent, and that talent can draw much bigger salaries in the private sector. But I do think we’re going to need a regulatory body in addition to whatever the overarching statutory framework is.

On the need for enforceable industry-wide regulation of AI and data center build outs:

Data centers are the most tangible way for people to express their concerns about their neighborhood, but also about their job, about the technology, and about the uncertainty of it all. And I think the initial concern, and I still think it’s quite a dominant concern, is over the impact on jobs and the nature of work. But what has reached the fore more recently is concern about runaway AI and the danger it poses. What will the concern look like a month or two months from now? I don’t know, but I do think it’s not going away. And as the AI bills — and I’ve introduced several — indicate, not just mine, but others, most of those bills are bipartisan. […] My bill on the data centers would force them to pay the costs so that consumers don’t have to. It’s not the voluntary, “we pledge, we might, we’d like to; just don’t provide anything that will force us to observe those costs.” Those are mostly democratic bills. Republicans have largely adhered to the president’s line about not posing any real imposition. They want to pass fig-leaf kind of stuff, but not real stuff. But I think increasingly, as people hear from their constituents, there’ll be bipartisan interest in legislating this area.

###

title: AFTER LEADING BIPARTISAN EFFORT URGING DEPARTMENTS OF DEFENSE AND COMMERCE TO SECURE SILICON CARBIDE SUPPLY CHAIN FROM UNFAIR CHINESE COMPETITION, SCHUMER ANNOUNCES MASSIVE $1.5 BILLION FEDERAL...
text:
Schumer Says Transformative 30-Year DOD Loan Commitment Positions Wolfspeed As A Supplier Of Silicon Carbide Semiconductors Essential To U.S. National Security, Catalyzing Domestic Chip Production & Creating Good-Paying Jobs In The Mohawk Valley

As Longtime Champion Of Wolfspeed, Schumer Previously Delivered The CHIPS Investment Tax Credit From His Bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law To Expand Production & Workforce At Wolfspeed’s Fab In Marcy

Schumer: We’re Making The Mohawk Valley A Key Stop On Upstate NY’s Rapidly Growing Semiconductor Superhighway

After leading a bipartisan delegation of U.S. Senators urging the Secretaries of Defense and Commerce to support a whole-of-government response to preserve and strengthen domestic manufacturing of silicon carbide, Schumer today announced a massive $1.5 billion investment from the U.S. Department of Defense (“DoD”) for Wolfspeed to supercharge manufacturing of its silicon carbide semiconductors, which are critical for next-generation applications across aerospace, defense, and infrastructure.

Schumer, building on years of tireless advocacy in support of Wolfspeed, including delivering the federal CHIPS Investment Tax Credit as part of his bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law, said that this 30-year, $1.5 billion loan commitment through the DoD’s Office of Strategic Capital would enable Wolfspeed to expand production of their state-of-the-art semiconductors for use by the defense supply chain, creating good-paying jobs at its industry-leading fab in the Mohawk Valley and would also expand Upstate New York’s rapidly growing Semiconductor Superhighway.

“I’ve been advocating for years for the federal investment needed for Wolfspeed to scale domestic production of silicon carbide chips, which this $1.5 billion DoD investment would supercharge. I have been leading the bipartisan charge to strengthen the domestic manufacturing of silicon carbide because of how critical it is to our national security and to outcompeting China. Wolfspeed is powering American technological leadership, national security, and international competitiveness from their state-of-the-art semiconductor fab at the Marcy Nanocenter, and their silicon carbide chips would define the next generation of innovation,” said Senator Schumer. “After fighting for more than a decade to transform Upstate New York into a globally recognized semiconductor superhighway, this is yet another example that the work is paying off here in Oneida County. I will never stop fighting to create good-paying jobs, protect our national security, and deliver for communities across the Mohawk Valley.”

In a recent bipartisan letter led by Schumer, he and the other senators explained that silicon carbide is the foundational substrate for a critical class of next-generation semiconductors thanks to its unique combination of high voltage tolerance, thermal conductivity, and switching speed, which make it both indispensable across advanced defense systems, electric grid infrastructure, 5G telecommunications, and the modern automotive sector.

“We believe the scale and 30-year tenor of this conditional commitment reflects the long-term importance of the technology and manufacturing capabilities Wolfspeed has built in the United States,” said Robert Feurle, Chief Executive Officer of Wolfspeed. “This financing would strengthen our continued advancement of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, reinforcing our efforts to build a more resilient U.S. semiconductor and defense industrial base.”

On the heels of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the U.S. and Beijing launching its Made in China 2025 initiative, making silicon carbide a national industrial, military, and economic priority, Schumer emphasized that accelerating U.S. global leadership in the development and production of cutting-edge silicon carbide, gallium nitride, and other high bandgap semiconductors produced by companies like Wolfspeed as well as onsemi, with operations in both the Hudson Valley and Central New York, is critical to countering China’s efforts to dominate the global silicon carbide semiconductor industry and supply chain. Over the last five years, Chinese producers have increased their share of the global silicon carbide market from under 5 percent to nearly 50 percent.

Schumer added, “As I’ve been warning for years, we cannot let the CCP get its hands on our advanced chips and the manufacturing equipment needed to produce them. It's time to stand up to Xi for the sake of the American people and for global security. We must act now to bolster and secure the silicon carbide semiconductor industry before it's too late.”

Schumer has fought for decades to position the Mohawk Valley and Upstate NY to attract billions of dollars in new investment, create tens of thousands of good-paying jobs, and ascend as a national leader in advanced manufacturing and defense technologies. In addition to creating the conditions for companies like Wolfspeed to grow and thrive, Schumer is actively working with Oneida County and Mohawk Valley EDGE to help lure additional semiconductor, manufacturing supply chain, and defense technology companies to the Marcy Nanocenter, which the Senator has long called one of the premier, shovel-ready sites in the entire country, as well as the Griffiss Business & Technology Park.

“This $1.5 billion federal commitment further demonstrates that the groundwork laid by Oneida County continues to pay off and recognizes the critical role Wolfspeed plays in the semiconductor ecosystem. The advanced semiconductor technologies being developed by Wolfspeed have important applications for our national defense and complement the groundbreaking research and innovation taking place at the Air Force Research Laboratory in Rome. Having these capabilities in our community strengthens Oneida County’s position in the nation’s semiconductor and defense technology ecosystem, and this announcement reinforces the importance of continuing to grow that presence. I thank Senator Schumer for his bipartisan work to help make this commitment possible and for his continued efforts to support semiconductor manufacturing and national security in our region,” said Anthony J. Picente Jr., Oneida County Executive

“Today’s announcement is another significant vote of confidence in Wolfspeed, the Marcy Nanocenter, and the growing semiconductor ecosystem taking root in Upstate New York. We are grateful to Senator Chuck Schumer for his relentless advocacy on behalf of Wolfspeed and the broader semiconductor industry. His leadership has helped position New York and the Mohawk Valley as critical contributors to America’s advanced manufacturing, economic competitiveness, and national security. This conditional financing commitment further reinforces the importance of Wolfspeed’s operations in Marcy and the long-term opportunities that lie ahead for our region,” said Marc Barraco, Chief of Staff, Mohawk Valley EDGE.

Thanks to Schumer’s bipartisan CHIPS & Science Law, Upstate New York is undergoing a historic transformation into an internationally recognized epicenter of semiconductor manufacturing, innovation, and workforce development. The senator landed and delivered billions of dollars to realize Micron’s historic $100+ billion semiconductor megafab in Onondaga County – which broke ground earlier this year and is currently proceeding ahead of schedule – creating over 50,000 new good-paying jobs and thousands of construction jobs. The senator fought for and successfully delivered a designation and $40 million implementation award to launch the NY Smart I-Corridor Tech Hub, establishing Upstate NY as a national hub for workforce training, innovation, and manufacturing of semiconductor technologies. The senator also delivered a $32 million CHIPS funding agreement for Corning Incorporated to fuel its $315 million investment to increase the production of its specialized glass vital for semiconductor manufacturing in Northern NY, creating 300 good-paying manufacturing and construction jobs.

Schumer has also been a leading champion for national security innovation and economic development across the region. Schumer has fought tirelessly to deliver billions of dollars in annual appropriations and federal contracts to Rome’s Air Force Research Lab, and drive hundreds of millions of dollars of annual economic impact across the Mohawk Valley and more than 1,000 good-paying jobs at Rome Lab and across its burgeoning defense industrial base. Schumer delivered a $30 million federal Defense Production Act investment, driving TTM Technologies’ $130 million expansion to manufacture cutting-edge printed circuit boards critical and create up to 400 good-paying jobs in the Town of DeWitt. Schumer has also successfully secured more than $100 million in annual appropriations and federal contracts over the last decade for Saab to expand the footprint of its global headquarters in East Syracuse, adding hundreds of good-paying new jobs and tens of thousands of square feet of new production capacity.

A copy of the Schumer-led delegation letterto the Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Commerce is included below:

Dear Secretaries Hegseth and Lutnick:

We write to draw your attention to a critical matter at the intersection of national security, economic competitiveness and trade policy: the accelerating Chinese government effort to dominate the global silicon carbide semiconductor industry and supply chain, and the urgent need for a whole-of-government response to preserve and strengthen trusted domestic and allied manufacturing of silicon carbide.

Silicon carbide is the foundational substrate for a critical class of next-generation semiconductors that are indispensable across advanced defense systems, AI data centers, electric grid infrastructure, 5G telecommunications, and the modern automotive sector. Silicon carbide's unique combination of high-voltage tolerance, thermal conductivity, and switching speed makes it irreplaceable in high-performance air, land and sea propulsion systems, directed energy weapons, and air and missile defense systems.

Since launching its Made in China 2025 initiative, Beijing has recognized the military and economic importance of silicon carbide and made global domination in the sector a national industrial priority. In the last five years, Chinese producers have increased their share of the global silicon carbide wafer market from less than 5 percent to nearly 50 percent today.

Clearly, China intends to undermine another strategically important industry built on American technology and ingenuity. If this campaign succeeds, the United States will find itself dependent on adversary supply chains for materials essential to our most advanced defense systems and critical technological infrastructure. The domestic supply chain is already under significant pressure and we are at risk of losing industry leaders and globally competitive manufacturers to this coordinated campaign. The time to act is now, before we reach the crisis stage where remedies are impossible or far more expensive and time-consuming.

We encourage you to leverage Defense Production Act authorities, critical minerals designations, Buy America requirements, and any other authorities at your disposal to ensure the U.S. can protect its silicon carbide supply chain.

title: Senate passes three of Sen. Tim Scott’s bills to strengthen taxpayer protections
text:
WASHINGTON — Three bills introduced by U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) unanimously passed the Senate as part of the Taxpayer Assistance and Service (TAS) Act, legislation aimed at modernizing IRS technology, strengthening customer service standards, and protecting taxpayer rights in disputes. Sen. Scott’s provisions include the IRS Accountability and Taxpayer Protection Act, the Tax Court Parity Act, and the Tax Relief for Innocent Spouses Act.

“Hardworking Americans deserve a tax system that works for them, not against them. My three bills strengthen taxpayer protections and fix inconsistencies in our tax system so Americans are treated fairly,” said Sen. Scott. “By unanimously passing these commonsense reforms, the Senate is making it clear that the American people should not have to pay the price for flaws in our tax system. I’ll continue standing up for American taxpayers and fighting to help them keep more of their hard-earned money where it belongs – in their pockets, not the government’s.”

The IRS Accountability and Taxpayer Protection Act aims to protect taxpayers from improper or automated penalties by requiring IRS employees to get approval from a supervisor before approving or denying penalties.

The Tax Court Parity Act would protect taxpayers’ rights by granting the Tax Court the authority to review and correct decisions in prior cases in limited circumstances of clerical errors, newly discovered evidence, fraud or misconduct concerns, or defective judgments.

Lastly, the Tax Relief for Innocent Spouses Act would provide innocent spouses relief from tax debts caused by their spouse’s hidden incomes or mistakes by allowing the Tax Court to review the full scope of evidence in appeal cases. This protection is essential for spouses facing domestic abuse or who lack access to financial information.

Full text of the legislation can be found here.

title: Van Hollen Calls On Risch, Foreign Relations Committee to Hold Hearing Into Embassy Officials’ Reported Obstruction from Congress of Information Around Deaths of American Citizens in West Bank
text:
Following reporting from the New York Times yesterday that a U.S. Embassy official, David Milstein, and Ambassador Mike Huckabee have obstructed congressional inquiries into the killings of American citizens in the West Bank, U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, is calling on the Committee’s Chairman, Senator Jim Risch (R-Idaho) to hold hearings on this matter. According to the New York Times reporting, embassy official David Milstein, a political appointee, altered the contents of a report requested by Senator Van Hollen and 30 of his Senate colleagues into the deaths of American citizens in the West Bank. Given this reporting, Senator Van Hollen is calling for a hearing into the withholding of this information as well as the release of the original report intended for Congress.

“I write to respectfully request that the Senate Foreign Relations Committee hold a hearing on concerning reports regarding how Ambassador Mike Huckabee and his advisor, David Milstein, have obstructed congressional inquiries into the lack of accountability for the killing of American citizens and ongoing violence in the West Bank. The American people deserve answers about what’s happening in the West Bank, especially when it comes to the deaths of American citizens. It is unacceptable that Amb. Huckabee and his staff continue to cover up and block access to essential information about these killings. Congress must seek answers. Regardless of political party, we should not accept the withholding of information from Congress and the precedent this sets in undermining our constitutional responsibility,” the Senator begins.

“The job of a U.S. ambassador, and their staff, whether a political or civilian employee, is to defend and protect U.S. interests. As these reports lay bare, both Ambassador Huckabee and David Milstein have failed to do so. They have undermined the essential functions of the U.S. embassy in Israel, which includes protecting and assisting American citizens, as well as reporting unvarnished facts on the ground back to Washington. Instead, Amb. Huckabee and David Milstein have become apologists for the most extreme Israeli government in history, even when the Israeli government actions undermined the Trump Administration’s own stated priorities,” he continued.

“In March of this year, 30 of my colleagues joined me in sending a letter to Secretary Rubio and Ambassador Huckabee concerning the death of Nasrallah Abu Siyam, a 19-year-old Palestinian shot and killed in the West Bank by violent Israeli settlers during an attack on Palestinian farmers. In the letter, we asked the Ambassador to hold the government of Israel accountable for the killings of nine Americans citizens over the last four years, as well as to provide ‘an update on the status of investigations into the killings of all the other Americans killed in the West Bank since January 2022.’ […] We never received that update,” Senator Van Hollen noted.

“We now know the real reason why we never received that update. According to a report from the New York Times, when Embassy staff received our letter, they drafted a report that detailed the status of each investigation into the Americans killed in the West Bank. The report said that no one had been held accountable for any of these killings. Milstein stonewalled the report and instead insisted ‘that the embassy should send a letter saying that Israel was properly handling the investigations.’ This is an unacceptable example of an unelected staffer obstructing Congress from obtaining critical information on the killing of American citizens and violence in the West Bank,” the Senator stressed.

“In the Department’s response to our March 2026 letter, they insisted that that ‘The Department’s highest priority is the safety and security of American citizens abroad.’ We must hold them to this standard and hold a hearing to determine what the Department knows, as well as request the original report written by embassy staff on the status about these killings,” the Senator closed.

The text of the Senator’s letter is available here and below.

Dear Senator Risch,

I write to respectfully request that the Senate Foreign Relations Committee hold a hearing on concerning reports regarding how Ambassador Mike Huckabee and his advisor, David Milstein, have obstructed congressional inquiries into the lack of accountability for the killing of American citizens and ongoing violence in the West Bank. The American people deserve answers about what’s happening in the West Bank, especially when it comes to the deaths of American citizens. It is unacceptable that Amb. Huckabee and his staff continue to cover up and block access to essential information about these killings. Congress must seek answers.

The job of a U.S. ambassador, and their staff, whether a political or civilian employee, is to defend and protect U.S. interests. As these reports lay bare, both Ambassador Huckabee and David Milstein have failed to do so. They have undermined the essential functions of the U.S. embassy in Israel, which includes protecting and assisting American citizens, as well as reporting unvarnished facts on the ground back to Washington. Instead, Amb. Huckabee and David Milstein have become apologists for the most extreme Israeli government in history, even when the Israeli government actions undermined the Trump Administration’s own stated priorities.

In March of this year, 30 of my colleagues joined me in sending a letter to Secretary Rubio and Ambassador Huckabee concerning the death of Nasrallah Abu Siyam, a 19-year-old Palestinian shot and killed in the West Bank by violent Israeli settlers during an attack on Palestinian farmers. In the letter, we asked the Ambassador to hold the government of Israel accountable for the killings of nine Americans citizens over the last four years, as well as to provide “an update on the status of investigations into the killings of all the other Americans killed in the West Bank since January 2022.” We never received that update. Instead, in their response to us, we were told that the Embassy “has been working closely with our Israeli counterparts to ensure accountability for these deaths” but that further coordination of these issues with Israel have run into “logistical and operational challenges” due to the war with Iran.

We now know the real reason why we never received that update. According to a report from the New York Times, when Embassy staff received our letter, they drafted a report that detailed the status of each investigation into the Americans killed in the West Bank. The report said that no one had been held accountable for any of these killings. Milstein stonewalled the report and instead insisted “that the embassy should send a letter saying that Israel was properly handling the investigations.” This is an unacceptable example of an unelected staffer obstructing Congress from obtaining critical information on the killing of American citizens and violence in the West Bank. I ask you join me in requesting the Department provide Congress with that original draft report so we can get the answers we requested.

This reporting, as well as previous reports, go on to show that Milstein sought to downplay cables that described the horrific mass killings of Palestinians seeking aid at the now defunct Gaza Humanitarian Foundation disruption sites, where thousands of Palestinians were killed seeking food. Milstein also used his position to portray recent Israeli government actions which gave them more control over the West bank and made it easier for Israelis to buy West Bank land, at odds with President Trump’s opposition to West Bank annexation, as a “domestic matter,” and has rewritten or delayed multiple cables to paint the actions of the government of Israel in a more favorable light. This includes reversing cables on settler violence from mentioning Israel’s failure to curb settler violence to praising them for taking action. Previous reporting also found that Milstein’s control over Embassy procedures has created a chilling effect throughout the Embassy, undermining core functions of the Department’s work. Milstein was also implicated in the firing of a State Department communications officer working on Israeli-Palestinian affairs for recommending mentions in State Department materials of opposing forced displacement of Palestinian civilians and sympathy for journalists killed in Gaza.

In the Department’s response to our March 2026 letter, they insisted that that “The Department’s highest priority is the safety and security of American citizens abroad.” We must hold them to this standard and hold a hearing to determine what the Department knows, as well as request the original report written by embassy staff on the status about these killings.

title: Van Hollen, Elfreth Lead Lawmakers in Urging Fisheries Commission to Protect Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coast, Support Menhaden Conservation Measures
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) and U.S. Representative Sarah Elfreth (D-Md.), along with nine of their colleagues, pressed the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (Commission) Atlantic Menhaden Management Board Chair Joe Cimino to prioritize an ecosystem-based management approach that supports a sustainable menhaden population, urging the Commission to move forward with the strongest menhaden protections proposed. The lawmakers stressed the importance of menhaden as a critical forage species that other wildlife species depend on and emphasized that management for long-term sustainability is key to supporting good-paying jobs in all menhaden-dependent fisheries.

Senator Van Hollen and Representative Elfreth were joined in sending this letter by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), and Representatives April McClain Delaney (D-Md.), Frank Pallone (D-N.J.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), and Bobby Scott (D-Va.).

The lawmakers begin, “The Chesapeake Bay is an especially important habitat for Atlantic menhaden because, as the nation’s largest estuary, it provides a major nursery area for menhaden and many other important species managed by the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (Commission). Conservation-minded management principles are critical for the Chesapeake Bay menhaden; menhaden management not only impacts countless communities and businesses reliant on an abundant menhaden population, but also the health of other wildlife populations up and down the Atlantic coast that depend on this fish species for survival. During its consideration of updated management strategies for Atlantic menhaden in the Chesapeake Bay and coastwide, the Commission must prioritize an ecosystem-based management approach that supports long-term menhaden abundance and sustainable commercial and recreational fisheries. We urge the Commission to move forward with the strongest menhaden protections proposed in the Commission’s Draft Addendum II, as well as with precautionary management measures for the Atlantic coastwide quota.”

“Menhaden are called ‘the most important fish in the sea’ for good reason. As a forage species, menhaden perform the critical task of consuming plankton and turning it into energy-rich animal protein that nourishes other wildlife. From iconic Chesapeake Bay fish species like striped bass (rockfish) – which are one of the most popular recreational fish species along the Atlantic, accounting for $7.7 billion in GDP annually – to birds of prey such as osprey and eagles, sea turtles, and even marine mammals like whales and dolphins, a wide variety of animals depend on menhaden as a food source. As a result, decreases in menhaden population have serious implications for other species; for example, there is strong evidence linking declining menhaden populations to recent declines in osprey reproduction in the Chesapeake Bay. Given the importance of menhaden to the health of the Chesapeake Bay and the entire marine food web, the Commission must carefully consider the ecosystem-level impacts of Atlantic menhaden harvest in their management decisions and promote risk-averse strategies that prioritize the ecological benefits menhaden provide,” they continue.

On the health of the ecosystems along the Atlantic coast, the lawmakers note, “It is our view that Atlantic menhaden are a public resource that benefit Atlantic coast communities in many ways, and so managing this species for long-term sustainability is key. A robust menhaden population is necessary to sustain all menhaden-dependent jobs, including those that rely on menhaden for bait, such as in the culturally significant Chesapeake Bay blue crab fishery and other commercial and recreational fisheries up and down the Atlantic coast. Left in the water, menhaden also support a highly productive ecosystem and provide a key food source for other commercially and recreationally valuable fish species – such as striped bass, bluefish, weakfish, and bluefin tuna – so it is important that the Commission take into account how menhaden management measures will impact both the health of menhaden and non-menhaden fish populations.”

“We urge the Commission to implement strong protections for Atlantic menhaden in order to support a sustainable, abundant menhaden population that can benefit all the fisheries and communities that depend on it,” the lawmakers conclude.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Chair Cimino,

The Chesapeake Bay is an especially important habitat for Atlantic menhaden because, as the nation’s largest estuary, it provides a major nursery area for menhaden and many other important species managed by the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (Commission). Conservation-minded management principles are critical for the Chesapeake Bay menhaden; menhaden management not only impacts countless communities and businesses reliant on an abundant menhaden population, but also the health of other wildlife populations up and down the Atlantic coast that depend on this fish species for survival. During its consideration of updated management strategies for Atlantic menhaden in the Chesapeake Bay and coastwide, the Commission must prioritize an ecosystem-based management approach that supports long-term menhaden abundance and sustainable commercial and recreational fisheries. We urge the Commission to move forward with the strongest menhaden protections proposed in the Commission’s Draft Addendum II, as well as with precautionary management measures for the Atlantic coastwide quota.

Menhaden are called “the most important fish in the sea” for good reason. As a forage species, menhaden perform the critical task of consuming plankton and turning it into energy-rich animal protein that nourishes other wildlife. From iconic Chesapeake Bay fish species like striped bass (rockfish) – which are one of the most popular recreational fish species along the Atlantic, accounting for $7.7 billion in GDP annually – to birds of prey such as osprey and eagles, sea turtles, and even marine mammals like whales and dolphins, a wide variety of animals depend on menhaden as a food source. As a result, decreases in menhaden population have serious implications for other species; for example, there is strong evidence linking declining menhaden populations to recent declines in osprey reproduction in the Chesapeake Bay. Given the importance of menhaden to the health of the Chesapeake Bay and the entire marine food web, the Commission must carefully consider the ecosystem-level impacts of Atlantic menhaden harvest in their management decisions and promote risk-averse strategies that prioritize the ecological benefits menhaden provide.

It is our view that Atlantic menhaden are a public resource that benefit Atlantic coast communities in many ways, and so managing this species for long-term sustainability is key. A robust menhaden population is necessary to sustain all menhaden-dependent jobs, including those that rely on menhaden for bait, such as in the culturally significant Chesapeake Bay blue crab fishery and other commercial and recreational fisheries up and down the Atlantic coast. Left in the water, menhaden also support a highly productive ecosystem and provide a key food source for other commercially and recreationally valuable fish species – such as striped bass, bluefish, weakfish, and bluefin tuna – so it is important that the Commission take into account how menhaden management measures will impact both the health of menhaden and non-menhaden fish populations.

We support the Commission’s continued use of ecological reference points – such as striped bass – to guide Atlantic menhaden management decisions, and we encourage the Commission to adhere to the principles of ecosystem-based fishery management. By accounting for Atlantic menhaden’s role as prey for Atlantic coast species that depend on it for survival, the Commission can help to ensure a balanced approach to Atlantic menhaden management.

Ultimately, science-based decision-making is critical, which is why we fought to secure funding for Chesapeake Bay Atlantic Menhaden abundance research in the FY26 appropriations bill. We look forward to seeing the results of this study, which will provide critical information to inform future management decisions.

In the meantime, worrisome signs in the Chesapeake Bay – from dwindling osprey populations to reduced bait fishery landings – indicate that Atlantic Menhaden populations may be declining in the Bay, underscoring the importance of strategic, risk-averse management decisions today. Until better menhaden abundance data is available to inform management decisions, the Commission must put in place additional precautionary management measures, using the ecological reference point target as a goal, to ease pressure on vulnerable species that depend on menhaden.

We urge the Commission to implement strong protections for Atlantic menhaden in order to support a sustainable, abundant menhaden population that can benefit all the fisheries and communities that depend on it.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and your efforts to sustainably manage Atlantic Menhaden in a manner that supports both the environment and local communities.

title: Van Hollen Joins McClain Delaney, Colleagues in Call to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
text:
U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) joined Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (D-Md.), along with Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), Don Beyer (D-Va.), Kweisi Mfume (D-Md.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), and Sarah Elfreth (D-Md.), in urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.

The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.

At a time when AI safety concerns are sky-high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.

The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.

The lawmakers request answers in three areas:

Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.

Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.

Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.

The letter calls for a pause until lawmakers can better understand the FAA’s decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. The co-leads emphasize that modernizing air traffic control must prioritize safety, transparency, and the expertise of the people responsible for keeping our skies safe.

The full text of the letter is availble here and below.

Dear Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford:

We write to express our concerns regarding the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) rollout of the AI-enabled Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool to help manage air traffic above the National Capital Region (NCR) at the Ronald Reagan Washington National (DCA), Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall (BWI), and Washington Dulles International (IAD) airports. The NCR is one of the busiest airspaces in the country and is still reeling from the impacts of the tragic midair collision of a passenger flight and military helicopter over DCA, in which 67 people died. We are incredibly concerned by the use of the NCR region to pilot AI tools in safety-critical aviation systems, especially as we have not seen any safety evaluation and testing reports, nor have we been made aware of any efforts to train aviation safety personnel on how best to use the tool. Given extensive recent reporting on AI cybersecurity incidents and other unpredictable behavior from AI systems, we are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death.

We understand that the SMART tool was built through a 12-year, $875 million contract. Yet here has been little transparency from either the Department of Transportation (DOT) or the FAA on how the AI systems underlying the SMART tool were tested, how it is being integrated into air traffic control (ATC) systems, and how the tool’s recommendations may impact already overburdened airspace and air traffic controllers. Nor has information been shared with local officials as to why the NCR, the region in which the deadliest U.S. air disaster in nearly 25 years occurred just last year, was chosen as the pilot test region. This, and other recent tragic aviation accidents such as the fatal March runway crash at LaGuardia Airport in New York, have highlighted the need for more investment in safer skies. need to modernize ATC systems - Congress appropriated $12.5 billion last year to do just that. However, any upgrades and changes to ATC systems must be made with safety as the first priority. We recognize the urgent need to modernize ATC systems - Congress appropriated $12.5 billion last year to do just that. However, any upgrades and changes to ATC systems must be made with safety as the first priority.

However, we have heard from several sources that frontline aviation safety workers were notified of the SMART tool rollout mere days in advance or not at all, giving them no time to learn how the system works, how it is incorporated into their workflow, and what oversight and accountability mechanisms maintain aviation safety standards. There is already a shortage of air traffic controllers, and we are concerned that integrating this new technology into the workflows of already-overworked aviation safety personnel could have deleterious consequences. The air traffic control systems and processes currently in place are complex and we don’t know what impact AI-enabled tools might have on these systems and resulting safety. Decades of research shows that people tend to over-rely on automated recommendations, a phenomenon known as automation bias, particularly under overworked conditions. Adding new, untested layers to these systems, especially those that are not yet “ready to immediately transform flight operations”, according to airline industry officials, must be done in partnership with all stakeholders in the aviation safety ecosystem.

We understand that the rollout of the SMART AI tool in the NCR on Monday, September 21, is part one of a phased rollout that begins with a 90-day evaluation period before broader, nationwide deployment. However, given the egregious lack of transparency around the initial rollout, especially at a time where there is so much public concern around the use of AI in critical systems, we ask that you pause any use of the SMART tool until we can better understand your decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. We ask that you respond to the following questions no later than October 19, 2026:

Pre-Deployment Testing & Evaluations

1. Did the FAA make a formal In-Service Decision before SMART began operational use?

a. If so, which official and office made it, on what date, and on what basis?

b. Was the decision made within the FAA's Air Traffic Organization, or did Department of Transportation leadership direct or approve the launch date?

2. Was a Safety Risk Management evaluation conducted under the Air Traffic Organization's Safety Management System, and was a Safety Risk Management Document completed and signed? If so, please provide it.

3. Were any standard acquisition or safety review steps waived or truncated to meet the September 21 launch?

4. What AI models does SMART use and how has the FAA validated their accuracy? Please provide detailed information regarding what pre-deployment testing and evaluations were conducted on the AI models underlying SMART, as well as measures of SMART tool

5. What factors did you consider in your decision to pilot this system in the National Capital Region rather than other regions? How was the final determination made and who made the determination?

6. OMB Memorandum M-25-21 categorizes AI used in “traffic control systems and other systems controlling physical transit” as high-impact, requiring pre-deployment testing, an AI impact assessment with independent review, and sufficient operator training. Has the Department determined SMART to be high-impact AI? If so, please provide documentation of the practices completed under Section 4(b). If the Department has determined it is not high-impact, or waived any practice, please provide the written determination required under Section 4(a).

Stakeholder Consultation & Training

7. What consultations did you conduct before deploying the SMART tool? What input did you solicit, and what feedback did you receive? Specifically include, at minimum, information regarding consultations with:

a. the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority

b. the Maryland Aviation Administration,

c. the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, and

d. airline industry officials.

8. What training did aviation safety personnel receive prior to deployment of the SMART tool?

9. How will the tool be integrated into existing ATC systems and processes?

10. What weight are controllers and traffic management specialists expected to give SMART recommendations when making decisions as compared to other factors? Do they have the ability to manually override SMART recommendations, including after local facility leadership has accepted them? If so, what is the process, and how are those overrides documented?

11. How are recommendations, and whether they were accepted or overridden, tracked and evaluated? Are they recorded in the National Traffic Management Log or a similar system?

12. Did the FAA satisfy any applicable collective bargaining or labor consultation obligations before deploying SMART? Please describe what notice was provided to the exclusive representatives of affected employees and when.

Assessments & Oversight

13. What data will be tracked in the 90-day evaluation?

14. What specific metrics will determine whether the 90-day evaluation is a success? How will progress toward that goal be measured, and who will conduct the evaluation?

15. What is the timeline for further implementation of this system and what benchmarks will determine if the deployment process should continue?

16. What is your plan for ensuring public transparency and trust-building with the flying public and aviation industry as you deploy the SMART tool?

17. Who will provide oversight of the system?

18. What system do you have in place to enable independent oversight of the SMART tool, and who is responsible for conducting oversight (including but not limited to review by the National Transportation Safety Board following an incident)? Please provide details regarding your audit process of overseeing how the SMART tool reaches its recommendations, what actions are taken or not taken in response to these recommendations, and any safety implications of those decisions.

a. In the event that a SMART recommendation contributes to a loss of separation or other safety incident, who bears responsibility - the controller who accepted the recommendation, the FAA, or the developer? Has the FAA made any determination on this question?

Sincerely,

title: Warner Condemns Trump’s Push for Public Execution
text:
WASHINGTON— U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement in response to President Donald Trump’s push to publicly execute the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting:

“The Fort Hood shooting was a horrific act of violence that took 13 innocent lives and devastated military families. The perpetrator was convicted and sentenced to death, and nothing changes the gravity of his crimes. But there is a fundamental difference between carrying out a lawful sentence and turning an execution into a public spectacle.

“Public executions are the hallmark of authoritarian regimes like Iran and North Korea, not the United States of America. There is a reason that almost no countries in the world engage in this barbaric practice. Beyond the profound moral concerns, a public execution could hand terrorist organizations a propaganda victory, fuel radicalization, and put American service members, diplomats, and citizens overseas at greater risk. Justice for the victims does not require creating unnecessary threats to our national security.

“Unfortunately, this is part of a much broader pattern. From proposing public executions to threatening to interfere in our elections, President Trump continues to challenge the principles and practices that distinguish America from authoritarian regimes. With the election just weeks away, I am particularly concerned about his willingness to abuse the powers of the federal government to interfere with how Americans cast their ballots and how those votes are counted. Free and fair elections are the foundation of our democracy, and we cannot allow the United States to go down the path of countries where those in power decide whether and how elections take place.”

###

title: Warner, Kaine Statement on the Army’s Report Into DCA Midair Collision
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) released the following statement on the Army’s report into the January 2025 midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) that killed all 67 people aboard both aircraft:

“The Army’s report underscores the need for comprehensive aviation safety legislation that modernizes our air traffic control systems, improves aircraft visibility and collision-avoidance technology, and strengthens coordination between military and civilian aviation authorities. The Army’s report reveals troubling gaps in coordination between military flights and the FAA in the most congested airspace in the country – airspace Congress jammed even more flights into over our repeated objections. It also identified inadequate equipment used by the helicopter to communicate with the DCA tower and transmit its position to surrounding aircraft.

“It is clear – following the release of this report and an earlier report released by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) – that systemic and organizational failures, compounded by limitations in aircraft equipment and safety technology, were significant contributors to the tragic accident near DCA that claimed 67 lives. We owe it to the families who lost loved ones that night, and to all Americans who fly in our airspace, to take action to prevent another tragedy, including improved technology requirements and reduced traffic at DCA.”

Sens. Warner and Kaine have been closely involved in the response to and investigation of the January 29 collision near DCA. In the immediate aftermath of the tragedy, the senators met with first responders, offered condolences to the victims’ families and loved ones, and secured passage of a resolution honoring those who lost their lives. In February, the senators responded to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) final report on the crash and have continued pushing for reforms to prevent another tragedy. The senators supported the Rotorcraft Operations Transparency and Reform (ROTOR) Act, legislation to strengthen aviation safety at DCA and similarly sized airports and improve coordination between the FAA and Department of Defense. In September, the senators introduced the DCA Air Safety Act to address longstanding safety concerns by capping hourly arrivals, reducing the clustering of flights, and removing 30 slots at DCA. Even before the January 2025 collision, the senators consistently sounded the alarm about hazardous overcrowding in DCA’s airspace and called on Congress to reduce the number of slots at DCA.

title: Welch, Blumenthal, Min, Scanlon Initiate Probe into Influence of Cabinet Members in Trump's Pardon of Convicted Felons
text:
Lawmakers demand answers from HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin about their roles in Trump’s decision to grant presidential pardons

WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on The Constitution, alongside U.S. Representative Dave Min (D-CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Anti-Corruption Task Force, were joined by U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Representative Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-05), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Constitution and Limited Government, in raising questions about the role of cabinet members in securing presidential pardons, as part of their ongoing investigation into executive clemency actions since January 20, 2025.

The bicameral group of lawmakers are looking into whether U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin used their access to inappropriately influence President Trump’s decision to grant full presidential pardons to convicted felons Trevor Milton and Troy Lake.

“Public reports of high-profile individuals—including yourself—appealing directly to the President on behalf of pardon recipients risk subversion of the established pardon review processes by financial influence and political access,” write the lawmakers. “Article II, Section 2, Clause 1 of the U.S. Constitution authorizes the President to ‘grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offenses against the United States, except in Cases of Impeachment.’ The U.S. Supreme Court has characterized executive clemency as ‘an act of grace’ exercised for the ‘public welfare.’ President Trump’s use of this authority appears to deviate from this traditional purpose.”

The lawmakers conclude: “Congress has a compelling interest in ensuring that the constitutional pardon power is exercised with fairness and transparency. Given these circumstances, we are seeking additional information to better understand the extent to which influence and access have overridden the standard pardon review process.”

In their letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the lawmakers request answers about Secretary Kennedy’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to pardon convicted fraudster Trevor Milton, who defrauded and misled investors regarding technology and products related to his company, Nikola Corporation. The victims of Mr. Milton’s fraud include individuals who lost their retirement savings and others who had never invested in the stock market before. President Trump’s pardon eliminated Milton’s obligation to potentially pay $660 million in court-ordered restitution to his victims. Milton did not serve any of his four-year prison sentence.

“According to public reporting, you personally appealed to the President to grant Mr. Milton a pardon, arguing that he had been unfairly prosecuted by the previous administration’s Justice Department. Days before granting Mr. Milton’s pardon request, President Trump reportedly told him to call you and thank you for convincing the President to grant him a pardon,” write the lawmakers. “Your reported involvement in this matter is particularly troubling, given that Mr. Milton reportedly donated $750,000 to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) Political Action Committee (PAC), which was launched in late 2024 by senior members of your presidential campaign to unite your supporters behind President Trump. Public reporting also indicates that Mr. Milton and his wife donated approximately $1,800,000 to President Trump’s 2024 reelection campaign a month before the election.”

In their letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin, the lawmakers demand answers about the administrator’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to grant a full presidential pardon to Troy Lake, and a subsequent corporate pardon to Lake’s company, Elite Diesel Service Inc. Lake’s conviction arose from allegations that he and his company disabled the monitoring components of emissions control systems on hundreds of heavy-duty commercial trucks.

The lawmakers write: “According to public reporting, two friends of Mr. Lake petitioned you in an August 2025 email, urging you to reach out to the President to request a pardon. Mr. Lake’s wife publicly attributed progress on her husband’s pardon efforts to your subsequent intervention. Such progress included a phone call with Sean Hayes, a White House attorney who works closely on pardons.”

The lawmakers’ letters seek information from HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin regarding:

The nature of their relationships with the pardoned felons;

The process by which clemency requests were initiated and considered;

Whether intermediaries, lobbyists, or advocates were involved;

Any contacts with Trump Administration officials or associates;

Their role in any other clemency decisions made by the Trump Administration;

Whether financial contributions or payments were made in connection with clemency efforts; and

The extent of third-party advocacy supporting the requests.

Read and download the lawmakers’ full letters to HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin.

In May, Senator Welch and Rep. Min sent letters to 17 individuals who received pardons or commutations under circumstances that warrant further congressional scrutiny, including several individuals connected to major fraud schemes, financial crimes, and high-profile political or financial relationships tied to President Trump and his associates. The earlier letters sought information regarding the clemency process, including whether financial contributions, lobbyists, intermediaries, or personal connections played a role in securing presidential clemency.

Among the individuals who received letters are convicted fraudsters, political fundraisers, corporate executives, and wealthy donors, such as Changpeng Zhao, whose cases have generated public reporting suggesting unusual access to Trump’s network of political allies and associates, direct lobbying efforts, large political donations, or other concerning connections surrounding their clemency requests.

The lawmakers continued their investigation in June, sending four additional letters to the Department of Justice’s Office of the Pardon Attorney, the White House Office of Records Management, the White House Pardon Czar, and the United States Secret Service.

title: Welch, Blumenthal, Schiff Continue Probe into DHS Misuse of Taxpayer Dollars, Demand Answers from DHS Over New Reporting on Noem’s Luxury Jet Purchases
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on the Constitution, alongside U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.),Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, escalated their effort to obtainrecords and information from Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin about the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) squandering of taxpayer funds and repeated steering of no-bid contracts to political allies under former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. In their letter to Secretary Mullin, the Senators urged DHS to ensure accountability for corrupt contracting decisions and ensure open competition among future prospective contractors.

The Senators pointed to allegations recently reported in The New York Times that in the final hours of former Secretary Kristi Noem’s tenure, DHS: “delivered a windfall to one of her political donors by buying five airplanes from the man’s firm at a substantial markup.”

The Senators wrote: “On the last day of Secretary Noem’s tenure, DHS purchased one Boeing 737 jet from Daedalus for $108 million, despite that aircraft previously appearing on the market with an asking price below $90 million. The interior of that aircraft included ‘a stand-up bar, two bedrooms, marble showers and a table covered in manta ray skin.’ Another two 737 aircraft were purchased by DHS from Daedalus for $45 million each, prices that experts estimated ‘were millions of dollars higher than the typical market value for jets of that age.’”

“The staggering sums expended on these aircraft and the eleventh-hour approval of the no-bid contract used to purchase them from a company led by a political donor to Secretary Noem appears to illustrate a brazen giveaway by Secretary Noem to her political ally, William Walters,” the Senators continued. “The fact that a separate company led by Mr. Walters, Salus Worldwide Solutions, has received separate no-bid contracts under Secretary Noem’s leadership only amplifies the appearance of impropriety and potential violations of federal law.”

The Senators concluded: “Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential corruption involved in the Department’s aircraft purchases and widespread no-bid contracting.”

In August, Senators Welch, Blumenthal, and Schiff called out DHS’ reliance on no-bid contracts since the beginning of the second Trump Administration and raised concerns that the owner of the company that received the award also runs a company alleged to have solicited kickback payments from former DHS official Corey Lewandowski.

title: Welch Joins Groundbreaking for New Affordable Housing Project in Burlington
text:
BURLINGTON, VT — Today, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit, joined the Champlain Housing Trust to celebrate the groundbreaking of 30 new permanently affordable condominium homes for sale to low-income households in Burlington’s Cambrian Rise neighborhood. A majority of the 30 new condos developed will be sold to homebuyers earning at or below 80% of the average median income (AMI) to eliminate obstacles to homeownership for lower-income Vermonters.

“Vermont’s housing affordability crisis has wreaked havoc across our state, and skyrocketing housing prices are right at the center of it. Home prices have more than doubled in the last ten years, making it tougher than ever for families to achieve the American dream of homeownership,” said Senator Welch. “The Champlain Housing Trust’s newest project is a great example of how we can leverage federal investments to increase access to affordable housing. I’ll continue to fight for policies that help bring down housing costs and make homeownership a reality for more working families in Vermont.”

“This development brings jobs to the community and builds Burlington’s tax base. So not only are these condos affordable to the people who will buy them next year, they are making Burlington more affordable overall,” said Michael Monte, CEO, Champlain Housing Trust. “And the lasting impact of retaining affordability through our shared equity homeownership program will have a ripple effect for future generations of City residents.”

The project is made possible through the deployment of $20 million in New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC), a federal program that utilizes tax credits to incentivize private investments in community development and economic growth in distressed communities. Senator Welch cosponsored the New Markets Tax Credit Extension Act, which permanently extended the NMTC Program last year.

View photos from the event below:

Senator Welch has led bipartisan efforts to address Vermont’s affordable housing crisis. Last month, the Senator introduced the Supporting Small Affordable Housing Developers Act, new legislation that would exempt grants supporting affordable housing development from taxation to empower small, rural housing developers to build more affordable housing. Senator Welch also cosponsored the Build American Efficiency Act, bipartisan, bicameral legislation to help homebuilders cut costs and red tape as they work to address the national housing shortage.

In March, Senator Welch introduced the bipartisan FARM Home Loans Act to spur rural economic growth by helping more homebuyers qualify for rural housing assistance. The Senator is also a cosponsor of the First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act, legislation that aims to support middle-class Americans purchasing their first home, and the End Rent Fixing Act, which would crack down on companies that help landlords increase rents in already high-priced markets. The Senator is also a cosponsor of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which was signed into law earlier this year.

The Senator’s bipartisan, bicameral HOPE for HOMES Act, which helps lower energy costs for homeowners and reduce greenhouse gas emissions while also investing in the workforce, was included as part of the Biden-Harris Administration’s historic Inflation Reduction Act.

title: Whitehouse Warns of Global Climate Risk and Calls for Action at OSCE Parliamentary Assembly
text:
Whitehouse calls out climate damage, insurance collapse, and corrupt fossil fuel influence

Industry, front groups, Russia and far-right comprise Axis of Climate Evil

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), the Senate Ranking Member of the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe (the “Helsinki Commission”), warned of the massive global risk posed by climate change and called for collective action at the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Parliamentary Assembly’s 24th Autumn Meeting.

As part of a bipartisan delegation, Whitehouse co-led a session of the OSCE Parliament entitled, “Strengthening Energy Sovereignty within the OSCE Area: Security, Efficiency, Sustainability.” In his speech to the OSCE Parliament, the Senator warned of massive climate-driven disruption to Earth’s natural systems collapsing insurance, mortgage and real estate markets, and called on governments to combat the new “Axis of Climate Evil” protecting the industry’s wrongful “free-to-pollute” business model. An excerpt of his remarks is below:

“For our own safety, we need to get more serious about the politics of climate change if we’re going to head this off. The fossil fuel industry fights fiercely to pollute for free. Its pollute-for-free business model is not only morally and economically a sin and a subsidy, it is now lethal to our climate safety as humankind.

“But they won’t give it up. They depend on polluting for free. So a battle looms.

“In a battle, my friends, you need to know your adversary.

“Everywhere, fossil fuel operates through front groups. In most places, fossil fuel funds the far right, as paid allies. Vladimir Putin’s covert schemes in Europe both disrupt democracy and prop up fossil fuel, his primary revenue. In the United States, the political right, fueled by dark money, still denies climate science. That is the enemy arrayed against you: fossil fuel, and all its front groups and dark money; Vladimir Putin, and all of Russia’s anti-democracy mischief; and far-right political groups that deny climate change.”

The meeting took place in Andorra la Vella, Andorra. Whitehouse and U.S. Senator Roger Wicker (R-MS), Senate Chair of the Helsinki Commission, participated in committee meetings of the OSCE Parliament alongside Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) and Representative Marc Veasey (D-TX). Whitehouse attended bilateral meetings with the Ukrainian and Canadian delegations. Whitehouse also participated in events on authoritarian information manipulation, Russia’s coercive recruitment of foreign nationals into its armed forces, and Hungary’s democratic renewal.

In February, Whitehouse and Wicker participated in the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly Winter Meeting, where they pushed the U.S. and our European allies to cooperate to shut down Russia’s shadow fleet that fuels the Russian oil and gas economy. In July, Whitehouse and Wicker again led a delegation to the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly’s Annual Meeting, during which the OSCE Assembly overwhelmingly adopted two Whitehouse amendments to crack down on the Russian shadow fleet and spotlight the systemic and illegal Russian resettlement operation in occupied Ukraine.

Whitehouse’s as-delivered speech to the OSCE Parliament this week is below. Video is available here.

Good morning.

I am going to start with one word: zettajoule. What is that? A joule is the unit of heat energy; zetta means it has 21 zeroes — not a billion joules, or a trillion joules, but a billion trillion joules. A billion trillions. A massive amount of heat.

All the energy generated in a year, by all of humankind, across all of Planet Earth, is only half a zettajoule. The price we pay for the fossil fuel component of that half-zettajoule, is that 14 zettajoules of excess heat go into our oceans every year. Multiple Hiroshima bombs per second worth of heat.

This is part of the uncounted price of fossil fuel energy. Those of you who have coasts, know what fossil fuel is doing to our oceans: the rising seas, the displaced fisheries, the dying coral reefs, the worsening storms.

Every energy question is subordinate to the question whether we will protect Earth’s natural systems from unbounded fossil fuel pollution.

The damage humanity sustains from fossil fuels in climate-driven floods and wildfires has a leading indicator, in the insurance sector. Markets predict. Across my country, and probably yours, climate risks are making whole areas uninsurable. In my country, and perhaps yours, that means properties become unmortgageable. For most homeowners, that means a significant loss in property value.

This is a warning, but it’s not my warning. There are many very clear financial warnings. They warn of a cascade. Climate risk crashes insurance markets, insurance collapse crashes mortgage markets, mortgage collapse crashes property values, and general economic collapse follows — like the global crash of 2008, but likely without the rebound.

These warnings aren’t from green groups, liberal groups, progressive groups — they’re coming from the top of the financial sector: from the top of big mortgage companies like Freddie Mac, big insurers like Allianz and Aon, key banks like the Federal Reserve and Bank of England, even the International Financial Stability Board. Economist magazine has warned of a $25 trillion hit to global real estate markets.

The author Ernest Hemingway talked about going bankrupt happening gradually, then all at once. This crash could well happen all at once, and it could happen soon.

For our own safety, we need to get more serious about the politics of climate change if we’re going to head this off. The fossil fuel industry fights fiercely to pollute for free. Its pollute-for-free business model is not only morally and economically a sin and a subsidy, it is now lethal to our climate safety as humankind.

But they won’t give it up. They depend on polluting for free. So a battle looms.

In a battle, my friends, you need to know your adversary.

Everywhere, fossil fuel operates through front groups. In most places, fossil fuel funds the far right, as paid allies. Vladimir Putin’s covert schemes in Europe both disrupt democracy and prop up fossil fuel, his primary revenue. In the United States, the political right, fueled by dark money, still denies climate science. That is the enemy arrayed against you: fossil fuel, and all its front groups and dark money; Vladimir Putin, and all of Russia’s anti-democracy mischief; and far-right political groups that deny climate change.

We face climate peril as fossil fuel disrupts Nature’s systems; and we face the more immediate, systemic economic peril that prefigures it; so we must face up now to the political peril right now of the fossil fuel industry, its armada of front groups, its political meddling through far-right groups it funds, and the malign influence of the petro-state Russia.

Collectively, they amount to a new Axis of Evil, determined to ruin society’s ability to meet the climate challenge that fossil fuel pollution causes. It’s time to ready ourselves for battle.

When the zettajoules pile up, and something very bad happens all at once, we will bitterly regret any failure to prepare or failure to fight. Thank you.

title: Wyden Calls for Public Release of Report on White House-Funded Surveillance Programs, Including National Database of Flock and Other ALPR Images
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ron Wyden, D-Ore., called for the White House to release a report it commissioned examining the privacy impacts of surveillance activities funded by the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), including a program that scoops up data from Flock cameras and other license plate readers across the country and a dragnet phone surveillance program called Hemisphere.

Wyden learned of the report as part of his oversight of the Hemisphere phone surveillance program, which mined trillions of American phone records under an arrangement between AT&T and the federal government. The White House ultimately ended that program in 2025 after repeated requests from Wyden and Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz. The Hemisphere program was operated by the Houston High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) program and paid for with funds from the ONDCP.

After Wyden began questioning ONDCP about its funding of the Hemisphere program, ONDCP informed Wyden’s staff that it had commissioned the nonprofit technology research firm MITRE to study privacy issues related to the HIDTA program. However, the ONDCP refused to share the report with Wyden’s office when it was finished in 2024, and has continued to keep it hidden from the public.

Recently, 404 Media reported that local law enforcement agencies are funneling data from Flock and other license plate reader cameras into a national database, also operated by the Houston HIDTA.

“Flock’s AI surveillance cameras have sparked a nationwide backlash against unnecessary government intrusion into Americans’ lives,” Wyden said. “As Congress debates solutions to protect our privacy and civil liberties, the MITRE report could provide important information about how these cameras and other surveillance programs are already impacting Americans’ rights. The White House should make MITRE’s findings public as soon as possible.”

Wyden was the first member of Congress to question Flock over its security and privacy practices, and has defended Americans’ privacy rights against unnecessary government surveillance for decades.

The full letter is available here.
