title: Young Highlights Indiana’s Leadership in Biotech at IU Symposium
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) addressed Indiana University’s Biotechnology Symposium in Indianapolis on Thursday and highlighted Indiana’s growing role in the life sciences industry and the national security implications of biotechnology.

Young, who chairs the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB), delivered opening remarks and participated in a fireside chat with NSCEB Vice Chair Dr. Michelle Rozo and Commissioner Dr. Dov Zakheim. The discussion focused on how Congress is advancing the Commission’s recommendations, China’s biotech ambitions, why the U.S. needs to stay ahead, and expanding opportunities for Hoosier workers.

“Biotechnology is critical to our national security, economic competitiveness, and quality of life. Our National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology laid out a roadmap to ensure the United States leads the next age of biotechnology, and Indiana University is well-positioned to help turn that vision into a reality. By bringing together talented researchers across disciplines, IU is advancing the kind of innovation that will strengthen America’s leadership in this critical sector,” said Senator Young.

During the symposium, IU announced six research awards through its National Security Biotech for Defense program. The awards support interdisciplinary research projects focused on advancing biotechnology applications in areas including battlefield medicine, biological threat detection, advanced materials, and biomanufacturing.

title: Smith Welcomes CMS Administrator Dr. Oz to Blair
text:
Yesterday, Congressman Adrian Smith (NE-03) joined Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz for a tour of Memorial Community Hospital and Health System, a critical access hospital in Blair.

During the tour, Smith and Oz met with hospital staff to discuss the challenges facing rural healthcare providers and opportunities to strengthen access to care through telemedicine, support rural healthcare workforce development, and advance initiatives like the Rural Health Transformation Program.

"Critical access hospitals like Memorial Community Hospital play a vital role in the communities they serve, by ensuring patients have access to quality care close to home. I am grateful to have strong partners like Administrator Oz who take the time to visit rural communities, listen to healthcare providers, and understand the challenges they face. I look forward to continuing to work together to strengthen rural healthcare and ensure every Nebraskan has access to quality care, regardless of their ZIP code,”said Congressman Smith.

"Rural health systems have been underfunded and under resourced for decades, but thanks to President Trump’s Rural Health Transformation Program, we’re empowering states to tackle that problem head-on by making the investments these communities need,”said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz.“I’m grateful to Congressman Smith for meeting with me and to Memorial Community Hospital for hosting us, so that together, we can discuss the improvements RHTP dollars are already driving and how additional funding can build on that progress over the remaining four years of the program.”

"We are glad to be part of efforts to strengthen healthcare access in rural communities. We appreciate Congressman Smith and Dr. Oz taking the time to visit MCH and hear directly from the providers and caregivers serving patients every day. These conversations help ensure that rural voices are heard and that policy decisions reflect the realities facing rural healthcare, allowing us to continue providing high-quality care close to home,”said Memorial Community Hospital and Health System President and CEO Manuela Banner.

title: REP. BOEBERT, 2A CAUCUS CO-CHAIR, CELEBRATES JUSTICE DEPARTMENT DECISION TO DISMANTLE NATIONAL FIREARMS ACT, DELIVERING FOR GUN OWNERS
text:
LONE TREE, CO. — Rep. Lauren Boebert, Co-Chair of the Second Amendment Caucus, celebrated the Department of Justice and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives guidance that dismantles deep state burdens on gun owners under the National Firearms Act for short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, suppressors, and “any other weapons,” delivering for gun owners.

“This is a long-overdue win for law-abiding Americans and a direct result of both the courts and Congress doing the right thing,” said Rep. Boebert. “I was proud to vote for the One Big Beautiful Bill, which included the provision that eliminated the NFA tax on short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, suppressors, and certain other firearms. Once the tax was gone, the registration scheme lost its constitutional foundation. The Justice Department decision finally puts that reality into practice for gun owners across the country.

The guidance follows an August ruling by the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF. The court held that key NFA registration, approval, and related requirements could no longer be enforced for those categories after Congress eliminated the making and transfer taxes. The Department of Justice declined to appeal, and ATF has now stated it will not enforce the prior approval, registration, tax-stamp, and related NFA requirements for these items nationwide, effective October 9, 2026.

“Congratulations to Gun Owners of America and the other plaintiffs for fighting this case and securing the injunction that made this possible. The Second Amendment is not a suggestion, and this guidance is a meaningful step toward treating it that way.”

Rep. Boebert has introduced the Freedom from Taxes Act (H.R. 8921) to eliminate the final categories remaining in the NFA. View the bill here:

https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/8921

title: De La Cruz Holds Brooks County Congressional Record Ceremony
text:
WASHINGTON - This week, Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (TX-15) held the inaugural Brooks County Congressional Record Ceremony to honor the Falfurrias Fire Department's 100 years of service to the community.

"It was an honor to present the Falfurrias Fire Department with an official Congressional Record commemorating 100 years of service to Falfurrias and surrounding communities. One of my greatest privileges as your Congresswoman is sharing our community's stories on the House floor and ensuring our local heroes are forever remembered in our nation's history." - Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz

Background:

Earlier this year, Congresswoman De La Cruz recognized the Falfurrias Volunteer Fire Department for a century of dedicated service to South Texas. Full speech can be found here.

Delivering for the community remains a top priority. Since coming to Congress, De La Cruz has secured $3M for the new Brooks County Public Safety Complex.

title: Comisionado Residente y congresistas presentan legislación para fortalecer el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández (D-PR) junto a los congresistas Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL) y Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) presentaron el Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), legislación bipartita que busca corregir una disparidad histórica en el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico, cambiando la fórmula federal para calcular los pagos y aplicando el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que se utiliza para las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses.

“Estamos priorizando lo básico: que nuestros adultos mayores tengan acceso a los médicos y servicios de salud que necesitan. Este año logramos un aumento importante en los fondos de Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico. Ahora queremos dar el próximo paso y corregir de una vez y por todas la disparidad que por años ha afectado a la Isla”, dijo el Comisionado Residente Hernández.

“Como medico de emergencias, sé que cuando la atención está fuera de alcance, los adultos mayores pagan el precio”, dijo el Congresista Raúl Ruiz, M.D. “Los puertorriqueños pagan Medicare en los mismos términos que todos los estadounidenses, y sin embargo, a sus planes Medicare Advantage se les paga cerca de un 40 por ciento menos. Esa brecha ha reducido las redes de proveedores, recortado beneficios y puesto bajo presión a médicos y hospitales. Este proyecto de ley es una solución específica y de sentido común. Agradezco a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y a al Comisionado Residente Hernández, por trabajar conmigo para brindar a los adultos mayores la cobertura justa que se han Ganado.”

“Estoy orgulloso de unirme al comisionado residente de Puerto Rico Hernández y a los representantes Bilirakis y Ruiz para presentar la Ley bipartidista de Equidad en Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico, con el fin de realizar ajustes geográficos a los niveles de referencia de Medicare Advantage en la isla e igualarlos a los de las Islas Vírgenes de los Estados Unidos. Esto nos acerca a lograr la plena paridad entre la isla y el territorio continental. Los puertorriqueños son ciudadanos estadounidenses y merecen el mismo acceso a los beneficios de atención médica que todos los estadounidenses”. dijo el Congresista Darren Soto.

“Los adultos mayores merecen acceso confiable a los servicios de salud de calidad que se han ganado a través de Medicare, sin importar dónde vivan”, expresó el congresista Gus Bilirakis. “Medicare Advantage desempeña un papel importante en la atención médica de los beneficiarios en todo Puerto Rico. Debemos garantizar que el programa reciba un financiamiento justo y sostenible para que nuestros adultos mayores puedan seguir recibiendo atención de sus médicos y contando con los tratamientos y beneficios que necesitan. Me enorgullece unirme a los congresistas Ruiz, Soto y Hernández para presentar el proyecto de ley bipartidista Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act, que busca corregir las desigualdades que han persistido por años, mejorar el acceso a los servicios de salud y brindar mayor estabilidad a los pacientes y a los proveedores de atención médica.”

“Esta legislación representa un paso importante para atender un problema estructural que por años ha afectado los pagos de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. Con aproximadamente el 96% de los beneficiarios de Medicare en la Isla acogidos a Medicare Advantage, la metodología utilizada para establecer las tarifas de referencia para Puerto Rico debe reflejar la realidad del mercado al que sirve. Agradecemos al congresista Ruiz, a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y al comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández Rivera por unirse en una solución bipartita que utilizaría a las Islas Vírgenes de Estados Unidos como referencia geográfica comparable y ayudaría a fortalecer el acceso a servicios de salud para cientos de miles de beneficiarios en Puerto Rico. MMAPA respalda firmemente esta iniciativa y espera continuar colaborando con el Congreso y los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS) para promover un programa de Medicare Advantage más estable y sostenible para Puerto Rico”, expresó Solage De Lahongrais, presidenta de la Asociación de Productos de Medicaid y Medicare Advantage de Puerto Rico (MMAPA).

Más de 650,000 puertorriqueños dependen de Medicare Advantage para recibir sus servicios de salud, lo que convierte al programa en una pieza fundamental del sistema de salud de Puerto Rico. Sin embargo, la fórmula federal que determina cuánto dinero reciben los planes médicos se basa, en parte, en los gastos de los pacientes de Medicare tradicional, que representan una pequeña minoría en la Isla. Esto provoca que los pagos se calculen utilizando información que no refleja adecuadamente los costos de ofrecer servicios médicos en Puerto Rico, lo que ha contribuido a una disparidad en el financiamiento del programa durante años.

El Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act busca corregir de manera permanente esta disparidad. A partir de 2027, el proyecto requeriría que Medicare utilice para Puerto Rico el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que aplica a las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses al calcular los pagos a los planes Medicare Advantage. Este cambio busca que los fondos federales respondan mejor a los costos de ofrecer servicios de salud en la Isla.

La medida permitiría establecer una fórmula de financiamiento más justa y estable, reducir la dependencia de ajustes administrativos que se revisan año tras año y dar mayor certeza a los pacientes, médicos, hospitales y demás proveedores de salud que dependen del programa.

La legislación se presenta en un momento importante para los beneficiarios de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. A pocos días de comenzar el periodo anual de inscripción abierta de Medicare, cientos de miles de adultos mayores se preparan para evaluar sus opciones de cubierta médica para el próximo año. El proyecto representa un nuevo paso en las gestiones que ha impulsado el comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández desde el Congreso para corregir las desigualdades en el financiamiento del programa.

A principios de este año, cuando los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS, por sus siglas en inglés) propusieron un aumento nacional de apenas 0.09% en los pagos de Medicare Advantage para 2027, el Comisionado Residente encabezó una carta bipartita firmada por 17 congresistas, incluidos Raul Ruiz y Darren Soto, para reclamar un trato más justo para Puerto Rico. Tras estas gestiones y los esfuerzos del sector de salud de la Isla, CMS anunció un aumento de aproximadamente 4% para Puerto Rico, superior al promedio nacional de alrededor de 2.5%.

###

Hernández, Ruiz, Soto, and Bilirakis Introduce Bill to Strengthen Medicare Advantage Funding in Puerto Rico

WASHINGTON, DC — Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), alongside Representatives Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL), and Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), bipartisan legislation that would fix a longstanding Medicare Advantage funding disparity by changing how Washington calculates payments to Puerto Rico, using the same standard applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.

“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Hernández.

"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned.”

"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz, Soto, and Hernández in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers.”

“I am proud to join Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Hernández and Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans.” said Congressman Darren Soto.

“This legislation represents an important step toward addressing a longstanding structural challenge in Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico. With approximately 96% ofMedicare beneficiaries on the Island choosing Medicare Advantage, the methodology used to establish Puerto Rico’s benchmarks must reflect the reality of the market it serves. We thank Congressman Ruiz, Representatives Bilirakis and Soto, and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández Rivera for coming together on a bipartisan solution that would use the U.S. Virgin Islands as a comparable geographic reference and help strengthen access to care for hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. MMAPA strongly supports this effort and looks forward to continuing to work with Congress and CMS to advance a more stable and sustainable Medicare Advantage program for Puerto Rico”, said Solage De Lahongrais, President of the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA).

More than 650,000 Puerto Ricans rely on Medicare Advantage for their healthcare coverage, making it a cornerstone of the island’s healthcare system. Yet a key part of the federal funding formula relies on healthcare spending among traditional Medicare patients, who represent only a small fraction of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. As a result, payments are calculated using a limited picture of healthcare costs on the island, contributing to a longstanding funding disparity.

The Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act seeks to permanently address one of the disparities in the federal payment formula. Beginning in 2027, the legislation would require the geographic adjustment used to calculate Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico to match the adjustment applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.

This change would help establish a fairer, more stable funding structure for Puerto Rico, reduce the need for year-to-year administrative adjustments, and provide greater certainty for the patients, physicians, hospitals, and healthcare providers who depend on the program.

This legislation comes at a critical time for Puerto Rico's patients and healthcare providers. With Medicare's annual open enrollment period just days away, hundreds of thousands of seniors will soon be reviewing their coverage options for the coming year. This legislation marks the next step in the Resident Commissioner’s ongoing efforts in Congress to close this funding gap.

Earlier this year, when the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a national Medicare Advantage payment increase of just 0.09% for 2027, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández led a bipartisan letter signed by 17 members of Congress, including Representatives Raul Ruiz and Darren Soto, urging CMS to address the payment disparity affecting Puerto Rico. Following this effort and continued advocacy from Puerto Rico’s healthcare sector, CMS announced an increase of approximately 4% for the island, exceeding the national average of roughly 2.5%.

title: Important legislation protecting American shrimpers advances in Congress
text:
Written and submitted for publication by the Southern Shrimp Alliance.

October 10, 2026

Important legislation supporting American shrimpers has now advanced in Congress.

S. 5613, the Ecuador Shrimp Tariff Act Introduced Wednesday

On Wednesday, Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS) announced the introduction of S. 5613, the Ecuador Shrimp Tariff Act that would gradually increase tariffs imposed on shrimp from Ecuador to reach 40 percent in 2029.

Modeled after S. 2868, the India Shrimp Tariff Act, that Senator Hyde-Smith co-sponsored with Senator Bill Cassidy, MD (R-LA) in September of last year, the legislation also imposes a ten cent per kilogram duty on imports of shrimp from all sources in order to fund increased inspections of imported catfish and shrimp and expands the coverage of the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) country-of-origin labeling (COOL) requirements to include cooked shrimp and cooked crawfish products.

The Ecuador Shrimp Tariff Act recognizes that with substantial support from U.S.-taxpayer backed international financial institutions like the World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and the Inter American Development Bank, Ecuador’s shrimp exports to the United States have exploded. Through the first seven months of this year, Ecuador has now become the single largest supplier of frozen warmwater shrimp to this market, accounting for 40% of total import volume and overtaking India for the first time.

These two countries – Ecuador and India – currently account for three out of every four pounds (75%) of frozen warmwater shrimp imported into the United States. The intense competition for sales between the Ecuadorian and Indian shrimp industries is not just driving down prices for U.S. shrimpers but is also pushing other suppliers out of the American market, with import volumes from Indonesia falling by 17% and from Vietnam by 33% in the first seven months of 2026 compared to the same time period in 2025.

H.R. 10580, Let Americans Buy with Explicit Labeling (LABEL) Act, Introduced in the House; S. 5526, Agricultural Act of 2026, Clears Senate Agriculture Committee

On Thursday of last week (September 24th), Congressman Tim Moore (R-NC) and Congressman Randy Weber (R-TX) introduced H.R. 10580, the Let Americans Buy with Explicit Labeling (LABEL) Act. The legislation is the House companion to Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith’s (R-MS) S. 3065 introduced in October of last year and co-sponsored by Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) and Senator Adam Schiff (D-CA).

Explaining the need for the legislation, Congressman Moore observed: “Every American deserves to know where their food comes from. The LABEL Act helps ensure consumers have clear information about where their seafood was caught or raised and how it was produced, right on the front of the package.”

In August, Senator Hyde-Smith’s LABEL Act was included as an amendment to S. 5526, the Senate’s Agricultural Act of 2026 (Farm Bill 2.0). With the LABEL Act incorporated as Section 12605 (“Country of Origin and Method of Production Labeling for Fish”) of S. 5526, the Farm Bill 2.0 also passed out of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry on Thursday of last week (September 24th).

In addition to the LABEL Act, the Senate’s Farm Bill 2.0 includes a section requiring the USDA to issue a report on international shrimp trade in order to boost the competitiveness of domestic shrimp in global and domestic markets (Section 3402), as well as a report on expanding seafood processing capacity in the United States (Section 12607). The Farm Bill 2.0 also formally establishes the USDA’s Office of Seafood (Section 12606) and expands eligibility of certain USDA programs to encompass American seafood producers (Sections 5216 and 10114).

S. 4974, Making America’s Food Safer Act, Passed the Senate on Monday

On Monday, September 28th, by unanimous consent, S. 4974, Making America’s Food Safer Act passed the Senate. Sponsored by Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) and co-sponsored by Senators Bill Cassidy, MD (R-LA) and Tim Kaine (D-VA), Section 4 of S. 4974 authorizes the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to order the destruction of any imported article subject to FDA regulation that presents a significant public health concern.

The grant of this same authority was initially included in Congressmen Clay Higgins’ (R-LA) and Troy Carter’s (D-LA) bi-partisan H.R. 2715, the Destruction of Hazardous Imports Act, that passed the House by voice vote in July.

By passing S. 4974 and H.R. 2715, both the House and Senate in the 119th Congress have now voted to authorize the FDA to order the destruction of imports that pose significant public health concerns. However, in order to become law, the House will need to pass S. 4974 the Making America’s Food Safer Act or the Senate pass H.R. 2715, the Destruction of Hazardous Imports Act.

title: King Releases Statement on New ‘Deal’ to Ease Sanctions on Russia, Fund Putin’s Aggression Against Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME) released the following statement amidst news that the White House has made an agreement to ease sanctions on Russian oil which will inevitably not ease the burden on Americans at the gas pump, yet help fund Vladimir Putin’s war of aggression against Ukraine:

“Americans nationwide are struggling with the cost-of-living – from prices at the pump to the cost of essentials at the grocery story – mostly due to Trump’s unconstitutional war in Iran and his devastating tariffs on our long-standing allies.

“Instead of pursuing solutions that are consistent with America’s values, President Trump has decided to ease energy sanctions on Russia. In doing so, he chose Putin over the American people, which will ultimately help fuel that autocracy’s bloody, unprovoked war of aggression on Ukraine.

“This so-called deal with Russia will do little for America and much for Vladimir Putin as he seeks to sustain his murderous campaign on Ukraine. To put this so-called deal into perspective, it amounts to 300,000 tons of diesel for October and then 500,000 for November – which may sound like a lot, but according to the administration’s own numbers is roughly the amount of diesel the American people use in a single day. This helps Russia far more than it helps the United States.

“Adding insult to injury, today’s deal is a slap in the face to every member of Congress who voted for the Lindsay Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act just last month which was designed to honor the memory of a strong defender of democracy and punish the leaders of these rogue nations. Every member of Congress who voted for this bill – 86 in the Senate, 262 in the House – should be demanding an immediate reversal of this decision.

“At the end of the day, this deal from the White House is an attempt to boost their short-term political prospects at the true cost of the American people. We are helping one adversary (though it’s questionable if the White House considers Putin that) and showing weakness to another due to Iran’s Strait of Hormuz oil blockade. This deal comforts our enemies and will do little for Americans. It’s a fraud.”

title: Murphy's Behind-the-Scenes Details of CODEL to the Gulf
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, on Saturday authored a Substack article offering the day-by-day details and post-travel reflections of his Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to the Middle East, which included stops in Doha, Qatar and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. In the piece, Murphy lays out why he chose to visit the Gulf in the midst of an active war with Iran, explaining the urgent need for Congress to directly assess the war’s damage, repair relationships, and hear the latest on the Trump administration’s negotiations to bring the war to an end.

Murphy described his candid conversations with the Qatari Emir and Saudi Crown Prince on their countries’ cooperation with President Trump’s corruption of American foreign policy. Murphy also detailed the Department of Defense’s unprecedented decision to deny him access to the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar - despite decades of precedent for DOD supporting CODELs to American military bases under active threat - and block military leaders in the region from even providing a standard briefing on the war’s progress. Murphy also provided on-the-ground details of damage to the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia, as well as energy facilities in the region which play a substantial role in the global energy economy, likely driving prices up for Americans for years to come.

Read Senator Murphy’s full reflections on his trip to the Gulf below or HERE.

I refuse to accept this moment as normal. The United States is in the middle of a massive, deadly, backbreakingly expensive war in the Middle East - a war opposed by 70 percent of Americans - and Congress has not taken one single vote to authorize it. It is an illegal, unconstitutional war that has made our nation dramatically less safe. And I believe that it is my responsibility as a United States Senator to do exceptional things to help bring it to an end.

So, as soon as the Senate recessed for the fall election season, I got on a plane and headed for the Middle East - the first Democratic Senator to visit the Gulf since the war began. What did I hope to accomplish? First, I wanted to see for myself the damage done to U.S. basing in the region and the impact of the war on our partner nations. When at war, I have found there is no substitute for going into the theater and seeing the conflict firsthand. Second, I wanted to hear from leaders in the region about the path to end the war, and their view of the mistakes the U.S. has made that have caused this disastrous war to drag on this long. Third, I wanted to bring some hard messages to our partners in the region about Trump’s corruption of foreign policy.

This is the behind-the-scenes account of my visit.

QATAR

Dinner with the negotiators

On Friday evening, I boarded a plane bound for Doha, Qatar. My plan was to spend a day in Doha, since the Qataris are the primary interlocutors between the U.S. and Iran. I would also travel to the largest U.S. base in the region, Al Udeid, located in Qatar. Al Udeid sustained significant damage from Iranian strikes, and if Americans are going to be asked to send billions of dollars for repairs, I wanted to see the damage with my own eyes.

After a long flight, I had planned to simply meet with our U.S. Embassy officials upon my arrival Saturday night. But just before departing, I learned that Ali Al Thawadi, the Qatari diplomat who has been conducting shuttle diplomacy between the U.S. and Iran, wanted to host me for dinner to talk about the status of negotiations. Over a two-hour dinner, Al Thawadi told me that a deal to end the war was still possible, but if achieved, it would be limited in scope. It would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, provide Iran with significant sanctions relief (providing billions to the Iranian regime), and might include some small commitments to constrain their nuclear program. I told him that though that sounded like a terrible deal, I would support almost any deal to end the war since America’s security, treasury and reputation were hemorrhaging each day the war continued.

At the end of dinner, Al Thawadi started checking his phone more frequently and then somewhat abruptly suggested we take dessert in his sitting room. Was something breaking with the Iranians, I wondered? No, in fact. As we sat down in his living room, he pointed to the television.

“We are playing Saudi Arabia in the semifinals of the Gulf Cup! It’s gone to penalty kicks!”

For a few moments, he tried to keep the conversation going while watching the game, but the entire room was clearly and appropriately distracted by the game, as the Saudi goalkeeper made save after save. “Why don’t we just take a break and watch the game?” I suggested. After Qatar lost the game on penalty kicks (3-2), the mood quieted somewhat and I politely excused myself from a productive meeting that had run past three hours.

Meeting with the Emir

On Saturday, I conducted a series of meetings with Qatari officials, including the head of state, the Emir of Qatar Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. The Qataris have been uniquely helpful partners to the United States over the years. They often serve as mediators of conflicts, like they are now. They host 1,000 Afghan refugees, at our request. Al Udeid and its thousands of American troops are there. I thanked the Emir for this partnership, and we discussed regional issues, like Iran, Yemen and Lebanon.

But I also had another message to deliver: my deep concern over the gift of a Qatari luxury jet to President Trump - a jet Trump has promised to take for his personal use after he leaves office. The Emir defended the gift as intended for the U.S. government and noted that Qatar had not done anything illegal. I told him that though I know how much pressure Trump put on Qatar to deliver the gift, we had to have zero tolerance on the corruption of U.S. foreign policy. Last year, I actually forced a vote on the Senate floor to suspend military sales to Qatar as a consequence of the plane gift, and I warned him that Qatar’s relationship with the United States would be damaged by any actions to personally enrich Trump or his family. A gift of that size to the President of the United States is corruption, plain and simple. I left hoping that my message was heard.

The cover up

By the time I left this meeting, it had become clear that I would not succeed in fulfilling the primary purpose of my visit: going to the Al Udeid base to talk to U.S. military leaders and troops about the war, and see the serious damage done to the facility.

I have visited many active theaters of war during my time in Congress. This is my job: to do oversight over U.S. military operations overseas, especially during times of war. Congress - not the President - decides questions of war, and we cannot exercise our warmaking power or our power to appropriate or withhold funds for war without seeing it firsthand.

Previous presidents have been very serious about honoring our constitutional responsibility. I toured Baghdad with our troops in the middle of some of the most active fighting there. I helicoptered to forward operating bases in Afghanistan that were being targeted by daily Taliban attacks at the height of the Afghanistan War. Never before have I been denied access to visit our troops overseas during times of active war. But this president is no ordinary president.

I made several formal requests to see Al Udeid ahead of my visit. Then, three days before I departed, I spoke in person with the U.S. CENTCOM Commander in charge of the war, Admiral Brad Cooper, and told him about my worry that I would be denied access in violation of the Constitution. I also told him that I had been told by the Department of Defense that I would be denied even a briefing by military leaders in the region. He told me the base visit policy was made by Secretary Hegseth, not him. He also said he was surprised that we were being denied even the opportunity to talk with his team and that he would look into that question.

Apparently he could not change Hegseth’s mind because by Saturday afternoon it was clear we would see no military installations nor meet with any military leaders while in Qatar. It was an outrageous decision - part of a coordinated cover up to hide the true costs and consequences of the war. I was furious but determined to make my time in Qatar as productive as possible. So I asked the Qataris to bring me out to their massive natural gas processing port, Ras Laffan, to see the damage Iranian drones had done there.

Ras Laffan

Ras Laffan is a breathtaking place. We all take for granted that our lights turn on and off reliably, and our home heat adjusts easily from season to season, but at Ras Laffan, you see the immense mechanical and human effort necessary to convert a fossil fuel into a source of energy that creates electricity and heating for billions of people. Gas production plants sprawl over miles of oceanside desert, for as far as the eye can see. 110,000 laborers live in camps throughout the complex (only men, with most allocated 8 square meters of living space per man), operating, building, and repairing the facility.

But the facility, aside from the ongoing construction, is largely idle - for two reasons. First, with the Strait of Hormuz constricted, only one natural gas tanker can travel through it per day (compared to ten per day prior to the war). Second, the Iranians hit two key areas of the facility (with precision strikes designed to do maximum damage), taking offline much of the work to liquify gas for transport. The repairs will cost billions and take three years to finish. Seventeen percent of Qatar’s gas exports are gone, and as a result, global prices will remain high for the long term.

Seeing the damage in person was important. And I was glad the Qataris (and the U.S. State Department) helped me see it. From Ras Laffan, we traveled directly to the airport, and I boarded a plane to Riyadh for my first visit ever to Saudi Arabia.

SAUDI ARABIA

A near mass casualty event

I have been perhaps the most vocal critic of Saudi Arabia and its leader, Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman (colloquially referred to as “MBS”), over the past decade. I organized an effort to stop President Obama’s plan to provide U.S. support for Saudi Arabia’s war in Yemen in 2016, and I have been a loud critic of MBS’s campaign of domestic and foreign repression of free speech, including the infamous murder and dismemberment of American resident journalist Jamal Khashoggi.

But I chose to come to Riyadh for two reasons, both of which I explained to the Saudi Ambassador to the U.S., Princess Reema bint Bandar Al Saud, when I asked her to meet with me in September. First, I think it’s important for MBS and other Saudi officials to hear from opponents of the war and critics of his policies, not just Trump acolytes, many of whom are simply involved in a foreign policy grift, using their positions to make money from the Gulf. Second, despite its deep imperfections, Saudi Arabia is still a key partner in the region, especially when it comes to ending the war. And despite my criticism, there have been substantial cultural reforms in the Kingdom over the last decade that I wanted to see for myself.

My first stop in Riyadh on Monday morning was the U.S. Embassy for briefings with U.S. officials. While I was there, they showed me the immense damage that had been done to a section of the embassy by two Iranian drones that hit the building in the middle of the night during the early days of the war. No photographs have been released of the damage, and I might have been the first Member of Congress to see it in person (another reason why these visits are important). What I can say is that if the attack had happened in the middle of the day instead of the middle of the night, many Americans would be dead. As I stood in the dark, now abandoned space, I brimmed with anger at our president, who started this war without any real plan to keep our troops and diplomats safe. We are all very lucky this attack wasn’t a truly catastrophic one.

MBS

I thought hard about whether to meet with Mohammed bin Salman. What message would I send to meet face to face with a leader who subjects people who criticize him to beheading and ordered the murder of a Washington Post journalist ? But, on the other hand, what good does it do to avoid him, so that he only speaks with domestic sycophants and foreigners who refuse to confront him face to face? I chose to meet him.

MBS has a habit of keeping visitors guessing as to when and if he will meet them, with the appointed time often ending up being in the middle of the night. Once in Riyadh, I heard the story of a very high-level U.S. official who was told to go to the city of Jeddah to meet with MBS, and then waited hours for the meeting only to be finally told that MBS was in fact not even in Jeddah. This may burnish his mysterious reputation, but it certainly does not make friends. And Saudi Arabia needs friends.

I was told to keep Monday evening clear and I would be summoned to the palace at some point during the night. But then, in the late morning that day, as I was readying for lunch with longtime Saudi diplomat, Adel al-Jubeir, I was told that MBS was ready to meet me and asked if I could immediately come to the palace. I did, and after waiting there only a few minutes, MBS met me in a grand room, along with his Foreign Minister, National Security Advisor and Princess Reema. He began with a long recitation of the history of U.S.-Saudi relations and how important our partnership is. He finished by stressing his support for America’s global leadership, for which he believes there is no alternative. I told him I agree that our nations are inextricably linked, and that I want to think about how to bring back this partnership and resolve our disagreements.

For the next hour, we had a candid discussion about American values, domestic political dissent and Saudi Arabia’s financial support for the Trump family (Trump’s companies have done deals in the Kingdom recently and Saudi Arabia is a key investor in Middle East envoy Jared Kushner’s private equity fund). He defended both his campaign of repression (as necessary to prevent a revolution against his social reforms, he claimed) and his Trump family investments (just business deals, he said). I imagine he seldom has vocal critics like me in his palace, but he didn’t shy away from a spirited discussion. There was, of course, no meeting of the minds, but I believe it’s important for him to understand that his nation’s relationship with America will remain fragile as long as political opponents are hunted and Trump investment opportunities are favored.

We spent the second hour of our meeting discussing Iran and Yemen. He knew, of course, that I have long opposed Saudi Arabia’s military intervention in Yemen. So he didn’t try to convince me - as he has been trying to convince Trump - that the U.S. should support his current ground campaign there with air cover. But I did concede that comparing today’s conflict to the prior era of fighting was not fair. The truce in Yemen was only interrupted because of Trump’s war in Iran. The Houthis, in order to support their ally Iran, began to fire at ships in the Red Sea and moved to control more territory along the Bab Al Mandeb Strait - along with sending missiles and drones into Saudi Arabia, in response to Trump’s attacks on Iran. I do not think it’s in Saudi Arabia’s interest to restart a long ground war in Yemen, but I understand they need to defend themselves from Houthi attacks. I told him that.

Missiles overhead

Over the rest of the day Monday and through Tuesday, I met with local Saudi citizens and other members of the government (including the Foreign Minister and Energy Minister). I will admit that the social transformation happening in Saudi Arabia is real. After dinner on Tuesday with the Foreign Minister, I watched a group of women walking on the street together, one with her head fully covered, one with a lightly wrapped hijab, and one with no head covering at all. As many women were driving on the roads as men. Movie theaters were open and busy, and men and women sat together in cafes. This social opening is no excuse for tightened political repression, but it is real and meaningful.

As our departing flight drew closer, we took more urgent note of reports of nightly missiles being fired at Riyadh from Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen. These warnings, combined with the sight of the horrible damage to our embassy, was a reminder that the war Trump began in February has completely spiraled out of control. Yemen is a battle zone again. Saudi Arabia suffers nightly attacks. Thousands are dead and wounded in Lebanon as a result of a new war with Israel. All of this horror and carnage was a totally predictable result of Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran. And seeing it all for myself - wondering whether our flight would be able to leave as the Houthis targeted the Riyadh airport - reinforced for me, in a unique, personal way, the ongoing, compounding disaster Trump has caused.

That is why these visits are critical. And it’s why Hegseth and Trump are so deeply committed to stopping Members of Congress from seeing the consequences of the insane, voluntary war they started. They know that if more of us saw in person the immense damage done to U.S. bases, or had the chance to directly interrogate war leaders about their sure-to-fail war plans, support for the war in Congress would dry up fast.

Once on the plane home, my staff forwarded me more breaking news out of Saudi Arabia. A missile had struck the Riyadh airport, perhaps just prior or after our takeoff. Another disastrous result of a disastrous war.

title: The New York Times: Democrats Press Pentagon on Iran Civilian Deaths
text:
Democratic lawmakers are pressing the Pentagon to answer questions about U.S. airstrikes that killed civilians in Iran, in a possible preview of the party’s oversight agenda should it win control in the midterm elections next month.

The members focused on a strike in September in which three adults and two children at a wedding were killed. The strike also injured some 70 people.

In a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the House Democrats have demanded the Pentagon provide an account of the strike on Sept. 1 as well as other incidents in which large numbers of civilians were killed.

“This is the latest in an alarming pattern of civilian casualty incidents in strikes carried out by the United States in Iran since the war began,” the lawmakers wrote.

The House Democrats, for now, have little leverage to pressure the Department of Defense for answers. But should the party take control of one or both chambers of Congress, the issue of civilian casualties in the Iran war could well become a focus.

The effort, led by Representatives Jason Crow of Colorado, Sara Jacobs of California and Yassamin Ansari of Arizona, had 74 signatures in all, demonstrating broad concern within the Democratic caucus.

The Pentagon has not acknowledged responsibility for the strike, saying only that an internal review is underway by U.S. Central Command. But a visual investigation by The New York Times found that the wedding, in Kuhestak, Iran, was struck by a bomb that had been released by American forces as they carried out intense attacks in southern Iran.

Neither the Pentagon nor Central Command, the department within the military with responsibility over the Middle East, has provided granular details of its military operations in Iran or of potential errant strikes that killed civilians. The department has also closed the area of the Pentagon where the press used to work from and placed tight controls on reporters’ entering the building.

In addition to the strike on the wedding, there have been a number of incidents of civilian casualties, most notably an attack on a Navy base in southern Iran in the opening hours of the war that destroyed an elementary school, killing at least 175 people.

The members of Congress said the number of strikes that had killed civilians was troubling, as was the lack of transparency from the Trump administration over the war more broadly.

“We are deeply alarmed by the continued pattern of civilian casualties resulting from U.S. operations in the war in Iran, and the apparent lack of action and accountability from the Department,” the lawmakers wrote in the letter. “Acknowledging such incidents, accepting responsibility, and learning from them makes our forces stronger, more effective, and an example to the world. When we fail to do so, it has the exact opposite effect.”

The letter from the lawmakers cited both the reporting from The Times and The Washington Post.

In the letter, the lawmakers ask the Pentagon if the U.S. military carried out the strike and what the intended target was. They also ask for details about any investigation into the strike in Kuhestak.

The lawmakers have also reinstated their earlier demand for information about the Pentagon’s review of the strike on the elementary school. More broadly, they are seeking information about another strike in Lamerd, Iran, on that same day, Feb. 28, that also reportedly caused civilian deaths as well as an accounting of other possible errant strikes.

The letter to Mr. Hegseth was sent on Oct. 8 and released publicly Sunday.

Asked for comment, a Defense Department spokeswoman reiterated an earlier statement from Central Command that the reports of the strike on the wedding originated on Iranian state media. “The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the I.R.G.C.,” the statement said, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.

Mr. Crow, who helped lead the effort, is a former Army Ranger who served in the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. Since joining Congress, he has consistently worked on the issue of harm to civilians in war. He was a driving force behind a law establishing the military’s Civilian Protection Center of Excellence and other measures aimed at minimizing errant attacks on civilians.

He has also collaborated with Ms. Jacobs on the issue of civilian casualties. In 2022, the two lawmakers were part of a group that founded a caucus in Congress to help protect civilians during conflict.

But Mr. Crow has been in the cross hairs of Mr. Hegseth’s Pentagon. He was one of six lawmakers who recorded a video telling U.S. service members they did not need to obey unlawful orders. President Trump accused the lawmakers of sedition and treason.

title: VICTORY ON THE HUDSON: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND LOCAL ADVOCATES CELEBRATE SUCCESS OF RYAN’S LAW THAT PERMANENTLY BANS BARGES ON THE HUDSON RIVER
text:
After years of relentless advocacy by Congressman Ryan, bipartisan lawmakers, and local advocates, the “Hudson River Protection Act” – which permanently bans harmful, polluting barges from docking in the Hudson River – is now law

Ryan joined local advocates, including representatives from Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson, to celebrate the community victory years in the making; Ryan first introduced the bill in 2023 following attempts to allow dangerous barges to anchor in the Hudson, contaminating drinking water for Hudson Valley residents and destroying the environment

POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan joined local experts and advocates to celebrate the success of his Hudson River Protection Act. After years of relentless advocacy by Congressman Ryan, bipartisan elected officials at the local, state, and federal levels, and community experts and advocates, Ryan’s bill permanently banning harmful, polluting barges from docking in the Hudson is now law.

Ryan first introduced the Hudson River Protection Act in 2023, following attempts to erode protections preventing harmful, polluting barges from using the Hudson River as a parking lot – threatening to contaminate drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and destroy the environment. He has been fighting for years, alongside the Hudson Valley community – with the invaluable partnership of organizations including Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson – to advance this legislation.

“If there’s one thing we can all agree on it’s making sure our drinking water is clean and that our Hudson River is safe and protected. For far too long, big corporations have polluted and put at risk our precious River in pursuit of profits. But not anymore. The Hudson is more than a river – it’s the lifeblood and the heartbeat of our community,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Today we celebrated the years of effort by every single member of our Hudson Valley community. I especially want to thank my partners at Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson for their tireless work and commitment to protecting the Hudson. Never again will big corporations be able to turn our River into a parking lot for dangerous barges, polluting the drinking water for 100,000 of our neighbors. This victory proves that when the Hudson Valley stands up with one voice to demand change, we can accomplish anything.”

“As the Coast Guard reviews comments and finalizes its rulemaking barring new anchorages along the Hudson River, we look back to celebrate the Hudson River Protection Act as a powerful testament to what we can accomplish when communities come together to defend the river they depend on,” said Riverkeeper Associate Director of Government Affairs Jeremy Cherson. “For nearly a decade, Riverkeeper and thousands of New Yorkers have fought to ensure that the Hudson is protected from the risks posed by new commercial vessel anchorages. This law honors that persistence by safeguarding critical habitat, protecting drinking water for more than 100,000 people, and making clear that the Hudson is not a place for industrial exploitation. We’re grateful to Congressman Pat Ryan, our partners, and the countless Hudson Valley residents who raised their voices and refused to let the river’s future be put at risk.”

“The Hudson 7 is an intermunicipal council representing seven Mid-Hudson municipalities that rely on the Hudson River as a drinking water source. More than 107,000 people in Dutchess and Ulster Counties depend on the river for their drinking water, with five treatment plants drawing directly from the Hudson to serve communities including Rhinebeck, Esopus, Lloyd, Hyde Park, and Poughkeepsie,” said Gary Bassett, Mayor of the Village of Rhinebeck and Chair of the Hudson 7. “The river doesn’t follow municipal boundaries. A spill doesn’t stop at a town line, and a flood doesn’t stop at a county line. Protecting this shared resource requires regional cooperation and strong federal leadership. Today, we thank Congressman Ryan for his sustained leadership in advancing the Hudson River Protection Act.”

“Residents of Ulster County have a deep and abiding appreciation for the Hudson River. County Executive Metzger recognizes and supports the more than 9,000 county residents who draw their drinking water from the Hudson River, and the thousands more who enjoy fishing, boating, picnicking, and hiking along the waterfront. On behalf of the Department of Environment, we express our appreciation to Congressman Ryan and the advocacy groups who worked tirelessly to secure passage of this legislation,” said Andy Bicking, Director of Ulster County’s Department of Environment.

“Without the Hudson River Protection Act, our river was at risk of becoming a busy highway and parking lot for marine vessels carrying crude oil or other dangerous cargo. Scenic Hudson is proud to have partnered with Congressman Ryan to finally put an end to this threat. The Hudson River Protection Act, introduced and championed by the Congressman, will permanently prevent efforts to add new upper Hudson River anchorages, protecting the ecological health of the river and the health of those who rely on it for drinking water and recreation. Scenic Hudson will continue to partner with our friends in the Hudson Valley, Albany, and Washington to vigilantly protect this critical waterway,” said Carli Fraccarolli, Scenic Hudson's Government Relations Manager.

Congressman Ryan’s “Hudson River Protection Act” bans additional barge anchorages in the Hudson, which pollute the drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and damage the Hudson’s diverse ecosystem.

In 2023, when the Coast Guard issued an Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) signaling an attempt to erode protections preventing commercial vessels from anchoring in the Hudson River, Ryan immediately raised the alarm, warning of devastating environmental and health impacts for the river ecosystem and broader community.

After a more than two month delay, Michael Emerson, the Director of Marine Transportation Systems, provided a woefully insufficient response that left the door open for dangerous oil barges to line the Hudson.

In October of 2023, Ryan was joined by Riverkeeper, Scenic Hudson and the Hudson 7 in demanding the Coast Guard uphold the anchoring ban. Ryan gave a speech on the House Floor, calling on Hudson Valley families to join the fight and shared a form for those interested to register their opinion. The new MSIB, issued in November 2023 in response to overwhelming community outrage, temporarily paused the Coast Guard’s plan to allow dangerous barges to line the Hudson River but doubled down on their plan to allow unlimited anchoring in the future.

Congressman Ryan’s greatest concern has been that the Hudson River serves as the primary water supply for seven communities in his district, and serves as the backup drinking water supply for our nation’s largest city, New York City. Additionally, more oil barges on the Hudson will increase the risks of a catastrophic spill. This is especially concerning for the more than 100,000 people that draw their drinking water from the Hudson River.

Barges often carry oil, asphalt, and other hazardous materials, which pollute the river with their noisy generators and “stadium” lighting. The Hudson River and its connected waters are also home to more than 200 species of fish and provide spawning and nursery habitat for striped bass, shad, and herring that support fisheries up and down the entire Atlantic coast. The River has seen significant efforts to restore the habitats of endangered fish species which are jeopardized by barge anchors dragging along the River bottom.

President Trump signed the “Hudson River Protection Act” into law as part of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), wherein Congressman Ryan secured numerous other wins including a pay raise for troops.

title: Cantwell, Colleagues Urge Spirit Airlines & Google to Protect Workers’ Privacy Amid Sale of Data for AI Training
text:
Cantwell, Colleagues Urge Spirit Airlines & Google to Protect Workers’ Privacy Amid Sale of Data for AI Training

Legislators call for halt in employee data transfer until privacy protections are enacted

EDMONDS, WA – U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and senior member of the Finance Committee, joined her House and Senate colleagues in a letter to Spirit Airlines CEO, Dave Davis, and Google CEO, Sundar Pichai, urging the companies to protect the privacy of thousands of former Spirit employees.

The letter responds to the proposed $10 million sale of Spirit’s internal data to Google for the purpose of training artificial intelligence systems. Court findings revealed that the proposed sale would include approximately 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages, employee records, timecards records, payroll and tax information, and employment contracts. Workers created and provided this information as a condition of their employment, and it may contain highly sensitive details, including medical information and accommodation requests.

“This sale presents uncharted territory,” wrote the legislators. “Innovation should not come at the expense of workers’ privacy or the confidentiality of information they were required to provide as a condition of employment. The unprecedented scale and sophistication of modern artificial intelligence make it particularly important that privacy protections keep pace with the technology.”

Sen. Cantwell and her colleagues called for no employee-related information to be transferred until protections are in place to ensure that workers’ sensitive information cannot be identified, profiled, or misused.

The letter also warned that removing names, email addresses, and other direct identifiers does not necessarily make a dataset anonymous, particularly when modern AI systems can identify patterns across large datasets and connect seemingly unrelated pieces of information. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has recognized that de-identified data can be re-identified in certain circumstances.

The legislators urged the companies to initiate an independent review and create enforceable restrictions governing the use of sensitive employee information.

Sen. Cantwell was joined by Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and 108 House members in co-signing the letter. Several unions have also expressed their support for the letter.

title: Cantwell Helps Dedicate New Visitor Center & Plaza at Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial
text:
Cantwell Helps Dedicate New Visitor Center & Plaza at Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial

In 1942, 227 Japanese Americans living on Bainbridge Island were the first Americans to be forcibly removed & interned during WWII; In 2008, Congress passed Cantwell’s legislation designating location as a National Historical Site; Sunday’s ceremony marks the final stage in a decades-long project to complete the memorial site

BAINBRIDGE, WA – Today, U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA) joined survivors of Japanese American internment, members of their families, leaders of the Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial Association (BIJAEMA), and members of the National Parks Service for a dedication ceremony of a new visitor center and plaza at the memorial.

"A difficult and shameful chapter, but that is exactly why this site is so important -- it serves to acknowledge and memorialize the wrongs committed here in the name of national security, and to help educate future generations. It will stand as an enduring symbol of what should never happen again," Sen. Cantwell said.

"On this very site, March 30th, 1942, American citizens of Japanese descent were stripped of their civil liberties, stripped of their property, stripped of their community, and their freedoms, based on nothing more than their heritage and appearance. It [was] a clear violation of their constitutional rights and our values as Americans," she continued. "We see the same injustices being implied in immigration policy and federal policies that target and exclude based on heritage and appearance. So, today's [new] visitor center and the exhibition will remind all of us that exclusion is wrong. It will explain what happened here, and commit to never letting it happen again."

Bainbridge was the first internment site nationwide where Japanese Americans were forcibly removed and incarcerated under President Franklin D. Roosevelt's Executive Order 9066 following Japan’s attack on Pearl Harbor during World War II. On March 20, 1942, 277 Japanese Americans were gathered on the Eagledale Ferry Dock to be sent to Manzanar Relocation Center in California and later Minidoka Relocation Center in Idaho. In all, 12,892 residents from Washington state were sent to detainment camps.

In 2006, Sen. Cantwell and then-Representative Jay Inslee (D, WA-01) spearheaded legislation that granted National Historical Site status to the Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial. This legislation was signed into law in 2008.

In 2010, Sen. Cantwell and Rep. Inslee visited the memorial for a tour and to celebrate a $183,000 National Park Service grant they helped secure that year for the memorial’s education wall.

Between 2022 and 2023, Sen. Cantwell helped secure $767,102 in National Park Service funding through the Japanese American Confinement Sites grant program to help complete the Visitor Center. The new Visitor Center represents the final major phase of the Memorial’s more than two-decade development.

The center includes permanent interpretive exhibits, historic artifacts, educational space accommodating up to 75 participants, an outdoor amphitheater and plaza, and improved accessibility.

title: Senator Collins, Bipartisan Group of Senators Issue Joint Statement Opposing Imports of Russian Diesel
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins joined a bipartisan group of senators, including Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Thom Tillis (R-NC) and John Curtis (R-UT) in issuing the following statement opposing Russian diesel fuel imports to the United States:

“Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine. Congress was clear: The U.S. should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our NATO Allies.

“President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law. The Administration has also failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course.”

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody and Governor DeSantis Join Local Leaders in Recovery Efforts Following Direct Strike from Hurricane Isaias
text:
Senator Moody joined Gov. DeSantis at his briefing at a Milton Waffle House and will be attending another briefing with Gov. DeSantis at Grayson Beach State Park later this afternoon.

PENSACOLA, Fla. — Today, U.S. Senator Ashley Moody joined Governor Ron DeSantis for multiple stops across Northwest Florida to assess damage and observe ongoing disaster recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias.

“Isaias was a major hurricane, and it will take time to rebuild what was destroyed. Floridians are resilient and I am committed to working alongside Governor DeSantis to make sure communities that suffered damage have the resources needed to recover. Every level of government was prepared for Isaias, and now every level of government is fully engaged in supporting recovery,”said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Moody was on the ground with Governor DeSantis Friday morning in Pensacola for a pre-landfall briefing, urging residents in the path of the storm to complete preparations quickly, fortify their homes, and follow directions from local officials. “We will weather this storm together,” she said at the time.

Today, Senator Moody and Gov DeSantis stopped at a Waffle House in Milton and will be holding a briefing at a damaged roadway where recovery operations were actively underway.

President Trump approved the emergency declaration requested by Governor DeSantis, following Senator Moody’s letter to the Administration prior to hurricane Isaias making landfall.

Senator Moody continues to coordinate closely with federal partners, including FEMA, to help ensure timely assistance reaches impacted communities. Her office can assist Floridians navigating federal agencies—submit requests at Moody.Senate.Gov or call toll-free in Florida at 866-630-7106.

For additional storm resources and recovery tips, visit Senator Moody’s Storm webpage at Moody.Senate.gov/Storm-Preparation.

During her time in the U.S. Senate, Senator Moody helped recover billions in FEMA public assistance for Florida communities recovering from prior storms and advanced the TRACK Act to improve transparency in the recovery process.
