title: Murphy on Face the Nation: Americans Should Be Furious at Trump's Spiraling Crisis in the Middle East
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, on Sunday joined Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan. In the immediate aftermath of Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia, which killed at least 12 people, including an American citizen, and injured at least 300 others, Murphy discussed how the Trump administration’s incompetence and short-sightedness has destabilized an entire region.

Fresh from his own Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to Doha, Qatar and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Murphy also discussed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s cover-up of the costs and impact associated with the Iran war, as well as the Trump administration’s broader failure to protect American troops and American military bases. Murphy’s full readout is available here and on Substack.

Drawing from what he witnessed in the region on his recent CODEL, Murphy laid out the full, devastating picture of Trump’s failed war with Iran: “I was in that airport the day before, having visited the Saudis and the Qataris, who are trying to negotiate an end to the war. I mean, listen, what I saw on the ground is a war that is spiraling out of control. You have a dozen dead. A full-blown new war between the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. You have the Iranians restarting their missile programs. They never, we never eliminated their drone program. They're restarting their nuclear program. Gas prices are at $6 in some states… Gas prices, diesel prices, food prices through the roof. 20 Americans dead. $100 billion spent. If the Trump administration was trying to lose this war, they couldn't do worse than they are doing. This is a humiliation to the United States. The war is getting bigger and more dangerous, not smaller and more limited.”

Murphy blasted Hegseth’s attempts to cover up the war’s damage and stressed that Congress cannot support more funding for the war until transparency is restored and sustained: “There is a cover-up underway to try to hide from the American public the cost of this war and the debacle that it has caused in the region. So, how could we assess whether we want to rebuild these facilities if the administration is denying us the ability to see them or even to understand the scope of the damage? I mean, the blockage of basic congressional oversight responsibilities here is absolutely egregious.”

Murphy explained why the only remaining avenue to protect American troops in the Middle East is an immediate end to the war: “The best way to support our troops and our people in the region is to end this war, to unilaterally end American hostilities, and to frankly ask our partners in the region to do the work of reopening the Strait and reopening the Red Sea… the president is saying that he is considering after the election going back to war with Iran, and so of course Iran's response to that is going to be an escalation of the war… This is a president who is showing just humiliating levels of incompetence in war making, and escalation is just going to bring more misery for the American taxpayers and for people who live in that region.”

He also pointed out that Donald Trump’s gross incompetence in warmaking has resulted in billions of dollars of wasted taxpayer money: “Donald Trump was so fundamentally unprepared for this war that within days of the war starting, our billion-dollar air bases and naval bases in the region were obliterated by the Iranians. Every single American should be furious about that, not just because Americans died, but because their taxpayer dollars at scale were wasted. And so, yes, we should reconsider whether we should rebuild them if we can't protect them. And this president is incapable of protecting our people in the Middle East.”

A full transcript of the interview is available below. A full video of the interview is available here.

Brennan: Yesterday there were 309 people injured, 12 killed, including one American, in this attack on the airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. President Trump said the U.S. both may join strikes, but also that the U.S. is talking to the Houthis-that's the Iran-backed group that carried out this strike, do you support retaliation? And do our Saudi partners, who you were just visiting, deserve the American support?

Murphy: Yeah, I was in that airport the day before, having visited the Saudis and the Qataris, who are trying to negotiate an end to the war. I mean, listen, what I saw on the ground is a war that is spiraling out of control. You have a dozen dead. A full-blown new war between the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. You have the Iranians restarting their missile programs. They never, we never eliminated their drone program. They're restarting their nuclear program. Gas prices are at $6 in some states.

Brennan: They’re restarting their nuclear program?

Murphy: There's evidence of that at one of the primary sites in which we think they are digging underground. They are restarting nuclear research activities. Gas prices, diesel prices, food prices through the roof. 20 Americans dead. $100 billion spent. If the Trump administration was trying to lose this war, they couldn't do worse than they are doing. This is a humiliation to the United States. The war is getting bigger and more dangerous, not smaller and more limited. And it's an advertisement for every single member of the House and the Senate who voted for this war, who continues to support this war, to be booted out of office this November.

Brennan: But in regard to this particular strike, the U.S. has not committed to retaliating on our partners, the Saudis' behalf. Do you think that would be appropriate?

Murphy: No, I don't think the United States should go to war in Yemen. I mean, this administration is absolutely incompetent in war making, and so just as we have made the Middle East worse and more chaotic by getting involved in a war against Iran, we would simply escalate and make the situation even more dangerous if we then went to war not only with Iran but with the Houthis in Yemen as well.

Brennan: Well, in many ways, there's this argument about U.S. credibility in the region and continued presence. The Congressional Budget Office says it's unable to estimate the cost of damage to American bases because the Pentagon hasn't provided the information, and the extent of rebuilding is unclear. The extent is unclear because the intent is unclear, and some Democrats have even said they want to shrink the U.S. presence. I believe you also favor drawing down the U.S. military presence. Are you going to vote to rebuild the installations you saw that were damaged?

Murphy: Well, I didn't see any installations. I mean, that that's the issue: is that we have-

Brennan: I thought you saw the embassy.

Murphy: Well, I saw the embassy, but the most expensive rebuild would be of the naval base in Bahrain and our air base in Qatar, and right now members of Congress are being denied the ability to see the damage at these bases because there is a cover-up underway. There is a cover-up underway to try to hide from the American public the cost of this war and the debacle that it has caused in the region. So, how could we assess whether we want to rebuild these facilities if the administration is denying us the ability to see them or even to understand the scope of the damage. I mean, the blockage of basic congressional oversight responsibilities here is absolutely egregious.

Brennan: You said that you had evidence shared with you of possible rebuilding of Iran's nuclear program. Was that a classified briefing? Was that a briefing that the administration did share with you?

Murphy: No, that's open source reporting: that the Iranians are are potentially starting to dig deeper to rebuild some of the capacities in Pickaxe Mountain.

Brennan: Okay, because the Pentagon does say they need additional funds for the war we are currently in with Iran. How do you balance the political statement and the intent to end [the war] against the question of whether we are supporting and protecting our people who are still in the region?

Murphy: Yeah, the best way to support our troops and our people in the region is to end this war, to unilaterally end American hostilities, and to frankly ask our partners in the region to do the work of reopening the Strait and reopening the Red Sea. The reality is, so long as the potential continues-

Brennan: Just walk away?

Murphy: Well, the president is saying that he is considering after the election going back to war with Iran, and so of course Iran's response to that is going to be an escalation of the war. The president needs to bring this war to an end, and that will be the quickest way that the waterways will be reopened. Again, this is a president who is showing just humiliating levels of incompetence in war making, and escalation is just going to bring more misery for the American taxpayers and for people who live in that region.

Brennan: Just to put a fine point on it, I mean the Iranians want the U.S. to withdraw from the region. Do you favor a drawdown of U.S. troops from the region?

Murphy: Well, I think the United States is always going to have to have a presence in that region. But let's just be honest: we don't have a naval base any longer in Bahrain. We don't have an effective base in Qatar because, minutes into the war, the Iranians took those bases out. So, at the very least, if we're going to rebuild any capacity in that region, we're going to have to find a way to protect it. Donald Trump was so fundamentally unprepared for this war that within days of the war starting, our billion-dollar air bases and naval bases in the region were obliterated by the Iranians. Every single American should be furious about that, not just because Americans died, but because their taxpayer dollars at scale were wasted. And so, yes, we should reconsider whether we should rebuild them if we can't protect them. And this president is incapable of protecting our people in the Middle East.

Brennan: The Pentagon did disclose yesterday 20 fatalities, American fatalities.

Murphy: Extraordinary.

Brennan: I want to ask you a bit about politics. Our CBS polling shows Republicans they do have perhaps a turnout problem compared to Democrats, but when it comes to perception, 58% of registered voters polled by CBS say they view the Democratic Party as weak. What is the affirmative Democratic message other than we're not Trump?

Murphy: Well, I mean, listen, we are in the middle of a war that is a disaster for the American people. I mean, people can't afford food; they can't afford to fill their gas tank. Farms are going bankrupt at a record rate. So, I mean, let's just be honest: the the most important thing that the American people are thinking about right now is getting these people out of power because this has been a disaster for the world, for America's reputation, and for the economy.

But yes, I think we need to be bold in our ideas and our proposals for how we're going to fix this mess. And so we should promise that if we win this election, we are not going to fund this war, right? We're not going to approve money for the Department of Defense without a commitment from the Trump administration that this war ends. We're going to take on this corruption - not just Trump's corruption, but the entire corruption of the federal government. If you elect us, we're going to work to get billionaire and corporate and anonymous money out of politics. To the extent that people see us as weak, I think historically it's been because our ideas haven't been big enough, our tactics haven't been bold enough. And yes, in the closing days of this campaign, we can promise people: if you elect us, we are going to take on his corruption, we are going to end this war, and that, supplemented with the higher prices and the debacle of the war with Iran, I think could result in a landslide.

Brennan: You're hitting the trail, as I understand it. North Carolina, Florida, Michigan, Minnesota. You're going to help out one of our other guests in New Hampshire. But let me ask you about the Florida decision. The Senate candidate Angie Nixon there has aligned herself with Democratic socialists over the summer. Does that give you pause at all, or when you talk about big ideas, is that the kind of big idea you want to endorse?

Murphy: Well, I also think we should just be a big tent, right? There's, I think, a pretty big difference between Chris Pappas in New Hampshire and Angie Nixon in Florida. And if we want to win elections, we should welcome people who have a diverse set of ideas into the party. The people of Florida-

Brennan: But then you got to govern!

Murphy: Well, the people of Florida will decide, right, right, whether they want Angie Nixon or whether they want Senator Moody, who has basically said nothing about the growing, massive corruption scandals in this administration. But as a party, I think we should welcome a lot of different people with a lot of different ideas in, and then let the voters decide.

Brennan: Senator Murphy, thank you for your time today.

Murphy: Appreciate it.

title: Doggett: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Violates the Law
text:
Sponsor of 2022 Russian Energy Import Ban Says Trump Rewards Putin While Blaming Zelensky

WASHINGTON, D.C.—U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), a longtime champion of cutting off Russian energy revenue whose name is on the 2022 Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act (Public Law 117-109), today said President Trump's deal with Vladimir Putin to allow Russian diesel into the United States directly violates that law.

On Friday, after a Trump call with Putin, the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued General License 135, authorizing the sale, delivery, offloading, and “importation into the United States” of Russian diesel through April 7, 2027.

“In 2022, my name was on the first law banning Russian fossil fuel imports to deny Putin funding for his brutal invasion of Ukraine,” said Rep. Doggett. “Now Trump is directly violating that law, lifting sanctions to permit the first Russian diesel imports into the United States since the law took effect, without satisfying the specific legal conditions it requires. He illegally rewards his pal Putin while once again blaming Zelensky for not capitulating to Putin. Meanwhile, every day Putin murders more Ukrainian civilians.”

What the law requires

The Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act passed the House 413–9 and the Senate unanimously, and was signed into law on April 8, 2022. It bans the importation of all Russian energy products classified under chapter 27 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, which includes diesel.

The law permits the President to end the ban only by certifying to Congress that Russia has:

reached an agreement to withdraw its forces and end hostilities that is accepted by Ukraine's government;

ceased to pose an immediate military threat to any NATO member; and

recognized the right of the Ukrainian people to freely choose their own government.

The President must first consult with the Ways and Means, Foreign Affairs, Finance, and Foreign Relations Committees and submit a report at least 45 days before certifying. Any termination takes effect only after 90 days, during which Congress may enact a resolution of disapproval. None of these steps has occurred, and none of the conditions has been met.

Bipartisan concern

Rep. Doggett's concerns are shared across party lines. A bipartisan group of senators has recognized the illegality of Trump’s action. On NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday, Senator Thom Tillis (R-NC) said there is “a legitimate case for saying the president's not following the law” and warned that the deal will put American lives at risk, citing the Kremlin's ties to Iran. Former Vice President Mike Pence called lifting the sanctions a betrayal of the late Senator Lindsey Graham's legacy.

The deal comes weeks after President Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law, and only weeks after he publicly called on President Zelensky to stop Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel infrastructure, blaming Ukraine rather than the war with Iran for high fuel prices.

title: Congressman Don Davis Joins Congressional Ferry Caucus to Advocate for Eastern North Carolina’s Coastal Communities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced he has joined the Congressional Ferry Caucus. As a member of the caucus, he will join 17 of his colleagues to focus on federal investment in our nation's ferry system.

"Ferries in eastern North Carolina's coastal communities are essential. They connect kids to school, residents to doctor visits, and workers to their jobs," said Congressman Don Davis. "As a new member of the bipartisan Congressional Ferry Caucus, my focus is to advocate for more federal investment in the ferry system so that coastal communities can remain connected."

The State of Washington operates the largest ferry system in the nation, and North Carolina's ferry system follows as the second-largest.

There are a total of seven scheduled ferry routes that link eastern North Carolina communities. Ferries provide access to basic needs and necessities, support the local economy through tourism and trade, and are still a significant part of their daily lives. Ferry transportation is vital to our residents and businesses along the coast.

Representatives Emily Randall (WA-06), Nick Begich (AK-AL), John Garamendi (CA-08), and Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) are the founding members of the caucus, which was created in June 2025 to raise awareness in Washington, D.C., of our nation's ferry system among Congressional members and their staff.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts AAPI Roundtable in Palisades Park
text:
Above: Gottheimer hosts AAPI Roundtable.

PALISADES PARK, NJ —Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable with Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) leaders and community members from across North Jersey at the Palisades Park Library to discuss the challenges facing the AAPI community and what Washington can do to help. Joined by local elected officials, community organizations, educators, health care advocates, small business owners, and cultural and ethnic associations, Gottheimer outlined his work on health care, affordability, small business, anti-Asian hate, public safety, immigration, and education, and heard directly from participants about what their neighbors need most.

“The AAPI community represents different ethnicities, languages, faiths, and traditions, but the same drive to strengthen our communities. That’s why I’m working so hard in Washington and across the aisle to support you. But celebrating this community isn’t enough,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).

Across the Fifth District, roughly 127,000 residents are Asian American, or about one in six. This includes nearly half of Englewood Cliffs and more than forty-three percent of Fort Lee. Palisades Park, which has the highest percentage and density of Korean residents of any town in the country, is located within the District.

Gottheimer, a member of the Korea, India, Taiwan, Asia Pacific American, and Pacific Islands Caucuses and Co-Chair of the American Sikh Congressional Caucus, discussed the following priorities and his relevant legislation with attendees:

Mental Health Emergency Care: Gottheimer secured $2 million to expand the behavioral health emergency department at New Bridge Medical Center in Paramus, growing it from 19 to 49 beds, with 30 beds dedicated to mental health and substance abuse treatment and 50 new clinical jobs. He is also part of the bipartisan push to extend and reform the ACA enhanced premium tax credits.

Affordability: As Co-Chair of the bipartisan SALT Caucus, he is pushing the SALT Deductibility Act to fully restore the SALT deduction. His Tariff Impact Act would require the Congressional Budget Office to review the economic impact of any new tariff before they take effect.

Medicaid and CHIP: New restrictions on lawfully present immigrants, part of the OBBB law that he voted against, recently took effect. Roughly 300,000 New Jersey residents could lose Medicaid or fail to get it, mostly because of paperwork.

Small Business: Under a policy that took effect March 1, 2026, the SBA no longer backs loans to businesses with any non-citizen ownership. Even a green card holder with a 1 percent stake disqualifies a business. In FY2024 alone, the agency backed 8,900 loans worth $7.2 billion to Asian-owned businesses.

Anti-Sikh Hate: Gottheimer introduced the Sikh American Anti-Discrimination Act with Congressman David Valadao (R-CA) in January 2026. It would create a DOJ Task Force on Anti-Sikh Discrimination, set a federal definition of anti-Sikh hate, develop education programs, and report annually to Congress. New Jersey is home to roughly 100,000 Sikhs.

Public Safety: Gottheimer announced $42 million in FEMA funding in July 2026, split between $21 million statewide and $21 million for Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties. It covers radios, drones, K-9 units, and security upgrades for houses of worship such as cameras, alarms, guards, and reinforced doors. His bipartisan Invest to Protect Act would authorize $50 million a year for five years to help police departments with fewer than 200 officers with recruitment, training, mental health resources, and body cameras. He invited houses of worship that have not applied for Nonprofit Security Grants to call his office.

Immigration: More than 1.2 million people are stuck in the employment-based green card backlog, nearly eighty percent from India, with a projected 179-year wait for an Indian EB-2 applicant. He voted to eliminate the per-country caps on employment-based green cards and says the country can secure the border and enforce its laws while treating people fairly.

ICE Oversight: Gottheimer introduced the ICE Standards Act in January 2026, after the Minneapolis shootings. It would require stronger training, body and dash cameras, clear uniforms and ID, efforts to verify citizenship before detention, and limits on enforcement at schools, hospitals, and houses of worship. He also visited Delaney Hall and worked to secure the release of a 17-year-old girl, Ariadna, in time for her high school graduation.

Education: Gottheimer discussed the administration’s freeze of $23 million in English learner funding for New Jersey and cancellation of nearly $1 billion in school mental health grants. He supports doubling the Pell Grant and pointed to the roughly $5 billion the American Rescue Plan he helped write, negotiate, and pass in 2021, and delivered to Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions. He also introduced a resolution recognizing AANAPISI Week.

Gottheimer was joined by Assemblywoman Ellen Park, Chair of AAPI Caucus, Assemblywoman Shama Haider, Assemblyman Al Barlas, Mayor of Palisades Park Chong Paul Kim, Mayor of Harrington Park Joon Chung,Yogi Virk, President of the Sikh Chamber of Commerce, Daniel Song, Palisades Park County Committee Member, Closter Councilman Christopher Cho, Palisades Park Councilman Charlie Changkyun Shin, Mahwah Councilwoman Michelle Crowe Paz, Englewood Cliffs Councilman Philip Zhi Liang, River Edge Councilwoman Priti Dhariwal, Sara Kim, Senior Director of Public Health and Research Center at Korean Community Services NY & NJ, Teresa Baik, Director of Education of Korean Community Services NY & NJ, Farhat Khan, President of the Cultural Society of Bergen County, Palisades Park Councilman Christopher Kwak, Eun Ju Hong, President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Tom Choi, Vice President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Jae-eun Ahn, Vice President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Christina Kim, with the Fort Lee Fire Prevention, Serena Pak, Director of the Youth Council of Fort Lee, Hyunjung Kim, Advisor of ComposTogether at the Youth Council of Fort Lee, Harrington Park, Ludi Hughes, Chairwoman of Asian American Heritage Council of NJ and Chairwoman/Founder of the Filipino American Festival, Inc, Amber Reed, Co-Executive of AAPI of New Jersey, John Sohn, President of the Korean American Nail Assocation of NJ, Ellen Jeon, Executive Director and Advisor of the Asian American Youth Council, Anne Y. Kim Cha, President of the Korean American Senior Citizens Association of NJ, Donald Yu, Vice President of the Korean American Senior Citizens Association of NJ, Ella Chorong Lee, Library Director of the Palisades Park Public Library.

title: Deadline to Apply for a Nomination to a U.S. Service Academy One Month from Today

title: Kean Holds Roundtable to Address Childhood Mental Health
text:
(October 12, 2026) BRIDGEWATER, NJ – Last week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) hosted a community roundtable at the Bridgewater Township Municipal Building to discuss childhood mental health in coordination with the reintroduction of the Healthy Minds for a Better Future Act.

The Healthy Minds for a Better Future Act would establish a task force at the Department of Education and the Department of Health and Human Services focused on middle school mental health.

“We must do everything we can to support the mental health of our children,” said Congressman Kean. “As a father, I understand that a parent’s greatest priority is ensuring their child’s well‑being. I was grateful for the opportunity to host this roundtable and bring together local leaders, parents, and school staff to hear directly about the challenges students face today. Conversations like these help us identify meaningful ways to support middle school students so they can thrive both academically and emotionally.”

“Our children are growing up in a world that presents challenges many of us never had to face at their age,” said Bridgewater Mayor Matthew Moench. “Between social media, online bullying, and the pressures of everyday life, too many young people are struggling in silence. As parents, educators, and community leaders, we have a responsibility to make sure every child knows they are valued, supported, and never alone. I appreciate Congressman Kean's leadership in bringing attention to this important issue and working toward solutions that put the well-being of our children first.”

“As a middle school parent and Wait Until 8th supporter, I believe protecting our children’s mental health means giving them time to grow without the pressures of smartphones and social media,” said Wait Until 8th Advocate Lauren Becht. “Schools can be powerful partners by supporting families who choose to delay, teaching students to recognize and navigate online pressures, and making mental health resources easy for families to find. Just as important, children need to feel safe asking for help when they need it. I appreciate Congressman Kean bringing parents into this conversation and focusing on the well-being of our middle schoolers.”

“Youth mental health requires a community-wide commitment. As a parent of three and with experience of serving as a member of the Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School Board, as well as serving on the board of nonprofit organizations, I understand the importance of supporting children during these pivotal years,” said Bridgewater-Raritan School District Board of Education and United for Impact Board Member Lucy Li. “Congressman Kean’s bill is an important step toward turning that commitment into action, and I encourage an approach that brings together schools, families, faith and cultural organizations, nonprofits, and other community partners to provide coordinated, accessible support. At United for Impact, we believe strong community connections are essential to youth well-being and prevention, and we welcome the opportunity to help build partnerships that extend support within and beyond the classroom and make a lasting difference in children’s lives.”

“As a New Jersey-certified school counselor, I chose this career because I recognized the growing need for mental health support in our schools and wanted to be part of the solution,” said New Jersey Certified School CounselorNisha Ali. “School counselors do far more than provide individual and group counseling; we work closely with families, administrators, and Child Study Teams to help students navigate challenges, heal from trauma, and succeed both academically and emotionally. As concerns surrounding student mental health and safety continue to grow, we must advocate for more school counseling positions in every district across New Jersey to ensure that all students receive the support, resources, and care they need to thrive.”

title: CNMI Native Cecilia Lizama Salvatore Champions Pacific Heritage
text:
We are proud to see Saipan native Dr. Cecilia Lizama Salvatore featured in the Field Museum’s Talk Story: Pacific and Filipino Voices in the Museum in Chicago. Dr. Salvatore has dedicated her career to preserving Pacific Island cultural heritage and ensuring that Indigenous communities have a voice in how their histories are documented and shared. She has served as a professor and coordinator of the Archives and Cultural Heritage Program at Dominican University, collaborated with the Field Museum on its Pacific Islands collection, and serves on the inaugural Board of Directors of IPIKU, a partnership focused on Marianas and Micronesian heritage. She earned her Ph.D. in Library and Information Sciences from the University of Texas at Austin and, in 2000, was honored by the CNMI Legislature as the first Chamorro woman from the CNMI to earn a Ph.D. from UT Austin. Her accomplishments continue to make the Commonwealth proud. If you’re in Chicago, we encourage you to check out this special conversation on October 27 from noon to 1:15pm at the Field Museum. title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Make Abusers Pay for Suing Survivors Into Silence
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C., (Oct. 12, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced the Speak Your Truth Act, legislation to protect survivors from perpetrators who use defamation lawsuits to silence them.

Under the bill, a survivor who prevails in a defamation or libel case brought against them in federal court would be entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, paid by the plaintiff. The protection covers factual statements, made without malice, about sexual assault, sexual harassment, or discrimination the speaker personally experienced. This includes workplace harassment and discrimination, retaliation for reporting or opposing it, and harassment or discrimination by the owner of a housing authority accommodation. It applies to cases filed in or removed to federal court.

“Survivors should never have to choose between their voice and their bank account,” said Congresswoman Mace. “If you are a survivor telling the truth about what happened to you, the last thing you should fear is being bankrupted by the person who hurt you for telling it. Too often, abusers use the courts as a weapon. They file the lawsuit, run up the legal bills, and wait for survivors to go away. The Speak Your Truth Act changes the math. Sue a survivor for telling the truth and lose, and you pay. The truth is not defamation.”

Defending a defamation suit can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. Many survivors stay silent rather than risk it. The Speak Your Truth Act puts the cost of a failed suit where it belongs: on the person who filed it.

Professor Victoria Burke, Esq., of Southwestern Law School, an attorney and advocate who has worked to end the use of retaliatory defamation lawsuits to silence survivors, provided the following statement in support of the bill:

"As the architect of the Speak Your Truth Act nationwide movement, I have witnessed firsthand how protecting survivors transcends political divisions. Already enacted in five states with bipartisan support, this legislation reflects a simple principle: survivors deserve to be heard, not silenced. I am especially grateful to Congresswoman Nancy Mace for bringing this legislation to Congress. A survivor herself, she understands the threat of retaliatory defamation lawsuits firsthand. After courageously speaking out about her own experience, she faced a defamation lawsuit. Her experience underscores precisely why these protections are so urgently needed,” said Burke.

Burke also pointed to the Epstein files vote as evidence of why survivors need these protections.

“We saw Democrats and Republicans unite in an overwhelmingly bipartisan vote to release the Epstein files. Yet even on Capitol Hill, brave Epstein survivors feared naming their alleged abusers because of the threat of retaliatory defamation lawsuits. No survivor should fear being sued into silence for speaking about sexual abuse. The Speak Your Truth Act seeks to change that by protecting survivors who speak out in good faith from weaponized defamation lawsuits. Every survivor deserves the freedom to speak their truth,” added Burke.

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELERATES VIRGIN ISLANDS-PUERTO RICO FRIENDSHIP DAY

U.S. Virgin Islands—Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett joins our local community in celebrating Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Weekend, culminating today on Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Day. The holiday honors the deep and enduring bonds of family, culture, and shared history between the people of the U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico. “The Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico are bound by far more than the waters between us,” said Congresswoman Plaskett. “From enslaved Africans who escaped the Danish West Indies to find freedom in Puerto Rico, to Puerto Ricans who came to our islands in the early 1900s to cut cane and seek opportunity, to the families who live, work, and worship across our shores today, we share a common thread of resilience, culture, food, faith, and kinship. On this Friendship Day and Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we are reminded that as people of color, telling our own stories is essential. When we tell them with truth and pride, we preserve our history, strengthen our unity, and ensure our children know who they are.”

title: Rep. Salinas and Tualatin Celebrate New Hydropower System Turning Drinking Water Into Clean Energy
text:
Tualatin, OR — The City of Tualatin is celebrating the completion of a first-of-its-kind hydropower project that allows the city’s drinking water to create clean, renewable energy. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) joined city leaders, representatives from Oregon’s Department of Energy and project partners, including Energy Trust of Oregon and Portland General Electric (PGE), to mark the completion of the 56-kilowatt in-pipe hydropower system at the Tualatin City Services facility. The project is expected to generate more than 270,000 kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity each year — enough to fully power the City Services facility and save the city an estimated $26,000 each year.

“Building a more affordable future demands innovative ideas. That’s exactly what Tualatin is doing with their new in-pipe hydropower project,” said Rep. Salinas. “Adding clean energy like hydropower to our water systems and solar to our homes and buildings can help bring down energy costs and combat the affordability crisis. Projects like this show how communities can create clean energy by making the most of the infrastructure we already rely on. Strong local partnerships and federal support can help make more of these projects possible.”

Along with the system, the city also installed additional infrastructure that will eventually help keep operations running during major outages or emergencies. In the future, the city plans to add a microgrid and large battery capable of powering critical municipal buildings on its own.

“Building a more resilient Tualatin is central to our climate action plan,” said Frank Bubenik, mayor of Tualatin. “This project shows how we can use innovative infrastructure to strengthen reliability and lay the groundwork for future backup power. It’s the kind of smart investment that can improve reliability, reduce energy costs and help protect our community for the long term.”

The system is installed where drinking water from Bull Run Reservoir enters Tualatin’s water distribution system. Developed by Oregon-based InPipe Energy, the system captures unused pressure to generate 24/7 carbon-free electricity without interrupting water delivery.

Energy Trust of Oregon, a nonprofit funded by customers of investor-owned utilities’ that helps communities, organizations, and families connect to clean, renewable energy provided more than $270,000 in cash incentives for the project and supported the project’s design.

Across Oregon, Energy Trust is working with cities, water districts and rural communities to turn critical municipal infrastructure into new sources of reliable, local clean energy. Renewable energy projects — whether hydropower, solar or battery-supported systems — help communities cut energy costs and strengthen resilience in the face of climate-related challenges.

“When cities are willing to explore innovative ideas, they can unlock far more value from the infrastructure than they already have,” said Tracy Scott, director of energy programs with Energy Trust of Oregon. “This project will generate renewable power while helping Tualatin reduce its energy costs year after year, leaving more resources available for other community priorities. That’s the kind of practical, lasting value we’re looking to help communities achieve.” This project was also partially funded by PGE’s Green Future Renewable Development Fund, which is made possible by PGE Green Future customers who support impactful small-scale local renewable energy projects.

“It’s the incredible support of PGE customers who are helping bring local clean energy projects like this one in Tualatin to life,” said PGE local government affairs senior manager, Meredith Armstrong. “Through our Green Future program, PGE customers are choosing to support impactful renewable energy projects for healthier and more energy resilient communities.”

These funds were combined with a grant from the Oregon Department of Energy and an anticipated federal investment tax credit. Altogether, grants, incentives and anticipated tax credits covered more than 85% of the project’s $920,000 total cost.

The environmental benefits of this project extend beyond energy generation. The area surrounding the turbine was replanted and landscaped to meet Backyard Habitat Certification Program standards, using native, wildlife-friendly plants to create habitat for pollinators and wildlife. The Backyard Habitat Certification Program is a collaboration between Columbia Land Trust and Bird Alliance of Oregon.

As the City continues implementing its Climate Action Plan, Tualatin’s project demonstrates how communities can use existing infrastructure to generate clean energy, reduce costs and advance climate goals. It’s an example of how local innovation and strong partnerships can create lasting benefits for the community.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Introduces Resolution to Protect Christopher Columbus Monuments on Columbus Day
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) on Columbus Day, introduced a resolution supporting the preservation and protection of statues and monuments honoring Christopher Columbus, including the historic Columbus Monument in Syracuse, New York.

Tenney’s resolution recognizes the historical and cultural significance of Columbus monuments and the communities that built and maintained them. The Columbus Monument in Syracuse was funded by working class Italian immigrants, many of whom faced discrimination and persecution, and was dedicated in 1934 as a testament to their heritage and contributions to the city. The resolution condemns efforts to remove the Syracuse monument, supports preserving Columbus statues and monuments for future generations, and reaffirms the importance of protecting American history as the United States celebrates the 250th anniversary of its founding.

“History is our collective memory, and tearing down monuments does not change or erase the past,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “The Columbus Monument in Syracuse represents generations of hardworking Italian Americans who overcame discrimination, built strong communities, and made lasting contributions to our state and nation. Preserving our history does not mean ignoring its complexities or pretending that historical figures were perfect. It means understanding our past, learning from it, and ensuring future generations can do the same. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, we should preserve these important pieces of our shared history and continue building on the promise of our great nation.”

title: NEW: Trump Threatens Survival of Initiative Baldwin Created to Support American Dairy
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) is demanding the Trump Administration reverse course on a policy that threatens to shut down the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative, a program Senator Baldwin created to help small- and medium-sized dairy businesses expand their product line and diversify their revenue streams. On September 30, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) rolled out a new unattainable requirement that the four Dairy Business Innovation Initiative Centers, one of which is in Wisconsin, provide a 25 percent match for federal funding. All four centers – through which DBII funding is awarded – have warned they do not have the capital to comply with this requirement, threatening their ability to provide grants to family farms and small dairy businesses.

“By requiring each Dairy Business Innovation Center to provide a match that Congress never intended and centers do not have the resources to meet, USDA is threatening the program’s survival and the success of the farmers and producers that it supports,” wrote Senator Baldwin in a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This new financial hurdle comes at a time when dairy farmers are already struggling financially with fewer market opportunities and record-high fuel prices amid President Trump’s trade war and war in Iran. I urge USDA to reverse this new requirement and ensure that the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives may continue providing a lifeline for dairy farmers and processors when they need it most.”

Last month, USDA issued the Fiscal Year 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity to the four Dairy Business Innovation Centers in Wisconsin, Vermont, Tennessee and California, and for the first time, attached a new requirement that the centers provide a 25 percent cash match—up to $1 million from each center—in order to receive federal funds that support dairy businesses. The centers have indicated they do not have the capital available to meet this new matching requirement, putting the future of the program at risk. This comes after the Trump Administration chose to freeze funding for the program in early 2025. USDA finally released funds after Baldwin demanded they restart payments that had already been awarded to farmers.

In her letter, Senator Baldwin requested that USDA reissue the Notice of Funding Opportunity for the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives without the new matching requirement. Senator Baldwin also highlighted how this new requirement comes as President Trump’s war in Iran and tariffs are jacking up the cost of diesel, fertilizer, and transportation for Wisconsin farmers.

“The Administration’s decision to put new barriers in the way of assistance for dairy farmers comes when they can afford it the least. Wisconsin farmers do backbreaking work to produce world-class products that feed the world. The President came into office promising to support our farmers but instead has taken every opportunity to make their livelihoods increasingly more difficult. Between the trade war and unnecessary war in Iran, Wisconsin farmers are paying more for everything. I request that the Administration reverse course on this decision,” Senator Baldwin concluded.

DBII is a lifeline for dairy farmers and processors, providing direct farm technical assistance, business consulting, strategic planning, marketing, product development, and distribution. DBI centers have awarded more than $106 million in grants to 911 dairy businesses since 2019. Additionally, a significant portion of Dairy Business Innovation funds are dedicated as small-dollar grants to small- and medium-sized, family-owned businesses. Senator Baldwin successfully created the DBI Initiatives through the Dairy Business Innovation Act in 2018, which passed as part of the 2018 Farm Bill.

“Many dairy farmers and processors are struggling to make it right now, faced with soaring fuel prices, the volatility of trade and tariffs, and a labor shortage. They need the support Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives provide now more than ever – and they know that adding a cost-share provision to the program will end it,” said Rebekah Sweeney, Wisconsin Cheese Makers Association senior director of programs and policy. “We are grateful Sen. Baldwin is giving voice to this concern, and we urge every member of Congress to work to see this provision removed – and full funding restored.”

Full text of the letter can be found here.

Dear Secretary Rollins,

I am writing to raise serious concerns about the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) newly imposed matching requirement on the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives (DBII), which threatens to undermine a proven resource of funding that supports dairy farmers and processors in Wisconsin and across the country. By requiring each Dairy Business Innovation Center to provide a match that Congress never intended and centers do not have the resources to meet, USDA is threatening the program’s survival and the success of the farmers and producers that it supports. This new financial hurdle comes at a time when dairy farmers are already struggling financially with fewer market opportunities and record-high fuel prices amid President Trump’s trade war and war in Iran. I urge USDA to reverse this new requirement and ensure that the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives may continue providing a lifeline for dairy farmers and processors when they need it most.

Last month, USDA issued the Fiscal Year 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity to the four Dairy Business Innovation Centers in Wisconsin, Vermont, Tennessee and California, and for the first time, attached a new requirement that the centers provide a 25 percent cash match—up to $1 million from each center. USDA indicated in their notice that the agency would only accept cash and would refuse any in-kind contribution, such as technical assistance, to meet the requirement. The centers do not have the capital available to meet this new matching requirement, putting the future of the program at risk. Congress has consistently supported the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives on a bipartisan basis and has provided funding for the program without requiring centers to provide a cash match. By imposing this new requirement, USDA is adding a financial condition that Congress never intended and that could effectively bring a successful, bipartisan program to an end.

I request that USDA reissue the Notice of Funding Opportunity for the Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives without the new matching requirement. These initiatives are a lifeline to dairy farmers and processors in over 40 states by providing direct farm technical assistance, business consulting, strategic planning, marketing, product development, and distribution. Additionally, a significant portion of Dairy Business Innovation funds are dedicated as small-dollar grants to small- and medium-sized, family-owned businesses. These dairy businesses provide job opportunities in rural communities and help their economies thrive.

The Administration’s decision to put new barriers in the way of assistance for dairy farmers comes when they can afford it the least. Wisconsin farmers do backbreaking work to produce world-class products that feed the world. The President came into office promising to support our farmers but instead has taken every opportunity to make their livelihoods increasingly more difficult. Between the trade war and unnecessary war in Iran, Wisconsin farmers are paying more for everything. I request that the Administration reverse course on this decision

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

title: Senator Collins, Pentagon Announce Second Guided-Missile Destroyer to Be Built at BIW
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins, Chair of the Appropriations Committee, announced that the Pentagon has certified Bath Iron Works’ (BIW) production capacity, clearing the way for the Department to order an additional guided-missile destroyer (DDG) to be built at BIW in Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27).

Senator Collins has consistently advocated for two ships in the FY27 budget to send a steady production signal to the shipyard, including in her comments on the President’s Budget Request and questioning of Navy officials in Appropriations hearings.

Read the announcement:

Following a comprehensive, multi-phase due diligence review, the Pentagon has determined that significant operational and managerial improvements at General Dynamics Bath Iron Works (BIW) have established the capacity and stability necessary to support the potential construction of a second guided-missile destroyer (DDG).

The Department’s thorough review evaluated production throughput, schedule adherence, quality assurance benchmarks, supply chain resilience, and workforce optimization at the Bath, Maine shipyard. Based on verifiable performance enhancements and leadership initiatives implemented across the facility, the Department concluded that building an additional Arleigh Burke-class (DDG 51) destroyer at BIW is feasible and strategically advantageous for the Navy's fleet, should Congress secure the necessary funding.

“Our national security requires an industrial base that can respond to demands for increased speed and volume,” said Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. “After a rigorous review, Bath Iron Works has proven it has the capacity and stability to support construction of a second destroyer. While the operational improvements we have seen at BIW are a significant step in the right direction, the shipyard must continue this momentum to fully resolve legacy production challenges – sustained performance is essential. The Department will continue to partner with contractors who prioritize execution, accountability, and the rapid modernization of our forces.”

“Today’s decision by the Department validates the capacity of Bath Iron Works (BIW) and the hard work of its highly skilled 6,800 employees who build the best ships in the world. I have advocated for a second destroyer to be included in this year’s budget, and I worked with the Administration during its careful review and repeated visits to BIW to verify the ability of the shipyard to construct another ship while continuing to complete its current workload,” said Senator Susan Collins. “This certification will help keep our Navy strong and support BIW as a steady source of good-paying Maine jobs. I will continue to work to ensure our shipbuilders have the resources to meet the Navy’s needs at a time when China is relentlessly expanding its fleet.”

The decision to certify the shipyard's capacity for a second destroyer aligns with the Administration’s broader, aggressive campaign to revitalize the U.S. Maritime Industrial Base and outmatch global pacing threats. To counter aggressive ship-construction timelines by foreign adversaries, the Department is prioritizing long-term stability and capacity-building across the domestic shipbuilding supply chain.

Through targeted modernization investments, workforce development initiatives, and streamlined procurement processes, the Administration is actively expanding America's sovereign shipbuilding capacity. Ensuring that key shipyards like Bath Iron Works can reliably scale and sustain high-rate production is a cornerstone of the Department’s strategy to maintain global maritime dominance and protect American interests worldwide.

title: Heinrich Leads Resolution Recognizing Indigenous Peoples’ Day
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) led the introduction of a resolution to recognize the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples’ Day, celebrating the rich histories, unique cultures, and lasting contributions of Indigenous Peoples across the United States.

The resolution also supports the official designation of Indigenous Peoples’ Day as a federal holiday. Indigenous Peoples' Day is currently celebrated on the second Monday of October in over 200 municipalities and 17 states, including New Mexico.

“Since time immemorial, Native people have called the land we now know as New Mexico and the United States home. Their histories and legacy deserve enormous respect. That is why I am proud to continue leading the effort in the Senate to mark the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples’ Day.

“I have the honor of working with the 23 Tribes and Pueblos in New Mexico, as well as with Tribal Nations across Indian Country. What I hear from Tribal leaders is consistent and clear: the federal government must step up and uphold its treaty and trust responsibilities, respect Tribal sovereignty, and stop attacking the programs and resources that Tribal members rely on. I wholeheartedly agree.

“As we recognize Indigenous Peoples’ Day, today and every day, let us honor the rich history, cultures, and contributions of Tribal Nations and Native people — and stand shoulder to shoulder with Tribes to ensure their languages, traditions, and cultures continue to be passed down to future generations.”

The resolution is cosponsored by U.S. Senators Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Angus King (I-Maine), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.).

The resolution is endorsed by the National Congress of American Indians (NCAI), Pueblo of Acoma, Alaska Federation of Natives, National Council of Urban Indian Health (NCUIH), Navajo Nation, All Pueblo Council of Governors (APCG).

title: ICYMI: Senator King and Mark Hertling Warn America’s Military Posture Is Putting Global Stability at Risk
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — In an opinion piece published in the New York Times today, U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME) joined retired U.S. Army Lieutenant General and former Commander of the U.S. Army in Europe, Mark Hertling, arguing the White House and Pentagon are putting global stability at risk. In the article, King and Hertling further argue that weakening our military readiness and casting doubt on our commitment to allies raises the risk of a larger war against adversaries like Russia, China, and others.

“The problem of escalating instability, unfortunately, is not confined to Europe’s eastern frontier. The danger of war between America’s autocratic adversaries and our democratic allies is rising around the world for one simple, troubling reason: The enemies of liberal democracy increasingly think America is weak and fickle,” wrote King and Hertling. “That perception is based in no small part on the current administration’s inexplicable abandonment of the strategy that kept the peace in much of the world during the Cold War: deterrence. The basic approach to defense that emerged from the cataclysm of World War II was simple: If you strike us, we will respond so overwhelmingly that your country will be decimated, so you’d better not start anything. With the development of nuclear weapons, this concept was neatly captured by the unfortunate phrase “mutually assured destruction.”

They continued, “A similar deterrent is buttressed by our worldwide structure of alliances. Forward bases, mutual defense pacts, intelligence sharing and economic cooperation together have provided an enormous asymmetric advantage over China and Russia, neither of which has many friends, let alone allies.”

“The grave danger we now face is that the current administration has undermined both prongs of deterrence strategy in different theaters — a lack of will in Ukraine and a lack of capacity in Iran,” King and Hertling concluded. “…Deterrence works only if it’s credible, and the actions of the administration over the past two years — in spite of all the bluster about lethality and testosterone — have severely compromised that credibility, and with it, the safety and security of our country.”

As a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC), Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Strategic Forces, and the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence (SSCI), Senator King is recognized as an authoritative voice on national security and foreign policy issues, including on the importance of the deterrence strategy. In June 2026, he supported provisions in the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 that strengthen support for Ukraine and counter Russia and invest in Maine’s shipbuilding to ensure American destroyers are built in American shipyards – all notable improvements to American deterrence. Additionally, in a previous SSCI hearing, King emphasized the importance of establishing and clearly communicating an effective cybersecurity deterrence policy.

You can read the full opinion piece here or below.

+++

Lethality and Testosterone Will Get Us Only So Far

By Angus King and Mark Hertling

Mr. King is an independent U.S. senator from Maine. Mr. Hertling was a three-star general in the U.S. Army.

Enemy drones over Romania. Wayward missiles in Poland. Sabotage in Germany. Every week brings some new Russian provocation as President Vladimir Putin steps up his efforts to divide Europe and undermine support for Ukraine. As Western militaries scramble to respond, the prospect of the war spilling over into NATO territory rises.

The problem of escalating instability, unfortunately, is not confined to Europe’s eastern frontier. The danger of war between America’s autocratic adversaries and our democratic allies is rising around the world for one simple, troubling reason: The enemies of liberal democracy increasingly think America is weak and fickle.

That perception is based in no small part on the current administration’s inexplicable abandonment of the strategy that kept the peace in much of the world during the Cold War: deterrence.

The basic approach to defense that emerged from the cataclysm of World War II was simple: If you strike us, we will respond so overwhelmingly that your country will be decimated, so you’d better not start anything. With the development of nuclear weapons, this concept was neatly captured by the unfortunate phrase “mutually assured destruction.”

Although principally associated with the nuclear standoff with the Soviet Union, deterrence also underlay our longtime strategy for avoiding a conventional conflict with a near-peer adversary like China or Russia. Rather than mutually assured destruction, this kind of deterrence works by America’s maintaining a sufficiently strong conventional force that any potential adversary will realize the futility of attacking us or our allies.

The challenge to this strategy at its inception in the 1950s was that aggressors rarely attack their potential victims all at once, but rather one at a time, usually proclaiming their ambitions are limited. Hitler started with the Sudetenland and Czechoslovakia and only then went on to Poland, Belgium and France. Mr. Putin has started with Ukraine.

To counter this problem and the very real threat of Soviet expansionism after World War II, NATO’s Article 5 established the principle that an attack on one member state would be considered an attack on all — and such an attack would be met with a combined response from the European countries and the United States.

A similar deterrent is buttressed by our worldwide structure of alliances. Forward bases, mutual defense pacts, intelligence sharing and economic cooperation together have provided an enormous asymmetric advantage over China and Russia, neither of which has many friends, let alone allies.

Deterrence worked: Although the United States has been involved in regional conflicts over the past decades, there has been no direct military confrontation between the major powers on the scale of the two world wars.

But two of this strategy’s essential elements — capacity and will — are now in short supply. The potential adversary has to believe that the United States and its allies have the weapons and forces to hold them at risk, and, just as important, that we have the will to use that force when necessary. The effectiveness of deterrence depends entirely on what the adversary believes; if either our capacity or our will is in doubt, deterrence fails and catastrophe becomes more likely.

The grave danger we now face is that the current administration has undermined both prongs of deterrence strategy in different theaters — a lack of will in Ukraine and a lack of capacity in Iran.

By essentially abandoning Ukraine, we have gutted the “will” prong. The Europeans have stepped up, but our absence has sent the unmistakable signal to President Xi Jinping of China and to Mr. Putin that we don’t have the stomach for a prolonged conflict. This is the opposite of deterrence; it is closer to an invitation.

Moreover, just as Mr. Putin is probing Eastern Europe, the Pentagon is reducing active American troop levels in Germany and pulling back on rotational deployments to Eastern Europe. This sends a clear signal that we are indifferent to Russian aggression beyond Ukraine: again, precisely the wrong message at precisely the wrong time.

Iran has offered Mr. Putin and Mr. Xi a tutorial in our tactics and the limitations of our military power. After seven months of on-again, off-again bombing and an economic blockade, virtually none of the strategic goals announced at the beginning of the war have been achieved, while our stock of munitions has been severely degraded and our regional bases have been exposed as vulnerable.

Similarly, our 52 days of attacks on the Houthis in Yemen last year seem to have done little to diminish their capacity to put shipping in the Red Sea at risk. Iran and the Houthis are much lesser powers than China or Russia, and Mr. Putin and Mr. Xi will judge accordingly their chances against our air defenses, offensive capability and economic power in any future conflict.

It won’t be easy to regain what we have lost, but there are several places to start. One is to re-engage in the defense of Ukraine, including by vigorous enforcement of the just-passed Russia sanctions bill. Another is to reverse the misguided withdrawal of our forces in Eastern Europe, thus sending the message to Mr. Putin that Article 5 is alive and well. And finally, we should quit undermining our allies if we want them there when we need them.

Deterrence works only if it’s credible, and the actions of the administration over the past two years — in spite of all the bluster about lethality and testosterone — have severely compromised that credibility, and with it, the safety and security of our country.

Angus King is an independent U.S. senator from Maine who serves on the Senate Armed Services Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence; Mark Hertling is a retired U.S. Army Lieutenant General and a former commander of the U.S. Army in Europe.

title: Amo Highlights Rhode Island’s Blue Economy at Roger Williams Oyster Farm and Hinckley Yacht Services
text:
Bristol, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) continued his 2026 Blue Economy Tour today with visits to Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities and Hinckley Yachts’ expanded Portsmouth facility, highlighting the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy.

At Roger Williams, Amo toured the shellfish farm, hatchery, and research labs with faculty and researchers to discuss advances in shellfish production, aquaculture, and blue biotechnology, as well as opportunities to prepare students for careers in the Blue Economy. They also discussed federal policies to support aquaculture, fisheries, and environmental conservation. At the newly expanded Hinckley Yachts facility in Portsmouth, Amo met with workers and discussed the skilled trades and maritime jobs that keep Rhode Island moving.

“Rhode Island’s Blue Economy means cutting-edge research, skilled jobs, and businesses building the future right here in the Ocean State,” said Congressman Gabe Amo. “At Roger Williams, researchers are advancing aquaculture and blue biotech. At Hinckley, skilled workers are building and servicing world-class yachts. I’m looking forward to bringing what I learn on this tour back to Washington to help inform how to grow these industries, create opportunities for Rhode Islanders, and protect our ocean.”

“We were pleased to welcome Congressman Gabe Amo to Roger Williams University as a stop on his Blue Economy Tour. At RWU, marine research, hands-on student learning, and partnerships with Rhode Island’s aquaculture industry come together to address real-world challenges facing our coastal communities,” said Margaret Everett, Provost, Roger Williams University.” Touring our Marine and Natural Sciences building and CEED facilities offered an opportunity to showcase how university research and education support a sustainable blue economy and help prepare the next generation of marine science professionals.”

"CEED’s research, education, and collaborations support a thriving, sustainable aquaculture industry in Rhode Island. With our industry partners, we’re advancing aquaculture technology and blue biotechnology, while preparing the next generation of professionals to address challenges facing our coastal ecosystems,” said Koty Sharp, Director, Roger Williams University Center for Economic & Environmental Development. “We’re excited to share with Congressman Amo how university research can power our state’s growing Blue Economy.”

“Hinckley is investing in our flagship Portsmouth yard to create a premier facility that reinforces Rhode Island’s leadership in the marine trades and reflects the craftsmanship at the heart of our business,” said Peter Clark, Chief Development Officer, Hinckley Yachts. “By modernizing the yard and enhancing the working environment, we aim to attract the next generation of marine trades talent while providing our highly skilled team with opportunities to build rewarding, long-term careers.”

Background

Congressman Amo kicked off his 2026 Blue Economy Tour with a visit to REGENT Craft, where he helped cut the ribbon on their new electric Seaglider factory.

Rhode Island’s Blue Economy directly employs 36,000 Rhode Islanders and contributes over $5 billion to the state’s gross domestic product every year.

In 2024, Congressman Amo toured Rhode Island’s First Congressional District to highlight the Ocean State’s leadership in the Blue Economy across labor, education, business, and defense.

title: Ansari Leads 74 House Democrats in Demanding Answers on Civilian Deaths in Iran
text:
WASHINGTON – Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), and Jason Crow (CO-06) led 74 House Democrats in demanding answers from Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on a September 1 strike at a wedding in Kuhestak, Iran, that reportedly killed five civilians, including two children, and injured dozens. The lawmakers demand a full account of the strike and answers about the broader pattern of civilian harm resulting from Trump’s U.S. military operations in Iran, including whether U.S. forces were responsible and what steps the Department is taking to prevent further civilian casualties.

In their letter, the lawmakers write, “We are once again writing with grave concern regarding the conduct of the Administration’s war in Iran. Specifically, there are devastating reports of civilian casualties at a wedding in the town of Kuhestak, Iran, on September 1, 2026. This is the latest in an alarming pattern of civilian casualty incidents in strikes carried out by the United States in Iran since the war began on February 28, 2026.”

They further state, “The Post reported that six U.S. Navy aircraft-launched weapons targeted a communications complex near the home where the wedding was taking place and that one weapon missed its intended target. Accordingly, we demand urgent answers regarding the United States’ role in this strike, why the strike proceeded given the clear risk of significant civilian harm, and what steps the Department is taking to prevent further civilian casualties in Iran.”

Ansari’s letter is co-signed by Representatives Gabe Amo (RI-01), Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Becca Balint (VT-AL), Ami Bera (CA-03), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Greg Casar (TX-35), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Jim Costa (CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Jason Crow (CO-06), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Christopher Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Bill Foster (IL-11), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús García (IL-04), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Al Green (TX-09), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Henry Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), William Keating (MA-09), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), James McGovern (MA-02), Gregory Meeks (NY-05), Analilia Mejia (NJ-10), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Grace Meng (NY-06), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Dave Min (CA-47), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Joe Neguse (CO-02), Eleanor Norton (DC-AL), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Maxine Waters (CA-43).

Read the letter below.

Dear Secretary Hegseth,

We are once again writing with grave concern regarding the conduct of the Administration’s war in Iran. Specifically, there are devastating reports of civilian casualties at a wedding in the town of Kuhestak, Iran, on September 1, 2026. This is the latest in an alarming pattern of civilian casualty incidents in strikes carried out by the United States in Iran since the war began on February 28, 2026. While the Department has not publicly acknowledged responsibility for this incident, the Washington Post recently reported that there is a “high likelihood” that the U.S. was responsible for the incident, citing an official familiar with the operations. Furthermore, analysis from U.S. weapons experts has suggested that the explosion was caused by a U.S. glide bomb.

The Post reported that six U.S. Navy aircraft-launched weapons targeted a communications complex near the home where the wedding was taking place and that one weapon missed its intended target. Accordingly, we demand urgent answers regarding the United States’ role in this strike, why the strike proceeded given the clear risk of significant civilian harm, and what steps the Department is taking to prevent further civilian casualties in Iran. The consequences of this American strike have been devastating: 5 civilians were killed as a result of the strike in Kuhestak, including a 4-year-old boy and a 16-year-old boy, and dozens of civilians were injured.

This incident is regrettably among the latest in a string of civilian casualty incidents arising from the U.S.-led war in Iran. This includes a strike at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran, on the first day of the war that killed a reported 175 civilians, including 120 children. While it has been reported that a preliminary investigation by the Department found that the U.S. military was responsible for the strike, over six months later the Department has still not publicly acknowledged responsibility for the strike nor released the findings of its investigation. Similarly, reporting and independent analysis indicate that U.S. forces were responsible for a strike at a youth sports hall in Lamerd, Iran, that killed 21 civilians, including 7 children, on February 28. While the Department has denied responsibility, analysis by weapons experts found that the damage pattern is consistent with that of an American Precision Strike Missile (PrSM).

We are deeply alarmed by the continued pattern of civilian casualties resulting from U.S. operations in the war in Iran, and the apparent lack of action and accountability from the Department. Acknowledging such incidents, accepting responsibility, and learning from them makes our forces stronger, more effective, and an example to the world. When we fail to do so, it has the exact opposite effect.

This is why it is all the more alarming that amid these devastating incidents, the Department has also severely degraded the civilian harm mitigation and response (CHMR) programs and personnel designed to prevent, respond to, and learn from civilian harm. Understanding the civilian environment – including the location of civilian objects and critical infrastructure such as schools and gymnasiums, and patterns of life including large gatherings such as weddings – was intended to be a key aspect of this program. Yet CHMR staff at CENTCOM have reportedly dwindled from over 10 to just one full-time staff. The Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, which was mandated by Congress and designed to support combatant commands in this lifesaving work, has been cut from over thirty down to just seven.

On March 12, 2026, 121 Members of the U.S. House of Representatives wrote to you demanding answers regarding civilian casualties caused by Operation Epic Fury and the Department’s civilian protection efforts. The Department refused to provide any answers, simply stating “The United States Central Command (USCENTCOM) has initiated an investigation of this incident and appointed an investigating officer from outside the USCENTCOM chain of command. USCENTCOM will share the results of this investigation with Congress once it is completed.”

Nearly seven months into the war, Congress and the American public still lack basic information about the findings of that investigation and the measures the Department has taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring again.

The strike in Kuhestak makes that failure all the more troubling. In response to the reports regarding U.S. responsibility for the strike in Kuhestak, a spokesperson for the U.S. Central Command stated “The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.” Similarly, Vice President Vance said at a press briefing recently that he was “skeptical” of reports that the U.S. was responsible for the bombing, while acknowledging that the incident was under investigation. We are concerned this lack of transparency from this Administration is becoming a pattern, given the Department also initially denied responsibility for the Minab strike and has yet to release the investigation related to that incident.

The American people deserve answers on not just this strike, but the Department’s pattern of civilian harm resulting from U.S. military operations in Iran. To that end, we insist on answers to the following questions no later than October 26, 2026.

Did U.S. forces carry out the September 1, 2026 strike in Kuhestak, Iran, that killed 5 civilians and injured dozens? If so, what was the target and why was the decision taken to execute the strikes? What was the assessed civilian harm risk of the strikes, and what steps were considered or taken to prevent civilian harm?

Has the Department formally initiated an investigation into the September 1 strike in Kuhestak? If so, please provide the date on which the investigation began, the office responsible for conducting it, whether the investigating officer is independent of the operational chain of command, and the expected timeline for completion.

What is the status of the USCENTCOM investigation into the February 28 strike at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab? On what date will the Department provide Congress with the full findings of that investigation, including its conclusions regarding U.S. responsibility and the circumstances that led to the reported civilian casualties? On what date will the unclassified version of these findings be made available to the public?

Did the Department conduct an initial review of whether it is possible the U.S. was involved in the Lamerd strike on February 28, 2026? What were the results of that initial review? Was additional information provided after the fact, and did this alter the initial review results at all?

Did the Department conduct a civilian harm assessment of whether it is more likely than not that civilian harm occurred as a result of this strike? What were the results of this assessment? Was additional information provided after the fact, and did this alter the initial review results at all?

Has the Department conducted an administrative investigation, such as an AR 15-6, into the strike? If so, when was the investigation initiated, when are the findings due to the commander, and when will its findings be provided to Congress and released publicly?

What steps, if any, has the Department taken to prevent civilian harm in targeting practices since the apparent U.S strikes in Minab on February 28, 2026? Please detail any specific policies that have been implemented.

How many U.S. investigations, initial reviews, and civilian harm assessments into civilian casualties arising from operations in Iran have been initiated since February 28, 2026 and how many have been completed? Please provide details of all ongoing and completed investigations.

Sincerely,

Yassamin Ansari

Member of Congress

Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.gov to learn more.
