title: Congressman Baird Introduces Bill to Establish U.S.-Sudan Natural Resources Partnership to Protect Civilians in Region
text:
Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04) introduced H.R. 10795, the Sudan IMPACT Act, to establish an agricultural and minerals partnership between the United States and Sudan, tied to Sudanese improvements in civilian protection.

The Sudan Investing in Minerals, Partnership, Agriculture, Commerce, and Trade (IMPACT) Act would provide American agricultural and mining equipment, technology, and expertise in exchange for Sudanese natural resources. The partnership is contingent upon the U.S. Secretary of State determining that Sudan has demonstrated significant progress in civilian protection, political stability, and responsible management of natural resources.

“Sudan’s civil war is devastating lives and holding back its future. Economic opportunity could play a major role in helping the Sudanese people build a more peaceful and prosperous country, but protecting civilians must come first,” said Congressman Baird.

“Sudan’s mineral resources could help expand the supply of materials we use in technologies that Americans rely on every day, like phones and cars, while creating opportunities for the Sudanese. This legislation offers a path toward greater economic cooperation with the United States, provided Sudan’s government shows real progress in protecting its people,” Baird added.

The partnership could include farm equipment, precision agriculture and irrigation technology, agricultural processing equipment, mining and geological surveying technology, and assistance to improve mine safety and environmental cleanup.

title: Congressman Biggs Takes Action to Fight Medicaid Fraud Across the United States
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA – Congressman Andy Biggs (AZ-05) co-sponsored H.R. 10636, the Medicaid Fraud Prevention Act, legislation requiring states to strengthen their efforts to identify and combat fraud, waste, and abuse in their Medicaid programs.

Under the legislation, states would be required to conduct a comprehensive Medicaid fraud risk assessment at least once each year. The assessments would identify and rank the most significant fraud, waste, and abuse vulnerabilities, estimate the amount of taxpayer dollars potentially at risk of improper expenditure, evaluate the effectiveness of existing program integrity tools, and identify gaps in data sharing, oversight, and enforcement.

The legislation follows a recent warning from the Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that Arizona was one of eight states reporting “zero fraud referrals and overpayments recovered in Medicaid managed care.” The Administrator gave the states “30 days to double-check their numbers and make sure oversight is happening on the ground.”

The warning adds to growing concerns about Arizona’s oversight of federal taxpayer dollars.

Earlier this year, Gustav Chiarello, Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, informed Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs that the state had failed to comply with the federal Single Audit deadline for four consecutive fiscal years. States receiving federal funding, including Medicaid dollars, are required to submit annual audits examining financial reporting and compliance with federal requirements. Continued failure to meet those requirements could jeopardize Arizona’s eligibility for certain federal HHS funding. Arizona’s overall Medicaid improper payment rate is estimated to be over six percent.

“For far too long, governments at every level have allowed a festering culture of fraud and waste of monumental proportions across the United States,”said Congressman Biggs.“Government officials have a responsibility to be good stewards of taxpayer dollars and ensure that Americans’ hard-earned money is spent appropriately and protected from fraud. Unfortunately, under the current state administration, Arizona has been an unwilling participant in the critical effort to hold bad actors accountable and root out fraud wherever it exists.

“I’m pleased to co-sponsor the Medicaid Fraud Prevention Act to establish a clear baseline for states to identify fraud, recover improper payments, and correct deficiencies in their Medicaid programs. Arizona officials must take these responsibilities seriously. Taxpayers deserve accountability, and continued failures in oversight risk both federal funding and the public’s trust.”

title: Bilirakis Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Fix Medicare Advantage Payments in Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. Congressman Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12), joined by Representatives Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA-25), Darren Soto (D-FL), and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), have introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act. This bipartisan bill would correct a long-standing formula gap that underpays Medicare Advantage in Puerto Rico.

How it works: Medicare Advantage plans receive a fixed monthly payment from the federal government for each senior they enroll. Part of that payment is based on the local cost of care, which is measured by the average geographic adjustment (AGA). Puerto Rico's AGA is much lower than it should be. The formula relies on spending in traditional Medicare (fee-for-service), but very few beneficiaries in Puerto Rico use fee-for-service, since most are enrolled in MA. Basing the AGA on such a small population understates what care actually costs on the island, and MA plans receive a lower benchmark payment for each senior as a result.

This bill would set Puerto Rico's AGA equal to that of the U.S. Virgin Islands, a territory with similar socioeconomic circumstances, so that payments reflect the true cost of delivering care.

The problem

Over 680,000 Puerto Rico beneficiaries rely on Medicare Advantage, over 90 percent of all Medicare beneficiaries on the island.

Puerto Rico receives about 40 percent less per beneficiary than the U.S. average.

Benchmark rates run roughly 20 percent below those in the U.S. Virgin Islands.

The payment gap has led to smaller provider networks and reduced benefits, and doctors and hospitals absorb lower reimbursements. This threatens the quality and availability of healthcare services in Puerto Rico.

"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz and Soto in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers."

"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned."

“I am proud to join Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans," said Congressman Darren Soto.

“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández.

"I would like to thank my friend and former colleague, Gus Bilirakis, for introducing the Medicare Advantage Fairness Act in support of Medicare enrollees in Puerto Rico. Close to 680,000 Puerto Rico residents choose to receive their care through Medicare Advantage (MA), making it the preferred coverage option on the island. Yet MA rates in Puerto Rico are approximately 41% below the national average and 20% below those in the U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI). This bill proposes a fix that would adjust MA rates based on those in the USVI, providing a much-needed boost to our residents, health care sector, and economy. I look forward to continuing our work together in support of Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries in Puerto Rico and across our nation, " said Puerto Rico Governor Jenniffer González-Colón.

The legislation would create a self-adjusting link: if the U.S. Virgin Islands' adjustment changes, Puerto Rico's would move with it. It is a targeted fix for a formula that has never reflected the true cost of care on the island.

title: REP. BOEBERT BACKS PRESIDENT TRUMP'S DIESEL RELIEF MEASURES TO HELP COLORADO FAMILIES AND PRODUCERS
text:
LONE TREE, CO — U.S. Representative Lauren Boebert (R-CO) is backing President Trump’s diesel relief actions that put Colorado families, farmers, ranchers, and truckers first.

Red-Dyed Diesel Executive Order

President Trump’s executive order temporarily allows tax-free red-dyed diesel for broader use and defers the federal diesel excise tax through year’s end, delivering immediate savings for producers and families.

“These steps directly address affordability by putting money back in the pockets of Colorado producers and the families who rely on lower fuel and goods costs,” said Rep. Boebert. “Every dollar saved at the pump helps keep operations running and food moving.”

Diesel Supply Agreements

Europe / G7 Reserve Release: G7 release of 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from strategic reserves over four months to boost global supply.

Russian Diesel Supply Agreement: Agreement for the supply of diesel volumes to U.S. and global markets.

“I support strong pressure on Russia, but I will not sacrifice American prosperity for symbolism. Pragmatic deals that deliver for our people are how we win,” said Rep. Boebert.

“Sometimes deals aren’t perfect. Russia’s actions in Ukraine are wrong, but we cannot let American families keep getting squeezed while we hold out for a flawless outcome overseas. Temporary, targeted steps securing more diesel for the market are practical ways to help people in Colorado,” said Rep. Boebert.

What They Are Saying: President Trump Delivers Immediate Diesel Relief

Call to Suspend Diesel Exports

Rep. Boebert has also called for a temporary pause on U.S. diesel exports through January 2027, followed by a joint review by Congress and the Administration.

title: Ciscomani Named American Energy Champion
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani has been recognized as an American Energy Champion by the American Energy Alliance (AEA), achieving a perfect 100% score on the AEA’s American Energy Scorecard for the 119th Congress.

"Arizona thrives when we embrace an all-of-the-above energy approach that strengthens domestic production and keeps our energy supply reliable and affordable," said Rep. Ciscomani. "I'm honored to receive the American Energy Champion Award from the American Energy Alliance in recognition of my voting record supporting American energy. As the most bipartisan member of Arizona’s congressional delegation, I believe in working across the aisle to advance practical energy solutions that strengthen our infrastructure, protect consumer choice, and deliver results for Arizonans."

He has been a steadfast advocate of an all-of-the-above energy approach, consistently supporting efforts to strengthen domestic energy production, enhance grid reliability, and protect consumer choice. In addition, Ciscomani has championed critical investments in Southern Arizona’s energy infrastructure and helped advance policies that preserve local consumers' energy options.

The American Energy Alliance recognizes lawmakers who champion affordable, reliable energy, consumer choice, and market-driven policies.

"Energy is fundamental to our prosperity as a country, as individuals, families, and businesses, and energy policy can have real consequences. Never has the discussion of affordable, reliable energy been more important or more prevalent than it is now. As we approach elections this year, voters deserve factual information about what their elected officials are doing to ensure America’s energy security, keep energy prices down, and ensure grid reliability. The Scorecard gives constituents the opportunity to look beyond speeches and political rhetoric and evaluate lawmakers based on their actions. The American Energy Alliance applauds this year’s energy champions and thanks them for their leadership in prioritizing American energy," said AEA President Thomas Pyle.

Earlier this year, Representative Ciscomani played a pivotal role in securing nearly $700 million in federal support to modernize coal generation assets nationwide, a move that bolstered grid reliability and safeguarded energy access. Notably, the Arizona Electric Power Cooperative (AEPCO), operator of the Apache Generating Station, located approximately 80 miles east of Tucson, was awarded $20,826,000 through the U.S. Department of Energy. The Apache Generating Station remains a critical source of electricity for Cochise County, delivering power to homes, schools, hospitals, and businesses in Willcox, Benson, and rural communities across Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

In Congress, Representative Ciscomani is also a proud cosponsor of the Energy Choice Act (H.R. 3699), legislation that would prohibit state and local governments from restricting the connection, modification, or expansion of energy services based on the type or source of energy delivered. The bipartisan effort aims to further protect consumer choice and prevent unnecessary government interference in energy decisions for local households and businesses across Arizona. Representative Ciscomani also cosponsors the bipartisan Streamlining Home Installation of New Energies (SHINE) Act (H.R. 6981), legislation that would make local permitting for residential solar and other home energy systems more streamlined and affordable.

title: CORREA INTRODUCES BIPARTISAN BILL TO FREE INNOCENT PARTNERS FROM DEBT THEY DIDN'T CREATE
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Lou Correa (D-CA), alongside Congresswoman Laurel Lee (R-FL), introduced the bipartisan Bankruptcy Relief for Innocent Partners Act, which would ensure that people are not stuck with debt from fraud their partner committed alone, and that survivors of domestic and financial abuse are not forced to stay in dangerous relationships for financial reasons.

"If you didn't commit the fraud, you shouldn't carry the debt for the rest of your life," said Correa. "For a survivor of abuse, that debt can be a chain. Abusers use debt to control their partners and keep them from leaving. This bill removes one more chain."

“No one should be left responsible for debt caused by a partner’s fraud they neither knew about nor participated in,” said Laurel Lee. “For victims of domestic or financial abuse, being forced to bear the financial consequences of a partner’s wrongdoing can compound an already devastating situation. The Bankruptcy Relief for Innocent Partners Act is a matter of fundamental fairness. It provides meaningful relief for innocent individuals while ensuring our bankruptcy laws hold those who commit fraud accountable.”

The bill amends the Bankruptcy Code so that only the person who committed fraud is barred from discharging the resulting debt. Innocent partners would get the same fresh start as any other honest filer. The bill also protects survivors of domestic and financial abuse from being forced to stay in a relationship for financial reasons.

"NACBA strongly endorses this legislation because a person can be held legally responsible for someone else’s fraud without having committed fraud themselves. Bartenwerfer blurred that critical distinction in bankruptcy, allowing an innocent debtor to be saddled for life with a debt arising from misconduct they neither knew about nor could prevent. This bill would restore a simple rule: the extraordinary consequence of nondischargeability for fraud should follow the person who committed the fraud. It does not excuse wrongdoing or eliminate anyone’s underlying liability—it ensures that an honest debtor is not denied a fresh start because of someone else’s misconduct. We're grateful to Representative Correa and his colleagues on both sides of the aisle for taking it up," said Richard Nemeth, President, National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys (NACBA).

“Ninety-nine percent of domestic violence survivors experience economic abuse and half experience coerced debt. Beyond the hard costs, coerced debt creates an economic ripple effect by damaging credit, and preventing a survivor from accessing housing, employment and the basic resources needed to be safe. The Bankruptcy Relief for Innocent Partners Act would provide critical relief to domestic violence survivors who are burdened with debt through no fault of their own. By naming the fraud, this legislation will remove a substantial barrier to bankruptcy relief, offering a pathway to economic security and safety for domestic violence survivors across the nation,” said Erika Sussman, Founder & Executive Director, Center for Survivor Agency and Justice.

View the bill text here.

Background

In Bartenwerfer v. Buckley, a couple ran a house-flipping business together, and one partner committed fraud without the other's knowledge. After the couple filed for bankruptcy, the Supreme Court ruled that current law did not allow the innocent partner to discharge the fraud-related debt.

The issue is especially serious in abusive relationships. Half of domestic abuse survivors report experiencing "coerced debt," where abusers use debt to maintain control and limit their partners' economic resources.

title: Crow Presses Pentagon Over Civilian Casualties during Trump’s Iran War
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is demanding answers on a strike that resulted in civilian casualties at a wedding in Iran, reported to have been carried out by the U.S. military during Trump’s war of choice.

According to The New York Times, at least five people were killed, including two children, and nearly 70 more were injured while attending a wedding due to a military strike in the town of Kuhestak, Iran. Additional reporting indicates a high likelihood that the bomb used was launched by American forces as they carried out intense attacks in southern Iran.

Joining Crow in his letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth are Congresswomen Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ) and Sara Jacobs (D-CA). The group previously led their Democratic colleagues pressing the Administration for answers on a U.S. strike on an Iranian girls’ elementary school where at least 175 civilians, many of them children, were killed. The Pentagon has yet to provide a sufficient update on the incident.

“We demand urgent answers regarding the United States’ role in this strike, why the strike proceeded given the clear risk of significant civilian harm, and what steps the Department is taking to prevent further civilian casualties in Iran,” Crow and his colleagues wrote. “The consequences of this American strike have been devastating: 5 civilians were killed as a result of the strike in Kuhestak, including a 4-year-old boy and a 16-year-old boy, and dozens of civilians were injured.”

They continued, “We are deeply alarmed by the continued pattern of civilian casualties resulting from U.S. operations in the war in Iran, and the apparent lack of action and accountability from the Department. Acknowledging such incidents, accepting responsibility, and learning from them makes our forces stronger, more effective, and an example to the world. When we fail to do so, it has the exact opposite effect.”

Crow, Co-Chair of the Protection of Civilians in Conflict Caucus, has demanded answers on Secretary Hegseth’s attempts to dismantle civilian protections at the Pentagon.

Crow’s service as a combat veteran in Iraq and Afghanistan informs much of his work in Congress aimed at increasing civilian protection in combat. He helped pass legislation codifying the creation of the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, and has passed major portions of his Protection of Civilians in Military Operations Act and Department of Defense Civilian Harm Transparency Act.

A PDF of the letter can be found here, with full text appearing below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth,

We are once again writing with grave concern regarding the conduct of the administration’s war in Iran. Specifically, there are devastating reports of civilian casualties at a wedding in the town of Kuhestak, Iran, on September 1, 2026. This is the latest in an alarming pattern of civilian casualty incidents in strikes carried out by the United States in Iran since the war began on February 28, 2026. While the Department has not publicly acknowledged responsibility for this incident, the Washington Post recently reported that there is a “high likelihood” that the U.S. was responsible for the incident, citing an official familiar with the operations. Furthermore, analysis from U.S. weapons experts has suggested that the explosion was caused by a U.S. glide bomb.

The Post reported that six U.S. Navy aircraft-launched weapons targeted a communications complex near the home where the wedding was taking place and that one weapon missed its intended target. Accordingly, we demand urgent answers regarding the United States’ role in this strike, why the strike proceeded given the clear risk of significant civilian harm, and what steps the Department is taking to prevent further civilian casualties in Iran. The consequences of this American strike have been devastating: 5 civilians were killed as a result of the strike in Kuhestak, including a 4-year-old boy and a 16-year-old boy, and dozens of civilians were injured.

This incident is regrettably among the latest in a string of civilian casualty incidents arising from the U.S.-led war in Iran. This includes a strike at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran, on the first day of the war that killed a reported 175 civilians, including 120 children. While it has been reported that a preliminary investigation by the Department found that the U.S. military was responsible for the strike, over six months later the Department has still not publicly acknowledged responsibility for the strike nor released the findings of its investigation. Similarly, reporting and independent analysis indicate that U.S. forces were responsible for a strike at a youth sports hall in Lamerd, Iran, that killed 21 civilians, including 7 children, on February 28. While the Department has denied responsibility, analysis by weapons experts found that the damage pattern is consistent with that of an American Precision Strike Missile (PrSM).

We are deeply alarmed by the continued pattern of civilian casualties resulting from U.S. operations in the war in Iran, and the apparent lack of action and accountability from the Department. Acknowledging such incidents, accepting responsibility, and learning from them makes our forces stronger, more effective, and an example to the world. When we fail to do so, it has the exact opposite effect.

This is why it is all the more alarming that amid these devastating incidents, the Department has also severely degraded the civilian harm mitigation and response (CHMR) programs and personnel designed to prevent, respond to, and learn from civilian harm. Understanding the civilian environment – including the location of civilian objects and critical infrastructure such as schools and gymnasiums, and patterns of life including large gatherings such as weddings – was intended to be a key aspect of this program. Yet CHMR staff at CENTCOM have reportedly dwindled from over 10 to just one full-time staff. The Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, which was mandated by Congress and designed to support combatant commands in this life saving work, has been cut from over thirty down to just seven.

On March 12, 2026, 121 Members of the U.S. House of Representatives wrote to you demanding answers regarding civilian casualties caused by Operation Epic Fury and the Department's civilian protection efforts. The Department refused to provide any answers, simply stating “The United States Central Command (USCENTCOM) has initiated an investigation of this incident and appointed an investigating officer from outside the USCENTCOM chain of command. USCENTCOM will share the results of this investigation with Congress once it is completed.” Nearly seven months into the war, Congress and the American public still lack basic information about the findings of that investigation and the measures the Department has taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring again.

The strike in Kuhestak makes that failure all the more troubling. In response to the reports regarding U.S. responsibility for the strike in Kuhestak, a spokesperson for the U.S. Central Command stated “The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.” Similarly, Vice President Vance said at a press briefing recently that he was “skeptical” of reports that the U.S. was responsible for the bombing, while acknowledging that the incident was under investigation.We are concerned this lack of transparency from this Administration is becoming a pattern, given the Department also initially denied responsibility for the Minab strike and has yet to release the investigation related to that incident.

The American people deserve answers on not just this strike, but the Department’s pattern of civilian harm resulting from U.S. military operations in Iran. To that end, we insist on answers to the following questions no later than October 26, 2026.

Did U.S. forces carry out the September 1, 2026 strike in Kuhestak, Iran, that killed 5 civilians and injured dozens? If so, what was the target and why was the decision taken to execute the strikes? What was the assessed civilian harm risk of the strikes, and what steps were considered or taken to prevent civilian harm?

Has the Department formally initiated an investigation into the September 1 strike in Kuhestak? If so, please provide the date on which the investigation began, the office responsible for conducting it, whether the investigating officer is independent of the operational chain of command, and the expected timeline for completion.

What is the status of the USCENTCOM investigation into the February 28 strike at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab? On what date will the Department provide Congress with the full findings of that investigation, including its conclusions regarding U.S. responsibility and the circumstances that led to the reported civilian casualties? On what date will the unclassified version of these findings be made available to the public?

Did the Department conduct an initial review of whether it is possible the U.S. was involved in the Lamerd strike on February 28, 2026? What were the results of that initial review? Was additional information provided after the fact, and did this alter the initial review results at all?

Did the Department conduct a civilian harm assessment of whether it is more likely than not that civilian harm occurred as a result of this strike? What were the results of this assessment? Was additional information provided after the fact, and did this alter the initial review results at all?

Has the Department conducted an administrative investigation, such as an AR 15-6, into the strike? If so, when was the investigation initiated, when are the findings due to the commander, and when will its findings be provided to Congress and released publicly?

What steps, if any, has the Department taken to prevent civilian harm in targeting practices since the apparent U.S strikes in Minab on February 28, 2026? Please detail any specific policies that have been implemented.

How many U.S. investigations, initial reviews, and civilian harm assessments into civilian casualties arising from operations in Iran have been initiated since February 28, 2026 and how many have been completed? Please provide details of all ongoing and completed investigations.

title: Ezell Introduces Legislation to Modernize Marine Mammal Protection Act
text:
Congressman Mike Ezell (MS-04), Chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, introduced legislation to modernize the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) of 1972, improve regulatory certainty, and ensure federal permitting decisions are based on the best available scientific data.

The legislation would update requirements governing the incidental take of marine mammals during otherwise lawful activities, including maritime operations, infrastructure development, and other projects in coastal waters. By clarifying regulatory standards and streamlining the permitting process, the bill seeks to reduce unnecessary delays while maintaining protections for marine mammal populations.

“Along the Mississippi Gulf Coast, our maritime industry, ports, shipyards, and coastal communities depend on the ability to carry out critical projects without unnecessary federal red tape,” Ezell said. “We can protect our marine resources while also ensuring that federal regulations are grounded in sound science and common sense. This legislation brings much-needed clarity and predictability to the permitting process, helping support American jobs, strengthen our maritime industry, and keep important projects moving forward.”

"On behalf of the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources, I'm pleased to support these proposed modifications, which bring clarity and common sense reform to the Marine Mammal Protection Act without weakening its core function," General Spraggins, Director of the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources, said. "Replacing ambiguity with more explicit and defined standards will positively impact both the resources allocated for conservation related work and the marine resources in our waters."

"The introduction of this legislation represents an important step toward ensuring that MMPA implementation is guided by clear statutory standards and the best available science," Dustin Van Liew, EnerGeo Alliance SVP Global Policy, said. "We commend Congressman Ezell for his leadership in introducing language that reflects years of energy industry engagement and policy development aimed at improving regulatory certainty while maintaining robust protections for marine mammals."

Specifically, the legislation would:

Modernize the definition of harassment: Update the Marine Mammal Protection Act's definition of harassment to focus on actual injury or disturbance rather than the potential for those impacts.

Establish clearer scientific standards: Define a “negligible impact” based on whether an activity is reasonably likely to significantly and adversely affect the annual survival rate of a marine mammal species or stock.

Streamline incidental take authorizations: Remove certain statutory limitations on the duration and number of marine mammals covered by incidental take authorizations, providing greater flexibility and predictability for project planning.

Improve mitigation and monitoring requirements: Direct federal agencies to establish appropriate, practicable, and economically feasible conditions to minimize impacts on marine mammals, along with efficient monitoring and reporting requirements.

Prevent unnecessary project disruptions: Ensure conditions imposed through specified incidental take authorizations do not alter the basic design, location, scope, duration, or timing of an otherwise lawful activity.

Strengthen science-based decision-making: Require federal determinations under the Marine Mammal Protection Act to rely on the objective application of the best available scientific and commercial data, without precautionary assumptions that could bias those determinations.

The Marine Mammal Protection Act plays an important role in conserving marine mammal populations. However, its permitting requirements can also affect maritime construction, port improvements, offshore operations, and other activities important to coastal economies.

Ezell's legislation seeks to provide a more predictable regulatory framework that allows these activities to move forward while retaining federal oversight and requirements to minimize impacts on marine mammals.

As Chairman of the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee and Vice Chairman of the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries, Ezell has prioritized policies that support America's maritime capabilities, strengthen coastal economies, and promote responsible management of marine resources.

title: Fischbach, MN GOP Delegation Slam Walz for Rejecting Federal Fuel Relief and Leaving Minnesota Farmers and Families to Pay the Price
text:
WASHINGTON, DC - Congresswoman Fischbach (MN-07) led Minnesota's Republican Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to Governor Tim Walz following his refusal to align Minnesota with President Trump’s Executive Order authorizing highway use of red dye diesel. The letter calls on Walz to rethink his decision and follow suit to help lower diesel costs for Minnesota’s truckers, farmers, and drivers.

President Trump’s order opens access to untaxed, lower-cost red dye diesel, cutting per-fill costs by roughly $60 for a standard tank. By addressing state-level enforcement and fuel testing, Minnesota could have unlocked meaningful savings for farmers and haulers. While neighboring North Dakota took proactive steps to provide relief to its producers, Governor Walz flatly rejected any effort to lower costs, leaving Minnesota’s agricultural producers and truckers at a disadvantage during peak harvest season.

"Governor Walz and Democrats have made their priorities crystal clear: they would rather choose petty political opposition than give relief to struggling Minnesota families and farmers," said Rep. Fischbach. "President Trump provided a way to slash diesel costs, and Governor Walz chose partisan obstruction over lower costs. Our farmers are in the field working around the clock to feed and fuel our country. Instead of helping them, the Walz administration is threatening them with penalties for using lower-cost fuel. It is an insult to our rural communities, and it proves once again that Minnesota Democrats would rather watch fuel prices skyrocket to save their egos than give hardworking Minnesotans a break at the pump."

The letter also points out that North Dakota announced it will not enforce fuel checks or penalize drivers using red dye diesel on highways. Governor Walz’s refusal to follow Trump or North Dakota directly hurts Minnesotans. By forcing local haulers to buy higher-priced clear diesel, Minnesota is bottlenecking cross-state harvest commerce and driving up transportation costs that will be passed on to everyday consumers at the grocery store.

Congresswoman Fischbach vowed to continue fighting for energy affordability measures and called out state leadership for continually turning its back on Minnesota’s rural economy.

title: GRAY, PADILLA, SCHIFF DEMAND ANSWERS FROM ICE IN RESPONSE TO INCREASED ENFORCEMENT ACTIVITY IN MENDOTA
text:
Congressman Adam Gray (CA-13), Senator Alex Padilla, and Senator Adam Schiff are demanding answers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) following reports of increased enforcement activity and resident detentions in Mendota beginning on October 5.

In a letter to Acting ICE Director David Venturella, the lawmakers requested details about the operations’ purpose and scope, the number of individuals detained, and the safeguards in place to protect due process and minimize disruption to local families and businesses.

“Mendota is a hardworking agricultural community, and families should not have to fear going to work or taking their kids to school,” the lawmakers wrote. “Federal immigration laws must be enforced, but how that happens matters. We need answers about what’s taking place, who is being targeted and whether people’s rights are being protected.”

The letter emphasizes the importance of protecting public safety and due process while recognizing the essential role farmworkers play in the Central Valley economy and America’s food supply.

“The people of Mendota deserve to know why these operations are taking place and what safeguards are in place to protect their families and community,” the lawmakers wrote. “The federal government’s responsibility to enforce immigration law does not give it license to create fear across an entire community.”

title: Grothman: American Workers Should Come First in Their Own Country
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) introduced the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act, which would close an outdated loophole that allows H-1B dependent employers to bypass certain American worker protections. Senator Jon Husted (R-OH) has introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

“American workers should come first in their own country,” said Grothman. “Employers should not be able to use a salary threshold established nearly three decades ago to bypass protections for qualified Americans. There is no excuse for leaving this threshold unchanged when it should have been raised years ago. Washington’s failure to act shows how little the Establishment cares about unemployed Americans when employers want access to cheap foreign labor. This bill would update that threshold and help ensure American workers have a fair opportunity to compete for these jobs.”

“For decades, companies have been able to sidestep hiring American workers because of a salary threshold that hasn’t budged since 1998. That’s not modernization, that’s a loophole. This bill simply asks that when a company is heavily reliant on these visas and wants to bring in more H-1B workers, they shouldn’t be relying on an outdated law to get around offering these jobs to qualified American workers first,” said Husted.

Background Information

Under current law, H-1B dependent employers, companies whose H-1B share of their workforce exceeds a particular threshold, must attest that they have first tried to hire American workers before sponsoring additional H-1B visas. However, employers are exempted if they pay the H-1B worker at least $60,000 per year, or if the worker holds a master’s degree or higher.

The $60,000 threshold was set in 1998 and was intended to be twice the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) National Average Wage Index at the time. It has never been adjusted for inflation. Today, the SSA National Average Wage Index is nearly $70,000, meaning the original threshold, adjusted for inflation, would be nearly $140,000.

The Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would replace the fixed $60,000 threshold with a dynamic standard equal to two times the national average wage index, as calculated by the SSA. This would ensure the threshold keeps pace with wage growth going forward, rather than remaining frozen in place.

title: Following Hinson’s Advocacy, EPA Announces Proposed Rule to Reallocate 100% of Exempt Biofuels Gallons
text:
Image

October 13, 2026

Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (IA-02) applauded the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposed supplemental rule to reallocate 100% of exempted biofuels gallons, ensuring refinery exemptions don’t cut into demand for American-made biofuels. This announcement follows relentless advocacy from Rep. Hinson, including an agreement she helped secure in August and a visit from EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin to an Iowa ethanol facility on Monday.

“Biofuels should be front and center in any plan to unleash domestic energy production and lower costs at the pump. Earlier this year, the administration announced the strongest biofuels blending targets in history, driving demand for Iowa ag products and new investment in our rural communities.

“Today’s proposal reflects the 100% reallocation agreement I helped secure in August—making sure refinery exemptions don’t reduce demand for homegrown biofuels and our farmers and producers are made whole. With farmers facing such difficult conditions right now, getting this across the finish line is a big deal. I’m grateful to Administrator Zeldin for working with me to protect the Renewable Fuel Standard, and I’ll keep pushing relentlessly for Iowa farmers and biofuels producers throughout this process.” – Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

Background:

In August, the EPA granted small refinery exemptions for 29 refineries – totaling 1.76 billion renewable identification numbers (RINs) – allowing them to avoid certain biofuels blending requirements.

Following the announced exemptions, Hinson worked directly with EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and other administration officials to help secure an agreement to move forward with 100% reallocation of new exempt gallons.

Read her statement pushing for action HERE.

Last week, Hinson joined a bipartisan letter urging the administration to move forward with the proposed rule with 100% reallocation. Without 100% reallocation, exemptions would reduce biofuels blending levels, putting even more financial pressure on our farmers.

On October 12, Hinson hosted EPA Administrator Zeldin at an ethanol facility in Dyersville, where she reiterated the importance of protecting demand for Iowa biofuels and making farmers whole.

“St. Francis is home to the only open-heart surgery program in Columbus, and the Chattahoochee Valley is very proud of its distinction as the first Purple Heart Hospital in Georgia. I am honored to represent St. Francis and the incredible people of Columbus in Congress, and I look forward to continuing our partnership to improve the lives of families across our Congressional District.”

title: Joyce Tours New Lake County Public Safety Center Construction Site
text:
PAINESVILLE, OH – On Friday, Congressman Dave Joyce (OH-14) and Lake County Sheriff Frank Leonbruno toured the construction site for the new Lake County Public Safety Center. The project represents a key investment in local safety and security of the community. The three-and-a-half-story facility will have capacity for 504 individuals and span approximately 250,000 square feet.

The project will also include technology and security enhancements designed to support law enforcement and improve care for the people housed in the facility. These enhancements are supported in part by $4.2 million in community project funding secured by Congressman Joyce through the Fiscal Year 2026 Commerce, Justice, and Science appropriations bill.

“As a former prosecutor, the safety and well-being of Northeast Ohio’s communities continue to be among my top priorities,” said Congressman Joyce. “By equipping law enforcement and corrections staff with better technology, communication tools, and resources, we can create a safer environment inside the facility while supporting better outcomes for the community. I am glad to have played a vital role in moving this project forward and improving public safety.”

“As Sheriff of Lake County, I want to thank Congressman Dave Joyce for his support for our new jail project and his assistance in obtaining $4 million at the federal level to fund our technology needs. This new state-of-the-art facility will bring expanded treatment for medical, mental health, and addiction services to help us return inmates to society better than when they first arrived at our doors,” said Lake County Sheriff Leonbruno.

Background

The current Lake County Jail opened in 1990 and has served the county for more than three decades. While the facility has received updates over the years, some of its technology and infrastructure date back to its original construction. The new Lake County Public Safety Center is being built to replace the aging facility and provide updated space and resources for modern corrections operations. The Lake County Public Safety Center is scheduled to open in the summer of 2027.

title: Kaptur, Latta Introduce Bipartisan Legislation Honoring Fremont’s Rutherford B. Hayes Library and Museums
text:
Fremont, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) and Congressman Bob Latta (OH-05) introduced a bipartisan resolution in recognition of the United States’ first Presidential library, the Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library and Museums. This year marks the 110th Anniversary of the Library and Museums and the 150th Anniversary of Rutherford B. Hayes’ Presidential campaign.

“The Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library and Museums have left an indelible mark on our region throughout its 110 years, and I am honored to celebrate an institution that serves as a model for preserving and celebrating Ohio and American history,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “In creating the first Presidential Library, Hayes’ descendants showed the nation how to commemorate history in a manner that honors the sacrifices of those that came before and that seeks to teach future generations of the responsibility of citizenship.”

“I’m proud to co-lead this resolution to honor and celebrate the 110th anniversary of the Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library & Museums in Fremont, Ohio and the 150th anniversary of his Presidential campaign,” said Congressman Bob Latta (OH-05). "The Hayes Library was our nation’s first Presidential Library, and beginning in the 120th Congress, this historic place will call Ohio’s Fifth Congressional District home. President Hayes was a devoted public servant who dedicated his career to Ohio and our nation. It’s important that we preserve significant elements of American history, such as the Hayes Library, to ensure future generations can learn about the lives of figures who have had a positive impact on our country."

Born in Delaware, Ohio in 1822, Hayes served as a Governor of Ohio and as the 19th President of the United States. After his death, Hayes’ children cemented their father’s legacy by creating the Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library and Museums at the Hayes’ residence at Spiegel Grove in Fremont, Ohio. The library and museums were the first of their kind, and they preserve the former President’s personal library, his military service records, and materials and artifacts from his Presidency. The museums also takes careful effort to preserve and collect materials that showcase life along Lake Erie’s south shoreline, along with artifacts from Ohio’s history and other former presidents. It was used as a model for constructing the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum in New York, the first official Federal Presidential library. Following the path of the Hayes and Roosevelt institutions, 16 Federal Presidential libraries exist today.

title: Kaptur, Murray: As Families Pay More & More for Energy, Reports Show Trump Energy Department Withholding Billions and Playing Politics
text:
Toledo, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, released the following statement on the Trump Administration holding back or cutting off Billions of dollars Congress provided the Department of Energy to bring new energy online and lower Americans’ energy costs. Four recent reports detail how, over the last 18 months, President Trump’s policies have raised energy costs for families and delayed and defunded critical energy investments.

“President Trump hasn’t just sent gas prices through the roof with his war with Iran; he and his Administration have systematically held up and cut off energy investments Congress has made that should be lowering families’ energy bills. Congress gave the Department of Energy tens of Billions of dollars to build out the power grid and cut the costs that families pay to heat and cool their homes. But the Trump Administration is still holding that money back and letting politics decide which projects survive. This President’s corruption is already sending Americans’ energy bills higher. The Constitution gives Congress the power of the purse. We will keep pressing until this money reaches the projects and families it was meant for,” said Kaptur and Murray.

Congress provided funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the annual Energy and Water Development appropriations bills for a variety of cost-cutting energy investments. The funding supports power lines, grid upgrades, home energy savings, and bringing more power online. But starting in January 2025, the Trump Administration froze funds for energy programs andkept them frozen after Kaptur and Murray demanded answers. The Department announced the cancellation of 24 awards worth $3.7 Billion in May 2025 and another 321 worth nearly $8 Billion on October 1, 2025. In July 2026, the Department’s lawyers admitted in court that the October cancellations were based solely on the politics of each recipient’s state.

Four reports released recently show the Department of Energy is failing to spend money Congress provided—driving up Americans’ costs—and it is letting politics drive its decisions:

Recent analysis from Energy Innovation, which includes state-level impacts, found that the Trump Administration’s energy policy changes since January 2025, including the Department’s cancellation of hydrogen hub funding, will cost households an additional $920 Billion for energy from 2026 through 2040, or about $6,500 more in energy costs per household.

The Department of Energy Alumni Network and Lawyers for Good Government reported that a year after the Department cancelled hundreds of awards, 61 percent of terminated awards remain in limbo, 69 percent of the awards the Department said it would keep have received negligible funding in the past six months, and another 1,731 projects worth $3.9 Billion have heard nothing from the Department.

The Natural Resources Defense Council published internal Department records, obtained through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit, indicating that DOE’s committee reviewing awards for termination was made up entirely of political appointees and Department of Government Efficiency staff. This follows DOE’s earlier admission in court that its decision to cancel energy projects “was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state.”

The EFI Foundation found that 94 percent of the $57.5 Billion Congress provided DOE through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act has still not reached recipients, and $29.3 Billion, or 51 percent, has not been legally committed to any project.

title: Kennedy, New York Delegation Demand DHS Release $87 Million in Counterterrorism Funding Still Owed to New York
text:
One Year After Trump Promised Full Reversal of Funding Cuts, First Responders Statewide are Still Without Millions in Federal Investments

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee’s Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology, led members of the New York Congressional Delegation in urging the Department of Homeland Security to immediately release $87 million in FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Program (HSGP) funding that is still owed to New York. Their letter, sent to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, highlights the danger of withholding this funding from one the largest states in the nation and a top target for international and domestic terrorism.

“One year ago, President Trump promised to restore New York counterterrorism funding in full after slashing the state’s allocation by nearly 90 percent. Yet today, DHS refuses to release $87 million that is still missing,” said Congressman Kennedy. “As Ranking Member of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee, I know how critical these preparedness investments are. They help law enforcement and first responders across New York, from Buffalo to Manhattan, plan for emergencies, train for real world terrorism threats, and get the equipment they need to keep our communities safe. These preparedness grants were born out of the aftermath of the deadliest terror attack in American history, a tragedy that changed New York State forever. DHS’s refusal to restore $87 million for the state is not just reckless – it poses a direct threat to public safety.”

In September 2025, DHS issued HSGP award notifications that cut New York’s allocation by 86 percent, or $187 million, leaving the state with just $30 million compared to roughly $220 million in FY24. In October 2025, following bipartisan advocacy, President Trump committed to restoring full funding at approximately $220 million. After a court order in Noem v. Illinois that found Trump unlawfully cut emergency grant funding, the administration released $100 million, but $87 million is still owed to New York.

The missing funds affect every county in the state, including Erie and Niagara, and represent $11 million in losses for New York City. The letter warns that without full restoration, DHS is severely limiting local law enforcement’s ability to plan, train tactical teams, procure equipment, and conduct operations. Created in the wake of the September 11th attacks, HSGP has protected New York State for decades. The delegation underscored that the funds are due 25 years after 9/11 and one year after the President’s promise.

title: Malliotakis Urges CMS to Improve Medicare Coverage for Breast Cancer Screenings for Women with Dense Breast Tissue
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) sent a letter to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz urging the agency to review and update Medicare coverage policies for supplemental breast ultrasounds for women with dense breast tissue. The request follows a change in how Medicare coverage policies were interpreted under the Biden Administration in 2024.

In her letter, Malliotakis raised concerns over reports of Medicare coverage denials for supplemental breast ultrasounds, which can help detect cancer that may be missed during traditional mammograms. She urged CMS to review its policies to ensure women have access to additional screenings when recommended by their physicians.

“Early detection saves lives, and during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, we are highlighting the importance of ensuring women have access to the screenings and care they need,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “Last week, I visited Staten Island University Hospital to discuss the importance of early detection and the advances being made in breast cancer prevention and treatment. Part of that effort is making sure women can access additional screenings when recommended by their doctors, especially those with dense breast tissue, where cancer can be more difficult to detect through traditional mammograms. That's why I'm urging Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to review its current policies and address coverage barriers that could prevent women from receiving these potentially lifesaving screenings.”

title: Representative April McClain Delaney Joined 99 Democratic Lawmakers in Slamming Department of Education for Failure to Enforce Title IX and Protect Student Survivors
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) member Maxine Dexter (OR-03), DWC member Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), DWC Chair Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) and Rep. Mark Takano (CA-41) led a letter to the Office of the Inspector General at the Department of Education. The letter urges the Acting Inspector General to open an investigation into the Department’s gutting of the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) and Title IX rollbacks and its impact on the Department’s ability to enforce Title IX protections for student survivors of sexual assault and harassment. 99 House Democrats joined the effort.

The call for the investigation comes after Jane Doe’s story from Cornell University and Kendall Francis’ story from Louisiana State University (LSU) sparked a national outcry about the high rate of sexual violence on college campuses. Additionally the survivors’ stories have renewed scrutiny of how colleges and universities respond, and how the Department of Education enforces Title IX protections for survivors.

One in four undergraduate women experience sexual assault or rape while in college. Sexual violence against women on college campuses is a public health crisis, yet significant barriers remain that block accountability and protections for students. Changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities under the Trump administration have only made that worse and have undermined the Department’s ability to properly investigate complaints and enforce Title IX protections.

As of January 2025, OCR reportedly faced a backlog of nearly 12,000 civil rights cases, while the administration reduced OCR’s workforce by nearly half. The Department has closed zero college sexual harassment or sexual violence cases. The Department also formalized weaker protections and processes for student survivors: narrowing the definition of sexual harassment, reducing school liability, and implementing intimidating investigative and hearing procedures that are retraumatizing to survivors.

Without proper federal enforcement and institutional accountability, Title IX protections become just words on a page. The Department of Education is failing student survivors. Protections for survivors are not partisan and should always be a priority, however the Department’s rollback of vital protections creates additional barriers for survivors and is leaving them to fend for themselves in their most vulnerable moments.

In their letter, the members explained how the Department’s changes will leave student survivors vulnerable and why an investigation is necessary:

“We urge the Office of Inspector General to immediately open an investigation into the Department’s failure to adequately enforce Title IX protections for survivors of sexual harassment and assault, including whether changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities have undermined the Department’s ability to protect students, investigate complaints in a timely manner, and hold institutions accountable.”

The members outlined the Department’s policies that have weakened protections for student survivors:

“At the same time that OCR’s staff and regional capacity were substantially reduced, the Department announced and pursued Title IX enforcement priorities concerning transgender students’ participation in athletics and access to sex-separated facilities, and also dismantling Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) programs. These reprioritizations do nothing to address the backlog of sexual violence cases.”

The letter also explains how reprioritizations and restructuring by the Department have decreased OCR’s capacity to investigate cases of sexual violence on campus:

“This restructuring threatens to further delay investigations, erode OCR’s institutional expertise, and create additional barriers for survivors seeking accountability. These reprioritizations, staff reductions, and the interagency agreement raise significant questions about whether OCR has sufficient capacity to investigate Title IX complaints, communicate with complainants, and fulfill its civil rights enforcement responsibilities in a timely and effective manner.”

The members also outlined what they are urging the Inspector General to investigate:

Examining whether the Department has fulfilled its legal and administrative responsibilities to investigate and resolve Title IX complaints in a timely and effective manner.

The causes and consequences of the absence of resolution agreements involving college sexual harassment and assault complaints since January 2025.

Whether reductions in OCR staffing, the closure of regional offices, or changes in enforcement priorities have contributed to delays, backlogs, or failures to resolve these complaints.

Examining whether OCR has sufficient staffing, resources, policies, and procedures to effectively enforce Title IX and protect students from sex discrimination, including sexual harassment and violence.

Identifying how survivors have been harmed by these changes.

Lastly, the members asked the Inspector General to answer the following questions:

How many Title IX sexual harassment and sexual violence complaints are currently pending before OCR, and how long have they been pending?

How have processing times, case closures, investigations, and resolution agreements changed since January 2025?

Have staffing reductions or office closures affected OCR’s ability to investigate complaints or communicate with survivors?

Have Department officials directed, formally or informally, OCR personnel to deprioritize certain categories of Title IX complaints?

What safeguards are currently in place to ensure Title IX complaints involving sexual violence receive timely and appropriate review?

What corrective actions are necessary to ensure the Department is meeting its obligations to protect students under Title IX?

Read the full letter here.

title: Congressman McCormick Introduces Own Not Rent Act to Expand Homeownership Opportunities for American Families
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) introduced the Own Not Rent Act (H.R. 10784), legislation aimed at expanding homeownership opportunities by allowing state governments to guarantee portions of mortgages to allow for smaller down payments without mortgage insurance, helping first-time homebuyers save for a down payment, reducing financial barriers, and incentivizing the construction of new homes.

The legislation would establish tax-advantaged down payment savings accounts, expand penalty-free retirement withdrawals for first-time homebuyers, and provide new tax incentives for homebuilders constructing owner-occupied housing.

“The fact that the median age of a first-time homebuyer has reached 40 years old is unacceptable. Hardworking Americans are doing everything right, yet the dream of owning a home remains out of reach,” said Congressman McCormick. “Homeownership is one of the most important ways families build financial security and generational wealth. The Own Not Rent Act removes financial barriers, helps families save, and encourages the construction of homes Americans can actually own. We should be helping the next generation build their futures, not forcing them to remain renters.”

The Own Not Rent Act is endorsed by the National Association of REALTORS (NAR).

This bill would:

Allow eligible first-time homebuyers to make up to $25,000 in annual tax-deductible contributions, with a maximum account balance of $100,000.

Increase the lifetime limit on penalty-free retirement withdrawals for qualified first-time home purchases from $10,000 to $25,000.

Permit tax-advantaged employer contributions to employees' down payment savings accounts.

Provide eligible homebuilders a tax credit equal to 35 percent of qualifying construction costs for newly built owner-occupied homes.

Encourage qualifying state-backed mortgage insurance and guarantee programs.

title: Menendez and Krishnamoorthi Push for Stronger Energy Drink Safety Rules to Protect Kids
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressmen Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (“HHS”) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. calling on HHS to update federal research and guidance on high-caffeine energy drinks and conduct a comprehensive assessment of their consumption and health effects among school-aged children.

“Kids are consuming more caffeine than ever, and Sarah Katz’s tragic death exposed how dangerous poor labeling and hidden caffeine levels can be,” said Congressman Menendez. “We are calling on HHS to update federal caffeine guidelines, protect our children, and ensure parents and teachers have the information they need to keep children safe.”

“Energy drink use among kids is at record levels, while caffeine-related emergency room visits among middle and high school students have roughly doubled,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “These products can pose serious health risks to children, yet the federal government is still relying on outdated research and guidance. Our government needs to catch up and give parents, schools, and health care providers the information they need to keep kids safe.”

In 2022, 21-year-old Jersey City native Sarah Katz died after drinking an energy drink that was improperly labeled. Congressman Menendez reintroduced the bipartisan Sarah Katz Caffeine Safety Act last year to increase transparency of caffeine in food and beverages. The bill would also require the Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) to conduct a safety review for caffeine and support a study to examine how caffeine impacts vulnerable populations, including children.

Today, nearly one in four high school seniors consume energy drinks daily, up from one in six in 2022. From 2017 to 2023, caffeine-related emergency department visits among middle and high school students roughly doubled. Despite this uptick, official CDC guidance still relies in part on a 2013 SAMHSA report using emergency department visit data from 2007 to 2011.

The lawmakers also raised concerns about a lack of federal oversight and caffeine labeling requirements for energy drinks. FDA guidance is over ten years old, nonbinding, and provides no recommended caffeine limit for children or adolescents.

Menendez and Krishnamoorthi requested that HHS conduct a comprehensive assessment of energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children and provide answers to the following questions:

What research is HHS currently conducting or funding on energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children, including interactions between energy drinks and prescribed stimulant medications?

When will SAMHSA or another HHS component update its 2013 analysis with national estimates of energy drink-related emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and deaths among minors?

Does FDA intend to evaluate or establish recommended limits on caffeine intake for children and adolescents? FDA has listed draft guidance on labeling caffeine content as a 2026 priority. When will that guidance be issued, will it recommend that manufacturers disclose caffeine content in milligrams, and does FDA intend to pursue binding labeling requirements?

How is HHS tracking adverse events involving children and energy drinks, including cardiac events, reports submitted to FDA, and poison center data? What trends has the Department identified since 2020?

Has HHS engaged with USDA on revisiting federal school nutrition standards that permit caffeinated beverages in high schools, given USDA’s 2016 commitment to continue monitoring FDA’s work on caffeine?

The lawmakers called on HHS to make the assessment publicly available so parents, schools, and healthcare providers can understand the risks these products pose and the steps being taken to address them.

In my state of Louisiana, just with the big, beautiful bill, the Working Families Tax Cuts, the average Louisianian has a tax cut of $2,915. That's money in their pocket they did not have to send to Washington just because we implemented the bill. The average household income went up by almost $5,400 just because of our policies.

We also have the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years. We have a secure border. We've not released a single illegal alien into the country in 16 straight months. We have more jobs, more opportunity. We created a million private sector jobs in the last 19 months in this country. The success goes on and on. Lowest prescription drug costs in 60 years. That's because we did what we said we were going do, and you have to keep those commonsense principles and policies going because we have much more to do ahead of us.

On the contrast between the Republican and Democrat economic agenda:

If you look across the board objectively as economists do, we have incredible economic growth. We are reshoring American manufacturing. We're bringing jobs back here to this country. As I'm traveling around in the swing districts, people are feeling that. They're feeling the effect. We cut taxes on tips, overtime, Social Security. In this state, almost 68% of our workforce gets a huge benefit from no taxes on overtime. We have 700,000 senior citizens no longer paying taxes on their Social Security – that's because of the legislation that we passed. Not a single Democrat in Congress voted for any of that. It was all Republicans. Now, here's the question. Do you want to turn the country back over, the governance in Congress over, to the people who brought you $5 gasoline under Biden and Harris and 40-year high inflation at 9.1%? I don't think so.

On Republican efforts to protect local communities from energy rate hikes and continue SI development:

The infrastructure for SI is important for national security, and we have to continue it, but it must be done in a way that heeds and respects community concerns. People are rightly concerned about all this. We passed, for example, the Ratepayer Protection Act out of the House right before we left for this district work period. We sent it over to the Senate with only three dissenting votes. It was a bipartisan vote. And the Senate Democrats blocked it. The solution is to have common sense and steady hands at the wheel, address this new technology in a way that harnesses its potential for the American people, but also ensures that we don't over-regulate it, have government stop it with a moratorium, and then lose that race to China. That would be devastating for our country.

title: Rep. Min and Sen. Welch Lead Probe into Role of Trump Cabinet Members in Obtaining Pardons of Convicted Felons
text:
Washington, DC. — This week, U.S. Representative Dave Min (D-CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Anti-Corruption Task Force, alongside U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on The Constitution, was joined by U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Representative Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-05), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Constitution and Limited Government, in raising questions about the role of cabinet members in securing presidential pardons, as part of their ongoing investigation into executive clemency actions since January 20, 2025.

The bicameral group of lawmakers are looking into whether U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin used their access to inappropriately influence President Trump’s decision to grant full presidential pardons to convicted felons Trevor Milton and Troy Lake.

“Public reports of high-profile individuals—including yourself—appealing directly to the President on behalf of pardon recipients risk subversion of the established pardon review processes by financial influence and political access,” write the lawmakers. “Article II, Section 2, Clause 1 of the U.S. Constitution authorizes the President to ‘grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offenses against the United States, except in Cases of Impeachment.’ The U.S. Supreme Court has characterized executive clemency as ‘an act of grace’ exercised for the ‘public welfare.’ President Trump’s use of this authority appears to deviate from this traditional purpose.”

The lawmakers conclude: “Congress has a compelling interest in ensuring that the constitutional pardon power is exercised with fairness and transparency. Given these circumstances, we are seeking additional information to better understand the extent to which influence and access have overridden the standard pardon review process.”

In their letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the lawmakers request answers about Secretary Kennedy’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to pardon convicted fraudster Trevor Milton, who defrauded and misled investors regarding technology and products related to his company, Nikola Corporation. The victims of Mr. Milton’s fraud include individuals who lost their retirement savings and others who had never invested in the stock market before. President Trump’s pardon eliminated Milton’s obligation to potentially pay $660 million in court-ordered restitution to his victims. Milton did not serve any of his four-year prison sentence.

“According to public reporting, you personally appealed to the President to grant Mr. Milton a pardon, arguing that he had been unfairly prosecuted by the previous administration’s Justice Department. Days before granting Mr. Milton’s pardon request, President Trump reportedly told him to call you and thank you for convincing the President to grant him a pardon,” write the lawmakers. “Your reported involvement in this matter is particularly troubling, given that Mr. Milton reportedly donated $750,000 to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) Political Action Committee (PAC), which was launched in late 2024 by senior members of your presidential campaign to unite your supporters behind President Trump. Public reporting also indicates that Mr. Milton and his wife donated approximately $1,800,000 to President Trump’s 2024 reelection campaign a month before the election.”

In their letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin, the lawmakers demand answers about the administrator’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to grant a full presidential pardon to Troy Lake, and a subsequent corporate pardon to Lake’s company, Elite Diesel Service Inc. Lake’s conviction arose from allegations that he and his company disabled the monitoring components of emissions control systems on hundreds of heavy-duty commercial

trucks.

The lawmakers write: “According to public reporting, two friends of Mr. Lake petitioned you in an August 2025 email, urging you to reach out to the President to request a pardon. Mr. Lake’s wife publicly attributed progress on her husband’s pardon efforts to your subsequent intervention. Such progress included a phone call with Sean Hayes, a White House attorney who works closely on pardons.”

The lawmakers’ letters seek information from HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin regarding:

The nature of their relationships with the pardoned felons;

The process by which clemency requests were initiated and considered;

Whether intermediaries, lobbyists, or advocates were involved;

Any contacts with Trump Administration officials or associates;

Their role in any other clemency decisions made by the Trump Administration;

Whether financial contributions or payments were made in connection with clemency efforts; and

The extent of third-party advocacy supporting the requests.

Read and download the lawmakers’ full letters to HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin.

In May, Senator Welch and Rep. Min sent letters to 17 individuals who received pardons or commutations under circumstances that warrant further congressional scrutiny, including several individuals connected to major fraud schemes, financial crimes, and high-profile political or financial relationships tied to President Trump and his associates. The earlier letters sought information regarding the clemency process, including whether financial contributions, lobbyists, intermediaries, or personal connections played a role in securing presidential clemency.

Among the individuals who received letters are convicted fraudsters, political fundraisers, corporate executives, and wealthy donors, such as Changpeng Zhao, whose cases have generated public reporting suggesting unusual access to Trump’s network of political allies and associates, direct lobbying efforts, large political donations, or other concerning connections surrounding their clemency requests.

The lawmakers continued their investigation in June, sending four additional letters to the Department of Justice’s Office of the Pardon Attorney, the White House Office of Records Management, the White House Pardon Czar, and the United States Secret Service.
