title: Moylan Announces Historic Final Step to Award Medal of Honor to Guam Hero Sergeant Major Juan Ogo Blaz
text:
(Hagåtña, Guam) — Congressman James Moylan announced during a press conference Wednesday morning that the years-long effort to award the Medal of Honor to the late U.S. Army Sergeant Major Juan Ogo Blaz has reached its final stage, with the nomination now awaiting the approval of signature from President Donald Trump.

Joined by Blaz's daughter Darlene Blaz and his wife Dionisia Blaz, local leaders, and Guam veterans, Moylan shared the historic development following a favorable determination by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth supporting the upgrade of Blaz's Distinguished Service Cross to the Medal of Honor.

The announcement marks the closest Guam has ever come to securing the nation's highest military honor for one of its own. Following the President’s signature, Blaz will become the first ever CHamoru servicemember from Guam to receive the Medal of Honor.

“As a U.S. Army veteran myself, this moment is deeply personal and emotional. Sergeant Major Blaz represents the very best of who we are as a people. His extraordinary courage and sacrifice reflect generations of sons and daughters of Guam who have answered our nation's call to serve,” said Congressman Moylan. “For an island whose people have given so much in defense of our country, this recognition would be more than an honor for one extraordinary warrior. It would be a profound acknowledgment of the patriotism, courage, and sacrifice of generations of Guam service members. We have come closer than ever before, and we will soon finally see Sergeant Major Blaz receive the recognition he so rightfully deserves.”

During the press conference, Moylan recounted the extraordinary acts of valor that earned Blaz the Distinguished Service Cross, the Army's second-highest military decoration for valor.

On January 18, 1969, during the Vietnam War, Blaz, then a Staff Sergeant serving with the 82nd Airborne Division, assumed command after his platoon leader was wounded. Under intense enemy fire, he helped evacuate injured soldiers and led an assault against enemy positions.

Despite suffering a wound to his shoulder, Blaz continued fighting. When his platoon was pinned down by heavy machine-gun fire, he charged across a ravine to silence an enemy weapon, sustaining a second wound in the process. Refusing medical evacuation, he continued risking his life to mark enemy positions with smoke grenades, enabling supporting helicopter gunships to strike their targets. Only after the enemy positions had been neutralized did he accept medical treatment.

Moylan emphasized that the historic milestone represents years of sustained advocacy and cooperation among Blaz's family, Guam veterans, congressional colleagues, and senior defense officials.

During his first term in Congress, Moylan worked alongside Colonel Danny Santos to advance the effort. In 2024, he successfully offered an amendment to the FY2025 National Defense Authorization Act authorizing the President to award Blaz the Medal of Honor. He also entered letters from Guam veterans and community leaders supporting Blaz's recognition into the Congressional Record.

Moylan continued advocating directly with senior defense leadership, personally raising Blaz's case with Secretary Hegseth during his visit to Guam and maintaining subsequent dialogue with the Department of War.

He also joined former Congresswoman Madeleine Bordallo at the Pentagon, where they discussed the case directly with Secretary of the Army Daniel Driscoll.

Most recently, Moylan led a bipartisan congressional letter joined by 16 Members of Congress formally urging President Trump to grant final approval for Blaz's Medal of Honor.

Sergeant Major Blaz passed away on September 3, 2024, at the age of 78. Just months earlier, Moylan had personally informed Blaz that the House had advanced legislation authorizing the Medal of Honor for his service. Following his passing, Moylan honored Blaz on the House floor and pledged to continue pursuing the recognition on his behalf.

Darlene Blaz, daughter of Sergeant Major Blaz reflected on the historic moment. “My heart feels quite heavy, and yet, it has never felt more light. Heavy, because it saddens me to know that my father is no longer with us to experience the reality of this long awaited moment—his moment, and knowing that it is one step away is incredibly exciting,” said Blaz. “We are truly grateful for the people who made this possible. Congressman Moylan, thank you from the bottom of my heart. Danny Santos, you have played a big role over the years campaigning towards this effort. It’s hard to believe this moment is becoming a reality. Fifty seven years is a lifetime. Although I am saddened that my father is not here, I know he is in spirit.”

Wednesday's press conference also brought together members of Guam's veteran community and local leaders, including Army Veteran Vice Speaker Tony Ada and Senator Sabrina Salas Matanane, Chairperson of the Committee on Health and Veterans Affairs, in recognition of the significance of this milestone for Guam.

With the nomination now awaiting the President's final signature, Moylan expressed optimism that the long-awaited recognition will soon become a reality, honoring not only Blaz's extraordinary heroism but also the enduring legacy of military service and sacrifice among the people of Guam.

title: Neguse, Bennet, Hickenlooper Urge Federal Agencies to Restore Cell Service in Boulder County
text:
Lafayette, CO — Following recent reports of unacceptable cellular service issues across Boulder County, Congressman Joe Neguse and Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper penned a letter to the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) urging the agencies to meet with cellular carriers immediately and resolve the issues.

The three major cellular carriers apparently limited their Boulder County coverage earlier this year to comply with federal signal transmission rules surrounding the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone north of Boulder. These federal signal limits protect ongoing research at several government agencies, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the U.S. Geological Survey.

“We write to urge your agencies to assist in resolving major reported cellular network outages in Boulder County, Colorado, following signal adjustments made to comply with National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) regulations protecting the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone,” wrote Neguse, Bennet, and Hickenlooper.

The lawmakers also pressed the NTIA and FCC to find a collaborative solution that will quickly address community concerns, particularly preserving access to cellular coverage as a vital public safety resource.

“Full cell phone coverage is indispensable to everyday life. When people leave their homes, they expect to be able to use their cell phones for navigation, payment, and communication with others. Cell phones are also vital for public safety in Boulder County, which is prone to rapidly escalating wildfires.”

They concluded with a call for swift solutions and asked that the FCC and NTIA keep congressional offices and local governments updated on the outcome of the requested meeting and progress toward restoring full connectivity.

“[W]e respectfully request that FCC and NTIA officials meet with carriers immediately in order to find a solution that will allow them to restore functional cellular service to their customers as soon as possible. We also request that you update our offices and local governments on the outcome of that meeting and report back to us on your progress as all parties work to restore full connectivity,” the lawmakers concluded.

Read the full letter HERE and below:

October 13, 2026

The Honorable Brendan Carr

Chairman

Federal Communications Commission

45 L Street NE

Washington, DC 20554

The Honorable Arielle Roth

Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information

Administrator, National Telecommunications and Information Administration

1401 Constitution Avenue NW

Washington, DC 20230

Dear Chairman Carr and Assistant Secretary Roth,

We write to urge your agencies to assist in resolving major reported cellular network outages in Boulder County, Colorado, following signal adjustments made to comply with National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) regulations protecting the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone.

As we understand it, in late 2024, the NTIA Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS) notified three major cellular carriers that they needed to modify their signals received within the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone, the 50-mile radius where federal regulations limit radio transmission frequency that could otherwise interfere with the research of the ITS, National Institute of Standards and Technology, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and U.S. Geological Survey. The three major carriers have publicly stated that they have since adjusted their signals to comply with Table Mountain frequency limits.

However, these signal adjustments appear to have significantly downgraded cellular network coverage for Boulder County consumers. Our constituents in the nearby towns of Longmont and Niwot have filed more than 100 formal complaints with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) reporting that they cannot make phone calls or use data on their cell phones, even when their devices indicate full network coverage. While the three major carriers have publicly indicated they will further upgrade their networks to compensate for the necessary signal reductions, our constituents lack vital cell connectivity in the interim.

Full cell phone coverage is indispensable to everyday life. When people leave their homes, they expect to be able to use their cell phones for navigation, payment, and communication with others. Cell phones are also vital for public safety in Boulder County, which is prone to rapidly escalating wildfires. Our constituents use their cell phones to notify their families and friends that they are safe during wildfire season and to warn neighbors of unpredictable wildfire shifts. For example, the 2021 Marshall Fire, which killed two people and burned nearly 1,000 structures, progressed so rapidly that many residents would not have known to immediately evacuate had they not been alerted by a phone call or text from someone they knew.

Given all of the foregoing, we respectfully request that FCC and NTIA officials meet with carriers immediately in order to find a solution that will allow them to restore functional cellular service to their customers as soon as possible. We also request that you update our offices and local governments on the outcome of that meeting and report back to us on your progress as all parties work to restore full connectivity.

Sincerely,

###

title: Ocasio-Cortez, McClain Delaney, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth Lead Calls to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Don Beyer (VA-08), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), and Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) are leading a congressional letter urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.

The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.

“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”

The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” said Congressman Don Beyer.

"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume.

“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”

At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.

The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.

The lawmakers request answers in three areas:

Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.

Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.

Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.

The letter calls for a pause until lawmakers can better understand the FAA’s decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. The co-leads emphasize that modernizing air traffic control must prioritize safety, transparency, and the expertise of the people responsible for keeping our skies safe.

###

title: Olszewski and McBride Introduce ASSURE Act to Expand Voter Registration Opportunities
text:
With the midterm elections just weeks away, voter registration deadlines are fast approaching across the country. In Maryland, the deadline to register is today, October 13.

“As a government teacher, I spent years teaching my students that democracy only works when people participate in it,” said Congressman Olszewski. “That participation requires something basic: making sure people can register to vote and have their voices heard. If someone is interacting with their government to access veterans benefits, Social Security, or another federal service, we should use that opportunity to make sure they know how to register to vote.”

“Access to the ballot box should be a basic promise of our democracy, not a privilege that depends on who occupies the White House,” said Congresswoman McBride. “The ASSURE Act puts that principle into practice by restoring voter registration opportunities that President Trump has rolled back and ensuring Americans have access to reliable election information. At a moment when this administration continues to undermine voting rights, particularly for Black Americans and communities of color, this work is more urgent than ever. I’m grateful to Rep. Olszewski for his leadership on this legislation, and I’ll keep fighting to ensure every eligible voter can make their voice heard.”

The ASSURE Act – short for the Agency Support for Secure and Universal Registration Enhancement Act – codifies a Biden-era executive order, later reversed by President Trump, that directed federal agencies to integrate voter registration opportunities into services Americans already use. It also restores a longstanding policy – also reversed by President Trump – that permits nonpartisan groups to provide voter registration assistance and civic participation information at naturalization ceremonies for new Americans.

Together, these measures would give eligible Americans more opportunities to register without having to seek out a separate government office, website, or registration event.

Olszewski has made expanding civic participation and strengthening democratic institutions a central focus of his work in Congress. He has also supported legislation to make Election Day a national holiday and require states to offer same-day voter registration.

“We should make it easier for eligible Americans to participate in our democracy – not put up unnecessary barriers,” Congressman Olszewski said. “The ASSURE Act is a simple idea: meet people where they are, make registration easier, and make our democracy more accessible to everyone who is eligible to participate.”

title: Congressman Patronis Joins Senator Rick Scott to Provide an Update for Hurricane Isaias Recovery
text:
DESTIN, FL – Today, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (R-FL) joined Senator Rick Scott (R-FL), Okaloosa County Sheriff Eric Aden, State Representatives Patt Maney, and other local officials to provide Northwest Floridians with an update on recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias.

Congressman Patronis said, “I want you to err on the side of caution. Your first call for any damage at your house needs to be to your insurance agent, your insurance carrier, the Florida Department of Financial Services, or even call our office. We will connect you or help connect you or help walk you through the process of getting in touch with your insurance carrier.

Residents should remain vigilant against scams and verify contractors before agreeing to repairs. Never operate generators indoors or in enclosed spaces due to the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning. EV owners should also follow manufacturer guidance for safely handling and charging vehicles that may have been exposed to floodwaters. Taking these precautions can help keep you and your family safe as our communities recover.

To watch the press conference in full click here.

Congressman Patronis: “Senator Scott has always said, which always stuck with me, is we can replace your stuff, but we can't replace you. And I've used that line over and over and over. And thank you for heeding the warnings for evacuation. This is why the outcome and loss of life was non-existent in Okaloosa County, but it also comes back from great leadership at the sheriff's office, emergency management, and the county commission, and all of our municipal leaders.

I want to talk to you a little bit about now what's called the financial recovery. You're going to be approached because of this wind event that we dealt with. There's going to be down trees everywhere. The week before whatever this storm was called, Isaias, whatever, the week before we had all the rain, so the ground was soft. So you got all these trees that are down. That is definitely causing a challenge for our fiber companies, our power companies, our communication companies to do their job because the trees have to be removed.

So now what you're being dealt with, you're getting very aggressive tactics by tree trimmers and tree remover operations that come door-to-door, and they're going to only want cash to do that transaction. I want you to err on the side of caution. Your first call for any damage at your house needs to be to your insurance agent, your insurance carrier, the Florida Department of Financial Services, or even call our office. We will connect you or help connect you or help walk you through the process of getting in touch with your insurance carrier.

Your insurance carriers have been very good about doing pre-event emails. I got emails from my carrier saying, "Hey, a storm has hit. Can we help you file a claim?" So, look for those emails. They will hold your hand and walk you through the process. My carrier even has a smart app where you can take photos of the damage and upload it, where you're kind of your own adjuster.

The good thing about it is if you took photos of your home prior to the storm to show what it looked like beforehand, and now you've got those photos after the storm showing the damage, that's just going to speed up the process because what the insurance company's trying to figure out is, what do I owe you? So, they're going to come out with their own adjuster, which is just a nice way of saying an investigator. They want to investigate the damage so they can figure out how much do I need to pay out to the Smith household.

So, in saying that, now you're going to have the tree trimmers that are going to be predatory, but now you're going to have what are called public adjusters and attorneys and other type of contract management folks. They're not from here. They're not your neighbors. They are not your friends, okay? They're going to try to get in between you and your claim that you're going to get. In some cases, that's going to be the largest check you've ever had in your hands in your whole entire life. And those predators know that, and they will want you to sign a contract of management where they're going to get a piece of the action.

Friends, please err on the side of caution and do not sign anything. I can't state that enough. There is not a single signature ever required to get a single dollar from your insurance company. Do not sign anything. As long as you're doing that, you allow your insurance company to assess the damage, get you your money, and you start the rebuilding process.

These predators know that there's poor communications right now. They know that power is down. And you know what? They know you're vulnerable. And it's sad because they're going to come and they're going to be so courteous and nice. They're going to be carrying gas cans. They're going to have cases of water. They're going to try to get you to drop your guard. Do not take the bait. They're nice people, but they are not truly true to their word. They're just trying to make a living, and they're trying to do it off of your naivety and your own generosity because they feel like, you know, we all need help. But understand, as you'll see, what are called insurance villages that'll pop up in the region. I've talked to the CFO. They're going to bring insurance carriers together, and it'll be your opportunity to go sit face-to-face with your insurance company and work through those claims.

The insurance companies, they want to close claims because when the claim is closed and they give you your money, they can go out and start focusing their resources on other open claims. If you've got any problems, again, insurance agent, insurance carrier, my office, or the Department of Financial Services, let us help you get through that. If you've got any problems with what you feel like is a predatory action, let us know. Or heck, call the sheriff. The sheriff don't want them here either. He will run them out of town. And again, it's going to be here for these first few weeks because they know that power is not established, communications aren't established, and they want to take advantage of you because you don't know where to turn.

The last thing I'll leave with you is two things. Some of you are operating on generators. Please understand those generators can never operate inside of your house, okay? They have to be outside of your house. They cannot be in your garage. They can't be near an open window. But as you're running that generator for whatever comfort that you want, you need to get it away from your house and let it operate. There's some instructions that go along with it about cooling and shutting it down and how many hours they can operate. Please abide by those because we don't want to turn around and have a fire or an accident after the fact at your home.

And then the last thing, if you're sitting with an e-bike or an EV or a golf cart that ended up getting caught up in the submerged water from flooding, understand that right there is an accident, a fire waiting to happen. Lithium-ion batteries and salt water don't mix. It looks totally fine, but as soon as you try to put a load on it or use it, you will short the battery. And a lithium-ion battery, even submerged underwater, does not extinguish. So, please don't have an accident after the storm, especially after we've done so well.”

title: Pressley Lauds Cambridge EZRide and Success of Fare-Free Transit, Renews Push for Freedom to Move Act
text:
Rep. Pressley, Sen. Markey Lead the Freedom to Move Act, Federal Legislation to Enact Fare-Free Transit & Close Transit Equity Gap

Video from Media Avail (YouTube) | Photos (Dropbox)

CAMBRIDGE – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) joined the Charles River Transportation Management Association, City of Cambridge, Cambridge Redevelopment Authority, local elected officials, and advocates for a roundtable discussion and ride on the EZRide shuttle—a fare-free shuttle service connecting Kendall Square, Cambridge neighborhoods, and North Station—to highlight the importance and success of fare-free transit.

In Congress, Congresswoman Pressley co-leads the Freedom to Move Act alongside Senator Ed Markey, which would provide $25 billion in funding for transit agencies to offer fare-free service and improve on existing transit service offerings.

“Fare free transit is essential and it is time we invest in public transit as the public good that it is—and that is proof positive by the success of the EZRide shuttle in Cambridge,” said Congresswoman Pressley. “As Massachusetts fare-free systems continue to prove and as riders shared with me today, fare-free transit makes life more accessible, affordable, and safe for workers and families across the country. That’s why I’m fighting for national fare-free transit through our Freedom to Move Act and I’m grateful to Charles River Transportation Management Association, City of Cambridge, Cambridge Redevelopment Authority, and community partners for making this a reality in the Massachusetts 7th.”

“Charles River Transportation Management Association and EZRide appreciates the opportunity today to present the EZRide model for providing fare-free open to the public last mile circulation transit in the corridor between North Station and Eastern Cambridge since 2002. The City of Cambridge committed to climate goals while redeveloping its post-industrial economic corridor along the Charles River, creating a framework for collaboration amongst public and private stakeholders to create an efficient, frequent, affordable transit designed to meet the needs of the riders.” – Charles River Transportation Management Association

“The Cambridge Redevelopment Authority is proud that the KSTEP Fund has been instrumental in launching the expansion of fare-free transit on the EZRide bus route,” said Tom Evans, Executive Director of the Cambridge Redevelopment Authority (CRA). “This type of creative public-private partnership is vital to improve access to the innovation hub of Kendall Square for employees, neighbors and visitors from around the region.”

“EZRide has become a leading example of how fare-free public transportation can be successfully delivered through collaboration and creative funding partnerships,” said Cambridge City Manager Yi-An Huang. “By leveraging public investment alongside private and development-related contributions, the program has transformed individual commitments into broad community benefits. The result is a transportation service in Cambridge and Boston that expands opportunity, supports our climate goals, strengthens our economy, and demonstrates a scalable model for improving mobility for everyone.”

Through the Kendall Square Transit Enhancement Program (KSTEP), administered by the Cambridge Redevelopment Authority (CRA) in partnership with the City of Cambridge and other public and private stakeholders, approximately $1 million has been committed to support the Charles River TMA, which operates EZRide, in delivering a two-year expansion of service and maintaining its fare-free operation.

Photos from the event are available here and footage from the media availability following the event is available here.

Congresswoman Pressley has long championed fare-free transit in Congress. In July 2025, Rep. Pressley and Senator Markey re-introduced the Freedom to Move Act which would provide $25 billion in funding for transit agencies to offer fare free service and improve on existing transit service offerings.

The Freedom to Move Act would support state and local efforts to promote public transportation as a public good for all by:

Establishing a $5 billion competitive grant program per year to support state and local efforts to implement fare-free public transportation systems;

Investing in efforts to improve the safety and quality of public transportation services, particularly in low-income and historically underserved communities; and

Ensuring grantees use funds to address and close equity gaps in current transit systems.

In August 2026, Rep. Pressley and Sen. Markey released a new report detailing the success of fare-free transit in MA. The report, titled Making Transit Free, Frequent, and Reliable: Massachusetts shows the need for federal investment in fare-free transit, highlights the need for increased federal investments in fare-free transit.

Rep. Pressley and Sen. Markey originally introduced the Freedom to Move Act in June 2020. Following the bill’s introduction, Senator Markey, Congresswoman Pressley, and then-Councilor Michelle Wu published an op-ed that discussed the bill and the need to fund public transportation as a public good.

In July 2020, the House of Representatives passed the Moving Forward Act that included a fare-free pilot program modeled after the two lawmakers Freedom to Move Act.

In March 2021, Senator Markey and Congresswoman Pressley reintroduced the Freedom to Move Act.

In August 2022, Rep. Pressley and Senator Markey called on the MBTA to make the entire T fare-free for the duration of the Orange Line’s shutdown.

title: Ramirez Introduces the Reimagining Safety Act, Legislation to Dismantle DHS, Abolish ICE, Reimagine Community Safety
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, introduced the Reimagining Safety Act, a legislation to dismantle the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and create the Department of Community Safety. The landmark community-led legislation would create a new human- and community-centered federal department that promotes collective safety, repeal the authorities that give DHS its power, and redirect DHS funds to programs that working families rely on.

The Reimagining Safety Act is a first-of-its-kind bill and the first time community stakeholders designed a cabinet-level department. The Reimagining Safety Act would:

Establish the Department of Community Safety

Dismantle DHS, preserving the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and Customs functions

Abolish ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP)

Reinvest funds in our communities

Limit government surveillance, rein in unlawful abuses of data, and curb militarized enforcement

Begin the process of establishing a separate civil immigration system

“Every person dead in detention, shot or killed by ICE and CBP, every neighbor deported to a third country, every family separated, every community FEMA failed, every miscarriage due to substandard care, every dissenter wrongfully branded, targeted, and persecuted as ‘terrorist,’ and every threat against our elections by Trump, Markwayne, and Miller is a reason DHS must be dismantled and something new must take its place. There are more than a million reasons to take action today,” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “DHS was founded out of a profound national trauma, established to violate our rights under the pretense of securing our safety. But we cannot add new pains to old ones.”

The introduction follows a community press action on September 23, when Congresswoman Ramirez stood with Illinois public officials, civil society, and community members to announce the Reimagining Safety Act.

“Instead of the weapon DHS has proven to be, we need a department built on the best parts of who we are and can be, and the best examples of how we can take care of each other in hard times. I am proud to have led that work with the organizations in my district and nationally,” added Ramirez. “Building something new, creating in a time of destruction, is a revolutionary act. It is proof of our hope and belief in what is possible even in dark times. A different world is possible because the people have the power to reshape our government and reimagine how we cultivate safety and collective well-being.”

The legislation’s original cosponsors include Congressmembers Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Jim McGovern (MA-02). The bill is endorsed by a coalition of more than 40 national and local cross-issue organizations, including Muslims for Just Futures, Casa DuPage Workers Center, Latino Union of Chicago, Muslim Civic Coalition, Organized Communities Against Deportations, La Casita de ut ac, Albergue Tochan Nuestra Casa, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights, AL OTRO LADO, League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), Free Speech for People, Immigration Advocacy Law Group, Decolonize Sudan, The Right to Immigration Institute/Dignidad, American Friends Service Committee, Servicio Internacional para la Paz, Global Exchange, Immigrant Welcome Network of Johnson County, Council on American-Islamic Relations Chicago (CAIR-Chicago), US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Center for Constitutional Rights, Alliance of South Asians Taking Action Power (ASTA Power), Women Cross DMZ, Haitian Bridge Alliance, Arise Chicago, Palenque LSNA, Zero Hour, MADRE, Mijente, Indivisible Chicago Alliance, Grassroots Collaborative, Warehouse Workers for Justice, Jewish Council on Urban Affairs (JCUA), Rising Majority Action Front, IL Poor People’s Campaign, Sustainable Economies Law Center, National Nurses United, Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC), Defending Rights & Dissent, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, DREAM of Detroit, and United States Solidarity Economy Network, Charity and Security Network, Muslim Advocates, IMEU Policy Project, and Detention Watch Network.

The legislation comes as DHS-related violence continues to occur around the country, with the most recent shooting in New York. To this day, 58 people have died in ICE custody since January 2025, especially in for-profit private detention centers with limited oversight. For more than a year, IL-03 has been targeted, terrorized, and attacked by DHS with zero accountability. And over the last 23 years of the Department of Homeland Security, the agency has targeted and criminalized communities, militarized enforcement, and expanded the surveillance state. Congresswoman Ramirez has led the calls for accountability of DHS and its leadership.

title: Rep. Roy Asks HHS to Investigate CAIR, Islamic Groups for Potential Abuse of Taxpayer Grants and Terrorism Ties
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Chip Roy (TX-21) sent a letter to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr. asking his department to further investigate the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and several other Islamic groups for their potential abuse of taxpayer-funded grants and ties to terrorism.

The letter asks HHS to investigate whether these groups “meet the standards for suspension and debarment under federal regulations” after “new research suggests that HHS funding of terrorist-linked organizations was much more widespread than previously understood.”

The letter continues: “A recent study found nearly $80 million in HHS-originated grants to extremist groups, many with ties to foreign terrorists. The overwhelming majority were approved during the Biden-Harris administration and included cash handouts to Afghan immigrants and $14 million in grants to radical foreign groups.”

Read the full letter here.

The Daily Signal wrote an exclusive report on the letter, which you can read here.

Co-signers of the letter include: Representatives Michael Cloud (R-TX), Randy Weber (R-TX), Buddy Carter (R-GA), Randy Fine (R-FL), Clay Higgins (R-LA), Keith Self (R-TX), Andrew Clyde (R-GA), and Mary Miller (R-IL).

Rep. Roy’s Other Actions on CAIR:

On April 27, Rep. Roy sent a letter to Secretary Kennedy Jr. urging HHS to suspend funding for CAIR and its affiliates and initiate debarment proceedings after a DOJ investigation found suspected misuse in federal grants by CAIR. On June 10, following the letter, Secretary Kennedy Jr. announced his department opened an investigation.

Under Secretary Kennedy’s leadership, HHS has decisively fought against suspected fraud and misuse of taxpayer dollars at hands of opportunity groups like CAIR.

Additionally, on April 9, Rep. Roy introduced the Designating Hamas Affiliates in America Act of 2026 to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist Organization, blocking its assets and prohibiting U.S. persons from interacting with the organization.

title: SCHNEIDER BLASTS TRUMP DECISION TO LIFT SANCTIONS ON RUSSIAN DIESEL
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10), a member of the House Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, released a statement opposing President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to lower diesel prices in the U.S. as prices shoot up to over $6 a gallon.

“Nearly five years since the start of Russia’s unprovoked, illegal war against Ukraine, President Trump inexplicably continues to side with Putin and his anti-democracy agenda,” said Schneider. “Meanwhile, as American soldiers are fighting and dying in Trump’s ill-conceived war with Iran, and American families are paying the price at the pump, Russia is helping Iran target U.S. forces. President Trump is finding new ways to help Putin and worsen the state of the war in both Ukraine and the Middle East. For the more than 20 months he has been in office, Trump has had the power to impose sanctions on Russia and bring an end this war. He has chosen to do neither. Now, by lifting sanctions and allowing the United States to buy Russian diesel, the President is filling Putin’s coffers while doing little to lower diesel prices here. I will work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to block Trump’s purchases of Russian oil and stand with Ukraine in its fight for independence, sovereignty, and the West’s security.”

title: ICYMI: “Maintaining A Strong Community Is a Shared Responsibility:” Congresswoman Lee Discusses Her Life and Service in Southern Nevada
text:
LAS VEGAS, NV – Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) was featured in the October issue of the Desert Foothills Living Magazine. She discussed her years of nonprofit experience before coming to Congress, her upbringing, and life with her family.

Read more below:

Desert Foothills Living: A Life Rooted in Family, Service & Community

October 2026 | Brandilyn Hallcroft

For Susie Lee, home has always been about more than a house or a neighborhood. It is about opening the door, bringing people together, helping others feel welcome, and doing her part to strengthen the community around her.

Susie raised her two children, Nevada “Nevie” Lee, 26, and Cody Lee, 21, in Eagle Hills. The family moved to the neighborhood when Nevie was in third grade, and Summerlin became the backdrop for countless family traditions, outdoor adventures, celebrations, and everyday moments.

“I love living in Southern Nevada, and especially Summerlin,” Susie shared. “It’s been a great place to raise my children.”

Susie’s commitment to family, hard work, and community service began long before she arrived in Nevada. Born and raised in a working-class family of 10 in Canton, Ohio, she grew up as one of eight children. Her father was a military veteran who worked in a steel plant, while her mother stayed home to care for their large family.

Susie’s first job was delivering newspapers, not simply to earn spending money, but to help her parents make ends meet. After graduating from public schools, she attended Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, paying for her education through scholarships, loans, and part-time jobs. Mindful of the financial burden, she completed a five-year program that allowed her to accomplish six years of college-level work in less time.

Following graduation, Susie worked for an environmental economics consulting firm in Boston. In 1993, she moved to Las Vegas, arriving during the intense heat of August and wondering what she was doing in the middle of the desert. She soon found her purpose here.

When Jan Jones Blackhurst launched her campaign to become Nevada’s first female governor, Susie jumped at the opportunity to get involved. Although the campaign was unsuccessful, it led to another important chapter when Jones Blackhurst established the MASH Center, a one-stop resource center serving people experiencing homelessness, and asked Susie to run it.

Susie had never worked specifically in the homelessness field, but she understood nonprofit leadership. More importantly, she felt increasingly drawn to work that could create lasting opportunities for children and families.

Several years later, the late Elaine Wynn recruited Susie to establish the Inner-City Games, now known as After-School All-Stars. Susie later served as president of Communities In Schools of Nevada, helping it grow into the state’s largest dropout prevention program. Her years of nonprofit leadership ultimately helped shape her approach to public service and her work in Congress.

Throughout her career, Susie was fortunate to learn from pioneering women who served as mentors and demonstrated the difference strong leadership can make. Those lessons, combined with the values she learned from her parents, continue to guide her today.

While Susie’s professional life has centered on service, her personal life has always revolved around her children, her community, and plenty of time outdoors.

Sports were an important part of Susie’s childhood. She and her siblings participated primarily in swimming and basketball, and Susie became both a synchronized and competitive swimmer. She continued competing throughout high school and at Carnegie Mellon University.

That love of athletics was passed down to Nevie and Cody. When they were young, Susie encouraged them to try different activities until they discovered sports they genuinely enjoyed. Between the two children, those experiments included soccer, fencing, competitive swimming, and basketball. Cody eventually found his place playing lacrosse with Rough Riders Lacrosse, while Nevie participated in synchronized swimming with the Nevada Desert Mermaids. Drawing on her own experience as a collegiate swimmer, Susie even stepped in to help coach the Desert Mermaids.

Nevie was also a Girl Scout, Cody was a Boy Scout, and both children took piano lessons with Miss Maya in Summerlin. Sundays often began with a family hike in Red Rock Canyon, a tradition Susie credits with helping her children develop their own appreciation for nature.

Today, the family continues to enjoy hiking, biking, skiing, and climbing at Red Rock. Susie is an avid hiker and cyclist and can often be found on the trails at Red Rock Canyon before her workday begins. She also enjoys supporting Southern Nevada’s small businesses and restaurants and connecting with residents at local community events.

At home, Susie is joined by her two dogs, Bridger, a Labradoodle, and Teton, a Sheepadoodle. The dogs fit naturally into a family that has never needed much of an excuse to celebrate. Susie once organized a neighborhood dog birthday party, complete with a birthday cake made from dog food. She also hosted an 11/11/11 party and always made sure Nevie and Cody’s birthdays felt special.

Hosting has long been one of Susie’s favorite ways to bring people together. Thanksgiving and Easter were major occasions in the Lee household, and Susie made a point of inviting anyone who might not have somewhere else to go. At least one evening each week, friends or family could be found gathered in her backyard for a barbecue.

Her enthusiasm for creating community extended throughout Eagle Hills. When her children were younger, Susie organized neighborhood scavenger hunts that sent local kids door-to-door collecting items from houses along the block. Halloween remains her favorite holiday, and she especially loves greeting generations of trick-or-treaters at her home.

Travel is another important part of the family’s story. Whether in summer or winter, Susie, Nevie, and Cody enjoy taking an outdoor-focused trip each year. The specific destination may change, but mountains, nature, and time together remain the common thread.

After more than three decades in Las Vegas, Susie continues to appreciate the people and places that make Southern Nevada feel like home. She believes maintaining a strong

community is a shared responsibility that requires residents to participate, speak up, and remain engaged.

“Southern Nevada is an incredible place to live, work, and raise your kids, and it’s because of all the incredible residents who call it home,” Susie said. “It takes all of us to continue to keep this a great place to raise our families. We all need to pitch in, get involved, speak up, and especially, vote.”

For Susie, that message is not simply about public service. It reflects the way she has lived throughout her life: working hard, welcoming others, showing up for her neighbors, and never missing an opportunity to bring people together.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Introduces Legislation to Crack Down on Medicare Home Health Fraud and Protect Seniors
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) introduced the House companion to Senator Susan Collins' Medicare Home Health Payment Integrity and Protection Act, legislation to crack down on Medicare home health fraud, protect taxpayer dollars, and ensure seniors can continue receiving quality care in their own homes.

Fraudulent Medicare claims can distort the data used to calculate payments to home health agencies, potentially reducing reimbursements for legitimate providers across the country. These concerns have grown as suspicious billing patterns and an unusually high concentration of home health agencies in Los Angeles County have drawn scrutiny. The Medicare Home Health Payment Integrity and Protection Act would strengthen provider screening, increase inspections of high-risk agencies, and give the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) additional tools to detect and prevent fraud before payments are made. The legislation would also address potentially distorted Medicare payment rates and require CMS to examine how fraudulent claims have affected reimbursements for legitimate home health providers.

The legislation builds on Tenney's November 2025 letter to CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz urging the agency to investigate fraudulent billing practices, correct potentially distorted payment data, and prevent further harm to seniors and home health providers. In her letter, Tenney highlighted suspicious billing patterns in Los Angeles County, which accounted for nearly 10 percent of nationwide Medicare home health spending in 2024 despite representing only about 2 percent of traditional Medicare beneficiaries. She also raised concerns about access to care in NY-24, where Medicare home health utilization declined by 39 percent between 2018 and 2024.

“Home health care is a lifeline for seniors who want to remain safe and independent in their own homes,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Fraudulent providers are stealing taxpayer dollars, undermining Medicare, and putting legitimate home health agencies at risk. Seniors in Upstate and Western New York should not lose access to care because of fraudulent billing schemes across the country. Last November, I called on CMS to address this problem, and now I am joining Senator Collins to advance legislation that strengthens oversight, roots out fraud, and protects fair reimbursement for honest providers. We must protect Medicare for the seniors who depend on it and the taxpayers who fund it.”

title: Rep. Tokuda Condemns Trump Administration’s Rescission of Pacific Studies and Language Funding at UH Mānoa
text:
Hawaiʻi — U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda (HI-02) met with University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa leadership, faculty, and students to address the Trump Administration’s recent effort to rescind nearly $1 billion pocket rescission package, which included almost $70 million in cuts to Title VI international education programs that have historically supported Pacific and Asian studies, foreign-language education, and related international education programs at UH Mānoa.

UH Mānoa applied for $2.8 million in grants that would have supported the Center for Pacific Islands Studies (CPIS) and the Center for Southeast Asian Studies (CSEAS) within the College of Arts, Languages, & Letters, but no awards will be made due to the rescission. Prior funding cuts to Title VI international education programs have already contributed to the loss of numerous Pacific language courses, including Tahitian, Marshallese, and Māori, along with Foreign Language and Asian Studies (FLAS) scholarships. In addition, the recission could also force the university to eliminate court interpreter training programs, student positions, professional development opportunities, and new curriculum development.

During the meeting, Rep. Tokuda emphasized Hawaiʻi’s unique position in the Pacific and the importance of maintaining strong relationships with Pacific nations through a deep understanding of the region’s languages, cultures, and histories.

“The President does not get to pick and choose which laws to follow. Congress approved this funding, and the Administration cannot run out the clock to let it disappear. That undermines Congress’s power of the purse and ignores local needs. It is not responsible budgeting; it is cruel and shortsighted,” said Rep. Tokuda. “UH has long been the tip of the spear for language training and cultural competency in the Pacific. With the region vital to our national and financial security, cutting such a modest investment is reckless. We should strengthen these ties, not dismantle them.”

“We are deeply grateful to Congresswoman Tokuda for standing with the University of Hawaiʻi and advocating for the restoration of this critical funding,” said UH Mānoa Chancellor Vassilis Syrmos. “These programs support our students and faculty while strengthening the language, cultural, and regional expertise essential to Hawaiʻi’s unique role in the Pacific. The loss of this funding has immediate consequences for our students and programs, and we appreciate Congresswoman Tokuda’s leadership and commitment to protecting these important investments.”

Rep. Tokuda has consistently supported strong federal funding for Title VI international education programs through the annual appropriations process. This year, she joined several colleagues in a joint letter to the House Appropriations Committee requestion $86 million in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027. As Congress finalizes the FY2027 spending package, Rep. Tokuda will continue pushing to restore these funds, secure strong funding for next year, and defend Congress’s constitutional authority over federal spending.

title: Underwood Secures More Than $500,000 in Federal Funding for Child Care, Youth Homelessness, Suicide Prevention, University Research, and More in Northern Illinois
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, Representative Lauren Underwood announced a new round of federal funding she has secured for child care, youth services, university research, and crisis intervention in northern Illinois.

As a member of the Appropriations Committee, Underwood has made securing federal resources for our community a top priority. The following funds will support programs in the 14th District with federal resources:

Lewis University, Romeoville, Illinois – $125,000

Lewis University in Romeoville has been awarded $125,000 in federal funding through the Center for Mental Health Services at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

This grant will help stand up a network of supports to meet the growing mental health needs of Lewis University students. The program will provide screenings, assessments, referrals for services, training, education, and an awareness campaign. Project Safety Net will also help identify students who are at risk for suicidal behavior, increase protective factors that promote mental health, and reduce risk factors for suicide.

Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley, Ottawa, Illinois – $235,524

Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley in Ottawa has been awarded $235,524 in federal funding through the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

This grant helps create and strengthen community-based programs that meet the immediate needs of runaway and homeless youth under 18 years old. The grant is through the Basic Center Program at ACF, which also works to reunite young people with their families or locate appropriate alternative placements.

Northern Illinois University, DeKalb, Illinois – $34,064

Northern Illinois University has been awarded $34,064 in federal funding through the Office of Public Health and Science at the Department of Health and Human Services.

This grant will fund a project researching the responsible conduct of research into AI, Open Science, and Partnerships.

City of Aurora, Aurora, Illinois – $128,000

The City of Aurora has been awarded $128,000 in federal funding through Office of Justice Programs at the Department of Justice (DOJ).

This grant will fund the City of Aurora’s Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Training Program Initiative. The purpose of this project is to expand specialized training for public safety personnel to improve responses to individuals experiencing mental illness or behavioral health crises. The project will take place in Aurora, IL and will serve community members who interact with police, school resource officers, dispatchers, and detention personnel. The initiative will train and certify approximately 45 personnel through the Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board’s 40 hour CIT curriculum.

title: Vindman Takes Fight Against NextEra-Dominion Merger Directly to Virginia SCC Hearing
text:
Vindman Joins Local Elected Officials and Advocates in Calling on Regulators to Put Main Street Ahead of Wall Street

Fairfax, Va. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) delivered remarks at the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing at the Fairfax County Government Center, urging regulators to reject the proposed NextEra-Dominion merger over concerns about its impact on Virginia families and utility ratepayers.

Vindman joined local elected officials and community advocates in raising the alarm about the proposed merger, which he warned could further drive up electricity costs for Virginians already struggling with rising utility bills.

Vindman Joins Advocates & Local Officials in Rallying Against the NextEra-Dominion Merger

Prior to the hearing, Vindman joined advocates for a rally outside the Fairfax County Government Center, where attendees called for greater accountability and stronger protections for Virginia ratepayers.

“Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on, and the last thing hardworking families need is a merger that could send their utility bills even higher,” said Vindman. “The State Corporation Commission has a responsibility to protect the people it serves. That means looking out for Main Street, not Wall Street. I urge the Commission to reject this bad deal for Virginians.”

Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger. He has continued to raise concerns about rising electricity costs, corporate accountability, and the need to ensure that Virginia families are not forced to shoulder the costs of unchecked data center growth.

Vindman’s remarks, as prepared, are below. Click here to watch a video of his testimony.

—

Good evening. Thank you for holding this public event so you can hear directly from Virginians.

I’m Congressman Eugene Vindman, and I represent about 800 thousand residents in Virginia’s Seventh District.

I’m here tonight for a simple reason: I believe the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion is a bad deal for Virginians.

I urge the Commission to reject it.

I was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to speak out against this merger.

And I did so in a letter to the Commission, which I hope you all read.

Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on. I hear it everywhere I go.

Families are opening their utility bills each month wondering how much more they can possibly be expected to absorb.

This merger gives them every reason to worry that those bills will go even higher.

Here’s the thing about utilities: Virginians don’t get to shop around for their electricity provider.

Where you live determines who keeps your lights on and your home warm in the winter.

That gives utility companies enormous power, and with that power comes a responsibility to the people they serve.

It is not a license to squeeze more money out of hardworking families.

NextEra’s own record should concern us. Customers of its Florida subsidiary have seen their utility bills rise by 33 percent. Now NextEra wants to take control of the utility serving millions of Virginians.

NextEra sees enormous profits to be made in Virginia, particularly with the explosion of data centers.

But I’ve been crystal clear: data centers must pay their fair share.

Virginia families should not be subsidizing corporate expansion through higher electricity bills.

This Commission’s job is to protect Main Street, not Wall Street.

My concerns do not start and end with rates, however. I am very concerned about what this merger would do to the company’s accountability structure.

Dominion is a Virginia company. Its decisions affect Virginia families, Virginia businesses, and Virginia communities every single day.

Under the proposed ownership structure, three-quarters of the new company’s board would be controlled from Florida.

And there are serious questions about NextEra’s conduct in Florida. The company agreed to a $150 million settlement over allegations involving political interference. That sounds like corruption.

That record raises concerns about the influence this company could wield over Virginia’s energy future.

When Virginians have a problem with their power bill, they deserve answers here in Virginia.

I surveyed my constituents about this deal.

More than 950 Virginians responded, and 80 percent opposed the merger.

Their concerns were remarkably consistent, worried about higher bills, less accountability, and even more power concentrated in the hands of a massive utility.

Those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.

This Commission has a responsibility to protect Virginia ratepayers.

Electricity is an essential service, not a luxury. And the privilege of serving millions of Virginians comes with an obligation to put those customers first.

I respectfully urge you to put Virginia families ahead of Wall Street profits and reject this merger.

Thank you.

###

title: Trump Administration Announces New Funding to Support Rural Healthcare Workers and Expand Maternal Care Across Missouri
text:
Today, the Trump Administration announced more than $2.3 million in federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding to strengthen Missouri’s rural healthcare workforce and expand access to maternal care. This investment supports two targeted workforce initiatives in Missouri: expanding affordable, dependable childcare for rural healthcare professionals and delivering funding to establish a certified nurse midwife training program.

This transformational funding will deliver $1.46 million to tackle healthcare recruitment and retention challenges across rural Missouri. The funding will expand a cost-sharing childcare program that brings the state, rural health employers, and families together to make dependable childcare more affordable for healthcare workers, providing peace of mind that their loved ones are cared for while they care for their patients. In addition, $879,000 will support initial work to establish Missouri’s first certified nurse midwife training program, with rural clinical rotations designed to build a pipeline of maternal care providers for underserved communities.

The Rural Health Transformation Program is expanding access to quality healthcare, regardless of a patient’s zip code, and equipping rural health systems with the workforce and infrastructure needed to deliver timely care. This funding will make critical investments to strengthen rural healthcare, expand access to lifesaving services, and bring modern technology to communities across Missouri.

“Supporting rural healthcare workers and the community that relies on them is incredibly important. This funding will directly strengthen and expand access to maternal health care here in Missouri so moms and children have access to the care they need and deserve, and I was proud to vote for this funding in the Working Families Tax Cut legislation. I will always work to support families in Missouri and across the country, and I thank the Administration for joining me in prioritizing parents and their children,” said Rep. Ann Wagner.

“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”

“Every state knows best what its rural communities need, and thanks to President Trump’s Rural Health Transformation Program, they now have the resources to meet those needs,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “As states put these resources to work, we’re focused on turning these investments into meaningful, sustainable improvements for the health systems that serve rural Missourians.”

Today’s investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.

“As Missouri’s Rural Health Transformation Program continues to make strides in strengthening rural healthcare access with community-driven solutions, this funding brings much-needed childcare support for rural healthcare workers and expands access to critical maternal care across our state,” said Gov. Mike Kehoe. “We appreciate the Trump Administration’s continued focus and partnership in working to create stronger, healthier rural communities.”

"Rural hospitals across Missouri have been struggling for decades. Thanks to the Trump Administration, this $2.3 million award will expand access to maternal care and childcare support for rural healthcare workers. This investment will not only support our healthcare workers but also help ensure families in rural Missouri can access the quality care they deserve. I’m proud to have supported this program through the Working Families Tax Cut Act, and I’ll continue fighting to ensure rural Missourians get the care they need," said Sen. Eric Schmitt.

“This Administration has demonstrated a strong commitment to strengthening rural healthcare across Missouri, and this additional investment will build on those efforts to address critical workforce shortages and expand access to maternal care in our rural communities,” said Rep. Bob Onder. “As a physician, I know how important it is for patients to have access to quality care when they need it most. This funding will help ensure Missouri families can receive the care they need and that qualified healthcare professionals are there to provide it.”

“Rural Missouri families deserve quality care close to home, and that starts with the people who deliver it. This Rural Health Transformation Program funding is part of the largest ever single investment in rural health care through Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts. It will expand access to childcare for rural healthcare workers and stand up a certified nurse midwife training program so we can recruit and keep more caregivers in our communities. That’s real help for mothers and for the workforce that keeps rural hospitals and clinics open. I’m grateful the Trump Administration is putting these dollars to work in Missouri,” said Rep. Mark Alford.

"The future of rural healthcare depends on having a trained workforce," said Rep. Sam Graves. "This funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts law will help recruit and retain healthcare professionals, while expanding the availability of maternal care, which is critically needed in North Missouri. These types of investments are why we created the Rural Health Transformation Program, and I’m pleased to see the Trump Administration continue to direct this money to Missouri.”

“A rural mom shouldn’t have to drive an hour or more to find someone to deliver her baby. That’s exactly why I authored and fought for the Rural Health Transformation Program in the One, Big, Beautiful Bill. This funding will help Missouri recruit and retain the nurses and healthcare workers our rural communities depend on, and it will bring maternal care closer to home for families across southeast Missouri and the entire state. I’ll keep fighting to make sure rural Missouri is a place where moms can raise a family and get the care they need right where they live,” said Rep. Jason Smith.

Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Missouri for fiscal year 2026.

Key initiatives the overall RHTP funding will focus on include:

Building the rural healthcare workforce: Supporting recruitment, training, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.

Strengthening rural facilities and access: Supporting partnerships, operational improvements, and care-delivery changes that help rural providers maintain essential services and improve access.

Advancing innovative care and payment models: Supporting new approaches to delivery and financing designed to improve quality, strengthen primary care, and support sustainable rural healthcare.

Expanding community-based and preventive care: Investing in school-based care, mobile services, and other community strategies that improve prevention, address chronic disease, and expand access to care.

Modernizing rural healthcare technology: Expanding remote care and data-driven tools to improve coordination and extend healthcare services to rural communities.

The Trump Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen rural America by investing in solutions that modernize technology to promote health and well-being for rural communities. Led by CMS, the RHTP is moving beyond the failed one-size-fits-all approach and giving rural communities the tools to build stronger, more innovative, and more sustainable health systems that deliver better care and better outcomes for the Americans they serve.

title: Baldwin Secures $15 Million to Improve Highway Safety and Expand Truck Parking Along I-41 in Dodge County
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) announced she successfully secured $15 million in federal funding to boost highway safety, improve two rest areas, and expand truck parking along Interstate 41 in Dodge County. Senator Baldwin advocated for the funding to the Trump Administration, citing the corridor’s essential role in connecting Wisconsin manufacturing and agricultural industries to markets and the need to keep truck drivers and roadways safe. The funding comes through the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highway Projects (INFRA) grant program, which received an influx of resources through the Baldwin-backed Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

“Wisconsin truck drivers work hard every day to deliver the goods we rely on, support our farmers and manufacturers, and keep our Made in Wisconsin economy moving forward,” said Senator Baldwin. “But when truck drivers can't find a safe place to pull over and rest, it puts them and everyone else on the road at risk. That's why I am proud to bring home this investment that will give truck drivers more safe places to rest, help prevent accidents that clog up our highways and put folks in harm’s way, and make our roads safer for everyone who uses them.”

“WisDOT is thrilled to receive this grant to help transform two more safety rest areas in Wisconsin into modernized, safer, and accessible facilities,” said WisDOT Secretary Kristina Boardman. “We’ve already seen success applying previously awarded federal grants to upgrade safety rest areas with accessible facilities and extra truck parking in Sparta, Denmark, and Maribel. We know access to truck parking is critical to the success of Wisconsin’s manufacturers, farmers, and businesses. WisDOT’s recently completed truck parking study documented a lack of truck parking in areas of the state. This grant will help directly address that issue by adding more than 100 truck parking spaces between the two safety rest areas along a rural stretch of I-41 in Dodge County. We’re excited to get to work and make these improvements.”

The funding will be used to:

Add approximately 106 commercial truck parking spaces across two safety rest areas, Safety Rest Area 63 Lomira and Safety Rest Area 64 Theresa, along I-41, including a new staging area for oversized and overweight vehicles.

Improve highway safety by adding lighting to parking areas and entrance and exit ramps and modernizing ramp designs to meet current standards.

Upgrade rest area facilities to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and add family-friendly amenities, including changing stations.

According to WisDOT, the I-41 corridor carries approximately 35,400 vehicles per day, with commercial trucks accounting for 33-37% of traffic, connecting Wisconsin's manufacturing and agricultural industries to domestic and global markets. However, a lack of reliable truck parking contributes to unauthorized shoulder or ramp parking, putting truck drivers and American families at risk. Per WisDOT, in Wisconsin between 2017 and June 2025, approximately 93% of fatal crashes and 92% of injury crashes involving a parked CMV (Commercial Motor Vehicle) occurred when the CMV was parked in an unauthorized location.

The Baldwin-backed Bipartisan Infrastructure Law increased INFRA’s budget over five years by 78%, investing approximately $8 billion into the grant program. In July, Senator Baldwin sent a letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urging him to support this project.

title: Bipartisan Senators Call on Trump to Rescind Russian Diesel Deal & Implement Sanctions Authorized by Congress Last Month on Enablers of Putin's War Against Ukraine
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Susan Collins (R-ME), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Alan Armstrong (R-OK), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Jack Reed (D-RI), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mitch McConnell (R-KY) and John Cornyn (R-TX) wrote President Donald Trump urging him to rescind his recent agreement with President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian-origin diesel fuel into global markets.

“Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded,” the senators wrote.

The senators urged Trump to instead take swift action to implement sanctions authorized by the recently passed Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which President Trump signed into law in September.

“These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict,” the senators wrote.

The full text of the senators’ letter is available here and copied below.

Dear Mr. President,

Congress and the American people support ending the Russia-Ukraine war, which has cost hundreds of thousands of lives over the last four and a half years because Russia chose to invade its neighbor. A brokered peace, however, must be on just terms. It must uphold democratic values, the sovereignty and security of Ukraine, and their people’s right to choose their future.

The deal you struck with President Vladamir Putin on October 9th will not achieve just ends, nor will it benefit Americans. The Treasury Department’s General License No. 135, which lifts sanctions on Russia’s diesel exports, only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians. Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded.

We also recognize the urgent need to lower energy costs for American families and address the disruptions caused by the war with Iran. However, allowing Russian-origin diesel into global markets will offer limited to no relief to Americans. It will have a negligible impact on fuel prices, but the revenues the Kremlin will receive from this agreement will undoubtedly finance its desired war of attrition and advance its security cooperation with China, Iran, and North Korea. It will also endanger servicemembers operating overseas in support of Operation Epic Fury.

Last month, Congress passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which you swiftly signed into law. Both chambers passed the legislation with resounding, bipartisan votes, clearly demonstrating our intent and granting you the authorities to broker a just and fair peace. These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict. For decades, America has stood as the bastion of freedom against tyranny, and American presidents have embodied our nation’s resistance to tyrants. Putin is a tyrant. Withdraw from this agreement, rescind General License No. 135, and execute the authorities provided under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Maintain our legacy – and the duty America holds – as leader of the free world.
