title: PHOTOS: Senator Moody Brings Together Law Enforcement Professionals During Crime Prevention Month, Introduces New Legislation to Encourage Citizens to Help Fight Crime
text:
TAMPA, Fla.—Senator Ashley Moody today was joined by dozens of Florida law enforcement professionals in Tampa during National Crime Prevention Month. In Hillsborough County, Senator Moody thanked HCSO deputies and law enforcement officials from across the Tampa Bay region for what they do to keep Floridians safe and spotlighted her ongoing work to support law enforcement—including new legislation to encourage citizens to help in the fight against crime. Nationwide, the FBI recently reported a historic drop in violent crime, and Senator Moody continues to work with the administration and law enforcement to build on that progress and keep communities safe.

“It’s National Crime Prevention Month and I joined dozens of law enforcement professionals today in Tampa to thank them for all they do to protect Floridians. While it’s important that we continue working to support the important work of our law enforcement officers, it is vital that citizens are empowered to help fight crime. I worked to create a statewide tip hotline **TIPS as Attorney General, and as Senator, I’m introducing new legislation to help citizens remain anonymous when collecting reward money for helping officers make an arrest. Together, we will continue building a Stronger, Safer Florida,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

Senator Moody’s new legislation is endorsed by the Florida Association of Crime Stoppers, Florida Sheriffs Association, Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association, and National Fraternal Order of Police.

“On behalf of the Florida Association of Crime Stoppers, we applaud Senator Ashley Moody for introducing S. 5644 and for recognizing the unique role Crime Stoppers organizations play in supporting law enforcement and protecting the anonymity of those who provide critical information. Crime Stoppers has operated successfully for 50 years because citizens trust that they can provide information anonymously and, when eligible, receive a reward without compromising that anonymity. This legislation addresses an important federal reporting requirement that can create challenges when Crime Stoppers programs make cash reward payments.

“We are grateful to Senator Moody for listening to the concerns of Crime Stoppers programs and taking action to help preserve the integrity of the anonymous reward process. We deeply appreciate her leadership in the United States Senate and her continued commitment to supporting law enforcement, public safety, and the Crime Stoppers mission. S. 5644 will help ensure that Crime Stoppers organizations can continue doing what they do best—providing citizens with a safe and anonymous way to help law enforcement solve crimes and make our communities safer,” said Kelly McLaren, President, Florida Association of Crime Stoppers.

“On behalf of the Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association, representing Crime Stoppers programs across 14 states and two U.S. territories, we commend U.S. Senator Ashley Moody for introducing S. 5644 and for recognizing the importance of protecting the anonymous reward process that is fundamental to the Crime Stoppers mission. For 50 years, Crime Stoppers has provided citizens with a trusted and anonymous way to share critical information with law enforcement. The success of our programs depends upon maintaining that trust, including when eligible tipsters receive cash rewards for information that helps solve crimes and bring wanted individuals to justice.

“S. 5644 addresses a federal reporting requirement that can create challenges for Crime Stoppers organizations when issuing cash reward payments. We appreciate Senator Moody’s leadership in the United States Senate and her willingness to listen to the concerns of Crime Stoppers programs and take action on an issue that impacts programs throughout our region and across the country. The Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association is proud to support legislation that strengthens the ability of Crime Stoppers organizations to protect anonymity, support law enforcement, and continue building safer communities,” said Amy Southards, President, Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Moody recently introduced a bill to protect the anonymity of Crime Stoppers tipsters when they collect rewards for information that leads to an arrest. The bill would exempt qualifying nonprofit Crime Stoppers cash-reward transactions from certain federal currency transaction reporting requirements, addressing barriers to paying rewards while protecting tipster anonymity.

Senator Moody worked with Florida Crime Stoppers as Attorney General to enact a statewide hotline for citizens to report crime anonymously using **TIPS. Following the success of **TIPS, Moody worked with Crime Stoppers USA to enact the program nationwide. This new legislation builds upon this work by protecting citizens’ anonymity when collecting rewards for helping law enforcement make arrests.

Senator Moody is a long-time supporter of the rule of law and of law enforcement officers. Since becoming Florida’s newest Senator, Moody has:

Introduced the Halo Act to shield federal officers from those who seek to threaten and harass them on duty.

Supported the Graham Hoffman Act, which would allow the U.S. to use the full force of state and federal law to prosecute those who assault first responders and act as a deterrent to anyone considering such acts of violence.

Introduced the HELPER Act to make homeownership more obtainable for Florida heroes, including law enforcement officers.

Co-Sponsored the HALT Fentanyl Act, which was signed into law by President Trump. The new law assists law enforcement officers in getting fentanyl traffickers off the streets and permanently classifies fentanyl-related substances under Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.

Sponsored the RIPPLE Act, which would expand the 287(g) program and provide resources to state law enforcement to more efficiently get criminal illegal aliens out of communities; and

Advanced six bills to support law enforcement, strengthen public safety and deliver critical tools to officers out of the Judiciary Committee during Police Week earlier this year.

At today’s event, Senator Moody also highlighted the important work to stop the flow of deadly drugs into Florida communities.

Senator Moody continues to combat the nation’s fentanyl crisis by cosponsoring Tyler’s Law and most recently the PRESS Act.

Tyler’s Law would require HHS to issue guidance on whether hospital emergency departments should implement fentanyl testing as a routine procedure for patients experiencing an overdose.

PRESS Act would criminalize the intentional importation of pill press machines and unlisted precursor chemicals with the intent to manufacture illicit drugs.

title: Murkowski, Colleagues Urge President to Reverse Russian Diesel Deal, Enforce Sanctions
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) joined Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Susan Collins (R-ME), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Alan Armstrong (R-OK), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mitch McConnell (R-KY), and John Cornyn (R-TX) in sending a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to reverse his recent agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian-origin diesel fuel into global markets.

“Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded,” the senators wrote.

The senators urged Trump to instead take swift action to implement sanctions authorized by the recently passed Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which President Trump signed into law in September.

“These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict,” the senators wrote.

The full text of the senators’ letter is available here and copied below.

Dear Mr. President,

Congress and the American people support ending the Russia-Ukraine war, which has cost hundreds of thousands of lives over the last four and a half years because Russia chose to invade its neighbor. A brokered peace, however, must be on just terms. It must uphold democratic values, the sovereignty and security of Ukraine, and their people’s right to choose their future.

The deal you struck with President Vladamir Putin on October 9th will not achieve just ends, nor will it benefit Americans. The Treasury Department’s General License No. 135, which lifts sanctions on Russia’s diesel exports, only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians. Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded.

We also recognize the urgent need to lower energy costs for American families and address the disruptions caused by the war with Iran. However, allowing Russian-origin diesel into global markets will offer limited to no relief to Americans. It will have a negligible impact on fuel prices, but the revenues the Kremlin will receive from this agreement will undoubtedly finance its desired war of attrition and advance its security cooperation with China, Iran, and North Korea. It will also endanger servicemembers operating overseas in support of Operation Epic Fury.

Last month, Congress passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which you swiftly signed into law. Both chambers passed the legislation with resounding, bipartisan votes, clearly demonstrating our intent and granting you the authorities to broker a just and fair peace. These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict. For decades, America has stood as the bastion of freedom against tyranny, and American presidents have embodied our nation’s resistance to tyrants. Putin is a tyrant. Withdraw from this agreement, rescind General License No. 135, and execute the authorities provided under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Maintain our legacy – and the duty America holds – as leader of the free world.

title: ICYMI: Senator Murray Visits New Community Nature Center at the Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge, Highlights Longstanding Support for Conservation
text:
***PHOTOS HERE***

Ridgefield, WA – U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, toured the Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge’s new Community Nature Center, which officially opened in May. The Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge has over 5,000 acres of wetlands, grasslands, and forests along the Columbia River floodplain and is especially well known for migratory birds and waterfowl, bald eagles, sandhill cranes, and deer. The Community Nature Center is a new public space designed to be an environmental education hub and a welcoming community gathering space. The Center took several years of planning and construction and includes classroom and meeting spaces, visitor information and orientation areas, outdoor education and explorations areas, and improved trail access. It will eventually feature interactive interpretive exhibits and expanded nature exploration areas.

“As the city of Ridgefield continues to grow, the new Community Nature Center will be a valuable way to preserve the community’s connection to nature,” said Senator Murray. “This project is the product of decades of work by local, state, and Tribal partners to make sure we are not just preserving the natural beauty of our state, but that we’re making it more accessible to everyone. I’m proud to have worked to protect federal funding to help make this Center a reality.”

The project was led by the nonprofit Friends of the Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), with the goal of creating a “gateway to nature” for families, school groups, and people who may not already feel connected to outdoor spaces. The Refuge has been preparing for the Community Nature Center for over a decade, and it was part of a larger initiative to allow for a continuous 5-mile experience through the City of Ridgefield, the Refuge, and the Port of Ridgefield. In February 2021, Senator Murray sent a letter, along with Senator Cantwell and former Representative Herrera Beutler, to USFWS, pressing the agency to maintain funding in the FY22 budget for the Center after it was initially removed from the agency’s five-year plan.

In FY26, Senator Murray secured $56.7 million for Partners for Fish and Wildlife, including $1.28 million for Washington State Regional Fisheries Enhancement Groups, which carry out important ecosystem restoration projects to support salmon recovery efforts. Senator Murray also secured $5.4 million for the Lower Snake River and Columbia River Basin through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, to assist states and tribes with critical capital and maintenance projects to improve salmon and steelhead facilities along the basin.

title: Murray, Kaptur: As Families Pay More & More for Energy, Reports Show Trump Energy Department Withholding Billions and Playing Politics
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, released the following statement on the Trump administration holding back or cutting off billions of dollars Congress provided the Department of Energy to bring new energy online and lower Americans’ energy costs. Four recent reports detail how, over the last 18 months, President Trump’s policies have raised energy costs for families and delayed and defunded critical energy investments.

“President Trump hasn’t just sent gas prices through the roof with his war with Iran; he and his administration have systematically held up and cut off energy investments Congress has made that should be lowering families’ energy bills. Congress gave the Department of Energy tens of billions of dollars to build out the power grid and cut the costs that families pay to heat and cool their homes. But the Trump Administration is still holding that money back and letting politics decide which projects survive. This president’s corruption is already sending Americans’ energy bills higher. The Constitution gives Congress the power of the purse. We will keep pressing until this money reaches the projects and families it was meant for,” said Murray and Kaptur.

Congress provided funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the annual Energy and Water Development appropriations bills for a variety of cost-cutting energy investments. The funding supports power lines, grid upgrades, home energy savings, and bringing more power online. But starting in January 2025, the Trump Administration froze funds for energy programs and kept them frozen after Kaptur and Murray demanded answers. The Department announced the cancellation of 24 awards worth $3.7 billion in May 2025 and another 321 worth nearly $8 billion on October 1, 2025. In July 2026, the Department’s lawyers admitted in court that the October cancellations were based solely on the politics of each recipient’s state.

Four reports released recently show the Department of Energy is failing to spend money Congress provided—driving up Americans’ costs—and it is letting politics drive its decisions:

Recent analysis from Energy Innovation, which includes state-level impacts, found that the Trump administration’s energy policy changes since January 2025, including the Department’s cancellation of hydrogen hub funding, will cost households an additional $920 billion for energy from 2026 through 2040, or about $6,500 more in energy costs per household.

The Department of Energy Alumni Network and Lawyers for Good Government reported that a year after the Department canceled hundreds of awards, 61 percent of terminated awards remain in limbo, 69 percent of the awards the Department said it would keep have received negligible funding in the past six months, and another 1,731 projects worth $3.9 billion have heard nothing from the Department.

The Natural Resources Defense Council published internal Department records, obtained through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit, indicating that DOE’s committee reviewing awards for termination was made up entirely of political appointees and Department of Government Efficiency staff. This follows DOE’s earlier admission in court that its decision to cancel energy projects “was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state.”

The EFI Foundation found that 94 percent of the $57.5 billion Congress provided DOE through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act has still not reached recipients, and $29.3 billion, or 51 percent, has not been legally committed to any project.

title: Rosen, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Establish Federal Strategy on Critical Minerals
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV), John Hickenlooper (D-NV), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Tim Sheehy (R-MT), and Kevin Cramer (R-ND) introduced a bipartisan bill to establish a federal strategy on critical minerals. The National Critical Minerals Council Act would establish a National Critical Minerals Council to develop and implement a national strategy on critical minerals and build reliable supply chains at home and abroad. Critical minerals play a key role in powering the majority of modern technological innovations, including vehicles, smartphones, and defense systems. However, China dominates the global market, with the U.S. being 100% reliant on imports for 16 key critical minerals.

“As the world races to acquire and leverage the critical minerals that power the modern economy, the United States needs an efficient and effective plan to secure these important resources,” said Senator Rosen. “I am proud to help introduce this bipartisan bill to ensure the United States has the infrastructure it needs to secure critical minerals and remain at the forefront of modern development.”

title: AS VERIZON PROPOSES TRANSITION AWAY FROM COPPER LANDLINES, SCHUMER DEMANDS TRANSPARENCY, NO COST HIKES, AND RELIABLE SERVICE FOR RURAL NEW YORKERS
text:
Schumer Seeks Assurances From Verizon That New Yorkers—Including Seniors, Residents On Fixed Incomes, and Small Businesses—Won’t Face Higher Costs And Be Forced To Pay More For Essential Phone Service

Schumer Says Alternative Equipment Must Provide Reliable Emergency Service & 911 Access During Power Outages, Especially For Residents In Rural Communities With Limited Connectivity

Schumer To Verizon: Landlines Are Lifelines

As Verizon transitions away from copper-wire landlines, generating widespread confusion and concern for many New Yorkers, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer today called on Verizon to ensure that all New Yorkers have uninterrupted, reliable service, are protected from higher costs, and will be provided transparency from the company about what any new, alternative technologies might mean for them, including their ability to contact emergency services and stay connected during power outages.

Verizon is currently seeking approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to discontinue legacy plain old telephone service (POTS) delivered over copper. Customers in New York who utilize copper-wire landlines, many of whom are seniors as well as residents of rural communities, are worried about what this means for the reliability and accessibility of service. Schumer demanded answers from Verizon and said the company must engage with residents to ensure there are no safety, reliability, and connectivity challenges.

“As Verizon moves to transition away from copper landlines, Upstate New Yorkers are concerned about losing a vital connection. They deserve clear answers about what this means for their ability to stay connected and make ends meet. That’s why I’m turning up the volume on Verizon, demanding transparency, affordability, and a commitment to working with communities to make sure this critical service is not interrupted for customers now connected via copper landlines,” said Senator Schumer. “Verizon must guarantee that this transition will not mean higher costs—especially for seniors, residents on fixed incomes, or small businesses—and that any alternative options will provide reliable service to contact emergency services, including during power outages. This is crucial in rural Upstate communities where there are limited connectivity options.”

Verizon is currently transitioning away from copper-wire landlines, which can be expensive and time-consuming to repair, according to the company, towards other alternatives like fiber, fixed wireless, cellular wireless, and satellite. Currently, the company is sending notices to customers in New York and across the country who still use copper landlines. As New Yorkers receive these letters, many residents are worried they will lose service, not have a reliable connection during a time of need, or be forced to pay more if the FCC approves this change. Schumer underscored that for seniors, landlines are lifelines, and that modernizing Verizon’s network should not come at the cost of small businesses and those on fixed incomes.

In addition, across Upstate New York, residents in rural communities continue to rely on traditional copper landlines as a critical lifeline during natural disasters and other emergencies. Traditional POTS can remain operational during power outages because the line is powered from the telephone network, rather than solely from electricity in a home. Traditional copper service provides a well-established fixed connection to a specific service address, while replacement technologies can introduce additional questions about wireless coverage, power backup, indoor signal strength, network congestion, and the performance of connected devices during emergencies. For many rural households, cell service is unreliable, and newer, modern infrastructure alternatives like fiber may not yet reach their homes or communities. These reliable landlines are vital for seniors and rural residents to ensure they can contact emergency services when they need them most, especially in areas with weak or nonexistent cellular coverage or access to broadband.

Schumer also described how, according to local fire inspectors, there are many small businesses and restaurants that still use copper landlines for their fire alarm dialups. This change could cost these small businesses thousands of dollars to transition to new alternatives, such as cell or internet dialups, depending on the size of the system they need. Some small businesses have or are actively transitioning, but those that have not could potentially face compliance violations and increased costs associated with the change.

Schumer explained that Verizon has filed two separate applications seeking authority to discontinue legacy copper-based POTS service. The first covers portions of nine states. A second application filed on September 9 covers portions of nine additional states, including New York, as well as the District of Columbia. Schumer is also urging the FCC to extend the review timeline of the second application, which applies to New York, to ensure that the proposal can be fully assessed and that customers can be directly informed by Verizon as to what any potential changes at their home or business might mean for them.

The Communications Workers of America (CWA) has opposed the FCC’s Network Modernization Order under Chairman Brendan Carr, in which the Commission removed essential protections under Section 214, eliminated traditional network change filings, greenlit replacement alternatives such as basic 5/1 Mbps mobile wireless or third-party voice, and preempted state and local regulations that impede service discontinuance. CWA, consumer advocates, and local officials are concerned that dismantling oversight without enforceable protections applicable to major carriers threatens service reliability, 911 emergency access, backup power during outages, and telecommunications jobs.

Schumer’s letter to Verizon can be found HERE or below:

Dear Mr. Schulman,

I write today amid reports that Verizon is seeking approval from the Federal Communications Commission to phase out traditional copper-based landline service. Many residents across New York have already begun receiving notices about the transition from copper to other alternatives and are concerned about what these changes will mean for them.

Across Upstate New York, many areas and rural communities have weak or nonexistent cellular coverage or access to broadband. Copper landlines have been essential for rural and senior citizens to stay connected and access help, keep small businesses up and running, and help New Yorkers stay connected in cellular dead zones as well as during power outages.

As Verizon begins to transition away from copper landlines for modern alternatives like fiber or wireless, I implore you to ensure no household sees their service interrupted or costs increased. Furthermore, I request a written response to the following questions that have been raised by constituents and community leaders:

Will Verizon physically test service at the customer's premises—or is it relying solely on FCC coverage maps, carrier coverage maps, or database information?

What does Verizon consider to be an “equivalent replacement” for a plain old telephone service copper landline?

How will the viability of new technologies—such as fiber, wireless, and satellite—be assessed for each address in New York?

What is the specific process that Verizon follows when determining if an equivalent replacement is an adequate alternative?

Will the replacement remain available during severe weather, extended power outages, cellular network congestion, many calling 911 simultaneously?

Will Verizon certify that each proposed replacement technology is compatible with fire alarm communicators, medical alert systems, elevator emergency phones, security systems, fax machines, and other equipment currently connected to copper POTS?

How and when will customers be informed of Verizon’s determination regarding whether their residence is equipped to receive an equivalent replacement service?

How can customers challenge Verizon’s determination that an equivalent replacement is an adequate alternative?

Will Verizon commit to not disconnecting copper connections while a customer is actively disputing the adequacy of the replacement?

If replacement equipment fails, and telephone service becomes unable, what is Verizon’s restoration time?

How long will Verizon’s replacement service—including battery backup—remain operational during a power outage?

What will the total cost to the customer be when the copper landline service is replaced—including all charges, equipment, taxes, installation, activation, battery back-ups, wiring, early termination, bunded-service requirements, and fees?

Will Verizon guarantee that customers will not pay more for the replacement service than they currently pay for their plain old telephone landline?

Will the price be guaranteed for a specific period of time, or can Verizon increase the rate after the customer is forced to transition?

Will customers have an opportunity to demonstrate that the replacement is inadequate based on actual service conditions at their address?

Will Verizon commit to conducting additional outreach to rural communities, seniors, customers with disabilities, and small businesses that may have greater difficulty transitioning from copper-based service?

While I am encouraged to see Verizon promise continued service to those without FCC-approved alternative equipment, I urge you to transparently engage with customers and work diligently to ensure that customers have all the information they need regarding this proposal. I appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.

###

title: Sens. Scott, Padilla introduce bill to bridge gap in veteran services
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) introduced the Building Readiness and Integration for Dependents Going to Civilian Environments (BRIDGE) Act of 2026, legislation to support military and veteran families during the transition from military to civilian life. This bill would establish a pilot program focused on practical tools, peer support, and community engagement to improve emotional, social, and financial outcomes for transitioning families.

Thousands of service members leave the Armed Forces and face significant challenges navigating employment, healthcare, education, benefits, and community reintegration. While the Department of Defense’s Transition Assistance Program provides important pre-separation services, many military families still struggle to access personalized and coordinated support during this major life transition.

This bill would establish a Department of Defense (DoD) pilot program to provide support through community connections and additional resources to assist service members and their families. This legislation also addresses the gap by providing whole-family support, building community connections, reducing isolation, and equipping families with the tools to thrive during and after the transition.

“South Carolina is blessed to be home to thousands of our nation’s heroes,” said Sen. Scott. “The men and women of the Armed Forces – and their families who have sacrificed alongside them – have earned the best possible support as they transition to civilian life. The BRIDGE Act empowers local communities to provide military families with tailored assistance, because the best solutions are often built closest to home.”

“For too long, the servicemembers and their families have had to navigate the transition from military to civilian life without the resources needed to thrive,” said Sen. Padilla. “We must do more to ensure that military families have the support they need after they leave active duty. Our bipartisan BRIDGE Act would create a pilot program to help us prioritize programs that focus on bridging the gap in services for veterans and military families.”

The bill is endorsed by Blue Star Families, Wounded Warrior Project, American Legion, National Military Family Association (NMFA), Veterans of Foreign Wars, and Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS).

“Our 2025 Military Family Lifestyle Survey found that 58% of respondents described their transition from military to civilian life as ‘difficult’ or ‘very difficult,’” said Blue Star Families CEO Kathy Roth-Douquet. “The BRIDGE Act recognizes that successful transition requires personalized, whole-family support that helps families build long-term stability, resilience, and connection as they move into civilian life. We are grateful to Sens. Padilla (D-CA) and Scott (R-S.C.) for championing this legislation and for their continued leadership in support of military and veteran families.”

“The BRIDGE Act recognizes that transitioning from military service is a major life change for both Service members and their families,” said Jose Ramos, vice president for government and community relations, Wounded Warrior Project. “By expanding access to personalized, community-based transition support, this pilot program helps address critical gaps in employment, wellness, and family readiness as military families move into civilian life. Wounded Warrior Project appreciates Alex Padilla’s leadership and urges Congress to advance the BRIDGE Act and help strengthen the Transition Assistance Program for future generations of Service members and their families.”

Specifically, the legislation would strengthen transition support by:

Establishing a three-year DoD pilot program at four military installations to provide community-based, whole-family transition support for service members and families transitioning to civilian life.

Providing personalized services for service members within one year of separation and their families, including peer support, spouse employment assistance, skills training, benefits navigation, and dedicated transition coordinators to build individualized transition plans.

Require DoD and Veterans Affairs (VA) coordination, prioritizing service members facing involuntary or accelerated separations, and requiring tracking of employment, financial stability, and family wellbeing outcomes with a final report to Congress.

title: Rep. Young Kim Convenes Roundtable to Accelerate Adoption of Next-Generation Firefighting Technologies
text:
ORANGE COUNTY, CA – Today, Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) convened a roundtable of federal, state, and local firefighting agencies, wildfire innovation and policy partners, and wildfire technology companies to discuss barriers to adopting cutting-edge wildfire technologies and how the federal government can help get lifesaving tools onto the fireground faster.

Participants included the Orange County Fire Authority, Anaheim Fire and Rescue, City of Orange Fire Department, U.S. Wildland Fire Service, U.S. Forest Service, FireWERX, Irvine Ranch Conservancy, Megafire Action, ALERTCalifornia, Earth Fire Alliance, Metrea, Paladin, and Tablet.

While state and local agencies are advancing wildfire innovation, federal land management agencies lack a streamlined process to test and deploy emerging technologies. The Orange County Fire Authority has established its own Fire Innovation Unit, and California recently passed SB 1079 to create a similar unit within CAL FIRE.

Rep. Kim’s Fire Innovation Unit Act would bring this approach to the federal level by allowing companies, nonprofits, and universities to test new tools alongside firefighting agencies. The legislation would establish clear performance standards and coordinate procurement to help proven technologies move more quickly from testing to the fire line.

“Our first responders are stretched thin, and we need every tool available to protect our communities,” said Rep. Young Kim. “Many of these tools already exist, and innovators are developing even more, but too many face barriers to testing and adoption. I appreciate our fire chiefs, federal partners, and wildfire innovators coming together to identify where coordination breaks down. I look forward to bringing their insights back to Congress and working with my colleagues to cut through red tape and get the very best technology into our first responders’ hands.”

“As wildfire season grows in scope and intensity, the fire service must continuously evolve at an equal or greater pace,” said TJ McGovern, Fire Chief of the Orange County Fire Authority. “OCFA has long harnessed emerging technology to transform wildland firefighting, and Congresswoman Kim’s leadership in bringing key partners together will help accelerate that innovation and better protect firefighters and the communities we serve.”

“We are grateful to Representative Young Kim for convening this roundtable and for her leadership on wildfire. FireWERX supports agency-led Fire Innovation Units that evaluate and adopt the most promising innovations to end the wildfire crisis, so firefighters have what they need and communities are safer and more resilient.”

title: Amo Visits Solid State Power to Highlight Ocean State Manufacturing on Blue Economy Tour
text:
Pawtucket, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) continued his Blue Economy tour with a stop at Solid State Power’s manufacturing facility in Pawtucket to highlight the importance of new battery technology to maritime innovation.

“Rhode Island manufacturers, like Solid State Power, are developing cutting-edge battery technology, creating good-paying jobs, and propelling our state’s Blue Economy into the future,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “It was an honor to meet with Solid State’s team and tour their newly expanded facility in Pawtucket. Whether making our marinas cleaner or powering submersibles exploring the deepest wells of our oceans, their team of engineers and technicians are making discovery possible and maritime battery power a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels. I will keep supporting their innovative work in Congress and fighting for federal policies so Rhode Islanders can keep building the technology fueling our Blue Economy.”

“Advanced energy systems are quickly becoming critical infrastructure for our Navy, our commercial fleets, and the autonomous platforms reshaping maritime operations. Rhode Island has the engineering talent and ocean heritage to lead in this space, and Solid State Power is proud to be building that capability in Pawtucket,” said Tom Calef, President and CEO of Solid State Power. “We appreciate Congressman Amo's leadership in making sure companies like ours have the support to grow and hire here at home.”

Background

Congressman Amo kicked off his 2026 Blue Economy Tour with a visit to REGENT Craft, where he helped cut the ribbon on their new electric Seaglider factory. Next, Amo visited Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities. Then, Congressman Amo toured Hinckley Yachts’ expanded Portsmouth facility, highlighting the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy.

Rhode Island’s Blue Economy directly employs 36,000 Rhode Islanders and contributes over $5 billion to the state’s gross domestic product every year.

In 2024, Congressman Amo toured Rhode Island’s First Congressional District to highlight the Ocean State’s leadership in the Blue Economy across labor, education, business, and defense.

title: Ansari, Stanton, Grijalva Press GardaWorld Over Unanswered Questions After Company Secures New $1.2 Billion ICE Contract
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. RepresentativesYassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) demand answers from GardaWorld Federal Services (GWFS) following its latest $1.2 billion contract to expand immigration detention facilities in Florence, Arizona. The lawmakers also pressed the company to answer questions it failed to address in a previous inquiry related to the Surprise warehouse facility.

The new contract, awarded September 21, raises fresh concerns about transparency and coordination with local governments. According to reporting, the Town of Florence was not notified of the planned expansion and had no additional information about the contract.

"It is deeply concerning that, despite the significant scale of these projects and their potential impact on surrounding communities, local governments continue to learn about them only after contracts have been awarded," the lawmakers wrote.

The letter also presses GWFS on questions left unanswered from the lawmakers’ March 2026 inquiry into its contract with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to convert a warehouse in Surprise into an immigration detention facility. In its April response, GWFS deferred many questions to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and failed to address basic questions about its own detention experience, staffing, facility assessments, and subcontracting plans. The lawmakers are demanding full answers.

The lawmakers also raised concerns about GWFS' previously undisclosed role in the environmental review of the Surprise warehouse. The City of Surprise revealed that a company representative had requested information for the assessment, despite neither GWFS nor federal agencies publicly disclosing its involvement.

The lawmakers are requesting written responses within 15 business days of receipt of the letter, including answers about:

Experience and staffing: GWFS' qualifications to manage both projects, personnel overseeing operations, and plans to subcontract construction, medical care, staffing, or facility management.

Facility safety: Structural and code-compliance assessments of the Surprise warehouse, including plans for ventilation, extreme heat mitigation, fire safety, and medical care.

Environmental review: GWFS' role in the Surprise environmental assessment and its experience conducting comparable federal reviews.

Florence expansion: Specific projects, facilities, and task orders planned under the $1.2 billion contract, including their scope and cost.

Local coordination: Consultations with Surprise, Florence, Maricopa and Pinal counties, school districts, and public safety agencies.

Taxpayer costs: Whether GWFS or DHS will cover increased demands for emergency medical services, fire protection, and law enforcement rather than shifting those costs to local taxpayers.

"The communities surrounding the Surprise and Florence facilities deserve transparency," the lawmakers concluded.

title: Rep. Ansari Celebrates Her Bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act Becoming Law
text:
The legislation marks Ansari’s first bill passed into law

WASHINGTON – Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) celebrated the recent signing into law of her bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act, legislation to increase transparency and accountability for taxpayer-funded federal projects that are significantly over budget or behind schedule. President Donald Trump signed the bill into law following its passage in both chambers of Congress.

“The American people deserve transparency and accountability for how their tax dollars are spent, especially as families struggle with the rising costs of everyday essentials,” said Rep. Ansari. “While the level of corruption across the federal government right now is stunning and unprecedented, this is a truly longstanding, bipartisan issue. Taxpayers deserve this transparency. And now they’ll have a great deal more.”

Text of Rep. Ansari’s Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act HERE.

The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act requires the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to compile and submit an annual report to Congress identifying qualifying taxpayer-funded projects and detailing changes to their scope, estimated costs, and projected completion dates. The reporting requirement will give the public greater insight into federal projects experiencing significant delays or cost overruns.

The House of Representatives originally passed the legislation in July 2026. The Senate approved the bill in September, sending it to the President for his signature and final enactment into law.

Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.govto learn more.

title: Balint, McGovern Meet with Vermont and Massachusetts   Businesses on U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions
text:
BRATTLEBORO, VT — Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Becca Balint (VT-AL) and Jim McGovern (MA-02) met with Vermont and Massachusetts business owners to discuss the economic consequences of Trump’s ongoing trade tensions with Canada. The roundtable, held in Brattleboro, included Canadian Consul General Bernadette Jordan and the Director of Economic Affairs from the Quebec Government Office in Boston, and gave business owners an opportunity to share how tariffs and unpredictable trade policy are negatively affecting their costs, customers, employees, and ability to plan for the future.

The meeting also underscored the importance of maintaining strong relationships between communities on both sides of the border. Business owners and regional stakeholders emphasized that cross-border commerce supports jobs, sustains rural industries, and connects families and communities throughout Vermont, Massachusetts, and the New England region.

“Vermont and Canada have been neighbors, partners, and friends for generations,” said Congresswoman Becca Balint. “As a part of this conversation, we heard directly from business owners who are paying the price for this administration’s reckless trade war. They are facing higher costs, losing customers, and putting plans for growth on hold because they can’t count on the rules staying the same. That uncertainty hurts workers, families, farmers, and small businesses across Vermont and broader New England. I’m grateful to Rep. McGovern for joining us in standing up for our regional economy. We need a stable, predictable trade relationship with Canada, and I’ll keep working with him and our partners across the region to push for a trade policy that reflects our shared economic interests and gives our businesses the stability they need to succeed.”

“Trump’s trade war with Canada is destroying American businesses and livelihoods,” said Congressman Jim McGovern. “It was heartbreaking to hear from small business owners in Massachusetts and Vermont about how these tariffs are devastating their businesses. Let’s be clear: Canada isn’t paying Trump’s tariff tax. American workers, families, and small businesses are. Trump’s tariffs are wrecking our economy, killing jobs, driving businesses to the brink, and damaging our relationship with one of our closest trading partners. Congresswoman Balint and I will keep fighting to overturn these illegal tariffs, protect our small businesses, and put working people first.”

New England’s regional economy is deeply connected to Canada through agriculture, forestry, manufacturing, tourism, and cross-border supply chains. Businesses participating in the discussion described additional costs ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars, lost Canadian customers, delayed investments, and difficult decisions about staffing and production.

For many businesses, the uncertainty surrounding trade policy is compounding the financial strain. Companies are being forced to reconsider suppliers, absorb additional expenses, raise prices, delay investments and equipment upgrades, and devote significant staff time to navigating changing rules and pursuing tariff relief.

Representatives Balint and McGovern are committed to bringing the concerns raised during the discussion back to Washington and continuing to work toward a more stable U.S.-Canada trade relationship that supports New England’s workers and businesses.

text:

title: The Washington Post op-ed on Smith's legislation'The U.S. can’t ignore the horrors of forced organ harvesting'
text:
By Robert P. George

Published October 14, 2026

Robert P. George is the McCormick professor of jurisprudence and director of the James Madison Program in American Ideals and Institutions at Princeton University.

More than 170,000 solid organ transplants are performed each year, yet that constitutes less than 10 percent of global demand. Nefarious actors have long been keen to fill the gap through what international law describes as coercion, deception and abuse of power or of a position of vulnerability. The organ trade is estimated to generate between $840 million and $1.7 billion annually.

Many Americans have heard of the most egregious examples of forced organ harvesting. Communist China has been credibly accused of targeting members of ethnic and religious minority groups, such as Falun Gong and Uyghur Muslims, who are disfavored or regarded as a threat to the state.

The practice is a reality in many other parts of the world as well. Britain’s first successful prosecution for organ trafficking under the Modern Slavery Act took place in 2023. A 21-year-old Nigerian man had been brought to London for what he was told was a new job. In reality, the man’s host, a doctor, was planning to remove one of his kidneys in a private operation for the daughter of a Nigerian senator. Lagos state, in southwest Nigeria, enacted an organ harvesting prohibition law in 2024 in part because of threats of ritual harvesting and human sacrifice.

(Illustration by Michelle Kondrich/The Washington Post; iStock)

Closer to U.S. soil, Latin American cartels are getting involved in the illegal organ trade. A tragic case came to light last year in which the Jalisco New Generation Cartel allegedly performed Caesarean sections, killing the mothers to harvest their organs and sell the babies to families in the United States. According to intelligence officials, these infants were exchanged for roughly $14,000 each.

Organ donation can be a lifesaving gift of modern medicine. It must never, however, be an occasion of injustice or an assault on the sanctity of human life. Nor may it be conducted in such a way as to instrumentalize people, in effect treating the lives and well-being of some as worth more than others. Wherever people forget that all human lives have fundamental and equal value, such moral catastrophes abound. The Department of Health and Human Services, for example, recently decertified Network for Hope, a prominent organ donation provider based in Kentucky, because of concerns that “potential donors may not have been deceased at the time organ procurement was initiated.” (The group “strongly disagrees” with the decision and plans to appeal it.)

It was good news, therefore, that in May 2025 the U.S. House considered H.R. 1503, the Stop Forced Organ Harvesting Act, from Rep. Chris Smith (R-New Jersey). The proposal, which passed by a vote of 406-1, affirms that it will be U.S. policy “to combat international trafficking in persons for purposes of the removal of organs” and to “hold accountable” anyone implicated in the practice. The bill now awaits a vote in the Senate, where it has stalled for months.

It could be that some members of that chamber wonder why Americans should care about violations of human rights in other countries. The answer lies in the Declaration of Independence and Constitution, which recognize that those rights aren’t granted by any government. No merely human authority created them, and no merely human authority may legitimately violate them. Thus, if another country attempts to do so or permits anyone else to, the U.S. ought to take such information seriously as it formulates its foreign policy. The provisions of the Stop Forced Organ Harvesting Act — imposing sanctions, asset freezes, visa bans and passport revocations on those complicit — would make clear that the U.S. opposes the theft of organs wherever it occurs.

That’s of a piece with long-standing policy on similar matters. The U.S. has affirmed the importance of human dignity through international treaties and conventions that oblige us to defend the vulnerable and condemn states that abuse human rights. One of these documents is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a great moral achievement in the wake of two world wars. Like our own Declaration, it reminds us that humans have worth — dignity — not in virtue of any special qualities (strength, beauty, intelligence, social standing), but simply because of their humanity. As its first article states: “They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.”

I’ve seen firsthand how policymakers can protect human dignity in practice. In 2015-16, when I served as chairman of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, we successfully called on the State Department to continue designating all severe violators of religious freedom as “countries of particular concern,” including China. We even addressed the subject of organ harvesting in China, especially the targeting of Falun Gong members, though we didn’t know nearly as much as we know now about the scope of the evil, such as the additional targeting of Uyghurs, Tibetans and Christians.

Identifying countries in this manner gives the government a toolbox of policy options to pressure offenders. The Stop Forced Organ Harvesting Act would do the same to individuals and entities that are complicit in such abuses.

title: CORREA INTRODUCES BILL TO PREVENT AND TREAT SILICOSIS, PROTECT WORKERS IN ORANGE COUNTY
text:
Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act would fund education, screening, and care for workers exposed to silica

ANAHEIM, Calif. – Representatives Lou Correa (CA-46) and Maxine Dexter (OR-3) introduced the Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act, which would create a federal grant program to help healthcare facilities educate the public about silicosis and provide prevention and treatment measures for those affected.

Silicosis is entirely preventable by stopping silica dust from entering the lungs. Because there is no cure or way to reverse the lung damage it causes, prevention is vital.

"No worker should lose their ability to breathe because of the job they do to support their family," said Congressman Lou Correa. "In Anaheim's Tile Mile, workers who cut manufactured stone countertops are being diagnosed with silicosis at alarming rates. Silicosis is preventable, and early detection can save lives. This bill puts resources into the hands of the clinics and hospitals that treat these workers, so they get the care they need before it's too late."

"A paycheck should never come at the cost of your ability to breathe,” said Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. “As a pulmonologist, I know the devastating impacts of lung disease. As cases rapidly increase, it is critical that we are educating those that are most at risk for this irreversible disease. The Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act will create funding for healthcare facilities to disseminate information and raise awareness about this progressive lung disease. We must protect the people whose hard work builds our communities."

The Silicosis Prevention and Treatment Act creates a grant program to award healthcare providers with federal funding to:

Conduct outreach and education to increase awareness of silicosis

Provide screening, diagnosis, and treatment of silicosis

Education programs for patients, family members, and workers in industries heavily impacted by silicosis

Pulmonary rehabilitation and other patient care and coordination

Read the bill text here.

Background

Silica is a common mineral found in sand, quartz, and other types of rock. Exposure can cause silicosis, a disease that scars the lungs, makes breathing difficult, and can lead to irreversible complications. Approximately 2.3 million people are exposed to silica on the job, including in construction and mining.

Correa's district is home to the Tile Mile in Anaheim, where many workers cut and fabricate manufactured stone countertops, a process that releases silica dust. Orange County alone accounts for 135+ of California’s 662+ confirmed silicosis cases.

There is no cure for silicosis, but awareness and early treatment can help people identify symptoms sooner and prevent or manage lung damage.

title: CORREA PRESENTS $1,092,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO ELIMINATE PFAS CONTAMINATION FROM IMPACTED WATER WELLS
text:
Funding will ease costs for Santa Ana ratepayers, who would otherwise bear the full cost of well improvements

SANTA ANA, Calif. – Today, U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) presented a check for $1,092,000 in federal funding to the City of Santa Ana to fund the project to eliminate PFAS contamination from impacted water wells.

“This is the third time I have secured federal funding to support the betterment of our water, with over $5.5 million having been allocated to funding water treatment, clean water well construction, and contamination cleanup projects in our district,” said Rep. Correa. “These funds will ensure compliance with California state and federal drinking water health standards and provide our residents a safe, local, drought-proof water supply for years to come. I’m proud that our cities continually rank near the top in California for meeting safety standards and know that we will continue to preserve that legacy.”

“Access to clean and safe drinking water is essential to the health and well-being of our community. This $1 million investment will help Santa Ana strengthen its water infrastructure and address contaminants like PFAS, ensuring we continue to provide high-quality drinking water for our residents and future generations. We are grateful to Congressman Correa for his continued partnership and commitment to securing critical federal resources that directly benefit Santa Ana families,” said Santa Ana Mayor Valerie Amezcua.

The Orange County Groundwater Basin, an underground aquifer system, supplies approximately 85% of the drinking water for 2.5 million residents in north and central Orange County. Santa Ana relies heavily on the basin, and PFAS have been detected in 15 of the city's 20 drinking water wells.

Santa Ana and other affected water retailers have built PFAS treatment facilities, a response expected to cost approximately $100 million. That burden falls on ratepayers, many of whom meet California's definition of disadvantaged or low-income. Losing this local supply would mean importing water, raising costs for the communities least able to afford it.

The federal funding secured by Rep. Correa will remove PFAS contamination from impacted wells, which will ease costs for local ratepayers and support compliance with California state and federal drinking water health standards.

Rep. Correa secured funds for this project through the FY26 community project funding process, during which the congressman secured $14.4 million for CA-46 projects.

title: Dingell, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Delay 340B Rebate Model, Protect Access to Affordable Medicine
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (R-PA-08), Tracey Mann (R-KS-01), and Lois Frankel (D-FL-22) introduced the 340B Rebate Model Delay Act, bipartisan legislation to delay implementation of the federal government’s 340B rebate model, citing concerns that the new system could create significant financial and administrative risks for healthcare providers and patients.

“Families in Michigan are already struggling to pay for healthcare,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “Safety-net providers are not in the financial position to front this money, especially in light of Medicaid cuts, and will either have to hike up prices for patients or stop offering lifesaving drugs. This bill would delay the implementation of this rebate model so we can ensure people’s lives are not put at risk.”

Under the rebate model, participating providers would pay the full price of certain prescription drugs upfront and receive the 340B discount later through rebates. This could create cash-flow pressures, increase administrative burdens, and make it more difficult for community health centers, hospitals, and other safety-net providers to maintain access to affordable medications.

“Patients and providers should not have to bear the risks of an untested change to a program that helps deliver affordable medicines to communities across the country,” said Congressman Bresnahan. “Congress needs more time to evaluate the potential financial and administrative consequences of the rebate model and ensure that any changes to 340B protect patients and the providers who serve them.”

“Rural hospitals and health care providers across the Big First District rely on the 340B program to stretch limited resources and continue providing quality care close to home,” said Congressman Mann. “The new rebate model would force these providers to pay higher upfront costs and wait to be reimbursed, putting unnecessary financial strain on facilities that already operate on tight margins. This legislation provides certainty for our rural health care providers by stopping the rebate model through 2028 and protecting their ability to serve patients in rural communities.”

“Safety-net hospitals and community health centers are lifelines for low-income families, seniors, and people without health insurance,”said Congresswoman Lois Frankel.“Our bipartisan bill stops a new requirement forcing these providers to pay full price for prescription drugs and then wait for rebates. Their limited resources should go toward caring for patients, not waiting for drug companies to pay them back. We should be making it easier for people to get the medicine they need, not putting more financial strain on the hospitals and clinics they depend on.”

The 340B Drug Pricing Program allows eligible healthcare providers serving underserved communities to purchase covered outpatient drugs at discounted prices and stretch limited resources to provide care.

Bill text can be found HERE.

title: Rep. Fischbach Joins Minnesota Republican Delegation to Demand Increased Election Security
text:
Washington, DC - Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) joined Minnesota’s Republican congressional delegation in sending a letter to Governor Tim Walz and Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon regarding the recent indictments of noncitizens voting in Minnesota’s elections and demanding election security.

"Only American citizens should vote in American elections, and these indictments prove why we need the SAVE America Act signed into law," said Rep. Fischbach. "I have pushed for voter integrity and voter transparency. Now Walz, Simon, and Minnesota Democrats must do the same."

Background:

On September 30, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) announced that a federal grand jury indicted ten individuals for voter fraud, charging them with falsely claiming citizenship to vote in Minnesota’s elections, including the 2022 and 2024 general elections and the 2026 primary election. All of this follows over a year of requests from the DOJ for information on Minnesota’s voter lists and compliance with federal election guidelines.

Minnesota’s election laws have created an ideal environment for voter fraud. Over the last several years, Congresswoman Fischbach and Minnesota Republicans took the following actions to sound the alarm on Minnesota’s election security weaknesses:

On January 31, 2023, Congresswoman Fischbach joined Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil and the Minnesota Republican delegation in sending a letter to Secretary Simon asking how his office plans to investigate claims that DACA recipients and other noncitizens were voting in Minnesota’s elections.

On October 2, 2024, Congresswoman Fischbach again joined Chairman Steil and the Minnesota Republican delegation in sending a letter to Secretary Simon and Minnesota Department of Public Safety Commissioner Bob Jacobson to voice their concerns over reports that noncitizens in Minnesota have been receiving ballots.

On November 20, 2024, Congresswoman Fischbach and the Minnesota Republican delegation sent a letter to Secretary Simon demanding that his office take action to restore trust in Minnesota’s election process.

On December 23, 2024, Congresswoman Fischbach and the Minnesota Republican delegation sent a letter to Secretary Simon demanding transparency after it was confirmed that 20 ballots were likely illegally disposed of in Shakopee’s 10th precinct.

title: Garamendi Statement on Trump Lifting Russian Fuel Sanctions
text:
FAIRFIELD, CA – Today, Rep John Garamendi (D-CA-08), a senior member of the House Armed Services, released the following statement on President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel fuel:

“President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel fuel and reach an agreement with Vladimir Putin to bring more than 300,000 tons of Russian diesel onto American and global markets is a terrible decision.

“This amount of fuel represents less than a single day of diesel consumption by the American transportation sector and will do little to meaningfully reduce the price Americans pay at the pump. More importantly, allowing Russia to sell this fuel undermines American national security and provides additional revenue to Putin as he continues his brutal war of aggression against Ukraine.

“The national security implications extend well beyond Ukraine. Russia is actively supporting Iran, a country currently at war with the United States. According to U.S. intelligence reporting, Russia has provided Iran with information that could help its military target American warships, aircraft, and other military assets throughout the Middle East. This intelligence assistance threatens the lives of American service members who are already facing Iranian attacks.

“At a time when Russia is helping Iran target American forces, President Trump is opening the door for hundreds of millions of dollars in additional Russian diesel sales. That revenue strengthens the Russian economy and undermines our efforts to pressure Putin to end his aggression.

“The United States has imposed strong economic sanctions on Russia for good reason. Those sanctions are intended to deny Putin the resources necessary to sustain his war against Ukraine and threaten American national security interests.

“We should not be easing economic pressure on a country that is helping our enemies target American troops. President Trump’s decision contradicts our national security objectives, undermines our support for Ukraine, and puts American interests at risk. He should reverse it immediately.

title: Congressman Gonzalez Delivers Over $9 Million in Federal Funds for Cameron County
text:
Washington, D.C.—Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) announced $9,182,608 in federal funds for Cameron County to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue and provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry. The project will include roughly 305 dedicated parking truck spaces. This investment will also support roadway improvements, driver amenities, security features, an automated weight station, and intelligent parking system technology.

“South Texas is an international hub for trade and commerce, and our infrastructure must keep pace with heightened demands,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “As working families continue to struggle with rising costs, this $9.1 million federal investment will provide commercial truckers with support to maintain efficient operations when supplying our region and the rest of the country with goods and materials. As your Congressman, I proudly passed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that authorized this funding, and I will continue working to ensure our ports of entry and the workers who keep it running have the resources they need to operate efficiently.”

title: Reps. Haridopolos and McClellan Introduce Legislation to Establish National American History and Founders Month
text:
October 14, 2026

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-08) and Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (D-VA-04) introduced the bipartisan and bicameral National American History and Founders Month Act to empower Americans to be active citizens through a deeper understanding of our Nation's early history, its founders and founding ideals, and the civic duties within the American experience.

“This year, we celebrated 250 years of freedom, independence, and the enduring principles that have shaped our nation,”said Congressman Haridopolos. “We are truly lucky to live in the greatest country in the world, and we must never take that blessing for granted. As a former history teacher, I know that by teaching future generations about our nation's founding and the sacrifices that made our freedoms possible, we can ensure America's remarkable story continues to inspire for generations to come.”

“Our nation was established 250 years ago on the revolutionary idea that the power of government derives from the people in order to secure the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “To ensure that all citizens can participate in our government by, of and for the people, each generation must fully understand the rich and complex history of its founding. The National American History and Founders Month Act provides an opportunity to reflect on that history and recommit to ensuring the great American experiment endures.”

“This nation has lasted 250 years not because its documents are self-executing, but because in every generation enough Americans understood what they had inherited,” said Dr. Jennifer London, President and Founder of NAHFMO. “I am deeply grateful to Representatives Haridopolos and McClellan for introducing this bill together, which would give National American History and Founders Month a permanent place in federal law and invite schools, families and communities to learn about the people, ideals and events that built this nation. With a companion bill already introduced in the Senate by Senators Wicker, Kaine and McCormick, and the country marking the anniversary of its founding, this is the right moment.”

title: Hoyer Statement on Unannounced Starlink Terminal Restrictions in Ukraine
text:

title: Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (both D-MD), and U.S. Representatives Glenn Ivey (MD-04) , Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) released the following statement regarding last night’s ruling by a federal judge, temporarily halting the Trump Administration’s efforts to close the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center (BARC) in Beltsville, Maryland:

“As we’ve said time and again, this Administration’s attempts to shutter BARC are not only unwise – they’re illegal. BARC conducts critical research that helps farmers across our nation put food on the table for American families – including combatting serious threats to our agriculture, like cyclospora and avian flu. Last night’s ruling from a federal judge made plain: the Administration’s efforts are in clear violation of Congressional intent. We will continue fighting back against the Trump Administration’s lawless attempts to close this facility, undermining its crucial research on behalf of American farmers and families.”

The lawmakers have repeatedly stressed the importance of maintaining BARC, including, most recently pushing Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins on this matter in April. Additionally, they have raised this issue in Committee hearings with Administration officials and fought for language in Congressional Appropriations and the most recent Continuing Resolution.

title: Lawmakers Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
text:
Letter follows Labor Day incident where individuals were arrested in the middle of the night while camping at Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, 4 of 5 are still being held at Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center

PNW records devastating 2026 wildfire season – Members voice concern USFS is misusing taxpayer funds by directing resources outside of USFS scope and mission

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, U.S. Congresswoman Emily Randall (D, WA-06), and Representatives Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.

This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.

“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.

The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.

The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.

The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:

Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?

Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.

Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.

What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?

What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?

Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?

Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?

The full text of the letter is available HERE.

title: OREGON LAWMAKERS URGE CONTINUED SUPPORT FOR OREGON’S HAZELNUT INDUSTRY
text:
Eugene, OR – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led members of Oregon’s congressional delegation in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins that calls on the Department to deliver critical federal support to Oregon’s hazelnut industry under the federal Section 32 purchase program.

“The hazelnut industry is a massive and integral part of our state’s agricultural economy; its size and longevity represent generations of farmers and handlers who have dedicated their lives to producing and distributing a product many communities depend on for their livelihoods,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers’ letter calls on USDA to include Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases, supporting growers, harvesters, processors, and agricultural economies primarily in Oregon’s Willamette Valley during a period of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty in a global market.

They stressed, “In recent years, disruptions in important export markets caused by these compounding issues have been particularly difficult for certain kernel sizes and grades that are high-quality, marketable food products but have fewer commercial outlets. These imbalances and market losses create uncertainty and pressure for our farmers and producers and threaten the steady distribution needed to prevent compounding product surpluses year-to-year.”

In addition to Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), and Val Hoyle (OR-04).
