title: Jayapal, Randall Lead PNW Members in Demanding Answers on NWDC Contract
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) and Emily Randall (WA-06) are leading Members from Washington and Oregon in demanding answers and transparency into ongoing efforts by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to purchase existing immigration detention centers currently owned and operated by private prison companies like GEO Group and CoreCivic. Currently, the GEO Group contract with the Northwest Detention Center (NWDC) is set to expire in October 2026.

Earlier this summer, ICE purchased two CoreCivic detention centers in California for $1.5 billion and facilities in Kansas and Minnesota for $734 million. Despite these facilities having been purchased by ICE, CoreCivic will continue managing operations. In October, ICE purchased three detention facilities in Adelanto, California, from GEO Group for $950 million. Similarly, GEO will continue running the facilities and says ICE is considering buying 10 facilities or more from the company.

“We are deeply concerned about the potential purchase of these facilities, as it appears to be an attempt to circumvent oversight and accountability at detention facilities. Both GEO Group and DHS have stated that acquiring these facilities is aimed, at least in part, at circumventing attempts by states to conduct oversight at immigration detention centers located within their borders,” wrote the Members.

Any attempt to dodge oversight is particularly troubling at the NWDC, as Washington State recently had to go to court to ensure access to the facility for state Department of Health officials. There is serious cause for concern if this purchase is being made to shield ICE and GEO from oversight efforts by putting the facility under federal ownership.

There are also troubling financial incentives. Under the Trump administration, GEO and CoreCivic have reaped enormous financial benefits. In 2025, both companies received an additional $2 billion in profit each, a 13 percent increase in revenue, and there has been a revolving door between the Trump administration and these companies — including border czar Tom Homan and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, who were previously employed by GEO.

“As of March 2026, the Washington State Department of Health received over 3,500 complaints about [NWDC]. Individuals have reported being sexually assaulted by an officer in their unit; unsanitary conditions, including unclean drinking water, worms, hair, and metal in food, and black mold in showers; and insufficient medical care. State oversight is an essential way to help ensure that the people detained in these facilities at U.S. taxpayer expense are being treated with dignity. Attempting to circumvent such oversight by purchasing substandard detention facilities and continuing to allow such inhumane conditions to persist is unacceptable,” continued the Members.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle S. Bynum (OR-05), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “WE’RE GOING TO RELENTLESSLY FOCUS ON OUR AFFORDABILITY AGENDA”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s The Weeknight, where he emphasized that House Democrats remain committed to holding the crooks who are ripping off the American people accountable and lowering the high cost of living in our fight for an affordable America.

MICHAEL STEELE: Democratic Leader, House Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York. Sir, you are a Trumpbuster. Are you not? Welcome to the program.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, it’s great to be with you. We’re working hard to make sure that on November 3, we can begin the process of decisively breaking MAGA extremism in the United States of America and win back control of the House of Representatives.

SYMONE SANDERS-TOWNSEND: So, Leader Jeffries, how are you all going to do that? Give us the—I know you hate to make predictions, but give us some numbers, because I was looking, and the last time Donald Trump was President in the midterm election, he lost a little over 40 seats. Okay, Democrats gained about net, I think, 42, maybe 43 seats. Someone in my ear will tell me if I’m wrong. How many seats do you think you are going to get?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, we’re working hard to win every possible seat. We, of course, have to get to 218 and then we’ll try to win as many seats on top of that as possible. What we do know from the 2018 election, where we were able to regain control of the House of Representatives, is that 75% of the seats that we flipped in 2018 were just won by Donald Trump in 2016. And so our opportunity to go deeper and deeper into the map is a real thing. And we have extraordinary candidates, whether those are doctors or nurses or farmers or pastors, police officers, firefighters, educators, union leaders, social workers, of course, a Tejano music superstar from the Rio Grande Valley in Texas, a smokejumper and combat veterans like Cait Conley as well as Rebecca Bennett, who are going to flip seats in New York and New Jersey.

MICHAEL STEELE: So, sir, Symone wanted the numbers, and I’ll give you a number. I’ll give you my number. My number is 40. Look, I know what we did in 2010. I was told I couldn’t do much better than 39. This environment is nothing like 2010, you know, for Democrats as it was for Republicans in this cycle. So there’s a real—there’s a real opportunity here to, yes, get to that 218 and expand that majority because you’re going to need it, to be quite honest, and you know that, I know that. It’s going to work to the benefit of the Democrats to have some oomph behind that number so you don’t have to live on the margins and the edges. And this, I think it’s something—the reason I raised it, sir, because I think it’s something for voters to know. You just can’t half-step it, folks. You just can’t pussyfoot around and just kind of give the Democrats a little bit of power. You’re either going to fully commit, or you’re not, right? You’ve got incredible races. You’ve got the opportunity to pick up a governorship in the state of Florida with David Jolly. You’ve got excitement in the state of Mississippi, sir. Mississippi. Symone calls Mississippi six weeks ago. Y’all need to pay attention. And here we are. So you’re on the cusp of some really important stuff. I think at this stage, at least how I looked at it in 2010, is like, where do I advance the margin? Where do I advance the ball so I go beyond what I’m going to need to be successful? Because I know on the other side, if it’s close, this team that you’re dealing with in the House? Mike Johnson and crew? Oh baby, you know they’re going to do everything in their power to get in your way. There’s still a question, sir, about whether or not Mike Johnson is even going to turn over the gavel when you take the House. That’s how much this number has to be a big one. So that’s my thought. I wanted to share that with you. What do you think?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, I appreciate that, Michael. We’ve got to run through the finish line and try to run up the numbers as high as we can, of course, so that we’re in a position to decisively govern on behalf of the American people. Like, when we’ve made clear that we are fighting for an affordable America, that we are committed to driving down the high cost of groceries and gas and housing, that we’ve committed to fighting to make healthcare affordable for every single American, we mean it when we say it and we want to be able to do it.And the more robust the majority, the better we’ll be able to overcome Republican obstruction in ways that, of course, will be designed just to stop progress. And we have an opportunity to be able to win big in the House, in the Senate, in governors races all across the country, certainly in state legislative bodies, where we can flip seats throughout America. And—but we can’t take anything for granted because we know the other side is going to throw up every possible obstacle to try to stop this from being a free and fair election, which is why we’ve put together the largest voter protection effort in modern American history.

LUKE RUSSERT: Leader Jeffries, while Democrats certainly have the wind at their back, the popularity of the Party is still very low. But it seems that a lot of people want to vote for the Democratic ticket this time because they want a check on Donald Trump. I was thinking about the last time Democrats had a big House majority, and that was in 2009. And they passed the stimulus, they passed healthcare, they passed a lot of meaningful legislation, but the stimulus in particular, the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, people did not understand it. It wasn’t marketed well. It wasn’t sold well. It was marketed so poorly that the man sitting to my right actually used it against Democrats just after the ’08 recession and got 63 Republicans elected to the House. So my question to you is now, with the wind at your back, with a lot of Republicans saying, ‘You know what? We’re going to throw in the towel in the House. We’re going to try and save these seats that are a lean red.’ It’s because the ones that are toss-ups are gone. What can you say to the American people that you’re going to do in the first 100 days that lets them know that Democrats are checking Donald Trump? And for the Independents that might not like you that much or don’t go to the Democratic side all the time, what can you offer them up in the first 100 days so that people can see the distinction between the two parties?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what we’ve made clear is that we’re going to relentlessly focus on our affordability agenda. There are some things that we are going to have to do immediately to reverse a lot of the damage that’s been done. We’re going to fight to reverse these Medicaid cuts. We’re going to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits, which will help make health insurance premiums more affordable for over 20 million Americans directly and tens of millions more whose premiums have increased indirectly, even if they may be on private insurance. That has to be dealt with. We’re going to fight to end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which we know has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. Now, the average gas price being north of $4 for an extended record period of time, that’s outrageous. And we also need to make sure we reclaim congressional authority in terms of tariffs so we can end these Trump Tariffs, which have also increased costs on everyday Americans in terms of groceries and goods by thousands of dollars per year. We also are going to focus on accountability because when you have folks in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people. And so, we’ve made clear to anyone out there who’s been stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people that, beginning on day one, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable and disrupt business as usual.

LUKE RUSSERT: Quick follow-up on there. Are special committees possible for corruption? Could you have a special committee about the corruption the Trump White House has engaged in, especially what he’s been doing with his sons? And could you have a special committee about the Epstein files? Are those possible with subpoena power?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the oversight work is going to be led by House Judiciary Committee Democrats. And of course, Jamie Raskin is the leader and the next Chair of the Judiciary Committee, along with House Oversight Committee Democrats, where Robert Garcia, the top Democrat and the next Chair of Oversight, has been doing a tremendous job pushing to hold the crooks accountable, even in the minority, and doing a tremendous job, of course, as it relates to the transparency and accountability that we need to deliver for the Epstein survivors and for the American people. LUKE RUSSERT: It’s possible.

SYMONE SANDERS-TOWNSEND: Before we let you go, Leader Jeffries, obviously earlier this week, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s D.C. home was raided. There was a warrant that was issued, and DHS officials, HSI specifically, executed that warrant at her home. The government says it is part of an ongoing criminal investigation. What can you tell us about what your knowledge is of this investigation? One. But two, are you concerned that more members of your Caucus are going to be targeted? I just—right now we’ve got Ilhan Omar. I’m thinking about Congresswoman LaMonica McIver, who is currently facing 17 years in prison for a felony if she is convicted for doing her job, I would argue. What are you doing to protect your members from this—well, it’s not just a threat at this point? The government is making good on his promises of retribution.

LEADER JEFFRIES: As Congresswoman Ilhan Omar has bravely and heroically and courageously said, she’s not going to be intimidated and she won’t be silenced. title: Kean Visits Bernards Township to Highlight $1.84 Million for Pleasant Valley Park
text:
(October 14, 2026) BERNARDS TOWNSHIP, NJ – This week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) visited Bernards Township to highlight the $1.84 million he secured in a House Appropriations bill for the Pleasant Valley Park culvert and paths.

The funding will be used for the construction of a culvert at Pleasant Valley Park. Currently, hundreds of vehicles per day drive through the stream that intersects the park road, negatively impacting the water quality. The construction of a culvert will reduce water pollution, provide a safe crossing to the rear of the park, and allow the construction of new paths throughout the park. Additionally, the project greatly expands walking and exercise opportunities, especially for the veterans who live at Valley Brook Village, the HUD Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing apartments on the Lyons VA campus next to the park.

“I was pleased to secure more than $1.8 million in federal funding to support this critical project in Bernards Township,” said Congressman Kean. “Pleasant Valley Park is a place where the community, including families and visitors from the VA Lyons campus, can come together to enjoy the outdoors. Unfortunately, frequent roadway flooding can make the park inaccessible. These funds will help ensure Pleasant Valley Park remains safe, accessible, and enjoyable for everyone.”

“It was great to welcome Congressman Tom Kean Jr. for an onsite tour of our $1.84 million Community Funding Project, including the culvert at Pleasant Valley Park and the new pathways that will provide connectivity to the park and existing trails,” said Bernards Township Mayor Ana Duarte McCarthy. “We are pleased and appreciative of the Congressman’s advocacy as the project advances for consideration for FY2027 funding.”

“Pleasant Valley Park is truly a gem of Bernards Township, busy year-round with sports teams, youth and adult recreation, concerts and Plays in the Park, and even the ski club’s departures,” said Bernards Township Committeewoman Jennifer Asay. “This project will protect the stream that runs through it, provide a safe crossing to the rear of the park, and add new walking paths for residents including our veteran neighbors next door at Valley Brook Village.”

“We couldn’t be more grateful for Congressman Kean’s support for this important project here in Bernards Township,” said Bernards Township Committeeman Andrew McNally. “Congressman Kean has consistently secured federal support for our residents here in Bernards as our voice in Washington.”

In August, Congressman Kean delivered $835,000 to Bernards Township through FY2026 Community Project Funding to upgrade the Police Department’s current radios, which can only operate on one frequency. This federal funding will be used to purchase 89 tri-band radios that cover multiple frequencies, streamlining coordination and strengthening emergency response. Learn moreHERE.

title: Reaction to California Attorney General’s Lawsuit to Protect National Archives in San Bruno
text:
SAN BRUNO, CA – Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15), who has been demanding answers from the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) and authored the National Archives Protection Act, issued the following statement in response to California Attorney General Rob Bonta announcing a lawsuit to block the closure of the San Francisco National Archives, located in San Bruno, CA:

“The National Archives and Records at San Bruno tell the important story of what has happened here in the Bay Area and local communities have every right to want direct access to their history. The National Records and Archives Administration (NARA) failed to conduct any kind of public input process and didn’t engage with stakeholders who are impacted before making a decision to close this facility and relocate fragile, sensitive documents over 1,500 miles away.

I am glad to see California Attorney General Rob Bonta file a lawsuit to stop NARA’s closure of the facility, and emphasizing how important it is for state agencies, university researchers and tribes to have access to these records.

While I’m pleased to see the Attorney General take action today, I am also pushing for federal legislation with the National Archives Protection Act and will be doing everything in my power to prevent the closure through other means like the federal budget process.

The fact that we have developed a bipartisan, nationwide coalition of federal lawmakers interested in preserving these archives demonstrates the unique and irreplaceable value they hold. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive.”

In June 2026, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) announced it would be closing the San Francisco (San Bruno) and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. The local facility in San Bruno houses culturally-significant archives from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific island territories, and Tribes. Its records hold deep value to the community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and much more.

Read more about Rep. Mullin’s National Archives Protection Act, and NARA’s dismissive response to a letter he co-authored with Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) along with 37 federal lawmakers, urging them to stop the closure.

title: Larsen, Murray Urge Trump Administration to Fund Sumas and Lynden Border Station Modernization Projects
text:
U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02), top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair on the Senate Appropriations Committee, sent a letter to General Services Administration (GSA) Administrator Edward Forst requesting GSA prioritize construction of two stalled border station projects in Northwest Washington. Senator Murray and Congressman Larsen sent this letter on September 22 and have yet to receive response from GSA.

“It has come to our attention that Washington state’s Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Ports of Entry (LPOE) projects are temporarily prevented from moving forward,” the lawmakers wrote. “We write to express our concern regarding this decision by General Services Administration (GSA).”

A land port of entry (LPOE) is a federal border facility used to control the entry and departure of people and cargo at a land border. Congress appropriated $3.4 billion to modernize 26 LPOEs across the United States in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law of 2021, which both Senator Murray and Representative Larsen helped become law. As of August 12th, 2026, the GSA has temporarily prevented nine of those projects from moving forward, including the Kenneth G. Ward Land Port of Entry in Lynden and the Sumas Land Port of Entry.

“Both LPOEs are vital border crossings for Washington state and Canada and play a significant role in trade and economic development that is relevant to the economic vitality of the United States,” the lawmakers continued. “Delaying these projects will have consequential impacts on the nation’s supply chain, labor market, and national security.”

Rep. Larsen and Sen. Murray stressed the importance of certainty about the status of the border station projects for city officials in Sumas and Lynden to plan for the impact that construction will have to downtown buildings and the local economy.

“These projects are also key to local development plans in the cities of Sumas and Lynden, where the LPOEs are located,” the lawmakers wrote. “LPOE modernization will impact several existing buildings in Sumas’s downtown core, and Lynden is preparing to take on additional commercial traffic. Prolonged uncertainty on project timelines will only lead to more disruption and delays in economic development of these cities.”

The lawmakers urged GSA Administrator Forst to prioritize the Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Port of Entry projects when the GSA reassesses the prioritization of the remaining nine LPOEs in the coming months and requested continued updates on decisions regarding the projects.

The full text of the letter can be read here.

Larsen and Murray Conduct Oversight of GSA Under the Trump Administration

As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray has led oversight of GSA’s reckless effort to dump federal properties, pressing the Trump administration on why it terminated leases without notifying Congress as required by law, and how veterans, taxpayers, Tribal members, and farmers would still get the in-person help they depend on. Murray continues to hold the Trump administration accountable for skirting the law, keeping Congress in the dark, and cutting off services families rely on.

In a Transportation & Infrastructure Committee oversight hearing in March, Rep. Larsen raised concerns about the GSA’s tumultuous first 14 months under the Trump administration and a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that the GSA signed with the Defense Ministry of Pakistan without providing evidence of the GSA’s legal jurisdiction to enter into the MOU or engage in redeveloping the private hotel.

This July, Rep. Larsen and Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Ranking Member Greg Stanton (AZ-04) sent a letter to Administrator Forst seeking answers about the agency’s involvement with the renovation of the Roosevelt Hotel and reporting from Bloomberg that the GSA signed a $1.4 million contract with Sullivan & Cromwell—a law firm with significant ties to the Trump administration—to provide legal services regarding the privately-owned property.

title: Larson Statement on the 2027 Social Security COLA Announcement
text: “Today’s announcement demonstrates just how hard President Trump’s affordability crisis has hit our seniors," said Larson. “As Americans struggle to make ends meet, a small bump in benefits is always welcome news—but for many seniors living on fixed incomes, it won’t be enough to keep pace with rising costs. With insolvency looming, we are only a few years away from automatic benefit cuts for everyone on Social Security if Congress does not act. Rather than come to the table with solutions, this administration and their allies in Congress have been laser-focused on breaking the system from within, so they can privatize Social Security. They have slashed staff and services at the Social Security Administration, making it harder for seniors to get their benefits in full and on time, and Speaker Johnson has even teased a plan to cut benefits if Republicans hold their majorities in the House and Senate. We cannot let that happen. Americans are depending on their Congress to enhance benefits—not cut them—and Democrats are ready to act. Our plan will stop these automatic cuts, boost benefits across the board, and ensure no one can retire into poverty after a lifetime of work, all by finally making the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share. It is time for a vote.”

title: Lawler to Introduce Bill Cracking Down on Candidate Coordination With Super PACs
text:
Washington, D. C. – 10/14/26… Today, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) announced the Stop Illegal Super PAC Coordination Act, legislation to crack down on coordination between congressional candidates and super PACs to prohibit joint fundraising committees (JFC) from placing political advertising expenditures disguised as solicitations.

Under current Federal Election Commission (FEC) rules, joint fundraising committees can bring together candidates and certain political committees that accept unlimited contributions. While the FEC has permitted these arrangements for fundraising solicitations and event announcements, its guidance has not specifically addressed political advertising expenditures by these committees, allowing candidates to spend almost unlimited amounts on media buys. This legislation would stop this unfair practice by prohibiting these joint fundraising committees from purchasing broadcast, cable, satellite, or paid digital advertising, while allowing them to continue traditional fundraising activities.

“Coordination of this kind between political campaigns and super PACs allows candidates to skirt campaign finance laws and funnel unlimited money into their campaigns. Americans deserve transparency and accountability in our elections. We need clear rules that prevent candidates from using these arrangements to get around campaign finance limits and protect the integrity of our elections,” said Congressman Lawler.

Congressman Lawler is one of the most bipartisan members of Congress and represents New York's 17th Congressional District, which is just north of New York City and contains all or parts of Rockland, Putnam, Dutchess, and Westchester Counties. He was rated the most effective freshman lawmaker in the 118th Congress, 8th overall, surpassing dozens of committee chairs.

title: Cities of Gilroy and Mountain View Advance Protections Restricting ICE Facility Construction
text:
SAN JOSÉ, CA – Today, Congressmembers Sam Liccardo (CA-16) and Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) congratulated the City of Gilroy and City of Mountain View for taking steps to keep ICE out of their communities.

“After plans for an ICE detention center just outside Gilroy were halted in federal court, local leaders are taking action to make it harder for ICE to construct future facilities,” said Rep. Liccardo. “By acting now, local leaders can protect the health and safety of their residents and restrict DHS should they attempt to convert industrial or commercial property into an ICE detention center. I thank Mayor Greg Bozzo, Mayor Emily Ann Ramos and the Gilroy and Mountain View City Councils for joining communities across our region in using their local authority to push back against ICE infrastructure in our community.”

On October 13, the Mountain View City Council adopted an interim urgency ordinance temporarily restricting new detention or custodial facilities. The action follows the Gilroy City Council's unanimous vote on October 5 to establish a 45-day moratorium on new detention facilities within city limits.

"I applaud the Cities of Gilroy and Mountain View for taking a stand in support of transparency, accountability, and the rule of law,” said Rep. Zoe Lofgren. "These ordinances send a clear message that no law enforcement agency should be allowed to expand its power without first demonstrating that it follows the law. ICE has too often failed to adhere to the legal standards, policies, and procedures that govern every other law enforcement agency. Unless and until ICE complies with those requirements and is held to the same standards of accountability as all law enforcement, its detention capacity and authority should not be expanded."

“Mountain View has long been committed to protecting our diverse community, where nearly 43% of residents are foreign-born,” said Mountain View Mayor Emily Ann Ramos. “We listened to the concerns raised by many residents when the U.S. Department of Homeland Security planned to develop a proposed immigration detention and processing facility in Santa Clara County, just outside Gilroy, which was halted by a lawsuit. Thanks to Congressman Liccardo’s encouragement for cities to consider interim land use controls, our City Council has now adopted an emergency ordinance to place a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities in Mountain View.”

“Gilroy’s future should reflect the values that define our community: care for one another, pride in our agricultural heritage, and a commitment to a safe, healthy, and thriving city,” Gilroy Mayor Greg Bozzo said. “Gilroy City Council members share our residents’ concerns about these types of facilities and their potential impacts on our future. By unanimously adopting this temporary moratorium, our Gilroy City Council has once again shown our commitment to those values and the long-term well-being of our community. I am thankful for Congressman Sam Liccardo's focus on real collaboration and his commitment to Gilroy's interests.”

Liccardo, who represents portions of Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties, released a toolkit in August to help local governments use zoning laws and building regulations to mitigate the expansion of ICE detention facilities and safeguard community health and safety. San Mateo County, Monterey County, The City of San José and Napa County have already advanced such ordinances. Several other city councils have now directed their staff to begin this process, and several more ordinance changes are in the pipeline.

title: Congressman Christian Menefee Hosts First-Ever Telephone Town Hall with Hundreds of Houston Constituents
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) hosted his first-ever telephone town hall, connecting with hundreds of constituents across Texas’s 18th Congressional District for an hour-long discussion on the issues affecting Houston families. During the event, Congressman Menefee answered questions directly from constituents on a wide range of topics, including rising costs, healthcare, the war in Iran, environmental protections, and opportunities to work across the aisle with Republicans to address challenges facing the district. He also shared updates on his ongoing work in Congress and throughout the Houston community.

"Hearing directly from the folks I represent is the most important part of my job," said Congressman Christian D. Menefee. "Families across Houston are working hard, but their paychecks aren't going as far as they used to. They're worried about paying for groceries, keeping their healthcare, and making sure their communities are safe. These are the concerns I'm hearing every day, and they're exactly what I'm fighting to address in Washington."

Affordability was a major focus of the conversation, with one constituent, Tyler, asking what Congressman Menefee was doing to address rising grocery prices as families struggle to stretch their paychecks. In response, Menefee highlighted his support for legislation to raise wages, expand tax credits, and lower everyday expenses, including the Living Wage for All Act, the Paycheck Fairness Act, and legislation to establish a permanent $300 monthly Child Tax Credit. Drawing on his own upbringing, Menefee discussed how programs such as WIC, free and reduced-price school lunches, Pell Grants, and GI Bill benefits helped his family and shaped his commitment to protecting the social safety net.

Throughout the town hall, participants also responded to three live survey questions addressing some of the most pressing issues facing the country. An overwhelming 93% of respondents said their groceries, rent, or utility bills have become more expensive, while 90% said they oppose President Trump and Republicans' war in Iran. Additionally, 53% reported that they or someone they love had been affected by Republicans' Medicaid cuts.

"These results tell us exactly what families across Houston are worried about," said Congressman Menefee. "People are tired of watching their bills go up while Washington Republicans make life harder for working families. They're worried about losing their healthcare, and they want an end to this war. I'm going to keep taking their concerns directly to Washington and fighting for the relief they deserve."

The town hall builds on Congressman Menefee's ongoing efforts to remain accessible and responsive to the residents of Texas's 18th Congressional District. Since taking office, Menefee and his team have closed more than 500 constituent service cases and helped recover over $1 million for constituents navigating federal agencies.

Congressman Menefee plans to host additional telephone town halls to continue connecting with constituents, answering questions, and providing updates on his work in Houston and Washington. Constituents can learn more about his work or request assistance with a federal agency by visiting Menefee.House.Gov or calling the main District Office at 713-655-0050.

title: Speaker Johnson Recognizes Damon & Tammy Magee as 2026 Angels in Adoption Honorees
text:
WASHINGTON — Speaker Johnson, in partnership with the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute (CCAI), recognized Pastor Damon Magee and his wife Tammy Magee as 2026 Angels in Adoption honorees. Damon, Pastor at King’s Temple United Pentecostal Church in Shreveport, and his wife, Tammy, are both biological and adoptive parents and have served as foster parents to numerous children.

Every year, members of Congress nominate an individual, family, or organization to be recognized for demonstrating a commitment to improving the lives of children in need of permanent, loving homes. Speaker Johnson nominated the Magees, who by opening their home to foster care and adoption, have graciously given a loving home to nearly 10 children and inspired numerous families in their church community to follow in their footsteps.

“Pastor Damon and Tammy Magee have faithfully opened their hearts and home, living out their calling to uphold the sanctity of every human life through foster care and adoption. The Magees are the biological parents of two children, adoptive parents to two more, and have served as foster parents to seven children over the years,” Speaker Johnson said. “I am honored to recognize Damon and Tammy as our 2026 Angels in Adoption honorees, and I am touched by their willingness to answer God’s call to care for so many children in our community and inspire other families to do the same.”

“We are incredibly humbled to be honored and are grateful for the opportunity to share our story with our nation's leaders. You never know the difference you can make in the world by investing in one child,” Pastor Damon and Tammy Magee said. "Our greatest joy is that in the last two years we have seen eight other families in our church join in the foster and adoption community with many more to come by faith."

Background: Since 1999, CCAI’s Angels in Adoption program has upheld a tradition of celebrating the extraordinary efforts of individuals, couples, families, and organizations who work tirelessly to advocate for children in need of a family. Throughout the 27 years, over 3,200 Angels have received this special honor. Honorees are awarded at CCAI’s annual Angels in Adoption Gala every fall in Washington, D.C.

title: Nunn, Iowa Leaders Highlight $1 Million Wapello County Scam, Urge Senate to Pass GUARD Act
text:
“Scammers stole more than $1 million from a Wapello County farmer who spent a lifetime earning it. His case showed why local deputies need better tools to trace stolen money and pursue the criminals behind these schemes,” said Rep. Nunn. “I introduced the GUARD Act because Iowa law enforcement asked for the resources to follow the money and hold these criminals accountable. We delivered overwhelming bipartisan support in the House. Now the Senate must finish the job, send this bill to the President’s desk, and ensure Iowans can retire with confidence that the savings they earned are protected.”

In 2024, scammers using a fake Instagram account spent months gaining the farmer’s trust and took more than $1 million, his entire life savings. When they learned he still had money left, they sent two men from New York to collect it in person. Sheriff Phillips and his deputies arrested both men on their second trip to Wapello County, but by then the money was gone, and the people running the scheme were overseas.

According to the FBI, Iowans lost $96 million to fraud in 2025, an increase of more than 85 percent from the year before. Many of those cases fall to local sheriffs and police departments, which often lack the tools to trace money if it’s converted to cryptocurrency or leaves the country entirely.

The GUARD Act would allow state, local, and Tribal law enforcement to use existing federal grant funding for fraud investigations, financial analysis software, and specialized training, without authorizing new federal spending. It would also clarify how federal agencies can help local investigators use blockchain tracing tools to recover stolen savings.

Iowa law officials and financial leaders spoke in support of the GUARD Act:

“When criminals use technology and international networks to steal from our citizens, local law enforcement needs the resources and partnerships to follow the money and pursue those responsible—no matter where the investigation leads,” said Wapello County Sheriff Don Phillips. “The GUARD Act would help us do exactly that, and the Senate needs to pass it before another Iowa family loses a lifetime of savings.”

“Thank you, Congressman Nunn, for your leadership and commitment to combating financial fraud,” said Melissa Spurgin, First Iowa State Bank chief financial officer and Iowa Bankers Association chair. “Iowa’s banking industry works every day to educate customers and stop fraud. The GUARD Act will strengthen these efforts by providing the necessary tools and resources to fight financial fraud and hold fraudsters accountable.”

“The GUARD Act presented by Congressman Nunn allows the city of Ottumwa to take what we are working on with awareness and education and move into action with the resources necessary to bring justice to those that would prey on the innocent, unsuspecting citizens,” said Ottumwa Mayor Ben Foote. “The Senate needs to protect the innocent and get this bill to the President’s desk.”

“No one should spend a lifetime working, saving, and building a future in Wapello County only to have a scammer steal it all at a moment’s notice. We’ve seen firsthand the devastating impact these crimes have on our residents and families, and our local law enforcement officers need more resources to fight back,” said Wapello County Supervisor Carrie Teninty. “Congressman Nunn’s GUARD Act would strengthen the partnerships between local law enforcement and federal investigators to help bring those criminals to justice — and the Senate needs to do its job and get this bill to the President’s desk.”

The GUARD Act passed the House Financial Services Committee unanimously in May and advanced through the full House in September. The bipartisan bill is supported by the Iowa Bankers Association, Iowa Credit Union League, AARP Iowa, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Capital One, and other organizations. The bill has cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee and now awaits a vote in the full Senate.

title: Rep. Panetta Leads Call for Transparency, Accountability  in the Administration’s Global Health Strategy
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) wrote a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio requesting greater transparency and stronger oversight of the Trump Administration’s “America First Global Health Strategy.” Rep. Panetta led 34 other lawmakers in calling for the public release of global health agreements and detailed answers about how the Administration will measure results, monitor spending, and respond to the misuse of U.S. taxpayer dollars.

Following the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and the transfer of foreign assistance responsibilities to the U.S. Department of State, the Administration announced roughly $16 billion in bilateral assistance programs for 36 countries. Under the new model, assistance goes directly to foreign governments. However, only a handful of the agreements have been made publicly available, and the lawmakers raised concerns that many participating governments have a history of corruption involving foreign assistance.

“While we applaud efforts to build up global health mechanisms that fight HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola and other infectious diseases, this new model raises significant concerns about the efficient and transparent use of U.S. taxpayer dollars,” wrote Rep. Panetta and his colleagues. “Given that the Administration’s dismantling of USAID was triggered by alleged wasteful spending, we want to ensure this new foreign assistance model is free of waste, fraud and abuse.”

The lawmakers highlighted the multiple layers of oversight USAID used to monitor funding provided to nongovernmental organizations and other implementing partners, including contracting officers, program officials, technical experts, and the USAID Office of Inspector General. They cited testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office and the USAID Office of Inspector General indicating limited ability to track or audit funds sent directly to foreign governments. While acknowledging the need to modernize foreign assistance, the lawmakers warned that shifting to government-to-government assistance requires clear safeguards to protect taxpayer dollars.

“Failure to implement these programs thoughtfully, while ensuring accountability to the taxpayer, jeopardizes American leadership in the global health space, which is second to none. It also encourages nations to seek partnerships with our adversaries, while making America less safe, less strong and less prosperous,” continued the lawmakers.

The lawmakers requested written responses explaining how the Administration will define success and monitor whether the health agreements meet their objectives, who will oversee that work, and what staffing, technical expertise, and funding will support it. They also asked the State Department to identify the systems and safeguards it will use to track and audit spending and explain how it will respond to allegations or evidence of misuse, including whether it will immediately suspend assistance.

To ensure taxpayers can review these commitments, the lawmakers called for all existing and future global health agreements to be made publicly available. They requested a detailed explanation if the State Department cannot release the agreements.

The letter was also signed by Reps. Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Sanford Bishop (GA-02), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Jim Costa (CA-21), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Jared Golden (ME-02), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Bill Keating (MA-09), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Dave Min (CA-47), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Johnny Olszewski (MD-02), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Dina Titus (NV-01), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25).

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to express concerns about transparency and oversight of the Administration’s new bilateral international assistance model, which grants money directly to foreign governments. Following the dissolution of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), and the transfer of foreign assistance to the U.S. Department of State, the Administration announced roughly $16 billion in bi-lateral assistance programs for 36 countries and launched the America First Global Health Strategy. While we applaud efforts to build up global health mechanisms that fight HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola and other infectious diseases, this new model raises significant concerns about the efficient and transparent use of U.S. taxpayer dollars.

Since the bi-lateral international assistance agreements were signed with host countries, only a handful have been made available to the U.S. public for review. Furthermore, many of the foreign governments that have signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with the State Department have a history of corruption with respect to foreign assistance.

USAID had several layers of accountability mechanisms built to help monitor funds sent to nongovernmental organizations (NGO) and other implementing partners, including country-based contracting officers, programmatic officials and U.S.-based technical officials, as well as the USAID Office of Inspector General (OIG). Testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office and the USAID OIG indicate that there is limited ability to track or audit U.S. taxpayer dollars sent directly to foreign governments. While many development stakeholders agree that a foreign assistance model based primarily on international NGOs needs improvement and modernization, the wholesale adoption of government-to-government assistance without accountability or transparency raises serious questions.

Given that the Administration’s dismantling of USAID was triggered by alleged wasteful spending, we want to ensure this new foreign assistance model is free of waste, fraud and abuse. We therefore request written responses to the following questions:

1) Please detail how the Administration will monitor and evaluate these health agreements to ensure they meet their objectives. How will success be defined?

2) Who will be charged with monitoring and evaluating these bi-lateral assistance agreements? What resources, including staffing, technical capacity, and financial support, are being deployed to support these efforts?

3) How will the State Department respond to allegations or evidence of improper use of U.S. taxpayer dollars used in foreign assistance? Do you plan to immediately cut off all aid if U.S. taxpayer money is not used for its intended purpose? If not, please explain why.

4) Please detail how the Administration plans to track and audit U.S. taxpayer dollars sent to foreign governments to ensure they are used for their purposes of supporting global health programs. What systems, tools, and safeguards are in place to ensure adequate monitoring and evaluation?

5) We request that all previously signed, as well as all future, global health agreements be made publicly available. If you are unable to do so, please provide a detailed explanation of why you can’t make these agreements publicly available for review to U.S. taxpayers.

Failure to implement these programs thoughtfully, while ensuring accountability to the taxpayer, jeopardizes American leadership in the global health space, which is second to none. It also encourages nations to seek partnerships with our adversaries, while making America less safe, less strong and less prosperous.

Thank you for your attention to these questions as we work toward a shared goal of ensuring quality oversight of a critical tool in our national security apparatus.

Sincerely,

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN, NEW YORK DELEGATION DEMAND TRUMP ADMINISTRATION RELEASE $87 MILLION IN COUNTERTERRORISM FUNDING STILL OWED TO NEW YORK
text:
One Year After Trump Promised Full Reversal of Funding Cuts, First Responders Statewide are Still Without Millions in Federal Investments

KINGSTON, NY – Congressman Pat Ryan joined members of the New York Congressional Delegation in demanding the Trump Administration to immediately release $87 million in FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Program (HSGP) funding that is still owed to New York. Their letter, sent to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, highlights the danger of withholding this funding from one the largest states in the nation and a top target for international and domestic terrorism.

“Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the President has waged targeted political attacks on New York State. When he cut this counterterrorism funding, New Yorkers across the state fought back and won. Now, a year later, we’re demanding Trump deliver the rest of what’s rightly ours,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “As Trump’s war with Iran continues, Americans want and deserve to feel safe. Now is the absolute last time to be cutting security funding. The need is especially stark following the grim 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks – the tragedy that changed our state forever and inspired these vital preparedness programs in the first place. Trump’s DHS has an obligation to release these funds and protect New Yorkers.”

In September 2025, DHS issued HSGP award notifications that cut New York’s allocation by 86 percent, or $187 million, leaving the state with just $30 million compared to roughly $220 million in FY24. In October 2025, following bipartisan advocacy, President Trump committed to restoring full funding at approximately $220 million. After a court order in Noem v. Illinois that found Trump unlawfully cut emergency grant funding, the administration released $100 million, but $87 million is still owed to New York.

The missing funds affect every county in the state, including Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster, and represent $11 million in losses for New York City. The letter warns that without full restoration, the Trump Administration is severely limiting local law enforcement’s ability to plan, train tactical teams, procure equipment, and conduct operations. Created in the wake of the September 11th attacks, HSGP has protected New York State for decades. The delegation underscored that the funds are due 25 years after 9/11 and one year after the President’s promise.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Pou Reveals New Details of Massive Data Center Diesel Spill
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) today revealed new details about the September 11, 2026 diesel spill at a data center in Secaucus, including a more than seven-hour delay in reporting the incident to state authorities and unanswered questions about its environmental impact.

These findings, obtained after Pou sought answers from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection, were shared in a letter to Secaucus Mayor Michael Gonnelli as the state continues investigating the roughly 5,500-gallon spill.

On October 2, 2026, Congresswoman Pou wrote to NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak seeking a full accounting of the spill, including how it occurred, a timeline of the disaster, the extent of the damage, and what safeguards would be put in place to prevent similar catastrophes.

“Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways,” Congresswoman Pou writes Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli about the data center damage around his community.

Key Findings from the NJDEP’s Preliminary Investigation

Approximately 4,000 gallons of diesel have been recovered from the storm sewer line and drainage canals: NJDEP reports an unspecified amount was absorbed by cleanup materials. How much diesel remains in surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways is unknown.

No evidence was found that diesel reached the Hackensack River: But NJDEP acknowledged reports of “discolored vegetation along the river’s southeastern edge, downstream from the affected tributary.” NJDEP is investigating if the discoloration was caused by the diesel spill.

The data center falls below the threshold for certain state safeguards against major facilities. NJDEP determined that the facility is not subject to New Jersey’s major-facility discharge prevention requirements, including secondary containment systems, physical security measures, and visual inspections.

Cleanup efforts continue, and Equinix has taken corrective measures. NJDEP has confirmed that emergency responses were undertaken following the spill. According to separately published reports, Equinix has reportedly terminated a facility site engineer and suspended automatic fuel polishing operations nationwide.

The state probe remains ongoing with no completion date announced. The agency has committed to releasing its final report publicly and will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.

Secaucus and surrounding communities have lived with pollution for decades. Contamination from industrial sites and landfill runoff led the Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River a Superfund site in 2022. Now as a major cleanup is underway, the September 11 Equinix spill has seen over 5,000 gallons of diesel released into the local environment.

The Secaucus spill comes amid growing national attention to the environmental impact and public costs of rapidly expanding data centers.

Timeline of the September 11, 2026 Diesel Spill

12:20PM: The spill may have begun as early as just after noon, following a failure of the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank during an internal fuel transfer.

~4:00PM: Equinix’s fuel polishing process stopped although diesel continued leaking.

6:36PM: An Equinix guard discovered the spill, approximately six hours after it may have begun.

6:46PM: Within 10 minutes of discovering the spill, Equinix isolated the fuel lines and halted the generator.

7:06PM: Spill containment kits were deployed.

7:11PM: Equinix contacted its emergency contractor.

7:43PM: Equinix notified NJDEP of the spill, more than seven hours after it may have begun. The Secaucus Fire Department arrived around the same time.

9:45PM: Equinix’s emergency contractor arrived at the facility, more than three hours after the spill was discovered.

September 12, 6:07AM: Secaucus and the local health department received electronic notification of the spill, nearly 18 hours after it may have begun.

The text of Congresswoman Pou’s letter to Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli is below.

Dear Mayor Gonnelli:

I write to share new information over the recent data center fuel spill in Secaucus that released over 5,000 gallons of diesel fuel into waterways near the Hackensack River. On October 2, I wrote to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (“NJDEP”) demanding answers about the spill at the Equinix facility, including a timeline of events and information about its environmental impact. NJDEP responded to several of my questions. Although more information is forthcoming, I want to share what we have learned so far, including additional details Equinix recently provided to my office and to NJDEP.

On September 11, 2026, Equinix conducted an internal fuel transfer operation, during which the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank failed. Equinix has stated that the spill may have begun as early as 12:20 PM and continued until approximately 4:00 PM when fuel polishing stopped. After roughly six hours of diesel fuel leaking, an Equinix security guard discovered the spill at approximately 6:36 PM. Within 10 minutes, the facility isolated the fuel lines and halted the associated generator. Around 7:06 PM, spill kits were deployed and by 7:11 PM, Equinix contacted its emergency environmental contractor. Equinix reported the incident to the NJDEP Hotline at 7:43 PM—over seven hours after the spill began. Around that same time, the Secaucus Fire Department arrived at the facility—Equinix’s own emergency environmental contractor arrived roughly two hours later at 9:45 PM. NJDEP also directed environmental booms to be deployed to stop the diesel fuel from spreading into the drainage tributary for the Hackensack River. NJDEP also directed the use of additional equipment to vacuum and clean up the spill.

More than a month after the spill, important questions remain unanswered. Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways.

NJDEP continues to investigate the incident, including whether the vegetation discoloration was caused by the fuel spill, but has not provided a timeline for completing its probe. NJDEP has promised to provide me with additional information as it becomes available. The agency has committed to making its final report public so our community can understand the full extent of any damage. Once the report is completed, NJDEP will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.

Importantly, within a week of the spill, NJDEP inspected the Equinix facility and determined that its fuel storage capacity falls below the threshold for New Jersey’s major facility discharge of petroleum and other hazardous substance prevention requirements. These requirements include having physical security measures, impermeable secondary containment and diversion systems, and visual inspections and monitoring.

While NJDEP has confirmed that appropriate emergency responses were undertaken following the spill and that cleanup efforts continue, and although Equinix appears to have terminated an employee serving as a facility site engineer and has halted automatic fuel polishing nationwide, more must be done to keep our communities safe. My office will continue to work with you, the Town of Secaucus, state agencies, and federal regulators to address the aftermath of this incident and prevent similar spills in the future.

Sincerely,

Nellie Pou

Member of Congress

title: Pressley, City of Boston Announce More Than $16 Million to Modernize Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park
text:
Pressley, City of Boston, Sec. Matias, State Rep. Consalvo Announce Initial Phase of Renovations that include Energy Retrofits, Accessibility Upgrades, Sustainable Infrastructure, and Workforce Opportunities

BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), alongside Mayor Michelle Wu, Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) Secretary Juana Matias, Representative Rob Consalvo, and Boston Housing Authority (BHA) Administrator Kenzie Bok,joined residents to announce more than $16 million in state, city, and federal funding to modernize the Fairmount public housing community in Hyde Park. This announcement represents the latest investment in the city’s public housing communities.

The funding includes $1M of Community Project Fund investment secured by Congresswoman Pressley and Senators Edward Markey and Elizabeth Warren, a $10 million High Leverage Asset Preservation Program (HILAPP) grant from EOHLC, and $5 million in City of Boston capital funding for the Fairmount Modernization Project. The Boston Public Health Commission has granted funds for open space improvements and community garden installations. Together, the funding will create a more accessible and resilient community.

“Residents in the Massachusetts 7th not only deserve a safe, stable place to call home, but also one that reflects modern-day needs in accessibility, resiliency, and sustainability—and this essential funding to modernize the Fairmount Apartments will do exactly that,” said Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley. “This investment is a reflection of community input realized and I’m grateful for every engaged resident who made their voice heard. I’m proud to deliver this funding alongside our city and state partners in Mayor Wu, Secretary Matias, Administrator Bok, Rep. Consalvo, and others to invest in existing public housing and improve livability for our communities.”

“Over the last five years, Boston has built nearly 16,000 new units of housing throughout our neighborhoods. In order to make our city a home for everyone, we must also preserve and modernize the affordable homes that already exist,” said Mayor Michelle Wu. “I’m grateful to all our partners for helping secure funding for this comprehensive, multi-phase renovation of the Fairmount Apartments, and I look forward to working with residents to deliver beautiful, upgraded homes for these families.”

“The Boston Housing Authority is so grateful to our city, state, and federal partners for investing in our public housing communities,” said Kenzie Bok, Administrator of the Boston Housing Authority. “With this funding, Fairmount will remain a welcoming place for families to call Hyde Park home for decades to come.”

The BHA is kicking off a Master Planning process for the Fairmount community, creating an area-wide vision while beginning a first phase of physical improvements. The initial phase of upgrades will focus on modernizing unit interiors, making 5% of apartments fully accessible, electrifying heating and hot water systems, and adding cooling. It will also include building envelope improvements and installing green stormwater infrastructure to support the community’s long-term sustainability and climate resilience.

“Thanks to Governor Healey’s Affordable Homes Act, HLC has been able to expand the funding needed to improve the state’s public housing system,” said Housing and Livable Communities Secretary Juana Matias. “We’re not just building new housing, but investing in the homes we already have and the people who live in them. The preservation of Fairmount Apartments is exactly what that commitment looks like.”

“I am thrilled that this enormous investment is happening at the Fairmount Housing Development, literally blocks away from my home here in Hyde Park,” said State Representative Rob Consalvo. “This partnership between the State, City, and Federal government will ensure that the residents of this development will be able to live in safe, modern and accessible units now and for years to come.”

An additional federal investment secured by the Congressional delegation is going to support flood mitigation for affordable housing developments, including BHA properties. The city and BHA have collaborated on multi-site stormwater projects serving the Fairmount, Gallivan, and Franklin Field communities, an effort bolstered by this federal backing. The project will fund a community garden and new rain gardens to mitigate stormwater pollution and prevent flooding. Through Boston’s PowerCorps program, local residents will be trained to build and maintain the rain gardens while earning green career credentials.

“As the District 5 City Councilor, Chair of the Boston City Council’s Housing Committee, and someone who grew up in public housing, I know firsthand how important it is for families to have a place they can be proud to call home,” said Councilor Enrique Pepén. “This $16 million investment in the Fairmount Apartments is exactly the kind of commitment our residents deserve, one that strengthens our communities, improves quality of life, and ensures families can continue to thrive in the neighborhoods they call home. I’m grateful to our state and federal partners for their collaboration and commitment to making this important investment possible.”

“This $16 million investment is an exciting step forward in advancing affordable, accessible, and high-quality housing for residents of Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park,” said Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune. “By investing in our public housing communities, we are strengthening neighborhoods and ensuring that families have safe, stable homes where they can thrive. I look forward to seeing the lasting impact these improvements will have on Fairmount residents for years to come.”

Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park was constructed in 1951 and includes over 200 units of state public housing.

As a Member of the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance of the House Financial Services Committee (FSC), Rep. Pressley has consistently advocated for policies that affirm housing as a human right and center the dignity and humanity of all people.

In June 2026, the 21st Century Road to Housing Act passed Congress and included four bills led by Congresswoman Pressley that would address the housing crisis and increase pathways to equitable and affordable housing. The bills will address bias in home valuations, expand affordable housing, strengthen oversight of corporate landlords, and help families reach financial stability. The bill became law despite Donald Trump’s refusal to sign it.

Rep. Pressley’s four bills in the housing package include:

The Appraisal Modernization Act. This bill would promote equity and combat systemic bias in the home appraisal process that has disadvantaged many current and aspiring homeowners—especially homeowners of color.

The Innovation Fund Act. This bill would establish a grant program to reward communities that are taking innovative steps to increase housing supply.

The Renter Resource Center Act. This bill would protect renters and strengthen oversight of corporations by creating a database of institutional investors that buy single-family homes, requiring HUD to provide resources to renters, and more.

Helping More Families Save Act. This bill would help families receiving federal housing assistance achieve financial independence as a pathway to wealth building by modernizing and expanding HUD’s Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program.

Following Trump’s refusal to sign the package into law without advancing his voter suppression bill, Rep. Pressley joined lawmakers in demanding Trump support the housing package and the essential, expanded access to housing it would deliver for Americans.

In May 2026, during Fair Housing and Second Chance Month, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) and Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) reintroduced the Housing for Formerly Incarcerated Reentry and Stable Tenancy (Housing FIRST) Act of 2026, bold legislation to help people who are formerly incarcerated and those with criminal histories access safe and stable housing. The bill would advance housing justice and help disrupt the prison-to-homelessness pipeline by removing unjust barriers to housing and limit tenant screening criteria for criminal records in background checks.

In April 2026, Rep. Pressley along with Rep. DeLauro and Rep. Gomez, founder and co-chair of Congressional Renters Caucus, introduced the Housing Emergencies Lifeline Program (HELP) Act to protect tenants facing illegal evictions, crack down on credit reporting of evictions, and more.

In March 2026, Rep. Pressley joined Financial Services Committee Democrats in a comment letter condemning HUD’s proposed mixed-status families rule, which would increase evictions, separate families, and increase homelessness across the country.

In January 2026, Rep. Pressley, alongside Congresswomen Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Ilhan Omar (MN-05) held the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ (CPC) Lowering Costs Taskforce’s first shadow hearing, titled “Building the New American Dream: Lowering Housing Costs for All.” The shadow hearing brought together housing experts and CPC Members to advance solutions to lower costs by building more affordable, public, and market-rate housing; cracking down on corporate and landlord greed; and expanding federal assistance for low-income families.

In December 2025, Rep. Pressley convened local advocates and community partners to sound the alarm on the housing crisis created by Donald Trump.

In December 2025, Rep. Pressley underscored the need to support grandfamily and kinship households, which are vital to preventing homelessness and keeping families and communities whole.

In November 2025, Rep. Pressley joined House Financial Services Committee Ranking Member Maxine Waters (CA-35) and 52 colleagues in sending a letter to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner, calling on him to rescind a recent HUD decision to slash essential Continuum of Care (CoC) program funding.

In November 2025, Rep. Pressley introduced the Appraisal Modernization Act, legislation to promote equity and combat systemic bias in the home appraisal process that has disadvantaged many current and aspiring homeowners—especially homeowners of color.

In May 2025, Rep, Pressley, along with Representatives Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), and Greg Casar (TX-35), reintroduced the Tenants’ Right to Organize Act, legislation to protect the power of tenants, including those with federal vouchers, to organize.

In June 2024, Rep. Pressley, along with Representatives Maxine Waters (CA-43) and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), re-introduced the Tenant Empowerment Act, bold legislation to strengthen HUD tenant protections and provide renters with the tools necessary to improve the quality of their homes.

In March 2024, Rep. Pressley, along with Mayor Wu, visited Roxbury to celebrate the $1,000,000 in federal funding she secured to provide emergency childcare support for families experiencing homelessness in the City of Boston.

In March 2024, Rep. Pressley, along with Senators Warren and Markey, applauded the final passage of $850,000 in federal community project funding for The Pryde, an affordable housing development for LGBTQ+ seniors in Hyde Park.

In March 2024, Rep. Pressley urged Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell to cut interest rates to boost home affordability and construction of affordable housing.

In January 2024, Rep. Pressley, during a House Financial Services Committee Hearing, highlighted the growing housing crisis and how appraisal bias and discriminatory tenant screening practices exacerbate the racial wealth and homeownership gaps, especially for Black communities.

In January 2024, Rep. Pressley celebrated the $2.4 million in federal funding she secured to support the community-led transformation of the Clarendon Hill housing community, an ethnically, linguistically and economically diverse neighborhood in Somerville.

In December 2023, Rep. Pressley requested the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to provide data on housing needs for Medicaid beneficiaries and feedback on challenges the agency is having in covering housing support for people requiring home and community-based services (HCBS).

In July 2023, Rep. Pressley, along with Chairwoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) and Congresswoman Cori Bush (MO-01), reintroduced the Housing Emergencies Lifeline Program (HELP) Act, critical legislation to provide much-needed assistance to those facing eviction amid the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

In September 2021, Rep. Pressley joined Rep. Bush and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) in introducing the Keeping Renters Safe Act of 2021 to enact an urgently needed nationwide eviction moratorium.

On July 2021, ahead of the expiration of the previous CDC eviction moratorium, Reps. Pressley, Bush, Gomez and their progressive colleagues sent a letter renewing their calls for President Biden and CDC Director Rochelle Walensky to extend the federal eviction moratorium and prevent the historic and deadly wave of evictions that would occur if the government failed to do so.

On July 30, 2021, Rep. Pressley joined House Financial Services Committee Chairwoman Maxine Waters (D-CA) in introducing the Protecting Renters from Evictions Act of 2021, legislation to extend the eviction moratorium through the end of the year.

In June 2021, Rep. Pressley, along with Reps. Gomez and Bush, led over 40 of their colleagues on a letter urging President Biden and CDC Director Walensky to extend and strengthen the moratorium for the duration of the public health crisis.

In June 2021, Congresswoman Pressley, along with Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN), re-introduced the Rent and Mortgage Cancellation Act, a bill to institute a nationwide cancellation of rents and home mortgage payments through the duration of the coronavirus pandemic.

On May 18, 2021, Reps. Bush and Pressley sent a letter to the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), calling on the CDC to strengthen and extend the federal moratorium on evictions, ensuring families can remain safely in their homes for the duration of the COVID-19 global health emergency.

On July 28, 2020, Rep. Pressley, Rep. DeLauro and Sen. Harris introduced the Housing Emergencies Lifeline Program (HELP) Act to provide much-needed, layered assistance to those facing eviction amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

On July 24, 2020, in a Financial Services Committee hearing, Rep. Pressley discussed the unprecedented financial cliff facing millions of renters and homeowners, the economic consequences of millions losing their homes, including the ability to return to work, and why funding for legal representation is so critical.

On May 11, 2020, Reps. Tlaib, and Joe Neguse (D-CO) urge House and Senate leadership to include $11.5 billion in funding for Emergency Solutions Grants (ESG) in the next relief package to aid the nation’s homeless population who are experiencing heightened vulnerability during the COVID-19 pandemic.

On April 10, 2020, Rep. Pressley urged Congressional leadership to prioritize recurring monthly cash payments to those most at-risk during the COVID-19 crisis. This funding would allow people to cover all their bills, including rent.

On April 17, 2020, Reps. Pressley, Ilhan Omar (D-MN) and colleagues introduce the Rent and Mortgage Cancellation Act, a bill to institute a nationwide cancellation of rents and home mortgage payments through the duration of the coronavirus pandemic.

On March 23, 2020, Reps. Pressley and Rashida Tlaib (D-MI) introduced the Public Health Emergency Shelter Act of 2020, legislation to provide critical funding to states and local governments responding to the needs of families and individuals experiencing homelessness during the COVID-19 crisis. This legislation was included and passed through the HEROES Act and H.R. 7301, the Emergency Housing Protections and Relief Act of 2020.

On March 19, 2020, Rep. Pressley, along with progressive lawmakers and organizations, introduced the Housing is a Human Right Act to authorize more than $200 billion in federal spending over 10 years for crucial housing infrastructure and reduce homelessness.

On March 18, 2020, Reps. Pressley, Katie Porter (D-CA) and Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) wrote to HUD calling for a moratorium on evicting renters during the coronavirus pandemic.

In July 2019, Rep. Pressley announced legislation that would prohibit the use of biometric recognition technology in most public and assisted housing units funded by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), protecting tenants from biased surveillance technology.

In November 2019, Rep. Pressley and Rep. Tlaib wrote to HUD blasting the agency for ignoring low-income tenants seeking to save their homes.
