title: Amata Highlights Pacific Healthcare Initiative for American Samoa, the Focus of Recent Meetings
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is highlighting several key healthcare ideas for American Samoa and the region that were put forward in her meeting with Governor Pulaali’i Nikolao Pula; Dr. Peter N. Bretan, a renal surgeon, urologist and former multi-term president of the California Medical Association; and Dr. Eileen Natuzzi, who has extensive experience working with healthcare efforts and goals for the underserved Pacific Islands. The two doctors also met with LBJ Tropical Medical center leaders, and Amata and Dr. Natuzzi followed up by discussing the practicalities with LBJ Board Member Taimalelagi Dr. Claire Tuia Poumele, including discussing drone medicine transport with Major Si’imoa Galoia.

Pictured with MAJ Si’imoa Galoia, LBJ Board Member Taimalelagi Dr. Claire Tuia Poumele, Eileen Natuzzi MD discussing health care advancements for our islands

Training LBJ surgeons to provide urological procedures

During this visit, Dr. Bretan and Dr. Natuzzi met with the medical director and the surgeons at LBJ to review the data on Overseas Medical Referrals for enlarged prostate resections, also known as TURPs.

In 2026 alone, 40 patients from American Samoa were referred to New Zealand for this prostate care. This number has been significantly increasing each year. The estimated cost of travel and stay in New Zealand exceeds $400,000 ($10,000/person). The total ongoing savings to Medicaid is an estimated $800,000 when the facility and professional fees are included.

In contrast, establishing a transurethral vaporization prostate resection (TUVP) program by training the general surgeons to do the procedure would cost less than $100,000. In addition to the TUVP procedure, training can include:

Trans urethral vaporization bladder

Trans rectal prostate biopsy

Removal of kidney stones using Shockwave lithotripsy.

This training could begin as soon as January 2027, provided needed equipment is purchased.

Establishing a regional Trauma system

Working with Pacific Island Health Officers Association (PIHOA), a U.S.-Affiliated Pacific Islands (USAPI) trauma readiness program has been funded by Pacific Command (PACOM). This would establish a regional trauma system that can respond to natural disasters as well as kinetic warfare. Healthcare staff throughout the USAPIs will be certified in ATLS and ATCN. In addition to training, American Samoa could serve as a strategic medical stockpile location.

Establishing a medical drone program and supporting Manu’a

In a meeting with the DOH, DHS, DOE and the Governor, the cost of sending urgent medical supplies to the Manu’a Islands by boat and plane was a key point of discussion. The technology is now available, and in use elsewhere, for drones to carry medicines, blood products and vaccines to the islands and bring laboratory specimens back. This conveyance can save time and money while improving care through faster availability. A number of drones are built that can be used for this purpose. (Kite Aero and Zipline).

Based on the fact that Tafuna High School has a national award-winning drone team: the Toa Drone Team, American Samoa’s students could be trained so that upon graduation there is a ready workforce that can be appropriately certified within current laws and regulations to pilot the Vertical Take Off and Landing (VTOL) and Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS), creating local jobs for young people in American Samoa.

Further possibilities for future expansion of drone use piloted from American Samoa could include patrolling EEZ waters for illegal fishing, human trafficking and drug running, contributing to search and rescue, monitoring weather impacts, and ferrying supplies in conjunction with Apia.

Establishing mainland medical school partnerships

Under this plan, to foster training and support, negotiations would start between George Washington Medical School and LBJ/ASG in order to establish bidirectional exchanges of medical students, doctors and faculty. The goal would be to expand services, provide continuing support for doctors and nurses, and introduce U.S. medical students to healthcare in the Pacific Islands.

“Thank you to Dr. Bretan for his important insights, and Dr. Natuzzi, who has focused for years on ways to bring about better care to remote islands like ours,” said Congresswoman Aumua Amata. “Successfully establishing these ideas together, or even a few of them, would be key improvements to our health system here. Thank you to Governor Pulaali’i for meeting with these medical experts to discuss these initiatives that can provide new tools for our doctors as they are always working to save lives and bring improvements to LBJ.”

title: Randall, Jayapal Lead PNW Members in Demanding Answers on NWDC Contract
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representatives Emily Randall (WA-06) and Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) led Members from Washington and Oregon in demanding answers and transparency into ongoing efforts by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to purchase existing immigration detention centers currently owned and operated by private prison companies like GEO Group and CoreCivic. Currently, the GEO Group contract with the Northwest Detention Center (NWDC) is set to expire in October 2026.

Earlier this summer, ICE purchased two CoreCivic detention centers in California for $1.5 billion and facilities in Kansas and Minnesota for $734 million. Despite these facilities having been purchased by ICE, CoreCivic will continue managing operations. In October, ICE purchased three detention facilities in Adelanto, California, from GEO Group for $950 million. Similarly, GEO will continue running the facilities and says ICE is considering buying 10 facilities or more from the company.

“We are deeply concerned about the potential purchase of these facilities, as it appears to be an attempt to circumvent oversight and accountability at detention facilities. Both GEO Group and DHS have stated that acquiring these facilities is aimed, at least in part, at circumventing attempts by states to conduct oversight at immigration detention centers located within their borders,” wrote the Members.

Any attempt to dodge oversight is particularly troubling at the NWDC, as Washington State recently had to go to court to ensure access to the facility for state Department of Health officials. There is serious cause for concern if this purchase is being made to shield ICE and GEO from oversight efforts by putting the facility under federal ownership.

There are also troubling financial incentives. Under the Trump administration, GEO and CoreCivic have reaped enormous financial benefits. In 2025, both companies received an additional $2 billion in profit each, a 13 percent increase in revenue, and there has been a revolving door between the Trump administration and these companies — including border czar Tom Homan and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, who were previously employed by GEO.

“As of March 2026, the Washington State Department of Health received over 3,500 complaints about [NWDC]. Individuals have reported being sexually assaulted by an officer in their unit; unsanitary conditions, including unclean drinking water, worms, hair, and metal in food, and black mold in showers; and insufficient medical care. State oversight is an essential way to help ensure that the people detained in these facilities at U.S. taxpayer expense are being treated with dignity. Attempting to circumvent such oversight by purchasing substandard detention facilities and continuing to allow such inhumane conditions to persist is unacceptable,” continued the Members.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle S. Bynum (OR-05), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).

title: RILEY TAKES ON STREAMING GIANTS WITH BILL TO END AD-FREE BAIT-AND-SWITCH
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) introduced the Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act, legislation to crack down on streaming companies that promise customers commercial-free viewing, then change the rules and force them to sit through advertisements.

Many digital streaming platforms that built massive user bases on promises of commercial-free viewing have later added advertisement to their default tiers for both live and on-demand programming. For example, RedZone – the NFL’s popular streaming service – recently announced it would broadcast advertisements for the first time in its 17-year history. Outraged fans viewed the change as a bait-and-switch that fundamentally breached the ad-free experience they had already purchased.

“If you pay for ad-free, you should get ad-free. It’s that simple,” Riley said. “For years, football fans were promised seven hours of commercial-free football. Now the big streaming companies are moving the goalposts to squeeze even more money out of hardworking people. Upstate New Yorkers are sick and tired of getting ripped off. My bill makes these companies honor their promises and gives fans what they paid for.”

RedZone is not alone in its change from an ad-free model. Across the industry, major streaming platforms are introducing commercials into previously ad-free tiers, often forcing users to pay an additional surcharge to restore the uninterrupted experience they originally signed up for. The Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act would prohibit streaming services from adding commercials to paid subscriptions originally advertised or offered as commercial-free within one year or the length of the original contract.

The Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act is endorsed by the Sports Fans Coalition.

“If sports fans pay extra to watch games without additional commercial interruptions, they should get what they pay for – no ads. We thank Congressman Josh Riley for throwing the flag on the bait-and-switch some streaming services are pulling on fans,” said David Goodfriend, Chair of the Sports Fans Coalition.

You can read the text of the legislation HERE.

title: Port of Wilmington Awarded Federal Grant to Expand Capacity,...
text:
WILMINGTON, NC - Today, Congressman David Rouzer (NC-07) announced the U.S. Department of Transportation has awarded the Port of Wilmington $6,002,296 for port improvements through the Infrastructure for Rebuilding America (INFRA) program.

This award will support the development of 140 commercial motor vehicle parking spaces, 50 freight container staging positions, as well as secure and smart operations infrastructure at the Port of Wilmington in New Hanover County, North Carolina.

“The Port of Wilmington connects Southeastern North Carolina to the world. As freight demand continues to grow, these improvements will help move goods more efficiently, strengthen our supply chains, and support the businesses, workers, and communities who rely on the port,” said Congressman Rouzer. “I’m pleased to see this investment come to our community, which will help ensure the Port of Wilmington can continue to support economic growth across the region.”

"This award and the associated projects work in concert to propel North Carolina Ports to achieve its winning aspiration of being the Southeast’s most trusted, preferred, efficient, customer centric gateway by providing seamless, diversified total cost-advantage solutions for customers, bolstering North Carolina’s economy," said Brian Clark, Executive Director, North Carolina State Ports Authority. "We appreciate Congressman Rouzer’s ongoing support."

The project will help the port accommodate growing freight volumes, expand truck parking and container staging capacity, and reduce delays through more efficient coordination of pickups and deliveries. As a vital economic asset for southeastern North Carolina, the Port of Wilmington connects regional businesses to domestic and international markets. These improvements will help the port meet future freight demand and support continued economic growth across the region.

title: Rep. Roy Demands Answers from FDA on Delayed Review of Biden’s Mail-Order Abortion Pill Policy
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Chip Roy (TX-21) sent a letter to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas demanding answers after the agency indicated that its safety review of mifepristone would not be completed until March 2027, despite assurances that the Biden Administration’s January 2023 modifications to the drug’s dispensing requirements would be addressed by fall 2026. Those modifications eliminated the in-person dispensing requirement and expanded distribution through the mail.

Rep. Roy wrote: “House Republicans cannot be expected to continue funding the implementation of the January 2023 REMS modifications indefinitely while FDA repeatedly extends its review without committing to corrective action.”

The letter comes after Rep. Roy earlier this year agreed to withdraw his amendment that would have prohibited federal funds from being used to implement the Biden Administration’s changes to the mifepristone REMS framework, based on a good-faith understanding that the FDA would complete and publish the mifepristone safety study this fall.

As Roy states in the letter:

“I did not withdraw my amendment so that FDA could conduct an open-ended review while continuing to administer the Biden Administration’s policy.”

He further warned:

“If FDA will not act to reverse the Jan 2023 REMS modifications, including reinstating the in-person dispensing requirement, Congress must act. Absent prompt action, I will seek to include my amendment in the next continuing resolution to prohibit taxpayer dollars from being used to implement, administer, or enforce the Jan 2023 REMS modifications.”

You can read the full letter here.

title: SCHNEIDER INTRODUCES LEGISLATION TO PROTECT ACCESS TO ONLINE RESOURCES FOR LGBTQ STUDENTS
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL –Today, during LGBTQ history month, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) introduced legislation to ensure critical online LGBTQ resources are not blocked at schools and public libraries. Currently, public schools and libraries that receive discounted telecommunications and internet rates through the Federal Communication Commission (FCC) E-Rate program must enforce an internet safety policy that in some cases leads to the blocking of useful LGBTQ resources. The Don’t Block LGBTQ Act would clarify that schools and public libraries that block LGBTQ resources would lose access to discounted rates under the E-rate program.

“During LGBTQ History Month, we celebrate the countless LGBTQ Americans who have strengthened our communities and helped move our country forward,” said Schneider. “LGBTQ Americans, especially young people, deserve access to information, support, and resources that can make a meaningful difference in their lives. I'm proud to introduce this legislation to ensure LGBTQ individuals are not prevented from receiving support – whether asking health questions, responding to bullying, or seeking advice about coming out to family and friends.”

According to the American Psychological Association, the majority of LGBTQ+ youth have turned to a mental health professional or experienced symptoms of anxiety. Access to resources on where to reach for help is critical to ensuring youth have the support they need.

title: SCHNEIDER, MURPHY INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN LEGISLATION TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO MEDICAL SUPPLIES
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL — Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congressman Greg Murphy, M.D., (NC-03) introduced the bipartisan Access to Medical Supplies Act, which would exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare’s Competitive Acquisition Program for five years to protect Medicare beneficiaries who rely on them.

“Everyone deserves access to the medical supplies that will improve their quality of life and improve their well-being. Unfortunately, the new rule from CMS making ostomy and urological medical supplies part of a competitive bidding program undermines this goal,” said Schneider. “These are highly specialized prosthetics, and a sweeping rule like this should never be put in place without patient, provider, and supplier feedback. I’m proud to work with my Ways and Means colleague Dr. Murphy to introduce the bipartisan Access to Medical Supplies Act to pause this rule and ensure patients continue to receive the medical supplies they need.”

“Patients who rely on urological and ostomy supplies should not be forced to sacrifice the products that work best for them,” said Murphy. “As a physician, I know that every patient has different medical needs, and access to the right supplies can make a meaningful difference in their health and quality of life. This legislation will give patients, physicians, and policymakers time to evaluate competitive bidding and ensure that any future program protects access to the supplies patients need.”

The Access to Medical Supplies Act would:

Exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare’s Competitive Acquisition Program for five years, from January 1, 2028, through December 31, 2032.

Establish a technical expert panel of patients, caregivers, clinicians, suppliers, manufacturers, and other stakeholders to evaluate the impact of competitive bidding and recommend changes.

Establish a demonstration project to assess the impact of competitive bidding on patient access and health outcomes before broader implementation.

title: Congresswoman Scholten Introduces Legislation to Expand Conservation Efforts, Federal Funding Opportunities for Great Lakes Region
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Representatives Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Tim Walberg (R-MI-05), Marcy Kaptur (D-OH-09), Bill Huizenga (R-MI-04), David Joyce (R-OH-14), Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) and Tom Barrett (R-MI-07) introduced the Regional Great Lakes Partnership Act. The bipartisan, bicameral bill would expand access to federal support for the Great Lakes region, including for conservation research and programs.

“As the largest freshwater system in the world, the Great Lakes are one of Michigan’s greatest assets,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “I’m proud to join my colleagues on both sides of the aisle in supporting the Regional Great Lakes Partnership Act. This commonsense bill will strengthen the research and coordination that keeps the Great Lakes region healthy. Investing in our Great Lakes is investing in our future, and it’s crucial that we conserve this resource for the next generation.”

“The Great Lakes and their connected waterways are invaluable resources for Michigan and the United States,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “As a Co-Chair of the Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, I am proud to help introduce this bipartisan bill to strengthen federal support for Great Lakes research and conservation for future generations to enjoy these national treasures.”

“Michigan is the Great Lakes state, period. Jobs, recreation, and tourism across the Midwest depend on a healthy and flourishing Great Lakes ecosystem,” said Congresswoman Stevens. “I’m proud to work alongside my colleagues of both parties to ensure that Michigan receives our fair share of federal investment that will protect and preserve our Lakes for generations to come.”

“The Great Lakes are a critical resource for the economies and communities that surround them,” said Congressman Joyce. “As Co-Chair of the Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, I am proud to be an original co-sponsor of this bipartisan legislation, which will strengthen federal partnerships and expand funding opportunities to advance the research, coordination, and conservation efforts needed to protect the Great Lakes — ensuring they remain a resource our communities can rely on for generations to come.”

“As the largest freshwater system in the world, the Great Lakes are central to Michigan’s economy, identity, and long‑term prosperity,” said Congressman Walberg. “The bipartisan Regional Great Lakes Partnership Act ensures the region receives its fair share of federal support, strengthening the research and conservation work needed to protect this indispensable resource. We must equip our partners with the tools necessary to safeguard the waters and communities that rely on a healthy Great Lakes ecosystem.”

“As a Co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, I helped introduce this legislation to close a gap in a national program that benefits only coastal ocean states. The bill continues our work together to ensure the federal government levels the playing field to commit equivalent, well‑deserved resources to our Great Lakes region,” said Congresswoman Kaptur. “The Great Lakes are central and essential to Northwest Ohio’s livelihood and economic well-being, and enabling the Great Lakes Commission to participate in this NOAA program will strengthen data sharing, enhance information access, and improve management of our coastal and ecosystem resources. In Lake Erie’s Western Basin, home to the shallowest and southernmost shoreline in the Great Lakes system, we face these challenges in real ways and will continue to lead in advancing research and information exchange for the benefit of our entire region.”

“As Co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, I have made it my mission to have the federal government recognize the Great Lakes as a national priority,” said Congressman Huizenga. “The Regional Great Lakes Partnership Act furthers this objective by enhancing the Great Lakes Commission’s steadfast work to protect and conserve Michigan’s most valuable natural resource.”

“Protecting the Great Lakes means protecting our water, wildlife, and communities throughout the region,” said Congressman Barrett. “This bipartisan legislation will help bring federal resources to the table and strengthen the partnerships already working to preserve our state’s natural resources. I’m proud to work with colleagues from across the region to ensure our Great Lakes remain healthy for generations to come.”

This legislation would designate the Great Lakes Commission (GLC) as the official regional Great Lakes Partnership within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Regional Ocean Partnerships Program. This designation would expand opportunities for the Great Lakes region to access existing federal funding, supporting the Great Lakes Commission’s longstanding work to coordinate research, conservation, and restoration efforts across the region.

The Great Lakes Commission (GLC) brings together eight U.S. states and two Canadian provinces to protect the Great Lakes and promote economic growth in the Great Lakes basin. The GLC is composed of the states of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin.

NOAA’s Regional Ocean Partnerships (ROPs) coordinate interstate ocean and coastal resource management efforts and create opportunities for increased efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Although NOAA administers four Regional Ocean Partnerships (ROPs) across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Gulf, and West Coast, the Great Lakes currently lack an ROP. Designating the GLC as the region’s ROP will ensure the Great Lakes region receives its fair share of program funding.

Companion legislation, introduced in the Senate by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and Bernie Moreno (R-OH), has been advanced by the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

Read the full text of the billhere.

title: Sherman Joins House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats in Condemning Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), a senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, joined Ranking Member Gregory W. Meeks and fellow Committee Democrats in condemning President Trump’s decision to authorize purchases of Russian diesel, warning that the move would enrich Vladimir Putin and undermine U.S. support for Ukraine:

“President Trump is blaming Ukraine for rising fuel costs to distract from the real cause: his war of choice in Iran. The American people are paying the price for this president’s decisions, and now he is filling the Kremlin’s war chest. It is a shameful betrayal of Ukraine, our European allies, and everything the United States stands for.

“We welcome the bipartisan condemnation of this deal. But condemnation alone is not enough. When Republicans have had the chance to do more, most have refused.

“In April, HFAC Democrats introduced the End Russian Oil Windfalls Act, legislation that would bar the administration from issuing the very licenses Trump is now using to enrich Putin. Republicans declined to cosponsor it and Republican leadership has not moved it since.

"If Republicans are genuinely outraged by this deal they should join us, pass this legislation, and put a check on a president who is more interested in appeasing Putin and enriching himself and his inner circle than defending American interests or our commitments to Ukraine. Congress has the power to act.”

Sherman and his Democratic colleagues also renewed calls for passage of the End Russian Oil Windfalls Act (H.R. 8222), legislation introduced in April to prevent the administration from issuing such licenses.

title: Rep. Tlaib introduces bill to remove and prohibit Flock cameras, mass surveillance technologies
text:
INKSTER, MICH. – U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) introduced the Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act today with community leaders in front of a Flock camera in Inkster, Michigan, whose city officials just signed a long-term contract with the mass surveillance company. The bill would prohibit the use of federal funds to purchase or operate any automated mass surveillance systems, including automatic license plate readers like Flock. It would also require state and local governments to divest from such systems to remain eligible for certain federal law enforcement grants.

It is the only bill in Congress designed to completely prohibit the use of automated mass surveillance technology, including biometric surveillance systems and facial recognition technology.

“The mass surveillance crisis is not a dystopian fantasy—it is already here. Our children and neighbors cannot go to the park, drive down the street, go to work, or exercise their Constitutional rights without their privacy being breached,” said Rep. Tlaib. “Flock’s technology isn’t making us safer. Instead it has been used to stalk people, mis-identify and arrest innocent people, surveil protestors, and wrongfully record our neighbors. My bill would prevent our government on all levels from selling us out to Big Tech companies that trample our civil rights for profit.”

Over 200 cities and counties, including Westland and Lincoln Park in Michigan, have cancelled their Flock contracts due to resident outrage. According to Data for Progress, a majority of voters — 52% — view Flock unfavorably, a sentiment that continues to grow as Flock and its abuses become more widespread.

“People everywhere are starting to recognize that conflating surveillance with safety makes communities less safe,” said Tawana Petty, digital and data justice organizer from Detroit. “The persistent abuse of Flock cameras and other surveillance systems by law enforcement agencies across the United States, and the lack of transparency by the companies that market them has caused an awakening among residents and city government agencies who are ridding themselves of the technologies. The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act is responsive to the national call to protect all neighbors from being stalked and harmed by reckless actors and opportunistic corporations.”

“Flock cameras are overall dangerous to a free society,” said Geri Biggs, Dearborn resident and community advocate. “There have already been cases cited where individuals have been illegally stalked, including young women, by individuals in positions of power with nefarious intentions.Allowing this information to be shared with companies poses a threat to the civil rights of us all, and at the very least can be intimidating to the most vulnerable in our communities.”

“Flock cameras are a significant invasion of people’s privacy and need to be seriously controlled, or eliminated,” said Larry Biggs, Dearborn resident and community advocate. “As soon as information is gathered by Flock, it can be shared with other law enforcement agencies, including ICE and CBP, with no control. All other invasions of people’s privacy must get a search warrant or have probable cause. Flock cameras have no such requirements.”

“Flock and other vendors of AI-surveillance technology pose an existential risk to our democracy,” said Elijah Nemr, member of Metro Detroit Democratic Socialists of America. “With capabilities ranging from video and audio capture, to the processing and permanent storage of our most sensitive data, every person who values their independence and privacy must oppose this technology in all of its forms. DSA has successfully organized to end Flock in Westland, and we will continue organizing with our neighbors to get Flock out of our communities!”

“The spread of mass surveillance systems is an existential threat to political and personal freedom,” said Jibran Ludwig, Legislative Strategist at Fight for the Future. “We have seen the current administration weaponize these tools to terrorize immigrant communities and protestors, while simultaneously forcing every single person into dragnet surveillance that puts us all in danger. But the threat goes far beyond our current political moment: the history of mass surveillance is an endless litany of abuse at every level. This bill is an urgent effort to uproot the mass surveillance systems which have been built up from the local level and down from the federal.”

“Indivisible is proud to endorse the Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act. These automated mass surveillance systems don’t just violate our fundamental rights to privacy and civil liberties – they fuel Big Tech’s broader efforts to harvest as much of our personal information as possible so they can bleed our bank accounts dry and monopolize markets,” said Andrew O’Neill, National Advocacy Director of Indivisible. “We’ve also witnessed Republicans increasingly weaponize warrantless mass surveillance as a fascist tool for political gain and to help their donors profit off massive amounts of our stolen data. This isn’t new, and it has nothing to do with safety or justice: the first surveillance laws in the U.S. passed in 1712 targeted Black, mixed-race, and Indigenous people, weaponizing public safety to enforce white supremacy. Ever since, surveillance systems and increasingly sophisticated technologies have been intentionally and disproportionately deployed in predominantly Black and low-income communities. It’s more urgent than ever that Congress protect our communities from these attacks.”

The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act comprehensively removes automated mass surveillance systems and similar technologies by:

Prohibiting federal funds being used by federal, state, or local government entities to purchase, deploy, install, maintain, access, lease, or operate any automated mass surveillance system, including automated license plate readers like Flock, biometric surveillance systems, and facial recognition technology.

Prohibiting the federal government or any employee or officer of an agency acting in an official capacity from using any automated mass surveillance systems or information derived from such systems.

Requiring the removal of any automated mass surveillance system deployed or operated with federal funding.

Requiring any unit of government in possession of data generated by federally-funded automated mass surveillance systems to permanently delete that data.

Rendering data obtained in violation of the Act’s provisions inadmissible in court.

Requiring state and local governments applying for certain federal law enforcement funding to certify that they do not operate or access automated mass surveillance networks.

Read the full bill text here.

The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act is cosponsored by 6 members of Congress: U.S. Reps. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

title: Trahan, Markey, Warren, McGovern Demand Study of Impacts of Amazon’s Westborough Drone Program
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senators Edward J. Markey (D-MA), and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Congressman Jim McGovern (MA-02) wrote to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator Bryan Bedford and Amazon.com, Inc. CEO Andy Jassy urging Amazon to work with the FAA to conduct an Environmental Assessment of its proposed drone delivery facility in Westborough, Massachusetts, before launching operations there. Communities have raised concerns about the Amazon Prime Air drone delivery program’s impact on the environment and residents’ quality-of-life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy.

In the letters, the lawmakers wrote, “Despite the noise and environmental risks of Amazon’s drone operations, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has authorized operators such as Amazon to deploy their fleets without completing a site-specific Environmental Assessment (EA) of their impact on the surrounding communities. This decision is especially problematic in Massachusetts localities, given the differences between it and previously studied communities, local opposition, and the inadequate treatment of the risks associated with transporting hazardous-materials.”

The lawmakers continued, “An independent resident survey, with more than 1,200 responses as of early October 2026, found 92 percent of respondents opposed the proposed Westborough facility. At a state level, Massachusetts is one of 15 states currently suing the FAA for its nationwide FONSI. In other words, Amazon is now trying to quickly move drone operations into Massachusetts under a streamlined regulatory process the state itself is challenging. These are precisely the community-specific noise, safety, and quality-of-life concerns a site-specific EA and comment period exist to surface and address.”

The lawmakers urged, “These concerns – applying the FONSI to a community different from those previously assessed by the FAA, significant local opposition, and the limited evaluation of hazardous material risks – warrant requiring Amazon to complete a site-specific EA, with a public comment period, before the FAA authorizes Prime Air operations in Massachusetts.”

title: Massachusetts Awarded $142 Million in Federal Home Heating Assistance Funds
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) highlighted the awarding of $142,330,091 in federal funding to Massachusetts through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP). The early allocation follows Trahan’s request for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to release Massachusetts’ LIHEAP funding before the end of the month to combat surging home heating costs.

“No family in Massachusetts should have to choose between heating their home and affording groceries or medicine,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “With heating oil prices up nearly 75 percent from last year, that choice is becoming a reality for far too many households. Releasing these funds early will help families prepare for the winter ahead. But this year’s allocation falls short of last year’s at a time when the need is greater than ever. Congress must act to restore and strengthen this lifeline.”

This year’s $142.3 million allocation is nearly $4 million less than Massachusetts’ initial allocation last year, which totaled $146 million. The drop is driven by the expiration of the five-year LIHEAP increase included in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which delivered an additional $6.4 million to the Commonwealth last year alone over the baseline $139.6 million allocation.

Crude oil prices have topped $100 per barrel multiple times this year, most recently on September 15. Because heating oil is refined from crude, those spikes hit Massachusetts households hardest. State utility shutoff moratoriums protect many families through the coldest months, but they do nothing for households that must pay in full before a heating oil delivery.

The LIHEAP program has long been underfunded. On average, just 20 percent of eligible households receive assistance each year. In 2023, Trahan led an effort toincrease federal LIHEAP funding. Earlier this month, Trahan, Senator Elizabeth Warren, and Congressman Stephen Lynch led 24 of their colleagues in pressing the Department of Energy to act on soaring heating oil costs and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP, which it has tried to eliminate.

Massachusetts residents can learn more about and apply for heating assistance HERE.

title: Congressmen Carter, Thompson Visit Nation’s Largest Permanent ICE Migrant Detention Facility
text:
NATCHEZ, MS – Today, Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, and Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA), Committee Member, released the below statement on their surprise oversight visit yesterday to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility at Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC) in Mississippi, the nation’s largest migrant detention facility.

“One of Congress’ primary responsibilities is oversight of federal agencies, and we exercised that power – and legal right – in an unannounced visit to ACCC after a summer of crises, protests, and power outages. We wanted an unvarnished look at the institution to make sure that facility problems highlighted in correspondence our offices and in public inspection reports are being addressed, and that everyone in the facility has access to their constitutional due process rights. Regardless of a person’s station in life, they are still human and deserve safe shelter with adequate, sanitary food and water, and access to health care.

“We continue to have concerns that detainees aren’t able to obtain access to adequate mental health services, a full understanding of what crimes they are charged with, and transparency and accountability for when ACCC staff fail in upholding their constitutional rights. As the Trump administration continues to weaponize ICE against communities across the country, we will continue rigorous oversight of immigrant detention facilities so that the law is followed and immigrants have access to their full constitutional rights.”

Background

Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC), operated by the private prison company CoreCivic, is the largest permanent immigration detention facility in the U.S. and detains an average of 1,878 men daily.

In the past six months, ACCC and the men detained there have experienced multiple crises. In May 2026, ICE’s Office of Detention Oversight inspected ACCC and downgraded the facility from a “Superior” rating to “Acceptable/Adequate,” with only 24 of 28 standards met. In July, nearly 70 detainees submitted a petition to the warden demanding an end to the practice of placing three detainees in cells meant to hold two people. During the week of August 10, 2026, a lengthy power outage at ACCC left detainees without air conditioning for two days in nearly 100-degree heat. On August 22, 2026, around 100 male detainees started a protest over poor living conditions, spoiled food, and meager rations.

title: Reps. Carter, Moskowitz Introduce the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act to Strengthen Campus Resilience
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA) and Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Co-Chairs of the Disaster Preparedness and Recovery Caucus, introduced the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act. This legislation authorizes $100 million in annual federal funding for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to distribute to higher education institutions. These grants would improve institutions’ capacity, planning, and facilities to better prepare for, and respond to, disasters and other emergencies that directly impact students, administrators, and staff. The need for greater disaster preparedness was evident when Hurricanes Katrina, Ida, and Irma devastated universities in Louisiana and Florida, and when wildfires forced evacuations of California campuses.

“Our climate crisis makes extreme weather events more frequent and severe, so we need to ensure uniquely vulnerable communities, such as our colleges and universities, have the support and resources they need to prepare for and respond to disasters and emergency situations,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m partnering with Rep. Moskowitz to introduce this legislation and take necessary steps toward preparing our institutions of higher education for protecting the lives, housing, property, and futures of our young adults and the staff that support them before disaster strikes – not after a storm has already arrived.”

“As Florida’s former emergency management director, I know that the time to prepare for a disaster is before it strikes. No student should be left wondering where to go or whether their campus can keep them safe when a disaster hits,” said Congressman Moskowitz. “Families send their children to college trusting that their safety is a priority. That responsibility starts long before the first evacuation order.”

Background

American colleges and universities function as small communities, often housing tens of thousands of students, staff, and researchers in concentrated areas, making them uniquely vulnerable to a range of natural disasters and other emergencies. Campus shootings and other acts of violence, from Virginia Tech to Michigan State, have shown that institutions need well-rehearsed active-threat plans and protocols, reliable mass-notification systems, trained threat-assessment teams, and coordination with local law enforcement. Additionally, climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of hurricanes, wildfires, floods, extreme heat, and other events that can shut down campuses, displace students, and damage infrastructure.

Institutions have a duty of care for the many students who live on campus far from family, including international students, students with disabilities, and low-income students who face additional challenges. Investing in comprehensive emergency planning, resilient infrastructure, continuity-of-operations strategies, accessible communication, and other resources protects lives, preserves academic and research missions, and limits financial impacts. As these threats become more frequent and often overlap, campuses need additional support to make preparedness a core institutional responsibility.

The Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education strengthens higher education resilience by establishing a $100 million annual FEMA grant program to help eligible higher education institutions create or expand emergency management and preparedness capacity.

Eligible uses of grant funds include personnel costs to expand emergency preparedness; creating or updating comprehensive institutional emergency management plans; infrastructure and facility construction or improvements for emergency operations centers or areas of refuge; and equipment and technology to enhance interagency coordination.

title: Congressman Turner Visits ﻿Battle Sight Technologies in Dayton
text:
DAYTON, OH — Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10) recently visited Battle Sight Technologies in Dayton to tour the company’s facility, see demonstrations of its latest technologies, and meet with company leadership to discuss its work supporting warfighters and other frontline personnel.

Battle Sight Technologies is a Dayton-founded, veteran-owned small business developing and commercializing technologies for military, law enforcement, first responder and emergency-management use.

During the visit, Rep. Turner received a firsthand look at Battle Sight’s production capabilities and the groundbreaking technology designed to support American war fighters. He also discussed the challenges small defense companies face in moving promising technologies from research and prototyping into procurement and production.

The company’s work reflects the role local small businesses play in strengthening the defense industrial base and bringing new capabilities to the warfighter.

Rep. Turner has long fought to strengthen the Miami Valley’s defense and innovation economy and support local companies developing technologies that serve national security and public safety needs.

title: Rep. Turner, Mayor Ethan Reynolds, ﻿Xenia City Council and Green County Commission Honor Gil Whitney
text:
XENIA, OH — Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10) joined Xenia Mayor Ethan Reynolds with Xenia City Council Members Wesley Smith, James Crawford, Rachel Huffman, and Jesse Rubio, and Greene County Commissioners Sarah J. Mays and Richard Gould at the Xenia Post Office to applaud Rep. Turner’s legislation to rename the facility the “Gil Whitney Post Office Building,” honoring the longtime WHIO broadcaster whose warning helped save lives during the devastating 1974 Xenia tornado. Rep. Turner’s legislation passed the House of Representatives with the support of Ohio’s entire House delegation.

Two of Gil Whitney's children, John and Jennifer were also in attendance.

“More than fifty years ago, as one of the deadliest storms in our region’s history closed in on Xenia, Gil Whitney identified the imminent danger and took action to warn his neighbors,” said Rep. Turner.

“People in Xenia still remember that warning and the lives Gil saved. Naming this post office after him ensures that the community he protected will always remember the heroism he showed when it mattered most.”

Gil Whitney spent much of his career at WHIO Television and Radio and also served his community as a volunteer firefighter and through numerous local organizations.

title: Congressman Valadao Urges Administration to Protect Critical Central Valley Head Start Programs
text:
WASHINGTON – Last week, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Administration for Children and Families (ACF) Assistant Secretary Alex J. Adams regarding the recent Head Start Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM). In his letter, he urged the administration to ensure that the final rule upholds current Head Start performance standards and gives fair consideration to public comments submitted by programs in CA-22.

On August 7, 2026, HHS and ACF proposed a federal rule that would make significant changes to how Head Start programs operate in the Central Valley. This includes removing the nationwide Head Start standards, requiring English-only learning in classrooms, lowering the cap on federal funding for administrative expenses, and changing the staff-to-child classroom ratios in order to create more program flexibility, reduce red-tape, and ensure local and state decision-making. Despite these goals, the NPRM falls short of maintaining the program standards that have been central to Head Start’s success.

“The proposed rulemaking would fundamentally reshape the nationwide Head Start program by eliminating performance standards that have been central to its success for decades. While the administration describes the proposal as an effort to modernize the program and provide greater flexibility to state and local leaders, it also creates significant uncertainty for the communities and families that rely on Head Start,” wrote Congressman Valadao. “Removing the performance standards would shift administrative burden onto already strained programs, requiring them to navigate a complex set of state and local regulations. Providers are concerned that removing clear performance standards could leave key requirements open to subjective interpretation, making it more difficult for programs to understand and meet federal expectations, potentially putting longstanding Head Start grants at risk.”

While the proposed rule does have a process for programs seeking exemptions from certain requirements like the English-only provision and the administrative cost cap, there is no clear timeline for agency review and decision-making on waiver requests. This lack of clarity would force Head Start providers to operate with uncertainty for an unspecified amount of time while the federal government makes decisions that directly affect their ability to continue operations. In the letter, Congressman Valadao expressed support for modernizing the Head Start program to strengthen outcomes for children and parents.

Congressman Valadao has been a strong supporter of Head Start throughout his time in Congress. He has visited several classrooms to see firsthand how the program invests in the success of Central Valley families and has consistently advocated for increased funding to support its work.

Read the full letter here.

title: Vindman Introduces ‘Make Data Centers Pay Act’ to Protect Virginians from Rising Electricity Costs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to protect hardworking Virginia families and small businesses from being forced to shoulder the rising electricity costs associated with the growing electricity demands of data centers.

The Make Data Centers Pay Act would amend the Federal Power Act to require large and medium-sized data centers to pay the full incremental costs associated with their electricity use, preventing those expenses from being passed on to residential customers and small businesses.

“Families in Virginia and across the country should not have to pay higher electricity bills to subsidize some of the largest and most energy-intensive data centers and computing facilities in the world,” said Vindman. “As data centers and artificial intelligence drive growing demand for electricity, we need to make sure the companies benefiting from that growth pay their fair share. My bill puts ratepayers first and protects hardworking Virginians from being stuck with higher utility bills to subsidize billion-dollar corporations.”

Under the legislation, covered data centers and high-density computing facilities with electricity demands of at least 20 megawatts would be required to cover the incremental costs of serving their electricity needs. This would help ensure that the costs of infrastructure and electricity service needed to support these facilities are borne by the companies driving that demand, rather than shifted onto everyday ratepayers.

BACKGROUND

Vindman has been a champion for holding data centers and electric utilities accountable.

In August 2026, he introduced the Smart Data Center Policy Act to prevent data center development near neighborhoods, schools, and parks.

Vindman also introduced the Home Energy Affordability Act to limit how often utilities can change residential utility rates and change prices for everyday Virginians, as well as the Utility Hikes Transparency Act, which would create the first comprehensive, machine-readable federal database of retail utility rate changes in the United States.

He has also fought against corruption in the energy sector by championing the Energy Utility Lobbying Ban Act, which would bar former government officials from lobbying on behalf of the companies they used to regulate.

What’s more, Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy, raising concerns about its potential impact on electricity rates and Virginia consumers.

Most recently, he delivered remarks at a Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing on the proposed merger, urging regulators to reject the proposal and put the interests of ratepayers ahead of corporate profits.

title: Womack’s Truck Parking Funding Put to Use in Arkansas’s Third District and Across Nation
text:
ARKANSAS — October 14, 2026… Today, House Appropriations Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (THUD), and Related Agencies Subcommittee Chairman Steve Womack (AR-3) announced that the Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT) is set to receive a $23 million grant to design and construct truck parking infrastructure in Crawford County along the future segment of I-49. The grant is part of the Department of Transportation’s (USDOT) Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highway Projects (INFRA) program.

Chairman Womack’s THUD appropriations bill funds the Department of Transportation, including the INFRA program. In his Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 and 2027 THUD appropriations bills, Chairman Womack allocated $200 million to address the national truck parking shortage. The I-49 truck parking project is one of fourteen projects across 12 states awarded INFRA program Track 2 funding to build safe and accessible commercial truck parking infrastructure.

Chairman Womack said, “Truckers are the cornerstone of our interstate commerce. We depend on these hardworking men and women to transport goods and fuel across our country, keeping store shelves stocked and gas tanks filled. A lack of adequate truck parking nationwide puts a strain on drivers, creates safety risks for the traveling public, and jeopardizes our supply chain. This is why I prioritized funding to build truck parking infrastructure in my transportation appropriations bill for two consecutive years. Our truck drivers should not have to worry about finding a safe place to park, no matter where they are. I’m proud that future truckers traveling along I-49 in Crawford County will have that peace of mind, building on the generational benefits that this new interstate segment brings to the River Valley.”

ARDOT Director Jared Wiley said, “Congressman Womack’s leadership in transportation funding has benefited the Arkansas Department of Transportation and the citizens of the Natural State for many years. His efforts at the national level have ensured that $200 million in vital funding is dedicated to much-needed truck parking infrastructure across the country in both fiscal years 2026 and 2027. With Womack’s support, Arkansas was able to secure a $23 million INFRA grant that will pave the way for a new rest area and truck parking facility along future Interstate 49 in Crawford County between the Gun Club Road and Clear Creek Road interchanges. This grant award will help bolster efforts by a wide array of transportation professionals who understand the value of safe and predictable parking for those who keep our economy moving.”

Background: ARDOT will receive $23,024,000 to complete the final design and construction of a new safety rest area and truck parking facility along future I-49 in Crawford County, Arkansas, between the Gun Club Road and Clear Creek Road interchanges. The facility will feature dedicated parking infrastructure accommodating approximately 137 trucks and approximately 49 passenger vehicles. Additionally, the project includes construction of northbound and southbound access ramps, internal one-way circulation roadways, stormwater detention ponds, site utilities, and lighting.

Chairman Womack has secured $21 million in Community Project Funding for the construction of the 14-mile Alma to Barling segment of I-49, including $18 million in FY 2022 and $3 million in FY 2026. With Chairman Womack’s support, ARDOT received a $25 million USDOT RAISE grant in 2024 for the project.

See the full list of awards HERE.

Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) has represented Arkansas’s Third Congressional District since 2011. He is a member of the House Appropriations Committee.

title: President Trump Signs Blackburn’s Bill to Support Music Tourism Into Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) released the following statements after President Trump signed into law their bipartisan legislation, the American Music Tourism Act, to support music tourism in Tennessee and across the country:

“The Volunteer State is home to so many iconic landmarks for tourists to experience – from Graceland in Memphis to the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville to Dollywood in Pigeon Forge,” said Senator Blackburn. “Music tourism has such a positive impact on Tennessee’s economy, and we need to ensure that fans from all over the world continue to celebrate our state’s rich history of music for generations to come. The American Music Tourism Act will promote and support the fast-growing tourism industry, and I am pleased it has been signed into law by President Trump.”

“We're glad to see our American Music Tourism Act become law,” said Senator Hickenlooper. “Our new law will drive even more visitors to our outstanding venues across Colorado.”

The American Music Tourism Act is co-sponsored by U.S. Senators Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), and Ted Budd (R-N.C.).

BACKGROUND

Music tourism – both the act of visiting sites important to the history of American music culture and the act of traveling for concerts and music festivals – is a vital industry for American culture and an economic driver for our communities.

Music tourism has emerged as a top travel trend, with the market forecasted to reach $11.3 billion in revenue by 2032.

The United States, which boasts one of world’s largest music industries that generates over $43 billion in revenue each year, is one of the main beneficiaries of this international interest in music tourism.

THE AMERICAN MUSIC TOURISM ACT

The American Music Tourism Act will leverage the existing tourism framework within the Department of Commerce to highlight and promote music tourism in the United States.

Specifically, this law will require:

The Assistant Secretary to implement a plan to support and increase music tourism for both domestic and international visitors; and

A report to Congress on the successes and vulnerabilities of the Assistant Secretary’s goals to increase travel and tourism.

Click here for bill text.

ENDORSEMENTS

This legislation is endorsed by the National Independent Venue Association, Nashville Songwriters Association International, the Recording Academy, the Tennessee Entertainment Commission, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame & Museum, National Music Publishers Association, the Tennessee Department of Tourist Development, Broadcast Music, Inc., the Memphis Rock 'n' Soul Museum, Memphis Tourism, the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, Recording Industry Association of America, Overton Park Shell, Society of Composers and Lyricists, andGlobal Music Rights.

“Independent venues and festivals are the lifeblood of local communities, not just as cultural hubs but as powerful engines of economic activity…Fans travel for them. They book hotels, fill restaurants, and shop on Main Street because a show is happening that night. The American Music Tourism Act is a jobs bill. We are thrilled the House and Senate have prioritized driving domestic and foreign visitors to the nation’s music attractions and independent stages. Now, we encourage the President to sign it and give the country its first national strategy for music tourism. It is a bipartisan policy that treats live music as the economic asset it already is. We are grateful to Senators Marsha Blackburn and John Hickenlooper and to Representatives Diana Harshbarger and Nanette Barragán for their leadership, and to the Senate Commerce and House Energy and Commerce committees for moving forward this bill,” said Stephen Parker, Executive Director, National Independent Venue Association.

“The Nashville Songwriters Association International (NSAI) is elated that the American Tourism Act has been enacted. As the owner of an iconic music venue, The Bluebird Café, we acutely understand the economic and social impact of music tourism. The music tourism market is projected to exceed $11 billion in revenue by 2032. With adoption of this Act we expect that the music tourism industry can thrive beyond that expectation,” said Bart Herbison, Executive Director, Nashville Songwriter’s Association International.

“Today is a great day for music people everywhere. The signing of the American Music Tourism Act recognizes what we've always known: music doesn't just move us; it moves local economies. From the venues that anchor their neighborhoods to the creators who fill them, this law honors the real impact of music on communities across the country. We're grateful to Senators Blackburn and Hickenlooper and Representatives Harshbarger and Barragán for their bipartisan leadership, and to the president for signing this into law. The Recording Academy has championed this since day one, and we're proud to see it cross the finish line,” said Harvey Mason jr., CEO, Recording Academy.

“The passage of the American Music Tourism Act is a major win for Tennessee and for music communities nationwide. This legislation strengthens our ability to showcase Tennessee’s iconic music destinations and drive economic growth through increased tourism,” said Bob Raines, Executive Director, Tennessee Entertainment Commission.

“The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame honors the artists whose music connects us all. We share stories of the people, events, and songs that shape our world through digital content, innovative exhibits, live music, engaging programs, and our annual Induction Ceremony, and have welcomed more than 15 million visitors from all 50 states and around the world to our Museum in Cleveland, Ohio. We support the American Music Tourism Act to reinforce our music community’s massive economic and emotional impact on the U.S. and beyond,” said Greg Harris, President & CEO, Rock & Roll Hall of Fame & Museum.

“U.S. music venues showcase songwriter’s work for travelers from all over the world. We are pleased to see the American Music Tourism Act pass into law, which we expect will lead not only to commercial growth but also a greater appreciation of American music, history, culture, and creators. We greatly appreciate Senators Blackburn and Hickenlooper’s continued leadership and focus on protecting and encouraging music creation and consumption,” said David Israelite, President & CEO, National Music Publishers Association.

title: Senators Coons, Cornyn introduce bipartisan bill to strengthen civics education
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.) and John Cornyn (R-Texas) introduced the bipartisan Strengthening Civics Education Act, legislation to strengthen civics and history education in schools across the country and ensure students have the knowledge and skills needed to understand American government and participate in civic life.

“Civic engagement lies at the heart of our democratic process,” said Senator Coons. “As we celebrate 250 years as a nation, I am proud to partner with Senator Cornyn on this bipartisan effort to support the preparation of strong civics educators, the promotion of a full understanding of civics among our students, and the training of a new generation of active citizens.”

“It is our duty to ensure future generations learn and uphold the values that formed the bedrock of our nation more than 250 years ago, but studies have shown that teachers don’t have the resources they need to help teach these critical topics,” said Senator Cornyn. “The Strengthening Civics Education Act will help equip educators with the tools necessary to strengthen students’ foundational knowledge of our country’s history, institutions, and system of government and impart the importance of civic engagement.”

The majority of American students lack basic proficiency in civics and U.S. history, and the most recent national assessment showed eighth-grade civics scores declining in 2022 after more than two decades of stagnation. Civics education remains uneven across the country: just six states require a year-long civics course, and only one in five social studies teachers report feeling well prepared to support civic learning.

These gaps reflect a broader nationwide underinvestment in civics education. Students cannot fully understand the institutions that govern their lives or meaningfully participate in civic life if they are not given the opportunity to learn how those institutions work. As the United States marks the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, Senators Coons and Cornyn are seeking to reverse that trend by strengthening civics educators and education.

The Strengthening Civics Education Act would take several steps to strengthen civics and history education nationwide:

Strengthen civics and history education: Reauthorize and expand the existing American History for Freedom program to support education on American political thought and history, representative democracy, constitutional democracy, free institutions, and Western civilization

Support teachers: Require grantees to collaborate with local educational agencies to give elementary and secondary school teachers opportunities to deepen their knowledge of civics and history, while supporting teacher preparation initiatives focused on civics and history

Expand access to open educational resources: Promote the development and use of high-quality, open educational resources on American political thought and history and the impact of American representative democracy and constitutional democracies around the world

Strengthen national civics assessments: Require the National Assessment of Educational Progress to assess student achievement in civics and history in grades four,eight, and 12 at least once every two years, with a methodology designed to provide statistically significant state-level data

Connect students and teachers with federal opportunities: Establish an America250 Civics clearinghouse, a publicly available website compiling federal scholarship and fellowship opportunities related to civics for students and teachers

Protect state and local control: Clarify that nothing in the legislation would allow the federal government to prescribe a national curriculum in civics or history or supersede state and local control over instruction

The legislation is endorsed by the CivxNow coalition, the nation’s largest cross-partisan coalition working to prioritize civics education, with more than 410 members.

“The teaching of modern democracy requires that our schools and educators have the innovative resources they need to reach and engage today’s young people – and it requires that our school systems can track and understand what works and what does not,” said Louise Dubé, CEO of iCivics. “The Strengthening Civics Education Act will help make both of those possible.”

“Since 1965, the Center for Civic Education has known that robust support for civic learning and engagement is essential to the American system of self-government. Every school, at every level deserves more opportunities to foster the principles and practices of constitutional democracy. The Strengthening Civics Education Act advances that essential goal. By requiring regular national assessment in civics and history, investing in teacher preparation, and expanding access to high-quality open resources, this legislation sends a clear signal that civic education is not an optional addition to a well-rounded education, it is essential to it. As our nation marks 250 years, the Center for Civic Education supports this bill and calls for civic education to receive the same commitment we have long given to other core subjects,” said Dr. Donna Phillips, president and CEO, Center for Civic Education.

“The Delaware Center for Civics Education is extremely grateful to Senator Coons for remaining a consistent champion of civics education and for co-sponsoring a bipartisan bill that aims to improve how civics is taught and learned. This initiative could not be better timed as it comes at a highly polarized moment in our nation’s history. We are grateful for the opportunity to endorse this bill,” UD Center for Civics said.

“One of the American Bar Association’s core goals is to Advance the Rule of Law and the first objective under that goal is to increase public understanding of and respect for the rule of law and the legal process,” ABA President Barbara J. Howard said. “One way to accomplish this goal is to provide high-quality civic education for people throughout their lives — but beginning as children. The Strengthening Civics Education Act will help ensure that young people understand and appreciate what the rule of law means in their daily lives and that they emerge from school with the knowledge and skills they need to secure American democracy now and in the future.”

“For generations, the Y has helped young people build the knowledge, skills, and confidence to participate in civic life through programs like YMCA Youth and Government. The Strengthening Civics Education Act would expand opportunities for nonprofits to partner with colleges and universities to bring meaningful civic education experiences to more youth nationwide. We are proud to support this bipartisan effort to strengthen civic engagement and prepare the leaders our communities need,” said YMCA of the USA CEOSuzanne McCormick.

The text of the bill is available here.

title: Working Families Tax Cuts Help More Americans Save for Health Care
text:
Washington, D.C.—The Working Families Tax Cuts are making it easier for Americans to save for health care expenses by expanding access to Health Savings Accounts (HSAs). Before the law took effect, only 2 percent of people insured through the federal Affordable Care Act marketplace were enrolled in HSA-eligible plans, which provides a tax-advantaged way to save for qualified medical expenses. By making bronze and catastrophic Affordable Care Act plans HSA-compatible and permanently allowing coverage of certain telehealth services before the deductible is met, the law has expanded HSA eligibility to an estimated 10 million Americans.

“Health savings accounts give families greater control over their health care decisions and how they spend their health care dollars,” said U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho). “By expanding access to these important tax-advantaged tools, the Working Families Tax Cuts are giving millions more Americans the opportunity to save for the care that best meets their needs.”

Key wins:

Makes health insurance plans which cover telehealth and remote care services pre-deductible HSA-eligible

Allows enrollees in bronze and catastrophic Affordable Care Act plans to contribute to an HSA

Allows qualified individuals to contribute to an HSA while participating in a direct primary care service (DPC) arrangement, which allows patients to pay a flat recurring fee for routine care

What they are saying:

“In many cases, the DPC model allows physicians to offer enhanced access and more personalized care than is typically possible under a traditional fee-for-service system… The AAFP greatly appreciates that [the Working Families Tax Cuts] eliminated the prohibition on using health savings account (HSA) funds to pay for a DPC arrangement.” – American Academy of Family Physicians Board Chair Dr. Jen Brull

“Catastrophic plans better reflect the core purpose of insurance—protection against high-cost, unpredictable events—while allowing consumers greater control over routine spending. Combined with expanded health savings account (HSA) eligibility contained in the Working Families Tax Cuts, expanded access to catastrophic plans enables consumers to direct premium savings into tax-advantaged accounts rather than inflated premiums.” – Brian Blase, Gabrielle Minarik and Christopher Medrano of Paragon Health Institute

title: Sens. Cruz, Lee File Amicus Brief Challenging Disbarment of Attorney John Eastman
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sens. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Federal Courts, Oversight, Agency Action, and Federal Rights, and Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, filed an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review the disbarment of Dr. John Eastman related to his legal representation of President Donald Trump. In the brief, the senators argue that Supreme Court review is necessary to clarify the constitutional limits on attorney discipline, protect free speech, and safeguard Americans’ right to independent legal counsel.

Excerpts from the amicus brief are below, and the full text of the brief can be viewed here.

“First, attorneys keep their Free Speech Clause rights when they advocate for clients—and that protection must include room to press disputed and even losing arguments. ‘[T]he First Amendment’s protections extend to licensed professionals much as they do to everyone else.’ Chiles v. Salazar, 607 U.S. 627, 642–43 (2026). And our law develops because advocates ask courts to extend, modify, or reject it.

“Zealous advocacy will disappear if professional survival depends on whether bar regulators later agree with an attorney’s legal analysis. This Court has explained that ‘regulating the content of professionals’ speech poses the inherent risk that the Government seeks not to advance a legitimate regulatory goal, but to suppress unpopular ideas or information.’ NIFLA, 585 U.S. at 771.

“Threatening lawyers’ licenses for controversial advocacy deters willing counsel and therefore burdens clients’ right to petition. A lawyer deciding whether to undertake a controversial representation must account for whether regulators may later characterize his advocacy as unreasonable, false, or professionally forbidden. The prospect of professional exclusion therefore affects representation long before any bar proceeding begins.

“The decision below’s refusal to apply strict scrutiny demands this Court’s review. ‘Because First Amendment freedoms need breathing space to survive, government may regulate in the area only with narrow specificity.’ Button, 371 U.S. at 433. Yet even as the California Bar pursued an ideological crusade against what the decision below itself called “core political speech,” the Review Department never applied strict scrutiny.”

title: Durbin Receives Proclamation From Chicago Metropolitan Agency For Planning In Recognition Of Decades Of Advocacy For Illinois Infrastructure Projects
text:
CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today attended a Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) board meeting, where he was presented with a proclamation in recognition of his decades of public service. Before Durbin received the proclamation, he participated in a brief moderated panel with CMAP leaders—Erin Aleman, Executive Director of CMAP; Gerald Bennett, Mayor of Palos Hills, Illinois; and Gia Biagi, Illinois Transportation Secretary and Metropolitan Planning Organization Policy Committee Chair. Durbin raised the success of the Chicago Region Environmental and Transportation Efficiency (CREATE) Program, a public-private partnership to complete 70 rail projects to reduce rail congestion in the Chicago region. Durbin has helped to secure more than $800 million in federal funding for CREATE.

Throughout his time in Congress, Durbin has supported various infrastructure programs. This includes the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant program, which has awarded more than $30 million to Illinois projects like the Odgen Avenue Corridor Improvement Project in Cook County; the PROTECT grant program which has bolstered the state’s climate resiliency with more than $33 million in funding for Illinois projects; and the All Stations Accessibility Program, which has provided Illinois with more than $184 million to improve accessibility at transit stations across the state.

“Investing in our state’s infrastructure is a win for everyone. We build stronger connections between every region of Illinois, bring great jobs to the state, and ensure that all traveling through our region have a safe and efficient route,” Durbin said. “CMAP has been an invaluable partner in pushing our state’s infrastructure projects forward and preparing for the future, and I look forward to continuing to see CMAP’s leadership make a difference across Illinois.”

A photo of Durbin receiving the proclamation can be found here.

CMAP is a comprehensive planning organization for Cook, DuPage, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry, and Will Counties and 284 communities of northeastern Illinois. In 2010, Durbin secured a $4.25 million federal grant for CMAP’s GO TO 2040 community planning initiative to help CMAP implement its comprehensive plan for a sustainable future.
