title: In Arizona, Gallego Touts Plan to Strengthen Middle Class, Meets with Arizona Students
text:
Senator Gallego discussed economic opportunity, civic engagement, early voting, and education during stops in Phoenix and Chandler

PHOENIX – This past weekend, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) met with Arizona families, students and media to discuss his plan to strengthen the middle class, encourage civic participation and expand educational opportunities across the state.

Gallego met with members of Phoenix-area media to discuss his economic policy plan to rebuild America’s middle class, titled “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream.” The five-pillar plan called for, among other provisions, a tax on data centers and AI, a New Deal-style public service jobs program and raising the minimum wage to $20 per hour, with the goal of building an economy that works for middle-class families.

In Chandler, Gallego joined Chandler High School students for a Latino Leadersconversation about how culture, background and personal experiences can shape a career and become strengths in pursuing future goals. Gallego shared his own journey into public service, lessons from his career and advice for students before taking questions from the students.

Senator Gallego speaks with Chandler High School students

“I love meeting students. It matters to me. I think growing up, and having opportunities to meet people that were in different careers and seeing them was key to me,” Senator Gallego said after the conversation. “That kind of thing helped me understand where my future can be.”

Gallego later joined Frankie Pastor, grandson of former Congressman Ed Pastor, for an “AZ Barrio Stories” conversation focused on the importance of education and expanding opportunities for Arizona students. The discussion highlighted Gallego’s education plan and his priorities for strengthening educational access and outcomes across the state.

Senator Gallego with Dr. Jose Leyba and Frankie Pastor on the set of “AZ Barrio Stories”

title: What They Are Saying: Senator Gallego Unveils his Economic Policy Plan to Rebuild America’s Middle Class
text:
WASHINGTON — Last week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) released his sweeping economic policy plan to rebuild America’s middle class. The five-pillar plan, “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream,” includes a tax on data centers and AI, a New-Deal style public service jobs program, and raising the minimum wage to $20-per-hour to build an economy by-and-for the middle class — not the elites.

Read the full plan HERE.

Since its release, the plan has received praise from advocacy groups, union leaders, and community leaders. The plan has also garnered attention on social media and received coverage from major news outlets.

Here’s what they are saying:

“Senator Gallego’s plan is the kind of bold thinking we need to rebuild the American middle class. Not only does the plan call for improvements to existing policies, such as increases in the minimum wage and overtime, but it also advances transformative reforms like sectoral bargaining that can dramatically boost union membership and coverage. This is a plan to take seriously,” said David Madland, Senior Fellow, Center for American Progress.

“This is one of the most ambitious agendas I’ve seen to reconnect the living standards of working families to overall economic growth. That project requires strong action on many different fronts, which is precisely what this agenda provides,”said Jared Bernstein, former Chairman, United States Council of Economic Advisers.

“Corporate billionaires and CEOs are getting rich off of the backs of their employees while, at the same time, they are trying to silence voices and squelch concerted action and bargaining aimed at improving workplaces. I applaud Senator Gallego for recognizing the vital importance of empowering the working class in order to address economic, racial and social justice gaps that just keep widening. His laudable intention is to help everyday Americans regain appropriate wages and benefits earned through hard work and receive the dignity and respect that they richly deserve. His comprehensive plan aims to re-level the playing field for working families by tackling this current Administration’s elevation of corporate interests above workers’ rights. It rightly promotes collective worker power and workplace democracy, including through sectoral bargaining, which would address income inequality and wage stagnation, raise labor standards for all, and end a corporate competitive race to the bottom that fails to focus on the quality of goods and services provided to the public. Elected officials need to heed the call, as Senator Gallego has, to restore balance and give everyone opportunities to attain the American dream,” said Jennifer Abruzzo, Former General Counsel, National Labor Relations Board.

“Over 12,000 hard working Starbucks Workers United members across 45 states salute Senator Gallego for his innovative commitment to giving workers the tools to better our lives. We strongly agree that a clear path to the middle class starts with a union contract. We know that taking concrete steps to enhance workers rights and triple union density, while supporting a strong industrial policy that creates manufacturing jobs are essential to a broad based recovery. We see the complexity of AI in our worksites and support a stronger voice for workers and communities in regulating tech, data centers, and the growing use of automation that threaten our jobs and community well-being. At Starbucks Workers United, we know that our communities will thrive when all of us can ‘Salir Adelante,’” said Michelle Eisen, Union Leader, Starbucks Workers United.

“AI could be the most disruptive technology of our lifetimes. Right now, decisions about this technology are being made by just a small subset of Silicon Valley CEOs, when they should be made by the American people. Senator Gallego’s AI pillar meets this challenge head-on, by protecting workers directly and empowering their collective bargaining power through their unions. We hear from Americans throughout this country that they want urgent action, and this plan’s comprehensiveness matches the moment,” said Alex Bores, Co-Founder and Board President, Who Decides.

“Every day, CPLC sees how economic insecurity affects families. We welcome Senator Gallego’s focus on quality jobs and pathways to stability, helping more people build secure futures in their communities,” said Alicia Nunez, President and CEO, Chicanos Por La Causa (CPLC).

“At a time when billionaires, CEOs and mega-donors seem to be getting anything they want from the federal government while working families get left behind, it’s refreshing to see Senator Gallego’s plan to strengthen the middle class. Senator Gallego has made working people the core of his plan, recognizing that creating good union jobs is the key to both putting more money in workers’ pockets and enabling them to build better lives for themselves and their families. It’s past time for Congress to get to work on some of these ideas to finally put workers first,” said Claude Cummings, Jr., President, Communications Workers of America (CWA).

“UNITE HERE has been proud to partner with Senator Gallego and strongly endorses his plan to re-create the middle class. Organizing non-union workers is the best way to build worker power in the United States and fight back against the White House’s overreach — driven by ruthless bosses and Wall Street executives trying to undermine democracy and crush unions,” said Gwen Mills, President, UNITE HERE.

“Arizona’s working people are tired of living on edge, struggling to make ends meet while the wealthy elite continue to hoard profits. Higher wages, stronger benefits, protections against the unregulated, untested use of artificial intelligence, and making it easier for workers to join a union are core tenets of our labor movement, and we are pleased to see them reflected in Senator Gallego’s plan to recreate the middle class. We look forward to continuing to work together to build an Arizona where workers can pay bills, buy groceries and gas, afford to see a doctor, and take our family out to a movie once in a while. When working people thrive, Arizona’s communities and economy are stronger,” said Fred Yamashita, Executive Director and Secretary-Treasurer, Arizona AFL-CIO.

“On the heels of the historic win by Banner Health primary care clinicians who just formed the state of Arizona’s first physician and advanced practice practitioner union, we should remember what forming a union is. It is an exercise of every American’s right to come together with their colleagues for shared interests as expressed in the National Labor and Relations Act of 1935. Exercising their right to say enough is enough, and demand that a workplace is a space of collaboration rather than domination in the name of profits guided into the hands of a few. Over time we have seen corporations gain largely unchecked power and leverage to union bust and prevent workers from taking a more active role in their workplaces. What happened at Banner is proof that tides are changing and that change is possible when it is done alongside their local community. Unionizing is a manifestation of the deepest level of care for one’s workplace, rooted in the belief that a better future is possible for all. The UAPD proudly endorses Senator Ruben Gallego’s economic vision to triple union density by 2035 in the state of Arizona,” said Sebastian Gomez, Organizer, Union of American Physicians and Dentists.

“Through my work supporting small businesses and attracting investment from Mexico, I’ve seen what entrepreneurs can accomplish when they have access to capital and the right support. Community lenders like CDFIs, strong cross-border partnerships, and affordable housing for workers and their families all help businesses grow and hire locally. I support Senator Gallego’s focus on expanding opportunities in smaller cities, rural areas, and tribal and border communities. Entrepreneurs should have a real chance to build a successful business in the place they call home,” said Francisca Villegas, Chief of Mexican Direct Investment, City of Tucson.

“In Santa Cruz County, ‘QUEREMOS SALIR ADELANTE.’ We want to see that promise carried across generations. We want our young people to have the opportunity to build meaningful careers and strong families, our working families to achieve stability, and our older generations to know that a lifetime of hard work has led to security and the dignity of being able to retire.

“In workforce development, we have the privilege of helping people take those next steps by connecting job seekers to real employment opportunities and creating pathways through training, apprenticeships, and career development. Helping people find work is important but helping them find opportunities that can lead to long term stability is just as important. We also see another side of our workforce that deserves our attention. We see older workers who have spent 30, 40, or even 50 years in industries like produce and distribution, people who helped build the economy and community we have today, still performing physically demanding work well into their 70s because they simply cannot afford to retire.

“Rebuilding the middle class should mean that hard work leads somewhere. It should mean creating opportunities for the next generation while honoring the generation that came before them. After a lifetime of work, our older generations should be able to retire with dignity without worrying about whether they can afford rent, groceries, health care, and other basic necessities. That is what salir adelante should look like across generations,” said Zaida Bustamante, Executive Director, ARIZONA@WORK Santa Cruz County.

“Sen. Gallego’s middle-class plan recognizes that small businesses must be at the center of our nation’s economic future, including as emerging technologies reshape the way businesses operate and compete. Small entrepreneurs should have the ability to join together and bargain for affordable access to new technologies, helping ensure that innovation expands opportunity rather than deepening the advantages of the largest corporations. This plan also recognizes the importance of strengthening small-business economies beyond superstar cities, including rural, tribal, and border communities that too often bear the costs of trade without seeing enough of its benefits. By expanding access to capital, supporting local entrepreneurship, and ensuring trade policy works for Main Street businesses, we can build an economy where small businesses and their workers have a meaningful opportunity to thrive,”said Lauren Bealore, National Director of Policy & Programs, Main Street Alliance.

“SMART members across the United States work tirelessly to build and move our nation, whether ensuring kids breathe quality air in schools or transporting people and freight. In return, we don’t ask for much — the ability to provide for our families, stay healthy, and live a life with dignity. But for too long, our economy hasn’t worked for people who actually work for a living. And from coast to coast, Americans are demanding change.

“Senator Ruben Gallego’s Middle Class Plan recognizes that we aren’t asking for handouts. We’re asking for a system that rewards workers, not corporate elites. We’re asking for a fair shot. That’s what SMART fights for every day, and it’s what every working person in this country deserves. We will continue that fight on behalf of SMART members and working Americans nationwide, and we urge all elected leaders to join us in fighting for an economy that works for all of us,” said the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART Union).

“This agenda charts new American trade policies that benefit U.S. workers and producers, build fairer markets, deconcentrate political power, and strengthen our resilience and national security. It recognizes what’s at stake — we cannot have well-paid jobs, thriving Main Street businesses, safe and affordable medicine and food, green energy and transportation, or productive investment over financialization, unless we replace both the neoliberal NAFTA-WTO agenda and Trump’s Oligarch First tariff corruption,” said Lori Wallach, Director, Rethink Trade.

“Communities like San Luis have tremendous potential, but we need the tools and investment to turn that potential into long-term economic opportunity. Our focus is on helping small businesses and entrepreneurs grow, expanding access to capital, strengthening our infrastructure, and leveraging our position along the U.S.-Mexico border to attract manufacturing, food processing, logistics, and other quality job-creating industries. I appreciate that Senator Gallego’s plan recognizes the unique needs of rural and border communities and the importance of making sure federal economic development resources reach communities like ours,” said Armando Esparaza, Economic Development Director, City of San Luis.

“Americans are facing difficult financial decisions everyday and Senator Gallego understands that more than most. Senator Gallego’s plan to ease Americans financial burdens is multi faceted and we are glad to see a core pillar of the plan is to increase the percentage of workers that are members of a union. It has been proven numerous times union members earn higher wages and better benefits which gives working families the ability to live the American dream and not paycheck to paycheck,” said Jason Sangster, Business Manager, Ironworkers (IW) Local 75.

See what people had to say about Senator Gallego’s middle class plan on social media:

“Sen. Ruben Gallego breaks down his new economic plan.”

See additional coverage below of Senator Gallego’s middle class plan:

NBC News: Sen. Ruben Gallego rolls out an economic agenda as he weighs a 2028 White House bid[Scott Wong, 10/7/2026]

Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., who is eyeing a possible presidential bid in 2028, rolled out a new, national economic plan Wednesday that calls for boosting the minimum wage to $20 per hour and a New Deal-style public service jobs program funded by taxes on artificial intelligence companies and unpopular data centers.

“There’s a lot of changes that are coming because of AI that we’re not prepared for. There’s been a lot of bad things that have been happening for the middle class for the last 40 years that we have not really changed, either. And that’s why I think you have this real anxiety out there that working America feels,” Gallego said in an interview Tuesday.

“I always felt like, you know, if I put 40 hours’ worth of honest work together, I would have enough to support my family, and then feel comfortable enough to go to a movie,” he continued. “That’s not happening anymore, and so that’s the most important focus of this plan.”

The Washington Post: Ruben Gallego, weighing a presidential run, debuts a new economic plan[Theodoric Meyer, 10/7/2026]

In an interview, Gallego said he is putting out the plan to help shape his party’s agenda if Democrats retake the Senate next month in the midterm elections. But he acknowledged that it also lays out some of the policies he would champion if he runs for president.

“We want to make sure people kind of have a viewpoint of where my position is, where my heart is when it comes to where working-class America is,” Gallego said.

Gallego’s plan involves dozens of ideas, including raising the federal minimum wage to $20 an hour by 2030, requiring employers pay twice a worker’s usual wage for overtime work instead of time-and-a-half, mandating that companies offer paid sick leave and vacation and steps to strengthen unions.

Semafor: Gallego rolls out ambitious plan to insulate workers against AI[Burgess Everett, 10/7/2026]

“People that are working right now don’t feel like their hard work is actually bringing them anything in return … and going into election season, people want to know where Democrats stand,” Gallego told Semafor in an interview this week.

Gallego said he’s ready to maximize Democratic authority to get it done. He proposed putting as much of his proposal as he can in a party-line budget reconciliation bill that Democrats can pass with a simple majority if they control the House, Senate, and White House come 2029.

Bloomberg: Senate Democrat Gallego Floats AI Tax to Fund Economic Jobs Plan[Chris Cioffi, 10/7/2026]

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.)’s New Deal-style plan would boost the minimum wage to $20 per hour from $7.25, provide public jobs for workers displaced by AI, and steer trade policy away from what he called the “reckless” policies under President Donald Trump. Funded by the new taxes on the sector, Gallego said his plan would bring stability to middle-income American workers, who are struggling to navigate nascent AI-caused workforce disruptions.

Gallego’s plan would be funded by a so-called “robot” tax to discourage job dislocation and maintain company payroll contributions for jobs that have been outsourced to AI. It also calls for imposing a 10% data center excise tax while taking away bonus depreciation and deductions for state and local taxes.

POLITICO, Decoded Newsletter: Inside AI safety’s hottest club[Christine Mui, Sam Sutton, Brendan Bordelon, and Calder McHugh, 10/7/2026]

GALLEGO POLICY GLIMPSE — Potential 2028 hopeful Sen. Ruben Gallego jumped on the phone with Decoded to preview the new economic blueprint he’ll roll out later this morning that would create a New Deal-style public service jobs program funded by new taxes on large AI companies, data centers and tokens.

Why it matters: The economy of Gallego’s home state has benefitted substantially from a recent acceleration in chips manufacturing, which has been supercharged by the AI boom. And while the senator’s playbook nods at the technology’s upside — giving a special shoutout to the Nvidia Blackwell chips that are produced in Arizona — he also writes that “we must slow AI development and regulate it.”

title: Gillibrand Calls For Legislation To Improve Social Security Benefits Following Announcement Of 2027 COLA
text:
80% of Social Security Recipients Say Similar COLA Would Not Adequately Compensate For Rising Cost Of Living

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) called for passage of her legislation to strengthen Social Security benefits following the release of the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA). The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced this morning that Social Security benefits will increase by 3.6% in 2027.

“Our seniors have spent a lifetime of hard work paying into Social Security, but their checks simply aren’t keeping up with rising costs,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This year’s cost-of-living adjustment is not enough to make up for skyrocketing costs for groceries, gas, heating, and healthcare in President Trump’s America. As the top Democrat on the Senate Aging Committee, I’m fighting to pass the Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act to protect and expand Social Security benefits long-term by changing the formula used to calculate COLAs to better account for the expenses that seniors face.”

The 3.6% COLA comes as rising costs are making it harder for American seniors to make ends meet. Already, New Yorkers have paid over $5,500 more due to President Trump’s reckless policies. In September alone, inflation rose to 3.7%.

The 2027 COLA will amount to an increase of about $75 per month. 80 percent of current Social Security recipients say a similar increase would not adequately compensate for the rising cost of living.

Senator Gillibrand’s Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act—which was introduced last year—would direct SSA to adjust benefits based on the Consumer Price Index for Americans aged 62 or older (CPI-E), rather than the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners (CPI-W). The CPI-E more accurately accounts for the actual costs incurred by older Americans, such as medical expenses and prescription drug costs—making it a more reflective index to use when calculating benefits.

Additionally, this week, Senator Gillibrand sent a letter to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics urging the administration to improve data collection for the CPI-E. This letter follows the Trump administration’s attempt to cut funding to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in Fiscal Year 2027, as well as reports that staffing cuts at BLS have already eroded the reliability of economic data.

The text of the Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act can be found here. Senator Gillibrand’s letter to the Bureau of Labor Statistics can be found here.

In addition to the Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act, Senator Gillibrand has proposed multiple pieces of legislation to help ensure that seniors can continue to get the full benefits they are owed and to reverse disastrous Trump administration cuts to SSA:

The Social Security Expansion Act would extend the solvency of Social Security for 75 years by requiring the wealthiest American households to pay their fair share of payroll taxes. Under the current formula, a CEO making $20 million a year pays the same amount into Social Security as individuals making $184,500 a year. This legislation would lift the cap on Social Security, requiring income above $250,000 to be subject to the Social Security payroll tax and thus increasing the amount paid into the Social Security trust fund to increase its longevity.

The Keep Billionaires Out of Social Security Act would reverse Trump administration cuts to SSA, prohibit unnecessary Social Security field office closures, boost staffing levels to help reduce wait times and make it easier for seniors and people with disabilities to get help over the phone, protect Americans’ data, and provide the resources SSA needs to help approve earned benefits quickly.

title: Grassley Hosts Seventh Federal Judiciary Youth Summit
text:
POLK COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today welcomed students and educators from 11 central Iowa high schools to his seventh Federal Judiciary Youth Summit held in Des Moines.

The summit provides students the opportunity to get first-hand insights into the judicial branch of government and is part of Grassley’s longtime effort to foster civic participation and understanding of government among the next generation. This year, Grassley was joined by U.S. District Judge Rebecca Ebinger and U.S. Attorney David Waterman. Grassley recommended both Ebinger and Waterman to serve in the Southern District of Iowa and supported their nominations through the U.S. Senate.

During the question-and-answer session, Grassley answered students’ questions on his professional background and his personal mentors, as well as his advice for overcoming challenges and establishing a work-life balance.

“I greatly appreciated meeting with students and educators today to discuss the federal judicial system, a branch of government that’s essential to our system of checks and balances,” Grassley said. “I always enjoy hearing from Iowa’s next generation and I hope this experience fuels their interest in civic engagement for years to come. Thank you to everyone who took time out of their day to attend, and thank you to Judge Ebinger and Mr. Waterman for sharing their experiences and working tirelessly to secure justice for Iowans.”

“I’m a government civics teacher and I think today’s event was a wonderful opportunity and glimpse into how our U.S. government works … I think [Senator Grassley] is the essence of what this country stands for because he’s meeting the people who he represents, and I think that if every politician did what he did we would have a much better system of government and the foundations and principles that we stand for. Now I believe and I’m more encouraged by people like Senator Grassley.” – J.W. Reed Christian Academy Teacher

“The Youth Summit was amazing. It was very informational and inspiring. I just really like how [the speakers] showed how they cared about us and that they wanted to hear our voices and that are voices mattered.” – J.W. Reed Christian Academy Student

“I really liked [the summit]. I was very intrigued and very interested to hear what [the speakers] had to say. It gave a lot of insight about just government in general, but also, about how the state works and how the districts actually come together and work together ... I’m very thankful for the Youth Summit seminar. Very insightful.” – J.W. Reed Christian Academy Student

Grassley with attendees from J.W. Reed Christian Academy

Download photos from Grassley’s Federal Judiciary Youth Summit HERE.

Background:

As chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, Grassley is responsible for vetting and processing nominees for lifetime appointments to the federal bench. Under Grassley’s leadership, the committee has advanced 60 federal judges so far this Congress, 57 of whom have already been confirmed by the Senate, marking the fastest pace since the Reagan administration. He has successfully confirmed over 100 district judges throughout his tenure as Judiciary Chairman.

SIGNED INTO LAW: Hassan-Ernst Bill to Expose Government Waste
text:
WASHINGTON – Bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan and Joni Ernst (R-IA) to increase government transparency was recently signed into law. The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act requires disclosure of any government project that is $1 billion over budget or five years behind schedule.

“Granite Staters deserve to know that their hard-earned tax-dollars are being spent responsibly,” said Senator Hassan. “This commonsense, bipartisan bill will give the public greater visibility into how their tax dollars are being used and it will help Congress identify wasteful spending. I am pleased to see this bill signed into law and I will continue working with my colleagues of both parties to protect taxpayer dollars and increase government transparency.”

This legislation is part of Senator Hassan’s ongoing efforts to save taxpayer dollars and cut waste, fraud, and abuse in the federal government. Her bipartisan bill, the Stop Secret Spending Act, which would require billions of dollars in previously undisclosed federal spending to be made public on USAspending.gov., was recently signed into law.

In her role as Ranking Member of the Joint Economic Committee, Senator Hassan has led several bipartisan hearings focused on ways to improve government efficiency. Earlier this year, Senator Hassan helped pass into law a bipartisan bill that helps prevent payments from being unintentionally sent to individuals who have died. Last year, the Senator’s Government Service Delivery Improvement Act – which improves the ways in which federal agencies deliver services, including health benefits and student loan programs, to the public – passed into law. Senator Hassan also helped pass into law the Grant Transparency Act to bring more transparency into federal agencies' competitive grant selection process.

title: Heinrich Meets with New Mexicans to Discuss How Landmark Bipartisan Legislation Will Lower Costs, Create Jobs, & Hold Data Centers Accountable
text:
PHOTOS

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. — This week, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, met with New Mexicans to discuss his newly introduced Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, legislation that will lower utility bills, create good-paying jobs, and force data centers to fully pay for their grid upgrades, as well as their share of the existing grid — resulting in savings for New Mexico families.

Heinrich hosted a roundtable discussion with members of UA Local 412, LiUNA Local 16, Painters and Allied Trades District Council 36, and New Mexico Building and Construction Trades Council to underscore how his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will create more high-quality jobs New Mexicans can build their families around, lower electricity bills, and require data centers to fully pay for the costs they create.

PHOTO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) Meets with New Mexicans to Discuss His Landmark Legislation to Create More Jobs, Lower Electricity Bills, and Require Data Centers to Fully Pay for Costs They Create, October 12, 2026.

“We want to build the jobs in New Mexico that you can build a family around, and that's what unions are all about. That's the way I grew up with my dad,” said Heinrich. “My Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is going to generate benefits for our skilled workers in the state of New Mexico for a very long time to come. This bill is about building the infrastructure and manufacturing capacity we need with union labor for the future of our country — and making sure that those jobs are right here in New Mexico.”

Heinrich hosted a second roundtable discussion with Pattern Energy, Grid United, Black Forest Partners, RioSol New Mexico, and NM Renewable Energy Industries Association to highlight how his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will bring more energy projects online faster and lower utility bills for New Mexico families by speeding up the federal process for reviewing and approving energy projects. Right now, 83% of energy projects stuck in the interconnection queue are clean energy projects.

Heinrich’s legislation will get those projects up and running to address rising demand, while creating greater certainty for energy projects approved and financed across presidential administrations by prohibiting any administration from improperly delaying or blocking clean energy projects without facing legal action or fines.

PHOTO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) Hosts a Roundtable with Clean Energy Companies on How His Landmark Legislation Will Bring More Energy Projects Online Faster and Lower Utility Bills for New Mexico Families, October 12, 2026.

“Our whole premise as we approached this permitting bill was: How do we create a faster process, not lower the bar on standards,” said Heinrich. “My Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help us create more certainty and predictability for projects permitted and financed across administrations – so that energy companies can get projects from idea to go, faster. That means more clean energy projects can get off the ground, more good-paying jobs, and more investments in New Mexico communities.”

Additionally, Heinrich joined a roundtable discussion hosted by ABB and the National Association of Manufacturers to highlight how his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will create more jobs and spark a manufacturing renaissance in New Mexico and nationwide by creating a construction boom and increasing demand for American-made machinery and equipment.

PHOTO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) Meets with Manufacturers to Discuss His Landmark Legislation that Will Create More Jobs and Spark a Manufacturing Renaissance in New Mexico, October 12, 2026.

“We need permitting reform to put more electrons on the grid. It results in more jobs, and it's the one thing that can bring down the pressure on the cost of electricity and energy right now,” said Heinrich. “The folks at ABB make the components that really build out the grid across the country, and so they're supplying the individual components that connect from the grid, through the utility, to the neighborhood. The more of these projects move forward, the more demand there is for the things that they manufacture right here in Albuquerque, New Mexico.”

title: Hickenlooper, Murkowski, King Make Bipartisan Push to Protect Integrity of Satellite Weather Data
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper, Lisa Murkowski, and Angus King sent a bipartisan letter urging the Department of Defense (DoD) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to prioritize the integrity of satellite weather data as the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) approaches end of service.

“For decades, DMSP’s Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) has supported hurricane forecasting, severe-weather monitoring, polar and sea-ice analysis, and military operations in data-sparse and denied environments. That coverage is now shrinking as legacy polar-orbiting microwave sensors age out. ” wrote the senators. “To improve and prevent degradation of numerical weather prediction and tactical forecasting, the DoD and NOAA should evaluate the transition across the broader space architecture, including commercial satellite systems that can complement government capabilities.”

Weather forecasters, researchers, and military planners have used data from DMSP satellites for decades to predict and monitor other extreme weather patterns. Last month, the U.S. Space Force announced they would maintain the DMSP fleet until at least 2028 until it transitions to a new replacement architecture.

The senators concluded: “Weather data continuity is essential to national security, public safety, and economic resilience. Extending DMSP is a promising step, and we urge the DoD and NOAA to proactively identify and fill anticipated gaps before legacy degradation or replacement delays create preventable risks.”

Last year, the DoD reversed its decision to stop sharing DMSP data with NOAA and the scientific community after Hickenlooper and Murkowski urged DoD and NOAA to reconsider and address the implications canceling DMSP would have on weather forecasting and scientific research, especially in polar regions. Congress extended DMSP operations in the FY26 National Defense Authorization Act and a Hickenlooper-led amendment to the bill ensured the continuity of data sharing for the duration of the DMSP mission.

“With increasing national attention on changes in the Arctic, including Greenland, and the associated economic, geopolitical, and strategic implications, it is critical that we maintain our ability to monitor and understand conditions on the ground,” said Mark Serreze, Distinguished Professor of Geography and Director of the National Snow and Ice Data Center in the Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences at the University of Colorado Boulder. “The DMSP satellites have been a key asset in this regard for decades. Colorado is a national leader in scientific research of the polar regions and we applaud the efforts of Senator Hickenlooper to raise attention to this important matter.”

title: Hoeven: UND to Assess Technology for Department of War Counter-Drone Task Force
text:
GRAND FORKS, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today marked the start of a formal partnership between the University of North Dakota (UND) and the U.S. Department of War’s (DoW) Joint Inter Agency Task Force (JIATF) 401. With support from the Northern Plains UAS Test Site, UND will assess counter-drone technology on behalf of JIATF 401, the agency responsible for coordinating counter-drone defense development across the entire DoW. Specifically, under the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) that was signed today:

JIATF 401 has entered into a first of its kind agreement with UND, giving the university a central role in its counter-drone efforts.

The task force will share objectives and technical standards with UND, helping to guide the university’s research and testing.

UND will serve as the task force’s clearinghouse, identifying promising counter-UAS technologies that warrant further evaluation and development, while sorting out technologies that fall short of the DoW’s needs.

Hoeven has been working with UND and JIATF 401, including Task Force Director Brig. Gen. Matthew Ross, to advance the agreement. To this end, the senator has met repeatedly with BG Ross, both in North Dakota and Washington, D.C., to move this initiative forward:

Hoeven convened a meeting in his office in November 2025 with senior DoW officials, including BG Ross, where the senator made the case for leveraging North Dakota’s UAS ecosystem to meet warfighter needs.

This meeting resulted in the Technology Readiness Experimentation (T-REX) event that was held at Camp Grafton earlier this year.

T-REX was a two-week event that Hoeven worked to organize with JIATF 401 and the North Dakota National Guard, which allowed DoW officials to evaluate promising counter-drone technologies.

In July, Hoeven followed up on these efforts during a meeting with BG Ross with the goal of formalizing the relationship between UND and JIATF 401.

These meetings helped make clear the support that UND could provide to JIATF 401’s counter-drone work and led to the MOU being finalized today.

“Small drones have changed warfare, a fact we’ve seen clearly in Ukraine, the Middle East and even over our own military bases. JIATF 401 was founded specifically to address this new threat and leads the effort to develop and deploy counter-drone technology across the entire Department of War. Now, UND will serve as the clearinghouse for this task force, leveraging the expertise of its researchers and the capabilities of the Northern Plains UAS Test Site to assess technologies that can be used to detect, protect against and neutralize threats from unmanned aircraft,” said Hoeven. “I appreciate General Ross for recognizing the potential of this partnership and for working with me to make it a reality. Between Project ATLAS, which we announced yesterday, and the MOU signed today, it is clear to anyone who wants to develop drone and counter-drone technology, North Dakota is the place to be.”

title: Husted joins bill to disrupt cartel operations, prevent flow of deadly drugs into the U.S.
text:
“Strengthening southbound inspections will help disrupt cartel operations, keep illegal firearms out of their hands and reduce the flow of fentanyl and other deadly drugs into our communities.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) joined Sens. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) and James Lankford’s (R-Okla.) bipartisan Enhancing Southbound Inspections to Combat Cartels Act. This bill would increase inspections of traffic going from the U.S. to Mexico, which would help combat the flow of illicit firearms and money that fuel drug cartels.

“As we continue working to secure our southern border, we also need to cut off the weapons and funding that allow drug cartels to operate. Strengthening southbound inspections will help disrupt cartel operations, keep illegal firearms out of their hands and reduce the flow of fentanyl and other deadly drugs into our communities. I will continue supporting commonsense efforts to secure our border and keep Americans safe,” said Husted.

“Dismantling drug cartels requires cutting off the flow of illegal firearms and cartel money moving from the U.S. into Mexico, which help give cartels the resources to continue to operate and flood our communities with deadly drugs. This bipartisan legislation significantly enhances our southbound inspection capabilities, which will help disrupt cartel operations and reduce the trafficking of fentanyl, which has devastated communities across New Hampshire and nationwide,” said Hassan.

“With border crossings at a record low, the results speak for themselves. President Trump’s leadership is making America safer; the southern border is much more secure than it was a year ago. But US Customs and Border Protection still doesn’t have the resources they need to stop gun smuggling to the criminal cartels in Mexico. We need to ensure border law enforcement has the personnel and technology to crack down on criminal activity that puts Americans at risk,” said Lankford.

The Enhancing Southbound Inspections to Combat Cartels Act would:

Require that at least 10% of southbound vehicles are inspected, to the extent practicable.

Authorize at least 100 additional Homeland Security Investigations agents to investigate the smuggling of guns and money from the U.S. into Mexico.

Authorize at least 100 additional Homeland Security Investigations agents to investigate drug smuggling, human trafficking, child trafficking and unauthorized entries from Mexico into the U.S.

Authorize 50 additional x-ray inspection systems for southbound inspections.

This bill builds on Husted’s work to stop the flow of fentanyl into American communities. Husted supported the HALT Fentanyl Act, which was signed into law by President Trump. This law makes the temporary class-wide scheduling order for fentanyl-related substances permanent, closing a dangerous loophole that drug traffickers continue to exploit.

Sens. Markey, Warren, Reps. McGovern, Trahan Demand FAA, Amazon Study Impacts of Amazon’s Westborough, Mass. Drone Program Before Launching Drone Delivery
text:
Lawmakers argue the FAA and Amazon are bypassing crucial, site-specific environmental review process, limiting local input

Letter to the FAA (PDF) | Letter to Amazon (PDF)

Washington (October 14, 2026) - Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Representatives Jim McGovern (MA-02) and Lori Trahan (MA-03) today wrote to Bryan Bedford, Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and Andy Jassy, Chief Executive Officer of Amazon, urging Amazon to work with the FAA to conduct an Environmental Assessment of its proposed drone delivery facility in Westborough, Massachusetts, before launching operations there. Communities have raised concerns about the Amazon Prime Air drone delivery program’s impact on the environment and residents’ quality-of-life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy.

In the letters, the lawmakers wrote, “Despite the noise and environmental risks of Amazon’s drone operations, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has authorized operators such as Amazon to deploy their fleets without completing a site-specific Environmental Assessment (EA) of their impact on the surrounding communities. This decision is especially problematic in Massachusetts localities, given the differences between it and previously studied communities, local opposition, and the inadequate treatment of the risks associated with transporting hazardous-materials.”

The lawmakers continued, “An independent resident survey, with more than 1,200 responses as of early October 2026, found 92 percent of respondents opposed the proposed Westborough facility. At a state level, Massachusetts is one of 15 states currently suing the FAA for its nationwide FONSI. In other words, Amazon is now trying to quickly move drone operations into Massachusetts under a streamlined regulatory process the state itself is challenging. These are precisely the community-specific noise, safety, and quality-of-life concerns a site-specific EA and comment period exist to surface and address.”

The lawmakers urged, “These concerns — applying the FONSI to a community different from those previously assessed by the FAA, significant local opposition, and the limited evaluation of hazardous material risks — warrant requiring Amazon to complete a site-specific EA, with a public comment period, before the FAA authorizes Prime Air operations in Massachusetts.”

title: In Aftermath of Isaias, Senator Moody Calls for Increase in Total Allocation for Florida National Guard to Better Protect Floridians
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—In the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias making landfall in Florida last week, Senator Ashley Moody is leading efforts to increase the total allocation for the Florida National Guard. Guardsmen play a vital role in protecting Floridians, including in the aftermath of storms where they help rescue and recovery efforts. Although the population in Florida has risen dramatically over the past several years, the size of the Florida National Guard has remained stagnant. Senator Moody is calling on the Department of War to increase National Guard personnel to continue to effectively serve Floridians whenever they are called upon.

“In the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, we saw once again just how critical the Florida National Guard is to keeping our communities safe—but while Florida’s population has grown in recent years, the size of our National Guard has not kept pace.That’s why I’m leading an effort to increase the number of Guardsmen allocated to our state. Florida’s National Guard is always there when we need them. We need to make sure they have the personnel and resources to continue answering the call,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Moody is joined by U.S. Representatives Aaron Bean, Gus Bilirakis, Vern Buchanan, Mario Diaz-Balart, Dr. Neal Dunn, Randy Fine, Scott Franklin, Carlos Gimenez, Mike Haridopolos, Laurel Lee, Cory Mills, Jimmy Patronis, and John Rutherford in the effort.

Read full letter here.

Ahead of Isaias, Senator Moody joined Governor Ron DeSantis to discuss preparedness efforts, including the mobilization of thousands of National Guard members. After the storm, Senator Moody and Governor DeSantis conducted an on-the-ground assessment of some of the damage and thanked Guard members for their response efforts.

Approximately 5,000 Florida National Guard soldiers and airmen were activated to respond to Hurricane Isaias. Guard members conducted route clearance, reconnaissance, humanitarian assistance, flood mitigation and search-and-rescue operations.

Eight Florida National Guard members rescued a family during the Hurricane Isaias response. The soldiers worked together to rescue four family members from a sinking pickup truck beside an Interstate 10 off-ramp.

title: At WSU in Pullman, Murray Launches Public Health for America Working Group, Delivers Address to Chart What Comes Next After Trump & RFK Jr., and Discusses Key Public Health Challenges with Local Leaders and Experts
text:
READ MORE: Senator Murray announces members of new public health initiative

NYT: A Public Health-Minded Senator Asks: What Comes After Trump and Kennedy?

***LIVESTREAM OF DISCUSSION FROM KHQ HERE***

***PHOTOS OF EVENT HERE***

Pullman, WA — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, formally launched the Public Health for America Working Group. Senator Murray delivered a speech outlining the mission of the working group and then was joined by WSU faculty and state and local public health officials for a panel discussion on the working group’s goals and the future of public health in Washington state and across the country.

Murray’s working group will seek to develop the ideas, safeguards, and legislation needed to restore trust in public health and build a stronger, public health system that is more resilient to political attacks. It follows nearly two years of unprecedented attacks by President Trump and Secretary Kennedy on the agencies, scientists, and institutions that keep Americans safe and healthy.

“I’ve worked with health secretaries under five presidents. Republicans and Democrats. People I agreed with and people I disagreed with. But at the end of the day, every one of them understood that their job was to protect the health of the American people. They listened to the scientists. They trusted the experts. And when a crisis hit, we could pick up the phone and work together. I have never seen anything like what we’re seeing now. The genuine malice toward experts. The sheer hostility towards science. None of that is a policy disagreement. It’s a complete break from how every administration before this one—of either party—has approached the job. I’m not going to mince words here: Trump and RFK Jr. have put our public health system on life support. Trust among the public is in free fall. Our nation has simply never been more unprepared for serious public health threats,” said Senator Murray. “All of us who care about the future of public health need to come to grips with a hard reality: If we had a healthy public health system—it would not have been so easy to snap in half. Instead, the system we had before was already underfunded, already stretched thin, and already far too vulnerable to politics. If we are going to meet this moment, we have to build something stronger. And we have to start by rebuilding trust.”

“The charge of my working group is simple. First, we need to repair the trust that has been shattered. And second, we need to reinforce it against future political attacks. We have to build something that can’t be broken the next time someone decides science is inconvenient. Public health policy can’t become a political football that shifts every four years based on political ideology. It has to be reliably grounded in science and facts,” Senator Murray continued. “I’ll tell you: I’ve passed more bipartisan health policy into law than nearly all of my colleagues in Congress. And I’ve done it by understanding you can’t reach a deal without trust—it’s the foundation of every deal I’ve ever brokered. You build trust by listening to people’s concerns, understanding their perspectives, and answering their questions honestly—even when that means saying you don’t know the answer yet…But we know that when it comes, we need a public health system that is already trusted, and already prepared. Not one that is warped by politics and distracted by conspiracies. Families are counting on us to keep them safe. I know—because I’ve been that mother worried about the pesticides being sprayed near my kids. I’ve been that teacher worried about outbreaks spreading in my classroom. Every one of those times—I knew I could trust what CDC told me. I want every family in this country to have that again.”

Since taking office, President Trump and Secretary Kennedy have taken unprecedented steps to politicize public health agencies, overrule experts, promote misinformation, and undermine trust in the nation’s public health infrastructure.

Secretary Kennedy has fired thousands of federal public health experts—including all 17 members of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) and a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Director for refusing to rubberstamp his anti-vaccine views before reviewing the scientific evidence. Under Secretary Kennedy, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has halted promising research, taken down data for deadly diseases, refused to accurately report measles deaths, promoted false anti-vaccine information, and more. These steps have severely undermined public trust—with polls showing trust in CDC recommendations dropping from 77% to 50% over Trump’s first year in office this term.

The mission of Murray’s working group is not simply to restore what existed before January 2025, but to design a public health system that is stronger, more resilient, and structurally protected from political interference—no matter who holds the White House or controls Congress. The working group will convene roundtables with researchers, providers, state, local, and Tribal health officials, and former career federal scientists; host public conversations on the future of public health; engage directly with communities and trusted messengers; and respond in real time as key public health decisions unfold. Its findings will inform nonpartisan, evidence-based policy proposals as Murray works to build consensus around legislation to rebuild public health in America stronger and more resilient than ever before.

Senator Murray has a long record as a leader on public health, including; pushing for permanent funding for public health infrastructure; serving on the Center for Strategic and International Studies’ Commission on Strengthening America’s Health Security; and serving as the top Democrat on the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee for several years—including during the COVID-19 pandemic. She has negotiated and passed key public health legislation like the American Rescue Plan; PREVENT Pandemics Act; the SUPPORT Act which helped address the opioids crisis; the 21st Century Cures Act; and bills reauthorizing key Food and Drug Administration (FDA) programs and pandemic preparedness programs.

More information on the Public Health for America Working Group is available HERE.

Senator Murray’s remarks, as delivered, are below:

“Public health is maybe not the hottest topic in politics or on social media—but the students here know how much it actually matters.

“Quick show of hands: how many of you had to learn through a screen during middle or high school?

“Exactly—that’s why today’s conversation matters.

“In public health, we say an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. That’s not just true of disease—it’s also true of corruption, incompetence, and political interference. Unfortunately, it is painfully clear right now that these are threats our public health system was simply not equipped to prevent.

“Curing them is going to take some serious work. That’s why I’m here today.

“Under President Trump and RFK Jr., we’ve seen an outbreak of corruption, chaos, and political interference ripping through our public health system. I’m not going to stand up here and list every single thing Secretary Kennedy has done to our public health system. We’d be here all afternoon—and frankly, I want to leave time to talk about how we fix it.

“But I do want to be straight with you about the damage. Because it is real, it is serious, and pretending otherwise doesn’t help anyone.

“I’ve worked with health secretaries under five presidents—Republicans and Democrats. People I agreed with, and people I disagreed with. But at the end of the day, every one of them understood that their job was to protect the health of the American people.

“They listened to the scientists. They trusted the experts. And when a crisis hit, we could pick up the phone and work together.

“I have never seen anything like what we’re seeing now. The genuine malice toward experts, the sheer hostility toward science—none of that is a policy disagreement. It’s a complete break from how every administration before this one—of either party—has approached the job.

“I’m not going to mince words here: Trump and RFK Jr. have put our public health system on life support. Trust among the public is in free fall. Our nation has simply never been more unprepared for serious public health threats.

“Losing experts and staff across our health agencies, funding being illegally withheld—that’s bad enough. But we’re also dealing with a whole lot of disinformation coming at us online, often incentivized by some kind of profit-making scheme.

“How many of you have come across health advice on TikTok or Instagram in the last few days? How many of you were certain that information was absolutely correct? If you needed public health advice, where would you look for it? Would you ask your doctor? Talk to your parents? Would you check the CDC website? Would you ask AI?

“This is one of the big challenges we’ve got to grapple with, too. This isn’t about the sanctity of science or how experts are treated. At the end of the day, this is about our families.

“When a daycare needs help fighting a measles outbreak—that is public health. When a hospital is looking for recommendations to reduce maternal mortality—that is public health. When the library has concerns about its drinking water, when the rec-league has concerns about wildfire smoke, when the cafeteria has concerns about contaminated lettuce—raise your hand if you want to make sure our lettuce doesn’t give people life-threatening explosive diarrhea? That’s what I thought; me too—all of that is public health, and it is just the start.

“At the end of the day—public health is about public safety. We have to remember that. When our loudest public health megaphone becomes an echo chamber for conspiracies, that is a lot bigger than a political problem—it is a life and death problem.

“Not every national security threat is about war or AI. We cannot fully protect the American people if we just buy more bombs and leave public health in the dust.

“COVID taught us all this lesson very painfully, and it is outrageous to see this Administration trying to rewrite that history and erase the lessons we should be learning from—even as the world just nervously watched a potential outbreak in Russia.

“How are we supposed to be prepared for the next public health threat when it seems like our Health Secretary is more likely to cover up a measles outbreak than admit vaccines don’t cause autism?

“However, I want to be clear—as bad as things are right now, I’m not here to throw up my hands and just say how awful everything is. I’m here to roll up my sleeves and get to work on how we fix it.

“I believe with a dose of the right medicine—some hard work, some common sense, and serious accountability for RFK Jr. and Trump. We can break this fever. We can save our public health system.

“Think of how rapidly public health has deteriorated under RFK’s leadership— it stands to reason that we could build it back pretty quickly, too.

“But, after we do that, things cannot just go back to business as usual. All of us who care about the future of public health need to come to grips with a hard reality: if we had a healthy public health system, it would not have been so easy to snap in half.

“Instead, the system we had before was already underfunded, already stretched thin, and already far too vulnerable to politics. If we are going to meet this moment, we have to build something stronger—and we have to start by rebuilding trust.

“Which is why I decided to turn to some people I trust for help: Patty Hayes, Dr. Joshua Sharfstein, Dr. Jeffery Levi, Dr. Helen Chu, and Dr. Vin Gupta. This is a group of nonpartisan experts, dedicated to public health and public service, with experience managing the COVID response in King County and Seattle, conducting medical research on vaccines, and making science-based decisions at agencies like the FDA, the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, and the Office of National AIDS Policy.

“I’m incredibly excited and grateful to have these individuals joining me to launch the Public Health for America Working Group. I’m especially glad to be having one of our first events here at my alma mater, WSU, and to be joined by some incredibly knowledgeable local public health experts to discuss the challenges we face.

“The charge of my working group is simple. First, we need to repair the trust that has been shattered. Second, we need to reinforce it against future political attacks.

“We have to build something that can’t be broken the next time someone decides science is inconvenient. Public health policy can’t become a political football that shifts every four years based on political ideology. It has to be reliably grounded in science and facts.

“Sounds great, right? But how do we do it? I have ideas already: I believe we ought to limit the number of political appointees at our health agencies like CDC. I know we need more stable and consistent funding for our state and local health agencies, but there’s another dimension to this outside of policy—trust.

“I’ve passed more bipartisan health policy into law than nearly all of my colleagues in Congress—and I’ve done it by understanding you can’t reach a deal without trust. It’s the foundation of every deal I’ve ever brokered. You build trust by listening to people’s concerns, understanding their perspectives, and answering their questions honestly—even when that means saying you don’t know the answer yet.

“I am sincerely determined to talk to anyone and everyone about what comes next to rebuild public health in America. Then, out of those conversations, we will build trust, and we will bring back new ideas for legislation that will help build a stronger public health system.

“I started today by saying an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. That’s what this working group is about—it’s a tall order, but Congress needs to deliver on this. Not just repairing the damage but making sure it can never happen this easily again.

“As smart as the members of this Working Group are, none of us know what the next public health threat will be. A measles outbreak worse than what we’re facing today? Anti-microbial resistance? Tick-borne diseases? There are so many possibilities. But we know that when it comes, we need a public health system that is already trusted and already prepared—not one that is warped by politics and distracted by conspiracies.

“Families are counting on us to keep them safe. I know because I’ve been that mother worried about the pesticides being sprayed near my kids. I’ve been that teacher worried about outbreaks spreading in my classroom.

“Every one of those times, I knew I could trust what CDC told me. I want every family in this country to have that again.

“To the students here today: this is your fight too. The public health system we build is the one you’ll inherit, and the one you’ll run. So, if you’ve got ideas—if anyone has thoughts they want to share—go ahead and email me at publichealth@murray.senate.gov.

“So, with that, it’s great to be here at WSU. This university trains the people who staff our public health system, and its research helps keep families safe far beyond Pullman. I’m excited to have a discussion with some great public health leaders about what comes next.”
