title: Murray, Baldwin Call on Education Department to Abandon its Latest Tactic to Cut Grant Funding to Communities
text:
By significantly increasing the “frontloading” of grants, the Trump admin is preventing over $600 million from reaching schools and students this year

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Ranking Member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, sent a letter to Department of Education Secretary Linda McMahon calling on her to reverse the department’s significantly expanded use of “frontloading” grants, which has dramatically reduced the number of recipients of federal funding.

The Department of Education began using the tactic—wherein it pays for a multi-year grant fully up front instead of one year at a time, thereby dramatically decreasing the number of grants it awards—across a number of grant programs in unprecedented ways in fiscal year 2026. This has occurred at the same time the Department of Education and the Office of Management and Budget are seeking broader authority to terminate grants, raising the specter that they will terminate some of these grants in the future, and the funding will never reach communities that need it—yet another backdoor way of withholding appropriated funding.

“This administration has chosen—brazenly and repeatedly—to prioritize its own backwards agenda over the needs of students, families, and communities across the United States. The Department of Education’s extensive ‘frontloading’ of grants is just the latest example,” write Murray and Baldwin. “By ‘frontloading’ grants—paying out many years of a multi-year grant in one lump sum instead of funding a larger number of grants right now—your Department is dramatically reducing the number of students and schools that are helped by federal funding. This policy defies congressional intent and effectively cuts investment in communities across the country.”

In their letter, Murray and Baldwin explain how frontloading grants for several programs resulted in a steep drop-off in awards made in fiscal year 2026: “Instead of deploying funds immediately to hundreds of additional communities for essential education and related services, the Department is withholding approximately $630 million in appropriated resources across approximately 35 grant programs, preventing those funds from reaching students and families now. These are all programs where the Department has historically funded grants on an annual basis. If the Department continued that practice in administering these programs, the Department could have awarded well over 1,000 additional grants this year, supporting everything from evidence-based student literacy programs, to improving student mental health, to recruiting and preparing high-quality teachers, to supporting additional education research and to helping first-generation students succeed in college.”

They conclude: “This policy is indefensible. The Department must immediately abandon this approach and administer appropriated funds in full alignment with both the law and the needs of the communities that rely on these programs.”

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Secretary McMahon:

This administration has chosen—brazenly and repeatedly—to prioritize its own backwards agenda over the needs of students, families, and communities across the United States. The Department of Education’s (Department) extensive “frontloading” of grants is just the latest example. By “frontloading” grants—paying out many years of a multi-year grant in one lump sum instead of funding a larger number of grants right now—your Department is dramatically reducing the number of students and schools that are helped by federal funding. This policy defies congressional intent and effectively cuts investment in communities across the country: the Department could have funded well over 1,000 more grants by committing funds for use without delay. The Department should immediately reverse this deeply misguided and unacceptable approach to implementation of federal appropriations, including funds provided in the FY2026 appropriations law.

In implementing this policy, the Department is intentionally and sharply limiting the number of new grants it will award, by concentrating funds into fewer grants and withholding significant portions of appropriated resources for use in future budget periods. The decisions made to frontload a huge swath of departmental grants came just weeks after the Secretaries of Education and Health and Human Services and Acting Secretary of Labor wrote a letter to Congressional leadership touting the purported success of the illegal interagency agreements (IAAs) they have reached, which highlighted there were “record application levels” for certain grant competitions compared to prior years .1 Needless to say: record application levels are meaningless to students and families when the Department is choosing to fund fewer new grants under these competitions .2

This policy blatantly disregards congressional directives and withholds urgently needed federal resources from the very communities these programs are meant to serve. Instead of deploying funds immediately to hundreds of additional communities for essential education and related services, the Department is withholding approximately $630 million in appropriated resources across approximately 35 grant programs, preventing those funds from reaching students and families now. These are all programs where the Department has historically funded grants on an annual basis—if the Department continued that practice in administering these programs, the Department could have awarded well over 1,000 additional grants this year, supporting everything from evidence-based student literacy programs, to improving student mental health, to recruiting and preparing high-quality teachers, to supporting additional education research and to helping first-generation students succeed in college.

This policy is indefensible. The Department must immediately abandon this approach and administer appropriated funds in full alignment with both the law and the needs of the communities that rely on these programs. Congress expects no less, and the public deserves no less.

Last year, the Department stated that literacy was its top priority.3 Yet its recent actions tell a different story. The FY2026 appropriations law provided $30 million for the Innovative Approaches to Literacy (IAL) program, which supports improved literacy for children and students from birth through 12th grade—including strengthening school libraries and expanding early literacy services in low-income communities nationwide. When the Department issued its grant competition notice earlier this year, it indicated that it would make 25 to 35 new awards using these funds .4 Unfortunately, just weeks ago, the Department announced that it would make only four new awards and would set aside $13 million for future years of these grants. Those funds could have been used to make roughly 25 additional awards. It is inexplicable that a Department claiming literacy as its top priority would so drastically limit the number of new grants supporting evidence-based literacy programming. In addition, the number of new awards is also a dramatic reduction from the last grant competitions under the Biden administration in FY2023 when 12 new awards were made and FY2021 when 29 new awards were made with total IAL program funding at the same or a smaller level.5 This Department of Education is doing significantly less to support evidence-based literacy despite its claim of “supercharging” evidence-based literacy programming.6

Sadly, the Department also has chosen to restrict grants that support child care for low-income student parents so they can pursue postsecondary education and workforce training. Congress provided $75 million to the Child Care Access Means Parents in School Program (CCAMPIS) in the final FY2026 appropriations law, funding that is critical to ensuring low-income students receive the support they need while attending college. The Department estimated it would make 148 awards with the CCAMPIS appropriation when it published the notice inviting applications earlier this year and did not announce an intention to frontload.7 Yet, when the Department announced the new CCAMPIS grantees for FY2026, it made only 40 total new awards and set aside $53 million for future years of these grants. It is perplexing that an Administration that says it wants to improve affordability for Americans and help Americans find good-paying jobs would curtail a program that helps Americans afford higher education and workforce training.

In addition, there are widespread teacher shortages facing our local public schools. According to a recent analysis of Department data, there are an estimated 425,412 teaching positions either unfilled or filled by teachers not fully certified for their assignments, representing about 1 in 8 of all teaching positions nationally .8 Yet, the Department restricted the number of new grants to help train effective educators through the Supporting Effective Educator Development program this year, limiting it to just 16 new awards when it could have funded dozens more.9 Similarly, the Department only awarded 12 grants under the Teacher Quality Partnership (TQP) program and set aside $59 million of the $70 million appropriation for future years of these grants. Sadly, the Department also chose to front load most of the appropriation for the Augustus Hawkins Centers of Excellence Program which supports teacher preparation programs in minority-serving institutions, by setting aside over $14 million for future years.

Finally, while state and local education leaders and educators continue to face an ongoing and urgent need for actionable evidence on challenges for education policy and practice, the administration has basically shuttered its research arm, the Institute for Education Sciences (IES) since last January.10 IES chose not to make new awards from grant competitions posted in 2024 to which institutions had already applied for funding and issued no new awards from grant competitions in FY2026.11 As a result, IES simply frontloaded existing research grants in order to meet its spending requirement by September 30, 2026.12 Unfortunately, this same story is repeated throughout the Department’s mishandling of many grant programs this year.

There is no meaningful benefit to this policy change, and certainly nothing that outweighs the significant costs of withholding this funding. The Department is doing this because it wants to eliminate the Department of Education, eliminate these programs, and significantly cut funding for schools. It does not increase certainty for grantees because at the same time, the Department and Office of Management and Budget are both proposing changes to grants management rules that empower agencies to terminate grants for any reason. This suggests even more nefarious motives—awarding funding that can only be used in future years now while empowering agencies to terminate that very funding in the future before it ever reaches students and schools.

The Department has proposed to rewrite the Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR) that govern grant programs Congress has authorized it to administer.13 One of the major changes in the EDGAR proposal would allow the Secretary of Education to terminate multi-year grants “for convenience”. OMB has proposed similar changes in its federal financial assistance regulation that would rewrite uniform guidance governing grants management government-wide. That proposed rule would empower political appointees to terminate grants for any reason. If the proposed changes to EDGAR or OMB’s uniform guidance were to go into effect, this means the Department could easily terminate all these frontloaded funds, effectively terminating a large swath of FY2026 funds that Congress appropriated on a bipartisan basis. This would also make it more difficult for grantees to hire staff and plan to achieve grant objectives as efficiently and effectively as possible. And it would mean that the Department could satisfy Congressional requirements to obligate funds for programs and activities and later turn around and terminate the very grants that were made to satisfy Congressional spending requirements in future fiscal years.

Students deserve timely access to evidence-based literacy resources; parents deserve access to childcare services that allow them to pursue postsecondary education; and all students should have a classroom staffed by a high-quality educator. Congress provided resources for these purposes, and the Department has an obligation—not an option—to use them accordingly.

Sincerely,

###

title: Murray Celebrates Opening of New Agricultural Research Service Plant Sciences Building at WSU After Years of Fighting to Secure Funding
text:
Murray: “At a time when our federal research enterprise is under serious threat by overt political interference and a hollowing out of our scientific workforce, today’s milestone offers a bright spot. This new building is a reminder of the incredible potential and opportunity we have when we invest in agricultural research—and when we do it consistently.”

ICYMI: Senator Murray, Secretary Vilsack Speak at Groundbreaking of New Agricultural Research Service Plant Sciences Building at WSU Murray Secured $125 Million to Build

Pullman, WA — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and a Washington State University (WSU) alum, attended the ribbon-cutting of the brand-new Agricultural Research Service (ARS) Plant Sciences Building on WSU’s campus. Senator Murray led the years-long fight to secure $125 million in federal funding for the building.

The newly-completed building will house ARS and WSU researchers focused on improving the health, sustainability, and profitability of dryland and irrigated agriculture in the Pacific Northwest. The building includes cutting-edge facilities for four ARS research units where scientists will focus on the health and sustainability of Pacific Northwest agroecosystems—and critical challenges facing national and global agriculture. The collaborative research between ARS and WSU will benefit growers, commodity groups, agricultural businesses, and American consumers who rely on this partnership to find solutions to agricultural and environmental problems.

“As someone who has fought for this project at every step, in every funding bill I helped write, for over twenty years now, I know it’s been a long road to today—with plenty of hurdles: from economic crises, to forced federal budget cuts, and, of course, a full-blown pandemic. At every twist and turn, I’ve been proud to lock arms with the community here at WSU and go to bat for this building and this research on the Appropriations Committee. Because in farming, in research, and in Congress, the surest path to success is the same, you need persistence, and you need patience,” Senator Murray said. “At a time when our federal research enterprise is under serious threat by overt political interference and a hollowing out of our scientific workforce, today’s milestone offers a bright spot. This new building is a reminder of the incredible potential and opportunity we have when we invest in agricultural research—and when we do it consistently. The answers discovered here in Pullman will help producers weather a rapidly changing climate and navigate an increasingly tough farm economy. And the students inspired here, will spend their careers advancing this research and ensuring that legacy persists.”

As a senior appropriator and former Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Senator Murray led the effort in Congress to secure $125 million in federal funding for the ARS building over multiple fiscal years. After pushing for the project for many years, Murray secured $105 million in the Fiscal Year 2019 funding bill for ARS to construct the new facility. But when the COVID-19 pandemic hit, supply chain issues and inflation delayed the project and increased the estimated cost of the building. In FY23, Murray secured an additional $20 million for the project, allowing WSU and ARS to finally move forward with construction. In 2023, Senator Murray attended the groundbreaking for the building and spoke on WSU’s excellence in agricultural research.

Senator Murray has been a longtime advocate for Washington state’s farmers and has always advocated for major investments in cutting-edge agricultural research—like the research conducted at Washington State University, ARS, and all across Washington state. The agriculture appropriations bill for Fiscal Year 2026 that Senator Murray wrote as Vice Chair of the Appropriations Committee provided $1.85 billion for ARS, and $1.67 billion for the National Institute of Food and Agriculture—rejecting President Trump’s budget request to slash core capacity funding for land-grant universities, like WSU, across the country and other key research and extension activities, which make important, practical information available to agricultural producers, small business owners, consumers, families, and young people.

Compared to FY24, ARS is down more than 2,300 people or 30% of their staff after an aggressive Deferred Resignation Program by Trump’s USDA and subsequent hiring freezes. Murray has been a vocal critic of the Trump administration’s efforts to decimate America’s federal research enterprise, warning her colleagues that President Trump’s haphazard and callous decimation of key federal agencies is both inefficient and will cost taxpayers more in lost research and productivity. In every government funding bill she negotiates, Murray has fought, and will keep fighting, to protect every corner of America’s world-class research enterprise, from the labs searching for new cures to the scientists keeping our farms and food supply strong.

Since its origins in 1931, collaborations between WSU and ARS have exemplified one of the strongest federal-state partnerships in the nation. These collaborations benefit growers, commodity groups, agricultural businesses, and U.S. consumers who rely on this partnership to find solutions to agricultural and environmental problems. In the new Plant Sciences Building, scientists will investigate wheat health, genetics and quality; grain genetics and physiology; sustainable Pacific Northwest agroecosystems; and plant germplasm introductions and evaluations. Members of the WSU Departments of Plant Pathology, Crop and Soil Sciences, and Horticulture will share space and work closely in the new facility alongside federal researchers on projects that improve crops and sustainable practices and reduce the impacts of weeds, pests, and diseases on agriculture in the Pacific Northwest. More information on the project is HERE.

Senator Murray’s remarks, as prepared, are below:

“As a proud Coug, it is always wonderful to be back in Pullman. I have memories all over this campus. There’s the time I met my husband. There’s the time I won my first political fight—changing the dress code so women could wear pants to the dining hall, not just dresses and skirts.

“And—more relevant to today—there was the time, just three years ago, that I joined everyone to break ground on this new Ag-Research center! When I joined you for the groundbreaking of this building—I noted how appropriate it was that we were digging up soil and putting down roots to grow something truly special.

“And how excited I was to come back again when this place was up and open, and bustling with students, researchers, and ideas. Well, here we are—and it’s everything I could’ve hoped for!

“As someone who has fought for this project at every step, in every funding bill I helped write, for over twenty years now, I know it’s been a long road to today—with plenty of hurdles: from economic crises, to forced federal budget cuts, and, of course, a full-blown pandemic.

“At every twist and turn, I’ve been proud to lock arms with the community here at WSU and go to bat for this building and this research on the Appropriations Committee. Because in farming, in research, and in Congress, the surest path to success is the same, you need persistence, and you need patience.

“And today? The persistence pays off! Today? The wait is over! But, not the work—that is just beginning!

“Because now that this building is open, students, faculty, and researchers are going to be walking through these doors, rolling up their sleeves, getting their hands dirty, and diving into some of the biggest challenges facing our farmers.

“At a time when our federal research enterprise is under serious threat by overt political interference and a hollowing out of our scientific workforce, today’s milestone offers a bright spot. This new building is a reminder of the incredible potential and opportunity we have when we invest in agricultural research—and when we do it consistently.

“The answers discovered here in Pullman will help producers weather a rapidly changing climate and navigate an increasingly tough farm economy. And the students inspired here, will spend their careers advancing this research and ensuring that legacy persists.

“Everyone here knows farming and agriculture are crucial to Washington state. We have over 30,000 farms and ranches. With over 160,000 people working on them growing apples, potatoes, wheat, cherries, blueberries—and a whole lot more. And what grows in Washington state, goes across the country—and across the world!

“But just as families count on Washington state farms for high-quality produce, our farms count on research happening right here to help them find new ways to protect crops, reduce costly inputs, and grow more food for more people.

“Here at WSU, students and researchers are fighting threats that destroy crops like potato blight, wheat and barley scab, and little cherry disease. Here at WSU, we are looking at how Artificial Intelligence can help our farmers. And don’t forget our leadership in the other AI, I’m speaking of course about: Apple Innovation! Move over iPhone—I think everyone knows Sunflare is the most exciting apple release on the horizon!

“And beyond growing seeds into new apples, this is a place where minds grow, where curiosity is nurtured, where new ideas take root, and where hard work bears fruit—in more ways than one!

“It’s worth remembering, that while we usually say ‘you reap what you sow’ as a word of warning. It’s really deeper than that—it’s a reminder. A promise, that says when you plant something, when you pour your time and effort into something, your heart and soul, it will grow.

“So, make sure you focus on growing things that are truly worthwhile. I think about that every spring when I plant flowers in my garden. And it motivates me every time I see a problem and choose to roll up my sleeves.

“If you want to grow something, if you want to build something, if you want to discover something, if you want to change something—you’ve got to put in the work. And no one works harder than a Coug!

“Which is why, as excited as I am to be here today, to see this project in bloom, the visit I’m most excited about—is always the next one. Because I know I’ll be back—and that the next time I visit, there will be a whole new crop of discoveries coming in.

“So, as you all continue to build on the incredible work happening here, know that I am going to continue my work fighting to support you in the other Washington.”

title: Padilla, Schiff, Gray Demand Answers from ICE in Response to Increased Enforcement Activity in Mendota
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.), along with U.S. Representative Adam Gray (D-Calif-13), demanded answers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) following reports of increased enforcement activity and resident detentions in Mendota beginning on October 5.

In a letter to Acting ICE Director David Venturella, the lawmakers requested details about the operation’s purpose and scope, the number of individuals detained, and the safeguards in place to protect due process and minimize disruption to local families and businesses.

“Mendota is a hardworking agricultural community, and families should not have to fear going to work or taking their kids to school,” the lawmakers wrote. “Federal immigration laws must be enforced, but how that happens matters. We need answers about what’s taking place, who is being targeted and whether people’s rights are being protected.”

The lawmakers also questioned whether local law enforcement was consulted, where detainees are being held, and what steps ICE is taking to address concerns raised by Mendota’s mayor and City Council.

They further emphasized the importance of protecting public safety and due process while recognizing the essential role farmworkers play in the Central Valley economy and America’s food supply.

“The people of Mendota deserve to know why these operations are taking place and what safeguards are in place to protect their families and community,” the lawmakers concluded. “The federal government’s responsibility to enforce immigration law does not give it license to create fear across an entire community.”

Padilla has been a leader in opposing the Trump Administration’s cruel and indiscriminate mass deportation agenda. Last week, Padilla visited an ICE holding facility in downtown Los Angeles to examine conditions firsthand and demand answers from federal officials. He also visited a de-facto immigration detention facility at San Francisco International Airport earlier this month. In August, Padilla called out the Trump Administration’s continued abuses of power and demanded DHS immediately halt its reckless plan to equip ICE officers with electric shock gloves. In June, Padilla and Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) sounded the alarm over the significant increase in deaths among detainees in ICE custody since January 2025, expressing concern over the announcement of the 50th reported death in ICE custody under the Trump Administration.

Full letter is available here and below:

Dear Acting Director Venturella:

We write to express serious concern about reports of increased Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) activity in Mendota, California, beginning October 5, 2026, and to request an immediate explanation of the purpose, scope, and conduct of these operations.

The Mayor and City Council of Mendota have already formally expressed their concerns about the fear and uncertainty these enforcement activities are creating in their community. Their message is clear: Families should not be afraid to go to work, parents should feel safe taking their children to school, and residents should be able to go about their daily lives without fear.

Mendota is a hardworking agricultural community whose families have spent generations helping feed our state and nation. Its farmworkers are essential to the Central Valley economy and America’s food supply and their contributions deserve recognition and respect. Federal immigration laws must be enforced, but how those laws are enforced matters. Immigration enforcement should prioritize individuals who pose genuine threats to public safety, respect due process, and avoid unnecessarily disrupting families, businesses, and entire communities.

Reports of federal agents conducting operations in Mendota and detaining residents have raised serious questions about the objectives and methods of these activities. The resulting fear extends well beyond those directly involved in enforcement actions and threatens the stability of a community that depends on its agricultural workforce.

As Mendota and California’s representatives in Congress, we have a responsibility to demand answers and ensure that federal enforcement activities respect the rights, dignity, and safety of the people we represent.

Accordingly, we request answers to the following questions:

What circumstances or specific enforcement objectives prompted the increased ICE activity in Mendota and surrounding communities beginning October 5?

How many individuals have been detained during these operations, and how many were identified as posing a threat to public safety?

Where have detained individuals been transported or held, and what procedures are in place to ensure access to legal counsel and due process?

Were local law enforcement agencies notified or consulted before these operations? If so, which agencies?

What policies or instructions have been provided to agents to prevent unnecessary detention, protect family unity, and minimize disruption to schools, workplaces, and agricultural operations?

What steps will ICE take to address the concerns formally raised by Mendota’s mayor and City Council?

The people of Mendota deserve to know why these operations are taking place, who is being targeted, and what safeguards are in place to protect their families and community.

The federal government’s responsibility to enforce immigration law does not give it license to create fear across an entire community. Mendota’s families deserve public safety, due process, and respect. We expect ICE to uphold all three.

We look forward to your prompt response to the questions outlined above.

Sincerely,

###

title: Padilla, Schumer Announce Recruitment of 100 + Senate Staff and Plans to Deploy to Nine States Ahead of Midterms
text:
First-of-its-kind Senate program will put trained congressional observers on the ground to document any voter interference or threats to election workers in 2026 midterm Senate contests as Trump escalates efforts to undermine election integrity

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration and California’s former Secretary of State, and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) announced that more than 100 Senate Democratic staff have been recruited and trained as official congressional election observers to be deployed to polling sites across nine states. Trained staff will serve as official congressional observers and document any attempted voter interference, threats against election workers, misinformation, disinformation, or other attempts to meddle with elections, both on Election Day and in the post-election canvass and certification process.

Padilla and Schumer launched Senate Democrats’ participation in the first-of-its-kind Senate Election Observer Program in June to counter Trump’s ongoing election threats and to promote transparency, protect voter confidence, and ensure the Senate has objective, on-the-ground information in Senate races.

“Donald Trump has made clear that he wants to ‘take over the voting’ in state-run elections. Election interference is unconstitutional and illegal and Congress will be watching,” said Senator Padilla. “We’ve recruited more than 100 Senate staffers to serve as official election observers across nine states to document potential voter interference, threats against election workers, and attempts to undermine the democratic process. Every eligible American deserves to cast a ballot free from intimidation, and every vote deserves to be counted fairly. We’re taking this step to ensure that any attempt to interfere with the right to vote is documented, exposed and met with accountability.”

“Donald Trump is trying to steal the election – but Democrats and the American people won’t let him,” said Leader Schumer.“Our elections are free and secure, but we cannot take that for granted. I am grateful for the Senate staff members who are raising their hand to help build trust in our upcoming election and protect the sanctity of our democracy. Trump has fought harder to rig the elections than he has to bring down costs. His record-breaking unpopularity comes from his agenda failing families, and no amount of his election meddling can change that. The voters will decide the next election—not Trump.”

The prepared deployment comes with nearly 20 days until Election Day and as President Trump continues to sow doubt in the integrity of American elections and threaten the foundations of free and fair voting. His Administration has pushed sweeping voter roll purges, issued executive orders aimed at restricting voting, sought to limit mail-in and absentee voting, and pressed Congress to pass the so-called SAVE America Act. The Administration has also faced allegations of unlawful efforts to access state voter data.

The Senate Election Observer Program will not interfere with election officials in the performance of their duties or seek to influence election results in any way. It will:

Put trained congressional observers on the ground: Train and designate Democratic Senators’ official staff to observe polling locations and sites where ballots are counted and elections are canvassed and certified

Document any election interference: Deter election interference, promote confidence in American elections, and help ensure free and fair elections in 2026. Observe and record any election issues, including potential instances of voter interference, threats targeting election workers, impacts of election misinformation or disinformation, and any issues regarding the canvass or certification of elections

Strengthen congressional oversight: Gather on-the-ground information about U.S. Senate elections to assist the Senate Rules Committee in addressing any potentially contested Senate elections. Inform the Committee’s legislative and oversight work related to election administration

Operate under established authority: The same authority as the long-running House of Representatives’ Election Observer Program

Senate Democrats’ Election Observer Program is similar to the long-running program in the House of Representatives and follows the October 2024 passage of the Confirmation of Congressional Observer Access (COCOA) Act, which confirmed the constitutional authority of Congress, specifically the Chair and Ranking Members of the Committee on House Administration and Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, to designate congressional election observers. Senate Republicans are also launching a program under the same authority.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections and California’s former Secretary of State and chief election officer, Padilla has championed election security and voting rights issues. Last month, Padilla introduced the Freedom From Intimidation Act, legislation to prohibit firearms at polling places to protect voters and poll workers. Padilla also demanded DHS Secretary Mullin immediately halt election interference efforts and led the congressional response to the bombshell whistleblower report that DHS agents violated state laws as part of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” In August, Padilla led 27 of his Senate colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop their illegal voter roll purges before Election Day.

###

title: Ricketts Champions AI Innovation and Safety
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, is leading the charge to position the United States as a leader on Artificial Intelligence (AI) innovation and safety.

“A world where Communist China leads the AI race is bad for the United States and the entire world,” said Senator Ricketts. “That’s why I support efforts to strengthen American innovation while creating guardrails to ensure Americans’ safety.

“Communist China knows no boundaries when it comes to competition. Beijing sees AI as a way to beat us both militarily and economically. But American innovation is superior. We have the resources, technology, and opportunity to win.

“Winning the AI race means preventing China from gaining access to our most advanced technology. It also means implementing commonsense guardrails to protect Americans without stifling innovation.

“The stakes are high. Maintaining America’s global leadership in AI is a matter of national security. We need smart policies that protect Americans, sustain innovation, and ensure the future of AI is led by the United States.”

Senator Ricketts has championed legislation to strengthen AI innovation and development, protect America’s competitiveness against Communist China, and prioritize Americans’ safety and security.

The Secure and Feasible Exports of Chips Act (SAFE Chips Act). This bill would limit the export of advanced AI chips to Communist China. It would protect America’s technological advantage and prevent Communist China from using U.S.-designed chips to accelerate its AI capabilities.

Read the SAFE Chips Act here.

Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware Act (MATCH Act). This bill would prevent Communist China from buying “chokepoint” semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME) technology from the United States and our allies that they cannot build themselves. It would close gaps in allied export controls that Communist China exploits to acquire sensitive semiconductor technology and advance its domestic chip industry.

Read the MATCH Act here. Read Senator Ricketts’ Washington Times op-ed here.

Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act (GUARD Act). This bill would ban AI companions for minors. It would require age verification and mandatory AI disclosures for all users to protect children from AI chatbots.

Read the GUARD Act here.

U.S. Technology Procurement and Access to Trusted Hardware Act (Tech PATH Act). This bill would support the procurement of American cyber and digital technology by partner countries. It would help our allies and partners adopt trusted American technology while reducing reliance on technology from Communist China and other foreign adversaries.

Read the Tech PATH Act here.

Ratepayer Protection Act. This bill would give states and local communities the leverage to negotiate on data centers in communities. It would prevent ratepayers from footing the bill for the full utility costs of data centers needed to operate.

title: Risch, Crapo, Wyden, Merkley Introduce Three-Year Reauthorization of Secure Rural Schools Program
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Jim Risch, Mike Crapo (both R-Idaho), Ron Wyden, and Jeff Merkley (both D-Ore.) introduced bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act program (SRS) for three years, providing continued support for rural schools and counties home to nontaxable federal land to fund education, road maintenance and other essential services.

“Secure Rural Schools funding is a commitment the federal government made to Idaho’s rural counties, helping them maintain roads, schools and other essential services,” said Risch. “As we work to restore the timber revenues that have long sustained these communities, Congress must honor that commitment and reauthorize SRS.”

“Counties across Idaho should not have to repeatedly face uncertainty about whether the federal government will uphold its responsibility to communities containing vast amounts of tax-exempt federal land,” said Crapo. “Without action, rural schools and counties will lose resources they rely on to maintain roads, support schools and provide basic services. This three-year reauthorization provides needed stability, but we must continue working toward a permanent solution that gives these communities the predictability they need to effectively plan and budget for the future.”

“Secure Rural Schools is a lifeline for rural Oregon,” said Wyden. “I’ll be working as hard as I can to get this bill across the finish line, but the well-being of rural America shouldn’t be dependent on Congress getting its act together to renew this funding every few years. It’s past time to get rural communities off the financial rollercoaster and deliver a permanent funding solution.”

“The SRS program provides crucial payments that are a lifeline for rural communities here in Oregon and across America—keeping schools open, maintaining roads, restoring watersheds, and providing funding for police officers and firefighters to keep families safe,” said Merkley. “A three-year extension of the program is critical to ensuring the federal government upholds its promise to our communities and that local governments can reliably access these important resources.”

“More than 700 counties across the country depend on the Secure Rural Schools program. Counties applaud Senators Crapo, Wyden, Risch and Merkley for leading this bipartisan legislation that will keep schools operating, roads and bridges maintained and public safety services funded in rural communities. SRS was reauthorized already once this Congress with overwhelming, bipartisan support. Now that it has lapsed again, Congress must act quickly to preserve SRS for rural counties across the country by passing this bipartisan legislation, so counties and communities have fiscal certainty.” – Matthew Chase, Executive Director, National Association of Counties (NACo)

“Secure Rural Schools funding is vital to Idaho counties, supporting the maintenance of county roads and bridges, search and rescue services on federal lands, and K-12 education. As this critical funding nears expiration, we urge Congress to reauthorize the program for an additional three years to ensure counties can continue to meet these essential obligations. We thank Senator Crapo and his team for their continued efforts to raise awareness of this program’s importance to Idaho communities.” – Seth Grigg, Executive Director, Idaho Association of Counties

“Idaho’s rural schools shouldn’t be disadvantaged simply because so much of the land surrounding their communities is federally owned. Secure Rural Schools recognizes that reality and provides critical resources that help rural communities support their students. I applaud Senator Crapo’s commitment to providing Idaho’s rural communities greater stability through this essential funding while honoring the local control that allows communities to determine how best to serve their students.” – Debbie Critchfield, Idaho Superintendent of Public Instruction

Background

Congress created SRS in 2000 to provide financial assistance to counties with federally owned forestlands that are exempt from collecting local property taxes. Historically, rural counties received a share of receipts generated from timber harvests on federal lands. As timber harvests and associated revenues declined, SRS was established to provide predictable resources for counties and school districts that had historically relied on those receipts.

Crapo, Wyden, Risch and Merkley have worked together for years to maintain the program and provide greater certainty for rural communities. Most recently, the Senators led bipartisan legislation reauthorizing SRS through Fiscal Year 2026 and restoring lapsed payments for Fiscal Years 2024 and 2025. That legislation was signed into law in December 2025. Without further congressional action, the program will again expire after Fiscal Year 2026.

The U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Bureau of Land Management administer SRS payments. Funding is distributed using a formula that takes into account historic timber receipts, economic activity and other factors that vary by county. Depending on the payment title and eligible lands, SRS funding supports schools and roads, projects benefiting federal lands and specified county services such as emergency response and wildfire preparedness.

In Idaho, 34 of the state’s 44 counties received SRS payments in 2023. Under Idaho law, 30 percent of SRS funding is directed to schools, while the remaining 70 percent supports roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects.

title: PHOTOS: Sen. Schiff Travels to Canada for CODEL to Discuss Trade Disruption Impacts on California, Golden State Agriculture
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), the first Senator from California to serve on the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry in three decades, visited Canada this past week for a Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to share concerns about the impact that U.S.-Canada trade disruptions are having on California’s industries, including on agricultural goods like wine and dairy products.

Senator Schiff sought to learn more about Canada-California collaboration, shared experiences from California farmers and producers he’s met while serving as Senator, and discussed expansion opportunities for California businesses in Canadian markets.

“I met with officials to talk about the trade dispute with the United States and the different tariffs, and also to convey the sentiments of my California constituents and how they’re feeling the impacts…[and] to understand the Canadian reaction and how Canadians are feeling about U.S. products as well as the United States of America. I went there not to negotiate USMCA or any trade agreement, but rather to talk about the [Canadian] boycotts on alcohol, and how this is having a particular impact on the wine industry… [and] disputes over dairy, disputes over beef, and other products between our countries, our mutual energy reliance, and other issues. And I found the visit to be incredibly illuminating and helpful,” said Senator Schiff about his trip.

Canada is one of California’s largest trading partners and export markets, with cross-border commerce supporting California industries including technology, aerospace, agriculture, manufacturing, transportation equipment, and consumer goods. California and U.S. wine, for example, have generated upwards of $1 billion in annual sales in Canada in recent years. However, California farmers and producers have been disproportionately impacted by bans on the sale of U.S. alcohol by some Canadian provinces.

Senator Schiff visited Alberta to meet with the province’s Premier Danielle Smith, Agriculture Minister Tara Sawyer, and Utilities Minister R.J. Sigurdson. Schiff visited a rodeo breakfast in Edmonton and flipped pancakes for attendees alongside Premier Smith. Schiff then traveled to Ottawa, where he met with Canadian Minister for Agriculture Heath MacDonald and Member of Parliament Mona Fortier. Schiff also met with staff at the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa, the American Chamber of Commerce—which promotes American trade and investment in Canada—and American businesses in Canada.

Background: Senator Schiff has previously raised concerns about the impact that bans on U.S. alcohol placed by Canadian provinces have had on California agriculture. In June, he wrote to the Premier of Québec saying, in part, “I have had the great fortune of spending time with and learning about the challenges and opportunities of California’s winegrowers. They take great pride in their work, are essential to the state and national economy, and have brought tremendous value – in culture and in taste – to Americans and Canadians alike. Reopening the market to American wine would restore consumer choice and signal a commitment to restoring fair and balanced trade for Québecois consumers and American wineries who have no connection to the underlying trade disputes.”

title: Slotkin, Coons, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Sanction Israeli Settlements in the West Bank
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) joined legislation to sanction companies, individuals, and other entities that help develop Israeli settlements in the E1 area of the West Bank. The legislation was led by Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) and joined by Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Ron Wyden (D-OR), and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), among others.

Israel approved more than 3,000 housing units in E1, just last year, and has recently opened bidding to construction firms. If built, the settlements could split the West Bank in two and seriously undermine the viability of a future Palestinian state. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly said after approving the plan that “a Palestinian state will not be established.”

“Amid increasing violence, displacement, and fear for Palestinian civilians in the West Bank, the E1 project would make peace in the region harder to achieve and it is not in the interest of Israel’s long-term security or America’s,” said Slotkin. “For 30 years, Republican and Democratic administrations have opposed this project, and the United States should make clear that anyone who profits from this construction will face consequences for undermining long-term stability and prosperity, as well as displacing more of the Palestinian people.”

“For decades, American presidents from both parties have warned successive Israeli governments that construction in E1 threatened the viability of a Palestinian state and was unacceptable to the United States,” said Coons. “As Palestinian civilians face a campaign of devastation and fear from violent extremist settlers, the United States must send a strong message that this behavior is unacceptable and that it remains committed to freedom, security, prosperity, and self-determination for all Israelis and Palestinians.”

The bill would sanction any foreign person the Treasury Secretary finds responsible for or complicit in building settlements or related structures in E1, including by bidding on E1 tenders. It would also sanction anyone who organizes, directs, finances, or facilitates moving Israeli civilians into E1 settlements.

The bill is also cosponsored by Senators Michael Bennet (D-CO), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), and Peter Welch (D-VT).

Full bill text is available here.

title: Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland

“As we’ve said time and again, this Administration’s attempts to shutter BARC are not only unwise – they’re illegal. title: Welch Joins Visiting Nurses and Hospice Providers in Rutland to Discuss Innovations to Develop Vermont’s Rural Health Care Workforce
text:
RUTLAND, VT — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), a member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on Health Care, this week joined the VNA & Hospice of the Southwest Region and VNAs of Vermont to discuss new innovations that aim to develop Vermont’s rural health care workforce. At the event, the Senator highlighted the importance of home health and hospice agencies, which are critical partners in Vermont’s efforts to curb health care costs, transform care, and ensure that the health care system can meet the needs of Vermont communities.

“Rural communities across the country have the same health care workforce challenges, whether it’s a red state or blue state. The innovative work being done at VNA & Hospice of the Southwest Region to not just build but keep their workforce, including their new nurse residency program, is exactly what we should be replicating across the country,” said Senator Welch. “I’ll continue doing all I can to find bipartisan solutions that create jobs for health care providers in Vermont and expand opportunities for rural communities.”

“Nearly every Vermonter receiving home health or hospice services is someone who is not in a hospital or nursing home bed, directly reducing costs and increasing bed capacity for those who need care in those settings, while supporting Vermonters’ ability to age or heal at home. Home health and hospice agencies are pivotal to our ability as a state to reform or transform how and where health care is delivered, and how much it costs, and they are leading as innovators to grow and strengthen our rural health care workforce,” said Eric Covey, Executive Director, VNAs of Vermont.

“When we talk about the challenges facing rural Vermont, one thing becomes very clear: we have to continuously be creative. We have to find new ways to build our workforce, new ways to support the people who are already doing this work, and new ways to make sure Vermonters can receive the care they need close to home. The Nurse Residency Program gives us an opportunity to build that structure and make that investment possible. Innovative solutions like this one will be critical to recruiting, training, and retaining the workforce of skilled clinicians needed to care for the Vermonters who depend on us the most,” said Jessica Boutin, Chief Executive Officer, VNA & Hospice of the Southwest Region.

View photos from the event below:

Six agencies in the State of Vermont are investing nearly $4 million in grant funds to work with and recruit additional ‘new to home health and hospice’ nurse residents. By pairing residents with preceptors experienced in the field, with a curriculum focused on honing the competencies necessary to thrive, this program will build confidence, and competence, while empowering existing staff to grow professionals as trainers and mentors, impacting recruitment and retention of our care-at-home workforce.

Senator Welch is a champion for rural health care and has worked across the aisle to lead legislation to improve access to care, including the Rural Hospital Support Act, Improving Access to Medicare Coverage Act, Rural Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act, Fair Funding for Rural Hospitals Act, Multigenerational Home Caregiver Credit Act, and the CONNECT for Health Act.

title: Wyden Presses Trump Administration over Political Interference in Commerce, Census Data
text:
Wyden raises concerns over potential for political interference in 2030 Census, nonpartisan data collection

Washington, D.C. – Senator Ron Wyden, D-Ore., today demanded answers from the Trump administration following reports that the Commerce Department has stripped away protections against political influence in its Scientific Integrity Policy.

“The Department’s recent decision in August 2026 to quietly strip explicit prohibitions against political interference from its Scientific Integrity Policy is yet another attempt by the Trump administration to undermine scientific facts and data that do not align with its own priorities,” Wyden wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “Doing away with these safeguards could also result in biased reports that violate federal law under the Information Quality Act, which requires agencies to maintain the quality, objectivity, and integrity of the information they share with the public.”

The unannounced policy shift comes shortly after the U.S. Census Bureau published an unauthored, highly irregular report on noncitizen voting—a document data and elections experts widely criticized for its flawed methodology and complete lack of peer review. An NPR investigation revealed that the report was spearheaded by the America First Policy Institute, a conservative group with deep ties to Donald Trump.

Wyden stressed that doing away with these guardrails is an open invitation for political interference in nonpartisan data relied on by communities and small businesses for everything from census counts to inflation metrics and hurricane forecasts. Wyden also voiced concerns over the implication of political influence by the Trump administration in the upcoming 2030 Census in an effort to suppress political participation of Trump’s political opponents and reallocate federal funding for vulnerable communities.

title: Alford Announces $16.2 Million U.S. DOT Grant to Modernize COLT Railroad in Columbia
text:
Today, Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04) announced that the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) has awarded $16,207,000 through the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program to the City of Columbia, Missouri.

The funding will support the COLT Railroad Modernization Program, a vital initiative to upgrade the 21.4-mile Columbia Terminal Railroad (COLT) connecting Columbia and Centralia. Rep. Alford strongly championed this project, helping to secure the grant funding through robust advocacy, including sending a formal letter of support with Rep. Bob Onder (MO-03) to the FRA.

"The COLT railroad is a critical economic lifeline for Mid-Missouri, connecting our local manufacturers, agricultural producers, and building materials suppliers to the national freight network," said Congressman Alford. "I was proud to lead the charge and help secure this grant to ensure our region remains at the cutting edge of transportation innovation. This major investment will modernize our infrastructure, enhance safety, and pioneer autonomous rail technology right here in Missouri—all while supporting local jobs and boosting our economic competitiveness."

Project Summary

The total cost of the COLT Railroad Modernization Program is $20,827,000, backed by $16,207,000 in federal CRISI funding and $4,620,000 in non-federal cost shares contributed by private sector partners and the City of Columbia. Key components of the project include:

Autonomous Rail Technology Demonstration: Deploys self-propelled, autonomous railcar equipment to conduct the first documented demonstration of autonomous railcar operations on a regulated short line in the United States.

Phased Operational Safety Framework: Establishes an FRA-approved test program, progressing safely from terminal switching to maintenance-of-way activities and full mainline revenue-service demonstrations across 57 at-grade crossings.

Track and Infrastructure Upgrades: Procures and installs 36,000 sustainable, 100% American-made Evertrak composite rail ties, completes track tamping across approximately 6 miles of upgraded track, replaces three degraded turnout switches, and builds two Level 2 terminal charging units.

Workforce Development: Develops a comprehensive workforce training curriculum for remote operators, field engineers, and maintenance technicians in partnership with the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association.

Economic and Safety Growth: Preserves and expands rail access for Mid-Missouri businesses along a corridor that generates $670 million in total sales, supports 243 jobs, and drives state and local tax revenue.

title: Ansari Introduces Bipartisan IRAN Act to Expand Internet Freedom for the Iranian People
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Claudia Tenney (NY-24) introduced the bipartisan Internet Reach and Access Now (IRAN) Act to strengthen U.S. efforts to help the Iranian people access the open internet, communicate securely, and overcome the Iranian regime’s censorship, surveillance, and internet shutdowns.

“Freedom of expression and access to unrestricted information are fundamental human rights. The Islamic Republic regularly shuts down or restricts internet access while committing mass atrocities,” said Congresswoman Ansari. “President Trump has said 'help is on the way' for the Iranian people. Ensuring unrestricted internet access would actually help people immediately. I’m proud to introduce the IRAN Act, a bipartisan, noncontroversial, and not militarily invasive bill that would do just that.”

Iran remains one of the world’s most restrictive digital environments, with the regime routinely restricting internet access to suppress dissent, conceal human rights abuses, and isolate the Iranian people. The IRAN Act strengthens the U.S. internet freedom strategy for Iran by requiring regular reviews, implementation assessments, and congressional reporting, while evaluating emerging technologies such as VPNs, decentralized and peer to peer networks, and direct to cell satellite communications. The legislation also seeks to expand cybersecurity training and secure digital tools for journalists, human rights defenders, and other civil society actors, and directs greater coordination among federal agencies to help ensure U.S. sanctions and export controls do not unintentionally hinder access to open internet technologies.

title: Barrett, Gluesenkamp Perez Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Crack Down on Elder Fraud
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) and Congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) introduced the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act to establish a 24/7 hotline and website to serve as a one-stop shop for reporting scams and fraud targeting seniors. The platform would help law enforcement catch and prosecute criminals while offering seniors resources to protect themselves from potential scams.

Fraud costs American seniors billions of dollars every year. The latest reporting by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) found that adults aged 60 and older lost about $2.4 billion to fraud in 2024 alone.

“Fraudsters are constantly targeting seniors to cheat them out of their hard-earned retirement,” Barrett said. “These sophisticated scammers pose as federal agencies, banks, and even loved ones, while artificial intelligence is making impersonation easier than ever. Families need resources to recognize and quickly report suspected fraud. By establishing a 24/7, one-stop shop for addressing elder fraud, this bipartisan bill will protect vulnerable seniors and empower law enforcement to crack down on these criminals.”

“People who steal from seniors and retirees are the lowest of the low. No one should have to navigate impenetrable government websites or spend hours stuck on hold trying to report these scams,” said Gluesenkamp Perez. “My bill makes it simple, you call one number or go to one site and your report goes directly to the investigator you need. When we give law enforcement the tools to fight back, they can respond immediately and take on these predatory scammers.”

Currently, the Department of Justice (DOJ) operates an elder fraud hotline, but it is only available during business hours, and finding relevant information from different federal agencies can be difficult.

Under the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act, the FTC and DOJ would be responsible for operating a 24/7 elder fraud hotline and website, which would enable a senior or loved one to file a complaint about any fraud or scam, submit a message allegedly from the federal government to verify whether it is legitimate, and request a connection with the appropriate federal, state, and local authorities.

The website would also provide resources for combating the most common types of elder fraud and scams — including resources at relevant federal agencies.

title: Opposition To Trump’s Vanity Arch Grows
text:
Staunch opposition to Donald Trump’s proposed vanity arch grew sharpy in early October, as veterans, residents, and workers expressed hostility to the project, and the Northern Virginia county that surrounds the site filed suit against it.

On October 1st, as NPR reported: “Veterans, retirees and lawmakers spoke out — against its scale, its cost, its lack of Congressional approval, its gaudiness, its intrusion on nearby Arlington National Cemetery and more.”

On October 7th, per the Associated Press: “The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump’s proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.”

On October 8th, the Washington Post reported: “Arlington County’s local elected body sued to block construction of President Donald Trump’s planned triumphal arch on Thursday, arguing that administration officials bypassed a key review process in their push to begin work on the structure.”

Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington County, Arlington National Cemetery, and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), today issued the following statement:

“The Administration’s pursuit of Donald Trump’s deeply disrespectful arch has broken the law repeatedly, and now people from many backgrounds are banding together to fight it. I applaud Arlington County’s legal challenge, which rightly confronts the Administration’s illegal attempts to bypass legally required processes to assess the project’s impacts on the local community. Trump wants to avoid these assessments because everyone knows what an honest study would say: this arch is a costly boondoggle that would increase traffic and decrease air safety for the local community. The latter point has also been echoed by workers on the planes that fly in and out of DCA, and the safety concerns would be multiplied many times over if the structure were used as a base for military drones. The bottom line is that Trump’s arch is morally repugnant, and as his pursuit of it gets more corrupt the opposition will continue to grow.”

Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.

title: REP. LAUREN BOEBERT IN THE DAILY CALLER ON SMALL TOWNS DESERVING THEIR OWN ZIP CODES
text:
LONE TREE, CO – Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04) published an op-ed urging Congress to pass her bipartisan bill that would grant unique ZIP codes to dozens of small communities across Colorado and the nation.

“Rural communities are far too often overlooked in Washington; they deserve a voice in Congress, and their local concerns should be turned into practical law,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

Rep. Boebert wrote, “I introduced H.R. 3095, the Unique ZIP Code bill. This legislation would direct the Postal Service to create single, unique ZIP codes for scores of communities that have waited far too long for basic recognition.” H.R. 3095 passed the House with strong bipartisan support.

“Working across the aisle on practical solutions that strengthen our communities is exactly what Coloradans expect from their representatives,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

“Unique ZIP codes are not a symbolic gesture. They are tangible changes that improve mail delivery accuracy, help emergency services respond to the right location, strengthen local identity, support businesses in operating and growing, and ensure that tax and census data accurately reflect the communities that actually exist. For the 73 communities included in this legislation, unique ZIP codes are long-overdue practical relief,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

“And this legislation has garnered support from more than just Colorado’s lawmakers. It is backed in both chambers by a bipartisan coalition of members from 17 states, including California, Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Oklahoma, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and more,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “I will continue to work with my colleagues and Congressional leadership to get this legislation passed and signed into law, so that all local voices continue to be heard.”

title: Buchanan, Moody and Members of the Florida Delegation Urge Department of War to Expand Florida National Guard
text:
Florida Ranks 53rd Out of 54 States and Territories in Guardsmen Per Capita While Carrying One of the Nation’s Heaviest Operational Burdens

Letter Calls to Expand Florida National Guard Personnel to Match Growing Population and Mission

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan joined Senator Ashley Moody (R-Fla.) and 12 other members of the Florida congressional delegation on a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth urging the Department of War to review the Florida National Guard’s authorized force structure and approve an increase in its total allocation of personnel.

The Florida National Guard has roughly 12,000 authorized personnel serving a state of approximately 23.5 million people. Measured per capita, Florida ranks 53rd out of 54 states and territories with a National Guard component, a smaller ratio than states such as Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana, while the Guard carries one of the heaviest operational burdens in the nation.

“Floridians have seen time and time again the importance of our National Guard in stepping up for our families and communities,” said Buchanan. “As an Air National Guard veteran, I have witnessed firsthand how our Guardsmen answer the call every time disaster strikes, but Florida’s Guard has not grown to keep pace with our growing population. They deserve the personnel and resources to match the mission, and I urge the Department of War to give Florida the force structure it needs to continue keeping our communities safe.”

The letter notes that Florida Guardsmen are currently called out 106 days a year, compared with the 39 duty days required by statute, which drives fatigue and strains retention as the same soldiers and airmen are deployed again and again for hurricane response, disaster relief and overseas missions.

The lawmakers also emphasize that Florida is ready to fill the ranks. The Florida National Guard has maintained an average of 103 percent assigned strength over the past five years, and state military leaders have said Florida draws from a recruitable population larger than that of 28 states. In 2025, the Florida Legislature adopted Senate Memorial 314 urging Congress and the National Guard Bureau to examine the Guard’s allocation and allow an increase in its force structure.

Joining Moody, Patronis and Buchanan in signing the letter are Reps. Aaron Bean (R-Fla.), Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.), Mario Diaz-Balart (R-Fla.), Neal Dunn (R-Fla.), Randy Fine (R-Fla.), Scott Franklin (R-Fla.), Carlos Gimenez (R-Fla.), Mike Haridopolos (R-Fla.), Laurel Lee (R-Fla.), Cory Mills (R-Fla.), Jimmy Patronis (R-Fla.) and John Rutherford (R-Fla.).

Buchanan has long been a strong advocate for Florida’s service members and for strengthening the state’s disaster preparedness and response. Earlier this year, he secured 10 amendments in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act.

Read the full letter HERE or below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write to respectfully urge you to conduct a review of the Florida National Guard’s authorized force structure and to approve an increase in its total allocation. The Florida National Guard carries one of the heaviest operational burdens in the nation with one of the smallest per-capita allocations.

Under 10 U.S.C. § 10503, the Secretary of War—in consultation with the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Secretaries of the Army and the Air Force—sets the end strength allocation for the National Guard Bureau. Governor DeSantis, the Florida Legislature, and the Florida National Guard have made clear that the Florida National Guard stands ready to grow.

The Florida National Guard has roughly 12,000 authorized personnel in total. Although the state population is approximately 23.5 million, there are roughly 53 Guardsmen per 10,000 citizens, which is smaller than states such as Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana. Measured per capita, Florida ranks 53rd out of 54 total states and territories that possess a National Guard component.

Reporting has noted that Florida’s total allocation has held at roughly 12,000 for decades even as the state’s population has multiplied several times over.

As Major General John Haas, The Adjutant General of Florida, testified before the State Senate in 2025, Florida is so under- resourced relative to its population that matching the national median ratio of service members to citizens would more than double the Guard’s current force structure.

Florida’s strategic value to the Department of War is unmatched. It plays a critical role in allowing the Joint Force to achieve the administration’s goals set forth in the National Defense Strategy. This is especially true when it comes to homeland defense and ensuring American dominance across the Western Hemisphere. As such, Florida’s impact on executing the objectives of the administration’s priorities is both real and tangible.

The Florida National Guard has one of the highest operational tempos in the country. Earlier this year, state leaders documented that the Florida Guard expended as many workdays in eighteen months as it had in the preceding twenty years.

This was largely driven through the COVID-19 response, hurricane and disaster relief, and overseas deployments. As such, the Florida National Guard has struggled with retention due to high deployment demands, especially since they are currently called out 106 days a year compared to the statutory required 39 duty days.

A force structure frozen in place while both population and mission demand climb steadily forces the repeated redeployment of the same soldiers and airmen, driving fatigue and placing strain on retention.

Florida also offers the Department something that cannot be found in many other states: a deep, willing recruiting base and a demonstrated propensity to serve. State military leadership has publicly stated that Florida draws from a recruitable population larger than that of twenty-eight states and can fill the ranks if given the authorization.

This is backed by sustained performance. The Florida National Guard has maintained an average of 103% assigned strength for the past five years. In short, the demand signal, the strategic rationale, and the manpower supply all point the same direction.

In 2025, the Florida Legislature formally adopted Senate Memorial 314, a memorial to the Congress of the United States urging that the National Guard Bureau examine the present allocations of the Florida National Guard and allow an increase in its force structure.

It cited the National Guard Bureau’s own April 2021 report to Congress, “Impact of U.S. Population Trends on National Guard Force Structure,” which acknowledged that the Guard “may need to evaluate re-allocating mission sets to other geographic areas to keep pace with changing demographics across the country.” Florida’s population trend is precisely the kind of demographic shift the Bureau anticipated.

We are grateful for your service and for your leadership of the Department of War. We kindly ask that the Department give Florida the force structure that is needed to adequately respond to the missions assigned to them. We welcome the opportunity to discuss this further with you at your earliest convenience.

###

title: Congresswoman Bynum Statement on Silver Rail Elementary Shooting
text:
Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) released the following statement following the Silver Rail Elementary School shooting in Bend.

“They’re killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear,” said Rep. Bynum. “I feel this deep, deep, deep in my soul. Our whole community does. Our whole state does.
