title: Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas
text:
AUSTIN, TEXAS – On Thursday, October 15th, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas), alongside Representatives Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and five other members of Congress held a field hearing to investigate the numerous ICE shootings across Texas, including the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez.

Representatives Greg Casar, Bennie G. Thompson, and Pramila Jayapal were joined by Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), Lou Correa (CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), and Al Green (TX-09).

The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.

“Texas has become the epicenter of Trump’s deadly deportation machine, so we brought Members of Congress from across the country to Austin to see it firsthand,” said Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas). “ICE shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez, a DoorDash driver and a father, in the back then denied him medical care. They even tried to deport him so he could never speak the truth. Donald Trump's ICE isn't going after the worst of the worst — it's gone after people like Wilber, who have no criminal record. We will fight to hold the perpetrators in this administration accountable, and not provide another dime in funding to this rogue agency."

“Democrats came to Austin today to demand justice and accountability for Wilber Garcés-Pérez and the others that have been shot by immigration agents in Texas. If Republicans refuse to conduct any oversight of the Trump administration, we must do so in their place,” added Congressman Bennie G. Thompson. “What we heard today was powerful and informative. Make no mistake: we will do everything possible to hold this administration accountable for what it is doing. This violence, lawlessness, and chaos in our communities must end.”

“Twenty-five days ago, ICE agents in Austin, Texas shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez in the back. Instead of taking him to the hospital, they locked him up in a detention center and did not allow him to have surgery for 11 days. This is not the most recent shooting by ICE, and is one of nearly a dozen that we know of since Trump returned to office,” said Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. “ICE is a lawless, rogue agency that is causing generational trauma in communities across the country. House Democrats today are doing the oversight work that Republicans refuse to do — and we will continue to do everything possible to protect our communities from Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”

"The shooting and medical neglect of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez follows the many other cases that have become synonymous with cities being swarmed with masked, armed federal agents and the nation’s dangerous descent into tyranny: Renée Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastian Guerrero, and too many others. No life is meaningless, and each individual assaulted or killed by our immigration system is someone's child, someone's sibling, someone's parent, and they all still belong here with us,” said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. “Unless you’re Native American, we all come from somewhere else. The Trump immigration system is structured and staffed as a deportation machine that violates individuals' constitutional rights. Democrats will fight for an immigration system that honors our history and sets forth a reasonable, compassionate path to citizenship."

“President Trump got elected on the promise to go after the “worst of the worst.” Instead, since January, federal immigration agents have detained over 500 U.S. citizens and killed at least three. ICE is arresting people with no criminal record to hit political quotas while cutting training and lowering hiring standards,” said Congressman Lou Correa. “There is an urgent need for major reforms to keep our communities safe from violence. DHS was created to defend Americans against foreign terrorists. Instead, we have permanent residents and American citizens being shot by ICE agents in our streets.”

"In Texas, we have witnessed at least three ICE shootings since this administration began its aggressive, unprecedented enforcement actions,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “People across our community in Houston are still reeling from the shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Just last weekend, ICE agents ran over and gravely injured Miguel Parra Hernandez while pursuing someone else. ICE's reckless and brutal actions are not only unprecedented, they're unconstitutional. They are making us less safe, creating fear and danger for immigrants and citizens alike. This Republican-led Congress that has enabled this lawlessness has utterly failed Wilber Garcés-Pérez, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Ruben Ray Martinez, and so many others. All Americans deserve better from our government, and that is why I joined Congressman Casar, Ranking Member Thompson, Congresswoman Jayapal, and my Democratic colleagues in Austin today to hear from some of the many people impacted, learn more, and demonstrate our commitment to bringing justice, accountability, and change.”

“Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we’re seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE’s recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead they’ve been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both.

“No President is above the law, and no federal agency should be allowed to serve as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner while operating with impunity,” said Congressman Al Green. “Under President Trump, ICE has been emboldened to use deadly force against people in our communities while the administration evades transparency and accountability, engaging in a cover-up. These shootings are not isolated incidents. They are part of a deeply troubling pattern of conduct that threatens the constitutional rights and lives of people in this country.”

The Members of Congress’ full remarks can be found here.

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.

Castro Nominates 25 Latino Recordings for Preservation in the Library of Congress
text:
SAN ANTONIO, TX— To close out Hispanic Heritage Month, today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) released his annual list of Latino songs, albums, and broadcasts nominated for preservation in the National Recording Registry at the Library of Congress, established in 2000 to preserve recordings with cultural, historic, or aesthetic significance to American life. The Library of Congress adds 25 recordings each year and now holds 700 titles. Yet Latino artists account for fewer than 5 percent of the registry, despite Latinos making up nearly 20 percent of the U.S. population.

This year’s list was shaped by suggestions from the public and adds new nominations from Maná, Julio Iglesias, Los Lobos, Jon Secada, Mazz, and The Royal Jesters. It also renews Rep. Castro’s nomination of the first full-time Spanish-language radio broadcast in the United States, which aired on KCOR in San Antonio in 1946. Congressman Castro is also submitting a separate list of nominations honoring Texas artists.

"It is essential to continue to appropriately include and celebrate the contributions of Latino artists who are part of the American story," Congressman Castro wrote in his nomination letter. "The National Recording Registry’s existence speaks to the importance of preserving music and audio in American culture and society. Latino music’s influence sparks innovation and sways trends across the music industry."

Since Congressman Castro began submitting nominations in 2022, the Library of Congress has inducted 10 titles from his lists. These include Juan Gabriel’s “Amor Eterno,” Héctor Lavoe’s “El Cantante,” Irene Cara’s “Flashdance…What A Feeling,” Daddy Yankee’s “Gasolina,” Vicente Fernández’s “El Rey,” Freddy Fender’s “Before the Next Teardrop Falls,” Lin-Manuel Miranda’s “Hamilton,” and most recently Pérez Prado’s “Mambo No. 5” and José Feliciano’s “Feliz Navidad,” both selected in 2026.

title:
Reps. Castro,
Ciscomani, Espaillat Renew Push to Honor Hispanic-Serving Institutions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congressional Hispanic Caucus Vice Chair of Diversity and Inclusion, Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06), and Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, re-introduced a bipartisan resolution to honor Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs) and uplift their important work shaping the landscape of American higher education.

“Quality education is the foundation of opportunity in this country,” said Congressman Castro (TX-20). “This bipartisan resolution honors the contributions of hundreds of Hispanic-Serving Institutions nationwide, including the 112 such institutions here in Texas. These places of learning empower students and help young people overcome barriers to thrive. I thank the educators, faculty administrators, and staff who work tirelessly each day to ensure that HSIs can support and provide opportunities to millions of students.”

“Hispanic-Serving Institutions are opening doors to opportunity and helping more students achieve the American Dream,” said Congressman Ciscomani (AZ-06). “From Cochise College, Pima Community College, and Eastern Arizona College in my district our three state Universities - UofA, ASU, and NAU, these institutions are giving students, including many who are the first in their families to attend college, a path to a brighter future. I’m proud to support this bipartisan resolution recognizing National Hispanic-Serving Institutions Week and celebrating the vital role these schools play in strengthening Arizona’s communities and workforce.”

“Higher education is a critical pathway to economic opportunity and Hispanic Serving Institutions have opened doors for millions of Latino and Hispanic students to pursue college degrees,” said Congressman Espaillat (NY-13). “New York State is home to nearly 40 two- and four-year HSIs that serve almost 300,000 students. Unfortunately, the massive federal funding cuts and legal attacks from the Trump Administration have left many students and faculty without a clear path forward. This resolution reaffirms our commitment to protecting these communities and HSIs’ crucial work to support Latino and Hispanic students across the nation.”

“During HSIs Week, HACU joins colleges and universities across the country to recognize and raise awareness of the vital work our 645 HSIs do to expand access to education, advance opportunity, promote equity and fairness, and strengthen our communities,” said HACU President and CEO Dr. Antonio Flores.

The resolution uplifts HSIs by:

Recognizing the achievements and goals of Hispanic-Serving Institutions across the United States;

Expressing support for the designation of the week beginning on September 14, 2026, as “National Hispanic-Serving Institutions Week”; and

Calling on the people of the United States and interested groups to observe the week with ceremonies, activities, and programs to demonstrate support for Hispanic-Serving Institutions in honor of Hispanic Heritage Month.

text:

"I am deeply troubled by allegations that the Chinese government conducted a spying operation here in the United States targeting the son and family of President Lai Ching-te. title: Ciscomani Honors Local Heroes at Sixth Veteran Servant Leader Award Ceremony, Meets with Veterans Advisory Council
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani recognized 27 local veterans and a longtime veteran advocate during his sixth Veteran Servant Leader Award Ceremony, celebrating their ongoing dedication to the Southern Arizona community. In addition, Congressman Ciscomani convened his Veterans Advisory Council to provide a legislative update and listen directly to local veterans on the issues impacting them and their families.

"It was truly a privilege to recognize these 27 hometown heroes for their continued service and leadership in our communities. Together, they represent more than 430 years of military service, and their commitment to serving others did not end when they took off the uniform. It was also an honor to recognize a strong veteran advocate in our community who has dedicated decades to supporting Southern Arizona’s veterans,” said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. “I also had the opportunity to meet with my Veterans Advisory Council to hear firsthand about the challenges facing our local veteran community. I will continue bringing these priorities to Washington and fighting to ensure our veterans and their families receive the benefits, resources, and support they have earned.”

The honorees represented Cochise, Graham, Pima, and Pinal counties, with service spanning the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force. Each recipient received an award certificate and challenge coin. Additionally, Vietnam War veterans also received a Vietnam Veteran Lapel Pin in recognition of their service.

For the first time, Ciscomani also presented a posthumous award to honor William Porter. After Porter’s daughter, Linda, sought help obtaining her father’s military medals, the office secured a Presidential Unit Citation Award for presentation to her and continued working to confirm his military rank at separation.

Read local coverage of Ciscomani's sixth Veteran Servant Leader Awards HERE.

Ciscomani represents nearly 80,000 veterans in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District. Since taking office in 2023, his office has returned more than $9 million to local veterans through congressional casework, helping constituents resolve issues involving VA benefits, survivor benefits, and TRICARE. Beyond casework, Ciscomani is advancing legislation to address gaps in veterans’ benefits, education, and health care. He has introduced four veterans-focused bills:

Rural Veterans’ Improved Access to Benefits Act of 2025 (H.R. 3951), which expands the types of licensed health care professionals who can conduct VA disability exams, helping rural veterans access evaluations closer to home.

VETS Opportunity Act (H.R. 1458), which expands Post-9/11 GI Bill education benefits to include hybrid skilled-trade training programs, helping veterans prepare for in-demand careers.

Prioritizing Veterans Survivors Act (H.R. 1228), which strengthens the VA’s Office of Survivor Assistance to better support veterans’ surviving family members.

AIR CARE for Vets Act (H.R. 9666), which establishes a pilot program using advanced four-dimensional functional lung imaging to improve the identification of respiratory disorders and lung diseases linked to military service.

Ranked as the most bipartisan member from the Arizona congressional district, through his work on the House Veterans’ Affairs and Appropriations Committees, Ciscomani is working to ensure veterans have access to the care, benefits, and resources they have earned. By listening directly to veterans, supporting their families, and advancing legislation to address their needs, he remains committed to delivering results for those who have sacrificed so much in service to our nation.

title: Ciscomani Touts $900,000 for Pima Community College STEM Education
text:
TUCSON — Representative Juan Ciscomani returned to his alma mater, Pima Community College, today to spotlight his leadership in preliminarily securing $900,000 in federal funding aimed at expanding workforce training and preparing Pima County students for in-demand STEM careers.

As a first-generation college graduate, Ciscomani understands the transformative power of education. Now serving as Arizona’s sole representative on the House Appropriations Committee, he is dedicated to directing critical federal resources to local institutions like Pima Community College, ensuring students today can access the same life-changing opportunities he experienced.

“Pima Community College helped open doors for me, and I want to make sure the next generation has those same opportunities,” said Rep. Ciscomani. “As Arizona’s sole Appropriator, I’m fighting to deliver $900,000 for Project Catalyst to modernize facilities, expand access to STEM and business programs to better prepare students for the jobs that will drive Arizona’s economy forward. Every single investment I fight for in Congress is targeted where it will have the most impact and help Southern Arizona build the workforce it needs for the future.”

Leaders at Pima Community College are applauding Congressman Ciscomani’s efforts to champion federal investment in workforce initiatives.

"Pima Community College was honored to give Congressman Ciscomani a first-hand view of how the funds he secured will be used to teach our STEM students the skills they need succeed," said Dr. Jeffrey Nasse chancellor of Pima Community College. "Because of the congressman’s position on the House Appropriations Committee, the college's Project Catalyst will be able to use these dollars to support our continuing effort to keep our workforce programs in STEM--including pre-engineering--and business fields up to date and relevant to rapidly changing workforce needs in these fields."

The $900,000 in federal funding would support Project Catalyst, an innovative, industry-driven initiative at Pima Community College designed to strengthen workforce development and drive economic opportunity across the region. This investment will modernize engineering instructional facilities and create flexible HyFlex-enabled classrooms, increasing access to high-demand STEM and business programs. By aligning coursework with current industry needs, Project Catalyst will give students the skills they need to excel in competitive careers, while contributing to Arizona’s long-term economic growth.

This latest effort builds on his ongoing commitment to expanding workforce training opportunities throughout Southern Arizona. In 2024, he secured $2.7 million in federal funding for Pima JTED’s new 50,000-square-foot workforce development center, and he is now advocating for an additional $3 million to support the JTED Workforce Training Center for Technological Innovation. Together, these investments total $5.7 million, expanding hands-on training and preparing local students for high-demand careers.

As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, Representative Ciscomani continues to leverage his leadership to connect students across Arizona’s Sixth District with pathways to in-demand careers. These efforts are helping local employers find skilled workers and ensuring Southern Arizona’s workforce remains competitive for years to come.

title: CLARKE REINTRODUCES REAL POLITICAL ADS ACT TO STRENGTHEN TRANSPARENCY IN AI-GENERATED POLITICAL ADVERTISING
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

October 15, 2026

MEDIA CONTACT:

e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov

c: 202.913.0126

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09) reintroduced the REAL Political Ads Act, legislation to strengthen transparency and accountability in political advertising by requiring disclosure when generative artificial intelligence (AI) is used to create images or videos in political advertisements.

A recent Quinnipiac poll found that 55 percent of Americans are concerned about the growing risks associated with artificial intelligence, and a recent Blue Rose Research poll found that 74 percent of voters believe AI-generated voices should be prohibited in political calls to protect transparency. Those concerns are compounded in the context of the Federal Communications Commission’s proposal to waive the federal ban on unsolicited AI-generated political robocalls, as well as in the widespread use of AI by the Trump Administration and across the political spectrum to attack political opponents and spread disinformation.

“As generative AI technologies continue to evolve, clear disclosure standards to preserve transparency are essential to civic engagement. Unfortunately, Congress has failed to keep up the pace with this rapidly advancing technology, leaving voters vulnerable to AI-generated misinformation and disinformation,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “This legislation would ensure voters know when political ads use AI-generated images and videos. If AI content can manipulate and deceive people on a large scale, it can be a serious threat to our democracy and have devastating consequences for our national and election security.”

“Voters deserve to know that the election information that we read, watch, and listen to is honest. AI makes it far too easy for campaigns to create convincing content intended to mislead voters, and too often it’s at the expense of voters of color and other communities historically pushed to the margins. Congresswoman Clarke’s REAL Political Advertisements Act would help ensure that every voter can make informed decisions based on the facts,” said Alejandra Montoya-Boyer, Vice President of The Leadership Conference’s Center for Civil Rights and Technology.

This legislation is co-sponsored by: Reps. Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Jim Costa (CA-21), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).

title: CORREA, SMITH INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BRIGHT BEGINNINGS ACT TO EXPAND CHILDCARE FOR CHILDREN WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
text:
Bill would create a tax credit of up to $10,000 for childcare providers to purchase specialized equipment; Correa to host "Together on the Spectrum" community event Saturday in Santa Ana

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Lou Correa (D-CA) and Chris Smith (R-NJ) introduced the Bright Beginnings Act, bipartisan legislation that would establish a federal tax credit of up to $10,000 per year for childcare centers and providers to purchase the equipment needed to serve children with developmental disabilities.

“Every child deserves a safe, supportive place to learn and grow, and every parent deserves peace of mind while they work. The Bright Beginnings Act helps childcare providers get the tools they need to welcome children with developmental disabilities, and helps families stay in the workforce without sacrificing their child's care,” said Rep. Correa.

Approximately 1 in 5 children in the United States, or 14.5 million, have special healthcare needs, and 1 in 12 children diagnosed with a developmental disability require specialized support and accommodations. Yet 27 percent of parents of children with disabilities report difficulty finding adequate childcare. Delayed or absent services limit children's development and often force families to cut work hours or leave their jobs entirely, deepening financial strain.

“Parents of children with disabilities go above and beyond to provide for their children, while often shouldering additional economic burdens associated with costs of care. Too often these families are forced between taking care of a loved one and earning a paycheck. The Bright Beginnings tax credit would assist eligible childcare centers and enable them to meet the costs of providing safe and appropriate services for children with disabilities, and peace of mind for their parents who need to work to support them,” said Rep. Smith.

The Bright Beginnings Act encourages childcare centers to invest in specialized equipment and create environments where children can grow and engage in the ways that best suit them. Specifically, the bill:

Establishes a federal tax credit of up to $10,000 per year for eligible providers

Covers qualifying expenditures for equipment that accommodates children with developmental disabilities

Expands access to specialized care for families who are struggling to find it

“Access to high-quality, inclusive child care can make a meaningful difference in the lives of children with autism and their families, yet too many providers lack the resources needed to create fully accessible and supportive environments where every child can thrive,” said Keith Wargo, President and CEO of Autism Speaks. “We are grateful for Representative Correa's leadership in introducing the Bright Beginnings Act and recognizing the importance of ensuring child care settings are equipped to serve children with autism and other developmental disabilities. By promoting access and innovation in child care settings, this legislation would help providers strengthen their ability to support children with autism - expanding their opportunities to learn, develop and thrive alongside their peers from the very start.”

“Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, play, and thrive in a supportive childcare environment. Tax credits that help providers invest in accommodations for Autistic children and children with developmental disabilities can reduce financial barriers and expand access to inclusive care. The Autism Society of America applauds this legislation and its commitment to helping more children participate, connect, and reach their full potential,” said Joseph Joyce, President and CEO of the Autism Society of America.

The bill is endorsed by Access Ready Inc., Autism Speaks, Autism Society of America, Easterseals, TDI for Access, and The Learning Disabilities Association for America.

View the bill text here.

Together on the Spectrum

In conjunction with the bill's introduction, Rep. Correa will host Together on the Spectrum this Saturday in Santa Ana. The event grew out of Rep. Correa's desire to create a space to bring children and families together. The free community event is open to neurodivergent youth ages 5–18 and their families, and will feature activities and information on autism and neurodiversity, Regional Center services, family support and advocacy, therapy and developmental services, and safety and emergency preparedness. Federal resources will also be available. Participating organizations include Corazones Especiales, Regional Center of Orange County, Santa Ana PD, TACA (The Autism Community in Action), United Across Borders Foundation, Easterseals, and the Orange County Children's Therapeutic Arts Center, among others.

Press interested in attending should RSVP to krislyn.tatum@mail.house.gov.

title: Rep. Costa Leads Bipartisan Push for Full Implementation of Graham Russia Sanctions Law
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, joined Co-Chairs of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Representatives Mike Quigley (IL-05), Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Joe Wilson (SC-02) in leading a bipartisan letter urging President Trump to fully implement the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026ahead of its first enforcement deadline on October 18. The lawmakers called on the Administration to strengthen economic pressure on Russia, cut off revenue financing Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine, and bring Russia to the negotiating table.

“As Russia prepares to wage a fifth winter campaign against Ukraine, the United States has an opportunity to reinvigorate peace efforts by placing maximum pressure on Vladimir Putin and the governments and networks that finance his war,” the lawmakers wrote. “Utilizing the tools for economic pressure in this law will be decisive in forcing Putin to take peace talks seriously.”

In the letter, the lawmakers urged the Administration to:

Fully enforce mandatory sanctions against Russian officials, oligarchs, banks, state enterprises, and foreign entities helping Russia evade existing restrictions.

Impose secondary tariffs on major purchasers of Russian energy, targeting revenue from oil and gas sales that continues to finance Russia’s war.

Crack down on sanctions evasion, including foreign financial institutions, shadow fleet operators, and intermediaries facilitating Russian energy transactions.

Protect U.S. allies by applying exceptions and tariff adjustments for countries actively reducing their dependence on Russian energy.

Strengthen congressional oversight by providing implementation details, tariff justifications, and measurable benchmarks to assess the effectiveness of sanctions.

The lawmakers emphasized that Russia continues to rely heavily on oil and gas exports to finance its military operations, while intensifying attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Black Sea, threatening global food security. The letter also calls on the Administration to reverse course in issuing general licenses that could reopen Russian energy transactions and restore revenue to the Kremlin. The lawmakers requested answers ahead of the October 18 deadline on which sanctions and tariffs will be implemented, whether any provisions will be delayed or waived, and how the Administration will measure their effectiveness.

The letter was signed by Don Bacon; Sanford Bishop; Salud Carbajal; Ed Case; Steve Cohen; Jim Costa; Danny Davis; Madeleine Dean; Brian Fitzpatrick; Jared Golden; Josh Gottheimer; Steny Hoyer; Marcy Kaptur; John Mannion; Michael McCaul; Robert Menendez; Dan Newhouse; Mike Quigley; Melanie Stansbury; Dina Titus; Jill Tokuda; and Joe Wilson.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Easing Russian Sanctions
text:

title: Davids Demands Accountability Following ICE Sweeps in Southwest Kansas, Citing Threats to Ag Economy and Grocery Prices
text:
Today, Representative Sharice Davids called on Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to answer for the economic fallout of recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforcement sweeps in southwest Kansas. Davids highlighted the severe disruption to Kansas’ agricultural economy, local small businesses, and food supply chains following sudden enforcement sweeps, which could raise beef and grocery prices.

"I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent... ICE operations in western Kansas... where sudden enforcement sweeps... immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region,” wrote Davids. “While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform... we need immediate accountability. I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic."

Recent federal enforcement operations in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, sparking widespread panic across southwest Kansas — a crucial hub responsible for more than 20 percent of the nation’s daily cattle slaughter.

The abrupt operations severely disrupted local meatpacking plants, causing a nearly 16 percent single-day drop in fed-cattle slaughter and an overall 8.5 percent week-to-week decline, according to USDA reports. Local businesses were forced to temporarily close their doors, while union representatives and economists warned that halting plant operations will drive beef prices far beyond ground beef's already elevated $7.16-per-pound average.

Major Kansas agricultural organizations have voiced sharp criticisms of the uncoordinated federal actions:

"These ICE operations are having a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving. Additionally, these types of disruptions will lead to higher beef prices for consumers… These disruptions come at a time of enhanced focus and pressure on the cattle and beef supply chain. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain. Frustratingly, the harm these actions cause to cattle producers last for days and weeks after such operations conclude.” — Kansas Livestock Association

“Kansas dairy farms depend on a reliable workforce to provide consistent, around-the-clock care for animals. Recent [ICE] enforcement activity has created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. We urge federal officials to carry out enforcement actions in a lawful, orderly, and transparent manner that respects due process and provides clear, timely communication to affected employers, workers, local law enforcement, and communities.” — Kansas Dairy Association

Read Davids’ full letter here or below

Dear Secretary Mullin,

I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations in western Kansas, where sudden enforcement sweeps in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, and immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region.

I believe in the importance of enforcing federal immigration laws and protecting Kansas families from crime. In this instance, however, I have heard concerns from agriculture and business stakeholders about how these activities were conducted and their impact on communities across the state. Kansans have shared with me several instances of citizens and documented persons being targeted on their way to work or going about their day, and in many cases, local law enforcement was not consulted.

Southwest Kansas is a crucial hub for American agriculture – home to more than 20 percent of the country’s daily cattle slaughter. ICE’s activities corresponded with an 8.5 percent drop in cattle slaughter week-to-week according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture as meatpacking capacity was significantly disrupted. The Kansas Livestock Association stated last month that these operations, “[had] a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving…. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain.”

This comes as Americans are struggling with staggeringly high grocery prices – including the price of ground beef jumping 7.9 percent year-to-year – and the smallest cattle herd in decades.

The immigration enforcement efforts also delivered a notable hit to Kansas’ dairy industry, which accounts for more than $3 billion in economic impact and 11,000 jobs statewide. The Kansas Dairy Association shared that ICE’s activities, “created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States.”

While your agency frames these multi-day September 2026 operations as targeted at individuals with criminal histories, the immediate fallout has inflicted severe collateral damage on southwest Kansas’s economy, national food supply chains, and working families already struggling at the checkout counter. In addition to notable impacts on the agriculture sector, ICE’s activities led to local business closures and school absences.

These extreme actions leave Kansans feeling less safe, strain local economies, and disrupt national supply chains. While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform – securing our border against violent crime and drug trafficking while supporting our agricultural sector – we need immediate accountability.

I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic.

Sincerely,

title: DelBene Leads Bipartisan Scrutiny of Meta’s Data Center Tax Credits
text:
Today, Representatives Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Greg Steube (FL-17), and Mike Thompson (CA-04) led an effort expressing concerns about reports that Meta is seeking to use the federal research tax credit for its data center buildout. In a bipartisan letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the lawmakers emphasized that any claims by Meta for the federal research tax credit must meet the clearly defined requirements.

Congress established this tax credit in 1981 amid concerns about declining private-sector research investment and U.S. global technological competitiveness. By reducing the cost of qualifying research, the credit is meant to encourage businesses to pursue projects involving technical uncertainty and experimentation, rather than simply purchasing and deploying proven technology.

“We are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit,” wrote the lawmakers. “The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.”

To qualify for the credit, research must meet a four-part test, including being technological in nature, addressing technical uncertainty, seeking to develop or improve a product or process, and involving a process of experimentation. Certain activities, including research conducted after commercial production begins and duplication of an existing product or process, are excluded. The lawmakers emphasized that the scale or configuration of a data center does not, by itself, establish that its construction and equipment costs qualify.

“Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business,” continued the lawmakers.

“The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment,” concluded the lawmakers.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), John James (MI-10), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Victoria Spartz (IN-05), Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).

title: Leger Fernández Introduces Bill to Hold ICE Accountable for Arrests and Detentions of U.S. Citizens
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) introduced the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act to make sure American citizens wrongfully arrested or detained by immigration enforcement officers can fight back in court. Her legislation would prevent individual officers and the government from claiming qualified or sovereign immunity to avoid accountability and give individuals five years to sue. It would also require courts to award successful plaintiffs $500,000, plus $100,000 for each additional day of detention after the first day.

“ICE does not get to trample on your rights and walk away without consequence. They cannot hide behind their masks and act like they have a license to break the Constitution,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. “Our government has handcuffed, hauled away, and locked up more than 500 American citizens. Citizens have been deported — including Brian Garcia Morales, who spent four months trying to get home. ICE is proving that nobody is safe from their handcuffs — and that is the purpose, to terrorize our Latino and immigrant communities. My bill is about justice for those Americans and accountability for the officers and a government who violate Americans’ rights.”

A ProPublica investigation documented 506 U.S. citizens detained by immigration agents since the start of the second Trump administration, including children and Americans detained while recording enforcement operations. The reporting underscores the urgent need for a clear path to accountability when officers violate citizens’ rights.

Leger Fernández’s legislation would allow U.S. citizens arrested or detained without a warrant or without probable cause to sue the officers involved and the United States in federal court. It would remove immunity defenses that can shield officers and the government from liability under current law.

Specifically, the legislation would:

Give American citizens a path to justice if immigration officers or other officers enforcing immigration laws arrest or detain them after January 20, 2025, without probable cause or a warrant.

Prevent officers from claiming absolute or qualified immunity and waive the federal government’s sovereign immunity for these lawsuits.

Require $500,000 in damages for successful plaintiffs, plus $100,000 for each day of detention after the initial day, reasonable attorney’s fees, and appropriate injunctive relief.

Give citizens five years to bring a claim, while preserving their ability to seek compensation under other laws. Currently, a person bringing a case under the Federal Tort Claims Act only has two years to act.

Rescind remaining unobligated ICE funding provided under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

title: Rep. Garbarino, Kean, and Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Address Fentanyl Crisis
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (NY-02), Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07), Congressman Jeff Van Drew (NJ-02), and Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) introduced the Fight Against Fentanyl Act, a bill to permit the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) to be used for the purchase of fentanyl testing kits and opioid reversal agents by law enforcement agencies.

The Byrne JAG grant program is the leading source of federal funding to state and local police jurisdictions. The Fight Against Fentanyl Act would amend the Byrne JAG program to allow state and local police agencies to purchase fentanyl test kits and opioid reversal agents using federal funds.

“Fentanyl continues to devastate families and communities on Long Island and across the country. I’m proud to join Congressman Kean in leading the Fight Against Fentanyl Act to ensure law enforcement has access to the tools they need to combat this deadly drug and save lives,” said Congressman Garbarino.

“Access to fentanyl testing kits and opioid reversal agents is essential to prevent overdoses and deaths,” said Congressman Kean. “It is essential that we get first responders the tools they need to combat this deadly epidemic. I am pleased to work with Representatives Van Drew, Garbarino, and Lawler to introduce this legislation to take steps towards safeguarding communities from the devastating impact of fentanyl.”

"Fentanyl is different from anything we have dealt with before because such a small amount can be deadly,” said Congressman Van Drew. “We have to attack this problem from every direction. The Fight Against Fentanyl Act is one piece of that by helping local law enforcement use existing federal grant dollars for fentanyl testing kits and overdose reversal drugs. If there is something we can put in the hands of our police officers that can help catch fentanyl or save somebody’s life, they should have it.”

“Substance use disorder and fentanyl are destroying families across the country, and we must work together at every level to combat this crisis. This legislation gives law enforcement the resources they need by allowing Byrne JAG grants to fund fentanyl testing kits and lifesaving opioid reversal agents that can mean the difference between life and death. I was proud to support this legislation last Congress, and I will continue working to give our communities the tools they need to fight back,” said Congressman Lawler.

Congressman Garbarino has consistently worked to support local law enforcement and ensure officers have the resources they need to keep Long Island communities safe. As Chairman of the House Committee on Homeland Security, he has made combating illicit drug trafficking, including the flow of deadly fentanyl into the United States, a top priority. He continues to advocate for border security and increased support for law enforcement to combat the fentanyl crisis and protect families on Long Island and across the country.

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Target Scammers who Prey on Older Americans
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — This week, Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Tom Barrett (MI-07) introduced the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act, a piece of legislation designed to streamline the reporting process for elder fraud. This bill will create an inter-agency framework to give law enforcement and prosecutors better information to fight fraud.

Reporting fraud is the first step to recovering stolen funds or preventing other would-be victims from falling prey to the same scam. Right now, there are ten federal agencies, most with their own separate intake channels, and a poorly coordinated set of federal reporting sites, plus 50+ state portals, with no single number to call and no designated first-click destination. As a result, fraud reporting is an overly complicated process that handicaps law enforcement efforts to quickly respond and, in some cases, recover stolen funds. This legislation will address these barriers.

Specifically, this legislation would:

Designate a single front door for elder-fraud reporting, reachable two ways, by phone and on the web, to route each request to the federal agency whose mandate fits.

The hotline should answer 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The website should also include digital resources for combatting the most common types of scams.

The new reporting framework would be similar to VSAFE, introduced by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs in 2024 to create a single number and website specifically for veterans to report fraud, scams, and predatory practices.

“People who steal from seniors and retirees are the lowest of the low. No one should have to navigate impenetrable government websites or spend hours stuck on hold trying to report these scams,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “ My bill makes it simple, you call one number or go to one site and your report goes directly to the investigator you need. When we give law enforcement the tools to fight back, they can respond immediately and take on these predatory scammers.”

“Fraudsters are constantly targeting seniors to cheat them out of their hard-earned retirement. These sophisticated scammers pose as federal agencies, banks, and even loved ones, while artificial intelligence is making impersonation easier than ever,” said Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07). “Families need resources to recognize and quickly report suspected fraud. By establishing a 24/7, one-stop shop for addressing elder fraud, this bipartisan bill will protect vulnerable seniors and empower law enforcement to crack down on these criminals.”

“When an older American falls victim to fraud, every minute counts. Yet victims and families are often left navigating a fragmented reporting system when they need help the most. No one should have to figure out which government agency to call while their life savings are at risk. By establishing a single national entry point, available around the clock, the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act of 2026 represents an important step toward protecting older Americans.”

Yuksel Aydin, Director of the anti-scam website seniors.hcsk.org

“Reporting a scam should be as simple as one click or one call. But today, older adults who’ve been scammed face a maze of reporting options, leaving them unsure where to turn and often not reporting at all. Combating fraud requires a system that makes it easy for people to report scams and for authorities to track them. By creating one front door, a single website, and hotline, the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act would give the growing number of older adults targeted by scammers the help they deserve.”

Ramsey Alwin, President and CEO, National Council on Aging

During the appropriations process this year, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez advanced multiple provisions targeting scammers and helping working families keep their hard-earned money. This included encouraging the Department of Justice to pursue further action against crypto scams targeting older Americans and instructing law enforcement to work across jurisdictions to combat fraud and scams.

The legislation is supported by the National Council on Aging and seniors.hsck.org.

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Visits Ukrainian Community in Ramsey, Slams Appeasement of Dictator Putin, Calls for TPS Extension to Keep Ukrainian Families Safe
text:
Above: Gottheimer Visits St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church in Ramsey.

RAMSEY, NJ — Today, Thursday, October 15, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) visited St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church in Ramsey, where he met with parishioners and faith leaders from North Jersey’s Ukrainian community. He discussed his support for Ukrainian families in the Fifth District, the urgent need to extend Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Ukrainians living in the United States, and America’s continued commitment to standing with Ukraine in its war with Russia.He also slammed the Trump Administration’s appeasement of dictator Vladimir Putin, including its new deal to import Russian diesel.

“North Jersey’s Ukrainian community has shown incredible strength, faith, and generosity, and they have my full support. We must extend TPS so Ukrainian families here are not sent back into a war zone, and we must keep standing with Ukraine as it fights for freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. America’s commitment to Ukraine cannot waver,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).

TPS for Ukrainians is currently set to expire on Monday, October 19, 2026, which puts at risk neighbors, workers, and students who fled amid Russia’s invasion and have since built lives here. Congressman Gottheimer called on the Administration to extend TPS protections so these families are not forced to return to an active war zone.

Gottheimer also criticized the Trump Administration’s new deal with Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel. It comes just weeks after the President signed the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which Gottheimer supported, that Congress passed to choke off the energy revenues that fund Putin’s war. Gottheimer argued that the deal breaks our own laws and hands Putin’s war machine a lifeline funded by American taxpayers.

The Congressman also reaffirmed his support for Ukraine abroad. He stressed that the United States must continue to back Ukraine’s defense against Russian aggression and stand firmly with its people.

Gottheimer was joined by Maria Keniuk, Church Trustee; Irene and Victor Hurlinsky; Jed Sunden, Director of the American Ukraine Committee and the American Ukraine PAC; Jackie Colgan, American Association for Ukraine; Oleksandr Tran, President of Svitanok; Anna Move, President and Co-Founder of the Leonid Foundation; and Tanya Khapko, Mike and Oksana Dyakiv, Ivan Durbak, and Nadiya Dovhan, members of St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church.

text:

title: Hayes, Dingell Introduce Bill to Hold Schools Accountable for Mishandling Reports of Sexual Assault
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05) joined Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) to introduce the Title IX Take Responsibility Act, legislation that would hold schools accountable for mishandling reports of sexual assault and provide survivors a stronger path towards justice.

The legislation amends Title IX; a U.S. federal civil rights law passed as part of the Education Amendments of 1972 that bans sex-based discrimination in any education program or activity receiving federal money. The bill would reform how schools handle sexual assault and harassment by replacing outdated legal loopholes with clear accountability.

"One incident of sexual violence is one too many," said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes. "I am committed to protecting students, supporting survivors, and ensuring college campuses are safe learning environments for all. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act will put the responsibility on educational institutions for any mishandling of sexual assault reporting and failure to prevent further assaults. This legislation should be considered immediately, and I thank Congresswoman Dingell for partnering on this effort."

"For far too long, outdated legal loopholes have allowed educational institutions to turn a blind eye to reports of sexual assault, leaving survivors without justice or support," said Congresswoman Dingell. "Title IX was enacted to protect students, not to shield institutions from accountability when they fail to keep campuses safe. This bill closes these gaps and ensures that every student has access to a safe learning environment free from abuse."

Under current Supreme Court precedents, schools can only be held liable if high-level officials had "actual notice" and reacted with "deliberate indifference," creating an incentive for institutions to turn a blind eye. This bill eliminates that defense by holding schools legally responsible if they knew or reasonably should have known about the abuse and failed to take effective action. It also expands access to justice by allowing survivors to hold schools accountable in federal court for monetary damages and legal fees.

The legislation is endorsed by End Rape on Campus, Just Solutions, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence (NAESV), National Organization for Victim Advocacy (NOVA), Ujima, Volare, YWCA,

Survivors should never have to choose between their safety and their education. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act affirms survivors’ rights to support, to make their own choices about reporting, and to seek justice when their access to education is harmed. It also gives schools clear standards that reflect what effective, survivor-centered response looks like. NOVA strongly supports this bill,” said Claire Ponder Selib, Executive Director, National Organization for Victim Advocacy.

"Schools must take sexual misconduct more seriously. We're abandoning survivors and ignoring the enormous impact of sexual violence on their educational attainment, health, and quality of life. This is unacceptable. The National Alliance to End Sexual Violence applauds Representatives Dingell and Hayes for re-introducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. We must have more accountability," said Monika Johnson-Hostler, President & CEO, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence.

“YWCA USA is unwavering in our pursuit of a world where all women and girls can thrive. To meet that mission, it is essential that every student can learn in an environment free from sexual violence. Sadly, we know that violence does occur. The deeply disturbing reports from Cornell University underscore that passing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is an essential and overdue step that would hold our educational institutions more responsible for protecting students from the start and accessing swift, meaningful pathways to justice and healing,” said Kate Kasper, VP of Public Policy and Advocacy, YWCA USA.

“I’m grateful to Reps. Dingell and Hayes for reintroducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. At moment when the Dept of Education is rolling back protections under Title IX and leaving survivors of sexual violence vulnerable, this bill would strengthen protections and where appropriate, hold institutions accountable,” said Lisalyn Jacobs, CEO of Just Solutions.

“Survivors should not have to sacrifice their education because an institution failed to respond meaningfully to sexual harassment or violence. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act strengthens survivors’ ability to enforce their rights and recognizes that students should be able to access meaningful support without being required to pursue an investigation. Survivors deserve options that protect their safety, well-being, and ability to continue their education,” said Volare CEO Bridgette Stumpf.

title: Hudson Highlights Innovation, School Safety Technology at UNC Greensboro
text:
GREENSBORO, N.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Representative Richard Hudson (NC-09) visited UNC Greensboro, where he met with Chancellor Franklin D. Gilliam Jr. to discuss the university’s work in defense, energy, and workforce development, including its iCOMMAND Project and BRIGHT Institute.

“Lives are being changed every day at UNC Greensboro. They are also doing some exciting work that can make a real difference for our country,” said Rep. Hudson. “From supporting our servicemembers and veterans to developing new energy technology, there is a lot happening at UNCG. I appreciated Chancellor Gilliam taking the time to bring me up to speed on the work they’re doing.”

Following the meeting, Hudson visited the UNCG Police Department for a demonstration of ZeroEyes, an artificial intelligence and human-verified security system founded by former Navy SEALs designed to detect visible firearms and quickly alert authorities. ZeroEyes does not use facial recognition technology and is designed to protect public safety without targeting law-abiding gun owners.

“As one of the strongest supporters of the Second Amendment in Congress and someone who has worked to make our schools safer, I believe we can protect our rights and give law enforcement better tools to stop violence before it happens,” said Rep. Hudson. “I appreciated getting to see this technology and learning how ZeroEyes is working to keep people safe without using facial recognition or targeting law-abiding gun owners.”

“We’re grateful to Rep. Hudson for joining us and to the UNCG Police Department for hosting today’s demonstration. Their officers take protecting this campus seriously, and we’re proud to work alongside them,” said Mike Lahiff, CEO and co-founder of ZeroEyes. “We created ZeroEyes to give police an earlier warning and a chance to act before someone gets hurt. That’s why we do this, and it’s what keeps our team working around the clock.”

Background

UNCG serves roughly 19,000 students and offers more than 150 undergraduate and over 200 master’s and doctoral programs.

Hudson previously visited UNCG in November 2025 to learn more about the university’s iCOMMAND Project and BRIGHT Institute.

The iCOMMAND Project conducts research and develops technology to protect, train, and support military personnel, veterans, and their families. Its work includes advanced manufacturing, health and physical resilience, bio-industrial manufacturing, and efforts connecting academic research with the DEVCOM Soldier Center and helping servicemembers transition into civilian careers.

The BRIGHT Institute focuses on helping make North Carolina a leader in next-generation energy and battery technology by bringing together research, industry, and workforce development.

ZeroEyes was founded by former Navy SEALs and uses artificial intelligence with human verification to detect visible firearms through existing security cameras. The technology does not use facial recognition, does not identify people based on clothing, skin tone, or other personal characteristics, and is designed to detect illegally brandished firearms rather than target lawful gun owners. When a potential weapon is flagged, a trained specialist reviews the image before an alert is sent to first responders and local officials.

title: Gov Watchdog Finds National Security Gaps in Mining of Critical Minerals on America’s Public Lands
text:
GAO could not confirm that seven of 15 sampled mining companies were incorporated in the United States, finds major gaps in what the government knows about foreign investment in mining on federal lands

Washington, D.C. – As the United States races to reduce its reliance on foreign countries for critical minerals, the federal government has been handing out exclusive rights to mine America’s public lands without checking whether the people and companies receiving those rights meet the requirements to hold them, even allowing companies with ties to our adversaries to mine our public lands according to two new Government Accountability Office (GAO) reports released today by Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.).

"Our mining laws date back to 1872, and we’re still running the system like it’s the Wild West. We’ve somehow managed to hand out mining claims for generations without doing the most basic homework on who gets to hold them. And for all of Trump’s tough talk about China, he seems awfully comfortable inviting foreign-owned mining companies onto Americans’ public lands without checking who’s backing them. Congress needs to modernize our mining laws and bring some basic accountability to who profits from our public lands,” said Ranking Member Huffman.

Federal law reserves mining claims on public lands for U.S. citizens and companies incorporated in the United States. The Bureau of Land Management, which runs the mining claim system, does not collect citizenship information from claimants, does not record whether they qualify, and rarely checks in the first place. A BLM official told GAO that companies from foreign adversary nations could hold claims on federal lands through U.S. subsidiaries, and claimants do not have to disclose whether a foreign company or government owns part of them.

When GAO reviewed a sample of 15 companies holding mining claims, investigators found no evidence that seven of them were incorporated in the United States, as the law requires. When GAO asked BLM for help confirming where these companies were incorporated, the agency had no additional information to offer.

In a second report, GAO reviewed ownership information for 43 operators of critical minerals mines on federal lands and found that at least 25 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. In at least two cases, Chinese entities had a financial interest in the parent companies.

Mining claims grant the exclusive right to extract minerals such as copper and gold, royalty-free, for as long as the holder pays annual fees. Claimants do not have to disclose whether a foreign company or government owns part of them. Australia and Canada, two of the world’s top mineral producers, require foreign investors to disclose their owners and have forced some to sell stakes in critical minerals companies on national security grounds.

GAO recommends that the Bureau of Land Management collect citizenship information from mining claimants and document that they qualify.

Read the GAO’s first report about citizenship requirements here.

Read the GAO’s second report about information on foreign investment here.

Background

The United States depends heavily on foreign countries for critical minerals such as copper and lithium, which go into everything from electric vehicle batteries and power lines to phones and medical equipment. GAO has warned that this dependence leaves supply chains open to disruption by adversary nations. Federal lands cover nearly one-third of the country and are a significant source of these minerals.

Under the General Mining Act of 1872, individuals and companies stake claims on most federal lands without agency approval, and BLM has recorded an average of more than 60,000 new claims every year since 2021. Since 2025, President Trump has issued a series of executive orders to expand mining on federal lands and cut reliance on foreign minerals. GAO’s findings show his administration has not taken the most basic step to keep those minerals in the right hands: confirming who holds the claims and preventing our adversaries from taking our resources. A secure domestic supply of critical minerals starts with knowing who controls the mines on public lands.

title: Smith Leads Lawmakers in Urging USDA to Mitigate Impact of Theileria on U.S. Cattle Industry
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08), Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, recently led a group of lawmakers in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins urging the Department to expand and prioritize research on Theileria orientalis Ikeda and related tick-borne livestock diseases.

“We write to express our increasing concern regarding the rapid spread of Theileria orientalis Ikeda, a disease carried primarily by the invasive Asian longhorned tick. Since its first detection in the United States in 2017, this tick has spread to more than 20 states and continues to expand its range each year. This emerging disease poses a growing threat to the cattle industry. This industry, and the rural communities that depend on it, cannot absorb an unchecked, spreading disease with no approved treatment. We are urging USDA to prioritize additional research and surveillance to better understand and mitigate its impacts on the U.S. cattle industry,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Land-grant universities across the country, including the University of Missouri, the University of Arkansas, Virginia Tech, and Kansas State University, have worked diligently to track this disease, confirm new cases, and educate ranchers on prevention. However, surveillance and outreach alone cannot substitute for a vaccine or effective treatment, and it should not fall to individual states to carry the full weight of researching a disease that has been detected in a growing number of states across the country,” the letter continues.

Other lawmakers who signed onto the letter include Congresswoman Ann Wagner (MO-02), Congressman Bob Onder (MO-03), Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04), Congressman Rick Crawford (AR-01), Congressman Randy Feenstra (IA-04), Congressman Mark Messmer (IN-08), Congressman Tracey Mann (KS-01), Congressman Derek Schmidt (KS-02), Congressman Don Bacon (NE-02), Congressman Adrian Smith (NE-03), and Congressman John Rose (TN-06).

title: Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas
text:
AUSTIN, TEXAS – On Thursday, October 15th, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas), alongside Representatives Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and five other members of Congress held a field hearing to investigate the numerous ICE shootings across Texas, including the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez.

Representatives Greg Casar, Bennie G. Thompson, and Pramila Jayapal were joined by Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), Lou Correa (CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), and Al Green (TX-09).

The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.

“Texas has become the epicenter of Trump’s deadly deportation machine, so we brought Members of Congress from across the country to Austin to see it firsthand,” said Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas). “ICE shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez, a DoorDash driver and a father, in the back then denied him medical care. They even tried to deport him so he could never speak the truth. Donald Trump’s ICE isn’t going after the worst of the worst — it’s gone after people like Wilber, who have no criminal record. We will fight to hold the perpetrators in this administration accountable, and not provide another dime in funding to this rogue agency.”

“Democrats came to Austin today to demand justice and accountability for Wilber Garcés-Pérez and the others that have been shot by immigration agents in Texas. If Republicans refuse to conduct any oversight of the Trump administration, we must do so in their place,” added Congressman Bennie G. Thompson. “What we heard today was powerful and informative. Make no mistake: we will do everything possible to hold this administration accountable for what it is doing. This violence, lawlessness, and chaos in our communities must end.”

“Twenty-five days ago, ICE agents in Austin, Texas shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez in the back. Instead of taking him to the hospital, they locked him up in a detention center and did not allow him to have surgery for 11 days. This is not the most recent shooting by ICE, and is one of nearly a dozen that we know of since Trump returned to office,” said Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. “ICE is a lawless, rogue agency that is causing generational trauma in communities across the country. House Democrats today are doing the oversight work that Republicans refuse to do — and we will continue to do everything possible to protect our communities from Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”

“The shooting and medical neglect of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez follows the many other cases that have become synonymous with cities being swarmed with masked, armed federal agents and the nation’s dangerous descent into tyranny: Renée Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastian Guerrero, and too many others. No life is meaningless, and each individual assaulted or killed by our immigration system is someone’s child, someone’s sibling, someone’s parent, and they all still belong here with us,” said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. “Unless you’re Native American, we all come from somewhere else. The Trump immigration system is structured and staffed as a deportation machine that violates individuals’ constitutional rights. Democrats will fight for an immigration system that honors our history and sets forth a reasonable, compassionate path to citizenship.”

“President Trump got elected on the promise to go after the “worst of the worst.” Instead, since January, federal immigration agents have detained over 500 U.S. citizens and killed at least three. ICE is arresting people with no criminal record to hit political quotas while cutting training and lowering hiring standards,” said Congressman Lou Correa. “There is an urgent need for major reforms to keep our communities safe from violence. DHS was created to defend Americans against foreign terrorists. Instead, we have permanent residents and American citizens being shot by ICE agents in our streets.”

“In Texas, we have witnessed at least three ICE shootings since this administration began its aggressive, unprecedented enforcement actions,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “People across our community in Houston are still reeling from the shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Just last weekend, ICE agents ran over and gravely injured Miguel Parra Hernandez while pursuing someone else. ICE’s reckless and brutal actions are not only unprecedented, they’re unconstitutional. They are making us less safe, creating fear and danger for immigrants and citizens alike. This Republican-led Congress that has enabled this lawlessness has utterly failed Wilber Garcés-Pérez, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Ruben Ray Martinez, and so many others. All Americans deserve better from our government, and that is why I joined Congressman Casar, Ranking Member Thompson, Congresswoman Jayapal, and my Democratic colleagues in Austin today to hear from some of the many people impacted, learn more, and demonstrate our commitment to bringing justice, accountability, and change.”

“Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we’re seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE’s recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead they’ve been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both.

“No President is above the law, and no federal agency should be allowed to serve as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner while operating with impunity,” said Congressman Al Green. “Under President Trump, ICE has been emboldened to use deadly force against people in our communities while the administration evades transparency and accountability, engaging in a cover-up. These shootings are not isolated incidents. They are part of a deeply troubling pattern of conduct that threatens the constitutional rights and lives of people in this country.”
