title: Kiggans, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. Discuss Healthcare Workforce Challenges, Tour Regional Health Professions Center at TCC
text:
VIRGINIA BEACH, VA — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) welcomed U.S. Department of Health & Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to Virginia’s Second District for a tour of Tidewater Community College’s (TCC) Regional Health Professions Center and a healthcare roundtable with local professionals and industry stakeholders. The visit focused on addressing the healthcare workforce shortage and improving recruitment and retention, as well as expanding access to high-quality healthcare throughout the region.

Prior to the roundtable, Congresswoman Kiggans and Secretary Kennedy toured the Regional Health Professions Center to see firsthand how TCC is educating and training the next generation of healthcare professionals. The facility opened in 2012 and boasts state-of-the-art medical equipment to give students hands-on experience to prepare them for a variety of jobs in the healthcare field.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As a geriatric nurse practitioner, access to quality, efficient care starts with having a competent and well-trained workforce. Every day, TCC is preparing the next generation of young men and women to enter the healthcare profession with the skills and experience they need to succeed. As staffing shortages continue to impact communities across our nation, investing in these programs is critical to ensure patients receive the timely care they deserve. I’m grateful to Secretary Kennedy for visiting Coastal Virginia to see firsthand the important role institutions like TCC play in preparing students for the real-world challenges of patient care.”

Following the tour, Congresswoman Kiggans and Secretary Kennedy participated in a roundtable discussion with local healthcare professionals and industry stakeholders to hear about the challenges facing Coastal Virginia’s healthcare workforce.

“These conversations inform the work I do in Washington every day,” said Kiggans. “These men and women have firsthand experience training future healthcare professionals, and it’s incredibly important that we hear their concerns to ensure they have the resources they need to succeed. I’m thankful to Secretary Kennedy for coming to Virginia’s Second District, and I look forward to continuing to work with the Secretary and HHS to identify practical solutions that address the challenges facing our healthcare professionals and the patients they serve.”

As a geriatric nurse practitioner and Vice Co-Chair of the Congressional Nursing Caucus, Congresswoman Kiggans remains committed to supporting legislation and initiatives that strengthen healthcare education and workforce development.

Background:

In May 2025, Rep. Kiggans joined her Congressional Nursing Caucus colleagues in introducing the Title VIII Nursing Workforce Reauthorization Act of 2025, a bill to address the national nursing workforce shortage by supporting educational programs across the country. Read the press release here.

In May 2025, Rep. Kiggans introduced the Magnifying Opportunities to Recruit and Educate (MORE) Nurses Act alongside Congressman Jim Acosta (CA-21). This bill directs the National Advisory Council on Nurse Education to investigate policy solutions and federal programs that can aid in resolving the issue. Read the press release here.

title: Kiggans Hosts USDA Leadership to Highlight Aquaculture, Hold Industry Roundtable
text:
CAPE CHARLES, VA — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) welcomed U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Farm Service Agency (FSA) leadership to Virginia’s Eastern Shore for a tour of local aquaculture operations and a roundtable discussion with industry stakeholders. Congresswoman Kiggans was joined by FSA Administrator Bill Beam, USDA Under Secretary for Marketing and Regulatory Programs Dudley Hoskins, Director of the Office of Seafood Mike Illenberg, and Assistant Secretary for Congressional Relations Yvette Herrell.

The visit began with a tour of Cherrystone Aqua-Farms, where officials received a firsthand look at the region’s shellfish aquaculture operations and their contributions to Coastal Virginia’s economy. Following the tour, Congresswoman Kiggans and USDA leadership met with local aquaculture producers and industry stakeholders in Cape Charles to discuss challenges facing the industry, recent oyster mortality events, and opportunities to improve access to federal resources.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “Virginia’s Eastern Shore is home to some of the most hardworking aquaculture producers in the country. As the representative of a coastal district, I know how important it is to not only preserve our shorelines, but also ensure our producers have the resources they need to overcome the environmental challenges they face on a daily basis. I’m grateful to Administrator Beam, Under Secretary Hoskins, Director Illenberg, and Assistant Secretary Herrell for taking the time to visit Virginia’s Second District and hear directly from the men and women who make this industry so successful.”

In September 2026, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans joined Congressman Rob Wittman (VA-01) in writing a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins requesting that the Farm Service Agency coordinate with state agencies and researchers to assess widespread oyster mortality across Coastal Virginia and determine whether affected counties qualify for a Secretarial natural disaster designation. Read her press release here.

“Following the devastating losses to the Shore’s oyster populations, it was especially important to speak with USDA to assess whether federal assistance will be available to the Commonwealth’s producers,” said Kiggans. “It’s very encouraging that the USDA has established the Office of Seafood to help strengthen coordination between Washington and our communities, and I look forward to continuing our work to support our growers on the Eastern Shore.”

As the representative of a coastal district and a member of the House Committee on Natural Resources, Congresswoman Kiggans remains committed to supporting Coastal Virginia’s agriculture and aquaculture industries, strengthening local economies, and ensuring producers have access to the federal resources necessary to sustain their operations.

Background:

The Commonwealth of Virginia is the nation’s leading producer of Eastern oysters and hard clams. According to the Virginia Institute of Marine Science, shellfish aquaculture generated approximately $81 million in farm-gate sales in 2024, up 52% from 2018, including $29 million in oysters and $52 million in hard clams.

Virginia growers sold approximately 43.4 million market oysters and 195 million market hard clams in 2024, supporting more than 700 direct full- and part-time jobs. Cherrystone Aqua-Farms is part of this significant Eastern Shore industry.

Shellfish aquaculture also supports coastal water quality and habitat. Oysters filter water and remove suspended particles, while oyster reefs provide habitat and can contribute to shoreline protection.

title: Krishnamoorthi Joins Warren, Garcia, Bipartisan Lawmakers in Introducing Bill to Hold Bankers Who Financed Jeffrey Epstein’s Sex Trafficking Operation Accountable
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.) today joined U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, and Congressman Robert Garcia (D-Cal.), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee, along with Congressmen Ro Khanna (D-Cal.) and Thomas Massie (R-Ken.), and Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee, in introducing the bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act. The bill seeks accountability for the financial institutions and bank executives that may have enabled disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation.

“Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation left a money trail, and Wall Street has serious questions to answer. Our legislation will force federal regulators to release their records, investigate the banks and executives who may have enabled his crimes, and hold lawbreakers accountable,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “Epstein’s survivors deserve the full truth, no matter how powerful or well-connected those responsible may be.”

Extensive reporting and congressional probes have revealed the degree to which Wall Street empowered Epstein’s crimes. According to The New York Times Magazine, executives at JPMorgan assisted Epstein in evading internal controls meant to intercept suspicious activity, allowing him to avoid scrutiny. An August investigation by Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden's staff found “significant evidence that JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, and Bank of America violated federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to screen and report Epstein’s suspicious financial transactions in a timely manner.”

Krishnamoorthi has previously joined Warren in pressing Goldman Sachs over its handling of Kathryn Ruemmler’s ties to Epstein, and joined Warren and Khanna in demanding answers from Barclays about former CEO Jes Staley’s relationship with Epstein. At a May hearing with Epstein survivors, Krishnamoorthi also demanded that the Treasury Department release suspicious activity reports tied to Epstein’s financial transactions.

The Epstein Wall Street Records Act would:

Require federal financial regulators, including the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to disclose supervisory records related to Epstein and his associates to Congress and the American people, while protecting survivors' identifying information.

Force the financial regulators to investigate Epstein-connected banks and executives for possible banking, securities, or illicit financing violations.

Require industry bars or civil penalties for executives found to have committed qualifying violations, as well as referrals to the Department of Justice when regulators identify possible federal crimes.

“I have spent the last year calling on Donald Trump’s financial regulators to launch investigations into the big banks and executives who may have enabled Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes,” said Ranking Member Warren. “Since they have failed to act, Congress must. The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people.”

“Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around,” said Ranking Member Garcia. “We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned.”

“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act is about transparency and releasing financial records that are critical to holding the Epstein Class accountable and fighting to get justice for the survivors. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill,” said Representative Khanna.

“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act requires the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the SEC to release their files on Jeffrey Epstein’s money,” said Representative Massie. “The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files. This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”

“For far too long, financial institutions have leveraged their power, influence, and privilege to evade accountability. Their role in enabling Jeffrey Epstein’s decades of sexual exploitation and abuse demands serious scrutiny. That is why World Without Exploitation is proud to support the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026,” said Becca Zipkin, Vice President of Policy and Programs, World Without Exploitation. “We must follow the money to uncover the truth and ensure that the financial institutions that enabled this abuse are held accountable. Survivors deserve transparency, accountability, and the justice they have long been denied."

The cosponsors of the Epstein Wall Street Records Act include: Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), as well as Representatives Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Shontel Brown (D-Ohio), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Tex.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.), Wesley Bell (D-Mo.), Lateefah Simon (D-Cal.), Dave Min (D-Cal.), James Walkinshaw (D-Va.), Christian Menefee (D-Tex.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Kweisi Mfume (D-Md.), Greg Casar (D-Tex.), and Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.).

title: Krishnamoorthi Responds to Attempted Mass Shooting at His Family’s Hindu Temple in Aurora, Warns of Surging Anti-Indian Hate
text:
SCHAUMBURG — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) issued the following statement after authorities arrested a 19-year-old man accused of attempting to carry out a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. According to prosecutors, the suspect, who espoused white supremacist and neo-Nazi beliefs, allegedly attempted to open fire Sunday before his rifle jammed. After he told coworkers what happened and shared plans to try again, they alerted police, who arrested him before he could return.

“I am horrified that a white supremacist attempted to carry out a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans at the Hindu temple in Aurora where my family worships. My family and I were there when the attack was attempted last Sunday. The threat of such violence shows how dangerous anti-Indian hatred and white supremacy have become, and we cannot wait until innocent people are killed to take these threats seriously. I am grateful to the suspect’s coworkers who alerted police and commend the law enforcement officers who intervened. Every American deserves to live and worship without fear, and we must stand together against hatred in all its forms.”

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces $1.4 Million for Chemung County Sewer Improvements
text:
Washington, D.C.—October 15, 2026… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced that Chemung County has been awarded a $1.4 million grant from the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) to improve wastewater infrastructure at the Southern Tier Logistics Business Park in the Village of Horseheads. Combined with $1.4 million in state funding, the project represents a total investment of $2.8 million in critical infrastructure to support future business and industrial growth.

The project will fund the construction and rehabilitation of approximately 4,500 linear feet of sewer main, installation of new manholes, construction of a modern pump station and restoration of abandoned sewer lines. These improvements will expand system capacity, improve reliability and ensure the business park can provide dependable, environmentally compliant wastewater service for current and future employers.

The upgrades will help prepare the former military depot site for redevelopment as a manufacturing, warehousing and logistics hub, strengthening its ability to attract new investment and support economic growth throughout Chemung County and the Southern Tier. Construction is expected to take three years, after which the Chemung County Sewer District will own and maintain the upgraded system.

“This significant $1.4 million investment will make critical sewer improvements that are necessary for the Southern Tier Logistics Business Park to continue the redevelopment of the former Holding Point military depot. We can’t expect to attract jobs and economic development if we don’t have the public infrastructure to support the growth and that’s why I’ve been so focused on securing federal dollars to help position projects like this one. By helping prepare this property for development, we are paving the way for new private investments in manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics to strengthen the Southern Tier’s long-term economic future.”

The Appalachian Regional Commission is an economic development agency of the federal government and 13 state governments that invests in communities across the Appalachian region. Its mission is to strengthen economic growth and help Appalachian communities achieve greater socioeconomic parity with the nation.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Easing Russian Sanctions

title: ICYMI: Lawler, FHWA Administrator McMaster Highlight Safety Improvements Near Putnam Hospital
text:

title: Sánchez, Sewell lead 55 Democrats in opposing U.S. Withdrawal from International Labor Organization
text:
WASHINGTON – Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee Ranking Member Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.) and Oversight Subcommittee Ranking Member Terri Sewell (D-Ala.) today led 55 of their House Democratic colleagues in calling on the Trump administration to maintain United States participation in the International Labor Organization (ILO), which brings together governments, workers and employers to establish international labor standards. Those standards help protect American workers from being undercut by other countries with weaker labor standards.

Reports that the administration is considering withdrawal come amid a severe budget crisis at the ILO, driven largely by the Trump administration’s failure to pay approximately $300 million in outstanding U.S. membership dues.

“At the same time that the Administration has called on countries to improve labor standards, it is reportedly considering a withdrawal from the very institution that develops those standards and helps governments implement them,” the members wrote. “Notably, USTR relied on ILO data in conducting [its Section 301] investigations, underscoring the organization’s value to U.S. efforts to identify and combat forced labor.

“If the Administration believes that weak labor standards distort trade and disadvantage American workers and firms, withdrawing from an institution whose standards, research, and expertise it relies upon to address those concerns runs counter to American interests.”

In addition to Sánchez and Sewell, the letter was signed by Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Donald Beyer (D-Va.), Suzanne Bonamici (D-Ore.), Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Texas), Danny Davis (D-Ill.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Suzan DelBene (D-Wash.), Christopher Deluzio (D-Pa.), Mark DeSaulnier (D-Calif.), Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), Lloyd Doggett (D-Texas), Dwight Evans (D-Pa.), Sylvia Garcia (D-Texas), Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Steven Horsford (D-Nev.), Val Hoyle (D-Ore.), Glenn Ivey (D-Md.), Jonathan Jackson (D-Ill.), William Keating (D-Mass.), Robin Kelly (D-Ill.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), Greg Landsman (D-Ohio), John Larson (D-Conn.), Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Morgan McGarvey (D-Ky.), James McGovern (D-Mass.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Gwen Moore (D-Wis.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.), Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Stacey Plaskett (D-V.I.), Mark Pocan (D-Wis.), Nellie Pou (D-N.J.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Andrea Salinas (D-Ore.), Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.), Robert Scott (D-Va.), Terri Sewell (D-Ala.), Brad Sherman (D-Calif.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Greg Stanton (D-Ariz.), Thomas Suozzi (D-N.Y.), Mike Thompson (D-Calif.), Dina Titus (D-Nev.), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), Norma Torres (D-Calif.), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.), Maxine Waters (D-Calif.) and Frederica Wilson (D-Fla.).

The full text of the letter is available HERE and follows:

October 15, 2026

Secretary Rubio

U.S. Department of State

2201 C Street NW

Washington, D.C. 20520

Dear Secretary Rubio:

We write to express our deep concern regarding reports that the Administration is preparing to withdraw the United States from the International Labor Organization (ILO). Such a decision would undermine the organization’s core mission of establishing and promoting international labor standards in the global economy and would be difficult to reconcile with the Administration’s stated pro-worker trade agenda. These reports come amid a severe budget crisis at the ILO, which is largely due to the Administration’s failure to pay approximately $300 million in outstanding U.S. membership dues. Unlike most international organizations, the ILO’s unique tripartite structure gives governments, workers, and employers the central role of developing international labor standards to combat the global “race to the bottom” that has undermined wages and working conditions here in the United States and around the globe.

The labor standards developed and articulated by the constituents of the ILO underpin the labor provisions in U.S. trade agreements, which require trading partners to adopt, maintain, and effectively enforce labor laws related to eliminating forced labor, child labor, and employment discrimination, while also protecting workers’ fundamental right to organize unions and bargain collectively. Such obligations are vital to levelling the playing field by preventing other countries from gaining an unfair advantage through common forms of labor exploitation. But negotiated commitments are only as effective as the institutions that implement them. For decades, the ILO has helped governments put these commitments into practice through technical assistance, training, advisory services, reporting, investigations, and capacity-building support to labor inspectorates.

Several U.S. trading partners have reportedly sought ILO assistance in response to the Administration’s recent imposition of Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies for failing to impose or effectively enforce prohibitions on imports produced with forced labor. Other partners have sought to extend ILO programming that is a key U.S. trade condition for access to the U.S. market. Yet, at the same time that the Administration has called on countries to improve labor standards, it is reportedly considering a withdrawal from the very institution that develops those standards and helps governments implement them. Notably, USTR relied on ILO data in conducting these investigations, underscoring the organization’s value to U.S. efforts to identify and combat forced labor. If the Administration believes that weak labor standards distort trade and disadvantage American workers and firms, withdrawing from an institution whose standards, research, and expertise it relies upon to address those concerns runs counter to American interests.

The ILO’s value extends beyond government enforcement and directly benefits American companies operating in global supply chains. Through programs such as Better Work, a joint initiative of the ILO and the International Finance Corporation, factories receive auditing, training, and support to improve compliance with national laws and international labor standards. Improved transparency at the factory level enables companies to identify risks in their supply chains, address problems before they become more serious, and avoid reputational damage through responsible sourcing practices. The American Apparel & Footwear Association and other U.S. business organizations recently highlighted the important role of the ILO in strengthening labor enforcement in sourcing countries, addressing forced labor, and maintaining a competitive environment for American companies and workers.

The ILO’s role in advancing U.S. trade policy is well illustrated in Haiti, where U.S. law ties preferential market access to labor law compliance and integrates the ILO into that statutory framework. In September, Congress reauthorized the Haitian Hemispheric Opportunity through Partnership Encouragement Act (HOPE) and the Haiti Economic Lift Program Act (HELP). Under these programs, Haiti is mandated to work with the ILO to implement the Technical Assistance Improvement and Compliance Needs Assessment and Remediation (TAICNAR) program. The ILO’s Better Work program in Haiti operates the core compliance component of TAICNAR, conducting factory assessments, supporting remediation, and providing technical assistance to strengthen industrial relations and labor law enforcement. If the ILO is unable to continue performing these functions, Haiti will be unable to meet the labor compliance requirements Congress established as a condition of these trade preferences—programs that continue to enjoy strong bipartisan support.

Finally, the United States withdrawal from the ILO will only serve to expand China’s influence at the organization and deprive us of a key forum for holding them accountable for systemic labor rights violations. For example, in 2022 the United States delegation to the ILO’s annual conference played a decisive role in rallying support from governments, workers, and employers to condemn China’s use of forced labor camps to “re-educate” Uyghurs and other ethnic minorities in China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR). A U.S. withdrawal will not halt the development of international labor standards; rather, it will strip American policymakers, workers, and employers of their ability to shape their creation and implementation in a manner that reflects our values. Walking away cedes strategic leverage to a major economic competitor over the very rules that govern fair competition in the global marketplace. This exposure is particularly critical as the ILO facilitates the development of standards for emerging issues, including the platform economy, artificial intelligence, and workplace health and safety. American workers and companies will ultimately be impacted by these international standards, regardless of whether the United States chooses to participate in their creation.

Accordingly, we urge the Administration to maintain full United States membership in the ILO and utilize appropriated Contributions to International Organizations (CIO) funds to expeditiously pay the approximately $300 million in arrears. Abandoning the ILO does not protect American interests. Instead, it diminishes our ability to enforce trade agreements, taints our supply chains, and hands a strategic victory to our economic competitors. The United States must maintain its seat at the table to ensure that global labor standards are driven by American values, interests, and priorities.

To assist Congress in monitoring the implementation of U.S. trade policy and funding mandates, please provide comprehensive responses to the following questions by October 30, 2026:

Given the Administration’s extensive reliance on ILO data to execute recent Section 301 tariff enforcement actions, what concrete steps is the Department of State taking to ensure the ILO remains fully funded and operationally viable so that U.S. trade enforcement mechanisms are not compromised?

Because Congress has explicitly tied preferential market access for Haiti to the execution of the TAICNAR program, what immediate actions is the Department taking to ensure that the U.S. remains fully engaged in the ILO framework so as not to jeopardize the legal compliance of these congressional trade preferences?

In alignment with the 2025 National Security Strategy’s mandate to protect American workers from foreign economic distortion, what is the Department’s explicit plan to utilize the United States' permanent seat on the ILO Governing Body to actively counter China's expanding influence over global standard-setting?

Out of funds appropriated by Congress under the CIO account for Fiscal Years 2024, 2025, and 2026, what is the exact timeline for the Department to release the necessary funds to clear the outstanding $300 million in arrears and stabilize U.S. standing and voting rights within the organization?

title: Lofgren Demands Answers to Outstanding Oversight Requests, Warns EPA that Lack of Cooperation is Unacceptable
text:
(Washington, DC) - On Tuesday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin demanding that he comply with outstanding congressional oversight requests from the Committee.

“Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record.”

In closing, she writes: “EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.”

In her letter, Ranking Member Lofgren requires a response from EPA to the Committee’s outstanding oversight requests by no later than 5:00 pm Friday, November 6th, 2026.

Access the letter here and below.

Dear Administrator Zeldin,

Agencies are required to comply with congressional oversight. It is an obligation, not a choice. But under your leadership, the EPA appears to have forgotten that basic principle. Since President Trump took office in January 2025, I have made multiple requests to the agency for internal records, documents, and communications related to various topics. These oversight requests are crucial to my ability to properly carry out my oversight duties as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, which possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development programs at EPA. However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record. Instead, the agency has merely responded with letters that deflect questions rather than answering them. That was never acceptable. It becomes less tolerable with each passing month. I am writing to you to reaffirm my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress, and to formally notify the agency that they remain outstanding. I expect EPA to promptly comply.

Since your confirmation as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on January 29th, 2025, roughly 20% of the agency’s workforce has quit, retired, or been fired. Irreplaceable laboratory facilities have been shut down. The independent Office of Research and Development (ORD) has been wiped out. Scientific capacity has been gutted, scientific integrity is compromised, industry capture is widespread, and climate denialism is ascendant. In short, EPA’s basic mission to use the best available science to protect human health and the environment has been damaged under your leadership.

To take just one of countless examples, I have learned that the Office of Air and Radiation (OAR), acting under direct orders from former Assistant Administrator Aaron Szabo, has refused to grant the Office of Applied Sciences and Environmental Solutions (OASES) permission to conduct or publish virtually any air pollution research without prior approval from OAR political leadership. OASES is the ostensible successor to ORD, which was a global scientific leader in air quality and air pollution research. It is my understanding that OAR has categorically denied OASES the authority to conduct and publish its own air-related research without OAR political approval, except for narrow circumstances in which technical support from OASES cannot be avoided for OAR to meet certain statutory obligations. Indeed, OASES cannot even independently initiate air-related research without approval from OAR political appointees. OAR can only assert this control because of the agency’s new “no surprises” policy for OASES, which appallingly requires that OASES research “must be supported by appropriate political leadership” before it can proceed. The policy is a clear violation of scientific integrity, and the notion that EPA’s primary science office cannot even study air pollution without getting permission from the political appointees of a different office would be laughable if it was not so dangerous.

In my role as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I have attempted to conduct oversight of these types of actions. There are many reasons for this oversight: to document the damage done to the agency and its workforce; to understand the scientific capabilities that have been lost and the implications of those losses for human health and the American people; to identify violations of scientific integrity and administrative procedure; and to comprehend why all of this happened in order to inform legislative efforts to reverse it and prevent it from ever happening again. Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities. The agency has been non-responsive to my requests and has utterly failed to comply. I am now reaffirming these oversight requests to provide the agency with a second opportunity to demonstrate the appropriate degree of deference and respect for congressional prerogatives. I expect EPA’s full and prompt responsiveness to each of the requests detailed below, which are long overdue:

1. Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs)

On March 26th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with several other Democratic Committee Members requesting that the agency “provide the Committee with your Agency RIF and Reorganization Plan immediately upon transmitting it to OMB and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).” The context for this request was the revelation that EPA’s ARRP proposed to “eliminate the Office of Research and Development as an EPA National Program Office” while pushing “a majority (50-75%)” of ORD’s employees out of the agency. Of course, that is exactly what happened. But EPA never provided its Phase One and Phase Two ARRPs to the Committee, which has hindered the Committee’s ability to understand the motivations and decisions that led to the elimination of ORD. For instance, information revealed last year in a lawsuit related to agency ARRPs appeared to suggest that disagreements may have existed between EPA and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regarding the elimination of ORD. Without reviewing the ARRPs themselves, the Committee cannot properly assess the agency’s position towards ORD and the bureaucratic actions that contributed to its demise.

2. Laboratory Budget and Staffing Levels

On May 27th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo requesting that the agency “share the projected post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the facilities that will remain open.” The “facilities” in this case referred specifically to the ten field laboratory and research facilities managed by ORD. These research laboratories are a crown jewel of EPA science, and the agency’s intention to eliminate ORD had raised the alarming prospect that the laboratories might be shut down as well. EPA has not subsequently acted to do so, and the laboratories appear to be continuing under the management of different program offices. But while I am relieved that they continue to operate, I remain concerned that staffing shortages and reduced scientific capabilities at the former ORD laboratories could undermine their ability to appropriately study environmental hazards. EPA’s unwillingness to provide basic budgetary and personnel information for its research laboratories impedes the Committee’s ability to evaluate whether they remain capable of supporting core agency activities.

3. Endangerment Finding Repeal Documents and Communications

On August 18th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Amo requesting that the agency provide “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and OMB, the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team, regarding “the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.” I also requested “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report developed by DOE’s Climate Working Group, and “all documents and communications” within EPA regarding “the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.” These oversight requests relate to the repeal of the 2009 Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding, which the agency proposed in July 2025 and finalized in February 2026. I continue to have concerns about potential violations of administrative law in the agency’s rulemaking process to repeal the Endangerment Finding. The documents and communications that I requested are central to the Committee’s ability to conduct oversight of the agency’s actions. EPA’s refusal to provide them only strengthens my belief that these records remain highly material to my review and must be disclosed without delay.

4. Status of PFNA IRIS Assessment

Dr. Maureen Gwinn, the EPA Deputy Associate Administrator for Science, testified before the Science Committee’s Subcommittee on Environment on June 4th, 2026. The subject of her testimony was OASES and the general status of environmental research and development at the agency after the elimination of ORD. During that hearing, I questioned Dr. Gwinn about the agency’s decision earlier in 2026 to disavow chemical assessments conducted by the Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS). In particular, I asked about the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, which press reports indicate has been fully completed for more than a year but which the agency refuses to finalize and publish. In response, Dr. Gwinn told me that she was “not sure of the details on that” and said that she would “have to get back to you.” She also stated that she would “go back and confirm” the status of the PFNA assessment. While that hearing took place over four months ago, the agency has not provided any subsequent information regarding the PFNA assessment and whether it ever intends to finalize and publish the assessment, nor has it offered any scientific justification for refusing to do so. I continue to seek clarity on whether the IRIS assessment for PFNA, a dangerous and highly toxic PFAS chemical, will ever see the light of day under this administration.

5. Administration Delays of Environmental Research

At the same June 4th Environment Subcommittee hearing with Dr. Gwinn, one of my colleagues, Representative Suzanne Bonamici, questioned Dr. Gwinn about whether the agency under its current leadership had sought to delay or suppress any environmental research due to its perceived lack of alignment with administration priorities. Specifically, Representative Bonamici asked whether “any proposed research products, even one, [had] been delayed, modified, or declined because they did not align with the priorities set by political appointees?” In response, Dr. Gwinn acknowledged that “there have been delays” due to the agency’s review of whether certain research products complied with President Trump’s various Executive Orders. But when Representative Bonamici followed up and directly asked “what was the topic of the research,” pertaining to research that had been halted, Dr. Gwinn could only respond that she would “have to get back to you on that.” The agency has not provided any further information regarding which specific research topics were “delayed, modified, or declined” due to the political directives of agency leadership. This information is highly material to the Committee’s ability to understand the current state of scientific integrity at EPA, as well as the role played by political appointees in influencing the environmental research being conducted by the agency.

In summary, the following oversight requests remain outstanding and require compliance on the part of the agency. Please produce the requested records no later than 5:00 PM on Friday, November 6th, 2026:

1. Please provide to the Committee the EPA’s Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs) transmitted to OMB and OPM pursuant to OMB Director Russ Vought’s February 2025 memo.

2. Please provide to the Committee the post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the agency’s field laboratory and research facilities that remain open.

3. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and OMB regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.

4. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.

5. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.

6. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report titled, “A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate.”

7. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) within EPA regarding the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.

8. Please provide to the Committee a written update regarding the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, including whether any scientific work remains ongoing for the assessment and the date by which the agency intends to finalize and publish the assessment.

9. Please provide to the Committee a list of all research products that have been delayed, modified, or declined since January 20th, 2025, due to the agency’s review or conclusions regarding the alignment of scientific research with administration priorities, including the topics of the research products.

EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.

Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development.

title: Malliotakis, Lanza, Tannousis Highlight State Policies Driving Up Utility Bills, Legislative Efforts to Lower Energy Costs
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) joined State Senator Andrew Lanza, Assemblyman Michael Tannousis, and Stefano Sena, owner of Bocelli Restaurant, to highlight how costly New York State energy policies and mandates are driving up utility bills for families and businesses, while outlining federal efforts to increase domestic energy production, strengthen grid reliability and lower electricity costs.

New Yorkers pay approximately 60% more for electricity than the national average, placing a significant financial burden on hardworking families and small businesses. The lawmakers highlighted how state energy mandates, taxes and regulatory decisions are contributing to rising costs, including rate increases approved by the New York State Public Service Commission (PSC), whose members are appointed by the Governor, and the state's closure of the Indian Point Nuclear Power Plant that provided 26% of New York City's electricity supply.

Over the past five years, the PSC has approved two major multi-year rate plans for Con Edison, further increasing costs for ratepayers. The lawmakers also noted that state and local taxes, fees and surcharges make up roughly one-third of a customer's utility bill.

"Families and small businesses are being forced to pay more than 60% above the national average because of costly energy mandates, excessive taxes and misguided policies coming out of Albany. While Washington is working to expand American energy production, strengthen our electric grid and deliver more affordable, reliable power, New York State continues to pursue policies that drive costs higher. We need to reverse course, provide relief to ratepayers and ensure families can afford to keep their lights on and heat their homes," said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis.

“Electricity costs more on Staten Island, in New York City, and New York State for one simple reason: because of Democrat elected officials’ policies, regulations, and taxes,” said Senator Andrew Lanza. “If they were to remove the taxes on electricity, suspend them, that Congresswoman Malliotakis mentioned, we would overnight have the lowest electricity costs in America.”

"The rising utility costs that are driving residents out of New York are the direct result of mandates and taxes imposed by the Governor and Democratic-controlled legislature. Albany’s mandates have consistently increased the cost of living in New York and we need new leadership to put our state on a corrective course. The evidence is clear when the state is sitting on a massive $2.4 billion “Energy Tax” surplus that is waiting to be utilized on whatever pet project the Governor deems fit instead of returning it to the ratepayers," said Assemblyman Michael Tannousis.

title: MATSUI ACTS TO PROTECT AMERICANS FROM HIGH COSTS AT THE GAS PUMP
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) introduced legislation to require the Department of Transportation (DOT) to examine whether it can strengthen fuel efficiency requirements to counter high gas prices and reinstate penalties for automakers that fail to produce fuel-efficient vehicles.

“Across the country, Americans are being squeezed by high gas prices, rising grocery bills, and everyday costs that keep stretching family budgets thinner,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Gas Money Saved Act meets people where they are by strengthening fuel efficiency standards that help drivers spend less on gas for years to come. This is a practical step to lower everyday costs, give families more breathing room, and build a cleaner, more efficient transportation future.”

“With gas prices skyrocketing because of President Trump’s prolonged and illegal war, we must take immediate steps to give American consumers some relief,” said Congresswoman Titus. “In May 2026, gas prices rose at a rate ten times higher than the rate of inflation. In Nevada, they now average $5.45 per gallon. Coupled with higher prices on groceries and other goods because of the Trump tariffs, families are struggling to make ends meet.”

Congresswoman Matsui, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and Rep. Dina Titus (NV-01), a member of the House Transportation Committee, introduced the Gas Money Saved Act to review Corporate Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards and reinstate fuel-efficiency requirements that were stripped away by Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill in 2025. Companion legislation has been introduced in the Senate by Senator Ed Markey (D-MA).

“Fuel economy standards help American drivers get around without breaking the bank while gas prices are high, but Trump and the Republicans gutted these standards as part of their crusade to put Big Oil above American families,” said Senator Markey. “Auto innovation should give consumers better choices, not cut corners at their expense. The Gas Money Saved Act would make sure American drivers have fuel-efficient vehicle options that are cheaper to fill up and hold automakers to account—a cost-saving measure that is especially critical as the Trump Administration would rather spend billions on an illegal war than keep costs low for Americans.

title: MATSUI, LEADER SCHUMER, MARKEY, MENENDEZ, MENG LEAD COLLEAGES IN DEMANDING TRUMP FCC WITHDRAW PROPOSAL TO UNDERMINE E-RATE PROGRAM
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), and Representatives Rob Menendez (D-NJ) and Grace Meng (D-NY), led nearly the entire Senate Democratic Caucus and more than 60 members of the House Democratic Caucus in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to withdraw the Commission’s damaging proposal to eliminate or limit the E-Rate program. In June, the Carr FCC voted to open a rulemaking examining E-Rate, which helps schools and libraries across the country afford reliable internet access.

For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped close the digital divide by ensuring that students and library patrons can access the internet regardless of their income or ZIP code. In 2025, E-Rate helped more than 158,000 schools and libraries pay recurring broadband bills, increase bandwidth, maintain secure internal Wi-Fi networks, and replace aging infrastructure. Ending or sharply curtailing E-Rate would impose severe costs on schools and libraries while weakening economic growth, undermining American technological leadership, and jeopardizing national security.

The E-Rate program has invested more than $69 billion to connect schools and libraries to the internet across the country. Massachusetts schools and libraries have received more than $950 million from the E-Rate program and another $97 million from the Emergency Connectivity Fund, a $7 billion program that Senator Markey created within the American Rescue Plan to provide devices and connectivity for students and educators at home.

In the letter, the lawmakers wrote, “Schools and libraries help develop the next generation of engineers, scientists, and cybersecurity professionals, including in communities that have historically lacked access to those opportunities. Cutting E-Rate would narrow that talent pipeline. Maintaining connectivity in every school and library is therefore an investment in America’s technological leadership, economic competitiveness, and national security.

The lawmakers continued, “We strongly support measures to protect children online and address concerns around excessive screen time. But cutting E-Rate is not a child-safety measure. E-Rate funds broadband connectivity — not laptops, tablets, applications, or online content — and recipients must already comply with the Children’s Internet Protection Act, including by using filtering and blocking tools, adopting internet-safety policies, and educating students about appropriate online behavior. States and local communities, meanwhile, are developing targeted policies governing when and how students use devices in schools — an appropriate way to address screen-time concerns, rather than cutting broadband support. The Commission should not use child safety as a pretext to dismantle the secure, managed broadband infrastructure that schools and libraries need to educate students and help them navigate the digital world safely.”

The letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

title: McBath Leads Colleagues in Urging TSA Administrator to Respect the Dignity of Hard-Working Agents
text:
In the last year, TSA officers have been forced to work 88 days without on-time payment. Now, leadership has taken away their chairs.

Atlanta, GA – Today, Representative Lucy McBath (GA-06), is leading 37 of her House colleagues in urging TSA Administrator David P. Cummins support the well-being of TSA agents and the safety of the nation by reversing his decision to remove their chairs at document check stations in airports around the country. This letter is officially endorsed by AFGE, AFGE TSA Council 100, and AFGE TSA Local 554 in Atlanta. McBath, who was a flight attendant for 30 years before she came to Congress, represents many of the employees of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International—America’s busiest airport.

“Transportation Security Officers, or TSOs, have an incredibly important job. They are the first line of defense in keeping Americans and their families safe during air travel,” the members write. “Since October of last year, officers at TSA have been forced to work 88 days without being paid on time. They have had to fight in court to protect their collective bargaining agreement from being unilaterally canceled and are now being told that they are not allowed to sit down while they perform their duties at checker stations. It is abundantly clear that these changes are intended to try to push officers out of their jobs with TSA, not to keep the American people safe or improve service.”

“This is about more than chairs,” the members continue. “This is about the respect that every person in the United States deserves at work and on the job. American workers are tired of being treated as expendable.”

“TSA officers have continued to show up and protect the traveling public through government shutdowns, delayed pay, and attacks on their collective bargaining rights. Removing chairs from document checker stations is yet another unnecessary hardship placed on an already strained workforce, and I commend Congresswoman McBath and her congressional colleagues for standing with our officers and demanding the dignity, respect, and working conditions they deserve,” said Aaron Barker Jr., President of AFGE Local 554.

In addition to Representative Lucy McBath, the letter is signed by Representatives Nanette Barragán, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Kathy Castor, Jasmine Crockett, Danny Davis, Mark DeSaulnier, Lois Frankel, Maxwell Frost, Robert Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Pablo Hernández, Val Hoyle, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Hank Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Tim Kennedy, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Betty McCollum, Christian Menefee, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Emily Randall, Mary Gay Scanlon, Greg Stanton, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Nikema Williams, and Frederica Wilson.

title: McCaul, Costa, Colleagues Urge "Full and Faithful" Implementation of Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas) joined Congressman Jim Costa (D-Calif.) and 20 bipartisan colleagues in sending a letter to President Trump urging "full and faithful" implementation of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

McCaul introduced and championed the legislation in the House alongside Congressman Steny Hoyer (D-Md.) and a bipartisan group of colleagues. As the law's initial October 18 implementation deadline approaches, the members thanked President Trump for signing the bill and called on his administration to use the full force of its sanctions and tariff authorities to increase pressure on Vladimir Putin and reinvigorate peace efforts. They also raised concerns about the Treasury Department's October 9 authorization of transactions involving Russian-origin diesel and urged a revocation of the issued license.

In addition to McCaul and Costa, the letter was signed by Reps. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), Sanford Bishop (D-Ga.), Salud Carbajal (D-Calif.), Ed Case (D-Hawaii), Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.), Danny Davis (D-Ill.), Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.), Jared Golden (D-Maine), Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio), Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Steny Hoyer (D-Md.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Robert Menendez (D-N.J.), Dan Newhouse (R-Wash.), Mike Quigley (D-Ill.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Dina Titus (D-Nev.), Jill Tokuda (D-Hawaii), and Joe Wilson (R-S.C.).

Full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Mr. President:

As Russia prepares to wage a fifth winter campaign against Ukraine, the United States has an opportunity to reinvigorate peace efforts by placing maximum pressure on Vladimir Putin and the governments and networks that finance his war. We write to thank you for signing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law, and to urge its full and faithful implementation by the first deadline on October 18. Utilizing the tools for economic pressure in this law will be decisive in forcing Putin to take peace talks seriously.

Timely and complete execution of the first round of mandatory sanctions will deter Russia’s increasing attacks on Ukrainian civilians and their livelihoods. Russia has intensified strikes on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure and on cargo ships that carry global supplies of grain, and it is blocking food and medicine from reaching civilians in occupied territories. Just as Iran’s attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz threatened global energy markets, Russia’s campaign against shipping in the Black Sea threatens global food security and demands an equally firm response. The Kremlin’s fearful response to this law underlines its power to finally force Russia to stop the killing. The Administration’s sanctions against the illicit A7 network propping up Russia and Iran’s war efforts is a strong opening salvo in this effort.

We therefore urge the Administration to apply the Graham law’s sanctions to their fullest extent and without delay. Designations should reach the officials, oligarchs, banks, and state enterprises directing and financing the war, as well as the foreign banks, shadow fleet operators, and intermediaries that help Russia evade restrictions. We are particularly concerned by Treasury's October 9 issuance of General License 135, which authorizes transactions involving Russian-origin diesel, including imports into the United States. We urge the Administration to revoke this license and not issue further general licenses that reopen Russian energy transactions and restore revenue to the Kremlin's war chest.

Methodical application of the law’s secondary tariffs will cut into the energy revenue that sustains Russia’s war and make clear that the countries financing it will share in its cost. Oil and gas sales remain the Kremlin’s most important source of income, and China and India remain its largest purchasers of crude. The law directs tariffs on the largest importers of Russian energy and the leading facilitators of sanctions evasion, and we call on the Administration to apply them precisely. Country determinations should rest on authoritative trade and maritime data, and the methodology behind them must be shared with Congress. Tariff rates should serve as leverage to secure verifiable commitments to reduce purchases of Russian energy, easing as reductions are demonstrated.

Precise targeting of these tariffs will also preserve the allied unity that has constrained Russia’s war economy. European allies have committed to eliminating their imports of Russian oil and gas by the end of 2027, and many have already made substantial reductions. The law provides exceptions and rate adjustments for countries taking such steps, and we ask the Administration to apply them as Congress intended. Penalizing partners who are already cutting off Moscow and supporting Ukraine would undercut America’s greatest leverage over the Kremlin—the powerful international coalition working to isolate Putin while his invasion continues.

Disciplined use of the law’s waiver authority and close consultation with Congress will sustain this pressure over time and demonstrate global credibility. We ask that any waiver be narrow, time-limited, and tied to measurable reductions in support for Russia’s war, and that no waiver be used to defer the law’s core provisions. We further request timely delivery of the required tariff justifications and a briefing for the committees of jurisdiction following the October 18 deadline, as well as regular updates ahead of each 180-day review. In advance of the deadline, we respectfully request answers to the following questions:

What actions will the Administration complete by October 18 to demonstrate that the law’s mandatory sanctions, secondary tariffs, and prohibitions are being fully implemented, and will any provision be delayed or waived?

Which Russian officials, oligarchs, banks, and state enterprises will be designated by October 18, and will these designations extend to the foreign banks, shadow fleet operators, and intermediaries that help Russia evade sanctions?

Which countries will be subject to secondary tariffs by October 18? What trade and maritime data was used to identify them, and how will the exceptions and rate adjustments be applied to allies reducing their purchases of Russian energy?

What benchmarks will the Administration use to demonstrate to Congress and the American people that these measures are increasing pressure on Putin, such as reductions in Russia’s energy revenue and in third-country purchases of Russian oil and gas?

How does the Administration reconcile General License 135 with the existing statutory ban on Russian energy imports, and what impact does it expect the license to have on Russia's energy revenues?

Putin has repeatedly shown that he responds to pressure, not goodwill. With the October 18 deadline approaching, we again urge you to implement this law fully and faithfully. This will make clear that American resolve is bipartisan and durable, and that the cost of continuing this war will only grow until Russia comes to the negotiating table. We remain committed to Ukraine’s defense and to a just and lasting peace. We stand ready to work with your Administration to ensure this law achieves the purpose for which Congress enacted it.

title: Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland

title: McClellan, Whitehouse Investigate EPA’s Decision to Exempt Data Center Power Plants from Acid Rain Protections
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), last month launched a bicameral investigation into the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) guidance exempting data center power plants from the Acid Rain Program (ARP).

By EPA’s own admission, the decision to issue new guidance came at the behest of data center companies. And according to the EPA press release issuing the new guidance, the agency took this action to “further President Trump’s agenda promoting data centers.”

“EPA’s new ARP guidance is a handout to the richest and most powerful companies in the world. And this handout comes at the expense of Americans’ health and the safety of our ecosystems and communities that were, prior to the inception of the ARP, regularly drenched in dangerous acidic rainfall,” the lawmakers wrote in their letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin.

The ARP regulates the emission of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) from power plants. SO2 and NOx are both harmful to human health, damaging the respiratory system and worsening heart disease. They are also linked to adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, kidney damage, autoimmune disorders, and cancer.

The pollutants are also the primary causes of acid rain. Prior to the ARP, acid rain poisoned rivers, lakes, and streams; damaged forests; killed and sickened aquatic animals; and corroded buildings, monuments, and statues.

“EPA explicitly bills its new guidance as a means to facilitate data center development. In so doing, EPA misapprehends its own mission, which is to ‘protect human health and the environment,’ as stated in black and white on the agency’s own website,” continued the lawmakers.

“Bizarrely, under EPA’s new guidance, massive new gas-fired power plants large enough to power cities would be exempt from NOx and SO2 caps under the ARP only as long as they do not serve the public electricity grid and instead exclusively power a privately-owned data center. This is a perverse outcome, and it is contrary to Congress’s design for the Clean Air Act, which creates specific and comprehensive regulatory requirements for significant pollution sources like these,” added the lawmakers.

The lawmakers, together with Senators Ed Markey (D-MA) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), requested answers from EPA by October 7th about the agency’s decision-making process while crafting this new guidance, as well as any information regarding the agency’s communications with data center companies. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Cory Booker (D-NJ), and 24 Members of the House of Representatives also signed the letter. EPA has not yet responded to the lawmakers’ letter.

title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE HONORS ROCHESTER STUDENT AZALEA DIETZ WITH CONGRESSIONAL AWARD GOLD MEDAL
text:
(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle recognized Rochester student Azalea Dietz with the Congressional Award Gold Medal, the highest honor bestowed by the United States Congress upon young civilians. The prestigious award recognizes Dietz's exceptional dedication to community service, personal development, physical fitness, and exploration.

“Azalea represents the very best of the next generation of leaders in our community,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I am proud to recognize her achievements with this prestigious honor, and I hope her example inspires other young people across our community to get involved, pursue their passions, and discover the difference they can make.”

A student at Rochester's School of the Arts, Dietz has demonstrated a wide-ranging commitment to service and personal achievement. She volunteered at a local music and arts center, where she worked with children, assisted with summer camp activities, and supported the center's operations and photography needs. Her service also extended internationally to Portugal, where she volunteered at an animal rescue center caring for puppies and at a food bank packaging essential supplies for families in need. As part of her Congressional Award journey, Dietz planned and completed a five-day hiking expedition through the Adirondack Mountains alongside her mother and brother, tackling trails on Whiteface Mountain, Mount Jo, and Ampersand Mountain.

Established by Congress in 1979, the Congressional Award is a nonpartisan, voluntary, and noncompetitive program designed to encourage young Americans to set goals, challenge themselves, and make meaningful contributions to their communities. The program recognizes achievement in four areas: Voluntary Public Service, Personal Development, Physical Fitness, and Expedition/Exploration.

Young people interested in participating in the Congressional Award program are encouraged to contact Congressman Morelle's office to learn more about the program, eligibility requirements, and how to get started.

title: Griffith Signs Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud
text:
U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance unveiled a Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. The pledge consists of six pillars to secure federal programs, coordinate anti-fraud actions across government agencies and deliver justice to those who illegally take advantage of taxpayer-funded benefits. As a Congressional leader supporting Republicans’ “War on Fraud,” U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) signed onto Vice President Vance’s pledge.

In response to signing the pledge, Congressman Griffith issued the following statement:

“I am proud to stand by Vice President Vance and Republicans focused on waste, fraud and abuse in the federal government.

“By signing this pledge, I reaffirm my commitment to fundamental actions that protect taxpayer-funded benefits, stop fraud and support vulnerable American patients.

“Republicans in Congress agree: fraudulently taking advantage of Americans who benefit from federal health care programs and privileges is WRONG!”

BACKGROUND

Congressman Griffith is a supporter of numerous Congressional actions to combat fraud.

As the Health Subcommittee Chairman for the House Energy and Commerce Committee, Griffith is a lead Committee investigator into health care fraud.

Recently, Lynchburg, Virginia, officials notified residents that more than $60,000 in SNAP benefits were stolen from Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards. The stolen benefits cannot be currently replaced, leaving SNAP participants without their fully allotted funds and putting them at risk of going hungry.

Responding to this news, Congressman Griffith issued his support as co-sponsor to the SNAP Anti-Theft and Victim Compensation Act.

In September, Congressman Griffith also introduced an anti-fraud bill to protect Medicaid, H.R. 10621 – the Medicaid Fraud Fighting and Taxpayer Protection Act.

Earlier this summer, as part of efforts to crack down on birth tourism and fraudulent activity that exploits U.S. citizenship laws, Congressman Griffith introduced H.R. 9724, the End Birthright Citizenship for Territories Act.

title: Neal Announces $735,000 Earmark for the Berkshire Innovation Center’s Cybersecurity Learning and Testing Facility
text:
Pittsfield, MA – Today, Congressman Richard E. Neal joined Ben Sosne, Executive Director for the Berkshire Innovation Center (BIC), Pittsfield Mayor Peter Marchetti, state and local officials, and local business leaders and stakeholders to announce a $735,000 earmark for the BIC’s Cybersecurity Learning and Testing Facility. This allocation was made possible through Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) from the U.S. Department of Commerce. Congressman Neal included funding for this project in the Fiscal Year 2026 spending bill.

Since opening in 2020, the BIC’s 20,000-square-foot facility has provided regional manufacturers and STEM businesses with advanced R&D equipment, state-of-the-art lab and training facilities, and opportunities to collaborate with renowned research partners, as well as internship and apprenticeship programs for local students. Through collaborations with area businesses, educational institutions, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders, the BIC helps foster technological advancement and workforce development, thereby strengthening the region’s manufacturing sector and enabling businesses to grow and compete in an ever-changing economy.

“Today is a great day for the City of Pittsfield, as we welcome the news that the Berkshire Innovation Center will be expanding its capabilities with the help of a $735,000 earmark I was proud to secure,” said Congressman Richard E. Neal. “Whether it’s our local governments, our educational institutions, or our water systems, sophisticated challenges stemming from cybersecurity threats are confronting every sector of our economy. With the establishment of the Cybersecurity Learning and Testing Facility, the BIC will be able to prepare the next generation of our skilled workforce by providing meaningful hands-on training, ensuring our communities have the resources needed to protect critical infrastructure and safeguard public services.”

Funding secured by Congressman Neal will help establish the Cybersecurity Learning and Testing Facility, the next phase of the BIC’s Manufacturing Academy. An industry-led educational hub, the Manufacturing Academy seeks to close the knowledge gaps of local supply chain capabilities and the needs of larger manufacturers through ongoing education, training, and technology assistance. As one piece of a larger educational module, the Cybersecurity Learning and Testing Facility will serve as a centralized hub for monitoring, detecting, and responding to cybersecurity threats within manufacturing facilities, with a focus on enhancing resilience and safeguarding critical assets. The facility will provide essential monitoring of systems, networks, and applications for supply chain manufacturers serving the defense industrial base, while supporting workforce development to strengthen cybersecurity in other local industries and municipalities.

“Congressman Neal has been a tremendous partner to the BIC, and his support is helping us address a growing challenge facing manufacturers across our region,” said Ben Sosne, Executive Director for the Berkshire Innovation Center. “Cybersecurity requirements are becoming increasingly complex, particularly for companies in the defense supply chain. Our goal is to bring together manufacturers, technology providers, and partners like General Dynamics and Synagex to help companies navigate these requirements and take practical steps forward. This is an opportunity to build something meaningful in Western Massachusetts that helps our manufacturers compete and grow.”

Under guidelines issued by the Senate and House Appropriations Committees, members of Congress requested CDS funding for projects in their state for Fiscal Year 2026. CDS requests were restricted to a limited number of federal funding streams, and only state and local governments and eligible non-profit entities were permitted to receive CDS funding. This project is one of fifteen CDS projects submitted by Congressman Neal, investing in a variety of initiatives throughout the First Congressional District of Massachusetts.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Introduces Resolution Commemorating National Nonviolence Week
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) introduced a resolution commemorating National Nonviolence Week, which occurs annually during the first week of October. Congresswoman Williams introduced a similar resolution in 2021 and 2022 during National Nonviolence Week. Congressman John Lewis historically introduced resolutions to mark National Nonviolence Week during his time in Congress.

The resolution raises awareness of youth violence, the need to become a more peaceful society, and the important role Georgia’s Fifth Congressional District played in America’s history of nonviolent social change.

Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) said:

“Violence in every form is far too pervasive in our country. However, the work of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and my friend and predecessor, John Lewis, both of whom were champions of nonviolence, can inspire us to create a more peaceful country. I am proud to build on their legacy every day in Congress, but especially during National Nonviolence Week, as we continue advancing nonviolent social action in the Fighting Fifth and across our nation in pursuit of a more equal and equitable world.”

The resolution reads in part:

“Whereas the principle of nonviolence has been a core philosophy of many successful social change movements: Now, therefore, be it Resolved, That the House of Representatives—supports the goals and ideals of ‘‘National Nonviolence Week’’ to raise awareness of youth violence in the United States and the benefits of practicing nonviolence principles; and encourages the people of the United States, State and local officials, middle schools and high schools, law enforcement agencies, and other interested groups to observe ‘‘National Nonviolence Week’’ with appropriate programs and activities that promote awareness and prevention of youth violence.”
