title: Rep. Panetta Leads Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) and Greg Steube (FL-17) wrote a bipartisan letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressing concerns about reports that Meta is seeking to use the federal research tax credit for its data center buildout. The bipartisan letter, co-led by Reps. Mike Thompson (CA-04) and Suzan DelBene (WA-01), emphasized that any claims by Meta for the federal tax credit must meet the clearly defined requirements for qualified research and experimentation.

Congress established the research tax credit in 1981 amid concerns about declining private-sector research investment and U.S. technological competitiveness. By reducing the cost of qualifying research, the credit is meant to encourage businesses to pursue projects involving technical uncertainty and experimentation, rather than simply purchasing and deploying proven technology.

“We are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit,” wrote the lawmakers. “The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.”

To qualify for the credit, research must meet a four-part test, including being technological in nature, addressing technical uncertainty, seeking to develop or improve a product or process, and involving a process of experimentation. Certain activities, including research conducted after commercial production begins and duplication of an existing product or process, are excluded. The lawmakers emphasized that the scale or configuration of a data center does not, by itself, establish that its construction and equipment costs qualify.

“Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business,” continued the lawmakers.

“The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment,” concluded the lawmakers.

In addition to Reps. Panetta, Steube, Thompson, and DelBene, the letter was also signed by Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), John James (MI-10), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Victoria Spartz (IN-05), Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Bessent:

In light of concerning reports that Meta Platforms, Inc. is seeking to claim the research credit under 26 U.S.C. § 41 for substantial expenditures associated with its data center buildout, we write as Members of Congress to reaffirm that the credit is intended to incentivize qualified research and experimentation, not subsidize the routine deployment of existing technology. We believe that the credit remains a critical support for American innovation, but that an overly expansive interpretation of qualifying expenditures risks undermining its purpose by subsidizing ordinary capital investment rather than encouraging genuinely novel research.

Congress created the research credit as part of the Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981 in response to declining private-sector research and development investment and concerns about U.S. technological competitiveness. The credit was designed to encourage companies to undertake additional research and experimentation, not to subsidize ordinary capital investment or the deployment of established technology.

Internal Revenue Code Section 41 and Treasury Regulation 1.41-4 establish specific requirements for activities to constitute qualified research. Research must satisfy the IRS four-part test, which mandates the research must aim to develop or improve a product, process or technique, be technological in nature, eliminate uncertainty about capability, design, or methodology and importantly belong to a process of experimentation. A company must pinpoint the specific components of a project that are technically uncertain and prove it used scientific experiments to overcome that uncertainty.

These limitations are particularly important in distinguishing genuine research and experimentation from ordinary commercial activity. IRS guidance makes clear that research conducted after the beginning of commercial production and the duplication of an existing product or process do not qualify. Likewise, uncertainty about how best to configure or implement existing technology does not, alone, establish that a taxpayer has undertaken the process of experimentation required by Section 41. The IRS has repeatedly found that proven and commercially available equipment and technology is not eligible for the credit.

As a result, we are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit. The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.

Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business.

The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment.

We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.

###

title: Pappas Leads Bipartisan Call to Increase Home Heating Assistance Funding
text:
Today Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) led a bipartisan group of 73 members in calling on the House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in emergency supplemental appropriations for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27).

In the letter, the members wrote, “As the war with Iran remains unresolved, energy prices are expected to keep rising, with heating oil up 60% since February. LIHEAP’s $4 billion in funding for the last fiscal year would fall significantly short in meeting the needs of American families this fiscal year.”

“LIHEAP is a critical lifeline for low- and moderate-income individuals, but even if your household qualifies, LIHEAP does not provide guaranteed security. Five out of six families who qualify for LIHEAP receive no financial assistance due to the program’s woefully underfunded status. When adjusting for inflation, LIHEAP funding is lower now than it was in 1981 when the program was first created. If LIHEAP was funded at the same level as it was 45 years ago, the program would have received nearly $7 billion in FY27,” they continued.

“Emergency LIHEAP assistance is urgently needed as winter weather approaches and colder temperatures have already begun. Families should not have to choose between staying warm and purchasing other essential items like food, medication, or rent. Congress must act and not leave families in the cold,” they concluded.

LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff last year and President Trump’s repeated demand to cut all funding for the program has put this assistance at risk. In response, Pappas led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025. Pappas also led a bipartisan letter in November 2025 calling for immediate distribution of funds following delays in LIHEAP allocations to states. In April of this year, Pappas again led his colleagues in a bipartisan letter following additional LIHEAP delays from HHS.

Last month Pappas led a group of 116 bipartisan members in calling on HHS to take all necessary steps to ensure that LIHEAP funds are distributed to the states as soon as possible and no later than November 1, 2026. Pappas also recently introduced the American Homes First Act which would redirect $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush to LIHEAP.

title: Chairman Pfluger Unveils USAFA Board of Visitors Semiannual Report Ahead of Meeting in Colorado Springs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11), Chairman of the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) Board of Visitors (BoV), formally sent the Board's comprehensive, forward-looking semiannual report of recommendations for the Academy to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

This report fulfills one of the Board's key statutory responsibilities and delivers a strategic roadmap to strengthen institutional effectiveness at the United States Air Force Academy. It centers on improving athletics, establishing a dedicated funding line for the Academy, and incorporating the newest technology into cadet courses.

"Airpower is relied on more heavily than ever to deter our adversaries and defend our interests around the world, and the Air Force Academy produces the leaders who deliver it. It’s our responsibility to make sure they have the resources, facilities, and training to succeed. As Chairman, I am grateful to my fellow Board members for their dedication and expertise, which are reflected in this report and its recommendations to prepare cadets for the demands of modern warfare. I look forward to working with my colleagues and Air Force Academy leadership to put these recommendations into action," said USAFA Board of Visitors Chairman August Pfluger (TX-11).

“As American air power remains critical to our national defense, we must ensure U.S. Air Force Academy cadets receive the training, education, and development needed to meet the demands of modern warfare. I am confident that the Board’s recommendations, in our report to Secretary Hegseth and Secretary Meink, will strengthen the Academy’s capacity to better prepare the next generation of Air Force officers to lead with excellence and defend our nation against evolving threats,”said Senator Ted Budd (R-NC).

“This report represents more than a year of hard work for the USAFA BoV in its effort to strengthen and improve the Air Force Academy—a premier institution for developing our future military leaders and commanders. The recommendations it lays out are focused on critical issues like cadet and instructor professional development, and especially infrastructure improvement. I look forward to working with Secretary Hegseth and the Department to implement these recommended changes and continue to position USAFA for the future with lasting improvements to meet the ever-evolving threats and increasingly complex operational environment," said Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL).

"Serving as a student at the Air Force Academy is a patriotic commitment, and the Air Force Academy Board of Visitors honors their commitment by building on the Academy’s incredible legacy for future generations of cadets. I’m grateful to my fellow board members as we share the responsibility to ensure excellence across-the-board at the Academy, from academics to athletics to infrastructure and support services. We owe it to the cadets to give them the best education and experience possible, improving our officer corps and the capabilities of the greatest Air Force in the world,"said Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND).

“The Air Force Academy and the cadets who attend this institution are essential for our national security,” said Senator Mike Rounds (R-SD). “This report makes important recommendations with regard to the training and education these cadets receive, including improvements for athletic program governance and placing greater emphasis on important programs like drone technology. It’s an honor to serve on the Air Force Academy’s Board of Visitors, and I look forward to continuing our work to improve the Academy for future generations.”

"I am proud of the work the USAFA Board of Visitors continues to accomplish. I encourage the adoption of this report’s recommendations including the establishment of a dedicated Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization funding line, to help bring Academy infrastructure up to the high standard our Cadets deserve. As well as the retention of the 70th Flying Training Squadron, and I was proud to include language in the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act to do that. I look forward to ensuring the Academy has the resources it needs to train the next generation of Air Force and Space Force leaders," said Rep. Jeff Crank (CO-05).

“As we take steps to protect ourselves from tomorrow's national security threats, it is essential now more than ever that we restore the Air Force Academy to 4,400 cadets, resolve the issue of aging infrastructure, and provide Space Force Guardians with a permanent home to maintain American superiority in air and space,” said Rep. Don Davis (NC-01).

You can read the report in its entirety HERE or see key recommendations below:

1. Establish a dedicated Facilities, Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Funding Line

2. Reform the Air Force Academy Athletic Cooperation (AFAAC) Structure and Governance

3. Open the Cadet Chapel in Phases

title: Pingree Joins Bipartisan Call to Increase Home Heating Assistance Funding
text:
Today, Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) and a bipartisan group of 73 members called on the House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in emergency supplemental appropriations for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27).

In the letter, led by New Hampshire Congressman Chris Pappas, the members wrote, “As the war with Iran remains unresolved, energy prices are expected to keep rising, with heating oil up 60% since February. LIHEAP’s $4 billion in funding for the last fiscal year would fall significantly short in meeting the needs of American families this fiscal year.”

“LIHEAP is a critical lifeline for low- and moderate-income individuals, but even if your household qualifies, LIHEAP does not provide guaranteed security. Five out of six families who qualify for LIHEAP receive no financial assistance due to the program’s woefully underfunded status. When adjusting for inflation, LIHEAP funding is lower now than it was in 1981 when the program was first created. If LIHEAP was funded at the same level as it was 45 years ago, the program would have received nearly $7 billion in FY27,” they continued.

“Emergency LIHEAP assistance is urgently needed as winter weather approaches and colder temperatures have already begun. Families should not have to choose between staying warm and purchasing other essential items like food, medication, or rent. Congress must act and not leave families in the cold,” they concluded.

LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills,including more than 45,000 households in Maine, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff last year and President Trump’s repeated demand to cut all funding for the program has put this assistance at risk. In response, Pingree and 89 of her Congressional colleagues in called for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025.

Last week, Pingree and a group of 24 Members of Congress representing Northeastern states pressed the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year. In Maine, which uses more residential heating oil per capita than any other U.S. state, the statewide average price of heating oil recently hit a record $6.02 a gallon—marking an 80% increase over last year.

Pingree is a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee and has long fought to protect and fully fund LIHEAP.

title: Op-Ed: Mainers are in for a harsh winter— thanks to Republicans
text:
Read my Op-Ed in The Portland Press Herald

Between the mountains of snow, the waves of bitter cold and the occasional Nor’easter, we Mainers are no strangers to harsh winters.

This winter could be one of the hardest in recent memory. And not because of the weather. The statewide average price of heating oil just hit a record $6.02 a gallon. As of Sept. 28, it was still averaging $5.96 — up nearly 79% from the same week last year. At today’s price, a 250-gallon fill-up costs about $1,490 — an expense many Maine families will face more than once this winter.

Meanwhile, gas prices are hovering around $4.40 per gallon as of Sept. 25, according to Maine Public.

As if all this wasn’t awful enough, the number of Mainers receiving assistance through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) has fallen by 13% — 13,000 people in all, including 7,000 children. Another 31,000 Mainers are projected to lose MaineCare coverage over the next year.

Add it all up and this winter is going to put an enormous strain on Maine families — especially those who can least afford it.

This looming crisis is the result of choices President Trump and congressional Republicans made. Choices they continue to defend.

Let’s back up to July 4, 2025, when the president signed his hallmark legislation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, into law.

The “Big Ugly Bill” is a more accurate name. It slashed Medicaid by $1.2 trillion and SNAP by $211 billion over the next decade, all while handing hundreds of billions of dollars in tax breaks to the wealthiest Americans and biggest corporations.

Far from offsetting those devastating cuts, the Big Ugly Bill’s ludicrous tax breaks are projected to increase federal deficits by $4.6 trillion, according to the Congressional Budget Office.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act also handed $175 billion to the Department of Homeland Security, helping turbocharge the Trump administration’s cruel immigration enforcement agenda and bringing chaos and violence to communities across the country. That includes Maine, where an ICE agent shot and killed 25-year-old Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford on July 13.

The young father was not the target of ICE’s operation that morning. He had no criminal history, and we don’t have body camera footage of the shooting. His family has still not been contacted by the federal government and is still waiting for a full accounting of what happened.

This bill will go down as one of the most irresponsible, destructive, and costly pieces of legislation in American history. Not just in terms of its fiscal recklessness, but its human toll as well: nearly 13 million fewer people enrolled in Medicaid by 2034 and roughly 2.4 million fewer people receiving SNAP in an average month, according to CBO estimates. Its consequences will reach every community in America, in shuttered rural hospitals, overwhelmed food banks and increased costs for state and local governments.

The Big Ugly Bill alone would have been devastating enough for Maine. Then Trump’s reckless, unauthorized war of choice in Iran has kicked every one of these crises into overdrive. In the nearly eight months since the war began — a conflict Trump insisted wouldn’t last more than a few weeks — the global economy has been thrown into turmoil.

The on-again, off-again closure of the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most important shipping chokepoints, has sent energy prices skyrocketing — and disrupted the flow of goods around the world. When the world’s energy supply gets squeezed, everyone pays more. In a state like Maine, where a colder-than-average winter can mean the difference between keeping the heat on and putting on extra layers just to stay warm, the potential consequences are catastrophic.

None of this had to happen. These crises have been created or made worse by Trump’s policies — and by congressional Republicans’ refusal to push back on the president and stand up for their constituents.

And now, with Americans staring down record energy costs, Speaker Mike Johnson sent the House home early for a seven-week campaign recess. Rather than staying to work on the many challenges facing our nation, Republicans tucked tail and left.

Republicans could’ve chosen to help you. They chose to help the already-rich get even richer — and to give an army of masked, heavily armed and utterly unaccountable ICE agents virtually unlimited resources to terrorize our communities.

My Democratic colleagues and I have been fighting them every step of the way. We’ve voted against these devastating cuts. We’ve introduced legislation to protect healthcare and food assistance. We’ve demanded accountability for an administration that continues to put its deeply unpopular agenda ahead of the people it’s supposed to serve.

And we are demanding action on the heating crisis: end the war in Iran, protect the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, reverse changes to the Home Owner Managing Energy Savings Rebates and High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebate programs and reinstate the energy efficiency tax credits Republicans eliminated. Speaker Johnson should call the House back to Washington so Congress can get to work.

We will keep fighting — at every turn, and for as long as it takes. Because Mainers deserve better. They deserve a government that makes their lives more affordable — not one that cuts their healthcare and food assistance, sends energy prices through the roof and hands massive tax breaks to the people who need them least.

Mainers have survived plenty of hard winters. But the hardships coming this winter are the result of decisions made by Republicans in Washington, who would rather leave town than fix the problems they created.

title: Amata Highlights American Samoa Constitution Day, and 70th Anniversary of Historic Photo and Appointment
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is highlighting American Samoa’s Constitution Day, October 17th, and Thursday’s 70-year mark of American Samoa’s first Samoan governor pictured with the President of the United States for the exchange of the governorship to the first Samoan to hold the office.

On October 15, 1956, Uifa’atali Governor Peter T. Coleman was pictured with President Dwight D. Eisenhower, Interior Secretary Fred Seaton, and departing appointed Governor Richard Lowe.

“This is the 70th anniversary of that historic moment, our American Samoan-born Governor on the day he took office standing with the great President Eisenhower, and it will always be a milestone in our islands’ self-determination and self-governance,” said Congresswoman Amata.

“On Saturday, we have another related major milestone, our Constitution Day. On October 17, 1960, our first Constitution went into effect, 60 years after our Tutuila forefathers joined the United States and 56 years after Manu’a joined,” continued Amata. “These two special dates in our history will always be paired closely, along with other key developments and our Flag Day most of all. Our forefathers successfully gave us the chance to treasure our Samoan way and be part of a great country. They would be proud to see that generations since have served honorably and our islands’ self-government has advanced with additional milestones, while our people are raising up leaders of the future who will be ready to continue this legacy.”

title: Ahead of Elections, Ramirez, Immigration Advocates Introduce a People-Centered Vision for Immigration Reform
text:
Chicago, IL – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, immigration advocates, and community members unveiled the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform, a resolution outlining policy priorities to preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. As the elections approaches and the House of Representatives prepares for the 120th Congress, the resolution calls on the House of Representatives to pass real protections for immigrant communities.

The resolution calls on Congress to transform our immigration system and advance humane immigration reform with:

Pathways to citizenship for the millions of undocumented, long-term residents of the United States who are our family members, friends and neighbors;

Humanitarian protections that welcome with dignity those who are seeking safety and asylum in the United States, upholding our domestic and international legal obligations to provide refuge to those in need; and

Expanded legal pathways for family and employment immigration, recognizing that family unity and strengthened protections for all workers in the United States are foundations of thriving communities for all.

“For years, administration after administration, Congress after Congress, has promised relief and has asked our communities to wait for the ‘right time,’ for the ‘politically convenient time,’” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “So today, we announced the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform – a resolution that reaffirms the commitment of Members of Congress to act in defense of our immigrant communities and preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. Now is the time to build a system that honors the contributions of our immigrant neighbors. No more excuses or peros.”

The resolution’s original cosponsors include Representatives Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-04), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Federica S. Wilson (FL-24), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), and Al Green (TX-09).

“Immigrants have bound our communities together, continue to contribute to our economy, and embody everything that Americans are made of and striving to be. All of which they do while asking nothing in return but the opportunity to reach for and obtain the American Dream,” said Congresswoman Yvette Clarke. “The 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States must not be only the opportunity to reflect on how far we have come; it must be an obligation to remember the terrible price that we pay to reach here. The People’s Vision for Immigration Reform is in large part the only future for this nation worth fighting for.”

“It’s time to send out a strong vision of where we need to be. We have spent an awful lot of time in Washington talking about immigration enforcement this year, but not nearly enough time talking about how we fix the system that has been broken for decades,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “We need an immigration system that gives people a fair chance. We can start by making progress now. That’s why I’m leading the discharge petition of the American Dream and Promise Act; we are just one signature away from getting a forced vote. We need to get serious about real reform, not another round of empty promises.”

The bill is endorsed by a coalition of more than 60 national and and local organizations, including Immigration Law Center (NILC), Fair Immigration Reform Movement (FIRM) and FIRM Action, National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC), League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), Haitian Bridge Alliance, United We Dream (UWD), Refugees International, National Partnership for New Americans (NPNA), Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC), Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), Human Rights First, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, Justice in Motion, Indivisible, Service Employees International Union (SEIU), National Health Care for the Homeless Council, United Parent Leaders Action Network (UPLAN), Children's Rights, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, Community Change Action, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR) and ICIRR Action, CAIR Chicago, Grassroots Collaborative, Warehouse Workers for Justice, National Korean American Service and Education Consortium (NAKASEC), Indivisible Chicago Alliance, Hana Center, Here to Stay Community Land Trust, Illinois Unidos, PASO, Organized Communities Against Deportation (OCAD), Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition, Jewish Council on Urban Affairs (JCUA), Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC), Popular Democracy, Florida Immigrant Coalition (FLIC), SIREN, Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice, Maine People's Alliance, We are CASA, Workers Defense Action Fund, Make the Road States, Voces de la Frontera, Make the Road New York, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA), Council of Mexican Federations in North America (COFEM), Sunflower Community Action, East Bay Sanctuary Covenant (EBSC), Federación de Clubes Michoacanos en Illinois (FEDECMI), Nebraska Appleseed, and Pineros Y Campesinos Unidos Del Noroeste (PCUN).

“Over the last 40 years we’ve seen the consequences, not only the inability of Congress to prioritize legislation, but of the overreach of the Trump administration that has taken a sledgehammer to refugee admissions, temporary protected status, health care and food access and the basic simple notion that all people in this country deserve due process under the law,” said Lawrence Benito, ICIRR Executive Director. “We know we need permanent solutions, not chaos and fear. We’re here today to recommit to dignity and respect for all through legalization and keeping families together.”

“Let me be clear: Our economy works because of workers, and for generations, immigrant workers have poured their sweat, their strength, and their labor into building this country. Working families deserve to go to work, provide for their families, and return home safely without fear of being detained or disappeared,” Laura Garza, Executive Director at Arise Chicago. “Now is the time to demand real protections for communities. It’s time to expand pathways to citizenship and ensure all working families can live and work with dignity and safety. As communities mobilize across the country, we stand together in our power to change our country’s direction.”

“Immigrants deserve a system that provides dignity, fairness, and a real opportunity for a life in this country. Congress must do its job to defend our neighbors by creating viable pathways. Otherwise, the executive branch will be able to continue to sow chaos in our communities, return refugees to danger, and trample our Constitution,” said Keren Zwick, Executive Director at the National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC). “NIJC stands ready to advance lasting solutions, even as we continue to fight the problems this administration created.”

“At PASO, we see the resilience of our communities, but resilience should never mean having to live in fear. Instead of being supported, our communities are increasingly being targeted because of their immigration status. But we have resisted, organized, advocated, and continue doing the work to prepare families for citizenship and help them navigate the immigration system. We have done our part, and now the federal government must do theirs. Because the truth is, no matter how much we prepare our communities, if the federal government fails to create real pathways to citizenship, our families will continue to face barriers,” Marien Casillas Pabellon, PASO Executive Director.

“While ICE and DHS terrorize our communities and attack and deport our neighbors, Congress has not acted. While most Americans support creating and ensuring legal pathways to citizenship for immigrants, Congress has done nothing. Their silence enables this administration's campaign of terror against immigrants and their families. Today, as voters, we must demand that our elected representatives take action to create pathways to citizenship and legal status and protect immigrants and their families from abuse by our government,” said Kathy Tholin with Indivisible Chicago.

“Asians are the fastest-growing racial group in the US, and 1 out of 7 undocumented immigrants is Asian. We are longstanding generations, mixed-status families, and new Americans who call this country home. We are all affected by the militarized violence, immigration backlogs, unaffordable costs, and attacks by this President and some Congress members against anyone they think doesn’t belong,” said Danae Kovac, HANA Center Executive Director. “Immigration affects all of us, and let me be clear: our country needs pathways to citizenship. HANA Center will continue to fight alongside Congresswoman Ramirez for Citizenship for All, not only for a pathway to citizenship, but also for the healthcare, education, climate justice, and more that we all need and deserve. Together, we, the people, can create an America where every person belongs and thrives.”

“It is long past time to lift up families and embrace the worth of each of our neighbors. It is time to reject the politics of fear and division that have marked too much of the discussion around immigration in recent years,” said Ed Yohnka, ACLU Illinois Director of Communications and Public Policy. “In recent months, we have seen how years of rhetoric meant to stall meaningful immigration reform can be turned to justify a military-style invasion of our communities and cause too many hard-working people to live in fear and isolation. Immigration policy does not have to be this way. Immigration policy can be based on a commitment to family unification, a commitment to fairness and due process, and a recognition of the dignity and worth that people from other countries and other cultures bring to the United States.

“As a recently naturalized citizen, I have a message to those like me who can now exercise that power. The power of our vote. Let’s show our humanity in how we treat our neighbors, but also let’s show solidarity at the ballot box,” Fasika Alem, United African Organization (UAO) Programs Director. “Elections matter. Make a plan and vote.”

“Our church is home to Indigenous people and to immigrants, old and new. People without documents worship in our assemblies and lead our ministries. Scripture commands: ‘Love the stranger as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.’ For decades, our church has urged compassionate ways for longtime undocumented neighbors to gain legal status,” said Bishop Erik Christensen of the Metropolitan Chicago Synod of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America. “Forty years ago, Congress opened a path to citizenship and those who received status in time became citizens, homeowners, and neighbors. Now is the time to finish that work.

"As a Haitian immigrant, experiencing the agonizing pain and fear of the Haitian community every day who have lost TPS, I particularly welcome the resolution, because it brings to light all the changes needed in our immigration system to ensure the safety of our immigrant friends and family members who are here and deserve justice and dignity,” said Tessa Petit, Florida Immigrant Coalition Executive Director and Co-Chair of FIRM. “It is time for immigrants to no longer be treated as political pawns and sub-creatures, and this resolution will engage Congress to put an end to the abuse of our communities.”

“1 of every 4 ICE arrests happen in Texas. In just over three months, ICE shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin, hospitalized Miguel Parra-Hernandez after striking him with an ICE vehicle in Houston, and has separated countless of families,” said Lizeth Chacon, Workers Defense Executive Director. “Immigrant workers and their families strengthen and build our state – Texas is their home, and for many it has been for more than 30 years. It's time for Congress to act, for there to be an end to ICE violence and a real pathway to citizenship for all immigrant workers and their families.”

“For 25 years, my mother and I were both undocumented. We were able to adjust to legal permanent residency because we qualified for a U visa, something that only undocumented immigrants who are victims of a violent crime could apply for. There are over 12 million undocumented immigrants in the United States who have no pathway to citizenship and I sure wish not a single one ever needs to apply to a U visa,” said Jose-Arnulfo Cabrera, National Campaigns and Congressional Affairs Deputy Director, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA). “But that is how broken our immigration system is and why Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution is quite important today.”

The violence of the Department of Homeland Security under the Trump administration has only served to underscore citizenship's importance. Last week, a five year old child had to watch his father get shot by agents of our government. He is only the latest child to be failed by the unimageable cruelty of the DHS's at-all-costs approach to mass deportations,” said Ben D’Avanzo, National Immigration Law Center. “But he was also failed by our completely broken immigration system that has allowed families to go without health care, be abused by their employers, and stripped of longtime protections. This resolution represents the right pathway, one that upholds our core values and refuses to pit immigrant communities against each other.”

“LULAC is proud to support Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution to protect immigrant families, defend workers, and create pathways to citizenship. As America celebrates 250 years of independence, we should remember who helped build this country,” said Dr. Ray Serrano, National Director of Research & Policy, League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC). “Congress needs to act. Keep families together. Protect workers. Give people a fair chance at citizenship. Our families helped build this country. We deserve a place in its future.”

“The Haitian and other immigrant communities are being terrorized, racially profiled and persecuted by an immigration enforcement system that has placed families in fear of separation, detention, deportation, and forced return to a country facing profound humanitarian and security challenges,” said Guerline Jozef, Executive Director of Haitian Bridge Alliance. “The Reimagining Safety Act offers an opportunity to fundamentally rethink a system that has caused enormous harm to immigrant communities and provide pathways to people who have an integral, essential part of our communities across the U.S. Safety cannot be achieved through fear. It must be grounded in dignity, due process, family unity, and the protection of human rights.”

title: Rep. Torres Announces Power To The Players Act, Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Games
text:
Today, Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15) announced he will introduce the Power To The Players Act, legislation that would direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish regulations protecting consumers’ ability to own and play the video games they purchase.

Over the past few years, video game companies have moved toward digital-only games and consoles, removing the option to buy or use physical games. These digital games are often sold as revocable licenses rather than owned outright, leaving players dependent on the company’s continued support. NBA 2K25 is a clear example. The game, which retailed for $69.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the All-Star Edition, will be delisted from digital storefronts on October 30 and will have its online servers shut down on December 31, only two years after its initial release. No consumer should have a game they paid for pulled out from under them on a company’s arbitrary timeline.

“When you pay for a game, you should own it,” said Rep. Torres. “Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”

Under the bill, buying a video game would give the consumer ownership of the game rather than a license to play it. Games with online functionality would also be required to provide an offline mode before the servers supporting them are shut down.

The legislation aims to close the gap between buying a game and owning it. By preserving consumers’ ability to own and resell their games, the bill would ensure that players can keep playing the games they paid for with friends and family for years to come.

title: Sherman & Lawmakers Challenge Trump Administration’s Effort to Restart California Oil Pipeline
text:
SHERMAN OAKS, CA — Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32) joined Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Congressman Salud Carbajal (D-CA), and a coalition of Democratic lawmakers in challenging the Trump Administration’s efforts to restart the Sable Offshore oil pipeline in California, arguing that the Administration is unlawfully invoking national defense powers to benefit the fossil fuel industry.

In an amicus brief filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, Sherman and his colleagues urged the court to reverse a lower court ruling that allowed the pipeline to continue operating despite questions surrounding the Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA).

The lawmakers argue that the Trump Administration has failed to demonstrate any legitimate national defense necessity for restarting the pipeline, which had remained idle for nearly 11 years. Instead, they contend that the Administration is misusing extraordinary federal authority to circumvent California law and financially benefit a politically connected oil company.

The brief also raises concerns about potential pay-to-play politics, noting that the project was headed by a Trump donor and questioning whether the Administration's intervention was motivated by national security considerations or political favoritism.

Sherman and his colleagues emphasized that the Defense Production Act was intended to address genuine national defense needs, not provide the federal government with unchecked authority to intervene on behalf of private companies.

The lawmakers urged the Ninth Circuit to reverse the district court's denial of a preliminary injunction, arguing that the lower court failed to adequately scrutinize the Administration's national defense justification.

The effort was led by Senators Whitehouse, Padilla, and Schiff, along with Congressman Carbajal. Sherman joined Senator Tammy Duckworth and ten other House Democrats in signing the brief.

text:
OAKLAND, CA – Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12) has completed her second town hall tour since being sworn into Congress in January 2025. In 2026, she held town halls in all seven cities that she represents in California’s 12th Congressional District, reaching thousands of constituents in Oakland, Berkeley, Albany, San Leandro, Alameda, Piedmont, and Emeryville.

This year’s town hall tour builds on Congresswoman Simon’s previous 2025 town hall tour where she held eleven town halls across the East Bay, reaching more than 15,000 constituents in person, virtually, and by telephone.

“As the Trump Administration and Republicans in Congress continue to cut vital programs and services while funding the unlawful, violent terrorization our immigrant communities, hearing stories and the impacts of the Republican agenda on the families living in our communities everyday has been invaluable. Every single day I take the voices from our district and fight for better conditions and resources in Congress,” said Congresswoman Lateefah Simon. “I am grateful to every community member from Albany to San Leandro who joined me on this year’s town hall tour to raise the issues most important to you and how I can continue to serve and fight for us. Though this year has brought challenges, the resilience and joy of the East Bay inspires me every day, and I look forward to continuing to meet with and hear from neighbors across our beautiful district.”

During her town hall tour, the Congresswoman shared updates with constituents on: (1) the Congresswoman’s legislative work in Congress during her second year, including her work as a member in the House Oversight Committee and Small Business Committee; (2) recent bills she’s introduced to support small business owners, public transportation, and workers with disabilities; (3) recent efforts to protect reproductive, disability, labor, and civil rights; (3) the over $11.1 million in federal Community Project Funding that the Congresswoman secured for projects across the East Bay; (4) updates on the Congresswoman’s work to oppose the proposed Oakland coal export terminal funded by the Trump Administration and demand answers on the status of the Alameda Point Veterans Affairs outpatient clinic and columbarium project, (5), attacks on immigrant communities and resources to help; and (6) how Californians can stay involved and continue to fight back.

title: Rep. Summer Lee Celebrates $850,000 in Federal Funding for New West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center
text:
Photos (Dropbox)

PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 15, 2026 — Yesterday, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined West Mifflin Borough officials and community leaders for a ceremonial groundbreaking and check presentation celebrating $850,000 in federal funding she secured for the planned West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center.

The funding, secured through the federal Community Project Funding process, will support the development of a new community facility at 371 Camp Hollow Road, creating a dedicated space for recreation, wellness, youth activities, senior programming, and community gatherings.

“I’m proud to have secured $850,000 in federal funding to help make the new West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center a reality,” said Rep. Lee. “Folks in West Mifflin deserve a space where kids can grow, seniors can stay active, and families have somewhere to come together—right in their own backyards. I'm grateful to our borough leaders and state partners for helping bring us this far and look forward to seeing how this space transforms generations to come.”

"The Borough of West Mifflin extends its sincere thanks to Congresswoman Summer Lee for helping secure this funding. This project represents an important investment in West Mifflin’s future, creating opportunities for recreation, community programs, senior services, and activities for residents of all ages. We are grateful to Congresswoman Lee for her support and partnership in helping bring this vision closer to reality. This project will be a valuable asset to our community and region for generations to come,” said Michael Moses, Council President.

The project will transform an undeveloped site into a community destination designed to serve residents of all ages. Plans for the facility include indoor athletic and recreational spaces, public meeting rooms, youth activities, senior programming, and spaces for civic and community services.

Alongside the $850,000 in federal funding secured by Rep. Lee, the project has received an additional $425,000 through Pennsylvania's Statewide Local Share Account program, bringing combined federal and state funding commitments to $1.275 million.

Through her Community Project Funding efforts, Rep. Lee has secured direct investments for community-based organizations, including a $1 million CPF award to the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank, $450,000 to the Trade Institute of Pittsburgh, over $1.5 million in federal support for the Tree of Life rebuilding and healing initiatives, $1 million in Community Project Funding for historic renovations at the Carnegie Library of Homestead, more than $1 million in federal funding to combat blight and revitalize housing in North Braddock, and $1 million to help turn vacant office space into affordable homes, create good-paying jobs, and bring new life to downtown Pittsburgh.

These projects are part of more than $24.9 million in Community Project Funding secured during her time in Congress. Rep. Lee’s office has consistently directed federal dollars to historically overlooked communities to ensure equitable access to opportunities and long-term regional growth and stability.

title: Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia Joins Field Hearing in Austin to Examine ICE Shootings Across Texas
text:
AUSTIN, T.X. — Today, Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29) joined Democratic Members of Congress for a field hearing in Austin to examine shootings involving federal immigration agents across Texas and demand greater transparency and accountability from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The hearing was led by Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX-35), Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS-02), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal (D-WA-07), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement.

Also participating were Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA-02), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX-07), and Al Green (D-TX-09).

The hearing examined incidents involving federal immigration agents, including the July 7 killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, the killing of Ruben Ray Martinez, and the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez in Austin.

The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.

"Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we're seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE's recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability," said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. "In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead, they've been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both."

title: Congressman Taylor Introduces Bill to Return More Federal Lands Revenue to Ohio
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Dave Taylor (OH-02) today introduced the Acquired Lands Revenue Modernization Act, which would increase the share of qualifying revenue states receive from energy development on federally acquired lands. This bill would double the share of revenue generated through energy development in the Wayne National Forest back to southern Ohio communities. Senator Bernie Moreno (R-OH) introduced companion legislation in the Senate today.

“Ohio is leading the nation in energy development, and the Wayne National Forest plays a critical role in that effort,” said Congressman Taylor. “With more than 240,000 acres of land located almost entirely in Ohio’s Second Congressional District, our communities deserve to reap more of the rewards of energy development taking place in our own backyard. I’m proud to lead this effort to keep revenue close to home and ensure southern Ohio communities share in the economic benefits of American energy production.”

Under current law, states receive 25% of qualifying revenue generated from energy development on federally qualified lands, while the government retains 75%. The Acquired Lands Revenue Modernization Act would establish an even 50/50 revenue split, returning a greater share from federal land leases, rentals, and royalties to the states where development occurs. This change would provide additional resources to support communities near these projects.

The Acquired Lands Revenue Modernization Act will be referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources for consideration. The full bill text is available here.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Introduces Bipartisan IRAN Act to Expand Internet Freedom for the Iranian People
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswomen Claudia Tenney (NY-24) and Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) today introduced the bipartisan Internet Reach and Access Now (IRAN) Act to strengthen U.S. efforts to help the Iranian people access the open internet, communicate securely, and overcome the Iranian regime’s censorship, surveillance, and internet shutdowns.

Additional cosponsors of the legislation include Representatives Virginia Foxx (NC-5), Maria Elvira Salazar (FL-27), Dave Min (CA-47), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1), Mike Lawler (NY-17), Ilhan Omar (MN-5), Stephanie Bice (OK-5), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), Jake Auchincloss (MA-4), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and André Carson (IN-7).

Iran remains one of the world’s most restrictive digital environments, with the regime routinely restricting internet access to suppress dissent, conceal human rights abuses, and isolate the Iranian people. The IRAN Act strengthens the U.S. internet freedom strategy for Iran by requiring regular reviews, implementation assessments, and congressional reporting, while evaluating emerging technologies such as VPNs, decentralized and peer to peer networks, and direct to cell satellite communications. The legislation also seeks to expand cybersecurity training and secure digital tools for journalists, human rights defenders, and other civil society actors, and directs greater coordination among federal agencies to help ensure U.S. sanctions and export controls do not unintentionally hinder access to open internet technologies.

“The Iranian regime knows that access to information is a threat to its grip on power, which is why it relies on censorship, surveillance, and internet blackouts to silence the Iranian people,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “The United States should stand with the courageous Iranians demanding basic freedoms by helping them stay connected to one another and the outside world. The bipartisan IRAN Act strengthens our internet freedom strategy, supports secure technologies that can overcome the regime’s censorship, and improves coordination across our government so these efforts deliver real results. The Iranian people deserve the ability to communicate freely, access independent information, and expose the regime’s brutality to the world.”

“Freedom of expression and access to unrestricted information are fundamental human rights. The Islamic Republic regularly shuts down or restricts internet access while committing mass atrocities,” said Congresswoman Ansari. “President Trump has said 'help is on the way' for the Iranian people. Ensuring unrestricted internet access would actually help people immediately. I’m proud to introduce the IRAN Act, a bipartisan, noncontroversial, and not militarily invasive bill that would do just that.”

This legislation is supported by the Public Affairs Alliance of Iranian Americans (PAAIA):

“The Iranian regime has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to shut down the internet to isolate the Iranian people and facilitate the violent suppression of dissent, as we saw during the January 2026 crackdown on protesters. The revised IRAN Act strengthens the U.S. response by improving coordination across the federal government, ensuring our internet freedom strategy keeps pace with emerging technologies, and helping preserve access to satellite communications over Iran. Helping ordinary Iranians stay connected, access independent information, and communicate with the outside world not only supports their democratic aspirations, but also advances broader U.S. national security interests by promoting the free flow of information and greater transparency. PAAIA thanks Representatives Claudia Tenney and Yassamin Ansari for their bipartisan leadership and encourages all Members of Congress to support and help pass this important legislation.” - PAAIA

title: Rep. Dina Titus Introduces Legislation to Protect Americans from High Costs at the Pump
text:
Congresswoman Dina Titus introduced legislation today to require the Department of Transportation to examine whether it can strengthen fuel efficiency requirements to counter high gas prices and reinstate penalties for automakers that fail to produce fuel-efficient vehicles.

“With gas prices skyrocketing because of President Trump’s prolonged and illegal war, we must take immediate steps to give American consumers some relief,” Congresswoman Titus said. “In May 2026, gas prices rose at a rate ten times higher than the rate of inflation. In Nevada, they now average $5.45 per gallon. Coupled with higher prices on groceries and other goods because of the Trump tariffs, families are struggling to make ends meet.”

Congresswoman Titus, a member of the House Transportation Committee. and co-sponsor Doris Matsui, (CA-7), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, introduced the Gas Money Saved Act to review Corporate Fuel Economy (CAFÉ) standards and reinstate fuel-efficiency requirements that were stripped away by Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill in 2025. Companion legislation has been introduced in the Senate by Senator Ed Markey (D-MA).

“These giveaways to Big Oil and automakers worsened the pain at the pump and should not stand,” Congresswoman Titus said.

“Fuel economy standards help American drivers get around without breaking the bank while gas prices are high, but Trump and the Republicans gutted these standards as part of their crusade to put Big Oil above American families,” said Senator Markey. “Auto innovation should give consumers better choices, not cut corners at their expense. The Gas Money Saved Act would make sure American drivers have fuel-efficient vehicle options that are cheaper to fill up and hold automakers to account—a cost-saving measure that is especially critical as the Trump Administration would rather spend billions on an illegal war than keep costs low for Americans.”

“Across the country, Americans are being squeezed by high gas prices, rising grocery bills, and everyday costs that keep stretching family budgets thinner,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Gas Money Saved Act meets people where they are by strengthening fuel efficiency standards that help drivers spend less on gas for years to come. This is a practical step to lower everyday costs, give families more breathing room, and build a cleaner, more efficient transportation future.”

The Gas Money Saved Act would:

Require DOT to reevaluate Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE)standards if gas prices rise at a rate five times faster than inflation over a six-month period, and;

Restore and increase financial penalties on automakers if their car and truck fleet does not meet fuel efficiency standards.

title: Representatives Torres and Fleischmann Lead Bipartisan Bill to Build America’s Advanced Manufacturing Workforce
text:
Legislation expands workforce training and connects workers with good paying careers in growing manufacturing industries

Washington, D.C. – Today, during National Manufacturing Month, Representatives Norma Torres (CA-35) and Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03) introduced the bipartisan Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act of 2026, legislation to help workers train for and connect with advanced manufacturing careers. The legislation, which was inspired by the successful public-private partnership that created the InTech Center at Chaffey College in Fontana, would direct the Department of Labor to initiate pilot projects between local community colleges, state and tribal colleges, local boards, advanced manufacturers, and Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) centers that are focused on education, training, and apprenticeship programs for advanced manufacturing jobs.

“Manufacturing is a cornerstone of the Inland Empire’s economy, and we need to make sure our workforce is prepared for the jobs of tomorrow,” said Congresswoman Torres. “The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act will bring manufacturers, community colleges, and workforce partners together to give workers the skills they need to secure good-paying careers while helping American manufacturers find the talent they need to grow. Investing in American manufacturing means investing in American workers, and I am proud to partner with Congressman Fleischmann on this bipartisan effort.”

“Manufacturing is the backbone of America, driving our economy, creating jobs, and building the foundation of our nation’s prosperity. East Tennessee is leading the way in America’s reindustrialization, showing how innovation and hard work can revitalize our manufacturing sector. This legislation is vital to keeping America competitive and strong. I am honored to champion this effort in Congress and remain committed to supporting American manufacturing and the dedicated people who power it,” said Congressman Fleischmann.

The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act would amend the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to establish pilot projects focused on advanced manufacturing education and training. The bill would support partnerships between advanced manufacturers and community colleges, workforce development boards, Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers, local educational agencies, and other eligible organizations. Programs could include classroom and hands on learning, on-the-job training, and registered apprenticeships and pre-apprenticeships.

The legislation would prioritize dislocated and unemployed workers. Eligible recipients must demonstrate their capacity to teach the skills needed for advanced manufacturing jobs and provide workers with a recognized postsecondary credential.

The bill is inspired by the public-private partnership at the InTech Center at Chaffey College, a regional training center that trains and upskills students and employed workers for in-demand technical careers at no cost. In 2014, the Chaffey College and the Inland Empire Regional Training Consortium (IERTC) received a $15 million grant from the Department of Labor, which resulted in the 2016 opening of the InTech Center, a partnership between Chaffey College and California Steel Industries (now Nucor-CSI). The center was California's first public-private workforce training partnership in advanced manufacturing. Located in Fontana, CA, the center now works with more than 70 employers in the region and is an example of how federal funding can jumpstart successful public-private workforce development programs in advanced manufacturing.

Earlier this month, Reps. Torres and Fleischmann led a bipartisan resolution recognizing National Manufacturing Day and the contributions of manufacturers and workers across the country. In 2022, Reps. Torres & Fleischmann also secured the inclusion of their bicameral, bipartisan National MEP Supply Chain Database Act in the CHIPS and Science Act (Public Law 117-167) to help manufacturers prepare for future supply chain challenges.

title: Congressman Turner Honors Jenell Ross for Decades of Community Service
text:
DAYTON, OH — Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10) honored Jenell Ross with a Community Service Award on Thursday, recognizing her decades of leadership in the Dayton business community, her philanthropic work and her commitment to serving the Miami Valley.

“I’ve known Jenell and the Ross family for more than 30 years, and I’ve had the privilege of watching her carry forward an extraordinary family legacy while building one of our region’s most respected businesses,” said Rep. Turner. “Whether through her business, her philanthropy or her service to organizations across our community, Jenell has always understood that leadership comes with a responsibility to help others. I’m proud to recognize her for the extraordinary difference she has made in Dayton.”

Jenell’s father, Bob Ross, was the first African American Buick dealer in Ohio, and the first African American Mercedes-Benz dealer in the country. After his passing, Jenell stepped up to lead the family business. She became vice president of Bob Ross Auto Group at just 27 years old before eventually becoming president of the company, which flourished under her leadership as one of the region’s most respected businesses.

Jenell became the only second-generation African American female automobile dealer in the United States and the first African American Chair of the American International Automobile Dealers Association.

When Jenell’s mother, Norma Ross, tragically passed away from breast cancer, Jenell established the Norma J. Ross Memorial Foundation, which has raised hundreds of thousands of dollars for breast cancer research and awareness. She’s also served numerous community organizations and institutions throughout the Miami Valley while continuing to lead the family business founded by her father.

title: Congressman Valadao Supports Legislation to Reinvest Federal Funds Back Into State Medicaid Programs
text:
WASHINGTON – Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) supported the Helping Encourage Lawful Payments and Strengthen Transparency, Anti-fraud, Tips, and Enforcement Strategies (HELP STATES) Act by joining as an original co-sponsor. This bill would allow states to retain a larger share of the federal portion of Medicaid overpayments recovered from fraud and require those dollars to be reinvested in state efforts to prevent, detect, and combat fraud, strengthening the program for the future.

This bill was introduced by Reps. Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07), Rob Wittman (VA-01), Jen Kiggans (VA-02), Young Kim (CA-40), and Rob Bresnahan (PA-08) and is part of a larger package of 14 bills to incentivize federally-funded health program fraud-fighting efforts.

“Medicaid provides critical support to families across the Central Valley, and it’s important we do everything we can to ensure funds are properly distributed,” said Congressman Valadao. “I’m proud to support the HELP STATES Act, which would give states a greater incentive to crack down on fraud, reinvest recovered funds into preventing future abuse, and ensure benefits reach the people they’re intended to help."

Background:

Under current law, when a state recovers an improper Medicaid payment due to fraud, it usually must return the federal government’s share of that recovery. The HELP STATES Act would allow a state to retain up to 25% of the federal share of a qualifying fraud recovery. These funds would be used by states to support Medicaid program-integrity activities aimed at preventing, identifying, and recovering fraudulent payments.

title: Vindman Leads Effort in U.S. House to Ban Live-Streaming of Military Executions in the United States
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced the American Integrity Act to prohibit the live-streaming of executions under the Uniformed Code of Military Justice following President Donald Trump’s decision to cancel Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s plans to broadcast the execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the horrific 2009 Fort Hood shooting.

The bill would establish a federal prohibition on live-streaming military executions, ensuring that such broadcasts cannot be authorized by future administrations.

The legislation comes after widespread opposition to the proposal, including from Vindman, who publicly called on Hegseth to reverse course and abandon plans to turn Hasan’s execution into a public spectacle.

“Having overseen the post-trial legal proceedings in Nidal Hasan’s case, I know firsthand the gravity of his horrific crimes. I believed then, and I believe now, that he should face the fullest consequences of the law,” said Vindman. “But there is a fundamental difference between carrying out justice and turning an execution into a public spectacle. Live-streaming executions is what terrorists and authoritarian regimes do. I’m glad the president ultimately reversed course, but we should never have reached this point in the first place. The American justice system must uphold the rule of law and the dignity of our institutions. My legislation will ensure that no future administration can turn an execution into a televised spectacle.”

The bill is sponsored by U.S. Representatives Ro Khanna (Calif.-17), Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-02), and George Whitesides (Calif.-27).

Click here to read the full bill text.

BACKGROUND

As an Army Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer, Vindman oversaw the post-trial legal proceedings following Hasan’s attack at Fort Hood. His direct involvement in the case gave him firsthand experience with the gravity of Hasan’s crimes and the importance of ensuring justice is carried out.

title: Walkinshaw Introduces Bill to Cool Federal Properties, Cut Smog, and Lower Energy Costs
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) introduced the Heat Island Reduction Act, which would require federal agencies to plan cost-effective upgrades that cool their properties, improve air quality, and lower energy costs.

Parking lots and dark rooftops soak up heat and hold it, which warms nearby communities, raises cooling bills, and speeds the formation of smog. The bill targets federal properties in areas that already fail federal smog standards.

Northern Virginia is already working on the problem. This summer, more than 80 volunteers teamed up with the Faith Alliance for Climate Solutions and George Mason University’s Virginia Climate Center to map where heat hits hardest across Fairfax County, Arlington, and Alexandria. What they found points to simple fixes: more trees, more shade, and cooler surfaces. Walkinshaw’s bill would apply the same approach to federal properties nationwide.

“Extreme heat endangers workers, worsens the air our families breathe, and drives up cooling costs,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Volunteers here in Northern Virginia are working to pinpoint where heat hits hardest. The federal government should take the same hard look at its own properties and start with the fixes that deliver the most. Shade trees and cooler roofs protect federal workers and visitors and lower the cooling bills taxpayers pay.”

The Heat Island Reduction Act would:

Within six months: Require agencies to plan cooling fixes, such as trees, shade, cool roofs, and cooler pavement, for their properties in areas that fail federal smog standards.

Six months later: Require agencies to set out each project’s cost, funding source, and timeline, and to update these plans every two years.

Every year: Require the General Services Administration to report to Congress on progress, spending, and changes in temperature and energy use.

At every step: Prioritize cost-effective fixes and build them into routine repairs and construction.

Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20) and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC) are original cosponsors.
