title: Wittman, Deputy Secretary Danly Visit Yorktown, Newport News
text:
Newport News, VA – Congressman Rob Wittman (VA-01) hosted Deputy Secretary of Energy James Danly in Virginia’s First District for site visits to the Jefferson Lab (JLAB) and Naval Weapons Station Yorktown. The purpose of the visit was to highlight JLAB’s role in advancing U.S. scientific research, cutting-edge technology, and national security, and Naval Weapons Station Yorktown’s energy needs and opportunities to strengthen energy security and grid resilience.

“Virginia’s First District is home to world-class research facilities and critical military installations that play an essential role in our economic and national security,” said Rep. Wittman. “It was a pleasure to welcome Deputy Secretary Danly to the First District to showcase the groundbreaking work being done at Jefferson Lab and discuss the importance of reliable, resilient energy infrastructure at Naval Weapons Station Yorktown. From investing in scientific innovation to modernizing our military installations, we must ensure that our nation has the technology, infrastructure, and resources necessary to remain competitive and maintain a strong national defense.”

Background:

At Jefferson Lab, Congressman Wittman and Deputy Secretary Danly discussed the Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission and investments in scientific research, including accelerator technology, materials science, and innovations with potential applications in energy and national defense. The visit highlighted Jefferson Lab’s contributions to American scientific leadership, STEM workforce development, and the Hampton Roads region's growing research and technology sectors.

At Naval Weapons Station Yorktown, discussions focused on strengthening the installation’s energy security, modernizing critical infrastructure, and improving grid resilience to support military readiness. The visit also provided an opportunity to explore the potential applications of advanced nuclear technologies, including small modular reactors (SMRs), in providing reliable power to critical defense installations and nearby communities.

As vice chairman of the House Armed Services Committee and chairman of the Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee, Congressman Wittman remains committed to strengthening America's defense capabilities, supporting technological innovation, and ensuring our military installations have the reliable energy infrastructure necessary to carry out their missions.

title: Baldwin, Murray Call on Education Department to Abandon Latest Tactic to Cut Grant Funding to Communities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Ranking Member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, called on Department of Education Secretary Linda McMahon to reverse the department’s policy that is dramatically reducing the number of recipients of federal funding. This concerted effort to get fewer grants and fewer resources to local communities is in line with the Administration’s stated goal to shutter the Department of Education entirely.

The Department of Education significantly expanded its use of “frontloading” grants— the tactic wherein it pays for a multi-year grant fully up front instead of one year at a time, thereby dramatically decreasing the number of grants it awards—across a number of grant programs in unprecedented ways in Fiscal Year 2026. This has occurred at the same time the Department of Education and the Office of Management and Budget are seeking broader authority to terminate grants, raising the specter that they will terminate some of these grants in the future, and the funding will never reach communities that need it—yet another backdoor way of withholding appropriated funding.

“This administration has chosen—brazenly and repeatedly—to prioritize its own backwards agenda over the needs of students, families, and communities across the United States. The Department of Education’s extensive ‘frontloading’ of grants is just the latest example,” wrote the Senators in a letter to Sec. of Education Linda McMahon. “By ‘frontloading’ grants—paying out many years of a multi-year grant in one lump sum instead of funding a larger number of grants right now—your Department is dramatically reducing the number of students and schools that are helped by federal funding. This policy defies congressional intent and effectively cuts investment in communities across the country.”

Senator Baldwin’s office has heard directly from Wisconsin schools whose funding was impacted by the Trump administration’s decision, including Madison Area Technical College, for a program to help low-income student parents access childcare while pursuing higher education. While the program had previously been awarded a competitive grant and funded on an annual basis from Fiscal Year 2022 to Fiscal Year 2026, they were not selected for funding when reapplying for the grant as the Trump Administration dramatically cut the number of programs they funded in the childcare access program. In their letter, Murray and Baldwin explain how frontloading grants for several programs resulted in a steep drop-off in awards made in fiscal year 2026.

“Instead of deploying funds immediately to hundreds of additional communities for essential education and related services, the Department is withholding approximately $630 million in appropriated resources across approximately 35 grant programs, preventing those funds from reaching students and families now. These are all programs where the Department has historically funded grants on an annual basis,” wrote the Senators. “If the Department continued that practice in administering these programs, the Department could have awarded well over 1,000 additional grants this year, supporting everything from evidence-based student literacy programs, to improving student mental health, to recruiting and preparing high-quality teachers, to supporting additional education research and to helping first-generation students succeed in college.”

“This policy is indefensible. The Department must immediately abandon this approach and administer appropriated funds in full alignment with both the law and the needs of the communities that rely on these programs,” they concluded.

“We can’t move forward on equitable access to student success and workforce development in Wisconsin while ignoring the basic supports that make that happen. Losing CCAMPIS funding threatens to interrupt Madison College students’ education at the very moment they are building a better future for their families. We must work together on a solution for student parents to keep learning, complete their credentials and contribute to Wisconsin’s economic prosperity,” said Dr. Jennifer Berne, President of Madison Area Technical College.

The full letter is available here and below:

Secretary McMahon:

This administration has chosen—brazenly and repeatedly—to prioritize its own backwards agenda over the needs of students, families, and communities across the United States. The Department of Education’s (Department) extensive “frontloading” of grants is just the latest example. By “frontloading” grants—paying out many years of a multi-year grant in one lump sum instead of funding a larger number of grants right now—your Department is dramatically reducing the number of students and schools that are helped by federal funding. This policy defies congressional intent and effectively cuts investment in communities across the country: the Department could have funded well over 1,000 more grants by committing funds for use without delay. The Department should immediately reverse this deeply misguided and unacceptable approach to implementation of federal appropriations, including funds provided in the FY2026 appropriations law.

In implementing this policy, the Department is intentionally and sharply limiting the number of new grants it will award, by concentrating funds into fewer grants and withholding significant portions of appropriated resources for use in future budget periods. The decisions made to frontload a huge swath of departmental grants came just weeks after the Secretaries of Education and Health and Human Services and Acting Secretary of Labor wrote a letter to Congressional leadership touting the purported success of the illegal interagency agreements (IAAs) they have reached, which highlighted there were “record application levels” for certain grant competitions compared to prior years. Needless to say: record application levels are meaningless to students and families when the Department is choosing to fund fewer new grants under these competitions.

This policy blatantly disregards congressional directives and withholds urgently needed federal resources from the very communities these programs are meant to serve. Instead of deploying funds immediately to hundreds of additional communities for essential education and related services, the Department is withholding approximately $630 million in appropriated resources across approximately 35 grant programs, preventing those funds from reaching students and families now. These are all programs where the Department has historically funded grants on an annual basis—if the Department continued that practice in administering these programs, the Department could have awarded well over 1,000 additional grants this year, supporting everything from evidence-based student literacy programs, to improving student mental health, to recruiting and preparing high-quality teachers, to supporting additional education research and to helping first-generation students succeed in college.

This policy is indefensible. The Department must immediately abandon this approach and administer appropriated funds in full alignment with both the law and the needs of the communities that rely on these programs. Congress expects no less, and the public deserves no less.

Last year, the Department stated that literacy was its top priority. Yet its recent actions tell a different story. The FY2026 appropriations law provided $30 million for the Innovative Approaches to Literacy (IAL) program, which supports improved literacy for children and students from birth through 12th grade—including strengthening school libraries and expanding early literacy services in low-income communities nationwide. When the Department issued its grant competition notice earlier this year, it indicated that it would make 25 to 35 new awards using these funds. Unfortunately, just weeks ago, the Department announced that it would make only four new awards and would set aside $13 million for future years of these grants. Those funds could have been used to make roughly 25 additional awards. It is inexplicable that a Department claiming literacy as its top priority would so drastically limit the number of new grants supporting evidence-based literacy programming. In addition, the number of new awards is also a dramatic reduction from the last grant competitions under the Biden administration in FY2023 when 12 new awards were made and FY2021 when 29 new awards were made with total IAL program funding at the same or a smaller level. This Department of Education is doing significantly less to support evidence-based literacy despite its claim of “supercharging” evidence-based literacy programming.

Sadly, the Department also has chosen to restrict grants that support child care for low-income student parents so they can pursue postsecondary education and workforce training. Congress provided $75 million to the Child Care Access Means Parents in School Program (CCAMPIS) in the final FY2026 appropriations law, funding that is critical to ensuring low-income students receive the support they need while attending college. The Department estimated it would make 148 awards with the CCAMPIS appropriation when it published the notice inviting applications earlier this year and did not announce an intention to frontload. Yet, when the Department announced the new CCAMPIS grantees for FY2026, it made only 40 total new awards and set aside $53 million for future years of these grants. It is perplexing that an Administration that says it wants to improve affordability for Americans and help Americans find good-paying jobs would curtail a program that helps Americans afford higher education and workforce training.

In addition, there are widespread teacher shortages facing our local public schools. According to a recent analysis of Department data, there are an estimated 425,412 teaching positions either unfilled or filled by teachers not fully certified for their assignments, representing about 1 in 8 of all teaching positions nationally. Yet, the Department restricted the number of new grants to help train effective educators through the Supporting Effective Educator Development program this year, limiting it to just 16 new awards when it could have funded dozens more. Similarly, the Department only awarded 12 grants under the Teacher Quality Partnership (TQP) program and set aside $59 million of the $70 million appropriation for future years of these grants. Sadly, the Department also chose to front load most of the appropriation for the Augustus Hawkins Centers of Excellence Program which supports teacher preparation programs in minority-serving institutions, by setting aside over $14 million for future years.

Finally, while state and local education leaders and educators continue to face an ongoing and urgent need for actionable evidence on challenges for education policy and practice, the administration has basically shuttered its research arm, the Institute for Education Sciences (IES) since last January. IES chose not to make new awards from grant competitions posted in 2024 to which institutions had already applied for funding and issued no new awards from grant competitions in FY2026. As a result, IES simply frontloaded existing research grants in order to meet its spending requirement by September 30, 2026. Unfortunately, this same story is repeated throughout the Department’s mishandling of many grant programs this year.

There is no meaningful benefit to this policy change, and certainly nothing that outweighs the significant costs of withholding this funding. The Department is doing this because it wants to eliminate the Department of Education, eliminate these programs, and significantly cut funding for schools. It does not increase certainty for grantees because at the same time, the Department and Office of Management and Budget are both proposing changes to grants management rules that empower agencies to terminate grants for any reason. This suggests even more nefarious motives—awarding funding that can only be used in future years now while empowering agencies to terminate that very funding in the future before it ever reaches students and schools.

The Department has proposed to rewrite the Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR) that govern grant programs Congress has authorized it to administer. One of the major changes in the EDGAR proposal would allow the Secretary of Education to terminate multi-year grants “for convenience”. OMB has proposed similar changes in its federal financial assistance regulation that would rewrite uniform guidance governing grants management government-wide. That proposed rule would empower political appointees to terminate grants for any reason. If the proposed changes to EDGAR or OMB's uniform guidance were to go into effect, this means the Department could easily terminate all these frontloaded funds, effectively terminating a large swath of FY2026 funds that Congress appropriated on a bipartisan basis. This would also make it more difficult for grantees to hire staff and plan to achieve grant objectives as efficiently and effectively as possible. And it would mean that the Department could satisfy Congressional requirements to obligate funds for programs and activities and later turn around and terminate the very grants that were made to satisfy Congressional spending requirements in future fiscal years.

Students deserve timely access to evidence-based literacy resources; parents deserve access to childcare services that allow them to pursue postsecondary education; and all students should have a classroom staffed by a high-quality educator. Congress provided resources for these purposes, and the Department has an obligation—not an option—to use them accordingly.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senator Baldwin Brings Home $34 Million to Repair and Upgrade Green Bay Rail Bridge, Improve Safety and Reliability
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) announced she helped secure $34 million in federal funding for the Fox Valley and Lake Superior Rail System (FOXY) to repair and upgrade the Luxemburg Swing Bridge over the Fox River in Green Bay, improving safety and reliability for freight rail and maritime traffic. The funding comes through the Baldwin-backed Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and annual government funding bills and will help upgrade the aging bridge, reduce service disruptions, and strengthen a critical transportation link for Wisconsin businesses.

“Wisconsin businesses rely on our railways and waterways to get their Made in Wisconsin products to customers across the country,” said Senator Baldwin. “But when aging infrastructure causes delays and disruptions, it hurts our businesses, costs them time and money, and makes it harder for them to compete. That’s why I’m proud to bring home this investment to repair and modernize this critical bridge, keep folks safe, and make sure Wisconsin businesses have the reliable infrastructure they need to grow and succeed.”

“The Fox Valley & Lake Superior Rail System (FOXY) is thrilled to accept this federal award and thanks Senator Baldwin for her strong support,” said Ken Lucht, Assistant Vice-President of Government Affairs for Watco. “A resilient and modernized freight rail network has a direct positive impact on our economy and public safety throughout Brown County.”

Built in 1923, the Luxemburg Swing Bridge plays a critical role in connecting businesses in Green Bay and Brown County to freight rail service, including Wisconsin's transportation and paper industries. The bridge currently carries over 25,000 carloads of freight annually; however, after more than a century of service, the bridge is in need of critical repairs to ensure it can continue serving Wisconsin businesses.

The $34 million investment from the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) grant program will support the rehabilitation and modernization of the Luxemburg Swing Bridge, including upgrades to its mechanical, electrical, and structural components to improve safety and reliability. The improvements will help eliminate frequent service interruptions to freight rail and maritime commerce and allow the bridge to accommodate railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds.

In June, Senator Baldwin advocated to the Trump Administration for the project’s funding, citing the widespread consequences for Wisconsin businesses if the bridge were to fail.

title: Banks Urges FDA to Crack Down on Illicit “Research Use Only” Drugs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) led a group of senators urging the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to work more closely with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and other law enforcement agencies to stop vendors from misusing “for research only” labeling to sell unapproved, potentially dangerous drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients to Americans.

In a letter to Acting FDA Commissioner Diamantas, Banks highlighted widespread online sales of knockoff and counterfeit retatrutide, an investigational drug that has not been approved by the FDA. America’s Poison Control centers reported a 265 percent increase in poisonings related to illicit retatrutide in the first four months of 2026 compared to the final four months of 2025. Banks requested a briefing on the FDA’s efforts to work with law enforcement and protect American patients.

Read the full letter here or below.

Dear Mr. Diamantas:

Online drug and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) vendors are increasingly exploiting the “for research use only” labeling authority to make illicit profits selling drugs that have not been approved or even evaluated yet by the FDA. We are concerned that “for research use only” has become a dangerous loophole that undermines the FDA’s authority.

As you know, “for research use only” drug compounds are intended solely for laboratory research and are not intended for human therapeutic or clinical use. They are not FDA-approved for human use, are not subject to usual Current Good Manufacturing Practices, and not subject to quality-control or stability-testing requirements. As a result, they are vulnerable to contamination, impurity, mislabeling, and misuse.

Misuse of “for research use only” labeling authority is fostering gray and black markets on the internet. The wide availability of knockoff retatrutide illustrates the risks. Retatrutide is an investigational drug, currently in phase 3 clinical trials, that has demonstrated potential to promote weight loss and improve knee pain, lower back pain, and sleep apnea, among other ailments. It has not been approved by the FDA. Yet, many online vendors are already selling poor-quality retatrutide to Americans, and many of these companies source their APIs from unregulated manufacturers in China. This has dangerous consequences. America’s Poison Centers reported a 265% increase in poisonings related to illicit retatrutide in the first four months of 2026 compared to the last four months of 2025.

The FDA has issued warning letters to at least seven companies for marketing retatrutide “for research use only” while simultaneously promoting it to the general public to treat obesity, diabetes, and other human uses on their websites and social media. The FDA has also issued warning letters to more than a dozen other companies for selling unapproved retatrutide, lacking adequate directions for use, and making false or misleading claims. In some cases, products marketed as retatrutide contain no retatrutide at all, evidenced by federal charges against a Florida seller earlier this year.

We commend the FDA’s enforcement efforts, but we urge you to work more closely with U.S. Customs & Border Protection and other law enforcement agencies to take these illicit drugs off the market and hold the companies selling them accountable. Their foreign supply chains rely on concealment, falsified paperwork, and deliberately mislabeled shipments to evade customs detection. These are all crimes in their own right. Stronger security at ports of entry, more investigations of affiliated companies, and prosecutions are badly needed.

We respectfully request a briefing on the “for research use only” labeling authority and the FDA’s enforcement strategy, covering the following topics:

The FDA’s assessment of the extent of use, misuse, and trends in the “for research use only” labeling authority.

The FDA’s coordination with Customs & Border Protection and other federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies to identify and interdict illicit drugs and APIs.

The FDA’s capacity to identify, investigate, and take enforcement action against API and drug vendors that evade or break the law.

Thank you for your leadership on this important issue

###

title: Bennet Visits U.S. Pacific Command, Japan, and Taiwan to Deepen Cooperation, Underscore Support for Strengthened Indo-Pacific Deterrence
text:
From left: American Institute in Taiwan Acting Director Judy Kuo, Senator Michael Bennet, Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, and Secretary-General of Taiwan’s National Security Council Joseph Wu

Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence (SSCI), recently concluded a visit to Japan and Taiwan, during which he met with senior leaders, including Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te, and discussed concrete steps to enhance joint efforts to strengthen defense and deter threats in the Indo-Pacific. Prior to visiting the region, Bennet also visited U.S. Pacific Command (PACOM) Headquarters in Hawaii, where he held consultations and received briefings on the U.S. posture and security cooperation.

“This trip reinforced my belief in the necessity of further cooperation with key allies and partners like Japan and Taiwan to advance a free and open Indo-Pacific, which is essential to U.S. national security and prosperity,” said Bennet. “In every meeting, Japan and Taiwan’s leaders underscored both the vital role of the United States and their readiness to contribute their fair share to our collective deterrence. I will continue pressing for passage of my legislation to enhance regional intelligence cooperation, to bolster space collaboration with Taiwan, and to share drone expertise learned in Ukraine with our partners in both Taipei and Tokyo. I will also continue pushing the Trump administration to advance the billions of dollars in arms sales to Taiwan that Congress has already authorized and appropriated. These bipartisan efforts are critical to ensure peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait and across the Indo-Pacific, a region inextricably tied to America’s future.”

In Hawaii, Bennet met U.S. military leadership, including PACOM Deputy Commander Lt. Gen. George Rowell, Pacific Air Forces Deputy Commander Lt. Gen. David Iverson, and Space Forces – Pacific Commander Brig. Gen. Brian A. Denaro. Bennet discussed how greater intelligence cooperation can support regional deterrence, as well as the critical role Colorado-based U.S. Space Force, U.S. Army, and other units play in this effort.

From left: Space Forces – Pacific Senior Enlisted Leader Chief Master Sgt. John W. Harms, Senator Bennet, and Space Forces – Pacific Commander Brig. Gen. Brian A. Denaro

In Japan, Bennet met senior Japanese officials including Chairman of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s Policy Research Council Takayuki Kobayashi and State Minister of Defense Kiyoshi Odawara, as well as U.S. Ambassador to Japan George Glass. Bennet expressed his support for Japan’s ongoing intelligence reforms, underscoring the opportunity the reforms would create for stronger U.S.-Japan intelligence cooperation. Bennet also discussed his legislation in the SSCI-passed FY27 Intelligence Authorization Act (IAA) to bolster intelligence cooperation with Indo-Pacific allies, particularly Japan. Additionally, he reaffirmed the U.S. desire to strengthen cooperation — both bilaterally and through other mechanisms — on defense co-production, advanced technology, artificial intelligence, and space, including in Colorado.

Senator Bennet with Takayuki Kobayashi, Chairman of the Liberal Democratic Party’s Policy Research Council

In Taiwan, Bennet met key leaders including President Lai Ching-te and Legislative Yuan Speaker Han Kuo-yu, as well as American Institute in Taiwan Acting Director Judy Kuo. Bennet commended the Taiwan government and legislature’s efforts to bolster defense spending, including for unmanned aerial systems (UAS). He emphasized that there is strong bipartisan support in the U.S. Congress for maintaining peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait, including through the sale of the defensive weapons necessary for Taiwan to maintain a sufficient self-defense capability. He also reaffirmed Congress’s bipartisan support for full implementation of the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances. Additionally, he expressed his support for passage of legislation he sponsors to provide double-taxation relief on U.S.-Taiwan cross-border investment to remove cross-border investment barriers.

Senator Bennet (left) with Legislative Yuan Speaker Han Kuo-yu (right)

Bennet leads several efforts to strengthen cooperation with Indo-Pacific allies and partners to enhance regional deterrence.

He authored a provision in the FY27 SSCI-passed IAA directing the strengthening of intelligence cooperation with U.S. allies in the Indo-Pacific, particularly Japan, and collaboration with Taiwan as appropriate. Bennet also leads legislation to enhance U.S-Taiwan space cooperation – which passed out of committee earlier this year. He wrote legislation in the FY27 Senate Armed Services Committee-passed National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to ensure the transmission of U.S.-Ukraine UAS expertise to Taiwan and Japan, among other partners.

Additionally, Bennet leads legislation requiring a Government Accountability Office report on how delays of U.S. foreign military sales (FMS) to Japan, the Philippines, South Korea, and Taiwan affect the U.S. ability to build, posture, and sustain deterrence along the First Island Chain, as well as legislation to assess the expansion the U.S.-led Multinational Force-Operation Olympic Defender to include additional Indo-Pacific allies such as Japan. Bennet secured versions of both of these in the FY27 NDAA report.

Earlier this year, ahead of May 2026 summit between President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping, Bennet and Senator John Curtis (R-Utah) led 10 bipartisan colleagues on a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reaffirming congressional support for the Taiwan Relations Act and underscoring their belief that there should be no unilateral changes to this policy nor any new U.S. declaratory policy on Taiwan.

Last year, Bennet passed into law legislation requiring the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a strategy to strengthen U.S.-led multilateral efforts to deter China’s aggression in the Indo-Pacific, including in the Taiwan Strait. In November 2025, the President signed into law legislation Bennet co-sponsored requiring regular State Department reviews of and updated guidelines on U.S. engagement with Taiwan.

Bennet sponsors additional legislation to streamline U.S. arms sales to Taiwan; to codify the Six Assurances as foundational U.S. policy toward Taiwan; to strengthen Taiwan’s international standing; to support Taiwan’s partnerships in Latin America and the Caribbean; and to deter China’s aggression against Taiwan by identifying targets for sanctions the United States could rapidly impose if China moves against Taiwan; and to provide expedited double-tax relief on U.S.-Taiwan cross-border investment.

title: Blackburn, Duckworth Bipartisan Bill to Improve Life-Saving Emergency Communication Technology Passes Committee
text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – The U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation (CST) passed bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.) that would improve emergency communication technology used to help save lives. The bipartisan ITS Codification Act would codify the Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS), which currently serves as the research and engineering laboratory at the National Telecommunications and Information Administration, and require ITS to develop emergency communication and tracking technologies to help locate trapped individuals in confined spaces where conventional radio communication is limited.

The House companion bill, led by U.S. Representatives Earl “Buddy” Carter (R-Ga.) and Brittany Pettersen (D-Colo.), passed the House by voice vote in July 2025. The legislation will now be considered by the full Senate.

title: Booker, Warren Urge FTC to Investigate Anticompetitive, Deceptive Practices in Online Home-Buying Marketplace
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, sent a letter to Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chair Andrew Ferguson urging the agency to investigate anticompetitive and deceptive practices by dominant online real estate platforms that are driving up costs for homebuyers and deepening the nation’s housing affordability crisis.

“We urge you to now investigate anticompetitive and deceptive practices in the home-buying market, using every enforcement tool available to restore competition to the entire online real estate marketplace,” wrote the Senators. “Today, too many people are locked out of the American dream of homeownership.”

The letter follows an August 24, 2026, stipulated order in which the FTC required Redfin to reenter the online rental market after Zillow paid the company to shut down its internet rental listing service. Booker called that settlement a step forward for renters and urged the Commission to apply the same scrutiny to the home-buying market, using every enforcement tool available to restore competition across the online real estate marketplace.

The letter highlights worsening affordability nationwide. The national median home price has reached an all-time high of approximately $434,900, with median monthly mortgage payments of $2,199, consuming nearly 25 percent of median monthly income. Stagnant wages and rising costs for utilities, healthcare, and transportation have made it increasingly difficult for families to cover everyday expenses while saving to buy a home. As a result, the median age of a first-time homebuyer has reached an all-time high of 40, up from the late 20s in the 1980s, as high rents make it increasingly difficult to save for a down payment.

The Senators' letter identifies three specific practices that warrant FTC investigation:

Undisclosed commission-sharing arrangements. Online listings often feature a “contact agent” button that can route prospective buyers to platform-affiliated agents who have agreed to remit a share of their commission back to the platform, without disclosing the arrangement to buyers.

Steering to affiliated mortgage lenders. Platform-affiliated agents are frequently required to direct buyers to affiliated mortgage lenders that charge higher rates and impose worse loan terms, again without disclosure.

Anticompetitive use of private listings. Dominant brokerage firms are increasingly marketing homes only to a select group of buyers rather than the public, artificially restricting the available housing stock to the benefit of the brokerage’s own agents and to the detriment of buyers, sellers, and competing firms.

The letter cites a study finding borrowers who shop around for a mortgage saved an average of $80,000 over the life of their loan, underscoring the potential cost of captive lending arrangements. Younger and first-time homebuyers are particularly vulnerable to these practices, the letter argues, because they are navigating the largest financial transaction of their lives with incomplete information and may assume that online platforms offer a more affordable path to homeownership.

This letter builds on Senator Booker’s ongoing efforts to lower housing costs for Americans and expand access to affordable housing. Last month, Senator Booker introduced the Transit-Oriented Housing Development Act, legislation that would make significant investments in affordable housing near transit hubs and create 2 million housing units nationwide. Booker was also a cosponsor of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, landmark legislation that became law earlier this year to expand housing supply, reduce barriers to homeownership, and lower housing costs for families.

title: Senators Collins, King Announce More Than $37 Million for Freight Rail Upgrades in Northern Maine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Susan Collins, Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Angus King announced that the Maine Department of Transportation (MaineDOT) has been awarded $37,040,000 for the Northern Aroostook Rail Gateway Modernization and Safety Project. This funding will support the rehabilitation of approximately 90 miles of railroad tracks in northern Maine, including in Fort Kent, Madawaska, and Van Buren.

The funding was awarded through the U.S. Department of Transportation Federal Railroad Administration's (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. In July 2026, Senators Collins and Angus King sent a letter to the FRA in support of MaineDOT's application for this funding, highlighting the importance of the rail corridor to northern Maine's forest products and agricultural industries.

The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) provided an additional $5 billion for the CRISI Program from Fiscal Years 2022 through 2026. Senator Collins was part of the core group of 10 senators who negotiated the IIJA.

“Freight rail is essential to northern Maine’s economy, connecting our forest products and agricultural industries to markets across the country and around the world,” said Senators Collins and King. “This $37 million investment will help modernize aging rail infrastructure and increase railcar capacity, making it easier and safer for Maine businesses to move their products. By strengthening this critical rail corridor, this funding will support local jobs and help keep Aroostook County’s forest products and agricultural industries competitive for years to come.”

Specifically, the project will rehabilitate approximately 90 miles of the Maine Northern Railway's Madawaska Subdivision and the Eastern Maine Railway's Van Buren Subdivision. Improvements will include replacing aging rail, crossties, and ballast, as well as rehabilitating a key railroad bridge.

Since joining the Senate Appropriations Committee in 2009, Senator Collins has helped direct more than $2 billion in federal funds to Maine’s transportation infrastructure.

title: Cortez Masto, Senate Democrats Demand Answers on EPA Surveillance of Medication Abortion Drugs in Drinking Water
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) joined a letter led by U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-Wash.) urging U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin to remove mifepristone and misoprostol from a list of contaminants targeted for surveillance in drinking water in a study that the agency announced in September. Cortez Masto was one of the first Senators to raise the alarm about the EPA study.

Zeldin previously told the Senate Appropriations Committee that he was “not aware” of any efforts to detect medication abortion drugs in water. The surveillance study comes after a pressure campaign by anti-abortion groups who have urged the EPA to retool environmental protection laws to monitor and ultimately restrict abortion medications that are safe for humans and the environment.

“We write to express our serious concerns with the recent announcement that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to take up a surveillance study to track the presence of the medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water,” the Senators began. “This action is a stark departure from past EPA practice and serves to further this administration’s attacks on reproductive health care and distracts from your agency’s critical role protecting Americans from known chemical pollutants in our water systems.”

The Senators note that mifepristone and misoprostol have been deemed safe for patients by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for over 25 years and reaffirmed as safe for the environment as recently as 2025. “While there is no scientific evidence that would support mifepristone and misoprostol as candidates for surveillance by the EPA, there has been a targeted political pressure campaign by anti-abortion activists to urge the agency to use the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and other environmental authorities to surveil and regulate medication abortion drugs,” they wrote.

The Senators called out Zeldin for stating that he had no knowledge of efforts to target mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water when the EPA had engaged in conversations with radical anti-abortion groups and encouraged them to pressure the agency to regulate abortion medication.

“It is deeply alarming that this kind of radical, anti-science campaign might have an audience at the EPA,” they continued. “This study is a departure from the EPA’s historic role in protecting our water and air from actual threats to human health and the environment. Instead, this study opens the door to new attacks on safe and accessible reproductive health care, undermining the safety and privacy of patients around the country.”

The lawmakers wrote that the EPA’s responsibility is to regulate contaminants that harm human health and the environment, not drugs that are well-documented to be safe and effective but disrupt Republican efforts to control women’s bodies. “Taxpayers fund EPA to protect their health and the environment, not to advance a political campaign against women’s health care,” they concluded.

In addition to Senators Cortez Masto and Murray, the letter was joined by the entire Senate Democratic caucus.

The full text of the letter is available here.

Senator Cortez Masto is a fierce advocate for women’s reproductive rights. Last November, she sent a letter to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary expressing alarm over the Trump administration’s plans to conduct “its own review of the evidence” on the safety and effectiveness of mifepristone. Cortez Masto is leading legislation to protect the right of women to cross state lines to seek abortion care, to repeal the Comstock Act, and to expand health insurance coverage of birth control throughout the country. She voted against the confirmation of Secretary Kennedy in part because of his inability to answer questions regarding women’s health care rights.

title: Cortez Masto, Wyden, Whitehouse Question Meta’s Use of Billions in Tax Credits to Subsidize AI Data Center Construction
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) called on Meta, Facebook’s parent company, to justify its use of billions in federal research and development (R&D) tax credits to fund its rapid buildout of AI data centers in a letter to CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

According to recent reporting, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental “pilot models,” and therefore eligible for federal R&D tax credits. These tax credits are intended to incentivize experimental research, not to scale up existing infrastructure. As Meta spends billions of dollars on AI data centers, its R&D tax credits have grown from $700 million in 2023 to $4 billion in 2025.

“The federal research credit can be a useful and necessary tool to support our nation’s innovation economy and cutting-edge research,” the Senators wrote. “Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard.”

If the reporting is accurate, Meta’s R&D tax credit claims would represent more than ten percent of all research tax credits claimed in the U.S., based on Joint Committee on Taxation figures.

“Any effort by Meta to use A.I. data center expansion as eligible for research credits is potentially a significant misapplication of federal tax law that merits further investigation,” the Senators continued.

Meta has a long record of attempting to lower its tax bill through dubious tax credit claims. In 2013, Meta claimed that $4.1 billion Zuckerberg received by exercising stock options should be eligible for research credits. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) challenged that claim and is seeking $355 million in back taxes from Meta.

The Senators demanded that Meta provide the following information:

Whether Meta has claimed R&D tax credits related to the buildout and operation of its AI data centers and, if so, its legal justification for doing so;

Whether Meta has claimed to the IRS on federal tax filings that its AI data centers are “pilot models” in order to qualify for federal R&D tax credits;

Whether Meta posits that expenses related to AI data centers are eligible for R&D tax credits while those related to non-AI data centers are not and, if so, its legal justification for doing so;

Whether Meta consulted with experts from professional accounting firms prior to claiming federal R&D tax credits and, if so, whether the firms advised it to claim the tax credits; and

How much of the $6.6 billion in federal R&D tax credits Meta claimed from 2023 to 2025 was related to the construction or operation of AI data centers.

Senators Cortez Masto, Wyden, Whitehouse, Warren, and Hassan were joined in the letter by Senators Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) and Peter Welch (D-Vt.).

The full text of the letter can be found here.

Senator Cortez Masto has worked to ensure that regulations concerning AI innovation and use take privacy, national security, and environmental considerations into account. She urged the CEOs of Spirit Airlines and Google to protect the privacy of former Spirit employees as the airline plans to sell employee data to train Google AI. Last year, Cortez Masto’s legislation to prohibit American investment in Chinese AI companies was passed into law. When President Xi Jinping visited the U.S., she urged President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with him for the development, testing, and use of AI models. Cortez Masto voted against a Republican bill that claimed to regulate AI data centers but was entirely voluntary and instead pushed for legislation with real teeth.

title: Cramer, Wicker Strengthen Transatlantic Security Ties
text:
Lawmakers Meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy Amid Russian Attacks, Reaffirm U.S. Support for Ukraine and Regional Security Cooperation

***Click herefor media resources.***

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) and Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) Chairman Roger Wicker (R-MS) to Ukraine, where they discussed developments in the war with Russia and their joint strategic security objectives. Cramer and Wicker also traveled to Spain, Andorra, and Poland, where they joined allied military and civilian leaders from across the continent intent on bolstering national security cooperation and addressing defense challenges in Central and Eastern Europe.

“I’m grateful to join my Senate colleagues on this important trip to strengthen our partnerships with European allies and reaffirm our commitment to transatlantic security,” said Cramer, chair of the SASC Airland Subcommittee and member of the Senate Ukraine Caucus. “Meeting with President Zelenskyy and hearing from young Ukrainians who escaped Russian-occupied territories was a powerful reminder of what is at stake. We must stand with Ukraine, confront Russian aggression, and work alongside our allies to protect freedom and security for generations to come. This trip has also renewed my conviction to increase our energy security, our food security and our mineral security in order to weather conflicts and honor our alliances should the need arise. Peace through strength requires the conviction to lead as well as the ability to defend our homeland and our allies until we have achieved victory.”

In Kyiv, the delegation met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Russian attacks targeted infrastructure across the country. Following the meeting, Zelenskyy said in a post on X that air raid alerts remained in effect throughout the discussion because of the threat posed by jet-powered Shahed drones. He added Russian strikes had damaged two schools in Kyiv since the beginning of the month and hit bridges, energy facilities, and other critical infrastructure.

“We can only protect ourselves from this terror by working together, and we discussed how the United States can help save lives,” said Zelenskyy on X. “Of course, we expect the Lindsey Graham Act to be implemented. This is a matter of political will, and it is now important to show leadership and fully cut off the financial flows sustaining Russia’s war machine. We also discussed other necessary steps, including expediting licensing for Patriot missile production. Ukraine is ready not only to produce ballistic missile interceptors for its own needs, but also to strengthen the United States and its allies through joint production. I thank the United States for its unwavering support.”

Cramer and his colleagues also attended the 24th Autumn Meeting of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Parliamentary Assembly in Andorra, which included personal accounts from young Ukrainians who escaped Russian-occupied territories. Afterward, Cramer said, “We must never forget the thousands of children taken by Russia in Putin’s unprovoked, illegal attack on Ukraine.”

Cramer then joined Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other participants in the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland. In addition to a bilateral meeting with commander of United States European Command and Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus G. Grynkewich, Cramer also discussed the role of energy as a tool of geopolitical influence and potential vulnerability in times of conflict.

Cramer last traveled to Ukraine with a bipartisan congressional delegation in January 2022, shortly before the Russian invasion, meeting with Zelenskyy and reaffirming U.S. support as Russian forces built up along Ukraine’s border. The senators voiced solidarity with Ukraine amid escalating Russian aggression, the ongoing conflict in the Donbas, and Russia’s occupation and illegal annexation of Crimea.

title: FRA Awards Over $24 Million for Rail Infrastructure Upgrades in North Dakota
text:
BISMARCK, ND – The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) awarded $23.6 million to the Red River Valley & Western Railroad (RRVW) and $690,825 to Bottineau County through the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. The funding will support rail infrastructure improvements, enhance safety, and improve transportation efficiency across North Dakota.

“This funding will allow the modernization of a large portion of railway between Gwinner and Wyndmere—two-thirds of which was laid down before the end of World War I, and the rest before the Great Depression,” said U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Chair of the Senate Environment and Public Works Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure. “Old rail is susceptible to thermal misalignments, and frigid North Dakota winters can break joint bars and increase the risk of derailments. The grant will ensure RRVW can continue supporting North Dakota’s agricultural shippers with dependable, modern rail service.”

In April, the North Dakota Delegation wrote a letter to FRA in support of the project and earlier this year Cramer led his colleagues in urging continued funding for the CRISI program.

Additionally, Bottineau County’s award will target rail safety improvements, including a railroad crossing near a school zone and increased grain-handling capacity.

title: Ahead Of The Midterm Elections, Durbin, Padilla, Warner, & Peters Request Information From DOJ & FBI Regarding The Trump Administration’s Attempted Attacks On Our Elections
text:
In the letter, the Ranking Members also urge the DOJ and FBI to provide information related to the agencies’ coordination with DHS, the U.S. Intelligence Community, and the White House in these efforts to undermine our election security

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, along with U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Ranking Member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, Mark Warner, Vice Chair of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and Gary Peters, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel requesting information regarding the alarming series of actions the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the FBI have undertaken to target state and local governments’ election administration efforts—and to understand the extent of the agencies’ coordination with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the U.S. Intelligence Community, and the White House in these efforts.

The Senators wrote, “Under your leadership, DOJ and the FBI have sought to upend our federalist system by seizing ballots and election materials, seeking the personal information of election workers and volunteers, showing up at the homes of election officials for questioning, threatening election officials with prosecution, attempting to compel states to provide the federal government with unredacted voter rolls, and raiding the offices of a voting rights nonprofit—often at the apparent behest of President Trump and White House officials, including Stephen Miller. Director Patel has reportedly urged the FBI to persist in these fishing expeditions by exhorting agents to ‘look harder’ because ‘this is a push from 47,’ and senior DOJ officials have threatened to fire or override prosecutors who choose not to pursue election fraud cases that FBI or DHS agents bring them, in contravention of longstanding DOJ rules for prosecutors.”

The Senators continued, “These efforts have occurred as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) has taken unprecedented steps to investigate unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud and as the then-Director of National Intelligence took extraordinary steps to insert herself into an already-troubling FBI raid of a local election facility. Taken together, these actions constitute a disturbing, whole-of-government campaign that has weaponized federal law enforcement to relitigate the 2020 election that President Trump lost, attempting to undermine the constitutional election administration powers of states ahead of the 2026 midterm elections and seeking to sow confusion and fear among voters and state and local election officials.”

In the letter, the Senators outline the timeline of the Trump Administration’s attempted efforts to undermine our elections. The weaponization of DOJ and the FBI as part of this effort became clear last year, when the head of the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) began filing lawsuits against multiple states to demand they produce unredacted copies of their voter registration lists. CRT sued Fulton County, Georgia last December, seeking records related to the 2020 election. Following this lawsuit, on January 28, 2026, the FBI executed a search warrant at the Fulton County election office in Union City, Georgia. Additionally, the then-Director of National Intelligence inexplicably attended this raid—and escalated this breach of protocol the following day, when she met with FBI agents who had conducted the raid and called President Trump to address the agents. The letter continues to highlight various counties and states the FBI or DOJ has targeted for election-related investigations. These states include Michigan and Arizona—two states President Trump lost in the 2020 election.

The letter also raises concerns that FBI Director Patel is refusing to rule out sending FBI agents to polling locations on Election Day—an illegal tactic that would inevitably intimidate voters.

The Senators continued, “The concern over this Administration engaging in intimidation tactics related to the election is not unwarranted. Just one month before election day, President Trump continues to float the idea that he has legal authority to declare a national emergency or invoke the Insurrection Act around the midterms. Moreover, DOJ has already sought to intimidate election officials across the country.”

CRT’s abandonment of its historic mission to protect the right to vote has also bled into the election monitor program, which the Division has in the past used to deploy federal monitors at polling places and ballot counting locations to respond to “incidents of discrimination or interference with the right to vote.” This year, CRT is planning to deploy more than 1,000 election monitors across the country on Election Day, including individuals who helped challenge President Trump’s 2020 election loss.

Just this week, DOJ attempted to escalate these efforts, laying the groundwork to potentially challenge ballots ahead of Election Day with a letter to California election officials, which demanded that they verify the citizenship of individuals listed in a DOJ-provided thumb drive within 48 hours and threatened legal action if they do not follow the Department’s instructions on handling the ballots of these individuals.

The Senators concluded, “Furthermore, it is impossible to ignore the brazen partisan intentions behind these actions—not just due to President Trump’s repeated, baseless accusations that Democrats must cheat to win elections, but in light of the unethical political actions you have each taken in recent weeks, including your appearances at an August campaign rally in New York, and Attorney General Blanche’s appearance at the Republican Party’s midterm convention in Texas and a campaign event in North Carolina for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley. It is our constitutional duty to conduct oversight over these unprecedented abuses of power to improperly meddle with state and local election administration in the midterm elections that are already underway. The American people deserve to know why federal resources are being diverted from mission critical work to ensure their safety and instead devoted to this costly and, should it further escalate, potentially criminal crusade.”

The Senators also noted that despite this brazen, partisan, and coordinated effort to undermine the constitutional structure of our democracy, the rule of law will prevail—countless patriotic Americans across the country are working tirelessly to combat this chaos and distrust and ensure that every eligible American is able to cast their ballot and that their vote is counted. Americans should have confidence that their voices will be heard in November and that these efforts by the Trump Administration to weaponize federal law enforcement to meddle in the midterm elections will ultimately fail.

In the letter, the Senators request responses to a number of questions and materials related to the Administration’s attempts to undermine our elections no later than October 29, 2026.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Ernst Names Small Business of the Week, Sorensen Studios
text:
RED OAK, Iowa – U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), Chair of the Senate Small Business Committee, today announced her Small Business of the Week: Sorensen Studios of Adair County. Throughout the 119th Congress, Chair Ernst plans to recognize a small business in each of Iowa's 99 counties.

“The mural of the story is that Sorensen Studios is a prime example of creative entrepreneurship,” said Chair Ernst. “Maria and Ray Sorensen’s commitment to their business, community, and our nation’s veterans rocks.”

The idea for Sorensen Studios began when Ray “Bubba” Sorensen started helping his now-wife, Maria, on her journalism projects at Iowa State University. As the two worked together, it was clear they made a great team. In 2008, Maria and Bubba opened Sorensen Studios, using Bubba’s artistic talent and Maria’s knack for photography and logistics.

For nearly two decades, Sorensen Studios has been owned and operated by Maria and Bubba. In 2013, Sorensen Studios started the Freedom Rock Tour, with the goal of putting signature painted rocks honoring veterans in all 99 of Iowa’s counties. Today, there is a Freedom Rock in every Iowa county, and the Sorensens have started the 50-State Freedom Rock Tour to highlight and thank veterans across the country. The pair also launched the Freedom Rock Foundation, a nonprofit created to maintain Freedom Rocks, with a board made up of veterans. In addition to Sorensen Studios, Bubba is a state representative for the 23rd district in the Iowa House of Representatives.

Stay tuned as Chair Ernst continues to recognize outstanding Iowa small businesses with her Small Business of the Week award.

###

title: Fischer, Energy Secretary Talk Biofuels with Ag Industry
text:
LOUISVILLE – U.S. Senator Deb Fischer (R-NE) and U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright visited with ag producers from across Nebraska to discuss E15 and the cost of fuel. The roundtable was hosted by the Nebraska Farm Bureau with Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE), Don Bacon (NE-02), and Adrian Smith (NE-03) also in attendance.

“E15 is one of the most direct ways we can provide relief at the pump,” Fischer said. “Secretary Wright understands a diverse energy mix of oil, gas, renewables, nuclear, and biofuels makes the United States stronger and more resilient during market disruptions. I’m glad he had a chance to hear firsthand from Nebraska’s producers about the challenges they face.”

“We held a productive meeting with Nebraska’s farmers where we discussed the Trump administration’s commitment to doing everything we can to lower the cost of energy, including supporting Nebraska’s growing biofuels industry,” Wright said. “It’s no coincidence that in a state with such hardworking Americans and leaders, growth and prosperity are surging.”

Fischer secured a provision in the Farm Bill allowing for the year-round sale of E15. The Farm Bill advanced out of the Senate Agriculture Committee on September 16, 2026.

President Donald Trump has urged Congress to approve the permanent, year-round sale of E15.

title: Gillibrand Statement On Trump Administration Withholding Iran School Bombing Report Until After Midterms
text:
GILLIBRAND: “Withholding This Report Until After The Election Is Not Only Disgraceful, It Is Cowardly.”

Today, following reports that top Pentagon officials intend to withhold the results of the Defense Department’s “all-but-complete” investigation into the U.S.’ bombing of an Iranian elementary school in February – the worst civilian casualty incident caused by the U.S. military in decades – until after the midterm elections, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, member of the Senate Armed Services and Intelligence Committees, released the following statement:

“Secretary Hegseth has decided that politics is more important than our national security and innocent children’s lives. Withholding this report until after the election is not only disgraceful, it is cowardly. We have waited months – release the report. Congress and the American people deserve full transparency and accountability around this attack, and I will not rest until we have it. If Secretary Hegseth and this administration put as much effort into protecting civilians as they do into dodging accountability, those children might still be alive, and we wouldn’t be in this reckless war with Iran.”

Despite ample reporting that Pentagon investigators have found that the U.S. was at fault for the Minab school bombing, Trump administration officials have not publicly taken responsibility for the strike or the resultant civilian deaths. President Trump himself has suggested multiple times that the strike was not the U.S.’ fault and has even blamed Iran. Additionally, Secretary Hegseth has spent his tenure deriding the rules of engagement and cutting DoD programs that aim to prevent harm to civilians during war, including slashing civilian harm mitigation and response staff at the U.S. combatant commands by over 90 percent.

Senator Gillibrand has repeatedly pressed the Trump administration for answers on the Minab school strike and pushed for the results of the Pentagon’s investigation to be made public. Some of these actions include:

March 12: Senator Gillibrand questions EUCOM Commander and NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe ​​Gen. Alexus Grynkewich on processes involved in the Minab school bombing, including how the school may have been targeted and Secretary Hegseth’s cuts to civilian harm mitigation efforts at DoD

March 27: Senator Gillibrand, colleagues demand bipartisan Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) investigation into Minab school bombing, including what systems or mechanisms DoD used during Operation Epic Fury to prevent civilian harm incidents

April 30: Senator Gillibrand grills Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war, including civilian casualties at schools and hospitals

May 14: Senator Gillibrand presses CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper on NYT report on 22 schools being damaged by U.S.-Israeli strikes in Iran, including the Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab

July 13: Senator Gillibrand leads her colleagues in a letter calling for the swift completion and release of the Pentagon’s investigation into the Minab school strike

July 14: Senator Gillibrand demands accountability from military leadership about the lack of transparency around the Minab school bombing and the Pentagon’s failure to release its report

title: Grassley, Hinson Support for Public Safety Funding Yields “Resoundingly Positive” Results for Iowa
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), working alongside U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), community leaders and the U.S. Department of Justice, has secured over $42,000,000 in federal public safety funding for Iowa during the 119th Congress, including over $6,811,000 for communities across northeastern Iowa.

Read more from the Cresco Times Plains Dealer about a recent grant, backed by Grassley and Hinson, that’s helping supercharge public safety in Howard County:

“For the Howard County Sheriff's Office grant, the U.S. Department of Justice's Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) granted the substantial $1,364,725 federal award. In addition to Hinson, U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley, a staunch proponent of law enforcement funding, played a pivotal role in securing this grant for Howard County.

“As Congresswoman Hinson and key allies like Senator Grassley amplify their support for public safety initiatives in rural Iowa, the impact of federal funding on local communities and emergency response capabilities remains resoundingly positive. Through innovative partnerships and proactive investments, Howard County stands poised to navigate emergencies with enhanced preparedness and reinforced security, ensuring the prosperity and safety of its residents."

Tomorrow, Grassley and Hinson will join local law enforcement officers in Eldora to discuss Iowa’s public safety needs and how a $3,054,209 federal grant headed to the Hardin County Sheriff’s Office will strengthen services in the region.

Thanks to the ongoing work of Grassley, Hinson and community leaders, Iowans in Hardin, Howard, Franklin, Winneshiek, Linn, Tama, Black Hawk and Dubuque counties have received a total of $6,811,252 in 2025 and 2026 to support public safety:

The Hardin County Sheriff’s Office received $3,054,209 to modernize the department’s equipment and interoperable communications systems.

The Howard County Sheriff’s Office received $1,364,725 to support the department’s critical law enforcement technology, equipment and infrastructure.

The Kids First Law Center, a legal organization in Linn County, received nearly $500,000 to expand its Building Safer Schools program, which aims to reach and redirect at-risk youth, support child victims and prevent youth violence.

The AGWSR Community School District in Franklin and Hardin counties received $500,000 to bolster school security.

Helping Services for Youth & Families, a nonprofit in Winneshiek County, received $500,000 to support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence and stalking.

The Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa received over $268,000 to help address the needs of crime victims.

Waypoint Services for Women, Children and Families, a nonprofit in Linn County, received over $250,000 to support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence and stalking.

The City of Mount Vernon received $200,000 to provide mental health training to first responders across Iowa.

Linn County received over $70,000 to replace outdated law enforcement equipment, enhance officer safety and improve efficiency within the Cedar Rapids Police Department, Marion Police Department and the Linn County Sheriff’s Office.

Black Hawk County and the Cities of Waterloo and Cedar Falls received over $48,000 to support law enforcement officers tasked with combating illicit drugs, gun violence and gang activity.?

The City of Dubuque received over $33,600 to assist local law enforcement with enforcement, prevention and tactical response efforts.

The City of Eldora received over $11,000 to support the Eldora Police Department Technology and Training Initiative, aimed at enhancing officer training and improving public safety outcomes.

The City of Mason City received over $10,000 to establish a canine program within the Cerro Gordo County Sheriff’s Office to assist in suspect tracking, building searches, narcotics detection and officer safety.

title: Grassley Nominates Iowan to Serve on U.S. Senate Curatorial Advisory Board
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) nominated Stefanie Kohn of Cedar Rapids to serve on the U.S. Senate Curatorial Advisory Board. Kohn is the Curator at the National Czech & Slovak Museum & Library in Cedar Rapids. Grassley nominated Kohn in his capacity as U.S. Senate President pro tempore.

“The Senate’s Curatorial Advisory Board is a key resource for the Senate Curator’s office as they preserve our history and share exhibits, publications and programs with the public. As Senate President pro tempore, it’s my honor to nominate an Iowan, Stefanie Kohn, to serve on this distinguished board. As the National Czech & Slovak Museum & Library’s Curator, Stefanie is more than qualified, and I look forward to her appointment,” Grassley said.

The nomination must now be approved by U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and U.S. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) before Kohn can be appointed. In 2020, Sean Ulmer of the Cedar Rapids Museum of Art was appointed to the board after Grassley nominated him for the role.

Background:

The Senate Curatorial Advisory Board provides recommendations to the U.S. Senate Commission on Art about the acquisition and care of the Senate's archives and architecture. It also provides administrative and executive support to the Senate Curator and the Senate Curator’s Office.

title: ICYMI—Hagerty Joins Varney & Co. on Fox Business to Discuss Iran, Russia, and Debanking
text:
