title: Hickenlooper, Colleagues Challenge EPA on Surveillance of Medication Abortion Drugs in Drinking Water
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper and the entire Senate Democratic caucus demanded U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin remove medication abortion drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol from a list of contaminants targeted for surveillance in drinking water in an EPA study announced in September.

The study comes after a years-long pressure campaign by anti-abortion groups, who have urged the EPA to use environmental laws to monitor and ultimately restrict abortion medications that are safe for people and the environment. In their letter, the senators called out Administrator Zeldin, who previously told the Appropriations Committee that he was “not aware” of any efforts to detect medication abortion drugs in water.

“We write to express our serious concerns with the recent announcement that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to take up a surveillance study to track the presence of the medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water,” the senators wrote. “This action is a stark departure from past EPA practice and serves to further this administration’s attacks on reproductive health care and distracts from your agency’s critical role protecting Americans from known chemical pollutants in our water systems.”

The senators note that mifepristone and misoprostol have been deemed safe for patients by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for over 25 years, and reaffirmed as safe for the environment as recently as 2025.

“It is deeply alarming that this kind of radical, anti-science campaign might have an audience at the EPA,” write the senators. “This study is a departure from the EPA’s historic role in protecting our water and air from actual threats to human health and the environment. Instead, this study opens the door to new attacks on safe and accessible reproductive health care, undermining the safety and privacy of patients around the country.”

In May 2026, Hickenlooper, alongside the entire Senate Democratic caucus, introduced a resolution affirming that mifepristone is safe and effective. After the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, Hickenlooper introduced the Women’s Health Protection Act to guarantee access to abortion nationwide, but Republicans blocked its passage.

Hickenlooper previously introduced the Right to Contraception Act, which would codify and strengthen the legal right to contraceptives. He also cosponsored the Right to IVF Act, which would establish a national right to in-vitro fertilization (IVF) services, as well as the Expanding Access to Family Planning Act to protect and expand access to reproductive health care – including birth control and cancer screenings.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Administrator Zeldin:

We write to express our serious concerns with the recent announcement that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to take up a surveillance study to track the presence of the medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water. This action is a stark departure from past EPA practice and serves to further this administration’s attacks on reproductive health care and distracts from your agency’s critical role protecting Americans from known chemical pollutants in our water systems.

Mifepristone has been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in medication abortion in combination with misoprostol since 2000. Decades of scientific research have repeatedly shown that both mifepristone and misoprostol are safe and effective for patients, with mifepristone having been used safely by more than 7.5 million people in the United States since then. Mifepristone’s approval followed a robust scientific review of both the drug’s human safety and environmental health impacts. In 1996, the FDA conducted an Environmental Assessment under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) to assess the potential impacts of mifepristone on the environment. This NEPA assessment resulted in a Finding of No Significant Impact and “concluded that the product can be manufactured, used, and disposed of without any expected adverse environmental effects.” This finding was reaffirmed by the FDA as recently as January 2025. Further, over three decades of scientific research have repeatedly shown that both mifepristone and misoprostol are safe and effective for patients. Misoprostol was first approved by the FDA to treat gastric ulcers in 1988 and has been approved for use in medication abortion in combination with mifepristone since 2000. There is no scientific evidence – recent or otherwise – that demonstrates a need for an EPA surveillance study on misoprostol.

While there is no scientific evidence that would support mifepristone and misoprostol as candidates for surveillance by the EPA, there has been a targeted political pressure campaign by anti-abortion activists to urge the agency to use the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and other environmental authorities to surveil and regulate medication abortion drugs. In January 2025, Politico reported that the anti-abortion rights organization Students for Life was encouraging its supporters to weaponize environmental laws to attack medication abortion. Students for Life leadership described this novel use of the SDWA and other environmental authorities as “using the devil’s own tools against them.” In November 2025, leaders in the EPA’s Office of Water met with the group and encouraged Students for Life to have its members contact the agency and pressure it to regulate abortion medications. When asked about this effort, Students for Life’s head of policy ludicrously stated that “people need to understand that they are likely drinking other people’s abortions” — a categorically false statement.

At a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on May 13, 2026, to review your budget request for Fiscal Year 2027, you were directly asked about these conversations given the House Republican language that was specifically not included in the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations bill. You replied, “I’m not aware of the agency doing anything with that.” In spite of this assurance, the EPA announced this September that it would, for the first time, include mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites in a surveillance study on emerging contaminants. Students for Life celebrated this announcement as victory for its political pressure campaign, saying in an interview that the group is “finally being heard” by the EPA.

It is deeply alarming that this kind of radical, anti-science campaign might have an audience at the EPA. This study is a departure from the EPA’s historic role in protecting our water and air from actual threats to human health and the environment. Instead, this study opens the door to new attacks on safe and accessible reproductive health care, undermining the safety and privacy of patients around the country. We are also concerned that the EPA’s new focus on medication abortion drugs pulls resources and attention away from PFAS, pesticides, and other well-documented contaminants that years of research have shown pose an actual threat to human health and the environment.

No credible evidence shows mifepristone is a threat to America’s drinking water, but there’s plenty of evidence that anti-abortion groups have been asking EPA to concoct bogus studies that say otherwise. Taxpayers fund EPA to protect their health and the environment, not to advance a political campaign against women’s health care.

We strongly urge you to revise this study to remove mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites from the list of emerging contaminants targeted for surveillance. Additionally, we request that you provide the following information no later than October 31, 2026:

1. Your agency’s justification for the surveillance of mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites in this study, including the statutory, regulatory, and scientific basis for its inclusion.

2. Your agency’s process for determining which pharmaceuticals and chemicals were included in this surveillance study.

3. The anticipated timeline for this study and information on how the study’s results will be shared.

4. How this study may be used in relation to the regulatory process under the SDWA.

5. A full list of all meetings between EPA staff and outside organizations to discuss the potential surveillance or regulation of mifepristone and/or misoprostol and its metabolites, including under the Safe Drinking Water Act or any other statute or regulation enforced by your agency.

6. All correspondence between EPA staff and Students for Life since January 20, 2025.

###

title: Hirono, Senate Committee Leaders, Tri-Caucus Chairs Press Trump Administration on Illegal Reallocation of Funding for Minority Serving Institutions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI) led a bicameral coalition—including Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Appropriations Committee Vice Chair Patty Murray (D-WA), Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and other related agencies (LHHS) Appropriations Subcommittee Ranking Member Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Senate Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Dick Durbin (D-IL), and Senators Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), and Alex Padilla (D-CA), alongside Congressional Tri-Caucus Chairs Grace Meng (D-NY), Adriano Espaillat (D-NY), and Yvette Clarke (D-NY)—in pressing U.S. Department of Education (ED) Secretary Linda McMahon on the Administration’s illegal decision to redirect funding from Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs) to other institutions. In a letter to Secretary McMahon, the members emphasized that while increasing funding for those institutions is important, the additional investments cannot come at the expense of MSIs that serve millions of students nationwide. The letter also reiterated the illegal nature of the decision to redirect funding that was statutorily authorized in specific amounts for specific purposes—in clear violation of the law.

“This administration unnecessarily reallocated half of these funds in order to put out a press release leading up to midterm elections touting how much funding it was providing to HBCUs and Tribal Colleges—while robbing MSIs of investments Congress has provided them. It is offensive that the Trump administration is pitting these institutions of higher education and the students they serve against each other, and going to extra lengths to do so,” the members wrote.

There are currently more than 800 federally recognized MSIs which include Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions (AANAPISIs), Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian-Serving Institutions (ANNHSIs), Native American-Serving Non-Tribal Institutions (NASNTIs), and Predominantly Black Institutions (PBIs). These MSIs serve more than 5 million students collectively and have been receiving Congressionally directed federal support for more than 30 years.

In December 2019, Congress passed and President Trump signed into law the bipartisan Fostering Undergraduate Talent by Unlocking Resources for Education Act (FUTURE Act), permanently authorizing $255 million in mandatory funding for HBCUs, TCCUs, and MSIs.

“The law is clear. Congress mandated that funds, with specific statutorily prescribed amounts, be provided for each grant program with specific statutorily defined purposes in each fiscal year,” the members wrote.

The members outlined how the mandatory funding from the FUTURE Act leaves no room for the Trump Administration to redirect funding from MSIs to any other programs or purposes—reiterating the illegal nature of the decision.

“To be clear, mandatory funding for [these institutions]—as provided by the FUTURE Act—cannot be reallocated for other purposes or programs without explicit authorization from Congress. ED does not have the unilateral authority to reallocate these funds,” the members continued

The members concluded their letter by emphasizing the importance of supporting all MSIs—not just HBCUs and TCCUs.

“ED must immediately remedy these illegal actions and restore the funds that were illegally taken away from HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, NASNTIs, and PBIs. Increases in funding for HBCUs and TCCUs should not come at the expense of other critical institutions of higher education,” the members concluded.

In addition to Senators Hirono, Sanders, Murray, Baldwin, Durbin, Luján, and Padilla the letter was cosigned by Senators Chris Coons (D-DE), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Jack Reed (D-RI), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Ed Markey (D-MA), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Mark Warner (D-VA) Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), and Michael Bennet (D-CO).

In addition to Representatives Meng, Espaillat, and Clarke the letter was also cosigned by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Mark Takano (D-CA), Danny Davis (D-IL), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Judy Chu (D-CA), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (D-IL), Dina Titus (D-NV), Paul Tonko (D-NY), Melanie Stansbury (D-NM), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), Robin Kelly (D-IL), Jimmy Gomez (D-CA), Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA), Emily Randall (D-WA), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX), Joaquin Castro (D-TX), Ed Case (D-HI), J. Correa (D-CA), Susan Bonamici (D-OR), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Robert Menendez (D-NJ), Ted Lieu (D-CA), Mike Thompson (D-CA), Derek Tran (D-CA), Lateefah Simon (D-CA), George Whitesides (D-CA), Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Greg Stanton (D-AZ), Linda Sánchez (D-CA), Chellie Pingree (D-ME), Darren Soto (D-FL), Juan Vargas (D-CA), Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ), Jennifer McClellan (D-VA), Kevin Mullin (D-CA), and Robert Garcia (D-CA).

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Secretary McMahon:

Your recent decision to reallocate mandatory funding for Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs) in Fiscal Year 2025 and Fiscal Year 2026 is an illegal violation of Congress’ spending authority under the Constitution. No court has found these programs that Congress has funded to be unconstitutional, and the administration’s mere belief that they are does not give it the necessary authority to spend those funds for any other purpose or program. Many of us previously sent you a letter urging you to allocate Title III and Title V discretionary and mandatory funds as Congress directed to the more than 800 federally-recognized MSIs, which include Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions (AANAPISIs), Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian-Serving Institutions (ANNHSIs), Native American-Serving Non-Tribal Institutions (NASNTIs), and Predominantly Black Institutions (PBIs). Combined, these institutions enroll more than 5 million students in rural and urban communities in states across the country. The Higher Education Act created the statutory framework for grants to these institutions, and has been in place for more than 30 years.

In December 2019, Congress passed and President Trump signed into law the bipartisan Fostering Undergraduate Talent by Unlocking Resources for Education Act (FUTURE Act), permanently authorizing $255 million in grant funds for MSIs, Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), and Tribally Controlled Colleges and Universities (TCCUs). The funds are allocated across seven grant programs, each with a designated funding amount beginning in Fiscal Year 2020 and continuing thereafter. This authorization was an extension of prior mandatory appropriations that began in Fiscal Year 2008 and then expired.

Reallocation of Funds Designated for HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, and NASNTIs

On September 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) announced it would reallocate FY25 and FY26 mandatory funds Congress had specifically allocated for MSIs to HBCUs and TCCUs. In the news release announcing this illegal action, ED announced a “significant, one-time investment of more than $174 million in additional funding to strengthen” HBCUs, and “a one-time award of more than $61 million in additional funding” for TCCUs.

While we strongly support additional funding for HBCUs and TCCUs, increasing funding for some institutions should not come at the expense of others. Furthermore, as previously stated, ED has no authority to redirect mandatory funding for MSIs—in this case, for HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, and NASNTIs—for other purposes or programs. In fact, the entire basis for invalidating and redistributing these funds seems to be a U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) opinion from December 2, 2025, which wrongly determined that both discretionary and mandatory grants for HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, and NASNTIs, and discretionary grants for PBIs, were unconstitutional—without any judicial decision squarely dictating such a conclusion, and lacking any statutory authority to spend mandatory funds for anything other than their required purposes.

Shortly thereafter, ED stated that it was evaluating the full impact of the OLC opinion on the programs. ED then took several actions which made clear that it would not fund the programs, including by not allowing institutions to reapply for eligibility for the programs, and not including them in the eligibility matrix for Title III and Title V funds.

Reallocation of Funds Designated for PBIs

Even by its own baseless standards, the administration determined in the December 2025 OLC memo that the race-based provisions of this program could be severed and stated that ED could continue to provide these competitive grants for the authorized uses in this program, regardless of whether the grant recipient is a PBI. However, rather than adhering to the statute authorizing this grant program—or even OLC’s own wrongful guidance—ED allocated these funds to grantees under a different program with a separate purpose.

Unnecessarily Accelerating Obligation of FY26 Mandatory Funds

On top of all of this, the Trump administration took the completely unnecessary step of obligating FY26 mandatory funding for these programs a full year before it has historically been done, and a full year before the funds expire. These funds are available for two years—funds becoming available in FY26 are available for obligation through FY27. If ED only continued to award funds on the schedule it has historically, FY26 funds would be awarded this time next year.

The administration has claimed it reallocated these funds so they did not lapse and go to waste. While the Trump administration is perfectly willing to let appropriated funds lapse in other cases, including most recently with international education and migrant and seasonal farmworker education programs, half of the MSI funds it reallocated were not going to lapse this year. Even if one were to take the administration’s misguided legal view of these programs at face value, for half of these funds the choice was not between reallocating funding or having the funds lapse. The administration has said repeatedly it wants to work with Congress on solutions to address the legal status of these programs. While we fundamentally disagree with the administration’s view, the administration could have simply continued to administer these funds on the timeline it always has—which means obligating the FY26 funds next September—and waited to see if Congress enacted a solution or a court ruled on the constitutionality of these programs over the course of the next year. In fact, Congress did enact a temporary and albeit imperfect fix in the FY26 Consolidated Appropriations Act when faced with the fact that the Trump administration would otherwise let discretionary funding for MSIs lapse.

This administration unnecessarily reallocated half of these funds in order to put out a press release leading up to midterm elections touting how much funding it was providing to HBCUs and Tribal Colleges—while robbing MSIs of investments Congress has provided them. It is offensive that the Trump administration is pitting these institutions of higher education and the students they serve against each other, and going to extra lengths to do so. If President Trump and this administration were serious about investing in all of these institutions—as each of us is—the president would push for more funds for them instead of seeking to slash education programs while supersizing the Pentagon’s budget.

The law is clear. Congress mandated that funds, with specific statutorily prescribed amounts, be provided for each grant program with specific statutorily defined purposes in each fiscal year. To be clear, mandatory funding for HBCUs, TCCUs, HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, NASNTIs, and PBIs—as provided by the FUTURE Act—cannot be reallocated for other purposes or programs without explicit authorization from Congress. ED does not have the unilateral authority to reallocate these funds.

The Executive Branch’s improper use of mandatory funds plainly violates Article I of the Constitution, which delegates the spending power to Congress. By failing to follow the law and fund programs as Congress directed, and to instead allocate funds for other unauthorized purposes, the Executive Branch has clearly exceeded its Constitutional authority. ED must immediately remedy these illegal actions and restore the funds that were illegally taken away from HSIs, AANAPISIs, ANNHSIs, NASNTIs, and PBIs. Increases in funding for HBCUs and TCCUs should not come at the expense of other critical institutions of higher education. We would welcome the opportunity to work on a bipartisan basis with the administration to increase investments in MSIs, HBCUs, and TCCUs.

Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

###

title: Hoeven Announces More Than $27 Million In LIHEAP Funding For North Dakota & Tribal Communities
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven today announced that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has awarded more than $27 million through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) to help North Dakota households and tribal communities afford home heating and energy costs.

The funding includes:

$20,760,234 to the State of North Dakota.

$2,458,803 to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa.

$1,639,202 to the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe.

$1,366,002 to the Spirit Lake Tribe.

$1,092,801 to the Three Affiliated Tribes (Fort Berthold).

“LIHEAP provides important assistance to families across North Dakota during cold winter months,” said Hoeven. “These funds will help ensure low-income households are able to keep their homes warm and safe.”

LIHEAP is a federally funded program that helps eligible low-income households manage home energy costs, including heating assistance and energy-related emergencies.

title: Hoeven: Red River Valley & Western Railroad Receives $23.6 Million for Rail Infrastructure Improvements
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven today announced that the Red River Valley & Western Railroad (RRVW) has received a $23.6 million grant from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) through the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. Hoeven led the North Dakota Congressional delegation in sending a letter of support for RRVW’s grant application to modernize aging rail infrastructure earlier this year. The funding will support the replacement of approximately 26 miles of rail and the construction of a new siding near Wahpeton to improve safety and efficiency.

In addition, the FRA awarded $690,825 to Bottineau County through the CRISI Program to support rail safety improvements, including a railroad crossing near a school zone and increased grain-handling capacity.

“These investments will help improve rail safety, increase efficiency and strengthen North Dakota’s transportation infrastructure,” said Hoeven. “Reliable rail service is essential to getting our agricultural and energy products to market, and these projects will help support our producers, businesses and communities across the state.”

title: Husted in East Palestine for regional first responder training center announcement, leads Team Tressel Fitness Challenge with elementary students in Youngstown, visits Ohio manufacturers at Vallourec Star
text:
“Whether it’s training first responders, getting kids moving, or backing the workers who build American steel, these visits are about investing in Ohio’s people and Ohio’s communities.”

YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today joined Youngstown State University (YSU) to announce a new regional first responder training center in East Palestine, led the Team Tressel Fitness Challenge with students at Harding Elementary School in Youngstown, and visited Vallourec Star in Youngstown to meet with Ohio manufacturers and job creators.

At the East Palestine Fire Department, Husted joined Gov. Mike DeWine (R-Ohio), Lt. Gov. Jim Tressel and YSU President Bill Johnson to announce the YSU Resiliency, Adaptability, Preparedness, Innovation for Disaster (RAPID) project. The center will give career and volunteer first responders hands-on training for rail-related emergencies, hazardous materials incidents and other dangerous situations. It builds on Norfolk Southern’s $20 million commitment to YSU, announced November 2025, in the wake of the 2023 train derailment.

“This center will give career and volunteer first responders the specialized training they need to be ready for dangerous and unpredictable situations. We pledged that East Palestine won’t be forgotten, and this is a great example of a public-private partnership working to make that happen. The next step is passing my Railway Safety Act so first responders can get the protective equipment they need to stay safe on the job,” said Husted.

At Harding Elementary School, Husted joined Lt. Gov. Tressel to lead about 170 third through fifth grade students through cardio, strength, flexibility and balance exercises. Husted also talked with students about the importance of nutrition and sleep.

“Getting kids moving, eating well and getting enough sleep sets them up to learn, grow and succeed. I’m grateful to Lt. Gov. Tressel for leading this effort, and to the students and teachers at Harding Elementary for bringing it to life,” said Husted.

At Vallourec Star, Husted toured the Youngstown facility and spoke with workers about wins in Washington for manufacturers. The company makes seamless steel pipe used in energy infrastructure and has invested more than $1.5 billion in the United States over the past 15 years, creating more than 500 jobs. A new premium threading line is set to open at the Youngstown facility in November 2026.

“Ohio workers make the steel pipe that keeps American energy production strong, and Vallourec is a great example of what happens when companies invest in Ohio. I’ll keep fighting for policies that help our manufacturers grow, create good jobs and compete with anyone in the world,” said Husted.

These visits build on Husted’s work for Ohio communities, workers and manufacturers. In the Senate, Husted is supporting:

title: Husted secures more than $1.6 million in federal funding for Ohio fire departments
text:
“Our firefighters and EMT’s run toward danger every single day to keep Ohioans safe, and they deserve the training, equipment and staffing to do that job well.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today announced that he secured more than $1.6 million in federal funding for five Ohio fire departments through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) and Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) programs.

Husted successfully advocated for the funding by submitting letters of support on behalf of each department’s grant application.

“Our firefighters and EMT’s run toward danger every single day to keep Ohioans safe, and they deserve the training, equipment and staffing to do that job well. I’m proud to have supported these five Ohio departments as they secured the resources they need to protect their communities,” said Husted.

The five Ohio departments receiving funding are:

The City of Defiance Fire Department: $230,336 to give seven firefighters advanced rescue training.

The Woodlawn Fire Department: $347,619 for a new ambulance.

The Eastlake Fire Department: $74,620 to install new equipment in the firehouse.

The City of Franklin Division of Fire & EMS: $340,000 for new medical equipment.

The Painesville City Fire Department: $620,084 to hire six additional firefighters.

Background:

FEMA’s AFG program provides direct federal funding to eligible fire departments, nonaffiliated EMS organizations and state fire training academies for essential equipment, training, protective gear, vehicles, facility safety improvements and responder health and wellness. Its purpose is to strengthen the safety and readiness of firefighters and the public facing fire and related hazards.

FEMA’s SAFER program funds fire departments and volunteer firefighter organizations to build and sustain an adequate firefighting force, either by paying for additional firefighters or by recruiting and retaining volunteers. Its central goal is to help communities meet industry standards, maintain 24-hour protection where needed and carry out core fire and emergency-response missions.

title: Kelly Introduces Bill to Ban Public Broadcasts of Military Executions
text:
Legislation would prohibit public broadcasts of military executions and prevent taxpayer dollars from being used to record or publicly distribute execution footage

Today, Arizona Senator Mark Kelly introduced the No Public Executions in America Act to prohibit the public broadcasting of military executions and prevent taxpayer dollars from being used to record or publicly distribute footage of executions carried out under federal law.

The legislation comes after Secretary Hegseth announced plans to publicly broadcast the execution of Nidal Hasan, a military prisoner who was sentenced to death for killing 13 people and wounding dozens more in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting. While President Trump has since reversed that decision following calls for him to do so, the bill establishes a permanent prohibition on publicly broadcasting military executions and bans the use of taxpayers’ funds to broadcast federal executions.

“Livestreaming an execution is un-American and dangerous. It is the kind of thing we see with regimes like Iran and the Taliban in Afghanistan, and it won’t make Americans any safer,” said Kelly. “The No Public Executions in America Act will put a stop to this plan and any like it in the future.”

Background:

The No Public Executions in America Act would prohibit federal officials and individuals acting under the authority of the Department of Defense from recording or publicly broadcasting executions conducted under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) and ban federal funds to be used in the broadcasting of executions.

Specifically, the legislation would:

Prohibit public broadcasts of military executions, including livestreaming, recording, publishing, or distributing execution footage.

Prevent taxpayer dollars from being used to record or publicly distribute executions carried out under any federal law, including military commissions.

The legislation would apply to all executions carried out after the bill becomes law, regardless of when the death sentence was imposed or approved by the president.

title: Senators Collins, King Announce More Than $37 Million for Freight Rail Upgrades in Northern Maine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Susan Collins, Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Angus King announced that the Maine Department of Transportation (MaineDOT) has been awarded $37,040,000 for the Northern Aroostook Rail Gateway Modernization and Safety Project. This funding will support the rehabilitation of approximately 90 miles of railroad tracks in northern Maine, including in Fort Kent, Madawaska, and Van Buren.

The funding was awarded through the U.S. Department of Transportation Federal Railroad Administration's (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. In July 2026, Senators Collins and Angus King sent a letter to the FRA in support of MaineDOT's application for this funding, highlighting the importance of the rail corridor to northern Maine's forest products and agricultural industries.

The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) provided an additional $5 billion for the CRISI Program from Fiscal Years 2022 through 2026. Senator Collins was part of the core group of 10 senators who negotiated the IIJA.

“Freight rail is essential to northern Maine’s economy, connecting our forest products and agricultural industries to markets across the country and around the world,” said Senators Collins and King. “This $37 million investment will help modernize aging rail infrastructure and increase railcar capacity, making it easier and safer for Maine businesses to move their products. By strengthening this critical rail corridor, this funding will support local jobs and help keep Aroostook County’s forest products and agricultural industries competitive for years to come.”

Specifically, the project will rehabilitate approximately 90 miles of the Maine Northern Railway's Madawaska Subdivision and the Eastern Maine Railway's Van Buren Subdivision. Improvements will include replacing aging rail, crossties, and ballast, as well as rehabilitating a key railroad bridge.

title: Heinrich, Luján, & Vasquez Call for Independent Review of WIPP Hoist Collapse, Greater DOE Engagement
text:
Following an August incident in which a hoist cable snapped during safety testing, New Mexico lawmakers emphasize the importance of worker safety, transparency, and operational stability at WIPP

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, alongside U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), and U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) sent a letter urging the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to ensure an independent, transparent investigation of an August 19 incident at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP), where an empty lift plunged 1,600 feet to the bottom of the shaft after a cable snapped during safety testing.

The lawmakers are calling for DOE to actively participate in the review, with the full engagement of the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA), and to ensure workers are kept informed of the findings and any corrective actions.

“This incident is deeply alarming, and it comes against a backdrop of ongoing, documented concerns about the condition of WIPP’s aging hoist infrastructure. The safety of WIPP’s workers must come first. These individuals deserve nothing less than full confidence in the systems and procedures on which their lives depend,” said the lawmakers to DOE Office of Environmental Management Assistant Secretary Tim Walsh.

The lawmakers continued, “We urge the Department to ensure a thorough, transparent investigation of the August 19 incident and to solicit the full engagement of the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) as an independent party in that review. Given the nature of the event and the facility’s history of hoist-related failures, an independent assessment of these incidents is essential to credibility—both for workers and for the communities that depend on WIPP’s continued safe operation.”

“This incident also highlights what we understand to be a pattern of unproductive and unsustainable tensions between some WIPP workers and Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, the facility’s prime contractor. These dynamics, if unaddressed, present their own risk to the safe and stable operation of the facility. A workforce that does not trust the contractor responsible for their safety is a major operational risk,” the lawmakers underscored.

The lawmakers concluded their letter by urging DOE to ensure an investigation of the incident that is transparent and responsive to WIPP workers’ concerns.

“We want to be clear: the Department of Energy bears ultimate responsibility for the safe, stable, and long-term operation of WIPP…Workers must be kept fully informed of findings and corrective actions, and their safety concerns must be meaningfully addressed, not managed,” the lawmakers concluded.

The full text of the letter is here and below.

Secretary Walsh:

We write to express our growing concern for the safety of workers at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP) following the August 19, 2026, incident involving the Air Intake Shaft (AIS) hoist, in which a five-person emergency lift plunged to the bottom of the shaft after its cable snapped during testing. This incident is deeply alarming, and it comes against a backdrop of ongoing, documented concerns about the condition of WIPP’s aging hoist infrastructure. The safety of WIPP’s workers must come first. These individuals deserve nothing less than full confidence in the systems and procedures on which their lives depend.

We urge the Department to ensure a thorough, transparent investigation of the August 19 incident and to solicit the full engagement of the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) as an independent party in that review. Given the nature of the event and the facility’s history of hoist-related failures, an independent assessment of these incidents is essential to credibility—both for workers and for the communities that depend on WIPP’s continued safe operation.

This incident also highlights what we understand to be a pattern of unproductive and unsustainable tensions between some WIPP workers and Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, the facility’s prime contractor. These dynamics, if unaddressed, present their own risk to the safe and stable operation of the facility. A workforce that does not trust the contractor responsible for their safety is a major operational risk.

We want to be clear: the Department of Energy bears ultimate responsibility for the safe, stable, and long-term operation of WIPP. That responsibility is not delegable to a contractor. We therefore ask that DOE be proactively engaged as an active participant in the investigation and resolution of this incident. Workers must be kept fully informed of findings and corrective actions, and their safety concerns must be meaningfully addressed, not managed.

Sincerely,

title: Luján, ColleaguesQuestion Meta’s Use of Billions in Research and Development Tax Credits to Subsidize Its AI Data Center Construction Boom
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), a member of the Senate Finance Committee, joined Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and U.S. SenatorsSheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), and Peter Welch (D-Vt.) in calling on Meta to justify its use of billions in federal research and development tax credits to fund its rapid buildout of AI data centers, in a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

According to recent reporting, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental “pilot models”, and therefore eligible for federal R&D tax credits. That is a potential misuse of that credit, which is intended to incentivize experimental research, not to scale up established computing infrastructure. As Meta spends tens of billions of dollars on AI data centers, its R&D tax credits have grown from $700 million in 2023, to $4 billion in 2025.

“The federal research credit can be a useful and necessary tool to support our nation’s innovation economy and cutting-edge research,” the members wrote. “Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard.”

If the reporting is accurate, Meta’s R&D tax credit claims would represent more than 10 percent of all research tax credits claimed in the U.S., based on Joint Committee on Taxation figures.

“Any effort by Meta to use A.I. data center expansion as eligible for research credits is potentially a significant misapplication of federal tax law that merits further investigation,” the senators continued.

Meta has a long record of attempting to lower its tax bill through dubious tax credit claims. In 2013, Meta claimed that $4.1 billion Zuckerberg received by exercising stock options should be eligible for research credits. The IRS challenged that claim and is seeking $355 million in back taxes from Meta.

The members demanded Meta answer the following questions:

Has Meta claimed tax credits under Section 41 of the Internal Revenue Code for tax years 2023 through 2025, related to the buildout and operation of its A.I. data centers? If yes, please describe the legal justification for claiming these federal research credits, the types of research and experimentation expenditures Meta claimed were eligible for the federal research credit, and the total dollar amount of federal research credits Meta claimed for expenses related to A.I. data centers.

Has Meta claimed to the IRS on federal tax filings that its A.I. data centers are “pilot models” in order to qualify for the federal research credit under Sections 41?

Has Meta taken the position that expenses related to A.I. data centers are eligible for the federal research credit while expenses related to non A.I. data centers are not? If yes, please provide a legal analysis explaining why Meta believes that expenses related to its A.I. data centers are eligible for federal research credits while data centers unrelated to A.I. are not.

Did Meta consult with experts from EY or any other professional accounting firms prior to making the decision to claim federal research credits for expenses related to A.I. data centers? If yes, please describe these interactions and whether EY or any other professional service firms advised Meta that expenses related to A.I. data centers qualified for the federal research credit.

Did EY or any other professional accounting firm or law firm provide an opinion or opinions on whether expenses related to A.I. data centers were eligible to be claimed for the research credit? If so, please provide copies of such opinions.

In 2023, Meta disclosed that it claimed $700 million in federal research and development tax credits. How much of those tax credits was related to the construction or operation of A.I. data centers? Please specify how much of the federal research credits Meta claimed that year was for the purchase of microchips, computing equipment and other materials necessary to build or operate A.I. data centers.

In 2024, Meta disclosed that it claimed approximately $2 billion in federal research and development tax credits. How much of those tax credits was related to the construction or operation of A.I. data centers? Please specify how much of the federal research credits Meta claimed that year was for the purchase of microchips, computing equipment and other materials necessary to build or operate A.I. data centers.

In 2025, Meta disclosed that it claimed approximately $3.9 billion in federal research and development tax credits. How much of those tax credits was related to the construction or operation of A.I. data centers? Please specify how much of the federal research credits Meta claimed that year was for the purchase of microchips, computing equipment and other materials necessary to build or operate A.I. data centers.

Why did Meta claim that $4.1 billion in stock-based compensation for Mark Zuckerberg between 2008 – 2010 was a “qualified research expense”? Please provide a detailed justification as to why the CEO compensation for Mr. Zuckerberg serves a research or experimental purpose.

Does Meta intend to continue challenging the $355 million in back taxes the IRS is seeking related to treating Mr. Zuckerberg’s stock-based compensation as a qualified research expense? If yes, why?

The full letter is here.

title: Markey, Merkley Announce Joint Resolution of Disapproval on U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal, Setting Up Senate Vote
text:
Washington (October 15, 2026) – Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) and Senator Jeff Merkley, co-chairs of the bicameral Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group today introduced a Joint Resolution of Disapproval (JRD) that gives the Senate an opportunity to debate and vote on the proposed U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal before it goes into effect.

Under federal law, the agreement will go into effect after a 90-day congressional review period, unless Congress passes a JRD. The Markey-Merkley JRD sets up a vote for the Senate to consider the resolution after November 29.

“The US-Saudi nuclear deal is about megatons, not megawatts. Trump should not be sharing nuclear bomb technology with a nation that US intelligence says may want nuclear weapons. Even worse, the deal fails to meet the nonproliferation Gold Standard, by allowing Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, an essential step to producing a bomb, but not requiring the strongest international inspections. This deal is the starting gun for a Middle East nuclear arms race. Congress must reject it,” said Senator Markey.

“Giving Saudi Arabia access to U.S. civilian nuclear energy technology without ironclad protections to make sure it doesn't provide a foundation for a nuclear bomb is unacceptable. It is essential that nations pursuing civilian energy programs agree to the ‘gold standard’ of restrictions on fuel reprocessing and enrichment and rigorous inspections to ensure that a nuclear energy program doesn’t become a covert nuclear weapons program,” said Senator Merkley. “We can’t sleepwalk into a decision this consequential. The law gives Congress the power to review and block a deal like this, and the Senate will now have the chance to fulfill its statutory responsibility before it’s too late.”

If enacted, the Markey-Merkley JRD would block the Trump Administration’s U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation agreement, referred to as a “123 agreement.” The current agreement lacks two critical components necessary to prevent a nuclear arms race in the Middle East.

The first is the “gold standard” for 123 agreements, which requires that a nation forego reprocessing of spent fuel and the enrichment of uranium to create nuclear fuel. Enrichment and reprocessing facilities create a significant infrastructure for the development of a nuclear weapons program. The second is a requirement that a nation sign on to the Additional Protocol, which turns the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) from accountants into investigators that can make sure that a nation is not pursuing development of a nuclear weapon.

If a 123 agreement with Saudi Arabia proceeds without the “gold standard” and the Additional Protocol, it raises significant risks. One risk is that Saudi Arabia will pursue a covert nuclear weapons program. A second risk is that the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which agreed to both the “gold standard” and the Additional Protocol, could opt out of those requirements because its 123 agreement allows the UAE to renegotiate if the U.S. gives another Middle East state a more favorable deal. A third is that Iran would undoubtedly reject any future restriction on its nuclear program that Saudi Arabia had not been held to. Taken together, these factors significantly raise the risk of nuclear weapon proliferation and the possibility of future conflicts in a nuclear-armed world.

Previously, Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the same leader that U.S. intelligence found approved the operation to kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi, said that if Iran acquires a nuclear weapon, then Saudi Arabia will develop one as well. Despite public reporting indicating that President Trump would mandate Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel as part of the agreement, there is also no formal mention of this requirement in the deal.

Full text of the Joint Resolution of Disapproval can be found by clicking here.

On September 16, Senators Markey and Merkley led a bipartisan group of Senators to press the Trump administration to declassify and publicly release the two side letters accompanying the proposed U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation agreement, referred to as a “123 agreement.”

As a founder of the national Nuclear Freeze movement, Senator Markey has long been the Congressional leader on ending the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

On August 26, Senator Markey urged Congress to reject the Trump-Saudi nuclear deal after the Trump administration sent to Congress a nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia that would open the door to providing the Kingdom with the means to produce nuclear weapons materials but would not require the most stringent safeguards against the development of those weapons.

On July 31, Senators Markey and Merkley, along with Representatives John Garamendi (CA-08) and Don Beyer (VA-08), co-chairs of the Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group, published an opinion piece slamming Trump’s Saudi nuclear deal, citing then-Senator Marco Rubio’s understanding that handing nuclear weapons to Saudi Arabia would be disastrous.

On March 25, Senators Markey and Merkley reintroduced the No Nuclear Weapons for Saudi Arabia Act, legislation that would mandate that any nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia can go into effect only if it receives the affirmative vote of Congress.

On March 18, Senator Markey led his colleagues in writing to Secretary Rubio demanding the Trump administration must meet the “gold standard” of nuclear non-proliferation protections by denying Saudi Arabia the means to produce weapons-grade uranium and plutonium, materials that could be used in a nuclear bomb.

In November 2025, Senator Markey and Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, urging the Trump administration to include the strongest possible “gold standard” nonproliferation measures in any nuclear cooperation agreement with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to foreclose any pathway to a nuclear weapon.

In November 2024, Senator Markey wrote to the Biden administration seeking answers about any agreement that would normalize relations between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Israel in exchange for civil nuclear energy cooperation and a U.S. defense commitment to the Kingdom.

As far back as 2017, Senator Markey pressed the first Trump administration on the status of all current and ongoing discussions between the United States and other countries, including Saudi Arabia, on 123 agreements after it was reported that former National Security Advisor Michael Flynn was peddling a plan to build nuclear reactors throughout the Middle East.

title: Sen. Markey, Leader Schumer, Reps. Matsui, Menendez, Meng Lead Colleagues in Demanding Trump FCC Withdraw Proposal to Undermine E-Rate Program
text:
Lawmakers argue that dismantling E-Rate will widen the digital divide and raise costs for the communities that can least afford it

Letter Text (PDF)

Washington (October 15, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee and author of the E-Rate program, along with Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Representatives Doris Matsui (CA-07), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), and Grace Meng (NY-06), today led nearly the entire Senate Democratic Caucus and more than 60 members of the House Democratic Caucus in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to withdraw the Commission’s damaging proposal to eliminate or limit the E-Rate program. In June, the Carr FCC voted to open a rulemaking examining E-Rate, which helps schools and libraries across the country afford reliable internet access.

For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped close the digital divide by ensuring that students and library patrons can access the internet regardless of their income or ZIP code. In 2025, E-Rate helped more than 158,000 schools and libraries pay recurring broadband bills, increase bandwidth, maintain secure internal Wi-Fi networks, and replace aging infrastructure. Ending or sharply curtailing E-Rate would impose severe costs on schools and libraries while weakening economic growth, undermining American technological leadership, and jeopardizing national security.

The E-Rate program has invested more than $69 billion to connect schools and libraries to the internet across the country. Massachusetts schools and libraries have received more than $950 million from the E-Rate program and another $97 million from the Emergency Connectivity Fund, a $7 billion program that Senator Markey created within the American Rescue Plan to provide devices and connectivity for students and educators at home.

In the letter, the lawmakers wrote, “Schools and libraries help develop the next generation of engineers, scientists, and cybersecurity professionals, including in communities that have historically lacked access to those opportunities. Cutting E-Rate would narrow that talent pipeline. Maintaining connectivity in every school and library is therefore an investment in America’s technological leadership, economic competitiveness, and national security.

The lawmakers continued, “We strongly support measures to protect children online and address concerns around excessive screen time. But cutting E-Rate is not a child-safety measure. E-Rate funds broadband connectivity — not laptops, tablets, applications, or online content — and recipients must already comply with the Children’s Internet Protection Act, including by using filtering and blocking tools, adopting internet-safety policies, and educating students about appropriate online behavior. States and local communities, meanwhile, are developing targeted policies governing when and how students use devices in schools — an appropriate way to address screen-time concerns, rather than cutting broadband support. The Commission should not use child safety as a pretext to dismantle the secure, managed broadband infrastructure that schools and libraries need to educate students and help them navigate the digital world safely.”

The letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK HOSTS PENNSYLVANIA RED TAPE DIALOGUES IN PHILADELPHIA
text:
PHILADELPHIA, PA — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) today hosted the Pennsylvania Red Tape Dialogues at Temple University in Philadelphia, joined by former Arizona Governor Doug Ducey and business leaders from across the Commonwealth. This first-of-its-kind event brought together C-suite executives, small and mid-sized business owners, federal and state regulators, and policy experts to identify burdensome regulations and develop practical solutions to help Pennsylvania businesses grow, create jobs, and compete.

Senator McCormick convened business leaders across ten industries critical to Pennsylvania’s economy for direct, industry-by-industry problem-solving. Participants addressed challenges ranging from permitting delays and duplicative requirements to outdated regulations and inefficient government processes that prevent businesses from investing, hiring, and expanding.

“Pennsylvania is home to some of the most innovative businesses and hardest-working people in America, but too often, unnecessary regulations and government bureaucracy stand in the way of their success,” said Senator McCormick. “Today, we brought business leaders and regulators together in Philadelphia to identify what’s holding them back and find practical solutions. My goal is to make it easier to invest, expand, and create good-paying jobs right here in Pennsylvania.”

“I applaud Senator McCormick for bringing Pennsylvania’s business leaders together today and leading the charge on regulatory reform,” said former Arizona Governor Doug Ducey. “Regulation has a role in protecting public health and safety, but streamlining burdensome rules can unlock real economic potential.”

Unlike traditional conferences or listening sessions, the Pennsylvania Red Tape Dialogues focused on producing concrete, actionable recommendations to help Pennsylvania businesses. Business leaders representing ten industries, including manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, defense, transportation, retail, higher education, and housing, worked directly with regulators and policymakers to identify specific barriers and potential reforms.

Turning Recommendations into Results

Within 60 days, Senator McCormick will compile the recommendations presented at the Pennsylvania Red Tape Dialogues into a report and deliver it directly to federal and state officials positioned to act.

To ensure accountability, Senator McCormick will publicly track the progress of those recommendations, identifying what has been completed, what remains underway, and what still requires action.

The Pennsylvania Red Tape Dialogues build on Senator McCormick’s broader efforts to convene leaders from business, government, and academia to unlock economic potential, create good-paying jobs, and expand opportunities for Pennsylvania. Following the Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit in Pittsburgh and the Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit in Carlisle, this initiative continues Senator McCormick’s commitment to bringing decision-makers together to deliver tangible results for Pennsylvania workers, businesses, and communities.

A second risk is that the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which agreed to both the “gold standard” and the Additional Protocol, could opt out of those requirements because its 123 agreement allows the UAE to renegotiate if the U.S. gives another Middle East state a more favorable deal. A third is that Iran would undoubtedly reject any future restriction on its nuclear program that Saudi Arabia had not been held to. Taken together, these factors significantly raise the risk of nuclear weapon proliferation and the possibility of future conflicts in a nuclear-armed world.

Previously, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the same leader that U.S. intelligence found approved the operation to kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi, said that if Iran acquires a nuclear weapon, then Saudi Arabia will develop one as well. Despite public reporting indicating that President Trump would mandate Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel as part of the agreement, there is also no formal mention of this requirement in the deal.

Merkley began his career in public service as a nuclear weapons policy analyst at the Pentagon and the Congressional Budget Office and has been sounding the alarm over the U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal. He has partnered with Markey—as a fellow co-chair of the bicameral Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group—to press the Trump Administration on its secrecy surrounding the agreement and slam the deal as reckless.

Full text of the Joint Resolution of Disapproval can be found by clicking here.

title: New Moreno Bill Targets Incentives For Data Centers With One-Hundred Percent Federal Tax
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) introduced a bill to implement a one-hundred percent tax on state and local incentives and ban federal giveaways for data centers, protecting taxpayers from footing the bill for data centers and ensuring that large technology corporations pay their own way.

“Taxpayers will not subsidize data centers, period. When state and local governments hand out corporate welfare to these massive corporations, the federal government must intervene and shut it down,” said Senator Moreno. “The American people deserve a government that fights for them, not one that serves as a piggy bank for mega-corporations.”​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Background:

Data centers are essential to America’s dominance in the SI race. However, hyper-scalers must pay into the system that they are benefitting from to ensure the American public can also reap the rewards of this technology. In the past, the American taxpayer was subsidizing data center expansion through federal, state, and local tax breaks to the tune of billions.

The RECLAIM Act would flip that paradigm on its head, prohibiting the federal government from subsidizing trillion-dollar Big Tech companies. After all, they can than afford it.

In addition, this bill would institute a 100% federalexcise tax on any state or local grant or tax exemption that SI hyper-scalers leverage for data centers. As a result, Big Tech will have to use their own funds – not Americans’ hard earned taxpayer money – to fund their operations.

Data center development in the United States is essential, but gargantuan Big Tech companies should pay their own way. Technological dominance will be built on a symbiotic relationship between industry and the American people, not government handouts.

title: In Nespelem, Murray Meets with the Confederated Colville Tribes to Discuss Wildfire Recovery Support
text:
Murray: “There is not a single dollar I won’t pursue if it means helping communities across the state recover and rebuild from these devastating fires.”

***PHOTOS AND B-ROLL HERE***

Nespelem, WA — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, met with the Confederated Colville Tribes to hear their concerns following wildfire season and discuss next steps of recovery after the August wildfires that devastated the Colville Reservation. Senator Murray visited Nespelem saw areas where a private owner has worked to thin the forest on their property in ways consistent with tribal work and efforts to mitigate wildfire risks and joined a roundtable with the Colville Business Council to learn more about what the community needs to recover and mitigate wildfires.

On the Colville Reservation, the Kaiser Canyon Fire burned approximately 138,293 acres and the Modrite Fire burned around 57,594 acres. Combined, these fires devastated nearly 200,000 acres, impacting forest, grassland, residential areas, along with sacred and culturally significant tribal sites. The fires caused extensive damage to tribal infrastructure, 150 cultural sites, and at least 33 homes were destroyed. The fires caused smoke damage to tribally owned facilities, including critical infrastructure such as the Lucy Covington Government Center, healthcare facilities, and community centers. Large portions of forested land and natural habitats were destroyed, severely affecting local wildlife populations, including endangered species such as the Sharp-tailed grouse. The Kaiser and Modrite Fires also setback the Colville Tribes’ forestry program, a major source of revenue and jobs for the Colville Tribe.

“I know this has been a terrible wildfire season for you and the devastation and loss this community has faced is heartbreaking. This community has endured the unthinkable—and as you rebuild, I want everyone in this room to know that I am with you every step of the way,” Senator Murray said. “I know this recovery will be long—but I want you to know that I’m here with you for the long haul. I will fight to ensure the Colville Tribes have the resources necessary to rebuild and be prepared to respond to wildfires in the future. I know that the Colville’s recovery will not be measured in days or weeks—it will be measured in months and years. I am here to support you no matter how long it takes. There is not a single dollar I won’t pursue if it means helping communities across the state recover and rebuild from these devastating fires.”

“This past summer was an especially bad fire season on the Colville Reservation. The best way to feel the impact of a severe fire event is to come and walk through the ashes with your own feet,” said Cindy Marchand, the Chairwoman of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation. “Senator Murray’s visit to the Colville Reservation today to view the fire damage displays her care for the citizens of this community and her commitment to assisting our recovery. This comes as no surprise since Senator Murray has been a good long-term partner with the Colville Tribes on many issues. The Colville Tribes welcomes continued collaboration with the Senator as we both strive to make the Colville Reservation and the State of Washington better places to live for all citizens.”

Supporting investments in wildfire prevention and response continues to be a top priority for Senator Murray, particularly as she negotiates this year’s government funding bills. Murray has been outspoken against the Trump administration’s efforts undermine much of the federal workforce that supports wildfire prevention and response work year-round. As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, in the Interior and Environment appropriations bill for Fiscal Year 2026, which Senator Murray negotiated and helped pass into law, Murray worked to include essential investments in wildfire preparedness and suppression. In FY26, she secured $6.13 billion for the U.S. Forest Service, with separate additional funding for the Wildfire Suppression Operations Reserve. The bill rejected the steep $1.4 billion cut to the Forest Service’s non-fire budget proposed by President Trump and provides funding for the Forest Service to improve forest restoration and fire risk reduction efforts on federal lands. The FY26 bill also fully funds essential wildfire preparedness and suppression efforts by providing $4.25 billion for wildfire suppression, of which $2.85 billion is for the Wildfire Suppression Operations Reserve Fund and continues to support the increased pay for federal firefighters enacted into law last year. Senator Murray continues to push back against Trump’s FY27 budget request, to protect our public lands.

title: Murray, Larsen Urge Trump Administration to Fund Sumas and Lynden Border Station Modernization Projects
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02), top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, sent a letter to General Services Administration (GSA) Administrator Edward Forst requesting GSA prioritize construction of two stalled border station projects in Northwest Washington. Senator Murray and Representative Larsen sent this letter on September 22 and have yet to receive response from GSA.

“It has come to our attention that Washington state’s Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Ports of Entry (LPOE) projects are temporarily prevented from moving forward,” the lawmakers wrote. “We write to express our concern regarding this decision by General Services Administration (GSA).”

A land port of entry (LPOE) is a federal border facility used to control the entry and departure of people and cargo at a land border. Congress appropriated $3.4 billion to modernize 26 LPOEs across the United States in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law of 2021, which both Senator Murray and Representative Larsen helped become law. As of August 12, 2026, the GSA has temporarily prevented nine of those projects from moving forward, including the Kenneth G. Ward Land Port of Entry in Lynden and the Sumas Land Port of Entry.

“Both LPOEs are vital border crossings for Washington state and Canada and play a significant role in trade and economic development that is relevant to the economic vitality of the United States,” the lawmakers continued. “Delaying these projects will have consequential impacts on the nation’s supply chain, labor market, and national security.”

Sen. Murray and Rep. Larsen stressed the importance of certainty about the status of the border station projects for city officials in Sumas and Lynden to plan for the impact that construction will have to downtown buildings and the local economy.

“These projects are also key to local development plans in the cities of Sumas and Lynden, where the LPOEs are located,” the lawmakers wrote. “LPOE modernization will impact several existing buildings in Sumas’s downtown core, and Lynden is preparing to take on additional commercial traffic. Prolonged uncertainty on project timelines will only lead to more disruption and delays in economic development of these cities.”

The lawmakers urged GSA Administrator Forst to prioritize the Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Port of Entry projects when the GSA reassesses the prioritization of the remaining nine LPOEs in the coming months and requested continued updates on decisions regarding the projects.

The full text of the letter can be read here.

Murray and Larsen Conduct Oversight of GSA Under the Trump Administration

As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray has led oversight of GSA’s reckless effort to dump federal properties, pressing the Trump administration on why it terminated leases without notifying Congress as required by law, and how veterans, taxpayers, Tribal members, and farmers would still get the in-person help they depend on. Murray continues to hold the Trump administration accountable for skirting the law, keeping Congress in the dark, and cutting off services families rely on.

In a Transportation & Infrastructure Committee oversight hearing in March, Rep. Larsen raised concerns about the GSA’s tumultuous first 14 months under the Trump administration and a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that the GSA signed with the Defense Ministry of Pakistan without providing evidence of the GSA’s legal jurisdiction to enter into the MOU or engage in redeveloping the private hotel. The Transportation and Infrastructure Committee has jurisdiction over the GSA.

This July, Rep. Larsen and Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Ranking Member Greg Stanton (AZ-04) sent a letter to Administrator Forst seeking answers about the agency’s involvement with the renovation of the Roosevelt Hotel and reporting from Bloomberg that the GSA signed a $1.4 million contract with Sullivan & Cromwell—a law firm with significant ties to the Trump administration—to provide legal services regarding the privately-owned property.
