title: Murray Leads Senate Democrats in Demanding Answers on EPA Surveillance of Medication Abortion Drugs in Drinking Water
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, led the entire Democratic caucus in a letter to U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin urging the EPA to remove medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol from a list of contaminants targeted for surveillance in drinking water in a study that the agency announced in September.

In their letter, the lawmakers demand answers on the study from EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, who previously told the Appropriations Committee that he was “not aware” of any efforts to detect medication abortion in water. The surveillance study comes after a years-long pressure campaign by anti-abortion groups who have urged the EPA to retool environmental protection laws to monitor and ultimately restrict abortion medications that are safe for humans and the environment.

“We write to express our serious concerns with the recent announcement that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to take up a surveillance study to track the presence of the medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water,” the Senators write. “This action is a stark departure from past EPA practice and serves to further this administration’s attacks on reproductive health care and distracts from your agency’s critical role protecting Americans from known chemical pollutants in our water systems.”

The senators note that mifepristone and misoprostol have been deemed safe for patients by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for over 25 years, and reaffirmed as safe for the environment as recently as 2025. “There is no scientific evidence – recent or otherwise – that demonstrates a need for an EPA surveillance study,” they write.

“While there is no scientific evidence that would support mifepristone and misoprostol as candidates for surveillance by the EPA, there has been a targeted political pressure campaign by anti-abortion activists to urge the agency to use the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and other environmental authorities to surveil and regulate medication abortion drugs,” the lawmakers continue.

Murray and colleagues also call out Zeldin for stating that he had no knowledge of efforts to target mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water when the EPA had engaged in conversations with radical anti-abortion groups and encouraged them to pressure the agency to regulate abortion medication.

“It is deeply alarming that this kind of radical, anti-science campaign might have an audience at the EPA,” write the senators. “This study is a departure from the EPA’s historic role in protecting our water and air from actual threats to human health and the environment. Instead, this study opens the door to new attacks on safe and accessible reproductive health care, undermining the safety and privacy of patients around the country.”

The lawmakers write that the EPA’s responsibility is to regulate contaminants that harm human health and the environment, not drugs that are well-documented to be safe and effective but disrupt Republican efforts to control women’s bodies. “Taxpayers fund EPA to protect their health and the environment, not to advance a political campaign against women’s health care,” they conclude.

The senators are also requesting all correspondence between EPA staff and Students for Life since January 20, 2025, and information on the EPA’s justification and process for monitoring medication abortion in the study.

Murray was joined by U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) and U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Richard Durbin (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Ed Markey (D-MA), Christopher Murphy (D-CT), Jon Ossoff (D-GA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Gary Peters (D- MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Administrator Zeldin:

We write to express our serious concerns with the recent announcement that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to take up a surveillance study to track the presence of the medication abortion drugs mifepristone and misoprostol in drinking water. This action is a stark departure from past EPA practice and serves to further this administration’s attacks on reproductive health care and distracts from your agency’s critical role protecting Americans from known chemical pollutants in our water systems.

Mifepristone has been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in medication abortion in combination with misoprostol since 2000. Decades of scientific research have repeatedly shown that both mifepristone and misoprostol are safe and effective for patients, with mifepristone having been used safely by more than 7.5 million people in the United States since then. Mifepristone’s approval followed a robust scientific review of both the drug’s human safety and environmental health impacts. In 1996, the FDA conducted an Environmental Assessment under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) to assess the potential impacts of mifepristone on the environment. This NEPA assessment resulted in a Finding of No Significant Impact and “concluded that the product can be manufactured, used, and disposed of without any expected adverse environmental effects.” This finding was reaffirmed by the FDA as recently as January 2025. Further, over three decades of scientific research have repeatedly shown that both mifepristone and misoprostol are safe and effective for patients. Misoprostol was first approved by the FDA to treat gastric ulcers in 1988 and has been approved for use in medication abortion in combination with mifepristone since 2000. There is no scientific evidence – recent or otherwise – that demonstrates a need for an EPA surveillance study on misoprostol.

While there is no scientific evidence that would support mifepristone and misoprostol as candidates for surveillance by the EPA, there has been a targeted political pressure campaign by anti-abortion activists to urge the agency to use the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and other environmental authorities to surveil and regulate medication abortion drugs. In January 2025, Politico reported that the anti-abortion rights organization Students for Life was encouraging its supporters to weaponize environmental laws to attack medication abortion. Students for Life leadership described this novel use of the SDWA and other environmental authorities as “using the devil’s own tools against them.” In November 2025, leaders in the EPA’s Office of Water met with the group and encouraged Students for Life to have its members contact the agency and pressure it to regulate abortion medications. When asked about this effort, Students for Life’s head of policy ludicrously stated that “people need to understand that they are likely drinking other people’s abortions” — a categorically false statement.

At a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on May 13, 2026, to review your budget request for Fiscal Year 2027, you were directly asked about these conversations given the House Republican language that was specifically not included in the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations bill. You replied, “I’m not aware of the agency doing anything with that.” In spite of this assurance, the EPA announced this September that it would, for the first time, include mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites in a surveillance study on emerging contaminants. Students for Life celebrated this announcement as victory for its political pressure campaign, saying in an interview that the group is “finally being heard” by the EPA.

It is deeply alarming that this kind of radical, anti-science campaign might have an audience at the EPA. This study is a departure from the EPA’s historic role in protecting our water and air from actual threats to human health and the environment. Instead, this study opens the door to new attacks on safe and accessible reproductive health care, undermining the safety and privacy of patients around the country. We are also concerned that the EPA’s new focus on medication abortion drugs pulls resources and attention away from PFAS, pesticides, and other well-documented contaminants that years of research have shown pose an actual threat to human health and the environment.

No credible evidence shows mifepristone is a threat to America’s drinking water, but there’s plenty of evidence that anti-abortion groups have been asking EPA to concoct bogus studies that say otherwise. Taxpayers fund EPA to protect their health and the environment, not to advance a political campaign against women’s health care.

We strongly urge you to revise this study to remove mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites from the list of emerging contaminants targeted for surveillance. Additionally, we request that you provide the following information no later than October 31, 2026:

1. Your agency’s justification for the surveillance of mifepristone and misoprostol and their metabolites in this study, including the statutory, regulatory, and scientific basis for its inclusion.

2. Your agency’s process for determining which pharmaceuticals and chemicals were included in this surveillance study.

3. The anticipated timeline for this study and information on how the study’s results will be shared.

4. How this study may be used in relation to the regulatory process under the SDWA.

5. A full list of all meetings between EPA staff and outside organizations to discuss the potential surveillance or regulation of mifepristone and/or misoprostol and its metabolites, including under the Safe Drinking Water Act or any other statute or regulation enforced by your agency.

6. All correspondence between EPA staff and Students for Life since January 20, 2025.

Sincerely,

title: Murray Slams Trump for Threatening Millions of Americans with Financial Chaos by Stupidly Upending Federal Student Aid Office
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, issued the following statement in response to reports that the Trump administration is moving to strip the Federal Student Aid office out of the Department of Education:

“When did creating an entirely new federal agency to do the exact same work that’s already being done equate to efficiency? The law is clear: Federal Student Aid belongs at the Department of Education, and the Trump administration cannot move it without an act of Congress—nor have they even bothered consulting Congress.

“This office manages more than $1.6 trillion in debts owed by more than 40 million borrowers—tens of millions of Americans are depending on government to actually work here. Trump has already pushed out nearly half its staff—this intentional sabotage only threatens to create true financial chaos in people’s lives.

“Every family filling out the FAFSA, every student counting on a Pell Grant, and every borrower trying to make a student loan payment will pay for Trump’s idiotic obsession with abolishing the Department of Education. Americans do not support abolishing the Department of Education—they just want a financial aid system that works. I will keep fighting to block this illegal move every way I can, and it is past time for Republicans to join Democrats and put an end to this nonsense.”

Senator Murray has led the fight against the Trump administration’s efforts to dismantle the Department of Education. As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray helped negotiate the fiscal year 2026 funding bill for the Department. That bill rejected $12 billion in proposed cuts to the Department of Education and President Trump’s request to abolish it. Murray also fought to include ironclad language in the bill barring Secretary McMahon from using illegal interagency agreements to strip out the Department’s core responsibilities and hand them over to other agencies—Republicans refused, and Murray has continued to push back as the Department has signed new agreements. In July, Murray offered three amendments in the HELP Committee to stop these illegal transfers. Murray was successful in passing an amendment with strong bipartisan support out of committee which would require the Department to tell Congress and the public what each illegal interagency agreement costs taxpayers.

Murray has also unflinchingly called attention to the administration’s nonstop efforts to block critical funds for students and teachers at every turn, issuing a statement just yesterday to call attention to the administration’s latest efforts to cut grant funding—and always using every tool at her disposal to stand up for public education.

Murray forcefully opposed McMahon’s nomination from the outset. She has called attention to the administration’s mass firings at the Department at every turn, she has led public forums in the Senate on the damage the Trump administration is doing to public education, and she has rallied with students and teachers to stand up for the critical support the Department of Education provides America’s students.

Senator Murray has championed students and families at every stage of her career—fighting to help ensure every child in America can get a high-quality public education. Among other things, Senator Murray negotiated the bipartisan Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), landmark legislation that she got signed into law, replacing the broken No Child Left Behind Act. As a longtime appropriator, she has successfully fought to boost funding to support students and invest in our nation’s K-12 schools, and she has secured significant increases to the Pell Grant so that it goes further for students pursuing a higher education. Senator Murray also successfully negotiated the FAFSA Simplification Act, bipartisan legislation to reform the financial aid application process, simplify the FAFSA form for students and parents, and significantly expand eligibility for federal aid.

title: Padilla, Durbin, Warner, Peters Demand Answers on Trump Administration’s Efforts to Interfere in Midterm Elections
text:
Ranking Members also press DOJ and FBI to provide information related to the agencies’ coordination with DHS, the U.S. Intelligence Community, and the White House in these efforts to undermine our election security

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, and Senators Mark Warner, Vice Chair of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and Gary Peters, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, demanded answers regarding the alarming series of actions the Trump Administration has undertaken to undermine state and local election administration.

In a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel, the Senators raised concerns about the extent of the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) and FBI’s coordination with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the U.S. Intelligence Community, and the White House in efforts to interfere with the midterm elections.

“Under your leadership, DOJ and the FBI have sought to upend our federalist system by seizing ballots and election materials, seeking the personal information of election workers and volunteers, showing up at the homes of election officials for questioning, threatening election officials with prosecution, attempting to compel states to provide the federal government with unredacted voter rolls, and raiding the offices of a voting rights nonprofit—often at the apparent behest of President Trump and White House officials, including Stephen Miller,” wrote the Senators. “Director Patel has reportedly urged the FBI to persist in these fishing expeditions by exhorting agents to ‘look harder’ because ‘this is a push from 47,’ and senior DOJ officials have threatened to fire or override prosecutors who choose not to pursue election fraud cases that FBI or DHS agents bring them, in contravention of longstanding DOJ rules for prosecutors.”

The Senators outlined the timeline of the Trump Administration’s attempted efforts to undermine elections. The weaponization of DOJ and the FBI as part of this effort became clear last year, when the head of the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) began filing lawsuits against multiple states to demand they produce unredacted copies of their voter registration lists. CRT sued Fulton County, Georgia last December, seeking records related to the 2020 election. Following this lawsuit, the FBI executed a search warrant at the Fulton County election office in Union City, Georgia.

Additionally, then-Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard inexplicably attended this raid—and escalated this breach of protocol the following day, when she met with FBI agents who had conducted the raid and called President Trump to address the agents.

“These efforts have occurred as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) has taken unprecedented steps to investigate unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud and as the then-Director of National Intelligence took extraordinary steps to insert herself into an already-troubling FBI raid of a local election facility,” continued the Senators. “Taken together, these actions constitute a disturbing, whole-of-government campaign that has weaponized federal law enforcement to relitigate the 2020 election that President Trump lost, attempting to undermine the constitutional election administration powers of states ahead of the 2026 midterm elections and seeking to sow confusion and fear among voters and state and local election officials.”

The Senators also raised concerns about Patel refusing to rule out sending FBI agents to polling locations on Election Day—an illegal tactic that would inevitably intimidate voters.

“The concern over this Administration engaging in intimidation tactics related to the election is not unwarranted,” wrote the Senators. “Just one month before election day, President Trump continues to float the idea that he has legal authority to declare a national emergency or invoke the Insurrection Act around the midterms. Moreover, DOJ has already sought to intimidate election officials across the country.”

Just this week, the DOJ attempted to escalate these efforts, laying the groundwork to potentially challenge ballots ahead of Election Day with a letter to California election officials, which demanded that they verify the citizenship of individuals listed in a DOJ-provided thumb drive within 48 hours and threatened legal action if they do not follow the Department’s instructions on handling the ballots of these individuals.

“Furthermore, it is impossible to ignore the brazen partisan intentions behind these actions—not just due to President Trump’s repeated, baseless accusations that Democrats must cheat to win elections, but in light of the unethical political actions you have each taken in recent weeks, including your appearances at an August campaign rally in New York, and Attorney General Blanche’s appearance at the Republican Party’s midterm convention in Texasand a campaign event in North Carolina for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley,” the Senators concluded. “It is our constitutional duty to conduct oversight over these unprecedented abuses of power to improperly meddle with state and local election administration in the midterm elections that are already underway. The American people deserve to know why federal resources are being diverted from mission critical work to ensure their safety and instead devoted to this costly and, should it further escalate, potentially criminal crusade.”

The Senators also noted that despite this brazen, partisan, and coordinated effort to undermine the constitutional structure of our democracy, the rule of law will prevail—countless patriotic Americans across the country are working tirelessly to combat this chaos and distrust and ensure that every eligible American is able to cast their ballot and that their vote is counted. Americans should have confidence that their voices will be heard in November and that these efforts by the Trump Administration to weaponize federal law enforcement to meddle in the midterm elections will ultimately fail.

Padilla has consistently advocated for protection against the Trump Administration’s election interference efforts. Padilla joined Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) in launching the first-ever Senate Election Observer Program to protect the 2026 midterms and maintain election integrity nationwide and serves as part of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force. Yesterday, Padilla announced that more than 100 Senate Democratic staff have been recruited and trained as official congressional election observers to be deployed to polling sites across nine states. Last month, Padilla introduced the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act, legislation to protect voters and election workers from intimidation and threats of violence at polling places. Padilla also led the congressional response to the bombshell whistleblower report that DHS agents violated state laws as part of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” and called for an immediate investigation into the agency’s misconduct. Last month, Padilla also led his Senate colleagues in demanding DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin immediately halt the Department’s efforts to assert federal control over, and undermine public trust in, the 2026 midterm elections. In August, Padilla and Warner led a group of colleagues in pressing the DOJ on their compliance with federal voting laws, cautioning against the misuse of any federal election monitors to target jurisdictions in a partisan manner or interfere with voting or state and local election officials’ administration of the voting process.

title: Padilla Statement on Trump’s DOJ Lawsuit Against California and Los Angeles Election Officials
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, released the following statement after the U.S. Department of Justice sued California’s Secretary of State and Los Angeles County’s Registrar Recorder to prevent them from calculating ballots sent to a list of alleged ineligible voters without any legal basis or supporting evidence:

“We’ve seen this coming: Donald Trump’s Department of Justice with no authority is now actively trying to interfere in the 2026 elections and strong-arm California into purging names from our voter rolls and blocking mail ballots based purely on vague allegations less than three weeks before Election Day. This lawsuit has no legal basis or evidence behind it and is nothing more than a blatant abuse of power designed to sow distrust in our elections and threaten Americans’ right to vote. title: As Trump Drives Up Home Heating Costs, Reed Welcomes $23.5 Million in LIHEAP Aid to Help RIers Lower Their Utility Bills
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI -- As families brace for cold weather and higher utility bills, over $3.6 billion in federal funding for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) is being released by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS) this week following a bipartisan request led by U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI), Susan Collins (R-ME) and Lisa Murkowski (R-AK).

Senator Reed, a leading member of the Senate Appropriations Committee and a Congressional champion for LIHEAP, welcomed the release of the $23,574,007 in LIHEAP assistance for Rhode islanders.

LIHEAP helps low-income households and seniors on fixed incomes pay their energy bills. The program can assist with a variety of home energy sources, including: electricity, oil, and gas. It also helps reduce energy costs through improved energy efficiency initiatives. Nationwide, an estimated 6 million households received assistance with heating and cooling costs through LIHEAP over the last year.

“LIHEAP is a real lifesaver, especially for vulnerable families facing surging utility bills. This $23.5 million for Rhode Island will hopefully ease some financial stress for families that are already stretched thin and being hit by the Trump Administration’s higher fuel prices. It’s critical that we get this assistance out into the community to help families in need,” said Senator Reed, who led efforts to include over $4 billion for LIHEAP in the latest appropriation law.

According to the National Energy Assistance Directors Association (NEADA), home heating fuel costs are expected to rise as much as 50 percent this winter, with houses that use heating oil in line for the biggest price spikes. About a third of Rhode Island households use home heating oil, which gets delivered to their homes by trucks, according to the Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources. And during cold winter months, a typical home relying on heating oil alone can use 100 gallons in just a few weeks.

The current price for a gallon of diesel fuel - which is priced similarly to home heating fuel -- is $6.34 in Rhode Island. Last year, a gallon of diesel fuel averaged around $3.80.

Last month, Reed, Collins, and Murkowski, along with 28 of their Senate colleagues urged the Trump Administration to release the LIHEAP funds as soon as possible and at the highest level possible to ensure the funding gets out into the community.

“LIHEAP helps households in need manage their home heating expenses. This new infusion of federal LIHEAP aid will provide meaningful support to thousands of families and seniors across the state. It will help them cope with surging energy costs and ease the strain on household budgets. Releasing these LIHEAP funds also helps local small businesses that supply home heating fuel to customers with fixed or limited incomes,” said Senator Reed.

LIHEAP is administered by states and accessed in Rhode Island through local Community Action Agencies. Eligibility for LIHEAP is based on income, family size, and the availability of resources.

In FY 2026, over 27,400 Rhode Island households received primary LIHEAP grants that averaged over $300 and over 3,200 Rhode Island households received additional crisis grants that averaged nearly $690 to cover home energy costs. The amount of money LIHEAP provides varies from year to year based on how many people in need apply, the cost of fuel, and the type of fuel.

Rhode Islanders wishing to learn more about LIHEAP may click here to reach the Rhode Island Department of Human Services website to get information and links to an online application.

Senator Reed noted that while the release of these federal funds to state agencies is good news, he remains deeply concerned about the Trump Administration decimating the LIHEAP staff and the impact it could have on the federal government’s ability to effectively manage the program and assist states with LIHEAP going forward. Reed says he has no doubt that President Trump will once again try to eliminate LIHEAP altogether but vowed to continue working on a bipartisan basis to include LIHEAP funding in future Appropriations laws.

title: SCHUMER DELIVERS $1.4 MILLION TO IMPROVE WASTEWATER INFRASTRUCTURE IN CHEMUNG COUNTY
text:
New Fed Investment From Appalachian Regional Commission, Which Schumer Boosted In Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, Will Improve Infrastructure At Business Park And Support New Economic Growth

Schumer Previously Delivered More Than $200M From His Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law For Water System Improvements In Chemung County

Schumer: Fed $$ Flowing For Water Infrastructure In Chemung County

U.S. Senator Charles E. Schumer today announced $1,400,000 through the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) for Chemung County’s Sewer Improvement for Economic Growth project. This federal investment will support the development of 4,500 linear feet of sewer main to expand system capacity, improve reliability, and support new industrial and commercial growth in the Village of Horseheads and Chemung County.

“I’m proud to deliver $1.4 million from my Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law to improve wastewater infrastructure in Chemung County. This new investment builds on millions I’ve previously secured by helping develop thousands of feet of sewer main to expand system capacity and support new economic growth in Horseheads and the entire county,” said Senator Schumer. “I will never stop fighting to secure infrastructure investments, support business and economic growth, and keep Upstate New Yorkers safe and healthy.”

Schumer explained these federal funds will help complete critical wastewater infrastructure improvements at the Southern Tier Logistics Business Park in the Village of Horseheads, ensuring reliable, resilient, and environmentally compliant sewer service for current and future employers. The project includes constructing and rehabilitating sewer mains, installing new manholes, building a modern pump station, and restoring abandoned lines to support the site’s redevelopment from a former military depot into a competitive manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics hub. These enhancements will expand sewer capacity, strengthen business park readiness for advanced industry investment, and support economic growth throughout the Southern Tier. Construction is expected to take three years.

Schumer has a long history of supporting water system improvements in Chemung County. In 2024, he delivered an unprecedented $200 million in federal funding for water system improvements to modernize and expand the Milton Street Wastewater Treatment Plant and support the County’s ongoing efforts to install new equipment, increase treatment capacity to stop sewer overflows, and construct cost-effective wastewater improvements to ensure the facility’s compliance with federal and state requirements. In addition, Schumer delivered $1 million to consolidate two wastewater treatment plants, Milton Street and Lake Street, into a single, regional treatment facility in the fiscal year 2023 federal budget.

In 2021, Schumer negotiated and secured $1 billion for the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Law, to be dispersed over five years, starting with $200 million in fiscal year 2022. This significant boost in funding has been used to support economic development, infrastructure, workforce, and other community development projects as well as programs intended to improve the quality of life, stimulate business growth, and create good-paying job opportunities in local communities like those in the Southern Tier and Western New York.

The Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) is an economic development partnership agency of the federal government and 13 state governments, focusing on 423 counties across the Appalachian Region. ARC’s mission is to innovate, partner, and invest to build community, capacity, and strengthen economic growth in Appalachia. New York State receives an allocation of resources from the ARC each year to fund area development in NYS’s 14-county Appalachian Region. The New York counties are represented by one of three Local Development Districts: Southern Tier West (STW) based in Salamanca, NY and comprised of Allegany, Cattaraugus, and Chautauqua counties; Southern Tier Central (STC) based in Corning, NY and comprised of Chemung, Schuyler, and Steuben counties; and Southern Tier 8 in Binghamton, NY and comprised of Broome, Chenango, Cortland, Delaware, Otsego, Schoharie, Tioga, and Tompkins counties.

title: Congressman Rick Allen's Retire through Ownership Act Signed into Law by President Trump
text:
Yesterday, President Donald J. Trump signed S. 2403, the Retire through Ownership Act, into law. Congressman Rick W. Allen (GA-12) introduced the House version of this bill last year, which would provide legal and regulatory clarity in the formation of new Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs). Congressman Allen issued the following statement upon the bill becoming public law:

"I recently visited Farmers Home Furniture headquarters in Dublin, Georgia. This innovative company transitioned to 100% employee ownership through an ESOP model in 2013. During my visit, we heard firsthand feedback that the ESOP has undeniably resulted in employee success and retention, in turn allowing the entire company to thrive. That is what the American Dream is all about and exactly why the Retire through Ownership Act is so important. ESOPs are a tried-and-true method for ensuring more Americans can enjoy a secure retirement, and by eliminating the regulatory ambiguity these plans often face, more employees will now share in the success they have helped deliver. I was proud to champion this bill during the 119th Congress and thank President Trump for signing it into law," said Congressman Allen.

"The Retire through Ownership Act is about protecting retirement security and preserving jobs in our local communities, and Rep Rick Allen’s leadership addresses a challenge that has hindered employee ownership for decades," said James Bonham, President and CEO of the ESOP Association. "His efforts will give employee owners in Georgia and everywhere greater confidence in how their shares are valued, and business owners a clearer path toward ESOP transitions. We applaud Rep. Allen for helping deliver this commonsense solution."

BACKGROUND: On September 16, 2026, the House of Representatives passed S. 2403 with overwhelming bipartisan support, sending it to President Trump's desk. Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs) let workers build retirement savings by owning stock in their company. When an ESOP buys stock in a private company, an independent appraiser helps determine what that stock is worth. The Department of Labor (DOL) has not yet finalized clear rules for how private company stock should be valued in an ESOP transaction. That leaves ESOP trustees without a clear federal standard to follow when deciding whether the price is fair—creating uncertainty and legal risk for trustees and businesses.

S. 2403, the Retire through Ownership Act, gives ESOP trustees a clearer rule to follow: If an independent appraiser follows the Internal Revenue Service’s longstanding guidelines to determine what a company is worth, the ESOP trustee can rely on that appraisal to decide if the price is fair.

title: Amo, Auchincloss, Balint Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Burlington ICE Facility

title: Amo Leads Colleagues in Calling on State Department and CDC to Investigate the Death of a Russian Plague Laboratory Worker
text:
Providence, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) led 6 colleagues in calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Centers for Disease Control (CDC) Director Erica Schwartz to take swift action in response to the death of the Russian laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East from a “pneumonia of undetermined origin.”

The lawmakers write:

“We urge you to take swift and thorough action in response to the death of the laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, including investigation and surveillance to understand the possible spread of infection. Conflicting reports regarding the cause of death, the quarantine of individuals who may have been exposed, and the institute’s work with plague and other dangerous pathogens warrant scrutiny by the United States government.”

“We are increasingly alarmed that President Donald Trump’s dangerous decision to withdraw the U.S. from the World Health Organization (WHO) has made it more difficult for the U.S. to receive information from Russia and coordinate with our international partners in responding to this incident.”

“Infectious diseases do not stop at borders, and fear and inaction from uncertainty can itself become a public-health risk. The State Department and the CDC must act now to get the facts, use every available channel to assess the threat, prepare the United States for any potential spread, and keep Congress and the American people informed.”

The full letter can be found here.

The letter was signed by Representative Gabe Amo (D-RI-01), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30), William Keating (D-MA-09), Stephen Lynch (D-MA-08), Seth Moulton (D-MA-06), Mike Quigley (D-IL-05), and Dina Titus (D-NV-01).

Background

As Vice-Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Congressman Amo has consistently fought to protect American global health programs, save lives abroad, and keep Americans healthy and safe.

In August, Congressman Amoled 137 Members of Congress in a letter demanding that the Trump administration release international affairs funding, including Global Health Programs funding, before its expiration and stop proposed changes to the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

In July, Amoled a Democratic effort on the House floor to stop Trump’s dangerous disinvestment in diplomacy and global health in the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act of 2027.

In June, Congressman Amoled 76 colleagues in a letter demanding answers about delays in detecting and responding to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda after the Trump administration reduced global health funding, staffing, and internal coordination.

title: Auchincloss, Amo, Balint Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Burlington ICE Facility
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

CONTACT: Georgina.Burros@mail.house.gov

The Burlington, Massachusetts U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility serves as the New England regional headquarters and field office.

Burlington, MA – TODAY, Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04), Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01), and Congresswoman Becca Balint (D-VT-AL) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit to the Burlington Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility. This site is a short-term facility, designed to temporarily detain individuals for no longer than 12 hours. Under the Trump administration, there have been consistent reports of ICE detainees being held there for days without proper food, beds, or showers.

Congressman Auchincloss previously conducted an oversight visit of the Burlington ICE facility in June of 2025. During this visit, the lawmakers asked detailed questions about access to legal counsel, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law.

“Today I conducted an unannounced inspection of the Burlington ICE facility. Persistent congressional oversight, in concert with public pressure, has driven modest improvements to detention operations over the past year since my previous inspection in June of 2025. I will continue oversight and accountability measures in pursuit of due process and human dignity,” said Congressman Auchincloss (D-MA).

“ICE and Border Patrol continue to negatively impact our communities and that’s why I conducted my congressional oversight with a visit to the Burlington facility unannounced,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “During my inspection of the Burlington facility with Congressman Auchincloss and Congresswoman Balint, we witnessed individuals held for processing, questioned ICE regarding our constituents’ concerns, and pressed for more humane treatment of those in custody. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”

“Vermonters deserve answers about what’s happening to people from our state who are being held in ICE custody,” said Congresswoman Becca Balint (VT-AL). “This facility was designed for stays of no more than 12 hours, but people have been held for days without basic necessities. We went in unannounced because we wanted to see the conditions for ourselves and get answers. ICE has a responsibility to treat people humanely and follow the law, and we’re going to hold them to it.”

Please find below excerpts of Rep. Auchincloss’ remarks from the media briefing, lightly edited for clarity:

“We conducted a congressionally authorized, unannounced inspection of this Burlington facility, and met with leadership, as well as reviewed and inspected the facilities in which the detainees are held. We asked detailed questions regarding medical care, access to legal services, dietary procedures and nutrition, the detainee processing protocols, procedures, and timelines, as well as the nature of operations throughout the region, to target detainees and then to pass detainees along to more permanent facilities.

What we have seen is that because of sustained congressional oversight and accountability, and because of sustained public pressure, there is a trend towards more targeted enforcement operations. Yet, there is persistent broken trust between this failed agency and the community, and there remain unacceptably long detention periods for certain of these detainees.

…Speaking for myself, I think the greatest need there is also the quality and the…infrastructure for food preparation. It is still ad hoc. There has been improvement since I was here [last year] for one of my constituents in terms of the quality [and] freshness of the food.

But this is not a facility that is designed to accommodate human beings for days at a time. It's designed to accommodate human beings for hours at a time. And as Congresswoman Balint said, because of the limited number of beds available to women at Stratford, it is the women detainees who are being kept here longer, for days at a time; and that is an unacceptable scenario.”

title: Scott Honored as “Port Champion” by Virginia Maritime Association
text:
NEWPORT NEWS, VA – Congressman Bobby Scott (VA-03) was honored Thursday with the Virginia Maritime Association’s (VMA) “Port Champion” Award in recognition of his longstanding leadership and advocacy for the Port of Virginia and the Commonwealth’s maritime industry. The award recognizes Congressman Scott’s efforts to secure critical federal investments in Virginia’s maritime infrastructure.

“I am honored to receive this recognition from the Virginia Maritime Association,” said Congressman Scott. “The Port of Virginia is a critical economic engine for Hampton Roads and the entire Commonwealth. I have been proud to work with my colleagues in the Virginia congressional delegation and our maritime partners to secure investments that strengthen our infrastructure, support good-paying jobs and ensure Virginia remains competitive in global trade. I look forward to continuing that partnership to support our maritime industry for generations to come.”

Full text of the resolution from the Virginia Maritime Association can be found below.

WHEREAS, the Virginia Maritime Association is privileged to have had the service of Congressman Robert “Bobby” Scott as the U.S. Representative for the Third District of the Commonwealth of Virginia since 1993, following service in the Virginia House of Delegates from 1978 to 1983 and the Senate of Virginia from 1983 to 1993, and as the first African American elected to Congress from Virginia in more than a century, and

WHEREAS, Congressman Scott chaired the Committee on Education and Labor in the 116th and 117th Congresses, served in the 114th, 115th, 118th Congresses and currently serves as the Ranking Member and serves as a member of the Committee on the Budget, and has strengthened the skilled trades our terminals and shipyards depend upon, and

WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has been a steadfast champion of ‘Wider, Deeper, Safer®’, working with the Virginia delegation to complete the Norfolk Harbor Widening and Deepening Project and give the Commonwealth the deepest commercial channels on the East Coast at fifty-five feet, and

WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has likewise championed the deepening of the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River, on behalf of the marine terminals, shipyards, and waterfront industries whose berths depend on it, and

WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has consistently and generously supported this Association, joining our members year after year at the Annual Maritime Banquet and the Navigation Summit in a spirit of cooperation and partnership, and

WHEREAS, through these efforts, Congressman Scott has strengthened Virginia’s maritime transportation system and positioned the greater Port of Virginia and the Commonwealth as leaders in global trade,

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Virginia Maritime Association that sincere appreciation is expressed for the splendid service extended and readiness to assist the Maritime Industry as a “Port Champion” promoting, protecting, and encouraging Virginia’s ports.

IN TESTIMONY WHEREOF, witness by these signatures this fifteenth day of October 2026 and the seal of the Association.

title: Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley Demand Answers from USPS About Mail Delivery Problems on Oregon Coast
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [10/16/26] – Representative Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley demanded answers from the United States Postal Service (USPS) about significant ongoing mail delivery issues in Astoria and surrounding areas.

The lawmakers noted that the city government, county government, and several downtown businesses are within a few blocks of the Astoria Post Office, but they have not been receiving mail regularly, and some are not receiving mail at all.

“The Astoria Post Office will not hold mail for city officials to pick up, which has caused major disruptions in local commerce and governance,” the Members of Congress wrote. “Payments sent through the mail to the city are being delivered late or not being delivered at all and downtown businesses are experiencing sporadic delivery. We are hearing concerning anecdotes indicating that Amazon packages, which are delivered via USPS in Astoria, are still regularly arriving on time. It’s unacceptable that mail from a billion-dollar retailer is successfully delivered to its destination on time, but mail to and from local small businesses is unreliable.”

The Members of Congress demanded answers to a series of oversight questions and requested that USPS set a time to meet with local elected officials in Clatsop and Columbia counties. They also requested USPS hold an informational session within the next 60 days for residents to discuss the agency's plans to address these issues.

“Timely, reliable mail delivery is essential infrastructure. Businesses, residents, and local governments rely on USPS for commerce, communication, medications, and more,” the Members of Congress wrote. “This is not an exhaustive list of issues with USPS brought to our attention.”

On October 15, 2026, Representative Bonamici visited the Astoria Post Office in person and asked to speak with the Postmaster to try to find a solution to the late and missing mail. The Postmaster denied the request.

The full letter can be read here and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

We write with significant concerns about the state of operations of the United States Postal Service (USPS) in northwest Oregon. Many community members from across the region are alarmed about inconsistent and unacceptable USPS delivery.

In Astoria, the city government, county government, and several downtown businesses have not been receiving mail regularly, and some are not receiving mail at all. This is happening despite the Astoria Post Office’s central location, just minutes away from Astoria City Hall and the county government building. Additionally, the Astoria Post Office will not hold mail for city officials to pick up which has caused major disruptions in local commerce and governance. Payments sent through the mail to the city are being delivered late or not being delivered at all and downtown businesses are experiencing sporadic delivery. We are hearing concerning anecdotes indicating that Amazon packages, which are delivered via USPS in Astoria, are still regularly arriving on time. It’s unacceptable that mail from a billion-dollar retailer is successfully delivered to its destination on time, but mail to and from local small businesses is unreliable.

The city had scheduled a meeting with the Astoria Postmaster to work to resolve the issue, but the Postmaster did not attend, and the meeting has not been rescheduled.

In Warrenton, USPS has been looking for a new post office location for several years. When the city of Warrenton has asked USPS about location options, USPS directs inquiries to a third-party contractor. This contractor directs all inquiries back to the USPS, resulting in a frustrating cycle where constituents are no closer to getting answers to their questions.

In Gearhart, roughly half the residents in town must travel to the Seaside post office to get their mail which is an unacceptable inconvenience for Gearhart residents. We have been advised that one possible solution involves the placement of a 950-unit cluster box which is exceedingly difficult for a town this size. It is unacceptable that residents of Gearhart cannot receive home delivery or at least have cluster boxes installed at several points throughout the community. The USPS must find a reasonable solution. Furthermore, there are concerning reports that mail pickup is inaccessible on Saturdays to Gearhart residents.

Recently, residents in Gearhart have heard rumors that the Seaside Post office will be remodeled to accommodate permanent mail pick up for Gearhart residents. Though Gearhart residents want a permanent solution to the problems they experience receiving mail, travelling to Seaside is not a practical or acceptable long-term or permanent solution.

Similar issues of concern also exist in Columbia County. In Rainier, roughly a third of the town is not included in the mail route and must use a PO Box. If mail is addressed to a home that is ineligible for home delivery instead of to their PO Box, the mail is not held – it is returned to sender. In a world where people often shop online, many online retailers don’t offer a format for a PO Box address, resulting in orders never reaching their intended addresses. Finally, it is concerning that not every residence is eligible for home delivery in Rainier, considering the small size of the town and well-maintained streets.

Timely, reliable mail delivery is essential infrastructure. Businesses, residents, and local governments rely on USPS for commerce, communication, medications, and more. This is not an exhaustive list of issues with USPS brought to our attention.

We ask that you respond to us in writing within 14 days of receipt of this letter outlining how the USPS will address the issues described and answer the following questions:

When will Astoria downtown businesses, city government, and county government receive regular mail services?

When will USPS announce a new location for the Warrenton post office? What is the current status of the search? Please provide the name and contact information for a specific person who can provide updates to the city.

Why are so many Gearhart residents unable to receive mail at their doors?

What is the plan to deliver mail to residents in Gearhart and/or provide additional PO boxes in Gearhart?

Why are some residents of Rainier, who live within city limits, unable to receive mail at home?

If these issues are caused by post offices being understaffed, what is USPS doing to remedy this?

In light of the volume and gravity of these concerns, we respectfully request that USPS set a time to meet with local elected officials in Clatsop and Columbia counties. We also ask that USPS hold an informational session within the next 60 days for residents to discuss the agency's plans to address these issues.

Our offices will gladly work with USPS and community leaders to find mutually agreeable times and locations for these meetings.

Sincerely,

###

title: Case Receives National Award For Championing Local Franchise Businesses Across The Country
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Representative Ed Case (Hawai‘i – District 1) was among several members of Congress recently honored as “Franchise Champions” by the International Franchise Association (IFA).

According to the IFA, there are more than 2,800 franchise locations in Hawai‘i, with close to 30,000 employees. These largely local small businesses franchise under well-known brands like L&L Drive-Inn, McDonald’s, Subway, 7-Eleven, Ace Hardware and SERVPRO, and now generate more than $3 billion in annual revenues.

"These lawmakers have shown they will stand up for Main Street, and we are proud to honor them with the Franchise Champion Award," said Michael Layman, IFA chief advocacy officer.

"Franchise small businesses across America power jobs and serve their communities, and they depend on lawmakers for a regulatory climate that will allow the franchise business model to grow now and into the future."

Case said: “As someone who worked over three decades in Hawai‘i businesses, I fully understand what it takes to create, own, grow and work in a business, especially small businesses which are the backbone of our local economy. Extra effort and different business models are required to address various challenges including taxes, regulations and high costs. Franchising offers a great and proven model avenue for many of our own to succeed in business, generating local jobs and contributing to our economy.”

The IFA is the world’s oldest and largest organization representing franchising worldwide. IFA works through its government relations and public policy, media relations, and educational programs to protect, enhance and promote franchising and the more than 832,000 franchise establishments that support nearly 8.8 million direct jobs, $907.3 billion of economic output for the U.S. economy, and almost 3 percent of the Gross Domestic Product.

Case has also championed the broader interests of our country’s small businesses throughout his almost-twelve years in Congress. In 2023 he was honored with a Special Congressional Award by the Small Business Council of America (SBCA), a national, non-profit organization representing some 100,000 privately held and family-owned small businesses.

The SBCA award recognized Case’s support of the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), of funding for services managed by the SBA, and of various federal loan programs to help small businesses. The SBCA had previously given him the same award in 2006 during his earlier Congressional service when he served on the House Committee on Small Business.

Case has also worked to advance national and Hawai‘i small businesses through his House Appropriations Committee, on which he is now serving his eighth year.

As a current example, for current Fiscal Year 2027 his Committee included his requests for key programs that directly benefit Hawaii’s small businesses including:

· $828 million for the SBA;

· $140 million for Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) which supports six SBDCs in Hawai‘i;

· $32 million for the Microloan Technical Assistance Program; and

· $27 million for the Women’s Business Centers Program, which supports the Patsy T. Mink Center for Business and Leadership.

Attachment: picture of award

title: Rep. Costa Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Defense Innovation Through Partnership with Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee's Subcommittee on Europe and the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Don Bacon (NE-02), Wesley Bell (MO-01), and Mike Quigley (IL-05) introduced the bipartisan H.R. 10772 Frontline Innovation Act. This legislation will authorize the Department of Defense’s Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, allowing the United States to benefit directly from innovations developed and refined on the battlefield in Ukraine.

Ukraine has emerged as a leader in developing modern defense technologies as it continues to defend itself against Russia’s invasion. Ukrainian companies are developing advanced drones unmanned systems, and electronic warfare tools that are being tested and improved under real combat conditions against a determined adversary. These innovations offer valuable opportunities to strengthen U.S. defense capabilities while supporting Ukraine’s ongoing efforts to defend its sovereignty.

However, existing U.S. defense cooperation agreements have not kept pace with these technological advancements. The last U.S.-Ukraine agreement on exchanging military research and development information dates back to 2001. Although the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) has worked with the Ukrainian government and firms since 2023, legal barriers currently limit its ability to expand these partnerships and invest directly in Ukrainian defense technologies.

“Ukraine has demonstrated extraordinary resilience in the face of Russia’s aggression, and Ukrainians are innovating and developing new defense technologies under some of the most challenging conditions imaginable,” said Congressman Costa. “This bipartisan bill will help strengthen our national security by investing in technologies that have been tested on the battlefield, while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight to defend its sovereignty.”

“Ukraine is fighting for its survival against Putin’s illegal invasion, and its forces have been forced to innovate at an extraordinary pace,” said Rep. Bacon. “They are proving new drones, unmanned systems and electronic warfare capabilities against Russia in real combat, and our military should be learning from that experience. I’m joining Rep. Costa in introducing the bipartisan Frontline Innovation Act to help bring battlefield-proven technologies into our own defense innovation system and strengthen our military while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight for freedom.”

"Standing with Ukraine is in America’s own interest, and the Frontline Innovation Act is a smart, practical way to do it. Every day, Ukrainian forces are developing and testing new technologies on the battlefield, providing valuable lessons that can help make our own servicemembers safer and prepared for the challenges of tomorrow,” said Rep. Bell. "As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know our military must have the best tools and technology, and after my recent trip to Ukraine, I can see how much Ukrainian battlefield innovation has to offer. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan legislation to learn from our partners’ battlefield experience and help them continue defending their freedom.”

"When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the entire world expected Kyiv to fall within days. Instead, the strength, resilience, and innovation of Ukrainians and the Ukrainian military have kept the capitol free for over four years. The United States should learn from Ukraine's battlefield innovation to strengthen and modernize our own military to ensure our forces are prepared for a new generation of threats," said Representative Mike Quigley, a Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus. "The Frontline Innovation Act would enable the U.S. military to accelerate defense innovation while continuing to support Ukraine as a critical ally."

The Frontline Innovation Act would:

Expand defense cooperation by authorizing the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, notwithstanding any other provision of law.

Strengthen U.S. defense capabilities by directing DIU to ensure the United States benefits from technologies developed and refined through Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s invasion.

Allow technology proven in combat to reach the U.S. military faster while creating new opportunities for the American defense industrial base to gain new partners and a larger market.

Support Ukraine through increased investment and cooperation, allowing both countries to collaborate on developing the next generation of defense capabilities.
