title: SBA Offers Relief to Small Businesses and Nonprofits Impacted by Grand Canyon Flooding
text:
This week, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced the availability of low-interest federal disaster loans for small businesses and private nonprofit organizations experiencing economic losses from the recent flash flooding at Grand Canyon National Park.

The disaster declaration, issued on October 13, covers Coconino, Gila, Mohave, Navajo, and Yavapai Counties in Arizona, as well as Kane and San Juan Counties in Utah.

As a result, SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program is now open to eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations with financial losses directly tied to the flooding.

These loans help cover working capital needs and operating expenses that could have been met had the disaster not occurred. Importantly, applicants may qualify even if their business or nonprofit did not sustain physical damage.

For additional information or to begin an application, please click here, call SBA’s Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. Individuals who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability may dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

The deadline to submit economic injury applications is July 13, 2027.

title: MS Now: Democrats demand Trump explain Ukraine satellite cutoffs
text:
Congressional Democrats on the House Armed Services and Intelligence committees are demanding President Donald Trump explain why Ukrainian forces’ access to SpaceX Starshield services was restricted earlier this week.

In a letter first reported by MS NOW, Rep. Jason Crow, D-Co., ranking member of the Armed Services Committee; Adam Smith, D-Wash., ranking member of the Select Committee on Intelligence; Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn.; and Rep. George Whitesides, D-Calif., lambasted the Trump administration for refusing to respond to congressional inquiries on who directed changes to Ukraine’s access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink services.

The lawmakers were not satisfied with either the possibility that Elon Musk’s company SpaceX independently made the decision — which Musk has denied — or the U.S. government made the call.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government,” Musk wrote Oct. 14 on X. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”

The Democratic lawmakers want the Trump administration to explain exactly who controls the crucial satellite connections Ukraine uses to defend itself.

“If a private company can unilaterally restrict a critical operational service governed by a signed contract with the Department of Defense during an active conflict, it raises serious concerns about public accountability and the outsized influence of private actors over U.S. national security matters,” the lawmakers wrote.

“If, on the other hand, the direction was given by your Administration, it raises serious questions about U.S. defense policy regarding Russia and Ukraine,” they added. “Either way, the American people, our allies, and Ukraine deserve to know why this decision with life-threatening consequences was made.”

A U.S. official, granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive situation, told MS NOW that “no such request was ever made by the President.” The White House ignored repeated questions on whether another administration official or agency directed the change.

“As his popularity plummets at home, he’s shamefully abandoning our allies and once again cozying up to dictators,” Crow said in a statement, referring to Trump. “We need to stand with the people of Ukraine as Russia continues its war of aggression, not fund Putin’s war machine that is killing civilians.”

The Democrats noted the disruption to Ukraine’s military operations and defense capabilities put civilians at risk. The satellite signal disruptions also came amid Trump’s diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin and pressure on Ukraine to stop attacking Russian energy sites, despite its adversary failing to abide by the so-called energy ceasefire announced by Trump.

They asked for a response by Oct. 30.

Their letter, which did not include any Republican signatories, follows a bipartisan Senate effort calling for the Department of Defense Inspector General to investigate the Starlink disruptions in Ukraine.

On Thursday, Senate Foreign Relations Committee Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., led a bipartisan letter seeking an investigation into whether the restricted Starshield service put U.S. diplomatic, military, and security personnel inside Ukraine in danger and who approved the disruptions.

Starshield speeds began to improve on Thursday, according to Ukrainian chargé d’affaires in Washington Denys Sienik.

“We hope all will be resumed to the previous level,” Sienik said in a statement. “Speed ​​is critical for logistics, and for intercepting the jet-powered Shahed drones especially when Russia constantly uses them to attack our cities and commit war crimes and when Foreign Minister Lavrov openly states that Russia opposes a ceasefire.”

A source familiar with the matter told MS NOW the Ukrainian government has yet to receive any response from SpaceX or the Pentagon.

Wednesday “saw one of the most massive Shahed attacks, occurring precisely when our defense system’s speed was being throttled, and the circumstances behind this are deeply concerning,” said the source, who was granted anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations.

title: Crow Demands Trump Administration Explain Disruptions to Starshield
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is demanding President Donald Trump explain why Ukrainian forces’ access to SpaceX’s Starshield was reportedly restricted earlier this week. This decision disrupted their military operations, crippling their air defense and putting Ukrainians at further risk to deadly Russian aerial bombardments.

According to SpaceX, any limits on speed or usage of Starshield is decided by the U.S. military and the President. The Trump administration has not publicly stated who authorized these changes, when authorization was given, and what the intended purpose was.

Joining Crow on this letter are Ranking Member of the Armed Services Committee Adam Smith (D-WA), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Jim Himes (D-CT), and member of the House Armed Services Committee Congressman George Whitesides (D-CA).

“The President’s failed policies and reckless war with Iran has raised prices. As his popularity plummets at home, he’s shamefully abandoning our allies and once again cozying up to dictators,” said Congressman Crow. “We need to stand with the people of Ukraine as Russia continues its war of aggression, not fund Putin’s war machine that is killing civilians.”

Crow and his colleagues wrote: “According to SpaceX, any limits on speed or usage of Starshield are decided by the U.S. military and the President. To date, your Administration has refused to respond to Congressional inquiries on who directed these changes to Ukraine’s Starshield services.”

They continued: “In this context there are two possibilities – either SpaceX independently made the decision to restrict Ukrainian Starshield service, or the U.S. Government directed them to do so. If a private company can unilaterally restrict a critical operational service governed by a signed contract with the Department of Defense during an active conflict, it raises serious concerns about public accountability and the outsized influence of private actors over U.S. national security matters. If, on the other hand, the direction was given by your Administration, it raises serious questions about U.S. defense policy regarding Russia and Ukraine. Either way, the American people, our allies, and Ukraine deserve to know why this decision with life-threatening consequences was made.”

Congressman Crow has been a strong supporter of the Ukrainian people. He recently introduced a bill to protect Ukrainian nationals already in the U.S. against the threat of deportation by extending their Temporary Protected Status (TPS). When Putin’s invasion began, Crow immediately called for the U.S. to send military and humanitarian support to Ukraine, for international sanctions against Russia, and for a stronger NATO alliance to meet these new security threats. Weeks later, as Ukrainians fled their homes, Congressman Crow and other members advocated for an expedited immigration status for Ukrainians to the U.S. Crow has visited Ukraine several times since Russia’s invasion.

The Congressman has been one of the earliest and strongest supporters of military, development, and humanitarian assistance for Ukraine. He voted for, and strongly advocated for, every supplemental package provided to Ukraine.

A PDF of the letter can be found here, with full text appearing below:

President Trump,

On October 14, 2026, Ukrainian forces reported that unexpected restrictions on their SpaceX Starshield satellite communications services severely disrupted their military operations, crippling their air defense and putting Ukrainians at further risk to deadly Russian aerial bombardments. These restrictions came as officials in your Administration were actively pressuring Ukraine to limit strikes on Russia, particularly on oil refineries. The reported goal of your Administration’s pressure campaign was to pump more Russian diesel into global markets, amidst high fuel prices caused by your war with Iran.

According to SpaceX, any limits on speed or usage of Starshield are decided by the U.S. military and the President. To date, your Administration has refused to respond to Congressional inquiries on who directed these changes to Ukraine’s Starshield services.

In this context there are two possibilities – either SpaceX independently made the decision to restrict Ukrainian Starshield service, or the U.S. Government directed them to do so. If a private company can unilaterally restrict a critical operational service governed by a signed contract with the Department of Defense during an active conflict, it raises serious concerns about public accountability and the outsized influence of private actors over U.S. national security matters. If, on the other hand, the direction was given by your Administration, it raises serious questions about U.S. defense policy regarding Russia and Ukraine. Either way, the American people, our allies, and Ukraine deserve to know why this decision with life-threatening consequences was made.

Please provide responses to the following questions by October 30, 2026:

Who authorized the speed restrictions on Starshield services provided to Ukraine?

a. Was this an independent SpaceX decision, a U.S. Government directive, or a coordinated effort between SpaceX and the U.S. Government?

b. What was the intent of the speed restrictions when authorized?

Was there any communication between the White House, the Pentagon, or other parts of the U.S. Government and SpaceX on the decision to implement speed restrictions?

Was there any communication between the White House, the Pentagon, or other parts of the U.S. Government and Russia on a decision to restrict Starshield services for Ukraine prior to any directive to SpaceX to implement such speed limitations?

Were the operational consequences of restricting Starshield services for Ukraine assessed before the decision took effect, including potential impacts on Ukrainian forces and/or their air defense capabilities?

Why were Ukrainian forces not given advanced notice of this restriction?

We will not allow your Administration to abandon our commitment to Ukraine by siding with Putin over the Ukrainian people and undermining their fundamental right to defend their sovereignty and freedom.

title: Davids Urges Federal Action as Kansas Small Businesses Squeezed Out of Tariff Refunds While Large Corporations Cash In
text:
Today, Representative Sharice Davids demanded immediate action to ensure Kansas small businesses receive the tariff refunds they are owed. Following this year’s Supreme Court ruling overturning the president’s reckless tariffs, the federal government began processing billions of dollars in refunds. However, while major corporations get massive paydays, local Kansas mom-and-pop shops are facing bureaucratic hurdles that leave them behind.

"Small businesses should not need a team of lawyers or customs specialists to recover money they are owed," wrote Davids in a letter to the Small Business Administration (SBA) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). "The businesses with the fewest resources should not face the greatest barriers to recovering their money while large corporations are better positioned to navigate the system... I urge the administration to ensure that the refund process works for the small businesses that need this relief most."

Data from the Center for American Progress highlights the stark disparity facing Kansas main streets: the average Kansas small business importer has recovered just $49,000 in refunds compared to the $140,000 they paid out in tariffs. Meanwhile, some of the nation’s largest corporations — which possess internal legal teams and outside specialists to navigate the complex application process — have secured refunds worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

In her letter, Davids outlined how many small businesses were forced to absorb higher costs passed down by suppliers, yet remain ineligible or unable to navigate the current non-automatic refund process. She is calling on the SBA and CBP to create a realistic, streamlined, and accessible path for small businesses, including direct guidance and a simplified application process for small firms that have not yet applied.

This action builds directly on Davids’ ongoing efforts to protect Kansas workers and small businesses from unfair trade practices. Davids previously supported the RELIEF Act, legislation designed to provide automatic, hassle-free tariff refunds to small businesses and hardworking families who bore the financial burden of reckless tariff policies.

The administration’s reckless tariff policies have hit Kansas hard, driving up costs for families and threatening small businesses and farmers. Average American households will pay $2,500 more this year because of these policies. Local industries, including agriculture, manufacturing, and retail, have faced higher costs for imported goods, forcing some businesses to raise consumer prices, cut jobs, or close entirely.

Read Davids’ full letter here or below

Dear Administrator Loeffler and Commissioner Scott,

I write to share my concerns about the impact of the Trump Administration’s trade war and tariff refund process on Kansas small businesses. Local small businesses have already paid the price of higher tariffs. Now, as the federal government works to return billions of dollars in tariffs that were collected, small businesses are at risk of being left behind.

The Center for American Progress estimates the average Kansas small business importer has only received $49,000 in refunds, compared with the $140,000 paid in tariffs (as of August 2026). At the same time, some of the nation’s largest corporations have received refunds worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Following the Supreme Court’s decision earlier this year overturning President Trump’s broad International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs, Customs and Border Protection (CBP) began processing refunds for eligible businesses. These refunds are not automatic. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta found that larger firms are somewhat more likely to receive or seek refunds, relying on internal staff or outside firms to navigate the process.

Kansas small businesses often lack the staff to navigate a complicated federal refund process. Some may also be ineligible to apply, even though they ultimately paid higher prices because of tariffs. For example, a tariff may be passed from an importer to a small business through a supplier, but the refund may go to the original importer — not the small business that absorbed the higher cost.

Small businesses should not need a team of lawyers or customs specialists to recover money they are owed.

I urge the Small Business Administration to work with CBP and other federal agencies to create a realistic, efficient, and accessible path for small businesses to receive the tariff refunds they are owed. This should include a straightforward process for businesses that have not yet applied, as well as clear guidance and assistance for small businesses navigating the process.

The businesses with the fewest resources should not face the greatest barriers to recovering their money while large corporations are better positioned to navigate the system. I urge the administration to ensure that the refund process works for the small businesses that need this relief most.

Sincerely,

title: Dingell, Colleagues Introduce Legislation Honoring Doris Miller and Prohibiting Renaming of Naval Vessels After Sitting Presidents
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), and Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) introduced the U.S.S. Doris Miller Act and the Department of Defense Renaming Integrity and Ethics (DORIE) Act. These two pieces of legislation would honor the legacy of Mess Attendant Third Class Doris “Dorie” Miller and ensure that the Navy aircraft carrier currently under construction retains his name.

The U.S.S. Doris Miller Act would express the sense of Congress regarding the naming of a naval aircraft carrier in Miller’s honor. Miller famously manned an anti-aircraft gun during the attack on Pearl Harbor in World War II, despite having never been trained to operate the weapon, and helped carry wounded soldiers to safety even after being ordered to abandon ship. He was the first Black service member to receive the Navy Cross, the Navy’s second-highest award for valor.

The Department of Defense Renaming Integrity and Ethics (DORIE) Act would prohibit the naming of Department of Defense assets, including military bases, ships, and other military installations, after sitting presidents. The DORIE Act would amend Title 10 of the United States Code, which is the section of federal law that outlines the legal framework, roles, missions, and organization of the U.S. Armed Forces and the Department of Defense. This comes after an unprecedented proposal by Navy leadership to rename the aircraft carrier U.S.S. Doris Miller in honor of President Donald Trump.

“Doris Miller represented courage, sacrifice, and the essential role African Americans have played in defending this country,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “Naming this carrier after him is more than honoring one extraordinary sailor—it recognizes that African Americans are an essential part of American history. No sitting president has ever been able to, nor should they be able to, name a vessel after themselves. I am proud to support the U.S.S. Doris Miller Act to ensure American heroes are honored for their sacrifice.”

“Black history is American history, and you cannot tell the story of the Second World War without the story of Doris (Dorie) Miller,” said Congressman Kweisi Mfume. “Doris Miller’s life was one of extraordinary bravery and patriotism, and I will continue to fight against any and all efforts to minimize or denigrate that history. The aircraft carrier that was scheduled to be named in his honor represents a fitting tribute to the estimable legacy of Dorie Miller. It is the very least that we owe to this great American hero who like so many before him, laid down his life for his country. Taking his name off that ship to instead name it for President Trump while he is still in office would be a disgrace. That has never been the practice of our government, nor should it be now. No sitting President, of any party, should have a ship, a base, or any other military asset named after them while in office. That is just one of the many reasons why I am proud and honored to support the DORIE Act. It's the right thing to do.”

“Doris Miller put himself in harm’s way to save his fellow sailors, and he did it at a time when segregation limited what Black servicemembers were allowed to do. His courage deserves to be celebrated, not forgotten,” said Congressman Bell. “As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I will continue working to ensure our sailors are honored for their service, and that their legacy is never erased. Our warships should carry the names of those who gave something to this country, and few gave more than Dorie Miller. That’s why I’m proud to champion these bills.”

title: Congressman Don Davis Calls on FCC to Preserve the E-Rate Program
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) sent a letter to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr calling on the FCC to protect the E-Rate Program for schools and libraries. The E-Rate Program helps schools in rural communities afford the reliable broadband connectivity their students need.

“For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped give students in rural communities, including across eastern North Carolina, the tools they need to learn and succeed. Since 1998, North Carolina’s public schools and libraries have received more than $1 billion in E-Rate discounts, helping our state to become the first to connect all K-12 classrooms to high-speed broadband,” said Congressman Don Davis.

North Carolina’s Department of Public Instruction reports that for every dollar of state funding spent on E-Rate-eligible goods and services, schools received over three dollars in value in Fiscal Year 2025, and that in 2024 the state recouped 99 percent of the fees the Commission collected from North Carolina residents and businesses.

E-Rate provided about $30 million to public school districts in North Carolina's First Congressional District from 2021 through 2025.

"If the FCC pulls back on E-Rate, we will be at risk of losing vital services many of our families and rural communities depend on," added Davis.

Congressman Davis also called on the FCC to restore E-Rate program support for school bus Wi-Fi and internet hotspot services.

The full letter is available HERE.

title: CONGRESSMAN DOWNING'S BILL CROW TRIBE WATER RIGHTS SETTLEMENT AMENDMENTS ACT SIGNED INTO LAW
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last night, President Trump signed the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025 into law. Senator Steve Daines spearheaded the bill in the Senate, while Congressman Troy Downing championed it in the House of Representatives. The legislation updates the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 to provide the Crow Tribe with greater flexibility to develop water infrastructure and keep long-overdue projects on the reservation moving forward.

The original settlement ratified the water rights compact between the Crow Tribe and the State of Montana. It authorized the Bureau of Reclamation to rehabilitate the Crow Irrigation Project (CIP) and construct a Municipal, Rural, and Industrial (MR&I) water system.

S. 240 modernizes that framework by converting the MR&I component from a single centralized project into a more flexible, localized approach. Instead of one large system, the legislation allows the Tribe to develop smaller water and wastewater projects tailored to the needs of individual communities across the reservation.

In addition, the legislation extends the Crow Tribe's exclusive right to develop a hydropower project at the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam for five years, through 2030, helping support future energy development on the reservation.

“This bill delivers on a long-standing commitment to the Crow Tribe by giving the Tribe more flexibility to move critical water projects forward. It supports needed water infrastructure and preserves the Tribe’s right to pursue hydropower development at Yellowtail Afterbay Dam. I’m proud to see it signed into law by President Trump,” said Downing.

“This bill is a necessity for the Crow Tribe and surrounding communities and will ensure the tribe has the resources they need to deliver safe, reliable access to clean water to the reservation and complete a hydropower project to bring new baseload generation to the region. I’m grateful for everyone who pushed this legislation through, and I look forward to seeing the impacts this will have on water safety and the Crow Tribe community,” said Daines.

“The federal government must ensure tribal water settlements work as intended. S. 240 gives the Crow Tribe greater flexibility to complete critical drinking water and irrigation projects while extending its exclusive right to pursue hydropower development at Yellowtail Afterbay Dam. I commend Senator Daines and Rep. Downing for championing a practical solution that strengthens tribal self-determination and supports long-term economic growth on the Crow Reservation,” said House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman.

“Today’s legislation unties the Tribe’s hands and allows us to use previously appropriated funds to construct a more efficient system of regional water treatment and improved wells," said Chairman Frank Whiteclay, Crow Tribe of Indians

title: Joint Economic Committee: Families in El Paso Have Had to Spend Thousands More Under Trump Administration
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) reacted to the latest report from the Joint Economic Committee (JEC) detailing how the average household in El Paso has had to spend thousands of dollars more for goods and services under the Trump administration and Republican rule. Instead of working to curb inflation, policies like the president's tarriffs and his war in Iran have pushed prices even higher.

“The Trump economy has had a crushing impact on our community. Families in El Paso have had to pay thousands of dollars more for goods and services as a result of devastating decisions that Donal Trump and Republicans have made over these last two years," said Congresswoman Escobar. "Despite repeated promises from Donald Trump to end inflation on day 1, his policies have increased the cost of living and created an economic crisis. This report is further proof that El Pasoans should take him and his party at his word when he says that he doesn't think about Americans' financial situations at all."

According to the JEC, the price increases have affected:

Housing Costs

Families have had to spend an additional $281 on housing costs such as rent and mortgage payments since President Trump took office.

Grocery Costs

Americans paid an additional $310 for groceries in President Trump’s first year than in 2024, and grocery prices are now more than 4% higher than when Trump took office. Beef and coffee prices are hitting Americans especially hard. Since the President took office, the average price of ground beef has risen almost every month to a record high of more than $7 per pound. Coffee prices also spiked and are now more than $9 per pound.

Energy Costs

Gas prices have soared since the start of Trump’s Iran War. In total, people across El Paso have spent an additional $218 million on gas since the beginning of the war. That has cost the average family in El Paso an additional $853 in gas costs.

Healthcare Costs

Because of Trump and Republicans’ refusal to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax cuts that help people afford their health insurance, monthly premiums for ACA plans rose over 50% on average in 2026 compared to last year. Meanwhile deductibles surged to record highs, increasing by more than $1,000 on average.

title: Fitzpatrick Statement on Federal Indictment of Bucks County Man Charged with Making Threats Against Him
text:

title: ‘Trump’s EPA Broke the Law’: Garamendi, DeSaulnier React to Watchdog Report, Demand Trump Return $19 Million to Contra Costa
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative John Garamendi (D-CA-08) and Representative Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) issued the following statement after the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the government watchdog, published Garamendi’s requested report finding that the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) decision to block a $19 million Community Change Grant to Contra Costa County violated the law.

This news comes more than one year after Reps. Garamendi and DeSaulnier confronted the EPA for violating federal appropriations law and federal court injunctions by canceling a $19.1 million Community Change Grant awarded to Contra Costa County for its North Richmond Community Resilience Initiative.

“The GAO confirmed what we knew all along: President Trump’s EPA broke the law, and now I’m demanding they pay us back,” said Congressman Garamendi. “This funding was, and still is, not a suggestion. Congress mandated years ago that these funds be delivered to frontline communities like North Richmond, which, because of President Trump’s blatant abuse of the law, has continued to suffer the health impacts of extreme pollution. Not only has Trump’s EPA acted in ways that break the law, but because of its callousness and disregard for the American people, it is endangering the health and wellbeing of some of our nation’s most vulnerable residents. The people of North Richmond deserve better. Trump took away their money, and now they need to give it back.”

“Over a year ago, I was proud to stand with Congressman Garamendi in calling on the Trump Administration to reverse course as they illegally clawed back over $19 million in federal funding for environmental protection efforts from Contra Costa County,” said Congressman DeSaulnier. “Now the GAO, an independent government watchdog agency, has confirmed the Administration violated the law in stealing this money and we demand it be reinstated immediately.”

Background

In spring 2025, the EPA terminated a $19.1 million Community Change Grant awarded to Contra Costa County for its North Richmond Community Resilience Initiative. The initiative is one of 105 applications selected for the Inflation Reduction Act’s Community Change Grants Program, the largest national investment in environmental and climate justice.

The $19.1 million in funding was allocated directly to the community for the initiative, which aimed to build a resilience center for emergencies and natural disasters and to plant 65 trees along the Verde Elementary schoolyard to shield students from pollution caused by a new distribution center.

In response to the news of the cancellation, Congressman Garamendi and Congressman DeSaulnier sent a letter to Trump-appointed EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin stating that the agency flagrantly violated the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act without any explanation or due process.

In response to Garamendi and DeSaulnier’s letter, the EPA provided little to no justification for the cancellation, saying only that the agency does not support programs or organizations that promote or take part in DEI or “environmental justice” initiatives.

Congressman Garamendi then requested a report on the Trump Administration’s actions from the GAO, which published its decision on the termination of the Community Change Grants on October 7. The GAO found that the EPA violated the law and noted that Garamendi and DeSaulnier’s letter to the EPA and the agency’s response also helped inform its determination.

title: Rep. Garbarino Introduces Legislation to Rename Medford Post Office in Honor of Decorated Vietnam War Veteran Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-02) introduced legislation to designate the United States Postal Service facility in Medford, New York, in honor of Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos, a decorated United States Marine Corps veteran and longtime postal employee who dedicated his life to serving his country and community.

Gunnery Sergeant Santos served with distinction during the Vietnam War, earning the Silver Star, one of the nation's highest military decorations for valor in combat, among numerous other honors. Following his military service, Santos continued his commitment to public service through a career with the United States Postal Service, working for many years at the Medford Post Office that the legislation seeks to rename in his honor.

"Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos was an American hero who dedicated his life to serving our country and his fellow Long Islanders," said Rep. Garbarino. "His bravery and sacrifice during the Vietnam War earned him some of our nation's highest military honors, but his commitment to service did not end when he returned home. He went on to serve the Medford community for years through his work at the local post office. Renaming this facility in his honor is a fitting tribute to a man who gave so much to our nation and our community. I'm proud to introduce this legislation to ensure his legacy is remembered for generations to come."

Born on February 9, 1940, in Ponce, Puerto Rico, Santos passed away on March 30, 2026, at the age of 86 on Long Island. His legacy of military service and dedication to his community continues to be honored by fellow veterans and Long Islanders.

title: Rep. Gillen and House Minority Whip Clark Hold Fireside Chat on Impacts of Rising Healthcare Costs on Long Island
text:

GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) and Whip Katherine Clark (MA-05) hosted a fireside chat with Nassau County residents and leaders at Harmony Health in Garden City to discuss how rising healthcare costs are affecting Long Island and the country. Both lawmakers discussed a path in Congress to lower healthcare costs, extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) premium tax credits and reverse the $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

"Long Island’s hardworking families, care workers and providers are being crushed by rising healthcare costs and the GOP majority’s $1 trillion cut to Americans’ coverage,” said Rep. Gillen. “Alongside Whip Clark, we’re fighting to pass bipartisan solutions to reverse these cuts, restore the ACA tax credits, lower costs and protect the people who care for us. Together in Congress, we will continue working to ensure that quality healthcare is more affordable for all Americans.”

“Congresswoman Laura Gillen is fighting every day for the quality, affordable healthcare that Long Island families deserve," said Democratic Whip Katherine Clark. “It was a privilege to join her in the 4th District of New York and discuss House Democrats’ agenda to deliver for working families. In the 120th Congress, we will reverse this administration’s harmful cuts and pass legislation to ensure everyone can get the medical care they need, when they need it.”

“Congresswoman Gillen has been a strong and consistent advocate for healthcare and for the needs of the communities we serve, and we are deeply grateful for her continued support” said David Nemiroff, Chief Executive Officer of Harmony Healthcare Long Island. “We also extend our sincere thanks to Whip Clark for coming to Long Island and lending her voice and leadership to this critical issue. At a time when access to affordable, high-quality healthcare is more important than ever for our patients and families, this level of advocacy and engagement makes a meaningful difference. We appreciate their partnership and unwavering commitment to the health and well-being of our communities.”

She has fought against cuts to Medicaid and SNAP in the OBBBA, led and signed bipartisan letters opposing policies that would increase healthcare costs or jeopardize cancer research and safety-net hospitals and called on congressional leadership to protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid.

Rep. Gillen has also supported legislation to lower prescription drug costs by expanding Medicare drug price negotiations, permanently extend Affordable Care Act tax credits. Additionally, she has championed bipartisan legislation to protect safety-net hospitals, streamline Medicare Advantage prior authorization for seniors and increase transparency and affordability in dental and vision coverage.

title: As Admitted Party in Liberty Utilities Rate Case, Goodlander Demands Answers on Service Refusals
text:
Concord, N.H. — Continuing her fight to hold Liberty Utilities accountable after its refusal to provide new or expanded natural gas service for customers in the Lakes Region, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) today served discovery questions in the company’s rate case before the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission. The questions build on Goodlander’s months of oversight and successful effort to put Liberty’s Lakes Region service denials under review, demanding answers on the company’s decisions, costs, and plans to end the moratorium.

Liberty is asking the Commission to approve a $35.8 million annual increase in distribution rates, which would add about $26 a month to a typical residential heating bill, while also continuing to refuse new or expanded service in the Lakes Region.

In June, Goodlander sent Liberty 13 questions about the moratorium. Liberty responded with a five-page letter leaving the majority of questions unanswered, including basic ones regarding who at the company made the decision, how many customers have been turned away, and what the pipeline upgrade will cost. As a formal party to the rate case, Goodlander can now require answers through the Commission’s discovery process.

The questions press Liberty to explain who decided to impose the moratorium, how many customers have been denied service and why, and why critical pipeline upgrades were delayed.

Goodlander is also demanding details on the cost and timing of temporary and permanent fixes, whether affected customers will be compensated, and the company’s profits and payments to its parent company.

“For months, families and small businesses across our Lakes Region have been left in limbo while Liberty leaves basic questions unanswered. Who decided to deny them service? Why does the timeline for a permanent fix keep slipping? Who will foot the bill?” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “Families in New Hampshire deserve answers, reliable service, and real accountability. Now that we’ve secured a seat at the table in this case, I’m using every tool available to demand those answers on the record. I won’t quit until the people I work for get the answers and solutions they deserve.”

Read the full questions HERE.

Goodlander has made lower energy costs and investor-owned utility accountability a focus of her work in Congress:

Goodlander previously filed a petition to intervene in Liberty Utilities’ rate case, with the Public Utilities Commission granting it last month. Following Goodlander’s advocacy, the PUC also agreed to take up Liberty’s decision to deny new or expanded service to towns across the Lakes Region – identifying Liberty’s “moratorium” on new natural gas service in the Lakes Region as an issue that belongs in this PUC proceeding.

Goodlander urged the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission to reconsiderEversource’s approved 43.4 percent rate increase and helped introduce the Lowering Utility Bills Act to rein in excessive profits at investor-owned utilities.

She introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation to accelerate hydropower production and lower energy costs, launched a bipartisan Hydropower Caucus to do the same, and joined efforts to protect ratepayers from potentially costly utility transactions.

Before taking office, Goodlander served as a Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division, where she took on corporate monopolies driving up costs for families and small businesses.

title: As New Hampshire Home Prices Hit a Record $575,000, Goodlander Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Cut the Delays Driving Up the Cost of Building a Home
text:
85% of Granite State households cannot afford the median home. Goodlander’s bipartisan Build More Homes Act, co-led with Republican Congressman Jefferson Shreve, would put pre-approved home designs that save builders time and money under the microscope, so more communities can use what works

Concord, N.H. — Today, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) introduced the bipartisan Build More Homes Act to attack one of the most expensive and least visible obstacles to building a home in New Hampshire: the months a homebuilder is often forced to spend drawing up plans and waiting for them to be reviewed before a single shovel goes in the ground.

The bill, which Goodlander is leading with Congressman Jefferson Shreve (R-IN-06), directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct the first nationwide review of housing “pattern books” — catalogs of pre-reviewed, permit-ready home designs that let builders skip costly custom design work and get approved faster, while giving towns and cities homes that fit the character of their neighborhoods.

This bill takes aim at some of the most preventable costs in homebuilding: architecture, review, and delay.

“New Hampshire is in a full-blown housing crisis: 85% of households across our state are priced out of this cornerstone of the American Dream,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “Nurses, teachers, firefighters, electricians, and hardworking people of all ages are being pushed out of the communities they love and the communities that depend on them. I’m using every tool I have to lower the sky-high housing costs New Hampshire families face and make it cheaper and faster to build the homes we urgently need. Our bipartisan Build More Homes Act is about cutting costs and red tape, and learning from communities like Lebanon that are already showing us what works.”

A Full-Blown Housing Crisis

New Hampshire’s housing crisis has never been worse. According to Housing is New Hampshire’s Future, the report New Hampshire Housing released last month:

The median single-family home hit a record $575,000 in June 2026. A family needs to earn about $189,000 a year to afford it, and only 15% of New Hampshire households — and just 4% of renters — earn that much.

The median rent statewide is $2,011 a month. A worker needs to earn $38.67 an hour to afford it, while the typical Granite Stater earns about $26 an hour.

Prices across the Northeast have risen about 28% — gasoline 67%, food 31% — while median household income has grown only about 4% after inflation since February 2020.

New Hampshire added 25,872 homes from 2020 through 2025, just 39% of what the state needs by 2030. The state is building about 5,174 homes a year; it needs more than 8,100 a year to catch up.

What Builders Are Up Against

New Hampshire’s homebuilders face rising costs at every step. President Trump’s tariffs have jacked up the price of lumber, and builders estimate recent tariffs add roughly $10,900 to the cost of a typical new home. His war in Iran has driven up the price of the diesel that hauls materials to every job site. Moreover, government regulation now accounts for $131,734 — more than 1 in every 4 dollars (26.4%) — of the average price of a new single-family home, according to a June 2026 study by the National Association of Home Builders. That’s up from $93,870 in 2021, the biggest jump NAHB has ever recorded between its studies. And 94% of developers say complying with regulations delays their projects, by about 7 months on average — exactly the kind of delay pre-approved designs are built to cut.

Goodlander’s Build More Homes Act

Pre-approved designs go straight at the “soft costs” of architecture, review, and delay. Communities with these programs most often report savings of $5,000 to $10,000 per homeand approvals that come weeks to months faster, according to a May 2026 Pew report that identified more than 40 jurisdictions using them. But the Congressional Research Service has found that there has been little systematic research into the impacts of these designs. Goodlander’s Build More Homes Act closes that gap, so towns, builders, and Congress know what saves the most money and gets homes built fastest.

In Lebanon, New Hampshire, the city’s Pattern Zones initiative pairs pre-approved, code-compliant designs for duplexes, triplexes, and small apartment buildings with rules tailored to existing neighborhoods, making room for new homes on underused lots while preserving neighborhood character. Next door, Vermont’s 802 Homes initiative is building a statewide catalog of small-home and multi-unit designs for both traditional and off-site construction; Maine enacted legislation requiring the preparation of pre-approved building types for municipalities to adopt; and Bangor already offers pre-approved plans for accessory dwelling units, triplexes, and fourplexes. Repeatable designs also open the door for factory-built homes, connecting housing production to the region’s manufacturing economy and to pioneering New Hampshire companies that already build homes off-site.

The bill builds on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which Goodlander helped get across the finish line this summer and which created a Pattern Book Grant Program based on a provision she cosponsored. That program’s required research is limited to the communities that receive grants. The Build More Homes Act broadens the lens to programs nationwide, helping policymakers and communities measure how these designs affect the time and cost of building housing.

Fighting to Lower Housing Costs for New Hampshire

“I came to Congress to lower costs, and housing is where families feel it most,” said Goodlander. “I helped get the ROAD to Housing Act into law. I’m taking on the corporate landlords using algorithms to rig rents, because I did that work at the Justice Department. And I’m working with Republicans and Democrats to clear away every rule that makes it slower and more expensive to build a home in New Hampshire. I won’t stop until every Granite Stater has a fair shot at a home they can afford.”

The Build More Homes Act is the latest step in Goodlander’s fight to bring down housing costs:

Got the biggest housing law in years across the finish line. Goodlander helped passthe bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act through the House, sent it to the President’s desk, and saw it become law in July 2026 — including 6 provisions she cosponsored to speed up homebuilding with pre-approved designs, cut red tape for rural housing, expand modular and manufactured homes, support resident-owned communities, help veterans use their home-loan benefits, and clarify Build America, Buy America rules for the HOME program.

Cutting costly delays for affordable housing. With Republican Rep. Mike Flood, Goodlander introduced the Build Housing Affordably Act to study and temporarily pause federal sourcing rules that are delaying affordable housing projects, and to force faster waiver decisions. The bill is backed by more than 30 national housing organizations, including the National Council of State Housing Agencies, the National Association of Home Builders, and Habitat for Humanity International.

Taking on corporate landlords rigging rents. Goodlander leads the End Rent Fixing Act to outlaw the algorithmic price-fixing tools that cost renters at least $3.8 billion in 2023 — the same practices she took on at the Justice Department.

Cutting red tape on manufactured homes. Goodlander joined Republicans to pass the bipartisan Affordable HOMES Act to remove federal rules that drive up the cost of manufactured housing for first-time buyers, young families, and seniors.

Financing more homes. Goodlander helped introduce the bipartisan SUPPLY Act to help homeowners finance accessory dwelling units, and is an original cosponsor of the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, which has helped NeighborWorks Southern New Hampshire alone build 550 apartments. She also cosponsored the Empty Lots to Housing Act to turn surplus public land into homes.

Protecting Granite Staters at risk of losing their homes. Goodlander helped deliver more than $14 million to New Hampshire organizations fighting homelessness, pressed HUD to prevent 170,000 people from losing their homes in the dead of winter, and joined the delegation last month in urging HUD to release overdue housing funds.

Bringing New Hampshire’s voices to Washington. Goodlander convened builders, lenders, and housing advocates at a Concord housing roundtable, launched the Lowering Costs Caucus, welcomed $500,000 to create workforce housing for health care staff at Speare Memorial Hospital in Plymouth, and called on the President to cut tariffs on building materials and act on the housing crisis.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $3.7 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Sussex County
text:
Above: Gottheimer Announces $3.7 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Sussex County.

NEWTON, NJ — Today, October 16, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced that he successfully clawed back $3.68 million in new federal Homeland Security funding for Sussex County first responders, helping upgrade emergency communications, expand counterterrorism training, and strengthen public safety while delivering real tax relief for local families.

The federal investment Gottheimer secured will replace aging equipment and move Sussex County toward a single, interoperable communications standard, so local, county, and State Police can communicate clearly and seamlessly across town lines when seconds matter most. By clawing back federal dollars to North Jersey communities and first responders, Gottheimer is helping lift high costs off local budgets, reducing the burden on Sussex County taxpayers to pay for essential public safety equipment and helping lower property taxes for local families.

Video of Gottheimer’s announcement can be found here.

“When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $3.68 million in federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Sussex County first responders, families, and towns. I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the Law Enforcement Caucus and member of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus.

“We know that Josh Gottheimer is the claw back king,” said Sussex County Prosecutor Daniel M. Perez. “He works day in and day out to claw back federal taxpayer funds for first responders in Sussex County. You may not know this, but every day Josh wakes up and says ‘how can I redirect federal funds back to Sussex County? How can I claw back taxpayer dollars from Moocher States?’ Then he goes to work, reaches across the aisle, and delivers results for our families.”

The funding will be used as follows:

Sussex County Prosecutor’s Office, $300,000: A countywide interoperable radio system linking every municipal law enforcement agency, the New Jersey State Police, and the Sheriff’s Office. It will also fund protective gear and other equipment for the Sussex County Rescue Task Force.

Sussex County Sheriff’s Office, $200,000: 7/800 MHz radios that integrate with the New Jersey State frequency, migrating the county’s dispatched towns onto the State’s upgraded system.

Andover Township First Responders, $200,000: A public safety video network system and training.

Branchville First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Frankford First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Franklin Borough First Responders, $200,000: Video network enhancement and a virtual-reality law enforcement training system.

Hamburg Borough First Responders, $150,000: Public Safety video security project and training.

Hampton First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Hardyston Township First Responders, $200,000: A public safety video network system and training.

Lafayette Township Office of Emergency Management, $200,000: Communications upgrades in the Emergency Operations Center to support interoperability and continuity of operations, plus training.

Montague First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Newton First Responders, $100,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Sandyston First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Sussex Borough First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

Vernon Township First Responders, $200,000: Active-threat response gear and training.

Wantage First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.

The $3.7 million funding includes previously announced upgrades:

$500,000 for security upgrades at the Andover train station;

$200,000 for a real-time intelligence platform in Newton;

$30,000 for a thermal search-and-overwatch drone in Vernon, so officers can run night searches and respond to incidents safely;

$50,000 for every police department in the Fifth District, including all of Sussex County, for counterterrorism training;

This investment builds on Gottheimer’s years-long work to claw more federal dollars back to North Jersey from Washington. This year alone, he has secured roughly $21 million in Homeland Security grant funding across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties for law enforcement, first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection. Since coming to Congress, Gottheimer has helped increase the return of federal funds to the Fifth District by more than 357%, delivering an average savings of more than $750 for each household in the Fifth District.

Gottheimer was joined by Newton Mayor Matthew Dickson, Sussex County Prosecutor Dan Perez, Sussex County Commissioners Alan Henderson and David Silverthorne, Chief of Detectives Nicholas Elmo, Detective Andrew Moore, and Lt. Kyle Phlegar of the Sussex County Prosecutor’s Office, Andover Police Chief Eric Danielson, Newton Police Chief Daniel Finkle, Newton Police Lts. Jared Zappa and Russell Post, Wantage Township Mayor Justin VanderGroef, Vernon Township Mayor Anthony Rossi, Vernon Police Chief Daniel B. Young, Vernon Police Lt. Sean Perry, Lafayette Township Committeeman Kevin O’Leary and Kevin McGill, Branchville Councilman Jeffery Lewis, Montague Township Committeeman Fred Merusi, Sussex Councilman John Ross, Confidential Aide to the Commissioners Ken Schwemmer, Frankford Committeeman Ken Sharrock, Frankford Committeeman Ryan Phillips, Frankford Municipal Clerk Lori Niemstedt, local first responders, and community leaders.

title: Grijalva, Kelly Blast Trump Administration’s Push for National School Voucher Scheme
text:
Tucson, AZ — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva and Senator Mark Kelly condemned new Treasury Department regulations advancing a national school voucher scheme created under Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, warning that Arizona’s experience with universal school vouchers shows exactly what happens when taxpayer dollars are diverted to private schools without adequate oversight.

The Treasury Department recently releasedregulations implementing the federal school voucher tax credit established under H.R. 1. The program provides a tax credit of up to $1,700 for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including organizations supporting private and religious schools. The new regulations would double the credit for married couples.

In response, Senator Kelly introduced the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal the voucher scheme created under H.R. 1. Rep. Grijalva alongside Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) introduced the same legislation in the House.

“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Congress must act to ensure taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, rather than subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud.”

“Arizona is a clear example of the consequences of diverting taxpayer dollars to private school vouchers: fraud, benefits going to families who can already afford private school, and public schools losing funds they desperately need. Not to mention a giant hole blown in our budget,” said Sen. Kelly. “Now, the Trump administration wants to take that same approach nationwide. We should be investing in public schools that serve all kids, not expanding a voucher program that risks more waste and abuse.”

Arizona’s universal Empowerment Scholarship Account program now costs taxpayers more than $1 billion annually and has faced repeated allegations of waste, fraud, and abuse.

In one case, two out-of-state individuals pleaded guilty to creating dozens of fictitious “ghost students” and using forged documents to obtain more than $110,000 in taxpayer-funded voucher dollars. Other reporting has found voucher funds used for questionable purchases, including Disneyland trips, diamond rings, and lingerie.

title: Reps Grijalva, Clarke Lead 63 Members of Congress in Urging USCIS to Address Processing Backlog Costing Lawfully-Present Immigrants Their Healthcare
text:
Tucson, AZ — Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva and Congresswoman Yvette Clarke, alongside 61 Members of Congress, sent a letter urging U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to immediately expedite pending green card applications for immigrants who have lost or are at risk of losing Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Medicare, and Affordable Care Act premium credits as a result of new eligibility restrictions under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) that went into effect on October 1st.

The lawmakers warn that thousands of lawfully-present immigrants, including refugees, asylum recipients, and survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking, could lose access to critical healthcare while waiting for USCIS to process their green card applications providing permanent residency. More than 281,000 lawfully present immigrants across nine states and Washington, D.C., were identified as facing the loss of Medicaid coverage beginning October 1. Nationwide, the Congressional Budget Office estimates that 1.4 million lawfully present immigrants will become uninsured by 2034 under Republicans’ healthcare eligibility restrictions.

The letter highlights the case of an Arizona woman with stage four metastatic breast cancer who lost her Medicaid coverage on October 1. Although she is lawfully present in the United States, delays in processing her green card application have left her without coverage for the chemotherapy she depends on to survive.

The lawmakers argue that eligible applicants should not lose access to healthcare because their immigration applications are caught in processing backlogs.

“Because Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs), that have already waited any required time, retain federal eligibility under health law, these individuals are losing their health insurance simply because they are trapped in a bureaucratic bottleneck. This is a backlog crisis that lies within the administrative capabilities of USCIS to resolve and the agency cannot allow its own administrative delays to cause catastrophic gaps in their healthcare,” the letter wrote.

They also warn that these delays could increase healthcare costs for federal and state governments by forcing patients to forgo preventive treatment until their conditions become more severe.

In their letter, the lawmakers call on USCIS to take three immediate steps:

Establish an emergency expedited processing pathway for Form I-485 adjustment of status applications for individuals who face the imminent loss of healthcare coverage because their applications remain pending.

Clarify expedited processing criteria to explicitly recognize the imminent loss of federal or state healthcare coverage as grounds for expedited processing under severe financial loss or humanitarian considerations.

Coordinate with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and state agencies to provide guidance on delaying coverage terminations for individuals with pending adjustment of status applications.

“In Arizona, more than 20,000 lawfully present refugees and immigrants are at risk of losing their healthcare due to USCIS processing bottlenecks, including a woman with stage-four breast cancer and a nine-year-old boy with epilepsy who depends on Medicaid to attend school,” said Rep Grijalva. “These cuts, thanks to Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, are forcing Arizona families to choose between their health and their financial security. USCIS needs to act with urgency so that their bureaucratic delays do not cost people their lives.”

"Needless red tape should never be the determinant between life and death,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “While thousands of immigrant American families remain stuck in a bureaucratic backlog that risks ripping their healthcare out from under them, USCIS has a moral obligation to ensure all those caught in its processing bottleneck do not suffer due to circumstances beyond their control. Government inefficiencies are not the fault of immigrant communities, and they deserve better than to suffer the consequences of them."

You can read the full letter here.

title: Houchin Signs VP Vance Pledge to Fight Fraud
text:
Congresswoman Erin Houchin (IN-09) joined Vice President JD Vance in the fight against fraud. Combatting fraud has long been a priority of Congresswoman Houchin, who leads H.R. 5967, the Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act, and is a member of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

“Each year, fraudsters cost Americans billions of dollars, and the problem is only growing,” said Rep. Houchin. “While Democrats allowed fraud to go unchecked and increase exponentially during the Biden presidency, Republicans are working to ensure that Americans and their tax dollars are protected from criminal fraud. I am proud to support Vice President Vance and the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud in protecting Americans from being scammed.”

The Pledge reads:

I pledge to join the fight and do everything in my power to ensure that:

1. Vulnerable Americans, such as the elderly, indigent, and disabled, are protected from fraudsters who seek to prey on them.

2. Taxpayer-funded programs serve law-abiding Americans, not illegal aliens or fraudsters.

3. Taxpayer-funded benefits are not used by fraudsters to buy mansions or luxury cars.

4. Public agencies and officials work tirelessly and aggressively, coordinating at all levels of government, to stop fraud before payments go out the door.

5. Fraudsters face justice for their crimes in a court of law. Convicted fraudsters will be imprisoned and barred from ever receiving another penny of taxpayer dollars.

6. Illegal alien fraudsters are promptly arrested, prosecuted, imprisoned, and deported, never able to take advantage of Americans’ generosity again.

title: REP. HOYLE JOINS REP. ZINKE AND REP SCHRIER TO INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN NORTHWEST WETLANDS VIP ACT
text:
Eugene, OR – This week, during National Wildlife Refuge Week, Representative Val Hoyle, Rep. Ryan Zinke (MT-01) and Rep. Kim Schrier (WA-08) joined conservation partners in the Pacific Northwest to introduce the bipartisan Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program (VIP) Act.

“Conservation is a team effort, and everyone needs to play their part,” said Rep. Hoyle. “Our bipartisan bill supports habitat restoration and active management of invasive species across Northwest wetlands that support Tribes, farmers and other local economies. This work will strengthen our climate resilience, supporting these lands for the next generation.”

“Good conservation starts by bringing everyone to the table,” said Rep. Zinke. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act gives farmers, ranchers, Tribes, sportsmen and local communities a way to work together on voluntary projects that restore wetlands and keep working lands working. That’s how we protect habitat and water for the next generation. I'm proud to support this legislation.”

“Farmers, Tribes, and local communities across our region rely on wetlands and the species they protect,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I am proud that this bipartisan bill will take a meaningful step to make sure Washingtonians continue to benefit from these important habitats that are a critical part of our ecosystem.”

The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act would create a new grant program under the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) to provide critical water infrastructure and on-the-ground habitat needs for birds in the Columbia River Basin and along the Washington and Oregon coasts.

This legislation is supported by a host of nonpartisan, regional conservation organizations, including. Ducks Unlimited the Coalition of Oregon Land Trusts (COLT), Montana Wildlife Federation, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership (TRCP), Pacific Birds Habitat Joint Venture (Pacific Birds), Trout Unlimited, Oregon Agricultural Trust, Washington State Audubon, and more.

“We’re thankful to Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for introducing the Northwest Wetlands VIP Act in the House of Representatives. The future of conservation is on private working lands. This important legislation will bring much-needed resources for landowners to more effectively provide multi-benefits for people, wildlife, agriculture, and wetlands in the Northwest and the Columbia River Basin.” said Jeff McCreary, Ducks Unlimited Director of Operations for the Western Region.

"The Columbia River?Basin holds critical habitat for migratory birds and other wetland-dependent species,” said Joe Buttafuoco, COLT Executive Director. “COLT and our members are thrilled about the bipartisan NW?Wetlands VIP?Act. This bill would offer grants that land trusts, Tribes, private landowners, and nonprofits can use to improve habitat, manage invasive species, and restore floodplain connectivity. Thank you to Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for advancing this important legislation."

“Wetlands on the coast of Oregon and Washington and within the Columbia River Basin are vital for millions of waterbirds and wetland-dependent species. Support for durable ecosystems, strong partnerships, and natural and working landscapes will deliver real benefits for wildlife, communities, and the economy of the Pacific Northwest. The NW Wetlands VIP Act emphasizes collaboration — consistent with Pacific Birds’ partnership-driven approach. This bill will provide resources for the installation, maintenance, and replacement of critical infrastructure, which aligns with Pacific Birds’ goal to support long-term habitat management while emphasizing multi-species benefits and multi-benefit projects, and empowering collaborative on the ground action,” said Glenn Lamb, Vice Chair of the Pacific Birds Habitat Joint Venture Management Board.

“The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act would bring critical infrastructure dollars to Pacific Northwest farmers and ranchers. These water management projects not only enhance and restore wetland habitat for migratory birds, but also help producers improve agricultural production on parts of their properties. The Act also provides funding to support conservation easements, which protect farms and ranches for agriculture and associated habitat,” said Nellie McAdams, Executive Director of Oregon Agricultural Trust.

“Montana’s waterfowl hunters and anglers depend on healthy, connected wetlands, and the birds we chase each fall rely on habitat across the entire Columbia River Basin. The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act gives ranchers, farmers, and Tribes a voluntary way to restore that habitat while keeping working lands working, so our kids and grandkids still have ducks in our skies and fish in our rivers,” said Frank Szollosi, Executive Director of the Montana Wildlife Federation.

"TRCP appreciates Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier introducing the NW Wetlands VIP Act,” said Michael O’Casey, Director of Public Lands for the Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership. “As someone who learned to hunt and fish among the many wetlands and sloughs at the mouth of the mighty Columbia River, and who has seen firsthand the impact of development and fragmentation, this legislation would provide a healthy boost to wetland conservation for both private landowners and the public.”

“The Association of Northwest Steelheaders strongly supports S.1615 and the continued commitment to policies that protect and strengthen the future of our fisheries, waterways, and outdoor heritage," said James Adkins, Executive Director, Association of Northwest Steelheaders. "Healthy rivers and responsible stewardship are essential to sustaining wild fish populations, supporting local communities, and preserving opportunities for future generations of anglers. Prime habitat for migrating waterfowl also provides critical rearing habitat for juvenile salmon, steelhead and other endangered aquatic species of the Pacific Northwest. We appreciate congressional leadership in advancing this important legislation.”

“The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act recognizes the importance of investing in wetland infrastructure and habitat restoration projects that benefit both working lands and wild places,” said Christopher Borgatti, Policy & Conservation Manager for Backcountry Hunters & Anglers. “BHA applauds Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for championing this commonsense investment in the future of wetlands, waterfowl, and public access throughout the Columbia River Basin and coastal wetlands.”

“Healthy wetlands provide a critical foundation for healthy rivers,” said Lindsay Slater, Trout Unlimited Vice President of Government Affairs. “By incentivizing voluntary restoration and conservation, the bipartisan Northwest Wetlands VIP Act will improve water quality, sustain coldwater fisheries, and benefit the communities that depend on them. Trout Unlimited supports this collaborative approach that helps landowners, sportsmen, and conservation partners work together in the Columbia River Basin and along the coast of Oregon and Washington to restore habitat while keeping working lands working.”

“Healthy wetlands are essential to birds, coastal ecosystems, and the people and communities who help care for these landscapes,” said Amanda Kaplan, vice president for the National Audubon Society’s Washington state office. “The Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act would give landowners, Tribes and conservation partners resources to restore and improve wetland habitat that shorebirds and waterfowl depend on across the Columbia River Basin and the Pacific Northwest coast. By supporting voluntary conservation efforts, this legislation would also strengthen Audubon’s work with ranchers and other landowners to improve habitat on working lands throughout the region. We thank Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for introducing this bipartisan bill.”

“Healthy wetlands are essential to healthy river systems, supporting fish, waterfowl, and other bird species while helping ensure clean drinking water,” said Liz Hamilton, Policy Director for the Northwest Sportfishing Industry Association. “We thank Representatives Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for working with Ducks Unlimited to advance this important legislation. These projects will create jobs during implementation and support long-term employment across the region through the outdoor recreation economy.”

"Healthy wetlands are foundational to Washington’s economy, ecosystems, and communities,” said Washington Association of Land Trusts (WALT) Executive Director Erik Kingfisher. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act would provide much needed investments in enhancing, maintaining and restoring these vital lands across the Columbia River Basin, Washington coastal zone, and throughout the Puget Sound. As land trusts with the skills to make these projects happen across our beautiful state, we support this bipartisan legislation that would empower landowners through a voluntary, partnership-based approach to establish an open space legacy and enable the care and restoration of these lands to sustain them for future generations."

title: Smith Helps Secure More Than $2.3 Million for Rural Healthcare Workers and Access to Maternal Care in Missouri
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, the Trump Administration announced more than $2.3 million in federal investment to strengthen Missouri’s rural healthcare workforce and expand access to maternal care. This funding is part of the Rural Health Transformation Program’s (RHTP) historic $50 billion investment in rural healthcare, which Rep. Jason Smith (MO-08) authored as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts, also known as the One, Big, Beautiful Bill.

“A rural mom shouldn’t have to drive an hour or more to find someone to deliver her baby,” said Rep. title: Kaptur Announces $50 Million in Federal Railroad Administration Investment in Rail Infrastructure for Northwest Ohio Rail Infrastructure
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) announced investments of nearly $50 Million in Rail Infrastructure for Northwest Ohio. The Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway will receive a $43.5 Million award through the US Department of Transportation’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. The award will be used to make improvements to the Toledo Swing Bridge over the Maumee River. Congresswoman Kaptur, the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority, and representatives from the Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway will hold a press conference Monday in Toledo to announce further details related to this major funding award. In addition, the Ohio Rail Development Commission (ORDC) will receive a $5.6 Million FRA CRISI award to be used to update track infrastructure along a section of the Indiana Northeastern Railroad in Williams County.

“Our railways are a crucial mode of transportation connecting our region, the industrial heartland of America, to markets around the world,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “I am thrilled to see this investment in railways here in Northwest Ohio. Access to strong and safe rail infrastructure is vital for trade across the Great Lakes Region, connecting us to global markets. The Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway Company is an important part of our economy, moving tens of thousands of freight cars each year. I look forward to seeing how their improvements bolster trade and increase rail safety for years to come.”

"The Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority is glad to see that the rehabilitation of the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway Bridge over the Maumee River will be moving forward with the assistance of the CRISI program,” said Thomas Winston, President & CEO of the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority. “This project not only improves the efficiency of railroad operations in the port area but also improves the reliability of the functionality of the bridge, making it safer and reducing potential delays for maritime traffic moving though the area."

Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway’s award seeks to rehabilitate and modernize the Toledo Swing Bridge over the Maumee River. This includes the rehabilitation of eight of the eleven bridge spans and replacing timber fender systems on the bridge. Upon completion, the upgrades will increase the bridge’s capacity to support up to 286,000-pound railcars.

“I am thrilled that the Ohio Rail Development Commission is the recipient of this tremendous investment in rail infrastructure,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). The Indiana Northeastern Railroad Company operates over 100-miles of track throughout our region, and today’s award will allow them to improve parts of that track right here in Northwest Ohio. By making our rail systems safer, we are creating more jobs and increasing the trade that flows through our community. When our railroads are stronger, our nation is stronger.”

“We are grateful to the Federal Railroad Administration for selecting these crucial projects to receive federal funding,” said Ohio Rail Development Commission Executive Director Matthew Dietrich. “These investments directly deliver on our commitment to upgrading vital infrastructure, enhancing safety, and strengthening freight service reliability across Northwest Ohio.”

The Ohio Rail Development Commission’s award will be used to improve sections of track on the Indiana Northeastern Railroad in Williams County. Improvements will be made to extend sidings, replace rail, and resurface track along nine miles of the rail system.

Creating reliable, efficient, and affordable transportation for people and products remains a strong priority for Congresswoman Kaptur. In 2024, she secured a total of $18.57 Million in FRA awards for the Northern Ohio & Western Railway and the Napoleon, Defiance, & Western Railway. These two awards were made possible through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, of which Kaptur was a staunch advocate as it moved through Congress.
