title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Put Parents in Charge of Their Children's Education
text:
WASHINGTON, DC. (Oct. 15, 2026) - Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) introduced the School Freedom Act of 2026, legislation empowering parents, not Washington bureaucrats, to decide where their children's federal education dollars go.

The School Freedom Act creates School Freedom Accounts, allowing federal education funding to follow the student instead of the system. Parents could direct those funds toward public schools, private schools, charter schools, homeschool curriculum, tutoring, career and technical education, online learning, and other approved educational expenses.

"Parents know their children better than any bureaucrat in Washington ever will," said Congresswoman Mace. "For decades, we've poured billions into a one-size-fits-all education system while student achievement has stagnated and families have been left with fewer choices. It's time to put parents back in the driver's seat."

Under the legislation, existing federal elementary and secondary education programs would be phased out and replaced with School Freedom Accounts funded on a per-student basis. Families who choose to keep their children in public school can direct those federal funds to their local public school. Families who choose another educational path can use those same federal dollars for approved educational expenses which best meet their child's needs. The bill would also allow states to contribute state dollars to the accounts and parents to make tax-advantaged contributions to the accounts.

The legislation also allows unused funds to roll over into a Higher Education and Skills Obtainment Fund, giving students the opportunity to use remaining federal education dollars for college, career and technical education, or other eligible postsecondary education expenses.

"Our goal is simple: every child deserves access to the best education possible," Mace added. "This bill gives families more choices and the freedom to invest in the educational path best suited for their child."

The School Freedom Act also preserves the independence of private, religious, and homeschool education providers while giving parents greater flexibility to customize their children's education through tutoring, educational therapies, online coursework, vocational training, testing, instructional materials, and other qualifying educational services.

If enacted, the transition would begin immediately, with existing federal K-12 education programs phased out by June 30, 2027, and School Freedom Accounts available beginning with the 2027-2028 school year.

This bill has the support of Club for Growth, a leading advocacy organization supporting school choice.

title: Mackenzie Introduces Legislation to Protect Religious and Ethnic Minorities in Syria
text:
Washington, D.C. — This week, Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, introduced the Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act, legislation aimed at strengthening accountability for human rights abuses and persecution targeting religious and ethnic minority communities in Syria.

The legislation comes amid continued reports of violence, religious persecution, unlawful detention, forced displacement, and other human rights abuses targeting minority populations in Syria, including Christian and Alawite communities.

"Reports of violence and persecution against religious and ethnic minorities in Syria are deeply concerning, and those responsible for these abuses must be held accountable," said Congressman Mackenzie. "This legislation is necessary to strengthen congressional oversight, identify individuals responsible for serious human rights violations, and ensure the United States is using the tools available to hold perpetrators accountable. Protecting religious freedom and fundamental human rights must remain a priority as Syria navigates its future."

“The introduction of the Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act by Congressman Ryan Mackenzie is an important step toward ensuring that the persecution of Syria’s religious and ethnic minorities is not ignored and that those responsible for serious human rights abuses are held accountable. For Alawites and other vulnerable communities, accountability is essential to preventing further violence, protecting innocent civilians, and securing a future grounded in dignity, equality, and the rule of law. We are grateful to Congressman Mackenzie for his leadership and urge Congress to support meaningful measures that protect all Syrians, regardless of their faith or ethnicity. The future of Syria must be one in which no community lives in fear because of its identity,” said Dr. Morhaf Ibrahim, President, Alawites Association of the United States (AAUS).

“The future of Syria’s Christian communities and their ancient heritage depends on whether those who persecute Christians and other vulnerable communities are held accountable. The Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act provides an important framework to identify those responsible for serious abuses and pursue targeted consequences against them. IDC strongly supports Congressman Mackenzie’s leadership in ensuring that the United States remains engaged in protecting Syria’s vulnerable communities and making clear that religious persecution will not be met with silence or impunity,” said Richard Ghazal, Executive Director, In Defense of Christians.

“Syria cannot build a legitimate and stable future while Christians and other religious and ethnic communities continue to face persecution, exclusion, displacement, or fear because of their identity. For Syria’s indigenous peoples and communities—including Christian Syriacs/Assyrians, Armenians and Rum, as well as Kurds, Druze, Alawites, Yezidis, Jews, and other vulnerable groups—survival in their ancestral homeland cannot depend on promises alone; it requires security, accountability, equal participation, and the protection of their identity, heritage, and historic presence. The Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act sends an important message: those responsible for persecution, forced displacement, extrajudicial killings, forced religious conversions, and other serious abuses must face consequences. We are deeply grateful to Congressman Ryan Mackenzie for his leadership and for standing with Syria’s persecuted communities,” said Robert Ozgun, President, American Syriac Union.

The Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act would require the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, to submit a report to Congress within 90 days of enactment identifying senior Syrian officials and affiliated individuals credibly alleged to have participated in, facilitated, or concealed serious human rights abuses against religious and ethnic minorities.

The legislation would also require a determination of whether targeted measures should be imposed under existing U.S. sanctions authorities. These measures could include asset freezes, visa restrictions, and other financial or immigration-related penalties against individuals responsible for serious human rights abuses.

Congressman Mackenzie has also engaged with members of the Syrian-American community throughout the Lehigh Valley and worked with congressional colleagues to raise concerns about religious persecution and the treatment of vulnerable populations in Syria.

The bill is supported by In Defense of Christians, the American Syriac Union, and the Alawites Association of the United States.

title: McGovern Leads Push for Rubio to Center Human Rights in Upcoming U.S.-India Talks
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman James P. McGovern, Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee and Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, along with Representatives Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-04), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Eleanor Norton (DC), and Ilhan Omar (MN-5), sent a letter urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to prioritize human rights in his discussions this weekend with Indian officials.

“The United States-India relationship has historically been rooted in democratic values, constitutional governance, and strong people-to-people ties,” the Members wrote. “As the world’s largest democracies and state parties to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, the U.S. and India have an obligation to promote and defend the rights to freedom of assembly and expression.”

The lawmakers highlighted reports of mass detentions, excessive use of force, internet shutdowns, and restrictions on peaceful assembly by Indian authorities amid protests over examination irregularities, youth unemployment, and, most recently, the purge of more than 130 million people from voter rolls. They also raised concerns about reports that individuals associated with Indian diplomatic missions photographed and monitored protesters in Washington, D.C., Chicago, and San Francisco.

The lawmakers affirmed that freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and the right to vote are fundamental democratic principles shared by the United States and India. They urged Secretary Rubio to address these concerns directly with Indian counterparts during his visit and take the following steps:

Press the Indian government to initiate thorough, transparent, and independent investigations of alleged human rights violations connected to the law enforcement response to protests;

Encourage the release of any individuals detained in contravention to Indian and international law for peacefully exercising the rights to freedom of expression and assembly;

Thoroughly investigate reports that Indian diplomatic missions engaged in the surveillance and intimidation of protesters within the United States; and

Pursuant to Section 6 of the Arms Export Control Act, assess whether India has engaged in a consistent pattern of acts of intimidation or harassment directed against individuals in the United States and is thus ineligible for arms sales.

The full text of the letter is available here.

title: Rep. Mfume Commends Postal Workers, Requests Briefing on Suspicious Mailings to Congressional Offices
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Kweisi Mfume (D-MD), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations, sent a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner and Chief Postal Inspector Gary Barksdale requesting a briefing on the suspicious mailings sent this week to congressional offices and state election offices. In the letter, Congressman Mfume commends the Postal Service employees who intercepted several of the letters before they were delivered and honors the postal workers who face the greatest risk from dangerous mail.

“I commend the Postal Service and Postal Inspection Service employees who, according to state election officials and a Senate office, intercepted several of these letters before they were delivered,” wrote Congressman Mfume. “As the investigation continues, I want to make sure Congress has a clear picture of the threat and of any support the Postal Service needs to address it.”

“This week’s mailings are also a reminder that the people most exposed to dangerous mail are the postal employees who handle it first,” Congressman Mfume continued. “Our country learned this at great cost in 2001, when two employees of the Brentwood processing facility in Washington, D.C., both Maryland residents, died after anthrax letters addressed to Senate offices passed through their facility. We owe them and their families a lasting debt.”

“I thank these inspectors, and the letter carriers, clerks, and mail handlers who keep doing this work every day, often without knowing what is inside the envelopes they carry,” Congressman Mfume concluded.

In the letter, Congressman Mfume requests a briefing on the following:

The approximate number of suspicious mailings identified to date, including how many were addressed to congressional offices and how many were intercepted before delivery;

How the Postal Service and the Postal Inspection Service identified and intercepted these mailings;

How and when the Postal Inspection Service shares information about threats in the mail with the Capitol Police and the House and Senate Sergeants at Arms;

The steps taken to protect postal employees who may have processed or delivered these letters; and

Any changes to procedures adopted after earlier suspicious mailings, and any additional resources the Postal Inspection Service needs to address these threats.

title: THOMPSON, WITTMAN INTRODUCE RESOLUTION DESIGNATING 2026 NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE WEEK
text:
Washington - Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA-04) and Robert Wittman (R-VA-01) introduced a resolution supporting the designation of the week beginning October 10, 2026 as National Wildlife Refuge Week.

The resolution celebrates the diversity of wildlife and habitats protected by the National Wildlife Refuge System and the many recreational opportunities these public lands provide, including hunting, fishing, wildlife observation, and photography. Since President Theodore Roosevelt established the first national wildlife refuge in 1903, the system has played a vital role in conserving wildlife, protecting threatened and endangered species, and preserving America’s natural heritage for future generations.

“Our national wildlife refuges play a vital role in protecting wildlife and preserving America’s natural heritage,” said Thompson. “They safeguard wetlands, forests, and coastal areas, provide essential habitat for migratory birds and endangered species, and give Americans opportunities to enjoy hunting, fishing, and wildlife observation. National Wildlife Refuge Week celebrates the importance of these public lands and the need to conserve them for future generations.”

“Virginia is home to many national wildlife refuges, " said Rep. Wittman. “In the First District, places like the Rappahannock River Valley National Wildlife Refuge protect critical habitat, support the health of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, and preserve opportunities for hunting, fishing, and outdoor recreation. I am proud to recognize National Wildlife Refuge Week alongside my colleagues as we work to support the health and conservation of these important sites and ecosystems so they can be enjoyed by future generations.”

“For more than 100 years, the National Wildlife Refuge System has protected our wildlife and ecosystems in Delaware and across the nation while strengthening local economies,” said Senator Coons. “Wildlife refuges like Bombay Hook and Prime Hook are part of what make Delaware what is it today, supporting biodiversity, jobs, and providing amazing opportunities to enjoy the outdoors. I’m proud to recognize National Wildlife Refuge Week alongside my Senate and House colleagues to highlight these incredible spaces contributions to our states and nation.”

“National Wildlife Refuge Week is an opportunity to celebrate the extraordinary places that sustain our nation’s wildlife, connect people with nature, and preserve our natural heritage for future generations. We are grateful to Congress for recognizing the importance of the National Wildlife Refuge System and the dedicated people who care for these special places. This resolution is a meaningful reminder that wildlife refuges are a shared national treasure, and that protecting them is an investment in the health of our ecosystems, our communities, and generations to come,” said Desirée Sorenson-Groves, President and CEO, National Wildlife Refuge Association.

The National Wildlife Refuge System includes 573 national wildlife refuges, 38 wetland management districts, and five marine national monuments spanning more than 850 million acres across every state and U.S. territory. The system supports hundreds of species of birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, and fish, and provides protection for more than 380 threatened and endangered species.

Thompson is a longtime outdoorsman and conservationist who has helped conserve nearly 5 million acres of North American wetlands and uplands through his legislative work and service on the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission.

National Wildlife Refuge Week recognizes the vital contributions of the National Wildlife Refuge System to wildlife conservation, outdoor recreation, local economies, and the preservation of America’s natural resources.

In addition to Reps. Thompson and Wittman, the resolution’s original cosponsors include Representatives Andre Carson (IN-07), Ed Case (HI-01), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Michael Guest (MS-03), Val Hoyle (OR-04), and Kevin Mullin (CA-15).

Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) and Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) will introduce a companion resolution in the Senate.

The full text of the resolution can be found here.

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 10.16.26
text:
American coal requires fighters in its corner. In our corner of Virginia, I am proud to be in the ring to support a vital industry for communities in Virginia’s Ninth Congressional District.

As such, I have supported legislation and signed many letters as one of the co-chairs of the United States House of Representatives Coal Caucus.

Some of those letters have gone to encourage the Trump Administration to be aggressive in promoting coal.

And the President, always a coal supporter, has heard our voice.

Perhaps no president this century has been as supportive of coal as President Donald Trump.

What has happened since Trump’s January 2025 inauguration?

Numerous pro-coal Executive Actions. I proudly attended events at the White House to celebrate announcements which invest in America’s beautiful clean coal, fight anti-coal actions taken by Presidents Obama and Biden and give coal a seat at the energy table.

The Obama-Biden “War on Coal” constrained American coal production, which encouraged the world to look elsewhere for coal.

Countries like India and China, looking to support the energy needs of their billion-plus populations, view American coal as a key resource.

According to a graphic online from Visual Capitalist, in 2024, China and India accounted for nearly 35% of U.S. coal exports.

China in particular is historically a major buyer of U.S. metallurgical coal, which is the type of coal used to make steel. The coal mined in Southwest Virginia is mainly metallurgical coal and had been sold to China in the first Trump Administration.

But the Chinese Communist Party took actions to disrupt American coal access to Chinese markets, threaten U.S. coal mining jobs and rattle our coal communities.

Data provided by the U.S. Energy Information Administration notes the impact of Chinese tariff increases on U.S. coal exports. From 2024 to 2025, U.S. coal exports to China dropped a dramatic 92 percent!

In response to China’s anti-U.S. coal moves, I helped lead efforts to engage the Trump Administration.

As Chinese President Xi Jinping prepared to visit DC for trade negotiations, I requested President Trump prioritize American coal in the negotiations.

Following the late September negotiations, President Trump announced that China will import at least 10 million metric tons of American coal in 2027 and another 10 million metric tons in 2028!

This announcement means coal business in America will get a boost. Foreign belief in American coal will continue to present major opportunities for economic growth, domestic coal jobs and certainty for America’s coal operators.

I am proud to help secure this trade win for American communities. It is a positive outcome that confirms the strong demand for resources that our miners work every day to produce.

I am also fighting for another positive outcome that impacts our region’s coal.

Currently, one of the last remaining coal-fired power plants in Virginia is the Virginia City Hybrid Energy Center (VCHEC) in St. Paul, Virginia.

As one of the 10 newest coal plants to be constructed in America, VCHEC employs world-class emissions control technologies that reduce carbon harms to the environment. Further, the plant cleans up waste coal sites, like gob piles, and eliminates mine drainage.

The current VCHEC owner and operator is Dominion Energy. However, Dominion is engaged in a new merger proposal with NextEra Energy.

Should the merger secure approval from Virginia regulatory authorities, it would potentially put the VCHEC under the control of NextEra.

As an advocate for VCHEC, I voiced the plant’s importance to both Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger and the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC), the regulatory authority responsible for reviewing the merger proposal.

With a SCC decision expected in January, I will continue to monitor discussion on the merger and its potential impacts on VCHEC.

Protecting our region’s coal assets through the VCHEC is essential to support coal jobs, provide net environmental benefits as shown by our clean coal technologies and serve reliable as well as affordable electricity.

Coal plants can be particularly helpful for our electric grid to withstand challenges and prevent the threat of blackout periods.

Accordingly, while the Department of Energy works to ensure there is enough energy available for American consumers, I believe Southwest Virginia coal is an indispensable resource that can help meet the growth in electricity demands.

Further, as a co-chair of the Congressional Coal Caucus, I will continue fighting and promoting energy solutions and trade relationships that boost the prospects for American coal.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/. title: Statement from Office of Congressman Moulton Regarding Suspicious Letter Received in Mail

SALEM. MA — Today, Congressman Seth Moulton’s (MA-06) District Office in Salem, Massachusetts received a suspicious letter in the mail matching descriptions of previously reported suspicious mail sent to Congressional and election officials nationwide. The letter was addressed to “Seth Moulton” and had the same return address as letters received by other officials on October 15, 2026. An image of the letter is attached.

Out of an abundance of caution, using the guidance given by the House Sergeant at Arms in response to the nationwide reports and investigation, Congressman Moulton’s staff did not open the letter and instead, immediately reported the letter to Salem Police Department (SPD) and the US Capitol Police. SPD officers and FBI agents came to the Salem District Office to investigate the letter. During their examination of the letter, law enforcement discovered a white, powdery substance inside. Subsequent testing did not identify any substances of concern.

title: Pappas Joins Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers
text:
Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) joined a bipartisan letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressing concerns about reports that Meta is seeking to use the federal research tax credit for its data center buildout. The bipartisan letter emphasized that any claims by Meta for the federal tax credit must meet the clearly defined requirements for qualified research and experimentation.

Congress established the research tax credit in 1981 amid concerns about declining private-sector research investment and U.S. technological competitiveness. By reducing the cost of qualifying research, the credit is meant to encourage businesses to pursue projects involving technical uncertainty and experimentation, rather than simply purchasing and deploying proven technology.

“We are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit,” wrote the lawmakers. “The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.”

To qualify for the credit, research must meet a four-part test, including being technological in nature, addressing technical uncertainty, seeking to develop or improve a product or process, and involving a process of experimentation. Certain activities, including research conducted after commercial production begins and duplication of an existing product or process, are excluded. The lawmakers emphasized that the scale or configuration of a data center does not, by itself, establish that its construction and equipment costs qualify.

“Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business,” continued the lawmakers.

“The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment,” concluded the lawmakers.

title: Reps. Pettersen, Beatty, & Kelly Lead Members Demanding Answers on Miscarriages in Detention
text:
WASHINGTON – Representatives Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Joyce Beatty (OH-03) and Robin Kelly (IL-02) today announced their demand for answers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) about its failure to account for miscarriages and other pregnancy-related medical outcomes of its detainees since Donald Trump has aggressively increased the detention of undocumented immigrants, legal immigrants, and even in some cases American citizens. In a letter to Acting Director David Venturella, the lawmakers warn that a full year of pregnancy-related outcomes remains unaccounted for as reports describe pregnant women struggling to obtain basic and emergency medical care.

According to agency records, at least 18 women miscarried while in custody from January 2025 through October 3, 2025. Yet, despite these alarming and unprecedented numbers, ICE has failed to collect, maintain, or disclose data on miscarriages since the last report on October 3, 2025.

“Women are reporting pregnancy emergencies without adequate care, and ICE cannot even account for how many women have miscarried in its custody. That is appalling,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “As a mom, I’m horrified by what these women describe. ICE must answer for these failures, provide the missing records, and ensure every person in its custody receives the care they need.”

“I’m horrified by the growing number of reported miscarriages and the blatant disregard for women’s health in ICE detention facilities,” said Congresswoman Joyce Beatty. “Donald Trump’s Department of Homeland Security has a responsibility to account for these pregnancy-related medical outcomes and ensure that women in its custody are receiving the care they need. We cannot allow a lack of transparency and accountability to put more women and unborn children at risk. We are demanding answers, and we won’t stop until we have them.”

"In the first 9 months of the second Trump administration alone, at least 18 women miscarried in ICE custody, and since then ICE has just stopped counting. Pregnant women in custody have continuously been denied access to routine and emergency medical care. Where is their humanity?" said Congresswoman Robin Kelly. "My colleagues and I are demanding accountability and real answers. Everyone – no matter where you're from – deserves to be treated with dignity and respect."

“It is well documented that incarceration significantly worsens maternal health outcomes and increases risks for pregnancy loss, including miscarriages and adverse birth events, due to high stress, poor nutrition, and limited access to quality medical care,” the members wrote in the letter. “Firsthand accounts from detainees indicate they are struggling to access routine and emergency medical care, including not being scheduled for blood tests or an ultrasound to confirm a healthy pregnancy and not receiving prenatal vitamins. The agency has also reportedly denied repeated requests for medical records from detainees, leaving them in the dark about their medical history and the need for any additional follow-up care.”

ICE’s own policy says it generally should not detain people known to be pregnant, postpartum, or nursing for administrative immigration violations, unless release is prohibited by law or exceptional circumstances exist. When those individuals are detained, the policy requires access to specialized medical care and restricts the use of certain restraints. Despite those safeguards, records cited in the letter show that the number of pregnant women and adolescents in detention rose from at least 87 in October 2025 to 101 in November 2025.

The lawmakers describe reports of delayed emergency treatment, barriers to specialist care, and people going without blood tests, ultrasounds, or prenatal vitamins. Some detainees have also reportedly been denied repeated requests for their medical records, making it harder to understand their treatment and obtain follow-up care.

The letter demands complete responses by November 6, 2026, including:

The number of pregnant people detained and how ICE justifies detention under its “exceptional circumstances” standard.

A full accounting of miscarriages, stillbirths, serious pregnancy complications, hospitalizations, and emergency transfers since October 3, 2025.

An explanation of missing data, efforts to recover it, and when agency leadership learned about reporting failures.

Records of outside medical care that was denied or delayed, complaints about pregnancy-related care, and investigations into potential violations.

Trump’s expansion of immigration detention does not give ICE free rein to disregard its own safeguards or evade congressional oversight and dehumanize those within its custody. The agency is responsible for the people it holds—and must answer for their treatment.

Reps. Pettersen, Beatty, and Kelly were joined in their effort by 64 other Members, including: Rep. Quigley (D-IL), Rep. Watson Coleman (D-NJ), Del. Homles Norton (D-DC), Rep. Lynch (D-MA), Rep. Crockett (D-TX), Rep. Ansari (D-AZ), Rep. Pocan (D-WI), Rep. S. Garcia (D-TX), Rep. H. Johnson (D-XX), Rep. Velazquez (D-NY), Rep. Chu (D-CA), Rep. Carson (D-IN), Rep. Gay Scanlon (D-PA), Rep. Tlaib (D-MI), Rep. Clarke (D-NY), Rep. Morrison (D-MN), Rep. DeGette (D-CO), Rep. Kamlager Dove (D-CA), Rep. Neguse (D-CO), Rep. Mejia (D-NJ), Rep. Budzinski (D-IL), Rep. Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Rep. Salinas (D-OR), Rep. Brownley (D-CA), Rep. Deluzio (D-PA), Rep. Crow (D-CO), Rep. Simon (D-CA), Rep. Randall (D-WA), Rep. Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Rep. Frost (D-FL), Rep. F. Wilson (D-FL), Rep. Escobar (D-TX), Rep. C. Garcia (D-CA), Rep. Barragan (D-CA), McIver (D-NJ), Rep. Thanedar (D-MI), Rep. Ramirez (D-IL), Rep. T. Kennedy (D-NY), Rep. Balint (D-VT), Rep. Khanna (D-CA), Rep. Torres (D-NY), Rep. Goldman (D-NY), Rep. Titus (D-NM), Rep. A. Smith (D-WA), Rep. N. Williams (D-GA), Rep. Castro (D-TX), Rep. DelBene (D-WA), Rep. DeSaulnier (D-CA), Rep. Tokuda (D-HI), Rep. Moulton (D-MA), Rep. McCollum (D-MN), Rep. McClain Delaney (D-MD), Rep. Waters (D-CA), Rep. Stevens (D-MI), Rep. Costa (D-CA), Rep. Ross (D-NC), Rep. T. Carter (D-LA), Rep. Grijalva (D-AZ), Rep. Dexter (D-OR), Rep. Nadler (D-NY), Rep. S. Lee (D-NV), Rep. Leger Fernandez (D-NM), Rep. Jayapal (D-WA), Rep. Amo (D-RI).

Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen has repeatedly pushed back against Trump’s harmful immigration policies and efforts to pour billions more into ICE and CBP without meaningful accountability. She has voted against enforcement funding packages, backed legislation requiring agents to visibly identify themselves, and supported restoring protections for schools, hospitals, and places of worship. Alongside Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper, she demanded that the administration abandon plans for a new ICE detention facility in Hudson, Colorado. She has also pressed for answers about prolonged detention in field office holding cells and proposed safeguards to protect detained parents’ children and prevent immigration detainees from being held in federal prisons.

See the full text of the letter HERE and below.

Dear Acting Director Venturella:

We write to raise our urgent concerns about the treatment of pregnant individuals in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody and the agency’s failure to fully account for pregnancy-related medical outcomes within its detention system.

Recent reporting, supported by internal agency documents and firsthand accounts from detainees, raises significant questions regarding ICE's compliance with agency policy, the adequacy of prenatal and emergency medical care provided in detention facilities, and the agency's oversight of pregnancy-related health outcomes. Many individuals have also been detained in temporary holding facilities that can be overcrowded, and lack basic access to water and plumbing. These reports suggest that pregnant individuals in ICE custody may have experienced delayed emergency treatment, barriers to specialty care, inadequate prenatal services, and difficulties obtaining medical records.

Under ICE Directive 11032.4, “ICE should not detain, arrest, or take into custody for an administrative violation of the immigration laws individuals known to be pregnant, postpartum, or nursing unless release is prohibited by law or exceptional circumstances exist.” Under this Directive, if a pregnant, postpartum, or nursing person is detained, the facility is required to provide them with access to certain forms of specialized medical care and is prohibited from using certain restraints. Records show that, despite this policy, ICE has detained more pregnant individuals than at any point in the preceding year. In October 2025 there were at least 87 pregnant women and adolescents in detention with that number increasing to 101 in November 2025.

According to agency records, at least 18 women miscarried while in custody from January 2025 through October 3, 2025. Yet, despite these alarming and unprecedented numbers, ICE has failed to collect, maintain, or disclose data on miscarriages since the last report on October 3, 2025. As a result, a full year of pregnancy-related outcomes remain unaccounted for within a detention system for which your agency bears direct responsibility. This lack of transparency is deeply troubling, undermines meaningful oversight, and leaves Congress and the public unable to assess the safety, adequacy, and quality of medical care provided to pregnant individuals in ICE custody.

It is well documented that incarceration significantly worsens maternal health outcomes and increases risks for pregnancy loss, including miscarriages and adverse birth events, due to high stress, poor nutrition, and limited access to quality medical care. Firsthand accounts from detainees indicate they are struggling to access routine and emergency medical care, including not being scheduled for blood tests or an ultrasound to confirm a healthy pregnancy and not receiving prenatal vitamins. The agency has also reportedly denied repeated requests for medical records from detainees, leaving them in the dark about their medical history and the need for any additional follow-up care.

ICE’s inability to follow agency Directives, provide adequate medical care, and maintain accurate records of pregnancy-related medical outcomes is unacceptable. Please provide complete and timely responses to the following questions by November 6, 2026:

How many pregnant individuals has ICE detained since January 20, 2025? Please also provide how many of those individuals have been detained since October 3, 2025.

What criteria does ICE use to determine whether detention of a pregnant individual satisfies the "exceptional circumstances" standard referenced in ICE directive 11032.4?

How many pregnant individuals were released from detention pursuant to that directive since January 20, 2025? Please also provide how many of those individuals have been detained since October 3, 2025.

How many miscarriages, stillbirths, pregnancy-related hospitalizations, emergency medical transfers, and other serious pregnancy complications occurred among individuals in ICE custody since October 3, 2025?

If you cannot provide complete data regarding pregnancy outcomes during any portion of that period, please explain:

.Why such data are unavailable;

What information was affected;

What steps have been taken to recover missing information.

On what date did ICE leadership first become aware of concerns regarding miscarriage reporting and deficiencies in agency tracking systems?

. Please identify all briefings, memoranda, reports, or communications provided to senior ICE and DHS leadership concerning these matters and on what date those materials were sent.

How does ICE ensure timely access to prenatal, postpartum and OBGYN care, including but not limited to ultrasounds, laboratory tests, and prenatal vitamins?

Since October 2025, how many requests for outside obstetric care, specialist consultations, or hospital referrals were:

Approved;

Denied;

Delayed; or

Otherwise not completed.

Please provide the number of requests for medical records submitted since October 25th by pregnant detainees or their legal representatives.

What was the average response time for fulfilling those requests?

If applicable, please provide the number of complaints filed alleging

delayed, denied, or incomplete access to medical records.

How many complaints, grievances, incident reports, or allegations concerning pregnancy-related medical care have been filed since October 2025?

How many resulted in formal investigations?

How many investigations substantiated violations of policy, medical standards, or contractual requirements?

We look forward to your prompt response.

title: Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen Demands Answers on New Trump Administration Effort That Could Jeopardize CO Substance Use Disorder Treatment
text:
LAKEWOOD – Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) today announced her effort demanding answers from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) about new Trump Administration guidance that could jeopardize addiction treatment and other essential services funded through state Medicaid programs. In Colorado, those programs support residential and inpatient treatment, in large part because of Pettersen’s work as a state legislator.

Last year, Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans made a historic, nearly $1 trillion cut to Medicaid in their One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), provisions which Pettersen has introduced legislation to repeal. But now, Trump’s Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has released guidance expressing the Administration’s intent to “reduce federal [Medicaid] outlays,” ringing alarm bells that the Administration is attempting to further cut Medicaid after devastating cuts could leave over 7 million people without health care. With changes potentially taking effect as early as January 1, 2027, Pettersen led eight other members in pressing CMS to preserve existing services and state flexibility—and provide clarification within 10 days of receiving their letter.

“Like so many Americans, my mom was overprescribed opioids when she hurt her back when I was just 6 years old, which led to a decades-long addiction. When she was cut off from her prescription opioids without access to treatment, my mom turned to heroin and fentanyl to avoid withdrawal. I watched her being turned in and out of the ICU from overdoses while begging for help with nowhere to go. In my fight to save my mom’s life, I saw firsthand how broken our healthcare system was,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen.

Pettersen continued, “Medicaid did not cover treatment for those who were struggling with addiction, so I fought to change that —drawing down hundreds of millions of dollars a year for the critical care people desperately need. But everything we have done to address the opioid epidemic in this state is being dismantled by Trump and Republicans. That’s why I’m demanding answers and fighting back.”

This recent guidance from CMS is described as “early notice” ahead of forthcoming rulemaking, leaving states to prepare for potentially significant changes without these final requirements. States must navigate that uncertainty while implementing the broader Medicaid changes in H.R. 1. Pettersen and her colleagues are pressing CMS to explain its expectations before disrupted funding becomes disrupted care.

For more than six decades, Section 1115 Medicaid waivers have allowed states to test new approaches, expand benefits, and improve access to care. Colorado uses this flexibility to cover inpatient and residential substance use disorder treatment. Access to that care helps people recover while reducing costly emergency care and hospitalizations.

As a state legislator, Pettersen passed legislation directing Colorado to seek a waiver covering residential and inpatient addiction treatment. That waiver took effect in 2021. Today, up to an estimated 20,000 people annually access licensed residential and intensive substance use disorder services, with nearly 50,000 Coloradans receiving support across the continuum of care each year.

Over the program’s first five years, Colorado expanded its residential treatment provider network, integrated medication-assisted treatment and naloxone into emergency departments, primary care settings, and community health clinics, and expanded inpatient mental health coverage. Colorado has also reported a 35% decline in fentanyl-related deaths, highlighting the importance of sustaining efforts to prevent overdoses and connect people with treatment.

Nearly one-third of all Medicaid spending flows through these Section 1115 demonstration projects. Changes to their financing could affect care nationwide, including long-standing programs that patients and providers already depend on.

Inspired by her mom’s struggle, Congresswoman Pettersen has fought to expand access to treatment to help people like her mother receive the care they need. Pettersen is also a co-chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Task Force, a coalition of over 100 members from both parties that work together to advance evidence-based policies that address the root causes and impacts of the mental health and addiction crises.

See the full text of the letter HERE and below.

Dear Administrator Oz:

We write today in response to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ (CMS) June 11th, 2026 State Medicaid Director letter (SMDL) sent regarding “Budget Neutrality and Certification by the Chief Actuary of CMS for Section 1115 Medicaid Demonstration Projects.”This guidance was issued to implement a provision of H.R. 1 that requires the CMS Chief Actuary to certify that section 1115 demonstration projects are budget neutral – a standard all section 1115 demonstration projects have been required to meet. Concerningly, however, the guidance clearly states an intent to “reduce federal outlays” – in other words, proposing additional federal cuts to Medicaid beyond the nearly trillion dollars cut through H.R. 1.

Section 1115 demonstration projects are the backbone of many state Medicaid programs, and states have long been required to ensure that they are budget neutral. For over six decades, demonstration projects have ensured that states have the flexibility to be innovative and meet the needs of their residents. For example, states rely on these demonstration projects to provide enhanced benefits to enrollees, expand coverage, and improve delivery systems to ensure people are able to access the quality care they need and deserve, among other priorities. CMS’s June 11thSMDL and forthcoming rulemaking stand to undermine these initiatives by setting forth a framework for upending long-standing budget neutrality requirements, and leaving states with more questions than answers about what standards they will need to imminently conform to.

Given the unique nature of each state demonstration project and each state’s Medicaid population, regular collaboration between the states and CMS have always been pivotal to ensuring states’ continued adherence to budget neutrality requirements. Instead of allowing states to foster creative solutions to meet the needs of their unique Medicaid population, CMS’ new framework threatens to reduce state flexibility, limit innovation, and narrow the approval pathway for certain health care initiatives.

Additionally, this guidance prompts numerous questions notwithstanding an incredibly compressed implementation timeline. Now, while working to operationalize massive changes to Medicaid programs as established by H.R. 1, states will also be required to interpret this complicated new framework and evaluate the implications for their own existing or proposed demonstration projects—even without final, robust guidance from CMS. In addition to the complexities of this new proposal, CMS indicated that the SMDL would only serve as “early notice” to inform changes expected from CMS’ imminent notice of proposed rulemaking. Given the changes taking effect as early as January 1, 2027, this timeline imposes a severe administrative burden on states, and leaves them in an operational limbo. Nearly one-third of all Medicaid spending flows through section 1115 demonstration projects and changes to disrupt the financing of these programs will have a direct impact on the health care that Medicaid beneficiaries across the country may receive.

Section 1115 demonstration projects have had a profound impact on our local communities nationwide. Given the importance of these programs, we ask that CMS carefully consider the implications of this guidance on states and their Medicaid beneficiaries. We have concerns that this new blanket framework will limit states’ ability to innovate and threaten existing services. Considering our concerns, we ask that the agency keep beneficiaries at the forefront, by preserving state flexibility to utilize section 1115 demonstration projects to best serve their residents. We also that the agency provide states with further clarification on the expectations of the June 11th guidance within 10 days of [receiving this letter].

We appreciate your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

U.S Representatives Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Joe Neguse (CO-02), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Yvette Clarke (NY-1)

title: Pingree, DeLauro: New GAO Report Builds Case for Congressional Action on Textile Waste
text:
Today, Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), founder of the Slow Fashion Caucus and Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies, and Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee, released a new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report on developing a textile circular economy in the United States. The report, requested by Pingree and DeLauro, builds on GAO’s December 2024 report on textile waste and lays out how policymakers can take federal action to address textile waste as momentum grows in states and other countries.

“GAO’s 2024 report made clear that the growing textile waste crisis demands federal leadership. Now, as states and other countries take action, this new report gives Congress an important resource to build on that momentum,” said Pingree. “Keeping textiles in use longer can cut pollution and create opportunities for American businesses that repair, reuse, and recycle them. I recently introduced the Textile Waste Reduction Act to lay the foundation for a coordinated national response. This report strengthens the case for that effort and outlines options for how Congress can seize this opportunity to reduce waste, support American businesses, and protect our environment.”

“States and countries around the world are already figuring out how to keep clothing out of landfills, and this report shows the United States does not have to be left behind,” said DeLauro. “A healthier textile economy means jobs in repair, resale, and recycling. It means less pollution in our soil and water. And it means lower costs for communities running out of landfill space. GAO found that what is holding us back is a lack of infrastructure, funding, and reliable data. Congress can fix all three. It is time to build a new kind of textile industry here at home – for the economy, for the environment, and for workers.”

GAO’s December 2024 report documented the environmental harms of textile waste and found that federal efforts to address it were fragmented and given a lower priority than other goals. GAO recommended that Congress consider directing and expressly authorizing federal entities to take coordinated action to reduce textile waste and advance textile recycling.

The new report broadens that work to examine a textile circular economy: a system that keeps clothing and other textiles in circulation through durable design, reuse, repair, and recycling. Drawing on research, site visits, and interviews with 49 stakeholders, GAO identifies potential benefits including new jobs and markets in secondhand retail, repair, recycling, and infrastructure development; reduced pollution and demand for raw materials; and changes in how consumers purchase and dispose of textiles.

GAO also identifies barriers to realizing those benefits, including limited domestic infrastructure and funding, gaps in comprehensive data, and a lack of common terminology and standards.

The report documents policies being proposed, enacted, or implemented in U.S. states and abroad, including textile producer responsibility programs in California, France, and the Netherlands, and the European Union. These efforts offer U.S. policymakers lessons as they consider how to support textile circularity nationwide.

GAO’s menu of policy options ranges from maintaining the federal status quo to expanding industry responsibilities, providing incentives such as tax credits, restricting textile disposal in landfills, improving data collection, and educating consumers. The report describes opportunities and considerations associated with these approaches without endorsing a particular option.

Textile waste is now one of the fastest-growing waste streams in the United States, with millions of tons of textiles discarded each year and the vast majority ending up in landfills. These discarded materials may leach contaminants including PFAS and microplastics into water and soil and increase costs on communities grappling with capacity shortages at landfills.

Despite the harmful impacts of this fast fashion-driven increase in textile waste, there has been no coordinated effort at the federal level to tackle this problem and support a more circular textiles economy.

In addition, over the past several decades, hundreds of thousands of fiber and textile jobs that once sustained communities across America have shifted overseas, harming American farmers and communities in the process.

Pingree founded and launched the Congressional Slow Fashion Caucus in June 2024 to create climate-smart policies to reduce, repair, rewear, and recycle textiles. The caucus has garnered widespread support, including from American Circular Textiles, the Garment Worker Center, Al Gore’s Climate Reality Project, Patagonia, ThredUp, fashion designer and slow fashion influencer Kelly Dempsey, and more.

title: WATCH: Pressley Slams Trump, Duffy for Unlawful Cancellation of $20M Grant for Roxbury Transit Improvements
text:
Transcript: Pressley Slams Trump, Duffy for Unlawful Cancellation of $20M Grant for Roxbury Transit Improvements

October 15, 2026

Boston, MA

Well, it is always good to be home, to be in the Massachusetts 7th, to be in the City of Boston, and certainly to be in the historic neighborhood that is Roxbury.

I only wish that I was here for a celebration and not to report a crime. This is theft.

The grant that was awarded after a competitive process was exactly that: awarded.

It was not charity. It was an investment long overdue, and one that was consistent with the visioning of community about what is needed here.

So it feels good to be home. I wish we were coming together for a different reason.

Under this 2.0 version of the Trump Administration, I decided early on that our strategy to combat the lawlessness of this administration would be to combat it with the rule of law, and that we would use litigation, we would use legislation, we would use agitation, we would use organization, we would use mobilization.

And that is what is necessary to resist and do everything we can to ensure that these funds that are owed are reinstated. I am grateful to our mayor for being exhaustive in defense of this federal investment.

I want to underscore the investment part. Every disparate outcome in the Massachusetts Seventh, including and especially where Black folks are concerned, is not naturally occurring.

It is the result of policy choices and federal divestment, and that is why this fight matters.

When we talk about transportation, we are talking about much more than just how to get from point A to point B. What does it matter if we do the work collectively of making a city more affordable, more livable, if you can’t navigate it?

This is about whether or not a parent can get their child to school safely. This is about whether or not an elder can get to a doctor. This is about whether or not a worker can get to their job without spending hours in transit. This is about whether or not people can breathe clean air and safely move through their own neighborhood.

There is a statistic that has been ingrained in my mind from my early work on transit justice, beginning on the Boston City Council, and it’s why I founded the Future of Transportation Caucus in Washington to fight for federal investment in transportation that centers equity, accessibility, connectivity, and sustainability. But the statistic that stays in my mind is from Livable Streets, and their report that said the average Black Boston bus rider was riding, waiting, transferring an additional 60 hours a year.

Now that might sound nominal, but that means that people are not experiencing a quality of life because they are in limbo. They are riding, waiting, transferring to get to work, to get to healthcare, to get to childcare, to get to church, or any place else they would like to.

And that is exactly why I advocated alongside community and our mayor to secure a $20 million federal investment for the Roxbury Resiliency Corridors project. Transit justice has always gone hand in hand with racial, economic, and environmental justice, and Roxbury knows that history all too well.

Melnea Cass Boulevard, Malcolm X Boulevard, Warren Street–these are some of the most important corridors in the heart of historic Roxbury. But for generations, they have reflected a transportation system that too often only prioritized cars and did not prioritize people enough, which is why you need investments in multimodal infrastructure.

Roxbury has lived with the consequences: unsafe infrastructure, unreliable transit, poor air quality, some of the highest asthma rates in the Commonwealth, and the scars of urban renewal and disinvestment.

So when we secured this funding, what we saw was an opportunity to do something different, to create dedicated bus corridors, safer bicycle facilities, better intersections, and more green infrastructure, more resilient streets.

Pastor Bodrick, Mayor Wu, when you were referencing this unlawful action by Secretary Duffy, you might have indicated that they didn’t give a reason. They gave a reason. It’s just an unacceptable one.

The reason was because there was anything in here having to do with electric vehicles and electrification because they don’t believe in climate change, and they did not want anything that had to do with the Inflation Reduction Act or the Green New Deal, and just because of that addition, they took an unlawful and rogue action to rescind this investment.

But again, at the end of the day, this is about people, not concrete and asphalt. It’s about making everyday life safer and more accessible for the people who live and work in Roxbury. And again, the community helped to shape that vision.

So after the federal government had awarded that Boston $20 million, this administration again canceled the funding and left the community to once again contend with the consequences.

So, Roxbury should not have to keep waiting. Roxbury has been waiting. So I stand with Mayor Wu and the City as they challenge the cancelation of this RAISE grant.

We secured these dollars because Roxbury deserves a transportation that works for the people who depend on it. Because communities that have experienced generations of disinvestment should not be the first to sacrifice when resources are on the line.

The people of Roxbury have made their priorities clear. They have shown up, spoken up, and helped envision what a safer, healthier, more connected neighborhood can look like.

Our responsibility now is to make sure that vision does not get taken away from them. Roxbury has waited long enough.

—

title: Quigley, Costa Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Defense Innovation Through Partnership with Ukraine
text:
Today, Chicago Congressman Mike Quigley (IL-05), Representative Jim Costa (CA-21), and members of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus introduced the bipartisan H.R. 10772 Frontline Innovation Act. This legislation will authorize the Department of Defense’s Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, allowing the United States to benefit directly from innovations developed and refined on the battlefield in Ukraine.

"When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the entire world expected Kyiv to fall within days. Instead, the strength, resilience, and innovation of Ukrainians and the Ukrainian military have kept the capital free for over four years. The United States should learn from Ukraine's battlefield innovation to strengthen and modernize our own military to ensure our forces are prepared for a new generation of threats," said Representative Mike Quigley, a Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus. "The Frontline Innovation Act would enable the U.S. military to accelerate defense innovation while continuing to support Ukraine as a critical ally."

Ukraine has emerged as a leader in developing modern defense technologies as it continues to defend itself against Russia’s invasion. Ukrainian companies are developing advanced drones, unmanned systems, and electronic warfare tools that are being tested and improved under real combat conditions against a determined adversary. These innovations offer valuable opportunities to strengthen U.S. defense capabilities while supporting Ukraine’s ongoing efforts to defend its sovereignty.

However, existing U.S. defense cooperation agreements have not kept pace with these technological advancements. The last U.S.-Ukraine agreement on exchanging military research and development information dates back to 2001. Although the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) has worked with the Ukrainian government and firms since 2023, legal barriers currently limit its ability to expand these partnerships and invest directly in Ukrainian defense technologies

“Ukraine has demonstrated extraordinary resilience in the face of Russia’s aggression, and Ukrainians are innovating and developing new defense technologies under some of the most challenging conditions imaginable,” said Congressman Costa. “This bipartisan bill will help strengthen our national security by investing in technologies that have been tested on the battlefield, while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight to defend its sovereignty."

“Ukraine is fighting for its survival against Putin’s illegal invasion, and its forces have been forced to innovate at an extraordinary pace,” said Rep. Bacon. “They are proving new drones, unmanned systems and electronic warfare capabilities against Russia in real combat, and our military should be learning from that experience. I’m joining Rep. Costa in introducing the bipartisan Frontline Innovation Act to help bring battlefield-proven technologies into our own defense innovation system and strengthen our military while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight for freedom.”

"Standing with Ukraine is in America’s own interest, and the Frontline Innovation Act is a smart, practical way to do it. Every day, Ukrainian forces are developing and testing new technologies on the battlefield, providing valuable lessons that can help make our own service members safer and prepared for the challenges of tomorrow,” said Rep. Bell. "As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know our military must have the best tools and technology, and after my recent trip to Ukraine, I can see how much Ukrainian battlefield innovation has to offer. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan legislation to learn from our partners’ battlefield experience and help them continue defending their freedom.”

The Frontline Innovation Act would:

Expand defense cooperation by authorizing the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, notwithstanding any other provision of law.

Strengthen U.S. defense capabilities by directing DIU to ensure the United States benefits from technologies developed and refined through Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s invasion.

Allow technology proven in combat to reach the U.S. military faster while creating new opportunities for the American defense industrial base to gain new partners and a larger market.

Support Ukraine through increased investment and cooperation, allowing both countries to collaborate on developing the next generation of defense capabilities.

title: RILEY DEMANDS HOME HEATING AID BE DELIVERED ON TIME FOR UPSTATE FAMILIES
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) is demanding the federal government get heating assistance to Upstate families on time as energy costs rise and colder weather approaches. Riley joined a bipartisan group of 116 lawmakers calling on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to release Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) funding to states as soon as possible, and no later than November 1, 2026.

“Upstate New Yorkers shouldn’t have to choose between staying warm or buying groceries. But while utility monopolies keep raising prices on working families, Washington bureaucracy is threatening to leave people out in the cold,” Riley said. “With winter right around the corner, the government needs to do its job, cut through the delays, and get this relief directly into the hands of the families who need it.”

Riley’s letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. highlights concerns about LIHEAP’s capacity to operate without dedicated staff following mass firings in April 2025. The letter urges Secretary Kennedy to ensure that the necessary personnel and resources are in place to make sure families receive assistance on schedule.

In addition to today’s actions, Riley has also signed onto a bipartisan letter urging the House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in emergency funding for LIHEAP to ensure that every family who qualifies for the program can receive the assistance they need. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 1.3 million households in New York; however, five out of six families who qualify for LIHEAP receive no financial assistance because of budget shortfalls.

You can read Riley’s letter to HHSHERE and his letter to the House Appropriations Committee HERE.
