title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Joins Colleagues for Unannounced Oversight Visit at Adelanto, Raises Concerns About Inhumane Conditions
text:
Adelanto, California — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, conducted an unannounced Congressional oversight visit of the Adelanto ICE Detention Center with her colleagues, Representatives Robert Garcia (CA-42), Judy Chu (CA-28), Norma Torres (CA-35), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Dave Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45). This is the first congressional oversight visit to the Adelanto ICE Detention Center since it was purchased by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in October. The Members investigated conditions at the facility, including reports of contaminated drinking water, mold and maggots in showers, lack of access to recreation, and significant delays in visitation.

“My colleagues and I performed our congressional oversight duties to investigate the Adelanto ICE Detention Center and the serious allegations of abuse and inhumane conditions,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “We hoped to speak with detainees about their experiences and the conditions at the facility, but when we were shown the common areas, it looked as if ICE rushed the detainees back to their cells. In addition to the common areas, we were also showed the kitchen and bathrooms, where my colleagues noticed mold and food that looked inedible. ICE agents also continued to spread Trump’s anti-immigrant rhetoric that demonizes the nearly 1,800 detainees at Adelanto.”

In October, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) purchased Adelanto from the GEO Group in an attempt to evade state and local oversight. This purchase occurred after Governor Gavin Newsom signed more than 20 bills aimed at pushing back against the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda.

Congresswoman Rivas continued: “At a time when our constituents are demanding answers and accountability, ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at Adelanto – similar to what my colleagues and I witnessed at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas. DHS and ICE cannot buy their way out of being held accountable for the terror they are causing in our communities. My colleagues and I will continue showing up at detention centers to hold this Administration accountable and stand up for our constituents.”

Background:

Congresswoman Luz Rivas has conducted eight oversight visits at immigration detention facilities in California and Texas, including at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building, the Adelanto Detention Facility, the California City Detention Facility, and the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. ICE blocked Congresswoman Rivas from conducting oversight of detention facilities three times: Once at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building and twice at the Adelanto Detention Facility.

Congresswoman Rivas has also sent six letters to ICE leadership calling for accountability into the conditions at detention centers and for transparency for detainees. In addition, she joined her colleagues for field hearings into ICE abuses in Los Angeles and Minneapolis-St. Paul.

In October, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) purchased two immigrant detention facilities in Adelanto for $950 million from the GEO group. The purchase of facilities is an attempt by DHS to avoid being held accountable to California’s laws pushing back on the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda.

title: Salinas, Wyden Lead 51 Lawmakers in Demanding Trump Administration Stop Fast-Tracking Deportations of Unaccompanied Children
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) led 51 Members of Congress in a bicameral letter against the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate the removal of unaccompanied children while dismantling their due process protections.

The letter — addressed to the U.S. Department of Justice, the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) — warns that these agencies are colluding to fast-track children’s cases at the very moment when their access to legal support has collapsed. The letter documents a pattern of practices across agencies that rob children of the ability to make their cases fairly, such as 24-hour asylum interview notices, “mega master” hearings, restricted continuances, and the closure of every pathway to counsel. The lawmakers demanded that the Trump Administration immediately reverse course and outlined 25 questions that the agencies must answer.

The letter is endorsed by the Acacia Center for Justice. Click here or see below for the full text of the letter:

Attorney General Blanche, Acting Director Owen, Director Edlow, and Mr. Wall:

We are concerned by how the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) are coordinating to accelerate the removal of unaccompanied children while systematically dismantling the due process protections Congress established under the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 (TVPRA), and we call on you to reverse course immediately. As a result of your directives, immigration courts are operating as part of the Trump administration’s larger deportation agenda and prioritizing speed and cruelty over due process and fair adjudication, with an increasing focus on unaccompanied children.¹ At the end of August 2026, a one-year-old child was asked to file her own asylum application with no legal representative stepping forward.² That is not an aberration; it is the predictable result of a coordinated effort to accelerate children's cases at the precise moment when the federally funded legal services infrastructure Congress mandated has been dismantled.³

After the administration failed to renew the existing contract with legal service providers that ended on July 31, 2026, they neglected to develop a coherent transition plan to ensure unaccompanied children continued to have access to legal service providers. Instead, they sought organizations that were incapable of performing this role because they lacked the expertise, infrastructure, and consents to responsibly manage this work to the great detriment of children.⁴ According to September 18, 2026, filings in Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (CLSEPA v. HHS), the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI), the sole current federal legal services provider for unaccompanied children, “has provided only a handful of Know-Your-Rights presentations and has entered representation of at most a few dozen unaccompanied children since August 5.”⁵ That gap is unfolding at the same moment that EOIR is accelerating children's cases and USCIS is scheduling asylum interviews with only a 24-hour notice.

Rather than slowing proceedings to account for the extraordinary gap in legal services for unaccompanied children, courts are increasingly imposing accelerated timelines and restricted continuances due to directives from DOJ and EOIR. For example, in Philadelphia in early August 2026, 28 children's cases were continued over a four-week period to facilitate representation. Although the TVPRA mandates that the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) “shall ensure, to the greatest extent practicable…that all unaccompanied children…have counsel to represent them in legal proceedings,” only six children obtained counsel from USCRI.⁶ This is despite the organization being repeatedly involved as a friend of the court asking for continuances. Also, in the same month in Houston, four children, out of a group of twelve cases involving unaccompanied children, were informed that their next continuance, scheduled within one to two weeks, would be their final opportunity to secure representation or they would be forced to represent themselves. In another case, a judge took pleadings from a child representing themself, instructing them they had to complete and file their own asylum application and provide the court with proof within a matter of weeks.

Earlier this year, EOIR started using “mega masters” and “rocket dockets” at the direction of the administration. These consist of one hearing for sixty to over one hundred people, including children.⁷ This format creates enormous confusion for individuals trying to identify a child’s court date and ensure their attendance, as well as pressure for immigrant children to plead, accept deadlines, or move forward without counsel. One mega master occurred in early August 2026 in Seattle, where one judge heard 106 cases in one day. Over 30 children were ordered to be removed in absentia. The next day, attorneys reported a docket of 99 cases, including 30 ordered to be removed in absentia. It is clear that children cannot meaningfully participate in these mega masters, but EOIR continues to force them to make life-altering decisions, under unprecedented legal proceedings and without adequate legal representation. Federal regulation prohibits an immigration judge from accepting “an admission of removability from an unrepresented respondent who is incompetent or under the age of 18 and is not accompanied by an attorney or legal representative, a near relative, legal guardian, or friend.”⁸ Where the child has no lawyer, the immigration judge is required to “direct a hearing on the issues.”⁹ “Mega masters” that produce in absentia removal orders against tens of unrepresented children in a single sitting cannot be reconciled with this requirement.

When children are forced to navigate our immigration system alone on widely truncated timelines and without adequate assistance, subpar language access, and sometimes without a merits hearing, DOJ and EOIR cannot ensure that these children have fair, individualized adjudications.

The acceleration in immigration court is being matched at USCIS. Beginning in the summer of 2026, the Houston Asylum Office began issuing asylum interview notices to unaccompanied children in Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) custody on as little as 24 hours' notice, a departure from the prior 21-day practice. On September 11, 2026, the ORR Unaccompanied Alien Children (UAC) Bureau issued a memorandum and accompanying job aid directing ORR care providers to facilitate virtual USCIS asylum interviews for children in custody, including by providing space, technology, and, where no interpreter has been provided by USCIS or the child's representative, by having care provider staff themselves serve as interpreters in confidential asylum proceedings.¹⁰ Reports indicate that children have already been interviewed on 24 hours' notice without legal representation. This practice compromises the confidentiality of the asylum application under 8 C.F.R. § 208.6; deprives children of any meaningful opportunity to prepare for a proceeding that Congress designed to be non-adversarial precisely because of children's unique vulnerabilities¹¹; and forecloses the possibility of counsel appearing on the child's behalf. Coming at the same moment that EOIR is accelerating removal proceedings and the Office of Principal Legal Advisor (OPLA) is opposing continuances, the practice signals coordination among agencies to close every remaining pathway to relief before a child can access it.

Additionally, there are concerns that court independence and EOIR biases have eroded protections for unaccompanied children. For example, there are reports that the Trump administration and EOIR leadership have hand-picked compliant immigration judges, and have pressured current immigration judges, sometimes with incentives, to prioritize completing cases and increasing removal numbers, with some judges even citing that a child’s case must be completed by the end of the calendar year. The Trump administration has hired immigration judges who are ready to implement its directives. In fact, of May 2026, EOIR hired 153 permanent immigration judges this fiscal year, which the agency touts as “the most in any single year in the agency’s history.”¹² Additionally, approximately 100 immigration judges left or were removed during 2025, including judges who reportedly did not comply with fast-tracked juvenile dockets. From January 2025 through July 2026, in absentia removal orders as a percentage of overall removal orders against unaccompanied children approximately doubled, and the asylum grant rate for unaccompanied children in removal proceedings fell from roughly 11% to approximately 1.5%.¹³

In another report, judges said that they received directives that constrain continuances, accelerate cases, limit friend of court services, permit cases without merits hearings, and order the removal of children with certain form of relief pending, such as Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS).¹⁴ Specifically, in Chicago in July and August 2026, a new judge appointed to the juvenile docket ordered at least eight SIJS eligible children removed because it would take so long for them to get a visa that it “didn’t matter.”¹⁵ This practice appears to draw on the Board of Immigration Appeals' November 2025 precedential decision in Matter of Cahuec Tzalam, which held that an immigration judge need not administratively close a child's case to allow USCIS to process a prima facie SIJS application, notwithstanding that SIJS is a form of humanitarian relief Congress created specifically to protect abused, abandoned, and neglected children.¹⁶ In practice, the decision has become a vehicle for removing SIJS-eligible children before USCIS can adjudicate their applications.

The interagency coordination underlying these developments has now received an additional legal foundation. On September 28, 2026, HHS published a revision to the ORR System of Records Notice (SORN 09-80-0321) eliminating three protections that had governed ORR's information sharing with DHS and other agencies: the requirement that ORR obtain a written advisory that shared information will not be used for immigration enforcement, the requirement that ORR make an individualized determination that each disclosure is in the best interest of the child, and the prohibition on further use or disclosure of shared information by the Department of State recipient.¹⁷ HHS characterized the removed best-interest requirement as “administratively burdensome” and “difficult to implement.”¹⁸ And on September 29, 2026, HHS published a Federal Register notice creating a new Unaccompanied Alien Children Legal Representation Division within the HHS Office of the General Counsel, staffed by federal employees whose ultimate principal is the same administration that operates ICE OPLA and directs EOIR.¹⁹ The convergence of these developments - accelerated dockets, accelerated interviews, streamlined information sharing, and federal employees representing children in proceedings against the federal government - is not coincidence; it is the operational shape of a coordinated policy.

As of September 2026, the Trump administration has also started creating hidden courts for pro se respondents at several federal buildings, including the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), EOIR’s headquarters, and the floor at 26 Federal Plaza in New York that is leased to DHS. Specifically, there have been reports of two children being sent to the EOIR headquarters. These dockets set up folks to miss their hearings and be ordered removed in absentia. Subjecting anyone to this practice, especially children, is particularly egregious.²⁰

These practices cannot be reconciled with the statutory framework Congress established for unaccompanied children. The TVPRA guarantees children access to counsel in formal removal proceedings; vests USCIS with initial, non-adversarial jurisdiction over children's asylum claims precisely because of children's unique vulnerabilities; and directs EOIR to cooperate with HHS in providing Legal Orientation Presentations to child custodians, a requirement EOIR has now stopped fulfilling.²¹ 24-hour asylum interview notices, “mega master” hearings, restricted continuances, and the closure of every pathway to counsel reads each of these provisions out of the statute by operation.

We therefore seek your written responses to the below questions no later than October 30, 2026.

1. What directives or other guidance has EOIR issued to immigration judges regarding case completion rates, continuances, and scheduling?

2. What accommodations do immigration judges make when children appear pro se in their hearings?

3. What EOIR directives or other guidance are in place regarding the timeline for docketing children’s cases (including expedited dockets)?

4. What criteria does EOIR use to assign or remove judges from children's or juvenile dockets?

5. Since January 2026, how many juvenile dockets have been scheduled with: a. 25-50 children scheduled to appear in one hearing? b. 50-100 children scheduled to appear in one hearing? c. over 100 children scheduled to appear in one hearing?

6. Since January 2026, how many unaccompanied children have been placed on in master calendar hearings with more than: a. 25-50 children in one hearing? b. 50-100 children in one hearing? c. over 100 children in one hearing?

7. What justification does EOIR have for eliminating specialized children’s dockets in January 2025?

8. What protections exist for an unrepresented child when the only person available to identify a language, procedural, or comprehension problem is not permitted to speak in certain courtrooms (i.e., friend of court)?

9. In master calendar hearings, including those with over 50 or over 100 children scheduled for one docket, how is EOIR ensuring that interpretation is provided for each child in their best language?

10. How does EOIR reconcile the practice of accepting pleadings and issuing removal orders against unrepresented children in mega master hearings with 8 C.F.R. § 1240.10(c)? Please produce any guidance, memoranda, or training materials EOIR has issued to immigration judges regarding 8 C.F.R. § 1240.10(c) since January 20, 2025.

11. How many unaccompanied children have been scheduled for asylum interviews on fewer than 21 days' notice since June 1, 2026? Please provide monthly totals broken down by asylum office and by whether the child was represented at the time of interview. How many of those interviews have taken place?

12. What is the policy or legal basis for USCIS's issuance of asylum interview notices to unaccompanied children on 24 hours' notice? Please produce all guidance, memoranda, and communications between USCIS and ORR, EOIR, ICE, or the White House regarding accelerated asylum interview scheduling for unaccompanied children since January 20, 2025.

13. How does USCIS verify representation status at asylum interviews for unaccompanied children? What is USCIS's practice when a USCRI attorney appears at an asylum interview for a child who has existing counsel of record?

14. Please describe USCIS's coordination with ORR on the September 11, 2026 “Care Provider Supporting Virtual Asylum Interviews” job aid, including the use of care provider staff as interpreters and the waiver-of-representative provision.

15. How many asylum cases for unaccompanied children has USCIS approved since January 2025? How many of those cases were for children in ORR custody?

16. What legal orientation presentations for custodians of unaccompanied children has EOIR provided in each month of 2026, consistent with 8 U.S.C. § 1232(c)(4)? If none, when did EOIR cease providing them and on what legal basis?

17. Please provide any communications between EOIR, DOJ, ICE OPLA, USCIS, and ORR (or any component of HHS) regarding the scheduling, prioritization, or acceleration of unaccompanied children's immigration cases since January 20, 2025, including communications regarding the September 28, 2026, revision to ORR System of Records Notice 09-80-0321.

18. Please produce any policies, memoranda, or guidance ICE OPLA has issued since January 20, 2025, regarding when OPLA attorneys are directed to oppose or not to oppose continuance requests in cases involving unaccompanied children, including cases in which the child has not yet obtained counsel or has not yet had an opportunity to consult with counsel.

19. Historically, OPLA attorneys were allowed to make inquiries, request a case be expedited, or an interview be scheduled with USCIS regarding applications for pending immigration benefits on behalf of children appearing in removal proceedings. Does that access no longer exist? If it no longer exists, when was that ability taken away from OPLA attorneys?

20. How many unaccompanied children have been ordered removed in absentia each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody?

21. How many unaccompanied children without counsel have been ordered removed each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody?

22. How many unaccompanied children have accepted voluntary departure at immigration court each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody? How many of those children had legal representation at the time of accepting voluntary departure?

23. How many children withdrew their applications for asylum with USCIS prior to their interviews? How many of those were in ORR custody? How many of those children had legal representation at the time of withdrawing?

24. How many unaccompanied children have been ordered removed without receiving an individual hearing in their case?

25. What policies or guidance does DHS have in place regarding OPLA’s role in children’s immigration proceedings, including when to ask for and/or not oppose requests for a continuance?

Thank you for your prompt attention to these urgent matters. We look forward to your immediate response.

Sincerely,

title: Rep. Sara Jacobs Pens Newsweek Op-ed on How to Win the AI Race
text:
Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51) penned an op-ed for Newsweek, arguing that her colleagues have largely misdiagnosed the AI race with China. She lays out how Congress needs to address AI on the societal, model, deployer, and impact levels in order to create AI systems that people trust more and would rather use. That is America’s competitive advantage and how to ensure systems around the world are built on American models.

Read Rep. Sara Jacobs’ Op-Ed Here

In part, Rep. Sara Jacobs said:

“While the U.S. is leading in frontier model capabilities and advanced computing infrastructure, China is outperforming us in model adoption. Chinese models’ share of usage on Open Router climbed from about 1 percent in 2024 to over 60 percent in May 2026. Chinese models are also cheaper and use less compute than leading American models. We may not ever build cheaper systems than China, but we can create systems that people trust more and would rather use. That is our competitive advantage and how we ensure systems around the world are built on American models.

“Still, many of my colleagues in Congress beat the drum for speed over safety in the name of competition. Speaker Mike Johnson recently said, “We’re not going to rush in and pass a piece of legislation that would do harm to the country and put China at an edge.” But what the speaker and many of my colleagues fail to understand is that we don’t have to choose between innovation or guardrails. The real question is: How do we build AI systems that people actually want to use and can safely rely on? That’s what winning looks like. Not necessarily being first—but being the most trusted, avoiding costly fixes and backlashes, and having real, lasting staying power. And it’s Congress’ job to get us there by addressing AI on four levels: societal, model, deployer, and impact.”

Background: Rep. Sara Jacobs has been a leader in AI safety throughout her tenure in Congress, sitting on the House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence last term and currently on the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy. She’s introduced several bills to address the everyday harms and catastrophic risks posed by AI, including the Sectoral AI Governance Act, the bipartisan AI Foundation Model Transparency Act, the bipartisan Economy of the Future Commission Act, the bipartisan ATOMIC Act, the AI Tax and Work Protection Act, and more. She’s also passed legislation into law to prevent AI from autonomously launching nuclear weapons and strengthening oversight and accountability of the Pentagon’s use of AI.

title: Schakowsky Statement on Suspicious Letter Sent to Skokie Office
text:
EVANSTON - Today, U.S. Representative Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) issued the following statement after her Skokie office received a suspicious letter, one of several reported at congressional offices across the country:

“Today, my Skokie office received a suspicious envelope similar to those reported at other elected officials’ offices in Illinois and across the country.

"Thanks to warnings from the House Sergeant at Arms, my team quickly identified the suspicious piece of mail and did not open it. We’re grateful to the Skokie Police Department and U.S. Capitol Police for their swift response and assistance.

"This will by no means deter me and my team from continuing our work and prioritizing the needs of Illinois’ 9th Congressional District.”

###

title: SCHNEIDER STATEMENT ON SUSPICIOUS MAIL IN LINCOLNSHIRE OFFICE
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL - Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) released the following statement after his Lincolnshire office received one of many suspicious letters sent to Congressional offices across the country.

"Yesterday, we saw the first reports of threatening mail with suspicious substances being sent to Congressional offices in the U. S. Capitol and across the country. Today, more offices, including mine, received these letters. Following protocol, we open all mail under a mail hood. Upon reviewing the threatening letter, we contacted the U.S. Capitol Police followed by the Lincolnshire Police Department. Lincolnshire Police and Fire, including a hazmat team, came to the office with specialized equipment from Lake Forest. They tested the letter and confirmed it did not contain any harmful substances. The space was deemed ‘all clear’ after a couple of hours. I am very grateful for the swift response of local law enforcement and fire department personnel and thankful that my team and the building is safe."

"The FBI is leading the investigations of these mailings nationwide. It is imperative that they follow all leads to apprehend and prosecute those responsible."

"Anyone or any group who thinks they can scare or intimidate Members of Congress or our teams from doing our job and work on behalf of the people we represent is sorely mistaken."

###

title: Congresswoman Scholten Statement on Threatening Letter She Received at Grand Rapids Office
text:
GRAND RAPIDS, MI – Today, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) received a threatening letter at her Grand Rapids, Michigan office that contained unidentified white powder. The letter, which claimed to be from the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), made a direct and specific reference to an impending “civil war” beginning after the election. The letter sent to Congresswoman Scholten is similar to those received at other congressional offices across the country. The DSA has not yet addressed the attacks, either to condemn them or to take or deny responsibility. The Grand Rapids Police Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) responded immediately.

The Congresswoman released the below statement on the incident.

“My first thoughts today are with my staff who opened the mail and the first responders on the scene. Everyone is safe. The people who work in congressional offices are public servants. They work every day to help constituents and serve their communities. No one should ever feel unsafe doing that work. I’m thankful to law enforcement for their professionalism, and I’m proud of my team for staying calm and looking out for one another.

“Even as law enforcement works to verify the authenticity of these letters sent to congressional offices, it is the responsibility of the DSA to condemn these threats done in its name—and to refute responsibility if there is none. Unfortunately, this is another instance where the DSA has excused or ignored extremism. Extremists resort to threats, intimidation, violence, and terrorism when they fail to convince others of their ideas on the merits. That is a sign of a weak mind and weak character. The DSA has allowed extremists in its movement who not only allow but justify violence as a viable means to achieve political ends.

“Regardless of party or origin, extremism must be rejected, condemned, and removed from our political discourse. Far too many leaders and civilians are looking the other way right now, and innocent people are being put in harm’s way. I won’t ever stop standing up to the bullies—on the right or the left. The American people deserve no less. My team and I will keep serving the people of West Michigan.”

title: Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Murray Visit Washington State Fire Training Academy, Affirm Commitment to Invest in Wildfire Prevention and Response
text:
***PHOTOS AND B-ROLL HERE***

North Bend, WA–Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) met with leaders and firefighters from Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol at the Washington State Fire Training Academy to tour their facilities and hear about what additional federal resources and policies could better support on-the-ground efforts to prevent and respond to wildfires and structural fires.

The lawmakers were joined by: Dave Upthegrove, Commissioner of Public Lands at Washington State Department of Natural Resources (DNR); Chad Cross, State Fire Marshal; Chief John R. Batiste, Washington State Patrol (WSP); and leaders from the Washington State Fire Academy, law enforcement, and DNR.

“Communities in the Eighth District and across Washington state are reeling from the damage of this season’s devastating wildfires that threatened lives, property, and businesses,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I was grateful to join Senator Murray and local leaders today to thank our first responders and discuss the federal resources our state needs to recover from and prevent catastrophic fires. In Congress, I’ll keep supporting our firefighters, bolstering local response efforts, and expanding fire prevention.”

“Washington state just suffered one of the worst wildfire seasons in history. That’s why I came here to listen to the people who managed these fires and understand what they need to continue this vital work. And we are hearing more and more now that wildfire season is year-round—so we need to be preparing for it that way as well,” said Senator Murray. “Now we aren’t just facing more environmental threats that worsen wildfires, we are also facing a President who has severely weakened the Forest Service and other critical agencies—from pushing out thousands of critical staff, blocking funding for crucial programs, and chaotically changing rules and procedures on a dime—Trump has left us worse off and less prepared to prevent future wildfires. But I am fighting back, tearing up his budget, and making sure we protect funding for the Forest Service and USDA so they can continue doing the hard work to prevent and fight wildfires. When we invest in fire preparedness, we save lives and communities. The Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol do incredible work to keep people safe. For my part, I will not stop pushing back hard for Washington state, our public lands, and for wildfire preparedness, prevention, and safety.”

2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.

In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.

title: Rep. Sewell Announces $27 Million Grant to Modernize Rural Rail Infrastructure in the Black Belt
text:
Washington D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) announced a $27 million Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) grant award to improve rail infrastructure and boost job creation in the Black Belt and Gulf Coast region.

Watch Rep. Sewell's video message here.

"I am thrilled to announce that we have secured $27 million in federal funding to modernize the Alabama & Gulf Coast Railway," said Rep. Sewell. "That means safer, more efficient rail service and more job opportunities for communities across the Black Belt. This investment builds on the $15.8 million in rail grants that we secured for the Black Belt in 2023, and it will be especially beneficial for Monroeville, Pine Hill, Linden, Demopolis, Boligee, and Pickensville."

"The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law continues to deliver for Alabama!" continued Sewell. "I was proud to vote for this transformational legislation, and I will keep fighting to bring more opportunities home to our district."

The proposed project was selected for Project Development, Final Design, and Construction and includes track rehabilitation and improvement on the Alabama & Gulf Coast Railway and the Eastern Alabama Railway in Alabama and Mississippi. The project will replace rail, ties, turnouts, and ballast, surface the track, modernize signals and communications, rehabilitate 34 at-grade crossings, and install trespassing signage.

The purpose of the CRISI Program is to invest in a wide range of projects within the United States to improve railroad safety, efficiency, and reliability; mitigate congestion at both intercity passenger and freight rail chokepoints to support the more efficient movement of both people and goods; enhance multi-modal connections; and lead to new or substantially improved intercity passenger rail transportation corridors.

The CRISI Program is authorized by 49 U.S.C. § 22907, and funds were made available by Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025, Div. A Tit. XIII, Pub. L. No. 119-4 (2025 Appropriation); the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, Div. D Tit. I Pub. L. No. 119-75 (2026 Appropriation); and Division J, Title II of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), Pub. L. No. 117-58 (2021).

title: Rep. Sewell Demands Immediate Reopening of Akron Post Office After Abrupt Closure Ahead of Midterm Elections
text:
Akron, AL — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) sent a letter to U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner and Senior Vice President of Facilities and Infrastructure Benjamin Kuo demanding the immediate reopening of the Akron Post Office after USPS abruptly shut down the facility on October 14, 2026, without warning to the community. Sewell spoke out against the closure on social media on Wednesday.

The closure came 16 days before the previously announced October 30 closure date and just weeks before the November midterm elections. Residents arrived to find the doors chained shut and their P.O. boxes dismantled, leaving many without clear instructions on how to access their mail at the Moundville location.

In her letter, Sewell raised serious concerns about conflicting information from USPS regarding the closure. While USPS cited failed lease negotiations, documentation provided to Sewell's office indicates that the property owner agreed in writing to maintain the existing rental rate through 2031. The property owner also denied issuing the notice to vacate that USPS cited as justification for the closure.

Sewell warned that the abrupt closure could jeopardize residents’ ability to receive and return absentee ballots in time to be counted. Completed absentee ballots must be received by Hale County by October 27, leaving voters with little time to navigate the disruption.

“By shuttering the Post Office without warning, USPS has jeopardized residents' ability to receive and return their absentee ballots in time to be counted,” Sewell wrote. “The possibility that eligible voters could be disenfranchised because of USPS's unilateral decision to close this facility, without adequate notice or a plan to protect election mail, is wholly unacceptable."

Sewell also questioned whether USPS followed federal requirements governing the suspension or discontinuance of postal services and raised concerns about the agency’s failure to provide adequate notice to residents.

In her letter, Sewell is requesting that USPS:

Immediately reopen the Akron Post Office.

Explain the circumstances surrounding the closure and provide documentation supporting USPS’s stated reasons.

Develop a plan to restore mail services at the Akron location through at least October 30, the previously announced closure date.

Detail the steps being taken to protect, process, and deliver all election mail, including ballots that were at the facility when it closed.

Provide documentation demonstrating compliance with federal regulations governing the suspension or discontinuance of postal services.

Sewell requested a written response from USPS by Monday, October 19, 2026.

“The residents of Akron, Alabama have the right to access their mail, including but not limited to Social Security checks, medications, bills, and ballots so they can exercise their sacred right to vote in the upcoming election,” Sewell wrote.

Read the full letter here.

title: Shreve Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Cut Red Tape, Build More Homes
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06) introduced the bipartisan Build More Homes Act today with Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), legislation to help communities reduce permitting delays, lower construction costs, and bring more homes to market.

The bill focuses on pattern books — collections of home designs approved in advance by local governments. These pre-approved plans can streamline permitting, saving builders time and money.

Currently, builders often face lengthy approval processes that can add thousands of dollars and months of delays to construction. Pattern books offer a practical alternative by allowing builders to use designs that have already undergone local review.

The Build More Homes Act directs a study of these practices, identifies successful approaches communities can adopt, and calls for specific recommendations tailored to rural areas.

“Homeownership is a pillar of the American Dream, but too many Hoosiers are being priced out,” said Congressman Shreve. “We need to make it easier and less expensive to build. My bill will help local communities find practical ways to cut red tape, shorten delays, and get more homes on the market.”

“New Hampshire is in a full-blown housing crisis: 85% of households across our state are priced out of this cornerstone of the American Dream,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “Nurses, teachers, firefighters, electricians, and hardworking people of all ages are being pushed out of the communities they love and the communities that depend on them. I’m using every tool I have to lower the sky-high housing costs New Hampshire families face and make it cheaper and faster to build the homes we urgently need. Our bipartisan Build More Homes Act is about cutting costs and red tape, and learning from communities like Lebanon that are already showing us what works.”

title: Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on U.S. Citizen and Marine Veteran Detained by ICE
text:

Rep. Subramanyam issues the following statement:

“I am appalled by the recent ICE targeting of a U.S. citizen and Marine veteran here in Loudoun County. This is not how America should treat our veterans. Our servicemembers deserve our utmost respect, and they and their families should not be targeted by federal immigration agents. This administration said they were going to go after the worst of the worst, but instead ICE continues to target law abiding, non-violent members of our community, including American citizens.

text:
Dân Biểu Derek Trần lên tiếng về thỏa thuận bồi thường $125 triệu của GKN
Friday, October 16, 2026
ORANGE COUNTY, California
– Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) đưa ra tuyên bố sau khi Biện Lý Cuộc Orange County thông báo đạt được thỏa thuận bồi thường trị giá $125 triệu với công ty GKN Aerospace, liên quan đến sự việc bồn chứa hóa chất độc hại hồi Tháng Năm, 2026, khiến 50,000 cư dân và cơ sở kinh doanh phải di tản.

Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết.
“Tôi hy vọng thỏa thuận này sẽ sớm được tòa phê chuẩn để có thể bắt đầu tiếp nhận hồ sơ yêu cầu bồi thường, đồng thời nhanh chóng cung cấp khoản hỗ trợ tài chính và hoàn trả các chi phí cần thiết cho những người bị ảnh hưởng. Tôi sẽ tiếp tục theo dõi sát sao tình hình để bảo đảm các gia đình, doanh nghiệp và tổ chức cộng đồng được bồi thường thỏa đáng.”
“Mọi người dân California đều xứng đáng được sống an toàn trong chính ngôi nhà của mình, không phải lo sợ bị buộc di dời hay xáo trộn cuộc sống. Dự Luật Minh Bạch Thông Tin Về Vật Liệu Nguy Hiểm (Hazardous Materials Transparency Act

title: El representante Tran emite un comunicado sobre el acuerdo extrajudicial de 125 millones de dólares de GKN
text:
Condado de Orange, California – El representante Derek Tran (CA-45) ha emitido la siguiente declaración en respuesta al anuncio de la Fiscalía del Condado de Orange de que ha alcanzado un acuerdo de 125 millones de dólares con GKN Aerospace tras la emergencia relacionada con un depósito de sustancias químicas tóxicas en mayo de 2026, que provocó la evacuación de 50000 residentes y negocios:

“Me tranquiliza ver que el Condado de Orange y GKN han llegado a un acuerdo que da prioridad a las necesidades de los residentes y los propietarios de pequeñas empresas que se vieron afectados por la evacuación forzosa de mayo”, dijo el representante Tran. “Espero que este acuerdo pueda superar rápidamente el proceso de aprobación judicial, para que podamos poner en marcha el proceso de reclamaciones y gestionar la ayuda económica y los reembolsos que tanto necesitan los afectados. Seguiré vigilando de cerca la situación para garantizar que las familias, las empresas y los socios comunitarios reciban una indemnización adecuada.’’

“Todos los californianos merecen sentirse seguros en su propio hogar, sin temor a ser desalojados ni a sufrir trastornos. Como su representante en el Congreso, supervisaré de primera mano la aplicación del plan de seguridad integral de GKN a medida que avancen en sus operaciones de fabricación.”

El acuerdo extrajudicial, presentado por la Fiscalía del Condado de Orange el lunes 12 de octubre, está pendiente de aprobación por parte del Tribunal Superior del Condado de Orange.

En respuesta a la evacuación de mayo de 2026, el representante Tran presentó la Ley de Transparencia sobre Materiales Peligrosos, que obligaría a instalaciones como GKN a informar adecuadamente a las comunidades en las que operan sobre las medidas de seguridad establecidas para proteger a los residentes y a las pequeñas empresas.

title: El representante Tran presenta una propuesta legislativa para reducir los costos de la vivienda para las familias del sur de California.
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – El representante Derek Tran (CA-45) ha presentado la Ley de Ayuda al Coste de la Vivienda para Inquilinos (COST), con el fin de ofrecer alivio a los inquilinos del sur de California que se enfrentan al aumento de los costes de la vivienda. La legislación establece créditos fiscales integrales para los inquilinos, lo que contribuye al compromiso constante del representante Tran de ampliar la asequibilidad de la vivienda.

"Los costos de la vivienda en todo el país, especialmente en el sur de California, han llegado a un punto crítico. Las familias apenas pueden pagar la renta, y mucho menos ahorrar para el futuro", afirmó el representante Tran. "Este proyecto de ley proporcionaría un alivio inmediato y tangible a los inquilinos necesitados, ayudándoles a mantener un techo sobre sus cabezas, a disponer de más margen en sus presupuestos para los gastos diarios o incluso a ahorrar para comprar una casa. Me enorgullece estar al frente de esta iniciativa en representación de todas las familias estadounidenses."

Las familias del sur de California se enfrentan a unos de los costes de vivienda más elevados del país, con un alquiler medio en el condado de Orange que supera los 3.200 dólares al mes y que se ha disparado casi un 40% desde 2017.

La propuesta legislativa introduce un nuevo crédito fiscal reembolsable básico del 8 % para las familias con unos ingresos brutos de 150 000 dólares o menos, con un límite máximo por hogar de 333 dólares al mes, lo que supone un total de 4 000 dólares al año. En el distrito 45 de California, esto beneficiaría a más de 75 000 hogares.

Mientras que otras medidas para reducir los costos de la vivienda tardarían tiempo en aplicarse, este proyecto de ley devuelve inmediatamente dinero a los inquilinos para que puedan hacer frente a los gastos de alimentación, medicamentos, cuidado de los hijos y otros gastos.

Esta iniciativa legislativa se suma al historial del representante Tran en la consecución de resultados en materia de vivienda para la región:

El representante Tran consiguió 250 000 dólares en financiación federal para apoyar la construcción de 2700 viviendas permanentes asequibles en todo el condado de Orange.

El representante Tran copatrocinó la Ley Saving the American Dream (Salvar el sueño americano) para crear un grupo de trabajo interinstitucional sobre la crisis de la vivienda, así como la Ley de Mejora de los Créditos para la Vivienda Asequible, destinada a financiar la construcción de más viviendas multifamiliares.

Además, el representante Tran votó a favor de la Ley "21st Century ROAD to Housing", que entró en vigor en julio de 2026 y tiene por objeto acelerar la construcción de viviendas y reducir los trámites burocráticos.

Puedes leer el texto completo del proyecto de ley AQUÍ.

title: Womack: The National Guard is indispensable to the force of the future
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—October 16, 2026…Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) authored an op-ed this week published in The Washington Times underscoring why the National Guard is indispensable to the force of the future and must be treated as such by Congress and the Department of War.

Congressman Womack spent thirty years serving in the Arkansas Army National Guard and is currently a senior member of the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee. His commentary outlines how the National Guard is a combat-tested force critical to serving our country at home and abroad yet is consistently required to carry out active component responsibilities with second-hand equipment, disproportional funding, and shrinking formations. Congressman Womack prescribes resourcing the Guard to modernize and remain prepared for the outsized role it plays in the joint force—an initiative he has continued to champion on the Defense Subcommittee.

Read Congressman Womack’s full op-ed below or HERE.

For 250 years, America has maintained a force to defend the homeland and deter aggression from overseas. Of all our storied services and capable components, only one force can, and has, shouldered that dual burden: the National Guard.

I know that force. Before my time in Congress, I served in the Arkansas National Guard and retired as a colonel after 30 years. However, the National Guard’s roots have created a paradigm in which it is often treated as “second-class.”

The National Defense Act of 1920 established the three components of the United States Army: the Regular Army, the National Guard, and the “Organized” Reserves. It characterized the National Guard as the “primary combat reserve” of the Regular Army.

The National Guard is more than a strategic reserve; it is an operational, combat-tested force that America relies on every day. And the numbers prove it.

In 2025 alone, more than 15,000 National Guard members deployed overseas in support of a broad range of missions. Roughly 13,000 National Guard members were on duty protecting the homeland from natural disasters, conducting security operations, and assisting civilian authorities. And through the State Partnership Program, the National Guard expanded relationships with 116 partner nations worldwide.

This already impressive track record is even more remarkable given their operating budget.

The Army National Guard composes 34.4% of the total Army end-strength but is asked to operate with only 15% of the operations and maintenance funding. The Air National Guard is no different: It makes up 21.9% of the total Air Force end strength, but has only 11% of the operations and maintenance funding.

When hurricanes, floods, fires, and cyberattacks threaten our local communities, the National Guard responds. When combatant commanders in Europe, Asia, South America, Africa, and the Middle East require trained formations, the National Guard is already in the rotation. And when the nation requires a show of strength, as it did recently with the conflict in Iran, the National Guard answers the call.

Yet, our budgeting and force-structure decisions require the National Guard to carry out active component responsibilities with second-hand equipment, disproportional funding, and shrinking formations.

We call this a “red star cluster” in the Army: a warning signal that needs to be addressed. In Congress, we call this a responsibility that needs to be taken seriously. History shows both the cost of neglecting readiness and the strategic value of investing in the National Guard.

In January 1941, the Arkansas National Guard’s 206th Coast Artillery Regiment was mobilized, trained and sent to defend Dutch Harbor in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands. On June 3, 1942, the Japanese Navy launched two aircraft carrier raids in the first ever aerial attack by an enemy on North American soil. Although surprised and outmatched technologically, these brave Arkansans beat back the Japanese in the opening battle of the Aleutian Islands campaign. The Battle of Dutch Harbor demonstrated what the National Guard can accomplish when the nation mobilizes and trains prior to combat.

But the regiment’s outdated weapons also illustrate the unnecessary risks created when National Guard formations are given yesterday’s equipment for tomorrow’s fight. Eight years later, Task Force Smith provided the opposite lesson on the Korean Peninsula — courage cannot compensate for an understrength, ill-equipped force.

“No more Task Force Smiths” is now a mantra that is invoked to caution against unpreparedness and is a warning against confusing capacity with capability.

That is why Congress must learn from both Dutch Harbor and Task Force Smith and invest in readiness over ambition. It is our obligation to modernize without hollowing out the force that must be prepared to defend at home and fight abroad.

The lesson is simple: when the National Guard is prepared in advance, it is the tip of spear; but when our nation waits until the crisis arrives, brave Americans pay the price.

For the National Guard, this means concurrent and proportional fielding. National Guard formations assigned the same missions and deployment timelines as the Regular Army, while also remaining responsible for defense of the homeland, require more funding and comparable equipment — not less.

Peace through Strength begins with forces that are ready. We should build the Regular Army to meet the challenges of tomorrow, but not at the expense of today’s capable and ready National Guard.

The National Guard is not the force of last resort. It is not the billpayer for the Regular Army. The National Guard is indispensable to the force of the future. It is time we funded, equipped, and employed it that way.

Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) has represented Arkansas’s Third Congressional District since 2011. He is a member of the House Appropriations Committee.

title: Baldwin, Evers Secure Nearly $220 Million for Passenger Rail Between Chicago and Waukesha, Jefferson, and Dane Counties
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers announced they have successfully secured over $218 million in federal funds to expand Amtrak’s Hiawatha passenger rail service in Wisconsin while strengthening a critical freight corridor that supports Wisconsin's economy. Specifically, a Federal Railroad Administration program will fund the final design and construction of the Hiawatha West Project, creating an intercity passenger service between Chicago and Waukesha, Jefferson, and Dane Counties. The Hiawatha West Project, which is funded by the Baldwin-backed Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and annual government funding bills, will also improve freight rail safety, speeds, and reliability, create 200 permanent jobs, and spur $46 million in annual economic benefits.

“Expanding passenger rail means more safe, easy ways to get to and from work or school, more tourists coming into our communities and buying things in our shops, and more good-paying jobs across our state,” said Senator Baldwin. “For our agricultural and manufacturing businesses that use freight rail, this investment will reduce delays and give them reliability and confidence that their products are getting in the hands of customers on time. I am proud to work with Governor Evers to bring home this investment to get folks where they need to go safely, support our Main Street businesses, and keep Wisconsin’s agricultural and manufacturing industries the powerhouses they are.”

“We’ve been working hard to build the safe, reliable 21st-century infrastructure needed to support Wisconsin’s growing 21st-century economy and workforce, and we’re excited to move this critical project forward to do just that,” said Gov. Evers. “We’re creating new passenger rail opportunities for folks to get to and from work, school, and other activities, all while creating 200 good-paying, family-supporting jobs that fuel our economy, and that’s a win-win for Wisconsin. I’m grateful for all the good work Sen. Baldwin and the historic Bipartisan Infrastructure Law have done to support essential projects like these across our state.”

Senator Baldwin advocated to the Trump Administration to fund this project, citing increased tourism and economic activity along the route, reduced delays and improved reliability for Wisconsin’s agricultural and manufacturing sectors, and increased safe transportation options for families and workers.

The federal funding comes from the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program and will be used to rehabilitate and expand the capacity of track, bridges, and crossings, and construct new intercity passenger rail stations. CRISI is supported by the Baldwin-backed Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which all of Wisconsin’s Republican congressional delegation voted against, and also Fiscal Year 2025 and Fiscal Year 2026 annual government funding bills, which Senator Baldwin voted for.

The investment comes after Baldwin and Evers recently secured more than $140 million from the Federal Railroad Administration to update up to 41 passenger locomotives, which serve Amtrak’s Midwest and Pacific Northwest routes, including the Milwaukee-Chicago Hiawatha route.

title: Blumenthal Slams Trump Waiver of Bipartisan, Congressionally Authorized Sanctions on Russian War Enablers
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), co-author of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act passed overwhelmingly by both the House of Representatives and the Senate, released the following statement in response to President Trump’s blanket waiver of primary and secondary sanctions against Russia and actors supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine. The sanctions authorized by the legislation target Russian officials, oligarchs, their family members, foreign persons, and Russian banks and financial institutions, as well as the Russian Shadow Fleet.

“Donald Trump confirms again that he stands on the side of a bloodthirsty thug and the enablers of Russia’s war machine and against the majority of Americans, their representatives in both houses of Congress, and our European allies,” Blumenthal said. “These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin. I hope my Republican colleagues will join me in condemning this craven, cowardly action.”

title: Senator Blumenthal: Week in Review 10/9/2026-10/16/2026
text:
Calling on Trump to Rescind Russian Diesel Deal

[Hartford, CT] – U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Susan Collins (R-ME), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Alan Armstrong (R-OK), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Jack Reed (D-RI), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mitch McConnell (R-KY) and John Cornyn (R-TX) wrote President Donald Trump urging him to rescind his recent agreement with President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian-origin diesel fuel into global markets.

“Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded,” the senators wrote.

The senators urged Trump to instead take swift action to implement sanctions authorized by the recently passed Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which President Trump signed into law in September.

“These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict,” the senators wrote.

The full text of the senators’ letter is available here.

Blumenthal further urged Trump to rescind his disastrous diesel deal with Russia on Twitter/X.

“I’m leading my colleagues in demanding the President rescind the disastrous Russian diesel deal. Appeasement spurs Putin to ignore serious peace talks, & the diesel debacle shows abject weakness. The first test for peace talks is whether Putin respects an energy infrastructure truce. Zelenskyy has agreed. Putin continues bombing. Once again, he’s playing Trump for a fool & hoping to weaponize a freezing, starving, bloody winter against Ukraine,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

“I’m leading 12 of my colleagues demanding that Trump rescind the disastrous Russian diesel deal. It betrays American security interests & brave Ukrainians fighting Putin’s bloody slaughter,” wrote Blumental with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal joined CNN to discuss his letter to Trump calling on him to rescind his diesel deal with Russia, urging U.S. support for Ukraine against Putin’s invasion.

“The American people should know that we are, in effect, aiding Putin, who is supporting Iran with intelligence and fiber optic technology. Iran is killing our sons and daughters, or wants to destroy our bases and ships and other assets. Putin is an adversary supporting an enemy at war with us, and yet we are regarding him as more deserving of support,” said Blumenthal. “In effect, what Donald Trump is doing is a pressure campaign, a coercion against Ukraine, trying to force concessions. He wanted an energy ceasefire, Zelenskyy said yes, Putin continued bombing the Ukrainian infrastructure. So, what we are going to do is demand answers, as we did in that letter that I helped lead against the diesel deal, and the kind of investigation that’s necessary to show the American people what the Pentagon is actually doing in aiding Putin.”

The interview can be found here.

Demanding FanDuel Fess Up About Targeting Problem Gamblers

Blumenthal held a press conference in Hartford to demand betting platform FanDuel provide full videos and information about whether personalized celebrity messages were used to exploit vulnerable consumers and entice addicts to further gamble.

“My message to FanDuel: fess up. Give us the videos that you’re using with personalized celebrity messages to addict gamblers and exploit their vulnerabilities,” said Blumenthal.

Blumenthal further highlighted his demands for answers from FanDuel on Twitter/X.

“FanDuel needs to fess up—provide the personalized celebrity videos it’s using to target & exploit problem gamblers. I’m demanding facts about its predatory practices,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

In August, Blumenthal originally wrote to FanDuel after reports that the sportsbook used a personal video message from Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Bryce Harper to target an individual suffering from gambling addiction. Blumenthal wrote again in September, after FanDuel failed to substantively address this Congressional inquiry. In their follow up response, FanDuel claimed the videos of celebrities and other VIPs were a token of appreciation for customers, however this contradicts reports that a bettor who’d lost $1.5 million on the platform was sent a video seemingly encouraging them to continue placing bets.

In a new letter, Blumenthal demands the sportsbook provide copies of each personalized video as well as information about whether the videos were sent to problem gamblers.

“While FanDuel claimed it ‘has not used personalized videos or messages to induce customers to continue gambling,’ that statement is clearly contradicted by the fact that the video of Mr. Harper that gave rise to these concerns was sent to an individual that had lost $1.5 million on bets on your platform,” wrote Blumenthal.

Blumenthal continued, “In addition, FanDuel claims to monitor a range of behaviors through ‘automated and manual proactive reviews to identify players who may be experiencing gambling harm,’ yet does not provide a full picture of how it uses this information, including whether that same data is used to target bettors with such predatory promotions.”

Blumenthal’s August letter can be found here, his September letter can be found here, and his most recent letter can be found here.

Blumenthal leads several efforts to address the growing issue of sports betting and prediction markets, including the GAME Act, legislation that would prohibit social media companies and other advertising websites from targeting minors with sports betting advertisements online and includes criminal penalties enforced by the Department of Justice, the Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet (SAFE Bet) Act, which would establish nationwide standards and safeguards for the mobile sports gambling industry, the Gambling Addiction Recovery, Investment and Treatment (GRIT) Act, which would dedicate a portion of federal sports betting revenue to addiction treatment, prevention, and research, and the Prediction Markets Security and Integrity Act, which prevents abuse and fraud in prediction markets.

Combatting Deadly Domestic Violence with Bill Keeping Guns Away from Abusers

Blumenthal announced the introduction of the Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act, which would restrict those under temporary restraining orders from purchasing or possessing a firearm and extends protections to domestic violence survivors who have been abused by their dating partners.

The bill is named in memory of Lori Jackson, a Connecticut mother who was tragically shot and killed by her estranged husband who had legally obtained a handgun even though he was subject to a temporary restraining order, and Nicolette Elias, an Oregon mother who, despite securing restraining orders and temporary stalking orders against her estranged and abusive ex-husband, was murdered by her former spouse in front of their children with a handgun that he refused to relinquish.

“Guns make domestic violence lethal. This loophole must be closed. Temporary protective orders must prohibit purchase or possessions of a gun. Prohibiting anyone under a protective order from possessing or purchasing a gun can help save lives, literally. I’ve introduced this measure, the Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act. I’m hoping it will have bipartisan support because domestic violence should be a bipartisan issue. This measure will close a loophole, prohibit anybody under a protective order, whether it is temporary or permanent, from possessing or purchasing a gun,” said Blumenthal at the press conference.

Blumenthal further highlighted the need for his legislation to protect survivors of domestic abuse and keep guns away from abusers on Twitter/X.

“Domestic violence becomes all the more lethal with the possession of a firearm. We must pass the Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act—it's a matter of life & death,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

The full text of the Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act can be found here.

Holding Animal Abusers Accountable

Blumenthal joined the Connecticut Humane Society to announce the introduction of the Puppy Protection Act, legislation to create stronger standards for veterinary care, housing and breeding for dogs. The bill would require larger enclosures, unrestricted access to exercise, socialization and more routine veterinary care for dogs in the care of a breeder.

Blumenthal also discussed his Better Collaboration, Accountability, and Regulatory Enforcement (CARE) for Animals Act, which he introduced last year. The bill would improve the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) ability to enforce the Animal Welfare Act (AWA) by clarifying that the DOJ has the authority to bring cases under the AWA like the U.S. Department of Agriculture does. It also gives DOJ additional enforcement remedies, including the ability to seek license suspensions and revocations, civil penalties, and forfeiture authority to seize and remove animals experiencing harmful treatment.

“We face an animal abuse crisis here in the state of Connecticut. The numbers of animal abuse cases have jumped 37 percent—which means we need federal legislation. I’ve proposed it, and it the legislation whose time has come,” said Blumenthal. “Thank you to the Connecticut Humane Society for all the great work you are doing, saving lives of creatures that are entrusted to us human beings.”

Blumenthal further emphasized the need for his legislation to bolster animal welfare on Twitter/X.

“Action is imperative against animal abuse—as CT cases increase by 37 percent this year. My bipartisan legislation would provide stronger enforcement & better protection. Thank you CT Humane Society for priceless care & advocacy,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal Bulletin

Blumenthal released a statement on Trump’s continued attacks on offshore wind.

Blumenthal demanded answers from VA Secretary Collins on the skyrocketing costs of Oracle's VA electronic health record contract.

Blumenthal called for home heating assistance with increased LIHEAP aid.

Blumenthal slammed concealed contributions behind Trump’s ballroom.

Blumenthal slammed efforts to ban books in America.

Average WA Family Has Paid an Additional $5,300 for Goods & Services Since Trump Took Office, Report Finds
text:
Average WA Family Has Paid an Additional $5,300 for Goods & Services Since Trump Took Office, Report Finds

Recently released data from the Joint Economic Committee shows how much Trump’s policies are costing Americans; Families in WA-01, WA-08, and WA-07 bore the biggest spike in expenses

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, the Joint Economic Committee (JEC) released state-by-state data revealing how much President Donald Trump’s policies -- including his sweeping tariffs, war in Iran, and cuts to health insurance -- have cost American families. The report shows that the average U.S. household has had to pay $4,700 more for goods and services since Trump took office in January 2025, despite promises from his administration to reduce costs and inflation.

In Washington state, the number is even greater; the average family has had to spend an additional $5,300 on goods and services since January 2025. That includes an extra $1,113 on housing costs, $310 on grocery costs, and $294 on electricity. Across the state, Washingtonians have paid an additional $2 billion in gas costs, or about $580 per family.

Below is a breakdown by congressional district of the extra costs to Washington families:

In response, U.S Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and senior member of the Senate Finance Committee, issued the following statement:

“Washington families are being saddled with more than $5,300 in additional costs because of the Trump Administration’s inflationary policies. Every month we see inflation grow faster than the pace of wages, making it harder to afford rent or mortgage payments and more expensive to feed your family or cover household utility bills. The failure to extend Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax credits has put peoples’ lives and health at risk because they are priced out of decent health insurance plans. This is the painful reality facing every household in Washington and across this country that this Administration continues to ignore.”

Sen. Cantwell is a staunch critic of Trump’s reckless policies and has worked to reduce costs for Washingtonians.

Immediately following President Trump’s April 2, 2025, ‘Liberation Day’ tariffs, Senators Cantwell and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) introduced the bipartisan Trade Review Act to reaffirm Congress’s key role in setting and approving U.S. trade policy. The Trade Review Act of 2025, modeled after the War Powers Resolution of 1973, would reestablish limits on the president’s ability to impose unilateral tariffs without the approval of Congress. She has also introduced the Tariff Refund Act of 2026, which would require refunds of Trump’s illegal tariffs, and the End Trump’s Tariffs Act to revoke the president’s global tariffs and curtail his ability to continue waging a unilateral trade war.

She also raised the alarm about how congressional Republicans’ failure to extend the ACA’s Enhanced Premium Tax Credits would hit Washingtonians’ pocketbooks hard – especially those living in rural areas. Sen. Cantwell published a case study showing that a typical Washington state middle-class married couple would see their monthly health insurance bill rise by an average of $1,049 per month.

Sen. Cantwell has also repeatedly voted for resolutions directing President Trump to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran.

title: PHOTOS: Capito Attends Inauguration of Concord University President Bethany Meighen
text:
ATHENS, W.Va. – Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) attended the inauguration ceremony of Dr. Bethany Meighen as the 13th president of Concord University in Athens, W.Va.

The ceremony, which was held at the Alexander Fine Arts Center, brought together university leadership, faculty, students, alumni, and members of the community to celebrate President Meighen and mark a new chapter for the university.

“Concord University has a long history of providing West Virginia students with a quality education and the tools they need to succeed, and I was glad to join the university community for this special occasion,” Senator Capito said. “As Concord begins this exciting new chapter, I look forward to working with President Meighen to build on the university’s successes, expand opportunities for students, and support the next generation of leaders in our state.”

BACKGROUND:

Senator Capito has been a longtime supporter of Concord University and its mission to provide educational opportunities for students across southern West Virginia. Throughout her role on the Senate Appropriations Committee, she has secured more than $11 million in Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) awards to support the university, with a particular focus on expanding health care education and strengthening West Virginia’s health care workforce.

In Fiscal Year 2022 (FY22), Senator Capito secured $2.45 million in CDS funding to help establish Concord’s nursing program, including $1.6 million for facility renovations, technology, and equipment, as well as $850,000 to support personnel and program development. Since its launch, the program has begun graduating nurses prepared to serve communities across West Virginia, helping address critical nursing shortages in the state.

Senator Capito continued her support in FY23, securing $1.05 million to establish Concord’s Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies program.

Most recently, in FY26, she secured an additional $7.5 million to support construction, renovations, and equipment for the expansion of Concord’s Center for Rural Healthcare Workforce Solutions, which will house nursing, physician assistant, and other health care programs.

President Meighen began her tenure as Concord University’s 13th president on July 1, 2025. She brings more than 20 years of experience in higher education leadership, including her previous role as vice president for academic and student affairs for the University of North Carolina System.

title: Senator Collins, Bipartisan Group of Senators Call for Investigation into Starlink Disruptions in Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Susan Collins, Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Jack Reed (D-RI), John Cornyn (R-TX), Chris Coons (D-DE), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) sent a letter to the Department of Defense’s Inspector General, Platte Moring III, calling for an investigation into the disruption of the U.S.-maintained Starshield systems for Ukrainian partners.

In the letter, the Senators highlight how the disruptions to these critical systems put U.S. diplomatic, military, and security personnel in danger and diminished Ukraine’s ability to defend itself. They urge the Inspector General to immediately launch an investigation and determine whether any U.S. officials approved of or had advance knowledge of the disruptions in service. The Senators also request that the Inspector General investigate whether U.S. personnel were unable to reach shelter during Russian attacks that occurred during these disruptions and if immediate corrective measures are being implemented to ensure the safety of American personnel.

“We are particularly alarmed by incidents in which U.S. diplomatic, military, and security personnel were unable to reach designated bunkers during Russian air raids, amid reported disruptions to intelligence-sharing and early-warning capabilities,” the Senators wrote. “We urgently request an Inspector General investigation into these incidents, including whether actions or decisions by the Department of Defense or its contractors contributed to these dangerous circumstances.”

“To use Starshield and Starlink as intended, Ukraine needs access to unlimited speeds, which was its service arrangement prior to this reported restriction,” they continued. “We understand that at least some relevant services are provided through contractual arrangements administered by the U.S. Space Force. Any restrictions on these capabilities, particularly without advance notification, raise serious questions about the Department of Defense’s contractual oversight and its responsibility to ensure continuity of essential services.”

“The United States government has a fundamental obligation to protect American personnel serving overseas. Disruptions to critical intelligence-sharing, threat-warning, or communications capabilities in an active war zone can have life-threatening consequences. The possibility that American personnel were endangered by preventable disruptions, inadequate coordination, or decisions made by their own government demands immediate scrutiny and accountability,” the Senators concluded.
