title: Kelly, Grijalva Blast Trump Administration’s Push for National School Voucher Program
text:
Kelly is leading legislation to repeal the federal voucher program and keep public dollars in public schools

Today, Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07) criticized new Treasury Department regulations that advance a national school voucher program created under Trump’s big bill, warning that Arizona’s experience with universal school vouchers shows the harm done when taxpayer dollars are diverted to private schools without adequate oversight.

The program provides a tax credit of up to $1,700 for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including organizations supporting private and religious schools, which states have limited ability to regulate. The new regulations would also double the credit for married couples.

In response, Kelly introduced the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal this voucher program. Grijalva, alongside Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) introduced the same legislation in the House.

“Arizona is a clear example of the consequences of diverting taxpayer dollars to private school vouchers: fraud, benefits going to families who can already afford private school, and public schools losing funds they desperately need. Not to mention a giant hole blown in our budget,” said Sen. Kelly. “Now, the Trump administration wants to take that same approach nationwide. We should be investing in public schools that serve all kids, not expanding a voucher program that risks more waste and abuse.”

“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Congress must act to ensure taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, rather than subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud.”

Arizona’s universal Empowerment Scholarship Account program now costs taxpayers more than $1 billion annually and has faced repeated allegations of waste, fraud, and abuse.

title: King, Colleagues Push to Protect Reliable Satellite Weather Data
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Angus King (I-ME), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), and Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) are highlighting the life-saving importance of reliable satellite weather data crucial for national security, public safety, and economic resilience across the United States. In a bipartisan letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Dr. Neil Jacobs, the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the senators urge the Department of Defense (DoD) and NOAA to ensure continued access to reliable satellite weather data as the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) nears the end of its service life.

Maine’s climate patterns have grown increasingly erratic in recent years, affecting public safety, economic prospects for farmers, and increased home energy needs to compensate for extreme high and low temperatures. DMSP satellite data has been widely used by weather forecasters, the scientific community, and the military to model weather patterns and environmental conditions. In 2025, the DoD reversed its decision to discontinue sharing critical DMSP data following concerns about the potential impact on global weather forecasting and research. Last month, the U.S. Space Force announced plans to sustain the program through at least 2028, as the government prepares to transition to replacement satellites.

“For decades, DMSP's Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) has supported hurricane forecasting, severe-weather monitoring, polar and sea-ice analysis, and military operations in data-sparse and denied environments. That coverage is now shrinking as legacy polar-orbiting microwave sensors age out” wrote the senators. “To improve and prevent degradation of numerical weather prediction and tactical forecasting, the DoD and NOAA should evaluate the transition across the broader space architecture, including commercial satellite systems that can complement government capabilities.”

The senators concluded that “weather data continuity is essential to national security, public safety, and economic resilience. Extending DMSP is a promising step, and we urge the DoD and NOAA to proactively identify and fill anticipated gaps before legacy degradation or replacement delays create preventable risks.”

Senator King, a member of the Senate Armed Services (SASC) and Intelligence Committees (SSCI), has continued to emphasize the importance of accurate weather prediction and meteorological data for public safety, national security, and economic survival. In 2025, King and his senate colleagues urged the Trump administration to reinstate terminated employees at the National Weather Service (NWS) and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), citing concerns for Maine fishermen as the state faced an unpredictable hurricane season.

For full text of the letter, see below or click HERE.

+++

Dear Secretary Hegseth and Administrator Jacobs:

We write to request more information regarding the status of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP). We are encouraged by the U.S. Space Force’s plan to sustain operations of the three remaining DMSP spacecraft through their functional end of life, currently estimated no earlier than 2028. While this extension buys critical time to cross-calibrate new instruments and prepare for transition to the planned replacement architecture, we are concerned that the systems being brought online may not fully restore the coverage, revisit frequency, and operational access that military and civilian forecasters have relied on with DMSP. We would welcome the opportunity to work with you to identify solutions to improve defense and civil forecasting abilities as DMSP transitions out of service.

For decades, DMSP's Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) has supported hurricane forecasting, severe-weather monitoring, polar and sea-ice analysis, and military operations in data-sparse and denied environments. That coverage is now shrinking as legacy polar-orbiting microwave sensors age out. We support the Department of Defense’s (DoD) investment in the Weather System Follow-on-Microwave (WSF-M) program and urge the resolution of test-resource constraints to reach full operational capability as quickly as possible. WSF-M is designed for microwave imaging, however, so it does not fully replace the vertical atmospheric profiles that SSMIS provides. In addition, the eventual retirement of DMSP leaves the early-morning orbital plane without dedicated U.S. microwave coverage, creating coverage gaps during critical windows of storm intensification.

To improve and prevent degradation of numerical weather prediction (NWP) and tactical forecasting, DoD and NOAA should evaluate the transition across the broader space architecture, including commercial satellite systems that can complement government capabilities. Both DoD and NOAA have recognized the value of commercial space data; establishing clear validation and acquisition pathways now will ensure these capabilities are integrated into operational models before the remaining DMSP sensors degrade or fails. To clarify the transition pathway, we respectfully request a written response within 30 days addressing the following questions:

1. WSF-M Readiness and Access. What is the current operational integration timeline for WSF-M data for military and civilian forecasters? What specific capability or coverage gaps will remain after WSF-M achieves full operational capability?

2. DMSP Data Quality and Sensor Degradation. How are DoD and NOAA monitoring and cross-calibrating performance across the remaining DMSP sensors? What specific degradation or quality thresholds will trigger the down-weighting or exclusion of DMSP data streams prior to 2028? Will DoD continue to share DMSP data with NOAA through the satellites' functional end of life?

3. Commercial Augmentation. What are the current results of NOAA’s Commercial Data Program (CDP) pilots and DoD evaluations regarding commercial microwave sounders, radio occultation instruments, and commercial data assimilation into the NWP models? What procurement, cybersecurity, data-rights, latency, risk factors, and model-integration steps remain before commercial data can be used at scale within operational models? What is the status of developing assessment criteria and validating new forward operators and assimilation tools for commercial data at the Joint Center for Satellite Data Assimilation (JCSDA)?

4. Governance and Resources. Which DoD component is primarily responsible for setting requirements, budgeting, acquiring, validating, and integrating space-based commercial weather data? How are DoD and NOAA coordinating this transition? Are current and planned resources sufficient to sustain transition activities and onboard commercial capabilities prior to DMSP end-of-life?

Weather data continuity is essential to national security, public safety, and economic resilience. Extending DMSP is a promising step, and we urge DoD and NOAA to proactively identify and fill anticipated gaps before legacy degradation or replacement delays create preventable risks. We look forward to your response and to working with you to maintain modern, uninterrupted environmental intelligence.

Sincerely,

###

title: Luján Joins Bipartisan Group of Lawmakers in Introducing Bill to Hold Bankers Who Financed Epstein Accountable
text:
“Epstein Wall Street Records Act” would force federal financial regulators to release Epstein-related records, take action against culpable banks and executives.

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), the original Senate sponsor of the Epstein Files Transparency Act, joined U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee; Congressman Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee; Congressmen Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), Thomas Massie (R-Ky.), and Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.); U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee; and a bipartisan group of lawmakers in introducing the Epstein Wall Street Records Act. The bill seeks accountability for the financial institutions and bank executives that enabled disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation.

Extensive reporting and congressional probes have revealed the degree to which Wall Street empowered Epstein’s crimes. According to The New York Times Magazine, executives at JPMorgan assisted Epstein in evading internal controls meant to intercept suspicious activity, allowing him to avoid scrutiny. A recent investigation by the Senate Finance Committee found “significant evidence that JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, and Bank of America violated federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to screen and report Epstein’s suspicious financial transactions in a timely manner.”

“The survivors of Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes deserve justice, transparency, and accountability,” said Senator Luján. “For too long, powerful banks and financial institutions have dodged accountability in their potential role in enabling Epstein’s abuse and crimes. This bipartisan legislation will help uncover the truth, hold those responsible accountable, and ensure that no one is above the law, regardless of their wealth or influence.”

The Epstein Wall Street Records Act would:

Require federal financial regulators, including the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to disclose supervisory records related to Epstein and his associates to members of Congress and the American people.

Force the financial regulators to investigate Epstein-connected banks and executives for possible banking, securities, or illicit financing violations.

Mandate industry bars and civil penalties for executives who assisted Epstein’s financial operations — as well as potential referrals of criminal violations to the Department of Justice if necessary.

“I have spent the last year calling on Donald Trump’s financial regulators to launch investigations into the big banks and executives who may have enabled Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes,” said Ranking Member Warren. “Since they have failed to act, Congress must. The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people.”

“Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around,” said Ranking Member Garcia. “We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned.”

“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act is about transparency and releasing financial records that are critical to holding the Epstein Class accountable and fighting to get justice for the survivors. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill,” said Representative Khanna.

“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act requires the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the SEC to release their files on Jeffrey Epstein’s money,” said Representative Massie. “The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files. This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”

“Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation left a money trail, and Wall Street has serious questions to answer. Our legislation will force federal regulators to release their records, investigate the banks and executives who may have enabled his crimes, and hold lawbreakers accountable,” said Representative Krishnamoorthi. “Epstein’s survivors deserve the full truth, no matter how powerful or well-connected those responsible may be.”

“For far too long, financial institutions have leveraged their power, influence, and privilege to evade accountability. Their role in enabling Jeffrey Epstein’s decades of sexual exploitation and abuse demands serious scrutiny. That is why World Without Exploitation is proud to support the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026,” said Becca Zipkin, Vice President of Policy and Programs, World Without Exploitation. “We must follow the money to uncover the truth and ensure that the financial institutions that enabled this abuse are held accountable. Survivors deserve transparency, accountability, and the justice they have long been denied.”

The co-sponsors of the Epstein Wall Street Records Act include: Representatives Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Shontel Brown (D-Ohio), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Maxwell Frost (D-Flo.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Tex.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.), Wesley Bell (D-Mo.), Lateefah Simon (D-Cal.), Dave Min (D-Cal.), James Walkinshaw (D-Va.), Christian Menefee (D-Tex.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Rep. Kweisi Mfume (D-Mary.), Rep. Greg Casar (D-Tex.) and Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.).

In July, Senator Luján introduced the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, legislation that gives standing to state attorneys general, the victims of Jeffrey Epstein and his co-conspirators, and members of Congress to challenge the Department of Justice (DOJ) in court for the DOJ’s failure to comply with the disclosure of materials required by the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Senator Luján also introduced and passed into law the original Epstein Files Transparency Act to ensure full transparency for the American people, accountability for those who conspired with Epstein, and justice for victims. Additionally, Senator Luján called for an independent audit and report to Congress about the DOJ’s practices in redacting information of the public release of the Epstein Files. Senator Luján also visited the DOJ to view the unredacted Epstein files.

title: Markey, Warren, Massachusetts Delegation Press DHS OIG to Investigate Inhumane Conditions at Burlington ICE Facility
text:
Letter Text (PDF)

Boston (October 16, 2026) — Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) joined Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and the entire Massachusetts delegation— Representatives Richard Neal (MA-01), Jim McGovern (MA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Katherine Clark (MA-05), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), and Bill Keating (MA-09)—in sending a letter to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Office of the Inspector General (DHS OIG) requesting an independent inspection of the Burlington ICE facility.

Over the past year, reports and evidence from advocates and attorneys show that ICE appears to have transformed the short-term administrative processing center into a de facto detention site—holding people for days and weeks in conditions that threaten their health, safety, and due process rights.

The lawmakers wrote to ICE in June 2025 following alarming reports that ICE was detaining people for days at a time despite the Burlington facility not being designed for overnight detention. ICE denied that it was violating its policies and instead pointed to their own self-inspection completed in March 2025. Members of the Massachusetts delegation have continued to exercise their constitutional responsibilities, making unannounced visits and inspecting the facility. Most recently, on September 8, 2026, Senator Warren and Representative Trahan conducted an unannounced visit to the Burlington facility.

“Days later, we learned via public reports that on the very same day that they visited, a federal judge ordered that ICE release a woman who had spent approximately four days at the facility. That woman, as described above, had recently miscarried and was denied adequate care during her multiday detention. Just one month prior, a 52-year-old woman was reportedly held at Burlington for 20 days,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Congress and the public deserve immediate transparency about ICE’s practices and the secretive use of this Massachusetts building as an unmonitored detention site. Congress has tasked DHS OIG under the 2024 Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act to conduct unannounced inspections of ICE detention facilities—including field offices and holding facilities—to ensure compliance with detention standards. Accordingly, we request that the DHS OIG conduct an inspection of the ICE and ERO Boston Field Office, headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and share its findings with Congress,” the lawmakers concluded.

Senator Markey has worked consistently to hold the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement regime accountable, and to demand transparency from ICE and DHS.

On August 18, Senator Markey led his colleagues in writing to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Dr. Mehmet Oz, and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, demanding that HHS immediately stop unlawfully transferring Medicaid data to DHS and ICE, and that DHS immediately stop unlawfully receiving Medicaid data transfers from HHS.

On August 8, Senator Markey released a comprehensive report, titled Under the Radar II: The Second Trump Administration’s Stealth Attack on the U.S. Immigration System, examining the second Trump administration’s quiet, systematic efforts to dismantle the U.S. immigration system.

On July 28, Senator Markey led 11 colleagues in writing to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, DHS Secretary Mullin, and Defense Secretary Hegseth demanding to know whether the Trump administration plans to deploy armed federal law enforcement officers at polling sites during the November 2026 elections, an escalation of the Administration’s assault on free and fair elections that is clearly meant to intimidate voters.

On July 17, Senator Markey conducted an official unscheduled oversight visit at the ICE field office in Scarborough, Maine, where he demanded answers about the recent, nearby shooting and killing of 26-year-old Johan Sebastián Guerrero by an ICE officer.

On July 16, Senator Markey and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) wrote to the ICE Boston Field Office in Burlington, Massachusetts, demanding a full, transparent, and independent accounting of this killing, given the office’s direct jurisdiction over enforcement operations in Maine and New England.

In January, Senator Markey wrote to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Boston Acting Field Office Director David Wesling, demanding answers about conditions at the ICE field office in Burlington, Massachusetts, and the conduct of ICE agents in the Commonwealth. This letter followed Senator Markey’s previous December letter to Acting Director Wesling, raising concerns about the cruel conditions at the Burlington field office.

title: Massachusetts Wins $130 Million in Federal Funding to Advance West-East Rail
text:
Boston (October 16, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey, and Congressmen Richard Neal (MA-01) and Jim McGovern (MA-02) today announced that Massachusetts has secured $130 million in federal funding for the Springfield Hub Modernization Project. The investment will improve existing passenger rail service along the Connecticut River Line (Knowledge Corridor) and help lay the groundwork for future West-East Rail connections between Boston, Springfield and Albany. The project is part of the state’s Compass Rail vision, centered on Springfield Union Station and building on existing Amtrak Vermonter, Hartford Line and Valley Flyer service.

The Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) was awarded the funding through the Federal Railroad Administration's (FRA) Fiscal Years 2025-2026 Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) grant program to support modernization of the rail infrastructure around Springfield Union Station.

The Springfield Hub Modernization Project is a key phase of the Springfield Area Track Reconfiguration Project. It will upgrade tracks, signals and other infrastructure to address a major rail bottleneck, reduce conflicts between freight and passenger trains, and allow more efficient operations and expanded rail service. This work will improve on-time performance, reduce delays and provide more schedule flexibility for Amtrak Vermonter and Valley Flyer passengers. The project will also create capacity for future passenger rail service while reducing unnecessary train idling, emissions and operating costs.

The funding is another major step in the Healey-Driscoll Administration's efforts to strengthen transportation connections across Western, Central and Eastern Massachusetts, expand access to jobs and economic opportunity, and make West-East Rail a reality.

“Building West-East rail is a once-in a-lifetime investment to connect Massachusetts’ communities and our regional economies like never before. It will mean lower costs, less congestion, and access to opportunity for families across the state,” said Senator Markey. “I’m proud to have secured this $130 million in federal funding alongside Governor Healey, Senator Warren, Congressman Neal and Congressman McGovern, bringing our total federal investment to more than $280 million to date, which will build the track to this more affordable, cleaner, better connected future.”

“This is a major win for Western Massachusetts and a big step forward for West-East Rail,” said Governor Healey. “This $130 million investment in Springfield will help us improve transportation, reduce congestion and connect more communities to jobs, housing and economic opportunity. I'm grateful to Senators Markey and Warren, Congressmen Neal and McGovern, and all of our partners for helping us secure this critical funding and move us closer to expanded passenger rail service across Massachusetts.”

“After announcing a $108 million CRISI grant just three years ago, I'm pleased to join Governor Healey in announcing yet another major milestone with this $130 million investment for West-East Rail,” said Congressman Richard Neal. “The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act was one of the most significant legislative achievements during my time as Chairman of the Ways and Means Committee. In the five years since it was enacted, Massachusetts has received more than $280 million to turn the vision of West-East Rail into reality. Needless to say, with the federal resources we've delivered and the steadfast support of Governor Healey and her administration, we are full steam ahead on a project that will transform regional mobility and economic opportunity in every corner of the Commonwealth.”

“West-East Rail is about making Massachusetts work better for everyone,” said Congressman Jim McGovern. “Completing the project will mean easier commutes, stronger local economies, greater access to jobs and opportunity, and a Commonwealth better connected from Boston to Worcester to Springfield and beyond. This $130 million is a major investment in that future, and I’m thrilled to see us take another important step toward getting West-East Rail done.”

“Governor Healey was a great basketball player in her day as a point guard, and what do point guards do? They distribute the ball in key assists in game winning shots. This is exactly what Governor Healey has done with this $130 million dollar investment to west-east rail and our Union Station,” said Mayor Domenic J. Sarno. “This continues to build momentum for the eventual trains to start running in the near future. I deeply appreciate her continued efforts to support Springfield and my administration to bring equity, and create more economic development, housing, and job opportunities for Springfield and Western Massachusetts. Also, a big shoutout to our Congressman Richie Neal, who has been the big champion for many years to bring Union Station back to life. I thank him again, and my Chief Development Officer Tim Sheehan for his efforts in working closely and in partnership with Congressman Neal and Governor Healey. We continue to move forward on making west-east rail become a reality.”

“Securing $130 million for Springfield rail improvements is an important step toward building a more reliable, connected and efficient passenger rail network,” said Interim Transportation Secretary Phil Eng. “Under the leadership of the Healey-Driscoll Administration, alongside Congressman Richard Neal, Senator Ed Markey, FRA Administrator David Fink, and our entire congressional delegation, we are pursuing every available federal dollar to advance transportation investments that improve quality of life across the Commonwealth. I want to applaud our Rail & Transit Division for making a strong case to our partners and stakeholders that investing in the Commonwealth’s rail network is key to strengthening the region, creating more jobs and access to job opportunities, and conditions for continued economic growth throughout western Massachusetts.”

“We’re pleased to see the consistent federal support of our efforts to grow passenger rail in New England – while maintaining a strong freight rail network—to achieve the promise of a more connected, integrated transportation network that will improve quality of life and generate economic opportunity for residents and visitors alike,” said Rail & Transit Administrator Meredith Slesinger, “We are especially grateful to CSX and Amtrak for their partnership and support.”

“This $130 million award reflects years of collaboration and a sustained commitment to bringing federal resources home to Massachusetts,” said Director of Federal Funds and Infrastructure Quentin Palfrey. “This grant adds to the significant federal funding we’ve already secured to advance West-East Rail, and demonstrates the importance of pursuing every available opportunity to support the Commonwealth’s long-term infrastructure priorities. We’re grateful to our congressional delegation, MassDOT and our federal partners for their continued efforts in moving these transformative projects forward.”

Springfield is a critical transportation hub for our regional rail network, including Union Station which supports passenger rail and regional and intercity bus services. The area is also home to West Springfield Yard, an important freight facility. These improvements will address existing capacity constraints, improve operational efficiency, and support future rail growth.

“West-East Rail is about more than connecting communities — it’s about creating good-paying union jobs, putting skilled workers to work, and building a stronger economy for all of Massachusetts,” said Colton Andrews, President of the Western Mass Building Trades. “This project will create opportunities for working families, support local businesses, and drive economic growth in communities that have been overlooked for far too long. I'm grateful for the leadership of Governor Healey, Secretary Eng and our federal delegation to secure this funding and support union jobs.”

“West-East Rail is an opportunity to put people to create good-paying union jobs and deliver the economic investment our communities deserve," said Robert Butler, Region 1 International Representative for the Northeast Regional Council of the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART) and MBTA Board Member. “From the workers building the rail line to the small businesses and local economies that will benefit from better connections, this project will create lasting opportunities for generations to come. Thank you to Governor Healey, MassDOT and our federal leaders for investing in our workers, our communities and our economy.”

Today's announcement builds on significant progress by the Healey-Driscoll Administration to advance West-East Rail and expand passenger rail service across Massachusetts. The administration previously secured $108 million in federal funding for the Inland Route which will connect Boston-Springfield-New Haven with two daily Amtrak roundtrips in 2030 as well as previous CRISI awards of $36.8 million to advance the design of the Springfield Area Track Reconfiguration Project and $1.75 million for preliminary engineering and environmental work. MassDOT is also advancing the service development plan for Boston-Albany service funded by a $3.5 million FRA Corridor Identification and Development grant.

Additionally, last week, Governor Healey announced a new agreement to advance critical rail infrastructure improvements in Pittsfield that will pave the way for permanent seasonal Berkshire Flyer service and expanded passenger rail in Western Massachusetts.

title: Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley Demand Answers from USPS About Mail Delivery Problems on Oregon Coast
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [10/16/26] – Representative Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley demanded answers from the United States Postal Service (USPS) about significant ongoing mail delivery issues in Astoria and surrounding areas.

The lawmakers noted that the city government, county government, and several downtown businesses are within a few blocks of the Astoria Post Office, but they have not been receiving mail regularly, and some are not receiving mail at all.

“The Astoria Post Office will not hold mail for city officials to pick up, which has caused major disruptions in local commerce and governance,” the Members of Congress wrote. “Payments sent through the mail to the city are being delivered late or not being delivered at all and downtown businesses are experiencing sporadic delivery. We are hearing concerning anecdotes indicating that Amazon packages, which are delivered via USPS in Astoria, are still regularly arriving on time. It’s unacceptable that mail from a billion-dollar retailer is successfully delivered to its destination on time, but mail to and from local small businesses is unreliable.”

The Members of Congress demanded answers to a series of oversight questions and requested that USPS set a time to meet with local elected officials in Clatsop and Columbia counties. They also requested USPS hold an informational session within the next 60 days for residents to discuss the agency’s plans to address these issues.

“Timely, reliable mail delivery is essential infrastructure. Businesses, residents, and local governments rely on USPS for commerce, communication, medications, and more,” the Members of Congress wrote. “This is not an exhaustive list of issues with USPS brought to our attention.”

On October 15, 2026, Representative Bonamici visited the Astoria Post Office in person and asked to speak with the Postmaster to try to find a solution to the late and missing mail. The Postmaster denied the request.

The full letter can be read here and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

We write with significant concerns about the state of operations of the United States Postal Service (USPS) in northwest Oregon. Many community members from across the region are alarmed about inconsistent and unacceptable USPS delivery.

In Astoria, the city government, county government, and several downtown businesses have not been receiving mail regularly, and some are not receiving mail at all. This is happening despite the Astoria Post Office’s central location, just minutes away from Astoria City Hall and the county government building. Additionally, the Astoria Post Office will not hold mail for city officials to pick up which has caused major disruptions in local commerce and governance. Payments sent through the mail to the city are being delivered late or not being delivered at all and downtown businesses are experiencing sporadic delivery. We are hearing concerning anecdotes indicating that Amazon packages, which are delivered via USPS in Astoria, are still regularly arriving on time. It’s unacceptable that mail from a billion-dollar retailer is successfully delivered to its destination on time, but mail to and from local small businesses is unreliable.

The city had scheduled a meeting with the Astoria Postmaster to work to resolve the issue, but the Postmaster did not attend, and the meeting has not been rescheduled.

In Warrenton, USPS has been looking for a new post office location for several years. When the city of Warrenton has asked USPS about location options, USPS directs inquiries to a third-party contractor. This contractor directs all inquiries back to the USPS, resulting in a frustrating cycle where constituents are no closer to getting answers to their questions.

In Gearhart, roughly half the residents in town must travel to the Seaside post office to get their mail which is an unacceptable inconvenience for Gearhart residents. We have been advised that one possible solution involves the placement of a 950-unit cluster box which is exceedingly difficult for a town this size. It is unacceptable that residents of Gearhart cannot receive home delivery or at least have cluster boxes installed at several points throughout the community. The USPS must find a reasonable solution. Furthermore, there are concerning reports that mail pickup is inaccessible on Saturdays to Gearhart residents.

Recently, residents in Gearhart have heard rumors that the Seaside Post office will be remodeled to accommodate permanent mail pick up for Gearhart residents. Though Gearhart residents want a permanent solution to the problems they experience receiving mail, travelling to Seaside is not a practical or acceptable long-term or permanent solution.

Similar issues of concern also exist in Columbia County. In Rainier, roughly a third of the town is not included in the mail route and must use a PO Box. If mail is addressed to a home that is ineligible for home delivery instead of to their PO Box, the mail is not held – it is returned to sender. In a world where people often shop online, many online retailers don’t offer a format for a PO Box address, resulting in orders never reaching their intended addresses. Finally, it is concerning that not every residence is eligible for home delivery in Rainier, considering the small size of the town and well-maintained streets.

Timely, reliable mail delivery is essential infrastructure. Businesses, residents, and local governments rely on USPS for commerce, communication, medications, and more. This is not an exhaustive list of issues with USPS brought to our attention.

We ask that you respond to us in writing within 14 days of receipt of this letter outlining how the USPS will address the issues described and answer the following questions:

When will Astoria downtown businesses, city government, and county government receive regular mail services?

When will USPS announce a new location for the Warrenton post office? What is the current status of the search? Please provide the name and contact information for a specific person who can provide updates to the city.

Why are so many Gearhart residents unable to receive mail at their doors?

What is the plan to deliver mail to residents in Gearhart and/or provide additional PO boxes in Gearhart?

Why are some residents of Rainier, who live within city limits, unable to receive mail at home?

If these issues are caused by post offices being understaffed, what is USPS doing to remedy this?

In light of the volume and gravity of these concerns, we respectfully request that USPS set a time to meet with local elected officials in Clatsop and Columbia counties. We also ask that USPS hold an informational session within the next 60 days for residents to discuss the agency’s plans to address these issues.

Our offices will gladly work with USPS and community leaders to find mutually agreeable times and locations for these meetings.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senator Moody Leads Congressional Effort Urging President to Approve State’s Major Emergency Disaster Declaration in Aftermath of Isaias
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—After a multi-day ground assessment of the damage caused by Hurricane Isaias, Senator Moody is leading congressional efforts urging the President to approve Governor Ron DeSantis’s request for a Major Emergency Disaster Declaration. Senator Moody made multiple trips to communities struck by Isaias with Governor DeSantis to assess damage and listen to local officials about what Florida needs to recover.

Additionally, Senator Moody is working closely with administration and state officials, including Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, to facilitate the quick provision of aid for affected Florida communities.

“Hurricane Isaias wreaked havoc on Florida’s Panhandle and Gulf Coast, and we are working to get those affected relief as quickly as possible. I’m grateful for Gov. DeSantis’s quick and proactive response to the disaster, especially following our assessment of the damage to Panhandle communities in the aftermath of Isaiah. I will continue to work with the governor and have been in constant contact with Sec. Mullin to make sure disaster assistance gets to those in need,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

The major emergency disaster declaration will include both public and individual assistance.

Ahead of Isaias, Senator Moody joined Governor Ron DeSantis to discuss preparedness efforts, including the mobilization of thousands of National Guard members. After the storm, Senator Moody and Governor DeSantis conducted an on-the-ground assessment of some of the damage and thanked Guard members for their response efforts.

Senator Moody continues working to secure long-sought FEMA disaster funds for hard-hit Florida communities. Since taking office, Senator Moody has recovered more than $2.4 billion for Florida.

Senator Moody introduced the TRACK Act (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process, which has now been passed into law.

The TRACK Act mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress.

If Floridians need help with federal agencies in the aftermath of Isaias, Senator Moody’s office can assist—visit Moody.Senate.Gov to learn more.

title: Murphy, Kelly, Schiff Slam Attorney General Blanche for Illegally Allowing Sale of Guns to Teenagers, Increasing Likelihood of School Shootings
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senators Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) on Friday led in a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche demanding answers on the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) decision to break with decades of precedent and unilaterally refuse to enforce a prohibition against the sale of handguns to people under the age of 21.

Murphy has led the charge in the U.S. Senate against the Trump administration’s corrupt dismantling of our nation’s gun laws, to the direct financial benefit of Trump’s friends, family, and donors in the gun industry. Earlier this year, Murphy pressed Blanche on his radical decision to legalize mail-order gun sales, in the process opening up a massive revenue source for a Donald Trump Jr.-owned company widely known as the “Amazon of Guns” - and making it substantially easier for violent criminals to acquire firearms. Murphy, Kelly, and Schiff also fought back against these ATF rule changes through the rulemaking comment process.

The Senators highlighted the enormous risks to public safety if handguns are placed in teens’ hands: “The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.”

The Senators laid out the decades-long, bipartisan consensus on banning gun dealers from selling firearms to teenagers: “Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that ‘it shall be unlawful’ for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21. Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.”

The Senators argued Blanche’s decision is another authoritarian power grab over the judicial branch and Congress: “The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has ‘deeply divided members of the federal bench.’ Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.”

The Senators concluded by requesting Blanche provide the following information on the authority and research supporting his decision:

A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

Murphy, Kelly, and Schiff were joined by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.).

A full transcript of the letter is available below. A copy of the letter is available here.

Dear Attorney General Blanche:

We write regarding the U.S. Department of Justice’s (the Department) decision to cease enforcement of longstanding federal restrictions on the sale of handguns to individuals under the age of 21 by federally licensed firearms dealers (FFLs). This significant change in federal enforcement policy raises serious questions about the Department’s legal justification, and we request information regarding the analysis underlying its decision.

On September 18, 2026, the Department’s Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) published a legal opinion concluding that 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1)—the federal prohibition on FFLs selling handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds—violate the Second Amendment, and that federal prosecutors may no longer prosecute FFLs that sell handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds who are not otherwise prohibited from gun possession.[1] Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that “it shall be unlawful” for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21.[2] Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.

The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has “deeply divided members of the federal bench.” Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.

The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.

The Department’s decision to unilaterally cease enforcement of this provision of law raises serious questions and concerns. Thus, we request the Department provide:

A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

Please provide the requested information and documents by November 16, 2026.

title: Murray & Schrier Visit Washington State Fire Training Academy, Affirm Commitment to Invest in Wildfire Prevention and Response
text:
Murray: “When we invest in fire preparedness, we save lives and communities. I will not stop pushing back hard for Washington state, our public lands, and for wildfire preparedness, prevention, and safety.”

***PHOTOS AND B-ROLL HERE***

North Bend, WA — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and U.S. Representative Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) met with leaders and firefighters from Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol at the Washington State Fire Training Academy, to tour their facilities and hear about what additional federal resources and policies could better support on-the-ground efforts to prevent and respond to wildfires and structural fires.

The lawmakers were joined by: Dave Upthegrove, Commissioner of Public Lands at Washington State Department of Natural Resources (DNR); Chad Cross, State Fire Marshal; Chief John R. Batiste, Washington State Patrol (WSP); and leaders from the Washington State Fire Academy, law enforcement, and DNR.

“Washington state just suffered one of the worst wildfire seasons in history. That’s why I came here to listen to the people who managed these fires and understand what they need to continue this vital work. And we are hearing more and more now that wildfire season is year-round—so we need to be preparing for it that way as well,” said Senator Murray. “Now we aren’t just facing more environmental threats that worsen wildfires, we are also facing a President who has severely weakened the Forest Service and other critical agencies—from pushing out thousands of critical staff, blocking funding for crucial programs, and chaotically changing rules and procedures on a dime—Trump has left us worse off and less prepared to prevent future wildfires. But I am fighting back, tearing up his budget, and making sure we protect funding for the Forest Service and USDA so they can continue doing the hard work to prevent and fight wildfires. When we invest in fire preparedness, we save lives and communities. The Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol do incredible work to keep people safe. For my part, I will not stop pushing back hard for Washington state, our public lands, and for wildfire preparedness, prevention, and safety.”

“Communities in the Eighth District and across Washington state are reeling from the damage of this season’s devastating wildfires that threatened lives, property, and businesses,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I was grateful to join Senator Murray and local leaders today to thank our first responders and discuss the federal resources our state needs to recover from and prevent catastrophic fires. In Congress, I’ll keep supporting our firefighters, bolstering local response efforts, and expanding fire prevention.”

“I appreciate Senator Murray visiting DNR’s fire academy to highlight the need for more investment and resources to help us prepare for and tackle wildfires,” said Washington State Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove. “The Federal government is a crucial partner, and I look forward to supporting Senator Murray as she fights to ensure critical agencies like the US Forest Service have the funding they need to join DNR in supporting communities, improving forest health, and responding to wildfires.”

Supporting investments in wildfire prevention and response continues to be a top priority for Senator Murray, particularly as she negotiates this year’s government funding bills. Murray has been outspoken against the Trump administration’s efforts to undermine much of the federal workforce that supports wildfire prevention and response work year-round. As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, in the Interior and Environment appropriations bill for Fiscal Year 2026, which Senator Murray negotiated and helped pass into law, Murray worked to include essential investments in wildfire preparedness and suppression. In FY26, she secured $6.13 billion for the U.S. Forest Service, with separate additional funding for the Wildfire Suppression Operations Reserve. The bill rejected the steep $1.4 billion cut to the Forest Service’s non-fire budget proposed by President Trump and provides funding for the Forest Service to improve forest restoration and fire risk reduction efforts on federal lands. The FY26 bill also fully funds essential wildfire preparedness and suppression efforts by providing $4.25 billion for wildfire suppression, of which $2.85 billion is for the Wildfire Suppression Operations Reserve Fund and continues to support the increased pay for federal firefighters enacted into law last year. Senator Murray continues to push back against Trump’s FY27 budget request, to protect our public lands.

Yesterday, Senator Murray visited the Confederated Colville Tribes to hear their concerns following wildfire season and discuss next steps of recovery after the August wildfires devastated the community. In August, following the devastating Spokane Complex Fires, Senator Murray visited families, first responders, and community leaders in Spokane to hear about the ongoing debris clean up and recovery efforts, and witness firsthand the state of local communities that were hit hard. Senator Murray also led Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in letters to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s requests for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance and Public Assistance.
