title: Rep. Aguilar Highlights How the Trump Administration’s Attacks on Head Start Will Hurt Inland Empire Kids
text:
The Trump administration is pushing for changes that will make it harder for children to learn, communicate with teachers or access the Head Start program altogether

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) held a press conference highlighting how the Trump administration’s attacks on Head Start will hurt children, parents and teachers in the Inland Empire. The administration’s proposed changes threaten to take away children’s health and support services, force bilingual children into English-only classrooms, limit enrollment for children from the neediest families and reduce training and support for teachers.

In San Bernardino County, many children come from working-class or lower-income families, are bilingual, or face challenges like homelessness and parents’ job instability. These proposed changes would harm these children the most, making it harder to learn, communicate and get the healthcare they need. You can watch the full video of the press conference here and find photos from the event above and here.

“When I worked as a Head Start teacher’s aide, I saw firsthand how this program invests in every aspect of childhood and gives kids a place to learn, grow and thrive,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “Now, Trump and Republicans are turning their backs on our nation’s most vulnerable children and their teachers by gutting federal support for important Head Start services. Here in the Inland Empire, that means kids will struggle to get health screenings, talk to their teachers or have a place to learn while their parents work to make ends meet. That’s not fair to our children or to the teachers who show up for them every day. I’ll keep fighting to reverse these harmful changes so every family in our region can build brighter futures.”

“The proposed federal overhauls to Head Start are a direct threat to our children and families,” said Stacie Perez, President and CEO, Volunteers of America Southwest. “Right here in San Bernardino, we see firsthand how high-quality early childcare breaks the cycle of poverty. When you eliminate dual-language frameworks or weaken classroom protections, you don’t just disrupt education—you directly derail a parent’s ability to work and achieve economic stability. We stand firmly with Congressman Aguilar in rejecting these rollbacks to protect the pipeline of upward mobility for our community.”

title: Ansari, Stanton, and Grijalva Statement on Suspicious Letters Sent to Arizona Offices
text:
PHOENIX – Today, U.S. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) released the following joint statement:

“This weekend, the FBI Phoenix Field Office and the Arizona Department of Homeland Security informed us that suspicious letters had been sent to our offices. Similar letters, many containing unknown substances, have been mailed to elected officials across the country.

The FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating. We’re grateful to law enforcement for acting quickly and keeping our staff and communities safe.

We will not be intimidated and we’ll keep doing the work that Arizonans elected us to do.”

The letters to Reps. Ansari and Grijalva were sent to former office addresses. The letter addressed to Rep. Stanton’s Mesa office was intercepted before delivery.

title: Bacon, Costa Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Defense Innovation Through Partnership with Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Representatives Don Bacon (NE-02), Jim Costa (CA-21), Wesley Bell (MO-01), and Mike Quigley (IL-05) introduced the bipartisan H.R. 10772 Frontline Innovation Act. This legislation will authorize the Department of Defense’s Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, allowing the United States to benefit directly from innovations developed and refined on the battlefield in Ukraine.

Ukraine has emerged as a leader in developing modern defense technologies as it continues to defend itself against Russia’s invasion. Ukrainian companies are developing advanced drones, unmanned systems, and electronic warfare tools that are being tested and improved under real combat conditions against a determined adversary. These innovations offer valuable opportunities to strengthen U.S. defense capabilities while supporting Ukraine’s ongoing efforts to defend its sovereignty.

However, existing U.S. defense cooperation agreements have not kept pace with these technological advancements. The last U.S.-Ukraine agreement on exchanging military research and development information dates back to 2001. Although the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) has worked with the Ukrainian government and firms since 2023, legal barriers currently limit its ability to expand these partnerships and invest directly in Ukrainian defense technologies.

“Ukraine is fighting for its survival against Putin’s illegal invasion, and its forces have been forced to innovate at an extraordinary pace,” said Rep. Bacon. “They are proving new drones, unmanned systems and electronic warfare capabilities against Russia in real combat, and our military should be learning from that experience. I’m joining Rep. Costa in introducing the bipartisan Frontline Innovation Act to help bring battlefield-proven technologies into our own defense innovation system and strengthen our military while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight for freedom.”

“Ukraine has demonstrated extraordinary resilience in the face of Russia’s aggression, and Ukrainians are innovating and developing new defense technologies under some of the most challenging conditions imaginable,” said Congressman Costa. “This bipartisan bill will help strengthen our national security by investing in technologies that have been tested on the battlefield, while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight to defend its sovereignty.”

"Standing with Ukraine is in America’s own interest, and the Frontline Innovation Act is a smart, practical way to do it. Every day, Ukrainian forces are developing and testing new technologies on the battlefield, providing valuable lessons that can help make our own servicemembers safer and prepared for the challenges of tomorrow,” said Rep. Bell. "As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know our military must have the best tools and technology, and after my recent trip to Ukraine, I can see how much Ukrainian battlefield innovation has to offer. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan legislation to learn from our partners’ battlefield experience and help them continue defending their freedom.”

"When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the entire world expected Kyiv to fall within days. Instead, the strength, resilience, and innovation of Ukrainians and the Ukrainian military have kept the capitol free for over four years. The United States should learn from Ukraine's battlefield innovation to strengthen and modernize our own military to ensure our forces are prepared for a new generation of threats," said Rep. Quigley, a Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus. "The Frontline Innovation Act would enable the U.S. military to accelerate defense innovation while continuing to support Ukraine as a critical ally."

The Frontline Innovation Act would:

Expand defense cooperation by authorizing the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, notwithstanding any other provision of law.

Strengthen U.S. defense capabilities by directing DIU to ensure the United States benefits from technologies developed and refined through Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s invasion.

Allow technology proven in combat to reach the U.S. military faster while creating new opportunities for the American defense industrial base to gain new partners and a larger market.

Support Ukraine through increased investment and cooperation, allowing both countries to collaborate on developing the next generation of defense capabilities.

title: Rep. Balint Statement on Suspicious Letter Intended for Vermont Office
text:
BRATTLEBORO, VT — Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL) released the following statement after being notified by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service of a letter intended for her office that is being handled by authorities:

“We have been notified by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service that a letter intended for our office may contain a suspicious substance. We are working closely with postal inspectors and the appropriate law enforcement agencies to ensure the letter is safely intercepted and tested,” said Rep. Balint. “Threats against public servants are serious, and the safety of my staff and the Vermonters we serve is my priority. We are grateful to the postal inspectors and law enforcement officials working to address these incidents, and we will continue serving Vermonters while the investigation proceeds.”

The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is coordinating the safe handling and testing of the letter, with the results and any further investigation to be handled by the appropriate federal authorities.

Rep. Balint’s office is coordinating with law enforcement and will share additional information if or when appropriate.

title: Congressman Baumgartner Welcomes New Funding for the ‘Feed the Future’ Innovation Lab at WSU for Animal Health Research
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, the State Department announced Washington State University was selected as one of eight Feed the Future Innovation Labs to receive new funding for its research on animal health. Through these Innovation Labs, the Department of State is investing in research that draws upon the strength of American universities to advance solutions that reduce global hunger, poverty, and malnutrition.

“Animal diseases, like the New World screwworm, threaten farmers’ livelihoods, our food supply and the prices families pay at the grocery store. I welcome the State Department’s long-term, strategic investment in advancing research that protects livestock and strengths food security,” said Congressman Micheal Baumgartner (WA-05), acknowledging Washington State University’s central role in the initiative.

The Innovation Labs are led by American land-grant universities, with links to 24 additional research and academic institutions in the United States and internationally. Auburn University, University of Mississippi, Kansas State University, the University of Georgia, the University of Hawaii and the University of Florida round out the research institutions recognized by the Department of State, today.

“Every dollar invested in Innovation Labs and in agricultural research strengthens U.S. farmers and exporters,” Baumagartner continued. “This is the sort of strategic aid that extends U.S. influence abroad and I congratulate Secretary Rubio for his leadership on modernizing U.S. foreign assistance.”

title: Congressman Baumgartner’s Statement on the Dell’s $250 Contribution into Childhood Investment Accounts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Michael Baumgartner (WA-05) released a statement on Michael and Susan Dell’s $250 contributions to Childhood Investments Accounts. Congress created these accounts in 2025 and they began receiving the Dell’s charitable deposits on Friday, October 9. Also known as “Trump Accounts,” Congress designed these tax-advantaged investment accounts to help families build long-term savings for children.

“I want parents to know what’s available to their children and how these accounts work,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “The Dell family’s generous contribution is separate from other funds that may be deposited into a Childhood Investment Account, including federal contributions for eligible newborns. I encourage families to check their child’s account and learn more about the options available to them by accessing official websites.”

More than 70 million children under 18 were enrolled in these new accounts, which can receive contributions from the federal government, family members, employers, and other contributors. But parents need to claim the accounts first. Michael and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion (non-taxpayer dollars) to provide $250 contributions to 25 million eligible children born between 2016 and 2024. The contributions were distributed based on zip code median family income, beginning with the lowest-income zip codes and expanding until 25 million eligible children were reached. All eligible children living on military bases, including Fairchild Airforce Base, were also included.

“Childhood Investment Accounts give families an opportunity to begin building financial resources from an early age,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “I was proud to vote for these accounts in Congress because they give working families another tool to save for their children’s future. By combining an initial federal contribution for eligible children with the ability to receive additional investments over time, we can help families build long-term savings and give children a stronger financial foundation.”

“My staff estimates that the the Dell family’s $250 contribution is available to eligible children in roughly 86% of zip codes fully or partially within Washington’s 5th District, offering over 75,000 of Eastern Washington kids a head start on college, technical training, opening a business or other investments for the future,” he continued.

Parents should visit the official U.S. Government Website to learn more about their child’s account, and verify at “Invest America” to see if their zip code qualifies for the Dell family’s $250 contribution.

title: Congressman Andy Biggs Calls on Department of War to Unlock Arizona's Copper Resources to Strengthen National Security
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA –U.S. Congressman Andy Biggs (AZ-05), alongside Arizona Congressmen Paul Gosar (AZ-09) and Eli Crane (AZ-02), sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth urging the Department of War to identify opportunities to expand domestic copper mining, processing, refining, and recycling on the approximately 3.12 million acres of defense land under its management in Arizona.

Arizona is the nation's leading copper-producing state, accounting for approximately 70 percent of all copper mined in the United States. With its abundant mineral deposits, skilled workforce, established infrastructure, and significant military presence, the state is uniquely positioned to play a central role in securing America's defense-related mineral needs.

"Arizona has been blessed with an abundance of natural resources that are essential to America's economic prosperity and national security," said Congressman Biggs. "For too long, our country has allowed unnecessary barriers and an overreliance on foreign supply chains to undermine our ability to produce the critical materials our military needs. Arizona already leads in copper production, and we have a tremendous opportunity to build on that strength. We should be looking at every responsible avenue to expand domestic production, unleash American industry, and ensure our military has a reliable supply of the resources necessary to defend our citizens and freedoms."

The letter specifically requests that the Department of War:

Identify suitable defense lands in Arizona that could support copper and other critical mineral mining, processing, and refining while remaining consistent with military training, testing, and readiness requirements.

Evaluate existing federal authorities, programs, partnerships, and investments that could accelerate domestic mineral production and processing, while identifying any additional legislative action Congress should consider.

Provide a briefing to the lawmakers within 90 days detailing potential sites and projects, available resources, and outstanding infrastructure or permitting requirements.

The lawmakers emphasized that utilizing Arizona's resources would help advance the administration's national security priorities while creating opportunities for American workers and strengthening domestic industrial capacity.

title: Carbajal Demands DHS Accountability Over Reports of Foreign Vessels Transporting Cargo Without Required Disclosures Under Jones Act Waiver
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), Top Democrat of the House Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin raising concerns over the department's administration and oversight of Jones Act waivers.

Carbajal’s inquiry follows recent reports indicating that foreign-flagged vessels have transported more than $40 million in petroleum products between U.S. ports without required disclosures, raising critical questions about whether federal tax, labor, and immigration laws are being properly enforced on foreign operators.

“I am writing to express concern regarding the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) administration and oversight of Jones Act waivers, particularly in light of recent reporting that foreign-flagged vessels have transported more than $40 million in petroleum products between U.S. ports without required disclosures, among other potential violations,” wrote Rep. Carbajal. “These reports raise significant questions about whether DHS and its component agencies are adequately enforcing federal law with respect to foreign vessels operating in U.S. domestic commerce.”

The full letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin:

I am writing to express concern regarding the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) administration and oversight of Jones Act waivers, particularly in light of recent reporting that foreign-flagged vessels have transported more than $40 million in petroleum products between U.S. ports without required disclosures, among other potential violations. These reports raise significant questions about whether DHS and its component agencies are adequately enforcing federal law with respect to foreign vessels operating in U.S. domestic commerce.

As you know, the Jones Act generally prohibits the transportation of merchandise between U.S. points unless a vessel is U.S.-owned, U.S.-documented, and U.S.-built. Recent waivers have been issued under 46 U.S.C. § 501(a), which permits the waiver of certain navigation and vessel-inspection laws only when necessary in the interest of national defense to address an immediate adverse effect on military operations. The statute does not, however, provide an exemption from any other federal requirements applicable to foreign vessels, vessel owners, operators, employers, or crewmembers.

Publicly available information indicates that more than 25 domestic voyages by foreign-flagged vessels have been completed under the current waiver, with some vessels conducting multiple voyages. Given the scale and duration of this activity, there must be a clear framework for ensuring continued compliance with federal law.

Recent IRS guidance further establishes that income earned by foreign corporations from operating vessels between U.S. ports under a Jones Act waiver constitutes domestic-source income and is not eligible for the international shipping exclusion under Section 883 of the Internal Revenue Code or related treaty benefits. This raises additional questions about DHS’s role in facilitating and enforcing compliance with federal tax requirements.

Accordingly, I respectfully request the following information:

Tax compliance. What steps has DHS taken, independently or in coordination with the Department of the Treasury and IRS, to ensure compliance with applicable federal tax requirements by foreign vessel owners, operators, charterers, and other waiver users? Has DHS provided Treasury or IRS with information identifying waiver users, vessel owners and operators, charterers, cargo interests, voyage dates, cargo movements, or other information necessary to identify potential tax obligations? Please describe the information provided, the frequency of transmission, and any related interagency agreements or procedures.

Immigration and crewmember status. Federal regulations generally provide that nonimmigrant crewmen admitted in D status may not be employed in connection with domestic movements of a vessel. How is DHS/CBP interpreting and applying this restriction to foreign officers and crewmembers serving aboard vessels engaged in domestic transportation under the waiver? What immigration classifications or other legal authorities permit such service? Has DHS/CBP identified instances in which a crewmember’s immigration status was inconsistent with domestic service, or in which a crewmember absconded? If so, what corrective or enforcement actions were taken? Please provide any guidance, memoranda, legal opinions, or internal directives addressing these issues.

Other federal requirements. Please describe the steps DHS and its component agencies have taken to ensure compliance with other applicable federal requirements, including maritime security, environmental protection, vessel safety and inspection, wage and hour, labor and employment, payroll and withholding taxes, harbor maintenance, customs, and any other requirements applicable to foreign vessels operating between U.S. points.

Interagency coordination and oversight. Please provide a description of all coordination between DHS and the Departments of Defense, Transportation, and Treasury; the IRS; U.S. Coast Guard; and other relevant agencies concerning operations under the waiver, including coordination regarding compliance with federal law and whether the statutory requirements for continued waiver authority remain satisfied.

The Administration has now authorized the waiver for an aggregate period of approximately 250 days, making oversight particularly important. Congress has a responsibility to ensure that a national-defense waiver is not being treated as a broader exemption from federal law. I therefore request a response addressing the matters above by October 31, 2026.

Background

Carbajal serves as Ranking Member of the House Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee.

title: REPS. CLARKE, GRIJALVA LEAD 63 MEMBERS OF CONGRESS IN URGING USCIS TO ADDRESS PROCESSING BACKLOG COSTING LAWFULLY-PRESENT IMMIGRANTS THEIR HEALTHCARE
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

October 19, 2026

MEDIA CONTACT:

e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov

c: 202.913.0126

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke and Adelita S. Grijalva, alongside 61 Members of Congress, sent a letter urging U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to immediately expedite pending green card applications for immigrants who have lost or are at risk of losing Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Medicare, and Affordable Care Act premium credits as a result of new eligibility restrictions under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) that went into effect on October 1st.

The lawmakers warn that thousands of lawfully-present immigrants, including refugees, asylum recipients, and survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking, could lose access to critical healthcare while waiting for USCIS to process their green card applications providing permanent residency. More than 281,000 lawfully present immigrants across nine states and Washington, D.C., were identified as facing the loss of Medicaid coverage beginning October 1. Nationwide, the Congressional Budget Office estimates that 1.4 million lawfully present immigrants will become uninsured by 2034 under Republicans’ healthcare eligibility restrictions.

The letter highlights the case of an Arizona woman with stage four metastatic breast cancer who lost her Medicaid coverage on October 1. Although she is lawfully present in the United States, delays in processing her green card application have left her without coverage for the chemotherapy she depends on to survive.

The lawmakers argue that eligible applicants should not lose access to healthcare because their immigration applications are caught in processing backlogs.

“Because Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs), that have already waited any required time, retain federal eligibility under health law, these individuals are losing their health insurance simply because they are trapped in a bureaucratic bottleneck. This is a backlog crisis that lies within the administrative capabilities of USCIS to resolve and the agency cannot allow its own administrative delays to cause catastrophic gaps in their healthcare,” wrote the Members.

They also warn that these delays could increase healthcare costs for federal and state governments by forcing patients to forgo preventive treatment until their conditions become more severe.

In their letter, the lawmakers call on USCIS to take three immediate steps:

Establish an emergency expedited processing pathway for Form I-485 adjustment of status applications for individuals who face the imminent loss of healthcare coverage because their applications remain pending.

Clarify expedited processing criteria to explicitly recognize the imminent loss of federal or state healthcare coverage as grounds for expedited processing under severe financial loss or humanitarian considerations.

Coordinate with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and state agencies to provide guidance on delaying coverage terminations for individuals with pending adjustment of status applications.

“Needless red tape should never be the determinant between life and death,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “While thousands of immigrant American families remain stuck in a bureaucratic backlog that risks ripping their healthcare out from under them, USCIS has a moral obligation to ensure all those caught in its processing bottleneck do not suffer due to circumstances beyond their control. Government inefficiencies are not the fault of immigrant communities, and they deserve better than to suffer the consequences of them.”

“In Arizona, more than 20,000 lawfully present refugees and immigrants are at risk of losing their healthcare due to USCIS processing bottlenecks, including a woman with stage-four breast cancer and a nine-year-old boy with epilepsy who depends on Medicaid to attend school,” said Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva. “These cuts, thanks to Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, are forcing Arizona families to choose between their health and their financial security. USCIS needs to act with urgency so that their bureaucratic delays do not cost people their lives.”

title: Cline Urges CMS to Improve Access to Rural Healthcare in Virginia’s 6th District
text:
FINCASTLE, VA – On September 22, 2026, Congressman Ben Cline (VA-06) sent a letter to Center for Medicare and Medicaid Administrator Mehmet Oz, urging the agency to reconsider the non-rural designations in Virginia’s Sixth District so more rural communities have the opportunity to receive funding to improve access to healthcare through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP).

“Expanding access to quality health care in rural Virginia is one of my top priorities,” said Rep. Cline. “I’m fighting to ensure families across the Shenandoah and Roanoke Valleys can get the care they need close to home. Too many rural communities face barriers to care, including long travel distances, limited transportation, and gaps in broadband access. The Rural Health Transformation Program is an important opportunity to strengthen rural health care systems, support innovative solutions, and improve access to care for underserved communities. I will continue working to ensure rural communities in Virginia’s 6th District have the resources and support they need to deliver timely, quality care to the people they serve.”

BACKGROUND: H.R. 1, the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, created the RHTP for states to receive funding to expand and enhance rural health care. On August 28, 2026, the Administration announced that Virginia was awarded $122 million to transform rural healthcare across Virginia. However, RHTP funding will be restricted to rural localities to ensure appropriate application of resources, and the current Center for Medicare and Medicaid’s definition does not include some counties and cities in Virginia’s Sixth District that should be eligible for RHTP funding.

title: Cline Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Streamline Copyright Registration for Photographers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Ben Cline (VA-06), alongside Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), introduced the Visual Artists Copyright Reform Act (VACRA), bipartisan legislation aimed at making copyright registration more affordable and accessible for photographers and small businesses who register large volumes of their work.

The legislation would modernize the copyright registration process at the U.S. Copyright Office, making it more affordable and efficient for visual artists who need to register large volumes of their work. By reducing unnecessary costs and administrative burdens, VACRA would help small businesses protect their intellectual property while spending more time doing what they do best.

Quote Attributable to Congressman Ben Cline (VA-06):

“Photographers deserve a straightforward, affordable way to protect the work they produce,” said Rep. Cline. “The current copyright registration process can be costly and burdensome, particularly for small businesses who create and register work in large volumes. This legislation would help modernize that process, strengthen protections for creators, and ensure they have the tools they need to safeguard their work and continue contributing to our economy and culture.”

Quote Attributable to Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37):

“Photographers and visual artists are vital to our creative world," said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. "I am proud to partner with Rep. Cline on these commonsense reforms to copyright law to allow for a more complete public registry of their integral works. This would ensure that photographers and all visual artists are full and effective participants in our copyright system. I’m proud to represent a vibrant district at the heart of America’s creative and entertainment economy and advance policies that protect creative rights."

Quote Attributable to Angela Kurkian, CEO, Professional Photographers of America:

"PPA thanks Representatives Ben Cline and Sydney Kamlager-Dove for their leadership, for introducing The Visual Artists Copyright Reform Act (VACRA) in the House, and we are proud to stand with our coalition partners in support of this important reform. When creators can meaningfully protect their work, they can continue creating,” said Angela Kurkian.

Quote Attributable to Thomas Maddrey, CEO, American Society of Media Photographers:

"The American Society of Media Photographers (ASMP) celebrates the leadership shown by Rep. Cline and Rep. Kamlager-Dove in introducing VACRA. This bill is designed to help the smallest of small businesses, which form the core engine powering our creative ecosystem. By introducing VACRA, Reps. Cline and Kamlager-Dove demonstrate their support for our photographers, artists, and all visual creators, and we thank them,” said Thomas Maddrey.

Quote Attributable to Melanie Porter, COO, ASMP, North American Nature Photography Association:

"Photography brings the beauty of the natural world to all communities. Through their introduction of VACRA, Reps. Cline and Kamlager-Dove show that breaking down barriers preventing visual artists from protecting their works and livelihoods is important and valuable. The North American Nature Photography Association (NANPA) applauds the support shown to our creative communities nationwide and thanks Reps. Cline and Kamlager-Dove for making this announcement. It would directly affect our 7,500+ Members of ASMP & NANPA and the millions of other visual creators across the country," said Melanie Porter.

Quote Attributable to Alex Garcia, President, National Press Photographers Association:

“The National Press Photographers Association (NPPA) strongly supports the Visual Artists Copyright Reform Act and thanks Representatives Ben Cline and Sydney Kamlager-Dove for their bipartisan leadership. Visual journalists routinely create thousands of images while documenting events of public importance, yet the cost and complexity of copyright registration can make protecting that work impractical. VACRA would modernize registration to better reflect how photographers work, helping them protect their livelihoods and sustain the visual journalism that informs our communities,” said Alex Garcia.

Quote Attributable to Stephanie Hayes, Executive Director, School Photographers of America:

“School Photographers of America supports VACRA and its goal of making copyright protection more accessible and practical for professional photographers. School photography companies create enormous volumes of images while relying primarily on families’ voluntary purchases, making workable copyright registration options especially important to our industry. We are grateful to the bill’s sponsors and Professional Photographers of America for advancing this effort and recognizing the needs of high-volume creators,” said Stephanie Hayes.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions
text:
NORWICH, CT — Today, U.S. Representatives John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:

“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.

“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.

“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”

title: Crow Statement on Suspicious Letter at Aurora Congressional Office
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO) issued the following statement after his congressional office in Aurora, Colorado, received a suspicious letter:

“Earlier today, my congressional office in Aurora received a letter with a suspicious substance. This appears to be one of many unfortunate instances across the country where congressional offices have received mail containing unknown, suspicious substances.

“My staff is safe, and our district office remains open for those who need assistance. Attempts to intimidate me or my team will not stop our work on behalf of Coloradans.

“I want to thank the FBI, U.S. Capitol Police, Aurora Police Department, and other law enforcement for swiftly working to investigate this matter and keeping everyone safe.”

###

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:

“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.

“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.

“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”

title: Congressman Don Davis Highlights Over $4 Million Recovered for Eastern North Carolina Families
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced that his office has recovered $4,044,144 for constituents from federal agencies so far in 2026. It is an increase of more than $1.58 million since June. Funds recovered include veterans' benefits, Social Security payments, tax refunds, Medicare and Medicaid issues, federal retirement benefits, and other cases where constituents needed assistance navigating the federal government.

"Our number one priority at all times is to put eastern North Carolina first so that our hard-working families receive the assistance and benefits that they have worked for. It's not just about doing paperwork, but we must cut through the red tape of the federal government," said Congressman Don Davis. "It's a way to deliver actual, life-changing help to our veterans, seniors, and families when they need it most."

Although the office cannot guarantee a specific outcome, staff members are available to help residents navigate federal agencies, obtain information about their case, and work to resolve issues related to federal programs, benefits, and services. Residents of North Carolina's First Congressional District who need help with a federal agency can visit dondavis.house.gov/services/help-federal-agency or call (252) 999-7600.

title: Rep. Foushee Introduces Resolution Recognizing Hunter Syndrome Awareness Week
text:
DURHAM, NC (October 19, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced a resolution designating the third week of October as National Hunter Syndrome Awareness Week, to reaffirm the commitment to increasing awareness and funding for research and treatments for Hunter syndrome.

“As Hunter syndrome continues to affect thousands of people across the globe, it is critical that Congress reaffirms our commitment to researching treatments for this disease which still has no cure,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “As modern medicine continues to develop, Congress has an opportunity to take steps towards advancing lifesaving treatment options for those suffering from this disease. I am proud to introduce this resolution recognizing National Hunter Syndrome Awareness Week to reaffirm our commitment to supporting those living with Hunter syndrome across the globe.”

Hunter syndrome is a rare genetic disorder which prevents the body from properly breaking down sugar molecules, causing progressive, irreversible damage to organs and muscle tissue. This disease affects approximately 500 boys in the United States alone, and nearly 2,000 worldwide.

title: Congressman Gallagher Urges FBI to Take Action Against Illegal Marijuana Grows in Northern California
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman James Gallagher (CA‑01) is calling on Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel to launch a coordinated federal investigation into the transnational criminal organizations operating thousands of illegal marijuana grows across Siskiyou and Shasta Counties. In a detailed letter sent today, Gallagher urged the FBI to work directly with local sheriffs, Homeland Security Investigations, and EPA Region 9 to dismantle the sprawling illicit industry that has overtaken parts of rural Northern California.

Illegal marijuana cultivation has rapidly expanded across rural Northern California as entire rural properties are now covered with rows of makeshift, plastic‑covered “hoop houses,” often relying on groundwater hauled in from nearby wells. Residents have faced depleted water supplies, threats to their safety, and contamination risks to agricultural land. A 2022 Siskiyou County Civil Grand Jury report estimated 5,000 large‑scale illegal cultivation sites, while more recent reporting suggests up to 7,000 illegal growers in the Mount Shasta Vista subdivision alone, potentially producing up to $2 billion annually.

“We can’t stand idly by as these criminals poison our water, destroy our land, and threaten the safety of rural families,” said Congressman Gallagher. “These illegal marijuana grows are run by transnational criminal organizations, some with suspected foreign financing, and they have no place in Northern California. The FBI must act now to support our sheriffs and bring these networks to justice.”

Illegal cultivation has also been documented on federal land, including the Shasta‑Trinity National Forest. Despite sustained enforcement efforts, the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office reported eradicating more than 332,000 illegal marijuana plants and seizing over 54,000 pounds of processed marijuana in 2025 alone.

Gallagher’s letter raises serious concerns that Chinese organized‑crime networks may be financing and directing portions of these operations. Investigators have identified cultivation properties owned by individuals outside the county, while on‑site managers often have no ownership interest, patterns consistent with foreign‑financed schemes uncovered elsewhere in California. A 2018 federal investigation in the Sacramento region revealed an organized marijuana trafficking network funded by wire transfers from China’s Fujian Province and supported by straw purchasers, resulting in civil forfeiture actions against more than 100 properties.

Compounding the threat is the widespread use of highly toxic, foreign‑manufactured pesticides, including chemicals banned in the United States and products bearing Chinese‑language labels suspected of being illegally imported. Siskiyou County investigators have identified more than 27 pesticides at illegal grow sites, some of which release toxic fumes when burned inside enclosed structures, further endangering first responders, contaminating water supplies, and potentially entering the illicit drug market without required safety testing. The crisis prompted the Siskiyou County Board of Supervisors to declare a local state of emergency on July 1, 2025, followed by EPA Region 9’s directive to investigate illegal pesticide importation and distribution.

Gallagher’s letter requests that the FBI:

Direct the Sacramento Field Office and Redding Resident Agency to work with Siskiyou and Shasta County Sheriffs and Homeland Security Investigations to pursue coordinated investigations into the criminal organizations financing and operating illegal grows, including potential foreign ties.

Coordinate with EPA Region 9 and federal partners on ongoing investigations into illegal pesticides recovered at these sites, including how they are entering the United States and whether their distribution is linked to broader criminal networks.

Brief Congress on current FBI efforts in Northern California and identify additional resources, authorities, or funding needed to support local eradication teams.

"The State of California has repeatedly turned a blind eye to the billion-dollar black market marijuana industry that has wreaked havoc on both Siskiyou County and across California. From weak legislation that all but greenlights illegal cultivation, to ignoring the environmental devastation and labor trafficking caused by these illicit industrial-scale operations, it is clear the State is unwilling to adequately combat this criminal enterprise,” said Siskiyou County Sheriff Jeremiah LaRue. “For too long, the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office has stood alone in the effort to end illegal marijuana cultivation and the proliferation of highly toxic pesticides in our County. Over the last five years, my agency has made over 800 arrests and eradicated over 2 million contaminated marijuana plants, but without broader support from State or Federal agencies, this destructive industry can continue to spread with impunity across America. This is why the involvement of federal agencies, including the FBI and EPA is urgently needed to disrupt the transnational criminal networks supporting these illicit operations across the United States. I commend Congressman Gallagher for elevating the issue of illegal marijuana cultivation and advocating for a stronger response to a crisis that continues to threaten California’s communities, natural resources, and public safety."

“Shasta County stands resolute with our neighbors in Siskiyou County in sending a clear message that illegal marijuana operations and the criminal enterprises that fund them are not welcome and will be shut down. We look forward to collaborating with the FBI to ensure private property rights are enforced and our natural resources in Northern California are safeguarded,” said Michael L. Johnson, Shasta County Sheriff.

title: Gallagher, Huizenga, Thompson, and Thanedar Introduce Bill to Create United States-India Interparliamentary Group
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman James Gallagher (CA‑01) introduced the United States–India Interparliamentary Group Act, a bipartisan bill establishing a formal forum for sustained engagement between the U.S. Congress and the Parliament of India. Gallagher, joined by House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee Chairman Bill Huizenga (MI‑04), Congressman Mike Thompson (CA‑04), and Congressman Shri Thanedar (MI‑13), underscored the importance of deepening cooperation with the world’s largest democracy across economic, security, and technological domains.

The legislation creates a structured, congressional‑level dialogue to advance shared interests, strengthen democratic institutions, and expand collaboration in areas including trade, critical and emerging technologies, defense, agriculture, and people‑to‑people ties. The group will serve as an official channel for lawmakers in both nations to exchange perspectives, identify opportunities for partnership, and address challenges facing the bilateral relationship.

“India is one of America’s most consequential partners, and our relationship will only grow more important in the decades ahead”, said Congressman Gallagher (CA-01). “Establishing a formal interparliamentary group ensures Congress plays a proactive role in strengthening this partnership, advancing shared democratic values, and expanding cooperation in critical areas like agriculture, specifically California wine and walnuts, technology, defense, and trade. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan effort.”

“As Chairman of the South and Central Asia Subcommittee, I see the US-India relationship—rooted in a common vision of a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific—as a defining moment of the 21st century. I’m proud to co-lead the United States-India Interparliamentary Group Act with Congressman Gallagher to further strengthen ties with the world’s largest democracy,” said Chairman Huizenga.

"I am glad to join Rep. Gallagher on legislation to establish the U.S.-India Interparliamentary Group to ensure that there is a permanent forum to strengthen ties, resolve issues, and partner on issues of mutual benefit. Strengthening our relationships with India is an opportunity to expand U.S. market access in India and support our California agriculture economy," said Congressman Thompson.

"The United States and India are natural partners that share democratic values and key economic and strategic interests. To further build this partnership, I'm proud to cosponsor the United States-India Interparliamentary Group Act to create a formal interparliamentary group between our two countries. I am grateful to Rep. Gallagher for his leadership on this issue and will continue to work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to strengthen this critical relationship," said Congressman Thanedar.

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Require Trades Experience on Board Investigating Nippon Dynawave Incident
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — This month, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez introduced the Chemical Safety Board Accountability Act, to ensure open board seats on the U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB) are filled in a timely manner by qualified candidates who have experience working in mills or other trades settings. The CSB is an independent watchdog tasked with investigating chemical incidents, including the incident at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company in Longview that killed 11 men, and making recommendations for safety improvements.

The Clean Air Act (CAA) states that the CSB’s governing body shall consist of five members, including a chairperson nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate. Currently, the board only has two members, and there is no indication of a plan to fill the empty seats. With two board members, the CSB can continue to carry out its statutory responsibilities, but a reduction to a single member could constrain the board’s ability to fulfill its mission. Under the CAA, there is no mechanism requiring empty board seats be filled and new board members are only required to be “technically and professionally qualified.” The bill introduced by Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez would amend the CAA to ensure board seats are filled quickly and by members with real experience working in the trades.

Specifically, this legislation would:

Amend the CAA to ensure that at least one Board member of the Chemical Safety Board has substantial experience in the trades.

Require that the President must fill vacancies within 90 days if a vacancy arises or a term expires.

Ensure that if the President fails to nominate someone within 90 days, they must submit a report to the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works that includes the reasons why the President did not submit a nomination and a plan to submit a nomination within the next 90 days. They must repeat this until they submit a nomination.

“When it comes to worker safety, we need a system that prioritizes people with actual skin in the game. Lab conditions aren’t mill conditions and ensuring that people investigating incidents and making recommendations on rules changes have real experience in the trades will help increase confidence in findings and usefulness of the recommendations,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “Since coming to Congress, ensuring working people have a seat at the table when rules are made has been a priority for me–and this is a step in the right direction.”

“Workers deserve a voice in the decisions that affect their safety, including the investigations that follow when something goes terribly wrong. People who have operated and maintained these facilities bring firsthand knowledge of the equipment, working conditions, and warning signs that must inform both an investigation and the recommendations that come out of it,” said Josh Estes, spokesperson for the Association of Western Pulp and Paper Workers. “The loss of 11 men at Nippon Dynawave makes this responsibility deeply personal for our union. We support Congresswoman Gluesenkamp Perez’s proposal to embed practical trades experience in the Chemical Safety Board’s leadership and ensure vacancies receive timely action. Families deserve answers, and workers deserve a fully functioning, independent board equipped to turn those answers into changes that save lives.”

Through her work on the House Appropriations Committee, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has fought to ensure that the CSB has the resources needed to perform their oversight and investigative work. In a major win this June, she was able to secure full funding for the CSB after the President’s budget proposed defunding the Board completely. In August of this year, the CSB released a report with initial findings on the Nippon Dynawave incident. In a statement that week, the Congresswoman highlighted the significant value of the Board and the dire need to ensure seats are filled with experienced trades workers.

####

title: Statement on Russia Sanctions Waiver
text:
VANCOUVER, WA – Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) issued the following statement on the President’s decision to sign an Executive Order yesterday waiving the sanctions on the sale of Russian oil Congress passed in the bipartisan Lindsay O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026:

“The President’s decision to issue a waiver of the recently passed Russia sanctions package is a betrayal of our ally Ukraine, the overwhelming will of Congress, and the national interests of the American people.

If Trump were serious about bringing down prices at the pump, he would end this disaster in Iran. And using American tax dollars to fund Russia through his proposed oil purchase is a shameful farce.

I am already working with a group of bipartisan members to introduce legislation that will block the President’s ill-conceived plan to purchase Russian oil. Congress must now also take steps to ensure that the sanctions we voted for and the President signed into law are fully executed and implemented.

Instead of continuing to aid and abet Putin’s fascist aggression, the President should do everything in his power to support our ally Ukraine. He should fully implement the sanctions package and reverse course on his plan to buy Russian oil.

The administration also needs to do everything in their power to immediately force the reversal of the Starlink throttle. I’m hearing directly from my constituents that their grandparents are being maimed getting water from a well in the middle of the Donbas. In the next Congress, there will be significant consequences for those responsible for facilitating Putin’s crimes.”

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County
text:
Above: Gottheimer Announces $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County.

BLOOMINGDALE, NJ — Today, October 19, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced that he successfully clawed back $1.2 million in new federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Passaic County first responders, helping upgrade emergency communications, expand counterterrorism training, and strengthen public safety while delivering real tax relief for local families.

“When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $1.2 million in federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Passaic County first responders, families, and towns. It shouldn’t be a fundraiser or a bake sale that decides whether a department can afford a working radio. I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the Law Enforcement Caucus and member of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus.

Video of Gottheimer’s announcement can be found here.

The federal investment Gottheimer secured will replace aging equipment and move Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford onto one interoperable communications standard, so police, fire, and EMS can communicate clearly and seamlessly across town lines when seconds matter most. By clawing back federal dollars to North Jersey communities and first responders, Gottheimer is helping lift high costs off local budgets, reducing the burden on Passaic County taxpayers to pay for essential public safety equipment and helping lower property taxes for local families.

The funding will be used as follows:

Bloomingdale First Responders, $400,000 (including the $100,000 announced in September): Response drones, active-threat gear such as ballistic shields, armor, and breaching kits, and communications equipment upgrades.

Ringwood First Responders, $300,000: A radio system upgrade, including new mobile radios in first-responder vehicles.

Wanaque First Responders, $300,000: Upgrades to interoperable radio systems, strengthening communications between the department, dispatch, and surrounding towns.

West Milford First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades.

Each department will also use part of its award for counterterrorism and other response training.

This investment builds on Gottheimer’s years-long work to claw more federal dollars back to North Jersey from Washington. This year alone, he has secured roughly $21 million in Homeland Security grant funding across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties for law enforcement, first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection.

Since 2017, he has clawed back more than $17 million in COPS grants for police departments across the Fifth District, including $2.9 million for upgraded first responder radio systems in West Milford in 2023 and $750,000 for new officers in West Milford in 2024. Since coming to Congress, Gottheimer has helped increase the return of federal funds to the Fifth District by more than 357%, delivering an average savings of about $750 for each household in the Fifth District.

Gottheimer was joined by Bloomingdale Mayor John D’Amato, Bloomingdale Police Chief Daniel Greenwood, Passaic County Prosecutor Camelia Valdes, Passaic County Sheriff Thomas Adamo, Passaic County Commissioner Nicholas Veliky, Bloomingdale Councilman David Bronkhurst, Bloomingdale Fire Chief Frank Neuberger, Ringwood Police Chief Ronald Porta, Wanaque Mayor Dan Mahler, Wanaque Councilman Ed Leonard, Wanaque Police Chief Keith Spillane, West Milford Mayor Michelle Dale, West Milford Sgt. Anthony Frassa, Ringwood Councilwoman Yvonne Echols, local first responders, and community leaders.

Below: Gottheimer Announces $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County.

Gottheimer remarks as prepared for delivery:

Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here in Bloomingdale, in beautiful Passaic County.

First, I want to start by thanking the hardworking people standing here with us today. Jersey’s finest. Our local police departments. Our Passaic County Prosecutor’s Office. Our Passaic County Sheriff’s Office. Everyone who answers the call, who stands in harm’s way, no matter the hour.

Every single day, rain or shine, late nights, early mornings, weekends, holidays, you put on the uniform, and you answer the call without hesitation. You put yourselves in harm’s way to keep our families and communities safe. You get our backs. And I want you to know, as ever, that I’ll always get yours.

Here in northern Passaic County, you cover a lot of ground. Long stretches of road. You roll up on a call at two in the morning, not knowing what’s on the other side of that door.

You chase down a stolen car. You stand post for hours outside a house of worship because a threat came in overnight. You respond to a terrorist threat or a heart attack. You do all of that – and never miss the routine calls. The fender-bender, the alarm going off, the neighbor dispute. The job doesn’t slow down just because the risks get bigger.

When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. And, despite your deep ties with the community, our officers are increasingly doing it in an environment where you’re not always treated with the respect you’re due.

You aren’t just officers who protect us. You are our neighbors. You coach our kids’ teams, and you sit next to us at church and at the diner.

Just over the last year, among others, you responded to a mother and her two children lost while hiking in West Milford, a live, fully charged grenade in Bloomingdale, a deadly house fire in Ringwood, a tragic, fatal crash in Wanaque, and those are just to name a few.

We all know that being a cop today is more complex than it was twenty years ago.

Today, our officers have to think about active shooters. Mass-casualty events. Threats against our synagogues, our churches, our mosques, our temples. Terrorist threats. Cyberattacks on the systems that keep our towns running, like our water systems and electric grid. Let’s be honest, it’s a different and fast-changing world. AI, cameras, drones, and real-time intelligence tools.

That is an enormous amount to ask of any officer, any department, any town. And, increasingly, our local and county departments don’t have the resources they need to keep up – manpower, training, updated radios, equipment, and communication systems.

Gear and training for the worst-case scenarios nobody wants to think about. But, every department has to be ready for those worst-case scenarios.

Let me talk about radios for a minute, because it sounds simple, but it is a matter of life and death. Reliable radios are the backbone of any emergency response. When police, fire, and EMS can all talk on the same system, they share information and coordinate in real time. When they can’t, people get hurt.

On 9/11, many firefighters in the North Tower never got the order to evacuate because their radios couldn’t reach them. Police who saw the collapse coming were on a separate system that couldn’t warn them. We can never let that happen again.

It’s not just terrorism or crime. Communications break down in storms and in everyday emergencies, like in a car wreck, a storm, or a forest fire, when systems get overwhelmed or simply can’t link up. Aging equipment and systems that can’t talk to each other should never be what stands between a first responder and the person who needs help.

Many of the towns I represent in Passaic County told me they simply didn’t have the latest equipment to communicate, including where there are huge distances between towers and plenty of woods and roads in between. In times of crisis, we shouldn’t ever accept radios that don’t work with the radios in the town over or with dispatch.

It’s the same way I feel about training. I know how stretched our departments are for resources. There simply aren’t enough resources to pay for all the training that’s required, including everything officers need to fight the latest terrorist threat or handle everyday crime.

That’s why I proudly introduced bipartisan legislation called the Invest to Protect Act, which passed the House. It allocates resources for training, and recruitment and retention bonuses for our officers, who are facing more stress than ever.

It’s also why, since 2017, I’ve fought hard in Washington, and successfully clawed back to Jersey more than $17 million in COPS grants for police departments across the Fifth District. I was proud to secure $2.9 million for upgraded first responder radio systems for West Milford in 2023.

And in 2024, I secured $750,000 for West Milford to hire new officers as part of the COPS Hiring Program. But, that only solved part of the problem, and, as I said, these needs are changing fast, especially with our communications equipment.

It shouldn’t be a fundraiser or a bake sale that decides whether a department can afford a working radio.

So, over the last months, after hearing from the prosecutor, the sheriff, the PBA, mayors, state and local officials, and, of course, many of the police chiefs, I went back to work in Washington, with my colleagues in Congress and with the Administration.

Months of meetings. Months of calls. Months of negotiations. I took the needs of our district directly to the White House, to the Secretary of Homeland Security, and to FEMA to make sure Jersey gets the funds we deserve.

Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $1.2 million in federal Homeland Security funding for Passaic County first responders, families, and towns.

Again, we are clawing back $1.2 million in federal dollars from Washington back to Passaic County. Those are dollars that are not coming from your property taxes and state income taxes – and they aren’t going to Moocher States like Alabama or West Virginia. They are coming back here, where they belong.

Let me break this out for you a little more. Of the $1.2 million, $400,000 will go to the Bloomingdale Police Department – including the $100,000 I announced on September 11th – for response drones and active-threat gear, like ballistic shields, armor, and breaching kits, and to upgrade their communications equipment. Another $300,000 will go to the Ringwood Police Department for a radio system upgrade, with new mobile radios in first-responder vehicles. $300,000 will go to the Wanaque Police Department to upgrade to interoperable radio systems. And $200,000 will go to the West Milford Police Department for radio communications upgrades.

And every one of those departments will also use part of its award for the terror and other response training that I mentioned.

When implemented, this funding will replace and upgrade aging equipment, and move these departments onto one interoperable standard, so that first responders across town lines are not locked onto systems that can’t talk to each other.

The primary use of these funds is radio upgrades, so that multiple agencies can talk to each other directly, on one channel. In Wanaque, that means stronger radio communications between the department, dispatch, and the surrounding towns. In Ringwood, it means new radios in the vehicles themselves. When the State police, the local police, fire, and EMS can all reach each other in an emergency, they can coordinate faster and save lives.

These resources will also help purchase drones and active-threat gear in Bloomingdale. These give our officers more eyes where they need them, and help them respond to incidents safely. So, our first responders are ready when the worst happens.

This year alone, across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties that I proudly represent, we have now secured roughly $25.5 million in Homeland Security grant funding for our law enforcement, our first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection.

Plus, I also helped claw back another $29.5 million in June for the state, which helped State Police, communications equipment, transit, for overtime for officers during the World Cup, counterterrorism, counter-drone operations, intelligence sharing, other threat training, and nonprofit security grants.

Finally, every police department in the Fifth Congressional District, including all of Passaic County – Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford – will receive $50,000 for counterterrorism training, because, as I said, it is not enough to have gear. This requires robust, sustained training, not just an informational binder on a shelf.

Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford will each receive the resources for vital training as part of their award.

By the way, the amounts I announced today are beyond and outside the traditional grants we fight to claw back every year – like LESO, $1 million for COPS, Byrne JAG, $1.48 million for AFGE, $965k for SAFER, and over $10 million in community-directed projects. Today’s numbers also don’t include the $1.7 million and $7.8 million over the last two years that I’ve already clawed back this year to protect our religious institutions in my district.

One point I want to make – these are your federal tax dollars coming home to Jersey. We send billions of dollars to Washington every year. The question is: how much of that money actually comes back to Jersey? For far too long, the answer has been not nearly enough. My job is to fight for every dollar I can, and claw it back here, where it belongs. For every dollar I get back of your federal tax dollars to Jersey, that means one less dollar hitting your local property tax or income tax lines. That’s a big deal.

That means federal dollars to help pay for a fire truck, like we did in West Milford in 2018, or equipment to keep firefighters safe, like oxygen masks or thermal imaging cameras, which I secured for Ringwood in 2020 and 2021.

Historically, states like Mississippi have gotten about $4.38 back for every dollar it sends to Washington. West Virginia gets about $4.23 back.

But in New Jersey? We get about 67 cents on the dollar. That’s the lowest in the nation.

That’s unacceptable. Why should the “Moocher States” get our money, instead of it coming back home to you?

That’s why I’m fighting every day to claw back your federal tax dollars and bring them home to Jersey. Since I’ve been in Congress, we’ve increased what we bring back home by more than 357 percent, about $750 per family.

For you, that means lower property taxes, better infrastructure, and more money in your pocket. That’s what today is. Jersey families’ own federal tax dollars, coming back home to protect Jersey.

Finally, I am so proud to stand here today. I am so grateful for everything these incredible public servants do for every single one of us, every single day.

I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders. Keeping them, and our families, safe is not a partisan issue. This isn’t red or blue – this is just red, white, and blue, and about taking care of the families we all represent.

I know that if we keep working together to support our communities, here in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead of us.

Thank you. May God bless you, your families, and our first responders.

title: Grijalva, Stanton, and Ansari Statement on Suspicious Letters Sent to Arizona Offices
text:
Tucson, AZ –- Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva, along with U.S. Representatives Greg Stanton (AZ-04) and Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), released the following joint statement after being notified by the FBI Phoenix Field Office and the Arizona Department of Homeland Security that suspicious letters had been sent to their offices.

“This weekend, the FBI Phoenix Field Office and the Arizona Department of Homeland Security informed us that suspicious letters had been sent to our offices. Similar letters, many containing unknown substances, have been mailed to elected officials across the country.

The FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating. We’re grateful to law enforcement for acting quickly and keeping our staff and communities safe. We will not be intimidated, and we’ll keep doing the work that Arizonans elected us to do.”

The letters addressed to Representatives Grijalva and Ansari were sent to former office addresses. The letter addressed to Representative Stanton’s Mesa office was intercepted before delivery.

title: Harshbarger Joins President Trump and First Lady at White House for Women’s Health Executive Order Signing
text:
“It is clear that President Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, and Secretary Kennedy have made women’s health a priority at the highest levels, and today’s executive order is yet another game changer for women and girls across America,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “By closing the research gap and harnessing advanced research technologies, this order will get treatments and cures to women faster. The Trump administration has already delivered for women, from making my Pregnancy.gov Act a reality through Moms.gov to helping families save on fertility medications through TrumpRx and sending new moms home with the postpartum supplies they need. Today’s order builds on that serious, results-driven commitment to making care more accessible and affordable for women at every stage of life. I’m grateful for their leadership and look forward to building on this work in Congress.”

Image

Image

The executive order, led by First Lady Melania Trump, builds on her “Five Pillars of Women’s Health Innovation”:

Direct research funding toward finding cures for conditions that affect women uniquely or disproportionately.

Use Super Intelligence to enhance our insight into female biology and speed up medical discoveries.

Accelerate the process of getting promising therapeutics from laboratories to female patients, while maintaining strict safety standards.

Ensure that medical breakthroughs are accessible and affordable to women, regardless of their financial circumstances.

Replace generations of silence with open conversation, education, and compassion surrounding women’s health.

The order directs the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a Women’s Health Division at NIH within 90 days to expand research into understudied conditions, from heart disease and cancer to endometriosis and menopause, increase the inclusion of women in clinical trials, and speed the translation of discoveries into clinical practice.

It also creates the White House Women’s Health Task Force, co-chaired by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, to turn research into better care and work with states, faith-based organizations, and the private sector to put it into practice.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions
text:
New Haven, CT — Today, U.S. Representatives John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:

“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.

“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.

“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”

title: Hoyer Statement on Suspicious Letter Received at District Office
text:
GREENBELT, MD – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after a potentially hazardous letter was received at his district office in Greenbelt, Maryland:

"Today, my district office in Greenbelt, Maryland, received a suspicious letter similar to those received by public officials across the country. The office has been evacuated, and, thankfully, my district staff are safe. I thank our law enforcement partners for their swift and diligent response, and I will continue to monitor this situation as it develops and remain vigilant for other possible threats.

"My district office staff work hard every day to deliver critical services to Marylanders across the Fifth Congressional District. It is unacceptable that their lives were put in danger. Intimidation efforts such as these are un-American and pose an existential threat to our democracy. We must not - and will not - allow them to prevent us from fulfilling our commitment to serving our communities."

title: REP. HOYLE ANNOUNCES OVER $200M FOR THE PORT OF COOS BAY
text:
Eugene, OR – Today, Representative Val Hoyle released the following statement after announcing more than $204 million in funding for the Port of Coos Bay.

“We're thrilled to see this game changing $204 million investment from the Department of Transportation to upgrade the Coos Bay rail line,” said Rep. Hoyle. “So many people worked incredibly hard to get us this far. These investments are transformational for communities across the South Coast and our supply chain resilience.”

Background:

This grant will fund the construction of upgrades to the Coos Bay Rail Line, including repairing and replacing track, ties, bridges and tunnels that are needed to bring the Pacific Coast Intermodal Port project closer to fruition.

Rep. Hoyle has been a champion to bring back funding for the Port of Coos Bay. This funding announcement brings Rep. Hoyle’s total amount of funding secured for the Pacific Coast Intermodal Project to nearly $300M. She previously secured $70 million in federal grants,including $29.75 million through CRISI, $25.018 million through INFRA, $11.25 through the Port Infrastructure Development Program and $3.993 million through the Rail Crossing Elimination Grant to support improvement to port and rail infrastructure.

title: Congressman Kean Accepting Applications for Spring 2027 Internship Program
text:
(October 19, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) announced that his offices in Washington, D.C. and Lebanon Borough, NJ are now accepting applications for the Spring 2027 Internship Program. This competitive program offers college students the chance to gain firsthand experience in the fast-paced environment of a congressional office.

Interns play an essential role in the daily operations of the office, working closely with staff members on a range of responsibilities, including legislative research, constituent services, communications, and more. Participating students will also gain valuable insight into the legislative process and the ways in which a Member of Congress serves the residents of their district.

“Interns are a critical part of our team and the work we do every day to serve the people of New Jersey,” said Congressman Kean “In both our New Jersey and Washington, D.C. offices, our interns make meaningful contributions while gaining valuable firsthand experience in public service. I look forward to welcoming our next class of interns this spring.”

Interested students must be currently enrolled in college and should complete the online application form at kean.house.gov/services/internships. The deadline to apply is Monday, November 16, 2026, at 11:59 PM. Positions are available in both the Washington, D.C. and District offices.
