title: Kean Celebrates Local Law Enforcement in Hometown Heroes Event
text:
(OCTOBER 19, 2026) CLARK, NJ – Last week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) hosted his third annual Hometown Heroes event, celebrating 30 first responders from across New Jersey’s Seventh Congressional District.

This year, Congressman Kean invited nominations from police, fire, and EMS departments throughout the district to spotlight exemplary individuals.

“As a former volunteer firefighter and EMT, my appreciation for first responders is personal,” said Congressman Kean. “Those experiences taught me firsthand the sacrifices that first responders make every day. I was pleased to celebrate the accomplishments and hard work of these brave men and women. Thank you to the first responders in New Jersey and throughout our nation.”

Photos from the event can be found HERE.

Honorees pictured from left to right:

Volunteer Firefighter Andrew Och - Far Hills-Bedminster Fire Department

Since becoming a member two years ago, Andrew has completed Firefighter I and II certifications, Hazardous Materials Technician training, Extrication Technician certification, and is currently completing his Swift Water Rescue Technician certification. In addition to his fire service commitments, Andrew serves as a driver with his town's Ambulance Squad and plans to obtain his EMT certification in Fall 2026. Despite balancing these responsibilities with full-time employment at a local company and coursework at a community college, Andrew consistently ranks among the Far Hills-Bedminster Fire Department’s top responders. His commitment to the community is evident in both his willingness to answer calls and his drive to continually expand his skills and knowledge.

EMT Ranee Muirhead - Scotch Plains Volunteer Rescue Squad

During her 7 years of service, Ranee has answered over 1,024 calls for assistance while juggling work and family. She spends over 50 hours a month answering calls as well as managing the responsibilities of her administrative positions on the Rescue Squad. For example, Ranee assumed the duties of treasurer for the organization and streamlined their budgeting and account receivable and account payable processes. Ranee was recently trained as a Mental Health Resilience Officer who will engage with members and help identify peers who might be experiencing mental health stressors. Ranee is extremely reliable, is often one of the first crew members to arrive for duty and often assumes responsibility for checking the ambulances and equipment before the other crew members arrive.

Auxiliary Police Officer Jack Ross - Fanwood Police Department

Jack has been a reliable and honorable member of the Fanwood Police Department for over 40 years. His service as a Special Law Enforcement Officer Class 2, and now as an Auxiliary Police Officer, has been invaluable to the advancement of the Police Department. He supervises the crossing guards and goes above and beyond to ensure that they are well-trained, safe, and properly equipped. He also has provided security for the Fanwood court and at Election Day polling places. Ross received the 2025 Shield Award sponsored by the Knights of Columbus and honoring those who have made a difference in their community.

Detective Sergeant Alex Wright - Readington Police Department

Detective Sergeant Wright currently leads the Readington Township Police Department's Detective Bureau, where he oversees criminal investigations and helps manage some of the department's most complex cases. He also serves as a department drone operator and is a member of both the Readington Township Police Department Fatal Crash Investigation Unit and the County Fatal Crash Investigation Unit. Wright is an experienced detective, a capable supervisor, and someone who can be counted on when an incident is serious, complicated, or requires someone willing to challenge every assumption in the room. Detective Sergeant Wright's supervisors describe him as dependable, knowledgeable, and willing to step into demanding situations without hesitation.

Lieutenant Jeff Melitski - Bernardsville Police Department

Jeff is a lifelong resident of Bernardsville, a graduate of Bernards High School and a member of the Bernards High School Sports Hall of Fame. The lieutenant is also the grandson of the late retired Bernardsville Chief of Police. He originally began his career as an officer with the Warren Township Police Department before being hired by the Bernardsville Police Department in 2002. Over his career, Jeff has served as a patrol officer, DARE officer, and Sergeant before attaining his current rank.

Volunteer EMT David Lai-Len - Long Hill First Aid Squad

Dave has been a volunteer EMT for 15 years. After earning his certification, he volunteered with the Liberty Corner First Aid Squad for 13 years, serving as LOSAP Officer, Treasurer, and President. He responded to over 300 calls yearly and committed over 2,000 duty hours yearly. Dave then joined the Long Hill First Aid Squad, Far Hills First Aid Squad, and Bernardsville Fire & Rescue Squad. He remains a member of Long Hill, being on duty three daytime/weekday shifts and several weekend shifts and serving last year as Vice President. In addition to volunteering as an EMT, Dave has deployed with the Red Cross and Team Rubicon. He is also an officer in VFW Post 7858, Bernardsville, where he was awarded a plaque for Exceptional Service as the Post Service Officer in 2018. Dave was also involved in the OCA, an Asian civil rights group, where he was awarded the 2008 National Unsung Hero Award and the Community Service Award in 2019.

Officers Nicholas Walsh & Liam Slack - Phillipsburg Police Department

Officers Slack and Walsh demonstrated courage, initiative, and exceptional dedication to duty during a serious medical emergency September 4, 2026. Both officers responded to a heavily wooded area where a juvenile had suffered a severe head injury from a falling rock. Upon learning that EMS had not yet reached the child and that the juveniles were stranded at the bottom of a steep, rocky embankment, the officers took immediate action. Officer Slack retrieved a medical kit and descended the hazardous terrain to assist the injured juvenile. Officer Walsh also descended, administered first aid by dressing the wound, and identified the safest and most efficient access point for additional responders. Demonstrating remarkable physical endurance, the officers carried the injured juvenile through the difficult, wooded terrain to awaiting EMS and fire personnel. The juvenile was later diagnosed with a skull fracture and brain bleed, underscoring the severity of the incident. Both officers' decisive actions, sound judgment, and willingness to enter hazardous conditions helped ensure the child received timely medical treatment. Notably, Officer Slack was only in his second month of service as a police officer, making his courage and initiative particularly commendable.

Life Honorary Members Gary Wagner and David Newby- Clark Volunteer Emergency Squad

Gary Wagner joined the squad in 1974 and has served the Clark community for over 50 years. He has held various line officer and delegate positions over his decades with CVES and frequently represents the squad at local community events, parades, and memorial services. He was part of the CVES response and support efforts during the September 11th aftermath. David has been an integral member of the Clark Volunteer Emergency Squad for more than 20 years. He started as a driver, supporting his son who was a member of the squad. Soon, Dave obtained his EMT certification. He has managed finances and secured external funding as Treasurer and as a member of the Squad’s Executive Board. David was awarded the “Pillar of Service” honor by the squad for his dedication and contributions.

Firefighter and Department President Walter Lata - Budd Lake Volunteer Fire Department

Walter responds to over 90% of the Budd Lake Volunteer Fire Department's more than 600 emergency calls annually. In addition to his response commitment, Walter serves as Department President and continually goes above and beyond the expectations of his position. He frequently takes on projects around the firehouse on his own personal time and often at his own expense, always striving to improve the department and its facilities for the benefit of all members. Walter's dedication extends beyond emergency response and the firehouse. He is actively involved in community events and consistently looks for opportunities to represent and promote the department in a positive manner.

Volunteer Firefighter Trent LaFord - Lopatcong Fire Department

While attending high school, Trent simultaneously enrolled in and completed the Warren County Fire Academy, earning his Firefighter I and II certifications as well as his Hazardous Materials Operations certification. He accomplished all of this while balancing his schoolwork and preparing for his senior-year football season, demonstrating discipline, dedication, and maturity well beyond his years. Trent will now attend Warren County Community College to pursue an associate degree in drone agriculture.

Kevin Saharic passed away in May of 2026. His family, including his wife and three daughters, accepted the honor on his behalf.

Chief Kevin Saharic - Lebanon Borough Fire Department

Kevin devoted more than 45 years to serving others through the fire and rescue service. His extraordinary dedication to the safety of his community earned the admiration and respect of all who knew him. He joined the Lebanon Fire Company in 1980 and served as Chief for 23 years. At the time of his passing, he served as Captain and Public Service Director for the Borough of Lebanon. Kevin was also a member of the Hunterdon County Fire Chiefs Association, a founding member of the FAST Team in Hunterdon County and the North Hunterdon Fire Alliance (Squad 51), and Secretary for the New Jersey State Firemen’s Relief Association. Kevin led with integrity and distinction. He received the Medal of Valor for rescuing a downed firefighter and a civilian during a fire. In 2024, Kevin was honored as Grand Marshal of the Lebanon Borough Fourth of July Parade in recognition of his countless contributions to the community. Throughout his distinguished career, Kevin consistently placed the safety of others before his own.

Additional Honorees Recognized:

Officer Joanna Coppola - Branchburg Police Department

Since joining the department, Officer Coppola has distinguished herself through her professionalism, integrity, and commitment to serving the community she grew up in. In 2025, she led the department in total arrests, as well as total DWI arrests, earning herself the "Rising Star Award" at the New Jersey Women in Law Enforcement Annual Conference and recognition from Mothers Against Drunk Driving.

First Lieutenant Kimberly Stang - Allamuchy‑Green First Aid Squad

A dedicated member of the Allamuchy‑Green First Aid Squad since 2009, First Lieutenant Stang has spent nearly her entire 17years of service in leadership roles. She recently led the complex design, build, and implementation of two new fully equipped and service ready ambulances, an extraordinary accomplishment for a fully volunteer organization. She responds to hundreds of 911 calls each year and remains one of the most reliable and trusted operational leaders. First Lieutenant Stang is an exceptional patient care provider, a steady incident commander, and a respected leader whose dedication has made a lasting impact on the Allamuchy-Green First Aid Squad and the community it serves.

Officer Robert Popelka - Stanhope Police Department

In February, Officer Popelka responded to a severe structure fire at the One Step Closer Animal Rescue OSCAR facility. He arrived to find part of the building engulfed in flames and several dogs trapped inside. Without hesitation, he moved through intense heat and heavy smoke, unlocking cages and freeing as many animals as possible. During this courageous effort, Officer Popelka sustained burns to his arms and hands, yet continued working until multiple dogs were safely removed from the flames. His swift actions prevented a far greater tragedy and demonstrated remarkable courage and compassion. Officer Popelka’s dedication, quick thinking, and willingness to put himself in harm’s way reflect the highest standards of public service. His actions stand as an inspiring example of his commitment to the community he serves.

President Callie Campbell - Westfield Volunteer Rescue Squad

As the President of the Westfield Volunteer Rescue Squad, President Campbell consistently demonstrates what it means to be a true leader and public servant. She dedicates countless hours to ensuring the success of the agency while going above and beyond to support those around her.

SLEO Todd Widitz and Officer Tyler Widitz - Bernards Township Police Department

Todd and Tyler serve the community of Bernards Township with a shared commitment to service, integrity, and courage. The Widitz’s willingness to answer the call, help those in need, and make a positive difference in their community reflects the highest ideals of the law enforcement profession. Their service is especially meaningful because it represents a legacy passed from one generation to the next. The example established by a father and carried forward by his son is a testament to the values of family, duty, and service.

HLEO Gianna DiMatteo, Dispatcher Judith Wolff, Detective Anthony Cirri, Detective Rony Giordano, Detective Patrick Rohan, Patrolman Erick Macarico, Patrolman Daniel Lalo, Patrolman David Jacob, Patrolman Joseph Fagan, and Patrolman Logan Kobis - Hopatcong Police Department

When Officers Anthony Cirri, Patrick Rohan, Daniel Lalo, Erik Macarico, Roni Giordano, David Jacob, Joseph Fagan, and Logan Kobis arrived at the confirmed structure fire, they were immediately confronted with a rapidly developing and dangerous situation involving more than forty dogs inside. Without hesitation, they worked alongside firefighters and rescue personnel to evacuate dogs from locked kennels while the building was actively burning. Their actions required them to operate in close proximity to heavy smoke, intense heat, and hazardous conditions, all while maintaining their focus on rescuing the animals and supporting the overall emergency response. Together, they worked seamlessly to save nearly all of the dogs housed in the facility. Dispatcher Judith Wolff played an equally critical role. She managed a high volume of 911 calls while simultaneously coordinating radio communications for police, fire, EMS, and animal control units. Her calm demeanor, professionalism, and ability to effectively manage resources ensured that responders received timely and accurate information throughout the fast‑moving emergency. Animal Control Officer Gianna DiMatteo, who also serves as the department’s Humane Law Enforcement Officer, was instrumental in safely handling, evacuating, and relocating the animals once they were removed from the building. Her expertise helped ensure that the dogs were properly transferred and cared for during and after the incident.

Chief Bruce Tynan - Hackettstown Fire Department Chief

A proud Korean War Veteran who served in the U.S. Army 1st Cavalry Division, Chief Tynan has dedicated more than seven decades to protecting and strengthening the Hackettstown community. As a 70‑year active member of the Hackettstown Fire Department, he has embodied service, leadership, and commitment. Chief Tynan has held numerous roles, including Treasurer Emeritus of Cataract Hose Co. No. 1, Treasurer of the Hackettstown Fireman’s Relief Association, Fire Marshal for the Town of Hackettstown, and Fire Official for Washington Township. Chief Tynan’s dedication to civic pride also stems beyond emergency services, having been the Grand Marshal to the American Legion Memorial Day Parade.

title: $618,481 to Launch Veterans Treatment Court
text: The Northern Mariana Islands Judiciary has been awarded $618,481 through the Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance Veterans Treatment Court Program to establish the Commonwealth's first Veterans Treatment Court. The four-year award will support the planning and implementation of a specialized veterans treatment track within the Mental Health Court, with the goal of expanding into a standalone Veterans Treatment Court program as capacity grows. The initiative will identify veterans involved in the justice system, provide evidence-based risk and needs assessments, and connect participants with individualized treatment, case management, judicial supervision, and recovery support services. Through partnerships with healthcare and community organizations, the program aims to improve access to treatment, increase successful program completion rates, and reduce recidivism among justice-involved veterans. Congratulations to the NMI Judiciary on securing this federal funding and advancing an important initiative to better serve the Commonwealth’s veterans.

title: Celebrating Humanities Month in the CNMI
text: I joined the Northern Marianas Humanities Council last week in proclaiming October as Humanities Month in the CNMI! I think back to the year we have had and the struggles our people continue to face. Through it all, I think there is a real purpose for the humanities in helping us understand the history that has brought us to where we are today, the people and communities around us, and how we imagine our path forward. The humanities give us an opportunity to reflect on our experiences, learn from one another, and better understand the stories and ideas that shape our islands. They are an important part of who we are and, just as importantly, where we are going. Congratulations to everyone involved in this year's proclamation ceremony, and thank you to the Northern Marianas Humanities Council for the work you do. I look forward to a month of celebrating the humanities here in the CNMI!

title: Expanding VA Healthcare Options for CNMI Veterans
text: Improving access to VA healthcare and services here at home has been one of my priorities since taking office. Our veterans deserve access to the care they have earned without having to travel thousands of miles to receive it. That is why I am so pleased with the Department of Veterans Affairs' announcement that it has signed a lease for a new VA Outpatient Clinic on Saipan! The new facility will expand access to primary care, audiology, mental health, and telehealth services, with patient services expected to begin in Fiscal Year 2027. Earlier this year, I coordinated a visit from staff of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee to the CNMI to examine potential sites and facilities for an expanded VA presence. That visit was an important opportunity to show our congressional partners firsthand the needs of our veterans and the opportunities to bring more services to our islands. I applaud the VA for taking this important step forward. Expanding the availability of healthcare and services for our veterans in the CNMI is something we have been working toward, and I am excited to see this progress. There is more work ahead, and I look forward to continuing our efforts to build a stronger, more permanent VA presence in the CNMI.

title: Purple Thursday at the District Office
text: On Thursday, our District Office participated in the Northern Marianas Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence’s Purple Thursday Challenge. In the month of October, we honor all victims, survivors, and advocates for domestic violence. We thank the Coalition for their collective movement to end violence in the Marianas. Join us in raising awareness against domestic violence in our schools and community. Stay tuned to our social media pages next week for the District Office’s Purple Thursday Challenge!

title: Regional Conversations on Greater VA Services Across the Marianas
text: I was recently invited to provide testimony on a Guam Senate resolution seeking to establish a VA Regional Office in Guam to serve veterans throughout the Western Pacific, including the CNMI and the Freely Associated States. Last week, I provided Senator Telo Taitague with my thoughts on the resolution and shared my interest in expanding the VA's presence throughout our region. Veterans in Guam and the CNMI face many of the same challenges accessing the healthcare, benefits, and services they have earned, and I believe there is a great opportunity for our islands to work together to address them. I also emphasized that the same interest in establishing a greater VA presence in Guam exists here in the CNMI. As we consider how to expand regional services, I want to see the CNMI included in those plans, with a permanent, fully staffed VA facility of our own and greater access to VA personnel and services right here at home. Thank you to Senator Taitague for the invitation and for raising this important issue. I look forward to continuing the conversation and exploring how Guam and the CNMI can work together to better serve our veterans.

title: Saipan International School Campus Visit
text: Our latest stop on our campus outreach journey was at Saipan International School. Your Congressional Office has a range of wonderful programs targeted toward our students. As we go around to the schools to present programs like Service Academy Nominations, Congressional Art Competition, Congressional App Challenge, or internships, we always leave optimistic about the bright futures our students envision. The optimism and promising futures of the students in Mr. Daryn Rouf’s class and all around SIS was truly inspiring to see. Thank you, Geckos!

title: Standing Together Against Domestic Violence
text: Every year, it is so important to me to participate in marking Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Surviving domestic violence takes tremendous strength, and I believe our community has an important role to play in standing behind survivors and those who have been impacted by abuse. We want every survivor to know that they are not alone, that we have their back, and that there are people ready to help. This month is also about reminding our entire community that domestic violence has no place in our islands, and that each of us has a responsibility to help put an end to it. Thank you to the Northern Marianas Coalition Against Domestic & Sexual Violence (NMCADSV) for the work you do throughout the year to support survivors, raise awareness, and bring our community together around this important cause. #2026DVAM #DomesticViolenceAwarenessMonth #ReclaimingHopeRestoringLight

title: Tackling the Big Issues with Student Journalists
text: I love student-led journalism. Having students both report on the news and offer their own perspectives brings together classroom learning and real-world issues in a way that often leads to new and interesting conversations about the topics of the day. It was an absolute joy to sit down with journalism students from the University of Guam and the student journalists behind Triton's Call, UOG's student news outlet, to talk about territorial representation, deep-sea mineral mining, and some of the major issues affecting our region. These were thoughtful questions about issues that will shape the future of our islands, and I really enjoyed the opportunity to hear their perspectives and share some of my own. Thank you to Thomas Manglona for connecting us and arranging this great interview. Take a look at our conversation here!

title: Welcoming Jillian Angeline to Washington
text: We welcomed Jillian Angeline, former KSPN 2 News and Saipan Tribune reporter, to the Washington congressional office on Friday. During her years in the Marianas, Jillian covered stories across our islands and built lasting friendships that she continues to cherish. She is now in Washington for a conference through her current role as Sales Manager for Commercial and Public Safety at EagleNXT. It was great to reconnect with someone who maintains such strong ties to the Northern Mariana Islands. Hafa Adai, Jillian, and thank you for stopping by.

title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions
text:
Hartford, CT — Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:

“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.

“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.

“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”

title: ICYMI: Liccardo Moves to Force Vote on Protections for Afghan Refugees
text:
SAN JOSÉ, CA— Today, The Mercury News reported on Congressman Sam Liccardo’s plans to bypass Republican House leadership and force a vote on his bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act. The legislation would restore Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for more than 8,000 Afghans at risk of deportation after the Trump administration ended their protections last year. Liccardo plans to file the discharge petition when Congress returns on November 9.

Read the full story below:

The Mercury News: Rep. Sam Liccardo’s bill to reinstate protections for Afghan refugees has stalled. Now, he’s turning to an obscure procedural rule to force a vote

By Grace Hase Published October 19, 2026

Silicon Valley Rep. Sam Liccardo’s bill to make Afghan immigrants once again eligible for temporary protected status has gone nowhere since it was introduced this summer, leaving more than 8,000 refugees nationally at risk for deportation. Now, the first-term congressmember plans to leverage an obscure procedural rule to advance the legislation.

Liccardo, who co-authored the “Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026” with Reps. Jason Crow, D-Colo., Don Bacon, R-Neb., and Maria Salazar, R-Fla., told the Bay Area News Group that he plans to file a discharge petition when Congress returns from recess on Nov. 9. The bill would offer Afghan refugees a shield from deportation as their immigration cases move forward, a status they held previously until the Trump administration ended the protection in 2025.

The legislative mechanism is a way for congressmembers to buck House leadership, which controls what bills proceed out of committee. If a discharge petition receives at least 218 signatures, it will force a vote on the bill.

Long considered a seldom-used tool with very little success, discharge petitions are finding new utility in the Trump era as House Speaker Mike Johnson holds a razor-thin majority that’s at risk in the upcoming midterm election.

Donna Crane, a lecturer in San Jose State University’s Department of Political Science, said that Republicans, who are facing dire reelection prospects, have used discharge petitions this year as a way to distance themselves from President Donald Trump. But for the minority party, she said, it’s also been an incredibly powerful instrument.

“This can be pretty much the only way of getting any control over the House floor schedule because the majority controls the entire schedule,” she said. “If you can hold your own group together and pick a few members off from the other side, then your bill is going to go to the floor.”

Reps. Ro Khanna, D-Santa Clara, and Thomas Massie, R-Kentucky, famously used a discharge petition last year to bypass House leadership in their quest to pry loose investigative records related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The discharge petition could mark a critical step in Liccardo’s efforts to reinstate TPS for Afghan nationals. The Trump administration has halted protections for immigrants from 13 countries as it looks to dismantle the program, which guards from deportation individuals who can’t safely return to their homes due to ongoing conflict or other disasters.

The Biden administration granted TPS to eligible Afghans in 2022 after the United States ended its military presence in the country the year prior.

“Regardless of political differences, we ought to be able to agree on the critical importance of keeping our promises as a country,” Liccardo said about his bill. “America promised thousands of Afghans who risked their lives as interpreters, as informants, as other support roles to our military; they risked their lives with the expectation that we would not betray them and put them in harm’s way for doing so.”

Joseph Azam, a Berkeley resident and the board chair of the Afghan-American Foundation, said that the end of TPS for Afghan nationals has “shaken people’s belief that protecting this population is a bipartisan priority.”

The decision, along with other moves by the Trump administration to ban Afghans from entering the U.S., has sent shockwaves throughout the Bay Area — especially in Fremont, which is home to one of the largest concentrations of Afghan immigrants in the country.

Azam said that it’s been “frustrating” to see Liccardo’s bill stall and applauded his plans to file a discharge petition.

“I think people who care about this population and care about the integrity of America’s word should use every tool in their toolbox,” he said. “Once it’s opened, I think that’s when the real pressure can start. Members of Congress need to step up and be counted on this issue, and they’ve gotten a pass for a while now, particularly under this new administration. I’m looking forward to people being held accountable and having to be on the record on where they stand.”

Whether Liccardo and his co-sponsors have enough signatures remains to be seen; however, the congressman said that having “five Republican co-sponsors is certainly a very strong indication.” There are 214 Democrats serving in the House of Representatives.

The success of a discharge petition filed earlier this year to force a vote on a bill that would extend TPS for Haitian immigrants could also be another positive indicator for Liccardo’s bill — four Republican congressmembers signed the discharge petition alongside Democrats, to reach the 218 threshold.

A spokesperson for Johnson did not respond to a request to comment about the discharge petition, but told reporters last year that “I am not a fan of discharge petitions. It is typically used as a tool against the majority.”

Regardless of who wins control of the House on Nov. 3, Liccardo said that Republicans up for reelection might be more emboldened to sign on.

“After Election Day,” he said, “I’d like to believe we’re going to have a lot more interest from a lot of those Republicans, particularly a lot of the veterans who served in Afghanistan, who understand what a betrayal this has been to essentially abandon our promise to protect Afghans who risked their lives alongside U.S. troops.”

title: Ranking Members Lofgren and Amo Demand Answers After GAO Report Reveals Trump-Inflicted Damage to America’s Future Weather Satellites
text:
(Washington, DC) – Today, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) and Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo (D-RI) sent a letterto National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Administrator Neil Jacobs regarding NOAA’s GeoXO satellite program. GeoXO is the future fleet of the nation’s weather satellites scheduled to replace the current satellites in the 2030’s and collect life-saving data to support weather forecasting. In early 2025, the Trump administration demanded that NOAA cut the GeoXO program by 50% and exclusively focus on the Agency’s “weather data needs,” disguising blatant climate denialism as an effort to cut costs. GAO released its report on Friday, October 16, 2026, and found that the Trump administration’s actions “put vital observations at risk.”

“Two fewer satellites and three fewer scientific instruments are not line items in a budget,” Ranking Members Lofgren and Amo write in their letter. “They represent a concrete, tangible weakening of America’s ability to understand the weather, the climate, and the world around us.”

The Members continue: “We now confront the real possibility that America’s next generation of weather satellites will be no better – or even worse – than the generation in orbit today. As GAO concludes in its report, ‘it is unclear whether GeoXO will improve, or even continue, the functionality available in the current generation of satellites.’ That is an unacceptable notion, and we are determined to return this program to its proper path."

In closing, the Members focus in on the hypocrisy of the administration’s claims that these cancellations are to save costs, pointing to the war in Iran: “In exchange for a less advanced, less capable next generation of weather satellites, the only meager rationale the Trump Administration can muster is $6.6 billion in reduced lifecycle costs. At a time when the war in Iran has cost the country an estimated $38 billion and counting while President Trump proposes to spend another $1.2 trillion on checks intended to lessen the political fallout of that war, it is hard to think of a more foolish, self-defeating way to save money than by stripping capabilities from a weather satellite program of vital long-term national significance. The Trump Administration has the wrong priorities, but NOAA must get GeoXO right. We expect nothing less.”

Read the letter here.

title: Harris’s PARITY Act Garners Support from Coalition of Free-Market Organizations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Mark Harris’s (NC-08) Promoting Access and Revenue Integrity Through Institutional Transparency (PARITY) Act is gaining nationwide support from leading free-market organizations. Consumer Action for a Strong Economy (CASE) and a coalition of 12 other organizations and advocates recently sent a letter to House and Senate leaders urging passage of the legislation, which would repeal the 90/10 rule in the Higher Education Act. Under current law, the rule applies only to proprietary institutions and requires them to derive at least 10 percent of their revenue from non-federal sources.

“I’m grateful to CASE and the coalition of freedom-advocating organizations for their continued support and work to advance the PARITY Act in both chambers,” said Congressman Harris. “The 90/10 rule unfairly singles out career and vocational schools while allowing other institutions to operate under a different set of standards. Students deserve the freedom to choose the education and career path that best fits their goals, and the PARITY Act would end this outdated double standard and ensure workforce-focused institutions can continue preparing the skilled professionals our communities and local economies depend on.”

“We are in strong agreement that U.S. higher education policy should establish high, consistent performance standards and provide institutions the freedom to compete and innovate. We believe students should be able to access education options that best suit their learning and career goals,” the coalition wrote in its letter to Senate HELP Committee Chairman Bill Cassidy and House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg.

BACKGROUND:

Title IV of the Higher Education Act authorizes federal student aid programs such as Pell Grants and Direct Loans. Institutions seeking to participate in these programs must meet a variety of eligibility requirements.

The 90/10 rule is one of those eligibility requirements, but it applies only to proprietary institutions. Public and nonprofit institutions that also receive federal student aid are exempt.

Through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, Congress enacted a universal earnings and return-on-investment framework tied to Title IV eligibility that applies across institution types. This outcome-based accountability system makes the 90/10 rule redundant and outdated. In the House-passed version, House Republicans repealed 90/10 completely, but the repeal was not included in the Senate’s version that became law.

Senator Jim Banks (R-IN) is leading the Senate companion bill.

The full coalition letter can be foundhere.

The full text of the PARITY Act can be foundhere.

title: THOMPSON, DOGGETT PARTNER ON BILL EXPANDING MEDICARE BENEFITS TO COVER DENTAL, VISION, AND HEARING
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Ranking Member of the House Ways & Means Health Subcommittee, announced that his colleague Rep. Mike Thompson (D-CA) will lead the effort to pass Rep. Doggett’s Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act in the next congress. As Rep. Doggett prepares to retire, he has tapped Thompson to carry forward this crucial legislation expanding Medicare coverage to include dental, vision and hearing benefits.

“Maintaining one’s dental, hearing, and vision health is critical to ensuring good nutrition, preventing cognitive decline, stopping falls, and more. I’ve always believed that expanding older Americans’ access to these kinds of healthcare just makes sense,” said Thompson. “I’m honored to work with my colleague Rep. Lloyd Doggett lead the effort to expand Medicare benefits in the next Congress.”

“We seek to assure more comprehensive health coverage for the more than 66 million seniors and disabled individuals who rely on Medicare,” said Doggett. “Though so important to overall health, Medicare coverage continues to be very limited for dental, vision, and hearing services. This expanded care could help prevent cognitive impairment and dementia, worsened chronic disease, and imbalance leading to falls with deadly consequences. This is an essential step to fulfilling the original promise of Medicare—to assure dignity and health for all. I’m pleased to work with Rep. Thompson, who has supported this bill for many years, to ensure this important legislation is carried forward.”

BACKGROUND

Expanding Medicare to cover dental, hearing, and vision services is overwhelmingly popular: A Data for Progress poll conducted in 2024 found that 92 percent of Americans supported expanding Medicare to provide dental, vision and hearing benefits.

Over 24 million Medicare beneficiaries have no dental coverage at all and have to pay out-of-pocket or forego needed care. Further, more than one in three Medicare beneficiaries have difficulty seeing and more than two in five Medicare beneficiaries have difficulty hearing.

After Republicans in Congress cut $1 trillion from our health care system in order to pay for tax breaks for the top one percent, Doggett and Thompson are fighting to reverse these cuts and to make it easier for seniors and people with disabilities to go to the dentist, audiologist and optometrist.

The Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act updates the Medicare benefits package to ensure that all beneficiaries have access to crucial items and services that are important to their overall health. Senator Bernie Sander (I-VT) leads the companion bill in the U.S. Senate. The bill makes the following changes to federal law:

Repeals the outdated statutory exclusion that currently prohibits Medicare from covering most dental, vision, and hearing care.

Expands Medicare benefits to include items and services such as dentures, preventative and emergency dental care; refractive eye exams and eyeglasses; and hearing aids and exams.

Provides for appropriate payment to health providers through Medicare Part B.

The Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act is endorsed by: Center for Medicare Advocacy, Community Catalyst, Public Citizen, Social Security Works, Center for Health and Democracy, MoveOn.org, Families USA, CareQuest Center for Oral Health, Justice in Aging, People’s Action, Medicare Rights Center and Advocates for Community Health.

title: Pallone, Booker Push to Protect Critical Fish That Sustain New Jersey’s Marine Wildlife and Fishing Industry
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) and Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) are calling for stronger protections for Atlantic menhaden, a small fish that plays an enormous role in New Jersey’s coastal ecosystem. Commonly known as bunker, menhaden are a vital food source for avian and marine wildlife. The lawmakers are urging the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (ASMFC) to significantly reduce fishing limits to ensure enough menhaden remain in the water to sustain the species that depend on them.

A 2025 scientific assessment found that the estimated average menhaden biomass was 37 percent lower than previously thought. The assessment also showed that cuts of 50 percent or more would be needed to reduce the likelihood of fishing pressure meeting or exceeding an ecological target designed to account for the food needs of striped bass. Despite those findings, the Commission reduced the coastwide catch limit by just 20 percent for 2026.

“This level of reduction is insufficient to address the ecological consequences of declining menhaden abundance. Reduced menhaden availability has been identified as the primary driver of low reproduction in ospreys throughout the Chesapeake Bay. A significant cut to the menhaden TAC is needed to prevent broad ecosystem impacts. We, therefore, urge the Commission to adopt a substantial reduction in the Atlantic menhaden TAC that reflects the best available science and supports the rebuilding of dependent species, and by extension the communities in our state and throughout the Atlantic Coast that rely on them,” the members wrote.

In a letter to ASMFC Atlantic Menhaden Management Board Chair Joe Cimino, Pallone and Booker warn that excessive menhaden harvesting, including industrial operations that process the fish into fish meal and oil, reduces the food available to predators throughout the Atlantic ecosystem. They argue that fishing limits must account not only for the health of the menhaden population itself, but also for the striped bass, bluefish and other species that depend on it.

The warning comes amid growing concerns about declining osprey reproduction along the Atlantic Coast. In New Jersey, researchers documented the state’s worst osprey breeding season in more than three decades in 2025. Research in the Chesapeake Bay has also identified reduced menhaden availability as a primary driver of poor osprey reproduction, underscoring the broader consequences of declining food supplies for coastal wildlife.

Mark Taylor states that, “As President of the Jersey Coast Anglers Association, with next year’s total allowable catch limits on the table, it’s vital that a major cut is made. We have been here before, and we saw our waters explode with life once the cutback was made back in 2013. Our member clubs all have watched menhaden disappear from New Jersey waters except for a short window in early spring and late fall. They’re gone. And when bunker disappear, everything that depends on them—striped bass, whales, tuna, dolphins, osprey, eagles—pays the price. We need fisheries managers to step in now and shut down industrial‑scale reduction fishing before it wipes out what’s left of the stock. At this point, a full stop on reduction fishing in the New Jersey–New York Bight isn’t just reasonable—it’s the only responsible move if we want our coastal ecosystem to recover.”

The Commission is expected to consider new coastwide fishing limits for 2027 through 2029 at its November meeting. Pallone and Booker are urging regulators to adopt a substantial reduction based on the best available science to protect New Jersey’s marine wildlife, recreational fishing communities and the health of the Atlantic Coast.

title: Rouzer Secures Federal Funding to Strengthen North Carolina’...

Corman to secure federal funding to modernize Raleigh and Fayetteville Railroad (RFCC), Carolina Lines (RJCS), and other rail lines to meet growing demand. I appreciate R.J. Corman’s commitment to these investments, which will strengthen North Carolina’s economy and the broader Southeast, enhance rail network resilience, and keep goods moving safely and efficiently.”

title: Congresswoman Schrier Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Wetland Habitats, Species in Washington State
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Congresswoman Val Hoyle (OR-04) and Congressman Ryan Zinke (MT-01) in introducing the Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program (NW VIP) Act, bipartisan legislation that would restore and protect wetland habitats and species in the Pacific Northwest. Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Sens. Mike Crapo (R-ID) and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

“Farmers, Tribes, and local communities across our region rely on wetlands and the species they protect,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I am proud that this bipartisan bill will take a meaningful step to make sure Washingtonians continue to benefit from these important habitats that are a critical part of our ecosystem.”

“Conservation is a team effort, and everyone needs to play their part,” said Congresswoman Hoyle. “Our bipartisan bill supports habitat restoration and active management of invasive species across Northwest wetlands that support Tribes, farmers and other local economies. This work will strengthen our climate resilience, supporting these lands for the next generation.”

“Good conservation starts by bringing everyone to the table,” said Congressman Zinke. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act gives farmers, ranchers, Tribes, sportsmen and local communities a way to work together on voluntary projects that restore wetlands and keep working lands working. That’s how we protect habitat and water for the next generation. I'm proud to support this legislation.”

BACKGROUND: The Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act would establish a federal grant and assistance program empowering government agencies, Tribes, nonprofits and landowners, among other entities, to work together in both restoring and enhancing habitats for wetland-dependent birds living in the Columbia River Basin and along the coast of Oregon and Washington.

These projects include water infrastructure and management and enhancement of vegetative habitat, which could be implemented on public, private, Tribal and other land determined by the U.S. Secretary of the Interior.

“We’re thankful to Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for introducing the Northwest Wetlands VIP Act in the House of Representatives. The future of conservation is on private working lands. This important legislation will bring much-needed resources for landowners to more effectively provide multi-benefits for people, wildlife, agriculture, and wetlands in the Northwest and the Columbia River Basin,” said Jeff McCreary, Director of Operations for the Western Region for Ducks Unlimited.

"Healthy wetlands are foundational to Washington’s economy, ecosystems, and communities,” said Washington Association of Land Trusts (WALT) Executive Director Erik Kingfisher. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act would provide much needed investments in enhancing, maintaining and restoring these vital lands across the Columbia River Basin, Washington coastal zone, and throughout the Puget Sound. As land trusts with the skills to make these projects happen across our beautiful state, we support this bipartisan legislation that would empower landowners through a voluntary, partnership-based approach to establish an open space legacy and enable the care and restoration of these lands to sustain them for future generations."

The Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act is endorsed by Ducks Unlimited, Pacific Birds Habitat Joint Venture, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership (TRCP), Trout Unlimited, Oregon Agricultural Trust, Washington State Audubon, Washington Association of Land Trusts and more.

title: Peters Leads San Diego Delegation in Demanding Explanation for ICE Surge at Schools and Other Sensitive Locations
text:
San Diego, CA. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led members of the San Diego Congressional delegation, Reps Juan Vargas (CA-52), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), and Mike Levin (CA-49), and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) in a letter to U.S. Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin on recent reports of increased immigration enforcement activity in San Diego and elsewhere in California. This comes a month after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of multiple U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrests outside their schools.

The Members cited more frequent reports and videos online of a growing presence of agents detaining individuals throughout San Diego. They stated that these practices are actually more harmful, as the “presence of ICE officers destabilizes the sense of safety schools offer and places an additional burden on school staff and local communities.”

The Members added that the “fear among students and families that these incidents cause can also negatively impact a student’s educational engagement, mental and physical health, academic performance, and developmental trajectories. Parents should be able to bring their children to class and return to pick them up without fearing that a routine school day could end in family separation. Teachers should be able to focus on teaching and students on learning.”

They also outlined how federal agents have been noted at other sensitive locations, such as hospitals, places of worship, and courthouses, which threatens the very safety these places are supposed to offer.

“When people are afraid to seek medical care, attend religious services, or appear in court, the consequences reach well beyond any individual arrest. These are places where people turn for help, and enforcement practices that discourage access leave entire communities less safe,” the Members added.

To address their concerns, the members demanded a response to the following questions;

Has DHS authorized an “Operation Safe California” or similar immigration enforcement operation for California? If so, what is the scope of the operation? Who authorized it? And when was it authorized?

Has DHS authorized enhanced immigration enforcement in San Diego, and, if so, how long is it expected to last? How many agents are involved?

Who are the intended targets, and what criteria govern whom officers or agents stop or detain?

Have officers or agents been directed or authorized to conduct enforcement at or near schools or other sensitive locations?

“San Diegans deserve a clear explanation of the federal activity being reported in our communities,” the Members concluded.

See the full letter here.

Background: As unregulated ICE activity has heavily increased throughout the second Trump Administration, Rep. Peters has called out DHS for allowing federal agents to terrorize communities without notice or consequences, leaving communities less safe.

Shortly after the arrests at San Diego schools, Rep. Peters hosted a virtual training event with Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) to ensure community members understand how to safely interact with federal law enforcement officers, what to do if they or their loved ones are detained by agents, and what resources are available to San Diego’s immigrant community.

And last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, which would establish stronger standards for immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict the use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Republicans to pass these commonsense reforms, but they have continued to block this bill from a vote.

title: Thompson, Colleagues Introduce Resolution Designating “Careers in Energy Week,” Recognizes the American Energy Industry Workforce
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) introduced a bipartisan resolution to designate the week of October 19 through October 23 as “Careers in Energy Week.” This resolution celebrates the contributions of our country’s highly skilled and growing energy workforce and encourages partnerships between industry and schools to highlight career pathways that strengthen local economies and the energy industry. Rep. Thompson was joined by Reps. Troy Carter (D-La.), Dan Meuser (R-Pa.), Henry Cuellar (D-Texas), Ryan Mackenzie (R-Pa.), Marc Veasey (D-Texas), and Thomas Kean Jr. (R-N.J.).

“The U.S. is a global leader when it comes to energy production, and the bipartisan Careers in Energy Week resolution recognizes the millions of hard working men and women who deliver safe and reliable energy, while highlighting the rewarding career opportunities available for students and adult learners,” Rep. Thompson said.

“Pennsylvania’s rural electric cooperatives are powered by a dedicated workforce committed to ensuring safe, reliable and affordable power. We commend Chairman Thompson for leading our Commonwealth and our nation in recognizing the importance of these jobs and raising awareness during “Careers in Energy Week.” These professionals are vital to our communities because they keep the lights on for all of us – and we’re looking to the next generation to learn these trades and do the same,” said Pennsylvania Rural Electric Association and Allegheny Electric Cooperative President and CEO Steve Brame.

“Careers in Energy Week recognizes energy professionals – those who keep our country running - while also highlighting the generational need to recruit people to and prepare them for energy careers. In-demand roles span the skilled trades, engineering, technology and business operations. This observational week is a signal for career-ready adults and students to explore dynamic energy careers that are essential to our communities, our economy, national security, and American life,” said Center for Energy Workforce Development Executive Director Missy Henrickson.

This resolution is supported by the Pennsylvania Rural Electric Association, National Rural Electric Cooperative Association, American Gas Association, American Petroleum Institute, American Public Gas Association, American Public Power Association, American Clean Power Association, Association of Energy Services Professionals, Clean Power Institute, Edison Electric Institute, Electric Power Research Institute, Hydropower Foundation, Interstate Natural Gas Association of America Foundation, National Mining Association, and Nuclear Energy Institute.

title: Congressman Tim Moore Announces Over $871 Million in Federal Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery Across North Carolina
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) announced more than $871 million in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for Hurricane Helene recovery across North Carolina, including the 14th Congressional District. Funding will go to the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT), U.S. Forest Service, and Eastern Federal Lands Division to support critical highway and transportation system repairs.

“The impact of Hurricane Helene is still being felt today, and now over $871 million is headed to North Carolina to help address this lasting damage,”said Congressman Moore. “From repairing highways like I-40 to rebuilding the roads in our national forests, these dollars will help restore the critical transportation infrastructure our communities depend on. I appreciate the Administration and the folks at DOT for helping ensure Western North Carolina’s recovery keeps moving forward.”

$858,000,000 will go to the North Carolina Department of Transportation to restore damaged areas of the federal highway system, including I-40, following Hurricane Helene. Numerous areas throughout the state experienced significant damage including flash flooding, landslides, rock fall, washouts, pipe blowouts, undermining, scour, bridge collapse, and downed trees. This funding will restore North Carolina federal highway systems to pre-disaster condition.

$13,250,000 will go to the Eastern Federal Lands Division and the U.S. Forest Service to repair North Carolina National Forests transportation systems that were affected by Hurricane Helene. This funding will support the full restoration of roadbeds and bridges, landslides and debris blocked roads, and culverts.

title: Rep. Tlaib introduces bill to restore temporary protected status for Yemen
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) introduced a bill to restore temporary protected status for Yemen, which the Trump administration officially terminated in July, following a legal battle. Conditions in countries designated for TPS are too dangerous for people to return safely. Those who qualify for TPS are allowed to remain in the U.S. temporarily.

Yemen is facing one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises amid an ongoing civil war and foreign siege and military intervention, including the Trump administration’s bombing of the country last year. The Department of State has placed Yemen under a Level 4 “Do Not Travel” advisory, citing violence, kidnapping, landmines and unexploded ordinances, as well as the re-emergence of diseases like cholera, polio, and measles.

Michigan, especially Rep. Tlaib’s district, is home to large Yemeni communities.

“The Trump administration is threatening our Yemeni neighbors, and I will not stand for it. DHS unjustly terminated temporary protected status for Yemen without care for the ongoing humanitarian catastrophe and escalating armed conflict facing the country,” said Rep. Tlaib. “The Trump administration was bombing civilians in Yemen as recently as last year and is currently trying to give the Saudi monarchy billions of dollars in bombs and jets to continue the devastation. The State Department explicitly warns against any travel to Yemen, and yet, this president wants to send our neighbors back as part of his racist mass deportation agenda. I am proud to represent one of the most Yemeni districts in the country. These are our family members, coworkers, friends, and neighbors. They belong here, and I will not turn my back on them.”

In April, Rep. Tlaib led 23 Members of Congress in urging the Trump administration to halt its planned termination of TPS for Yemen. Conditions in the country have only deteriorated since then.

The Yemen TPS Act is cosponsored by 14 Members of Congress: U.S. Reps. André Carson (IN-07), Jim Costa (CA-21), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-at large), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

The bill is also endorsed by 50 organizations: Adhikaar For Human Rights and Social Justice, African Communities Together (ACT), American Friends Service Committee (AFSC), Arab America, Arab American Family Support Center, Arab American Heritage Council (AAHC), Arab American Institute (AAI), Arkansas Community Organizations, Asian American Legal Defense and Education Fund, Center for Constitutional Rights, Center for Gender & Refugee Studies, Center for Nonviolent Solutions, Climate Refugees, Council on American-Islamic Relations, Democratic Progressive Caucus of Florida, Families For Freedom, Flint Alliance for Immigrant Rights, Grantmakers Concerned with Immigrants and Refugees (GCIR), Hindus for Human Rights Action, Houston Immigration Legal Services Collaborative, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights, Immigrant Defenders Law Center (ImmDef), Immigration Justice Action Team, Indivisible Mass Coalition, Justice Is Global, Kino Border Initiative, MADRE, Majdal: Arab Community Center of San Diego, Migrant Roots Media, Migrant Support Collective, Muslim Advocates, Muslims for Just Futures, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Network for Arab American Communities (NNAAC), National Partnership for New Americans, Never Again Action, Nicaraguan American Legal Defense and Education Fund (NALDEF), NM CAFe (Comunidades en Accion y de Fe), No Concentration Camps US, No Detention Centers in Michigan, NorCal Resist, North Shore Sides With Love, Northern Indivisible, Oasis Legal Services, ReThinking Foreign Policy, RootsAction, Syrian Community Network, United We Dream Network, We are CASA, Yemen Relief and Reconstruction Foundation.

title: Congressman Van Drew Congratulates Cape May on Desalination Plant Groundbreaking
text:
Washington, DC -Today, Congressman Van Drew congratulated Cape May on breaking ground on its new water desalination plant, a major investment in the area's drinking water supply.

Congressman Van Drew helped move the project forward by securing $1.75 million in Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) community project funding and $500,000 to support the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' involvement. He also helped authorize up to $40 million in additional federal assistance through the Water Resources Development Act. The project received another $8 million through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Rep. Van Drew supported, and he worked with Cape May to help advance its funding application through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection.

"We have been working with Cape May for quite some time to get the federal government involved and bring the necessary funding here," said Congressman Van Drew. "This is an important investment for the entire area, from our residents and local businesses to our schools, emergency services, and Coast Guard Training Center, which is undergoing a historic expansion. I am proud we could help make this happen. There is still work ahead, but this groundbreaking is a big step, and I congratulate Cape May on reaching it."

title: Rep. Vasquez Demands Answers From Forest Service on Trail Maintenance and Wildfire Preparedness
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), joined by 12 colleagues, sent a letter to U.S. Forest Service (USFS) leadership demanding answers on the agency’s efforts to maintain trails on public lands, which would ensure access to recreation and protect local communities from heightened fire risk. The letter follows up on an earlier letter raising concerns that USFS actions dramatically reduced the agency’s ability to adequately maintain public trails. That request followed a concerning report detailing a “trail maintenance crisis” with “impassable trails” and “unsafe bridges” due to staffing and budget cuts implemented by the Administration, leading to heightened wildfire risk.

“In April, I demanded answers from the Forest Service after concerning reports of our trails falling into disarray,” said Vasquez. “This is an urgent issue – my constituents know that overgrown brush increases wildfire risk, and the more there is this season, the more dangerous it becomes next season. This is a completely unnecessary risk – we have the tools to protect our communities, and I am calling on the Forest Service to use them.”

Read the full letter HERE.

Vasquez has fought to promote outdoor recreation, protect New Mexico’s public lands and reduce wildfire risks for rural communities throughout his time in Congress, including:

Supporting the bipartisan Fix Our Forests Act: Vasquez cosponsored and voted to pass legislation to improve forest management, reduce hazardous vegetation that fuels catastrophic wildfires, strengthen wildfire prevention and protect communities from devastating fires.

Holding USDA Accountable for Forest Service Staffing Cuts: Vasquez pressed USDA Secretary Rollins on how cuts to USFS personnel threaten wildfire preparedness, trail maintenance and public safety, emphasizing the critical role Forest Service crews play in maintaining trails, supporting firefighters and protecting rural communities.

Opposing the Administration’s USFS Restructuring: Vasquez pushed back against the Administration’s plans to close 57 Forest Service research stations and slash the agency’s workforce, warning that these cuts would undermine wildfire prevention, weaken forest management and threaten outdoor recreation opportunities across New Mexico.

The letter asks USFS to respond by October 30 and to provide updated information on the following:

Seasonal hiring: How many of the “up to 2,000” promised non-fire seasonal employees were hired and onboarded before the field season, where they were assigned, how many were primarily focused on trail work, and how many miles of trail they maintained.

Staff vacancies: How many trail maintenance positions are currently vacant, how the agency addressed the “critical field level vacancies” it identified, and which forests and ranger districts are most affected, following a 2025 internal report indicating some forest units had lost their entire trails staff.

Funding: Whether the agency can determine what it spends on staff and expenses for its trail program, and how that level has changed over the last two decades in inflation-adjusted dollars.

Volunteers and partners: How many people participated in the adopt-a-trail program this season, how many miles they maintained, how administrative burdens were reduced for partners, and how the agency is ensuring volunteers are trained and operating safely.

The backlog: How many miles of trail are in the maintenance backlog, and what federal funding would be needed to address it.

The proposed cut: Why the Forest Service’s budget justification proposes cutting the Capital Improvement and Maintenance, Trails line from $22 million in the FY26 enacted level to $8 million in the White House’s FY27 budget, a reduction of roughly two-thirds.

The ten-year goal: Whether the agency is on track to meet the objectives of its Ten-Year Trail Stewardship Challenge by 2030, and what barriers stand in the way.

title: Vindman Introduces Two Bills to Crack Down on Corruption and Strengthen Government Accountability
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) introduced two pieces of legislation that would crack down on corruption, strengthen government ethics standards, and ensure that public officials are held accountable for misconduct.

The two bills would close gaps in federal ethics and accountability laws by preventing lobbyists convicted of serious corruption-related offenses from holding senior positions in the executive branch and extending the period during which individuals can be prosecuted for lying to Congress.

“For too long, Washington has operated under a different set of rules, where well-connected insiders can abuse their positions of influence, mislead Congress, and evade accountability. That erodes public trust in our institutions and undermines the very foundation of our democracy. When individuals lie to Congress or exploit their connections for personal gain, there must be real consequences,” said Vindman. “These bills will close dangerous loopholes in our ethics laws, strengthen congressional oversight, and make clear that no one is above the law. The American people deserve leaders who serve the public interest, and I will continue fighting to hold Washington to that standard.”

The No Corrupt Lobbyists in Government Act would prohibit individuals who have been registered lobbyists within the past 10 years and have final criminal convictions for bribery, ethics violations or acting as unregistered foreign agents from serving in senior executive branch positions. The legislation would require current and prospective appointees to certify their eligibility and direct the Office of Government Ethics to screen candidates in coordination with the FBI and Department of Justice. Violators would face removal and financial penalties. Click here to read the full bill text.

The Honesty in Government Act would extend the statute of limitations for making false statements to Congress from five to 10 years. Congressional investigations can stretch across multiple presidential administrations, allowing individuals to evade accountability by delaying proceedings until the statute of limitations expires. The legislation would give prosecutors additional time to pursue cases involving false statements, concealment and fraudulent representations made during congressional oversight proceedings. Click here to read the full bill text.

BACKGROUND

This legislative package builds on Vindman’s broader efforts to combat corruption and strengthen government accountability.

This Congress, Vindman introduced the Sell Your Stocks or Step Down Act, legislation requiring senior government officials to divest their individual stocks before taking office and eliminating a special capital gains tax break associated with those sales.

He also introduced the bipartisan No Profiting from Public Service Act — legislation to prohibit public officials from trading individual stocks and participating in prediction markets — and the bipartisan Banning Lobbying and Safeguarding Trust (BLAST) Act, which would prohibit members of Congress from lobbying Congress after leaving office.

title: Walberg Signs VP's Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud
text:
Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) joined Vice President JD Vance in the fight against fraud by signing a pledge to ensure that American programs only benefit law-abiding citizens.

"Each year, fraudsters steal billions of dollars from hardworking Americans and taxpayer-funded programs," said Rep. Walberg. "Programs should support real American families, rather than fraudsters. I'm proud to join the Vice President in the fight against fraud to provide stronger protections for vulnerable Americans and hold fraudsters accountable. As Chair of the Education and Workforce Committee, I have been working with my colleagues to crack down on fraud in federal student aid and child care assistance programs. We must build on these efforts to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure support goes to those who need it, rather than those exploiting the system."

The Pledge reads:

I pledge to join the fight and do everything in my power to ensure that:

1. Vulnerable Americans, such as the elderly, indigent, and disabled, are protected from fraudsters who seek to prey on them.

2. Taxpayer-funded programs serve law-abiding Americans, not illegal aliens or fraudsters.

3. Taxpayer-funded benefits are not used by fraudsters to buy mansions or luxury cars.

4. Public agencies and officials work tirelessly and aggressively, coordinating at all levels of government, to stop fraud before payments go out the door.

5. Fraudsters face justice for their crimes in a court of law. Convicted fraudsters will be imprisoned and barred from ever receiving another penny of taxpayer dollars.

6. Illegal alien fraudsters are promptly arrested, prosecuted, imprisoned, and deported, never able to take advantage of Americans’ generosity again.

Background

Recent reports by the Government Accountability Office estimate that up to $521 billion are lost to fraud each year.

As Chairman of the Education and Workforce Committee, Rep. Walberg ushered legislation through the House to strengthen oversight and institute safeguards against fraud in federal student aid and child care programs. The No Aid for Ghost Students Act and Stop Child Care Scams Act would strengthen oversight and protect taxpayer dollars.

Rep. Walberg also sent letters to Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison earlier this year following reports of widespread fraud in Minnesota's Child Care Assistance Program.

title: Wasserman Schultz Statement on Suspicious Envelope Received by Her Office
text:
Sunrise, FL – Today, U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25) released the following statement regarding the arrival of a suspicious envelope, similar to those received around the country by Members of Congress, to her Sunrise district office:

"Today, like many other Members of Congress, my district office received a suspicious letter that was clearly designed to intimidate me and my staff. It will not work. Thankfully, Sunrise Police, local first responders, the FBI, and the U.S. Postal Service acted swiftly to ensure the safety of my staff and the other public servants who work in the same building. While initial tests were negative for any hazardous material, law enforcement will do further analysis as they continue their larger investigation.

"Sadly, this is not the first time my office has received threatening mail. Right before the 2018 election, improvised explosive devices were sent to prominent Democrats, media, and my office with the same terrorizing goal in mind. Such cowardly acts of coercion will not work and have absolutely no place in our politics. My hope is that all sides will condemn these weak, desperate attempts to bully their opponents. And to be clear, they will not deter me from fully representing my Broward County constituents."

####

title: Sen. Banks Applauds Nomination of Joseph Falvey to Serve on the U.S. District Court for Northern Indiana
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) released the following statement applauding President Trump’s nomination of Joseph Falvey to serve as a judge on the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Indiana. Joseph Falvey is the first judicial nominee to the Northern District of Indiana of the second Trump administration.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Joe Falvey has been a warrior for everything that makes America great. He served our country honorably in Afghanistan and has been helping Adam Mildred keep the Northern District of Indiana safe as an Assistant U.S. Attorney. I look forward to supporting his nomination and urge my colleagues to join me.”

Background:

Joseph Falvey is currently an Assistant U.S. Attorney, serving as Chief of the Appellate Division. He is a graduate of Yale Law School and the University of Notre Dame and previously worked at Jones Day as an Associate in the firm’s Issues & Appeals practice. Falvey clerked in the office of the Indiana Attorney General, and he also clerked for Chief Justice John Roberts and Judges Thomas Griffith of the D.C. Circuit and Dabney Friedrich of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. Falvey is a Marine Corps veteran and a Pat Tillman scholar.
