title: SENATOR MCCORMICK OUTLINES STRATEGY TO OUTCOMPETE CHINA IN A SPEECH ATTHE HUDSON INSTITUTE
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) today delivered remarks at the Hudson Institute outlining a strategy for the United States to outcompete the Chinese Communist Party by maintaining America’s technological edge, rebuilding industrial capacity, strengthening alliances, and defending the principles of freedom that underpin American leadership.

Watch Senator McCormick’s full remarks and fireside chat here:

Following his remarks, Senator McCormick joined former U.S. Representative and Hudson Institute Distinguished Fellow Mike Gallagher for a fireside discussion on U.S.-China relations, the role of allies and partners in America’s Indo-Pacific strategy, and how the United States can harness technology, industrial capacity, and allied strength to prevail in the strategic competition with China.

The event followed Senator McCormick’s recent official travel to Japan and South Korea, where he met with senior government, defense, and business leaders and visited the Korean Demilitarized Zone. In his remarks, McCormick argued that a successful strategy toward China will increasingly depend on strengthening America’s relationships with allies like Japan and South Korea.

“Two hundred and fifty years ago, our founders conceived a radical new nation, and it was dedicated to liberty and the creed that all men and women are created equal. Thomas Paine put it simply: ‘The cause of America is in a great measure the cause of all mankind.’ That’s why freedom-loving people around the world take risks, sometimes enormous ones, to be our friends, to be part of America,” said Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA). “And our commitment to freedom is not simply an ideal. It’s a source of national power. It’s who we are, but it’s who we project and what we project in the world. In the coldest realpolitik terms, a freer world makes America stronger.”

During the speech, Senator McCormick laid out four measures for determining whether the United States is succeeding in its competition with China:

Winning the innovation race,

Building more and faster while ensuring American workers prosper,

Strengthening alliances that can out-innovate and out-build China alongside the United States,

And confidently defending the values of freedom that have long strengthened American leadership.

You can review the Senator’s full remarks, as prepared, here.

title: Merkley, Wyden, Hoyle: $205 Million Federal Investment Coming to Port of Coos Bay Rail Project
text:
Coos Bay, OR – Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden joined U.S. Representative Val Hoyle (OR-04) today to announce $204,771,601 in federal funds for the Coos Bay Rail Line (CBRL) Upgrades Project in support of the Pacific Coast Intermodal Port Project (PCIP). This funding will go towards final design and construction of critical upgrades to address capacity and reliability, improve system and service performance of the Coos Bay Rail Line, and ensure the upgraded rail line will be able to sustain the PCIP’s proposed ship-to-rail connection.

“As Speaker of the Oregon House, I helped save the Coos Bay Rail Line because I saw how critical the Port of Coos Bay was to all those who call Oregon’s rural South Coast home. Congresswoman Hoyle, Senator Wyden, and I have worked together to secure this transformative federal investment. The grant will bring us closer to the Port of Coos Bay becoming the first fully ship-to-rail port facility on the West Coast—a watershed moment for the region and our state,” said Merkley. “The Port of Coos Bay project stands to create economic opportunities for working families by creating good-paying, local union jobs, and together, we’ll get this project over the finish line.”

“What great news for the South Coast and all of Oregon that the teamwork with Senator Merkley, Congresswoman Hoyle plus state and local officials has produced such a massive federal investment in this innovative rail project,” said Wyden. “This is a huge vote of confidence in the Port of Coos Bay’s fresh approach to generate thousands of good-paying jobs in our state and expand supply chain capacity for all of America. It’s more important than ever now to keep working to ensure this project stays moving forward.”

“We’re thrilled to see this game changing $204 million investment from the DOT to upgrade the Coos Bay rail line,” said Hoyle. “So many people worked incredibly hard to get us this far. These investments are transformational for communities across the South Coast and our supply chain resilience.”

“This is a defining moment for Oregon’s South Coast and a tremendous step forward for the Pacific Coast Intermodal Port,” said Kyle Stevens, President of the Oregon International Port of Coos Bay Board of Commissioners. “This $205 million investment recognizes the national significance of the project and puts us on a path toward constructing the critical rail infrastructure needed to bring a new West Coast container gateway to life. Oregon’s federal delegation has been a steadfast champion for our coastal communities, and we are grateful for their leadership in helping secure an investment that will create economic opportunities for generations to come.”

This latest funding to the Port of Coos Bay comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, which supports projects that modernize America’s freight and intercity passenger rail infrastructure to move people and goods. Earlier this year, Merkley, Wyden, and Hoyle announced over $11 million in federal funds from a Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP) grant for the Port of Coos Bay rail project.

title: Senator Moody Leads Delegation of Florida Congressional Members in Support of Major Emergency Disaster Declaration for Isaias Recovery
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Moody is leading a congressional effort urging the President to approve Gov. Ron DeSantis’s request for a Major Emergency Disaster Declaration. Senator Moody made multiple trips to communities struck by Hurricane Isaias with Governor DeSantis to assess damage and listen to local officials about what Florida needs to recover. Senator Moody continues to work closely with administration and state officials to facilitate the quick provision of aid to affected communities.

“In the wake of Hurricane Isaias, we remain focused on helping Florida families and communities recover from the devastating damage across the Panhandle and Gulf Coast. We’ve now secured the support of nearly every member of Florida’s congressional delegation in our effort urging the President to approve the state’s major emergency disaster declaration, and I will continue working closely with both state and federal officials to help get critical disaster assistance to those who need it most as quickly as possible,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

The major emergency disaster declaration will include both public and individual assistance.

Senator Moody is joined by Sen. Rick Scott and Reps. Aaron Bean, Gus Bilirakis, Vern Buchanan, Kat Cammack, Kathy Castor, Mario Diaz-Balart, Byron Donalds, Neal Dunn, Randy Fine, Lois Frankel, Scott Franklin, Maxwell Frost, Carlos Gimenez, Mike Haridopolos, Laurel Lee, Anna Paulina Luna, Brian Mast, Jared Moskowitz, Jimmy Patronis, John Rutherford, Maria Salazar, Darren Soto, Greg Steube, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Daniel Webster and Frederica Wilson in urging President Trump to approve the state’s declaration.

View the letter here.

Ahead of Isaias, Senator Moody joined Governor Ron DeSantis to discuss preparedness efforts, including the mobilization of thousands of National Guard members. After the storm, Senator Moody and Governor DeSantis conducted an on-the-ground assessment of some of the damage and thanked Guard members for their response efforts.

Senator Moody continues working to secure long-sought FEMA disaster funds for hard-hit Florida communities. Since taking office, Senator Moody has recovered more than $2.4 billion for Florida.

Senator Moody introduced the TRACK Act (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process, which has now been passed into law.

The TRACK Act mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress.

If Floridians need help with federal agencies in the aftermath of Isaias, Senator Moody’s office can assist—visit Moody.Senate.Gov to learn more.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Recognizes Plant City Police Sergeant for Life-Saving Actions
text:
PLANT CITY, Fla.—Senator Ashley Moody presented a Florida’s Finest Award to a Plant City Police Sergeant who saved a man’s life. In September, Sgt. Billy Harvester responded to a call for help, where he found a man lying unconscious. Sgt. Harvester determined the man to be suffering from a cardiac arrest, and he immediately responded, grabbing an AED from his patrol car, using it to shock the man back into consciousness and then performed CPR procedures until paramedics showed up—saving the man’s life. Senator Moody’s Florida’s Finest Award is presented to law enforcement officers or citizens for extraordinary lifesaving efforts.

“Law enforcement officers have to be ready to face anything when the call comes in—and Sgt. Harvester showed he was ready and capable when responding to that fateful call in September, grabbing his AED and saving a man’s life. I’m grateful for all that Sgt. Harvester and other officers do every day to protect Floridians, and I’m honored to present Sgt. Harvester with a Florida’s Finest Award,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

On Sept. 19, 2026, Sgt. Harvester responded to a residence regarding an unresponsive male with a known history of cardiac issues dating back to childhood. Recognizing the potential seriousness of the call, Sergeant Harvester demonstrated excellent judgment and preparedness by retrieving an AED from his patrol vehicle before entering the residence.

Upon entering the residence, Sergeant Harvester located the male upstairs and determined that he was in cardiac arrest. Sergeant Harvester immediately applied the AED, which analyzed the patient’s heart rhythm and advised that a shock was necessary. Sergeant Harvester administered the shock and immediately continued lifesaving efforts by performing CPR.

Sergeant Harvester continued CPR until the patient began breathing on his own. The man’s condition improved significantly prior to being transported from the residence.

Sergeant Harvester’s quick assessment of the situation, foresight in bringing the AED into the residence, immediate application of the device, and effective administration of CPR were instrumental in restoring the patient’s vital functions.

Senator Moody’s Florida’s Finest Awards honor citizens or law enforcement officers who demonstrate selfless courage and go above and beyond to save lives.

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Local Leaders Highlight Peters’ Leadership in Strengthening the Future of Selfridge Air National Guard Base
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, local leaders highlight Peters’ long-time efforts to strengthen the future of Selfridge Air National Guard Base. Throughout his time in the Senate, Peters has worked tirelessly to secure the base’s new KC-46A tanker aircraft and F15-EX fighter jets, two long-term, next-generation missions that will cement the base’s integral role in U.S. defense strategy for decades to come. Additionally, Peters secured funding and legislation to establish the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Northern Border Mission Center at Selfridge, which will ensure the base continues to play a critical role in both U.S. national and homeland security. The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“You think about Selfridge and there’s always been concern whether they are going to put something out or get rid of the base itself,” said Mark Hackel, Macomb County Executive. “But that concern has lessened over the years with people like Gary and other support that we have from our federal delegation.”

“Selfridge Air National Guard Base is custom ready to provide Northern Border Security,” said Macomb County Public Works Commissioner and former Michigan U.S. Congresswoman Candice Miller. “There has never been a question in my mind that Gary Peters is going to be there standing up for the people of Michigan. I can’t overstate how excited the community is, not just because of all the personnel that is going to be coming here, but the investment that’s going to happen.”

“He was relentless. He has always been a champion for Selfridge,” said Vicky Rowinski, Macomb County Director of Planning and Economic Development. “It was a big win with the F-15EXs that we now have a new fighter mission.”

Watch the “On the Job” video here.

Peters has made supporting the future of Selfridge Air National Guard Base a top priority. Prior to the F-15EX basing announcement in April 2025, Peters sent a letter urging the Air Force to base a new fighter mission at Selfridge. In 2025, Peters introduced bipartisan legislation seeking to preserve the U.S. Air Force’s fighter force structure and support the recapitalization of Air National Guard fighter missions, including at Selfridge. In January 2024, Peters helped announce that the U.S. Air Force selected Selfridge to host a new squadron of twelve KC-46A refueling tankers. This announcement came shortly after Peters led a bipartisan, bicameral group of Michigan delegation members in urging then-U.S. Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall to select Selfridge for a new squadron of these next-generation tankers, which will be deployed by the U.S. Air Force for at least the next 50 years.

To further strengthen Selfridge’s role in U.S. national and homeland security efforts, Peters established the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Northern Border Mission Center. Peters secured $3 million in March 2024 to operate this Center at Selfridge, where it is collocated with current DHS components. The Center will coordinate with state, local, and Tribal governments, and other key stakeholders, to ensure DHS and its operational components are able to fulfill their security mission at the Northern Border.

title: Peters Demands Answers on Wasteful Spending, Lack of Oversight of $260 Billion in DHS Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Gary Peters (D-MI), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding answers about wasteful spending, questionable contracting decisions, and a lack of oversight of more than $260 billion in funding provided to DHS through the Republican-passed One Big Beautiful Bill Act and the Secure America Act. Peters highlighted numerous instances of the Department mismanaging taxpayer dollars and raised concerns that insufficient safeguards and oversight could lead to further waste, fraud, and abuse.

“While the Trump Administration has claimed it is committed to maximizing government efficiency and reducing waste and abuse, current DHS spending and its lack of planning for any meaningful oversight of that spending raises questions about the sincerity of this commitment,” Peters wrote.

In his letter, Peters highlighted several examples of waste and mismanagement within the Department, including Customs and Border Protection awarding border wall construction contracts despite the federal government lacking access to more than half of the 700 miles where construction is planned, potentially leaving taxpayers on the hook for costly penalties. The letter also details how DHS wasted $20.5 million purchasing warehouses for immigration detention, only to later decide to sell those same properties.

Peters also raised concerns about reports that Secretary Mullin has used a Gulfstream G700 luxury jet for trips to his home state of Oklahoma and authorized the purchase of 12 additional aircraft, including five luxury jets. He also highlighted reporting that DHS used taxpayer dollars to purchase television advertisements prominently featuring President Trump, potentially in violation of federal law. Peters demanded answers about how the Department is preventing wasteful spending, ensuring accountability, and safeguarding taxpayer dollars

“Despite this suspected rampant waste and abuse of billions of taxpayer dollars, this Republican-controlled Congress has shown no appetite to exercise its constitutional oversight responsibilities. As a result, this abdication of Congress’s constitutional responsibility will almost surely amount to record levels of taxpayer-funded waste, fraud, and abuse,” Peters wrote.

During committee consideration of Republicans’ Secure America Act in June, Peters pushed for a vote on an amendment to the legislation which would have directed nearly $1 billion to the DHS Office of Inspector General for independent oversight of the Department. Republicans unanimously voted down the proposal.

title: Sen. Rick Scott Urges FCC to Keep Communist Chinese Companies on “Covered List”
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Rick Scott sent a letter to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr urging the FCC to keep Communist Chinese companies SZ DJI Technology Co. (DJI) and Autel Robotics Co. (Autel) on its “Covered List” despite the companies’ challenges to the designations. Senator Scott outlined years of Congressional oversight and cited clear national security concerns with DJI and Autel, including sensitive American data being funneled back to the CCP.

Senator Scott secured the passage of the Countering CCP Drones and Supporting Drones for Law Enforcement Act in the 2025 National Defense Authorization Act, adding these Chinese drone manufacturers to the U.S. government’s official list of communications equipment deemed a national security risk, banning them from U.S. markets.

Senator Rick Scott wrote, “Not only do DJI and Autel present unacceptable national security risks through data exfiltration risks and their support to America’s adversaries, but they have also been subsidized by the CCP, enabling them to destroy American manufacturing businesses. Since 2015, China has flooded the global market with artificially low-priced DJI and Autel drones subsidized by the Chinese government in an attempt to become the world’s drone factory. This illicit dumping has driven numerous American companies out of the market and out of business. The United States has a national security imperative to maintain a robust, resilient drone supply chain and industrial base. DJI and Autel have threatened that for years due to unfair trade practices.”

Senator Scott has worked for years to protect our country from the national security risks posed by drones manufactured in Communist China and has sought to prevent use of CCP drones by our government and military. He fought successfully to include an amendment in the FY 2025 NDAA that phases out licenses for new drone technology from companies like DJI and Autel, the former of which continuously evades oversight by reincorporating with new shell companies.

Read the full letter HERE or below:

Dear Chairman Carr:

I write today to object to the arguments outlined in the Petition for Reconsideration (Petition) filed by SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd. (DJI) and the Application for Review (AFR) filed by Autel Robotics Co., Ltd. (Autel) regarding the Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC) action to add DJI and Autel equipment to the Covered List. After years of classified briefings, investigations, letters, meetings, and hearings, it is clear to me that both DJI and Autel pose an unacceptable risk to the United States’ national security. I agree with the Administration’s determination that DJI and Autel present a national security threat and strongly support adding their technologies to the FCC’s Covered List.

In DJI’s Petition, the company erroneously states that prior to the passage of the Countering CCP Drones Act in the Fiscal Year 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) (P.L. 118-159), Congress did not conduct a thorough review of its technology to support the addition of DJI technology to the FCC’s Covered List. This argument is false. For multiple years, Congress investigated the threat DJI technologies pose to the United States through a series of classified briefings from the Intelligence Community and the Department of War (DOW), public hearings on the topic, meetings with industry representatives, and thorough analysis of public reporting and statements from DJI and Autel. As a result of this work, there are multiple bills, hearings, and letters in which both DJI and Autel are uniquely and publicly identified by Congress as presenting a national security risk to the United States.

Congress has repeatedly identified the data exfiltration risk posed by DJI equipment operating in America. In February 2022, the Countering CCP Drones Act, which specifically identifies DJI technology as a risk, was introduced for the first time in both the House and the Senate. Then-Senator Marco Rubio, a leading sponsor of the legislation, stated, “Chinese drone-maker DJI has repeatedly lied about its links to the Chinese Communist Party while collecting vast quantities of Americans’ data. The FCC should act immediately to further ban DJI by adding it to its Covered List.” The House unanimously passed the Countering CCP Drones Act, and it was signed into law as part of the FY25 NDAA (PL 118-159).

In 2024, the House Select Committee on China held a hearing titled, From High Tech to Heavy Steel: Combatting the PRC’s Strategy to Dominate Semiconductors, Shipbuilding, and Drones in which Committee Chairman John Moolenaar stated, “DJI, a Chinese firm, controls roughly 80 percent of the U.S. commercial drone market….congressional concern stems from the PRC having hundreds of thousands of spy-balloon equivalents operating daily across our Nation, not only jeopardizing our homeland but giving the PRC a dominant position in an industry that is already playing a key role on the front line of modern warfare.”

Through these letters, hearings, legislation, and meetings, Congress has urged the Executive Branch to take regulatory actions against DJI and Autel. As a result of this advocacy, Executive Branch agencies have taken multiple actions to limit DJI and Autel’s operations in the United States.

In 2017, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement bulletin stated that DJI “is providing U.S. critical infrastructure and law enforcement data to the Chinese government,” and that DJI drones were being used to “collect on U.S. critical assets.” In 2020, DJI was added to the Department of Commerce’s Entity List due to DJI’s facilitation of widespread human rights abuses in China through the use of its drones to surveil and monitor the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) detention camps in Xinjiang. In December 2021, the Department of the Treasury added DJI to its list of Chinese Military-Industrial Complex companies due to DJI’s support of biometric surveillance and tracking of ethnic and religious minorities in China. In October 2022, and recertified every year since, the DOW added DJI to its 1260H list of Chinese Military Companies due to DJI’s role in advancing the modernization efforts of China’s People’s Liberation Army. In addition to aiding the CCP in the brutal oppression of the Uyghur population and advancing modernization efforts of the PLA, DJI continues to export drones to America’s adversaries, including Russia and the cartels on our Southern Border.

The Department of Commerce added Autel to its Entity List in June 2024 due to its illicit shipments to Russia since the beginning of Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine and its attempts to acquire U.S. drone technology for use by the Chinese military. In 2025, the Pentagon added Autel to its list of Chinese Military Companies for its support in modernizing the People’s Liberation Army.

Not only do DJI and Autel present unacceptable national security risks through data exfiltration risks and their support to America’s adversaries, but they have also been subsidized by the CCP, enabling them to destroy American manufacturing businesses. Since 2015, China has flooded the global market with artificially low-priced DJI and Autel drones subsidized by the Chinese government in an attempt to become the world’s drone factory. This illicit dumping has driven numerous American companies out of the market and out of business. The United States has a national security imperative to maintain a robust, resilient drone supply chain and industrial base. DJI and Autel have threatened that for years due to unfair trade practices.

DJI’s Petition and Autel’s AFR also falsely assert that the U.S. Government did not do a review of their products prior to making the determination that its products present an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security. Following the addition of DJI and Autel to the Covered List, the DOW transmitted a classified report, in line with the requirements of Section 1709, detailing the threats posed by both DJI and Autel to the Congressional committees of jurisdiction. I have read and agree with the analysis detailed in the classified report concluding that DJI and Autel present an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security and that their technology should be on the FCC’s Covered List.

These Congressional and Executive Branch actions have been taken despite DJI and Autel’s extensive lobbying efforts, public media campaigns, and commissioned security reviews. Congress has reviewed DJI’s and Autel’s statements and reports and still confidently asserts that DJI and Autel present an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security.

For years, Congress has been working to remove DJI and Autel from the United States because of the threat they pose to the national and economic security of this country. I strongly support the Executive Branch’s actions to determine that these technologies present an unacceptable risk to our national security and their inclusion on the FCC’s Covered List. I look forward to continuing to work with you and the rest of the Administration to build out a strong American drone industrial base.

###

title: Sen. Rick Scott Visits Greece to Discuss NATO Security and Economic Cooperation with Greek Leaders
text:
ATHENS, Greece – This week, U.S. Senator Rick Scott, member of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee and Chairman of the U.S. Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower, traveled to Greece and met with Greek government leaders to discuss the U.S.-Greco alliance and America’s national security and economic interests in the Mediterranean. During his meetings, Senator Scott shared his goals for the U.S. and Greece to strengthen their collective security in Southeast Europe and the Mediterranean, enhance NATO cooperation among allies committed to the alliance’s collective security, and deter Russian aggression.

In Greece, Senator Scott met with members of the Greek Parliament, leadership of the Hellenic Coast Guard, Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis, Energy and Environment Minister Stavros Papastavrou, Chief of the Hellenic National Defense General Dimitrios Choupis, and Deputy Prime Minister Kostis Hatzidakis.

Senator Rick Scott said, “Greece is a crucial NATO ally, a reliable and credible partner to the United States, and our strategic relationship is actively reshaping the security and energy dynamics in Europe to advance American interests. Greece is the birthplace of democracy, and my meetings with leaders this week underscored Greece’s commitment to the United States and standing up against threats posed by the thuggish leaders in Russia and Turkey. America First requires a strong NATO, and Greece is a great example of the leadership America wants to see in Europe. Through our alliance, we are securing Southeast Europe, bolstering our own defenses, and ensuring the free world never bows to the tyranny of Putin and Erdogan.”

U.S. Senator Rick Scott meets with Deputy Prime Minister Kostis Hatzidakis in Athens, Greece on October 16, 2026.

title: Rosen Announces $3 Million in Federal Funding She Secured for Nevada Northern Railway
text:
ELY, NV – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) announced that she secured $3 million in federal funding to restore the Nevada Northern Railway. This funding was awarded through the Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Grant Program, which Senator Rosen helped fund through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that she helped write and pass. The federal funding will go toward the rehabilitation of nearly 127 miles of the 120-year-old rail corridor in White Pine and Elko Counties. The project will also reconnect the corridor to the national railroad system for the first time since 1999.

“For over a century, the Nevada Northern Railway has been a staple of Northern Nevada – first to serve copper mines in the area, and now as a historic and cultural destination,” said Senator Rosen. “I am proud to have secured the funding for the rehabilitation of one of Nevada’s most historic railways. I will continue supporting Nevada’s transportation and tourism industries by working to secure resources and funding for projects across Nevada.”

As a member of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Senator Rosen has been a strong advocate for Nevada’s transportation needs. This year, she helped secure $25 million in federal funding for the Sun Valley Boulevard Corridor in Northern Nevada. Last year, Senator Rosen joined Senate colleagues to demand that the Trump Administration stop funding cuts and prioritize safety following mass layoffs and the firing of essential transportation safety employees. She also helped secure critical funding to improve transportation for Tribal communities in Nevada.

title: SCHUMER, GILLIBRAND DELIVER $20+ MILLION FOR CRITICAL RAILWAY REPAIRS IN ROCHESTER-FINGER LAKES REGION & SUPPORT MAJOR BUSINESSES THAT RELY ON RAILWAY
text:
New Fed Funding Includes $11M To Replace Ten Miles Of Track In Wayne County And Nearly $10M To Replace Forty Miles Of Track Between Brockport And Lockport

Funding Comes From U.S. Department Of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure And Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, Which Senators Boosted In Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law

Schumer, Gillibrand: Getting Rochester-Finger Lakes Rail On Track For Safer Future!

U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand announced $20,843,235 in federal funding to make critical improvements to rail infrastructure in the Rochester-Finger Lakes region. The funding includes $11.2 million for the Ontario Midland Railroad and $9.6 million for the Falls Road Railroad. This federal investment comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program that the Senators fought to boost funding for in the Bipartisan Infrastructure and Jobs Law.

“This more than $20 million puts the Rochester-Finger Lakes region on track for a safer future. Thanks to significant federal funding from my Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, New York railroad companies from Lockport to Wayne County now have the resources they need to repair aging tracks that the region’s top employers, including Coca-Cola Fairlife, Xerox, Keurig Dr. Pepper/Motts, and more, rely on to grow,” said Senator Schumer. “These rail upgrades mean fewer trucks on the road, lower fuel consumption, and more jobs. I will continue fighting to deliver federal support for the infrastructure improvements Upstate New York needs.”

“This critical $20-plus million investment thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law will upgrade tens of miles of track across the Rochester–Finger Lakes region, ensuring our rail system is safer, faster, and more reliable,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies (THUD). “From Wayne County to Brockport and Lockport, our local railways keep New Yorkers and our businesses moving. These critical repairs will strengthen our supply chains, protect good-paying jobs, and help drive economic growth across Upstate New York.”

Ontario Midland Railroad (OMID) received $11,200,000 for the Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project, which will modernize deteriorating rail infrastructure while advancing several crucial long-term goals for OMID. The project will rehabilitate an approximately 10-mile segment of track in Wayne County, replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight at-grade crossings, replace seven turnouts, remove three turnouts, and perform associated ballast placement, tamping, and surfacing. These improvements will reduce truck traffic, lower fuel consumption, and support workforce growth and economic development. Schumer urged U.S. Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) Administrator David Fink to deliver this funding for the Rochester-Finger Lakes region.

Ontario Midland Railroad provides important freight rail service to agricultural, manufacturing, transload, and other commercial customers across the region. Schumer explained that current aging infrastructure creates an operational bottleneck, hindering efficiency and long-term success of the businesses and industries that rely on this corridor. Upgrading the East-West line will be the key to unlocking new job growth and sales opportunities for many of the region’s top employers, including the Coca-Cola Fairlife milk factory and Xerox’s campus in the town of Webster in Monroe County, as well as many of Wayne County’s top employers, including Keurig Dr. Pepper/Motts production facility, Sodus Cold Storage facility, and Fleishmann’s Vinegar factory. This upgrade would, in turn, benefit the economy of the overall area served by Ontario Midland Railroad and is key to the success of many of the region’s top employers, including Thatcher Chemical, Baldwin Richardson Foods, CRC Polymer Systems, Maco Packaging, K.M. Davies Co., and Nutrien Ag, which is a major supplier of fertilizer to local Wayne County farms, and more. This project would provide a critical boost in our efforts to grow new jobs and ensure on-time delivery of raw materials and on-time shipment of these companies’ products to market. Upgrades will enhance rail safety and streamline network performance, crucial to maintaining supply-chain continuity in a demanding modern economy.

"We are profoundly grateful to Senators Schumer and Gillibrand for their relentless advocacy and partnership in securing this critical 2025–2026 grant for the Ontario Midland Railroad. This federal support is a game-changer for our operations, ensuring we can maintain safe, reliable service and continue driving economic growth across the communities we proudly serve. They understand how vital robust short-line rail infrastructure is to Upstate New York, and we thank our Senators for standing with OMID to secure our future,” said Robert Babcock, Chairman, and Jeffrey Bauman, President of the Ontario Midland Railroad (OMID).

“We are pleased that the Federal Railroad Administration has approved the Ontario Midland Railroad’s application for funding under the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Program. This funding will support comprehensive modernization of Ontario Midland Railroad’s east-west corridor by replacing aging infrastructure with new rail and crossties. These upgrades are essential to eliminating current operational bottlenecks and improving track integrity, which in turn drives greater transportation efficiency across the Greater Rochester, NY region. By revitalizing this line, the project ensures our local manufacturing, agricultural, and transload partners have access to the high-capacity, resilient rail service they need to compete in today’s economy,” said Matt Hurlbutt, President and CEO of Greater Rochester Enterprise.

Brian Pincelli, Executive Director, Wayne County Economic Development & Planning, said, “Rail infrastructure is a significant element of economic development, and the OMID system supports key Wayne County agricultural and manufacturing industries. This funding will allow OMID to make key modernization investments that will serve the current and future county economy by removing existing operational bottlenecks, enhancing track integrity, and improving transportation efficiency throughout the region.”

In addition, Falls Road Railroad Co. received $9,643,235 for the Falls Branch Track, Crossing, & Bridge Project. The project includes the rehabilitation of approximately 40 miles of track and rail infrastructure between Brockport and Lockport. The project will replace rail and ties, add ballast, resurface main line track, rehabilitate a bridge, and resurface six at-grade crossings.

The Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, which Schumer crafted and led to passage in the Senate, included $5 billion over five years for the CRISI program. The program invests in various projects within the United States to improve railroad safety, efficiency, and reliability; mitigate congestion at both intercity passenger and freight rail chokepoints to support more efficient travel and goods movement; enhance multi-modal connections; and lead to new or substantially improved Intercity Passenger Rail Transportation corridors.

title: SCHUMER, GILLIBRAND DELIVER $3.1 MILLION TO MODERNIZE CENTRAL NEW YORK FREIGHT RAIL CORRIDOR CONNECTING CORTLAND COUNTY TO ONONDAGA COUNTY
text:
Senators Say NYS&W Main Line Is A Key Corridor For Freight Rail Needed To Support Central NY Businesses And Major Manufacturing Projects Like Micron

Thanks To Schumer’s Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, New Fed Investment Will Help NYS&W Upgrade Infrastructure Between Cortland And Virgil

Schumer, Gillibrand: Getting CNY Rail Infrastructure Back On Track!

After Schumer two years ago stood in Cortland to tout major federal funding to upgrade rail infrastructure in Cortland and Onondaga Counties, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today announced that the New York, Susquehanna & Western Railway (NYS&W) has received an additional $3,168,302 in federal funding to make critical improvements to the Main Line between Cortland and Virgil. This federal investment comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program that Schumer fought to boost funding for in the Bipartisan Infrastructure and Jobs Law. The senators said that with major new business and manufacturing investments like Micron happening in Central New York, it is more important than ever to upgrade the region’s aging rail infrastructure.

“New upgrades to NYS&W’s Main Line just got the green light! I’m proud to deliver more than $3 million in federal funding from my Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law for critical rail improvements between Cortland and Virgil,” said Senator Schumer. “With major new business and manufacturing projects like Micron underway in Central New York, it is more important than ever that the region is connected and has modern infrastructure. Two years ago, I stood in Cortland to deliver millions in federal funding to replace miles of near century-old rail, and I’m proud to deliver more for Central New York’s rail infrastructure today.”

“The NYS&W line keeps New Yorkers and our businesses moving,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies (THUD). “This critical $3.1 million investment from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law will modernize the rail system between Cortland and Virgil just in time for new corporations like Micron coming to the area. It is critical that with the uptick in new companies coming to Central New York, we have a rail system to match.”

“NYS&W is proud to receive this CRISI award, which funds $3.1 million in track rehabilitation and revitalization between Syracuse and Cortland, New York, including upgrades to Continuous Welded Rail. These critical infrastructure improvements will enhance operational safety, increase fuel efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, allow for higher track speeds, and improve service for NYS&W’s customers. NYS&W remains committed to supporting local businesses, strengthening regional supply chains, and promoting economic growth and development throughout Central New York. NYS&W is grateful for Senator Schumer’s unwavering support for investments in the regional and national rail network,” said James Bonner, President of NYS&W.

Schumer urged U.S. Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) Administrator David Fink to deliver this funding for Central New York. NYS&W will use this funding to remove slow zones, reduce maintenance costs, and enable 286,000-pound railcar capacity by helping install continuous welded rail and ties and renew ballast along approximately 4.5 miles of rail. The federal funding today comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. This award brings the total federal investment in NYSW’s project to $13,528,522, including $3,961,750 in FY23-24 CRISI funding, $3,467,348 in FY22 CRISI funding, and $2,931,122 in FY21 CRISI funding, all a direct result of the historic increases in funding for the program Schumer fought to secure in the Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law.

The Bipartisan Infrastructure & Jobs Law, which Schumer crafted and led to passage in the Senate, included $5 billion over five years for the CRISI program. The program invests in projects to improve railroad safety, efficiency, and reliability; mitigate congestion at both intercity passenger and freight rail chokepoints to support more efficient travel and goods movement; enhance multi-modal connections; and lead to new or substantially improved Intercity Passenger Rail Transportation corridors.

The NYS&W operates over 400 miles of track in New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania and is 286,000-pound gross weight capable on all lines. NYS&W serves over 85 customers and transports a wide range of commodities such as feed ingredients, lumber, and other building materials, chemicals, and aggregates for customers in New York State.

title: Warner, Kaine Announce $3.6 Million in Federal Funding for Shenandoah Valley Rail Improvements
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) announced $3,600,000 in federal funding to modernize the Shenandoah Valley Railroad, improving the safety, reliability, and efficiency of freight rail service for businesses throughout the region. title: Reed, Whitehouse Press Trump DOJ for Allowing Sale of Handguns to Teenagers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) today joined Senator Chris Murphy (D-CT), and several colleagues in sending a letter to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche demanding answers on the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) decision to break with decades of precedent and unilaterally refuse to enforce a prohibition against the sale of handguns to people under the age of 21.

Congress banned firearm dealers from selling handguns and handgun ammunition to people under the age of 21 in the Gun Control Act of 1968. But the Trump Justice Department concluded that the federal government may not impose criminal penalties on federally licensed dealers for selling handguns to 18 to 21 year olds.

In their letter, the twenty U.S. Senators highlighted the enormous risks to public safety of placing handguns in the hands of teenagers: “The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.”

The Senators laid out the decades-long, bipartisan consensus on banning gun dealers from selling firearms to teenagers: “Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that ‘it shall be unlawful’ for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21. Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.”

The Senators argued Blanche’s decision is another authoritarian power grab over the judicial branch and Congress: “The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has ‘deeply divided members of the federal bench.’ Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.”

The Senators concluded by requesting Blanche provide the following information on the authority and research supporting his decision:

1. A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

2. All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

3. Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

4. A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

In addition to Reed, Whitehouse, and Murphy, the letter is signed by U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-DE), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ed Markey (D-MA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Peter Welch (D-VT).

Full text of the letter follows:

Dear Attorney General Blanche:

We write regarding the U.S. Department of Justice’s (the Department) decision to cease enforcement of longstanding federal restrictions on the sale of handguns to individuals under the age of 21 by federally licensed firearms dealers (FFLs). This significant change in federal enforcement policy raises serious questions about the Department’s legal justification, and we request information regarding the analysis underlying its decision.

On September 18, 2026, the Department’s Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) published a legal opinion concluding that 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1)—the federal prohibition on FFLs selling handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds—violate the Second Amendment, and that federal prosecutors may no longer prosecute FFLs that sell handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds who are not otherwise prohibited from gun possession.[1] Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that “it shall be unlawful” for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21.[2] Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.

The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has “deeply divided members of the federal bench.” Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.

The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.

The Department’s decision to unilaterally cease enforcement of this provision of law raises serious questions and concerns. Thus, we request the Department provide:

1. A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

2. All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

3. Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

4. A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

Please provide the requested information and documents by November 16, 2026.

Sincerely,

title: Wyden Urges Executive Branch to Shield Sensitive Federal Websites From Spying to Protect the Privacy of Whistleblowers and All Americans
text:
FBI, FTC Tiplines Among Sites Currently Vulnerable to Spying; Use of Encrypted Client Hello Would Shield Visitors

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ron Wyden, D-Ore., today urged the executive branch to protect whistleblowers and Americans who visit federal websites by upgrading the security of hundreds of government websites that are currently vulnerable to surveillance.

Although the government protects the contents of nearly all website data, standard web encryption does not protect the names of websites that users visit, such as “reportfraud.ftc.gov.” Wyden urged the government to adopt a security technology called Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), which would shield website names from spying, in a letter sent today to the acting director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the deputy federal chief information officer of the United States.

“As data travels across the internet, hackers and foreign actors monitoring network connections can easily see these exposed website names,” Wyden wrote. “This visibility could lead to malicious eavesdroppers identifying whistleblowers, profiling cleared federal personnel, tracking Americans seeking crisis support, and mapping interactions between agencies.”

Wyden’s office identified numerous federal websites that could be protected by ECH against outside spying. Those websites include dozens of U.S. embassies, the FBI online tipline, the Department of Veterans Affairs online suicide prevention hotline and more. A non-exhaustive list of 350 vulnerable federal websites is attached to Wyden’s letter.

title: Rep. Young Kim Leads Commercial Diplomacy Roundtable to Expand Opportunities for Southern California Businesses
text:
ORANGE COUNTY, CA – Today, House Foreign Affairs East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee Chair Young Kim (CA-40), convened American businesses, international companies, and allied trade partners to discuss attracting foreign investment and unlocking new economic opportunities for Southern California.

The event, “Commercial Diplomacy in Action,” featured a fireside chat with Bill Edwards, Founder and CEO of Edwards Global Services and Chair of the District Export Council of Southern California, followed by a roundtable focused on expanding access to East Asian markets, strengthening supply chains, and improving federal investment resources, such as SelectUSA.

The discussion built on Rep. Kim’s ongoing efforts to strengthen U.S. commercial diplomacy and address gaps in how federal agencies support American businesses overseas, including inconsistent access to resources at U.S. embassies and diplomatic posts.

“Southern California is home to some of the hardest-working entrepreneurs and most innovative businesses in the country. Washington should be helping them succeed, not standing in their way,” said Rep. Young Kim. “When our businesses compete and win overseas, we create opportunities for American workers, strengthen our supply chains, and bring more investment back home. I appreciate Bill, our business leaders, and international partners for sharing what’s working and where Washington needs to do better. I’ll take their feedback back to Congress as I work to cut red tape, strengthen the State Department’s commercial diplomacy efforts, and make Southern California a top destination for investment.”

“Exports of U.S. products and services have never been more important to the economy of our country,” said Bill Edwards, Founder and CEO of Edwards Global Services and Chair of the District Export Council of Southern California. “Today’s session on commercial diplomacy highlights the importance of resources our government can bring to our exporters.”

Chairing the subcommittee hearing, “Implementing an America First Approach in the East Asia and Pacific Region,” on advancing an America First strategy to project peace through strength.

title: Rep. Ansari, RM Raskin Demand Answers on Trump Administration’s Efforts to Help Tate Brothers Evade Rape and Sex Trafficking Charges as They Face Extradition to U.K.
text:
Lawmakers Press Blanche and Rubio to Disclose Intervention and Answer Whether Administration Will Honor Extradition Requests

WASHINGTON -- Today, Rep. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee are demanding answers from Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the Trump Administration’s reported efforts to help Andrew and Tristan Tate evade criminal charges and whether it will comply with the United Kingdom’s request to extradite the brothers to face rape and sex trafficking charges. The longtime Trump supporters remain in federal custody and face a stunning 59 criminal charges in the United Kingdom.

“Despite the looming prosecutions, the Tate brothers have continued to accumulate new criminal accusations and charges since returning to the U.S. [...] However, given the Trump Administration’s reported willingness to intervene both internationally and domestically on the Tate brothers’ behalf as they face serious criminal charges involving violent crimes and given the failure of any official to provide substantive responses to Ranking Member Raskin’s previous correspondence, we remain skeptical that the Administration will sit on the sidelines rather than jump into the game to help the Tates,” wrote the lawmakers.

The brothers have continued to face new allegations of sexual violence and trafficking since returning to the United States. Less than two weeks after their arrival, Andrew allegedly assaulted his girlfriend, Bri Stern, in Los Angeles; reported text messages show him repeatedly telling her he wanted to hit and beat her and that she deserved it. Former right-wing influencer Lauren Southern also accused Andrew of choking and assaulting her in a Bucharest hotel room in 2018. The brothers were arrested in Miami in July 2026 after British authorities issued 38 additional charges, including nine additional rape counts between them, bringing the total to 59. Romanian prosecutors subsequently announced a second indictment, charging Andrew with trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering, and Tristan with complicity in those alleged crimes.

Rep. Ansari called on House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer on July 23 to investigate the Tate brothers’ ties to the Trump Administration. Chairman Comer has not responded.

Ranking Member Raskin first sought answers in April 2025 about Administration pressure on Romania to lift the brothers’ court-imposed travel restrictions. No Trump Administration official provided a substantive response. Instead, Special Presidential Envoy Richard Grenell called Judiciary Committee Minority staff to complain about the inquiry, which highlighted reports that he raised the Tates’ case with Romanian officials at the Munich Security Conference.

Subsequent reporting exposed further efforts by a Trump Administration official to help the brothers. ProPublica reported that White House official Paul Ingrassia, a former lawyer for the brothers, urged senior Department of Homeland Security officials to return electronic devices seized from them when they entered the United States in February 2025. Ingrassia denied intervening. Andrew Tate also reportedly cultivated a relationship with President Trump’s son Barron, with the two allegedly agreeing that the Romanian criminal case was an attempt to silence the brothers.

Reps. Ansari and Raskin are requesting disclosure of any consultations, communications or directives from Justice Department leadership concerning the extradition proceedings, including contacts with the prosecutors handling the case. They also seek an accounting of U.S. efforts to lift the Romanian travel restrictions, whether the Tates’ support for Trump influenced those efforts, and records of government engagement with Romanian officials, British officials and the brothers’ attorneys since January 20, 2025.

title: Vermont Delegation Announces More Than $60 Million in New Federal Funding to Complete Vermont’s Western Corridor Rail Line
text:
BURLINGTON, VT – U.S. Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL), U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), and U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) today announced the delivery of $60.3 million in new federal funding, administered by the Department of Transportation (DOT) to the Vermont Agency of Transportation (VTrans) to rehabilitate and complete approximately 60 miles of railway on Vermont’s Western Corridor rail line.

“Repairing and upgrading our transportation infrastructure is a win-win for Vermont’s rural communities. This federal funding will help improve safety and reliability on the Vermont Railway, and support the development of rural towns up and down the Western Corridor,” said the Vermont Delegation. “With this $60 million investment from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, the Western Corridor will be complete, and western Vermont will finally be connected to the New York Penn Station line.”

“This grant will support Vermont businesses who rely on rail to get their products to market regionally and nationally,” said Vermont Transportation Secretary Joe Flynn. “For bulk commodities, shipping by rail is often the most cost-effective, and upgrades to the Vermont Railway in western Vermont will enable our businesses to efficiently tap into the nation's major Class I railroads.”

This new funding will help replace rail, realign track, and upgrade ties, ballast, turnouts, and 22 at-grade crossings to enhance safety, improve system and service performance, and increase reliability of rail service in Vermont. The funding is made possible through DOT’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program.

title: Rep. Barr Applauds $43.6 Million Federal Grant Awarded to Kentucky-Based R. J. Corman
text:
Lexington, KY — Today, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) applauded the announcement that R. J. Corman Railroad Company, headquartered in Nicholasville, Kentucky, has been awarded a $43.6 million federal grant through the Federal Railroad Administration's (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. The funding will support the company's Southeastern Short Line Freight Rail Track Improvement Project, representing a total investment of approximately $62.3 million in freight rail infrastructure across the southeastern United States.

Congressman Barr advocated for R. J. Corman's successful grant application through a letter of support. The award highlights the important role Kentucky-headquartered companies play in strengthening America's transportation infrastructure, supporting domestic industries, and keeping American goods moving. Barr also recently welcomed U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to Kentucky to discuss regional transportation priorities.

“R. J. Corman is a great Kentucky success story, and I’m proud to support this $43.6 million investment in strengthening our nation’s freight rail infrastructure,” said Congressman Barr. “Reliable freight transportation is critical to moving American-made goods, supporting our farmers and manufacturers, and keeping our regional economy competitive. I was proud to advocate for this project through a letter of support and bring Secretary Sean Duffy to Kentucky recently to discuss important regional transportation priorities. This investment will strengthen supply chains and help businesses across the Southeast get their products to market more safely and efficiently.”

The project will fund critical infrastructure improvements across eight short line railroads in the southeastern United States. While the rail improvements will take place outside Kentucky, the project will be led by R. J. Corman, a Kentucky-headquartered company with a longstanding history in the American railroad industry.

The improvements will include replacing and rehabilitating aging rail, crossties, switches, ballast, grade crossings, and other track components to improve safety, reliability, and freight transportation efficiency. The participating railroads serve more than 120 shippers transporting agricultural products, manufactured goods, aggregates, chemicals, metals, energy products, and critical minerals.

“Short line railroads provide essential connections between American businesses and the national freight network,” said Justin Broyles, President and CEO of R. J. Corman Railroad Group. “This investment will allow us to strengthen the infrastructure that manufacturers, farmers, energy producers, and other businesses depend on every day. Improving these railroads means safer and more reliable freight transportation, stronger supply chains and better infrastructure to support American industry and economic growth.”

U.S. Congressmen James Comer (R-KY-01) and Hal Rogers (R-KY-05) also supported the project and recognized the role of Kentucky businesses in strengthening the nation's transportation network.

“R. J. Corman is a great example of Kentucky ingenuity and the success that comes from hard work. I am proud to support this $43.6 million investment, which will help modernize critical rail infrastructure, strengthen our economy, and support good-paying jobs. Our farmers, manufacturers, and businesses depend on reliable transportation networks to move their products and reach new markets. This grant will build on Kentucky’s economic strengths, create new opportunities, and help ensure our communities remain great places to live, work, and do business,” said U.S. Congressman James Comer (R-KY-01).

“The iconic red R. J. Corman trains moving through Kentucky and surrounding states are a reminder of the firm foundation that has been laid for our rail infrastructure and the bold investments required to keep America first. I was proud to support this important investment in our supply chain in Rural America, ensuring that our farmers and businesses have the infrastructure necessary for American-made deliveries,” said U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers (R-KY-05), Dean of the House.

Founded in 1973 and headquartered in Nicholasville, Kentucky, R. J. Corman Railroad Company operates 19 short line railroads across 11 states. The company employs approximately 1,400 people in 24 states and provides railroad services including track construction, emergency response, switching operations, and signal design and construction.

The federal award underscores the national reach of a Kentucky-founded business and its continued role in maintaining the infrastructure that American farmers, manufacturers, and businesses depend on.

title: USDA Delivers $8 Billion in Relief for American Farmers
text:
Dear Kentucky farmers,

You are the backbone of our Commonwealth and our nation's economy. You work long hours, take enormous risks, and help feed and fuel America. You deserve leaders in Washington who have your back.

This session of Congress, I voted for the largest investment in rural communities in history, to end the death tax on almost 2 million family farms, and to expand crop insurance for our farmers.

Right now, no issue is more important than lowering diesel fuel costs. I’ve been fighting to change the law and unleash Kentucky energy producers to create jobs and lower energy costs. In the meantime, I wanted to share today’s announcement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture providing $8B in new relief for American farmers through the Harvest Fuel Relief Program.

With rising input costs and market uncertainty continuing to squeeze our agricultural producers, this funding will provide much-needed relief to help farmers get through the harvest season.

Here's what Kentucky farmers need to know:

$8 billion in direct assistance will be made available to eligible farmers nationwide.

Payment rates will be announced in November for eligible Title I commodities.

Crop insurance will not be required to participate in the program.

Farmers are encouraged to establish a Login.gov account linked to USDA to prepare for the application process.

This new relief builds on President Trump's commitment to putting American farmers first, including $12 billion in previous bridge assistance and nearly $14 billion in payments through the Agriculture Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage programs.

President Trump is delivering for rural America, and I will continue fighting alongside him to ensure Kentucky farmers have the resources they need to succeed.

For more information about the program and how to prepare, visit USDA.gov/Farmers-First.

Thank you for everything you do for Kentucky and our country.

title: ICYMI: Secretary of Education Linda McMahon and Congressman Baumgartner Call on Governor Ferguson to Unlock Educational Tax Credits for Washington Families
text:
SPOKANE VALLEY, WA — Congressman Michael Baumgartner (WA-05) and Secretary of Education Linda McMahon visited the Chesterton Academy of Notre Dame in Spokane Valley to discuss challenges facing K–12 education and opportunities to expand educational options and support student success. They urged Governor Bob Ferguson to opt Washington into the Education Freedom Tax Credit program, which can help eligible public and private school students access tutoring, tuition assistance, special-needs services, and other qualifying educational support.

“One of our proudest accomplishments this Congress is creating the Education Freedom Tax Credit, allowing taxpayers to direct up to $1,700 toward scholarships that help students succeed,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “These scholarships can benefit students at schools like Chesterton Academy and public school students alike, helping families pay for tutoring, after-school programs, and other qualifying educational expenses.”

The pair also discussed the importance of expanding educational opportunities so families can choose the learning environment that best meets their families needs, regardless of income level.

“We are all united by the shared belief that every child, regardless of zip code or family income, deserves an education that reflects their families values and prepares them to succeed,” said Secretary McMahon. “A family’s income should never be the reason a child misses out on an education where he or she should thrive. Those scholarships can support tuition, tutoring, services for students with disabilities, and other qualifying educational expenses whether a child attends public school or private school,” she added.

“This is probably the most significant education policy reform, at least in the last 50 years, to create a sense of empowerment for every parent and every student and every taxpayer, that they can take control of the future of education,” Baumgartner concluded.

title: Buchanan Joins Bipartisan House Entrepreneurship Caucus to Support America’s Small Businesses
text:
“Small businesses are the backbone of our local economies and the heart of every community in America.”

Caucus Works to Cut the Barriers Keeping New Businesses from Starting and Growing

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, announced he has joined the bipartisan House Entrepreneurship Caucus.

“As a small business owner, I know how much sweat and sacrifice it takes to build something from nothing,” said Buchanan. “Small businesses are the backbone of our local economies and the heart of every community in America. Too many potential entrepreneurs never get off the ground because capital is hard to find and red tape is hard to clear. I’mproud to join this caucus to help make sure the next generation of entrepreneurs has every opportunity to achieve the American Dream.”

First established in 2019, the House Entrepreneurship Caucus is co-chaired by Reps. French Hill, R-Ark., Marc Veasey, D-Texas, Roger Williams, R-Texas, Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., David Schweikert, R-Ariz., and Don Beyer, D-Va. Williams also chairs the House Small Business Committee.

The caucus brings Republicans and Democrats together with entrepreneurs, startups and small business owners to address a decades-long decline in new business formation. Its members work to tackle the obstacles that keep new companies from starting and scaling, chief among them the difficulty of raising capital and the cost of complying with federal regulation.

Buchanan has been a small business owner for most of his life. Before coming to Congress, he spent more than 30 years in business, building a printing franchise that grew to more than 700 locations across 44 states and later founding a group of automotive dealerships across the country. He also served as chairman of both the Florida Chamber of Commerce and the Greater Sarasota Chamber of Commerce and sat on the board of directors of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. In Congress, he served on the House Small Business Committee before joining the Ways and Means Committee, where he has continued to champion pro-growth policies that help small businesses hire, expand and compete across America.
