title: Carbajal Hosts Former Secretary Xavier Becerra, State Senate President pro Tempore Monique Limón at Santa Barbara Latino Community Outreach Event
text:
On Friday October 16, U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) hosted former Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Xavier Becerra and California State Senate President pro Tempore Monique Limón in Santa Barbara for his annual “Cafecito Con El Congresista” event. The event featured remarks from Becerra, Limón, and Carbajal followed by a Q&A session with attendees.

Download photos here.

Carbajal’s “Cafecito” is an annual gathering that brings together the Central Coast Latino community to create an open forum for discussing local and national issues directly with elected officials. Carbajal has hosted the annual “Cafecito” event since 2017.

“Coming right on the heels of Hispanic Heritage Month, our Cafecito is an annual opportunity for our community to continue celebrating our heritage and the many contributions Latinos make to our country and the Central Coast,” said Rep. Carbajal. “I thank our special guests — Secretary Xavier Becerra and California State Senate President pro Tempore Monique Limón — for joining us today and sharing the stories of their incredible public service journeys. I also would like to extend my gratitude to everyone who participated in today’s discussion and made this yet another successful Cafecito.”

“I've had the privilege to experience leadership in California, in Washington, D.C., and I've learned that Californians must continue to be the leaders of this nation. To me, Latino Heritage Month is not just one day or one month — we must live and follow our values every day. And I believe that as difficult as things are, California still has the best days ahead of it. I want to thank leaders like Rep. Salud Carbajal for hosting constituent events like this Cafecito and state Senate Pro Tem Monique Limón, we are going to work closely with our leaders to make sure we make a difference in the lives of every Californian,” said Secretary Becerra.

“I was honored to close out Hispanic Heritage Month alongside Congressman Carbajal, Secretary Becerra, and community leaders at the annual Cafecito event. It was great to be able to share the work of the State Senate, how we are working to protect all Californians, and utilizing all branches of government to better the state. Thank you to Congressman Carbajal for hosting this event and thank you to former Secretary Xavier Becerra for the inspiring conversation,” said State Senate Leader Monique Limón.

Other attendees included members of the community along with representatives from the California State Assembly, City of Santa Barbara, City of Goleta, City of Santa Maria, City of Carpinteria, City of Guadalupe, City of Oxnard, City of Ventura, Ventura County Board of Supervisors, Santa Barbara County, Santa Barbara Unified School District, U.C. Santa Barbara, U.C. Merced, California State University Channel Islands, and Santa Barbara County Sheriff’s Office.

title: Arizona Has a New National Park!
text:
Cochise County, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani is celebrating the passage of his Chiricahua National Park Act (H.R. 6380), which President Trump signed into law this afternoon. This effort crossed the finish line after a decade of bipartisan work. Chiricahua National Park is now Arizona’s fourth national park and the second in Arizona’s Sixth District.

"I’m incredibly proud that my Chiricahua National Park bill is officially law, establishing Arizona’s fourth national park," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "After nearly a decade of work, persistence has finally paid off, and this historic effort has reached the summit. I’m incredibly grateful to our local partners, whose dedication and collaboration with my office were instrumental in getting this across the finish line. This achievement will preserve Arizona’s rich heritage for generations to come. As we celebrate our nation’s 250th anniversary, I cannot think of a better way to honor our history and natural beauty than by welcoming Arizona’s fourth national park, and the second national park in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District."

To mark this milestone in both Arizona and United States history, Rep. Ciscomani was joined by U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) Secretary Doug Burgum for a ceremony, remarks, and tour at Chiricahua National Park this afternoon. The celebration took place an hour after President Trump signed the bill into law.

"As America celebrates its 250th anniversary, President Trump is writing an exciting new chapter in our nation’s conservation history with the designation of Chiricahua as America’s 64th National Park," said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. "Arizona is home to some of the most extraordinary landscapes on Earth, and this historic designation will introduce even more Americans to the natural beauty and rich cultural heritage of southeastern Arizona while bringing new visitors, economic opportunities and investment to surrounding communities. Thanks to the leadership of Congressman Juan Ciscomani and our partners across Arizona, we’re ensuring this remarkable place can be enjoyed by Americans for generations to come."

Under the new law, the 102-year-old Chiricahua National Park joins Saguaro National Park in southern Arizona, Grand Canyon National Park in northern Arizona, and Petrified Forest National Park in eastern Arizona. The official designation of Chiricahua as a national park is expected to attract more visitors to southeastern Arizona, boosts local tourism, support local businesses, and create new economic opportunities throughout Cochise County and Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

Known as the "Wonderland of Rocks," Chiricahua National Park was first established as a National Monument in 1924 and protects a breathtaking landscape that attracts visitors from across the United States. Since his first year in Congress and his second bill introduced Representative Ciscomani has made the park’s designation a top priority, working closely with bipartisan colleagues in both chambers. His relentless advocacy culminated in this historic achievement.

Local leaders across southeastern Arizona have voiced strong support for the new national park designation, recognizing its national significance.

"The Chiricahua Mountains are one of Arizona’s greatest natural treasures, and recognizing Chiricahua National Monument as a National Park is a tremendous opportunity for Cochise County and future generations. This designation will bring greater national recognition to southeastern Arizona, strengthen our local economy, and support the businesses and communities that welcome visitors to this remarkable region. I want to thank President Trump for signing this important legislation into law and Congressman Ciscomani for his leadership and dedication in making this long-awaited designation a reality," said Chairman Frank Antenori.

"The Chiricahua Mountains are an important part of Cochise County’s history, natural beauty, and identity. Designating Chiricahua as a National Park will help introduce more visitors to everything southeastern Arizona has to offer, creating new opportunities for our rural communities, small businesses, and tourism industry. I sincerely appreciate President Trump signing this legislation into law, Congressman Ciscomani’s continued efforts, and the bipartisan cooperation that helped bring this important recognition to our region," said Supervisor Kathleen Gomez.

"This is a historic day for Willcox, Cochise County, and the entire State of Arizona. The Chiricahuas are one of our nation's greatest natural treasures, and designating them as a National Park will ensure future generations can experience their extraordinary beauty. This accomplishment would not have been possible without the tireless efforts of Congressman Juan Ciscomani, Senator Mark Kelly, HECHO, and the many partners who worked together to make this a reality. We are especially grateful to President Trump for signing this legislation and recognizing the importance of protecting this remarkable landscape," said Willcox Mayor Greg Hancock.

"The designation of Chiricahua National Park represents a tremendous opportunity for Willcox and the surrounding communities. As a gateway to the Chiricahuas, Willcox is uniquely positioned to benefit from increased visitation, new business investment, and additional tourism-related jobs. This designation will strengthen our local economy, support our small businesses, and introduce more visitors to everything southeastern Arizona and Cochise County has to offer. The economic benefits of this decision will be felt for generations," said Willcox City Manager Caleb Blaschke.

"Thanks to Representative Ciscomani’s determined efforts, Arizona has a new national park that will create jobs and economic growth in the region. Chiricahua now takes its rightful place among America’s most treasured public lands and will be a bucket list destination for millions of Americans for generations to come. I congratulate Representative Ciscomani and Arizona on being home to our newest crown jewel," said Chairman Westerman.

title: Ciscomani Welcomes Interior Secretary Burgum to Gunnison Copper’s Johnson Camp Mine in Southern Arizona, Highlights Investments in American Copper Production
text:
Cochise County, AZ - In a powerful show of partnership and progress, Representative Juan Ciscomani and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum came together at Gunnison Copper’s Johnson Camp Mine on Tuesday to spotlight Southern Arizona’s leadership in American mining. The occasion featured a dedication ceremony, an in-depth tour of the copper operation, and forward-looking discussions on strengthening the nation’s future through domestic critical mineral production.

"It was a privilege to join Secretary Burgum at Gunnison Copper today to celebrate the resurgence of domestic copper production, with Arizona leading the way," said Representative Juan Ciscomani. "Copper is a vital part of Arizona’s Five C’s and an essential resource for our economy and national security. In Congress, I have championed efforts to strengthen domestic mining, expand American production, and reduce our reliance on foreign sources. I’m incredibly grateful for the continued partnership with Gunnison Copper and its valuable contributions to Arizona’s economy and America’s mineral independence."

The visit highlighted Southern Arizona’s pivotal role in restoring U.S. mineral independence. Gunnison Copper marked the event by announcing wage increases and equity stakes for employees, underscoring how investment in workers is essential to building a resilient domestic supply chain for critical minerals. The event also featured the unveiling of a monument honoring the enduring values of country, service, hard work, and shared responsibility. The monument will serve as a permanent gathering place for employees and visitors to reflect on these principles and the purpose behind their work.

"We are honored to welcome Secretary Doug Burgum and Congressman Juan Ciscomani, and we deeply appreciate Congressman Ciscomani’s strong advocacy for Arizona’s mining industry and its workers," said Craig Hallworth, President and CEO of Gunnison Copper. "Our values—People First, Innovate Boldly, Act Responsibly, Strengthen Communities and Proudly American—guide our work to advance the Gunnison Copper Project, create skilled jobs and produce American copper that strengthens our nation’s security, prosperity and industrial independence."

"Under President Trump, America is once again becoming a mineral powerhouse," said Chairman of the National Energy Dominance Council and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. "By working with industry partners and leaders like Congressman Juan Ciscomani, we’re restoring America’s mining legacy and ensuring the minerals that power our economy, national security and modern way of life are mined and processed right here at home. America’s vast mineral wealth is one of our greatest strategic advantages, and projects like the Gunnison Copper Mine are helping unlock that potential, strengthen our supply chains and secure a future of American Energy Dominance for generations to come."

Representative Ciscomani’s commitment to Arizona’s mining future is clear as he fought to secure a historic $20 million investment for the University of Arizona’s School of Mining Engineering and Mineral Resources, supporting research, workforce development, and expansion of the San Xavier Underground Mining Laboratory. Copper is the backbone of the nation’s electrical grid, defense systems, and manufacturing base, making reliable robust supply of critical minerals not just an Arizona priority, but a domestic imperative.

At Johnson Camp, Gunnison Copper is turning Arizona’s mineral potential into American-made copper. Using Nuton, an innovative bioleaching technology developed by Rio Tinto, the operation has begun producing finished copper cathode by combining mining, leaching, and production at a single Arizona site. This breakthrough demonstrates how American innovation can unlock previously uneconomical copper resources, strengthen domestic processing, and reduce dependence on foreign supply chains. The nearby Gunnison Copper Project holds more than 5 billion pounds of measured and indicated copper resources and, at full development, could supply approximately 11% of U.S. refined copper production.

The visit celebrated both Arizona’s mining heritage and its future as a leader in American industry. A color guard from the Benson Veterans of Foreign Wars and a local marching band from Cienega High School led a flag-raising ceremony featuring the flags of the United States, Arizona, and Gunnison Copper. Secretary Burgum and Representative Ciscomani also participated in a ceremonial production blast, underscoring the scale of Arizona’s mining industry and the skilled workforce driving America’s domestic mineral resurgence.

title: Corpus Christi Approves First Step Toward $17.8M Grant to Replace Aging Water Lines
text:
KIII ABC News Corpus Christi

Sumiko A. Lara | October 20th, 2026

Aging water lines along Leopard Street and Up River Road could soon be replaced with the help of a $17.8 million federal grant.

The Corpus Christi City Council approved the first step Tuesday toward accepting the funding, which would cover 70% of the $25.4 million project.

The remaining $7.6 million would come from the city’s Water Capital Fund. City officials said the grant would eliminate the need to borrow more than $17.8 million for the project, helping reduce future costs for water customers.

The funding comes through a federal program supporting infrastructure near military installations. The project would improve water service for residents, Naval Air Station Corpus Christi and the Corpus Christi Army Depot.

“This federal investment will help modernize and strengthen the city’s water infrastructure that is critical to supplying water for both NAS Corpus Christi and the Corpus Christi Army Depot,” Congressman Michael Cloud said.

Corpus Christi was one of 26 communities nationwide selected for the funding and is receiving the grant through this program for the first time.

City Council must approve the ordinance a second time before the grant can be officially accepted. A final vote is scheduled for Oct. 27.

title: Rep. Costa Issues Statement on Suspicious Mail Received at District Office
text:

While the nature of this letter is still under forensic analysis, let me be clear: any attempts to instill fear and intimidation will not deter my dedicated staff and me from working for the people of our Valley. title: ICYMI in the Day: “People will die” from the Trump Administration’s Health Care Cuts
text:
NORWICH, CT – In case you missed it in the Day, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Connecticut’s Attorney General William Tong, and Connecticut Department of Social Services Commissioner Andrea Barton Reeves hosted a roundtable with patient advocates to discuss impending health care cuts coming as a result of President Trump’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” (H.R. 1), which passed Congress with only Republican votes and was signed into law by President Trump in July 2025.

Image

H.R. 1 made a nearly $1 trillion cut to Medicaid (HUSKY in Connecticut) to pay for a tax break for the top 1%. Under H.R. 1’s new Medicaid coverage requirements which begin on January 1st, 2027, it is estimated that 100,000 Connecticut residents will lose their HUSKY health care coverage.

Courtney continues to fight against the Trump Administration’s implementation of H.R. 1’s Medicaid cuts, including a rule by Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Department of Health and Human Services that would require cancer patients and patients suffering from other debilitating diseases to document that the disease actually impairs their ability to work or face losing their health care coverage.

FROM THE DAY:

Courtney described the new system imposed by the federal rules as “grotesque.”

“If you think of cancer patients with pancreatic cancer having to go out and do job searches so they can get their chemo and medication. … It's just unimaginable,” Courtney said. “Hopefully, we're going to see a change, hopefully in courts, and eventually in Congress, that is going to reverse this move that is just taking our country backwards, not forwards.”

Before and after Congressional Republicans passed H.R. 1, Congressman Courtney has railed against the Trump Administration’s health care cuts at town halls, visits to health care providers, and in Congressional committee hearings and House floor speeches. In the year since President Trump signed H.R. 1 into law, nearly eight million Americans lost their health care coverage. Millions more nationwide are expected to lose coverage when H.R. 1’s most significant health care cuts take effect on January 1st.

title: Rep. Craig Announces Savage’s Designation as a World War II Heritage City
text:
EAGAN, MN – Today, U.S. Representative Angie Craig announced that the National Park Service (NPS) has officially designated Savage, Minnesota a World War II (WWII) Heritage City, recognizing the city for its outstanding contributions during WWII and the community’s commitment to preserving its rich history.

Rep. Craig penned a letter of support to NPS last April, urging the agency to recognize Savage for its wartime contributions.

“The City of Savage and its residents played a critical role during World War II, and today, they are finally getting the recognition they deserve,” said Rep. Craig. “Whether it was offering translation services, building ships or distributing supplies to aid the war effort, folks in Savage went above and beyond to show their patriotism and commitment to America’s national security. I am proud that the National Park Service is designating Savage a World War II Heritage City and cementing its place in our nation’s history.”

From 1942-1944, Camp Savage was home to the secret Military Intelligence Service Language School (MISLS) where 6,000 Nisei American soldiers were trained in military intelligence and linguistics, significantly aiding U.S. forces throughout every campaign and major battle in the Asia Pacific.

According to Major General Charles Willoughby, the Nisei linguist soldiers helped shorten the Pacific war by two years, saving roughly one million American lives. After the victory in the Pacific, MISLS-trained linguists helped translate more than 20 million pages of documents and played a crucial role in postwar war crimes trials.

The City of Savage was also home to the Savage Shipyard, converted by Cargill to employ over 3,500 workers. The shipyard built 18 ships for the Navy and four tugboats for the Army, receiving an Army-Navy “E” award for excellence in the production of war equipment.

The City of Savage is unique in Minnesota for its preservation of heritage and legacy. Savage has established a memorial to Camp Savage and the MISLS at the Scott County Library. In addition, the Scott County Historical Society has been critical in cataloguing and preserving Savage’s wartime contributions.

title: Rep. Crane’s First Law Secures Continued Operation of Gila County Veterans Retreat
text:
Today, President Donald J. Trump signed H.R. 837 into law. The legislation, introduced by Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ), allows Gila County to take ownership of the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site for the continued operation of a veterans center on the property in Young, Arizona.

H.R. 837 is a reintroduction of the first bill Rep. Crane introduced in Congress, and it is the first of his bills signed into law. The new law caps an effort Gila County Supervisor Woody Cline began in 2017 to turn the former ranger station into a retreat for veterans and their families. The bill passed the House unanimously in two consecutive Congresses before clearing the Senate by unanimous consent on September 30.

The legislation directs the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Forest Service, to convey approximately 232.9 acres of the administrative site in the Tonto National Forest to Gila County. The county will cover all costs tied to the transfer, and the Congressional Budget Office estimated the bill would have no effect on the federal budget. Gila County now has 180 days to submit a written request for the land. Afterward, the Forest Service will complete the transfer.

In 2016, the Forest Service moved its Pleasant Valley administrative operations to a new site near Payson, leaving most of the property unused. Since 2021, Gila County has operated the land under a 20-year special use permit and has been developing it into the Pleasant Valley Veterans Retreat. However, the county still needs federal approval for projects under the permit. Rep. Crane’s new law will replace this arrangement with local ownership, giving the county the certainty it needs to invest in the retreat long-term and avoid overly burdensome regulations.

The center is the first of its kind in the region and primarily serves rural veterans and their families, including the nearly 5,500 veterans who call Gila County home. Transferring ownership to the county will preserve the property’s rich history while providing family housing, meeting and activity spaces, resource rooms, Veteran Ceremonial Grounds, and outdoor recreation.

Supervisor Cline testified before the House Committee on Natural Resources in 2023 on the significant impacts and outstanding resources the center would provide for the region’s veterans.

“This site will only be one of two sites in Arizona. There’s one in the southern part of Arizona and one in the northern part […] It’s huge for our local community as well. We have a local veteran community of about 100 people right there in that small town. And then right there between us and Payson, there’s roughly another 5,000-7,000 more right there. Having this accessible, not only to the local members, the state members, the national members, but also, we’re adjacent to the White Mountain Apache Tribe that is not very far away that has a number of veterans in that reservation as well that have been big supporters of this project. It means everything to these folks,” said Supervisor Woody Cline during hearing questioning.

Speaking to Supervisor Cline about the purpose of the veterans center, Rep. Crane stated, “One of the things I love so much about this project, is that you’re not coming here, Mr. Cline, and asking the federal government for any money. You’re actually trying to take something that’s a beautiful piece of land that’s not being used anymore and revitalize it into something amazing for some of our nation’s finest individuals.”

House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman previously stated, “America’s veterans and their families have sacrificed so much to defend our freedom, and Congress must do everything in its power to provide our servicemembers with proper care and opportunities. The commonsense, bipartisan land transfer provided by H.R.837 will do just that by opening up new experiences to veterans in the area for recreation and recovery. A veteran himself, Representative Crane has led on these issues this Congress, and I look forward to continuing to work with him to get this bill […] signed into law.”

title: Crow Earns Perfect “A” Grade for Fighting to Protect Democracy
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), co-chair of the End Corruption Caucus, earned a perfect “A” grade from pro-democracy group Defend the Vote. The legislative score reflects Crow’s work protecting every American’s right to vote, upholding the integrity of our elections, and combating corruption.

“Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans have attacked our democracy by sowing doubt in our elections and making it harder to vote. At every step of the way, I’ve fought back,” said Congressman Crow. “Every American has a right to elect their leaders and vote at the ballot box. I’ll continue fighting in Congress to protect our democracy, get dark money out of our politics, and take on special interests.”

Crow has also received a perfect 10/10 score from Democracy Defenders Action on their Stop Corruption Now Congressional Scorecard and an A+ from good governance group End Citizens United for his work to root out corruption in politics, the only member of Colorado’s House delegation to receive the grade.

Crow is fighting to protect elections in Colorado. He recently hosted an election security roundtable alongside local officials to coordinate and discuss efforts to keep Colorado’s election system strong.

Throughout his time in Congress, Crow has stood up to special interests and has not taken a dime of corporate PAC money. He is an original cosponsor of the TRUST in Congress Act to ban members of Congress and their families from owning or trading stocks and has led the call to ban members of Congress and their staff from insider trading on prediction markets. Crow is leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act and SHINE Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections.

Crow is also leading the charge against this Administration's corruption. He’s demanding answers about potential corruption and favoritism with federal contracts benefiting the Trump family; uncovering conflicts of interest at the Pentagon stemming from Pete Hegseth’s special adviser Tim Parlatore; and is leading a slate of historic pro-democracy reforms aimed at preventing presidential abuses of power, rooting out corruption, strengthening checks and balances, and protecting American elections against foreign influence.

title: Davids, Local Business Owners Discuss Responsible AI, Industry Growth
text:
OVERLAND PARK, KC — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined the KC Tech Council and more than a dozen business owners for a roundtable on emerging technology, artificial intelligence (AI), infrastructure, and business innovation. The conversation centered on finding a balance between economic growth and safety regulations — a perspective Davids plans to bring to Washington.

“Today was a real learning opportunity for me,” said Davids. “Artificial intelligence holds incredible promise for our small businesses, but we cannot ignore the real dangers. AI companies need to be held accountable especially when their products put kids at risk, and local communities shouldn’t be left footing the bill for the massive energy infrastructure these corporations require. I’m taking what I heard from our local business leaders today back to Washington to make sure Congress strikes the right balance between supporting economic growth and keeping our families safe.”

According to a recent survey, about 3 out of 4 small businesses use AI tools today, and almost all of them say it’s helping their business run better and faster. Even as local businesses use these technologies to grow, most Americans say the government needs to step in with basic safety rules. Recent national polls show that over 80 percent of voters want clear standards to keep AI safe for kids and families. Davids made clear that Washington must listen to both sides — helping local businesses succeed while putting sensible guardrails in place to protect the public.

During the discussion, attendees covered a wide range of policy areas impacting the regional economy, including:

Federal AI Policy and Data Privacy: Developing a clear, unified national framework for responsible AI deployment and strong federal data privacy standards.

Energy, Grid Capacity, and Infrastructure: Addressing high-power energy demands through permitting reform and targeted infrastructure investment.

Manufacturing and Supply Chain Resilience: Strengthening domestic manufacturing, electric vehicle (EV) battery investment, and supply chain security across the Midwest.

Healthcare IT and Interoperability: Improving healthcare data systems to enhance patient outcomes and streamline health IT operations.

Workforce Development and Veteran Training: Expanding tech training pathways, including funding for veteran tech workforce programs.

Small Business and Entrepreneurship: Increasing access to capital and federal resource programs for local startups and small business owners.

title: Dingell Receives Response from EGLE Regarding Los Alamos, Prompts Further Questions for EPA
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) is continuing to demand greater transparency on behalf of her constituents in Ypsilanti Township as it relates to the proposed University of Michigan (U-M) Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) research computing center at the Textile Road site.

Congresswoman Dingell recently sent a letter to the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) and Environmental Protection Agency requesting a formal review of the environmental status of the Textile Road Site. As promised, she is releasing EGLE’s response to her September 2026 inquiry. The congresswoman is still awaiting a response from the EPA to her inquiry.

The response from EGLE prompted additional questions for the EPA from Congresswoman Dingell. In her latest letter to the EPA, the congresswoman is requesting additional information regarding the environmental status of the Textile Road Site, as well as the final Work Plan document for the site.

In September 2026, Congresswoman Dingell expressed opposition to the proposed Los Alamos research computing center at the Textile Road site in Ypsilanti Township. This month, Congresswoman Dingell announced she is drafting a federal data center “Bill of Rights” and is seeking input on a proposed framework to ensure communities have a meaningful voice in decisions surrounding large-scale data center projects. Last week, she released the latest response from U-M to her most recent inquiry.

A copy of the response from EGLE can be found HERE.

A copy of the new letter to the EPA can be found HERE and text is below:

Dear Administrator Zeldin:

This letter is to request additional information regarding the environmental status of the Textile Road Site in Ypsilanti Township, which is a follow-up to my September 16, 2026 request to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE). As you know, this site has been selected for the proposed University of Michigan-Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) research computing center.

EGLE responded to my request for information on October 13, 2026. Their answers to my September 16, 2026 request prompt additional questions and requests as I seek to gain a full and clear understanding of the Textile Road Site’s environmental history and the potential implications of UM-LANL’s proposed research computing center.

EGLE’s response is attached and raises more questions for you. They are:

1. Are the responsible parties for this site, as determined by the EPA’s Administrative Order of Consent (Docket No. V-2-99-C-562), responsible for additional environmental testing, monitoring, remediation, or response?

2. Are groundwater monitoring requirements complete or are there continued requirements in accordance with the Administrative Order of Consent for this site?

3. Does the analytical data in the September 2003 Notice of Migration of Contamination depict the complete monitoring network?

4. Was the final Restrictive Covenant finalized and recorded with the Register of Deeds? If so, please provide this documentation.

Additionally, I request the final Work Plan document for the Textile Road Site.

The Ypsilanti Township community deserves a full environmental history of this site. Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to your response to these questions and requests, as well as to my September 16, 2026 request.

title: Fedorchak outlines rural health care priorities for North Dakota during Elgin and Bowman hospital roundtables
text:
Bowman, ND – Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-ND) outlined her priorities for strengthening rural health care across North Dakota during roundtables held at both Jacobson Memorial Hospital Care Center in Elgin and Southwest Healthcare Services in Bowman. Her agenda focuses on reducing costs and improving access, including extending support for Critical Access Hospitals and Community Health Centers, advancing rural health investments, and addressing the reimbursement and workforce challenges that threaten access to care close to home.

Meeting with hospital leadership and local and state officials, Fedorchak highlighted her newly introduced legislation to extend the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) for five years and North Dakota’s nearly $200 million award through the Rural Health Transformation Program.

“Rural hospitals like Jacobson Memorial and Southwest Healthcare are lifelines for the communities they serve, which extend for hundreds of miles in sparsely populated areas like southwest North Dakota,” Fedorchak said. “Our providers need practical solutions. That’s why I’m focused on: supporting reliable emergency services, expanding access to specialists, helping providers recruit and retain staff, and making federal reimbursement work better for rural communities. These conversations help guide that work so we can keep quality care close to home for North Dakotans.”

Fedorchak and Senator John Hoeven introduced legislation to extend FCHIP, which tests flexible Medicare payment models for Critical Access Hospitals in some of the country’s most sparsely populated communities. Three North Dakota hospitals participate: Jacobson Memorial Hospital Care Center in Elgin, McKenzie County Healthcare Systems in Watford City, and Southwest Healthcare Services in Bowman.

The program is scheduled to expire on December 31, 2026. A five-year extension preserves critical flexibilities that help participating hospitals provide additional skilled nursing beds, expand telehealth, and sustain ambulance services. The program aims to improve access and coordination while testing ways to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and Medicare costs.

In Elgin, FCHIP supports advanced life support ambulance services for patients facing cardiac emergencies, trauma, and transfers over long distances. Theteams of EMTs also play key staffing roles at the facility and provide 24/7 coverage. At other participating North Dakota hospitals, the program helps older residents receive nursing care in their home communities and connects patients with specialists through telehealth.

The extension legislation is endorsed by the National Rural Health Association, the North Dakota Hospital Association, and the Montana Hospital Association.

Fedorchak’s broader work to strengthen rural health care includes:

Supporting nearly $200 million for North Dakota’s rural health transformation. Fedorchak voted to establish the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program. North Dakota received nearly $199 million for FY2026 to strengthen rural care, support workforce recruitment and retention, and modernize facilities and technology.

Extending access to telehealth. Fedorchak voted to extend Medicare telehealth flexibilities through December 31, 2027, helping rural North Dakotans connect with providers and specialists without traveling long distances for care.

Reining in prescription drug middlemen. Fedorchak voted for the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act, which requires pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to disclose prescription drug costs, rebates, and fees to employers, helping them negotiate better deals and lower costs for patients.

Advancing more affordable coverage and greater patient choice. Fedorchak helped introduce the More Affordable Care Act (MACA), legislation that gives states greater flexibility to expand coverage options and allow eligible patients in participating states to use federal assistance through individual health accounts to purchase coverage and pay for care.

title: Fedorchak provides details on Harvest Fuel Relief program for American farmers
text:
Bismarck, ND – Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-ND) applauded the announcement of the $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program to help North Dakota farmers manage rising input costs, including diesel, during harvest season. Funded through the Commodity Credit Corporation (CCC), the program will provide one-time payments to eligible producers for the 2026 crop year.

“Farmers have told me the sharp spike in diesel prices right during harvest threatens to wipe away any profit they might have made this year. This investment provides much-needed relief for North Dakota farm families during a challenging season,” Fedorchak said. “I know North Dakota farmers want lower input costs, stronger commodity prices, and market certainty—not handouts from the federal government. Our long-term focus must be on expanding market access, strengthening domestic energy production, and building more American refineries and fertilizer plants to help our farmers compete and thrive.”

The Harvest Fuel Relief Program will be administered by the Farm Service Agency (FSA), with payments calculated using reported planted acres, USDA production cost estimates, and projected yields and prices.

Additional program details include:

Payment rates: Commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities will be announced in November, with additional eligible commodities to follow.

Producer applications: Eligible producers with a Login.gov account linked to USDA will receive pre-filled online applications ahead of the application period.

Additional commodities: Specialty crop growers, fishermen, and other non-Title I producers are encouraged to submit information about increased fuel costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov to help USDA determine payment rates.

The program builds on recent improvements to the Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) and Price Loss Coverage (PLC) programs, which took effect this month, providing additional support for producers facing challenging market conditions.

title: Fedorchak reminds North Dakota students of approaching Congressional App Challenge deadline
text:
Bismarck, ND — Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-ND) encourages middle and high school students across North Dakota to submit their projects for the 2026 Congressional App Challenge by Monday, October 26, at noon ET.

“North Dakota is full of bright, talented young people with big ideas. From agriculture to energy, innovation is part of who we are, and our students are the next generation of problem solvers,” Fedorchak said. “As technology continues to transform how we live and work, learning to develop these tools is more important than ever. The Congressional App Challenge is a great opportunity for students to put their creativity and skills to work. I encourage students across our state to take advantage of this opportunity and show what North Dakota ingenuity can do.”

The Congressional App Challenge is a nationwide competition that encourages middle and high school students to explore computer science, develop coding skills, and solve real-world problems through technology. Students are invited to design and create their own original software applications, with submissions accepted across a variety of platforms.

The competition provides students with hands-on experience in technology and encourages the next generation of American innovators.

title: Fitzpatrick Announces Additional $1.25 Million for United Way’s HELP Center, Building on $4.15 Million Commitment to Bucks County Families
text:
Levittown, PA – Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) announced a major victory for Pennsylvania’s First District, securing an additional $1.25 million in federal Community Project Funding for United Way of Bucks County’s new permanent headquarters and HELP Center in Levittown, bringing the total federal investment he has championed for the project to $4.15 million.

Building on the $2.9 million Fitzpatrick previously advanced through the FY24 appropriations process, this latest investment marks another major milestone in a years-long partnership to transform how Bucks County families access essential services, emergency assistance, and opportunities for long-term stability.

Since opening, the new HELP Center has served more than 3,200 unique neighbors, with United Way reporting a 60% increase in neighbors served compared to the previous quarter at its former location.

Remarking on the impact, Marissa Christie, President & CEO of United Way of Bucks County stated: “United Way of Bucks County’s new headquarters and HELP Center represents an extraordinary opportunity for Bucks County. Thanks to Congressman Fitzpatrick’s leadership and his commitment to this work, we can make it easier for more people to get the help they need, connect families with opportunities for greater financial stability, and build a stronger future for our neighbors. His support helped turn an ambitious vision into a reality that will benefit Bucks County for generations to come.”

“I’ve had the honor of working alongside Marissa Christie and the extraordinary United Way team for many years, and I’ve seen firsthand the difference their dedication makes in the lives of our neighbors. When Marissa shared her vision for a permanent home that could fundamentally improve how we serve families across Bucks County, I got to work. I made this project a priority and fought for $4.15 million in federal investment to help turn that vision into reality. Today, that vision is making a measurable difference—reaching more neighbors, connecting families with critical resources, and creating new pathways to stability and opportunity. That is the true measure of this investment: not simply the dollars committed, but the lives changed and the opportunities created. I’m grateful for United Way’s unwavering commitment to our community, and I look forward to building on our partnership to ensure more families have the support and opportunities they need to thrive,” said Fitzpatrick.

A Lasting Investment in Bucks County

The new HELP Center represents a significant expansion of United Way’s ability to meet both immediate needs and long-term challenges facing Bucks County families. The permanent facility will:

Expand access to critical assistance: Increase capacity to provide essential goods, emergency resources, and coordinated support to more individuals and families.

Strengthen community partnerships: Bring nonprofit organizations, municipal partners, and service providers together to improve coordination, reduce barriers, and ensure assistance reaches those who need it most.

Create pathways to greater stability: Connect families with workforce resources, housing and health-related assistance, and opportunities to achieve greater financial independence.

Delivering For Pennsylvania’s First District

The HELP Center investment is part of Fitzpatrick’s broader commitment to advancing community-driven projects throughout Bucks and Montgomery Counties.

Through the FY2026 Community Project Funding process, Fitzpatrick successfully championed more than $27.5 million for 11 community projects addressing critical local needs across Pennsylvania’s First District.

With this latest round of funding, Fitzpatrick has brought more than $80 million in federal Community Project Funding to PA-01 since FY2022, translating priorities identified by local communities into lasting investments in the people, services, and infrastructure that strengthen the region.

Together, these investments reflect Fitzpatrick’s community-first leadership, empowering local organizations, responding to community needs, and ensuring federal resources translate into meaningful, measurable, and lasting benefits for Bucks and Montgomery counties.

title: Fong Celebrates $1.37 Million Grant for State Route 58
text:
BAKERSFIELD, CA — Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) is announcing that the Kern Council of Governments has been awarded a $1.37 million discretionary grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation under the BUILD program. The funding will support a comprehensive feasibility and economic analysis of State Route 58 between Interstate 5 in Kern County and Interstate 15 in Barstow, including consideration of re-designating the route from State Route 58 to Interstate 40.

“State Route 58 is one of the most critical freight corridors in the entire country, connecting the Central Valley to national markets and carrying the goods that keep our economy moving,” said Congressman Fong. “This $1.37 million BUILD grant is an important first step towards upgrading this corridor and unlocking its full potential for Kern County and the nation. I am proud to have supported this effort and look forward to seeing this study lay the groundwork for necessary and essential improvements to one of California’s most vital transportation arteries.”

“State Route 58 is a critical transportation corridor connecting Barstow to the Central Valley and supporting the movement of goods throughout California and across the country,” said Congressman Jay Obernolte. “As freight traffic continues to increase, it is critically important that we evaluate opportunities to improve the safety, efficiency, and capacity of this roadway. This federal funding will help identify the infrastructure improvements needed to support economic growth and ensure this vital corridor can meet future transportation demands.”

"This grant is the first step to defining needed improvements to SR 58," said Jay Schlosser, Executive Director, Kern Council of Governments. "Once understood, we are looking to advance an understanding of the importance of this roadway to Kern County, the State of California, and the nation.”

State Route 58 is a nationally significant east-west freight corridor linking Interstate 40 and Interstate 15 with Interstate 5, providing a critical connection between Midwest and East Coast freight gateways and Central and Northern California. The corridor serves approximately 21,000 daily travelers, with truck volumes reaching up to 37 percent in certain segments. It is designated on the Strategic Highway Network and the National Highway Freight Network, and serves as the only year-round, all-weather trans-Sierra route.

The study funded by this grant will evaluate the requirements to upgrade State Route 58 to Interstate design standards and identify prioritized multimodal improvements along the corridor.

title: Fong’s Clergy Act to Support Faith Leaders Signed into Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, President Trump signed H.R. 227, the Clergy Act into law. This effort, led by Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) in the U.S. House of Representatives and Senator Katie Britt (R-AL) in the U.S. Senate, marks a major step forward in giving pastors and clergy members greater retirement security.

The Clergy Act establishes a one-time re-enrollment window for pastors and other clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security to voluntarily opt back in and begin contributing to their financial future.

Some pastors opted out decades ago, often due to inaccurate advice, only to later face significant financial hardship. Under previous law, this opt-out was permanent. For clergy who have spent their lives serving their communities and congregations, this restores the freedom to secure basic financial protection in retirement.

“Our faith leaders dedicate their lives to serving others and strengthening our communities,” said Congressman Fong. “The Clergy Act gives clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security the opportunity to re-enroll and secure their financial future. I’m proud this bipartisan legislation passed both chambers of Congress and was signed into law by President Trump. Thank you to Senator Britt for her partnership and to President Trump for his leadership and commitment to our faith community. Those who spend their lives caring for others deserve the opportunity to plan for their own future. This law is an important step toward making that happen.”

“I’m grateful to President Trump for signing the Clergy Act into law today and for standing with the faith leaders who serve our communities daily. Pastors, priests, and ministers are pillars of their communities for a reason, and they deserve the chance to build a secure retirement for themselves and their families. Many made this decision at the very start of their ministry without fully understanding what it would mean down the road, and I’m thrilled they will now have the chance to re-enroll in these important benefits. I’m thankful for Senator Hassan’s partnership and for Congressman Vince Fong’s leadership in the House in getting this commonsense, bipartisan bill to the President’s desk and now enacted,” said Senator Britt.

"America’s pastors and faith leaders spend their lives caring for others,” said Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith. “Many chose to opt out of Social Security when they were young and just starting their ministry. A single, sometimes ill-advised, decision made decades ago should not stand between them and a secure retirement. The Clergy Act gives them a second chance. I commend Representative Fong for standing up for our faith leaders and thank President Trump for signing this into law."

"Congressman Vince Fong's leadership on the Clergy Act will provide an additional option for many ministers as they prepare for retirement. We are grateful for his commitment to pastors and ministry families, and GuideStone stands ready to provide the education and resources ministers need to evaluate whether this opportunity is right for them," said Dr. D. Hance Dilbeck Jr., President and CEO of GuideStone Financial Resources of the Southern Baptist Convention.

"Catholic priests and religious leaders have dedicated their lives to service of Christ by ministering to the faithful and all those who are in need. As law, the Clergy Act will help enable them to obtain better financial well-being in their retirement. We are grateful to Congress for enacting this important legislation,” said Chieko Noguchi, Executive Director of the Office of Public Affairs, United States Conference of Catholic Bishops.

“Southern Baptists care deeply about ensuring that our ministers and their families are cared for in retirement after their years of obeying God’s call to serve in ministry. The ERLC is excited to see the Clergy Act signed into law, which will benefit eligible ministry families as they plan for their retirement. We are grateful to Rep. Vince Fong and Sen. Katie Britt for their leadership on the Clergy Act in Congress and to President Trump for signing the bill into law,” said Dr. Evan Lenow, President, Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention.

“I thank the President for signing the Clergy Act into law, and, again, I applaud the bipartisan leadership of Congressman Fong, Congressman Thompson, Senator Britt, and Senator Hassan in successfully advancing this bill in Congress,” said Evangelical Council for Financial Accountability (ECFA) President & CEO Michael Martin. “The temporary window this law opens for ministers to re-enter the Social Security system is a breath of fresh air for many servant leaders who may feel trapped by a decision they did not fully understand as they began their pastoral work.”

“By giving clergy who previously opted out of Social Security an opportunity to opt back in, the Clergy Act will create a pathway to a stronger financial foundation in retirement for those who have dedicated their lives to serving our communities,” said Christopher Wells, Executive Director, Church Alliance. “The Church Alliance is grateful that this important piece of legislation has been signed into law and looks forward to working with the Internal Revenue Service, Social Security Administration, and Congress on its implementation.”

“AARP is pleased to endorse this bipartisan and common-sense legislation to allow clergy members to opt back into earning Social Security and Medicare benefits for retirement,”said Jennifer Jones, Vice President, Financial Security and Livable Communities, AARP.

“Many pastors and ministry families will be helped by the Clergy Act becoming law. I am grateful to Congressman Vince Fong and all who worked diligently to make this possible, and I am thankful that pastors who qualify will now have the opportunity to re-enroll in Social Security and prepare more securely for their senior years,” said Dr. Paul Chappell, Pastor, Lancaster Baptist Church.

"Faith & Giving applauds the enactment of the Clergy Act, an important and long-overdue reform that will help provide greater financial security for clergy who have devoted their lives to serving others,” said Brian Walsh, Executive Director, Faith & Giving. "After years of championing this vital reform, we are especially grateful to Representatives Vince Fong and Mike Thompson and the other bipartisan champions who made this achievement possible."

Background on the Clergy Act

The Clergy Act creates a two-year window — covering taxable years beginning January 1, 2029, and January 1, 2030 — for eligible clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security to revoke their exemption and begin contributing. Importantly, this legislation does not modify existing Social Security regulations. Eligible clergy must still meet the standard 10-year contribution requirement to earn full retired-worker benefits, receiving benefits proportional to their contributions. The bill also requires the IRS and Social Security Administration to submit a plan to Congress outlining their strategy to inform clergy members of their eligibility to re-enroll.

Historically, Congress has approved limited re-enrollment windows, including in 1999 under the Ticket to Work Act.

The legislation was co-led in the House by Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-04). It passed the House Ways and Means Committee unanimously, 40-0, and overwhelmingly passed the House of Representatives with bipartisan support 350-5 before passing the Senate unanimously.

title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Introduces Bill to Close Tax-Avoidance Loophole Used by the Ultra-Rich
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, October 20, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) introduced the Pay Your Taxes Avoided by Borrowing (TAB) Act, legislation to close the “buy, borrow, die” loophole that lets the wealthiest Americans turn stock and other assets into spendable cash without ever paying tax on their gains.

A one-pager on the bill is available here. Full text is available here.

The ultra-wealthy avoid paying taxes on their fortunes with a strategy known as “buy, borrow, die.” Under current law, gains on stock, real estate, and other assets are taxed only when the asset is sold. So instead of selling, the ultra-wealthy buy assets that grow in value, borrow against them, and live on the loan proceeds, which are not counted as income. When they die, those assets pass to their heirs with a stepped-up basis that erases the untaxed gain, so the gain is never taxed.

The Pay Your TAB Act taxes large asset-backed loans at 23.8%, the top long-term capital gains rate plus the Net Investment Income Tax, so borrowing against a fortune is taxed the same way as selling it.

“The Pay Your TAB Act closes a loophole the ultra-wealthy use to avoid paying taxes on fortunes 99% of Americans can’t imagine. They don’t sell the stock, they borrow against it, and a loan isn’t counted as income,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “My bill taxes those loans at 23.8%, the exact rate they’d owe by selling, while protecting mortgages, business loans, car loans, and student loans that hardworking families actually carry. It’s simple, it’s fair, it’s constitutionally sound, and it can be enforced the day it’s signed.”

WHAT THE PAY YOUR TAB ACT DOES:

Imposes a 23.8% excise tax, paid by the borrower, on covered loans issued after December 31, 2026.

Applies only to the portion of a borrower’s total covered loans above $1 million, with related parties counted together so the threshold can’t be split.

Prevents double taxation by giving the borrower an offsetting long-term capital loss, equal to the taxed loan amount, when they later sell the asset that secured the loan.

Requires lenders to report covered loans above the threshold to the IRS and to borrowers, and directs Treasury to issue anti-avoidance rules.

WHAT IS EXEMPT:

Mortgages on a primary residence up to $3 million.

Qualified student loans.

Business loans, other than loans used to fund distributions.

Qualified margin loans used for trading securities.

Because the Pay Your TAB Act is an excise tax on the issuance of a loan, it rests on the same constitutional authority Congress has used to levy excise taxes since the nation’s founding. It applies only when a loan is issued, so it doesn’t require taxing unrealized gains on assets that have never been sold. The bill is also simple to enforce because the tax is based on the amount of the loan rather than on calculating the changing value of an asset.

title: On International Sloth Day, Rep. Frost Introduces SLOTHS Act, Alongside Congresswoman Lee, Local Leaders, and Animal Advocates to Prevent Animal Cruelty and Stop Sloth Trafficking
text:
Watch the Full Press Conference Here

ORLANDO, FL — Today, on International Sloth Day, Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) introduced the Stopping Legalized Organized Trafficking and Harm to Sloths Act (SLOTHS Act), legislation to prohibit sloth imports into the United States, with limited exceptions for research and conservation-focused breeding programs.

The legislation follows reports of widespread sloth deaths at the planned Sloth World attraction in Orlando. An unannounced state wildlife inspection in August 2025 raised concerns about conditions at the warehouse where the animals were housed. State records show 31 sloths died between December 2024 and February 2025, including 21 after arriving at a facility without electricity or running water.

The SLOTHS Act would prohibit sloth imports, with exceptions for deceased sloths imported for documented research and captive sloths transferred to Association of Zoos and Aquariums-accredited institutions for breeding programs, provided they were not taken from the wild after enactment. Violations could carry civil penalties of up to $20,000, criminal fines of up to $100,000 for knowing violations, cancellation of federal authorizations, and forfeiture of illegally imported sloths.

“We owe it to these animals, and to the people in our community who spoke up, to make sure a tragedy like this never happens again,” said Congressman Frost. “Sloths have highly specialized needs, and their care requires scientific expertise and accountability. The bipartisan SLOTHS Act is an important step toward protecting these vulnerable animals and ensuring their welfare comes first.”

“Protecting wildlife and supporting responsible conservation are goals we can advance together,” said Congresswoman Laurel Lee. “Sloths are a unique part of our natural world, and their well-being depends on care that meets their specialized needs. Following the tragic loss of dozens of sloths in Central Florida, the bipartisan SLOTHS Act will strengthen legal protections through targeted import restrictions while preserving important research and conservation programs. I appreciate Congressman Frost’s partnership and the advocates working to secure a better future for these animals.”

“I am grateful to see bipartisan legislation being filed in the United States Congress to protect wildlife and prevent the importation of wild-caught sloths into the United States. Wild animals deserve to live in the wild, free from human profit and exploitation. We'll continue to advocate for animal welfare at the state and local level as we support this federal effort,” said State Representative Anna Eskamani.

“As the team that took on the initial intensive care and stabilization of the surviving Sloth World sloths, the Board of Trustees, staff, and volunteers of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens appreciate and applaud Representatives Frost and Lee for introducing this legislation to protect a vulnerable species. After almost six months, we continue to see unusually strong stress reactions from some of the individual sloths at times when there is any deviation from their normal routine. These reactions demonstrate the long-term impact of the trauma these sloths have suffered through their importation and time at Sloth World. Sloths, like many other non-domesticated species, need and deserve experienced, highly-specialized care by professionals who stay abreast of the latest science and best practices about those species – the kind of experience they can find at accredited zoos and aquariums.” – Richard E. Glover, Jr., CEO Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens

"The Association of Zoos and Aquariums commends Representatives Maxwell Frost and Laurel Lee for their leadership in protecting vulnerable wild sloth populations from unethical exploitation. The SLOTHS Act will restrict and penalize bad actors while ensuring the vital conservation initiatives of credible institutions can continue. On behalf of AZA, we thank Representatives Frost and Lee for their bipartisan proposal and proudly support this effort to safeguard sloth species." - Dan Ashe, President and CEO of AZA

“The exotic pet trade and wildlife tourism industry treat sloths as novelties, but sloths are fragile wild animals that suffer and often die when removed from their native habitats. Restricting the importation of sloths into the U.S. will help curb the demand that drives the trade in these animals and protect them from a life of suffering. The Animal Welfare Institute applauds Representatives Frost and Lee for introducing the SLOTHS Act.” - Kate Dylewsky, Assistant Director of Government Affairs, Animal Welfare Institute

“After the deaths of 58 sloths at Sloth World, we made a promise to do everything in our power to make sure something like this could never happen again - and we meant it. But Sloth World was just the tip of the iceberg. It exposed a cruel and unnecessary trade in which hundreds of wild sloths are captured and sold as commodities every year, despite a mortality rate of up to 90%. The SLOTHS Act is an opportunity to finally draw a line and say that this is not acceptable. By closing the door on the importation of wild-caught sloths into the United States we can stop this cruelty at its source. We cannot undo the suffering of the sloths already caught up in this trade, but we can make sure their suffering was not in vain. We made a promise, and we will not stop fighting until this trade is brought to an end. We are so grateful to Representatives Frost and Lee for standing alongside us and taking action to help make that promise a reality.” — Dr. Rebecca Cliffe, Founder and Executive Director, The Sloth Conservation Foundation

“As sloths have grown more popular, so has their suffering. Sloth lovers are paying to interact with sloths, unaware they are contributing to a cruel industry. Most of these animals are ripped from the wild to endure inadequate living conditions and often painful deaths. The SLOTHS Act is a vital step toward ending this suffering. I am incredibly grateful to Representatives Frost and Lee for introducing this legislation to stop the removal of sloths from the wild for commercial import. Sloths belong in the rainforest, and the American people deserve to stop being misled.” — Sam Trull, MSc - Co-founder and Executive Director, The Sloth Institute

"What makes sloths so loveable also makes them targets for exploitation. Behind those sweet faces and slow movements lie complex life histories, long gestation periods, and specific environmental requirements. That's why the Stopping Legalized Organized Trafficking and Harm to Sloths (SLOTHS) Act's ban on importation into the US is so important. Congressman Frost and Congresswoman Lee are taking the initiative to help keep these cherished animals in the wild and out of a cruel trade driven by the desire for pets and selfies. Sloths deserve more than the inhumane fate that awaits them in the name of entertainment." - Danielle Kessler, US Director, International Fund for Animal Welfare

"The Sloth World disaster is a devastating reminder of the suffering wild animals endure because of lax oversight and inadequate legal protections. Dozens of sloths died, yet authorities found that no laws had been violated. Prohibiting the import of wild sloths is a critical step toward preventing future tragedies and protecting these remarkable animals from exploitation. We commend Congressman Frost and Congresswoman Lee for championing this important legislation," said Alicia Prygoski, Strategic Legislative Affairs Manager with the Animal Legal Defense Fund.

The SLOTHS Act is endorsed by the Sloth Institute, the Sloth Conservation Foundation, Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, the Association of Zoos and Aquariums, the Animal Welfare Institute, the Animal Legal Defense Fund, and the International Fund for Animal Welfare.

title: Congressman Harris Applauds $8 Billion USDA Relief Program for Farmers and Watermen
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Andy Harris, M.D. (MD-01), Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, applauded President Donald Trump and U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins for announcing $8 billion through USDA’s new Harvest Fuel Relief Program to help agricultural producers facing rising fuel costs and market disruptions.

Statement from Congressman Harris:

“Rising fuel costs are cutting into the earnings of farmers and watermen across Maryland’s Eastern Shore. I applaud President Trump, Secretary Rollins, and USDA for providing $8 billion in relief to help offset these costs. As Chairman of the House Agriculture Appropriations Subcommittee, I have pushed for a USDA Office of Seafood and for commercial watermen to be treated as agricultural producers with access to USDA programs.”

USDA will announce payment rates for major crops in November, with details for watermen to follow. Farmers are encouraged to prepare for the application process, while watermen can submit information on increased fuel costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov to help USDA determine payment rates.

For more information, visit USDA.gov.

title: Social Security Administration Takes Initial Action Following Pressure from Horsford and Cortez Masto, Fails to Provide Feasible Solution for Foster Care Youth
text:
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Following a joint letter from Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), the Social Security Administration (SSA) took initial steps to address a backlog of Social Security number applications for children in Clark County’s foster care system. The agency has processed 19 applications since the lawmakers reached out, leaving nearly 1,300 foster youth still waiting for the documents they need to access critical services.

SSA has proposed accepting records printed from Nevada’s statewide vaccination system, provided each record is accompanied by an individual certification letter from the Nevada Department of Human Services (DHS). However, Nevada DHS lacks the staffing capacity to produce a separate letter for every child, creating another administrative barrier.

“While I’m glad SSA heard our concerns and took action, I’m focused on a permanent solution that will provide these young people with the federal services they are entitled to,” said Rep. Horsford. “Nearly 1,300 children in Clark County’s foster care system are still waiting for the documents they need to access healthcare, secure employment, and move forward with their lives. These children should not be caught in bureaucratic red tape, and I will continue holding SSA accountable until every pending application is processed.”

“While some progress has been made in beginning to process Social Security number applications, Nevada’s foster youth are relying on the Social Security Administration to find a meaningful, long-term solution to this issue. We will continue to push the Administration to work with Clark County to support foster children across the Valley,” said Senator Cortez Masto.

“Following the leadership of Senator Cortez Masto and Congressman Horsford on this important issue, the County has met with representatives from the Social Security Administration and a solution was proposed through a grant exemption that would require the State of Nevada to write individual certification letters for each child,” said Kevin Schiller, Clark County Manager. “Unfortunately, while well-intentioned, this is not a workable solution, and these barriers continue to impact the quality of life of the vulnerable children we serve. The County sincerely hopes that an effective solution can be reached quickly.”

In December 2025, SSA notified CCFS that Social Security number applications for children in foster care must include records physically certified by the custodian of record. However, Clark County has operated under an electronic records system for civil and family cases since 2010. This documentation discrepancy has prevented children in foster care from obtaining Social Security cards, creating barriers to Medicaid and CHIP enrollment, family reunification, permanent placements, driver’s licenses, and employment opportunities.

In their joint letter, Rep. Horsford and Sen. Cortez Masto called on SSA to immediately process all pending applications, resolve the documentation discrepancy with CCFS by the end of 2026, provide a written response within 10 business days, and deliver regular updates on the backlog.

To date, the parties have not agreed on a workable solution. The lawmakers have noted administrative barriers at SSA and will continue working to establish a permanent solution that ensures no child in Clark County’s foster care system is denied access to essential services because of outdated documentation requirements.

title: LAWMAKERS CALL FOR UKRAINIAN TEMPORARAY PROTECTED STATUS (TPS) EXTENSION
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Rep. Val Hoyle (D-OR) and Rep. Bryan Fitzpatrick (R-PA) led over 50 of their colleagues in sending a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding the agency ensure that Ukrainian nationals legally in the United States, particularly those with Temporary Protected Status (TPS), are able to safely access and attend their immigration court hearings, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) interviews and other required legal appointments.

This push comes as DHS recently announced that over 100,000 of Ukrainians whose TPS benefits were slated to expire on October 19th, will retain their TPS protections and work permits until the Department makes a final decision. While this announcement provides much needed relief for TPS holders, the lack of a formal redesignation and extension could potentially exclude individuals who fled the same war and cause confusion and stress for people already facing uncertainty about their future, impacting their ability to keep work. Without any safe and durable path for Ukrainians to return home, these protections must be kept in place.

The lawmakers wrote: “A redesignation would extend eligibility to Ukrainians who arrived in the United States after the current designation's cutoff date, but who fled the same war under the same circumstances and would give affected individuals clarity regardingtheir status. Those who came to our shores fleeing violence and instability deserve the opportunity to rebuild their lives and go through our country’s legal processes.”

title: Rep. Ronny Jackson Announces $24.6 Million Federal Rail Infrastructure Investment Benefiting Rural Communities and Freight Rail Operations
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) announced that the Panhandle Northern Railroad LLC has been selected to receive up to $24,673,810 in federal funding through the Federal Railroad Administration’s (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program for its Revitalizing America’s Industrial Lifelines (RAIL) project.

The project will support track rehabilitation and infrastructure improvements across short-line railroads in Texas. This will include the Panhandle Northern Railway, which connects Borger, Texas, and the nation’s largest inland chemical complex, to the national rail network. The improvements will include installing new rail, switch timbers, and turnouts to enhance railroad safety, improve reliability, and strengthen freight rail operations. The project was selected for project development, final design, and construction and qualifies for the CRISI Program’s statutory set-aside for rural areas.

“Investing in our nation’s rail infrastructure is critical to keeping American goods moving safely and efficiently,” said Rep. Jackson. “Short-line railroads play an important role in connecting rural communities, supporting local industries, and strengthening our supply chains. This federal investment will help improve rail safety and reliability in TX-13 while supporting the infrastructure that businesses, workers, and communities depend on. I will continue working to ensure rural America receives the infrastructure investments it needs to grow and prosper.”

title: Dr. Joyce Announces Infrastructure Improvement Funding for James E. Van Zandt VA Medical Center
text:
October 20, 2026

Altoona, PA – Today, Congressman Joyce issued the following statement announcing more than $375,000 will go toward facility improvement requests for the James E. Van Zandt Veterans’ Administration Medical Center.

“The James E. Van Zandt Medical Center has been treating the heroes of our nation for more than seventy years," said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “Having served as a physician at the medical center, I understand the importance of maintaining the excellent quality of care that our veterans deserve. In Congress, I recognize that my obligation now is to serve those who answered the call to serve America.”

BACKGROUND

Congressman Joyce's work in Washington helped secure a $4.8 billion non-recurring maintenance budget for Fiscal Year 2026 which is the largest in the Veterans' Affairs department's history. Of the broader investment into our nation’s veterans, $375,104 from these funds will be used to make fire safety repairs and renovate the 4th floor of James E. Van Zandt Medical Center right here in Altoona.
