title: Krishnamoorthi Leads 105 Lawmakers Urging FBI Hate Crime Probe After Attempted Mass Shooting at His Family’s Hindu Temple in Aurora
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) today led 105 members of Congress, including the entire Illinois House Democratic delegation, every Indian American member of Congress, and Senators Dick Durbin, Tammy Duckworth, Andy Kim, and Chris Van Hollen, in urging FBI Director Kash Patel to investigate the attempted mass shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, as a potential federal hate crime. Krishnamoorthi and his family were worshipping at the temple when the attempted attack occurred on October 11. The lawmakers also demanded answers about the FBI’s efforts to identify and address credible online threats targeting Indian Americans, Hindu Americans, and other South Asian communities.

According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, tried to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled and later communicated plans to return before a coworker alerted police, who arrested him that day. Prosecutors allege that he authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu house of worship. Investigators recovered a rifle, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, body armor, and white supremacist imagery.

In the letter, the lawmakers write:

“The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention.”

The letter comes amid a surge in online hostility toward South Asians. A September 2026 report identified more than 542,000 anti-South Asian hateful posts on X between January 2025 and June 2026, with the monthly volume rising approximately 240 percent from January 2024 to June 2026. A Carnegie Endowment survey also found that 48 percent of Indian American respondents encountered racist posts targeting their community very or somewhat often since the start of 2025, while one in four reported being called a slur.

The lawmakers also criticize Trump Administration messaging that they warn risks legitimizing racial and religious stereotypes. They cite a Department of Homeland Security post depicting a Sikh man with the message, “Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh,” and a Department of Education post declaring “Make College Football Great Again” after a Texas Republican complained about South Asians attending a University of Texas football game.

The lawmakers continue:

“We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities.”

The lawmakers are seeking information on whether the FBI is examining potential racial, ethnic, and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals facilitated the alleged plot, and what steps the Bureau is taking to protect houses of worship and address credible threats without infringing on First Amendment protections.

The lawmakers requested a written response to the following questions, to the extent consistent with an ongoing investigation, by October 29, 2026:

Is the FBI investigating the alleged Aurora-area plot as a potential federal hate crime? If so, is that investigation examining both racial or ethnic bias and religious bias, and is the Bureau coordinating with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division and the appropriate U.S. Attorney’s Office?

Are investigators examining whether the defendant used online platforms to communicate threats, select potential targets, obtain assistance, or coordinate with others? Are they assessing whether any individuals encouraged or materially assisted the alleged plot?

What steps is the FBI taking, consistent with the First Amendment and applicable investigative authorities, to identify and assess credible online threats targeting Indian Americans, Hindu Americans, Sikhs, and other South Asian communities? How does the Bureau distinguish protected expression, including offensive speech, from threats and conduct warranting investigation?

What mechanisms exist for sharing actionable threat information with state and local law enforcement and potentially targeted houses of worship? What outreach and protective resources are being offered to affected communities following this alleged plot?

Does the FBI have adequate personnel, language expertise, and analytical capacity to assess threats involving anti-Indian, anti-Hindu, and broader anti-South Asian bias? What additional resources, if any, does the Bureau believe it needs?

The lawmakers conclude:

“No one should fear being targeted because of their ancestry, appearance, or faith, and no congregation should have to wonder whether gathering for worship will make its members targets of mass violence. We urge the FBI to investigate the evidence fully, pursue all applicable offenses, and provide affected communities with a clear account of the steps being taken to protect them.”

title: Larsen, Colleagues Succeed in Delaying New CBP Rule Harming Access to Lower-Cost Medications
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) released the following statement:

“In the past few months, my office has received dozens of messages from constituents worried about how they are going to afford prescription medications if the Trump administration's new CBP rule goes into effect on October 22. I urged the Administration to delay the rule and stop health care from getting even more expensive, and last week, the Trump administration caved to pressure and announced a delay of the rule. I will continue to advocate for a final rule that stops dangerous and illegal drugs from entering our country without stopping affordable prescription medications.”

On October 16, the Trump administration announced that it would delay implementation of new Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) procedures from October 22, 2026 to January 20, 2027. The new CBP procedures would increase regulations for international mail shipments, which could disrupt 2.3 million Americans’ longstanding ability to obtain lower-cost prescription medicines from Canada and other countries for personal use.

Earlier this month, Rep. Larsen joined a letter signed by 71 Members of Congress to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin, Acting Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Kyle Diamantas and Commissioner of CBP Rodney Scott, urging the agencies to ensure Americans can continue obtaining non-controlled prescription medicines from outside the country.

“For years, our constituents who have struggled with high prescription drug prices have obtained their medicines from pharmacies outside the United States, especially from Canada,” the Members wrote. “We are concerned that the new process could be implemented in a manner that prevents personal-use prescription medicines from being shipped to the United States or results in their routine refusal, including medicines Americans have long obtained from licensed pharmacies abroad.”

The full text of the letter is available here.

Larsen Fights for Affordable Health Care

Increasing access to affordable health care in Northwest Washington is a top priority for Rep. Larsen. He is fighting to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, and has hosted roundtables with Northwest Washington community members to discuss policies to expand access to affordable health care, including his legislation that would reverse burdensome paperwork requirements in Medicaid.

title: Larsen Highlights Federal Shipbuilding Funding Creating Local Jobs in Bellingham
text:
Last week, Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) toured All American Marine’s facility in Bellingham with Ron Wille (All American Marine, President and COO), Jim Wunderman (San Francisco Bay Ferry, Chair) and Raymond Scott (Echandia Marine, Head of Sales). All American Marine (AAM) is building electric ferries for San Francisco Bay Ferry (SFBF), and Echandia Marine is a Marysville business that provides batteries for SFBF’s ferries.

“Shipbuilding is alive and well in Northwest Washington, and it is creating local jobs that sustain families,” said Rep. Larsen. “As the top Democrat on the Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, I will continue to make investments in maritime infrastructure and passenger ferry systems that help regional economies grow.”

During the tour, Rep. Larsen operated a 550-ton CNC press brake and viewed two 30-foot MasterCam router tables. These pieces of equipment enable AAM to produce ferry vessels for SFBF, and AAM was able to purchase the equipment thanks to funding federal funding from the Small Shipyards Grant Program. Rep. Larsen helped AAM secure the grant to purchase the equipment in 2023.

“We were proud to welcome Congressman Larsen to All American Marine and show firsthand how federal investment in American shipbuilding translates directly into good-paying local jobs, modern manufacturing capabilities, and vessels being built right here in Bellingham, WA,” said Ron Wille, President and COO of All American Marine. “We are especially proud to be building San Francisco Bay Ferry’s first fully electric high-speed ferries, helping demonstrate what American shipyards and maritime technology can deliver for the next generation of passenger transportation.”

“These electric ferries can be built for roughly the same cost as diesel vessels but will cost less to operate and maintain,” said Jim Wunderman, Chair of SFBF.“We project vessel maintenance savings of 32% and the cost of electricity is anticipated to be at least 20% less than diesel fuel. These savings can be reinvested in the operation of more service to meet ferry demand that continues to surge.”

“Federal investment in shipyards like All American Marine creates demand that reaches well beyond the shipyard itself,” said Raymond Scott, Head of Sales at Echandia. “Our team in Marysville is proud to supply LTO battery systems for San Francisco Bay Ferry’s first fully electric high-speed ferries, and we thank Congressman Larsen for his leadership in making Northwest Washington a hub for the next generation of maritime technology."

On the T&I Committee, Rep. Larsen has been an advocate for the Small Shipyard Grant Program, which helps local shipyards make critical infrastructure investments. He has also been a champion for increasing federal funding for passenger ferries, which are critical to Northwest Washington’s rural communities and economy.

In August, Rep. Larsen announced the Small Shipyards Grant Program awarded $1.3 million to Everett Ship Repair LLC and Rozema Boat Works, Inc. Rep. Larsen also helped the Port of Bellingham secure $23.5 million from the Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) grant program in July.

title: Malliotakis, Morano Announce Agreement Between NYC and National Park Service to Fund Great Kills Park Remediation
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) and New York City Council Member Frank Morano today announced that New York City has signed a funding and implementation agreement with the National Park Service (NPS) to advance the remediation of radioactive contamination at Great Kills Park on Staten Island.

The agreement follows a July 28, 2026, letter from Malliotakis and Morano to National Park Service Acting Superintendent Minka Sendich and New York City Department of Environmental Protection Commissioner Lisa Garcia urging both agencies to finalize the necessary agreements and expedite the cleanup. The agreement marks a critical step toward the remediation of the Great Kills Ball Field that was condemned and closed to the public in March 2009 following the discovery of radioactive contamination.

Under the agreement, New York City is responsible for funding and completing the remediation, while the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers stands ready to perform the cleanup work on the City's behalf. Once the remediation is completed, construction of the levee and tide-gate portions of the East Shore Seawall can move forward, bringing the project closer to completion and ultimately providing critical coastal storm protection for Staten Island residents and their homes.

"Staten Islanders have waited more than twenty years for this contamination to be addressed, and this agreement is an important step toward finally getting the cleanup underway," said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. "Council Member Frank Morano and I have pushed the agencies involved to work together and eliminate unnecessary delays so we can move this project forward. Remediating Great Kills Park is critical to completing the East Shore Seawall and protecting our communities from future storms like Superstorm Sandy."

“After more than 20 years, it looks like we're finally moving from finger-pointing to actual progress at Great Kills Park. I want to give tremendous credit to Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis, who's been absolutely relentless in fighting to get this done. I'm proud to have worked alongside her to help break this logjam. This agreement is a major victory for Staten Island, but it's not the finish line. Now we need to turn signatures on paper into shovels in the ground. Cleaning up Great Kills Park isn't just about reclaiming a treasured public space. It's also about completing the East Shore Seawall and protecting thousands of Staten Islanders from the next Superstorm Sandy. Nicole and I aren't going to let up until the job is done," said Council Member Frank Morano.

title: McClellan and Haridopolos Introduce Legislation to Establish National American History and Founders Month
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and Congressman Mike Haridopolos (FL-08) introduced the bipartisan and bicameral National American History and Founders Month Act to empower Americans to be active citizens through a deeper understanding of our nation’s early history, its founders and founding ideals, and the civic duties within the American experience.

“Our nation was established 250 years ago on the revolutionary idea that the power of government derives from the people in order to secure the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “To ensure that all citizens can participate in our government by, of and for the people, each generation must fully understand the rich and complex history of its founding. The National American History and Founders Month Act provides an opportunity to reflect on that history and recommit to ensuring the great American experiment endures.”

“This year, we celebrated 250 years of freedom, independence, and the enduring principles that have shaped our nation,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “We are truly lucky to live in the greatest country in the world, and we must never take that blessing for granted. As a former history teacher, I know that by teaching future generations about our nation’s founding and the sacrifices that made our freedoms possible, we can ensure America’s remarkable story continues to inspire for generations to come.”

title: Congressman Menefee Backs Legislation to Protect Domestic Violence Survivors
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) announced his support of the Family Violence Prevention and Services Improvement Act of 2026 and the National Domestic Violence Awareness Month Resolution in recognition of Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Both measures support efforts to protect survivors, prevent domestic violence, and keep families safe.

“We need to do everything in our power to improve safety around survivors and their families, and stop this violence from ever happening in the first place,” said Rep. Menefee. “That means investing in early prevention, making sure a survivor has a safe place to turn the moment they ask for help, and ensuring our communities have the resources to break the cycle of abuse before someone gets killed. These bills will help make that happen.”

According to the Texas Council on Family Violence (TCFV), more than half of the survivors in Texas who sought emergency shelter were denied solely due to a lack of space.

The Family Violence Prevention and Services Improvement Act of 2026, led by Representative Lucy McBath (GA-06), would support trauma-informed shelter and support services, strengthen the National Domestic Violence Hotline, and expand community-based prevention programs.

Domestic violence is a public health crisis. Last year alone, 160 Texans lost their lives to domestic violence, leaving 223 children without one or both parents. Harris County recorded the highest number of intimate partner homicides of any county in Texas, underscoring the devastating toll this crisis continues to take on our communities.

The National Domestic Violence Awareness Month Resolution, led by Representative Al Green (TX-09), supports the goals and ideals of National Domestic Violence Awareness Month and calls on Congress to keep raising awareness of domestic violence and supporting programs to end it.

Congressman Menefee remains committed to supporting the organizations and advocates working on the front lines to protect survivors, prevent domestic violence, and ensure that no one has to face abuse alone. As a member of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, Congressman Menefee also supports federal policies aimed at addressing the dangerous intersection of domestic violence and gun violence, including efforts to keep firearms out of the hands of domestic abusers and protect families from further harm.

If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, help is available. Call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-SAFE (7233), text START to 88788, or visit thehotline.org.

title: Menendez Introduces Bill to Expand Access to Plug-In Solar and Lower Electric Bills
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) introduced the Socket Full of Sunshine Act, legislation that expands access to plug-in solar panels and helps families lower their utility bills The legislation would support rebates for eligible households, protect renters’ access, and require states to consider removing unnecessary regulatory hurdles. In New Jersey, monthly utility bills rose nearly 17 percent in 2025, twice the national average.

“Families are getting squeezed by electric bills that keep going up,” said Congressman Rob Menendez. “Plug-in solar is a simple, affordable way to cut those bills, but outdated rules and unnecessary fees are standing in the way. The Socket Full of Sunshine Act clears those barriers so more families, including renters, can start saving.”

A typical plug-in solar system consists of 1-4 panels, with current costs ranging from $285-$3,500 depending on size and inclusion of a battery. They can cut electricity bills by hundreds of dollars a year without complicated installation costs. The use of plug-in solar systems can also help households and businesses meet their energy needs through sustainable and renewable energy and lessen America’s dependence on fossil fuels and other sources of pollution.

While plug-in solar systems are intended to be “plug-and-play,” some utilities and state laws require that they be subjected to utility connection agreements that apply to larger rooftop solar installations. These agreements and other unnecessary installation costs or requirements can double the price of these systems and prevent renters, apartment dwellers, or other households from accessing this practical option to reduce electricity costs.

The Socket Full of Sunshine Act would:

Require states to consider removing barriers to plug-in solar, such as interconnection agreements and utility-imposed approvals, fees, insurance mandates, and equipment requirements;

Set clear safety standards for plug-in solar devices;

Create a $100 million annual Department of Energy grant program to fund state rebates of up to $1,000 for low- and moderate-income households;

Protect renters’ right to use plug-in solar devices; and

Create a label that shows consumers their expected electricity savings.

This legislation has been endorsed by the Sierra Club, the New Jersey chapter of the League of Conservation Voters, The Consumer Federation of America, Evergreen Action, the Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition, and Bright Saver.

“Plug-in solar can help households reduce energy bills, lower demand on the grid, and decrease dangerous emissions,” said Sierra Club Deputy Legislative Director for Clean Energy and Electrification Xavier Boatright. “This bill would help renters and low- and moderate-income households access the benefits of clean energy. We are grateful for Representative Menendez’s leadership in introducing this bill to bring American-made plug-in solar panels to more people.”

“Plug-in solar can help put clean energy within reach of more American families, giving renters and homeowners another way to manage their electricity costs. By expanding access to these technologies and providing rebates for low and moderate-income households, we can provide common sense ways to access cheaper clean energy,” said Allison McLeod, Interim Executive Director, New Jersey LCV. “The Socket Full of Sunshine Act recognizes that the benefits of the clean energy transition should be accessible to everyone. We applaud Representative Rob Menendez Jr. for advancing an approach that connects energy affordability, consumer choice, and American-made clean energy.”

“Balcony solar is a safe and accessible way to reduce individual home energy costs. This Act will bring solar power to far more American homes,” said Consumer Federation of America Director of Climate and Energy Policy Karim Marshall. “CFA enthusiastically supports the 'Socket Full of Sunshine Act' and applauds Representative Menendez for his visionary leadership in introducing this bill. It reflects a thoughtful and meaningful package of solutions that will enable consumers to save real money on their skyrocketing electric bills and ensure that deployment is done in the safest way possible.”

“Americans are being squeezed by record-high energy bills and they need relief now. The Socket Full of Sunshine Act would put solar energy and the savings it offers within reach for renters and low to moderate income households who have been shut out for too long,” said Evergreen Action Federal Affairs Director Dani Hupper. “By making it easier to access plug-in solar panels, this legislation will let families generate their own clean power and save hundreds of dollars a year on their bills. Solar is already saving families money. This bill makes sure renters and working families aren't left out.”

“As America works to rebuild its domestic solar manufacturing industry, we need to make sure growing demand for solar energy also supports the workers and companies making these products here at home,” said Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition Executive Director Mike Carr. “The Socket Full of Sunshine Act recognizes that expanding access to affordable solar energy and supporting American manufacturing should go hand in hand. By prioritizing American-made products and tying federal rebates to domestic manufacturing and content requirements, this legislation can help create new demand for U.S.-made solar products and strengthen our domestic supply chains. Plug-in solar offers another way for Americans to lower their electricity bills while supporting American jobs and building a brighter future for domestic manufacturing.”

“Representative Menendez has just taken a giant leap toward energy affordability for all Americans,” said Bright Saver Co-CEO and Co-Founder Cora Stryker. “10 states now have laws on the books to open the door to affordable solar that plugs into a standard outlet. Representative Menendez has just opened the door to energy equity in all 50 states, for renters and homeowners alike.”

Congressman Rob Menendez has been a leading voice for lowering energy costs for New Jersey families, earlier this year introducing the PRICE Act, the Data Center Transparency Act, and the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act which passed the House in September. Congressman Menendez has represented New Jersey’s Eighth District since 2023. He serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and its Subcommittees on Environment, Energy, and Communications and Technology. To learn more about his work, click here.

title: Menendez presenta un proyecto de ley para ampliar el acceso a la energía solar enchufable y reducir las facturas eléctricas
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – El Congresista Rob Menendez (NJ-08) presentó la Ley Enchufe Lleno de Sol, una legislación que amplía el acceso a paneles solares enchufables y ayuda a las familias a reducir sus facturas de servicios. La legislación apoyaría los reembolsos para los hogares elegibles, protegería el acceso de los inquilinos y exigiría a los estados considerar eliminar obstáculos regulatorios innecesarios. En Nueva Jersey, las facturas mensuales de servicios subieron casi un 17 por ciento en 2025, el doble de la media nacional.

"Las familias están siendo presionadas por facturas eléctricas que no paran de aumentar", dijo el Congresista Rob Menendez. "La energía solar enchufable es una forma sencilla y asequible de reducir esas facturas, pero las normas obsoletas y las tarifas innecesarias se interponen en medio. La Ley Enchufe Lleno de Sol elimina esas barreras para que más familias, incluidos los inquilinos, puedan empezar a ahorrar."

Un sistema solar enchufable típico consta de 1 a 4 paneles, con costos actuales que oscilan entre 285 y 3.500 dólares dependiendo del tamaño y la inclusión de una batería. Pueden reducir las facturas eléctricas en cientos de dólares al año sin costos de instalación complicados. El uso de sistemas solares enchufables también puede ayudar a hogares y empresas a cubrir sus necesidades energéticas mediante energía sostenible y renovable, y reducir la dependencia de Estados Unidos de los combustibles fósiles y otras fuentes de contaminación.

Aunque los sistemas solares enchufables están pensados para ser "enchufables y utilizables", algunas compañías eléctricas y leyes estatales exigen que estén sujetos a acuerdos de conexión de servicios públicos que se aplican a instalaciones solares grandes en tejados. Estos acuerdos y otros costos o requisitos de instalación innecesarios pueden duplicar el precio de estos sistemas e impedir que inquilinos, residentes de apartamentos u otros hogares accedan a esta opción práctica para reducir los costos eléctricos.

La Ley Enchufe Lleno de Sol sería:

Esta legislación ha sido respaldada por el Sierra Club, la sección de Nueva Jersey de la Liga de Votantes para la Conservación, la Federación de Consumidores de América, Evergreen Action, la Coalición de Fabricantes de Energía Solar para América y Bright Saver.

"La energía solar enchufable puede ayudar a los hogares a reducir las facturas de energía, disminuir la demanda en la red y disminuir las emisiones peligrosas", dijo Xavier Boatright, subdirector legislativo de Energía Limpia y Electrificación del Sierra Club. "Este proyecto de ley ayudaría a los inquilinos y a los hogares de ingresos bajos y moderados a acceder a los beneficios de la energía limpia. Estamos agradecidos por el liderazgo del Representante Menendez al presentar este proyecto de ley para llevar los paneles solares enchufables fabricados en Estados Unidos a más personas."

"La energía solar enchufable puede ayudar a poner la energía limpia al alcance de más familias estadounidenses, dando a los inquilinos y propietarios otra forma de gestionar sus costos eléctricos. Al ampliar el acceso a estas tecnologías y ofrecer reembolsos a hogares de ingresos bajos y moderados, podemos ofrecer formas sensatas de acceder a energía limpia más barata", dijo Allison McLeod, directora ejecutiva interina de la LCV de Nueva Jersey. "La Ley de Enchufes Llenos de Sol reconoce que los beneficios de la transición a la energía limpia deben ser accesibles para todos. Aplaudimos al Representante Rob Menendez Jr. por impulsar un enfoque que conecta la asequibilidad energética, la elección del consumidor y la energía limpia fabricada en Estados Unidos."

"La energía solar en balcón es una forma segura y accesible de reducir los costes energéticos individuales en el hogar. Esta ley llevará la energía solar a muchos más hogares estadounidenses", dijo Karim Marshall, director de Política Climática y Energética de la Federación de Consumidores de América. "La CFA apoya con entusiasmo la 'Ley de Enchufes Llenos de Sol' y aplaude al Representante Menendez por su liderazgo visionario al presentar este proyecto de ley. Refleja un paquete de soluciones reflexivo y significativo que permitirá a los consumidores ahorrar dinero real en sus facturas eléctricas disparadas y garantizar que su despliegue se haga de la manera más segura posible."

"Los estadounidenses están siendo presionados por facturas energéticas récord y necesitan alivio ya. La Ley Enchufe Lleno de Sol pondría la energía solar y los ahorros al alcance de los inquilinos y los hogares de ingresos bajos a moderados que han estado excluidos durante demasiado tiempo", dijo Dani Hupper, directora de Asuntos Federales de Evergreen Action. "Al facilitar el acceso a paneles solares enchufables, esta legislación permitirá a las familias generar su propia energía limpia y ahorrar cientos de dólares al año en sus facturas. La energía solar ya está ahorrando dinero a las familias. Esta ley asegura que los inquilinos y las familias trabajadoras no queden excluidos."

"Mientras Estados Unidos trabaja para reconstruir su industria nacional de fabricación solar, debemos asegurarnos de que la creciente demanda de energía solar también apoye a los trabajadores y empresas que fabrican estos productos aquí en casa", dijo Mike Carr, director ejecutivo de la Coalición Solar Energy Manufacturers for America. "La Ley Enchufe de Sol reconoce que ampliar el acceso a energía solar asequible y apoyar la manufactura estadounidense deben ir de la mano. Al priorizar los productos fabricados en Estados Unidos y vincular las devoluciones federales a los requisitos nacionales de fabricación y contenido, esta legislación puede ayudar a crear nueva demanda de productos solares fabricados en EE. UU. y fortalecer nuestras cadenas de suministro nacionales. La energía solar enchufable ofrece otra forma para que los estadounidenses reduzcan sus facturas eléctricas mientras apoyan los empleos estadounidenses y construyen un futuro más prometedor para la manufactura nacional."

"El Representante Menendez acaba de dar un gran salto hacia la asequibilidad energética para todos los estadounidenses", dijo Cora Stryker, codirectora ejecutiva y cofundadora de Bright Saver. "Ahora 10 estados tienen leyes para abrir la puerta a la energía solar asequible que se conecta a un enchufe estándar. El Representante Menendez acaba de abrir la puerta a la equidad energética en los 50 estados, tanto para inquilinos como para propietarios."

title: Congressman Moran Seeks Dedicated Artificial Intelligence Policy Fellow as Congress Works to Keep Pace with the Technology
text:
Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-01) is hiring an Artificial Intelligence Policy Fellow for his Washington office. The paid position will support his work on emerging technology and national security.

Artificial intelligence advances faster than standard legislative processes, spanning crucial areas such as national defense, trade and tax policies, economic growth, and U.S. competitiveness with China. As a member of the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Congressman Moran has spearheaded legislative efforts in this field, co-authoring the AI Kill Switch Act with Rep. Ted Lieu (CA-36), advancing the AI Incident Reporting Act, and leading other AI-related policy initiatives. Maintaining effective oversight of these evolving systems requires a dedicated expert focused entirely on tracking AI developments.

“I recognize both the risks and rewards of AI, and I’m confident we can simultaneously solve any potential problems while accelerating the benefits. Safety and innovation are not mutually exclusive. And, we seek to achieve both by being a trusted policy partner to all stakeholders who also seek thoughtful, well-reasoned and fact-based AI policies that are beneficial to the personal, economic, and national security interests of the United States and its citizens. To do this, we need to commit the resources and personnel to get the policy right for this ever-evolving technology,” said Congressman Moran. “This moment of innovation demands serious attention and bold action, and I am seeking someone who shares that same conviction and dedication.”

The AI Policy Fellow will:

Research AI capabilities and risks

Track AI-related legislation and hearings

Prepare the Congressman for engagement with think tanks, industry leaders, academia, and federal agencies

Candidates with experience in AI, policy research, or national security are encouraged to apply. Eligibility depends on experience. Applicants should send a one-page resume and a one-page, single-spaced cover letter as PDF attachments to Amanda.Baldwin@mail.house.gov. Additional materials may be requested.

title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE ANNOUNCES $500,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO SUPPORT SURVIVORS OF GUN VIOLENCE IN ROCHESTER
text:
(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle announced $500,000 in federal funding for Rise Up Rochester's Safe Housing Gun Violence Response Program, which provides critical assistance to individuals and families impacted by gun violence. The funding, secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding process, will help survivors access emergency housing relocation, victim advocacy, and other essential services as they work to rebuild their lives.

“Gun violence leaves lasting scars on individuals, families, and entire neighborhoods, and we have a responsibility to ensure survivors are not left to navigate the aftermath alone,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I'm proud to have secured this investment to strengthen the important work of Rise Up Rochester and help ensure more people in our community have the stability, security, and support they deserve.”

“Communities most impacted by gun violence deserve more than sympathy, they deserve resources,” said Chiamaka Ikpeze, Executive Director of Rise Up Rochester. “This funding allows us to provide immediate safety, housing support, and advocacy for survivors and families facing some of the hardest moments of their lives. We are deeply grateful for Congressman Joe Morelle and his commitment to our community.”

Rise Up Rochester, in partnership with Coordinated Care Services, Inc. (CCSI), will utilize the funding to address the immediate safety, housing, and recovery needs of gun violence survivors throughout Rochester. The Safe Housing Gun Violence Response Program will provide real-time relocation assistance and temporary housing support to help individuals and families move to safer living environments following incidents of gun violence.

The program will also provide victim advocacy, court accompaniment for survivors participating in legal proceedings, transportation assistance, and support services to help individuals navigate the challenges that often follow violent incidents. By combining immediate crisis intervention with longer-term stabilization efforts, the initiative aims to help survivors regain a sense of security while strengthening the safety and well-being of families and neighborhoods across Rochester.

title: Griffith Announces $1.5 Million EPA Brownfields Grant to Mount Rogers Planning District Commission
text:
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced new federal funding for U.S. communities through the Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment, Revolving Loan Fund and Cleanup grant program. The EPA awarded Mount Rogers Planning District Commission, based in Marion, Virginia, a $1.5 million assessment coalition grant to support brownfield inventories, planning, environmental assessments, community outreach and cleanup activities at a local brownfield site.

Congressman Griffith continues to voice his support for the Brownfields Program, which delivers millions of dollars to Southwest Virginia communities to help with potential economic development projects.

Following the EPA grant notice, U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) issued the following statement:

“Rural communities, including those in Virginia’s Ninth District, benefit economically and environmentally from the redevelopment of local brownfield sites.

“This EPA Brownfields grant for $1.5 million helps Mount Rogers Planning District Commission take steps to redevelop local brownfield sites.”

BACKGROUND

Mount Rogers Planning District Commission serves the Counties of Bland, Carroll, Grayson, Smyth, Washington and Wythe as well as the Cities of Bristol and Norton.

The Brownfields Program empowers states, communities and other stakeholders to work together to prevent, assess, safely clean up and sustainably reuse brownfields.

A brownfield site is real property, the expansion, redevelopment, or reuse of which may be complicated by the presence or potential presence of a hazardous substance, pollutant or contaminant.

Brownfield Assessment grants provide funding for brownfield inventories, planning, environmental assessments and community outreach.

According to the EPA, Assessment Coalition grants are designed for one “lead” eligible entity to partner with two to four eligible entities that do not have the capacity to apply for and manage their own EPA cooperative agreement and otherwise would not have access to Brownfields grant resources.

Congressman Griffith’s e-newsletter on the Program can be found here.

In 2025, Congressman Griffith announced that LENOWISCO Planning District Commission received multiple Brownfield-related grants from the EPA. That funding supported community-wide assessments of local brownfields.

Since 2019, other Ninth District communities to receive Brownfields Program funding include Pennington Gap in Lee County, Dublin and Pulaski in Pulaski County, Bluefield in Tazewell County, Martinsville City and Bristol City. Data available here.

Before his July 2025 appointment as Health Subcommittee Chairman, Congressman Griffith chaired the Subcommittee on Environment.

In March of 2025, Congressman Griffith chaired a hearing on the EPA’s Brownfields Program. Scott County Native and LENOWISCO Planning District Commission Executive Director Duane Miller testified to the panel and discussed the Program’s importance to Southwest Virginia communities.

In March 2026, Congressman Griffith’s remarks during a legislative hearing on the EPA Brownfields Program can be found here.

In June 2026, Congressman Griffith announced a $1 million EPA Brownfields grant for the City of Martinsville.

title: Pocan, Welch Lead 16 Members Urging Ag Sec. Rollins to Reissue Dairy Business Funding Opportunity
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Mark Pocan (WI-02) and U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) led a letter signed by 16 Members of Congress to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins, urging her to withdraw the newly added 25% cost-share requirement for the Dairy Business Innovation (DBI) Initiatives program and reissue the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) without a matching requirement.

The DBI Initiatives program was established by Congress as part of the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 to promote innovation in the dairy industry. It has retained strong bipartisan support ever since. The original law did not require recipients to match federal funding and this burdensome change comes when dairy farmers and businesses are already struggling as a result of volatility in markets and increases in costs.

“Today, the four existing initiatives serve dairy farmers and processors in 41 states and territories, representing 87 percent of the nation's milkshed,” the Members wrote. “They are the Dairy Business Innovation Alliance at the University of Wisconsin, the Northeast Dairy Business Innovation Center at the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets, the Pacific Coast Coalition at California State University, Fresno, and the Southeast Dairy Business Innovation Initiative at the University of Tennessee. Together they have awarded more than $106 million to 911 dairy businesses. Even so, they have been able to meet only about 35 percent of the demand they see through their competitive award processes. By law, at least half of each initiative's funding must go directly to grants to dairy businesses. The remainder supports technical assistance in business planning, marketing, and product development.”

“The need for this support has never been greater,” the Members continued. “Dairy farmers and processors are facing volatile markets, higher production and fuel costs, labor shortages, aging infrastructure, and growing competition. Small and mid-sized operations in particular depend on DBI to modernize equipment, develop new products, reach new markets, and keep viable outlets for farmers' milk. DBI works because it puts federal resources in the hands of regional partners with deep technical expertise and long-standing relationships with the dairy businesses they serve.”

“The organizations that host these initiatives are public universities and a state department of agriculture, working in partnership with a nonprofit trade association. They do not profit from DBI funding, and they generally do not have unrestricted resources to cover a 25 percent match,” the Members concluded. “The initiatives have told USDA that the new requirement could make continued operation of the program untenable. A requirement meant to stretch federal dollars could instead keep those dollars from reaching the farms and processors Congress intended to help.”

A digital copy of the letter can be found here.

title: Reps. Salinas, Thompson Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Lower Housing Costs and Support American Timber Industry
text:
Portland, OR — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Congressman Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15) introduced the bipartisan Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act, legislation to lower housing construction costs, strengthen American manufacturing, and create good-paying jobs in rural communities. The bill would provide tax incentives to expand domestic production of mass timber, an innovative wood building material that can help builders construct homes faster and at a lower cost.

As part of the bill rollout, Rep. Salinas visited Timberlab in Portland to tour their mass timber production facility and discuss the details of the bill.

“Every Oregon family deserves a home they can afford. Right now, Oregon needs to build nearly 500,000 new homes over the next 20 years to keep up with demand, but we simply aren’t building enough, and the restricted supply leads to increased prices,” said Rep. Salinas. “Mass timber can help us build faster and more affordably. Oregon has led the wood products industry for generations, and this bill provides the opportunity for Oregon workers lead what comes next. That means more homes for working families and more good jobs in the rural towns that helped build this state. I look forward to working with Rep. Thompson to get this done.”

"The northern tier of Pennsylvania historically has been a leader in timber production, and this important industry has done its part to drive local economies for generations,” said Rep. Thompson. “The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act will strengthen the forest products industry and fund future research, which will drive innovation and the future of timber usage,”

Mass timber products are made from layers of wood bonded or fastened together to create strong structural components, including large panels and beams. These materials are particularly well-suited for mid-rise housing projects, where traditional wood framing may not be practical and other construction materials may not be economical. Because mass timber components can be manufactured off-site and assembled quickly, they can reduce construction timelines and therefore costs.

Despite these advantages, manufacturers face significant barriers to expanding production. Building new facilities and purchasing specialized equipment require substantial upfront investments. Limited domestic manufacturing capacity has contributed to higher material prices, making it harder for builders to adopt mass timber construction.

The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act would:

Help manufacturers build new plants. The bill offers a 10 percent tax credit for investments in mass timber manufacturing facilities, including machinery, equipment, and buildings. It does this by adding mass timber to the existing Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit.

Reward research that brings costs down. This bill creates a 20 percent credit that covers every dollar a company spends on mass timber research, from new products to better production methods.

For Oregon, expanding mass timber manufacturing presents an opportunity to build on the state's timber and wood products industry while supporting economic growth in rural communities. Increased production could create new demand for American-grown wood, support family-wage manufacturing jobs, and help builders access more affordable construction materials.

“Americans want lower costs, and housing is their biggest bill,” said Adam Kovacevich, CEO of Chamber of Progress. “Housing costs too much because building costs too much, but mass timber frames go up in weeks. The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act will help American factories make more of it so we can build more, build faster, and bring rents down.”

The bill is endorsed by: American Wood Council, Chamber of Progress, Oregon Forest Industries Council, Washington Mass Timber Accelerator, and Weyerhaeuser.

title: On Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day, Congresswomen Simon, Randall, and Pressley Call for Disabled Women to be Paid Fairly, Introduce Resolution Recognizing the Need to Close the Wage Gap and Reduce Economic Barriers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, on Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day, Congresswomen Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), and Emily Randall (WA-06) announced they will introduce the Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution. This resolution recognizes the persistent pay disparity between disabled women and both disabled and nondisabled men, and it reaffirms the need to reduce systemic, economic barriers and advance economic equity for disabled women.

According to recent analysis from the National Partnership for Women & Families, disabled women continue to face high-wage gap disparities compared to their nondisabled male counterparts, earning 56 cents for every dollar paid to nondisabled men. The pay gap is even greater for disabled women of color, who are paid 46-55 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic nondisabled men. Additionally, working disabled mothers are paid 44 cents for every dollar paid to nondisabled fathers.

“Disabled women of color experience some of the largest pay gaps in our nation- impacting their ability to care for themselves and their loved ones,” said Congresswoman Simon. “This is an unacceptable reality, which is why I joined disability champions in Congress, Reps. Pressley and Randall, to introduce this resolution and demand action to undo systemic barriers to equal pay, break down the discrimination that disabled women face, and move towards a future where every individual is valued for their labor without discrimination based on gender, race, or disability.”

"Disability rights are human rights. It is shameful that in 2026, women with disabilities are paid 44 cents for every dollar paid to non-disabled fathers—and that wage gap only widens for working disabled women of color," said Congresswoman Pressley. “Our Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution makes it clear: We must put an end to this economic injustice and make sure everyone gets equal pay for equal work.”

“We all deserve to live full lives, to be treated with dignity and respect. All people with disabilities still face huge system barriers, and for disabled women they’re compounded,” said Rep. Randall. “Women with disabilities make less than non-disabled women, and less than disabled men. Government has to do better. As Chair of the Better Pay and Benefits Task Force, I’ll keep fighting for working people everywhere to get the pay and benefits they’ve earned so folks of all abilities can live and thrive in their communities.”

This resolution is endorsed by the Democratic Women’s Caucus, American Association of People with Disabilities (AAPD), Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN), National Partnership for Women & Families (NPWF), Disability Culture Lab (DCL), National Disability Rights Network (NDRN), Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), National Disabled Legal Professionals Association (NDLPA), Equal Rights Advocates (ERA), New Disabled South.

As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress and a mother of two, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon is committed to advancing disability rights and justice for Americans with disabilities, including women and mothers with disabilities.

title: WNBA REPONDS TO REP. STUTZMAN’S INQUIRY BY CALLING ENES FREEDOM AND ROYCE WHITE “MEN”
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a letter last month to WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, Congressman Marlin Stutzman (IN-03) asked, “If the WNBA has no definition of “women” why were Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White deemed ineligible to join the WNBA?”

In a stunning admission, Commissioner Engelbert replied by saying, “With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men.”

See for yourself here:

Image

This is the WNBA admitting that despite both Freedom and White declaring themselves women, the league does not honor their chosen gender. By announcing that Freedom and White are “both men,” the WNBA has taken a step towards deciding what a woman could be referring to in their bylaws but still fall dramatically short of a true definition. The WNBA also still has no publicly available policy governing eligibility of transgender of athletes.

“The WNBA has just taken the first step in defining what a woman is for the sports community,” said Congressman Stutzman. “By clearly labeling Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White as “men” they have acknowledged that identifying as a woman does not change basic human biology. While this is a step in the right direction, the glaring disrespect the WNBA still has for their fans and our national anthem needs to be corrected.”

title: Congressman Turner Announces $8.6 Million for Miami Conservancy District Dam Repairs
text:
DAYTON, OH — Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10) joined the Miami Conservancy District on Tuesday to announce $8.685 million in federal funding he secured for improvements to the Germantown, Englewood and Taylorsville dams.

“I’m pleased to announce that, through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process, I was able to secure $8,685,000 to make necessary improvements to the upstream walls of the Germantown, Englewood, and Taylorsville dams,” said Rep. Turner. “The amount of this investment reflects how competitive our community’s projects are at a national level, and it’s also a testament to how necessary this critical infrastructure project is to keep the Miami Valley safe.”

The three dams were constructed in the early 1920s following the devastating 1913 flood and are classified as high-hazard, Class One dams. At more than 100 years old, they are well beyond their original expected service life and require upgrades to meet modern engineering standards.

The project will strengthen the dams, improve their resiliency and extend their useful life by at least another 75 years.

title: Congressman Van Drew Calls for Independent Audit of Atlantic City Electric Digital Meters
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Van Drew called on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to help secure an independent audit of Atlantic City Electric's (ACE) digital smart meters after multiple South Jersey residents reported that their meters continued registering electricity usage even after they turned off their homes' main breakers.

"Something is very wrong here, and I am not going to stop until we get to the bottom of it," said Congressman Van Drew. "People are telling us they shut off the electricity to their entire homes, and the meters are still running. Bills have doubled and tripled, a federal audit already uncovered transmission overbilling issues, and families are paying more than ever despite promises of a rate freeze. The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities has done nothing to give these families relief, so I am asking the federal government to help get an independent audit. While FERC does not directly regulate residential meters, we need an independent review by a party with no financial ties to ACE or its parent company. I am not backing down until we get answers."

Residents who have noticed their digital meters continuing to register electricity usage after shutting off their main breaker, or whose meters have failed to properly account for electricity generated by their solar panels, are asked to report their experiences to his office by completing this form.

Rep. Walberg’s efforts to combat the opioid crisis across our nation:

As a member of the Bipartisan Heroin Task Force, Congressman Walberg has been committed to working with his colleagues to address the alarming opioid epidemic that is affecting communities in Michigan and sweeping the nation.

title: Walkinshaw Moves to Block Trump-Putin Diesel Deal That Would Bankroll Russia’s War
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, announced he is cosponsoring the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act, bipartisan legislation introduced by Congressman Gregory W. Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, to block President Trump’s deal to purchase and import Russian diesel.

“Americans struggling with rising costs should not be asked to bankroll Vladimir Putin’s war machine,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Putin is a war criminal who has devastated Ukrainian families and sent Russians to die in his war of aggression. Ukraine is a trusted partner of the United States, and its people deserve our support. Trump’s Russian diesel deal rewards Putin for prolonging this war. I’m joining this bipartisan legislation to block that deal, deny Putin revenue to fund his attacks, and help Ukraine secure a just and lasting peace.”

The legislation would:

Prohibit the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation from investing in Russian energy.

Revoke Treasury Department licenses allowing the Russian energy transactions targeted by the bill and prohibit future licenses.

Require the Trump administration to impose sanctions on Russian energy.

A copy of the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act is available here.

title: Budd Conducts Air Power Oversight at USAFA Following the Release of the Board of Visitors’ Semiannual Report
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.), member of the Senate Armed Services Committee and a member of the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) Board of Visitors (BoV), recently visited the Academy, where he gained firsthand insight into the rigorous education, training, and leadership development provided to Air Force cadets, following the Board’s semiannual report being sent to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. The report advances the BoV’s statutory mission by providing the Pentagon with a strategic framework to strengthen the Academy’s institutional effectiveness and cadet development.

“As American air power remains critical to our national defense, we must ensure U.S. Air Force Academy cadets receive the training, education, and development needed to meet the demands of modern warfare. I am confident that the Board’s recommendations, in our report to Secretary Hegseth and Secretary Meink, will strengthen the Academy’s capacity to better prepare the next generation of Air Force officers to lead with excellence and defend our nation against evolving threats,” said Senator Budd.

“Airpower is relied on more heavily than ever to deter our adversaries and defend our interests around the world, and the Air Force Academy produces the leaders who deliver it. It’s our responsibility to make sure they have the resources, facilities, and training to succeed. As Chairman, I am grateful to my fellow Board members for their dedication and expertise, which are reflected in this report and its recommendations to prepare cadets for the demands of modern warfare. I look forward to working with my colleagues and Air Force Academy leadership to put these recommendations into action,” said USAFA BoV Chairman, Representative August Pfluger (R-Texas-11)

During his visit to the USAFA, Senator Budd met with cadets—including nine North Carolinians—Academy leadership, and fellow Board members to conduct oversight, discuss opportunities to strengthen the airmanship experiences, and advance the Academy’s mission of developing the next generation of Air Force and Space Force officers.

BACKGROUND

Read the complete 2026 January – July Semiannual Report HERE.

Some notable recommendations made by the Board to the Secretary of War include:

• Reforming the Air Force Academy Athletic Cooperation (AFAAC) Structure and Governance

• Opening the Cadet Chapel in Phases

• Increasing Emphasis and Funding for Advanced Simulators and Drone Technology

• Elevating the Value of USAFA Officer Assignments

Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman U.S. Senator Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) appointed Senator Budd to the USAFA BoV in January 2026.

title: Cantwell: H.R. 1 Healthcare Cuts “Driving Up The Cost on All of Us”
text:
Cantwell: H.R. 1 Healthcare Cuts “Driving Up The Cost on All of Us”

NEW Report: WA hospitals facing $5.8 billion in lost revenue b/c of Republican healthcare cuts; all Washingtonians will feel the pain in the form of higher prices, longer ER wait times, and reduced services

SEATTLE, WA – Today, U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and senior member of the Finance Committee, joined local healthcare leaders and Diana, a stage 4 cancer patient from Lynnwood, to detail how Washingtonians will face higher healthcare costs and reduced services because of cuts to Medicaid passed as part of H.R. 1, (a.k.a. the “One Big Beautiful Bill”).

At the event, Sen. Cantwell released a report containing exclusive new data from the Washington State Hospital Association and the Washington Association for Community Health detailing the crushing financial losses expected to result from provisions in Trump’s H.R. 1 set to kick in on Jan. 1, 2027, that will kick more than 200,000 Washingtonians off their health insurance. Washington’s hospitals expect to lose $5.8 billion in revenue by 2033 and community health centers expect to lose $118 million next year alone. All because of H.R. 1’s Medicaid cuts.

"If you have private insurance, you can expect to see higher premiums because of these cuts," said Sen. Cantwell. " Already, healthcare costs for employer-sponsored insurance are set to rise at least 8.2 percent next year, and 22.2 percent for Washingtonians on the marketplace. So we all know this: When you drive down the cost of uncompensated care, you help keep healthcare costs in check. When you don't do that, you are literally driving up the cost on all of us. When hospitals are left to absorb these losses they have to make difficult decisions. Services will be cut. Hospitals will be closed."

At the event, healthcare leaders and doctors explained how these cuts will result in higher costs, longer emergency room wait times, and reduced healthcare services for ALL Washingtonians – even if they have the best health insurance possible. Hospital ERs and Community Health Centers are required by federal law to treat patients, regardless of their ability to pay.

Sommer Kleweno Walley, CEO of Harborview Medical Center, said that because of the cuts, Harborview will lose over $260 million in current revenue and coverage of up to $400 million in lost reimbursement by 2028 – 22% of the facility’s budget. “When you take hundreds of millions of dollars away from safety net hospitals like Harborview, you are not just putting care for Medicaid patients and uninsured patients at risk,” Kleweno Walley said. “You are putting Harborview's ability to serve our entire community at risk.”

Mike Glenn, CEO of Jefferson Healthcare -- which operates a hospital in Port Townsend -- noted that small, rural hospitals like theirs will feel even more harm. “Rural communities tend to be older and poorer communities than urban communities and more dependent on public payers like Medicare and Medicaid,” Glenn said. “At Jefferson for instance we are bracing for 1,000-2,000 residents losing access to Medicaid, a $6-8 million reduction in top-line revenue, and a $1-1.5 million increase in uncompensated care. In fact we are already seeing our uncompensated care number climbing, which we attribute to the reduction of insurance premium subsidies, forcing patients to abandon their coverage.”

“When a patient loses insurance their need for healthcare doesn't just disappear,” said Lisa Yohalem, CEO of HealthPoint Community Health Centers. “However, the reimbursement that supports that care does.”

Dr. Marie Vrablik, Medical Director of the Emergency Department at UW Medical Center – Montlake, noted that they are starting to see these impacts now, with a steep increase in emergency room patients in the last few months. “These cuts will not impact only folks who are covered by Medicaid, they'll impact all of us,” Dr. Vrablik said. “They'll impact any person waiting in an emergency department waiting room. Because as the ED fills up with patients needing acute unscheduled care, we'll all wait longer, our patients will get sicker, and our situation will only worsen.”

Dr. Lauren Whiteside, an Emergency Medicine physician at Harborview Medical Center, told the story of a patient who was admitted after his second fentanyl overdose in a week, started treatment, and was subsequently able to stay clean and find permanent housing. "This is what access to care can do,” said Dr. Whiteside. “The decisions we make about Medicaid and healthcare access are not abstract policy decisions. They shape when and how people get treatment."

Diana, a Stage 4 cancer patient living in Lynnwood, gave remarks via video: “I don't think there's a single chance that I would be alive today to talk to you if it hadn't been for Medicaid in Washington state. I cannot physically do the work requirements. Right now, I'm still shaking ... because I had chemotherapy yesterday. You might think 'I've got it made, I don't need Medicaid.' You are one accident, one gene that goes wrong away from no longer being able to handle your job and being unemployed and having to apply for Medicaid.”

title: Capito Secures Funding for WVU School of Dentistry
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), chairman of the Senate Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (Labor-HHS) Appropriations Subcommittee, announced a $15 million Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) award for West Virginia University’s (WVU) School of Dentistry from the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA).

This allocation, which was secured through a CDS request made by Senator Capito in Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26), will support renovations to WVU’s Dental School.

In August, Senator Capito attended the ribbon cutting for the school’s recent renovations, which were funded through a $12.6 million Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) award in Fiscal Year (FY) 2024, and a $15 million CDS award in FY26 secured by the senator.

“This funding represents a significant investment in education and health care in West Virginia,” Senator Capito said. “By continuing to modernize this facility, we are helping prepare the next generation of dentists and expanding access to dental care for families across West Virginia. I am proud to have helped secure this funding for the completion of this project, and I look forward to seeing the immense impact this investment will have on West Virginians for years to come.”

“Our commitment to education, community service, and patient care is central to our WVU School of Dentistry mission of improving the oral health and well-being of families throughout West Virginia,” Dr. Stephen Pachuta, dean of the WVU School of Dentistry, said. “The support we received from Senator Capito and the federal appropriations process for this extensive renovation and expansion project is generationally transformational for our communities. As West Virginia’s only dental school, we offer a Doctor of Dental Surgery, a Bachelor of Science in Dental Hygiene, and advanced specialty training. This project will significantly strengthen our educational foundation, helping to address workforce shortages while expanding access to high-quality care throughout our state and our region."

title: Cassidy Announces $5.81 Million to Improve Rail Services between Baton Rouge and New Orleans
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) announced that the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Railroad Administration will provide $5.81 million to replace five aging railroad bridges between Baton Rouge and New Orleans. This will make freight rail service safer between those two cities while laying the groundwork for an eventual passenger rail route. The grant is being funded via the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Program. That program is currently funded in part by Cassidy’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which was signed into law on November 15, 2021.

“This grant brings us one step closer to a passenger rail line between Baton Rouge and New Orleans,” said Dr. Cassidy. “It will also make our rail lines safer for freight trains. This is a win for Louisiana.”

According to the U.S. Department of Transportation, this grant will support project development, final design, and construction to replace five aging railroad bridges in St. James and St. Charles Parishes. When completed, this project is expected to increase safety, lower maintenance costs, and reduce both service disruptions and freight travel times along the affected rail lines.

Additionally, the Southern Rail Commission has proposed a passenger rail route connecting Baton Rouge, Gonzales, LaPlace, Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport, and downtown New Orleans. This project helps lay the foundation for passenger rail service to be established along that route.

title: Senator Collins Announces Maine Farmers, Fishermen and Lobstermen to Benefit from $8 Billion Agricultural Relief Package
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins announced that Maine’s farmers, fishermen, and lobstermen will benefit from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) new $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program, designed to help producers struggling with the high cost of diesel. Senator Collins worked directly with the White House and USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins to advocate for Maine’s fishing and agriculture industries, which have faced significant financial pressures due to rising fuel costs and other increased operating expenses.

“The rising cost of fuel and other inputs has placed significant financial strain on hardworking farmers, fishermen, lobstermen, and their families. After speaking with both the White House and Secretary Rollins, I am pleased to have been assured that Maine fishermen and lobstermen will benefit from the Administration’s new agricultural relief package,” said Senator Collins. “I will continue advocating for Maine’s fishermen, lobstermen, and specialty crop growers, who are integral to our state’s heritage, economy, and way of life, to ensure they receive the support they need to overcome these challenges.”

The new program will provide $8 billion in one-time payments to agricultural producers to help offset a portion of their increased production costs. USDA is expected to announce payment rates for major agricultural commodities in November, with details for other eligible producers, including fishermen and specialty crop growers, to follow. This follows USDA’s decision to create a new Office of Seafood in April.

USDA is encouraging fishermen and specialty crop growers to submit information about their increased fuel costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov to help inform payment rates under the program.
