title: Senators Coons, Blunt Rochester, Murphy, Kelly, Schiff press Attorney General Blanche on the illegal sales of guns to teenagers
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester (Both D-Del.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) on Friday led a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche demanding answers on the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) decision to break with decades of precedent and unilaterally refuse to enforce a prohibition against the sale of handguns to people under the age of 21.

The senators highlighted the enormous risks to public safety if handguns are placed in teens’ hands: “The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.”

The senators laid out the decades-long, bipartisan consensus on banning gun dealers from selling firearms to teenagers: “Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that ‘it shall be unlawful’ for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21. Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.”

The senators argued Attorney General Blanche’s decision is another authoritarian power grab over the judicial branch and Congress: “The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has ‘deeply divided members of the federal bench.’ Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.”

The senators concluded by requesting Attorney General Blanche provide the following information on the authority and research supporting his decision:

A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law

All legal materials concerning the department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20

Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20

A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action

Senators Coons, Blunt Rochester, Murphy, Kelly, and Schiff were joined by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.).

The full letter is available below.

Dear Attorney General Blanche:

We write regarding the U.S. Department of Justice’s (the Department) decision to cease enforcement of longstanding federal restrictions on the sale of handguns to individuals under the age of 21 by federally licensed firearms dealers (FFLs). This significant change in federal enforcement policy raises serious questions about the Department’s legal justification, and we request information regarding the analysis underlying its decision.

On September 18, 2026, the Department’s Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) published a legal opinion concluding that 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1)—the federal prohibition on FFLs selling handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds—violate the Second Amendment, and that federal prosecutors may no longer prosecute FFLs that sell handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds who are not otherwise prohibited from gun possession. Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that “it shall be unlawful” for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21. Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.

The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has “deeply divided members of the federal bench.” Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.

The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.

The Department’s decision to unilaterally cease enforcement of this provision of law raises serious questions and concerns. Thus, we request the Department provide:

1. A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

2. All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

3. Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

4. A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

Please provide the requested information and documents by November 16, 2026.

title: Cortez Masto, Warren Tour New Affordable Housing Community for Seniors, Discuss Bipartisan Housing Law
text:
***VIDEO AVAILABLE***

FTPs for TV stations is available here and additional photos are available here.

Las Vegas, Nev. – Today, U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) toured West Sahara Senior Living, a new 171-unit community that provides affordable one- and two-bedroom apartments to Southern Nevadans over the age of 55. Before the tour, the Senators discussed Southern Nevada’s affordable housing needs with community leaders.

The Senators talked about their work together to pass the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. This law aims to help build more homes, including more affordable housing communities like West Saraha Senior Living, by removing regulatory red tape that slows down housing development, improving existing federal housing programs, and authorizing new affordable housing grant programs.

“This year, Congress passed the biggest housing law in more than 30 years: the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “Senator Warren and I worked tirelessly to get this bill passed and to ensure it included provisions to stop big corporations from buying up homes. I’m glad that she could join me today to hear firsthand how much this law will mean to Nevadans.”

“It was good to be in Nevada and hear from local leaders about how the state is building more housing and helping to lower costs. Senator Cortez Masto was a leader in passing the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act that will increase housing supply and restricts out-of-state Wall Street investors from buying up homes. It’s a good step forward to address the housing affordability crisis, and Senator Cortez Masto and I will keep working to bring down housing costs,” said Senator Warren.

Senator Cortez Masto has been a leader working to lower housing costs and build more homes. She secured $40 million last year and more than $25 million so far this year in investments from the Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco to support the single-family bond program in Nevada. She has introduced bipartisan legislation to make homeownership more accessible and sustainable for working families, increase transparency at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, and improve federal rural housing programs. Last Congress, her AACE Act to cut red tape to speed up federal land transactions and lower housing costs was signed into law.

title: Duckworth, Durbin Announce More Than $12 Million In Funding For Southern Illinois Truck Parking Improvements
text:
[CHICAGO, IL] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today announced a total of $12,645,145 in federal funding for the Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) to support the Southern Illinois Truck Parking Expansion Project.

This funding, from U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) FY26 INFRA Track 2 program, will support the reconstruction and expansion of the Green Creek Southbound and Post Oak Southbound rest areas on Interstate 57 in Illinois by constructing new facilities, upgrading utilities and drainage, and adding approximately 38 truck parking spaces. In addition, the project will deploy Truck Parking Information Management System technologies including automated vehicle detection, electronic kiosks, and security equipment.

“Safe, reliable rest areas are essential for the truck drivers who keep our economy moving and the travelers who rely on Illinois’ roads every day,” Duckworth said. “This significant federal investment will expand truck parking and modernize rest areas in Marion County, increasing parking capacity, improving facilities and making travel safer for drivers.”

“Truck drivers are essential to keeping our economy moving, and they deserve safe, reliable places to rest while on the road. This $12.6 million dollar investment into our trucking industry will help expand parking along I-57 as well as improve safety at the Green Creek and Post Oak rest areas, giving drivers better access to the facilities that they need,” Durbin said. “It is vital to support funding for these improvements that keep our communities and our supply chains moving.”

This project will enhance trucker safety by more than doubling the current commercial parking capacity at two of the I-57 rest areas, while also modernizing aging infrastructure to reduce long-term maintenance costs. Expanded parking and regional parking information systems will also improve travel efficiency, saving drivers an estimated 36 to 44 minutes per route and strengthening supply chain reliability.

Durbin receives award in honor of his decades-long work on the Senate Judiciary Committee

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today was presented the Chicago Bar Association’s (CBA) Justice John Paul Stevens Award in recognition of his longstanding efforts to support the federal judiciary and his decades-long work on the Senate Judiciary Committee. During his remarks, Durbin noted that he has strongly supported the Legal Services Corporation throughout his tenure in Congress. This organization provides essential legal help to millions of Americans who could otherwise not afford it.

“It’s a privilege to receive this award today in honor of the great Justice John Paul Stevens,” said Durbin. “Justice Stevens taught me that government has the duty to treat every person fairly. I have carried that sentiment with me throughout my Senate career, including on the Senate Judiciary Committee—where we worked tirelessly to confirm highly qualified lifetime appointments to the federal judiciary. I’m proud of the work we have done and look forward to the success of the Committee in the future.”

Photos of Durbin at today’s event can be found here.

Established in 2000 and named in honor of the legendary U.S. Supreme Court Justice and native Chicagoan John Paul Stevens, these awards recognize lawyers and judges who best exemplify Justice Stevens’s legacy of pro bono and public service and his commitment to ensuring our justice system is fair and accessible for everyone in the community. Justice Stevens retired from the Supreme Court in 2010 after 35 years of distinguished service and died in 2019.

As Chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee during the Biden Administration, Durbin led the effort in the Senate to confirm 235 lifetime federal judges—the largest number of confirmations in a single term since the Carter Administration. These 235 judges represent more than a quarter of the federal bench. The 235 judicial confirmations include: 187 district court nominees; 45 circuit court nominees; one Supreme Court nominee; and two Court of International Trade nominees. During Durbin’s tenure in the U.S. Senate, 58 federal judges have been confirmed in Illinois—52 district judges and six Seventh Circuit Illinois seats.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Slam Attorney General Blanche For Illegally Allowing Sale Of Guns To Teenagers, Increasing Likelihood Of School Shootings
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined 19 of her Senate colleagues in a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche demanding answers on the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) decision to break with decades of precedent and unilaterally refuse to enforce a prohibition against the sale of handguns to people under the age of 21.

“The Trump administration should be doing more to keep guns out of the wrong hands – not less,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Refusing to enforce the law that bars dealers from selling handguns to teenagers makes our communities less safe and is a direct surrender to the gun lobby at the expense of American lives.”

In their letter, the senators highlighted the enormous risks to public safety if handguns are placed in teens’ hands, writing, “The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address.”

“Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that ‘it shall be unlawful’ for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21. Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the executive branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide,” the senators continued.

The senators concluded by requesting Blanche provide the following information on the authority and research supporting his decision:

A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-DE), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ed Markey (D-MA), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

Senator Gillibrand has long fought for commonsense gun safety laws. She wrote the interstate gun trafficking ban that became law as part of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, which has helped take over 6,000 guns off the streets. When the Trump administration stopped providing updates on prosecutions under the ban, Gillibrand successfully demanded that DOJ restore transparency and resume the updates. She also introduced the Age 21 Act to raise the minimum age to buy assault weapons to 21. In July, she called out the Trump administration’s dangerous rollbacks of gun safety regulations, like those that hold lawbreaking gun dealers accountable and keep guns away from people with serious mental illness.

The full text of the letter is available below. A copy of the letter is available here.

Dear Attorney General Blanche:

We write regarding the U.S. Department of Justice’s (the Department) decision to cease enforcement of longstanding federal restrictions on the sale of handguns to individuals under the age of 21 by federally licensed firearms dealers (FFLs). This significant change in federal enforcement policy raises serious questions about the Department’s legal justification, and we request information regarding the analysis underlying its decision.

On September 18, 2026, the Department’s Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) published a legal opinion concluding that 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1)—the federal prohibition on FFLs selling handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds—violate the Second Amendment, and that federal prosecutors may no longer prosecute FFLs that sell handguns to 18- to 20-year-olds who are not otherwise prohibited from gun possession.[1] Congress enacted this prohibition as part of the Gun Control Act of 1968, clearly stating that “it shall be unlawful” for an FFL to sell or transfer a handgun to a person under age 21.[2] Nearly 60 years later, the Department’s decision to stop enforcing this provision comes not because Congress repealed or amended the law, but because the Executive Branch has independently concluded that these provisions are unconstitutional. This decision raises serious questions about the Department’s execution of federal law, its communications with members of the gun industry, and the implications for the enforcement of federal firearms laws nationwide.

The Department’s OLC opinion acknowledges the constitutionality of age-based firearms restrictions has “deeply divided members of the federal bench.” Given the ongoing nature of this legal dispute, the Department’s decision that it may cease enforcement of federal law by executive fiat, rather than continue defending and enforcing the statute, represents an expansive and concerning assertion of executive authority.

The public safety implications of this decision are clear. Numerous mass shootings have been committed by perpetrators between the ages of 18 and 20, including the shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, where an 18-year-old fatally shot 19 students and two teachers and injured 18 others, as well as the shootings at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York; an Indianapolis FedEx facility and Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. These tragic examples underscore the public safety considerations at stake and the serious risks Congress sought to address. The Department’s decision to unilaterally cease enforcement of this provision of law raises serious questions and concerns. Thus, we request the Department provide:

A detailed explanation of the legal authority on which the Department relies to stop criminal and civil enforcement of these provisions, despite their continued status as federal law;

All legal materials concerning the Department’s decision to stop enforcing 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and (c)(1) against federally licensed firearm dealers that sell handguns to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20;

Any analysis conducted or reviewed by the Department regarding the potential public-safety consequences of changing federal enforcement policy for handgun sales to individuals between the ages of 18 and 20; and

A list of all investigations, prosecutions, and civil or criminal enforcement actions affected by the Department’s decision, including any matters declined, suspended, dismissed, or otherwise modified, and the reasons for each action.

Please provide the requested information and documents by November 16, 2026.

title: Grassley, Hinson, Nunn Push to Bring More Medical Residency Positions to Iowa
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and U.S. Reps. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) and Zach Nunn (R-Iowa) are urging the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to award Iowa more federally-funded residency positions to help address the state’s doctor shortage.

In a letter to CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, the lawmakers shared their support for UnityPoint Health’s application for additional Medicare-funded graduate medical education (GME) residency positions for its emergency medicine residency program.

“This new emergency medicine residency program deserves additional federal support to strengthen rural emergency medical care and Iowa’s physician workforce needs. More doctors being trained in rural America is good for patients and our nation’s health care system,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers highlighted the program’s benefits beyond adult emergency medicine, including pediatric emergency care and hands-on experience.

“[T]he co-location of Blank Children’s Hospital in this program gives medical residents experience with pediatric emergency medicine. Residents have integrated themselves into the Des Moines and nearby communities by serving as on-call physicians at sporting and concert events. Residents even serve in local emergency medical service operations to get additional experience,” the lawmakers continued.

The lawmakers described how the program benefits small town Iowa. Residents gain clinical experience more than 50 miles from Des Moines at Grinnell Regional Medical Center in Poweshiek County, which has a population of fewer than 20,000 people. A majority of the new program’s first class of residents will continue practicing in rural areas or in Iowa communities after they complete their residency.

Full text of the letter can be found HERE.

Background:

While chairing the Senate Finance Committee, Grassley in 2020 worked to add 1,000 additional Medicare-funded GME residency positions nationwide to strengthen America’s healthcare workforce – particularly in rural and underserved communities. This was the largest increase in Medicare-funded residency positions in over 25 years. CMS has so far awarded Iowa over 14 permanent additional GME residency positions as a result of the Grassley-backed law.

In response to Grassley, CMS confirmed it intends to meet the 10% rural hospital distribution threshold in the overall distribution of 1,000 residency positions. Grassley highlighted the importance of distributing medical residency positions to rural areas during a May 2024 Finance Committee hearing, in a March 2025 Finance Committee nomination hearing and on the Senate floor in May 2025.

title: Grassley Leads Iowa Congressional Delegation in Push to Protect Iowa’s Pork Industry and Stabilize Consumer Prices Amid U.S.-Mexico Trade Negotiations
text:
Click HERE for audio of Grassley discussing the letter

BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – Iowa’s congressional delegation, led by U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), is urging the Trump administration to consider the impact of its decision to terminate a trade agreement with Mexico that has threatened Iowa’s pork industry and contributed to higher tomato prices for American consumers. The lawmakers are asking the Trump administration to keep Iowa pig farmers and consumers in mind as they negotiate further with Mexico.

U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) and U.S. Reps. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa), Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), Zach Nunn (R-Iowa) and Randy Feenstra (R-Iowa) joined Grassley in the letter to U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

In response to the termination of the United States-Mexico Tomato Suspension Agreement (TSA) in July 2025, Mexico’s International Commercial Practices Unit launched an antidumping investigation into the American pork industry in December 2025.

“Iowa is the number one pork producing state in the United States,” the lawmakers wrote. “[O]ver one million metric tons of [U.S.] pork is exported to Mexico annually, resulting in over $2.85 billion in [U.S. pork] exports [to Mexico] in 2025 alone. This figure has more than doubled in the past six years under the United States Mexico Canada Agreement (USMCA).”

The lawmakers praised efforts to protect producers under international trade agreements, citing the administration’s successful work in securing record-breaking ethanol exports, beef exports to Australia and diversified soybean export markets.

“The removal of the TSA, however, has led to negative outcomes for Iowans,” the lawmakers continued. “The looming threat of retaliation from our number one export market creates a chilling effect on the pork industry that already faces headwinds domestically due to state regulations like California’s Proposition 12.”

Since the termination of the agreement, tomato prices increased 6.8% from September 2025 to September 2026, nearly double the rate of overall inflation. Tomatoes are the second highest consumed vegetable product in the United States.

“As negotiations continue with Mexico, we ask that you consider the impacts of seasonality disputes previously addressed in the TSA on Iowa pig farmers and United States covered tomato producers. We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to continuing to work with you to strengthen American production and consumer prices through trade,” the lawmakers concluded.

The letter is supported by the National Pork Producers Council.

“We appreciate Senator Grassley and the Iowa delegation standing up for Iowa’s pork producers and recognizing the serious trade risks they now face. Mexico is the largest export market for U.S. pork, and the antidumping investigation currently underway creates real uncertainty for producers who depend on that critical market. We welcome the delegation’s leadership in urging the administration to protect American pork producers as it works with Mexico to resolve these trade issues and preserve our industry’s strong, stable trading relationship,” said Rob Brenneman, National Pork Producers Council President and Washington County pork producer.

In September, Grassley and Ernst joined every Republican member of the U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee to advance the Farm Bill to the Senate floor. Every Democrat on the committee voted against the Farm Bill.

title: Grassley, Shaheen, Colleagues Issue Bipartisan Statement Ahead of Serbian Parliamentary Elections
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) joined U.S. Sens. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) and Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) in releasing a bipartisan statement ahead of Serbia’s upcoming parliamentary elections on October 25, 2026, calling for Serbian authorities to ensure the elections are free and fair.

“As Serbians prepare to go to the polls on October 25, we stand for their right to make their voices heard in free and fair conditions and urge all parties to respect the vote count and relevant processes for verifying electoral results. The United States has long supported Serbia’s path to Euro-Atlantic integration and has acknowledged its potential to promote stability in the Western Balkans. Robust democracy in Serbia is essential for each of those goals.

“Unfortunately, both Serbian and international election observers found serious infringements to the integrity of the previous parliamentary elections in 2022. We are now seeing similarly troubling signs ahead of the October 25 vote. Reports of unlawful wiretapping of opposition members and attempts to discredit and undermine election observation missions are deeply concerning, and Serbian authorities must ensure a level playing field for all parties and open access to the polls for all citizens.

“We urge the ruling party and all relevant institutions to ensure the peaceful, free and open conduct of the upcoming vote. We reaffirm the vital role that international and domestic observers play in safeguarding trust in the electoral process. The onus is on Serbian authorities to ensure that all institutions respect the role of citizen observers, journalists and candidates for office.”

Background:

The senators’ statement comes as independent election monitors are raising concerns that the upcoming elections will take place in a hostile environment for civil society, observers and opposition parties. According to Serbia’s independent, non-partisan Center for Research, Transparency and Accountability (CRTA) and the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe’s Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights, the campaign period has seen several instances of voter intimidation, abuse of administrative resources to benefit the ruling party and intimidation of opposition candidates by police. The CRTA noted that this campaign is “unlike any electoral process [it] has observed before” and identified cases of wiretapping of opposition candidates. These concerns are similar to shortcomings that were raised after the 2022 elections, which have still not been addressed by the ruling party.

title: Senator Hassan Highlights Efforts to Support Granite Staters in Recovery, Lower Housing Costs
text:
NEW HAMPSHIRE – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan toured new housing developments in Manchester and Rochester to highlight efforts to lower housing costs and support Granite Staters in recovery.

In Manchester, Senator Hassan joined Revive Recovery for a ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the opening of The Hive, a new recovery residence and resource center for women overcoming addiction. The Hive’s programming will include daily structure to aid in routine building, connections to outside supports like outpatient treatment or meetings, and a focus on rebuilding stability through housing, employment, emotional regulation and other skills.

“When you are in recovery, when you are making critical transitions, it is so important to have a safe place to call home,”Senator Hassan said. title: Hoeven Statement on $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program
text:
BISMARCK, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today issued the following statement after the Trump administration announced an $8 billion program to help farmers cover increased input costs during harvest season. The Harvest Fuel Relief program is funded through the Commodity Credit Corporation (CCC) and will provide assistance in a manner similar to the Farmer Bridge Assistance (FBA) program that Hoeven worked to advance. Under the program, the Farm Service Agency (FSA) will:

Provide a one-time payment to producers for losses during the 2026 crop year using a formula based on:

FSA reported planted acres.

Economic Research Service cost of production estimates.

World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates yields and prices.

Release commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities in November.

Payment information for additional eligible commodities will be released at a later date.

Producers of non-Title I commodities, including specialty crop growers and fishermen, are encouraged to provide data related to increased fuel costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov to help the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) determine payment rates.

Provide an online pre-filled application to eligible producers with a Login.gov account that is linked to USDA.

Pre-filled applications will be made available in advance of the application period announcement.

“Between the newly-announced Harvest Fuel Relief Program and the enhancements we made to ARC and PLC, which went into effect this month, producers are receiving meaningful assistance to help them cover their increased input costs during harvest,” said Hoeven. “We appreciate President Trump and Secretary Rollins for continuing to work with us to keep our farmers afloat during these challenging times. We will continue our efforts to pass a Farm Bill that further strengthens our farm safety net, secure better market access for producers and unleash American energy production to bring down input costs, including diesel and fertilizer prices.”

title: Kelly, Colleagues Demand Answers from EPA over Changes Threatening Clean Air at Grand Canyon, National Parks
text:
Senators raised concerns that changes to federal air pollution protections could threaten Arizona’s public lands, tourism, and local economies

This week, Arizona Senator Mark Kelly led his colleagues in demanding answers from Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin over recent changes to the Regional Haze Program that could weaken protections against air pollution at the Grand Canyon and national parks across the country.

In their letter, the senators raised concerns that the EPA is allowing states to avoid new pollution reductions and considering additional changes to the program, which was established to protect visibility at national parks and wilderness areas. The senators warned that weakening these protections could threaten public health, obscure iconic landscapes, and hurt local economies that depend on tourism.

The senators highlighted the importance of protecting clean air and visibility at national parks: “Preserving the iconic views of these treasured parks and wilderness areas is why Congress established the Regional Haze Program nearly fifty years ago, recognizing that some landscapes are simply too important to allow pollution to obscure. Yet today, 98 percent of national parks suffer from hazy skies, reducing visibility by an average of 50 miles.”

The senators emphasized that reducing haze-forming pollution also protects public health and local economies: “Haze is more than a visibility problem. The same fine particle pollution that obscures views at national parks across the country also poses great harm to public health. Fine particulate matter, including particles formed from sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides emissions, have been linked to asthma, decreased lung function, heart problems, and premature death in people with existing conditions. Reducing haze-forming pollution helps protect not only the views that draw millions of visitors to our national parks, but also the health of those visitors and nearby communities.”

The senators called on EPA to uphold the Clean Air Act and continue making progress toward restoring visibility at national parks: “Congress established the Regional Haze Rule to ensure that future generations can experience places like the Grand Canyon, Yosemite, Yellowstone, Shenandoah, Rocky Mountain, Crater Lake, and other national parks and wilderness areas as they were meant to be seen. It is important that changes to the program remain consistent with the Clean Air Act and continue making meaningful progress toward that goal.”

“Our national parks are priceless treasures, offering breathtaking views and unmatched experiences that inspire millions. For nearly thirty years, the Regional Haze Rule has safeguarded iconic landscapes while protecting the air our communities breathe. Any attempt to weaken protections is a direct threat to public health and decades of progress towards cleaner air. The EPA must strengthen protections, not undermine clean air for big industry’s gain. NPCA commends Senator Kelly’s leadership, alongside many other clean air congressional champions, for defending clean air for our national parks and people,” said Ulla Reeves, Director of the Clean Air Program at the National Parks Conservation Association.

Kelly was joined by Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Edward Markey (D-MA), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Jeffrey Merkley (D-OR), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Charles Schumer (D-NY), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Michael Bennet (D-CO).

title: Kelly Statement on Chiricahua Officially Becoming Arizona’s Fourth National Park
text:
Today, Arizona Senator Mark Kelly released the following statement after the Chiricahua National Park Act, legislation he first introduced in 2021 to designate Chiricahua National Monument in Cochise County as Arizona’s fourth national park, was signed into law by President Trump:

“Today is a historic day for Arizona. Making Chiricahua a national park has been a priority of mine since I first came to the Senate, so I’m thrilled this day has finally arrived,” said Kelly. “A bipartisan effort from the start, this is a win for the communities in southeastern Arizona and for everyone who worked to protect this extraordinary place so our kids and our grandkids can enjoy it.”

Background:

Kelly first introduced legislation to make Chiricahua Arizona’s fourth national park in 2021 and continued pushing for the designation in subsequent Congresses. Kelly and Senator Ruben Gallego introduced the latest Senate legislation, while Representatives Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-06) and Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04) advanced the legislation in the House. The House passed the bill in March, followed by the Senate in September.

Established in 1924, Chiricahua National Monument spans more than 12,000 acres of towering rock formations, canyons, and diverse wildlife in Cochise County. The designation will protect Chiricahua’s unique landscape for future generations while bringing more visitors and economic opportunities to southeastern Arizona. The law also includes protections for traditional cultural and religious sites and ensures continued access for Tribal members for traditional cultural and customary uses.

See what Arizona leaders are saying about Chiricahua becoming the state’s fourth National Park:

“This is a moment worth celebrating, not only because Chiricahua is now Arizona’s fourth national park, but also because of how we got here. We are grateful to Senator Mark Kelly for his leadership in advancing this effort alongside Senator Ruben Gallego and Representatives Juan Ciscomani and Greg Stanton. Their bipartisan collaboration helped give Chiricahua the national recognition it deserves for its ecological, cultural, recreational, and economic significance. At a time when our country feels deeply divided, this achievement shows what is possible when we put differences aside and work together to protect the public lands we all share,” said Camilla Simon, Executive Director of HECHO.

“I proudly supported the Chiricahua National Park Act, and I’m thrilled to have been part of the effort to make Chiricahua Arizona’s newest national park. As a combat veteran, I know firsthand the healing that can come from spending time on our public lands. A national park in my own backyard has given me a place to find that healing, and I’m excited for more people to have that opportunity at Chiricahua. This designation will bring so much to the surrounding communities, not only economic and recreational opportunities, but also the joy, connection and healing that these special places can provide,” said Eduardo Ramos, veteran, hunter and HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council.

“Chiricahua is one of those places you have to see with your own eyes to truly understand. Its landscape is breathtaking, and no matter how many times I visit, that feeling never changes. I had the privilege of being in Washington, D.C., advocating for Chiricahua when we learned that the bill had passed Congress, and being there for that moment was incredibly special. Now, to see what we advocated for become a reality with the President’s signature is something I’ll never forget. I’m proud that more people will have the opportunity to experience this extraordinary place,” said Eddy Corona, President of Outdoor Experience 4 All and member of HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council.

“The Chiricahuas in southeastern Arizona are a true hidden gem. Having hiked and camped there in the past, I can attest to its spectacular rock formations, incredible biodiversity, endless night skies, and abundant wildlife. This designation will boost the local economy and encourage more visitors to experience this unique landscape,” said Patty Contreras, Arizona State Representative and member of HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council.

“I’ve explored the outdoors throughout Arizona, but the Chiricahuas hold a particularly special place in my heart. I feel a deep spiritual connection to this landscape unlike anywhere else in the state. From the incredible rock formations to the abundance of wildlife, the Chiricahuas are truly one of a kind. It’s one of the few places in Arizona where I’ve been fortunate enough to encounter such a remarkable diversity of wildlife. It’s one of Arizona’s best-kept secrets, and I hope it never loses the qualities that make it so special. I’m excited about this step forward and hopeful that National Park designation will bring greater resources, and lasting protections to this extraordinary place,” said Adriana Garcia Maximiliano, Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council member.

“The first time I visited Chiricahua with my family, I was struck by its extraordinary beauty, rich history, and the deep significance it holds for so many Tribal communities. If I had to describe it in one word, it would be magical. As someone who has seen firsthand the benefits of having a national park near our community, I know how meaningful this designation could be for southern Arizona. It will create opportunities for local businesses, bring new tourism revenue, and strengthen the Southwest as a destination for people who come to experience our incredible public lands. But beyond the economic benefits, this is about reaffirming our commitment to conserving these special places for generations to come. National parks allow us to build a stronger economic future for our communities without sacrificing the landscapes, wildlife, and history that make them so extraordinary,” said Sarah Benatar, Coconino County Treasurer.

title: Kennedy discusses Acadiana’s economic growth with Oil Center Association, One Acadiana

title: Senator Marshall Applauds Trump Administration’s $8 Billion in Relief for Farmers Facing High Diesel Costs
text:
Wichita – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), applauded President Trump’s announcement of $8 billion in relief for American farmers through the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s new Harvest Fuel Relief Program. The announcement follows Senator Marshall’s September letter to USDA Secretary Rollins urging the Trump Administration to provide temporary, targeted relief for farmers and ranchers facing soaring diesel costs during the 2026 harvest season.

“To every Kansas farmer who kept harvesting through soaring diesel costs: help is on the way. After hearing directly from Kansas farmers about the strain these rising diesel costs were putting on their operations, we brought these concerns directly to President Trump and Secretary Rollins, urging them to provide relief,” said Senator Marshall.“This $8 billion in support is headed to the men and women who feed and fuel this country. Thank you, President Trump, for standing with our farmers, and thank you to our Kansas farmers for never quitting.”

In his September letter, Senator Marshall urged USDA to help farmers manage soaring diesel costs during the 2026 harvest, when fuel expenses were putting additional pressure on agricultural operations.

The Harvest Fuel Relief program will provide $8 billion in one-time payments to American farmers to help offset a portion of modeled losses during the 2026 crop year amid market disruptions and rising input costs. USDA will use a uniform formula based on planted acres, production costs, and crop yields and prices to determine support, with commodity-specific payment rates expected in November.

Senator Marshall thanked President Trump and Secretary Rollins for recognizing the challenges facing America’s agricultural producers and taking steps to help ensure Kansas farmers can continue doing what they do best – feeding and fueling our nation.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Protect Floridians Online
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody is working to protect Floridians online, including taking action to guard children from online predators as well as targeting cyber scammers looking to steal from seniors. In recognition of National Cybersecurity Month, Senator Moody is highlighting legislative efforts on behalf of Floridians.

“It’s National Cybersecurity Month, and I’m reminding Floridians that criminals don’t have to break into your home to steal from you—they can target you through a call, email or even a text. As U.S. Senator, I’m working to protect Floridians from online bad actors—including scammers, fraudsters, and child predators,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Moody is championing the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act, an effort she has been supportive of since she was Florida’s Attorney General. KOSA provides young people and parents with the tools, safeguards, and transparency they need to protect against online harms.

Senator Moody recently introduced the STOP Scams Against Seniors Act to help law enforcement investigate and prosecute criminals who target seniors through scams and financial fraud. Seniors are often the target of cyber scammers.

Senator Moody is an original cosponsor of the No FAKES Act, legislation to protect Americans from having their voice and image stolen and used in unauthorized AI generated digital replicas or deepfakes. Senator Moody passed the No FAKES Act out of the Senate Judiciary Committee in June.

Senator Moody introduced the SWIPES Act to give law enforcement stronger tools to prosecute gift card fraud, close loopholes criminals exploit and impose tougher penalties on those who knowingly target seniors. Gift card fraud occurs in many forms. Fraudsters are also known to set up fake websites that appear like legitimate sites consumers use to check gift card balances, and when a victim inputs the card’s information, the fraudsters can steal the funds.

As Florida Attorney General, Senator Moody created the Cyber Fraud Enforcement Unit in 2023. During Moody’s time as Attorney General, the unit froze more than $17 million in illicit funds tied to cryptocurrency scams, with 40 active crypto seizure cases involving senior citizen victims.

title: Warnock, Ossoff Secure Nearly $12.5 Million to Improve Rail Safety Across Southwest Georgia
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff successfully secured nearly $12.5 million in federal grant funding from the Department of Transportation to improve railway safety in Southwest Georgia

The funding will help rehabilitate rail lines, improve 40 railroad crossings, install measures to prevent trespassing, and improve safety and reliability

The funding will support improvement projects in Dawson, Cuthbert, Arlington, Bainbridge, Cordele, and Americus

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) secured $12,495,000 in federal funding to improve rail safety and infrastructure across central and southwestern Georgia. The funding, provided through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, will help rehabilitate rail lines, improve rail service, and increase reliability as part of the Heart of Georgia & Georgia Southwestern Rail Corridor Improvement Final Phase Project.

“Since coming to the Senate, I have been focused on strengthening rail safety and infrastructure in Georgia. That is why I am proud to champion efforts in the Senate to strengthen the CRISI program to deliver more resources to our state,” said Senator Warnock. “This latest grant will help reduce congestion, build new tracks, and strengthen existing rail infrastructure, making it safer, easier, and more efficient to move goods across our state.”

“After hearing from communities statewide about aging railroad infrastructure conditions, Senator Warnock and I elevated this as one of our highest priorities,” said Senator Ossoff. “We are delivering these resources through the bipartisan infrastructure law to communities across the State of Georgia to plan and begin construction to address this crisis. We’ve listened, we’ve heard, we’ve acted, and help is on the way.”

The Project will rehabilitate and improve five short line subdivisions across central and southwestern Georgia, including rail corridors serving Dawson, Cuthbert, Arlington, Bainbridge, Cordele, and Americus. Improvements will include replacing jointed rail with continuous welded rail, installing new ties, surfacing track, resurfacing 40 railroad crossings, renewing two turnouts, and installing trespasser prevention technology.

In 2024, Senators Warnock and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) secured more than $60 million in CRISI funding to strengthen railroad safety across Georgia, including funding for the Georgia Department of Transportation, Georgia Ports Authority, Patriot Rail Company, and OmniTRAX Holdings.

title: Ranking Members Padilla, Morelle Condemn the Department of Justice for Meddling in California’s Elections
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, and Ranking Member Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.-25), the top Democrat on the Committee on House Administration, sent a joint oversight letter to Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter after the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) sued California’s Secretary of State and Los Angeles County’s Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk with no legal basis or evidence in an attempt to prevent them from calculating ballots sent to a list of allegedly “likely” ineligible voters and threatened election officials with criminal prosecution.

Similar claims of lists from the Trump Administration supposedly identifying ineligible voters have proven overstated or false in the past, and they have included many eligible American voters. Both Padilla and Morelle’s committees have jurisdiction over federal elections in the Senate and House, respectively.

“The Department must serve the interests of Americans, not operate at the personal and political direction of the president or to advance the partisan interests of a political party,” the lawmakers wrote.

The DOJ itself has admitted that alleged noncitizen lists fabricated by the Trump Administration are unreliable. And while the DOJ’s allegations are entirely speculative, they create unnecessary burdens on California in the middle of an ongoing election that would force California officials to violate federal law. The DOJ’s intent is clear – undermine public confidence in the outcome of California’s elections to further President Trump’s baseless feud with a state that has rejected him three times.

“This is the second time in less than four months that the Department has responded to the President’s public demands to interfere in an ongoing election in California, and it is a blatant misuse of the Department’s resources and abuse of the Department’s authority… The Department’s attempt to disenfranchise thousands of American voters en masse, based on no evidence of any individual’s ineligibility, is a clear violation of Californians’ federal constitutional right to vote. The right to vote, of course, is also enshrined in the Constitution of California,” the lawmakers continued.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee and California’s former Secretary of State and chief election officer, Padilla has fought relentlessly to protect our elections and strengthen voting rights.

Last week, Padilla demanded that DOJ commit to not seize ballots or voting equipment during the midterm elections.

Last month, Padilla introduced the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act, legislation to protect voters and election workers from intimidation and threats of violence at polling places.

Padilla also led the congressional response to the bombshell whistleblower report that DHS agents violated state laws as part of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” and called for an immediate investigation into the agency’s misconduct, which has likely led to the creation of dubious lists of supposedly ineligible voters. He also urged California’s Attorney General to investigate the effects these actions could have on Californians.

Also last month, Padilla convened some of the country’s top labor leaders to discuss how to strengthen our democracy and mobilize against election interference.

In August, he led 27 of his Senate colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop its illegal voter roll purges before Election Day.

Padilla also joined Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) in launching the first-ever Senate Election Observer Program to protect the 2026 midterms and maintain election integrity nationwide and serves as part of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force. This week, Padilla announced that more than 100 Senate Democratic staff have been recruited and trained as official congressional election observers to be deployed to polling sites across nine states.

In June, Padilla joined his colleagues in introducing the Protect Our Polls Act to protect the integrity of American elections from federal interference by armed military or federal law enforcement.

Full letter is available here or below:

R. Trent McCotter

Acting Deputy Attorney General

United States Department of Justice

950 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW

Washington, D.C. 20530

Dear Acting Deputy Attorney General McCotter:

Your October 13, 2026, letters to California Secretary of State Dr. Shirley Weber (the “Letters”) and Dean Logan, Los Angeles County Registrar-Record/County Clerk, the Department of Justice’s (the “Department”) related October 15, 2026, complaint (the “Complaint”), and its October 16, 2026, letter to the Los Angeles County Counsel’s Office raise serious and unprecedented questions about political weaponization at the Department during an ongoing federal election.

The Department’s lawsuit and subsequent threat to use federal criminal law to interfere with the mailing and counting of ballots in California rests the on highly suspect legal and intellectual bases and raises questions about the standards of professional responsibility to which the Department should hold its attorneys. The Department must serve the interests of Americans, not operate at the personal and political direction of the president or to advance the partisan interests of a political party. In this instance, it appears that the Department has betrayed its historical duty “to enforce the laws of the United States . . . in a neutral and impartial manner.” As such, we require information from you related to the Department’s decision-making in this matter.

The Complaint’s claim “that California will count vote-by-mail ballots of likely noncitizen voters” bears no basis in fact—the Department makes no effort to present any evidence that any individuals included on the Trump Administration’s list of alleged noncitizens are ineligible to vote. Nor does the Department explain with any specificity why it doubts that California will fail to manage its voter rolls properly. Indeed, similar claims from the Trump Administration have proven dismally false in the past. For example, the Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”) made an outlandish and unsubstantiated claim that it had discovered 16,000 noncitizens on Nevada voter rolls—a claim that Nevada officials later determined was flatly incorrect; every person identified by DHS was a lawful United States citizen. In fact, the Department itself has admitted that alleged noncitizenship lists manufactured by the Trump Administration are unreliable.

But while the allegations underlying the Letters and the Complaint are entirely conjectural, the relief demanded would impose real and onerous burdens on California in the midst of an ongoing election. And the Department’s design here is clear—undermining public confidence in the outcome of California elections to further President Trump’s longstanding but baseless vendetta against a state that has, on three occasions, voted for the Democratic presidential nominee. This is the second time in less than four months that the Department has responded to the President’s public demands to interfere in an ongoing election in California, and it is a blatant misuse of the Department’s resources and abuse of the Department’s authority.

Glaring partisan motivation is not the only fatal flaw in the Department’s machinations. The Complaint plainly demands that California violate state and federal law. The Department’s attempt to disenfranchise thousands of American voters en masse, based on no evidence of any individual’s ineligibility, is a clear violation of Californians’ federal constitutional right to vote. The right to vote, of course, is also enshrined in the Constitution of California. In addition, the Department’s own guidance for compliance with the National Voter Registration Act (“NVRA”) states: “list maintenance activities that may violate the NVRA include comparing voter files to outdated or inaccurate records or databases, taking action that erroneously affects a particular class of voters (such as newly naturalized citizens).”

While you falsely accuse California and Los Angeles County officials of criminal violations, the Department’s demands here would violate federal statute: “No person acting under color of law shall fail or refuse to permit any person to vote who is entitled to vote . . . or willfully fail or refuse to tabulate, count, and report such person’s vote.” The Complaint’s baffling claim that California “knows that noncitizens might be registered to vote, and it knows the names of such individuals,” but that the state “still intends to count their vote without verifying the voter’s citizenship,” is, simply, fiction. Despite the Department’s attacks regarding “unverified statements of citizenship necessary to registering,” the truth is that voters in California make an attestation of citizenship under penalty of perjury to register to vote— similar to the vast majority of states and as set forth in federal law.

The Department is apparently seeking to create the disastrous and foreseeable outcome that tens of thousands of Americans—people who have already received and potentially cast ballots—could see their votes cast aside based on innuendo and defective data. The Department’s unprecedented demand that California arbitrarily segregate ballots and ignore the state’s legal responsibility to process and tabulate the ballots cast by eligible American voters runs afoul of the Constitution and the rule of law.

Further, the Department simply has no legal or constitutional authority to make such a demand on California. The Complaint woefully misstates—or simply misunderstands—the theory of federal preemption. The Department’s extreme demand that a federal court “[d]eclare that California’s actions here . . . are preempted and thus violate the Supremacy Clause,” would effectively abrogate the states’ clear and specific constitutional duty to regulate the time, place, and manner of elections in our Republic. The claims in the Letters and Complaint lack any basis in fact and the Department lacks any basis in legal authority.

Finally, the recent behavior of the Department in this and other matters raise serious concerns about the professional integrity and ethical responsibility expected of attorneys by the Department’s leadership. Federal law requires that attorneys at the Department comply with the professional responsibility rules of the states in which they practice. First, the Department of Justice Manual includes an election noninterference policy which states that the Department: “should generally avoid interfering or appearing to interfere with election administration, tabulation, validation, or certification.” Perhaps Americans should not be surprised that the Department is failing to adhere to its own standards when one of the key Department officials involved in threatening California election officials has reportedly stated “f[**]k the Justice Manual” in the context of another politically-motivated attempted criminal prosecution.

In addition, the Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of California, for example, make clear that it is professional misconduct for a lawyer to “engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or reckless or intentional misrepresentation,” or “engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.” The District of Columbia Bar holds its attorneys to almost identical standards. And as a recent opinion of the American Bar Association makes clear:

all lawyers, including government lawyers, have a responsibility to abide by the professional conduct rules applicable to their own conduct . . . and, if the direction provided by the supervisor is “a reasonable resolution of an arguable question of professional duty,” the subordinate may defer to it even if the subordinate would decide the issue differently. However, unless the superior’s direction meets that standard, following orders is no excuse and the subordinate lawyer is responsible for the lawyer’s own conduct.

In both the Letters and the Complaint, the Department’s stated motivations are spurious; they poorly conceal an unmistakable—and unethical—improper partisan motivation that comes through even more clearly in Department officials’ social media posts. Both the October 13 letter and the Complaint misrepresent the law and overstate the Department’s authority. And, in both the Letters and the Complaint, the Department attempts to subvert a free and fair American election. Any Department staff engaged in this effort should be wary as lapses in an attorney’s professional responsibilities have far-reaching, and expensive, repercussions.

In order to safeguard American elections, Congress must determine whether additional legislation is necessary to address the brazen misuse of the Department’s law enforcement powers for partisan purposes—in California or in any other state or jurisdiction in which the Department is considering, or may consider in the future, similar illegal action. Accordingly, in exercise of Congress’s oversight and legislative authority, we request that you provide the following information and materials no later than 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026:

Did the White House direct any aspects of the decision-making related to the Letters or the Complaint, or was the White House aware of or involved in any other way in developing and implementing the steps leading to and including the lawsuit against California?

How, and on what basis, did DHS or the Department identify the names provided to California?

Who was involved in the process by which these names were identified?

Did private parties provide any of the data that DHS or the Department delivered to California? If so, how much?

Why did the Department wait until now, weeks before the election, to first threaten California through the Letters and file the Complaint if, as the Department alleges, this data was assembled months ago?

Who was involved in the decision to send the October 13, 2026, letter to California and subsequently to file the Complaint?

For purposes of robust congressional oversight, please identify the specific senior advisory personnel who were responsible, including any who may have relevant information about the process.

Please also specifically identify every Department, other administration agency, or private party lawyer, who worked on the October 13, 2026, letter, the October 16, 2026, letter, or Complaint.

Did the Department consult private parties, or did such parties advise, upon the “legal theory” advanced in the Complaint against California?

What, precisely, does the Department mean when it refers to “thousands of likely noncitizens registered to vote in California”?

What threshold of “likelihood” did the DHS or the Department establish (especially considering the previous, and extensively erroneous, citizenship identification lists the Trump Administration has produced for other states)?

Please provide the complete matching methodology and criteria used to build the supposed list of noncitizens registered in the state of California. Identify every official who validated the list before it was given to a local election office.

Did any DHS personnel misrepresent themselves as California voters when attempting to access California voter data as part of the process to identify these names?

Federal law bars systematic voter purges within 90 days of a federal election. California mailed ballots on October 5, and the Department filed its complaint 19 days before Election Day. Did the Department’s lawyers produce any analysis of whether its request violates federal law? Please either produce said analysis or confirm none was conducted.

Did Department leadership or any individual involved in drafting the Letters or the Complaint consult the Department’s Office of Professional Responsibility or Department ethics counsel regarding the clear ethical and policy questions presented by the Department’s unprecedented constitutional claim to threaten, and then file suit against, a state within weeks of the November elections?

If so, what advice was received?

If no consultation took place, explain why.

Did DHS and the Department follow established agency cybersecurity practices in the creation, and transmittal, of the thumb drive delivered to Los Angeles Couty?

If so, please delineate the precise guidelines DHS and the Department followed.

If not, please explain why the Trump Administration chose to jeopardize both the private personal information of thousands of American citizens and the election infrastructure of Los Angeles County.

Who approved this method of delivery of sensitive voter data?

As Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration and a member of the House Appropriations subcommittee with oversight of the Department, and Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, who represents the State of California, we look forward to your prompt transmittal of the above requested information.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Alex Padilla — United States Senator, Ranking Member, Committee on Rules and Administration

Joseph D. Morelle — Member of Congress, Ranking Member, Committee on House Administration

title: Schatz Bill Targeting Illegal Fishing To Help Expose Foreign, Intentionally Mislabeled Ahi Signed Into Law
text:
WASHINGTON – The Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act, bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Brian Schatz (D-Hawai‘i) and Ted Cruz (R-Texas), was signed into law by President Trump. The bill directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of red snapper and certain species of tuna imported into the United States.

“Our new law will give law enforcement a powerful new tool to detect where ahi comes from, help prevent seafood fraud, and give consumers better, more accurate information on what they’re buying and eating,” said Senator Schatz.

Technology exists to chemically test and find the geographic origin of many foods, but not for tuna and red snapper. The new law will help to develop a field test kit that can be used to accurately ascertain whether fish were caught in U.S. or foreign waters, thus allowing federal and state law enforcement officers to identify the origin of the fish and intercept illegally caught or falsely labelled red snapper and tuna before it enters the U.S. market.

title: ICYMI: Sen. Schiff Tours CBP Facility at San Francisco International Airport in Oversight Visit Seeking Answers on Rights and Treatment of Detainees
text:
San Francisco, CA – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, conducted an oversight visit of the Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) facility at San Francisco International Airport (SFO) to learn firsthand about the facility’s conditions amid reports that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has been using it as a holding area to detain immigrants, including lawful permanent residents, for several days before transferring them to ICE facilities.

What was their access to medical treatment, and how do we determine whether they’re getting what they need? And finally, what was their access to counsel? People are at the whim of what CBP is doing, and they have no recourse, and families are terrified. We got some answers today, but I remain concerned about the practices at this facility. I’ll continue conducting oversight of the administration’s unlawful immigration policies,”said Senator Schiff about his visit.
