title: Amo Meets with Future Marine Trades Workforce and Blue Economy Leaders, Releases Blue Economy Report
text:
Providence, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) continued his 2026 Blue Economy Tour with visits to North Providence High School’s Marine Trades Program and Polaris MEP’s Manufacturing Day, highlighting the future of Rhode Island’s marine trades and manufacturing workforce. Following the stops, Amo led a roundtable with local environmental, labor, fishery, education, and business leaders to discuss the future of Rhode Island’s maritime economy and released his 2026 Blue Economy Report.

“Rhode Island’s Blue Economy is rooted in our maritime heritage and powered by the workers, students, and innovators building what comes next,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “This year's tour of our Blue Economy is highlighting exciting opportunities to grow good-paying jobs, strengthen our marine industries, and protect the waters that sustain us. I’ll bring these ideas back to Washington and keep fighting for the investment and support Rhode Island needs to lead the way.”

The full 2026 Blue Economy Report can be found here.

“RI’s Future in the Making gives students the opportunity to see firsthand what a career in modern manufacturing can look like. By connecting them with local manufacturers and letting them experience the technology, creativity and problem-solving that drive the industry, we can open their eyes to career paths they may never have considered. Investing in these experiences today helps build the skilled workforce Rhode Island manufacturers will need to grow and succeed in the years ahead,” said Matt Watson, Center Director of Polaris MEP.

“The Marine Trades pathway at North Providence High School is a perfect example of what our community believes CTE should encompass—students learning by doing, developing real-world skills, and seeing a direct connection between their education and future careers,” said Melissa Caffrey, Director of Pathways for the North Providence School District. “Our students are not simply learning about boatbuilding, composites, systems, and marine technology; they are working alongside industry partners, earning credentials, building confidence, and discovering opportunities they may never have considered before being an active participant in this program of study. What makes this program especially exciting is the collaboration between our school, the marine trades industry, and our community. We are preparing students for high-skill careers while showing them that their future can begin right here in North Providence.”

Background

Congressman Amo’s 2026 Blue Economy Tour has highlighted the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy. Amo visited REGENT Craft, where he helped cut the ribbon on their new electric Seaglider factory. Next, Congressman Amo visited Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities to explore advances in shellfish production, aquaculture, and blue biotechnology. Amo toured Hinckley Yachts’ Portsmouth facility to discuss the skilled trades and maritime jobs that keep Rhode Island moving. Later, Congressman Amo visited Solid State Power to highlight the importance of new battery technology to maritime innovation.

Rhode Island’s Blue Economy directly employs 36,000 Rhode Islanders and contributes over $5 billion to the state’s gross domestic product every year.

In 2024, Congressman Amo toured Rhode Island’s First Congressional District to highlight the Ocean State’s leadership in the Blue Economy across labor, education, business, and defense.

title: Bacon Announces More Than $82 Million in HHS Grant Funding for UNMC
text:
Funding Supports 151 Awards and Actions Across Biomedical Research, Cancer, Infectious Disease and Other Health Priorities

Washington, D.C. – Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02) announced today that the University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC) has received notification of 151 grant awards and funding actions from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services totaling $82,459,790 so far in 2026.

The announcement follows an appreciation breakfast hosted last week by UNMC and University of Nebraska System leaders to recognize Bacon's support for the university throughout his tenure in Congress. UNMC Chancellor H. Dele Davies, MD, praised Bacon's longstanding partnership with the university, while other leaders highlighted his support for infectious disease preparedness, military medicine and federal research partnerships.

The funding includes approximately $23.8 million for newly awarded projects and approximately $58.6 million in renewed, continued, extended and supplemental support for ongoing research and health programs.

“UNMC has earned its reputation as one of the nation’s premier medical research, infectious disease and biocontainment institutions,” said Rep. Bacon. “From pioneering cancer treatments and organ transplants to responding to Ebola, COVID and other public health threats, the team and leadership at UNMC have repeatedly proven they are among the very best in the world. Most recently, UNMC and Nebraska Medicine safely monitored 18 Americans exposed to a rare hantavirus strain, concluding the operation with zero confirmed cases. This more than $82 million investment will strengthen groundbreaking work in cancer, infectious disease, neuroscience, behavioral health and other critical areas, expand our public health capabilities and help prepare the next generation of health professionals. Nebraska is grateful to be home to this powerhouse of research and health care excellence, and we will continue working to ensure UNMC has the support needed to remain a national leader and improve lives in Nebraska and across the country.”

“The hard work of our faculty, staff and students has paid off with strong growth in almost every aspect of our research enterprise,” said Ken Bayles, PhD, UNMC Vice Chancellor for Research. “This growth is a testament to UNMC’s efforts to conduct research that leads to new life-saving cures, diagnostic tools, and treatment strategies – all of which help people in Nebraska and beyond. We appreciate Rep. Don Bacon, Sen. Deb Fischer, and the Nebraska federal delegation’s support of UNMC -- it is now up to us to deliver.”

The awards and funding actions are broadly divided into the following areas:

• $23,568,436 for biomedical science, research infrastructure and technology, including general biomedical research and training, research infrastructure, environmental health research, pharmacology and physiology, cross-NIH research support and medical technology development.

• $21,174,867 for clinical care, public health, workforce and community programs, including nursing, cardiovascular and lung disease, child health, vision, musculoskeletal and health-disparities research, as well as workforce training, maternal health, HIV/AIDS, public health preparedness, injury prevention and community health programs.

• $17,192,799 for brain, aging and behavioral health research, including neuroscience, neurological disorders, aging, mental health, drug-use and addiction research and alcohol research.

• $13,858,224 for cancer research, including cancer treatment, biology, prevention, detection and diagnosis.

• $6,665,464 for infectious disease and immunology research, including infectious disease, allergy, immunology and transplantation research.

New awards provide funding for newly selected projects or programs. Continued and renewed awards provide additional years of support for existing multiyear projects, including grants that have undergone competitive renewal. Extensions and supplemental awards provide additional time, resources or funding for previously approved programs.

The funding was awarded through agencies within HHS, including the National Institutes of Health, the Health Resources and Services Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Photos and additional information about the appreciation breakfast are available through UNMC's coverage of the event.

title: Congressman Thompson Joins Mississippi Delegation in Celebrating Vicksburg National Military Park Bill Signing
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02) joined members of the Mississippi Congressional Delegation in celebrating the signing of the Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act into law. The legislation, introduced by Congressman Thompson in the U.S. House of Representatives, allows the State of Mississippi to move forward with plans for a new visitor center and related improvements at Vicksburg National Military Park.

The House approved the legislation on March 16, 2026, followed by unanimous Senate passage. The new law makes a limited adjustment to the park’s boundaries, allowing the state to develop an interactive educational and visitor center and construct a connector road to improve access for visitors.

“Vicksburg National Military Park tells an important part of Mississippi’s story,” said Congressman Thompson. “This legislation will help ensure that future generations have the opportunity to learn about the Siege of Vicksburg, the impact of the Civil War on the people of this region, and the role of United States Colored Troops in the campaign.”

The State of Mississippi has committed $40 million toward the development of the new visitor center in partnership with Friends of Vicksburg National Military Park. The project is expected to expand educational opportunities, improve the visitor experience, and support tourism and economic activity in the region.

title: REP. BOEBERT ANNOUNCES INTENT TO CODIFY UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE FORT COLLINS/CSU REGIONAL HUB RELOCATION IN FY2027 AGRICULTURE APPROPRIATIONS BILL
text:
Lone Tree, CO — Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04) sent a letter to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, House leadership, and Appropriations leadership announcing her intent to codify the relocation of critical United States Department of Agriculture regional hub functions, personnel, and assets to Fort Collins and Colorado State University (CSU) in the Fiscal Year 2027 Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations bill. She plans to work in a bipartisan manner to advance the language.

“On July 24, 2025, Secretary Rollins made a historic announcement to move critical United States Department of Agriculture functions out of Washington and place them in the hands of the experts in Colorado at Fort Collins and Colorado State University,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “I look forward to working with the Trump administration and House leadership to resolve the outstanding issues surrounding this relocation by including language in the Fiscal Year 2027 bill to codify the move."

Rep. Boebert highlighted Fort Collins and CSU’s longstanding United States Department of Agriculture presence—including the National Wildlife Research Center, National Laboratory for Genetic Resources Preservation, Forest Service offices, APHIS, and ARS facilities—and the university’s deep expertise in agricultural research, animal health, nutrition, and natural resource management.

“Locating additional hub functions here will strengthen collaboration with producers, improve the practical application of research, and better serve rural America while reducing unnecessary concentration of bureaucracy in Washington,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

Locating more of the Department’s operations alongside CSU’s research capacity and Northern Colorado’s agricultural community will put federal expertise closer to the producers it serves and accelerate the translation of science into on-the-ground results.

Recent legal challenges have created uncertainty and delayed full implementation. These cases underscore the risk that administrative actions alone can be blocked by litigation, making statutory direction the most effective way to lock in the relocation permanently.

“There is no bigger champion of Colorado State University than my office,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “As a member of the House Natural Resources Committee, I can see no better purpose for our Colorado tax dollars to be spent than at CSU, leveraging its expertise to advance the nation’s agriculture priorities. Codifying this relocation in statute will provide clear congressional direction, resolve ongoing legal disputes over personnel and asset transfers, and better serve rural America.”

Rep. Boebert stands ready to work in a bipartisan manner with the Department, House leadership, and Appropriations leadership to advance the language and secure its inclusion in the final bill.

Read Secretary Rollins’ July 24, 2025 announcement

title: REP. BOEBERT WELCOMES USDA DROUGHT DISASTER DESIGNATION FOR BACA AND LINCOLN COUNTIES
text:
Lone Tree, CO — U.S. Representative Lauren Boebert (R-CO) highlighted a U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretarial disaster designation for drought that makes farm operators in affected Colorado counties eligible for Farm Service Agency (FSA) emergency loan assistance.

USDA designated Adams, Arapahoe, Bent, Cheyenne, Crowley, Douglas, El Paso, Kiowa, Larimer, Logan, Morgan, Prowers, Sedgwick and Weld counties as primary natural disaster areas due to severe drought conditions during the growing season.

Additionally, Contiguous counties in Colorado’s Fourth District include Adams, Baca, Bent, Douglas, El Paso, Elbert, Kiowa, Kit Carson, Lincoln, Logan, Morgan, Prowers, Phillips, Washington, Weld and Yuma.

“Farmers and ranchers across the Eastern Plains continue to face tough conditions from drought,” said Rep. Boebert. “This designation provides important access to emergency loan assistance for producers who need it. I encourage eligible operators to contact their local FSA office as soon as possible.”

Farm operators in primary and contiguous counties have eight months from the date of the designation to apply for FSA emergency loans. Each application is considered on its own merits based on production losses, security, and repayment ability.

Deputy Under Secretary, Brooke Appleton recently wrote a letter to Governor Polis to also include Baca and Lincoln Counties as Primary Natural Disaster Areas.

For more information, see attached letter here.

Please check with your local FSA office for your designation and application dates. The disaster designation number is 2026N00002040.

title: Bynum Calls for Halt on ICE Operations in Bend to Support Grieving Community
text:
Three children, ages 5, 8, and 11, and a teacher were killed and two more people, a 7-year-old student and a teacher, were critically injured.

“Recovery depends on people being willing to show up: to seek mental health care, to talk with investigators, to gather with neighbors and to send their kids back to school,” Rep. Bynum wrote in the letter. “The last thing we need is some goons with masks exploiting this tragedy to terrorize our community further.”

“Right now, ICE is standing between grieving families and the help they need. Silver Rail's students come from every background, and my office is hearing that immigrant families are staying away from the mental health and community services set up for them,” Rep. Bynum continued in the letter. “Parents fear that a trip to a school, a clinic, a church or a vigil could end in detention or deportation. … And who could blame them? Over the last year, we’ve seen masked federal agents drag people off our streets, detain American citizens and legal residents, and kill people in broad daylight.”

The full text of the letter is available HERE and below.

David Venturella

Acting Director

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement

500 12th Street SW

Washington, DC 20536

Dear Acting Director Venturella:

I write on behalf of a community in mourning. On October 15, a 16-year-old forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend and killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher. Two more people, a 7-year-old student and a teacher, were critically wounded. Bend will forever be changed by this unimaginable loss.

On the very morning our children were killed, ICE agents arrived in Deschutes County. They are still here, and they are keeping frightened families from the help this community has come together to offer them.

I respectfully request that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement cease its non-emergency enforcement operations in Bend and Deschutes County so that families can heal and access resources without fear, on top of grief.

The weeks ahead will ask a great deal of every family in Central Oregon. Children are returning to classrooms that no longer feel safe. Parents are attending vigils, funerals, and counseling sessions. Teachers, first responders, and healthcare workers are carrying a heavy load. Recovery depends on people being willing to show up: to seek mental health care, to talk with investigators, to gather with neighbors and to send their kids back to school. The last thing we need is some goons with masks exploiting this tragedy to terrorize our community further.

Right now, ICE is standing between grieving families and the help they need. Silver Rail's students come from every background, and my office is hearing that immigrant families are staying away from the mental health and community services set up for them. Parents fear that a trip to a school, a clinic, a church or a vigil could end in detention or deportation. We’ve even heard of parents unwilling to pick up their kids’ belongings from the Silver Rail investigation because of that fear. And who could blame them? Over the last year, we’ve seen masked federal agents drag people off our streets, detain American citizens and legal residents, and kill people in broad daylight.

As a result, children are grieving in isolation, families who need trauma care are going without it, and witnesses may hesitate to come forward. That harms not only immigrant households but the recovery of the entire community.

Pausing enforcement is not a political concession. It is basic decency and professionalism. Federal agencies routinely adjust operations in the wake of natural disasters and other emergencies so that people can seek shelter and aid without fear. The aftermath of a school shooting calls for the same judgment. At a minimum, I ask that ICE:

Cease non-emergency arrests, surveillance, and enforcement activity in Bend and Deschutes County while the community recovers.

Refrain from any enforcement at or near schools, hospitals, counseling centers, places of worship, memorial sites and vigils in the region.

Notify my office in advance of any operation in the area that ICE believes cannot be deferred, and explain why.

I ask that you respond to this request in writing by Monday, October 26. My staff stands ready to work with your office and with local leaders to support the families of Bend through this period.

The people of Bend are leaning on one another right now, neighbor to neighbor. Grief does not check immigration status. Every family in Bend deserves to mourn, heal, and seek help without fear. I urge you to let them.

Sincerely,

Janelle Bynum

Member of Congress

title: CORREA, 39 COLLEAGUES DEMAND ANSWERS ON THE DETENTIONS OF U.S. CITIZENS BY IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46), a senior member of the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security, led 39 colleagues in a letter to U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding answers on the detentions and constitutional violations of U.S. citizens by DHS federal agents during immigration enforcement operations.

The letter is in response to reporting that federal immigration agents have detained more than 500 American citizens during President Trump’s second term. These arrests are the explicit outcome of President Trump’s immigration crackdown, where rogue federal agents have continuously violated Americans’ constitutional rights to due process, equal protection, and freedom from unreasonable search and seizure. The use of immigration enforcement tactics against U.S. citizens has raised questions about what documentation is needed to prove U.S. citizenship or legal residency, resulting in conflicting answers from DHS officials.

“We write to express concerns over the continued detention of U.S. citizens by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) personnel during immigration enforcement operations and to request clarity regarding documentation necessary to prove citizenship or legal authorization to be present in the United States. Recent reporting has found that over 500 U.S. citizens have been detained by federal immigration authorities since the beginning of this Administration in January 2025, including more than 100 who were questioned about their citizenship. We remain concerned that the Department’s actions are violating American citizens’ constitutional rights to due process, equal protection, and freedom from unreasonable search and seizure, and request transparency regarding the Department’s actions,” the lawmakers write.

“While public reporting has shed light on these three encounters, the Department has failed to provide information on the number of U.S. citizens who have been detained or arrested as a result of immigration enforcement operations—despite repeated requests from Members of Congress. The U.S. Government Accountability Office issued a report in July 2021 finding that ICE did not know the extent to which its officers were taking enforcement actions against individuals who could be U.S. citizens, recommending the agency improve its data documentation on encounters with potential citizens. In February 2025, ICE clarified its process to collect data on encounters with potential U.S. citizens and issued a broadcast message to field officials to make sure data is accurate. Despite supposedly instituting improvements to its data collection, ICE has not released information on the number of U.S. citizens encountered during immigration enforcement operations,” the lawmakers continue. “In addition to denying repeated requests for transparency, the Department has failed to provide consistent information to the public regarding what constitutes proof of U.S. citizenship during an encounter with DHS personnel. In a letter dated April 21, 2026, former Acting Director Lyons wrote that ICE officers “may ask individuals to provide documentation of U.S. citizenship, foreign citizenship, or legal authorization to be present in the United States,” but DHS has yet to provide clear guidance on what documentation is considered sufficient”.

“All Americans are entitled to due process, equal protection under the law, and freedom from illegal search and seizure. We respectfully request your assistance in ensuring these rights are not denied by providing the aforementioned information,” the lawmakers concluded.

Specifically, the lawmakers requested answers to the following questions:

How many U.S. citizens have been detained, which includes investigative stops, by DHS since January 20, 2025?

Are your agents documenting all detentions of U.S. citizens, to include investigative stops? Where is this information being recorded?

How many U.S. citizens have been arrested by DHS since January 20, 2025?

What documentation does DHS consider sufficient to verify citizenship status?

What training do DHS officers and agents receive regarding how to determine whether an individual is a U.S. citizen?

This letter was signed by Representatives Nanette Barragán, Salud Carbajal, Joaquin Castro, Yvette Clarke, Judy Chu, Joe Courtney, Jim Costa, Jasmine Crockett, Mark DeSaulnier, Diana DeGette, Veronica Escobar, Adriano Espaillat, Sylvia R. Garcia, Vicente Gonzalez, Al Green, Dan Goldman, Pablo Jose Hernandez, Hank Johnson, Julie Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Timothy Kennedy, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Teresa Leger Fernandez, Stephen Lynch, Seth Magaziner, Dave Min, Jerrold Nadler, Richard Neal, Joe Neguse, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Mary Gay Scanlon, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Dina Titus, Norma Torres, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, and Maxine Waters.

title: UPDATE: SBA Opens Business Recovery Center in Tusayan Following Grand Canyon Flash Floods
text:
Last week, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced the availability of low-interest federal disaster loans for small businesses and private nonprofit organizations experiencing economic losses from the recent flash flooding at Grand Canyon National Park.

Since then, the SBA has opened a Business Recovery Center at Tusayan Town Hall (845 Mustang Drive, Tusayan, AZ 86023). Representatives are on hand to answer questions and walk applicants through the loan process weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. MST until the center closes on Friday, October 30. Walk-ins are welcome, and in-person appointments can be scheduled by clicking here.

The disaster declaration, issued on October 13, covers Coconino, Gila, Mohave, Navajo, and Yavapai Counties in Arizona, as well as Kane and San Juan Counties in Utah.

As a result, the SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program is now open to eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations with financial losses directly tied to the flooding.

These loans help cover working capital needs and operating expenses that could have been met had the disaster not occurred. Importantly, applicants may qualify even if their business or nonprofit did not sustain physical damage.

For additional information or to begin an application, please click here, call the SBA’s Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. Individuals who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability may dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

The deadline to submit economic injury applications is July 13, 2027.

title: Rep. Cuellar Secures $30 Million Authorization to Support Water Infrastructure in Zapata County
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Congressman Henry Cuellar, Ph.D. (TX-28) secured a $30 million authorization to support water infrastructure improvements in Zapata County, along with a directive to expedite erosion protection work in the Medina Colonia. The provisions were included in the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (WRDA 2026), which passed in the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee on Tuesday, July 14.

WRDA 2026 increases a previous authorization for Zapata County from $20 million to $30 million and expands it to support additional water infrastructure improvements.

The bill also directs the Corps of Engineers to expedite erosion protection work already underway in the Medina Colonia to help protect infrastructure from further damage.

“Zapata County has real needs when it comes to water infrastructure and erosion control, and WRDA 2026 responds to both,” said Congressman Cuellar. “Increasing the authorization and expanding its scope give the Corps of Engineers greater flexibility to support Zapata County’s water system, and directing the Corps to expedite the Medina Colonia erosion work gets families the protection they’ve been waiting for. I’ll keep pushing to see both provisions through to final passage.”

WRDA 2026 also includes several other TX-28 priorities, including expanded eligibility for Rio Grande Basin watershed and water quality programs, increased shoreline erosion protection opportunities for Rio Grande border counties and a higher authorization ceiling for the Corps’ Lakes Program.

###

title: Rep. Cuellar Secures $25 Million Authorization for Laredo Water Infrastructure
text:

The authorization was included in the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (WRDA 2026), which passed in the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee on Tuesday, July 14. “Laredo’s water and wastewater systems have to keep pace with our growth, and that means real investment in the infrastructure our families rely on every day,” said Congressman Cuellar. “This authorization gives the Corps of Engineers the resources it needs to support water loss reduction, flood mitigation and environmental restoration work across Laredo. title: Rep. Cuellar Secures Three Provisions Supporting Future Rio Grande Basin Water Projects
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Congressman Henry Cuellar, Ph.D. (TX-28) secured three provisions supporting future Corps of Engineers water studies and projects across the Rio Grande Basin and Texas border counties. The provisions were included in the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (WRDA 2026), which passed in the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee on Tuesday, July 14. Together, they expand opportunities for future water planning, flood protection and environmental restoration in South Texas.

One provision makes the Rio Grande Basin eligible for a comprehensive Corps of Engineers watershed assessment. The study could examine water supply, drought, flooding, ecosystem health and long-term water planning to help identify future infrastructure needs.

Another provision expands eligibility for Rio Grande border counties, including Webb, Zapata and Starr counties, to compete for future Corps projects that reduce flood damage, protect riverbanks and restore natural waterways.

Finally, a third provision strengthens the Rio Grande Basin's eligibility for future Corps of Engineers work related to harmful algal blooms and water quality. The designation supports future monitoring, the testing of new technologies and mitigation efforts to help address algal blooms in the Basin.

“The three provisions I secured in the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 put the Rio Grande Basin and our border counties in position to get more support in the future,” said Congressman Cuellar. “Being named an eligible basin or focus area is how projects like the ones we've already secured for Laredo, Starr County, Jim Hogg County and Zapata County get their start. I'll keep working to make sure South Texas has a seat at the table every time the Corps sets its priorities.”

title: Davids, Local Leaders Celebrate Completion of Multi-Decade Turkey Creek Flood Control Project
text:
KANSAS CITY, KS — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined representatives from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the City of Kansas City, Missouri, and the Unified Government of Wyandotte County and Kansas City, Kansas for a ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the final completion of the Turkey Creek Flood Control Project.

The project officially removes Downtown Merriam from the FEMA-designated floodplain, protecting hundreds of homes and over 80 local small businesses. The upgraded infrastructure also eliminates mandatory flood insurance requirements for impacted properties, unlocking significant new economic investment and growth for the area.

“After nearly three decades of work, today we are celebrating a major milestone that gives hundreds of families and business owners in our community the safety and peace of mind they deserve,” said Davids. “By removing Downtown Merriam from the floodplain, we are freeing local home and business owners from unpredictable flood threats and expensive insurance costs while opening up exciting new opportunities for local economic development. I’m proud to have worked alongside our local, state, and federal partners to bring these historic flood protections across the finish line.”

The Turkey Creek Flood Control Project originally kicked off in 1997, breaking ground on its first major construction phase in 2004. With the final project phase wrapping up this year, the completion marks the culmination of nearly 30 years of bi-state, local-federal collaboration designed to protect surrounding neighborhoods from destructive high-water events.

Davids worked directly to secure key federal resources to move the Turkey Creek project forward:

$500,000: Davids individually secured $500,000 in federal project funding to kickstart crucial design efforts, which directly contributed to removing Downtown Merriam from the FEMA floodplain.

$23.9 Million: Building on this progress, Davids previously announced $23.9 million in federal funding for the Upper Turkey Creek flood mitigation project through the bipartisan infrastructure law.

Kansas City, Kansas ranks as the fifth most vulnerable U.S. city to climate impacts, particularly severe urban flooding. Over the last decade alone, Kansas has endured more than 40 extreme weather events, costing the state up to $20 billion in damages. This project demonstrates how targeted infrastructure investments can directly protect local homes and businesses, lower costs for families, and unlock new opportunities for economic development.

title: Congressman Deluzio Announces $3.6 Million in Federal Grants to Support 15 Western PA Fire Departments
text:
CARNEGIE, PA — Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) announced that fifteen Western Pennsylvania fire departments are receiving a total of nearly $3.6 million in federal grant funding to support their public safety work. Many of these grant awards were successful following Congressman Deluzio’s office’s direct advocacy for this funding to come to Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) provided the funding via the Department of Homeland Security’s Fiscal Year 2025 Assistance to Firefighters (AFG) and Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant programs.

A total of $3,594,533.98 in federal funding is coming to fifteen fire departments in Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District. The majority of the funding awards will help thirteen Western PA fire departments purchase critical equipment, protective gear, emergency vehicles, training, and other resources through the AFG program. Two other departments will receive close to $1 million to support their firefighter recruitment and retention efforts through the SAFER program.

"I’m excited to announce that I’ve helped bring federal funding home to help Western Pennsylvania fire departments do the hard work to keep all of us safe,” said Congressman Deluzio. “These grants will help our local fire departments buy equipment, get new gear, and better recruit and retain the firefighters they need on the job. Our first responders show up for all of us in our times of need—I will always have their backs. I encourage other fire departments in Western Pennsylvania to apply for this funding—my office stands ready to support your applications as best we can.”

“New Brighton Borough and Fire Department officials are immensely grateful to Congressman Deluzio and his staff for his ongoing support and advocacy in securing this critical federal funding for the New Brighton Fire Department,” said Tom Albanese, Borough Manager of New Brighton. “Replacing our aging apparatus with a modern, state-of-the-art fire engine ensures our dedicated firefighters have the essential equipment needed to protect our residents and merchants. This substantial grant provides a vital boost to our local emergency services while easing the financial burden on the New Brighton community.”

title: Congresswoman Escobar Introduces Bill to Improve Port Staffing, Infrastructure Needs
text:
This week, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) introduced the Port Staffing Reporting Act, legislation requiring the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to assess staffing levels, operational challenges, and infrastructure needs at ports of entry across the United States.

“In El Paso, we see every day how our ports connect families, support businesses, and keep our economy moving,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “The Port Staffing Reporting Act will bring greater transparency and accountability to port operations and help ensure that our ports of entry are adequately staffed and performing at optimum for our region.”

The Port Staffing Reporting Act would require the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit an assessment to Congress within 90 days of the bill’s enactment, and every year after. The report would assess:

Staffing and personnel needs

Wait times and traffic flow

Infrastructure and technology

Economic impacts

Local port needs

The legislation would also require the Secretary of Homeland Security to brief the House and Senate committees with jurisdiction over homeland security within 30 days of submitting each assessment.

Ports of entry are critical to border security, international commerce, and the lives of border residents. However, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has reported that staffing levels have remained relatively flat even as trade and passenger volumes have increased. Staffing shortages can strain operations, contribute to delays, and make it more difficult to keep traffic moving efficiently.

“El Paso’s staffing challenges are real, but they’re also a symptom of a national problem across CBP. Field offices throughout the country are struggling to meet mission requirements with insufficient personnel. This bill represents a responsible and necessary step toward re‑evaluating staffing needs nationwide and ensuring Appropriators have the transparency required to fund CBP at levels that support recruitment, retention, and safe, effective port operations,” said Gus Sanchez, President NTEU Ch. 143.

"The Texas Border Coalition supports Rep. Escobar’s efforts to ensure the land ports of entry along the Southern Border are well equipped and well-staffed to ensure the smooth flow of cross-border commerce. We hope this feasibility study will show how important our land ports of entry are, particularly those along our southern border, to both national security and international commerce," said the Texas Border Coalition.

“NTEU is proud to endorse the Port Staffing Reporting Act. America's ports of entry are the front line for both national security and economic prosperity, and our CBP workforce are the people who work hard every day to make both possible. For too long, chronic understaffing has made that mission harder than it has to be. We appreciate Rep. Escobar's efforts to support our members and ensure that Congress has the facts they need to understand and address these staffing shortages. Our members and the American people deserve nothing less,” said NTEU National President Doreen Greenwald.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

title: Fitzpatrick Secures $4 Million for New Bensalem Fire Station to Modernize Emergency Response and Strengthen Public Safety
text:
Major federal investment will replace nearly 50-year-old facilities, strengthen coordination between career and volunteer firefighters, and enhance emergency protection across Bensalem Township.

LANGHORNE, PA — Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) announced a major victory securing $4 million in federal Community Project Funding to advance construction of Bensalem Township’s new Department of Public Safety Fire Station, a major step toward modernizing emergency response and strengthening public safety across the township.

The project will replace two nearly 50-year-old volunteer fire stations with a modern, centrally located facility uniting career and volunteer firefighters under one roof. Designed to improve response times, expand emergency coverage, and integrate fire, rescue, EMS, and command operations, the new station will give Bensalem’s first responders the infrastructure and operational capabilities they need to protect its residents and meet future public safety challenges.

“On behalf of the Bensalem Township Department of Public Safety and the firefighters who serve the community of Bensalem, we would like to express our appreciation and gratitude to Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick for providing necessary funding to assist the Township with the development of a new fire station. The construction of a new firehouse, along with improvements to existing infrastructure, remains a priority for Bensalem Township to ensure the continued delivery of safe, efficient, and reliable fire services to the community,” said William McVey, Director of Public Safety for Bensalem Township.

“This historic investment is a major step forward for public safety in Bensalem. The new facility will strengthen our emergency response capabilities, improve coordination between our career and volunteer firefighters, and provide our first responders with the resources and facilities they need to protect our community. We thank Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick for his support and commitment to bringing federal resources back to our community!” said Mark Antozzeski, Fire Chief of Bensalem Township.

“Our first responders are the foundation of public safety, and ensuring they have the resources their mission demands has long been one of my highest priorities as Co-Chair of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus,” said Fitzpatrick. “We are fortunate to have some of the finest right here in PA-1. Through years of working alongside Bensalem’s firefighters and public safety leaders, I’ve witnessed their extraordinary dedication, skill, and selfless service as they’ve adapted to the evolving needs of our community. Working closely with Mayor DiGirolamo, Director McVey, Chief Antozzeski, township leaders, and the firefighters themselves, we recognized the need for a modern, centralized facility that would strengthen their ability to protect our neighbors. So, I got to work and fought to secure $4 million to bring this vision to life. I’m grateful for their steadfast service and partnership, and look forward to continuing our work together to ensure they have the support, resources, and capabilities they need to continue safely and successfully protecting our community.”

Strengthening Emergency Response and First Responder Readiness

The new Department of Public Safety Fire Station will provide a centralized, purpose-built facility designed to meet Bensalem Township’s current operational needs while preparing its emergency services for future demands.

Key project improvements include:

Faster Response Times and Expanded Coverage: A strategically located facility designed to improve emergency access, streamline deployment, and strengthen protection for neighborhoods throughout Bensalem.

Greater Coordination and Operational Readiness: A unified station bringing career and volunteer firefighters together, strengthening communication, staffing readiness, training capacity, and command operations.

Modern Equipment and Emergency Response Capabilities: Expanded operational space to accommodate fire and rescue vehicles, EMS units, marine response equipment, and other critical resources necessary to respond to a broad range of emergencies.

Beyond replacing aging infrastructure, the project will establish a more coordinated, efficient, and resilient emergency response system—strengthening the township’s long-term preparedness while supporting the safety of both residents and the first responders who serve them.

Delivering For Pennsylvania’s First District

The Bensalem fire station is part of Fitzpatrick’s broader commitment to strengthening public safety, supporting first responders, and modernizing critical infrastructure throughout Pennsylvania’s First Congressional District.

Through the FY2026 Community Project Funding process, Fitzpatrick successfully championed more than $27.5 million for 11 community projects addressing critical local needs across Pennsylvania’s First District.

With this latest round of funding, Fitzpatrick has brought more than $80 million in federal Community Project Funding to PA-01 since FY2022, translating priorities identified by local communities into lasting investments in the people, services, and infrastructure that strengthen the region.

Together, these investments reflect Fitzpatrick’s community-first leadership, empowering local organizations, responding to community needs, and ensuring federal resources translate into meaningful, measurable, and lasting benefits for Bucks and Montgomery counties.

title: Congressman Dan Goldman Joins Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) in Reintroducing the 988 Implementation Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Dan Goldman (NY-10), Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) and Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01) reintroduced the 988 Implementation Act with Congressmembers Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Troy Carter (LA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Don Beyer (VA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Becca Balint (VT-AL), and Kim Schrier (WA-08). The comprehensive legislative package will provide states with federal resources to strengthen the crisis response infrastructure behind the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

The bill includes Rep. Goldman's Supporting 988 Crisis Stabilization Act to ensure that individuals in need of trauma-informed, clinically appropriate, and patient-centered care are not hindered by Medicaid, specifically when seeking short-term crisis receiving and stabilization services. These services can reduce psychiatric hospitalization, ensure referrals to community-based treatment, and avert arrest and incarceration for individuals experiencing a mental health crisis.

Specifically, the bill would clarify that Medicaid's longstanding payment prohibition on long term inpatient care does not apply to short-term crisis receiving and stabilization facilities run by community-based programs. The bill institutes guardrails to protect patients and requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services to issue guidance and collect data on crisis stabilization programs, including length of stay, facility size, diversion from law enforcement and incarceration, and other relevant categories.

Since its launch in 2022, the 988 Lifeline has receivedmore than 26 million calls, texts, chats, and ASL videophone contacts from people seeking help across America.

“Too many Americans in crisis are left without safe access to care,” said Congressman Goldman. “The 988 Lifeline is a proven system for getting people the help they need when they need it most. That's why I'm proud to join in introducing the 988 Implementation Act to give states better resources to bolster their crisis response infrastructure and develop a full continuum of care that prioritizes safety and dignity for all communities.”

“When someone reaches out for help in a moment of crisis, we have a responsibility to make sure help is there,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “988 has become a lifesaving resource for millions of Americans, but answering the call cannot be where our responsibility ends. We built a national front door to crisis care with 988. Now we need to strengthen what comes next by expanding mobile crisis response, increasing access to immediate community-based care, and connecting people to the treatment and support they need.”

“Everyday, millions of Americans face mental challenges and are unsure where to go for help,” said Congressman Fitzpatrick, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Taskforce. “The 988 hotline streamlines resources for those in need, as part of a network of over 200 local crisis centers, yet only thirteen-percent of adults are aware of this critical resource. I am proud to join a bipartisan group of colleagues in introducing the 988 Implementation Act to build upon the critical progress we have made, and further ensure that our communities are properly equipped with crisis-response services.”

“Americans deserve compassionate care when they are experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis,” said Congresswoman Barragán. “That is why I am joining Representatives Matsui and Fitzpatrick in introducing the 988 Implementation Act, bipartisan legislation to strengthen the 988 Crisis Lifeline. It includes the 988 Community Infrastructure Act, a bill I introduced to help communities build or expand the facilities they need, so people in crisis can get timely care in a more welcoming and appropriate setting—not an emergency room or with law enforcement. By investing in the critical 988 lifeline, we can improve access to trained mental health specialists and ensure that no one falls through the cracks when they need help most.”

“Our nation is facing an unprecedented mental health crisis, and all too often people who are struggling don’t know where to turn to for help,” said Congressman Carter. “The 988 Crisis Line is a lifeline for so many people in our country. It connects them to care, to treatment, and to hope. I’m proud to support this important legislation that prioritizes the mental health and wellbeing of American citizens by investing in community-based crisis response, breaking down barriers to accessing mental healthcare treatment, and ensuring everyone knows where to turn to in moments of crisis.”

“Calling 988 takes courage, and answering takes patience and care. Our job is to support both,” said Congresswoman Trahan, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force. “We all know someone who has struggled with mental health or substance use and wished there was more help within reach. This bill delivers it, with a faster response, a real place to turn, and trained professionals ready to pick up the phone.”

“I’m extraordinarily proud of the success of the 988 lifeline since its implementation. The high volume of calls and messages to 988 shows that Americans are still in dire need of improved mental health resources,” said Congressman Moulton. “It is critical that we continue advocating for more funding and expanded 988 services. The suite of bills contained within the 988 Implementation Act will provide federal support for states to enact 988 and crisis services, improve 988 implementation at the local level, expand access to critical services, and broaden awareness of available resources.”

“America’s mental health epidemic leaves millions of our neighbors without access to the care they desperately need,” said Congressman Raskin. “I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this critical bipartisan legislation that will greatly expand access to mental health crisis response teams, an expert presence beside our people during the darkest moments.”

“Since its launch, the 988 Lifeline has connected more than 26 million Americans with the support they need in moments of crisis,” said Congressman Beyer. “That’s an extraordinary achievement, and we must build on that success to save more lives and ensure no one falls through the cracks. Our 988 Implementation Act would further strengthen our crisis response system by ensuring trained professionals are available around the clock, crisis teams are equipped to respond in communities, and those in need can access care and services without facing financial barriers.”

“Every year, 988 call centers respond to hundreds of thousands of calls and work around the clock to provide callers with the mental health and crisis management care they need. The 988 Implementation Act will increase access to care with greater support, workforce development opportunities and more,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “I applaud Reps. Matsui and Fitzpatrick for their leadership on this critical issue, and I’m grateful that they incorporated my legislation to provide and expand coverage for behavioral health crisis response services into the bill. Together, we can improve mental health nationwide and ensure 988 continues to help those in our communities who need it most.”

“Especially during Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, I’m incredibly proud to be introducing the 988 and 911 Integration Act,” said Congresswoman Balint. “One of my top priorities in Congress is reducing stigma and taking real action to improve access to mental healthcare. We know that mental health affects not just individuals, but also their families and communities, too. This bill, alongside the broader 988 Implementation Act, would help local communities strengthen and better utilize 988 resources–a lifeline for those experiencing a behavioral health crisis–and bridge gaps in care in communities all over the country.”

“As a pediatrician, I have seen firsthand how severe our youth and adult mental health crisis has become,” said Congresswoman Schrier, M.D. “It is so important that when our family members, loved ones, and neighbors are in crisis, they can get immediate help. The 988 Crisis Line saves lives and strengthens our communities. We need to make sure that 988 teams are always available for every American as a reliable resource when our community members need help.”

As America’s mental health crisisworsens, 988 has spent the past four years demonstrating the lifesaving power of connecting people in crisis with the right help at the right time. A study published this year by the Journal of American Medical Association (JAMA) found that suicide deaths among children and young adultsfell 11% below projected levels following the launch of 988, the largest declines were seen in states where 988 use increased most.

But answering the call is only the first step. Someone experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis may also need a trained professional to respond in person, a safe place to receive immediate care, or assistance with continued treatment. Today, access to those services still vary significantly depending on where someone lives.

The 988 Implementation Act will help address those gaps in access to care by:

Strengthening federal funding for 988 regional and local call centers to deliver timely, 24/7 response to callers

Expanding community-based and mobile crisis response so trained behavioral health professionals can reach someone who needs in-person support

Improving access and affordability by requiring health insurance plans to cover crisis services

Growing crisis workforce development with more funding for training and scholarship opportunities

Increasing awareness of 988 through a national suicide prevention and crisis services campaign

The legislation is supported by more than 35 organizations including mental health advocates, clinical and medical professionals, state and local government officials, civil rights advocates, veterans, and more.

“The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline has transformed how people can access support during mental health, substance use and suicide crises,” said Hannah Wesolowski, Chief Advocacy Officer at the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI). “We must continue building this progress by ensuring 988 has the resources, infrastructure and workforce needed to meet the needs of people in crisis. NAMI is grateful to Rep. Matsui for the introduction of the 988 Implementation Act, which will help strengthen the Lifeline and ensure communities can deliver the compassionate, timely mental health response that people deserve.”

The 988 Implementation Act is endorsed by the following organizations: American Association for Psychoanalysis in Clinical Social Work, American Association of Psychiatric Pharmacists (AAPP), American Association on Health and Disability, American Group Psychotherapy Association, Anxiety and Depression Association of America, Association for Ambulatory Behavioral Healthcare (AABH), American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, Children and Adults with Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (CHADD), Connections Health Solutions, Crisis Text Line, Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance (DBSA), Easterseals, Inc., Global Alliance for Behavioral Health and Social Justice, Huntington's Disease Society of America, International Society for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurses, Lakeshore Foundation, Legal Action Center, NAMI, National Association of Pediatric Nurse Practitioners, National Association of Social Workers, National Association of State Directors of Developmental Disabilities Services, National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors, National League for Nursing, Overdose Prevention Initiative at the Global Health Advocacy Incubator Psychotherapy Action Network (PsiAN), SMART Recovery, Steinberg Institute, Sycamores, The American Counseling Association, The Miles Hall Foundation, The National Alliance to Advance Adolescent Health, The National Federation of Families, The Paramedic Foundation/American College of Paramedics/American Paramedic Association, The Trevor Project, Tourette Association of America, and Treatment Advocacy Center (TAC).

Bill text for the Supporting 988 Crisis Stabilization Act can be found here and full bill text for the 988 Implementation Act can be found here.
