title: SEED Symposium Connects Eastern Kentucky Manufacturers
text:
Manufacturers in Eastern Kentucky are securing federal contracts and building connections with major corporations through the Supplier Education & Economic Development (SEED) program.

The Eighth Annual SEED Contracting Symposium was held Wednesday, Oct. 21, at The Center for Rural Development in Somerset, Kentucky.

The event was developed to train, certify and prepare the region’s successful small manufacturers to do business with defense industry representatives.

Thirty-three Eastern Kentucky-based businesses participated in this year’s event, exhibiting their products and capabilities to defense contracting companies including The Boeing Company, Northrop Grumman Corporation, GE Aerospace and General Dynamics.

The event is a collaborative effort between the office of Fifth District Congressman Hal Rogers and Southeast Kentucky Economic Development Corporation. (SKED).

“I was proud to welcome NASA and several other prime federal contractors to southern Kentucky to meet with more than 30 businesses across our region. Various government operations need American-made products, from military gear to NASA’s planned Moon base. Thanks to the SEED Symposium, Eastern Kentucky companies can learn how to compete for those contracts and create more jobs here at home,” said Congressman Hal Rogers, who launched SKED in 1985.

Dwight D. Deneal, assistant administrator for NASA's Office of Small Business Programs, delivered the keynote address. Deneal leads agency-wide programs and policies to ensure equal opportunities for small businesses to support NASA’s mission.

“From precision machining to advanced manufacturing, Eastern Kentucky businesses belong in the supply chain that will take us to the Moon and beyond,” said Deneal.

SKED Executive Director Brett Traver works with the region’s small businesses to present the event.

“It’s a pleasure seeing the region’s small business owners making connections with prime contractors and each other at the SEED symposium every year,” said Traver. “We truly appreciate the folks who traveled here and gave a full day’s work for our event. Its benefit will pay off in the contracts made, jobs created, and lives improved here in Southern and Eastern Kentucky.”

SKED and its SEED partners, Kentucky Manufacturing Extension Partnership and KY APEX Accelerator, work with these businesses throughout the year to prepare them for the annual contracting symposium.

For more information about the Eastern Kentucky SEED Contracting Symposium or SEED, contact Brett Traver, SKED executive director, at 606-677-6102 or brett@skedcorp.com.

title: ICYMI: Congressman Pat Harrigan Pens Op-Ed on Delivering Rural Healthcare Investments for North Carolina
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—In a new op-ed for Carolina Journal, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) highlights how the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program he helped establish is already delivering results for North Carolina. He details how more than $213 million in first-year funding is being directed toward improving rural healthcare access and how his newly introduced REACH Act would build on those investments by addressing critical shortages of doctors, nurses, and mental health professionals.

You can read the full piece here or below.

The Rural Health Transformation Fund is delivering for NC

For millions of North Carolinians, the biggest obstacle to getting medical care is increasingly simple: finding someone nearby who can provide it.

In rural communities, hospitals are operating on thin margins, medical practices are struggling to replace retiring physicians, and families are driving farther for appointments that once could have been made close to home. When an emergency strikes, the distance between a patient and the nearest available care can have serious consequences.

North Carolina has roughly 3 million rural residents, the second-largest rural population in America. Yet 93 of our 100 counties face primary care shortages, and more than 90 have shortages of mental health professionals. These are staggering numbers for a state with some of the finest medical institutions in the country.

We have the expertise to address these challenges. What rural communities have lacked is a sustained commitment to putting those resources within reach.

That is beginning to change.

Last year, I voted for the Working Families Tax Cuts, which established the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program. It was one of the largest federal commitments to rural healthcare in American history, and North Carolina has already been awarded more than $213 million for the program’s first year.

Now we are seeing where those dollars are headed.

The Trump administration recently announced $20 million to expand telehealth and modernize healthcare technology across North Carolina. For smaller hospitals and medical practices, that means opportunities to replace outdated systems, improve patient records, strengthen cybersecurity, and connect people with specialists they might otherwise have to travel hours to see.

Additional investments are targeting some of the most difficult gaps in rural care. More than $17 million has been announced for behavioral health services, including three new mental health clinics, expanded opioid treatment in five counties, and mobile crisis teams in six more. The administration has also announced funding to strengthen rural emergency medical services and expand access to care through schools.

Consider the practical difference. A patient in Yadkin County who needs a specialist may be able to receive care closer to home. A family struggling to find mental health treatment may have another local option. An emergency medical service operating with limited resources may be better equipped to respond when minutes matter.

These are the kinds of improvements rural North Carolinians have been waiting for.

But money for equipment and facilities only gets us so far. One of the most serious problems facing rural healthcare is the shortage of people available to deliver it.

A modern clinic cannot treat patients without a physician. New technology cannot replace a nurse. And a community cannot maintain dependable healthcare when it struggles year after year to recruit medical professionals.

I recently introduced the REACH Act to address that problem directly. My legislation would provide a refundable $10,000 annual tax credit to eligible doctors, nurses, mental health professionals, and medical residents who choose to work in rural communities.

The goal is to make practicing medicine in a small town a more financially attractive decision. Medical professionals often graduate with significant educational expenses, and rural practices must compete with larger health systems for their services. Giving those professionals a meaningful incentive to serve underserved communities can help close that gap.

This is how I believe we should approach rural healthcare in Congress: Invest in the infrastructure communities need while addressing the workforce shortages that prevent patients from receiving care. Both problems demand attention, and progress on one makes the other more achievable.

The politics surrounding these investments also deserve some clarity.

Every congressional Democrat voted against the Working Families Tax Cuts, the legislation that created the Rural Health Transformation Program. Yet Gov. Josh Stein recently announced a $20 million rural health initiative funded through that very program.

I welcome the announcement. North Carolina should make full use of every available resource to strengthen rural healthcare. But it’s important to be clear about the legislative record: Congressional Republicans passed the law that established this $50 billion investment, and the funding now being announced is a direct result of that vote.

Of course, securing federal funding is only the beginning. The real measure of success will be whether a rural hospital can keep its doors open, whether a young doctor chooses to practice in a small town, and whether a family can get the care it needs without spending half a day on the road.

Those outcomes require more than a single appropriation or announcement. They require thoughtful investments, a stronger medical workforce, and accountability for how public dollars are spent.

I was proud to help establish the Rural Health Transformation Program, and I’m working to build on that investment through my REACH Act. North Carolina now has a significant opportunity to strengthen healthcare in communities that have spent far too long falling behind.

The funding is in place. The work is underway. Now our responsibility is to turn those investments into better care for the North Carolinians who need it.

title: Hinson, Scholten Introduce SCREENS Act to Help Patients Catch Cancer Earlier, Save Lives
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02) and Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) introduced the Standardizing Cancer Recommendations for Earlier Evaluation and Navigation of Screenings (SCREENS) Act. Senator Chuck Grassley (R-IA) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate. This bipartisan bill would help more Americans catch cancer earlier by making screening recommendations easier to understand and giving healthcare providers better tools to identify patients who may be at risk or overdue for screenings.

“So many Iowa families have been touched by cancer, including mine. Iowa’s rising cancer rates are unacceptable, and we have to do everything we can to reverse this trend. That starts with making early detection resources simple and accessible so we can catch cancer earlier, improve outcomes, and save lives. I will continue working across the aisle and leave no stone unturned in this fight.” – Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

“Early cancer detection saves lives, but for far too many Americans, navigating complicated health care recommendations can lead to missed screenings. I’m proud to join Rep. Hinson in introducing the SCREENS Act, which would help create a national, digital framework of cancer screening guidelines. Building this resource will give patients clear, easy-to-follow recommendations and help providers identify who is overdue so that more people in Michigan and across the country get the services they need when they need them.” – Congresswoman Hillary Scholten

“Detecting cancer early can save lives. I know that based on the personal experience of my wife, Barbara, a nearly 40-year breast cancer survivor. Unfortunately, patients and providers are navigating a complex and confusing maze just to keep up with cancer screening recommendations. By making these recommendations more accessible through technology, our SCREENS Act would strengthen cancer care and help save lives. This bill would proactively support Iowans by helping providers identify patients who could be overdue for a screening. I want to thank Congresswoman Hinson for her support for this legislation and her commitment to boosting cancer care in Iowa.” – Senator Chuck Grassley

Background:

Specifically, the SCREENS Act would:

Make cancer screening guidelines easier to access: Direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop a national digital framework for cancer screening and risk assessment recommendations that can be incorporated into electronic health records.

Help doctors catch potential risks earlier: Support technology that helps healthcare providers identify patients who may be at higher risk for cancer or overdue for recommended screenings.

Give patients clearer information: Make screening recommendations easier to understand and follow so patients can stay on top of their health.

Improve coordination with health plans: Require HHS to issue guidance to Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, and ACA plans on integrating electronic cancer screening tools.

Support innovation in cancer prevention and early detection: Authorize research and pilot projects to help bring these technologies into everyday medical practice.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON NEWS 12: “DRAMATIC CHANGE IS NECESSARY”
text:
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Tara Rosenblum in Brooklyn’s Shirley Chisholm State Park for a special edition of News 12’s Power & Politics, where he discussed the path to taking back the House of Representatives and how House Democrats are fighting for an affordable America.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You sound extraordinarily confident that the Democrats will be able to win back the House, but we have seen here in New York where the polls have gotten a lot of big races wrong lately. So what is it that you’re seeing on the ground that makes you feel so optimistic? That’s always the best barometer, right? On the ground, talking to the voters.

LEADER JEFFRIES: On the ground, I’ve been traveling the country talking to everyday Americans, and what’s clear is that dramatic change is necessary. The American people know that things aren’t going well. Too many Americans are drowning in this failed Trump-Republican economy.

TARA ROSENBLUM: And we’re going to talk a lot about the economy in this interview, but first I want to drill down and go hyper-local because, as you know, a number of the tightest House races in the country are playing out right here at home. So as you’re sitting down and you’re doing this midterm math, what are the local races that you feel are the most pivotal, the best pickup opportunities towards your path to the majority?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re working hard to make sure that Congressman Tom Suozzi and Congresswoman Laura Gillen are both reelected. They’re doing an extraordinary job on behalf of the people of Nassau County, fighting every day to try to make life more affordable. At the same period of time, in the northern New York City suburbs of Westchester and Rockland County, Cait Conley, a combat veteran, a patriot, a national security professional, is running an extraordinary race to win a seat currently held by a Republican Congressman, Mike Lawler.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You have called Mike Lawler an ‘unmitigated fraud,’ yet some of your fellow Democrats have broke ranks and endorsed him, like Jared Golden. What do you make of that? And I guess the more important question is, can you flip the House if you don’t win NY-17?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, NY-17 is going to be incredibly important, and Cait is doing a great job, and I believe that she is going to be elected to Congress in November. Jared is going to have to speak for his own decisions. He’s a retiring Member of Congress. He’s from Maine, hundreds of miles away. This is a race that’s going to be decided by people on the ground.

TARA ROSENBLUM: I know you’ve said that you will address this after Election Day. What do you think are the appropriate consequences for Democrats who break rank on important endorsements or critical votes?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll have a family conversation about the best way for us to proceed in the aftermath of the November 3 midterm elections. Right now we’ve got to be all-hands-on-deck to make sure that we’re successful.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You also mentioned the Long Island Congressman from our backyard, Tom Suozzi. He has made some recent statements expressing concern that the party is pouring a lot of resources into those pickup opportunities like NY-17, and perhaps short-changing safer seats like his. How do you respond to that? Is the party stretched too thin right now?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Our first priority will remain making sure that our incumbents like Tom Suozzi and Laura Gillen and Josh Riley here in New York and in other parts of the country are re-elected.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You know, it’s looking like a number of these tight races will come down to a few thousand votes, which means that these Independent voters will be pivotal, and when we’re out and about in the streets talking to our Independent voters, especially in the suburbs, you know, in the Hudson Valley, Long Island, New Jersey, a lot of them express just as much frustration as they feel with the President’s policies as they do with some of the leftward push from the Democratic Party. So how do you win over those Independents without alienating the progressives? And really the bigger question is, do you think that some of the Democrats’ policies have moved too far left to win the suburbs?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what unites the House Democratic Caucus, whether that is the progressive wing or New Dems or Blue Dogs, is the fact that all of us recognize life is way too expensive. And there’s a shared aspiration to make life better for everyday Americans, working-class Americans and middle-class Americans, including those hardworking American taxpayers in the suburbs. And that really is going to be our driving, core mission, because we know that a lot of promises were made by Donald Trump and Republicans with respect to affordability, and in my view, our view, they’ve left behind a graveyard of broken promises.

TARA ROSENBLUM: In addition to reversing some of Trump—President Trump’s policies, I know you’ve been an outspoken critic of his tariff decisions. Tell me a Democratic proposal that you would push for next year that would help out with affordability and help families afford food and fuel and housing costs.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s clear to us, as Democrats, that we need to dramatically build more housing that the American people can afford. And in this Congress, we were able to pass a housing affordability bill—that is now law—that will start that process, but it’s clear that more needs to be done. So, we can enhance and strengthen the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, which is a vehicle used by affordable housing developers to build housing that working-class folks and middle-class folks and everyday Americans can actually live in with dignity and respect. We need to lean into the affordable housing space in that regard by strengthening the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, increasingly used for moderate-income housing as well. I think we need to put money in the pockets of everyday Americans by doing things like expanding the Child Tax Credit, as well as the Earned Income Tax Credit. And, of course, we also need to end this war because the war has dramatically increased gas prices, fertilizer prices and diesel costs. And that’s had an impact on the American people that is hurting their pocketbooks.

TARA ROSENBLUM: And you’re referring to the Iran war?

LEADER JEFFRIES: That’s correct.

TARA ROSENBLUM: I know in a recent interview when you were asked about withholding funding, you stopped short. So if the Democrats take back the House, and if you become Speaker, and if President Trump continues this military option, will you pursue the House’s power of the purse to force an end to this war?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I don’t want to get out ahead of the appropriators and that effort, in terms of figuring out how we deal with this issue, will be led by Rosa DeLauro, who will be the top Democrat on the Appropriations Committee and the next Chair. But we do have to look at every available legislative mean in order to do what the American people want us to do, which is bring an end to this reckless, unnecessary war.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You have also said that should you—should the Democrats take back the House, you have said you will start ‘holding the crooks accountable on day one.’ And when I heard you say that, I was wondering—who is he referring to by ‘crooks,’ and what does accountability look like?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what we’ve said is that if folks are out there, and you have been stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people, that beginning on day one, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable. We’ve seen unprecedented corruption unleashed by the Trump Cartel, broadly defined, on the American people in ways that are inconsistent with delivering a government of the people, by the people and for the people. This executive branch, the Trump Cartel, is totally out of control. The American people know it. There’s a new scandal that arises every day. And we’ve got to clean that mess up.

TARA ROSENBLUM: You have repeatedly refused to rule out impeaching the President. So looking forward, in 2028, what would it take for you to consider a third impeachment?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out. The oversight efforts are going to be led by the House Judiciary Committee Democrats and Jamie Raskin, the next Chair of the Judiciary Committee, who’s doing an extraordinary job, and Robert Garcia, along with the House Oversight Committee Democrats, who’s done an incredible job in trying to make sure that we are delivering transparency and accountability to the American people. They’re both professionals, and it’s my expectation that the Democrats on these two committees are going to do right by the American people. And that means following the facts, applying the law, being guided by the Constitution and then letting the chips fall where they may.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Coming up, I ask Leader Jeffries who he thinks should lead the top of the Democratic ticket in 2028. Stay with us.

TARA ROSENBLUM: We continue our exclusive conversation now with Hakeem Jeffries, turning our focus to foreign policy and the future of the Democratic Party. Since we’re talking about the future—I know you’re not one to hang up the curtains ahead of time. I know that’s your style—but a number of the Democratic nominees who look poised to win in November, like Darializa Avila Chevalier, have said that, well, they have not yet said that they would support you for Speaker. I know you’ve met with all of them individually as well. In those private conversations, have they indicated to you what it would take to earn their support yet?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we haven’t had that conversation, and I haven’t asked anyone for their support in connection with what may happen on January 3, which will be the date of the new Congress, because I think it’s appropriate for us to focus on getting the job done in terms of what’s in front of us, and that’s winning in what will remain a challenging environment because of the evenly divided nature of the country.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Now we get to have some fun.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Okay.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Let’s talk 2028—

LEADER JEFFRIES: All right.

TARA ROSENBLUM: —and the future of the Democratic Party. I want you to name three people who you think could lead the Democratic presidential ticket. Just three.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s a great question, but the American people are going to make that decision. I’m not going to get out ahead of the American people. I think we’ve got a lot of tremendous candidates, some Governors, some Senators, a few Members of the House who may put their hat into the ring. But until they do so, and nobody is going to declare for the 2028 presidential race until after we get through the midterm elections, I’m going to defer commenting on who hypothetically could lead. We do need a dramatic change, a next-generation Democrat to lead the party forward.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Well, you mentioned next generation, and you mentioned House Members, so that made me think of Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, your fellow New Yorker. You have said that the sky’s the limit for her. Would you like to see her run for the White House, or do you think she should run for Chuck Schumer’s seat if he doesn’t run again?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, she’s going to have to make that decision on her own, which I assume she will over the next few months.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Would she be a good candidate for either of those offices?

LEADER JEFFRIES: She’d be a good candidate for whatever office she decides to run for. She’s an extraordinary leader who has done a great job in the House of Representatives. She’s been a great colleague. She’s led on a whole host of issues that matter to so many different New Yorkers and Americans all across the country. And it’s going to be interesting to see what decision she makes. I assume she’ll make one over the next couple of months.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Do you think Chuck Schumer should run again?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think Chuck Schumer has done a tremendous job in putting the Senate into play when so many people didn’t believe that possible. And now we’re going to take back the House and are on the doorstep of taking back the Senate. And so, I’m not going to get out ahead of any decisions that Chuck Schumer may or may not make.

TARA ROSENBLUM: I recently interviewed Congressman Pat Ryan from the Hudson Valley, and he sure sounded like he was interested in running for Chuck Schumer’s seat if he doesn’t run for reelection, and if AOC doesn’t run. What do you think of him as a candidate?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I haven’t talked to Pat about that, but Pat’s been a great patriot, a combat veteran, a principled next-generation leader, and I think he has a bright future.

TARA ROSENBLUM: I have to get your take now on immigration and specifically the ICE shooting that just happened in our backyard in the Bronx earlier this month. Where do you think the line should be held between immigration enforcement and protecting our immigrant communities?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, ICE is completely and totally out of control. And that’s the reason why, as House Democrats, we’ve made clear that we are not providing a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine. We think that dramatic changes are necessary in order to get the situation turned around with respect to ICE, including ensuring that there are state and local independent investigations so that when the law has been broken, there can actually be accountability. We want to make sure that ICE agents are required to obtain judicial warrants before they can break into any homes, seize any individuals in manners that we believe are often inconsistent with the spirit, or the actual Fourth Amendment. We think that ICE agents should be required to wear body cameras. The masks need to come down.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Ms. Chevalier was at that protest following the shooting and claimed she was thrown to the ground. And just yesterday, she called for Jessica Tisch, the NYPD Commissioner, to resign or be fired. What do you make of her comments?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I certainly support Mayor Mamdani’s leadership, and support his willingness to stick behind Commissioner Jessica Tisch, who I believe has done an extraordinary job in helping to keep the City of New York safe.

TARA ROSENBLUM: And of course, the divisions within your party also extend to Israel. And on October 7, you put out a statement. You said, ‘American policy in the Middle East must change dramatically.’ So what would that look like? Would you support conditioning aid to Israel going forward?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what I support is—we have to lift up two principles at the same time. Israel’s right to exist as a Jewish and democratic state, living side by side in peace and prosperity with an independent Palestinian state, so that we can provide dignity and self-determination to the Palestinian people, which they’ve long sought but have been unable to achieve. I think America needs to reinforce its commitment to a two-state solution in order to achieve a just and lasting peace. And that, to me, is where the overwhelming majority of the American people are at.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Let’s talk about now the recent rape case at Cornell, which has raised questions about how consent is defined and proven. Right now, the legal definition of consent varies state-to-state. Do you believe that there should be a uniform federal definition of sexual consent or a federal law establishing clear standards for sexual assault cases?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think we should take a look at that, and certainly as it applies to what takes place on college campuses and universities all across the country. This is a deeply searing, deeply troubling case. Serious allegations have been raised. It requires a very serious investigation. I have full faith and confidence in Attorney General Tish James and her office to professionally follow the facts and apply the law and make sure that there is justice that is brought to bear.

TARA ROSENBLUM: Coming up, we go beyond politics. A more personal side of Hakeem Jeffries. That’s next.

TARA ROSENBLUM: We’ve spent much of our conversation focused on the future of Congress, but to understand where Hakeem Jeffries may be heading next, we have to look back to where his story began, right here in Brooklyn. So we are sitting here in Shirley Chisholm State Park, and I know you’ve spoken a lot about the outsized influence she had on you as a young boy growing up in Brooklyn. She broke one of the biggest barriers in Congress, and now you could be on the cusp of breaking another. What do you think she would think of where you’re at right now on your journey?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, it’s an honor to stand on the shoulders—the legendary, iconic, heroic shoulders of a great leader like Shirley Chisholm, whose district I now largely represent in Brooklyn. She, of course, broke an extraordinary barrier in becoming the first African American woman ever to serve in the Congress. And she served with courage, with intellect and with boldness. And as I move forward, wherever that may lead, I look forward to continuing to channel, as best I can, her tremendous spirit of service.

TARA ROSENBLUM: And I know your father passed away in 2023 before he could see you reach this point. Your mother, who grew up right in our backyard in Connecticut, also helped shape your values and commitment to public service. If you make history as the first Black Speaker of the House—I could see those words hitting you as I say them—you think that your Dad would be so proud of that moment?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll certainly cross that bridge when we get to it in January. But it’s been a blessing to have been raised by my Mom and Dad here in Brooklyn in a union household, working-class neighborhood in Central Brooklyn, coming of age in the middle of the crack cocaine epidemic, a very difficult time, having grown up in the Cornerstone Baptist Church. And, of course, my Mom and Dad both instilling in my brother and I the value of hard work and caring for others and being community-centered. And so, as I travel along this journey, I know Dad is looking down upon my younger brother and I. And I can take comfort in that.

TARA ROSENBLUM: And now you’re raising two boys of your own. As you take off the politician hat and put on the dad hat, what worries you most about the America that they’re growing up in?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think the big question that has to be resolved for the American people is: Can we keep the American Dream alive?

TARA ROSENBLUM: But for now, Hakeem Jeffries’ political future rests with you, the voters, and in just a few weeks we’ll find out if his next chapter is one for the history books. I’m Tara Rosenblum. Thank you for joining us for this special edition of Power & Politics.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Kelly introduces "Behavioral Health Care Deregulation Act of 2026" to strengthen mental health support for American seniors
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Representative Mike Kelly (R-PA), a Co-Chair of the Congressional Mental Health Caucus, introduced the Behavioral Health Care Deregulation Act of 2026. This legislation improves mental health care and accessibility for Medicare recipients.

According to a 2025 report from the National Council on Aging, "One in five Americans will experience it in their lifetime. And nearly 15% of adults age 50 and older have some type of mental health disorder."

"As more Americans seek mental health treatment, it's important for Congress to address these critical issues as well. The Behavioral Health Care Deregulation Act cuts both the red tape and the stigma surrounding mental health care to ensure American seniors have the care they need in their golden years," said Rep. Kelly.

BACKGROUND

The Behavioral Health Care Deregulation Act of 2026:

Repeals Medicare’s 190-day lifetime limit on inpatient psychiatric hospital services.

Eliminates cost-sharing (coinsurance/deductibles) for inpatient psychiatric services for individuals admitted under state involuntary commitment orders.

Repeals specific administrative and regulatory requirements for inpatient psychiatric facilities to reduce provider burden.

Temporarily boosts Medicare reimbursement for Behavioral Health Integration (BHI) codes (175% in 2027, 150% in 2028, 125% in 2029) and waives budget neutrality for these increases.

Directs HHS to provide technical assistance and funding to help primary care practices adopt integration models starting January 1, 2027.

title: Following DHS’s Disclosure of Nearly $17 Million Expansion, Kennedy Makes Unannounced Visit to ICE Batavia Facility to Inspect Conditions and Conduct Oversight
text:
Kennedy Questions ICE Officials and Witnesses State of the Facility and its Detainees Firsthand

BUFFALO, N.Y. - After receiving written confirmation from Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin that ICE is proceeding with a nearly $17 million expansion at their Batavia facility, Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) made an unannounced visit to the Service Processing Center to witness firsthand the wellbeing of detainees, conditions of the facility, and to inspect the expansion. DHS held 653 individuals at Batavia as of July 2026 and has begun construction to create a new detention facility for women. DHS noted that, depending on the need, men may be housed in the new facility as well. More than 70% of the detainees at Batavia have no criminal history.

However, several questions about the expansion, medical care, and the treatment of detainees remained unanswered. Following his visit, Congressman Kennedy, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, sent a letter to DHS seeking additional information about the planned expansion, the availability of adequate medical care, the number and circumstances of individuals being detained, and policies impeding access to legal representation. The letter calls for greater transparency and accountability as DHS moves forward with its plans for the facility.

“Conducting oversight of federal agencies is one of my fundamental responsibilities in Congress, and I will not allow a nearly $17 million expansion of a federal detention facility to move forward without demanding answers. I went to Batavia to see the conditions firsthand, ask questions, and get clear answers about the planned expansion, medical care, and the treatment of detainees. When questions about medical care, the treatment of detainees, and access to legal representation remain, DHS has a responsibility to provide clear answers,” said Congressman Kennedy. “I will continue pressing for transparency and accountability to ensure taxpayer dollars are being spent responsibly and the basic needs of those in federal custody are being met.”

Pursuant to Section 527 of the FY2024 DHS Appropriations Act, DHS is legally obligated to allow Members of Congress to inspect detainee facilities without prior notice. This law has been upheld in federal court in the case of Neguse et al v. U.S. ICE et al.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Rep. Laurel Lee Joins Rep. Maxwell Frost to Introduce Bipartisan SLOTHS Act to Protect Vulnerable Wildlife
text:
Sanford, FL – Today, on International Sloth Day, Congresswoman Laurel Lee (FL-15) joined Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) at the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens to announce the introduction of the bipartisan Stopping Legalized Organized Trafficking and Harm to Sloths (SLOTHS) Act, legislation to prohibit the importation of sloths into the United States while preserving limited exceptions for legitimate research and accredited conservation breeding programs.

The legislation comes following a series of investigations into the deaths of more than 50 sloths connected to Sloth World, a planned Orlando tourist attraction that imported wild sloths from South America for commercial display. Investigative reporting by Inside Climate News first revealed the deaths in April, raising serious concerns about the conditions in which the animals were housed and the risks associated with transporting sloths from their natural habitats.

State records documented the deaths of 31 sloths between December 2024 and February 2025, including animals housed at a facility without running water or electricity. Subsequent investigations and reporting revealed that the death toll had risen to more than 50. Despite these findings, the Orange County Sheriff's Office concluded its investigation in August without finding evidence of criminal wrongdoing.

“More than 50 sloths died in Orlando, yet investigators found no violation of existing laws. That outcome should make all of us take a hard look at whether our laws are doing enough to protect these animals,”said Congresswoman Laurel Lee. “The bipartisan SLOTHS Act is a responsible step to prevent further harm by prohibiting sloth imports, with exceptions for legitimate research and accredited conservation breeding programs. I appreciate Congressman Frost's partnership and the advocates whose work brought this issue to light.”

“We owe it to these animals, and to the people in our community who spoke up, to make sure a tragedy like this never happens again,” said Congressman Frost. “Sloths have highly specialized needs, and their care requires scientific expertise and accountability. The bipartisan SLOTHS Act is an important step toward protecting these vulnerable animals and ensuring their welfare comes first.”

“I am grateful to see bipartisan legislation being filed in the United States Congress to protect wildlife and prevent the importation of wild-caught sloths into the United States. Wild animals deserve to live in the wild, free from human profit and exploitation,”said State Representative Anna Eskamani.“We'll continue to advocate for animal welfare at the state and local level as we support this federal effort.”

"The Association of Zoos and Aquariums commends Representatives Maxwell Frost and Laurel Lee for their leadership in protecting vulnerable wild sloth populations from unethical exploitation. The SLOTHS Act will restrict and penalize bad actors while ensuring the vital conservation initiatives of credible institutions can continue," saidDan Ashe, President and CEO of AZA. "On behalf of AZA, we thank Representatives Frost and Lee for their bipartisan proposal and proudly support this effort to safeguard sloth species."

“The exotic pet trade and wildlife tourism industry treat sloths as novelties, but sloths are fragile wild animals that suffer and often die when removed from their native habitats," said Kate Dylewsky, Assistant Director of Government Affairs, Animal Welfare Institute."Restricting the importation of sloths into the U.S. will help curb the demand that drives the trade in these animals and protect them from a life of suffering. The Animal Welfare Institute applauds Representatives Frost and Lee for introducing the SLOTHS Act.”

“After the deaths of 58 sloths at Sloth World, we made a promise to do everything in our power to make sure something like this could never happen again - and we meant it. But Sloth World was just the tip of the iceberg. It exposed a cruel and unnecessary trade in which hundreds of wild sloths are captured and sold as commodities every year, despite a mortality rate of up to 90%. The SLOTHS Act is an opportunity to finally draw a line and say that this is not acceptable," saidDr. Rebecca Cliffe, Founder and Executive Director, The Sloth Conservation Foundation. "By closing the door on the importation of wild-caught sloths into the United States we can stop this cruelty at its source. We cannot undo the suffering of the sloths already caught up in this trade, but we can make sure their suffering was not in vain. We made a promise, and we will not stop fighting until this trade is brought to an end. We are so grateful to Representatives Frost and Lee for standing alongside us and taking action to help make that promise a reality.”

“As sloths have grown more popular, so has their suffering. Sloth lovers are paying to interact with sloths, unaware they are contributing to a cruel industry. Most of these animals are ripped from the wild to endure inadequate living conditions and often painful deaths. The SLOTHS Act is a vital step toward ending this suffering," saidSam Trull, MSc - Co-founder and Executive Director, The Sloth Institute. "I am incredibly grateful to Representatives Frost and Lee for introducing this legislation to stop the removal of sloths from the wild for commercial import. Sloths belong in the rainforest, and the American people deserve to stop being misled.”

"What makes sloths so loveable also makes them targets for exploitation. Behind those sweet faces and slow movements lie complex life histories, long gestation periods, and specific environmental requirements. That's why the Stopping Legalized Organized Trafficking and Harm to Sloths (SLOTHS) Act's ban on importation into the US is so important," saidDanielle Kessler, US Director, International Fund for Animal Welfare. "Congressman Frost and Congresswoman Lee are taking the initiative to help keep these cherished animals in the wild and out of a cruel trade driven by the desire for pets and selfies. Sloths deserve more than the inhumane fate that awaits them in the name of entertainment."

"The Sloth World disaster is a devastating reminder of the suffering wild animals endure because of lax oversight and inadequate legal protections. Dozens of sloths died, yet authorities found that no laws had been violated," said Alicia Prygoski, Strategic Legislative Affairs Manager with the Animal Legal Defense Fund. "Prohibiting the import of wild sloths is a critical step toward preventing future tragedies and protecting these remarkable animals from exploitation. We commend Congressman Frost and Congresswoman Lee for championing this important legislation."

Sloths are particularly vulnerable to the stresses associated with international transportation and captivity. Their specialized diets, sensitivity to environmental changes, and unique physiological needs make proper care essential to their survival. The circumstances at Sloth World have raised broader concerns about the international trade of wild sloths and the need for stronger safeguards to prevent similar incidents.

The SLOTHS Act would:

Prohibit the importation of sloths into the United States, addressing the commercial demand that contributes to the international trade in these vulnerable animals.

Preserve limited exceptions for legitimate scientific research, including the importation of deceased sloths for documented research purposes.

Protect accredited conservation breeding programs by permitting eligible captive sloths to be transferred to Association of Zoos and Aquariums-accredited institutions, provided the animals were not taken from the wild after enactment.

Establish penalties for violations, including civil penalties of up to $20,000, criminal fines of up to $100,000 for knowing violations, cancellation of applicable federal authorizations, and forfeiture of illegally imported sloths.

Following the closure of Sloth World, the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens took in the facility's remaining sloths and provided specialized veterinary care. The zoo's involvement, along with the work of animal welfare advocates and conservation experts, helped draw attention to the challenges facing sloths in the commercial wildlife trade.

The SLOTHS Act has received support from the Sloth Conservation Foundation, the Sloth Institute, the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, the Association of Zoos and Aquariums, the Animal Welfare Institute, the Animal Legal Defense Fund, and the International Fund for Animal Welfare.

The legislation represents a bipartisan effort to address the risks associated with importing sloths into the United States while ensuring that qualified conservation and research institutions can continue their important work.

title: Bay Area Congressional Democrats Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to SFO Airport Detention Facility
text:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Today, Representatives Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jared Huffman (CA-02), and Aisha Wahab (CA-14) made an unannounced visit to inspect the detention facility being operated by Customs and Border Protection (CBP) at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). The facility has received scrutiny for some detainees being held for days, including lawful permanent residents.

“We are at SFO today to fulfill our responsibility as Members of Congress to conduct oversight and ensure that individuals in federal custody are being treated in accordance with the law,” the Members said. “There have been concerning reports of some people being detained for multiple days in a facility that was not designed for that purpose."

The Members were granted access to the facility with no advanced notice, as federal courts have upheld the authority of Congress to inspect federal immigration detention facilities.

Rep. Mullin was the first Member of Congress to visit the facility, located in his district, in August. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) have also visited the SFO facility this month. Rep. Sam Liccardo’s (CA-16) office supported the visit, but the Congressman was unable to attend in person. In June, Reps. Lofgren and Mullin also inspected the California City Detention Center, the largest ICE facility being operated in the state.

title: Harris Announces $1.9 Million Federal Grant to Combat Fraud in North Carolina
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) announced that the North Carolina Office of the State Auditor has been awarded approximately $1.9 million in federal funding through the Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance FY 2026 Special Attorneys Program. Harris helped secure the funding by joining a letter of support led by Senator Ted Budd alongside members of North Carolina’s congressional delegation. The funding will strengthen North Carolina’s ability to investigate fraud and hold wrongdoers accountable.

“North Carolina taxpayers work hard for every dollar they earn, and they deserve to know their money is being protected,” said Congressman Harris. “I’m proud to have supported this grant and grateful for State Auditor Dave Boliek’s leadership in rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse. Those who cheat the system must be held accountable, and this funding will help bring them to justice.”

In a letter thanking Congressman Harris for his support, North Carolina State Auditor Dave Boliek emphasized the impact the grant will have on his office’s investigative capabilities.

“This funding will significantly strengthen our ability to identify and investigate fraud involving public funds, coordinate with state and federal partners, support complex case development, and pursue appropriate enforcement actions,” Boliek wrote.

title: McBath Bill to Stop Human Trafficking Signed Into Law
text:
Atlanta, GA – Bipartisan legislation led by Rep. Lucy McBath (D-GA) and House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-MI) has been signed into law. H.R. 4307, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, strengthens the Department of Labor’s ability to identify signs of human trafficking and refer suspected cases to law enforcement. It marks McBath’s 13th piece of legislation to become law.

“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that too often goes unnoticed in workplaces and communities across the country,” said Rep. McBath. “We are giving Department of Labor employees the training and tools they need to recognize warning signs, help protect vulnerable individuals, and support efforts to hold traffickers accountable. I’m proud to see our bipartisan legislation signed into law and grateful to my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for their partnership in advancing this important measure.”

The Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act:

Provides Department of Labor employees with training to identify indicators of human trafficking during workplace inspections and investigations.

Establishes procedures for referring suspected trafficking cases to law enforcement.

Strengthens federal efforts to detect trafficking, protect victims, and prevent exploitation.

title: Rep. McDowell, Sen. Moran Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Recognizing Red Ribbon Week
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Addison McDowell (NC-06) and U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) introduced resolutions recognizing Red Ribbon Week from October 23 to October 31, 2026.

Red Ribbon Week is the nation's largest and longest-running drug prevention program. It raises awareness of the dangers of illicit drugs, promotes drug prevention efforts, and recognizes the law enforcement officers who work to keep communities across the country safe.

“I lost my little brother Luke to fentanyl, and I know firsthand the devastating toll these deadly drugs take on families,” said Rep. McDowell. “Red Ribbon Week is an important reminder that prevention starts with education, strong families, and supporting the men and women in law enforcement who work every day to keep our communities safe. We owe it to the next generation to do everything we can to prevent another family from experiencing that same heartbreak mine did.”

“Drug overdoses remain a leading cause of death in our nation, underscoring the importance of investing in efforts to fight illicit drugs and raise awareness about the dangers of drug use,” said Sen. Moran. “Red Ribbon Week provides the opportunity to educate others on the risks of illicit drugs, support prevention efforts and recognize the law enforcement officers who work every day to keep Kansans safe. I will continue working to combat illegal drugs and make certain that law enforcement is equipped with the resources needed to protect our communities and stem the flow of illegal drugs.”

Background:

Established nationally in 1988 by the National Family Partnership, Red Ribbon Week honors the memory of Enrique “Kiki” Camarena, a Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) special agent murdered in 1985 while working to combat illicit drug trafficking.

Today, Red Ribbon Week serves as a nationwide call to action, encouraging families, schools, and communities to educate young Americans about the dangers of drug use and promote drug-free lifestyles.

title: Rep. Mejia Denounces Israeli Detention of Constituent in West Bank
text:
For Immediate Release: October 21, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Glen Ridge, New Jersey — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) issued the following statement following the detention of a constituent of New Jersey’s 11th Congressional District, Dr. Alan Gordon, who was held for over seven hours by Israeli forces while peacefully assisting Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. Dr. Gordon was detained alongside American rabbis and advocates, including congressional candidate Brad Lander, and has since been released.

“I am relieved that Dr. Gordon and his fellow advocates have been released. Upon learning of his detention, my office immediately contacted the U.S. Department of State to advocate for his release. But let's be clear: The problem in the West Bank is not peaceful volunteers helping Palestinian families harvest their crops. It is violent settlers terrorizing Palestinian communities with the backing and protection of the Netanyahu government.

These volunteers traveled thousands of miles to stand alongside Palestinian farmers facing threats of violence, intimidation, and displacement. Instead of protecting these families from settler attacks, Israeli forces detained the very people trying to keep them safe. That is an outrageous abuse of power, and I unequivocally condemn it.

For generations, Palestinian families have cultivated this land, relying on their olive harvests to sustain their livelihoods. They should not need international volunteers to protect them from violence simply to harvest their own crops. Yet Netanyahu’s government continues to embolden violent settlers, expand illegal settlements, and use military force to deepen an occupation that denies Palestinians their fundamental rights.

I will continue to demand accountability for settler violence, freedom for those unjustly detained, and an end to the illegal occupation and annexation of Palestinian territory. A just and lasting peace demands more than words. It demands an end to displacement, an end to impunity, and a future where Israelis and Palestinians can live with freedom, dignity, and security,” said Congresswoman Mejia.

title: THOMPSON CALLS ON USDA TO GUARANTEE CALIFORNIA SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS RECEIVE FAIR SHARE OF $8 BILLION IN FUEL RELIEF
text:
Napa, CA – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) is demanding the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) provide clear guidance on how specialty crop producers will access USDA’s newly announced $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program and deliver fair assistance to farmers to offset rising fuel and production costs.

Announced on October 19, the program is said to provide one-time payments to farmers to help address market disruptions and increased input costs during the 2026 crop year from the Iran war and trade war. While USDA plans to release payment rates for major commodity crops in November, the department has yet to announce how payments will be determined for specialty crop producers.

“California’s specialty crop growers are facing rising fuel prices and higher production costs, and they deserve a fair shot at this assistance,” said Thompson. “Our fruit, vegetable, nut, and winegrape growers are essential to California’s agricultural economy. USDA needs to ensure that relief reflects the real costs of growing their crops and that these farmers aren’t left behind.”

In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, Thompson is requesting clarification on how specialty crop producers can access the program and how increased fuel costs will factor into payment calculations. USDA has encouraged specialty crop growers and other producers of non-Title I commodities to submit information about increased fuel costs for consideration when determining payment rates.

Thompson also raised concerns that previous federal assistance for specialty crop producers failed to adequately address their financial challenges. Specialty crop growers often face substantially higher per-acre production costs than traditional commodity producers and need assistance that reflects the unique expenses of their operations.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

The Honorable Brooke Rollins

Secretary

U.S. Department of Agriculture

1400 Independence Avenue, SW

Washington, DC 20250

Dear Secretary Rollins:

I am writing regarding the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) October 19, 2026 announcement of $8 billion in assistance through the Harvest Fuel Relief (HRF) Program to seek clarification on how specialty crop producers will be able to access this funding and to urge USDA to ensure that all agricultural producers receive equitable assistance.

Farmers across my district are facing significant financial pressures from rising fuel costs, increased production expenses, and continued market uncertainties. These challenges are particularly acute for specialty crop producers, including the growers of fruits, vegetables, nuts, and winegrapes who are essential to the California agricultural economy. While I appreciate the recognition of the need for additional assistance, it is critical that specialty crop producers are not once again left receiving disproportionately less assistance than other agricultural producers.

Earlier this year, USDA provided assistance to specialty crop growers through the Assistance for Specialty Crops Farmers program, following the announcement of the Farmer Bridge Assistance (FBA) Program. Unfortunately, the funding made available to specialty crop producers was insufficient to address the significant financial challenges facing these operations. Many specialty crop growers face substantially higher per-acre production costs than traditional commodity producers. The assistance provided did not adequately reflect these costs or the economic losses these producers have experienced.

USDA’s announcement indicates that payment rates for Title I commodities will be released in November, while the methodology for other eligible commodities will be announced at a later date. I am concerned that this approach could once again leave specialty crop producers with uncertainty about whether they will receive meaningful assistance and how that assistance will compare with payments to other producers.

Specialty crop growers deserve the same consideration and equitable access to federal assistance as producers of traditional row crops. While payment rates should account for differences in production costs and economic losses across commodities, no producer should receive less adequate compensation simply because of the type of crop they grow.

I strongly urge USDA to provide clear guidance to specialty crop producers as soon as possible and ensure that funding is distributed fairly across the agricultural industry. Relief should be based on the actual financial challenges facing farmers, not on whether they grow a traditional commodity or a specialty crop.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter. I look forward to your prompt response.

Sincerely,

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

title: THOMPSON DEMANDS ANSWERS FOLLOWING WOODLAND INCIDENT: “ICE IS NOT ABOVE THE LAW”
text:
Woodland, CA – On Tuesday, Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) contacted Acting Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) David Venturella to demand answers following reports that a vehicle operated by ICE personnel struck a pedestrian in Woodland.

“I demand that ICE immediately investigate this incident, fully cooperate with local law enforcement, and ensure that any individuals found to have engaged in misconduct or unlawful behavior are held accountable,” wrote Thompson.

“ICE is not above the law. Its actions have contributed to growing distrust and fear within our communities, making transparency and accountability all the more critical. Federal law enforcement officers must be held to the same standards of accountability as those they are sworn to enforce. Anything less undermines public trust and the rule of law,” he continued.

Thompson also demanded ICE immediately provide the following information to Thompson and his office’s counsel:

A preliminary account of the incident, including the circumstances surrounding the reported collision and whether the pedestrian sustained injuries.

Confirmation that ICE has initiated an investigation and referred the matter to the appropriate oversight authorities.

A description of the steps ICE has taken to cooperate with local law enforcement and preserve relevant evidence.

An explanation of the policies governing the operation of ICE vehicles during enforcement activities and how compliance with those policies will be evaluated in this case.

In addition to contacting Acting Director Venturella, Thompson remains in close communication with local law enforcement and local elected officials as more information becomes available.

Read the full text of Thompson’s letter here and below.

--

The Honorable David Venturella

Acting Director

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement

500 12th Street, SW

Washington, D.C. 20536

Dear Mr. Venturella:

I write to convey my serious concern regarding reports that a vehicle operated by U.S.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel struck a pedestrian in Woodland, California, on October 20, 2026. I demand that ICE immediately investigate this incident, fully cooperate with local law enforcement, and ensure that any individuals found to have engaged in misconduct or unlawful behavior are held accountable.

The safety of our communities must always come first. Federal law enforcement officers have a responsibility to protect public safety, exercise sound judgment, and uphold the law. When an incident involving federal personnel potentially endangers or injures a member of the public, the American people deserve a thorough, impartial investigation and a clear accounting of what occurred.

Accordingly, I request that ICE immediately refer this incident to the appropriate independent investigative authorities. ICE must also fully cooperate with the Woodland Police Department, the Yolo County District Attorney's Office, and any other state or local authorities with jurisdiction over this incident. This cooperation must include making relevant personnel available for interviews and providing access to evidence, including vehicle recordings, bodyworn camera footage, communications, and incident reports, as legally appropriate.

I also expect ICE to take immediate steps to preserve all evidence related to this incident and ensure that its personnel do not interfere with any independent investigation. If the investigation determines that a federal agent violated the law, departmental policy, or applicable standards of conduct, appropriate disciplinary action must follow, including referral for criminal prosecution where warranted.

To that end, I request that ICE provide my office with the following information:

A preliminary account of the incident, including the circumstances surrounding the reported collision and whether the pedestrian sustained injuries.

Confirmation that ICE has initiated an investigation and referred the matter to the appropriate oversight authorities.

A description of the steps ICE has taken to cooperate with local law enforcement and preserve relevant evidence.

An explanation of the policies governing the operation of ICE vehicles during enforcement activities and how compliance with those policies will be evaluated in this case.

ICE is not above the law. Its actions have contributed to growing distrust and fear within our communities, making transparency and accountability all the more critical. Federal law enforcement officers must be held to the same standards of accountability as those they are sworn to enforce. Anything less undermines public trust and the rule of law.

I request an initial response within seven days and continued updates as the investigation proceeds. I expect ICE's full cooperation in establishing the facts and ensuring accountability. To coordinate a response to this letter, please contact my counsel, Eric Hoffman, at eric.hoffman@mail.house.gov in my Washington, D.C., office.

Sincerely,

Mike Thompson

Member of Congress

title: THOMPSON LEADS WAYS AND MEANS DEMOCRATS IN DEMANDING IRS RELEASE WITHHELD DATA
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), Ranking Member of the House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax, announced that he led ten Ways and Means Democrats in demanding that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent explain why the Administration has failed to release critical IRS tax return data following the 2026 filing season. The lawmakers raised concerns that the Administration is withholding information that could reveal who is benefiting from Congressional Republicans’ tax law, which disproportionately benefits wealthy Americans.

“Congressional Republicans have spent months bragging about their tax law, but now that it's time to show Americans who is actually benefiting, the Administration is keeping the numbers hidden,” said Thompson. “The nonpartisan Joint Committee on Taxation projected that nearly two-thirds of the tax benefits would go to people making over $200,000 a year. If Congressional Republicans are so proud of their tax law, why won't they release the data? Americans deserve to know whether their tax dollars are helping working families or padding the pockets of the wealthy. The Administration needs to stop hiding the ball and release the numbers.”

According to recent reporting by POLITICO, detailed IRS tax return statistics originally scheduled for publication in July, with updated statistics expected in September, remain unreleased. The IRS reportedly transmitted the information to the Treasury Department and is awaiting approval to make it public. Meanwhile, the Administration has continued to publicize aggregate tax filing statistics that support its claims about the law.

The delayed data is particularly concerning following the passage of Republicans’ H.R. 1 tax law. According to an analysis by the nonpartisan Joint Committee on Taxation, taxpayers earning $200,000 or more were projected to receive approximately $337.6 billion in net federal tax reductions in 2027, representing roughly 62 percent of the $547.4 billion in tax reductions analyzed. Millionaires alone were projected to receive $114 billion.

In their letter, the lawmakers demanded that Treasury explain which statistical releases have been delayed, who is responsible for approving their publication, and whether any officials at the IRS, Treasury, or White House requested that the information be withheld for reasons unrelated to statistical accuracy or taxpayer confidentiality. They also called for the immediate publication of completed datasets and a schedule for releasing information showing how tax benefits are distributed across income levels.

“The Administration has found ample opportunity to celebrate its tax law. It should be equally willing to publish the numbers,” the lawmakers wrote. “Apparently, its enthusiasm for tax data diminishes when the numbers might invite scrutiny.”

The lawmakers requested a response from Treasury Secretary Bessent by October 28, 2026.

Joining Thompson in the letter were Representatives Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Danny K. Davis (IL-07), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Don Beyer (VA-08), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), and Steven Horsford (NV-04).

The full letter can be found here and below:

The Honorable Scott Bessent

Secretary

United States Department of the Treasury

1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW

Washington, D.C. 20220

Dear Secretary Bessent:

We write as Democratic Members of the Committee on Ways and Means to request an explanation for the continued delay in publishing detailed Internal Revenue Service (IRS) statistics following the 2026 tax filing season. This data is essential to understanding who is receiving tax benefits, evaluating changes needed to the tax code, and conducting meaningful congressional oversight. The Administration has found ample opportunity to celebrate its tax law. It should be equally willing to publish the numbers.

According to recent reporting by POLITICO, tax return statistics scheduled for release in July, followed by updated statistics in September, remain unpublished. The IRS reportedly provided the data to the Department of the Treasury and is awaiting approval to release them. Meanwhile, the Administration has readily promoted aggregate filing season statistics that support its preferred narrative. Apparently, its enthusiasm for tax data diminishes when the numbers might invite scrutiny.

The missing information is particularly important following enactment of H.R. 1, Public Law 119-21. The nonpartisan Joint Committee on Taxation’s July 29, 2025, distributional analysis, JCX-37-25, projected that taxpayers with incomes of $200,000 or more would receive approximately $337.6 billion of the $547.4 billion net federal tax reduction in 2027 attributable to the provisions analyzed, roughly 62 percent. Taxpayers with incomes of $1 million or more alone would receive $114 billion. These projections underscore why Congress needs timely information about who is claiming the law’s benefits as its provisions take effect.

If the Administration believes the evidence vindicates its claims, then you should publish the data.

title: Miller-Meeks Bill to Bring Manufacturing Jobs Back to Iowa Becomes Law

title: Murphy Hosts Successful Fifth Annual North Carolina WATERS Summit
text:

The purpose of this nonpartisan conference was to examine human adaptation strategies to waterway challenges in North Carolina and develop legislative plans to combat these challenges over the next 5, 25, and 100 years. title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Holds Veterans Town Hall
text:

title: Olszewski to Introduce “Direct Democracy” Constitutional Amendment to Create National Referendum Process for American Public
text:
(Washington, DC) — Congressman Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) tomorrow will introduce a constitutional amendment that would establish a national “direct democracy” process, giving Americans a new way to propose and enact federal laws when Congress fails to advance issues with broad public support.

Across the country, Americans agree on more than our politics often suggests. For example, overwhelming majorities support banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, requiring insurance to cover fertility treatment and requiring police officers to wear body cameras. Yet even when most Americans agree on an issue, turning that consensus into federal action can take years — if it ever happens at all.

Olszewski’s amendment would empower citizens with a constitutional avenue to pass or repeal laws when an increasingly politicized Congress refuses to take action on issues that enjoy overwhelming consensus.

“As a former social studies teacher, I believe deeply in representative democracy — but I also believe democracy works best when people have a meaningful voice in their government,” Congressman Olszewski said. “Too many Americans feel that policy change is too slow and that it is too heavily influenced by entrenched interests. My amendment reimagines and reinvigorates our American democracy to turn consensus into action.”

Under Olszewski’s proposal, citizens could propose a new federal law or repeal an existing federal statute by:

Gathering signatures equal to at least 5 percent of voters who participated in the most recent presidential election nationwide in at least 25 states;

Completing the signature-gathering process within an 18 month window;

Having the signatures independently verified;

Placing the proposal on the ballot at the next eligible national election; and

Securing approval from at least 60 percent of voters nationwide.

If approved by voters, the measure would automatically become federal law — or repeal an existing federal law — without requiring Congressional action or the President’s signature.

The ambitious criteria ensures that the process is reserved for proposals with significant and geographically widespread support, rather than narrow or fleeting public interests.

“The goal isn't to replace Congress — it’s to give the American people a constitutional backstop to a paralyzed Washington,” Olszewski said. “If Americans across the country organize, meet a rigorous threshold, and also vote by a supermajority to enact a law, their voice should matter.”

The amendment would require a two-thirds vote in Congress and ratification by three-fourths of the states before taking effect.

This is the third constitutional amendment proposed by Congressman Olszewski to promote accountability and strengthen the checks and balances foundational to our democracy. His ROBE Act would create 18-year term limits for Supreme County justices and his Pardon Integrity Act would enable Congress to override egregious presidential pardons.

title: Pallone Unveils Lifesaving Defibrillator at Perth Amboy Youth Sports Complex
text:
PERTH AMBOY, NJ – Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) joined Perth Amboy Mayor Helmin Caba, state lawmakers, and local advocates today to unveil a new automated external defibrillator (AED) and temperature-controlled SaveStation at the Veterans Memorial Youth Complex, giving young athletes access to lifesaving equipment in the event of a cardiac emergency.

The AED and SaveStation were donated by the John Taylor Babbitt Foundation during Sudden Cardiac Arrest Awareness Month, with support from the Sarah Katz Foundation and local advocates. The temperature-controlled station is designed to protect the equipment from the elements and make it accessible when an emergency occurs.

“When a young athlete suffers cardiac arrest on the field or court, every second matters, and having an AED nearby can mean the difference between life and death,” said Pallone. “I want to thank the John Taylor Babbitt Foundation for generously donating this lifesaving equipment and the Sarah Katz Foundation for its advocacy and support. More than 15 years ago, we lost Kittim Sherrod during track practice in Edison, and his tragic death inspired me to write the HEARTS Act, which I am proud to say is finally the law. That law will help schools get AEDs, train students and staff in CPR, and prepare for cardiac emergencies before they happen.”

Pallone has long championed efforts to prevent sudden cardiac deaths among young athletes. After 17 year old Edison High School athlete Kittim Sherrod died from cardiac arrest during track practice in 2009, Pallone authored legislation to expand access to AEDs and CPR training in schools. That effort ultimately led to the bipartisan HEARTS Act, which was signed into law by President Biden in December 2024.

The HEARTS Act, formally known as the Cardiomyopathy Health, Education, Awareness, Research, and Training in Schools Act, establishes a federal grant program to help schools and childcare centers obtain AEDs, provide CPR and AED training, and develop plans to respond to cardiac emergencies. The law also supports public education efforts to raise awareness of cardiomyopathy and sudden cardiac arrest, conditions that can strike young people without warning. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates that approximately 2,000 Americans under age 25 die from sudden cardiac arrest each year.

The unveiling brought together Pallone, Assemblywoman Yvonne Lopez, Perth Amboy Mayor Helmin Caba, David and JoAnne Babbitt of the John Taylor Babbitt Foundation, Mike and Jill Katz of the Sarah Katz Foundation, and Mike Papale of the In A Heartbeat Foundation, all united in their commitment to preventing sudden cardiac deaths.

The new equipment at Veterans Memorial Youth Complex, located at 500 Dorothy Avenue in Perth Amboy, will help ensure that young athletes and community members have access to an AED when seconds count.

“What Dave and JoAnne Babbitt have done in memory of their son, John Taylor, means a great deal to our community. Through their foundation, they're helping make sure other families have access to lifesaving equipment when every second counts. We're grateful for their generosity and for Congressman Pallone's leadership on the HEARTS Act and his continued efforts to make AEDs more accessible. As we welcome more children and families to our Veterans Memorial Youth Complex, knowing this equipment is available gives us one more way to help keep them safe. I hope we never need it, but I'm grateful it's here,” Mayor Caba.

“Sudden cardiac arrest remains a major public health crisis. Approximately 350,000 out of hospital cardiac arrests events occur annually in the U.S., with nearly 90% fatality. Survival may be 40-70% or higher for an out of hospital witnessed cardiac arrest with CPR started immediately and an AED delivering a shock within five minutes. It is the goal of the John Taylor Babbitt Foundation to train as many people as possible in CPR and AED usage and donate AED's to ensure communities like Perth Amboy are "Heart Safe". Immediate bystander response to sudden cardiac arrest events is critical. The John Taylor Babbitt Foundation has donated over 850 AED's and supported CPR training for over 8,000 people since its inception in 2006,” David and JoAnne Babbitt of the John Taylor Babbitt Foundation.
