title: CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES DESIGNATION OF CHARLOTTE AMALIE AS AN AMERICAN WORLD WAR II HERITAGE CITY
text:
For Immediate Release Contact: Tionee Scotland

October 21, 2026 202-808-6129

PRESS RELEASE

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES DESIGNATION OF CHARLOTTE AMALIE AS AN AMERICAN WORLD WAR II HERITAGE CITY

U.S. Virgin Islands — Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett (D-VI) issued the following statement after the National Park Service designated Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas, as an American World War II Heritage City on October 16, 2026. The designation recognizes the contributions of the people of the U.S. Virgin Islands to the nation’s World War II effort and the community’s work to preserve that history. Congresswoman Plaskett supported the nomination in an April 2026 letter to the National Park Service.

“I commend the Virgin Islands State Historic Preservation Office, the St. Thomas Historical Trust, our veterans’ organizations, and every community member who has worked to document, protect, and teach this history. Their efforts ensure that the sacrifices of that generation of Virgin Islanders remain part of who we are,” said Congresswoman Plaskett.

“This designation recognizes the service of Virgin Islanders during World War II, and it is long overdue,” said Congresswoman Plaskett. “I was proud to submit a letter to the National Park Service in support of Charlotte Amalie’s nomination. St. Thomas was a critical line of defense for the Caribbean and the Atlantic, protecting the shipping routes that sustained the Allied war effort. Virgin Islanders enlisted in the armed forces and built and staffed the installations that protected our waters. At home, residents observed rationing and blackout orders and manned air-raid posts. They did all of this while serving a country in which they lacked full representation. That record of service has never been forgotten in the Virgin Islands, and today the nation formally recognizes it.

“I thank the National Park Service for acknowledging Charlotte Amalie’s place in the American story. This honor belongs to our veterans, their families, every Virgin Islander who answered the call, and the community that has preserved this history,” Congresswoman Plaskett continued.

The Virgin Islands’ strategic importance to United States national security predates the war. In 1917, the United States purchased the Danish West Indies from Denmark to deny Germany a foothold in the Caribbean. By the time the United States entered World War II, Charlotte Amalie’s harbor had become a key hub for refueling, repairs, and logistical support. The U.S. Navy established a submarine base at Little Krum Bay, while Bourne Field and the seaplane base at Lindbergh Bay supported air patrols that tracked German submarine activity. A naval hospital, a communications center at Fort Christian, Marine Corps barracks, and coastal defenses on Water Island and Hassel Island completed an integrated military installation that helped protect vital supply routes through the Caribbean and to the Panama Canal.

Charlotte Amalie continues to honor its World War II heritage through historic preservation initiatives, memorials, educational programs, and commemorative events. The Virgin Islands State Historic Preservation Office documents and protects wartime military sites, including the former submarine base and historic harbor facilities. The Virgin Islands Veterans Memorial in Roosevelt Park and Veterans Drive along the waterfront honor those who served, and annual Veterans Day, Memorial Day, and Transfer Day commemorations keep this history alive.

The American World War II Heritage City program, administered by the National Park Service, was created in 2019 by the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act. The law allows the Secretary of the Interior to bestow this honorary designation on only one city or local jurisdiction in each state and territory.

title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Hosts Community Leaders for Listening Session on TPS for El Salvador
text:
LOS ANGELES – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) hosted community leaders and El Salvador Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders about the issues affecting the Salvadoran population. The conversation focused on the experiences, concerns, and priorities of the Salvadoran community in the San Fernando Valley. As of October 21, 2026, Salvadoran TPS holders continue to face uncertainty about their long-term immigration status, employment authorization, and ability to remain with their families in the United States.

“Thanks to the TPS designation for El Salvador, Salvadoran immigrants have built their lives, raised their families, and strengthened their communities here in the San Fernando Valley and across the United States – for many, the United States is the only country they have ever called home,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “Not only is the Trump Administration’s decision to force Salvadorans into legal limbo is not only heartless, but it is also harmful to communities across the country. Salvadoran immigrants fuel America’s success, and the extension of TPS would provide them the relief and the opportunity to continue strengthening our nation. I want to thank everyone who joined me for a productive listening session on how we can work together to protect TPS for the Salvadoran community. I will continue working with my colleagues to ensure the United States continues to uphold our nation’s values to uplift all who seek a better life in our country.”

Background:

Congresswoman Rivas invited leaders and representatives from Immigo, CARECEN, Arleta Neighbors in Action, One LA-IAF, and the Family Support Center Coordinator at Pacoima Charter School for a listening session on the issues Salvadoran TPS holders are currently facing.

Salvadorans are the third largest group of TPS holders, at approximately 170,000. Approximately 49,100 Salvadoran TPS holders are living in the Los Angeles metropolitan area. Salvadoran TPS holders contribute an estimated $5.4 billion to the U.S. economy and have a nearly 90 percent participation rate in the labor force.

The current TPS designation was given to immigrants from El Salvador on March 9, 2001, in response to the earthquakes that occurred in January 2001 and February 2001. Multiple extensions have been given to Salvadoran TPS holders since 2001. On September 9, 2026, DHS announced that Salvadoran TPS holders would retain their protections while the Administration considers a final determination regarding the designation. No timeline for that decision was provided. As of October 20, 2026, Salvadoran TPS holders continue to face uncertainty about their long-term immigration status, employment authorization, and ability to remain with their families in the United States.

On July 7, 2026, Congresswoman Rivas sent a letter urging Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to extend the TPS designation for migrants from El Salvador by July 11, 2026, 60 days before its expiration on September 9, 2026, for 18 months – the maximum extension allowed under law.

title: Rouzer, Murphy Champion Fifth Annual North Carolina WATERS S...
text:
GREENVILLE, NC - Today, North Carolina Congressmen David Rouzer (R-NC-07) and Greg Murphy, M.D. (R-NC-03) hosted the fifth annual Water Adaptation to Ensure Regional Success (WATERS) Summit in Greenville, North Carolina. This full day nonpartisan event brought together more than 175 local, state, and federal leaders, academic experts, and flood mitigation professionals to discuss solutions to waterway and flood mitigation challenges in North Carolina.

Since the last WATERS Summit, Congressman Rouzer has continued advancing legislation to address water-related challenges, streamline disaster assistance, and improve permitting.

“As communities grow in North Carolina, it's more important than ever to build them strong and resilient. That’s why I'm proud to help bring together industry leaders and public officials at the fifth annual WATERS Summit to identify ways to better protect North Carolinians from flooding," said Congressman Rouzer. "By leveraging modern technology and advancing legislative solutions in Congress, we can better prepare our state for future flood risks. I appreciate the partnership with Congressman Greg Murphy and everyone else who makes this a productive and collaborative summit.”

"It was a pleasure to host another successful WATERS Summit, convening so many incredible leaders from across North Carolina and our country to collaborate on flood mitigation," said Congressman Greg Murphy, M.D. "Waterway challenges and storm resiliency are not partisan issues - they are human issues. No recent example is greater than Hurricane Helene, which devastated our mountain neighbors, who we continue to support as they rebuild their lives. North Carolina faces unique challenges as a large state, and improving our infrastructure to withstand flooding is critical to our continued success and the preservation of our way of life."

As a senior member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, Congressman Rouzer secured several priorities in H.R. 9497, the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) of 2026. The legislation will help protect families from flooding while strengthening the resilience and durability of the nation’s ports and inland waterways.

Through WRDA 2026, Congressman Rouzer secured authorizations for critical infrastructure improvements involving ports, waterways, flood protection, and water infrastructure. These include Surf City’s 50-year federal beach renourishment project, multiple flood risk reduction studies for communities across Southeastern North Carolina, a feasibility study to improve water quality in the Cape Fear River in Cumberland County, and improvements to White Lake’s water infrastructure.

Congressman Rouzer is working to strengthen disaster response and improve coordination among federal agencies through H.R. 4669, the FEMA Act of 2025. Three of his bills were incorporated into the legislation, which advanced out of committee and awaits consideration by the entire House chamber.

Congressman Rouzer is also advancing permitting reform through H.R. 3898, the PERMIT Act, which passed the House in December 2025. The legislation streamlines permitting under the Clean Water Act, eliminate duplicative regulatory requirements, and provide greater clarity and predictability for infrastructure and energy projects.

The 2026 WATERS Summit featured speakers and participants from federal, state, and local government, as well as experts in infrastructure, flood mitigation, environmental quality, and disaster recovery. Speakers included Rep. David Rouzer (NC-07), Rep. Greg Murphy, M.D. (NC-03), U.S. Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC) and Ted Budd (R-NC) (both participating virtually), Wilmington Mayor Bill Saffo, Greenville Mayor P.J. Connelly, North Topsail Beach Mayor Richard Grant, NC State Senator Kevin Corbin, co-chair of the Governor’s WNC Recovery Committee, and Greenville City Manager Michael Cowin, among many others.

title: ICYMI: As Healthcare Costs Skyrocket, Congresswoman Schrier Joins Local Leaders, Patients to Discuss Her Bill to Cap Price of Insulin at $35 for all Americans
text:
BELLEVUE, WA - Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Overlake Medical Center and healthcare leaders, doctors, and patients this week to discuss the rising cost of medications, and her legislation to lower the price of insulin for all Americans.

Overlake Medical Center CEO Jon Duarte; Jason R. Fredrick, M.D., Overlake Clinics Endocrinology; Ingrid Gourley Mungia, VP, Overlake Medical Center Public Policy and Advocacy; Breakthrough T1D members; and patients joined the discussion with Congresswoman Schrier.

View footage from the event HERE.

BACKGROUND: Congresswoman Schrier is the first and only pediatrician in Congress, and has lived with Type 1 diabetes for over 40 years. Congresswoman Schrier recently introduced her bipartisan INSULIN Act to cap out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35, or 25% of the list price per month, for all Americans with diabetes. Congresswoman Schrier will additionally serve as the new Democratic Co-Chair of the Congressional Diabetes Caucus in the 120th Congress, where she will continue her work to lower healthcare costs, improve care, and bolster medical research.

“Costs across the board are far too high for patients and families in Washington state. As a doctor with Type 1 diabetes, I was so proud to cap insulin at $35 a month for seniors a few years ago. Now I’m working to bring $35 insulin to everyone with the INSULIN Act, and then bring down the cost of other lifesaving medications,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I was glad to join Overlake Hospital physicians, and T1D leaders and patients to discuss how we can work together to lower the cost of insulin and improve diabetes research, treatment, and self-management. I look forward to continuing my work in Congress to make healthcare more affordable and accessible, and will fight for the passage of my bill to cap the cost of insulin at $35 a month for all Americans with diabetes.”

“We see firsthand how high medication costs can affect patients and families,” said Jon Duarte, president and CEO of Overlake Medical Center & Clinics and chief executive of MultiCare’s North Sound region. “Reducing financial barriers will make it easier for people with diabetes to access the medication they need to live their healthiest lives.”

"My youngest son was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes at just 13 months old. Now 17 and a junior in high school, he has spent nearly his entire life managing this disease. For those of us with a family member living with T1D, insulin isn't an option or a luxury. It's a necessary part of our families' daily lives and an unavoidable cost of living. I'm thankful for Congresswoman Schrier's leadership on the INSULIN Act, as well as the many dedicated advocates across the T1D community fighting to ensure everyone has affordable access to the insulin they need to live,” said Keith Overa, Breakthrough T1D Greater Northwest Chapter Board of Directors.

title: Brown Introduces Legislation to Require Labels on AI-Generated Campaign Content
text:
Washington, DC – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) has introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act, legislation to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to deprive or defraud individuals of their right to vote and require disclaimers on AI-generated content.

The legislation would be enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and applies to federal, state, and local campaign content. The Securing Elections from AI Deception Act is endorsed by the NAACP, the Lawyer’s Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, and NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice. The legislation has 30 cosponsors in the House. Bill text available here.

This week, the New York Times reported that over $130 million in AI-generated ads have flooded the airwavesthis election year. According to analysis by Wesleyan University, 69% of ads with AI content do not have disclaimers.

Campaign ads featuring deceptive AI-generated have proliferated in recent years (Wall Street Journal, Reuters, New York Times), including ads featuring deepfake video and audio. In 2024, deepfake images of Trump with Black supporters spread online. In addition to deceiving voters, AI could also be used to spread false information regarding election information as a tactic to suppress voting rights. In 2020, robocalls targeting Black voters in Ohio spread deliberately false information relating to voting by mail procedures. AI technology has the potential to encourage similar efforts in the future and make them more persuasive.

“This isn’t complicated: voters deserve to know that the campaign content they see and hear is real. We need labels on AI-generated election content and we need to hold accountable those who use AI to knowingly spread false information. Pairing the latest technology with old-school dirty tricks is a dangerous combination. I’m proud to introduce the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act and will continue to defend the voting rights of every American,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown.

“Artificial intelligence cannot become another tool for voter deception and suppression. Black communities have long been targeted by efforts to mislead, intimidate, and exclude voters, and new technology can make those tactics more sophisticated and harder to detect. The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act puts necessary guardrails in place to protect voters and our democracy. The NAACP applauds Congresswoman Brown for her continued leadership,” said Cedric C. Haynes, NAACP’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Legislative Affairs.

“Every voter should know that the basic information they receive about how to vote and register is accurate. But without action from Congress, information can be as artificial as the so-called intelligence at creates it. With the growth of AI tools powering dis-information, we need to pass the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act so that Black voters are protected and the sources of dis-information are held accountable,” said Chanel Sherrod, Policy Advisor at the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law.

Brown serves at the Ranking Member on the Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee on the House Oversight Committee. Brown first introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act in 2024.

The Securing Elections from AI Deception Act

Requires Disclaimers on Election-Related Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence

Requires the use of a disclaimer for AI generated election content related to AI-generated images, text, video, audio or other media that includes

a simulation, alteration, or distortion of an image, video or audio of a candidate for federal, state, or local office

information about the time, place, manner, or requirements for voting or registering to vote for Federal, State, or local office

The disclaimer for AI generated content must include either:

the statement “AI Disclaimer: This output was generated by artificial intelligence” or

a symbol, similar in size and design to the copyright symbol, consisting of the letters “AI” in a circle

The disclaimer requirement would be regulated and enforced by the Federal Trade Commission under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission Act regarding unfair or deceptive practices

The Federal Trade Commission would be required to educate the public on the meaning and use of the disclaimer and report to Congress on its adoption and effectiveness

Prohibits the Use of Artificial Intelligence to Deprive or Defraud Individuals of the Right to Vote

Bars developers or deployers of artificial intelligence from using AI to intentionally deprive or defraud an individual of the right to vote in an election.

Including providing deceptive information regarding:

the time, place, or method of voting

eligibility requirements to vote or register to vote

the counting of ballots

the adjudication of elections

endorsements

the procedures or requirements for voting

Using deception, threats, intimidation, fraud, or coercion to prevent, interfere, or deter, or to attempt to prevent, interfere, or deter an individual’s right to

register to vote, vote, support or advocate for a candidate

serve as an election worker

Establishes a penalty of a fine or imprisonment for violating these prohibitions

title: Strickland, Eloise’s Cooking Pot, Thurston County Food Bank, Food Source Foundation Discussed SNAP Cuts and Food Resources for Families
text:
Tacoma, WA – Today, Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) led the Making a Difference Foundation/Eloise’s Cooking Pot, Thurston County Food Bank, The Food Source Foundation, and other community leadersat a press conference highlighting how the GOP-led federal cuts to SNAP are hurting American families and seniors, and food and nutrition resources for families in the South Sound.

“The Trump Administration continues to shred our social safety net, and take food out of the mouths of hungry children,” said Strickland. “SNAP is a critical program for seniors, families and children across the nation. Our local partners can help support families, but the damage from the Big Ugly Bill has been done.”

“On behalf of Making A Difference Foundation and Eloise’s Cooking Pot Food Bank, I want to thank Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland for bringing our community together and shining a light on the challenges families face in accessing food. Her willingness to create space for this conversation is an important step toward understanding the impact of these issues and working together on solutions. We are grateful for her leadership and for the opportunity to share what we are seeing in our community,” said Ahndrea L. Blue, President and CEO, Making A Difference Foundation and Eloise’s Cooking Pot Food Bank.

“Since the passage of H.R. 1 and changes to SNAP, our food pantries and satellite sites have repeatedly set new single-day attendance records. In 2026, nearly 25% of our pantry customers are first-time visitors. We have expanded evening hours and increased home delivery to meet this growing need, even as we receive significantly less food and resources through federal programs. Our community embraces the spirit of neighbor helping neighbor, but food banks cannot replace the reach of SNAP. Protecting this essential program helps ensure that children, seniors, and working families have the food they need to thrive,” said John Ficker, Thurston County Food Bank Executive Director.

“The Food Source Foundation has boots on the ground every day, serving our most vulnerable neighbors through several programs. I can tell you over the last two years we have had to increasingly ramp up our food service to meet the growing need. In the last three weeks since the beginning of October the need has grown exponentially, especially among our neighbors who are working full-time but still cannot afford to buy food,” said Chris Hyde, the Food Source Foundation Founder & Director.

“Behind every conversation about food assistance are real people and families trying to make ends meet. Protecting access to nutritious food helps strengthen the whole community. I hope today’s discussion leads to lasting support for the neighbors who need it,” said Sheree Staples, Eloise’s Cooking Pot Volunteer.

“Food is essential to every family’s health and stability. When people can access the food they need, they have more room to focus on their work, their children, and their future. I’m grateful to everyone working together to make sure our community is heard and supported,” said Jah Morgan, Eloise’s Cooking Pot Client.

Other local leaders Michelle Douglas, the CEO of Emergency Food Network; Stacy Crinch, the CEO of GoodRoots; and Seth Kirby, the Chief Impact Officer of Greater Tacoma Community Foundation were also in attendance.

You can watch the full press conference here.

Since the Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1), was enacted, SNAP participation nationwide has decreased by over 5 million people. In Washington state alone there has been a decrease of over 57,000 people while food bank usage has gone up by 9%. 44% of Washington SNAP participants are children.

Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. She is Whip of the New Democrat Coalition, Secretary of the Congressional Black Caucus, and is one of the first Korean-American women elected to Congress.

title: Bipartisan Bill Co-Led by Suozzi to Protect Americans from Online Dating Scams Signed Into Law
text:
Washington, D.C.—President Trump yesterday signed into law the bipartisan Romance Scam Prevention Act, co-led by Congressman Suozzi, which requires online dating platforms to inform users when they have interacted with someone banned for fraud. The bill will equip potential victims with essential information to help them avoid financial or emotional exploitation before it happens. Congressman Suozzi co-led this measure in the House alongside Reps. Valadao (R-CA), Pettersen (D-CO), and Goldman (R-TX). The Senate companion was led by Senators Blackburn (R-TN) and Hickenlooper (D-CO). This is the second Suozzi-led bill cracking down on online exploitation that President Trump has signed into law this Congress after the TAKE IT DOWN Act became law in May 2025.

“As technology changes faster than ever, criminals are finding new ways to use it to exploit Americans,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Dating apps have become a new frontier for scammers looking to manipulate people and steal their money. Congress must keep up. This commonsense law ensures users know when anyone they’ve interacted with on a dating app has been removed for fraudulent activity, giving them the information they need to protect themselves. I’m proud that Republicans and Democrats in both the House and the Senate, and the President of the United States, came together to get this done.”

Frauds perpetrated through online dating platforms, including apps and websites, often don’t end when the scammer is removed from the platform, especially if the conversations have moved to text messages, phone calls, or social media. Under this new law, potential victims will be alerted when anyone they have communicated with through a dating platform is removed for fraud, to ensure they know to stop communicating with the scammer and protect themselves from being swindled. The bill mandates that these notifications include clear warnings against sending money or other personal information to users for further protection.

This bill addresses an essential, expensive issue. In 2023, more than 60 million Americans used an online dating service. That same year, the Federal Trade Commission reported that "romance scams" resulted in the loss of more than $1.1 billion.

Suozzi helped lead the Romance Scam Prevention Act through Congress, working across the aisle to crack down on an emerging and dangerous type of online fraud. The bill builds on Suozzi’s work to root out waste, fraud, and abuse online. He is also a co-lead of the bipartisan TAKE IT DOWN Act, which was signed into law in May 2025 and established federal protections against the nonconsensual spread of intimate images, including AI-generated deepfakes. Both the Romance Scam Prevention Act and TAKE IT DOWN Act were endorsed by the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, where Suozzi serves as the Democratic Co-Chair.

“I’m extremely proud to see my bill, the Romance Scam Prevention Act, signed into law. Millions of Americans use online dating platforms to find meaningful relationships, making these platforms a target for scammers looking to exploit unsuspecting victims and take advantage of them financially. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation is an important step toward strengthening protections against online scams, and I’m grateful to everyone who worked to get this bill across the finish line and help keep Americans safe online,” said Congressman Valadao.

"Romance scammers stole almost $1.5 billion from innocent Americans in 2025 alone, turning online dating platforms into a tool for fraud. I’m proud to co-lead Rep. Valadao’s bipartisan Romance Scam Prevention Act, which has now passed both the House and Senate. By requiring online dating sites to alert users when they’ve interacted with someone removed for fraud, this bill helps stop scammers before they can steal another American’s hard-earned money,” said Congressman Goldman.

“Scammers prey on Americans looking for companionship, exploiting their trust and, in too many cases, stealing their life savings. The Romance Scam Prevention Act will put critical safeguards in place to protect all dating app users – but especially senior citizens – from fraudulent schemes. I am pleased to see President Trump sign this important legislation into law and take action to protect Americans from romance scams,” said Senator Blackburn.

“People turn to dating apps looking for love and connection, not to get scammed. Our bill puts real safeguards in place that will protect all dating app users, especially senior citizens, from harmful, fraudulent schemes. We’re glad to see our safeguards become law,” said Senator Hickenlooper.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Reminds Constituents Medicare Open Enrollment Is Underway
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswomen Claudia Tenney (NY-24) today reminded Medicare beneficiaries across New York's 24th Congressional District that the annual Medicare Open Enrollment Period is underway. From October 15 through December 7, 2026, eligible individuals can review their current Medicare coverage, compare available health and prescription drug plans, and make changes for 2027.

During Open Enrollment, Medicare beneficiaries can switch between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage, change Medicare Advantage plans, or join, switch, or drop Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage. Any changes made during this period will take effect on January 1, 2027. Beneficiaries who are satisfied with their current coverage generally do not need to take action, but should review any changes to their plan's premiums, benefits, prescription drug coverage, and provider networks for the upcoming year.

“Medicare provides health care coverage for millions of seniors, including more than 270,000 in New York's 24th Congressional District, and it is important that beneficiaries understand their options before the December 7 deadline,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Changes to premiums, prescription drug costs, and provider networks can have a significant impact on seniors living on fixed incomes. I encourage seniors on Medicare to review their coverage, compare available plans, and make informed decisions about their health care needs for the coming year. My office remains available to help constituents navigate federal agencies and access the resources they need.”

Medicare beneficiaries can access the following resources during Open Enrollment:

Medicare Plan Finder:Visit Medicare.gov/plan-compareto compare Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans available in your area.

title: Tokuda, Warnock, and Sherman Call for Federal Audit of Refunds of $166 Billion in Illegal Trump Tariffs
text:
HAWAIʻI — U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda (HI-02), alongside U.S. Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), the Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on International Trade, Customs, and Global Competitiveness, and Representative Brad Sherman (CA-32), the Ranking Member of the Financial Services Committee Subcommittee on Capital Markets, led a letter to the Government Accountability Office (GAO) requesting an audit of refunds for Trump's illegally collected tariffs.

In the letter, the lawmakers urge GAO to investigate how U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is managing the refunds and whether the financial benefits will reach the consumers who ultimately bore the costs of the tariffs.

Following the Supreme Court’s decision invalidating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariffs and a subsequent lower-court ruling ordering repayments, roughly $100 billion of the $166 billion collected from importers had been refunded as of August 2026.

“This is without question the largest tariff refund operation in U.S. history, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection had to create new systems and processes to handle this enormous task,” the lawmakers wrote. “We are concerned about the ability of the administration to completely and accurately refund all IEEPA tariffs. Additionally, we are concerned to what extent consumers, upon whom the financial burden of the tariffs fell, were able to receive any benefits from the refunds.”

“Trump’s illegal, reckless tariffs have made everyday Americans pay more while his corporate benefactors reap billions in rebates. Families and small businesses in Hawaiʻi, where costs are already too high, are left footing the bill," said Rep. Tokuda. "We’re demanding a full audit and a clear accounting of whether refunds are reaching the people who paid the price.”

“Georgians are already paying the price for the Trump administration’s reckless and illegal tariff policies. Now, the administration’s failure to deliver court-ordered refunds is putting additional financial strain on hardworking families and small businesses across the country,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. “The American people deserve a timely, accurate, and transparent refund process that lays bare the total economic devastation of the administration’s erroneous tariff agenda on hardworking consumers. That’s why I’m joining Congresswoman Tokuda in calling for a comprehensive investigation into how the U.S. Customs and Border Protection is handling these refunds.”

"Trump’s reckless tariffs have been an unjust tax on American families, driving up the cost of everyday life,” said Rep. Sherman. “Nowhere is the damage clearer than in housing. For Los Angeles families rebuilding after the wildfires, and for families across the country, tariffs have made homes harder to build. Families paid these illegal tariffs through higher prices, and they deserve to know whether the refunds will reach them. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Tokuda and Senator Warnock in calling for a full GAO audit."

The lawmakers are asking GAO to examine the accuracy and completeness of the refunds, identify which industries and importers received payments, and determine whether those savings reached wholesalers, retailers, and consumers.

A copy of the letter may be viewed here.

title: Representative Tran Demands Answers on the Detention and Deportation of Asian Americans Born Abroad to U.S. Servicemembers
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter with Democratic colleagues to Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin and Acting Director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) David Venturella, demanding answers on the detention and deportation of “Amerasians,” or individuals born in Asia to an Asian mother and U.S. serviceman during the Southeast Asia War between 1950 and 1982. Under the Amerasian Act of 1982 and the Amerasian Homecoming Act of 1988, many were able to gain Lawful Permanent Residency status in the United States. However, because they were not categorically naturalized and many do not have proper documentation of American paternity, Amerasians are now facing threats of deportation.

“It has been extremely difficult for Amerasians to verify their ancestry. Most of their fathers returned to the U.S. after their tours of duty. Many of their mothers destroyed documents to protect their children in fear of political retaliation and persecution,” said Rep. Tran in the letter.

In 2008, the United States and Vietnam signed a memorandum agreeing to halt the repatriation of Southeast Asian refugees who arrived in the U.S. prior to 1995. This agreement was heavily altered in November 2020, allowing a process for deporting immigrants who entered the U.S. before 1995. Protections were rolled back even more in June 2025, leaving an unknown number of Amerasians vulnerable to detention and deportation.

The letter was signed by Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus, Representative Grace Meng (NY-06), and Representatives Lou Correa (CA-46), Judy Chu (CA-28), Dave Min (CA-47), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Raja Krishamoorthi (IL-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), and Seth Moulton (MA-06).

Read the full letter HERE.

As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the only Vietnamese American in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to uplifting and representing the Vietnamese community on the national stage and protecting the rights of immigrants.

title: President Signs Congressman Valadao’s Romance Scam Prevention Act into Law
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, President Trump signed Congressman David Valadao's (CA-22) Romance Scam Prevention Act into law. This bipartisan bill will require dating apps and services to issue fraud ban notifications to users who have interacted with a person removed from the app for fraudulent activity.

Reps. Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Craig Goldman (TX-12), and Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) co-led the introduction of the bill in the House. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) and John Hickenlooper (D-CO) introduced the companion bill in the Senate.

“I’m extremely proud to see my bill, the Romance Scam Prevention Act, signed into law,” said Congressman Valadao. “Millions of Americans use online dating platforms to find meaningful relationships, making these platforms a target for scammers looking to exploit unsuspecting victims and take advantage of them financially. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation is an important step toward strengthening protections against online scams, and I’m grateful to everyone who worked to get this bill across the finish line and help keep Americans safe online.”

“As technology changes faster than ever, criminals are finding new ways to use it to exploit Americans,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Dating apps have become a new frontier for scammers looking to manipulate people and steal their money. Congress must keep up. This commonsense law ensures users know when anyone they’ve interacted with on a dating app has been removed for fraudulent activity, giving them the information they need to protect themselves. I’m proud that Republicans and Democrats in both the House and the Senate, and the President of the United States, came together to get this done.”

"Romance scammers stole almost $1.5 billion from innocent Americans in 2025 alone, turning online dating platforms into a tool for fraud,” said Congressman Goldman. “I’m proud to co-lead Rep. Valadao’s bipartisan Romance Scam Prevention Act, which has now passed both the House and Senate. By requiring online dating sites to alert users when they’ve interacted with someone removed for fraud, this bill helps stop scammers before they can steal another American’s hard-earned money.”

“Scammers prey on Americans looking for companionship, exploiting their trust and, in too many cases, stealing their life savings,” said Senator Blackburn. “The Romance Scam Prevention Act will put critical safeguards in place to protect all dating app users – but especially senior citizens – from fraudulent schemes. I am pleased to see President Trump sign this important legislation into law and take action to protect Americans from romance scams.”

“People turn to dating apps looking for love and connection, not to get scammed,” said Senator Hickenlooper. “Our bill puts real safeguards in place that will protect all dating app users, especially senior citizens, from harmful, fraudulent schemes. We’re glad to see our safeguards become law.”

Background:

Over 60 million Americans used an online dating service in 2023, and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) reported that romance scams resulted in victims losing over $1.1 billion. Criminals use false names and stories to lure individuals into conversation before manipulating them to give up sensitive information. When an online dating service provider becomes aware of a user committing fraudulent activity, like illegally obtaining money, the online dating service provider immediately deactivates the fraudulent user’s account. However, individuals who meet online often take their conversations to other communication platforms, so even when a fraudulent account is removed, an individual might not know they are still communicating with someone who was banned from the platform.

Read the full bill here.

title: Rep. Vasquez Demands Social Media CEOs do More to Stop Illegal Gun Trafficking, Protect Children
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 21, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to the CEOs of Meta, Telegram, and Snapchat urging them to do more to stop New Mexican youth from being able to buy, sell, and trade weapons illegally over social media platforms and messaging apps. The letter also demands that these companies do more to address youth violence and illegal activities on their platforms.

“From Las Cruces to Albuquerque, I work directly with law enforcement agencies in New Mexico that continue to raise concerns about this issue and the link between social media and increasing juvenile crime,” wrote Vasquez. “In my district, I continue to hear how your platforms, including Snapchat, are utilized to traffic firearms and deadly drugs, promote theft and criminal activity, facilitate cartel operations, and fuel a dangerous cycle of youth violence. Your failures have deadly consequences for my constituents.”

Recent reporting has raised concern about social media companies allowing interactions that fuel youth violence and weapon and drug trafficking across the Southwest and New Mexico communities.

Read the full letter HERE.

This letter builds on Rep. Vasquez’s work to hold social media companies accountable, combat cartels and prevent youth violence across New Mexico:

Sending a letter to social media CEOs demanding that they take action to curb illegal gun sales and cyber bullying on their platforms. This letter was sent after local law enforcement officers flagged illegal gun sales and bullying on these platforms as a driver of youth violence in New Mexico communities.

Cosponsoring the bipartisan Combating Cartels on Social Media Act to require DHS to develop and implement a national strategy to combat illicit recruitment of American citizens through social media.

Introducing the No More Narcos Act to create a coordinated educational campaign led by the Department of Justice to teach middle and high school students within 100 miles of the U.S.-Mexico border about the dangers of working with cartels.

Cosponsoring Sammy’s Law, a bipartisan bill to give parents more tools and protect kids on social media platforms.

title: Walberg’s Bipartisan Bill to Combat Human Trafficking Signed into Law
text:
Today, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) issued the following statement after President Trump signed into law H.R. 4307, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act. This bipartisan legislation strengthens the Department of Labor’s (DOL) ability to identify human trafficking, protect vulnerable individuals, and combat exploitation.

"Today, we took a collective step forward in addressing the scourge of human trafficking," said Rep. Walberg. "Very often, Department of Labor enforcement personnel are the first to encounter signs of human trafficking, forced labor, and exploitation; the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act provides these employees with the tools and knowledge needed to detect and address this heinous crime. I’m proud this bipartisan legislation is now law, strengthening protections for the most vulnerable—including women and children—from exploitation."

H.R. 4307, Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act:

Establishes guidelines to ensure DOL staff are provided needed training and equipped with sufficient tools and resources to report labor or sexual exploitation.

Establishes a clear framework for DOL employees to make referrals and further assist law enforcement in preventing labor or sexual exploitation.

Promotes DOL transparency and congressional oversight regarding DOL detection and response to human trafficking.

Congressman Walberg serves as the Chairman of the Education and Workforce Committee.

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper, DeGette, Pettersen, Neguse, Crow Demand DOJ Recognition & Accreditation Program Be Restored to Full Capacity
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet led Senator John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) and Representatives Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), Brittany Pettersen (D-Colo.), Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), and Jason Crow (D-Colo.) to state their strong support for the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Recognition and Accreditation (R&A) Program within the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) and demand that the DOJ immediately restore full staffing and operational capacity to this critical program following recent paralyzing disruptions and staffing cuts.

The R&A program is a vital resource for non-profit organizations that provide affordable, quality legal assistance to immigrants in need in Colorado and across the country. Without this program, immigrants and their families are forced to attempt to navigate these incredibly complicated and arduous legal proceedings alone.

“The R&A Program serves as a crucial bridge in our immigration system. By credentialing non-attorney staff and volunteers at eligible non-profits, the program expands access for immigrants to qualified counsel while easing severe court backlogs. Recent figures indicate that 71% of people facing deportation in Colorado immigration courts lack access to legal counsel. Unfortunately, recent administrative reassignments have depleted the program’s adjudicative staff, leaving the office without the necessary personnel authorized to approve or deny applications. This delays both new applications and routine renewals, stalling non-profits nationwide that meet every legal requirement,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The R&A Program delivers a low cost, high impact framework that supports the efficient administration of justice while protecting vulnerable communities. We urge you to take immediate action to restore its full operational capacity,” concluded the lawmakers.

Bennet has consistently fought against the Trump administration’s inhumane immigration policies. In August 2026, Bennet and Hickenlooper joined U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) and six of their Senate colleagues to demand answers from the Trump administration about recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) actions in airports.

Bennet and his staff have joined Crow and his congressional office in conducting consistent oversight visits to the Aurora, Colorado detention facility throughout the current Trump administration. Bennet also joined U.S. Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-Hawaii) and U.S. Representative Judy Chu (D-Calif.) to introduce the Protect American Values Act, legislation that would prevent federal funds from being used to implement, administer, enforce, or otherwise carry out the Trump administration’s finalized “public charge” rule.

In July 2026, Bennet joined U.S. Senator Angus King (I-Maine) and 37 of their Senate colleagues in calling for stronger accountability measures for ICE officers. In May 2026, Bennet and Neguse introduced three bills aimed at reforming the Department of Homeland Security, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection: the Keeping Immigrants and Destinations Safe Act; the Training, Responsibility, Uniforms, and Standards for Transparency Act; and the Oversight, Protection, and Enforcement Notification Act.

This letter is supported by key partners, including Compañeros: Four Corners Immigrant Resource Center in Durango, Hope Has No Borders in Denver, Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC), and Rocky Mountain Immigrant Advocacy Network (RMIAN).

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Attorney General Blanche and Acting Director Owen:

We write to express our strong support for the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Recognition and Accreditation (R&A) Program within the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) and to express serious concerns about recent disruptions and staffing cuts that have paralyzed this vital program. We urge you to immediately restore full staffing and operational capacity. Across Colorado, non-profit organizations depend on the R&A program to enable them to deliver affordable, quality legal assistance to low-income and vulnerable immigrants who would otherwise be forced to navigate complex legal proceedings alone.

The R&A Program serves as a crucial bridge in our immigration system. By credentialing non-attorney staff and volunteers at eligible non-profits, the program expands access for immigrants to qualified counsel while easing severe court backlogs. Recent figures indicate that 71% of people facing deportation in Colorado immigration courts lack access to legal counsel . Unfortunately, recent administrative reassignments have depleted the program’s adjudicative staff, leaving the office without the necessary personnel authorized to approve or deny applications. This delays both new applications and routine renewals, stalling non-profits nationwide that meet every legal requirement.

In Colorado, this operational disruption directly affects organizations serving both rural communities and urban centers. Key non-profit partners, including Compañeros: Four Corners Immigrant Resource Center in Durango, Catholic Charities of Southern Colorado in Pueblo, Hope Immigration Inc. in Colorado Springs, Iglesia de Jesucristo Pentecostal UPCI in Colorado Springs, and statewide coalitions like the Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC) rely on R&A credentials to maintain their legal service capacity. Without timely renewals and accreditation approvals, these trusted institutions risk losing their legal authority to represent local residents, leaving communities without reliable counsel.

To restore the operational integrity of the R&A Program and support community providers across Colorado, we request that the DOJ take the following immediate steps:

Immediately reassign or train senior adjudicators who possess explicit authority to approve and process Forms EOIR 31 (organizational recognition) and EOIR 31A (individual accreditation).

Clear the current application backlog and reinstate the 90-day processing standard to provide predictability for non-profit providers.

Reestablish transparent communication between EOIR leadership, recognized organizations, and community partners in Colorado and across the nation.

The R&A Program delivers a low cost, high impact framework that supports the efficient administration of justice while protecting vulnerable communities. We urge you to take immediate action to restore its full operational capacity.

We look forward to hearing from you on this important matter.
