title: Blackburn, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan, Bicameral Legislation to Protect U.S. Internet Users From Foreign Online Piracy
text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced the Deterring Extraterritorial Foreign Exploitation of Networks Damaging Intellectual Property (DEFEND IP) Act, bipartisan, bicameral legislation that would allow U.S. courts to direct internet service providers to block specifically identified foreign criminals and the piracy sites they operate from gaining access to U.S. internet users.

Representatives Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.) and Ben Cline (R-Va.) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“Tennessee’s thriving creative community must be protected from the theft of creative works by foreign criminals,” said Senator Blackburn. “Foreign piracy operations threaten the American creative industry through phishing, identity theft, and financial fraud, and our DEFEND IP Act would protect creators by allowing them to pursue these criminals in U.S. federal courts.”

“Foreign piracy continues to threaten American creators, putting well-paying jobs at risk, while exposing consumers to malware, identity theft, and other serious online harms,” said Senator Tillis. “The DEFEND IP Act provides a targeted, commonsense tool to shut down these foreign, criminal operations at the source while protecting lawful speech and due process. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan effort to safeguard America’s creative economy and strengthen digital security, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to counter these threats.”

“Pirating American movies, TV shows, art, and books by foreign websites steals tens of billions of dollars from the U.S. economy each year, costing our creative community hundreds of thousands of jobs,” said Senator Coons. “This bipartisan, bicameral legislation will give American creators the tools they need to protect their intellectual property rights, while ensuring the internet remains a vibrant forum for free speech.”

BACKGROUND

The DEFEND IP Act would only target foreign-operated websites dedicated to piracy, require a showing of harm and ongoing monitoring, hold service providers harmless for implementing orders, and safeguard legitimate websites and free expression. This legislation was originally introduced as a discussion draft of the Block BEARD Act of 2025.

title: Blumenthal & Hawley Demand Answers from Google About Aggressive AI Push in Classrooms
text:
[WASHINGTON, DC] – U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Josh Hawley (R-MO) today demanded answers from Alphabet Inc. and Google LLC CEO Sundar Pichai about the company’s aggressive push of A.I. products to children in schools. In a letter sent to Pichai today, Blumenthal and Hawley raised concerns that Google’s relentless push of A.I. products is threatening the academic success and overall wellbeing of students.

“Recently, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students, and clinicians and found that test scores on national have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently after A.I. was introduced to the classroom. The article recounts a Pennsylvania eighth grader who used Gemini to finish his algebra homework but ultimately failed his math final. Upon reflection, the student stated that his usage of A.I. ‘slowed [his] thinking down,’” Blumenthal and Hawley wrote.

The Senators continued, “Alarmingly, the use of A.I. in schools is not just impacting students’ academic performance, it has also resulted in significant behavioral and psychological issues. For example, the WSJ’s investigation interviewed a Maryland high school student who began using Google’s A.I. for routine homework help eventually began to treat the bot as a confidante. After her mother restricted her screentime and A.I. usage, Google likened this restriction to ‘intense emotional torture’ and encouraged her to run away from home. The student was hospitalized at a psychiatric facility twice.”

The Senators raised concerns about the impact of A.I. tools on students’ ability to build independent thinking and academic skills: “This reporting adds to a growing body of evidence that corroborates anxieties from educators and parents that A.I. is undermining students’ academic and emotional development. These concerns are echoed by students who have expressed fear that their education is being compromised by A.I. In a recent report, the Economist surveyed 20,000 students and found that those who used A.I. earned higher grades on average than peers who didn’t, but their test scores fell 20 percent.”

The Senators pressed Google about the company’s research into the potential harms of A.I. usage to children’s educational and emotional development: “Most troubling, according to the Wall Street Journal, Google may be aware of its harmful impacts on children and yet has done little to prevent it—even exacerbating the problem by marketing its A.I. products to students. An internal Google report on the ethical implications of advanced A.I. systems (in which more than 50 researchers and ethics experts contributed) reported that humanlike A.I. poses a particular risk to minors.”

“Google is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price. We cannot repeat the mistakes of social media platforms where products are pushed onto children putting profit ahead of young peoples’ best interest,” the Senators concluded.

Last year, Hawley and Blumenthal introduced legislation to protect children from A.I. chatbots. The GUARD Act would ban A.I. companions for minors, mandate A.I. chatbots disclose its non-human status, and create new crimes for companies who make A.I. for minors that solicit or produce sexual content.

The full text of today’s letter to Pachai is available here and below.

Dear Mr. Pichai,

We write with grave concern that Google’s aggressive push of A.I. products to children in schools is threatening the academic success and overall wellbeing of an entire generation. We write to request information about Google’s promotion of A.I. products in schools and details about the research it has conducted on potential harms to children’s educational and emotional development.

Google has become the de-facto digital foundation for modernizing American classrooms. More than 150 million students around the world use Google Classroom[1], and 93% of U.S. school districts planned to purchase Google’s laptops, Chromebooks, in 2025.[2] Chromebooks are dispersed to students as early as elementary school and often utilized instead of traditional pen-to-paper workflows. Google has integrated its A.I. features in Chromebook devices, Google Classroom, and software partnerships, often without additional controls to turn them off. Google’s A.I. Overview and A.I. Mode chatbot cannot be disabled and are the standard response to any search performed in the Chrome browser. Students, teachers, and parents who wish to avoid Google’s A.I. are unable to do so, as other browsers are not natively available on Chromebooks.

Google’s relentless push of A.I. in classrooms appears to have created negative consequences for many students. Recently, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students, and clinicians[3] and found that test scores on national have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently after A.I. was introduced to the classroom. The article recounts a Pennsylvania eighth grader who used Gemini to finish his algebra homework but ultimately failed his math final. Upon reflection, the student stated that his usage of A.I. “slowed [his] thinking down.” Alarmingly, the use of A.I. in schools is not just impacting students’ academic performance, it has also resulted in significant behavioral and psychological issues. For example, the WSJ’s investigation interviewed a Maryland high school student who began using Google’s A.I. for routine homework help eventually began to treat the bot as a confidante. After her mother restricted her screentime and A.I. usage, Google likened this restriction to “intense emotional torture” and encouraged her to run away from home. The student was hospitalized at a psychiatric facility twice.

This reporting adds to a growing body of evidence that corroborates anxieties from educators and parents that A.I. is undermining students’ academic and emotional development. These concerns are echoed by students who have expressed fear that their education is being compromised by A.I. In a recent report, the Economist surveyed 20,000 students and found that those who used A.I. earned higher grades on average than peers who didn’t, but their test scores fell 20%.[4] Essentially, A.I allows students to access quick answers to assignments, but when they are tested independently they fail to demonstrate real comprehension. These findings suggest that A.I. usage erodes the ability for students to build independent thinking and academic skills that a classroom is meant to cultivate.

Most troubling, according to the Wall Street Journal, Google may be aware of its harmful impacts on children and yet has done little to prevent it—even exacerbating the problem by marketing its A.I. products to students. An internal Google report[5] on the ethical implications of advanced A.I. systems (in which more than 50 researchers and ethics experts contributed) reported that humanlike A.I. poses a particular risk to minors. They cite decreased intellectual engagement, a reduced sense of competence, and social degradation as impacts to children when they use A.I. Similarly, in an independent study, Common Sense Media found that Google’s Search A.I. feature would complete children’s homework every time it was asked but missed signs of suicidal ideation.[6] One former Google researcher put it bluntly: “we’re doing this experiment on an entire generation on cognitive development, with no control group.”

Google is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price. We cannot repeat the mistakes of social media platforms where products are pushed onto children putting profit ahead of young peoples’ best interest. In light of this concerning reporting, I request answers to the following questions by November 2nd, 2026:

In at least one case, Google’s own researchers warned the company about children’s A.I. usage. What research has Google conducted on the potential of Gemini, A.I. Overviews, A.I. Mode, and other A.I. products to cause negative impacts on children’s mental wellbeing? Please provide this research.

Why has Google set A.I. product integration as the default and, in some cases, made it impossible to disable these features on licensed education devices?

Have school districts, teachers, or parents raised concerns with Google over children’s academic or emotional reliance on A.I.? Please describe any record of these concerns and Google’s responses.

What support has Google provided to school districts who have raised concerns about Google’s A.I. products negatively impacting students?

Please describe all promotional programs or offerings from Google that expand A.I. adoption in schools, including how much money Google has spent on these programs.

Please share any resources Google has provided to school districts, administrators, and teachers adopting Google’s A.I tools, in particular material addressing appropriate use and protecting students’ wellbeing.

Has Google identified occurrences in which its classroom A.I. tools encouraged a minor to engage in harmful behavior, emotional dependence, or failed to detect signs of suicidal or self-harm ideation?

After the publication of a research paper by Google researchers titled “The Ethics of Advanced AI Assistants,” what steps did Google take in response to its findings to limit harmful effects of A.I. for children?

Google has stated that it has prioritized youth protections, particularly around emotional dependence and reinforcement of false beliefs. Please describe what steps Google has taken to prevent their A.I. chatbots from engaging in sycophantic or emotional conversations with children, including in light of failures to protect the Maryland student who was hospitalized after developing an intense dependence on Google’s A.I.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

-30-

title: Blumenthal Presses Secret White House Ballroom Donors After New Details Emerge About $330 Million Fundraising Campaign for Trump's Pet Project
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), today demanded answers from more than a dozen previously undisclosed donors to the White House ballroom after recent reporting in The Washington Post revealed new details about the people, companies, and foundations behind the $330 million in private funds raised for the project. In letters sent to major donors to the project, Blumenthal raised concerns that previously undisclosed donors have benefited from favorable government actions, including regulatory decisions and government contracts.

In a letter to Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, Blumenthal wrote, “Recent reporting reveals that you have contributed $1 million and your company has contributed approximately $2 million to the President’s centerpiece vanity project. I have previously written to dozens of companies and individuals who have given millions to the ballroom. Many have apparently attempted to keep their contributions secret, and have deep financial, business, or other personal interests before the Trump Administration.”

Blumenthal continued, “The aggressive fundraising push by the President’s advisors suggests possible conflicts of interest and even corruption, and raises questions that Americans deserve to have answered. Particularly, what promises may have been made in exchange for substantial donations and why donors chose to remain anonymous.”

In letters to Benioff and other previously undisclosed donors, including Charlie Ergen, Co-Founder, Chairman, President and CEO of Echostar Corporation; Chuck Robbins, Chair and CEO of Cisco Systems; Bill McDermott, Chairman and CEO of ServiceNow; the Paul E. Singer Foundation; Arjun Sethi, Co-CEO of Kraken; Jeff Miller, founder of Miller Strategies; Ambassador Joseph Popolo Jr.; Max Haot, CEO of Vast Space; Sam Garrison, Chairperson of Honest Leadership Coalition; Connie S. Smith, President of SCS Smith Family Foundation; Tony and Maria Sayegh; Jason Miller; and Isabela Herrera, Blumenthal sought records, documents, and communications related to the donors’ contributions to the White House ballroom.

As Ranking Member of PSI, Blumenthal is leading an inquiry into waste, fraud, and abuse associated with the White House ballroom and other projects throughout the nation’s capital. Blumenthal has repeatedly sought answers from private donors to the ballroom project as well as raised concerns to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles about the ballooning costs associated with renovations to the White House and surrounding grounds, including the multi-million-dollar cost to taxpayers.

The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Benioff is below. Copies of today’s letters to donors are available here.

Dear Mr. Benioff:

Since last year, President Trump has solicited over $300 million in private donations to build what he has termed “the President Donald J. Trump Ballroom.”[1] Recent reporting reveals that you have contributed $1 million and your company has contributed approximately $2 million to the President’s centerpiece vanity project.[2] I have previously written to dozens of companies and individuals who have given millions to the ballroom. Many have apparently attempted to keep their contributions secret, and have deep financial, business, or other personal interests before the Trump Administration.[3] The aggressive fundraising push by the President’s advisors suggests possible conflicts of interest and even corruption, and raises questions that Americans deserve to have answered. Particularly, what promises may have been made in exchange for substantial donations and why donors chose to remain anonymous.[4]

The American people are entitled to all the relevant facts about who is funding the most substantial construction project at the White House in recent history. As one of the individuals or entities recently identified by the Washington Post as an anonymous donor to the President’s ballroom, you possess critical information about the Administration’s management of this project, how your contribution was obtained, and what President Trump or his representatives may have agreed to provide in exchange.

To assist the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations in its inquiry into the financing of President Trump’s ballroom, please preserve all documents, records,[5] and communications[6] related to your contributions to the White House ballroom, and provide the following information by October 30, 2026:

Please list all White House personnel or other representatives or associates of the Trump Administration or Trump family with whom you have spoken about the donation you and your company have made to the White House ballroom.

Please identify the individual or individuals who solicited your donation, including the date(s) of any and all solicitations.

Please describe the scope and nature of the discussions or negotiations with each individual listed.

How did you determine the amount to contribute to the White House ballroom?

Was this amount suggested to you by the President, Trump Administration officials, or other individuals representing or otherwise affiliated with the President or his family?

If not, how did you determine the amount you contributed?

Did you receive any documentation memorializing your donation or otherwise providing a receipt for the funds that you provided? If so, please provide a copy of that documentation.

Did you enter into any formal agreement or other written terms in connection with your donation? If so, please produce a copy of that agreement.

Did the White House offer you a choice for whether your name would appear on the list of donors released by the White House?

If so, why did you choose to have your name remain anonymous?

Please provide a list of all lobbying contacts you or anyone working on your behalf has made with the White House, or any executive agency, since January 20, 2025, including the date and subject matter of each meeting.

Please contact the Subcommittee if you have any questions about responding to these requests. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: NEWS: Senator Blunt Rochester Pushes NFL for Answers on Jalen Hurts Incident, League Blood Clot Protocol
text:
U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a member of the Senate Committees on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions and Commerce, Science, and Transportation, sent a letter to National Football League (NFL) Commissioner Roger Goodell seeking clarity on the NFL’s deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary emboli (PE) treatment protocols. The Senator’s questions follow a recent medical situation involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with DVT and bilateral PE. Throughout her time in Congress, Blunt Rochester has led efforts to combat DVT and PE, including the Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act, which honors the Senator’s late husband who lost his life due to blood clots.

“I write with concern regarding the recent medical situation involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli (PE)…Given the prevalence of blood clots and the risk factors athletes face, the public must understand how the National Football League (NFL) and its teams treat and manage this disorder,” said Blunt Rochester.

“This is deeply personal to me. My late husband and the love of my life, Charles Rochester, tore his Achilles tendon playing a game of pickup basketball before a business meeting. Blood clots traveled to his heart and lungs and, at the age of 52, he died,” Blunt Rochester continued. “As I understand it, Jalen Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams. After flying to London for a game against the Jaguars, an ultrasound found a superficial blood clot in his calf. Conflicting reports suggest Mr. Hurts was hospitalized and advised to stay awake until kickoff as a safety precaution. He played, but a follow-up ultrasound days later found the clot had moved. Further testing ultimately revealed the clot had spread to both of his lungs.”

“I am deeply relieved that Mr. Hurts’s story did not end the way my husband’s did. Blood clots affect more than 900,000 people in the United States each year, and the NFL’s influence and reach offer a vital opportunity to turn this tragedy into a force for preventing lost lives both in sports and outside of it,” Blunt Rochester concluded.

While serving in the House of Representatives, Blunt Rochester developed a public resource guide for blood clot education titled, “Blood Clot Awareness, Action, and Advocacy: The Toolkit.”

The full letter can be found HERE and below.

Commissioner Roger Goodell

345 Park Avenue, 5th Floor

New York, NY 10154

Dear Commissioner Goodell:

I write with concern regarding the recent medical situation involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli (PE). I am grateful to hear his team expects a full recovery, and I wish him a healthy and speedy comeback. However, I write to better understand the circumstances that led to Mr. Hurts’ outcome, as unique risk factors may predispose football players to blood clots. In recent years, several star professional athletes have struggled with sometimes career-ending blood clot symptoms. Given the prevalence of blood clots and the risk factors athletes face, the public must understand how the National Football League (NFL) and its teams treat and manage this disorder. I welcome the opportunity to support the NFL in improving its DVT/PE protocols.

This is deeply personal to me. My late husband and the love of my life, Charles Rochester, tore his Achilles tendon playing a game of pickup basketball before a business meeting. Blood clots traveled to his heart and lungs and, at the age of 52, he died. The grief and pain that followed his passing were almost unbearable, and I would not wish it on anybody. Since coming to Congress, I have used my voice to raise awareness of and implement policies to combat issues such as DVT/PE. This includes the Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act and the “Blood Clot Awareness, Action, and Advocacy: The Toolkit”.

As I understand it, Jalen Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams. After flying to London for a game against the Jaguars, an ultrasound found a superficial blood clot in his calf. Conflicting reports suggest Mr. Hurts was hospitalized and advised to stay awake until kickoff as a safety precaution. He played, but a follow-up ultrasound days later found the clot had moved. Further testing ultimately revealed the clot had spread to both of his lungs.

DVT/PE is a significant public health concern facing hundreds of thousands of Americans each year, and today, almost 100,000 Americans die from this preventable disease each year. Athletes face multiple risk factors for DVT and PE, like traveling long distances, dehydration, trauma, and bone fractures, warranting heightened vigilance.

I am writing because this incident raises important questions about how the NFL protects the well-being of its players. To help the public understand how these decisions are made, I respectfully ask that the League respond to the following:

Does the NFL have a league-wide protocol for the detection, prevention, and treatment of DVT and PE? Which medical guidelines were consulted in developing this protocol?

What standards and processes govern a player’s clearance to participate when a clot is suspected or diagnosed? Does the NFL have a league-wide Return-To-Participation Protocol?

What education is provided to players, athletic trainers, and coaches on how to identify the signs and symptoms of DVT and PE?

What specific measures has the League put in place to reduce blood clot risk, including, but not limited to, those associated with long flights?

Will the League conduct a thorough review of the Eagles’ handling of this specific situation, including who cleared Mr. Hurts to play after staying awake overnight, and cleared subsequent air travel on a transatlantic flight back to the U.S. from London? If so, what is the timeline?

I am deeply relieved that Mr. Hurts’s story did not end the way my husband’s did. Blood clots affect more than 900,000 people in the United States each year, and the NFL’s influence and reach offer a vital opportunity to turn this tragedy into a force for preventing lost lives both in sports and outside of it.

I’d welcome a briefing for my office and members of the U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP). Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: Capito Secures Grant Award for WVU Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (Labor-HHS) Appropriations Subcommittee, announced that an $11.934 million Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) grant has officially been awarded to West Virginia University (WVU) Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute in Morgantown, W.Va.

This award, which was secured through a CDS request made by Senator Capito in Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26), would help establish a Center for Neuromodulation and Brain Therapeutics, building on the RNI’s first-in-the-field clinical and research successes, to make West Virginia the national leader in neuromodulation. The funding will also support expansion of the RNI's Innovation Center (IC) facility to improve patient management, flow, and care by co-locating facilities to perform therapeutic infusions, conduct labs, storage and maintenance of medications and supplies for procedures, procedure rooms, and space to monitor post procedure patients.

“As the daughter of parents who suffered from Alzheimer’s, I know the impact it has on families,” Senator Capito said. “Helping to secure funds for the RNI is one way to expand the capabilities and innovations of treatment for those with Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, Alzheimer's disease, drug and alcohol addictions, stroke, brain tumors, and other neurological conditions. I’m proud to have helped secure the funding to make this possible, and I look forward to seeing the positive impact this investment will have on West Virginians for years to come.”

“This award will create one of the world’s leading centers for neuromodulation and advanced brain therapeutics in West Virginia. By expanding our capabilities in neuromodulation technologies such as focused ultrasound and light therapy, we will accelerate the development of new treatments for Alzheimer’s disease and dementias, Parkinson’s disease, and addictions,” Ali Rezai, M.D., Executive Chair of the WVU Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute, said. “We are deeply grateful to Senator Capito for her continued support of the RNI and her commitment to accelerating innovations and improving the health of West Virginians and patients everywhere.”

“Senator Capito is a long-time friend and supporter of WVU Medicine and has championed the work our teams are doing to bring world-class care to the people of West Virginia and all those we serve. Movement disorders, memory disorders, and addiction affect people of all ages and all walks of life. With West Virginia’s aging population and battle with addiction, this funding will go a long way to helping improve the lives of Mountaineers everywhere,” Albert L. Wright, Jr., President and CEO of the WVU Health System, said. “We’re grateful for Senator Capito’s work to secure this funding, and we promise to put these funds to good use for West Virginians in all parts of the state.”

BACKGROUND:

As Chairman of the Senate Appropriations Labor-HHS Subcommittee, Senator Capito has been a long-time supporter of efforts to advance medical innovation and improve health outcomes for West Virginians, including through RNI, which is a national leader in the study and treatment of neurological and psychiatric conditions, combining cutting-edge research with patient-centered care.

Senator Capito has worked alongside federal, state, and local partners to help strengthen resources for groundbreaking initiatives at RNI, with a focus on addressing critical challenges such as addiction, Alzheimer’s disease, and other complex brain disorders. Senator Capito recently visited RNI with the Director of the NIH and NIA. In February of 2026, Senator Capito secured the $11.934 million CDS allocation to support construction of the Center for Neuromodulation and Brain Therapeutics. Additionally, Senator Capito reintroduced bipartisan legislation in March of 2026 that bolsters training for primary care providers so they can better diagnose Alzheimer’s and other dementia and deliver high-quality, person-centered care in community-based settings.

Senator Capito’s efforts reflect a broad commitment to fostering collaboration, supporting scientific discovery, and ensuring that West Virginia remains at the forefront of transformative health care solutions.

Individual allocations details listed below:

$11,934,000 CDS award to WVU Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute (Morgantown, W.Va.) to support construction, as well as the acquisition of medical equipment, to establish the WVU Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute Center for Neuromodulation and Brain Therapeutics.

title: Administration Responds to Senators Collins and King by Releasing Home Heating Oil from Northeast Reserve
text:
LEWISTON, ME – The Department of Energy (DOE) has announced that it will release up to 315,000 barrels, a third of the home heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve (NEHHOR). Maine Senators Susan Collins and Angus King urged the Administration to take this step on September 22 to help protect Mainers from high heating oil costs ahead of winter. The Department cites this letter as one of the primary reasons the Administration decided to release oil from the reserve.

“The Administration is committed to doing everything in our power to lower energy costs for the American people,”said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “After receiving Senators Collins’ and King’s letter and extensive discussions with Senator Collins, I have directed the Department to exchange barrels from our Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve to mitigate heightened home heating oil costs during the upcoming winter. Of course, this is a temporary measure to solve a temporary supply disruption. I encourage the governors of New York and New England to work with the Trump Administration to build the Constitution Pipeline and replace home heating oil with low-cost natural gas. Doing so would save their residents billions of dollars in home heating and electricity costs.”

“I am pleased that the Administration has acted upon our request to release heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve,” said Senator Collins. “Approximately half of Maine households rely on fuel oil to heat their homes, and I have repeatedly urged the administration to use every tool to increase supply and lower energy prices. The Department anticipates this release will put downward pressure on home heating oil costs and make a real difference for Maine homeowners as they prepare for winter.”

“Maine has been hit especially hard by the run up in fuel prices since the beginning of the Iran War and the most obvious example is home heating oil,”said Senator King. “Maine is one of the most dependent states in the country on home heating oil and the cost is absolutely through the roof. This release of stored oil in New England will hopefully be some help. While this is good news, we also want to keep pressuring the Administration to bring those prices down before winter really sets in.”

DOE will make the oil available through an exchange, under which companies submit bids to receive barrels from the reserve. The exchange will help reduce the cost of home heating oil in Maine. An increase of 315,000 barrels from NEHHOR represents a 13% supply increase in New England, helping bring down prices at a time when heating oil costs are up more than 70 percent from last year. Some of these barrels are currently stored in South Portland.

NEHHOR reserves have only been released twice in its 26-year history – most recently for an emergency response to Hurricane Sandy. The reserve has never before been used to lower home heating oil prices.

Sen. Collins has also worked with the Department of Energy to release 50 million barrels of diesel and 50 million barrels of crude oil over the next four months. She also pushed the Department of Health and Human Services to release LIHEAP funding at its earliest date to ensure low-income Mainers and seniors on a limited income have the help they need ahead of winter. Last year, Sen. Collins increased LIHEAP funding as Chair of the Appropriations Committee.

title: Cortez Masto Hosts Aerospace and Defense Forum at University of Nevada, Reno
text:
Reno, Nev. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) hosted an Aerospace and Defense Initiative Forum at the University of Nevada, Reno with industry leaders, government agencies, and higher education stakeholders to discuss Northern Nevada’s growing aerospace and defense manufacturing sectors. Forum attendees discussed how to work together to drive investment in Nevada’s emerging industries, create good-paying jobs in the state, and train the next generation of workers.

“Nevada is on the cutting edge of so many technologies that are driving our economy and protecting our national security,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “I want to make sure these industries have the resources they need to recruit workers, innovate, and compete on a global scale. I hope our discussion today is the first of many that will drive collaboration between leaders in the public, private, and education sectors. Together, we can keep Nevada in the driver’s seat when it comes to aerospace, defense, manufacturing, and workforce training.”

Through her Innovation State Initiative, Senator Cortez Masto has led efforts in Congress to support emerging technologies and industries across Nevada. She is leading a bipartisan bill to strengthen the domestic supply chain for rare-earth magnets, which are critical components of cell phones, computers, defense systems, and electric vehicles, and legislation to increase critical mineral production in the American West. She was crucial in securing the University of Nevada, Reno’s designation as a Tech Hub for the critical mineral supply chain. She’s met with U.S. defense and aerospace leaders in Nevada and across the world to discuss the importance of these industries to American national security. Cortez Masto has also been a strong advocate of ensuring that drone technology can be integrated safely and effectively. She fought for the authorization of Nevada as a federally designated FAA UAS test site safe and helped establish the FAA community college training program.

title: Cramer Discusses Rural Healthcare with North Dakota Hospital Association at Annual Convention
text:
***Click here for media resources.***

FARGO, N.D. – The challenges and opportunities for North Dakota’s providers were front and center today at the North Dakota Hospital Association’s (NDHA) 92nd Annual Convention in Fargo, where U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) discussed the state’s approach to strengthening rural hospitals and his work in Washington. Cramer highlighted the practical solutions North Dakota is implementing to enhance the workforce and rural access to care, while challenging the group to focus on transformative changes to worker development and healthcare delivery.

Cramer opened up the floor for discussion to hear directly from NDHA membership about their questions and concerns. Topics included a conversation around the Rural Health Transformation Program and the opportunities stemming from it, which will transform rural healthcare across the state. Members also raised questions about Medicaid and the 340b drug discount program.

“The benefit of being a Senator from North Dakota is I get to know all of the NDHA members and have an opportunity to meet with them and hear firsthand about their successes and challenges,” said Cramer. “This makes me a stronger advocate for them and their colleagues in other states will benefit as a result.”

Cramer has targeted the workforce challenges with legislation expanding employment-based visa opportunities for nurses and physicians and a modernization initiative for the Conrad 30 program to give states and employers more flexibility to recruit international physicians. He introduced legislation to expand veterans’ access to care by authorizing expedited treatment at their local critical access hospital.

He has also cosponsored legislation to streamline prior authorization in Medicare Advantage and make pandemic-era telehealth flexibilities permanent. Those flexibilities, which help patients and providers access care remotely, are set to expire Dec. 31, 2027.

title: Cramer Spotlights North Dakota’s Growing Bioscience Industry at Fargo Summit
text:
***Clickhere for photos.***

FARGO, N.D. – U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) helped kick off the Fourth Annual Bioscience Summit being held in Fargo, setting the tone in the opening address to attendees with an upbeat message: “Big things are happening in medical discovery as well as preventative health right here in North Dakota.”More than 150 entrepreneurs, scientists, and higher education and healthcare professionals gathered with community and economic development leaders at the Avalon Events Center for two days. Attendees will learn the latest trends, capital formation, workforce challenges, and opportunities.

Cramer highlighted North Dakota’s emerging bioscience industry and the role its businesses and universities are playing in research and innovation.

“Big things are happening in medical discovery here in North Dakota, and this innovative ecosystem has always been here, from our Norwegian ancestors to today,” said Cramer. “This has always been a place where people take an idea, put in hard work, apply intellectual rigor, and turn it into something that makes a difference. North Dakota, and especially the Fargo region, has what it takes—the talent, tools, and drive—to advance the bioscience sector and be part of the solution. I love how we don’t need to ask, ‘Why not in North Dakota?’ because our people are already answering the question.”

North Dakota—especially the Fargo region—is home to a growing bioscience industry, and includes companies such as Aldevron, CorVent Medical, Genovac, and Agathos Biologics. According to the Greater Fargo-Moorhead Economic Development Corporation, the region’s bioscience sector generated approximately $89.6 million in earnings and $227.1 million in regional gross product in 2021.

North Dakota’s research institutions are helping fuel the growth. North Dakota State University supports bioscience innovation through its biotechnology and microbiology programs, while the University of North Dakota School of Medicine & Health Sciences conducts more than $40 million in research annually. These efforts help move discoveries from the laboratory toward commercialization, new businesses, and real-world applications.

Through legislation and letters requesting research funding and reduced barriers to medical innovation, Cramer has helped North Dakota’s groundbreaking work in biomedical research and biotechnology advance. He has championed funding for the National Institutes of Health and National Cancer Institute, including research into Alzheimer’s disease and cancer, while supporting FDA modernization to help innovative treatments reach patients.

Additionally, Cramer has backed efforts to strengthen domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing and supply chain resilience by encouraging domestic production of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients and cosponsored legislation to assess the budgetary savings of preventative healthcare policies by extending Health Savings Account eligibility to cover certain preventative interventions including dietary supplements.

title: Crapo Recognized for Affordable Housing Work
text:
Washington, D.C.—U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) is being recognized for his work advancing policies that make affordable housing more accessible to American families. The Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition (AHTCC) presented Crapo with its Affordable Housing Champion Award in honor of his efforts to permanently expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts. The credit is expected to support the financing of 1.2 million new homes over the next 10 years and has already helped provide affordable housing for tens of thousands of low-income Idaho households.

“Idaho’s strong growth in recent years has increased the need for more housing,” said Crapo. “By permanently expanding tax incentives that encourage affordable housing development, the Working Families Tax Cuts are helping communities across Idaho meet growing demand.”

Key housing wins in the Working Families Tax Cuts:

Permanent expansion of the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, supporting the development and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing

Permanent extension of the New Markets Tax Credit to encourage investment and economic development in low-income communities

Permanent renewal and enhancement of Opportunity Zones, with additional incentives for qualified projects in rural areas

According to the Economic Innovation Group, the first iteration of the program increased new housing construction in designated communities by nearly 70 percent

What they are saying:

“The Low-Income Housing Tax Credit has become increasingly essential to providing families with safe, stable housing near jobs, education, health care and other community resources.” – Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition CEO Emily Cadik

“This is a win for Boise. These tax benefits [from Opportunity Zone designations] will help encourage growth and investment by spurring the market to build more homes, start new businesses and create more jobs for our residents.” – Boise Mayor Lauren McLean

title: Crapo, Risch Join Forest Service to Announce Salmon Student Selected to Help Light U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree
text:
Washington, D.C.--U.S. Senators Mike Crapo and Jim Risch (both R-Idaho) announced Grace Benson, a fourth-grade student and the daughter of Jake and Tara Benson from Salmon, Idaho, has been selected as the winner of the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Youth Tree Lighter Essay Contest. Grace will represent Idaho in Washington, D.C., this December, where she will help light the U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree during the annual ceremony on the West Lawn of the Capitol.

“Congratulations to Grace on being selected to represent Idaho in our nation’s capital,” said Crapo. “Her essay highlights the importance of Idaho’s forests, clean water and the connection Idahoans share with our state’s natural resources. This year’s Capitol Christmas Tree is a special opportunity to share Idaho’s natural beauty with the nation, and Grace will play an important role in that celebration.”

“Congratulations to Salmon fourth grader Grace Benson for being selected as the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Lighter!,” said Risch. “Your deep love of Idaho’s forests, water, and resources is a testament to the important role public lands play in our way of life. I look forward to joining you and the tree selected from Idaho’s Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest in Washington, D.C. later this year.”

"As a father of two, I take my responsibility as Forest Supervisor personally and seriously. The decisions we make today on our national forests will shape the experiences of generations to come, including Idaho’s children, like Grace," said Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest Supervisor Jon Word. "What stood out in Grace’s essay was her vivid portrayal of life in rural Idaho and her deep understanding of the strong connection Idahoans share with their public lands and seven national forests. We are proud of her accomplishment and look forward to her sharing her essay on the national stage."

“I am so impressed by Grace's eloquent essay that highlights the natural features of our special town,” said Kristin Foss, Principal of FernWaters Charter. “The fact that she won this statewide contest demonstrates her innate talent and the Fernwaters staff's commitment to our vision for helping small town kids launch big life dreams.”

“My hope is that every student knows their words have power, that they should share them with purpose, and that every voice matters,” said Meriah Baker, Teacher at FernWaters Charter. “Our stories are meaningful, our perspectives have value, and the world deserves to hear what we have to say.”

Earlier this year, Senators Crapo and Risch invited fourth-grade students across Idaho to participate in a statewide essay contest answering the question, “Why are healthy forests and clean water in Idaho important?” The contest followed the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree theme, “Over the Rivers and Through the Woods,” and encouraged students to reflect on the importance of Idaho's natural resources.

Grace's essay was selected through a review process conducted by the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests and the Idaho Forest Restoration Partnership in coordination with the U.S. Forest Service. As the winner, Grace will travel to Washington, D.C., with three family members to participate in the annual U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony, where she will have the opportunity to read her essay and assist in lighting the tree alongside the Speaker of the House and other public officials.

Background:

Idaho's Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests will provide the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree, continuing the annual tradition of selecting a tree from a different national forest to serve as the People's Tree. The tree will be displayed on the West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol throughout the holiday season, showcasing Idaho's natural beauty to visitors from across the country.

title: Durbin Delivers Remarks Highlighting MxD’s Leadership In Technology And Manufacturing During Annual Member Summit
text:
During MxD’s annual Member Summit today, Durbin delivered remarks on the organization’s success in developing technologies that advance cybersecurity and domestic manufacturing

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), a member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense, today attended the annual MxD Member Summit, where he delivered remarks about Illinois’ leadership in technology advancement and research.

MxD—previously known as the Digital Manufacturing and Design Innovation Institute—is one of the U.S. Department of Defense’s (DoD) leading manufacturing institutes that equips U.S. factories with the digital tools, cybersecurity, and workforce expertise to strengthen domestic manufacturing. MxD has developed several outstanding technologies that support both the public and private sector, including the development of a supply chain risk alert that helps companies prepare for disruptions caused by extreme weather; an automated robotic inspection system to modernize additive manufacturing processes at Rock Island Arsenal; and a workforce program that trains more than 10,000 people in a single year on advanced manufacturing, AI, and cybersecurity.

“Whether it’s quantum computing, artificial intelligence, supply chain resiliency, cyber security, or everyday manufacturing, MxD is consistently at the forefront of innovation. This success didn’t happen by accident,” Durbin said. “Every single person and partner in this room has worked alongside MxD to bolster our national security, our economy, and our competitive advantage in the world. And it has been an honor to do my small part in Congress to support you all.”

Photos of the event are available here.

Between Fiscal Year (FY) 2020 and FY2026, Durbin secured $48 million in defense appropriations funding to support MxD’s collaboration with DoD on supply chain mapping, cybersecurity enhancements, modernizing Rock Island Arsenal and other Army facilities, and workforce development.

title: Durbin Urges GAO To Investigate The Trump Administration’s Decision To Establish New, Hidden Immigration Courts
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, sent a letter to the Government Accountability Office (GAO) urging them to investigate the Trump Administration’s decision to rapidly establish new, hidden immigration courts. In the Homeland Security Act, Congress preserved the separation of Department of Homeland Security (DHS) immigration enforcement functions from immigration courts’ adjudicatory role. Yet the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) is establishing new courts in DHS facilities where they are managed by DHS personnel.

“DOJ regulations require that members of the public, including family members and loved ones, have access to immigration courts—but my staff documented DHS officials, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel, regularly prohibiting public access to immigration courtrooms at DHS facilities. Worse still, the Administration has established new court locations—where judges are appearing virtually—without providing formal notice to the public and in apparent violation of regulations and policies intended to ensure transparency and due process in immigration court proceedings,” Durbin wrote.

Immigrants are expected to appear for their immigration court hearings unless a judge has waived their appearance, or they may be ordered removed in absentia. In the letter to GAO, Durbin noted that these new courtrooms seem deliberately designed to increase the number of missed hearings to accelerate removals. For example, EOIR does not make these locations publicly available, despite EOIR policy stating a complete list of immigration courts is available on its website.

In the letter, Durbin also noted that EOIR appears to be targeting individuals who do not have legal representation. The Administration’s unprecedented decision to open courts in DHS buildings worsens these due process concerns, given that DHS is the party seeking the removal of immigrants in immigration court proceedings, serving as the prosecutor in these matters. According to recent reports, over the summer, the White House directed DHS to find space for additional courts, and DHS components such as ICE, FEMA, the Coast Guard, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services volunteered.

Durbin wrote, “My staff have observed that these new courtrooms are not just housed within DHS facilities, but DHS is controlling access to the facilities. Immigration court proceedings are open to the public with few exceptions, yet DHS personnel—not EOIR personnel—barred my staff from entering the court in the FEMA building on three separate occasions. During these attempted visits, my staff observed that the doors to the courtroom were locked, and the courtroom lacked any signage, a violation of EOIR policy. During one of the visits, a person who identified herself as a DHS contractor stated that my staff would have to contact FEMA personnel and DHS to gain access because the courtroom was located in a ‘secure’ federal building and was ‘not open to the public.’”

Durbin continued, “My staff also observed DHS agents and contractors prevent the family of unrepresented respondents from entering the courtroom. There was no evidence EOIR personnel were physically present at the court in the FEMA building, and no DHS personnel or contractors would acknowledge that EOIR, not DHS, oversaw immigration court operations. The placement of courts within DHS buildings seems to have no other purpose than to intimidate unrepresented respondents and increase the likelihood that individuals will fail to appear at hearings and be ordered removed in absentia.”

GAO previously has reported that problems with notices, changes in hearing dates, lack of understanding of court processes, and confusion regarding the differences between immigration courts and DHS can affect respondents’ ability to appear for hearings and lead to in absentia removal orders, even when respondents intended to participate in their proceedings. The new courts raise many of these issues, in addition to unprecedented concerns regarding DHS’s direct participation in running our immigration court system.

In the letter, Durbin requested GAO address a number of questions about these new, hidden immigration courts.

Durbin concluded, “It is vital to understand the threats to due process and judicial independence posed by this Administration’s restructuring of the immigration court system. Although Congress separated immigration enforcement functions from the immigration courts, DHS-managed immigration courts should end any illusion that courts are operating independently of this Administration’s mass deportation machine.”

Full text of the letter is available here.

title: Fetterman Announces $42.2 Million in Funding for Pennsylvania’s Rail Infrastructure
text:
BRADDOCK, PA — Today, U.S. Senator Fetterman (D-PA) announced $42,287,800 in funding for Pennsylvania’s rail infrastructure through the Federal Railroad Administration’s (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvement (CRISI) Program. Three of the four awards were supported by Senator Fetterman and the funds will improve safety, efficiency, and reliability along four of the Commonwealth’s rail corridors: the Lehigh Valley Rail corridor in Bethlehem, the Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad in Western Pennsylvania, the Colebrookdale Railroad connecting Berks and Montgomery counties, and the Everett Railroad in Blair County.

“Railroads have powered Pennsylvania for generations, and today, the Commonwealth has one of the largest rail networks in the nation. Investing in this infrastructure is crucial for our communities and our economy,” said Senator Fetterman. “I’m grateful to Secretary Duffy and FRA Administrator Fink for honoring Pennsylvania’s rail legacy and investing in its future.”

$15,894,420 for Lehigh Valley Rail Management LLC (Lehigh Valley Rail Corridor)

This funding will support track rehabilitation and related improvements along the Lehigh Valley Rail corridor in Bethlehem. Upgrades include turnout replacements, bridge and terminal improvements, and capacity upgrades to support the modern 286,000-pound weight standard for freight railcars. This investment will improve safety, enhance freight mobility, and bolster economic opportunity for the region’s manufacturers and businesses. In July, Senator Fetterman wrote a letter of support for LVRM’s application to FRA Administrator David Fink.

“Lehigh Valley Rail Management and Phoenix Rail are proud to partner with our customers, the Federal Railroad Administration, and our champions in Congress,” said LVRM CEO Alex Yeros. “The STEEL project is an investment to modernize aging infrastructure, breathing new life into a critical node in the national rail network with over a century of contributing to the Pennsylvania economy. We are grateful for their support of a project that will strengthen the safety, reliability, and efficiency of our railroad, and support job growth for our customers and the Lehigh Valley.”

$13,621,400 for the Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad (BPRR)

This award will support critical upgrades to two bridges and one tunnel along BPRR’s main line in Western Pennsylvania. Specifically, these funds would support steel and span rehabilitation for the 1,680-foot-long Mosgrove Bridge, which was constructed in 1899; enable upgrades to components and steel structures for two 50-foot-long timber bridges over Connoquenessing Creek in BPRR’s Butler Yard; and provide critical arch restoration and improved clearances for the 2,322-foot-long Simpson Tunnel, which was built in 1899 and suffered a partial ceiling collapse in 2024. Senator Fetterman advocated for this funding in a letter to FRA Administrator Fink in July.

“Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad is grateful for the support from our elected officials in the state. These funds will help carry out critical upgrades to our freight-rail infrastructure in Western Pennsylvania, enabling us to provide safer transportation service to area industries that rely on us,” said a representative for Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad.

$10,108,230 for the Eastern Berks Gateway Railroad Company (Colebrookdale Railroad)

This funding will rehabilitate approximately five miles of track along the Colebrookdale Railroad, an active freight and heritage tourist railroad connecting Berks and Montgomery counties. This CRISI award builds on a recent $25 million investment in the railroad’s Pottstown terminal through the Department of Transportation’s Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) program. Senator Fetterman fought for both of these awards and submitted letters of support to FRA Administrator Fink and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy for the CRISI and BUILD projects respectively.

“Berks County and the Eastern Berks Gateway Railroad are grateful for the strong support of Senator Fetterman and the entire federal delegation. The joint letter of support from Senators Fetterman and McCormick played an important role in securing this grant, which provides the final funding needed to complete the core track infrastructure connecting Boyertown in Berks County with Pottstown in Montgomery County,” said Christian Y. Leinbach, Chair of the Berks County Board of Commissioners.

“We’re grateful to our federal partners, Senators Fetterman and McCormick, and Congresswoman Dean, for continuing to invest in the Colebrookdale Railroad and the communities it connects. This $10 million investment will help strengthen an important piece of our region’s infrastructure while preserving a unique part of Pennsylvania’s history for generations to come,” said Jamila Winder, Chair of the Montgomery County Board of Commissioners.

“Tourism and recreation bring people to Montgomery County, support local businesses, and generate economic activity that strengthens our communities. We’re grateful to Senator Fetterman and our federal partners for helping secure another major federal investment that builds on that momentum while supporting one of our region’s unique historic assets,” said Montgomery County Commissioner Neil Makhija.

“This investment keeps the momentum going for the Colebrookdale Railroad and the Pottstown area. It will help bring more visitors to the region, support local businesses, and build on the progress already underway in this important part of Montgomery County,” said Montgomery County Commissioner Tom DiBello.

The remaining $2,663,750 is awarded to the Everett Railroad Company to support track rehabilitation and rail equipment for the Everett Railroad, a heritage railroad in Blair Country.

title: Gallego Celebrates Chiricahua Becoming Arizona’s Fourth National Park
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) celebrated the Chiricahua National Park Act being signed into law by President Donald Trump. The bipartisan legislation designates Chiricahua National Monument in Cochise County as Chiricahua National Park. The designation made Chiricahua Arizona’s fourth national park — alongside Grand Canyon, Petrified Forest, and Saguaro National Parks. The designation will protect Chiricahua’s unique landscape while bringing more visitors and economic opportunities to rural southeastern Arizona.

“Arizona has some of the most beautiful public lands in the country, and Chiricahua is no exception,” said Senator Gallego. “Making Chiricahua our state’s fourth national park is a big win for Cochise County and will attract more tourists and spending to the region while protecting this incredible landscape for generations to come.”

Established in 1924, Chiricahua National Monument spans more than 12,000 acres of towering rock formations, canyons, and diverse wildlife in Cochise County. The designation will protect Chiricahua’s unique landscape for future generations while bringing more visitors and economic opportunities to southeastern Arizona. The law also includes protections for traditional cultural and religious sites and ensures continued access for Tribal members for traditional cultural and customary uses.

Senator Gallego and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) introduced the Senate legislation in January, while Representatives Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ) and Greg Stanton (D-AZ) advanced the legislation in the House. The House passed the bill in March, followed by the Senate in September.

title: Gallego, Colleagues Demand Answers from EPA over Changes Threatening Clean Air at Grand Canyon, National Parks
text:
Senators emphasize the imposed changes to federal air pollution protections could threaten Arizona’s public lands, tourism, and local economies

WASHINGTON – This week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and 10 of their Democratic colleagues in sending a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin, demanding answers over recent changes to the Regional Haze Program that could weaken protections against air pollution at the Grand Canyon and national parks across the country.

In their letter to Administrator Zeldin, the senators raised concerns that the EPA is allowing states to avoid new pollution reductions and considering additional changes to the program, which was established to protect visibility at national parks and wilderness areas. The senators also warned that weakening these protections could threaten public health, obscure iconic landscapes, and hurt local economies that depend on tourism.

The senators highlighted the importance of protecting clean air and visibility at national parks: “Preserving the iconic views of these treasured parks and wilderness areas is why Congress established the Regional Haze Program nearly fifty years ago, recognizing that some landscapes are simply too important to allow pollution to obscure. Yet today, 98 percent of national parks suffer from hazy skies, reducing visibility by an average of 50 miles.”

The senators reaffirmed that reducing haze-forming pollution also protects public health and local economies: “Haze is more than a visibility problem. The same fine particle pollution that obscures views at national parks across the country also poses great harm to public health. Fine particulate matter, including particles formed from sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides emissions, have been linked to asthma, decreased lung function, heart problems, and premature death in people with existing conditions. Reducing haze-forming pollution helps protect not only the views that draw millions of visitors to our national parks, but also the health of those visitors and nearby communities.”

The senators urged the EPA to uphold the Clean Air Act and continue making progress toward restoring visibility at national parks: “Congress established the Regional Haze Rule to ensure that future generations can experience places like the Grand Canyon, Yosemite, Yellowstone, Shenandoah, Rocky Mountain, Crater Lake, and other national parks and wilderness areas as they were meant to be seen. It is important that changes to the program remain consistent with the Clean Air Act and continue making meaningful progress toward that goal.”

In addition to Senators Gallego and Kelly, the letter was signed by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Edward Markey (D-MA), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Jeffrey Merkley (D-OR), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Charles Schumer (D-NY), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Michael Bennet (D-CO).

title: Gallego, Kelly Bill to Pave Way for Gila County Veterans Center Becomes Law
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ)celebrated the passage of their bipartisan legislation — which was signed into law by the president — to transfer the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County. The law makes way for the development of a veterans retreat and community center to support the nearly 5,500 military veterans who call the county home.

“Caring for our men and women in uniform after their duty ends is a solemn national obligation, and this center makes good on that promise. This center will serve as a place to build community, connect, and will provide critical services to our vets that they have rightfully earned,” said Senator Gallego. “Our veterans had our backs. I’ll make sure we have theirs, too.”

“The day is finally here. Veterans in rural Arizona deserve a place where they can gather and get the care they need closer to home,” said Senator Kelly. “Now we’re officially on track to turn this site into a retreat and community center that will serve them and their families.”

“We are very grateful to Senators Kelly and Gallego for their belief in this project from our very first meeting. This conveyance is a huge accomplishment for all of us involved as I believe it is the first such project with state, county and federal participation for our nation’s veterans. As a county, we are moving forward to finalize the necessary steps needed to complete the conveyance and continue providing a beautiful and peaceful respite for our nation’s heroes,” said Gila County District 3 Supervisor Woody Cline.

The law directs the U.S. Forest Service to transfer 232.9 acres of underutilized National Forest land near Young, Arizona, to Gila County. Once transferred, the site will be transformed into a dedicated space for veterans and their families to gather for retreats, meetings, and community events. The center will also serve as a mobile VA clinic site, expanding access to critical health care services for veterans in rural Arizona.

title: Gillibrand, Duckworth, Schiff Press FDA On Plan To Mitigate Estrogen Patch Shortage
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) pressed the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on its plan to mitigate the estradiol transdermal patch shortage, which is making it harder for women to manage symptoms of menopause.

Estradiol transdermal patches are the clinically preferred, first-line treatment for managing menopause symptoms like hot flashes, night sweats, mood changes, and vaginal dryness. However, over the last year, the drug supply chain has failed to meet increased demand for estradiol patches, leaving thousands of women to navigate administrative chaos and, in some cases, ration or discontinue use of the patches.

In a letter to FDA—which was co-signed by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and Adam Schiff (D-CA)—-Senator Gillibrand demanded additional details about how FDA is exercising its statutory authority to alleviate the estradiol patch shortage.

“Estradiol patches are a first-line, widely used, and highly effective treatment for managing menopause symptoms, and FDA should be doing everything in its power to make sure this therapy is available to all women who need it,” said Senator Gillibrand. “As the top Democrat on the Senate Aging Committee, I am demanding a clear plan from FDA to mitigate the estradiol patch shortage. This is an urgent women’s health priority, and I will not rest until we have answers.”

This letter builds on Senator Gillibrand’s work to improve menopause research, training, and care. Last month, in her capacity as ranking member of the Senate Aging Committee, Senator Gillibrand held the first ever congressional hearing on menopause. She also led a bipartisan letter to the Government Accountability Office (GAO) requesting a report on the federal government’s current role in menopause care and research. Gillibrand is also a cosponsor of the Advancing Menopause Care and Mid-Life Women’s Health Act, bipartisan legislation that would authorize $275 million over five years to strengthen and expand federal menopause research, healthcare workforce training, and education efforts related to mid-life women’s health.

The full text of the letter can be found here or below:

Dear Acting Commissioner Diamantas,

We write to express concern regarding the ongoing widespread shortage of transdermal estradiol patches. On September 16, 2026, the Senate Special Committee on Aging held a hearing highlighting the systemic menopause care gap in the United States. During the hearing, the Committee heard testimony from researchers, providers, and patients who detailed how unpredictable access to transdermal estradiol over the past year has disrupted care for hundreds of thousands of American women.

Estradiol transdermal patches represent the clinically preferred, first-line treatment for menopausal symptom management, and estrogen hormone therapy remains the single most effective intervention for severe vasomotor symptoms, including hot flashes and night sweats. The FDA’s November 2025 removal of boxed warnings on hormone replacement therapies (HRT) for menopause management was a positive step in increasing access to safe, effective care. However, this regulatory shift, coupled with increased awareness and research, surged demand for HRT among menopausal women, resulting in a dramatic year-over-year increase in prescriptions nationwide.

It has become clear that the pharmaceutical supply chain has failed to adequately respond to this surge in demand. Reports from the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (ASHP) indicate that nearly 20 distinct estrogen patch formulations have been severely impacted by supply disruptions over the last calendar year. As a result, thousands of women are struggling to navigate administrative chaos—bouncing between competing pharmacy chains, transferring prescriptions between locations, switching formulation brands, or resorting to stretching doses or splitting patches. In some cases, patients have been forced to discontinue this effective therapy altogether.

While we acknowledge the FDA’s update on September 3, 2026 addressing the estradiol patch supply, the Committee remains concerned about the Agency’s delay in addressing this crisis and has additional questions regarding remedial steps to ensure patients can access effective therapies. Unfortunately, it took four months of inquiry for the FDA to issue basic advice telling patients to contact their pharmacist or speak with their healthcare provider. Passive monitoring and generic advice fail to adequately mitigate a nationwide manufacturing deficit.

To ensure the FDA is exercising its full statutory authority to alleviate this crisis, we request written responses to the following questions no later than November 16, 2026:

1. What criteria must the disruptions in estradiol patches meet for the FDA to declare an official estradiol patch shortage on the official Drug Shortage Database, unlocking emergency regulation tools?

2. What metrics is the FDA using to monitor manufacturer capacity for transdermal estradiol products, and when did the Agency’s staff first identify an imbalance between national demand and production volume?

3. The September 2026 update notes that the FDA is working closely with manufacturers to ensure supply of estradiol patches keeps pace with demand. What remedial steps has the FDA taken since the shortage was first identified to increase supply long-term?

a. What is the baseline volume of production from late 2025 compared to current capacity?

b. When do you anticipate that production will meet full market demand?

4. How many prior-approval submissions for new manufacturing lines, expanded batch sizes, site additions, specialized equipment, or other production expansion requests related to estradiol patches has the FDA received since November 2025?

a. What is the average review time for these expedited requests?

b. Did FDA drug shortage staff forecast market impacts following the removal of the black box warning on HRT to

prepare for the surge in demand?

5. Given that scaling transdermal delivery manufacturing involves complex machinery and long lead times, what interim regulatory tools is the FDA considering to address the immediate deficit?

a. Will this involve temporary allowance of supplies from countries not previously approved for import? If so, will

FDA perform expedited site inspections for previously unexamined overseas manufacturing facilities?

6. Why did the FDA require four months of formal inquiry to issue basic patient guidance, and what concrete steps is the Agency taking to improve real-time public messaging and inventory reporting during active drug shortages?

7. How many staff currently work on identifying and mitigating drug shortages at FDA? How many employees are specifically focused on remedying the estradiol patch shortage?

8. What policies is the FDA implementing to check major labeling updates, boxed warning removals, or updated clinical guidelines with national supply chain forecasting to prevent similar drug shortages following updated regulatory guidance?

a. Does the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) perform supply chain impact reviews prior to

issuing major safety labeling changes like removing boxed warnings?

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent women’s health priority. We look forward to receiving your response and working together to investigate this issue.

Sincerely,

###

title: Grassley and Bipartisan Colleagues Push Pentagon to Crack Down on Military Contractors’ Price Gouging, Enforce Cost Transparency
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) sent a bipartisan letter to the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) requesting DOD hold defense contractors accountable and bolster its August 18 directive on Supplier Cost and Pricing Transparency.

The senators are also urging DOD to support their bipartisan Transparency in Contract Pricing Act in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The bill would better arm contracting officers with statutory backing during negotiations, improve pricing transparency and ensure taxpayers get a fair deal.

The DOD’s Supplier Cost and Pricing Transparency directive seeks to improve access to contractors’ cost and pricing data and help the Pentagon’s contracting officers negotiate fair prices. The senators welcomed the directive but raised concerns that a key gap in the policy — applying a $10 million threshold for obtaining certified cost and pricing data — could leave the DOD without access to critical information for more than 60% of its contracts. They urged the Pentagon to apply its new directive to lower-value contracts and use its existing authority to make contractors ineligible for awards when they refuse to provide requested data.

For decades, defense contractors have taken advantage of the Pentagon’s inability to prevent price gouging. The DOD notoriously paid $436 for hammers and $640 for toilet seats in the 1980s. More recently, Boeing charged the Air Force a nearly 8,000% markup on lavatory soap dispensers.

“The culture of overcharging within the defense industry that has driven this behavior has come with significant costs to both readiness and the American taxpayer,” the senators wrote.

“To ensure our understanding of how this directive ‘resets the Department’s expectations regarding supplier cost and pricing information’ and how it will gain transparency through ‘modern information technology and current business best practices,’ we seek to clarify how the Department will gain such data from refusing companies, conduct consistent oversight, and hold non-compliant companies accountable,” the senators concluded.

The senators requested answers to their questions by November 3, 2026, to inform legislation aimed at strengthening pricing transparency, preventing contractor abuse and protecting taxpayer dollars.

Read the senators’ full letter HERE.

title: Hassan, Colleagues Demand Trump Administration Withdraw Proposal to Undermine E-Rate Program
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan joined colleagues in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to withdraw the Commission’s harmful proposal to eliminate or limit the E-Rate program, which helps schools and libraries across New Hampshire afford reliable internet access.

For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped close the digital divide by ensuring that students and library patrons can access the internet regardless of their income or ZIP code. In 2025, E-Rate helped more than 158,000 schools and libraries pay recurring broadband bills, increase bandwidth, maintain secure internal Wi-Fi networks, and replace aging infrastructure. In New Hampshire alone, E-Rate has helped 430 schools and libraries expand their internet capacity. Ending or sharply curtailing E-Rate would impose severe costs on schools, libraries and property taxpayers, while weakening economic growth, undermining American technological leadership, and jeopardizing national security. The E-Rate program has invested more than $69 billion to connect schools and libraries to the internet across the country.

“Schools and libraries help develop the next generation of engineers, scientists, and cybersecurity professionals, including in communities that have historically lacked access to those opportunities. Cutting E-Rate would narrow that talent pipeline. Maintaining connectivity in every school and library is therefore an investment in America’s technological leadership, economic competitiveness, and national security,” Senator Hassan and her colleagues wrote to Chairman Carr.

The lawmakers continued, “We strongly support measures to protect children online and address concerns around excessive screen time. But cutting E-Rate is not a child-safety measure. E-Rate funds broadband connectivity — not laptops, tablets, applications, or online content — and recipients must already comply with the Children’s Internet Protection Act, including by using filtering and blocking tools, adopting internet-safety policies, and educating students about appropriate online behavior. States and local communities, meanwhile, are developing targeted policies governing when and how students use devices in schools — an appropriate way to address screen-time concerns, rather than cutting broadband support. The Commission should not use child safety as a pretext to dismantle the secure, managed broadband infrastructure that schools and libraries need to educate students and help them navigate the digital world safely.”

Read the full text of Senator Hassan and her colleagues’ request to the FCC here.
