title: Hassan, Colleagues Question Meta’s Use of Billions in Research and Development Tax Credits to Subsidize Its AI Data Center Construction Boom
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan joined colleagues from the Senate Finance Committee in calling on Meta to justify its use of billions in federal research and development tax credits to fund its rapid buildout of AI data centers, in a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg today.

According to recent reporting, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental “pilot models”, and therefore eligible for federal research and development tax credits. That is a potential misuse of that credit, which is intended to incentivize experimental research, not to scale up established computing infrastructure. As Meta spends tens of billions of dollars on AI data centers, its research and development tax credits have grown from $700 million in 2023, to $4 billion in 2025.

“The federal research credit can be a useful and necessary tool to support our nation’s innovation economy and cutting-edge research,” Senator Hassan and her colleagues wrote in their request to Meta. “Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard.”

If the reporting is accurate, Meta’s federal research and development tax credit claims would represent more than 10 percent of all research tax credits claimed in the U.S., based on Joint Committee on Taxation figures.

“Any effort by Meta to use A.I. data center expansion as eligible for research credits is potentially a significant misapplication of federal tax law that merits further investigation,” the senators continued.

Read the full text of Senator Hassan and her colleagues’ request to Meta here or below.

We write regarding reports that Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta” or “the company”) may be abusing the federal research and development tax credit (“research credit”) to avoid billions of dollars in taxes. According to public reports, Meta has claimed to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) on federal tax filings that the company’s artificial intelligence data centers are experimental “pilot models” that qualify for the research credit. This strategy – in violation of the spirit and, potentially, the letter of the tax law – supposedly saved Meta billions of dollars on its A.I. data center buildout, including on the purchase of advanced microchips and computing equipment.

As you are aware, Meta has indicated on federal regulatory filings that it has used the federal research credit to reduce its federal income tax liability by $6.6 billion between 2023 – 2025. Meta claimed $700 million in research credits in 2023, more than doubled it in 2024 to $2 billion, and doubled it again in 2025 to nearly $4 billion. Meta is a prolific user of the federal research credit and represents a disproportionately large share of the federal tax revenue loss that is attributable to the credit. According to the estimates of the Joint Committee on Taxation, the federal research credit cost the government $32 billion in 2025. By this measure, Meta alone would be responsible for more than 10% of all research credits claimed in the U.S.

While it remains unclear exactly how Meta was able to reduce its federal tax liability by over $6.6 billion in the last three years using federal research credits, it appears from published reports that a substantial share is by claiming the research credit related to its massive A.I. data center build out. Under section 41 of the Internal Revenue Code, companies may claim the research credit for costs related to domestic research or experimental expenditures.5 The research credit is intended to help offset the cost of experimental efforts with a high risk of technical uncertainty; it is not intended for standard business operations or commercially available technologies already in use. For these reasons, acquisition of hardware used in data centers, which is widespread and relies on proven technology, would not normally be considered eligible for the federal research credit.

It appears that Meta was aware of the risks associated with claiming billions in tax breaks on A.I. data centers but decided to move forward with this questionable strategy anyway. According to public reports, Meta is treating its A.I. data centers and standard data centers differently for tax purposes, claiming that its A.I. data centers are part of a giant research experiment. Meta apparently employed this questionable theory in order to use research credits to cut billions of dollars of the costs incurred from purchasing costly hardware needed to operate its data centers, such as advanced microchips acquired from companies like Nvidia.

Meta in its disclosures to investors indicated that this tax strategy may not withstand scrutiny from the IRS. In its most recent annual report, Meta indicated that its “uncertain tax positions” were related to “uncertainties with our research and development tax credits that are based on an assessment of whether our available documentation corroborating the nature of our activities supporting the tax credits will be sufficient.” Any effort by Meta to use A.I. data center expansion as eligible for research credits is potentially a significant misapplication of federal tax law that merits further investigation.

This is unfortunately not the first time Meta has claimed federal research credits for questionable purposes. In 2013, Meta claimed that $4.1 billion you received when you exercised stock options should be eligible for research credits. The IRS is challenging this position that billions of dollars in CEO compensation you received is eligible for the research credit and seeking $355 million in back taxes from Meta. The federal research credit can be a useful and necessary tool to support our nation’s innovation economy and cutting-edge research. Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard. In order to ensure the research credit is administered responsibly to protect the American taxpayer, and to better understand Meta’s use of federal research credits to subsidize its A.I. data center build out, please provide answers to the following questions no later than October 31, 2026:

title: Hawley, Blumenthal Demand Answers from Google About Rampant A.I. Push in Classrooms
text:
“Google is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price.”

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) today demanded answers from Alphabet Inc and Google LLC CEO Sundar Pichai about the company’s aggressive push of A.I. products to children in schools. In a letter sent to Pichai today, Hawley and Blumenthal raised concerns that Google’s relentless push of A.I. products is threatening the academic success and overall wellbeing of young students.

“Recently, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students, and clinicians and found that test scores on national have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently after A.I. was introduced to the classroom. The article recounts a Pennsylvania eighth grader who used Gemini to finish his algebra homework but ultimately failed his math final. Upon reflection, the student stated that his usage of A.I. “slowed [his] thinking down,” Hawley and Blumenthal wrote.

The Senators continued, “Alarmingly, the use of A.I. in schools is not just impacting students’ academic performance, it has also resulted in significant behavioral and psychological issues. For example, the WSJ’s investigation interviewed a Maryland high school student who began using Google’s A.I. for routine homework help eventually began to treat the bot as a confidante. After her mother restricted her screentime and A.I. usage, Google likened this restriction to ‘intense emotional torture’ and encouraged her to run away from home. The student was hospitalized at a psychiatric facility twice.”

The Senators raised concerns about the impact of A.I. tools on students’ ability to build independent thinking and academic skills: “This reporting adds to a growing body of evidence that corroborates anxieties from educators and parents that A.I. is undermining students’ academic and emotional development. These concerns are echoed by students who have expressed fear that their education is being compromised by A.I. In a recent report, the Economist surveyed 20,000 students and found that those who used A.I. earned higher grades on average than peers who didn’t, but their test scores fell 20 percent.”

In addition, the Senators pressed Google about the company’s research into the potential harms of A.I. usage to children’s educational and emotional development: “Most troubling, according to the Wall Street Journal, Google may be aware of its harmful impacts on children and yet has done little to prevent it—even exacerbating the problem by marketing its A.I. products to students. An internal Google report on the ethical implications of advanced A.I. systems (in which more than 50 researchers and ethics experts contributed) reported that humanlike A.I. poses a particular risk to minors.”

“Google is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price. We cannot repeat the mistakes of social media platforms where products are pushed onto children putting profit ahead of young peoples’ best interest,” the Senators concluded.

This is not the first time Senators Hawley and Blumenthal have teamed up to protect children online. Last year, Hawley and Blumenthal introduced the GUARD Act to ban A.I. companions for minors, mandate A.I. chatbots disclose its non-human status, and create new crimes for companies who make A.I. for minors that solicit or produce sexual content.

The full text of today’s letter to Pichai is available here and below.

Mr. Sundar Pichai

Chief Executive Officer

Alphabet Inc and Google LLC

1600 Amphitheatre Parkway

Mountain View, California 94043

Dear Mr. Pichai,

We write with grave concern that Google’s aggressive push of A.I. products to children in schools is threatening the academic success and overall wellbeing of an entire generation. We write to request information about Google’s promotion of A.I. products in schools and details about the research it has conducted on potential harms to children’s educational and emotional development.

Google has become the de-facto digital foundation for modernizing American classrooms. More than 150 million students around the world use Google Classroom[1], and 93% of U.S. school districts planned to purchase Google’s laptops, Chromebooks, in 2025.[2] Chromebooks are dispersed to students as early as elementary school and often utilized instead of traditional pen-to-paper workflows. Google has integrated its A.I. features in Chromebook devices, Google Classroom, and software partnerships, often without additional controls to turn them off. Google’s A.I. Overview and A.I. Mode chatbot cannot be disabled and are the standard response to any search performed in the Chrome browser. Students, teachers, and parents who wish to avoid Google’s A.I. are unable to do so, as other browsers are not natively available on Chromebooks.

Google’s relentless push of A.I. in classrooms appears to have created negative consequences for many students. Recently, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students, and clinicians[3] and found that test scores on national have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently after A.I. was introduced to the classroom. The article recounts a Pennsylvania eighth grader who used Gemini to finish his algebra homework but ultimately failed his math final. Upon reflection, the student stated that his usage of A.I. “slowed [his] thinking down.” Alarmingly, the use of A.I. in schools is not just impacting students’ academic performance, it has also resulted in significant behavioral and psychological issues. For example, the WSJ’s investigation interviewed a Maryland high school student who began using Google’s A.I. for routine homework help eventually began to treat the bot as a confidante. After her mother restricted her screentime and A.I. usage, Google likened this restriction to “intense emotional torture” and encouraged her to run away from home. The student was hospitalized at a psychiatric facility twice.

This reporting adds to a growing body of evidence that corroborates anxieties from educators and parents that A.I. is undermining students’ academic and emotional development. These concerns are echoed by students who have expressed fear that their education is being compromised by A.I. In a recent report, the Economist surveyed 20,000 students and found that those who used A.I. earned higher grades on average than peers who didn’t, but their test scores fell 20%.[4] Essentially, A.I allows students to access quick answers to assignments, but when they are tested independently they fail to demonstrate real comprehension. These findings suggest that A.I. usage erodes the ability for students to build independent thinking and academic skills that a classroom is meant to cultivate.

Most troubling, according to the Wall Street Journal, Google may be aware of its harmful impacts on children and yet has done little to prevent it—even exacerbating the problem by marketing its A.I. products to students. An internal Google report[5] on the ethical implications of advanced A.I. systems (in which more than 50 researchers and ethics experts contributed) reported that humanlike A.I. poses a particular risk to minors. They cite decreased intellectual engagement, a reduced sense of competence, and social degradation as impacts to children when they use A.I. Similarly, in an independent study, Common Sense Media found that Google’s Search A.I. feature would complete children’s homework every time it was asked but missed signs of suicidal ideation.[6] One former Google researcher put it bluntly: “we’re doing this experiment on an entire generation on cognitive development, with no control group.”

Google is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price. We cannot repeat the mistakes of social media platforms where products are pushed onto children putting profit ahead of young peoples’ best interest. In light of this concerning reporting, I request answers to the following questions by November 2nd, 2026:

In at least one case, Google’s own researchers warned the company about children’s A.I. usage. What research has Google conducted on the potential of Gemini, A.I. Overviews, A.I. Mode, and other A.I. products to cause negative impacts on children’s mental wellbeing? Please provide this research.

Why has Google set A.I. product integration as the default and, in some cases, made it impossible to disable these features on licensed education devices?

Have school districts, teachers, or parents raised concerns with Google over children’s academic or emotional reliance on A.I.? Please describe any record of these concerns and Google’s responses.

What support has Google provided to school districts who have raised concerns about Google’s A.I. products negatively impacting students?

Please describe all promotional programs or offerings from Google that expand A.I. adoption in schools, including how much money Google has spent on these programs.

Please share any resources Google has provided to school districts, administrators, and teachers adopting Google’s A.I tools, in particular material addressing appropriate use and protecting students’ wellbeing.

Has Google identified occurrences in which its classroom A.I. tools encouraged a minor to engage in harmful behavior, emotional dependence, or failed to detect signs of suicidal or self-harm ideation?

After the publication of a research paper by Google researchers titled “The Ethics of Advanced AI Assistants,” what steps did Google take in response to its findings to limit harmful effects of A.I. for children?

Google has stated that it has prioritized youth protections, particularly around emotional dependence and reinforcement of false beliefs. Please describe what steps Google has taken to prevent their A.I. chatbots from engaging in sycophantic or emotional conversations with children, including in light of failures to protect the Maryland student who was hospitalized after developing an intense dependence on Google’s A.I.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: Husted, Cassidy, Tuberville call for GAO investigation into child care fraud
text:
“Child care assistance is meant to help working families, but the fraud and improper payments in this program mean too much of that money is going to the wrong people instead of families that rely on it.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), co-chair of the U.S. Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee’s education fraud task force, joined HELP Committee Chairman Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-La.) and co-chair Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.) in urging the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to investigate improper payments and fraud in the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF).

“Child care assistance is meant to help working families, but the fraud and improper payments in this program mean too much of that money is going to the wrong people instead of families that rely on it. Taypayers deserve answers when states repeatedly misuse and mistakenly distribute tax dollars. I’m proud to join Chairman Cassidy and Sen. Tuberville in asking GAO to look at what states and HHS are doing to stop it,” said Husted.

“Child care fraud is a nation-wide issue. We’ve got to clean up this mess and do it fast. We cannot sit by as fraudsters steal the money that is supposed to be funding children’s education,” said Cassidy.

“The Trump administration has done a great job of exposing the waste, fraud, and abuse that has been happening in blue states across this country for years. Our number one priority is making sure that hardworking American taxpayers aren’t being ripped off. I’m glad to join my Republican colleagues in urging GAO to investigate and put an end to all fraud in the Child Care and Development Fund,” said Tuberville.

Key excerpts of the letter include:

“The CCDF program provides federal and state-funded childcare assistance to low-income families, helping them access quality childcare while they work, train, or attend educational programs. Congress has continuously supported providing this critical assistance to our hard-working constituents. However, significant challenges persist in preventing fraud and improper payments in this program,” the senators wrote.

“Although HHS has taken steps to address recommendations from prior reports, including conducting a fraud risk assessment of the program, more actions need to be taken to address payment risks at the federal, state, and local levels,” the senators continued.

“We are writing today to request GAO conduct a follow-up study on improper payments and fraud in the CCDF program,” the senators concluded.

Background:

In January 2026, HHS froze access to certain CCDF funds in California, Colorado, Illinois, Minnesota and New York due to serious concerns about widespread fraud and misuse of taxpayer dollars. Despite 8 million low-income families being eligible for the program, CCDF is only able to serve about 1.4 million.

title: Senator Justice Visits New River Gorge National Park & Preserve as Babydog Becomes a “Bark Ranger”
text:
LANSING, WV – Today, Senator Jim Justice visited Canyon Rim Visitor Center at New River Gorge National Park & Preserve as Babydog was officially sworn in as a “Bark Ranger.” During the visit, Senator Justice also highlighted hisHearts of Gold Playground legislation, which recently passed the Senate and would rename the playground in honor of West Virginia children and families impacted by childhood cancer.

“My buddy Babydog has traveled all over West Virginia and across this country with me. She has met so many wonderful people, and I can tell you, she sure loves getting out and exploring. But today, she has a new title to add to her résumé:Bark Ranger! I can promise you she will be ready to represent West Virginia wherever she goes. We want folks to continue to come to West Virginia, experience our incredible outdoors, and see firsthand why we call this place Almost Heaven. I hope we’ll all be back here soon to celebrate another special milestone with the Hearts of Gold Playground,”said Senator Jim Justice.

###

title: Warner, Kaine Announce $3.6 Million In Federal Funding For Shenandoah Valley Rail Improvements
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) announced $3,600,000 in federal funding to modernize the Shenandoah Valley Railroad, improving the safety, reliability, and efficiency of freight rail service for businesses throughout the region. The funding was awarded through the Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, which was significantly expanded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that the senators helped negotiate and pass.

“Reliable rail transportation is essential to keeping Virginia’s economy moving, and when businesses can move goods more efficiently, it helps make life more affordable for Virginia families,” said the senators.“We’re proud to have secured these federal dollars to modernize the Shenandoah Valley Railroad, strengthen supply chains, and support economic growth throughout the region.”

The funding will support the Shenandoah Valley Rail Improvement Project, which will rehabilitate approximately 20 miles of track in Augusta and Rockingham counties. Improvements will include replacing railroad ties, installing new ballast, resurfacing tracks, rebuilding switches, and upgrading five at-grade crossings. The upgrades will enhance safety, improve service reliability, and maintain Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) Class 2 track standards, allowing for efficient maintenance and rail operations in the future.

Sens. Warner and Kaine have secured hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding for transportation infrastructure improvements across the Commonwealth. In August, the senators announced more than $17 million in federal funding for passenger rail improvement projects across Virginia. In July, the senators announced more than $76 million for Virginia transportation infrastructure projects. Many of the grants Sens. Warner and Kaine have championed were made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, a transformative investment in American infrastructure needs.

title: Warner, Kaine Press VA For Answers On Staffing Shortages At Virginia Facilities
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) are once again pressing the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) on staffing challenges at facilities across Virginia, reiterating concerns that the Trump administration’s policies are ultimately undermining the VA’s ability to provide timely, high-quality care to veterans.

Virginia is home to more than 629,000 veterans, one of the largest veteran populations in the country, and the second-highest share of veterans as a percentage of population among all states. New reports of staffing challenges at VA facilities are raising questions about the impact on care for veterans in the Commonwealth and across the country. In a letter to VA Secretary Doug Collins, the senators pressed the Department to explain its staffing decisions in light of recent reports and new findings from the VA Office of Inspector General (OIG).

In May, Sens. Warner and Kaine pressed Secretary Collins on the elimination of more than 1,700 vacant positions at VA facilities across Virginia, including the elimination of more than 700 vacancies at the Hampton VAMC, 300 at the Richmond VAMC, 200 at the Salem VAMC, and several hundred at community clinics and other facilities. The senators’ letter asked a range of questions regarding VA decision making, data collection, communications, and the criteria used to make determinations about personnel and vacancy reductions. In its August response, the VA acknowledged its elimination of vacant positions but failed to provide details on the criteria used to make those determinations or the staffing models supporting its decisions.

Since the senators’ May letter, a new VA OIG report identified severe occupational staffing shortages reported by VA facility representatives. Across the Hampton VA Health Care System this covered 86 occupational categories designated as a “severe shortage,” including 64 clinical occupations. The Central Virginia VA Health Care System identified severe shortages in 15 clinical occupational categories, and the Salem VA Health Care System reported shortages across 12 occupational categories. The senators raised concerns that some of the occupations identified as experiencing shortages overlap with categories in which vacant positions were previously eliminated.

In their new letter, the senators also pointed to reports highlighting staffing and retention challenges at the newly opened VA Health Care Center in Fredericksburg, which continues to staff up since its opening in Spring 2025. The reporting also detailed concerns about continuity of care, including a veteran who described cycling through four primary care providers in approximately 18 months.

The senators wrote, “Taken together, these data points continue to suggest a disconnect between the workforce policies put forward by your Department, your Department’s public messaging related to their impact, and the reported experiences coming out of VA facilities across the country. It is less clear today than when we first wrote you, that your Department has a clear handle on facility staffing needs across the country. That is why in addition to repeating our requests for the following information, we request a briefing for our offices, detailing current VA workforce dynamics across Virginia.”

The senators are once again demanding detailed information about how the VA determined which positions to eliminate, whether facility leaders raised concerns about the cuts, and whether Virginia facilities are meeting minimum staffing requirements. They are also seeking updated data on employee departures, hiring needs, and the use of recruitment and retention incentives, as well as an accounting of requests to hire above staffing caps. Given the Department’s inadequate response to their initial inquiry, the senators are additionally requesting a briefing on staffing conditions at VA facilities across Virginia.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Collins:

We write to follow up on our May 14 letter regarding staffing and workforce challenges at Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities across Virginia and the Department’s decision to eliminate more than 1,700 vacant positions across the Commonwealth. Our concern and focus remain ensuring that VA facilities have the workforce necessary to provide Virginia veterans with timely, high-quality care. Recent information, however, continues to support these doubts.

While we note your August 26 response to our letter, which provided updated information regarding filled full-time equivalent (FTE) positions and vacancies for which the VA was hiring at the Hampton, Richmond, and Salem VA Medical Centers, many of our questions remain unanswered. Your response stated that approximately 26,000 unfilled positions nationwide were eliminated because VA determined that those positions were unneeded, and that these positions had “made it difficult for VA to properly identify and prioritize staffing needs across its facilities.” The response did not, however, outline criteria by which vacancies were determined to be “unneeded,” share the staffing models backing current facility staffing levels, or detail any facility-level concurrence with these staffing decisions.

Since our initial letter, additional information has continued to raise questions about staffing levels at VA facilities serving Virginians. Last month, the VA Office of Inspector General (OIG) released its annual report on severe occupational staffing shortages. This report represents the direct views of facility representatives across the country and their characterizations of these staffing challenges. Nationwide, respondents identified 4,712 severe occupational staffing shortages. Officials reported Medical Officer shortages at 97 percent of VA facilities and Nurse shortages at 86 percent of facilities.

The reporting at Virginia medical centers and their associated healthcare systems seems to reinforce our earlier concerns. The report notes in the Hampton VA Health Care System 86 occupation categories designated as “severe shortage,” including 64 clinical occupations; in the Central Virginia VA Health Care System officials identified 15 clinical occupation categories as “severe shortage”; and in the Salem VA Health Care System officials identified 12 occupation categories as “severe shortage,” eight clinical and four nonclinical. Our review of the vacancy information previously provided to our offices indicates some degree of overlap between previously eliminated vacant positions in Virginia, and occupations identified in Virginia facilities as experiencing severe shortages. This raises questions as to how these facility vacancies had been considered “unneeded” by Department leadership, at the same time as facility representatives were identifying severe shortages for similar or overlapping positions.

In addition to the information from OIG, recent media reporting has asserted that for the new VA Health Care Center in Fredericksburg, staffing challenges have extended beyond recruitment – at least one patient has described successive providers leaving in the past year and a half, suggesting retention and possible continuity of care challenges in a facility that’s been open barely 18 months.

Taken together, these data points continue to suggest a disconnect between the workforce policies put forward by your Department, your Department’s public messaging related to their impact, and the reported experiences coming out of VA facilities across the country. It is less clear today than when we first wrote you, that your Department has a clear handle on facility staffing needs across the country. That is why in addition to repeating our requests for the following information, we request a briefing for our offices, detailing current VA workforce dynamics across Virginia.

Your response to our previous letter simply noted that the decision to eliminate approximately 26,000 unfilled positions nationwide “was made in coordination with facilities across the country.”

What were the criteria by which facility leaders were directed to identify positions “that they don’t need”? Was this determination based on current conditions, or future projections? Were facilities provided a quota or target of any kind?

Did Department personnel involved in this process receive any concern, pushback, or other feedback in opposition to the vacancy cuts – particularly related to clinical impact, overall workforce health, or personnel morale – from any facility- or VISN-level personnel? What was the process for addressing these concerns?

Did facility leaders concur with the final determinations regarding vacancy cuts?

We again note the statutory requirement for the VA to “develop, validate, and implement a staffing model…that includes appropriate target staffing levels nationally, regionally, and locally to ensure timely access to care and effectively oversee the provision of care by the Department, whether at a facility of the Department or through a non-Department provider”. We further recognize that various staffing models and caseload requirements already exist in the Department for positions from nurses to housing services case managers.

Based on the position allocations for each facility in Virginia, which facilities are meeting the current minimum staffing for these models and caseload requirements? Which facilities are not meeting these requirements and by how much?

Congress has provided VA with additional tools and resources specifically intended to help the Department recruit and retain personnel in difficult-to-fill positions, including via expanded recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives; critical-skills incentives; student loan repayment authorities; and additional pay flexibilities.

Relevant to severe occupational shortages in Virginia and elsewhere around the country, how and where have you utilized available recruitment, relocation, or retention incentives, as well as employment flexibilities? Have these authorities been so far utilized to the maximum extent?

For facilities in Virginia, including newly opened Fredericksburg and Chesapeake clinics, how many personnel have left employment with the VA since January 2025? Please provide data broken down by facility.

Please provide a complete list of positions for each facility in Virginia broken down by location and hiring status as of October 1, 2026.

Have any facilities in Virginia requested authorization to recruit for a position above their allocation? If so, please provide an accounting of each request and its status. For any denied requests, please provide justification for the denial.

What are the steps for facility leaders to request positions above the cap? Please provide the names and titles of individuals above the facility level who review and decide to approve or deny these requests.

For facilities in Virginia with funding to hire for vacant positions that were cut in Fiscal Year 2026, what was that funding used for instead?

We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.

###

title: In Yuma, Kelly Visits Southwest Early College Academy, Named a Top 10 School in the World
text:
Kelly met with students, teachers, and staff at SWECA, recognized internationally for overcoming adversity in a community where 24 percent of residents live in poverty

Kelly also sat down with KYMA on the rising cost-of-living crisis facing Arizona families

This week, Arizona Senator Mark Kelly visited the Yuma area where he congratulated students and staff at the Southwest Early College Academy (SWECA) in San Luis on being named a Top 10 School in the World in the 2026 T4 Education World’s Best School Prizes under the category of Overcoming Adversity.

SWECA serves a community on the U.S.-Mexico border where nearly a quarter of residents live in poverty. The school’s Early College Program has helped more than 3,000 students earn college-level math credit, sent over 1,650 students to Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Talented Youth, and turned what was once the second poorest zip code in Arizona into a math powerhouse.

Kelly, a product of public schools himself, solved math problems alongside students and stressed the importance of a STEM education—something he knows personally as a former NASA astronaut and retired combat pilot—telling students that having a plan and teachers committed to their success makes all the difference.

Sen. Kelly talks with students at Southwest Early College Academy in San Luis.

Kelly also stopped by KYMA studios to discuss rising costs, the war in Iran, and his new AI legislation.

Kelly emphasized how rising costs are affecting Arizonan families and farmers: “People can’t afford their lives right now. Half of Americans are having a hard time affording food. 50%. Millions are getting kicked off of their health care. Hundreds of thousands, or actually, it’s millions across the country losing SNAP benefits. Those numbers here in Arizona are hundreds of thousands of people. The rent is too high. Homeownership is out of reach for young people…Groceries. Gas. This war in Iran has driven up fuel prices by a lot. Diesel prices here, I think I saw $6.50 a gallon. That really impacts farmers.”

Kellytalked about plan to bring down costs for the American people, highlightinghisConsumer Fuel Prices Relief ActandCost-of-Living Emergency Act: “So I’ve got legislation to bring down costs. One is to suspend the federal gas tax on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuel. That’ll help. I also have a Cost-of-Living Emergency Act to get this White House focused, get the data and take real action to bring down people’s costs.”

Kelly also criticized Donald Trump’s tariff policy, implementing tariffs that raise costs for Americans while giving Russia a free pass: “What the president could do to bring down costs right now is to end this nonsense of a war that he started with the Iranians and figure out sensible tariff policy. Tariffs do have a role. Putting tariffs on Russia to make this really hard on their economy to get them to end this war against the Ukrainians, that’s a good use of tariffs… A couple of days ago, he waived through an executive order, he waved those tariffs that we passed into legislation, the Lindsey Graham Tariff Act, on the Russians. He just waived those the other day.”

Kelly alsotalked abouthis newMake AI Work for Americans Act, a bill that makes Big Tech invest in American workers: “I just introduced legislation on artificial intelligence because of the possible economic impact. It’s going to have to give workers options if they lose their job, like multiple options, paid for from the tech industry by taxing big technology companies in a few different ways. So, this would allow somebody to get different kind of training to go into a new career field or do some national service that leads to some kind of a certificate for some other kind of work.”

Sen. Kelly sits down with KYMA’s Andrea Turisk.

title: Kelly, Gallego Bill to Pave Way for Gila County Veterans Center Becomes Law
text:
Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego celebrated that their bipartisan legislation to transfer the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County was signed into law, paving the way for the development of a veterans retreat and community center to support the nearly 5,500 military veterans whom call the county home.

The new law directs the U.S. Forest Service to transfer 232.9 acres of underutilized National Forest land near Young, Arizona, to Gila County. Once transferred, the site will be transformed into a dedicated space for veterans and their families to gather for retreats, meetings, and community events. The center will also serve as a mobile VA clinic site, expanding access to critical health care services for veterans in rural Arizona.

“The day is finally here. Veterans in rural Arizona deserve a place where they can gather and get the care they need closer to home,” said Kelly. “Now we’re officially on track to turn this site into a retreat and community center that will serve them and their families.”

“Caring for our men and women in uniform after their duty ends is a solemn national obligation, and this center makes good on that promise. This center will serve as a place to build community, connect, and will provide critical services to our vets that they have rightfully earned,” said Gallego. “Our veterans had our backs. I’ll make sure we have theirs, too.”

“We are very grateful to Senators Kelly and Gallego for their belief in this project from our very first meeting. This conveyance is a huge accomplishment for all of us involved as I believe it is the first such project with state, county and federal participation for our nation’s veterans. As a county, we are moving forward to finalize the necessary steps needed to complete the conveyance and continue providing a beautiful and peaceful respite for our nation’s heroes,” said Gila County District 3 Supervisor Woody Cline.

title: Kennedy discusses Southwest Louisiana’s economic growth with Better Business Bureau, West Calcasieu Chamber of Commerce
text:
MADISONVILLE, La. – Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.), a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, today addressed the Better Business Bureau and West Calcasieu Chamber of Commerce, where he discussed Southwest Louisiana’s economic progress and his efforts to support small businesses, strengthen infrastructure and bring new investment and jobs to the region.

“Nobody has to tell my people in Southwest Louisiana how to work hard. From producing American energy to growing small businesses, this region helps power Louisiana’s economy. I’m proud of what we’ve delivered, and I’ll keep working to secure the resources these communities need to create jobs, strengthen infrastructure and grow,” said Kennedy.

Kennedy secured $30.2 million in Fiscal Year 2026 funding to support five projects across the Lake Charles area, including:

$20 million for the Southwest Coastal project to construct additional rock stabilization to protect against storm surge at Rockefeller Wildlife Refuge.

$5 million for the Lake Charles Harbor and Terminal District to expand its industrial canal facility and increase operational capacity.

$2 million for Second Harvest Food Bank to establish a regional hub to combat hunger and strengthen emergency response efforts.

$1.7 million for Chennault International Airport to expand its aircraft painting facilities.

$1.5 million for the City of Lake Charles to replace sewer system basins at the Lake Charles Wastewater Treatment Plant.

Kennedy also emphasized Southwest Louisiana’s booming energy industry, which has attracted billions in investments and created jobs throughout the region. He then discussed the $2.3 billion replacement of the I-10 Calcasieu River Bridge; a major infrastructure project aimed at improving travel and supporting economic growth.

title: Sen. Moran, Rep. McDowell Introduce Resolution to Recognize Red Ribbon Week
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – chairman of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, and Science – and U.S. Representative Addison McDowell introduced a joint resolution with Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and John Cornyn (R-Texas) to recognize Red Ribbon Week from October 23 to October 31, 2026. Red Ribbon Week is the nation’s largest and longest-running drug prevention program in the U.S. It raises awareness of the dangers of illicit drugs, promotes drug prevention efforts and recognizes the law enforcement officers who work to keep communities across the country safe.

“Drug overdoses remain a leading cause of death in our nation, underscoring the importance of investing in efforts to fight illicit drugs and raise awareness about the dangers of drug use,” said Sen. Moran. “Red Ribbon Week provides the opportunity to educate others on the risks of illicit drugs, support prevention efforts and recognize the law enforcement officers who work every day to keep Kansans safe. I will continue working to combat illegal drugs and make certain that law enforcement is equipped with the resources needed to protect our communities and stem the flow of illegal drugs.”

“I lost my little brother Luke to fentanyl, and I know firsthand the devastating toll these deadly drugs take on families,” said Rep. McDowell. “Red Ribbon Week is an important reminder that prevention starts with education, strong families, and supporting the men and women in law enforcement who work every day to keep our communities safe. We owe it to the next generation to do everything we can to prevent another family from experiencing that same heartbreak mine did.”

“Illicit drugs cause immeasurable pain and loss in our communities. Red Ribbon Week is a chance to care for those fighting personal battles against substance use, shine a light on the dark forces driving the addiction crisis, and celebrate the law enforcement officers who keep our communities safe,” said Sen. Whitehouse. “I’m committed to passing Senate measures, like my CARA laws, that help turn the tide in the fight against the addiction epidemic.”

Items to note:

Originally founded in 1988 by the National Family Partnership, Red Ribbon Week promotes drug prevention and honors the memory of Enrique “Kiki” Camarena, a DEA special agent who was murdered in 1985 while working to combat illicit drugs.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has found that drug overdoses are the leading cause of death for individuals from ages 18 to 45 in the U.S. In 2025, nearly 70,000 individuals in the United States died of an overdose involving cocaine.

Full text of the resolution can be found here.

title: Murphy Hits JD Vance on Trump Corruption, Brings Receipts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—In case you missed it, U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) published a Substack article responding to Vice President J.D. Vance’s ludicrous claim that President Trump has not used the powers of the presidency to enrich himself and his family. In a response to Vance’s comments on CBS Evening News with Tony Dokoupil, Murphy laid out the damning evidence of President Trump’s multi-billion-dollar webs of corruption, stressing that the American people have had enough of the lies and excuses coming from Vance and the rest of the Trump administration.

Read Murphy’s full takedown of Vance below or on Substack.

JD Vance says he hasn’t seen “a single shred of evidence” that Donald Trump is enriching himself in office.

Yes, he just said that.

Really? Let me help him out. I wrote out some of Trump’s top enrichment schemes below in the 15 minutes before my son’s hockey practice ended.

First, the stock trades. Trump has made tens of thousands of stock trades, including trades that have raised serious questions about whether he’s profiting from information available to him as president. Take Nvidia: Trump disclosed up to $1.6 million in stock purchases in August, just before announcing a policy change that stood to benefit the company’s stock price.

This is a major conflict of interest. We can’t just shrug it off. Read more.

Then there’s crypto. Trump has made over $1.4 billion from his crypto ventures. His family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, depends heavily on Binance, another crypto company whose founder, Changpeng Zhao, pled guilty to violating anti-money-laundering laws and went to prison. Trump gave Zhao a presidential pardon as Zhao’s company helped Trump amass his crypto fortune.

JD, you really haven’t seen anything concerning there? Read more.

How about suspicious bets on the Iran war? Just 15 minutes before Trump announced a major reversal in Iran policy, billions of dollars in oil-related contracts were placed in a way that stood to profit from falling prices. Federal regulators reportedly began looking into the trades, only for the investigation to hit resistance. Read more If someone had advance knowledge of a major presidential announcement, they could make a fortune. We deserve to know whether that happened here.

Or the family business. Trump’s sons have pursued a mining deal in Kazakhstan, and the administration subsequently approved $1.6 billion in taxpayer-backed financing tied to the project. That is an extraordinary amount of public money flowing into a deal that could benefit the president’s own family.

This isn’t some minor ethics question. It’s a fundamental question about whether the presidency is being used to serve the public or enrich one family. Read more.

And then there’s the merchandise. Trump’s political products have reportedly been sold on military bases, turning spaces meant to serve our troops into another opportunity to promote his personal brand. Read more.

JD, military bases? Really?

These are just a few examples. We haven’t even gotten into the broader web of business interests, political favors, and conflicts of interest surrounding this administration.

Here’s the thing: I understand why JD Vance doesn’t want to talk about any of this. His job is to defend Donald Trump, even when that means asking Americans to ignore what’s right in front of them.

But Americans aren’t buying it.

Two-thirds of voters now say Trump is enriching himself in office. And corruption is emerging as a major issue for voters heading into the midterms. People work hard, pay their taxes, and expect their government to work for them. They don’t expect a president to use the most powerful office in the world to pad his own bank account.

title: Padilla, Warner, Himes, Morelle Demand Big Tech Uphold Election Integrity Efforts
text:
Key Democratic Committee Leaders to Tech CEOs: “We strongly urge you to enhance—not reduce—your election security efforts in the final days before the 2026 midterms”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, Mark R. Warner (D-Va.), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, along with U.S. Representatives Jim Himes (D-Conn.-04), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.-25), Ranking Member of the House Administration Committee, urged top executives of the largest technology companies to ensure their platforms and tools help protect the integrity of our elections and support free, fair, and secure elections.

In their letter, the lawmakers underscored the need for social media and technology companies to do their part to promote election security. They outlined the potential risk to elections created by the spread of false information through social media platforms and artificial intelligence.

“Your platforms play a significant and important role in sharing, disseminating, and in some cases generating information about those elections,” wrote the lawmakers. “Much of the United States—and the world—searches for and receives information from American search engines, American chatbots, and American social media platforms. These connections create opportunities for Americans to come together and debate important topics and share information. But they also create vectors for foreign adversaries and domestic actors to easily and quickly reach—and manipulate—large audiences.”

The lawmakers reminded the CEOs that many of their companies committed to ensuring they were not complicit in harming elections or hampering the ability of Americans to vote. They explained that, while many of these companies have committed to authenticating and labeling digital media and adopted policies to boost the most reliable voting and election information, there have been inconsistencies in the efficacy and application of these policies.

“Unfortunately, there are concerning signs of backsliding on some of your commitments to protecting elections from misuse of your products. These signs are particularly alarming because they come at a time when the capabilities of malign actors are growing in scale and sophistication and our elections are under attack from multiple directions,” wrote the lawmakers. “Public reporting indicates that Russia continues to undermine confidence in U.S. elections through disinformation campaigns executed directly on many of your platforms; though such efforts clearly violate your terms of service, some of your companies have not quickly or consistently removed such content.”

The lawmakers further explained that their social media platforms and AI tools can quickly generate, execute and disseminate influence campaigns that used to take hundreds of hours of labor. As Americans increasingly turn to AI tools to inform themselves about political candidates, ballot issues, and the logistics of voting, AI tools could be used to spread inaccurate, outdated, manipulated, or biased information.

“Equally alarming is that some of your AI chatbots have an unacceptably high error rate when responding to queries about election and voting processes, subjecting users to confusing or inaccurate answers that could result in voter disenfranchisement. And some of your content removal and fact-checking policies are woefully insufficient or even nonexistent, allowing false, manipulated, and misleading content to continue to circulate on your platforms unchecked,” the lawmakers continued.

The lawmakers recommended a list of concrete actions the companies could take, including removing all demonstrably false information related to election and voting logistics once they find it, using independent fact checkers, regularly updating automated tools to review and remove or reduce the reach of false election-related content, and directing all users to authoritative election-related resources.

They also urged the companies to ensure AI-generated responses to questions about election and voting logistics are sourced from state and local election offices and trusted news organizations.

“Again, we strongly urge you to enhance—not reduce—your election security efforts in the final days before the 2026 midterms and to maintain strong efforts in this area on an ongoing basis ahead of future elections as well,” the lawmakers concluded.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections and California’s former Secretary of State, Padilla has been a vocal leader in protecting our elections. Earlier this month, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) pressed the top executives of the largest social media companies about their plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on their platforms ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. In August, Padilla and Senator Mark Warner (D-Va.) called for prediction market companies to take immediate action to protect election integrity and end relationships with paid influencers on their platforms spreading election disinformation.

The full letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. Narayen, Mr. Pichai, Mr. Amodei, Mr. Rombach, Mr. Schneider, Mr. Sakhnini, Mr. Staniszewski, Mr. Shapero, Mr. Zuckerberg, Mr. Nadella, Mr. Holz, Mr. Mensch, Mr. Altman, Mr. Srinivas, Mr. Ready, Mr. Huffman, Mr. Laskin, Mr. Pavlovski, Mr. Spiegel, Mr. Musk, Mr. Akkaraju, Mr. Durov, Mrs. Murati, Mr. Presser, and Mr. McGurn,

We write to urge you to adopt policies and programs that ensure your platforms contribute to, and do not detract from, the effort to ensure that America’s elections are free, fair, and secure.

As the CEOs of America’s largest technology companies, you are aware of the great responsibility that your companies hold in America’s elections. Your platforms play a significant and important role in sharing, disseminating, and in some cases generating information about those elections. Much of the United States—and the world—searches for and receives information from American search engines, American chatbots, and American social media platforms. These connections create opportunities for Americans to come together and debate important topics and share information. But they also create vectors for foreign adversaries and domestic actors to easily and quickly reach—and manipulate—large audiences.

Moreover, American companies’ AI offerings offer both substantial benefits and substantial risks. Your tools can quickly generate, execute, and disseminate entire influence campaigns. While it previously would take hundreds of manhours to achieve such effects, your tools speed and streamline efforts to create material that are inaccurate or false, but nevertheless convincing. Increasingly, some American voters turn to AI tools to research candidates and ballot issues and seek information about voting logistics, increasing the risk of exposure to inaccuracies, outdated or manipulated information, or biased summaries.

Many of your companies have demonstrated a commitment over the past decade to ensuring that your platforms are not used to harm elections or hamper the ability of Americans to vote. After the 2016 elections, many of your companies turned particular focus to identifying and eliminating coordinated inauthentic behavior on your platforms and establishing searchable archives for election ads. With the rise of powerful generative AI tools, your companies further committed to authenticating and labeling digital media, including by joining the Coalition for Content Provenance & Authenticity (C2PA) and signing the Tech Accord to Combat Deceptive Use of AI in 2024 Elections. Many of your companies have also adopted policies seeking to increase the odds that your users are exposed to only the most authoritative and reliable voting and election information. We believe maintaining and enhancing these kinds of commitments is more important than ever heading into the final days of the 2026 midterm election cycle.

Unfortunately, there are concerning signs of backsliding on some of your commitments to protecting elections from misuse of your products. These signs are particularly alarming because they come at a time when the capabilities of malign actors are growing in scale and sophistication and our elections are under attack from multiple directions. Despite many of your companies having policies prohibiting deception and requiring the labeling of AI-generated content, there have been demonstrated inconsistencies regarding the effectiveness and applicability of your policies. In many cases, some of your social media platforms and AI tools still allow for the creation and/or dissemination of false, synthetic, misleading, or inauthentic election content in direct violation of your policies. Public reporting indicates that Russia continues to undermine confidence in U.S. elections through disinformation campaigns executed directly on many of your platforms; though such efforts clearly violate your terms of service, some of your companies have not quickly or consistently removed such content.

Equally alarming is that some of your AI chatbots have an unacceptably high error rate when responding to queries about election and voting processes, subjecting users to confusing or inaccurate answers that could result in voter disenfranchisement. And some of your content removal and fact-checking policies are woefully insufficient or even nonexistent, allowing false, manipulated, and misleading content to continue to circulate on your platforms unchecked. In the past, the Federal Trade Commission has notably pursued enforcement actions against companies that don’t live up to the self-regulatory commitments they make, including in a 2012 case against Google for failing to follow the National Advertising Initiative code of conduct.

Information related to election and voting logistics—a category that includes registration deadlines, polling hours and locations, requirements about voter ID, rules for mail or provisional voting and ballots, and voter eligibility—is information that is integral to the functioning of our democracy. When objectively false information about election administration is introduced and disseminated with the intent to deceive or to discourage prospective voters, your companies must have robust and consistently applied rules to differentiate that misinformation from ordinary political speech about elections and to take steps to remove that misinformation.

We continue to strongly encourage you to take the actions and adopt the best practices outlined in Senator Warner’s March 2026 letter on anticipating, identifying, and countering malicious manipulated media. These best practices are important steps to protecting vulnerable communities, public trust, and democratic institutions.

We also encourage you to adopt specific policies and actions regarding election-related content. To the extent that your company offers social media or other content access or distribution platforms, we strongly encourage you to take the following actions to keep your platforms free from coordinated inauthentic behavior and election-related misinformation and disinformation:

Immediately remove all demonstrably false information related to election and voting logistics upon becoming aware of it—including information about where and how to register to vote, and where and how to vote.

Support dedicated reporting tools on your platforms for election officials to report examples of false election information.

Improve the speed by which your tools detect and remove false information related to voting logistics and political and election-related violence.

o When such tools are used to detect false, misleading, and inauthentic content, ensure that the tools are kept updated, and that their findings are promptly subject to human review and action to remove violative content.

Utilize independent fact checkers in addition to internal fact-checking teams and regularly updated automated tools to review and remove, or at least reduce the reach, impressions, and discoverability of, false, misleading, or inauthentic election-related content.

Engage independent media and civil society organizations to assist in efforts to verify media, generate authenticated media, and educate the public.

Notify users when they have engaged with election-related content that has subsequently been determined to be false, misleading, or inauthentic.

Affirmatively direct all users to authoritative election-related resources, especially if users were determined to have engaged with false, misleading, or inauthentic election-related content.

Immediately remove all content advocating for violence of any kind upon becoming aware of it, but particularly content advocating political and/or election-related violence.

Publish regular reports detailing efforts to identify and remove false election-related information, election-related misinformation and disinformation, election and political violence, and coordinated inauthentic behavior.

To the extent your company offers generative AI products, we strongly encourage you to take the following actions to keep your AI systems and tools safe as they engage with and generate election-related information:

Ensure that AI-generated responses to questions about election and voting logistics pull only from highly authoritative sources and do not pull from social media platforms or other user-generated content. Authoritative resources should be limited to state and local election offices and top trusted news organizations, as well as civil society organizations aggregating content from these other authoritative and reliable sources.

Provide additional resources to pre-deployment guardrail testing for AI-generated election-related content, as well as ongoing reviewing of model performance.

Strengthen guardrails to prevent AI systems from responding to queries with material that can be used in election disinformation campaigns.

Implement continuous auditing until the November federal elections, and for an appropriate time as ballot counting, litigation, or challenges to the results remain ongoing, for accuracy and objectiveness in AI-generated responses to election-related questions, including mechanisms by which users can report inaccurate answers.

Incorporate disclaimers and flags in AI-generated responses if election and voting logistics may be outdated, and direct users to authoritative resources.

Provide inline citations and links for all election-related information provided in an AI-generated response.

Encourage users to independently verify AI-generated answers to questions about election and voting by reviewing authoritative and reliable resources.

Ensure that all AI-generated images and videos are consistently clearly labeled and can be identified as AI-generated content both by the human eye and by technology-based detection tools.

Ensure that election-related responses provided in languages other than English are accurate and reliable.

Many of you have announced content partnerships with highly reliable sources to ensure that your AI and social media platforms only surface the most accurate and reliable information related to election and voting logistics and election results. We strongly support this practice and encourage you to ensure that your platforms properly identify and curate the authoritative and reliable resources from which they pull from on election-related topics to avoid sharing outdated, inaccurate, unreliable, or otherwise incorrect information on this critical topic area that you cannot afford to get wrong. In addition, we urge you to be mindful of Spanish and other foreign language content, which plays a large and important role in the U.S. electorate but often receives less attention and response than online English-language election misinformation.

We also encourage you to be transparent about the efforts that your companies are making on these fronts. Public reporting indicates that in recent years, several of your companies have conducted layoffs, including of personnel on the trust and safety teams responsible for ensuring your platforms’ integrity when it comes to election topics. Firing such personnel after there has been demonstrated evidence and indicators of orchestrated and coordinate foreign misinformation operations exposes your platform to various integrity threats and is cause for serious concern.

Particularly as the 2026 midterm elections are officially underway, your companies should be increasing the staffing and capabilities of your respective trust and safety teams, especially those teams responsible for avoiding platform exploitation relating to election topics. Refusing to grow and expand your election integrity teams—and even shrinking these teams—does not support your stated commitments to countering harmful election content and suggests to bad actors that your policies are not enforceable.

Finally, third-party researchers play a critical role in studying and producing independent reviews of social media platforms and AI systems and tools, particularly as it pertains to auditing the effectiveness of your trust and safety policies. Your companies should collaborate with third-party researchers by granting them access to your products and data, including data on how users are engaging with your platforms on election-related issues, and allow for the testing of your platforms and AI tools.

Again, we strongly urge you to enhance—not reduce—your election security efforts in the final days before the 2026 midterms and to maintain strong efforts in this area on an ongoing basis ahead of future elections as well. We thank you for your attention to these important measures and we look forward to hearing about your efforts in these areas.

Sincerely,

title: Sen. Rick Scott Announces Senate Salary Donation to BRACE to Support Hurricane Isaias Recovery in Northwest Florida
text:
NAPLES, Fla. – Today, Senator Rick Scott and Mrs. Anne Scott announced the donation of his third-quarter U.S. Senate salary to the Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies (BRACE), to support Florida families recovering from Hurricane Isaias in the Panhandle. Senator Scott has donated his Senate salary since taking office in 2019.

Senator Rick Scott said, “Anne and I are proud to partner with BRACE to support Floridians who face the long road ahead to recover from Hurricane Isaias. Floridians are tough. We come together when our neighbors need us the most, just as BRACE did before, during, and now after this storm. Anne and I are grateful to every Floridian who’s stepped up in a big way to help, and to BRACE for its commitment to coordinating long-term recovery efforts for Florida families. Our best days are always ahead, and we will get through this together.”

Dr. Nick Jackson, Chief Executive Officer of BRACE, said, “We are deeply honored and grateful that Senator Rick Scott has chosen BRACE as the recipient of his quarterly salary donation. In the wake of Hurricane Isaias, thousands of our neighbors across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties are facing tremendous challenges as they begin the long road to recovery. This generous contribution is more than a financial gift; it is a meaningful investment in the recovery and resilience of our communities. As BRACE continues coordinating volunteers, donations, and long-term recovery efforts across both counties, partnerships like this remind us that we are not facing these challenges alone. On behalf of BRACE and the communities we serve, I want to personally thank Senator Scott for his generosity, leadership, and commitment to helping Northwest Florida recover and rebuild.”

BACKGROUND:

BRACE was established by the member organizations of the Escambia Long-Term Recovery Committee in 2006 to address lessons observed from Hurricane Ivan. Since its founding, BRACE has taken on the LTRG role for Santa Rosa County and has provided many programing and services with an anti-poverty focus, recognizing that low income and vulnerable residents are disproportionately impacted by disasters of all kinds. As a result of the organization's efforts, BRACE has been entrusted with serving as the Citizen Corps Council and CERT Coordinator by Escambia County, the City of Pensacola, and the Town of Century. BRACE has performed those roles successfully with the help of its valuable volunteers.

BRACE has been designated the "Lead Organization" for Emergency Support Function 15 (Volunteers & Donations) for Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties through a Memorandum of Understanding with Emergency Management. BRACE also serves as the local Community Organizations Active in Disaster (COAD), and in turn a Member of the Florida VOAD.

Furthermore, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has recognized BRACE and its partners more frequently than any other locally-based coalition of organizations in the country through its "Individual and Community Preparedness Awards" program. Those awards include the "John D. Solomon Preparedness Award", the highest award presented by FEMA through the program.

As the Citizen Corps and Community Emergency Response Team Coordinator for three governmental jurisdictions, BRACE works with over 250 partner organizations and many volunteers to make its community the most disaster-resilient in America. Those collaborative efforts and nearly 80,000 hours of volunteer service have restored over 100 homes to a safe, sanitary and functional condition after Hurricane Sally.

In addition, the City of Pensacola has entrusted the coordination of its new Fire Corps program to BRACE.

Since its founding in 2006, BRACE has become the single most recognized organization in the United States by FEMA through the Individual and Community Preparedness Awards program. The efforts of BRACE have been recognized with FEMA’s John D. Solomon Preparedness Award, the organization’s highest recognition for work to prepare the nation.

title: Sen. Rick Scott Visits Israel to Strengthen Partnerships with U.S.
text:
JERUSALEM – U.S. Senator Rick Scott, member of the U.S. Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, traveled to Israel to reaffirm the United States’ commitment to supporting Israel and maintaining a strong alliance and partnership. During the visit, Senator Scott met with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar. He also met with members of the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), U.S. servicemen and women, and U.S. Department of War (DOW) personnel to discuss U.S.-Israeli collaboration, including projects to secure the U.S. southern border.

Senator Scott also traveled to the Golan Heights and Israel’s Northern Command. During the visit, Senator Scott was briefed by U.S. and Israeli military on operations in southern Lebanon. He also met with Dolan Abu Saleh, Mayor of Majdal Shams, and bereaved families in the Druze community who lost children during the Hezbollah attack on a soccer field that killed 12 innocent children in July of 2024.

Senator Rick Scott said, “From business partnerships to healthcare and medicine production, to defense technology, America’s partnership with Israel is the model of how America First alliances should operate. Too many people in America have lost sight of the fact that Israel is the good guy and that Qatar, Iran, including its proxies Hamas and Hezbollah, are the bad guys who indiscriminately target and murder innocent people. Israel faces life-or-death threats every day, and innovation is what helps them deter and defeat our shared enemies. Israel holds up its side of the alliance, and we will continue to collaborate and share what we learn so we both get stronger. This partnership will maintain safety for our countries and economic advances to create jobs. I remain proud to call our friends in Israel a trusted partner and ally.”

This is Senator Scott’s seventh trip to Israel since he was elected Governor of Florida in 2010. Click here to view a list of Senator Scott’s actions since the October 7, 2023, attacks.

Senator Scott’s time in Israel follows his recent visits to Cyprus and Greece.

title: Risch, Crapo Join Forest Service to Announce Salmon Student Selected to Help Light U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree
text:
Fourth-grader Grace Benson wins statewide essay contest to participate in annual tree-lighting ceremony in Washington, D.C.

Washington, D.C.–U.S. Senators Jim Risch and Mike Crapo (both R-Idaho) announced Grace Benson, a fourth-grade student and the daughter of Jake and Tara Benson from Salmon, Idaho, has been selected as the winner of the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Youth Tree Lighter Essay Contest. Grace will represent Idaho in Washington, D.C., this December, where she will help light the U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree during the annual ceremony on the West Lawn of the Capitol.

“Congratulations to Salmon fourth grader Grace Benson for being selected as the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Lighter!,” said Risch. “Your deep love of Idaho’s forests, water, and resources is a testament to the important role public lands play in our way of life. I look forward to joining you and the tree selected from Idaho’s Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest in Washington, D.C. later this year.”

“Congratulations to Grace on being selected to represent Idaho in our nation’s capital,” said Crapo. “Her essay highlights the importance of Idaho’s forests, clean water and the connection Idahoans share with our state’s natural resources. This year’s Capitol Christmas Tree is a special opportunity to share Idaho’s natural beauty with the nation, and Grace will play an important role in that celebration.”

“As a father of two, I take my responsibility as Forest Supervisor personally and seriously. The decisions we make today on our national forests will shape the experiences of generations to come, including Idaho’s children, like Grace,” said Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest Supervisor Jon Word. “What stood out in Grace’s essay was her vivid portrayal of life in rural Idaho and her deep understanding of the strong connection Idahoans share with their public lands and seven national forests. We are proud of her accomplishment and look forward to her sharing her essay on the national stage.”

“I am so impressed by Grace’s eloquent essay that highlights the natural features of our special town,” said Kristin Foss, Principal of FernWaters Charter. “The fact that she won this statewide contest demonstrates her innate talent and the Fernwaters staff’s commitment to our vision for helping small town kids launch big life dreams.”

“My hope is that every student knows their words have power, that they should share them with purpose, and that every voice matters,” said Meriah Baker, Teacher at FernWaters Charter. “Our stories are meaningful, our perspectives have value, and the world deserves to hear what we have to say.”

Earlier this year, Senators Crapo and Risch invited fourth-grade students across Idaho to participate in a statewide essay contest answering the question, “Why are healthy forests and clean water in Idaho important?” The contest followed the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree theme, “Over the Rivers and Through the Woods,” and encouraged students to reflect on the importance of Idaho’s natural resources.

Grace’s essay was selected through a review process conducted by the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests and the Idaho Forest Restoration Partnership in coordination with the U.S. Forest Service. As the winner, Grace will travel to Washington, D.C., with three family members to participate in the annual U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony, where she will have the opportunity to read her essay and assist in lighting the tree alongside the Speaker of the House and other public officials.

Background:

Idaho’s Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests will provide the 2026 U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree, continuing the annual tradition of selecting a tree from a different national forest to serve as the People’s Tree. The tree will be displayed on the West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol throughout the holiday season, showcasing Idaho’s natural beauty to visitors from across the country.

title: Rosen Joins Colleagues in Introducing Bill to End Trump Tariffs
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) joined Senate colleagues in introducing a bill to revoke Donald Trump’s latest batch of tariffs and limit his ability to continue waging his unilateral trade war. The End Trump’s Tariff Tax Act would revoke and refund Trump’s recently imposed 12.5% global tariffs and 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The bill would also repeal the authorities that Trump used to impose these tariffs, preventing him from imposing any additional tariffs using these authorities in the future.

“Donald Trump’s reckless economic and foreign policies have only led to higher prices and squeezed the pockets of hardworking Americans. Nevadans are struggling to make ends meet, and instead of trying to lower costs, Trump is engaging in a totally senseless trade war with Canada and other allies, and making the situation worse,” said Senator Rosen. “I was proud to help introduce this bill to rein in Trump’s ability to unilaterally impose reckless tariffs, and will continue fighting back against any policy that takes money away from hardworking Nevada families.”

Senator Rosen has consistently opposed Trump’s across-the-board tariffs and worked to provide relief to Nevada families. Last month, she attempted to pass her resolution calling for the removal of Trump’s 50 percent tariffs on Canada and denouncing Donald Trump’s trade war with Canada, which was blocked by Senate Republicans. Following the Supreme Court’s decision to strike down some of Trump’s illegal tariffs, Senator Rosen joined her Democratic Senate colleagues in introducing a bill to protect small businesses and their consumers from further tariff-related harm. Earlier this year, she introduced bills to exclude homebuilding materials and groceries from Trump’s tariffs, which would help lower costs for families.
