title: Sen. Tim Scott accepting applications for spring 2027 internships
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) is now accepting applications for internships in his Washington, D.C., North Charleston, Columbia, and Greenville offices for spring 2027.

The internship program offers undergraduate and graduate students the opportunity to work with public service professionals and gain experience in constituent services, federal policy, and more. Students of all majors, particularly those studying governmental affairs, public policy, or communications, are welcome to apply.

Washington, D.C. Office: In Washington, interns will research legislation, attend congressional hearings and briefings, assist with press tasks, and help manage correspondence on various issues. Responsibilities also include answering phones and other administrative tasks. Interns in this office will gain a stronger understanding of the lawmaking process, while also improving their communication and customer service skills.

South Carolina Offices (North Charleston, Columbia, and Greenville): In the state offices, interns will take an active role in the community, working on state-based projects while also answering phones, completing research, and being an integral part of day-to-day office operations. Interns in these offices are able to assist with issues that affect South Carolinians each day.

Internship hours are flexible to accommodate students’ course schedules but generally run from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. Students may also gain course credit for completing the internship program. Interested students can apply through Sen. Scott’s website at www.scott.senate.gov/constituent-services/internships. For additional questions, contact the internship coordinator at Internships_Scott@scott.senate.gov or (202) 224-6121.

title: WATCH: Slotkin Responds to President Trump Saying She Should be Tried in Court
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last night, U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) posted a video response to President Donald Trump after he called for her to be tried in court. This comes after Slotkin called for accountability for the corruption of the Trump Administration.

Key excerpts from the video:

“I’ve been the target of attacks from D.C. Republicans and right-wing media. It culminated in President Trump just a few hours ago in the Oval Office saying that I should be tried in court.“

title: Tuberville Requests GAO Investigation into Child Care Fraud
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL), Co-Chairman of the HELP task force on fraud, joined U.S. Senators Bill Cassidy (R-LA) and Jon Husted (R-OH) in sending a letter to the Government Accountability Office (GAO), urging them to investigate the rampant level of improper payments and fraud in the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF).

For the fiscal year 2025, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) reported that CCDF had over $800 million in overpayments, representing about 4.5 percent of its payments. Further, in January 2026, HHS froze access to certain CCDF funds in California, Colorado, Illinois, Minnesota, and New York due to serious concerns about widespread fraud and misuse of taxpayer dollars. Despite 8 million low-income families being eligible, the CCDF is only able to serve about 1.4 million.

“The Trump administration has done a great job of exposing the waste, fraud, and abuse that has been happening in blue states across this country for years,” said Sen. Tuberville. “Our number 1 priority is making sure that hardworking American taxpayers aren’t being ripped off. I’m glad to join my Republican colleagues in urging GAO to investigate and put an end to all fraud in the Child Care and Development Fund.”

Read the letter below or here.

“Dear Acting Comptroller General Brown:

We are writing to request that the Government Accountability Office (GAO) initiate an audit of states’ payment integrity actions and oversight within the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF), with particular attention to state payment systems, administrative controls, and coordination with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The CCDF program provides federal and state-funded childcare assistance to low-income families, helping them access quality childcare while they work, train, or attend educational programs. Congress has continuously supported providing this critical assistance to our hard-working constituents. However, significant challenges persist in preventing fraud and improper payments in this program. For example, for fiscal year 2025, HHS reported that CCDF had over $800 million in overpayments, representing about 4.5 percent of its payments. Further, in January 2026, HHS froze access to certain CCDF funds in California, Colorado, Illinois, Minnesota, and New York due to serious concerns about widespread fraud and misuse of taxpayer dollars. In a July 2026 GAO report on federally funded state administered programs, your agency highlighted examples of recent fraud schemes that have occurred in the CCDF program.

Challenges with CCDF’s ability to maintain program integrity are longstanding. In 2010, GAO found that five states with large CCDF budgets (over $100 million each) had weak fraud prevention controls. In undercover tests, investigators attempted to circumvent selected states’ fraud prevention controls and found several vulnerabilities that could be exploited for fraud and abuse. You have also reported on difficulties in overseeing and monitoring CCDF program integrity risks. For example, in 2020, you reported that HHS did not clearly define what states should report on its program-integrity activities and the corrective actions that it plans to take to address root causes of improper payments. Although HHS has taken steps to address recommendations from prior reports, including conducting a fraud risk assessment of the program, more actions need to be taken to address payment risks at the federal, state, and local levels.

We are writing today to request GAO conduct a follow-up study on improper payments and fraud in the CCDF program. Specifically,

To what extent have fraud risk assessments and efforts to prevent and detect fraud and improper payments been incorporated into the CCDF program?

What are key eligibility and payment integrity risks and to what extent has the federal government and the states taken steps to address those risks? For example,

To what extent has the federal government and the states taken steps to ensure that beneficiaries and providers are eligible for the CCDF program?

To what extent has the federal government and the states ensured that providers are paid for the services that they provide and not just based on enrollment in childcare centers?

To what extent has the federal government and states ensured that providers are not overbilling the states for children that are enrolled in more than one federal childcare program (e.g., CCDF and Early Head Start)?

What, if any, additional actions need to be taken to address the payment integrity risks related to fraud posed in CCDF?

What lessons learned or better practices for accurately identifying and estimating improper payments (including fraud) and improving payment integrity can be leveraged across states?

How does HHS ensure that states are properly estimating their improper payments Rates?

Sincerely,”

title: Warner, Kaine Press VA for Answers on Staffing Shortages at Virginia Facilities
text:
WASHINGTON— U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) are once again pressing the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) on staffing challenges at facilities across Virginia, reiterating concerns that the Trump administration’s policies are ultimately undermining the VA’s ability to provide timely, high-quality care to veterans.

Virginia is home to more than 629,000 veterans, one of the largest veteran populations in the country, and the second-highest share of veterans as a percentage of population among all states. New reports of staffing challenges at VA facilities are raising questions about the impact on care for veterans in the Commonwealth and across the country. In a letter to VA Secretary Doug Collins, the senators pressed the Department to explain its staffing decisions in light of recent reports and new findings from the VA Office of Inspector General (OIG).

In May, Sens. Warner and Kaine pressed Secretary Collins on the elimination of more than 1,700 vacant positions at VA facilities across Virginia, including the elimination of more than 700 vacancies at the Hampton VAMC, 300 at the Richmond VAMC, 200 at the Salem VAMC, and several hundred at community clinics and other facilities. The senators’ letter asked a range of questions regarding VA decision making, data collection, communications, and the criteria used to make determinations about personnel and vacancy reductions. In its August response, the VA acknowledged its elimination of vacant positions but failed to provide details on the criteria used to make those determinations or the staffing models supporting its decisions.

Since the senators’ May letter, a new VA OIG report identified severe occupational staffing shortages reported by VA facility representatives. Across the Hampton VA Health Care System this covered 86 occupational categories designated as a “severe shortage,” including 64 clinical occupations. The Central Virginia VA Health Care System identified severe shortages in 15 clinical occupational categories, and the Salem VA Health Care System reported shortages across 12 occupational categories. The senators raised concerns that some of the occupations identified as experiencing shortages overlap with categories in which vacant positions were previously eliminated.

In their new letter, the senators also pointed to reports highlighting staffing and retention challenges at the newly opened VA Health Care Center in Fredericksburg, which continues to staff up since its opening in Spring 2025. The reporting also detailed concerns about continuity of care, including a veteran who described cycling through four primary care providers in approximately 18 months.

The senators wrote, “Taken together, these data points continue to suggest a disconnect between the workforce policies put forward by your Department, your Department’s public messaging related to their impact, and the reported experiences coming out of VA facilities across the country. It is less clear today than when we first wrote you, that your Department has a clear handle on facility staffing needs across the country. That is why in addition to repeating our requests for the following information, we request a briefing for our offices, detailing current VA workforce dynamics across Virginia.”

The senators are once again demanding detailed information about how the VA determined which positions to eliminate, whether facility leaders raised concerns about the cuts, and whether Virginia facilities are meeting minimum staffing requirements. They are also seeking updated data on employee departures, hiring needs, and the use of recruitment and retention incentives, as well as an accounting of requests to hire above staffing caps. Given the Department’s inadequate response to their initial inquiry, the senators are additionally requesting a briefing on staffing conditions at VA facilities across Virginia.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Collins:

We write to follow up on our May 14 letter regarding staffing and workforce challenges at Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities across Virginia and the Department’s decision to eliminate more than 1,700 vacant positions across the Commonwealth. Our concern and focus remain ensuring that VA facilities have the workforce necessary to provide Virginia veterans with timely, high-quality care. Recent information, however, continues to support these doubts.

While we note your August 26 response to our letter, which provided updated information regarding filled full-time equivalent (FTE) positions and vacancies for which the VA was hiring at the Hampton, Richmond, and Salem VA Medical Centers, many of our questions remain unanswered. Your response stated that approximately 26,000 unfilled positions nationwide were eliminated because VA determined that those positions were unneeded, and that these positions had “made it difficult for VA to properly identify and prioritize staffing needs across its facilities.” The response did not, however, outline criteria by which vacancies were determined to be “unneeded,” share the staffing models backing current facility staffing levels, or detail any facility-level concurrence with these staffing decisions.

Since our initial letter, additional information has continued to raise questions about staffing levels at VA facilities serving Virginians. Last month, the VA Office of Inspector General (OIG) released its annual report on severe occupational staffing shortages. This report represents the direct views of facility representatives across the country and their characterizations of these staffing challenges. Nationwide, respondents identified 4,712 severe occupational staffing shortages. Officials reported Medical Officer shortages at 97 percent of VA facilities and Nurse shortages at 86 percent of facilities.

The reporting at Virginia medical centers and their associated healthcare systems seems to reinforce our earlier concerns. The report notes in the Hampton VA Health Care System 86 occupation categories designated as “severe shortage,” including 64 clinical occupations; in the Central Virginia VA Health Care System officials identified 15 clinical occupation categories as “severe shortage”; and in the Salem VA Health Care System officials identified 12 occupation categories as “severe shortage,” eight clinical and four nonclinical. Our review of the vacancy information previously provided to our offices indicates some degree of overlap between previously eliminated vacant positions in Virginia, and occupations identified in Virginia facilities as experiencing severe shortages. This raises questions as to how these facility vacancies had been considered “unneeded” by Department leadership, at the same time as facility representatives were identifying severe shortages for similar or overlapping positions.

In addition to the information from OIG, recent media reporting has asserted that for the new VA Health Care Center in Fredericksburg, staffing challenges have extended beyond recruitment – at least one patient has described successive providers leaving in the past year and a half, suggesting retention and possible continuity of care challenges in a facility that’s been open barely 18 months.

Taken together, these data points continue to suggest a disconnect between the workforce policies put forward by your Department, your Department’s public messaging related to their impact, and the reported experiences coming out of VA facilities across the country. It is less clear today than when we first wrote you, that your Department has a clear handle on facility staffing needs across the country. That is why in addition to repeating our requests for the following information, we request a briefing for our offices, detailing current VA workforce dynamics across Virginia.

Your response to our previous letter simply noted that the decision to eliminate approximately 26,000 unfilled positions nationwide “was made in coordination with facilities across the country.”

What were the criteria by which facility leaders were directed to identify positions “that they don’t need”? Was this determination based on current conditions, or future projections? Were facilities provided a quota or target of any kind?

Did Department personnel involved in this process receive any concern, pushback, or other feedback in opposition to the vacancy cuts – particularly related to clinical impact, overall workforce health, or personnel morale – from any facility- or VISN-level personnel? What was the process for addressing these concerns?

Did facility leaders concur with the final determinations regarding vacancy cuts?

We again note the statutory requirement for the VA to “develop, validate, and implement a staffing model…that includes appropriate target staffing levels nationally, regionally, and locally to ensure timely access to care and effectively oversee the provision of care by the Department, whether at a facility of the Department or through a non-Department provider”. We further recognize that various staffing models and caseload requirements already exist in the Department for positions from nurses to housing services case managers.

Based on the position allocations for each facility in Virginia, which facilities are meeting the current minimum staffing for these models and caseload requirements? Which facilities are not meeting these requirements and by how much?

Congress has provided VA with additional tools and resources specifically intended to help the Department recruit and retain personnel in difficult-to-fill positions, including via expanded recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives; critical-skills incentives; student loan repayment authorities; and additional pay flexibilities.

Relevant to severe occupational shortages in Virginia and elsewhere around the country, how and where have you utilized available recruitment, relocation, or retention incentives, as well as employment flexibilities? Have these authorities been so far utilized to the maximum extent?

For facilities in Virginia, including newly opened Fredericksburg and Chesapeake clinics, how many personnel have left employment with the VA since January 2025? Please provide data broken down by facility.

Please provide a complete list of positions for each facility in Virginia broken down by location and hiring status as of October 1, 2026.

Have any facilities in Virginia requested authorization to recruit for a position above their allocation? If so, please provide an accounting of each request and its status. For any denied requests, please provide justification for the denial.

What are the steps for facility leaders to request positions above the cap? Please provide the names and titles of individuals above the facility level who review and decide to approve or deny these requests.

For facilities in Virginia with funding to hire for vacant positions that were cut in Fiscal Year 2026, what was that funding used for instead?

We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.

title: Ahead of Midterms, New Warnock Report Finds Election Officials Across Georgia Confident in Election Security
text:
Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock released a new report examining Georgia’s election preparedness ahead of the November elections

The report features testimony from election administrators across 10 Georgia counties, all of whom say they are prepared and confident in the security of the state’s midterm elections

Senator Warnock is calling on Congress to strengthen election security and protect access to the ballot box by investing in election administration

Senator Reverend Warnock: “It is now up to Congress to implement meaningful safeguards that maintain election integrity by protecting and supporting those on the frontlines”

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), one of the Senate’s leading advocates for voting rights, released a new report examining Georgia’s election preparedness ahead of the November midterm elections. The report draws on interviews with election officials from 10 geographically and politically diverse Georgia counties to assess the readiness of local administrators. Despite President Trump’s repeated, unsubstantiated claims of widespread voter fraud, election officials interviewed across Georgia overwhelmingly expressed confidence in the security of the 2026 elections.

“While President Trump continues to promote baseless lies to incite fear and chaos ahead of the midterms, Georgia’s election officials are doing the important work of ensuring every vote is securely counted,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. “It is now up to Congress to implement meaningful safeguards that maintain election integrity by protecting and supporting those on the frontlines.”

Based on interviews with election officials from counties governed by Democratic-led, Republican-led, and nonpartisan Board of Commissioners, Senator Warnock’s report affirms that local election administrators across Georgia feel well-equipped and prepared to manage the 2026 November elections. While confidence in election security is high among the Georgia officials interviewed, officials agreed that additional federal funding for election administration and security would help further strengthen their work.

In response to the new findings, Senator Warnock is calling on Congress to immediately pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which would restore key protections of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, and the Freedom to Vote Act, which would create national standards for early, absentee, and in-person voting; prevent partisan takeovers of local election administration; and improve election security. Additionally, he is urging his colleagues to support funding for the Election Assistance Commission’s Election Security Grant program to help county election boards modernize voting systems and infrastructure, maintain accurate voter registration databases, recruit and train poll workers, and keep elections safe and secure.

Senator Warnock is a leading voting rights advocate. Last month, he released a report examining the additional hurdles married women would face when registering to vote or updating their voter registration if the SAVE America Act were enacted. Earlier this year, he unveiled a comprehensive policy agenda to repair and strengthen American democracy in the wake of escalating attacks on the right to vote. Following the Supreme Court’s decision to gut the Voting Rights Act in April, Senator Warnock argued that voting rights legislation must be the number one priority for Democrats when they regain the majority in the U.S. Senate.

title: Welch, Pocan Lead 16 Members Urging USDA to Reverse Course on New Cost-Sharing Requirement that Hurts Dairy Farmers and Producers
text:
Lawmakers to Rollins: “A requirement meant to stretch federal dollars could instead keep those dollars from reaching the farms and processors Congress intended to help.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), a member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, joined U.S. Representative Mark Pocan (D-WI-02) in leading 16 bicameral lawmakers urging the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to reverse course on a new cost-share requirement for the Dairy Business Innovation (DBI) Initiatives program, which will burden America’s already struggling dairy industry.

In their letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins, the lawmakers highlight how USDA recently added 25% cost-share requirement for the DBI Initiatives program will hurt dairy farmers and processors already facing volatile markets, higher production and fuel costs, labor shortages, aging infrastructure, and growing competition. The lawmakers call on USDA to withdraw the new cost-share requirement for DBI and reissue the Notice of Funding Opportunity without a matching requirement.

“Today, the four existing initiatives serve dairy farmers and processors in 41 states and territories, representing 87 percent of the nation’s milkshed,” wrote the lawmakers. “They are the Dairy Business Innovation Alliance at the University of Wisconsin, the Northeast Dairy Business Innovation Center at the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets, the Pacific Coast Coalition at California State University, Fresno, and the Southeast Dairy Business Innovation Initiative at the University of Tennessee. Together they have awarded more than $106 million to 911 dairy businesses. Even so, they have been able to meet only about 35% of the demand they see through their competitive award processes. By law, at least half of each initiative’s funding must go directly to grants to dairy businesses. The remainder supports technical assistance in business planning, marketing, and product development.”

The lawmakers continued: “The need for this support has never been greater. Dairy farmers and processors are facing volatile markets, higher production and fuel costs, labor shortages, aging infrastructure, and growing competition. Small and mid-sized operations in particular depend on DBI to modernize equipment, develop new products, reach new markets, and keep viable outlets for farmers’ milk. DBI works because it puts federal resources in the hands of regional partners with deep technical expertise and long-standing relationships with the dairy businesses they serve.”

“The organizations that host these initiatives are public universities and a state department of agriculture, working in partnership with a nonprofit trade association. They do not profit from DBI funding, and they generally do not have unrestricted resources to cover a 25 percent match,” the lawmakers concluded. “The initiatives have told USDA that the new requirement could make continued operation of the program untenable. A requirement meant to stretch federal dollars could instead keep those dollars from reaching the farms and processors Congress intended to help.”

Joining Senator Welch and Rep. Pocan on this letter are Sens. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and Reps. Becca Balint (D-VT-AL), Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), Jim Costa (D-CA-21), Joe Courtney (D-CT-02), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH-02), John Mannion (D-NY-02), Gwen Moore (D-WI-04), Chellie Pingree (D-ME-01), and Gabe Vasquez (D-NM-02).

Read and download the lawmakers’ full letter to Ag Secretary Rollins.

The Senator has championed legislation to expand federal support for organic dairy farmers and ensure fair prices for family dairies, including the bipartisan Domestic Organic Investment Act, the Milk from Family Dairies Act, and the Organic Dairy Assistance, Investment, and Reporting Yields Act (O DAIRY) Act. The Senator also led 14 colleagues in introducing the Opportunities in Organic Act to reduce barriers to organic farming in Vermont. Senator Welch’s bipartisan bill, the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act, was signed into law earlier this year.

title: Welch Statement on Trump Administration Abandoning Disaster-Impacted States
text:
“President Trump’s efforts to dismantle FEMA and limit the federal government’s disaster response will put countless Americans in danger and destroy state and local economies. The Trump Administration has little concern or understanding of the limited capacity of state governments to respond in the wake of a disaster. State and municipal governments do herculean work after a disaster hits, but many communities simply do not have the capacity or budget to rebuild and repair. The federal government must help states weather the storm.

“Vermont’s catastrophic floods of 2023 and 2024 would have been impossible to recover from without the immediate, lifesaving response efforts provided by FEMA. I have no doubt our next flood or natural disaster will be harder to recover from because of President Trump’s misguided, reckless policies.

“FEMA reform must be done in a bipartisan and collaborative way, with state and local governments at the table, working with us, to improve this agency. FEMA does need to be fixed, and state and local governments should be empowered to spend federal disaster funds faster and more efficiently—but limiting federal aid and shifting even more administrative burden onto the states after a disaster will only make recovery more painful and more expensive.”

title: Young Announces More than $75 Million for Rail Infrastructure Projects Across Indiana
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) announced more than $75 million in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safey Improvement (CRISI) Program for seven rail infrastructure projects across Indiana.

The funding will support improvements to freight rail infrastructure, enhance safety, and strengthen the reliability of rail transportation throughout the state.

“Indiana’s rail infrastructure plays an important role in supporting our economy and connecting Hoosier businesses to markets across the country,” said Senator Young. “These investments will help improve rail safety, modernize aging infrastructure, and make our transportation network more efficient and reliable. I appreciate Secretary Duffy’s partnership in helping make these investments possible.”

CRISI Grant Awards:

Freight Rail Revitalization Project in Indiana and Illinois

Award: $25,168,800

Evansville Western Railway, Inc. will improve approximately 124.5 miles of railroad between Evansville, Indiana, and Okawville, Illinois. The project includes replacing rail and ties, installing safety equipment, constructing a locomotive maintenance facility, and rehabilitating 12 locomotives.

Program for Operational Workflows & Equipment Reliability (POWER)

Award: $15,231,696

Elkhart & Western Railroad, LLC will support upgrades to Patriot Rail’s locomotive fleet across 15 rail properties in 17 states. The project will replace aging locomotives and improve freight rail efficiency and reliability.

Coal and Corn in Hoosier Land Project

Award: $14,544,000

RailTex, Inc. will rehabilitate approximately 100 miles of railroad infrastructure in Indianapolis and Evansville. Improvements include replacing rails, ties, crossings, and signals, installing safety equipment, and repairing or replacing four aging bridges

Southeastern Indiana Corridor Improvement Project

Award: $7,915,813

The City of Madison Port Authority will rehabilitate approximately seven miles of Madison Railroad track in North Vernon, improve siding, and install a signal at a public railroad crossing. The improvements will increase rail capacity and reduce derailment risks.

Northwest Indiana Rail Connectivity and Expansion Project (NICE)

Award: $6,880,843

Chesapeake and Indiana Railroad, LLC will rehabilitate rail infrastructure in Hanna, La Crosse, and Wellsboro. The project includes replacing tiles, rehabilitating freight rail bridges, improving crossings, and constructing approximately one mile of new siding.

New Era Railroad State of Good Repair and Safety Improvement Project

Award: $3,195,432

New Era Railroad, LLC will rehabilitate approximately 12 miles of track in Wells, Huntington, and Grant counties, including replacing ties, improving track conditions, and rehabilitating two railroad crossings.

Freight, Rail Safety & Reliability Improvement Project

Award: $2,880,000

Chicago South Shore & South Bend Railroad will rehabilitate tracks in northern Indiana and northeastern Illinois, replace ties, improve switches, and upgrade four railroad crossings to enhance safety and reliability.

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces Nearly $1.7 Million for Healthcare Job Training and Technology Education at Inland Empire Community Colleges
text:
Crafton Hills College will receive over $1.1 million to train student EMTs, paramedics and nursing assistants and San Bernardino Valley College will receive nearly $600,000 to teach students responsible artificial intelligence (AI) usage

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced $1,69,2495 in grants for the San Bernardino Community College District. The funding will expand training at Crafton Hills College for healthcare and first responder jobs and teach San Bernardino Valley College students to use artificial intelligence responsibly in school and at work.

Of that funding, Crafton Hills College will receive $1,102,000 to expand EMT and paramedic apprenticeships, start a nursing assistant pathway at Pacific High School and create a new occupational therapy assistant program. Over five years, the funding will help train 220 EMT and paramedic apprentices, 115 nursing assistant students and 40 occupational therapy assistant students. It will also provide more than 1,500 students with workplace learning, educational planning and career guidance services.

San Bernardino Valley College will receive the remaining $590,495 to teach at least 5,000 students over five years how to use AI for research, communication, problem-solving and career preparation and how to prevent issues with accuracy, privacy and bias. The grant will also support student workshops, peer mentoring and a new course on AI. The funding will train 450 instructors and update at least 100 courses to incorporate responsible AI usage into teaching and learning.

“For students at San Bernardino Valley College and Crafton Hills College, a good-paying, successful career starts with a strong foundation,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “That’s why I’m proud to announce this funding to create job opportunities for future nurses and EMTs while making sure students learn to use AI the right way before they start their careers. I’m excited to see how these grants will help young people in the Inland Empire build their lives right here in our community.”

“Families want an education they can afford, close to home, that leads to a good-paying job,” said Diana Z. Rodriguez, Chancellor, San Bernardino Community College District. “These federal investments will help students at Crafton Hills College and San Bernardino Valley College finish school and prepare for careers in firefighting, nursing, the skilled trades and many other fields. We thank Congressman Aguilar, Congress and the U.S. Department of Education for helping our students build a better future here in the Inland Empire.”

“We are grateful for this investment in our students and our community,” said Dr. Gilbert J. Contreras, President, San Bernardino Valley College. “San Bernardino Valley College will continue our legacy of providing students with affordable pathways to meaningful wages. These resources help our students prepare for a world that is rapidly changing around them by strengthening our academic programs through responsible use of artificial intelligence and technology. This is an incredible investment in the future of our community.”

This funding comes from the U.S. Department of Education’s Strengthening Institutions Program (84.031A) grant awards.

title: Amo Concludes 2026 Blue Economy Tour at New NOAA Operations Center, Introduces Bipartisan QUAHOGS Act to Protect RI Shellfish
text:
Newport, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01) concluded his 2026 Blue Economy Tour in Newport by visiting the new National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Atlantic Marine Operations Center. Amo also announced the introduction of the bipartisan Quantifying Uncertainty and Action to Help Optimize Growth of Shellfish (QUAHOGS) Act with Congressman Andrew Garbarino (R-NY-02).

At Naval Station Newport, Amo visited the new facility that will manage NOAA’s Atlantic research vessel fleet and serve as homeport for NOAA ships Henry B. Bigelow, Okeanos Explorer, Thomas Jefferson, and the upcoming Discoverer. The center’s arrival in Rhode Island follows years of work by Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) to secure the relocation and federal funding needed to make it happen. Once operational, the facility will house and maintain NOAA research vessels that collect critical ocean data and support the fishermen, maritime businesses, and coastal communities that depend on NOAA’s research.

Amo also introduced the QUAHOGS Act in the U.S. House of Representatives to protect Rhode Island’s shellfish stock. The bill, which was introduced in the Senate by Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), establishes a research task force of federal agency representatives, fishery management councils, state representatives, scientists, and watermen to understand how to stop the decrease of shellfish populations along the United States East Coast.

“Rhode Island truly is the Ocean State,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01). “Throughout this year’s Blue Economy tour, I’ve met Rhode Islanders who work on our waters, study our oceans, and build what comes next. From NOAA’s research vessels to the fishermen who depend on healthy shellfish populations, we must invest in the science and solutions that keep this industry strong. I’m proud to introduce the bipartisan QUAHOGS Act to help address declining shellfish populations, protect our ocean, and support the good-paying jobs and coastal communities that make Rhode Island’s Blue Economy thrive.”

“Shellfishing has long been part of Long Island’s economy, including the famous Blue Point oyster that originated right here in my district,” said Congressman Andrew Garbarino (R-NY-02). “Declining shellfish populations threaten the fishermen and small businesses that depend on these waters. I’m proud to work with Congressman Amo on this bipartisan legislation to better understand what’s driving these declines and help protect this industry for future generations.”

Background

Congressman Amo’s 2026 Blue Economy Tour has highlighted the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy. Amo visited REGENT Craft, where he helped cut the ribbon on their new electric Seaglider factory. Next, Amo visited Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities to explore advances in shellfish production, aquaculture, and blue biotechnology. Amo toured Hinckley Yachts’ Portsmouth facility to discuss the skilled trades and maritime jobs that keep Rhode Island moving. Later, Amo visited Solid State Power to highlight the importance of new battery technology to maritime innovation. Then, Amo visited with students in the marine trades program at North Providence High School and Polaris MEP’s Manufacturing Day. Both programs introduce Rhode Island students to Blue Economy career opportunities.

Rhode Island’s Blue Economy directly employs 36,000 Rhode Islanders and contributes over $5 billion to the state’s gross domestic product every year.

In 2024, Congressman Amo toured Rhode Island’s First Congressional District to highlight the Ocean State’s leadership in the Blue Economy across labor, education, business, and defense.

title: Ansari Celebrates $625,000 Federal Grant Awarded to Redeem Neighborhoods for Youth Substance Use Prevention
text:
LAVEEN, AZ — Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) recently joined Redeem Neighborhoods and the Laveen Coalition at Collective Coffee in South Phoenix to celebrate their federal Drug-Free Communities (DFC) grant awarding up to $625,000 over five years to support youth substance use prevention efforts in the Laveen community.

“I’m proud to have worked with Redeem Neighborhoods to secure federal funding for youth substance use prevention efforts in Laveen. Every young person deserves the opportunity to grow up healthy, supported, and surrounded by people who believe in their potential,” said Rep. Ansari. “One of my top priorities in Congress is bringing federal dollars home to support community-driven solutions that give our families the tools and resources they need to succeed.”

“From the time we first met Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari when she served on the Phoenix City Council, she recognized the value of our work and the importance of investing in grassroots organizations like ours. She and her team didn’t just listen to our community—they partnered with us, opened doors, and created opportunities for our voices to be heard. As she has taken on greater leadership roles, that commitment has remained strong,” said Jeanette Arnds, Executive Director of Redeem Neighborhoods. “Her continued support, including helping secure federal funding for youth substance use prevention in Laveen, demonstrates what is possible when leaders invest in local organizations that know their communities best. We’re grateful to have a partner who continues to show up for South Phoenix and the families we serve.”

The grant, funded through the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP) and administered through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), will provide $125,000 annually to strengthen community-led prevention initiatives. Ansari submitted a letter of support for Redeem Neighborhoods’ application.

More information about the DFC program can be found HERE.

title: Ansari Leads Democratic Women’s Caucus in Standing with Greene-Placentia and Condemning Sexual Violence
text:
PHOENIX – This week, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), alongside Representatives Greg Stanton (AZ-04) and Grijalva (AZ-07), and the Congressional Democratic Women’s Caucus issued the following statement condemning the horrific sexual assault of Bernadette Greene-Placentia, a candidate for Arizona’s 8th Congressional District:

“The Arizona Congressional House Delegation and the Democratic Women’s Caucus condemn in the absolute strongest terms the grotesque attack and rape committed against Bernadette Greene-Placentia, candidate for Arizona’s 8th Congressional District. Our hearts go out to her as she navigates the severe trauma of this horrific and monstrous attack as well as to her family, friends, and staff who are standing with her through it.

“No candidate for office should be faced with physical or sexual violence, something which we have seen far too often across this country and in Arizona in particular.

“Sexual violence is a national crisis. According to RAINN, an estimated 443,634 rapes and sexual assaults occur annually in the United States, and nearly 9 in 10 victims of reported rape are women or girls. These numbers underscore the devastating scale of this violence and the disproportionate harm it inflicts on women.

“Sexual violence should have absolutely no place in our society or politics, and it’s high past time that we as a country do everything in our power to protect victims and address it with the severity it warrants.

“Far too many have survived sexual violence at some point in their lives and far too few have seen justice served on their behalf. We demand that the perpetrators of this attack are swiftly brought to justice and that Ms. Greene-Placentia is able to heal.”

title: Reps. Ansari, Grijalva and Dexter Join Reproductive Freedom for All to Advocate for Pregnant Women in Immigration Detention
text:
ELOY, AZ — Yesterday, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) and Maxine Dexter (OR-03), joined alongside Reproductive Freedom for All President Mini Timmaraju, for an oversight visit to the Eloy Detention Center to hear directly from women about their reproductive health experiences in immigration detention. Multiple pregnant women have previously been held at Eloy, including one who miscarried. This is a departure from the policies of previous administrations that typically did not hold pregnant people in detention.

“The inhumane conditions inside Eloy Detention Center are unconscionable. Maria, a high-risk pregnant woman, is being denied critical medical care and adequate food. My constituent, Lilianne, the wife of a U.S. citizen, was detained at her green card appointment and is now being denied basic feminine hygiene products. No one should be treated this way,” said Rep. Ansari. “All the while, the Trump Administration is pouring billions into ICE as private prison corporations like CoreCivic and GEO Group profit from detention. The level of cruelty and corruption is abundantly clear. This is a profound failure of human dignity, and we will hold this Administration accountable.”

This marked Ansari's fourteenth oversight visit to an ICE detnetion facility. This visit focused on the urgent need to protect reproductive health, ensure access to adequate medical care, and uphold the dignity of women in immigration detention. During the visit, the lawmakers heard from women about their experiences navigating pregnancy and accessing essential reproductive health supplies while detained. The lawmakers met with two women:

Maria Alejandra Valero Brinez, a 24-year-old Venezuelan woman and mother of a six-year-old son. She has valid employment authorization until 2029, a pending asylum petition, and no criminal convictions. She was living in Mesa, Arizona before she was detained in August. She is approximately five months pregnant, and described serious concerns about her pregnancy and access to adequate medical care while detained. She has experienced spotting and reported that she has to throw herself on the ground and plead for attention in order to receive medical care. When she was able to receive care, the doctors informed her she has a low-lying placenta — the same condition that led to a stillborn birth three years earlier. Despite having a high-risk pregnancy, she said she has not been able to receive images from ultrasounds or other information about her and her baby’s condition. Maria fears for their safety and well-being, especially given the lack of information about her pregnancy. She is also afraid to express any emotion about her current condition, as detainees are often placed into solitary confinement if they show any signs of emotional distress.

Maria also raised concerns about access to drinking water and food inside the facility. Despite clear doctor’s recommendations to receive double food portions, Maria reports that one guard routinely dismisses this and only gives her the standard single portion. Maria also reported that she was not given antibiotics following a dental abscess that led to a tooth extraction. Untreated bacterial infections have the potential to cause miscarriages. Earlier this year, Emmanuel Damas passed away due to complications from an untreated tooth infection after being held at the Florence Detention Center.

Lilianne (who only wishes to use her first name), a Cuban woman detained at Eloy, described difficulties obtaining sufficient menstrual hygiene products. She reported inconsistent access, with the number of products provided varying depending on the detention officer, raising concerns about the availability of basic necessities for women in custody.

“Maria and Lilianne’s stories show the deliberate cruelty at the heart of the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda. Their treatment is not just inhumane — it is a disgraceful failure of the government's legal duty to protect the people in its custody,” said Rep. Grijalva. “While private contractors rake in billions of taxpayer dollars, they are denying the most vulnerable individuals – including pregnant people – their most basic necessities, including medical care, clean drinking water, and adequate food. These corporations are profiting off human suffering, and the Trump Administration is footing the bill with our tax dollars. Maria, as well as all pregnant people in detention, deserve dignity, proper medical care, and immediate release.”

“Maria is desperate to protect the health and safety of her baby. The federal government, by blatantly ignoring medical guidelines and advice, is putting her and her baby’s life at risk,” said Representative Dexter, who is one of six Democratic doctors in Congress. “She must be released immediately. DHS is refusing basic human and civil rights to the people in these despicable facilities and shows zero concern for the lives of people in them. Pregnant women and children do not belong in ICE detention. I will continue to use my experience as a physician, a mother, and my power as a member of Congress to protect women and children in this country.”

“ICE is putting women’s health, pregnancies, and lives at risk—leaving them to plead for even the most basic care and access to menstrual products,” said Mini Timmaraju, President and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All. “I’m grateful to Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter for shining light on this crisis, and Reproductive Freedom for All is with them every step of the way in demanding an end to this cruelty.”

title: Auchincloss, Griffith Introduce Faster Clinical Trials Act
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

CONTACT: Georgina.Burros@mail.house.gov (Auchincloss)

AUCHINCLOSS, GRIFFITH INTRODUCE FASTER CLINICAL TRIALS ACT

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA) and Morgan Griffith (R-VA) released the Faster Clinical Trials Act. The proposal would speed the development of new treatments, invest in clinical research, and propel U.S. leadership in biomedical innovation.

For decades, the United States has led the world in biomedical research and development; the testing and approval process by which potential medicines are deemed safe and effective; and the distribution of those medicines into clinical settings. However, America’s fragmented and friction-filled clinical research enterprise has not kept pace with the speed of science nor the investment by other nations. The difficulty of integrating clinical trials into U.S. sites of care has slowed down American development, testing, and approval.

The Faster Clinical Trials Act would upgrade America’s science infrastructure—the data, research sites, and clear standards needed to develop treatments—while preserving the Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) high standards for safety and effectiveness.

Bringing trials into everyday care

This legislation would establish a Center for Clinical Trial Innovation (CCI) within the FDA’s drug review center. The CCI would lead implementation of the Cures in Care Initiative, working with clinical sites to bring research into routine care.

Within one year of enactment, the center would establish at least three trial networks, prioritizing community health centers, rural clinics, and other sites with fewer resources. Training, shared technology, and technical support would help providers conduct trials where patients already receive care.

Removing barriers with the FDA

The proposal would direct the FDA and federal partners to connect health records and research systems, protect patient privacy, and reduce duplicate ethics reviews.

It would create a faster review process for lower-risk Phase 1 trials, including qualified third-party reviews with quality checks by the FDA. It would also advance human-based models, artificial intelligence, and alternatives to animal testing.

To prevent avoidable delays, the FDA would address common causes of clinical holds and improve support for researchers. The bill would align global trial standards, strengthen oversight of foreign research, and promote generic and biosimilar competition. It would also strengthen the FDA’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub to support flexible trial designs and help developers navigate review.

Building better evidence for treatment

The draft would establish a legal framework for the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence and a process to update cancer drug labels using genomic evidence, helping identify patients who may not benefit from certain treatments.

It would also build on All of Us to establish a national biobank linking biological samples, genomic data, and health records.

Together, these changes aim to deliver better evidence and faster trials for American patients—not lower standards.

title: NEW REPORT: WEAK TRUMP ANTITRUST ENFORCEMENT AND BACKROOM DEALS ARE DRIVING UP COSTS FOR AMERICAN FAMILIES
text:
TEXT OF REPORT

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL) and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) released a new report, Settling For Less: How Trump’s weak antitrust enforcement and backroom deals are driving up costs, a comprehensive review of the second Trump Administration’s record of toothless antitrust settlements, dismissed enforcement actions, and widespread approval of massive corporate mergers, apparently creating a pay-to-play system that drives up costs and hurts consumers.

Senators Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Representatives Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.) and Jerry Nadler (D-N.Y.) joined in releasing the report.

During his campaign, President Trump promised to “Make America Competitive Again” and lower costs “on day one.” Instead, the Trump Administration has repeatedly sided with giant corporations, in some cases after the corporations made contributions to Trump’s vanity projects, rather than standing up for working families.

The new report highlights how the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) Antitrust Division and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have approved major mergers with little scrutiny, overridden enforcement recommendations from career staff, and pursued weak settlements favoring large corporations, often based on the influence of Trump-connected corporate lobbyists. The report also raises concerns about potential pay-to-play arrangements, revealing that many of the corporations benefitting from President Trump’s lax antitrust enforcement policies have contributed millions to President Trump’s political committees and Trump-affiliated projects. Specific topline findings of this investigation include:

The Trump Administration routinely rubber-stamps harmful corporate mergers that pose competition risks. Across real estate, media, telecommunications, retail, banking, airlines, health care, and entertainment industries, corporate giants have announced at least 330 large mergers totaling more than $2.2 trillion. These deals often cleared despite major antitrust concerns, serious warnings from expert career staff, and clear evidence that the mergers would harm consumers, workers, and small businesses.

For example, following the Justice Department’s approval of the Compass-Anywhere Real Estate merger over warnings from competition experts, Compass took control of up to 70% of home sales in some areas. That massive market power allows the company to dictate rules, squeeze out local brokerages, and hurt everyday homebuyers and sellers.

The Trump Administration routinely settles or dismisses antitrust enforcement actions without meaningful remedies. The Administration has allowed giant corporations facing antitrust lawsuits to settle with relatively small fines, narrow behavioral promises, no admissions of wrongdoing, and little or no restitution for the working families and small businesses harmed by the alleged anticompetitive conduct. In some cases, the Administration has simply walked away from a lawsuit, allowing alleged anticompetitive conduct to continue unchallenged.

In May 2024, the Justice Department and a bipartisan coalition of states filed an antitrust lawsuit to break up Live Nation Entertainment and its subsidiary Ticketmaster, alleging the company illegally monopolized the live entertainment industry and imposed inflated ticket prices and fees on millions of consumers. In 2025, Live Nation donated $500,000 to President Trump’s inaugural committee and brought on board a network of Trump-connected lobbyists and allies. Following meetings with Live Nation’s CEO and a reported phone call from President Trump directing the Justice Department to settle, the DOJ abruptly ended its lawsuit just one week into the trial. Instead of forcing a breakup of the company as originally sought, the government accepted a weak deal: minor rule changes at roughly twelve smaller venues and a fine equal to just four days of Live Nation’s revenue. If state Attorneys General had not decided to continue the case and ultimately won a jury verdict against Ticketmaster, millions of fans would have continued to be squeezed by ticket fees.

The Trump Administration’s weak antitrust enforcement appears to be driven by influence-peddling and is surrounded by a cloud of corruption. Corporations facing antitrust scrutiny have repeatedly hired lobbyists with ties to President Trump and senior Administration officials, made substantial contributions to President Trump’s political committees or vanity projects, and promised changes to their business models that are aligned with President Trump’s agenda in exchange for favorable enforcement decisions—mergers cleared, investigations dropped, or cases resolved through weak settlements. Combined, this recurring pattern suggests a pay-to-play system.

Paramount hired Ballard Partners—a Trump-connected lobbying firm—while competing to acquire Warner Bros. Larry Ellison, the father of Paramount controlling owner David Ellison, donated $45 million to a political group supporting President Trump’s 2024 election efforts. The Ellisons appeared to have cultivated what has been described as a “cozy alliance of mutual back-scratching” with President Trump as they sought approval for the Paramount/Warner Bros. merger. Paramount ultimately won the bid, and the merger received DOJ approval.

The Trump Administration’s failure to enforce antitrust laws raises consumers’ costs and limits choice. Across five vital sectors of the American economy—food and groceries, consumer goods, housing, health care, and media and entertainment—working families and small businesses stand to bear the brunt of the Administration’s corporate giveaways and antitrust inaction.

“The evidence of the Administration’s antitrust failures is woven directly into the daily budget of American households. Average monthly grocery bills have climbed to an all-time high, with some sources estimating the bill for a family of four at $1,430 a month. Average monthly rent hit a record high during this Administration at $1,910/month. The monthly price of health insurance has surged over 25 percent from 2025 to 2026 alone. And total U.S. credit card debt has soared to an all-time high of $1.28 trillion, while a February 2026 survey found that 53 percent of Americans do not have sufficient savings to cover a $1,000 emergency expense,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Meanwhile, the corporations benefiting from the Administration’s weak antitrust enforcement are enjoying an unprecedented windfall… The verdict on the Administration’s antitrust record is clear: in a complete betrayal of President Trump’s campaign promise to lower costs “on day one,” federal enforcers have surrendered market oversight to corporate giants in industry after industry, leaving American families to pay the price,” concluded the lawmakers.

title: ICYMI: Bice Joins Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport Expansion Groundbreaking
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Stephanie Bice attended the recent expansion of the Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport, which she helped secure $6 million in federal funding for. Read more below:

The Cities of Guthrie and Edmond joined state and federal leaders at Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport to celebrate the ribbon cutting of their new terminal expansion, marking a significant investment in the Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport’s future and the region’s aviation infrastructure.

The $7 million project includes a new approximately 5,500-square-foot terminal facility, nearly doubling the airport’s existing terminal space, along with approximately 150,000 square feet of additional aircraft parking apron. The expansion is designed to better accommodate based and visiting aircraft while enhancing the experience for pilots, passengers, businesses, and the broader community.

The ceremony featured remarks from Congresswoman Stephanie Bice, Senator Chuck Hall, Representative Nicole Miller, Guthrie Mayor Adam Ropp, Edmond Mayor Mark Nash, and Grayson Ardies, Executive Director of the Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics (ODAA).

“It was an honor to join local leaders to celebrate the expansion of the Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport,” said Congresswoman Stephanie Bice. “I was proud to secure the $6 million in federal funding for this project, which will double the terminal space, provide additional aircraft parking, and improve airport amenities. This is another great example of bringing taxpayer dollars back to Oklahoma to support the important work already being done in our communities.”

The project was funded through a combination of $6 million in federal funding secured through a Community Project Funding request supported by Representative Bice, $500,000 from the State of Oklahoma through the Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics, and a combined $500,000 local investment, with the Cities of Guthrie and Edmond each contributing $250,000.

The new terminal will offer a range of amenities designed to support aviation activity and create a welcoming destination for the public. Planned features include a restaurant serving airport visitors and the general public, an outdoor airside patio overlooking aircraft arrivals and departures, a conference room that will also serve as a public meeting space and aviation classroom, pilot offices, a 24-hour-access pilot lounge, and office space for fixed-base operator (FBO) and airport staff.

“This new terminal is a great example of how investments in aviation infrastructure can support communities and strengthen Oklahoma’s aerospace industry,” said ODAA Executive Director Grayson Ardies.“By expanding facilities and creating more opportunities for aviation education, business, and general aviation activity, Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport is positioning itself to serve the region for many years to come.”

The airport is home to a variety of aviation-related businesses, including flight schools, aircraft maintenance operations, composite aircraft-part manufacturing company Zivko Aeronautics, and a pipeline patrol company. Its 5,001-foot concrete runway can accommodate a wide range of business and general aviation aircraft, including business jets. Located near I-35 and outside the more congested airspace associated with Oklahoma City, the airport offers convenient access for business and general aviation operations.

The terminal expansion also reflects the longstanding partnership between Guthrie and Edmond. The two cities have jointly sponsored and supported the regional airport since 2004, demonstrating a shared commitment to regional collaboration and economic opportunity.

The new facility will serve as a front door to the region, welcoming visitors arriving for business, recreation, aviation activities, and other purposes while providing additional space for the airport’s continued growth.

title: REP. BOEBERT APPLAUDS $8 BILLION HARVEST FUEL RELIEF PROGRAM TO SUPPORT COLORADO FARMERS AND FAMILIES
text:
Lone Tree, CO — U.S. Representative Lauren Boebert (R-CO) today welcomed the Trump Administration’s announcement of the $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief (HFR) Program, which will deliver one-time payments to American farmers facing higher input costs and temporary market disruptions during this harvest season.

“The Trump administration and Secretary Rollins are putting Farmers First with real, targeted relief when our producers need it most. Colorado’s Fourth District has some of the most productive farms and ranches in the state. This support will help our wheat, corn, sorghum, millet, forage, and other crop growers manage soaring diesel costs during harvest so they can keep feeding America and keep their operations strong,” said Rep. Boebert.

The Harvest Fuel Relief Program, authorized under the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act and administered by the Farm Service Agency, provides proportional support based on planted acres, production cost estimates, yields, and prices. Commodity-specific payment rates for Title I crops are expected in November. The program builds on earlier 2026 assistance, including the Farmer Bridge Assistance program.

Colorado’s Fourth District is home to thousands of family farms spanning millions of acres, with major production of wheat, corn, sorghum, proso millet and forage crops, alongside a strong livestock sector.

Elevated diesel prices this fall have increased costs for equipment, irrigation, and transportation across the Eastern Plains and rural communities. This announcement complements other recent steps Rep. Boebert has supported to lower fuel costs for Colorado producers and families, including expanded access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel.

“Our farmers and ranchers in the 4th District work hard every day to feed this country. I will continue fighting to deliver practical relief, lower costs, and a stronger farm safety net so they can pass their operations on to the next generation,” said Rep. Boebert.

title: BOST HELPS SECURE $25 MILLION FEDERAL GRANT TO IMPROVE SOUTHERN ILLINOIS RAIL INFRASTRUCTURE
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Representative Mike Bost (IL-12) today announced that he has helped secure $25.1 million in federal funding for Evansville Western Railway to improve approximately 124.5 miles of freight rail infrastructure stretching from Evansville, Indiana to Okawville, Illinois.

“Southern Illinois has always played an important role in keeping America’s economy moving, and our railroads are a big part of that,” said Bost. “Whether it’s moving coal, agricultural products, or other critical materials, our businesses depend on safe and reliable transportation to get the job done. I’m proud to see this investment coming to our region because it means stronger infrastructure, safer rail operations, and more opportunities for the hardworking folks who call Southern Illinois home. I’ll keep working to make sure our communities have the resources they need to grow and succeed.”

The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Grant Program, will support major upgrades to the railway’s tracks, equipment, and maintenance facilities. The improvements will strengthen rail safety, improve service reliability, and support the efficient transportation of American-made energy products throughout the region.

The project will include replacing rail and ties, installing hot bearing detectors to identify potential equipment failures, constructing a new locomotive maintenance facility, and rehabilitating 12 locomotives. These improvements will help modernize the short-line railroad, reduce the risk of equipment failures, and ensure more dependable freight service for businesses throughout Southern Illinois and Southwestern Indiana.

title: Rep. Smith delivers remarks at HHS Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Summit
text:
The following are excerpts of remarks delivered by Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), the founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Alzheimer’s Caucus, at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS) first-ever Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Summit on Thursday, October 22nd, 2026:

Special thanks to Secretary Kennedy for his amazing efforts to combat Alzheimer’s Disease and for hosting the first-ever Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Summit.

And thanks to each of the panelists at today’s summit for bringing renewed visibility and the redoubling of efforts to alleviate the symptoms of, and someday cure, this catastrophic disease.

Twenty-seven years ago—in 1999—I, along with Senator Ed Markey, created the bipartisan Congressional Alzheimer’s Caucus, which I co-chair to this day. I was also the prime sponsor of the Ronald Reagan Alzheimer's Breakthrough Act, named for our late, great President, which would have doubled NIH funding for Alzheimer’s to $1.4 billion a year.

Then, after years of legislative struggle and with an all-important push from the Alzheimer’s Association, the big breakthrough came in 2011, when Congress passed the National Alzheimer’s Project Act, or NAPA—a law I co-authored.

NAPA created a new, frequently updated and expanded national strategy, with the ultimate goal of finding a cure. NAPA also created an advisory committee for a whole-of-government response to the crisis.

The impact has been profound. Alzheimer’s research funding for the NIH was $600 million in 2015. Now in Fiscal Year 2026, federal research for Alzheimer’s is over $3.8 billion—a 600% increase!

This funding has yielded real, tangible advancements in our understanding of Alzheimer’s and other dementias. Earlier this year, a NIH-funded study discovered a new biomarker test for Alzheimer’s that can distinguish between stages of the disease, marking an important advancement in our ability to find the condition early and mitigate cognitive decline.

None of this progress would be possible without the tireless advocacy of groups like the Alzheimer’s Association and countless individuals—including my good friend Christine Hopkins—who have shared their stories and championed much-needed research funding and support for Alzheimer’s.

That said, there is still much more work to be done. An estimated 7.4 million Americans above the age of 65 live with Alzheimer’s disease, or 1 in 9 individuals 65 or older. This number may increase to as many as 13 million by 2050.

While early detection and treatment makes a clear difference in maintaining cognitive function and overall quality of life, too often, Alzheimer’s and other dementias go underdiagnosed.

58 percent—more than half—of older adults with probable dementia in the United States are either undiagnosed or are unaware of their diagnosis.

There is also a critical need to provide more support for caregivers and support services. Over 12 million family members and other unpaid caregivers provided an estimated 19.6 billion hours of care to people living with Alzheimer's or other dementias in 2025. We can and should do more to ease the financial, physical, and mental burdens these caregivers face.

My colleagues on the Hill and I welcome Secretary Kennedy’s announcement of the newest National Plan, as well as his continued commitment to hearing from advocates and caregivers. It is hoped that the panels today will bring further insights into the experiences of those living with Alzheimer’s and highlight additional avenues for the federal government to boost innovation, improve care and support, and support prevention—and one day, God willing, a cure.

###

title: Congressman Cohen Introduces the Mobile Stroke Units Improve Health Outcomes Act
text:
WASHINGTON – Congressman Steve Cohen (TN-9), Congressman Andrew Garbarino (NY-2) and Congresswoman Joyce Beatty (OH-3) today introduced the Mobile Stroke Units Improve Health Outcomes Act, legislation creating incentives for deploying mobile stroke units and providing Medicare reimbursement for their services.

Congressman Cohen made the following statement:

“Every 40 seconds, someone in the United States has a stroke. Research is clear: access to timely treatment is critical for recovery, and mobile stroke units can provide it, bringing medical expertise to the patient and treating them on the way to the hospital. Particularly in rural areas where the nearest specialist can be an hour or farther away, the time saved between the stroke and treatment because of the availability of a mobile stroke unit can make a tremendous difference.”

Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (NY-02) made the following statement:

“When someone suffers a stroke, every minute matters. Stony Brook Medicine’s mobile stroke units are already helping save lives on Long Island, including in communities throughout my district. These units bring critical care directly to patients when they need it most. I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation to ensure Medicare reimbursement policies support these lifesaving services and help more patients get treatment as quickly as possible.”

Congresswoman Joyce Beatty (OH-3) made the following statement:

“As a stroke survivor, I know firsthand that when it comes to a stroke, every second matters. The difference between getting treatment in minutes instead of hours can mean the difference between a full recovery and a lifetime of disability. I’m proud to introduce legislation that will help ensure these units can receive Medicare reimbursement, expand access to faster treatment, and give more Americans a fighting chance at recovery. No one's chance of surviving a stroke should depend on whether lifesaving care can reach them in time.”

M. Shazam Hussain, M.D., the immediate past president of PRE-Hospital Stroke Treatment Organization (PRESTO), made the following statement:

“More than 795,000 Americans experience a stroke each year—about one every 40 seconds. Reducing time-to-treatment is key to improve patient outcomes. Mobile Stroke Units (MSUs) provide critical care that can make a difference for patients by providing a stroke diagnosis and initiating treatment en route to the hospital. The Mobile Stroke Units Improve Health Outcomes Act will make MSUs more financially feasible for hospitals to operate, deliver specialized stroke care, and improve health outcomes for Americans.”

Currently, mobile stroke units (MSUs) are expensive to operate and are not appropriately reimbursed for services under Medicare.

The Mobile Stroke Units Improve Health Outcomes Act would authorize Medicare to reimburse MSUs for care and treatment of acute stroke under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (HOPPS). It also provides an incentive for an MSU to serve rural communities through a rendezvous model, matching the incentive available under the ambulance fee schedule.

title: CORREA INTRODUCES VETS AND PETS ACT TO IMPROVE VETERANS’ MENTAL AND PHYSICAL HEALTH
text:
Bill would create a VA grant program for nonprofits to provide dogs and cats as companion pets for eligible Veterans.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) introduced the Vets and Pets Act, legislation that would establish a grant program at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) for nonprofit organizations that provide dogs and cats as companion pets for eligible Veterans. The bill aims to improve Veterans’ mental and physical health by making it easier and more affordable to welcome a pet into their lives.

“Our Veterans put their lives on the line to defend our democracy and our freedom, and too many came home carrying wounds we can’t always see,” said Rep. Correa. “They deserve peace, not a life of anxiety and depression. A dog or a cat can be a friend on the hardest days. This bill is a simple, practical way to give our Veterans that companionship and improve their quality of life.”

The VA’s National Center for PTSD found that 23 percent of Veterans using VA care have had post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) at some point in their lives, and that Veterans experience higher rates of PTSD than non-Veterans. PTSD is associated with anxiety and depression, and can lead to social withdrawal.

Research shows that animal companionship improves both the physical and mental health of Veterans. The Vets and Pets Act would help more Veterans experience those benefits by removing the cost barriers that keep many from having a pet.

The Vets and Pets Act would:

Provide grant funding to nonprofits that place dogs and cats with Veterans

Cover initial supplies, including a collar, leash, bedding, and one month of food

Cover the cost of spaying or neutering the pet

Cover all initial medications and vaccinations

View the bill text here.

title: Rep. Goldman Applauds Major Agreement for Fort Worth F-35 Program
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Craig Goldman (R-TX) applauds the new 10-year F-35 program investment framework agreement between the Department of War and Lockheed Martin, strengthening America's military capabilities while driving economic growth in Fort Worth.

“America’s military must remain unmatched to keep our enemies at bay and our allies safe. I am delighted that the Department of War is prioritizing long-term funding for the elite Lockheed Martin F-35 program. This agreement supports thousands of jobs across Texas’ 12th Congressional District and strengthens our defense inventory,” said Congressman Craig Goldman. “Continued support for this program will fuel Fort Worth’s economy, create new opportunities for hardworking Texans, and equip our military with the cutting-edge technology needed to defend our freedoms.”

"This multiyear framework strengthens the way we can plan and invest in the F-35 enterprise," said Lockheed Martin Chairman, President and CEO Jim Taiclet. "With the greater certainty that comes from the U.S. government's transformative approach to F-35 production and sustainment, we can make the upfront investments needed to expand capacity, improve efficiency, and build a more resilient supply chain. That's good for the taxpayer, good for our suppliers and, most importantly, good for the United States and its allies."

Background

Lockheed Martin’s F-35 Lightning II program is a critical part of the Fort Worth economy, supporting over 49,000 jobs and generating an estimated $9 billion in economic impact each year.

The new 10-year framework agreement with the Department of War outlines plans for 850 fighter jets and continued production of 156 aircrafts annually, providing long-term stability for Fort Worth's defense manufacturing workforce. The agreement also aims to strengthen supply chains, reduce production costs, and save taxpayers billions of dollars, pending congressional authorization and appropriations.

For more information, read the Lockheed Martin or the Department of War F-35 historic 10-year agreement press releases.

For media inquiries, please contact Aidan.heard1@mail.house.gov.
