title: Crow Talks Future of Foreign Policy with Young Leaders at University of Chicago
text:
CHICAGO — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, visited the University of Chicago Institute of Politics to outline his vision for a foreign policy that is rooted in working class values and representative of all Americans.

In his remarks, Crow called trust in the country’s foreign policy infrastructure “deeply broken,” having left working class communities behind. He discussed the importance of recruiting a new generation of leaders from different backgrounds and highlighted his work towards building a foreign policy that reflects the needs of working class Americans.

“Trust is deeply broken between Americans and our national security and foreign policy infrastructure,” Crow said. “People don’t believe it serves them, and they’re not wrong… The first step is to make it really clear that the point of our national security and foreign policy is pretty simple: it’s to protect Americans and to make people’s lives better—to reduce costs and support the middle class. That is the point.”

“There are 200 million Americans that live in so-called fly-over country. They can’t access that system. They can’t break into the pipeline of our elite institutions. And our institutions don’t reflect them, are out of touch with them, and don’t really understand where America is at. We’ve got to break that system and tap into the full talent and experience of the American people,” Crow concluded.

Facilitating the discussion was Rear Admiral John Kirby, the former spokesperson for the Department of Defense.

Congressman Crow continues to lay out his affirmative vision for Colorado and the country, including with speeches on the Future of American Foreign Policy at the Center for American Progress, the Munich Security Conference, and Foreign Policy for America’s Leadership Summit. He’s also fighting to build a future that brings Americans together, protects our democracy, and ensures leaders are accountable to working class Americans, outlining his vision for a New American Patriotism at Harvard University’s JFK Jr. Forum in conversation with Heather Cox Richardson and the McCain Institute's Sedona Forum.

title: Davids, Kansas Farm Leaders Discuss Protecting North American Trade, Fighting Tariffs, Supporting Rural Communities
text:
OLATHE, KS — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined Kansas farmers, agribusiness leaders, and the Kansas Farm Bureau for a roundtable discussion on the future of agricultural trade with Canada and Mexico. New data released at the event highlights just how much Kansas farmers depend on these North American markets and why trade certainty is critical for rural communities.

Originally, Davids voted alongside both Democrats and Republicans to pass the Trump-negotiated United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) when it was first negotiated. However, because the Trump Administration refused a full 16-year extension this year, farmers are now stuck in an endless cycle of annual negotiations, making it difficult to plan ahead, invest in equipment, or grow their businesses.

“Our farmers and producers need long-term stability — not the economic chaos we’re seeing after President Trump refused to renew the USMCA this year,” said Davids. “Canada and Mexico buy billions of dollars in Kansas crops and meat products every year. I was proud to vote to pass the original USMCA negotiated by President Trump because it supports thousands of local jobs. As we work through the agreement’s review, my focus is on protecting our farmers, keeping our markets open, and pushing back against reckless tariff policies that raise costs for families and threaten our rural communities.”

Since USMCA was enacted in 2020, Mexico and Canada have collectively scaled up imports of U.S. agricultural goods by $20 billion, totaling $60 billion in 2024. Economic models show that in 2024 alone, agricultural and seafood exports to Canada and Mexico generated $149 billion in total economic contribution to the U.S. economy, supporting nearly half a million American jobs and generating $36 billion in wages.

New data unveiled at the roundtable by Farmers for Free Trade underscores the massive role international trade plays in Kansas:

$3.0 Billion in Exports: In 2025, Kansas exported $3.0 billion worth of agricultural products to Mexico and Canada.

14,600 Local Jobs: Trade with our northern and southern neighbors directly supports 14,600 agricultural jobs across Kansas.

Top Export Markets: Mexico and Canada remain the largest buyers of Kansas goods, including top markets like meat products ($826 million), corn ($814 million), wheat ($355 million), grain and oilseed milling products ($263 million), and soybean farming ($200 million).

During the discussion, leaders talked about how trade uncertainty and broad tariffs are hurting local agribusinesses. Kansas lost 700 farms in 2025 alone, highlighting the real consequences of chaotic economic policies. Unstable tariff policies have driven up costs for families — with average American households paying roughly $2,500 more this year — while small businesses across the state face higher prices for goods and equipment.

Davids has consistently pushed back on blanket tariffs and supported bipartisan approaches to trade that protect consumers and keep American producers competitive. She previously spoke during a U.S. House Agriculture Committee hearing on the trade disruptions Kansas farmers face — a concern echoed by former Kansas Farm Bureau President Joe Newland. She also voted to end broad tariffs on Canada that drive up costs for families.

title: Dingell, Colleagues Express Concerns to CMS Regarding Complex Rehabilitation Technology Coverage
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), and colleagues expressed concerns about significant gaps in Medicare’s coverage and reimbursement framework for complex rehabilitation technology (CRT) — including customized power wheelchair systems — for beneficiaries living with serious physical and functional disabilities.

“Under current rules governing Medicare’s Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) benefit for CRT equipment, a component part must have already failed or malfunctioned before Medicare will cover any servicing of the equipment — meaning that routine, scheduled maintenance designed to prevent failure is categorically excluded from reimbursement. This framework is counterproductive in two respects. First, it drives avoidable equipment failures: problems that could be identified and corrected through routine maintenance instead go unaddressed until they become acute. Second, it undermines beneficiaries’ ability to plan,” said the lawmakers.

The lawmakers continued: “A second, related problem concerns the fact that Medicare’s coverage of repairs to customized power CRT equipment is conditioned on the beneficiary having a valid prescription on file dated within the prior twelve months. For beneficiaries who depend on power wheelchairs and similar equipment, this requirement creates an unnecessary and potentially harmful administrative obstacle.”

In a letter to CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the lawmakers highlighted CMS’s responsibility to the tens of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries each year who depend on complex rehabilitation technology to maintain their mobility and independence. The lawmakers encouraged prioritizing these reforms and maintaining an open discussion between offices.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Administrator Oz:

We write to raise concerns about significant gaps in Medicare’s coverage and reimbursement framework for complex rehabilitation technology (CRT) — including customized power wheelchair systems — for beneficiaries living with serious physical and functional disabilities. Two issues in particular warrant the agency’s attention: an outdated prescription renewal requirement that creates unnecessary administrative barriers to equipment repairs, and the absence of coverage for preventative maintenance on life-sustaining equipment. We urge the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to address both through regulatory action.

Lack of Coverage for Preventative Maintenance

Under current rules governing Medicare’s Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) benefit for CRT equipment, a component part must have already failed or malfunctioned before Medicare will cover any servicing of the equipment — meaning that routine, scheduled maintenance designed to prevent failure is categorically excluded from reimbursement. This framework is counterproductive in two respects. First, it drives avoidable equipment failures: problems that could be identified and corrected through routine maintenance instead go unaddressed until they become acute. Second, it undermines beneficiaries’ ability to plan.

Scheduled maintenance is predictable and can be arranged around a beneficiary’s care needs and daily life. Waiting for damage to occur makes servicing logistically unpredictable for individuals who rely on this equipment for mobility and independence.

CMS has the regulatory authority to modernize this framework, and we urge the agency to provide flexibility to allow for coverage of preventative maintenance on CRT systems. Doing so would reduce equipment failures and improve quality of life for beneficiaries.

Prescription Renewal Requirement for CRT Repairs

A second, related problem concerns the fact that Medicare’s coverage of repairs to customized power CRT equipment is conditioned on the beneficiary having a valid prescription on file dated within the prior twelve months. For beneficiaries who depend on power wheelchairs and similar equipment, this requirement creates an unnecessary and potentially harmful administrative obstacle.

By their nature, Medicare beneficiaries who qualify for customized power CRT equipment have severe, permanent medical conditions — such as spinal cord injury or cerebral palsy — for which the need for the equipment will not change over time. Requiring a prescription renewal as a precondition for repair coverage adds little clinical value for this population, and yet it can delay access to critical service when a component fails. Such delays carry real consequences for beneficiary health, function, and independence.

Importantly, the Social Security Act does not expressly mandate a twelve-month prescription renewal as a condition of repair coverage eligibility. We believe that CMS has regulatory authority to waive or modify this requirement. We urge the agency to do so without delay.

Conclusion

Each year, tens of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries depend on CRT systems and equipment to maintain their mobility and independence. Removing the prescription renewal barrier and providing coverage for preventative maintenance of CR equipment are targeted, achievable steps that would meaningfully improve care for this vulnerable population. We encourage CMS to prioritize both reforms and welcome the opportunity to discuss them further.

title: Dingell Introduces National Foster Care Improvement Legislation in Honor of Samier Amer
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) introduced the Samier Amer Foster Care Improvement Act, legislation that would require state foster care programs to ensure children are prioritized for placement with their relatives and put additional requirements in place for a fairer decision-making process when an agency places a child.

“The well-being and safety of children must be a top priority across the board, but especially when a child in foster care is being matched with a family,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “Whenever possible, we must keep families together and ensure children are placed into a safe and nurturing environment with relatives they know and love. Michigan now has the laws that make this possible, but only after the Amer family lost their children to the state’s foster care system. This bill would ensure the federal government follows Michigan’s example so future children or families don’t have to go through this painful experience.”

The Samier Amer Foster Care Improvement Act would require that states provide notice of decision to the child’s parents, relatives, or other legal guardian within 90 days of a placement decision. Additionally, the legislation would require states to establish procedures that would allow any of the parties who receive notice of the placement decision to request, within five days after receipt of the notice, documentation of the reasons for the state’s decision. It would also allow the child’s attorney to petition the court to review the decision and require that the court commence a review within seven days after receipt of the petition.

In 1985, Rehab and Ahmed Amer lost two of their children to Michigan’s foster care system after the accidental death of their son, Samier. Although cleared of any wrongdoing, the State refused to return the Amers’ children to their custody or allow a relative to care for the children. When Rehab’s brother petitioned to be a foster parent to the Amers’ children, he was denied even though he had previously served as a foster parent for other children. Since then, the Amer family has advocated tirelessly for improving foster care policies for all children.

title: Reps. Dexter, Grijalva, and Ansari Join Reproductive Freedom for All to Advocate for Pregnant Women in Immigration Detention
text:
ELOY, AZ — Yesterday, on Wednesday, October 21, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter (OR-03), joined Representatives Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) alongside Reproductive Freedom for All President Mini Timmaraju, for an oversight visit to the Eloy Detention Center to hear directly from women about their reproductive health experiences in immigration detention. Multiple pregnant women have previously been held at Eloy, including one who miscarried. This is a departure from the policies of previous administrations that typically did not hold pregnant people in detention.

The visit focused on the urgent need to protect reproductive health, ensure access to adequate medical care, and uphold the dignity of women in immigration detention. During the visit, the lawmakers heard from women about their experiences navigating pregnancy and accessing essential reproductive health supplies while detained. The lawmakers met with two women:

Maria Alejandra Valero Brinez, a 24-year-old Venezuelan woman and mother of a six-year-old son. She has valid employment authorization until 2029, a pending asylum petition, and no criminal convictions. She was living in Mesa, Arizona before she was detained in August. She is approximately five months pregnant and described serious concerns about her pregnancy and access to adequate medical care while detained. She has experienced spotting and reported that she has to throw herself on the ground and plead for attention in order to receive medical care. When she was able to receive care, the doctors informed her she has a low-lying placenta — the same condition that led to a stillborn birth three years earlier. Despite having a high-risk pregnancy, she said she has not been able to receive images from ultrasounds or other information about her and her baby’s condition. Maria fears for their safety and well-being, especially given the lack of information about her pregnancy. She is also afraid to express any emotion about her current condition, as detainees are often placed into solitary confinement if they show any signs of emotional distress.

Maria also raised concerns about access to drinking water and food inside the facility. Despite clear doctor’s recommendations to receive double food portions, Maria reports that one guard routinely dismisses this and only gives her the standard single portion. Maria also reported that she was not given antibiotics following a dental abscess that led to a tooth extraction. Untreated bacterial infections have the potential to cause miscarriages. Earlier this year, Emmanuel Damas passed away due to complications from an untreated tooth infection after being held at the Florence Detention Center.

Lilianne (who only wishes to use her first name), a Cuban woman detained at Eloy, described difficulties obtaining sufficient menstrual hygiene products. She reported inconsistent access, with the number of products provided varying depending on the detention officer, raising concerns about the availability of basic necessities for women in custody.

“Maria is desperate to protect the health and safety of her baby. The federal government, by blatantly ignoring medical guidelines and advice, is putting her and her baby’s life at risk,” said Representative Dexter, who is one of six Democratic doctors in Congress. “She must be released immediately. DHS is refusing basic human and civil rights to the people in these despicable facilities and shows zero concern for the lives of people in them. Pregnant women and children do not belong in ICE detention. I will continue to use my experience as a physician, a mother, and my power as a member of Congress to protect women and children in this country.”

“Maria and Lilianne’s stories show the deliberate cruelty at the heart of the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda. Their treatment is not just inhumane — it is a disgraceful failure of the government's legal duty to protect the people in its custody,” said Rep. Grijalva. “While private contractors rake in billions of taxpayer dollars, they are denying the most vulnerable individuals – including pregnant people – their most basic necessities, including medical care, clean drinking water, and adequate food. These corporations are profiting off human suffering, and the Trump Administration is footing the bill with our tax dollars. Maria, as well as all pregnant people in detention, deserve dignity, proper medical care, and immediate release.”

“The inhumane conditions inside Eloy Detention Center are unconscionable. Maria, a high-risk pregnant woman, is being denied critical medical care and adequate food. My constituent, Lilianne, the wife of a U.S. citizen, was detained at her green card appointment and is now being denied basic feminine hygiene products. No one should be treated this way,” said Rep. Ansari. “All the while, the Trump Administration is pouring billions into ICE as private prison corporations like CoreCivic and GEO Group profit from detention. The level of cruelty and corruption is abundantly clear. This is a profound failure of human dignity, and we will hold this Administration accountable.”

“ICE is putting women’s health, pregnancies, and lives at risk—leaving them to plead for even the most basic care and access to menstrual products,” said Mini Timmaraju, President and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All. “I’m grateful to Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter for shining light on this crisis, and Reproductive Freedom for All is with them every step of the way in demanding an end to this cruelty.”

title: Elfreth Appointed to Co-Chair New Maryland Maritime Task Force
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, was appointed by Governor Wes Moore to co-chair the newly established Maryland Maritime Task Force alongside Maryland Department of Commerce Secretary Harry Coker, Jr.

“It’s time for Maryland to lead our country’s maritime industry once again. Maryland is uniquely positioned with the location, infrastructure, industrial base, and workforce demand to become a leader today. We will be taking inspiration from what once was – back to the Baltimore clippers and the hundreds of Liberty ships built during World War II – to build a bright and successful future for Maryland's maritime industry,” said Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. “I have spent my first two years in Congress and on the Armed Services Committee fighting to bring back shipbuilding, invest in Coast Guard Yard Baltimore, and redevelop Curtis Creek. I want to thank Governor Moore for his leadership in convening the Maryland Maritime Task Force to expand on this work and steer the future of the Port of Baltimore and our maritime industry at this critical juncture.”

“Maryland’s infrastructure is perfectly suited to lead the nation's maritime industry, from building in-demand ships to creating positions for welders, mechanics, and engineers,” said Governor Moore. “This task force will help us capitalize on future opportunities to make our state’s economy more competitive through maritime projects that build more pathways to work, wages and wealth for Marylanders.”

“Maryland’s maritime heritage is woven into America’s story—from Kent County’s Captain Lambert Wickes who carried Benjamin Franklin to France, to Frederick Douglass who worked in Baltimore’s shipyards while enslaved, to generations of leaders educated at the United States Naval Academy,” said Maryland Department of Commerce Secretary Harry Coker, Jr. “This task force will build on that enduring maritime tradition to attract investment, advance innovation, and expand pathways into skilled, well-paying careers while strengthening our economy and our nation’s security.”

By way of executive order, Governor Moore created the Maryland Maritime Task Force to identify and pursue national and international maritime-related federal and commercial growth opportunities. The task force will help foster quick, strategic coordination among Maryland state agencies and local businesses to achieve maritime success and economic development across the state.

The task force will focus on several items including:

Completing the necessary actions to secure a Maritime Prosperity Zone designation for the state once Congress acts to create the program;

Working with stakeholders to develop a plan of action to advance and diversify the state’s maritime economy;

Identifying barriers encountered by public or private entities in pursuing national maritime opportunities and recommend legislative and regulatory actions to help overcome;

Coordinating and strengthening state and federal advocacy efforts, including international engagement, workforce training opportunities, grant programs, and more; and

Making recommendations for state business incentives, tax credits, and other economic development tools that can help expand and support Maryland’s maritime industries.

Other task force members include representatives from the Maryland Department of Commerce, Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Military Department, and Maryland Economic Development Corporation; up to five government officials with expertise or interest in the state’s maritime economy; the Port of Baltimore or the Port of Baltimore Alliance; the Maritime Technology Alliance; the Baltimore or Chesapeake Bay maritime industries; a maritime research entity; a maritime training program; and a labor union or trade association.

Additional collaborative partners may include the United States Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division; United States Coast Guard, Curtis Bay command; United States Naval Academy; United States Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District; and other subject matter experts to assist in developing strategies and identifying opportunities.

“The Port of Baltimore is one of the economic engines of Maryland and the heart of our maritime economy – and we need to ensure we maximize the benefits of this unique asset,” said Maryland Department of Transportation Secretary Katie Thomson. “In 2025, the Port of Baltimore handled the most containers ever, the most ship calls ever and more farm and construction machinery and forest products than any other U.S. port. We were proud that the Port began handling double-stacked containers on rail earlier this year following the completion of the $495 million Howard Street Tunnel Project; the new capacity will exponentially grow the Port’s business and create thousands of new jobs. We fully support Governor Moore’s effort to double-down on the growth of the Port and our entire maritime economy.”

“Every year, Maryland’s boating and fishing industries generate more than $700 million in added value to the state’s economy and represent the largest sector of the state’s approximately $10 billion outdoor recreation economy,” said Department of Natural Resources Secretary Josh Kurtz. “These industries draw tourists from around the world who discover the wonderful experiences our residents get to frequently enjoy on the beautiful Chesapeake Bay and the tidal rivers that connect our scenic landscapes. We look forward to working with our partners throughout the state to expand the state’s vibrant maritime economy through the development of Maritime Enterprise Zones.”

Maryland is uniquely positioned to contribute to the nation’s security, while advancing federal priorities that will strengthen the United States’ maritime capabilities. The federal framework for America’s Maritime Action Plan presents potential for Maritime Prosperity Zone designation in Maryland, an emerging opportunity for increased economic growth.

Maryland’s maritime industries contribute more than $10.2 billion annually to the state’s economy and support 115,000 jobs. The sector comprises marine transportation, shipbuilding and repair, national defense and security, world-class research on autonomous crafts, shipping and logistics, and tourism and recreation. The most recent addition to Maryland’s Maritime economy includes a $3.7 billion investment by Anduril Industries, which is locating its Arsenal-2 project – a 2 million square-foot software-defined shipyard – in Baltimore County, to expand America's submarine industrial base and support upwards of 14,000 jobs.

Maryland owes its maritime leadership to assets including the Port of Baltimore, and numerous private businesses, federal entities, and educational and workforce training institutions like the Seafarers Harry Lundeberg School of Seamanship in St. Mary’s County and the Maritime Institute of Technology and Graduate Studies (MITAGS) in Anne Arundel County. In Montgomery County, more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, and technicians work at the Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division – the U.S. Navy's primary center of excellence, research, development, and test facility for ships and ship systems. In Baltimore, the United States Coast Guard is planning a $1.5 billion investment to improve its Curtis Bay Yard to continue performing critical national security services on cutter vessels.

title: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher’s Bill To Expand Texans’ Access to Emergency Alerts Signed Into Law
text:
Legislation comes after July 4, 2025, Hill Country floods that killed more than 130 people

Today, the President signed a bill led by Congresswoman Fletcher with Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11), Congressman Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01), the Mystic Alerts Act, H.R. 7022. The Mystic Alerts Act improves Americans’ access to wireless emergency alerts by requiring the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to encourage mobile service providers to adopt satellite alerting capabilities—technology that allows more people to receive life-saving alerts even if they lack cellular service. The bipartisan effort follows the devastating floods in Central Texas last summer and seeks to address communication gaps to prepare communities.

“In Houston and across the state of Texas, we are still heartbroken and grieving the loss of beloved family members and the destruction of communities along the Guadalupe River in the summer of 2025, a disaster made worse by communication gaps and failures,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “This new law is a small but important way to provide a meaningful response to the devastating floods and to learn from the tragedy so that communities across the country do not have to experience the same pain and loss that Texans did last year. Nothing can bring back those that we lost in the flood, but we owe it to their survivors and to everyone we represent to do all we can to try to prevent another tragedy like it. I am thankful for Congressman Pfluger, Congressman Veasey, and Congressman Carter’s partnership in this effort and am thrilled to see this bill become law.”

Congresswoman Fletcher joined Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11), Congressman Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01) in introducing this legislation. Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) and Senator Jon Ossoff (D-GA) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate.

title: Rep. Gillen Introduces Bipartisan Bill with Local Mayors and Advocates to Fund PFAS Cleanup and Reduce Water Utility Costs for Long Islanders
text:
A video of the full bill announcement is available HERE.

ROCKVILLE CENTRE, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) held a press conference with local Long Island mayors and clean water advocates to announce her bipartisan Protect Clean Water Act. Introduced alongside Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-08), the legislation will help communities fund the removal of toxic per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), “forever chemicals,” and emerging contaminants from their water supply while relieving the financial burden on local ratepayers.

"For too long, Long Islanders have faced toxic cancer-causing PFAS contamination in our water while shouldering the high cost to make it safe,” said Rep. Gillen. “I am proud to introduce the bipartisan Protect Clean Water Act alongside local mayors and clean water advocates in the fight to secure clean, safe water for Nassau County. This bill will authorize federal funding that our communities need to protect our water supply for the future without driving up costs for working families.”

“Every family deserves access to clean, safe drinking water, regardless of where they live,” said Rep. Fitzpatrick. “Across Pennsylvania and the country, PFAS and other emerging contaminants threaten our water supplies and put communities at risk. I’ve spent years fighting to clean up contaminated sites, hold polluters accountable, and protect the health of communities. This bill ensures states have the dedicated funding they need to address these threats, remove harmful contaminants from drinking water, and protect our waterways for generations to come.”

“I want to thank Congresswoman Gillen for her continued partnership and her commitment to addressing the critical infrastructure needs of communities across the region,” said Rockville Centre Mayor Francis Murray. “Providing safe, reliable drinking water is one of the most important responsibilities we have as local government officials. Congresswoman Gillen’s bipartisan legislation to provide $10 billion over five years in federal funding for water contaminant remediation, including PFAS, represents an important step toward helping communities address emerging contaminants and make necessary investments to protect their water supplies.”

“I want to thank Congresswoman Gillen for addressing the contamination of our domestic water here on Long Island, especially in the Village of Freeport,” said Freeport Village Mayor Robert Kennedy. “I support Congresswoman Gillen’s foresight and initiative to protect our children and grandchildren from contaminated water here on Long Island and in Freeport.”

“Clean, safe drinking water is not a luxury but a necessity that every family deserves,” said Hempstead Village Mayor Waylyn Hobbs, Jr. “I commend Congresswoman Laura Gillen for her leadership and continued partnership with our office in protecting our drinking water while easing the financial burden on our residents. Here in the Village of Hempstead, we understand that every dollar matters, and this legislation is an important step toward ensuring safe, affordable drinking water for generations to come.”

”Thank you, Congresswoman Gillen and your talented team for your passionate support of the bipartisan Protect Clean Water Act,” said Garden City Mayor Edward Finneran. “The Mayor’s office and residents of Garden City have been zeroed in on clean and safe water for years. It seems to me that water issues, although crucial to our general quality of life, can sometimes be back-burnered in this busy world of ours. However, Rep. Gillen’s emphasis and hard work on the bill are a testament to her commitment that all families, especially young children in both her district and beyond, are provided with clean and safe water.”

In 2021, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) provided $5 billion to help communities remove PFAS and other emerging contaminants from their water systems. However, that funding expired at the end of fiscal year 2026.

The Protect Clean Water Act would authorize $10 billion in funding dedicated for PFAS and emerging contaminant remediation over five years through the Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds, giving communities critical federal support to invest in treatment technology and upgrade water infrastructure.

Removing PFAS is essential to protecting public health, though costly, as exposure to the chemical is linked to high cholesterol, birth defects and an increased risk of kidney and testicular cancers.

The American Water Works Association estimates that drinking water treatment investments alone could cost $2.7 billion to $3.5 billion annually. Local governments and water utilities will need to continue to increase their investment to make sure our water is free of PFAS. The Protect Clean Water Act would help communities address PFAS contamination while keeping water affordable for ratepayers.

“Toxic forever chemicals are pervasive in our water supply on Long Island and across the nation and must be removed in order to protect public health,” said Adrienne Esposito, Executive Director for Citizens Campaign for the Environment (CCE). “However, the high cost of installing treatment technology can cripple local budgets and raise costs for residents. This legislation provides much-needed increased federal funding that will allow communities to upgrade their water infrastructure, helping to provide clean and affordable drinking water to local residents. It is imperative that our drinking water is clean and affordable for all consumers. This bill achieves both essential goals. CCE commends Representative Gillen for her leadership in fighting to protect clean drinking water on Long Island and across the nation.”

"The Clean Water Construction Coalition applauds Representatives Gillen and Fitzpatrick for their bipartisan leadership in sustaining federal investment to help communities address PFAS and other emerging contaminants,” said Kyle England, Chair, Clean Water Construction Coalition. “The State Revolving Funds are proven, effective tools for delivering critical drinking water and wastewater infrastructure projects, while also prioritizing water affordability. Continued federal support will protect public health, strengthen local economies, and give communities the resources they need to meet these growing challenges.”

“The Association of Metropolitan Water Agencies is proud to support the Protect Clean Water Act,” said Dan Hartnett, Interim CEO, Association of Metropolitan Water Agencies. This legislation would provide public water systems with much-needed funding through the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund to address emerging contaminants, like PFAS. As public water systems face billions of dollars in costs annually to filter PFAS from our drinking water, more federal assistance will be crucial to ensure they have the resources to comply with EPA regulations and protect public health. AMWA thanks Representative Gillen for introducing this legislation and ensuring that public water systems can continue to provide the highest quality drinking water to their communities.”

“Clean water utilities are on the front lines of protecting public health and the environment, but as utilities work to address emerging contaminants like PFAS, the rising costs of advanced wastewater treatment and the current lack of scalable, affordable technologies to destroy PFAS will place real financial strain on public utilities, and by extension their local communities and ratepayers,” said Adam Krantz, CEO of the National Association of Clean Water Agencies (NACWA). “NACWA applauds Representatives Laura Gillen and Brian Fitzpatrick for their effort to ensure federal funding to help utilities address the public health concerns related to PFAS and other emerging contaminants.”

"Water reuse technologies can help communities control and remediate harmful substances like PFAS, but keeping our communities safe requires federal investment," said Bruno Pigott, executive director of the WateReuse Association. "WateReuse Association commends Representatives Gillen and Fitzpatrick for introducing legislation that will protect public health, create jobs, and invest in critical infrastructure."

The legislation is endorsed by the Clean Water Construction Coalition, the Association of Metropolitan Water Agencies, the National Association of Clean Water Agencies (NACWA), the WateReuse Association and Citizens Campaign for the Environment.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Reintroduces Bipartisan CARS Act to Combat Organized Auto Theft
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Thursday, October 22, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) reintroduced the bipartisan Combatting Auto Robbery at the Source, or CARS Act, to re-establish a National Auto Theft Bureau (NATB). The bill is co-led by Representative Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11).

“Auto theft isn’t just a property crime. It’s often run by organized rings that move stolen cars across state lines and out through our ports, and it puts families at risk, including in carjackings. Our law enforcement is doing everything it can, but they need a national clearinghouse to connect the dots in real time. The CARS Act will give them the intelligence, training, and resources to stop these criminals. To our law enforcement and the victims of auto theft here in Jersey, know that I stand with you,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).

“In recent years, we have seen an increase in car thefts across the tristate area, making New Yorkers feel less safe and negatively impacting their quality of life. License plate scanners I allocated funding for have helped identify and recover stolen vehicles. However, once these vehicles leave the city, it becomes harder,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11).“We know that many end up on ships at New Jersey ports and then are sold in other countries. By creating a national anti-auto theft bureau and strengthening coordination at all levels, law enforcement can better combat auto theft across the tristate area.”

The NATB would facilitate increased information sharing and collaboration between local, state, and federal law enforcement to better combat sophisticated, multistate and multinational auto theft rings. Gottheimer first introduced the CARS Act in April 2024 after touring the New Jersey State Police Real Time Crime Center, a state-of-the-art facility that unites the flow of information among state, county, and local law enforcement by distributing information on auto thefts and crime in real time.

In New Jersey, more than 1300 cars were stolen in 2025. Gottheimer’s Bipartisan CARS Act will:

Reinstate the National Auto Theft Bureau as a national clearinghouse for auto theft data. This will help our local, state, and federal law enforcement share information in real time.

Provide training, resources, and recommendations to private industry, the public, and law enforcement agencies on how to combat auto theft, including but not limited to specific designs that make a car more vulnerable to theft and online trends regarding auto theft.

Deliver grants to law enforcement agencies around the country to improve information sharing and implement best practices that have already been proven to mitigate car theft.

Gottheimer has long worked to fully equip law enforcement and crack down on auto theft. In April 2023, heconvened a roundtable with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Port Newark leadership, and state and local law enforcement on collaborative efforts to combat the surge in auto theft and carjacking. He previously held aroundtable with local law enforcement on the broader increase in burglaries and thefts. In 2022, hedemanded that DHS step up enforcement against interstate and international carjacking and auto theft, which has resulted in new federal, state, and local operations to recover stolen vehicles.

title: STATEMENT: Gottheimer Statement on Widespread Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Thursday, October 22, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) released the following statement:

“Artificial intelligence just uncovered critical flaws in PHP, the code behind roughly seventy percent of the world’s websites. Governments around the world, along with countless businesses, have pulled sites offline until patches are in place. Thankfully, researchers found these vulnerabilities and worked with developers on a fix before they were made public.

This is exactly what AI should be doing: helping us find and fix weaknesses before bad actors can exploit them. But we can’t let our guard down. The same speed that helps defenders find these flaws can help hackers and hostile foreign adversaries exploit them, and reports that attackers are already doing so show just how narrow that window is. I urge every business, school, and local government in North Jersey to patch their systems now.

That’s why we need clear guardrails, including mandatory pre-deployment testing of the most powerful AI models, so these tools strengthen our defenses rather than threaten our critical infrastructure, our economy, or our national security.”

title: Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter Join Reproductive Freedom for All to Advocate for Pregnant Women in Immigration Detention
text:
ELOY, AZ — Yesterday, on Wednesday, October 21, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Maxine Dexter (OR-03), alongside Reproductive Freedom for All President Mini Timmaraju, for an oversight visit to the Eloy Detention Center to hear directly from women about their reproductive health experiences in immigration detention. Multiple pregnant women have previously been held at Eloy, including one who miscarried. This is a departure from the policies of previous administrations that typically did not hold pregnant people in detention.

The visit focused on the urgent need to protect reproductive health, ensure access to adequate medical care, and uphold the dignity of women in immigration detention. During the visit, the lawmakers heard from women about their experiences navigating pregnancy and accessing essential reproductive health supplies while detained. The lawmakers met with two women:

Maria Alejandra Valero Brinez, a 24-year-old Venezuelan woman and mother of a six-year-old son. She has valid employment authorization until 2029, a pending asylum petition, and no criminal convictions. She was living in Mesa, Arizona before she was detained in August. She is approximately five months pregnant, and described serious concerns about her pregnancy and access to adequate medical care while detained. She has experienced spotting and reported that she has to throw herself on the ground and plead for attention in order to receive medical care. When she was able to receive care, the doctors informed her she has a low-lying placenta — the same condition that led to a stillborn birth three years earlier. Despite having a high-risk pregnancy, she said she has not been able to receive images from ultrasounds or other information about her and her baby’s condition. Maria fears for their safety and well-being, especially given the lack of information about her pregnancy. She is also afraid to express any emotion about her current condition, as detainees are often placed into solitary confinement if they show any signs of emotional distress.

Maria also raised concerns about access to drinking water and food inside the facility. Despite clear doctor’s recommendations to receive double food portions, Maria reports that one guard routinely dismisses this and only gives her the standard single portion. Rep. Grijalva also previously raised the alarm about the lack of access to clean drinking water at Eloy where detainees often have to wait for ice to melt in an igloo cooler that they have complained is not clean. Maria also reported that she was not given antibiotics following a dental abscess that led to a tooth extraction. Untreated bacterial infections have the potential to cause miscarriages. Earlier this year, Emmanuel Damas passed away due to complications from an untreated tooth infection after being held at the Florence Detention Center.

Lilianne (who only wishes to use her first name), a Cuban woman detained at Eloy, described difficulties obtaining sufficient menstrual hygiene products. She reported inconsistent access, with the number of products provided varying depending on the detention officer, raising concerns about the availability of basic necessities for women in custody.

“Maria and Lilianne’s stories show the deliberate cruelty at the heart of the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda. Their treatment is not just inhumane — it is a disgraceful failure of the government's legal duty to protect the people in its custody,” said Rep. Grijalva. “While private contractors rake in billions of taxpayer dollars, they are denying the most vulnerable individuals – including pregnant people – their most basic necessities, including medical care, clean drinking water, and adequate food. These corporations are profiting off human suffering, and the Trump Administration is footing the bill with our tax dollars. Maria, as well as all pregnant people in detention, deserve dignity, proper medical care, and immediate release.”

“The inhumane conditions inside Eloy Detention Center are unconscionable. Maria, a high-risk pregnant woman, is being denied critical medical care and adequate food. My constituent, Lilianne, the wife of a U.S. citizen, was detained at her green card appointment and is now being denied basic feminine hygiene products. No one should be treated this way,” said Rep. Ansari. “All the while, the Trump Administration is pouring billions into ICE as private prison corporations like CoreCivic and GEO Group profit from detention. The level of cruelty and corruption is abundantly clear. This is a profound failure of human dignity, and we will hold this Administration accountable.”

“Maria is desperate to protect the health and safety of her baby. The federal government, by blatantly ignoring medical guidelines and advice, is putting her and her baby’s life at risk,” said Representative Dexter, who is one of six Democratic doctors in Congress. “She must be released immediately. DHS is refusing basic human and civil rights to the people in these despicable facilities and shows zero concern for the lives of people in them. Pregnant women and children do not belong in ICE detention. I will continue to use my experience as a physician, a mother, and my power as a member of Congress to protect women and children in this country.”

“ICE is putting women’s health, pregnancies, and lives at risk—leaving them to plead for even the most basic care and access to menstrual products,” said Mini Timmaraju, President and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All. “I’m grateful to Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter for shining light on this crisis, and Reproductive Freedom for All is with them every step of the way in demanding an end to this cruelty.”

This visit was Representative Grijalva’s sixth oversight visit since being sworn into office in November of 2025. Her first visit was also to Eloy, where she successfully advocated for the release of Julia “La abuela” Benitez – a 79-year-old Cuban asylum seeker escaping political persecution that had been detained in Eloy for nine months and suffers from dementia.

title: Congressman Hamadeh Encourages Students to Compete and Be Recognized Through Art, Science, Civics, and Physical Fitness Opportunities
text:
Washington, D.C. - With important deadlines fast approaching, Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) is encouraging students across Arizona’s 8th Congressional District to take advantage of several opportunities to showcase their talents, demonstrate academic excellence, and earn congressional recognition.

From computer science and fine arts to military service, civic achievement, and physical fitness, Congressman Hamadeh is offering students multiple opportunities to challenge themselves, compete with their peers, and receive recognition for their accomplishments.

2026 Congressional App Challenge — Deadline: October 26

The deadline for the 2026 Congressional App Challenge is Monday, October 26, 2026, at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Last year’s winning app, Chronos, was developed by BASIS High School students Vignesh Nagarajan and Raghav Senthil Kumar. Chronos is a smart scheduling application designed to integrate multiple calendar platforms, including Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple Calendar.

The Congressional App Challenge is an initiative of the U.S. House of Representatives and is widely recognized as one of the nation’s premier student computer science competitions. Members of Congress host district-wide competitions that encourage middle and high school students to develop innovative applications.

Students may submit computer programs written in any programming language and designed for any computer-based platform.

Additional competition information and submission instructions are available through the Congressional App Challenge website.

U.S. Service Academy Nominations — Deadline: October 30

Students seeking a congressional nomination from Congressman Hamadeh to attend one of the nation's prestigious U.S. service academies must submit their completed application packages for the Class of 2031 by 3:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026.

Congressman Hamadeh looks forward to nominating exceptional student leaders, scholars, and athletes from Arizona’s 8th Congressional District to four of the nation's five service academies:

· U.S. Military Academy — West Point, New York

· U.S. Naval Academy — Annapolis, Maryland

· U.S. Air Force Academy — Colorado Springs, Colorado

· U.S. Merchant Marine Academy — Kings Point, New York

The fifth institution, the U.S. Coast Guard Academy in New London, Connecticut, does not require a congressional nomination.

Admission to a U.S. service academy is among the most competitive and prestigious educational opportunities available to graduating high school students. Cadets and midshipmen receive a world-class education, extensive leadership training, and preparation for careers of service to their country.

Most graduates incur a minimum five-year active-duty service obligation, although requirements vary by academy and program.

A congressional nomination is an essential step in the admissions process for four of the five academies, but it does not guarantee an appointment. Each academy makes its own admissions decisions based on academic achievement, leadership potential, physical fitness, character, and other qualifications.

2027 Congressional Art Competition — Students Encouraged to Prepare Now

Great art takes time. That is why Congressman Hamadeh is encouraging students to begin preparing their entries for next year's Congressional Art Competition.

Each spring, members of the U.S. House of Representatives sponsor the Artistic Discovery Contest, a nationwide competition celebrating the creativity and artistic talents of students in their congressional districts.

The competition is open to eligible students in grades 8–12 within Arizona's 8th Congressional District, including students enrolled in public, charter, private, homeschool, online, and alternative learning programs.

Emily Chen, a homeschool student, won the 2026 AZ-08 Congressional Art Competition with her artwork titled United in Dreams.

Her winning artwork earned a place in the United States Capitol, alongside artwork from students representing congressional districts throughout the country, where it could be viewed by visitors from across the nation and around the world.

Details about the 2027 competition, including submission requirements and deadlines, will be available on Congressman Hamadeh's website early next year.

In the meantime, Congressman Hamadeh encourages parents, guardians, and teachers to share this opportunity with talented young artists and help them begin preparing their entries.

Congressional District 8 Civics Initiative — No Deadline

Congressman Hamadeh's Congressional District 8 Civics Initiative is an ongoing student recognition program designed to promote civic literacy, constitutional understanding, and academic excellence among Arizona's high school students.

The Arizona Civics Test is a state-mandated requirement for high school graduation and the High School Equivalency Diploma.

High school students who earn a score of 95 or higher on the Arizona Civics Test are eligible to receive formal recognition from the Office of Congressman Abraham Hamadeh.

Participation is open to eligible students attending public, charter, private, and homeschool institutions throughout Arizona's 8th Congressional District.

There is no application deadline, allowing students to seek recognition after achieving the qualifying score.

Additional information is available on Congressman Hamadeh's official website.

Congressional District 8 Fitness Challenge — No Deadline

The Congressional District 8 Fitness Challenge is another ongoing recognition program designed to encourage physical fitness, personal discipline, and healthy lifestyles among students.

Aligned with the reestablished Presidential Physical Fitness Test, the initiative recognizes students who demonstrate achievement in key areas of physical fitness.

Participants who successfully meet the established fitness benchmarks for core strength, cardiorespiratory fitness, and upper-body strength are eligible to receive an official Certificate of Recognition from the Office of Congressman Abraham Hamadeh.

The program has no participation deadline, providing students with an ongoing opportunity to set fitness goals, improve their physical conditioning, and earn recognition for their accomplishments.

Congressman Hamadeh Celebrates the Next Generation

“Providing opportunities for the young people of Arizona's 8th Congressional District is one of the greatest joys of serving in Congress,” said Congressman Hamadeh.

“During my time in office, I have had the privilege of meeting remarkably talented, dedicated, and determined students who are eager to share their creativity, knowledge, and accomplishments with the world," stated Congressman Hamadeh. "Whether they are developing innovative technology, creating extraordinary works of art, pursuing military service, mastering the principles upon which our nation was founded, or committing themselves to healthy and disciplined lifestyles, these young Arizonans represent the very best of our future."

“I encourage every student, parent, guardian, and educator in our district to explore these opportunities. Our young people have tremendous potential, and I want to make sure they have every opportunity to succeed, achieve their goals, and receive the recognition they deserve,” concluded Congressman Hamadeh.

Students and families can learn more about these programs by visiting Congressman Hamadeh's official website at Hamadeh.House.gov.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces Legislation to Protect American Innovation and Strengthen Cyber Defenses
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10), alongside Congressman George Whitesides (CA-27), introduced the bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act, legislation to protect American innovation from foreign exploitation and strengthen cybersecurity defenses for critical infrastructure, including power grids, hospitals, and financial systems.

“Some of the greatest advances in artificial intelligence are happening right here in America, and we have a responsibility to make sure that technology is secure,” said Congressman Harrigan. “Our adversaries are already looking for ways to exploit these systems, and as AI becomes more powerful, the risks to our critical infrastructure will only grow. We need to get the companies developing this technology working directly with the people responsible for defending our power grids, hospitals, and financial systems. That's how we stay ahead of the threats and protect the Americans who depend on these systems every day.”

"AI is advancing at a breakneck pace, and every month we keep China and other adversaries from stealing our progress is a month we gain to build the safeguards this technology needs," said Congressman Whitesides. "This bill helps stop the theft of American AI models and makes sure the operators of our power grids, water systems, and other critical infrastructure are protected as AI makes cyberattacks faster, cheaper, and harder to stop. I’m proud to join Rep. Harrigan on this bipartisan effort."

The AI Cyber Defense Act directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to work with private-sector AI developers to establish voluntary standards for detecting and preventing AI distillation attacks, which can allow outside actors to extract valuable capabilities from advanced AI models. The legislation also establishes an AI Cybersecurity Roundtable bringing together technology companies and critical infrastructure operators to develop best practices for using artificial intelligence to strengthen cybersecurity defenses. Entities tied to China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba would be excluded from the eligible private-sector stakeholders involved in developing these standards.

Under the legislation, NIST would have 180 days following enactment to begin engaging industry stakeholders and establish the roundtable. The resulting voluntary standards and best practices would be made publicly available to help American businesses and critical infrastructure operators better protect their systems against emerging cyber threats.

title: Hayes, Lamont, Congressional Delegation Announce Additional Funding Reimbursement For Road and Bridge Repair Costs Related to August 2024 Storm
text:
WATERBURY – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Governor Ned Lamont, and the Connecticut Congressional Delegation announced the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) has approved another $15 million in emergency relief funding to reimburse the Connecticut Department of Transportation (CTDOT) for the costs of road and bridge repairs following the historic August 2024 rain and flooding event that impacted western Connecticut.

With this latest approval, federal emergency relief to CTDOT for this storm totals $43 million, covering most of the estimated $51 million in repair costs. It follows FHWA approval of $3 million in “quick release” funds in September 2024 and a $25 million reimbursement in October 2025. Immediately upon the impact of the storm, CTDOT began using available funds to make necessary repairs and reopen roads and bridges. These reimbursements replace that money so other CTDOT projects can proceed as planned.

Additionally, as part of FY2026, Congresswoman Hayes secured $1.5 million in Community Project Funding, to cover renovations and repairs for the Southbury Public Library following damages resulting from the August 2024 storm.

“In 2024, the Fifth District experienced extreme weather that left significant damage to critical infrastructure. Federal reimbursements like this recognize the efforts made at the state and local levels to respond quickly to emergencies and restore resources. As severe weather events become more frequent, I am actively working in Congress to improve our aging infrastructure and enhance our capacity to respond to disasters,” said Congresswoman Hayes.

“Extreme weather is putting more pressure on our infrastructure, and when historic flooding washed out roads and bridges in western Connecticut, we immediately got to work restoring those connections. This federal reimbursement helps ensure that emergency work doesn’t come at the expense of other projects. I’m thankful to our Congressional delegation and federal partners for making this happen,” said Governor Lamont.

“Emergency relief funding is what allows us to respond and then recover. This funding puts back the resources we used to get Connecticut moving again after the flooding. We appreciate our Congressional delegation, USDOT Secretary Duffy, and FHWA Administrator McMaster and his team for helping us move forward,” said Connecticut Transportation Commissioner Garrett Eucalitto.

“Traveling throughout affected areas after the storm, I saw firsthand the devastating impacts on local bridges and roads. This $15 million in federal funding will reimburse CTDOT for the swift repairs they completed following the floods. Our delegation fought hard for this funding and I’m proud we have continued to deliver relief to help our communities rebuild. As climate change creates more frequent and destructive storms, we must continue to make long-term investments in climate resilience to prevent future disasters, protect our infrastructure and keep our communities safe,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal.

“We’ve come a long way towards rebuilding western Connecticut’s infrastructure since those devastating 2024 floods, but we need to be proactive and prepare for when the next big storm hits. This federal reimbursement will keep CTDOT’s heroic emergency repair work funded while making important upgrades possible,” said Senator Chris Murphy.

“The August 2024 floods tore through our communities, washing out roads and bridges that families and businesses depend on every day. This additional $15 million, on top of the $28 million in federal funding already provided, means Connecticut can keep moving forward on our recovery. I am grateful to Governor Lamont, Commissioner Eucalitto, and CTDOT’s dedicated workforce for their tireless work to get our infrastructure back on its feet. When disaster strikes, no state should have to rebuild alone. As ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee, I will keep fighting to make sure federal help is there when our state needs it,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03).

“I’m thrilled the federal government is supporting Connecticut’s recovery after severe flooding wreaked havoc on infrastructure throughout the southwest of the state. With storms growing more severe due to climate change, it’s vital the federal-state disaster recovery partnership remains strong. Connecticut’s Congressional delegation stands united in working to deliver the resources our constituents need when crisis strikes,” said Congressman Jim Himes (CT-04).

Three bridges in Oxford and Southbury are currently in design for a future construction project, with those costs also eligible for emergency relief funds.

title: ICYMI: $3M grant from Hinson's office will upgrade county radios
text:
Hardin County has received a $3,054,209 public safety grant from Congresswoman Ashley Hinson’s office, which will be used to transition all 16 county public safety entities to the Iowa Statewide Interoperability Communication System (ISICS).

“This project represents a significant investment in the safety of our first responders and the citizens that we serve,” Hardin County Emergency Management Director McKenzie Burton said.

“Our current radio system has created communication barriers that often leave Hardin County isolated from surrounding counties, state agencies, and other public safety partners when we need to communicate beyond our county lines,” Burton continued. “During an emergency, reliable communication is not a luxury; it’s a necessity. Every second matters, and responders must be able to communicate clearly and coordinate resources and request assistance when lives are on the line.

“Transitioning to ISICS will allow our law enforcement, fire departments, EMS, and other public safety partners to communicate more effectively with one another and with agencies across Iowa,” Burton added. “This improved interoperability will strengthen coordination during major incidents, support faster and more effective mutual aid, and help ensure responders have the information they need to make critical decisions safely. Ultimately, this project is not just about radios. It is about protecting the people who answer the call, improving emergency response, and providing greater protection for the residents of Hardin County and the communities we serve alongside.”

On Oct. 16, dozens of local first responders met with Hinson and Senator Chuck Grassley at a roundtable in Eldora to discuss the grant.

“I’m here, and Congresswoman Hinson is for the same reason, to thank all you folks for keeping the peace in your different levels that you’re involved in law enforcement,” Grassley said. “We thank you for that, because it’s very, very important. And I think, when we talk about putting federal resources into local law enforcement, it emphasizes that, where I’m coming from and Congresswoman Hinson’s coming from, is that we don’t believe we should be defunding the police. We believe that we should be enhancing police efforts around this country.”

“I think a lot about what this project means, and when somebody is at that point, when they’re actually dialing 911, what they’re dealing with, it’s probably one of the worst moments of their life, right?” Hinson said. “Things are going awry, something’s wrong, and the last thing they need to be thinking about is someone might not be there, or there’s a miscommunication, or there’s a problem in getting the person to show up. We want them to know that someone’s going to be there quickly.”

“From a public safety standpoint, not just law enforcement, but fire and EMS, this is a huge step forward for us,” Hardin County Sheriff Dave McDaniel said.

“We’ve been on multiple deadly force issues in the law enforcement side, where we’re a block away from state patrol or partners from other counties, we simply cannot communicate. Where we’re ducking and dodging behind cars to go relay a message to somebody a half city block away, because we cannot communicate over the radios. We’ve had situations with officer-involved shootings, where we’ve had a border county deputy within a half a mile of the scene and had no idea anything was going on. So, when I say to you, Congresswoman, that this literally is a life and death matter and will save lives, it absolutely will.”

Other first responders spoke, describing issues they’d had communicating in the past. Speaking at the roundtable were Iowa Falls Fire Chief Scott Eisentrager, Eldora Mayor Denny Barnard, Radcliffe Fire Chief Chuck Raska, Whitten Fire Chief Ben Rooker, Iowa Falls EMS Director Corey Larson, Eldora Interim EMS Director Brooke Muldoon, and Iowa State Patrol District 9 Commander Jeremy Schaffer.

title: Jayapal, Sanders Demand Answers on Meta’s Potential Interference in Brazilian Elections
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), a Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) are demanding answers from Meta Platforms, Inc. following credible reports of Meta restricting or suppressing content associated with the campaign of incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva while amplifying or recommending content associated with the campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, thereby creating starkly unequal conditions in the digital environment.

“Given the critical role social media plays in political communication, it is unacceptable for any social media platform to favor one political candidate or party over another, whether deliberately or inadvertently,” wrote the Members. “As U.S. lawmakers who support free and fair elections at home and abroad, it is our responsibility to conduct oversight to ensure that U.S. social media platforms are not influencing the outcomes of elections abroad. We urge you to take immediate action to ensure that, going forward, candidates and their campaigns in democratic elections receive equal treatment and access on your platforms.”

On September 23, the Lula campaign’s Facebook advertising account was disabled unilaterally and without explanation, just 11 days before the first round of voting on October 4. From October 9 to October 10, Meta prevented the Lula campaign from paying to boost ads published on its Instagram account for nearly 24 hours. On October 20, Meta claimed that it had “completed the implementation of measures” to comply with orders from Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court after being fined twice for noncompliance with Brazilian election law. Brazil’s second round of elections will be on October 25.

“With Brazil’s runoff elections occurring in less than a week, we call for further clarification of these ‘measures’ and urge additional action to ensure that, going forward, candidates in democratic elections at home and abroad benefit from an even playing field on Meta’s platforms,” continued the Members.

The full text of the letter can be read here.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Greg Casar (TX-35), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús G. “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01), Summer L. Lee (PA-12), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Janice D. Schakowsky (IL-09), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Nydia M. Velázquez (NY-07).

title: Congressman Keith Self Introduces Bill to Repeal Diversity Immigration Visa Lottery
text:
Congressman Keith Self (TX-03) introduced a bill to repeal the Diversity Immigrant Visa Lottery.

The Diversity Immigrant Visa Lottery program offers permanent residence to up to 55,000 applicants annually from countries with historically lower levels of immigration to the US, many of them in Africa.

A California judge ruled the U.S. State Department must reinstate the program after the Trump administration had suspended it last December after a Portuguese national who received a visa through the program was suspected of killing four people in two separate shootings in Rhode Island and Massachusetts.

“We cannot allow activist judges to dictate our immigration policy,” said Congressman Self. “The American people elected Donald Trump and this Republican Congress to put America first. That means securing our borders and ending failed immigration policies. We cannot allow liberal judges to force the administration to continue a failed immigration program.”

title: Kelly, Schneider introduce bipartisan "Brews to Barns Act" to support small breweries & local farmers, strengthen local supply chains
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Representatives Mike Kelly (R-PA), Chairman of the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax, and Brad Schneider (D-IL), a member of the Ways & Means Committee, introduced the bipartisan "Brews to Barns Act," legislation that would establish a credit against the excise tax on beer for small brewers that donate spent grain for local agricultural use.

Additional co-sponsors of the Brews to Barns Act include House Agriculture Committee Chairman Glenn "GT" Thompson (R-PA), House Small Brewers Caucus Co-Chair Marilyn Strickland (D-WA), and Representatives Jeff Hurd (R-CO), John Larson (D-CT), and Josh Riley (D-NY).

"At their cores, local breweries and farms are small businesses who play integral roles in our communities. The Brews to Barns Act incentivizes a collaborative effort between small breweries and local farmers to strengthen local supply chains. It's a win-win for everyone," said Rep. Mike Kelly (PA-16), a Co-Chair of the House Small Brewers Caucus.

"Everyone in America—from working families to Main Street businesses—is feeling the bite of rising costs. Among those hit hardest are craft beer brewers and local farmers, which is why I am glad to join my colleagues in this bipartisan effort to help lower costs and prevent waste," said Rep. Brad Schneider.

“Pennsylvania’s farmers, ranchers, and brewers already know that good ingredients shouldn’t go to waste,” said Rep. Glenn Thompson (PA-15). “Across the Commonwealth, brewers continue to create partnerships with local farmers and ranchers to put their spent grain to use in agricultural production. The Brews to Barns Act will provide key incentives to build upon that relationship, helping lower input costs for producers while supporting local small businesses.”

“This tax credit for donating spent grain will lower costs for small brewers, benefit our local farmers and ranchers, and keep spent grain out of our landfills” said Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), a Co-Chair of the House Small Brewers Caucus. “This bill is a common-sense way to lower the cost of doing business, while supporting small brewers that boost our local economies.”

WHAT THEY'RE SAYING

"When we finish brewing a batch of beer, there's still plenty of nutrients in the grain that farmers can use to feed their livestock. Donating that grain to farmers is something we're proud to do, but it also takes time and resources. Craft brewers, like family farms, are constantly balancing rising costs, so this arrangement benefits both sides," said Jason Lavery, Co-Founder, Lavery Brewing Company in Erie, Pa. "The Brews to Barns Act would provide meaningful tax relief that we could reinvest directly into our brewery, helping us support our employees, upgrade equipment, and build a stronger business while continuing to support our local farmers.”

“Small breweries have a long history of supporting their communities, and their relationships with local farmers are an important part of that. By donating spent grain for agricultural use, brewers help turn a byproduct of the brewing process into a valuable resource for farmers," said Bart Watson, President & CEO, Brewers Association. "The Brews to Barns Act recognizes the value of these longstanding partnerships and helps ensure they can continue to thrive. We appreciate Reps. Kelly and Schneider's leadership in supporting the connections between America's brewers and farmers.”

title: Bay Area Congressional Democrats Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to SFO Airport Detention Facility
text:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Yesterday, Representatives Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Jared Huffman (CA-02), and Aisha Wahab (CA-14) made an unannounced visit to inspect the detention facility being operated by Customs and Border Protection (CBP) at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). The facility has received scrutiny for some detainees being held for days, including lawful permanent residents.

“We are at SFO today to fulfill our responsibility as Members of Congress to conduct oversight and ensure that individuals in federal custody are being treated in accordance with the law,” the Members said. “There have been concerning reports of some people being detained for multiple days in a facility that was not designed for that purpose.”

The Members were granted access to the facility with no advanced notice, as federal courts have upheld the authority of Congress to inspect federal immigration detention facilities.

Rep. Mullin was the first Member of Congress to visit the facility, located in his district, in August. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) have also visited the SFO facility this month. Rep. Sam Liccardo’s (CA-16) office supported the visit, but the Congressman was unable to attend in person. In June, Reps. Lofgren and Mullin also inspected the California City Detention Center, the largest ICE facility being operated in the state.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill To Expose How Many Dual Citizens Work In The Federal Government
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Oct. 22, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced the Dual Citizen Disclosure Act, legislation requiring an annual public accounting of every federal employee on the taxpayer-funded payroll who holds citizenship in a foreign country.

“Taxpayers fund the paychecks. Taxpayers deserve to know where the loyalties lie,” said Congresswoman Mace. “Right now, Americans have no way of knowing how many federal employees are citizens of another country. If someone on the federal payroll holds citizenship in any country other than the United States, the American people have a right to know. This bill ends the guesswork. Sunlight is the best disinfectant, and transparency in our government is not optional.”

The bill amends Section 1103 of Title 5, United States Code, which sets out the functions of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM). Under the legislation, the OPM Director must publish the list on OPM’s public website no later than one year after the bill becomes law and every year after.

The list covers each officer or employee of the federal government who is a U.S. citizen or national and is also a citizen or national of, or otherwise owes allegiance to, a country other than the United States. For each individual, the list must identify:

The foreign countries of which the individual is a citizen or national

The federal agency where the individual works

The title and annual rate of pay of the individual’s position

“Federal service is not a part-time commitment to America. You serve this country, and only this country. End of story,” Mace added.
