title: Representative Mannion Continues to Seek Answers From Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Harriet Tubman $20 Bill Redesign and Taxpayer Spending
text:
The Honorable Scott Bessent

Secretary of the Treasury

U.S. Department of the Treasury

1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW

Washington, DC 20220

Dear Secretary Bessent:

We write to follow up on your Department’s response to our August 14 letter urging the

Department to resume the indefinitely paused 10-year-effort to place abolitionist Harriet Tubman on the twenty-dollar bill, as it does not adequately address the status of this initiative. We again request clarification on the status of the redesign, as well as the past progress and investment Treasury has made toward this effort.

When we wrote to you in August, we requested the Department resume its long-overdue effort to portray Harriet Tubman on the twenty-dollar bill and provide a detailed update on the current status of the project. Unfortunately, your September response failed to address either request. In fact, your response failed toarticulate whether or not this initiative has been delayed or permanently discontinued. Therefore, we write again to request a detailed accounting of prior efforts at Treasury to advance former Secretary Lew’s announcement that Tubman would replace Andrew Jackson on the twenty-dollar bill, including specific actions taken and resources expended. In addition, we request an update on the current status of the project and proposed timeline for next steps.

In seeking increased transparency, we ask the following:

Since the April 2016 announcement, how much has the Department and the Bureau of Engraving and Printing spent in developing the new “Catalyst” series $20 note?

Of those costs, how much were dedicated toward the Tubman redesign, including but not limited to engraving, design work, plate development, and any other design and production-related activities?

Taxpayers deserve a return on their investments. Given the significant resources – financial and otherwise – already devoted to this effort, abandoning the redesign before completion would be a waste of taxpayer resources.

We understand and appreciate the counterfeiting and security concerns that guide the

development and timelines of currency designs and redesigns and agree that the Department should prioritize a process that addresses those concerns. Thankfully, there is an easy solution to this theoretical challenge. In moving forward with currency design and development, we urge you to ensure a thorough and robust anti-counterfeiting process. To that end, we encourage the Treasury to work with the Anti-Counterfeiting Deterrence (ACD) Committee to identify a path forward that resumes the Department’s prior work to place Tubman on the twenty-dollar bill while addressing any potential counterfeiting or security concerns.

We also urge you to apply and follow this anti-counterfeiting process consistently across the board when it comes to other current and potential future currency redesigns and new designs. As we noted in our initialAugust letter, the Department has debuted a design for and advanced plans to develop a new $250 paper currency note featuring President Trump’s likeness that would be ready to go into production as soon as Congressional authorization could be granted.

Again, in seeking transparency, we then ask the following:

If this newly proposed $250 note can be designed and prepared for production as soon as Congress authorizes it—even before anti-counterfeiting measures are finalized—why is the Tubman redesign timeline being handled differently?

Has the proposed $250 note undergone any anti-counterfeiting and security review to date? If so, what have those efforts looked like, and what was the timeline? If not, what would those efforts look like and what would their timeline be?

In addition to providing answers to the enumerated questions, we again urge you to resume and implement the now long-overdue effort to portray Harriet Tubman on the twenty-dollar bill prior to developing new currency notes.

title: Chairman Griffith Helps Lead Effort to Revamp Rural Patient Access to Clinical Trials, Accelerate New Treatments to Market
text:
Today, members of the U.S. House of Representatives unveiled legislation to revamp patient access to clinical trials. U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health, and U.S. Congressman Jake Auchincloss (D-MA), a member of the Subcommittee on Health, released a bill titled the Faster Clinical Trials Act, which aims to streamline clinical processes, reduce regulatory burdens and enhance FDA capacities to expand access to therapies and treatments for patients. The bill seeks to improve the clinical trial landscape, promoting clinical research in routine health care settings, accelerating new-treatment development, and increasing innovative therapy access.

“Patients in rural communities like Virginia’s Ninth District often travel hours to participate in clinical trials for needed medical treatments,” said Chairman Griffith. “This reality discourages people from participating in clinical trials and hampers research efforts.

“Clinical trials play a major role in treatment discovery and research breakthroughs, especially for rare diseases where there are few, if any, available therapies on the market at times. The Faster Clinical Trials Act will expand research efforts, facilitate treatment options and support American patients, particularly in rural America.

“I thank Congressman Auchincloss for his proactive work, including working with me and my team, to develop these ideas in a comprehensive bill. I look forward to continued collaboration on policy ideas.”

“This is a science infrastructure bill,” said Congressman Auchincloss. “Researchers need quality data to inform hypotheses and experiments, turnkey clinical sites to test safety and efficacy, and evidence-driven standards. Data, trials, and standards are R&D infrastructure, and this legislation upgrades that infrastructure for the century of biology. I'm grateful to Chairman Griffith for his partnership.”

BACKGROUND

The Faster Clinical Trials Act also contains measures that were included in the Energy and Commerce Committee bill, the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act, that passed out of Committee this year. These measures include the Biosimilar Red Tape Elimination Act led by Representative August Pfluger (R-TX) and the Expedited Access to Biosimilars Act led by Representatives Nick Langworthy (R-NY) and Kim Schrier (D-WA).

title: Congressman Moskowitz Issues Statement Following Arrest of Individual Who Threatened His Life
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Jared Moskowitz (FL-23) released the following statement after an individual was arrested in Boca Raton for threatening his life:

“A constituent of mine has just been arrested in Boca Raton, just a few miles from my house, for threatening my life. He is currently in the Palm Beach County Jail. I’m grateful to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) and local law enforcement for acting quickly to keep my family and me safe.”

This is not the first time Congressman Moskowitz has faced threats against his life. In 2024, authorities uncovered a potential assassination plot involving an armed individual who had included the Congressman on a list of targets alongside Jewish institutions and other locations. During the arrest, authorities discovered firearms, body armor, and a manifesto containing antisemitic rhetoric. The individual was subsequently sentenced to 25 years in federal prison. Following the incident, Congressman Moskowitz and his family have been under heightened security protection, including a law enforcement presence at their residence and additional security measures during public appearances.

The Congressman and his office remain in communication with the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and local authorities regarding this matter. The office will provide additional updates as more information becomes available.

title: Congressman Patronis Demands Answers from the ACC on Sports Betting Policies as the Conference Seeks Congressional Action on NIL
text:

Dear Commissioner Phillips and Board of Directors,

title: Congresswoman Pettersen Convenes Immigration Roundtable on ICE Oversight and Priorities for Next Congress, Unveils Bills Restricting ICE Access to Disaster Survivors’ Personal Data
text:
Congresswoman Pettersen at today’s immigration roundtable with representatives from Casa de Paz, Hispanic Contractors of Colorado, COLOR Latina, Mi Casa Resource Center, Rocky Mountain Immigrant Advocacy Network, Mi Familia Vota, American Friends Service Committee, Adelante Community Development, Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition, CLLARO, and Lideres Latines

LAKEWOOD – Today, Congresswoman Pettersen (CO-07) convened local leaders to discuss the ongoing abuses by Trump’s rogue Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency and discuss with local leaders their shared priority to strengthen oversight and establish guardrails to protect immigrant communities in the next Congress. Pettersen also first announced to the group that she, alongside Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) today introduced two bills to protect disaster survivors’ personal information from being used for the purposes of immigration enforcement. This comes after the devastating Aspen Acres and Willow Fires forced thousands of Coloradans to evacuate earlier this summer, raising concerns that data collected through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and non-government entities to issue re-entry cards to affected areas in the wake of a natural disaster could be accessed by immigration enforcement.

“From the very beginning, Trump’s ICE agency has acted without regard for basic human rights and safety – killing innocent people, detaining people in inhumane conditions, ripping families apart, and spreading fear throughout our immigrant communities. We need to rein in this agency and look ahead to what the next Congress can do to put real guardrails in place, hold ICE accountable, and protect our communities,” saidCongresswoman Pettersen. “And no family fleeing a wildfire should have to wonder whether to ask for help or evacuate out of fear that their information will be used to target them. I’m so grateful for everyone who joined me today to have an honest discussion on how we can protect our neighbors and our community.”

“Every family deserves access to resources following a natural disaster without fear that their information will be used against them,” said Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove. “I am proud to join Rep. Pettersen on this package to prevent ICE from accessing data collected in response to a natural disaster. No one should be able to take advantage of our immigrant neighbors during a vulnerable time.”

“No family should have to fear deportation when seeking safety from a wildfire or asking for help after a disaster,” said Alex Sánchez, president and CEO of Voces Unidas. “These bills would help protect the personal information Latino and immigrant families share to get emergency assistance. We thank Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen for her leadership and urge Congress to pass these protections.”

The roundtable brought together leaders from Casa de Paz, Hispanic Contractors of Colorado, COLOR Latina, Mi Casa Resource Center, Rocky Mountain Immigrant Advocacy Network, Mi Familia Vota, American Friends Service Committee, Adelante Community Development, Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition, CLLARO, and Lideres Latines to discuss how ICE’s enforcement practices are affecting immigrant communities across Colorado.

The group discussed the various abuses that ICE has carried out on communities, including the killings of multiple innocent people including American citizens, the long-term detention of individuals in temporary holding cells that lack basic access to sanitation, and repeated ICE operations in and around sensitive areas including schools and churches. Wait times for immigration cases, applications, and work authorization documents have also been affected, with certain applications now taking over 6 months to process – leaving families facing prolonged uncertainty about their immigration cases and ability to work. Pettersen focused the discussion on where gaps in services are leaving families without support as well as her priorities for the 120th Congress, including bipartisan opportunities to expand access to counsel, improve detention transparency, and strengthen protections for children and mothers.

During the discussion, Pettersen also announced the introduction of her two new bills, the Emergency Assistance Privacy Protection Act and the Disaster Data Protection Act. These bills prohibit FEMA from sharing disaster survivors’ personally identifiable information with ICE and prohibit ICE from obtaining disaster data collected by third parties without a judicial warrant, respectively. This followed the Congresswoman’s visits to areas affected by this year’s Willow and Aspen Acres Fires, which burned over 100,000 acres of land, including in Custer and Lake counties, and forced thousands to evacuate from their homes. Residents affected by the evacuations expressed concerns that the personal information collected by FEMA in the wake of a natural disaster to administer re-entry cards to evacuated areas could be accessed and used by ICE for non-targeted immigration enforcement. This raises larger concerns that members of the immigrant community would forgo evacuation orders or fail to properly identify themselves to first responders and other disaster response personnel out of fear that this information will be accessed by ICE.

Specifically, the Emergency Assistance Privacy Protection Act would:

Prohibit data sharing of any personally identifiable information collected by FEMA with ICE.

Full bill text can be found HERE.

Specifically, the Disaster Data Protection Act would:

Prohibit ICE from obtaining data collected by a third party during a disaster absent a criminal warrant.

Full bill text can be found HERE.

Under the Trump Administration, Congressional Republicans have repeatedly voted to send more money to ICE and immigration enforcement with no guardrails, including over $70 billion initially through H.R. 1 and an additional $70 billion this past summer for ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) over three years – even as the agency has come under fire for its conduct. Pettersen has consistently voted against allocating additional funds to ICE, calling for major regulatory oversight and guardrails to keep immigrant communities safe.

Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen has repeatedly pushed back against Trump’s harmful immigration policiesand efforts to pour billions more into ICE and CBP without meaningful accountability. She has voted against enforcement funding packages, backed legislation requiring agents to visibly identify themselves, and supported restoring protections for schools, hospitals, and places of worship. Alongside Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper, she demanded that the administration abandon plans for a new ICE detention facility in Hudson,Colorado. She has also pressed for answers about prolonged detention in field office holding cells and proposed safeguards to protect detained parents’ children and prevent immigration detainees from being held in federal prisons.

title: ANGELINE MUCKLE-JABBAR TO JOIN PRIVATE SECTOR FOLLOWING TENURE AS CHIEF OF STAFF TO CONGRESSWOMAN STACEY E. PLASKETT
text:
For Immediate Release Contact: Tionee Scotland

October 22, 2026 202-808-6129

PRESS RELEASE

ANGELINE MUCKLE-JABBAR TO JOIN PRIVATE SECTOR FOLLOWING TENURE AS CHIEF OF STAFF TO CONGRESSWOMAN STACEY E. PLASKETT

U.S. Virgin Islands— After years of dedicated service on Capitol Hill, Angeline M. Jabbar will depart the Office of Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett to join a leading Washington, D.C. law and government relations firm.

Angeline most recently served as Chief of Staff to Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett, representing the U.S. Virgin Islands in the U.S. House of Representatives. As Chief of Staff, Angeline provided strategic leadership and oversight of the Congresswoman's Washington, D.C. and district offices and worked closely with congressional leadership, Members of Congress, federal agencies, community leaders, private-sector organizations, and other stakeholders on legislative and policy priorities affecting the U.S. Virgin Islands and the nation.

During her tenure in the Office of Congresswoman Plaskett, Angeline served as Legislative Director, advancing the Congresswoman's legislative agenda and strengthening relationships across Capitol Hill and throughout the federal government. Her responsibilities included legislative strategy, staff management, congressional operations, and stakeholder engagement. She has been instrumental in mentoring numerous interns in the office.

Angeline also served as Congresswoman Plaskett’s liaison to the Congressional Black Caucus, Congressional Caribbean Caucus, and Congressional Caucus on Black Innovation, including work associated with their legislative and policy programming. She has been actively involved in developing relationships among national, Caribbean, and international stakeholders.

Prior to joining Congresswoman Plaskett's office, Angeline built a career spanning federal legislative affairs, government relations, public policy, and local government. Her professional experience includes working with former Congresswoman Donna M. Christensen; in the Office of D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser; as Judicial Clerk to former Virgin Islands Superior Court Judge Edgar Ross; and at the U.S. Department of Labor.

Throughout her career, Ms. Jabbar has worked on a broad range of legislative and policy matters, including economic development, housing, healthcare, education, energy, technology, agriculture, government operations, and issues affecting communities in the Caribbean and the U.S. Virgin Islands. That experience has given her a comprehensive understanding of the legislative process and the relationships necessary to advance complex policy priorities in Washington. Angeline is a graduate of Howard University and Georgetown University Law Center.

“Angeline has been an invaluable member of our team and a trusted adviser throughout her tenure in my office,” said Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett. “Her leadership, institutional knowledge, commitment to public service, and ability to bring people together have made a lasting contribution to our work on behalf of the people of the Virgin Islands. I am excited to see her take this next step in her career and know that she will continue to make an impact in Washington, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and many other locations.”

“I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to have served Congresswoman Plaskett and the people of my home, the U.S. Virgin Islands,” said Angeline. “Serving as Chief of Staff has been one of the most meaningful experiences of my professional career. I am proud of the work our team accomplished and of the relationships built.”

Angeline added, “I am excited to begin this next chapter of my career. My years in government have given me a firsthand understanding of how legislative and public policy decisions are developed and implemented. I look forward to bringing that experience to the firm and working with its clients and team to navigate the increasingly complex federal policy and government relations environment.”

In her new role, Angeline will advise clients on federal legislative and policy matters, government relations, and strategic engagement.

title: Amata Congratulates Peace Corps Volunteer Rosalina Macon
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is congratulating Peace Corps Volunteer Rosalina Macon, a former intern in the congressional office, and currently featured in an article on the Peace Corps website. She is from Manu’a and the villages of Utumea, Fagaalu, and Vailoa.

Rosalina Macon pictured in the congressional office with Ina Pa'au, Elijah Tavai, and Ola Foster

In her studies at North Carolina A&T State University, Rosalina twice had the opportunity to study abroad. Those in turn inspired her desire to reconnect deeply with her Samoan heritage, increase fluency in the Samoan language, and consider the Peace Corps with the idea of possibly serving in Samoa. Instead, she was offered the opportunity for a new experience staying in the Indo-Pacific region and serving in Indonesia, the world’s largest archipelagic nation of islands. It is the world’s fourth-most populous country, and in the top 15 in the world by total land area.

In Indonesia, after three months of focused training, then moving there on her birthday, she began teaching English while working on her use of the local language, Sundanese. She quickly established friendships and a special support network with three local English teachers she now calls her “sisters,” as well as finding a welcoming community from the locals.

Along with her teaching assignment at Islamic Middle School in Java, the world’s most populous island, she and the teachers there are implementing fun vocabulary words, strengthening students’ opportunities through an English club outside the structure of the classroom, and planning for an English camp.

Rosalina said, “It has been a privilege to serve as a Peace Corps volunteer in Indonesia. I’ve been blessed to work alongside my Indonesian counterparts and community to create projects together, and along the way I’ve learned so much about Indonesian culture while getting to share my own in return. Not every day is easy, but I’m constantly reminded that I represent more than myself. I carry my family and my communities in American Samoa and South Carolina with me, and I’m proud to represent them. Though service isn’t a foreign concept to me, this experience has simply been a continuation of that lifelong commitment.”

“Congratulations to Rosalina, who worked as an intern in our office in Tutuila. She has a bright future through her intelligence, assertiveness, and deep interest in influencing policy for the betterment of people’s lives,” said Congresswoman Amata. “She’s putting those interests to great use right now with the Peace Corps, which will lead to more open doors. I know her family and friends in American Samoa and South Carolina are following this phase of her life closely, and we are proud of her in American Samoa!”

Congresswoman Amata serves as Co-Chairman of the bipartisan Peace Corps Caucus in the U.S. House of Representatives, with Congressman John Garamendi (D-CA). They have worked for reauthorization legislation and emphasized the expansion of the Peace Corps back into more nations following pandemic recovery, including the Indo-Pacific region.

title: Rep. Torres Demands Answers from HUD on Abandonment of Fair Housing Enforcement for LGBTQ+ Americans
text:
Today, Congressman Ritchie Torres (NY-15) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner demanding answers about HUD’s current approach to fair housing enforcement, particularly the Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity’s (FHEO) enforcement of protections for LGBTQ+ Americans.

In 2021, HUD announced that the Fair Housing Act’s prohibition on sex discrimination covers discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, consistent with the Supreme Court’s reasoning in Bostock v. Clayton County. After the Trump Administration revoked Executive Order 13988 at the start of the President’s second term, HUD retreated from that enforcement posture. The Congressmember notes that this retreat is at odds with Secretary Turner’s own public pledge to uphold the Fair Housing Act for every American.

The consequences fall on people who already face disproportionate housing instability. According to the Williams Institute, 50 percent of LGBTQ+ adults own homes, compared with 70 percent of non-LGBTQ+ adults, and LGBTQ+ people are more likely to face discrimination in rental housing, mortgage lending, homeless shelters, and other housing-related services. A separate Equal Rights Center investigation found that almost half of older same-sex couples face some form of discrimination when seeking elder housing.

The letter cites ProPublica reporting on an Arkansas man who filed a complaint alleging he was denied housing because he is gay. HUD initially began processing his complaint, but after the change in administration he was told that allegations of sexual orientation or gender identity discrimination were no longer being investigated. Career staff have also reportedly faced efforts by political appointees to obstruct investigations, and whole categories of cases, including LGBTQ+ discrimination, appraisal bias, zoning restrictions, and language access, have reportedly received diminished priority or heightened political scrutiny.

The Fair Housing Act directs HUD to investigate filed complaints and generally complete investigations within 100 days. Rep. Torres is requesting that HUD account for the cases removed from its backlog and how each was resolved, provide monthly data on sexual orientation and gender identity complaints since January 20, 2025, identify which categories of discrimination have been deprioritized, disclose whether political appointees must preapprove routine investigative work, report current FHEO staffing compared with January 2025, and justify any decision to decline investigating discrimination complaints. The Congressmember has requested complete responses by November 1, 2026.

The full letter reads (PDF here):

“I write to request answers regarding the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) current approach to fair housing enforcement, particularly the enforcement of protections for LGBTQ+ Americans by the Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO).

“Housing is not a privilege reserved for those whom the presidential administration considers politically acceptable. It is the foundation upon which Americans build their lives, raise their families, maintain employment, and pursue prosperity. The federal government has a responsibility to ensure that Americans are not denied that foundation because of who they are or whom they love. These issues not only have direct consequences for my constituents in the Bronx, but the integrity of federal fair housing enforcement is a national concern that should matter to communities in every state and all Members of Congress.

“In 2021, HUD announced that the Fair Housing Act’s prohibition on sex discrimination would encompass discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. That position reflected the Supreme Court’s reasoning in its Bostock v. Clayton County decision that discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity is a form of sex discrimination in the employment context. In the decision authored by Justice Neil Gorsuch, the Supreme Court recognized that ‘it is impossible to discriminate against a person for being homosexual or transgender without discriminating against that individual based on sex.’ The decision provided critical clarity on the application of Bostock in discrimination cases.

“The consequences of this change in enforcement are not theoretical. Research from the Williams Institute demonstrates that LGBTQ+ people experience disproportionately high rates of poverty, housing instability, and homelessness. 50% of LGBTQ+ adults own homes, while 70% of non-LGBTQ+ adults own homes. LGBTQ+ people are further more likely to experience discrimination in rental housing, mortgage lending, homeless shelters, and other housing-related services. Transgender Americans and LGBTQ+ youth are particularly vulnerable to housing instability and homelessness. At the same time almost half of older same-sex couples face some form of housing discrimination when seeking elder housing.

“Against this backdrop, the Trump Administration’s actions are more than a change in bureaucratic priorities. They risk weakening the federal government’s willingness to protect one of the country’s most vulnerable populations from discrimination.

“At the outset of President Trump’s second term, the Administration revoked Executive Order 13988 and changed federal policy concerning recognition and protection for transgender Americans. HUD subsequently retreated from the enforcement posture that had recognized discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity as actionable under the Fair Housing Act. HUD’s retreat from enforcing sexual orientation and gender identity nondiscrimination protections is inconsistent with your public proclamations to support equal housing for every American. During your commemoration of Fair Housing Month last year you declared, ‘We at HUD will uphold the Fair Housing Act so every American has the opportunity to achieve the American dream.’ You went on to declare that, ‘Americans in rural, tribal, and urban communities should have the power to choose where to build their lives free of discrimination.’ Unfortunately, despite your words, HUD has continued to politicize enforcement of fair housing across the country.

“The consequences of this politicization have already been documented. According to reporting by ProPublica, an individual in Arkansas filed a housing discrimination complaint after allegedly being denied housing because he was gay. HUD initially began processing the complaint but following the change from the Biden Administration to the current Administration, the complainant was informed that allegations of discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity were no longer being investigated. Reporting has further documented that numerous fair housing cases have been halted or closed, including cases involving sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination.

“HUD’s response to this Arkansas man who alleged that he was denied housing because of his sexuality was to tell him, in effect, that the federal government has washed its hands of his discrimination claim. This sends a troubling message: that HUD views some victims of housing discrimination as no longer worthy of protection.

“That is unacceptable. Reports that the claims process has become an obstacle course for victims of discrimination warrant a clear response from HUD.

“The reports concerning political interference are especially disturbing. Career civil servants and attorneys have reportedly faced efforts by political appointees to obstruct investigations and enforcement activity. Meanwhile, categories of cases, including those involving LGBTQ+ discrimination, appraisal bias, zoning restrictions, language access, and environmental justice, have reportedly been subjected to diminished priority or heightened political scrutiny. Discrimination does not cease to exist because a political appointee finds the underlying civil rights theory inconvenient. Appraisal bias is not a ‘theory’ when discriminatory valuation deprives families of wealth; exclusionary zoning is not a ‘theory’ when government policies perpetuate segregation; discrimination against a transgender person is not a ‘theory’ when that person is denied a home because of their gender identity; and discrimination against an LGBTQ+ person is not a ‘theory’ when a landlord denies them housing because of whom they love.

“The Department’s obligation is to enforce the law, not to redefine discrimination out of existence. The Fair Housing Act directs HUD to investigate filed complaints and generally complete investigations within 100 days unless doing so is impracticable; when that deadline cannot be met, HUD must notify the parties in writing of the reasons. For these reasons, I request that HUD provide complete and specific responses to the following questions:

HUD has publicly cited reductions in the case backlog from the start of the Trump Administration to June 12, 2026. Of every fair housing complaint removed from that backlog, what was the basis of each complaint and how many cases were: (a) fully investigated and resolved on the merits; (b) settled; (c) administratively closed; (d) dismissed without a full investigation; or (e) halted or placed in inactive status?

How many fair housing complaints involving allegations of discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity has FHEO received, investigated, administratively closed, dismissed, charged, or otherwise resolved since January 20, 2025? Please provide the data by month, disposition, and FHEO region.

What categories of housing discrimination does HUD currently consider a priority for enforcement, and what categories have been formally or informally deprioritized since January 20, 2025?

Do political appointees require preapproval for routine investigative or litigation activities conducted by career attorneys and enforcement personnel? If so, what statutory, regulatory, or Departmental authority governs that review, and when did the requirement begin?

How many employees currently work for FHEO, and how does that figure compare with FHEO staffing levels on January 20, 2025? Please provide current staffing levels by headquarters and each regional office.

FHEO is required by statute to investigate fair housing discrimination complaints. What is the justification for declining to investigate discrimination complaints?

“I request that HUD provide complete responses, including the underlying data necessary to substantiate each answer, no later than November 1, 2026.

“Let me be unequivocal: the Administration does not get to unilaterally decide who is worthy of federal protections simply because the victims do or do not belong to a politically disfavored community. HUD cannot erase LGBTQ+ people from federal civil rights protections by changing a guidance document, starving an enforcement office of personnel, or placing political roadblocks in front of career investigators. HUD’s obligations to investigate and resolve cases of housing discrimination for every American have been made clear by Congress and the courts.

“The destruction of civil rights enforcement is itself a policy choice. The abandonment of LGBTQ+ Americans is itself a policy choice. Every complaint ignored, every investigation halted, and every victim denied a meaningful remedy is a consequence of that choice. HUD’s Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity was created to protect Americans from discrimination, not to protect discriminators from accountability. No administration has the right to turn federal civil rights protections into a political suggestion. HUD must enforce the law, and Congress must hold the Department accountable if it does not.”

title: Congresswoman Scanlon Introduces Bill to Fund High-Quality Civic Education and Engage Youth in the Democratic Process
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) today introduced the Teaching Engaged Citizenship Act, legislation to promote and expand high-quality, evidence-based civic education and service learning programming in K-12 public schools. The bill is introduced as federal and state funding and programs for civic education have dwindled in recent years.

According to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, funding for K-12 civics education increased from $7.75 million to $23 million between 2022 and 2024 to support teacher professional development, curriculum development, and student programming. However, recent budget proposals would cut $12 billion from K-12 education programs, including grants to increase access to civic education.

The Teaching Engaged Citizenship Act will create a Civic Education and Service Learning Grant Program to encourage the implementation of high-quality, evidence-based civic education and service learning programming in K-12 public schools. The bill would authorize the appropriation of $400,000,000 for the Civic Education and Service Learning Grant Program. It will also establish an Office of Civic Education within the Department of Education to promote civic education throughout the United States.

“High-quality civic education is critical to having an informed and engaged electorate, able to participate in a functioning democracy,” said Rep. Scanlon. “Expanding civic education helps young people understand their roles and responsibilities as citizens and empowers them to participate in our government and communities. I’m proud to introduce the Teaching Engaged Citizenship Act to expand civic education in our public schools for our next generation of leaders.”

The Teaching Engaged Citizenship Act will:

Establish the Civic Education and Service Learning Grant Program to award grants to eligible entities for promoting and expanding civic education in public elementary and secondary schools.

Create the Office of Civic Education within ED to promote civic education throughout the United States.

Requires the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) in civics and history to be administered in grades 4, 8, and 12, and to publish assessment data in the aggregate for the United States and separately for each state.

Establish an annual Excellence in Civics Award to highlight excellence in the development and teaching of civic education and service learning.

Support the development and distribution of educational materials and teaching resources related to civic education and effective citizenship by the Library of Congress, Institute of Museum and Library Services, and the National Archives.

title: SCHNEIDER, RANKING MEMBER MORELLE CONVENE ELECTION SECURITY ROUNDTABLE TO HEAR FROM LOCAL OFFICIALS AND ORGANIZATIONS
text:
Congressman Brad Schneider and Ranking Member Joseph D. Morelle host roundtable with local officials and organizations about election security

“President Trump continues to threaten access to the polls for millions of Americans,” said Schneider. “Trump has repeatedly pushed for passage of his so-called SAVE America Act that would make it harder to vote for millions of citizens, including deployed service members, disabled Americans, and individuals who change their name after marriage while voting by mail himself. And there are real concerns about other Administration actions in the coming weeks. Americans deserve to have full trust in our electoral system and faith that their vote will be counted fairly. I was proud to host this important convening alongside my friend and colleague Ranking Member Morelle who has been a steadfast leader in election security and ensuring the American people’s voices are heard. We will take the concerns we heard today back to Washington to advance commonsense solutions that ensure everyone has free and fair access to the ballot box.”

“Donald Trump’s election interference schemes are designed to undermine Americans’ confidence in our elections. But our elections are secure, we are prepared, and we are fighting back. Millions of Americans have already cast their ballots, and Election Day is fast approaching. Americans should check their registration status, vote early where available, and encourage their loved ones to make a plan to vote,” said Ranking Member Joe Morelle.

Last month, Rep. Schneider joined more than 250 current and former lawmakers to urge the Supreme Court to block President Trump’s executive order that would require states to provide a citizenship verification list to the Department of Homeland Security and give the Postal Service control over who can vote by mail. Millions of Americans utilize mail-in voting including deployed service members, seniors, and disabled Americans.

title: Rep. Peters, Labor, Clean Energy Leaders Urge Action on Permitting Reform
text:
San Diego, CA – Today, Rep. Scott Peters hosted a roundtable with leaders from the renewable energy and labor sectors to discuss local and federal efforts to hold data centers accountable, increase clean energy production, lower costs, and create jobs. After the roundtable, Rep. Peters joined leaders from the renewable energy and labor communities to urge the House and Senate to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) in this Congress to fix our outdated, broken federal permitting system.

Senators Whitehouse (D-RI), Capito (R-WV), Heinrich (D-NM), and Lee (R-UT) introduced the package on September 30th. The bill has strong reforms that will help us keep data center costs off our electricity bills, meet surging energy demand, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and outcompete countries like China.

Amid recent news of plans to develop Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR) into a data center, Rep. Peters also noted his opposition to the project and clarified how BAAJA will prevent ratepayers from paying for the rise in usage and the infrastructure costs of data centers nationwide.

“I've spent years calling for America to get out of our own way and build this critical infrastructure faster so we can lower costs, create jobs, fight climate change, and push back on data centers,” said Rep. Peters. “BAAJA still needs some adjustments and clarifications, but it ought to be voted on this Congress and I’m confident it will have strong bipartisan support. This is our chance for Congress to prove to the American people we can still accomplish big things. We can’t waste it.”

“Cleantech San Diego and our members share a goal of advancing San Diego’s access to reliable, affordable, clean energy, and that depends on getting projects built,” said Jason Anderson, President and CEO, Cleantech San Diego. “The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act and permitting reform championed by Congressman Scott Peters give developers confidence that a permit, once issued, will actually hold. This critical shift means renewable energy projects can get to market sooner to meet growing power demands and clean energy goals.

We greatly appreciate and commend Congressman Peters’ leadership and efforts to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, said Theresa Carroll, Vice President, Environmental and Land Compliance, GIS and Policy, AES US Renewables and Power. “AES supports a pragmatic, technology-neutral permitting policy that enables the development of the energy solutions needed to meet growing demand. We urge Congress to advance the bill and deliver meaningful permitting and transmission reforms that support reliable, affordable electricity for American families and businesses.”

Since coming to Congress, Rep. Peters has led some of the largest bipartisan efforts in Congress reform our outdated permitting process. Several of his bills are included in BAAJA, including SPEED and Reliability Act, CERTAIN Act, CLEAR Act, BIG WIRES Act, and ePermit Act. American builders, investors, labor groups, climate activists, and taxpayers want Congress to act by fixing our old and slow permitting system.

A livestreamed recording of the press conference can be viewed here. Additional photos from the event, courtesy of the office of Rep. Peters, can be viewed here.

Read Rep. Peters’ full remarks from the press conference below:

The environmental laws from the 1970s weren’t given to us on tablets by Moses. They were written by lawmakers trying to stop bad projects from harming our environment, and they did their job for the challenges we faced at that time. Today, we need to build more, faster to meet our current challenges: high energy bills, increased energy demand, and rapidly expanding data center needs.

That means we need to change how the federal government approves energy and infrastructure projects so we can lower costs and hold data centers accountable.

I've spent years calling for America to get out of our own way. Throughout this Congress, I've been introducing legislation and working with my colleagues to get permitting reform across the finish line.

At last, Congress is on the cusp of a bipartisan, comprehensive permitting reform deal that takes a great step toward fixing our broken permitting system.

Earlier this month, a bipartisan group of Senators compiled dozens of permitting reform proposals and introduced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA).

I’m gratified that several of my bills are included in the package and will increase energy supply, build more transmission, and make sure the backlog of clean energy projects get built with no more delays.

These and other reforms are a win for affordability, high-paying jobs, and our environment.

In our roundtable just now, I heard from local attorneys, energy providers, engineers, energy developers, and union leaders who all agree: process delays hurt everyone. We have the opportunity to fix that.

The package still needs some adjustments and clarifications, but it ought to be voted on this Congress and I’m confident it will have strong bipartisan support. American builders, investors, labor groups, climate activists, and taxpayers want Congress to fix our old and slow permitting system.

This would be really good for our country and it’s a chance for Congress to prove to the American people we can still accomplish big things. We can’t waste it.

Thank you to Jason Anderson with Cleantech San Diego and Theresa Carroll with AES US Renewables and Power for being here to talk about how your sectors would utilize the provisions in BAAJA to lower costs, employ skilled workers, and power a cleaner economy.

title: Congresswoman Sheri Biggs Fights to Keep Chinese Technology out of America’s Defense Systems
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Sheri Biggs (R-SC-03) introduced 3 new pieces of legislation today to address China’s dual-use technology. These bills focus on 3 key sectors- cellular modules, advanced robotics, and biotechnology- that the People’s Liberation Army of China uses to integrate commercial technology into its military capabilities. This legislation seeks to fill gaps in current U.S. policy by recognizing foreign capabilities, determining risks, and keeping our servicemen and women safe.

These standalone bills are based on amendments previously introduced by the Congresswoman for the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and the Blocking Foreign Cellular Modules in Defense Systems Act of 2026, S. 5598, introduced by Senator Banks (R-IN).

This legislation displays Congresswoman Biggs’ continued focus on putting America First and addressing threats to our national security.

"It is essential that our national security policy continues to evolve as the Chinese Communist Party looks to achieve military-civil fusion," said Congresswoman Biggs. "By strengthening the ability to assess and mitigate these risks, it enhances ongoing efforts to safeguard U.S. military personnel and our critical national security infrastructure.”

“Communist China is working every day to undermine America’s military advantage. We must identify and eliminate vulnerabilities in our defense systems and infrastructure before our adversaries can exploit them,” said Senator Banks. “Protecting our military from foreign supply chain threats is essential to keeping our nation safe.”

“Under its military-civil fusion strategy, the Chinese Communist Party has erased the line between its commercial sector and its armed forces. Beijing is exploiting that to embed itself in American supply chains and research and to undermine U.S. military systems,” said Alexandria Paolozzi Moore, Senior Director of Government Relations at FDD Action. “Technology doesn’t have to be built for the battlefield to be weaponized. That is why Washington needs to judge dual-use technology by who controls it and what that control makes possible. FDD Action supports these bills because they require the government to find, assess, and act on adversary-linked risks in biotechnology, cellular modules, and robotic systems. Congress should move these bills without delay.”

title: Congresswoman Simon Secures Over $1 Million in Federal Funding for Public Safety at Mills College at Northeastern University and Surrounding Oakland Neighborhood
text:
OAKLAND, CA – This week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12) announced $1,031,000 in Community Project Funding (CPF) for Mills College at Northeastern University Oakland. This federal funding will be used to purchase new emergency blue-light phone towers and security cameras that will help to improve public safety on campus and in the surrounding community.

Congresswoman Simon announced the funding alongside Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, Dean of Northeastern University Oakland Dan Sachs, Associated Vice President for Global Site Security Regina Coppa, and other Northeastern University leadership. This federal investment is part of Congresswoman Simon’s commitment to bringing federal resources back to the East Bay and supporting students, educators, and educational institutions who are creating the next generation of leaders in the East Bay.

This Community Project Funding (CPF) is a part of the $11.2 million dollars that Congresswoman Simon secured for 15 projects across the East Bay in Fiscal Year 2026. Each fiscal year, members of Congress can submit Community Project Funding requests for consideration with the House Committee on Appropriations.You can read about the 15 projects that Congresswoman Simon secured funding for in her first year here.

“Mills College at Northeastern University is one of the jewels of Oakland. I came to this campus as a student and young single mother and walked these paths with my child. I know this campus is home to far more than a university. It is home to the little ones at the preschool, the girls at Julia Morgan, the neighbors who swim in the pool and walk the trail, and the faculty and workers who keep it all running,” said Congresswoman Lateefah Simon. “This funding invests in every one of them and in the simple things that make a place safe: light, open paths, updated equipment like call booths. NE’s leadership is committed to a campus that takes responsibility for its neighbors as much as its own. Safety is a public good, and that is exactly the kind of investment Oakland deserves. Thank you to Mayor Barbara Lee for her partnership on this funding.”

"This campus changed my life when I came here as a single mother on public assistance, and this million-dollar investment continues that legacy of support by keeping our students, families, and neighbors safe," said Mayor Barbara Lee. "Before leaving Congress, I requested federal funding for this project, and I am deeply grateful to Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for carrying it forward so we can build the safe, thriving community Oakland deserves."

"We’re grateful to Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for her leadership in securing this funding for our Oakland campus," said Renee Jadushlever, Vice President for Campus Administration and Strategic Initiatives at Northeastern University. "It’s a place where students learn, do research, build community, and gain real-world experience with our industry partners across the region. This investment will help maintain the safety of our campus community while we continue to welcome our neighbors and deepen our connections across Oakland."

title: Rep. Steube Urges USTR to Protect Florida Growers in Mexico Trade Negotiations
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) sent a letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer urging the Trump administration to secure enforceable protections for Florida’s specialty crop growers as trade negotiations with Mexico continue.

“Florida farmers should not be forced out of business because of unfair trade practices that favor foreign producers,” said Rep. Steube. “For too long, Mexican produce imports have undercut our hardworking growers during our harvest seasons. President Trump is putting American farmers first, and any new trade agreement with Mexico must deliver real, enforceable protections for Florida’s agricultural industry.”

For years, Florida farmers have faced unfair competition from Mexican produce imports flooding U.S. markets during domestic harvest seasons, driving down prices and threatening American agricultural producers. Rep. Steube is calling for product-specific tariff-rate quotas to address these persistent challenges before any trade agreement with Mexico is finalized.

In his letter, Rep. Steube highlighted Ambassador Greer’s previous commitments to addressing seasonal import competition during the USMCA review process, including testimony before the House Ways and Means Committee acknowledging that existing trade remedies have failed to adequately protect domestic growers.

title: Congresswoman Lee Announces New Bipartisan Legislation to Protect Restaurants from Harmful Practices by Delivery Service Platforms
text:
Watch and download video here

LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) joined local small businessowner Kristen Corral, Co-Founder of Tacotarian and the Nevada Restaurant Association to announce the introduction of her bipartisan PROTECT Small Restaurants Act. This legislation will prohibit third-party delivery services (3PDs) from listing restaurants on their platforms without the restaurant’s permission.

“Our small, independent restaurants are already struggling from razor-thin profit margins and decreased tourism rates. The last thing they need is big corporations hurting their reputation and making it harder for them to bring costumers through their doors,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “That’s exactly why I introduced legislation to prohibit third-party delivery services from listing restaurants on their platforms without the restaurant’s permission. Restaurants deserve peace of mind that they’re free from this harmful practice while juggling everything else that comes with owning a small business.”

The success of services such as DoorDash, UberEats, and Grubhub have, in part, been at the expense of small independent restaurants. Since 2020, hundreds of thousands of cases have been reported of third-party delivery services listing restaurants on their platforms without authorization from the business owner. In many cases, these owners only discover these listings after receiving negative reviews of delivery orders they didn’t authorize or even offer from their establishments. Currently, there is no federal law prohibiting this predatory behavior.

“Small businesses are facing some of the toughest years we’ve seen in a very long time – margins are extremely thin and rising costs are impacting restaurants every day. And now, restaurants continue to find themselves listed on third party delivery platforms without their consent,” said Kristen Corral, Co-Founder of Tacotarian. “That matters because, at the end of the day, the last person to interact with your food is a delivery driver without the certifications and permits restaurants are required to have. I’m excited about the PROTECT Small Restaurants Act, and I want to thank Congresswoman Lee for her leadership on this issue.”

For many restaurant owners, average operating costs now range from 92.5% to 101.2% of revenue, meaning many operators are spending as much as or more than they generate in sales before taxes. Nearly nine in 10 independent restaurant owners surveyed said they raised menu prices to cope with rising costs.

The Providing Real Oversight of Third-parties Executing Certain Transactions for (PROTECT) Small Restaurants Act will:

Require third-party delivery systems (3PDs) to enter into partnership agreements with the restaurants for which the services deliver,

Prohibit 3PDs from arranging for the delivery of an order from a vendor without first obtaining a partnership agreement with the vendor expressly authorizing the 3PD to take orders and deliver meals prepared by the vendor,

Require 3PDs to remove vendors listed on their platforms without a valid partnership agreement within 10 calendar days of notification by the vendor, and

Strengthens the Federal Trade Commission’s ability to crackdown on this predatory practice by classifying these unauthorized listings as “unfair or deceptive acts” under the law to enforce these requirements.

The PROTECT Small Restaurants Act is endorsed by the National Restaurant Association, Independent Restaurant Association, and Nevada Restaurant Association.

“At the end of the day, what we're asking for is simple: if you spend years building a restaurant, investing your savings, hiring employees, and earning the trust of your community, someone else should not be able to take your name and profit from it. And if you're a consumer ordering food online, you deserve to know that the restaurant you're ordering from is actually preparing your food,” said Peter Saba, Senior Government Affairs and Communications Manager for the Nevada Restaurant Association. “These are basic protections that restaurant operators across the country deserve. On behalf of the Nevada Restaurant Association, we thank Congresswoman Lee and support passage of the PROTECT Small Restaurants Act.”

“Independent restaurants shouldn’t have their names, menus, and reputations used by third-party delivery platforms without their consent. When restaurants lose control over how their food is sold and delivered, they pay the price in lost revenue and customer trust. The PROTECT Small Restaurants Act is common sense: if a company wants to sell a restaurant’s food, it should have that restaurant’s permission,” said Erika Polmar, Executive Director, Independent Restaurant Coalition. “By requiring partnership agreements and giving the FTC the authority to enforce these protections, this legislation will help ensure independent restaurants have a say in how they are represented on third-party delivery platforms. We appreciate Representatives Susie Lee and John McGuire for standing up for the small businesses who anchor our communities, and we look forward to working with them to move this legislation forward.”

title: Rep. Sykes Introduces Legislation to Stop Law Enforcement Officers from Abusing Flock Cameras
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) introduced the Law Enforcement Accountability for Plate Reader Abuse (LEAP) Act to protect victims whose safety is put in jeopardy by law enforcement officials abuse of Flock cameras. According to the Washington Post, at least 50 law enforcement officials have been accused or charged with misusing Flock cameras or similar tools, with more than half of those incidents involving surveillance of romantic partners.

This bill holds state and local law enforcement agencies accountable for misuse of Flock cameras and other automated license plate reader (ALPR) technologies by their officers. If a state or local police department is receiving any funding from the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant or the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program, they must report to the Attorney General of the United States, if there is any misuse of the Flock cameras and what corrective measures were taken. As a condition of receiving funds, departments will be required to submit this information and submit to random audits from the Office of the Inspector General. If there are no corrective measures taken or there's a repeat offense, then the state or local department could lose 10% of their funding under these federal grant programs. If data is reported inaccurately, then the department could lose 15% of their funding.

“Law enforcement officials are trusted members of our communities. Abuse of Flock cameras and similar tools by law enforcement officers to stalk victims without their knowledge will not be tolerated,” said Rep. Sykes. “I introduced this legislation to protect victims whose safety has been put in jeopardy by rogue officers and to ensure that departments are holding those responsible accountable for their actions.”

title: Thompson, Salinas Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Lower Housing Costs and Support American Timber Industry
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Andrea Salinas (D-Ore.) introduced the bipartisan Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act, legislation to lower housing construction costs, strengthen American manufacturing, and create jobs in rural communities. The bill would provide targeted incentives to expand domestic production of mass timber, an innovative wood building material that helps builders construct homes faster and at a lower cost.

"The northern tier of Pennsylvania historically has been a leader in timber production, and this important industry has done its part to drive local economies for generations,” Rep. Thompson said. “The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act will strengthen the forest products industry and fund future research, which will drive innovation and the future of timber usage.”

“Every Oregon family deserves a home they can afford. Right now, Oregon needs to build nearly 500,000 new homes over the next 20 years to keep up with demand, but we simply aren’t building enough, and the restricted supply leads to increased prices,” Rep. Salinas said. “Mass timber can help us build faster and more affordably. Oregon has led the wood products industry for generations, and this bill provides the opportunity for Oregon workers to lead what comes next. That means more homes for working families and more good jobs in the rural towns that helped build this state. I look forward to working with Rep. Thompson to get this done.”

Mass timber products are made from layers of wood bonded or fastened together to create strong structural components, including large panels and beams. These materials are particularly well-suited for housing projects, where traditional wood framing may not be practical and other construction materials may not be economical. Because mass timber components can be manufactured off-site and assembled quickly, they can reduce construction timelines and costs.

The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act would:

Help manufacturers build new plants. The bill offers a 10% tax credit for investments in mass timber manufacturing facilities, including machinery, equipment, and buildings. It does this by adding mass timber to the existing Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit.

Reward research that brings costs down. This bill creates a 20% credit that covers every dollar a company spends on mass timber research, from new products to better production methods.

title: Congressman Tim Moore Announces Over $13 Million in FEMA Funding for Lake Lure, Rutherfordton, and Polk County
text:

title: Congresswoman Torres Introduces the Streamlining Affordable Housing Act To Lower Costs and Build Homes Faster
text:
Legislation would help states establish one-stop shops for affordable housing financing and consolidate housing agencies

Washington D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres introduced the Streamlining Affordable Housing Act, legislation to help states simplify affordable housing financing so projects can move forward faster and at lower cost. The bill would provide federal grants to help states consolidate their financing programs and establish one-stop shops where builders can access state funding through a single, universal application process.

Affordable housing developers must often stitch together funding from multiple public programs, each with separate requirements and timelines. Research from UC Berkeley’s Terner Center found that in California, each additional public funding source was associated with roughly four additional months in the development timeline and approximately $20,460 more in development costs per home.

To address this issue, Rep. Torres’ legislation authorizes $90 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029 to help states have the resources to reorganize fragmented financing systems, better coordinate programs, and make it easier for builders by creating a universal application for affordable housing financing. This past year, California took steps to create a new consolidated housing agency and a one-stop application process to reduce the delays and costs of navigating separate funding programs. Torres’ Streamlining Affordable Housing Act would help these and similar efforts, and support those already making progress.

“Families in the Inland Empire need homes they can afford, but too many affordable housing projects get stuck in a maze of applications and bureaucracy before construction can even begin,” said Congresswoman Norma Torres. “I’ve heard from developers who had to piece together nineteen sources of financing just to get one project off the ground. Every delay adds costs while families keep waiting. My bill would give states the resources to bring their financing programs together, create one application process, and get more affordable homes built so families can benefit.”

“We appreciate Congresswoman Torres’ longstanding advocacy for affordable housing and her willingness to listen to those working to build and preserve it. Her continued attention to the challenges facing our industry helps keep the need for affordable homes a priority.” — National CORE President Michael Ruane

“We applaud Representative Torres’ efforts to streamline access to affordable housing financing and support more efficient pathways to housing development. Reducing barriers and complexity in the funding process can help communities accelerate the development of much-needed affordable housing.” — Maria Razo, Executive Director, Housing Authority of the County of San Bernardino

The Streamlining Affordable Housing Act would establish a grant program at the Department of Housing and Urban Development that states and territories can opt into. The formula grants would help states:

Consolidate state financing entities and functions under one entity.

Create a one-stop shop by simplifying access to funding through a single, universal application process and technical assistance for builders.

The grants would reward states that undertake or complete both consolidation and application streamlining, unlocking additional flexibility for funds to also help improvements to permitting, zoning, regulatory processes, build state capacity, and access to low income Housing Tax Credits.

Participation would be voluntary, with formula funding, subject to appropriations, allocated among states that opt in based on a base grant of $500,000 and an additional amount based on the state’s population.

The bill would also require HUD to report to Congress on states’ use of the funding, identify best practices, and recommend further improvements.

title: Congressman Matt Van Epps Recognized by Americans for Prosperity with 2026 Pioneers for Prosperity Award
text:
NASHVILLE, TN – Americans for Prosperity (AFP) recognized Congressman Matt Van Epps with its 2026 Pioneers for Prosperity Award. The award recognizes members of Congress who actively advance policies that promote individual freedom, economic opportunity, and responsible government.

Click here to watch Rep. Van Epps accept this award on the Matt Murphy Show.

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Demands Immediate Passage of Aid to New Mexico Farmers Following Devastating Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 22, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to House leadership urging immediate passage of his CHILE Act, which would provide $5 billion in direct assistance to specialty crop farmers facing natural disasters and economic hardship. Following floods that wiped out chile crops in Southern New Mexico, this bill is more important than ever to provide necessary assistance before farmers are forced out of business.

“In New Mexico, these growers are the backbone of our agricultural communities, supporting generations of family farms and businesses. When these farmers lose their crops, the impacts ripple through the entire food supply chain, hurting farmworkers, local businesses, and families who depend on a reliable supply of American-grown food,” wrote Vasquez. “Without meaningful federal assistance, we risk losing family farms, weakening domestic food production, and becoming more dependent on foreign growers. Protecting our specialty crop farmers is not just an agricultural priority – it is a matter of food security and economic stability for the entire country.”

Read the full letter HERE.

The letter comes after devastating floods swept through southern New Mexico, destroying crops, damaging critical agricultural infrastructure, and threatening the livelihoods of family farmers. The flooding dealt another blow to New Mexico's chile, onion, and pecan growers, who were already grappling with extreme heat, prolonged drought, crop disease, shrinking market access, and rising production costs.

Despite these threats facing specialty crop farmers nationwide, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) lacks a permanent, dedicated disaster assistance framework for these producers. In addition to providing much needed assistance, the CHILE Act would create a dedicated program and protect our farmers from increasingly common extreme weather events and economic instability.

On October 4th, Rep. Vasquez hosted a meeting in Doña Ana County with local elected officials and visited families and farms impacted by the recent flooding. He visited Hatch, the McLeod/Garfield Dam, and surrounding areas to assess the impact of the flooding and what the community and farmers needed for recovery firsthand.

The CHILE is supported by the New Mexico Chile Association and Western Growers Association. The bill was introduced in the Senate by Ben Ray Lujan (D-NM).

This legislation builds on Rep. Vasquez’s long record of fighting for farmers and delivering real wins for New Mexico agriculture:

Rep. Vasquez secured several bipartisan winsin the process of passing this year’s Farm Bill through the House, including preventing the imposition of new red tape that would hinder growers’ access to the Specialty Crop Block Grant program.

Rep. Vasquez has held the USDA accountable countless times, including introducing his Honor Farmer Contracts Act, which ensures the USDA pays farmers what they’re owed.

He’s taken concerns directly from New Mexico’s farmers and ranchers to Washington and turned them into action through his Agriculture Advisory Group.

In January, Rep. Vasquez introduced the Farm and Family Relief Act to help farmers recover from chaos caused by the Administration’s reckless tariff policy.

title: Vindman Introduces Bill to Prevent Grocery Stores from Charging Shoppers Different Prices Based on Personal Data
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to prohibit large grocery retailers from using consumers’ personal information, facial recognition technology, and other surveillance tools to charge shoppers different prices for the same groceries.

With grocery prices already stretching household budgets, families across Virginia and the country are struggling to keep up with the rising cost of essentials. As Americans pay more for everything from milk and eggs to meat and produce, emerging pricing technologies threaten to make grocery shopping even more expensive and unpredictable.

The No Personal Data in Grocery Pricing Act would ban a practice known as surveillance pricing, in which retailers use personal data collected about shoppers, including their shopping habits, purchasing history, or other identifying information, to determine how much an individual consumer is charged for a product. The bill would also prohibit dynamic pricing at large grocery stores and their online platforms.

“Families across Virginia are already struggling with the rising cost of groceries. The last thing they need is to worry that the price of milk, eggs, or bread could change based on who’s buying it or what a retailer knows about them,” said Vindman. “Americans deserve to know they’re getting a fair price when they walk into a grocery store, without having their personal information used against them. Grocery stores should be focused on feeding families, not finding new ways to squeeze more money out of hardworking Americans. My legislation will put consumers first, protect their privacy, and ensure families aren’t paying more at the checkout counter because of invasive pricing practices.”

The legislation would apply to large retail food stores and their online shopping platforms, establishing protections against pricing practices that use personal information or automated systems to determine what consumers pay.

As grocery retailers increasingly adopt digital pricing systems and collect more consumer data, the legislation seeks to ensure that technological advancements do not come at the expense of consumer privacy, transparency, or affordability.
