title: Congressman Williams Op-Ed: If we want to lower costs for American families, it starts on the farm
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, the following Op-Ed by Congressman Roger Williams (TX-25), Chairman of the House Committee on Small Business, appeared in Agri-Pulse.

“The hardworking farmers and ranchers who feed our communities are facing rising production costs that ultimately reach the dinner tables of American families. When families across Texas’ 25th Congressional District reach out with affordability concerns, it’s clear Congress must act. That is why it is more important than ever to get the Farm Bill across the finish line.

“Since the 2018 Farm Bill was enacted, our farmers, economy, and communities have faced new challenges. Producers are facing rising input costs, changing markets, disease outbreaks, unpredictable weather, and the increasing cost of equipment and financing.

“A farmer doesn’t have the flexibility to decide on a piece of equipment, a new crop, or a future investment based on what Congress might do six months from now. Farming requires planning years in advance, and producers need a predictable and reliable framework before making investments that can determine the future and success of their operation.

“We must give our farmers the certainty they need to keep producing the safe, affordable food our families depend on.

“The House passed H.R.7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which addresses the needs of various crop producers across different regions. Under the leadership of Chairman Glenn Thompson and the House Agriculture Committee, this Farm Bill was shaped by more than 150 listening sessions with farmers. It expands access to credit, strengthens risk‑management tools, supports precision agriculture, and lowers energy costs in rural America. The legislation also invests in rural communities and reinforces conservation programs for working lands, which ensures American agriculture remains competitive in a challenging global landscape.

“More than 500 agricultural stakeholder organizations support H.R. 7567. This legislation’s broad support reflects exactly what I hear from producers throughout Texas.

“While these policies may sound like they are happening far away in Washington, they have very real impacts on rural America.

“One example is rural water. Section 6407 of the Farm Bill strengthens the Rural Decentralized Water Systems Program by supporting the construction, refurbishment, and servicing of well and wastewater systems, and authorizes funding for water-quality testing. For rural communities, access to safe and reliable water is a basic necessity.

“Agriculture is an important part of our small-business economy. As Chairman of the House Committee on Small Business, I have continued these conversations both back home in Texas and during hearings in Congress. I regularly hear from farmers and ranchers about the challenges they face and the policies that can help them grow their operations.

“I understand these challenges personally. I run a calf-cow operation and a ranch in Weatherford, Texas, and I have seen firsthand the work involved in raising livestock and caring for the land. Agriculture is part of the community I represent and the way of life I know.

“Agriculture is a major part of the future workforce we are building in Texas. In my district, Tarleton State University is preparing the next generation of agricultural leaders through programs in agribusiness, animal science, range and ranch management, sustainable agriculture, and other related fields.

“Last July, my House Republican colleagues and I passed H.R. 1, delivering significant tax relief for farmers, ranchers, and small businesses. Among its agricultural provisions, the law permanently increased the estate tax exemption to $15 million for individuals and $30 million for married couples, helping protect family farms and ranches from being forced to sell assets to pay estate taxes. It made 100 percent immediate expensing permanent, allowing producers to deduct the full cost of qualifying machinery and equipment purchases. For family farms all over Texas, these policies can save generations' worth of investment.

“We continued this work when passing the Working Families Tax Cuts, which strengthened the financial foundation for America's farmers and ranchers. The 2026 Farm Bill is the next step, giving producers the policy tools and certainty they need to build on those gains.

“If we want to lower costs for American families, it starts on the farm. Congress must finish the job and pass H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026.”

title: Banks Helps Secure Over $75 Million in Federal Grants for Indiana Rail Projects
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) applauded the Federal Railroad Administration’s selection of seven Indiana rail projects for up to $75,816,584 for the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program.

The funds will support rail infrastructure improvements across the state, including track and bridge rehabilitation, crossing upgrades, and equipment improvements.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Reliable rail infrastructure helps Indiana businesses move goods safely and efficiently and connects Hoosier communities to markets across the country. These investments will strengthen safety and reliability throughout the state.”

Northwest Indiana Rail Connectivity and Expansion Project ––– Up to $6,880,843: The Chesapeake and Indiana Railroad will replace ties, rehabilitate freight rail bridges, renew at-grade crossings, and rebuild approximately one mile of siding in Hanna, La Crosse, and Wellsboro.

Freight, Rail Safety & Service Reliability Improvement Project ––– Up to $2,880,000: The Chicago South Shore & South Bend Railroad will rehabilitate track in northern Indiana and northeastern Illinois, replace ties, rehabilitate switched, and upgrade four at-grade crossings.

Southeastern Indiana Corridor Improvement Project ––– Up to $7,915,813: The City of Madison Port Authority will support Madison Railroad improvements in North Vernon, including replacing approximately seven miles of rail, rehabilitating a siding, and installing a signal at a public crossing.

Freight Rail Revitalization Project in Indiana and Illinois ––– Up to $25,168,800: Evansville Western Railway will improve approximately 124.5 miles of rail line between Evansville and Okawville, Illinois. Work includes replacing rail and ties, installing hot bearing detectors, building a locomotive maintenance facility, and rehabilitating 12 locomotives.

Coal and Corn in Hoosier Land Project ––– Up to $14,544,000: The RailTex, Inc. award supports a project submitted on behalf of Indiana Southern Railroad. The Project will improve approximately 100 miles of track between Indianapolis and Evansville, including rail, ties, crossings, signals, and bridges.

Program for Operation Workflows & Equipment Reliability ––– Up to $15,231,696: Elkhart and Western Railroad will help Patriot Rail’s locomotive fleet across 15 rail properties in 17 states.

New Era Railroad State of Good Repair and Safety Improvement Project ––– Up to $3,195,432:New Era Railroad will rehabilitate approximately 12 miles of track in Wells, Huntington, and Grant Counties, replace ties, place ballast, and rehabilitate two at-grade crossings.

Background:

The CRISI program provides grants for rail projects that improve safety, efficiency, and reliability; the seven Indiana projects were selected for project development, final design, and construction. The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) FY 2025-2026 CRISI selections include the project descriptions and maximum grant amounts.

title: Bennet Leads Colorado Lawmakers to Demand Trump Administration Maintain an Effective & Functional Recreation.gov Online Booking System
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Conservation, Forestry, Natural Resources, and Biotechnology, led Senator John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) and Representatives Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Brittany Pettersen (D-Colo.), Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), Jeff Hurd (R-Colo.), and Jeff Crank (R-Colo.) in calling on the U.S. Department of Agriculture and the U.S. Department of the Interior to ensure the effectiveness and functionality of the Recreation.gov website as the agencies’ current contract ends and a new bidding process begins.

Recreation.gov is the primary link between millions of Americans and campgrounds, permits, passes, and other recreation opportunities on public lands. In Colorado, this website serves as an important connection between recreationists and the state’s public lands, National Parks, and National Forests, which contribute to an over $18 billion outdoor recreation economy.

Americans should have easy, unobstructed access to recreational opportunities on public lands, but many individuals have reported extreme challenges when attempting to obtain passes and permits due to autonomous bots and third-party actors that instantly reserve sought-after campsites, permits, and other recreation opportunities. With the current Recreation.gov contract expiring next year, it is important to identify the strengths and shortcomings of the current system, ensure operational continuity, and push for improvements that guarantee Americans’ seamless access to their public lands.

“Any major change to the Recreation.gov system should be carefully evaluated to ensure it benefits taxpayers, improves service quality, maintains operational continuity, and avoids reducing the capabilities upon which land managers and visitors currently rely. In addition, while the system must continue to evolve to address changing conditions – including the reported use of autonomous bots by third-party actors that unfairly obtain reservations at the expense of the American public – those improvements should be pursued in a way that preserves continuity for visitors and land managers alike,” wrote the lawmakers.

Bennet is a passionate advocate for public lands and safeguarding outdoor recreation. In February 2025, he led Hickenlooper and Neguse to reintroduce the Colorado Outdoor Recreation and Economy (CORE) Act. This legislation protects approximately 420,000 acres of public land in Colorado, establishes new wilderness areas, and safeguards existing outdoor recreation opportunities to boost the economy for future generations. That same month, Bennet joined Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.) and Roger Marshall (R-Kan.) to introduce the Voluntary Public Access Improvement Act, which would expand access to public lands for hunting, fishing, hiking, and other outdoor activities.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Undersecretary Boren and Deputy Secretary MacGregor:

We write to highlight the importance of maintaining an effective and functional Recreation.gov website. Created almost ten years ago, millions of Americans now use Recreation.gov every year to access campgrounds, permits, passes, and other recreation opportunities on federal lands. In Colorado, Recreation.gov enables Americans from all over the country to visit our state’s public lands, National Parks, and National Forests, facilitating the state’s $18.1 billion outdoor recreation economy. As the Departments’ reach the end of the current Recreation.gov contract, we urge you to ensure the system is able to continue serving as a reliable resource for Americans looking to take advantage of their public lands.

Any major change to the Recreation.gov system should be carefully evaluated to ensure it benefits taxpayers, improves service quality, maintains operational continuity, and avoids reducing the capabilities upon which land managers and visitors currently rely. In addition, while the system must continue to evolve to address changing conditions – including the reported use of autonomous bots by third-party actors that unfairly obtain reservations at the expense of the American public – those improvements should be pursued in a way that preserves continuity for visitors and land managers alike.

To that end, we respectfully request that you provide responses to the following questions:

Is the recompete process expected to result in a material change to the Recreation.gov system, including the types of services offered?

What steps is the Administration taking to ensure reliable access to Recreation.gov for all users as the recompete process begins?

What efforts are being developed or implemented to combat automated bots, improve communication about reservation availability and high-demand sites, and provide guidance on alternative destinations?

How are Administration officials engaging with the Recreation One Stop program office and industry partners to identify opportunities to improve the system?

Have DOI and USDA officials considered deviating from the current unified platform?

We look forward to working with you to ensure fair and open competition during the rebid process, and to guarantee Recreation.gov remains modern, reliable, secure, and responsive to the needs of the American people and the federal land managers who serve them.

title: Blumenthal Announces Congressional Inquiry into Starlink & Starshield
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), announced today a new inquiry into SpaceX’s Starlink and Starshield technologies, including how the taxpayer-funded military communications capability was degraded for Ukraine without notice, the process for making that decision, and the future implications of the Department of Defense’s singular dependence on SpaceX for critical satellite communications. Blumenthal’s letters to Hegseth and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk follow new reporting in the Wall Street Journal that Elon Musk ordered a restriction in Ukraine’s connectivity to these critical battlefield technologies following a conversation with President Donald Trump.

In a letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Blumenthal wrote: “A decision to degrade service, applied quickly and without notice, has disabled missions across an entire military theater. Whether that change was directed by the White House, DoD, or SpaceX, the episode raises urgent questions about who possesses the technical and legal authority to alter these capabilities, what safeguards govern that authority, and whether DoD has sufficient alternatives if SpaceX-provided services become unavailable.”

“Congress has a responsibility to ensure that capabilities paid for by the American people are governed by clear, lawful and accountable processes, and that DoD is not dependent on any single company for communications that our armed forces need to fight and survive.”

In a letter to Musk, Blumenthal asked for information about SpaceX’s contracts with the Department of Defense as well as the company’s ability to interfere with or alter access to Starshield. Last week, Blumenthal wrote SpaceX Acting General Counsel David Harris seeking additional answers about any involvement SpaceX may have had in Ukraine’s restricted access to Starshield as well as the role SpaceX plays in Ukraine’s ongoing access to Starlink technology.

The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Hegseth is available here. The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Musk is available here and below.

Mr. Musk,

On October 13, the Ukrainian military's access to SpaceX's Starshield satellite communications service was restricted without notice and new reporting indicates that it was at your direction.[1] This decision to limit critical technology for a key ally not only put Ukrainian forces at risk and their people in peril, but raises serious questions about who controls critical capabilities the U.S. government has spent billions of dollars to procure, how decisions to restrict it are made, and whether the U.S. Government’s reliance on SpaceX could expose U.S. forces to similar disruptions.[2] The Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (the “Subcommittee”) is opening an inquiry into the U.S. Government’s interaction with and reliance upon SpaceX technology including Starlink satellite services and Starshield. Accordingly, I write to request information and documents regarding not just the decision to limit Ukraine’s access to Starshield, but the federal government’s access to and dependance on Starlink and Starshield technology to protect our national security.

In the late evening of October 13, Ukrainian forces lost critical access to Starshield—the military-grade counterpart to SpaceX's Starlink network—after their access to speeds at which equipment could stay connected to the network was capped.[3] According to Ukrainian officials, devices using Starshield services stopped functioning properly when mounted on drones and other fast-moving platforms, all while Russia unleashed dozens of ballistic missiles across the country.[4] Ukraine said it received no advance warning and that several missions failed as a result.[5] On October 19, President Zelenskyy confirmed to me on a call that access to critical Starlink services remains degraded, including for systems traveling at speeds above 100 miles per hour, impairing Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones.

The public record now contains conflicting accounts of both who ordered the restriction and who implemented it. Early reporting initially attributed the restriction to SpaceX. On October 14, however, you asserted that Starshield systems are “owned and controlled by the US government,” and that limits on their use are set by the U.S. military and, ultimately, the President.[6] On October 15, 2026, Reuters cited two U.S. officials in reporting that the order to limit Ukraine's Starshield service originated inside the White House and was conveyed to DoD leadership.[7] A senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Kyiv was informed it was a White House decision.[8] However, a senior U.S. official, by contrast, said the President made no such request.[9] On October 16, President Trump further denied that the United States imposed any limit on Ukraine's Starshield access, adding to the conflicting public accounts of what occurred.[10] That same day, The Telegraph reported that it was you who pitched President Trump on implementing a speed cap, and that the President subsequently “agreed.”[11] New reporting now confirms that you spoke with the President and several other senior administration officials prior to and after imposing the speed cap.[12]

Satellite communications are no longer simply a support function. They now guide drones, communicate targeting data, coordinate logistics, and connect commanders and forces in the field.[13] DoD and the Intelligence Community have awarded SpaceX billions of dollars for national security capabilities, including Starlink and Starshield services, dedicated military satellite systems, and a classified reconnaissance constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office.[14]

The events in Ukraine show how a single point of control can be turned against the forces that depend on it. A decision to degrade service, applied quickly and without notice, has disabled missions across an entire military theater. Whether that change was directed by the White House, DoD, or SpaceX, the episode raises urgent questions about who possesses the technical and legal authority to alter these capabilities and what safeguards govern that authority.

Congress has a responsibility to ensure that capabilities paid for by the American people are governed by clear, lawful and accountable processes. To assist the Subcommittee’s understanding of these events and the federal government’s relationship with SpaceX as it relates to Starlink and Starshield, please provide written answers to the following questions by November 5, 2026.

From October 10 to October 15, 2026, please describe any Starshield or Starlink capabilities or access points that were restricted for Ukrainian assets, including the date the restriction went into place and the duration of that restriction.

For each restriction identified in response to Question 1, please identify all personnel involved in or notified of the decision to restrict Starshield services, including for example, the reported restriction affecting devices traveling faster than 100 mph. In the event that SpaceX was not directly involved in the decision, please detail when and how SpaceX was notified of that decision and how the directive to restrict capabilities was communicated to SpaceX.

For each restriction listed in response to Question 1, please describe the process for implementing the restriction, whether officials at SpaceX carried out the implementation, who those officials were, and, to the extent that DoD personnel were involved in the implementation, please describe their roles and list their names and titles.

Was Ukraine notified in advance of any changes to their ability to access Starshield? If not, why not? What protocols govern notice to partners before their access to U.S.-provided Starshield capabilities is changed?

Under SpaceX’s contracts with DoD, who holds the authority to activate, restrict, geofence, or shut off Starshield service, and under what conditions?

Can SpaceX technically alter, geofence or degrade Starshield service for U.S. or partner forces, without DoD authorization?

What is the legal and contractual basis for Ukraine's use of Starshield, and who has authority to modify or revoke that access?

Provide the total value of all SpaceX contracts, task orders, and other transactions with the U.S. Government for Starlink and Starshield services, terminals, and dedicated satellites since fiscal year 2020, by component and fiscal year. Provide all contract numbers, and indicate which awards were made on a sole-source basis and what justification was provided for that decision.

Please describe the extent to which Starshield is independent of the commercial Starlink network? Have outages or disruptions affected both at the same time, and what were the effects on U.S. or partner operations?

Please also produce the following documents and communications, for the period from January 1, 2026, to the present unless otherwise noted:

All Records[15] documenting, approving, or otherwise referring to the restriction of Ukraine’s access to Starlink or Starshield.

All communications, including emails, attachments, transmitted documents, text and messaging-app messages, memoranda, and notes of meetings or calls, between SpaceX and DoD, the Executive Office of the President, including the National Security Council, referring or related to any restriction or limitation of Ukraine's access to Starshield or Starlink.

All communications between SpaceX and the Government of Ukraine concerning any restrictions placed on their access to Starshield.

All contracts, task orders, transaction agreements, and modifications between SpaceX and DoD for Starlink or Starshield services, terminals, or satellites since fiscal year 2020 including any provisions on control, access, or service termination, and any sole-source justifications.

In addition, I request that SpaceX officials with direct knowledge of the Starshield restriction brief the Subcommittee no later than November 12, 2026. Classified material may be segregated and provided separately through appropriate channels. Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

title: Blumenthal Investigates Tether's Multimillion-Dollar Payment to Consulting Firm Owned by White House Official Who Previously Led Crypto Policy
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), today demanded answers from Tether over its reported multimillion-dollar payment to a consulting firm co-founded and controlled by Bo Hines, who served as the Executive Director of the White House Council of Advisers for Digital Assets. In a letter sent today to Tether CEO Paolo Ardonio, Blumenthal raised concerns that Tether reportedly paid millions of dollars to a business partially controlled by the White House official responsible for cryptocurrency policy, while that same official lobbied for loopholes in legislation on its behalf.

“According to The Wall Street Journal, in May 2025, Tether entered into a deal with the small consulting and investment firm Nxum to develop a “strategic brand and public affairs plan” for the stablecoin issuer…However, Nxum did have one particular advantage: its cofounder, Bo Hines, had been appointed ‘Executive Director of the Presidential Council of Advisers for Digital Assets’ for the Trump Administration the prior December and had recently begun working on stablecoin legislation for the White House,” Blumenthal wrote.

Blumenthal continued, “According to The Wall Street Journal, as the White House dropped enforcement actions against cryptocurrency firms and lobbied Congress for legislation favorable to the industry, over $6 million flowed into Nxum from Tether —all while Bo Hines sought special exemptions and dispensation on behalf of the firm…While Hines failed to divest his one-third stake in Nxum, according to messages seen by The Wall Street Journal, he worked closely over encrypted messaging applications with Nxum to coordinate lobbying, advocacy, and browbeating of members of Congress that were opposed to, or had sought changes to, pending stablecoin legislation.”

Blumenthal continued, “The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns, indicating that Tether was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety of issuing payments to a current White House official with such a direct role in shaping cryptocurrency legislation that was instrumental to its business.”

“Tether’s alleged multimillion-dollar payment to a firm controlled by the White House official primarily responsible for cryptocurrency policy implicates federal ethics, anticorruption, and lobbying laws,” Blumenthal concluded.

In a similar letter sent today to the CEO of Nxum Group, Todd Hines, Blumenthal sought records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying between Nxum, Bo Hines, and all associated parties.

As PSI Ranking Member, Blumenthal is leading an inquiry into the illicit use of cryptocurrencies and the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms. As part of this investigation, Blumenthal recently released a report detailing how Tether and its dollar-pegged stablecoin have become a significant financial lifeline within Iran’s shadow banking network. A copy of PSI’s report, “Tethered to Terrorism: Crypto & Iran’s Shadow Banking Network,” is available here.

The full text of today’s letter to Tether is available here and below. Blumenthal’s letter to Nxum Group is available here.

Dear Mr. Ardoino, Mr. Hines:

The Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (“PSI” or the “Subcommittee”) Minority is conducting an ongoing inquiry into the illicit use of cryptocurrencies and the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms. Recent reporting has revealed that Tether paid millions of dollars to a business partially controlled by the White House official responsible for cryptocurrency policy, while that same official lobbied for loopholes in legislation on its behalf. I therefore write to demand that you provide the Subcommittee with all records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying with the firm, Nxum, its cofounder Bo Hines, and all associated parties.

According to The Wall Street Journal, in May 2025, Tether entered into a deal with the small consulting and investment firm Nxum to develop a “strategic brand and public affairs plan” for the stablecoin issuer. Nxum had little history providing consulting services for successful cryptocurrency firms, previously having attempted to market a marijuana-themed digital asset and a Trump-themed meme coin, both of which failed. However, Nxum did have one particular advantage: its cofounder, Bo Hines, had been appointed “Digital Asset Policy Advisor” for the Trump Administration the prior December and had recently begun working on stablecoin legislation for the White House.

According to the WSJ, as the White House dropped enforcement actions against cryptocurrency firms and lobbied Congress for legislation favorable to the industry, over $6 million flowed into Nxum from Tether —all while Bo Hines sought special exemptions and dispensation on behalf of the firm. In May 2025, Tether agreed to pay Nxum $415,000 a month after the consulting firm had pitched it a “strategic lobbying and a full scale public relations and media awareness campaign.” While Hines failed to divest his one-third stake in Nxum, according to messages seen by the WSJ, he worked closely over encrypted messaging applications with Nxum to coordinate lobbying, advocacy, and browbeating of members of Congress that were opposed to, or had sought changes to, pending stablecoin legislation. Those messages also reportedly demonstrate that Tether was directly coordinating Nxum’s lobbying efforts on the GENIUS Act which would regulate stablecoins, with CEO Paolo Ardoino demanding that Nxum “obliterate” the legislation’s opponents. Mr. Hines personally lobbied for changes to the GENIUS Act that would predominantly benefit Tether by allowing it to continue operating outside of the United States and providing it more time to come into compliance with regulations—provisions that have become known as the “Tether loophole.”

The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns, indicating that Tether was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety of issuing payments to a current White House official with such a direct role in shaping cryptocurrency legislation that was instrumental to its business. Rather than directly contracting with Mr. Hines’s firm, Tether assigned its contract and sent its payments in cryptocurrency through a marketing firm, Notorious, that then passed to Nxum, after which it was split three ways and transferred again. As soon as Hines left the White House, Tether began to directly contract with and send payments to Nxum. Nxum later allegedly offered the director of Notorious over $300,000 and a stake in future Tether payments in return for a nondisclosure agreement. Within days of leaving the White House, Tether announced that it had hired Mr. Hines, ultimately naming him the CEO of its new Tether U.S. operations. These lucrative arrangements allowed Mr. Hines a new lifestyle that includes traveling by private jet.

Tether’s alleged multimillion-dollar payment to a firm controlled by the White House official primarily responsible for cryptocurrency policy implicates federal ethics, anticorruption, and lobbying laws. To assist the Subcommittee in its inquiry, please provide responses to the following requests for records and information by November 6, 2026:

1.) When did Tether first consider a potential business partnership with Nxum, and what were the circumstances under which Nxum began to do business with Tether?

a. Please provide a breakdown of all payments provided by Tether to Nxum, Notorious, or any individuals affiliated with either entity, including the date of payment, payment method, and any wallet addresses associated with cryptocurrency transactions.[JG2.1]

b. Please describe all consulting and lobbying services that Nxum has provided to Tether, regardless of whether those activities were specified under the written terms of any contract between the firms.

2.) Why did Tether use Notorious and its CEO Peter Vincer as an intermediary for its business partnership with Nxum? Why did Tether and Nxum begin to directly contract after Mr. Hines left the White House, and why did the firms later seek a nondisclosure agreement from Mr. Vincer?

3.) According to The Wall Street Journal, Mr. Hines coordinated with Mr. Vincer on the change of contract from Notorious to directly contracting to Nxum, even writing him “everyone has agreed that you are never to be f—ed.” What awareness or involvement did Mr. Hines have regarding Tether’s business relationship between Nxum, Mr. Vincer, and Notorious prior, during, and after any agreement?

4.) According to The Wall Street Journal, Nxum has recently sought further investment with the claim that Tether plans to purchase 25% stake in Nxum for $56 million. What is the current relationship between Nxum and Tether, and have the two firms discussed Tether potentially taking a stake in Nxum?

5.) Please provide all records, including communications and contracts, relating to any business dealings with Nxum. This includes, but is not limited to, any negotiations, draft contracts, or agreements between the firms, records involving or relating to Bo Hines, discussion of White House or state and federal regulators, lobbying on Tether’s behalf, or compliance with any laws and regulations applicable to Tether.

6.) Please provide all records, including communications and contracts, between Tether and Mr. Vincer and his firm Notorious. This includes, but is not limited to, any negotiations, draft contracts, or agreements related to Tether’s partnership with Nxum, coordination of payments, discussions of Mr. Vincer’s role in the firms’ partnership, the terminations of that role, and any request or negotiation over a nondisclosure agreement.

7.) Please provide all records relating to communications and contracts with Bo Hines between January 20, 2025 and August 9, 2025. This includes, but is not limited to, any discussion of White House or state and federal regulators or regulations, lobbying on Tether’s behalf or regarding cryptocurrencies, or Mr. Hines’ employment after leaving the White House.

Please contact the Subcommittee if you have any questions about responding to these requests.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: Blumenthal, Tonko, & Foushee Press Sportsbooks & Prediction Markets on Whether VIP Programs are Fueling Addiction
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and U.S. Representatives Paul Tonko (D-NY) and Valerie Foushee (D-NC) today demanded answers from major sportsbooks and prediction markets about their VIP programs and other manipulative rewards or promotions. In letters sent today to BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, Fanatics, Kalshi, and Polymarket, Blumenthal, Tonko, and Foushee sought details about the companies’ VIP programs, raising concerns about the exploitation of vulnerable bettors.

“As repeated stories from exploited gamblers and media reports have vividly documented, VIP programs are driving the gambling industry’s most susceptible customers into debt and addiction through rewards tied to waging ever-increasing amounts of money. The dangling of perks—which include access to exclusive events, videos from celebrities and athletes, and tickets to the Super Bowl—distract bettors from their financial losses and encourage betting when they otherwise would not,” the lawmakers wrote in a letter to BetMGM CEO Adam Greenblatt.

The lawmakers continued, “Unsurprisingly, VIP programs have been at the center of controversy in both independent investigations as well as litigation filed by victims of the gambling industry. FanDuel, for instance, offered one of its VIP customers a personal message from Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Bryce Harper at the height of their addiction. In addition, recent reporting from ProPublica revealed that DraftKings rewarded a journalist who imitated clear signs of problem gambling—including chasing losses, placing nonstop microbets, and betting on obscure events—with a VIP membership. Making matters worse, prediction markets are now enticing bettors with similar reward programs.”

“It is wholly unacceptable that the gambling industry profits at the expense of its most vulnerable customers’ financial and mental well-being,” the Senators concluded.

Blumenthal, Tonko, and Foushee have repeatedly pressed FanDuel about its reported use of celebrity promotional videos to exploit vulnerable consumers and entice addicts to further gamble. Today, the lawmakers are seeking answers about sportsbooks’ and prediction markets’ use of VIP programs, including whether the companies use artificial intelligence to track and target problem gamblers.

The text of the lawmakers’ letter to BetMGM is available below. Copies of letters sent today to BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, Fanatics, Kalshi, and Polymarket are available here.

Dear Mr. Greenblatt,

We write regarding the gambling industry’s widely documented exploitation of vulnerable bettors through predatory VIP programs. We are deeply concerned that BetMGM may be exploiting these individuals through BetMGM Rewards, its VIP program, and write to demand answers about this program, as well as any other manipulative rewards or promotions.

As repeated stories from exploited gamblers and media reports have vividly documented, VIP programs are driving the gambling industry’s most susceptible customers into debt and addiction through rewards tied to waging ever increasing amounts of money. The dangling of perks—which include access to exclusive events, videos from celebrities and athletes, and tickets to the Super Bowl—distract bettors from their financial losses and encourage betting when they otherwise would not.[1] Gambling companies are even using artificial intelligence to identify and target gamblers on a losing streak with promotions to continue reckless gambling.[2] In addition, gambling companies often assign these bettors an account manager to coordinate VIP perks. These managers further fuel the gambling industry’s exploitation by pushing rewards and non-stop promotions to bettors who exhibit clear signs of gambling addiction, even messaging them up to 100 times a day.[3]

Unsurprisingly, VIP programs have been at the center of controversy in both independent investigations as well as litigation filed by victims of the gambling industry. FanDuel, for instance, offered one of its VIP customers a personal message from Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Bryce Harper at the height of their addiction. In addition, recent reporting from ProPublica revealed that DraftKings rewarded a journalist who imitated clear signs of problem gambling—including chasing losses, placing nonstop microbets, and betting on obscure events—with a VIP membership.[4] Making matters worse, prediction markets are now enticing bettors with similar reward programs. For example, Kalshi launched its Platinum program to offer VIP customers with perks including merchandise, access to special events, and account managers.[5] This is especially concerning considering that prediction markets are actively flouting safeguards established by state gambling authorities and offering their products in states where sports betting is not legal.

It is wholly unacceptable that the gambling industry profits at the expense of its most vulnerable customers’ financial and mental well-being. Given the clear harms stemming from VIP programs such as BetMGM Rewards, we demand answers to the following questions no later than November 5, 2026:

Please provide the following information about enrollment and participation in BetMGM Rewards:

How many bettors are enrolled in BetMGM Rewards?

What is the average loss/gain of bettors in BetMGM Rewards over the six-month period prior to being enrolled in the program?

What is the average loss/gain of bettors in BetMGM Rewards after being enrolled in the program?

How many bettors in BetMGM Rewards have attempted to cut back their betting activity or close their accounts but were instead offered exclusive perks or offers? How many decided to keep betting after such offers?

How much does BetMGM earn in revenue from its VIP program?

Please fully list the perks, offers, and services that BetMGM has provided bettors in BetMGM Rewards, including whether it has ever sent videos from players or other celebrities to its customers to keep them engaged in gambling on the platform?

Please describe the review process customers must undergo before BetMGM offers them a VIP membership, including if BetMGM evaluates:

the total amount the customer had wagered beforehand and the amount that they had won or lost;

whether the customer had ever requested to suspend their account, pause notifications, or take action to limit their gambling on the platform;

whether the customer had ever exhibited any signs of problem gambling, regardless of if they sought help;

whether the customer had exhibited significant financial losses or economic hardship.

Does BetMGM ever coach or train its VIP managers to develop personal relationships with their clients in order to encourage more gambling?

Does BetMGM use artificial intelligence to track and target gamblers with perks and predatory promotions? If so, please describe how AI is used in this manner and what data about a bettor is used for these purposes.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

-30-

title: Cassidy: Higher Social Security COLA Makes Action on Insolvency Even More Urgent
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) joined Fox Business to discuss Social Security’s projected insolvency in six years, with a proposed benefit cut of up to 28.5 percent. Cassidy also discussed the 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment, which is $75 more per beneficiary. Cassidy warned that the increase in benefits means the Social Security Trust Fund could run out of money sooner than predicted if Congress fails to act.

“We now have five and a half years until the trust fund goes empty, at which point by law, there will be a 28.5 percent benefit cut, or Congress ignores the law and starts to borrow money like crazy to pay benefits. The clock is ticking,” said Dr. Cassidy.

“The fact that the COLA is that much higher obviously reflects recent inflation, but I think it’s going to drain the trust fund that much faster,” continued Dr. Cassidy.

Background

Cassidy has been outspoken in the media on the need to rescue Social Security from insolvency. He has outlined his plan to create a sovereign wealth fund independent of the Social Security Trust Fund. He has written extensively on his proposal in the Washington Post, the Wall Street Journal, State Affairs, and the Washington Examiner. On the U.S. Senate floor, Cassidy has repeatedly called on Congress to act to save the program, and challenged the U.S. Senate to stop being good politicians and start being good senators.

title: ICYMI: Cassidy, Letchuman Publish JAMA Viewpoint Calling on Congress to Reduce Overspending in Medicare Advantage
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA), and Sunjay Letchuman, M.D., published a Viewpoint in JAMA today outlining legislative reforms to reduce coding-related overpayments in Medicare Advantage. More seniors are now enrolled in Medicare Advantage than Traditional Medicare, and total Medicare spending continues to rise. In 2024, the U.S. spent over $1.1 trillion on Medicare, and taxpayers pay the price when overpayments to insurance companies push that number higher. Dr. Cassidy and Dr. Letchuman argue that addressing coding-related overpayments, or “upcoding,” is a critical first step toward a more sustainable Medicare program.

Read the full Viewpoint here or excerpts below:

For many years, the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) has found that Medicare spends substantially more for beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Advantage than it would have spent if those same beneficiaries were in traditional fee-for-service Medicare. In one of its most recent analyses, MedPAC estimated that total payments average 120% of what traditional Medicare would have spent for comparable beneficiaries. Much of this overpayment is attributed to more intensive diagnosis coding in Medicare Advantage and is thus called upcoding.

…

First, CMS should use 2 years of diagnostic data in the traditional Medicare beneficiary population to calculate the risk score against which the Medicare Advantage enrollee is compared… The Congressional Budget Office estimates this policy would reduce overspending by $124 billion over 10 years.

…

The second reform relates to in-home health risk assessments. During these assessments, a nurse or other clinician visits a Medicare Advantage enrollee’s home and administers questionnaires or uses diagnostic tools to screen for conditions such as depression or peripheral artery disease. Diagnoses that result from these visits are used for risk adjustment even when not confirmed by a physician or linked to subsequent treatment. The Office of Inspector General found that such diagnoses generated $3.5 billion in risk adjusted payments in 2023. CMS should exclude these diagnoses from counting toward a patient’s health status unless a physician confirms them or they are reflected in subsequent treatment.

…

The context for the third reform is that Congress requires CMS to apply a downward adjustment to Medicare Advantage risk scores to offset more intensive coding, with a statutory minimum of 5.9 percent. CMS has applied only this minimum every year since it took effect. This should be reformed in two ways. First, CMS should update the adjustment annually rather than leaving it fixed at the statutory minimum. The Congressional Budget Office estimates that increasing the minimum risk score reduction to 8 percent would reduce overspending by $159 billion over ten years. Second, Congress should direct CMS to apply the coding adjustment at the plan level rather than uniformly, starting with a small number of coding-intensity tiers, so that plans that code more aggressively receive a larger downward adjustment.

title: Daines Introduces Groundbreaking Crypto Legislation to Protect American Taxpayers
text:
“ADAPT Act” Updates Tax Code, Closes Loopholes, Protects American Innovation

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today introduced the “Aligning Digital Assets with Principles of Taxation (ADAPT) Act,” comprehensive legislation to modernize the federal tax treatment of digital assets and establish clearer, more administrable rules for taxpayers, businesses and the Internal Revenue Service. The bill provides tailored rules where blockchain technology presents genuinely different tax issues, applies familiar tax principles where digital assets function like traditional financial assets, and puts safeguards in place to protect the tax base. By providing taxpayers with tax certainty and clear rules of the road, the bill will remove barriers that make everyday use of regulated stablecoins and blockchain networks impractical to ensure investment and innovation occurs here at home.

Senators Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) and Tim Scott (R-S.C.) joined Daines in introducing the legislation.

“Digital assets have changed dramatically, but our tax code hasn’t kept up, and hardworking Americans are paying the price. The “Adapt Act” will modernize the Internal Revenue Code and make digital assets more accessible for everyday use by reducing unnecessary complexity, increasing compliance, protecting the tax base and supporting U.S. digital asset innovation. As America continues to lead in the development of cutting-edge technology, it’s critical that we provide clear guardrails to protect American taxpayers and promote innovation,” said Daines.

“Washington’s confusing, outdated tax rules have kept digital asset holders and businesses in the dark for decades. The ecosystem desperately needs a common-sense approach that treats crypto fairly while supporting its integration into the U.S. economy, and this legislation takes a step in the right direction,” ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​said Moreno.

“In a world where digital assets are evolving by the day, it is important that we have an up-to-date tax code that reflects our modern economy. By creating clear guidelines, closing loopholes, and applying the same tax rules to traditional securities and digital assets, the ADAPT Act will protect Americans’ investments and keep innovation on American soil,” said Scott.

Read the bill text HERE.

Background:

The ADAPT Act reforms the Internal Revenue Code by:

Making everyday payments workable by ending gain-or-loss tracking when Americans use GENIUS Act-regulated dollar stablecoins to buy goods and services, and by exempting network fees of $10 or less.

Providing parity with traditional financial assets by extending existing rules for securities and commodities, including securities-lending treatment, the mark-to-market election for dealers and traders, the trading safe harbor for foreign investors, and the streamlined rules for charitable gifts of publicly traded stock.

Closing loopholes by applying the wash sale and constructive sale rules to digital assets and by treating digital asset trading businesses the same as securities and commodities traders under the section 199A deduction.

Clarifies the treatment of digital asset investment trusts that stake proof-of-stake assets and expands qualifying-income rules for publicly traded partnerships to include specified digital asset income while excluding income from operating digital asset financial-services businesses.

Read a one-pager on the bill HERE and section-by-section HERE.

Statements of Support:

“We’re grateful to Senator Daines, Senator Scott, Senator Lummis, Senator Moreno, and the Senate Finance Committee for taking on the need for greater clarity in digital asset tax policy. Current tax rules were not written with digital assets in mind, and we appreciate their work to modernize the tax code and establish clearer, more practical rules for taxpayers and businesses.”— Lawrence Zlatkin, Vice President of Tax, Coinbase

“The introduction of the ADAPT Act marks an important moment for digital asset tax policy in the Senate, and reflects Senator Daines’ and his team’s thoughtful engagement on these issues. Americans who use digital assets have been left to navigate outdated and unclear guidance for far too long. We appreciate Senator Daines’ leadership in putting forward a concrete framework to change that. Our members are examining the legislation in detail, and we welcome the opportunity to continue working with Senator Daines and the Finance Committee as the digital asset tax eﬀorts advance. Alongside the progress made by the House Ways and Means Committee, the ADAPT Act brings Congress one step closer to comprehensive digital asset tax legislation, and we look forward to continued momentum in both chambers.”— Summer Mersinger, CEO, Blockchain Association

“Americans who use digital assets deserve tax rules that are clear, fair, and built for how this technology actually works. The ADAPT Act advances that goal. We thank Senator Daines and his colleagues for their leadership and stand ready to help move it forward.”— Ji Hun Kim, CEO, Crypto Council for Innovation.

“Fidelity Investments applauds Senator Daines for introducing the Aligning Digital Assets with Principles of Taxation Act (ADAPT) and appreciates the effort to advance a more practical and predictable tax framework for digital assets. Clear and workable tax rules are essential to fostering innovation, supporting responsible user adoption, and strengthening the United States’ position as a leader in the evolving digital asset marketplace. Fidelity looks forward to engaging with the Senate Finance Committee as this important legislation moves forward.” – Fidelity Investments

“The Aligning Digital Assets with Principles of Taxation (ADAPT) Act brings long-overdue clarity to how digital assets are taxed in the United States. The legislation would modernize the tax code to keep pace with digital asset innovation. With clear tax rules, Americans can comply with confidence, innovators can keep building here at home, and the United States can lead the global digital economy. The Digital Chamber applauds Senator Daines for introducing this critical legislation and looks forward to working with Congress to advance it.”— The Digital Chamber

title: Durbin, Grassley Urge Defense Secretary Hegseth, Secretary Of State Rubio To Swiftly Obligate Congressionally Appropriated Baltic Security Initiative Funding
text:
As Russian aggression intensifies around the Baltic region, the Senators request the funds be disbursed by the end of the year

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) and U.S. Senator Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Co-Chairs of the Senate Baltic Freedom Caucus, today sent a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging them to swiftly obligate Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Congressionally appropriated funds for the Baltic Security Initiative (BSI) as Russia intensifies its aggression around the Baltic region. Durbin and Grassley sent a letter in May requesting Hegseth and Rubio immediately release the stalled funds.

The Senators wrote, “We write to follow up on Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Congressionally appropriated funds for the Baltic Security Initiative (BSI). Since 2021, the BSI has enhanced the defense capabilities and interoperability of our Baltic allies. We urge you to ensure the swift obligation of this funding and execution of programs considering intensified Russian aggression in the region against key frontline allies.”

The Senators continued, “We welcome the BSI spend plan provided by the Department of Defense (DoD) on May 29, 2026, which targets investments in integrated defense, maritime security, irregular warfare, and other critical capabilities as required by statute. On September 15, a second update from DoD indicated that BSI was prioritized for notification and in its final stages of coordination, including with the Department of State. While this is important progress, escalating Russian threats, specifically against the Baltic States, demand more urgent U.S. security assistance.”

The Senators concluded, “In light of recent airspace incursions, gray-zone tactics, and heightened nuclear warnings against the Baltics, accelerating the delivery of assistance under the BSI must be a priority. We urge disbursement by the end of the calendar year and ask that you provide an update on such plans no later than November 19, 2026.”

In addition to Durbin and Grassley, the letter is signed by U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Cornyn (R-TX), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Michael Bennet (D-CO), and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ).

In a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing earlier this year, Durbin questioned Secretary Hegseth and Joint Chiefs of Staff General Dan Caine about the funds.

Durbin and Grassley have been champions in the Senate for the Baltic nations. Earlier this year, they introduced the Baltic Security Assessment Act of 2026, legislation that requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, to submit a report to the House and Senate Committees on Armed Services, Foreign Relations and Affairs, and Appropriations on emerging threats posed to the Baltic countries—Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.

Last March, Durbin and Grassley introduced the Baltic Security Initiative Act, bipartisan legislation to effectively codify the Baltic Security Initiative, which Durbin created in 2021 to enhance and strengthen U.S. security cooperation with the Baltics amid an increase of Russian hybrid attacks in the Baltics and across Europe, and Russia’s war in Ukraine. The program was codified in the FY 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.

In 2022, Durbin traveled to Vilnius, Lithuania, where he received the Aleksandras Stulginskis Star Award—only the second individual and first American to receive this award. It was granted to Durbin for his decades-long support of Lithuanian independence and democracy and his promotion of parliamentary values. He was in Vilnius four years ago on the morning Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Durbin’s mother immigrated to the U.S. as a child from Lithuania.

Full text of the letter can be found here and below.

October 22, 2026

Dear Secretary Hegseth and Secretary Rubio,

We write to follow up on Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Congressionally appropriated funds for the Baltic Security Initiative (BSI). Since 2021, the BSI has enhanced the defense capabilities and interoperability of our Baltic allies. We urge you to ensure the swift obligation of this funding and execution of programs considering intensified Russian aggression in the region against key frontline allies.

We welcome the BSI spend plan provided by the Department of Defense (DoD) on May 29, 2026, which targets investments in integrated defense, maritime security, irregular warfare, and other critical capabilities as required by statute. On September 15, a second update from DoD indicated that BSI was prioritized for notification and in its final stages of coordination, including with the Department of State. While this is important progress, escalating Russian threats, specifically against the Baltic States, demand more urgent U.S. security assistance. In light of recent airspace incursions, gray-zone tactics, and heightened nuclear warnings against the Baltics, accelerating the delivery of assistance under the BSI must be a priority. We urge disbursement by the end of the calendar year and ask that you provide an update on such plans no later than November 19, 2026.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

Sincerely,

title: Made in America: Trump Signs Ernst Bill to Secure Supply Chains and Boost Manufacturing
text:
WASHINGTON – This week President Donald Trump signed U.S. Senator Joni Ernst’s (R-Iowa) bipartisan Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act into law, taking a step toward securing America's supply chains, reducing dependence on foreign adversaries, and identifying new manufacturing opportunities in rural America.

The law directs the Secretary of Commerce to examine critical products currently imported into the United States and identify opportunities to manufacture those goods domestically, including in rural communities and industrial parks.

“When it comes to our national security, we cannot afford to depend on foreign adversaries for the critical goods that keep America running,” said Senator Ernst. “President Trump understands that Made in America should be the norm, not the exception, and I am grateful he signed my bipartisan bill into law. Iowa has the talent, expertise, and resources to help bring critical manufacturing back to America. This is an important step toward securing our supply chains, strengthening our national security, and bringing more opportunities to rural America.”

Ernst introduced the legislation alongside Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), while Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa) led the companion legislation in the House. The bill passed both chambers with bipartisan support, and the President signed it into law this week.

“Supply chains are critical to global competitiveness and our national security," said Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware). “I’m proud to see this bipartisan legislation become law to help identify where we are over-reliant on foreign imports for critical infrastructure and explore how we can bring that manufacturing back to the United States. These investments will strengthen domestic production, secure our supply chains, and support good-paying jobs right here at home.”

"America cannot continue outsourcing the production of critical goods and good-paying manufacturing jobs to foreign adversaries. We must strengthen our domestic manufacturing, secure our supply chains, and ensure America can produce the essential materials our nation depends on," said Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa). "This legislation creates a roadmap to bring manufacturing back and create new good paying jobs for Iowans. I’m proud to have led this legislation to put American jobs first and am grateful it was signed into law.”

The legislation builds on Ernst's efforts to strengthen domestic production, support American manufacturers, and safeguard critical supply chains from foreign adversaries.

title: Grassley, Cantwell Urge FTC to Finish Investigation into Pharmacy Benefit Managers’ Practices, Provide Final Recommendations to Congress
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) are urging the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to complete its long-running study of pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) as soon as possible and publicly release a final report with recommendations to Congress.

While the FTC issued interim staff reports in July 2024 and January 2025, the Commission has yet to complete its Section 6(b) study into PBM business practices that was opened in June 2022.

“The interim reports confirm the need for a final assessment. Both the July 2024 and January 2025 [interim reports] describe how concentration and vertical integration in the PBM industry has given leading PBMs the ability and incentive to increase drug costs, steer patients towards more expensive drug options, and operate with limited transparency,” Grassley and Cantwell wrote.

The senators praised the FTC’s efforts to secure proposed consent agreements with Express Scripts and Caremark but cautioned more action is needed to hold PBMs accountable and lower drug costs for American families.

“The two interim reports and proposed consent agreements provide substantial information, but they do not complete the study or provide a comprehensive set of recommendations. Congress needs a final report to evaluate whether existing antitrust and consumer protection laws adequately address the identified conduct and whether additional legislation is warranted,” the senators continued.

In 2022, Grassley and Cantwell led a bipartisan letter to then-Chairwoman Lina Khan in support of the study. In January 2024, they led a bipartisan group of senators in another letter urging the FTC to complete its investigation into the nation’s most powerful prescription drug middlemen.

“Prompt completion of the study will provide Congress, taxpayers, plan sponsors, patients, and pharmacies a clearer understanding of competitive conditions in the PBM market and help inform efforts to improve competition, lower prescription drug costs and protect patient access,” Grassley and Cantwell concluded.

Full text of the letter can be found HERE.

Learn more about Grassley’s efforts to lower prescription drug costs HERE.

title: Grassley Welcomes Over $1 Million in Federal Funding to Support Hazard Mitigation and Energy Projects in Iowa Communities
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) welcomed news from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) that Iowa will receive over $1 million in federal funding to benefit infrastructure projects across the state.

Funding comes from the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program, which supports pre-disaster hazard mitigation projects that strengthen infrastructure, reduce risks from natural hazards and build long-term resilience.

“I’m glad to see the Trump administration continue to prioritize the health and safety of Iowans by distributing this federal funding,” Grassley said. “The state and these communities will put the money to good use strengthening infrastructure for the future. In Washington, I’ll keep fighting to ensure our state gets the resources we need to continue to build and prosper.”

The FEMA awards are:

Statewide Electric Resilience Strategy: $373,297.12 to fund advance assistance, education and outreach as part of a BRIC Fiscal Year 2023 Notice of Funding Opportunity project.

Cedar Rapids Downtown Generator Project: $370,755 to fund generators and emergency power as part of a BRIC Fiscal Year 2023 Notice of Funding Opportunity project. You can find more details HERE.

Panora Utility Resiliency Project: $277,709 to fund utility protective measures as part of a BRIC Fiscal Year 2023 Notice of Funding Opportunity project.

title: N.M. Delegation Welcomes $18.5 Million to Improve Albuquerque Sunport’s Rail Spur, Restore 6 Miles of Track, & Expand Freight Opportunities Across the State
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee, and U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), and U.S. Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), and Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) are welcoming over $18.5 million from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the Albuquerque International Sunport’s Rail Spur Project, a key economic development initiative at New Mexico’s largest airport.

This grant is funded by Congress through the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program under the Federal Railroad Administration. The grant is being awarded to the City of Albuquerque to improve approximately six miles of existing railroad track near the Albuquerque International Sunport. Planned improvements include track upgrades, a new rail siding, and connections to nearby industrial properties, a retaining wall to prevent erosion, and advanced security and railcar monitoring technology.

The rail spur improvements will help meet the needs of businesses seeking efficient freight transportation options and support development in the surrounding region, including nearby Mesa del Sol. Together, these efforts represent a strategic investment in infrastructure that can help accommodate future commercial and industrial growth.

“Investing in New Mexico’s commercial infrastructure helps grow our economy and create good-paying jobs for New Mexico families,” said Heinrich, Member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee. “This $18.5 million federal investment will restore a critical section of track at the Albuquerque International Sunport, improve safety and freight service, and create new opportunities to move goods through one of the Southwest's most important cargo hubs.”

“This investment in the Albuquerque International Sunport’s Rail Spur Project will strengthen critical infrastructure and boost economic development in the region for years to come,” said Luján. “This $18.5 million federal investment will restore roughly six miles of track, improve safety and performance, and create a strong hub for businesses in the region. I’m proud to welcome this critical investment and will continue working to bring federal dollars home to New Mexico.”

“When we invest in our infrastructure, we invest in New Mexico’s future. These improvements to the Sunport’s rail spur will help local businesses move goods more efficiently, create new opportunities for economic growth, and strengthen our state’s ability to compete and grow. By connecting businesses to reliable freight transportation, we can support good-paying jobs and build a stronger economy for our communities,” said Leger Fernández.

“New Mexico is on the move! This $18 million investment will help rehabilitate six miles of rail near the Sunport laying the groundwork to move essential goods—from construction materials, to industrial supplies, and other bulk freight—more efficiently,” said Stansbury. “This project is an important step in lowering transportation barriers for businesses, strengthening our supply chains, and attracting new economic opportunities to our state. I’m proud to partner with the New Mexico delegation to bring home this $18 million to bring federal resources home to invest in our infrastructure, our economy, and our local communities.”

“I’m proud to welcome this much-needed investment to upgrade critical rail transportation infrastructure at the Albuquerque Sunport,” said Vasquez. “The New Mexico delegation will continue working diligently to ensure federal funds are directed where they’re most needed and have an impact on safety and economic growth. The track upgrades are a welcome boost to operations at the Sunport.”

“Albuquerque already has the airport, the rail line, the interstate connections, and the land. This investment helps us put those assets to work together,” said Albuquerque City Mayor Tim Keller. “Investments like this strengthen our competitive edge, connect local industry to new markets and help build a stronger economic future for communities across New Mexico.”

title: Hoeven Breaks Ground on New $74 Million Air Traffic Control Tower at Grand Forks International Airport
text:
GRAND FORKS, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today joined officials from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and Grand Forks International Airport to break ground on a new $74 million air traffic control tower. As a member of the Senate Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (THUD) Appropriations Committee, Hoeven worked to secure funding for the FAA’s Air Traffic Control Tower Replacement program, which provided funding for the project. The new tower will replace the existing facility, built in 1987, and stand 197 feet tall, nearly twice the height of the current 104-foot tower, with a 650-square-foot tower cab and a 22,800-squarefoot base building. The tower is expected to be operational in December 2029.

Grand Forks International Airport consistently ranks among the top 25 busiest airports in the nation, recording 320,996 takeoffs and landings in 2025, surpassing even Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, which recorded 297,737. To support this level of aviation activity and continued growth, Hoeven has worked to secure federal funding for major infrastructure improvements at Grand Forks International Airport, including:

$40 million in federal funding for the ongoing $60 million reconstruction of the airport’s primary runway, expected to be completed in 2028.

More than $50 million in federal funding for the $70 million extension and reconstruction of the airport’s crosswind runway, completed in 2024.

The new tower will also be one of the first facilities in the nation to showcase the Trump administration’s Brand-New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS). Congress provided $12.5 billion toward the nationwide air traffic control modernization effort in the Working Families Tax Cut Act.

“With 320,996 takeoffs and landings in 2025, Grand Forks International Airport recorded more aircraft operations than Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, demonstrating its position among the nation’s busiest airports, thanks in large part to the University of North Dakota’s world-class aviation program,” said Hoeven. “We’ve worked hard to ensure our airports can meet air service demand now and into the future. This new tower will improve safety and support continued growth, while our efforts to strengthen the air traffic controller workforce, including expanding training opportunities at UND, will help keep our skies safe and our aviation system operating efficiently.”

Hoeven has also worked to address air traffic controller staffing shortages and strengthen the workforce, including:

Advancing the John A. Hauser Mental Health in Aviation Act to modernize mental health policies and reduce barriers to care for pilots and air traffic controllers, which passed the Senate in September 2026.

Introducing the Air Traffic Control Workforce Development Act of 2025 with Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Jerry Moran to expand training opportunities, including at the University of North Dakota (UND), and improve recruitment and retention.

Securing provisions in the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 to improve air traffic controller staffing models and establish updated hiring targets.

Authoring the Air Traffic Controller Hiring Reform Act, signed into law in 2019, to prioritize hiring veterans and graduates of FAA-certified training programs, including UND.

title: Hoeven Outlines Efforts to Expand Health Care Access in North Dakota, Support Providers & Patients
text:
FARGO, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today addressed the North Dakota Hospital Association’s annual convention, where he thanked attendees for the essential services they provide to patients across the state and outlined his continued efforts to support rural health care providers and their patients. To this end, Hoeven is advancing:

Bicameral legislation he introduced with Representative Julie Fedorchak, along with Senator Kevin Cramer as a cosponsor, to extend the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) for five years.

FCHIP develops and tests health care delivery and reimbursement models for Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) in hyper-rural counties to improve health outcomes for patients and save Medicare costs.

Specifically, FCHIP provides a waiver to Medicare payment rules that

Allows hospitals to increase the number of available Skilled Nursing Facility or Nursing Facility beds.

Cover the costs required to facilitate and grow telehealth programs.

Removes mileage restrictions on ambulance services at each participating Critical Access Hospital.

Currently there are five CAHs participating in the program, including the following facilities in North Dakota:

Jacobson Memorial Hospital Care Center in Elgin.

McKenzie County Healthcare Systems in Watford City.

Southwest Healthcare Services in Bowman.

The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP).

The CONNECT for Health Act, bipartisan legislation he cosponsored to expand the availability of telehealth services.

“Health care access is a fundamental pillar of our communities’ quality of life, and we appreciate the hard work of all our providers to ensure patients can receive the care they need regardless of their ZIP code. Through initiatives like the Rural Health Transformation Program, we’re working to expand the services available, including through telehealth, upgrade our medical facilities and equipment and recruit and retain the health care workforce we need,” said Hoeven. “We’re positioned to make these widespread improvements because of the work we’ve put into our health care sector to date, including establishing a statewide fiber optic network that supports telehealth access and building state-of-the-art critical access hospitals. As a result, our state is on track to receive $1 billion over five years to transform health care delivery for our rural communities.”

Transforming Rural Health Care

Hoeven worked to establish the RHTP through the passage of the Working Families Tax Cut Act and supported Governor Armstrong and his team in putting forward a strong application. The state was awarded $200 million for the program’s first year, which is twice the program’s baseline amount and puts North Dakota on track to receive up to $1 billion over the five years of the program. The senator stressed that this success comes as a result of the state:

Investing in statewide fiber optic infrastructure.

Building a network of new, state-of-the-art CAHs.

Leveraging both telehealth and CAHs to recruit and retain health care professionals and provide access to a comprehensive continuum of care.

North Dakota has rolled out nearly $60 million to improve health care delivery, including $40 million for clinical equipment upgrades, $10 million for health care workforce retention and $1.5 million for mobile mammography services.

Expanding Telehealth Access

Hoeven has been a cosponsor of the CONNECT for Health Act since 2021 and is working to advance the legislation to expand coverage of telehealth services through Medicare and make permanent telehealth flexibilities that were provided in recent years. The legislation would:

Permanently remove all geographic restrictions on telehealth services and expand originating sites to include the home and other sites.

Permanently allow health centers and rural health clinics to provide telehealth services.

Allow more eligible health care professionals to utilize telehealth services.

Remove unnecessary in-person visit requirements for telemental health services.

Require more published data to learn more about how telehealth is being used, impacts of quality of care, and how it can be improved to support patients and health care providers.

-###-

title: Kennedy tours LNG Center of Excellence at McNeese State University
text:
MADISONVILLE, La. – Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.), a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, toured the new National Center of Excellence for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Safety at McNeese State University. Kennedy joined local LNG industry leaders and the presidents of McNeese State University and the University of Louisiana at Lafayette to discuss the center’s research and future plans.

“Louisianians have always known a thing or two about producing American energy. That’s why I fought so hard to bring this LNG Center of Excellence to McNeese, where some of the brightest minds in the business can help make American energy safer and stronger,” said Kennedy.

Kennedy championed the creation of the LNG Center of Excellence through the PIPES Act of 2020 and fought to ensure Louisiana was selected as its home. The U.S. Department of Transportation officially selected McNeese State University in May 2025, and the center opened in April 2026.

Kennedy also secured $5 million in Fiscal Year 2026 funding to support the center’s work to improve LNG safety, advance research and strengthen workforce development.

The center brings together federal agencies, industry leaders and universities—including McNeese State University, the University of Louisiana at Lafayette and Southern University—to strengthen LNG safety and support Louisiana’s energy industry.
