title: SENATORS MCCORMICK, FETTERMAN CELEBRATE NEARLY $3 BILLION U.S. STEEL INVESTMENT IN MON VALLEY
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Dave McCormick (R-PA) and John Fetterman (D-PA) today celebrated U.S. Steel’s Board of Directors approving a nearly $3 billion investment in a new hot strip mill at the company’s Edgar Thomson Plant in Braddock, Pennsylvania. This announcement comes after Senator McCormick’s successful push with members of the Pennsylvania delegation, particularly U.S. Representatives Dan Meuser (R-PA-09) and Mike Kelly (R-PA-16), to win the Trump administration’s support for the U.S. Steel–Nippon partnership.

“This is exactly what Senator Fetterman and I fought for: real investment, good-paying jobs, and a strong future for American steelmaking in the Mon Valley,” said Senator McCormick. “This is a major step toward delivering on the promises of the U.S. Steel–Nippon Steel partnership. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, and with Congressmen Meuser and Kelly’s strong support, we secured a historic agreement, and now we’re seeing that commitment turn into action. The Mon Valley helped build America, and with this investment, Pennsylvania steelworkers will help build its future.”

The new hot strip mill will increase annual production capacity from approximately 2.2 million tons to 3.5 million tons and expand the range of steel products U.S. Steel can produce for customers. Initial production is expected in late 2029.

The investment builds on the historic U.S. Steel–Nippon Steel partnership, which includes a broader commitment to invest $11 billion in U.S. Steel facilities. The partnership is expected to help secure the future of U.S. Steel’s Pennsylvania operations, protect more than 11,000 jobs in the Commonwealth, and create additional opportunities for American workers.

Senator McCormick recently traveled to Tokyo, Japan, and Seoul, South Korea, where he met with government officials and business leaders to strengthen economic and security partnerships and encourage additional investment in Pennsylvania. During the trip, he emphasized the opportunity to build on the U.S. Steel–Nippon Steel partnership and bring more jobs, capital, and industrial growth to the Commonwealth.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Cosponsors Legislation to Stop Digital Drug Dealers from Selling Fentanyl to Children
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody is fighting to protect children from online drug dealers selling fentanyl. Senator Moody is championing the No Fentanyl on Social Media Act, which would direct the Federal Trade Commission, in coordination with the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services, to report to Congress on minors’ access to fentanyl through social media, with recommendations to address this growing threat.

This builds on Senator Moody’s strong background on fighting the fentanyl crisis as Florida’s former Attorney General and now U.S. Senator.

“Drug traffickers adapt and continue finding new ways to push deadly fentanyl into our communities—including using social media to reach our children. As a mom, I’m always vigilant with regard to what my kid sees online. As Florida’s Attorney General, I made fighting the opioid crisis a major priority, and now in the Senate, I’m continuing the fight by championing the No Fentanyl on Social Media Act,” said Senator Ashley Moody. “This measure will expose how criminals use social media to sell fentanyl to minors and identify ways to stop them.”

BACKGROUND:

Florida recently announced that fentanyl deaths in the state have fallen more than 60% since 2023. According to the recent Florida Medical Examiners Commission’s 2025 Annual Drugs Identified in Deceased Persons Report, fentanyl-caused deaths decreased by 37% from 2024 to 2025. Additionally, Florida saw a 50% decrease in fentanyl analog deaths, 33% decrease in opioid-caused deaths, and a 12% decrease in total drug-related deaths overall.

Florida’s decrease in fentanyl-related deaths outpaces the national drop of 22%.

Fentanyl continues to be the leading cause of drug overdose deaths in the United States.

The No Fentanyl on Social Media Act would provide Congress with clear and accurate data on the scope of this crisis, along with a series of policy recommendations to help address it. It would also assess platform design features, drug trafficking tactics, the effectiveness of platform policies and actions taken by law enforcement, medical experts and other stakeholders to combat the spread of fentanyl.

Senator Moody has long fought to stop the flow of illicit fentanyl into Florida communities. As Senator, Moody championed and helped pass the HALT Fentanyl Act and sponsored the PRESS Act. Senator Moody also cosponsored Tyler’s Law.

The HALT Fentanyl Act, signed into law by President Trump, assists law enforcement officers in getting fentanyl traffickers off the streets and permanently classifies fentanyl-related substances under Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.

PRESS Act would criminalize the intentional importation of pill press machines and unlisted precursor chemicals with the intent to manufacture illicit drugs.

Tyler’s Law would require HHS to issue guidance on whether hospital emergency departments should implement fentanyl testing as a routine procedure for patients experiencing an overdose.

As Florida Attorney General, Senator Moody chaired the Statewide Task Force on Opioid Drug Abuse and secured a massive multibillion-dollar settlement from opioid manufacturers, distributors and pharmacies.

# # #

title: Federal Judge Cites Whistleblower in Case Blocking DHS Field Operations in California, Across the Country
text:
DOJ is also relying on the same unreliable data in its ongoing attempt to block counting of 20,000 ballots in California

SACRAMENTO, CA – A federal judge in the Northern District of California blocked DHS agents in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin from carrying out most field operations aimed at uncovering President Trump’s baseless claims of widespread voter fraud. The judge’s ruling cited a recent Department of Homeland Security (DHS) whistleblower disclosure received by Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with jurisdiction over federal elections and Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, and Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y). The court’s ruling found such operations rely upon flawed, rushed information assembled by the agency through suspicious methods, including something called “supplemental magic”, as laid out in the whistleblower disclosure. Known U.S. citizens are being swept up into the initiative, raising concerns about voter intimidation.

“Donald Trump has spent a decade peddling the Big Lie and baseless, disproven claims of mass voter fraud. Now, less than two weeks before Election Day, a federal court has blocked an effort that threatened to intimidate voters and sweep up innocent citizens and noncitizens who have not voted. Federal law protects whistleblowers from retaliation, and this latest victory for free and fair elections is possible thanks to the courage of the whistleblower who exposed how DHS is collecting and weaponizing flawed data,” Senator Padilla said. “But we must remain vigilant. Right now, the Trump Administration is trying to throw out votes in California based on information that they know is unreliable. And they’re threatening to expand this effort to other states as they try to protect themselves from accountability at the ballot box. We must continue to counter Trump’s baseless election lies and do everything in our power to ensure that all eligible voters are able to cast their ballots free from the fear or intimidation.”

Last week, in a political stunt apparently based on the same flawed data, Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ) sued California, alleging it had identified more than 20,000 people on their voter rolls who DHS said were “likely noncitizens.” DOJ officials admitted that the data were flawed, and a preliminary review by Los Angeles County found that out of a sample of 200 on the DHS-provided list, “38.9% indicate that they were born in the United States, which is strong evidence of citizenship” and that over 70% had no voting history and that many of the alleged ineligible voters on the DOJ list had never received a ballot. These new findings were not surprising based on the consistent pattern of the Trump Administration touting thousands of supposed ineligible voters on rolls, which then collapse under scrutiny. The federal judge in this case has set a hearing for October 27.

The DHS whistleblower made a protected disclosure to the Senators, which was released on September 14, 2026 and alleged:

DHS agents are being ordered to violate state laws and access sensitive voter information under false pretenses. Agents assigned to the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” are directed to use personal information from DHS data to lie to access voter information on state voter registration websites, making false attestations that they are a voter or are acting with a voter’s express authorization in order to access sensitive voter data.

Leadership is pressuring USCIS personnel to create law enforcement records with information that is likely to be false, which will have serious negative consequences for eligible American voters and other innocent individuals. USCIS headquarters admits that DHS data can conflict with state records and contain both uncertainties and inconsistencies. Yet agency leadership directed officers to create “TECS” federal law enforcement records that relied solely on unreliable DHS-provided voting or registration data, even if officers believe it to be unreliable.

Known U.S. citizens are being swept up into the initiative, based on faulty and rushed data that DHS compiled using “supplemental magic.” Naturalized U.S. citizens are being investigated through this initiative without their knowledge or ability to correct erroneous data, with law enforcement records being generated against them.

USCIS officers are facing demanding quotas and unrealistic timelines. Agency leadership is requiring five investigations per hour, or 12 minutes each, only further compounding the potential for errors.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee and California’s former Secretary of State and chief election officer, Padilla has fought relentlessly to protect our elections and strengthen voting rights.

title: Padilla, Durbin Lead Colleagues in Demanding DOJ Watchdog Probe White House’s Alleged Order to Investigate LA Protestors
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, and Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) demanded Department of Justice (DOJ) Inspector General Don Berthiaume open an investigation into the concerning activities detailed in a recent whistleblower disclosure alleging that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), under White House and DOJ leadership’s direction, opened unconstitutional investigations into Los Angeles protestors solely for exercising their First Amendment rights. The letter was co-signed by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.).

In their letter, the Senators highlighted the whistleblower’s allegations that, in one incident, the White House instructed FBI Director Kash Patel to have the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office open an investigation into the protesters solely based on First Amendment activity, violating agency policy and protestors’ constitutional rights.

“These investigations were opened following increased protests against aggressive immigration enforcement actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in the Los Angeles area,” wrote the Senators. “The Disclosure states that no actual or potential national security threat or federal criminal activity existed on which to predicate investigating the protesters. The Disclosure also alleges that the investigations pulled FBI employees and resources away from active cases involving drug trafficking, violent crime, and transnational criminal organizations. Although the whistleblower and others at the Los Angeles Field Office raised concerns that these investigations unlawfully targeted individuals for exercising their First Amendment rights, the investigations allegedly proceeded nevertheless.”

In addition to the investigation, the Senators urged Berthiaume to take immediate action to address potential misconduct within the FBI to prevent any additional wrongdoing.

“We request that you open an independent investigation into the troubling allegations detailed in the Disclosure, which describes DOJ and FBI leadership directing personnel to initiate investigations based solely on First Amendment activity under political pressure,” wrote the Senators. “We further request that you investigate whether and to what extent the FBI’s Domestic Investigations and Operations Guide—and any provisions concerning First Amendment activity therein — have been amended during Director Patel’s tenure.”

“Given the serious questions the Disclosure raises about the misuse of federal law enforcement resources and the legality and constitutionality of these directives to FBI personnel, please provide regular updates on the status of your investigation to the leadership of the Senate Committee on the Judiciary,” the Senators concluded. “If the Attorney General refuses to cooperate with an audit or investigation into these allegations, please notify us immediately.”

The whistleblower’s disclosure follows a chilling pattern in which the Administration has pursued Trump’s baseless claims at the expense of Americans’ safety. A separate, recent whistleblower disclosure alleges Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) leadership abruptly diverted USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate immigration officers from their national security-related duties and directed them instead to use illegal procedures and questionable data to identify purported “unlawful voters,” and create federal law enforcement records against them, including naturalized U.S. citizens. The Administration also redirected Homeland Security Investigations analysts from their typical work on criminal matters and to a so-called “tiger team” for the sole purpose of investigating, surveilling, and detaining students and other individuals based solely on their political opinions.

Padilla has fought to hold the Trump Administration accountable. In January, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced a bill to reaffirm the right to free speech and safeguard Americans from politically motivated harassment and prosecution.

The whistleblower disclosure is available here.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Inspector General Berthiaume:

On October 5, 2026, the Senate Committee on the Judiciary received the attached protected whistleblower disclosure (the Disclosure) through the Government Accountability Project. It reveals serious allegations that the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) opened unconstitutional investigations of protesters engaged in protected First Amendment activity.

According to the Disclosure, the White House, DOJ leadership, and FBI leadership directed the Los Angeles FBI Field Office to open two different investigations in 2025 based solely on individuals’ participation in First Amendment activity—in violation of agency policy and protesters’ constitutional rights. These investigations were opened following increased protests against aggressive immigration enforcement actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in the Los Angeles area. The Disclosure states that no actual or potential national security threat or federal criminal activity existed on which to predicate investigating the protesters. The Disclosure also alleges that the investigations pulled FBI employees and resources away from active cases involving drug trafficking, violent crime, and transnational criminal organizations. Although the whistleblower and others at the Los Angeles Field Office raised concerns that these investigations unlawfully targeted individuals for exercising their First Amendment rights, the investigations allegedly proceeded nevertheless.

The Disclosure includes credible whistleblower allegations of wrongdoing and abuse of power by DOJ and FBI leadership in two instances:

(1) Then-DOJ Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove directed the Los Angeles Field Office to open an investigation into any anti-ICE and CBP protestors demonstrating at federal buildings in Los Angeles without identifying any clearly articulated actual or potential national security threat, criminal activity, or vulnerability to such threats and activities; and

(2) After President Trump reportedly viewed a TikTok video of protestors in Alhambra, California that alerted neighbors about ICE’s presence and advised them of their legal rights, the White House instructed FBI Director Kash Patel to direct the Los Angeles Field Office to initiate an investigation into the protestors.

We request that you open an independent investigation into the troubling allegations detailed in the Disclosure, which describes DOJ and FBI leadership directing personnel to initiate investigations based solely on First Amendment activity under political pressure. We further request that you investigate whether and to what extent the FBI’s Domestic Investigations and Operations Guide—and any provisions concerning First Amendment activity therein—have been amended during Director Patel’s tenure. Based on the allegations in the Disclosure and due to the risk that the FBI may continue to violate agency policies and unlawfully target individuals exercising their constitutional rights, we believe a management alert may be appropriate to address this alleged misconduct immediately and prevent any additional wrongdoing or misuse of FBI personnel and resources while your office’s investigation is ongoing.

Given the serious questions the Disclosure raises about the misuse of federal law enforcement resources and the legality and constitutionality of these directives to FBI personnel, please provide regular updates on the status of your investigation to the leadership of the Senate Committee on the Judiciary. If the Attorney General refuses to cooperate with an audit or investigation into these allegations, please notify us immediately.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

###

title: WATCH: Padilla Conducts Unannounced Oversight Visit of Sacramento ICE Holding Center, Demands Answers After Unmarked ICE Vehicle Strikes California U.S. Citizen
text:
This is Padilla’s third unannounced oversight visit of an ICE detention center this month as the Trump Administration escalates immigration enforcement operations across California. Photos here. Video HERE.

SACRAMENTO, CA — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) conducted an unannounced oversight visit today to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) holding center in Sacramento, where he demanded answers about an incident this week in which an unmarked ICE vehicle struck Antonio Moreida. The visit comes as the Trump Administration ramps up immigration enforcement across California and the country, raising serious concerns about federal enforcement tactics, transparency, and accountability.

“I’m in Sacramento today to demand answers about the incident this week in Woodland when an unmarked ICE vehicle struck Antonio Moreida, an incident that has sadly become part of a broader pattern of excessive use of force by an agency operating with no accountability. We’ve seen this Administration repeatedly deflect, deny, and avoid responsibility, even in the face of clear evidence. Today’s visit only reinforced those concerns. I asked and confirmed that the agent responsible is still on the job and still out in the field. That is unacceptable. The public deserves a full investigation,” said Senator Padilla. “It’s also clear how much fear this Administration has created: even people following the legal immigration process are afraid to show up for appointments or pursue citizenship. No one should be afraid to follow the law. No federal agency is above the law, and when Democrats take back Congress, we will use our full investigative power to get answers and hold this Administration accountable.”

The Trump Administration’s aggressive tactics have created a climate of fear that extends beyond people targeted for enforcement, discouraging even those pursuing citizenship or complying with legal immigration processes from accessing government services. Padilla saw this firsthand during his tour, when he observed an immigration services office with a vast reduction of people present who would normally come in for immigration appointments, to pursue citizenship, and to follow the legal process. The reduction of people seeking immigration services underscores the chilling effect of the Trump Administration’s enforcement actions, as even those following the law are increasingly afraid to engage with the immigration system.

Padilla has repeatedly conducted oversight visits to immigration detention facilities across California to examine conditions firsthand and demand accountability from federal officials. His visits have included facilities in California City, Otay Mesa, San Francisco International Airport, and downtown Los Angeles. He will continue using his oversight authority to demand answers about the Trump Administration’s immigration enforcement operations and hold federal officials accountable.

title: WATCH: Padilla Breaks Down New Whistleblower Disclosure that White House Allegedly Targeted LA Protestors for Exercising 1st Amendment Rights
text:
Padilla unpacks allegations that the White House, DOJ leadership, and FBI leadership directed unconstitutional investigations into protestors and demands invoking 25th Amendment

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, released a video highlighting the Trump Administration’s repeated attacks on free speech, detailing a recent whistleblower disclosure that alleges that the White House illegally directed the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to open investigations into anti-ICE and CBP protesters in Los Angeles solely for their First Amendment activity. The disclosure further alleges that FBI leadership pursued these investigations despite believing they were unconstitutional.

Padilla has fought to hold the Trump Administration accountable. In January, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced a bill to reaffirm the right to free speech and safeguard Americans from politically motivated harassment and prosecution.

Excerpts from the video are below:

PADILLA REACTS TO TRUMP’S LOS ANGELES AND SAN DIEGO IRAN COMMENTS

As one of California’s United States senators, I take that seriously because the president’s job is to protect and serve the American people. Not just the people who voted for him, everyone. And when you’re commander-in-chief, your words carry enormous weight, especially when you’re talking about nuclear weapons.

And frankly, Americans have every right to question the president’s judgment and fitness for office when he makes statements like these. But here’s where things get interesting. Because the administration wants people to consider the context of Trump’s words. And that brings me to the other story.

So, let me get this straight. When Trump says something controversial, we’re supposed to consider the context. We’re supposed to understand what he really meant.

Okay. But when Americans criticize the president, according to a new whistleblower disclosure that came to my office, his administration allegedly wanted the FBI to investigate them. Now, that’s the hypocrisy here.

PADILLA UNPACKS RECENT WHISTLEBLOWER DISCLOSURE

According to the whistleblower, President Trump allegedly saw footage of protesters in Alhambra, California, warning their neighbors about immigration enforcement activity and informing them about the need for judicial warrants to enter private homes. They were using megaphones and speaking out against his mass deportation agenda.

[…]

The whistleblower alleges that FBI leadership recognized the constitutional concerns but pursued the investigations anyway under pressure from the White House. They also alleged that in a separate incident, FBI personnel were directed to investigate anti-ICE and CBP protesters at federal buildings in Los Angeles without evidence of actual or potential national security threats or federal criminal activity or vulnerability to such threats.

And while this was happening, according to the disclosure, FBI personnel were being pulled away from investigations involving violent crime, drug trafficking, and organized crime. The Trump administration is diverting federal law enforcement resources away from those investigations to examine people exercising their First Amendment rights.

PADILLA DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM FBI AND DOJ

How many Americans were targeted solely because of their constitutionally protected speech? What resources were diverted? What happened to the people who tried to raise concerns? And going forward, how will the FBI and the Department of Justice ensure that no one is investigated based solely on what they say?

PADILLA ON WHAT THIS MEANS FOR OUR COUNTRY

We’re watching a series of events that raise important questions about executive power. A president whose words about American cities spark national controversy. A whistleblower alleging that federal law enforcement was pressured to investigate political dissent and federal employees who, according to that disclosure, feared the consequences of refusing those directives.

These are different issues, but they all underscore why our Constitution places limits on presidential power because no president gets to decide which Americans deserve constitutional rights. No president gets to put personal loyalty above the law and no president is above accountability.

PADILLA’S EFFORTS TO HOLD TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ACCOUNTABLE

When I took my oath of office, I didn’t swear loyalty to a president or a political party. I swore to support and defend the Constitution of the United States, and I’m going to keep doing exactly that.

I’ll keep demanding answers about these whistleblower allegations. I’ll keep fighting to protect our constitutional rights. I’ll keep holding this administration accountable through every tool available to Congress.

Because the presidency doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to the American people. And the Constitution always comes first.

title: Senators Peters, Slotkin Announce More than $17 Million in Federal Support for Southeast Michigan Fire Departments
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Gary Peters (MI) and Elissa Slotkin (MI) announced that local fire departments across Southeast Michigan are set to receive more than $17 million in federal funding. The funding comes from the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG) and Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant programs. In 2024, Peters led the charge to extend these federal grant programs that help local fire departments address staffing needs, purchase equipment, develop fire training and education programs, and improve emergency medical services.

“Firefighters and first responders put their lives on the line to protect Michiganders. It’s absolutely essential that we provide them with the tools needed to do their jobs safely,” said Senator Peters. “I was proud to work in a bipartisan way to extend these vital grant programs, and I’m pleased this funding will help ensure fire departments across Southeast Michigan have the proper equipment and staffing levels necessary to keep our communities safe.”

“As elected officials, it is our responsibility to ensure that Michigan’s firefighters and front-line responders are protected. I join my colleague, Senator Gary Peters, in welcoming the more than $17 million in federal support for Southeast Michigan firefighters,” said Senator Slotkin. “We’ve worked in a bipartisan way to secure this essential grant funding. And now, these dollars will be used to address staffing needs, enhance safety training, and provide much-needed equipment for the brave folks who put their lives on the line every day to keep Michiganders safe.”

“Funding from grant programs like AFG and SAFER are vital to ensure our firefighters have access to the equipment and high-quality training that prepares them to meet the challenges of various incidents and hazards," said Joseph Murray, Fire Chief of the Dearborn Fire Department. “These critical federal investments will directly improve the Dearborn Fire Department's operational capacity and reduce the strain on our frontline crews during challenging incidents. We are deeply grateful to Senator Gary Peters for his continued advocacy in securing these vital federal resources.”

“Receiving AFG funding for new air packs, masks, and breathing-air bottles is a tremendous investment in the safety of our firefighters and the residents we serve,” said Stephen Kohut, Fire Chief for Armada Township. “For a small department like Armada Fire, this funding allows us to obtain critical protective equipment that would otherwise place a significant burden on our local budget, while ensuring our firefighters have the reliable equipment they need to safely protect our community.”

“These FEMA grants enable us to provide the highest-quality emergency response and community risk reduction services to our community,” said Brian Siriani, Deputy Chief of the Brighton Area Fire Authority. “Thank you to Congress for reinstating them.”

“This regional grant award is a tremendous example of what can be accomplished through cooperation, collaboration, and a shared commitment to serving our communities,” said Chief Matt Weil, North Oakland Fire Authority. “The Village of Holly, Groveland Township Fire Department, Oxford Fire Department, and NOCFA worked together with incredible resolve to bring this project across the finish line, and we’re thankful for the support of Senator Peters and our federal partners, and especially for the hard work of our grant-writing team who helped make this project possible.”

Below are descriptions of each project:

Michigan Association of Fire Chiefs: The Michigan Association of Fire Chiefs will receive $856,145 from the SAFER program to retain or expand emergency personnel staffing levels.

North Oakland County Fire Authority: The North Oakland County Fire Authority will receive $698,071 from the AFG program to purchase additional cardiac monitors. The funds are being split with Groveland Township, the village of Oxford, and the village of Holly.

Rochester Hills Fire Department: Rochester Hills Fire Department will receive $3,215,962 from the SAFER grant program. This investment will allow the department to hire 12 additional firefighters. These new firefighters will allow staffing for an additional ambulance and fire apparatus in the community.

Bruce Township Fire Department: Bruce Township Fire Department will receive $1,658,300 from the SAFER program to retain or expand emergency personnel staffing levels.

Brighton Area Fire Authority: Brighton Area Fire Authority will receive a total of $2,773,575 for two separate grant awards: $2,089,575 from the SAFER grant program to hire 12 additional full-time firefighters and $684,000 from the AFG program to purchase 73 Self-Contained Breathing Apparatuses (SCBAs) to replace out-of-compliance units.

Dearborn Fire Department: The Dearborn Fire Department will receive a total of $2,681,733 for two separate grant awards: $2,505,790 from the SAFER program to hire 12 additional firefighters and $175,943 from the AFG program to provide specialized hazard training to its crew members.

Lincoln Park Fire Department: Lincoln Park Fire Department is set to receive $1,984,015 from the SAFER program to retain or expand emergency personnel staffing levels.

Westland Public Service: The Westland Public Service will receive $555,894 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Charter Township of Van Buren: The Charter Township of Van Buren will receive a total of $480,426 from two separate grant awards: $449,154 from the SAFER program to retain or expand emergency personnel staffing levels and $31,272 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed strengthen operational safety.

Waterford Regional Fire Department: The Waterford Regional Fire Department is set to receive $455,545 from the AFG program to upgrade exhaust systems at Fire Stations throughout the region.

Richmond Lenox Emergency Management Services: Richmond Lenox Emergency Management Services will receive $401,893 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Southfield Fire Department: The Southfield Fire Department will receive $320,612 from the AFG program to provide Rapid Intervention Crew Training classes for all active department firefighters. These classes will provide critical training for crew members to manage lost or trapped incidents while on duty.

City of Roseville: The City of Roseville will receive $252,645 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Armanda Fire Department: The Armanda Fire Department will receive $224,761 from the AFG program for the purchase of firefighter health and safety equipment, including air packs and air bottles for interior firefighting operations.

Sterling Heights Fire Department: The Sterling Heights Fire Department will receive $198,454 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

City of Port Huron: The City of Port Huron will receive $221,418 from the AFG program for rope rescue operations and technician training for all Port Huron firefighters over the next two years.

Superior Township: Superior Township will receive $81,415 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Commerce Township: Commerce Township will receive $74,557 from the AFG program to purchase 10 portable radios to strengthen the department’s operational safety.

Pittsfield Township Fire Department: The Pittsfield Township Fire Department will receive $68,181 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Elk Township (Sanilac County): Elk Township will receive $42,285 from the AFG program to purchase vehicle-mounted exhaust capturing systems. These devices will help protect firefighters from dangerous exhaust gases while responding to an emergency situation.

City of Grosse Pointe Farms: The City of Grosse Pointe Farms will receive $57,142 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Lasalle Township: Lasalle Township will receive $29,333 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

City of New Baltimore: The City of New Baltimore will receive $28,403 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Hamtramck Fire Department: The Hamtramck Fire Department will receive $17,819 from the AFG program to invest in equipment needed to strengthen operational safety.

Peters’ Fire Grants and Safety Act reauthorized robust funding for the SAFER and AFG programs, as well as the United States Fire Administration (USFA), until 2028. It reauthorizes $95 million for USFA – a nearly $20 million increase from previously authorized levels. Fire departments use these federal programs to recruit and retain additional personnel, as well as buy up-to-date vehicles and equipment such as breathing air compressors, hoses, nozzles, and more. Funding from these programs can also be used to fund safety training and technical rescue training, as well as health screenings for firefighters. Peters is co-chair, and Slotkin is a member of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus, which works to advance initiatives which support first responders.

More information about these grants can be found here.

title: Sen. Rick Scott Concludes Trip with U.S. Allies in Mediterranean, Middle East to Strengthen U.S. Economy and Defend Shared National Security Interests
text:

This Funding Comes From The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Which Senator Rosen Helped Write And Pass

CARSON CITY, NV – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) applauded the announcement that $33.7 million in federal funding, which she helped secure through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, is headed to Nevada to bolster the state’s safe drinking water infrastructure. The funding comes from the Environmental Protection Agency and will be given to Nevada’s Department of Conservation and Natural Resources toward removing common contaminants found in drinking water and protecting public health.

“Every Nevadan deserves to have access to clean drinking water,” said Senator Rosen. “At a time when water shortages are worsening, it’s so important that we protect and conserve this essential resource. I am proud to have secured this important funding for our state, and I will continue pushing to ensure that every Nevadan has access to safe drinking water.”

Senator Rosen has helped communities across Nevada secure critical funding and support for water infrastructure projects. In August, Senator Rosen joined the ceremonial groundbreaking of the first-ever drinking water system in the Lehman Creek Residential Area, for which she helped secure funding. In May, Senator Rosen helped deliver federal funding to a water infrastructure project in Carlin to reduce water loss and ensure the security of their drinking water system. Senator Rosen also introduced bipartisan legislation to protect drinking water infrastructure from extreme weather events.

title: Schatz: More Than $80 Million Heading to Hawai‘i To Repair Roads, Bridges, Structures Damaged By Kona Low Storms
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Brian Schatz (D-Hawai‘i) announced that Hawai‘i is receiving nearly $81.4 million from the U.S. Department of Transportation to cover the costs of repairs to roads, bridges, and other structures that were flooded and damaged during the Kona low storms earlier this year.

“This new federal funding will help repair storm-damaged roads and structures as recovery from this year’s historic flooding continues. We’re going to keep working to deliver federal resources so that affected communities can get back on their feet,” said Senator Schatz.

A senior member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Schatz has led efforts urging federal support for Hawai‘i’s recovery from the Kona low storms and subsequent hurricanes this year, including by speaking to U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. In addition to this funding, the Hawai‘i Department of Transportation also received $2.3 million from the Federal Highway Administration’s Emergency Relief Program to repair bridges on Kaua‘i damaged by flooding in 2020.

title: SCHUMER, MORELLE ANNOUNCE $5.3+ MILLION TO BOOST MONROE COMMUNITY COLLEGE AS ONE OF AMERICA’S ONLY COMMUNITY COLLEGE OPTICS & PHOTONICS TRAINING CENTERS
text:
Schumer And Morelle Have Long Supported Department Of Defense’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP), Which Has Now Delivered $10+ Million For Monroe Community College

Schumer Fought To Secure Boosts In FY26 Federal Budget For Critical DoD Program To Strengthen MCC’s World-Class Optics & Photonics Engineering Programs, Giving Workers The Skills They Need For Good-Paying, Hi-Tech Local Jobs

Schumer, Morelle: New Fed $$ Is A Win-Win For Rochester-Finger Lakes Workforce, Local Businesses & America’s National Security

U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer and U.S. Congressman Joe Morelle today announced a $5,383,256 three-year grant award for Monroe Community College’s (MCC) optics program from the U.S. Department of Defense’s (DoD) Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP).

The lawmakers, in the federal Fiscal Year 2026 Defense Appropriations Bill, secured a critical increase for this program, and then personally advocated with DoD to push for MCC to compete for, and ultimately secure, this funding award to help grow its program. Schumer and Morelle explained that this major multi-year grant will provide critical support for MCC’s Optical Systems Technology program, boosting the pipeline of skilled talent for Rochester optics and photonics companies that are vital to U.S. national security and the regional economy. Today’s award follows a similar $5.1 million DoD MEEP grant that the lawmakers secured in 2023 to fund MCC’s optics program through 2026.

“This substantial $5 million in federal funding is a win-win for our top-notch workforce and local businesses critical to our national security. The Rochester-Finger Lakes region has a proud history of excellence and innovation in optics and photonics. This federal award will support Monroe Community College’s associate degree program in optics engineering, one of the first and only of its kind in the country,” said Senator Schumer. “Three years ago, I was proud to secure a critical increase in the federal budget to keep MCC’s optics training program running to train the next generation of optics technicians needed to support the high-tech manufacturing and semiconductor businesses that we are bringing to Upstate New York. Today, we are building on that success by connecting local students to good-paying jobs in Rochester.”

“A strong workforce is the foundation of a strong economy, and Monroe Community College is helping prepare the next generation of skilled workers for success,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “This $5.3 million investment will open doors to good-paying careers, strengthen our local Optics, Photonics, Imaging, and Lasers ecosystem, and bolster our national security. I’m proud to have secured this critical funding and continue building a stronger future for Rochester.”

“Monroe Community College is deeply grateful to Senator Schumer and Congressman Morelle for their continued advocacy and investment in our students, our institution, and the economic future of our region. This $5.3 million investment will help MCC expand access to high-quality education, hands-on training, and apprenticeship opportunities in the rapidly growing optics and photonics industries. Our optics program is a cornerstone of the Sydor Optics Advanced Technology Center, which was also made possible through previous federal funding championed by our federal delegation. We are especially grateful for their sustained commitment to building MCC's capacity to educate and train the next generation of skilled professionals. As a national leader in precision optics education, MCC is uniquely positioned to connect talented students with meaningful, family-sustaining careers while helping employers meet critical workforce needs. This latest investment builds upon that strong foundation and further reinforces Rochester's position as a national center for optics innovation and advanced manufacturing,” said Dr. DeAnna R. Burt-Nanna, President of Monroe Community College.

Schumer and Morelle explained that the DoD’s MEEP invests in programs that better position the current and next-generation manufacturing workforce vital for our nation’s defense innovation ecosystem and components that assure defense technological superiority. This is the third time MCC has been awarded funding through the MEEP program, as the nation’s first community college to administer associate degrees in precision optics. With this latest round of funding, MCC will be able to strengthen its existing program to grow the national workforce for the optics industry and give workers the skills they need for careers with major local employers in the region in the optics, photonics, and semiconductor industries. Specifically, MCC seeks to grow enrollment for this program for the in-demand optics industry and establish new training and apprenticeship opportunities.

Schumer and Morelle have been longtime advocates for Monroe Community College’s optics and photonics degree programs. In 2017, following their relentless advocacy, the lawmakers secured over $550,000 from the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Advanced Technology Foundation’s Education program for MCC to expand its optics and photonics degree programs, purchase new equipment, as well as develop a new curriculum and expand student outreach. In 2023, the lawmakers secured more than $5 million over three years for the program, made possible by their work securing $15 million in federal funding in FY23 for the DoD’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP), allowing MCC to apply for the funding they received in 2023. Similarly, this year, the lawmakers secured a $15 million boost in the MEEP program in the federal Fiscal Year 2026 Defense Appropriations Bill, and then personally advocated with DoD to push for MCC to compete and ultimately secure this new $5.3 million funding award to grow its training program.

This over $10M in MEEP funding has been instrumental in enabling MCC to supercharge its optics training program to significantly expand its program, create new skilled jobs, and provide local optics manufacturers with the vital workers they need. Specifically, thanks to this MEEP funding, the MCC optics program has been able to increase its student enrollment by 3,520 percent since 2015. This first-of-its-kind in the nation two-year training program provides a direct path to employment for hundreds of students and supports the lawmakers’ success in growing the semiconductor industry across Upstate New York.

A copy of the lawmakers’ letter in support of this MCC grant award to Dr. Jagadeesh Pamulapati, Principal Director for Science and Technology (S&T) Foundations, Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering is below:

We are pleased to write in support of Monroe Community College’s (MCC) pursuit to successfully apply and secure an award from the Department of Defense’s Manufacturing Engineering Education Program (MEEP) for MCC’s proposal, FOCUS-D: Fortifying Optics Capabilities for U.S. Security & Defense. Such funding will enable MCC to build on the success of MCC’s previous 2023 MEEP award, DEEPER OPS, to strengthen and expand educational training to prepare even more technicians for defense-relevant manufacturing and the domestic defense supply chain while helping to reverse the current nationwide shortage of these skilled optics workers who are in high demand with defense-relevant employers to support the nation’s domestic supply chain.

Monroe Community College is uniquely positioned to carry out this important work. Located in Rochester, New York, MCC is the nation’s first college to award associate degrees in precision optics and has built a strong foundation for technician education, workforce development, and employer-connected training. The Finger Lakes region is a nationally significant hub for optics, photonics, imaging, advanced manufacturing, and semiconductor activity, with more than 150 related companies and continued demand for skilled optics workers. We were pleased to help secure additional FY26 MEEP funding in order to provide continued support for the vital work done by MEEP grantees, including Monroe Community College to train workers to fill the jobs needed across the defense industrial domestic supply chain. By leveraging MCC’s nationally recognized optics workforce training programs, MCC’s FOCUS-D proposal will not only build on its proven successes of turning out well-prepared technicians to enter the defense supply chain workforce, but will accelerate and increase these training and career placement results with a stronger alignment to military, defense, and space applications, and deeper employer-connected pathways. MCC has already demonstrated strong results through its Optical Systems Technology program and prior federal support, including increased enrollment, expanded credential attainment, dual-enrollment pathways for high school students, and direct engagement with employers across the defense supply chain. MCC has long been one of Rochester’s great engines of opportunity, translating local talent into nationally significant skill.

With funding, MCC will enhance and expand its optics technician curriculum, accelerate flexible pathways into the field, modernize defense-relevant laboratory instruction, and deepen partnerships with defense employers through paid internships, apprenticeships, and employer-connected training. The project will support apprentices, incumbent workers, veterans, adult learners, career changers, and students entering the workforce, while expanding training in areas critical to military, defense, and space applications, including optical coatings, metrology, contamination control, infrared materials, high-energy optics, and directed energy systems. By growing a stronger pipeline of skilled technicians, MCC’s proposal will create a win-win for students and businesses in the optics supply chain: workers gain access to high-quality careers, while employers gain the trained talent needed to meet defense manufacturing need.

title: Shaheen Hosts Roundtable on Efforts to Address PFAS Contamination at Pease Tradeport, Discusses Career in Foreign Policy with Former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan at University of New Hampshire Security Forum
text:
(Durham, NH) – Today, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee, hosted a roundtable discussion to hear updates on efforts to address PFAS contamination at Pease Tradeport before traveling to Durham to sit down with former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan at the University of New Hampshire Carsey School of Public Policy’s 2026 Security Forum. Photos from today’s events can be found HERE.

In Portsmouth, Senator Shaheen convened Seacoast leaders and community stakeholders for a roundtable focused on discussing the most recent developments on efforts to address PFAS contamination at Pease Tradeport and to highlight the tireless efforts of local advocates who have worked alongside Senator Shaheen for over a decade to combat PFAS contamination in the region. At the roundtable, Shaheen discussed the United States Air Force’s engagement with the Portsmouth community and their recent response to a letter from the New Hampshire congressional delegation requesting a firm timeline for prompt funding and treatment of PFAS contamination in two municipal drinking water wells in Portsmouth before the water system falls out of compliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act. With Senator Shaheen set to retire at the end of this Congress, she also commemorated the progress Seacoast communities have made in combatting PFAS contamination and thanked local advocates, such as Andrea Amico, founder of Testing for Pease, for their unwavering commitment to addressing the issue.

“Since PFAS contamination was uncovered at Pease over a decade ago, New Hampshire has been leading the way to advance our understanding of the health impacts of PFAS and address these forever chemicals head on,” Senator Shaheen. “I’ve been so proud of the strides we’ve made to combat PFAS in our communities, and that is in large part due to the tireless work of local stakeholders who took it on themselves to raise the alarm and make real change. It has been my honor to partner with these folks during my time in the Senate. As I near retirement, I am confident our Seacoast communities will be safer and healthier in the years to come thanks to the work of advocates across the region.”

Senator Shaheen has been a leader in Washington on addressing PFAS issues in New Hampshire and across the country. In 2018, Senator Shaheen secured authorization and funding for the first ever nationwide study on the health impacts of PFAS in drinking water, with Pease Tradeport serving as the pilot study side. Since then, Senator Shaheen has continued to fight against PFAS contamination in the Senate. In the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Shaheen secured $10 billion to address PFAS and other emerging contaminants, which has delivered a total of $95 million to address PFAS in drinking water, including in private wells and other water sources across New Hampshire.

Then in Durham, Senator Shaheen joined former U.S. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan for a fireside chat at the University of New Hampshire Carsey School of Public Policy’s 2026 Security Forum. At the forum, Senator Shaheen provided her insights on some of the most pressing foreign policy challenges of today, including Russia’s war in Ukraine, the future of the NATO Alliance and the importance of bipartisanship in foreign policy. Senator Shaheen also discussed her recent visit to the Western Balkans, her efforts to promote female leadership abroad and the importance of American leadership in strengthening global democratic institutions. Shaheen then took questions from University of New Hampshire students.

“As President Trump continues to berate our nation’s closest allies, capitulate to dictators like Vladimir Putin and President Xi and engages in reckless wars in the Middle East, now more than ever we must make it clear that the foreign policy of this Administration is not in the best interest of the United States and does not represent the will of the American people,” said Senator Shaheen. “It will be up to our next generation of leaders to rebuild American leadership and credibility abroad.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Senator Shaheen is the top Democratic voice on foreign affairs in the United States Senate and fights to protect and advance American interests abroad and conducts critical oversight of the Trump Administration's foreign policy. In her role, Shaheen leads diplomatic efforts to strengthen key alliances, promote economic development and bolster democratic institutions across the globe. Senator Shaheen has served on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee since 2009 and is the first woman to serve as Ranking Member of the Committee.

title: Slotkin Joins Bipartisan Push to Hold Defense Contractors Accountable on Pricing
text:
For decades, defense contractors have taken advantage of the Pentagon’s inability to prevent price gouging

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) joined Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), and Joni Ernst (R-IA) in sending a bipartisan letter to Deputy Secretary of Defense Stephen Feinberg. The letter asks the Department to enforce the Pentagon’s August 18 directive on “Supplier Cost and Pricing Transparency” and to hold defense contractors accountable.

“The culture of overcharging within the defense industry that has driven this behavior has come with significant costs to both readiness and the American taxpayer,” wrote the senators.

The August 18 directive is meant to improve access to contractors’ cost and pricing data and help contracting officers negotiate fair prices. The senators welcomed the effort but warned of a key gap. The policy applies a $10 million threshold for obtaining certified cost and pricing data, which could leave the Department without access to critical information for more than 60 percent of its contracts. The senators urged the Pentagon to extend the directive to lower-value contracts. They also urged it to use its existing authority to make contractors ineligible for awards when they refuse to provide requested data.

“To ensure our understanding of how this directive ‘resets the Department’s expectations regarding supplier cost and pricing information,’ and how it will gain transparency through ‘modern information technology and current business best practices,’ we seek to clarify how the Department will gain such data from refusing companies, conduct consistent oversight, and hold non-compliant companies accountable,” concluded the senators.

The senators asked the Department to respond to their questions by November 3, 2026.

Read the full text of the letter here.

title: Van Hollen, Colleagues Press Meta’s Zuckerberg for Answers After No Kings Coalition Account Shut Off in Middle of No Kings National Demonstrations
text:
Today, U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) are calling on Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to answer questions on the temporary removal of the No Kings Coalition Instagram account in the middle of nationwide demonstrations organized by the group. The No Kings Day account was shut down and organizers were unable to access it as nearly three thousand events were held across the country where Americans expressed their support for democracy, the right to vote, and democratic institutions.

The lawmakers begin, “We are writing to seek answers regarding the removal of the No Kings Coalition Instagram account in the middle of nationwide protest demonstrations organized by the group. On October 17, 2026, Americans from all around the country gathered together in political demonstrations expressing support for democracy, the right to vote, and our democratic institutions organized by the No Kings Coalition. The No Kings Coalition uses Instagram as one of their primary platforms for communicating with participants, the public, and for hosting livestreams of their events. During the middle of these nationwide demonstrations, the No Kings Coalition’s Instagram account was mysteriously made invisible to the public, and the administrators were not able to access their account. The shutdown of the public page lasted well over an hour. Making matters worse, the lockout that prevented the account holders from even accessing their own page stretched for hours after the public page was restored, restricting their ability to communicate with supporters and protesters during the demonstrations despite the page being live.”

“We are especially troubled by Meta’s changing explanation for removing the account’s public visibility and the organizers' access during a nationally attended and well-publicized event. Andy Stone, Vice President of Communications at Meta, first shared that the account was shut down because very high frequencies of posting, sharing, or commenting triggered automated systems. The next day, Mr. Stone claimed that it had nothing to do with the account’s posting, sharing, or commenting but on their ‘reading’ behavior and the rate at which they were ‘reading profiles, posts, and hashtags’ on October 17. He also recognized that it ‘took additional time for [Meta] to straighten out the situation with admin access to the IG account.’ Not only are Meta’s shifting explanations alarming, the substance of the claims paint the picture that one of the largest social media companies in the world is somehow incapable of handling technical concerns about an account without shutting it down for hours,” they continue.

Noting that this is not an isolated incident, the lawmakers note, “This is not the first time that Meta has experienced shutdowns or lapses around political speech leading up to the 2026 elections. In September, Ohio Democratic Senate nominee Sherrod Brown shared that a technical glitch with Facebook’s advertising platform caused about half of his campaign advertisements on the platform to be taken down for over a day without notice. Additionally, in Brazil, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was unable to boost his Instagram posts for almost 24 hours, while his opponent, who is known to be connected with the Trump Administration, was able to boost posts during the same time span.”

“Furthermore, at a time when billionaires and big business, including Meta, are cozying up to the Trump Administration, we cannot ignore that it was a grassroots organization that is standing up to President Trump’s corruption that experienced this blackout. Meta’s close relationship with the Trump Administration is well documented. The company donated one million dollars to an inauguration fund for President Trump and five million dollars for Trump’s ballroom project. In settling a lawsuit, Meta also agreed to pay President Trump $25 million. The relationship between the Trump Administration, big business, and the media that these businesses run raises serious concerns over freedom of speech and the press,” the lawmakers conclude.

Among other questions, the lawmakers ask the following:

Did Meta or its representatives have any communication with the Trump Administration regarding No Kings or other pro-democracy protests? If so, who did you speak with and what did you discuss? Please provide all records of these interactions.

As raised by Meta’s Oversight Board, why was the No Kings Coalition’s account not included in Meta's cross-check program?

Was the decision to remove the No Kings Coalition account made by a human or by an automated process?

How will you guarantee that accounts sharing critical election and civic information are not incorrectly shutdown in the future? What steps will Meta take between now and election day to ensure that accounts sharing this information are not taken offline without notice?

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. Zuckerberg,

We are writing to seek answers regarding the removal of the No Kings Coalition Instagram account in the middle of nationwide protest demonstrations organized by the group.

On October 17, 2026, Americans from all around the country gathered together in political demonstrations expressing support for democracy, the right to vote, and our democratic institutions organized by the No Kings Coalition. The No Kings Coalition uses Instagram as one of their primary platforms for communicating with participants, the public, and for hosting livestreams of their events. During the middle of these nationwide demonstrations, the No Kings Coalition’s Instagram account was mysteriously made invisible to the public and the administrators were not able to access their account.

The shutdown of the public page lasted well over an hour. Making matters worse, the lockout that prevented the account holders from even accessing their own page stretched for hours after the public page was restored, restricting their ability to communicate with supporters and protesters during the demonstrations despite the page being live.

We are especially troubled by Meta’s changing explanation for removing the account’s public visibility and the organizers' access during a nationally attended and well-publicized event. Andy Stone, Vice President of Communications at Meta, first shared that the account was shut down because very high frequencies of posting, sharing, or commenting triggered automated systems. The next day, Mr. Stone claimed that it had nothing to do with the account’s posting, sharing, or commenting but on their “reading” behavior and the rate at which they were “reading profiles, posts, and hashtags” on October 17. He also recognized that it “took additional time for [Meta] to straighten out the situation with admin access to the IG account.” Not only are Meta’s shifting explanations alarming, the substance of the claims paint the picture that one of the largest social media companies in the world is somehow incapable of handling technical concerns about an account without shutting it down for hours.

This is not the first time that Meta has experienced shutdowns or lapses around political speech leading up to the 2026 elections. In September, Ohio Democratic Senate nominee Sherrod Brown shared that a technical glitch with Facebook’s advertising platform caused about half of his campaign advertisements on the platform to be taken down for over a day without notice. Additionally, in Brazil, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was unable to boost his Instagram posts for almost 24 hours, while his opponent, who is known to be connected with the Trump Administration, was able to boost posts during the same time span.

Meta’s own Oversight Board raised concerns over “recurring enforcement failures in Meta’s election integrity efforts.” Specifically, the Oversight Board argued that “the enforcement error regarding the No Kings account should have been caught by Meta's mistake-prevention systems. It remains unclear why Meta’s election integrity efforts did not lead to a much quicker resolution or why No Kings accounts were not included in Meta's cross-check program – which allows the company to designate important civic entities to ensure human review before a decision is made that could severely jeopardize participation in a significant political event.” As we approach the 2026 midterm elections, your company must ensure that critical information for voters is not censored.

Furthermore, at a time when billionaires and big business, including Meta, are cozying up to the Trump Administration, we cannot ignore that it was a grassroots organization that is standing up to President Trump’s corruption that experienced this blackout. Meta’s close relationship with the Trump Administration is well documented. The company donated one million dollars to an inauguration fund for President Trump and five million dollars for Trump’s ballroom project. In settling a lawsuit, Meta also agreed to pay President Trump $25 million. The relationship between the Trump Administration, big business, and the media that these businesses run raises serious concerns over freedom of speech and the press.

While the No Kings Coalition has regained access to their account, the public deserves answers to why the No Kings Coalition’s account was shut down in the middle of a national grassroots protest and how Meta will ensure that this will not happen again. Due to the time-sensitive nature of ensuring the availability of election and civic information, please respond to the following questions by October 29th, 2026:

title: Warnock, Colleagues Launch Bicameral Inquiry Into Trump Administration’s Handling of Tariff Refunds
text:
Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock led a bicameral coalition in pressing the Government Accountability Office to investigate the Trump administration’s failure to deliver timely and accurate tariff refunds

Senator Warnock is demanding answers about whether court-mandated refunds are being issued accurately and whether American consumers are ultimately benefiting from them

Earlier this year, the Supreme Court ruled that sweeping tariffs imposed by the Trump administration under emergency powers were illegal

Senator Reverend Warnock: “The American people deserve a timely, accurate, and transparent refund process that lays bare the total economic devastation of the administration’s erroneous tariff agenda on hardworking consumers”

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on International Trade, Customs, and Global Competitiveness, Representative Jill Tokuda (D-HI), and Representative Brad Sherman (D-CA) launched a bicameral inquiry calling on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to investigate the Trump administration’s handling of tariff refunds after the Supreme Court ruled that sweeping tariffs imposed under the President’s emergency powers were illegal.

“Georgians are already paying the price for the Trump administration’s reckless and illegal tariff policies. Now, the administration’s failure to deliver court-ordered refunds is putting additional financial strain on hardworking families and small businesses across the country,” said Senator Warnock. “The American people deserve a timely, accurate, and transparent refund process that lays bare the total economic devastation of the administration’s erroneous tariff agenda on hardworking consumers. That’s why I’m joining Congresswoman Tokuda in calling for a comprehensive investigation into how the U.S. Customs and Border Protection is handling these refunds.”

“Trump’s reckless tariffs are illegal, incompetent, and hitting working families where it hurts most: their wallets,” said Representative Tokuda. “In Hawaiʻi, where the cost of living is already too high, these tariffs are driving up prices on everyday goods for families and inputs for local farmers. Big corporations are positioned to get billions in refunds while working people are left footing the bill. We’re demanding a full audit to ensure this refund actually makes it back to the people who paid the price.”

“Trump’s reckless tariffs have been an unjust tax on American families, driving up the cost of everyday life,” said Representative Sherman. “Nowhere is the damage clearer than in housing. For Los Angeles families rebuilding after the wildfires, and for families across the country, tariffs have made homes harder to build. Families paid these illegal tariffs through higher prices, and they deserve to know whether the refunds will reach them. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Tokuda and Senator Warnock in calling for a full GAO audit.”

In the letter, the lawmakers raise concerns about the accuracy of the tariff refund process and question whether consumers, who bore the financial burden of higher prices as a result of the tariffs, will ultimately benefit from the refunds. Following the Supreme Court’s decision invalidating tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) and a subsequent lower-court ruling ordering repayments, roughly $100 billion of the $166 billion collected from importers had been refunded as of August 2026.

Senator Warnock continues to push back against the Trump administration’s reckless and illegal tariff agenda. Earlier this year, he introduced the Reclaim Trade Powers Act in an effort to end President Trump’s indiscriminate tariff policies, which have created uncertain market conditions for Georgia small businesses and have imposed higher prices on Georgia families.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and text is below:

“Dear Comptroller General Brown:

“On February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court issued its decision in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, holding that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) does not grant the president the power to establish tariffs. A subsequent ruling by the U.S. Court of International Trade requires the illegally collected tariffs to be refunded, and as of August 2026, about $100 billion collected under the unlawful IEEPA tariffs had been refunded, out of a total of $166 billion in tariffs charged to 330,000 importers on 53 million items.

“This is without question the largest tariff refund operation in U.S. history, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) had to create new systems and processes to handle this enormous task. We are concerned about the ability of the administration to completely and accurately refund all IEEPA tariffs. Additionally, we are concerned to what extent consumers, upon whom the financial burden of the tariffs fell, were able to receive any benefits from the refunds. For these reasons, we respectfully request that the Government Accountability Office initiate an audit and evaluation of CBP to review the following issues:

What actions has CBP taken to update its system to identify and calculate IEEPA refunds and related interest payments?

To what extent has CBP established controls to ensure IEEPA refunds are complete, accurate, properly authorized, and protected against improper or duplicate payments?

How many importers received IEEPA refunds? What sectors or industries do they represent? How much did they receive, and in which industries and product categories were refunds concentrated?

After receiving tariff refunds, how had importers transmitted the financial benefit downstream to wholesalers, retailers, or final consumers? What challenges did they encounter?

To what extent did the IEEPA refunds affect product availability, employment, investment, or firms’ decisions to absorb future cost increases?

“We hope GAO’s review will help illuminate how consumers have suffered from higher prices across a range of goods over the last year due to these unlawful IEEPA tariffs.

“Thank you for your consideration of our request.

“Sincerely,”

###

title: Welch Leads Eleven Senators in Demanding Trump Admin Secure Release of American High School Student Abducted and Held by Israeli Forces Without Charge
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) led eleven of his Senate colleagues in demanding that the Trump Administration secure the release of Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, an 18-year-old U.S. citizen and high school student, currently detained at Israel’s notorious Ofer prison. In their letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, the Senators emphasize that holding an American citizen for months without charge or due process is a violation of internationally recognized human rights, and call on the administration to directly engage with the Israeli government to secure Abdalkareem’s immediate release.

The Senators requested a response from Secretary Rubio and Ambassador Huckabee no later than November 6, 2026, given the conditions of Abdalkareem’s arbitrary detention. Abdalkareem has reported being mistreated by Israeli military forces and has contracted scabies in Ofer prison. To date, the U.S. Embassy has not been allowed to bring Abdalkareem vitamins or medicine.

Abdalkareem was abducted by Israeli forces around 3 a.m. on June 29, 2026, from his family home in the town of Jalazone, located in the occupied West Bank. He was detained just days before his 18th birthday, while in the middle of completing final high school exams.

On July 2, 2026, Israeli authorities issued an administrative detention order against Abdalkareem based on secret information not disclosed to his lawyers or family. “Administrative detention” is an abusive procedure used by Israeli authorities in the Israeli military courts whereby thousands of Palestinian civilians are held without charge or trial and without a plan to bring them to trial. Israeli authorities base most administrative detention on claims of secret information that is never seen by Palestinian detainees. At the same time, Israeli settlers occupying homes adjacent to the Palestinian villages are granted civil trials with evidence and due process. Abdalkareem’s administrative detention order expires on October 28, 2026, but can be renewed indefinitely.

“Abdalkareem’s arbitrary detention without due process is a violation of internationally recognized human rights. Ofer prison is the same facility where another American citizen, Mohammed Ibrahim, was previously held as a minor. While in detention he lost over a third of his body weight and contracted multiple illnesses, including scabies,” wrote the Senators. “On July 23, 2026, a congressional request was made to U.S. Consular Services for multivitamins and prophylactic scabies medication for Abdalkareem. On July 31, 2026, his father, Issa Safi, made a similar request. On September 23, 2026, we learned that Abdelkareem has now contracted scabies while in custody.”

The Senators continued: “Since Abdalkareem’s detention, his father has repeatedly sought consular assistance and basic information about his son’s welfare. On July 5, 2026, he contacted the U.S. Embassy’s American Citizen Services, requesting immediate intervention. We understand that Embassy staff spoke with him the same day and, in a July 8, 2026, email, indicated that they had requested permission to visit Abdalkareem and were seeking information from Israeli authorities. Yet no further updates were provided until Issa followed up on July 21, 2026, expressing urgent concern about deteriorating health conditions inside Ofer prison, including widespread malnutrition and scabies outbreaks, which he feared would put his son at serious risk. After that inquiry Embassy staff confirmed that a visit had been scheduled.”

“We understand that Embassy staff visited Abdalkareem at Ofer prison on July 23, 2026. During the visit, Abdalkareem reported being beaten during interrogation and expressed concern about missing his exams, which determine placement in university for Palestinian students. Further, he has been denied communication with his family and has had limited access to legal counsel,” the Senators continued. “We understand that the Embassy requested information from the Israeli authorities about whether Abdalkareem had been examined by medical staff upon his arrival and whether he was allowed access to the books required for his exams. In recent communications, Embassy officials informed the family that they have requested another visit, but that it would likely not occur until November.”

On July 24, 2026, the Bureau of Consular Affairs responded to a congressional inquiry that the Department “will provide all appropriate consular services” to Abdalkareem, including “necessary medication or medical attention, working to ensure detained U.S. citizens receive fair and transparent treatment, including access to legal counsel, and facilitating authorized communication with their family or others.”

The Senators concluded: “The State Department has repeatedly claimed that it ‘has no higher priority than the safety and security of U.S. citizens abroad.’ We share that view and urge you to match rhetoric with action by engaging the Israeli government directly to secure Abdalkareem’s immediate release and ensure his administrative detention order is not renewed. We further request that you inform the relevant Israeli authorities that detaining an American citizen in an Israeli military prison, without being informed of the allegations against him and without any opportunity to contest his detention, is a violation of international law and unacceptable conduct by a close ally of the United States.”

Joining Senator Welch on this letter are Sens. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), and Rev. Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.).
