title: Rep. Young Kim Introduces Tell the Government Once Act to Cut Red Tape for Americans on the Move
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) and Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) introduced the bipartisan Tell the Government Once Act to let Americans update their address with multiple federal agencies through a single online form.

Every year, millions of Americans move residences and must notify federal agencies like the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Social Security Administration (SSA), Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and U.S. Postal Service (USPS) one at a time. The IRS alone says a change of address generally takes 45 days to process. Missing even one agency can have serious consequences. Tax refunds, veterans’ benefits, Social Security payments, and important government notices can be delayed or sent to an outdated address.

The Tell the Government Once Act would streamline this outdated process by directing the General Services Administration (GSA) to create one voluntary form on Login.gov, which supports more than 180 million user accounts today. Through this secure online portal, Americans would verify their identity, enter a new address once, and decide which agencies receive it.

“Moving is stressful and expensive enough without having to track down four different federal agencies to tell each one the exact same thing,” said Rep. Young Kim. “A tax refund or a veteran’s benefit check should never go to the wrong address because of one missed form. My Tell the Government Once Act cuts through the bureaucracy so families can spend less time dealing with redundant paperwork and more time settling into their new homes.”

“We should be looking for every opportunity to make the government more efficient and easier to navigate for the American people,” said Rep. Suhas Subramanyam. “This bill does exactly that by allowing Americans to change their address though a single simple web form instead of through complicated agency documents. I’m proud to be introducing this bipartisan bill with Rep. Kim to save Americans’ time and energy.”

title: Arrington Celebrates Additional $8 Million Rural Health Investment, Including Support for West Texas
text:
Washington, D.C. – The Trump administration has announced an additional $8 million in funding through the Rural Health Transformation Program, established by Arrington's One Big Beautiful Bill, to strengthen rural health care across Texas.

The funding will support 28 rural health care providers, including Sudan Medical Clinic in Lamb County, through Texas' Rural Texas Strong initiative. These investments will help rural providers recruit and retain health care professionals, modernize medical equipment and facilities, and expand access to quality care while improving the prevention and management of chronic diseases.

In December, Arrington announced Texas had received the largest allocation of any state under the newly established Rural Health Transformation Program. As the author of the One Big Beautiful Bill, Arrington secured a historic $50 billion investment in rural health care over five years, including $1.4 billion for Texas. This latest announcement builds on the $51 million awarded in September to support 68 rural hospital districts and authorities through Texas' Make Rural Texans Healthy Again initiative.

"We won’t have the next generation of agriculture and energy producers providing America with food security and energy independence without access to basic health care in rural communities,” said Chairman Arrington. “That’s why we established the Rural Health Transformation Program through the One Big Beautiful Bill, securing a historic $1.4 billion investment for Texas. I’m proud to see the Trump Administration continuing to deliver through this program, now with $8 million for 28 rural health care providers across our state, including Sudan Medical Clinic in Lamb County. By strengthening our rural health care workforce, modernizing facilities and equipment, and expanding access to care, we’re securing a healthier, stronger future for Rural Texas.”

"President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live," said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. "We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again."

"President Trump made a historic commitment to rural America, and these investments are turning that commitment into better care for patients in communities across Texas," said Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. "This is what rural health transformation should look like: federal investment that is putting patients first, driving lasting improvements and expanding healthcare for the hardworking Americans who call these communities home."

"Your address should not determine the quality of care you receive," said Gov. Greg Abbott. "Rural Texas will not be left behind. This more than $8 million investment will expand access to care, strengthen facilities across Texas communities, and help to recruit and retain the next generation of healthcare professionals."

title: TAPinto article on Smith's remarks on Alzheimer's'Rep. Chris Smith Highlights Alzheimer's Research Advances, Calls for Greater Support for Patients and Caregivers'
text:
By Jeanne Wall

Published October 23, 2026 at 12:48 AM

NEW JERSEY — As millions of Americans live with Alzheimer’s disease and families shoulder the growing demands of caregiving, U.S. Rep. Chris Smith is highlighting advances in research, the importance of early detection and the need for continued federal investment in treatment and support.

Smith (R-N.J.), founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Alzheimer’s Caucus, delivered remarks Oct. 22 at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ first-ever Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Summit. The gathering brought attention to ongoing research, care challenges and efforts to improve the lives of people affected by Alzheimer’s and related dementias.

“Special thanks to Secretary Kennedy for his amazing efforts to combat Alzheimer’s Disease and for hosting the first-ever Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Summit,” Smith said.

He also thanked the summit’s panelists for helping bring renewed attention to the disease and efforts to alleviate its symptoms and ultimately find a cure.

Smith has been involved in Alzheimer’s advocacy for more than two decades. In 1999, he and Sen. Ed Markey established the bipartisan Congressional Alzheimer’s Caucus, which Smith continues to co-chair. He also sponsored the Ronald Reagan Alzheimer’s Breakthrough Act, which proposed doubling National Institutes of Health funding for Alzheimer’s research to $1.4 billion annually.

A significant legislative milestone followed in 2011, when Congress passed the National Alzheimer’s Project Act, which Smith co-authored. The law established a national strategy to address Alzheimer’s disease and created an advisory committee to coordinate a federal response.

According to Smith, federal Alzheimer’s research funding through the NIH has grown from $600 million in 2015 to more than $3.8 billion in fiscal year 2026, an increase of more than 600%.

“This funding has yielded real, tangible advancements in our understanding of Alzheimer’s and other dementias,” Smith said.

He pointed to a new NIH-funded biomarker test developed earlier this year that can distinguish between stages of Alzheimer’s disease, describing the research as an important advance in identifying the disease earlier and helping mitigate cognitive decline.

Understanding Alzheimer’s disease and the need for early detection

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive brain disorder that damages memory and thinking skills and eventually interferes with a person’s ability to carry out everyday activities. It is the most common cause of dementia, an umbrella term for conditions that affect memory, reasoning and other cognitive abilities.

Although Alzheimer’s is more common among older adults, it is not a normal part of aging. Researchers continue to investigate its causes, how it progresses and how treatments may help people maintain cognitive function for longer.

Early detection is an increasingly important part of that effort. While there is currently no cure, some treatments can slow the progression of Alzheimer’s in certain people during the early stages of the disease. An earlier diagnosis can also help patients and families discuss treatment options, plan for future care and access support services.

Research into biomarkers — measurable biological signs of disease — is expanding the tools available to researchers and clinicians. Some blood-based tests can help identify biological changes associated with Alzheimer’s, while newer research is exploring ways to assess disease stages and predict progression. These advances may improve diagnosis and treatment planning, although testing must be interpreted in the context of a person's symptoms and clinical evaluation.

The scale of the disease underscores the urgency. According to the Alzheimer’s Association’s 2026 Facts and Figures report, an estimated 7.4 million Americans age 65 and older are living with Alzheimer’s dementia. Without medical breakthroughs to prevent or cure the disease, that number could rise to approximately 13.8 million by 2060.

New Jersey is also significantly affected. The Alzheimer’s Association estimates that 185,000 state residents age 65 and older are living with Alzheimer’s disease, with hundreds of thousands of family caregivers providing essential support to people with dementia.

Despite advances in research and growing awareness, many people with dementia remain undiagnosed or unaware of their diagnosis. In his summit remarks, Smith cited an estimate that 58% of older adults in the United States with probable dementia are either undiagnosed or unaware of their diagnosis.

Caregivers face mounting demands

Beyond the effects on patients, Alzheimer’s disease places substantial emotional, physical and financial demands on families. Caregivers often help with daily activities, medical appointments, medications and household needs as the disease progresses, frequently while balancing jobs and responsibilities to other family members.

Smith cited estimates that more than 12 million family members and other unpaid caregivers provided approximately 19.6 billion hours of care to people living with Alzheimer’s or other dementias in 2025.

“We can and should do more to ease the financial, physical, and mental burdens these caregivers face,” Smith said.

The Alzheimer’s Association’s national data similarly illustrate the magnitude of that responsibility. Its 2026 report estimates that unpaid dementia caregiving reached an economic value of more than $446 billion in 2025, reflecting the extensive work performed by family members and friends outside the paid health care system.

Access to reliable information, caregiver education, respite services and community support can help families navigate the challenges of caring for a loved one with dementia. Such services are especially important as the number of people living with Alzheimer’s is expected to grow.

Continued federal focus

Smith welcomed the announcement of a new National Plan at the summit and emphasized the importance of continued engagement with advocates and caregivers.

He credited organizations such as the Alzheimer’s Association and individuals who share their personal experiences with helping advance research funding and support for affected families. Among those he recognized was his friend Christine Hopkins.

Smith said he hopes the summit’s discussions will offer further insight into the experiences of people living with Alzheimer’s and identify ways for the federal government to advance innovation, improve care and support, and strengthen prevention efforts.

The broader challenge, he said, remains finding better ways to address the disease while working toward a cure.

In his closing remarks, Smith expressed hope for continued progress in research and treatment, ending with the aspiration that, “one day, God willing, a cure” will be found.

title: Ciscomani Honors the Life and Legacy of Senator Jon Kyl
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani is honoring the life and legacy of Senator Jon Kyl, who passed away on September 17.

After Senator Jon Kyl’s passing, Rep. Ciscomani submitted the following text into the United States Congressional Record, to honor and remember the significant impact he had on Arizona and our nation.

"Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor the incredible life and legacy of Jon Kyl, a towering figure in the history of Arizona, who sadly passed on September 17, 2026.

Among the many thoughtful, forceful leaders our state has benefited from since joining the union in 1912, Jon Kyl was in a class all his own. His accomplishments as a member of this body and as a Senator are the stuff of legend. The Arizona that my family and seven and a half million others call home is a state that Jon Kyl helped shape.

Born in Nebraska and raised in Iowa, he moved west, looking forward to the future ahead of him. Jon Kyl earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona in 1964. This year, 2026, marks the 60th anniversary of his graduation from the University of Arizona law school. What he has achieved since then is an inspiration to anyone who aspires to a career in public service.

Over the course of his 26 years in office, Jon Kyl forged a reputation as a tireless workhorse and a principled leader. He also was a formidable campaigner, an articulate messenger and a fierce debater. Unlike me and many of my colleagues, Jon Kyl never lost an election.

His experience, judgment, and common sense are why Arizonans entrusted him with the responsibility to be our advocate in Washington. These are the same reasons I trusted him also. Among the very first I ever cast as a naturalized American, was a vote for Jon Kyl as United States Senator in 2006.

Senator Kyl set a high standard for representing Arizona in Congress. I believe everyone who knows him can agree that he is the truest embodiment of the word 'statesman.' He always prioritized the long-term good of our country over party or personal gain, and he did so with a moral compass that was spot-on.

Senator Kyl had a significant impact on me throughout the years. He was generous with his time even before I was elected, and after I became a Member of Congress, he gave me invaluable advice that went beyond the job. He shared with me how to take care of my family while working for the people of Arizona, words of wisdom which I still hold to.

I was extremely honored at the opportunity to speak on his life and legacy at the University of Arizona's inaugural Kyl Institute for National Security Forum in January. To know such a man as Jon Kyl was a privilege. I was proud to share how he impacted me and countless others, along with this amazing state we call home.

Senator Kyl had an indelible influence in Arizona, and I am proud to have witnessed the ways in which he served so faithfully. I thank him for all the work he did. The great state of Arizona would not be the same today without it.

In regard to his wife Caryll, his children and grandchildren, and all his loved ones and close friends, I am truly sorry for their loss. May my dear friend rest in peace."

Rep. Ciscomani will be attending Senator Kyl’s memorial service tomorrow, October 24.

You can find Rep. Ciscomani’s congressional record honoring Senator Jon Kyl HERE.

title: Rep. Crane Introduces Bill to Address San Carlos Irrigation Project Power Issues
text:
Yesterday, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) introduced H.R. 10864, the San Carlos Irrigation Project Divestiture Act of 2026, to end federal ownership of the San Carlos Irrigation Project (SCIP) electric system. The legislation seeks to address longstanding reliability and affordability problems facing roughly 10,000 residential customers.

Congress created SCIP in 1924 to irrigate land on the Gila River Indian Reservation and surrounding areas, later adding a hydroelectric system at Coolidge Dam. Over the following decades, the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) extended SCIP’s lines to homes and businesses across approximately 2,400 square miles. However, low river flows limited the dam’s output, and a flood in 1983 halted generation entirely.

SCIP now relies on short-term deals and the day-ahead market for power, as federal procedures make long-term contracts hard to secure. In turn, customers face expensive and inconsistent service. Because some facilities are more than 80 years old and SCIP cannot issue bonds to upgrade them, ratepayers absorb the cost through higher rates. Congress passed legislation in 1991 to authorize divestiture, but the conditions for the transfer were not met by the law’s 1992 deadline. Since then, efforts have stalled while the issues have worsened for rural Arizonans.

Rep. Crane’s bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to transfer SCIP’s electric transmission and distribution system, excluding Coolidge Dam and its generating facilities, following a plan developed with federal, state, Tribal, local, and private stakeholders. Importantly, the measure would waive the 1991 law’s reversion clause, which kept the system in government hands after the 1992 deadline passed, so the outdated provision could no longer block this new effort. It also preserves the Interior Department’s existing SCIP responsibilities under the Arizona Water Settlements Act. More broadly, the Secretary would be authorized to contract with Tribes, or other mutually agreed-upon entities, to sell, operate, or maintain BIA-run electric systems, subject to congressional review.

Rep. Crane believes the BIA was never meant to be a residential power company, and divestiture would free SCIP’s electric grid from nearly a century of bureaucratic constraints. After hearing from constituents whose livelihoods have suffered from unreliable, costly service, he asked the U.S. Department of the Interior’s Office of Inspector General in September 2025 to investigate SCIP. With no meaningful findings more than a year later, he drafted this measure with input from customers, Tribal leaders, and utility providers.

title: Dingell Statement on EPA Agreement with Gelman Sciences to Address Contaminated Aquifer in Ann Arbor
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (MI-06) released the following statement in response to the Environmental Protection Agency’s legal agreement with Gelman Sciences LLC to address 1,4-dioxane contamination in Scio Township and the City of Ann Arbor and establish the responsibilities for long-term remedial planning and near-term response actions.

"This agreement between the EPA and Gelman Sciences is a major step forward in addressing the decades-long contamination of our community's drinking water and environment. After six decades of advocacy from residents, local officials, and community leaders, we are seeing meaningful action to advance the cleanup of the Gelman site. This agreement establishes responsibilities for critical cleanup work, strengthens federal oversight, and moves us closer to the long-term restoration of the groundwater.

"Washtenaw County has lived with the impacts of 1,4-dioxane contamination for far too long. This will help accelerate the investigation and cleanup of the contamination, reduce the spread of the groundwater plume, and provide the community with additional resources to better understand the work ahead. This progress reflects the persistence of a community that has never stopped fighting for safe drinking water and accountability.

"I want to thank the EPA for their continued work and attention to this issue and for taking action to move this forward. I have spent years working with residents, federal, state, and local officials to ensure the Gelman plume receives the oversight and resources it deserves, and I will continue that work until the job is done. I will continue working with the EPA, state and local partners, and the community to ensure this cleanup is transparent, Gelman Sciences is held accountable, and residents have safe drinking water. Our communities deserve nothing less."

The agreement, known as an administrative settlement agreement and order on consent, requires Gelman Sciences to:

Conduct a remedial investigation and feasibility study which will determine the nature and extent of the contamination and evaluate potential cleanup approaches.

Excavate soils contaminated with 1,4-dioxane from the former burn pit area on Gelman’s property.

Increase the groundwater extraction and treatment rates in the eastern groundwater plume to reduce the spread of groundwater contamination.

Install additional groundwater monitoring wells to further define the easternmost extent of 1,4-dioxane groundwater contamination.

Provide grant funding for community groups to hire an independent technical advisor to help interpret and explain technical reports, site conditions, and the EPA’s proposed actions.

title: Dingell Presses United Airlines CEO After Continued Mishandling of Sexual Harassment on Flights

U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (MI-06) is calling for answers from United Airlines regarding reports of another incident of sexual harassment involving a woman seated next to a man who allegedly performed a lewd sexual act beside her. Reports indicate that no flight crew members assisted the woman, forcing her to climb over the alleged assailant’s seat to seek help.

The staff eventually moved the woman to another seat but did not alert authorities about the sexual act. In its response, United confirmed that it is opening an investigation but is not required to report passenger sexual misconduct to police or a federal agency.

“This second incident raises serious questions about United’s sexual misconduct protocol and its commitment to passenger safety, specifically the safety of women,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “United’s claim in its written response that they are working to strengthen its policies and training protocols is not enough. It is past time for United to have ‘conversations in their leadership meetings,’ as a customer service supervisor told the San Diego passenger. We need action, and we need it now.”

The Congresswoman continued, “Incidents like these are not exclusive to United, and sexual misconduct is a broader issue across the airline industry that demands attention and accountability. That is why I will be introducing legislation to strengthen passenger protections and ensure airlines take appropriate action in response to sexual misconduct. Addressing this kind of behavior is essential to ensuring that women can travel with safety and dignity. Airlines must do better.”

Last month, Congresswoman Dingell led a letter with the Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) demanding answers about a similar alleged assault that took place on another United Airlines flight. The airline responded in a letter stating that the company is looking into the matter. Congresswoman Dingell announced she is drafting new legislation to strengthen passenger protections and ensure airlines take appropriate action in response to sexual misconduct.

A copy of the follow-up letter to United Airlines can be found HERE and text is below:

Dear Mr. Kirby and Ms. Fariello:

This letter is regarding the second reported incident in less than a month involving a United Airlines passenger subjected to a passenger’s lewd behavior and an inadequate response from the airline. On a recent United flight from San Diego to Newark, a woman reported the misconduct to the flight crew and had to ask multiple times to change seats. Afterward, she was not given any guidance about reporting the incident until she contacted United herself days later. This follows reports from last month about a nearly identical incident, which I addressed in a letter to United alongside the Democratic Women’s Caucus on October 6, 2026. In its October 16, 2026, response, United provided an insufficient explanation, largely deferring responsibility for the incident to their regional partner, Republic Airways, who operated the flight, despite their own admission that Republic is under United’s operational control.

This second incident raises serious questions about United’s sexual misconduct protocol and its commitment to passenger safety, specifically the safety of women. United’s claim in its written response that they are working to strengthen its policies and training protocols is not enough. It is past time for United to have “conversations in their leadership meetings,” as a customer service supervisor told the San Diego passenger. We need action, and we need it now.

Incidents like these are not exclusive to United, and sexual misconduct is a broader issue across the airline industry that demands attention and accountability. That is why I will be introducing legislation to strengthen passenger protections and ensure airlines take appropriate action in response to sexual misconduct. Addressing this kind of behavior is essential to ensuring that women can travel with safety and dignity. Airlines must do better.

Please provide a written response by Friday October 30, 2026, detailing the concrete steps United will take to improve flight crews’ response to sexual misconduct incidents, including how they can more meaningfully support passengers who report inappropriate behavior.

title: Dexter, Larsen Introduce Bill to Stop Trump Admin from Rolling Back Veterans’ Benefits
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) and Rick Larsen (WA-02) introduced the Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act to restore male breast cancer as a presumptive illness under the Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act (PACT Act). October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and October 17 to 23 is Men’s Breast Cancer Awareness Week.

In September 2025, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) removed male breast cancer from the list of reproductive cancers considered presumptive under PACT to align with President Trump’s discriminatory executive orders. Male breast cancer has been linked to toxic exposure, and about 100 male veterans are diagnosed with breast cancer each year.

“Policy changes should be evidence-based and not based on political ideology and hate,” said Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. “That is why I was alarmed when last Fall, Secretary Collins removed male breast cancer as a presumptive illness to conform with Trump’s anti-trans mandates. As a member of the House Veterans Affairs Committee, I am proud to co-lead this bill with Rep. Larsen to restore male breast cancer as a presumptive condition under the PACT Act.”

“I am committed to ensuring veterans can access high-quality, timely health care for illnesses related to their military service, and this bill is an important step towards guaranteeing that,” said Representative Larsen. “Male veterans with breast cancer should not be denied the benefits they’ve earned because of this Administration’s political agenda.”

The legislation would designate male breast cancer as a presumptive illness under the PACT Act. PACT creates a presumption of service connection for certain disabilities and illnesses that have been linked to exposure to hazardous substances during military service.

The Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act is supported by the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) and Burn Pits 360, the only 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization to offer an independent burn pit exposure registry in which family members can record the names of warriors who served the nation but have passed away due to illnesses from toxic injury.

“Male breast cancer is rare, often caught late, and too easily overlooked, by patients and clinicians alike. For a veteran who breathed burn pit smoke for months or years, that diagnosis is hard enough without also wondering whether the PACT Act covers him,” said Julie Tomáška, PhD, U.S. Air Force (Ret.), Scientific Committee Chair at Burn Pits 360. “The science on military toxic exposures keeps pointing the same way: federal researchers found male breast cancer rates about 39% higher among Marines and sailors at Camp Lejeune, where the drinking water was contaminated with industrial solvents, than at Camp Pendleton. Yet last year VA stopped presuming those men's cancers are service-connected, while women with the same diagnosis still are. Reps. Larsen and Dexter's bill removes the guesswork and writes the answer into law, so every veteran, claims examiner and advocate works from the same clear standard.”

title: Fitzpatrick Introduces Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act to Block Russian Oil Imports and Defend Ukraine
text:
Bipartisan legislation would nullify Treasury's Russian oil waiver, reinforce federal law, and safeguard critical intelligence support for Ukraine

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1), Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and Chair of the House Intelligence Committee’s CIA Subcommittee, introduced the Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act of 2026, alongside Representatives Don Bacon (NE-2) and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-3), to uphold the federal prohibition on Russian energy imports and protect critical U.S. intelligence support for Ukraine.

The legislation follows the Treasury Department's October 9th issuance of General License 135, authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, including imports into the United States, despite a bipartisan federal law enacted in 2022 prohibiting Russian energy imports. The decision threatens to undermine congressional efforts to cut off the revenue streams sustaining Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine.

“Russia chose this war. Ukraine did not. The United States must leave no doubt about where it stands. We must not import a single drop of Russian oil. Congress made that decision with overwhelming bipartisan support in 2022, and that law remains in force. It is not a suggestion, nor should its intent be undermined through administrative waivers. We cannot demand accountability from Putin while opening American markets to the Russian energy that helps finance his war. Every exception sends Moscow the wrong message: that American resolve can be outlasted,” said Fitzpatrick. “President Reagan understood that strength is not the obstacle to peace. It is what makes a just peace possible. Our responsibility is to stand firmly behind Ukraine’s sovereignty and ensure America’s commitments are reflected in America’s actions. Peace becomes possible when aggression carries a cost greater than its reward. On that, there can be no ambiguity.”

“For years, President Trump criticized Europe for buying Russian energy and propping up Putin’s war economy. Further, Congress overwhelmingly voted to impose tough sanctions on Russia. Now, Trump wants to make it easier for Putin to sell diesel fuel. He is wrong,” said Bacon. “Americans overwhelmingly support Ukraine and oppose Putin’s aggression and war crimes. The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Against Russia Act nullifies the Russian diesel waiver, prohibits Treasury spending that violates the 2022 Russian oil import ban and provides intelligence support to Ukraine.” Congress must step up and force the President to support freedom and oppose the war criminal. America must stand with the Free World.”

“The President’s dirty deal to import Russian oil is running roughshod over our national interests and the bipartisan will of Congress and a bipartisan 2022 law explicitly banning the import of Russian oil. We won’t turn a blind eye to that,” said Gluesenkamp Perez. “This bill will rein in this reckless deal and make clear that my community doesn’t want any part of funding Putin’s fascist war in Ukraine and the ongoing attacks terrorizing families in the Donbas. If the President is serious about bringing down gas prices, he should end the war in Iran, not send our tax dollars to Putin.”

“The Administration’s decision to import Russian diesel is illegal, and Congress must move decisively to ensure the law is followed,” Daniel Balson, Director of Advocacy and Razom for Ukraine said. “Razom for Ukraine endorses Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick’s Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act and applauds the bipartisan effort to block the unlawful and immoral importation of Russian diesel. Only by projecting strength can we force Russia to come to the negotiating table. Weakness and deference will only prolong Putin’s war.”

“FDD Action applauds the introduction of the bipartisan legislation. The timely Congressional action represents a strategic and moral intervention on behalf of the bipartisan majority of American’s who support Ukraine in its fight for freedom. We urge members of Congress to support this crucial legislation and urge the Trump Administration to reconsider its diesel deal with the Kremlin," said Daniel Vaynshteyn, Associate Director of Government Relations, FDD Action.

The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act would:

Nullify the Treasury Department's Russian oil waiver, immediately rendering General License 135 ineffective and prohibiting future waivers or general licenses authorizing the importation of Russian energy products.

Strengthen enforcement of the existing import ban by prohibiting Treasury from expending funds on agreements that violate the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022.

Reinforce critical intelligence support for Ukraine, requiring relevant intelligence agencies to provide support for Ukraine's defense and notify congressional intelligence committees within 24 hours of any interruption.

Read the full text here.

Background

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and Chair of the House Intelligence Committee's CIA Subcommittee, Fitzpatrick has been at the forefront of bipartisan efforts to confront Russian aggression, strengthen Ukraine's defenses, and advance an American strategy rooted in peace through strength. His leadership has been informed by firsthand visits to Ukraine, including areas near the front lines, working closely with President Zelenskyy, Ukrainian military leaders, servicemembers, and civilians defending their nation against Russia's brutal and unprovoked invasion.

In Congress, Fitzpatrick has helped lead efforts to provide Ukraine with critical security assistance, expand sanctions against Russia, and hold the Kremlin accountable for its atrocities. His work includes helping advance the Ukraine Support Act through the House, championing the Peace Through Strength Against Russia Act, introducing the Countering Russia's War on Faith Act to address the persecution of religious communities, and leading bipartisan legislation demanding the return of abducted Ukrainian children. Most recently, he helped lead the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 through Congress and into law, establishing sweeping measures targeting the financial institutions, energy revenues, and sanctions-evasion networks sustaining Putin's war.

The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act builds on that record by reinforcing the existing prohibition on Russian energy imports, closing the door to administrative waivers, and protecting the intelligence support essential to Ukraine's defense. Together, these efforts reflect Fitzpatrick's longstanding commitment to a clear American objective: equip Ukraine to defend its freedom, deny Putin the resources to sustain his aggression, and secure a just and lasting peace that preserves Ukraine's sovereignty and independence.

title: Fitzpatrick Secures $1 Million to Revitalize Downtown Quakertown and Strengthen Critical Infrastructure
text:
Major investment will modernize essential infrastructure, enhance public spaces, and support long-term economic growth in the heart of Quakertown Borough.

Quakertown, PA — Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) announced a major victory for Quakertown Borough, securing $1 million in federal Community Project Funding for a comprehensive revitalization of its downtown district—modernizing critical infrastructure, improving accessibility and public safety, and strengthening the foundation for long-term economic growth and community development.

Building on Quakertown's ongoing downtown revitalization efforts, this investment will help strengthen the heart of the Borough as a center of commerce, connection, and community life. By enhancing public spaces, improving essential infrastructure, and creating a more accessible and welcoming downtown, the project will support local businesses, enhance quality of life for residents, and create new opportunities for the community's continued growth.

“Across Bucks and Montgomery Counties, our Main Streets are the pulse of our communities—supporting local businesses, creating jobs, and giving each of our towns its distinct character. For years, I've worked alongside business owners and community leaders to ensure our historic downtowns are not simply preserved, but positioned to prosper. In Quakertown, Borough leaders, local businesses, and residents have demonstrated tremendous initiative in revitalizing their downtown and laying the groundwork for future growth. Together, we identified the infrastructure improvements needed to build on that momentum, attract new investment, and expand economic opportunity, and I was proud to secure $1 million to help advance those efforts. I’m grateful for their partnership, and look forward to building on this progress together as Quakertown continues to thrive,” said Fitzpatrick.

Remarking on the significant of the funding, Doug Propst, Quakertown Borough Director of Finance, stated: “The Borough of Quakertown is extremely grateful to receive this $1 million investment from the federal government. These funds will be used in the Borough’s continued efforts to improve the downtown for residents, business, and visitors to Quakertown. We are especially grateful to Congressman Fitzpatrick for his efforts in obtaining this funding and commitment to the continued improvement of the community.”

Revitalizing Downtown Quakertown, Strengthening the Local Economy

The Quakertown Borough Streetscape Improvement Project will make targeted investments in the infrastructure and public spaces that support a vibrant, accessible, and economically resilient downtown.

Key project improvements include:

Modernized Parking and Downtown Accessibility: Renovating public parking facilities to improve convenience, circulation, and access to downtown businesses and community destinations.

Safer, More Connected Pedestrian Infrastructure: Upgrading pedestrian pathways and creating a new gateway to a future trail, strengthening walkability and connectivity throughout the downtown district.

Improved Stormwater Management and Infrastructure Reliability: Enhancing drainage systems and relocating electrical utilities underground to improve resilience, reliability, safety, and the appearance of downtown streets.

Stronger Foundations for Economic Growth: Creating more welcoming public spaces that complement the Borough’s ongoing investments in green space, public art, and downtown revitalization, encouraging greater foot traffic and supporting local commerce.

Delivering For Pennsylvania’s First District

The Quakertown streetscape project builds on Fitzpatrick's broader efforts to revitalize historic downtowns, support small businesses, modernize essential infrastructure, and strengthen local economies throughout Bucks and Montgomery counties.

Through the FY2026 Community Project Funding process, Fitzpatrick successfully championed more than $27.5 million for 11 community projects addressing critical local needs across Pennsylvania’s First District.

With this latest round of funding, Fitzpatrick has brought more than $80 million in federal Community Project Funding to PA-01 since FY2022, translating priorities identified by local communities into lasting investments in the people, services, and infrastructure that strengthen the region.

Together, these investments reflect Fitzpatrick’s community-first leadership, empowering local organizations, responding to community needs, and ensuring federal resources translate into meaningful, measurable, and lasting benefits for Bucks and Montgomery counties.

title: Gallagher Joins Bipartisan Push to Get Fix Our Forests Act Signed Into Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) joined a bipartisan coalition of House lawmakers in urging congressional leadership to include the Fix Our Forests Actin the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) or another moving legislative package to ensure the wildfire prevention legislation becomes law before the end of this Congress.

In a letter to House Speaker Mike Johnson, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers, and Ranking Member Adam Smith, the lawmakers warned that increasingly destructive wildfires are threatening American communities and military readiness. They called for immediate action on the bipartisan legislation, which would improve forest management and accelerate wildfire mitigation projects.

“Northern California knows all too well the devastation wildfires leave behind. We can avoid the billions of dollars in destruction by doing the vital work now to prevent these fires in the first place,” said Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01). “The bipartisan Fix Our Forests Act is a commonsense solution that will help us better manage our forests and protect our communities. Wildfires are also a growing threat to our military readiness and national security. The House has done its job. Now it’s time to get this bill in the FY2027 NDAA or any other legislative vehicle to ensure it is signed into law before the end of this Congress.”

The letter highlights the severity of the 2026 wildfire season, with roughly 66,000 fires burning more than 9 million acres nationwide by October. The United States spent 48 consecutive days at the highest national wildfire preparedness level, placing significant strain on firefighting resources.

Lawmakers also emphasized the growing threat wildfires pose to national security, pointing to the importance of proactive forest management in protecting military installations. At Beale Air Force Base in Northern California, the 9th Civil Engineer Squadron has taken a proactive approach by conducting prescribed burns to reduce hazardous vegetation and protect critical military infrastructure. Beale's efforts demonstrate how fighting fire with fire can reduce wildfire risks before disaster strikes, offering valuable lessons for protecting communities and strengthening military readiness nationwide.

Beyond the immediate danger, wildfires impose enormous financial costs on American families and taxpayers. The letter cites estimates placing the annual economic burden of wildfires between nearly $400 billion and $900 billion, while federal fire suppression costs average more than $2.5 billion annually.

The Fix Our Forests Act would help address these challenges by improving forest health and streamlining wildfire mitigation efforts before disasters strike. According to the letter, every dollar invested in wildfire mitigation can prevent approximately $3.75 in future damages.

The bipartisan coalition emphasized that the legislation has undergone a comprehensive committee process in both chambers and represents an opportunity for Congress to deliver meaningful wildfire reform.

“The wildfire crisis cannot wait,” the lawmakers wrote, urging congressional leadership to advance the legislation through the NDAA or another legislative vehicle before the end of the year.

title: Rep. Gallagher Calls for FBI Crackdown on Illegal Marijuana Operations in Northern California
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) appeared on Fox Business to call for federal action against illegal marijuana growing operations across Northern California, warning that suspected transnational criminal networks are overwhelming local law enforcement and threatening the North State's natural resources.

During the interview, Gallagher highlighted estimates of more than 7,000 illegal marijuana grows in Siskiyou County alone, raising concerns about possible connections to Chinese organized crime networks and Mexican drug cartels. He has called on FBI Director Kash Patel to provide federal investigative support to help local authorities dismantle the criminal enterprises behind these operations.

“What we've had is California decided to legalize recreational marijuana, and they brought a lot of those California taxes to it,” Gallagher said. “The people who actually went legit have been really hurt by the business. But the illicit market has grown exponentially, especially up in my district in the North State.”

Gallagher warned that illegal operations are damaging Northern California's forests and watersheds through the use of hazardous pesticides and other prohibited agricultural chemicals. He also raised concerns about possible human trafficking, noting that individuals found tending illegal grows may not be the people financing or controlling the operations.

The Congressman emphasized that investigators need to follow the money to determine whether shell companies and foreign criminal networks are financing the activity.

“That's why I've asked FBI Director Kash Patel to come in and provide some federal support, some federal investigation to really get to the bottom of this transnational criminal enterprise,” Gallagher said.

Gallagher also criticized Governor Gavin Newsom for failing to provide sufficient state resources to combat the growing problem, arguing that rural Northern California has been neglected while illegal operations continue to expand.

“We have not been getting the kind of support that we really need from our governor,” Gallagher said. “We have wanted more support from the state to help enforce the law, enforce our water quality standards, to really go after this enterprise that has just popped up in our backyard.”

Gallagher stressed that the potential involvement of international criminal organizations makes federal involvement especially important. He is seeking additional investigative resources to support local sheriffs and identify those responsible for financing and directing illegal cultivation operations.

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Visits Cowlitz County EMTs to Learn About Challenges Facing Emergency Medicine
text:
LONGVIEW, WA — Today, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez met with paramedics and EMTs at Medix Ambulance in Longview to learn about the unique challenges they face providing emergency care in and around rural communities. Emergency workers also gave the Congresswoman a tour of their facility and talked with her about their ongoing equipment needs to continue to provide high quality care. After the tour, the Congresswoman also met with members of the American Ambulance Association who recognized her with an award for her legislative excellence supporting EMTs and the EMS workforce.

Earlier this year, the Congresswoman introduced the bipartisan PARA EMT Act to address EMS staffing shortages by making it easier for experienced veterans to transition from medics to becoming certified paramedics and EMTs. The bill would establish grantmaking to strengthen recruitment and retention, and to study workforce conditions. It is designed to identify any barriers and consider potential benefits of implementing recruitment and retention strategies.

“When you call emergency services, the people who respond bring with them a unique combination of skill and bravery that you can’t get anywhere else. In rural areas–where we don’t take healthcare access for granted–the passions of public service and community building mean everything.” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “Thank you to the brave men and women at Medix Ambulance for taking the time to talk with me about the challenges facing EMS workers every day. I’m proud to continue making the investment needed to build a capable and durable workforce in such a vital field.”

title: RELEASE: Ahead of Early Voting, Gottheimer Announces Actions to Protect Election Integrity
text:
Above: Gottheimer announces his Election Integrity Strategy.

FORT LEE, NJ – Today, Friday, October 23, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced the next steps in his Election Integrity Strategy: bipartisan federal actions to protect poll workers, ballot drop boxes, and the peaceful transfer of power, with early voting set to begin in New Jersey tomorrow, October 24.

“The most sacred right our Constitution affords us is the right to vote. Early voting starts in New Jersey tomorrow. We cannot allow anyone or anything — at home or from abroad — to interfere with our elections. I’m announcing new federal actions to protect our poll workers, our ballot boxes, and our elections,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

Gottheimer’s Election Integrity Strategy includes three actions:

Introducing the bipartisan Election Worker and Polling Place Protection Act, with Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2), to expand federal protections for volunteers, the people who supply and maintain election equipment, and the family members of election officials.

Introducing the bipartisan Ballot Box Protection Act, with Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), which makes explicit that damaging or destroying a ballot drop box is a federal crime, giving prosecutors clear legal ground to quickly bring cases in federal court.

Leading a bipartisan letter with Congressman Bacon to ensure the continued peaceful transition of power. Seventeen Republicans and Democrats have signed so far, pledging to safeguard the integrity of the House, defend the state certification process, recognize the winners each state certifies under its own law, support adding every state’s certified winners to the House Clerk’s roll on the first day of the new Congress, and oppose any attempt to refuse or delay the seating of a Member-elect.

Supports early voting and extending the window to vote, voting by mail, and secure mobile voting.

Supports multilingual voting information at polling locations.

Pushing to increase Help America Vote Act funding to New Jersey so every county has the polling locations and machines it needs.

Opposes new barriers to voting, such as requiring a passport to register

Warns that foreign adversaries are using AI and social media to undermine American elections, including Russia, China, North Korea, and Iran.

Gottheimer, a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and Co-Chairman of the 9/11 Commission Review Task Force, witnessed the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol from the House Chamber. In 2022, working with Senator Susan Collins (R-ME) and the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, he led the House effort to pass the bipartisan, bicameral Electoral Count Reform Act, which is now law and closed the loopholes extremists tried to use to subvert the 2020 election.

“Protecting the integrity of our elections is essential to maintaining the public’s trust in our democratic process. Every American deserves to know that their vote will be counted and protected from interference. Those who intentionally destroy ballots or damage ballot boxes must be held accountable. I’m proud to once again join Congressman Gottheimer in introducing this bipartisan legislation to safeguard our elections and ensure every lawful vote is counted,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis.

Nationally, 38 percent of local election officials report experiencing threats, harassment, or abuse for doing their jobs, and about one in six said they had faced threats of violence. The Justice Department’s Election Threats Task Force reviewed more than 2,000 reports of threats and, by fall 2024, had charged just 20 people. In 2024, ballot drop boxes in Oregon and Washington State were set on fire, and the ballots inside were burned.

Last November, bomb threats forced polling places in Paterson, Ewing, and Bergen County to close temporarily, with additional threats at locations in Ocean, Monmouth, Essex, and Middlesex counties. Voters were redirected, officials later determined there was no credible threat, and a juvenile was arrested.

Gottheimer was joined by Senator Gordon Johnson, Bergen County Executive Jim Tedesco, Bergen County Clerk John Hogan, Fort Lee Mayor Mark Sokolich, Fort Lee Councilwoman Ila Kasofsky, Co-Executive Director of Amber Reedof AAPI NJ, and Fort Lee Councilmen Peter J. Suh and Harvey Sohmer.

Below: Gottheimer announces his Election Integrity Strategy.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Good afternoon. Thank you for welcoming us here to the Fort Lee Community Center.

I want to thank you all for your important work protecting our election workers, ballot boxes, and our democracy.

The most sacred right our Constitution affords us is the right to vote. That right is core to our democracy, our freedom, and fundamental to how we govern and to the peaceful transfer of power.

It’s also a reminder, that in the United States of America, the power is with the people. It’s a gift that many countries don’t afford. Thomas Jefferson wrote that governments derive “their just powers from the consent of the governed.” Voting is how we give that consent. It’s a chance for every American to have their voice heard, and to hold our leaders accountable. It’s why Lincoln rightly declared that “the ballot is stronger than the bullet.” In short, the right to vote at the polling booth right here or at the ballot box. It’s a huge privilege – and an enormous responsibility.

That’s exactly why we are here today.

Early voting starts in New Jersey tomorrow. We cannot allow anyone – or anything – at home or from abroad – to interfere with our elections. Today, I’m announcing new federal actions to protect our poll workers, our ballot boxes, and our elections.

Let me start with the poll workers who, beginning with early voting tomorrow, will help ensure we have free and fair elections. Thousands of poll workers here in New Jersey and across America are about to take on that critical responsibility of overseeing the voting process in the 2026 election.

Unfortunately, if the past is prologue, many of them will face unprecedented threats just for doing the job. We saw it right here in our own state last November. Emailed bomb threats forced polling places in northern and central New Jersey to close temporarily, in Paterson, in Ewing, and even here in Bergen County — along with threats at locations in Ocean, Monmouth, Essex, and Middlesex counties. Voters were redirected. Officials later determined there was no credible threat, and a juvenile was arrested. The disruption was real, and so was the fear. We cannot allow that to happen again.

According to the Brennan Center, thirty-eight percent of local election officials report experiencing threats, harassment, or abuse for doing their jobs. In their latest survey, about one in six said they’d faced threats of violence.

When threats come, accountability too often doesn’t. The Justice Department’s Election Threats Task Force reviewed more than two thousand reports of threats. By fall 2024, it had charged just twenty people. That’s absurd.

It should come as no surprise that experienced poll workers are quitting, and fewer people are willing to sign up. We are losing the very people who make our elections work, at the moment their work matters most.

Our poll workers and election officials are patriots. They serve not a particular party, but their fellow citizens and country, and they’re protecting the right to vote – and I’m taking steps today to protect them. The voices of Americans should echo in polling places, not the voices of bullies and extremists.

But, given online chatter, direct words from the President and his team, and what’s happened in recent elections, far too many Americans have lost faith in our system.

Many tell me that they lie awake at night worried that ICE or others from the Administration will interfere with the upcoming elections, or attempt, after the fact, to undermine the election results, including refusing to seat duly elected members of Congress.

It is imperative that Congress take every step to help restore our faith in the elections. As a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Co-Chairman of the 9/11 Commission Review Task Force, I understand what is at stake when the public trust is undermined. I witnessed it first-hand on January 6, 2021, in the Chamber of the United States House of Representatives.

I was in the House Chamber, and saw, with my own eyes, holding a gas mask, lawless thugs from the Proud Boys and Oath Keepers, including some from our own state, breach the United States Capitol. These insurrectionists used American flagpoles to beat police officers.

But, that night, after the chaos, we went back to work. We refused to let the insurrectionists thwart the will of the American people. Democrats and Republicans, together, finished the job and certified the election. I stood on the House floor next to my friend Tom Reed, then a Republican Congressman from New York and, at the time, my co-chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus. He crossed the aisle to stand with us.

That evening, I told the House: “Today, a group of lawless thugs sought to upend the Constitution and the peaceful transition of power because they didn’t like the outcome of the Presidential election.” But their attempt to obstruct democracy failed. “Their insurrection was foiled.”

Election denialism not only undermines our democracy; it also leads to the threats and violence we are talking about today. We cannot, and will not, tolerate election denialism or unrest. And no one should fear for their safety just for making sure ballots are counted fairly.

As I said, the threats don’t only come from a mob. There are threats coming from the current Administration to intimidate voters at polling locations. We will not let them. Our foreign adversaries are also working overtime, using AI, social media, and other online tools to try to undermine our elections. We will take every action to stop them. Ensuring secure, accessible, and reliable elections is fundamental to our national security and to the health of our democracy.

That’s why I’m proud to announce the next steps in my Election Integrity Strategy: to protect the right to vote, to protect election and poll workers, and to protect the very fabric of our democratic system from threats at home and abroad.

First, I’m reintroducing, with Congressman Don Bacon, a Republican from Nebraska, the bipartisan Election Worker and Polling Place Protection Act. It will expand protections for election workers and polling locations against threats of violence and harassment.

It protects volunteers, the people who supply and maintain election equipment, and the family members of election officials.

It covers threats against property, not just people. And, it makes it a federal crime to intentionally damage a polling place or a tabulation center.

It’s crystal clear: harassing, intimidating, or threatening an election official in a general or primary election is a crime, punishable by up to six months in jail or a $2,500 fine.

Second, I’m introducing my bipartisan Ballot Box Protection Act with Rep. Nicole Malliotakis from New York, which will make it explicit: damaging or destroying a ballot drop box is a federal crime.

Because it has happened. In 2024, in Oregon and Washington State, lawless thugs set fire to ballot drop boxes and burned the ballots voters had dropped in those boxes. One official called it a “direct attack on democracy.” That’s directly interfering with the right to vote.

In Bergen County, we have more than 35 of these ballot drop boxes. These are key to voting – especially given the President’s threats to the postal system and vote by mail. The disgusting attempts to burn ballots and erase the votes of countless citizens are un-American, and anyone who tries to interfere with our elections should be severely punished.

We need this legislation so there is legal ground to quickly prosecute, in federal court, those who commit these anti-American, anti-democratic acts. If you burn a ballot drop box, you will face a $20,000 fine for each ballot you burn and up to 20 years in prison. So, to the lawless thugs who are considering interfering with our democracy: don’t even think about it.

Third, and finally, I’m leading a bipartisan letter with Congressman Bacon to ensure the continued peaceful transition of power, and to put every one of us on the record.

This is work I’ve been doing for years. In 2022, with Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, working closely with the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, I led in the House the bipartisan, bicameral Electoral Count Reform Act. It is now the law of the land. It closed the loopholes extremists tried to use to subvert the 2020 election and to pressure the Vice President to undermine the election. There never should have been a question that a Vice President, or a slate of “fake electors,” could commandeer an election. Now, because of that law, the Vice President is purely ceremonial – he or she has no power in the election process.

In 2024, Congressman Bacon and I led the bipartisan Unity Commitment, signed by thirty-four Members of Congress, to respect the outcome of the presidential election, regardless of how it landed.

Now we’re doing it again for 2026. Seventeen of us have signed so far, Republicans and Democrats. In this letter, Members of Congress promise to safeguard the integrity of the House of Representatives, honor the votes of the citizens, and protect the 2026 congressional elections.

We pledge to defend the state certification process, including legitimate contestation within a state according to law, from outside interference. We pledge to recognize the winners each state certifies under its own law. We pledge to support the right of every state’s certified winners to be added to the House Clerk’s roll on the first day of the new Congress in January, as federal law requires. And, we pledge to oppose any attempt to refuse or delay the seating of a Member-elect who presents a validly issued election certificate. We’ve urged, and will continue to urge, all of our colleagues to join us.

Now more than ever, with domestic and foreign interference and threats to our democracy, it is critical that Americans are able to fully participate in our electoral process. Especially after the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, we in Congress must protect the right to vote and ensure every citizen can participate. Voting is the bedrock of our democracy, and protecting that right is why Congress initially passed the Help America Vote Act, or HAVA: to strengthen election systems, ensure access for every eligible voter, and invest in states like New Jersey to increase election access, resources, security, and integrity.

I’ve pushed to increase that funding to New Jersey, so that all counties have what they need – from polling locations to machines — to make exercising the right to vote, for those qualified, as easy as possible.

Protecting the vote also means making it possible to vote. Red or blue, win or lose, if you’re eligible to cast a ballot, we should make it as easy as possible, not put up barriers.

That’s why I’ve been a big supporter of early voting and of extending the window to vote. It gives working families, seniors, and folks juggling jobs and kids a real chance to make their voices heard.

It’s why I support voting by mail, and why I won’t let anyone mess with the Post Office to slow it down – and why I spoke out vociferously when the Administration directed the Postmaster General to interfere with vote-by-mail ballots.

It’s why we shouldn’t throw up new roadblocks, like requiring a passport just to register. Eligible Americans who have voted their whole lives shouldn’t be turned away because they’ve never owned one.

It’s why I believe we should ensure voting literature and information at voting locations is multilingual.

It’s why I’ve supported secure mobile voting, so that more voters can participate in our elections.

It’s why, as a member of the House Intelligence Committee, I’ve been focused for months, leading up to November, on election security and holding the administration’s feet to the fire. We cannot allow foreign governments or actors, whether that’s from Russia, China, North Korea, or Iran, to interfere with our elections.

Free and fair means two things: every eligible voter can cast a ballot, and every ballot cast is counted securely. We can, and we must, do both.

Our founders understood what was at stake. As he left the Constitutional Convention, Benjamin Franklin was asked what kind of government they had given us. His answer: “A republic, if you can keep it.”

Those leaders fought to protect our flag and our vote. We can’t let anyone intimidate us out of that inheritance. Not on our watch.

Without democracy, we would not have a country. So, again, I want to thank our courageous election workers who keep showing up, despite the efforts of those cowardly enough to try to intimidate them.

And I want to thank those who protect our ballots at drop boxes and at voting stations. We must always get their backs and show up for them, so they can work without fear as they uphold our voting process. That’s the strength of America and of our values.

With the legislation I’m announcing today, we’re taking a stand so that every voter can cast their ballot without fear, and every election worker can serve without threats. Because the right to vote is sacred, and it is our duty to defend it. There should be nothing partisan about this.

As a reminder, go to NJ.gov/vote to find your polling location. Early voting runs between 10 am and 8 pm on every day except Sunday, when the polls close at 6 pm.

In the greatest country in the world, when we put country over party, and fight to protect our election workers, our elections, and our democracy, I know that our best days will always be ahead of us.

May God bless you, your families, and may God continue to bless the United States of America.

title: Jayapal, Deluzio, Dingell, Ryan Introduce Bill to Lower Medicare Eligibility Age
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Debbie Dingell (MI-12), and Pat Ryan (NY-18) are introducing the Improving Medicare Coverage Act, legislation that would lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50 from 65 and make major coverage improvements.

“Lowering the Medicare eligibility age will be life-saving for the millions of Americans who are waiting an additional 15 years to be able to afford to see a doctor,” said Rep. Jayapal. “Expanding Medicare is not only popular, it is also morally the right thing to do. Millions leave the workforce before 65, and with Trump’s cuts to healthcare, many are now left without any options as they wait, sometimes years, for Medicare enrollment. Expanding this program is a commonsense step towards ensuring that all Americans have the care they deserve.”

“Especially after Trump’s healthcare cuts, expanding Medicare to Americans age 50 and up will save lives and get so many Americans the healthcare they need,” said Rep. Deluzio. “I am proud to support Rep. Jayapal’s Improving Medicare Coverage Act—this is an important steppingstone on the way to bigger healthcare reform where every American has good and decent healthcare.”

“For millions of Americans who cannot afford to go to the doctor, it is too late to receive preventive care by the time they reach age 65,” said Rep. Dingell. “The U.S. is the only industrialized nation that does not guarantee access to healthcare for all its citizens, and this needs to change now. I am proud to introduce this legislation to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50, improve the Medicare Savings Program, and make lifesaving drugs more affordable.”

“While Trump and Republicans cut your healthcare and raise your costs, we’re fighting back and putting your care first. But we’re not just reversing the harm – we’re building something better in its place, where millions more Americans will be able to access and afford the care they deserve right when they need it,” said Rep. Ryan. “This legislation expands healthcare coverage to millions of Americans, takes decisive action to lower costs, and makes sure that everyone who needs it has access to quality healthcare, and won’t have to wait to get the cancer screenings, preventative care, and prescriptions they need. This is a commonsense bill, and I look forward to passing it through the Democratically-controlled House next year.”

At age 50, the risks for several chronic conditions and cancers naturally increase. The median ages for many cancer diagnoses fall below 65 years of age: For instance, 61 is the average age for a breast cancer diagnosis. Adults in late middle age who lack health insurance are more likely to die or experience a preventable decline in their overall health. Lowering the healthcare eligibility age would improve the chances of being diagnosed early and surviving treatable diseases.

As of 2024, adults aged 55-64 made up 11.5 percent of the entire uninsured population in the U.S. The cuts to healthcare in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act are anticipated to remove 15 million Americans from their coverage, and 22 million Americans are paying over $1,000 more than they were before the Affordable Care Act tax credits expired. To address these cuts and the increased costs to planholders, lowering the Medicare eligibility age is an important step towards ensuring all Americans have health coverage. The legislation would also substantially reduce racial and ethnic health disparities in insurance coverage and healthcare.

In addition to lowering costs for older adults and improving patient outcomes, it is estimated that lowering the Medicare age could reduce costs for employers by up to 43 percent.

The Improving Medicare Coverage Act would:

Lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50;

Establish a Medicare Cost Assistance Program to replace the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), and the Qualifying Individual (QI) programs with one program covering specified Part A premiums and Part B premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance for individuals with incomes up to 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL).

Enhance prescription drug affordability by:

Expanding access to assistance with out-of-pocket costs under Medicare Part D for low-income seniors and individuals with disabilities;

Combining the existing Extra Help and Low Income Subsidy programs into one program;

Raising the eligibility from 135% FPL to 200% FPL; and

Removing the asset test.

Ensure that any individual making under 400% FPL who is not eligible for the Medicare Savings Program maintains the same eligibility for marketplace premium tax credits.

The Improving Medicare Coverage Act is cosponsored by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Everton Blair (GA-13), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), Salud O. Carbajal (CA-24), Greg Casar (TX-35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Steve Cohen (TN-09), J. Luis Correa (CA-46), Jason Crow (CO-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Jesús G. “Chuy” García (IL-04), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Sarah Jacobs (CA-51), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), James P. McGovern (MA-02), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Grace Meng (NY-06), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Joe Neguse (CO-02), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Adam Smith (WA-09), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).

This legislation is endorsed by Center for Health and Democracy, Labor Campaign for Single Payer, MoveOn, People’s Action Institute, Physicians for a National Health Program, Public Citizen, SEIU, United Auto Workers.

The full text of the legislation is available here.

title: Dr. Joyce Joins Logan Township United Fire Department to Celebrate Federal Investments in Public Safety
text:
October 23, 2026

Totaling $341,078, the secured grants support firefighter safety initiatives, emergency response capabilities, and community fire prevention programs

LOGAN TOWNSHIP, Pa. – On October 20, 2026, Congressman John Joyce visited the Logan Township United Fire Department at their Station 18 facility to see first-hand the federal funding he fought to secure for the department and its fire crew.

Firefighters, first responders, and officials of Logan Township United Fire Department proudly showcased the significant impact of three federal grants during a special gathering at the station.

“It was an honor to stand alongside the brave men and women of the Logan Township United Fire Department and see firsthand how the federal funding I fought for in Congress is strengthening their capabilities and helping keep our community safe,” said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “These dedicated volunteers sacrifice time away from their families to answer the call when their neighbors need them most. They deserve the best equipment, resources, and protective gear available to ensure they can carry out lifesaving missions safely and effectively. These federal investments are powerful and meaningful examples of how your tax dollars are used to directly benefit volunteer fire departments and the residents who depend upon their services.”

"On behalf of the Logan Township United Fire Department, I want to express our sincere appreciation and recognition of Congressman Dr. John Joyce for his continued support of the fire service and his commitment to the men and women who dedicate themselves to protecting our communities,” said Ronald Shoenfelt, Fire Chief of the Logan Township United Fire Department.“Volunteer fire departments face tremendous challenges in securing the financial resources necessary to provide safe and effective emergency services. Having the attention and support of our congressional representatives is critically important to our ability to meet these challenges. Congressman Joyce's personal visit to our department provided an opportunity to demonstrate firsthand the tremendous impact that federal investments have on firefighter safety and operational readiness. We are particularly grateful for his willingness to engage directly with our volunteers, recognize their sacrifices, and better understand the challenges facing today's volunteer fire service. We sincerely appreciate Congressman Joyce's recognition of the vital role that volunteer firefighters play in protecting our communities and his continued attention to the resources necessary to sustain these essential services."

BACKGROUND

The Logan Township United Fire Department used the grants to purchase 54 complete sets of structural firefighting turnout gear, acquire a slip-on firefighting tanker unit to enhance wildland firefighting capabilities and improve fire protection in areas with limited water supplies, and purchase approximately 2,800 smoke alarms and 800 combination smoke/carbon monoxide alarms for distribution to residents throughout the department’s fire protection districts.

Federal Grants Secured:

FEMA Assistance to Firefighters Grant

Federal Award: $231,428.00

Purpose: Purchase of 54 complete sets of structural firefighting turnout gear.

This equipment has been received and placed into service, representing a substantial investment in firefighter safety and the operational capabilities of the department.

U.S. Department of the Interior – Slip-On Tanker Grant

Federal Award: $35,250.00

Purpose: Acquisition of a slip-on firefighting tanker unit to enhance the department's wildland firefighting capabilities and improve fire protection in areas with limited water supplies.

FEMA Assistance to Firefighters Grant – Fire Prevention and Safety (FP&S)

Federal Award: $74,400.00

Purpose: Purchase and distribution of approximately 2,800 smoke alarms and 800 combination smoke/carbon monoxide alarms to residents throughout the fire protection districts. This initiative will allow the department to expand its community fire prevention and public education efforts by placing lifesaving detection equipment directly into the homes of residents.

Total Federal Funding: $341,078
