title: Opinion: The Next Chapter in the U.S.-Croatia Partnership
text:
If you want to understand why the relationship between the United States and Croatia matters, you do not have to look across the Atlantic. You can look around Northeast Ohio.

For more than 150 years, Croatian immigrants and their descendants have been part of the story of this region. They came to Cleveland in the late 1860s looking for opportunity, worked in our factories, on our railroads and in construction, built businesses and neighborhoods, and established churches, schools, and cultural organizations that remain part of our communities today.

That history is especially important in Ohio’s 14th Congressional District, which is home to around 10,000 Americans of Croatian ancestry—the largest Croatian American population of any congressional district in Ohio.

I grew up here. I have had the privilege of working alongside members of our Croatian American community, listening to their stories and seeing firsthand the pride they have in both their Croatian heritage and their Northeast Ohio home. Those relationships have shaped how I view our relationship with Croatia.

Croatia is not simply a country that happens to be an American ally. I see it as a country connected to our district through thousands of families, businesses, churches, and generations of shared history.

Croatia has transformed its place in the world. It joined NATO in 2009 and the European Union in 2013 and has become an important American partner in Southeast Europe. Its role in European energy security, including through the LNG terminal on the island of Krk, demonstrates the strategic value of that partnership.

Our economic relationship presents another opportunity.

As Co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Croatian Caucus, one of my priorities has been advancing the U.S.-Croatia Avoidance of Double Taxation Treaty. For Americans and Croatians who work, invest, or do business across both countries, being subject to two tax systems can create unnecessary complexity and cost. The treaty would establish clearer rules for how certain types of income are taxed and reduce the burden of double taxation.

In 2024, I led a letter with my fellow Caucus Co-Chairs urging Senate leadership to move the treaty forward. After being signed in 2022, the treaty was updated by a protocol signed in Dubrovnik in April 2026. On September 14, the Trump Administration sent the treaty to the Senate for its advice and consent to ratification.

That progress matters beyond Washington. It matters to Croatian American families in our communities and to businesses and investors abroad.

That is also why I helped relaunch the bipartisan Congressional Croatian Caucus in both the 118th and 119th Congresses. Through the Caucus, I have met with Croatia’s Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, as well as with Members of the Croatian Parliament and other Croatian leaders to discuss how our countries can work together on economic, cultural, and strategic opportunities.

The U.S. and Croatia have strong ties between our governments and institutions, but our relationship is strongest because it is built on our people.

Northeast Ohio helped make that relationship possible. Now we have an opportunity to help make it stronger.

Our Croatian American community has spent generations building Northeast Ohio. Strengthening the ties between Ohio and Croatia is one way we can build on that legacy for the next generation, and I look forward to continuing to work with my colleagues in Congress and our partners in Croatia to do so for Americans and Croatians alike.

title: Kaptur, Fitzpatrick, Quigley, Costa, Panetta, Kelly, Tillis, and Slotkin Urge Pentagon to Restore and Expand Starshield Access for Ukraine
text:
Read in the Washington Post: Ukraine says satellite access still restricted despite Trump saying otherwise

Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Congressman Mike Quigley (IL-05), Congressman Jim Costa (CA- 21), and Congressman Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), alongside US Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), urged Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and the Department of Defense (DoD) to expand its Starshield contract and restore Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite communications following recent disruptions. They specifically called for renewing unlimited-speed service to ensure Ukraine has the capacity it needs. The lawmakers also pressed the DoD to evaluate its authorities under the Defense Production Act to guarantee continued, reliable access.

“Ukrainian forces depend on these services for command and control, intelligence sharing, battlefield communications, and the operation of unmanned systems," the lawmakers wrote. “Any degradation in service, including reduced connection speeds, restricted geographic coverage, or interruptions in access, undermines Ukraine's military effectiveness and provides Russian forces with an operational advantage that will extend the conflict and put more civilians in harm's way.”

The lawmakers called on DoD to maintain the geographic coverage Ukraine needs for its lawful military operations, including over Russian territory, and to ensure any transition from commercial Starlink to government-contracted Starshield happens without interruption: “Decisions regarding service availability, coverage, and performance should not be left solely to the discretion of a private provider when they have direct consequences for Ukraine's ability to defend itself.”

In addition, the lawmakers urged DoD to evaluate its authorities under Title I of the Defense Production Act, which allows the federal government to require companies to give priority to government orders: “These authorities should be considered alongside existing contractual mechanisms to ensure that Ukraine maintains reliable access to the bandwidth, service levels, and geographic coverage required for its lawful military operations.”

“The United States and Europe have made significant investments in Ukraine's defense because of how a Russian victory would put our security at risk. Those investments should not be undermined by preventable disruptions to the communications infrastructure on which Ukrainian forces depend,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: Kaptur Office Statement On Suspicious Package Intended For Local NW Ohio Congressional Office
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, the office of Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) released the following statement regarding a suspicious package intended for delivery to her local office in Toledo, Ohio.

“Congresswoman Kaptur was advised this week that our local Northwest Ohio office was the intended recipient of a package containing a suspicious substance, similar to incidents reported involving other Congressional offices in Ohio and across the country. As earlier packages had made news nationwide, out of precaution, mail for our office was being held at a local postal facility and the package was intercepted," said Ben Kamens, Communications Director for the office of Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). "We want to thank the United States Postal Service's Postal Inspector for their swift response and efforts to ensure the safety of our Letter Carrier, Congressional staff, and Northwest Ohio constituents. We take this matter extremely seriously, and will continue to work with the Postal Inspector and both local and Federal authorities as the investigation into this package and others across the country continue. Acts of terror, harm, and intimidation have no place in our democracy and cannot be lightly dismissed. In the meantime both our Washington, and Northwest Ohio offices remain open and fully functional and will continue to serve those we represent day in and day out.”

The Congresswoman’s offices have advised constituents you can continue to reach out via her online office at Kaptur.House.Gov or you can reach her local office by phone at 419-259-7500.

title: Kean Urges Action to Make Air Travel Wheelchair Accessible
text:
(October 22, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – On Wednesday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) wrote to the Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration Bryan Bedford, and five major airline CEOs urging them to take steps toward the deployment of systems in their airline fleets to allow wheelchair users safe access to air travel.

Current Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations require wheelchair users to transfer out of their wheelchairs into a standard passenger seat and stow their wheelchairs onboard. Wheelchair users often find their expensive and essential wheelchairs damaged after being in the cargo hold leaving them with limited mobility options at their destination. For individuals with certain disabilities, the difficulty of moving into and out of a standard passenger seat can make commercial air travel physically prohibitive.

In past years, Congress has authorized reports and task forces to study the path forward to advancing in-cabin wheelchair restraint systems that allow wheelchair users to remain safely seated in their wheelchairs. A Transportation Research Board study authorized by the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 concluded that, with proper development, the implementation of in-cabin wheelchair restraint systems that meet FAA safety standards is technically feasible, and suggested further research and evaluation into the proper next steps. Now, Congressman Kean is engaging major airlines and the FAA/DOT on next steps in this process.

Congressman Kean wrote, “ I have spoken to many wheelchair users throughout New Jersey who fear the risk of their wheelchairs being damaged or lost in transit. Others highlight unique physical needs that can make transferring out of the wheelchair painful or impossible.”

Kean continued, “I respectfully request your engagement on the path forward to ensuring all Americans, regardless of physical ability, have the agency to access air travel without undue hardship.”

Read the full letter to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration Bryan Bedford HERE.

Read the full letter to airline CEOs HERE.

title: King-Hinds, NMTech Advance Effort to Bring GI Bill Benefits to Local Vocational Training
text:
Saipan – Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds announced that the Northern Marianas Technical Institute (NMTech) has formally submitted its application to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to participate in GI Bill education programs, advancing efforts to make technical and workforce training more accessible to veterans in the Commonwealth.

The effort began when a local veteran raised the issue during a King-Hinds town hall on Saipan, asking whether GI Bill benefits could be used for training at NMTech. Following that discussion, the Congresswoman met with NMTech Chief Executive Officer Jodina Attao and contacted the VA to determine what steps would be necessary for the institute to participate.

“This started with a veteran in our community raising a practical question about using the benefits they earned for training here at home,” King-Hinds said. “We took that question to the VA, worked with NMTech to understand the requirements, and now the institute has submitted its application. I am grateful to Jodina and her team for taking this important step toward expanding opportunities for our veterans.”

In response to the Congresswoman's inquiry, VA confirmed that it serves as the State Approving Agency (SAA) for educational and training institutions in the CNMI seeking approval to participate in GI Bill education programs. VA also clarified that accreditation, while helpful, is not required for an institution to pursue approval.

On August 18, 2026, VA contacted NMTech directly to outline the requirements for participation, including applicable reporting, recordkeeping, and oversight responsibilities. Following these discussions, NMTech submitted its application for approval and is now awaiting VA's determination.

“NMTech is excited about the opportunity to expand access to our technical training programs for the veterans who have served our nation,” said NMTech Chief Executive Officer Jodina Attao. “We believe our veterans should have the opportunity to put the education benefits they have earned toward developing new skills and building careers right here in the Commonwealth. We thank Congresswoman King-Hinds and her office for helping us navigate this process and for their continued support of our efforts to expand educational opportunities in the Marianas.”

NMTech's application remains subject to VA review and approval. Veterans will be able to use applicable GI Bill education benefits at the institute only after the institution and its eligible programs receive the necessary approvals.

“Veterans who want to learn a trade, build new skills, or prepare for another career should have the opportunity to do so without having to leave the Commonwealth,” King-Hinds added. “Our veterans earned these benefits through their service, and I want to see more of those benefits put to work here at home. I want to congratulate Jodina Attao and the entire NMTech team for the important work they continue to do to expand vocational education and training opportunities in the CNMI, and especially for exploring new ways to make these opportunities available to our veterans. My office will continue working with NMTech and the VA as the application moves through the approval process.”`````

title: Krishnamoorthi, Pettersen Lead 35 Lawmakers Demanding Answers on ICE’s Backdoor Access to Flock Surveillance Network
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) and Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (D-CO) today led 33 other House Democrats in demanding answers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) following reports that the agency has used local police to gain backdoor access to Flock Safety's nationwide license plate surveillance network. In a letter to Acting ICE Director David Venturella, the lawmakers demanded information about whose movements ICE has been tracking, how the information has been used, and what legal authority permits this surveillance. The letter follows Krishnamoorthi's previous investigation into Flock's surveillance practices and his introduction of the bipartisan NO FLOCK Act.

“ICE’s use of local police as a backdoor to access Flock’s license plate cameras and secretly track Americans’ movements is an outrageous abuse of power,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “The Trump administration cannot use local law enforcement to circumvent the Fourth Amendment and evade accountability. We are demanding answers about who ICE has been tracking, how this information has been used, and whether anyone has been detained or arrested as a result of this surveillance.”

“Reports that ICE is using local police as a backdoor to track people’s movements is terrifying and should alarm every single one of us. Especially during the Trump administration, which is looking for every opportunity to track and deport even law-abiding people,” said Congresswoman Pettersen. “I’m demanding answers about who ICE is tracking, how this information is being used, and what is stopping agents from abusing it. ICE does not get a blank check to spy on families and communities.”

Recent reporting uncovered more than 4,000 searches of Flock camera data by state and local law enforcement for federal authorities or potential immigration enforcement purposes. The reporting described how ICE obtained access through local police despite having no formal contract with Flock governing that access. Flock's automatic license plate readers record vehicle locations, allowing law enforcement to search camera networks and track individuals' movements across communities and state lines.

In their letter, the lawmakers write:

“The ability of federal agents to access vast quantities of location tracking data, without judicial authorization and without public disclosure, constitutes an unprecedented intrusion into the privacy of the general public, and must be explained immediately.”

The lawmakers requested responses by November 20, 2026, to the following questions:

How many times has an ICE agent obtained data from Flock Cameras, whether directly or through state or local law enforcement partners?

For what purpose is ICE accessing and obtaining data from Flock Cameras?

Have any individuals been detained, arrested, or otherwise subjected to enforcement actions as a result of information obtained from Flock Cameras? If yes, please provide that number.

What authority or legal statute is ICE purporting to operate under when accessing Flock Camera data? Please provide that authority or legal statute.

Does ICE maintain any internal policy governing the use of ALPR data obtained through third party or indirect means? If so, please provide that policy.

Has ICE conducted any legal review regarding whether accessing ALPR data through state or local partners complies with federal privacy protections, the Fourth Amendment, or DHS policy? If so, please provide that review. If not, please indicate whether the agency plans to do so.

Does ICE intend to formalize a contract or memorandum of understanding with Flock Safety or any other ALPR vendor?

Congressman Krishnamoorthi previously partnered with House Oversight Committee Ranking Member Robert Garcia to investigate Flock Safety's surveillance practices, including the use of license plate data to track women seeking abortion care and conduct unauthorized immigration enforcement. He also joined Senator Ron Wyden in calling for a Federal Trade Commission investigation into Flock's cybersecurity practices and introduced the bipartisan NO FLOCK Act with Congressman Michael Cloud to condition federal transportation funding on states restricting license plate reader use to specified public safety and toll enforcement purposes.

title: Krishnamoorthi Presents $2 Million Check for Elgin Community College’s Advanced Manufacturing Training
text:
CHICAGO — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi joined Chicago Deputy Mayor for Education and Youth Khari Humphries, Elgin Community College (ECC) President Dr. Peggy Heinrich, ECC Board of Trustees Chair Jennifer Rakow, HIRE360 Executive Director Jay Rowell, and Chicago Aldermen Stephanie Coleman, David Moore, and Gil Villegas at HIRE360’s Training and Business Development Center. Krishnamoorthi presented a ceremonial $2 million check representing federal funding he secured for advanced manufacturing training equipment at ECC.

The investment supports the college’s new 150,000-square-foot Manufacturing and Technology Center, which began classes in August and is already serving nearly 600 students through programs in robotics, automation, welding, HVAC, industrial maintenance, and energy management. The event also featured remarks from Deputy Mayor Humphries and firsthand accounts from HIRE360 apprenticeship program participants about their training and preparation for careers in the skilled trades.

“A four-year degree must not be the only path to a good-paying career,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “That's why I secured $2 million for advanced manufacturing training equipment at Elgin Community College and previously secured $1 million to help establish HIRE360's training center, where Jay Rowell and his team are doing tremendous work preparing Illinoisans for union apprenticeships. Whether students are learning to operate sophisticated equipment or training for the skilled trades, career and technical education gives them the skills employers need and the opportunity to build rewarding careers, support their families, and strengthen our economy.”

The investment builds on $936,000 Krishnamoorthi previously secured for ECC’s mechatronics and automation programs in 2023. He also secured $1 million in federal funding for HIRE360’s Training and Business Development Center, which opened in Chicago in 2024. This year, HIRE360’s pre-apprenticeship programs graduated 49 participants in Kane and Cook counties.

title: Larsen, Dexter Introduce Bill to Stop Trump Admin from Rolling Back Veterans’ Benefits
text:
Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) introduced the Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act to restore male breast cancer as a presumptive illness under the Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act (PACT Act). October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and October 17 to 23 is Men’s Breast Cancer Awareness Week.

In September 2025, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) removed male breast cancer from the list of reproductive cancers considered presumptive under the PACT Act to align with President Trump’s discriminatory executive orders. Male breast cancer has been linked to toxic exposure, and about 100 male veterans are diagnosed with breast cancer each year.

“I am committed to ensuring veterans can access high-quality, timely health care for illnesses related to their military service, and this bill is an important step towards guaranteeing that,” said Representative Larsen. “Male veterans with breast cancer should not be denied the benefits they’ve earned because of this Administration’s political agenda.”

“Policy changes should be evidence-based and not based on political ideology and hate,” said Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. “That is why I was alarmed when last Fall, Secretary Collins removed male breast cancer as a presumptive illness to conform with Trump’s anti-trans mandates. As a member of the House Veterans Affairs Committee, I am proud to co-lead this bill with Rep. Larsen to restore male breast cancer as a presumptive condition under the PACT Act.”

The legislation would designate male breast cancer as a presumptive illness under the PACT Act. PACT creates a presumption of service connection for certain disabilities and illnesses that have been linked to exposure to hazardous substances during military service.

The full text of the Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act is available here.

The Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act is supported by the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) and Burn Pits 360, the only 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization to offer an independent burn pit exposure registry in which family members can record the names of warriors who served the nation but have passed away due to illnesses from toxic injury.

“Male breast cancer is rare, often caught late, and too easily overlooked, by patients and clinicians alike. For a veteran who breathed burn pit smoke for months or years, that diagnosis is hard enough without also wondering whether the PACT Act covers him,” said Julie Tomáška, PhD, U.S. Air Force (Ret.), Scientific Committee Chair at Burn Pits 360. “The science on military toxic exposures keeps pointing the same way: federal researchers found male breast cancer rates about 39% higher among Marines and sailors at Camp Lejeune, where the drinking water was contaminated with industrial solvents, than at Camp Pendleton. Yet last year VA stopped presuming those men's cancers are service-connected, while women with the same diagnosis still are. Reps. Larsen and Dexter's bill removes the guesswork and writes the answer into law, so every veteran, claims examiner and advocate works from the same clear standard.”

Larsen and Dexter Fight for Veterans in the Pacific Northwest

This February, Representatives Larsen, Dexter, Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-05) and Jen Kiggans (VA-02) introduced the Mammography Access for Veterans Act, bipartisan legislation to expand veterans’ access to lifesaving breast cancer screenings.

In November 2025, Reps. Larsen and Dexter joined many of their colleagues in a letter calling on VA Secretary Doug Collins to immediately restore male breast cancer as a presumptive condition under the PACT Act and to provide Congress with data and analysis used to justify the policy change in November 2025.

In his time in Congress, Rep. Larsen has hosted more than 70 forums to hear directly from Northwest Washington state veterans about their needs. In 2025, he published ‘Listening to Veterans in Northwest Washington,’ a report capturing local veterans’ most pressing challenges and outlining policy recommendations for Congress and VA to address these concerns.

title: ICYMI: Lawler, Gottheimer Introduce Bipartisan Bill To Expand Organ Donor Registration
text:
Valhalla, N.Y. – 10/23/26… Yesterday, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) and Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) announced the introduction of the bipartisan Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act during a press conference at Westchester Medical Center. The legislation aims to make organ donor registration more accessible by allowing Americans to register through a wider range of federal and state applications and improving how donor registration information is shared across registries.

The bill is named in honor of Lauren Shields of Stony Point, New York, whose experience as a transplant recipient inspired a lifelong commitment to organ donation advocacy. At just eight years old, Lauren received a life-saving heart transplant after a viral infection caused heart failure. She later received a kidney transplant from her mother in 2020.

The Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act would expand opportunities for Americans to register as organ donors through applications they already complete, including those for Social Security benefits, Medicare, veterans’ benefits, passports, and federal individual income tax returns. The legislation would also direct the Department of Health and Human Services to establish a secure, automated electronic system to help update donor status across state and national registries.

Additionally, the bill would establish a grant program to help states incorporate donor registration into more applications and programs, including Medicaid, SNAP, WIC, and voter registration to make donor registration more accessible nationwide and help connect more patients with potentially life-saving transplants.

“Lauren Shields dedicated her life to giving others hope, and her legacy will continue to save lives for generations to come. I was proud to call Lauren a friend, and I know firsthand the impact she had on our community and her advocacy of organ donation. This legislation not only honors her life by making it easier for Americans to register as organ donors but it also helps ensure their wishes are reflected across all donor registries. At a time when thousands of Americans are waiting for a lifesaving transplant, this bipartisan legislation is an important step toward expanding access to organ donation and carrying forward Lauren’s extraordinary legacy,” said Congressman Lawler.

“When my mother was battling sarcoidosis, a rare lung disease, she tried valiantly to get a new lung – perhaps the only chance at saving her life. She never received one," said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). "The bipartisan Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act will build on Lauren’s legacy and make it easier for Americans to register as organ donors, say yes across our country – just as Lauren would have wanted.”

“Waitlist Zero is proud to support the Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act. This legislation will make it easier for Americans who want to give the gift of life to register as organ donors. Lauren understood the extraordinary power of organ donation personally. After receiving a heart transplant at just eight years old, Lauren devoted her life to advocating for organ donation. Tragically, Lauren died at just 26 while waiting for a kidney transplant. We can think of no more fitting tribute to her life than legislation that helps more Americans become organ donors and allows more patients to receive the lifesaving transplants they need. We are grateful to Representatives Lawler and Gottheimer for honoring Lauren’s remarkable legacy and championing lifesaving organ donation,” said Elaine Perlman, Executive Director, Waitlist Zero.

“Congressman Mike Lawler’s sponsorship of the Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act is a meaningful step toward increasing organ donor registration and expanding access to lifesaving transplants. It is especially fitting that this legislation honors Lauren Shields, a Rockland County resident whose life exemplified the extraordinary impact of organ donation. After receiving a heart transplant at age eight and a kidney transplant from her mother in 2020, Lauren became a passionate advocate who helped inspire New York’s Lauren’s Law and devoted her career at LiveOnNY to supporting organ donation and transplantation. Her legacy lives on through this important effort to provide hope to the thousands of Americans awaiting a lifesaving transplant. We commend Congressman Lawler for his leadership and commitment to advancing this vital cause,” said Mark E. Geller, MD, FACR, President and CEO, Montefiore Nyack Hospital, A member of the Montefiore Health System.

“For New York’s hospitals and transplant programs, every additional donor represents another opportunity to save a life. The Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act is a commonsense measure that makes it easier to register as a donor and expands access to lifesaving transplants. The hospital community thanks Representatives Mike Lawler (R-NY) and Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) for their leadership and advancing efforts to increase organ donation. We also applaud the legacy of Lauren Shields, whose tireless advocacy helped advance organ donation in New York and continues to inspire this important work nationwide,” said Kenneth E. Raske, President, Greater New York Hospital Association.

“The Healthcare Association of New York State has long supported efforts to raise awareness of organ and tissue donation and encourage donor enrollment,” said Thomas J. Quatroche Jr., PhD, president and CEO, HANYS. “The Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act will create more opportunities for individuals to easily register as organ donors, helping the more than 8,000 New Yorkers awaiting lifesaving transplants. I thank Rep. Lawler for his leadership on this critical legislation that will ultimately save lives.”

“As physicians, we see the profound impact transplantation can have on patients and families. Lauren Shields was a powerful example of that. After receiving a transplant as a child, she became a leading advocate for organ donation, helping shape policy in New York State,” said Julia Iyasere, M.D., MBA, Senior Vice President, System Chief Medical Officer at NewYork-Presbyterian. “This legislation builds on that progress by bringing the same approach to communities across the country. We commend Representatives Mike Lawler (R-NY) and Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) for championing this bipartisan effort.”

“Waitlist Zero is proud to support the Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act. This legislation will make it easier for Americans who want to give the gift of life to register as organ donors. Lauren understood the extraordinary power of organ donation personally. After receiving a heart transplant at just eight years old, Lauren devoted her life to advocating for organ donation. Tragically, Lauren died at just 26 while waiting for a kidney transplant. We can think of no more fitting tribute to her life than legislation that helps more Americans become organ donors and allows more patients to receive the lifesaving transplants they need. We are grateful to Representatives Lawler and Gottheimer for honoring Lauren’s remarkable legacy and championing lifesaving organ donation,” said Elaine Perlman, Executive Director, Waitlist Zero.

"Congressman Mike Lawler’s sponsorship of the Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act is a meaningful step toward increasing organ donor registration and expanding access to lifesaving transplants. It is especially fitting that this legislation honors Lauren Shields, a Rockland County resident whose life exemplified the extraordinary impact of organ donation. After receiving a heart transplant at age eight and a kidney transplant from her mother in 2020, Lauren became a passionate advocate who helped inspire New York’s Lauren’s Law and devoted her career at LiveOnNY to supporting organ donation and transplantation. Her legacy lives on through this important effort to provide hope to the thousands of Americans awaiting a lifesaving transplant. We commend Congressman Lawler for his leadership and commitment to advancing this vital cause," said Mark E. Geller, MD, FACR, President and CEO of Montefiore Nyack Hospital and Mount Sinai Health System.

“As physicians, we see the profound impact transplantation can have on patients and families. Lauren Shields was a powerful example of that. After receiving a transplant as a child, she became a leading advocate for organ donation, helping shape policy in New York State,” said Julia Iyasere, M.D., MBA, Senior Vice President, System Chief Medical Officer at NewYork-Presbyterian. “This legislation builds on that progress by bringing the same approach to communities across the country. We commend Representatives Mike Lawler (R-NY) and Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) for championing this bipartisan effort," said John Jurenko Senior Director of New York- Presbyterian.

“As physicians, we see firsthand how a transplant can change a patient’s life, enabling them to regain their strength, return to school, and make plans that once felt out of reach,” said David Lubarsky, MD, Chief Executive Officer of WMCHealth. “None of this is possible without organ donors and their families, and this legislation is a remarkable way to honor Lauren’s legacy and expand the number of patients who benefit from the gift of organ transplantation. Thank you to Congressman Lawler and Congressman Gottheimer for highlighting this critical need, to Lauren’s family for carrying in her advocacy, and all the physicians and organizations across the country that save lives every day.”

title: Silicon Valley Lawmakers Plan to Investigate Elon Musk’s Role in National Security Technology
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Silicon Valley lawmakers, Congressmen Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), and Ro Khanna (CA-17) demanded an immediate investigation into reports that Elon Musk’s SpaceX restricted critical military communications in Ukraine, disrupting drone operations and air defense systems against Russian attacks.

“Either a private contractor independently made life-and-death national security decisions, or President Trump directed the restriction of critical military communications supporting a U.S. ally,” the lawmakers wrote. “Either outcome raises profound concerns about the conduct of American foreign policy.”

The lawmakers warned that the controversy threatens America's national security, Silicon Valley's global reputation, and the credibility of American technology.

“As Silicon Valley’s elected members in Congress, we represent hundreds of innovation economy employers and workers whose livelihoods depend on the credibility of American technology abroad,” the lawmakers wrote. “Politically motivated service interruptions or erratic throttling will undermine reputations developed through decades of work that Americans have led to support our allies and customers throughout the world."

The lawmakers also put Musk's federal funding under scrutiny, questioning whether SpaceX should receive more than $700 million in taxpayer dollars for broadband service if it cannot reliably support critical national security missions.

“American taxpayers should never be left guessing whether the responsibility for critical national security decisions lies with their elected government or a private citizen with substantial financial interests in federal contracts,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers demanded an initial briefing within 14 days identifying who ordered the restrictions, whether they violated federal contracts, and whether similar vulnerabilities threaten other federal operations.

title: Malliotakis, Gottheimer Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Target Car Thefts
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) and Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) introduced the bipartisan H.R. 10872, Combatting Auto Robbery at the Source (CARS) Act to combat organized auto theft across New York, New Jersey and the tristate area.

Auto theft remains a serious problem in New York City, with nearly 9,110 vehicles stolen during the first nine months of 2026, according to recent NYPD data. Many auto theft rings operate across state lines, making greater coordination and real-time information sharing between law enforcement agencies critical to tracking stolen vehicles and apprehending those responsible. The NATB would help strengthen coordination among local, state and federal law enforcement to disrupt organized theft rings operating across the country and internationally.

Specifically, the bill would re-establish a National Anti-Auto Theft Bureau to:

Act as a national repository for information related to auto theft.

Facilitate real-time information sharing between federal, state, and local law enforcement.

Provide training, resources, and recommendations to multiple stakeholders on how to combat auto theft.

“In recent years, we have seen an increase in car thefts across the tristate area, making New Yorkers feel less safe and negatively impacting their quality of life. License plate scanners I allocated funding for have helped identify and recover stolen vehicles. However, once these vehicles leave the city, it becomes harder,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “We know that many end up on ships at New Jersey ports and then are sold in other countries. By creating a national anti-auto theft bureau and strengthening coordination at all levels, law enforcement can better combat auto theft across the tristate area.”

“A car can be replaced, but the scars from a violent carjacking, or a home invasion over a set of keys, can last a lifetime. For hardworking Jersey families who depend on their cars to get to work, school, and the doctor, a stolen car brings everything to a halt. We know a National Auto Theft Bureau works because it helped drive down auto theft before, and bringing it back is just common sense. By investing in tracking stolen cars, training our officers, and coordinating at every level of government, we can finally get ahead of these criminals. When it comes to public safety, you have to invest to protect,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer.

Rep. Malliotakis has secured over $9 million for the NYPD to purchase personal protective equipment, forensic equipment, patrol response vehicles, fixed plate reader systems, K-9 training and equipment, new tasers and belt-worn trauma kits.

title: Congressman Díaz-Balart Receives the 2026 Democracy Award from the National Endowment for Democracy at the Freedom Tower
text:
MIAMI, FL – Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart (FL-26), Dean of the Florida Delegation, Vice Chair of the House Committee on Appropriations and Chairman of the Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs, released the following statement after receiving the 2026 Champion of Freedom Democracy Award from the National Endowment for Democracy (NED):

ENGLISH:

"I am deeply honored to receive the National Endowment for Democracy’s 2026 Champion of Freedom Democracy Award at Miami’s historic Freedom Tower. As the son of Cuban exiles, receiving this recognition at a landmark that welcomed so many families fleeing communist tyranny carries special meaning. It is a reminder of America’s promise and our responsibility to stand as a beacon of freedom.

Throughout my service in Congress, I have worked to ensure that those fighting for liberty have a steadfast ally in the United States. That commitment is especially urgent in our own hemisphere, where generations of Cubans, Venezuelans, and Nicaraguans have demonstrated remarkable courage and resilience in the face of decades of authoritarian repression.

As Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs, I have consistently prioritized efforts that put America’s national security first and protect taxpayer dollars, while promoting freedom of speech, independence of the press, and democratic values worldwide. Advancing these freedoms supports our interests, strengthen our allies, and counters the regimes that seek to undermine us.

I thank the National Endowment for Democracy for this recognition and for more than four decades of supporting those confronting repression around the world. I remain committed to ensuring that their voices are heard, their sacrifices are remembered, and their struggle for freedom remains a priority of American foreign policy."

SPANISH:

"Me siento profundamente honrado al recibir el Premio de Campeón de la Libertad y la Democracia 2026 del National Endowment for Democracy en la histórica Torre de la Libertad en Miami. Como hijo de exiliados cubanos, recibir este reconocimiento en un lugar emblemático que acogió a tantas familias que huían de la tiranía comunista, tieneun especial significado. Es un recordatorio de la promesa de Estados Unidos y de nuestra responsabilidad de seguir siendo un faro de libertad.

En mis años de servicio en el Congreso trabajé para garantizar que quienes luchan por la libertad cuenten con un firme aliado en Estados Unidos. Ese compromiso es ahoraespecialmente urgente en nuestro propio hemisferio donde generaciones de cubanos, venezolanos y nicaragüenses han demostrado una enorme valentía y una resiliencia extraordinaria frente a décadas de represión autoritaria.

Como presidente del Subcomité de Asignaciones de la Cámara de Representantes para Seguridad Nacional, el Departamento de Estado y Programas Relacionados, mi prioridad constante a sido la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos y proteger el dinero de los contribuyentes a tiempo de promover la libertad de expresión, la independencia de la prensa y los valores democráticos en todo el mundo. Mi objetivo es que estas libertades fortalezcan nuestros intereses, consoliden nuestras alianzas y contrarresten a los regímenes autoritarios que buscan socavar estas libertades.

Expreso mi profundo agradecimiento al National Endowment for Democracy por otorgarme este reconocimiento y por su labor por más de cuatro décadas de apoyo a quienes enfrentan la represión en todo el mundo. Reitero que mantengo mi compromiso de garantizar que sus voces sean escuchadas, que sus sacrificios sean recordados y que su lucha por la libertad siga siendo una prioridad en la política exterior estadounidense."

title: McCaul Meets with Grimes County Judge to Discuss Terafab Development and Economic Growth
text:
NAVASOTA, Texas – This week, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas) met with Grimes County Judge Joe Fauth III to discuss the development of SpaceX's Terafab semiconductor manufacturing facility, its potential to drive significant economic growth in the region, and opportunities for coordination among local, state, and federal officials. The proposed 100-million-square-foot facility — the biggest in the world — represents a major investment in American semiconductor manufacturing, with its first phase expected to bring more than $16 billion in investment and create approximately 3,000 jobs to Grimes County.

"Terafab presents an extraordinary opportunity for Grimes County, the state of Texas, and our entire nation,” said Rep. McCaul. “This historic investment has the potential to create thousands of jobs, transform the local economy, and strengthen America's national security for years to come. I am extremely proud to see Central Texas leading the charge to onshore advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and I stand ready to support Judge Fauth and our local partners as we work to make this vision a reality."

title: Miller-Meeks, Energy and Commerce Chairman Guthrie Rally Southeast Iowa to Power the Largest Steel Mill in America
text:
BURLINGTON, IA — Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, M.D. (IA-01) hosted House Energy and Commerce Committee Chairman Brett Guthrie and local elected officials and business leaders for an energy roundtable in Burlington on how to power the $15 billion steel mill planned for Lee County, where construction is set to begin next year, and the new businesses and jobs expected to follow it.

Participants discussed the need for new natural gas infrastructure to deliver gas to the mill and surrounding development. Companies have passed on Iowa in the past because the natural gas needed to support their operations wasn't available, and Iowa lost jobs because of it. With a $15 billion mill now coming to Southeast Iowa, the region has the opportunity to close that gap.

"Iowa has watched jobs and businesses go elsewhere because we didn't have the energy to support them. That ends now. With a $15 billion steel mill coming to Lee County, we are going to build the natural gas infrastructure Iowa needs, and we are going to do it here," said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. "America produces the cleanest energy in the world. There is no reason to outsource our energy needs, and no reason to keep sending Iowa jobs overseas. Powering this mill means more good-paying jobs, more businesses, and more opportunity for hardworking Iowans."

Background

The Mill:

A $15 billion Mesabi Metallics steel mill, one of the largest in American history, is planned for Lee County, Iowa

Construction is set to begin next year, with steel production beginning in 2030

The project is expected to create 1,750 permanent jobs and support up to 6,000 construction jobs

It is projected to add $95 billion to the U.S. economy over the next decade

The mill is expected to produce up to 10 million tons of steel a year

Miller-Meeks' Role:

Congresswoman Miller-Meeks joined President Trump at the White House for the announcement of the project and has played a pivotal role in helping bring this historic steel mill to Iowa

She has led efforts to bring American manufacturing back to Iowa, including the Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act, signed into law by President Trump

She also voted to pass the Working Families Tax Cuts which helped boost domestic manufacturing across the country

title: Gotion Packs its Bags, Good Riddance
text:
Congressman John Moolenaar released the following statement in response to Gotion, a company beholden to the Chinese Communist Party, reaching a settlement agreement in its lawsuit against Green Charter Township, the community which wholly rejected it:

"Four years ago, Gotion came to Michigan with rosy promises, an influence campaign on local and state leaders, and misled the community about its ties to the Chinese Communist Party. When the residents of Green Charter Township repeatedly showed they did not support Gotion; instead of listening to the people, Gotion fought them, and attempted to bankrupt the town" said Moolenaar. "While it is unfortunate Michigan taxpayers will not receive restitution from the state subsidies Gotion refused to pay back, I am pleased the community can now rest knowing they stopped the CCP from getting a foothold in their small town."

Gotion is the “wholly-owned and controlled” subsidiary of its Chinese parent company, Gotion High-Tech, and receives subsidies from the Chinese government. On October 5, 2022 Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced Gotion agreed to build a battery component factory in Mecosta County. In November 2023, the residents of Green Charter Township rejected the Gotion project, recalling all members of the Township Board of Trustees who supported the project.

On September 17, 2025, the Michigan Strategic Fund notified Gotion the company was in default on its obligations established in its grant agreement with the state of Michigan: making no progress on its project in over 120 days, and by suing Green Charter Township. The state gave Gotion 30 days to resolve these issues, informing the company if it did not, its contract with the state would be terminated.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 10.23.26
text:
Major League Baseball (MLB) will crown new champions this fall.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers will compete for their first World Series championship in franchise history.

Just before Americans welcome a first-time baseball champion, Southwest Virginia welcomed a first-of-a-kind Hall of Famer to the region.

In October, 2025 Hall of Fame inductee Billy Wagner returned home for a dedication ceremony in downtown Tazewell.

Many in Southwest Virginia claim Billy Wagner as their own.

Wagner’s place of birth is Marion. But when he was with his aunt and uncle in his high school years, he lived in Tannersville.

He attended Tazewell High School where he was a dual-sport athlete in football and baseball.

Because of multiple broken right arms he suffered as a kid, he converted to pitching left-handed. Playing for the late Tazewell High School coach Lou Peery, Wagner became a pitching sensation.

Following his high school success, he stayed close to home playing for Ferrum College in Franklin County. After a dominant performance in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division III, where he set four records that stand to this day, Wagner was selected 12th overall in the 1993 MLB Draft.

To many MLB fans, Wagner is a legendary ballplayer. But to Virginians in our region, Wagner is more than that.

Wagner is a legendary human being who cares for Western Virginia.

On the day of the ceremony, I traveled to other events, including the Apple Dumpling Festival in Stuart and a fall festival thrown by the Radford Veterans of Foreign Wars.

When talking to constituents about my day’s plans, I mentioned that I’d later be attending the dedication ceremony in Tazewell.

I heard numerous accounts from people that Wagner the man was an amazing person.

One lady told me she got to know Wagner through one of his roommates at Ferrum. She recounted to me that Wagner is one of the finest men she has ever met, he cares about people and he gives back to his communities.

Wagner has a history of supporting childhood initiatives. Through the Wagner Family Foundation, Wagner helped direct resources to literacy initiatives, homeless outreach programs and organizations serving at-risk youth.

In 2005, Wagner founded the Second Chance Learning Center in Bluefield, Virginia. This Center provided tutoring and counseling services for local underserved children.

During Wagner’s 2025 Hall of Fame induction speech, he wore a Tazewell County pin and Ferrum College pin. Earlier this year, Wagner joined Ferrum baseball’s coaching staff.

Despite a time-consuming career that spanned 16 seasons and forced him to move back and forth across the country, Wagner never failed to support his family and stay connected with our region.

Wagner raised his four kids alongside his wife, Sarah, who is also a standout athlete from Ferrum College. Following her collegiate basketball career, she was inducted into the Ferrum College Hall of Fame. The Wagners deeply love their kids, including a son who plays in the MLB.

With the feedback I received, I headed to the Tazewell dedication ceremony.

I focused my remarks on the human side of Wagner that I learned about. I shared my earlier conversations in the day to highlight the kind of positive impact that Wagner had on his many friends here in Virginia.

Those that attended the ceremony included elected officials and community leaders. Coach Peery’s wife listened to Wagner comment about the role models that helped shape his life, and how her husband was almost like a father to Wagner.

The only thing that would have made the day better, according to Wagner, was if Peery was alive to celebrate this moment with him.

After opening by thanking God, Wagner’s emotional remarks praised Tazewell: “It was you guys that inspired me. The town of Tazewell means more to me than words can express…This is the hardest speech I have ever had to give, because you are my family and I love you.”

After the speeches, he threw a pitch to one of his former Tazewell teammates, who caught it on behalf of all of Wagner’s Tazewell and Ferrum teammates. It was a heater!

A new downtown park in Tazewell, “Billy Wagner Park,” features a statue of Wagner and a plaque noting his membership in the National Baseball Hall of Fame, something no other D-III athlete has ever done.

It was an honor for me to be there in person and celebrate with the community.

Wagner’s words and actions not only inspire athletes and athletic programs in our region. They inspire the human heart.

That is what Southwest Virginia is all about.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Moylan Outlines Legislative Milestones, Federal Investments & Priorities for Guam in 2026 Congressional Address
text:
(Hagåtña, Guam) — Congressman James Moylan delivered his 2026 Congressional Address Friday evening at the Guam Congress Building, highlighting legislative accomplishments, federal investments secured for Guam, and his continued efforts to lower the cost of living, strengthen the island's economy, and expand opportunities for Guam's families.

Addressing members of the 38th Guam Legislature, government leaders, community partners, and residents, Moylan reflected on nearly four years of congressional service, emphasizing the importance of bipartisan cooperation, strong federal partnerships, and ensuring that Guam's priorities are represented in Washington.

“Let’s build a Guam where a good job can support a family, where our children can pursue their ambitions, and where growing older does not mean having to leave the place we love. That is the future I will keep working for, with everyone willing to help us get there. It is an honor to serve you. Through every challenge ahead, my commitment remains: Guam first. Guam always”, said Congressman Moylan.

Among the major legislative accomplishments highlighted was House passage of two standalone bills introduced by Moylan during the 119th Congress: the Deliver for Veterans Act, which would require the Department of Veterans Affairs to cover shipping costs for adaptive vehicles provided to eligible veterans, and the Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act, which would provide qualifying students from Guam and other U.S. territories access to in-state tuition at covered public colleges and universities.

Moylan also highlighted federal funding secured for FY2026 to support critical road infrastructure, healthcare, public safety, emergency preparedness, housing assistance, and community facilities across Guam. Building on these investments, his office has submitted 20 additional Community Project Funding requests totaling nearly $145 million for FY2027, aimed at addressing further infrastructure needs and strengthening essential services throughout the island.

A central focus of the address was the rising cost of living. Moylan outlined ongoing efforts to expand Guam's access to affordable energy, pursue Jones Act relief and greater shipping competition, and address high airfares through the Pacific Island Flight Alternatives Act. He also reiterated his push to restore the $800 de minimis exemption for Guam and other U.S. territories, citing the financial burden that increased shipping costs, fees, and administrative requirements place on residents and local businesses.

The Congressman further discussed efforts to strengthen Guam's food security through expanded local agriculture, aquaculture development, and opportunities for local farmers, ranchers, and fishermen to supply fresh products to military installations. On economic development, Moylan highlighted initiatives to expand Guam's role in Navy ship repair, improve federal contracting opportunities for locally owned businesses, strengthen workforce training, and support tourism through the proposed inclusion of the Philippines in the Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program. He also discussed plans to pursue major regional summits on Guam to generate additional economic activity and strengthen the island's role in the Pacific.

During the address, Moylan recognized the late Sergeant Major Juan Ogo Blaz, whose nomination for the Medal of Honor has advanced to presidential consideration following a favorable determination by the Secretary of War. Blaz's daughter, Darlene, was also recognized as the Congressman reflected on her father's extraordinary courage and military service. Other priorities included establishing a Veterans Benefits Administration Regional Office on Guam, expanding access to passport services, advancing radiation exposure compensation legislation, and ensuring that the ongoing military buildup creates meaningful opportunities for Guam's workers, businesses, and communities.

Looking ahead, Moylan introduced his vision for stronger coordination between Guam's elected leadership and the federal government through the Guam-Federal Consultation Act, legislation that would establish a formal consultation process involving the White House and Guam's leaders to address federal policies affecting the island's future.

The Congressman also acknowledged Governor Lou Leon Guerrero and Lieutenant Governor Joshua Tenorio for their eight years of service and recognized the collaboration between their administration, local agencies, and his congressional office in advancing Community Project Funding priorities.

Throughout the address, Moylan emphasized that Guam's progress depends on sustained engagement in Washington, cooperation among local leaders, and a shared commitment to building an island where future generations can live, work, and thrive.

title: Rep. Panetta Joins Bipartisan, Bicameral Group of Lawmakers Urging Pentagon to Restore and Expand Starshield Access for Ukraine
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jim Costa (CA-21), alongside Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Thom Tillis (R-NC), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), urged Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and the Department of Defense (DoD) to expand its Starshield contract and restore Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite communications following recent disruptions. They specifically called for renewing unlimited-speed service to ensure Ukraine has the capacity it needs. The lawmakers also pressed the DoD to evaluate its authorities under the Defense Production Act to guarantee continued, reliable access.

“Ukrainian forces depend on these services for command and control, intelligence sharing, battlefield communications, and the operation of unmanned systems,” wrote the lawmakers. “Any degradation in service, including reduced connection speeds, restricted geographic coverage, or interruptions in access, undermines Ukraine’s military effectiveness and provides Russian forces with an operational advantage that will extend the conflict and put more civilians in harm’s way.”

The lawmakers called on DoD to maintain the geographic coverage Ukraine needs for its lawful military operations, including over Russian territory, and to ensure any transition from commercial Starlink to government-contracted Starshield happens without interruption.

“Decisions regarding service availability, coverage, and performance should not be left solely to the discretion of a private provider when they have direct consequences for Ukraine’s ability to defend itself,” continued the lawmakers.

In addition, the lawmakers urged DoD to evaluate its authorities under Title I of the Defense Production Act, which allows the federal government to require companies to give priority to government orders.

“These authorities should be considered alongside existing contractual mechanisms to ensure that Ukraine maintains reliable access to the bandwidth, service levels, and geographic coverage required for its lawful military operations,” added the lawmakers.

“The United States and Europe have made significant investments in Ukraine’s defense because of how a Russian victory would put our security at risk. Those investments should not be undermined by preventable disruptions to the communications infrastructure on which Ukrainian forces depend,” concluded the lawmakers.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth,

We write to express our serious concern about recent disruptions to Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite communications services and to urge the Department of Defense to take immediate steps to restore and sustain Ukraine’s access to these critical capabilities.

Reliable satellite communications are essential to Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russia’s ongoing aggression. Ukrainian forces depend on these services for command and control, intelligence sharing, battlefield communications, and the operation of unmanned systems. Any degradation in service, including reduced connection speeds, restricted geographic coverage, or interruptions in access, undermines Ukraine’s military effectiveness and provides Russian forces with an operational advantage that will extend the conflict and put more civilians in harm’s way.

We urge the Department to expand its existing Starshield contract to ensure Ukraine has the satellite communications capacity, coverage, and reliability necessary to sustain its military operations and renew Starshield’s unlimited-speed service. In the interim, the Department should take all necessary steps to ensure that Ukrainian forces maintain access to satellite communications at speeds and service levels at least equivalent to those previously available, through whatever combination of Starlink and Starshield services is necessary.

Critically, this should include maintaining the geographic coverage required for Ukrainian military operations, including connectivity over Russian territory where necessary to support Ukraine’s lawful military operations, consistent with applicable U.S. law and policy. Decisions regarding service availability, coverage, and performance should not be left solely to the discretion of a private provider when they have direct consequences for Ukraine’s ability to defend itself.

The Department should also ensure that any transition between commercial Starlink services and government-contracted Starshield capabilities occurs without interruptions or reductions in service. This requires sufficient contracted capacity, clear service-level requirements, and appropriate oversight to ensure that Ukraine’s operational needs are met.

We also urge the Department to evaluate the use of authorities under Title I of the Defense Production Act (50 U.S.C. § 4511), in coordination with the Department of Commerce as appropriate, to prioritize the provision and expansion of satellite communications services necessary to support Ukraine’s defense. These authorities should be considered alongside existing contractual mechanisms to ensure that Ukraine maintains reliable access to the bandwidth, service levels, and geographic coverage required for its lawful military operations.

The United States and Europe have made significant investments in Ukraine’s defense because of how a Russian victory would put our security at risk. Those investments should not be undermined by preventable disruptions to the communications infrastructure on which Ukrainian forces depend. Ensuring reliable access to satellite communications is essential to sustaining Ukraine’s defense and protecting U.S. national security interests.

We urge the Department to act expeditiously to expand its Starshield arrangements and ensure uninterrupted satellite communications support for Ukraine.

Sincerely,

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN INTRODUCES NEW LEGISLATION TO EXPAND  MEDICARE ELIGIBILITY AND LOWER HEALTHCARE COSTS ACROSS THE HUDSON VALLEY
text:
Ryan’s Improving Medicare Coverage Act lowers the Medicare age of eligibility from 65 to 50, massively expanding coverage and lowering costs for millions of Americans

Especially following the devastating cuts to healthcare that have defined Trump’s second term, Ryan’s bill is drawing a clear line in the sand that benefits will be not just restored, but expanded

POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan announced the introduction of his Improving Medicare Coverage Act, new legislation that will expand healthcare coverage to millions of Americans by lowering the Medicare age of eligibility from 65 to 50. Ryan’s co-leads on the bill are Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), who joined Ryan in Poughkeepsie, as well as Representatives Chris Deluzio and Debbie Dingell.

“While Trump and Republicans cut your healthcare and raise your costs, we’re fighting back and putting your care first. But we’re not just reversing the harm – we’re building something better in its place, where millions more Americans will be able to access and afford the care they deserve right when they need it,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “This legislation expands healthcare coverage to millions of Americans, takes decisive action to lower costs, and makes sure that everyone who needs it has access to quality health care, and won’t have to wait to get the cancer screenings, preventative care, and prescriptions they need. This is a commonsense bill, and I look forward to passing it through the Democratically-controlled House next year.”

“Lowering the Medicare eligibility age will be life-saving for the millions of Americans who are waiting an additional 15 years to be able to afford to see a doctor,” said Congresswoman Jayapal. “Expanding Medicare is not only popular, it is also morally the right thing to do. Millions leave the workforce before 65, and with Trump’s cuts to healthcare, many are now left without any options as they wait, sometimes years, for Medicare enrollment. Expanding this program is a commonsense step towards ensuring that all Americans have the care they deserve.”

“Especially after Trump’s healthcare cuts, expanding Medicare to Americans age 50 and up will save lives and get so many Americans the healthcare they need,” said Congressman Deluzio. “I am proud to support the Improving Medicare Coverage Act—this is an important steppingstone on the way to bigger healthcare reform where every American has good and decent healthcare.”

“For millions of Americans who cannot afford to go to the doctor, it is too late to receive preventive care by the time they reach age 65,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “The U.S. is the only industrialized nation that does not guarantee access to health care for all its citizens, and this needs to change now. I am proud to introduce this legislation to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50, improve the Medicare Savings Program, and make lifesaving drugs more affordable.”

“NYSNA nurses believe that healthcare is a human right ! As patient advocates, we are proud to stand with Congressman Ryan and Congresswoman Jayapal as they introduce this legislation here in the Hudson Valley. Lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 50 will ensure healthcare coverage for an additional 62 million people and lower employer costs. This legislation will help to address the disparity that exists in healthcare and address the needs that nurses see wherever they practice,” said Christina Evans, RN, NYSNA Director at Large.

At age 50, the risks for several chronic conditions and cancers naturally increase. The median ages for many cancer diagnoses fall below 65 years of age: for instance, 61 is the average age for a breast cancer diagnosis. Adults in late middle age who lack health insurance are more likely to die or experience a preventable decline in their overall health. Lowering the healthcare eligibility age would improve the chances of being diagnosed early and surviving treatable diseases.

As of 2024, adults aged 55-64 made up 11.5 percent of the entire uninsured population in the U.S. The cuts to healthcare in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act are anticipated to remove 15 million Americans from their coverage, and 22 million Americans are paying over $1,000 more than they were before the Affordable Care Act tax credits expired. To address these cuts and the increased costs to planholders, lowering the Medicare eligibility age is an important step towards ensuring all Americans have health coverage. The legislation would also substantially reduce racial and ethnic health disparities in insurance coverage and healthcare.

In addition to lowering costs for older adults and improving patient outcomes, it is estimated that lowering the Medicare age could reduce costs for employers by up to 43 percent.

The Improving Medicare Coverage Act would:

Lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50;

Establish a Medicare Cost Assistance Program to replace the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), and the Qualifying Individual (QI) programs with one program covering specified Part A premiums and Part B premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance for individuals with incomes up to 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL).

Enhance prescription drug affordability by:

Expanding access to assistance with out-of-pocket costs under Medicare Part D for low-income seniors and individuals with disabilities;

Combining the existing Extra Help and Low Income Subsidy programs into one program;

Raising the eligibility from 135% FPL to 200% FPL; and

Removing the asset test

Ensure that any individual making under 400% FPL who is not eligible for the Medicare Savings Program maintains the same eligibility for marketplace premium tax credits.

The Improving Medicare Coverage Act is cosponsored by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Everton Blair (GA-13), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), Salud O. Carbajal (CA-24), Greg Casar (TX-35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Steve Cohen (TN-09), J. Luis Correa (CA-46), Jason Crow (CO-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Jesús G. "Chuy" García (IL-04), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Sarah Jacobs (CA-51), Henry C. "Hank" Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), James P. McGovern (MA-02), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Grace Meng (NY-06), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Joe Neguse (CO-02), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Adam Smith (WA-09), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).

This legislation is endorsed by Center for Health and Democracy, Labor Campaign for Single Payer, MoveOn, People’s Action Institute, Physicians for a National Health Program, Public Citizen, SEIU, United Auto Workers.

title: Reps. Pettersen, Krishnamoorthi Lead Effort Demanding Answers on ICE’s Backdoor Access to License Plate Surveillance Network
text:
LAKEWOOD – Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) today led an effort demanding answers from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) following reports the agency has used local police to gain backdoor access to a nationwide license plate surveillance network, allowing the federal government to track private citizens’ movements. In the Members’ letter to Acting Director David Venturella, which was signed by 33 other Democrats, the Members press ICE to disclose whose movements it is tracking, what legal authority it relies on, and what safeguards protect the public from abuse.

“Reports that ICE is using local police as a backdoor to track people’s movements is terrifying and should alarm every single one of us. Especially during the Trump administration, which is looking for every opportunity to track and deport even law-abiding people,” said Congresswoman Pettersen. “I’m demanding answers about who ICE is tracking, how this information is being used, and what is stopping agents from abusing it. ICE does not get a blank check to spy on families and communities.”

“ICE’s use of local police as a backdoor to access Flock’s license plate cameras and secretly track Americans’ movements is an outrageous abuse of power,” saidCongressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “The Trump administration cannot use local law enforcement to circumvent the Fourth Amendment and evade accountability. We are demanding answers about who ICE has been tracking, how this information has been used, and whether anyone has been detained or arrested as a result of this surveillance.”

A recent investigation uncovered more than 4,000 searches of Flock Safety camera data by state and local law enforcement conducted for federal authorities or with a potential immigration focus. The reporting described how ICE obtained access through local law enforcement despite having no formal contract with Flock governing that access.

Flock’s automatic license plate readers capture vehicle information and locations, allowing law enforcement to search records across camera networks. Access to those records can reveal incredibly personal details about people’s daily routines and whereabouts, raising concerns about privacy and the potential misuse of information collected in communities across the country.

“Such chilling, unrestrained surveillance obtained without judicial authorization, contractual safeguards, or public transparency, represents far more than a procedural lapse—it represents the quiet expansion of a federal surveillance system operating out of sight and beyond any meaningful public oversight,” the Members write in the letter.

The letter requests answers by November 20, 2026, including:

How often ICE has accessed Flock camera data, directly or through state and local partners and for what purposes.

How many people have been detained, arrested, or subjected to other enforcement actions as a result.

What legal authority and internal policies govern ICE’s access to and use of this information.

Whether ICE has reviewed these practices for compliance with federal privacy protections, the Fourth Amendment, and Department of Homeland Security policy.

Whether ICE intends to establish a formal agreement with Flock safety or another license plate reader vendor .

Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen has consistently fought back against the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement overreach and defended due process. In the Colorado legislature, she helped pass legislation ensuring local law enforcement agencies do not serve as an extension of ICE. In Congress, she voted against legislation that would force Washington, D.C. police to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement and condemned ICE operations in schools, churches, and hospitals. This letter builds on her work to protect immigrant communities and demand accountability for federal enforcement practices that threaten people’s rights.

The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.

Dear Acting Director Venturella:

We write with serious concern regarding reports that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has been accessing data from Flock Safety automatic license‑plate‑reader (ALPR) cameras, an AI‑powered surveillance system, with no formal contract or governing agreement in place, creating serious concerns around data privacy and overreach. According to recent reporting, ICE has used state and local law‑enforcement agencies to conduct more than 4,000 searches of Flock camera data on its behalf, enabling ICE personnel to obtain personally identifiable information without a criminal warrant.

Not only is this protocol potentially illegal, exploiting this information side-door allows ICE personnel to query ALPR cameras deployed across multiple states – in effect granting federal agents access to a nationwide, continuously updated surveillance grid capable of tracking the movements of millions of people in real time. Such chilling, unrestrained surveillance obtained without judicial authorization, contractual safeguards, or public transparency, represents far more than a procedural lapse — it represents the quiet expansion of a federal surveillance system operating out of sight and beyond any meaningful public oversight.This is a serious breach of privacy and a clear departure from federal law and agency policy. The ability of federal agents to access vast quantities of location‑tracking data, without judicial authorization and without public disclosure, constitutes an unprecedented intrusion into the privacy of the general public, and must be explained immediately.

Please provide a response to the following no later than November 20, 2026:

How many times has an ICE agent obtained data from Flock Cameras, whether directly or through state or local law‑enforcement partners?

For what purpose is ICE accessing and obtaining data from Flock Cameras?

Have any individuals been detained, arrested, or otherwise subjected to enforcement actions as a result of information obtained from Flock Cameras? If yes, please provide that number.

What authority or legal statute is ICE purporting to operate under when accessing Flock Camera data? Please provide that authority or legal statute.

Does ICE maintain any internal policy governing the use of ALPR data obtained through third‑party or indirect means? If so, please provide that policy.

Has ICE conducted any legal review regarding whether accessing ALPR data through state or local partners complies with federal privacy protections, the Fourth Amendment, or DHS policy? If so, please provide that review. If not, please indicate whether the agency plans to do so.

Does ICE intend to formalize a contract or memorandum of understanding with Flock Safety or any other ALPR vendor?

We look forward to your prompt response.
