title: SIGNED INTO LAW: Pfluger's Mystic Alerts Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Trump signed Congressman August Pfluger's (TX-11) bipartisan, bicameral Mystic Alerts Act into law. This critical legislation modernizes America's emergency alert infrastructure by integrating satellite networks into the Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) system, helping ensure Americans can receive critical, life-saving alerts even when traditional communications infrastructure is damaged or nonexistent.

“I am grateful that President Trump signed the Mystic Alerts Act into law. After the devastating July 4th floods, it was clear that families in rural communities can’t be left in the dark when cell networks go down. By bringing satellite technology into our emergency alert system, we’re making sure warnings reach people when they need them most. I’m thankful to Senator Cornyn for championing the Mystic Alerts Act in the Senate and to Chairman Ted Cruz for moving it through the Senate Committee on Commerce. This law is a major step forward for emergency preparedness, and it means more Americans will get the warnings they need, no matter where they live,” said Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11).

Rep. Pfluger introduced this bipartisan legislation alongside Reps. Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Buddy Carter (GA-01), and Marc Veasey (TX-33). Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) and Senator Jon Ossoff (D-GA) led the Senate companion legislation.

“More than 130 people were tragically killed in the July 4th floods that ravaged Central Texas last year, many of whom did not receive emergency alerts due to compromised cellular networks that were knocked out by the storm,” said Senator John Cornyn (R-TX). “This law will address this technology shortfall and honor the memory of those lost by ensuring Texans and all Americans can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite even when disaster strikes, and I appreciate President Trump signing it into law.”

“The catastrophic 2025 Fourth of July floods devastated families and communities across Texas and demonstrated the importance of delivering timely emergency alerts. The Mystic Alerts Act strengthens our emergency alert systems, will help ensure life-saving alerts reach Americans when and where they need them, and will help protect American families and communities when future disasters strike. I was proud to support this legislation, advance it through the Senate Commerce Committee, and help secure its passage in the Senate. I thank and applaud President Trump for signing the bill into law," said Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX).

“When storms, disasters, or threats to public safety threaten our state, crisis management is key,” said Senator Jon Ossoff (D-GA). “Our bipartisan law will help upgrade America's emergency alert systems to keep Georgia families safe and informed.”

“The tragedy at Camp Mystic changed countless families forever, including my own. My two granddaughters survived those devastating floods, but their cousin, Janie Hunt, tragically lost her life. Nothing can bring back the lives lost that day, but we have a responsibility to act and he Mystic Alerts Act is an important step toward ensuring families receive lifesaving emergency warnings when every second matters. I thank President Trump for signing this bipartisan legislation into law and my colleagues in Congress for coming together to help protect American families. We cannot change what happened that day, but we can honor those we lost by working to save lives in the future," said Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01).

“In Houston and across the state of Texas, we are still heartbroken and grieving the loss of beloved family members and the destruction of communities along the Guadalupe River in the summer of 2025, a disaster made worse by communication gaps and failures,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07). “This new law is a small but important way to provide a meaningful response to the devastating floods and to learn from the tragedy so that communities across the country do not have to experience the same pain and loss that Texans did last year. Nothing can bring back those that we lost in the flood, but we owe it to their survivors and to everyone we represent to do all we can to try to prevent another tragedy like it. I am thankful for Congressman Pfluger, Congressman Veasey, and Congressman Carter’s partnership in this effort and am thrilled to see this bill become law.”

"I am honored to support the Mystic Alerts Act, and proud this act was signed into law. This bill will ensure that emergency alerts can be disseminated via satellite even when commercial cell providers are unable to provide service. This is an important step toward strengthening our nation’s emergency preparedness. Supporting this piece of legislation serves as a significant step and response to the devastation caused by last year’s floods in Texas and as a reminder of the importance of preparing for future flood disasters in our nation. When disaster strikes, every second matters, and no family should be left without critical information simply because the power or cell service is down," said Congressman Marc Veasey (TX-33).

Background:

On July 4, 2025, a devastating flood occurred in Central and West Texas, claiming over 130 lives. Multiple reports noted undelivered WEAs throughout the areas impacted by the disaster once cellular infrastructure was damaged.

The Mystic Alerts Act will:

· Allow cellular companies to partner with satellite communications providers to deliver WEAs during emergencies.

· Direct the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to establish the necessary rules and policies to preserve the effectiveness of WEA infrastructure while integrating satellite communications.

title: NEWS: After Pushback from Pressley & Others, USPS to Keep Fields Corner Post Office Open
text:
In a Last-Minute Reversal, USPS Announced It Has Secured a Lease Extension to Allow Fields Corner Branch to Remain Open at 218 Adams Street

Pressley Has Repeatedly Sounded the Alarm on USPS’ Service Cuts in Fields Corner, Allston, and Across the Massachusetts 7th

BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) applauded the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) announcement that it has secured a lease extension to allow the Fields Corner Post Office to remain open at 218 Adams Street in Dorchester. Following pushback from Congresswoman Pressley in partnership with colleagues and community leaders, USPS is canceling a planned closure that was set to take effect next week.

“This welcome reversal by USPS is a testament to public pressure and what is possible when we come together and raise our collective voices to defend our essential postal services. I’m glad the USPS is heeding our calls to keep the Fields Corner branch open and preserve this public good for residents who deserve an accessible and conveniently located post office to do their daily business,” said Congresswoman Pressley in a statement today. “While today is an important victory for our community, we continue to call on the USPS to stop gutting postal services across Massachusetts, and it can start by reopening the Allston branch and restoring daily service to those who need it.”

Congresswoman Pressley has repeatedly sounded the alarm on the USPS’ proposed cuts to service in Fields Corner, Allston, Grove Hall, and other neighborhoods in her district, and urged them to reverse course and preserve this essential public good for residents.

Congresswoman Pressley, along with Mayor Wu, City Councilor Liz Breadon, and community leaders held a rally this month to condemn the USPS’ plans to permanently close the Allston Post Office. Congresswoman Pressley also joined Senator Ed Markey and their Massachusetts colleagues on a letter demanding the USPS cease its campaign of post office closures across the Commonwealth.

Throughout her time in Congress, Congresswoman Pressley has championed for federal resources to support the United States Postal Service and its employees.

In December 2024, in a House Oversight Committee hearing, Rep. Pressley discussed the essential role that the United States Postal Service (USPS) plays in our communities and questioned USPS Postmaster General Louis DeJoy about the widespread delays and service failures that have severely impacted her constituents in the Massachusetts 7th.

In October 2024, Rep. Pressley joined postal workers from the American Postal Workers Union (APWU) for a rally in Boston to sound the alarm about the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) substandard performance and service to communities.

In August 2024, Rep. Pressley joined Senator Markey on a letter urging USPS to re-open postal facilities and improve service, spotlighting a larger statewide problem with postal service in Massachusetts.

On December 16, 2022, Rep. Pressley joined Reps. Lynch and Raskin in leading their colleagues on a letter urging the extension of COVID-19 workers’ compensation benefits for postal workers.

On February 25, 2021, Rep. Pressley called for postal banking to advance racial and economic justice during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.

On February 19, 2021, Rep. Pressley urged President Biden in a letter to replace Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and appoint a diverse United States Postal Service Board of Governors.

On August 22, 2020, Rep. Pressley delivered remarks on the House floor slamming Republican attacks on the United States Postal Service and shared constituent stories.

On August 21, 2020, Rep. Pressley and Rep. Payne lead their colleagues in a letter pushing party leadership to stand firm on postal service funding.

On August 25, 2020, Rep. Pressley questioned Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and the United States Postal Service Board of Governors Chairman Robert Duncan about the harmful impact policy changes at USPS had on the workforce during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.

On August 6, 2020, Rep. Pressley, and her colleagues sent a letter to Postmaster General Louis DeJoy expressing deep concerns about operational changes at the U.S. Postal Service that could have negative impacts on service standards and cause significant delays in mail delivery.

On May 29, 2020, Rep. Pressley joined progressive Members of Congress in a letter urging House and Senate leadership to include public banking in COVID-19 response.

title: Quigley, Kelly, Tillis, Slotkin, Fitzpatrick, Kaptur, Costa, and Panetta Urge Pentagon to Restore and Expand Starshield Access for Ukraine
text:
Chicago Congressman and Congressional Ukraine Caucus Co-Chair Mike Quigley (IL-05), U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), and Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Marcy Kaptur (D-OH-09), Jim Costa (D-CA- 21), and Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19) urged Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and the Department of Defense (DoD) to expand its Starshield contract and restore Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite communications following recent disruptions. They specifically called for renewing unlimited-speed service to ensure Ukraine has the capacity it needs. The lawmakers also pressed the DoD to evaluate its authorities under the Defense Production Act to guarantee continued, reliable access.

“Ukrainian forces depend on these services for command and control, intelligence sharing, battlefield communications, and the operation of unmanned systems," the lawmakers wrote. “Any degradation in service, including reduced connection speeds, restricted geographic coverage, or interruptions in access, undermines Ukraine's military effectiveness and provides Russian forces with an operational advantage that will extend the conflict and put more civilians in harm's way.”

The lawmakers called on DoD to maintain the geographic coverage Ukraine needs for its lawful military operations, including over Russian territory, and to ensure any transition from commercial Starlink to government-contracted Starshield happens without interruption: “Decisions regarding service availability, coverage, and performance should not be left solely to the discretion of a private provider when they have direct consequences for Ukraine's ability to defend itself.”

In addition, the lawmakers urged DoD to evaluate its authorities under Title I of the Defense Production Act, which allows the federal government to require companies to give priority to government orders: “These authorities should be considered alongside existing contractual mechanisms to ensure that Ukraine maintains reliable access to the bandwidth, service levels, and geographic coverage required for its lawful military operations.”

“The United States and Europe have made significant investments in Ukraine's defense because of how a Russian victory would put our security at risk. Those investments should not be undermined by preventable disruptions to the communications infrastructure on which Ukrainian forces depend,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: Randall to Introduce Resolution Calling for Disabled Women to be Paid Fairly
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week Congresswomen Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Lateefah Simon (D, CA-12), and Ayanna Pressley (D, MA-07), announced they will introduce the Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution. This resolution recognizes the persistent pay disparity between disabled women and both disabled and nondisabled men, and it reaffirms the need to reduce systemic, economic barriers and advance economic equity for disabled women.

“We all deserve to live full lives, to be treated with dignity and respect. All people with disabilities still face huge system barriers, and for disabled women they’re compounded,” said Rep. Randall. “Women with disabilities make less than non-disabled women, and less than disabled men. Government has to do better. As Chair of the Better Pay and Benefits Task Force, I’ll keep fighting for working people everywhere to get the pay and benefits they’ve earned so folks of all abilities can live and thrive in their communities.”

According to recent analysis from the National Partnership for Women & Families, disabled women continue to face high-wage gap disparities compared to their nondisabled male counterparts, earning 56 cents for every dollar paid to nondisabled men. The pay gap is even greater for disabled women of color, who are paid 46-55 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic nondisabled men. Additionally, working disabled mothers are paid 44 cents for every dollar paid to nondisabled fathers. According to the National Women's Law Center, disabled women in Washington state were paid as low as $0.65 for every dollar compared to nondisabled men.

This resolution is endorsed by the Democratic Women’s Caucus, American Association of People with Disabilities (AAPD), Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN), National Partnership for Women & Families (NPWF), Disability Culture Lab (DCL), National Disability Rights Network (NDRN), Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), National Disabled Legal Professionals Association (NDLPA), Equal Rights Advocates (ERA), New Disabled South.

“Disabled women of color experience some of the largest pay gaps in our nation- impacting their ability to care for themselves and their loved ones,” said Congresswoman Simon. “This is an unacceptable reality, which is why I joined disability champions in Congress, Reps. Pressley and Randall, to introduce this resolution and demand action to undo systemic barriers to equal pay, break down the discrimination that disabled women face, and move towards a future where every individual is valued for their labor without discrimination based on gender, race, or disability.”

"Disability rights are human rights. It is shameful that in 2026, women with disabilities are paid 44 cents for every dollar paid to non-disabled fathers—and that wage gap only widens for working disabled women of color," said Congresswoman Pressley. “Our Disabled Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution makes it clear: We must put an end to this economic injustice and make sure everyone gets equal pay for equal work.”

title: Rep. Salinas' Statement on USDA Reorganization Ruling
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, U.S. Representative Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Agriculture Subcommittee on Forestry and Horticulture, issued the following statement in response to a federal court order temporarily blocking portions of the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) proposed reorganization.

Earlier this month, U.S. District Judge Vince Chhabria extended an order temporarily halting reorganization activities at several USDA agencies while the court considers a lawsuit brought by a coalition of federal employee unions. The judge indicated that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed in their argument that the reorganization violates a provision of the Fiscal Year 2026 funding law restricting USDA's ability to carry out the reorganization without congressional approval. The proposed plan would have relocated thousands of USDA employees and consolidate offices across the country, raising concerns about disruptions to critical services for farmers, rural communities, and American families.

“For more than a year, I have raised concerns about this reckless plan and its consequences for the people who grow our food, protect our forests, and serve our rural communities," said Rep. Salinas. "This court order provides some much-needed relief for USDA employees and their families, but the fight is far from over. If Secretary Rollins believes in this plan, she should bring it to Congress, show us the data, and make her case in the open. Until then, will keep fighting to protect the essential services rural Oregonians rely on.”

title: SCHNEIDER, KELLY INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BREWS TO BARNS ACT TO SUPPORT SMALL BREWERIES & LOCAL FARMERS, STRENGTHEN LOCAL SUPPLY CHAINS
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL - Today, U.S. RepresentativesBrad Schneider (IL-10), a member of the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax, and Mike Kelly (PA-16), Chairman of the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax introduced the bipartisan Brews to Barns Act, legislation that would establish a credit against the excise tax on beer for brewers that donate spent grain for local agricultural use.

Additional co-sponsors of the Brews to Barns Act include House Agriculture Committee Chairman Glenn "GT" Thompson (PA-15), Representatives Jeff Hurd (CO-03), House Small Brewers Caucus Co-Chair Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Josh Riley (NY-19), and John Larson (CT-01).

“Everyone in America—from working families to Main Street businesses—is feeling the bite of rising costs,” said Rep. Schneider. “Among those hit hardest are craft beer brewers and local farmers, which is why I am glad to join my colleagues in this bipartisan effort to help lower costs and prevent waste.”

“At their cores, local breweries and farms are small businesses who play integral roles in our communities. The Brews to Barns Act incentivizes a collaborative effort between small breweries and local farmers to strengthen local supply chains. It's a win-win for everyone,” said Rep. Kelly, a Co-Chair of the House Small Brewers Caucus.

“Pennsylvania’s farmers, ranchers, and brewers already know that good ingredients shouldn’t go to waste,” said Rep. Thompson. “Across the Commonwealth, brewers continue to create partnerships with local farmers and ranchers to put their spent grain to use in agricultural production. The Brews to Barns Act will provide key incentives to build upon that relationship, helping lower input costs for producers while supporting local small businesses.”

“This tax credit for donating spent grain will lower costs for small brewers, benefit our local farmers and ranchers, and keep spent grain out of our landfills” said Rep. Strickland, a Co-Chair of the House Small Brewers Caucus. “This bill is a common-sense way to lower the cost of doing business, while supporting small brewers that boost our local economies.”

“Small breweries have a long history of supporting their communities, and their relationships with local farmers are an important part of that. By donating spent grain for agricultural use, brewers help turn a byproduct of the brewing process into a valuable resource for farmers," said Bart Watson, President & CEO, Brewers Association. "The Brews to Barns Act recognizes the value of these longstanding partnerships and helps ensure they can continue to thrive. We appreciate Reps. Kelly and Schneider's leadership in supporting the connections between America's brewers and farmers.”

You can find full bill text here.

title: Peters, Whitesides, Crank Urge Inclusion of Forestry Bill in Annual NDAA Package
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives Scott Peters (D-CA), George Whitesides (D-CA), and Jeff Crank (R-CO) led 28 House Members on a letter to Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), House Armed Services Committee (HASC) Chair Mike Rogers (R-AL), and HASC Ranking Member Adam Smith (D-WA) to urge the inclusion of the Fix Our Forests Act (FOFA) in the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), or any other must-pass vehicle, to ensure it becomes law this Congress.

The Members stated that the rising frequency and severity of devastating wildfires demand immediate action. In 2026 alone, roughly 66,000 fires burned through more than 9 million acres, or 132% and 141% of the 10-year average, respectively. At the same time, over 1,600 firefighters and support personnel are still assigned to catastrophic incidents across the country.

The Members explained that the crisis is a “significant – and growing – hazard to our military readiness and national security, endangering the safety of the American people, as well as the National Guard, Reserve forces, and other service members across the country.” They noted that by including FOFA in the 2027 NDAA, it could become law by the end of this Congress.

The Members highlighted several stark instances of the impact of recent wildfires, including those around key military installations in Washington and Arkansas that threaten weapons and munitions. These fires also force critical units like the National Guard to divert man-hours to firefighting. Additionally, the Members noted the economic toll as wildfires cost the U.S. between nearly $400 billion and almost $900 billion annually.

Preventing wildfires before they occur would save $3.75 in prevented damages for every $1 spent, and the “Fix Our Forests Act represents our best chance to realize those savings while improving forest health, streamlining wildfire mitigation, and defending communities across the country,” the Members continued. “It is the only package that is bipartisan, bicameral, and has undergone a comprehensive committee process in both chambers of Congress. It represents thoughtful legislation that will meaningfully address the wildfire crisis.”

Read a full copy of the letterhere.

Background:

Rep. Peters has been a vocal advocate for bipartisan, bicameral forestry and wildfire legislation, a priority for his constituents in San Diego, which is highly vulnerable to climate-driven wildfires. For the past two Congresses, Rep. Peters has been the House lead of the Fix Our Forests Act to establish requirements for managing forests on federal land, including requirements concerning reducing wildfire threats, expediting the review of certain forest management projects, and implementing forest management projects and other activities. The House passed this bill in January 2025. Prior to launching Fix our Forests, Rep. Peters has led the Save Our Sequoias Act to protect California’s giant sequoias from wildfire as one-fifth have been destroyed since 2015. Without faster, proactive forest restoration, more of these ancient trees will be lost. This bill would help federal, state, tribal, and local land managers accelerate critical forest restoration projects and strengthen the resilience of sequoia groves. The House passed the bill in March 2026.

title: Rep. Steube Supports Federal Funding for Cape Coral Bridge Replacement and Expansion
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.–-U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) sent a letter to the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) in support of Lee County’s Bridge Investment Program application to replace and expand the Cape Coral Bridge, which carries approximately 50,000 trips daily across the Caloosahatchee River.

“Southwest Florida is growing, and our infrastructure needs to keep up,” said Rep. Steube. “Families shouldn’t have to sit in endless traffic or worry about whether our roads can handle the next major hurricane. Lee County has put forward a strong proposal, and it’s time for the federal government to step up and support this investment.”

The project would replace two existing bridges and expand the corridor from four to six lanes. title: Rep. Suhas Subramanyam and Rep. Young Kim Introduces Tell the Government Once Act to Cut Red Tape for Americans on the Move
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) and Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) introduced the bipartisan Tell the Government Once Act to let Americans update their address with multiple federal agencies through a single online form.

Every year, millions of Americans move residences and must notify federal agencies like the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Social Security Administration (SSA), Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and U.S. Postal Service (USPS) one at a time. The IRS alone says a change of address generally takes 45 days to process. Missing even one agency can have serious consequences. Tax refunds, veterans’ benefits, Social Security payments, and important government notices can be delayed or sent to an outdated address.

The Tell the Government Once Act would streamline this outdated process by directing the General Services Administration (GSA) to create one voluntary form on Login.gov, which supports more than 180 million user accounts today. Through this secure online portal, Americans would verify their identity, enter a new address once, and decide which agencies receive it.

“We should be looking for every opportunity to make the government more efficient and easier to navigate for the American people,” said Rep. Suhas Subramanyam. “This bill does exactly that by allowing Americans to change their address though a single simple web form instead of through complicated agency documents. I’m proud to be introducing this bipartisan bill with Rep. Kim to save Americans’ time and energy.”

“Moving is stressful and expensive enough without having to track down four different federal agencies to tell each one the exact same thing,” said Rep. Young Kim. “A tax refund or a veteran’s benefit check should never go to the wrong address because of one missed form. My Tell the Government Once Act cuts through the bureaucracy so families can spend less time dealing with redundant paperwork and more time settling into their new homes.”

title: People’s Environmental Justice Caucus opposes Senate permitting reform bill
text:
WASHINGTON – The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus, founded by U.S. Reps. Summer L. Lee (PA-12), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), released the following statement in opposition to the U.S. Senate’s permitting reform bill:

“The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus stands with the nearly 200 community, labor, and environmental justice groups across the country urging Congress to reject the so-called ‘permitting reform’ deal that speeds up data center and fracked gas pipeline construction, limits communities’ ability to defend themselves from corporate polluters in court, threatens Tribal Nations’ sacred sites and cultural resources, and fails to deliver meaningful affordability or health protections our constituents desperately need.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 is a gift to Big Oil and Big Tech. This deal makes it easier to build the fossil energy infrastructure necessary to fuel the data center boom that is overwhelmingly opposed in neighborhoods from coast to coast. In the face of rising bipartisan disgust with data centers and pipelines, this deal eviscerates the limited tools communities already have to challenge developments that threaten their health and environment and effectively locks in dirty energy and destructive tech projects for generations. We should be strengthening judicial review, the Clean Water Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, and the National Environmental Policy Act, not undermining them to provide a rubber stamp to polluting projects.

“To make matters worse, this power grab doesn’t even meaningfully protect ratepayers from the soaring energy costs and toxic pollution that data center developments bring to their neighborhoods. Our residents are struggling to cope with overlapping climate, pollution, and affordability crises and need real action from Congress. This bad deal trades lifetimes of pollution and harm for pennies in relief. We urge Congress to reject this power grab and choose our communities over Big Oil and Big Tech.”

The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus, launched in March, exists to give frontline environmental justice communities a voice in Congress. The Caucus co-chairs are preparing to reintroduce the landmark Grijalva-McEachin Environmental Justice for All Act to reassert the public’s right to defend their health and environment, and will be kicking off a public participation process to solicit feedback on how to further strengthen these protections.

###

title: Congresswoman Torres Secures $172.5 Million for Local Projects in Water Resource Development Act
text:
Legislation advancing clean water, flood protection, and infrastructure priorities across the Inland Empire

Washington D.C. — Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) announced that she had secured numerous wins for communities in the 35th Congressional district in the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) of 2026. The bill, which recently passed the House of Representatives, includes $172.5 million in new and increased authorizations for Inland Empire water infrastructure in the 35th Congressional District. The legislation prioritizes federal assistance for local priorities submitted by Torres to improve water reliability, upgrade wastewater systems, and protect local communities from flooding.

“Families should be able to trust the water coming out of their taps and know their neighborhoods are protected when severe storms hit,” said Congresswoman Torres. “As we face a Super El Niño this year, I pushed to address aging pipelines, inadequate sewer service, and flood risks across the Inland Empire. These authorizations are a major step toward delivering those improvements and supporting the infrastructure and water supplies that our growing communities need. I will continue working to get this legislation across the finish line and secure funding to turn these priorities into completed projects.”

The House-passed WRDA 2026 includes:

$60 million in additional authorization for San Bernardino County, increasing the existing authorization from $24 million to $84 million and expanding eligible uses to include water supply and stormwater management.

A new $67.5 million authorization for San Bernardino and Riverside Counties for water and wastewater infrastructure, including water supply, distribution systems, stormwater management, and environmental restoration.

$40 million in additional authorization for Fontana, increasing the existing authorization from $16 million to $56 million and expanding eligible uses to include wastewater infrastructure, stormwater management, and water supply and distribution systems.

$5 million in additional authorization for the Inland Empire, increasing the existing authorization from $60 million to $65 million.

Advancing Local Water and Flood Protection Priorities:

In addition to securing increased funding authorizations for the Inland Empire, Torres submitted five environmental infrastructure priorities totaling more than $90.7 million. The bill’s expanded regional authorizations provide a pathway to pursue federal assistance for these projects:

Arrow Route Wastewater Treatment Phase III: Extend sewer service to an underserved, unincorporated area of Fontana, reducing reliance on failing septic systems that threaten groundwater quality.

Prado Regional Park Water Supply Project: Upgrade water storage, pumps, and irrigation infrastructure to maintain the park’s lake, protect natural resources, and preserve a valued community space in Chino.

West State Street Storm Drain Segments IIIB and IIIC: Improve drainage capacity in Montclair and Ontario to better protect homes, businesses, and roads from severe flooding.

Palo Verde Pipeline Replacement Project: Replace aging water lines in Montclair to improve water quality, reduce water loss, and strengthen water delivery and fire protection.

Lytle Creek Penstock: Rehabilitate a historic pipeline serving regional water supply and hydropower infrastructure to improve safety and long-term reliability.

Supporting Inland Empire Jobs Through Reliable Port Infrastructure

The bill also includes funding changes to help major ports, including the Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach, receive fairer, more predictable harbor maintenance funding. Nearly 40 percent of all imported U.S. consumer goods flow into these two ports and the Inland Empire, so ensuring donor ports can continue to invest in port infrastructure helps the Inland Empire workers in trucking, logistics, and manufacturing.

Ensuring Local Control of San Jose Creek Near Pomona

The bill would return local control of the San Jose Creek segment near Pomona to the Los Angeles County Public Works from the Army Corps of Engineers, helping the Los Angeles County Flood Control District manage the broader flood control system more efficiently. Reducing duplicative federal permitting requirements will help advance critical improvements that protect communities, revitalize and improve public safety in areas near the creek, and support water conservation.

title: Representative Tran Secures State Department Response on Vietnam's Human Rights Abuses
text:
Washington, D.C. – During last month’s United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) sent a letter to the U.S. Department of State demanding the U.S. government hold the communist Vietnamese government accountable for widespread human rights abuses. In a recent response, the Department of State affirmed its concerns about Vietnam’s human rights record and confirmed that these issues were discussed in a conversation between Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, Riley Barnes, and Vietnam’s Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dang Hoang Giang.

“As the United States Mission to the United Nations interacts with the delegation from the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, including Party General Secretary and State President Tô Lâm, I urge you to discuss human rights, call for the release of prisoners of conscience, raise concern about parts of the Penal Code that criminalize peaceful dissent, and affirm that stronger relations with Vietnam must be accompanied by measurable and verifiable progress on human rights,” said Representative Tran in the letter.

Read Representative Tran’s letter HERE.

“During the UNGA meetings, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor Riley Barnes expressed his concerns to Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Dang Hoang Giang on September 22, where he called for the release of unjustly detained political prisoners, including Le Huu Minh Tuan, and discussed transnational repression affecting U.S. citizens, freedom of expression, and religious freedom,” Katherine Bowles, Assistant Secretary, Bureau of Legislative Affairs, wrote in response.

Read the Department of State’s response HERE.

Representative Tran remains steadfast in demanding accountability for the Vietnamese government’s anti-democratic practices and human rights violations. As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the only Vietnamese American in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to uplifting and representing the Vietnamese community on the national stage and protecting the rights of immigrants.

In an April 2026 letter to General Secretary Tô Lâm, Congressman Tran demanded a visit with prisoners of conscience imprisoned by the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to monitor their well-being.

In April 2025, during the 50th commemoration of the Fall of Saigon, Congressman Tran held a roundtable with Vietnamese human rights activists and former prisoners of conscience to uplift their firsthand accounts of the oppression they faced at the hands of the Vietnamese government. Additionally, Tran introduced a congressional resolution to formally mark April 30, 2026 as the 51st anniversary of Black April.

Tran, a vocal advocate for advancing human rights in Vietnam, co-led H.R. 3122, the bipartisan Vietnam Human Rights Act, to hold Vietnamese communist officials accountable for human rights abuses and establish human rights and fair-trade priorities for U.S.-Vietnam relations.

Congressman Tran serves as the official sponsor of Le Huu Minh Tuan, a Vietnamese journalist who was wrongfully imprisoned by the communist government, through the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project and continues to fight for the release of prisoners of conscience around the world. In March 2025, Congressman Tran sent a letter to Secretary of State Rubio requesting their immediate assistance to secure the release of Le Huu Minh Tuan.

###

title: Congressman Valadao Hosts USDA/FSA Roundtable with Central Valley Producers in Tulare
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22), alongside Farm Service Agency Deputy Administrator for Farm Programs Jared Hagert, California State Farm Service Agency Executive Director Connie Conway, and U.S. Department of Agriculture California State Director for Rural Development Bryan Anguiano, hosted a roundtable discussion with farmers from across the Central Valley.

The roundtable conversation was focused on challenges our producers are facing, the need for a robust farm safety net, and critical USDA and FSA programs.

“Agriculture is the backbone of the Central Valley’s economy, and it’s important that our farmers have a seat at the table when decisions are made that affect their operations,” said Congressman Valadao. “That’s why I really appreciated the opportunity to bring together producers from across the Valley and USDA and California FSA leadership to discuss agriculture challenges, disaster preparedness heading into next year, and how we can better address the needs of local farmers. As the sole dairyman in Congress, I understand the uncertainty producers face, and I’ll continue working with our agricultural community and federal partners to ensure our farmers have the support they need to keep producing the food that feeds our nation.”

"Today’s forum with Representative Valadao and producers in the Central Valley was a valuable opportunity to hear concerns of producers and visit with them about the improvements to programs that the Farm Service Agency (FSA) is implementing,” said Jared Hagert, Deputy Administrator for Farm Programs at the Farm Service Agency.

"Today’s roundtable was a great opportunity to hear directly from the people who make the Central Valley a powerhouse for agriculture. These conversations help us understand what’s working, where we can improve, and how USDA can keep supporting the growth happening across this region. USDA appreciates Congressman Valadao’s leadership and being a strong voice for agricultural producers,” said Connie Conway, FSA Executive Director.

“USDA is committed to ensuring rural communities have the infrastructure, resources, and opportunities they need to prosper. Roundtables like today’s give us a clear understanding of local priorities, helping us shape investment priorities that strengthen the regional economy and improve quality of life for families across the Central Valley,” said Bryan Anguiano, Rural Development State Director.

title: Congressman Van Drew Introduces Bill to Reduce Crime on Public Transportation
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Van Drew announced the introduction of the Safe Transit Act, which would establish federal crime reduction standards for public transit agencies and tie their federal funding to their progress in keeping passengers safe.

"Across the country, innocent people are being stabbed, assaulted, and attacked on public transit for absolutely no reason," said Congressman Van Drew. "These are people going to work, coming home to their families, and just living their lives. It is sickening, and it has to stop. We cannot allow this kind of lawlessness to become normal in America. If transit agencies want federal taxpayer dollars, they need to show they are making real progress in keeping people safe. With this bill, we are going to set clear standards to hold them accountable and make sure public safety is a priority. Americans deserve to feel safe, and I will not accept anything less."

Background:

The Safe Transit Act would allow the Department of Transportation (DOT) to withhold federal transit funding from agencies that fail to make adequate progress toward federally established crime reduction targets. The bill would measure agencies against national crime statistics, require stronger fare evasion prevention infrastructure, and require large transit agencies to build their own apps, under standards the DOT sets, for passengers to report assaults and safety problems.

title: Vindman Introduces Legislation to Crack Down on Market Concentration Driving Up Costs
text:
The American Cost of Living Defense Act would increase transparency and strengthen federal oversight of concentrated markets for groceries, housing, prescription drugs, and other everyday essentials

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to strengthen federal oversight of market concentration and potential anti-competitive practices in industries that provide Americans with everyday essentials, from groceries and housing to prescription drugs and gasoline.

As families across Virginia and the country struggle with rising costs, the legislation would strengthen federal oversight of concentrated markets, identify potential drivers of higher prices, and provide greater transparency into the corporations that control the goods and services Americans rely on every day.

“American families are getting squeezed at every turn, paying more for groceries, housing, prescription drugs, and other basic necessities while powerful corporations rake in record profits,” said Vindman. “When a handful of giant corporations control the markets for everyday essentials, hardworking Americans are the ones left footing the bill. My American Cost of Living Defense Act will shine a light on corporate concentration, expose the practices that may be driving up prices, and hold powerful interests accountable. For too long, powerful corporations have had the upper hand while working families pay more and get less. It’s time we change that.”

The American Cost of Living Defense Act would direct the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to convene an interagency working group with the Department of Justice’s Antitrust Division, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

Every three years, the FTC would be required to publish a public report identifying the four largest firms by market share in each covered sector. The report would also examine corporate and supply-chain bottlenecks that may contribute to higher prices, as well as platforms or other market structures that may enable pricing coordination.

The legislation would focus on essential goods and services that affect household budgets, including groceries such as beef, poultry, eggs, and milk, housing rent, prescription drugs, motor fuel, and telecommunications services.

By making this information publicly available, the legislation would give consumers, policymakers, and federal regulators a clearer picture of where market concentration may be limiting competition and contributing to higher costs.

The American Cost of Living Defense Act is endorsed by the Economic Liberties Project.

title: Reps. Whitesides, Lofgren Introduce Bill to Protect Elections from Intimidation Tactics and Inference
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (CA-27) and Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) introduced the Stop Harassment and Intimidations in Elections through Legal Defenses (SHIELD) Our Elections Act, legislation designed to empower state attorney generals and voters to protect against illegal election interference from federal officials, extend the statute of limitations for federal election crimes, and prevent unlawful ballot seizures. The SHIELD Our Elections Act has a senate companion bill led by Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA).

The SHIELD Our Elections Act comes as President Trump escalates his rhetoric in the leadup to the 2026 midterm elections, threatening to nationalize voting and claiming widespread fraud in voter rolls. The President has also continued to repeat unsubstantiated claims of fraud and meddling in the 2020 election, an effort to undermine voter confidence in the democratic process. This legislation also comes on the heels of attacks on California’s elections, including ballot seizures in Riverside County and an ongoing effort to stop the state from counting up to 20,000 California ballots.

“Every eligible American should be able to cast their ballot without fear of intimidation or political interference,” said Rep. Whitesides. “Our elections belong to the people, not politicians looking to hold onto power. We need clear protections that safeguard ballots, hold anyone who breaks the law accountable, and give voters confidence that their voices will be heard. I’m proud to work with Rep. Lofgren and Senator Padilla to protect our democracy and uphold the right to vote.”

“Trump is terrified of facing accountability from America’s voters who have suffered from his policies, so he’s been trying to once again sow chaos and confusion,” said Rep. Lofgren. “We need to protect ballots from being improperly seized like we saw in Fulton County and Riverside County. As a former Chair of the House Administration Committee, which oversees federal elections, I’m proud to co-lead this bill with Rep. Whitesides that will defend the integrity of our elections and strengthen accountability for those who commit federal election crimes.”

Specifically, the SHIELD Our Elections Act:

Allows State Attorneys General and impacted voters to sue when federal officials unlawfully interfere with or intimidate them at polling places.

Strengthens accountability by extending the statute of limitations from five to nine years for key federal election crimes, including interference by armed forces and voter intimidation, to enable them to be brought by future administrations for past actions.

Protects ballots from improper seizure by limiting when state or federal law enforcement may seize ballots or election equipment and requiring court-authorized election officials to maintain joint custody whenever materials must be seized, especially prior to the resolution of an election.

The SHIELD Our Elections Act is led by Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) in the Senate and cosponsored by Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

Rep. Whitesides is joined by Reps. Nanette Barragán (CA-44); Everton Blair (GA-13); Shontel Brown (OH-11); Julia Brownley (CA-26); Salud Carbajal (CA-24); Gilbert Cisneros (CA-31); J. Luis Correa (CA-46); Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10); Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07); Laura Friedman (CA-30); John Garamendi (CA-08); Robert Garcia (CA-42); Al Green (TX-09); Maggie Goodlander (NH-02); Josh Harder (CA-09); Steven Horsford (NV-04); Val Hoyle (OR-04); Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06); Sara Jacobs (CA-51); Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37); Mike Levin (CA-49); Sam Liccardo (CA-16); Ted Lieu (CA-36); Doris Matsui (CA-07); Gregory Meeks (NY-05); Kevin Mullin (CA-15); Nancy Pelosi (CA-11); Brittany Pettersen (CO-07); Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05); Lateefah Simon (CA-12); Brad Sherman (CA-32); Melanie Stansbury (NM-01); Norma Torres (CA-35); Maxine Waters (CA-43); Nikema Williams (GA-05) as original cosponsors.

Bacon, Fitzpatrick, Gluesenkamp Perez Introduce Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act to Block Russian Oil Imports and Defend Ukraine
text:
Bipartisan legislation would nullify Treasury's Russian oil waiver, reinforce federal law, and safeguard critical intelligence support for Ukraine

Washington, D.C. – Representative Don Bacon (NE-02) joined Reps. Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01) and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) yesterday in introducing the Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act of 2026 to uphold the federal prohibition on Russian energy imports and protect critical U.S. intelligence support for Ukraine.

The legislation follows the Treasury Department's October 9th issuance of General License 135, authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, including imports into the United States, despite a bipartisan federal law enacted in 2022 prohibiting Russian energy imports. The decision threatens to undermine congressional efforts to cut off the revenue streams sustaining Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine.

“For years, President Trump criticized Europe for buying Russian energy and propping up Putin’s war economy. Further, Congress overwhelmingly voted to impose tough sanctions on Russia. Now, Trump wants to make it easier for Putin to sell diesel fuel. He is wrong,” said Rep. Bacon. “Americans overwhelmingly support Ukraine and oppose Putin’s aggression and war crimes. The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Against Russia Act nullifies the Russian diesel waiver, prohibits Treasury spending that violates the 2022 Russian oil import ban and provides intelligence support to Ukraine.” Congress must step up and force the President to support freedom and oppose the war criminal. America must stand with the Free World.”

“Russia chose this war. Ukraine did not. The United States must leave no doubt about where it stands. We must not import a single drop of Russian oil. Congress made that decision with overwhelming bipartisan support in 2022, and that law remains in force. It is not a suggestion, nor should its intent be undermined through administrative waivers. We cannot demand accountability from Putin while opening American markets to the Russian energy that helps finance his war. Every exception sends Moscow the wrong message: that American resolve can be outlasted,” said Rep. Fitzpatrick.“President Reagan understood that strength is not the obstacle to peace. It is what makes a just peace possible. Our responsibility is to stand firmly behind Ukraine’s sovereignty and ensure America’s commitments are reflected in America’s actions. Peace becomes possible when aggression carries a cost greater than its reward. On that, there can be no ambiguity.”

“The President’s dirty deal to import Russian oil is running roughshod over our national interests and the bipartisan will of Congress and a bipartisan 2022 law explicitly banning the import of Russian oil. We won’t turn a blind eye to that,”said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “This bill will rein in this reckless deal and make clear that my community doesn’t want any part of funding Putin’s fascist war in Ukraine and the ongoing attacks terrorizing families in the Donbas. If the President is serious about bringing down gas prices, he should end the war in Iran, not send our tax dollars to Putin.”

“The Administration’s decision to import Russian diesel is illegal, and Congress must move decisively to ensure the law is followed,” Daniel Balson, Director of Advocacy and Razom for Ukraine said. “Razom for Ukraine endorses Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick’s Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act and applauds the bipartisan effort to block the unlawful and immoral importation of Russian diesel. Only by projecting strength can we force Russia to come to the negotiating table. Weakness and deference will only prolong Putin’s war.”

“FDD Action applauds the introduction of the bipartisan legislation. The timely Congressional action represents a strategic and moral intervention on behalf of the bipartisan majority of American’s who support Ukraine in its fight for freedom. We urge members of Congress to support this crucial legislation and urge the Trump Administration to reconsider its diesel deal with the Kremlin,” said Daniel Vaynshteyn Associste directors of government relations FDD Action.

The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act would:

Nullify the Treasury Department's Russian oil waiver, immediately rendering General License 135 ineffective and prohibiting future waivers or general licenses authorizing the importation of Russian energy products.

Strengthen enforcement of the existing import ban by prohibiting Treasury from expending funds on agreements that violate the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022.

Reinforce critical intelligence support for Ukraine, requiring relevant intelligence agencies to provide support for Ukraine's defense and notify congressional intelligence committees within 24 hours of any interruption.

title: TAPinto Op-Ed by Rep. Smith'25th Anniversary of Homeless Veterans Assistance Act—my law that continues to truly help veterans'
text:
By U.S. Rep. Chris Smith

Published October 24, 2026 at 8:37 AM

Twenty-five years ago, an appalling number of our Nation’s heroes were living on the street.

It was a scandal: men and women—who courageously and selflessly stepped up and put their lives on the line to defend our great Nation—were without homes in the very country they served.

According to Veterans Administration (VA) estimates, in 2001 almost 300,000 veterans were experiencing homelessness in the United States on any given night. Of those, about 80% suffered from disabilities attributable to their military service—such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)—and many struggled with chemical dependencies on alcohol and drugs.

As the Chairman of the House Committee on Veterans Affairs at the time, I met with numerous veterans experiencing homelessness, as well as the Veteran Service Organizations (VSOs) working to address the problem. I was horrified to learn of the abject neglect endured by our brave men and women, many of whom had sustained permanent injuries and chronic illnesses as a result of their service.

Not only were they in dire need of housing, but their medical conditions too often limited them from transitioning into civilian life.

Something had to be done and it was.

In August of that year, I wrote the landmark HR 2716, the Homeless Veterans Comprehensive Assistance Act of 2001, which included provisions that strengthened at-home care programs, authorized important job training efforts, and expanded grants for transition programs to help incarcerated veterans reenter society.

It also, for the first time ever, authorized VA dental care coverage for homeless veterans to improve their oral, digestive, and heart health while boosting their appearance and self-confidence, which helps them to succeed in the work force.

This legislation—informed by the first-hand accounts of veterans who have struggled with housing insecurity and crafted with input from VSOs—targeted the problem of veteran homelessness with coordinated government efforts that addressed the root causes of the problem. This approach provided the proper roadmap for getting veterans off our streets and keeping them in stable housing situations with proper medical and supportive care.

After I chaired a critical congressional hearing on the legislation, and following its passage in both the House and Senate, it was signed into law in December 2001.

Today, the number of homeless veterans on any given night has dropped to 32,495—still far too many, but a remarkable decline nonetheless—thanks not only to the programs included in my law, but also to the important work of many VA partner organizations, as well as the best practices that have been implemented and added over the years.

Moreover, the Trump Administration and VA Secretary Doug Collins have continued to prioritize ending veteran homelessness.

Secretary Collins’ VA has permanently housed close to 52,000 veterans since January 2025—the highest number in seven years—partially through HUD/VASH vouchers, which were codified in my 2001 law. The HUD/VASH program, which pairs housing support with case management services, has awarded more than 116,000 vouchers since 2008, providing veterans with immediate stability, as well as ongoing care and resources.

My original law also created the Homeless Providers Grant and Per Diem Program, which provides grants for transitional housing, ensuring that veterans can continue to receive services and treatment while seeking more permanent homes. The VA recently announced $318 million in awards—to be distributed in Fiscal Year 2027—to community organizations that provide transitional housing, underscoring a renewed federal commitment to combatting veteran homelessness.

We have made incredible progress in the fight against veteran homelessness—but one homeless veteran is still one too many. While the current number of homeless veterans remains unacceptable, I am encouraged by this tremendous achievement and remain committed to ensuring that every veteran has access to the resources and care they have rightfully earned and wholeheartedly deserve.

title: Figures Calls for Major Disaster Declaration in Response to Hurricane Isaias Damage

title: Garbarino Announces Milestone of More Than 10,000 Constituent Cases Resolved
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-02) announced today that his office has successfully resolved more than 10,000 constituent cases and returned nearly 37 million dollars since he took office in 2021.

From helping veterans access benefits and assisting seniors with Social Security and Medicare to resolving passport delays and immigration issues, Garbarino's constituent services team works directly with federal agencies to help Long Islanders get the assistance they need.

“Helping Long Islanders is the most important part of my job, and I'm incredibly proud that my office has now resolved more than 10,000 constituent cases and helped return nearly $37 million to the people of my district,” said Congressman Garbarino. “I especially want to thank my dedicated constituent services team, who work hard every day to help Long Islanders get the benefits they've earned and the answers they deserve. Whether it's a delayed passport, an issue with Social Security, or trouble getting through to a federal agency, we are here to help.”

Among those assisted by Garbarino's office is Wojciech Krystkowiak, who received help navigating an immigration matter. Following the office's involvement, an immigration judge granted his application for relief, allowing him to remain legally in the United States.

“Thank you so much for this incredible news. Words cannot express how deeply grateful my family and I are for everything you and your office have done for us. Your support, dedication, and guidance throughout this process made a life-changing difference for me. You have truly given me a new beginning, and for that, I will be forever thankful. Please extend my heartfelt appreciation to your entire team for their hard work and kindness. Thank you once again for changing my life,” said Krystkowiak.

William Lynch also received assistance with his employment authorization application, which was subsequently approved.

“I have obtained my OPT visa and begun work. I appreciate all the help your office has provided. Best of luck,” said Lynch.

Lourdes Smith also received assistance from Garbarino's office in securing her passport. Following its issuance, Smith thanked the team for their help.

“Thank you so much to you and your team for helping me get my passport,” said Smith.

In addition to helping constituents navigate federal agencies, Garbarino's office also assists Long Islanders planning visits to Washington, D.C., including arranging tours of the U.S. Capitol and other historic landmarks.

Alyssa Byrnes, who recently visited Washington with her mother, praised the assistance she received from Garbarino's staff.

“It’s really nice to have a representative and an office that are so responsive and willing to help their constituents. It certainly doesn’t go unnoticed, and I wanted to make sure you all knew how much we appreciated it,” said Byrnes.

Long Islanders seeking assistance with a federal agency or interested in arranging tours during a visit to Washington, D.C. are encouraged to contact Congressman Garbarino's office at (631) 541-4225 or visit his official website.

title: Messmer Presents Purple Heart and Air Medal to Vietnam Veteran Gary Long
text:

title: Amata Pays Courtesy Call to PACOM Commander Admiral Paparo
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata, while in Hawaii attending a family funeral, paid a courtesy visit to U.S. Pacific Command headquarters, and PACOM Commander Admiral Samuel J. Paparo, including discussion of American Samoa and the U.S. military’s vast responsibilities of the Pacific region.

Congresswoman Amata and PACOM Commander Admiral Paparo on Thursday

Amata’s travel to Hawaii enabled her to be present at the memorial service, and surrounding family gatherings, for her mother’s sister, Kaho’oki’eki’e Julia Stewart Williams, who passed away peacefully at age 98 this month with family at her side.

Kaho’oki’eki’e Julia Stewart Williams

Amata’s aunt Julia was the younger sister of Kawaili’ula Nora Coleman, former First Lady of American Samoa. Nora served American Samoa for sixteen years as the wife of the longest serving and first elected indigenous Samoan Governor, Uifa’atali Peter T. Coleman, while Julia Williams was a lifelong education leader in Hawaii, teacher, children’s author, and 16-year director of the Kamehameha Schools Intermediate Reading Program.

During Congresswoman Amata’s visit with Admiral Paparo, they spoke in his office covering multiple topics, and Amata voiced her and American Samoa’s opposition to deep sea mining in nearby waters, with awareness that the Defense Department has longstanding interest in developing more sources for critical minerals, independent of China, for use in U.S. systems components, the fact driving the U.S. focus on American Samoa’s EEZ that was announced early last year.

“I voice our concerns at every meeting that could have any bearing on this issue at all, as it’s a top priority matter for our islands,” said Aumua Amata. “Of course, the Admiral was already highly informed of my position, our concerns, and American Samoa in general. I appreciated his time and conversation. He leads an enormous area of responsibility that secures the Pacific for trade, travel, fishing, tourism and cargo, as he described for me on his large map. Our people, with our high enlistment rate, have many reasons to support and appreciate our military. My ongoing message to Washington, as there are great power competitive interests focused on the Pacific, is that American Samoa is a strategic point that warrants further U.S. investment, and listening to our people.”

title: People’s Environmental Justice Caucus opposes Senate permitting reform bill
text:
WASHINGTON – The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus, founded by U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Summer L. Lee (PA-12), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), released the following statement in opposition to the U.S. Senate’s permitting reform bill:

“The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus stands with the nearly 200 community, labor, and environmental justice groups across the country urging Congress to reject the so-called ‘permitting reform’ deal that speeds up data center and fracked gas pipeline construction, limits communities’ ability to defend themselves from corporate polluters in court, threatens Tribal Nations’ sacred sites and cultural resources, and fails to deliver meaningful affordability or health protections our constituents desperately need.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 is a gift to Big Oil and Big Tech. This deal makes it easier to build the fossil energy infrastructure necessary to fuel the data center boom that is overwhelmingly opposed in neighborhoods from coast to coast. In the face of rising bipartisan disgust with data centers and pipelines, this deal eviscerates the limited tools communities already have to challenge developments that threaten their health and environment and effectively locks in dirty energy and destructive tech projects for generations. We should be strengthening judicial review, the Clean Water Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, and the National Environmental Policy Act, not undermining them to provide a rubber stamp to polluting projects.

“To make matters worse, this power grab doesn’t even meaningfully protect ratepayers from the soaring energy costs and toxic pollution that data center developments bring to their neighborhoods. Our residents are struggling to cope with overlapping climate, pollution, and affordability crises and need real action from Congress. This bad deal trades lifetimes of pollution and harm for pennies in relief. We urge Congress to reject this power grab and choose our communities over Big Oil and Big Tech.”
