title: Crow Demands SpaceX Explain Role in Starshield Disruptions
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is demanding SpaceX CEO Elon Musk explain what he and his company know about the disruptions that occurred to Ukraine’s Starshield satellites. The letter also asks whether SpaceX has restored access, if they discussed any of this with Vladimir Putin, and if the company considered the impacts of this decision.

According to the reporting, Musk was involved in the disruption after speaking with administration officials, including President Donald Trump.Since the disruptions occurred, Ukrainian civilians have been killed by Russian strikes, and U.S. personnel have been put at risk.

"Unelected billionaires and private corporations should not decide what is in the best interest of America's national security. Trump and Musk are pointing fingers at each other, and someone is not telling the truth, said Congressman Crow. “We need answers about what happened. These life-and-death decisions endangered US diplomats and embassy staff, and led to civilian deaths in Ukraine. Trump is abandoning our allies.”

Joining Crow in his letter to Musk are Senators Peter Welch (D-VT), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee Gregory Meeks (D-NY), and Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee Jim McGovern (D-MA).

Crow and his colleagues wrote: “You have publicly asserted that limits to Starlink access are ‘decided by the U.S. military and ultimately POTUS.’ Yet public reporting indicates that you personally brought the suggestion to President Trump to slow down Ukrainian communications through SpaceX’s Starlink systems, and U.S. government officials have reportedly indicated that you personally ordered the speed cap on Ukrainian military use of Starshield.

“As a publicly traded company, SpaceX has a legal obligation to disclose to shareholders and the public material events that could affect your business model. The revelation that you personally wielded control over a foreign country’s military communications would require disclosure of elevated risks for corporate governance, geopolitical exposure, and potential adverse actions by foreign governments,” they continued.

Congressman Crow has been a strong supporter of the Ukrainian people. Upon news of the Starshield disruption, he immediately pressed the Trump Administration for answers on who authorized the changes and what its impacts were. He recently introduced a bill to protect Ukrainian nationals already in the U.S. against the threat of deportation by extending their Temporary Protected Status (TPS).

When Putin’s invasion began, Crow immediately called for the U.S. to send military and humanitarian support to Ukraine, for international sanctions against Russia, and for a stronger NATO alliance to meet these new security threats. Weeks later, as Ukrainians fled their homes, Congressman Crow and other members advocated for an expedited immigration status for Ukrainians to the U.S. Crow has visited Ukraine several times since Russia’s invasion.

The Congressman has been one of the earliest and strongest supporters of military, development, and humanitarian assistance for Ukraine. He voted for, and strongly advocated for, every supplemental package provided to Ukraine.

Full text of the letter is available below:

Dear Mr. Musk

Your company’s Starlink communications system has been instrumental in allowing Ukraine to defend itself against Russian missile and drone attacks targeting civilians. Access to Starlink has recently been throttled or cut off entirely, without a clear explanation as to why.

Since the failure of his ground invasion, Russian leader Vladimir Putin turned to a brutal air campaign targeting Ukrainian civilians to wear down public morale. Just last month, more than 300 Ukrainian civilians were killed and 2,000 injured by Russian drone and missile strikes. Ukraine has built an innovative network of drone systems to defend against the thousands of strikes launched each month by Russia. However, these life-saving systems often depend on Starlink’s military version, Starshield, for accurate communication and transmission of targeting data.

Last week on October 13, 2026, Ukrainian officials said that their forces suddenly lost access to Starshield communications inside Ukraine for drones moving over 100 miles per hour. That interruption halted Ukraine’s ability to guide its self-defense drones against incoming Russian missiles and drones and stopped Ukrainian attacks against Russian positions. That very night, Russia launched a record-setting coordinated drone and missile barrage at Ukrainian civilian energy infrastructure, using at least 39 ballistic and hypersonic missiles and 128 Shahed-type drones. The strikes killed at least three civilians, including a child, and injured at least 21.

You have publicly asserted that limits to Starlink access are “decided by the U.S. military and ultimately POTUS.” Yet public reporting indicates that you personally brought the suggestion to President Trump to slow down Ukrainian communications through SpaceX’s Starlink systems, and U.S. government officials have reportedly indicated that you personally ordered the speed cap on Ukrainian military use of Starshield. Reports published yesterday indicate that President Trump called you to personally ask for restoration of Starshield capabilities and the President has asserted it was restored, and yet public reports indicate the system remains severely restricted for Ukraine’s defense forces.

As a publicly traded company, SpaceX has a legal obligation to disclose to shareholders and the public material events that could affect your business model. The revelation that you personally wielded control over a foreign country’s military communications would require disclosure of elevated risks for corporate governance, geopolitical exposure, and potential adverse actions by foreign governments. We therefore ask for your responses to the following by October 31, 2026:

1. Have you or any SpaceX official at any point discussed limiting Starlink access for Ukrainian forces inside Russia or Ukraine with Russian President Vladimir Putin, President Trump, or any officials or representatives acting on their behalf? Please provide any such communications or records of communications.

2. Did you, SpaceX, or entities operating on SpaceX’s behalf reduce, shut off, or throttle Starlink access to Ukrainian forces this month—either inside Russia or Ukraine? If so, why and on whose orders?

3. Have you or any official at SpaceX communicated to Ukrainian officials any conditions or actions required for a full or partial resumption of Starlink access for Ukrainian defense forces?

4. Did President Trump or the White House, in fact, make a request to restore Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield systems? Have those systems been fully restored? If so, when? And if not, why not?

5. Which specific individuals, agencies, or entities control the operational decisions from this day forward on restoring full and non-capped access to Starlink and Starshield communications systems for Ukrainian forces?

title: Figures Urges Disaster Aid for Alabama After Isaias
text:
MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WDNews) — U.S. Rep. Shomari Figures is urging President Donald Trump to approve Alabama’s request for a major disaster declaration following Hurricane Isaias, according to his office.

Figures sent a letter Oct. 24 supporting Gov. Kay Ivey’s Oct. 23 request. He pointed to damage across southern Alabama, including several Wiregrass counties.

“Hurricane Isaias was a Category 2 hurricane with damaging winds of 105 miles per hour and extensive rainfall that impacted the Gulf Coast and produced significant flooding, massive power outages, and widespread damage throughout the State of Alabama,” Figures wrote.

“As recovery efforts are ongoing, I urgently request that the Administration approve the State of Alabama’s request as quickly as possible.”

The letter identified Barbour, Butler, Coffee, Conecuh, Crenshaw, Dale, Geneva, Henry, Houston, Lowndes, Monroe, Pike and Washington counties as the areas hardest hit.

According to Figures’ letter, almost every resident in Conecuh County lost power at some point during the storm. Monroe County sustained significant damage to power lines and other critical infrastructure, including communications systems.

Figures also reported that a Barbour County resident died in a storm-related vehicle crash involving fallen trees.

“While the effects of Hurricane Isaias may continue to impact the state for quite some time, promptly approving this major disaster declaration request will help ensure that the people of Alabama are prepared for the recovery phase ahead,” Figures wrote.

He closed the letter by pledging support for recovery efforts.

“Alabamians are resilient, and with cooperation at all levels of government, we will rebuild stronger than ever. I stand ready to provide any support necessary, and I thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.”

title: Hoyer Sends Letter to Armed Services Committees Requesting an Investigation on Starlink and Starshield Restrictions in Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) sent a letter to House Committee on Armed Services Chairman Mike Rogers (AL-03) and Senate Committee on Armed Services Chairman Roger Wicker (R-MS) requesting they investigate the decision to suspend Ukraine’s full access to Starlink and Starshield. In Congressman Hoyer's letter, he calls for the committees to subpoena Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to testify on the source of the suspension.

“Ukraine has depended on reliable access to these systems in order to guide warfighters, drones, and cruise missiles as it works to repel Russia’s criminal and illegal invasion of its territory,” said Congressman Hoyer. “If full access to Starlink and Starshield are not restored soon, many Ukrainians will die, and recent battlefield gains against the invader may be lost. That this technology is indispensable for Ukraine’s defense and crucial for continuing its battlefield momentum is unquestionable.”

“Congress has steadfastly supported Ukraine in its fight for freedom, including through assistance funding and sanctions legislation that were enacted with broad, bipartisan support in both the House and Senate,” Congressman Hoyer continued. “The American people and their representatives have a vested interest in making sure that these efforts have not been in vain and American support is delivered and sustained as intended.”

To read the full letter, click here or see below:

The Honorable Mike Rogers

Chairman

House Committee on Armed Services

2216 Rayburn House Office Building

Washington, D.C. 20515

The Honorable Roger Wicker

Chairman

Senate Committee on Armed Services

228 Russell Senate Office Building

Washington, D.C. 20510

Dear Chairmen Rogers and Wicker:

As you are aware, the recent restrictions on the use of Starlink and Starshield technologies by Ukrainian forces have had a devastating effect on battlefield operations and on air defense for civilian areas. Ukraine has depended on reliable access to these systems in order to guide warfighters, drones, and cruise missiles as it works to repel Russia’s criminal and illegal invasion of its territory. If full access to Starlink and Starshield are not restored soon, many Ukrainians will die, and recent battlefield gains against the invader may be lost. That this technology is indispensable for Ukraine’s defense and crucial for continuing its battlefield momentum is unquestionable.

Congress has steadfastly supported Ukraine in its fight for freedom, including through assistance funding and sanctions legislation that were enacted with broad, bipartisan support in both the House and Senate. The American people and their representatives have a vested interest in making sure that these efforts have not been in vain and American support is delivered and sustained as intended. Consequently, Congress must investigate the source of the decision to suspend full access to Starlink and Starshield – whether it was the determination of SpaceX and its leadership independently or whether it came at the direction of the Trump Administration. To that effect, I ask that your committees subpoena Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to testify and answer that question definitively, along with examining any communications relating to the slowdown of Starlink or Starshield. Congress also must understand exactly what the relationship has been between the Defense Department and SpaceX with regard to controlling Starlink and Starshield coverage for the Ukraine-Russia theater of war.

The people of Ukraine are looking to us for help, and the people of the United States – who strongly support Ukraine’s fight for liberty, sovereignty, and international law – are looking to us for answers. We owe it to our constituents to ensure that the will of Congress – as reflected by passing multiple appropriation bills and with over 300 votes to pass the Ukraine Support Act through the House and to enact the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law – is respected by this Administration. It would be not only idiotic for the United States actively to advantage Russia on the battlefield; it would be completely contrary to the intent of Congress and the American people.

We must never tip the scales toward its autocracy and criminal invasion rather than to support Ukraine’s heroic fight for democracy.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely yours,

title: Reps. Lofgren, Whitesides Introduce Bill to Protect Elections from Intimidation Tactics and Inference
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – On Friday, Reps. Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) and George Whitesides (CA-27) introduced the Stop Harassment and Intimidations in Elections through Legal Defenses (SHIELD) Our Elections Act, legislation designed to empower state attorney generals and voters to protect against illegal election interference from federal officials, extend the statute of limitations for federal election crimes, and prevent unlawful ballot seizures. The SHIELD Our Elections Act has a senate companion bill led by Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA).

The SHIELD Our Elections Act comes as President Trump escalates his rhetoric in the leadup to the 2026 midterm elections, threatening to nationalize voting and claiming widespread fraud in voter rolls. The President has also continued to repeat unsubstantiated claims of fraud and meddling in the 2020 election, an effort to undermine voter confidence in the democratic process. This legislation also comes on the heels of attacks on California’s elections, including ballot seizures in Riverside County and an ongoing effort to stop the state from counting up to 20,000 California ballots.

"Trump is terrified of facing accountability from America’s voters who have suffered from his policies, so he’s been trying to once again sow chaos and confusion,” said Rep. Lofgren. “We need to protect ballots from being improperly seized like we saw in Fulton County and Riverside County. As a former Chair of the House Administration Committee, which oversees federal elections, I’m proud to co-lead this bill with Rep. Whitesides that will defend the integrity of our elections and strengthen accountability for those who commit federal election crimes.”

“Every eligible American should be able to cast their ballot without fear of intimidation or political interference,” said Rep. Whitesides. “Our elections belong to the people, not politicians looking to hold onto power. We need clear protections that safeguard ballots, hold anyone who breaks the law accountable, and give voters confidence that their voices will be heard. I’m proud to work with Rep. Lofgren and Senator Padilla to protect our democracy and uphold the right to vote.”

Specifically, the SHIELD Our Elections Act:

Allows State Attorneys General and impacted voters to sue when federal officials unlawfully interfere with or intimidate them at polling places.

Strengthens accountability by extending the statute of limitations from five to nine years for key federal election crimes, including interference by armed forces and voter intimidation, to enable them to be brought by future administrations for past actions.

Protects ballots from improper seizure by limiting when state or federal law enforcement may seize ballots or election equipment and requiring court-authorized election officials to maintain joint custody whenever materials must be seized, especially prior to the resolution of an election.

The SHIELD Our Elections Act is led by Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) in the Senate and cosponsored by Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

Reps. Lofgren and Whitesides are joined by Reps. Nanette Barragán (CA-44); Everton Blair (GA-13); Shontel Brown (OH-11); Julia Brownley (CA-26); Salud Carbajal (CA-24); Gilbert Cisneros (CA-31); J. Luis Correa (CA-46); Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10); Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07); Laura Friedman (CA-30); John Garamendi (CA-08); Robert Garcia (CA-42); Al Green (TX-09); Maggie Goodlander (NH-02); Josh Harder (CA-09); Steven Horsford (NV-04); Val Hoyle (OR-04); Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06); Sara Jacobs (CA-51); Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37); Mike Levin (CA-49); Sam Liccardo (CA-16); Ted Lieu (CA-36); Doris Matsui (CA-07); Gregory Meeks (NY-05); Kevin Mullin (CA-15); Nancy Pelosi (CA-11); Brittany Pettersen (CO-07); Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05); Lateefah Simon (CA-12); Brad Sherman (CA-32); Melanie Stansbury (NM-01); Norma Torres (CA-35); Maxine Waters (CA-43); Nikema Williams (GA-05) as original cosponsors.

title: Bacon, Bell Introduce Bipartisan Resolution to Establish a National Day of the Deployed
text:
The bipartisan resolution designates October 26 as a day of recognition honoring all U.S. service members deployed overseas and their families

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Don Bacon (R-NE-02) and Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) today introduced the bipartisan National Day of the Deployed resolution.

The legislation designates October 26 as a day of recognition honoring all U.S. service members currently deployed overseas and the families who support them at home. The observance formally recognizes the sacrifices made by deployed service members who serve far from home, often in harm’s way, as well as their loved ones who shoulder the burden of separation and uncertainty in their absence.

“The American men and women who are deployed around the globe to protect and defend our national interests are the front lines of defense for our democracy,” said Rep. Bacon. “I gladly served and deployed for my country. The all-volunteer force underpins everything we hold sacred as a nation, and the fact that they and their families sacrifice so much for our freedoms is a testament to their dedication. This recognition of the ‘Day of the Deployed’ is the least we can do for them.”

“Every deployment asks something of the person in uniform and of the people waiting for them at home. The missed birthdays, the empty chair at the table, the long stretches without a phone call: those are sacrifices and an honorable commitment to this nation. As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I’m proud to join Rep. Bacon in making sure our service members and their families know that this country sees them and is grateful for their incredible sacrifices,” said Rep. Bell.

title: Alaska Delegation Announces Nearly $105 Million for Six Critical Port Infrastructure Projects Across Alaska
text:
ANCHORAGE, ALASKA—U.S. Senators Dan Sullivan and Lisa Murkowski and Congressman Nick Begich (all R-Alaska) today announced nearly $105 million in U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) awards to six critical port and maritime infrastructure projects across Alaska through the Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP). The investments will support the modernization and expansion of ports, harbors, docks, and related infrastructure serving communities from Southeast Alaska to the Aleutians and the Arctic.

“Alaska is a resource-rich but infrastructure-poor state, and expanding our critical infrastructure has been one of my highest priorities since coming to the Senate,” said Senator Sullivan. “My team and I worked hard to secure this $105 million in new investments—another major win for our coastal communities and part of the generational infrastructure opportunities we are creating across Alaska. With more coastline than the rest of the country combined, our ports and harbors are lifelines for our communities, our economy, and our national security. That's why we fought to change federal law to ensure Alaska projects can fairly compete for these investments. From our ports and rural docks to broadband, aviation safety, energy, water and sanitation, rural health care, and military infrastructure, we are making investments on a scale that will benefit Alaskans for generations. I want to thank Secretary Sean Duffy, Under Secretary Ryan McCormack, and MARAD Administrator Stephen Carmel for their leadership and commitment to addressing Alaska's unique infrastructure needs.”

“The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act continues to deliver for Alaska,” said Senator Murkowski. “These projects will improve safety and efficiency while helping ensure Alaska can continue to serve as a gateway for commerce, transportation, and our national security. I’m proud to have worked with the delegation to drive further federal investment to modernize our ports and build the infrastructure Alaska’s future demands.”

“Since day one, we have been advocating for critical investments in Alaska’s ports and harbors, making their strategic importance clear to the Administration and advancing these priorities through our work in Congress,” said Congressman Begich. “Alaska's ports are critical to our state's maritime economy and America's strategic presence in the Arctic and North Pacific. From modernizing Kodiak’s St. Herman’s Harbor to expanding Nome’s deep-draft port capabilities, these investments will support Alaska’s commercial fishing sector, maritime security, and strengthen our transportation and supply chain networks. I appreciate the Administration's recognition of Alaska's strategic importance, and I will continue working to ensure our state has the infrastructure necessary to support good-paying jobs and lasting economic growth.”

Alaska Port Infrastructure Development Program Awards

The six projects receiving funding are:

DeLong Dock Replacement Project — Whittier: $50,593,488. Funding will support the replacement of aging maritime infrastructure serving Southcentral Alaska's transportation network and regional supply chains.

Ounalashka Arctic and North Pacific Maritime Hub — Unalaska: $4,402,403. Funding will advance maritime infrastructure supporting commercial fisheries, shipping, and maritime operations in the North Pacific and Arctic.

Saint Herman Harbor Recapitalization Project, Phase 2A — Kodiak: $26,070,000. Funding will support improvements to a vital facility serving Kodiak's commercial fishing fleet and maritime economy.

Arctic Deep-Draft Port, Local Service Facilities — Nome: $11,250,000. Funding will support local service infrastructure associated with the expansion of Nome's Arctic deep-draft port, strengthening maritime access, commerce, emergency response, and national security.

Port of Alaska Modernization Program, Stevedore Support Facilities and Landside Operations Readiness Project — Anchorage: $6,394,000. Funding will support operational improvements associated with modernizing Alaska's principal maritime cargo hub.

Kake Marine Cargo Dock Development Project — Kake: $6,287,220. Funding will advance maritime cargo infrastructure serving the Southeast Alaska community.

Historic Infrastructure Investments Across Alaska

The awards build on billions of dollars in federal infrastructure investments secured for Alaska in recent years, including major projects to improve ports and harbors, expand broadband connectivity, strengthen aviation safety, modernize military and Coast Guard installations, improve rural energy infrastructure, and transform rural health care.

Ports, Harbors, and Maritime Infrastructure: Hundreds of millions of dollars in federal investments supporting Alaska's ports and harbors, including approximately $324 million in recent Port Infrastructure Development Program awards, $250 million for Nome's Arctic deep-draft port, $249 million for the Port MacKenzie Rail Extension, and more than $169 million for the Don Young Port of Alaska modernization.

Aviation Safety and Airport Infrastructure — Nearly $500 Million: Planned FAA investments over three years to modernize aviation infrastructure and strengthen safety across Alaska, including $80 million for at least 110 weather observing systems and 64 aviation weather camera sites, $40 million for the FAA's Alaska Aviation Safety Initiative, and additional airport and air traffic infrastructure improvements.

Broadband Connectivity — Billions in Federal Investments: Historic investments to expand high-speed internet connectivity across Alaska, including the state's $1.017 billion BEAD allocation, with more than $629 million supporting 29 initial broadband deployment projects.

Highways, Roads, and Bridges — More Than $230 Million in Recent Awards: Including $183.4 million in additional federal highway funding and more than $50 million for transportation resilience projects, alongside ongoing federal highway formula funding and major road and bridge improvements statewide.

Alaska Marine Highway System — More Than $900 Million: Federal investments supporting ferry operations, vessel replacement, terminal improvements, and the modernization of Alaska's essential marine transportation network.

Military and Coast Guard Infrastructure — Billions in Investments: Including the $7 billion multi-year JBER recapitalization effort, more than $1.2 billion in Interior Alaska military construction, more than $1.4 billion in Coast Guard construction and infrastructure across Alaska since 2015, and major investments in Arctic defense, missile defense, and icebreaker capabilities.

Rural Energy Infrastructure — More Than $325 Million: Including up to $150 million for the Beluga–Healy Transmission Project, up to $125 million for five rural Alaska clean energy projects, and $50 million announced in October 2026 to strengthen rural energy infrastructure and reduce costs.

Rural Health Care — Approximately $1.4 Billion Over Five Years: Alaska's share of the historic Rural Health Transformation Program, including nearly $249 million awarded this year alone supporting 254 projects to expand access to care, modernize rural health infrastructure, strengthen the health care workforce, and improve health outcomes.

Water, Sanitation, and WRDA Infrastructure — Hundreds of Millions of Dollars: Including more than $182 million in previously announced federal water infrastructure investments and a proposed $240 million Alaska-specific authorization for rural water and sanitation projects, alongside major Army Corps infrastructure initiatives supporting Nome's port, Juneau flood protection, and Western Alaska coastal resilience.

title: Bilirakis Leads Bipartisan, Bicameral Effort to Expand Access to Benefits for Veterans with Rare Muscle Disease
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12) led a bipartisan, bicameral group of lawmakers in urging Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Secretary Doug Collins to recognize Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM) as a presumptive service-connected condition. The designation would help Veterans living with this rare, progressive, and incurable muscle disease access disability benefits without having to individually prove that their military service caused their illness. The effort builds on a letter Bilirakis sent to the VA earlier this year. He is now joined by 53 lawmakers in calling for action to address the significant obstacles Veterans with IBM face when seeking benefits.

“Our Veterans should not have to spend years fighting a devastating disease while also fighting a burdensome bureaucracy to receive the benefits they have earned,” said Congressman Bilirakis. “Veterans living with Inclusion Body Myositis face progressive muscle weakness, declining independence, and tremendous uncertainty for themselves and their families. With this disease reported at substantially higher rates among Veterans, the VA must take these concerns seriously and establish a fairer pathway to benefits. I am proud to lead this bipartisan effort to ensure these Veterans are heard, treated fairly, and given the support they deserve.”

According to data reviewed by The Myositis Association (TMA), IBM affects approximately 189 out of every one million Veterans, compared with 15 out of every one million civilians - more than 12 times the prevalence. Like Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), IBM is a progressive, incurable disease that can cause profound physical limitations. Yet, while the VA recognizes ALS as a presumptive service-connected condition for qualifying Veterans, Veterans diagnosed with IBM must establish service connection through an individualized claims process.

“Thank you to each Member of Congress who signed on to this letter and supported military veterans who live with inclusion body myositis. The Myositis Association proudly stands with you in calling upon the Veterans Benefits Administration at the US Department of Veterans Affairs to approve a presumptive service connection for veterans with IBM,” said Rich DeAugustinis, Chair of TMA board of directors. “TMA is especially grateful for the longtime leadership and empathy of Representative Gus Bilirakis, the lead sponsor, who has brought tremendous visibility to the needs of veterans and care partners living with IBM working with Representatives Mike Thompson, Sarah Elfreth, and Senator Tammy Baldwin. Your continued courage in demanding the very best for those who have served is inspirational!”

“Veterans diagnosed with IBM must navigate a lengthy and burdensome individualized claims process to establish direct service connection ... Yet unlike ALS patients, Veterans with IBM are not afforded a presumptive pathway to benefits, resulting in inconsistent adjudications and inequitable outcomes,” the lawmakers wrote.

The consequences for affected Veterans and their families can be substantial. The Myositis Association reports that a review of VA records found an 82% denial rate for IBM claims. Some Veterans have sought professional assistance and spent more than a decade pursuing appeals before securing recognition that their condition is service-connected. These challenges are compounded by the absence of a dedicated VA disability diagnostic code for IBM, which can complicate documentation and accurate disability ratings. Because the disease’s cause remains unclear, establishing an individual medical link to military service presents an additional obstacle. Recognizing IBM as a presumptive service-connected condition would remove the requirement for qualifying Veterans to individually establish that link, helping reduce administrative burdens and promote more consistent decisions.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine is reviewing the relationship between selected military exposures and eight conditions, including IBM. Findings are expected in summer 2027. While supporting that research, the lawmakers emphasized the immediate needs of Veterans already living with the disease.

“While we look forward to the findings of that review, we respectfully emphasize that Veterans currently suffering from IBM should not be left waiting for recognition and relief,” the lawmakers continued.

Congressman Bilirakis is leading the House effort alongside Representatives Sarah Elfreth (D-MD) and Mike Thompson (D-CA), with Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) leading the effort in the Senate. The House Members who signed the letter are listed below in alphabetical order.

title: Cleaver, Fletcher, Sanders, 111 Colleagues Demand Trump Stop Illegally Blocking Solar for All
text:
(Kansas City, MO) – Today, U.S. Representatives Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO) and Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX) and U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) led 111 of their colleagues to demand that the Trump administration immediately restore the Solar for All program—a landmark initiative to help working-class families afford rooftop solar and community-based solar energy.

In 2022, Democrats in Congress passed the Solar for All program into law to slash utility bills, promote clean energy job training, and invest in American manufacturing. The program will create tens of thousands of good-paying jobs, lower residential electricity bills by at least 20% for more than 900,000 households and save working families more than $8.7 billion in electric costs over the lifetime of the solar panels.

The Trump administration has withheld $7 billion in Solar for All funding since August 2025. This past September, two federal district courts ruled that the administration’s attempts to terminate Solar for All are illegal, and ordered the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to restore funding for the program. Cleaver, Fletcher, and Sanders filed an amicus brief earlier this year supporting the case against the Trump administration.

“Currently, nearly $7 billion that Congress allocated to slash utility bills, create jobs, and strengthen the electric grid is sitting idle in the EPA’s bank account instead of working to benefit American families,” the lawmakers wrote. “As hardworking Americans grapple with skyrocketing energy bills, Solar for All stands to deliver meaningful savings to hundreds of thousands of households.”

“The EPA’s illegal termination of Solar for All has left states, communities, and businesses across the country in limbo. Nevertheless, the program’s grantees stand ready to put Solar for All dollars to work on residential solar projects to slash utility bills and create many thousands of good jobs,” the lawmakers concluded. “The EPA must immediately restore Solar for All and ensure projects nationwide proceed to implementation as Congress intended.”

title: RELEASE: Congressman Cloud Introduces the Ending Patient Runaround Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Michael Cloud (TX-27) introduced the Ending Patient Runaround Act to return transparency and patient rights to our healthcare systems, giving Americans more control over their coverage.

Health insurance was created to protect Americans from financial debt, but Americans are facing opaque billing, restrictions on networks, and unwarranted changes to their coverage after enrollment. Individuals often can’t even reach a representative that speaks English when they call for help. The Ending Patient Runaround Act addresses these issues to protect Americans from hidden costs and surprise bills.

Key provisions of the bill include:

Creating Universal Savings Accounts, incorporating legislation originally introduced by Rep. Diana Harshbarger (R-TN) and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX), allowing Americans to save up to $10,000 a year ($20,000 for married couples)

Requiring insurance companies to have 30 days to approve or deny a treatment request.

Prohibiting insurance companies from cutting coverage for a drug or service after an individual has already enrolled.

Requiring insurers to disclose billing codes, reimbursable amounts, and the full list of covered services and procedures before a person enrolls.

Requiring insurers to reimburse out-of-network providers the same amount as in-network providers for the same procedure.

Renaming catastrophic plans as “Basic Plans,” opening them to purchasers of any age, and allowing them to be sold on the ACA Exchange.

Insurance providers must assign you a single customer service point of contact based in the United States and proficient in English.

Requires insurers to pay back overbilled patients more than they were overcharged.

“Health insurance exists to protect families and make healthcare more affordable, yet, Americans can’t even get English-speaking representatives on the phone,” said Rep. Cloud. “The Ending Patient Runaround Act puts patients first, with transparency even before they sign up.” concluded Rep. Cloud.

Healthcare should work for the people who depend on it, not the insurance companies that profit from it.

title: Courtney Applauds Announcement of First U.S. Submarine Assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West in Western Australia
text:
NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee and Co-Chair of the bipartisan Friends of Australia Caucus, applauded the announcement of USS COLORADO (SSN 788) as the first Virginia-class fast-attack submarine assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) at HMAS Stirling in Western Australia. The USS COLORADO is scheduled to commence its rotation at SRF-West in late 2027.

“Today’s announcement marks yet another milestone achievement for the AUKUS security agreement, which was authorized by an act of Congress in 2023. The USS COLORADO will serve as the inaugural fast-attack submarine rotation at SRF-West and with it will come regional security enhancements for all three AUKUS nations,” Courtney said. “The COLORADO was built by southeastern Connecticut’s shipbuilders and tradesmen at Electric Boat. These highly talented men and women have taken the U.S. commitments to AUKUS and unprecedented demand to grow and recapitalize the U.S. attack and ballistic missile submarine fleet all in stride. It’s their work and expertise that maintains undersea supremacy for us and our allies today and for decades to come.”

“The activation of SRF-West puts Australia one step closer along the Optimal Pathway to Australia operating its own nuclear-powered submarine capability,” Courtney continued. “The combination of U.S. and UK attack submarine rotations and Australian nuclear-powered submarines will transform allied naval posture in the Indo-Pacific. AUKUS Pillars I and II continue full steam ahead with Congress and the Navy in lock step with the UK and Australia.”

STRONG SUPPORT FROM U.S. NAVY LEADERS

On April 22, 2026, in an exchange with Rep. Courtney, U.S. Indo-Pacific Command Commander Admiral Samuel Paparo stated, “In every regard in Pillar I, we're on track. We're making strides in Pillar II among these nontraditional systems here. And to have a rotational base in the Indian Ocean is absolutely essential."

On May 14, 2026, in an exchange with Rep. Courtney, Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle stated, “[I] fully support AUKUS Pillar I, fully support Sam Paparo’s statement, and I look forward to standing up submarine squadron three later this year and making sure that Submarine Rotational Force-West becomes alive and getting the first Virginia-class transfer to Australia next year as we continue to build out where they eventually buy a U.S. submarines.”

SRF-WEST INVESTMENT FROM AUSTRALIA

The Australian government has allocated A$2.2 billion (AUD) for priority projects for SRF-West, as part of an A$8 billion commitment through the next decade at HMAS Stirling. SRF-West operations will include intermediate submarine maintenance for both the U.S. and UK.

MORE RECENT AUKUS NEWS

Last week, the three AUKUS nations successfully tested and operated new autonomous capabilities and announced new payloads for unmanned systems – significant progress towards Pillar II’s first marquee project.

Also last week, the United States and Australia announced the groundbreaking of a new expansion of Bird-Johnson Propeller Company in Mississippi, funded in part with Australia’s $3 billion commitment investment into the U.S. submarine industrial base, of which $2 billion has thus far been delivered.

title: Rep. Goldman Supports Fort Worth’s Massive Manufacturing and Job Creation Victory
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Craig Goldman (R-TX) applauded Carrier’s plans to invest $600 million in a new advanced manufacturing facility in Fort Worth, supporting the city’s manufacturing industry and fueling the local economy.

“The future of American manufacturing is being built right here in Fort Worth. Carrier’s commitment to our city is a testament to our strong workforce, pro-business environment, and thriving economy,” said Congressman Craig Goldman. “This investment will create new opportunities for hardworking Texans while strengthening our state’s position as a national leader in advanced manufacturing. I look forward to seeing Fort Worth continue to thrive as we attract new investments, drive economic growth, and expand opportunities for Texans.”

Background

Carrier, a global leader in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) technology, announced plans to invest more than $600 million in a new advanced manufacturing facility in Fort Worth, Texas. After a competitive nationwide search, Carrier chose Fort Worth to house the largest single-facility investment in company history, underscoring North Texas’ competitive business climate and strength as a national manufacturing hub.

The project is expected to create approximately 1,500 jobs, expand the region’s manufacturing workforce, and strengthen Fort Worth’s position as a major hub for industrial innovation.

title: Crow Introduces Bill to Expand Medicare, Lower Eligibility Age
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO) introduced legislation to expand Medicare and lower the eligibility age to 50 from 65, helping to lower healthcare and prescription drug costs and strengthen the Medicare Savings Program.

As Republicans have cut healthcare to pay for tax breaks for the wealthiest Americans, Crow’s Improving Medicare Coverage Act will help ensure fewer Americans will be forced to choose between paying their bills and seeing a doctor.

Joining Crow in introducing this bill are Representatives Pramila Jayapal (D-WA), Chris Deluzio (D-PA), Debbie Dingell (D-MI), and Pat Ryan (D-NY).

“We live in the richest country in the world. Coloradans shouldn’t have to choose between seeing a doctor and paying for their groceries,” said Congressman Crow. “Under Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans, healthcare has only gotten more expensive. This bill will help to lower costs and expand access by allowing more Americans who want it to get their healthcare through Medicare. This bill will save lives, lower costs, and ensure every American has affordable healthcare.”

This bill is supported by Center for Health and Democracy, Labor Campaign for Single Payer, MoveOn, People’s Action Institute, Physicians for a National Health Program, Public Citizen, SEIU, United Auto Workers.

Crow strongly opposed H.R. 1, Republicans’ One Big Ugly Bill, which cut healthcare coverage for millions of Americans, is bankrupting rural hospitals, and is adding trillions of dollars to the national debt. He is a cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act to deliver comprehensive healthcare to every American with no premiums, no copayments, and no deductibles.

As a veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, Crow has fought for better healthcare for our servicemembers, including expanding dental care to reservists and access to quality healthcare for servicemembers and their families. He’s also worked to improve care for active-duty servicemembers suffering from traumatic brain injuries and improve approaches to trauma care on the battlefield. He’s also worked to ensure our veterans are taken care of. Last November, Crow introduced a package of bills to improve services that veterans and their families rely on and strengthen the benefits they earned through their service.

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: DeLauro: “Trump is cashing in on his Iran War while Americans pay more at the pump”
text:
Today, Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) responded to reports that President Donald Trump’s oil stock holdings have gained millions in value since he launched the Iran War. Over the weekend, President Trump boasted about the profits the U.S. oil and gas industry have reaped while Americans pay painfully high prices at the pump.

“President Trump bragged this weekend about how much money oil and gas corporations are making. What he left out is that his own oil and gas holdings nearly doubled in value since he started his war of choice with Iran: from $12.6 million to $46 million at the end of 2025, to between $22.5 and $81.6 million today.

“While Americans pay more at the pump because of a war President Trump started – a war with no clear strategic goal and no plan to end – giant corporations and their investors, like President Trump, are cashing in.

“The American people will not tolerate a government that manufactures global chaos and then sends them the bill. President Trump is lining his own pockets and those of his billionaire friends at the expense of millions of working families. His gains must be investigated, and we must bring an end to the Iran War to finally bring down the price of oil.”

title: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. Celebrates 100 Years of the Bridge of the Gods in Cascade Locks
text:
CASCADE LOCKS, OR – Today, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), presented the Port of Cascade Locks with a Congressional Record tribute honoring the Bridge of the Gods’ centennial and the generations who have kept the Gorge connected.

“For a century, the Bridge of the Gods has connected people to jobs, families and the extraordinary beauty of the Gorge,” said Congresswoman Dexter. “This anniversary belongs to the generations who built, maintained and cared for this landmark. I’m proud to recognize their work in the Congressional Record and celebrate the Cascade Locks community that keeps this history alive.”

Opened in 1926, the bridge spans the Columbia River between Oregon and Washington. Owned and operated by the Port of Cascade Locks, this steel-truss cantilever structure has become an important transportation link used by residents, visitors, cyclists, and Pacific Crest Trail hikers.

"For a century, the Bridge of the Gods has connected our Gorge communities and supported the people and businesses that call this place home,” said Jeremiah Blue, Executive Director of the Port of Cascade Locks. “We thank Congresswoman Dexter for her service to Cascade Locks and for honoring the bridge's legacy in the Congressional Record. We’re proud to be stewards of this landmark and committed to preserving it for future generations."

The Congressional Record tribute recognizes the bridge’s lasting contributions to the region and celebrates a century of connection, community and preservation.

title: Dexter, Merkley, Wyden, Bonamici, Announce $12.4 Million for Affordable Housing in Portland
text:
Portland, OR – U.S. Representatives Maxine Dexter (OR-03) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), as well as, U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden, today announced that $12,418,414 in federal funds are coming to Portland to help Oregonians continue to access affordable housing. The funds to Home Forward of Portland will ensure there is no lapse in the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program—also known as Section 8—which supports families, the elderly, and Americans with disabilities in accessing affordable housing.

“Safe, abundant, and affordable housing is the bedrock of healthy, thriving communities,” said Dexter. “As housing costs rise, I am so grateful to bring this funding back to Home Forward of Portland to help keep Oregon families housed. I will continue to keep up the fight to deliver the dignified housing every single individual in our state deserves.”

“All Oregonians deserve a safe, affordable place to call home,” said Merkley. “As folks in Portland and across Oregon struggle with rising housing costs, we must do everything we can to help families searching for a decent roof overhead. I’ll keep fighting to support public housing authorities across our state and deliver the necessary federal resources to tackle our housing affordability crisis.”

“Housing is a human right and it’s essential that federal policies move toward that goal with significant investments in Oregon and nationwide,” said Wyden. “This $12 million-plus in federal resources will help Oregonians working to find housing they can afford in Portland. I’ll never stop working to provide similar affordable housing funds for communities across our state in the ongoing battle to support people working to make ends meet.”

“The cost of housing can make or break a family’s budget,” said Bonamici. “Affordable housing programs, such as the Housing Choice Voucher Program, are essential safety nets when the housing market can’t meet the needs of the community. This award will enable the Housing Authority of Portland to continue its essential work to support our most vulnerable households and keep roofs over the heads of countless Portland families.”

The federal funding is being awarded to Home Forward from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) through its HCV Program. These HCV Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) Set-Aside Shortfall funds are provided to Public Housing Agencies (PHAs) to ensure there is no lapse in the HCV Program.

title: Figures backs Alabama disaster declaration after Hurricane Isaias
text:
U.U.S. Representative Shomari Figures, D-Alabama, sent a letter to President Donald Trump supporting Governor Kay Ivey’s request for a major disaster declaration following Hurricane Isaias.

“I am writing in strong support of Alabama Governor Kay Ivey’s October 23, 2026, request for a Major Disaster Declaration due to Hurricane Isaias,” Figures wrote in a letter to the White House on Friday. “Hurricane Isaias was a Category 2 hurricane with damaging winds of 105 miles per hour and extensive rainfall that impacted the Gulf Coast and produced significant flooding, massive power outages, and widespread damage throughout the State of Alabama. As recovery efforts are ongoing, I urgently request that the Administration approve the State of Alabama’s request as quickly as possible.”

Under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, the president can declare a major disaster to make federal assistance available after a catastrophe. A declaration gives federal agencies, including the Federal Emergency Management Agency, broader authority to provide aid to affected areas.

Ivey previously asked Trump for a declaration.

In his letter, Figures stressed that a major disaster declaration could help Alabama recover from the Category 2 storm, which caused at least two deaths in central Alabama.

“While the effects of Hurricane Isaias may continue to impact the state for quite some time, promptly approving this major disaster declaration request will help ensure that the people of Alabama are prepared for the recovery phase ahead,” Figures wrote.

“Alabamians are resilient, and with cooperation at all levels of government, we will rebuild stronger than ever,” Figures added. “I stand ready to provide any support necessary, and I thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.”

As of publication, Trump had not approved a major disaster declaration for Isaias.

title: Fitzpatrick Secures $5 Million for New Edgely Bridge Project in Bristol Township
text:
Funding advances long-term transportation solution to improve public safety, strengthen emergency access, and ease commercial traffic through residential neighborhoods

Bristol Township, PA — Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) announced he has secured $5 million in federal Community Project Funding to advance planning and engineering for a long-term bridge and transportation solution in Bristol Township. The investment will help address the infrastructure and traffic challenges highlighted by the nearly two-year closure of the Randall Avenue Bridge, which strained local roads, disrupted emergency access, and diverted heavy commercial traffic through residential neighborhoods.

The funding will support the evaluation and development of potential infrastructure improvements to provide safer, more reliable transportation connections for residents, businesses, and emergency responders. Potential approaches include a proposed Haines Road Bridge connecting Haines Road across the railway corridor to North Radcliffe Street, as well as potential improvements to the Randall Avenue Bridge. Fitzpatrick has worked closely with Bristol Township leaders to help restore access to the Randall Avenue Bridge, which reopened in January 2026, while continuing to support efforts to identify a lasting solution to the community’s transportation challenges.

“The closure of the Randall Avenue Bridge highlighted just how critical reliable infrastructure is to our residents, businesses, and emergency services. While reopening the bridge was an important accomplishment, our focus has always been on finding a permanent, long-term solution that improves public safety, accommodates commercial traffic, and reduces the impact of heavy vehicles traveling through our residential neighborhoods. Congressman Fitzpatrick has been an invaluable partner throughout this process, from his direct involvement in helping restore access to the Randall Avenue Bridge to securing this significant $5 million federal investment. His continued commitment to Bristol Township is helping us move forward with the planning and engineering necessary to evaluate the proposed Haines Road Bridge and develop a transportation solution that will benefit our community for generations to come. We sincerely appreciate his partnership and continued advocacy on behalf of Bristol Township,” said Randee J. Mazur, Township Manager, Bristol Township.

“Reopening the Randall Avenue Bridge was essential, but it was never the finish line. The closure exposed a larger challenge for Bristol Township: strained local roads, heavy commercial traffic moving through residential neighborhoods, and concerns about reliable access for our first responders. From day one, we worked alongside Township leaders to restore access and pursue a permanent solution. This $5 million investment is an important step in bringing us closer to advancing the planning and engineering for a safer, more reliable crossing that will protect our neighborhoods, support local businesses, and strengthen critical transportation connections for generations to come. My sincere thanks to the entire Township Leadership team, Randee Mazur, and the residents of Bristol Township for their continued partnership—I look forward to carrying this momentum forward as we work to build safer, stronger, better-connected Bristol Township.” said Fitzpatrick.

Delivering For Pennsylvania’s First District

Through the FY2026 Community Project Funding process, Fitzpatrick successfully championed more than $27.5 million for 11 community projects addressing critical local needs across Pennsylvania’s First District, including:

$1.25 Million for United Way’s HELP Center

$4 Million for Bensalem Township’s new Department of Public Safety Fire Station

$1 Million to Revitalize Downtown Quakertown

With this latest round of funding, Fitzpatrick has brought more than $80 million in federal Community Project Funding to PA-01 since FY2022, translating priorities identified by local communities into lasting investments in the people, services, and infrastructure that strengthen the region.

Together, these investments reflect Fitzpatrick’s community-first leadership, empowering local organizations, responding to community needs, and ensuring federal resources translate into meaningful, measurable, and lasting benefits for Bucks and Montgomery counties.

title: Gallagher Introduces Legislation Following Horrific Discovery of 117 Dead Dogs at Northern California Animal Rescue
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following the disturbing discovery of 117 dead dogs buried at a Northern California animal rescue, Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) introduced Dunkin's Law, legislation aimed at strengthening federal protections for companion animals and holding negligent pet-care facilities accountable.

In June, investigators with the Humboldt County Sheriff's Office uncovered mass burial sites at Miranda's Rescue Animal Sanctuary in Fortuna, California. Authorities recovered 117 intact canine remains, along with additional skeletal remains. Preliminary examinations of 70 dogs revealed evidence of gunshot wounds in many of the animals.

The discovery came as part of an ongoing investigation into allegations of animal cruelty and fraud at the facility, which had advertised itself as a no-kill rescue. Investigators have also raised questions about the whereabouts of hundreds of dogs transferred to the organization. No criminal charges have been filed in connection with the investigation.

“What investigators uncovered in Humboldt County is absolutely sickening,” said Congressman Gallagher. “People entrusted these animals to a rescue believing they would be protected, only for authorities to discover more than a hundred dead dogs buried on the property. We need to get to the bottom of what happened, and anyone found responsible for breaking the law must be held accountable. These animals deserve better.”

The tragedy underscores concerns about accountability at facilities entrusted with the care of companion animals. While the investigation in Humboldt County continues, Gallagher's legislation would establish a federal legal remedy when animals are harmed, neglected, or killed in covered commercial facilities.

Dunkin's Law is named in honor of Dunkin, the beloved dog of Madeleine “Maddie” White and Andrew Fedyk, whose heartbreaking loss after leaving him at a boarding facility helped inspire the legislation.

“Dunkin was so much more than a pet to us. He was family, and losing him has been absolutely devastating,” said Maddie and Andrew. “When we trusted someone else to care for him, we never imagined we would have to face this kind of heartbreak. Nothing will ever bring Dunkin back, but knowing that his story could help protect other animals and spare another family from experiencing this pain means everything to us. We are incredibly grateful to Congressman Gallagher for listening to our story and taking action to make sure families have a voice when something like this happens.”

Under current law, companion animals are often treated primarily as property, which can limit the legal remedies available when they are injured or killed. Dunkin's Law would amend the Animal Welfare Act to recognize certain companion animals, including dogs and cats, as sentient beings.

The legislation would establish a federal civil cause of action for owners whose pets suffer harm, neglect, or death while in the custody of covered commercial pet-care businesses, including boarding facilities and grooming operations. Owners could seek economic and noneconomic damages, including veterinary expenses and emotional distress, as well as reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs.

Importantly, the legislation would also establish a path to civil accountability for animal rescues and shelters convicted of unlawfully euthanizing companion animals under applicable state or local law.

“Whether it's a family losing a beloved pet at a boarding facility or the horrifying allegations coming out of Humboldt County, the message is the same: caring for animals comes with a responsibility,” Gallagher continued. “Our pets aren't just property. They're family. When that trust is violated, families deserve a real path to justice.”

Dunkin's Law would apply prospectively and would not determine liability in the ongoing Miranda's Rescue investigation.

title: Gluesenkamp Perez Announces Mobile Office Hours in Lewis County
text:

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Visits Pacific County Hospital to Discuss the Challenges Facing Rural Hospitals
text:
SOUTH BEND, WA — Last week, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez visited and toured Willapa Harbor Hospital, a critical access hospital in Pacific County. The Congresswoman spoke with hospital staff about new imaging suite improvements funded by her community project funding request and about the challenges facing rural healthcare. As a Critical Access Hospital, Willapa Harbor Hospital is more than 15 miles from the nearest hospital with only secondary road connections between facilities.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez secured just over $1 million in community project funding for upgrades to Willapa Harbor Hospital in last year’s appropriations cycle. The hospital is using this funding to modernize their imaging systems with new X-ray, ultrasound and CT equipment. The hospital has already received new ultrasound equipment and has initial approval for a new CT system. They anticipate further upgrades to X-ray and scanning equipment will be approved in the near future. Having this equipment means patients can remain close to home while receiving the care they need. The previous old imaging equipment was past its service life and frequent outages required some patients take life flights to other hospitals.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez meets with hospital staff to discuss the challenges of providing rural healthcare.

“When you live in a rural community, there’s this constant back of mind worry about the what-ifs of healthcare access. Hospitals like Willapa Harbor are getting fewer and further between, and that really is an anxiety for so many people,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “Aging equipment and systems are becoming more and more expensive to repair or replace, and health cuts–like the ones I voted against–aren’t helping our communities get on their feet. I’m proud to be working to bring home funding that will go toward making sure our rural communities have reliable healthcare access.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez is working to improve access to quality, reliable healthcare in Southwest Washington. Earlier this summer, she visited Ocean Beach Health, another Critical Access Hospital in Pacific County, to see federally funded improvements and a new women’s clinic. This Congress she also passed the Rural Veterans’ Improved Access to Benefits Act, aimed at expanding access to disability exams to veterans living in rural areas, and introduced the More Nurses in Rural Schools Act to improve healthcare access for children in rural areas.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez voted against H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law on July 4, 2025. This law eliminated Medicaid eligibility for roughly 17 million Americans–including 31,000 in Southwest Washington. The bill also terminated the temporary expansion of the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, which helped cover healthcare coverage costs for lower-income households. Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez co-led the Bipartisan Premium Tax Credit Extension Act to extend these tax credits for one year and enact pharmacy benefit reforms to bring down the cost of healthcare.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Leads Intelligence Committee Trip to Djibouti
text:
Above: Gottheimer with a service member from New Jersey.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, returned from a congressional delegation (CODEL) to the Republic of Djibouti. There, he met with the U.S. Ambassador, military leaders, and U.S. service members stationed at Camp Lemonnier, including service members from New Jersey. He received briefings on America’s national security priorities in the region, with a focus on combating the threat posed by the Iran-backed Houthi terrorists in Yemen.

“Our service members in Djibouti are on the front lines, keeping terrorists from threatening the American homeland and our allies,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I was proud to meet with the men and women who serve there, including those from New Jersey, and to thank them for their extraordinary sacrifice for our country. The Houthis, backed by Iran, have attacked commercial ships and threatened global trade, and we must keep the pressure on them. America’s presence in this region is essential to fighting terrorists, safeguarding trade routes, and keeping America safe.”

Djibouti is home to Camp Lemonnier, the largest U.S. military base in Africa and the headquarters of Combined Joint Task Force – Horn of Africa (CJTF-HOA), part of U.S. Africa Command. Established in 2002 after the September 11 attacks, CJTF-HOA’s U.S. service members work to build partner nation capacity, promote regional security and stability, dissuade conflict, and protect U.S. interests across East Africa.

Djibouti sits beside the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a chokepoint for a significant share of global trade. With Iran-backed Houthi attacks threatening commercial vessels in the Red Sea, Gottheimer stressed the need to protect freedom of navigation and keep supply chains and prices stable for Jersey Families. He also received briefings on counterterrorism operations across East Africa.

Gottheimer also raised serious concerns about the growing military and economic footprint of the Chinese Communist Party, which operates an overseas military base in Djibouti, and emphasized that the United States must stay engaged and offer a strong alternative to Beijing’s coercion. Gottheimer also received briefings on counterterrorism operations across East Africa.

Below: Gottheimer with the US Ambassador to Djibouti.

title: Declaración del Comisionado Residente ante las redadas de ICE en Puerto Rico
text:
Me solidarizo con la comunidad inmigrante ante las redadas de ICE. Las leyes migratorias pueden y deben ejercerse sin violencia, con compasión y respeto a los derechos humanos.

Desde enero de 2025, he exigido explicaciones a las autoridades federales sobre los operativos de ICE en Puerto Rico, tanto mediante comunicaciones oficiales como en vistas públicas. He apoyado el Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, para limitar operativos en lugares como escuelas e iglesias; denunciado la entrega de datos personales de inmigrantes por el Gobierno de Puerto Rico; y copatrocinado el Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act, para reformar la detención migratoria, el Immigration Enforcement Staff Body Camera Accountability Act, para exigir cámaras corporales a los agentes, y el No Secret Police Act, para exigir que se identifiquen durante los operativos. En junio de 2026, también me opuse a un presupuesto republicano que asignaba $70 mil millones adicionales a ICE y CBP sin suficientes medidas de rendición de cuentas.

A nuestra comunidad inmigrante, les exhorto a conocer sus derechos y consultar la información que hemos compartido en nuestras redes sociales.

title: Jayapal, Raskin, Thompson, Garcia, Clarke, Casar Lead Members in Denouncing Raid on Omar’s Home
text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security and Enforcement, Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Committee, Robert Garcia (CA-42), Ranking Member of the Oversight Committee, Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security Committee, Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus, and Greg Casar (TX-35), Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, are leading 175 Members of Congress in denouncing the politically motivated Department of Homeland Security (DHS) raid on Representative Ilhan Omar’s (MN-05) home in Washington, D.C.

“This weaponization of law enforcement to harass a sitting Member of Congress 22 days before an election is unprecedented and unacceptable,” wrote the Members. “We stand with Congresswoman Omar and condemn the weaponization of law enforcement against her. You have already disgraced the offices you hold, and we demand you to refrain from taking any further actions that could affect the outcome of the upcoming election.”

The probe into Congresswoman Omar reportedly concerns her late father’s filing of immigration paperwork after she fled Somalia’s civil war at age eight. She has been a U.S. citizen since she was 17. Trump officials have continuously and baselessly asserted criminal activity by Omar, and this is not the first instance of retribution by Trump’s administration, which has made a habit of targeting perceived political enemies.

“Your actions are clearly driven by a pre-determined political outcome rather than an objective pursuit of justice,” continued the Members. “Political attacks should play no role in federal law enforcement, but they have here.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN HOUSTON: “THE MASS DEPORTATION MACHINE UNLEASHED BY DONALD TRUMP HAS GOT TO END”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Reps. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) and Christian Menefee (TX-18) in Houston’s Segundo Barrio for a press conference about House Democrats’ commitment to ending ICE’s reign of terror that is brutalizing our immigrant communities and hurting the economy.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s an honor and a privilege to be back in Houston. […] It was a very informative roundtable where we heard about the brutality and the fear that Trump’s violent mass deportation machine has been creating here in Houston, similar to what has gone on all across the country. Taxpayer dollars should be used to make life more affordable for the people here in America, not to brutalize and kill American citizens or violently target and kill law-abiding immigrant communities, as was the case horrifically here in Houston just a few months ago. We believe that immigration enforcement should be fair, just and humane. The Trump administration promised that immigration enforcement was going to target violent felons. That’s not what’s happening. The mass deportation machine unleashed by Donald Trump has been targeting law-abiding immigrant communities like those here in Houston, and it’s got to end.

Everything has become more expensive here in America because of Donald Trump’s failed and toxic policies. The One Big Ugly Bill ripped away Medicaid from the American people. The One Big Ugly Bill enacted the largest cut to nutritional assistance, $186 billion, in American history, and at the same period of time gave ICE a $75 billion slush fund so that these taxpayer dollars could be used to brutalize and kill American citizens and law-abiding immigrant communities. It’s unacceptable, unconscionable and un-American. And as House Democrats, we’re committed to getting the situation turned around. We know we have a broken immigration system. We know it needs to be fixed in a comprehensive and bipartisan way.

I’m thankful for the leadership of Sylvia Garcia in pushing forward with the Dream and Promise Act. That is just the beginning of what needs to happen in terms of [ending] this national nightmare that the people here in Houston and all across America have been experiencing and get to a much better place here in the United States of America, which will certainly include dramatic change as it relates to immigration enforcement and our continued commitment not to give a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine.

title: Türkiye Caucus Co-Chair Statement Celebrating National Day
text:
Washington, DC – Representatives Joe Wilson (R-SC), Steve Cohen (D-TN) and Aumua Amata Coleman Radewagen (R-AS), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Caucus on U.S.-Türkiye Relations and Turkish Americans, issued the following statement:

“Congratulations to the people of Türkiye and Turkish Americans on this 103rd commemoration of the founding of the Republic of Türkiye.

“Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the Turkish Republic in 1923, introducing sweeping social and political reforms that laid the foundation for modern Türkiye. Today, as a critical bridge between Europe and the Middle East, Türkiye plays an indispensable role in maintaining regional balance and addressing complex geopolitical dynamics across Eurasia and the Mediterranean.

“As Co-Chairs of the Congressional Caucus on U.S.-Türkiye Relations and Turkish Americans, we recognize Türkiye’s strategic contributions to transatlantic security and diplomacy. From hosting the 2026 NATO Summit in Ankara to aiding conflict de-escalation, maritime security, and humanitarian efforts across the region, Türkiye continues to serve as a pivotal partner in global peacebuilding.

“This year, as we also celebrate 74 years of Türkiye’s NATO membership, we honor its crucial role on the alliance’s southeastern flank. Holding the second-largest military force in NATO, Türkiye remains central to collective defense, defense technology collaboration, and regional defense integration.

“On the eve of the centennial of the establishment of diplomatic relations between United States and Türkiye that will be celebrated in 2027, we congratulate the Turkish people and Turkish Americans on Republic Day 2026 and look forward to deepening the strategic, economic, and cultural bonds between our two nations.”
