title: Dr. Joyce Sends Letters Requesting Answers Following Multiple Train Derailments in Blair County
text:
October 26, 2026

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman John Joyce sent letters to the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and Norfolk Southern seeking answers after at least four train derailments occurred in Blair County since February of this year. The most recent incident occurred on October 23, 2026, in Altoona, where at least 11 train cars derailed including cars carrying hazardous materials.

Specifically, the letters request answers on the findings of completed investigations, what response protocols were carried out, what federal support is necessary to prevent future derailments, and what steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the community and personnel.

“As the grandson of two railroad workers, rail safety is part of my heritage, and now it’s part of my responsibility in Congress to get to the bottom of these glaring failures,” said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “Our communities deserve answers, and the safety of residents and passengers must never be compromised. This oversight effort is an important step toward holding Norfolk Southern accountable for its lack of response to the increase in derailments and ensuring that Norfolk Southern steps up and meets the highest standards of safety for the community.”

Congressman John Joyce is a cosponsor of the Railway Safety Act of 2026, a bipartisan piece of legislation that would update safety regulations for freight cars and require improved coordination and support for local first responders.

Within the last week, Congressman John Joyce addressed these concerns with the Logan Township United Fire Department Chief Rusty Shoenfelt and 40 fire crew members who serve the area around the Horseshoe Curve.

Read the letter to the FRA here.

Read the letter to Norfolk Southern here.

title: Kaptur Announces $1 Million US DOJ Investment in Lucas County's Smart Reentry Demonstration Initiative
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) announced an award of $1 Million for the Smart Reentry Demonstration Initiative in Lucas County. The Lucas County Criminal Justice Coordinating Council will receive the award through the US Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance and allocate it for the Smart Reentry Demonstration Initiative in Lucas County that helps former inmates reenter the community by addressing the housing instability faced by individuals who are released from state prisons.

“Every individual deserves the opportunity to rebuild their life and return to their community with the support and resources needed to succeed,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “I am proud to support Lucas County’s Smart Reentry Demonstration Initiative, which will address housing instability, expand access to employment, and provide comprehensive case management for individuals returning home from state prisons. By helping participants secure transitional housing and build pathways to long-term stability, this initiative will reduce the rate of repeated offenses and strengthen public safety across Northwest Ohio. I look forward to seeing the lasting impact of this effort as we work to ensure that our returning neighbors have a meaningful opportunity for a successful fresh start.”

“This federal investment through Second Chance Act (SCA) funding strengthens our community’s ability to support returning citizens with the stable housing and coordinated services they need to safely and successfully reintegrate into our community,” said Holly Matthews, Executive Director, Toledo Lucas County Criminal Justice Coordinating Council. “We are grateful for this opportunity to advance a data‑driven model that reduces recidivism, improves public safety, and expands long‑term housing stability in Lucas County.”

“When people commit a crime, and then serve their time, it is in our community's best interest to help them become productive returning citizens,” said Judge Tim Kuhlman, Chair, Criminal Justice Coordinating Council. “This grant will help us help them to be successful.”

This initiative aims to place approximately 30 individuals annually in transitional housing through a master-leasing model while providing comprehensive case management services. Participants will be selected based on assessments indicating a moderate to high risk of reoffending. Through individualized, comprehensive support including workforce development and employment placement services, participants will be assisted in securing and maintaining stable employment with the goal of transitioning to permanent housing within 6–9 months.

Supporting individuals who are released from prison and easing their transition into our communities has remained a strong priority for Congresswoman Kaptur. In 2024, she secured a total of $678,332 to the Lucas County Criminal Justice Coordinating Council to support individuals with substance use disorders through treatment alternatives to incarceration, expanded access to resources, and community partnerships that reduce recidivism and promote recovery.

title: Kean Spotlights $3 Million for Passaic River Regional Flooding Mitigation Project
text:
(October 26, 2026) BERKELEY HEIGHTS, NJ– Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) recently visited Passaic River Park in Berkeley Heights to see firsthand where the $3 million he secured in a House funding bill will be utilized.

The funding will be used for the clearing of major obstructions from Passaic River tributaries and the shoring up of stream banks in the river towns of Berkeley Heights, Long Hill, New Providence, Summit, and Chatham Borough, which will decrease area flooding and soil erosion, while improving and protecting soils and water quality. This project will focus on strategic, environmentally responsible de-snagging and debris removal in the most-clogged stretches of the tributaries leading into the Passaic River, representing an important flood mitigation strategy to improve the hydraulic capacity of the river tributaries and reduce flood risk.

“Residents in the area know the detrimental impacts of the Passaic River Basin flooding,” said Congressman Kean. “Local municipalities have experienced repeated and severe flooding events in recent years, resulting in significant public safety hazards, damage to public infrastructure, damage to property, roadway closures, emergency response impacts, and disruption to residents and businesses. I am pleased to secure this federal funding to ensure that families in these communities are safe and can continue to live in their homes.”

“Flooding doesn’t stop at municipal borders, and neither can our efforts to address it,” said Berkeley Heights Township Mayor Angie Devanney. “This $3 million federal investment in the Passaic River Regional Flood Mitigation Project is an important step toward protecting homes, businesses and families in Berkeley Heights and our neighboring communities. I’m grateful to Congressman Kean for championing this funding and proud of the regional partnership we’ve built to turn shared concerns into meaningful action.”

“Long Hill, New Providence, Berkeley Heights, and Summit have joined together to work with Congressman Kean to secure $3 million so we can address the flooding issues around the Passaic River Basin,” said New Providence Mayor Al Morgan. “The residents of our town know firsthand how devastating the flooding can be. We are grateful to the Congressman for his aid in getting our communities this critical funding.”

“We are very grateful to Congressman Kean for his work to secure these funds for Summit and our neighboring towns who are also battling this ongoing issue,” said Summit Mayor Elizabeth Fagan.“With severe storms becoming more frequent, residents all throughout this area continue to lose land and suffer significant damage to their properties. This funding represents a critical investment in protecting our residents, mitigating future flood damage, and building more resilient communities for the long term.”

Since taking office, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. has secured more than $14.5 million for water infrastructure in New Jersey’s Seventh Congressional District through the Community Project Funding process.

In July, Congressman Kean announced that 18 Community Project Funding requests made by his office totaling $17,765,906, are included in key House funding bills for the upcoming fiscal year. Learn more HERE.

title: Kean Visits New Somerville YMCA Preschool Classrooms, Longtime Project Comes to Fruition
text:

title: Kiggans, Goodlander Work to Strengthen Oversight of Navy’s Shipyard Modernization Program
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) and Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) introduced the Shipyard Modernization Sustainment Act, a bill that strengthens Congressional oversight over the Navy’s Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) by requiring a series of independent reviews of its cost, progress, and timeline.

These reviews would be conducted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) led by the Comptroller General and include annual reviews, congressional briefings, and a final report by 2031.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “If the United States wants to remain the world’s most powerful naval fighting force, we must ensure our shipyards have the necessary infrastructure to keep our fleet mission-ready. SIOP is a vital initiative that will modernize our shipyards and equip our workers with the tools and resources they need to maintain the fleet for years to come. However, Congress has a responsibility to keep the program on schedule and to hold it accountable for the efficient use of taxpayer dollars. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Goodlander in this effort to strengthen GAO oversight, preserve the integrity of the program, and support our national security.”

SIOP aims to modernize dry docks and upgrade equipment at the nation’s four public shipyards—Norfolk Naval Shipyard, Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility, and Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility—to better support the maintenance needs of the Navy’s increasingly advanced fleet. GAO has previously found SIOP could take over 50 years to complete and cost over $200 billion.

As a Navy veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, Congresswoman Kiggans remains committed to ensuring our servicemembers have the resources, equipment, and infrastructure necessary to maintain operational readiness and carry out their missions safely and effectively.

Read the bill here.

Background:

In June 2026, Rep. Kiggans announced the House Armed Services Committee’s markup of the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act. Read her press release here.

In October 2025, the Congresswoman introduced the Pay Our Public Shipyard Workers Act which would protect the paychecks of the civilian and military workforce during government shutdowns. Read her press release here.

title: E’Anna Palacios Won Brings CNMI Pride to South Korea
text:
We’re incredibly proud to see E’Anna Palacios Won, a daughter of the Northern Marianas, making her mark on the international stage. Raised in Saipan, E’Anna was selected fifth overall in the 2026 draft to play professional basketball with South Korea’s Cheongju KB Stars. She previously represented the CNMI at the 2022 FIBA Women’s Micronesian Cup, helping bring home a silver medal along with her sister, Ky’Sonna. E’Anna’s journey reflects the determination, Chamorro pride, and strong family and community values that define our islands. Her success reminds our young people, especially our young girls, that no matter how small our islands may be, our dreams have no limits. Congratulations, E’Anna! The CNMI is cheering you on!

title: Krishnamoorthi Leads 256 Cosponsors in Bipartisan Resolution Designating July as Indian American Heritage Month
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) today introduced a bipartisan resolution with 256 cosponsors honoring generations of Indian American contributions to the United States and supporting the designation of July as Indian American Heritage Month. More than 5.2 million Indian Americans call the United States home. The resolution celebrates their contributions across science and medicine, technology and business, public service and the military, education and philanthropy, arts and culture, and athletics.

“Indian Americans have helped shape this country for generations, from breakthroughs that have saved lives and businesses that have created jobs to lifetimes of service in our military and public office,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “I’m proud to lead 256 of my colleagues in designating July as Indian American Heritage Month to honor that legacy and celebrate the many ways Indian Americans continue to enrich our country.”

The designation of July as Indian American Heritage Month commemorates the signing of the Luce-Celler Act by President Harry S. Truman on July 2, 1946, which made people of Indian descent eligible for naturalization as American citizens. The resolution also honors the Indian American community’s religious and cultural diversity and the generations of Indian Americans who have contributed to the nation’s cultural, economic, and civic life.

title: Congressman David Kustoff Helps Secure a $20.3 Million Federal Grant for West Tennessee Railroad
text:
MEMPHIS – Congressman David Kustoff (R-TN-08) today applauded the announcement that the West Tennessee Railroad has been awarded $20.3 million for the West Tennessee Rail Modernization Project through the Federal Railroad Administration’s (FRA) Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program.

“Reliable freight rail service is essential to the economic success of West Tennessee,” said Congressman Kustoff. “Our farmers and manufacturers depend on these rail connections to get their products to market, and this investment will make freight service safer and more efficient. I am pleased to have helped secure this significant funding for our region, and I thank Federal Railroad Administrator David Fink for recognizing the importance of this project to West Tennessee.”

The project will replace rail and ties, rehabilitate 25 at-grade crossings, replace turnouts, and extend an interchange siding. These improvements are expected to eliminate existing speed restrictions and reduce the risk of derailments. The project will improve rail infrastructure serving Obion, Weakley, Gibson, Madison, Chester, and McNairy counties, including lines through Milan, Jackson, Humboldt, Dyer, Trenton, and Henderson.

This funding builds on West Tennessee Railroad’s 2024 CRISI grant, which Congressman Kustoff also supported. The earlier project is now entering the construction phase. Together, these investments will help strengthen the long-term viability of freight rail service throughout West Tennessee.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill To Ban Three Dangerous Preservatives Found On America’s Grocery Shelves
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Oct. 26, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace introduced the Eliminating Dangerous Preservatives Act to crack down on harmful preservatives in our food supply and put the health of American families first.

The bill would ban butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT), and tertiary butylhydroquinone (TBHQ) from food intended for human consumption by classifying food with these ingredients as adulterated under federal law. Manufacturers would have two years to reformulate their products before the ban takes effect.

“You should not need a chemistry degree to figure out what is in your food,” said Congresswoman Mace. “Butylated hydroxyanisole. Butylated hydroxytoluene. Tertiary butylhydroquinone. Most Americans cannot even pronounce these preservatives, yet they are in the food on our grocery store shelves. Enough is enough. It is time to put American health ahead of corporate convenience. We are cleaning up America’s food supply and holding manufacturers accountable.”

The Eliminating Dangerous Preservatives Act would:

Ban three preservatives from the food supply: Classify any food intended for human consumption containing BHA, BHT, or TBHQ as adulterated under federal law, banning their sale, manufacturing, and distribution.

Give manufacturers two years to reformulate: Establish a two-year implementation freeze before new restrictions take effect.

Require federal regulations: Direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue regulations implementing the new requirements.

Demand accountability: Require a report to Congress three years after implementation detailing food manufacturers’ reformulation efforts, and recommendations for additional legislative or regulatory action.

The Eliminating Dangerous Preservatives Act is part of Rep. Mace’s broader Make America Healthy Again agenda, alongside the REAL Sugar Act, the PEPTIDES for Veterans Act, the SOUND Pesticide Research Act, the Pesticide Transparency on Federal Land Act, the Pesticide Harm Accountability Act, and the Pesticide Data Transparency Act.

title: McClellan Introduces Bill to Maintain Program to Support New and Underserved Farmers
text:
Washington D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) and Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) introduced H.R. 10914, the Farming Opportunities Training and Outreach Grant Program Reauthorization Act, to better support new, underserved and veteran farmers with improved access to training, education and technical assistance. Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) introduced the Senate companion legislation in June of 2026.

Rural farmers and ranchers have served as the backbone of the American economy since its founding, and agriculture remains the number one private industry in Virginia. Yet new farmers, especially those from underserved communities, can face immense challenges getting their business off the ground. The Farming Opportunities Training and Outreach (FOTO) Program improves success rates for these farmers.

“As the number one private industry in Virginia, agriculture keeps our local economies and communities running. Yet Virginia’s farms, more than 90 percent of which are individual or family-owned, often struggle to turn a profit. Extreme weather, rising costs and unstable markets make the difference between a good year and a bad year,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “The FOTO Program exists to lend a helping hand to underserved farmers just starting out to navigate these challenges. My bill will extend this invaluable resource to further ensure that our farmers have every tool at their disposal to thrive.”

This bill reauthorizes the FOTO Program from 2027 to 2031. It would also ensure the program can better serve the growing number of Hispanic, American Indian, Black and Asian farmers by allowing grants to support interpretation and translation services as part of outreach and technical assistance. The bill would additionally strengthen accountability by requiring USDA to collect and report data on FOTO grant awards and recipients, including demographic information, to help ensure the program is effectively reaching the producers it is intended to serve.

“Agriculture offers an array of rewarding careers and opportunities for people from every background, but we must do more to make sure everyone who wants to get into the industry has a fair shot. That’s why I’m proud to join Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan on the Farming Opportunities Training and Outreach Grant Program Reauthorization Act. This important legislation reauthorizes and strengthens the FOTO program and helps ensure that the USDA reaches the producers it is intended to serve,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown, Vice Ranking Member House Committee on Agriculture.

“Farmers and ranchers are the backbone of Oregon’s economy, but too many people who want to start a farm have trouble getting the training and resources they need to succeed,” said Congresswoman Salinas. “In the Willamette Valley, we know how important it is to support the next generation of farmers and ensure that everyone has a fair shot at success. This bill will help new farmers access the training, mentorship, and technical assistance they need, while breaking down language barriers that too often stand in their way. I’m proud to help lead this effort to strengthen our agricultural communities and support the next generation of farmers.”

This bill is endorsed by the National Family Farm Coalition, Rural Coalition, Virginia Coalition of Immigrant Rights (VACIR) and Virginia State University.

“The FOTO Program helps dismantle some of the barriers that face beginning farmers and ranchers and historically underserved producers,” said Tiffany Bellfield El-Amin, President of the National Family Farm Coalition, and Executive Director of Kentucky Black Farmers Association. “We thank Congresswoman McClellan for introducing this crucial bill, which would reauthorize and improve the program so that more farmers and ranchers from diverse backgrounds can enter the industry, which is especially important as each year sees dwindling numbers of small and mid-size farms. While this bill makes needed improvements to FOTO, Congress must also fully fund it annually so that it can realize its full potential.”

“Rural Coalition and our diverse community-based members commend Congresswoman McClellan for introducing the ‘Farming Opportunities Training and Outreach Grant Program Reauthorization Act of 2026.’ The long-standing FOTO programs have played a critical role in improving access to USDA programs by ensuring farmers and ranchers have the direct support they need to navigate federal agriculture programs and to run successful farm operations,” said Lorette Picciano, Executive Director of Rural Coalition. “At a time when producers face growing challenges, the qualified technical assistance FOTO programs provide to farmers and ranchers from all backgrounds and operation types remains an important investment in the future of agriculture in this nation.”

“VACIR is proud to support Virginia’s agricultural community that ensures our families have healthy food on the table. Without Virginia farmers, many of whom are increasingly from diverse backgrounds, there is simply no food,” said Monica Sarmiento, Executive Director of VACIR. “We applaud Congresswoman McClellan’s leadership on this important matter. We hope that Congress acts quickly to reauthorize this vital food security program that supports rural communities with funding, jobs and opportunities.”

Virginia State University wrote the following:

“As an 1890 land-grant institution, VSU works directly with farmers and communities across Virginia. Through our Extension and Small Farm Outreach programs, we see firsthand the value of trusted technical assistance, strong partnerships, and helping producers successfully access USDA programs and resources.

“Agriculture is Virginia’s largest private sector industry and farmers are the backbone of that success,” said Virginia Secretary of Agriculture and Forestry Katie Frazier. “We need to support the next generation of farmers and provide them with the resources and programs to navigate the early years of building a farm business to build a foundation for their long-term resilience and stability. We thank Congresswoman McClellan for supporting these programs and her commitment to Virginia’s farmers.”

title: Amid Heightened Cybersecurity Risks, McCormick Introduces Bill to Protect Critical Infrastructure
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) introduced the Common-Sense Cloud Security Act to strengthen America’s cloud cybersecurity by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop updated standards to protect sensitive data, prevent cyberattacks, and secure critical infrastructure.

The legislation would strengthen protections against unauthorized access and malicious activity while establishing a voluntary certification program to help cloud service providers meet modern cybersecurity standards.

“In 2026, nearly everything we do relies on the cloud. From our financial information and medical records to our national security and critical infrastructure, our most sensitive information is stored and accessed through cloud-based systems,” said Congressman McCormick. “Our adversaries, including China, are constantly looking for ways to exploit vulnerabilities, launch cyberattacks, and steal sensitive American information. We cannot afford to leave Americans exposed to these threats. The Common-Sense Cloud Security Act strengthens our cyber defenses, protects sensitive information, and keeps America one step ahead of our adversaries.”

The Common-Sense Cloud Security Act would require NIST to work with federal cybersecurity officials, cloud service providers, critical infrastructure operators, and academic experts to address vulnerabilities in cloud environments, including through the use of artificial intelligence to detect suspicious activity.

The Common-Sense Cloud Security Act would:

Require NIST to report to Congress on federal implementation, private-sector adoption challenges, and recommendations to improve cloud cybersecurity.

Update FedRAMP to align with new cloud security standards and strengthen cybersecurity disclosures for federal cloud providers.

Establish a voluntary, tiered Cloud Security Certification Program using independent, accredited testing laboratories.

Encourage artificial intelligence to detect unusual or suspicious activity in cloud environments.

Develop a methodology to assess the scope of cloud security breaches and how far a compromise could spread.

Strengthen cyberattack prevention, detection, and mitigation, including vetting, authorization, and continuous monitoring of third-party software integrations.

Direct NIST to update cloud cybersecurity standards, including stronger digital identity protections linking account credentials to specific devices.

title: McGovern Continues Demanding Answers from DHS on El Salvador TPS
text:
WASHINGTON—Congressman James P. McGovern (D-MA), Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee and Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, is leading 43 colleagues in again demanding answers from the Department of Homeland Security over the future of Temporary Protected Status for approximately 200,000 Salvadorans living in the United States.

In July, McGovern led 80 Members of Congress in urging DHS to extend TPS for El Salvador, warning that terminating the designation would harm the American economy and potentially return people to a country facing severe human rights and economic crises. The letter detailed deteriorating human rights conditions in El Salvador, including mass arbitrary detentions, forced disappearances, deaths in custody, and reports that people deported to the country have been incarcerated upon arrival without judicial review or due process. More than three months after the lawmakers first wrote to DHS, approximately 200,000 Salvadoran TPS holders and their families remain in limbo.

“The Department of Homeland Security has had months to answer our straightforward questions. Salvadoran TPS holders should not have to live their lives wondering every day whether the government is going to rip the rug out from under them,” said McGovern.

In their follow-up letter sent on October 22, the lawmakers note that the administration failed to respond to their July letter urging an extension of TPS for Salvadorans—even as the deadline to extend the designation has come and gone.

“On July 9th, 2026, we sent the attached letter to your office urging you to extend the Temporary Protected Status designation for El Salvador. As of October 22, 2026, we have still not received a response,” the lawmakers wrote. “Since we sent that letter, the initial expiration date of the designation has passed. The Department of Homeland Security has provided no further information as to whether the TPS designation for El Salvador will be cancelled or extended. As a result, over 200,000 Salvadorans are currently living in limbo.”

Salvadoran TPS holders have lived and worked lawfully in the United States for decades. Nine out of ten participate in the U.S. workforce, contributing billions of dollars to the economy and paying approximately $1.5 billion in federal, state, and local taxes each year. More than 150,000 U.S.-citizen children have a Salvadoran TPS-holder parent in the American workforce.

“Keeping hundreds of thousands of people in this kind of legal limbo is cruel and wrong,” McGovern added. “They deserve to know whether they can keep working, supporting their families, and living in the communities they have called home for decades. Silence is not an acceptable answer.”

The full text of the October 22 follow-up letter is available here.

The July 9 letter, signed by 80 Members of Congress, is available here.

###

McGovern is a leading voice on U.S. relations with El Salvador in Congress. Earlier this year, heled 27 Members of Congress in demanding information about Salvadorans deported by the United States and held incommunicado in El Salvador’s notorious CECOT prison, citing serious concerns about due process, enforced disappearance, and documented abuses in Salvadoran detention facilities. Leading human rights organizations have documented mass arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearances, deaths in custody, and serious due process violations under the Bukele government, some of which may constitute crimes against humanity..

McGovern has also organized multiple congressional hearings into Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele’s suspension of civil liberties and rule of law which has been used to target journalists, human rights defenders, trade unionists, and political opponents.

title: Congressman Christian D. Menefee to Host Virtual Discussion with Rep. Joe Morelle on Election Security and Protecting Voting Rights
text:
HOUSTON, TX — With Election Day quickly approaching, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) and Congressman Joe Morelle (NY-25), the top Democrat on the House Administration Committee, are sitting down for a virtual Q&A discussion amongst one another on Tuesday, October 27th at 6:30 PM CT/ 7:30 PM ET to address concerns about voter registration, federal involvement in elections, and voter intimidation, as well as the steps Democrats are taking to protect every eligible American’s right to vote.

With Election Day just days away, the goal of this virtual discussion is to reassure constituents about the security of our elections, explain their rights, and provide practical guidance on how to ensure their votes are counted.

The discussion will also include a live question-and-answer session, giving viewers the opportunity to submit questions directly to the members of Congress.

To learn more and tune into the discussion, visit menefee.house.gov/electionsecurity.

title: Speaker Johnson Joins Fox News Sunday
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, Speaker Johnson joined Shannon Bream on Fox News Sunday to discuss House Republicans’ record of results in the 119th Congress and the clear contrast between Republican and Democrat candidates across the country.

“Every voter has to ask themselves a simple question. Which candidate is best for me and my family, my children, my aging parents?” Speaker Johnson said. “In every one of these cases, the Republican is offering commonsense solutions and a steady hand at the wheel. And the Democrats are becoming increasingly crazy.”

Watch the full interview here.

On House Republicans’ record of delivering for the American people:

We effectively made a contract with America in 2024, and we have done everything that we said we were going to do. Secured the border tight. We gave the largest tax cut in U.S. history. We made the largest spending cut in U.S. history as well, $1.6 trillion to try to get the government to work more efficiently and effectively. We cut massive Biden-era regulations. We had a million jobs added in the private sector alone in the last 19 months. It goes on and on and on. Every voter has to ask themselves a simple question. Which candidate is best for me and my family, my children, my aging parents?

In every one of these cases, the Republican is offering commonsense solutions and a steady hand at the wheel. And the Democrats increasingly are going crazy. There's an insurgent Marxist left that has taken over that party. Conservative Leaders

“Under Speaker Johnson’s leadership, House Republicans have delivered a series of major Second Amendment and outdoor-heritage victories. They restored the gun rights of veterans, zeroed out the $200 NFA tax in the One Big Beautiful Bill—opening the door to dismantling large parts of the nearly 100-year-old National Firearms Act—voted to block the use of Merchant Category Codes that would have created a backdoor registry of firearm purchases, voted to protect the use of traditional ammunition for hunters and sportsmen, and voted to return the management of wildlife resources to the states. The NRA is proud to stand with Speaker Johnson and House Republicans as they continue to deliver historic victories for law-abiding gun owners across our country.” — John Commerford, Executive Director, National Rifle Association’s Institute of Legislative Action

“Speaker Johnson knows that the foundation of a strong government is the protection of innocent human life. As Speaker of the House, he has been a fearless and consistent advocate for life. From defending the Hyde Amendment to supporting legislation that protects unborn children and helps their mothers, the Speaker has made the protection of human life an integral part of his work in Congress. For that, we are very grateful!” — Carol Tobias, President, National Right to Life

“Speaker Johnson has done a masterful job leading the House of Representatives despite a historically small majority. National Taxpayers Union is particularly thankful for his efforts to deliver permanent tax relief for workers, families and businesses and his commitment to tackling our debt crisis by rooting out waste in federal programs. Day in and day out, Speaker Johnson has worked for a better fiscal future, as evidenced by his Taxpayers' Friend Award from NTU – the only one given to a Speaker for their voting record in the past 30 years.” — Pete Sepp, President, National Taxpayers Union

“Under Speaker Mike Johnson’s strong leadership, the House has delivered historic border security funding and passed the landmark Laken Riley Act. Speaker Johnson is leading the fight to secure our borders, protect American families, and ensure dangerous criminal illegal aliens are held accountable and deported. His leadership has delivered real results for the American people.” — Mike Hough, Co-President, NumbersUSA

“Senior citizens, particularly financially struggling seniors, know their lifeblood, Social Security and Medicare, will always be protected by Speaker Mike Johnson and his knowledgeable and dedicated staff. On behalf of more than 13 million grateful seniors, the 60 Plus Association salutes the Speaker for his continued dynamic leadership of House Republicans.” — Jim Martin, Founder & Chairman, 60 Plus Association

“Throughout his tenure as Speaker, Mike Johnson has demonstrated a commitment to advancing policies that encourage entrepreneurship, support job creation, and expand economic opportunity. His leadership has helped keep the needs of America's small businesses and job creators at the forefront of the national policy conversation. We appreciate his continued efforts to champion an environment where entrepreneurs can invest, innovate, grow, and create jobs.” — Alfredo Ortiz, Vice Chairman, Job Creators Network

"Speaker Johnson has helped set an example for 'servant leadership' for every politician in Washington.” — Tom Fitton, President, Judicial Watch

“During his three year tenure, Speaker Johnson has done what seems impossible in today’s political culture: He has been unwaveringly principled, mission-focused, and effective while overseeing the slimmest House majority in modern history. Speaker Johnson got the Working Families Tax Cuts over the finish line, creating a legacy of historic policy wins that impact education, healthcare, and welfare programs, as well as taxes. He achieved these wins while modeling conservatism at its best. We are grateful for his leadership and dedication, and look forward to working with him in the future to create more lasting change for America.” — Carrie Lukas, President, Independent Women’s Forum

“Speaker Mike Johnson has been on the front lines of the ‘culture war’ since entering Congress, defending religious freedom, the sanctity of human life, and biblical values, including traditional marriage.” — Jim Daly, President, Focus on the Family

“Speaker Johnson has been a steady champion for parents and for the local school board members who answer to them. Over the last three years he has kept the House focused on parents' rights and on keeping education decisions close to home, and families across the country are better off for it.” — Bridget Ziegler, Director, School Board Action Program, 1776 Project Foundation

“As longtime friends of Speaker Johnson, it is no surprise to us that he has brought integrity, dignity, and honor to the office. His impeccable character, steady manner, crisp clarity as a communicator, and deft leadership have been a source of encouragement to our nation these last three years. In a time when principled leadership is in short supply, Speaker Johnson’s steadfast commitment to our great God and our great country is an admirable and consequential model for others with a similar charge. We are grateful for his leadership and his friendship and pray that God will continue to grant him wisdom, strength, and courage as he continues carry the enormous weight of this responsibility on behalf the American people.”— Douglas Napier, Executive Chairman & CEO; & Greg Scott, Executive Vice President, 1792 Exchange

“Speaker Johnson has shown real leadership by refusing to give in to the panic about AI and keeping the focus on the open, permissionless innovation that keeps America in the lead. That same mindset shows up on energy, where he led the House in passing bipartisan reforms to unlock American energy. Abundant energy and free innovation go hand in hand and it's clear the Speaker understands both.” — Taylor Barkley, Director of Federal Government Affairs, Abundance Institute

"The Speakership of Mike Johnson is historic for a number of reasons but two are especially notable. Never in the History of the United States has the House of Representatives elected as Speaker a member who didn’t seek it. Never in the History of the United States has the House of Representatives been so narrowly divided between our two great political parties. Yet, Mike Johnson has managed to navigate the circumstances and this Congress has had enormous success. Historians will recall the Johnson Speakership as one of the most accomplished in our nation's history.” — Bob McEwen, U.S. House of Representatives Former Member, Ohio

“Every generation has to defend freedom against evil. The only question is who is standing on the wall. For three years it has been Mike Johnson, and he has not flinched. He took the gavel in the middle of chaos, with one of the slimmest majorities in modern history, and stood strong for core American principles. Only a man armed with the kind of steadfast faith that our Speaker has can accomplish what he has accomplished.” — Matt Faraci, CEO, CongressStrong Action

“Congratulations to Speaker Johnson on three years of leadership. Under his gavel, Congress has been a great partner to American consumers, from passing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which locked in some of the biggest tax cuts working families have seen, to shielding Americans from the worst of the radical left’s agenda. Speaker Johnson is a true statesman and one of the most steadfast allies we’ve had. We look forward to continuing to work with him and his team in the years ahead.” — Sal Nuzzo, Executive Director, Consumers Defense

“Since his election to be Speaker of the House on October 25, 2023, Speaker Mike Johnson has tirelessly led the House of Representatives to help U.S. taxpayers by passing impactful tax cuts for families and small businesses and significant legislation to eliminate waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement in the federal government. CCAGW congratulates and thanks Speaker Johnson for his unparalleled leadership and extraordinary commitment to protecting taxpayers and promoting a more efficient and less wasteful government.” — Tom Schatz, President, Council for Citizens Against Government Waste

“Speaker Johnson eloquently spelled out his guiding principles years ago in his '7 Core Principles of Conservatism’ - which every American should read - and since becoming Speaker has managed to make progress on them in a landscape defined by gridlock and pessimism. He took on arguably the most difficult job in Washington under challenging circumstances and in an even more challenging environment, including a historically narrow majority and countless factors outside his control. Since then, he has gamely led the House and achieved policy victories that will save taxpayers thousands, began the process of badly needed entitlement reform, expanded educational opportunities for children, and more. I am proud to stand with Speaker Johnson and am grateful he humbly took on the thankless task of leading the People’s House three years ago.”— Akash Chougule, President, The Foundation for Research on Equal Opportunity

“The ERLC is grateful for Speaker Johnson’s tremendous leadership in service to our nation over the past three years. As Speaker of the House, he has not abandoned his faith but boldly proclaimed the truth about issues important to Southern Baptists like the sanctity of human life, the necessity of free religious exercise, and God’s good design for marriage, gender, and the family. He has acted with humility, charity, and grace in challenging political times. We continue to pray that the Lord gives him wisdom and courage as he serves in this role.” — Dr. Evan Lenow, President, Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention

“Under the leadership of Speaker Johnson, the House of Representatives has fought tirelessly to secure our borders, keep our communities safe, and restore integrity to our immigration system. The House has passed vital legislation, from the Laken Riley Act strengthening mandatory detention of criminal aliens and cracking down on crime, to two reconciliation packages making landmark investments in border security and immigration enforcement funding, to the SAVE America Act ensuring that only American citizens have a say in American elections. FAIR applauds Speaker Johnson for his deep commitment to reform that puts the interests of American citizens first and looks forward to building on that momentum to permanently put an end to asylum fraud, parole abuse, and mass catch-and-release policies so that no future presidential administration can ever again repeat those same failed policies.” — Joe Chatham, Director of Government Relations, Federation for American Immigration Reform

“Speaker Johnson has been a consistent ally of worker freedom. He understands that a paycheck belongs to the worker, not the union boss. Congratulations to the Speaker on three years of steady, principled leadership.” — Aaron Withe, CEO, Freedom Foundation

“Congratulations to Speaker Johnson on three years leading the House. He has served with dignity, steadiness, and deep respect for the institution, holding together the narrowest of majorities to deliver real results, including rolling back the costly green energy subsidies that drove up Americans’ energy bills. When he took the gavel, I said he was the right man at the right time for one of the toughest jobs in Washington. He has proven that to be true.” — Tom Pyle, President, Institute for Energy Research

“From one Speaker to another, I want to congratulate Speaker Johnson on his third anniversary as Speaker of the US House of Representatives. Against all odds, against daunting challenges, and against the relentless unfair and downright ridiculous criticisms of the left and the comms team known as the national corporate media, Speaker Johnson has delivered for the American People. And most importantly, he as stood in the gap as a beacon of hope, freedom, and liberty, always reminding us that America’s better days lie ahead of it for those that want to join him in protecting, preserving, and advancing the American Dream.” — Former Missouri House Speaker Tim Jones, Founder, Leadership for America

“Speaker Johnson has proven himself to be a tested, steadfast, and faithful leader. The House Republican Conference is more unified, more spiritually grounded, and stronger because of his leadership. Liberty Counsel Action is proud to call Speaker Johnson a friend.” — Mat Staver, Founder & Chairman, Liberty Counsel Action

“We applaud Speaker Johnson’s commitment to mothers and babies across the country, his strong bold pro-life witness, and his passion for protecting every life. Defunding Big Abortion back in 2025 was a critical achievement that would not have been possible without his incredible leadership. We are grateful for his continued dedication to defending life and in advancing policies that support moms, babies, and their families through pregnancy and beyond.” — Hayden Sledge, March for Life Action

His support for legislation to safeguard sensitive supply chains and restrict American investment in China’s military modernization has helped translate concern about China's predatory actions into concrete action. That sustained focus is essential to protecting America’s security and economic leadership.” — Leland Miller, Commissioner, U.S.-China Economic & Security Review Commission

“Throughout his three-year tenure, Speaker Mike Johnson has been a tremendous leader and ally in pressing for limited and responsible government, policies that promote economic growth and prosperity, and a national security policy that puts the American people first but also recognizes the importance of supporting strong allies like Israel.

His relentless and principled leadership was decisive in securing passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill/Working Families Tax Cut Act. "We are deeply appreciative of Speaker Johnson's principled leadership and the partnership we have enjoyed with his talented and accessible team. We look forward to ongoing collaboration with Speaker Johnson and his team throughout the remainder of this legislative term and in the years ahead.” — Star Parker, Founder, Center for Urban Renewal and Education

"The Association of Christian Schools is grateful for Speaker Johnson's three years of service as Speaker of the House. He has proven himself a champion of Christ, working for the good of all Americans. We are especially grateful for his work to advance school choice in the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which will open up educational opportunities for millions of children. His commitment to religious liberty is a hallmark of his leadership which is significantly noteworthy and appreciated. Thank you, Speaker Johnson.” — P. George Tryfiaties, Vice President for Public Policy & Legal Affairs, Association of Christian Schools International

“In his three years at the helm, Speaker Johnson has shown the world that he leads to accomplish what is right, not what is easy. He has stood with America and Israel when such was not always politically expedient. CUFI’s more than 10 million members will always appreciate his courage, leadership and steadfast support.” — Pastor John Hagee, Founder & Chairman, Citizens United for Israel Action Fund

“Speaker Mike Johnson has been a stalwart champion of protecting religious liberty, combating antisemitism, and expanding educational freedom. Agudath Israel of America particularly appreciates the Speaker’s leadership in advancing the historic Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, which will help expand educational opportunities for millions of families across the country, regardless of the type of school their children attend. We are also deeply grateful for the Speaker’s open-door policy and the accessibility of his office, which has consistently welcomed our input, listened to the concerns of the Orthodox Jewish community, and worked with us on issues that matter most to the families we represent.” — Rabbi AD Motzen, National Director of Government Affairs; & Rabbi Yossie Charner, Director of Congressional Affairs, Agudath Israel of America

“Three years in, Speaker Johnson has governed with a steadiness and respect for first principles that's increasingly rare in Washington. “Thank you Speaker Johnson most importantly for your steadfast commitment to your Lord & Savior and the example you give. Thank you for all you've done to advance conservative principles from tax reform to school choice and promoting American exceptionalism. You've held the coalition together and advanced conservative policies that help every American keep more of their hard earned money, educate their kids and further the American dream.” — Chris Burger, Founder & CEO, Rotunda Public Affairs

“With a razor-thin majority, Speaker Johnson has achieved nothing short of a miraculous results for the American people. As chief architect of the American family tax cuts in the one big beautiful bill he never forgot about following through on promises made to the taxpayers. The record of the GOP majority deserves affirmation by the voters.” — Gary Marx, President, Madison Strategies

"Parents Defending Education Action thanks Speaker of The House, Mike Johnson for his 3 years of service in Congress. Speaker Johnson has been a champion for American children and families. We are proud to continue in our collaborative efforts with Congress and the Speaker to continue to bring about the Golden Age of America.” — Dr. Terry Stoops, Director of Government Affairs, Parents Defending Education Action

"Heartland Impact congratulates Speaker Mike Johnson on three years of leadership and commend the Republican majority in Congress for advancing lower taxes, American energy production, and relief from federal overreach. Building on the One Big Beautiful Bill’s expansion of access to American energy resources, we look forward to working with the next Congress to streamline permitting, expand reliable power generation, and deliver more affordable, more reliable energy for American families and businesses.” — Cameron Sholty, Executive Director, Heartland Impact

Industry Leaders

As Speaker Johnson marks three years leading the House, we applaud his leadership and the entire House Republican leadership team for delivering wins that will benefit Americans for generations to come.” — Mike Sommers, President & CEO, American Petroleum Institute

The American Sugar Cane League appreciates the Speaker's leadership and continued engagement on issues affecting our growers, processors, and the rural communities that depend on a strong domestic sugar industry. We look forward to building on that work in the years ahead.”— Jamison Cruce, Vice President of Government Relations, American Sugar Cane League

We appreciate Speaker Johnson’s leadership in advancing these efforts and look forward to continuing our work together to strengthen American enterprise, promote economic growth, and reinforce the vital role of the LBM industry in our nation’s economy.” — Jonathan Paine, President & CEO, National Lumber & Building Material Dealers Association

"NAB congratulates Mike Johnson on his three-year anniversary as Speaker of the House. We appreciate his deep understanding of the vital role local broadcasters play in our communities, and his leadership in supporting policies that enable our trusted local journalism and lifeline services.” — Curtis LeGeyt, President & CEO, National Association of Broadcasters

“With Speaker Johnson marking his third anniversary as Speaker of the House, we recognize the importance of policies that help our members grow and create jobs. Estate tax relief, making the 20 percent small business deduction permanent, immediate expensing, and allowing 529 accounts to cover career and technical education are important wins for our members. We appreciate the Speaker's focus on promoting careers in the skilled trades. Developing the next generation of skilled workers is essential to the future of the petroleum equipment industry and the communities we serve. PEI thanks Speaker Johnson for supporting the businesses and workers who keep America’s petroleum equipment industry strong.” — Jason Blake, President, Petroleum Equipment Institute

“For three years, Speaker Johnson has brought impactful leadership to Congress, and SEMA and the small businesses and manufacturers of the automotive aftermarket industry have benefited greatly. The legislation that Speaker Johnson has shepherded during his tenure have been necessary boosts to our nation's economy and personal liberties; from stopping electric vehicle mandates that would have forced Americans into cars and trucks that do not meet their needs, to backing small businesses and innovators through permanent, reduced tax rates, to increased deductions for small businesses. Our automotive aftermarket industry is stronger and better positioned for future growth and success because of our champions in Congress like Speaker Johnson.” — Karen Bailey-Chapman, Senior Vice President of Public and Government Affairs, Specialty Equipment Market Association

“As Speaker Johnson marks three years leading the House of Representatives, the National Association of Manufacturers recognizes his leadership in helping secure passage of H.R.1, the most pro-manufacturing tax law in a generation. By making critical pro-growth tax provisions permanent, this landmark legislation has provided America’s manufacturers with the certainty they need to invest, create jobs, raise wages and strengthen communities across America. We appreciate Speaker Johnson’s work to advance policies that strengthen manufacturing competitiveness and look forward to building on this progress.” — National Association of Manufacturers

“From repealing unworkable EV mandates to enacting landmark tax reform that will make it easier for job creators to plan and invest, Speaker Johnson has delivered significant wins for America’s truckers. On behalf of the 8.4 million hardworking men and women who keep our supply chain moving, we want to thank the Speaker for his leadership and service.” — American Trucking Association

“The tax and reconciliation package led by Speaker Johnson and House Republicans provides businesses and workers with greater certainty to plan, invest and grow. We appreciate the caucus’ work to deliver that certainty, and look forward to continued leadership on permitting reform to support investment in America’s infrastructure and economy.”— Association of American Railroads

“The National Cotton Council commends Speaker Mike Johnson for his strong leadership and unwavering commitment to American agriculture. So far during his tenure, Congress has delivered critical economic assistance to producers and secured historic improvements to the farm safety net through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. We look forward to continuing to work with Speaker Johnson to expand opportunities for U.S. cotton.” — National Cotton Council

“We appreciate Speaker Johnson’s leadership that has put American workers and American manufacturing at the center of the agenda. The Working Families Tax Cuts advanced those priorities through critical provisions, including no tax on overtime and expensing for manufacturing equipment, helping our workers keep more of what they earn, and steelmakers invest in America’s future.” — Steel Manufacturers Association

“We first met Speaker Mike Johnson while he was serving in the state legislature and since that time he has consistently advocated for and supported efforts to create a reasonable regulatory environment that allows banks, their customers, and their communities to reach their potential. Just as important as his support for helpful legislation, has been his opposition to measures that would create unnecessary roadblocks to economic growth. As the first person representing Louisiana to hold the position of Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, we thank Speaker Johnson for his leadership and commend him for his accomplishments.” — Louisiana Bankers Association

title: THOMPSON LEADS BIPARTISAN EFFORT TO EXPAND VA BENEFITS FOR VETERANS WITH SERVICE-CONNECTED DISEASES
text:
Santa Rosa, CA – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), Representatives Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), and Sarah Elfreth (D-MD) and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) led a bipartisan effort urging the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to recognize Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM) as a presumptive service-connected condition, helping veterans with the debilitating disease access the benefits they have earned through their service.

IBM is a progressive, incurable neuromuscular disease that causes muscle weakness, loss of mobility, difficulty swallowing, and other serious complications. Despite its significant clinical and pathological similarities to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), which the VA already recognizes as a presumptive service-connected condition, veterans diagnosed with IBM must navigate a lengthy and burdensome process to establish that their disease is connected to military service.

“As a combat veteran, I know how important it is that veterans who served our country receive the care and benefits they have earned,” said Thompson. “Inclusion Body Myositis is a progressive, incurable disease that can rob veterans of their mobility and independence. They should not have to fight a lengthy claims process while living with this devastating disease.”

Thompson’s effort has been supported by the advocacy of The Myositis Association and Jane and Ross Liscum, whose work has helped raise awareness of the challenges veterans with IBM face and the need for greater recognition of the disease. Their continued support has helped bring attention to this issue and build support for action to assist affected veterans.

Ross Liscum, a U.S. Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Vietnam in 1969-70 and was exposed to Agent Orange, described his experience living with IBM and the importance of recognizing the disease.

“I never imagined that after serving my country, I would have to fight another battle just to have my disease recognized,” said Ross Liscum, USMC Veteran, Santa Rosa, CA. “Recognition of IBM as a presumptive service-connected condition would mean that veterans and their families would no longer have to fight this battle alone.”

“As the wife of a Combat Vietnam USMC Veteran living with Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM), I have watched this devastating, progressive disease gradually rob my husband of his strength, independence, and quality of life. Here in Sonoma County, we are one family living with the consequences of this disease, but veterans and their families across America are facing these same heartbreaking struggles. I am deeply grateful to Congressman Mike Thompson for his leadership,” said Jane Liscum, Proud Wife & Caregiver of USMC Vietnam Combat Veteran, Santa Rosa, CA. “These veterans have already served and sacrificed for our country. They deserve to have their voices heard, their illnesses taken seriously, and their claims fairly evaluated. Our veterans should not have to fight their own government for recognition while fighting a disease that is taking away their independence and dignity. Congressman Thompson's compassion, commitment, and leadership give our family, and so many others, something invaluable: hope.”

“Thank you to each Member of Congress who signed on to this letter and supported military veterans who live with inclusion body myositis. TMA proudly stands with you in calling upon the Veterans Benefits Administration at the US Department of Veterans Affairs to approve a presumptive service connection for veterans with IBM,” said Rich DeAugustinis, Chair, The Myositis Association (TMA) board of directors. “The Myositis Association is especially grateful for the leadership and empathy of the four letter sponsors, who have brought tremendous visibility to the needs of veterans and care partners living with IBM. Special thanks to Representatives Gus Bilirakis, Mike Thompson, and Sarah Elfreth; and to Senator Tammy Baldwin. Your continued courage in demanding the very best for those who have served is inspirational!”

“Veterans living with IBM should not be left waiting for recognition and relief,” continued Thompson. “I’m grateful to The Myositis Association and the Liscums for their persistence on behalf of these veterans. We must keep working to make sure those who sacrificed for our country receive the support they earned.”

In their letter to VA Secretary Doug Collins, the lawmakers urge the Department to use its existing regulatory authority to add IBM as a presumptive service-connected condition. This change would help veterans access earned benefits without having to individually establish a direct connection between their diagnosis and military service.

Joining Thompson in the letter were Representatives James Baird (IN-04), Aaron Bean (FL-04), Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Sanford Bishop (GA-02), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), André Carson (IN-07), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Donald Davis (NC-01), Jake Ellzey (TX-06), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Cleo Fields (LA-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), French Hill (AR-02), Jeff Hurd (CO-03), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Henry Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Michael Lawler (NY-17), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13), Lucy McBath (GA-06), James McGovern (MA-02), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), Doris Matsui (CA-07), Sarah McBride (DE-00), Carol Miller (WV-01), Ralph Norman (SC-05), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), August Pfluger (TX-11), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Emily Randall (WA-06), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Rich McCormick (GA-07), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Maria Elvira Salazar (FL-27), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Thomas Suozzi (NY-03), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Derrick Van Orden (WI-03), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

Read the full text of Thompson’s letter HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Collins,

We respectfully write to request your consideration of amending Title 38 § 3.318 to include Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM) as a presumptive service-connected condition under VA regulation. Currently, Veterans diagnosed with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) after active duty receive presumptive service connection due to the disease’s severity, progression, and association with military service. However, IBM – a progressive, incurable neuromuscular disease with significant molecular, clinical, and pathological similarities to ALS – remains excluded. As a result, Veterans diagnosed with IBM must navigate a lengthy and burdensome individualized claims process to establish direct service connection, despite growing evidence linking environmental exposures during military service to both ALS and IBM. Experts, including Dr. Thomas Lloyd of Baylor University (formerly of Johns Hopkins University) and Dr. Todd Cohen of the University of North Carolina, have highlighted the overlap between these conditions and the heightened exposure risks faced by military populations. According to a review by Dr. Julie Tomaska, a former member of the VA National Research Advisory Council, the prevalence of IBM among Veterans is approximately 189 per million, compared to 15 per million in the civilian population. The review also found that Veterans with IBM experience significantly higher mortality rates and often develop the disease 10 to 15 years earlier than the civilian population. Like ALS, IBM causes irreversible muscle weakness, loss of mobility and fine motor function, difficulty swallowing, and eventually respiratory failure. There is currently no cure or effective treatment. Yet unlike ALS patients, Veterans with IBM are not afforded a presumptive pathway to benefits, resulting in inconsistent adjudications and inequitable outcomes.

According to a July 2025 VA Freedom of Information Act response, 6,771 Veterans nationwide are currently receiving care for IBM through the VA healthcare system. The same response reflects a 221% increase in diagnosed cases since 2010, underscoring the growing impact of this debilitating disease and the need for further research into potential service-related and environmental causes. This issue also aligns with broader congressional efforts to better understand neurological diseases associated with toxic exposures, including work being done through the Healthy Brains Act and a current National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine review examining links between military-related exposures and neurodegenerative conditions, including IBM. While we look forward to the findings of that review, we respectfully emphasize that Veterans currently suffering from IBM should not be left waiting for recognition and relief. Given the relatively limited but clearly identifiable affected population, we believe this matter may be appropriately addressed through the Department’s existing regulatory authority.

Thank you for your continued commitment to our nation’s Veterans and for your consideration of this important request.

Sincerely,

title: ICYMI: Rep. Min Demands Answers from ICE Following Oversight Visit to Irvine Facility
text:
Irvine, CA — Last week, Representative Dave Min (CA-47), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, attempted to conduct an oversight visit at a reported U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) office in Irvine, California. Rep. Min was joined by Irvine Councilmember Melinda Liu.

The visit followed repeated attempts by Rep. Min's office to arrange an inspection of the facility amid concerns about reports that ICE has used commercial office spaces elsewhere to temporarily detain individuals, potentially in violation of local zoning ordinances. Despite multiple requests, ICE repeatedly declined to facilitate a visit, and Rep. Min was not granted entry on Thursday.

Federal appropriations law prohibits the use of funds to prevent members of Congress from entering Department of Homeland Security facilities, including ICE facilities, for oversight purposes.

Read more below.

Orange County Register

Government officials attempt visit to reported ICE office in Irvine

Victoria Le

Congressman Dave Min and local officials attempted a Thursday morning visit to office space in Irvine that reports have said has been leased for Immigration and Customs Enforcement purposes. Irvine Councilmember Melinda Liu and her chief of staff and members of Min’s office joined the congressman in the visit.

After knocking on the door, Min was met at intervals by three employees, the third of whom said he was not in a position to admit Min and attempted to schedule a visit for another time.

“There have been reports from other office buildings ICE has leased that they have used those illegally, against local zoning ordinances, to temporarily detain people and that they have refurbished some of the offices into temporary holding cells,” Min said. “And that’s the first thing I want to check out.”

Min said his office has asked several times via email to tour the office but was repeatedly told “ICE will not be facilitating a visit at this time.”

“We’ve been in touch with ICE here and our staff has had a series of communications indicating that we’d like to come by, that I’d like to stop by,” Min said. “Today was mentioned as a specific date.”

“We’re going to wait to hear back and see if ICE connects with us.,” Min said of next steps. “We’ll keep following up. We’ll go back to the drawing board.”

title: Nunn Cuts Ribbon on $1 Million CDL Training Pad at Indian Hills Community College
text:
“A four-year degree isn’t the only path to a good-paying job, and we’re making sure more Iowans can build successful careers right here at home,” said Rep. “Indian Hills continues to be a tremendous asset to Ottumwa and Southeast Iowa. Investments like this help create more opportunities for young Iowans right here in our community,” said Ottumwa Mayor Ben Foote. “It’s these opportunities to build the foundation for future growth in Ottumwa.”

title: Congresswoman Schrier’s Bill to Strengthen American Manufacturing Signed Into Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) announced that her Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act was signed into law. The bipartisan legislation will assess and strengthen domestic manufacturing of critical infrastructure goods to bolster manufacturing in rural communities.

“I am proud to announce that my Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act was signed into law,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “This new law will ultimately create jobs and boost local and rural economies. We need a clear understanding of what products our country absolutely needs to manufacture and what products our country is best equipped to manufacture, and this law will inform us about the role American manufacturing will play in the years ahead. I look forward to continuing this bipartisan work to strengthen our local economies and support rural communities.”

BACKGROUND: The Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act directs the Secretary of Commerce to study which high-demand critical infrastructure products are currently imported, assess the costs of domestic production, and evaluate the feasibility of manufacturing these goods in rural communities and industrial parks.

Critical infrastructure sectors include national security, the economy, public health, and safety. The findings must be reported to Congress within 18 months of enactment.

title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Schrier Hikes Portion of Enchantments with Local Leaders, Urges Trump Administration Again to Address Worsening Conditions
text:
LEAVENWORTH, WA – On Friday, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Chelan County leaders, environmental advocates, and a former U.S. Forest Service employee on a hike in the Enchantments Wilderness Area. During their visit, Congresswoman Schrier and local leaders collected litter on the trail, seeing firsthand the deteriorating conditions in the area that have threatened the environment, visitor safety, conservation efforts, and local economies.

View photos and b-roll from the hike HERE.

Following her visit, Congresswoman Schrier sent a letter further urging the Trump Administration to restore adequate Forest Service staffing levels, improve trail conditions, and implement a day-use reservation system to address overcrowding and preserve this incredible wilderness area.

“Given that permanent staffing at the Wenatchee River Ranger District is still at critically low levels, it remains impossible to properly carry out basic duties of parking and trail enforcement, waste management, public safety, and forest health management, let alone the planning and implementation of a brand-new day-use management system,” Congresswoman Schrier writes. “Restoring permanent staffing positions to carry out this vital work remains a necessary first step to properly addressing issues at The Enchantments.”

The letter continues, “I strongly urge the Forest Service to identify and take short-term measures with strong community consultation to increase public safety and help relieve the local ecosystem of the wilderness before the start of the 2027 field season.”

Read the full letter HERE.

BACKGROUND: The Trump Administration’s Forest Service cuts forced the Wenatchee River Ranger District, which staffs the Enchantments, down to just one employee from 11 in 2025. Insufficient staffing has led to diminished capacity to serve visitors, inadequate land management, and overflowing toilets that threaten Icicle Creek: Leavenworth’s drinking water source.

Congresswoman Schrier has urged the Trump Administration to remedy these deteriorating conditions and pressed the administration to address poor Forest Service trail conditions and insufficient staffing in the Enchantments.

Congresswoman Schrier held a roundtable discussion in July with local leaders, emergency responders, outdoor enthusiasts, and volunteers to discuss the impacts of the Trump Administration’s cuts to the USFS on the Enchantments Wilderness Area.

title: Rep. Sewell Calls on President Trump to Approve Major Disaster Declaration Following Hurricane Isaias
text:
Washington D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) joined fellow members of the Alabama Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to President Trump supporting Governor Ivey’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for certain Alabama counties to unlock additional federal resources to aid in recovery from Hurricane Isaias.

“For the past two weeks, Alabamians have joined together to assist their neighbors with supplies and donations,” said Rep. Sewell. “Our emergency managers, first responders, and volunteers are doing all they can with the resources available, but the widespread damage created by Hurricane Isaias cannot be reasonably managed without additional federal support.”

“I agree with Governor Ivey that a Major Disaster Declaration is essential to provide the federal assistance necessary to support our hardest hit communities,” continued Sewell. “I am calling on the president to approve this request as soon as possible. The people of Alabama are resilient, and together we will rebuild our communities stronger than ever.”

The Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (Stafford Act), 42 U.S.C. §§ 5121-5207 § 401 states in part that: "All requests for a declaration by the president that a major disaster exists shall be made by the governor of the affected state." Once the PDA is complete and the state, tribal nation, or territorial government determines that the damage exceeds their resources, the governor or tribal chief executive may submit a declaration request to the president through their FEMA regional office.

The president can declare a major disaster for any natural event, including any hurricane, tornado, storm, high water, wind-driven water, tidal wave, tsunami, earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, mudslide, snowstorm, or drought, or, regardless of cause, fire, flood, or explosion, that the president determines has caused damage of such severity that it is beyond the combined capabilities of state and local governments to respond. A Major Disaster Declaration provides a wide range of federal assistance programs for individuals and public infrastructure, including funds for both emergency and permanent work.

Governor Kay Ivey submitted the request for a Major Disaster Declaration for the State of Alabama as a result of Hurricane Isaias Friday evening. The governor specifically requested individual assistance for Conecuh, Escambia, and Monroe Counties and the Poarch Band of Creek Indians; public assistance, including direct federal assistance, for Baldwin, Barbour, Butler, Choctaw, Clarke, Coffee, Conecuh, Covington, Crenshaw, Dale, Dallas, Escambia, Geneva, Henry, Houston, Lowndes, Marengo, Monroe, Perry, Pike, Sumter, Washington, and Wilcox Counties; and hazard mitigation statewide.

title: Rep. Garcia, Leader Jeffries, and Rep. Menefee Join Houston Workers to Highlight How ICE's Reign of Terror is Worsening the Affordability Crisis

title: Thompson, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Support Small Breweries and Local Farmers, Strengthen Local Supply Chains
text:
U.S. Representative Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) joined colleagues to introduce the bipartisan Brews to Barns Act, legislation that would establish a credit against the excise tax on beer for brewers that donate spent grain for local agricultural use. Rep. Thompson was joined by Reps. Mike Kelly (R-Pa.), Brad Schneider (D-Ill.), Jeff Hurd (R-Colo.), John Larson (D-Conn.), Josh Riley (D-N.Y.), and Marilyn Strickland (D-Wash.).

“Pennsylvania’s farmers, ranchers, and brewers already know that good ingredients shouldn’t go to waste,” Rep. Thompson said. “Across the Commonwealth, brewers continue to create partnerships with local farmers and ranchers to put their spent grain to use in agricultural production. The Brews to Barns Act will provide key incentives to build upon that relationship, helping lower input costs for producers while supporting local small businesses.”

“At their cores, local breweries and farms are small businesses who play integral roles in our communities. The Brews to Barns Act incentivizes a collaborative effort between small breweries and local farmers to strengthen local supply chains. It's a win-win for everyone,” said Rep. Kelly, Co-Chair of the House Small Brewers Caucus.

“Everyone in America—from working families to Main Street businesses—is feeling the bite of rising costs,” Rep. Schneider said. “Among those hit hardest are craft beer brewers and local farmers, which is why I am glad to join my colleagues in this bipartisan effort to help lower costs and prevent waste.”

“Small breweries have a long history of supporting their communities, and their relationships with local farmers are an important part of that. By donating spent grain for agricultural use, brewers help turn a byproduct of the brewing process into a valuable resource for farmers," said Bart Watson, President & CEO, Brewers Association. "The Brews to Barns Act recognizes the value of these longstanding partnerships and helps ensure they can continue to thrive. We appreciate Reps. Kelly and Schneider's leadership in supporting the connections between America's brewers and farmers.”

Read the full bill text here.
