title: Deluzio, Jayapal, Dingell, Ryan Introduce Bill to Lower Medicare Eligibility Age
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-12), and Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18) introduced the Improving Medicare Coverage Act, legislation that would lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50 from 65 and make major coverage improvements.

“Especially after Trump’s healthcare cuts, expanding Medicare to Americans age 50 and up will save lives and get so many Americans the healthcare they need,” said Congressman Deluzio. “I am proud to support Rep. Jayapal’s Improving Medicare Coverage Act—this is an important steppingstone on the way to bigger healthcare reform where every American has good and decent healthcare.”

“Lowering the Medicare eligibility age will be life-saving for the millions of Americans who are waiting an additional 15 years to be able to afford to see a doctor,” said Congresswoman Jayapal. “Expanding Medicare is not only popular, it is also morally the right thing to do. Millions leave the workforce before 65, and with Trump’s cuts to healthcare, many are now left without any options as they wait, sometimes years, for Medicare enrollment. Expanding this program is a commonsense step towards ensuring that all Americans have the care they deserve.”

“For millions of Americans who cannot afford to go to the doctor, it is too late to receive preventive care by the time they reach age 65,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “The U.S. is the only industrialized nation that does not guarantee access to health care for all its citizens, and this needs to change now. I am proud to introduce this legislation to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50, improve the Medicare Savings Program, and make lifesaving drugs more affordable.”

“While Trump and Republicans cut your healthcare and raise your costs, we’re fighting back and putting your care first. But we’re not just reversing the harm – we’re building something better in its place, where millions more Americans will be able to access and afford the care they deserve right when they need it,” said Congressman Ryan. “This legislation expands healthcare coverage to millions of Americans, takes decisive action to lower costs, and makes sure that everyone who needs it has access to quality healthcare, and won’t have to wait to get the cancer screenings, preventative care, and prescriptions they need. This is a commonsense bill, and I look forward to passing it through the Democratically-controlled House next year.”

Adults in late middle age who don’t have health insurance are more likely to die or experience a preventable decline in their overall health. The risks for several chronic conditions and cancers naturally increase at age 50. The median ages for many cancer diagnoses fall below 65 years of age: for instance, 61 is the average age for a breast cancer diagnosis. Lowering the Medicare healthcare eligibility age would improve the chances of more people getting early diagnoses and surviving treatable diseases.

As of 2024, adults aged 55-64 made up 11.5 percent of the entire uninsured population in the U.S. The cuts to healthcare in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act are anticipated to kick 15 million Americans off their healthcare coverage, including more than 12,500 people who count on Medicaid in Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District. Around 22 million Americans are paying more than $1,000 more for their healthcare than they were before the Affordable Care Act tax credits expired. To take on these cuts and the increased costs to plan holders, lowering the Medicare eligibility age is an important step towards ensuring all Americans have health coverage. The legislation would also substantially reduce racial and ethnic health disparities in insurance coverage and healthcare.

In addition to lowering costs for older adults and improving patient outcomes, it is estimated that lowering the Medicare age could reduce costs for employers by up to 43 percent.

Specifically, the Improving Medicare Coverage Act would:

Lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50;

Establish a Medicare Cost Assistance Program to replace the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), and the Qualifying Individual (QI) programs with one program covering specified Part A premiums and Part B premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance for individuals with incomes up to 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL).

Enhance prescription drug affordability by:

Expanding access to assistance with out-of-pocket costs under Medicare Part D for low-income seniors and individuals with disabilities;

Combining the existing Extra Help and Low-Income Subsidy programs into one program;

Raising the eligibility from 135% FPL to 200% FPL;

Removing the asset test;

Ensuring that any individual making under 400% FPL who is not eligible for the Medicare Savings Program maintains the same eligibility for marketplace premium tax credits.

The Improving Medicare Coverage Act is cosponsored by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Everton Blair (GA-13), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), Salud O. Carbajal (CA-24), Greg Casar (TX-35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Steve Cohen (TN-09), J. title: Leger Fernández Advances $4.5 Million for Eastern New Mexico Projects, Building on $458 Million Already Secured for the Region
text:
Five projects supporting clean water, health care, and public safety in Clovis, Hagerman, Hobbs, Texico, and Roswell pass House Appropriations Committee.

SANTA FE, NM — Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) announced that $4,516,436 in federal funding for five critical projects in Eastern New Mexico has passed the House Appropriations Committee as part of the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations process.

The funding would help expand mental health care for children in Clovis, improve drinking water infrastructure in Hagerman and Texico, strengthen public safety in Hobbs, and renovate a community health clinic in Roswell.

The investments build on more than $458 million in federal funding Leger Fernández has already secured for Eastern New Mexico since taking office, supporting water infrastructure, health care, public safety, broadband expansion, and other critical community needs.

The two projects advancing through the House Appropriations Committee are:

$1.5 million for Horizon Behavioral Health Center in Clovis to help build a juvenile crisis stabilization and treatment facility serving Eastern New Mexico.

$746,868 for Hagerman to connect an unused high-yield well to the town’s water system and improve access to clean, reliable water.

$772,700 for the Hobbs Police Department to support de-escalation training and body-worn cameras.

$746,868 for Texico to replace aging waterlines, reduce leaks, and improve water pressure and reliability.

$750,000 for La Casa de Buena Salud to renovate its Roswell South Clinic, which provides primary care, behavioral health, and telehealth services.

“Mayors in my district often talk about how their smaller communities are sometimes forgotten - I’ll always remember them. Our rural communities are essential to who we are as a State and I am glad I’m able to support clean water infrastructure for both Hagerman and Texico. La Casa de Buena Salud and the Town of Clovis are showing us how we can build quality health care and juvenile behavioral health centers close to where people live. Finally, when police officers are trained to de-escalate, everyone is safer,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. “I've already brought home $458 million for Eastern New Mexico, and I'm not stopping there. Now, we're one step closer to delivering another $4.5 million to make sure our families have reliable drinking water, our children can get mental health treatment close to home, and our communities have the resources they need to thrive. Rural communities should never be left behind, and I'll keep fighting to bring these investments home.”

Building on $458 Million Delivered for Eastern New Mexico

$452,840,000 for the Eastern New Mexico Rural Water System, a major regional infrastructure project to deliver a reliable water supply to communities across Eastern New Mexico.

$1,200,000 for a waste transfer facility in Portales.

$963,000 to support child trauma survivors in Roswell.

$959,752 for wastewater treatment improvements in Lovington.

$600,000 for health care services in Clovis and Portales.

$500,000 for street improvements in Portales.

$369,750 for senior center improvements in Lovington.

$267,000 for police training in Curry County.

$250,000 for broadband expansion in Curry County.

These investments have helped strengthen essential infrastructure, expand access to health care, improve public safety, and support communities throughout Eastern New Mexico.

The additional $4.5 million for Eastern New Mexico was included in the House Appropriations Committee's Fiscal Year 2027 funding bills. This is a major step for these projects, but before becoming law, the legislation must pass the full House, reach agreement with the Senate, and be signed by the President.

title: Fong Launches Bipartisan Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) announced the formation of the Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus. Rep. Fong is joined in this effort by co-chairs Reps. Ken Calvert (CA-41), George Whitesides (CA-27), and Rep. Gabe Vasquez (NM-2). Reps. Jay Obernolte (CA-23), Julia Brownley (CA-26), and Mike Haridopolos (FL-8) are also joining the caucus.

The purpose of the caucus is to educate Members of Congress, congressional staff, and the public about the importance of our nation's military ranges and test facilities, which play a critical role in advancing research and development and test missions for our military. Technology development plays an important role in ensuring our warfighters have the resources needed for success, and our military ranges and test facilities are foundational to this effort.

"From NAWS China Lake and Edwards Air Force Base to the Mojave Air and Space Port, our community is the heart of America's military research, test, and development enterprise,” said Congressman Vince Fong. “America's military ranges and test facilities are where our nation's warfighters get their edge, and I am proud to represent some of the most critical in the world. This caucus will ensure that Members of Congress understand what is at stake, fight for the resources these facilities need, and protect the missions that keep America ahead of our adversaries. I am grateful to be joined by colleagues on both sides of the aisle who share that commitment."

"The Antelope Valley is home to world-class facilities where we develop, test, and build aircraft to keep our country competitive,” said Congressman George Whitesides. “I'm proud to join Rep. Fong in launching this bipartisan caucus to make sure every member of Congress understands how critical institutions like Plant 42, NASA Armstrong, and Edwards AFB are to the Department of Defense's research, development, and test mission. Keeping America's edge means investing in the ranges, the infrastructure, and the skilled workforce that make that testing possible."

“California’s 23rd District is home to five military installations, including some of our nation’s premier military training, testing, and development facilities,” said Rep. Jay Obernolte. “These bases play a critical role in advancing the technologies and capabilities that support our national defense. The Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus will help ensure Congress understands the importance of these facilities and the role they play in keeping the United States at the forefront of military readiness.”

“As the proud representative of Naval Base Ventura County, I understand firsthand the strategic importance of our military ranges and test facilities to our national security and supporting our nation’s defense readiness,” said Congresswoman Julia Brownley. “To further strengthen these critical national security assets, I have consistently championed legislation to support our Major Range and Test Facility Bases and ensure they are equipped to meet our evolving defense needs. As a member of the Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus, I will continue working to ensure our Armed Forces have access to the resources, cutting-edge technology, and state-of-the-art facilities necessary to carry out their missions.”

“As the proud father of a U.S. Air Force Airman serving in explosive ordnance disposal, I understand firsthand how critical military ranges and test facilities are to preparing our warfighters for success,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “I’m proud to join this bipartisan caucus to strengthen military readiness, advance defense innovation, and ensure our servicemembers have the tools and training they need to keep America safe.”

title: Gallagher Introduces Dunkin’s Law Following Tragic Loss of Family Dog, Horrific Discovery at Northern California Animal Rescue
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) introduced Dunkin’s Law, legislation to strengthen federal protections for companion animals and hold negligent pet-care facilities accountable. The legislation comes amid growing concerns about animal welfare, including the heartbreaking loss of a family dog named Dunkin and the disturbing discovery of 117 dead dogs at a Northern California animal rescue.

The legislation is named in honor of Dunkin, the beloved dog of Madeleine “Maddie” White and Andrew Fedyk, who lost their dog after leaving him in the care of a boarding facility. Their experience,which drew national attention, helped inspire Gallagher's effort to provide families with meaningful legal recourse when animals are harmed or killed by those entrusted with their care.

“For most of us, pets are family,” said Congressman Gallagher. “When someone trusts a boarding facility or another business to care for their pet, they should be able to expect that animal will be safe. What happened to Dunkin is heartbreaking, and no family should have to go through that kind of loss without a meaningful path to justice. This bill is about holding people accountable when that trust is broken.”

“Dunkin was so much more than a pet to us. He was family, and losing him has been absolutely devastating,” said Maddie and Andrew. “When we trusted someone else to care for him, we never imagined we would have to face this kind of heartbreak. Nothing will ever bring Dunkin back, but knowing that his story could help protect other animals and spare another family from experiencing this pain means everything to us. We are incredibly grateful to Congressman Gallagher for listening to our story and taking action to make sure families have a voice when something like this happens.”

The legislation also addresses concerns raised by a separate animal welfare investigation in Northern California.

In June, investigators with the Humboldt County Sheriff's Office uncovered mass burial sites at Miranda's Rescue Animal Sanctuary in Fortuna, California. Authorities recovered 117 intact canine remains, along with additional skeletal remains. Preliminary examinations of 70 dogs revealed evidence of gunshot wounds in many of the animals. The disturbing discovery was detailed in a FOX40 report.

The discovery came during an investigation into allegations of animal cruelty and fraud at the facility, which had advertised itself as a no-kill rescue. Investigators also raised questions about the whereabouts of hundreds of dogs transferred to the organization. At the time of the initial reporting, no criminal charges had been filed in connection with the investigation.

“What investigators uncovered in Humboldt County is absolutely sickening,” Gallagher continued. “People entrusted these animals to a rescue believing they would be protected, only for authorities to discover more than a hundred dead dogs buried on the property. We need to get to the bottom of what happened, and anyone found responsible for breaking the law must be held accountable. Animals deserve better, and so do the families who love them.”

Under current law, companion animals are often treated primarily as property, limiting the legal remedies available to owners when their pets are injured or killed through negligence or misconduct. Dunkin’s Law would amend the Animal Welfare Act to recognize certain companion animals, including dogs and cats, as sentient beings and establish a federal civil cause of action for owners whose animals suffer harm, neglect, or death while in the care of a covered commercial facility.

The legislation would apply to paid pet-care businesses, including boarding kennels and daycare operations, as well as grooming and training facilities.

Importantly, Dunkin’s Law would also establish a path to civil accountability for animal rescues and shelters convicted of unlawfully euthanizing companion animals in violation of applicable state or local law.

“Whether it's a family losing a beloved pet at a boarding facility or the horrifying allegations coming out of Humboldt County, the message is the same: caring for animals comes with a responsibility,” Gallagher said. “A family shouldn't be told their dog was nothing more than damaged property when negligence leads to tragedy. We need laws that recognize the seriousness of that loss and give families a real opportunity to hold those responsible accountable.”

The legislation would establish prospective federal protections and would not determine liability in the Miranda's Rescue investigation.

title: Congressman Gonzalez Secures $1 Million in Federal Funds for City of La Feria
text:
Contact: Alexis Torres

La Feria, Texas—Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), joined by City of La Feria Mayor Olga Maldonado, La Feria City Commissioners, and other local leaders, delivered $1 million in Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Community Project Funding to mitigate stormwater flooding and prevent property damage. Specifically, the investment will be used to install a new storm sewer pump station in the City of La Feria’s La Bonita neighborhood.

“When extreme weather hits flood-prone areas like the Rio Grande Valley, we must ensure that South Texas families and businesses are protected against flooding,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “With this $1 million investment that I successfully passed into law to install a new sewer pump station, we are making a real difference in the daily lives of La Feria residents. I’d like to thank Mayor Maldonado, City Commissioners, and all City staff for partnering with me to strengthen the local economy, public safety and resiliency.”

"The City of La Feria is incredibly grateful to Congressman Vicente Gonzalez and his team for their continued support. This gracious funding for the La Bonita drainage project will positively impact stormwater management and prevent flooding in one of the City's most affected areas,” said Mayor Maldonado.

In March 2025, the Rio Grande Valley experienced devastating storms, with some areas receiving 10 to15 inches of rain in less than 48 hours. Due to low terrain, communities in South Texas are at an elevated risk of dangerous floods that can result in the loss of life and cause damage to homes, small businesses, and other critical infrastructure.

title: Reminder: Trump Promised to Address Water Shortage Eight Months Ago. We’re Still Waiting.
text:
Contact: Alexis Torres

Corpus Christi, Texas — Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) reiterated his call for President Trump to follow through on his promise to address the ongoing water crisis in Corpus Christi. Eight months ago, on February 27, 2026, the President said, during an appearance at the Port of Corpus Christi, that he would approve a request for federal water funding. The Administration has not followed through on that promise and there is still no clear path forward to provide a reliable, long-term water supply for the region that meets the needs of our families, businesses, refineries, and communities.

“Donald Trump and his Administration promised the people of Corpus Christi a solution to our water crisis. Eight months later and we’re still waiting,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “For nearly two years, I’ve sounded the alarm in Washington, and I remain ready to work with local, state, and federal partners to get our region the water it urgently needs. Families are already struggling to make ends meet due to rising costs from tariffs and an illegal war in Iran. We cannot expect these same working families to shoulder the financial burden of building water infrastructure that will sustain our local population and safeguard our national security. The federal government must intervene. Mr. President, you made us a promise; it is long overdue for you to deliver.”

Congressman Gonzalez has consistently advocated for Coastal Bend priorities in Congress, including the need for federal funding to improve regional water security by constructing a desalination plant in Corpus Christi. In addition to testifying before the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure last January, he also took to the House floor on September 15, 2026, to urge Speaker Mike Johnson, President Trump, and his Administration for immediate action.

Watch the Congressman’s full floor speech HERE. The transcript is full is below:

Mister speaker I urge you to make President Trump fulfill his promise to the Corpus Christi community.

Corpus Christi heard him clearly. When the President visited our city, he called our request for federal water funding a “serious money ask.” He then made a commitment to the people of Corpus Christi: “We’re going to take care of it.”

Today, I am asking him to keep that promise. And I urge you to ensure he does. Water is not a partisan issue. It is not a luxury, and it cannot wait for another election or another round of political speeches. Reliable water is essential for our families, our hospitals, our schools, our military installations, our small businesses, and the thousands of workers who keep the Port of Corpus Christi moving.

I was born and raised in Corpus Christi. This is my hometown, and I know its people. They work hard, pay their taxes, and help power the economy of Texas and the United States. They should not have to wonder whether their community will have enough water to survive and grow.

We need the Administration to immediately identify the federal funding available, designate the responsible agency, and provide a firm timetable for delivering the support the President promised.

If congressional action is required, send us the request. I am ready to work with Republicans, Democrats, state leaders, and local officials to get this done! Everyone has a responsibility here. Local and state leaders must do their part, and the federal government must honor its commitment.

Mister Speaker, remind the President that Corpus Christi welcomed him. Its people listened to him, and they took him at his word. Now is the time for action. Release the federal support. Help us secure a dependable, long-term water supply. A promise made in Corpus Christi must be a promise kept. Our families cannot live on promises. They need water—and they need it now!

title: Congressman Rogers, NASA Administrator, Astronaut celebrate space exploration at Morehead State University
text:
Rogers delivers more than $7.5 million for space science program

MOREHEAD, KY (October 27, 2026) – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) welcomed NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and astronaut Stephen Bowen to Morehead State University (MSU), one of NASA’s partners on the Deep Space Network.

Isaacman is the fourth administrator of the nation’s leading aeronautics agency to visit MSU over the last decade. MSU’s Space Science Program has drawn growing national attention for its high-powered space tracking stations and advanced aerospace education and engineering program.

“What an exciting time to hear from our friends at NASA, as the historic Artemis era continues. Morehead State University’s Space Science students have a front-row seat to America’s space race, as they work directly with NASA to track each mission and engineer cube satellites for space flight,” said Congressman Rogers. “Thanks to new partnerships with private companies and institutions like Morehead State University, we are advancing the global race for space exploration faster than ever before.”

“Morehead State is already playing a real role in America’s return to the Moon. Students and faculty helped develop Lunar IceCube, supported Odysseus on the lunar surface, and helped connect the mission to NASA’s Deep Space Network through Morehead’s 21-meter ground station, demonstrating meaningful capabilities for what comes next,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Chairman Rogers has been a strong advocate for this university and America’s space program, and it was great to see firsthand the talent here in eastern Kentucky that will help carry Artemis forward.”

Administrator Isaacman presented Congressman Rogers with a framed Kentucky flag that was aboard the historic Artemis II space flight that circled the moon in April 2026.

As chairman of Commerce, Justice, Science and related agencies, the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee that funds NASA, Rogers works diligently to advance America’s competitive edge over China in the space race, a critical priority for the nation’s military, economic and geopolitical interests.

On Tuesday, Rogers delivered a check for $7.54 million for Morehead State University’s Space Science Center’s payload operations. The fiscal year 2026 Community Project Funding that Congressman Rogers secured was signed into law by President Trump in February.

“It is an honor to host NASA Administrator Isaacman and Astronaut Stephen Bowen on our campus. Our space science program is growing and we continue to contribute to the academic and economic development of the space industry. We are also appreciative of the support that Congressman Hal Rogers has provided to MSU over the years as we build out space science program. The three of them here today speak to the strength we have in the future of space exploration.” Dr. Jay Morgan, President of MSU.

“Federal funding efforts led by Congressman Rogers has transformed space research at Morehead State University. It has helped us build capacity to provide lunar tracking and data services with our satellite ground station - NASA Deep Space Station -17. This latest round of funding will continue to advance our technology in that area and also improve our Mission Operations Center to allow us to provide payload and mission support services to NASA and commercial space programs,” said Dr. Ben Malphrus, MSU Space Science Center Director.

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on Facebook, Instagram and X.

title: Comisionado Residente anuncia más de $45.3 millones en aportaciones federales de FEMA para proyectos en Puerto Rico
text:
CAGUAS, PUERTO RICO — El comisionado residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, anunció nueve asignaciones de fondos federales de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA, por sus siglas en inglés) que suman $45,355,453.06 en aportaciones federales para proyectos de reconstrucción y mitigación de riesgos en Puerto Rico, relacionados con los huracanes María y Fiona.

Las asignaciones notificadas incluyen proyectos de vivienda pública, infraestructura de agua y alcantarillado, instalaciones gubernamentales y educativas, así como obras de control de inundaciones.

Entre los proyectos que recibirán estas aportaciones federales se encuentran:

$528,964.87 para reparar el Complejo Deportivo AOB en el municipio de Caguas, tras los daños ocasionados por el huracán María.

$13,552,603.64 para trabajos permanentes en el residencial público Manuel A. Pérez.

$900,000.01 para reparar o reemplazar componentes exteriores, la fuente, superficies de hormigón, áreas de estacionamiento y otros elementos de las instalaciones de la Administración de los Tribunales.

$3,197,919.86 para medidas de mitigación de riesgos en trabajos permanentes de la Autoridad de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AAA), bajo el proyecto FAASt HMP.

$7,200,000 para trabajos permanentes en el residencial público Sabana Abajo.

$2,790,000 para trabajos permanentes en el residencial público Las Violetas.

$235,808.61 para reparar o reemplazar componentes interiores y exteriores de edificios del Departamento de Educación afectados por el huracán Fiona.

$16,385,256.07 para reparaciones permanentes en el proyecto Troncal Juncos-Gurabo de la AAA, tras el huracán Fiona.

$564,900 para el Proyecto de Control de Inundaciones de Mariana, destinado a trabajos de control de inundaciones y estabilización de la costa.

“Cada asignación representa una oportunidad para adelantar proyectos que Puerto Rico lleva tiempo esperando. Ahora es importante que esos fondos se obliguen y se inviertan, para que los proyectos puedan seguir adelante y no se queden detenidos por falta de recursos”, manifestó el Comisionado Residente.

Las primeras ocho asignaciones corresponden al programa de Asistencia Pública de FEMA, mientras que la asignación para Mariana corresponde al Programa de Subvenciones para la Mitigación de Riesgos (HMGP, por sus siglas en inglés). En el caso del proyecto de Mariana, la aportación federal cubre el 100% del costo total identificado.

En conjunto, los nueve proyectos representan un costo total de $50,332,181.15, de los cuales $45,355,453.06 corresponden a aportaciones federales de FEMA, según las notificaciones recibidas.

FEMA informó que las obligaciones de fondos se realizan directamente al Gobierno de Puerto Rico. Corresponde al Gobierno completar los procesos de revisión y la documentación necesaria para que los recipientes elegibles reciban los fondos mediante los procedimientos de reembolso aplicables.

title: Comisionado Residente presenta proyecto bipartita para reducir el costo de medicamentos a beneficiarios de Medicare
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández presentó al H.R. 10874 – Medicare Low Income Subsidy Equality Act of 2026, un proyecto de ley bipartita que ampliaría la elegibilidad al programa de Subsidio por Bajos Ingresos (LIS, por sus siglas en inglés) de Medicare Parte D a residentes de Puerto Rico y territorios estadounidenses, para ayudar a personas mayores y personas con discapacidades de bajos ingresos a costear sus medicamentos recetados.

En los 50 estados y Washington, D.C., los beneficiarios elegibles de Medicare tienen acceso al programa federal Extra Help, que ofrece asistencia económica para cubrir las primas, los deducibles y otros gastos relacionados con medicamentos recetados. Sin embargo, Puerto Rico y territorios estadounidenses, como Guam, las Islas Vírgenes, Samoa Americana y las Islas Marianas del Norte, están excluidos de este programa y dependen de un sistema de financiamiento distinto que limita su acceso a los mismos beneficios disponibles en los estados.

“Nuestra prioridad es atender lo básico, y la salud es básica. Miles de adultos mayores no pueden pagar sus medicinas.. Esta medida busca darles más dinero para sus medicamentos”, expresó Hernández.

“Durante demasiado tiempo, a quienes consideran a Guam su hogar se les ha excluido del acceso a uno de los programas más importantes de Medicare para nuestros residentes de bajos ingresos. Me enorgullece unirme al congresista Hernández para presentar la Ley de Igualdad del Subsidio para Personas de Bajos Ingresos de Medicare (Medicare Low Income Subsidy Equality Act) con el fin de corregir este problema”, expresó el congresista James C. Moylan. “Al trabajar a través de las líneas partidistas para encontrar soluciones sensatas, estamos cumpliendo con nuestros beneficiarios de Medicare y luchando por un trato justo para quienes consideran los territorios y estados libres asociados su hogar”.

“Me enorgullece unirme a este esfuerzo para garantizar que los beneficiarios de Medicare en Puerto Rico y los demás territorios puedan acceder a todos los beneficios de Medicare Parte D. Los puertorriqueños somos ciudadanos americanos y merecemos tener acceso a los mismos beneficios que reciben los ciudadanos en los estados”. expresó Soto.

“MMAPA respalda firmemente el Medicare Low Income Subsidy Equality Act of 2026, que extendería a Puerto Rico la asistencia federal para medicamentos recetados que ya reciben los beneficiarios elegibles en los estados. Ningún adulto mayor debería tener que poner en riesgo su salud por no poder costear sus medicamentos, y el lugar donde reside no debe determinar su acceso a esta asistencia esencial”, expresó Solange De Lahongrais, presidenta de MMAPA.

El Medicare Low Income Subsidy Equality Act busca cerrar una brecha histórica en la cobertura de Medicare y garantizar que los beneficiarios de bajos ingresos en Puerto Rico y territorios estadounidenses tengan acceso a la misma asistencia para medicamentos recetados disponible en el resto de Estados Unidos.

Este proyecto enmendaría la Ley del Seguro Social para permitir que los beneficiarios elegibles de Medicare en Puerto Rico y territorios estadounidenses puedan recibir los mismos subsidios de bajos ingresos de la Parte D disponibles en los estados. Específicamente, la medida:

Ampliaría la elegibilidad al programa Extra Help: Permitiría que los beneficiarios de Medicare que cumplan con los requisitos en Puerto Rico y otros territorios estadounidenses reciban asistencia federal para cubrir las primas, los deducibles y los copagos de sus medicamentos recetados.

Establecería criterios uniformes de elegibilidad por ingresos: Aplicaría las guías federales de pobreza utilizadas en los 48 estados contiguos y Washington, D.C., para determinar la elegibilidad de los residentes de los territorios.

Mantendría el apoyo federal a los territorios: Ajustaría la estructura actual de financiamiento de Medicaid para tomar en cuenta la transición hacia subsidios federales directos para medicamentos recetados.

Establecería una fecha de implementación: Permitiría que la asistencia ampliada de Medicare entre en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, siempre que la medida sea aprobada a tiempo.

title: Joyce, Congressional Croatian Caucus Urge Ratification of U.S.-Croatia Double Taxation Treaty
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Congressional Croatian Caucus Co-Chairs Dave Joyce (OH-14) and Nanette Barragán (CA-44), along with Vice Chairs Claudia Tenney (NY-24) and Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), sent a letter urging the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to swiftly approve the U.S.-Croatia tax treaty and send it to the full Senate for ratification.

The treaty, which reduces the burden of double taxation on cross-border investment, was initially signed in December 2022 and updated by a protocol signed on April 28, 2026, to align it with current U.S. law. President Trump transmitted the treaty to the Senate for ratification on September 14, 2026.

“The United States and Croatia are close allies, and this treaty will give taxpayers and businesses in both countries greater certainty when they invest across borders,” said Congressman Joyce. “Ohio’s 14th District is home to around 10,000 Croatian Americans, and as Co-Chair of the Congressional Croatian Caucus, I urge my Senate colleagues to act swiftly and ratify this treaty.”

“We must ratify the U.S.-Croatia tax treaty to strengthen our economic partnership and deepen the longstanding relationship between our two nations,” said Congresswoman Barragán. “By reducing the burden of double taxation and providing greater certainty for businesses and investors, this agreement will help expand trade, encourage investment, and create new opportunities on both sides of the Atlantic. As Co-Chair of the Congressional Croatian Caucus, I urge the Senate to advance this treaty and reaffirm our commitment to a strong U.S.-Croatia partnership.”

“The United States and Croatia have built a strong relationship, but our outdated tax policies continue to create unnecessary obstacles for businesses and investors in both countries,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Americans should not face double taxation simply because they do business with one of our closest European allies. This treaty is long overdue and will help American businesses compete, encourage new investment, and strengthen our economic partnership with Croatia. As Vice Chair of the Congressional Croatian Caucus, I urge the Senate to ratify this agreement without further delay.”

“Croatia is an important economic partner and a valued NATO ally of the United States,” said Congressman Lieu. “As Vice Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Croatian Caucus, I am honored to work with my colleagues to advance our shared interests. The Avoidance of Double Taxation Treaty will benefit American and Croatian taxpayers, as well as strengthen the ties between our two countries. I respectfully urge Chairman Risch and Ranking Member Shaheen to approve this treaty.”

“Americans should not be punished for doing business with Croatia—one of our proud NATO allies,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Our tax system needs a lot of work to make it work well for hardworking people—this is one step we can make to bring some fairness into the system, grow new investment, help American businesses compete, and strengthen America’s economic partnership with Croatia.”

Read the full letter here.

Background

This letter builds on ongoing efforts by Congressman Joyce and the Congressional Croatian Caucus to strengthen U.S.-Croatia relations. These efforts include a 2024 letter urging the Senate to work with the Department of the Treasury to resolve outstanding issues with the tax treaty and a 2023 letter calling for the swift confirmation of a U.S. Ambassador to Croatia. Congressman Joyce has also met with Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, Members of the Croatian Parliament, and other Croatian leaders to discuss opportunities for continued cooperation between the two countries.

title: Brownley Joins Bipartisan Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) announced that she is joining the newly-formed Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus. The caucus is led by Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) and co-chairs Congressmen Ken Calvert (CA-41), George Whitesides (CA-27), and Gabe Vasquez (NM-2). In addition to Congresswoman Brownley, Congressmen Jay Obernolte (CA-23) and Mike Haridopolos (FL-8) are also joining the caucus.

The purpose of the caucus is to educate Members of Congress, congressional staff, and the public about the importance of our nation’s military ranges and test facilities, which play a critical role in advancing research and development and test missions for our military. Technology development plays an important role in ensuring our warfighters have the resources needed for success, and our military ranges and test facilities are foundational to this effort.

“As the proud representative of Naval Base Ventura County, I understand firsthand the strategic importance of our military ranges and test facilities to our national security and supporting our nation’s defense readiness,” said Congresswoman Brownley. “To further strengthen these critical national security assets, I have consistently championed legislation to support our Major Range and Test Facility Bases and ensure they are equipped to meet our evolving defense needs. As a member of the Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus, I will continue working to ensure our Armed Forces have access to the resources, cutting-edge technology, and state-of-the-art facilities necessary to carry out their missions.”

“From NAWS China Lake and Edwards Air Force Base to the Mojave Air and Space Port, our community is the heart of America’s military research, test, and development enterprise,” said Congressman Fong. “America’s military ranges and test facilities are where our nation’s warfighters get their edge, and I am proud to represent some of the most critical in the world. This caucus will ensure that Members of Congress understand what is at stake, fight for the resources these facilities need, and protect the missions that keep America ahead of our adversaries. I am grateful to be joined by colleagues on both sides of the aisle who share that commitment.”

“The Antelope Valley is home to world-class facilities where we develop, test, and build aircraft to keep our country competitive,” said Congressman Whitesides. “I’m proud to join Rep. Fong in launching this bipartisan caucus to make sure every member of Congress understands how critical institutions like Plant 42, NASA Armstrong, and Edwards AFB are to the Department of Defense’s research, development, and test mission. Keeping America’s edge means investing in the ranges, the infrastructure, and the skilled workforce that make that testing possible.”

“California’s 23rd District is home to five military installations, including some of our nation’s premier military training, testing, and development facilities,” said Congressman Obernolte. “These bases play a critical role in advancing the technologies and capabilities that support our national defense. The Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus will help ensure Congress understands the importance of these facilities and the role they play in keeping the United States at the forefront of military readiness.”

“As the proud father of a U.S. Air Force Airman serving in explosive ordnance disposal, I understand firsthand how critical military ranges and test facilities are to preparing our warfighters for success,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “I’m proud to join this bipartisan caucus to strengthen military readiness, advance defense innovation, and ensure our servicemembers have the tools and training they need to keep America safe.”

title: Kelly honors latest Community Champions in Butler County
text:
BUTLER, PA -- During a ceremony at his Butler District Office, U.S. Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA) on Tuesday honored two new Community Champions.

Kelly honored Mark Gordon, Chief of Economic Development and Planning for Butler County, Pa., a position he has held for nearly a decade.

Mark has overseen the rapid growth and development across Butler County. Notably, Mark has been an instrumental partner at the local level, connecting with community and government leaders to help transform Butler County into what it is today. His steady leadership and clear vision for the county – including the development of the Gateway 228 project, which connects the growing communities of Cranberry Township, Mars, Seven Field, and Valencia – is a major reason for our region’s success.

Kelly also honored local businessman Scott Docherty.

Both as a business leader and as a neighbor, Scott has spent years giving back to the Saxonburg community and all of Butler County. As president of the steel building manufacturer CID Associates, Scott made a donation of $1,000 to Saxonburg borough in 2024. Earlier that year, he spearheaded a donation drive that raised $3,150 to help save John Roebling’s original wire rope workshop, which has stood in Saxonburg for roughly 185 years. These are just two examples of Mr. Docherty’s dedication and service to the community he loves.

"For years, Mark Gordon and Scott Docherty have been instrumental leaders in communities across Butler County. They are most deserving of this award," said Rep. Kelly.

BACKGROUND

The Community Champion Award recognizes and thanks service-minded individuals throughout Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District for selfless and significant contributions to their surrounding communities.

Each winner is presented with an official award plaque from Rep. Kelly’s office, a flag flown over the U.S. Capitol building, and a statement of congratulations entered into the official Congressional Record.

title: Kennedy Leads Letter Urging FTC to Block $29.1 Billion Sysco-Restaurant Depot Merger
text:
Kennedy and Colleagues Warn Proposed Acquisition Threatens Independent Restaurants, Local Jobs, and Affordability by Eliminating a Critical Source of Price Competition

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) led his colleagues in sending a letter to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) urging rejection of Sysco Corporation’s proposed $29.1 billion acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot. Members warned that the merger would reduce competition, drive up costs for independent restaurants, and threaten the small businesses that anchor local economies across Western New York and the nation.

Across the country, independent restaurants are already facing mounting financial pressure, with food costs up 38 percent nationwide since 2019 and nearly half of restaurant operators reporting that their businesses were unprofitable in 2025. Sysco’s acquisition of Restaurant Depot would eliminate a critical source of price competition, leaving independent restaurant owners with fewer options to control costs and putting additional pressure on businesses already struggling to keep prices affordable for their customers.

“Independent restaurants are part of the fabric of Western New York. They employ our neighbors, support local suppliers, and give our communities places to come together. These small businesses are already being squeezed by rising food prices and operating costs, and they cannot afford another hit,” said Congressman Kennedy. “This merger would put even more power in the hands of a major distributor while taking away one of the few tools independent restaurants have to keep their costs down. When competition disappears, small businesses pay the price and those costs ultimately reach the families sitting down at the table. The FTC must stand up for independent businesses, protect competition, and reject this deal.”

“Independent restaurants are already struggling because of rising food costs,” said Congresswoman Becca Balint (VT-AL). “By buying Restaurant Depot, Sysco would eliminate a key source of competition that independent restaurants rely on to get a fair price on food and supplies. That means higher costs for local restaurants and more expensive meals for working families. We need regulators to be serious about pushing back against this wave of corporate consolidation so that people can afford to live their lives and so our small, local businesses can have a fair shot.”

“Independent restaurants are operating on razor-thin margins, and Restaurant Depot is one of the few tools they have to check broadline prices and keep their costs in line. We are grateful to Congressman Tim Kennedy for his leadership urging the FTC to reject Sysco's proposed acquisition of Restaurant Depot. When competition disappears from the supply chain, the consequences reach well beyond a restaurant’s doors putting farmers, local artisans and the economic stability of communities at risk.” Erika Polmar, Executive Director, Independent Restaurant Coalition

Lawmakers underscored the importance of protecting competition as families and small businesses continue to face affordability challenges. Allowing further consolidation in the foodservice supply chain would leave independent restaurants with fewer choices and less leverage to manage costs, threatening the local businesses and jobs that communities depend on.

Background

Restaurant Depot operates 167 warehouse locations across 35 states, serving more than 725,000 independent restaurants and foodservice operators. Its cash-and-carry model allows restaurant owners to compare prices directly with traditional wholesale distributors like Sysco and negotiate more competitive terms. This proposed acquisition would place both distribution channels under the same corporate ownership, eliminating an important check on pricing in the foodservice supply chain. Independent restaurants employ approximately 11 million workers nationwide and support more than five million additional jobs across supply chains that include farms, fisheries, dairies, equipment suppliers, and specialty food producers. By hiring locally, purchasing from local suppliers, and banking with local financial institutions, these businesses help sustain the communities they serve. The FTC has previously recognized the competitive risks of consolidation in foodservice distribution: in 2015, the Commission opposed Sysco’s proposed acquisition of US Foods, arguing that the merger would substantially reduce competition and likely increase prices for restaurants. After a federal district court granted the FTC’s request for a preliminary injunction, the companies abandoned the deal.

Full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Statement from Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds on EVS-TAP Suspension
text:
Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds issued the following statement regarding the Department of Homeland Security’s announcement suspending the CNMI Economic Vitality and Security Travel Authorization Program (EVS-TAP):

“Following today's announcement, I spoke directly with the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, and House leadership regarding the suspension of the CNMI Economic Vitality and Security Travel Authorization Program (EVS-TAP) and its potential consequences for the Commonwealth.

“Secretary Mullin personally assured me that he will work directly with the CNMI to better understand and address the underlying issues that led to this temporary suspension. I want to emphasize that EVS-TAP has been suspended, not terminated. We have experienced interruptions to travel programs serving the Commonwealth before, and we will work through this together with our federal partners to address the concerns that have been raised and find a path forward, just as we have done before.

“The safety and security of our Commonwealth, our residents, and our visitors must always be a serious consideration. EVS-TAP was established with safeguards that allow the Department of Homeland Security to suspend the program when security or law enforcement concerns arise. These safeguards are an important part of protecting our community and maintaining the integrity of the program. As we work to better understand the circumstances behind this suspension, we will work with our federal partners to address the concerns identified and support the program’s resumption as quickly as possible.

“I have made clear to our federal partners the urgency of this matter. Our tourism industry is already facing tremendous challenges, and a prolonged disruption would have serious consequences for our businesses, workers, and families. We must also consider the immediate effects on airlines, travel arrangements, and the businesses that depend on visitor arrivals.

“My immediate priority is securing the resumption of EVS-TAP as quickly as the outstanding concerns can be resolved.”

title: Larsen Continues to Press ICE for Answers about Local Activity
text:
Today, Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) wrote to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) regarding Larsen’s visit to ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) suboffice in Ferndale on October 9th:

“I support HSI’s mission to investigate and apprehend individuals involved in cross-border criminal activity, including human and drug trafficking,” said Rep. Larsen. “However, I am concerned by reports that HSI personnel, including those in Northwest Washington, have been reassigned to conduct civil immigration enforcement. HSI agents should be focused on investigating serious criminal activity, not diverted to support the President’s mass deportation agenda."

Rep. Larsen is conducting robust, close oversight of Trump’s immigration enforcement in Northwest Washington. In addition to ICE’s HSI facility, Rep. Larsen visited ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) facility in Ferndale in July 2026 and the privately-run ICE detention facility in Tacoma in June 2025.

“This is not case-closed on oversight of ICE activity in our region,” said Rep. Larsen. “I will keep pushing to get answers and accountability for my community. My office stands ready to help family members locate their loved ones in ICE custody and access legal services – call 425-252-3188 or go to larsen.house.gov/helping-you/visas-and-immigration.htm.”

Rep. Larsen’s full letter to Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella is available here and below.

October 27, 2026

Dear Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella:

Thank you for the opportunity to visit the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Blaine field office in Ferndale, Washington on October 9, 2026.

I support HSI’s mission to investigate and apprehend individuals involved in cross-border criminal activity, including drug smuggling, human trafficking and child exploitation. However, I am concerned by reports that HSI personnel, including those in Northwest Washington, have been reassigned to conduct civil immigration enforcement alongside ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO).

According to an August 20, 2026 report by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General (OIG), HSI agents devoted 800 percent more hours to immigration enforcement in Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 than in FY 2024. During the same period, hours spent investigating fentanyl-related crimes fell by 31 percent, while fentanyl seizures by HSI agents declined by 39 percent.1 HSI agents should be focused on investigating serious criminal activity, not diverted to support ERO’s civil immigration enforcement operations as part of the President’s mass deportation agenda.

To better understand whether HSI’s operations in Northwest Washington have been affected by the diversion of HSI staff to civil immigration enforcement, please provide the following information no later than Friday, November 20, 2026:

1. Since January 20, 2025, how many HSI agents assigned to the Blaine field office have been reassigned, detailed or otherwise assigned to support ERO operations? For each reassignment, please provide the number of personnel involved, the date the reassignment began and the duration.

2. Since the start of FY 2023 on October 1, 2022, how many agent hours at HSI Blaine have been dedicated to supporting the ERO mission of civil immigration enforcement? Please provide this data by year for FY 2023 through FY 2026.

3. Since the start of FY 2023, how many agent hours at HSI Blaine have been dedicated to investigating fentanyl-related criminal activity? Please provide this data by year for FY 2023 through FY 2026.

4. Since the start of FY 2023, how many fentanyl seizures have agents at HSI Blaine carried out? Please provide this data by year for FY 2023 through FY 2026.

5. Since January 20, 2025, have HSI officers received any directives, orders or guidance to expand or limit their work with ERO? If so, please provide copies of any relevant directives, orders or guidance and their dates of issuance.

6. Has the HSI Blaine facility been used to detain individuals arrested by ERO? If so, please provide exact dates and details of these detentions.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

title: City of Palo Alto Advances Protections Restricting ICE Facility Construction
text:
PALO ALTO, CA – Today, Bay Area Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16), congratulated the City of Palo Alto for adopting an interim ordinance that temporarily restricts the development of ICE detention facilities within their jurisdiction.

“ICE detention centers have no place in our neighborhoods, and local leaders don't need to wait until one opens to take action,” said Liccardo. “By acting now, Palo Alto joins a growing coalition of Bay Area communities using local land-use authority to protect their communities by restricting DHS from converting commercial or industrial properties into detention centers. I thank and commend Mayor Vicki Veenker and her colleagues on the Palo Alto City Council for expanding this regional effort to protect our communities.”

Liccardo, who represents portions of Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties, released a toolkit in August to help local governments use zoning laws and building regulations to mitigate the expansion of ICE detention facilities and safeguard community health and safety. The cities of San José,Mountain View, and Gilroy, along with the counties of San Mateo, Monterey, and Napa have already advanced such ordinances. Several other city councils have now directed their staff to begin this process, and several more ordinance changes are in the pipeline.

“Palo Alto is proud to take proactive steps to protect the health, safety, and well-being of our residents,” said Palo Alto Mayor Vicki Veenker. “By adopting this temporary ordinance, we join cities and counties across the Bay Area in using our local authority to protect our neighbors and restrict the development of ICE detention facilities in our community.”

title: Lofgren Announces $1 Million+ Federal Grant for Groundbreaking Vision Research Based in Gilroy
text:
“California is where great minds come to take their ideas and change the world, and I’m proud to see this groundbreaking research happening in Gilroy,” said Rep. Zoe Lofgren. “As the leading Democrat on the House Science Committee and as a longtime advocate for accessibility, I’m proud to see XR Navigation receive this NIH grant. I’m very happy about the potential this technology holds to open opportunities for blind and low-vision people, and I commend the researchers on their important work."

"XR Navigation is excited to perform research and commercialize digital maps that state and local governments subject to the April 2027 Americans with Disabilities Act Title II rule deadline, and other welcoming entities, can incorporate to make their digital maps fully usable to blind and low-vision users for the first time,” said Brandon Biggs, CEO of XR Navigation. title: Rep. McGuire, Rep. Griffith Announce Nearly $25 Million in Grants for Regional Economic Development Coalition Projects
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – The U.S. Department of Commerce Economic Development Administration (EDA) has awarded $24,791,450 in grants for economic development projects promoting additive manufacturing technologies. The breakdown of the grants is as follows:

$16,972,068 to support the Virginia Tech College of Engineering in designing products that employ additive manufacturing processes

$4,413,327 to support the Institute for Advanced Learning and Research in training 2,000 workers in advanced manufacturing skills through expanded apprenticeship programs

“Additive manufacturing and advanced materials processing operations continue to grow in the region, as highlighted by recent announcements that MELD Manufacturing of Southwest Virginia will build a new 12,000-square foot facility,” said U.S. Congressmen Morgan Griffith (VA-09) and Rep. John McGuire (VA-05). “These EDA grants for nearly $25 million help our region expand its additive manufacturing base, generate local manufacturing jobs and strengthen economic development coalitions. This money is to be supported by additional money from the region and industry partners.”

Nearly $25 million in federal funding supported by $195 million in total commitments will train 2,000 workers and give local manufacturers the test beds to design, prototype, and bring new products to market faster than ever before,” said U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

title: Rep. Mejia Leads 17 Colleagues in Letter to USDA Demanding Answers on Cuts to Nutrition Programs for Seniors
text:
Lawmakers demand accountability for Trump administration's SNAP restrictions and proposed elimination of critical food assistance for nearly 700,000 low-income seniors

Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) led a coalition of 17 representatives in a letter to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins demanding answers regarding the Trump administration's cuts to federal nutrition assistance programs and their impact on older Americans struggling with rising food, housing, and health care costs.

President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” slashes federal food assistance by $187 billion through 2034, while imposing new work requirements that put SNAP benefits at risk for older adults. At the same time, the Trump administration has proposed eliminating the Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP), which helps nearly 700,000 low-income seniors put food on the table. Together, these policies will make it harder for older Americans to afford groceries as the cost of living continues to rise.

“Older Americans who spent their lives working and contributing to their communities should not have to sacrifice their health, housing, or other basic needs just to put food on the table. Your Department must account for the consequences of these policies and demonstrate how it will protect older Americans from hunger. Anything less is unacceptable,” said the lawmakers.

The letter demands comprehensive data on seniors who have lost or experienced reductions in SNAP benefits, the impact of expanded work requirements, and USDA's plans to protect access to affordable, nutritious food. Lawmakers also seek answers regarding the administration's proposal to eliminate CSFP despite Congress maintaining its funding.

The letter requests a written response from Secretary Rollins by November 6, 2026.

Representatives Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Frederica Wilson (FL-24), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Cleo Fields (LA-06), André Carson (IN-07), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Nanette Diaz Barragán (CA-44), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), and Andrea Salinas (OR-06) also signed the letter.

title: THOMPSON, FONG'S CLERGY ACT BECOMES LAW
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Rep. Mike Thompson (D-CA-04) and Rep. Vince Fong’s (R-CA-20) announced their bipartisan Clergy Act was signed into law. Thompson successfully passed the Clergy Act through the House of Representatives earlier this year, after securing unanimous support in House Ways and Means Committee. The Clergy Act establishes a one-time re-enrollment window for pastors and other clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security to voluntarily opt back in and begin contributing to their financial futures.

“Faith leaders play a critical role in supporting our communities — offering them the flexibility to opt in to Social Security as they plan for retirement just makes sense. I’m glad to have co-led this bipartisan effort with Rep. Fong and I am proud that our bill was signed into law,” said Thompson.

BACKGROUND

The Clergy Act establishes a one-time re-enrollment window for clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security, many in their youth, to voluntarily opt back in. Some of our faith leaders opted out decades ago, often due to inaccurate advice or conscientious objection, only to later face significant financial hardship. Under previous law, this opt-out was permanent. For clergy who have spent their lives serving their communities and congregations, this legislation restores the freedom to secure basic financial protection in retirement.

The Clergy Act creates a two-year window – covering taxable years beginning January 1, 2028, and January 1, 2029 – for eligible clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security to revoke their exemption and begin contributing. Importantly, this legislation does not modify existing Social Security regulations. Eligible clergy must still meet the standard 10-year contribution requirement to earn full retired-worker benefits, receiving benefits proportional to their contributions. The bill also requires the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and Social Security Administration to submit a plan to Congress outlining their strategy to inform clergy members of their eligibility to re-enroll. Historically, Congress has approved limited re-enrollment windows, including in 1999 under the Ticket to Work Act.

The Clergy Act is supported by a broad coalition of faith-based and retirement security organizations, including the National Association of Evangelicals, Church Alliance, Evangelical Council for Financial Accountability (ECFA), GuideStone Financial Resources, and Lancaster Baptist Church.

title: THOMPSON SECURES $115 MILLION IN FEDERAL DOLLARS OWED TO LOCAL RESIDENTS
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) announced his team has reached a new milestone in constituent services: Over $115 million federal dollars returned back to the pockets of residents.

An important part of Thompson's job is to help residents of California's Fourth Congressional District navigate the complex federal agency system – and to fight to get people the benefits they are owed by the federal government. Since Thompson’s team began tracking casework data in 2016, Mike Thompson and his office have worked to close over 17,000 cases for residents and returned over $115 million owed to constituents by federal agencies. Money returned to constituents includes veterans and survivor benefits, Social Security checks, IRS refunds, and more.

“My team and I pride ourselves on cutting through red tape and delivering for people. Whether we’re working to secure backpay for wrongly denied Social Security checks or helping the surviving family members of a veteran get the benefits they deserve, my team and I are always here to help. Casework on behalf of residents is the unseen side of my job and also one of the most important parts of my job. I look forward to continuing to close cases and get things done for members of our community,” said Thompson.

BACKGROUND

By the time someone turns to their Congressperson for help with a federal agency, they are often at the end of their rope. Many Americans report experiencing bureaucratic backlogs and dead ends when dealing with understaffed federal agencies. Thompson and his team believe this is unacceptable.

Constituents from across the Fourth District have commented on the help Mike Thompson’s office provided to them in navigating federal agencies:

“The IRS was mistakenly demanding thousands of dollars from me; for a year I couldn’t get them to admit their error. At my wit’s end, I called Mike Thompson’s office. [His staff] listened, collected all my information and began advocating for me. His persistence and skill made all the difference; finally got resolution and vindication. Many, many thanks for this invaluable service!” said Christina from Napa County.

“My Social Security benefit was incorrectly reduced, and for over a year I couldn’t get a response from the Social Security Administration. My wife urged me to reach out to Congressman Mike Thompson’s office, and I met his staff during office hours in Dixon. Within a week, SSA corrected my benefit and sent $5,000 in back pay. I’m truly grateful for the Congressman and his dedicated staff—they made a real difference,” said Mahdi from Solano County.

“I am a Navy veteran suffering the health effects of radiation exposure while on active duty. I had fought with the VA bureaucracy for sixteen years for compensation and had my claim denied on my third and final appeal. I had lost all hope. That’s when Congressman Thompson stepped in. Through his tireless efforts this injustice was reversed and I was granted 100 percent service-connected disability and compensation. I can now focus my energy and attention on my health instead of reams of fruitless paperwork. Thank you Congressman Thompson,” said Paul from Sonoma County.

“I’m a small business owner and a mom. When my health took a serious turn it became impossible for me to keep working, I felt like my whole world was collapsing. After Social Security denied my disability claim, I was devastated and didn’t know where to turn. That’s when I contacted Congressman Mike Thompson’s office. From the very first conversation, Mike Thompson’s team treated my case like it mattered deeply to them. Because of their determination and expertise, the agency ultimately granted my appeal. I can say without hesitation that I would not have gotten this result on my own. Mike Thompson and his team literally saved my life,” said Crystal from Yolo County.

“I want to say THANK YOU for all the assistance [Rep. Thompson] provided in helping to resolve my issue with the FAA. I had an accident in October of 2024 and because of that accident, I was unable to retain my pilot privileges until I could get it reinstated. I am a flight instructor and this is how I make my living and support my family. With [Rep. Thompson’s] help and guidance, I was able to get my pilot privileges reinstated. It is my belief that without the assistance of your office, this process would have been significantly delayed,” said Tim from Lake County.

Fourth District residents who need help with passports and visas, veterans benefits, IRS issues, agricultural issues, small business assistance, immigration, Medicare and Medicaid, or residents facing any other problem navigating the federal government can contact Thompson’s office at mikethompson.house.gov/contact/help-federal-agency or call his nearest office:

title: ICYMI: Grassley, Miller-Meeks Op-Ed: Republicans Are Expanding Access to Primary Care in Iowa
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) and Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA) wrote an op-ed published in The Hawk Eye highlighting how Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts Act is expanding access to primary care in communities across Iowa. The lawmakers specifically highlight improved access to a new and growing field of medicine called direct primary care (DPC).

Republicans worked hard to pass the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, preventing the largest tax increase in American history and putting more money back into the pocketbooks of seniors and families. The law also expanded access to primary care in communities across Iowa. As a result, Iowa families have better access to a new and growing field of medicine called direct primary care (DPC).

DPC is a locally delivered, patient-centered model of care that puts patients and their doctors, physician assistants, or nurse practitioners at the center of health care, rather than insurance companies and middlemen.

DPC was enabled under state law in 2018 and further protected in 2026. Now, thanks to the Republican Working Families Tax Cuts Act, Iowa families can use their health savings accounts (HSAs) to improve access to primary care.

DPC is a simpler way to get routine physicals, urgent care, and other primary care services. Patients pay a monthly subscription and get access to a primary care provider of their choice. Through this relationship, patients can communicate directly with their provider and typically get same-day or next-day service instead of waiting days or weeks to get care. Patients establish a relationship with a health care provider and utilize their services as often as they want without paying more.

Thanks to the new tax law, families can use tax-free money, through their HSA or flexible spending account (FSA), to pay for a membership-based model of care that lets them choose a primary care provider of their choice and gain access to a suite of care options under this direct primary care service arrangement.

More health care providers are turning to DPC because it allows them to spend more time with patients and less time dealing with paperwork and insurance company approvals. Across Iowa, direct primary care providers are opening their doors and growing in rural communities and suburban areas.

When patients have access to timely and high-quality primary care, they have better health outcomes and live longer.

Thanks to the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, more Iowa families can access direct primary care and get the timely care they need.

title: Pallone Leads NJ Delegation Members in Urging Trump to Approve Federal Disaster Assistance Following Devastating September Nor’easter
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today lead a letter with Representatives Donald Norcross (NJ-01), Jeff Van Drew (NJ-02), Herbert Conaway, Jr. (NJ-03), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Robert Menendez, Jr. (NJ-08), Nellie Pou (NJ-09), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) to President Trump urging him to swiftly approve Governor Sherrill’s recent request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the powerful nor’easter that battered New Jersey from September 23 through September 29, 2026.

The request follows a September 28 letter from Pallone calling on state and federal officials to immediately assess storm damage in anticipation of a federal disaster declaration. Those assessments have now confirmed nearly $27 million in damage across Atlantic, Cape May, and Monmouth counties.

“We are writing to express our support for Governor Sherrill’s request to declare a Major Disaster for the State of New Jersey for the impacts sustained from this severe weather event,” the lawmakers wrote. “The nor’easter brought dangerous conditions to our state causing substantial erosion. In some parts of our state, six to seven feet of tidal flooding inundated businesses and homes, municipal infrastructure such as piers and bulkheads were severely damaged, and vehicles on the street were submerged in flood water. While it appears that flood control projects, berms, and raised homes saved many areas from even worse damage, the destruction left behind from this storm is significant.”

On October 26, Governor Sherrill requested federal assistance to help communities cover the costs of storm cleanup, repair damaged roads, bridges, utilities, and other public infrastructure, and strengthen protections against future storms. A Major Disaster Declaration would unlock federal funding to help the Garden State recover from damage that local governments cannot afford to address on their own.

The full letter to President Trump is hereand below:

President Trump:

From September 23 to 29, 2026, communities across New Jersey were hit by a powerful nor’easter storm that resulted in intense rainfall, tidal surges, and forceful winds. We are writing to express our support for Governor Sherrill’s request to declare a Major Disaster for the State of New Jersey for the impacts sustained from this severe weather event.

The nor’easter brought dangerous conditions to our state causing substantial erosion. In some parts of our state, six to seven feet of tidal flooding inundated businesses and homes, municipal infrastructure such as piers and bulkheads were severely damaged, and vehicles on the street were submerged in flood water. While it appears that flood control projects, berms, and raised homes saved many areas from even worse damage, the destruction left behind from this storm is significant. A post-storm assessment by the New Jersey Department of Environment’s Office of Costal Engineering determined that eight federal coastal storm risk management projects were significantly damaged. In its joint Preliminary Damage Assessments (PDAs), FEMA validated damages totaling $26,976,037 for Atlantic, Cape May, and Monmouth counties. The costs associated with these counties greatly exceed federal thresholds that indicate whether the impact to a jurisdiction exceeds the jurisdiction’s capacity to fund the cost of recovery.[1] The scope of this emergency requires critical support from the federal government for the State to recover from this storm.

Governor Sherrill requested activation of FEMA’s Public Assistance Program (Categories A-G) and the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) to reimburse costs to repair public infrastructure and fund projects that will prepare our state for the impacts of future catastrophic events. We urge you to use the authority granted under Section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 5121-5207 and 44 C.F.R. § 206.36 to expeditiously declare a Major Disaster for this nor’easter, so the State of New Jersey can effectively recover from this disaster and address vulnerabilities created by this storm.

Responding to major disasters is not just the federal government’s job, it’s America’s promise.
