title: Rep. Moore, Sen. Justice Join Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation to Promote Historic Preservation and Tourism
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Riley M. Moore joined Senator Jim Justice (R-WV) and Keven Walker, CEO of the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation, today for the “Stand Up for West Virginia’s Battlefields” event to highlight the Shenandoah Valley Access, Legacy and Outdoor Recreation (VALOR) Act and its potential to strengthen historic preservation, expand tourism, and drive economic growth in West Virginia’s Eastern Panhandle.

“West Virginia’s history is inseparable from the Civil War, and we have a responsibility to preserve the battlefields where so many gave their lives to help shape our state and our nation. I’m proud to join Senator Justice in championing the Shenandoah VALOR Act to help protect these historic sites while creating new opportunities for tourism, supporting local businesses, and strengthening our economy in the Eastern Panhandle. We can preserve our heritage while continuing to grow our communities, and I’m proud to work alongside Senator Justice and the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation to make that vision a reality,” said Congressman Riley M. Moore.

“West Virginia’s history is American history, and we ought to be doing everything in our power to preserve it. The brave men who fought and sacrificed so much during the Civil War deserve to be remembered, and we have a responsibility to make sure future generations understand what happened right here in our state. This bill is about protecting that legacy while bringing more visitors to the Eastern Panhandle, creating jobs, and putting more dollars into our local communities. I’m proud to be working with Congressman Riley Moore and the Shenandoah National Battlefield Foundation to get this over the line,” said Senator Jim Justice.

"At the core of all we do is the belief that our shared history can unite the people of our nation; that there is strength and inspiration for our own times to be found in the struggles of the past. Preservation is more about the future than the past, and ensuring the preservation of West Virginia's Battlefields are a part of that clear vision,” said Keven Walker, Chief Executive Officer of the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation.

The Shenandoah VALOR Act would expand the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District to include Jefferson, Berkeley, and Morgan counties in West Virginia, as well as Rockbridge County in Virginia. The legislation would extend a proven model for battlefield preservation and heritage tourism to communities that have historically missed out on preservation funding and tourism opportunities.

Since the National Historic District was established in 1996, the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation has preserved more than 8,000 acres across 11 Virginia battlefields and developed visitor centers, museum exhibits, and public trails. A 2017 National Park Service study found that the district attracts more than two million visitors annually, generates approximately $293 million in economic impact, supports nearly 4,000 jobs, and produces more than $20 million in tax revenue.

The legislation would bring similar opportunities to West Virginia while protecting private property rights. Preservation would rely on willing sellers, prohibit the use of eminent domain, and require federal preservation funding to be matched dollar-for-dollar by private donations or state and local government partnerships.

The Shenandoah VALOR Act has earned bipartisan support from West Virginia’s and Virginia’s congressional delegations, as well as the Jefferson, Berkeley, and Morgan County commissions.

title: Congresswoman Scholten Introduces Bipartisan SCREENS Act to Improve Early Cancer Detection
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) introduced theStandardizing Cancer Recommendations for Earlier Evaluation and Navigation of Screenings (SCREENS) Act. This bipartisan bill would help more Americans catch cancer earlier by making screening recommendations easier to understand and giving healthcare providers better tools to identify patients who may be at risk or overdue for screenings. Congresswoman Scholten was joined by Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02) and Senator Chuck Grassley (R-IA) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate.

“Early cancer detection saves lives, but for far too many Americans, navigating complicated health care recommendations can lead to missed screenings,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “I’m proud to join Rep. Hinson in introducing the SCREENS Act, which would help create a national, digital framework of cancer screening guidelines. Building this resource will give patients clear, easy-to-follow recommendations and help providers identify who is overdue so that more people in Michigan and across the country get the services they need when they need them.”

“So many Iowa families have been touched by cancer, including mine. Iowa’s rising cancer rates are unacceptable, and we have to do everything we can to reverse this trend. That starts with making early detection resources simple and accessible so we can catch cancer earlier, improve outcomes, and save lives. I will continue working across the aisle and leave no stone unturned in this fight,” said Congresswoman Ashley Hinson.

“Detecting cancer early can save lives. I know that based on the personal experience of my wife, Barbara, a nearly 40-year breast cancer survivor. Unfortunately, patients and providers are navigating a complex and confusing maze just to keep up with cancer screening recommendations. By making these recommendations more accessible through technology, our SCREENS Act would strengthen cancer care and help save lives. This bill would proactively support Iowans by helping providers identify patients who could be overdue for a screening. I want to thank Congresswoman Hinson for her support for this legislation and her commitment to boosting cancer care in Iowa,” said Senator Chuck Grassley.

Specifically, the SCREENS Act would:

Make cancer screening guidelines easier to access: Direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop a national digital framework for cancer screening and risk assessment recommendations that can be incorporated into electronic health records.

Help doctors catch potential risks earlier: Support technology that helps healthcare providers identify patients who may be at higher risk for cancer or overdue for recommended screenings.

Give patients clearer information: Make screening recommendations easier to understand and follow so patients can stay on top of their health.

Improve coordination with health plans: Require HHS to issue guidance to Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, and ACA plans on integrating electronic cancer screening tools.

Support innovation in cancer prevention and early detection: Authorize research and pilot projects to help bring these technologies into everyday medical practice.

Read the full text of the SCREENS Act here.

The legislation builds on Congresswoman Scholten’s bipartisan work to expand access to cancer screenings, including the CATCH IT Act, which would increase federal investments in preventative health equipment, like mammogram machines and mobile cancer screening tools in rural communities.

title: Congresswoman Lee, Culinary Union Call on Station Casinos to Negotiate a Fair Contract After U.S. Supreme Court Denial

Because of the tenacity of the workers at Red Rock Casino, we were thrilled to celebrate this big win,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “Now, I urge Station Casinos to negotiate in a fair and timely manner to produce a fair contract that is fair, and just. Workers can’t afford to wait another 17 years without a contract.”

Red Rock Casino workers won. On September 4, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court denied Station Casinos' emergency attempt to block the federal order requiring Red Rock Casino to recognize and negotiate with the Culinary Union and that order is now in effect.

Workers at Red Rock Casino voted to unionize in 2019 and have waited nearly seven years for this moment. For the sake of their employees and the Las Vegas community, Culinary Union and elected leaders say it is time for Station Casinos to move forward and negotiate a fair contract now.

“It’s not every day that Nevada casino workers get to say ‘the Supreme Court is on my side,’” said Ted Pappageorge, Secretary-Treasurer for the Culinary Union. “We can say that now because the Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court recently stopped the latest legal maneuver by Station Casinos to stop workers from exercising their right to join a union under federal law. Even the U.S. Supreme Court is telling Station Casinos, a Nevada gaming company with a privileged gaming license, that they cannot circumvent the law. So today we’re sending a clear message to Station Casinos: Respect workers and follow the law. The law is on the side of the workers. Leaders of the Nevada Congressional delegation, Dina Titus, Steven Horsford, and Susie Lee are standing with workers, and the next Governor of Nevada, Aaron Ford, is on the side of workers. Station Casinos, It's time to lay down the sword and pick up the pen. We look forward to winning a fair contract.”

“Station Casinos just had the best financial quarter in its history. Workers have helped build that success and securing a fair union contract at Red Rock Casino is how Las Vegas moves forward together,” said Diana Valles, President of the Culinary Union. “Station Casinos workers need a raise. Station Casinos workers at luxury resort properties - Green Valley Ranch and Red Rock - are behind an average of $14,400 on annual wages when compared to Culinary Union members employed on the Las Vegas Strip. This fight has always been based on one simple truth: Station Casinos workers are not second-class workers. Station Casinos did everything they could to bust the Union, but we will never give up. It’s time for a contract, now!”

“The courts have spoken. It is time for Station Casinos to come to the table and negotiate a fair contract now,” said Attorney General Aaron Ford. “On the picket line, in the courtroom, and at the bargaining table, I’m standing in solidarity with Red Rock Casino workers until they get the contract they’ve earned.”

“Workers all over Nevada and across the country will see this victory and understand what worker power and union solidarity look like,” said Congressman Steven Horsford. “As co-chair of the Congressional Labor Caucus, I will continue fighting to make the Faster Labor Contracts Act law, so workers everywhere have the right to a fair contract without having to rely on the Supreme Court to bring employers to the table. This victory is about more than a contract. It’s about unity, fairness, and respect for the hardworking men and women who make Las Vegas run. Every worker deserves to be treated with dignity, have their voice heard, and share in the prosperity they help create.”

“As a member of the House Labor Caucus, I am proud to stand with Local 226 in their fight for better wages and working conditions,” said Congresswoman Dina Titus. “The decision from the Supreme Court is a win for the workers at Station Casinos, but there is more to be done. That is why I am advocating for common sense policies like the PRO Act and the Faster Labor Contracts Act.”

title: Congressman Carter Statement on Louisiana v. Callais Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), released the following statement following the motion-to-dismiss hearing held in Shreveport, LA, on Louisiana v. Callais, to determine whether the legal challenge to the final Black-majority congressional district in Louisiana can move forward:

“Fair representation in our democracy doesn’t just mean lines on a map — it’s about whether Black Americans and other Americans of color have a meaningful opportunity to make their voices heard in government and obtain access to good schools, safe roads, and quality health care. The Callais plaintiffs got what they want earlier this year: the Supreme Court eviscerated the Voting Rights Act further, giving permission to conservative state legislators in Louisiana and around the country to eliminate Black-majority congressional districts. As a result, fair political representation for Black communities will take a huge blow this Election Day. But this wasn’t enough; now these plaintiffs want to eliminate the last remaining Black-majority congressional district in Louisiana – a state that is one-third Black and has six congressional districts. I will continue fighting to protect the right to vote and the principles of fair representation in Congress by passing the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.”

Background

In April 2026, the Supreme Court issued a ruling in the Callais case that struck down Louisiana’s previous congressional map and further eviscerated Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Following the Supreme Court’s decision, Louisiana eliminated one of its two Black-majority districts. Earlier today, a motion-to-dismiss hearing was held in Shreveport, Louisiana. At the hearing, the original plaintiffs in the Louisiana v. Callais case presented a challenge to Louisiana’s remaining majority-Black congressional district. Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill has requested the case be dismissed.

title: Rep. Watson Coleman Secures $715,000 in Federal Funding for Delaware River Basin Commission
text:
Today, Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) announced $715,000 in federal funding for the Delaware River Basin Commission’s (DRBC) work protecting water resources across the Delaware River Basin.

The Congresswoman was joined by DRBC Executive Director Kristen Bowman Kavanagh, DRBC Director of External Affairs Beth Brown, New Jersey State Geologist Steve Domber, Ewing Mayor Bert Steinmann, local officials, and community partners.

The funding will fulfill the federal government’s signatory funding share for the DRBC, supporting its scientific research, water quality monitoring, engineering, and regulatory programs. The Commission’s work helps maintain safe water supplies while preparing communities for the effects of climate change, including flooding and drought.

“As New Jersey’s sole Appropriator, I have been committed to securing federal funding for the Delaware River Basin Commission because millions of people depend on this resource every day,” said Congresswoman Watson Coleman. “We have a responsibility to protect the water our communities rely on and ensure that every community benefits from that investment. Environmental justice must be part of that work, particularly for communities that have faced a disproportionate share of environmental burdens. This funding will help the DRBC continue its work to engage in meaningful research and protect water quality while supporting sustainable water management throughout the basin.”

“Throughout her time in Congress, Representative Watson Coleman has demonstrated a deep commitment to the communities and resources of the Delaware River Basin,” said DRBC Executive Director Kristen Bowman Kavanagh. “The Congresswoman understands that protecting our shared water resources is essential to the prosperity and resilience of our region. We are proud to recognize her years of public service and grateful for her impactful leadership and support for the DRBC.”

The Delaware River Basin spans 13,539 square miles across parts of Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania. It includes all or parts of 42 counties and 868 municipalities across 22 congressional districts and provides water to more than 14.2 million people, including about 2 million New Jersey residents.

Established in 1961, the DRBC brings the federal government and the four basin states together to coordinate water resource management. Its responsibilities include water quality protection, water supply planning, flood loss reduction, drought management, conservation, and watershed planning.

Commission signatory funding supports the scientific and regulatory work needed to protect water resources over the long term. This work also supports environmental sustainability and water equity by helping communities prepare for changing conditions and ensuring that the benefits of clean, reliable water are shared across the basin.

Congresswoman Watson Coleman has continued to champion federal funding for the DRBC, recognizing the importance of regional cooperation in protecting the Delaware River Basin and the communities that depend on it.

title: Wied Helps Secure $30 Million Grant to Strengthen Wisconsin's Energy Production
text:
DE PERE, WI – The U.S. Department of Transportation announced today that Wisconsin will receive a $30 million grant through its Port Infrastructure Development Program, following Congressman Wied’s advocacy for the funding.

The $30,407,281 grant will fund the Lake Michigan Marine Highway Transportation Energy Project, which will extend a pipeline from Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport to the U.S. Venture terminal at Port Milwaukee. The project will strengthen domestic energy production and help lower energy costs over the long term.

“I am very pleased to see this funding come to Wisconsin to strengthen our ports, increase domestic energy production, and help lower costs for Wisconsinites. I contacted Secretary Duffy to advocate for this funding, and I thank him for investing in our great state. Continuing to unleash American energy is crucial to reducing our dependence on foreign countries, and this project will help support long-term efforts to lower energy costs for Wisconsin families,” said Congressman Wied.

Background: Wisconsin relies on refined fuels to power our transportation network, making them a cornerstone of the state’s $450 billion economy. U.S. Venture, headquartered in Appleton, WI, has supplied Wisconsinites with gasoline and diesel fuel for more than 70 years. In 2016, a 110-mile pipeline that moved this fuel from Milwaukee to the Green Bay Terminal Complex was decommissioned, threatening the fuel supply for Northeastern Wisconsin and Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. Since the pipeline closed, diesel-powered tanker trucks have hauled fuel from Milwaukee to Green Bay. On average, 75 tanker trucks per day travel the I-43 corridor in Eastern Wisconsin to supply the Green Bay terminal. Access to a reliable, refined fuel supply remains essential to our businesses and families. With support from the U.S. Department of Transportation, U.S. Venture and the Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT) will extend a fuel line at the General Mitchell International Airport (MKE) six miles along I-794 to Port Milwaukee and add additional fuel storage at Port Milwaukee. This will allow fuel to be loaded onto barges at Port Milwaukee for transport across our underutilized Lake Michigan maritime highway to Green Bay. A single barge can carry approximately 4.2 million gallons of fuel, or the equivalent of 500 tanker truck loads. Barging fuel from Milwaukee to Green Bay would significantly reduce exhaust, noise, congestion, and road wear. This project would also bring in more revenue for both Port Milwaukee and the Port of Green Bay, in alignment with the goals and priorities of the ports and WisDOT. Further, it would increase the region’s access to domestically produced fuel and protect the reliability of our essential fuel supply from the weather disruptions that often occur in our state.

Last year, Congressman Wied led Congressmen Bryan Steil (WI-01), Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05), Glenn Grothman (WI-06), and Tom Tiffany (WI-07) in a letter to the USDOT to advocate for this grant funding.

title: Hickenlooper Demands Answers About ICE’s Secretive Domestic Air Transfer Network
text:
ICE’s domestic air network has exploded to over 18,000 flights since Trump took office, with zero transparency or accountability into operations and costs

Repeated transfers can disrupt access to counsel, medical care, and pressure individuals to self-deport, with some detainees being transferred 15+ times

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper demanded answers from the Department of Homeland Security, sending a letter questioning the substantial increase in domestic transfer flights that move detainees in Immigration and Custom Enforcement (ICE) custody between ICE detention centers and deportation staging facilities.

In his letter, Hickenlooper highlighted the number of so-called “shuttle” flights carrying detainees between immigration detention centers and deportation staging facilities has increased substantially since President Trump took office, with over 18,000 domestic shuttle flights reportedly conducted since January 2025. The frequency with which individual detainees are transferred has also increased. A 2026 investigation identified detainees transferred nine, twelve, and thirteen times. In another reported case, between May and July 2025, a 20-year-old man with no criminal record was transferred 15 times between facilities in Florida, California, Arizona, Hawaii, and Louisiana. This expanded network and frequency creates more confusion and chaos for detainees – a majority of which have never been convicted of a violent crime – that can disrupt access to legal counsel, cut off communication with family and community members, and delay medical care.

“We are concerned by the scale and frequency of these transfers, the costs to taxpayers, and the impact repeated transfers can have on detainees’ access to legal counsel, medical care, and other essential services,” wrote Hickenlooper. “Repeated transfers have significant consequences for detainees and their families. Transfers often disrupt communication with counsel, delay attorneys’ and families’ abilities to locate detainees (particularly due to lags and policy changes pertaining to ICE’s Online Detainee Locator System), and interfere with continuity of medical care. Detainees have also reported difficulties accessing commissary funds following transfers.”

By analyzing millions of flight records, reviewing federal detention data, examining court filings and documenting specific flights, investigative reporters led by local Colorado station 9News/KUSA-TV found a vast domestic transportation system that ICE uses to move detainees from one part of the country to another, often multiple times, before those detainees are deported or released.

According to Human Rights First, 8,721 domestic transfer flights were recorded in 2025, compared to 3,975 in 2024. In July 2026, 1,363 flights were recorded – a 75 percent increase from July 2025. In August 2026, 1,267 flights were recorded across 56 U.S. cities. Between January and July 2025, 12 percent of detainees were transferred four or more times.

In addition, Hickenlooper demanded transparency into the costs of these more than 18,000 domestic shuttle flights to the American taxpayer. Just six multi-leg flights chartered by DHS to transport detainees to and from Guantanamo Bay in 2026 cost $979,000, according to a 2026 Department of Defense Inspector General report.

Watch Hickenlooper’s interview with 9News HERE.

Hickenlooper requested written responses to the following questions:

Domestic transfer flights: How many domestic transfer flights did ICE conduct between January 1, 2025, and September 1, 2026? Please provide a monthly breakdown, including the departure and arrival cities for each leg of the transfer and the cost of each leg of these flights.

Purpose of transfers: What percentage of domestic transfer flights were to removal staging facilities, and what percentage were to other detention facilities?

Facility capacity: For domestic transfer flights to other detention facilities, how many transfers originated from facilities operating below 85 percent of capacity? Please provide the number of transfers by originating facility alongside the monthly average daily population of the facility at the time of the transfer.

Frequency of transfers: How many individuals in ICE custody were placed on domestic transfer flights more than once during this period? Please provide the number and percentage of detainees transferred one, two, three, four, or more times.

Continuity of services: What policies and procedures does ICE use to ensure that transferred detainees maintain uninterrupted access to counsel, medical care, prescribed medications, and commissary funds?

Access to counsel: If an individual transferred to a different ICE facility has a pending virtual attorney visit scheduled, how does ICE ensure that the meeting can take place? Additionally, how does ICE ensure that detainees who are transferred don’t have to re-register their attorney for legal calls upon arrival at new facilities?

Medical care: What is ICE’s policy when a receiving facility does not include a detainee’s current medication in its formulary? Under that circumstance, what options is the detainee provided in terms of medical care?

Ground transportation: Between January 1, 2025 and September 1, 2026, how much has ICE spent on moving detainees between ICE facilities via ground transportation?

Transfers by AOR: For each ICE Area of Responsibility (AOR), please provide monthly counts of transfers out of the AOR involving individuals without a final order of removal. Please disaggregate these figures by air and ground transportation and include the estimated cost associated with these transfers.

Hickenlooper has been outspoken in the face of ICE’s lawlessness and demanded a top-to-bottom overhaul of the agency to stop ICE from terrorizing our communities. Hickenlooper also voted against the DHS funding bill because it failed to overhaul ICE. He has consistently pushed for more oversight andtransparency for federal immigration enforcement efforts, and has worked to help families desperately searching for loved ones arrested by ICE. In January, Hickenlooper spoke on the Senate floor to denounce the horrifying killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, condemn the reports that families in Eagle County found “death cards” left in the cars of family members taken by ICE agents, and to demand the overhaul of ICE. He’s shown up at ICE facilities previously to conduct congressional oversight visits and raise concerns about ICE disregarding due process. He helped launch an investigation into ICE’s unlawful obstruction of congressional oversight, introduced legislation to ban ICE from wearing masks, and pushed to cut back the excessive funding that MAGA Republicans gave to ICE.

title: Cammack’s Push to Crack Down on Prison Cellphones Gains Ground at FCC
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, which oversees the FCC, today welcomed a major win in her push to shut down contraband cellphones in prisons. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr announced the agency will vote next month on final rules that, for the first time, would allow state and local correctional facilities to use targeted cellphone-jamming technology. The Order will be voted on at the FCC’s November 19 Open Meeting.

Rep. Cammack has worked the issue on multiple fronts. She met with Chairman Carr on the issue and met several times with Florida Department of Corrections leaders to work through the threat contraband phones pose inside the state’s prisons and find a resolution. Last year, she joined Congressman David Kustoff (TN-08) and other colleagues in a letter urging Chairman Carr to advance the rulemaking and give correctional institutions additional tools, warning that inmates have used these devices to orchestrate criminal activity from behind prison walls.

“Contraband cellphones turn prison cells into command centers. Inmates use them to order hits and run criminal enterprises from behind bars,” said Congresswoman Kat Cammack. “That threat lands especially close to home in our district, which has roughly 15 state prisons and correctional institutions, more than any other congressional district in America. Giving our correctional officers the ability to shut these phones off will save lives and cut the crime being run from the inside. We worked this issue directly with Chairman Carr and with Florida’s Department of Corrections leaders, and I’m grateful the Chairman is moving on it. Now Congress needs to finish the fight and make this authority permanent.”

"The criminal use of contraband cell phones is a growing crisis that demands immediate action to maintain public safety and keep our officers and institutions safe," said Florida Department of Corrections Secretary Richard Comerford. "Florida is thankful for the leadership of FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, Representative Kat Cammack, Governor Ron DeSantis, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, and all of our correctional partners for recognizing this security threat and working to counteract this criminal enterprise."

Contraband cellphones remain a widespread problem in correctional facilities nationwide. A 2024 study found that prison authorities recovered more than 25,000 cellphones in a single year, with two participating facilities each recovering more than 6,000 devices. While the FCC has authorized other technologies to combat contraband phones, it has never before allowed jamming.

Under the proposed final order, jamming would be an option for state and local correctional facilities, and no facility would be required to use it. Facilities pursuing jamming must meet technical standards and pass testing to show the system does not cause harmful interference outside designated areas. Jamming would be limited to a Commission-authorized containment area where wireless device use is already prohibited. Wireless carriers, FirstNet, public safety coordinators, and 911 authorities would receive advance notice of on-site testing, and nearby communities would be notified before deployment.

The FCC will also seek public comment on additional measures to close loopholes that allow contraband cellphones to operate on other frequencies, strengthen protections for public safety communications, and explore potential “quiet zones” around correctional facilities.

The announcement follows congressional efforts to address the issue, including the Cellphone Jamming Reform Act, introduced by Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR) and Congressman David Kustoff (R-TN), which would establish permanent statutory authority for correctional facilities to deploy cellphone-jamming technology.

title: Carbajal Joins Garamendi in Opposing Trump Administration Proposal to Use Cal Poly Maritime Academy Ship for Mass Deportations
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), top Democrat of the House Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, joined U.S. Representative John Garamendi (D-CA-08) in demanding that Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin discard any plans to use ships for deportation. They cited “enormous operational, safety and legal challenges” and warned that deportations by sea would “take days” and “require many security personnel and cost the taxpayer millions of dollars.” Carbajal and Garamendi’s demands come after New York Times reporting revealed that DHS is considering using ships for mass deportations and identified Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s training ship, the Golden Bear, as a possible vessel.

“If the Trump administration follows through on this proposal, it would represent another escalation of their brutal immigration enforcement tactics. ICE already operates without sufficient transparency or public accountability, and deploying maritime vessels as floating prisons will only open the door to potentially more abuses. As the top Democrat overseeing the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee and a Senior Member of the Armed Services Committee, I am proud to stand with Congressman John Garamendi and my colleagues in opposing the use of the Golden Bear — or any vessel — for mass deportations,”said Rep. Carbajal.

“Mark my words, Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, and ICE will never use the Golden Bear for their mass deportation agenda,” said Rep. Garamendi. “Not only is deporting migrants by ship impractical, but it’s also deeply inhumane. We have already seen how Trump’s reckless diversion of our government and military resources to support immigration enforcement costs our military readiness. This move would be the same for our sealift capacity. I’m proud to stand with Congressman Carbajal on this issue and I will continue to use every lever of oversight at my disposal to make sure we halt Trump and Mullin’s ICE from escalating their already inhumane and cruel mass deportation agenda. Hands off the Golden Bear.”

The full letter can be found HERE.

Background

Carbajal is a leader in fighting the Trump administration’s extreme immigration policies.

In October 2026, Carbajal visited the Santa Maria ICE facility — marking his third visit since 2025 — as part of his ongoing investigation into the recent surge in ICE activity on the Central Coast.

Carbajal visited the Adelanto ICE processing facility in May 2026 to meet with detainees, three of whom are Central Coast constituents. The Congressman also assessed conditions in the facility and inquired about the reported deaths of detainees.

Carbajal is a co-sponsor of the No Secret Police Act, which would require law enforcement officers and agents of DHS engaged in border security and civil immigration enforcement to clearly display identification and insignia when detaining or arresting individuals and to ban them from using home-made, non-tactical masks.

title: Smith: Alexander brothers’ 30-year sentences underscore urgent need to reauthorize landmark anti-trafficking law to assist victims
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), author of the landmark Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 (TVPA) (PL 106-386), issued the following statement after Alon, Oren, and Tal Alexander were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for their roles in a decade-long sex trafficking and sexual abuse scheme:

“These sentences send a powerful message: wealth, privilege, and social status do not put anyone above the law. The Alexander brothers used their resources and influence to lure women and minors into situations where they were drugged, sexually assaulted, and raped. Their victims deserve justice, and I commend the courage of the survivors who came forward to help secure these convictions.

“When I authored the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000, we established a landmark federal framework to investigate and prosecute human traffickers, impose serious criminal and civil penalties, and protect victims. The federal sex trafficking statutes at the heart of this case reflect that framework, as well as the critical role that Congress has played in strengthening our Nation’s response to these horrific crimes.

“Despite this progress, we must continue to strengthen our laws, support survivors, and prevent exploitation before it happens. That is precisely why Congress must pass my new, bipartisan anti-human trafficking law, the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2025 (HR 1144).

“This legislation would reauthorize and strengthen critical anti-trafficking programs and funding across the federal government, support robust investigations and prosecutions, and help survivors rebuild their lives through a number of support services.

“HR 1144 would also strengthen prevention efforts to protect children from human trafficking and sexual abuse, including by tightening the torniquet on the child sex tourism industry.

“The Alexander brothers’ sentences are another reminder of why we must remain steadfast in our mission to end human trafficking. The United States must continue to champion this critical issue by holding perpetrators accountable, protecting the vulnerable, and ensuring that both law enforcement and survivors have the resources they need.

“I urge my colleagues to immediately advance HR 1144 and renew our Nation’s commitment to preventing trafficking, protecting victims, and prosecuting traffickers.”

title: Congressman García on the Life and Legacy of Dolores Huerta
text:
CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) issued the following statement honoring Dolores Huerta’s life and legacy:

“Today, our hearts are heavy with grief as we mourn a giant of the labor, feminist, and civil rights movements. Dolores Huerta was one of the fiercest and wisest women I have ever known. As co-founder of the United Farm Workers, she poured her soul into leading the boycotts, strikes, and relentless contract negotiations that improved the lives of countless farm workers.”

“A trailblazing feminist, she opened Gloria Steinem’s eyes to the critical power of intersectionality across race and class, embracing the deeply personal fight for reproductive rights and helping raise awareness among Latinas about the right to choose.

“For over seven decades, she fought tirelessly for the voiceless, organizing marginalized communities for economic, political, and social justice. Through the Dolores Huerta Foundation she trained grassroots leaders and inspired generations to stand up and speak out.

“I am forever grateful for her friendship and for her support when I ran for mayor of Chicago in 2014. Walking the campaign trail with Dolores was a learning experience. She was persuasive and could lighten up every conversation with voters.

“Dolores gave us the rallying cry that echoes in our hearts forever: “¡Sí se puede!” (Yes, we can!)—because in her world, no obstacle was too great and no hope was out of reach.”

“When the painful revelations of the abuse she endured at the hands of Cesar Chavez came to light, our hearts broke for the quiet burden she carried for decades. Yet, in true Dolores fashion, she refused to let pain define her; instead, she continued to transform -heartache into a powerful, unstoppable force for change.”

“Dolores will be remembered for her unbreakable spirit and tireless fight for working people. Rest in power, my dear friend.”

A video clip of Rep. García talking about Dolores can be found on this link.

title: El Congresista García Sobre la Vida y el legado de Dolores Huerta
text:
CHICAGO — El Congresista Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) emitió la siguiente declaración en honor a la vida y el legado de Dolores Huerta:

“Hoy, con nuestros corazones llenos de pesar, honramos a una figura monumental de los movimientos laborales, feministas y de derechos civiles. Dolores Huerta ha sido una de las mujeres más valientes y sabias que he conocido. Como cofundadora del Sindicato de Trabajadores Agrícolas (United Farm Workers), dedicó su alma a liderar boicots, huelgas e intensas negociaciones contractuales que mejoraron la vida de innumerables trabajadores agrícolas”.

“Como pionera del feminismo, ayudó a Gloria Steinem a comprender el poder fundamental de la interseccionalidad —que abarca tanto la raza como la clase social—, al tiempo que abanderaba la lucha profundamente personal por los derechos reproductivos y creaba conciencia entre las mujeres latinas sobre su derecho a decidir”.

“Durante más de siete décadas, luchó incansablemente por quienes no tenían voz, organizando a comunidades marginadas en busca de la justicia económica, política y social. A través de la Fundación Dolores Huerta, formó a líderes comunitarios e inspiró a generaciones a alzar la voz y defender sus convicciones”.

“Estaré siempre agradecido por su amistad y por el apoyo que me brindó cuando me postulé para la alcaldía de Chicago en 2014. Hacer campaña junto a Dolores fue una experiencia de gran aprendizaje; ella poseía una gran capacidad de persuasión y lograba infundir alegría en cada conversación con los votantes”.

“Dolores nos regaló un grito de lucha que resonará en nuestros corazones para siempre: ‘¡Sí se puede!’ Porque, en su visión del mundo, ningún obstáculo era demasiado grande y ninguna esperanza estaba fuera de alcance”.

“Cuando salieron a la luz las dolorosas revelaciones sobre los abusos que sufrió a manos de César Chávez, nuestros corazones se rompieron al conocer la carga silenciosa que ella llevó durante décadas. Sin embargo, fiel a su esencia, Dolores no permitió que el dolor la definiera; por el contrario, transformó ese sufrimiento en una fuerza poderosa e imparable a favor del cambio”.

“Dolores será recordada por su espíritu inquebrantable y su lucha incansable en favor de los trabajadores. Descansa, querida amiga”.

title: HECHO Applauds Ciscomani's Bill Establishing Chiricahua as America's 64th National Park
text:
Tucson, AZ - A week after President Trump signed Representative Juan Ciscomani’s Chiricahua National Park Act (H.R. 6380) into law, Hispanics Enjoying Camping, Hunting, and the Outdoors (HECHO) and its Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council members are celebrating the historic designation of Chiricahua as Arizona’s fourth national park. Following nearly a decade of bipartisan collaboration, the designation recognizes the ecological, cultural, recreational, and economic significance of this unique landscape while creating new opportunities for conservation, tourism, and surrounding communities.

HECHO, an organization dedicated to ensuring Hispanic communities have a voice in public lands and conservation decisions, joined local leaders, conservation advocates, veterans, and community members in recognizing the significance of this milestone.

Their unique perspectives reflect the importance of protecting Arizona’s natural heritage while ensuring future generations can experience the beauty, history, and opportunities that Chiricahua has to offer.

"I’m so grateful for our incredible partners, including HECHO, who worked across party lines to advocate for Chiricahua’s national park designation. This decade-long effort built the momentum and garnered the federal attention needed to get this across the finish line," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "HECHO’s commitment to conservation and its work bringing diverse voices to the table helped demonstrate the broad, bipartisan support behind this historic designation. This achievement will preserve Arizona’s rich heritage for generations to come. As we celebrate our nation’s 250th anniversary, I cannot think of a better way to honor our history and natural beauty than by welcoming Arizona’s fourth national park, and the second national park in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District."

"This is a moment worth celebrating, not only because Chiricahua is now Arizona’s fourth national park and the enactment marks the culmination of years of work, but also because of how we got here. We are especially grateful to Congressman Juan Ciscomani for championing this effort and his leadership in bringing Chiricahua the national recognition it deserves for its ecological, cultural, recreational, and economic significance. His work, alongside Representatives Greg Stanton and Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego, shows what we can accomplish when Republicans and Democrats come together around our shared public lands. At a time when our country feels deeply divided, this is a meaningful example of finding common ground for conservation." — Camilla Simon, Executive Director of HECHO

"I proudly supported the Chiricahua National Park Act, and I’m thrilled to have been part of the effort to make Chiricahua Arizona’s newest national park. As a combat veteran, I know firsthand the healing that can come from spending time on our public lands. A national park in my own backyard has given me a place to find that healing, and I’m excited for more people to have that opportunity at Chiricahua. This designation will bring so much to the surrounding communities, not only economic and recreational opportunities, but also the joy, connection and healing that these special places can provide." — Eduardo Ramos, veteran, hunter and HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council

"Chiricahua is one of those places you have to see with your own eyes to truly understand. Its landscape is breathtaking, and no matter how many times I visit, that feeling never changes. I had the privilege of being in Washington, D.C., advocating for Chiricahua when we learned that the bill had passed Congress, and being there for that moment was incredibly special. Now, to see what we advocated for become a reality with the President’s signature is something I’ll never forget. I’m proud that more people will have the opportunity to experience this extraordinary place." — Eddy Corona, President of Outdoor Experience 4 All and member of HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council

"The Chiricahuas in southeastern Arizona are a true hidden gem. Having hiked and camped there in the past, I can attest to its spectacular rock formations, incredible biodiversity, endless night skies, and abundant wildlife. This designation will boost the local economy and encourage more visitors to experience this unique landscape." — Patty Contreras, Arizona State Representative and member of HECHO’s Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council

"I’ve explored the outdoors throughout Arizona, but the Chiricahuas hold a particularly special place in my heart. I feel a deep spiritual connection to this landscape unlike anywhere else in the state. From the incredible rock formations to the abundance of wildlife, the Chiricahuas are truly one of a kind. It’s one of the few places in Arizona where I’ve been fortunate enough to encounter such a remarkable diversity of wildlife. It’s one of Arizona’s best-kept secrets, and I hope it never loses the qualities that make it so special. I’m excited about this step forward and hopeful that National Park designation will bring greater resources, and lasting protections to this extraordinary place." — Adriana Garcia Maximiliano, Hispanic Conservation Leadership Council member

"The first time I visited Chiricahua with my family, I was struck by its extraordinary beauty, rich history, and the deep significance it holds for so many Tribal communities. If I had to describe it in one word, it would be magical. As someone who has seen firsthand the benefits of having a national park near our community, I know how meaningful this designation could be for southern Arizona. It will create opportunities for local businesses, bring new tourism revenue, and strengthen the Southwest as a destination for people who come to experience our incredible public lands. But beyond the economic benefits, this is about reaffirming our commitment to conserving these special places for generations to come. National parks allow us to build a stronger economic future for our communities without sacrificing the landscapes, wildlife, and history that make them so extraordinary." — Sarah Benatar, Coconino County Treasurer

"The balancing rocks at Chiricahua make it one of the most unique and beautiful places on Earth, which is exactly why I’m thrilled to see it become Arizona’s fourth national park. This historic designation will help protect and preserve Chiricahua’s natural beauty for generations to come, while boosting tourism from around the world and growing our economy." — Arizona House Democratic Leader Oscar De Los Santos

HECHO works to ensure Hispanic communities have a meaningful voice in the conservation of America’s public lands. Through its advocacy and partnerships, the organization helps advance conservation efforts that reflect the needs and values of local communities. HECHO is committed to protecting the natural and cultural heritage of the Southwest for future generations.

title: Rep. Crane’s Office Helps Arizonans Recover More Than $12 Million Owed by Federal Agencies
text:
Since January 2023, the office of Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) has helped return $12,181,269.26 to constituents of Arizona’s Second Congressional District. Over that same period, his staff has resolved 4,017 individual cases. This money is not new federal spending. Rather, it reflects delayed or stalled payments Arizonans were already owed, such as tax refunds, retirement and disability benefits, and veterans’ compensation.

As a Member of Congress, Rep. Crane can contact federal agencies on behalf of those he represents. When residents run into problems with the Internal Revenue Service, Social Security Administration, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and others, his team helps them clear bureaucratic hurdles. This work often involves checking the status of a claim, identifying paperwork errors, and following up for an answer.

However, there are limits to what casework can accomplish. Staff cannot override an agency’s decision, intervene in court proceedings, or guarantee a specific outcome. Instead, the goal is to ensure each case receives a fair and timely review. Some matters, such as driver’s licenses and unemployment insurance, are handled at the state level. In those situations, residents are directed to the proper state agency.

To expand access, Rep. Crane’s team has held mobile office hours 232 times. Because the district covers a large portion of Arizona, a round trip to Prescott may take most of the day. These local visits bring assistance closer to home.

To open a case, constituents must first sign a privacy release form. Under the Privacy Act of 1974, agencies generally require this written consent before sharing a person’s records with a congressional office. If you need support navigating the federal government, please click here to get started. You can also call the Prescott District Office at (928) 286-5338 to speak directly with a caseworker.

title: WATCH: Davids Highlights Mounting Economic Pressures on Kansas Families, Demands Solutions to Lower Costs
text:
Today, Representative Sharice Davids (KS-03) and Defend America Action hosted a virtual press briefing alongside Kansas House Minority Leader Brandon Woodard and healthcare policy expert Jessica Schubel to address the growing cost-of-living crisis hitting households across the state.

"Every day, Kansans are making impossible choices between paying for groceries, filling up their gas tanks, or keeping their health coverage. I was raised by a single mom, so I get it. But too many politicians in D.C. are completely out of touch with what that feels like,” said Davids. “We don't need political games or policies that treat Kansas families and farmers like collateral damage. We need common-sense, bipartisan solutions that lower costs and give everyday people a fair shot to get ahead."

During the call, Davids highlighted how rising grocery bills, record utility and fuel prices, housing crunches, and federal healthcare cuts are squeezing working families, agricultural producers, and small business owners. Grounding her remarks in stories from local constituents — including a Kansas pastor overwhelmed by community requests for emergency bill assistance — Davids called for pragmatic, bipartisan action to lower everyday expenses rather than partisan D.C. games.

A full recording of today’s virtual press briefing can be watched HERE.

Recent economic data and state reporting detail the compounding cost burdens facing Kansas households and key industries:

Rising Cost of Living & Grocery Prices: The average Kansas household has paid an estimated $4,400 more for everyday essentials since early 2025. Grocery costs remain elevated, with ground beef hitting a record high of over $7 per pound and local food banks like Harvesters reporting record demand for assistance.

Kansas Home Insurance & Housing Crunch: Kansas homeowners now pay the fourth-highest home insurance premiums in the country — averaging $4,095 annually (71 percent above the national average). Meanwhile, a Kansas worker must earn $21.70 an hour to afford a modest two-bedroom rental, and homebuilders estimate that federal tariffs add nearly $10,900 in material costs per new home built.

Agricultural Sector Strain: Spiking diesel prices and global supply disruptions caused fertilizer costs to double during planting season, costing Kansas farmers an estimated $83.2 million more in fuel expenses. Concurrently, policy changes waiving foreign beef tariffs have undercut domestic producers in Kansas’s $11.7 billion cattle sector.

Healthcare & ACA Premium Spikes: Recent federal budget cuts stripped healthcare coverage from thousands of Kansans, while the expiration of ACA tax credits caused insurance premiums to skyrocket for over 182,000 Kansans — resulting in an average 181 percent premium increase for impacted enrollees. Over 15 Kansas healthcare facilities face budget cuts, reduced service capacity, or closure threats.

Energy & Fuel Costs: Regular gas in Kansas reached $4.00 per gallon last week (up 44.8 percent from last year), while diesel hit an all-time state record of $6.25 per gallon on September 22. In addition, state regulators approved an energy rate increase, further raising monthly utility bills for Kansas families.

Davids has worked to lower costs for Kansans, including capping insulin at $35 for seniors, lowering prescription drug prices through Medicare negotiation, expanding affordable housing supply, strengthening Kansas agriculture and local food systems, supporting year-round E15 fuel access to lower prices at the pump, and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits that help families afford health coverage. She has fought reckless tariffs and extreme Medicaid cuts that are closing rural hospitals and increasing healthcare costs for Kansas families.

Davids was raised by a single mom who served in the Army for 20 years. She knows what it’s like to struggle to put food on the table, stretch every dollar, and make difficult choices between paying for groceries, healthcare, gas, or rent. That experience continues to shape her focus on lowering costs for working families and making sure everyday people — not just billionaires and large corporations — have a fair shot at getting ahead.

title: DeLauro Statement on Death of Dolores Huerta
text:
Today, Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) released a statement following news that Dolores Huerta, a champion in the American labor movement, passed away:

“Dolores Huerta was a giant of the labor movement. As co-founder of the United Farm Workers, she spent her life fighting to ensure a safe workplace and fair wages were guaranteed rights for all workers. From the grape boycott, which I participated in, to the first law that gave Californian farmworkers the right to bargain collectively – she changed the course of the American labor movement.

Being in her company was a reminder that every fight won in the labor movement was won by workers who did not give up or take no for an answer. Dolores never gave up. And neither will we.

title: Finstad Sends Letter to FEMA Administrator Calling for Action Regarding Federal Disaster Mitigation and Response Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) joined U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN), and Representatives Betty McCollum (MN-04), Pete Stauber (MN-08), Angie Craig (MN-02), and Kelly Morrison (MN-03) in sending a letter to Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Administrator Cameron Hamilton regarding prolonged delays and disruptions to federal disaster mitigation and response funding for Minnesota communities. FEMA has not awarded any of Minnesota’s 11 Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) applications related to the 2024 storms and flooding, pending grants which would support mitigation projects in Blue Earth and Rock Counties and the cities of Wabasha and Winona.

Last week, Congressman Finstad spoke with FEMA Administrator Hamilton, discussed the status of these projects, and requested a timeline for Wabasha’s HMGP for their generator lift project, Blue Earth County’s HMGP for home buyouts due to the June 2024 flooding, and Rock County’s Buffalo Ridge Regional Railroad Authority Public Assistance Grant.

The letter reads:

Dear Administrator Hamilton:

We write to urge you to address prolonged delays and disruptions to federal disaster mitigation and response funding for Minnesota, which assist our constituents recovering and preparing for disasters. We ask that you quickly approve these grant applications and move forward with obligations and payments for pending grants.

Minnesota has submitted eleven Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) applications related to record storms and flooding in 2024 (DR-4797-MN), none of which have received an award. Now more than two years since the disaster, FEMA has not provided the state of Minnesota’s Homeland Security and Emergency Management (HSEM) Division with a timeline for decisions on these applications. This funding is crucial for advancing recovery and mitigation work across the state, and its delay is straining local governments already operating under constrained resources. Applicants for pending HMGP grants include the cities of Wabasha, Rockville, Waterville, and Winona, as well as the Bassett Creek Watershed Management Commission and Le Sueur and Blue Earth counties. In particular, Blue Earth County residents have waited more than two years for FEMA’s decision on much-needed funding related to the partial failure of Rapidan Dam in June 2024. Also pending are HMGP applications that support state disaster mitigation capacity as well as updates to hazard mitigation plans for White Earth Nation and 13 counties: Itasca, Kandiyohi, Carlton, Cass, Dodge, Le Sueur, McLeod, Renville, Koochiching, Mahnomen, Rock, Stevens, and Traverse.

Funding delays extend further beyond these mitigation grants related to the 2024 flooding and storms. Minnesota’s FY23 Building Resilient Infrastructure & Communities (BRIC) management costs remain unpaid and without an update since May 2026. Those funds support state emergency management staff salaries. Public Assistance (DR-4531-MN) to reimburse Minnesota counties and hospitals for pandemic-related costs remains pending with FEMA’s deadline to close all associated costs approaching. We share our constituents’ concerns about FEMA’s ability to obligate and pay these funds within the required timeline, leaving Minnesota on the hook for emergency protective measures and other costs that the federal government is obligated to reimburse.

We urge you to act swiftly to deliver these resources to Minnesota communities and provide a definitive timeline for these funding decisions and process, as well as engage with the state’s HSEM Division to clarify the criteria and process for the administration’s review of these grants. If there are any concerns or barriers that would prevent payment, we request a written explanation and timeline for corrective action.

Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. Impacted communities repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but timely federal assistance is critical to recovery and mitigation efforts. Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

Sincerely,

Amy Klobuchar, United States Senator

Tina Smith, United States Senator

Betty McCollum, Member of Congress

Pete Stauber, Member of Congress

Angie Craig, Member of Congress

Brad Finstad, Member of Congress

Kelly Morrison, Member of Congress

title: Fong Announces $2.575 Million Investment in Cutting-Edge BioSynthetic Capabilities at China Lake
text:
RIDGECREST, CA — Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) announced that the Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) at Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake has been awarded $2.575 million through the Department of War’s Central Laboratory Investment Program (CLIP) to develop BioSynthetic Capabilities for Fuels, Polymers, and Energetics.

“NAWCWD China Lake is the most advanced military laboratory and test enterprise in the world,” said Congressman Fong. “This investment reinforces the innovation from China Lake and ensures our community continues to lead the way. By building cutting-edge biosynthetic capabilities here, we are strengthening our domestic supply chains, reducing reliance on adversaries for critical materials, and ensuring our warfighters have access to the most innovative technologies available. This investment is a win for China Lake, the men and women serving our country at this critical installation, our local economy, and our national security.”

This investment will help American scientists and engineers at NAWCWD China Lake develop new biological processes to manufacture the fuels, materials, and chemicals our military needs. Rather than relying on supply chains that run through China or other adversaries for critical materials, this technology allows us to grow and produce them ourselves using biological methods. It is a critical step in bringing the manufacturing of key defense materials back to American soil, using cutting-edge science to do it.

The CLIP award will fund the acquisition of advanced instrumentation, like robotics and high-throughput screening equipment, to enable the rapid discovery and creation of novel enzymes for producing fuels, polymers, and energetics. The new facility will directly support key Department of War programs including the Tri-Service Biotechnology for a Resilient Supply Chain (T-BRSC) program and the Distributed Bioindustrial Manufacturing Investment Program (DBMIP), both of which align directly with National Defense Strategy priorities.

Critically, this investment supports domestic production of chemical precursors that are currently sourced from adversarial nations, reducing vulnerability in defense supply chains. It also helps bridge the “valley of death” between early-stage enzyme discovery and the production of sufficient materials for further technical readiness testing. This gap has prevented laboratory breakthroughs from translating into real-world capabilities.

CLIP funds the development of high-priority science and technology infrastructure across the Department of War’s research and engineering enterprise. Out of thirty proposals received nationally, NAWCWD China Lake’s BioSynthetic Capabilities proposal was one of only four selected.

title: Gallagher Announces More Than $60 Million in Federal Funding for Yreka Western Railroad
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) announced that the U.S. Department of Transportation has selected the Yreka Western Railroad Rehabilitation Project in Siskiyou County to receive more than $60.2 million in federal funding to modernize critical rail infrastructure connecting Yreka and Montague.

The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration's Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, will support the rehabilitation of approximately 8.5 miles of railroad track, improving safety and reliability along the line.

“Rural communities like Yreka and Montague deserve safe, reliable infrastructure that supports their local economies,” said Congressman Gallagher. “This is a major investment in Siskiyou County that will help bring aging railroad infrastructure up to modern standards and strengthen the transportation network our communities depend on. I'm pleased to see these federal dollars coming back to the North State.”

The project will replace aging rails and railroad ties, upgrade track foundations, and make improvements to bridges and nine railroad crossings. These upgrades will bring the line from Federal Railroad Administration Excepted Track status to Class 2 standards, allowing it to accommodate railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds.

The federal grant totals $60,230,094, with Yreka Western Railroad providing a 25 percent non-federal cost share. The project was selected for funding covering project development, final design, and construction.

The investment is part of a federal program focused on improving railroad safety and reliability, with dedicated support for infrastructure projects in rural communities.

title: Rep. Gallagher Highlights Legislative Accomplishments and Early Results for California's North State
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) today highlighted his legislative accomplishments and constituent service efforts since being sworn into Congress in June of 2026, underscoring his commitment to delivering results for California's North State.

In his first several months in office, Gallagher has made lowering costs for California families a top priority, introducing legislation aimed at making housing more affordable and reducing the financial burdens facing North State communities. He has introduced 10 bills, cosponsored more than 58 pieces of legislation, and co-led 15 bipartisan efforts to deliver practical solutions for Northern California.

"When I was sworn into Congress, I made a promise that the North State would have a strong voice in Washington," said Congressman Gallagher. "That means fighting for reliable water, protecting our communities from catastrophic wildfires, and making sure rural Northern California gets the attention it deserves. We've made a strong start, but there's plenty more work to do."

Among Gallagher's legislative accomplishments is the bipartisan Revitalizing Rural America Act, introduced alongside Congressman Mike Thompson, which would expand access to rural health care, boost support for local agriculture, and make it easier for small communities to secure federal funding. The legislation also includes provisions aimed at making housing more affordable and easing financial burdens on rural families.

Gallagher also introduced the Affordable Power for Host Communities Act, which would provide a 20% discount on electricity bills for consumers in communities that host renewable energy facilities. The legislation recognizes Northern California's significant contributions to the state's renewable energy production while ensuring local residents benefit through lower energy costs.

Additionally, the House passed Gallagher's resolution to overturn California's Commercial Harbor Craft rule, which would impose costly new regulations on vessels operating in California’s ports and waterways. Overturning the rule would prevent $2.5 billion in additional costs from being passed along to American consumers, thus helping keep everyday goods more affordable for California families.

Beyond introducing new legislation, Gallagher assumed sponsorship of two bills previously championed by the late Congressman Doug LaMalfa: the Orland Project Water Management Act, which addresses water management needs in the North State, and the Pacific Flyway Habitat Enhancement Act, which supports habitat conservation and restoration efforts. Through carrying these bills forward, Gallagher is continuing LaMalfa’s efforts toward priorities important to the North State.

Gallagher also helped secure nearly $160 million for water and wastewater infrastructure projects across the district in the House-passed Water Resources Development Act. The proposed investments would support improvements to aging infrastructure and strengthen essential services in rural communities.

His work has also included efforts to support wildfire survivors. Gallagher's AB 2700, legislation he originally introduced while serving in the California State Assembly, was signed into law. The measure establishes a path for wildfire victims to receive the remaining 30% of the compensation they are owed by PG&E.

"Legislation is only part of the job. We also have a responsibility to make sure Washington is working for the people we represent," Gallagher continued. "Whether it's helping a constituent receive benefits they've been waiting on or fighting for infrastructure investments, our office is focused on getting results."

Gallagher's constituent services team has helped return more than $6 million to constituents through assistance with federal agencies and outstanding benefits or reimbursements. Our team has successfully helped veterans, wildfire victims, and our constituents get the government service they deserve.

Gallagher has also sent 34 letters to federal agencies addressing issues affecting Northern California. In a bipartisan letter, Gallagher urged the Department of Health and Human Services to reconsider proposed changes to Head Start that could weaken early childhood services in rural communities. The lawmakers highlighted concerns raised by local providers, warning that reduced staffing standards and changes to developmental screening requirements could make it harder for vulnerable children to receive the support that they need.

Gallagher also sent a letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, calling for a review of federal wine-labeling rules that allow products labeled “American” to contain up to 25 percent imported wine without disclosing its foreign origin. He raised concerns about tax treatment that could disadvantage domestic winegrape growers and urged expanded access to international markets, including India and Vietnam, to create more opportunities for California producers. He has also worked hand in hand with the Administration and Office of the United States Trade Representative on trade deals that give walnut growers better access to markets and fairer prices.

"The North State has a strong voice in Congress, and I'm going to keep using it to fight for the hardworking people who call this region home," Gallagher said. "We're just getting started."

title: “Hands off the Golden Bear”: Garamendi, Carbajal Demand DHS Not Consider Deportations on Ships
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressmen John Garamendi (CA-08) and Salud Carbajal (CA-24), two senior members of the House Armed Services Committee and Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, demanded that Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin discard any plans to use ships for deportation. They cited “enormous operational, safety and legal challenges” and warned that deportations by sea would “take days” and “require many security personnel and cost the taxpayer millions of dollars.” Garamendi and Carbajal’s demands come after New York Times reporting revealed that DHS is considering using ships for mass deportations and identified Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s training ship, the Golden Bear, as a possible vessel.

“Mark my words, Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, and ICE will never use the Golden Bear for their mass deportation agenda,” said Congressman Garamendi. “Not only is deporting migrants by ship impractical, but it’s also deeply inhumane. We have already seen how Trump’s reckless diversion of our government and military resources to support immigration enforcement costs our military readiness. This move would be the same for our sealift capacity. I’m proud to stand with Congressman Carbajal on this issue and I will continue to use every lever of oversight at my disposal to make sure we halt Trump and Mullin’s ICE from escalating their already inhumane and cruel mass deportation agenda. Hands of the Golden Bear.”

“If the Trump administration follows through on this proposal, it would represent another escalation of their brutal immigration enforcement tactics. ICE already operates without sufficient transparency or public accountability, and deploying maritime vessels as floating prisons will only open the door to potentially more abuses. As the top Democrat overseeing the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee and a Senior Member of the Armed Services Committee, I am proud to stand with Congressman John Garamendi and my colleagues in opposing the use of the Golden Bear — or any vessel — for mass deportations,” said Congressman Carbajal.

Garamendi and Carbajal’s letter is the latest oversight action addressing President Donald Trump’s misuse of the military for his mass deportation agenda.

On December 10, 2025, Congressman John Garamendi (D-CA-08) and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) released a report detailing the Trump administration’s diversion of funds and resources from the Department of Defense (DoD) to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for immigration enforcement.

In January 2025, after discovering that military planes from Travis Air Force Base were used to deport undocumented immigrants, Congressman Garamendi demanded answers from the Department of Defense. After Garamendi pushed back, DHS and the DoD later moved away from using military aircraft for deportations.

In February 2025, Garamendi demanded answers about the Trump administration’s attempt to divert much-needed medical personnel to the Guantanamo Bay detention facility. After the letter was sent, the military canceled its orders.

In May 2025, after plans were floated to turn Travis into a mass migrant detention center, Garamendi and Representative Mike Thompson (D-CA-04) pushed back. DHS later dropped its plan to turn the military base into a detention center.

title: Rep. Gillen Recovers Over $4.2 Million For Nassau County Taxpayers Since Taking Office
text:
GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced that she has returned over $4.2 million to Nassau County residents owed by the federal government and closed more than 3,300 cases since taking office. As the representative for New York’s Fourth Congressional District, Rep. Gillen has helped constituents recover overpaid taxes, collect disability and retirement benefits, return home from conflict zones abroad and navigate federal agencies.

Earlier this year, Rep. Gillen recovered $540,000 in COVID-era tax savings for Chaminade High School, including $150,000 in interest. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) wrongly withheld these Employee Retention Credit funds for more than five years due to coding errors. Rep. Gillen’s office worked with the Taxpayer Advocate Service and the IRS to reclassify the school from a government entity to a non‑governmental, tax‑exempt nonprofit private school. This change allowed the school to qualify for critical savings, which were used to retain teachers and support staff during the height of the pandemic.

"When I took office, I promised to put more money back in Long Islanders’ pockets and help cut through the bureaucracy and red tape in Washington,” said Rep. Gillen. “I’m proud to have recovered more than $4.2 million for Nassau County residents from federal agencies, including delayed tax refunds, Social Security and veterans benefits, along with other critical savings. I’ll continue to do all I can to ensure Long Islanders receive the money they’re owed from the federal government.”

Last September, a Long Beach constituent requested help from Rep. Gillen’s office after her initial application for Social Security Disability benefits was rejected. After Rep. Gillen intervened, the constituent’s case was heard by an Administrative Law Judge in seven months instead of the usual timeframe of up to 18 months. The judge issued a favorable decision for the constituent and granted $44,000 in retroactive benefits and $2,463 in monthly benefits, allowing her to stay in her home.

Rep. Gillen and her office have helped constituents with urgent matters, including:

Retrieving more than $1.4 million in Social Security benefits.

Recovering nearly $1.6 million from delayed IRS returns, tax bill settlements and IRS overcharges.

Securing nearly $128,000 in veterans benefits.

Rep. Gillen and her office assist constituents with issues involving Social Security benefits, IRS tax refunds, VA disability claims, OPM retirement benefits, Medicare coverage, passport applications and other federal agencies.

Rep. Gillen’s office regularly hosts in-person mobile office hours throughout Nassau County to help constituents open cases and get federal assistance. Constituents can RSVP to mobile office hours here.

Constituents who need assistance with a federal agency can call 516-739-3008 or visit Rep. Gillen’s website at https://gillen.house.gov/services/help-federal-agency.
