title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Ban the Import of Russian Oil
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Last week, Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Don Bacon (NE-02) introduced the Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act to block the President’s deal to buy Russian oil and affirm support for Ukraine. This legislation is the result of the administration announcing a deal to issue new waivers which authorize importing Russian diesel, despite a bipartisan federal law enacted in 2022 prohibiting Russian oil imports. The President’s deal directly undermines the will of Congress, which acted decisively in 2022 to block oil revenue that Putin used to fund his fascist war on Ukraine.

Specifically, the Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act would:

Nullify the Treasury Department’s Russian oil waiver, immediately rendering General License 135 ineffective and prohibiting future waivers or general licenses authorizing the importation of Russian energy products.

Strengthen enforcement of the existing import ban by prohibiting Treasury from expending funds on agreements that violate the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022.

Reinforce critical intelligence support for Ukraine, requiring relevant intelligence agencies to provide support for Ukraine’s defense and notify congressional intelligence committees within 24 hours of any interruption.

“The President’s dirty deal to import Russian oil is running roughshod over our national interests and the bipartisan will of Congress and a bipartisan 2022 law explicitly banning the import of Russian oil. We won’t turn a blind eye to that,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “This bill will rein in this reckless deal and make clear that my community doesn’t want any part of funding Putin’s fascist war in Ukraine and the ongoing attacks terrorizing families in the Donbas. If the President is serious about bringing down gas prices, he should end the war in Iran, not send our tax dollars to Putin.”

“Russia chose this war. Ukraine did not. The United States must leave no doubt about where it stands. We must not import a single drop of Russian oil. Congress made that decision with overwhelming bipartisan support in 2022, and that law remains in force. It is not a suggestion, nor should its intent be undermined through administrative waivers. We cannot demand accountability from Putin while opening American markets to the Russian energy that helps finance his war. Every exception sends Moscow the wrong message: that American resolve can be outlasted,” said Rep. Fitzpatrick. “President Reagan understood that strength is not the obstacle to peace. It is what makes a just peace possible. Our responsibility is to stand firmly behind Ukraine’s sovereignty and ensure America’s commitments are reflected in America’s actions. Peace becomes possible when aggression carries a cost greater than its reward. On that, there can be no ambiguity.”

“For years, President Trump criticized Europe for buying Russian energy and propping up Putin’s war economy. Further, Congress overwhelmingly voted to impose tough sanctions on Russia. Now, Trump wants to make it easier for Putin to sell diesel fuel. He is wrong,” said Rep. Bacon. “Americans overwhelmingly support Ukraine and oppose Putin’s aggression and war crimes. The Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Against Russia Act nullifies the Russian diesel waiver, prohibits Treasury spending that violates the 2022 Russian oil import ban and provides intelligence support to Ukraine.” Congress must step up and force the President to support freedom and oppose the war criminal. America must stand with the Free World.”

Southwest Washington is home to one of the largest communities of Ukrainian immigrants and refugees in the US. Last month, the Congresswoman reaffirmed her commitment to the Ukrainian community in Southwest Washington by voting for a comprehensive package of sanctions targeting Russia and anyone who facilitates sanctions evasion–and has called on the President to fully implement this sanctions package. Further, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has been a proud supporter of Ukraine’s fight to stop Russia’s invasion and has worked continuously to aid Ukrainian refugees displaced by the conflict. In 2024, she introduced the Defending Borders, Defending Democracies Act and voted to pass H.R. 813, allocating over $60 billion in funding for Ukrainian defense. More recently in the FY27 Defense Appropriations markup, she spoke in support of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, a provision to strengthen domestic manufacturing capability to support Ukrainian defense.

Additionally, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez supports Ukrainians living in Southwest Washington through her casework operation, helping constituents facing issues with federal agencies. To get in touch or learn about how her office can help with federal agencies, please visit her casework page or Ukrainian Language casework page.

title: New Hampshire Congressional Delegation Applauds Delivery of Over $5.9 Million to New Hampshire Electric Co-Op
text:
Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (NH-D), and U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan (NH-D) applauded the delivery of over $5.9 million in federal funding to the New Hampshire Electric Cooperative (NHEC).

“When the April 2024 storm tore down power lines and poles across our state, New Hampshire Electric Co-op crews worked long, hard hours in brutal conditions to get the lights back on,” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “Granite Staters shouldn’t be left holding the bill for that recovery. I’m glad to see more than $5.9 million in federal disaster funding coming home to New Hampshire to reimburse the Co-op. The power of this Co-op is that it’s owned by its members, so this money goes right back to the people it serves. I’ll keep fighting for every penny that’s yours.”

“Last year’s severe winter storms created enormous wind and flooding across New Hampshire, leading many Granite Staters to lose power. Thanks to the work of emergency response crews working around the clock, the damage to our electrical infrastructure was repaired but at great cost to small communities with limited resources,” said Senator Shaheen. “I’m glad to see that more than five million dollars in federal funding is headed to the New Hampshire Electric Cooperative to help cover these expenses and better prepare our critical infrastructure for the future.”

“It is critical that our communities have the resources that they need to recover and rebuild in the face of severe storms,” said Senator Hassan. “This federal funding will help New Hampshire communities repair critical infrastructure damaged by severe weather, improve flood protections, and strengthen our state’s emergency preparedness. I will continue working to bring federal resources back to New Hampshire to ensure that our communities have the support that they need to recover from severe storms and prepare for future disasters.”

“This federal funding supports the reconstruction of critical infrastructure by NHEC and protects the well-being of Granite Staters,” said Congressman Pappas. “I’ll continue working to deliver resources back to New Hampshire to update old or damaged infrastructure, strengthen our storm preparedness, and keep people safe.”

Background:

In April 2024, a severe winter storm brought strong winds and flooding that damaged the NHEC electrical distribution system, threatening the health and safety of Granite Staters. Strong winds damaged power lines, utility poles, and transformers, causing power outages in Belknap, Carroll, Grafton, Rockingham, and Sullivan Counties.

title: When the Victim Becomes the Target, The Moral Collapse of American Politics
text:
There are moments in the life of a nation when the question is no longer whether we have lost our political civility, but whether we are in danger of losing our moral civilization. We have come upon such a moment. Political campaigns have always been contentious. Democracy is not a Sunday school picnic. It is a contest of ideas, competing convictions, personal ambitions, and sometimes enormous egos. Candidates are expected to challenge one another's records, question their judgment, and expose their failures. That is the legitimate business of democratic politics.

But there ought to be a boundary beyond which political ambition dare not travel. Surely that boundary must include the dignity of a child who has suffered sexual violence. When a political campaign reaches into the painful history of a rape survivor, enlists members of her family, and transforms childhood trauma into an instrument of political attack, it crosses a moral boundary that no decent civilization should accept. Consider the extraordinary contradiction. A child is violated. Her innocence is assaulted. Her security is shattered. She struggles to survive an experience no child should ever endure. Years later, having overcome that suffering and built a life of accomplishment, she discovers that the machinery of political ambition is prepared to turn her own family history into ammunition against her. The victim becomes the defendant. The survivor becomes the suspect. And the tragedy becomes a television commercial.

What kind of political culture produces such a spectacle? What does it say about our national conscience when the suffering of a child becomes a strategy for winning public office? There is something profoundly disturbing about a political culture that condemns violence in its speeches while exploiting the wounds of violence in its advertisements. There is something morally incoherent about proclaiming devotion to family values while using the broken relationships within a family as instruments of public humiliation. And there is something deeply contradictory about invoking the protection of women and children while making the suffering of a woman who was once a vulnerable child the centerpiece of a political attack. The issue is larger than one candidate, one advertisement, or one election. It concerns the moral architecture of the American republic. We have become remarkably sophisticated in the instruments of political persuasion and dangerously careless about the human beings upon whom those instruments are employed.

We can measure public opinion by the hour, target advertisements to individual households, and manipulate images, emotions, and anxieties with extraordinary precision. We have developed technologies capable of reaching millions of people instantaneously, yet we appear increasingly incapable of exercising the moral restraint that should govern their use. Technological sophistication is no substitute for moral development. A civilization may possess satellites in the heavens and still harbor cruelty in its heart. It may develop artificial intelligence while displaying a tragic deficiency of human compassion. It may master the science of communication while forgetting the elementary morality of what ought never to be communicated.

This is the great paradox of our age: We are becoming more advanced in our instruments of power while appearing less disciplined in our exercise of moral responsibility. And that should trouble every American, regardless of political affiliation. The measure of a political campaign cannot simply be whether it wins. It must also include what it is willing to sacrifice in pursuit of victory. What does it profit a campaign to win an election while forfeiting its conscience? What does it profit a candidate to acquire public office by exploiting private suffering? And what does it profit a nation to celebrate political victory while tolerating the degradation of its most

vulnerable citizens?

There is no political office so exalted that it justifies humiliating a survivor of sexual violence. There is no campaign strategy so clever that it can transform cruelty into courage. And there is no electoral victory so magnificent that it can redeem the deliberate abandonment of human decency. A survivor does not forfeit her dignity because she enters public life. She does not surrender her humanity because she seeks public office. Her childhood trauma does not become the property of political consultants merely because her name appears on a ballot. Public service invites scrutiny. It does not authorize the weaponization of sexual violence.

There must remain some sanctuary for human suffering, some respect for childhood innocence, some recognition that even in the fierce competition for political power, certain

things are morally indefensible.

We are sometimes told that this is simply the reality of modern politics. Campaigns are brutal. Elections are competitive. Winning requires hard choices. But the fact that something has become commonplace does not make it morally acceptable. Slavery was once customary. Segregation was once defended as the natural order. The exclusion of women from political participation was once considered an unquestionable

feature of American society. The history of moral progress is the history of people courageous enough to challenge the prevailing customs of their age. Every great advance in human dignity began with the recognition that what society had learned to tolerate was something society should never have accepted. That same moral examination is required of our political culture today. The question is not simply whether a campaign advertisement is legally permissible. The deeper question is whether it is morally defensible.

Legality establishes the minimum requirements of public conduct. Morality asks something more demanding of us. It asks whether we have considered the suffering of others. Whether we have respected their

humanity. Whether our pursuit of power has overwhelmed our capacity for compassion. And whether we still recognize that some wounds are too sacred to be converted into political weapons. A democracy cannot survive on constitutional procedures alone. It requires a moral culture capable of sustaining those procedures. It requires citizens who understand that political opponents remain human beings, that public disagreement need not become personal degradation, and that victory without restraint can become its own form of defeat. For the ultimate measure of a civilization is not how it treats the powerful, the celebrated, or the victorious. It is how it treats the wounded.

A nation reveals its character in the presence of suffering. And when we begin to exploit the wounds of children for the ambitions of adults, we are doing more than lowering the standards of political discourse. We are diminishing the moral stature of the republic itself. We must recover the conviction that human dignity is not a campaign commodity, that compassion is not political weakness, and that decency is not an outdated virtue.

The suffering of a child must never become the entertainment of a nation. There is something especially tragic about a society that teaches children to report abuse,

encourages survivors to find their voices, and celebrates the courage required to overcome trauma, only to permit that very trauma to be used against them when they enter public life. What message does that send to the next frightened child who wonders whether speaking the truth will someday become a source of public humiliation? What message does it send to women who have struggled for years to reclaim their dignity? And what message does it send about the moral priorities of those who seek to govern?

America has overcome periods of extraordinary injustice not because cruelty disappeared on its own, but because people of conscience refused to normalize it. That responsibility has not expired. We must insist that the pursuit of political power remain subordinate to the preservation of human dignity. For when politics becomes more important than people, when ambition becomes more sacred than innocence, and when winning becomes more valuable than decency, we have not advanced toward a more enlightened civilization. We have simply learned to practice an ancient barbarism with modern technology.

And perhaps the greatest danger facing our democracy is not that we have forgotten how to distinguish right from wrong. It is that we may be becoming comfortable with the distinction and choosing to ignore it. The most frightening darkness is not the darkness that comes when the sun has set. It is the darkness that descends when the conscience of a nation has gone silent.

title: Kaptur, Finstad, Davis Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Protect US Pork Producers from Animal Disease
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) introduced H.R. 10911, the US Swine Health Improvement Plan Act alongside Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) and Congressman Don Davis (NC-01). The legislation is also cosponsored by Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-02). This bipartisan bill would formally establish a voluntary US Department of Agriculture (USDA) regulatory program to be known as the US Swine Health Improvement Plan (US SHIP) to certify that herds at pork farms and pig breeding facilities across the country meet strong health standards. The goal is to prevent, detect, and respond to animal diseases such as African Swine Fever and Classical Swine Fever, which have appeared in recent years in the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

“With this legislation, we are supporting our Nation’s agricultural trade economy and helping to protect animal health, public health, and the security of our food supply by preventing future animal disease outbreaks,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture. “We are also helping US pork producers reach international markets, and, most importantly, we are protecting the economic livelihood of family farms, including those I represent across Northwest Ohio.”

“I’m proud to represent one of the top pork-producing congressional districts in the country,” said Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01), member of the House Agriculture Committee. “This critical, bipartisan legislation to formally establish the US Swine Health Improvement Plan will ensure our pork producers in southern Minnesota and across the country have the support and resources they need to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks. As a member of the House Agriculture Committee, I remain committed to ensuring our farmers and producers have the tools they need to succeed.”

“North Carolina is the third-largest hog-producing state in the country. Our swine industry is a large part of the state’s agricultural economy and food supply," said Congressman Don Davis (NC-01), member of the House Agriculture Committee. "A voluntary US Department of Agriculture framework for animal disease monitoring and herd health certification can help farmers and allow for a more timely response to disease outbreaks in order to protect our economy and food supply."

This House bill complements a Senate measure, S. 4893, introduced earlier this year by Senator Jon Husted of Ohio and builds on a pilot program the swine industry launched several years ago with USDA funding and State animal health officials’ support. The program follows the model of the National Poultry Improvement Plan, which has protected the poultry industry for more than 90 years from diseases such as avian influenza or the bird flu that affected Ohio in late 2024 and 2025. Today, 38 States take part in this voluntary swine health improvement pilot program. The legislation would formally authorize the program in Federal law, set funding levels for it over the next five years, and direct USDA to establish an advisory committee to recommend how the program should be administered. The advisory committee would also study broader swine health challenges and recommend how the Federal Government can help the swine industry and States respond when problems arise. By strengthening and expanding the piloted US Swine Health Improvement Plan, Congress can help swine facilities obtain health certifications and improve the marketability of domestic pork products.

The legislation is supported by the Ohio Pork Council, whose representatives recently met with Congresswoman Kaptur to discuss the importance of preventing animal disease outbreaks and the success of the pilot program, and by the National Pork Producers Council (NPPC).

“On our farms, protecting pig health is a responsibility we take seriously every day,” said Jarred Black, Ohio pork producer and Ohio Pork Council President. “Disease preparedness also requires coordination across farms, state lines, and government agencies. Establishing permanent authority for US SHIP would strengthen that partnership. We thank Congresswoman Kaptur for helping move this producer priority forward.”

“Funding and formalizing the US Swine Health Improvement Plan are key to strengthening the health of our Nation’s swine herd,” said Pat Hord, NPPC President-elect and Ohio pork producer from Bucyrus, Ohio. “A formal advisory committee will help ensure that producer and industry expertise inform US SHIP’s implementation and continued improvement, supporting a science-based approach to disease prevention and animal health. We appreciate Representatives Kaptur, Finstad, and Davis for recognizing the value of collaboration between producers and the federal government in protecting the future of American family farms and pork production.”

Ohio’s 9th Congressional District ranks in the top sixth of all Congressional districts nationwide in hog and pig sales value, totaling more than $37 Million across 139 farms. More broadly, the legislation supports Ohio’s approximately 2,500 pig farmers who raise pigs on more than 3,500 farms statewide. Many of these are family farms in Northwest Ohio, including the Vennekotter family farms that Congresswoman Kaptur visited last week in Putnam County.

Congresswoman Kaptur is working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to include this legislation in any final Farm Bill that may be negotiated and passed by the end of the year. She also supports a pending rulemaking proposed by USDA to formalize the program in Federal regulations, which the legislation she has introduced would require be done by the Administration within one year.

A full copy of the bill text can be found by clicking here.

title: Congressman Kean Visits Triad Tool with NJMEP
text:
(October 28, 2026) BRANCHBURG, NJ – Last week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) visited Triad Tool Company Inc. with the New Jersey Manufacturing Extension Program to meet members of the company’s leadership team and learn about its manufacturing operations.

Triad Tool is a family-owned contract manufacturer founded in 1933, specializing in close-tolerance Computer Numerical Control (CNC) precision machining. Now under fourth-generation leadership, the company provides CNC machining and turning, wire EDM, abrasive waterjet, inspection, and build-to-print subassembly services. They serve commercial and military aviation, power generation, and telecommunications customers, including NASA, Raytheon, SpaceX, and RTX.

“New Jersey has the talent, ingenuity, and industrial expertise to lead the next generation of American manufacturing, and companies like Triad Tool are proving it every day,” said Congressman Kean. “Our responsibility in Congress is to ensure that businesses like these have the tools to compete and grow. That means strengthening domestic supply chains, expanding access to skilled workforce training, and advancing commonsense policies that encourage innovation and private investment.”

Kean continued, “Triad Tool’s longstanding commitment to New Jersey and its workforce underscores what’s at stake: protecting good-paying American jobs, creating opportunities for the next generation, and ensuring the United States remains a global leader in advanced manufacturing.”

“The New Jersey Manufacturing Extension Partnership (NJMEP) applauds Rep Tom Kean Jr. for supporting New Jersey Manufacturers,” said Judith Fleischer, Special Projects at New Jersey Manufacturers Extension Program, Inc. “He has visited numerous companies over the last few years and most recently, Magna-Power Electronics and Triad Tool. NJMEP thanks him for this effort.”

“Triad Tool was honored to welcome Congressman Tom Kean Jr. and the NJMEP team to our facility,” said Triad Tool CEO John Staudinger. “For many years, NJMEP training grants have helped us recruit and train young people for highly skilled careers manufacturing critical components for America’s aerospace and defense industries. Congressman Kean’s support for strong national defense investment and well-targeted tariffs that level the playing field for American manufacturers is important to bringing work home, protecting our industrial base, and creating good-paying jobs here in New Jersey”

Staudinger continued, “We appreciate his taking the time to meet our team, see our capabilities firsthand, and support our efforts to retain and grow this 93-year-old New Jersey manufacturing company.”

title: Cancel the Cuts: Kennedy, 1199SEIU, and Western New York Healthcare Leaders Warn of Looming Medicaid Requirements
text:
With New Rules Set to Take Effect January 1st, State Health Officials Estimate at Least 475,000 New Yorkers Could Lose Medicaid Access

Kennedy Vows House Democrats Will Fight to Protect Care and Affordability

BUFFALO, N.Y. - Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) joined 1199SEIU, a coalition of organized labor, and leaders from local hospitals, nursing homes, and community health centers at 1199SEIU’s offices in Buffalo to warn that new federal Medicaid work requirements taking effect January 1st will put coverage and care at risk for hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers.[1] The leaders called on Congressional Republicans to cancel the cuts and pledged to fight to protect the healthcare safety net.

“Starting January 1st, Western New Yorkers who rely on Medicaid will face new barriers to care, where one missed form could mean losing their health coverage,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans added red tape that puts coverage at risk for people who need it most. With clinics closing, nursing homes struggling to stay open, and hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers already losing Essential Plan coverage, our healthcare system cannot afford more cuts. House Democrats are fighting to reverse these cuts and protect the healthcare safety net that Western New York’s families, hospitals, and nursing homes depend on.”

“Make no mistake- this isn't actually about work. We know that 92% of Medicaid enrollees either work, go to school, provide care for someone, or are unable to work due to illness or disability. These “work requirements” aren’t about promoting work; they’re about taking healthcare away from the people who need it most. We cannot ignore the lessons we have learned from states like Georgia and Arkansas, whose attempts to incorporate these requirements into their Medicaid eligibility only resulted in loss of coverage and loss of access to preventative care that saves lives,” said Grace Orr, 1199SEIU Vice-President for WNY Nursing Homes.

Under the Big, Ugly Bill, many adults aged 19-64 on Medicaid must either show 80 hours a month of work, school, job training, or community service, or earn at least $580 a month, and must also renew their coverage every six months instead of annually.[2] The rules apply to new applicants starting January 1st and to current enrollees at renewal beginning on March 1st.[3] The NYS Department of Health estimates that at least 475,000 New Yorkers could lose Medicaid because of new work requirements and more frequent eligibility checks. The state’s uninsured population is also estimated to grow by 45 percent, from roughly 1 million to as many as 1.45 million uninsured individuals.[4] The Congressional Budget Office estimates the work requirements alone will increase the number of uninsured Americans by 5.3 million by 2034, and that 70 percent of those who lose coverage at the bi-annual renewals will lose it for procedural reasons such as missing paperwork.[5]

The impact will be felt across Western New York, where tens of thousands of the 300,000 Medicaid enrollees in Erie and Niagara Counties will be impacted by the new requirements.[6] Joint Economic Committee Democrats project that more than 42,000 people in Kennedy’s district, including more than 39,000 Medicaid enrollees, will lose coverage by 2034 because of Republican healthcare cuts.[7]

The damage has already begun. About 450,000 New Yorkers lost Essential Plan coverage on July 1st, and nearly 178,000 of them have not enrolled in another plan through the state marketplace, according to the NYSDOH.[8] Clinics in Amherst, Tonawanda, and Buffalo have closed, Erie County Medical Center has cut roughly 150 jobs, and the Richmond Nursing Home in Springville has received state approval to close.

New York State Senator April N.M. Baskin said, "Thousands of New Yorkers have already been kicked off their health insurance this year following federal cuts that impacted the Essential Plan. Now, beginning in January, new Medicaid requirements threaten to put even more New Yorkers at risk of losing their coverage. These policies create unnecessary barriers to health care and threaten access to coverage for families across Western New York and throughout our state. We should be making health care more accessible, not making it harder for people to stay insured.”

“People who depend on Medicaid should not have to fight through more red tape to keep their health coverage,” said Senator Jeremy J. Zellner. “Someone working multiple jobs or unpredictable hours should not lose access to their doctor or prescriptions because they cannot keep up with government paperwork. I stand with Congressman Kennedy in opposing requirements that put working families at risk and place more strain on the hospitals and providers serving Western New York.”

Assemblymember Jon D. Rivera said, “The new Medicaid work requirements are a cruel, unnecessary barrier that will take health care away from people who need it most. Millions of Americans who qualify for coverage will be forced to navigate a maze of government paperwork, putting their health and financial security at risk. At a time when families are already struggling with the rising cost of living, Republicans are making it harder for people to see a doctor, afford their prescriptions and get the care they need. These cuts will mean more uninsured families, more medical debt and more preventable suffering. Health care should be a basic necessity. Instead, Republicans are attempting to make it a privilege that depends on someone’s ability to navigate bureaucratic red tape.”

"Medicaid is a lifeline for hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers, providing access to essential health care, prescription medications, and long-term care,” said Assemblymember Karen McMahon. “These new federal requirements threaten to take that coverage away from the most vulnerable in society, creating additional barriers to care and placing greater strain on our hospitals, nursing homes, and community health centers. We must protect access to affordable health care, not make it harder for people to get the care they need. I join Congressman Kennedy, 1199SEIU, and health care leaders across Western New York in calling on Congress to cancel these cuts and protect the Medicaid safety net that so many of our families rely on."

“Medicaid work requirements will create significant barriers to healthcare for individuals and families who already face challenges accessing their essential services," said Erie County Legislator Lawrence Dupre. "We must prioritize policies that protect access to care and ensure that no one loses their healthcare because of unnecessary hurdles.”

“Our health is the foundation of how we perform in everyday life,” said Niagara Falls City Councilmember Bridgette Myles. “When you feel good, you are able to do good. As a Niagara Falls City Council Member, I believe it is important to educate our community about the upcoming Medicaid changes, how residents may be personally affected, and what resources are available to help them maintain their healthcare coverage.”

“I totally support Congressman Kennedy’s stance on these Medicaid work requirements,” said North Tonawanda Councilmember Will Schulmeister. "These work requirements will hurt many people in need."

"Community health centers like Jericho Road serve people who have nowhere else to turn. Medicaid work requirements add administrative burdens on patients already navigating the complex challenges that poverty imposes upon them. Many who qualify will lose coverage because they can't keep up with the documentation," said Dr. Allana Krolikowski, CEO of Jericho Road Community Health Center. "Community health centers must also dedicate scarce staff and resources to help patients prove their eligibility in addition to caring for them. In American healthcare, health insurance is essential to accessing care. When people lose coverage, they delay preventive care, skip medications, and end up sicker, and our entire community pays the price. We urge our leaders to protect coverage, not erect new barriers to it."

“Jewish Family Services of WNY has a significant share of clients who could lose Medicaid coverage and ultimately access to critical healthcare services under these new work requirements,” said Molly Carr, CEO of Jewish Family Services of WNY. “They are meaningful contributors to our community who deserve to receive care with dignity, respect, and compassion, and Medicaid provides access to these services that clients are unable to get elsewhere.”

"Too many eligible patients risk losing coverage because of burdensome paperwork requirements, not because they don't qualify," said Joanne Haefner, President and CEO of Neighborhood Health Center of WNY. "We want people to know that our health center is here for them -- to assist with insurance applications and to continually provide care no matter a person's insurance status."

Kennedy cosponsors the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act (H.R. 10692), which would repeal the Big, Ugly Bill’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions and fully restore funding for New York’s Essential Plan. House Democrats are fighting to reverse Republican healthcare cuts and deliver affordable healthcare for every American.[9]

title: LaHood Joins U.S. Secretary of Energy Wright and EDF Director Beard to Announce $5 Billion Investment in Nuclear Fleets and Lower Costs for Families
text:
Washington, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Darin LaHood (IL-16) joined U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and DOE Energy Dominance Financing Director Gregory A. Beard at the Byron Clean Energy Center to announce a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization across Constellation Energy’s nuclear fleet in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania.

"This $5 billion investment is critical to the future of American energy security and providing Americans with more affordable, reliable energy," said Rep. LaHood. "I commend President Trump, Secretary Wright, and Director Beard for recognizing the importance of investing in our existing nuclear fleet, especially here in Illinois, and their work to support American jobs and strengthen our electric grid. I remain committed to working closely with Secretary Wright, the Department of Energy, and the Trump Administration to strengthen energy reliability, support good-paying jobs, and lower costs for hardworking families."

“The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump’s American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation’s nuclear fleet,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “Uprates that maximize power generation from our existing nuclear facilities are yet another example of the commonsense energy addition policies the Trump Administration is embracing—ensuring more affordable, reliable, and secure energy for American families and businesses.”

“EDF is delivering on President Trump and Secretary Wright’s commitment to unleash American nuclear power by financing projects that modernize and expand our nation’s existing nuclear plants,” said EDF Director Gregory A. Beard. “These investments will add more reliable baseload power to the grid, help lower electricity costs, strengthen our nation’s energy security, and fuel long-term American prosperity.”

Background:

This crucial investment represents a major milestone in the American Nuclear Renaissance by advancing President Trump’s Executive Order Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base and DOE’s Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE), expediting the expansion of America's nuclear capacity by maximizing power generation from existing reactors.

The projects will add enough electricity to power more than 930,000 homes—lowering costs and strengthening grid reliability in Illinois, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and across the PJM region. The investments will support more than 10,000 project-related jobs across Constellation’s nuclear fleet while delivering affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses.

title: Larsen Urges Voters to Return Ballots to Drop Boxes and Pushes Back on New USPS Policy
text:
Last week, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) expressed concerns to the United States Postal Service (USPS) about delays in postmarking ballots delivered in Northwest Washington.

“Between August and October 2026, I visited local election offices in Whatcom, Skagit, Snohomish, Island and San Juan counties,” said Rep. Larsen. “During these visits, local election officials raised concern that changes to USPS policy may delay postmarking for mail-in ballots. Delays in postmarking can cause mail-in ballots to be wrongly rejected for being late, even if the ballots were mailed on election day.”

In his letter to USPS, Rep. Larsen requested the agency answer questions about the steps it is taking to ensure this policy change does not harm eligible voters in Washington state. Rep. Larsen also published an op-ed in the Cascadia Daily News urging voters to return their ballots to official drop boxes.

“The Washington Secretary of State’s office recommends voters return their ballots to drop boxes managed by local election officials, which bypasses the postmarking process,” said Rep. Larsen. “Regardless of who you vote for, I am working to make sure your voice is heard in our democracy.”

Rep. Larsen is a strong advocate for free and fair elections, expanding access to the ballot and Washington state’s vote-by-mail system. Earlier this month, he reintroduced legislation to protect U.S. citizens who face disenfranchisement because of restrictive voter identification laws (America Votes Act). Rep. Larsen is also the co-founder of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus.

The full text of Rep. Larsen’s op-ed in the Cascadia Daily News is available here.

The full text of Rep. Larsen’s letter to USPS is available here and below.

October 24, 2026

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

I am concerned about the accuracy of postmark dates on ballots delivered in Washington’s Second District. County election officials in my district have raised concern that a United States Postal Service (USPS) initiative may result in election offices’ rejecting mail-in ballots for being late, despite voters mailing ballots by election day. To address these concerns, I urge USPS to restore daily evening mail pickups at post offices before the November 3 elections. Reinstating this commonsense policy will ensure ballots are accurately postmarked, delivered and counted in accordance with Washington state law.

Between August and October 2026, I visited local election offices in every county in Washington’s Second District. During these visits to Whatcom, Skagit, Snohomish, Island and San Juan counties, I saw firsthand the important work of local election officials who administer our local, state, and federal elections. Thanks to the dedicated efforts and those of volunteers, local elections offices ensure every eligible ballot is secure and accurately counted.

However, during these visits, local election officials raised concern that changes to USPS policy may delay postmarking for mail-in ballots. Washington state law permits counting ballots received after an election if the ballots are postmarked by election day. The state relies on accurate postmarking to implement its election laws and ensure all legally cast ballots are counted. Delays in postmarking can cause mail-in ballots to be wrongly rejected for being late, even if the ballots were mailed on election day. To ensure that Washington’s elections are secure and fair, USPS must reliably postmark ballots delivered to state election offices.

In April 2025, USPS established a Regional Transportation Optimization (RTO) initiative that eliminated afternoon or evening collections at certain post offices more than 50 miles from a regional processing center. For these applicable locations, mail deposited later in the day is not collected until the next business day for transportation to a processing facility, potentially delaying postmarking and delivery. An audit from the Postal Service Inspector General indicated RTO can result in mail getting postmarked on different days than their actual date of mailing.

Following the August 2026 primary elections in Washington state, Senator Maria Cantwell and Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs issued alarming findings about ballot rejection rates during that election period. According to the report, the statewide rate of ballots rejected for late postmarks increased by 32 percent in August 2026 when compared to those in the 2024 primary.

An analysis from Brookings raises further concern that RTO is contributing to the rise of late ballot rejections, showing that RTO exposure nearly doubled the rate ballots are rejected for arriving late. In Washington state, locations covered by RTO saw rates increase by 142 percent, the largest of the three states in Brookings’ analysis. Voters who submit their ballots on time should not lose the opportunity to have their votes counted because of preventable postal delays.

Postal workers provide an invaluable service to people across the United States, helping individuals receive their medications, ballots, paychecks, bills and other necessities. They often work long hours and manage operations with limited staff and resources, especially during peak season and during elections.

To ensure ballots are accurately postmarked for the November 3 election, I request answers to the following questions in writing no later than October 30, 2026:

1. Will USPS restore twice-daily collections and provide postal workers with the resources they need to effectively implement this change?

2. How is USPS working with states like Washington to ensure ballots are postmarked to accurately reflect the date they were mailed?

3. What steps is USPS taking to inform people in locations covered by RTO that postmarking may be delayed and that individuals should submit their ballots early to avoid rejection?

Thank you for your attention to this urgent request and for the work postal employees do every day to serve Northwest Washington.

title: REP LIEU STATEMENT ON THE PASSING OF DOLORES HUERTA
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Ted W. Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) issued the following statement on the passing of American labor leader and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta.

Dolores Huerta dedicated her life to fighting for others. As co-founder of the United Farm Workers of America, she championed farm workers’ rights and helped advance the labor movement across industries. Her decades of advocacy transformed the lives of farm workers and helped pave the way for greater labor protections nationwide.

Huerta was also a passionate advocate for immigrants, minorities, LGBTQ+ people, and women. She faced beatings, arrests, and death threats – but never wavered in her fight for a better and more just future for all.

title: House Democratic Committee Leaders Request Frontier AI Companies Report Misalignment & Safety Incidents to Congress Within 48 Hours
text:
“While there is no question now that Congress must act to address gaps in AI governance, we must have the best information available to undertake that complicated process in a thoughtful and productive way.”

(Washington, DC) – House Democratic Committee leaders with jurisdiction over artificial intelligence wrote to five of the nation’s leading frontier AI companies today requesting information and ongoing reporting to Congress about AI model misalignment and safety incidents within 48 hours of incident detection. The letters follow an alarming rise in reports of AI models taking unintended and potentially unsafe actions during testing, raising questions about the safety of AI models as well as the adequacy of monitoring and evaluation at the frontier AI companies.

The letters were signed by Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ), Science, Space, and Technology Committee Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), and Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (D-MD). Collectively, the three committees have jurisdiction over the development and deployment of AI as well as potential penalties for its misuse.

“In the absence of any mandatory reporting requirements or common guidelines regarding what incidents should be reported, to whom, in what detail, and at what intervals, companies such as yours have been left to develop your own de facto standards on a voluntary basis,” Pallone, Lofgren, and Raskin wrote. “And the Trump Administration has been content to rely on voluntary disclosures and self-regulation by the AI industry.”

The Democratic Committee leaders continued, “But that approach will not suffice; it relies too heavily on the consistent goodwill of all AI companies to voluntarily disclose incidents that might expose them to liability and reputational damage. While there is no question now that Congress must act to address gaps in AI governance, we must have the best information available to undertake that complicated process in a thoughtful and productive way.”

The lawmakers asked each company to provide a full accounting of identified incidents by November 11, 2026. The Democrats also requested the companies notify the committees within 48 hours of discovering any new or previously unknown incidents; and requested notification within 24 hours if critical infrastructure appears to be involved.

The Democratic Committee leaders sent oversight letters to the following companies:

Anthropic

Google

Meta

OpenAI

SpaceXSI

title: Malliotakis Announces Federal Funding to Expand Science & Stewardship Program at Freshkills Park
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) today joined Mark Murphy, President of the Freshkills Park Alliance and Administrator of Freshkills Park, to announce nearly $687,000 in federal funding she secured to expand the Science & Stewardship Program at Freshkills Park. The funding will provide the initial framework, infrastructure and field equipment necessary to establish long-term environmental research at the park and support its continued transformation from a former landfill into a hub for conservation.

The funding will support research equipment, environmental monitoring tools, data systems and greenhouse resources to help scientists study the park’s wildlife and habitats. Researchers will collect baseline data on the condition of Freshkills’ grasslands, wetlands and shorelines, which will help guide restoration and habitat maintenance in the years ahead. The funding will also provide opportunities for students to gain hands-on experience through internships and training in environmental science and conservation.

“Freshkills was once the world’s largest landfill, and today we are helping transform it into a place for environmental research, education and recreation,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “I’m proud to have secured this federal funding to expand the Science & Stewardship Program at Freshkills Park, give researchers the tools they need to study and protect this unique landscape, and create new learning opportunities for students. This project will help ensure that a site once associated with waste and pollution can benefit Staten Islanders for generations to come.”

“This congressional appropriation is a transformative investment in the future of the Freshkills Park Alliance and our science and research programs. We are deeply grateful to Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis and her dedicated staff for their unwavering support and tireless three-year effort to secure this critical funding. This investment will help us expand our research capabilities, advance environmental science, and establish Freshkills Park as a premier regional destination for scientific research, education, and discovery,” said Mark Murphy, President, Freshkills Park Alliance.

title: Malliotakis, Brooklyn Elected Officials Highlight State Policies Driving Up Utility Bills, Legislative Efforts to Lower Energy Costs
text:
(BROOKLYN, NY) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) joined State Senator Steve Chan and Assemblymembers Lester Chang, Michael Tannousis, and Alec Brook-Krasny to highlight how costly New York State energy policies and mandates are driving up utility bills for families and businesses, while outlining federal efforts to increase domestic energy production, strengthen grid reliability and lower electricity costs.

New Yorkers pay approximately 60% more for electricity than the national average, placing a significant financial burden on hardworking families and small businesses. The lawmakers highlighted how state energy mandates, taxes and regulatory decisions are contributing to rising costs, including rate increases approved by the New York State Public Service Commission (PSC), whose members are appointed by the Governor, and the state's closure of the Indian Point Nuclear Power Plant that provided 26% of New York City's electricity supply.

Over the past five years, the PSC has approved two major multi-year rate plans for Con Edison, further increasing costs for ratepayers. The lawmakers also noted that state and local taxes, fees and surcharges make up roughly one-third of a customer's utility bill.

"Brooklyn families and small businesses are being forced to pay more than 60% above the national average because of costly energy mandates, excessive taxes and misguided policies coming out of Albany. While Washington is working to expand American energy production, strengthen our electric grid and deliver more affordable, reliable power, New York State continues to pursue policies that drive costs higher. We need to reverse course, provide relief to ratepayers and ensure families can afford to keep their lights on and heat their homes," said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis.

"New York pays among the highest rates in the country for utilities, but there are so many solutions that our Governor and the other side of the aisle will not agree to. They keep blaming the federal government, Con Edison, and National Grid, when it is the Democrat policy that is the problem. How come the other 49 states don't have this problem that we do then?" said Senator Steve Chan.

“Our neighbors and local businesses need to survive and thrive in this economy. Our Republican team will fight for affordability by repealing congestion pricing, cutting taxes, and lowering service fees on electric bills. We will always fight for you,” said Assemblymember Lester Chang.

"The rising utility costs that are driving residents out of New York are the direct result of mandates and taxes imposed by the Governor and Democratic-controlled legislature. Albany’s mandates have consistently increased the cost of living in New York and we need new leadership to put our state on a corrective course. The evidence is clear when the state is sitting on a massive $2.4 billion “Energy Tax” surplus that is waiting to be utilized on whatever pet project the Governor deems fit instead of returning it to the ratepayers," said Assemblyman Michael Tannousis.

title: Harris Announces Nearly $20 Million to Modernize Rail Infrastructure in South-Central North Carolina
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) announced that Aberdeen Carolina & Western Railway (ACWR) has been awarded $19.9 million from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) through the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. This summer, Congressman Harris advocated for the investment in a letter to the FRA.

“Modernizing our rail infrastructure in Stanly and Montgomery counties will improve safety, strengthen freight transportation, and support the businesses that drive our local economy,” said Congressman Harris. “I was proud to support this project because a safe, reliable rail network is essential to ensuring south-central North Carolina remains economically strong and competitive for years to come. This nearly $20 million federal investment is a major win for North Carolina’s 8th District.”

The funding will support approximately 30 miles of rail upgrades in Stanly and Montgomery counties, replacing aging track dating back to the early 1900s with modern continuous welded rail. These improvements will enhance safety, increase freight capacity, and improve the efficiency of rail transportation for businesses and industries throughout the region.

“A healthy rail network is critical to take freight off of our nation’s highways, and we thank the FRA and USDOT for supporting projects like ours,” said Anthony Menzies, CEO of Aberdeen Carolina & Western Railway.

The federal grant is part of a $41 million infrastructure investment, with ACWR and the North Carolina Department of Transportation providing the remaining 52 percent in non-federal matching funds. The project builds on previous improvements to ACWR’s Piedmont rail corridor, which serves agricultural producers, manufacturers, and other businesses throughout south-central North Carolina.

title: Rep. Miller Welcomed SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler to Quincy, Highlights Trump Administration’s Historic Economic Achievements
text:
QUINCY, IL — Today, Congresswoman Mary Miller (IL-15) welcomed U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Administrator Kelly Loeffler to Quincy for a series of visits highlighting the Trump Administration’s accomplishments in strengthening American manufacturing and supporting local small businesses across IL-15.

During the visit, Rep. Miller and Administrator Loeffler met with local business owners and employees, including Quincy Metal Fabricators and Thyme Square Bakery & Cafe, to discuss the importance of expanding domestic production, supporting skilled American workers, and creating new economic opportunities in rural Illinois.

“It was a special privilege to welcome Administrator Loeffler back to her home state of Illinois and showcase the hardworking Americans who keep our communities thriving,” said Congresswoman Mary Miller. “Thanks to President Trump and his remarkable administration, we are cutting taxes, eliminating burdensome regulations, and putting American workers and small businesses first. I will continue fighting alongside this administration to ensure our local manufacturers and Main Street businesses have every opportunity to succeed.”

“It was a privilege to join Congresswoman Mary Miller in Quincy and to meet with the hardworking small business owners and manufacturers who are the backbone of its economy,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “From the factory floor to rural America and Main Street, Illinois’ entrepreneurs are hiring and growing again thanks to President Trump’s America First agenda that rewards hard work. Through historic Working Families Tax Cuts, deregulation, and fair trade, the Trump SBA is proud to work with leaders like Congresswoman Miller to put American workers and job creators first.”

Background:

SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler is a former U.S. Senator and businesswoman who grew up working on her family's farm in Bloomington, Illinois. She now leads the SBA, which supports approximately 36 million small businesses nationwide.

The Working Families Tax Cuts passed by Republicans made the 20% small business tax deduction permanent, providing long-term tax certainty for Main Street businesses and encouraging investment, expansion, and job creation.

title: MATSUI STATEMENT ON THE PASSING OF DOLORES HUERTA
text:
SACRAMENTO, CA – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) released the following statement after the passing of labor leader and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta.

“We have lost an American hero with the passing of Dolores Huerta,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “Dolores changed the course of our nation’s history. In the fields of the Central Valley and in our State Capitol here in Sacramento, she faced down entrenched opposition on behalf of the workers who put food on America’s tables. And she won, securing rights and protections they had been denied for far too long. She embodied the very best of California–the conviction that ordinary people, organized and determined, can change what others insisted never would. Her words, ‘Sí, se puede,’ remain our call to action, and her legacy lives on in every person who marches for a better future. It was an honor to know her. Our state is fairer and stronger because of her courage. My prayers are with all of Dolores’ family and loved ones during this difficult time.”

title: Chairwoman McClain Brings Home $2.25 Million for Armada Fire Station Upgrades
text:
ARMADA, MI – House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) announced $2.25 million in federal Community Project Funding she secured for upgrades to the Armada Township Fire Department.

“Armada's firefighters and paramedics show up for their community day and night. Our first responders deserve a station equipped to meet the demands of the job,” Chairwoman McClain said. “I'm proud to bring $2.25 million back to our community to support the men and women who keep our families safe. This investment will strengthen emergency response and make a lasting difference for families across Armada Township and surrounding communities. The Armada Township and USDA Rural Development helped make these upgrades possible.”

The funding will support the rehabilitation and expansion of the fire station as the department transitions from a volunteer-based operation to providing full-time fire and paramedic services around the clock. The upgrades will help ensure Armada's firefighters and paramedics have a facility equipped to serve the community.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Mejia Leads Five Bills to Strengthen Small Businesses, Cut Red Tape, and Improve Disaster Relief
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), a member of the House Small Business Committee, has led five bills in the 119th Congress to cut bureaucratic red tape, streamline disaster assistance, expand access to federal resources, and protect small-business owners and workers.

“Small businesses are the backbone of our local economies, yet too often they lack the support and resources they need to succeed. Whether recovering from a disaster, navigating federal programs, or protecting their rights, entrepreneurs deserve a government that invests in their success. From Belleville to Jefferson and everywhere in between, I'm fighting to ensure our small businesses have the tools, resources, and opportunities they need not just to survive, but to thrive,” said Congresswoman Mejia.

Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act (H.R. 10355)

Advanced unanimously out of the House Small Business Committee

Requires the Small Business Administration (SBA) to maintain consistent, accurate, and up-to-date disaster loan outreach materials, helping business owners navigate federal assistance programs when disaster strikes. The bipartisan bill advanced out of committee in September and awaits a vote on the House floor.

Fast Track Disaster Relief Act (H.R. 10344)

Cuts administrative barriers to disaster recovery by allowing the SBA to obtain necessary tax information directly from the IRS to determine eligibility for disaster loans. This would help streamline the application process and reduce unnecessary paperwork for businesses seeking assistance.

CLEAR Feedback Act (H.R. 10343)

Requires federal agencies to provide clearer, more detailed feedback to small businesses denied federal research and innovation funding. Businesses would receive explanations of why their applications were rejected, helping entrepreneurs improve future proposals, compete, and receive federal opportunities.

SCORE for Small Business Act of 2026 (H.R. 10785)

Reauthorizes the SCORE program, which provides free mentoring, business counseling, and educational resources to entrepreneurs nationwide. The legislation strengthens program oversight and supports online tools that help small-business owners access expert guidance.

Businessowner Immigration Rights and Responsibilities Information Act (BIRRIA) of 2026 (H.R. 9943)

Co-led by Reps. Nydia Velázquez, Gilbert Cisneros, and Analilia Mejia

Requires the SBA to provide accessible, multilingual “know-your-rights” resources to small-business owners and employees during immigration enforcement actions. The legislation would help businesses understand their constitutional protections, comply with federal law, and prepare for potential enforcement encounters.

title: Congressman Menefee Hosts Election Security Discussion with Rep. Joe Morelle, Outlines Efforts to Protect Voters Ahead of Election Day
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) hosted a virtual discussion Tuesday evening with Congressman Joe Morelle (NY-25), Ranking Member of the House Administration Committee, to address concerns among Houston voters about election security, voter intimidation, and potential federal interference in the November 3 midterm elections.

With Election Day less than a week away, the two lawmakers discussed the steps congressional Democrats, election officials, and civil rights organizations are taking to protect voters, respond to threats, and ensure legally cast ballots are counted.

“What I'm hearing most from folks here on the ground is, 'Do y'all have a plan?'” said Congressman Menefee. “We want to know that the folks that we elected to serve in the United States Congress who are not beholden to Donald Trump, who are open to standing up to Donald Trump, that they actually have a plan.”

During the discussion, Morelle detailed House Democrats' election security preparations, including an assessment of approximately 150 potential threats to the midterm elections. His team has spent months developing response strategies and coordinating with attorneys, civil rights organizations, and election protection advocates across all 50 states.

“We have been planning this for months and months,” Rep. Morelle said. “We came up with about 150 different threats that we felt were likely to come from the Trump administration.”

Rep. Morelle also highlighted a series of legal victories against Trump administration efforts to interfere with election administration, including attempts by the Department of Justice to obtain sensitive voter information from states.

“States are 27 and 0 against the Department of Justice's illegal attempts to force states to turn over their voter rolls,” Rep. Morelle said. “Any team that goes 0 and 27, you'd think you'd think about maybe a different direction. But this is Donald Trump's Department of Justice, so they're going to keep plodding along. But we are winning at every turn against them.”

Rep. Morelle acknowledged the anxiety many Americans are feeling ahead of Election Day but emphasized that months of legal preparation and coordination have helped protect the integrity of the election. He also pointed to court rulings blocking changes to mail voting procedures and Congress's failure to enact additional restrictions proposed under the SAVE America Act.

The lawmakers addressed several concerns raised by Houston voters, including:

Federal agents at polling places – Rep. Morelle discussed federal restrictions on armed personnel at polling locations and said legal teams are prepared to seek immediate court intervention if unlawful voter intimidation occurs.

Department of Justice election monitors – The lawmakers discussed the legal limits on federal election monitors, emphasizing that monitors may observe election activity but cannot interfere with voting or ballot counting.

Protecting eligible voters – Rep. Morelle highlighted a recent legal victory in California, where a federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration's emergency attempt to set aside ballots associated with approximately 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The ruling marked an early victory for state election officials fighting to protect eligible voters from improper ballot restrictions.

Delays in election results – Rep. Morelle explained that some states may take additional days to count legally cast ballots, particularly mail ballots, and emphasized that accuracy must remain the priority.

Voting rights legislation –Reps. Menefee and Morelle discussed the importance of strengthening the Voting Rights Act, opposing unnecessarily restrictive voter identification requirements, and protecting access to the ballot box.

The discussion also addressed concerns about attempts to challenge election results after Election Day. Rep. Morelle explained that legal teams and election observers are preparing to monitor ballot counting and respond to potential challenges to certification.

Rep. Morelle emphasized that the preparations extend beyond Congress, with thousands of attorneys, volunteers, and advocates working alongside organizations including the League of Women Voters, Brennan Center for Justice, Common Cause, ACLU, NAACP, and Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law.

Rep. Menefee also emphasized the importance of restoring federal voting rights protections, including the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which he has cosponsored.

“What I heard is there is a team of folks within the House Democratic caucus, but also in the broader infrastructure of civil rights organizations, legal advocacy organizations that are staying on top of this stuff,” Rep. Menefee said. “If people show up to the polling sites to intimidate who are not supposed to be there, we will be in communication with lawyers to get action taken immediately.”

With early voting underway in Texas, Rep. Menefee encouraged constituents to make a plan to vote before the October 30 early voting deadline or on Election Day, November 3.

Voters can find information about polling locations, acceptable identification, and voting procedures at HarrisVotes.com.

Anyone who experiences voter intimidation, encounters problems casting a ballot, or has questions about their voting rights can contact the nonpartisan Election Protection Hotline at 1-866-OUR-VOTE (1-866-687-8683).

“Vote for whoever you want to vote for. But the important part is that if you're eligible to vote, you should vote,” Rep. Menefee said in closing.

title: Rep. Min and 39 Colleagues Demand Answers on the Detentions of U.S. Citizens by Immigration Enforcement
text:
Washington, DC. — Last week, U.S. Representative Dave Min (CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, joined 39 colleagues in a letter to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding answers on the detentions and constitutional violations of U.S. citizens by DHS federal agents during immigration enforcement operations.

The letter is in response to reporting that federal immigration agents have detained more than 500 American citizens during President Trump’s second term. These arrests are the explicit outcome of President Trump’s immigration crackdown, where rogue federal agents have continuously violated Americans’ constitutional rights to due process, equal protection, and freedom from unreasonable search and seizure. The use of immigration enforcement tactics against U.S. citizens has raised questions about what documentation is needed to prove U.S. citizenship or legal residency, resulting in conflicting answers from DHS officials.

“We write to express concerns over the continued detention of U.S. citizens by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) personnel during immigration enforcement operations and to request clarity regarding documentation necessary to prove citizenship or legal authorization to be present in the United States. Recent reporting has found that over 500 U.S. citizens have been detained by federal immigration authorities since the beginning of this Administration in January 2025, including more than 100 who were questioned about their citizenship. We remain concerned that the Department’s actions are violating American citizens’ constitutional rights to due process, equal protection, and freedom from unreasonable search and seizure, and request transparency regarding the Department’s actions,” the lawmakers write.

“While public reporting has shed light on these three encounters, the Department has failed to provide information on the number of U.S. citizens who have been detained or arrested as a result of immigration enforcement operations—despite repeated requests from Members of Congress. The U.S. Government Accountability Office issued a report in July 2021 finding that ICE did not know the extent to which its officers were taking enforcement actions against individuals who could be U.S. citizens, recommending the agency improve its data documentation on encounters with potential citizens. In February 2025, ICE clarified its process to collect data on encounters with potential U.S. citizens and issued a broadcast message to field officials to make sure data is accurate. Despite supposedly instituting improvements to its data collection, ICE has not released information on the number of U.S. citizens encountered during immigration enforcement operations,” the lawmakers continue.

“In addition to denying repeated requests for transparency, the Department has failed to provide consistent information to the public regarding what constitutes proof of U.S. citizenship during an encounter with DHS personnel. In a letter dated April 21, 2026, former Acting Director Lyons wrote that ICE officers “may ask individuals to provide documentation of U.S. citizenship, foreign citizenship, or legal authorization to be present in the United States,” but DHS has yet to provide clear guidance on what documentation is considered sufficient”.

“All Americans are entitled to due process, equal protection under the law, and freedom from illegal search and seizure. We respectfully request your assistance in ensuring these rights are not denied by providing the aforementioned information,” the lawmakers concluded.

Specifically, the lawmakers requested answers to the following questions:

How many U.S. citizens have been detained, which includes investigative stops, by DHS since January 20, 2025?

Are your agents documenting all detentions of U.S. citizens, to include investigative stops? Where is this information being recorded?

How many U.S. citizens have been arrested by DHS since January 20, 2025?

What documentation does DHS consider sufficient to verify citizenship status?

What training do DHS officers and agents receive regarding how to determine whether an individual is a U.S. citizen?

This letter was signed by Representatives Lou Correa, Nanette Barragán, Salud Carbajal, Joaquin Castro, Yvette Clarke, Judy Chu, Joe Courtney, Jim Costa, Jasmine Crockett, Mark DeSaulnier, Diana DeGette, Veronica Escobar, Adriano Espaillat, Sylvia R. Garcia, Vicente Gonzalez, Al Green, Dan Goldman, Pablo Jose Hernandez, Hank Johnson, Julie Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Timothy Kennedy, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Teresa Leger Fernandez, Stephen Lynch, Seth Magaziner, Jerrold Nadler, Richard Neal, Joe Neguse, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Mary Gay Scanlon, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Dina Titus, Norma Torres, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, and Maxine Waters.

title: Griffith Announces More Than $2.1 Million DOT Public Safety Grant to Tazewell County
text:
The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) has awarded the County of Tazewell, Virginia, a $2,118,842 grant. The funding supports the installation of safety improvement features such as double centerline, edge line striping and warning signs, among others. U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) issued the following statement:

“Tazewell County has identified six high-risk corridors with rural two-lane roads that pose risks to the safety of motorists, travelers and pedestrians.

“This DOT grant for more than $2.1 million helps Tazewell County make road improvements that reduce the risk for fatal and serious injury crashes.”

BACKGROUND

This grant money was made available through the DOT Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Grant program.

Road improvements will include 10.8 miles of double centerline striping, 10.7 miles of rumble strips, 1.38 miles of high-friction surface treatments, 60 signs, and targeted transition zone upgrades.

Project work will be directed towards Jewell Ridge Road, Falls Mills Road, Baptist Valley Road, Wardell Road, Indian Creek Road and Kents Ridge Road.

In May 2026, Congressman Griffith authored a letter of support for a local transportation safety project in Tazewell County.

title: Griffith Announces $1 Million ARC Grant for Lee County

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Condemns Trump’s Continued Effort to Remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) led 11 Congressional colleagues in a letter condemning President Trump’s October 7 memorandum establishing a “committee of inquiry” to investigate allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made false statements about her mortgages. The letter also calls for the cancellation of her November 5 hearing.

Trump previously sought to fire Cook over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud. Ultimately, in a 5-4 decision earlier this year, the Supreme Court ruled Trump could not immediately remove her.

Lisa Cook is the first Black woman to serve on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, an HBCU-educated economist, and a native Atlantan. She is a qualified governor whose unparalleled perspective has informed how we have navigated the Trump economy.

The Members wrote:

“We condemn your decision to convene this so-called “committee of inquiry” to examine the allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. We are concerned that this “committee of inquiry” is designed with a predetermined goal, given it is comprised solely of three participants whom you appointed to your administration, and whom have allegiances to you. This sham committee demonstrates your effort to fire Governor Cook at any cost, without legitimate cause. There is nothing impartial about that, and no one is fooled. We urge you to call off your effort to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.”

“We urge you to rescind your October 7 memorandum and cancel the November 5 hearing. If you believe there is cause to remove Governor Cook, put the evidence before an independent arbitrator agreed to by both sides, in a proceeding open to the public and the press. If your case is as strong as you claim, it will withstand scrutiny from someone you do not control.”

title: Rep. Panetta’s Statement on the Passing of Dolores Huerta
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) issued the following statement on the passing of labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta.

“I am deeply saddened by the passing of Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers and a pioneer in the fight for labor and civil rights, women’s rights, and equality.

“Her lifetime of advocacy and action helped generations of farmworkers secure better wages, safer working conditions, and a voice on the job. Dolores inspired the fight for many farmworkers to achieve the American Dream and give their children a better life. Her legacy is felt well beyond our local agricultural communities on the central coast of California and throughout our country.

“My heart is with her family, friends, and all those who carry forward her pursuit of giving farmworkers fairness and our children a brighter future.”
