title: New Hampshire Congressional Delegation Applauds Delivery of Over $5.9 Million to New Hampshire Electric Co-Op
text:
U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (NH-D), U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan (NH-D), Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), and Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) applauded the delivery of over $5.9 million in federal funding to the New Hampshire Electric Cooperative (NHEC).

"Last year's severe winter storms created enormous wind and flooding across New Hampshire, leading many Granite Staters to lose power. Thanks to the work of emergency response crews working around the clock, the damage to our electrical infrastructure was repaired but at great cost to small communities with limited resources," said Senator Shaheen. "I'm glad to see that more than five million dollars in federal funding is headed to the New Hampshire Electric Cooperative to help cover these expenses and better prepare our critical infrastructure for the future."

“It is critical that our communities have the resources that they need to recover and rebuild in the face of severe storms,” said Senator Hassan. “This federal funding will help New Hampshire communities repair critical infrastructure damaged by severe weather, improve flood protections, and strengthen our state’s emergency preparedness. I will continue working to bring federal resources back to New Hampshire to ensure that our communities have the support that they need to recover from severe storms and prepare for future disasters.”

“This federal funding supports the reconstruction of critical infrastructure by NHEC and protects the well-being of Granite Staters,” said Congressman Pappas. “I’ll continue working to deliver resources back to New Hampshire to update old or damaged infrastructure, strengthen our storm preparedness, and keep people safe.”

“When the April 2024 storm tore down power lines and poles across our state, New Hampshire Electric Co-op crews worked long, hard hours in brutal conditions to get the lights back on,” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “Granite Staters shouldn't be left holding the bill for that recovery. I'm glad to see more than $5.9 million in federal disaster funding coming home to New Hampshire to reimburse the Co-op. The power of this Co-op is that it's owned by its members, so this money goes right back to the people it serves. I'll keep fighting for every penny that's yours.”

Background:

In April 2024, a severe winter storm brought strong winds and flooding that damaged the NHEC electrical distribution system, threatening the health and safety of Granite Staters. Strong winds damaged power lines, utility poles, and transformers, causing power outages in Belknap, Carroll, Grafton, Rockingham, and Sullivan Counties.

title: Pelosi Statement on the Passing of Dolores Huerta
text:
Washington, D.C. — Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi issued the following statement on the passing of labor leader Dolores Huerta:

“Today, we sadly mourn the loss of Dolores Huerta, a leader in the American labor movement and a champion for civil rights who lead with courage and determination.

“Dolores was a dear friend, and we all responded to her rallying cry, ‘Sí se puede,’ which inspired generations of Americans to believe in the power of collective action. I was honored to host Dolores’ birthday celebration at the United States Capitol when she turned 90, a compliment she returned to me at the California Democratic Party Convention in San Francisco earlier this year.

“May it be a comfort to her family and loved ones that so many mourn their loss and are praying for them at this sad time.”

title: CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CONDEMNS BRUTAL ATTACK ON YOUNG MAN
text:
For Immediate Release Contact: Tionee Scotland

October 28, 2026 202-808-6129

PRESS RELEASE

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CONDEMNS BRUTAL ATTACK ON YOUNG MAN

U.S. Virgin Islands — Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett released the following statement in response to a video circulating on social media that shows a young man being beaten, apparently because of his sexual orientation:

“I was very upset by the video of a young man being beaten by several individuals, seemingly for no reason other than who he is.

“All of our children matter. Every one of them is part of our community, and every one of them deserves to grow up safe, free to be exactly who they are. An attack on one of our young people because of who they are is an attack on all of us and on the values of respect and family that define us as Virgin Islanders.

“I am asking on the Virgin Islands Police Department to investigate this attack as a hate crime under the territory’s Hate-Motivated Crimes Act and to work with federal partners as needed to ensure those responsible are held fully accountable. I urge anyone with information to come forward to law enforcement. The violence and anti-social behavior among our young people has to be addressed. As a community we need to also reflect on the continued taping and circulation of violent, negative videos; it doesn’t reflect positively on our values as a people.

“To this young man and his family: you are not alone. Our community stands with you, and we are praying for your healing.”

title: Congressman Riley M. Moore Celebrates National Park Foundation Grant for C&O Canal National Historical Park
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Riley M. Moore celebrates the National Park Foundation’s announcement of $12 million in grants supporting 30 innovative programs across 40 national parks, including the C&O Canal National Historical Park.

Congressman Riley M. Moore released the following statement:

“The National Park Foundation’s grant to support the C&O Canal National Historic Park is great news for West Virginia and will help preserve the C&O Canal for historic and recreational purposes for future generations. The C&O Canal is an important part of our region’s heritage, and I’m glad to see investments that will help protect our parks, improve public safety, and enhance the experience for visitors.”

The grants will help national parks and their partners test new technologies and innovative approaches to managing natural, cultural, and historic resources, strengthening public safety, and improving visitor education and interpretation.

title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Mourns the Loss of Dolores Huerta
text:
LOS ANGELES – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) – the first Latina to represent California’s 29th Congressional District – released the following statement mourning the loss of civil rights leader Dolores Huerta:

“I join my neighbors, friends, and community in mourning the loss of Dolores Huerta, a trailblazer in the civil rights movement and an icon to many. Through her decades of activism fighting labor injustices and inequality, Dolores became an inspiration for generations of organizers and changemakers to continue demanding for a better and just future for all.

“Even in her final months, Dolores continued using her voice to speak truth to power. Her courage to come forward about her own sexual assault earlier this year empowered other women to share their stories and find their voices.

“Dolores’ legacy will live on in every person she empowered to speak up, every worker continuing to fight for dignity and fair treatment, and every generation moving the struggle for justice forward. May we honor her memory by continuing the fight she dedicated her life to.”

###

title: Congressman Robert Garcia Statement on Passing of Dolores Huerta
text:
LONG BEACH, CA – Today, Congressman Robert Garcia (CA-42) released the following statement on the passing of labor leader and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta.

“Dolores Huerta was one of the bravest and most relentless advocates for working families and farm workers that America has ever seen.

Her work changed lives across the country, including those of families across my community and our state. Dolores helped raise workers’ wages and benefits, fought for women’s rights, and built invaluable grassroots voter engagement efforts. Her lifelong commitment to activism and empowerment transformed countless labor unions, feminist movements, and progressive organizations for the better.

She was a kind person who lived through struggle and pain but always tried to do the right thing. She has inspired generations and her legacy will never be forgotten,” said Congressman Robert Garcia.

title: Congressman Pete Stauber Leads Letter Urging Air Force Secretary to Base F-35 Fleet at the 148th Fighter Wing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Pete Stauber (MN-08), joined by members of the Minnesota delegation, sent a letter to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink urging him to base a fleet of F-35 Fighter Jets at the 148th Fighter Wing in Duluth, Minnesota. This letter was sent as the Department of the Air Force reviews scoring criteria for the formal basing process that evaluates candidate sites for major weapons systems and personnel.

“As threats from dangerous adversaries continue to escalate, America must remain ready to respond,” said Congressman Pete Stauber. “The 148th Fighter Wing already plays a crucial role in defending the homeland, and equipping them with the most lethal, survivable, and connected fighter jet would further strengthen their mission. The brave men and women of the 148th who serve alongside our active-duty forces deserve the best equipment available so they can execute their duties and return home safely. As a strong supporter of the 148th Fighter Wing, I have long fought to base the F-35 here in the Northland, and I will continue my advocacy until the job is done.”

In the letter, Congressman Stauber emphasized the 148th’s stellar performance during recent operations in the Middle East, importance to homeland defense, strategic location, prime airspace, State Partnership Programs, and local support as reasons for the F-35 to be based there.

Read the full letter HERE.

Congressman Stauber has been advocating for the F-35 to be based at the 148th Fighter Wing since he took office in 2019.

title: Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia Statement on the Passing of Dolores Huerta
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29) released the following statement on the passing of legendary labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta at age 96:

“I am heartbroken by the passing of Dolores Huerta. Our country has lost a giant in the fight for civil rights, workers’ rights, and justice. And I have lost a dear friend who inspired me and countless others across generations.

“I grew up in Palito Blanco, Texas, picking cotton in the fields under the hot sun. I know how hard that work is and the sacrifices farmworkers and their families make every day. Dolores dedicated her life to making sure those workers were seen, heard, and treated with dignity. She stood up to powerful interests, organized communities, and fought for fair wages and better working conditions for the people who put food on our tables.

“She was also a proud feminist and a fierce champion for women’s rights. Dolores paved the way for Latinas like me. At a time when Mexican American women were too often told to sit down and stay quiet, Dolores stood up and showed us that our voices mattered and that ordinary people could accomplish extraordinary things.

“And I’ll always smile remembering how every time Dolores came to Houston, she wanted to go to a Tex-Mex restaurant for some carne guisada. Those are the little things that made her so special to those of us who knew her.

“My heart goes out to her family, her loved ones, and the people whose lives she touched. We must honor her by continuing the fight for dignity, equality, and justice that she dedicated her life to.

“Descansa en paz, gran amiga. Seguiré la lucha que tú empezaste.”

###

HOUSTON, TX — Hoy, la congresista Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29) realizó el siguiente comunicado sobre el fallecimiento, a los 96 años, de Dolores Huerta, legendaria líder sindical y defensora de derechos civiles.

"Me duele profundamente la muerte de Dolores Huerta. Nuestro país ha perdido a una gran luchadora por los derechos civiles, los derechos de los trabajadores y la justicia. Y he perdido a una querida amiga que me inspiró y a muchas otras personas de distintas generaciones.

"Yo crecí en Palito Blanco, Texas pizcando algodón en los campos bajo el sol caliente. Sé lo duro que es ese trabajo y los sacrificios que los trabajadores del campo y sus familias hacen todos los días. Dolores dedicó su vida a luchar para que los trabajadores fueran vistos y tratados con dignidad. Ella se enfrentó a los poderosos, organizó comunidades y luchó por salarios justos y mejores condiciones de trabajo para los que ponen la comida en nuestras mesas.

"Ella era una feminista orgullosa y una gran defensora de los derechos de las mujeres. Dolores abrió el camino para latinas como yo. En una época cuando a las mujeres mexicoamericanas muchas veces les decían que se sentaran, que se hicieran a un lado y que se quedaran calladas, Dolores alzó la voz y nos demostró que nuestra voz importaba y que la gente común podía lograr cosas extraordinarias.

"Y siempre recordaré con una sonrisa que cada vez que Dolores venía a Houston, ella quería ir a un restaurante de Tex-Mex a comer carne guisada. Esos pequeños detalles eran parte de lo que la hacía tan especial para quienes la conocíamos.

"Mi corazón está con su familia, sus seres queridos y todas las personas a las que tocó con su vida. La mejor manera de honrarla es seguir luchando por la dignidad, la igualdad y la justicia, como ella lo hizo toda su vida.

"Descansa en paz, gran amiga. Seguiré la lucha que tú empezaste."

title: ICYMI: Centre Daily Times: ‘Excellent news for the region.’ Penn State to Establish Manufacturing Hub in DuBois
text:
BELLEFONTE, Pa. — U.S. Representative Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) celebrated the U.S. Department of Commerce’s recent announcement awarding Penn State $39.9 million to establish the DuBois Center for Innovation. Rep. Thompson worked with Secretary Howard Lutnick to secure the funding.

From the Centre Daily Times

..."U.S. Rep. Glenn “GT” Thompson, R-Howard, described the development as “excellent news for the region.”

“Our region is the epicenter of the world’s powdered metals industry, and this investment will ensure that we remain globally competitive into the future,” Thompson said in a written statement. “I was proud to push for this project, which will significantly enhance the regional talent pipeline and global competitiveness in an area facing persistent workforce shortages.”

Penn State said the grant from the U.S. Economic Development Administration is expected to catalyze nearly $200 million in public and private investment. Up to three-quarters of the total could come from “potential investment” from Bunting Magnetics & Magnetic Applications.

The hub is to be designed to grow the region’s manufacturing economy and accelerate innovation in the pressed metals industry, a specialized field that uses pressure, heat and technology to transform fine metal and other material powders into high-performance components and products."

title: Congressman Tim Moore Announces $11.2 Million in FEMA Funding for Lake Lure, Fallston, and NC Emergency Management
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) announced $11,209,597.27 in federal funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for Hurricane Helene recovery across Lake Lure, Fallston, and North Carolina. Projects include critical road bridge and building repairs, dam gate restoration, and emergency protective measures.

“Recovery from Hurricane Helene is about rebuilding while also making our communities safer for the future,” said Congressman Moore. "This $11.2 million investment will repair the road bridge and dam gates in Lake Lure, restore the Friendship Methodist Church in Fallston, and give North Carolina Emergency Management the resources it needs for damage assessments and protective measures. I’m grateful to the Administration and FEMA for keeping Western North Carolina’s recovery a top priority."

$753,823.35 will go to the Town of Lake Lure to fund the repair or replacement of the road bridge damaged by Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$582,773.16 will go to the Town of Lake Lure to fund the restoration of the dam gates as a result of Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$111,276.54 will go to the Friendship Methodist Church of Fallston to fund the repair of the building interior and exterior components damaged by Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$7,822,559.22 will go to North Carolina Emergency Management to support emergency protective measures as a result of Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 403 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$1,939,165.00 will go to North Carolina Emergency Management to fund comprehensive damage assessments as a result of Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 403 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

title: Congresswoman Norma Torres Statement on the Passing of Civil Rights Icon Dolores Huerta
text:
Ontario, CA — Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) released the following statement on the passing of Dolores Huerta:

“My heart is heavy as we mourn the loss of Dolores Huerta, a fearless leader whose courage changed this country and whose example changed what generations of Latinas believed was possible.

“I admired Dolores deeply. She stood up in spaces where Latinas like us were dismissed, underestimated, and told to wait our turn. She organized, she led, and she demanded that our voices carry weight in the decisions shaping our lives. For so many of us, her example made it easier to find our own voice and the courage to use it.

“Dolores understood that the people who feed this nation deserve to live with dignity. She helped farmworkers turn collective action into better wages, safer working conditions, and a powerful movement for justice. She challenged a country that depended on their labor while too often turning away from their suffering.

“My heart is with her family, her loved ones, and the generations of organizers who carry her teachings with them. Dolores gave so much of her life so that others could live with greater dignity and opportunity. May she rest knowing how profoundly she changed our country. Por siempre, sí se puede.”

title: Congressman Matt Van Epps, Governor Lee, and Members of the Tennessee Delegation Urge President Trump to establish New U.S. Space Academy in Tennessee
text:
NASHVILLE, TN – Rep. Van Epps, Governor Lee, Senators Marsha Blackburn and Bill Hagerty, and Rep. Scott DesJarlais announced Tennessee’s intention to pursue having the United States Space Academy in the Volunteer State. The initiative, established by President Donald J. Trump to strengthen America’s space superiority, presents an opportunity to build on Tennessee’s existing strengths and prepare the next generation of leaders for America’s future in space.

Rep. Van Epps said, “Tennessee offers readily available land, world-class aerospace testing infrastructure, an established academic partner, and a strong network of space, defense, and research institutions. These assets uniquely position Tennessee to serve as the home of the United States Space Academy. As a West Point graduate, I understand the importance of world-class institutions to educate, train, and commission officers for our service branches. I’m confident Tennessee is the best place to equip our armed forces to conduct effective space operations and secure our national security interests in space.”

Governor Lee stated, “Someone has to determine what the future looks like, and I’ve long believed that should be Tennessee. From leading the nation in clean, reliable nuclear energy to developing the workforce needed to win the future, the Volunteer State is already leading the next era of American innovation. I’m grateful to President Trump for his leadership to establish the United States Space Academy and to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and the Presidential Commission for their work to bring this vision to life. We look forward to building on our momentum to create new job opportunities for Tennesseans and strengthen America’s leadership in space for generations to come.”

Senator Marsha Blackburn said, “From Arnold Air Force Base to Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Tennessee has powered our nation’s space and defense enterprise for generations, making us the natural home for the U.S. Space Academy. I am honored to stand with Governor Lee behind our state’s bid to educate and train the next generation of astronauts, engineers, scientists, and warfighters who will keep America dominant in space.”

Senator Bill Hagerty said, “Tennessee has the workforce, infrastructure, and determination needed to train the next generation of American space leaders and strengthen our nation’s future in space. I am pleased to stand with Governor Lee as we pursue bringing the United States Space Academy to the Volunteer State.”

Congressman Scott DesJarlais stated, “I’m pleased to join with Governor Lee in letting folks know about the great potential for Tennessee to be the home of the United States Space Academy. Tennessee has a great academic reputation in aerospace, science, and engineering, and the University of Tennessee Space Institute has been a national leader in developing these skills for years. With UTSI and Arnold Air Force Base, and a significant number of our citizens already commuting and working in the defense and aerospace sectors in Huntsville—the new home of the United States Space Force—there is a natural synergy, educational and technical experience, and geographical advantage to our state that would make it a natural fit for the academy.”

title: Walberg Honors Jackson County Veteran
text:
Today, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) recognized Harvey Lake of Jackson as the Veteran of the Month for October. The Congressman presented Harvey with the Congressional Record containing his remarks honoring Harvey's service and dedication to our country.

Harvey was drafted into the United States Army in 1972 and completed his basic training at Fort Knox, Kentucky, followed by Advanced Individual Training at Fort Jackson, South Carolina, where he trained as a 63B20 Wheel Vehicle Mechanic.

Harvey was stationed in Ludwigsburg, Germany, where he served for over 18 months with Company B, 34th Signal Battalion, VII Corps. His unit played an important role in relaying communications to the VII Corps at Kelly Barracks in Stuttgart, Germany, and contributing to the United States’ efforts during the Cold War.

Harvey completed his service in June 1974 and was later honorably discharged from the Army in June 1978 at the rank of Specialist 4. For his service, Harvey earned the National Defense Medal, Marksman recognition, and a Wheel Vehicle Mechanic Certificate.

His commitment to our nation is also part of a proud family tradition of military service. His father served during World War II as a B-24 gunner in the Pacific, while his brother Roger also answered the call to serve in the United States Army and was honorably discharged.

"It is my privilege to recognize Harvey Lake of Jackson as the Veteran of the Month for October," said Rep. Walberg. "Harvey faithfully served our nation during the Cold War, contributing to critical communications operations in Germany. His honorable service to the United States and his continued devotion to his community serve as an inspiration to us all. On behalf of a grateful nation, I am proud to recognize Harvey Lake for his lasting contributions and extend my deepest gratitude for his service and sacrifice."

You can view pictures of the presentation here.

Background

Congressman Walberg's office is accepting submissions for the Veteran of the Month program, an initiative to honor the exemplary contributions of veterans in Michigan's 5th Congressional District. Each month, Congressman Walberg will recognize one outstanding veteran, celebrating their commitment to serving our community and their exceptional service in the military.

title: Congressman Weber Joins Secretary Duffy and Congressman Babin for Historic Energy and Maritime Announcements at the Sea Power Summit
text:
HOUSTON, TEXAS - Today, Congressman Randy Weber (TX-14) joined U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy and Congressman Brian Babin (TX-36) at Port Houston for the Sea Power Summit, where Secretary Duffy delivered a pair of wins for the Gulf of America by modernizing LNG safety regulations for the first time since 2001 and licensing a new LNG export port offshore Matagorda, Texas.

The new safety rule is expected to save over $100 million and fast-track new LNG projects, while the Matagorda port will support 2,000 construction jobs and up to 855 permanent jobs and expand America's LNG export capacity by 7 to 9%.

The Matagorda port sits just down the coast from Brazoria County, and its jobs and growth will ripple across the Texas Gulf Coast. Texas' 14th District already anchors that coastline, with seven ports and three LNG terminals producing about 27% of America's gasoline, 60% of its jet fuel, and 80% of the fuel our military runs on.

Click here to watch Rep. Weber's Remarks at the Sea Power Summit!

"Unleashing American energy and restoring American maritime dominance go hand-in-hand. These are two of the Trump Administration's top priorities – and today's Sea Power Summit proves we can deliver real results," said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. "From approving a massive deepwater port license at record speed to modernizing outdated LNG regulations for the first time in two decades, USDOT is creating an economic boom for the Gulf of America. When our energy and maritime industries thrive, Texas wins."

"The Texas Gulf Coast represents the very best of America. Our people work hard, fly under the radar, and show up the moment the country needs them," said Congressman Randy Weber (TX-14). "Today, Secretary Duffy returned the favor and came down to the Gulf of America to show up for us. What starts here in our little slice of heaven doesn't stay here for long, and all 342 million Americans will reap the benefits of these major announcements for years to come."

Under President Trump's leadership, the Administration and Congressman Weber continue to deliver for American energy and the Texas Gulf Coast:

In January 2026, the Maritime Administration took over deepwater port licensing from the Coast Guard, cutting red tape and speeding up new energy supply lines for America.

The Maritime Administration delivered $35 million to America's small shipyards, a 300% increase in funding for 2026, and is delivering nearly $1 billion to modernize America's ports.

Congressman Weber's Pipeline Safety Authorization Act of 2026 (H.R. 9338) advanced through the Energy and Commerce Committee in July.

Congressman Weber secured $17.9 million in FY26 to dredge and maintain the Galveston Ship Channel, along with more than $9 million to deepen the Sabine-Neches Waterway.

The House's FY27 Energy and Water bill includes $12.7 million that Rep. Weber secured for Galveston Harbor and Channel maintenance, plus another $100 million to continue deepening the Sabine-Neches Waterway.

Rep. Weber's priority to expedite a new Sabine-Neches feasibility review passed the House in WRDA 2026.

title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Bill to Bring Transparency and Accountability to Public Safety Power Shutoffs After County-Wide Outage
text:
The Public Safety Power Shutoff Data Transparency Act would create the first national reporting program for preventive power shutoffs, giving families, first responders, and hospitals the information they need to plan and stay safe

WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Rep. George Whitesides (CA-27) announced his introduction of the Public Safety Power Shutoff Data Transparency Act directing the U.S. Department of Energy to establish a standardized federal reporting program for Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events.

Nearly 70,000 households across Los Angeles and Ventura counties went without power two weeks ago under preventive shutoffs. There is currently no consistent, nationwide record of when these shutoffs happen, how long they last, who they affect, or how well communities were warned. Earlier, Southern California Edison warned that close to 260,000 customers across the region could lose power, many of them in the Santa Clarita Valley. Neighborhoods in Canyon Country, Bouquet Canyon, and Castaic Junction were among those cut off, and restoration often takes eight hours or more after winds subside while crews inspect lines. Hospitals and other emergency response facilities were unsure if they would also be impacted by the public safety power shutoffs.

“After thousands went without power weeks ago, and hospitals and first responders were left uncertain how the power shutoffs would affect their facilities, it’s clear that we need to take concrete steps to address this issue,” said Rep. George Whitesides. “Power shutoffs can be a critical tool during extreme fire weather, but if we don’t track, report, and communicate these outages to the public, we have no way of making them less disruptive. My bill will bring transparency and accountability to the process, to make sure individuals and first responders understand when an outage is coming, how long it will last, and how many people will be affected.”

The Public Safety Power Shutoff Data Transparency Act would:

Require standardized federal reporting of every PSPS event so that utilities serving 25,000 or more customers – and smaller utilities operating in designated high-risk wildfire areas – must report to the Department of Energy within seven days of starting and ending a shutoff. Reports cover the geographic extent of the outage, its start and end times, the number of customers and critical services affected, the hazard conditions that prompted it, how the utility communicated with the public, and how it coordinated with state, local, Tribal, and emergency-response agencies.

Direct the DOE to collect, publish, and analyze PSPS data to show the frequency, duration, and regional trends of shutoffs, including impacts on rural, low-income, and Tribal communities.

Require utilities to report which critical services (including health centers and other emergency response facilities) will be affected by the shutoff. DOE would also be required to share PSPS information with the Department of Health and Human Services, hospitals, emergency medical services networks, FEMA, and state emergency management agencies, so those planning for patient care and emergency response have the data they need.

Give local governments a voice by allowing them to submit verified feedback and supplemental data on how shutoffs affected their communities.

Minimize red tape by allowing DOE to build the new reporting fields into existing outage-reporting forms, such as Form OE-417, to avoid duplicating work for utilities.

Ensure hospitals and other critical health infrastructure are properly notified and considered when utilities plan PSPS events.

The bill also includes protections for sensitive and security-related information submitted by utilities, while keeping aggregated summaries available to the public.

title: ICYMI: Hickenlooper Discusses Medicaid Cuts and Rising Healthcare Costs with Coloradans
text:
5 million Americans have already lost access to healthcare

DENVER – In case you missed it, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper heard from Coloradans struggling to afford healthcare, including those impacted by Republicans’ $1 trillion cut to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.

During the discussion, Coloradans described losing Medicaid coverage and making difficult trade-offs to afford care. Jamie Jenkins, pictured above, is the adoptive-parent of five disabled kids on Medicaid. This year, Medicaid stopped paying for in-home nursing for two of them.

“We’re fighting, and it is medically necessary. My kids will die [without it],” she said.

Watch Hickenlooper’s reaction HERE.

Hickenlooper has been a vocal opponent of the healthcare cuts in H.R.1, which threatens coverage for 240,000 Coloradans. Hickenlooper voted against the measure and has traveled across Colorado since its passage to learn about the law’s impact on Coloradans.

In July, Hickenlooper celebrated committee passage of his bipartisan Patients Deserve Price Tags Act, which would require hospitals and insurers to post prices up front. The bill will help lower healthcare prices through creating opportunities for consumers to compare prices, leading to competition among providers to lower costs.
